surprises.description: The preview noted that Avista had paused processing a service request for a 500 MW data-center project. Management went further, removing the project from the capital plan and pausing the MOU while it addresses internal processes and affordability protections; it also said it would not proceed without preserving reliability and delivering a net benefit for existing customers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Avista removed the 500-megawatt data center project from its capital plan and paused the MOU to work through internal processes and customer affordability protections.” Management said it “will not proceed with a new large data center customer unless existing customer reliability is maintained and there is a net benefit for current customers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Avista signed an MOU with a 500 MW data-center developer in May 2026, then paused processing the service request on Jun 12, 2026.”

surprises.description: The preview said a late-2026 Washington rate-case decision was expected, but did not flag that reaching a settlement could be difficult. Management cited a fundamental disagreement over the four-year plan term, with a September hearing and a mid-December order expected; it also described public counsel’s disputes over return and the power supply adjustment, while saying staff’s position was relatively close.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects a settlement to be difficult due to fundamental disagreement over the 4-year plan term,” with a hearing set for September 17–18 and a commission order expected mid-December. Public counsel’s disagreements center on return level and a power supply adjustment, while staff’s position is “relatively close to the company’s.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Washington rate case. Four-year case filed Jan 16, 2026; WUTC decision expected late 2026.”

surprises.description: The preview did not mention Spokane-area wildfires or service interruptions. The call reported that fires had left about 7,300 electric customers and 5,300 natural gas customers without service, a new operational disruption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Multiple wildfires near Spokane have left roughly 7,300 of Avista's 429,000 electric customers and about 5,300 of its 386,000 natural gas customers without service.”

surprises.description: Despite the wildfire-related outages, management said Avista’s facilities did not start the fires and the infrastructure impact was far below the scale that would require securitization. It also expects minimal regulatory lag because the damaged assets are long-lived and may seek cost recovery after assessing the damage, limiting the potential financial exposure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Avista stated its facilities were not involved in starting any of the Spokane-area fires, reducing potential liability exposure.” The monetary infrastructure impact is “nowhere near the scale that would require securitization”; management expects “minimal regulatory lag impact” and may file a UTC cost-recovery petition after the assessment.

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate a wildfire-related transmission constraint or its repair. Management said a key transmission line had been repaired and energized, significantly reducing the risk of new outages from capacity constraints, although other lines and distribution damage still require assessment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Crews repaired and energized a key transmission line, significantly reducing the risk of new outages from system capacity constraints,” though “a few transmission lines and significant distribution damage remain to be assessed.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged non-utility investment marks as a source of headline-EPS uncertainty, citing clean-tech valuation losses in Q2 2025, but did not indicate that a public-market investment would drive a strong current-quarter result or that the gain might reverse next quarter. Management said an EIP investment, ERock, going public drove a strong quarter and warned that an expected next-quarter gain will likely reverse at ERock’s current stock price.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The nonregulated segment delivered a strong quarter driven by an EIP investment (ERock) that went public,” but “an expected gain next quarter will likely reverse given the current ERock stock price.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-utility investment marks. Clean-tech fund valuation losses drove the Q2 2025 miss and are the main source of headline-EPS noise.”

surprises.description: KRYS reported diluted EPS of $1.79, above the preview’s preferred $1.70 estimate but below its conflicting $1.89 estimate. The quarter therefore beat the more reliable estimate modestly, while missing the higher published estimate by a similar margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net income rose to $54.8 million ($1.79 diluted EPS).
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 EPS of $1.70 as the more reliable anchor and also cited a conflicting $1.89 estimate.

surprises.description: The preview described ex-U.S. growth as a key narrative, but European and Japanese revenue was essentially flat quarter-over-quarter. Management attributed this to a reserve provision during German pricing negotiations, while saying underlying vial demand grew by double digits sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: European and Japanese revenue was essentially flat quarter-over-quarter due to a reserve provision tied to ongoing German pricing negotiations, though management said underlying vial demand grew by double digits sequentially.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called ex-U.S. (Germany, France, Japan) “the growth narrative” and flagged the ex-U.S. ramp as a swing factor.

surprises.description: The KB801 study is taking longer to produce data than the preview’s enrollment timeline suggested: KRYS is expanding it into a global trial with EU sites, and now expects data in early 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: The KB801 study in neurotrophic keratitis is being expanded to a global trial with EU sites, pushing expected data into early 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said KB801 was expected to complete 60-patient enrollment by year-end.

surprises.description: KRYS said it had more than 730 U.S. reimbursement approvals, exceeding its initial target of 60% penetration of the roughly 1,200 identified patients. The preview did not identify this approval target or milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company achieved more than 730 U.S. reimbursement approvals, surpassing its initial 60% penetration target of the ~1,200 identified patient pool, with 35-50 new approvals added per quarter.

surprises.description: KRYS disclosed that several programs beyond the pipeline milestones highlighted in the preview—including KB111, KB407, and two KB707 programs—are advancing toward registrational study starts in 2027. The preview did not flag these additional 2027 study-start plans.
surprises.fact_evidence: Multiple pipeline programs (cystic fibrosis KB407, Hailey-Hailey KB111, inhaled KB707 in NSCLC, and intratumoral KB707 in Gorlin syndrome) are advancing toward registrational study starts in 2027.

surprises.description: KRYS reported late-line NSCLC response rates for inhaled KB707, a result not anticipated in the preview. With no expected response-rate benchmark provided, the result is notable but cannot be judged against a stated bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: Inhaled KB707 showed a 36% monotherapy and 31% pembrolizumab-combination response rate in late-line NSCLC.

in_line: Q2 revenue was $119.2 million, essentially matching the preview’s preferred $119.05 million consensus estimate.
Gross margin was 95%, matching the preview’s expectation that it hold at or above 95%.
The company reaffirmed FY2026 non-GAAP R&D and SG&A guidance of $175–195 million, consistent with the guide highlighted in the preview.
KB803 remained on track for a readout later in 2026, consistent with the preview’s expectation of topline results in Q4 2026.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.55, above the preview’s $0.53–$0.54 consensus range and at the high end of company guidance. The beat was modest, but positive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS rose 8% year-over-year to $0.55, landing at the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus … $0.53 … or $0.54”; company guidance was “$0.52 – $0.56.”

surprises.description: BSG comps declined 2.1% rather than showing the return to growth the preview was watching for. This was a clear negative gap against that qualitative expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BSG comparable sales declined 2.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Beauty Systems Group returning to growth” and “Any sign of return to growth.”

surprises.description: Net sales of $935 million came in about $4 million below the preview’s roughly $939 million consensus, although sales remained within company guidance. The gap was small.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 fiscal 2026 net sales totaled $935 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~$939.3M” consensus (also “$939.38M” from another source); company guidance was “$932M – $942M.”

surprises.description: BSG’s operating margin fell 20 basis points to 12.3%, reversing the prior quarter’s reported margin expansion. The preview did not forecast a BSG margin decline, and the decline came despite BSG gross margin expanding.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Segment operating margin declining 20 basis points to 12.3% despite gross margin expanding 70 basis points to 40.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited prior-quarter BSG segment operating margin of “12.4%, +90 bps.”

surprises.description: The company did not trim its FY26 EPS outlook, despite the preview identifying a trim as the likeliest negative catalyst; instead, it narrowed the range around the same $2.06 midpoint. This was a modestly favorable outcome versus that downside risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Narrowing full-year fiscal 2026 guidance, tightening adjusted diluted EPS to $2.04–$2.08 (from $2.02–$2.10).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A trim to the $2.02–$2.10 range would be the most likely negative catalyst.”

in_line: Comparable sales were flat, matching the preview’s expectation of approximately flat comps.
Gross margin expanded 40 basis points, providing the margin gains the preview said consensus needed to support EPS.
Fuel for Growth remained on track for approximately $45 million in FY26 savings, consistent with the preview’s focus on pacing against that target.

surprises.description: Twist reported Q3 revenue of $118.4 million, above both its $114–115 million guidance and the $114.55 million consensus. The roughly $3.9 million consensus beat was solid but below the preview’s bull-case threshold of $116 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue reached a record $118.4 million,” while the actual Q3 beat was “only ~$4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Company guidance | $114–115M”; “Consensus | $114.55M”; bull scenario: “Revenue at or above $116M.”

surprises.description: Twist raised FY26 revenue guidance to $456–457 million, a substantially larger outlook than the preview’s $442–447 million range. The approximately $12 million midpoint increase exceeded the Q3 revenue beat, turning a modest quarterly beat into a stronger full-year outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $456-457 million (up $12 million at midpoint), while the actual Q3 beat was only ~$4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026: Company guidance is $442–447M”; the preview’s bull case was guidance “raised above $447M,” while its base case was “tightened toward the high end but not raised.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue guidance of $123–124 million points to a sharp sequential increase from Q3, rather than the roughly flat-to-modestly-up Q4 implied by the preview’s arithmetic. It also implies about 25% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue is guided to $123-124 million, implying ~25% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q4 at “about $113.6–117.6M” and described that as “roughly flat to modestly up from Q3.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA loss of about $11.3 million was worse than the preview’s rough $5–8 million loss range, making the quarter’s operating result weaker than expected. Management nevertheless reaffirmed Q4 breakeven, as previously targeted.
surprises.fact_evidence: Twist posted “a Q3 adjusted EBITDA loss of ~$11.3 million” and “reaffirmed its expectation to reach adjusted EBITDA breakeven in Q4 fiscal 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Q3 result materially worse than roughly –$5M to –$8M would make Q4 breakeven hard to reach”; the company had targeted breakeven “in Q4 FY26, not Q3.”

surprises.description: Gross margin came in at 52.8%, above the preview’s threshold of 52% for meeting the FY26 target. It also improved 120 basis points sequentially from the 51.6% reported in Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin was 52.8%, up 120 basis points sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said gross margin “needs to return above 52% to hit the FY target.”

surprises.description: DNA Synthesis and Protein Solutions grew 39% year over year, a strong result against the preview’s concern that NGS growth might remain around Q2’s 12%. The preview expected H2 growth led by NGS but did not anticipate growth at this reported rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DNA Synthesis and Protein Solutions revenue grew 39% year-over-year to $56.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NGS grew 12% in Q2. Management promised NGS-led H2 growth”; the bear scenario included “NGS growth still around 12%.”

surprises.description: Academic and government revenue rebounded to 32% year-over-year growth and rose 21% sequentially, after only 3% growth in the prior quarter. That was a sharp reversal from the weak academic-spending backdrop highlighted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Academic and government revenue rebounded sharply to $15.5 million, up 32% year-over-year and 21% sequentially, versus just 3% growth the prior quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “Agilent noted academic and government spending down 5%” and that this “argues against expecting broad upside.”

surprises.description: Twist said it expects to meet or exceed triple-digit percentage growth in AI-enabled drug-discovery orders in FY26 and expressed confidence in repeating that growth in FY27. The FY26 level is broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of doubling, but confidence in another triple-digit-growth year was additional forward commentary.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects to meet or exceed triple-digit percent order growth for AI-enabled drug discovery in fiscal 2026 and reaffirmed confidence in repeating triple-digit order growth in fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had stated AI-related orders were “on track to double in FY26”; it did not describe an FY27 triple-digit-growth outlook.

surprises.description: The company disclosed that about $2 million of Q3 OpEx was one-time employee transition cost and said the changes are expected to reduce Q4 OpEx by more than $5 million. The preview did not anticipate this cost action or the indicated savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 OpEx of $98.7 million included ~$2 million in one-time employee transition costs expected to drive over $5 million in OpEx reduction in Q4.”

in_line: FY26 AI-enabled drug-discovery order growth guidance of at least triple-digit percentage growth broadly confirmed the preview’s expectation that orders were on track to double in FY26.
Management reaffirmed its previously stated target of adjusted EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY26, despite the larger-than-anticipated Q3 loss.

surprises.description: Revenue was about $67 million, below the preview’s $73.8–$75.3 million aggregator consensus by roughly 9–11%. It was nevertheless above the preview’s own $50–$60 million base estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Revenue grew approximately 8% to roughly $67 million from $62.1 million in Q1.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue: ~$73.8M–$75.3M from aggregators; Base: Revenue ~$50–60M (my estimate). The preview also cautioned that the ~$74M estimate looked stale.

surprises.description: ABTC mined 932 BTC, exceeding the preview’s bull-case threshold of 850 BTC by about 10% and setting a production record.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 Bitcoin production reached a record 932 BTC, up approximately 14% from 817 BTC in Q1, driven by production rather than price.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Bull: ≥850 BTC mined.

surprises.description: Revenue per Bitcoin was about $71,900, well above the preview’s expectation that realized price would fall toward the low-$60Ks. The actual figure was down only 5% from Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: Revenue per Bitcoin was about $71,900, down 5% from $76,000.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Realized price per BTC likely falls toward the low-$60Ks.

surprises.description: Quarter-end holdings reached 8,002 BTC, slightly above the preview’s 7,500–7,900 base range, while satoshis per share rose 11% and share count grew only 3%. This was better per-share accumulation than the preview’s concern about below-NAV ATM dilution suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: The strategic Bitcoin reserve grew nearly 1,000 BTC (about 14%) to 8,002 BTC at quarter end; satoshis per share rose about 11% quarter-over-quarter; share count grew only about 3% versus 14% Bitcoin growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base: holdings ~7,500–7,900. The preview also warned that issuing stock below NAV dilutes BTC per share and flagged ATM issuance or a pause as a key issue.

surprises.description: President and Interim CFO Matt Prusak is departing effective August 4, with Head of Derivatives Paul Sacks taking over as Interim CFO. The preview did not flag an imminent senior-management departure.
surprises.fact_evidence: President and Interim CFO Matt Prusak is departing effective August 4, with Head of Derivatives Paul Sacks stepping in as Interim CFO.

in_line: Gross margin compressed slightly to 49% from 52%, as the preview expected margin pressure; cost to mine remained nearly flat at about $36,500 per Bitcoin versus $36,200 in Q1.
The unrealized fair-value loss on digital assets was $71.2 million, within the preview’s estimated $60–90 million range for the non-cash mark-to-market loss.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $199 million versus the preview’s $184.72 million consensus, about 8% above expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total company revenue grew 19% year-over-year to $199 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 Revenue … Consensus $184.72M.”

surprises.description: The reported Q2 loss was much smaller than expected: the company reported a $0.02-per-share loss versus the preview’s expected $0.09 loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss narrowed to $1.4 million (-$0.02 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 EPS … Loss of $0.09.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $830–$860 million from $800–$850 million, above the preview’s baseline range. It also lifted net yield growth guidance to 4.5%–5.5%, for which the preview gave no prior range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $830-$860 million (from $800-$850 million) and lifted net yield growth guidance to 4.5%-5.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 tour revenue: $800–850M (reaffirmed 5/5/26).” The preview also identified a revenue-guidance raise as a key swing factor.

surprises.description: The newly launched 2028 deployment generated twice the revenue of the prior year’s launch period, a particularly strong forward-bookings result not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The newly launched 2028 deployment generated twice the revenue of the prior year's launch period.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA rose 31% and the margin expanded 150 basis points despite elevated fuel costs; the preview gave no quarterly EBITDA estimate or margin expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 31% to $32.5 million, with margins improving 150 basis points to 16.3% despite elevated fuel costs.”

surprises.description: Fuel costs were a substantial operating headwind: they rose 64% year over year even as fuel consumption fell, and management is modeling about $100-per-barrel oil for the rest of the year. The preview did not flag fuel costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fuel costs rose $2.7 million or 64% year-over-year to 5.3% of Lindblad revenue,” while “fuel consumption was cut more than 3%”; management is “modeling ~$100/barrel oil for the rest of the year.”

in_line: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed at $130–$140 million, matching the preview’s baseline range.

Occupancy and yield remained strong in the seasonally lighter quarter: occupancy was 91%, above the 90% target, and net yield reached a record, consistent with the preview’s focus on whether Q1’s strong trends would persist. Q2 occupancy was below Q1’s 93%, and yield growth was 4.3% versus Q1’s 7%.
2027 bookings continued to pace ahead of 2026 in both segments, in line with the preview’s focus on bookings into 2027 and its note that management had previously cited record advance bookings.

surprises.description: Marriott reported Q2 global RevPAR growth of 3.4%, above the preview’s 1.5%–2.5% guidance range. The beat was especially strong in U.S. and Canada, while international RevPAR declined slightly.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global RevPAR rose 3.4% in Q2, with U.S. and Canada up 5% (the highest quarterly increase in 13 quarters) and luxury RevPAR up over 9%, while international RevPAR declined slightly.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Worldwide RevPAR +1.5% to +2.5%.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted diluted EPS was $3.19, above both the $3.06 consensus and the top of Marriott’s $2.99–$3.06 guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted diluted EPS rose 20% year-over-year to $3.19.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS $2.99–$3.06” and “Consensus $3.06.”

surprises.description: Marriott raised its full-year RevPAR outlook to 3%–3.5% growth from 2%–3%, and forecast Q3 growth of 3.5%–4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marriott raised full-year 2026 global RevPAR guidance to 3%-3.5% growth and now expects Q3 RevPAR up 3.5%-4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 company guidance: RevPAR +2–3%.”

surprises.description: Marriott signed new co-branded card agreements with JPMorgan Chase and American Express, despite the preview noting that no agreement had been announced. The agreements are expected to add about $30 million in partial-year 2026 fees and $100–$125 million to annual co-brand card fees by 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New long-term co-branded credit card agreements with JPMorgan Chase and American Express are expected to add ~$30 million in incremental 2026 fees (partial year) and $100-$125 million to co-brand card fees by full-year 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The U.S. co-brand card renegotiation is excluded from guidance, and no new agreement had been announced as of the cutoff.”

surprises.description: The full-year EBITDA outlook moved above the prior range: the new $5.97–$6.03 billion guidance is higher than the previous $5.88–$5.97 billion range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA is guided to $5.97-$6.03 billion (up 11-12%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 company guidance … adj. EBITDA $5,880–5,970M.”

surprises.description: Middle East RevPAR fell sharply, but the reported decline and estimated full-year drag were less severe than the preview’s modeled or guided expectations: the quarterly fall was 43% versus a Zacks model assumption of about 50%, and the full-year global RevPAR drag is now about 100 basis points versus 100–125 basis points previously.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Middle East RevPAR fell 43% in Q2 due to regional conflict, and the full-year drag on global RevPAR is now estimated at ~100 basis points (improved from prior 100-125 bps).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The FY26 guide assumes the conflict shaves 100–125 bps off global RevPAR” and “Zacks models about a 50% Middle East RevPAR decline in Q2.”

surprises.description: Full-year net rooms growth is now trending toward the low end of the 4.5%–5% range, rather than tracking comfortably within the prior outlook; Marriott cited Middle East construction delays.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year net rooms growth is now trending toward the low end of the prior 4.5%-5% range, primarily due to Middle East construction delays.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net rooms growth +4.5–5.0%.”

surprises.description: Marriott disclosed a new guest-satisfaction incentive that can reimburse up to 50 basis points of gross room revenue and will be paid by Marriott and recorded in owned/leased/other expenses, creating a cost exposure not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marriott is launching a new ITR guest-satisfaction incentive of up to 50 basis points of gross room revenue fee reimbursement, paid by Marriott (not the system fund) and hitting the owned/leased/other expense line.”

surprises.description: Owned/leased net revenue was cut to $175–$185 million, with Marriott citing a $27 million litigation accrual—an unanticipated one-off expense in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Owned/leased net revenue was cut to $175-$185 million partly due to a $27 million litigation accrual.”

surprises.description: Marriott’s Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $1.59 billion exceeded the preview’s $1.525–$1.550 billion guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 13% to $1.59 billion.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross fee revenue was $1.58 billion, above the preview’s $1.538–$1.553 billion guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total gross fee revenues up 13% to $1.58 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross fee revenues $1,538M–$1,553M (+10–11%).”

surprises.description: Marriott said Q4 would face midterm-election headwinds and receive no World Cup benefit, tempering the preview’s framing of the World Cup as a potential demand wave.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 facing headwinds from midterm elections and no World Cup benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance was set May 6, before the World Cup demand wave.”

surprises.description: The global pipeline reached a record of about 629,000 rooms, up nearly 7% year over year, with record first-half signings—an expansion the preview did not forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The global pipeline grew nearly 7% year-over-year to a record ~629,000 rooms, with over 279,000 rooms under construction and record first-half signings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a prior-quarter pipeline of “about 590,000 rooms” but gave no expectation for Q2 pipeline growth or signings.

surprises.description: The planned shareholder return for 2026 is now over $4.5 billion, above the preview’s already-stated target of more than $4.4 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects to return over $4.5 billion to shareholders this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capital return above $4.4B.”

surprises.description: Tyson cut full-year adjusted operating income guidance from the previously expected $2.2–$2.4 billion to $2.1–$2.3 billion. The main driver was a much worse expected full-year Beef loss: $500–$650 million versus the prior $350–$500 million outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tyson cut its full-year adjusted operating income guidance to $2.1-$2.3 billion,” driven primarily by “a worse full-year beef loss now expected between $500 million and $650 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted operating income: raised to $2.2–$2.4B at the Q2 report”; “Beef segment adjusted operating loss: $350–500M for the full year.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.99, below the preview’s $1.00–$1.03 range of consensus estimates, although it was just one cent below the low end of the alternate estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $0.99.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $1.03 (Zacks consensus)” and “Adjusted EPS (alt.) $1.00–$1.01.”

surprises.description: Sales were $13.9 billion and essentially flat, below the preview’s $14.1 billion estimate and its expected 1.8% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total company sales were essentially flat at $13.9 billion.”

surprises.description: Management raised the Prepared Foods full-year operating income midpoint to $1.325 billion, an unanticipated positive outlook update; the preview had identified Prepared Foods as an expected earnings support but gave no segment guidance estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised the Prepared Foods full-year operating income guidance midpoint to a range of $1.3-$1.35 billion.”

surprises.description: Management described a new competitive big-bird genetics line and its rollout across the harvest, with an expected boost to both genetics and domestic Chicken results—an initiative and benefit not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new competitive big-bird genetics line will represent about 75% of big-bird harvest by year-end 2025 with the remainder in fiscal 2027, expected to boost both the genetics and domestic chicken P&Ls.”

surprises.description: Management said about three-quarters of Chicken operating income now comes from a demand-committed model rather than commodity spot markets, an unflagged indication of reduced exposure to spot-market volatility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “About three-quarters of chicken operating income now runs on a demand-committed model rather than commodity spot markets.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s concern about elevated debt and dividend sustainability, Tyson reported substantial liquidity, debt reduction, free cash flow, and shareholder returns, including additional buybacks after quarter-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $4 billion in liquidity, net leverage of 2.1x, reduced gross debt by about $800 million, generated $913 million free cash flow year-to-date, and returned $652 million to shareholders plus another $49 million in buybacks since quarter-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “elevated debt and dividend sustainability as valuation risks.”

in_line: Beef remained a drag amid tight cattle supply, consistent with the preview’s expectation that Beef would remain under pressure.

Chicken remained an earnings support, consistent with the preview’s expectation that Chicken would be a main earnings support; the call reported $488 million of operating income, up $40 million year over year.
Prepared Foods remained a substantial earnings contributor, consistent with the preview’s expectation that it would be a main support, even though quarterly operating income was down slightly.
The qualitative fiscal 2027 outlook for growth in volume and profitability was consistent with the preview’s expectation of higher FY27 adjusted EPS than FY26.

surprises.description: COHN reported diluted EPS of $0.94, well above the preview’s weak $0.42 estimate—more than twice as high. The preview cautioned that $0.42 was low-confidence and that there was no meaningful published consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income attributable to shareholders was $3.6 million or $0.94 per fully diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “MarketBeat ‘current estimate’ Q2 2026 EPS | $0.42, low confidence”; the preview adds, “there is no meaningful published consensus to beat or miss.”

surprises.description: Investment banking and new issue revenue reached $54 million, materially above the $45.7 million Q1 level the preview used as the advisory run-rate benchmark. The preview anticipated a strong SPAC market but said Cohen’s share of that activity was unknown.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Investment banking and new issue revenue reached $54 million, up from $45.7 million in the prior quarter,” driven primarily by “SPAC M&A and SPAC IPO transactions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The upside scenario expected “near or above $45.7M advisory run-rate”; the preview also said, “Cohen's share of that activity is not known.”

surprises.description: Adjusted pretax income rose to $10.1 million from $4 million in Q1, stronger than the preview’s base-case description of “modest net income.” This reinforces the stronger-than-expected profitability, though the preview gave no specific adjusted pretax forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted pretax income surged to $10.1 million, more than doubling from $4 million in the prior quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario described “modest net income.”

surprises.description: Equity-method affiliates generated a $3 million loss, larger than the $527,000 loss in Q1 that the preview cited as the recent comparison. A $2.1 million credit reduced the net loss to $900,000, so the final impact was partly offset.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Loss from equity method affiliates widened to $3 million, largely from the Columbus Circle Capital II SPAC,” while “a $2.1 million offsetting credit reduced the net loss to $900,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Q1 loss of $(527)K” and flagged “the size of ... equity-method affiliate losses.”

surprises.description: COHN reported that Columbus Circle Capital Corp. III completed a $230 million IPO after quarter-end, with 2.28 million founder shares allocated to the company. The preview discussed the strong SPAC market but did not identify this completed IPO or the resulting allocation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Columbus Circle Capital Corp. III completed a $230 million IPO on July 9-10, with 2.28 million SPAC founder shares currently allocated to the company.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Cohen's share of that activity is not known.”

in_line: The $0.25 quarterly dividend was maintained, as the preview expected.
The Columbus Circle Capital Corp. II–Elroy Air business combination remained on the previewed timeline: the agreement had been signed, and closing was anticipated in Q4 2026.

surprises.description: PLOW raised full-year guidance above the ranges investors had going into the quarter: sales to $765M–$805M from $750M–$795M, adjusted EBITDA to $120M–$135M from $110M–$125M, and adjusted EPS to $2.90–$3.40 from $2.55–$3.05.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to net sales of $765M-$805M, adjusted EBITDA of $120M-$135M, and adjusted EPS of $2.90-$3.40.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Current FY2026 guidance as of May 4: net sales $750–795M, adjusted EBITDA $110–125M, and adjusted diluted EPS $2.55–3.05.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $1.22, well above the preview’s $0.93 consensus estimate, rather than the expected year-over-year decline. The result was about 31% above consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EPS increased 7% to a record $1.22.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 FY2026 consensus: Adj. diluted EPS $0.93, implied change −18.4%.

surprises.description: Work Truck Attachments sales were $129.3M, roughly 10% below the preview’s approximately $143M estimate, despite rising 20% year over year. The expected shift in preseason shipments to Q3 may explain some of the gap, but the segment still came in below its estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Work Truck Attachments net sales jumped 20% to $129.3 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Work Truck Attachments sales: ~$143M.

surprises.description: Work Truck Solutions sales were $85.3M, about 8% below the preview’s ~$93M estimate; strong municipal demand only offset, rather than eliminated, softness in commercial operations.
surprises.fact_evidence: Work Truck Solutions net sales were roughly flat at $85.3 million, as strong municipal demand offset softness in commercial operations.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Work Truck Solutions sales: ~$93M.

surprises.description: Consolidated sales narrowly missed the preview’s $216.8M consensus, coming in at $214.6M, or about 1% below estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Consolidated Q2 2026 net sales increased 10% to a record $214.6 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Net sales consensus: $216.8M.

surprises.description: Management disclosed a substantial municipal demand and capacity opportunity not raised in the preview: the new Missouri facility added about 10% municipal capacity, production dates are booked well into 2027, and backlog is near its 2022 record.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company added roughly 10% more municipal capacity with its new Missouri facility now operational, and is booking municipal production dates well into 2027 with backlog near its 2022 record.

surprises.description: Management said plow and hopper dealer inventories are lower than in recent years, creating an additional inventory-rebuilding demand boost on top of strong retail sales; the preview did not identify this as a demand driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: Dealer field inventories for plows and hoppers are lower than in recent years, providing an additional demand boost from inventory rebuilding on top of strong retail sales.

surprises.description: Year-to-date free cash flow was negative $32.5M and had fallen $14.6M, with higher inventory and receivables cited as the cause. The preview did not discuss or flag this cash-flow pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: Year-to-date free cash flow fell $14.6 million to negative $32.5 million on higher inventory and receivables.

in_line: Management reiterated the expected preseason attachment shipment split of roughly 50-50 between Q2 and Q3, versus 60-40 last year; the preview had flagged that timing shift and its effect on quarterly results.

surprises.description: Diluted EPS of $4.27 exceeded the preview’s $3.69–$3.79 consensus estimates by roughly 13%–16%. It was nevertheless within Matson’s already-public preliminary range of $4.12–$4.30.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS increased 46.2% year-over-year to $4.27.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus EPS sits below management's own preliminary range of $4.12–$4.30”; estimates listed were $3.69, $3.79, and $3.74.

surprises.description: Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to expect consolidated operating income above 2025’s $499.8 million. The preview identified updated guidance as a key issue but did not give an expected level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, now expecting consolidated operating income to exceed the $499.8 million achieved in 2025.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed that Q3 Ocean Transportation operating income is expected to be about 45% above Q3 2025, driven by higher rates and volume. The preview pointed to China service running near capacity through peak season, but did not quantify this earnings outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 Ocean Transportation operating income is guided to be approximately 45% higher than the $147.4 million posted in Q3 2025, driven by both higher rates and volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management said China service was expected to run “at or near capacity through peak season.”

surprises.description: Matson expects Q4 Ocean Transportation operating income to be modestly below Q4 2025, tempering the strong Q3 outlook. The preview did not flag the prior year’s elevated post-trade-agreement demand or forecast a Q4 decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 2026 Ocean Transportation operating income is expected to be modestly lower than the $136 million in Q4 2025, reflecting a normalization versus last year's elevated post-trade-agreement demand.”

surprises.description: SSAT’s contribution was down year over year, and management expects its full-year contribution to fall below 2025’s $32.5 million. The preview did not identify SSAT as a concern or give an expectation for its contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The SSAT joint venture contributed $4.8 million in Q2, down $2.5 million year-over-year, with full-year 2026 contribution expected below the $32.5 million achieved in 2025.”

surprises.description: Matson reported a low-teens-million-dollar fuel-cost undercollection across all trade lanes because of the Iran conflict, although it expects to recover the amount by year-end. The preview did not anticipate this temporary cost and recovery issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company had undercollected fuel costs across all trade lanes by a low-teens millions of dollars amount at quarter-end due to the Iran conflict, but expects full recovery by year-end.”

surprises.description: Southeast Asia cargo had grown to 20%–25% of weekly China-service volume, but at slightly lower all-in rates and higher operating costs than China-direct cargo. The preview discussed China volume and peak-season capacity but did not describe this change in cargo mix or its cost trade-off.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Southeast Asia cargo now represents 20% to 25% of weekly China service volume, up significantly from early 2025, though at slightly lower all-in rates and higher operating costs than China-direct cargo.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted China service volume and management’s expectation that it would run “at or near capacity through peak season.”

in_line: Q2 consolidated operating income of $158.9 million and net income of $129.4 million were within the preliminary ranges of $153.0–$160.0 million and $124.8–$130.3 million, respectively.
China service container volume rose 15.2% year over year, as already reported in the preview.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was slightly below the lower preview estimate and further below the higher one: $96.1 million versus cited estimates of $96.65 million and $105.83 million. The call said it was in line with company expectations, so the miss is relative to the preview’s external estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $96.1 million” and was “in line with company expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Benzinga ... Revenue est. $96.65M”; “ChartMill ... Revenue est. $105.83M.”

surprises.description: Adeia raised its long-term annual revenue target to $600 million from $500 million, a 20% increase not anticipated in the preview. Management attributed the increase primarily to doubling the annual semiconductor opportunity to $200 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its long-term annual revenue target to $600 million from $500 million,” driven primarily by “doubling the semiconductor opportunity from $100 million to $200 million annually.”

surprises.description: Non-Pay-TV recurring revenue grew sharply and is now nearly twice the size of Pay-TV recurring revenue, indicating more progress in diversification than the preview discussed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-Pay-TV recurring revenue grew 54% year-over-year in Q2 and is now nearly double the size of Pay-TV recurring revenue.”

surprises.description: The quarter produced a record 12 new customers, alongside six license agreements, including a multiyear Google media portfolio renewal and a new RPX e-commerce deal. The preview flagged license activity as important but did not anticipate this customer count or these specific developments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company closed 6 license agreements and added a record 12 new customers in Q2, including a multiyear Google media portfolio renewal and a new RPX e-commerce deal.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “License deals signed in Q2. Count, new versus renewal, and any large OTT or semiconductor names.”

surprises.description: Semiconductor revenue reached $14.8 million in Q2 and about $48 million year-to-date, already exceeding the roughly $26 million generated in all of last year. The preview watched for semiconductor deal names but gave no expectation for this revenue acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Semiconductor revenue was $14.8 million in Q2 and about $48 million year-to-date ... up sharply from roughly $26 million for all of last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “License deals signed in Q2. Count, new versus renewal, and any large OTT or semiconductor names.”

surprises.description: Management said the new RPX e-commerce business could grow to roughly 10% of total revenue, a sizeable opportunity not raised in the preview. The RPX agreement licenses 10 member companies at once.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The RPX agreement licenses 10 member companies at once, and management believes the e-commerce business can grow to roughly 10% of total revenue.”

surprises.description: Management warned that unpredictable Fubo litigation timing could pressure near-term Pay-TV results. The preview flagged the lawsuit as an issue to watch, but did not report this specific near-term business risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company noted that “litigation timing is unpredictable and could pressure near-term Pay-TV results,” while saying the case is separate from the Disney agreement.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Fubo litigation. Suit filed July 1, 2026, after quarter-end...”

in_line: Adeia reiterated FY2026 revenue guidance of $395 million to $435 million and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of approximately 55%, as the preview identified reaffirmation or a change as the main guidance issue.
Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin was 58.7%, which the call said was in line with company expectations.
The company continued the capital-return and debt-paydown actions the preview was watching: it repurchased about $10 million of shares, paid the $0.05 dividend, and made debt payments.

surprises.description: Hess Midstream reported Q2 net income of $174 million, above its guided range of $150–160 million. The result exceeded the top of the expected range by $14 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income was $174 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net income | $150–160M”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $314 million, above the expected $295–305 million range, exceeding its top by $9 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $314 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA | $295–305M”

surprises.description: The gross adjusted EBITDA margin reached approximately 85%, well above the company’s 75% target. The company attributed part of the difference to OpEx timing and minor one-time credits, so the margin level may not be fully representative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross adjusted EBITDA margin reached approximately 85% in Q2 2026, well above its 75% target, aided partly by OpEx phasing shifts into the second half and minor one-time credits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “75% target”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted buyback pace as an open question after Q1 repurchases. Hess Midstream made no Q2 buyback and instead paid down $87 million on its revolver; this favors debt reduction over immediate shareholder returns.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company did not execute a share buyback in Q2 2026, instead paying down $87 million on its revolving credit facility.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that adjusted free cash flow was about 2% lower than Q1 and expects a further decline in Q3 as capital spending rises. The preview gave annual FCF guidance but did not flag this near-term cash-flow decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow was approximately $232 million in Q2 2026, a roughly 2% decrease from Q1, with Q3 free cash flow expected to decline further due to higher capital spending.”

in_line: The company reiterated full-year 2026 adjusted free cash flow guidance of $910–960 million, as the preview expected.

Full-year net income guidance of $650–700 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $1.225–1.275 billion remained unchanged and approximately flat at the midpoint versus 2025, consistent with the preview.
Management’s expectation of a second-half volume recovery is consistent with the preview’s view that 2H26 was the catch-up period; management now specifies at least 5% volume growth.

The approximately $280 million of excess adjusted free cash flow after targeted distribution growth, and the plan to allocate it between debt repayment and shareholder returns, match the preview’s expectations.
The leverage outlook of about 3.0x declining toward approximately 2.5x by 2028 was already identified in the preview.

surprises.description: AEIS reported Q2 revenue of $574 million, above the $544.33 million consensus and the $560 million high end of company guidance. The result was a stronger beat than the preview’s base case of about $545 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $574 million,” exceeding “the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was “$544.33M”; company guidance was “$540M ± $20M”; the base scenario was “~$545M.”

surprises.description: Q2 EPS of $2.74 substantially exceeded the $2.20 consensus and the $2.18 midpoint of company guidance. The gap was much larger than the preview’s base-case EPS range of $2.20–$2.35.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EPS of $2.74 rose 83% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus non-GAAP EPS was “$2.20”; company guidance was “$2.18 ± $0.25”; the base scenario was “$2.20–2.35.”

surprises.description: AEIS raised its full-year 2026 revenue-growth target to the low-to-mid-30% range, well above the prior low-to-mid-20% range. The preview’s base case anticipated reaffirmation of the existing full-year outlook, not this sizable increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth target to the low-to-mid-30% range, up from the prior low-to-mid-20% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario said “FY growth reaffirmed”; the preview also described the prior outlook as “FY2026 data center growth in the mid-30% range.”

surprises.description: Semiconductor revenue reached a record $278 million, up 27% sequentially and 33% year-over-year. The preview highlighted the second-half outlook but gave no expectation for a record Q2 or such a sharp sequential increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Semiconductor revenue hit a record $278 million, up 27% sequentially and 33% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided “2H semiconductor revenue up more than 30% Y/Y” and noted that “a weak AEIS semi number would stand out”; it provided no Q2 segment estimate.

surprises.description: Management said second-half semiconductor revenue should grow nearly 50% year-over-year, considerably faster than the preview’s expectation of growth above 30%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Second-half revenue [is] expected to grow nearly 50% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had guided “2H semiconductor revenue up more than 30% Y/Y.”

surprises.description: Data Center Computing full-year growth guidance rose to at least 50%, versus the preview’s expectation that management would reaffirm growth in the mid-30% range. The Q2 revenue itself was slightly below Q1, consistent with the preview’s expected sequential moderation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data Center Computing revenue of $192 million grew 35% year-over-year, and full-year data center growth guidance was raised to at least 50%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the question was whether management would “reaffirm mid-30% FY2026 data center growth”; it also said the Q2 decline was guided.

surprises.description: Gross margin was 41.9%, or 40.7% excluding IEEPA tariff refunds. Even excluding the refunds, that was above the preview’s expected 40.3–40.6% range; operating margin also expanded to 21.9%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved 380 basis points year-over-year to 41.9% (40.7% excluding IEEPA tariff refunds), and operating margin expanded 730 basis points to 21.9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected non-GAAP gross margin “against the 40.3–40.6% guided band” and described the bull case as “gross margin ≥40.5%.”

surprises.description: IEEPA tariff refunds added 120 basis points to reported gross margin, a favorable one-off contribution not anticipated in the preview. The preview had instead flagged tariffs and input costs as potential offsets.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin was “41.9% (40.7% excluding IEEPA tariff refunds).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Tariffs and input costs were flagged as offsets” and included “Tariff and input-cost quantification” among the items to watch.

surprises.description: Q3 guidance calls for about $640 million in revenue and $3.00 EPS, with record results expected. The preview flagged Q3 guidance as a catalyst but supplied no numerical Q3 estimate; the revenue outlook implies a strong sequential increase from Q2’s $574 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of ~$640 million (±$20 million) and EPS of $3.00 (±$0.25), implying continued record results.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Q3 FY2026 revenue and EPS guidance against the ~$545M Q2 base” as a catalyst but gave no Q3 revenue or EPS forecast.

surprises.description: AEIS now sees line of sight to gross margin above 43%, with new-product mix—not just volume leverage—identified as the primary driver. The preview mentioned above 43% as a long-term goal, but did not indicate this degree of visibility or the stated driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management sees line of sight to gross margin above 43%, with product mix from new products cited as the primary driver beyond volume leverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “a long-term goal above 43%.”

surprises.description: Management projected more than 20% revenue growth in 2027 across all markets. The preview said capacity investments underpin the FY2027 growth case but did not provide an expectation for growth above 20% or across every market.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company projects over 20% revenue growth in 2027 across all markets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the capacity updates “underpin the FY2027 growth case,” without specifying a growth rate or market breadth.

surprises.description: The Thailand factory is expected to begin generating production revenue in Q4 2026, and full build-out is expected to support roughly $5 billion of revenue-generating capacity. The preview anticipated a facility update but gave no such scale or production timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly $5 billion of revenue-generating capacity once its new Thailand factory is fully built out, with Thailand's first production revenue expected in Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “expect an update on Malaysia, Philippines, and Mexico capacity and the Thailand facility,” which “underpin the FY2027 growth case.”

surprises.description: The company raised 2026 CapEx guidance to $180–195 million to support customer ramps and capture upside; the preview discussed capacity needs but did not anticipate a CapEx increase or give a spending outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised 2026 CapEx guidance to $180-195 million” to support customer ramps and capture upside.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview anticipated capacity updates but provided no CapEx expectation.

surprises.description: Inventory increased by 10 days to 145 days as the company prepared for customer ramps and potential upside. The preview flagged inventory change and cash flow as watch items but did not indicate that inventory would rise further.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management … increased inventory by 10 days to 145 days (turns at 2.5x) to support customer ramps and capture upside.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Operating cash flow and inventory change” as a catalyst and noted a prior-quarter inventory build, but did not state an expected Q2 inventory level or direction.

surprises.description: AEIS provided a product-roadmap timeline that was not covered in the preview: initial revenue from 800-volt data center products is expected in late 2027, with high-volume production in 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “800-volt data center products [are] expected to reach high-volume production in 2028 with initial revenue in late 2027.”

in_line: Data Center Computing revenue was $192 million, slightly below Q1’s $194.2 million, consistent with the preview’s warning that Q2 data center revenue would moderate sequentially on customer delivery timing.

surprises.description: TG raised 2026 U.S. BRIUMVI guidance to $890–$905 million from $885–$900 million and global revenue guidance to about $950 million from about $925 million. The global outlook is $25 million above the prior company outlook and also above the preview’s $942.5 million consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 U.S. BRIUMVI net revenue guidance to $890 million-$905 million and total global revenue to approximately $950 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue | Total global ≈ $925M”; “FY26 U.S. BRIUMVI | $885–900M”; consensus total revenue “$942.5M.”

surprises.description: Q2 U.S. BRIUMVI revenue exceeded the company’s $220 million outlook but came in slightly below the preview’s roughly $230 million consensus estimates. The result is a modest beat against company guidance, but not against consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 U.S. BRIUMVI net product revenue was approximately $228 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 revenue | U.S. BRIUMVI net product revenue ≈ $220M”; consensus was “$230.77M” and “$229.77M.”

surprises.description: Reported diluted EPS was $0.05, far below the preview’s $0.31–$0.43 consensus range. The preview warned that consensus might not capture the manufacturing ramp and that a headline EPS miss would be low signal; the call attributed the low result to about $55 million of subcutaneous and secondary-source manufacturing charges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net income was $7.8 million ($0.05 per diluted share), but excluding ~$55 million of subcutaneous and secondary-source manufacturing charges, net income would have been approximately $62 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 EPS … $0.41”; other estimates were “$0.31” and “$0.43.” The preview also said headline EPS misses “should be treated as low signal” because models might not fully reflect the “~$100M subcutaneous manufacturing ramp.”

surprises.description: TG gave a stronger exit trajectory than the preview specified: it expects quarterly U.S. BRIUMVI revenue above $250 million exiting 2026, equivalent to a $1 billion annualized run rate, and expects its first $1 billion-plus U.S. BRIUMVI revenue year in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TG expects to exit 2026 with quarterly U.S. net revenue exceeding $250 million, hitting a $1 billion annualized run rate and setting up its first $1 billion-plus U.S. BRIUMVI revenue year in 2027.”

surprises.description: The call put a potential timeline and substantial market opportunity around subcutaneous BRIUMVI that the preview did not discuss: Phase III top-line results are expected around year-end 2026 or early 2027, targeting a self-administered anti-CD20 segment where TG does not currently compete and potentially more than doubling the addressable market.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subcutaneous BRIUMVI Phase III top-line results are expected around year-end 2026 or early 2027,” targeting the “35%-40% self-administered anti-CD20 segment where TG currently does not compete, potentially more than doubling the addressable market.”

surprises.description: The call described pipeline activity beyond the BRIUMVI topics covered in the preview: a registration-directed Phase II study in myasthenia gravis, a Phase II study in treatment-resistant schizophrenia, and expansion of azer-cel into several neuroimmune diseases, with more than 20 patients enrolled.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pipeline expansion includes a registration-directed Phase II study in myasthenia gravis, a Phase II study in treatment-resistant schizophrenia, and the azer-cel CD19 CAR-T program (over 20 patients enrolled, expanded to MS, MG, CIDP and NMO) with a clinical update expected in the second half of the year.”

surprises.description: The stated full-year operating-expense range extends to $400 million, whereas the preview cited about $350 million of R&D and SG&A excluding stock-based compensation, in addition to manufacturing costs. The lower end matches that figure, but the upper end allows for as much as $50 million more in core operating expense.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year OpEx guidance of $350 million-$400 million plus ~$100 million in manufacturing-related expenses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “R&D+SG&A ex-SBC ≈ $350M, plus ≈ $100M subcutaneous manufacturing/start-up costs.”

in_line: The ENHANCE single 600-mg initiation-infusion approach was already anticipated: the preview said the Phase III topline supported single Day-1 dosing and that submission was targeted for 2H 2026. The call’s confirmation and potential availability as early as mid-2027 are consistent with that expected convenience upgrade and development path.

surprises.description: Ameresco reported $515 million of Q2 revenue, well above the preview’s $460–$465 million estimates. That is roughly 11% above the higher estimate, rather than the near-consensus result the preview described as the base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue grew 9% to $515 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $465.18M” and “~2.5% YoY decline (implies ~$460M)”; the base scenario was “Near consensus.”

surprises.description: The preview identified the EPS outlook as a key risk, but Ameresco raised its full-year non-GAAP EPS range from $1.06–$1.28 to $1.15–$1.35. The increase is supported by a newly expected tax benefit tied to a planned accounting-policy change, so the raised range is not solely an indication of stronger underlying operations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance to $1.15–$1.35, supported by a new expected tax benefit rate of 25%–40% tied to a planned accounting policy change for transferable tax credits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS: $1.06–$1.28”; the preview said to watch whether the range was “narrowed, reaffirmed, or cut.”

surprises.description: Ameresco’s Q2 awards were far beyond the backlog trends discussed in the preview: the company booked a record $1.8 billion, roughly double any prior quarter, including $1.2 billion in data-center awards. It also said the current data-center awards could grow to $2 billion and that at least five more opportunities were in the pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record new awards of $1.8 billion in Q2 2026, roughly double any prior quarter,” including “$1.2 billion for data centers”; management said the awards “could grow to as much as $2 billion” and there were “at least five additional data center opportunities in the pipeline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Backlog and contracted-project trends. Q3 FY2025 backlog rose 33% to $2.5B. Current backlog is the forward indicator to check.”

surprises.description: Management said the data-center awards are not an immediate revenue step-up: projects will convert to contracts over 6–24 months, with the major revenue impact expected in 2028–2030. It also described them as ordinary EPC work recognized over time, with high-teens margins, rather than asset sales or capitalized balance-sheet items—timing and accounting details the preview did not address.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data center projects are expected to be recognized as normal EPC percent-complete revenue with margins in the high teens”; they will have “minimal near-term financial impact,” with awards converting “over 6–24 months” and major revenue impact “between 2028 and 2030.”

surprises.description: Ameresco disclosed closing the Neogenix JV with HACI while retaining 70% ownership, alongside $471 million of new financing commitments, including $400 million related to Neogenix. The preview did not flag this transaction or financing activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company closed its Neogenix JV with HACI (retaining 70% ownership) and secured $471 million in new financing commitments in Q2, including $400 million related to the Neogenix transaction.”

surprises.description: Profitability improved despite the preview’s concern about margin disappointment after the prior-quarter EPS miss: gross margin reached 17.7%, improving both year over year and sequentially, while adjusted EBITDA rose 12%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improving to 17.7% year-over-year and sequentially”; “Adjusted EBITDA rose 12% to $62.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “Margin trajectory” after the Q1 EPS miss and noted that “the market has punished revenue beats that came with margin or guidance disappointment.”

in_line: Non-GAAP EPS was $0.20, matching the preview’s $0.20 EPS consensus estimate.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $360.7 million, above both the $345.4 million consensus and the top of the $340–350 million company guidance range. The beat was about 4% versus consensus and exceeded the guidance ceiling by $10.7 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $360.7 million, up 28.8% year-over-year, exceeding the top end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Company guidance (Q2) $340M – $350M (midpoint $345M) | Consensus $345.4M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $48.8 million, substantially above the previewed $38–40 million guidance range, despite the preview’s warning that larger, higher-volume enterprise billers were pressuring profitability. The reported record margin and 740-basis-point year-over-year improvement also indicate stronger profitability than that concern suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 54% year-over-year to $48.8 million, achieving a record margin of 41.3% and a 740 basis point improvement over the prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | $38M – $40M”; the preview also said “Shifts toward high-volume enterprise billers have pressured profitability even as revenue accelerates.”

surprises.description: Paymentus raised its FY26 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance rather than reaffirming the prior ranges. Revenue guidance moved from $1.425–1.440 billion to $1.443–1.458 billion, while adjusted EBITDA moved from $165–172 million to $175–185 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $1.443-1.458 billion … and adjusted EBITDA of $175-185 million (raised ~6.8% at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue $1.425B – $1.440B”; “FY26 adj. EBITDA $165M – $172M.” The preview asked “Whether revenue … and EBITDA … are raised again” and called a raise “the likely swing factor.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS of $0.25 exceeded even the high end of the preview’s cited consensus range of $0.16–$0.20. The gap was 25% versus the highest cited estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income rose 66.7% to $32.4 million, or $0.25 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS … $0.20 (MarketBeat, Jul 27); $0.18 (Investing.com, retrieved Aug 1); $0.16 (Wolfe Research via Defense World, Jul 22).”

in_line: The preview flagged pressure on profitability from larger, higher-volume enterprise billers; contribution margin declined slightly to 32.7% from 33.4%, which is consistent with that anticipated pressure, even as contribution profit per transaction improved.

surprises.description: Revenue was expected around $3.21–$3.23 billion, but Vertex reported $3.3 billion, roughly 2–3% above that range. The reported 12% year-over-year growth included an approximately 170-basis-point benefit from foreign exchange.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached $3.3 billion, up 12% year-over-year, with an approximate 170 basis point benefit from foreign exchange rates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue ~$3.21–3.23B consensus.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $4.73 versus the preview’s $4.85 estimate, a shortfall of about 2.5%. EPS grew only 5% year over year, below the expected 7.3% growth; SG&A rose 45% while R&D grew just 1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was $4.73, representing only 5% growth versus prior year, as SG&A rose 45% year-over-year to $520 million while R&D grew just 1% to $889 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (non-GAAP) $4.85 (+7.3% YoY).”

surprises.description: Vertex raised full-year revenue guidance instead of merely reaffirming the prior range: the new $13.1–$13.2 billion outlook lifts the previous $12.95–$13.1 billion range. The preview had identified reaffirmation as the base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Vertex raised full-year 2026 total revenue guidance to $13.1-13.2 billion, while maintaining expectations of $500 million or greater from non-CF products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Whether the company reaffirms the $12.95B–$13.1B range”; the base scenario was “Guidance reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: JOURNAVX’s gross-to-net normalization is now expected in the first half of 2027, later than prior expectations. Vertex attributed the delay to heavier-than-forecast patient-support-program use amid restricted coverage: only 180 million of roughly 260 million covered lives have unrestricted access, while about 80 million face restrictions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Vertex now expects JOURNAVX gross-to-net to normalize in the first half of 2027 (later than prior expectations) due to heavier-than-forecast use of the patient support program amid restricted coverage”; “only 180 million have unrestricted access, with ~80 million subject to restrictions like quantity limits or prior authorizations.”

surprises.description: CASGEVY had declined after the prior quarter, but instead delivered a sharp sequential rebound: revenue rose about 75% to $76 million, and first-half infusions exceeded all of 2025.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CASGEVY delivered $76 million in Q2 revenue, up roughly 75% sequentially and over 150% year-over-year, with more infusions in H1 2026 than in all of 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CASGEVY declined after the prior quarter,” with sequential trends listed as a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: The preview noted the expected November 30 FDA decision for povetacicept, but did not anticipate the BLA acceptance reported on the call or the accompanying Phase III efficacy results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FDA accepted the BLA for povetacicept in IgAN with a November 30, 2026 PDUFA date, backed by RAINIER Phase III data showing 52% proteinuria reduction and 70%+ reductions in hematuria and Gd-IgA1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FDA decision expected November 30, 2026. Pre-decision commentary will be watched.”

surprises.description: Vertex reported FDA clearance of the VX-017 IND, a universal-donor islet-cell therapy for type 1 diabetes, and said the approach could double its addressable market from about 60,000 to about 120,000 patients. The preview did not flag this development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FDA cleared the IND for VX-017, a universal-donor (blood type O) islet cell therapy for type 1 diabetes, which Vertex expects to double its addressable market from about 60,000 to about 120,000 patients.”

in_line: JOURNAVX prescription volume was rising as the preview anticipated: the call reported approximately 535,000 prescriptions and monthly scripts doubling from about 50,000 in January to about 100,000 in June.

The ALYFTREK ramp was described as progressing well in the preview; the call reported more than $1 billion of first-half revenue and more than one in three eligible patients in Germany and the UK on the drug.
The preview cited November 30, 2026 as the expected povetacicept FDA decision date, and the call reported that same date as the PDUFA date.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $200.6 million, above the preview’s $194.72 million consensus and above the $193 million–$198 million implied by the company’s 9%–11% decline guidance. The 7.6% year-over-year decline was therefore less severe than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 7.6% year-over-year to $200.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $194.72M”; Q2 guidance was “down 9%–11% YoY,” implying roughly “$193.2M–$197.6M.”

surprises.description: The company raised the low end of its FY2026 revenue outlook by $10 million, from $825 million–$875 million to $835 million–$875 million. The midpoint rose by only $5 million, so the improvement was modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was revised to $835 million-$875 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY2026 revenue guidance was “$825M–$875M.”

surprises.description: Profitability guidance improved on adjusted operating margin and adjusted EPS, but worsened on GAAP EPS: adjusted margin is now 4%–6% versus 2%–4%, and adjusted EPS is $1.05–$1.45 versus $0.75–$1.25, while diluted EPS is -$0.42 to $0.17 versus $0.07–$0.62. The revisions are mixed rather than uniformly better.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company narrowed profitability guidance to adjusted operating margin of 4-6%, diluted EPS of -$0.42 to $0.17, and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.05-$1.45.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY2026 guidance: “Adjusted operating margin: 2%–4%”; “GAAP diluted EPS: $0.07–$0.62”; “Adjusted diluted EPS: $0.75–$1.25.”

surprises.description: The outlook indicates that revenue pressure continues into Q3: management expects an 8%–10% year-over-year decline, even though revenue should be higher sequentially than Q2. The preview flagged whether coding and WISeR headwinds would stabilize or keep affecting H2, but did not provide a Q3 forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for an 8-10% year-over-year revenue decline (though sequentially higher than Q2) and approximately break-even adjusted operating income as marketing spend steps up.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Whether it is stabilizing or still growing into H2 will likely matter more than the headline beat or miss.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a larger full-year cumulative coding and reimbursement impact than the preview quantified: $120 million–$130 million, alongside a Q2 impact of about $40 million. The Q2 impact itself was within the preview’s $40 million–$50 million expectation, but the full-year figure makes the continuing burden explicit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was revised to $835 million-$875 million, reflecting an estimated $120 million-$130 million total impact from coding and reimbursement disruption”; Q2 was impacted by “approximately $40 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had expected the “WISeR/coding revenue headwind” to be “$40M–$50M in Q2”; the preview also asked whether it was “stabilizing or still growing into H2.”

surprises.description: The company introduced Project Horizon, which is expected to free up $30 million of annualized growth-investment capacity but will bring $20 million–$25 million of pre-tax restructuring charges, most of them in Q3. The restructuring costs and supply-chain impairments were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inspire launched Project Horizon, expected to create $30 million of annualized growth investment capacity while incurring $20 million-$25 million of pre-tax restructuring charges (90% in Q3), including $16 million-$20 million of non-cash impairments from supply chain consolidation.”

surprises.description: New proposed 2027 reimbursement rates are favorable for hospital outpatient and ASC settings but unfavorable for physician billing: the proposed hospital and ASC rates rise 12% and 15%, respectively, while the physician rate for CPT 64582 falls about 4%. The preview did not flag these proposed rates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CMS's proposed 2027 rates would increase hospital outpatient reimbursement 12% to $35,414 and ASC reimbursement 15% to $31,722, but cut physician reimbursement for CPT 64582 by about 4% to roughly $699, with final rates due in November.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that two Medicare Administrative Contractors require a -52 modifier for CPT 64582, reducing payment by as much as 30% of the national average. This payer-specific payment reduction was not mentioned in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Two Medicare Administrative Contractors currently require the -52 modifier when billing CPT 64582, applying payment reductions ranging from 0% to 30% of the $723 national average Medicare payment.”

surprises.description: The single-lead CPT application had been rejected in April and is now scheduled for review by the AMA editorial panel in September. The application is still described as on track for the January 1, 2028 implementation date the preview cited, so the process update adds uncertainty without changing the stated timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A revised Category 1 CPT code application will be reviewed at the September AMA editorial panel, keeping a potential single-lead code on track for January 1, 2028 implementation after an initial April rejection.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A permanent code for the single-lead system is reportedly effective January 1, 2028.”

in_line: The Q2 coding, reimbursement, and WISeR disruption was estimated at about $40 million, within the preview’s expected $40 million–$50 million Q2 headwind.
Despite the revised CPT application process, the potential single-lead code remains on track for January 1, 2028, the timing cited in the preview.

surprises.description: Revenue was expected to be about $1.81 billion, or 80% year-over-year growth; Palantir reported $1.935 billion and 93% growth, exceeding the estimate by about $125 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue grew 93% year-over-year to $1.935 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (consensus) | ~$1.81B, +80% YoY.”

surprises.description: The preview expected a full-year revenue raise toward 75% growth. Instead, Palantir raised its 2026 outlook to $8.15–$8.158 billion, or 80% growth, well beyond that level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $8.15–$8.158 billion (80% growth), an 11-point increase and the largest ever full-year guidance raise.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Oppenheimer expects a full-year guidance raise and looks for the ~71% growth guide to move toward 75%+.”

surprises.description: U.S. commercial growth did more than hold at the prior 133% rate: it accelerated to 149%, with revenue reaching $764 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. commercial revenue accelerated to 149% year-over-year growth (28% sequentially) reaching $764 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Whether +133% growth and $1.2B TCV hold up.”

surprises.description: U.S. commercial TCV bookings reached $2.132 billion, far above the prior-quarter $1.2 billion level the preview questioned whether the company could sustain; the new quarter was also nearly $800 million above the previous record.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company closed a record $2.132 billion in U.S. commercial TCV bookings, up 153% year-over-year and nearly $800 million above the prior highest quarter.”
