surprises.expectation_evidence: “Whether +133% growth and $1.2B TCV hold up.”

surprises.description: The full-year U.S. commercial revenue target was lifted from more than $3.2 billion to more than $3.424 billion, a stronger outlook than the preview’s standing guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. commercial guidance lifted to over $3.424 billion (at least 134% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “US commercial revenue >$3.2B (~120% growth).”

surprises.description: Adjusted free cash flow reached $1.22 billion and full-year guidance rose to $4.5–$4.7 billion, above the preview’s $4.2–$4.4 billion outlook despite its warning that the prior quarter set a high bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow hit a record $1.22 billion at a 63% margin, and full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance was raised to $4.5–$4.7 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow: Q1's $925M sets a high bar against the $4.2–4.4B FY guide.”

surprises.description: GAAP diluted EPS was $0.41 versus the preview’s $0.28 consensus estimate. The reported figure included a $0.03 benefit from unrealized SpaceX holding gains.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income reached $1.062 billion (55% margin) with GAAP EPS of $0.41, aided by a $0.03 tailwind from unrealized SpaceX holding gains.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP diluted EPS (consensus) | $0.28.”

surprises.description: Net dollar retention rose to 157%, up 700 basis points sequentially from the 150% reported in the prior quarter, showing faster expansion within existing customers than the preview had specifically projected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net dollar retention jumped 700 basis points sequentially to 157%, indicating accelerating expansion within the existing customer base.”

surprises.description: The Rule of 40 score climbed to 155%, up 10 points sequentially from the 145% reported for Q1; the preview did not forecast this further increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Rule of 40 score reached 155%, a 10-point sequential increase and the 12th consecutive quarter of expansion, on a 62% adjusted operating margin.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin fell to 86% because Palantir took on cloud-hosting costs for a government customer, a margin pressure the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin declined to 86% due to costs from taking on cloud hosting for a government customer.”

surprises.description: Management warned of a significant Q3 expense increase from new-hire seasonality, an upcoming cost ramp not mentioned in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “warned of a significant Q3 expense ramp from new-hire seasonality.”

surprises.description: Karp set a notably ambitious target for overall business growth to match or exceed U.S. commercial growth over the next 18 months; the preview did not report this outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CEO Alex Karp set an ambitious target to grow the overall business at a rate equal to or above U.S. commercial growth for the next 18 months.”

surprises.description: The preview put Q3 adjusted EPS consensus at $1.65–$1.66; Cabot reported $1.67, a small beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cabot delivered Q3 fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.67.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 FY26 adj. EPS | $1.66”; “Q3 FY26 adj. EPS | $1.65.”

surprises.description: Instead of leaving FY26 EPS guidance at $6.00–$6.50, Cabot raised the floor to $6.15 and lowered the ceiling to $6.45. The range is narrower, with a midpoint of $6.30, slightly below the preview’s $6.33 consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company tightened its fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $6.15-$6.45 from the prior $6.00-$6.50 range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance: $6.00–$6.50”; FY26 adjusted EPS consensus “$6.33.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted possible battery-materials deceleration as a key risk; instead, Cabot cited battery-materials growth as a driver of a 19% year-over-year increase in Performance Chemicals EBIT.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Performance Chemicals segment EBIT rose 19% year-over-year to $68 million, aided by battery materials growth and pricing actions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Battery Materials. Revenue grew 43% in Q2, with a ~$40M FY26 EBITDA target. A deceleration would matter more than the dollar amount.”

surprises.description: The CEO’s planned retirement and the CFO’s appointment as successor were not flagged in the preview; Cabot also said it is searching for a new CFO.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CEO Sean Keohane will retire effective September 30, 2026, with CFO Erica McLaughlin appointed as the next President and CEO and a search underway for a new CFO.”

surprises.description: Cabot disclosed that it had replaced a planned Michigan greenfield battery facility with expansions at two existing U.S. sites. The preview flagged the battery business but did not anticipate this change in project or the roughly $125 million investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cabot replaced its planned Michigan greenfield battery facility with brownfield expansions at two existing U.S. sites, investing roughly $125 million with capacity expected online in 2028 and sufficient for about three years of growth.”

surprises.description: The high end of FY26 capex guidance fell by $15 million, from $230 million to $215 million, while the low end stayed at $200 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management narrowed fiscal 2026 capex guidance to $200-$215 million (cutting the high end by $15 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Other FY26 guidance: … capex $200–230M.”

surprises.description: Cabot raised its operating tax-rate range by one percentage point at both ends, to 28%–30% from 27%–29%, an unexpected cost headwind relative to the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management … raised the operating tax rate range to 28%-30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Other FY26 guidance: operating tax rate 27–29%.”

surprises.description: Cabot said Q4 would have modest sequential EBIT declines from seasonality and margin normalization. The preview discussed possible Q4 demand softening, but did not flag this specific EBIT decline and margin-normalization outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management … warned Q4 will see modest sequential EBIT declines from seasonality and margin normalization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management tied the low end to Middle East–driven Q4 demand softening.”

in_line: Cabot reaffirmed its approximately $40 million FY26 Battery Materials EBITDA expectation, consistent with the preview’s stated target.
The preview identified the EU determination and possible pre-buy/excess-inventory distortion as an issue to watch; the provided call facts do not report a distinct outcome on that issue.
The preview expected the FY26 EPS range might be narrowed; Cabot did narrow it, although the revised endpoints and midpoint differ from the prior range and consensus.

surprises.description: Q2 net sales were $1.566 billion, above the preview’s roughly $1.50 billion consensus and even above its $1.52 billion bull-case threshold. The gap was about 4% versus consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated net sales rose 92% year-over-year to $1.566 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus ~$1.50 bn”; bull scenario: “Revenue at or above $1.52 bn.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $2.73, above the preview’s $2.48–$2.56 consensus range. The preview cautioned that consensus EPS basis was unclear, so the comparison is not fully like-for-like.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS grew 8% to $2.73.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS … $2.48 … or $2.56”; the preview also says “Neither states GAAP vs. adjusted.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $404 million, above the preview’s $385 million bull-case threshold, despite no quarterly EBITDA consensus estimate being available.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA reached $404 million (25.8% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Bull scenario: “adj. EBITDA at or above $385 M”; the preview says adjusted EBITDA consensus was “Not found.”

surprises.description: The legacy Allison Transmission business grew 6% to a quarterly record of $860 million, rather than the preview’s plausible flat-to-down outlook for the unit. The full-year guidance increase was also driven predominantly by this business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The legacy Allison Transmission business unit achieved a quarterly record of $860 million in net sales, up 6% year-over-year”; “The guidance increase … is driven predominantly by the Allison Transmission business unit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Transmission BU was still –4% YoY in Q1, so a flat-to-down print is a plausible base case.”

surprises.description: Management raised the full-year sales and adjusted EBITDA ranges above the previously reaffirmed ranges, with midpoint increases of about $150 million and $80 million, respectively. The new ranges are $5.8–$6.0 billion in sales and $1.465–$1.575 billion in adjusted EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to net sales of $5.8-6.0 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $1.465-1.575 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave existing FY26 guidance of “$5,575–5,925 M” net sales and “$1,365–1,515 M” adjusted EBITDA, and said it had been “reaffirmed May 4, 2026.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted free-cash-flow guidance was raised to $745–$865 million, from the preview’s previously stated $655–$805 million range. The new midpoint is $75 million higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance … adjusted free cash flow of $745-865 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a FY adjusted FCF range of “$655–805 M” and said Q1’s $103 million meant “the back half must carry most of the conversion.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted free cash flow was a record $281 million, a stronger quarterly conversion than the preview’s focus on the low Q1 result and the need for most conversion in the second half would suggest. The result also came despite substantial material-cost headwinds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record quarterly adjusted free cash flow of $281 million rose 84% year-over-year despite mid-teens material cost headwinds from steel and aluminum.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. FCF: Q1 was $103 M against a FY range of $655–805 M, so the back half must carry most of the conversion.”

surprises.description: The reported wins included more than 7,000 French tactical trucks, an award not mentioned among the preview’s defense items. This adds a defense-program win beyond the BAE and EAGLE awards the preview already discussed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wins covering 7,000+ French tactical trucks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted the BAE CV90 MkIV order and “a roughly 3,000-vehicle EAGLE V award”; it did not mention a French tactical-truck win.

surprises.description: The EAGLE award was already known at roughly 3,000 vehicles, but the call said it could cover up to 5,000, indicating additional potential volume beyond the preview’s stated award size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “~3,000 (up to 5,000) EAGLE armored vehicles.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A roughly 3,000-vehicle EAGLE V award with General Dynamics European Land Systems.”

surprises.description: Rising steel and aluminum costs compressed legacy margins, with aluminum up nearly 25% quarter-over-quarter and customer recovery delayed by 6–12 months. The preview did not flag this near-term margin pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Legacy business margins were compressed by rapidly rising commodity costs, with aluminum up nearly 25% quarter-over-quarter”; “a substantial portion is recoverable from customers on a 6-to-12-month lag.”

surprises.description: Although the preview noted expected initial synergy realization later in 2026, management said essentially no material synergies were included in 2026 EBITDA guidance and described a staged path, with 40% realized by end-2027 and full realization by 2029.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Essentially no material synergies baked into 2026 EBITDA”; “40% realized by end of 2027, 80% by 2028, and full realization by 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said initial realization was expected “later in 2026” and asked whether “any was booked in Q2.”

surprises.description: The company fully repaid the remaining $150 million revolver balance while targeting 2x leverage, a debt-repayment and deleveraging detail not anticipated in the preview’s capital-allocation discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full repayment of the remaining $150 million revolver balance as the company targets 2x leverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s capital-allocation checklist noted a Q1 buyback and the $0.29 dividend but did not mention repaying the revolver.

in_line: The $250 million BAE Hägglunds CV90 MkIV order was already disclosed in the preview; the call confirmed the order.
The roughly 3,000-vehicle EAGLE award was already identified in the preview; the call confirmed the award, with potential volume up to 5,000 treated separately above.
The $120 million annual run-rate synergy target remained in place, as the preview said it had been reiterated.
The $0.29 dividend matched the dividend level the preview said had been raised in Q1.

surprises.description: Snap reported Q2 revenue of $1.6 billion, above the preview’s $1.52–$1.55 billion company-guidance range and roughly $1.53 billion consensus. Revenue growth of 19% also exceeded the preview’s roughly 14% expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue grew 19% year-over-year to $1.6 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … Consensus $1.53B (+13.97% YoY)” and “Company guidance (Q2) $1.52B – $1.55B.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was well above the company’s expected Q2 range: $250 million versus guidance of $175–$200 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose $208 million year-over-year to $250 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … Company guidance (Q2) $175M – $200M.”

surprises.description: Advertising growth accelerated more than the preview’s modest-recovery setup suggested: ad revenue grew 9%, compared with 3% in Q1. The preview had highlighted reacceleration as a key question.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Advertising revenue up 9% to $1.28 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 ad revenue grew only 3% YoY” and the preview asked about “Ad revenue reacceleration” and “modest ad recovery.”

surprises.description: Ad-conversion measures improved sharply, adding evidence of stronger ad performance beyond the revenue result: app purchase volume rose 128% and total platform conversions rose 56%. The preview focused on ad recovery but did not anticipate these specific gains.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cost per install down 8%, cost per purchase down 18%, app purchase volume up 128%, and total platform conversions up 56% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Ad revenue reacceleration” was ranked as the top metric to watch.

surprises.description: Snap said adjusted costs grew only 4% while revenue grew 19%, a favorable sign of cost discipline against the preview’s focus on whether the announced savings program was being delivered. The call did not quantify progress against the preview’s more than $500 million annualized-reduction target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Achieving 19% revenue growth against just 4% adjusted cost growth in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said investors would look for “evidence the >$500M annualized reduction is on track.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year infrastructure-cost outlook by $50 million at both ends of the range, citing added AI and machine-learning investment. That is a cost headwind alongside the preview’s focus on cost savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year infrastructure cost guidance was raised to $1.65–$1.70 billion from $1.60–$1.65 billion, driven by additional AI and machine learning infrastructure investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “Cost-savings delivery” and the target of “more than $500M in annualized cost reductions in H2 2026.”

surprises.description: Snap disclosed Q3 revenue and EBITDA guidance with a caveat that World Cup ad spending is normalizing and year-over-year comparisons are tougher. The preview specifically looked for Q3 guidance to reaffirm the ad-recovery story, so this explanation qualifies the strong Q2 ad momentum, though no Q3 consensus range was provided for comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue guidance of $1.70–$1.74 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $300–$350 million reflect normalizing World Cup ad spending and tougher year-over-year comparisons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked “Whether the company reaffirms the ad-recovery story” and identified Q3 guidance as a catalyst.

surprises.description: Management shifted the company’s primary financial objective to free cash flow per share, a strategic emphasis not raised in the preview. The call also reported eight consecutive quarters of positive free cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company shifted its primary financial objective to free cash flow per share”; “Free cash flow was $121 million in Q2 (marking eight consecutive positive quarters), with trailing 12-month free cash flow of $706 million.”

surprises.description: Snap described Specs’ commercial launch as coming later this fall but said it expects mass-market adoption only toward the end of the decade. That is a longer adoption horizon than the preview’s open question about Specs monetization might have led investors to focus on.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Specs, priced at $2,195, will hold a launch event September 16 with commercial launch later this fall, though management expects mass-market adoption only toward the end of the decade.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Specs AR glasses ($2,195 launch price) monetization commentary” as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: Management guided to sustained positive net income beginning in 2027, a longer-term profitability outlook that the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “guided sustained positive net income beginning in 2027.”

in_line: Other revenue grew 85%, broadly matching the preview’s expectation of continued strong subscription and other-revenue momentum after Q1 growth of 87%.
Specs retained the $2,195 price already stated in the preview.

surprises.description: BWXT raised its 2026 outlook across revenue, adjusted EBITDA, EPS, and free cash flow rather than merely reaffirming it. The new adjusted EBITDA midpoint is $10 million higher, and free cash flow guidance is $30 million higher than before.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance: revenue to approximately $3.8 billion, adjusted EBITDA to $662-$672 million (up $10 million at midpoint), EPS to $4.70-$4.80, and free cash flow to $345-$360 million (up $30 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Does the company hold, raise, or cut the revenue, EBITDA, EPS, and FCF ranges?” The preview listed prior guidance of at least $3.75B revenue, $650–665M adjusted EBITDA, $4.60–4.75 non-GAAP EPS, and $315–330M free cash flow.

surprises.description: Commercial Operations grew much faster than the preview’s general discussion of commercial nuclear demand would suggest, and BWXT raised its full-year segment revenue-growth outlook from about 30% to about 45%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commercial Operations revenue grew 72% (33% organic) with adjusted EBITDA more than doubling (up 123%) to $36 million at an 11.9% margin, and full-year revenue growth guidance was raised to ~45% from ~30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “commercial nuclear components demand” but gave no segment growth estimate; it also said segment-level detail was not covered in depth.

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s focus on margin stabilization, adjusted EBITDA grew substantially more slowly than revenue, indicating that the margin pressure had not clearly stabilized in Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue rose 18% year-over-year” while “adjusted EBITDA grew 7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 adjusted EBITDA margin compression (~17.2% vs. ~19.0%) is the main concern. Management flagged higher corporate expenses from restructuring initiatives as a Q2 headwind. Watch whether margins stabilize.”

surprises.description: Government Operations’ full-year revenue-growth outlook was cut from the low teens to the high single digits, even as its margin outlook improved. That is a weaker growth outlook but better expected profitability than the prior guidance implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Government Operations full-year revenue growth guidance was lowered to high single digits from low teens due to stronger HPDU cost performance, but adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was raised to ~20.5% from >19%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified Government Operations as an issue to watch but did not give segment guidance expectations.

surprises.description: Backlog slipped modestly from Q1’s record level, rather than building further or holding steady, although the high book-to-bill and year-over-year growth temper the concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog reached $8.4 billion, up 40% year-over-year but modestly lower sequentially, with a trailing 12-month book-to-bill of 1.7x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Backlog. Record $8.65B at Q1. Look for further build or any burn-down commentary.”

surprises.description: BWXT announced a sale of most of its medical and Kinectrics stable-isotope enrichment businesses, a significant portfolio change not anticipated in the preview. The transaction brings substantial upfront cash but removes the businesses’ revenue after closing, while BWXT retains a minority stake and shared upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BWXT announced the sale of just over 80% of its medical and Kinectrics stable isotope enrichment businesses to Nordic Capital for $750 million upfront, with shared economics allowing consideration up to $800 million, retaining a 20% minority equity stake.” The businesses represent “approximately $130 million of 2026 revenue” and will have “no revenue post-close.”

surprises.description: Management described a credible chance of winning at least one new-build nuclear equipment order before year-end, tied to several reactor opportunities. This was a concrete near-term order opportunity not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects a credible opportunity to secure at least one new-build nuclear equipment order before year-end, tied to SMR opportunities at Darlington, AP1000 projects, and X300 reactors.”

surprises.description: BWXT found ways to monetize reactor technology it had shelved after a large prior investment, through an exclusive licensing agreement and a separate floating-platform feasibility study. The agreements preserve royalty, manufacturing, and IP rights, though the feasibility work is not itself an order.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BWXT signed an exclusive land-based mPower licensing agreement with Applied Atomics and a floating-platform feasibility study with Core Power, retaining royalty rights, exclusive manufacturing rights, and IP to monetize technology it had shelved after spending ~$400 million.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $902 million was broadly in line with the preview’s conflicting consensus estimates of $891.8 million and $903.8 million.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $711 million, above the $704.5 million consensus and the $707 million top of the preview’s guidance range; organic growth was also reported slightly above the high end of guidance. The revenue gap was modest, but the quarter came in ahead of the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pro forma organic growth was 3% in Q2, coming in slightly above the high end of guidance, with total revenue of $711 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (pro forma) | Consensus $704.5M | Company guidance $699–707M”; “Organic growth | ~2–3% | 2–3%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $1.41 substantially exceeded the $1.23 consensus and even the preview’s bull-case range of $1.28–$1.32. The beat was partly supported by $16 million of one-time tariff refunds and a lower tax rate that management said reverses in Q4, so not all of the upside was recurring.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pro forma adjusted EPS was $1.41, well above guidance, with roughly half the upside from $16 million in one-time tariff refunds and about one-third from a lower 16% tax rate that reverses in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS | Consensus $1.23”; the bull scenario expected “$1.28–1.32.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year organic growth guidance to 4%–5% from 3%–4%, above the preview’s base expectation of a reaffirmation or only a slight raise. This was a more meaningful improvement than the preview’s 3%–4% full-year outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year organic growth guidance was raised to 4%-5% from the prior 3%-4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 organic growth | 3–4%”; “In-line to slightly raised is the base case.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance rose by $0.10 to $5.30–$5.40, above the prior $5.20–$5.30 range and the $5.25 consensus. The preview treated a reaffirmation as the base case, while this raise reaches the preview’s bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS guidance was raised $0.10 to $5.30-$5.40.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EPS | Consensus $5.25 | Company guidance $5.20–5.30”; the base case was “FY guide reaffirmed or narrowed high,” while the bull case called for “$5.30–5.40.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted operating margin was 29.3%, well above the preview’s roughly 27% expectation; even excluding tariff refunds, it exceeded the 27% guidance assumption. Full-year margin guidance also increased by 30 basis points to 28.7%, rather than remaining at 28.4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margins were 29.3% in the quarter, and even excluding tariff refunds, margins exceeded the 27% guidance assumption; full-year margin guidance was lifted 30 basis points to 28.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating margin | ~27% | ~27%”; “FY26 adj. operating margin | ~28.4% | 28.4%.”

surprises.description: Diagnostics grew 11% organically, including double-digit reproductive health growth and high-single-digit immunodiagnostics growth, and remained strong even excluding the Genomics England sequencing contract. The preview expected overall organic growth of about 2%–3% but did not forecast this level of Diagnostics growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Diagnostics segment grew 11% organically, with reproductive health up double digits and immunodiagnostics up high single digits, remaining strong even excluding the Genomics England sequencing contract.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Organic growth | ~2–3%”; the preview did not provide a Q2 Diagnostics growth estimate.

surprises.description: Life Sciences declined 3% organically, with Signals software down approximately 20% on difficult comparisons, despite the preview highlighting positive pharma/biotech demand and a return to growth in academic/government in Q1. The mid-20s ARR growth and expected second-half return to double-digit Signals growth temper the weakness; the preview had specifically identified software ARR quantification as an open question.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Life Sciences segment declined 3% organically, dragged down by an approximate 20% decline in Signals software due to difficult comps, though software ARR grew in the mid-20s and management expects a return to double-digit growth in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pharma/biotech ran low-double-digit organic in Q1. The US academic/government segment turned positive in Q1”; “Watch for any quantification of software ARR; currently this is a multiple story, not an estimate story.”

surprises.description: The company entered Q3 with its strongest instrument backlog in 3–4 years, and demand for Opera Phenix OptIQ high-content screening systems was outpacing production capacity. Management consequently upgraded full-year platform growth guidance from low to mid-single digits; the capacity constraint may limit how quickly demand converts to sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Company entered Q3 with its strongest instrument backlog in 3-4 years, driven by high-content screening (Opera Phenix OptIQ) order velocity outpacing production capacity, prompting an upgrade of full-year platform growth guidance from low to mid-single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Instrument book-to-bill and tariff/FX quantification. The credibility test for the 2H acceleration.”

surprises.description: Management reported emerging demand from nontraditional, AI-focused customers building AI-driven drug discovery platforms, an opportunity the preview did not identify. It remains too early for the company to quantify the potential, so this was a new qualitative signal rather than a forecastable contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management signaled emerging demand from nontraditional AI-focused customers building AI-driven drug discovery platforms, but said it remains too early to quantify the magnitude of this opportunity.”

in_line: The China immunodiagnostics divestiture advanced to a definitive agreement on expected terms, with closing anticipated by the end of 2027, consistent with the preview’s expectation of definitive progress and a 2H27 close.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $249.7 million, far above the $32.54 million consensus and the preview’s $30–35 million base case. The company reported $62.5 million of Rigel license revenue, $126.4 million of accelerated Pfizer deferred revenue, and a $50 million Pfizer approval milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue of $249.7 million in Q2, driven by a $62.5 million Rigel license (of which $35 million was received), $126.4 million of accelerated Pfizer deferred revenue, and a $50 million Pfizer milestone from VEPPANU's approval.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 Consensus: Revenue $32.54M”; the preview’s base case was “$30–35M.”

surprises.description: The expected 2026 start for ARV-102’s next PSP trials has slipped to 2027. The preview identified the FDA hold as the most important issue and said the start was tied to FDA clearance, with the prior guidance pointing to mid-2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FDA requested additional information before authorizing the Phase Ib trial, and Arvinas now expects to begin its next PSP clinical trials in 2027 rather than 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FDA placed the planned Phase 1b in PSP on hold pending chronic non-human-primate toxicology data, guided to ‘mid-2026’”; the preview also listed “ARV-102 hold status versus expectations of resolution.”

surprises.description: Rather than advancing ARV-806 itself as investors might have expected from the planned Phase 1 data “later this year,” Arvinas decided to advance the KRAS G12D program only through a partner. The call does not specify a revised data date.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Arvinas made the strategic decision to advance its KRAS G12D program (ARV-806) only through a partner, citing capital allocation priorities.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ARV-806 (KRAS G12D) initial Phase 1 data. Dose escalation finished ahead of schedule. Management said data would come ‘later this year.’”

surprises.description: ARV-393’s initial data remains on track for year-end 2026, but most patients were dosed below the expected efficacious range, and the cohorts are weighted toward T-cell lymphoma. More mature monotherapy and combination data, including DLBCL patients, will not come until 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Initial Phase I data for ARV-393 is on track for release by year-end 2026, though most patients were dosed below the expected efficacious range and the cohorts skew toward T-cell lymphoma patients”; “More mature ARV-393 monotherapy and glofitamab combination data, including DLBCL patients, will be disclosed in 2027.”

surprises.description: Arvinas reported a $52.7 million liability for remaining VEPPANU development obligations, a deal-related balance-sheet obligation not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Arvinas booking a $52.7 million liability for remaining VEPPANU development obligations.”

surprises.description: ARV-027 has progressed into multiple-dose dosing, with proof-of-mechanism data targeting more than 50% degradation expected in the first half of 2027. This program milestone was not covered in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ARV-027 … completed single ascending dose cohorts and entered multiple-dose dosing, with proof-of-mechanism data (muscle exposure and AR degradation) targeting >50% degradation expected in the first half of 2027.”

surprises.description: Arvinas said its first immuno-oncology PROTAC, ARV-6723, is on track to begin enrolling patients in Phase I within weeks, with single-agent activity reported in seven checkpoint-resistant preclinical models. The program was not mentioned in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The HPK1 degrader (ARV-6723) … is on track to begin Phase I enrollment in patients within the coming weeks, showing single-agent activity in 7 checkpoint-resistant preclinical models.”

in_line: The preview flagged cash runway into the second half of 2028 as important; Arvinas reaffirmed that runway despite ending Q2 with $567.9 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $25 million, below the preview’s consensus range of about $29.3–$32.5 million. The preview expected a transitional quarter with shrinking mining revenue, but the reported result was weaker than the estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $25 million, down from $35 million in Q1, reflecting the decommissioning of bitcoin mining at Black Pearl amid the transition to contracted data center revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $29.28M”; alternatives of “$29.79M” and “$32.52M.”

surprises.description: The net loss was much larger than expected: diluted EPS was a loss of $0.65 versus preview estimates ranging from a loss of $0.11 to $0.24, including a consensus estimate of a $0.21 loss. The preview warned that warrant remeasurement could distort GAAP EPS, but the reported loss still substantially exceeded those estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 GAAP net loss of $268 million ($0.65 per diluted share), widening from a $114 million loss in Q1, primarily due to a $150.5 million noncash warrant remeasurement loss.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS -$0.21”; alternatives of “-$0.11” and “-$0.24.” The preview also noted that GAAP EPS was distorted by “derivative and warrant remeasurement.”

surprises.description: Black Pearl began earning rent earlier than the preview’s October expectation: initial capacity was delivered two months ahead of schedule and rent started in August. This is an acceleration for the initial capacity, while the remaining delivery deadlines were unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cipher delivered initial data center capacity at Black Pearl two months ahead of schedule at the tenant's request, with rent commencing in August, though the remaining Black Pearl delivery deadlines stay unchanged.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Black Pearl rent commencement (AWS): October 2026.”

surprises.description: The Stingray bond attracted unusually strong demand and achieved better pricing than the preview’s already-known 6% coupon implied: it was approximately 8x oversubscribed and priced tighter than prior bonds despite widening credit spreads.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cipher priced an $810 million project-level senior secured bond for Stingray at a 6% coupon (its lowest to date), which was approximately 8x oversubscribed and priced tighter than prior bonds despite widening credit spreads.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the company had “$810M of 6.000% Stingray notes due 2031” priced in June.

surprises.description: Management said near-term commitments should not require additional equity, addressing the preview’s dilution concern more favorably than the open-ended funding question suggested. The company also reported $870 million of unrestricted liquidity and no cash borrowings on its revolver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cipher ended Q2 with ... $870 million of unrestricted liquidity ... and no cash borrowings on its $200 million revolver, and management does not expect to require additional equity for near-term commitments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called funding for Reveille and Ulysses an “open question” and said “any sign of common equity issuance would be a clear negative.”

surprises.description: An unexpected Texas interconnection audit delayed the expected ERCOT Batch Zero results and introduced timing uncertainty. Management said the delay could increase the value of Cipher’s 477 megawatts available outside the batch process, making the effect mixed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Texas Governor Abbott issued a letter the day before the call requesting an interconnection queue audit, delaying the expected Friday ERCOT Batch Zero results and creating timing uncertainty, though management believes it increases the value of Cipher's 477 megawatts available in 2027 outside the batch process.”

surprises.description: Cipher added up to 1.1 gigawatts of potential Texas capacity, including the option-based Apollo site and a Stingray expansion. This expands the future development pipeline, although the Apollo capacity is potential rather than contracted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company added up to 1.1 gigawatts of potential new Texas capacity this quarter, including a 900-megawatt site called Apollo (option-based, near San Antonio, targeting 2031) and a 200-megawatt Stingray expansion.”

surprises.description: Projected average annualized NOI from the three executed campus leases rose slightly from the prior-quarter figure cited in the preview, from about $787 million to approximately $793 million. The increase is positive but small.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The three executed data center campus leases are expected to generate approximately $793 million of average annualized net operating income from October 2026 through September 2036.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “projected average annualized NOI of about $787M (Oct 2026–Sept 2036)” in the prior quarter.

in_line: The transition away from bitcoin mining reduced revenue in the quarter, consistent with the preview’s description of Q2 as a wind-down quarter before HPC lease revenue ramps.
Odessa’s reported operating metrics—207 megawatts, about 11.6 exahash per second, 17.2 joules per terahash, and 346 bitcoin mined—matched the Q1 operating figures cited in the preview.

surprises.description: DuPont reported adjusted EPS of $1.88 versus the preview’s $1.76 consensus, a $0.12 beat and the top of the preview’s $1.83–$1.88 bull-case range. The preview expected a beat, but the reported result was at the high end of its outcomes; $0.15 of the year-over-year EPS increase came from below-the-line items and $0.17 from stronger operations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew 21% year-over-year to $1.88, driven by $0.17 from stronger operations and $0.15 from below-the-line items.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS $1.76 (Zacks)”; “A beat is expected, so the size matters.”

surprises.description: The full-year EPS midpoint rose to $7.24, slightly above the preview’s roughly $7.14 consensus and above its stated threshold of a raise to about $7.20. The preview identified FY26 EPS guidance as the largest swing factor, so the raise was positive but only modestly exceeded that bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DuPont raised full-year 2026 guidance to slightly above 4% organic growth, $1.760 billion operating EBITDA, and $7.24 adjusted EPS midpoint (up $0.15…).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EPS $7.14–$7.15”; “Anything below a raise to about $7.20 is a disappointment.”

surprises.description: Q2 operating EBITDA was $448 million against the preview’s approximately $430 million estimate, while the EBITDA margin expanded 80 basis points despite the anticipated price/cost headwind. This was a stronger operating result than the preview’s estimate implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating EBITDA increased 8% to $448 million with margin expanding 80 basis points to 24.6%, despite a 30 basis point headwind from price/cost dynamics.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating EBITDA ~$430M”; “The guide embeds a roughly 30bp Q2 margin headwind.”

surprises.description: Water did not deliver the anticipated mid-single-digit recovery: sales grew only low single digits, and DuPont cut the full-year Water outlook to low-to-mid single digits. Middle East conflict-related project delays contributed to the shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Water sales grew only low single digits due to Middle East conflict-driven project delays… prompting a full-year Water outlook cut to low-to-mid single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Water returning to growth. The HWT mid-single-digit organic guide depends on water turning positive after the Q1 catch-up.”

surprises.description: The company announced a $250 million Q3 share repurchase while also retaining more than $1 billion of capacity for targeted Water and Healthcare/CDMO acquisitions. This resolves the preview’s buyback-versus-healthcare-M&A debate with a plan to pursue both, rather than signaling only one use of the proceeds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to launch a $250 million share repurchase in Q3 while retaining over $1 billion of capacity for mid-teen valuation M&A targeting Water and Healthcare/CDMO opportunities.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Use of Aramids proceeds. About $1.2B of cash is in hand, with about $1.275B left on the $2B buyback authorization. Management has flagged healthcare M&A.”; “Healthcare M&A versus incremental buyback.”

surprises.description: DuPont’s cash-conversion outlook improved beyond the stated 90% full-year target: Q2 free-cash-flow conversion was 127%, and full-year conversion is now expected closer to 100%. The preview did not discuss cash conversion, so this was an unanticipated positive update relative to the target cited on the call.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow of $326 million delivered 127% conversion, with full-year conversion now expected closer to 100%, ahead of the 90% target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Ahead of the 90% target.”

surprises.description: DuPont disclosed that its roughly $70 million EV battery adhesives business is expected to grow into triple digits by 2026–2027, with the broader EV portfolio approaching half of its $900 million automotive business. The preview did not flag this specific growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The EV battery adhesives business (~$70 million revenue today) is expected to grow into triple digits by 2026-2027, with the broader EV portfolio approaching half of the $900 million automotive business.”

in_line: Net sales were $1.8 billion, close to the preview’s $1.818 billion consensus and the company’s approximately $1.8 billion guidance.
The reported 30-basis-point Q2 price/cost headwind matched the preview’s anticipated margin headwind.
The preview expected full run-rate pricing in the second half; the call described about two points of second-half growth from carryforward pricing and said price/cost would be dollar-neutral.

surprises.description: The preview estimated quarter-end cash and investments of $375–390 million and total liquidity of $510–525 million. Eve reported $403 million in cash and $531 million of total liquidity, above those estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: Eve ended Q2 with “$403 million in cash and total liquidity of $531 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash + Inv. $375–390M” and total liquidity estimated at “~$510–525M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected first-half burn to run at a pace that annualized above $270 million and watched for burn near the upper end of the $225–275 million guide. Management instead expects full-year cash consumption near the midpoint of the range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half 2026 total cash burn was $118 million” and full-year cash consumption is expected “near the midpoint of the $225-275 million guidance range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “H1 at a Q1-level pace annualizes above $270M, at or above the top of the range”; the preview also described the base case as burn “in upper half of range.”

surprises.description: The reported Q2 net loss was substantially smaller than the preview’s estimated loss of about $62 million. The preview’s EPS consensus was -$0.18, but the call facts do not provide actual EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss was $34 million in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied net loss ~-$62M,” derived in the preview from consensus EPS.

surprises.description: Q2 R&D fell sharply to $29 million from roughly $55 million in prior quarters because supplier agreements were better than expected. Management said the reduction is not a new run rate: R&D is expected to return to around $50 million per quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 R&D fell to $29 million (versus roughly $55 million in prior quarters) due to better-than-expected supplier agreements, but is expected to return to around $50 million per quarter going forward.”

surprises.description: The preview expected full transition flights in Q3 as part of the 2026 flight-test progress to watch. Eve said the milestone has slipped into Q4, with another 30–40 flights needed before the lifters can be powered off at 90 knots.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full transition flights slipped from Q3 into Q4 2026,” requiring “30-40 more flights” before lifters are powered off at 90 knots.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified the “~300-flight 2026 target” and said the flight-test envelope was still early; it also noted the “first partial transition flight on Aug 3.”

surprises.description: The preview described about 60 flights in Q1 and said reaching roughly 300 flights in 2026 would require a sharp increase in sortie rate. Eve reported 66 flights by the end of Q2, indicating only limited progress toward that target during the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: The prototype had completed “66 flights logging 2 hours 46 minutes of airtime.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Flight count against the ~300-flight 2026 target. Reaching it from about 60 in Q1 needs a sharp increase in sortie rate.”

surprises.description: The preview’s expected first conforming-prototype flight was mid-2027; Eve now plans the first crewed conforming-prototype flight in the second half of 2027, a later timing window. The call did not provide an update on the preview’s late-2026 assembly-completion expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The first crewed conforming prototype flight is planned for the second half of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guide is assembly complete in late 2026 and first flight mid-2027.”

surprises.description: Management newly quantified potential Embraer synergies at $100–150 million over three years. Most of the savings are expected in 2027 and 2028, with less than one-third captured in 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management identified $100-150 million in potential synergies with Embraer over three years,” with “less than one-third expected to be captured in 2026.”

surprises.description: Eve disclosed a roughly $100 million, multi-year capex plan for modular production capacity, including a step-up to around $50 million in 2027. The preview did not provide a capex expectation, and the spending adds to planned cash needs while funding capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Capex is planned at approximately $20 million in 2026, rising to around $50 million in 2027 and $30-40 million in 2028 (about $100 million total) for modular production capacity.”

surprises.description: The call added a specific timing estimate for European certification: EASA approval is expected 12–15 months after ANAC and FAA approval. The preview discussed certification timing but gave no European-certification timeline to compare against.
surprises.fact_evidence: “European (EASA) certification expected 12-15 months after ANAC and FAA approval.”

in_line: Management said liquidity is sufficient to fund operations through 2028 without new funding, consistent with the preview’s focus on reaffirmation of the funded-through-2028 position.

The 2028 certification and entry-into-service target was maintained, in line with the preview’s expectation that 2028 would be reaffirmed; the call also cited roughly 12 months of post-first-flight testing, matching the preview’s description.
Partial transition flights had begun and reached 30 knots, consistent with the preview’s note that the first partial transition flight had already occurred before the call.

The two new LOIs covered 46 aircraft and the stated total backlog remained about 2,700 aircraft; the preview cautioned that additional non-binding LOIs were less important than binding-order conversion, and the call facts report no new binding-order conversion.

surprises.description: Kimberly-Clark lowered its full-year outlook, whereas the preview’s base case assumed FY26 guidance would be reaffirmed. The call attributed the cut to one-off items including the China disruption, the distribution-center fire, and North American retailer inventory reductions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered its full-year outlook due to discrete one-off items including the China disruption, an L.A. distribution center fire (~$22 million/80 bps Q2 headwind), and North American retailer inventory reductions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base assumes organic growth in line with category and FY26 reaffirmed”; the preview also said the FY26 attributable EPS guide was “reaffirmed at roughly flat, or hedged.”

surprises.description: A China diaper-business disruption from social-media safety claims emerged unexpectedly and is expected to weigh on second-half results. Management estimated a roughly 200-basis-point top-line headwind, about $70 million of operating profit and $0.16 of EPS, split between Q3 and Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A China diaper business disruption from social media safety claims (only impacting the final 2 weeks of June) is expected to be a ~200 basis point top-line headwind in the second half, roughly $70 million in operating profit and about $0.16 of EPS, split evenly across Q3 and Q4.”

surprises.description: North American shipments fell well behind consumption as retailers reduced inventory, adding a headwind beyond the preview’s focus on category growth and North American operating profit. Shipments were down 1.4% while consumption grew 0.3%, and the inventory reductions contributed to the outlook cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North American consumer shipments lagged consumption by about 170 basis points in Q2, with shipments down 1.4% versus consumption growth of only 0.3%”; the outlook was lowered partly due to “North American retailer inventory reductions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted North American operating profit and expected organic growth “in line to ahead of category,” but did not flag retailer inventory reductions.

surprises.description: Category growth was weaker than the preview’s roughly 2.5% global-category backdrop suggested: North American weighted category growth slowed to 1.9% from 3.7% the prior quarter, while global trailing-12-month growth slipped to about 2%. Management also cited increasing pressure on lower-income consumers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Weighted category growth in North America moderated sequentially from 3.7% last quarter to 1.9%, with global trailing-12-month category growth slipping from ~2.5% to ~2% amid increasing pressure on lower-income consumers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the outlook as organic growth “in line to ahead of category (~2.5%)” and expected the base case to have organic growth “in line with category.”

surprises.description: Q2 organic sales were about 100 basis points below management’s internal expectations, despite the preview’s expectation of roughly 2.5% organic growth. The call did not provide the reported organic-sales growth rate, so the shortfall versus the preview’s estimate cannot be quantified directly.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 organic sales came in roughly 100 basis points below internal expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Organic sales growth: ~+2.5%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating profit and EPS came in above expectations despite the organic-sales shortfall, helped by an unexpected $45 million tariff refund. The refund was about half of what the company had paid in North America.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received a $45 million tariff refund in Q2 (about half of what it paid in North America), which drove adjusted operating profit and EPS above expectations despite the organic sales miss.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS attributable to KMB” consensus was “$2.01 (range $2.00–2.01).”

surprises.description: The distribution-center fire’s Q2 operating-profit cost was substantially below the preview’s estimate, although its organic-sales impact was broadly in the preview’s anticipated range. The call cited about $22 million of cost versus the preview’s roughly $50 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An L.A. distribution center fire (~$22 million/80 bps Q2 headwind).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “West Coast distribution center fire: ~70–80bps off organic growth and ~$50M off operating profit.”

surprises.description: Kimberly-Clark announced a proprietary alternative natural-fiber program that the preview had not anticipated. The company said land was acquired and a pilot facility was breaking ground, with the program aimed at improving margins and reducing forest-fiber cost volatility; the investments are already included in current results and outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Kimberly-Clark unveiled a proprietary alternative natural fiber program (with land already acquired and a pilot facility breaking ground) aimed at improving margins and reducing forest fiber cost volatility, with investments already embedded in current results and outlook.”

in_line: Kenvue remained on track to close in the second half, now expected in Q4, consistent with the preview’s 2H26 timing; management also expressed increased confidence in the $1.9 billion cost-synergy target, without committing to additional synergies.

Management said it expects to fully offset second-half inflation and keep full-year price-net-of-cost inflation roughly neutral, consistent with the preview’s expectation that mitigation would help address cost pressure in the second half.
Kimberly-Clark continued to deliver positive volume-plus-mix growth and hold global weighted market share, broadly consistent with the preview’s focus on innovation and volume/mix.

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was cut from $133–140 million to $133–136 million, lowering the top end while leaving the bottom unchanged. Management attributed the reduction to higher COGS from stronger-than-expected demand for premium-beef LTOs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cut its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $133-136 million,” attributing the reduction “entirely to higher COGS from stronger-than-expected demand for premium beef LTO offerings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA | $133–140M” and “A trim is the bear case.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $34.5 million, below the preview’s derived $36–38 million bogey. That is a shortfall of roughly $1.5–3.5 million, despite year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 13.5% to $34.5 million (9.7% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA | Not published; derived bogey ~$36–38M.”

surprises.description: Revenue came in below the $359.4 million consensus at $354.7 million, and growth was 15.2% rather than the preview’s expected 16.7%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue rose 15.2% to $354.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $359.4M (+16.7% Y/Y).”

surprises.description: The company lowered its longer-term unit-opening ambition to about 50 company-owned restaurants annually beginning in 2027, rather than continuing roughly 10% growth. The stated trade-off is prioritizing positive free cash flow and a stronger balance sheet.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered its long-term unit growth target to about 50 company-owned openings annually beginning in 2027 (down from ~10% growth) to prioritize positive free cash flow starting in 2027 and strengthen the balance sheet.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “any capital-allocation shift” and noted that “Management said in May it was evaluating buybacks,” but did not anticipate a lower unit-growth target.

surprises.description: Same-restaurant traffic improved substantially from Q1’s negative 2.0% to negative 0.4%, with June turning positive. That is much better than the preview’s concern that traffic might remain around negative 2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-restaurant traffic was slightly negative at -0.4% but improved 160 basis points sequentially from Q1, with June turning positive.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A second straight ~−2% quarter with no weather excuse would confirm the bear case.”

surprises.description: Same-restaurant sales grew 3.4%, above the preview’s guide-anchored range of roughly 1–3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue rose 15.2% to $354.7 million, driven by 3.4% same-restaurant sales growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Same-restaurant sales | ~1–3% (guide-anchored).”

surprises.description: The company raised the low end of its full-year same-restaurant sales guidance to 1.5% and its total revenue growth guidance to 12.5%, an upward revision to its outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised the low end of full-year same-restaurant sales guidance to 1.5-3% and total revenue growth to 12.5-14%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited same-restaurant sales guidance of “1–3%” and listed FY revenue consensus of “$1.38B,” but did not forecast an increase to either company guidance range.

surprises.description: The full-year commodity outlook was revised down from 1–3% inflation to flat-to-up 1.5%, a more favorable commodity cost outlook than the preview expected management to reaffirm. Management still expects inflation to return in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 benefited from ~1.6% commodity deflation (eggs, avocados, bacon), but full-year commodity inflation guidance was revised to flat-to-up 1.5% with inflation expected to return in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior-quarter guidance was “commodity inflation 1–3%,” and the preview said to watch for “reaffirmation of commodity (1–3%)” inflation.

surprises.description: Restaurant-level operating margin increased to 18.8% from Q1’s 18.5%, rather than merely holding at the prior-quarter level as the preview focused on. The improvement included a 30-basis-point labor benefit despite wage inflation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restaurant-level operating profit margin improved 20 basis points to 18.8%, aided by a 30 basis point labor improvement from a right-sized manager staffing model, despite 4.1% wage inflation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 margin was “18.5%” and to “Watch whether it holds as pricing rolls off.”

surprises.description: Management reported strong brand-awareness gains and said 17% of newly acquired customers had already returned for a second visit, tracking above average. The preview did not identify these customer-engagement measures as expectations to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Unaided brand awareness rose more than 50% and aided awareness increased 15% since early 2025, with 17% of newly acquired customers already returning for a second visit, tracking above average.”

in_line: Management cautioned that Q3 faces the toughest comparison and would land at or below the low end; the preview had already warned that fading H2 pricing could leave comps at or below the low end of the full-year range.

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $1.27, about 4% above the preview’s $1.22 consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS grew 15.5% to $1.27.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. (non-GAAP) EPS | Consensus | $1.22.”

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $3.5 billion, roughly 4% above the preview’s $3.36–$3.37 billion revenue estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 global sales grew 6.7% to $3.5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$3.36B (Zacks) vs. ~$3.37B (MarketBeat/Yahoo).”

surprises.description: Instead of reaffirming the full-year outlook, Henry Schein raised both ranges: sales growth to 4.5%–5.5% from 3%–5%, and non-GAAP EPS to $5.29–$5.39 from $5.23–$5.37.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 sales guidance to 4.5%-5.5% growth (from 3%-5%) and non-GAAP EPS to $5.29-$5.39 (from $5.23-$5.37).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether the company “reaffirms, raises, or narrows” the $5.23–$5.37 EPS range and described reaffirmation as the base case.

surprises.description: The company said high-growth, high-margin businesses already account for almost half of operating income and are on track to exceed the 50% goal by end-2027, indicating progress ahead of that stated target’s timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “High-growth, high-margin businesses now represent almost 50% of total operating income, on track to exceed the 50% goal by the end of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management’s stated target was to “exceed the 50% goal by the end of 2027.”

surprises.description: The EPS outlook increase was partly offset by a newly disclosed reduction in expected remeasurement gains: $11 million is projected for 2026 versus $38 million in 2025, with no further gains assumed for the rest of 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The EPS guidance raise was partially offset by lower expected remeasurement gains, now projected at just $11 million for 2026 versus $38 million in 2025, with no further gains assumed for the rest of the year.”

surprises.description: Henry Schein disclosed a $200 million Q2 share repurchase, a capital-allocation action not flagged in the preview; approximately $455 million remains authorized.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased 2.6 million shares for $200 million at an average price of $76.69 during Q2, with approximately $455 million remaining authorized.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.45, far above the preview’s $0.26 consensus estimate and the company’s pre-release commitment to at least $0.23. That was a much larger upside gap than the preview’s discussion of a possible consensus miss implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$0.45 non-GAAP diluted EPS.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS | $0.26”; management said EPS would be “at or above the high end” of $0.20–0.23.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 40%, above the preview’s roughly 38% consensus estimate and the 37–39% full-year guide. The preview had noted the quarter was expected to be at or above 38%, but the reported margin was stronger still.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Profitability remained strong with a 40% adjusted EBITDA margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin | ~38%”; FY2026 guide was “37–39%,” and the pre-announcement was “at or above high end,” so “≥38%.”

surprises.description: RPO reached $894 million, above the preview’s roughly $800–820 million scenario range, and carried a 3.7-year average life. The growth was aided by the company’s first nine-figure annual revenue commitment, adding a large-customer concentration consideration to the stronger-than-expected backlog.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Remaining performance obligations surged more than 12x year-over-year to $894 million with a 3.7-year average life, aided by the company landing its first 9-figure annual revenue commitment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “RPO about $800–820M” and it flagged “Multiple nine-figure annual commitments” as a bull and bear case, with concentration as a swing factor.

surprises.description: The July equitization of $472 million of 0% 2030 notes left effectively no dilution and brought pro forma net leverage to about 0.7x—well below the preview’s roughly 3x year-end 2026 target. This was a substantially stronger balance-sheet outcome than the preview’s funding-risk framing anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In July, the company equitized $472 million of its 0% 2030 convertible notes with effectively no dilution, bringing pro forma net leverage to approximately 0.7x, well below its 4x guideline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “Net leverage target about 3x by year-end 2026” and described capacity funding as a key risk, with “Any sign of a new equity or convert raise” as the largest single downside risk.

surprises.description: The highest-spending customer cohorts accelerated, with $1 million-plus customer ARR growing 214% and its share of total ARR rising from 9% to 23%. That gives the preview’s concentration concern a more pronounced quantified form, even as large-customer growth supports expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$100,000-plus customer ARR growing 98%, $500,000-plus growing 160%, and $1 million-plus growing 214%, and the top cohort rose from 9% to 23% of total ARR year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Customer concentration is also a swing factor” and noted that a quantified top-customer disclosure would be new information. It cited Q1 $1M+ customer ARR growth of 179%.

surprises.description: The inference engine had attracted more than 6,000 customers since its late-April launch, while inference services grew nearly 800% year over year. The preview expected strong AI ARR and an inference-heavy mix, but did not anticipate this specific launch adoption and service growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inference services grew nearly 800% year-over-year” and the “inference engine” attracted “over 6,000 customers since its late-April launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on AI ARR of “$230–260M” and whether “the inference-weighted mix holds”; it did not state an expectation for inference-engine customer adoption.

surprises.description: DigitalOcean said it had recently raised list prices on numerous GPU fleets by approximately 30%, a pricing action the preview did not anticipate. The call also said pricing had very little impact on the record incremental ARR figure, so the reported ARR acceleration was not primarily price-driven.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company recently raised list prices on numerous GPU fleets by approximately 30%”; management noted pricing “had very little impact” on the $93 million of incremental ARR.

surprises.description: The company said it will no longer highlight net dollar retention as a key metric, despite reporting Q2 NDR of 102%. The preview did not anticipate this change in metric disclosure, so its implications are unclear.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company stated it “will no longer highlight net dollar retention (102% in Q2) as a key metric.”

in_line: Revenue was $281 million, within the preview’s $279–282 million base-case range and consistent with its pre-announcement framing of approximately 29% year-over-year growth, despite being above the high end of company guidance.
AI customer ARR was $234 million, within the preview’s $230–260 million range; 85% came from inference services and core cloud, consistent with the expected inference-weighted mix.

The raised FY2026 revenue guide of $1.17–1.18 billion, Q4 exit growth of 35% or more, and reiterated confidence in 50%+ growth for 2027 were in line with the preview’s expected guide raise, 35% exit-growth scenario, and >$1.7 billion / 50%+ 2027 framework.
Committed capacity of approximately 155 megawatts was already reflected in the preview, which noted the July 20-megawatt signing and approximately 155 megawatts of capacity.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.21, well above the preview’s $0.09–$0.10 consensus range. EBITDA also rose 27% to $7.7 million, alongside the earnings beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS more than doubled to $0.21”; “EBITDA up 27% to $7.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 consensus” diluted EPS of “$0.10 (MarketBeat) / $0.09 (Zacks).”

surprises.description: Revenue was $148 million, above the preview’s roughly $143 million consensus and its implied slight year-over-year decline. The reported 3% growth was a clear upside to that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated Q2 2026 revenue rose 3% year-over-year to $148 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue” consensus of “$142.9M (MarketBeat) / $143.4M (Zacks),” implying “-0.5% to -0.8% Y/Y.”

surprises.description: Branded Products grew substantially rather than landing roughly flat after Q1’s pull-forward: revenue was $98 million, up 6%, versus the preview’s implied $92–93 million. Its gross margin also expanded nearly a point, helping segment EBITDA rise 25%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Branded Products… grew revenue 6% to $98 million with gross margin expanding nearly a full point to 36.5%, driving a 25% increase in segment EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 pulled revenue forward out of this quarter,” and consensus implied Branded Products would be “roughly flat at ~$92–93M.”

surprises.description: Contact Centers still declined 4% year over year, rather than showing the Q2 growth the preview identified as a test of the back-half growth outlook. The second consecutive sequential improvement and management’s expectation that onboarding costs reverse in the back half temper the miss, but do not change the year-over-year decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Contact Centers revenue declined 4% year-over-year to $23 million but improved sequentially for the second consecutive quarter”; gross margin fell 170 basis points due to onboarding investments “management expects to reverse in the back half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Contact Centers were “guiding to back-half growth” and that “Q2 growth is the credibility test for the H2 guide.”

surprises.description: Healthcare Apparel remained under pressure: revenue fell 4% and gross margin dropped 260 basis points, while management said pressure would continue through the rest of 2026 and improvement was not anticipated until 2027. That is weaker and more prolonged than the preview’s open question of whether the segment had stabilized.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Healthcare Apparel revenue fell 4% to $27 million with gross margin down 260 basis points to 32.9%”; management expects “continued Healthcare Apparel margin pressure through the balance of 2026,” with improvements anticipated in 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “whether Healthcare Apparel mix has stabilized” as a key question and identified it as a source of gross-margin pressure.

surprises.description: A $2.6 million noncash inventory write-down weighed on Healthcare Apparel’s gross margin, a specific charge the preview had not identified. A $1.8 million net tariff refund benefit partly offset it; the preview had flagged tariff refunds as a possible one-time boost, not this offsetting combination.
surprises.fact_evidence: Healthcare Apparel gross margin was “hurt by a $2.6 million noncash inventory write-down partially offset by a $1.8 million net tariff refund benefit.”

surprises.description: The company recognized a separate $2.6 million noncash trade name impairment in Healthcare Apparel, reducing GAAP net income to $1.2 million, or $0.08 per diluted share. The preview did not anticipate this charge; it did not affect cash or operating cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A pretax noncash trade name impairment of $2.6 million ($2 million net of tax, or $0.13 per diluted share) was recognized in the Healthcare Apparel segment”; GAAP net income was “$1.2 million or $0.08 per diluted share.”

surprises.description: Management gave a more concrete near-term expansion signal than the preview’s general expectation of M&A commentary: a Contact Center acquisition or a Philippines call center startup is likely this year. The preview did not specify a likely transaction or startup timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management signaled “a Contact Center acquisition or Philippines call center startup is likely this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “M&A commentary” among the narrative items to watch.

in_line: Management reaffirmed the FY2026 net sales guidance of $572–$585 million and adjusted diluted EPS guidance of $0.54–$0.66, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the range would be reaffirmed or narrowed.

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin was 30.6%, below the preview’s expected 32–33% and below its stated 31% bear-trigger level. This fell short of the margin needed to support the preview’s expected second-half profitability bridge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin was 30.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs about 32–33% to make the EBITDA guide”; “A print below 31% breaks the 2H bridge regardless of revenue.”

surprises.description: Q3 guidance implies only 8% adjusted EBITDA growth at the midpoint, a marked slowdown from Q2’s 28% growth. The preview said the FY midpoint required about 23% adjusted EBITDA margin in the second half; Q3’s midpoint guidance implies a margin below that level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $150-170 million (18% growth at midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA of $32-37 million (only 8% growth at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The FY midpoint (20.2% on $620M) requires about 23% in 2H26 on roughly $319M of revenue.”

surprises.description: BLAO rose to a company-record $801 million, up about 5.7% sequentially from the preview’s cited $758 million Q1 level, rather than being flat or down. About $700 million has planned delivery dates in the next four quarters, adding near-term delivery visibility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New orders of approximately $207 million produced a 1.3 book-to-bill ratio, lifting backlog and awarded orders (BLAO) to a company-record $801 million”; “Approximately $700 million of BLAO has planned delivery dates in the next four quarters through Q2 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sequential growth is slowing while revenue accelerates. Flat-to-down q/q BLAO is the bear trigger.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $163 million modestly exceeded the roughly $160 million consensus, though it remained within the company’s guided range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $163 million, up 47% year-over-year and within the guided range.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $31.6 million, above the roughly $30 million consensus, although still within the $28–33 million guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew ~28% year-over-year to $31.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$30M (guide midpoint) | $28–33M.”

surprises.description: Net debt increased to $181.1 million and the company temporarily expanded its revolver by $50 million amid heavy first-half inventory investment. The preview flagged inventory and the need for a large second-half cash-flow reversal, but did not anticipate this additional borrowing and leverage detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt rose to $181.1 million with leverage at 1.6x adjusted EBITDA, and the company temporarily expanded its revolving credit facility by $50 million amid heavy first-half inventory investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating cash flow burn of $41.4M on inventory build”; “FY guide needs $65–85M of OCF, implying a large 2H reversal of Q1's burn.”

surprises.description: The TerraFlow MOU, which the preview described as unquantified, was sized at up to 5 GW annually, with revenue expected to begin in 2027. That gave investors a more concrete scale and timing for the opportunity than the preview had.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A TerraFlow MOU supporting up to 5 GW annually (revenue starting in 2027).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Aug 3 TerraFlow MOU (vanadium flow, up to 5 GW/yr) is unquantified, so expect sizing questions on the call.”

surprises.description: Shoals reported that it prevailed in its 2025 ITC case against Voltage, with the damages trial expected to conclude in Q3 and related legal expenses expected to fall away in Q4. The preview did not flag this litigation outcome or the prospective expense reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Shoals prevailed in its 2025 ITC case against Voltage, with the district court damages trial expected to conclude in Q3 2026, after which related legal expenses should fall away in Q4.”

surprises.description: The Air Link data-center product was described as differentiated and expected to command premium margins. The preview had discussed data-center content sizing, but did not mention a premium-margin opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The differentiated Air Link data-center product expected to command premium margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AI data center content framed at $50–60M per GW.”

in_line: Full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed, as the preview identified reaffirmation as the base case.
International BLAO was $102 million, broadly in line with the preview’s approximately $100 million estimate.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $4.37, well above the preview’s $3.77 consensus and far stronger than the roughly 6.8% year-over-year growth implied by consensus. It rose 24% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $4.37, up 24% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS (Q2) … $3.77”; “Implies about +6.8% YoY vs. $3.53.”

surprises.description: Revenue was about $1.7 billion, above the preview’s roughly $1.659 billion consensus, and grew 3% as reported rather than declining as the preview’s comparison implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $1.7 billion, up 3% year-over-year as reported and 2% FX neutral.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue (Q2) … ~$1.659B”; “Implies about −2.4% YoY vs. ~$1.70B in Q2 FY25.”

surprises.description: FY26 guidance was raised as expected, but the new floors were stronger than the preview’s prior guidance and consensus: EPS is at least $14 versus a $13.61 consensus, EBITDA at least $1.57 billion versus $1.545 billion, and free cash flow at least $1.185 billion versus $1.160 billion.
