surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was raised, with EBITDA now at or above $1.57 billion (up $40 million operationally), adjusted EPS at or above $14, and free cash flow at or above $1.185 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA ≥$1.545B”; “FY26 adj. EPS ≥$13.25 … Consensus $13.61”; “Other FY26 guidance: FCF ≥$1.160B.” The preview also said EPS, EBITDA, and FCF “are likely to be raised again.”

surprises.description: Conferences grew about 12% FX neutral, well ahead of the preview’s expected 3.5% growth, making the segment’s contribution much stronger than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Conferences revenue grew about 12% FX neutral to $244 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Conferences. Expected +3.5% YoY, the one segment growing clearly.”

surprises.description: Contract-value growth missed the preview’s key thresholds: total CV grew 2% against a bar of at least 3%, while ex-U.S. federal CV grew 3.3% against a bar of at least 3.5%. Growth did accelerate for a second consecutive quarter, but remained below those expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total contract value reached $5.3 billion, growing 2% year-over-year—a second consecutive quarter of acceleration and a 70-basis-point improvement from Q1—while ex-U.S. federal CV grew 3.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The bar is total CV at or above 3% and ex-Federal at or above 3.5%.”

surprises.description: Retention commentary was better than the preview’s prior-quarter baseline for GBS: wallet retention rose to 99% from 98%, and management said downsell activity was stabilizing and in-quarter retention rates were rising. GTS retention held at 97%, or 99% excluding federal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GTS retention improved to 97% (99% ex-Fed) and GBS wallet retention was 99%, with downsell activity stabilizing and in-quarter retention rates rising as leading indicators of future growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GTS 97% (99% ex-Federal), GBS 98%”; “Holding blended retention at or above 97.5% is the main evidence against the view that AI tools are replacing research subscriptions.”

surprises.description: Consulting’s forward indicators improved despite the preview’s concern about the segment’s reduced revenue outlook: bookings rose 17% and backlog grew 9% year over year, the first backlog increase since Q1 2025. The call also reported revenue of $142 million, but the preview gave no quarterly revenue expectation for comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consulting revenue declined to $142 million but bookings rose 17% and backlog grew 9% year-over-year for the first increase since Q1 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consulting revenue ≥$510M (cut $60M at Q1).”

surprises.description: New-business trends were mixed rather than uniformly improving: GTS turned positive year over year, but GBS new business fell further, even as total new-business dollars rose sequentially. The preview had highlighted weak Q1 new business and the prospect of an inflection, but did not forecast this divergence between the two businesses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GTS new business rose 2% year-over-year while GBS new business fell 5%, though total new business dollars increased about 10% sequentially to roughly $240 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GTS new business −4% YoY, GBS −2%”; the bull scenario anticipated management saying “new business has inflected.”

surprises.description: Management described a split in client conditions: midsized enterprises had mid-single-digit CV growth and found AI adoption easier, while larger, more global enterprises faced greater budget pressure and uncertainty. The preview did not anticipate this contrast by client size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Midsized enterprise clients delivered mid-single-digit CV growth as their lower complexity enabled easier AI adoption, whereas larger, more global enterprises faced greater budget pressure and uncertainty.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed its commitment to adjusted EPS growth above 12% compounded annually over the next three years, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the commitment would hold unless the outlook softened.
The preview expected EPS, EBITDA, and free cash flow guidance to be raised; all three were raised. The stronger-than-expected new guidance levels are captured above.
The preview expected the federal headwind to be largely lapped in Q2; the call said the federal business was providing a significant tailwind as the company lapped prior headwinds.

surprises.description: Leidos reported Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $3.26, well above the preview's $2.90–$2.91 consensus range. The gap was about 12% relative to consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS of $3.26.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS | $2.90–$2.91.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $4.6 billion, above the preview's $4.435 billion consensus by about 3.7%. This was stronger than the expected 4.5% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 7% year-over-year (4% organically) to a record $4.6 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $4.435B”; the preview described this as “+4.5%” year over year.

surprises.description: Leidos raised its 2026 revenue and EPS guidance rather than reaffirming it, the preview's base case. The midpoint increases were $100 million for revenue and $0.05 for EPS, with larger increases at the lower ends of the ranges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised the midpoint of 2026 revenue guidance by $100 million, EPS guidance by $0.05, and lifted the lower ends of ranges (revenue +$200 million, EPS +$0.10).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance action. Reaffirm is the base case. A raise would be a strong signal”; the base scenario said “FY guide reaffirmed or narrowed.”

surprises.description: The VA suspended incentive payments for all medical disability exam vendors through the rest of 2026, an unexpected headwind. Leidos said it had incorporated the suspension into its raised guidance and expects the Q4 run-rate to be the 2027 baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The VA suspended incentive payments for all medical disability exam vendors for the remainder of 2026, a headwind that is fully incorporated into the raised guidance, with Q4 run-rate expected to be the baseline for 2027.”

surprises.description: The preview expected only about 0.5–1% organic growth in consensus, but Leidos reported 4% Q2 organic growth and forecast approximately 7% organic revenue growth for the rest of the company in 2026, excluding health-related BVA changes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 7% year-over-year (4% organically)” and “Excluding the health-related BVA changes, the rest of Leidos is expected to grow approximately 7% organically in revenue and 19% in adjusted EBITDA in 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “That implies consensus models organic growth of only about 0.5–1%.”

surprises.description: Defense bookings were much stronger than the preview's roughly 1.0–1.1x expectation for company-wide book-to-bill: Defense posted 2.2x in Q2 and 1.9x on a trailing-twelve-month basis. Management also forecast high-single-digit Defense growth for the year, or double digits excluding the transitioning airborne ISR business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Defense posted a 2.2 book-to-bill in Q2 (1.9 trailing-twelve-months) and is expected to grow high-single-digits for the year, or double digits excluding the transitioning airborne ISR business”; the company also cited “a $12 billion defense-tech pipeline expected over the next 12 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected book-to-bill of “about 1.0–1.1x” and warned that “a second straight sub-1.0x quarter would undercut management's claim that awards ‘pick up significantly’ through the year.”

surprises.description: Health revenue contracted as a fourth vendor was fully incorporated into the VBA contract, a revenue decline not called out in the preview. Management expected Health revenue to remain around Q2 levels for the rest of the year, with non-GAAP operating margins near 20%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Health segment revenue contracted due to a fourth vendor being fully incorporated into the VBA contract, but is expected to sustain around Q2 levels for the rest of the year with non-GAAP OI margins near 20%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on whether Health would hold its “20%” margin floor and described the base case as “Health in the low 20s”; it did not flag this revenue contraction.

surprises.description: Cash generation was especially strong: Q2 operating cash flow and free cash flow set company records for the quarter, and full-year operating cash flow guidance increased while CapEx expectations fell. The preview had described the approximately $1.80 billion operating cash flow target as weighted to the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company generated a Q2-record $793 million in operating cash flow and $761 million in free cash flow, and raised full-year operating cash flow guidance by $50 million while cutting CapEx expectations to roughly $250 million”; free cash flow guidance was “up about $150 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 operating cash flow: about $1.80B” and “Free cash flow $270M, against the roughly $1.80B full-year operating cash flow target, which is weighted to the second half.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted buyback pace as a signal that management viewed the sell-off as overdone. Leidos completed its prior authorization with a $66 million buyback but approved a new authorization of only $20 million, while also saying its valuation was at multiyear lows.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Leidos completed its 2022 share repurchase authorization with a $66 million buyback and the Board approved a new $20 million … repurchase authorization, with management noting the valuation is at multiyear lows and M&A targets are currently expensive.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Buyback pace” and said “Repurchases at about 9.5x earnings would signal management sees the sell-off as overdone.”

in_line: Company-wide net awards produced a 1.1 book-to-bill, within the preview's expected range of about 1.0–1.1x.
Leidos paid down the remaining $300 million of Entrust-related commercial paper, consistent with the preview's note that management planned to retire $300 million of commercial paper in 2026.

surprises.description: Q2 IMCIVREE sales were $71.3 million versus the preview’s roughly $67.3 million estimate. U.S. sales of $51 million were also well above the preview’s $41–43 million estimate, driving a much stronger U.S. reacceleration than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global net product sales of IMCIVREE reached $71.3 million in Q2 2026, up 19% sequentially, with $51 million (72%) generated in the U.S.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “IMCIVREE net product revenue … ~$67.3M”; “The full preview's Q2 US estimate is about $41–43M.”

surprises.description: The acquired-HO launch had greater reach than the preview’s early-launch figures suggested: Rhythm reported more than 400 start forms and approximately 300 unique prescribers in 14 weeks, versus more than 150 forms and about 110 prescribers in the first six weeks. It also disclosed 66 clinical-trial patient conversions, but did not say how many patients had converted to paid or reimbursed therapy.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In the first 14 weeks since March 19 approval, Rhythm received more than 400 start forms from approximately 300 unique prescribers for acquired hypothalamic obesity, including 66 converted clinical trial patients.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “More than 150 start forms in the first six weeks after the March 19, 2026 approval, about 40 of them clinical-trial conversions”; watch for “a paid/reimbursed conversion count and prescriber depth” (Q1: about 110 unique prescribers).

surprises.description: HO-specific coverage policies had already reached 25% of Medicaid and 35% of commercial covered lives by quarter-end, with no GLP-1 step edits. That is concrete progress by the early end of the preview’s expected June–December policy window.
surprises.fact_evidence: “By the end of Q2, HO-specific positive coverage policies were secured for approximately 25% of Medicaid and 35% of commercial covered lives, with no GLP-1 step edits required.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided 3–9 months from approval for HO-specific policies, meaning June through December 2026. Movement toward the near end is a bull signal.”

surprises.description: RM-718’s week-16 mean BMI reduction of 11.6% exceeded the 10.1% figures cited for setmelanotide and bivamelagon, making the result more differentiated than the preview’s base case of solid but not differentiated data. No generalized hyperpigmentation was observed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RM-718, the weekly MC4R agonist, delivered a mean BMI reduction of 11.6% at week 16 in HO patients, favorably comparable to setmelanotide (10.1%) and bivamelagon (10.1%), with no generalized hyperpigmentation observed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “RM-718 solid but not differentiated” in the base case; the preview also flagged BMI reduction and tolerability, including hyperpigmentation, as key things to watch.

surprises.description: The small RM-718 Phase II trial had two early adverse-event discontinuations among 11 patients, including uncontrolled nausea. This is a tolerability concern not reflected in the preview’s base-case expectation of solid data, although tolerability was identified as a key debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In the RM-718 Phase II trial, 2 of 11 enrolled patients discontinued due to adverse events (injection site reactions and uncontrolled nausea) within the first 4 weeks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “tolerability (hyperpigmentation, nausea)” and described its base case as “RM-718 solid but not differentiated.”

surprises.description: GAAP loss per share was narrower than the preview’s consensus estimate: $0.73 versus an expected loss of $0.82 per share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss per share was $0.73 for Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP) … Consensus (Q2 2026) $(0.82).”

surprises.description: International revenue fell to $20.3 million from $23.2 million in Q1, below the roughly $24–26 million implied by the preview’s total-revenue estimate and U.S. estimate. The decline included a $3.8 million retrospective French contribution charge, $2.3 million of which related to 2025 revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International revenue declined to $20.3 million from $23.2 million, primarily due to a $3.8 million retrospective French contribution charge, of which $2.3 million related to 2025 revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated total Q2 revenue of “~$67.3M” and U.S. revenue of “about $41–43M”; those figures imply roughly $24–26 million from outside the U.S.

surprises.description: Rhythm reduced the midpoint of full-year non-GAAP R&D expense guidance by $20 million, citing CMC work shifted from late 2026 to early 2027. The company said this shift would not affect clinical timelines, so the reduction was not presented as a delay to the clinical program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rhythm reduced the midpoint of its full-year non-GAAP R&D expense guidance by $20 million (to $175-195 million) as certain RM-718 and bivamelagon CMC activities shifted from late 2026 to early 2027, without affecting clinical timelines.”

surprises.description: The call gave a specific Japan approval and launch target of Q4 2026 and a Germany launch target in the first half of 2027, providing more concrete timing and European launch detail than the preview had available.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Japan approval and commercial launch for acquired HO are anticipated by Q4 2026, with European country launches beginning in Germany in the first half of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Bivamelagon Phase 3 design and Japan approval timing” as a catalyst and said a “firm Japan timeline” would support the 2027 narrative; it gave no specific Japan or Europe launch dates.

in_line: The company reiterated a cash runway of at least 24 months, consistent with the prior-quarter runway cited in the preview.

surprises.description: Strata raised 2026 revenue guidance to $285–295 million from $260–275 million, above the preview’s $275.8 million consensus; it also raised adjusted EBITDA guidance to $33–35 million from $29–33 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Strata raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $285-295 million from $260-275 million previously, and increased adjusted EBITDA guidance to $33-35 million from $29-33 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue consensus | $275.8M”; “FY26 revenue guidance | $260–275M”; “FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance | $29–33M.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $72.5 million, above the preview’s $68–70 million management framework. The preview had also framed roughly $72 million as the bull-case level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue grew 60.7% year-over-year to $72.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue (mgmt framework) | ~$68–70M”; the bull scenario listed “Revenue | ~$72M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $7.9 million, exceeding the preview’s roughly $6.8–7.0 million expectation; the 10.9% margin also topped the expected roughly 10%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $7.9 million in Q2 2026 from $6.4 million in Q1, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 140 basis points to 10.9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 adj. EBITDA margin (mgmt) | ~10%, or ~$6.8–7.0M”; the key metric was “Adj. EBITDA vs. ~$7.0M.”

surprises.description: Clinical revenue rose to $24.3 million, well above the preview’s roughly $21 million framework. Growth remained substantial even excluding acquisitions, and transplant clinical revenue grew 23.8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Clinical revenue rose 22.6% sequentially to $24.3 million (15.1% excluding Q2 acquisitions), led by 23.8% growth in transplant clinical revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s logistics-growth analysis assumed “Clinical growing to ~$21M”; it also flagged “Transplant Clinical growth” as a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: Logistics gross margin missed the expected return to 20% or more: it was 18.4% in Q2. Management now expects only 18.5–20% in the second half and a return to 20% in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Logistics gross margin fell to 18.4% in Q2 2026 versus 19.3% in Q1 and a 20% expectation, with management guiding to 18.5-20% for the second half and a return to 20% in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided margins to “remain in the 20% range” for the rest of 2026 and called for “Logistics gross margin ≥ 20%.”

surprises.description: Instead of logistics being roughly flat as the preview inferred, management disclosed a customer-related headwind and expects Q3 logistics revenue to fall high single digits sequentially. The roughly 3% revenue headwind from the customer is expected to fully hit in Q3 before recovering by Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Logistics faces a roughly 3% revenue headwind from one nonexclusive customer that reduced flying for one organ type starting in June, expected to fully hit in Q3 before recovering by Q4”; “Q3 logistics revenue [is expected] to decline high single digits sequentially due to the customer headwind and summer seasonality.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview inferred that “Logistics [would be] roughly flat at ~$48M sequentially” and described management’s Q2 total-revenue framework as “low single digits” sequential growth.

surprises.description: The shift toward higher-margin clinical is expected to be much more pronounced than the preview quantified: clinical is projected to account for roughly 40% of second-half revenue and nearly 50% of gross profit, versus 30% and 35% in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The business mix is shifting toward higher-margin clinical, expected to reach roughly 40% of revenue and nearly 50% of gross profit in the second half, up from 30% and 35% respectively in Q1 2026.”

surprises.description: Strata had already completed three bolt-on clinical acquisitions year-to-date, adding over $20 million of revenue and $6.3 million of projected annualized adjusted EBITDA at mid-single-digit multiples; the preview only flagged tuck-in M&A as something to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed three bolt-on clinical acquisitions year-to-date at mid-single-digit multiples, adding over $20 million of revenue and $6.3 million of projected annualized adjusted EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s capital-deployment item said, “Watch for tuck-in M&A.”

surprises.description: Trex guided Q3 sales to $305–320 million, above the preview’s base-case range of about $285–300 million and its stated Q3 catalyst range. The low end is only slightly above the base-case ceiling, but the high end is a meaningful upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 net sales are guided to $305 million to $320 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Q3 ~$285–300M”; its catalyst checklist cited the “~$285–300M range.”

surprises.description: Trex raised its full-year adjusted gross margin outlook to approximately 38%, rather than keeping the previously stated 37.5% level. That is a favorable half-point improvement over the preview’s expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 adjusted gross margin guidance was raised to approximately 38% from 37.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the July guidance had “not restated the ~37.5% FY adj. GM guide” and listed the base case as “GM held near 37.5%.”

surprises.description: Despite the stronger sales outlook, adjusted EPS was $0.62, two cents below the $0.64 consensus. The call said a $5 million noncash obsolete-equipment write-down reduced adjusted diluted EPS by $0.03.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.62,” including “a $0.03 negative impact from a $5 million noncash write-down for obsolete equipment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Adj. EPS $0.64.”

surprises.description: Management indicated that the Q3 sales outlook implies flat-to-down year-over-year revenue in Q4, citing geopolitical uncertainty. That is more cautious than the preview’s expectation that H2 would outperform H1, although the preview did not give a specific Q4 estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The implied Q4 outlook suggest[s] flat-to-down year-over-year revenue,” which management attributed to “conservatism amid geopolitical uncertainty.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management expected “H2 to outperform H1.”

surprises.description: Trex reported more than 100 basis points of temporary manufacturing inefficiencies as production ramped, alongside a 37.9% gross margin. The preview had identified Arkansas depreciation and railing mix as margin headwinds, but did not flag these additional ramp-related inefficiencies.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 37.9%,” including “over 100 basis points of temporary manufacturing inefficiencies from rapidly ramping production.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “about 250 bps” of annual headwinds, including “170–180 bps from Arkansas depreciation and 70–80 bps from railing mix,” and gave a base case of gross margin “held near 37.5%.”

surprises.description: Railing returned to double-digit sales growth and entry-level Trex Enhanced products had their first meaningful sales increase in years. This was a more encouraging demand signal than the preview’s framing of railing mainly as a near-term mix drag, while the sell-in versus sell-through question remained open.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Railing sales returned to double-digit growth” and Trex Enhanced basic products “posted their first meaningful sales increase in years, signaling the entry-level consumer's return.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described railing as “a mix drag” near term and called separating “real demand from restocking” central to the call.

surprises.description: Trex said the Little Rock ramp-up had been accelerated by more than six months, with roughly half the lines expected to be producing by year-end. The preview discussed Arkansas depreciation but did not anticipate this faster ramp; the company said most margin benefits would still come in 2027 and beyond.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Little Rock facility ramp-up was accelerated by over six months,” with “roughly 50% of lines expected in production by year-end” and “most margin benefits realized in 2027 and beyond.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Arkansas depreciation as a margin headwind but did not state an expectation for an accelerated ramp or a year-end production milestone.

surprises.description: Trex planned up to an additional $150 million of repurchases for the rest of 2026, on top of about $51 million bought back in Q2. The preview noted the existing $150 million commitment and raised the possibility of a new authorization, but did not anticipate this additional amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to repurchase up to an additional $150 million of shares during the remainder of 2026,” after buying back “approximately $51 million in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “$150M of buybacks, including a $100M ASR, was committed in H1” and advised investors to “Watch for a new buyback authorization.”

in_line: Q2 net sales were $418 million, essentially matching the preview’s $418.1 million consensus and the pre-announced figure.
Adjusted EBITDA was $112 million, in line with the approximately $112 million figure already disclosed before the release.

surprises.description: Wayfair reported 7.5% revenue growth, above the preview’s 6–7% base case and the growth implied by its $3.46 billion consensus estimate. The result was a modest upside to the expected pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenue grew 7.5% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario was “Revenue $3.46–3.50B (+6–7%)”; its consensus estimate was “$3.46B.”

surprises.description: The U.S. category was expected to be down mid-single digits, but management reported flat-to-slightly-positive U.S. category growth. That was the first such growth since 2021, a materially better market backdrop than the preview described.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 marked the first quarter of flat-to-slightly-positive year-over-year U.S. category growth since 2021.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Management framed Q2 as a category down mid-single digits.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for a second consecutive quarter of active-customer growth; Wayfair delivered growth of more than 3%, up from 1.4% in Q1. Orders also rose 6% year over year and more than 12% sequentially, the strongest Q2 sequential increase since 2020, while AOV rose 1.2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Orders rose 6% year-over-year and over 12% sequentially versus Q1—the strongest Q2 sequential order growth since 2020—while AOV grew 1.2% and active customers rose more than 3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “A second straight quarter of [active customer] growth would turn one datapoint into a trend.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached the top of the company’s $208–242 million guidance range, with a 6.9% margin versus the preview’s 6.5% base case. That was better than the base expectation, though just below the preview’s 7% bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $242 million at a 6.9% margin, the best margin since 2021.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case assumed “EBITDA ~6.5%”; its bull case called for “EBITDA margin ≥7%.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow was not merely positive after Q1’s –$106 million: it reached $301 million, more than 30% above the year-earlier quarter. That substantially exceeded the preview’s stated need for a return to positive cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow reached $301 million … up more than 30% year-over-year and the best quarterly cash generation since Q2 2020.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “A return to positive FCF is needed after –$106M in Q1” and identified “FCF still negative” as a bear-case risk.

surprises.description: Wayfair’s U.S. business grew 8.7%, its best post-COVID performance, while International revenue declined 1.3% on weakness in Canada and the U.K. The preview focused on overall share spread and did not flag this pronounced geographic split.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The U.S. segment [accelerated] to 8.7% growth (its best post-COVID performance) while International declined 1.3% due to weakness in Canada and the U.K.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed “Revenue growth and share spread,” saying management expected its share spread to hold “at high single digits”; it gave no geographic segment expectation.

surprises.description: Specialty retail brands grew nearly 20% and Perigold more than 35%, far faster than the core Wayfair business; Perigold also outgrew a low-single-digit luxury market. The preview did not identify this brand-level outperformance as an expected driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Specialty retail brands grew nearly 20% and Perigold grew more than 35% in Q2, both meaningfully outpacing the core mass Wayfair business”; Perigold grew double digits while the “broader luxury home market grew low single digits.”

surprises.description: Management guided to high-single-digit Q3 revenue growth, above the preview’s mid-single-digit-or-better threshold. The preview had noted the company’s historical mid-single-digit guidance, so the higher indicated pace was an upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 to high single-digit revenue growth—above its historic mid-single-digit guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “The buy-side wants mid-single-digit-or-better revenue growth” and described historical guidance as “Mid-single-digit growth.”

surprises.description: The store plans went beyond the preview’s two named 2026 openings: Wayfair now expects three large-format openings in 2026 and has signed five leases for 2027. The reported customer reach and supplier-owned inventory also provided new store-economics detail the preview said would be new information.
surprises.fact_evidence: “3 large-format stores opening in 2026 and 5 leases signed for 2027,” with “over 50% of store customers” new to the file and supplier-owned inventory keeping combined CapEx in the low-single-digit percentage of revenue.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Store openings in Columbus (summer) and Denver (November) are planned” and that “Any store-level economics would be new information.”

surprises.description: Wayfair reported a $400 million high-yield note issuance to redeem its 2028 converts, a two-notch Fitch upgrade, and stock-based compensation about 40% below its level two years ago. These financing, credit-rating, and compensation developments were not anticipated in the preview; the debt replacement itself is not clearly a net balance-sheet improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Completed its shift away from convertible debt by issuing a $400 million high-yield note to redeem 2028 converts,” “earned a 2-notch Fitch upgrade,” and “cut trailing-12-month stock-based compensation ~40% versus two years ago.”

in_line: The Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin guide of 6–7% met the preview’s expectation of no step-down in EBITDA margin.

surprises.description: AdaptHealth cut full-year continuing-operations adjusted EBITDA guidance to $490–520 million from $680–730 million, a much steeper reduction than the preview’s already-cautious discussion of a recast after the Diabetes Health sale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “slashed full-year continuing operations adjusted EBITDA guidance to $490-520 million from a prior $680-730 million,” driven by the divestiture, capitated contract issues, and a supplier price hike.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$680–730M” and said management had deferred comprehensive guidance updates until the call.

surprises.description: Q2 continuing-operations revenue was far below the preview’s $840–860 million company guide and $848.6 million consensus, despite double-digit year-over-year growth. Most of the organic growth came from the West Coast capitated contract rather than the base business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenue from continuing operations was $740.3 million,” with 15.9% organic growth, “though the West Coast capitated contract contributed 10.7 of those organic growth points versus only 5.2 points from the base business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 revenue consensus of “$848.6M” and company guidance of “$840–860M.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA and margin came in well below the preview’s roughly $160 million and 19% expectation. Management attributed the pressure to elevated West Coast capitated-contract costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin compressed to 17.8% ($132.0 million) from $136.4 million a year earlier due to elevated West Coast capitated contract costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected Q2 adjusted EBITDA of “~$160M” and cited company guidance of “~19% margin, ~$160–163M.”

surprises.description: The West Coast capitated contract was weaker and more costly than the preview anticipated: it underperformed in Q2, is expected to weigh further on the second half, and is not expected to reach run-rate profitability until next year.
surprises.fact_evidence: The contract “underperformed by $15 million in Q2 and is expected to cost an additional $40 million in the second half,” with run-rate profitability expected “next year,” though management still targets a 20% long-term margin.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 guidance was about a 19% margin, with “labor normalization promised by quarter-end,” and described the H2 EBITDA requirement to reach the unrevised annual guide.

surprises.description: A manufacturer’s contract termination and immediate price increase create a substantial new second-half cost, with no mitigation secured yet—an additional headwind not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A major manufacturer terminated its contract and imposed an immediate price increase effective July 1, creating a $30 million second-half impact that is currently fully reflected in guidance with no mitigation yet secured.”

surprises.description: The full-year free-cash-flow outlook was cut sharply, and Q2 cash flow was negative rather than merely modest. The preview had expected a heavily back-half-loaded year, including roughly $100 million in each of Q3 and Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was negative $20.9 million in Q2” on $166.2 million of capex, including about $25 million of one-time purchases; full-year free cash flow is now guided to “$80-120 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 FCF guidance of “$175–225M” and said the CFO had flagged Q2 FCF as “modest” with “about $100M each in Q3 and Q4.”

surprises.description: The Diabetes Health sale leaves a sizable amount of corporate overhead in continuing operations, and management expects to remove only about half of it within 12 months of closing. The preview flagged stranded costs as an issue but did not indicate this scale or slow removal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Diabetes Health divestiture leaves roughly $60 million of stranded corporate overhead in continuing operations, of which only about half is expected to be removed within 12 months of closing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to ask for “any stranded-cost disclosure” after the sale and the recast guidance.

surprises.description: The company recorded a large noncash goodwill impairment tied to reallocating costs around the diabetes divestiture; the preview did not anticipate a new impairment in this release.
surprises.fact_evidence: “recorded a $144.2 million noncash goodwill impairment tied to the diabetes divestiture cost reallocation.”

surprises.description: The new Humana OneHome agreement was consistent with the preview’s expectation that a capitated partnership might be announced, but its disclosed scale was substantial: 478,000 members and capitated revenue exceeding three times the prior year.
surprises.fact_evidence: AdaptHealth “signed a new Humana OneHome capitated agreement transitioning 478,000 members in South Florida and Texas,” expanding capitated revenue to “$103.3 million (about 14% of revenue), more than 3x the prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the CEO had teased a new partnership “soon” and that whether one was announced was “a key catalyst.”

surprises.description: AdaptHealth executed a $19 million annualized cost restructuring during Q2, an offsetting cost action not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company executed a $19 million annualized cost restructuring in Q2.”

in_line: A new capitated partnership was anticipated as a possible announcement: the preview noted that the CEO had teased one as “soon” and listed an announcement as a key catalyst.

surprises.description: Whirlpool reported Q2 ongoing EPS of negative $0.21, versus the preview’s positive $0.08 consensus. The result missed by $0.29 per share and turned an expected profit into a loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales were $3.5 billion with ongoing EPS of negative $0.21.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Ongoing EPS | $0.08”

surprises.description: Q2 net sales were $3.5 billion, below the preview’s $3.61 billion consensus by about 3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales were $3.5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $3.61B”

surprises.description: Whirlpool lowered full-year EPS guidance, attributing the reduction solely to higher interest expense, raised from $300 million to $350 million. The preview identified whether the $3.00–$3.50 EPS guide remained live as the key question, so this was weaker than the expected guide hold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year EPS guidance was lowered solely due to raised interest expense (from $300 million to $350 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “May 6, 2026 (current): Ongoing EPS $3.00–$3.50”; “Is the $3.00–$3.50 ongoing EPS guide still live?”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted the free-cash-flow commitment, but Q2 consumed about $1.1 billion, driven by lower earnings and seasonal working capital. Full-year guidance was maintained at $300 million, which is below the preview’s stated commitment of more than $300 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow in Q2 was a consumption of approximately $1.1 billion, driven by lower earnings and seasonal working capital, though full-year free cash flow guidance is maintained at $300 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow (FCF) against the >$300M commitment.”

surprises.description: Tariffs were a material cost headwind: the net impact was unfavorable by 200 basis points in Q2, with similar costs expected in Q3 and Q4. The preview flagged tariff and pricing effects but did not quantify a burden of this size or duration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net tariff impact was an unfavorable 200 basis points in Q2 driven by Section 232 implementation, and management expects similar tariff costs in Q3 and Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Tariff and pricing effects. The Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs… Section 232 and 301 measures remain. Whether competitor price cuts forced Whirlpool to give back announced increases is unclear.”

surprises.description: SDA Global had strong underlying demand, but a temporary trade-inventory burn tied to a late-quarter order depressed reported top-line results. That contrasts with the preview’s expectation of 12.7% sales growth, although the call facts do not give the actual sales figure or quantify any shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SDA Global delivered ~12% EBIT margin with underlying U.S. POS growth of 16% and high-teens global sell-through, but a temporary Q2 trade inventory burn from a late-quarter order depressed reported top-line results.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SDA Global sales | $226.5M | +12.7%”

surprises.description: Beyond the already flagged $150 million 2026 cost-takeout target, Whirlpool disclosed an additional $60 million annualized EBIT benefit from consolidating distribution centers, alongside footprint moves expected to benefit primarily in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company targets $150 million in cost takeout in 2026 (including ~$60 million from automation) plus additional footprint moves in Amana, Argentina, and Mexico that will primarily benefit 2027, with an added $60 million annualized EBIT benefit from consolidating distribution centers from 126 down to 90.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “On May 6, Whirlpool also committed to more than $150M of structural cost takeout in 2026.”

surprises.description: Whirlpool sold its minority stake in Beko Europe BV for about $128 million, resulting in roughly $84 million of net cash consideration. The preview did not flag this transaction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Whirlpool sold its minority stake in Beko Europe BV for approximately $128 million, generating roughly $84 million of net cash consideration.”

in_line: MDA North America sales were $2.4 billion, close to the preview’s $2.419 billion consensus; the segment’s margin recovery and Whirlpool’s 50-basis-point sequential overall EBIT-margin improvement were consistent with the preview’s focus on sequential margin recovery.

The operational outlook was reaffirmed at about 4% full-year EBIT margin and about 1.5% revenue growth, broadly consistent with the preview’s current guidance of approximately 4.0% EBIT margin and about $15.0 billion in net sales.

surprises.description: Waters reported $1.645 billion of Q2 revenue, above both the $1.6223 billion consensus and the $1.616–$1.631 billion company guide. The beat was modest, especially since the total includes the acquired businesses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total company as-reported revenue was $1.645 billion.”

surprises.description: Organic constant-currency growth reached 9%, about 100 basis points above the guide’s 8% high end. That was stronger than the preview’s roughly 7% consensus expectation despite a prior-year pull-forward headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Organic revenue grew 9% in constant currency, beating the high end of guidance by roughly 100 basis points despite absorbing a 1% headwind from prior-year pull-forward.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Organic CC growth | ~+7% | +6.0% to +8.0%.”

surprises.description: The acquired Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions businesses generated $817 million, above the preview’s roughly $802 million guide. They also returned to growth, at 4% reported and 6% excluding China, after flat growth in the prior quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$817 million from the acquired BD Biosciences and Diagnostic Solutions businesses”; “grew 4% reported (6% ex-China), a 400 basis point acceleration versus last quarter's flat growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Acquired-business revenue vs. the ~$802M guide”; “A second straight beat would support the turnaround narrative.”

surprises.description: Management raised the full-year organic growth range to 7%–9%, lifting the high end above 8%. The preview identified a raise above 8% as a bull-case trigger, rather than its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 organic constant currency growth guidance to 7%-9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 organic CC +6.5% to +8.0%”; “Bull: ... raises the high end of FY organic CC above 8%.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that a stronger U.S. dollar was consuming about $0.25 of EPS on the full-year outlook, a material headwind not identified in the preview’s FY EPS expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A stronger U.S. dollar consumed roughly $0.25 of EPS on the full-year outlook.”

surprises.description: Cost actions are now expected to deliver $75 million of 2026 savings versus the preview’s $55 million synergy target, with roughly $200 million of run-rate savings and a $50 million Q4 P&L benefit largely already in hand. The savings are also ahead of schedule.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cost actions are expected to yield $75 million in 2026 savings and approximately $200 million in run-rate savings ... ahead of schedule, with a $50 million Q4 P&L benefit largely already in hand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management targets $55M of cost synergies in 2026, with results beginning in Q3”; “Q2 is the quarter management must show the Q3 synergy ramp is real.”

surprises.description: GLP-1 testing revenue grew more than 40%, well ahead of the prior assumption of about a 30-basis-point contribution to company growth. The regional growth figures also show strength across the Americas, Europe, and India.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GLP-1 testing revenue grew over 40% in the quarter, with Americas up over 30%, Europe over 36%, and India nearly doubling, running well ahead of the prior ~30 basis point contribution assumption.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Empty; the preview did not discuss GLP-1 testing growth.

surprises.description: China microbiology declined only at a low-teens rate, much less than the modeled 30% decline. That made the result materially better than the expectation stated on the call.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China microbiology declined only low-teens versus a modeled 30% decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “China microbiology declined only low-teens versus a modeled 30% decline.”

surprises.description: China pharma grew at a double-digit rate in the first half and became accretive to growth. The preview did not identify that as an expected growth contributor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China pharma grew double digits in the first half (accelerating from 6% last year) and is now accretive to growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Empty; the preview discussed China Flow-cytometry localization, not China pharma growth.

surprises.description: Net price realization in the acquired businesses reached 90 basis points, above the historical 50-basis-point level. The preview did not flag this pricing progress.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net price realization in the acquired businesses reached 90 basis points in Q2, up from a historical 50 basis points, on the path toward a 150 basis point target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Empty; the preview did not discuss acquired-business net price realization.

surprises.description: Management described a pipeline of 76 U.S. pharma reshoring expansion sites, with about $100 billion of CapEx and roughly 70% tied to existing Waters accounts, as a potential Analytical Sciences tailwind from 2027 to 2030. The preview did not anticipate this quantified opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is tracking 76 U.S. pharma reshoring expansion sites (about half under construction, ~$100 billion CapEx) with roughly 70% tied to existing Waters accounts, expected to drive an Analytical Sciences tailwind from 2027 to 2030.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Empty; the preview did not discuss a quantified reshoring-site pipeline.

in_line: Adjusted EPS was $3.05, at the high end of the $2.95–$3.05 company guide; the preview’s base scenario anticipated $3.05–$3.13.

Full-year adjusted EPS guidance of $14.45–$14.65 was broadly in line with the preview’s base-case expectation of about $14.50–$14.65, although management also cited a $0.25-per-share currency headwind.

surprises.description: ADTRAN's non-GAAP gross margin was 40.7%, slightly below the preview's 41–42% base-case range. Management attributed the decline to supply constraints that limited shipments of higher-margin products.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin declined to 40.7%, down from 43% in Q1 2026 and 41.4% a year ago, driven by supply constraints limiting shipments of higher-margin products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: ... GM ~41–42%”; the preview also said a print “of 40% or below” would suggest structural erosion.

surprises.description: Enterprise, government and cloud revenue grew 47% year over year, while hyperscaler revenue surged 97%. The preview focused on optical growth and the delayed customer project but did not anticipate this scale of growth in these customer groups.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue from enterprise, government and cloud customers grew 47% year-over-year and 19% sequentially, reaching 25% of total company revenue”; “Hyperscaler revenue surged 97% year-over-year, driven by data center interconnect.”

surprises.description: Management quantified that reaching its 10% operating-margin target requires roughly $310–320 million of revenue and 42–43% gross margin. That revenue level is above Q2 revenue and the midpoint of Q3 guidance, and the required gross margin is well above Q2's result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management estimates reaching its 10% operating margin target requires revenue of roughly $310-320 million at 42-43% gross margin.”

surprises.description: The refinancing brought a specific financing benefit not detailed in the preview: borrowing costs fell by 200 basis points and the facility's maturity extends to 2031.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed a refinancing of its credit facility led by JPMorgan, reducing borrowing costs by 200 basis points and extending maturity to 2031.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that ADTRAN had closed a “$350M JPMorgan-led senior secured facility” and asked whether it was defensive liquidity or growth capital, but did not state the cost reduction or maturity.

in_line: Q2 revenue of $281.1 million was within the pre-announced $280–282 million range and close to the preview's operative consensus of $281.2 million.
Q2 non-GAAP operating margin of 3.8% was within the pre-announced 3.5–4.0% range.

Q3 revenue guidance of $275–295 million and non-GAAP operating-margin guidance of 1.5–5.5% matched the ranges already reported in the preview; the lack of a Q3 rebound in the delayed customer's orders was consistent with the preview's discussion of the delay and Q3 outlook.
Optical Networking Solutions remained a growth engine, consistent with the preview's expectation of continued optical growth and constructive optical commentary.

surprises.description: Q2 sales of $2.04 billion exceeded the preview's $1.96 billion consensus (and the alternate $2.0 billion estimate), while 10% organic growth was well above the roughly 6–7% expected. The organic result shows stronger underlying growth than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 sales reached a record $2.04 billion, up 15% year-over-year, with organic sales up 10% and acquisitions adding 5 points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $1.96B (Zacks; some sources say $2.0B)” and “Consensus implies roughly +6–7% organic after M&A and FX.”

surprises.description: EPS of $2.09 beat both the $1.99 consensus and the top of the $1.96–$2.00 guidance range, a larger result than the preview's base and bull scenarios anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS was a record $2.09, up 17% and above the guidance range of $1.96 to $2.00 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $1.99” and the bull scenario forecast “$2.05–2.08.”

surprises.description: AMETEK raised full-year EPS guidance to $8.20–$8.30, above the $8.13 consensus and stronger than the preview's most likely modest-raise scenario of about $8.05–$8.20. The new range reaches the preview's bull-case high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AMETEK raised full-year EPS guidance to $8.20-$8.30 (up 10-12%) from the prior $7.94-$8.14.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 Adj. EPS | $8.13” and the base scenario expected a raise “to ~$8.05–8.20”; the bull scenario expected “$8.15–8.30.”

surprises.description: Orders and backlog were stronger than the preview's threshold-based expectations: organic orders rose 25%, and backlog reached $4.1 billion versus the preview's watch level of about $3.9 billion. The 1.12 book-to-bill met the preview's expectation of at least 1.0.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Orders were a record $2.3 billion, up 28% overall and 25% organically, building record backlog of $4.1 billion (up 21% since year-end) with a book-to-bill of 1.12.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for at or above 1.0 and backlog near $3.9B.”

surprises.description: EMG delivered unusually strong results that the preview did not identify as a specific expected driver: organic sales grew 15%, organic orders grew 35%, and core margins expanded 290 basis points, with Paragon Medical's medtech strength leading.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EMG delivered exceptional results with 15% organic sales growth, 35% organic orders growth, and core margins up 290 basis points to 26.2%, led by Paragon Medical's medtech strength.”

surprises.description: Core margins expanded 110 basis points and incrementals were about 40%, above the preview's 35% incremental assumption. The margin expansion was within the preview's bull-case range of 100–150 basis points, so the surprise is mainly the stronger-than-assumed incrementals.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core operating margins expanded 110 basis points to 27.1%, driven by ~40% incrementals, positive price over inflation/tariffs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance assumes 35% incrementals” and the bull scenario expected “margin expansion of 100–150 bps.”

surprises.description: Management raised its productivity target to $160 million, an operational update the preview did not flag or quantify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core operating margins expanded 110 basis points to 27.1%, driven by ~40% incrementals, positive price over inflation/tariffs, and raised productivity target of $160 million.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that half of Indicor's revenue base is recurring, a favorable acquisition-quality detail not covered in the preview. The stated 10–12% cost-synergy range and second-half closing expectation, by contrast, were in line with the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The $5 billion Indicor acquisition is expected to close in the second half, with management increasingly confident in 10-12% cost synergies and Indicor's 50% recurring revenue base.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected Indicor to close in “2H 2026” and flagged “quantified synergies (10–12% of sales).”

in_line: Book-to-bill was 1.12, meeting the preview's expectation of at least 1.0, even though orders and backlog exceeded its stated watch levels.
Free-cash-flow conversion was 111%, broadly consistent with the prior full-year guidance of 110–115%.
Indicor remained expected to close in the second half, and the stated 10–12% synergy range matched the range the preview said to watch for.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $1.84, well above the preview’s anchored consensus of about $1.27–$1.28 and even the $1.42 outlier. The beat was substantially larger than the preview’s base-case range of roughly $1.27–$1.40.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EPS was $1.84.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anchor on about $1.27–$1.28”; base scenario: “EPS about $1.27–$1.40.”

surprises.description: ADM raised FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.15–$5.60, not merely toward the preview’s $4.80 consensus but above it at both ends. This also sharply exceeded the previous $4.15–$4.70 guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.15-$5.60,” up roughly $1.00 at both ends from the prior range.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EPS” consensus: “$4.80”; the preview said the Street appeared to expect “a second guidance raise.”

surprises.description: AS&O delivered an especially strong result: segment operating profit rose 129% to $867 million, with large gains in both Crushing and Ag Services. The preview identified a clean AS&O beat driven by crush as a bull case, but the reported surge was a pronounced realization of that upside rather than the base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AS&O segment operating profit surged 129% year-over-year to $867 million, with Crushing up ~$330 million to $363 million and Ag Services up 159% to $293 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Bull scenario: “Clean AS&O beat driven by crush rather than MTM”; preview also called crush margins and biofuel policy “the main driver of the story.”

surprises.description: Nutrition operating profit reached $172 million, above the preview’s explicitly stated bull-case threshold of $140 million. The profit increase came despite revenue declining 5%, with Human and Animal Nutrition each up more than 50%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nutrition segment operating profit rose 51% to $172 million despite revenue declining 5% to $1.9 billion, with both Human and Animal Nutrition each up over 50% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Bull scenario: “Nutrition above $140M.”

surprises.description: ADM raised its expected 2026 net benefit from the 45Z tax credit to about $250 million, a sizable increase from its prior estimate of about $150 million. The preview flagged biofuel-policy durability as an issue to watch but did not anticipate this specific increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its expected 2026 net benefit from the 45Z tax credit to approximately $250 million, up from prior guidance of about $150 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Biofuel policy commentary: durability of the 45Z credit into 2027.”

surprises.description: Management said it is evaluating a return to opportunistic share repurchases later this year, alongside the quarterly dividend. The preview discussed capital allocation mainly in terms of the announced crush expansion and potential capex, and did not flag possible buybacks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage was 1.6x at June 30 (targeting ~2x by year-end), and management is evaluating a return to opportunistic share repurchases later this year alongside its 378th consecutive quarterly dividend of $256 million.”

surprises.description: Management quantified a natural-colors opportunity that was not covered in the preview: a roughly $1 billion U.S. addressable market and a target of $80–$100 million in operating profit over time. This is a newly disclosed potential contribution rather than a reported current-period result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The natural colors transition represents a ~$1 billion U.S. addressable market from which ADM targets $80-$100 million in operating profit over time.”

in_line: The preview expected a Q2 mark-to-market reversal to provide a mechanical tailwind and specifically cautioned that timing effects should be separated from operating performance. Q2 included about $100 million of net positive mark-to-market and timing impacts, while management said the first-half carried net negative position would reverse mostly in Q3.

The preview identified crush and biofuels as the main drivers to watch. Global oilseed crush volumes grew nearly 5% year over year, and ethanol margins were higher both sequentially and year over year, consistent with that focus.

The four-plant crush expansion had already been announced before the preview; the call supplied a roughly $100 million total cost and said its capital intensity is about one-quarter that of greenfield builds.

surprises.description: The preview put Q2 adjusted EPS consensus at $1.41; The Andersons reported $2.15, a sizable beat. Adjusted EBITDA was also $140 million, although the preview gave no EBITDA consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.15 and adjusted EBITDA of $140 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS | $1.41 | Investing.com, retrieved Aug 2, 2026.”

surprises.description: The preview expected investors to assess renewables earnings against full ownership of TAMH and whether margins held excluding 45Z credits, while noting that management said the Q2 crush looked good. Instead, renewables produced record Q2 adjusted pretax income of $88 million, supported by record production, higher margins and strong demand; the results description does not provide an ex-45Z figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Renewables generated record Q2 adjusted pretax income of $88 million … on record second-quarter ethanol production, higher margins, and strong domestic and export demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Renewables pretax income and adjusted EBITDA ex-45Z. Separates operating margin from credits.” Also: “CEO said May 6 that crush ‘looks good for Q2 and Q3.’”

surprises.description: The preview flagged full-year 45Z credit quantification as a key issue but supplied no full-year amount. Management now expects $90–100 million for 2026 and said credits should be relatively evenly split across quarters, with $24 million recorded in Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company recorded $24 million of 45Z tax credits in the quarter and expects $90-100 million for the full year, with credits split relatively evenly across quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year 45Z quantification. Any FY2026 credit framing would reset FY26 and FY27 models.”

surprises.description: The Houston soybean meal export terminal was previously guided for Q3 2026, but management now expects it to be fully operational in Q4, indicating a later timing than the preview led investors to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Houston soybean meal export terminal is expected to be fully operational in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Project timing: Port of Houston soybean meal export capacity (guided Q3 2026) and the Clymers, IN debottleneck (late 2027).”

surprises.description: Agribusiness adjusted pretax income reached $20 million, modestly above the preview’s cited $17 million year-ago and $17.9 million Q1 reference points; fertilizer also performed above expectations despite late-quarter price declines.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Agribusiness adjusted pretax income rose modestly to $20 million from $17 million, with fertilizer performing above expectations despite domestic fertilizer prices dropping late in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Agribusiness adjusted pretax attributable versus the $17M year-ago and $17.9M Q1 marks.”

in_line: Full-year capital spending guidance remained approximately $225 million excluding acquisitions, as indicated after Q1.
Management reaffirmed the $7.00 run-rate EPS target for the end of 2028, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: The preview expected NCA comparable operating earnings of about $225 million, up from $208 million a year earlier. Instead, NCA segment operating earnings fell 2.4%, as Millersburg start-up costs and capacity constraints offset low-single-digit volume growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North and Central America segment operating earnings declined 2.4% year-over-year,” with “roughly $5 million in Millersburg start-up costs and capacity constraints” offsetting low-single-digit volume growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NCA comparable op. earnings $225M”; the preview said consensus implied “+8%” growth from $208M.

surprises.description: South America substantially outperformed the preview’s $53 million operating-earnings estimate: earnings surged 64%, while volumes grew mid-teens. The preview had noted April volume growth of 20%, but did not anticipate the World Cup-driven demand against a flattish regional market.
surprises.fact_evidence: “South America was the standout region with mid-teens volume growth and a 64% surge in segment operating earnings, aided by World Cup-driven customer demand against a flattish regional market.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “South America comparable op. earnings $53M”; the preview also noted “April volumes running +20%.”

surprises.description: Global shipped volume growth exceeded the preview’s threshold of 3% or better, reaching 4.3% in Q2. Growth across all three regions also extended the company’s volume-growth streak to six quarters.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global shipped beverage can volumes increased 4.3% year-over-year in Q2 2026 with growth across all three regions, marking the sixth consecutive quarter of volume growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs +3% or better to support the full-year build.”

surprises.description: Comparable EPS appears to have modestly exceeded the preview’s $0.99 consensus: 14.4% growth from the prior-year $0.90 implies approximately $1.03. The preview’s base case was $0.99–$1.02.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Comparable diluted EPS grew 14.4% year-over-year.” The preview gives Q2 2025 comparable EPS of $0.90, so the reported growth implies about $1.03.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Comparable diluted EPS $0.99 (Zacks); $0.98 on some feeds”; the base scenario was “$0.99–$1.02.”

surprises.description: EMEA operating earnings grew only 6.6%, below the preview’s $161.2 million estimate. Applying the reported growth to the preview’s $129 million prior-year base implies about $138 million, roughly $23 million below that estimate; Benepack contributions were largely offset by the divested Saudi Arabian business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EMEA volumes grew mid-single digits with segment operating earnings up 6.6%, though Benepack contributions were largely offset by the divested Saudi Arabian business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EMEA comparable op. earnings $161.2M”; the preview lists Q2 2025 actual as $129M and says to treat the dollar levels as the anchor.

surprises.description: Ball disclosed a larger and more concentrated Millersburg start-up-cost burden than the preview quantified: about $35 million for 2026, with roughly $30 million in the second half. The preview flagged the plant’s second-half ramp but did not give an expected cost amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year Millersburg start-up costs are expected to total approximately $35 million, with roughly $30 million landing in the second half and no start-up costs anticipated in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Millersburg, Oregon ramps in 2H26” but gave no start-up-cost estimate.

surprises.description: First-half repurchases were well behind the pace implied by the preview’s estimate of roughly $150 million per quarter: only about $100 million had been completed. The full-year plan remains intact, requiring a much heavier second-half pace to reach at least $600 million of buybacks.
surprises.fact_evidence: Ball plans “at least $600 million in buybacks” as part of approximately $800 million of 2026 shareholder returns, but “only ~$100 million of repurchases” were completed in the first half.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$600M+ of repurchases implies roughly $150M per quarter.”

in_line: Ball reaffirmed its full-year target of 10%-plus comparable EPS growth, as the preview’s base case expected a reaffirmation without an upgrade.
The free-cash-flow outlook remained above $900 million, matching the preview’s stated target.

The full-year shareholder-return plan remained approximately $800 million, including at least $600 million of buybacks, although first-half repurchase pace was below the preview’s implied quarterly pace.
The regional full-year volume outlook matched the preview’s expectations: North America and South America at the low ends of their ranges, and EMEA above its 3%-5% range.

surprises.description: Caterpillar reported Q2 sales and revenues of $20.5 billion, well above the preview’s $19.31 billion consensus (and alternate estimates of $18.9–19.0 billion). The 24% year-over-year increase was also above the preview’s expected 14.4–16.6% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 sales and revenues reached a record $20.5 billion, up 24% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $19.31B”; alternate estimate “~$18.9–19.0B”; consensus growth estimates of “+16.6%” and “+14.4%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $8.17, far above the preview’s $6.25 consensus. The preview expected roughly 32% year-over-year growth, whereas reported adjusted EPS rose 73%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted profit per share rose 73% to $8.17, exceeding company expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS | $6.25”; expected year-over-year growth of “+32.4%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating margin reached 21.9%, above the preview’s estimate of about 19.1%. The call attributed part of the 430-basis-point year-over-year increase to $392 million in IEEPA tariff recoveries.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating profit margin was 21.9%, a 430 basis point increase over the prior year, boosted by $392 million in IEEPA tariff recoveries.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating margin | ~19.1%”; the preview described a 150-basis-point year-over-year increase.

surprises.description: Caterpillar raised its full-year sales-growth outlook from low double digits to mid- to high-teens. The preview identified a low-teens raise as a possible bull trigger, so the reported range went materially further.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year 2026 sales and revenues growth outlook to mid- to high-teens, up from prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior guide was “low double-digit sales growth”; the preview called “an explicit raise to low-teens growth” a bull trigger.

surprises.description: Backlog grew by $9 billion sequentially to a record $72 billion. That exceeded the preview’s base-case increase of $1–3 billion and its bull-case threshold of $5 billion, although it was below the $11.5 billion increase in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog grew sequentially by $9 billion to a record $72 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “backlog up $1–3B”; the bull case expected “backlog up $5B+ q/q.”

surprises.description: Sales to users in power generation surged 72%, above the preview’s expectation that power-generation growth would hold near Q1’s 41%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sales to users in power generation surged 72% on data center demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Power gen growth needs to hold near +41%”; the preview also identified growth below roughly 25% as a bear-case concern.

surprises.description: Full-year 2026 tariff costs were expected to be $2.2–2.4 billion based on the prior guidance; the new estimate is about $2.2 billion, at the low end of that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 tariff costs are now expected to be around $2.2 billion (low end of the prior range).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior estimate was “$2.2–2.4B”; the preview said “a further trim is a clean margin beat.”

surprises.description: Caterpillar generated record MP&E free cash flow of $5.1 billion, despite the preview’s concern that the power-generation capacity build was becoming a growing call on cash. The preview gave no cash-flow estimate, but the reported record is a marked contrast with Q1’s $0.6 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Caterpillar generated record MP&E free cash flow of $5.1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Free cash flow and capex” and said “the power-gen capacity build is a growing call on cash.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that Caterpillar is restarting production of its 10-megawatt gas reciprocating engine platform, adding about 1.5 gigawatts of capacity with shipments beginning in Q4. The preview did not anticipate this production restart.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is restarting production of its 10-megawatt gas reciprocating engine platform, bringing about 1.5 gigawatts of capacity online with shipments beginning in Q4.”

surprises.description: Power and Energy orders were extending as far out as 2030. This was more forward order visibility than the preview expected, which described a beat-and-reaffirm without quantified forward orders as the most likely path.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Caterpillar is taking Power and Energy orders as far out as 2030.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “the bar on 2027 orders is high” and that “a beat-and-reaffirm without quantified forward orders” was the most likely path.

surprises.description: Caterpillar returned $2.2 billion to shareholders, including $1.5 billion in buybacks and dividends and an 8% dividend increase. The preview did not forecast or discuss this level of capital returns.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Returned $2.2 billion to shareholders via $1.5 billion buybacks and dividends, including an 8% dividend increase.”

in_line: Power and Energy’s margin was 24.6%, recovering from Q1’s 20.6%, in line with the preview’s expectation that the margin would recover.

Construction Industries remained strong: sales rose 35%, and sales to users increased for a sixth consecutive quarter. The preview had flagged dealer inventory as an issue to assess; the reported $400 million dealer inventory increase shows that restocking contributed alongside ongoing end-user growth.

surprises.description: The preview’s working EPS bar was about $1.05–$1.10, but Harmony reported diluted EPS of $1.28. That was a clear earnings beat despite the preview’s base case of roughly $1.00–$1.15.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income more than doubled to $75.4 million ($1.28 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A working bar of roughly $1.05–1.10 is more useful than $0.97”; the base scenario expected “$1.00–1.15.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted uncertainty about whether the sequential revenue jump reflected durable demand or gross-to-net favorability. Harmony reported about 450 patient additions, its highest Q2 increase in WAKIX’s history, supporting a strong underlying-demand explanation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “WAKIX added approximately 450 patients in Q2,” the “highest Q2 increase in the brand's history,” with 4 of the last 5 quarters exceeding 400 additions.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the “Quality of the ~21% sequential revenue jump” and said “Demand-driven growth is durable; gross-to-net favorability is not.”

surprises.description: The preview expected BP-205 Phase 1 SAD data, with positive data identified as a bull-case driver, but it did not specify the reported profile. The data showed once-daily-supporting half-life, high selectivity, and no serious cardiovascular, hepatic, or visual adverse events in 72 volunteers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BP-205 showed a ~25-hour half-life supporting once-daily dosing” and “no serious cardiovascular, hepatic, or visual adverse events across 72 volunteers”; it also demonstrated “over 600-fold selectivity” for orexin-2 over orexin-1.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “BP-205 Phase 1 SAD data” as a checkpoint and named “positive BP-205 data” as a bull-case driver.

surprises.description: The preview’s EPS adjustment assumed roughly 79% gross margin, but cost of product sold was 24.2% of revenue, implying a lower product gross margin. Harmony attributed the increase to new royalties under its Novitium license.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cost of product sold rose to 24.2% of net revenue from 19% a year ago, primarily due to new royalties tied to the Novitium license agreement signed in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s EPS adjustment used “~79% gross margin.”

surprises.description: The preview anticipated possible in-licensing and BD-related expense, but Harmony described plans for multiple business development transactions rather than a single large deal. This adds specificity about the company’s intended deal-making, though the facts do not quantify timing or spending.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company had “$962.5 million in cash and investments against $155 million in debt,” providing “firepower for multiple planned business development transactions rather than a single large deal.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “shown appetite for in-licensing” and flagged “R&D expense and any embedded BD upfronts.”

surprises.description: Beyond the SAD data expected in the preview, Harmony laid out a further BP-205 development schedule: multiple-ascending-dose data in Q4 2026, a Phase Ib study beginning in Q3, and multiple Phase II CNS trials beginning in mid-2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Upcoming BP-205 catalysts include multiple ascending dose data in Q4 2026, a Phase Ib sleep-deprived volunteer study starting Q3 with data in early 2027, and multiple Phase II CNS trials beginning mid-2027.”

surprises.description: The call provided favorable franchise-protection detail not covered in the preview: WAKIX exclusivity through March 2030 and patent protection for BP-205 and pitolisant GR/HD that could extend into the 2040s. Ongoing AET/Sandoz litigation leaves some uncertainty around WAKIX.
surprises.fact_evidence: “WAKIX exclusivity is protected to March 2030 including pediatric exclusivity, with 6 of 7 ANDA filers settled and litigation ongoing with AET/Sandoz,” while “BP-205 composition IP extends to 2043 and pitolisant GR/HD patents could extend the franchise into the 2040s.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was expected at about $261 million based on the July 16 preannouncement; the call reported record WAKIX quarterly net revenue of $261.3 million.
The preview said reaffirmation of FY26 revenue guidance was the base case. Harmony reiterated its $1.00–$1.04 billion guidance.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $93.3 million, about 5% below the preview’s ~$98.1 million consensus. However, the reported 1% year-over-year growth was better than the preview’s expectation of an approximately 6% reported decline, so the headline was mixed rather than uniformly weak.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue grew just 1% year-over-year to $93.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue ~$98.1M”; the preview says this “implied ~6% reported decline, reflecting the April 2026 divestiture.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.08, below the preview’s $0.10 consensus. The shortfall was $0.02 per share, even though adjusted EPS was flat year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS held flat at $0.08.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $0.10.”

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted EPS range of $0.31–$0.36 is below the preview’s expected $0.35–$0.41 range. The new range lowers both the floor and ceiling, with only a narrow overlap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted diluted EPS is guided to $0.31-$0.36.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $0.35–0.41.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was lowered to 29%–31%, versus the 30%–32% range the preview said was in place. The company attributed the reduction to stranded costs related to the divestiture, rather than underlying performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year EBITDA margin guidance was lowered to 29%-31% from the prior 30%-32%, attributed to divestiture-related stranded costs rather than underlying performance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin 30–32%.”
