surprises.fact_evidence: “Scientific Instruments segment posted 10% organic bookings growth … led by greater than 50% growth in semi”; semiconductor metrology had “first-half organic order growth over 30% and revenue growth over 15%,” with “9-24 month lead times delaying revenue conversion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview set “a third straight quarter above 20% growth” as the semiconductor metrology bookings bar.

surprises.description: Despite the Q2 EPS beat, Bruker reiterated FY26 non-GAAP EPS guidance at $2.10–$2.15 rather than raising it above $2.15 or moving the range higher as the preview said the market was looking for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was reiterated at $2.10-$2.15 non-GAAP EPS (15-17% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The market is looking for a raise above $2.15 EPS, or at least a move to the high end.”

surprises.description: The reported FY26 revenue range was lowered to $3.54–$3.57 billion, below the previously reaffirmed $3.57–$3.60 billion range, because the assumed FX tailwind was cut from 1.5% to 0.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FX tailwind was cut from 1.5% to 0.5%, lowering reported revenue guidance to $3.54-$3.57 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue | Company guidance | $3.57 – $3.60B (reaffirmed May 6, 2026).”

surprises.description: Bruker disclosed a $135 million noncash goodwill impairment that drove a GAAP diluted loss per share of $0.41, tied to underperforming automation and spatial biology businesses. The preview did not anticipate this charge or the resulting GAAP loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported a GAAP diluted loss per share of $0.41, driven by a $135 million noncash goodwill impairment tied to its underperforming automation and spatial biology businesses.”

surprises.description: Management said about $20 million of revenue would move from Q3 into Q4 because of semiconductor customer delivery timing, leaving Q3 organic revenue roughly flat to slightly up and sequential margins and EPS lower. The preview did not flag this specific near-term timing disruption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately $20 million of Q3 revenue is shifting to Q4 due to semiconductor customer delivery timing, leaving Q3 organic revenue roughly flat to slightly up with sequentially lower margins and EPS.”

surprises.description: Management gave a specific, very strong Q4 outlook: revenue around $1 billion, with roughly two-thirds already in backlog, and meaningful year-over-year gains in organic growth, margin, and EPS. The preview did not provide this Q4 revenue or backlog outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects a very strong Q4 with revenue around $1 billion (of which roughly two-thirds is already in backlog) driving meaningful year-over-year gains in organic growth, margin, and EPS.”

surprises.description: Beyond the previously announced $140 million annualized savings program, Bruker said its new four-group operating structure is expected to generate another $20 million in 2027 and support a longer-term target of double-digit EPS growth and EBIT margins moving back toward 20%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new four-group operating structure [is] expected to add $20 million more in 2027, supporting a target of double-digit EPS growth and margins moving back toward 20% EBIT.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted the cost-savings program had been raised to “~$140M annualized from $100–120M,” but did not mention another $20 million of savings or the stated longer-term targets.

in_line: Organic revenue growth turned positive at 2.8% (3.4% excluding tariff refunds), consistent with management’s previewed low-to-mid-single-digit Q2 organic growth outlook, although total revenue missed consensus.
Scientific Instruments’ book-to-bill remained above 1.0 for a fourth consecutive quarter, as the preview flagged as a key milestone.
The company remained on track for the previously announced $140 million of annualized cost savings in 2026.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $229 million, about 6% above the roughly $215 million consensus and above the $214–216 million company guide. That is a much stronger result than the preview’s base scenario of $224–228 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 41% year-over-year to a record $229 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … Consensus $215.1–215.2M”; the preview’s base scenario was “$224–228M.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY2026 revenue growth guidance to 33–34%, above the preview’s expected raise to 29–30% in its base case and even above its 31–33% bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to 33%-34% from prior 27%-28%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guide: raise to 30% or higher”; the bull scenario expected “Raised to 31–33%.”

surprises.description: Marketplace revenue grew 45%, well above the company’s 35–36% guide and the preview’s 44%+ bull threshold. Growth accelerated rather than merely continuing at the expected pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marketplace revenue accelerated to 45% year-over-year growth to $215 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Marketplace revenue growth: 35–36% YoY”; the bull scenario expected “44%+.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA of $14.1 million exceeded the $11–12 million company guide, though it was within the preview’s $13–15 million base scenario. Profitability was better than the formal guide but not beyond the preview’s base expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA improved $10.2 million year-over-year to $14.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA $11–12M” in company guidance; the preview’s base scenario was “$13–15M.”

surprises.description: Marketplace gross margin was 34.7%, below the preview’s 36%+ expectation. Management’s stated 35–40% target and AI-related improvement plans point to future expansion, but do not change the shortfall versus the Q2 bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marketplace gross margin was 34.7% (flat sequentially, up ~100 bps in first half), with management targeting expansion into a 35%-40% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Marketplace gross margin… The bar is 36%+.”

surprises.description: Supplier services revenue was $13.9 million, below the preview’s expectation of roughly flat revenue from about $15 million a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Services revenue was $13.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Supplier services: ‘Roughly flat’”; Q2’25 actual was “~$15M.”

surprises.description: Buyer and larger-account metrics showed stronger wallet expansion and customer additions than the preview’s recent benchmark: revenue per active buyer rose 21% versus 17% in Q1, and $50,000-plus accounts had record quarterly net adds. The preview highlighted wallet-share gains and enterprise ramp as key issues but did not forecast this degree of momentum.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Active buyers increased 20% year-over-year to 89,557, with net adds of 3,976, the highest number in 10 quarters, while marketplace revenue per active buyer rose 21%”; “$50,000” accounts had “a record 175 quarterly net adds,” and enterprise revenue from larger customers “grew over 40%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue per active buyer grew 17% YoY in Q1”; the preview said “Wallet-share expansion matters more than the raw buyer count” and listed “enterprise and aero-defense ramp” as a bull-case driver.

surprises.description: The preview cited management’s commitment to at least 20% incremental adjusted EBITDA margins, but the reported year-over-year EBITDA increase implies roughly 15% incremental margin: $10.2 million of EBITDA improvement on about $66 million of added revenue. This fell short of that benchmark even though EBITDA beat the quarterly guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA improved $10.2 million year-over-year”; revenue was $229 million versus $163 million in Q2’25.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has committed to at least 20% incremental adj. EBITDA margins.”

surprises.description: The Siemens partnership was described as a contributor to 2027 results, with only modest product-related costs in 2026 guidance. That places the expected payoff later than the preview’s bull-case idea of the Siemens funnel converting, with no material 2026 contribution indicated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Siemens partnership [is] expected to positively impact 2027 results but only modest product-related costs [are] embedded in 2026 guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bull scenario cited “Siemens funnel converting”; the catalyst checklist called for “quantified Siemens contribution.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $377.4 million, slightly above the preview’s roughly $376.2–376.3 million consensus, and adjusted EPS of $1.73 exceeded the cited $1.69–$1.70 estimate. Both were modest beats rather than the near-consensus results described in the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue rose 8% year-over-year to $377.4 million, with adjusted EPS up 16.1% to $1.73.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS … ~$1.70 (one source: $1.69)”; “Revenue … ~$376.2–376.3M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected home health to return to growth in the second half and identified Q2 as an early read on that trajectory. Q2 same-store revenue was still down 2.8%, although that was a notable improvement from the 6.6% first-quarter decline and new admissions rose 9.8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Home health same-store revenue declined 2.8% but improved from a 6.6% first-quarter drop, with same-store new admissions up 9.8% following new leadership hires.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided to growth in 2H FY2026. Q2 is the first real read on whether that is happening.”

surprises.description: Profitability was stronger than the preview’s expectation of merely exceeding 12%: Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin reached 13%, and management said the full-year margin was tracking toward the higher end of the 12%–13% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 13% in Q2, with management guiding full-year margin toward the higher end of its 12%-13% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin above 12%” was the full-year color from the Q1 call; the preview also flagged the “>12% FY target.”

surprises.description: The tax rate was above the preview’s mid-20% expectation and management expects it to remain in the upper 20s, citing the expiration of the Work Opportunity Tax Credit program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The tax rate rose to 26.9% and is expected to stay in the upper-20% range due to expiration of the Work Opportunity Tax Credit program at the end of 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “An effective tax rate in the mid-20% range.”

surprises.description: A Medicare Cap accrual of just over $3 million, primarily in Ohio, pressured hospice margins—an unflagged cost headwind. Management said it expects no additional cap expense and sees potential mitigation for the rest of the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A Medicare Cap accrual of just over $3 million, primarily in the Ohio market, pressured hospice margins, though management expects no additional cap expense and potential mitigation for the rest of the year.”

surprises.description: Operating cash flow rose sharply, but the increase included roughly $20 million of first-half working-capital benefits that management does not expect to recur. The preview did not set an expectation for cash flow, so the reported strength came with an important qualification.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow surged to $40 million from $22.5 million a year earlier, aided by roughly $20 million in first-half working capital benefits that are not expected to persist.”

surprises.description: Management reported a stronger acquisition-funding position than the preview discussed: bank debt fell by $30 million sequentially, while the company had about $100 million in cash and $577.8 million of revolver availability, supporting larger acquisitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced bank debt to $64.3 million (down $30 million sequentially) with ~$100 million cash and $577.8 million in revolver availability, positioning it for larger acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s M&A item focused on “confirmation of closing or integration commentary” on the pending Indiana deal; it did not anticipate an update on increased acquisition capacity.

surprises.description: The call included new 2027 payment-rate updates: the proposed home health rule offers a 2.1% net increase, while the final hospice rate is 2.3%, down from 2.6% for 2026. The home health update is favorable, while the lower hospice increase is comparatively less favorable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The proposed 2027 home health rule offers a 2.1% net rate increase and the final 2027 hospice rate of 2.3% (below 2026's 2.6%).”

surprises.description: Management said the Medicaid 80/20 provision could potentially be eliminated by year-end, an unanticipated potentially favorable policy development in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects the Medicaid 80/20 provision to potentially be eliminated by year-end.”

surprises.description: The consolidated caregiver fill rate improved to 84%–85%, and management attributed the improvement to faster-than-expected adoption of the caregiver app in Texas. This was an operational upside not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The consolidated fill rate improved to 84%-85% from the lower 80s, driven by faster-than-expected caregiver app adoption in Texas.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management described caregiver app adoption as “faster-than-expected.”

in_line: Personal Care organic growth and hospice census growth remained positive, consistent with the preview’s watch for “same-store growth in personal care and average daily census growth in hospice, both of which were positive in Q1.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $19.9 million, about 12% above the $17.80 million consensus, rather than merely the sequential step-up the preview anticipated. It was also a record, up 15% sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $19.9 million,” up “15% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 Consensus” revenue was “$17.80M”; the preview said this implied “the first real sequential step-up in a year.”

surprises.description: Exagen raised its full-year revenue range to $72–75 million from $70–73 million, instead of simply reaffirming the prior range. The new midpoint is also above the preview’s $71.67 million FY2026 consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $72-75 million from the prior $70-73 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the company’s guidance was “$70–73M” and that reaffirmation was the “minimum”; narrowing toward the high end was described as the bull trigger. FY2026 consensus was “$71.67M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was just over 61%, above the preview’s roughly 58.8% FY2026 consensus and Q1’s 59.0%. Management also now expects to exit 2026 at 60% or above, with a mid-60s long-term target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached just over 61% (up ~90 basis points year-over-year),” and management expects to “exit 2026 at 60% or above” and targets “mid-60s over time.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~58.8% (FY26E)”; the preview also noted Q1 gross margin of “59.0%” and flagged slower margin improvement as a concern.

surprises.description: Cash collections from claims older than 360 days contributed more than $1 million to the quarter’s ASP, so the ASP result was partly supported by lumpy, out-of-period collections rather than only current-period reimbursement progress. The preview specifically questioned whether another aged-claims contribution would support Q2 ASP.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The quarter's ASP benefited from over $1 million collected on claims older than 360 days”; TTM ASP was $446, up 4%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called out “ASP quality” and asked “how much of the ASP line in Q2 comes from in-period collections versus another aged-claims contribution”; it said aged claims accounting for ASP gains would point to the bear case.

surprises.description: Cash was just under $25 million at quarter-end, above the preview’s base-case expectation of cash in the high teens. First-half cash collections were also $9 million higher than in the first half of 2025, providing a positive counterpoint to the Q1 cash drawdown concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended Q2 with “just under $25 million in cash,” and “total first-half 2026 cash collections exceeded first-half 2025 by $9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “cash holds in the high teens” and highlighted quarter-end cash and the Q1 drawdown as the main swing factor.

surprises.description: The adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to essentially breakeven, a much stronger Q2 profitability result than the prior quarter’s $2.2 million loss might have suggested. Management tempered the result by saying it does not expect the near-breakeven level to continue in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to roughly $0.1 million (essentially breakeven) versus a $1.7 million loss in Q2 2025,” but management “does not expect this near-breakeven level to be sustained in the second half of 2026.”

surprises.description: Pharma services produced record quarterly revenue above $1 million, up more than 200% year over year, while its contract backlog grew by about $1 million to over $6 million. The preview did not discuss this segment, so this was an unanticipated source of growth and backlog expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pharma services generated record quarterly revenue exceeding $1 million (up over 200% year-over-year), with contract backlog growing about $1 million to over $6 million.”

in_line: AVISE CTD volume growth was strong but broadly consistent with the preview’s expectations: volume rose 11% year over year, versus the high-single-digit growth assumption embedded in FY2026 guidance and the preview’s 10%-or-more bull-case threshold.

surprises.description: NRG reported adjusted EPS of $1.49, well below the preview’s roughly $1.80 consensus estimate. Adjusted EBITDA grew strongly, but acquisition-related interest expense and depreciation and amortization more than offset that growth at the EPS level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA rose 34% year-over-year to $1.2 billion, but adjusted EPS declined to $1.49 from $1.73 as acquisition-related interest expense and D&A offset higher EBITDA during the de-leveraging period.”

surprises.description: NRG said it expects to track below the midpoint of its reaffirmed 2026 guidance, a weaker outlook than a plain reaffirmation would imply. The company cited softer Texas load and power prices, Winter Storm Fern supply costs, and $70 million of incremental RGGI costs; Houston around-the-clock prices were also far below the planning assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NRG reaffirmed its 2026 guidance but expects to track below the midpoint due to softer Texas load and power prices, Winter Storm Fern supply costs, and $70 million of incremental RGGI costs from Virginia rejoining the program.” Houston prices “averaged $33 per megawatt hour … 8% below last year and well below the company's 2026 planning assumption of $52.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A plain reaffirm leaves the low end live; narrowing to the upper half would be the bull trigger.”

surprises.description: NRG announced a major hyperscaler project in Q2 even though the preview’s base case expected no anchor data-center deal in the quarter. The aligned terms cover an initial 1.2 GW, potentially expanding to 2.4 GW, with a 15-year-or-longer term and substantial availability-based, separately cost-recovered cash flows.
surprises.fact_evidence: NRG “aligned on principal commercial terms with an investment-grade global cloud and AI hyperscaler for a 1.2 gigawatt Bring Your Own Power project in Texas, with potential to expand to 2.4 gigawatts.” The project is expected to generate “$500 million of annual adjusted EBITDA and $375 million of annual free cash flow before growth,” targets a “12%-15% pretax un-levered IRR,” has an initial term “of at least 15 years,” and supports “95% of the project's free cash flow via availability-based Capacity Payments independent of data center utilization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The awaited catalyst is an anchor hyperscaler deal tied to the 5.4 GW GE Vernova/Kiewit JV; management guided to ‘sometime in 2026’ without a specific quarter.” The base scenario anticipated “no anchor data center deal.”

surprises.description: Beyond the initial hyperscaler project, NRG disclosed a much broader potential contracted-growth opportunity: secured turbine and EPC capacity and PJM uprates support an illustrative $1.2 billion of contracted free cash flow by 2030, alongside a 14%-plus adjusted EPS CAGR expectation for the base business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 1.2 gigawatt project represents only the first tranche of 5.4 gigawatts of secured turbine and EPC capacity through 2032, plus ~2 gigawatts of PJM uprate opportunities, supporting an illustrative $1.2 billion contracted free cash flow opportunity by 2030 on top of a base business expected to deliver 14%-plus adjusted EPS CAGR through 2030.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified an anchor hyperscaler deal tied to the 5.4 GW JV as a catalyst, but did not cite the broader PJM opportunity or an illustrative $1.2 billion contracted free-cash-flow opportunity.

surprises.description: Funding the project will reduce planned net debt reduction and push NRG’s 3x leverage target back by a year, from 2028 to 2029. That is a capital-allocation trade-off not raised in the preview’s discussion of the data-center catalyst or buyback plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The project spend does not change guidance but reduces planned net debt reduction, extending the timeline to reach the 3x leverage target from 2028 to 2029.”

in_line: NRG reaffirmed its 2026 guidance range, matching the preview’s base-case expectation of a plain reaffirmation, although management added that it expects to track below the midpoint.
Adjusted EBITDA of $1.2 billion was at the bottom of the preview’s own derived estimate of roughly $1.20–$1.35 billion.

surprises.description: Entegris reported Q2 revenue of $883 million, well above the preview’s $839.9 million consensus and the $845 million top of company guidance. The 11% year-over-year growth was a substantially stronger result than the preview’s expected roughly 8% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 11% year-over-year to $883 million, exceeding guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus (Zacks, 7/31/26) $839.9M”; company guidance “$815M – $845M”; management’s Q2 signal implied “roughly $871M, or about +8% YoY.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $0.93, above the preview’s $0.83 consensus and the $0.84 high end of guidance. This was a notable earnings beat, not merely revenue growth translating into results near expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $0.93.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus (Zacks, 7/31/26) $0.83”; Q2 guidance “$0.76 – $0.84.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $905 million–$935 million is far above the preview’s roughly $871 million implied outlook and its $865 million–$880 million base scenario. The midpoint is about 5.6% above the preview’s implied figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance implies ~14% year-over-year revenue growth ($905M-$935M).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 revenue guide vs. ~$871M”; the base scenario expected a Q3 midpoint of “$865–880M.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted gross margin reached 47.6%, 35 basis points above the top of the preview’s guidance range. The preview had flagged margin improvement and its drivers as a key debate, but the reported margin was modestly above the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin reached 47.6%, its highest level since early 2022, improving 70 basis points sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 gross margin guidance was “46.25% – 47.25%”; the preview said to watch “whether the residual gain reflects real productivity.”

surprises.description: CapEx-related revenue grew 15% in Q2, a stronger inflection than the preview’s expectation that this revenue would improve through the second half and turn positive. The preview had highlighted this as important to reaching the higher Q4 revenue implied by consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CapEx-related revenue up 15%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management “expects CapEx-driven revenue to improve through 2H”; “This segment must inflect” for the preview’s Q4 consensus outlook to be reachable.

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was $120 million, below the preview’s roughly $140 million-plus quarterly pace needed to reach about 3.0x leverage by year-end. This is a shortfall against the cash-flow expectation, even though the company reported debt repayment and a better year-end leverage outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was $120 million (14% of sales).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Reaching about 3.0x by year-end requires roughly $140M+ of quarterly FCF.”

surprises.description: Despite Q2 free cash flow falling short of the preview’s indicated quarterly pace, management now expects year-end leverage in the high-2x range, better than the preview’s approximately 3.0x target. The company also repaid $200 million of debt in the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$200 million of debt repayment and reducing net leverage to 3.4x, with management now expecting to end the year in the high 2x range versus prior expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q1 net leverage was “3.6x, with a target of about 3.0x by year-end 2026.”

surprises.description: The Q4 outlook implies mid-teens year-over-year growth, above the preview’s roughly 11% implied growth and roughly $917 million revenue estimate. However, the expected sequential growth rate is about 4%, slightly below the preview’s implied 5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue is expected to grow ~4% sequentially from the Q3 midpoint, representing mid-teens year-over-year growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “roughly $917M for Q4,” “+11% YoY and +5% sequential.”

surprises.description: Management raised its 2026 MSI growth forecast to 7%–8% from its initial mid-single-digit assumption. This is an upward revision to the company’s own outlook; the preview did not provide an MSI-specific forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its 2026 MSI growth forecast to 7%-8% from an initial mid-single-digit assumption.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Initial mid-single-digit assumption.”

surprises.description: Management described a pipeline of more than 20 major leading-edge capacity expansions, but said fab-construction benefits would mostly accrue in 2027. That provides a sizable longer-term opportunity while placing most of the cited capacity-expansion benefit later than the preview’s focus on improving CapEx-driven revenue through 2H 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tracking over 20 major leading-edge capacity expansions globally (8-10 advanced logic, 7-8 advanced memory, 6-8 advanced packaging), with fab construction benefits mostly accruing to 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “fab-construction forecasts improved” and management “expects CapEx-driven revenue to improve through 2H.”

surprises.description: Molybdenum precursor demand is growing rapidly: it rose more than 20% year over year in Q2 and is expected to roughly double in 2026, driven by NAND scaling to more than 300 layers. The preview did not flag this product-specific growth opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Molybdenum precursor demand grew over 20% year-over-year in Q2 and is expected to roughly double in 2026 versus 2025, driven by NAND scaling to 300-plus layers.”

surprises.description: Entegris exited a small, dilutive U.S. life sciences fluid-management business and announced another facility closure. The preview noted that portfolio actions could be a topic, but did not anticipate these specific moves or that Logan would be the third dilutive facility rationalization since late 2025.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Exited its U.S. life sciences fluid management business (less than $20 million annual revenue, dilutive margins) and announced closure of its Logan, Utah facility, its third dilutive facility rationalization since late 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said governance “may affect tone on M&A and portfolio actions.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $10–11 million below the preview’s roughly $493–494 million consensus and fell year over year, rather than growing slightly as consensus implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $483.3 million, down 1.4% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$493.4M …; $494.3M on a second Investing.com page … Implies roughly +0.6–0.8% y/y.”

surprises.description: Attendance declined despite the preview’s expectation that the weak weather comparison could allow growth; the decline was attributed partly to lower international visitation, which the preview had flagged as needing to stabilize.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A 2.9% attendance decline of approximately 179,000 guests due to the Easter calendar shift and lower international visitation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Failing to grow attendance against that comp would undercut the forward-indicator story” and “The ~80K-guest drag in Q1 needs to show signs of stabilizing.”

surprises.description: The reported profit measures weakened rather than matching the growth implied by the preview’s EPS estimate: adjusted EBITDA fell, and net income was down substantially year over year. The call facts do not provide actual EPS for a direct EPS comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA fell $10.8 million to $195.5 million and net income dropped to $63.3 million from $80.1 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS | $1.69 … | $1.45 GAAP … Implies ~17% y/y growth.”

surprises.description: Admission spending per guest fell further than the preview’s latest reported decline, even as in-park spending reached a record; admission per capita was down 1.8% versus the preview’s cited Q1 decline of 0.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In-park per capita spending up 5.1% to a quarterly record while admission per capita declined 1.8% due to product mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Admissions per cap fell 0.5% in Q1.”

surprises.description: The preliminary July update showed revenue down about 2%, with several weather and air-quality disruptions, providing a negative summer trading update not quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “July revenue was down approximately 2%, hurt by wildfires, air quality issues, excessive heat and rain, though admission per capita turned positive.”

surprises.description: The paid pass base was down year over year despite the preview noting season-pass sales had been pacing well ahead earlier in the season; deferred revenue was only modestly higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Deferred revenue rose about 2% year-over-year to $211.9 million, while the paid pass base was down 1% versus June 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Season-pass sales were pacing ~12% ahead of 2025 through April 30.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed credible third parties interested in buying some or most of the real estate, with offers it said compare favorably to the company’s public equity market value; the preview did not identify this as a potential development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is engaged with multiple credible third parties interested in acquiring some or most of its real estate, with valuations offered that compare very favorably to the company's public equity market value.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed sponsorship revenue above $15 million for 2026 and a target of at least $30 million in coming years, an additional revenue opportunity not raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects over $15 million in sponsorship revenue in 2026, targeting at least $30 million in coming years.”

surprises.description: Management said it remains on pace for a $50 million gross cost-savings target, above the preview’s cited roughly $30 million annualized savings initiative; the measures are described on different bases, so the comparison is not exact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Remains on pace for its $50 million gross cost savings target for 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Progress on the ~$30M annualized savings initiative.”

surprises.description: The company raised its growth/ROI capital spending budget to $75–85 million, an increased spending commitment that was not discussed in the preview and could compete with capital returns for cash.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its 2026 growth/ROI CapEx budget to $75-85 million (from prior levels), alongside $180-190 million in core CapEx.”

surprises.description: Management reported early Howl-O-Scream booking sales ahead of last year after introducing new Sony Pictures horror IP, an encouraging early demand signal not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Introduced new Sony Pictures horror IP into Howl-O-Scream with early booking sales running ahead of last year.”

in_line: In-park per-capita spending reached a quarterly record, as the preview expected the record trend to hold through the quarter.

surprises.description: Consolidated revenue growth was 4%, ahead of the preview’s roughly 2% consensus growth expectation. The reported growth included 2% same-unit growth and contributions from recent acquisitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated revenue grew 4%, driven by 2% same unit growth plus non-same unit activity from recent acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue: $477.3M – $478.5M” versus “Q2 FY25 Actual: $468.8M,” implying about 1.8%–2.1% growth.

surprises.description: Same-unit growth was only 2%, below the preview’s stated level for a meaningful beat, as 4% pricing was offset by falling volumes. Patient service volumes declined 2% and NICU days fell 3%, marking another negative volume quarter against the preview’s bear-case concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same unit pricing rose 4%”; “Same unit patient service volumes fell 2% with NICU days down 3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Above +3% total same-unit would be a real beat”; the preview also said “A second negative volume quarter would be the bear case's strongest evidence.”

surprises.description: Payer mix improved substantially rather than staying stable and unchanged: it was up 135 basis points year over year and 120 basis points versus Q1, with management seeing no deterioration like that reported by peers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Payer mix improved 135 basis points year over year and 120 basis points versus Q1 2026,” and management reported “no signs of the payer mix deterioration seen by peers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The July 15 pre-announcement described payor mix as “stable and unchanged” for Q2, with “no adverse shifts seen.”

surprises.description: The company repurchased nearly twice as many shares in Q2 as in Q1, buying just under 2 million shares versus 1.0 million in Q1. The buybacks since August 2025 have reduced shares outstanding from 87 million to 81 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased just under 2 million shares in the quarter,” bringing total buybacks since August 2025 to 7 million shares and reducing shares outstanding “to 81 million from 87 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 repurchases of “1.0M shares” and identified “A larger buyback” as an upside lever.

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed the $280–$300 million full-year EBITDA range rather than narrowing it toward the upper half, despite Q2 EBITDA landing close to the preview’s run-rate estimate. The preview characterized a plain reaffirmation as a mild disappointment and said narrowing to $290–$300 million was the minimum buy-side hope.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $76 million,” and the company “reaffirmed its full-year 2026 outlook of $280 to $300 million in adjusted EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A plain reaffirmation after the July 15 update would be a mild disappointment. A narrow to $290–300M is the minimum buy-side hope.”

surprises.description: The company flagged one-time executive transition costs as pushing 2026 G&A toward the high end of its range, an expense item not raised in the preview’s discussion of cost pressures. Management said the costs should step down in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “G&A expense is expected to land at the higher end of a $230 to $240 million range for 2026, elevated by one-time executive transition costs that should step down in the second half.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $76 million was broadly in line with the preview’s derived ~$77 million anchor.

Same-unit pricing rose 4%, in line with the preview’s expectation that pricing would hold near 4%; management also said the RCM collections tailwind is expected to dissipate in the second half, as the preview had anticipated.

surprises.description: Diluted EPS was $0.15, above the preview’s $0.105 consensus estimate (and the alternative $0.11 figure). Revenue of $36.9 million was only modestly above the $36.35 million working consensus and landed at the top of the preview’s implied $36.3–$36.9 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income increased to $3.2 million ($0.15 per diluted share)” and “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $36.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS: $0.105 (one source shows $0.11)” and “Treat $36.4M as the working revenue bar”; the preview’s arithmetic says the 6–8% guide implies “$36.3M–$36.9M for Q2.”

surprises.description: Wound Care grew much faster than the preview’s cautious watchpoints implied: the call reported 154% growth, driven mainly by compression devices for lymphedema. The preview had highlighted $2.4 million or more as a level to watch and warned that growth might decelerate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wound Care revenue surged 154% ($2.1 million), driven mainly by compression devices for lymphedema, which accounted for nearly 90% of the increase.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for $2.4M or more, and whether growth is decelerating”; “Under $2.3M with slowing growth would weaken the bull case.”

surprises.description: Patient Services gross margin fell to 61.8% from 64.2% because of lower-margin Wound Care mix and higher pump maintenance costs. The preview emphasized potential ERP and cash-conversion risks but did not flag this margin pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Patient Services gross margin declined to 61.8% from 64.2% due to a larger mix of lower-margin Wound Care revenue and higher pump maintenance costs.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was approximately $8.6 million with a 23.4% margin, slightly ahead of the preview’s $8.4 million and 23.1% base case and comfortably above its 22% threshold for keeping guidance credible.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 7.6% to approximately $8.6 million, with EBITDA margin expanding over 1 point to 23.4% from 22.3% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario estimated “$8.4M / 23.1%” and said “the margin needs to be 22% or higher to keep the full-year guide credible.”

in_line: Pro forma revenue growth was 7.5%, within the preview’s cited 6–8% annual growth guide and consistent with its base case of about 7% growth.
Management reaffirmed the 6–8% pro forma revenue-growth guidance and low-to-mid-20% adjusted EBITDA margin outlook, as the preview expected.

The GE restructuring reduced revenue while improving Device Solutions profitability, as the preview anticipated: it expected a quarterly GE revenue headwind of roughly $1.7–$1.8 million, while the reported reduction was $1.6 million and Device Solutions gross margin improved.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $1.17 billion, implied by 90% growth from the $614.5 million reported a year earlier, versus the preview’s roughly $1.07 billion consensus. That is a clear revenue beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 revenue grew 90% year-over-year; the preview gives Q2 FY2025 revenue of $614.5 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue: ~$1.07B (+74% YoY).

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS of $5.80 exceeded both preview estimates of $5.01 and $5.20, by about 12% to 16%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted diluted EPS grew 116% from $2.69 to $5.80.

surprises.description: Management raised FY2026 guidance across revenue, adjusted EPS, and adjusted EBITDA. The new adjusted EPS midpoint of $20.00 is also above the preview’s approximately $18.89 full-year consensus, which was already above the prior guidance midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $4.0-$4.15 billion, adjusted diluted EPS of $19.70-$20.30, and adjusted EBITDA of $891-$916 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Whether management raises the range again ... Consensus already sits slightly above the $18.73 midpoint.

surprises.description: E-Infrastructure grew 192%, far exceeding the preview’s expectation of growth at rates approaching 60% or higher during 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: E-Infrastructure revenue grew 192% with adjusted operating margins at 24%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management guided the segment to grow at rates approaching 60% or higher during 2026.

surprises.description: Management cautioned that Q3 orders could soften and backlog could decline sequentially because awards are lumpy, before stronger awards in Q4 2026 and early 2027. This tempers the preview’s focus on continued backlog expansion, although management attributed the risk to timing rather than weakening demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management warned that award timing lumpiness could produce softer Q3 orders and a sequential backlog decline, with stronger awards expected in Q4 2026 and early 2027, emphasizing this reflects timing not weakening demand.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Backlog: Whether the $5.2B combined backlog keeps expanding.

in_line: Combined backlog continued expanding from the preview’s $5.2 billion prior-quarter level, reaching $5.6 billion.

surprises.description: The preview’s revenue consensus implied a 24.2% year-over-year decline, but reported production sales declined only 1.2%. That was a much shallower decline than the forecast implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 production sales declined 1.2% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $60.05M” versus year-ago actual of “$79.2M,” with “Implied YoY” of “−24.2%.”

surprises.description: The preview said management expected the truck cycle to begin recovering in H2 2026. Instead, truck sales remained a major drag, falling 23% year over year and accounting for 40% of product sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Truck represented 40% of total product sales and declined 23% year-over-year, remaining the primary headwind to consolidated growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said in May it expects the truck cycle … to begin recovering in H2 2026.”

surprises.description: Sales outside truck grew 20.8%, helping limit the overall decline despite the steep truck contraction. The preview flagged diversification-related markets as an issue to watch but did not anticipate growth of this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding the truck market, sales across remaining end markets grew 20.8%, reflecting successful diversification.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Powersports momentum, new business wins, and Mexico capex progress” were listed as key issues to watch.

surprises.description: The company had secured nearly $26 million in new business during the first half and said it remained on track for its $50 million full-year target. The awards were all new programs, with about 65% outside traditional truck and powersports markets, adding a more specific and favorable picture of the wins than the preview provided.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nearly $26 million of net new business wins in the first half,” “on track for its $50 million full-year target,” with “100% being new (not replacement) programs and ~65% outside traditional truck and powersports markets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “new business wins” as a key issue to watch and noted “$63M of FY2025 new business wins” were expected to ramp.

surprises.description: Awards secured over the prior 24 months were said to provide line of sight to production revenue opportunities above $300 million in 2027. The preview discussed the ramp of 2025 awards but did not flag this larger opportunity outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over $112 million in new business awards secured over 24 months provide line of sight to production revenue opportunities that could exceed $300 million in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the $63 million of 2025 awards would ramp, but gave no expectation for more than $300 million in 2027 production revenue opportunities.

in_line: Diluted EPS was $0.21, matching the preview’s $0.21 consensus estimate.
Management reiterated fiscal 2026 sales guidance of flat to up approximately 5%, consistent with the standing guidance in the preview.
The expectation that the majority of the $63 million in 2025 program awards would contribute meaningfully in the second half was reiterated, with full run rate expected in 2027.

surprises.description: Consolidated sales were $143 million, well above the preview’s $128.6–129.6 million consensus range—roughly 10% above its high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated sales rose 23% year-over-year to $143 million.”

surprises.description: Modern Oral net sales reached $68 million, substantially above the preview’s roughly $54 million base case and above even its bull-scenario threshold of $60 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Modern Oral gross and net sales grew 149% and 128% year-over-year respectively, with net revenue reaching $68 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base | … Modern Oral ~$54M net”; “Bull | … Modern Oral net ≥$60M.”

surprises.description: The company raised Modern Oral 2026 sales guidance much more than the preview’s then-current ranges implied: net sales guidance moved to $260–270 million from $210–225 million, and gross sales guidance to $330–350 million from $280–300 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 Modern Oral net sales guidance to $260-270 million from $210-225 million, and gross sales guidance to $330-350 million from $280-300 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Modern Oral gross sales $280–300M”; “Modern Oral net sales $210–225M.”

surprises.description: Modern Oral’s gross-to-net deduction was lower than the preview’s flat-at-about-25% base case: $87 million gross sales and $68 million net sales imply a deduction of about 22%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross revenue of $87 million” and “net revenue reaching $68 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base | … gap flat near 25%”; the preview also highlighted watching whether the gross-to-net gap widened from Q1’s roughly 25%.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $15 million, below the preview’s $16–19 million base-case range, although within its $12–15 million bear case. Management attributed the 50% year-over-year decline to heavy sales and marketing investment and ZigZag softness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell 50% year-over-year to $15 million (11% margin), driven by heavy sales and marketing investment and ZigZag softness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base | … Adj. EBITDA $16–19M”; “Bear | … Adj. EBITDA $12–15M.”

surprises.description: Management gave a long-term gross-margin target of approximately 70% once U.S. manufacturing is fully scaled, with the launch dependent on FDA approval expected by year-end. The preview discussed tariffs, margins, and regulatory commentary but did not anticipate this specific margin target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management targets approximately 70% long-term gross margins once U.S. manufacturing is fully scaled, pending FDA regulatory approval expected to launch by year-end.”

in_line: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was maintained at $70–90 million, matching the preview’s base case expectation that the range would be reaffirmed.
The company reiterated the target for chain-store count to increase 70% year-over-year by year-end 2026, matching the preview’s stated target.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $293.2 million, about $11 million above the preview’s roughly $282.2 million consensus estimate. The preview’s base case was near consensus, so the revenue result was a clear positive beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $293.2 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 revenue: ~$282.2M (MarketBeat) ... $282.24M (TradingView)”

surprises.description: The new 120-MW power contract carries expected annualized adjusted free cash flow of about $55 million on roughly $190 million of project capital, with payback under 3.5 years. The preview noted a 120-MW PPA, but did not anticipate these economics or the longer contract tenors: management now sees 15–20 years versus its initial 10-year target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Atlas signed its first behind-the-meter contract, a 120-megawatt PPA ... requiring ~$190 million in project capital and expected to generate ~$55 million of annualized adjusted free cash flow with a cash-on-cash payback under 3.5 years”; “contract tenors (now 15-20 years vs. an initial 10-year target) have grown substantially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Power segment ramp. Progress against the 1.4 GW Caterpillar framework, the 120 MW five-year PPA, and the >550 MW deployment target by mid-2027.”

surprises.description: Management said only 2–4 projects may be needed to contract the remaining uncommitted power capacity, rather than its prior assumption of 8–10. Larger projects and longer tenors mean fewer contracts could fill the capacity than previously thought.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now believes only 2 to 4 projects (versus a prior assumption of 8 to 10) could contract its remaining uncommitted power capacity, as project sizes and contract tenors ... have grown substantially.”

surprises.description: The new contract is not expected to produce meaningful cash flow soon: the Socorro facility is scheduled to electrify at the end of Q1 2027, with revenue recognition beginning in Q2 2027. The preview highlighted a mid-2027 power deployment target but did not flag that meaningful cash flow from this contract was still roughly a year away.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Socorro facility electrifies at the end of Q1 2027 with revenue recognition beginning in Q2 2027, so meaningful cash flow from this contract is roughly a year away.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “... the >550 MW deployment target by mid-2027.”

surprises.description: Sand volumes were weaker and less certain than the preview’s expectation that they would remain elevated: Q2 volumes were 5.6 million tons and below expectations, while Q3 guidance spans 5.3–6.0 million tons. Management also said it is deliberately giving up some near-term volume by holding pricing on tenders to seek better 2027 pricing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 sand volumes of 5.6 million tons came in below expectations due to late-June rig moves and schedule changes, with Q3 volumes guided to a wide 5.3-6.0 million ton range”; “intentionally trading near-term sand volumes to hold pricing, aiming to force ‘capacity discovery’ and drive accretive 2027 pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 commentary said volumes should ‘remain elevated for the remainder of 2026.’”

surprises.description: Q3 EBITDA guidance of $30–45 million implies a sequential step-down from Q2’s $49.5 million, rather than the steady operating backdrop suggested by the preview. Management attributed the decline to customer completion breaks and its decision to hold pricing on sand tenders.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 EBITDA guidance is $30 million to $45 million, a sequential step-down from Q2's $49.5 million, driven by customer completion breaks (~40-50% of variance) and a deliberate decision to hold pricing on sand tenders.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: Near consensus ... EBITDA near guide, volumes steady”; “Q1 commentary said volumes should ‘remain elevated for the remainder of 2026.’”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $49.5 million, essentially matching the company’s approximately $50 million guidance flagged in the preview.

surprises.description: The preview expected Asia-Pacific tapioca cost pressure to start reversing in Q2. Instead, tapioca route prices were up more than 40% since the start of the year, and management said margin pressure would persist until pass-throughs caught up over roughly one to 1.5 quarters.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tapioca route prices are up more than 40% since the start of the year due to weather-related supply constraints,” creating “near-term margin pressure” until pass-throughs catch up over “roughly 1 to 1.5 quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 should be the first quarter where Asia-Pacific tapioca cost pressure reverses.”

surprises.description: The preview cited adjusted EPS guidance of $10.45–$11.15 and raised the possibility of a low-end narrowing. The reported $10.30–$10.90 range is lower at both ends, including a floor below the preview's bear-case threshold of $10.45.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reaffirmed full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $10.30 to $10.90.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $10.45–$11.15”; the preview asked whether the range would be “reaffirmed or narrowed to the low end.”

surprises.description: Ingredion's full-year adjusted operating income outlook deteriorated from the prior flat-to-down-low-single-digit framing to down mid-single digits. The call attributed the revision to the sale of the majority stake in Pakistan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted operating income was revised to down mid-single digits after the sale of its majority stake in the Pakistan business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The May 5 outlook was “adjusted operating income flat to down LSD.”

surprises.description: The U.S./Canada food and industrial ingredients business remained weak: sales fell 7%, and its full-year operating income is now expected to decline 20%–25%. The preview was watching for a recovery from the Q1 operating-income trough of $34 million, although it gave no annual segment forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Food and Industrial Ingredients U.S./Canada net sales declined 7% and operating income fell to $58 million”; full-year segment operating income is “now guided down 20% to 25%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified the “F&II—U.S./Canada operating income trend off the $34M Q1 trough” as a key issue.

surprises.description: Full-year operating cash flow guidance was reduced by $25 million at both ends of the range versus the preview's $725–$825 million guide, despite the preview's focus on tracking against that target.
surprises.fact_evidence: Year-to-date cash from operations was $123 million after $231 million of working-capital investment, and full-year operating cash flow is now guided to “$700-$800 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating cash flow $725–825M.”

surprises.description: The company raised its planned capital spending by $50 million at both ends of the preview's range, citing funding for Argo reliability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Capex raised to $450-$490 million to fund Argo reliability.”

surprises.description: Q2 net sales beat the preview's $1.81 billion consensus estimate by about $40 million, or roughly 2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales rose 1% to $1.85 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 net sales consensus: “$1.81B.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating income fell 5%, better than the high-single-digit decline Ingredion had framed for Q2 in May. This was also within the preview's base-case expectation of a 4%–6% decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income fell 5% to $258 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The May call framed adjusted operating income as “down high-single-digits”; the preview's base scenario expected it to “fall about 4–6%.”

surprises.description: Texture & Healthful Solutions posted unusually strong results: 7% volume growth and its second-highest quarterly operating income ever. The preview discussed the segment's cost outlook but did not anticipate this level of volume growth or earnings performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Texture & Healthful Solutions delivered its “second-highest quarterly operating income ever,” with sales up 5% on “7% sales volume growth,” its ninth consecutive quarter of volume growth.

surprises.description: The call introduced a potentially consequential industry development absent from the preview: a competitor plans to close a facility representing about 5% of U.S. industry capacity in 2027, which management expects to affect contracting dynamics.
surprises.fact_evidence: A competitor's announced closure of a facility representing “about 5% of U.S. industry capacity in 2027” is expected to “meaningfully impact industry contracting dynamics going forward.”

in_line: Argo had been expected to return to operation during Q2; it exited June at normal production rates, with management expecting historical margins by year-end.
Tate & Lyle shareholder approval had already been reported before the release, and the call reiterated the preview's roughly 18-month path to about 2.5x net leverage.

surprises.description: Merck's Q2 revenue was $16.6 billion, above the preview's $16.33 billion consensus, and grew 5% rather than the roughly 3.3% growth implied by the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was $16.6 billion, up 5% (4% ex-FX).”

surprises.description: KEYTRUDA family sales reached $8.4 billion, beating the preview's $8.06 billion consensus and growing 4% rather than the expected 1.3%. The call also cautioned that U.S. growth will moderate as indications approach peak penetration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “KEYTRUDA family sales rose 4% to $8.4 billion,” with U.S. growth expected to moderate as key indications reach peak penetration.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Keytruda (total, Q2) … $8.06B”; “+1.3% y/y; sharp slowdown from Q1's +12%.”

surprises.description: The Q2 loss was less severe than expected: Merck reported a loss of $0.13 per share versus the preview's $0.26 loss consensus. The Terns charge was also slightly smaller than the roughly $2.35 per-share charge anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 loss of $0.13 per share,” driven by a “one-time $2.31 per share” Terns charge.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS (Q2, as reported) … –$0.26”; the Terns charge was expected to be “~$2.35/sh.”

surprises.description: Merck raised its full-year revenue outlook above the prior range: both the low end and high end moved up, from $65.8–$67.0 billion to $66.3–$67.3 billion. That is a stronger update than the preview's base case of narrowing the range toward the upper half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised and narrowed full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $66.3–$67.3 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior company range was “$65.8B–$67.0B”; the preview's base case was that “FY guidance is narrowed toward the upper half.”

surprises.description: Merck lowered its full-year gross-margin outlook to approximately 81% because of higher inventory reserves, an unfavorable update not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year gross margin was lowered to approximately 81% on higher inventory reserves.”

surprises.description: Management said positive Phase III readouts for sac-TMT, tulisokibart, and IDXD are arriving faster than the previously expected 2027 timing, indicating a quicker pipeline cadence than that timing implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management cited “positive Phase III readouts for sac-TMT (endometrial cancer), tulisokibart (ulcerative colitis induction), and IDXD occurring faster than the previously expected 2027 timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Previously expected 2027 timing.”

surprises.description: WELIREG secured its first earlier-stage indication, an adjuvant renal-cell-carcinoma approval, a product milestone the preview did not mention.
surprises.fact_evidence: “WELIREG … recently secured its first earlier-stage indication (adjuvant renal cell carcinoma) via the LITESPARK-022 approval.”

in_line: The company remained on pace for approximately $3 billion in share repurchases, consistent with the preview's focus on the planned ~$3 billion buyback pace.

surprises.description: Powell's revenue was below the preview's $318.3 million consensus, at $312 million; the alternate estimate of about $321.5 million was higher still. The shortfall was modest, despite 9% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue grew 9% year-over-year to $312 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $318.3M (+11.2% YoY)” and “Alternate revenue estimate | ~$321.5M.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS was $1.42, below the preview's $1.49 adjusted-EPS consensus and short of the expected return to double-digit EPS growth. The comparison is not perfectly like-for-like because the call reports diluted EPS while the preview cites adjusted EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income rose to $52.2 million ($1.42 per diluted share) from $48.2 million ($1.32 per diluted share) a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $1.49 (+12.9%).” The preview also says, “Consensus expects EPS growth to return to double digits (+12.9%).”

surprises.description: Orders were exceptionally strong: Powell reported a record $934 million, roughly double the prior quarter, and a 3.0x book-to-bill. The preview highlighted orders as a key watch item, but this scale of intake—including a $400 million-plus data-center award and other large awards—was a substantial result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record quarterly new orders of $934 million, nearly 3x higher than the prior year and roughly double the prior quarter, producing a book-to-bill ratio of 3.0x.” Orders included “a $400 million-plus Phase 1 behind-the-meter mega data center order,” a “~$75 million” fertilizer facility award, a “~$60 million” LNG award, and “over $350 million of diversified awards.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Backlog and orders after the >$400M data-center award. Any new mega-project disclosures would be the main datapoint.”

surprises.description: Backlog reached $2.4 billion, up $619 million sequentially from the $1.8 billion reported at the prior quarter-end and surpassing $2 billion for the first time. The known post-quarter data-center award provided a reason to expect growth, but the reported level was a major step up.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog reached a record $2.4 billion, $967 million higher year-over-year and $619 million higher sequentially, surpassing $2 billion for the first time in the company's 79-year history.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Backlog $1.8B at end of March 2026 ... including a >$400M data-center order awarded after quarter-end.”

surprises.description: Petrochemical revenue deteriorated rather than showing signs of stabilization: it fell 49%, compared with the 37% year-over-year decline in Q2 cited in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Petrochemical revenue fell 49%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Petrochemical trend. The segment fell 37% YoY in Q2. Signs of stabilization would help.”

surprises.description: Powell disclosed that only about 54% of backlog is convertible over the next 12 months, down from the low 60% range last quarter. The company attributed the lower share to the large order intake, so the record backlog also includes a smaller near-term-convertible proportion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately $1.3 billion (about 54%) of backlog is convertible over the next 12 months, down from the low 60% range last quarter due to the large recent order intake.”

surprises.description: Management announced substantial capacity additions not anticipated in the preview: a Board-authorized leased facility of about 300,000 square feet and a near-complete yard expansion, with total footprint expected to grow over 20% by fiscal year-end 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Capacity expansion initiatives, including a Board-authorized ~300,000 sq ft leased facility (available in fiscal Q2/Q3 2027) and the near-complete Jacintoport yard expansion (335,000 sq ft, supporting over $100 million of incremental annual revenue), will grow total footprint over 20% by end of fiscal 2026.”

surprises.description: Management warned that craft labor availability may become a challenge in fiscal 2027–2028, introducing a potential constraint on executing the higher backlog and planned capacity growth that the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management warned “craft labor availability may become a challenge in fiscal 2027-2028.”

in_line: Gross margin was 30.6%, roughly flat year-over-year, consistent with the preview's cited May comment that margins should “remain consistent with the performance levels achieved in the prior year.”

surprises.description: Centuri reported Q2 revenue of $962 million, well above the preview’s $836 million consensus estimate—about 15% higher than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record $962 million in Q2 2026 revenue,” up 33% year-over-year.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.24, above the preview’s primary consensus estimate of $0.20, though the preview noted substantial disagreement among estimate sources.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income of $24.4 million ($0.24/share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $0.20 (primary)” and “Q2 consensus EPS ranges from $0.13 to $0.45 across aggregators.”

surprises.description: Centuri raised its full-year revenue guidance above the range in force before the release. It also lifted the low end of adjusted EBITDA and adjusted net income guidance, while leaving their high ends unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was raised to revenue of $3.59-$3.79 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $285-$310 million, and adjusted net income of $60-$75 million,” incorporating JJ White and about $12 million of fuel headwind.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The guidance in force was “Total revenue | $3.24–$3.54B,” “Adjusted EBITDA | $280–$310M,” and “Adjusted net income | $55–$75M.” The preview also said “Guidance action” was a key metric and that a raise, “especially to EBITDA,” would be the cleanest bull signal.

surprises.description: The preview expected annual bookings of 1.1–1.2x revenue; Centuri reported year-to-date book-to-bill of 1.3x and a 2026 bookings target of about $4.4 billion, indicating stronger booking pace than that benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nearly $850 million in Q2” bookings brought year-to-date bookings “above $2.2 billion at a 1.3x book-to-bill,” with a target of “~$4.4 billion in total 2026 bookings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY target is 1.1–1.2x, below H1 2025's 2.3x.”

surprises.description: Despite the revenue and guidance strength, base gross profit margin fell to 7.9%, and management cited fuel costs and gas-capacity investments as meaningful pressures—worse than the preview’s base-case expectation of margins being roughly in line.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Base gross profit margin declined to 7.9% from 8.9% a year ago,” with a combined “95 basis point hit” from elevated fuel costs and gas capacity investments.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario anticipated “Margins roughly in line.”

surprises.description: Centuri’s Q2 U.S. Gas margin was only 4.2% despite 45% revenue growth, but management guided to about 7.5% gas margins in the second half. That recovery outlook was not specified in the preview and adds a favorable path beyond the current-quarter result.
surprises.fact_evidence: U.S. Gas revenue “grew 45% to $489.5 million,” while gross margin fell “to 4.2% from 7.8% due to onboarding costs,” with management “guiding to ~7.5% gas margins in the second half.”

surprises.description: Centuri made an unpreviewed $62 million cash acquisition of JJ White, which it expects to add over $20 million of annualized gross profit while maintaining its year-end leverage target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Acquired JJ White for approximately $62 million cash from existing liquidity,” expecting it to “add over $20 million of annualized gross profit while maintaining the 2x year-end leverage target.”

surprises.description: Centuri disclosed a $9 million write-off of old City of Chicago receivables, which reduced U.S. Gas revenue; the preview had not flagged this item. The company said it had not budgeted for collection and there was no cash-flow impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wrote off $9 million of pre-2020 City of Chicago receivables, reducing U.S. Gas revenue but with no cash flow impact as collection was not budgeted.”

surprises.description: Centuri announced its largest-ever data center project, a $125 million award, and said its data center opportunity pipeline is about $2 billion; the preview had identified data-center progress as a catalyst but did not anticipate these reported figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Secured its largest-ever data center project, a $125 million electrical infrastructure award,” and “holds about $2 billion of data center opportunities in its pipeline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Data center and bid-work progress” as a catalyst, without specifying an award or pipeline size.

surprises.description: Centuri said it expects to exit 2026 with more than $3.6 billion of 2027 revenue coverage, a 20% organic increase, providing stronger forward visibility than the preview had specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expects to exit 2026 with over $3.6 billion of 2027 revenue coverage (a 20% organic increase).”

surprises.description: Management reported bid margins up more than 10% year over year, a favorable quantified update on bid-work economics that the preview had identified as relevant to the long-term margin framework but had not quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported bid margins up more than 10% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Data center and bid-work progress” as underwriting the 2029 framework, but gave no expected bid-margin change.

in_line: U.S. Gas gross margin was 4.2%, just above the preview’s stated 4%+ threshold for a clearly positive margin and avoiding the bear-case outcome of a second negative quarter.
Q2 bookings were below the record $1.8 billion Q2 2025 level, consistent with the preview’s expectation that bookings would decelerate from that record quarter.
Management reaffirmed the 2029 base gross margin target of 9.7%; the preview had identified the longer-term framework as relevant but did not forecast a change to that target.

surprises.description: Cummins was expected to post a consolidated EBITDA margin of roughly 18.5%–19.1%, but Q2 margin was 17.5%. The company attributed the decline to tariffs and higher variable compensation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record EBITDA of $1.7 billion,” though “EBITDA margin declined to 17.5% from 18.4% a year ago due to tariffs and higher variable compensation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied EBITDA margin ~18.5–19.1%”; the preview also said consensus implied a margin “about 60–100 bps above the FY guide midpoint of 18.1%.”

surprises.description: Q2 EPS was below both preview estimates: $6.73 versus $7.33 consensus and $7.21 in the alternative compile. The reported figure included $0.21 per share of unfavorable discrete tax items, which explains part, but not all, of the gap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net earnings were $932 million, or $6.73 per diluted share,” with “$29 million ($0.21 per share) in unfavorable discrete tax items.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS $7.33” and “EPS (alt.) $7.21.”

surprises.description: Cummins raised its full-year revenue growth outlook to 10%–13%, above the prior 8%–11% range in the preview. This was a stronger update than the preview’s H2 math suggested was needed to stay within the existing guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth outlook to 10%-13% (from 8%-11%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue growth: +8% to +11%”; the preview said staying inside that guide required H2 growth of roughly 10%–16%.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue modestly exceeded the preview’s consensus estimate: $9.5 billion compared with $9.33 billion. That is a small beat, even though the preview had already expected growth of about 8% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q2 2026 sales of $9.5 billion, up 9% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $9.33B” and “+7.9%.”

surprises.description: Power-generation demand was particularly strong in China, with China revenue including joint ventures up 30% and power-generation equipment sales up 88%. The preview discussed data-center demand but did not anticipate these China growth figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China revenues including joint ventures rose 30% year-over-year to $2.3 billion, with power generation equipment sales up 88% on accelerating data center demand.”

surprises.description: Cummins disclosed a multiyear agreement with a global hyperscaler that provides visibility into several gigawatts of future backup-power genset demand, a new source of demand visibility not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Signed a multiyear agreement with a global hyperscaler securing visibility into several gigawatts of future backup power genset demand.”

surprises.description: Diesel genset demand is extending well beyond the near-term horizon: new 95-liter orders are booking into the second half of 2028, and management said demand is still growing rather than plateauing. The preview did not anticipate this lead-time update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diesel genset lead times have extended, with new 95-liter orders now booking into the second half of 2028, and demand continues to grow rather than plateau.”

surprises.description: Management quantified a coming reduction in incentive-compensation pressure: it expects the expense to be about $25 million lower per quarter in H2 and roughly $200 million lower going into 2027. The preview asked about the H2 margin bridge but did not forecast this source of relief.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Higher incentive compensation tied to record earnings weighed on Q2 margins across segments but is expected to be ~$25 million lower per quarter in H2 and reset roughly $200 million lower going into 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Management's framing will set the H2 margin bridge,” and noted uncertainty about “Tariff/IEEPA recovery durability.”

surprises.description: The Board approved a 10% quarterly dividend increase, extending Cummins’ streak of annual dividend growth to 17 years. The preview did not flag a dividend increase as an expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board approved a 10% increase in the quarterly dividend—the 17th consecutive year of dividend growth.”

surprises.description: Cummins laid out a phased transition for EPA 2027 engines: limited X15 and X10 production begins in January 2027, with the full X15 ramp in Q4, while current X12, L9, and B-platform engines remain on sale through 2027. The preview flagged EPA 2027 as an issue but did not anticipate this specific schedule.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Under EPA's proposed 2027 rule flexibilities, Cummins will pursue a phased transition—beginning limited X15 and X10 production in January 2027 with full X15 ramp in Q4 2027—while continuing to sell current X12, L9, and B-platform engines through 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “The FY26 guidance, especially the NA Class 8 assumption” and said orders were spilling into 1H27 “ahead of EPA 2027,” but did not give a production-transition schedule.

in_line: Power Systems Q2 EBITDA margin was 24.5%, essentially in line with the preview’s 24.7% consensus estimate.

surprises.description: The preview expected Q2 EPS of $11.28–$11.30; Grainger reported diluted EPS of $12.01, a clear beat of roughly 6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS up over 20% to $12.01.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS | $11.28 (Zacks)” and “EPS | $11.30.”

surprises.description: The preview estimated total organic daily sales growth of about 8.5% and revenue of roughly $4.95–$4.96 billion. Grainger reported 13.7% daily organic constant-currency sales growth, well above the growth estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 reported sales grew 10.3% (13.7% on a daily organic constant currency basis).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$4.95–4.96B | +8.8%” and “Total organic daily sales growth | ~8.5% (est.).”

surprises.description: The preview expected full-year EPS guidance of $44.25–$46.25 to be reaffirmed, raised, or narrowed; Grainger raised it to $45.50–$47.25, with the midpoint more than $1 above the prior midpoint. It also raised daily organic constant-currency sales growth guidance from 9.5%–12.0% to 11.5%–13% and operating margin guidance from 15.6%–16.0% to 15.8%–16.2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year EPS guidance to $45.50-$47.25 (up over 17% at the midpoint), an improvement of over $1 versus prior guidance”; “Full-year daily organic constant currency sales growth guidance was raised to 11.5%-13%, with operating margin guidance increased to 15.8%-16.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS: $44.25–$46.25”; “Daily organic constant-currency sales growth: 9.5%–12.0%”; “Adjusted operating margin: 15.6%–16.0%.” The preview described reaffirming, raising, or narrowing EPS guidance as the question to watch.

surprises.description: The preview flagged tariff and cost pressure as a margin risk, but Q2 gross margin expanded 100 basis points; 90 basis points came from EPA/tariff refunds on Grainger-imported products. That refund benefit also means the strong Q2 margin is not fully recurring.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 100 basis points to 39.5%, including a 90 basis point tailwind from EPA/tariff refunds on Grainger-imported products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Margin versus tariff and cost pressure. Q1's guidance raise leaned on strong MRO demand and price realization. Watch whether tariff-related cost and price timing returns as a margin risk.”

surprises.description: The preview expected High Touch Solutions sales growth of about 7.4% on an organic daily basis; the reported segment growth was 11.9%. The call also described strong demand across manufacturing, government, contractors, and retail.
