surprises.fact_evidence: “High Touch Solutions grew sales 11.9% with operating margin up 70 basis points to 17.3%, benefiting from strong manufacturing, government, contractor, and retail (data center-linked) demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “High-Touch Solutions N.A. sales | ~$3.81B (+7.4% organic daily).”

surprises.description: The preview expected Endless Assortment organic daily growth of 12.2%; the segment instead grew 20.6% on a daily organic constant-currency basis. Its operating margin also rose 160 basis points to 11.5%, a segment margin outcome the preview did not specify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Endless Assortment sales rose 20.6% on a daily organic constant currency basis, with Zoro U.S. up 18.4% and MonotaRO up 24% in local constant currency, and segment operating margin up 160 basis points to 11.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Endless Assortment sales | ~$1.03B (+10.8%; organic daily +12.2%).”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that roughly $45 million of MonotaRO sales came from customers prebuying petroleum-related products amid the Middle East conflict. That boost had fully subsided and was expected to slow MonotaRO’s second-half growth; the preview did not flag this timing factor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “MonotaRO's growth included roughly $45 million of customer prebuying of petroleum-related products tied to Middle East conflict, a benefit that has fully subsided and will slow second-half growth.”

surprises.description: The call gave a strong near-term sales update—July sales were up more than 13% daily organic constant currency and Q3 sales were expected to exceed $5 billion, up over 12%—but also guided to operating margin in the mid-15% range as tariff refunds lap. The preview provided no Q3 sales or margin outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Preliminary July sales are up north of 13% daily organic constant currency, supporting Q3 guidance of over $5 billion (up over 12%), with Q3 operating margin expected to drop to the mid-15% range as tariff refunds lap.”

surprises.description: The call said data center-related project spending added about 90 basis points to High Touch growth, while diluting gross margin but remaining neutral to operating margin. The preview did not identify this demand source or its margin mix effect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data center-related project spend added about 90 basis points to High Touch growth this year, boosting revenue but diluting gross margin while remaining neutral to operating margin.”

surprises.description: The CFO announced she would step down effective September 4, 2026, with the controller named interim CFO and an external search to begin. The preview did not mention a CFO transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Deidra Merriwether is stepping down effective September 4, 2026, with VP Controller Laurie Thompson appointed interim CFO and an external search to begin immediately.”

in_line: Q2 operating margin was 16.1%, close to and just above the prior 15.6%–16.0% full-year guide band the preview highlighted as a benchmark for a pullback from Q1's 16.7%.

surprises.description: PSEG’s Q2 non-GAAP operating EPS was $0.86, above the preview’s roughly $0.80 consensus (and the cited $0.794 estimate), despite the preview noting that Zacks’ model did not predict a beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 non-GAAP operating earnings of $0.86 per share,” up from $0.77 a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP EPS” consensus: “$0.80” and “$0.794”; Zacks said its model “does not predict an earnings beat.”

surprises.description: The reported GAAP result appears below the preview’s alternate-basis diluted EPS estimate: GAAP net income was $0.67 per share, versus the cited $0.83 estimate. The call fact gives GAAP net income per share, so the comparison is less direct than the non-GAAP comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income fell to $0.67” per share from $1.17 a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 diluted EPS” consensus: “$0.83”; the preview labels this an “Alternate basis.”

surprises.description: PSE&G plans to bring forward its base-rate filing substantially, targeting year-end 2026 rather than the previously required 2029 deadline. The preview discussed rate increases as a tailwind but did not flag this accelerated filing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PSE&G plans to file to update base rates by year-end 2026, pulling forward from the previously required 2029 deadline,” citing regulatory lag and distribution rate-base additions.

surprises.description: A PJM transmission cost-allocation change is expected to benefit customers by about $65 million annually prospectively, with roughly $33 million of benefit through year-end 2026; the preview did not identify this benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A PJM transmission cost allocation change effective June 1, 2026 will deliver roughly $33 million in customer benefit through year-end 2026 and an expected prospective annual benefit of approximately $65 million.”

surprises.description: PSEG disclosed a prospective headwind from possible elimination of the RTO transmission incentive: about $40 million of annual net income, or roughly $0.08 per share, beginning in 2027. This specific policy risk was not in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Potential elimination of the 50 basis point RTO transmission incentive represents an annual headwind of about $40 million net income (roughly $0.08 per share) effective January 2027, with no impact on 2026 results.”

surprises.description: PSEG Nuclear cleared about 3,600 MW in PJM’s latest auction at the $325/MW-day collar ceiling, modestly below the prior $333; the preview discussed nuclear offtake talks but did not anticipate or provide an auction-price expectation. The uncapped price would have been $555, making the cap a constraint on the potential price.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PSEG Nuclear cleared approximately 3,600 megawatts” at “$325 per megawatt day (the collar ceiling)” for 2028–2029, “a modest decline from the prior $333,” versus an uncapped price of $555.

surprises.description: The quarter’s nuclear output and pricing more than offset the loss of expired zero-emission certificates, providing a positive operating offset to the cost pressures the preview said investors would be watching. The preview did not specify an expectation for generation or ZEC replacement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PSEG Nuclear generated 7.8 terawatt hours of carbon-free baseload power in the quarter at a 92% capacity factor,” and “the absence of expired zero emission certificates was more than offset by higher realized prices and generation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Cost headwinds vs. rate tailwinds,” including higher interest, O&M and depreciation costs.

surprises.description: PSE&G announced residential gas-bill reductions and a sizable ZEC refund to customers, neither of which was anticipated in the preview; the provided facts do not quantify the effect on PSEG earnings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PSE&G filed to lower residential gas bills by more than 5% beginning October 1 and is refunding roughly $166 million of zero emission certificates over 12 months to customers.”

surprises.description: PSEG said its five-year investment program can be funded without new equity or asset sales, removing a potential need for dilution or divestitures that the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PSEG's $24 billion to $28 billion five-year capital investment program, including $22.5 billion to $25.5 billion of regulated CapEx, can be funded without issuing new equity or selling assets.”

in_line: PSEG reaffirmed 2026 non-GAAP operating EPS guidance of $4.28–$4.40, consistent with the preview’s stated guidance and base-case expectation of a reaffirmation.

surprises.description: Q2 consolidated revenue was about $85.8 million, above the preview’s $83.0 million estimate; the reported 6.4% year-over-year decline was also milder than the preview’s projected 9.4% decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated net revenues fell 6.4% year-over-year to approximately $85.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My Q2'26 estimate” for net revenue was “~$83.0M (−9.4% YoY).”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA came in at $11.7 million, modestly above the preview’s $11.0 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated adjusted EBITDA declined 16% to $11.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My Q2'26 estimate” for adjusted EBITDA was “~$11.0M.”

surprises.description: Digital revenue fell 8.4% to $9.4 million, contrary to the preview’s expectation—based on the CFO’s comments—that Q2 digital revenue would be up or at least flat to positive year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Digital segment declined 8.4% to $9.4 million, driven by reduced DEI-focused spending and broader macroeconomic caution among clients.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the CFO stated Q2 digital revenue “is actually up” and the division was “confident about making their numbers”; it also flagged “Digital flat or better YoY.”

surprises.description: TV One had 27.3 million traditional linear Nielsen subscribers, below the preview’s 28.5 million watch threshold and down from 34.3 million a year earlier, indicating sharper subscriber erosion than that threshold anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TV One's traditional linear Nielsen subscribers dropped to 27.3 million from 34.3 million a year earlier, reflecting accelerating cord-cutting in linear cable.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist set “TV One subscribers at or above 28.5M.”

in_line: Management lowered FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance from $60 million to the mid-$50 million range, consistent with the preview’s base case of a trim to $52–56 million.

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $1.94, well above the $1.52 consensus and even above the preview’s bull-case range of $1.72–$1.85. The per-share result was substantially stronger than investors were led to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was $1.94” for the quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS $1.52” consensus; the bull scenario projected “$1.72–1.85.”

surprises.description: Fee-related earnings rose 49% year over year and the FRE margin expanded to 53% from 51%, aided by strong fee-related performance revenues. The preview flagged FRE presentation and performance-revenue disclosure as important but did not anticipate this level of reported growth or margin expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fee-related earnings rose 49% year-over-year to $124 million, with FRE margin expanding to 53% from 51% a year earlier, aided by strong fee-related performance revenues.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any change to stock-based compensation treatment or fee-related performance revenue disclosure would matter more than an EPS beat.”

surprises.description: Evergreen net inflows were nearly $640 million, below the preview’s base-case range of $700 million–$1.1 billion. Although 10 of 12 funds had positive flows and platform AUM surpassed $19 billion, the aggregate inflow was lighter than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Evergreen platform generated nearly $640 million of net inflows and surpassed $19 billion in AUM, with 10 of 12 funds showing positive net inflows while the non-U.S. multi-strategy equity fund posted net outflows.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario projected “net inflows $0.7–1.1B.”

surprises.description: Hamilton Lane reported two specific portfolio monetizations that the preview did not identify: Russell is expected to generate about $50 million of proceeds and an $18 million gain, while Canoe’s Bloomberg acquisition is expected to generate about $30 million of proceeds and a $15 million gain. These are additional prospective gains beyond the preview’s general call to watch realization commentary.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Russell (expected ~$50 million proceeds, ~$18 million gain, closing Q1 CY2027)” and “Canoe's Bloomberg acquisition (~$30 million proceeds, ~$15 million gain).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch incentive fees … and realization commentary.”

surprises.description: Securitize had become public at $6.94 per share, leaving Hamilton Lane with about 1.5 million shares subject to a 180-day lockup. The preview discussed unrealized carry and realizations generally but did not anticipate this specific public listing or the resulting potential liquidity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Securitize (now public at $6.94/share with ~1.5 million shares under a 180-day lockup).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Unrealized carried interest. $1.546B across 124 vehicles at 3/31/26, +23% Y/Y. Watch incentive fees … and realization commentary.”

in_line: Management and advisory fees were $161 million, within the preview’s $158–166 million base-case range.
The direct equity fund raise closed at $3.8 billion, matching the preview’s stated final-close amount.
The $0.60 quarterly dividend and $2.40 fiscal 2027 target, representing an 11% annual increase, matched the preview.

surprises.description: MPC reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $17.73, above the preview’s consensus figures of $14.52 and $13.26 and also above its $17.00–$18.50 bull-case range’s lower end. The earnings result was substantially stronger than the preview’s base-case EPS range of $13.50–$15.00.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS $14.52 (Zacks) or $13.26 (Barchart mean)” and “Base | Adj. EPS $13.50–$15.00”

surprises.description: R&M performance was stronger than expected: Q2 capture reached 112%, above the preview’s 95–100% base-case range, and R&M adjusted EBITDA was about $6.7 billion versus $5.80 billion consensus. The preview had identified capture as the highest-signal measure and warned that below about 95% would indicate a quality miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “System-wide R&M margin capture reached 112% in Q2” and “R&M segment adjusted EBITDA was approximately $6.7 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “R&M adj. EBITDA $5.80B”; “Base ... capture 95–100%”; “capture below about 95% would turn a headline beat into a quality miss.”

surprises.description: Management gave a specific Q3 capture headwind from about $290 million of turnaround expenses at Gulf Coast and Mid-Con conversion units, and noted Q3 has historically been the most muted quarter for capture. The preview’s main Q3 catalyst was confirmation that July’s record cracks were being realized and that Q3 margins were holding near those levels; the call facts instead highlight the headwind and provide no such confirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects ... approximately $290 million in turnaround expenses ... creating a capture headwind, and Q3 has historically been the most muted quarter averaging 95% capture.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management framing Q3 capture and realized cracks as holding near July levels would be the main upside trigger.”

surprises.description: The regional utilization results diverged from the preview’s assumptions: Gulf Coast utilization beat its 99% guide at 100%, while West Coast utilization missed its 96% assumption at 93%. Overall utilization was in line at 94%, with Mid-Con also matching its 87% guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Refineries ran at 94% overall utilization ... Gulf Coast at 100% ... West Coast at 93% ... and Mid-Con at 87%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Crude utilization ... 94% (Gulf Coast 99%, Mid-Continent 87%, West Coast 96%).”

surprises.description: MPC said year-to-date unplanned downtime was the lowest of the decade, a stronger operating reliability result than the preview had specifically anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date unplanned downtime was the lowest of the decade.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Utilization versus the 94% guide, including the West Coast assumption ... and any unplanned downtime.”

surprises.description: MPLX raised its 2026 growth-capital outlook by $500 million to $2.9 billion, pulling forward Gulf Coast fractionation spending. The preview did not flag an increase in MPLX growth capital.
surprises.fact_evidence: “MPLX raised its 2026 growth capital outlook by $500 million to $2.9 billion, pulling forward Gulf Coast fractionation spending.”

surprises.description: MPLX is targeting 12.5% annual distribution growth in both 2026 and 2027. The preview mentioned a 12.5% target but did not indicate that the target covered both years, so the 2027 commitment extends the stated outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[MPLX] is targeting 12.5% annual distribution growth in both 2026 and 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “12.5% MPLX distribution growth target.”

surprises.description: Management reported that more than 9 million bpd of global refining capacity was offline, about 4 million bpd above historical norms, and used that backdrop to support an enhanced mid-cycle outlook into 2027. The preview flagged a possible raised through-cycle view as important but did not anticipate this specific capacity evidence or the stronger outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 9 million bpd of global refined capacity offline—about 4 million bpd above historical norms—with over 2.8 million bpd ... of Russian capacity down, supporting an enhanced mid-cycle outlook into 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Whether management raises its through-cycle earnings view matters more for the multiple than the quarter itself.”

surprises.description: Renewable Diesel adjusted EBITDA rose about $277 million year over year, with 95% utilization after the Martinez turnaround. The preview did not provide an expectation for this segment’s results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Renewable Diesel segment adjusted EBITDA rose approximately $277 million year-over-year with utilization at 95% post-Martinez turnaround.”

surprises.description: Q2 working capital provided a large $3.8 billion source of cash, but the call also noted that some of the benefit came from crude-exchange timing and that SPR barrels must be repaid. The preview did not anticipate this sizable, partly temporary cash-flow contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Working capital was a $3.8 billion source of cash in Q2 from higher payables, crude exchange timing, and inventory draws, with an obligation to repay SPR barrels.”

in_line: Overall refinery utilization was 94%, matching the preview’s 94% company guide.
Net refinery throughput was nearly 3 million barrels per day, broadly matching the preview’s approximately 2.99 million bpd expectation.
Share repurchases were $2.5 billion, at the upper end of the preview’s expected $2.0–$2.5 billion Q2 range.

surprises.description: Knife River raised FY26 revenue guidance to $3.4–$3.6 billion from $3.3–$3.5 billion, lifting both ends of the range. The preview expected the company might raise or narrow its guidance but gave $3.3–$3.5 billion as the existing range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $3.4–$3.6 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance (FY26): $3.3B – $3.5B”; the preview said investors would look for “a raise or narrowing” of the range.

surprises.description: Despite reaffirming FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $520–$560 million, management said results are trending toward the midpoint rather than the upper end. That fell short of the preview’s expectation that the company might retain its prior “upper half” trajectory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reaffirmed adjusted EBITDA guidance of $520–$560 million while signaling results are trending toward the midpoint rather than the upper end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had said results were “trending toward the upper half” of the FY26 revenue and adjusted EBITDA ranges; the preview’s base scenario anticipated the “upper half” language being kept.

surprises.description: Aggregate volumes grew 14%, with product-mix-adjusted pricing up 8%, substantially exceeding the preview’s expectation of mid-single-digit aggregates price and volume growth. The reported pricing increase was only 3% because a large sale of lower-priced natural fines diluted the mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aggregate volumes grew 14% (75% organic, 25% from acquisitions) with product-mix-adjusted pricing up 8%, though as-reported pricing rose only 3% due to a 630,000-ton sale of lower-priced natural fines.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Guidance assumptions included “mid-single-digit aggregates price/volume growth.”

surprises.description: The company cut its full-year aggregate margin expansion outlook to roughly 100 basis points from the prior 200-basis-point target. Higher delivery volumes and fuel surcharges booked at cost were cited as pressures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aggregate margin expansion guidance for the year was lowered to roughly 100 basis points from a prior 200-basis-point target, pressured by 41% higher delivery volumes and fuel surcharges booked at cost.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior 200-basis-point target is stated in the call facts; the preview did not discuss aggregate margin guidance.

surprises.description: Management identified roughly $24 million of Q2 external headwinds from higher energy costs, delayed projects in Texas, Hawaii and Alaska, and unfavorable project type or incentive timing. The preview did not anticipate these specific pressures; they provide context for the flat reported adjusted EBITDA, which was up 7% excluding property-sale gains.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Three external headwinds totaling roughly $24 million in Q2: ~$6 million from higher energy costs, ~$10 million from delayed projects (Texas, Hawaii, Alaska), and ~$8 million from unfavorable project type/timing of incentives.” Adjusted EBITDA was flat as reported but rose 7% excluding asset-sale gains.

surprises.description: Knife River said Strata is expected to deliver a record 2026 and outperform its original EBITDA projections by more than 15%, helped by a record North Dakota DOT budget. The preview discussed acquisition contributions generally but did not anticipate this level of outperformance from Strata.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Strata acquisition is expected to deliver a record 2026, outperforming original EBITDA projections by more than 15%, supported by a record North Dakota DOT budget.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “M&A contribution” and noted deals supported expected growth, but gave no Strata-specific forecast.

surprises.description: Ready-mix production costs fell 6% per cubic yard and gross profit rose 21%; the preview anticipated mid-teens ready-mix volume growth but did not flag these cost and profit gains. Asphalt also reported 24% volume growth and 24% gross-profit growth, with no asphalt-specific expectation in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ready-mix volumes rose 15% (aided by Texcrete, expected to double Texas volumes) with production costs down 6% per cubic yard and gross profit up 21%; asphalt volumes rose 24% with gross profit up 24%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “mid-teens ready-mix volume growth”; it provided no ready-mix cost, gross-profit, or asphalt forecast.

surprises.description: Net leverage ended Q2 at 3.2x, above the 2.9x level cited from Q1, although management expects to finish 2026 near its 2.5x long-term target with no revolver borrowings. The preview specifically flagged leverage versus 2.9x as something to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ended Q2 at 3.2x net leverage (vs. 3.1x a year ago), and expects to finish 2026 near its 2.5x long-term target with no revolver borrowings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “net leverage versus 2.9x at Q1.”

surprises.description: The company added $400 million to its Term Loan B at a lower rate, a financing action not anticipated in the preview. Management still expects year-end leverage near its long-term target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company amended its Term Loan B to add $400 million at a lower rate.”

in_line: Q2 revenue growth of 13% was close to the preview’s approximately 12% year-over-year expectation.
Ready-mix volume growth of 15% was consistent with the preview’s expectation of mid-teens growth.

The company reaffirmed FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance at $520–$560 million, the range shown in the preview, although management’s midpoint-oriented outlook was weaker than the preview’s expected upper-half trajectory.

surprises.description: FreightCar America cut its FY2026 delivery, revenue, and adjusted EBITDA ranges, citing a delayed second-half production ramp that shifts some deliveries into early 2027. The new ranges are 3,500–3,900 railcars, $410–$460 million of revenue, and $36–$45 million of adjusted EBITDA, well below the previously reaffirmed guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company revised guidance downward to deliveries of 3,500–3,900 railcars, revenue of $410–$460 million, and adjusted EBITDA of $36–$45 million, due to a delayed second-half production ramp shifting some deliveries into early 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Guidance reaffirmed: 4,000–4,500 deliveries, $500–$550M revenue, $41–$50M adjusted EBITDA, back-half weighted.

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin fell to 5.5%, far below the preview’s focus on whether Q1’s 16.8% margin could hold. Lower deliveries, weaker fixed-cost absorption, and the realignment charge contributed to the decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin was 5.5% ($6.2 million), down from 15% ($17.8 million) a year earlier, driven by lower delivery volumes, reduced fixed cost absorption, and the $2.2 million realignment charge.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Gross margin durability after Q1's 16.8%, given mix shift toward higher-volume deliveries; the bear scenario cited margin fading from Q1's 16.8%.

surprises.description: Against the preview’s $0.01 Q2 EPS consensus, FreightCar America reported a $0.94-per-share GAAP loss. A $24.9 million non-cash warrant remeasurement loss drove most of the headline gap; adjusted net loss was $0.02 per share.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company reported a net loss of $30.1 million ($0.94 per diluted share), largely driven by a $24.9 million non-cash warrant remeasurement loss, versus an adjusted net loss of just $0.02 per share.
surprises.expectation_evidence: EPS consensus (Q2 FY2026): $0.01.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue modestly beat the $110.4 million consensus, reaching $113.1 million, although it was still down year over year. This was a small positive relative to the preview’s estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue was $113.1 million, compared with $118.6 million a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus (Q2 FY2026): $110.4M.

surprises.description: Aftermarket revenue grew 13% year over year, a marked slowdown from the 86% growth reported in Q1, despite aftermarket momentum being a key item to watch. Revenue was still growing, but at a much slower rate than the preview’s recent growth reference might suggest.
surprises.fact_evidence: Aftermarket revenue grew 13% year-over-year and now represents roughly 10% of total revenue.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Aftermarket momentum. Q1 growth was 86% YoY, and the company has made two acquisitions in twelve months.

surprises.description: The company disclosed a Castaños structural realignment that cost $2.2 million in Q2 but is expected to deliver about $12 million in annualized savings beginning in Q3. The preview did not flag this action or its near-term cost and prospective savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: A structural realignment of the Castaños operation cost $2.2 million in Q2 but is expected to generate approximately $12 million in annualized cost savings, with benefits beginning in Q3.

surprises.description: A shareholder’s warrant exercise sharply reduced the warrant liability and left the company with positive stockholders’ equity, while management said it should reduce future earnings volatility without incremental EPS dilution. This balance-sheet and earnings-volatility development was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: A shareholder's warrant exercise reduced the warrant liability from $119.4 million to $14 million, turned stockholders' equity positive to $36.2 million, and should reduce future earnings volatility without incremental EPS dilution.

surprises.description: Management disclosed a long-term aftermarket gross-margin target of roughly 32–33% and framed aftermarket as a key growth platform following the July acquisition. The preview noted aftermarket momentum and the acquisition but did not provide this margin target.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is targeting a long-term gross margin around 32–33% for aftermarket and views it as a key growth platform after closing Southern Parts and Equipment in July.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Aftermarket momentum. Q1 growth was 86% YoY, and the company has made two acquisitions in twelve months; watch integration detail on the call.

surprises.description: FreightCar America reported that its roughly 2,600 new-car orders represented about 45% of total industry new-car orders and about 56% of the addressable market excluding tank cars. The preview already disclosed roughly 3,000 Q2 orders, but not this market-share detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company booked approximately 3,000 units in Q2, including about 2,600 new railcars representing roughly 45% of total industry new railcar orders and about 56% of the addressable market excluding tank cars.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 orders totaled about 3,000 railcars, called a “commercial inflection point”; backlog growth is largely known.

in_line: Q2 orders were approximately 3,000 units, consistent with the preview’s already-disclosed order inflection; backlog increased from 2,058 units worth $156 million at Q1-end to 3,972 units worth about $344 million.
Q2 revenue remained lower year over year, as the preview anticipated: $113.1 million versus $118.6 million in Q2 2025.

surprises.description: WLFC reported split-adjusted diluted EPS of $1.31, well above the preview’s $0.90 consensus estimate. The gap is about 46%, despite the preview noting that consensus came from a single analyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS of $1.31.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus EPS (Q2) … $0.90 post-split.”

surprises.description: Utilization slipped to 85% from 85.8% in Q1, rather than recovering toward the preview’s 88% bull-case signal. The preview warned that a further sequential decline would undercut the lease-rent story.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Average fleet utilization declined to 85% from 87.2% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A further sequential slip would undercut the lease-rent story. A recovery toward 88% would be the cleanest bull signal.”

surprises.description: Short-term maintenance reserve revenue fell to $39 million from $50.2 million as customers flew fewer hours on older engines amid elevated fuel prices and the Iran conflict. The preview did not flag this kind of decline in reserve revenue as a Q2 expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Short-term maintenance reserve revenues fell to $39 million from $50.2 million a year earlier as customers flew fewer hours on less fuel-efficient CFM56 and V2500 engines amid elevated fuel prices and the Iran conflict.”

surprises.description: Recent asset sales produced a $32 million gain, above both Q1’s $18.0 million and Q2 2025’s $27.6 million. The preview highlighted gains on sale as a key earnings driver and described its base case as a normal gain on sale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recent asset sales of $224.8 million producing a $32 million gain (14.2% gross margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … Near $175M … normal gain on sale”; the preview also said to compare Q2 gains with “Q1’s $18.0M and the prior year’s $27.6M.”

surprises.description: Willis Aviation Capital AUM grew nearly 80% year over year to $1.4 billion, and management said fund seeding was largely complete, with future growth expected from third-party purchases. The preview did not anticipate this pace or the shift in the source of future growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Willis Aviation Capital AUM grew nearly 80% year-over-year to $1.4 billion, with fund seeding now largely complete and future growth expected to come from third-party purchases.”

surprises.description: Management and advisory fees more than doubled to $5.5 million, with $2.8 million from GP fees on the newly launched Blackstone and Liberty Mutual funds. This fee contribution was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management and advisory fees more than doubled (up 113%) to $5.5 million, driven by $2.8 million in GP fees from the newly launched Blackstone and Liberty Mutual funds.”

surprises.description: Overall AUM increased 21% year over year to about $4.4 billion, with balance-sheet assets making up 67%. The preview did not set an expectation for this portfolio growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Assets under management grew 21% year-over-year, from roughly $3.6 billion in Q2 2025 to about $4.4 billion in Q2 2026, with balance sheet assets making up 67% of AUM.”

surprises.description: Management cited roughly $1.3 billion of deployable capital across discretionary funds, undrawn revolver capacity, and low leverage as resources for its growth pipeline. The preview raised funding and leverage for the WNG acquisition as a key question but did not anticipate this amount of available capital.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company holds roughly $1.3 billion of additional deployable capital in discretionary funds, undrawn revolver capacity, and low leverage of 2.78x to fund its growth pipeline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Funding the $379.3M WNG acquisition” was a ranked issue to watch; the preview said management’s “funding and leverage commentary on the call matters.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed advanced discussions to establish another engine repair center in Asia, an expansion possibility not raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In advanced discussions to establish another engine repair center in Asia.”

surprises.description: The average lease rate rose to 1.03% from 1.0%, even as utilization declined. The preview focused on utilization and lease-rent growth but did not specify an expectation for the average lease rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The average lease rate ticked up from 1.0% to 1.03%.”

in_line: WLFC signed the Pratt & Whitney engine storage and lease-return agreement, which the preview had already identified as a recently announced agreement.
The company completed the 3-for-1 stock split, consistent with the preview’s split alert.
The dividend was adjusted to $0.133 per share after the split, as the preview said the dividend had been maintained at that post-split amount.
The $200 million 2.5% convertible notes due 2031 were consistent with the financing item the preview had flagged; the preview also anticipated incremental interest and potential dilution.

surprises.description: TransDigm raised its FY26 revenue-guidance midpoint by $150 million and its EBITDA-guidance midpoint by $100 million; adjusted EPS guidance increased to $41.04 from the prior range midpoint of $39.52. The preview’s base case was for guidance to be narrowed within the existing range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year fiscal 2026 guidance,” lifting the revenue midpoint “by $150 million to $10.51 billion” and EBITDA as defined “by $100 million to $5.52 billion,” with adjusted EPS “now expected at $41.04.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: ~$2.68B | ~$10.25 | In-line; guide narrowed within range.”

surprises.description: After commercial transport aftermarket revenue grew 18% in Q3, TransDigm lifted its commercial aftermarket growth outlook to the low-double-digit range, above the prior high-single-digit to low-double-digit range. The preview described the prior range as the FY assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commercial transport aftermarket revenue grew 18% versus the prior year, prompting the company to raise commercial aftermarket growth guidance to the low-double-digit range from the prior high-single-digit to low-double-digit range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY guidance assumes high-single to low-double-digit growth.”

surprises.description: TransDigm raised its full-year free-cash-flow outlook by about $100 million, to approximately $2.6 billion. The preview said it had not found a free-cash-flow consensus and did not state an expected change to the company’s prior outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year free cash flow guidance raised to approximately $2.6 billion from $2.5 billion.”

in_line: EBITDA as defined margin was 52.8%, below the 54.4% year-ago margin, consistent with the preview’s expectation that acquisition-heavy revenue mix would dilute margin versus last year.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was about $75 million, well above the preview’s $44.17 million consensus estimate. The preview cautioned that revenue was low-conviction because of deferred-revenue mechanics, but the reported figure still substantially exceeded that estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 net loss widened to $194.3 million ($1.36/share) from $175.2 million ($1.26/share) a year earlier, while total revenue rose to ~$75 million from $28 million driven by collaboration agreements and REDEMPLO sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $44.17M”

surprises.description: Arrowhead said it would spend $215 million on a priority review voucher to cut the sNDA review from 10 months to 6 months, and targeted a potential Q2 2027 launch. The preview expected an sNDA filing before year-end 2026 but did not anticipate the voucher purchase or this accelerated-launch target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Arrowhead acquired an FDA priority review voucher for $215 million … to shorten the sNDA review from 10 months to 6 months”; management “targets a potential accelerated launch in the second quarter of 2027” and projects “a greater than 3x return on the investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “sNDA filing timing, reaffirmed for ‘before end of 2026.’ A slip would weaken the 2027–28 ramp.”

surprises.description: Management put peak annual sales for the sHTG indication at $3 billion to $4 billion, describing it as substantially larger than FCS. The preview did not give an sHTG sales estimate or flag this market-size claim.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management estimates the sHTG indication could drive peak sales of $3 billion to $4 billion per year, with the overwhelming majority in the United States, representing a substantially larger opportunity than FCS.”

surprises.description: The reported loss per share was $1.36, worse than the preview’s expected loss of about $1.28 per share. The miss was modest relative to the expected loss, despite the large revenue beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 net loss widened to $194.3 million ($1.36/share).”

surprises.description: REDEMPLO revenue was approximately $2.4 million, just below the preview’s $2.5–3.5 million model range. Prescriptions more than doubled quarter-on-quarter, but the reported new-prescription pace of 20–30 per week was around or below the preview’s roughly 30-per-week base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “REDEMPLO commercial revenue reached approximately $2.4 million for the quarter (more than double the ~$1 million in fiscal Q2), with prescriptions more than doubling quarter-on-quarter at a run rate of 20-30 new prescriptions per week.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net product revenue. Model is ~$2.5–3.5M”; “~30 new Rx/week.”

surprises.description: The company outlined a broader upcoming readout slate than the preview identified: ARO-DIMER-PA data in September and ARO-INHBE and ARO-ALK7 obesity data in Q4. The preview highlighted ARO-MAPT as the main remaining 2H26 pipeline catalyst but did not mention these additional readouts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Multiple near-term catalysts are expected in September, including first clinical readouts for ARO-DIMER-PA … with additional ARO-INHBE and ARO-ALK7 obesity data in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ARO-MAPT Phase 1 data guided to 2H26”; “ARO-MAPT 2H26 data reaffirmation, the main pipeline catalyst left in 2H26.”

surprises.description: Arrowhead said its commercial field force would expand from addressing over 5,000 HCP targets for FCS to over 20,000 targets for sHTG. The preview discussed launch trajectory and patient metrics but did not anticipate this scale of target-market expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The commercial field force is scaling from addressing over 5,000 HCP targets in FCS to over 20,000 targets for the broader sHTG opportunity.”

in_line: Management said the sHTG sNDA is expected before the end of 2026, consistent with the preview’s stated filing timeline.
ARO-MAPT remained a 2H26 catalyst; the preview had flagged Phase 1 data in that period.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $1.83 versus the preview’s $1.63 consensus, a substantial beat. The $0.08 tariff-refund benefit explains part, but not all, of the gap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased nearly 30% year-over-year to $1.83,” including “an $0.08 net benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $1.63” consensus; the preview also cited a buy-side whisper of “about $1.68–1.72.”

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted EPS midpoint rose to $6.20, above the preview’s roughly $6.00 reference point, rather than merely reaffirming the prior outlook. The midpoint increase also lifts implied growth to 16% from 13%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $6.05-$6.35 (up $0.20 at midpoint), now implying 16% growth versus the prior 13%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY26 adjusted EPS guidance midpoint was “about $6.00” and that “a simple reaffirm after a Q2 beat would read as soft.”

surprises.description: Q2 sales exceeded the $1.233 billion consensus by about $27 million, with reported growth also above the preview’s expected year-over-year growth rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total sales rose 7.5% year-over-year to $1.26 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $1,233M” consensus, implying “+5.2%” year-over-year growth.

surprises.description: The company reported strong companywide operating leverage: adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 190 basis points year over year, and organic incremental margins exceeded 40% even excluding the refund benefit. The preview highlighted tariff and price-cost pressure, but gave no companywide EBITDA-margin estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 19.6% from 17.7% a year ago, with organic incremental margins exceeding 40% even excluding the tariff refund benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that Q1 Engineered Bearings margin was “down 120 bps YoY, as about $20M of tariff cost offset pricing” and said a margin below about 19.5% would suggest the price/tariff spread remained negative.

surprises.description: Industrial Motion sales growth came in above the preview’s expectation that the segment would grow faster than Q1’s 12%, while the segment also posted a markedly higher margin than its Q1 level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Industrial Motion posted record quarterly sales of $454 million (up 14.6%) with EBITDA margins of 23.3%, up 500 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a full quarter of Bijur Delimon “should lift IM revenue growth above Q1’s +12%”; Q1 Industrial Motion margin was reported as 21.5%.

surprises.description: The belts divestiture was expected to close in Q3, but the call added a quantified benefit: it is expected to raise Industrial Motion’s pro forma EBITDA margin by more than 200 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pending belts divestiture, expected to close in Q3, is projected to structurally improve Industrial Motion EBITDA margins by more than 200 basis points on a pro forma basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Belts divestiture timing and proceeds” and said H2 would be softer “as the belts divestiture closes in Q3,” but did not specify a margin benefit.

surprises.description: Second-half guidance includes a $0.10 EPS headwind for strategic aerospace and defense staffing investments, a cost not identified in the preview’s explanation of the expected softer H2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management embedded a $0.10 EPS headwind in second-half guidance, mostly tied to strategic investments in aerospace and defense operations to add operative headcount amid a growing backlog with book-to-bill well above 1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said H2 would be softer as the belts divestiture closed in Q3 and listed the Q1 pull-forward and backlog direction as issues to watch; it did not mention an EPS headwind from staffing investments.

surprises.description: The call pointed to a growing aerospace and defense backlog with book-to-bill well above 1, providing a positive demand signal on the backlog question the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company cited “a growing backlog with book-to-bill well above 1” in connection with aerospace and defense operations.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Backlog and the ~1% pull-forward” and said to watch whether backlog grew sequentially and year over year.

surprises.description: An $8 million IEEPA tariff refund provided a discrete $0.08 net EPS benefit that the preview did not identify as part of the quarter’s expected earnings.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 adjusted EPS “includ[ed] an $0.08 net benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds ($8 million).”

in_line: The expected Q3 timing of the belts divestiture was reiterated.

The preview anticipated a softer second half as the belts divestiture closed; management likewise described a roughly 2.5-point step-down in H2 organic growth, citing seasonality, tougher pricing comparisons, and ramping-down belt sales.

surprises.description: SMP’s sales growth was stronger than the preview’s consensus implied: Q2 sales grew 6.7% on the stated tariff-refund-adjusted basis, versus consensus revenue growth of about 3.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated net sales grew 6.7% in Q2 2026 (adjusted for tariff refund accounting).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $511.7M” versus Q2 FY2025 actual of “$493.9M,” implying “+3.6%.”

surprises.description: Temperature Control substantially exceeded the preview’s approximate $132 million downside threshold, reaching $152 million with margin improvement. However, management said the increase was aided by preseason orders shifting into Q2 rather than stronger end-demand, tempering the quality of the beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Temperature Control sales surged 15.7% to $152 million with adjusted EBITDA margin improving to 18.2%, though the gain was aided by preseason order timing shifting into Q2 rather than end-demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything below about $132M suggests the shift did not materialize or summer sell-through disappointed.”

surprises.description: Deleveraging progressed faster than the preview’s concern that a sharp cash-flow swing was needed to keep the year-end target alive: net debt fell by about $89 million from the Q1 level and leverage declined from 3.0x to 2.5x. The cash-flow improvement was partly driven by inventory reduction and tariff-refund timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt fell to $510.2 million with a leverage ratio of 2.5x EBITDA”; first-half operating cash flow was “$58.3 million,” “$64.2 million better than last year,” driven by “significant inventory reduction and tariff refund timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 operating cash flow must swing sharply positive” and “Getting from 3.0x to 2.0x in three quarters is aggressive.”

surprises.description: Vehicle Control sales declined rather than merely decelerating from Q1, landing below the preview’s level that would suggest Q1 had borrowed from Q2. Customer point-of-sale growth remained in the low single digits and was weighted toward pricing, which points to limited underlying volume strength.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Vehicle Control sales fell 1.6% to $198.6 million,” while “customer POS remained up in low single digits with strength weighted toward pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “below +2% suggests Q1 borrowed from Q2.”

surprises.description: SMP reported record adjusted EBITDA dollars, but its 12.1% margin came in slightly below the preview’s roughly 12.3% implied consensus margin. The dollar result itself was close to the preview’s estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A record $63.5 million in adjusted EBITDA in Q2, representing 12.1% of net sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (implied) ~$63M / ~12.3% margin.”

surprises.description: Management warned that Engineered Solutions’ growth would slow through the rest of the year because Q2 was the segment’s last quarter of easy comparisons. The preview focused on a recovery in the segment’s margins, while this call added a caution about the growth outlook; the reported facts do not state whether margins recovered.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Engineered Solutions sales rose 16.8% but this marked the last quarter of easy comparisons, and management expects the segment's growth rate to slow through the remainder of the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Engineered Solutions margin recovery” as a key metric and described the prior decline as “temporary.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that Q2 IEEPA tariff refunds will be partly shared with customers and that replacement Section 301 tariffs leave total tariff exposure only nominally lower. This limits the prospect of the refunds translating into lasting, retained tariff relief.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received IEEPA tariff refunds in Q2 that it expects to partly share with customers, while replacement Section 301 tariffs net to only a nominal reduction in total tariff exposure.”

in_line: Adjusted diluted EPS of $1.40 was within the preview’s $1.39–$1.42 consensus range.
Full-year guidance was maintained at low-to-mid single-digit sales growth and an 11%–12% adjusted EBITDA margin, as the preview’s base case expected guidance to be reaffirmed.
Nissens’ 2.3% local-currency growth was broadly consistent with the preview’s report of 2.7% local-currency growth in Q1; the Q2 reported increase also included favorable currency conversion.

surprises.description: ATEC reported Q2 revenue of $214 million, above the preview’s $211.24 million consensus and roughly $212 million implied by guidance. Growth was 15% rather than the expected roughly 14%, a modest beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached $214 million, up 15% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue” consensus: “$211.24M (+13.9% YoY)”; the preview also cited “~$212M implied” and roughly “14%” growth.

surprises.description: ATEC raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook to about $140 million and a 16% margin, rather than simply reaffirming the prior $134 million, 15% margin outlook. Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $36 million, with margin expanding 420 basis points to 17%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to approximately $140 million (16% margin) from $134 million”; Q2 adjusted EBITDA was “$36 million” and margin expanded “420 basis points to 17%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY26 adjusted EBITDA: “~$134M / 15% margin (reaffirmed).”

surprises.description: Revenue per case weakened more than the preview anticipated: Q2 was down 2.7% year over year, and management moved full-year guidance from flattish to a low-single-digit decline. Management attributed about three-quarters of the Q2 shortfall to biologics, whose attachment remained below prior-year levels.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue per case declined approximately 2.7% year-over-year”; “Full-year revenue-per-case guidance was cut from flattish to a low-single-digit decline, with about three-quarters of the Q2 shortfall attributed to biologics.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year revenue-per-case guidance was cut from flattish” (the prior flattish outlook is stated in the call facts; the preview did not flag revenue per case).

surprises.description: Although total EOS revenue was at the preview’s roughly $17 million threshold, established EOS Insight accounts showed a strong early implant-revenue ramp: approximately 32% growth within six months of going live. That cohort performance was not anticipated in the preview’s focus on EOS installation timing and the risk of a difficult second-half ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Established EOS Insight accounts showed implant revenue rising approximately 32% within six months of going live.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “To hit the $77M FY guide, Q2–Q4 EOS must total ~$63M”; “Any Q2 EOS number below ~$17M puts an implausible H2 ramp on the table.”

in_line: Surgical revenue grew 17%, matching the preview’s expectation of a Q2 print near +17%.
EOS revenue was $17 million, matching the preview’s approximate $17 million prior-year comparison point and its threshold for avoiding a more difficult H2 ramp.
Full-year revenue guidance remained approximately $882 million, as the preview expected it could be reaffirmed.
Q2 free cash flow was about $1 million, close to the preview’s expectation of approximately zero; full-year free cash flow guidance of at least $20 million was also maintained.
The expected annual interest-expense reduction of more than $6 million from the refinancing was reiterated.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was above $10 billion, versus preview consensus of $9.43–$9.45 billion. That is a substantial beat against the expected roughly 3% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenues exceeded $10 billion in Q2 2026, a 10% year-over-year increase.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q2'26 consensus | $9.43–9.45B” and “YoY | +2.9%.”

surprises.description: Amgen raised its full-year guidance, lifting the revenue range and raising the EPS floor and ceiling. The new EPS midpoint is about the preview’s $22.90 consensus, but the higher floor is more favorable than the preview’s concern that anything short of a floor raise would disappoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Amgen raised full-year 2026 guidance to total revenues of $38.2 billion to $39.4 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $22.30 to $23.50.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior guide was “Revenue | $37.1B – $38.5B” and “Non-GAAP EPS | $21.70 – $23.10”; the preview noted “a raise to the floor” was the clearest bar and said “Anything short of raising the floor is a negative surprise.”

surprises.description: Repatha sales exceeded the preview’s estimate, with both dollars and growth ahead of the modeled result. Sales of $953 million were about $49 million above the $904.4 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repatha delivered $953 million in sales growing 37% year-over-year, with new-to-brand prescriptions growing more than 50% in the U.S.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Zacks models Repatha at $904.4M (+29.9%).”

surprises.description: Amgen disclosed that a Q3 business-development deal will bring a $100 million upfront R&D payment and a meaningful sequential increase in operating expenses, a near-term expense headwind not identified in the preview. The preview’s cost concern was cybersecurity remediation, not this transaction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A Q3 business development transaction will trigger a $100 million upfront R&D payment, contributing to an expected meaningful sequential increase in Q3 operating expenses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called cybersecurity costs “the highest-variance unknown on the call” but did not mention a business-development payment or expected Q3 expense increase.

surprises.description: Amgen stopped development of AMG 513, a Phase I obesity asset, which the preview had not anticipated. The early stage limits the apparent scale of the setback, particularly alongside the ongoing MariTide program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Amgen discontinued development of AMG 513, a Phase I obesity asset.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that CFO Peter Griffith is departing and Thomas Dittrich is taking over; the preview did not flag an impending finance-leadership change. The facts provided do not state a reason or operational impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Peter Griffith departs as Thomas Dittrich takes over.”

in_line: Prolia and XGEVA combined sales declined 33% year over year to $1.1 billion, in line with company expectations and the preview’s focus on expected biosimilar erosion.
The full-year operating-margin outlook remained roughly 45%–46%, matching the preview’s cited 45%–46% FY26 guide.

surprises.description: Q1 revenue was $166 million, about 10.8% above the preview’s $149.8 million consensus estimate. The reported 27% year-over-year growth therefore materially exceeded the expected 14.4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 revenue reached $166 million, up 27% year-over-year, exceeding company expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue ... Consensus $149.8M” and “+14.4% YoY.”

surprises.description: Management raised FY2027 revenue guidance to $650–670 million from $630–650 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $145–155 million from $135–145 million, rather than merely reiterating the existing outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised FY2027 guidance to revenue of $650-670 million (from $630-650 million) and adjusted EBITDA of $145-155 million (from $135-145 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY27 guidance of “$630–650M” revenue and “$135–145M” adjusted EBITDA, and said “Reiteration versus a raise is the likely swing factor.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $0.19, about 36% above the preview’s $0.14 consensus. The call also reported that GAAP net loss narrowed to $3.2 million from $14.1 million a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income more than tripled to $24.1 million ($0.19 per share) from $7 million ($0.06) a year ago, while GAAP net loss narrowed to $3.2 million ($0.03) from $14.1 million ($0.13).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS ... Consensus $0.14 (Zacks); Craig Hallum at $0.10.”

surprises.description: On-device solutions accelerated to 15% year-over-year growth from 5% in Q4, despite the preview flagging soft device volumes. International ODS was especially strong, with nearly 80% growth and 40%+ RPD expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “On-device solutions revenue rose 15% year-over-year to $110 million, with international ODS growing nearly 80% driven by both higher device volumes and 40%+ RPD expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q4 On-Device Solutions grew “+5%” and described “soft U.S. device volumes.”

surprises.description: Profitability improved sharply: adjusted EBITDA grew 69% and its margin expanded about 640 basis points, while non-GAAP gross margin rose to 49.4% and cash operating expenses increased only 7%. The preview flagged margins as an issue to watch but did not specify an expected improvement of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 69% year-over-year to $42.5 million, with margin expanding roughly 640 basis points to 25.6%”; “Non-GAAP gross margin improved to 49.4% from 47.3% a year earlier ... while cash operating expenses rose only 7%.”

surprises.description: The company reported significant deleveraging and a concrete borrowing-cost benefit: net leverage was down to 2.5 turns from over five turns a year earlier, and crossing a post-quarter threshold reduced the rate on its largest loan tranche by 50 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage improved dramatically from over five turns a year ago to 2.5 turns, and a post-quarter leverage threshold triggered a 50 basis point reduction on the largest loan tranche.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “any comment on the ~$354M debt load” and “Progress ... on ... deleveraging plans.”

surprises.description: Cash generation was substantially stronger than the preview discussed: cash from operations more than doubled and non-GAAP free cash flow improved by roughly $10 million to $11.3 million. The company also ended with $43.2 million of cash while reducing total debt by more than $8 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash from operations more than doubled to $17.9 million and non-GAAP free cash flow improved roughly $10 million to $11.3 million, while cash ended at $43.2 million and total debt declined over $8 million to $352.9 million.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a notable improvement in workforce productivity, with revenue per employee rising from about $800,000 to over $1 million, attributed to AI-driven automation and operating leverage. The preview discussed AI monetization but did not anticipate this specific productivity result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue per employee rose from about $800,000 a year ago to over $1 million, reflecting AI-driven automation and operating leverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “AI monetization and gross margin” and mentioned DTiQ and Ignite Graph, but did not set an expectation for employee productivity.

in_line: AGP growth remained very strong but was essentially in line with the preview’s expectation that the pace be sustained: growth was 56%, compared with 57% in Q4. The company reported a second consecutive quarter above 50% growth.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was a $0.53 loss, versus the preview’s $0.33-loss consensus, a materially larger loss than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS was a loss of $0.53.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | –$0.33 (range –$0.33 to –$0.34)”

surprises.description: Instead of the expected seventh consecutive year-over-year improvement in adjusted EBITDA, the company reported a $12 million loss, down $4 million from Q2 2025. The loss was within the preview’s base-case range, but the year-over-year deterioration contradicted the improvement thesis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $12 million (a $4 million decline versus Q2 2025).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A seventh straight Y/Y improvement, with TBHC consolidated, is the most bullish outcome.”

surprises.description: Revenue grew 28% year over year, below the preview’s 31.5% consensus growth estimate. The reported facts do not give a revenue dollar figure, so the gap versus the $371.1 million estimate cannot be quantified directly.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total omnichannel revenue increased 28% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 26.8%, above the preview’s cited 24–26% company-guidance band, including its 26% upper end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 310 basis points to 26.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | Company guides 24–26%”; the preview also flagged “Gross margin vs. the 24–26% band.”

surprises.description: Management guided Q3 gross margin to close to or potentially touching 30%, a materially higher near-term level than the preview’s cited 24–26% margin outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 2026 revenue to $505–$525 million with gross margins improving materially to close to or potentially touching 30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 outlook (Feb 2026) calls for ... 24–26% gross margin.”

surprises.description: The base e-commerce business grew for a second consecutive quarter after 19 straight quarters of revenue declines. That improvement in the underlying business was not reflected in the preview’s concerns about customer declines and its cautious organic-growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The base e-commerce business grew year-over-year for a second consecutive quarter, reversing 19 straight quarters of revenue decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 outlook ... calls for low-to-mid-single-digit organic growth”; the preview also said another double-digit active-customer decline “would undercut the brand-recovery thesis.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a sizable integration and restructuring cash program: $30–$40 million through year-end, including about $20 million for warehouse consolidation, alongside a target of more than $50 million in annualized savings and a return exceeding 100%. The preview anticipated integration costs and funding needs but did not specify this cash commitment or savings target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company targets more than $50 million in additional annualized cost savings over the next 12 months, expecting a cash-on-cash return exceeding 100% on integration spending”; it expects to “deploy $30–$40 million in cash through year-end,” with “about $20 million earmarked for supply chain consolidation to as few as 2–3 warehouses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guides $13–14M per quarter of integration and restructuring charges for Q2 and Q3”; the preview also flagged “Cash and liquidity” and the Q3 funding plan.

surprises.description: Management outlined a path to mid- to high-single-digit EBITDA margins in a mid-cycle housing market, contingent on home sales recovering to 5–5.3 million, gross margin reaching about 35%, and $50 million of SG&A reduction. This is a more specific and higher-margin ambition than the preview’s cited expectation of becoming EBITDA-positive by 2028, though it is conditional rather than a near-term forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management projects a path to mid- to high single-digit EBITDA margins in a mid-cycle housing market of 5–5.3 million home sales ... requiring ~35% gross margins and $50 million of SG&A reduction.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 outlook ... and EBITDA-positive by 2028.”

surprises.description: Management said pending acquisitions are valued at more than $2.5 billion, a scale not quantified in the preview, which identified F9 and Fathom as pending but gave no total value.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total pending acquisitions valued at over $2.5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “F9 Brands and Fathom are pending.”

surprises.description: The parent company announced it will rebrand as Neighborhood Intelligence and move from the NYSE to Nasdaq under ticker NXH effective August 17, a corporate and listing change not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The parent company will rebrand as Neighborhood Intelligence and begin trading on NASDAQ under ticker NXH effective August 17, transitioning from the NYSE.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identifies the company as “Bed Bath & Beyond, Inc. (NYSE: BBBY)” and says it “re-took the name and ticker on Aug 29, 2025.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA of a $12 million loss was within the preview’s base-case range of a $10–$14 million loss, although it was worse year over year.
Cash and restricted cash totaled $126 million, above the preview’s roughly $110 million level to watch for; the preview’s $110 million reference was a threshold, not a precise expected balance.

surprises.description: Alight reported Q2 revenue of $511 million, above the preview’s $490–505 million company-guidance range and roughly $14–16 million above the cited $494.9–497.1 million consensus estimates. This was a moderate upside gap despite revenue declining year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue of $511 million exceeded market expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance (Q2): $490M – $505M”; consensus was “$494.9M” and “$497.1M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $92 million, above the preview’s $80–90 million guidance range and its $85 million midpoint. The 18% margin also represented a smaller year-over-year contraction than the roughly 700 basis points implied by the preview’s discussion of Q2 guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $92 million at an 18% margin,” compared with $127 million and a 24% margin a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA $80M – $90M (midpoint $85M)”; the preview said guidance “implies about a 700 bp YoY margin contraction.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.91 exceeded both preview consensus figures of $0.69 and $0.75 by a substantial amount, even though EPS fell sharply year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS dropped to $0.91 from $2.09 a year earlier.”

surprises.description: Alight restored full-year 2026 guidance, whereas the preview identified reinstating a framework as an open question. Its $400–415 million adjusted EBITDA outlook is also slightly above the preview’s assumed $380–400 million range, though the ranges overlap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $2.078-2.098 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $400-415 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “withheld full-year 2026 guidance” and that “reinstating a credible FY26 framework would be a bull catalyst”; its estimated FY26 adjusted EBITDA was “$380–400M.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was above the preview’s $35–45 million guidance range, with $48 million generated in the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$101 million generated year-to-date including $48 million in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 guidance is $35–45M.”

surprises.description: The call introduced a weak Q3 outlook of $55–61 million in adjusted EBITDA, with annual enrollment expenses weighing on the quarter and a significant Q4 rebound implied. The preview gave no Q3 estimate or specific expectation for this quarterly pattern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects revenue of $469-479 million and adjusted EBITDA of just $55-61 million due to annual enrollment expenses, implying a significant Q4 rebound.”

surprises.description: Expected full-year free-cash-flow conversion is only 40–43% of EBITDA, below the preview’s stated long-run conversion range of 44–50%. The preview did not provide a full-year FCF estimate, so the comparison is to that longer-term benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year free cash flow conversion is expected to be roughly 40-43% of EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management frames long-run conversion at 44–50% of adj. EBITDA.”

surprises.description: The call provided a longer-term turnaround timeline not laid out in the preview: management expects momentum in 2027 and quarter-over-quarter growth plus AI-driven margin expansion beginning in 2028. It also reported expanding account-executive coverage from 100 to 500 clients.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management framed a multi-year turnaround, expecting momentum in 2027 and quarter-over-quarter growth plus AI-driven margin expansion beginning in 2028, while account executive coverage was expanded from 100 to 500 clients.”

surprises.description: The call facts do not provide a quantified renewal or retention rate, despite the preview identifying that metric as an important unresolved issue and warning that silence could be read negatively.
surprises.fact_evidence: The reported call facts cite recurring revenue down 4.3% and attribute the decline to weak prior commercial execution, but give no quantified renewal or retention rate.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The absence of a quantified renewal rate was a key factor in the February disappointment, so a specific number matters”; “Silence here may be read negatively.”

in_line: Recurring revenue declined 4.3% year over year, broadly consistent with the preview’s concern about the trend after it had been down 4% in Q1.

surprises.description: Emerson delivered 6% underlying sales growth, above the roughly 5% growth in the preview’s company guidance. Underlying orders grew 7%, also exceeding the preview’s 6% confirmation threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Underlying sales grew 6% and underlying orders grew 7% in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company Guidance” was “~+5% underlying”; the preview said to watch for “orders at or above 6%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $1.71 beat the $1.68 consensus and topped the upper end of the $1.65–$1.70 company guidance range. The gap was small, but the result exceeded both reference points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew 13% year-over-year to $1.71, exceeding the top of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS” consensus was “$1.68”; company guidance was “$1.65–$1.70.”

surprises.description: Adjusted segment EBITDA margin reached 28.5%, 50 basis points above the approximately 28% level the preview said Q3 needed to achieve.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted segment EBITDA margin expanded 140 basis points to 28.5%, driven by better-than-expected volume, favorable segment mix, and price cost exceeding inflation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 needs ~28% segment margin”; the consensus table also listed approximately 28%.

surprises.description: The expected Q3 trough in Middle East disruption did not clearly arrive: Emerson reported an approximately $25 million Q3 revenue headwind and expected a similar impact in Q4, rather than describing Q3 as the trough.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Middle East conflict and effectively closed Strait of Hormuz created an approximately $25 million Q3 revenue headwind, with a similar impact expected in Q4 and a roughly $100 million full-year impact.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 should be the trough”; the preview also identified “first rebuild orders” as a clear positive.

surprises.description: Growth in semiconductor and power markets was exceptionally strong, with semiconductor sales up 53% and power sales up 37%. The preview did not flag these vertical results as an expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Growth verticals were up 27% overall, with semiconductor sales up 53% (orders up 70%) and power sales up 37% (Ovation orders up 31%).”

surprises.description: Emerson’s project funnel expanded by $1.2 billion to $12.4 billion, with sizable power and LNG funnels and Ovation lead times extending into late 2027 and 2028. The preview did not set an expectation for these project indicators.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The project funnel grew $1.2 billion to $12.4 billion (up 8% year-over-year), with power now at $3 billion and LNG at $2.2 billion, and Ovation lead times now extend into Q4 2027 and 2028.”

surprises.description: Software annual contract value grew 9%, and management expressed confidence it would exit the year above 10% growth. The preview did not identify ACV as a key expectation or provide a comparison point.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Annual contract value (ACV) of software grew 9% year-over-year to $1.68 billion, with management confident of exiting the year at 10%-plus growth.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow was strong at $1.3 billion, but the reported increase was helped by $82 million of tariff refunds and tax timing shifts into Q4. The preview expected a material second-half cash-flow build, but did not anticipate these contributors to the quarter’s result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 free cash flow rose 36% to $1.3 billion at a 27.1% margin, boosted by $82 million in tariff refunds (accounted for on a cash basis and excluded from adjusted results) and tax timing shifts into Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FCF must build materially in 2H to hold the $3.5–$3.6B guide.”

surprises.description: Emerson raised its full-year underlying sales growth outlook to 3.5%, above the roughly 3% outlook described after Q2 in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year guidance was raised to 5% GAAP sales growth, 3.5% underlying growth, and approximately $3.6 billion free cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 had “Cut FY26 underlying sales growth to ~3% from ~4% on Middle East disruption.”

in_line: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to approximately $6.55, in line with the preview’s base-case ask for a raise to at least $6.55 and within its cited $6.45–$6.55 range.
Full-year free cash flow guidance of approximately $3.6 billion was at the top of the preview’s $3.5–$3.6 billion range.
The commitment to return approximately $2.2 billion to shareholders was consistent with the preview’s FY26 capital-returns figure.

surprises.description: The preview said Q2 adjusted EPS guidance was at least $1.25; the call reported consolidated EPS of $2.19. The comparison is not perfectly like-for-like because the preview cited adjusted EPS and the result is consolidated, but the reported figure was substantially higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The combined entity produced Q2 pretax income of $64.5 million with Sun Country contributing $13.4 million during its stub period, yielding consolidated EPS of $2.19.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS (Q2) | At least $1.25”; the preview also says “The EPS result is largely pre-announced.”

surprises.description: The preview identified Q3 fuel near or above $4.20 per gallon as the central risk; management instead assumed $3.80 in Q3 and $3.70 in Q4. That is a notably more favorable fuel outlook than the preview’s key-risk scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided full-year 2026 consolidated EPS of greater than $6 … assuming fuel of $3.80/gallon in Q3 and $3.70/gallon in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If management guides Q3 fuel materially above $4.20 without an offsetting revenue story, the raised-guidance narrative weakens”; the base scenario expected Q3 to be “framed cautiously on fuel.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s expectation that capacity might normalize in H2, scheduled-service capacity is guided down about 5.5% year over year in Q3. The company also tied a temporary back-half reduction in off-peak MSP capacity to Sun Country pilot attrition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for … scheduled service capacity down about 5.5% year-over-year”; “Sun Country experienced elevated junior pilot attrition in Minneapolis-St. Paul … prompting a temporary reduction of off-peak MSP capacity in the back half of the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether strong TRASM “reflects pricing or capacity discipline matters for the H2 outlook as capacity normalizes”; its bull case expected “H2 demand supports capacity growth rather than further cuts.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged CASM ex-fuel as an issue to watch but did not anticipate cost increases of this scale: management expects legacy Allegiant nonfuel unit costs up 9–10% and consolidated nonfuel CASM ex-cargo up 10–12% in Q3, the peak year-over-year increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Legacy Allegiant nonfuel unit costs expected up 9-10% and consolidated nonfuel CASM ex-cargo up 10-12% in Q3, marking the peak year-over-year CASM ex increase.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “CASM ex-fuel and the premium pivot” as a key issue and cited Q1 CASM ex-fuel “up 7.1% YoY,” but gave no expectation of a 9–12% Q3 increase.

surprises.description: The newly agreed pilot contract carries a large near-term cash cost that the preview did not flag: a roughly $275 million retention bonus will be paid from cash, pushing net leverage to its peak. This adds a substantial capital and leverage burden despite the preview’s expectation that leverage would remain below 3.0x at close.
