surprises.fact_evidence: “The company will pay a pilot retention bonus of approximately $275 million (including payroll taxes) from cash on hand in the coming weeks, expected to push net leverage to its peak from the current 2.6x pro forma level.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said net adjusted debt/EBITDAR was “targeted below 3.0x at close” and its bear scenario cited “leverage above 3.0x”; it did not mention a retention bonus.

surprises.description: Full-year aircraft CapEx rose to about $850 million, well above the preview’s prior $570–590 million guide. The call also described a faster-growing MAX fleet, adding to the scale of the capital-spending outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “737 MAX aircraft represented 21% of scheduled service ASMs in Q2 … with the MAX fleet expected to grow by ~20 aircraft in 2027 to 45-47 in-service planes and full-year 2026 CapEx raised to approximately $850 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FY aircraft capex guide $570–590M” from Q1.

surprises.description: The combined company reported a 9.2% operating margin and said it led U.S. carriers for the third consecutive quarter, a notably strong operating outcome not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of demand, capacity cuts, and cost pressures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The combined entity … [had] a 9.2% operating margin, the best of any U.S. carrier this quarter”; it was “leading the industry in operating margin for the third consecutive quarter.”

surprises.description: The Expedia partnership gained meaningful early traction shortly after launch, with 3% of bookings already coming through the channel and more than half from net-new customers. The preview did not anticipate this channel or report an expected adoption level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The newly launched Expedia partnership went 100% live on July 10 and already accounts for approximately 3% of bookings, with more than half coming from net-new customers.”

surprises.description: Cobrand card remuneration was up 24% year over year, and management described a goal of doubling its share of revenue from 5% to 10%. The preview did not identify this as a watch item or set an expectation for card growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cobrand card remuneration rose 24% year-over-year toward a goal of doubling from 5% to 10% of revenue.”

in_line: Management reiterated the preview’s stated target of at least $140 million in annual Sun Country synergies by 2029 and supplied a single operating certificate target of the first half of 2028, addressing the preview’s request for a timeline.

surprises.description: Arista raised FY2026 revenue guidance to approximately $12.6 billion, well above the preview’s expected raise to roughly $11.9–12.0 billion and published consensus of $11.6–11.7 billion. It was the third guidance increase this year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance for the third time this year to approximately $12.6 billion (40% growth), an incremental $1.1 billion above the prior $11.5 billion projection”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “room for a raise to roughly $11.9–12.0B”; consensus “~$11.6–11.7B”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was just over $3.0 billion, exceeding the $2.83 billion consensus and even the preview’s roughly $2.90–2.95 billion whisper range. The preview’s bull case topped out at $3.02 billion, so the result was near its upper bound.
surprises.fact_evidence: “total revenue of just over $3 billion, up 37.7% year-over-year and above guidance of $2.8 billion”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was “$2.83B”; the “Whisper bar” was “roughly $2.90–2.95B,” and the bull scenario was “$2.96–3.02B.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin was 63.4%, above the preview’s roughly 62–62.5% expectation and the key threshold it identified. The reported figure was helped by tariff refunds and customer mix, though management also cited end-customer mix as a year-over-year headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin was 63.4%”; it was “aided by tariff refunds (20-30 bps benefit) and customer mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin” consensus was “~62–62.5%”; the preview called “~62%” its “pass/fail line.”

surprises.description: The AI revenue outlook was only modestly above the preview’s published $3.5 billion expectation, rather than reaching the preview’s $3.7–3.8 billion base-case range or $4.0 billion bull/whisper level. The call facts cite both an AI fabrics goal of at least $3.5 billion and a broader AI target of at least $3.6 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “full-year 2026 AI fabrics goal set at least $3.5 billion”; elsewhere, “at least $3.6 billion AI target in 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 AI revenue at “$3.5B,” while its base scenario expected “AI ~$3.7–3.8B” and its catalyst checklist cited an “AI target vs. $4.0B.”

surprises.description: International revenue reached $697.8 million, or 23% of total revenue, versus 15.5% of revenue in the prior quarter. The preview did not flag this sharp change in geographic mix or provide an expectation for it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International revenue jumped to $697.8 million (23% of total) from 15.5% last quarter, driven by organic growth and geographic mix shifts among large global customers.”

surprises.description: Arista reported that AI Etherlink switch adoption had passed 100 cumulative customers. The preview did not set an adoption expectation or identify this customer milestone as a debate to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI Etherlink switch adoption surpassed 100 cumulative customers, up from just 4-5 in 2024.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that Scale-Across is expected to contribute about $1.2 billion, or roughly 30%, of the 2026 AI target. The preview discussed overall AI revenue expectations but did not anticipate this breakdown or Scale-Across contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Scale-Across is expected to represent about 30% (~$1.2 billion) of Arista's at least $3.6 billion AI target in 2026.”

in_line: Multiyear purchase commitments increased from $8.9 billion in Q1 to approximately $9.7 billion in Q2, consistent with the preview’s expectation that commitments could keep rising and its focus on persistent supply constraints. The call described industry-wide tightness as expected to persist through 2028.

surprises.description: The preview asked whether EXPAREL could sustain roughly 7% volume growth, but Q2 volume growth slowed to about 4%, and net sales grew only 3%. Management attributed the pressure to slower elective soft-tissue procedures, especially inpatient cases, as well as vial mix and discounting.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EXPAREL net sales grew only 3% to $109.5 million as volume growth of ~4% (a step down from prior quarters) was partially offset by vial mix shift and discounting from a third GPO”; “Elective soft tissue procedures slowed, particularly in the hospital inpatient setting, weighing on EXPAREL volumes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Can the ~7% Q1 pace hold?” and consensus revenue of “~$191M implies roughly 5.5% y/y growth.”

surprises.description: Management cut full-year total revenue guidance by $10 million at both ends of the range, rather than reaffirming or raising it. The accompanying $10 million reduction in SG&A guidance partly offsets the concern, and management said the changes reflect the Zimmer transaction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered full-year 2026 total revenue guidance to $735-$760 million (from $745-$770 million) and SG&A guidance to $310-$330 million (from $320-$340 million) to reflect the Zimmer transaction.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance action. Does management reaffirm or raise the $745–770M revenue range?”

surprises.description: Pacira completed a sale of iovera to Zimmer Biomet, a transaction not discussed in the preview. It brings $70 million upfront and as much as another $70 million in revenue-based milestones, while Pacira retains participation in the spasticity program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pacira completed the divestiture of iovera to Zimmer Biomet on July 31, 2025, for up to $140 million ($70 million upfront plus $70 million in revenue-based milestones), while retaining participation in the spasticity program.”

surprises.description: UnitedHealthcare added separate reimbursement for EXPAREL outside the surgical bundle and put ZILRETTA on its preferred drug list without prior authorization. The preview did not flag these coverage changes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “UnitedHealthcare added separate reimbursement outside the surgical bundle for EXPAREL, bringing total covered lives to well over 150 million (roughly 50% of the market), and placed ZILRETTA on its preferred drug list without prior authorization.”

surprises.description: The call added a year-end catalyst that the preview did not anticipate: a registrational study of the iovera spasticity program, despite the iovera divestiture. The preview did expect year-end PCRX-201 and ZILRETTA shoulder-OA updates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Three key pipeline catalysts are expected by year-end 2026: top-line data from PCRX-201 Part A (Phase 2 knee OA), ZILRETTA shoulder OA Phase 3 results, and the iovera spasticity registrational study.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ZILRETTA Phase 3 (shoulder OA) topline is expected by year-end 2026. Also watch PCRX-201 knee-OA gene therapy Phase 2 progress.”

surprises.description: LG Chem filed for EXPAREL approval in South Korea, with revenue positioned to begin in 2027; the preview did not mention this potential market entry.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LG Chem filed for EXPAREL approval in South Korea, positioning revenue to begin in 2027.”

surprises.description: In the preview’s discussion of generic entry starting in early 2030, the call also reported EXPAREL patent exclusivity extending into the 2040s. That provides a longer-dated durability detail not included in the preview, though the preview’s stated generic-entry settlement remains relevant.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EXPAREL patent exclusivity extending into the 2040s.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The April 2025 settlement lets Fresenius Kabi/eVenus sell volume-limited generic bupivacaine liposome starting in early 2030.”

in_line: Full-year EXPAREL guidance was reiterated at $600–$620 million, as in the preview’s stated guidance.
The preview expected year-end ZILRETTA shoulder-OA Phase 3 results and PCRX-201 knee-OA Phase 2 progress; the call listed those programs among expected year-end catalysts.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $275 million, above the preview’s working estimate of $262–265 million and even above its $270 million bull-case threshold. The result was stronger than the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached approximately $275 million, up 20% year-over-year (16% on a constant currency basis).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Working assumption: consensus revenue ≈ $262–265M”; bull scenario: “Revenue $270M+.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $1.05 materially exceeded the preview’s $0.95 consensus estimate (and its $0.92 alternative). The beat was much larger than the preview’s base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose 18% to $1.05 from $0.89.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 adj. EPS … Consensus $0.95 (alt. $0.92)”; base scenario: “$0.94–0.97.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was approximately $109 million, ahead of the preview’s roughly $103 million estimate. The margin was within the expected 39–40% band, so the surprise was in the dollar amount rather than margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 18% to approximately $109 million”; “adjusted EBITDA margin slipped to 39.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 adj. EBITDA ~$103M (author estimate)”; “FY margin guide 39–40%.”

surprises.description: Latin America Payments and Solutions grew 42% in constant currency, well above the preview’s expectation that LatAm constant-currency growth would hold above 20%. Segment adjusted EBITDA also rose 70%, adding to the strength of the result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Latin America Payments and Solutions revenue surged 52% year-over-year to $131 million (42% constant currency)”; “segment adjusted EBITDA jumped 70% to $40 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview ranked “LatAm organic constant-currency growth” as the key metric and described the bull case as “LatAm cc holds above 20%.”

surprises.description: Business Solutions revenue fell 9%, rather than improving to the roughly 5% decline the preview inferred for Q2. The Popular contract discount remains a headwind, with its year-over-year impact not set to anniversary until Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Business Solutions revenue fell 9% to $59 million due to the 10% Popular contract discount, with the associated year-over-year headwind set to anniversary in Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY guide “implies Q2 improves to about −5%.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY26 revenue guidance to $1.085–1.095 billion, above the preview’s cited prior range of $1.073–1.085 billion and consensus of $1.08 billion. The new low end equals the old high end, while the new high end is higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $1.085–$1.095 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue | Company guidance | $1.073–1.085B (raised from $1.024–1.036B) | Consensus $1.08B”; the preview’s bull case was a raise to “≥$1.09B.”

surprises.description: FY26 adjusted EPS growth guidance of 8.8–11.7% is higher than the preview’s expected company range of 6.6–9.9%. The increase puts the new range’s low end above the prior expected low end and its high end above the expected high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS growth of 8.8%–11.7% from $3.62 in 2025.”

surprises.description: The FY26 revenue outlook includes roughly 200 basis points of FX tailwind, more than the preview’s estimate of about 135 basis points. That means a larger share of the outlook’s growth benefit is attributed to currency than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: FY26 revenue guidance “including roughly 200 basis points of FX tailwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Guidance includes ~135 bps of FY FX tailwind from BRL.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a multi-year Transbank agreement, with results expected to begin being affected in the second half of 2027 and the merchant migration fully ramping in 2028. The preview did not flag this agreement or its future contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The multi-year Transbank agreement in Chile—one of the largest acquirers in Latin America—is expected to begin impacting results in the second half of 2027 and fully ramp in 2028 as a migration of the existing merchant base.”

surprises.description: The company repurchased about 2 million shares for $47 million and replenished its buyback authorization to $150 million. The preview did not discuss this level of repurchases or the authorization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased approximately 2 million shares for $47 million during the quarter, paid $3 million in dividends, and the board replenished the buyback authorization to $150 million.”

surprises.description: Net debt and leverage were higher than a year earlier, with leverage at 2.55x trailing EBITDA versus 1.95x, primarily following the Dimensa acquisition. The preview focused on Dimensa’s expected revenue contribution but did not flag this balance-sheet increase; liquidity was still reported as strong.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt reached approximately $1 billion with leverage rising to 2.55x trailing EBITDA (from 1.95x a year ago) primarily due to the ~$199 million Dimensa acquisition, while liquidity remained strong at ~$420 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed “Dimensa’s two-month revenue” and said it “needs to land near $12M,” but did not state an expectation for debt or leverage.

surprises.description: Management said AI-driven efficiency benefits are expected to enter the financial outlook starting in 2027. The preview did not anticipate this prospective source of efficiency gains.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expects AI-driven efficiency benefits to be incorporated into financial outlook starting in 2027.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 39.8%, within the preview’s cited 39–40% band.

Cybersecurity remediation costs were anticipated as a possible Q2 expense: the preview said remediation and legal costs from the disclosed incident “may hit the P&L,” and the call reported remediation costs. The call also said operations were not disrupted.

surprises.description: Booking Holdings reported 5% room-night growth, above both its 2%–4% company guide and the preview’s 3.7% consensus estimate. That was a modest but clear volume beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 room nights grew 5%, exceeding the high end of guidance by about 1 percentage point.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Room nights | 320.6M … +3.7%”; company guide “+2% to +4%.”

surprises.description: Gross bookings grew 9%, materially faster than the preview’s 5.8% consensus estimate and the company’s 4%–6% guide. The 8% constant-currency growth also exceeded the preview’s high-single-digit constant-currency framework.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross bookings rose 9% (8% constant currency).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross bookings | $49.42B … +5.8%”; company guide “+4% to +6%”; FY framework: “constant-currency gross bookings high-single digits.”

surprises.description: Revenue grew 8%, above the preview’s 5.8% consensus estimate and the company’s 4%–6% guide. Constant-currency growth was 7%, also above the guide’s 2%–4% constant-currency range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue increased 8% (7% constant currency).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $7.19B … +5.8%”; company guide “+4% to +6% (cc +2% to +4%).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was approximately $2.6 billion and grew 9%, ahead of the 4%–6% growth implied by the company’s guide. The preview’s implied estimate was about $2.2 billion, so the reported result was also a substantial dollar beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $2.6 billion grew 9% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$2.2B (implied, not a sourced sell-side mark)”; company guide: “+4% to +6%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $2.54 exceeded the preview’s $2.44–$2.46 consensus range by about 3%–4%. The company said a 6% reduction in share count helped the result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS of $2.54 rose 15%, aided by a 6% reduction in share count.”

surprises.description: The full-year gross-bookings outlook is now high-single-digit growth, down from the preview’s high-single- to low-double-digit framework. Management attributed the change primarily to weaker flight-ticket growth, while leaving the accommodation outlook largely unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered its full-year gross bookings outlook, now expecting high single-digit growth, primarily due to lower flight ticket growth while the accommodation outlook remains largely unchanged.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company FY26 framework: gross bookings growth high-single to low-double digits.”

surprises.description: Q3 room-night guidance of 3%–5% is below the preview’s cited buy-side expectation of 5%–7%; its midpoint is 4%. Guidance for gross bookings, revenue, and adjusted EBITDA is 4%–6% growth, signaling a slower near-term pace than the preview’s expected recovery scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for room night growth of 3%-5% and gross bookings, revenue, and adjusted EBITDA each growing 4%-6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The buy side wants Q3 room nights at +5% to +7%”; the preview’s base scenario also expected “Q3 room nights +5–7%.”

surprises.description: Management raised expected annual run-rate transformation savings to about $650 million from $550 million, with the additional $100 million expected mainly in 2027. The preview had not identified a planned savings increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised expected annual run-rate savings from the transformation program to approximately $650 million from $550 million … with the incremental $100 million from procurement to be realized primarily in 2027.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for quantified AI benefits in cost or conversion, but the call reported that traffic from large language models remains immaterial and has not meaningfully increased. That provides little evidence of the AI-related traffic tailwind the preview wanted to see.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Traffic received from large language models on both paid and unpaid bases remains significantly below 1% of room nights and has not moved materially in recent quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management needs to show agentic AI … as a cost and conversion tailwind”; the preview listed “AI proof points with numbers” as a catalyst.

surprises.description: Connected Trip transactions grew at a low-double-digit rate—more than twice Booking.com’s total transaction growth—and made up a low-double-digit share of transactions. The preview did not flag this operating metric, so the reported pace is a positive new data point rather than a result against a stated estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Connected Trip transactions grew low double digits—more than twice Booking.com's total transaction growth—and represented a low double-digit percentage of total transactions.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA growth was slightly faster than revenue growth, consistent with the preview’s FY26 framework; the call reported EBITDA growth of 9% versus revenue growth of 8%, with margin expanding nearly 40 basis points.
The $3.7 billion of Q2 buybacks was close to the preview’s expectation of a buyback pace near the prior-quarter record of $3.6 billion.

surprises.description: Crexendo delivered only 7% consolidated organic growth in Q2, below the preview’s roughly 10.6% implied expectation and its 11% threshold for a clean outcome. The 11% year-to-date rate does not offset the quarterly shortfall against that Q2 expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated organic growth was only 7% for the quarter (11% year-to-date).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus appears to embed about 10.6% core organic growth for Q2”; “Anything at or above 11% is a clean outcome; below 11% challenges the double-digit thesis.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $0.12, above the preview’s estimates of $0.08 or $0.10. Adjusted EBITDA also rose 46% to $4.1 million, although the preview did not give an EBITDA estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income reached $4.1 million ($0.12 per share) and adjusted EBITDA rose 46% to $4.1 million at a 17% margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (non-GAAP): $0.08 (Zacks) or $0.10 (alt. tracked estimate).”

surprises.description: Consolidated gross margin reached 66%, well above the preview’s 61% watch level. Software solutions margin was 70%, also above the preview’s 68% bull-case marker; product margin improved to 44% from 31% in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin improved 500 basis points sequentially to 66%, with software solutions at 70% ... service at 67%, and product at 44%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A slide below 60% would raise questions”; “Software solutions margin above 68% supports the bull case”; catalyst checklist: “Gross margin held at or above 61%.”

surprises.description: ESI contributed $6.9 million in Q2, exceeding the preview’s roughly $6.2–$6.3 million full-quarter benchmark. Its monthly contribution also rose from $2.1 million in March to an average of $2.3 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ESI acquisition contributed $6.9 million in Q2 revenue, growing from $2.1 million in March to an average of $2.3 million per month.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A full quarter well below roughly $6.2M would suggest attrition in the acquired base”; catalyst checklist: “ESI full-quarter revenue versus about $6.3M.”

surprises.description: Cash ended Q2 at $18.3 million, above the $7.2 million reported for Q1 in the preview, and year-to-date operating cash flow was up 89%. The preview had highlighted balance-sheet and possible equity-raise concerns, though the reported cash balance remains below the $31.4 million pre-acquisition level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $18.3 million in cash (down from $31.4 million) after using $26.2 million for ESI, while generating $4.8 million in operating cash flow year-to-date, up 89%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash $7.2M, down from $31.4M at year-end 2025 after the ESI purchase”; “Any hint of an equity raise would likely be poorly received.”

surprises.description: Perpetual license revenue fell by $700,000 from the prior-year quarter as new licensees placed smaller initial orders of about $250,000. Upgrade orders were larger, averaging roughly $300,000–$350,000, but the preview did not flag this weakness in initial license sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Perpetual license revenue fell $700,000 versus the prior-year quarter, as new licensees opted for smaller initial orders (~$250,000) with upgrade orders averaging 50% higher (~$300,000-$350,000).”

surprises.description: RPO grew 97% year over year, accelerating from the 56% growth reported in Q1 and providing visibility over the next 60 months. The preview reported the Q1 figure but did not set a Q2 RPO expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Remaining performance obligation surged 97% year-over-year to $139 million, providing strong visibility into future revenue recognized over the next 60 months.”

surprises.description: The call reported monetization from CAIRO, a new AI receptionist: about $120 per account per month, or 35% above a typical Telecom Services customer’s $340 average revenue. The preview did not mention the product or this incremental revenue opportunity; management said AI revenue is expected to become meaningful in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new CAIRO AI receptionist product added an average of ~$120 per account per month, a 35% increase over the typical Telecom Services customer's $340 average revenue, with AI revenue expected to become meaningful in 2027.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $24.6 million was essentially in line with the preview’s stale $24.63 million consensus, despite the call describing it as a beat versus analyst expectations.
Management reaffirmed the $100 million revenue run-rate goal by year-end 2026, as the preview’s base case anticipated.

surprises.description: Revenue was $29.8 million, well below the preview’s derived estimate of about $33.5 million. The shortfall was larger than the preview’s stated revenue-estimate uncertainty of roughly $1 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $29.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$33.5M (derived, not published)” and “about ±$1M of slop.”

surprises.description: Net income was $1 million, or $0.01 per diluted share, below even the preview’s lower clean-EPS range of $0.02–0.04 and below the cited consensus estimates of $0.04–0.06.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income fell to $1 million ($0.01 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The company's own model implies Q2 GAAP EPS of $0.02–0.04” and consensus was “$0.04” from MarketBeat and “$0.06” from Zacks.

surprises.description: The ingredient business was only $5.4 million, with management expecting a year-over-year decline amid competitive pressure and lower Life Extension purchases. That is weaker than the preview’s stated need for B2B and ingredient sales to stabilize.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ingredient business generated only $5.4 million” and “is expected to decline year-over-year due to competitive pressure from NMN and NAD, partly reflecting lower purchases from Life Extension.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “B2B and ingredient lines. These drove the Q1 shortfall and need to stabilize.”

surprises.description: Selling and marketing rose sharply as a share of sales, and management expects that elevated spending to continue. The preview flagged operating-expense pressure but did not anticipate this level of marketing expense or its persistence.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Selling and marketing expense jumped to 34% of net sales from 26.4% a year ago,” and management indicated “this elevated run rate will continue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Q1 ... opex rose 26%” and highlighted “Clean earnings power,” but did not state an expectation for elevated marketing spending to continue.

surprises.description: Management framed 2026 as an investment year and described 2027 as the period for accelerated growth, suggesting the acceleration the preview said was needed in H2 may be deferred.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management framed “2026 as an investment year and a springboard for accelerated growth in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 delivered +5% ex-ARS, so H2 must accelerate sharply.”

surprises.description: E-commerce grew 14%, above the preview’s concern threshold of roughly 10%; management estimated growth would have been 19% without a temporary Amazon listing issue. The issue was resolved, so the underlying growth was stronger than the reported figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “E-commerce revenue grew 14% to $20.5 million,” and growth “would have been 19% absent a temporary Amazon marketplace listing issue in June that has since been resolved.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If it decelerates below ~10%, the growth story weakens.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 64.8%, essentially stable year over year, rather than the preview’s expected 63.5–64.0% range and 100–150 basis-point decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin held roughly stable at 64.8% versus 65% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~63.5–64.0%” and implied “−100 to −150bp.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a substantial estimated value for NB4168’s Ataxia-Telangiectasia indication, plus a potentially transferable priority review voucher. The preview focused on the R&D budget and funding, not this potential asset value.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management estimated the indication “could support a net present value of $200-400 million,” plus “a potential transferable priority review voucher recently valued at $150-180 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Pharma R&D budget and funding language” as a key item to watch, but gave no valuation expectation for NB4168 or a voucher.

surprises.description: The projected remaining NB4168 development cost was only about $30 million through approval over four years, with first-in-human studies expected next year and the company expected to remain cash-flow positive. This was a favorable, more concrete funding picture than the preview’s open question about the pharma budget.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total drug development spending for NB4168 from now through approval is projected at only about $30 million spread over four years,” with first-in-human studies expected next year, “keeping the company cash-flow positive.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Pharma R&D budget and funding language against $63.8M net cash.”

surprises.description: China cross-border revenue through May had already surpassed the prior full-year total, and the company had received Mainland China approval for topical and skincare products. The preview did not flag this commercialization progress.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China cross-border revenue through May 2026 already exceeded the full-year 2025 total (which was under $1 million),” and the company “recently received topical/skincare product approval in Mainland China though dietary ingredient approval remains pending.”

surprises.description: NanoClouds sold out its limited run, with strong new-to-brand and repeat purchases, leading to a broader relaunch. The company also said two large global skincare companies were discussing potentially exclusive Niagen deals; neither development was anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NanoClouds sold out its limited run of 3,000-4,000 units with strong new-to-brand and repeat purchases,” prompting a broader October/November relaunch, while “two large global skincare companies are in discussions about potentially exclusive Niagen deals.”

surprises.description: Papzimeus revenue rose far more sharply than the preview’s broad expectation of a step-up from Q1: Q2 revenue was $53.1 million, more than 145% above Q1’s $21.6 million. That is a much stronger sequential result than the preview’s base case of modest growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$53.1 million in Papzimeus revenue in Q2 2026, up more than 145% from $21.6 million in Q1”; “total revenue of $55 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Papzimeos sequential growth off the $21.6M Q1 base”; the base scenario expected “Modest growth from Q1,” while the bull scenario expected a “Clear step-up from $21.6M.”

surprises.description: Precigen reported a profit instead of the Q2 loss expected by consensus: net income was $20.1 million, or $0.05 per diluted share, and operating income was $22.6 million. This was also an early profitability milestone, reached before Papzimeus’s first FDA-approval anniversary.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Quarterly net income of $20.1 million ($0.05 per diluted share) and operating income of $22.6 million, reaching profitability before the drug's first FDA-approval anniversary.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 EPS” consensus: “–$0.01”; the preview’s bull scenario said “Beat –$0.01.”

surprises.description: Management tempered the strong launch outlook by saying quarterly revenue should keep growing but at a mathematically diminishing rate. The preview highlighted meaningful acceleration implied by FY26 revenue consensus, so this is a caution that growth rates will moderate, even as revenue continues to rise.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expects future quarterly revenue growth to continue but at a mathematically diminishing rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY26 revenue consensus was “~$124.4M” or “~$126.9M,” which the preview said “implies meaningful acceleration”; its bull scenario also cited “Growth sustained.”

surprises.description: The company reported broad payer access and said the permanent J-code helped bring previously hesitant institutions on board, indicating an adoption benefit beyond simply tracking the J-code’s gross-to-net effects. The preview identified J-code dynamics as a key issue but did not anticipate this reported acceleration in institutional adoption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Payer coverage grew by approximately 18 million covered lives in Q2 to roughly 315 million total commercial and government lives, representing nearly all potential covered lives in the US”; the permanent J-code “accelerated adoption by bringing previously hesitant institutions on board.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “gross-to-net dynamics after the J-code took effect” and “J3404 gross-to-net effects.”

surprises.description: Precigen disclosed seven-year adult RRP market exclusivity for Papzimeus through August 2032, a competitive-protection development the preview did not flag. Management said it protects against prospective competition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FDA granted seven-year market exclusivity for Papzimeus in adult RRP through August 2032, providing protection against prospective competition.”

surprises.description: The company reported a 95% Q2 gross margin but said margins will settle lower, in the high-80% to low-90% range, once remaining pre-launch inventory is consumed in Q3. The preview gave no margin expectation, so the notable new information is the expected normalization from the Q2 level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin was 95%, but management guided that steady-state margins will stabilize in the high-80% to low-90% range (roughly 10% COGS) once remaining pre-launch inventory is consumed in Q3.”

in_line: Management reiterated that Precigen expects to fund operations through cash-flow breakeven by the end of 2026, as the preview identified as a key expectation.

surprises.description: Marqeta reported adjusted EBITDA of $37 million, well above the roughly $32 million expected, with 31% year-over-year growth. Its 21% net revenue margin also exceeded the preview’s implied margin of about 18.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 31% year-over-year to $37 million (21% net revenue margin, 31% gross profit margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: +10–12% → $31.9–32.5M”; the preview also said this implied “margin contraction from 19.3% to about 18.6%.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA growth expectations to the low 30s, above the preview’s expectation of mid-to-high-20s growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year outlook, now expecting adjusted EBITDA growth in the low 30s.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance … adj. EBITDA growth mid-to-high 20s%.”

surprises.description: The Cash App new-issuance headwind worsened from the preview’s roughly 1.5% full-year framing: Marqeta expects little to no new issuance by year-end and estimates about a 2-point drag on second-half gross profit growth, with a possible run-rate impact above 2 points in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marqeta began seeing a modest decline in Cash App new issuance around mid-June (roughly 10% below expected), stepping up in July”; it expects “little to no new issuance by year-end” and estimates a “~2 point second-half gross profit growth drag.” Management said the 2027 run-rate impact “could exceed a 2-point growth impact.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had cut the “Block/Cash App headwind to FY gross profit … to ~1.5%” and that “a move back toward 2% would break the H2 bridge.”

surprises.description: The Q3 outlook calls for only 5%–7% gross profit growth, below the preview’s implied second-half pace of roughly 7%–9%; net revenue growth is also expected to slow to 6%–8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for a sharp deceleration to 6%-8% net revenue growth and 5%-7% gross profit growth, about a 10-point step down from Q2,” driven by tougher comparisons, renewal timing, the TransactPay lap, BNPL, and Cash App diversification.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY guidance implied “H2 gross profit growth of roughly 7–9%” and flagged tougher BNPL comparisons, but expected the H2 bridge to remain intact in its base scenario.

surprises.description: Full-year GAAP net income expectations rose to the high $20 millions, well above the preview’s roughly $15 million outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Marqeta is “now expecting … GAAP net income in the high $20 millions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance … GAAP net income ~$15M.”

surprises.description: Marqeta raised the low end of its full-year gross profit growth outlook from 10% to 11%, rather than reiterating the 10%–12% range the preview expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year outlook … gross profit growth to 11%-12%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY gross profit guidance as “+10–12%” and said reiterating “10–12% reads as conservative.”

surprises.description: Full-year revenue growth guidance was narrowed to 12%–13% from 12%–14%, lowering the upper end and midpoint of the prior range rather than simply reiterating it.
surprises.fact_evidence: Marqeta narrowed “revenue growth guidance to 12%-13%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY net revenue guidance as “+12–14%” and its base scenario expected FY guidance to be reiterated.

surprises.description: Q2 GAAP net income was about $8 million, above the preview’s expected range of roughly $0–5 million. The quarter was also Marqeta’s second consecutive GAAP-profitable quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income was approximately $8 million ($0.07 EPS), the company's second consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP net income: ~Breakeven” and consensus “~$0–5M.”

surprises.description: The board approved a new $150 million buyback after the company had largely used its existing $100 million authorization, a larger capital-return commitment than the preview specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: Marqeta “repurchased 3.2 million shares … largely exhausting its $100 million authorization, and the board approved an additional $150 million buyback.”

surprises.description: Marqeta disclosed that the average deal size signed in Q2 had risen more than 90% year over year, reflecting a shift toward larger, established enterprise and Fortune 500 customers; the preview did not anticipate this operating metric or strategy update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The average deal size signed in Q2 rose over 90% year-over-year,” reflecting a shift toward “larger, more established enterprise and Fortune 500 customers.”

surprises.description: International volume grew more than 40% and reached 20% of TPV, a significant expansion not called out in the preview. Management said this growth, along with large-customer growth, contributed to a slightly lower gross profit take rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International volume grew over 40% year-over-year and reached 20% of total TPV,” contributing with large-customer growth to a “one-basis-point year-over-year decline in gross profit take rate to approximately 10 basis points.”

surprises.description: Q2 net revenue reached $176 million, above the $172.9 million consensus and the top of the company’s guided range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenue grew 17% to $176 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave consensus of “$172.9M (+15.0%)” and company guidance of “$171.4–174.4M.”

surprises.description: Gross profit was $122 million with 17% growth, above the preview’s derived $119–121 million estimate and the 14%–16% growth guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit grew 17% to $122 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross profit at “~$119–121M” and noted Q2 guidance of “+14–16% → $118.6–120.6M.”

in_line: TPV growth remained at 32%, consistent with the preview’s bull-scenario threshold of “TPV +32%+” and the preview’s note that Marqeta had recently sustained growth above 30%.
Non-Block TPV continued to grow more than twice as fast as Block TPV, matching the preview’s key diversification check that non-Block growth needed to hold at about 2x Block’s rate.
Gross profit take-rate compression continued: the preview explicitly said take-rate compression was ongoing, and the call reported a one-basis-point year-over-year decline.

surprises.description: US procedures grew 21% to just over 13,100, below the preview’s base-case expectation of 13,300–13,800. Management attributed the softer growth to weakness in legacy AquaBeam accounts, not newer Hydros accounts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “US procedures totaled over 13,100 in Q2, growing 21% year-over-year, but the growth was softer than expectations due to concentrated weakness in legacy AquaBeam accounts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “US procedures” of “~13.3–13.8K.”

surprises.description: Management cut full-year US procedure guidance to 54,000–56,000, substantially below the prior 60,200–64,100 range cited in the preview—about 7,000 fewer procedures at the midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered full-year 2026 US procedure guidance to 54,000-56,000 (25-29% growth), implying an approximately 7,000-procedure reduction at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Standing FY2026 guidance was “US procedure growth +39–48% (about 60.2–64.1K procedures).”

surprises.description: Despite the procedure-guidance cut, PROCEPT maintained its $390–410 million revenue outlook. The preview’s base case anticipated narrowing revenue guidance to roughly $385–398 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Maintaining total revenue guidance of $390-410 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario anticipated “FY26 narrowed to low end (~$385–398M).”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin reached 66%, above the preview’s roughly 65% expectation, although the result was aided by a $2.9 million tariff recovery. Full-year gross-margin guidance remained approximately 65%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin was 66% (versus 65% prior year), aided by a $2.9 million tariff recovery, while full-year gross margin guidance was maintained at approximately 65%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 gross margin consensus was “~65%”; standing FY guidance was “Gross margin ~65%.”

surprises.description: US system ASP was approximately $495,000, above the preview’s cited expectation that new-system ASP would be $450,000–$460,000 for the rest of 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company placed 65 Hydros systems in Q2 … at a record-high US ASP of approximately $495,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: After Q1, “Management guided new-system ASP down to $450–460K for the rest of 2026.”

surprises.description: Replacement activity was stronger than the company had modeled: 14 replacement units were sold in Q2, and management now expects about 40 for the full year. The preview did not flag replacement sales as an expected driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Replacement system activity accelerated, with 14 units in Q2 exceeding internal models, and the company now expects approximately 40 replacement sales for the full year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “14 units in Q2 exceeding internal models.”

surprises.description: The expense outlook worsened: full-year operating expense guidance rose above the preview’s approximately $350 million, and the adjusted EBITDA loss range shifted from $30–$17 million to $30–$35 million, with the company citing increased commercial and patient-activation investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year operating expense guidance to $355-360 million and narrowed adjusted EBITDA loss guidance to $30-35 million, funding increased commercial and patient-activation investments through offsetting corporate cost trade-offs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Standing FY2026 guidance was “Opex ~$350M” and “Adj. EBITDA loss of $(30)M to $(17)M.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $94.5 million exceeded the $92.64 million consensus estimate, though it remained within the company’s $91–95 million quarterly guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $94.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus was “$92.64M”; company guide was “$91–95M.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 2026, as the preview specifically flagged as an outcome to watch.
Full-year gross-margin guidance remained approximately 65%, in line with the preview’s standing guidance.

surprises.description: OneSpan raised its 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA ranges instead of simply reaffirming them: revenue moved to $248–252 million from $244–249 million, and adjusted EBITDA to $67–71 million from $64–68 million. The hardware range also rose to $46–48 million from $43–45 million, on stronger first-half bookings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $248-252 million (from $244-249 million) and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $67-71 million (from $64-68 million).” Hardware guidance “was increased to $46-48 million (from $43-45 million) due to stronger first-half bookings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the company’s guidance was revenue of “$244–249M” and adjusted EBITDA of “$64–68M,” and described the base case as “FY guidance reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $60.5 million was above the preview’s lower consensus estimates and grew rather than declining as the Zacks estimate implied. It was, however, close to the preview’s roughly $60 million alternative estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue grew just 1% year-over-year to $60.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed revenue estimates of “$57.75M (−3.5% YoY)” and “$58.3M,” while also noting an alternative of “~$60M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin came in below the preview’s expected 29–30% floor, at 27.9%. The preview’s bull case called for at least 31%, so profitability was weaker than the watched margin range even though full-year EBITDA guidance was raised.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined to $16.9 million (27.9% margin) from $17.6 million (29.5%), reflecting increased costs from acquisitions and organic go-to-market investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin “holds at 29–30% or better”; its bull case called for “31% or more.”

surprises.description: Digital agreements delivered much stronger growth and profitability than the preview’s overall low-growth setup suggested: revenue rose 25.2% and operating income nearly doubled, with margin reaching 35.7%. The preview gave no specific segment forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The digital agreements division delivered 25.2% revenue growth to $19.5 million, with operating income nearly doubling to $7 million (35.7% margin) from $2.9 million (18.4%) a year ago, boosted by strong overage revenue.”

surprises.description: Cybersecurity was a pronounced weak spot: revenue fell 7.5%, while operating income dropped from $19.8 million to $13.8 million and margin contracted from 45% to 34%. The preview flagged a contract-related ARR headwind but did not forecast this segment decline or the size of its profit deterioration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cybersecurity division revenue declined 7.5% to $40.9 million and operating income fell to $13.8 million (34% margin) from $19.8 million (45%),” pressured by “a $3 million known headwind, hardware/perpetual maintenance declines, and acquisition costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted management had flagged an “expected ~$3M Q2 ARR headwind from two contract non-renewals,” but gave no cybersecurity revenue or operating-income expectation.

surprises.description: Subscription revenue grew much faster than total revenue and increased its share of the business, reaching 77% of revenue versus 70% a year earlier. The preview discussed subscription revenue from Q1 but did not set a Q2 subscription or mix expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subscription revenue grew 11% to $47 million and now represents 77% of total revenue, up from 70% a year ago.”

surprises.description: DigiPASS One had launched as the preview anticipated, but the call indicated its revenue impact would be mainly in 2027, with Verify still at the customer proof-of-concept stage. That puts meaningful monetization later than the preview’s emphasis on the product as a second-half topic might suggest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company launched its new DigiPASS One authentication platform, integrating the Knock Knock and Build 38 acquisitions,” but “DigiPASS One Verify [is] still in customer proof-of-concept stage and revenue impact expected mainly in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said DigipassONE had launched “too late for Q2 numbers but likely central to second-half commentary.”

in_line: ARR was $189.7 million, down from $192.1 million in Q1; the preview said a flat-to-down sequential print could still be on plan because of the expected contract non-renewals.
The DigiPASS One launch itself was already known before the release; the preview noted the July 22 launch and expected the product to feature in second-half commentary.
The quarterly dividend remained 13 cents, consistent with the preview’s note that the company had a $0.13 quarterly dividend.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was negative $0.3 million, about $1.85 million below the preview’s roughly $1.55 million consensus estimate. The company attributed the shortfall to a $1.2 million non-cash reversal of Q1 revenue after changing assumptions on SK On milestone payments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was negative $300,000,” hurt by “a $1.2 million reversal of Q1 revenue tied to changed assumptions on SK ON milestone payments,” which was “non-cash with no associated cost reversals.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$1.55M (MarketBeat, 7/28/26).”

surprises.description: The preview described partner evaluation for a 500-metric-ton commercial facility, while management now expects to announce a South Korean commercial-scale electrolyte-production joint venture by year-end and said one prospective partner is already discussing a draft term sheet. That is a more concrete near-term step than the preview described.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects to announce a joint venture for commercial-scale electrolyte production in South Korea by the end of the year,” with “one of three prospective partners already in draft term sheet discussions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management is evaluating partners for a 500-metric-ton electrolyte facility, with demand focused in Korea rather than North America.”

surprises.description: Instead of reporting evaluation feedback or a clear continuation, management said the Samsung SDI–BMW Phase 1 evaluation agreement is due to expire at the end of September and that discussions about a new framework are ongoing. The status therefore leaves continuation unresolved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Phase 1 Joint Evaluation Agreement with Samsung SDI and BMW is set to expire at the end of September,” and the company is “in discussions to continue collaboration on a new framework.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Samsung SDI / BMW evaluation feedback” as a catalyst to watch, noting that Samsung SDI had received electrolyte samples under the joint evaluation agreement.

surprises.description: The preview said electrolyte demand was focused in Korea rather than North America, but management reported growing U.S. customer interest from humanoid robotics companies and new interest from defense and aerospace. It also cautioned that domestic cell manufacturing is not yet available at scale, so the interest is not yet backed by scaled local production.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management noted “growing US customer interest from humanoid robotics companies plus new interest from defense and aerospace,” but “sees no domestic cell manufacturing at scale yet.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Demand [is] focused in Korea rather than North America.”

surprises.description: The preview’s base case anticipated steady cash burn, but operating expenses edged up from Q1 and the operating loss rose from $26.3 million to $30.3 million. This was a modest increase in quarterly spending despite the slightly better-than-consensus EPS result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses of $30 million (up slightly from $29.4 million in Q1)” and a “Q2 operating loss of $30.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario described “cash burn steady,” and identified the Q1 operating loss as “about $26M.”

in_line: EPS was a one-cent beat: the reported loss of $0.11 per share was slightly better than the preview’s consensus loss estimate of $0.12.
The pilot-line schedule remained broadly consistent with the preview: commissioning was targeted for year-end 2026, and management said commissioning would start in Q4.

surprises.description: Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $1.28, well above the preview’s cited $0.98 Reuters/LSEG consensus and above its $1.05–$1.20 base-case range. The result was still down from $1.41 a year earlier, but the decline was much smaller than the preview’s roughly 22% decline implied by consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS declined to $1.28 from $1.41.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 EPS ... $0.98 (Reuters/LSEG, ~Aug 2026)”; the base scenario forecast “Non-GAAP EPS $1.05–1.20.”

surprises.description: Net sales of $649.1 million were modestly above the preview’s roughly $630–640 million estimate, although year-over-year growth of 1% was broadly consistent with its expectation of roughly flat sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 consolidated net sales rose just 1% year-over-year to $649.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “‘Roughly flat YoY,’ about $630–640M”; the preview also described a base scenario of “$615–645M.”

surprises.description: Professional services revenue declined 5.1%, a milder drop than the preview said was plausible, despite project delays tied to product delivery. However, the segment’s gross margin also fell 230 basis points to 36.9%, a deterioration the preview did not specifically flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Professional services revenue declined 5.1% to $68.1 million due to project delays tied to product delivery, while gross margin in that segment fell 230 basis points to 36.9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A double-digit decline is plausible” for professional services revenue.

surprises.description: Working-capital indicators improved substantially: inventory fell by $54.9 million from the preview’s cited $200.9 million level, and the cash conversion cycle shortened 10 days sequentially. The preview had highlighted elevated inventory and working capital as areas to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The cash conversion cycle improved 10 days sequentially to 41 days as inventory fell $54.9 million to $146 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “At 3/31/26 ... inventory $200.9M (+66.8% YoY). Operating cash flow is the tell.”

surprises.description: Managed services passed $50 million in quarterly sales for the first time and grew more than 15%, an unanticipated revenue proof point in the preview’s discussion of AI and memory-related programs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Managed services net sales surpassed $50 million for the first time, growing over 15% year-over-year, driven by data center and cloud demand.”

surprises.description: Security gross billings grew 15.6%, with multiyear enterprise software licensing agreements contributing to the growth. The preview focused on overall gross billings but did not anticipate or provide a specific security-growth expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Security gross billings grew 15.6% and represented 24.2% of gross billings on a trailing 12-month basis, aided by multiple multiyear enterprise software licensing agreements.”

surprises.description: Management authorized repurchases of up to 1.5 million shares, a stronger stated buyback commitment than the preview’s reference point of only 90,000 shares repurchased in Q4 FY2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Returned $26.7 million in dividends and $53.1 million in buybacks over the past year, plus a new authorization to repurchase up to 1.5 million shares.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Only 90k shares were repurchased in Q4 FY26, against $410.8M cash and a raised $0.27 quarterly dividend.”

surprises.description: Retail project delays remained customer-specific, with revenue expected only in the back half of the year or later. That suggests slower conversion timing than the preview’s base case, which assumed backlog was up but conversion timing was unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retail project delays remain customer-specific with revenue expected only in the back half of the year or later.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario assumed “backlog is up but conversion timing is unchanged.”

in_line: Management maintained FY2027 guidance, matching the preview’s base case of a reiteration.
Consolidated gross margin was 23.3%, within the preview’s 23.0%–24.0% base-case range; the preview also anticipated that memory-related cost inflation could pressure product-margin percentages.
Open orders and backlog being up was expected: the preview cited management’s prior comments that open orders and backlog were up and assumed backlog growth in its base case.
The $0.27 quarterly dividend was consistent with the preview, which noted that the dividend had already been raised to $0.27.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $311 million, well above the preview’s $259–266 million consensus range and even its $285 million bull-case estimate. The 26% margin also supported a higher full-year margin outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $311 million with a margin of 26%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA” consensus: “~$259–266M”; preview bull scenario: “$285M.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $1.190–$1.210 billion comes in below the preview’s roughly $1.21 billion implied bar at the low end and has a $1.20 billion midpoint. The company also described slower year-over-year growth, with FX, Prime Day timing, and non-recurring World Cup spending weighing on the comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $1.190-$1.210 billion implies decelerating growth of 13-15%, pressured by roughly 3 points of sequential headwinds from FX, Prime Day timing, and non-recurring World Cup spend.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue (implied bar): ~$1.21B (+15%).” The preview also says, “A Q3 guide starting near $1.19B or below would be read as a negative.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue reached $1.180 billion, beating the preview’s $1.147 billion consensus and the company’s $1.133–1.153 billion guidance range. Growth of 18% also exceeded the preview’s expected 15%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $1.180 billion, growing 18% year-over-year (17% constant currency).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue” consensus: “~$1,147M (+15%)”; company guide: “$1,133–1,153M (+14–16%).”

surprises.description: UCAN revenue grew 18%, well above the preview’s 12.4% expectation, and was the primary source of the Q2 outperformance. This was stronger than the preview’s threshold for concern, which was growth below 11%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “UCAN revenue accelerated 5 points sequentially to 18% year-over-year growth, reaching $880 million and serving as the primary driver of Q2 outperformance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “U.S. & Canada revenue” consensus: “$837.4M, +12.4%”; “Growth below 11% would weaken the view that the core market is stable.”

surprises.description: Management raised its FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin outlook to approximately 30%, rather than merely reaffirming the preview’s expected 29% target. That is a favorable change against a preview that highlighted the challenge of achieving the target and the risk of investment spending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $311 million with a margin of 26% (up 130 basis points year-over-year), prompting management to raise full-year 2026 EBITDA margin guidance to approximately 30% from 29%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026: Company target of ~29% adjusted EBITDA margin”; the preview flagged “FY26 margin target (~29%)” as a key issue.

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS growth was reported at 30%, far above the preview’s expected 9.1% growth. The call attributed the uplift in part to repurchases reducing net dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date the company repurchased over $2 billion of stock (nearly 111 million shares at an average $18 price), reducing Q2 net dilution 12% year-over-year and driving 30% non-GAAP EPS growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS” consensus: “$0.36 (+9.1% YoY).”

surprises.description: Europe faced a more difficult picture than the preview’s description of “modest disruption”: growth was only 7% in constant currency, with cross-border retailer regulatory pressure also cited. Management said Q3 would be the region’s toughest comparison of the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Europe growth decelerated to 12% reported (7% constant currency) amid go-to-market restructuring and cross-border retailer regulatory pressure, with Q3 expected to be the most difficult comparison of the year for that region.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had flagged “modest disruption” in Q2 from “leadership restructuring and go-to-market changes in Europe and Rest of World.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed unusually low-cost AI infrastructure: open-source models cost less than 8% as much per transaction as comparable closed proprietary models. The preview raised AI investment as a possible margin risk but did not anticipate this cost advantage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company uses open source AI models achieving cost per transaction at less than 8% of comparable closed proprietary models, supporting margin expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warned that “‘investing behind AI’ language would be a negative,” but did not describe an expected AI-model cost advantage.

surprises.description: The call gave favorable Performance+ adoption and effectiveness metrics that the preview had not identified: adopters increased lower-funnel spending more than twice as fast as non-adopters, and recent model updates improved SMB ROAS by 28%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 30% of lower funnel revenue ran through Performance+ campaigns as of Q1, with adopters growing lower funnel spend more than twice as fast as non-adopters and recent model updates driving a 28% ROAS improvement for SMBs.”

surprises.description: Management said Q2 was expected to be the peak for stock-based compensation, with both SBC dollars and year-over-year growth stepping down from Q3. The preview discussed cost pressures and restructuring savings but did not flag this near-term SBC decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 stock-based compensation rose due to the annual grant cycle at a lower stock price and is expected to be the year's peak, with both SBC dollars and year-over-year growth stepping down starting Q3.”

in_line: Global MAUs were 640 million, within the preview’s stated 638–642 million estimate for the likely buy-side bar, although above the preview’s potentially stale 631 million consensus figure.

surprises.description: Rigel raised the upper end of its full-year revenue guidance by $5 million, with the increase coming from contract revenue rather than Vepinu. The preview listed FY26 contract revenue at $20–25 million and said a guide increase to include Vepinu would be the bullish outcome; the reported increase was instead supported by strong first-half contract revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rigel raised the upper bound of its full-year guidance by $5 million,” driven by increasing contract revenue guidance to “approximately $30 million” on strong first-half performance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 revenue guidance of “$275–290M” and said, “Raising the $275–290M guide to include VEPPANU would be the most bullish outcome.” It also listed contract revenue guidance of “$20–25M.”

in_line: FY26 product sales guidance stayed at $255–265 million, matching the preview’s stated company guidance.

Vepinu’s expected August commercial availability remained on schedule: management said it should be available in the middle of the month, consistent with the preview’s note that August availability had been promised.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $510.3 million, about $10.2 million above the preview’s roughly $500.1 million consensus estimate and at the bottom of its bull-case range. That is a modest beat versus the consensus baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated net revenue was $510.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue | ~$500.1M”; bull scenario: “Revenue | $510–518M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $208 million, above the preview’s derived base-case range of $198–204 million, though below its $210–216 million bull range. The preview had no published EBITDA consensus, so the comparison is to its scenario estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $208 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base scenario: “Adj. EBITDA | $198–204M”; bull scenario: “Adj. EBITDA | $210–216M.”

surprises.description: Green Valley Ranch disruption was about $7 million, roughly $2 million below the preview’s $9 million estimate for the East Tower. This was a smaller-than-expected temporary drag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Green Valley Ranch's hotel renovation removed over 21,000 room nights in Q2, causing about $7 million in temporary disruption, less than the previously guided $9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$9M from Green Valley Ranch East Tower”; catalyst: “Disruption dollars against the $9M GVR and $2–3M Durango guide.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed an approximately $8 million one-time anniversary and brand-marketing expense for Q3 that the preview did not anticipate. Management expects a net positive top-line effect, but the expense is a new near-term cost.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company will incur an approximately $8 million one-time 50th anniversary and brand marketing expense hitting Q3 corporate expense, though management expects a net positive top-line effect from the campaign.”

surprises.description: The call reported no Q2 share repurchases, with capital directed toward project spending. The preview specifically flagged buyback activity and remaining authorization as a capital-allocation question, but did not predict whether repurchases would occur.
surprises.fact_evidence: “No share repurchases made in Q2 as capital was directed toward project spend.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capital allocation: buyback activity against about $573M of remaining authority.”

surprises.description: The call reported active work on two greenfield projects and a Durango room-and-spa expansion, with further details expected in early 2027—development plans not anticipated in the preview. These are prospective projects rather than committed openings, so the update is limited in scope.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is actively working on two greenfield projects plus a Durango room-and-spa expansion, with more details expected in early 2027.”

in_line: Las Vegas operations’ 45.2% adjusted EBITDA margin remained above the preview’s 45% watch level; the preview said a second straight result below 45% would weaken the bull thesis.
Green Valley Ranch’s full hotel product, including the East Tower, is expected back online in September, consistent with the preview’s mid-September reopening expectation.
North Fork remains on budget at approximately $750 million and on pace for an early Q4 2026 opening, consistent with the preview. The call facts provided no quantified fee.

surprises.description: The preview set a service organic growth bar above 7%; Transcat reported 13%, six percentage points above that threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Organic service growth of 13%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Service organic growth vs. the ‘>7%’ bar management set for Q1.”

surprises.description: The indicative $0.38 EPS consensus was surpassed on an adjusted basis but missed substantially on a GAAP basis: adjusted EPS was $0.51 while GAAP EPS was $0.14. The preview noted that the consensus EPS basis was unclear, so the comparison is mixed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP diluted EPS was $0.14 and adjusted diluted EPS was $0.51.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 EPS … $0.38 … Page does not say whether GAAP or adjusted.”

surprises.description: Distribution profitability weakened: gross margin fell sharply and adjusted operating income declined, an unfavorable development not flagged in the preview. Management attributed the margin comparison partly to unusually high vendor rebates in the prior-year quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Distribution gross margin fell 380 basis points to 31.4% due to unusually high prior-year vendor rebates, and adjusted operating income declined 12% to $4.3 million.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed high-single-digit service organic growth for FY2027, consistent with the preview’s stated company guidance.
Service gross margin expanded year over year, matching the preview’s expectation that the promised improvement would be confirmed.

surprises.description: Revuforj revenue was $55 million, well below the preview’s implied $61–62 million bar. Its 12% sequential growth also fell short of the 25–27% growth the preview said would be needed to reach that bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revuforj net revenue was $55 million” and was “up” 12% quarter-over-quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revuforj net revenue (Q2): ~$61–62M”; hitting total-revenue consensus “needs about $61M” and “requires Revuforj growth of about 25–27% sequentially.”

surprises.description: Total revenue was $72.8 million, below the $79.4 million consensus in the preview, although it was close to the preview author’s $73 million base scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 revenue was $72.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue (Q2): $79.4M” consensus; the preview also listed a “Base” scenario of “~$73.0M.”

surprises.description: Revuforj new patient starts fell to 250 from about 330 in Q1, despite total prescriptions increasing sequentially. The preview flagged starts as a key metric to watch but did not give a specific forecast for them.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New patient starts declined sequentially to 250,” while total prescriptions were “up 15% QoQ”; management called the decline “a temporary anomaly.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 had about 330 starts” and “Watch for share data on competitive dynamics.”

surprises.description: The reported cash balance was substantially above the preview’s stated threshold for easing financing concerns. The balance included proceeds from a convertible-notes offering, so the increase was not solely from operations.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended Q2 with “$575 million in cash including $244 million net from June’s $250 million 2.25% convertible notes offering” and said it maintained “full funding through profitability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said that “reporting cash above $305M would ease financing concerns.”

surprises.description: Management added two Q4 clinical updates not listed in the preview’s catalyst calendar: a NUP98 relapsed/refractory publication and updated frontline AML trial data.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company cited pending fourth-quarter catalysts including “NUP98 relapsed/refractory publication” and “updated frontline AML trial data.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q4 pipeline items included Phase 2 IPF data, frontline cGVHD data, and a revumenib myelofibrosis proof-of-concept start; it did not list NUP98 or updated frontline AML data.

in_line: Niktimvo collaboration revenue was close to, and slightly above, the preview’s implied estimate: $18.1 million versus about $17.5 million. The preview also cited Incyte-reported Niktimvo sales of $60.3 million, close to the reported $60 million net revenue.

The transplant-pause cohort began returning to therapy as the preview expected: 50% of patients who proceeded to transplant had resumed therapy, up from 45% last quarter. The 70–80% figure was described as the ultimate target, not an expected Q2 rate.

The roughly $400 million R&D-plus-SG&A guidance, excluding about $50 million of noncash stock compensation, and the statement that cash would fund the company through profitability were consistent with the preview.
The preview’s anticipated Q4 Phase 2 IPF and frontline cGVHD data remained among the pending catalysts.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $190 million, roughly $6 million above the preview’s $184.17 million consensus estimate. That is a modest beat, with growth of 21% versus the preview’s expected 17%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached approximately $190 million, up 21% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: The company raised the low end of its FY26 revenue range by $10 million, to $737 million, while leaving the $757 million high end unchanged. The raised range excludes revenue from PAD Aviation, ENHANCE Part B, and DENOVO.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TransMedics raised the low end of full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $737 million to $757 million ... while excluding any contribution from PAD Aviation, ENHANCE Part B, or DENOVO.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue: $727–757M (+20–25%)”; the preview said to watch for “a raise, a trim, or a reiteration.”

surprises.description: FY26 adjusted operating margin guidance fell to 12.5%–14%, below the roughly 16% level implied by the preview’s prior margin guidance. Management attributed the reduction primarily to higher planned OCS Kidney investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted operating margin guidance was cut to approximately 12.5%-14% ... down from the prior ~16% expectation ... primarily due to higher planned OCS Kidney investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin: up to ~250 bps below 2025”; the preview noted 2025 operating margin of 18.5%.

surprises.description: Service gross margin rose sequentially from about 27% to 35% as aircraft were double-shifted and fleet utilization increased, a better Q2 service-margin result than the preview’s warning about margin dilution from faster flight growth suggested. Management cautioned that service margin would normalize lower in the seasonally soft second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Service gross margin improved sequentially from ~27% in Q1 to 35% in Q2 via double-shifting aircraft and higher fleet utilization, but management guided this will normalize lower in the seasonally soft second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Flight growth outpacing OCS growth is dilutive to margin.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that PAD Aviation had closed and would begin consolidation in Q3, with expected dilution to both gross and operating margins and no financial guidance yet. The preview did not flag this acquisition or its margin effect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The newly closed PAD Aviation acquisition in Germany will be consolidated starting Q3 and is expected to be dilutive to both gross and operating margins, with no financial guidance yet provided.”

in_line: Service revenue grew faster than product revenue, consistent with the preview’s warning that flight growth was outpacing OCS growth and could weigh on margins.

surprises.description: July sales grew 18% year over year, accelerating six points from Q2 and well above the preview’s low-teens pace implied by the recent run rate. This was a stronger Q3-to-date reacceleration than the preview’s base case of solid commentary suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “July net sales increasing approximately 18% year-over-year, a 6-point acceleration from Q2's growth rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything well below the low-teens pace implied by the April run-rate would weaken the reacceleration story”; UBS expected “solid” Q3-to-date commentary.

surprises.description: Unexpected tariff refunds lifted Q2 EPS to $0.26, above the preview’s $0.22 estimate, and contributed to reported gross margin of 56.6% versus the 54.1%–54.6% guide. The benefit was material: without the six-cent EPS contribution, EPS would have been about $0.20, and adjusted EBITDA excluding its $5.6 million refund benefit would have been about $21 million versus the preview’s implied $25–$27 million range.
