surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS rose to 26 cents … including a 6-cent benefit from IEPA tariff refunds”; adjusted EBITDA was $27 million “including a $5.6 million tariff refund benefit”; gross margin was 56.6%, including “roughly 160 basis points of tariff refund benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Tariff refunds filed April 20 with 60–90 day timing were explicitly excluded from guidance”; Q2 gross margin guidance was 54.1%–54.6%, and consensus diluted EPS was $0.22.

surprises.description: Even excluding the tariff-refund contribution, gross margin rose about 90 basis points year over year on AI-driven markdown recalibration. That contrasts with the preview’s concern about freight and materials headwinds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding roughly 160 basis points of tariff refund benefit, underlying gross margin rose about 90 basis points year-over-year on AI-driven markdown recalibration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Input costs for freight and materials are a headwind.”

surprises.description: Active-customer growth reached 11%, above the preview’s 8% threshold, and the customer base surpassed 3 million with the largest quarterly increase in four years. The scale and pace exceeded the preview’s roughly 2.95–3.00 million expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month active customers accelerated to 11% growth year-over-year, surpassing the 3 million milestone with a 115,000 quarterly increase—the highest quarterly growth in four years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Active customer growth of at least 8%”; estimated TTM active customers were “~2.95M–3.00M.”

surprises.description: International sales grew 16%, above the preview’s roughly 15% watch level, and the Middle East rebounded to strong double-digit growth rather than continuing the slowdown flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International sales grew 16% year-over-year … with the Middle East rebounding to strong double-digit growth despite a weak start.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged a “meaningful Middle East slowdown that began in March and persisted into Q2” and said to watch whether international growth fell “below about 15%.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that 2026 initiatives will consume about two points of adjusted EBITDA margin, including roughly 150 basis points for marketing and 50 basis points for G&A, pressuring near-term profitability. The preview focused on a possible second G&A increase or marketing above 15.8%, but did not describe this investment burden.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is investing approximately two points of adjusted EBITDA margin in 2026 (about 150 bps in marketing and 50 bps in G&A) to seed long-term initiatives, pressuring near-term profitability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a “second raise” in G&A or “marketing above 15.8% of sales” would signal that growth was being bought rather than earned.

surprises.description: The Cardi B Grow Good beauty venture showed unusually strong early demand—selling out its first drops within hours, with repeat purchases near 40%—but inventory constraints limited sales. This was a more specific and stronger demand signal than the preview’s general possibility that GrowGood inventory might land well.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Cardi B Grow Good beauty joint venture sold out within hours across its first drops, achieved a repeat purchase rate approaching 40%, generated 670,000 Instagram followers, and carries gross margins accretive to the business, though inventory constraints limited sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull scenario said “owned-brand and GrowGood inventory land well.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was negative $11 million while inventory increased 25% year over year. The preview did not flag this cash-flow and inventory development, and inventory growth was notably faster than Q2 sales growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was negative $11 million on unfavorable working capital and inventory rose 25% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: The company repurchased nearly 500,000 Class A shares for about $10 million, more than 1% of the Class A stock, a capital-allocation action not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased nearly 500,000 Class A shares at an average price of $19.98 (about $10 million, over 1% of Class A stock).”

in_line: Q2 net sales of $347 million were within the preview’s $342.7 million–$347.0 million consensus range and its $345 million–$350 million base scenario.
Full-year gross margin guidance remained at 53.5%–54.0%, as the preview expected the existing range to be reiterated.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $197 million, above the preview’s $188.4 million consensus, and organic growth was 10% versus the roughly 6% the preview said the Street appeared to expect. In-ground pool sales rose 23% (14% organic), with management attributing most of that growth to volume and share gains.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales grew 14% year-over-year to $197 million, with 10% organic growth”; “In-ground pool sales rose 23% (14% organic)”; about 3 points of in-ground pool growth came from price and the remainder from volume/share gains.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $188.4M (+9.1% Y/Y)” and “the Street appears to embed only about 6% organic growth.”

surprises.description: Rather than narrowing guidance to the lower half of the prior range as the preview considered the base case, management raised its full-year sales-growth midpoint from 9% to 11.7% and adjusted EBITDA-growth midpoint from 12.7% to 15.2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, lifting the midpoint of sales growth to 11.7% from 9% and adjusted EBITDA growth to 15.2% from 12.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A narrowing to the lower half is the base case”; the preview also said a bull case would involve guidance “reaffirmed or narrowed to the upper half.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 35.5%, well below the preview’s 37.1% benchmark. Management attributed about 140 basis points of the 160-basis-point decline to $2.8 million of ramp-up costs after demand outpaced production early in the quarter, and expects to recover most of those costs in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined 160 basis points to 35.5%” due to “approximately $2.8 million (~140 bps) of incremental ramp-up costs”; management expects to recover “the majority” in the second half.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin at or above 37.1%. This would show that cost gains outrun resin and freight.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $40 million, below the preview’s $43–45 million base-case estimate; adjusted EBITDA margin also contracted 50 basis points to 22.6%. The preview did not have a published EBITDA consensus, so the comparison is to its scenario estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 12% to $40 million, but adjusted EBITDA margin contracted 50 basis points to 22.6% from 23.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview base scenario: “Adj. EBITDA | $43–45M.” The preview states these scenario figures “are my estimates … not published guidance.”

surprises.description: Reported diluted EPS was $0.11, below the preview’s $0.17 normalized EPS expectation, although the measures are not directly comparable. Net income fell to $13 million, with management citing an unfavorable $5 million foreign-currency swing that the preview had not identified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income fell to $13 million ($0.11 per diluted share) from $16 million ($0.13) a year ago, hurt by an unfavorable $5 million foreign currency swing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS | $0.17 (normalized).” The preview cautioned that the GAAP-versus-adjusted gap was about $0.02 per share per quarter and said to “check the bridge before treating a GAAP headline as a miss.”

surprises.description: Net leverage was 2.2x, better than the preview’s expected 2.3–2.5x range for Q2, and management expects it to fall below 2x by year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total debt was $280 million with net leverage of 2.2x, expected to fall below 2x by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for leverage moving back toward 2.3–2.5x.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a completed restructuring and early-retirement program with $2.5 million in annualized savings, but also a one-time $1.5 million charge expected in the second half—an unanticipated near-term expense alongside the savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed restructuring and early retirement programs yielding $2.5 million in annualized savings, with an associated one-time $1.5 million charge in the second half.”

surprises.description: Management flagged new vinyl-liner price increases as a partial offset to rising commodity and freight costs. The preview had identified an explicit mid-season price increase as a bull-case signal, though the call facts also describe cost pressure that may limit the benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management flagged rising Middle East-related commodity and freight costs, “partly offset by surcharges and new vinyl liner price increases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A bull case shows an explicit mid-season price increase or positive Q3 order-file color.”

surprises.description: Teradata reported Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $0.69, well above the preview’s $0.55–$0.56 consensus range and $0.57 guidance ceiling. The call attributed the beat primarily to higher recurring revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $0.69, beating the top end of guidance by $0.12, driven primarily by higher recurring revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS | ~$0.55–0.56”; company guide: “$0.53–$0.57.”

surprises.description: Q2 recurring revenue grew 3% year over year, rather than the roughly flat result expected, and exceeded the high end of company guidance by 3 percentage points. Teradata said timing of on-premise revenue recognition contributed to the upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recurring revenue grew 3% year-over-year to $363 million,” which was “3 points above the high end of guidance due to timing of on-premise revenue recognition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A roughly flat y/y print is expected”; company guide: “−2% y/y to flat.”

surprises.description: Cloud ARR growth was materially below the preview’s buy-side bogey: it grew 8% as reported and 9% in constant currency, rather than the 12–13% growth the preview said was needed to sustain the cloud-growth narrative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cloud ARR grew 8% as reported (9% in constant currency), coming in below the low-double-digit cloud growth target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs about +$24–30M sequentially to reach ~$710–716M, which is 12–13% y/y”; the checklist called for “Public cloud ARR at or above $710M with a sequential add of $25M or more.”

surprises.description: Total ARR grew only 1% as reported, or 2% in constant currency. That was weak against the preview’s FY26 growth guide of 2–4% and its Q2 bogey of roughly $1.52–$1.535 billion, although Teradata reaffirmed its full-year ARR outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total ARR grew only 1% as reported (2% in constant currency).” Teradata “reaffirm[ed]” its total ARR outlook.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total ARR growth +2–4%”; “Q2 needs roughly $1.52–1.535B to keep the FY guide credible.”

surprises.description: Teradata raised FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $2.65–$2.73, above the previous $2.55–$2.65 range. The new high end is $0.08 above the prior high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Teradata raised its FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $2.65-$2.73.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS $2.55–2.65”; the preview’s scenarios also described a reaffirmed FY26 outlook as the base case.

surprises.description: Teradata raised its adjusted free cash flow outlook to $330–$350 million, above the prior $320–$340 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[It] increased its adjusted free cash flow range to $330-$350 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted FCF $320–340M, excluding the SAP settlement.”

surprises.description: The Q3 outlook called for recurring revenue to decline 4% to 2% and total revenue to decline 6% to 4% year over year, with management attributing the outlook to revenue recognition shifted into the first half under ASC 606. The preview highlighted Q3 guidance and the first-half pull-forward as key questions but did not anticipate these specific revenue declines.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company guided Q3 recurring revenue to decline 4% to 2% year-over-year and total revenue to decline 6% to 4%, reflecting revenue recognition shifted into the first half under ASC 606.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 guidance and 2H shape” were flagged as a key item to watch; the preview said the key question was whether Q1 upfront revenue was “a pull-forward from 2H or … normal timing.”

in_line: Non-GAAP operating margin was 21.5%, within the preview’s expected Q2 range of 20–22%.
Q3 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $0.55–$0.59 included the preview’s cited Q3 consensus of about $0.58.
Teradata reaffirmed its FY26 total ARR, total revenue, and recurring revenue outlooks, consistent with the preview’s base case of a reaffirmed FY26 outlook.

The company maintained its policy of using 50% of adjusted free cash flow for buybacks, consistent with the preview’s stated policy. The preview also said settlement cash would go to deleveraging first; the call reported that Teradata paid off the remaining $450 million term loan.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $12.12, slightly below the preview’s $12.20 consensus. GAAP EPS was higher at $12.66 and rose 71% year over year, but the call attributed part of that growth to a $23 million contingent loss in the prior-year quarter that did not recur.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income was $12.12 per diluted share”; “GAAP net income reached $12.66 per diluted share in Q2 2026, up 71% year-over-year,” partly because “a $23 million contingent loss in the prior year” did not recur.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 EPS” consensus: “$12.20” (read as adjusted EPS).

surprises.description: The loan-portfolio cash-flow forecast declined 0.3%, a larger revision than the preview’s base case of revisions near Q1’s 0.1% decline. The outcome was within the preview’s warned-about downside range, but worse than the base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Forecasted net cash flows from the loan portfolio declined $39.1 million (0.3%) in the quarter,” versus “$9 million” last quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “Revisions near Q1 level”; the preview also warned that a return to “the −0.3% to −0.5% revisions of 2024–25” could remove much of the EPS bar.

surprises.description: The provision forecast change was much larger than the decline in undiscounted cash flows: $82 million versus $39 million. The call attributed the roughly $43 million gap mainly to prepayments continuing to arrive more slowly than forecast, a detail the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The provision forecast change was $82 million versus a $39 million undiscounted cash flow decline,” with the “roughly $43 million gap driven mainly by prepayments continuing to come in slower than forecast for several consecutive quarters.”

surprises.description: Market share in the first two months of the quarter was 4.9%, above the preview’s cited 4.5% level for January–February 2026, indicating a recovery beyond the preview’s stated share figure. It remained below the year-ago level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core segment market share ... was 4.9% for the first two months of the quarter,” down from 5.3% a year ago.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Market share fell to 4.5% (Jan–Feb 2026) from 5.2% a year earlier.”

surprises.description: Although the quarter’s 1% year-over-year volume decline was close to the preview’s expectation of moderation toward flat, volume turned positive in June and rose more than 20% in July. That late-quarter acceleration went beyond the preview’s near-flat framing, though July benefited from soft comparisons.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consumer Loan assignment unit volume declined only 1% year-over-year in Q2,” with “monthly volume turning positive in June and up over 20% in July (aided by soft comparisons).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether “the volume decline keeps moderating toward flat” and its base scenario anticipated “volume stable.”

surprises.description: The 2025 loan vintage modestly underperformed during the quarter rather than simply holding steady as the preview’s key issue framed it, although it remained within 10 basis points of its initial forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 2025 loan vintage experienced modest underperformance during the quarter but remains within 10 basis points of its initial forecast.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “check whether the 2025 and 2026 vintages held.”

surprises.description: The call described an AI-enabled transformation and a management team increasingly made up of professionals from outside auto lending. The preview noted leadership departures and the CFO handover, but did not flag this broader change in management composition or strategy.
surprises.fact_evidence: The management team is “increasingly composed of non-auto-lending professionals focused on an AI-enabled transformation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “CFO Joe Billante takes over” and that “Board and executive departures followed in July.”

in_line: Consumer Loan assignment volume declined 1% year over year, broadly matching the preview’s expectation that the decline would moderate toward flat.

surprises.description: The preview put Q2 revenue consensus at $49.9 million; Amwell reported $52 million, about 4% above consensus and at the top of its prior $48–$52 million guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue was $52 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $49.9M” consensus; company guidance was “$48–52M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected an adjusted EBITDA loss of about $3 million, but Amwell’s loss was about $1 million. This was a substantially better result than the consensus and guidance midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to approximately $1 million, the closest to break-even in company history.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~−$3M (guide midpoint)” and company guidance of “−$4M to −$2M.”

surprises.description: The preview described the DHA contract as unconfirmed and treated silence after the expected July timing as a negative signal. Instead, DHA issued an intent to award Amwell a sole-source direct contract, although negotiations remain ongoing and the transition is still ahead.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Defense Health Agency issued an intent to award a sole-source direct contract to Amwell”; negotiations are ongoing, with “a targeted transition in the coming months” and a “drop-dead deadline of July 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “I found no public Amwell announcement confirming a new direct contract” and “Silence on a deadline that has passed is a negative signal.”

surprises.description: Amwell raised the low end of its full-year revenue outlook by $5 million, while leaving the high end unchanged. The preview said a second consecutive raise would be a clear positive and warned that a cut toward $195 million would confirm the bear case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised the low end of full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $200 million-$205 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY2026 revenue guidance was “$195–205M”; “A second consecutive raise would be a clear positive,” while “A cut toward $195M would confirm the bear case.”

surprises.description: Subscription revenue came in above the preview’s $24.5 million marker for a potentially bottoming trajectory and rose sequentially. However, the preview also looked for improving churn commentary, which the provided call facts do not report.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subscription revenue at $25.7 million” and “up 3.2% sequentially,” though down 36.5% year over year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A sequential print at or above about $24.5M with improving churn commentary would suggest the reset is bottoming.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted cash burn and the risk of burn re-accelerating, but Amwell ended the quarter with more cash and marketable securities than its Q1 balance and no debt.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $196 million in cash and marketable securities and zero debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported Q1 cash and investments of “$179M” and “about $4M debt,” and warned that burn “re-accelerating above about $8–10M would weigh on the stock.”

surprises.description: Management gave a new target of returning to mid-teens revenue growth in 2027, contingent on closing government pipeline contracts; the preview discussed the government pipeline but did not set out this growth target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management targets a return to double-digit (mid-teens) revenue growth in 2027 contingent on closing government pipeline contracts.”

surprises.description: Management also projected roughly 1,000 basis points of gross-margin improvement by Q4 2027, attributing it to a shift toward subscription revenue. The preview did not set out a margin outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin was 53%” and management projected “roughly 1,000 basis points of margin improvement by Q4 2027 driven by subscription mix shift.”

surprises.description: Management newly said it plans to divest non-core assets and consolidate around a single platform. The preview noted past divestitures but did not flag another planned portfolio and platform consolidation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is “planning to divest non-core assets and consolidate around a single platform.”

in_line: Q3 revenue guidance of $46–$48 million is within the preview’s implied H2 run rate of about $45–$50 million per quarter.
Management reiterated positive operating cash flow in Q4 2026, as the preview identified that target as central to the thesis.

surprises.description: BuzzFeed’s revenue fell 21.8% year over year, a steeper drop than the preview’s base case of a decline roughly in line with Q1’s 12.4% fall. The preview noted there was no published Q2 revenue consensus, so this was a miss against its stated scenario rather than a consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue fell 21.8% year-over-year to $36.3 million from $46.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: Roughly flat y/y decline, in line with Q1 trend.” The preview reported Q1 revenue was “down 12.4% y/y.”

surprises.description: The restructuring was more specific and extensive than the preview’s general expectation of cost actions: BuzzFeed cut about 35% of company-wide headcount and expects roughly $30 million in annualized savings, with $6.5–$8.5 million in one-time costs. It also cited roughly $5 million of lease savings through 2029 and other expense controls.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BuzzFeed reduced headcount by approximately 35% across the entire company, expected to yield roughly $30 million in annualized savings at a one-time cost of $6.5–$8.5 million”; additional measures include “terminating a UK office lease (about $5 million in savings through 2029), reduced professional fees, hiring freezes, and strict travel limits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for Allen’s “cost actions,” but did not specify a reduction of this scale or the associated savings and costs.

surprises.description: Time spent, which BuzzFeed identified as its primary engagement metric, declined year over year. The preview did not flag this metric or signal an expected decline, though the metric did improve sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Time spent, the primary engagement metric, declined 11% year-over-year to 62.3 million hours in Q2 2026, though it rose 1.7 million hours sequentially from Q1.”

surprises.description: Content revenue reversed from the growth that the preview had highlighted as a potential bright spot: the preview noted content was the only growing line in Q1, up 69% year over year, but Q2 content revenue declined by $700,000. The preview did not give a Q2 content forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue declines included “content ($700K).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described content as “the only growing line (+69% y/y in Q1).”

surprises.description: BuzzFeed announced a new sales representation arrangement with Allen Media Group to pursue advertising across premium TV, streaming, and local broadcast. The preview discussed possible integration with Allen Media interests but did not anticipate this specific agreement or its reach into those channels.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BuzzFeed entered a sales representation agreement with Allen Media Group to expand ad monetization across premium TV, streaming, and local broadcast, while retaining full control over pricing, packaging, and inventory.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “integration with Allen Media interests” as an item to watch, without specifying a sales representation agreement.

surprises.description: Management described an ambition to turn BuzzFeed into a free streaming service and a “super app,” a more specific strategic direction than the preview’s discussion of Allen’s strategic plan, asset sales, and the BuzzFeed AI unit.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company is “aiming to become a free streaming service and ‘super app.’”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “Allen’s strategic plan,” including “integration with Allen Media interests, cost actions, asset sales, and the mandate for the BuzzFeed AI unit.”

in_line: BuzzFeed continued to withhold quarterly guidance during its transformation, consistent with the preview’s note that guidance had been withdrawn and its base case of “liquidity update without new framework.”

The Allen investment and leadership transition were not new surprises: the preview said the investment had closed and Byron Allen had become Chairman and CEO, with Jonah Peretti moving to lead BuzzFeed AI.

The preview anticipated that proceeds would partly pay down debt. The company reported a $20 million term-loan paydown, leaving $25 million of principal, about $5 million of net debt, and expected annual interest savings of more than $2 million.

surprises.description: BlackLine reported a 23.3% non-GAAP operating margin, above the preview’s roughly 22% consensus and above the company’s 21.5%–22.5% guidance range. The margin beat was substantially larger than the small revenue beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 23.3% from 22.1% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin” guidance of “21.5%–22.5%”; Street consensus “~22%.”

surprises.description: ARR grew only 6% (about 7% excluding FX), and reached $719 million, below the preview’s $725–735 million and 9%+ growth marker. That left ARR growth well short of the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ARR grew 6% (approximately 7% excluding a 1-point FX headwind) to $719 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ARR of $725–735M (9%+ growth) keeps the story intact.”

surprises.description: Net revenue retention was 102.4%, or about 104% after normalizing for FX, below the preview’s 106%+ marker and down from the 105% reported in Q1. Management linked the pressure to lower user adds under unlimited-user platform pricing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Dollar-based net revenue retention was 102.4% (about 104% normalizing for FX), pressured by lower user adds from the shift to unlimited-user platform pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NRR of 106%+ would suggest platform pricing is expanding wallet share.”

surprises.description: The company kept its full-year revenue guidance at $765–769 million rather than making the modest increase anticipated in the preview’s base case, despite Q2 revenue above consensus. The range was maintained despite an incremental FX headwind of about $1 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was maintained at $765-769 million (9.2%-9.8% growth) despite an incremental ~$1 million FX headwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario anticipated “guide nudged up by the beat”; the preview also listed company guidance of “$765–769M” and consensus of “~$766.8M.”

surprises.description: About $8 million of deals expected to close in Q2 slipped beyond quarter-end as mega-enterprise sales cycles lengthened by roughly 40–45 days. Half had closed by the call, so the reported issue was delayed timing rather than all of those deals being lost.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately $8 million of deals expected to close in Q2 slipped past quarter-end, of which half had already closed by the earnings call, driven by elongated mega-enterprise sales cycles extended by roughly 40-45 days.”

surprises.description: Verity Prepare had already contributed more than $20 million of platform ACV, and Verity accounted for most platform upsell interest; its customer count nearly quadrupled quarter over quarter. The preview highlighted pricing and attach as open questions but did not anticipate this level of disclosed commercial traction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Verity Prepare has contributed to more than $20 million of platform ACV to date, with over 80% of platform upsell interest tied to the Verity suite, and Verity customer count grew nearly fourfold quarter-over-quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Verity Prepare” was flagged for “Pricing model and attach rate”; the preview said Q1 had “strong adoption growth but no disclosed revenue.”

surprises.description: Management said platform conversion and Agentic adoption should add at least 2 points of incremental revenue growth next year, with growth exiting 2026 at double digits and accelerating further in 2027. The preview focused on near-term platform conversion milestones but did not lay out this forward growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects platform conversion and Agentic adoption to add at least 2 points of incremental revenue growth next year, supporting an exit from 2026 at double-digit growth with further acceleration in 2027.”

surprises.description: BlackLine disclosed broad AI adoption: about 90% of eligible customers were AI-enabled, 77% were actively using AI, and feature actions rose more than 220% sequentially. The preview discussed the AI-repricing narrative but did not anticipate these adoption and usage figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly 90% of eligible customers (about 3,500) are AI-enabled and 77% (about 3,000) are actively using AI, with feature usage reaching nearly 13 million actions in the quarter, up over 220% sequentially.”

surprises.description: BlackLine repurchased $38 million of shares and increased its authorization by another $100 million, leaving about $280 million of capacity and earmarking roughly all free cash flow for repurchases. The preview did not flag this level of capital return.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BlackLine generated $36.5 million of free cash flow, repurchased 1.2 million shares for $38 million, and the Board approved an additional $100 million buyback increase, bringing total remaining capacity to approximately $280 million, with ~100% of free cash flow earmarked for repurchases.”

surprises.description: The company reported unusually large average deal sizes and a greater share of multiyear commitments, strengthening the mix behind its backlog. The preview tracked RPO and cRPO growth but did not anticipate these specific deal-size and renewal-book figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RPO grew 17% to over $1.1 billion and current RPO grew 11%, both outpacing revenue and ARR growth, driven by 24% larger average deal sizes and multiyear commitments rising to 56% of the renewal book from 45% a year ago.”

surprises.description: BlackLine named large post-quarter customer wins, including Vodafone, Royal Dutch Shell, and two of the six largest U.S. banks. The preview highlighted customer losses as a concern but did not anticipate these specific wins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New customer wins including Vodafone, Royal Dutch Shell, and two of the top six largest U.S. banks signed post-quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Customer count” and said “Another decline of about 100 would contradict” management’s expectation that churn would diminish.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $187.8 million slightly exceeded the preview’s consensus range of roughly $187.0–187.6 million, while remaining within company guidance. This was a small beat rather than the larger revenue outcome in the preview’s bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 9.2% to $187.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Street consensus was “~$187.0–187.6M”; company guidance was “$186.0–188.0M.”

in_line: Platform ARR reached over 17% of eligible ARR, matching the preview’s roughly 17%–19% expected Q2 path and tracking toward the 25% full-year target.
RPO and current RPO grew 17% and 11%, respectively, close to the prior quarter’s 18% and 12%; the RPO-to-current-RPO growth gap did not widen.

surprises.description: Bio-Rad reported Q2 revenue of about $651 million, above the preview’s $624–630 million consensus range and the roughly $622 million sequential steer; revenue was up 10% sequentially rather than the expected ~5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was approximately $651 million” and “rising 10% sequentially from Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue ~$624–630M”; management’s sequential steer was “a ~5% sequential lift” to “about $622M.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $2.62, above the preview’s $2.46 estimate and essentially unchanged year over year, rather than the roughly 6% decline implied by consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $2.62 versus $2.61 in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS ~$2.46” and “~ -6%” year over year.

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating margin reached 12.5%, well above the preview’s estimated 10–11% and above the roughly 12.3% Q2–Q4 average the preview said was needed to reach the FY margin midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin was 12.5%,” up from 6.6% in Q1.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op margin ~10–11% (est.)”; the preview said Q2–Q4 needed to “average about 12.3%” to hit the 11% midpoint.

surprises.description: Clinical Diagnostics grew 8.3% currency-neutral, returning to growth and materially exceeding the segment’s previewed full-year range of -3% to +1%; the preview’s bull case only anticipated a return to roughly flat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Clinical Diagnostics segment returned to growth” and was “up 8.3% currency-neutral.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed segment guidance of “Clinical Diagnostics -3% to +1%” and described the bull case as “Clinical Diagnostics CN returns to roughly flat.”

surprises.description: Life Science sales fell 5.1% currency-neutral, worse than the previewed full-year segment guidance range of -3% to -1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Life Science sales fell to $252 million, down 5.1% currency-neutral.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed segment guidance of “Life Science -3% to -1%.”

surprises.description: Bio-Rad announced a restructuring with $30–35 million in annualized net savings and roughly 40–50 basis points of incremental operating-margin expansion in 2027, but also expects about $90 million in one-time costs. The preview flagged a possible named cost program, but did not anticipate these quantified benefits and costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: The restructuring is “expected to deliver $30-$35 million in annualized net cost savings” and “roughly 40-50 bps of operating margin expansion in 2027,” with “a ~$90 million one-time cost.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “Watch for a named cost or restructuring program” and identified a “cost program named” as a bull-case driver.

surprises.description: China declined in the high teens and is expected to create a further $4 million headwind for the rest of 2026, an additional regional drag not identified in the preview’s discussion of Middle East and blood-typing headwinds.
surprises.fact_evidence: China, “representing about 6% of total revenue, declined in the high teens” and created “an estimated $4 million headwind for the remainder of the year.”

surprises.description: Digital PCR instruments grew more than 20%, but total ddPCR revenue grew only 6% currency-neutral because consumables declined slightly and pull-through remained below expectations. The preview had highlighted Stilla accretion as a checkpoint but did not flag weak consumables pull-through.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Digital PCR (ddPCR) revenue grew 6% currency-neutral with instrument revenue up more than 20%, though consumables revenue declined slightly year-over-year with pull-through still below expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Stilla accretion by midyear is the checkpoint for digital PCR” and noted Q1 digital PCR instrument revenue was “+24%.”

surprises.description: Bio-Rad reported repurchasing about 110,000 shares for roughly $32 million, an actual capital-return action beyond the preview’s discussion of capital allocation as a possible catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased approximately 110,000 shares for about $32 million at an average price of $281.57,” with “roughly $206 million remaining under Board authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Any strategic review, monetization step, or capital-return plan announced on the call would dominate the reaction.”

surprises.description: Management confirmed active, constructive engagement with Elliott and cited broad alignment on execution, capital allocation, and closing the gap between value and share price. It reiterated that the Sartorius stake can be monetized at the right time and price, but announced no specific monetization step.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management confirmed “active, constructive engagement with activist investor Elliott Management,” citing “broad alignment” and reiterating “the Sartorius stake is monetizable at the right time and price.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified Elliott and Sartorius as a key debate and said a “strategic review, monetization step, or capital-return plan” would be consequential.

in_line: Management reaffirmed the FY2026 currency-neutral revenue growth guidance of -3% to +0.5% and non-GAAP operating-margin guidance of 10%–12%, matching the preview’s stated guidance and its expectation that reaffirmation was the minimum acceptable outcome.
The reaffirmed FY2026 non-GAAP gross-margin guidance of 53%–54% was in line with the preview’s stated range.

surprises.description: Compass reported Q2 revenue of $4.3 billion, above both the $4.0–$4.2 billion company range and the preview’s roughly $4.06–$4.11 billion consensus. Pro forma year-over-year growth was 14.3%, well above the preview’s +4–6% organic-growth base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached a record $4.3 billion, up 14.3% year-over-year on a pro forma basis and exceeding the high end of guidance of $4.0-$4.2 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $4.06–4.11B”; “Q2 organic revenue growth of +4–6% is a reasonable base case.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $363 million, above the preview’s $310–$350 million guidance range and the roughly $330 million midpoint; it also exceeded the preview’s $340–$350 million buy-side whisper.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA hit a record $363 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$330M (guide midpoint) | $310–350M”; “buy-side whisper sits above the printed consensus, at roughly ... $340–350M adj. EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was far stronger than the preview’s near-breakeven expectation, adding $210 million to cash during the quarter. The preview said Q2 near-breakeven had been pre-announced and emphasized the full-year positive-FCF outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash on hand rose $210 million quarter-over-quarter to $694 million, driven by $180 million of free cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow | ~breakeven”; “close to breakeven or slightly negative” (CFO); “Q2 near-breakeven was pre-announced.”

surprises.description: Brokerage GTV grew 16% against a 6% market, widening Compass’s outperformance to about 1,000 basis points from roughly 600 basis points in Q1. The preview highlighted share gains as a key debate but cited narrower Q1 outperformance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Brokerage GTV grew ~16% year-over-year versus a market up 6%, reflecting roughly 1,000 basis points of outperformance, an acceleration from ~600 basis points in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Organic GTV and transactions vs. market”; “Q1 GTV grew +7.3% against a market at +1.5%.”

surprises.description: Net debt to adjusted EBITDA fell to 3.3x from 4.2x in Q1, with management expecting it to reach the 2s by year-end. The preview flagged leverage and cash generation as important but gave no comparable near-term leverage target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt to adjusted EBITDA improved by roughly one turn quarter-over-quarter to 3.3x from 4.2x in Q1, with management expecting the ratio to reach the 2s by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow and leverage. Q2 near-breakeven was pre-announced, so the FY reiteration matters more than the quarter.”

surprises.description: Compass completed its $300 million year-1 cost-synergy action target five months early and now expects to action $330 million in 2026, with about $150 million realized through the P&L. The preview anticipated another synergy increase, so the increase itself was expected; the early completion and realization detail add upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Compass actioned its entire $300 million year-1 cost synergy target five months ahead of plan and now expects to action $330 million in 2026, with ~$150 million realized through the P&L.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A third raise is the highest-probability upside catalyst”; “A reiteration alone is neutral to negative given positioning.”

surprises.description: Management described unusually strong Bay Area results after the quarter: Compass standalone-brand revenue there rose 19% in both July and August, and 140 San Francisco homes closed at least $1 million above asking in H1 versus eight a year earlier. The preview did not anticipate this specific strength.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bay Area revenue in the Compass standalone brand rose 19% year-over-year in both July and August, supported by AI-driven wealth effects, with 140 San Francisco homes closing $1M+ above asking in H1 versus just eight a year ago.”

surprises.description: Management presented a scenario in which adjusted EBITDA reaches $1 billion even with home sales flat at 4.1 million, and $2.5 billion at 6 million sales, while $1.8 billion of NOLs could shield roughly $470 million of future cash taxes. The preview referenced the $1 billion run-rate narrative but not the larger upside case or tax shield.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The scenario analysis projects $1 billion in adjusted EBITDA at a flat 4.1 million home sales market, scaling to $2.5 billion at 6 million home sales, with $1.8 billion of NOLs shielding roughly $470 million of future cash taxes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A miss at the low end would weaken the $1B run-rate EBITDA narrative.”

in_line: The preview anticipated a further synergy increase as a likely catalyst; Compass did raise its 2026 action target, from the previously stated $300 million to $330 million.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $158,000, well above the preview’s roughly $75,000 consensus estimate and above the $50,000–$100,000 company range. The preview said a result below $50,000 would be a real negative surprise, but the reported figure instead exceeded the top of the range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was only $158,000, consisting primarily of wafer delivery fees to Atomera's large IDM customer.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$75K (company guide $50K–$100K)” and “A print below $50K would be a real negative surprise.”

surprises.description: Atomera reported clearing a significant manufacturability milestone with one of its two active GAA customers, advancing that customer toward possible license negotiations. The preview expected customer-wafer results around Q3 or Q4, while the call described a milestone that could lead to negotiations as early as late 2026, though additional tests could push that by about nine months.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Atomera cleared a significant manufacturability milestone with one of two active gate-all-around customers,” with license negotiations potentially beginning “as early as late 2026” or slipping “roughly 9 months if additional test rounds are required.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Two customers are at stage 3 of 4, running MST on customer-supplied wafers” and the timeline “points to Q3 or Q4 2026.”

surprises.description: Atomera reported opening a NAND flash opportunity that management said could more than double MST’s total addressable market. The preview did not identify NAND as an opportunity to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company opened an entirely new market opportunity in NAND flash memory,” which could “more than double MST's total addressable market since NAND ships more wafers annually than DRAM.”

surprises.description: The call reported a major GaN-on-silicon RF performance result and said the technology could support power amplifiers and fully integrated RF front ends, extending the potential market. The preview discussed GaN commercialization but did not anticipate these specific performance results or the power-amplifier application.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GaN-on-silicon RF breakthrough delivered linearity roughly 1,000x better than the GaN-on-silicon reference at benchmark drive level, with 2-3 orders of magnitude improvement across the full power range”; the results can support “power amplifiers,” “fully integrated RF front ends,” and potentially expand TAM into the “power-amp market.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a June 4 release claimed “a more than 10x reduction in parasitic channel charge” and urged investors to “watch for a named partner or a revenue model with timing.”

surprises.description: Atomera described a new 4F2 DRAM value proposition in response to AI-driven demand for vertical architectures, validated with multiple customers and accepted for an IEEE conference. The preview did not discuss this DRAM approach.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI-driven demand pushed manufacturers toward vertical/3D architectures,” prompting Atomera to establish a “new 4F2 DRAM value proposition validated with multiple customers and accepted for an IEEE conference in September.”

surprises.description: The quarter-end cash balance came in above the preview’s expected $36–$37 million, despite $3.9 million of cash used in operations during Q2. That is a modestly better cash position than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash, equivalents and short-term investments declined to $38.4 million as of June 30, 2026, from $41.1 million at March 31, with $3.9 million of cash used in operations during Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “About $36–37M is expected at the end of Q2.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year 2026 non-GAAP operating expense guidance to the high end of the $18.25–$18.75 million range, rather than reaffirming the preview’s $18.5 million expectation. The increase is modest, but it is a higher cost outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its full-year 2026 non-GAAP operating expense guidance to the high end of its $18.25-$18.75 million range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP opex | $18.5M FY26, reaffirmed” and “FY26 non-GAAP opex of $18.5M.”

surprises.description: Management warned of significant structural cost increases from equipment leases, metrology, and fabrication that will weigh more heavily in 2027. The preview discussed 2026 expense guidance and cash burn but did not flag this specific future cost pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “warned of significant structural cost increases from tool leases, metrology and fabrication that will hit more heavily in 2027.”

surprises.description: Atomera said it did not win the PowerAmerica GaN power program, a new negative outcome not mentioned in the preview. The call put the program’s value at about $300,000.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Atomera did not win the PowerAmerica GaN power program (worth only ~$300,000).”

surprises.description: The call provided no new information on STMicroelectronics, leaving the possible re-engagement discussed in May unconfirmed. The preview had specifically highlighted ST re-engagement as an issue to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “No new updates on its STMicroelectronics relationship.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “STMicroelectronics re-engagement” and noted that management had “recently got some results” suggesting re-engagement.

in_line: The non-GAAP loss of $5 million was broadly consistent with the preview’s non-GAAP EPS estimate of –$0.13, rather than a material earnings surprise.
No ATM sales occurred during the quarter, consistent with the preview’s focus on ATM issuance as a dilution risk rather than an expected source of financing.

surprises.description: Wynn Al Marjan Island’s opening moved to September 2027, roughly nine months later than the Q1 2027 opening cited in the preview. That is a larger delay than the preview’s base case of a modest delay while remaining in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The opening was pushed to September 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Al Marjan Island (UAE) opening guided to Q1 2027”; the base case expected a “modest delay, still 2027.”

surprises.description: Al Marjan’s project budget increased by about $600 million, with about half attributed to regional conflict disruptions. Wynn also expects another $140 million of equity for its 40% share, while remaining project equity including Enclave is guided at approximately $525 million to $650 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wynn Al Marjan Island's total project budget was increased by approximately $600 million,” with “about half attributed to regional conflict disruptions,” requiring “an additional $140 million of equity for Wynn's 40% share.” Remaining project equity, including Enclave, is “approximately $525 million to $650 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “~$3.9B investment” and identified “a budget increase” as an under-priced risk.

surprises.description: Macau adjusted property EBITDA was $297 million, substantially above the preview’s roughly flat year-over-year base case and the cited $254 million prior-year figure. This came despite unfavorable VIP hold, while mass drop increased 5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Macau generated $297 million of adjusted property EBITDA on $1 billion of revenue at a 29.6% margin,” with unfavorable VIP hold reducing results by “over $8.6 million” and mass drop “up 5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview watched Macau EBITDAR “vs. $254M prior year” and described the base case as “Macau roughly flat y/y.”

surprises.description: Las Vegas adjusted property EBITDA of $215.2 million came in below the preview’s $225–235 million base-case range and the cited $235 million Q2 record. Unfavorable hold cost just over $3.6 million, although casino revenues rose 5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wynn Las Vegas delivered $215.2 million of adjusted property EBITDA on $643.2 million of revenue at a 33.5% margin,” with “unfavorable hold costing just over $3.6 million and casino revenues up 5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “Las Vegas about $225–235M”; it also flagged results against “the $235M Q2 record.”

surprises.description: Macau’s 2026 expansionary CapEx outlook was lowered to $350–400 million from the preview’s $400–450 million guidance, even as the outlook includes the Enclave hotel tower and the newly approved Wynn Palace Event Center and theater.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total 2026 expansionary CapEx in Macau is now expected to land in the $350 million to $400 million range,” tied to “the Enclave hotel tower and the newly approved Wynn Palace Event Center and theater.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$400–450M Macau” in 2026 project CapEx guidance.

surprises.description: Encore Boston Harbor’s EBITDA and margin improved from the weak Q1 level the preview highlighted: EBITDA was $56.1 million and margin was 26.8%, versus Q1’s $50.5 million and 24.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Encore Boston Harbor generated $56.1 million of adjusted property EBITDA on $209.3 million of revenue at a 26.8% margin,” while OpEx per day was “up only 2.9% despite labor pressure.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “Q1 margin fell to 24.6% from 29.6% a year earlier” and that Boston “has produced small misses.”

surprises.description: Shareholder returns remained active during the heavy-capex period: Wynn repurchased $75 million of shares in the quarter, and Wynn Macau raised its final dividend to $150 million from $124 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company maintained a “$0.25 per share Wynn Resorts dividend,” raised the Wynn Macau final dividend “to $150 million from $124 million,” and made “$75 million in share repurchases during the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said an “accelerated buyback would signal confidence” amid heavy capex, while “a leverage-preservation message would reinforce the bear case.”

surprises.description: Management reported unusually low Las Vegas hold in July, adding a near-term gaming-results concern, although drop volumes and RevPAR grew. The company deferred details until the next call.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported unusually low hold in Las Vegas during July, though drop volumes and RevPAR grew, with specifics deferred to the next call.”

surprises.description: Macau trading started Q3 slightly weaker year over year, with rolling volumes and mass drop down early in the quarter, before improving in late July and early August. The preview did not flag this specific mixed near-term pattern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Macau rolling volumes and mass drop were down slightly year-over-year in early Q3 due to the World Cup and seasonality, but improved in late July and continued into early August.”

surprises.description: The preview put Q1 revenue at $180–185 million of guidance and about $182–186 million of consensus. 8x8 reported $190.2 million of total revenue and $185.3 million of service revenue, exceeding the top of the respective guidance ranges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 total revenue was $190.2 million” and “service revenue was a record $185.3 million,” both “exceeding guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Company guidance (Q1) $180M–$185M | Consensus ~$182.3M … or ~$186.0M”; “Service revenue | $175M–$180M.”

surprises.description: The preview listed FY2027 revenue guidance of $727–747 million and highlighted any change as a key issue. 8x8 raised service revenue guidance by $18 million and total revenue guidance to $745–765 million, but left operating income and EPS guidance roughly unchanged, so the higher sales outlook did not come with a higher profit outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year service revenue guidance by $18 million to $725-$745 million and total revenue to $745-$765 million, while holding operating income at roughly $70 million and EPS at $0.33-$0.38.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2027 (full year): Guidance revenue $727M–$747M”; the preview also says “Any change is likely the biggest swing factor” and lists FY EPS guidance of “$0.33–$0.38.”

surprises.description: The preview gave Q1 gross margin guidance of 63.5–64.5% and flagged margin trajectory as a key debate. Gross margin instead fell to 61.6%, below the guidance floor, and 8x8 set FY gross margin guidance at 60.5–61.5% as lower-margin usage offerings grew.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 61.6% due to mix shift toward lower-margin usage-based offerings, and full-year gross margin guidance was set at 60.5% to 61.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin | 63.5%–64.5%”; the preview also flags “Forward guidance and margins” and says usage mix affects gross margin.

surprises.description: Q1 operating performance was stronger than the preview’s margin range suggested: operating margin reached 9.9%, above the 8.5–9.5% guidance range, and operating income was above the high end of guidance. Operating expenses fell by more than $8 million year over year, mostly in sales and marketing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating income reached $18.9 million (9.9% margin) above the high end of guidance, aided by operating expenses falling more than $8 million YoY, mostly in sales and marketing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin | 8.5%–9.5%.”

surprises.description: The preview cited Q1 EPS consensus of about $0.07. Fully diluted EPS came in at $0.09, the high end of company guidance, exceeding that consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income was $13.6 million with fully diluted EPS of $0.09, at the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS (diluted) … Consensus … ~$0.07.”

surprises.description: Operating cash flow was expected to be $10–12 million, but reached $17 million, substantially above the top of that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow of $17 million significantly beat guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash flow from operations | $10M–$12M.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted rapid usage growth but gave no forecast for the next quarter’s pace. 8x8 guided to platform usage growth slowing to 30–35% in Q2 from 63% in Q1, a sharp deceleration despite the tougher comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 guidance calls for platform usage growth to slow to 30-35% YoY (from 63%) against a tougher comparison.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag the upcoming debt reclassification or refinancing timeline. 8x8 said its term loan will become a current liability next quarter as it approaches its August 2027 maturity, and management offered confidence in refinancing but no specifics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The term loan (maturing August 2027) will reclassify to current liabilities next quarter, and management expressed confidence in refinancing but offered no specifics.”

surprises.description: The preview anticipated early AI attach commentary but supplied no adoption benchmarks. 8x8 reported AI solution adoption up 121% year over year and rapid AI Studio uptake, with more than 200 organizations and 2,900 agents within 3.5 months of launch and half converting to paying customers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI solution adoption grew 121% YoY, AI Studio surpassed 200 organizations and 2,900 agents within 3.5 months of launch (half converting to paying customers).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AI product monetization. … Early attach commentary could move the stock.”

surprises.description: The preview did not quantify expectations for broader product adoption. 8x8 said customers using three or more products increased 18% year over year, and those customers represented about 38% of recurring revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customers using 3+ products rose 18% YoY to about 38% of recurring revenue.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for Medicare submissions to fall no worse than about 35%; they fell 44%. That was a steeper decline than the preview’s downside warning threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Medicare submissions declined 44%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A submissions drop of 40%+ combined with LTV:CAC slipping would signal demand loss, not discipline”; the checklist also looked for “submissions down no worse than about 35%.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted a goal of LTV:CAC at or above 1.3x, but the call reported Medicare Advantage LTV down 1% and total acquisition cost per MA-equivalent approved member up 16%. The call did not provide LTV:CAC, so these figures point to weaker Medicare unit economics without confirming whether the 1.3x target was missed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Medicare Advantage LTV declined 1%” and “total acquisition cost per MA-equivalent approved member rose 16%,” including a “42% increase in customer care/enrollment cost per member.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for LTV:CAC holding at or above 1.3x.”

surprises.description: The preview noted reduced marketing spend as an AEP-2027 issue, but the company said Q3 marketing spend would be cut even more than the 45% year-over-year reduction in Q2. Management linked that to steeper enrollment and revenue declines, with most of the annual marketing budget shifted to Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 marketing spend will be cut even more than the 45% year-over-year reduction seen in Q2, implying steeper enrollment and revenue declines, with the majority of the annual marketing budget deployed in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “whether the reduced marketing spend from a major MA payor persists” and described H2 revenue as “almost all in Q4/AEP,” but did not anticipate a further Q3 cut beyond Q2’s reduction.

in_line: Q2 revenue was $33.6 million, within the preview’s $33.3–$35.2 million estimate range and close to its roughly $33.9 million mean.
Management reaffirmed FY2026 revenue, GAAP net income, adjusted EBITDA, and operating cash flow guidance, matching the preview’s base expectation of reaffirmation.

The FY2026 net adjustment revenue outlook of $16–$20 million remained within the preview’s cited $8–$20 million range; the reported Q2 tail revenue of $7.6 million had no specific quarterly consensus estimate in the preview.

surprises.description: CRCT reported diluted EPS of $0.19 versus the preview’s $0.04 consensus, but the profit beat was largely driven by one-time tariff refunds and a royalty settlement reserve release. Excluding one-time items, operating income would have been about $23 million rather than the reported $47.4 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income rose to $39.1 million (19 cents per diluted share) … but was significantly boosted by one-time items”; “Excluding one-time items, operating income would have been about $23 million versus the reported $47.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | $0.04”

surprises.description: Revenue was $156.3 million, about $11.5 million below the $167.8 million consensus and below the preview’s base range of $164–168 million. The decline was also much steeper than the consensus-implied year-over-year decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue declined approximately 9% year-over-year to $156.3 million.”

surprises.description: Product revenue fell to $71.3 million, about $8.7 million short of the preview’s roughly $80 million expectation and down 22% year over year. The preview’s base case anticipated a smaller 10–13% decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Product revenue fell 22% year-over-year to $71.3 million due to lower volumes, promotional pricing, and a lower-priced machine mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Products revenue consensus is about $80M”; “Products down 10–13%” in the base scenario.

surprises.description: Despite the product-revenue decline, global cutting-machine sellout and sell-in units both grew double digits. That is a positive counterpoint to the preview’s concern that the new bundle-only transition could stall at retail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global cutting machine sellout units and sell-in units both grew double digits, aided by an earlier Prime Day and the new Joy 2 and Explore 5 bundles.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bear: … Bundle-only transition stalls at retail”; the preview also described Q2 as “the first clean sell-through quarter.”

surprises.description: Paid subscribers reached just over 3.1 million, above the preview’s 3.05–3.08 million range, with 93,000 net additions year over year. Platform revenue growth itself was close to expectations, but subscriber levels were better than the preview’s range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Paid subscribers increasing 93,000 (over 3%) year-over-year to just over 3.1 million”; platform revenue “grew just over 5% to $85 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Paid subscribers vs. about 3.05–3.08M”; base case: “Platform up 5–6%.”

surprises.description: Active users grew 1% year over year and were flat sequentially, with management calling it the first Q2 engagement stabilization since 2022. This was more encouraging than the recent engagement trend highlighted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Active users grew 1% year-over-year and were flat sequentially, marking the first Q2 engagement stabilization since 2022.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 “90-day engaged users 3.35M (-1% YoY)” and flagged “seasonal softness in Q2 and Q3.”

surprises.description: Management said it expects to remain profitable and cash-flow positive in every quarter of 2026, a more specific full-year assurance than the preview’s account of no formal FY26 guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expects to remain profitable and cash-flow positive each quarter of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance: None. Management has not given formal Q2 or FY26 guidance.”

surprises.description: The preview identified a buyback re-authorization or increase as the more likely capital-return lever, but the reported update was $7.5 million of repurchases and $21.6 million left on the existing authorization, with no increase reported. The regular $0.10 semiannual dividend was paid as the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased 1.7 million shares for $7.5 million (leaving $21.6 million of the $50 million authorization), paid a $0.10 semiannual dividend.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A buyback re-authorization or upsize is the more likely capital-return lever”; “A buyback upsize with $29.1M remaining would be the most likely positive surprise.”

in_line: Excluding the $17.9 million tariff refunds and $6.4 million royalty settlement reserve release, gross margin was about 58.9%, broadly in line with the preview’s roughly 57% base case and its expectation of lower margins.
Platform revenue grew just over 5%, in line with the preview’s 5–6% base-case expectation.
The $0.10 semiannual dividend was paid, consistent with the preview’s reference to a $0.10 July 2026 dividend.

surprises.description: The preview said investors should expect a FY26 adjusted EPS midpoint raise of about $0.40 or more, but DaVita simply reconfirmed guidance, leaving the midpoint at $14.65. That was less than the anticipated upgrade.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DaVita reconfirmed full-year 2026 guidance” with “$14.65” for adjusted EPS.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Only a midpoint raise of about $0.40 or more on adj. EPS clears the bar”; the expected revised range was “roughly $14.75 – $15.50.”

surprises.description: Q2 treatment growth reached 56 basis points, above the preview’s Q1 growth reference of 40 basis points and its expectation that growth accelerate as the second Fresenius patient tranche arrived. However, DaVita’s updated full-year range is lower than the 50–75 basis-point range stated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. dialysis treatments grew 56 basis points” versus Q2 2025; full-year treatment growth is now expected “near the top end of its 25-50 basis point range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The FY guide is +50 to +75 bps”; growth not accelerating above Q1’s “+40 bps” would be “a weak signal,” and the remaining Fresenius transfers were expected in Q2.

surprises.description: Patient-care costs were down sequentially, but year-to-date cost growth was already above the stated full-year target range. That points to more cost pressure than the company had expected for the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Patient care cost per treatment declined about $3 sequentially,” though “year-to-date PCCs grew more than 3%” versus the first half of 2025, “above the expected full-year growth range of 1.25%-2.25%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Above the expected full-year growth range of 1.25%-2.25%.”

surprises.description: DaVita disclosed a larger ACA-related commercial-mix headwind for 2027 than for 2026, as new patients enter with lower commercial mix. The preview discussed the 2026 headwind but did not flag the larger following-year amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: The declining commercial mix is expected to create a “$40 million headwind in 2026 and a larger $70 million headwind in 2027,” largely from new patients entering at lower commercial mix.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited an ACA headwind “at about $40M” and said management might change its numbers in Q2.

surprises.description: The proposed 2027 ESRD payment rule again has a base-rate increase below industry cost trends, indicating reimbursement would not keep pace with costs. The preview did not specify this payment-rule expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The proposed 2027 ESRD payment rule again includes a base rate increase that tracks below industry cost trends.”

surprises.description: CMS cut its estimate for phosphate-binder spending by nearly $500 million, an additional policy-related pressure not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CMS has cut its phosphate binder spend estimate by nearly $500 million.”

surprises.description: DaVita secured supply of expanded HD dialyzers, but the financial benefit from improved mortality is not expected to begin until 2028 and will be insignificant near term. The preview did not mention the dialyzers or this delayed financial contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: DaVita “secured supply of FDA-approved Nipro expanded HD dialyzers compatible with existing machines,” but the financial benefit “only begin[s] in 2028 and remain[s] insignificant near-term.”

surprises.description: IKC’s adjusted operating income was above expectations, but management attributed the result to revenue timing, making the beat less indicative of underlying performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “IKC delivered $40 million of adjusted operating income above expectations due to revenue timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Above expectations due to revenue timing.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow came in just above the preview’s approximate level below which the FY range and buyback math would be pressured. The cushion was small.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 free cash flow was “$256 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FCF below about $250M would pressure the range and the buyback math.”

in_line: Adjusted EPS of $4.02 was essentially in line with the preview’s contested consensus range of $3.88 to $4.01, landing just above its upper end.
Adjusted operating income of $579 million was close to the preview’s roughly $573 million implied quarterly bar.
Full-year RPT growth remained expected at 1%-2%, in line with the preview’s stated FY26 RPT guide; the preview had also anticipated an orderly step-down as commercial mix declined.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.84, versus the preview’s $1.09 consensus estimate—a shortfall of $0.25, or about 23%, despite year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income was $19 million ($0.84 per share) in Q2 2026”; adjusted EPS improved 53% over Q2 2025.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $1.09” for Q2 FY26 consensus.

surprises.description: The quarter produced a $29 million GAAP net loss even though adjusted net income was positive. The preview did not give a GAAP estimate; the loss came from $84 million of negative fair-value adjustments, including a $24 million non-cash convertible-note charge tied to an approximately $11 share-price increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported a GAAP net loss of $29 million for the quarter, driven by $84 million in negative fair value adjustments including a $24 million non-cash charge on convertible notes tied to an ~$11 per share stock price increase.”

surprises.description: Management gave a more specific return outlook for the Onity portfolio than the preview had: the roughly $70 million book-value asset is expected to earn a mid-teens yield, with the contribution flowing through the P&L in the second half of 2026. The preview expected little Q2 contribution and was looking for quantified post-close accretion, but did not state a yield expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Completed the acquisition of a $5.2 billion HECM MSR portfolio from Onity,” with “a book value of roughly $70 million expected to earn a mid-teens yield flowing through the P&L in the second half of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 should show almost no P&L contribution but a larger servicing book and a cash outflow”; the preview also asked for “Onity accretion and cash used.”

surprises.description: A $42 million non-cash deferred-tax-asset valuation-allowance release boosted results, and management said the effective tax rate should be more normalized going forward. The preview did not anticipate this one-off benefit or the tax-rate outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $42 million non-cash tax benefit from releasing the deferred tax asset valuation allowance boosted results,” with “a more normalized effective tax rate going forward.”

surprises.description: The retail channel showed substantial productivity gains: funded loans rose 33%, submissions rose 19%, and loans funded per call-center loan officer increased nearly 30% sequentially with sales capacity stable. The preview expected a step-up in overall fundings but did not anticipate these retail operating-leverage metrics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retail channel showed strong operating leverage with funded loans up 33%, submissions up 19%, and funded loans per call center loan officer increasing nearly 30% sequentially on stable sales capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Submissions lead fundings by about a quarter, so Q2 should step up.”

surprises.description: FOA disclosed $58 million of cash generated from originations and capital-markets activities in Q2 and approximately $116 million for the first half; the preview did not set an expectation for this cash-generation measure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company generated $58 million in cash from originations and capital markets activities in Q2 and approximately $116 million in the first half of 2026.”

surprises.description: Management identified retiring the remaining $150 million of senior secured notes in November as its primary capital priority, with buybacks, dividends, or further deleveraging only afterward. The preview did not discuss this capital-allocation order.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management's primary capital priority is retiring the remaining $150 million of senior secured notes this November, with buybacks, dividends, or further deleveraging considered only afterward.”

surprises.description: Management reported $326 million of HECM MSR adjusted net asset value supported by only $46 million of financing, or roughly 14% leverage, and said it intends to increase that financing to unlock flexibility. The preview did not address the portfolio’s leverage level or plans to increase it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The HECM MSR adjusted net asset value totaled $326 million as of June 30 with only $46 million of financing (roughly 14% leverage), which management intends to increase to unlock financial flexibility.”

in_line: Reverse mortgage funded volume was $730 million, within the preview’s roughly $700–760 million expected range and close to the approximately $735 million quarterly run rate cited as needed for the full-year volume guide.
The company reaffirmed full-year funded-volume guidance of $2.8–$3.1 billion and adjusted-EPS guidance of $4.50–$5.00, as the preview’s base scenario expected.
The Onity acquisition had closed by quarter-end, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the deal closed on June 30.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $458.8 million, well above both the $400–410 million company guide and the roughly $412 million consensus the preview highlighted. The result also came despite the preview’s flagged shipment-timing and mix headwinds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $458.8 million, exceeding the guided range of $400-410 million, with consolidated organic growth of 19.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $411.7M consensus”; “Company Q2 revenue guide $400–410M”; and the preview flagged shipment-timing and mix headwinds.

surprises.description: Management raised its full-year organic growth outlook to 19–23%, rather than merely reiterating the $1.70–1.76 billion revenue guidance the preview described as the base case. It also gave strong Q3 and Q4 growth ranges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 organic revenue growth guidance to 19-23%, up from the prior 15-20% goal, with Q3 guided to 19-25% and Q4 to 19-31%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 revenue guidance of “$1.70–1.76B” and said “a mere reiteration may disappoint,” while describing another raise as “the bull hope.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA exceeded its $30–35 million Q2 guide, despite the preview’s concern about overhead absorption and less favorable mix. The preview did not provide an EBITDA estimate, so the comparison is to the call’s stated guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $38.2 million came in above the high end of the $30-35 million guidance range, driven by higher revenue and favorable mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Q2 adjusted-EBITDA guide was not explicitly broken out in available coverage.”

surprises.description: Kratos disclosed a substantial shekel-related earnings headwind that the preview did not flag: it reduced Q2 adjusted EBITDA by $2.5 million and is expected to weigh on full-year EBITDA by $5–7 million, limiting second-half margin expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A strengthening Israeli shekel reduced Q2 adjusted EBITDA by $2.5 million and is expected to create a $5-7 million EBITDA headwind for the full year, limiting second-half margin expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Margins and cash” and overhead absorption, but did not mention a shekel headwind.

surprises.description: Management put much larger numbers on the hypersonics opportunity than the preview’s general call to watch for hypersonics program color: it sees the business roughly doubling in 2026 and more than tripling its 2025 size by 2027.
