surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue $100.18B” and “Revenue consensus implies a sharp slowdown to +1.3% from Q1's +6.2%.”

surprises.description: The reported 87.4% medical benefit ratio was substantially better than the preview’s 89.3% consensus. CVS said about 140 basis points of the result came from favorable prior-year development and individual-exchange risk-adjustment updates, so the reported gap included those benefits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Health Care Benefits delivered an 87.4% medical benefit ratio, but this included approximately $500 million (140 basis points) benefit from favorable prior year development and individual exchange risk adjustment updates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Medical Benefit Ratio (MBR) 89.3%.”

surprises.description: CVS raised Pharmacy and Consumer Wellness full-year adjusted operating income guidance to at least $6.4 billion, $220 million above its prior guidance. The preview listed prior guidance of at least $6.18 billion and expected only a $90 million increase from the earlier level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pharmacy and Consumer Wellness full-year adjusted operating income guidance was raised by $220 million to at least $6.4 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The standing guidance was “PCW adj. operating income ≥$6.18B | +$90M.”

surprises.description: CVS raised cash-flow-from-operations guidance to at least $11.5 billion, $2 billion above its prior guidance and well above the preview’s standing $9.5 billion outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 cash flow from operations guidance was raised by $2 billion to at least $11.5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The standing guidance was “Cash flow from operations ≥$9.5B.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted operating income grew about 35%, with growth across all operating segments. That contrasted with the preview’s concern that Health Services operating income had fallen 7% in Q1 and its bear case that Health Services operating income could decline again.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted operating income reached $5.2 billion (up ~35%) ... with growth across all operating segments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “CVS Health Services adjusted operating income down 7% y/y” in Q1 and described the bear case as “Health Services AOI down again.”

surprises.description: CVS’s preliminary 2027 adjusted EPS outlook of at least $8.44 was slightly above the preview’s $8.37 consensus estimate, although the call described the outlook as matching consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management preliminarily called for 2027 adjusted EPS of at least $8.44 (matching consensus).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year consensus: FY2026E adjusted EPS $7.44; FY2027E $8.37.”

surprises.description: CVS disclosed 2027 Caremark pressures not specified in the preview: membership declines tied to a more disciplined selling season, retention trending slightly below historical norms, and continued 340B pressure. These add caution to the outlook despite the preliminary EPS target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CVS warned of 2027 headwinds including Caremark membership declines from a more disciplined selling season, a retention rate trending slightly below historical norms, plus continued 340B program pressure.”

in_line: CVS reaffirmed a mid-teens adjusted EPS CAGR through 2028, consistent with the preview’s focus on whether management would hedge that outlook.

surprises.description: Elanco reported Q2 revenue of $1.368 billion, about $58 million above the preview’s ~$1.31 billion consensus and above the $1.325 billion high end of company guidance. Organic constant-currency growth was 8%, versus the guided 4–6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “8% organic constant currency revenue growth in Q2, with total revenue of $1.368 billion” and “outperforming the high end of guidance for revenue.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $288 million, substantially above the preview’s ~$250 million consensus and the $260 million high end of guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 21% to $288 million” and the company “outperform[ed] the high end of guidance for…adjusted EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.34 exceeded the preview’s $0.27 consensus (and the alternate $0.28 estimate) as well as the $0.28 high end of company guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased 31% year-over-year to $0.34,” exceeding expectations and the high end of guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS | $0.27 (Zacks); $0.28 at some feeds | $0.25–$0.28”

surprises.description: Elanco raised its FY26 outlook across revenue, EBITDA, and EPS rather than merely reiterating or making a limited revenue-only revision: the OCC growth range’s low end rose to 6%, and both the EBITDA and EPS ranges moved above their prior highs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year guidance to 6-7% organic constant currency growth,” adjusted EBITDA of “$1.01-1.035 billion,” and adjusted EPS of “$1.10-1.16.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $5,010–5,085M (+5–7% OCC),” “Adj. EBITDA $975M–1.005B,” and “Adj. EPS $1.03–1.09.” The preview also said a simple reiteration could read negatively and highlighted whether the raise would reach EPS and EBITDA.

surprises.description: The FY26 innovation revenue target was raised again, to approximately $1.25 billion, rather than remaining at the preview’s $1.2 billion target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The full-year innovation revenue target was raised by $50 million to approximately $1.25 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “innovation revenue $1.2B (raised $50M)”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted gross margin reached 58.1%, above the preview’s roughly 57% estimate and above the 57.8% year-ago comparison. Elanco also raised its full-year gross-margin-expansion guidance to 50 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 80 basis points to 58.1% in Q2, with full-year gross margin expansion guidance raised to 50 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin | ~57%” and “Adjusted gross margin…needs to be flat to up y/y.”

surprises.description: U.S. Pet Health grew 11%, clearing the preview’s key risk threshold of mid-single-digit growth and supporting the growth story the preview was watching.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. Pet Health…grew 11%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything below mid-single digits in Q2 would undercut the H2 acceleration story.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s warning about a hard Farm Animal comparison, U.S. Farm Animal grew 11%; global ruminants were up 17% reported. The supplied facts do not give total Farm Animal organic growth, but the reported figures show strength in these businesses despite the flagged comparison risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. Farm Animal…grew 11%” and “global ruminants rose 17% reported.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Farm Animal against a hard comp. Q1 grew 13% OCC; Q2 laps pre-tariff China buying and Middle East shipment timing.”

surprises.description: Zenrelia was the company’s largest growth contributor, with broad and repeat use: it was treating over 2.5 million dogs, reached more than 60% of the U.S. clinic base, and had an over-80% reorder rate. The preview did not flag this product-level traction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Zenrelia was the largest contributor to total company growth,” treating “over 2.5 million dogs,” with “~18,000 U.S. clinics (>60% of the base),” an “over-80% reorder rate,” and “40%+ first-line usage.”

surprises.description: Credelio Quattro gained share and expanded distribution faster than anything anticipated in the preview: it added 4 market-share points in Q2 and reached over half of U.S. clinics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Credelio Quattro gained 4 points of market share in Q2 (on top of 3 points in Q1) and expanded to over half of U.S. clinics, adding ~3,000 clinics since Q1.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses grew 10% in constant currency, faster than organic revenue growth, and management expects about 11% growth in Q3. Management attributed the spending to DTC investment and said it was directly correlated with market-share gains, making the cost pressure a trade-off rather than an unqualified deterioration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses grew 10% in constant currency (outpacing organic revenue growth), driven by DTC investments management cited as directly correlated to market share gains, with Q3 OpEx expected to rise ~11%.”

surprises.description: Elanco tightened its year-end net-leverage target to approximately 3x from a 3.0–3.2x range and had already reduced net debt by roughly $90 million year to date.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Improved its year-end net leverage target to approximately 3x from a prior 3x-3.2x range,” ending Q2 at 3.1x after cutting net debt by roughly $90 million year to date.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “year-end net leverage 3.0–3.2x.”

surprises.description: The preview expected full-year GMV growth to return by Q4; management upgraded its outlook to expect GMV growth for full-year 2026, independent of a macro or housing-market recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management upgraded its full-year 2026 outlook to expect year-over-year GMV growth, up from prior expectation of growth only in Q4, independent of any macro or housing market recovery.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management reaffirmed ... GMV growth returning by Q4 2026 without macro help.

surprises.description: The preview expected positive full-year free cash flow, but management said positive free cash flow in 2026 is no longer likely because of an accounting reclassification tied to payment processor agreements. The positive full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was maintained.
surprises.fact_evidence: An accounting reclassification tied to payment processor agreements means the company is no longer likely to generate positive free cash flow in 2026, though it maintains its positive full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management reaffirmed positive full-year adj. EBITDA and positive free cash flow.

surprises.description: Q2 GMV was $96 million, above the preview's roughly $88–89 million expectation and above the $91 million high end of guidance. The preview had expected the Q4 inflection to be the turning point, not this level of Q2 growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 GMV reached $96 million, up 7% year-over-year, exceeding the high end of guidance and marking the strongest growth since Q4 2024.
surprises.expectation_evidence: GMV: ~$88M–$89M (buy-side); company guidance $86M–$91M.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached approximately 6%, well above the preview's roughly 0% to +1% expectation and the guidance high end of +2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA margin came in at approximately 6%, an improvement of over 13 percentage points year-over-year and well above the high end of guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adj. EBITDA margin: ~0% to +1%; company guidance -2% to +2%.

surprises.description: The preview expected the take rate to be around 25% and flagged at least 25% as a key threshold, but management lowered its full-year outlook to 24–25% from 25–26%, citing a mix shift toward higher-value orders with lower blended commission rates.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company lowered its full-year revenue take rate outlook to 24-25% (from 25-26%) due to a mix shift toward higher-value orders carrying lower blended commission rates.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Take rate: ~25.0%; catalyst: “Take rate at or above 25% and AOV growth at or above 5%.”

surprises.description: Net revenue was $23.3 million, above both the preview's estimates of $22.23–$22.68 million and the $22.6 million high end of company guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net revenue grew 5% to $23.3 million, also beating the high end of guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Net revenue consensus: $22.23M or $22.68M; company guidance $21.6M–$22.6M.

surprises.description: Order values grew faster than the preview's key threshold: average order value rose 10%, versus the preview's expectation of at least 5%, and median order value also rose 10%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Average order value rose 10% to approximately $2,850, while median order value also grew 10% to about $1,500, signaling broad-based order value expansion.
surprises.expectation_evidence: AOV growth at or above 5%.

surprises.description: The preview cited a new $10 million buyback authorization and watched for execution; the company repurchased approximately $11.1 million of shares in Q2, exhausted its 2026 authorization, and ended the quarter with cash down $17.6 million sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company repurchased approximately 2.4 million shares for $11.1 million in Q2, exhausting its 2026 authorization, and drove cash down $17.6 million sequentially to $67.7 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Authorized a new $10M buyback on May 11, 2026; “Buyback execution” was a catalyst, and the company held ~$85M in cash with no debt as of 3/31/26.

in_line: Active buyers fell 10%, consistent with the preview's base-case range of buyers still down 8–10%, though the preview said narrowing declines would support the bull case.
Management maintained its positive full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: The preview put Q2 adjusted EPS ex-cat consensus at $5.16, implying a 7.1% year-over-year decline. Assurant instead reported adjusted EPS ex-cat growth of 19%, alongside 18% adjusted EBITDA growth, and said it achieved a second consecutive quarter of record earnings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA grew 18% and adjusted EPS grew 19%, both excluding catastrophes, marking a second consecutive quarter of record earnings.”

surprises.description: Assurant raised its full-year outlook from low-single-digit growth to mid-single-digit growth in adjusted EBITDA and EPS ex-cat, or about 10% underlying growth. The preview had expected low-single-digit reported growth and cited a $94 million reserve-development headwind; the call cited a lower $71 million headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year 2026 outlook, now expecting mid-single-digit growth in both adjusted EBITDA and EPS excluding cats, or approximately 10% underlying growth excluding $71 million of lower favorable prior year reserve development.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA and adj. EPS ex-cat: low-single-digit growth (high-single-digit underlying)” and “Development headwind: $94M from reduced prior-year reserve development.”

surprises.description: Global Housing adjusted EBITDA ex-cat rose 18% to $287 million, sharply contradicting the preview’s expectation of a Q2 decline on the reserve-development comparison. Assurant attributed the result to a favorable non-cat loss ratio and lower cat reinsurance costs after the April 1 placement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global Housing Q2 adjusted EBITDA excluding cats grew 18% ($43 million) to $287 million, aided by a favorable non-cat loss ratio of ~35% and lower cat reinsurance costs following the April 1 placement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Housing down ~13–16% on development comp” in the base scenario; the preview also said Q2 FY25 Global Housing adjusted EBITDA ex-cat rose 18% to $244.2M.

surprises.description: Global Lifestyle adjusted EBITDA rose 21% ($43 million), above the preview’s estimated $215–225 million range. Connected Living grew 29%, or 22% after excluding about $10 million of non-run-rate benefits, so the reported growth was strong but partly benefited from items not expected to recur at the same rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global Lifestyle adjusted EBITDA rose 21% ($43 million), with Connected Living EBITDA up 29% ($39 million), though normalized growth was 22% after excluding ~$10 million of non-run-rate benefits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Global Lifestyle adj. EBITDA” preview estimate “~$215–225M vs. $201.4M last year.”

surprises.description: The full-year Global Housing outlook shifted from a modest ex-cat decline to modest growth, reversing the direction the preview said investors were expecting.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year segment guidance was raised to low double-digit growth for Global Lifestyle (led by Connected Living) and modest growth for Global Housing excluding cats.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Global Housing: modest ex-cat decline.”

surprises.description: Global Lifestyle’s full-year growth outlook was raised to low double digits, above the preview’s approximately 10% expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year segment guidance was raised to low double-digit growth for Global Lifestyle (led by Connected Living).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Global Lifestyle: ~+10% growth.”

surprises.description: The lender-placed placement rate was 2.02% and flat year over year, but it fell sequentially because a client transferred higher-placement-rate loans to a non-Assurant servicer. That sequential decline is a risk for the business, though total tracked loans still grew 9%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total tracked loans in lender-placed grew 9% to over 34 million, while the placement rate of 2.02% was flat year-over-year but down sequentially due to a client transferring higher-placement-rate loans to a non-Assurant servicer.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “placement rate falls faster than expected” as a bear-case risk and said to watch whether the placement rate falls faster.

surprises.description: Assurant reported winning a new lender-placed insurance partnership with Freedom Mortgage, a top 10 servicer with about 2.6 million loans. The preview did not identify this partnership; it is expected to ramp over the next year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Assurant won a new lender-placed insurance partnership with Freedom Mortgage, a top 10 U.S. mortgage servicer with approximately 2.6 million loans that will ramp over the next 12 months.”

in_line: The full-year share-repurchase target was raised to the upper end of the $300–350 million range, consistent with the preview’s guidance summary, which already characterized the buyback outlook as being at the upper end.

surprises.description: Recursion lowered its 2026 cash operating expense guidance to $375 million, below the preview’s already-sub-$390 million outlook, while saying it would maintain all outcome targets. That is a better cost outlook without a stated reduction in goals.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered its 2026 full-year cash operating expense guidance to $375 million,” representing “a nearly 40% reduction from comparable 2024 pro forma expenses while maintaining all outcome targets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash operating expenses under $390M for FY2026.”

surprises.description: REC-4881 showed a 43% median polyp-burden reduction after three months, with the effect sustained three months after treatment stopped. The preview highlighted the FDA path but gave no expectation for this clinical efficacy or durability result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “REC-4881 in FAP showed a median polyp burden reduction of 43% after 3 months of treatment” and “durable effects sustained 3 months off treatment.”

surprises.description: The preview was watching for REC-7735 pipeline decisions in the second half of 2026; Recursion reported that the FDA cleared its IND and that the Phase I trial is expected to start later this year. This provides a concrete advancement rather than an unresolved go/no-go.
surprises.fact_evidence: “REC-7735 received FDA IND clearance” and “the Phase I ZINNIA trial will initiate later this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “REC-7735 and REC-102 calls were guided for 2H26.”

surprises.description: Genentech advanced the collaboration’s first novel neuroscience target into a joint early discovery program. The preview watched for Roche/Genentech nominations but did not anticipate this specific target advancement or the platform validation attached to it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Genentech advanced the collaboration's first novel neuroscience target into a joint early discovery program,” marking “early validation” that the platform can discover previously unexplored, biologically-validated targets.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for a third accepted Phenomap, new Roche/Genentech nominations, and contributions from Bayer and Merck KGaA programs.”

surprises.description: The call highlighted more than $500 million in realized partnership cash inflows and more than a dozen successful Sanofi and Roche-Genentech discovery milestones, plus substantial potential payments for future Roche-Genentech programs. The preview focused on possible Q2 collaboration revenue and milestones but did not set an expectation for this cumulative scale or per-program economics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over $500 million in realized partnership cash inflows, including more than a dozen successful discovery milestones with Sanofi and Roche-Genentech”; Roche-Genentech yielded “more than $260 million in upfront and milestone payments,” with “potential for over $300 million in additional milestones for each future small molecule program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Collaboration revenue and new milestones. Watch for a third accepted Phenomap, new Roche/Genentech nominations, and contributions from Bayer and Merck KGaA programs.”

surprises.description: Recursion reported that its engine advances candidates using about 330 compounds over roughly 1.5 years, versus industry benchmarks of about 2,500 compounds over four years. The preview did not flag this speed and capital-efficiency comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recursion's engine advances candidates using roughly 330 compounds over about 1.5 years, compared with industry benchmarks of roughly 2,500 compounds over 4 years.”

surprises.description: The company announced hires from Microsoft Research and drug design to lead AI and drug design, respectively. The preview did not signal these leadership appointments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Strengthened leadership by hiring Dr. Hoifung Poon (from Microsoft Research) as Chief AI Officer and Dr. Donovan Chin to head drug design.”

in_line: The company reaffirmed an operating runway into early 2028, consistent with the preview’s expectation of runway into early 2028 with no additional financing.
The REC-4881 FDA regulatory update is expected before year-end, consistent with the preview’s expectation of an FDA engagement-pathway update in the second half of 2026.

surprises.description: Insulet cut its full-year U.S. Omnipod growth outlook to 17–19%, below the preview’s 18–20% guide. Management tied roughly two-thirds of the reduction to weaker-than-expected Type 2 retention and utilization, especially during the first 90 days of onboarding; Type 2 patients were still over 40% of new starts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cut its full-year U.S. Omnipod growth outlook to 17-19%,” citing “worse-than-anticipated Type 2 retention and utilization trends as roughly two-thirds of the guidance reduction.” Type 2 patients were “over 40% of U.S. new customer starts,” but retention and utilization were lower than for Type 1, concentrated in “the critical first 90 days of onboarding.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “U.S. Omnipod growth vs. +18–20% guide”; the preview also said to watch whether “Type 2 stayed about 40% of new starts, and any disclosure on attrition.”

surprises.description: International Omnipod growth guidance was raised to 30–32% constant currency on strong first-half momentum. The preview flagged the Spain launch but did not anticipate this guidance increase or the strength of the international outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised international Omnipod full-year growth guidance to 30-32% constant currency,” citing “strong first-half momentum,” including Omnipod 5 becoming “Australia's #1 pump for new users” and a Spain launch.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed the “Spain launch” among competitive framing to watch, but gave no international growth outlook or expected guidance increase.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $1.36 came in below the preview’s $1.42 consensus midpoint and even below its $1.38 low-end estimate, despite year-over-year growth of about 42%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew approximately 42% year-over-year to $1.36.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adjusted EPS consensus was “$1.42 midpoint (range $1.38–$1.47).”

surprises.description: Margins were substantially stronger than the preview’s recall-cost and gross-margin concerns suggested: adjusted gross margin expanded 320 basis points, and adjusted operating margin expanded 140 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 320 basis points year-over-year to 72.9%,” driven by productivity gains, positive pricing, and higher volumes; adjusted operating margin expanded “140 basis points” to 19.3%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “Gross margin and recall costs” as a key metric to watch, noting Q1 adjusted gross margin was down 90 basis points year over year and asking how much recall cost landed in Q2.

surprises.description: The company raised its 2026 adjusted EPS growth outlook to at least 30%, above the preview’s cited company outlook of greater than 25%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reiterated full-year targets of approximately 100 basis points of operating margin expansion and now expects adjusted EPS growth of at least 30% for 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY26 adjusted EPS guidance was “>25% growth.”

surprises.description: Management’s preliminary outlook pointed to a mid-teens total-company constant-currency revenue growth exit rate in 2026, below the preview’s 21–23% FY26 growth outlook. This signals a weaker exit pace, although the call fact does not say the full-year target itself was changed.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “preliminarily expects total company constant currency revenue growth to exit 2026 in the mid-teens.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue growth: 21–23% cc total company.”

surprises.description: Management introduced a wide preliminary 2027 U.S. Omnipod growth range of 9–14% (12% midpoint), assuming no benefit from remediation actions. The preview had no comparable 2027 U.S. growth expectation, so the range adds a notably cautious forward signal rather than contradicting a stated consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2027 U.S. Omnipod growth framed in a wide 9-14% range (12% midpoint) that assumes no benefit from remediation actions.”

surprises.description: Management attributed the U.S. guidance problem to execution rather than pricing, competition, or GLP-1 pressure, and said pricing was stable to slightly up. That is more reassuring on competitive and pricing pressure than the preview’s emphasis on competitors and potential recall-driven attrition, though it leaves execution challenges as the stated issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “explicitly attributed the guidance cut to execution challenges rather than pricing, competition, or GLP-1 pressure,” and said “pricing remains stable to slightly up.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged competitive entrants and said below-guide U.S. growth could point to “recall-driven attrition”; it also listed “Competitive framing” as a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: Q2 constant-currency revenue slightly exceeded the company’s quarterly growth guide, even though reported revenue was essentially at the preview’s dollar consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total company revenue reached $802 million, growing 23.5% reported and 22.7% constant currency, exceeding company expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The company’s Q2 guide was “+20–22% cc”; the preview’s reported-dollar consensus was “~$803M.”

in_line: Reported Q2 revenue of $802 million was essentially in line with the preview’s approximately $803 million consensus estimate.
Type 2 patients made up over 40% of U.S. new customer starts, broadly matching the preview’s expectation of about 40%.
The company reiterated its target of approximately 100 basis points of full-year operating margin expansion, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the full-year outlook could be reaffirmed.

surprises.description: Geron reported Q2 RYTELO revenue of $57.5 million, above the preview’s consensus range of $55.3 million–$56.3 million. Sequential growth was also 11%, versus roughly 6.6% implied by the preview’s Q1 comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenue grew 17% year-over-year and 11% quarter-over-quarter to $57.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (RYTELO net) | $55.3M (range $55.3M–$56.3M)” and “Implied sequential growth vs. Q1's $51.8M is about +6.6%.”

surprises.description: Management moved from simply reaffirming the $220 million–$240 million full-year RYTELO guidance range to expecting revenue to land in its mid- to high end. That is a more favorable outlook than the preview’s base case of a reaffirmed range without an indicated upper-half bias.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now expects to land at the mid- to high end of its full-year 2026 RYTELO net revenue guidance range of $220 million to $240 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full reaffirmation of $220M–$240M versus narrowing”; the base scenario also anticipated “guide reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed that it is evaluating a modification to the IMPACT MF interim-analysis event threshold, a trial-design issue the preview did not flag. The projected timelines, including the final overall-survival analysis in the second half of 2028, remain unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Geron is evaluating a modification to the event threshold for the interim analysis of the Phase III IMPACT MF trial, though projected timelines and the final OS analysis in second-half 2028 remain unchanged.”

surprises.description: First-half revenue rose about 24% while operating expenses fell 4%, a favorable combination the preview’s discussion of opex, burn, and the path to breakeven did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half 2026 net revenue increased approximately 24% versus the prior-year period, while total operating expenses decreased 4% over the same period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Opex and burn” and said the FY opex guide implied “about $58M–$60M per quarter”; it did not project falling first-half expenses alongside revenue growth.

surprises.description: RYTELO demand grew 5% quarter over quarter, slightly below the roughly 6% demand growth cited in the preview. The increase in prescribing accounts was stronger at 8%, so the demand indicators were not uniformly weak.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RYTELO demand grew 5% quarter-over-quarter with an 8% increase in prescribing accounts, expanding the footprint to roughly 1,575 accounts since launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Demand growth of about 6%” and described a 5–6% demand-growth backdrop.

surprises.description: The call supplied new detail on lower-risk MDS: first- and second-line starts were 34% on a rolling 12-month basis, and management estimated 8,000 eligible U.S. second-line patients. The preview did not quantify this treatment-line mix or patient pool.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First- and second-line patient starts reached 34% on a rolling 12-month basis, with an estimated 8,000 eligible second-line lower-risk MDS patients in the U.S.”

surprises.description: Management put a scale estimate on the ex-U.S. lower-risk MDS opportunity, saying the patient opportunity is in the thousands and comparable to the U.S. The preview expected a European-strategy update before year-end but did not provide this market-size comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to disclose its European commercialization strategy for lower-risk MDS before year-end, estimating an ex-U.S. patient opportunity in the thousands comparable to the U.S.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “promised an update before year-end” on the European commercial plan.

in_line: Full-year total operating expense guidance remained $230 million–$240 million, as expected.
Q2 gross-to-net deductions were 20.7%, close to the prior quarter’s roughly 21%, and management maintained the previously indicated low-to-mid-20s range for the rest of the year.

The IMPACT MF projected timelines remained unchanged, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the interim analysis was due in the second half of 2026 and the final analysis in the second half of 2028.
Management still plans to disclose its European commercialization strategy before year-end, as the preview anticipated.

surprises.description: NYT added 280,000 digital subscribers, below the preview’s roughly 320,000 Street-implied expectation. That was within the preview’s 265,000–300,000 base-case range and near its cited buy-side whisper, so the shortfall was limited.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company added “280,000 net new digital subscribers in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Street was “at ~12.84M, implying ~320K net adds”; its base scenario was 265K–300K and its inferred buy-side whisper was ~260K–290K.

surprises.description: Digital advertising grew faster than the preview’s high-teens guide and estimate, rather than merely clearing the preview’s threshold for a healthy result.
surprises.fact_evidence: Digital advertising revenues grew 20.7% to $114 million, “beating guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited company guidance of “high teens” growth and estimated digital advertising at ~$110–112M; it said growth below ~15% would frame the result as a one-quarter comp effect.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS modestly exceeded the preview’s consensus, though the result was close to the top of its base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted diluted EPS rose 19% to $0.69.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed adjusted diluted EPS consensus of $0.67 and a base scenario of $0.66–$0.69.

surprises.description: Adjusted operating costs grew faster than the company’s 8%–9% guidance. Management attributed the overshoot to variable compensation tied to financial outperformance, rather than structural cost changes.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted operating costs grew 10%, exceeding the 8%–9% guidance, primarily due to incremental variable compensation tied to financial outperformance rather than structural changes.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated adjusted operating costs at ~$596–602M based on company guidance of “+8–9%.”

surprises.description: NYT’s Q3 digital subscription revenue growth outlook is below its recent pace, pointing to a slowdown after Q2’s 16.4% growth. The preview did not give a Q3 digital subscription revenue estimate, so this comparison is to the recent trend rather than a stated Q3 consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 guidance calls for digital subscription revenue growth of 12%–15%, below recent trends, partly due to the cohort mix impact from paywalling the Mini game in last year's Q3.

surprises.description: Management described headwinds to sustaining advertising momentum that were not covered in the preview: big tech platforms are sending less traffic to publishers, video monetization remains a minor contributor, and NYT faces strong ad-supply comparisons in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management acknowledged big tech platforms are driving less traffic to publishers and that video monetization currently plays only a minor role in advertising growth as the company laps strong ad supply comps in the back half of the year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on Q2 digital advertising versus the “high teens” guide and the harder Q2 comparison; it did not discuss declining platform traffic or video’s limited contribution.

surprises.description: The company disclosed that part of 2026 free cash flow is supported by benefits that are not expected to persist: a tax-related benefit and first-half working-capital gains expected to reverse. This makes the cash-flow figure less recurring than the preview’s discussion of the company’s LTM FCF and return target suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: 2026 free cash flow includes an approximately $60 million tax-related benefit, the majority of which is not expected to recur beyond fiscal 2026, and some first-half working capital gains are expected to reverse.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited $542M of LTM free cash flow and the company’s commitment to return at least 50% of free cash flow over the mid-term, without mentioning the tax benefit or working-capital reversal.

in_line: Digital subscription revenue of $408M and total subscription revenue of approximately $538M were within the preview’s guide-implied ranges of ~$400–410M and ~$529–539M, respectively.
The company remained on track toward the 15M subscriber milestone, as the preview noted.
First-half shareholder returns of about $160M were consistent with the preview’s cited commitment to return at least 50% of free cash flow over the mid-term.

surprises.description: Net new ARR was $85 million, well above the preview’s estimated $45–55 million Q1 range. The $85 million included $13 million from Bindplane, but organic net new ARR was still up 41%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net new ARR reached $85 million, up 66% overall and 41% organically after excluding the $13 million Bindplane acquisition contribution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “An estimate of roughly $45–55M CC is needed to stay on plan.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating margin reached 29%, above the 27.4–28.0% Q1 guide, rather than showing the weaker margin implied by the preview’s expectation of a back-half-loaded recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin was 29%, beating guidance by 100 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 is guided to 27.4–28.0% against a full-year target of about 29.5%, so recovery is back-half loaded.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $0.48, beating the $0.44–$0.45 company guide and the roughly $0.44 consensus, and reaching the preview’s bull-case range rather than its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $0.48 came in $0.03 above the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS (diluted) … Company guide … $0.44–0.45”; “Consensus … ~$0.44”; “Base … $0.45–0.46.”

surprises.description: Dynatrace raised FY27 non-GAAP EPS guidance by $0.04 to $1.97–$1.99, above the prior $1.93–$1.95 range; the preview said reaffirmation was the default.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS guidance was raised $0.04 to $1.97–$1.99.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2027 guidance … to be reaffirmed or revised”; “A reaffirmation is the default.”

surprises.description: Q1 total and subscription revenue both exceeded the high end of guidance: total revenue was $555 million versus $551 million, and subscription revenue was $530 million versus $527 million. The revenue beat was modest relative to the preview’s consensus and base-case ranges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 total revenue was $555 million and subscription revenue was $530 million, both up 15% and exceeding the high end of guidance by 100 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Company guide … $547–551M | Consensus … ~$549.5M”; “Subscription revenue … Company guide … $523–527M.”

surprises.description: The company reported record new-logo ARR growth above 160%, with 122 new logos and an average land size near $285,000; land size had increased for five consecutive quarters. The preview did not anticipate this reported level of new-customer momentum.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record new logo ARR growth of more than 160%, adding 122 new logos with an average land size of nearly $285,000, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of increasing land size.”

surprises.description: Management reported unusually strong AI adoption and usage evidence, including over 1,000 customers monitoring AI/LLM workloads and AI-capability customers growing consumption 1.5 times faster. This was a more concrete positive counterpoint to the preview’s concern about perceived softness in AI differentiation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 1,000 customers now monitoring AI/LLM workloads (up from ~850)”; “Customers using AI capabilities show consumption growth 1.5x higher than non-AI cohort customers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The May sell-off was driven by perceived softness on AI differentiation and pricing power against Datadog, Elastic, and hyperscaler-native tools.”

surprises.description: Log management had reached nearly $200 million in annualized consumption and doubled in only two quarters, an acceleration the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Log management, the fastest-growing product category, reached nearly $200 million in annualized consumption—doubling in just two quarters—while continuing to grow well above 100%.”

surprises.description: Management now expects net retention to inflect higher in the second half as most DPS renewals occur then, adding a more optimistic trajectory than the preview’s flat-at-110% base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects NRR to inflect higher in the back half as 70% of DPS renewals occur then.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … NRR flat at 110%.”

surprises.description: CFO Jim Benson announced plans to retire by fiscal year-end, with a successor search and transition underway; the preview did not flag an impending CFO departure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Jim Benson announced plans to retire by the end of the fiscal year, with a successor search underway and a transition expected.”

surprises.description: Dynatrace reported $275 million of share repurchases, or 7.1 million shares, in Q1; the preview did not mention or set an expectation for repurchases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Share repurchases increased to $275 million (7.1 million shares) in Q1.”

in_line: Net retention was 110%, in line with the preview’s stated current level and its base-case expectation of remaining flat at 110%.
The FY27 constant-currency ARR growth range was maintained at 15.5%–16.5%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the range would likely be reaffirmed.

surprises.description: Q2 comparable net sales were $1.8 billion, above the preview’s $1.76 billion consensus estimate, and management said sales exceeded company expectations. The gap is modest, especially since some feeds rounded the estimate to $1.8 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose 4.2% on a comparable basis to $1.8 billion” and “exceeding company expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $1.76B (some feeds round to $1.8B)”

surprises.description: Management raised FY26 comparable net sales growth guidance again, to 2%–4% from 1%–3%, whereas the preview said sales guidance was more likely to hold. This is a clear upward revision to the outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 comparable net sales growth guidance for a second consecutive quarter to 2%-4%, up from the prior 1%-3% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sales guidance looks more likely to hold.”

surprises.description: Direct Delivery net sales returned to growth at 0.4% a quarter earlier than the preview’s recovery timeline, which anticipated breakeven net customer adds in Q2 and modest growth in the second half. The improvement was not volume-led: management said it came from price/mix while the customer base remained smaller.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Direct delivery net sales returned to growth at 0.4%, a 340 basis point sequential improvement and one quarter ahead of expectations, though driven by price/mix rather than volume as the customer base remained smaller.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided Q2 to breakeven in net customer adds and modest growth in the second half.”

surprises.description: Despite the sales growth, comparable growth was almost entirely driven by price/mix, with slightly negative volume overall. The preview discussed sales growth expectations but did not anticipate this weak volume contribution, making the composition of growth a concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total comparable growth was almost entirely price/mix-driven, with a 4.3% price/mix contribution offset by a negative 0.1% volume contribution.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was $385 million, at the high end of the preview’s estimated $370–385 million range, and increased year over year as the preview said the quarter needed to show growth.
Comparable adjusted EBITDA margin rose 10 basis points year over year, broadly in line with the preview’s base-case expectation of roughly flat year-over-year margin.
The FY26 adjusted EBITDA range was reaffirmed at $1.465–$1.515 billion, consistent with the preview’s base case of an unchanged range.
Full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance remained $790–$810 million; the preview listed that range as existing company guidance.
Management cited a tighter freight market and higher spot transportation rates, consistent with the preview flagging freight and related costs as issues to watch.

surprises.description: The preview modeled Q2 AFFO per share at $0.73–$0.75; Lineage reported about $0.76, slightly above that range and ahead of consensus estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 total AFFO was approximately $198 million, or $0.76 per share, and was ahead of internal expectations and consensus estimates.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AFFO/share: $0.73–$0.75 (modeled)”

surprises.description: The preview expected FY26 AFFO guidance to be $2.75–$3.00, with an upper-half narrowing viewed as positive. Lineage raised the range to $2.80–$3.05 rather than merely reaffirming or narrowing it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Increased AFFO per share guidance to $2.80-$3.05 (from $2.75-$3.00).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AFFO/share: $2.75–$3.00”; “A narrowing to the upper half would be a positive. A plain reaffirmation after the recent run would read as a disappointment.”

surprises.description: The preview expected FY26 same-store NOI guidance of negative 4% to negative 1% to remain unchanged. Lineage raised the range to negative 3% to flat, despite the expected second-half reduction in FX support.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year same-store NOI guidance to negative 3% to flat (from negative 4% to negative 1%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 company guidance (unchanged on the Q1 call): Same-store NOI: (4)% to (1)%.”

surprises.description: The preview modeled Q2 adjusted EBITDA at $318–$325 million. Lineage reported approximately $320 million, within that range, although the call said it was ahead of consensus estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was approximately $320 million” and was “ahead of internal expectations and consensus estimates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: $318–325M (modeled, not published consensus).”

surprises.description: The preview described Q2 physical occupancy of 75–76% as seasonally normal, but Lineage reported a 90-basis-point year-over-year increase—the first year-over-year occupancy gain since going public and a turn after 2025 declines.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-store physical occupancy rose 90 basis points year-over-year, marking the first year-over-year occupancy gain since the company went public and an inflection after 2025 declines.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Physical occupancy normally falls in Q2, so a 75–76% print is not negative on its own.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged a portfolio transaction as a major catalyst and said repeated silence would hurt. Lineage disclosed plans to divest over $1 billion of assets and promised a strategic-review update by year-end, but did not announce a completed sale, JV, or portfolio transaction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management plans to divest over $1 billion of assets, with a comprehensive strategic review update expected by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Portfolio review. Leverage is above the target range, so an announced asset sale, JV or portfolio transaction would be the largest single catalyst. Repeated silence on this would hurt.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a major facility fire and an estimated $15 million adjusted EBITDA drag across Q3 and Q4, which the preview had not anticipated. Guidance excludes any business-interruption insurance recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Big Bear facility fire (~500,000 sq ft, ~85,000 pallet positions, roughly 1% of global capacity) is expected to create a ~$15 million adjusted EBITDA drag across Q3 and Q4, though guidance excludes any business interruption insurance recovery.”

surprises.description: The preview’s stated FY26 guidance had GIS NOI at 0% to positive 2%; Lineage lowered its outlook to negative 4% to negative 2%, citing a legal settlement and lagging carrier rate pass-throughs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The GIS segment's full-year NOI outlook was lowered to negative 4% to negative 2% (from 0% to positive 2%), driven by a $7 million legal settlement and lagging carrier rate pass-throughs.”

surprises.description: The preview did not lay out a quarterly NOI path. Management now expects Q3 to be the toughest year-over-year comparison, with same-store NOI growth below Q2 levels, followed by close to flat growth in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects Q3 2026 to be the toughest year-over-year comparison with same-store NOI growth likely below Q2 levels, while Q4 is projected to reach close to flat year-over-year same-store NOI growth.”

in_line: Q2 same-store NOI declined 2.9% year-over-year, within the preview’s modeled range of negative 2% to negative 3%.

surprises.description: Kaltura reported $46.9 million of Q2 revenue, above both the $46.0 million top of company guidance and the $45.60 million consensus estimate, rather than landing near the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $46.9 million… exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue… Q2'26 Company Guidance $45.2M – $46.0M; Consensus $45.60M.”

surprises.description: Subscription revenue was $45.6 million, exceeding the $44.1 million high end of guidance; the preview had expected $43.3 million–$44.1 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subscription revenue of $45.6 million… exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Subscription revenue… Q2'26 Company Guidance $43.3M – $44.1M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $5.9 million, far above the $2 million–$3 million guidance range and the preview’s bull-scenario threshold of $3.5 million. Its 12% margin also substantially exceeded the preview’s implied 4.4%–6.5% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached a record second-quarter high of $5.9 million… above the $2-3 million guidance range, with margin expanding 300 basis points to 12%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA… Q2'26 Company Guidance $2.0M – $3.0M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin… 4.4% – 6.5%.”

surprises.description: Kaltura raised its full-year 2026 guidance, including adjusted EBITDA guidance to $15.8 million–$17.2 million, above the preview’s previously stated $13.8 million–$15.2 million range. The preview had identified a cut as a key risk, so the upward revision is better than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was raised… adjusted EBITDA at $15.8-17.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full year 2026… adj. EBITDA $13.8M – $15.2M”; the preview also says “Any further cut would remove the profitability support for the stock.”

surprises.description: Gross margins reached records: 75% non-GAAP gross margin overall and 79% for subscriptions. The preview did not anticipate these margin highs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A record non-GAAP gross margin of 75%, driven by a record 79% non-GAAP subscription gross margin.”

surprises.description: Kaltura signed 14 new deals including AI offerings—double its prior record, with nine involving Agentic Avatars—but the combined contract value was only about $1 million. The number of deals was much stronger than the preview’s reference to three small AI deals in Q1, while the modest aggregate value limits the scale implied by the count.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A record 14 new deals including AI offerings—double its prior record—with nine including the new Agentic Avatars product, but combined total contract value was only about $1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Three AI-related deals, described as ‘small.’”

surprises.description: The AI-related pipeline for H2 2026 and 2027 exceeded 500 opportunities, representing about $17 million in non-weighted potential annual contract value. The preview flagged the lack of AI dollar disclosures but did not anticipate this pipeline scale; its unweighted nature means it is potential rather than booked revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The AI-related sales pipeline for H2 2026 and 2027 now exceeds 500 opportunities representing approximately $17 million in non-weighted potential annual contract value.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “First disclosure of AI or PathFactory revenue or ARR”; the preview also notes “no disclosed dollar figures yet.”

surprises.description: Management said H2 new subscription bookings could potentially exceed 2.5 times H1 bookings, a stronger bookings outlook than the preview’s discussion of second-half revenue growth implied but did not quantify in bookings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects H2 new subscription bookings to potentially exceed 2.5 times the amount booked in H1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The guide implies second-half revenue growth of about 4.6%”; no H2 bookings target was provided.

surprises.description: PathFactory contributed $4.9 million of subscription revenue, higher than expected, although management still expects attrition and revenue headwinds from its standalone product over the next few quarters. This gives a larger near-term contribution than expected but also confirms ongoing product-related headwinds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PathFactory contributed $4.9 million in subscription revenue this quarter, higher than expected, but management anticipates continued attrition and revenue headwinds from its core standalone product over the next few quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 is the first quarter with a full PathFactory contribution”; “PathFactory's standalone revenue and ARR have not been disclosed.”

surprises.description: Gross retention reached its strongest level since Q4 2022, an improvement not identified in the preview’s retention expectations. Net dollar retention was 96%, however, below the preview’s 97%-or-higher level that would indicate churn had annualized.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net dollar retention was 96%, up from 95% prior quarter but down from 101% a year ago, while gross retention hit its strongest level since Q4 2022.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A print of 97% or higher would suggest the churn has annualized”; the base scenario expected “NDR 95%–96%.”

in_line: Net dollar retention of 96% was within the preview’s stated base-case range of 95%–96%, although it did not reach the 97% threshold the preview associated with churn annualizing.

The M&T segment’s 10% year-over-year revenue decline and continued declines expected in 2026 were consistent with the preview’s expectation that M&T would decline again and its stated 2027 recovery narrative.
Meaningful AI revenue contribution remains deferred to 2027, consistent with the preview’s statement that management had already deferred meaningful new-product revenue to “more meaningful in 2027.”

surprises.description: Global Payments lowered its full-year outlook: normalized constant-currency adjusted net revenue growth is now about 4–5%, versus the preview’s roughly 5% target, and adjusted EPS is $13.60–$13.80 rather than the prior $13.80–$14.00 range. Management said the outlook assumes the Middle East travel impact persists through the rest of 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management lowered its full-year outlook,” guiding to normalized constant currency adjusted net revenue growth of “~4-5%” and adjusted EPS of “$13.60-$13.80,” assuming the Middle East travel impact persists through the rest of 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says the FY26 EPS range was “$13.80–$14.00” and the FY normalized revenue growth target was “~5%”; it also says a plain reaffirmation would disappoint relative to positioning.

surprises.description: Normalized adjusted operating-margin expansion was only 70 basis points, well short of the preview’s expected 120–140 basis points in its base case and its call for a visible step-up toward 150–170 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margins expanded 70 basis points on a normalized basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case called for margin up “120–140 bps”; its key-issues section said Q2 needed a visible step-up toward “+150–170 bps.”

surprises.description: Adjusted net revenue was $3.16 billion, above the preview’s estimated $3.00–$3.05 billion range, although the preview cautioned that revenue bases differed and the consensus figure might be GAAP.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted net revenue was $3.16 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated adjusted net revenue might land “nearer $3.00–3.05B” and its base scenario was “about $3.00–3.05B.”

surprises.description: Despite the higher adjusted-revenue dollar figure, normalized revenue growth was 4%, below the preview’s stated 5% constant-currency threshold for maintaining the acceleration narrative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net revenue was $3.16 billion, up 4% on a normalized basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 needed “at least 5% cc to keep the acceleration narrative intact.”

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate the Middle East conflict as a demand headwind: management reported that reduced travel volumes tied to the conflict cut Q2 growth by about 100 basis points and factored the impact into the lower full-year outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 growth absorbed “an approximately 100 basis point headwind from reduced travel volumes tied to the Middle East conflict”; the full-year outlook assumes the impact persists through the rest of 2026.

surprises.description: Shareholder returns were already more than halfway toward the unchanged 2026 commitment by Q2, with about $550 million returned during the quarter. The preview flagged return pacing as something to watch but did not project this pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company returned “approximately $550 million to shareholders in Q2” and is “now more than halfway toward its over $2 billion 2026 capital return commitment,” which “remains unchanged despite the guidance cut.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “the pace of buybacks against the >$2B 2026 commitment” as something to watch; it gave no Q2 pacing estimate.

surprises.description: Genius operating indicators were notably strong, though revenue contribution remains modest: bookings rose more than 25% sequentially, new-customer yields rose 75% year over year, and new merchant locations per sales professional increased 30%. The preview did not discuss Genius.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Genius momentum strengthened with bookings up over 25% sequentially, new customer yields up 75% year-over-year, and a 30% increase in new merchant locations per sales professional, though revenue contribution remains modest one year after launch.”

surprises.description: The reported segment figures added positive detail absent from the preview: Enterprise grew 7% normalized despite an approximately 400-basis-point Middle East headwind, while Platforms grew 7% with value-added-services revenue up 25%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Enterprise delivered “$838 million in revenue” and “growing 7% normalized despite an ~400 basis point Middle East headwind”; Platforms posted “$628 million in revenue (7% growth)” with “value-added services revenue up 25%.”

in_line: Adjusted EPS was $3.46, matching the preview’s $3.46 consensus estimate and its base-case range of $3.46–$3.52.
Management reaffirmed the cumulative $7.5 billion capital-return expectation by the end of 2027, consistent with the preview’s stated $7.5 billion commitment across 2025–2027.

surprises.description: Backlog reached $421.8 million, about 40% above a year ago and well above the preview’s $320–350 million base scenario and $350 million bull-case threshold. This was a much stronger demand signal than the preview’s expected first year-over-year backlog increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Manufacturing backlog surged approximately 40% to $421.8 million from $302 million a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Backlog $320–350M” in the base scenario; “backlog >$350M” in the bull scenario. The preview also called a year-over-year increase “the first in several quarters.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue is now expected to grow at a mid-single-digit rate year over year, excluding Homes Direct. The preview provided no Q2 growth estimate, so this is better than the flat-sales trajectory implied by the prior Q1 outlook, rather than a beat against an explicit Q2 forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company guided Q2 revenue to grow mid-single digits year-over-year, excluding the newly acquired Homes Direct which will be additive but immaterial.”

surprises.description: Sales slightly exceeded even the top of the preview’s consensus range: $710.2 million versus a high estimate of $709.4 million. The beat was small, and sales were also consistent with the company’s approximately-flat Q1 outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales increased 1.3% year-over-year to $710.2 million, slightly ahead of expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus was “$702.0M – $709.4M”; company guidance was “Approximately flat YoY.”

surprises.description: The cost outlook combines a continuing substantial margin drag with a more favorable inflation trend: Q2 adjusted gross margin guidance still implies about 200 basis points of year-over-year pressure, but input-cost inflation is leveling off rather than accelerating as the preview described. The outlook is therefore mixed against expectations of a peak headwind this quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted gross margin guidance of 25-26% implies roughly 200 basis points of year-over-year headwind driven primarily by elevated input costs, though inflation is leveling off.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had flagged “accelerating input inflation” and said “the headwind peaks this quarter.”

in_line: Adjusted EPS of $0.88 matched the bottom of the preview’s $0.88–$0.92 estimate range.
U.S. homes sold rose 1.8% to 7,089 while industry shipments declined roughly 5%, consistent with the preview’s expectation of share gains in a weak industry.

The preview expected an effective tax-rate increase of 3–4 points as the energy-efficient-home credit expired; the reported rate rose from 21% to about 25% and is expected to remain elevated through fiscal 2027.
Homes Direct closed in Q2 as previewed, with 11 Western stores and about $70 million in sales; it remains excluded from the Q2 revenue-growth guidance.
The preview flagged ongoing channel-mix pressure on ASP. ASP rose only 0.6%, with gains offset by shifts toward lower-priced independent and community sales.
The preview flagged buyback pace and a refreshed $150 million authorization. The company repurchased $50 million during the quarter and renewed the authorization at $150 million.

surprises.description: The preview used a roughly $350 million placeholder for Q3 revenue, with a $330–360 million base-case range. SolarEdge guided to $310–340 million, a lower range and a midpoint about $25 million below that placeholder; management also said the usual Q3 U.S. pickup is not expected in the softening market.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $310–340 million implies a sequential decline,” with “no typical Q3 pickup expected in the softening U.S. market.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3'26 revenue guide versus a ~$350M sell-side placeholder”; the base scenario gave “$330–360M.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was well above the preview’s roughly 25% consensus and exceeded the company’s 27% guidance ceiling. The result included a $13.3 million IEEPA tariff-refund benefit, even though the preview said the approximately $55 million refund was excluded from guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin expanded for the sixth consecutive quarter to 28.6% ... beating guidance and including a $13.3 million benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Non-GAAP gross margin ~25%” consensus and a “23–27%” company guide; it also said “The ~$55M IEEPA tariff refund is excluded from guidance.”

surprises.description: SolarEdge reported positive non-GAAP operating income of $10.2 million, above the preview’s expectation of breakeven EBIT at the guidance midpoint. The preview had specifically identified a positive print as the first since 2023; Q2 also marked the company’s first non-GAAP profitability since Q2 2023.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income of $10.2 million and non-GAAP net income of $3.6 million ($0.05 per diluted share), marking its first non-GAAP profitability since Q2 2023.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The company guide was “Close to breakeven EBIT at midpoint”; the preview said, “A positive print would be the first since 2023.”

surprises.description: European revenue grew much faster than the preview’s Europe demand read-through suggested: SolarEdge’s Europe revenue more than doubled year over year, while the cited Enphase read-through showed Europe up 35% year over year. The preview did not give a direct SolarEdge Europe revenue estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “European revenue more than doubled year-over-year to $154.4 million (up 36% quarter-over-quarter).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s geographic-mix section cited the Enphase read-across: “Europe up 35%.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s concerns about weak U.S. residential demand and a sharp decline in the Enphase read-through, SolarEdge’s U.S. revenue fell only 2% sequentially. The preview did not provide a direct Q2 SolarEdge U.S. revenue estimate, so this is a favorable comparison with the risks it highlighted rather than a beat against a company-specific forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. revenue declined 2% sequentially to $154.9 million amid soft resi demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited U.S. residential sell-through “down 34% YoY” in the Enphase read-across and noted SolarEdge Q1 U.S. revenue was “–20% QoQ.”

surprises.description: SolarEdge disclosed that its 3-phase Nexis platform had already shipped more than $60 million in Q2 as its European rollout began. The preview flagged Nexis as an item to watch but gave no shipment or order-book expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 3-phase Nexis platform began meaningful rollout in Europe with shipments exceeding $60 million in Q2,” with a single-phase launch planned for Q1 2027.

surprises.description: The call highlighted substantial U.S. commercial rooftop penetration: more than half of installations in the most recent report and deployments on over 60% of Fortune 100 company rooftops. The preview flagged U.S. C&I allocation and pricing but did not anticipate or quantify this level of penetration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SolarEdge captured more than 50% of U.S. C&I rooftop installations in the most recent report and is installed on rooftops of over 60% of Fortune 100 companies.”

surprises.description: The company gave Q3 non-GAAP gross-margin guidance of 22–26%, below Q2’s 28.6%, attributing the decline largely to lower fixed-cost absorption on reduced volume. The preview discussed Q2 gross margin but did not give a Q3 margin expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 non-GAAP gross margin is guided to approximately 22–26%, down from Q2 largely due to lower fixed-cost absorption on reduced volume and excluding any potential IEEPA refunds.”

surprises.description: The call added a new long-term AI-factory power-conversion opportunity: the SST solution had demonstrated 99% efficiency in labs, with a working system targeted by year-end 2026 and pilot installations planned for 2027. The preview did not mention this product or roadmap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The AI factory SST solution demonstrated 99% efficiency in labs, with a working system targeted by end of 2026, pilot installations in 2027, and volume shipments in 2028.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $346.2 million was modestly above the $341.7 million consensus, while remaining within the company’s $325–355 million guidance range.
Non-GAAP EPS of $0.05 was close to the preview’s Zacks consensus of $0.04.
The absence of significant safe-harbor revenue pull-forward matched the preview’s stated expectation that Q2 guidance did not include a significant pull-forward.
The company reaffirmed full-year positive free cash flow and maintained 2026 capex guidance of $60–80 million, in line with the preview’s stated targets.

surprises.description: Gross bookings were expected around $57.2 billion, with company guidance topping out at $57.75 billion; Uber reported more than $58 billion, above both the Street figure and the guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross bookings grew 22% year-over-year to more than $58 billion, exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross Bookings: $57.2B (Street)” and company guidance of “$56.25–57.75B.”

surprises.description: The preview put non-GAAP EPS consensus at $0.81–$0.83. Reported 35% year-over-year growth, against the preview’s $0.63 prior-year figure, implies roughly $0.85—above that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS grew 35% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS: $0.83 (Zacks) / $0.81 (Street)” and Q2 FY25 actual of “$0.63.”

surprises.description: The preview expected investors to focus on AV deployment counts and per-trip economics. Uber reported that AV trips are still less than 0.5% of roughly 300 million weekly trips, showing that current commercialization remains very small.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AV trips currently represent less than 0.5% of Uber's total volume of roughly 300 million trips per week.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Investors want live vehicle counts and per-trip economics, not commentary.”

surprises.description: The preview raised a report that Waymo might end its Uber partnership and said management’s answer mattered. Uber included Waymo among partners expected to support additional launches, rather than describing an exit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Additional launches through partners like Zoox, Waymo, and Baidu.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Jul 24 FT report said Waymo is exploring ending its Uber partnership… Management's answer on the call matters.”

surprises.description: Uber reported a concrete AV rollout of seven live cities and a target of 15 by year-end, with more markets planned for 2027. The preview sought deployment numbers, so this provides a specific city-count update, though not the vehicle counts or per-trip economics it requested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Uber is live with AV partners in 7 cities and on track to reach 15 cities by year-end, with plans for many more markets in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AV deployment numbers. Uber has committed over $10B across 30+ AV partners. Investors want live vehicle counts and per-trip economics, not commentary.”

surprises.description: The preview noted Uber’s planned AV investment of over $10 billion, but the call added that each Uber dollar has helped partners raise $2.50 and that Uber is committed to delivering 120,000 vehicles over the next few years.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Uber's planned $10 billion AV investment spans multiple years and has helped partners raise an additional $2.50 for every $1 Uber invested, alongside a commitment to deliver 120,000 vehicles over the next few years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Uber has committed over $10B across 30+ AV partners.”

surprises.description: The preview sought financial and antitrust details on the Delivery Hero deal; the call instead added a strategic reach claim: the deal is expected to bring Uber to nearly 100 markets and roughly double the markets with both mobility and delivery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Uber's agreement to acquire Delivery Hero is expected to expand reach to nearly 100 markets and roughly double the number of markets offering both mobility and delivery.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The $14.8B all-stock deal… needs accretion, dilution, and antitrust detail.”

surprises.description: The preview’s bull case identified mobility reacceleration as a potential driver; Uber said US mobility trips and bookings accelerated, citing insurance-savings reinvestment, product innovation, and suburban markets as contributors.
surprises.fact_evidence: “US mobility trips and gross bookings accelerated in Q2 driven by insurance savings reinvestment, product innovation, and suburban (SPARs) markets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bull scenario cited “Mobility reaccelerates” as a key driver.

surprises.description: Uber reported a nearly 500-basis-point year-over-year decline in mobility revenue take rate, with about 400 basis points attributed to an optical UK business-model change; despite the decline, mobility operating-income margin was 7.6%. The preview did not flag this take-rate issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mobility revenue take rate declined nearly 500 basis points year-over-year, with about 400 basis points attributable to an optical UK business model change, while mobility operating income margin remained strong at 7.6%.”

surprises.description: Uber said trailing 12-month free cash flow surpassed $10 billion for the first time, a milestone the preview did not mention or set an expectation for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month free cash flow surpassed $10 billion for the first time in company history.”

surprises.description: The preview asked for buyback plans but gave no timeline or target. Uber said it had repurchased $3.5 billion of stock year-to-date and plans to rebuild repurchases within months toward a target of 50% of free cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Uber… has bought back $3.5 billion of stock year-to-date, with plans to rebuild share repurchases within months toward its 50%-of-free-cash-flow target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The catalyst checklist asked for “buyback plans.”

surprises.description: Uber reported that only 20% of consumers use both rides and Eats, while cross-platform users are growing 1.5 times faster than single-product users. The preview did not flag these cross-product usage and growth figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Only 20% of consumers use both rides and eats, and cross-platform users are growing 1.5x faster than single-product users.”

surprises.description: Restaurant-level margin was 23.0%, 0.5 percentage point above the 22.5% consensus estimate and at the top of the company’s 22.0%–23.0% range. Record-high beef costs pressured margins, but 60 basis points of labor efficiency partly offset them.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restaurant-level profit margin declined 90 basis points year-over-year to 23.0% of Shack sales,” driven primarily by “record-high beef costs (up mid-teens)” and “partially offset by 60 basis points of labor efficiency.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Restaurant-level margin ~22.5%”; company guidance was “22.0%–23.0%.”

surprises.description: Management kept the full-year adjusted EBITDA and net income ranges, avoiding another cut, but guided to the low end rather than offering an unqualified reaffirmation. Persistent beef inflation and higher fuel and distribution costs were cited as reasons for the cautious outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “guided full-year adjusted EBITDA and net income to the low end of the $225-$235 million range due to persistent beef inflation and higher fuel and distribution costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the key question was whether the company would “reiterate $225–235M or cut again,” and that a reiteration “would be a mild upside surprise.”

surprises.description: Same-Shack sales were 3.5%, above the preview’s 2.5%–3.0% expectation, though an estimated 90-basis-point World Cup benefit put underlying comps around the mid-2% range. Traffic grew 2.0%, countering the preview’s concern that comps might be driven by pricing despite negative traffic.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-Shack sales grew 3.5% (2.0% traffic, 1.5% price mix), but excluding an estimated ~90 basis point World Cup benefit, comps were closer to mid-2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated same-Shack sales of “~+2.5–3.0%” and flagged the concern that the comp could be “all pricing on negative traffic.”

surprises.description: The company said its prior 2025–2027 target of at least 50 basis points of annual restaurant-margin expansion is under review, with that margin goal the main uncertainty. The unit-growth target was not identified as the same concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: The prior three-year targets of “low-teens unit growth and 50+ basis points of annual restaurant margin expansion are under review,” with “the restaurant margin goal being the key uncertainty rather than unit growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “unit-growth moderation” or other strategic changes.

surprises.description: Shake Shack will stop providing quarterly guidance and move to annual-only guidance, a reporting-policy change the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Shake Shack is discontinuing quarterly guidance in favor of annual-only guidance going forward, aligning with industry best practices.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed specific near-term pricing roll-offs and left open the possibility of further price increases as beef costs stayed elevated into July. The preview flagged beef and H2 pricing as issues, but did not anticipate these roll-off details or the possibility of additional increases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 2% of pricing rolls off in August and an additional 1.4% rolls off in December, while beef costs remained elevated into July, leaving open the possibility of further price increases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Beef costs and H2 pricing” as a key issue and noted the concern that pricing-led comps could confirm a “value-war concern.”

surprises.description: Comparable app-channel sales grew nearly 30% and the app exceeded 10% of channel mix; the preview had not provided an app-sales expectation. Management described it as the company’s highest-frequency and most incremental channel.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Comparable app channel sales grew nearly 30% year-over-year and the app now represents just over 10% of channel mix,” and was described as “the highest-frequency and most incremental channel.”
