surprises.description: Other operating expenses rose 80 basis points, partly because of higher delivery commissions, an expense pressure not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Other operating expenses rose 80 basis points partly due to higher delivery commissions.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $417.6 million was close to the approximately $416 million consensus estimate and within the company’s $415–$420 million guidance range.
The company opened 16 company-operated Shacks in Q2, in line with the preview’s estimate, and reaffirmed its expected 60–65 openings for 2026.

surprises.description: Amprius reported Q2 revenue of $34 million, above the preview’s $29.08–$29.30 million consensus by roughly 16–17%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $34 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus” revenue: “$29.08M” or “$29.30M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 27%, beating the preview’s roughly 24% estimate and exceeding the 23–25% range it identified as the key margin debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 27% in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin: Not polled (~24% is an author estimate)” and the key issue was “Gross margin vs. about 24%.”

surprises.description: The company raised its FY2026 revenue floor to at least $140 million from $130 million, whereas the preview described reaffirmation of at least $130 million as the base case and a raise to at least $135 million as the bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 guidance for the second consecutive quarter to at least $140 million revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A reaffirmation is the base case”; the bull scenario called for “FY guide raised to ≥$135M.”

surprises.description: Amprius raised its FY2026 gross-margin target to at least 28%, above the 25% target the preview said management had reaffirmed after Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 guidance … to … at least 28% gross margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management reaffirmed a 25% FY gross margin target.”

surprises.description: The FY2026 net-loss limit is now $10 million or less, less favorable than the preview’s stated company guidance of a net loss below $8 million and no more than $0.06 per share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reiterated 2026 … a net loss of $10 million or less ($0.08 or less per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Company FY26 guidance: “net loss <$8.0M (≤$0.06/share).”

surprises.description: GAAP loss per share was $0.04, one cent worse than the preview’s $0.03 loss estimate; the reported loss included a noncash warrant fair-value adjustment, while adjusted net loss was $3.2 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss narrowed to $5.1 million (negative $0.04 per share) … including a onetime noncash $1.9 million warrant fair-value adjustment; adjusted net loss was $3.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 GAAP EPS consensus: “($0.03).”

surprises.description: Amprius disclosed a new $24 million order from a European drone manufacturer, with deliveries expected over roughly 2.5 quarters; the preview did not identify this order.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Won a new $24 million order from a European drone manufacturer for SA124 SiCore cylindrical cells, expected to be delivered over roughly 2.5 quarters.”

surprises.description: The company announced a three-year Stark Future contract expected to generate at least $100 million through 2029, with shipments beginning early next year; the preview did not anticipate this contract.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Signed a 3-year contract with Barcelona-based Stark Future expected to generate at least $100 million in revenue through 2029, with shipments starting early next year.”

surprises.description: Amprius said its cells are used by half of the 19 drone makers invited to the Fort Carson demonstration, where the Department of War plans to order 60,000 drones from top performers. This shows participation in the defense opportunity, but the call facts do not report an order conversion yet.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Amprius cells are used by half of the 19 drone manufacturers invited to the Department of War's Fort Carson demonstration, after which the DoW plans to order 60,000 drones from top performers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “new US manufacturing partners and defense order conversion” as a catalyst to check.

surprises.description: Cash increased to $74.5 million, consistent with the preview’s desire for stable or rising cash, but the company said the quarter’s increase was funded by warrant and option exercises; the preview had highlighted receivables collection as a possible source of cash support and equity-raise concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ended Q2 with $74.5 million cash and no debt, up $12.2 million in the quarter, funded by $12.3 million from warrant exercises and $4.5 million from option exercises with no ATM program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Stable or rising cash, helped by receivables collection, would ease concern about an equity raise.”

in_line: SiCore was 98% of revenue, broadly consistent with the preview’s report that SiCore was 97% of Q1 product revenue.
FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance above $4 million was reiterated, in line with the preview’s stated company target of at least $4 million.

surprises.description: Azenta reported Q3 revenue of $161 million versus the preview’s $149.2 million consensus, a beat of about 8%; revenue also exceeded company outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 total revenue was $161 million,” exceeding company outlook.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $149.2M (MarketBeat, Jul 28, 2026; TradingKey $149.29M).”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $0.16, above the preview’s roughly $0.11 consensus estimate by $0.05.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $0.16.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | ~$0.11 (MarketBeat $0.1138; TradingKey $0.11).”

surprises.description: Instead of the risk of a further cut or guidance narrowing toward the low end, Azenta raised its FY2026 revenue range to $613–618 million and improved its organic outlook from down 2% to up 1% to flat to up 1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to $613-618 million and improved organic revenue outlook to flat to up 1% (versus prior down 2% to up 1%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any further cut, or a narrowing to the low end, is the main risk”; the base scenario expected the “FY guide narrowed toward $603–610M.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s concern that another weak Multiomics quarter could call its trajectory into question, Multiomics grew 8% overall and North America improved from a mid-teens first-half decline. The recovery was qualified: North America remained below year-ago levels, with some Q3 gains from delayed NIH projects catching up and a $3 million order pulled forward from Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Multiomics growing 8%”; “Multiomics North America improved from a mid-teens decline in the first half but remained below prior-year levels,” partly due to delayed projects catching up and “a $3 million preclinical order pulled forward from Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A second weak quarter would question the December 2025 long-range plan”; “Multiomics trajectory under new leadership.”

surprises.description: Sample Management Solutions grew 9% organically, a stronger segment-level result than the preview’s equipment-decline concern suggested, although the call still cited lower volumes in automated stores and cryogenic systems.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sample Management Solutions growing 9% organically”; its gross-margin decline was “driven by lower volumes” in automated stores and cryogenic systems.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Automated Stores and Cryogenic Systems drove the Q2 organic decline. Order and backlog commentary matters more than revenue.”

surprises.description: The segment margin picture was sharply divergent: Sample Management Solutions gross margin fell 750 basis points to 45.9%, while Multiomics gross margin rose 550 basis points to 46.5%. This adds a pronounced SMS margin deterioration even as Multiomics improved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sample Management Solutions gross margin fell 750 basis points year-over-year to 45.9%”; “Multiomics gross margin improved 550 basis points to 46.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin is where management flagged the problem.”

surprises.description: Q4 organic revenue is now expected to decline at a low-single-digit rate, unlike the preview’s implied Q4 reported revenue range of $161–178 million against $159.2 million a year earlier. The company attributed the organic decline to an unusually difficult comparison with Multiomics’ record Q4 FY2025.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects Q4 organic revenue to decline low single digits due to a tough comparison against Q4 2025, which was Multiomics' highest quarterly revenue in company history.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 at consensus implies Q4 of $161–178M against $159.2M a year ago.”

surprises.description: Azenta activated its buyback, repurchasing about 2.3 million shares for $50 million, after having made no repurchases under the authorization to date.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased approximately 2.3 million shares for $50 million,” with “roughly $200 million available under the buyback authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$250M buyback authorization with zero repurchased to date”; “continued inaction would be notable.”

surprises.description: Azenta completed the B Medical Systems divestiture for about $63 million, including a $35 million short-term vendor loan, and recorded a $6.5 million partial reversal of its held-for-sale valuation allowance—transaction and accounting details not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Completed the B Medical Systems divestiture on July 1 for approximately $63 million ($28 million cash plus a $35 million short-term vendor loan) and recorded a $6.5 million partial reversal of a held-for-sale valuation allowance.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed about $1 million of Q3 automated-stores remediation costs and a $5–6 million expected FY2026 impact, while remediation on the three remaining flagged systems is complete pending final customer testing and acceptance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Automated stores quality remediation cost about $1 million in Q3 with a total fiscal 2026 impact expected between $5-6 million”; remediation on “the 3 remaining flagged systems is complete and awaiting final customer testing and acceptance.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 11.4%, below the 12.3% year-ago comparison but consistent with the preview’s base case that margin would recover while remaining below that comparison; it also rose 610 basis points sequentially.
The company maintained its full-year free-cash-flow improvement outlook of 10–15%, matching the preview’s reported guidance.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue fell 11% year over year, worse than the preview’s roughly 8.2% decline implied by consensus. The call attributed the drop to network revenue down 34%, reduced low-quality paid marketing and weaker demand for larger jobs; U.S. requests fell 6% and leads fell 13%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 11% year-over-year,” driven by “a 34% drop in network revenue,” reduced low-quality paid marketing and a demand shift away from larger jobs; U.S. service requests fell 6% and leads fell 13%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $255.50M” versus Q2 FY2025 actual of $278.22M, “Implies about -8.2% y/y.”

surprises.description: Angi recorded a large, unanticipated non-cash impairment on its U.S. reporting unit. Although it did not affect cash, liquidity or covenants, the charge was triggered by a sustained decline in market capitalization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$235 million non-cash goodwill and trade name impairment charge entirely on its U.S. reporting unit,” triggered by “a sustained decline in market capitalization”; it had “no impact on cash, liquidity, or covenants.”

surprises.description: The large Pro business showed notable momentum that the preview did not discuss: it was growing more than 20% with fewer than 10 sellers deployed, while win rates and capacity per Pro improved. Management also described substantial potential to expand penetration and revenue in this segment.
surprises.fact_evidence: The large Pro segment is “growing more than 20% year-over-year with fewer than 10 sellers deployed,” with plans to reach 30 sellers by year-end. Pro win rates rose roughly 20% year-over-year, average capacity per Pro grew about 13%, and capacity improved from down 13% in Q1 to roughly flat in July. Management estimated roughly $2.5 billion in revenue by matching small-to-midsized penetration, and a longer-term $5 billion opportunity before Pro software and services.

surprises.description: AI progress was further along than the preview’s expectation of beginning agent testing within several weeks: the first Pro agent was already live with dozens of Pros and about 80% retention. Angi also reported profitable ChatGPT ad revenue, an early monetization milestone not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Angi is generating “roughly $3 million revenue run rate on ChatGPT ads at a profit”; its first Pro AI agent, AI Front Desk, “is live with dozens of Pros and about 80% retention.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had targeted first agent testing “within several weeks,” full migration within 12 months, and material revenue acceleration in 2027.

surprises.description: Management gave a more encouraging near-term margin signal than the preview’s cautious framing of the roughly $50 million annual adjusted EBITDA less CapEx figure as only a directional floor: it reaffirmed that target and said July EBITDA margin was already several hundred basis points above Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “reaffirmed its target of approximately $50 million in annual adjusted EBITDA minus CapEx” and stated “July EBITDA margin was already several hundred basis points above Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The CFO framed about “$50M/yr of Adj. EBITDA less capex as a directional floor, not a commitment.”

surprises.description: Angi disclosed a specific shift of about $6 million in Q2 TV spending to higher-ROI channels and expects another comparable reduction in Q3. The preview discussed note repurchases as the live capital-allocation lever, not this marketing-spend reallocation.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “reallocated about $6 million of inefficient TV spend in Q2 to higher-ROI channels and expects to remove a comparable amount in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Further note repurchases at a discount are the live lever.”

in_line: Management did not reinstate guidance, consistent with the preview’s base case of “no guidance reinstated.”
Management continued to target accelerated growth in 2027, consistent with the preview’s expectation of “material revenue acceleration in 2027.”

surprises.description: BioCryst’s total revenue outlook rose to $690–$715 million, well above the previously reaffirmed $635–$660 million range and above the Street’s $669.4 million estimate. The increase was a clear departure from the preview’s expectation that guidance might simply be reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 total revenue guidance to $690-$715 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue FY26: $635–660M”; “FY26 revenue (Street): $669.4M”; the preview said a raise was “the cleanest bull catalyst.”

surprises.description: Quarterly total revenue was far above the preview’s $166–$169 million build: the reported growth included a $55.7 million navenibart license upfront payment that the preview’s build did not anticipate. The preview itself flagged a higher aggregator estimate as an outlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue grew 45% year-over-year on a comparable basis, boosted by $55.7 million recognized from the navenibart European license upfront payment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: ~$166–169M (my build)”; “ORLADEYO consensus plus ~$5–8M other.” The preview called the $183.3 million aggregator figure an “Outlier; not reconcilable.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating profit of $113.2 million greatly exceeded the preview’s estimate of roughly $58–$62 million. The gap was substantially larger than an ordinary quarterly beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company posted a non-GAAP operating profit of $113.2 million for the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating profit: ~$58–62M (my estimate).”

surprises.description: ORLADEYO revenue was $158.2 million, slightly below the $161 million consensus and below the preview’s $165 million catalyst threshold, although it fell within the preview’s $158–$164 million base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ORLADEYO revenue reached $158.2 million in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ORLADEYO net revenue: $161M”; the catalyst checklist called for “ORLADEYO at or above $165M.” The base case was “$158–164M.”

surprises.description: Pediatric pellets had already generated 47 prescriptions by July 31, exceeding the company’s expected total for all of 2026. The preview anticipated availability around early August but did not suggest this level of early uptake.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ORLADEYO pediatric pellets received 47 prescriptions through July 31, already exceeding the total expected for all of 2026, with several prescriptions coming from physicians new to prescribing ORLADEYO.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pediatric ORLADEYO pellets were slated for early August availability after a manufacturing delay.”

surprises.description: Management said new injectable competitors were mainly taking share from older injectables such as TAKHZYRO rather than from ORLADEYO. That was reassuring relative to the preview’s focus on possible competitive erosion and patient-start trends.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management indicated new injectable competitors are primarily displacing older injectables like TAKHZYRO rather than ORLADEYO.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Competitive erosion. Twelve approved HAE therapies now exist, including KalVista's EKTERLY and CSL's Andembry. Watch new patient starts, persistence”; the preview also flagged competitive erosion as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: The ALPHA-ORBIT trial completed enrollment ahead of schedule and was described as the largest blinded HAE trial ever and already overpowered. The preview expected Q3 2027 top-line data but did not flag accelerated enrollment or the trial’s scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enrollment for the pivotal ALPHA-ORBIT navenibart trial was completed ahead of schedule as the largest blinded HAE trial ever, with top-line data expected in Q3 2027 and the study already overpowered.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Navenibart topline data is expected Q3 2027.”

surprises.description: BioCryst reported positive cash flow even excluding the license upfront payment and ended the quarter with more than $350 million in cash. The preview highlighted the balance sheet and obligations but did not forecast this level of cash or underlying cash generation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended with just over $350 million in cash, generating positive cash flow even excluding the license upfront payment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited prior-quarter cash of “$259M ($331M pro forma with the $70M Neopharmed upfront)” and flagged the balance sheet and obligations for attention.

surprises.description: Paid reimbursement reached 84%, up from 83% a year earlier and close to the stated 85% long-term target. That was a favorable datapoint on the paid-conversion issue the preview said to monitor, though the preview gave no specific expected rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The paid reimbursement rate for ORLADEYO improved to 84% from 83% a year prior, with a long-term target of 85% and typical seasonal declines of 1-2 points expected in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Competitive erosion” section: “Watch new patient starts, persistence”; catalyst checklist: “Competitive datapoints: patient starts, persistence, and paid conversion.”

surprises.description: Management introduced flexibility to use excess cash flow for business development, debt reduction, and/or buybacks. The preview called for capital-structure commentary, but did not anticipate buybacks or this range of possible uses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management ... signaled flexibility to pursue business development, debt reduction, and/or buybacks with excess cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Capital structure commentary on the $395M term loan and $447.5M royalty obligation.”

surprises.description: BioCryst also gave an update on its Netherton syndrome program: the BCX17725 proof-of-concept trial remained on track for 12 patients, with early Part 4 clinical data expected by year-end. This program and its update were not addressed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The BCX17725 Netherton syndrome proof-of-concept trial is on track to reach 12 patients with early Part 4 clinical data expected by year-end, targeting a market with no approved therapies.”

in_line: ORLADEYO full-year revenue guidance remained $625–$645 million, as previously stated in the preview, despite the pediatric launch delay.
The non-GAAP operating cost range of $420–$440 million was already the guidance cited in the preview after the June update.
Navenibart top-line data remained expected in Q3 2027, as the preview anticipated.

surprises.description: CDW reported $6.6B of Q2 sales, up 10%, well above the preview’s $6.21B–$6.26B consensus range and expected 3.8%–4.7% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales of $6.6 billion (up 10%).”

surprises.description: CDW raised its full-year outlook: gross profit growth is now expected in the mid-single digits, and non-GAAP EPS growth at the high end of high-single digits. The preview’s prior outlook was low-to-mid-single-digit gross profit growth and EPS growth at the high end of mid-single digits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year guidance, now expecting mid-single-digit gross profit growth [and] high-end high-single-digit non-GAAP EPS growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross profit growth of low-to-mid single digits” and “Non-GAAP EPS growth at the high end of mid single digits.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin fell to 20.1%, materially below the preview’s derived 20.6%–20.9% expectation and below its 20.5% concern threshold. CDW attributed the decline to large enterprise hardware deals and a lower services mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin declined 70 basis points year-over-year to 20.1%, driven by mix shift toward large enterprise hardware infrastructure deals and lower relative services contribution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~20.6% to 20.9% (derived) | flat to -20bps”; “A gross margin below about 20.5% would be a problem.”

surprises.description: Despite the full-year gross profit outlook being raised, CDW now expects 2026 gross margin modestly below 2025, with second-half margin below the second half of 2025. That is weaker than the prior expectation of gross margin approximately in line with 2025.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 gross margin is expected to be modestly below 2025, with second-half gross margins projected below second-half 2025 levels due to product and end-market mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin approximately in line with 2025.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $2.91, above the $2.80 consensus and the $2.79–$2.83 range implied by the prior high-single-digit growth guidance. EPS growth also outpaced gross profit growth, indicating a better operating-leverage trend than the preview’s Q1 comparison suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $2.91 (up 11.9%)”; “Non-GAAP EPS growth of 11.9% and operating income growth of 7% both exceeded gross profit growth of 6.3%, signaling an inflection toward improved operating leverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | $2.80”; “Non-GAAP EPS: high single-digit YoY growth, which is $2.79 to $2.83”; Q1 had “SG&A [that] rose 7.0% against gross profit growth of 6.0%, a negative operating-leverage spread.”

surprises.description: First-half adjusted free-cash-flow conversion was only 42% of non-GAAP net income, substantially below the stated 80%–90% target. Management tied the shortfall to roughly $400M of inventory growth and expects it to normalize by year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half adjusted free cash flow was $278 million (42% of non-GAAP net income), well below the 80-90% target, driven by a roughly $400 million inventory increase that management expects to normalize by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Well below the 80-90% target.”

surprises.description: Services revenue grew only 1%, with deployment timing and customers prioritizing hardware and cloud holding it back. The preview did not flag this expected weakness; management now anticipates a catch-up beginning around year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Services revenue grew only 1% due to deployment timing and customer prioritization of hardware and cloud, though management expects a services catch-up beginning around year-end.”

surprises.description: CFO Al Miralles announced plans to retire in 2027, with a successor search underway. The preview did not mention an impending CFO transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Al Miralles announced plans to retire in 2027 after completion of an orderly transition, with a search for his successor currently underway.”

in_line: Gross profit was about $1.3B, within the preview’s derived $1.29B–$1.31B range; its 6.3% growth was consistent with the prior mid-single-digit gross profit growth guidance.

surprises.description: Astec cut FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $160–175 million from $170–190 million, rather than reaffirming the prior range as the preview’s base case anticipated. Management attributed the reduction mainly to asphalt plant deliveries moving into Q4 2026 and Q1 2027, and said it expects roughly one-third of second-half EBITDA in Q3 and two-thirds in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Astec cut its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance from $170M-$190M to $160M-$175M,” primarily because “asphalt plant deliveries” are “shifting to Q4 2026 and Q1 2027”; second-half adjusted EBITDA is expected to be “roughly one-third in Q3 and two-thirds in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY26 guide was “$170–190M (reaffirmed at Q1)” and its base scenario expected “FY guide reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.94, below the preview’s $1.05 consensus estimate, though close to the author’s lower $0.95 estimate. This was a meaningful miss against consensus despite year-over-year EPS growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $0.94 versus $0.90 a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Adj. EPS” consensus of “$1.05” and the author’s estimate of “$0.95.”

surprises.description: Infrastructure Solutions margin moved in the opposite direction from the recovery the preview said would validate the thesis: it compressed by 130 basis points, rather than returning toward 17–18%. Management pointed to a mix shift toward lower-margin mobile paving equipment.
surprises.fact_evidence: Infrastructure Solutions margin “compressed 130 basis points due to an unfavorable mix shift toward lower-margin mobile paving equipment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a return toward “17–18% would signal pricing has caught up to tariffs” and identified “recovery to 17%+” as a key catalyst.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA and margin came in a little below the preview’s central expectations: $42.6 million and 10.4%, versus the $44–47 million estimate and roughly 11.0% margin estimate. The result was close to the author’s $43 million EBITDA estimate, but did not meet the consensus-derived margin hurdle.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA was “$42.6 million (up 26%)” and adjusted EBITDA margin was “10.4%,” up 20 basis points year over year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adj. EBITDA ~$44–47M” and “Adj. EBITDA margin ~11.0%”; its own EBITDA estimate was “$43M.”

surprises.description: Material Solutions delivered strong sales and profit growth, with margin expansion, but the preview did not set a Q2 segment forecast against which to measure the result. The reported performance is a notable positive in a quarter when Infrastructure Solutions margins weakened.
surprises.fact_evidence: Material Solutions net sales “jumped 43% to $179.8 million,” adjusted EBITDA rose “54.5% to $22.1 million,” and margins expanded “90 basis points to 12.3%.”

surprises.description: Parts and service revenue was a substantial strength that the preview did not forecast: it grew 34.8% and accounted for about one-third of quarterly sales. This provides a significant source of revenue beyond equipment deliveries, though the preview supplied no comparison estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Parts and service revenue “grew 34.8% to $135.5 million,” reaching “33.2% of net sales in the quarter and 35% year-to-date.”

surprises.description: The proposed highway legislation had more favorable core funding provisions than the preview’s general discussion of reauthorization timing conveyed: despite a smaller headline figure, it would increase core highway funding and the guaranteed formula-funded share. The near-term outlook remains constrained because management said a continuing resolution appears more likely.
surprises.fact_evidence: The proposed Build America 250 Act has a “$580 billion headline” but raises core highway funding “~7% ($351B to $376B)” and the guaranteed formula-funded share from “87% to 90%”; “only a continuing resolution appears likely near-term.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called reauthorization timing and potential order deferrals a “swing factor” and noted the Surface Transportation Bill expires September 30, 2026.

surprises.description: Backlog rose substantially from the Q1 exit and was much larger year over year, while the preview had flagged sequential backlog growth and book-to-bill of at least 1.0 as important tests. The reported increase is positive, although the call facts do not provide a book-to-bill figure to directly check against that threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: Backlog “surged 57.9% year-over-year to $601.1 million,” including Material Solutions backlog growth of “150.6% from organic and inorganic sources.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “sequential change from the $549.2M Q1 exit and book-to-bill of 1.0 or better.”

in_line: Q2 net sales were broadly in line with expectations: $408.1 million versus the preview’s $405.5 million consensus and $402 million author estimate.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.38, well below the preview’s $0.46–$0.49 consensus range. The preview expected EPS to benefit from normalization of Q1 SG&A costs, but the reported result was a clear miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EPS was $0.38”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $0.46–$0.49”

surprises.description: Archrock cut the top of its FY26 adjusted EBITDA range by $30 million, from $915 million to $885 million, rather than raising or reaffirming the range. The preview identified a trim as a bear-case outcome, although it also described narrowing toward the upper half as the base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered the top end of its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $865-$885 million from the prior $865-$915 million,” citing “lube oil and make-ready cost pressures, AMS customer deferrals, and higher stock-driven incentive compensation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Narrowing to the upper half is the base case”; the bear scenario included guidance “trimmed.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $213 million, below the preview’s estimated $222–$226 million. That is a shortfall of roughly $9–$13 million against an estimate the preview noted was not polled consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $213 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$222–226M” (author estimate, not polled consensus).

surprises.description: Contract operations margin was 71%, one percentage point below the 72% level the preview highlighted, and management expects about 70% in the second half despite cost headwinds. That is weaker than the preview’s base-case expectation that margins hold at 72% or higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Contract operations delivered 94.4% utilization and a seventh consecutive quarter of adjusted gross margin above 70% at 71%, with management guiding to around 70% margins in the second half despite cost headwinds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Contract operations adj. gross margin vs. 72%”; the base scenario assumed “Contract ops margin holds at 72% or higher.”

surprises.description: Aftermarket services revenue fell to $42 million from $65 million a year earlier as customers deferred major maintenance amid high crude prices. The preview did not flag this segment decline, though the segment’s adjusted gross margin improved from 23% to 24%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aftermarket services revenue fell to $42 million from $65 million a year ago as customers deferred major maintenance amid high crude prices, though segment adjusted gross margin improved to 24% from 23%.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a $1.4–$1.6 billion growth-capital plan for 2027–2030, implying annual spending 40–45% above 2026 and adding roughly 1 million horsepower. The preview was focused on growth capex and contract coverage, but did not anticipate this multiyear spending framework; it also leaves the share of 2027 horsepower already contracted unspecified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A long-term capital allocation framework targeting $1.4-$1.6 billion of cumulative growth capital from 2027-2030 to add roughly 1 million new horsepower, implying roughly a 40-45% increase in average annual spend versus 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The key disclosure is what share of 2027 newbuild horsepower is already contracted”; the preview also noted the company was “committing capital ahead of contracts.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for visible buyback acceleration, but the reported capital-return details were a 25%–35% operating-cash-flow return target and $113 million of remaining authorization, without a stated acceleration in repurchases. This leaves the specific buyback shift the preview was watching unconfirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Archrock plans to return 25%-35% of operating cash flow to shareholders and retains $113 million of remaining share buyback authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The market is looking for buyback acceleration rather than more ‘dry powder’ language”; a “visible buyback acceleration would be a real narrative shift.”

surprises.description: Operating horsepower was 4.5 million, down from 4.7 million a year earlier, largely because the company sold about 165,000 nonstrategic horsepower. The preview did not flag this fleet reduction as an expected development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating horsepower declined to 4.5 million from 4.7 million year-over-year largely due to the sale of ~165,000 nonstrategic horsepower.”

surprises.description: Caterpillar engine lead times were nearly 200 weeks, longer than the roughly 160 weeks cited in the preview, with orders now placed for 2029 delivery. The extended timeline is a more pronounced supply constraint than the preview described.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Caterpillar engine lead times remain extended at nearly 200 weeks with orders now placed for 2029 delivery.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With Caterpillar lead times near 160 weeks…”

surprises.description: Archrock signed an eight-year contract, with a two-year extension option, covering about 665,000 horsepower for midstream applications. The preview sought disclosure about 2027 newbuild contracting but did not anticipate this specific long-term contract; the reported facts do not say what portion, if any, represents 2027 newbuild coverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Signed an 8-year long-term contract (with a 2-year extension option) with an existing strategic customer covering approximately 665,000 horsepower for midstream applications.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The key disclosure is what share of 2027 newbuild horsepower is already contracted.”

surprises.description: All three rating agencies had positive outlooks after Moody’s and S&P revisions, a favorable credit-development disclosure not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “All three rating agencies now have positive outlooks after Moody's and S&P revisions.”

in_line: The quarterly dividend was raised to $0.23; the preview had already noted the July increase to $0.23.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $26.2 million, slightly above the company’s $26.0 million guidance ceiling and the preview’s $24.39 million consensus estimate. The beat was modest rather than a major departure from expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $26.2 million,” coming in “slightly above the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Company guidance (Q2) | $22.0M – $26.0M | Consensus | $24.39M”

surprises.description: The company reported a broader covenant problem than the preview’s cash-shortfall scenario: it also breached the minimum direct-margin covenant, and all credit-agreement borrowings were classified as current liabilities. Waivers mean the debt is not callable, but the additional breach and accounting consequence were not flagged in the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with only $11.2 million in cash, falling below its $15 million minimum unrestricted cash covenant, and also breached its minimum direct margin covenant, requiring lender waivers.” “All outstanding credit-agreement borrowings were reclassified as current liabilities as of June 30th, though waivers meant the debt is not callable.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base | ... Cash short of $15M but paired with a waiver.” The preview also noted that “First covenant tests” begin with Q2.

surprises.description: The preview highlighted the difficulty of generating roughly $96–100 million in second-half revenue, but FTC Solar said about 80% of that revenue is already covered by booked projects in execution, with further decisions that could take coverage above 100%. That provides more visibility into the demanding H2 target than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “About 80% of second-half revenue is already covered by booked projects in execution, with additional decisions expected that could push coverage above 100%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 was $17.3M and Q2 is guided to $22–26M, so H2 would need roughly $96–100M, far above the best quarter on record ($32.9M in Q4 2025).”

surprises.description: FTC Solar secured a new $20 million equity line of credit, a financing source the preview had identified as a possibility but not as an expected transaction. It had not been used as of the call, so it offers potential liquidity support but also introduces possible equity dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company secured a $20 million equity line of credit (ELOC) with an institutional investor to bolster liquidity, though it has not yet been utilized.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Financing and dilution. Any new financing or reversal of the ATM termination plan.”

surprises.description: The company reported sizable new customer orders, including a 400 MW purchase order involving a top-five EPC and developer and a first-time approximately 100 MW 1P order from an existing 2P customer. The preview raised backlog and bookings as issues to watch but did not anticipate these specific wins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FTC received a new 400 MW purchase order from a top-five EPC for a top-five developer, plus a first-time ~100 MW 1P order from an existing 2P East Coast customer.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Backlog and bookings. $543M contracted backlog at Q1, plus timing on a 1 GW safe-harbor award.”

surprises.description: FTC Solar said it had entered India with multiple wins and secured new Australian projects, including a project of more than 330 MW beginning deliveries in H2. These geographic entries and awards were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has entered India with multiple wins up to 100+ MW and secured new Australian projects (~90 MW plus a 330+ MW project starting deliveries in H2).”

in_line: FTC Solar reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance of at least 40%, in line with the preview’s expectation that the roughly 40% target would be reiterated.
Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss of $9.8 million was within the company’s previewed Q2 guidance range of $10.5 million to $7.4 million in losses.

Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was negative at -5.1%, within the previewed guidance range of -6.4% to +4.0%; the preview described a positive print as a possible sign of improvement, not as a guaranteed outcome.
The cash balance fell below the $15 million covenant, but lender waivers were obtained, matching the preview’s base-case scenario of cash below the threshold paired with a waiver.

surprises.description: BrightView cut FY2026 adjusted free cash flow guidance to $70–$80 million from $100–$115 million, citing fuel and self-insurance impacts. The preview had flagged the existing FCF target as vulnerable, but this was a substantial reduction from the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow guidance was cut to $70-$80 million from the prior $100-$115 million due to fuel and self-insurance impacts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. FCF: $100–115M”; the preview also said “a weak Q3 cash number makes the FCF guide the next thing to fall.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was $718 million, about $8 million below the $726.1 million consensus, and grew only 1.3% rather than the expected roughly 2.5%. Land Maintenance growth was partly offset by lower snow revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 total revenue rose 1.3% to $718 million, driven by Land Maintenance growth partially offset by lower snow revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $726.1M”; “Implied Y/Y | +2.5%.”

surprises.description: Reported adjusted EBITDA of $96 million was well below the preview’s roughly $115–$120 million estimate. However, excluding the $16 million self-insurance adjustment and $4 million fuel headwind, EBITDA would have been $116 million, within the expected range; management said the insurance charge largely reflected older claims and should not recur.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported adjusted EBITDA was $96 million”; excluding “a $16 million self-insurance adjustment and $4 million fuel headwind,” it “would have been $116 million.” The charge was “largely tied to adverse development of 2023-and-prior claims,” and management said it “should not recur.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$115–120M (derived).”

surprises.description: BrightView guided to Q4 Land growth of 3%–6%, above the 2%–3% full-year Land growth range the preview highlighted. Ancillary revenue is the key swing variable, so the upper end depends on that contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Guides Q4 Land growth of 3%-6%, with ancillary being the key swing variable.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “Land maintenance organic growth” guidance of “+2–3%” and said Q3 was the clean read on whether the growth inflection was real.

surprises.description: Customer retention and frontline turnover both improved substantially: retention rose about 250 basis points year over year, while turnover fell about 7 percentage points. The preview discussed the Land growth inflection but did not flag these workforce and customer metrics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customer retention improved about 250 bps year-over-year to 84.6%, and frontline turnover declined about 7 percentage points.”

surprises.description: The Land contract book showed sustained improvement, growing 4% since the second half of 2025 and improving 100 basis points sequentially, with five consecutive quarters of net new business growth. The preview focused on whether Land revenue growth would continue, but did not anticipate these contract-book details.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The land contract book has grown 4% since the second half of 2025 (a 100 bps improvement sequentially), marking five consecutive quarters of net new business growth.”

surprises.description: BrightView reported adding 200 net sellers since the end of 2024 and increasing new contract sales about 20% year to date, alongside $4 million of Q3 and $16 million of year-to-date sales investment costs. The preview did not discuss these Land sales-force investments or their costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Added a net 200 sellers since end of 2024 (toward a 500 target), lifting new contract sales ~20% year-to-date,” with sales investments costing “$4 million (60 bps) in Q3 and $16 million (80 bps) year-to-date.”

in_line: Q3 Land Maintenance revenue grew 2.3%, within the preview’s 2%–3% FY growth guidance range; it was the second consecutive quarter of organic growth, consistent with the preview’s stated return-to-growth watchpoint.
FY2026 total revenue guidance was effectively maintained: the new $2.75–$2.78 billion range has a midpoint close to the prior $2.745–$2.795 billion range.
Fuel was flagged in the preview as a likely EBITDA pressure point. The call quantified a $4 million headwind and said efficiency measures and hedging mitigated roughly $2 million of it.

surprises.description: Eos reported adjusted gross margin of negative 52%, substantially less negative than the preview’s pre-released gross-margin range of negative 69% to negative 73%. The comparison is not fully like-for-like because the call figure is adjusted, a definition issue the preview had flagged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin was negative 52% and product adjusted gross margin improved to negative 40%,” with “the seventh consecutive quarter of gross margin improvement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | -69% to -73%” in the pre-released Q2 figures.

surprises.description: The FY26 revenue range was narrowed to $300–350 million: its $300 million floor matched the preview’s expected low end, but the $350 million ceiling was above the preview’s illustrative $300–330 million narrowing. Management said the reduction from the prior $300–400 million range reflects manufacturing consolidation, not an operating shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Eos tightened its 2026 revenue guidance to $300-350 million” and framed the reduction as “a strategic manufacturing consolidation decision rather than an operating shortfall.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A narrowing to about $300–330M would be in line”; the prior company range was “$300–400M (stale range).”

surprises.description: The call disclosed substantial concentration in one Frontier Power-related entity: it accounted for roughly 80% of Q2 revenue and now represents about half of backlog. The preview discussed Frontier funding and pipeline but did not flag this degree of revenue and backlog dependence.
surprises.fact_evidence: “One Frontier Power-related project accounted for roughly 80% of Q2 revenue,” and “roughly 50% of backlog now derives from that single affiliated entity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Cash and Frontier funding” and “Frontier's first project pipeline,” but did not state an expectation about customer concentration.

surprises.description: Eos gave a quantified manufacturing-consolidation plan with a short stated payback, while acknowledging it reduces near-term revenue at the top of the guidance range. The preview anticipated a guide update but did not describe this facility move or its expected cost savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidating Line 1 into the Thorn Hill facility is expected to deliver an additional 10-15% reduction in conversion costs with an estimated payback period of approximately 9 months,” while “temporarily sacrific[ing] near-term revenue at the top of guidance.”

surprises.description: The call put a very large pipeline beside a much smaller backlog and identified conversion, rather than origination, as the main challenge. The preview did not provide a pipeline estimate or identify this as the central commercial bottleneck.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pipeline grew to $24.6 billion (nearly 112 GWh), up 31% year-over-year,” versus “a backlog of $807 million,” with management “framing conversion rather than origination as the key challenge.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $68.8 million matched the preview’s pre-released $68–69 million range and $68.77 million consensus estimate.
The $807 million backlog and approximately $364 million of cash were already included in the preview’s pre-released figures.

Adjusted EBITDA loss of $71.4 million was worse than Q1’s $68 million loss, but broadly fit the preview’s view that sequential improvement was uncertain; the preview said a result better than $65 million would be a positive surprise.

surprises.description: Cencora’s adjusted operating income grew 17%, above the company’s 12%–14% growth guidance cited in the preview. That was a meaningful operational beat against the stated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income grew 17% to $1.2 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted operating income growth: 12–14%.”

surprises.description: U.S. Healthcare Solutions operating income rose 16% to $966 million, topping the preview’s roughly $941 million estimate. The growth also accelerated from 7% last quarter and remained double-digit organically excluding One Oncology and the lost oncology customer.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. Healthcare Solutions operating income grew 16% to $966 million, delivering double-digit organic growth even when excluding One Oncology and the lost oncology customer, a sharp acceleration from 7% last quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “U.S. Healthcare Solutions operating income: $940.9M”; the preview said “a result of $960M or more would de-risk the Q4 ramp.”

surprises.description: International Healthcare Solutions operating income rose 21% as reported, far above the preview’s expectation of about 1.4% growth. The call attributed some of the strength to favorable timing of manufacturer price adjustments, so the reported pace may not be fully recurring.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International Healthcare Solutions operating income rose 21% as-reported (23% constant currency) to $166 million, aided by favorable manufacturer price adjustment timing in a developing market country.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “International Healthcare operating income: consensus is only +1.4% against a weak prior-year comp.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EPS grew 12%, ahead of the roughly 9.3% growth implied by the preview’s $4.37 consensus estimate versus the $4.00 prior-year result. The call said $1 billion of opportunistic repurchases supported the quarter’s EPS growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 adjusted EPS grew 12%, supported by $1 billion of opportunistic share repurchases executed at an average price of $268 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS: $4.37”; the preview listed “Q3 FY25 Actual” of “$4.00.”

surprises.description: Management said a mid-fiscal-year close of the MWI/Covetrus merger would create a roughly $0.35 EPS headwind in fiscal 2027. The preview discussed deal timing and regulatory scrutiny, but did not flag this specific future earnings burden.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A mid-fiscal-year MWI/Covetrus merger close would create a ~$150 million operating income headwind, netting to roughly a $0.35 EPS headwind, as a modeling consideration for fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Cencora “does not assume a close before its September fiscal year-end” and identified deal timing as a live Q&A topic.

surprises.description: Cencora said U.S. revenue would land in the lower half of its 4%–6% growth range, a softer outlook than simply maintaining the range cited in the preview. The preview did not provide a specific expectation for where within that range U.S. growth would fall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided U.S. revenue to the lower half of the 4%-6% growth range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue growth: 4–6%.”

surprises.description: Despite lowering its own International revenue growth outlook because of the stronger dollar, management’s approximately 8% growth expectation was well above the preview’s segment consensus, which implied roughly flat revenue. The preview cautioned that segment estimates might be stale, tempering the comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management ... lowered International revenue growth expectations to approximately 8% (7% constant currency) due to a stronger dollar.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “International Healthcare revenue: $7.79B” versus “Q3 FY25 Actual” of “$7.8B” and “YoY” of “~0%.”

surprises.description: Gross profit margin expanded 61 basis points to 4.16%, largely because of the One Oncology acquisition. The preview highlighted uncertainty about One Oncology’s contribution but did not anticipate this margin expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit margin expanding 61 basis points to 4.16%, largely driven by the One Oncology acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called this “the first clean quarter” for OneOncology and said to “look for a quantified number and integration commentary”; it gave no margin expectation.

surprises.description: Cencora lowered its International revenue growth outlook to about 8% (7% constant currency) because of the stronger dollar. The preview supplied no company International revenue growth guidance, so the change itself cannot be measured against a prior previewed company outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management ... lowered International revenue growth expectations to approximately 8% (7% constant currency) due to a stronger dollar.”

in_line: Consolidated revenue of $84.8 billion was essentially in line with the preview’s $84.89 billion consensus.
The fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS guidance moved up modestly, as the preview’s base case anticipated: the range rose from $17.70–$17.90 to $17.75–$17.95.

surprises.description: Total segment operating income grew 21%, above the preview's roughly 15% growth expectation and exceeding the company’s prior guidance. The reported revenue growth was 7%, slightly below the preview’s 7.5% consensus growth estimate, although it exceeded company guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total segment operating income grew 21% and total company revenue rose 7% in fiscal Q3, exceeding the company's prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total segment OI… ~$5.3B… ~+15%”; revenue consensus was “$25.4–25.5B” versus “$23.65B” a year earlier, or “+7.5%.”

surprises.description: Experiences delivered record Q3 revenue, operating income, and margin, while domestic attendance turned positive and guests and per-capita spending also grew. The preview expected improved attendance, but framed a positive attendance result as the bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Disney Experiences delivered record fiscal Q3 revenue of $10 billion, up 10% year-over-year, with record segment operating income and margin”; “Domestic parks saw 3% attendance growth and 4% per capita spending growth, while global guests rose 4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Turning positive would be a bull datapoint”; the base case expected attendance to be “improved” without turning positive.

surprises.description: Q3 SVOD operating margin reached 13%, above the preview’s full-year minimum-margin expectation of at least 10%. The company remained on track for double-digit streaming margins for FY26.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Disney delivered a 13% SVOD operating margin in fiscal Q3 and remains on track for double-digit streaming margins in fiscal 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had committed to “at least 10%” Entertainment SVOD margin for full-year FY26.

surprises.description: Disney raised its FY26 share-repurchase plan to at least $9 billion, above the preview’s expectation of at least $8 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Share repurchases for fiscal 2026 were raised from an initial ~$7 billion to at least $9 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 buybacks of “at least $8B.”

surprises.description: Experiences FY26 operating-income guidance was raised to the high end of the previously provided high-single-digit growth range. The preview did not specify an Experiences outlook, so this is an upward revision rather than a comparison with a stated preview forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Experiences segment OI guidance was raised to the high end of the previously provided high-single-digit growth for fiscal 2026.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a substantial investment plan now, despite the preview’s expectation that capacity and capital-expenditure questions might be deferred until D23. The plan includes $9 billion of Experiences CapEx in FY26 and a $60 billion, 10-year parks investment cycle.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans… $9 billion in Experiences CapEx in fiscal 2026 as part of a $60 billion 10-year parks investment cycle.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “may defer capacity and capex questions” to D23 Expo.

surprises.description: Some titles, including The Mandalorian and Grogu and live-action Moana, underperformed, a negative content result not anticipated in the preview. Management nevertheless reaffirmed its adjusted EPS growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management reaffirmed double-digit adjusted EPS growth “despite underperformance from titles like The Mandalorian and Grogu and live-action Moana.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call described the titles as having “underperformance.”

surprises.description: A roughly $100 million tariff refund boosted Experiences operating income in the quarter, but the benefit was temporary: the full-year tariff impact was expected to net to essentially zero and did not drive the raised guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately $100 million in tariff refunds hit Experiences segment OI in the quarter, but the full-year tariff impact nets to essentially zero and did not drive the raised guidance.”

surprises.description: Upfront advertising commitments were strong, with total volume up double digits and sports volumes up low teens, and Super Bowl inventory sold out. The preview did not identify this advertising demand as an expectation to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Upfront advertising showed total volume commitments up double digits and sports volumes up low teens with Super Bowl inventory sold out.”

surprises.description: Despite strong upfront volume commitments, SVOD advertising pricing faced pressure from rising streaming supply, an unfavorable development not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SVOD ad pricing faced pressure from rising streaming supply.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed double-digit adjusted EPS growth for FY26 and FY27, consistent with the preview’s expectation of approximately 12% FY26 growth and double-digit FY27 growth.
Disney remained on track for double-digit FY26 streaming margins, consistent with the preview’s expectation of at least 10% for the full year.

surprises.description: Revenue was well above the preview’s $453.9M–$457.7M consensus range: Griffon reported $481M, with 7% organic growth rather than the preview’s roughly flat like-for-like base case. The preview expected price/mix gains but modeled residential volume declines; reported volume instead grew 1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue grew 7% organically to $481 million, driven by 6% favorable price/mix and 1% volume growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $453.9M (alt. feed $457.7M)” and “Base: $452M to $458M (~flat LFL)”; the preview also expected “Volume -5% to -6%, price/mix +5%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS came in above both the $1.33 consensus and the preview’s estimated $1.38–$1.42 buy-side bar, reaching $1.51. It also exceeded the preview’s $1.45+ bull-scenario threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income from continuing operations was $68 million, or $1.51 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $1.33”; “I estimate roughly $1.38 to $1.42”; Bull scenario: “$1.45+.”

surprises.description: Despite the revenue beat, profitability fell short of the preview’s margin hurdle: adjusted EBITDA margin was 25.9%, below the roughly 27.2% second-half margin needed for the year and the preview’s Q3 catalyst of about 27.5%. The call attributed the limited EBITDA growth to higher material and SG&A costs, and gross margin declined year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 adjusted EBITDA rose only 2% to $125 million as increased material and SG&A costs offset revenue gains, and EBITDA margin was 25.9%”; “Gross margin declined to 47% from 48.7% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Reaching $458M for the year requires about $251M in 2H on roughly $924M of revenue, a margin near 27.2%”; catalyst: “Adj. EBITDA margin at or above ~27.5%.”

surprises.description: Fiscal 2026 interest expense guidance was reduced by $13M, from the preview’s $93M figure to $80M, a better outcome than the preview’s existing guidance implied. The company attributed the reduction to debt repayment and interest income from transaction PIK notes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 interest expense guidance was cut by $13 million to $80 million due to debt paydown and interest income from transaction PIK notes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 company guidance … interest expense $93M”; the preview also asked, “Ask whether guidance includes” the non-cash interest income from PIK notes.

in_line: Griffon maintained full-year guidance of $1.8B in revenue and $458M in adjusted EBITDA, as the preview identified reaffirmation at those levels as the base case.
Q3 adjusted EBITDA of $125M was within the preview’s $125M–$129M base-case range, even though the margin was below its stated hurdle.
The Australasia joint venture closing and its $181M cash, $49M note, and 49% retained equity interest matched the transaction terms already described in the preview.

surprises.description: GXO reported $3.4 billion of Q2 revenue, below the preview’s roughly $3.45–$3.46 billion consensus, and organic growth was 3.4%. That was weaker than the 4.6%–4.7% year-over-year revenue growth implied by consensus and below the 4%–5% full-year organic-growth range investors were watching.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $3.4 billion, up 4% year-over-year and 3.4% organically.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$3.45–3.46B | +4.6%–4.7%” and “Watch whether Q2 lands at the high or low end” of the 4%–5% full-year organic growth range.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.59 slightly exceeded the $0.58 consensus estimate. The beat was small, rather than a substantial upside surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS of $0.59.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS | $0.58.”

surprises.description: New business wins were notably stronger than the preview’s Q1 reference point: GXO reported $410 million in Q2, up more than 30% year over year and its strongest commercial quarter in three years, versus the $227 million of Q1 wins cited in the preview. The preview expected a comparable Q2 disclosure but did not anticipate this level of momentum.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New business wins reached $410 million in Q2, up more than 30% year-over-year, marking the company's strongest commercial quarter in three years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 cited a record $2.7B pipeline and $227M of new annualized contract wins. A comparable disclosure is likely in Q2.”

surprises.description: Management outlined a margin improvement trajectory that the preview did not identify: expansion in the second half of 2026 accelerating into 2027, with an EBIT-margin target above 6% compared with the current 3.5%–4%. Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin itself was flat year over year, so the surprise is the forward outlook rather than current-quarter expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin held flat at 6.4% versus a year ago, but management guided to margin expansion in the back half of 2026 accelerating into 2027, targeting EBIT margin above 6% from the current 3.5%-4%.”

surprises.description: GXO said it resumed share repurchases, buying back $21 million year to date and leaving approximately $280 million under authorization. The preview did not anticipate a resumption of buybacks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company resumed share repurchases, buying back $21 million year-to-date with approximately $280 million remaining under authorization, citing an undervalued stock.”

surprises.description: North American commercial indicators were particularly strong, with pipeline up 34% year over year, first-half wins up 85%, and strategic-vertical wins nearly three times last year’s pace. The preview discussed company-wide wins and pipeline, but did not flag this regional acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North America, cited as the largest growth opportunity, saw Q2 pipeline up 34% year-over-year and first-half wins up 85%, while strategic vertical wins ran at nearly 3x last year's pace.”

in_line: FY2026 organic revenue growth guidance remained 4%–5%, and the EBITDA and EPS guidance midpoints were unchanged from the prior ranges, consistent with the preview’s base case of a held outlook. The ranges were narrowed.
The sales pipeline remained at a record $2.7 billion, consistent with the preview’s reference to a record $2.7 billion Q1 pipeline.

surprises.description: Q2 collaboration revenue was $65 million, above the preview’s roughly $48–55 million base case for the Gilead fee, because Kymera also reported a $20 million Sanofi milestone for KT-485 entering Phase I. The call said no additional revenue is expected for the rest of 2026, so the higher quarter was milestone-driven rather than an indication of continuing revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 collaboration revenue was $65 million, comprising a $45 million Gilead option exercise fee and a $20 million Sanofi milestone for KT-485 entering Phase I, with no additional revenue expected the rest of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Gilead’s “$45M” fee would be recognized in Q2 and gave a base scenario of “About $48–55M on the milestone.”

surprises.description: Management set a more specific efficacy benchmark for KT-621 than the preview anticipated: it expects BROADEN-2 results to be in the ballpark of dupilumab’s week-16 results in prior atopic dermatitis studies. This is a forward-looking expectation, not a reported trial result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “KT-621's efficacy in BROADEN-2 is expected to be in the ballpark of dupilumab's week-16 results in prior AD studies, with the trial powered against elevated modern placebo rates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the buy-side efficacy bar was “roughly EASI-75 of at least 50% at the top dose” and flagged the efficacy bar and disclosure plan as key issues.

surprises.description: Kymera described a broader development and execution ambition than the preview had outlined: it is building capabilities for potentially more than 10 Phase III studies over the next 2–3 years and identified a KT-621 asthma Phase 2b trial, with top-line data expected by late 2027 and a 52-week open-label extension. The scale of this plan also implies substantial execution demands.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is building capabilities to execute potentially more than 10 Phase III studies over the next 2-3 years, including a KT-621 asthma Phase 2b (BREADTH) with top line data expected by late 2027 plus a 52-week open-label extension.”

surprises.description: The call announced leadership changes that the preview had not anticipated: CMO Jared Gollob is retiring but will remain an adviser through year-end, Terence Rooney from J&J will succeed him, and Felix Baker will become board chairman. The call also cited new hires from Takeda and Sanofi; the shareholder implications are not clear from the information provided.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Chief Medical Officer Jared Gollob is retiring (staying as adviser through year-end), succeeded by Terence Rooney from J&J, alongside a board chairman transition to Felix Baker and new hires from Takeda and Sanofi.”

in_line: BROADEN-2 enrollment and timing were consistent with the preview: it had already noted enrollment was completed early and the readout had been pulled forward to year-end 2026; the call reaffirmed year-end 2026 top-line data and a mid-2027 Phase III start.
Cash and investments of approximately $1.5 billion and runway into 2029 matched the preview’s stated cash and runway expectations.

KT-579 healthy-volunteer data in Q4 2026 remains within the preview’s 2H26 timing window. Its targets of greater than 90% IRF5 degradation and 50–80% biomarker reductions also match the preview’s stated disclosure bar.

surprises.description: Management had pointed to roughly 6% growth, but core sales grew 4.9% and reported sales grew 3.2%. Reported sales were essentially in line with the $172.6M consensus, so the shortfall was mainly against the more ambitious growth trajectory.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net sales grew 3.2% to $172 million, with core business net sales up 4.9%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the key issue was revenue versus the “roughly +6% growth management pointed to in May.” Consensus was $172.6M.

surprises.description: American Performance remained in decline instead of reaching the preview’s base-case expectation of flat growth, although the decline narrowed substantially from Q1. This left the division short of the preview’s bull case of a return to growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: American Performance sales declined 2.1% but improved sequentially from a 9.7% Q1 decline.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario assumed “American Performance flat”; its bull scenario assumed the division “turns positive.”

surprises.description: Margins weakened rather than benefiting from the expected help from a volume recovery: gross margin fell to 41% and adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 19.6%. Management attributed the pressure to higher tariffs and the absence of a prior-year tariff-related benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin fell 72 basis points to 41% and adjusted EBITDA margin declined 223 basis points to 19.6%, largely due to higher tariff costs and a prior-year one-time non-cash tariff capitalization benefit of $3–3.5 million that did not repeat.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a volume recovery should help” gross margin and set gross margin above 42% as a bull-case outcome.

surprises.description: A one-time IEEPA tariff refund of about $10–11M boosted adjusted net income to more than double the year-earlier level and also helped free cash flow. The preview did not anticipate this refund, so the earnings and cash-flow strength included a nonrecurring benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted net income more than doubled year-over-year to $24 million from $10.6 million, aided by a one-time ~$10–11 million IEEPA tariff refund; quarterly free cash flow was also aided by the refund.

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s focus on the divestiture’s possible effect on guidance, the reported quarter included a GAAP net loss rather than a profit, with the company attributing it to the divestiture of Brothers Trucks and Scott Drake.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company reported a GAAP net loss of $2.4 million versus net income of $10.9 million a year earlier, driven by the divestiture of non-core restoration brands Brothers Trucks and Scott Drake.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the Scott Drake and Brothers Trucks sale and said it was unclear whether it was already reflected in the May guidance cut; it did not anticipate a GAAP loss.

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow exceeded the preview’s already strong $35.7M year-earlier comparison, reaching $40.9M. The result was partly supported by the one-time tariff refund.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company generated $40.9 million in quarterly free cash flow, up $5.2 million year-over-year, aided by the one-time IEEPA tariff refund.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that Q2 was seasonally strong and that last year’s $35.7M was a record comparison.

surprises.description: Leverage declined only from 3.84x to 3.74x, a relatively limited step toward the below-3.5x year-end target despite the preview’s expectation that it move meaningfully lower. The company nevertheless reaffirmed that target and said leverage was at its lowest level in four years.
surprises.fact_evidence: Leverage was reduced to 3.74x, its lowest level in four years, with the company reaffirming its target of ending 2026 below 3.5x.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said leverage needed to “move meaningfully off 3.84x” to approach the below-3.5x target.

surprises.description: The company quantified the previously described national-retailer opportunity at approximately $12M of new placements launching in Q3. The preview had called the partnership meaningful but said its size was not yet disclosed.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company secured approximately $12 million of new national retailer placements launching in Q3.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the partnership had been described only as “meaningful incremental annual business” and listed its sizing as a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: Three divisions outside American Performance delivered double-digit core growth, a stronger segment picture than the preview’s discussion of the overall sales outlook and its focus on American Performance suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: Modern Truck & Off-Road grew 15.7%, Euro & Import 13.1%, and Safety & Racing 13.8%; three of four divisions posted double-digit core growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed the aggregate revenue outlook and highlighted American Performance, but did not identify expected double-digit growth in these three divisions.

surprises.description: Management said cost reductions were expected to reach or exceed the top of the announced $5–7M range by year-end, a stronger execution outlook than the preview had identified.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects cost reduction initiatives to deliver at or above the top end of its $5–7 million range by year-end.

surprises.description: The company made a further $15M voluntary debt repayment after quarter end, bringing voluntary debt reduction since September 2023 to $115M; the preview anticipated a leverage step-down but did not mention this additional repayment.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company made a $15 million voluntary debt repayment after quarter end, bringing total voluntary debt reduction to $115 million since September 2023.

surprises.description: Portfolio rebalancing involved a broader operational pullback than the preview’s focus on the sale of two restoration brands: the company reported four brand divestitures, facility closures, a smaller warehouse footprint and workforce, and removal of about 7,000 low-margin SKUs.
surprises.fact_evidence: Year-to-date rebalancing included divesting four brands, eliminating two facilities, cutting warehouse footprint by about 95,000 square feet, reducing workforce about 5%, and removing about 7,000 low-margin SKUs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed the Scott Drake and Brothers Trucks divestiture but did not describe these broader portfolio and operating changes.

in_line: Net sales of $172 million were approximately in line with the preview’s $172.6 million consensus estimate.
The company reaffirmed its full-year guidance, consistent with the preview’s base scenario that the FY2026 range would be maintained.
The company repurchased approximately $2 million of stock during the quarter, answering the preview’s question about whether shares were actually repurchased.

surprises.description: Revenue was $8.3 million, just below the preview’s $8.36–$8.89 million consensus range. The shortfall from the low end was small.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $8.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue vs. ~$8.4–8.9M consensus range.”

surprises.description: The company reported an operating loss of about $200,000 rather than roughly breakeven. SG&A rose to $1.5 million from $1.2 million, driven largely by one-time noncash stock option expenses, although net income and EPS were essentially breakeven as expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company posted an operating loss of about $200,000”; “SG&A rose to $1.5 million from $1.2 million a year ago, driven largely by one-time noncash stock option expenses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “roughly breakeven.”

surprises.description: Inventory increased to $8.6 million rather than drawing down after Q1, continuing the build ahead of the relocation. This was a downside to the preview’s stated focus on whether inventory would draw down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventories grew to $8.6 million from $5.6 million at the start of the year, reflecting buffer stock building ahead of the planned facility relocation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The question is inventory drawdown and cash burn.”

surprises.description: Congressional funding was approved for CPS HybridTech Armor ballistic shields on Navy destroyers, with contracts expected later this year. That creates a path for the product to return to revenue, a development the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Congressional funding has been approved for CPS HybridTech Armor ballistic shields on Navy destroyers, with contracts expected to be issued later this year, marking a return to revenue for that product.”

surprises.description: The facility move has advanced from having no site selected to being close to finalizing a lease for a location twice the current size. However, the timeline has slipped, and design, permitting, construction, and installation together are expected to take roughly 10–12 months.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is close to finalizing a lease for a new facility twice the size of its current location, though the timeline has slipped”; “3-4 months for design and permitting followed by 7-8 months for construction and equipment installation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “No site selected as of the Q1 call”; “Watch for a signed site, capex, and cost estimates.”
