surprises.fact_evidence: Migration “delivered double-digit increases in CPM and fill rates versus last year”; June was “the best month of ad growth in at least two years,” and integration was “tracking ahead of plan with faster-than-expected CPM lift.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for Disney and ESPN integration updates.”

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed expectations for positive free cash flow in both fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028, a forward-looking commitment the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company reaffirmed expectations for positive free cash flow in both fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028.

surprises.description: The company disclosed that Co-Founder and COO Alberto Horihuela will move to a Founder Advisor role by year-end, while remaining through 2027. The preview did not flag this leadership transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Co-Founder and COO Alberto Horihuela will transition to a Founder Advisor role by year-end and remain through 2027.”

surprises.description: Management highlighted refinancing flexibility from current cash exceeding the face value of the 2029 convertible notes, a specific source of optionality not covered in the preview’s cash discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company said current cash exceeded the face value of its 2029 convertible notes, “providing refinancing optionality.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on cash versus the year-end commitment and warned that “Q3 cash below $220M would put pressure on the year-end commitment.”

in_line: Q3 North America revenue of $1.474 billion was close to the preview’s roughly $1.50 billion consensus estimate and within its stated ±$30 million uncertainty range.
Adjusted EBITDA of $19.1 million was within the preview’s estimated $10–$25 million range.
Management reaffirmed the fiscal 2028 adjusted EBITDA target of at least $300 million, as the preview’s bull case expected.
Cash of $236.4 million was above the preview’s $220 million Q3 risk threshold, and management still expected year-end cash above $200 million.
The new CEO deferred detailed strategy across the four growth pillars to the November call, consistent with the preview’s expectation of potentially non-committal first-call commentary.

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EPS was $2.96, well above the preview’s $2.31 consensus estimate. That is a 28% beat, exceeding even the preview’s implied Q4 guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EPS reached a record $2.96.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $2.31 (+579% y/y)”

surprises.description: FY26 adjusted EPS finished at $4.57, above the company’s prior $3.75–$4.00 guidance range. This exceeded the preview’s stated full-year guidance ceiling.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY26 adjusted EPS rose to $4.57.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance (FY26): Adjusted EPS $3.75–$4.00.”

surprises.description: FY27 adjusted EPS guidance has a $4.65 midpoint, below the preview’s roughly $5.40–$5.50 NTM consensus implication, although it is above the preview’s base-case guide range. The guide also relies heavily on price and tariff surcharges, with volume projected at just 1–4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 guidance projects… adjusted EPS of $4.15–$5.15 (midpoint $4.65, roughly flat versus FY26's $4.57)”; price and tariff surcharges contribute “40–43%,” with volume of “just 1–4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus implies NTM EPS near $5.40–$5.50”; the base scenario expected FY27 adjusted EPS of “$3.50–$4.25.”

surprises.description: The favorable raw-material timing benefit is more front-loaded than the preview’s expectation that it would carry into H1 FY27: Q1 alone includes about $2.25 per share, and the benefit is expected to be substantially behind Kennametal by the start of Q3. Management also described a mid-teens Q4 FY27 EBITDA margin as a clean FY28 starting point, far below the reported Q4 peak.
surprises.fact_evidence: The benefit is “largely front-loaded,” “substantially behind the company by the start of Q3 FY27,” and “Q1 alone” includes “~$2.25 of favorable timing per share”; Q4 FY27 EBITDA margin is guided to the “mid-teens.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The May framework assumed price-raw benefit carrying into H1 FY27”; management had attributed “$2.45 of full-year EPS to tungsten price-raw timing, mostly in Q4.”

surprises.description: FY27 free cash flow conversion is expected to reach only about 20% of adjusted net income, a limited recovery after negative FY26 free operating cash flow and against the preview’s emphasis on an inventory unwind and cash-flow improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 free cash flow [is] expected at only ~20% of adjusted net income”; FY26 free operating cash flow was “negative $79 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The FY27 conversion target is the most important non-EPS line”; the preview also highlighted the “inventory unwind timeline.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed an unexpected approximately $0.25-per-share FY27 headwind from higher interest expense as debt increased, which weighs on the earnings outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects a ~$0.25 EPS headwind from higher interest expense in FY27 due to increased debt.”

surprises.description: Kennametal also flagged a 23% Bolivia FX headwind after the government ended its preferential exchange program, a new adverse factor not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A 23% Bolivia FX headwind after the government ended its preferential exchange program.”

surprises.description: Energy demand was notably stronger than the preview’s discussion of soft end markets: Q4 energy sales surged, and the FY27 U.S. land rig-count outlook shifted from an expected decline to growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The energy end market surged in Q4 (up 101% overall, +135% in infrastructure),” and the rig-count outlook was revised “from a mid-single-digit decline to high-single-digit growth for FY27.”

surprises.description: The stated restructuring-savings commitment is larger than the preview’s assumed $10 million of incremental savings: management is committed to $110 million by FY27 and had already realized $27 million in FY26.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Committed to $110 million of restructuring savings by end of FY27,” with “$27 million in FY26.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The May framework assumed… $10M of incremental restructuring savings.”

in_line: The preview expected FY26 tungsten price/raw-material timing gains to be concentrated mostly in Q4; the call reported about $252 million of favorable timing in Q4.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $175 million, above the preview’s $169–171 million base case and its own $170 million estimate. That is a clear upside gap, although it matched the preview’s bull-case figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA rose 6% year-over-year to $175 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The full preview's own estimates were revenue $434M, adj. EBITDA $170M, adj. EPS $2.03”; base scenario: “Adj. EBITDA $169–171M.”

surprises.description: U.S. RevPAR rose only 1.3%, below the preview’s 2.5% estimate and its base scenario of 2–3%. The FIFA World Cup contributed about 60 basis points, so the reported result included a temporary event-related lift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. RevPAR increased 1.3% year-over-year”; “the FIFA World Cup contributing about 60 basis points to Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The full preview's own estimates were … U.S. RevPAR +2.5%”; base scenario: “U.S. RevPAR +2 to +3%.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance fell to $6.86–7.10 from $6.92–7.14, despite the higher EBITDA outlook. Management attributed the lower range to higher expected interest expense and a higher effective tax rate, partly offset by repurchases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted diluted EPS guidance was set at $6.86-7.10, reflecting higher expected interest expense and a higher effective tax rate partially offset by share repurchases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed maintained FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance of “$6.92” to “$7.14.”

surprises.description: The EBITDA guidance increase was smaller and less firmly placed in the upper range than the preview’s base case anticipated: the new range is $635–650 million, versus the preview’s expected narrowing to roughly $640–650 million. It is still a modest increase from the prior $632–647 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance for adjusted EBITDA to $635-650 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 EBITDA guidance action. Raise, narrow, or reaffirm the $632–647M range”; base scenario: “FY narrowed to ~$640–650M.”

surprises.description: The U.S. room base improved to nearly flat year-over-year, with openings at a seven-year high and exits at a six-year low. The preview expected an improvement but cited falling room counts and was watching for a turn toward positive growth, so the sharp improvement in openings and exits is better than that setup suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. net rooms growth is now nearly flat year-over-year as Q2 gross room openings hit a 7-year high (up 27% year-over-year) and room exits fell 50% to their lowest level in 6 years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “U.S. rooms fell to 497,881 at March 2026, from 500,562 a year earlier”; management had “guided U.S. net rooms growth back to positive within the year,” and the preview said to watch whether Q2 “turns positive or at least improves sequentially.”

surprises.description: Global net rooms growth guidance increased to approximately 1.5%, above the preview’s roughly 1% expectation. The preview did not anticipate this higher target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global net rooms growth to approximately 1.5% (up from ~1%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 “Global net rooms growth ~+1%.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a $9.5 million Q3 comparison headwind from prior-year liquidated damages that are not expected to recur. The preview did not flag this near-term EBITDA drag, though management linked the nonrecurrence to improved franchisee retention.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 EBITDA comparisons face a headwind from roughly $9.5 million of prior-year liquidated damages that are not expected to recur, reflecting improved franchisee retention.”

surprises.description: The company reported a strong loyalty contribution increase alongside membership growth, neither of which was addressed in the preview. Loyalty membership reached 77 million, up 7%, and loyalty contribution rose by more than 250 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Loyalty membership grew 7% year-over-year to 77 million and loyalty contribution rose more than 250 basis points.”

surprises.description: The U.S. conversion pipeline was up 24% year-over-year, and management expected conversions to make up about 90% of 2026 U.S. openings. The preview did not identify this conversion momentum or the expected opening cadence.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The U.S. conversion pipeline is up 24% year-over-year and 6% sequentially, with conversions expected to represent ~90% of 2026 U.S. openings and about 75% of year-to-date signed agreements expected to open this year.”

surprises.description: Hotel-development capital outlays fell sharply as Choice continued its exit from hotel ownership, with the first asset sale now expected in the first half of 2027. The preview did not discuss this ownership transition or its timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Capital outlays for hotel development declined 80% year-over-year in the first half as the company exits hotel ownership, with the first asset disposition expected in the first half of 2027 (~$450 million of owned hotels among $650 million in related balance sheet assets).”

in_line: Adjusted EPS of $2.02 was close to the preview’s $2.03 estimate and above the cited $1.96–1.97 consensus range.
Full-year U.S. RevPAR guidance of 0–1.25% was broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of a move toward roughly 0–1%.
The U.S. royalty rate rose 11 basis points, consistent with the preview’s focus on the royalty-rate trend and its cited Q1 increase of 11 basis points.
The company reiterated its $175–225 million 2026 share-repurchase plan, matching the guidance cited in the preview.

surprises.description: Hagerty raised its FY2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook to $270–280 million, well above the prior $236–247 million range and the preview’s view that a raise above $250 million was the meaningful bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lifted adjusted EBITDA guidance to $270-280 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance ($236–247M)” and “A raise above $250M would re-rate the stock.”

surprises.description: The company now guides to FY2026 GAAP net income of $18–30 million, reversing the preview’s expectation of a full-year GAAP net loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Set GAAP net income guidance of $18-30 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said company guidance was “GAAP net loss $(51)M to $(41)M” and listed FY26 EPS estimates of “$(0.10) to $(0.47).”

surprises.description: Hagerty’s written premium growth outlook rose to 16–17% from 15–16%, while first-half growth was already 19%, above the pace implied by the prior guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year 2026 written premium growth guidance to 16-17% (up from prior 15-16%)”; “First-half 2026 written premium grew 19%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Written premium: No formal consensus; guide implies +15–16%” and company FY guidance of “written premium +15–16%.”

surprises.description: Retention was 88%, below the preview’s 88.5% watch level, and continued to ease rather than stabilizing: it fell 50 basis points year over year and 30 basis points sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retention held at an industry-leading 88%, though it declined 50 basis points year-over-year and 30 basis points sequentially due to a modest downtrend in the core book.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “retention ≥ 88.5%” and said “Two consecutive quarters of decline while new business booms would suggest growth is being bought.”

surprises.description: Marketplace revenue rebounded sharply, with Q2 revenue up 48% to $40 million, contrary to the preview’s concern that strong auction activity could continue to coexist with weak marketplace revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 marketplace revenue up 48% to $40 million”; first-half marketplace sales grew 17%, led by Broad Arrow’s 74% first-half sales increase and a 91% sell-through rate.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q1 marketplace revenue fell 12% to $25.7M despite record auction sales” and identified “Strong auction totals with weak marketplace revenue” as the pattern to watch.

surprises.description: Hagerty disclosed a post-quarter acquisition of Bennett’s, a major UK specialty motorcycle insurer, which the preview did not anticipate. The deal triples Hagerty’s UK scale, but the facts provided do not establish its financial impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hagerty acquired Bennett's, the UK's second-largest specialty motorcycle insurer, for £34 million after quarter-end, tripling its scale in the UK market.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue approached $100 million, far above the preview’s $68.4–69.5 million consensus range. That is roughly 44% above the high end of the estimate range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue approached $100 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 Revenue … $69.5M … or $68.4M.”

surprises.description: Flotek raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $340–350 million from $270–290 million, a much larger full-year outlook than the preview’s consensus of $285.2 million and existing company guidance suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised 2026 guidance to revenue of $340-350 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance (FY26): $270–290M”; “Consensus … $285.2M.”

surprises.description: Flotek raised 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $47–51 million from $36–41 million. The preview listed the prior guide but had no consensus estimate for adjusted EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised 2026 guidance to … adjusted EBITDA of $47-51 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 Adj. EBITDA $36–41M”; “Not found” for consensus.

surprises.description: GAAP EPS was $0.26, twice the preview’s $0.13 consensus, and net income rose to $10 million. The result was a substantial upside to the expected per-share earnings figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income rose to $10 million ($0.26 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 EPS (GAAP diluted) … $0.13.”

surprises.description: Chemistry Technologies revenue rose 53% year over year, exceeding the preview’s qualitative expectation of an inflection after a 33% year-over-year external Chemistry decline in Q1. The result was also achieved despite a 5% decline in North American frac fleet count.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Chemistry Technologies revenue grew 53% year-over-year despite a 5% decline in North American frac fleet count.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management promised a Q2 inflection after a 33% YoY external decline in Q1”; “external Chemistry revenue would rise from Q2 onward.”

surprises.description: The PREPA opportunity progressed from a potential backlog subject to an active court stay in the preview to a won 10-year contract expected to generate approximately $400 million of backlog. The preview had already noted that the opportunity contributed no 2026 revenue, so the award is a positive development but not a near-term guidance contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Flotek won a 10-year contract to support Puerto Rico's PREPA 400-megawatt gas power project, expected to generate approximately $400 million in revenue backlog through 2036.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The ~$400M potential backlog announced Aug 3 contributes no 2026 revenue and faces an active court stay.”

surprises.description: International Chemistry revenue reached $10.6 million, up from $1.9 million in Q1, as Flotek expanded to four frac fleets in Saudi Arabia’s Jafurah field. The preview anticipated a Chemistry inflection overall but did not flag this rapid international ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International chemistry revenue reached $10.6 million, up 172% year-over-year and up from $1.9 million in Q1, driven by expansion to 4 frac fleets in Saudi Arabia's Jafurah field.”

surprises.description: Flotek disclosed a new scale-up in its digital measurement business: deployments or contracts rose 56% sequentially to 89 units, and management expects analyzers on over half of active North American e-frac and gas-powered fleets by year-end. The preview did not identify this operating metric or penetration target as an expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Digital valuation measurement devices deployed or contracted grew 56% sequentially to 89 units”; “expects proprietary real-time analyzers on over 50% of active North American e-frac and gas-powered fleets by year-end.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a power-services pipeline exceeding $1 billion and expects to have measurement or control over roughly 5 gigawatts of power by Q1 2027—commercial scale not discussed in the preview. The conversion and timing of that pipeline were not quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management cited a total power services pipeline exceeding $1 billion and expects to have measurement or control over roughly 5 gigawatts of power by Q1 2027.”

surprises.description: The guidance excludes any Q4 revenue from the unrenewed Montana Power Services contract, worth about $6 million per quarter. This qualifies the otherwise large guidance increase and is a downside risk to the Montana-related revenue the preview discussed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Guidance conservatively excludes any Q4 revenue from the unrenewed Montana Power Services contract (~$6 million/quarter).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said Data Analytics would grow sequentially in Q2 on the Montana utility contract (~$12M expected 2026 revenue).”

surprises.description: Flotek reported unusually low overhead and no ABL borrowings: G&A was under 8% of revenue, versus nearly 12% a year earlier and the lowest quarterly rate in at least a decade, while leverage remained below 1x. The preview did not set expectations for these cost or balance-sheet measures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “G&A expenses fell to under 8% of revenue from nearly 12% a year ago, the lowest quarterly rate in at least a decade, while leverage remained below 1x and ABL borrowings were reduced to zero.”

in_line: The preview expected the PREPA opportunity to contribute no 2026 revenue; management likewise said the contract’s revenue was not included in 2026 guidance.

Data Analytics accounted for 51% of company gross profit, close to the preview’s Q1 reference of 50%; the supplied call facts do not give Q2 Data Analytics revenue to compare directly with the preview’s $11–12 million estimate.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $1.27, well above both the $1.06 consensus estimate and management’s prior $1.05–$1.07 indication. The roughly 20% beat was much larger than the preview’s base-case expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS essentially flat at $1.27 versus $1.26 a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $1.06”; management said Q2 EPS would be “very similar to Q1, maybe a penny or two higher,” implying “$1.05–$1.07.”

surprises.description: Revenue reached $491.4 million, exceeding the $462.35 million consensus and even the preview’s $472–478 million bull-case range. That is a materially stronger result than the expected roughly 5% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenues rose 12% year-over-year to $491.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $462.35M” consensus; the bull scenario forecast “$472–478M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $50.1 million, below the preview’s modeled $52–54 million range, even as revenue substantially beat consensus. The gap was modest but ran counter to the expected 6–10% year-over-year EBITDA growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA edged up only modestly to $50.1 million from $49.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$52–54M (modeled),” with expected year-over-year growth of “+6–10%.”

surprises.description: Oilfield Services performed much more strongly than the preview’s cautious outlook suggested: revenue rose 14%, operating income rose 40%, and the added DRA capacity was nearly sold out. Management was also discussing another expansion, despite the preview saying DRA capacity was maxed out in Q2 and describing management as only cautiously optimistic on heavy-crude opportunities.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oilfield Services was the standout with revenue up 14% to $115.4 million and operating income up 40% to $8.7 million”; “DRA capacity added is nearly sold out with strong Middle East demand” and management is “discussing a further DRA expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said DRA capacity is ‘maxed out in Q2 and Q4’ and only ‘cautiously optimistic’ on heavy-crude opportunities.”

surprises.description: Performance Chemicals’ operating income was $16.4 million, modestly above the preview’s roughly $15 million base case. The result showed a stronger recovery than the base case, though it did not reach the preview’s $18 million-plus level associated with a clear bull-case result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Performance Chemicals revenue grew 9% to $190.3 million … driving 15% operating income growth to $16.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The author's base case is about $15M”; “Above about $18M would support” the recovery thesis.

surprises.description: Management described additional prospective Oilfield Services growth avenues—new technologies and potential Mexico opportunities within roughly six months—that were not part of the preview’s stated outlook. These remain prospective rather than confirmed revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New oilfield technologies and potential Mexico opportunities are expected within roughly six months.”

surprises.description: The North Carolina plant repairs are expected to produce more than 10% additional Performance Chemicals capacity next year without additional capital expenditure. The preview anticipated a recovery from the disruption but did not flag this scale of capacity gain or the no-CapEx benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The North Carolina Performance Chemicals plant repairs are about 60% complete, expected to finish by end of Q4, with efficiency gains projected to add north of 10% capacity for next year without additional CapEx.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Performance Chemicals should show sequential operating-income growth in Q2 and be “significantly better” in Q3, but did not specify an added-capacity gain.

in_line: Fuel Specialties experienced the anticipated margin compression from cost inflation and pricing lag: gross margin fell 1.5 points to 36.6%, and management warned that the lag could cause further sequential pressure in Q3 before stabilizing.

Performance Chemicals operating income recovered from the disrupted Q1 level and came in near the preview’s roughly $15 million base case, rather than reaching the preview’s $18 million-plus bull-case threshold.

surprises.description: Q2 EPS was $2.45, above the preview’s $2.21–$2.24 consensus estimates and just above the company’s $2.00–$2.40 guidance range. That made the quarter stronger than the preview’s base case of $2.15–$2.35.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 delivering $2.45.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS | $2.21” and “Adj. EPS (alt) | $2.24”; company guidance was “$2.00 – $2.40.” The preview’s base scenario was “$2.15 – $2.35.”

surprises.description: Management said EM adjusted EBIT should grow at double-digit rates, closer to 15%, for the year despite substantial absorption, divestiture and equity-earnings headwinds. That is a more favorable full-year outlook than the preview’s emphasis on EM EBIT being guided down year over year and sequentially, although the preview’s segment estimate referred to Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EM is expected to grow adjusted EBIT at double-digit rates (closer to 15%) this year” despite a “$45 million inventory-reduction absorption hit, $35 million of lost EBIT from the Micromax divestiture, and about $10 million of equity earnings decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Engineered Materials adj. EBIT | ~$200M | Implied | $190 – $210M | vs $214M (down)”; the preview also said it was “Guided down year over year and sequentially.”

surprises.description: The Ibn Sina JV outage is reducing expected equity earnings by about $10 million for the year, with nearly all the impact falling in Q3. The preview did not flag this specific earnings headwind or its quarterly timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Equity earnings will be about $10 million lower than originally anticipated this year because the Ibn Sina joint venture did not operate for much of Q2, with nearly all the impact hitting Q3.”

surprises.description: Accelerated Lanaken and EM closures bring a heavier inventory-absorption burden into the second half, including an additional $20 million charge in Acetyl Chain. The preview discussed an expected EM nylon absorption hit but did not anticipate this incremental AC charge from the pulled-forward closures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Accelerated closure of the Lanaken acetate tow plant and pulled-forward EM closures are driving a heavier second-half inventory absorption hit, including an incremental $20 million absorption charge in AC in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “~$50M absorption hit from nylon inventory drawdown” in EM, but did not mention an incremental AC absorption charge.

surprises.description: Management described a multi-year cash-generation outlook, framing the maintained 2026 FCF range as a sustainable baseline for the next few years. The preview expected the $700–$800 million 2026 target to be maintained, but did not anticipate that longer-term framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 free cash flow was $140 million despite an almost $200 million working capital build in the quarter,” and the “$700 million to $800 million” full-year guide was “now framed as a sustainable baseline for the next few years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 FCF | $700 – $800M (raised in May).”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a broader $80–$100 million cost-reduction target for 2027, with some Lanaken and nylon/EM footprint savings already expected in 2026. The preview mentioned nylon savings but not this combined target or the Lanaken savings timetable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management has taken actions targeting $80 million to $100 million of cost reductions for 2027,” with “roughly one-third of Lanaken's $20-25 million savings and about half of the $30-35 million nylon/EM footprint savings captured in 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview referenced “~$30M of Nylon 66 cost savings” as an offset to EM’s inventory absorption hit.

surprises.description: The company set out a $1 billion divestiture commitment through 2027 and said it was about halfway there after Micromax. The preview expected another deal but did not cite this larger cumulative target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is committed to $1 billion of divestitures by end of 2027, is about halfway there after Micromax.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the CFO expected to “sign another deal this year,” but did not state a $1 billion divestiture target.

surprises.description: Management highlighted electronics and medical as profit-rich growth platforms, including a data-center server opportunity with three times the content of traditional servers. The preview did not identify these end markets or the potential AI-server opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Electronics represents about 10% of revenue but 10-15% of contribution margin, and medical is under 10% of revenue but roughly 20% of contribution margin,” with an AI data-center server “content opportunity [of] 3x traditional servers.”

in_line: Full-year 2026 EPS guidance was reaffirmed at roughly $6, close to the preview’s $6.05 consensus and prior guidance framework.
The $700–$800 million full-year 2026 FCF target was maintained, as the preview expected.

The net-debt path was broadly in line with the preview: around $10 billion at year-end 2026 and around $9 billion in 2027, with leverage below 5x this year versus the preview’s roughly 4.8x year-end expectation.

Asian acetyl margins had moderated from their early-Q2 spike, while Western Hemisphere margins remained elevated; the preview anticipated Asian moderation and emphasized the importance of Western pricing.
The preview anticipated an EM inventory-absorption hit of roughly $50 million; the call cited a $45 million EM inventory-reduction absorption hit.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $1.96, above the preview’s $1.81 consensus estimate by $0.15, or about 8%. The decline from $2.00 a year earlier was also much smaller than the preview’s expected 9.5% drop.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $1.96 versus $2.00 a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS | $1.81” and “Implied Y/Y | −9.5%.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 35.5%, well above the preview’s 34.0–34.5% base case. Management also said it expects further expansion in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 240 basis points to 35.5% … with further expansion expected in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base case is 34.0–34.5%” and “Gross margin ≥34.0%.”

surprises.description: Management increased the plant-consolidation savings target to at least $20 million and the total Project Apollo annualized savings target to at least $25 million, rather than merely reaffirming the preview’s $20 million plant-consolidation target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised the plant consolidation component of Project Apollo from $15 million to at least $20 million, lifting the total program's annualized savings target to at least $25 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management targets $20M annualized savings from plant consolidation. Any raise to that target would be a catalyst.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was about $2.6 million below the preview author’s roughly $70 million estimate, even though adjusted EPS beat consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined 6.4% to $67.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA | ~$70M (my estimate, not a consensus figure).”

surprises.description: Freight and fuel costs were a larger reported pressure than the preview’s estimate: management cited roughly $4.7 million of net cost pressure in the quarter, while the preview estimated about $3.5 million for the second half if fuel held. Distribution expenses also rose to 11.6% of sales from 9.8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA … hurt by roughly $4.7 million in net freight and fuel cost pressures”; “Distribution expenses rose to 11.6% of sales from 9.8% … reflecting roughly $5 million in higher freight and fuel costs before surcharge offsets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management sized a ~$3.5M H2 headwind if fuel holds.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed an expected $17 million insurance collection in August from the Holly Ridge plant-fire settlement. The preview discussed a prior-year insurance gain but did not anticipate this current-period cash recovery; no earnings impact was specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expects to collect about $17 million in insurance proceeds in August from the Holly Ridge plant fire settlement.”

in_line: Net sales were $426 million versus the preview’s $425.8 million consensus estimate, essentially in line.
Frozen beverage sales were $106.7 million, within the preview’s expected range of about $106–110 million.
The bakery sales headwind was about 3.5% of sales in Q3 and is expected to ease to roughly 2.5% in Q4, matching the preview’s Q3 and Q4 volume-reduction framing.

surprises.description: FTEK's June 30 APC backlog reached $14.3 million, roughly double the preview's $7 million year-end level and above the preview's $7 million-range bull-case threshold. The company said about $10.5 million is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APC backlog reached $14.3 million at June 30, 2026—the largest quarter-end backlog since 2018 and up from $7 million at year-end 2025—with about $10.5 million expected to be recognized in the next 12 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Backlog roughly flat” was the base case; the bull case cited “a 6/30 backlog in the $7M range or higher.”

surprises.description: The reported data-center pipeline was described as approximately $75–$100 million per project, whereas the preview described a $75–$100 million pipeline across 8–10 projects. If those figures refer to comparable pipeline measures, the reported opportunity per project is substantially larger than the preview led investors to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The data center sales pipeline approximates $75–$100 million per project,” with pollution-control units priced at “$1–$4 million” and projects ranging up to “30–40 units.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$75–100M pipeline across 8–10 projects at $1–3M each.”

surprises.description: APC and consolidated gross margins fell sharply, with management attributing APC's decline to project mix and execution costs. The preview did not flag a margin decline as an expected issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin declined to 41% from 46% year-over-year, with APC margin dropping sharply to 36% from 44% due to project mix and execution costs.”

surprises.description: The FuelChem demonstration is now paused and is not expected to restart until mid-Q4; any commercial conversion could contribute revenue in 2027. That is later than the preview's near-term conversion watch, which pointed to this quarter or Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A paused FuelChem demonstration is expected to restart in mid-Q4 2026 and, if converted to a commercial account, could add $2.5–$3 million in annualized revenue in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the demo could add “$2.5–3.0M annualized,” noted management had said “later in the year,” and said FUEL CHEM conversions were flagged for “this quarter” or “Q3.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was slightly below the published $6.71 million consensus, though it cleared the preview's more useful $6.0 million threshold and exceeded its base-case revenue range. The consensus was explicitly described as a weak, potentially stale anchor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated Q2 2026 revenues rose 17% to $6.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 Consensus” revenue was “$6.71M (suspect)”; the preview said the more useful test was whether revenue “clears $6.0M” and gave a base scenario of “$5.3–5.7M.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed that CEO Vincent Arnone will retire effective August 10 and be succeeded by Ramesh Nagahali. The preview did not anticipate a leadership transition; it noted the successor's M&A and operating experience as relevant to potential acquisition strategy.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CEO Vincent Arnone will retire effective August 10, 2026, after 27 years, succeeded by Ramesh Nagahali, who brings M&A and operational experience relevant to potential acquisition strategy.”

surprises.description: Q2's net loss was larger than the one-analyst EPS consensus implied: the reported diluted loss was $0.04 per share versus an expected $0.02 loss. The loss did, however, fall within the preview's base-case EPS range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss widened to $1.2 million ($0.04 per diluted share) from $689,000 ($0.02 per diluted share) a year earlier, with adjusted EBITDA loss of $1.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 EPS consensus was “$(0.02)”; the base scenario gave EPS of “$(0.04)–$(0.05).”

surprises.description: A data-center opportunity remained unawarded and conditional: the call described one inquiry that may convert to a commercial award by the end of Q3, through a capacity reservation agreement, with potential material revenue in 2027. The preview had looked for $3–$5 million to close by the end of Q2 or early Q3, while also warning that a data-center award was unlikely in the release itself.
surprises.fact_evidence: “One data center inquiry may convert to a commercial award before the end of Q3 2026 via a capacity reservation agreement, potentially generating material revenue in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had cited “$3–5M expected to close ‘by end of Q2 or early Q3’”; the preview also said “The data center award is unlikely to come in the release itself.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance: revenue to exceed 2025, FuelChem approximately at prior-year levels, and APC above 2025. The preview said reaffirmation was the base case.

Cash and debt were broadly in line with the preview's balance-sheet description: the company had approximately $29.6 million in cash and investments and no debt, versus the preview's approximate $30 million cash-and-investments and zero-debt figures.

surprises.description: Continuing-operations revenue was $334 million, about 9–11% below the preview’s $368.8–$375.5 million consensus range. Management attributed the shortfall to lower metal prices and Greens Creek concentrate produced in Q2 but not sold until early August, shifting that revenue into Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue from continuing operations fell to $334 million” and a “timing gap where Greens Creek silver concentrate was produced but not sold until early August, shifting that revenue into Q3.”

surprises.description: Keno Hill’s full-year silver guidance was cut to 2.2–2.6 million ounces, and management said meaningfully higher production is not expected until roughly the end of 2029. The preview noted permit constraints but its base case anticipated production guidance being reaffirmed, so the lower guidance and later ramp are worse than that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Keno Hill's full-year silver guidance was cut to 2.2-2.6 million ounces” and a ramp-up to “meaningfully higher production” is “not expected until roughly the end of 2029 pending permits and infrastructure investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: Production and cost guidance are reaffirmed”; the preview also said the 440 tpd ramp depended on permit amendments “not expected until mid-2029.”

surprises.description: Greens Creek received a guidance upgrade: full-year silver production guidance rose to 8.0–8.3 million ounces, while cash costs improved to negative $12.15 to negative $12.00 per ounce. The preview expected production guidance to be reaffirmed, though it had flagged lower costs as a possible positive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year Greens Creek guidance to 8.0-8.3 million ounces of silver with cash costs improving to negative $12.15 to negative $12.00 per ounce.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Production guidance (15.1–16.5 Moz Ag, 51–55 koz Au)” and “Base: Production and cost guidance are reaffirmed”; on costs, “A cost guidance cut is plausible and would be a positive.”

surprises.description: Lucky Friday’s cash-cost guidance was lowered to $9.00–$9.75 per ounce. The preview anticipated a possible cost-guidance cut, so the direction is favorable but broadly consistent with a flagged expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered Lucky Friday cash cost guidance to $9.00-$9.75 per ounce.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A cost guidance cut is plausible and would be a positive.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a proposed Greens Creek pyrite concentrate circuit that could add 1.0–1.2 million ounces of silver and 10,000–15,000 ounces of gold annually, with $40–60 million of capital spending. This was not discussed in the preview and introduces a potential production-growth project, although it is not expected to begin production until Q4 2027 to H1 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: The circuit “could add roughly 1.0-1.2 million ounces of silver and 10,000-15,000 ounces of gold annually” with “$40-60 million” of capital and first production targeted for “Q4 2027 to H1 2028.”

surprises.description: Hecla disclosed more than 600,000 ounces of gold in Greens Creek tailings, with an estimated in-situ value near $6.1 billion at June 30 prices. The preview did not mention this potential resource, though its viability remains unproven and Phase 3 metallurgical testing is only starting.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Greens Creek tailings reprocessing project contains over 600,000 ounces of gold with an in-situ value estimated near $6.1 billion at June 30 prices,” and “Phase 3 metallurgical test work” is commencing.

surprises.description: Management said fuel is only about 3% of consolidated costs, limiting the company’s exposure to oil-price spikes. The preview did not identify this cost insulation as a factor, so it is a favorable new detail about operating-cost sensitivity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fuel represents only about 3% of the consolidated cost structure” because of “high-grade underground mining and hydro-based power.”

surprises.description: Lucky Friday reported record quarterly silver production of 1.5 million ounces on higher mill rates. The preview expected roughly 3.9 million ounces of total company silver production and did not flag a mine-level record, so this is favorable site-level operating news, though the call facts do not provide total Q2 production to compare with consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lucky Friday posted a record 1.5 million ounces of silver on higher mill rates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Silver production ~3.9 Moz”; the base case expected “Volumes in line.”

in_line: Quarterly free cash flow was $136 million, nearly matching Q1’s record $144 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the operating story and strong free cash flow would remain intact.

Management framed full-year free cash flow as a price-deck sensitivity: about $500 million at $50 silver and $3,500 gold, rising toward $700–800 million at higher prices. The preview anticipated that the prior “>$700M” figure, set at $75 silver and $4,500 gold, might be rebased to spot or presented as a sensitivity.

surprises.description: EOG reported adjusted EPS of $5.07, slightly below the preview’s $5.08–$5.10 consensus range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS of $5.07.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS … $5.10 (Zacks …) or $5.08 (Barchart).”

surprises.description: EOG’s strip-price estimate of $8 billion in 2026 free cash flow is below the roughly $8.5 billion record-level figure cited in the preview. The call’s figure is explicitly at strip pricing, so the comparison is not necessarily like-for-like.
surprises.fact_evidence: “At strip pricing, the 2026 plan generates $8 billion in free cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management framed FY26 free cash flow at a record ~$8.5B.”

surprises.description: EOG returned just over $1.8 billion in the quarter, including $1.3 billion of buybacks—an acceleration from the $402 million of Q1 buybacks that the preview described. The preview specifically flagged an accelerated repurchase pace as a positive possibility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Returned just over $1.8 billion to shareholders in Q2 ($540 million in dividends and $1.3 billion in buybacks).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “An accelerated repurchase pace or a dividend action would be a clear positive”; Q1 buybacks were “$402M.”

surprises.description: EOG’s UAE exploration wells produced more than 25,000 barrels of oil per well in their first 30 days and were naturally flowing before artificial lift, exceeding expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The UAE exploration wells produced an average of over 25,000 barrels of oil per well in their first 30 days, exceeding expectations while naturally flowing before artificial lift.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Exceeding expectations.”

surprises.description: EOG announced a new Austin Chalk sweet spot in Lavaca County, with 60,000 net acres leased and about 125 remaining two-mile locations—adding roughly a full year of drilling inventory with sub-one-year payouts at $65 WTI. The preview did not flag this play or inventory addition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Organically leasing 60,000 net acres at $1,200/acre with ~125 remaining 2-mile locations adding roughly a full year of drilling inventory and payouts under one year at $65 WTI.”

surprises.description: Utica Encino execution was better than the preview’s watch item implied: EOG exceeded its $150 million synergy target ahead of schedule, cut direct well costs below $600 per foot, and improved base production by 5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Utica Encino acquisition exceeded its $150 million synergy target ahead of schedule, drove direct well costs below $600 per foot, and improved base production by 5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gas and Utica/Encino execution. Dorado spending was cut on weak near-term Henry Hub; watch gas volume guidance and Utica completion and cost evidence.”

surprises.description: EOG reported substantial well-cost reductions in the Delaware and Eagle Ford beyond anything quantified in the preview: Delaware costs were down $15 per foot year-to-date, and Eagle Ford costs reached a company low.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Delaware Basin direct well costs fell $15 per foot year-to-date to under $710 per foot, while Eagle Ford well costs dropped to below $525 per foot, the lowest in company history.”

surprises.description: EOG’s Janus gas plant was running at more than 99% utilization and delivering over $0.65/Mcf of netback uplift, a positive operational result amid the preview’s concern about weak near-term gas economics and gas execution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EOG’s Janus gas plant is running above 99% utilization delivering a netback uplift of over $0.65/Mcf.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Dorado spending was cut on weak near-term Henry Hub; watch gas volume guidance and Utica completion and cost evidence.”

surprises.description: Alongside the preview’s emphasis on weak near-term Henry Hub economics, management offered a constructive longer-term gas demand outlook, forecasting U.S. natural gas demand growth of 3%–5% annually through the end of the decade.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company forecasts U.S. natural gas demand growth of 3%-5% CAGR through the end of the decade.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Dorado spending was cut on weak near-term Henry Hub.”

in_line: EOG reaffirmed 2026 capital expenditures at $6.5 billion, in line with the preview’s expectation that spending would remain around $6.5 billion.
The commitment to return at least 70% of 2026 free cash flow matched the preview’s stated return commitment.

surprises.description: The preview expected the headline profit to be driven by a non-cash derivative reversal. Instead, Gran Tierra reported $25 million of net income and attributed the turnaround to stronger commodity prices and lower operating costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income was $25 million,” versus a $119 million loss in the prior quarter and a $13 million loss in Q2 2025, “driven by stronger commodity prices and lower operating costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The headline Q2 profit will likely reflect a non-cash derivative reversal, not operations.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $85 million, below the preview’s estimate of about $95 million despite the higher Q2 commodity-price environment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $85 million,” from $74 million in the prior quarter and $77 million in Q2 2025.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA vs. about $95M (my estimate).”

surprises.description: Gran Tierra disclosed a definitive agreement to sell all of its Colombia and Ecuador oil businesses. The preview discussed Colombia policy and the Ecopetrol JV, but did not anticipate a sale of both businesses; the transaction’s shareholder implications are unclear because terms were not discussed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gran Tierra entered a definitive share purchase agreement to sell all of its Colombia and Ecuador oil businesses,” subject to special stockholder approval; management declined to discuss details.

surprises.description: Working-interest production fell to about 41,500 barrels per day, down 9% sequentially, with temporary artificial-lift failures contributing to the decline. The preview highlighted planned Ecuador waterflood injections as a possible source of H2 volume support, although it did not give a Q2 production forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 average working interest production was approximately 41,500 barrels per day, down 9% sequentially and 12% year-over-year,” reflecting dispositions and temporary lift-system failures at Acordionero and Cohembí.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Ecuador waterflood start-up. Iguana and Perico injection was guided for late Q2 or early Q3, and any confirmation would matter for H2 volumes and costs.”

surprises.description: The company made a substantial additional note repurchase after quarter-end: $50 million face value at a 10% discount, beyond the $6 million bought back in the first half. The preview flagged further repurchases as something to watch but did not anticipate this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gran Tierra repurchased “$6 million face value” of its 2031 notes during the first half and bought back “an additional $50 million face value at a 10% discount after quarter-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for further open-market note repurchases.”

surprises.description: Gran Tierra completed its $123 million Suroriente capital carry, with the post-carry period beginning July 18 and management expecting improved block economics and cash generation. The preview did not flag this milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed its $123 million capital carry commitment in Suroriente,” and the post-carry period is expected to improve economics and cash generation on the block.

surprises.description: The lodgepole disposition removed more asset-retirement obligations than the $9 million sale proceeds and also reduced production, which management characterized as a net benefit. This asset-level cleanup was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company sold a “54% working interest for $9 million” while removing “$13 million in asset retirement obligations” and roughly 850 barrels per day of production, “resulting in a net benefit.”

surprises.description: New Canadian resource reports identified contingent and prospective resources, with drilling planned for 2027. The preview did not discuss these reported resource estimates, though the prospective resources are unrisked.
surprises.fact_evidence: The reports assigned Canadian assets approximately “6.5 million barrels of 2C contingent resources” and “about 67 million barrels of combined unrisked best-estimate prospective resources” across Dawson Clearwater and Mount Head.

in_line: Net debt was essentially unchanged from the Q1 figure the preview cited: $479 million at Q2 end versus $481 million at Q1.

surprises.description: GBLI kept a full-year Belmont Core premium-growth target of about 15% despite only 3% growth in the first half, rather than softening the guide as the preview’s base case expected. However, the target is at the low end of the prior 15–20% range, making the required second-half growth particularly steep.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management reaffirmed full-year Belmont Core gross written premium growth of ~15% over 2025, despite only 3% growth in the first half, implying very strong double-digit growth is required in the second half.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected the “FY growth guide softened”; it also said that anything under about $110M of Q2 GWP “suggests the guide gets cut or softened.”

surprises.description: The expense ratio reached 40.9%, above the preview’s 40% threshold for concluding the expense program was not yet working and well above the level that would signal progress. Management now targets a return to roughly 36% only by the latter half of 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: The expense ratio is elevated at 40.9%, running roughly 4.5 points above long-term targets due to Catalyx/Kaleidoscope technology investments, with management targeting a return to ~36% by the latter half of 2028.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “A reading below 39% suggests the program is working. A reading at 40% or higher suggests it is not.”

surprises.description: Valiant Re assumed reinsurance premiums surged 79% in Q2, with treaty count also expanding. The preview did not identify this business as a major growth driver or flag an expectation for a surge.
surprises.fact_evidence: Valiant Re assumed reinsurance premiums surged 79% in Q2 to $21.5 million (43% for the half), with in-force treaties expanding to 22 after adding 3 new treaties in the quarter.

surprises.description: Specialty products premiums fell 36% in Q2 because products were terminated, a steep decline not anticipated in the preview; the ongoing programs were nearly flat, limiting the weakness in the continuing book.
surprises.fact_evidence: Specialty products premiums fell 36% in Q2 to $7.8 million due to terminated products, though the 11 ongoing programs were only down 1%.

surprises.description: Penn-America returned to growth at 2% after two quarterly declines, a modest improvement, but management also described intensifying E&S competition, flat first-half rate change, and moderating rate momentum. The preview focused on a growth inflection in Wholesale Commercial rather than this segment specifically.
surprises.fact_evidence: Penn-America returned to growth (+2% in Q2) after two consecutive quarterly declines, but management flagged intensifying E&S competition with flat first-half rate change and moderating rate momentum.

in_line: The accident-year combined ratio was 94.7% in Q2, within the preview’s 94–95% base-case range.
Management said reserves remain solidly above actuarial indications, consistent with the preview’s stated reserve position.
No share buybacks are currently planned, consistent with the preview’s expectation that buybacks would not occur in 2026.

surprises.description: Government Services adjusted operating income guidance fell to $55–65 million from the preview’s $70–80 million range. The new range includes Berry contracts and is still described as roughly 60% above the 2025 midpoint, but it is a material reduction from the prior guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Government Services 2026 guidance was updated to $475 million-$495 million in revenue and $55 million-$65 million in adjusted operating income, roughly 60% above the 2025 midpoint after including Berry contracts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Government Services adj. operating income $70–80M.”

surprises.description: Offshore Energy Services guidance was raised by $10 million at both ends, despite the preview’s expectation that the key task was to deliver against the existing range. Management cited stronger rates and activity, along with contracts lasting longer than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Offshore Energy Services segment's 2026 adjusted operating income guidance was raised to $235 million-$245 million on stronger rates, activity, and longer-than-expected contracts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance: … Offshore Energy (OES) adj. operating income $225–235M.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was approximately $79.8 million, inferred from Q1’s $59.3 million plus the reported $20.5 million sequential increase, just above the preview’s approximate $73–78 million estimate. The increase was helped by lower repairs and maintenance costs, easing the cost risk highlighted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenues rose $23.1 million and adjusted EBITDA increased $20.5 million sequentially, driven by higher utilization, fuel revenues, and lower repairs and maintenance costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: ~$73–78M.”

surprises.description: Delayed Leonardo AW189 deliveries and related transition costs created an approximately $8 million adverse impact to 2026 Government Services operating income—an additional, specific supply-chain headwind not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Continued supply chain challenges, particularly delayed Leonardo AW189 deliveries, adversely impacted 2026 Government Services adjusted operating income by approximately $8 million through elevated KPI penalties and prolonged transition costs.”

surprises.description: Operating cash flow swung to a substantial Q2 inflow after the Q1 outflow, delivering a stronger recovery than the preview’s open question about whether working capital would normalize.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow swung to $41.4 million positive in Q2 from an $8.3 million use in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether working capital normalizes after Q1's −$12.6M.”

surprises.description: A UKSAR2G fuel-price adjustment mechanism unexpectedly cost Government Services $1.5 million. Management said it had tightened the contract mechanism and the hit should not recur.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A jet fuel price spike hurt Government Services profitability by $1.5 million due to a UKSAR2G deferred price adjustment mechanism, which has since been tightened via contractual amendment and should not recur.”

surprises.description: Management newly said the Berry acquisition is expected to be immediately accretive to earnings, free cash flow, and EBITDA margins; the preview noted the acquisition but did not give an expectation for its near-term contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: Berry Aviation “is expected to be immediately accretive to earnings, free cash flow, and EBITDA margins.”

in_line: Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was affirmed at $295–325 million, matching the preview’s stated range.

Q2 revenue was approximately $411.8 million, inferred from Q1 revenue of $388.7 million plus the reported $23.1 million sequential increase; this falls within the preview’s approximate $407.3–415.6 million consensus range.
Berry Aviation closed in Q3, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the acquisition would close in Q3.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $1.23 billion, well above the preview’s $1.0796 billion published consensus and its $1.10–$1.12 billion buy-side whisper. The reported 34% growth also substantially exceeded the preview’s consensus growth estimate of 17.2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $1.23 billion, up 34% year-over-year, with 30% organic growth excluding the SE&M acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $1.0796B”; the preview also estimated a “buy-side whisper” of “~$1.10–1.12B revenue.”

surprises.description: Q2 EBITDA of $128.6 million greatly exceeded the preview’s implied $92–95 million estimate. EBITDA margin also expanded to 10.4%, with especially strong E&M profitability: its margin reached 10.8%, versus the preview’s 8.5% threshold for challenging management’s timing explanation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 EBITDA rose 53% to a record $128.6 million, with EBITDA margin expanding 130 basis points to 10.4% from 9.1%.” E&M EBITDA was “up 72% with margin expanding 190 basis points to 10.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EBITDA | Not found (no formal consensus); ~$92–95M implied from FY guide and seasonality”; the preview also said “A Q2 [E&M] margin of 8.5% or higher would challenge management’s ‘timing’ framing of Q1.”

surprises.description: Backlog reached $4.55 billion, substantially clearing the preview’s $3.8 billion watchpoint. The reported 53% year-over-year increase, and the estimate that roughly 80% converts within 12 months, indicate stronger near-term backlog support than the preview’s threshold alone implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog grew 53% year-over-year to $4.55 billion, driven by E&M backlog up 62%, with roughly 80% expected to convert within 12 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Backlog needs to clear $3.8B, and book-to-bill above 1.0x, to support the valuation.”

surprises.description: Management raised FY2026 guidance materially above the prior range: even the new low ends are above the old high ends for both revenue and EBITDA. This was a stronger raise than the preview’s stated catalyst of getting above $4.4 billion of revenue and $360 million of EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $4.5–4.7 billion and EBITDA of $410–425 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior guidance was “revenue $4.3–4.4B, EBITDA $345–360M”; the catalyst checklist called for guidance “raised above $4.4B revenue / $360M EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Net leverage was reported at just 0.3x, with management citing flexibility for further acquisitions. The preview specifically identified leverage around the already-announced Epsilon deal as something investors would watch, though it did not give a numerical leverage expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage stood at just 0.3x, far below the 1.5x–2x target range, providing substantial flexibility for continued M&A activity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: For the Epsilon acquisition, the preview said: “Watch whether it is folded into the guide and what pro-forma leverage looks like.”

in_line: Epsilon remained excluded from current guidance, as the preview said it was not in the guide.

The lower second-half margin assumption indicates margins are not expected to stay at the first-half level, consistent with the preview’s expectation that elevated margins would normalize after Q1’s timing-driven improvement.

surprises.description: The preview expected FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $220–230 million to be reaffirmed. Management kept the range but said results were trending toward its lower end, a softer signal than a straightforward reaffirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Full-year guidance was maintained, but management signaled results are trending toward the lower end of the range.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The buy side expects maintenance, so anything softer will likely reset the stock”; the preview also said reaffirmation was the key item.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $54.2 million, below the preview’s roughly $56 million threshold for keeping the full-year range credible. Adjusted EPS of $1.16 also missed the current $1.22 consensus, though the EPS gap was modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA declined to $54.2 million from $56.2 million a year earlier,” and adjusted diluted EPS was “$1.16 versus $1.17.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 adjusted EBITDA of “about $56M or more” was needed and listed current adjusted EPS consensus of “$1.22.”

surprises.description: First-half adjusted free cash flow was only $3.7 million, far short of the recovery the preview was watching after Q1’s negative $3.0 million. The preview specifically warned that weak recovery could call the buyback runway into question.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow collapsed to $3.7 million for the first six months of 2026 from $48.7 million a year earlier,” driven by higher capex, marketing timing, and compensation and interest payments.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “Adj. free cash flow recovery and Q2 buyback disclosure” and said “a weak FCF recovery would question the buyback runway.”

surprises.description: Applebee’s comps fell 1.8%, contrary to the preview’s positive-comps base scenario and the company’s 0% to +2% full-year comp guidance. The tough April comparison explains some of the weakness but does not erase the shortfall versus that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Applebee's posted negative 1.8% comp sales,” hurt by a tough April comparison against last year’s Sizzlin’ Skillets.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Applebee’s FY26 comp guidance of “0% to +2%” and a base scenario of “Applebee's +0.5–1.5%.”

surprises.description: IHOP delivered +1.5% comps rather than the preview’s flat base-case expectation, and management said it had outperformed Black Box on both traffic and sales for a third consecutive quarter. That is a better operating result than the preview’s concern about whether IHOP could turn positive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “IHOP delivered positive 1.5% comps and its third consecutive quarter of outperforming Black Box on both traffic and sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario assumed “IHOP flat” and said “A negative print would undercut management's case that all three brands are flat to positive.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $240.9 million exceeded the current $236.1 million consensus, but the increase was driven by restaurant takebacks rather than stronger franchise revenue. This makes the headline beat lower quality than the revenue figure alone suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenues rose 4.4% to $240.9 million, but this was driven by restaurant takebacks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 revenue consensus of “$236.1M” and cautioned that “a headline revenue beat may be low quality” because of the NRP consolidation.

surprises.description: Excluding advertising, franchise revenue fell 6% because there were fewer franchise units and lower termination fees. The preview warned about revenue quality and consolidation, but this reported franchise-revenue decline makes the underlying weakness concrete.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding advertising, franchise revenues actually fell 6% due to fewer franchise units and lower termination fees.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “separate the 53-unit consolidation from underlying growth” and flagged revenue quality as a key issue.

surprises.description: Applebee’s commodity costs rose 8.2%, markedly more than IHOP’s 1.6%, with full-year inflation expected to remain mid-single-digit at Applebee’s versus low-single-digit at IHOP. This adds a brand-specific cost pressure not quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Applebee's commodity costs rose 8.2% (driven by beef and lapping favorable contracts) versus just 1.6% at IHOP,” with full-year guidance of mid-single-digit and low-single-digit inflation respectively.

surprises.description: Despite the weak first-half free-cash-flow result, DIN repurchased $29 million of shares year to date, about 7% of shares outstanding, and authorized another $100 million of buybacks. That is a substantial continuation of capital returns despite the cash-flow concern highlighted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company returned $9 million to shareholders in Q2 ($7 million buybacks, $2 million dividends) and repurchased $29 million year-to-date—about 7% of shares outstanding—under a new $100 million authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Adj. free cash flow recovery and Q2 buyback disclosure” and said weak FCF could “question the buyback runway.”

surprises.description: Dual-brand conversions were reported to generate roughly twice the sales of single-brand locations, with conversion costs stabilizing around $1 million. The preview did not set an expectation for these economics, so this is a newly disclosed favorable operating opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Dual-brand conversions are generating roughly 2x single-brand sales levels at a stabilizing conversion cost of about $1 million,” with 45 locations open toward a year-end target of 80.

surprises.description: DIN disclosed that its 136 company-owned restaurants are near breakeven EBITDA and have AUVs in the low $2 millions versus about $3 million for the system, and that management is considering refranchising. This reveals a weak owned-restaurant portfolio and a potential change in ownership strategy not addressed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company owns 136 restaurants (about 4% of the system) tracking near breakeven EBITDA, with AUVs in the low $2 millions versus a system average near $3 million, and management is beginning to consider refranchising.”

in_line: Management maintained the FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance range of $220–230 million, as the preview expected, although its comment that results were trending toward the lower end was softer than expected.

surprises.description: The preview put Q2 revenue around $20.4–20.6 billion; 48% growth from Q2 2025 implies revenue of roughly $23 billion, a substantial beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue grew 48% versus Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue consensus is much tighter, at about $20.3–20.5B”; the preview's base case was “about $20.6B.”

surprises.description: The preview's base case was $9.10–9.40 EPS before IPR&D, while Lilly reported $8.38 including a $3.30 charge. Adding back that charge implies $11.68 before IPR&D, well above the preview's ex-charge estimate, although the charge materially reduced reported EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was $8.38 (including $3.30 of acquired IPR&D charges).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The source preview's own base case is ... non-GAAP EPS of $9.10–9.40 before IPR&D, or $6.50–7.50 after the charge”; it also lists “EPS, ex-large IPR&D” of $8.84.

surprises.description: Lilly raised its FY2026 revenue range to $85–87 billion, above the preview's base-case expectation of $83–85 billion and also above its bull-case range of $84–86 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lilly raised full-year revenue guidance to $85–$87 billion (up $3 billion at the low end and $2 billion at the high end).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's base scenario expected the band to be “raised to $83–85B”; its bull scenario expected “FY revenue band raised to $84–86B.”

surprises.description: The preview said the gross-margin and operating-leverage story needed to hold, with Q2 gross margin consensus at 83.4%. Lilly reported 86.3% gross margin and a 9-point expansion in performance margin, indicating stronger margin performance than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin rose 1.3 points to 86.3% and non-GAAP performance margin expanded 9 points to 54.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | 83.4% | 82.5% | Hudson Labs consensus”; the preview also says “the operating leverage story needs to hold.”

surprises.description: The preview warned that U.S. price erosion above the low-to-mid-teens annual guide could put EPS at risk. Q2 U.S. net price declined 3%, or 9% excluding favorable rebate and discount adjustments—less erosion than that annual guide, though the adjusted figure is nearer its low end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. net price declined 3% (or 9% excluding favorable rebate/discount estimate adjustments).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guides to low-to-mid-teens percent price erosion for FY26”; the preview also flags “US realized price vs. ‘low-to-mid-teens’ erosion guide.”

surprises.description: The preview described Foundayo as tracking well behind oral Wegovy, with weekly scripts declining from their peak. Lilly instead reported a sharp expansion in prescribers and new starts, with volume doubling late in July.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Orforglipron (Foundayo) prescribers grew from about 8,000 to 36,000, U.S. new starts reached roughly 1 in 4, and management cited volume doubling in the last week of July versus a month earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Foundayo (orforglipron) ... is tracking well behind Novo's oral Wegovy”; IQVIA showed scripts “down three straight weeks from a 21,648 peak.”

surprises.description: The preview expected a revenue-guidance raise but highlighted risk to EPS from price erosion. Lilly also raised its EPS outlook by $2.78 at the midpoint before a $3.03-per-share IPR&D charge impact; the resulting $35.50–36.50 range has a lower high end than the prior $35.50–37.00 range, so the underlying improvement was more favorable than the headline range suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lifted non-GAAP EPS guidance to $35.50–$36.50, a $2.78 midpoint increase before the $3.03 IPR&D charge impact.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS: $35.50–37.00” at Q1; the preview also says “Erosion above the guided range would put the FY EPS range at risk regardless of volume.”

surprises.description: The preview gave no Q2 geographic outlook, but Lilly reported strong growth across multiple ex-U.S. markets, including 93% in China and 136% in the rest of the world.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ex-U.S. revenue surged with China up 93%, rest-of-world up 136%, Europe up 55% and Japan up 30% in constant currency.”

surprises.description: The preview noted that retatrutide's BLA timing was a watch item but did not anticipate Phase III results. Lilly reported positive results in three Phase III trials, including high-dose weight loss approaching bariatric-surgery levels and substantial knee-pain reduction, and plans a U.S. BLA submission in Q1 2027 despite ongoing litigation over the biologic pathway.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retatrutide posted positive results in three Phase III Triumph trials (with high-dose weight loss approaching bariatric-surgery levels and ~75% osteoarthritis knee-pain reduction), and Lilly plans a U.S. BLA submission in Q1 2027 despite ongoing FByOA litigation over the biologic pathway.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's catalyst checklist said: “Watch for BD pace, retatrutide BLA timing, and manufacturing capex.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag a new Medicare obesity-coverage program. Lilly said the bridge program gives 20 million eligible seniors access for $50 per month and expands U.S. obesity-medicine coverage by 35%, with early uptake primarily injectable and often from new patients.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Medicare GLP-1 bridge program launched July 1 gives 20 million eligible seniors obesity coverage at $50 per month, expanding U.S. obesity-medicine coverage by 35%, with early uptake skewing ~80% injectable and 60%-70% new patients.”

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate the reported adjuvant RET-positive lung-cancer result: selpercatinib reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 83% versus placebo.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Selpercatinib reduced risk of recurrence or death by 83% versus placebo in adjuvant RET-positive lung cancer.”

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate the reported pirtobrutinib CLL trial result: progression or death fell 45%, and 68% among patients previously treated with a BTK inhibitor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pirtobrutinib cut progression or death by 45% (68% after prior BTK inhibitor) in previously treated CLL.”

surprises.description: Q2 sales of $250 million exceeded the $237.54 million consensus by about 5%. Much of the increase was sulfur pass-through, which management said had no material EBITDA impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 sales were $250 million”; approximately “$55 million” of the $74 million year-over-year increase was sulfur cost pass-through “with no material EBITDA impact.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $237.54M”

surprises.description: Full-year sales guidance rose to $1.02–1.06 billion, well above the prior $890–970 million range and the $966.73 million consensus. The increase is partly a pass-through effect: sulfur pass-through is now expected to be $220 million rather than $155 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 sales guidance was raised to $1.02-1.06 billion (from $890-970 million), driven partly by higher sulfur pass-through now expected at $220 million versus $155 million prior.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $966.73M | $890–970M”; “Sulfur pass-through assumption is about $155M.”

surprises.description: The company raised the low end of its legacy-business EBITDA outlook to $185 million and expects legacy EBITDA growth of about 11% at the midpoint. The preview’s base case anticipated no organic raise, so this points to a better legacy outlook than that scenario expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $195-207 million, with legacy business guidance low end lifted to $185 million”; management sees “legacy business EBITDA growing about 11% year-over-year at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base ... FY range narrowed to about $196–208M including Calabrian; no organic raise.” The preview also said to watch for “an organic EBITDA raise stated separately from the Calabrian contribution.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance increased at the low end, from $40–55 million to $45–55 million. The top end is unchanged, but the company now expects at least $5 million more cash flow than under its prior guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance was raised to $45-55 million.”
