surprises.fact_evidence: “A one-time charge of approximately $3 million will hit Q3 selling expenses (excluded from adjusted EBITDA) related to a planned distribution center relocation.”

surprises.description: The regional results showed a pronounced split: Australia/New Zealand declined 13%, while rest-of-world sales rose 50.5% on the new UK distribution center; US sales grew 2.1%. The preview said segment detail was not covered and offered no regional expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Australia/New Zealand region net sales declined 13% to $39.8 million”; US sales grew “2.1% to $110.7 million” and rest-of-world grew “50.5% to $9.6 million driven by the new UK distribution center.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted: “segment and unit-economics detail is not covered.”

surprises.description: Princess Polly’s disclosed expansion plan extended beyond the preview’s near-term store-count discussion: management said it could add up to 10 US stores in 2027, with five leases signed, and sees long-term potential for at least 100 US stores.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Princess Polly operates 13 US stores plus two Australian locations, plans up to 10 new US stores in 2027 (five leases signed), and sees long-term potential for at least 100 US stores.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Princess Polly was at 13 US stores and had a target of 17 US and 2 Australian stores by year-end; it did not mention a 2027 plan or 100-store potential.

surprises.description: Culture Kings plans to resume opening US stores in Q4 2026, its first new US locations since 2022. The preview did not flag this reopening or provide an expectation for it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Culture Kings will open its first new US stores since 2022 in Q4 2026 (Puerto Rico and a major metro), targeting 4,500-6,000 sq ft formats smaller than the Las Vegas flagship.”

surprises.description: The balance sheet strengthened, with total debt down to $99.9 million and net leverage improving to 3.37x. That was a favorable update against the preview’s focus on a $109.6 million debt balance and whether tariff-refund cash would be applied to debt, although the call facts do not say whether the refund was collected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total debt [was] down 8.1% to $99.9 million, and net leverage improving to 3.37x from 3.5x a year ago”; inventory was down 13.6% to $79.9 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “$109.6M debt balance” and said to watch “cash collected in Q2 and whether it goes to the $109.6M debt balance.”

surprises.description: Customer metrics were mixed: active customers grew 4.4%, but total orders dipped 0.5% while average order value was flat. The preview gave no expectation for these measures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month active customers rose 4.4% to 4.31 million while average order value held steady at $78 and total orders dipped 0.5% to 2.04 million.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA of $8.7 million was within the preview’s implied $8.7–8.9 million consensus range and the company’s $8.5–9.0 million Q2 guidance.
The full-year net sales guidance of $625–635 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $30–32 million were reiterated, as the preview’s base case expected the revenue range to be reaffirmed.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $9.41 substantially exceeded the preview’s $7.40 working midpoint, although it was close to the preview’s roughly $9.40 peer-implied figure and above its roughly $9 buy-side bar. The reported result included about $450 million of favorable mark-to-market impacts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted earnings were $3.8 billion, with adjusted EPS of $9.41” and were “boosted by roughly $450 million of favorable mark-to-market impacts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The preview uses $7.40 as a working midpoint”; it also says the peer read-through “points to about $9.40 for PSX” and puts “the buy-side bar near $9.00.”

surprises.description: Management indicated a faster and more ambitious debt-reduction path than the preview anticipated: net debt was $16.5 billion at quarter-end, is expected below $16 billion by year-end, and the company plans to reach its $17 billion target ahead of schedule. It also introduced a lower net-debt target of approximately $13.5–14 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expects net debt below $16 billion by year-end,” plans “to hit its $17 billion debt target ahead of the 2027 schedule,” and signaled “a new net debt target of approximately $13.5 billion to $14 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists a “debt target of $19B by YE2026 (then $17B by YE2027).”

surprises.description: Refining capture was strong, with 98% of the market indicator captured in Q2, and management guided to about 95% capture in Q3 rather than signaling the caution the preview identified as a risk. The preview did not give a specific capture-rate forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Refining captured 98% of its market indicator in Q2,” with “roughly 95% capture in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warns that “any Q3 caution would weaken the bull case” and says realized margin below “about $18–20/bbl would read as a capture-rate failure.”

surprises.description: Refining operating cost was already close to the $5.50-per-barrel 2027 target, suggesting faster progress toward the goal than the preview’s target-only discussion established. Management also described the cost-reduction work as structural and permanent.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Refining Q2 operating cost of $5.57/barrel is closing in on the annualized $5.50/barrel target for 2027,” supported by “over 200 cost-reduction initiatives” described as “structural and permanent.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview notes Q1 refining opex of “$6.21/bbl, with a target of $5.50 by 2027.”

surprises.description: Management signaled an increase in share repurchases in the second half, addressing the preview’s call for a buyback step-up. The reported Q2 return included $379 million of buybacks, but the preview gave no numerical quarterly repurchase expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: PSX returned “$887 million to shareholders in Q2, including $379 million of buybacks,” and “expects to increase share repurchases in the second half of the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says the market would want “a step-up in quarterly repurchases, given the at-least-50%-of-operating-cash-flow return policy.”

surprises.description: Rodeo Renewable Fuels had an unexpectedly strong operating and market backdrop: utilization reached a record above nameplate, while renewable diesel prices and RINs roughly doubled versus 2025. The preview did not flag these as drivers to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rodeo Renewable Fuels ran above nameplate at record 106% utilization,” with “RD prices and RINs roughly doubling versus 2025 due to the Iran conflict.”

surprises.description: A one-time $100 million tariff-refund benefit was reported, an earnings tailwind not identified in the preview. The separate $47 million renewable mark-to-market gain was part of a broader reversal possibility the preview had already raised.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 included “a one-time $100 million tariff-refund benefit and a $47 million mark-to-market gain.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a new Mid-Continent-to-Western U.S. fuel project, with final investment decision expected within about a month and delivery beginning in late 2029. The preview discussed rising midstream investment but did not identify this project or its near-term FID timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Western Gateway Mid-Continent-to-Western U.S. fuel project is expected to reach FID within about a month and begin delivering by late 2029.”

surprises.description: Management highlighted substantial refining capacity outages in Asia, the Middle East, and Russia, and quantified the benefit to annual EBITDA from a wider WTI/WCS spread. The preview did not identify these specific market factors or the $140 million-per-dollar sensitivity.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management flagged “roughly 7 million barrels/day of Asian/Middle East refining and 1.4 million b/d of Russian capacity” offline and said “every $1 widening in the WTI/WCS spread adds about $140 million to annual EBITDA.”

in_line: Midstream remained on track for the $4.5 billion annualized run-rate EBITDA target by year-end 2027, which the preview had already cited as the target.
Management’s commitment to return over 50% of operating cash flow to shareholders was consistent with the preview’s stated capital-return policy.

surprises.description: A10 reported Q2 revenue of $80.1 million, above the preview’s derived estimate of about $77 million. The beat was roughly 4% despite the preview’s base case of $77–79 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue of $80.1 million, up 15.5% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (Q2) … Consensus ~$77M (derived)” and base case “$77–79M.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS was $0.25, materially above the preview’s estimated GAAP EPS of $0.15–$0.17. The preview also noted that GAAP and non-GAAP EPS should not be confused; this comparison uses its GAAP estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 diluted EPS was $0.25 (net income of $18.7 million).”

surprises.description: Management raised FY26 revenue growth guidance to 12%–14% from 10%–12%, and EPS growth guidance to 14%–16% from 12%–14%. That exceeded the preview’s stated bar of lifting the revenue floor to about 12% or taking EPS growth above 14%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to 12%-14% (from 10%-12%) and EPS growth guidance to 14%-16% (from 12%-14%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The market now needs the revenue floor lifted to about 12% or the EPS growth range taken above 14%.”

surprises.description: Product revenue reached $49 million and grew approximately 25%, beating the preview’s $44–46 million estimate and exceeding its roughly 14% growth threshold for supporting reacceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Product revenue grew approximately 25% year-over-year in Q2, reaching $49 million (61% of total).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Product revenue: ~$44–46M (57–59% mix)” and “Needs roughly $45M+ and +14% or better.”

surprises.description: The Microsoft relationship expanded on a multi-year basis with mutual performance commitments and no prebuy requirements. The preview identified Microsoft as the central AI-related opportunity and risk and asked whether AI revenue was recurring or lumpy; the reported commitments and absence of prebuys provide more concrete and reassuring terms than it anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A significant multi-year expansion of its Microsoft relationship with mutual performance commitments, but no prebuy requirements.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Microsoft engagement … is the core bull driver and the core bear risk” and “Check … whether AI revenue is recurring or lumpy.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin was 30.5%, above the preview’s FY26 target range of 28%–30%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA … $25.4 million (30.5% of revenue).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin … FY26 target range” of “28–30%.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted the risk that free cash flow might miss again after Q1’s timing-related impact. A10 reported Q2 free cash flow of $26.9 million, providing a positive update on that flagged concern, although the preview gave no Q2 cash-flow estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was $26.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If FCF misses again, Q1's ‘timing’ explanation becomes a trend.”

surprises.description: The preview focused on AI and hyperscaler concentration as a key risk; the reported customer mix instead showed enterprise customers at 60% of Q2 revenue and about half of trailing-12-month revenue, with management describing growth as balanced versus service providers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enterprise customers represented 60% of Q2 revenue and about half of trailing-12-month revenue, reflecting balanced growth versus service providers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AI/hyperscaler concentration” was a key issue to watch, including customer-concentration disclosure.

surprises.description: The preview did not flag geographic divergence, but A10 reported that the Americas benefited from AI infrastructure build-outs while EMEA and Japan faced geopolitical and macroeconomic pressures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Americas region accounted for 68% of global revenue, benefiting from AI infrastructure build-outs, while EMEA and Japan faced geopolitical and macroeconomic pressures.”

in_line: Non-GAAP gross margin was 80.3%, within the preview’s 79%–81% guidance range and around its roughly 80% expectation.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $49.1 million, below the roughly $51.96 million consensus and the preview’s $50–53 million base case. The shortfall was modest at the headline level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenues fell to $49.1 million in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue consensus was ~$51.96M”; the base scenario was “$50–53M.”

surprises.description: Auryxia revenue came in at $25.5 million, below the preview’s $28–31 million base case and around $30 million implied expectation. This puts the result in the preview’s downside range for generic erosion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Auryxia revenue dropped to $25.5 million from $47.2 million due to generic competition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Auryxia revenue vs. about $30M implied,” with a base case of “$28–31M”; it also warned that “a print below about $26M would cut FY26 materially.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a $1.9 million commercial reorganization expense that the preview did not flag. It contributed to the quarter’s loss, though the preview already expected a loss-making quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company reported a net loss of $8.9 million, “including a $1.9 million commercial reorganization expense.”

surprises.description: Management’s runway statement was qualified by the need to refinance the senior secured term loan. The preview anticipated a reaffirmation of more than two years of runway but did not identify this refinancing condition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents were approximately $155.5 million” and management believes it funds operations “for at least two years assuming a planned refinancing of its senior secured term loan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had committed only to “more than two years” of runway; the preview said a runway statement was a key point to watch.

surprises.description: Management reported no meaningful DaVita adoption inflection yet, despite the rollout of a dosing protocol. The preview highlighted DaVita and large-dialysis-organization discussions as important, but this report indicates near-term adoption remains limited while management expects implementation to support growth into 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DaVita, representing 200,000 patients, has not yet shown a meaningful adoption inflection,” though it rolled out a “village-wide three-times-weekly dosing protocol in early June” and management expects implementation to drive growth into 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “contract talks with large dialysis organizations such as DaVita” and “2027 post-TDAPA framing” as key issues, and described named large-dialysis-organization talks as part of its bull scenario.

surprises.description: Akebia initiated an ebribafusp Phase II basket trial, a pipeline development not anticipated in the preview. Initial data is not expected until 2027, so the immediate news is progress rather than a near-term readout.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Akebia initiated a Phase II open-label basket trial of ebribafusp enrolling up to 30 patients” across three kidney diseases, with “initial data expected in 2027.”

surprises.description: Commercial metrics showed broader Vafseo reach and patient persistence: about one-third of prescribers were outside USRC, some previously discontinued QD patients restarted, and first-refill adherence was high. The preview focused on exit patients and revenue but did not anticipate these specific indicators.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately one-third of Vafseo prescribers are now outside of USRC,” “roughly 25% of previously discontinued QD patients have restarted therapy,” and “first-refill adherence has reached about 89%.”

in_line: Vafseo revenue and patient growth were broadly in line with the preview: revenue was $21.3 million versus expectations near $20 million, and more than 10,500 active patients versus an expected 10,000–11,000 exit patients.
The VOICE trial result was consistent with the preview’s account that the interim analysis met stopping criteria and showed hospitalization benefits versus ESAs.
The expected 2027 revenue decline was confirmed: the preview already cited consensus for a 22.6% decline and flagged the end of TDAPA on December 31, 2026 as a key pricing issue.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $70 million, about $50 million above the $20 million guidance midpoint—far stronger than the preview’s base case of $20–35 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $70 million” and “exceeded the guidance midpoint by approximately $50 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | $20M | ≈ guide”; the base scenario expected “$20–35M.”

surprises.description: Q2 medical margin reached $197 million, about $74 million above the $123 million guidance midpoint and well beyond the preview’s bull-case threshold of $150 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 medical margin was $197 million” and “beat[] the guidance midpoint by roughly $74 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Medical margin | $123M | ≈ guide”; the bull scenario called for “$150M+.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to an $85 million midpoint, above the previous $10–40 million range and the preview’s cited $75 million threshold for removing the implied H2 loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to approximately … $85 million adjusted EBITDA at the midpoints.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Previous FY2026 guidance was “Adj. EBITDA: $10–40M”; the preview flagged “≥$75M as the raise that would remove the implied H2 loss.”

surprises.description: FY2026 medical margin guidance rose to $485 million, above the previous $350–400 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to approximately … $485 million medical margin … at the midpoints.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Previous FY2026 guidance was “Medical margin: $350–400M.”

surprises.description: Management doubled its 2026 year-over-year risk-adjustment estimate, net of the V28 impact, to about 3% from the 1.5% estimate given at Q1. The preview did not anticipate this estimate change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 2026 year-over-year risk adjustment estimate was raised to approximately 3% net of the V28 impact, double the prior 1.5% estimate given at Q1.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s focus on a 7% FY2026 cost-trend assumption and Q1’s 7.4% trend, management reported better underlying experience: the 2025 estimate improved to 5.8% and Q1 2026 trends developed into the low 6% range. It nevertheless kept a roughly 7% assumption for the rest of 2026 because paid-claims visibility is limited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The full-year 2025 cost trend estimate improved to 5.8% from the 6.2% estimated at Q1, while Q1 2026 trends developed favorably into the low 6% range.” Management “prudently reserved Q2 cost trend in the low 7% range and assumes roughly 7% for the remainder of 2026 due to limited paid claims visibility.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance assumes 7.0% for FY26. Q1 recorded 7.4%.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that Part D is now less than 15% of the book and intends to reduce that exposure further, while recording Part D net in revenue to limit seasonality. The preview anticipated possible Q2 commentary but did not specify this exposure level or approach.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Part D exposure now sits at less than 15% of the book,” with management intending “to reduce it further while recording Part D net in revenue to limit seasonality effects.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said reconciliation data arrives in Q3 2026, so Q2 may only bring commentary.”

surprises.description: Management reported substantial ACO REACH savings and quality results and forecast $25–30 million of ACO REACH EBITDA in 2026; the preview provided no expectation for these results or the EBITDA contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 2024 ACO REACH results delivered $229 million in gross savings with a 96% average quality score across eight ACOs,” and management expects “$25-30 million ACO REACH EBITDA in 2026.”

in_line: FY2026 revenue guidance of approximately $5.8 billion remained within the prior $5.68–5.81 billion range.
Management retained roughly a 7% cost-trend assumption for the remainder of 2026, consistent with the preview’s 7.0% FY2026 assumption.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $310 million, about $8.5 million above the preview’s $301.5 million consensus and also above the company’s prior $300–303 million guide. That is a clear upside to the current estimate, although the preview noted an older pre-guidance consensus near $310 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 GAAP revenue was $310 million, up only 1.2% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP revenue | $301.5M | $300–303M”

surprises.description: Management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $1.207–1.217 billion from the preview’s expected $1.185–1.205 billion range, making the projected decline at the midpoint less severe. The unlevered free-cash-flow range also moved up slightly, while the adjusted operating-margin target remained at 37%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to GAAP revenue of $1.207–1.217 billion (a 3% decline at midpoint) with a 37% adjusted operating margin and unlevered free cash flow of $403–423 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guide (unchanged since May): revenue $1.185–1.205B”; “unlevered FCF $400–420M.”

surprises.description: Net revenue retention fell to 89%, one percentage point below the preview’s 90% flat expectation. This was weaker than expected but remained within the preview’s 89–90% base-case range and above its 88% bear trigger.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenue retention fell to 89% in Q2, a step down from 90% in the prior three quarters, pressured by longer sales cycles and software weakness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue retention | 90% (flat)”; “A print of 88% or below is the bear trigger.”

surprises.description: The already-weak downmarket ACV trend worsened, falling 12% year over year versus 11% in Q1, while upmarket ACV growth slowed to 3% from 5%. This extends the deterioration the preview had flagged in both areas.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Downmarket ACV declined 12% year-over-year”; “upmarket ACV grew only 3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Downmarket ACV –11% Y/Y and worsening”; “upmarket +5%.”

surprises.description: The company recorded a $651 million noncash goodwill impairment charge, an unanticipated large charge attributed primarily to the decline in market capitalization after Q1 results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company recorded a $651 million noncash goodwill impairment charge primarily driven by the decline in market capitalization following Q1 results.”

surprises.description: The data-led operations business grew 20%, and ACV from customers spending at least $1 million rose 16%, showing areas of substantial growth not highlighted in the preview. The preview’s concern about large customers focused on a different measure: the count of $100K-plus ACV customers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The operations business (primarily data, not seat-based) grew 20% year-over-year, and ACV from $1 million-plus customers rose 16%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating margin reached 35%, modestly above the preview’s guide-implied 34.5% margin, implying better operating-income performance than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income margin reached 35%, up 130 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating income | ~$104M (guide-implied) | $103–106M | ~34.5% margin.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed specific capital actions not anticipated by the preview: it repurchased shares and retired senior notes below face value, producing an $11 million gain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased 6.3 million shares at an average price of $4.51 for $28 million and retired $58.5 million of senior notes for $48 million, generating an $11 million gain.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The company has over $1B of remaining buyback authorization and 2.4x net leverage on $1.3B gross debt.”

in_line: The FY2026 adjusted operating-margin target remained at 37%, matching the preview’s expected 37% margin.

The preview anticipated continued restructuring activity and $45–60 million of charges across Q2–Q3; the reported $35 million charge is consistent with that broad expectation, though the call facts also say several hundred more reductions are expected.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $41 million, far above the preview’s own ~$15 million model. The preview noted there was no clean consensus figure and warned that deferred-revenue timing made the headline less informative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 GAAP revenue was $41 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Preview's own model (not consensus): Q2 revenue ~$15M.”

surprises.description: Arcus raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $65–75 million from the prior $50–65 million range. The new range is higher than the company’s previous guide, although its midpoint is below the preview’s cited Street estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “full-year 2026 guidance of $65-75 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company FY26 revenue guide: $50–65M (raised from $45–55M at Q4-25).”

surprises.description: The preview expected the ARC-20 update around mid-2026 and said a delay to ESMO would be a mild disappointment; Arcus instead plans to present the data at an October investor event before ESMO. The planned update is broader than the preview’s expected ~45-patient combo update, spanning more than 200 patients and including late-line overall-survival looks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In an October investor event before ESMO, Arcus will release ARC-20 data across first, second, and late-line settings from over 200 patients, including OS looks with ~28 months median follow-up in the 120-patient late-line monotherapy cohort.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ARC-20 casdatifan + cabozantinib update (~45 patients, IO-experienced). Guided for ‘mid-2026’”; “A delay to ESMO (Oct 2026) would be a mild disappointment.”

surprises.description: Arcus disclosed a 7% primary progression rate in the first-line casdatafan-plus-Zim cohort, compared with roughly 30% for historical anti-PD-1 monotherapy—a favorable efficacy signal not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The casdatafan plus Zim first-line cohort showed a 7% primary progression rate (2 of 30 patients) versus roughly 30% for anti-PD-1 monotherapy historically.”

surprises.description: The preview said the first-line Phase 3 design and partner were unresolved; Arcus named PEAK-20 as a registrational Phase 3 of casdatafan plus Ipi-Nevo and said it remains on track to start by year-end 2026. This makes the first-line trial design more concrete than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A registrational frontline Phase 3 trial called PEAK-20, evaluating casdatafan plus Ipi-Nevo, is on track to be initiated by the end of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “1L Phase 3 design and partner. Candidate partners include BMS/BioNTech pumitamig (6/3), AVEO tivozanib (7/22), and Summit ivonescimab (7/22). Which backbone is chosen determines whether the 1L opportunity is underwritable.”

surprises.description: Rather than only resolving a single first-line backbone, Arcus said it had executed multiple collaborations with BMS, Summit, and Aveo to test casdatafan combinations, while retaining full program rights outside Japan and certain Asian territories.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Arcus executed multiple new collaborations (BMS, Summit, Aveo) to test casdatafan combinations while retaining full program rights outside Japan and certain Asian territories.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Candidate partners include BMS/BioNTech pumitamig (6/3), AVEO tivozanib (7/22), and Summit ivonescimab (7/22). Which backbone is chosen determines whether the 1L opportunity is underwritable.”

surprises.description: Management said casdatafan now has no competition in the frontline HIF-2-alpha inhibitor space after Merck’s LightSpark 012 failure, an unexpected improvement in the competitive picture.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Following Merck's LightSpark 012 failure, management states casdatafan now has no competition in the frontline HIF-2-alpha inhibitor space.”

surprises.description: Management described casdatafan as having potential to become a $5–10 billion drug and the backbone therapy across all lines of clear cell RCC treatment—a much more expansive stated ambition than the preview discussed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management believes casdatafan has potential to become a $5-10 billion drug and expects it to become the backbone therapy across all lines of clear cell RCC treatment.”

surprises.description: Arcus reported that AB102 is entering the clinic this month, with PK data expected in Q4 2026; this pipeline milestone was not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The AB102 oral MRGPRX2 antagonist is entering the clinic this month with PK data expected in Q4 2026.”

surprises.description: Arcus said the pancreatic cancer Phase 3 PRISM-1 study of quemliclustat is expected to read out in the first half of 2027, a specific pipeline catalyst absent from the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pancreatic cancer Phase 3 PRISM-1 study of quemliclustat is expected to read out in the first half of 2027.”

in_line: PEAK-1 enrollment remains on track for completion by year-end 2026, consistent with the preview’s stated enrollment target.

Cash and investments were $775 million at June 30, matching the preview’s ~$775 million model; management still expects year-end cash near $600 million and runway into at least the second half of 2028.
The first-line Phase 3 remains on track to start by year-end 2026, consistent with the preview’s prior timing expectation.

surprises.description: The preview expected Q2 adjusted EBITDA to be a loss of $0.5–1.0 million under company guidance, or around breakeven to a $0.5 million loss by consensus. Instead, Zevia reported positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $0.5 million exceeded expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: Loss of $0.5–1.0M”; consensus was “~breakeven to -$0.5M.”

surprises.description: The preview estimated gross margin around 47–48% and described back-half pressure as slight. Q2 margin came in at 48.9%, but Q3 is now expected to fall to approximately 46%, alongside an adjusted EBITDA loss of $3–3.5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin was 48.9% in Q2 but is expected to fall to approximately 46% in Q3”; Q3 guidance calls for “an adjusted EBITDA loss of negative $3 million to negative $3.5 million” due to elevated aluminum costs, deeper promotions, and higher marketing spend.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross margin at “~47–48%” and said management indicated “slight pressure” in the back half.

surprises.description: The preview anticipated that the new CEO might discuss strategy or route-to-market changes, but did not identify singles as a priority. The CEO named singles the top priority and sized the opportunity at about $80 million, with Zevia holding essentially no share in that format.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new CEO identified the singles format as the top priority, estimating an ~$80 million opportunity” given 20% share in multi-pack soda and essentially zero share in singles.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for numbers versus a deferred strategy review, plus any route-to-market or SKU changes.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a further $3–5 million of planned cost savings beginning in Q1 2027, beyond the $20 million already removed. The preview did not flag this specific additional savings plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is “on track to achieve $3-5 million in additional cost savings, primarily in COGS and selling expenses, beginning in Q1 2027, on top of $20 million already removed from the business.”

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate the reported scale of the Cardi B campaign or a follow-on co-developed product. Management reported substantial campaign reach and engagement and said the signature product is planned for early January 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: The campaign generated “nearly 29.5 billion social video views, 1.8 billion PR earned media impressions, and over 1.7 million engagements”; a new Cardi B co-developed signature product is planned for “early January 2027.”

in_line: Q2 net sales were $45 million, at the high end of the pre-announced range and consistent with the preview’s approximately $45 million high-end expectation.
Full-year net sales guidance of $170–175 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of a $2–4 million loss were maintained, as the preview expected.
First-half sales growth of 10.4% was consistent with the preview’s estimate of about 10% growth.
The approximately $11 million combined fuel and aluminum cost pressure and the plan for no further price increases this year were already flagged in the preview.

surprises.description: Blue Bird reported Q3 revenue of $517 million, above the preview’s $498.7 million consensus and roughly $500 million company-guide midpoint. That is a clear, moderate beat on the quarter’s top line.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue of $517 million (up $119 million year-over-year)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $498.7M (Zacks) | ~$500M midpoint”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $71 million, ahead of the preview’s derived $66–68 million range. The preview expected roughly 13.3–13.6% consolidated margin; reported EBITDA margin was 13.8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “record Q3 adjusted EBITDA of $71 million” and “compressing EBITDA margin to 13.8%”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$66–68M (derived)” and “Adj. EBITDA margin | ~13.3–13.6% (derived)”

surprises.description: Legacy Blue Bird’s adjusted EBITDA margin was 16.1% excluding Micro Bird, above the preview’s expectation that core margin would run about 14.7–15%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “an ex-Micro Bird record of 16.1%”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “legacy BLBD (running about 14.7–15%)”

surprises.description: Micro Bird contributed about $123 million in quarterly revenue, versus the preview’s estimate of roughly $100 million. The preview expected consolidation to add revenue, but the reported contribution was materially larger than that estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Micro Bird was consolidated for the first time, contributing ~$123 million in revenue”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consolidation adds roughly $100M of quarterly revenue”

surprises.description: Micro Bird reduced reported gross margin by 180 basis points, more dilution than the preview’s expected 100–120 basis points. This was a larger margin drag than anticipated, even though the resulting consolidated EBITDA margin was above the preview’s estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “reducing reported gross margin by 180 basis points”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “adjusted EBITDA margin falls roughly 100–120 bps”

surprises.description: Adjusted free-cash-flow guidance rose to $125–135 million from the prior $100–125 million range, exceeding the preview’s stated full-year target at the upper end and raising its low end by $25 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “adjusted free cash flow of $125-135 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted FCF $100–125M”

surprises.description: Blue Bird disclosed that unit sales fell 7% year over year because GSA and fleet units were held in finished-goods inventory, with revenue recognition pushed into Q4 and fiscal 2027. The preview did not flag this unit decline or the timing shift; it only provided a derived unit estimate, and the call facts give no actual unit count to compare with it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “unit sales fell 7% year-over-year due to a large number of GSA and fleet units held in finished goods inventory that will be revenue-recognized in Q4 and fiscal 2027”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My 3,100–3,300 unit estimate is derived and could move materially with Micro Bird's Type A mix.”

surprises.description: Blue Bird announced an expanded Ford collaboration to enter the Class 5–6 commercial strip-chassis market, a business the preview did not anticipate. The plan adds a stated $1.4 billion to its addressable market and targets about 10,000 units by 2030 and more than $100 million of longer-term adjusted EBITDA; production is expected in Q1 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “expanded collaboration with Ford to design, manufacture and sell next-generation F-53/F-59 Class 5-6 commercial strip chassis, running through 2033 with extension potential to 2036”; “expands Blue Bird's total addressable market by $1.4 billion, targeting ~10,000 units by 2030 and generating longer-term adjusted EBITDA of $100 million-plus at 14-15% margins”; “Chassis production is expected to begin in calendar Q1 2028”

surprises.description: The new chassis entry has a defined near-term funding requirement that was not covered in the preview: the Detroit Chassis assets cost $7 million, but the broader market entry requires about $90 million of investment in 2027, including $50 million of CapEx. The company said this would require no equity dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Detroit Chassis asset acquisition costs only $7 million, with total chassis market entry requiring a ~$90 million investment in 2027 (of which $50 million is CapEx), and no equity dilution.”

surprises.description: Average Blue Bird bus revenue per unit rose about $10,000 year over year, with price increases, tariff recovery, and EV mix cited as drivers. The preview did not anticipate this ASP increase; management characterized tariff management as margin-neutral.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Average Blue Bird bus revenue per unit rose approximately $10,000 year-over-year, driven mainly by price increases plus tariff recovery and EV mix, reflecting margin-neutral tariff management.”

in_line: The full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint moved only modestly, to $247.5 million from the prior range’s $245 million midpoint, consistent with the preview’s base case of a nudge toward about $250 million.
Full-year revenue guidance stayed at a $1.75 billion midpoint, in line with the preview’s prior $1.725–1.775 billion range.
The preview expected Micro Bird consolidation to pull down reported margins, and the call reported a diluted consolidated margin, although the gross-margin reduction was larger than previewed.
The roughly 4,900-unit combined backlog includes about 1,300 Micro Bird units, leaving approximately 3,600 units excluding Micro Bird—close to the preview’s reference point of just under 3,600 units.

surprises.description: TTM reported Q2 net sales of $1.0 billion, above the preview’s $964.55 million consensus and the $970 million top of its guidance range. The roughly 4% beat over consensus was a meaningful upside surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q2 2026 net sales of $1.0 billion,” “exceeding guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … Consensus $964.55M”; Q2 guidance was “$930–970M.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $0.99, beating the preview’s $0.92 consensus and exceeding the $0.88 guidance ceiling. The gap to consensus was about 8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS reached an all-time high of $0.99 per diluted share … beating guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS … Consensus $0.92”; Q2 guidance was “$0.82–0.88.”

surprises.description: Q3 guidance was substantially above the preview’s derived bar: sales of $1.10–$1.14 billion versus roughly $1.03–$1.06 billion, and EPS of $1.21–$1.27 versus roughly $0.98–$1.05. This points to a much stronger near-term outlook than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for net sales of $1.10–$1.14 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $1.21–$1.27, with further sequential growth expected in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Derived Q3'26 bar … Roughly $1.03–1.06B revenue and $0.98–1.05 non-GAAP EPS.”

surprises.description: TTM raised its 2026 sales outlook to about $4.4 billion, above the preview’s roughly $4.0 billion Street revenue assumption and the prior $4 billion target. EPS guidance approaching $5 also exceeded the preview’s estimated non-GAAP range of $3.70–$3.80.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to approximately $4.4 billion in sales (above the prior $4 billion target) with non-GAAP EPS approaching $5.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 street revenue of ~$4.00B”; “the non-GAAP FY26 figure is closer to $3.70–3.80.”

surprises.description: Data Center and Networking was 40% of Q2 sales, two percentage points below the preview’s 42% guide. That shortfall was followed by a much higher Q3 outlook: the segment is expected to reach 49% of sales as N+M production ramps.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data Center and Networking sales surged 91% year-over-year to represent 40% of Q2 sales, and are expected to jump to 49% of net sales in Q3 as N+M production ramps.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Data center and networking share of sales against the 42% guide.”

surprises.description: TTM said the N+M asymmetrical PCB ramp will contribute about $600 million in second-half revenue, with yields already exceeding expectations and margins expected to improve. The preview discussed H2 growth generally but did not anticipate this scale or the better-than-expected yields.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The N+M asymmetrical PCB ramp involves about $600 million of revenue in the second half (roughly one-third in Q3, two-thirds in Q4) with yields exceeding expectations and margins expected to improve.”

surprises.description: TTM disclosed that its 90-day cancellable backlog had risen 81% year over year to $901 million, a substantial demand indicator not quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 90-day cancellable backlog [was] up 81% year-over-year to $901 million.”

surprises.description: The call reported A&D growth of 14%, a $1.7 billion backlog, and a record qualified proposal pipeline above $7 billion. The preview gave no A&D growth, backlog, or pipeline expectations, so these sizeable opportunity measures were not anticipated there.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The A&D segment grew 14% year-over-year with a $1.7 billion backlog and a record qualified proposal pipeline exceeding $7 billion.”

surprises.description: TTM said the pending STG and ILFA acquisitions will add less than 5% to sales but be moderately EBITDA-accretive and give it its first European footprint. The preview flagged the deals and their undisclosed purchase price, but did not provide expectations for their contribution or strategic impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pending acquisitions of Switzerland's STG and Germany's ILFA … will add less than 5% incremental sales, be moderately EBITDA-accretive, and establish TTM's first European footprint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The purchase price has not been disclosed”; the preview flagged “STG / ILFA acquisition” and said “a coherent capital-allocation answer is needed.”

surprises.description: A deal-related currency swap created a $14 million non-cash GAAP loss, an acquisition-related charge not mentioned in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A deal-related currency swap created a $14 million non-cash GAAP loss.”

in_line: Commercial book-to-bill was 1.63, close to the preview’s prior-quarter reference of 1.65; the preview had identified this metric as a key demand indicator.

surprises.description: The call said ad-supported streaming grew 10%, helped by non-recurring World Cup advertising, and that growth should normalize to mid-single digits in Q4. The preview gave no ad-supported growth or Q4 trajectory, so the call added both a temporary boost and a near-term slowdown outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ad-supported streaming grew 10% on an adjusted basis, boosted by non-recurring World Cup ad spending, and is expected to normalize to mid-single-digit growth in Q4.”

in_line: The preview said operating cash flow had already risen 209% to $142 million; the call likewise reported a 209% surge.
The call reaffirmed the 50–60% operating cash flow conversion target and said conversion was 55% over the last nine months, within that range.

The call reaffirmed high-single-digit revenue growth and double-digit adjusted OIBDA and EPS growth targets, as well as the high end of the 150–200 basis-point FY26 margin-expansion target flagged in the preview.

The call’s expectation that AI licensing would contribute materially to subscription streaming growth starting in FY2027 was consistent with the preview; it did not provide the quantitative bridge the preview identified as an open question.

surprises.description: Revenue was $83.3 million, above the preview’s $77.83 million consensus, and organic growth of 6.7% was also ahead of the preview’s roughly 4.3% estimate. The reported year-over-year decline was 10.9%, less severe than the preview’s implied 16.8% decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 reported revenue was $83.3 million, down 10.9% year-over-year … but organic revenue grew 6.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $77.83M”; “Revenue (organic, derived) … ~+4.3% organic.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was far above the preview’s estimated $5.5–6.5 million, even though the reported $14.5 million includes one-time items. The underlying adjusted EBITDA margin was also a record 9.8%, showing that the result was not solely the headline figure including those items.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $14.5 million (17.3% margin including one-time items)”; “all-time-high underlying adjusted EBITDA margin of 9.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$5.5–6.5M.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook to $23–25 million from $20–23 million, rather than reaffirming the prior range as the preview’s base case expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year guidance: … adjusted EBITDA to $23-25 million (from $20-23 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … FY guide reaffirmed”; “FY26 adjusted EBITDA guide ($20–23M). Reaffirm, narrow, or trim.”

surprises.description: Full-year organic revenue growth guidance increased to 5–7% from 4–6%, taking the range above the prior ceiling after Q2 organic growth exceeded the preview’s estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year guidance: organic revenue growth to 5-7% (from 4-6%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance: … FY organic growth 4–6%”; the base scenario expected the “FY guide reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Underlying adjusted gross margin reached 43.8%, above the preview’s estimated 42–43% range and its 43% threshold for a bullish result. Reported gross margin was higher still at 48.4%, but included a one-time tariff refund and apparel-liquidation dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Underlying adjusted gross margin of 43.8% (up ~340 bps)”; “Reported gross margin of 48.4% included a one-time $6.6 million tariff refund and dilution from apparel liquidation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin | ~42–43%”; “Holding at or above 43% with EBITDA in line is the bullish combination.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted gross margin guidance moved from “low 40%s” to “mid-40s,” a meaningful step-up from the prior outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year guidance: … adjusted gross margin to mid-40s (from low-40s).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 … adjusted gross margin guided to ‘low 40%s’”; the preview’s base scenario expected the FY guide to be reaffirmed.

surprises.description: Wipes consumption grew much faster than the category, led by flushable wipes, despite the preview not specifying an expected wipes growth rate. The reported outperformance was especially strong in flushables.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The total wipes portfolio grew consumption 26% versus 2% category growth, with flushable wipes up over 200%.”

surprises.description: Personal care grew substantially faster than its category, with the company retaining its #2 position in total baby personal care; the preview did not set a personal-care growth expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Personal care grew 19% versus 5% category growth, maintaining the #2 position in total baby personal care.”

surprises.description: The company had repurchased $18.7 million of shares year-to-date, more than the preview’s $11.3 million executed through May 1 implied for the remaining program. That leaves less of the $25 million authorization available than the preview’s approximately $13.7 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased 5.6 million shares for $18.7 million year-to-date.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buyback: $11.3M of $25M executed through May 1”; “Remaining ~$13.7M of the $25M buyback.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow was $35.3 million and the company ended the quarter with $105.9 million in cash and no debt. The preview did not provide an expectation for quarterly free cash flow or the quarter-end cash and debt position.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Generated $35.3 million in free cash flow (versus negative $3.8 million prior year)”; “ended the quarter with $105.9 million in cash and zero debt.”

surprises.description: The Q1 FY2027 revenue guide is $450–460 million, above the preview’s implied $425–435 million range and its stated $450 million threshold for a stronger outlook. Management also guided to a 27.1% operating margin and $0.40–0.42 EPS, for which the preview gave no Q1 estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 guidance calls for revenue of $450-460 million with operating margin of 27.1% (±40 bps) and EPS of $0.40-0.42.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 consensus of $1.80B implies a Q1 of roughly $425–435M” and “A guide above $450M would push FY27 estimates up.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue exceeded both the top of company guidance and consensus, though the gap was modest. Revenue was $443.1 million versus a guidance high end of $437 million and preview consensus of $432.95 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 FY2026 revenue reached $443.1 million … above the high end of guidance ($427-437 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Company guidance … $427–437M”; “Consensus … $432.95M.”

surprises.description: Q4 EPS came in above the top of the company’s range and consensus: $0.34 versus guidance of $0.29–0.31 and consensus of $0.30.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EPS of $0.34 exceeding the $0.29-0.31 guidance range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS … Company guidance … $0.29–0.31”; “Consensus … $0.30.”

surprises.description: Management pulled forward its target for a $500 million-plus quarterly revenue run rate: it now expects to reach that level during calendar 2027 rather than by exiting fiscal 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now expects to reach a $500 million+ quarterly revenue run rate during calendar 2027, pulled forward from the prior target of exiting fiscal 2028.”

surprises.description: NSE operating margin reached 20%, above the 18.7% guide and the preview’s stated watchpoint of clearing 20%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NSE … operating margin surging to 20% from just 4.6% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NSE operating margin. Guided to 18.7%. … Clearing 20% would be an early sign the margin path is working.”

surprises.description: NSE revenue was above the top of its guided range, reaching $353.9 million against guidance of $340–348 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NSE revenue grew 69.2% year-over-year to $353.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NSE revenue | $340–348M.”

surprises.description: The data center ecosystem reached approximately half of NSE revenue, moving beyond the preview’s description of a share approaching the high 40s. Excluding Spirent, the data center business more than doubled year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The data center ecosystem now accounts for approximately 50% of NSE revenue”; “Excluding Spirent, the data center business more than doubled year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management described it as ‘approaching high-40s%’ in Q3. Crossing 50% would support the AI-test thesis.”

surprises.description: FY2026 EPS exceeded the preview’s $0.94 consensus at $1.00, while revenue was slightly above the $1.51 billion consensus at $1.518 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY2026 revenue was $1.518 billion … and EPS doubling to $1.00 from $0.47.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 revenue / EPS … Consensus … $1.51B / $0.94.”

surprises.description: The company raised $575 million gross through a follow-on share offering and used the proceeds to fully repay Term Loan B. The debt repayment addresses the preview’s balance-sheet concern, but the offering also increased diluted shares to 261 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Completed a follow-on offering issuing ~12.78 million shares at $45 for $575 million gross, using proceeds to fully pay off the Term Loan B, raising diluted share count to 261 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash and investments $508.0M against total debt of $1,080.8M”; the preview said a second negative operating-cash-flow quarter would shift debate toward the balance sheet.

surprises.description: Q1 guidance includes a net $0.02 EPS benefit from an $11 million tariff refund, partly offset by variable costs from an extra 14th week—an earnings contribution not mentioned in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Including a net $0.02 benefit from an $11 million tariff refund offset by an extra 14th week of variable costs.”

surprises.description: Management said CPO revenue is beginning in the current quarter and is expected to accelerate in December; the preview discussed data-center testing but did not flag this product timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CPO (co-packaged optics) revenue is beginning this quarter and expected to accelerate in December.”

surprises.description: Wireless products remained a weak spot, with demand described as anemic, although stable; the preview did not identify wireless as an issue to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wireless products remain a weak spot with anemic but stable demand.”

surprises.description: The preview’s Nereus launch case centered on about $2.5 million of Q2 revenue, with a $2–3 million base scenario. Vanda recognized only $1 million, while $12.6 million of the $15.2 million initial wholesaler stocking was constrained because of demand and return uncertainties.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nereus generated only $1 million in recognized net product sales in Q2 2026,” and “$12.6 million of the $15.2 million initial wholesaler stocking was constrained due to demand and return uncertainties.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NEREUS revenue vs. ~$2.5M”; the base scenario assumed “NEREUS $2–3M.”

surprises.description: Cash was higher than the preview’s roughly $155 million estimate, at $170 million, and management said funding should last through at least the end of 2027. That is better than the preview’s expected cash balance, despite the continued cash decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash, equivalents and marketable securities fell to $170 million” and management was “still guiding to funding through at least end of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “At roughly $50M per quarter, cash would fall to about $155M at 6/30”; the preview also flagged a print below $150M as a key concern.

surprises.description: The preview said the -$0.60 consensus EPS implied that operating expenses would need to fall sharply from Q1. Instead, the company reported a $62.5 million net loss and said R&D and SG&A were higher, driven by clinical programs and commercial launches.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Vanda posted a Q2 2026 net loss of $62.5 million,” driven by “higher R&D and SG&A tied to clinical programs and commercial launches.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus EPS of -$0.60 implies opex must fall sharply from Q1 levels to hit that number.”

surprises.description: Hetlios sales fell 66%, and a shipment timing issue pushed roughly $7 million of revenue into Q3. The preview noted prior generic-related pressure but did not flag a shipment shift of this size; the delayed sales make the quarter’s reported decline partly a timing issue as well as a product-sales weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hetlios net product sales fell 66% year-over-year to $5.6 million” due to generic competition and “a shipment timing issue that pushed roughly $7 million of revenue into Q3 2026.”

surprises.description: Vanda disclosed that the Hetlios jet-lag application is proceeding to a formal FDA administrative hearing through December 2026, with a favorable judge recommendation only hoped for in early 2027. This added a regulatory process and timing uncertainty not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Hetlios jet-lag disorder application is proceeding to a formal FDA administrative hearing culminating in December 2026,” with “a favorable judge recommendation hoped for in early 2027.”

in_line: Vanda reaffirmed FY2026 total revenue guidance of $240–290 million, with a $265 million midpoint close to the preview’s $262.1 million consensus estimate; the preview had identified reaffirmation as a positive signal.
FNAPT sales of $36 million were close to the preview’s roughly $35 million Q2 base-case assumption.

surprises.description: Vir reported $238.9 million in license and collaboration revenue, well above the preview’s $135.88 million consensus estimate. That was below the preview’s $255–265 million bull case for full upfront recognition, but the reported figure was still a substantial beat versus consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: Vir recognized $238.9 million in license and collaboration revenue.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue: $135.88M. The preview’s bull scenario estimated $255–265M with full $240M upfront recognition.

surprises.description: Vir’s Q2 R&D expense was $135.3 million, above the preview’s modeled range of $105–112 million. The increase included a $48 million Sanofi milestone payment and hepatitis delta manufacturing costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: R&D expense rose to $135.3 million from $97.5 million a year prior, largely due to a $48 million milestone payment to Sanofi and hepatitis delta manufacturing costs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: R&D: Model range $105–112M.

surprises.description: The 96-week SOLSTICE results showed substantially higher viral suppression on Elapseron/Tobevibart combination therapy than on tobevibart alone, alongside stronger hepatitis B surface antigen reductions and ALT normalization. The preview did not set an expectation for these results.
surprises.fact_evidence: At 96 weeks, 88% of intention-to-treat patients on the combination achieved undetectable virus (97% under last-observation-carried-forward), versus 53% on tobevibart monotherapy. Roughly 90% of combination patients had hepatitis B surface antigen below 10 IU/ml versus 25% on antibody monotherapy, and ALT normalization was 53% despite about half of patients having cirrhosis.

surprises.description: The combination therapy also had a favorable reported safety profile: only mild-to-moderate transient flu-like symptoms and no treatment-related serious adverse events or discontinuations. The preview did not flag a safety expectation for these results.
surprises.fact_evidence: The combination showed a favorable safety profile with only mild-to-moderate transient flu-like symptoms and no treatment-related serious adverse events or discontinuations.

surprises.description: Vir completed enrollment in all three registrational ECLIPSE hepatitis delta studies, an operational milestone not identified in the preview. The preview did, however, expect the stated readout timing, which remained unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: Vir completed enrollment across all three registrational ECLIPSE hepatitis delta studies.

surprises.description: Drug substance PPQ manufacturing is complete for both Elapseron and Tobevibart, with drug product PPQ batches progressing and management saying the major manufacturing expenses are behind it. The preview did not anticipate this manufacturing update.
surprises.fact_evidence: Drug substance PPQ manufacturing is now complete for both Elapseron and Tobevibart, drug product PPQ batches are progressing, and the major manufacturing expenses are now behind the company.

surprises.description: Vir described active dosing across VIR5500 monotherapy and several combination cohorts, and said it aims to begin Phase 3 registration trials next year. The preview instead highlighted expected H2 2026 response data for VIR-5818 and did not provide an expectation for VIR5500.
surprises.fact_evidence: For VIR5500, Vir is dosing patients across three monotherapy and multiple combination cohorts (enzalutamide, docetaxel, darolutamide) at step-up doses of 800, 2,000, and 3,500 mcg/kg, with ambition to start Phase 3 registration trials next year.

surprises.description: Management said current U.S. HDV diagnosis rates are only 10–15% and could reach 25% or more. The preview did not discuss diagnosis rates or this potential change in the diagnosed population.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management estimates current US HDV diagnosis rates at only 10-15% and believes they could reach 25% or more.

surprises.description: The preview focused on the CFO transition and asked for a permanent-hire timeline; the call facts report active interviews for both a CFO and a CMO, adding a CMO search but giving no hiring timeline in the reported facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company is undergoing CEO-cited management transition and actively interviewing for both a new CMO and CFO.
surprises.expectation_evidence: CFO commentary: timeline for a permanent hire.

in_line: Cash and investments were approximately $1.01 billion, consistent with the preview’s expectation of about $1.0 billion and above its $980 million checkpoint; the company reiterated runway into the second half of 2028.
ECLIPSE 1 top-line data remained expected in Q4 2026, with ECLIPSE 2 and 3 readouts in Q1 2027, as the preview anticipated.
The expected Astellas payment amounts—$240 million upfront plus a $75 million equity investment—were received in Q2.

surprises.description: Alto reported adjusted EBITDA of $23.7 million, well above the preview’s derived $17–18 million bar. The preview expected a seasonal step-up, but the reported result was substantially stronger, supported by a $19 million swing to positive gross profit and $5.1 million of 45Z tax credit earnings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA improved by $23.9 million year-over-year to $23.7 million,” driven by “a $19 million swing to positive gross profit and $5.1 million in 45Z tax credit earnings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … ~$17–18M is my derived bar” and “Q2 is driving season, so a seasonal step-up is expected; the question is its size.”

surprises.description: GAAP EPS was $0.15, nearly twice the preview’s $0.08 consensus estimate. The preview cautioned that GAAP EPS can be distorted by unrealized derivative gains and losses, but the reported figure still exceeded the stated estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income attributable to common stockholders was $11.4 million ($0.15 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP) … Consensus … $0.08.”

surprises.description: Net sales of $246 million exceeded the preview’s consensus range of $231.2–$235.9 million. The reported total was above even the high end of the range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated net sales rose $27 million to $246 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales … Consensus (varies by source) $231.2M – $235.9M (midpoint ~$233M).”

surprises.description: Alto’s term debt fell to $29.9 million after an $8.5 million Q2 repayment, a much larger reduction than the preview’s simple expectation that debt would be below the prior-quarter $38.4 million balance. The quarter also generated $28.5 million of operating cash flow, while cash finished at $24 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company paid down $8.5 million in term debt during the quarter, bringing total 2026 principal payments to $25.1 million and reducing outstanding term debt to $29.9 million”; it “generated $28.5 million in operating cash flow” and ended with “a $24 million cash balance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Balance sheet. Term loan below $38.4M, cash above $20M,” with Q1 term debt of $38.4 million.

surprises.description: The preview flagged Brazilian competition as a possible export headwind, but did not anticipate Middle East disruptions raising freight costs as an additional cause of lower renewable-fuel export volumes. Alto redirected production to higher-margin domestic fuel-grade ethanol, partly mitigating the pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Renewable fuel export volumes declined due to Middle East geopolitical disruptions raising freight costs and boosting Brazil's competitiveness into Europe,” while the company “redirected production toward higher-margin domestic fuel-grade ethanol.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Brazilian competition could compress” export premiums; the bear scenario also included “export softness.”

surprises.description: Alto established a new $50 million at-the-market equity program, a potential source of shareholder dilution that the preview did not flag. The call also cited more than $10 million of high-return capital projects, but did not say the ATM proceeds would fund them.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company established a new $50 million at-the-market equity program.”

in_line: The 45Z annual opportunity was broadly in line with the preview: Alto remains on track to qualify at least 90 million gallons and expects $15–16 million of net income after monetization costs. The $7.9 million accrued year-to-date implies roughly $4 million in Q2, near the preview’s expected $3.5–4.5 million recognition.
The Pekin debottlenecking project’s full benefit is expected in Q4 2026, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the project’s benefit would arrive in Q4.
Cash ended at $24 million, above the preview’s stated $20 million threshold.

surprises.description: Q2 diluted EPS was $0.52, below the preview's $0.56 consensus estimate and slightly below its $0.53 base-case scenario. The call attributed the year-over-year decline largely to smaller favorable workers’ comp adjustments than a year ago.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income fell to $0.52 per diluted share from $0.70 a year earlier, driven largely by smaller favorable workers' comp adjustments of $2 million versus $8.8 million in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | $0.56”; the preview’s base scenario also estimated “EPS | ~$0.53.”

surprises.description: Gross billings grew 2.6%, below the preview’s Q2 base-case assumption of 3.5%. The preview did not provide a directly comparable consensus estimate for gross billings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross billings rose 2.6% year-over-year to $2.29 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario assumed “Billings +3.5%.”

surprises.description: Total PEO worksite employees grew only 1%, below the preview’s 1.5% Q2 base-case assumption. Client workforce reductions resumed and offset strong new-client additions, leaving growth weaker than the preview’s already cautious hiring outlook implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total PEO worksite employees grew only 1% as strong controllable growth of ~4,500 net new client WSEs was offset by client workforce reductions that resumed in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario assumed “WSE +1.5%”; the preview also identified same-store client hiring as a key signal to watch.

surprises.description: Management lowered the full-year gross billings growth range to 3%–4% from 3%–5%, rather than reaffirming the existing outlook as the preview expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management narrowed full-year guidance, cutting gross billings growth to 3%-4% (from 3%-5%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management FY2026 guidance (reaffirmed at Q1): gross billings +3–5%”; the preview said “Reaffirm is the base case.”

surprises.description: Management also reduced its full-year average WSE growth range to 2%–3% from 2%–4%, tightening the outlook below the preview’s expected reaffirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management narrowed full-year guidance, cutting … average WSE growth to 2%-3% (from 2%-4%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management FY2026 guidance (reaffirmed at Q1): … average WSE +2–4%”; the preview said “Reaffirm is the base case.”

surprises.description: The full-year gross margin range was cut to 2.7%–2.75% from 2.7%–2.85%. That is weaker than the preview’s 2.90% model level and its expected guidance reaffirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management narrowed full-year guidance, cutting … gross margin to 2.7%-2.75% (from 2.7%-2.85%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s key metric was gross margin “at or above 2.90%”; its base scenario assumed “~2.90%” and it described a guide cut to the low end as the bear trigger.

surprises.description: Management reported an unusually sustained run of workers’ comp price increases that is already more than offsetting rising claims. The preview anticipated California rate increases as a future tailwind, but did not anticipate eight consecutive months of increases or the first such streak in a decade.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company achieved eight consecutive months of workers' comp price increases—its first in a decade—which are more than offsetting rising claim costs.”

surprises.description: New-client acquisitions rose 17% and asset-light market billings grew 73%, with three more asset-light locations expected to convert to traditional branches in the second half. The preview did not flag these growth rates or conversions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New client acquisitions rose 17% year-over-year and the asset-light markets grew billings 73%, with three additional asset-light locations expected to convert to traditional branches in the back half of the year.”

surprises.description: The East Coast posted another quarter of double-digit growth, while the two largest California markets were flat. The preview had flagged California hiring as an issue to monitor but did not anticipate this specific regional split.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The East Coast region delivered its 21st consecutive quarter of double-digit growth (+16%), while Southern and Northern California—the two largest markets—were flat due to client workforce reductions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 NorCal at -2% and SoCal at +2%, and said to watch “same-store client hiring.”

in_line: The 6.6% California workers’ comp rate increase was expected to take effect in September 2026; the call confirmed it is effective September 2026. The expectation that rate increases would support margin improvement in 2027 was also broadly consistent with management’s description of 2026 as the gross-margin low watermark and expected improvement in 2027.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $68.8 million, about $4 million above the top of Beyond Meat’s $60–65 million guide and above both preview consensus estimates. The 8.2% year-over-year decline was also much smaller than the preview’s cited 18.9% consensus decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenues fell 8.2% year-over-year to $68.8 million but beat the high end of the $60-65 million guidance range by roughly $4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue | Company guidance (Q2) $60M – $65M | Consensus … $60.8M … or $62.43M”; “StockStory, −18.9% Y/Y.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA loss was worse than the preview’s modeled range, despite the revenue beat: the loss was $27.7 million, versus an expected loss of roughly $20–24 million. The loss also widened as a share of revenue, to 40.2% from 33% a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $27.7 million (-40.2% of net revenues) from a $24.7 million loss (-33%) a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … ~−$20M to −$24M.”

surprises.description: Management’s Q3 revenue range of $60–65 million implies a sequential decline from Q2’s $68.8 million, tempering the stronger-than-expected Q2 result. The preview provided no Q3 revenue outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 net revenue guidance of $60-65 million implies a sequential decline from Q2's $68.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 | None provided”; the preview gives no Q3 guidance expectation.

surprises.description: Cash use of roughly $18 million was above the preview’s hoped-for $10–12 million burn, though it remained below the preview’s roughly $20 million level that would reopen financing concerns. The decline in six-month operating cash use is a counterpoint, making the result mixed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash used excluding financing activities fell 44% (about $14 million) to roughly $18 million, and six-month operating cash use dropped to $23.2 million from $58 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Burn near $10–12M supports the runway story. Burn above about $20M reopens the financing question.”

surprises.description: An $11 million arbitration-settlement credit from a former co-manufacturer helped reduce operating expenses, a favorable one-off item not anticipated in the preview. The reported 19% operating-expense decline therefore included a material settlement benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses dropped 19% year-over-year to $36.7 million, aided by an $11 million credit from an arbitration settlement with a former co-manufacturer.”

surprises.description: The regional picture was sharply uneven: U.S. retail and foodservice revenues declined, while international retail grew 16.5%; management also cited industry-funded “misinformation” campaigns as a continued drag on domestic demand. The preview flagged foodservice portfolio changes but did not anticipate this geographic contrast or the cited demand explanation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. retail net revenues declined 9.9% to $29.6 million and U.S. food service fell 27.6% to $8 million,” while “international retail [was] up 16.5% to $18.5 million” and management cited “misinformation” campaigns as a continued domestic-demand drag.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Foodservice portfolio changes” as a key metric to watch and said management would give “additional detail”; it provided no regional revenue expectations.

surprises.description: Beyond Meat announced a move into functional beverages with Beyond Immerse as a new growth pillar, a product expansion the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is expanding into functional beverages via its Beyond Immerse launch as a new growth pillar.”

in_line: Gross margin was 8.5%, within the preview’s approximate 8%–11% range.

surprises.description: Coherus guided to FY2026 revenue of $57–62 million, well below the preview’s $73.02 million consensus. The preview said that consensus depended on roughly $16–20 million of non-product revenue, so the new range points to a materially lower revenue outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $57-62 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 revenue | $73.02M”; the preview also said the consensus “implies roughly $16–20M of non-product revenue.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash and investments were $105.3 million, about $20–30 million below the preview’s estimated $125–135 million range and below its roughly $130 million watch level. Management attributed about $39 million of the quarterly decline to TSA obligations, which are expected to diminish into 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash, cash equivalents and investments fell to $105.3 million at end of Q2 from $167 million at Q1, with about $39 million of the decline due to TSA obligations expected to diminish into 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 exit cash at roughly $125–135M”; the catalyst checklist called for “Q2 cash at or above roughly $130M.”

surprises.description: The casdozokitug first-line HCC data timeline moved later than the preview’s mid-2026 timing: initial data is now expected in Q4 2026 because only about half the 72 patients have had three scans. The preview had identified a hard date as positive and a softened timeline as a risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The casdozokitug first-line HCC triplet study is 72 patients, but only about 50% have had 3 scans, pushing initial data availability to Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guided ‘mid-2026,’ enrollment complete”; a “hard date (such as a named Q3 venue) would be a positive” and “vaguer language than Q1's would signal a slip.”

surprises.description: The preview expected tagmokitug initial data around mid-2026, but the reported head-and-neck findings remain immature and uncleaned, with formal disclosure of mature data projected for October. That leaves the fuller readout later and less definitive than the preview’s timing implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Formal disclosure of mature head and neck squamous cell carcinoma tagmokitug data is projected for October 2026”; early data “remains immature and uncleaned.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Tagmokitug (CCR8) Ph1b data. Initial data guided mid-2026.”

surprises.description: The $37.5 million UDENYCA milestone earn-out was not achieved in Q2, so a potential source of the non-product revenue the preview said was needed for consensus is not yet realized. It remains eligible in Q3, so the payment is delayed rather than ruled out.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $37.5 million UDENYCA milestone earn-out was not achieved in Q2 based on buyer-reported results, but remains eligible for achievement in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY2026 consensus “implies roughly $16–20M of non-product revenue, such as a BD upfront, license payment, or the Intas milestone.”

surprises.description: Early tagmokitug head-and-neck data showed a potential activity signal in resistant patients, particularly among HPV-positive patients and those with higher TIRI scores.
