The preview flagged the upcoming data but did not anticipate these reported efficacy observations; they are preliminary and uncleaned.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The TAGMO-TORI combination rescued PD-1 inhibitor activity in resistant patients, with greater benefit in HPV-positive patients and those with higher TIRI scores,” though “data remains immature and uncleaned.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Initial data guided mid-2026, with ESCC and CRC cohorts in 2H26.”

surprises.description: Three studies are now fully enrolled, including the CADILYZE first-line HCC study and tagmokitug head-and-neck and colorectal cohorts. The preview discussed the programs and data timing but did not flag full enrollment across these studies as an expected milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Three studies are now fully enrolled: the CADILYZE first-line HCC study, and the tagmokitug head and neck squamous cell and colorectal cancer cohorts.”

surprises.description: Q2 R&D and SG&A were both lower year over year, and SG&A has declined for six consecutive quarters. The preview gave Q1 expense levels but did not set an expectation for these Q2 reductions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 R&D from continuing operations fell to $21.4 million from $26.3 million year-over-year, and SG&A dropped to $21.0 million from $26.0 million, marking six consecutive quarters of declining SG&A.”

in_line: LOQTORZI sales of $13.6 million and 15% quarter-over-quarter growth landed at the top of the preview’s estimated $13.0–13.6 million range and matched the stated 10–15% quarterly growth guide; the preview also flagged $13.5 million or more as a key threshold.
Management reiterated a $15 million LOQTORZI quarter target in 2026 and a $30 million quarter target in 2027, consistent with the preview’s $15 million and $30–35 million quarterly targets.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $133.5 million, above the preview’s $122.07 million consensus and its implied $127–129 million after allowing for the expected Flyover contribution. The preview said a Flyover-driven headline beat was likely, but the reported result still exceeded that adjusted expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 14% year-over-year to a record $133.5 million,” driven by Tabacón and growth across existing geographies.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus” revenue was “$122.07M”; the preview said consensus “may be missing roughly $5–7M of Flyover revenue” and that “a headline beat is likely.”

surprises.description: EBITDA margin fell roughly 90 basis points, as poor weather hurt the higher-margin attractions business while lower-margin lodging outperformed. The preview focused on yield, visitation, and Q3 bookings but did not flag this margin pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EBITDA margin declined roughly 90 basis points year-over-year,” because “poor weather disproportionately hurt the high-margin attractions business while lower-margin lodging outperformed.”

surprises.description: Tabacón’s adjusted EBITDA grew more than 20% in its first year under Pursuit, bringing its effective purchase multiple down to nearly 9x. The preview did not discuss Tabacón’s performance or acquisition returns.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tabacón grew adjusted EBITDA over 20% in its first year of ownership, lowering the effective purchase multiple to nearly 9x.”

surprises.description: Pursuit reported a $4.6 million pretax gain from Jasper wildfire business-interruption insurance, a one-off benefit not mentioned in the preview. It was excluded from adjusted EBITDA, so it did not boost that key operating measure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pursuit reported a $4.6 million pretax gain from Jasper wildfire business interruption insurance (excluded from adjusted EBITDA),” with total proceeds since 2024 of approximately $29 million.

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $32.7 million was within the preview’s derived expectation of roughly $32–34 million.

The $5 million increase in full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $128–138 million was largely attributed to Flyover and Eagle Wing, consistent with the preview’s expectation that guidance would be trued up for those businesses while core guidance remained unchanged.
The 6% increase in attraction effective ticket price was in line with the preview’s base-case expectation of 5–6% yield growth.

surprises.description: SenesTech’s gross margin reached 73.6%, above the preview’s 66–69% base-case range and even the bull scenario’s threshold of 69%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached a company record of 73.6%,” improving “510 basis points sequentially and 810 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “gross margin 66–69%”; the bull scenario expected “gross margin ≥ 69%.”

surprises.description: Despite cash of $5.1 million being close to the preview’s estimate, management said it would fund operations for only at least nine months and raised the likelihood of a future capital raise. That is a weaker runway outlook than the preview’s cited guidance of runway into Q3 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended the quarter with “$5.1 million in cash,” which management expects to fund operations for “only at least the next 9 months,” “raising the likelihood of a future capital raise.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited prior management guidance of “runway into Q3 2027” and said cash “should be near $5.3M on the Q1 burn rate.”

surprises.description: The call reported continued record-setting momentum in July, a follow-through update the preview did not anticipate: e-commerce and subscription revenue both increased from June to new records.
surprises.fact_evidence: July e-commerce revenue was a record “$245,000 (up 19% from June)” and subscription revenue was a record “$52,000 (up 22% from June).”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $770,000 was within the preview’s rough $750,000–$800,000 estimate and exceeded the $689,000 prior record, as the preview anticipated.
The 186% sequential increase in e-commerce revenue matched the growth stated in the pre-announcement.
The reported 117% increase in combined Amazon/e-commerce subscribers was consistent with the pre-announcement that the active online subscriber base had more than doubled sequentially.
Quarter-end cash of $5.1 million was close to the preview’s estimate of about $5.3 million.

surprises.description: Q3 combined revenue guidance of $285–$295 million is well above the preview’s roughly $255 million street-math estimate and its $250–$265 million base case. The guide also exceeds the preview’s $280 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for combined revenue of $285-$295 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 combined revenue versus the roughly $255M ‘street math’ figure”; Base: “$250–265M”; Bull: “$280M+.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue beat the $145.09 million consensus by about 8.5%, coming in at $157.4 million. The preview’s bull case began at $158 million, just above the reported result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $157.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus | $145.09M”; Bull scenario: “Q2 Revenue $158M+.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $2.34 exceeded the $1.93 consensus by about 21%, and also topped the preview’s bull-case threshold of $2.30.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income reached $65.7 million, or $2.34 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus | $1.93”; Bull scenario: “Q2 EPS $2.30+.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin reached 67.1%, 2.1 percentage points above the roughly 65% expected level. The result also exceeded the preview’s 66% threshold for a favorable Q3 blended-margin guide, although no Q3 blended-margin guidance is provided in the call facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded to 67.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin | ~65.0% ±1.0 pt | ~65%”; Catalyst checklist: “Blended gross margin guide of 66% or higher.”

surprises.description: The acquired TPD is expected to contribute about $85 million in Q3, above the preview’s roughly $75 million quarterly assumption. Management also says it is tracking well above the original $300 million annualized run-rate target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TPD … is expected to contribute ~$85 million in Q3 alone, tracking well above its original $300 million annualized run-rate target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Renesas in at ~$75M/quarter”; “Management says the business will do ‘at least $300M’ in the 12 months after close.”

surprises.description: The Q2 growth was broader than the preview’s specific focus on triple-digit Datacenter/Comms growth: every business unit and region grew more than 50% year over year. The preview did not identify that breadth as an expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Every business unit and region growing more than 50%.”

surprises.description: Management warned that interest income will fall to about $4 million in Q3 after the acquisition financing proceeds were deployed. The preview discussed the zero-coupon notes and dilution, but did not flag this near-term reduction in interest income.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management funded the acquisition with a $1.35 billion zero-coupon convertible notes offering due 2031, but warned Q3 interest income will drop to ~$4 million after proceeds were deployed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed “$1.35B of 0% convertible notes due 2031” and said “EPS accretion depends on share count, not interest.”

surprises.description: Management expressed confidence that growth will continue into 2027, including 100% growth in 1.6T optical-module revenue, with 800G also growing, and said it sees no signs of a slowdown. The preview did not set out this product-level outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In 2027, the company expects its 1.6T optical module revenue to grow 100% (with 800G also growing)”; management “sees no signs of slowdown in 2027.”

surprises.description: Management said timing integration into chiplets and modules could expand SiTime’s CED serviceable addressable market by $2.5 billion by 2030, a growth opportunity not raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Timing integration into chiplets and modules could expand its CED SAM by $2.5 billion by 2030.”

in_line: CED growth remained triple-digit: the preview said Datacenter/Comms needed to hold triple-digit year-over-year growth, and the call reported CED growth of 181%.
TPD’s approximately 70% gross margin matched the preview’s stated expectation of about 70%.
The $1.35 billion zero-coupon convertible notes due 2031 were consistent with the financing terms described in the preview.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $531 million, above the preview’s $512.3–$515.6 million consensus range, and grew 10% rather than the roughly 6%–7% implied by estimates. Recurring and other revenue reached $505 million versus $485.7 million expected, with management describing the strength as broad-based and not driven by one-off factors.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached $531 million, up 10% year-over-year, with recurring and other revenue of $505 million, up 11%, described as broad-based strength with no one-off factors.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $512.3M” (alternatives: “$513.1M / $515.6M”); “Recurring & other revenue | $485.7M”; “Consensus expects +6.7%.”

surprises.description: Instead of reaffirming the existing full-year revenue outlook, Paycom raised it to $2.197–$2.212 billion, above the prior $2.175–$2.195 billion range. The new 7%–8% growth outlook is also a step up from the prior 6%–7% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $2.197–$2.212 billion (7%–8% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue: $2.175–2.195B (+6–7%)”; the preview identified “FY26 guidance: raise or reaffirm” as the main driver and described its base case as “FY reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $235 million, beating the preview’s estimated $213–$218 million range by roughly 8%–10%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $235 million in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | No clean published consensus; ~$213–218M estimated.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance rose to $1.007–$1.022 billion from $950–$970 million, with the new midpoint implying a record 46% margin. This is a larger step-up than the revenue-guidance increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised… adjusted EBITDA guidance to $1.007–$1.022 billion, implying a record 46% margin at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: $950–970M”; the preview’s base case said “FY reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: The 44.2% Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 320 basis points year over year, a strong result against the preview’s expectation that a second quarter of margin expansion would support the efficiency story.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $235 million in Q2, expanding margins by 320 basis points year-over-year to 44.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 is seasonally the weakest margin quarter (41.0% in Q2’25). A second quarter of expansion would support the efficiency story.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $2.78, above even the preview’s highest cited estimate of $2.64, and well above its more comparable $2.28 estimate. The preview had also highlighted that buybacks were doing much of the EPS work; the call reported 11 million shares repurchased in the first half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income was $128 million ($2.78 per diluted share)”; “repurchased approximately 11 million shares in the first half of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS | $2.28”; alternatives “$2.38 / $2.64”; “Diluted shares fell sharply, so buybacks are doing much of the EPS work.”

surprises.description: Paycom newly expects 2026 free cash flow to exceed $650 million, citing sustainable process and labor efficiencies that should bring free-cash-flow margins closer to EBITDA margins. The preview did not flag a free-cash-flow outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow is now expected to exceed $650 million in 2026, driven by sustainable process and labor efficiencies bringing free cash flow margins closer to EBITDA margins.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed substantial savings from its data-center investment: roughly $100 million in R&D savings this year and more than $30 million in avoided third-party fees. The preview did not anticipate or quantify these benefits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Last year's $100 million+ investment in data centers to host proprietary AI models is generating roughly $100 million in R&D savings this year plus $30 million+ in avoided third-party fees.”

surprises.description: The outlook assumes about $105 million of interest income on client funds, slightly above the preview’s unchanged $103 million annual assumption; average daily client funds were reported up 9% to $2.9 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Guidance assumes no rate changes for the rest of the year, with interest on funds held for clients of approximately $105 million and average daily client funds of $2.9 billion (up 9%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Interest on client funds: ~$103M”; the preview also flagged the “$103M FY assumption” and average daily balance growth for monitoring.

surprises.description: Management said new sales reps are reaching productivity faster than prior classes, a favorable early signal for the sales reorganization the preview said would be tested in Q2. The call facts provided no bookings figure, so this does not establish that the anticipated bookings inflection had occurred.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expanded sales teams from 8 to 10 members, adding over 100 new reps as incremental headcount, with new reps reaching productivity faster than prior classes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bookings and the sales reorganization. Management said Q1 book sales were ‘according to budget’ and expected inflection later in the year. Q2 is the first quarter where this is testable.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $61.9 million, about 18% above the $52.5 million consensus estimate and above even the preview’s $56–$59 million bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $61.9 million,” up 45% year-over-year and 40% sequentially.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $52.5M (range cited $52.4–52.5M)” and the bull scenario called for “$56M–$59M.”

surprises.description: The adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed much more than the preview’s hoped-for move toward $20 million: it was $9.6 million, versus $26.7 million in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss was $9.6 million, a 33% year-over-year improvement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Narrowing toward $20M would support management's cost-action timeline.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP gross margin was 58%, well above the preview’s 50% bar, rather than merely holding around that level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin was 58% (flat YoY but up 8 points sequentially).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Holding 50% is the bar” and the base scenario expected “gross margin roughly flat.”

surprises.description: The company raised the lower end of its FY2026 revenue range by $5 million, to $230 million, and clarified that the range excludes LivePerson revenue. This modestly improves the outlook while showing it does not depend on the pending acquisition contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $230 million to $260 million, excluding any contribution from the pending LivePerson acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The existing company guide was “$225M–$260M”; the preview said the base case was “Guide reaffirmed at $225M–$260M” and flagged whether it included LivePerson as “the key call question.”

surprises.description: Loss per share was narrower than consensus on both stated bases: GAAP loss was $0.10 versus an expected $0.13, and non-GAAP loss was $0.02 versus an expected $0.03.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss was $42.8 million ($0.10 per share) while non-GAAP net loss was $9 million ($0.02 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “EPS, adjusted | −$0.03” and “EPS, GAAP | −$0.13,” and cautioned to compare each result on the same basis.

surprises.description: SoundHound reported an eight-figure customer commitment signed in under 90 days from demo to contract, a specific large, contracted win that the preview identified as the kind of evidence investors were looking for but did not anticipate reporting this quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed an 8-figure customer commitment in under 90 days from initial demo to contract,” serving customers across 20 countries through a channel deal.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the bull case needed “named enterprise wins, a disclosed backlog or committed-bookings figure, or confirmation that H2 large deals are contracted rather than pipelined.”

surprises.description: The LivePerson transaction advanced beyond the preview’s focus on the upcoming shareholder vote: all key regulatory clearances were secured, and management expected the deal to close before year-end. The update also cited 25 Fortune 100 brands and elimination of LivePerson’s debt.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The LivePerson acquisition secured all key regulatory clearances and is expected to close before year-end, adding 25 of the Fortune 100 brands and eliminating LivePerson's debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted the “LivePerson stockholder vote, August 20, 2026” and described the $350M–$400M FY2027 framework as including LivePerson.

surprises.description: Management reported unusually strong OASYS-related commercial traction, including 100% restaurant renewal rates for key accounts and more than doubling SMB smart-answering revenue—metrics the preview did not flag as expected outcomes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “OASYS, launched in May 2026, is driving record win rates across demos, RFPs, and pilots, with restaurant renewal rates hitting 100% for key accounts and SMB ‘smart answering’ revenue more than doubling year-over-year.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed the FY2027 revenue framework of $350 million to $400 million, conditional on the LivePerson acquisition closing in the second half of 2026; the preview already cited that company framework.

surprises.description: OraSure withdrew the InteliQuick CT/NG FDA submission and no longer expects clearance or a U.S. launch in 2026, rather than reaching the midyear clearance and H2 revenue ramp discussed before the release. The preview identified a timeline slip as a major downside risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: OraSure withdrew its FDA submission for the InteliQuick CT/NG molecular self-test and no longer expects FDA clearance or U.S. launch in 2026, planning to resubmit after incorporating FDA feedback.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management said CT/NG rapid molecular self-test clearance was expected at “midyear,” with revenue ramping in H2; the preview said a slip into 2027 would be a bear trigger.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $30.6 million, above both the $30 million top of company guidance and the preview’s working consensus estimate of roughly $29.0–29.3 million. The preview expected a top-half-of-guidance quarter, but not a result above the range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Total Q2 2026 revenue was $30.6 million, up 9.7% sequentially and exceeding the company's guidance range.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Company guidance was $27M–$30M; the preview treated ~$29.0–29.3M as the working consensus number and said consensus implied a top-half-of-range quarter.

surprises.description: Gross margin improved rather than remaining near Q1 levels: GAAP margin rose to 43.5% and non-GAAP margin to 44.2%. The preview’s Q2 expectation was margins similar to Q1’s 42.3% GAAP and 43.4% non-GAAP.
surprises.fact_evidence: GAAP gross margin expanded 120 basis points sequentially to 43.5%, while non-GAAP gross margin rose to 44.2% from 43.4%, driven by lower scrap and operational efficiencies.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Company gross-margin guidance was “similar to Q1” (42.3% GAAP / 43.4% non-GAAP).

surprises.description: Despite negative operating cash flow, quarter-end cash was $161 million—above the preview’s roughly $155 million level that it flagged as a sign of accelerating burn. Operating cash flow was also less negative than the approximately $14 million reported for Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: Operating cash flow was negative $9.9 million in Q2; the company ended the quarter with $161 million in cash and cash equivalents.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said that if Q2 cash fell below about $155M, the burn would be accelerating; it cited Q1 operating cash burn of about $14M.

surprises.description: OraSure paused share repurchases to preserve balance-sheet flexibility, buying back only $2 million of shares in Q2. The preview noted Q1 buybacks but did not flag a Q2 pause or a shift in capital-allocation priorities.
surprises.fact_evidence: OraSure paused share repurchases in Q2 (buying back only 647,000 shares for $2 million) to prioritize balance sheet flexibility for product launches.

surprises.description: The CT/NG delay is not expected to increase cash usage because reduced milestone payments on the contingent consideration are expected to more than offset resubmission costs. That limits the financial impact of the regulatory setback, which the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: The InteliQuick delay is not expected to increase cash usage, as reduced milestone payments on the ~$20 million contingent consideration will more than offset incremental resubmission costs.

surprises.description: Sample Management Solutions revenue grew 9% sequentially to $9.9 million, a rebound from the flat Q1 revenue and subdued NIH and academic demand described in the preview. The preview did not forecast a recovery in this business.
surprises.fact_evidence: Sample Management Solutions revenue was $9.9 million, up 9% sequentially.
surprises.expectation_evidence: In Q1, Sample Management Solutions revenue was flat at $9.1M, with NIH and academic demand described as “subdued.”

surprises.description: Management reported that Sickle SCAN revenue is growing twice as fast in 2026 as in 2025, a favorable growth update not mentioned in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Sickle SCAN revenue is growing twice as fast in 2026 as in 2025.

in_line: Q3 revenue guidance of $29.5–32.5 million broadly matches the preview’s roughly $29–32 million expectation.
Management reaffirmed its target of breakeven operating cash flow entering 2027, consistent with the preview’s account of the prior-quarter commitment.

surprises.description: Root now expects 2026 policies in force to be roughly flat versus 2025 if competition persists, despite entering the quarter with PIF up 9% year over year. That is a weaker growth outlook than the preview’s roughly 4% full-year revenue-growth estimate implied, and Q2 PIF had already fallen sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Policies in force grew 6% year-over-year to 484,000 but declined sequentially,” and management guided that “full-year 2026 PIF will likely be roughly flat versus 2025's ~482,000 if the competitive environment persists.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 PIF “495,429, up 9% Y/Y” and FY2026 revenue consensus of “~$1.58B” versus $1.52B in FY25, or “+4%.”

surprises.description: The 92.1% net combined ratio was better than the preview’s 94–95% estimate, but the improvement came mainly from a 26% expense ratio rather than stronger loss performance: the net loss and LAE ratio stayed around 66%. Management also said the low expense ratio is not sustainable and pointed to roughly 29% as the normalized run rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The net combined ratio improved 3 points year-over-year to 92.1%,” driven mainly by “a lower net expense ratio of 26%,” while the “net loss and LAE ratio held broadly flat at 66%.” Management said 26% “is not sustainable,” citing reduced performance-based equity compensation, and guided to Q1/Q4's “~29% level as a normalized run rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated a net combined ratio of “~94-95%” and said a “sub-92% print driven by current-accident-period results” would be a stronger signal; it also cited Q2/Q3 loss-ratio guidance of about 60–62%.

surprises.description: Q2 net income of $25 million puts first-half net income at about $61 million, already well above the preview’s inferred full-year 2026 range of roughly $38–40 million. That is a substantially stronger earnings run rate than the preview anticipated, although the preview acknowledged its annual estimate was its own reading rather than company guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income rose 15% year-over-year to $25 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said CFO commentary “implies about $38-40M” of 2026 net income and that “$36M was already booked in Q1,” while noting this was “my reading, not a company figure.”

surprises.description: Revenue came in slightly below the preview’s consensus estimate, and GWP declined rather than recovering toward flat or positive growth. The GWP decline was within the preview’s base-case range, so the shortfall versus the more optimistic recovery catalyst was limited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue increased just 2% year-over-year to $389 million, while gross written premium actually declined 2% to $340 million amid a highly competitive direct market.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview put Q2 revenue consensus at “~$392.5M” and said to “look for a return toward flat or positive growth” in GWP; its base scenario allowed GWP “flat to -3%.”

surprises.description: Root recorded a full impairment on private-equity investments, cutting reported net investment income to about half of the portfolio income before the impairment. The preview did not flag this charge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Root recorded a $4.4 million full impairment on private equity investments (only $600K original cash cost), reducing reported net investment income to $5 million versus ~$10 million underlying portfolio income.”

surprises.description: Management said average premiums were down year over year and estimated rates are about 3% overpriced, with modest rate decreases planned. The preview discussed softer industry rates and competition but did not anticipate Root’s specific pricing assessment or planned cuts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Average premiums fell year-over-year with management estimating rates are roughly 3% (low single digits) overpriced, signaling planned modest rate decreases ahead.”

surprises.description: Root disclosed plans to spend about $10 million in the second half testing upper-funnel acquisition channels, ahead of a Q4 pricing-model launch. This is an unanticipated investment that could add near-term costs while testing potential growth initiatives.
surprises.fact_evidence: Root “plans ~$10 million in H2 R&D spend to test new upper-funnel acquisition channels ahead of a Q4 pricing model launch.”

surprises.description: Root launched in New Jersey and said it now covers 37 states and more than 80% of the U.S. population, with a near-national footprint targeted by the end of 2027. The preview did not anticipate this geographic expansion update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company launched New Jersey to reach 37 states covering over 80% of the U.S. population, targeting a near-national footprint by end of 2027.”

in_line: Root repurchased more than $20 million of shares under its $75 million authorization, delivering the visible buyback execution the preview was watching for rather than the negative case of no repurchases.

Partnership and independent-agent channels continued gaining share, consistent with the preview’s note that those writings had risen more than 30% year over year in Q1 and that channel mix was a key issue to watch.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $0.1 million, below even the preview’s lowest estimate of $1.0 million and far below the $8.91 million and $19.0 million alternatives. The preview expected Fluor’s FEED work to have rolled off, but the reported result was weaker than every cited estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: NuScale reported Q2 2026 revenue of just $0.1 million, down sharply from $8.1 million a year earlier, due to the completion of Fluor's RoPower FEED Phase 2 work in late 2025 with no comparable current activity.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue (Zacks) $1.0M; Revenue (GuruFocus) $8.91M; Revenue (9-analyst mean, alt. compiler) $19.0M. The base scenario expected ~$0.5–2M.

surprises.description: The company reported approximately $1.9 billion in cash, cash equivalents and investments, versus the preview’s expectation of roughly $830–850 million absent a PPA. Management said the rise in longer-term investments reflected treasury reclassification rather than new fundraising, but the reported total was still dramatically above the preview’s expected balance.
surprises.fact_evidence: NuScale closed Q2 2026 with approximately $1.9 billion in cash, cash equivalents and investments, an increase of $900 million since March 31, 2026. Its balance sheet investments rose to roughly $800 million, reflecting a treasury reclassification into longer-term high-grade instruments rather than new fundraising.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Absent a PPA, Q2 cash should land near $830–850M.”

surprises.description: The Romania project appears to have a longer runway to a notice to proceed than the preview’s financing-close watchpoint suggested: it still awaits a new government seating and prime-contractor contracting, with about a year of pre-EPC work before final notice to proceed and potential revenue in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: The RoPower project in Romania (6 modules at a former coal site) awaits a new Romanian government seating and prime-contractor contracting, with pre-EPC work extending roughly a year to final notice to proceed and potential revenue in 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The next phase is gated on pre-EPC financing. Watch for financing close.”

surprises.description: The TVA discussions now describe a potential 6-to-8 GW deployment, extending above the preview’s description of an agreement covering up to 6 GW. This is a larger potential program, though the call still described discussions rather than a signed PPA.
surprises.fact_evidence: ENTRA1 Energy is advancing active discussions with the Tennessee Valley Authority toward a definitive PPA for a potential 6-to-8 gigawatt deployment.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Sept 2025 TVA–ENTRA1 agreement covers up to 6 GW and remains non-binding.”

surprises.description: NuScale described a substantial supplier network already moving toward contracted and in-production components, an execution-readiness update not covered by the preview. More than half of over 60 specialized suppliers have signed master agreements, and some components have been in production for two years.
surprises.fact_evidence: NuScale has assembled a network of more than 60 specialized suppliers and has already signed master supplier agreements with more than half of them, with many components—including heavy forgings at Doosan—already in production over the past two years.

surprises.description: The call quantified a possible regulatory head start for a new U.S. project: roughly 60% of the prior CFPP license application could be carried over, potentially saving time and regulatory cost. The preview did not discuss this reuse potential.
surprises.fact_evidence: Approximately 60% of the prior CFPP project's Combined Construction and Operating License Application (COLA) can be carried over to a new U.S. project, potentially saving significant time and regulatory cost.

surprises.description: Management put NuScale’s OEM/module scope at roughly 30% or more of total project cost, a project-economics detail absent from the preview. The rest of project cost would go to EPC and other contractors.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects NuScale's OEM/module scope to represent roughly 30%+ of total project cost, with the remainder going to EPC and other contractors.

surprises.description: Management gave a construction-duration estimate of a little under 40 months from first safety-related concrete pour to mechanical completion, excluding NRC licensing time. The preview had not provided a construction schedule benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: Construction from first safety-related concrete pour to mechanical completion is expected to take a little less than 40 months, excluding upfront NRC licensing time.

in_line: The preview expected Fluor’s RoPower FEED Phase 2 work to have rolled off and anticipated very low Q2 revenue in its base case; the call attributed the lack of comparable activity to that work’s completion in late 2025, even though revenue came in below the cited estimates.

The preview expected the TVA PPA to remain unsigned while discussions continued to advance, with a signing targeted for later in 2026. The call described active discussions toward a definitive PPA but did not report a signed agreement.

surprises.description: Q2 loan production was $672.6 million, below the preview’s $700–$780 million base range and even below its roughly $680 million level that would challenge the second-half growth story. Production was up 5.2% sequentially and units rose 3.3%, but dollar volume remained weaker than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total loan production was $672.6 million,” down from $725 million a year ago; production increased 5.2% over Q1’s $639 million, while unit production rose 3.3%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario projected originations of “$700M – $780M,” and said “Anything below about $680M would challenge the second-half growth narrative.”

surprises.description: Portfolio growth was slower than the preview’s expected roughly 5% sequential increase: UPB reached $7.0 billion, up only 2.2% from Q1. That also put year-over-year growth at 19%, below the roughly 25% growth cited in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The total loan portfolio grew to $7.0 billion in UPB, a 19% year-over-year increase and 2.2% sequential increase from Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “About +5% q/q would put the book near $7.15–7.2B” and described the portfolio as “up about 25%.”

surprises.description: Portfolio NIM came in above both the 3.5% FY26 target and the preview’s 3.50%–3.56% base range, rather than merely stabilizing around the guide. It was also up 10 basis points from Q1, despite remaining below the unusually high year-ago level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Portfolio NIM was 3.66%, above the 3.5% target and up 10 basis points from Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited management’s “NIM stabilizing around 3.5% for FY26” and a base-case NIM of “3.50% – 3.56%.”

surprises.description: Management’s second-half outlook was stronger than the preview’s expectation that meaningful growth would resume: management expects second-half originations to beat last year’s levels and said July submissions set a company record. The preview anticipated second-half acceleration, but not an explicit expectation to exceed last year or record submissions.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects origination volumes to “increase in the second half and beat last year’s levels,” and said “July was the best month ever for submissions”; no formal guidance was provided.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview quoted prior guidance for “meaningful volume growth in the second half” and described the base case as “2H language intact.”

in_line: GAAP net income and EPS dipped slightly, in the direction of the preview’s roughly 13% expected year-over-year GAAP EPS decline; the call attributed the dip mainly to a higher effective tax rate rather than weaker business performance.
New HFI originations carried an approximately 10% weighted-average coupon, consistent with the preview’s focus on 10%+ coupons as evidence of pricing discipline.
NPL resolutions remained above par: the preview emphasized that resolutions above 100% supported the thesis, and the call reported 102.7% net gains and 107.7% total recoveries.

surprises.description: Enact raised its 2026 capital-return guidance to $550–600 million, above the preview’s expectation that it would reaffirm the roughly $500 million target. That is $50–100 million more than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enact raised its 2026 capital return guidance to $550-600 million, up from prior guidance of $500 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capital return about $500M”; the base scenario expected “guides reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating EPS of $1.26 exceeded the preview’s $1.19–$1.21 working range, beating the top of that range by five cents.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted operating income was $177 million, with diluted EPS of $1.26.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Working band: EPS $1.19–$1.21.”

surprises.description: Enact lowered its full-year operating-expense forecast to $205–210 million from the prior $215–220 million guide, rather than simply reaffirming the previous range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 operating expenses (excluding reorganization costs) are now forecast at $205-210 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY2026 guidance would be “re-tested” and the base scenario assumed “guides reaffirmed”; the prior expense guide was “$215–220M.”

surprises.description: Management now expects delinquencies to rise in the second half, and cited newer purchase vintages with higher LTVs and DTIs as a factor. The preview had only noted that delinquencies “may tick up,” so the call made the expected increase more definite and added specific risk factors.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects delinquency rates to rise in the second half of 2026 due to seasonality and newer, lower-HPA purchase vintages carrying higher LTVs and DTIs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management noted delinquencies “may tick up” on portfolio aging.

in_line: New insurance written was $15 billion, at the high end of the preview’s roughly $13–15 billion range.
The 14% loss ratio was within the preview’s 13–16% base-case range; the preview had also flagged favorable reserve development as an important factor to assess.
Persistency held at 80%, matching the preview’s Q1 baseline of 80%.
The $127 million returned to shareholders in Q2 was close to the preview’s roughly $125 million quarterly pace benchmark.

surprises.description: The preview derived adjusted EPS of about $1.20–$1.30 and expected EPS to be down year over year on a tough comparison. TPC reported $1.74, up 23% year over year, well above that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS up 23% to $1.74.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS ~$1.20–1.30 (derived)” and the base scenario expected “adj. EPS down Y/Y on tough comp.”

surprises.description: The preview expected FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to be affirmed at $4.90–$5.30, while TPC raised the range to $5.15–$5.45. Management also said it expects higher earnings in 2027, a further-year outlook not included in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.15-$5.45, up from the prior range of $4.90-$5.30, and expects even higher earnings in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 company guidance: Adjusted EPS $4.90–$5.30” and the base scenario expected “guide affirmed.”

surprises.description: The preview estimated backlog of $19.2–$19.8 billion and warned of a possible third consecutive decline, with book-to-bill near 0.6–0.9. Instead, backlog was near-record at $19.9 billion and book-to-burn was just over 1x.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog stood at a near-record $19.9 billion with a book-to-burn just over 1x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 backlog estimate … $19.2–19.8B”; awards implied “book-to-bill near 0.6–0.9 and a third straight backlog decline.”

surprises.description: The preview gave Civil a 12%–15% margin guide; the reported 15.3% margin exceeded the top of that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Civil segment operating margin reached 15.3%, exceeding the top of its 12%-15% target range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Civil margin guide (2026): 12–15%.”

surprises.description: The preview said a year-over-year decline in operating cash flow was likely. The call instead reported record first-half operating cash flow, up 17% year over year, with only a small contribution from dispute resolutions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record first-half operating cash flow of $334 million (up 17% YoY) was driven mostly by organic operations, with only a small amount from dispute resolutions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Y/Y decline is likely and largely mechanical.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag a dividend increase. TPC raised its quarterly dividend by 50%, introducing a larger shareholder return than the preview had anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board raised the quarterly dividend 50% to $0.09 per share.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a potential-opportunity pipeline exceeding $200 billion over the next three to four years, including $4.6 billion of near-term Indo-Pacific bids for the Guam subsidiary. The preview discussed backlog and announced awards, but gave no expectation for a pipeline of this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A pipeline exceeding $200 billion in potential opportunities over the next 3-4 years (roughly triple the level of two years ago), including $4.6 billion of near-term Indo-Pacific bids for its Guam subsidiary.”

in_line: Specialty Contractors' 2.2% Q2 operating margin was within the preview's stated 2026 margin guide of 1%–3%.

surprises.description: Veeco reported Q2 revenue of $193 million and non-GAAP EPS of $0.33, above both the preview’s consensus estimates and the top of its company-guidance ranges. Non-GAAP operating income was $23 million, also well above the preview’s $1 million–$10 million guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $193 million with non-GAAP operating income of $23 million and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.33, exceeding guidance and Street expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … $170M – $190M” company guidance and “$180.1M” consensus; “Non-GAAP EPS … $0.20 – $0.32” company guidance and “$0.26” consensus; “Operating income … $1M – $10M.”

surprises.description: Veeco raised its FY2026 revenue outlook to $780 million–$810 million from $740 million–$800 million, putting both ends above the prior range’s lower end and lifting the upper end. The preview had flagged reaffirmation or a cut as possibilities, rather than a higher revenue range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Veeco raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $780-810 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (reiterated 5/5/26): Revenue $740M – $800M”; the preview asked whether the ranges would be “reaffirmed, narrowed to the lower half, or cut.”

surprises.description: The FY2026 non-GAAP EPS range was cut to $1.36–$1.61 from $1.50–$1.85, despite the higher revenue outlook. Veeco attributed the reduction to growth investments, including about $10 million in incremental operating expenses and an approximately 75-basis-point reduction in full-year gross margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered non-GAAP EPS guidance to $1.36-1.61 due to growth investments”; “approximately $10 million of incremental operating expenses” and “reduce full-year 2026 gross margin by roughly 75 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance … non-GAAP EPS $1.50 – $1.85”; the preview said to watch whether EPS guidance was “reaffirmed, narrowed to the lower half, or cut.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $200 million–$220 million has a $210 million midpoint, above the preview’s $195 million–$205 million base-case range and at the preview’s bull-case threshold. It also clears the preview’s roughly $200 million minimum run-rate concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects revenue of $200-220 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base” scenario: “$195M – $205M midpoint”; “Bull” scenario: “Midpoint of $210M or higher”; the preview also said the Q3 midpoint needed to be “roughly $200M or higher.”

surprises.description: Q3 gross-margin guidance of 41%–42% is ahead of the preview’s expectation that second-half margins would need to move “toward 40%.” This points to a stronger near-term margin level than the preview’s stated target path.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects … gross margin of 41-42%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management needs to move margins toward 40% in the second half for the EPS ramp to work.”

surprises.description: Veeco announced $200 million of advanced-packaging orders for wet-processing and lithography systems, primarily for delivery in 2027. The preview flagged a same-day order announcement as a catalyst but did not identify an order of this size or this delivery timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company secured $200 million in advanced packaging orders for wet processing and lithography systems during Q2, primarily for delivery in 2027.”

surprises.description: A Tier 1 logic customer completed its evaluation and ordered a second next-generation NSA system for shipment in the second half of 2026. The preview did not flag this customer evaluation or follow-on order.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A Tier 1 logic customer completed evaluation and placed a follow-on order for a second next-generation nanosecond annealing (NSA) system to ship in the second half of 2026.”

surprises.description: Veeco said it plans to more than double advanced-packaging and silicon-photonics capacity during 2027 using internal production and Southeast Asian outsourcing partners. The preview did not anticipate this scale of capacity expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to more than double advanced packaging and silicon photonics capacity during 2027 through internal production and Southeast Asian outsourcing partners.”

surprises.description: Veeco newly indicated that 2026 compound-semiconductor revenue should approximately double from 2025, an outlook the preview did not mention. This is a positive segment outlook, though the preview provides no comparable expectation to measure the gap against.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Compound semiconductor revenue is expected to approximately double in 2026 versus 2025.”

in_line: Data storage revenue is expected to double year over year, matching the preview’s statement that data storage was guided to double in 2026.
The merger remains targeted to close in the second half of 2026, with China antitrust approval still outstanding, consistent with the preview’s focus on pending Chinese approval and merger timing.

surprises.description: The call reported a $950 million upfront payment from the Moderna settlement, with roughly $770 million going to Genevant and the remainder to Arbutus. The preview did not anticipate a settlement payment of this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received a $950 million upfront payment from the Moderna settlement, with roughly $770 million going to Genevant and the remainder to Arbutus.”

surprises.description: Management said a favorable ruling in the '498 Federal Circuit case could yield another $1.3 billion and that three new international lawsuits against Pfizer and BioNTech were filed in July. The preview did not flag this additional litigation-related potential recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A favorable appellate ruling in the ongoing '498 Federal Circuit case could yield an additional $1.3 billion, while three new international lawsuits against Pfizer and BioNTech were filed in July.”

surprises.description: The call gave a near-term dermatomyositis launch target: by the end of September 2026, with the PDUFA date in the current quarter after priority review. The preview did not discuss this launch or give a timing expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roivant expects to launch brepiprazole (brepocitinib) in dermatomyositis by the end of September 2026, with the PDUFA date falling in the current quarter following priority review.”

surprises.description: Management described the dermatomyositis launch as “slow and steady,” noting that only low-to-mid single-digit percentages of patients have prior off-label JAK experience and that about 200 referral centers treat roughly half of U.S. patients. The preview gave no launch-uptake expectation or warning of a gradual rollout.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided to a 'slow and steady' dermatomyositis launch,” with “only low-to-mid single-digit percentages of patients” having prior off-label JAK experience and “about 200 myositis referral centers” treating roughly half of U.S. patients.

surprises.description: Brepocitinib showed a greater than 20-point advantage over placebo on the cutaneous sarcoidosis CSAMI scale, far above the 5-point clinical-meaningfulness goal. The preview did not identify this study or set an efficacy expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Brepocitinib showed a greater than 20-point benefit on the CSAMI scale versus roughly nothing on placebo, well above the 5-point clinical meaningfulness goal.”

surprises.description: The company had already initiated the Phase III cutaneous sarcoidosis study ahead of schedule, with a 140-patient, 16-week design and data expected in 2028. The preview did not mention this program or trial timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company initiated its Phase III cutaneous sarcoidosis study (ahead of schedule) — a 140-patient, 16-week, 3:2 randomized trial with data expected in 2028.”

surprises.description: The call added a second-half 2026 top-line readout for PH-ILD, while also cautioning that the study is mostly Phase II and is not powered for six-minute walk distance. The preview did not flag PH-ILD or set a timing expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Top-line PH-ILD data from the mostly (Phase II) study is expected in the second half of 2026,” with management hoping for “a clear PVR signal” but saying it is “not powered for six-minute walk distance.”

surprises.description: The call outlined multiple additional second-half 2026 readouts—NIU top-line data and CLE proof-of-concept data, alongside DroTRA/difficult-to-treat RA Part 2 data with FDA feedback—that the preview did not lay out as part of its catalyst calendar. The CLE timing itself was in line with the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Multiple key readouts are expected in the second half of 2026, including NIU top-line data, DroTRA/difficult-to-treat RA Part 2 data with FDA feedback, and CLE proof-of-concept data.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said CLE was “Guided to H2 2026” and listed D2T RA registrational topline timing as “Guided to H2 CY2026.”

surprises.description: Roivant repurchased about $200 million of stock in the quarter, at an average price in the high $20s, compared with around $10 per share in the earlier $1.5 billion repurchase round. The preview said capital allocation would be discussed but did not anticipate a repurchase or its scale and price.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roivant repurchased about $200 million of stock in the quarter (slightly more including March), buying back at an average price in the high $20s versus around $10 per share in the earlier $1.5 billion round.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Roivant framing of Immunovant within its capital-allocation narrative” as a catalyst to watch, without specifying a buyback.

in_line: CLE timing remained in the second half of 2026, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Amylyx narrowed the expected Q3 Lucidity readout to late August or early September, rather than leaving the timing at a broad quarterly window. The last participant has completed the final visit, although the database remains blinded and unlocked.
surprises.fact_evidence: “expects top-line data ... in late August or early September 2026”; “the last participant having recently completed their final visit though the database remains blinded and unlocked.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has said it expects topline data from LUCIDITY in Q3 2026”; “a named month would be a positive one.”

surprises.description: Cash ended Q2 at $250.8 million, above the preview’s $240–245 million estimate, and Amylyx reaffirmed runway into 2028 through potential approval and launch milestones.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ended Q2 2026 with $250.8 million in cash and marketable securities”; “providing anticipated runway into 2028 through key milestones including potential FDA approval and commercial launch in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Expected cash of about $240–245M at 6/30”; the preview also said the “into 2028” claim “may depend on sub-consensus launch spend or on an equity raise.”

surprises.description: SG&A was $21.9 million, well above the preview’s $18–19 million on-plan range and above its $21 million burn-concern threshold. Amylyx attributed the increase to a one-time legal charge and commercial investment; lower R&D partially offset it, leaving total operating expenses up 7% year over year at $45.7 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A increasing to $21.9 million (from $15.6 million) due to a one-time legal charge and commercial investments, while R&D fell to $23.8 million (from $27.2 million) on reduced PSP spending”; “Total operating expenses rose 7% year-over-year to $45.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The full preview treats $18–19M as on-plan and above $21M as a burn concern.”

surprises.description: NDA preparation appears further along than the preview’s description of pre-writing sections: Amylyx said the 16-week Lucidity outcome is the last remaining piece needed to complete the NDA and that all other sections are actively being prepared. No submission timing was provided in the facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “the 16-week double-blind Lucidity outcome is the last remaining piece needed to complete the NDA, with all other sections actively being prepared.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said on the Q1 call that it is pre-writing NDA sections before unblinding.”

surprises.description: Amylyx disclosed a sizable estimated U.S. PBH population, including roughly 120,000 people with the Roux-en-Y gastric bypass history studied in Lucidity. The company said this still represents a substantial addressable market even under a narrow-label scenario; the preview did not provide market-size expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “approximately 160,000 people in the U.S. are living with PBH, of which roughly 120,000 had Roux-en-Y gastric bypass ... representing a substantial addressable market even under a narrow label scenario.”

surprises.description: Amylyx said Lucidity is powered at least 90% to detect a 35% treatment effect while tolerating up to a 50% placebo response, and cited a 55% reduction on the relevant composite endpoint in Phase 2. These trial-design and prior-data details were not addressed in the preview and are supportive context, not a Lucidity outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “powered at least 90% to detect a 35% treatment effect versus placebo, using conservative assumptions that tolerate up to a 50% placebo response”; prior Phase 2 data showed “a 55% reduction in the level 2/level 3 composite hypoglycemic endpoint.”

surprises.description: Amylyx disclosed that a label limited to Roux-en-Y patients could require an additional confirmatory study for sleeve-gastrectomy patients, a potential development burden not raised in the preview. Management characterized such a study as efficient and not overly burdensome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “If FDA restricts the label to Roux-en-Y gastric bypass patients, Amylyx believes an additional confirmatory study for sleeve gastrectomy patients would be efficient and not overly burdensome.”

surprises.description: Amylyx reported a second Gubra research collaboration, announced in July, to develop peptide candidates for another undisclosed rare endocrine disease. The preview flagged partnership activity as something to watch but did not anticipate or describe this collaboration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “entered a second research collaboration with Gubra in July to develop peptide candidates for another undisclosed rare endocrine disease.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “any partnership or ex-US licensing for avexitide” as a narrative risk to watch, but did not forecast a partnership.

surprises.description: Amylyx reported week-96 Wolfram syndrome data showing stabilization or improvement on AMX-0035. The preview flagged the timing of these data, but did not state an expected result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AMX-0035 for Wolfram syndrome (week 96 data showing stabilization/improvement).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch ... AMX0035 Wolfram Week 96 data timing.”

surprises.description: A PBH-specific ICD-10 code is set to take effect October 1, 2026, a new development not mentioned in the preview. Management said it is not required for reimbursement and that patients can already be identified through claims analysis, limiting its stated importance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A PBH-specific ICD-10 code will become effective October 1, 2026, though management noted it is not required for reimbursement and patients can already be identified via claims analysis.”

surprises.description: Amylyx said it has no competitors with a comparable profile in PBH, a favorable competitive-positioning claim not covered in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported no competitors with a comparable profile in PBH.”

in_line: AMX-318 remains in IND-enabling studies with a 2027 IND filing target, consistent with the preview’s reference to 2027 IND timing.

surprises.description: GoodRx reported Q2 revenue of $200.4 million, above the preview’s roughly $193.2–$193.6 million consensus estimates. The beat was about 3.5%–3.7%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $200.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $193.2M” and “Revenue | ~$193.6M.”

surprises.description: The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $790–805 million from $765–785 million, and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $240–250 million from at least $235 million. Management also said it was on track for year-over-year revenue growth earlier than previously expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $790-805 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $240-250 million, putting it on track for year-over-year revenue growth earlier than previously expected.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance: revenue $765–785M and adj. EBITDA ≥$235M” and the preview says a reaffirm at the midpoint would be “a soft negative.”

surprises.description: Pharma Direct revenue reached $61.6 million, above the preview’s $53 million watch level. GoodRx also raised its full-year Pharma Direct growth expectation to more than 70%, rather than merely reaffirming growth above 50%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pharma Direct revenue grew 76% year-over-year to $61.6 million” and management “raised its full-year Pharma Direct growth expectation from 50% to more than 70% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pharma Direct at or above $53M, with FY growth above 50% reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $63.7 million, exceeding the preview’s own derived estimate of roughly $56–59 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $63.7 million, representing a 31.8% adjusted EBITDA margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA consensus was not published; the preview's ~$56–59M figure is its own derived estimate.”

surprises.description: Prescription transaction revenue was $106.4 million, below the preview’s approximately $111 million reference level. Management expects continued moderation in this revenue as consumers shift toward subscriptions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Prescription transaction revenue was $106.4 million” and management “expects continued moderation in MAC and prescription transaction revenue as consumers shift to subscriptions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Prescription transactions versus about $111M.”

surprises.description: Monthly active consumers were 5 million, below the 5.3 million level the preview highlighted as a sign of stabilization. The call attributed the decline to a deliberate shift toward subscriptions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Monthly active consumers declining 12% year-over-year to 5 million, reflecting a deliberate shift toward subscriptions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “MACs at or above 5.3M” and “A second straight quarter at about 5.3M suggests the user base has stabilized.”

surprises.description: Subscription revenue rose 39% while subscription plans grew 14%, indicating higher revenue per plan. The preview identified Companion’s near-term revenue impact as small but did not provide an expectation for total subscription revenue or revenue per plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subscription revenue rose 39% year-over-year to $28.5 million, while subscription plans grew only 14%, indicating rising average revenue per plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The $14.99/month subscription launched May 27–28, 2026, so Q2 revenue impact is small. Member adds and attach rate are the focus.”

surprises.description: GoodRx said it had made GoodRx Companion its primary subscription offering over Gold. The preview noted Companion’s launch and pricing but did not flag replacing Gold as the primary offering.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company launched GoodRx Companion in May at $14.99/month (or $9.99/month annually) … and made it the primary subscription offering over Gold.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GoodRx Companion. The $14.99/month subscription launched May 27–28, 2026, so Q2 revenue impact is small.”

surprises.description: CFO Chris McGinnis departed, a management change the preview did not anticipate. The replacement is a 10-year company veteran, which provides continuity but does not remove the unexpected departure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Chris McGinnis departed and was replaced by Justin Fengler, a 10-year company veteran previously serving as Chief Strategy and Operations Officer.”

surprises.description: ESAB’s core organic growth turned positive at 2.5%, well ahead of the preview’s flat-to-down 1% base-case expectation. That indicates a stronger underlying demand and growth recovery than the preview’s key debate assumed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core organic growth of 2.5% driven by double-digit growth in automation and equipment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario anticipated “Organic ~flat to −1%,” and the preview called core organic growth the “real bar.”

surprises.description: Q2 sales of $766 million exceeded the preview’s $747.3–$750.1 million consensus range. The beat was modest relative to the expected sales level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q2 total sales of $766 million, up 13% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus Q2 revenue was “$747.3M – $750.1M.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance fell to $5.40–$5.50, below the prior $5.70–$5.90 range the preview highlighted as a key guide to watch. The reduction is notable despite the acquisition being incorporated into the updated outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EPS guidance is $5.40–$5.50.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed prior FY26 core adjusted EPS guidance of “$5.70 – $5.90” and asked whether it would be held.

surprises.description: The quarter’s adjusted EBITDA margin was 19.5%, at the bottom of the preview’s implied 19.5%–20.0% range and below its approximate 19.8% watch level. Management attributed the year-over-year decline to price-cost neutrality and commercial investments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 8% to $150 million, but adjusted EBITDA margin declined 90 basis points year-over-year to 19.5% due to transitory price-cost neutrality and targeted commercial investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave an implied margin range of “~19.5% – 20.0%” and identified “Core adj. EBITDA margin vs. ~19.8%” as a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: Management quantified a financing drag on Q2 EPS: debt financing reduced it by $0.13 and equity financing by another $0.03. The preview flagged share count and preferred-dividend treatment, but did not anticipate or quantify these specific impacts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total debt financing impacted Q2 EPS by $0.13 and equity financing created a $0.03 headwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “EPS bridge: share count and preferred dividend” and said “Diluted share count and its treatment matter.”

surprises.description: The Middle East, 7–8% of ESAB’s business, was down roughly 10–11%, while logistics costs there had tripled because of the conflict. The preview did not flag this regional disruption; management said rebuilding could eventually restore prior growth rates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Middle East, representing 7–8% of ESAB's business, was down double digits (~10–11%) with logistics costs tripling due to conflict, though rebuild efforts could restore prior ~20% growth rates.”

surprises.description: Management described DFI as a high-margin asset, with roughly 65% gross margins and 30% EBITDA margins, and cited a cross-selling funnel approaching $450 million plus about $20 million of targeted cost synergies. The funnel’s conversion is expected to take time and materialize mainly in 2027 and beyond, limiting the near-term benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DFI is a premier asset delivering high single-digit growth with approximately 65% gross margins and roughly 30% EBITDA margins”; its “cross-selling funnel with ESAB is approaching $450 million,” with conversion expected “mainly in 2027 and beyond,” and “roughly $20 million in cost synergies targeted.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA of $150 million was at the top of the preview’s implied Q2 range of approximately $146–$150 million.
The full-year organic growth outlook remained 2–4%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the prior core organic guidance might be held.
The preview anticipated an acquisition-inclusive FY26 guidance recast; the company provided updated sales and EBITDA guidance incorporating about nine percentage points from acquisitions.

surprises.description: The preview expected FY2026 revenue growth of 4.0%–6.5%, with an organic constant-currency floor of 2.5%. EPAM instead cut guidance to 3.2%–4.2% reported growth and 2%–3% organic constant currency.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management lowered full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to 3.2%-4.2% reported (2%-3% organic constant currency), citing North American weakness.
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY2026 revenue growth +4.0% to +6.5% (organic cc +2.5% to +5.0%).

surprises.description: The preview said consensus math implied Q3 revenue of about $1.44–$1.46 billion. EPAM guided to $1.410–$1.425 billion and also said revenue would be flattish from Q3 to Q4, indicating a weaker second-half trajectory than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $1.410-$1.425 billion implies only 1.7% year-over-year growth at the midpoint, with revenue expected to be flattish from Q3 to Q4.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus math implies Q3 around $1.44–$1.46B. A guide well below that suggests the large vendor-consolidation deals slipped again.

surprises.description: The preview highlighted a possible start to pipeline conversion in the second half of 2026. Instead, large AI-led deals with existing clients remained unsigned, with meaningful revenue contribution pushed into the first half of 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: A pipeline of large AI-led deals (Agentic managed services, application maintenance) with existing clients remains unsigned, with meaningful revenue contribution now pushed to first half of 2027 rather than second half 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Bull: Management says pipeline conversion has started ("signed," not "in the pipeline"). The preview also says Q3 below the implied range could suggest large vendor-consolidation deals slipped again.

surprises.description: The preview expected Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $3.14. EPAM reported $3.38, a clear beat of roughly 8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Non-GAAP diluted EPS grew 22% year-over-year to $3.38.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Non-GAAP diluted EPS consensus: $3.14.

surprises.description: The preview expected Q2 revenue of about $1.407 billion, near the midpoint of company guidance. EPAM reported $1.415 billion, at the high end of its outlook range and modestly above consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue was $1.415 billion, up 4.5% year-over-year reported and 3.4% organic constant currency, coming in at the high end of the outlook range.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus ~$1.407B (+~4.1% YoY); company guide $1.400B–$1.415B.

surprises.description: The preview expected Americas growth to reaccelerate in its bull scenario. Instead, the Americas grew only 0.5%, while EMEA grew 10.9%, showing a pronounced regional divergence and weakness concentrated in EPAM’s largest region.
surprises.fact_evidence: Americas, representing 57% of revenue, grew only 0.5% year-over-year, while EMEA (41% of revenue) grew 10.9% (9.4% constant currency).
surprises.expectation_evidence: Bull: “Americas growth reaccelerates.”

surprises.description: The preview warned that a second negative cash-flow quarter would be a concern and described positive Q2 operating cash flow as the base case. Operating cash flow was still negative at -$2 million, DSO rose to 82 days, and EPAM cut its full-year free-cash-flow conversion outlook to around 70%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 operating cash flow turned negative at -$2 million (versus +$53 million a year ago) with DSO rising to 82 days, prompting a cut in full-year free cash flow conversion guidance to around 70% versus the typical 80%-90%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: A second negative quarter would be a serious concern. Base scenario: “OCF positive but unremarkable”; the catalyst checklist also calls for operating cash flow recovery after Q1’s -$36.4M.

surprises.description: The preview expected the 15%–16% non-GAAP operating-margin range to remain the profitability target and flagged a possible trim as negative. EPAM instead raised its profitability guidance to the high end of that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Non-GAAP gross margin improved to 32% from 30.1% a year earlier, and management raised profitability guidance to the high end of the 15%-16% adjusted operating margin range.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Non-GAAP operating margin 15%–16%; “Trimming the FY margin band would be a negative signal.”

surprises.description: The preview estimated that roughly $145–$155 million of Q2 AI-native revenue was needed for straight-line progress toward the $600 million target. EPAM reported more than $160 million, above that expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Pure AI native revenues exceeded $160 million (over 11% of business), marking the sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit sequential growth and keeping the company on track for its $600 million 2026 target.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Straight-line progress to $600M requires roughly $145–$155M in Q2.

surprises.description: Q1 revenue was $339 million, up 6%, versus the preview’s $327.9 million consensus and 2% implied growth. The result exceeded the revenue bar by about $11 million and growth by 4 percentage points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6% (both reported and organic) to $339 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $327.9M” and “Implied Y/Y +2.0%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $1.14 was above the preview’s $1.07–$1.09 consensus range, beating even its higher estimate by 5 cents.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased 4% to $1.14.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $1.07 – $1.09.”

surprises.description: Management raised FY27 revenue-growth guidance to 5%–8% reported and 4%–7% organic, from the prior 4%–7% reported and 3%–6% organic outlook. The preview identified a guidance change as a key issue but described reaffirmation as its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year FY27 guidance to 5%-8% reported revenue growth and 4%-7% organic growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 guidance: Revenue growth of 4–7% reported, 3–6% organic” and “Base: … FY27 guide reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Plasma grew 8% organically, above the preview’s stated 6% threshold for the most bullish outcome. The preview had highlighted share gains and Persona PLUS conversions as the key swing factors, and the reported growth was aided by share gains and pricing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Plasma revenue grew 8% organic” and was “aided by share gains and Persona PLUS pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Plasma organic growth above 6% would be the most bullish datapoint.”

surprises.description: Persona PLUS was rolling out ahead of schedule, improving yield by more than 5% over prior Persona offerings, with management saying it could reach the entire U.S. market this year. The preview flagged conversions as a swing factor but did not anticipate this rollout pace or yield improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Persona PLUS is delivering yield improvements exceeding 5% over prior Persona offerings,” with rollout “ahead of schedule at 30-40 centers per week” and potential to convert “the entire U.S. market this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Persona PLUS conversions and share gains are the swing factors.”

surprises.description: Interventional Technologies returned to 3% organic growth, supporting the anticipated inflection after a 9% FY26 decline. However, sensor-guided technologies remained weak because of ensoETM softness and OEM weakness, a headwind not highlighted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Interventional Technologies returned to growth at 3% organic,” while “sensor-guided technologies were dragged down by ensoETM softness and OEM weakness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “IVT fell 9% in FY26. Management called Q4 the inflection point” and “A second straight quarter of IVT growth supports the Hospital guide.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 60.4%, above the preview’s roughly 59.4% consensus, even though the year-over-year comparison was down 40 basis points as expected. Management said margin expanded after excluding a roughly 200-basis-point prior-year benefit from upfront software-license revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 gross margin was 60.4%, down 40 basis points year-over-year, but expanded excluding a ~200 basis point prior-year benefit from upfront software license revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin ~59.4%” and “Implied Y/Y -40 bps.”

surprises.description: Q1 operating cash flow was $52 million, roughly three times the prior year, and trailing-12-month free-cash-flow conversion was 106%. This was stronger cash generation than the preview’s discussion of an approximately 80% FY27 conversion outlook and an inventory build suggested, although Q1 conversion itself was 75%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow conversion reached 75% of adjusted net income in Q1 (106% on a trailing 12-month basis), with operating cash flow of $52 million, roughly 3x the prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FCF conversion ~80% (vs. 89% in FY26), with an inventory build.”

surprises.description: The company paid down $100 million of revolver debt and said M&A was off the table for now in favor of organic growth and deleveraging. The preview did not flag this capital-allocation stance or a debt repayment as an expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company paid down $100 million of revolver debt (to $200 million outstanding)” and stated “M&A [is] off the table for now in favor of organic growth and deleveraging.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed FY27 adjusted operating-margin expansion of 50–100 basis points, consistent with the preview’s stated outlook.
Management continued to expect FY27 adjusted EPS growth broadly in line with reported revenue growth, matching the preview’s guidance summary.
The $153 million CSL-customer-loss and liquid-solutions-divestiture overhang was fully lapped, consistent with the preview’s framing of FY27 as the first year without that comparison distortion.

surprises.description: The preview expected reported revenue and attendance to fall because of the park sales, but the retained parks grew: same-park attendance rose 4% and net revenue 2%, despite 44 fewer operating days. These same-park figures are not directly comparable to the preview’s consolidated consensus estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “On a same-park basis, Q2 2026 attendance rose 4% … and net revenue increased 2% … despite 44 fewer operating days.”
