surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said the divested parks were ~10–11% of attendance but only ~6% of EBITDA, so reported revenue and attendance should fall YoY.”

surprises.description: Although the preview said Six Flags had withheld formal guidance all year, management gave a forward directional outlook: adjusted EBITDA is expected to grow year over year in both Q3 and Q4, with the larger opportunity in Q4. The outlook is notable given the stated Q3 calendar and wildfire headwinds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects adjusted EBITDA to grow year-over-year in both Q3 and Q4 2026, with the larger growth opportunity weighted toward Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The company does not give formal FY2026 guidance”; the preview also flagged “Possible narrative shift on guidance” and asked whether management would “reintroduce guidance or targets.”

surprises.description: The preview said the company did not provide formal FY2026 guidance, but the call included a specific full-year capital-expenditure range of $400 million to $425 million. The preview supplied no expected capex range for comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year capital expenditures are guided to the $400 million to $425 million range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The company does not give formal FY2026 guidance.”

in_line: Margins expanded year over year, consistent with the preview’s expectation that margins would rise; the call reported roughly 120 basis points of same-park expansion.
Management said all asset-sale proceeds will be used to pay down debt, consistent with the preview’s statement that the EPR proceeds were earmarked for debt paydown.

surprises.description: Kemper reported a $464.8 million net loss, driven primarily by a $460 million non-cash goodwill impairment in specialty auto. The preview focused on adjusted operating EPS and did not flag a goodwill write-down or a GAAP loss of this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss of $464.8 million, or $7.90 per share, driven primarily by a $460 million non-cash goodwill impairment in its specialty auto segment”; the impairment was “triggered by a sustained stock price decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted operating EPS” consensus was “$0.32 – $0.33”; the preview did not mention a goodwill impairment.

surprises.description: Adjusted operating income was $0.45 per share, above the preview’s $0.32–$0.33 consensus range by roughly 36%–41%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted consolidated net operating income was $26.3 million, or $0.45 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted operating EPS” consensus: “$0.32 – $0.33.”

surprises.description: Kemper recorded a separate allowance for credit losses on surplus notes issued to Kemper Reciprocal Exchange, and about $15 million of notes still remain to be evaluated. The preview did not flag this charge or the remaining evaluation risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $16.6 million after-tax ($21 million pre-tax) allowance for credit losses” was recorded, with “roughly $15 million of surplus notes remaining to be evaluated going forward.”

surprises.description: Commercial auto reported $17.7 million of adverse prior-year reserve development, continuing a roughly five-quarter pattern. The preview identified reserve strengthening as a risk, but the repeated development and its reported amount show that the risk materialized.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported results were hurt by $17.7 million of prior year reserve development, marking roughly the fifth consecutive quarter of adverse development.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New-CEO reserve review. … Reserve strengthening is a risk.”

surprises.description: Management said commercial auto’s reserve concentration is prompting meaningfully higher rates and tighter underwriting, even at the expense of near-term growth. The preview expected commercial auto to be grown and did not anticipate this explicit pullback in underwriting for reserve-risk reasons.
surprises.fact_evidence: Commercial auto has “about $1 billion in reserves, 90% tied to bodily injury coverage and 45% concentrated in litigious California,” prompting management to “take meaningfully more rate and tighten underwriting at the expense of near-term growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “California is being shrunk; Florida/Texas and commercial auto are being grown.”

surprises.description: Personal auto remained unprofitable despite the improved underlying combined ratio, and management said California needs double-digit rate increases to restore profitability. The preview expected California rate actions to start helping, but did not state that double-digit increases would still be needed.
surprises.fact_evidence: Personal auto’s normalized underlying combined ratio improved to 105.2%, “but remains unprofitable and requires double-digit rate increases in California to restore profitability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had guided to “initial benefits from California rate actions in Q2, with more meaningful impact in 2H 2026.”

surprises.description: California personal auto policies fell 10% sequentially, reducing the state’s share of the portfolio by 2.5 percentage points in the quarter. The preview expected California shrinkage, but the reported sequential decline gives a sharper indication of its pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “California’s share of the personal auto portfolio declined 2.5 percentage points during the quarter, driven by a 10% sequential decline in policies in force.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “California is being shrunk”; the preview said to “watch whether California PIF falls.”

surprises.description: Kemper disclosed more than $80 million of cumulative annualized run-rate restructuring savings, up $20 million from the prior quarter. The preview did not identify restructuring savings as an expected result or catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “identified more than $80 million of cumulative annualized run-rate restructuring savings (up $20 million from last quarter).”

in_line: Personal auto’s normalized underlying combined ratio improved to 105.2%, consistent with the preview’s base-case range of about 105%–106%, though it narrowly missed the preview’s stated sub-105% inflection threshold.
California personal auto policies declined, matching the preview’s expectation that California would be shrunk.
Commercial auto policies in force grew 9.2% year over year, consistent with the preview’s expectation that commercial auto would be grown.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $76.1 million, below the preview’s rough $82–88 million estimate. Excluding Longridge, EBITDA was a record $48.7 million, but that does not erase the shortfall against the preview’s estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA reached $76.1 million”; “excluding Longridge (held for sale) it was a record $48.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My own rough estimate is $82–88M”; the preview also said its “core EBITDA” base case was $82–88M.

surprises.description: Wheeling’s targeted cost synergies are now described as $20 million, below the $23 million target cited in the preview. Management said the integration is about 80% complete, but the full impact will not appear until Q3 and Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Wheeling integration is roughly 80% complete with $20 million of targeted cost synergies on track, though full impact will not appear until Q3 and Q4 as initiatives ramp.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$10M of the $23M targeted synergies realized.”

surprises.description: Jefferson’s crude ship volumes were temporarily reduced by Middle East volatility, a near-term operating headwind not flagged in the preview. Management expects the volumes to recover in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Crude ship volumes were temporarily reduced by Middle East volatility and are expected to recover in Q3.”

surprises.description: Transtar volumes were softer because US Steel overhauled its largest Gary Works blast furnace. Higher-priced Wheeling carloads offset the weakness by lifting blended pricing, so the volume pressure did not translate into an unmitigated pricing impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Transtar volumes were softer in Q2 due to US Steel's overhaul of its largest Gary Works blast furnace, but this was offset by higher-priced Wheeling carloads driving higher blended pricing.”

surprises.description: FIP acquired Tidewater Logistics for $45 million in cash, adding an expected $9 million of annual EBITDA, but funded the purchase with an add-on to the parent-level term loan. The specific acquisition and debt funding were not laid out in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company acquired Tidewater Logistics at the end of Q2 for $45 million in cash, expected to add approximately $9 million of annual EBITDA, funded via an add-on to the parent-level term loan.”

surprises.description: Management identified more than $50 million of incremental annual EBITDA potential from new rail revenue sources, an upside opportunity not quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management estimates in excess of $50 million of incremental annual EBITDA potential from new rail revenue sources.”

surprises.description: Management put a value of more than $50 million of EBITDA on three Jefferson expansion projects that require little to no additional capex. The preview noted that three customer expansions were under negotiation but did not give an EBITDA estimate or indicate the low-capex potential.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A separate $50 million-plus opportunity from three Jefferson expansion projects requiring little to no additional capex.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for ... the status of three customer expansions under negotiation.”

surprises.description: Management said Repauno Phases 1 and 2 together can handle nearly 100,000 barrels per day and represent roughly $80 million of annual EBITDA, adding a quantified earnings opportunity beyond the preview’s schedule-focused discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Combined Phase 1 and 2 can handle nearly 100,000 barrels per day representing roughly $80 million of annual EBITDA.”

in_line: Repauno Phase 2 remains targeted for completion by year-end 2026, with revenue expected to begin in early 2027, consistent with the preview’s fall/end-2026 completion and early-2027 revenue baseline.
The Longridge sale is still expected to close in Q3, consistent with the preview’s base scenario.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $653 million, far above the preview’s roughly $496 million management-implied bar and also above the $597.7 million published consensus. The preview expected revenue roughly in line with Q1; management said the result exceeded its expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached $653 million, up 31% versus Q1 … both above management’s expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … Management-implied Q2 ~$496M”; Q2 revenue was guided “in line with Q1.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $28 million exceeded the preview’s roughly $22 million management-implied expectation, although it was within the preview’s derived $25–30 million consensus range. The beat was also partly due to prior-year development recognized earlier than expected, tempering the underlying improvement into Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $28 million … above management’s expectations”; outperformance stemmed from “recognizing prior-year development originally expected in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA … ~$22M” management-implied; “~$25–30M (derived, not published)” consensus.

surprises.description: Evolent raised its FY2026 revenue range to $2.6–$2.7 billion from $2.4–$2.6 billion and narrowed its adjusted EBITDA range to $120–$135 million, lifting the midpoint. That is better than the preview’s key question of whether the existing guide would merely be reaffirmed or cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $2.6-$2.7 billion (from $2.4-$2.6 billion) and narrowed adjusted EBITDA guidance to $120-$135 million (from $110-$140 million), raising the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guide ($110–140M). Reaffirm, trim, or cut”; the base scenario expected the EBITDA guide to be held and revenue potentially trimmed.

surprises.description: Management made a firm 2027 commitment: adjusted EBITDA midpoint at or above $150 million and revenue growth above 25%, supported by contracts already under agreement. The preview did not set out a 2027 outlook or anticipate this level of commitment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Committed to a 2027 adjusted EBITDA midpoint at or above $150 million and expects revenue growth of more than 25% in 2027, based on contracts already under agreement.”

surprises.description: Q2 MER came in at 95%, above the preview’s approximately 93% expectation, with management attributing the increase to the Highmark Performance Suite launch. The full-year MER expectation remained around 93%, so the reported quarterly pressure was not accompanied by a higher full-year expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 medical expense ratio was 95%, up ~200 basis points from Q1's 93%, driven by the May 1 Highmark Performance Suite launch, with full-year MER still expected around 93%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “MER … ~93%” management-implied for Q2; the preview’s base scenario also had MER at “~93%.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for Q3 launch confirmation on expansion contracts, including a national payer oncology/cardiology expansion expected to launch in Q3. The call described an oncology Performance Suite partnership with an expected launch by December 2026, later than that Q3 window, while giving the opportunity a larger stated annualized revenue figure of about $300 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new oncology Performance Suite partnership with an existing imaging client covering ~1.5 million lives across 11 states is expected to launch by December 2026 and generate ~$300 million in annualized revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The 4.5M-lives advanced imaging expansion and the national payer oncology/cardiology expansion (>$200M annually) both launch in Q3 2026”; the preview said a specific launch date was needed.

surprises.description: The Auth Intelligence platform is producing concrete automation gains: auto-approval rates rose by as much as 20 percentage points, and the system now handles over one-third of authorizations that previously needed manual clinical review. The preview mentioned AI as a possible source of opex leverage but did not anticipate these quantified operating results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Auth Intelligence AI platform … has lifted auto-approval rates by up to 20 percentage points (e.g., 55% to 75%) and now handles over one-third of authorization volume previously requiring manual clinical review.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bull scenario said “the AI auto-approval initiative shows up as opex leverage.”

surprises.description: The timing of EBITDA improvement shifted later: Q2’s beat included development originally expected in Q3, leaving only about $4–$7 million of increase from Q2 to Q3. That is below the preview’s expected $10–$15 million Q3 improvement, although the expected Q3-to-Q4 increase of $7–$15 million remains broadly consistent with the preview’s Q4 step-up expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA outperformance stemmed from recognizing prior-year development originally expected in Q3, so the Q2-to-Q3 increase was cut to ~$4-$7 million with Q3-to-Q4 expected at $7-$15 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sequential EBITDA improvement of $10–15M expected in Q3 and Q4.”

surprises.description: Management quantified a Medicaid expansion membership headwind that the preview had not identified: an expected roughly 20% industry-wide decline translates to 4–5% lower Medicaid membership for Evolent, with Tech & Services revenue likely flat to down in 2027. This adds a specific headwind to the longer-term outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects a ~20% decline in Medicaid expansion members industry-wide, translating to a roughly 4-5% Medicaid membership headwind for Evolent, with Tech & Services revenue likely flat to down in 2027.”

in_line: Full-year MER remained expected around 93%, consistent with the preview’s approximately 93% MER expectation, even though Q2 MER was higher.
Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $28 million was within the preview’s derived $25–30 million consensus range, despite exceeding the lower management-implied estimate.

surprises.description: Intellia reported a strong Phase III HAELO result for lonvo-z: the trial met its primary and all key secondary endpoints, with an 87% reduction in mean monthly attacks versus placebo. The preview focused on BLA timing rather than an efficacy readout, so it did not set an expectation for this result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “achieved statistical significance on the primary and all key secondary endpoints,” showing “an 87% reduction in mean monthly attacks versus placebo”; 62% of patients were “entirely attack-free and therapy-free,” and every patient had an attack-rate reduction.

surprises.description: The lonvo-z treatment arm also had a favorable safety profile in the HAELO data, with no serious adverse events and only Grade 1 or Grade 2 treatment-emergent adverse events. The preview did not discuss expected lonvo-z safety results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “All treatment-emergent adverse events” were Grade 1 or Grade 2, with “no serious adverse events in the treatment arm as of the data cutoff.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s focus on clean liver safety after nex-z re-enrollment, Intellia disclosed Grade 3+ transaminase elevations associated with the HLA C*05:01 allele, including all five highest elevations, and rare Grade 4 events. The events were uncommon and mostly resolved without intervention, and the company has added HLA typing and monitoring.
surprises.fact_evidence: Among more than 600 samples, C*05:01 carriers (12%) had “significantly higher rates of Grade 3+ transaminase elevations,” and “all five highest elevations” were in carriers. Grade 4 elevations occurred in less than 1% of MAGNITUDE patients, were transient and mostly resolved without intervention; HLA typing and monitoring measures were implemented.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Any new Grade 3/4 transaminase event would revive platform-risk concerns” and identified “clean liver safety on re-enrollment” as a bull-scenario driver.

surprises.description: Intellia reported substantial nex-z TTR lowering—90% on average, to below 20 micrograms per milliliter, reached within a month and maintained across patients dosed since 2021. The preview did not provide an expectation for nex-z’s TTR-lowering performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Nex-z demonstrated a “90% mean TTR reduction,” with serum TTR “below 20 micrograms per milliliter,” achieved within one month and maintained consistently across all patients since 2021 dosing.

surprises.description: Ending cash of $628.4 million exceeded the preview’s base-case cash range of $605–620 million, although it met the preview’s broader expectation of at least $600 million. The stated runway into at least 2028 was as expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: Intellia ended Q2 with “$628.4 million in cash” and runway “into at least 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case projected “cash ~$605–620M” and its checklist called for cash “at or above $600M,” with “at least into 2028” repeated.

surprises.description: Management gave a reassuring update on MAGNITUDE’s blinded event rate, saying it remained within the company’s internal projected range, while also reporting enrollment above 650 patients. The preview flagged the trial’s enrollment and safety as issues to watch but did not anticipate this specific update.
surprises.fact_evidence: MAGNITUDE had “enrolled over 650 patients with a blinded event rate within their internally projected range.”

in_line: Lonvo-z BLA timing remained consistent with the preview’s expectation of H2 2026 completion and a potential H1 2027 launch: management expects FDA acceptance by year-end and a potential U.S. launch in the first half of 2027.

Nex-z enrollment and dosing resumed in both Phase III trials in Q2 after the holds were resolved, consistent with the preview’s focus on re-enrollment progress; MAGNITUDE-2 enrollment remains on track to finish later this year.
The $106.6 million Q2 net loss was close to the preview’s implied net loss of roughly $108 million.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was expected around $310 million, with company guidance of $310 million ± $20 million. Instead, revenue rose 36.2% sequentially and 123% year over year and exceeded guidance, a stronger result than the preview’s central estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 FY2026 revenue increased 36.2% sequentially and 123% year-over-year, exceeding guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $310M” consensus; “$310M ± $20M” company guidance.

surprises.description: Q3 EPS substantially exceeded the preview’s estimates: the call’s Q3 figures were $1.20 non-GAAP and $1.07 GAAP, versus expectations of $1.00 and about $0.87, respectively.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q4 EPS was “up from Q3's $1.07 GAAP and $1.20 non-GAAP EPS.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS | $1.00”; “GAAP diluted EPS | ~$0.87.”

surprises.description: The Q4 outlook was well above the preview’s implied bar: revenue guidance of $375 million versus about $328 million, and non-GAAP EPS of $1.42 versus about $1.13. Both the revenue and earnings outlook point to a stronger next quarter than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 FY2026 revenue to $375 million”; “Q4 FY2026…non-GAAP EPS to $1.42.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied Q4 bar (derived, not published): about $328M revenue and $1.13 non-GAAP EPS.”

surprises.description: Advanced Solutions revenue set a new high, exceeding the prior quarter’s record by 20%. That contrasts with the preview’s report that the segment had declined sequentially in Q2 on lower refurbished-system sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Advanced Solutions segment revenue exceeded last quarter's record by 20%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “APS was down sequentially on lower refurbished-system sales.”

surprises.description: Management put a sizable FY2027 TCB revenue range on the table—$150 million to $200 million, implying 50–100% growth over the FY2026 target. The preview discussed the FY2026 target but did not give an FY2027 TCB forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management projects thermal compression bonding (TCB) revenue of $150 million to $200 million in FY2027, implying 50-100% growth over the FY2026 target.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged possible memory and China digestion, but management described very high utilization and orders extending unusually far into the future. China utilization was over 95%, utilization was around 90% in memory and general semiconductor, and inbound POs reached into fiscal Q2 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Utilization rates reached over 95% in China and around 90% across memory and general semiconductor end markets, with inbound POs extending unusually far into fiscal Q2 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Memory and China. Watch whether DRAM share gains continue and whether China is digesting.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that it had quadrupled traditional wire-bonding capacity over two quarters and had previously supported $400 million quarterly run rates. The preview discussed investment to support roughly $400 million of annual Advanced Solutions revenue, but did not anticipate this scale of traditional wire-bonding capacity or quarterly run-rate capability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company increased its traditional wire bonding capacity 4x over the past two quarters and indicated it has previously supported $400 million quarterly run rates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 capex was raised from about $12M to about $22M, to support roughly $400M of annual Advanced Solutions revenue by 1H FY2027.”

surprises.description: Management added a demand rationale not covered in the preview: data centers now account for approximately 40% of the NAND market, and those applications rely on wire bonding at least as much as smartphones and PCs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management stated data center now represents approximately 40% of the NAND market and relies on wire bonding at least as much as smartphones and PCs.”

surprises.description: Management said it plans to deliver a hybrid-bonding tool to a customer in the first half of FY2027. The preview discussed TCB and an HBM qualification, but did not mention this hybrid-bonding customer delivery milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to deliver a hybrid bonding tool to a customer in the first half of fiscal 2027.”

in_line: Q4 gross margin guidance of 48% matched the preview’s expectation of at least 48%.
Management maintained its FY2026 TCB target of more than $100 million, consistent with the preview’s stated target.

surprises.description: KDP reported Q2 EPS of $0.57, above the preview’s $0.55 consensus estimate and management’s expectations. EPS growth of 16.3% also exceeded the preview’s cited 12.2% consensus growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 EPS grew 16.3% to $0.57, exceeding company expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS | $0.55 (one provider shows $0.5370)” and “Y/Y | +12.2%.”

surprises.description: Total net sales growth was faster than the preview’s expected 72.3% growth, though the reported increase was largely driven by the JDE Peet’s acquisition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total net sales up 74.6%, largely driven by the JDE Peet's acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s consensus table showed net sales growth of “+72.3% at $7.17B.”

surprises.description: U.S. Refreshment Beverages grew 10% in sales, ahead of the preview’s roughly 7% growth expectation, with volume/mix of 6.5 points also above the preview’s 5-point watch level. The preview had not expected this much strength in the company’s key growth engine.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. Refreshment Beverages… delivered 10% net sales growth (6.5 points volume/mix, 3.5 points pricing) and 11.9% operating income growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus implies growth decelerating to about +7%. Watch whether volume/mix stays at or above 5 points.”

surprises.description: U.S. Coffee remained under substantial pressure: operating income fell 24.7% and pod shipments declined even excluding the Peet’s reporting shift. That contrasts with the preview’s expectation of meaningful coffee-margin easing in Q2 after Q1 was described as the peak in year-over-year pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. Coffee operating income fell 24.7% due to green coffee inflation and tariffs, with pod shipments down 11.6% as reported (8.3% excluding the Peet's reporting shift).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “On the Q1 call, management said Q1 was the peak year-over-year margin pressure for coffee, with meaningful easing in Q2 and more substantial improvement in 2H.”

surprises.description: Management now expects legacy KDP sales growth at the high end of its 4–6% range, a more favorable outlook than simply carrying forward the full range cited in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now expects growth at the high end of the 4-6% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY2026 build included “legacy KDP at 4–6% constant-currency sales and EPS growth.”

surprises.description: Management warned that JDE Peet’s Q2 profit contribution likely marks its 2026 quarterly high watermark, citing timing benefits and the Peet’s K-Cup reporting shift. The preview did not flag that near-term contribution could be lower after this quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The JDE Peet's segment generated $2.8 billion in net sales and $414 million in operating income, but management warned this Q2 profit likely represents the high watermark for quarterly earnings contribution in 2026 due to timing benefits and the Peet's K-Cup reporting shift.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a new 2% non-cash EPS headwind from purchase-price-allocation depreciation, offset by a one-time cash benefit from tariff refunds, leaving the net EPS impact neutral. Neither offsetting item was anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An incremental 2% non-cash depreciation EPS headwind from the JDE Peet's purchase price allocation, offset by a one-time cash benefit from tariff refunds, netting to neutral EPS impact.”

surprises.description: Pro forma leverage was 4.4x at quarter end, slightly better than the preview’s cited mid-year level of about 4.5x, indicating somewhat faster progress on deleveraging than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pro forma management leverage improved to 4.4x at quarter end (slightly better than expected).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Net leverage about 4.5x at mid-year” and that leverage needed to be visibly moving down.

surprises.description: The energy portfolio’s scale and share milestone were not raised in the preview: it has surpassed 9% market share and become a roughly $1.5 billion net-sales business, with a double-digit share already achieved in 15 major customers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The energy portfolio crossed 9% market share (up from under 1% four years ago), now a ~$1.5 billion net sales business led by Bloom, GHOST, and C4, tracking toward a double-digit share goal already achieved in 15 major customers.”

in_line: Full-year guidance was reaffirmed: low-double-digit constant-currency EPS growth and total net sales of $25.9–26.4 billion, as the preview identified reaffirmation as the base case.
The approximately $2.5 billion full-year free-cash-flow target was maintained, consistent with the preview.
The Global Coffee Co. separation remains targeted for early 2027 and the CEO search is underway; the preview already described the search and that timeline.

surprises.description: BRINSUPRI revenue was $309.2 million, about $24 million above the preview’s roughly $285 million estimate and above the $290 million level it highlighted. Sequential growth was 49%, versus the preview’s 28% consensus growth estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BRINSUPRI generated $309.2 million in revenue in its third full quarter of launch, up 49% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “BRINSUPRI revenue: ~$285M”; “Q/Q revenue growth: +28%”; and “The $290M+ level matters most for the stock.”

surprises.description: Insmed raised 2026 BRINSUPRI revenue guidance to $1.25–1.4 billion, well above the preview’s $1.10 billion-or-higher level to watch. The preview warned that simply reiterating at least $1 billion would be disappointing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 BRINSUPRI revenue guidance to $1.25-1.4 billion, up from prior guidance of greater than $1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 BRINSUPRI guide at or above $1.10B”; “An increase to about $1.1B or higher is the figure to watch.”

surprises.description: The company reported about 7,000 new BRINSUPRI patients, beating the 6,300 expected, and said all came from organic demand after the ready-and-waiting cohort was exhausted. The preview specifically identified this as the first quarter without that cohort and flagged slower organic starts as a risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BRINSUPRI added approximately 7,000 new patients in Q2, beating the prior expectation of 6,300, with all coming from organic demand as ready-and-waiting patients are exhausted.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 is the first quarter without the pre-launch cohort, so new patient starts show organic demand. Watch for slower new starts”; the preview also derived about 6,300 organic starts from prior-quarter figures.

surprises.description: BRINSUPRI gross-to-net guidance was narrowed and shifted favorably to the mid-to-high 20s, rather than the prior mid-20s to low-30s range. That is better than the preview’s concern that gross-to-net could move toward the low-30s end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BRINSUPRI gross-to-net guidance was improved and narrowed to mid-to-high 20s from mid-20s to low 30s.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for … gross-to-net moving toward the low-30s%”; the prior range was “mid-20s to low-30s%.”

surprises.description: Insmed raised BRINSUPRI’s global peak-sales estimate to greater than $7 billion from greater than $5 billion. The preview did not provide a peak-sales expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BRINSUPRI's global peak sales estimate was raised to greater than $7 billion from greater than $5 billion, excluding potential upside from comorbid COPD and asthma populations.”

surprises.description: The TPIP peak-sales estimate rose threefold to greater than $6 billion from greater than $2 billion, assuming success across four indications. The preview discussed upcoming TPIP data but gave no peak-sales estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TPIP's peak sales estimate was increased threefold to greater than $6 billion from greater than $2 billion, assuming clinical and regulatory success across all four indications (PH-ILD, PAH, PPF, IPF).”

surprises.description: The company disclosed TPIP 12-month open-label extension results in this release, earlier than the preview’s Q3 2026 timing, with reported improvements in walking distance and NT-proBNP and high treatment continuation. The preview did not set expectations for the results themselves.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TPIP's 12-month PAH open-label extension showed ~55-meter 6-minute walk improvement, ~60% NT-proBNP reduction, 91% treatment continuation, and 65% of patients reaching refined low-risk status.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “TPIP Phase 2b OLE data, guided for Q3 2026.”

surprises.description: Insmed raised the combined peak-sales estimate for its three lead assets to more than $14 billion, a 75% increase from the prior estimate above $8 billion. The preview did not discuss a combined peak-sales estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Combined peak sales estimates for the three lead assets now exceed $14 billion, a 75% increase from the prior greater than $8 billion projection.”

in_line: The company reiterated its expectation to reach cash-flow positivity in 2027 without raising additional capital, as the preview expected management to reaffirm; it also ended Q2 with approximately $1.2 billion in cash, in line with the preview’s stated cash position.
Payer approval rates remained around 90%, consistent with the preview’s prior-quarter launch metrics.

surprises.description: Q2 same-club sales came in at 1.7%, above the preview’s modeled 0–1% range and the roughly 0% implied by the annual outlook. The beat was modest and came entirely from rate growth, not member growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “System-wide same club sales grew 1.7% in Q2 2026.” The growth was “driven entirely by rate growth (over 100% of the comp) rather than member growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Modeled estimates for Q2 adj. EBITDA (~$150M), SCS (~0–1%), and total members (~21.4–21.5M) are the author's own and are not consensus.” The preview also said Q1’s +3.5% and the ~1% full-year guide “imply roughly 0% for Q2–Q4.”

surprises.description: Planet Fitness raised its full-year EPS growth outlook to about 6% from 4%, a larger increase than the preview’s May-revised outlook. The company attributed the improvement to share repurchases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year EPS growth outlook to approximately 6% (from 4%) driven by share repurchases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The revised FY2026 outlook listed “Adj. EPS growth” at “~4% (~$3.19).”

surprises.description: The member count landed in the preview’s base range, but it was flat sequentially, and the sales comp was not being supported by member growth. That is weaker evidence of a membership-funnel recovery than the preview’s 21.6M-or-more threshold for the fix appearing to work.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 ended with “21.5 million members,” “flat compared to Q1,” and same-club sales growth was driven “entirely” by rate growth rather than member growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Roughly 21.6M or more would suggest the fix is working” and gave a base scenario of “21.4–21.5M.”

surprises.description: Revenue exceeded the early-August consensus estimate, coming in about $9 million higher than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose 7% to $365 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus was “$355.8M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was slightly above the preview’s modeled estimate, although the preview identified that figure as an author estimate rather than consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 3.5% to $153 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave a modeled Q2 adjusted EBITDA estimate of “~$150M” and noted it was “the author's own and [not] consensus.”

surprises.description: Average attrition was at the midpoint of its historical range, rather than in the top half that management had guided investors to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Average monthly attrition was 3.5%, the midpoint of the historical 3%-4% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “guided attrition to the top half of its 3–4% monthly range.”

surprises.description: The company announced a national test of a $10 Classic Card promotion, a promotional price move not flagged in the preview. Management said it was not a permanent rollback of the $15 price.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company will test a $10 Classic Card promotion nationally later this quarter” and said it “is not intended to roll back the $15 price permanently.”

surprises.description: Planet Fitness completed the sale of its Australia franchise stake and indicated it may also exit its Spain territory and some corporate clubs, capital-recycling moves the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed the sale of its Australia franchise stake to Franchise Equity Partners” and signaled “potential future exits of its Spain territory and select corporate clubs to recycle capital.”

in_line: Ending members were 21.5M, matching the preview’s modeled 21.4–21.5M base range, even though the count was flat sequentially.
The nationwide rollout of the Black Card price increase remained paused, consistent with the preview’s account that management had already paused it and that resumption was a key item to watch.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $37.4 million, above the preview’s modeled $34–35 million bar. That is a stronger result than the central expectation, although it falls within the preview’s bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA rose 29% year-over-year to $37.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$34–35M (modeled, not a published Street line)” and the catalyst checklist cites “the ~$34–35M implied bar.”

surprises.description: Attributed lives exceeded the upper end of the prior full-year guidance, rather than merely supporting another increase to the outlook. The preview expected a second raise, but did not anticipate that lives would already be above the former ceiling.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Attributed lives now above the high end of prior guidance”; Privia serves “over 1.64 million attributed lives.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A second raise would signal continued momentum” and prior guidance was “1.600–1.625M.”

surprises.description: Management now expects 70%–80% of full-year adjusted EBITDA to convert to free cash flow, a range that extends materially below the preview’s expectation of about 80%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expects 70% to 80% of full-year adjusted EBITDA to convert to free cash flow as a full cash taxpayer.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY26 guidance included “about 80% of adj. EBITDA converting to FCF.”

surprises.description: CMS may delay final MSSP reconciliation results until November, creating an atypical year-end cash-flow pattern that the preview did not flag. Management expects minimal impact on accruals and no issue receiving the cash, which limits the stated concern to timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CMS may delay final MSSP reconciliation results for performance year 2025 until November, creating an atypical year-end cash flow dynamic”; management expects “minimal impact on accruals and no issues receiving the cash.”

in_line: The preview said holding adjusted EBITDA at about 27% or more of care margin would support operating leverage; Q2 was 28.3%, broadly consistent with that expectation.

The preview expected FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance to be raised, and the company did raise it. The revised guidance ranges were not provided in the call facts, so the size of the increase cannot be compared with the preview’s scenarios.
Management’s long-term EBITDA-to-care-margin ambition of 30%–35% and roughly 20% long-term EBITDA growth target were consistent with the targets discussed in the preview.

surprises.description: Q2 operating cash burn was $11.1 million, above the preview’s $9–10 million base case and the company’s $8–9 million quarterly guide. Management nevertheless reiterated the $32–36 million full-year burn outlook, expecting a lower pace in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash burn (including CapEx) was $11.1 million in Q2, running above the guided $8-9 million quarterly average,” while “full-year burn guidance of $32-36 million was reiterated with expectations for a lower second-half pace (~$12 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “burn $9–10M”; it also flagged “Cash burn vs. the $8–9M/quarter guide” and said a second overshoot would turn a one-time explanation into a pattern.

surprises.description: Palladyne secured rights to Americanize and manufacture IAI’s Harop, Harpy, and Mini Harpy munitions, a substantial new program not anticipated in the preview. The potential is very large, but initial units depend on a government demand signal and may be about 18 months away.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “secured rights to Americanize and manufacture IAI's Harop, Harpy, and Mini Harpy loitering munitions,” which management believes “could ultimately generate hundreds of millions to billions of dollars in revenue,” with initial units potentially available “in about 18 months once a government demand signal materializes.”

surprises.description: A defense prime placed a follow-on order for more than 1,000 Brain FC1 units, valued at about $2.3 million, with the order five times larger than its prior one. The preview did not identify this customer order as an expected result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A defense prime placed a follow-on order five times larger than its prior order, covering more than 1,000 Brain FC1 units valued at approximately $2.3 million.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed $2.3 million of stock-based compensation from June executive equity awards, contributing to G&A of $8.1 million. This was an unanticipated expense item, even though reported GAAP EPS fell within the preview’s base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “G&A rising to $8.1 million driven by $2.3 million in stock-based compensation from June executive equity awards.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was about 29%, a little below the preview’s 30–33% base-case range. Management attributed the pressure to low manufacturing utilization and setup costs for new programs not yet covered by revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin was approximately 29%, held down by manufacturing utilization running well below capacity and setup costs for new programs not yet covered by revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “GM 30–33%” and flagged gross margin against a “~30% base.”

surprises.description: Palladyne said it had submitted proposals for more than 20 Department of War funding programs with aggregate initial potential value of several hundred million dollars. This expands the disclosed opportunity pipeline, though the proposals are not awards.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has submitted proposals for more than 20 Department of War funding programs with aggregate initial potential value of several hundred million dollars.”

surprises.description: Backlog was about $24.6 million, slightly above the preview’s $24.0 million figure, and the company reported roughly $13 million of new Q2 bookings. The preview had flagged backlog and conversion timing, but not the quarter’s bookings figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog grew to approximately $24.6 million (a 43% increase from $17 million in Q1), reflecting roughly $13 million of new bookings during the quarter,” with a majority expected to convert over the next 12–18 months.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Backlog (6/30) | $24.0M” and said management expected a “majority” to convert over 12–18 months.

in_line: Q2 revenue was $5.8 million, matching the preview’s figure, which it noted had already been pre-announced.
FY2026 revenue guidance of $24–27 million was reaffirmed, as the preview’s base case expected; the preview had identified the H2 ramp as the main guidance risk.
Cash and marketable securities were approximately $43.7 million, in line with the preview’s approximately $44.0 million estimate.
GAAP diluted EPS was a loss of $0.27, within the preview’s base-case range of a $0.25–$0.27 loss; the consensus EPS basis was noted as unclear.

The $2.9 million Air Force robotics contract expansion to more than $10.6 million total was in line with the preview, which said the STRATFI option had been exercised and identified the $2.9 million award.

surprises.description: Oscar’s Q2 MLR was 79.2%, about 3.8 percentage points below the roughly 83% implied by consensus and within the preview’s bullish 79%–81% scenario. The preview’s base case was 82.5%–83.5%, so claims costs were substantially better than the central expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 medical loss ratio improved nearly 12 points year-over-year to 79.2%,” aided by favorable prior period development and disciplined pricing.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied MLR: back-solving the $0.37 consensus gives roughly an 83% Q2 medical loss ratio”; the base scenario expected “82.5–83.5%.”

surprises.description: Q2 earnings from operations were $389 million, while the preview said the existing full-year guide implied an operating loss across Q2–Q4. The actual quarter therefore delivered substantial operating profit rather than the loss implied by that outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 earnings from operations improved $619 million year-over-year to $389 million, with operating margin expanding 16 points to 8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The guide implies an operating loss across Q2–Q4.”

surprises.description: Oscar reported a large favorable prior-period adjustment, including an approximately $160 million favorable 2025 CMS risk-adjustment true-up. The preview had highlighted prior-period risk-adjustment development as a concern, including $85 million of adverse prior-year development in Q1, so this favorable Q2 adjustment was a notable reversal and boosted reported MLR.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total favorable prior period development was $164 million in Q2 (including a ~$160 million favorable 2025 CMS risk adjustment true-up) and $232 million year-to-date, boosting reported MLR.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 “carried $85M of adverse prior-year risk-adjustment development” and flagged the risk-adjustment accrual and prior-period development as items to watch.

surprises.description: The Q2 SG&A ratio fell to 14.2%, reaching Oscar’s long-term target roughly a year earlier than planned. That is a stronger cost-ratio outcome than the prior full-year guidance range of 15.8%–16.3% suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A expense ratio hit a record-low 14.2% in Q2, a 450 basis point year-over-year improvement, reaching the company's long-term target roughly a year ahead of plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 SG&A ratio guidance of “15.8%–16.3%.”

surprises.description: Oscar raised full-year earnings-from-operations guidance by $250 million to $500 million–$700 million. The preview’s base case anticipated a raise to roughly $500 million–$650 million, so the new range broadly matched that expectation but extended $50 million above its upper end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year 2026 earnings from operations guidance was raised $250 million to a range of $500 million-$700 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario anticipated guidance “raised modestly to ~$500–650M EFO”; its bull case cited a raise to “$700M+ EFO.”

surprises.description: Oscar lowered its full-year MLR guidance by 90 basis points at the midpoint, to 81.5%–82.5%. This is an improvement from the previously guided 82.4%–83.4% range and is favorable beyond the preview’s central Q2 MLR expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year MLR guidance improved 90 basis points at the midpoint to 81.5%-82.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior full-year MLR guidance was “82.4%–83.4%.”

surprises.description: The first 2026 Wakely morbidity report was favorable to Oscar’s pricing, offering a potential upside tailwind that management had not fully included in guidance. The preview identified favorable morbidity as a possible bull-case catalyst, but it was not part of its base-case expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The first 2026 Wakely morbidity report (claims through April) came in favorable to pricing, representing a potential upside tailwind that management has not fully credited in guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case cited a “Wakely morbidity tailwind released into reserves”; its base case instead described results as “tracking to plan.”

surprises.description: Oscar’s full-year SG&A ratio outlook improved by 20 basis points, to 15.6%–16.1%. This is a modest additional cost-ratio improvement beyond the previously guided range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A ratio guidance improved 20 basis points to 15.6%-16.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior FY26 SG&A ratio guidance was “15.8%–16.3%.”

surprises.description: Management now expects back-half membership churn of roughly 2%–4% per month, double its prior expectations, because CMS eligibility disenrollments were delayed. Management said this is a timing issue with no revenue impact, but the higher churn rate was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now expects back-half membership churn of roughly 2%-4% per month (double prior expectations) due to delayed CMS eligibility disenrollments, but characterized it as timing with no revenue impact.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 opened at about 3.0 million paid members and called for confirming “~2.9–3.0M ending members with healthy morbidity”; it did not flag elevated back-half churn.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $4.9 billion was above the preview’s main $4.71 billion consensus and above its $4.65–$4.80 billion base scenario, although it was close to the $4.93 billion alternative estimate. This was a modest beat amid wide estimate dispersion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 70% year-over-year to $4.9 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed revenue consensus of “$4.71B” and a base scenario of “$4.65–4.80B,” while also noting an alternative estimate of “$4.93B.”

in_line: Q2 effectuated membership of 2.96 million was within the preview’s expected range of roughly 2.9–3.0 million.
Full-year revenue guidance was reaffirmed at $18.7 billion–$19.0 billion, the same range cited in the preview as the existing guidance.

surprises.description: The Catalent Indiana inspection classification was still pending, and management said it had drifted beyond the FDA’s typical 90-day guidance period after the April reinspection. The preview anticipated that classification could remain pending, but also expected an update on the call; the added delay leaves the main regulatory uncertainty unresolved for longer.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FDA inspection classification for the Catalent Indiana facility remains pending, drifting beyond the typical 90-day guidance period following the April 2026 reinspection.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said it would update on Catalent's status on this call.”

surprises.description: Scholar Rock raised $63 million net through its ATM before approval. The preview flagged a pre-approval equity raise as a negative signal, though it did not specify whether or how much ATM financing would be used in Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$492 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, including $63 million in net ATM proceeds during the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A pre-approval equity raise would be a negative signal. Watch ATM usage in Q2.”

surprises.description: The BLA included two independent fill/finish facilities, giving Scholar Rock a separate approval path if Catalent is delayed; the second site also had more commercially ready vials than Catalent. The preview expected confirmation of second-site supply, but did not anticipate that both facilities would already be in the BLA as independent paths.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company submitted its BLA with two independent fill/finish facilities (Catalent Indiana and a second site), providing two separate potential paths to approval to reduce launch risk”; it also had “more commercially-ready apitegromab vials from its second fill/finish facility than from Catalent Indiana.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Second fill-finish facility. Management guided to commercial drug product in hand in early Q3. Confirmation de-risks approval and launch.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash and marketable securities were $492 million, slightly above the preview’s estimated range of $420–480 million, even with the reported ATM proceeds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Scholar Rock ended Q2 2026 with $492 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash + marketable securities: $420–480M.”

surprises.description: The call reported that Scholar Rock had launched a randomized, placebo-controlled Phase II FSHD trial, a pipeline milestone not covered in the preview. Management also gave a later-this-year timing for SRK-439 Phase I top-line data and said it was pursuing post-approval regulatory engagement for subcutaneous apitegromab.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company launched a randomized, placebo-controlled Phase II FORGE trial in FSHD (60 patients) and expects top-line Phase I data for SRK-439 later this year, while pursuing subcutaneous apitegromab regulatory engagement post-approval.”

in_line: Q2 operating expenses were $108.9 million, within the preview’s $108–118 million estimate.
The September 30 PDUFA date remained in place, and management said the company was launch-ready ahead of it, consistent with the preview’s base case of an unchanged PDUFA date.
The second facility had commercial-ready product, consistent with the preview’s expectation for confirmation of commercial drug product in hand in early Q3.

The European path remained dependent on Catalent Indiana while the EMA awaited the FDA inspection classification; the preview had already flagged that the EU filing could require a facility change and that this could delay the European timeline.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $16.7 million, far above the preview’s $9.20 million consensus and its informal $10.5 million reference point. The reported result was also a much faster sequential ramp than the consensus-implied 13.6% increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $16.7 million,” up “107% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $9.20M” consensus; the preview also says “A good print is likely around $10.5M or higher,” identifying that as its inference rather than a sourced whisper number.

surprises.description: Management’s internal revenue targets imply $37–39 million in the second half, far above the roughly $18.3 million the preview said was implied by full-year consensus. These are described as internal targets, not formal guidance; the Q3 target also implies a sequential dip before the targeted Q4 ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management cited internal targets of “$12-14 million in Q3” and “$25 million in Q4,” with Q3 lower because of infrastructure buildout.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 plus Q2 consensus leaves about $18.3M for H2 against the $35.6M full-year consensus, a flat ~$9.1M per quarter.”

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate a demand wave of more than 60,000 drones under Phase 2 in the second half, mostly in Q4. That points to a much larger near-term order opportunity than the preview’s cited known orders, although the call also indicates capacity may constrain fulfillment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “More than 60,000 drones are expected to be ordered” in the second half of 2026, “mostly in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited known orders of “$12.8M” and “$2.1M” and noted that the company did not consistently report a formal backlog.

surprises.description: Management introduced an aspirational 2027 revenue target of $250 million, far above the preview’s $52.25 million FY2027 consensus. The ambition is qualified by current capacity that supports only about $20 million per quarter, so achieving the target depends on substantial expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management cited “$250 million as the aspirational 2027 revenue target”; current 70,000-square-foot capacity supports “only about $20 million per quarter.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed supply-chain disruption from outgrowing an electronics vendor, an execution problem not identified in the preview’s capacity discussion. This adds a concrete near-term production risk amid the anticipated demand ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 faced “outgrowing an electronics vendor causing supply chain disruptions.”

surprises.description: The company also reported an intermittent quality issue on a motor SKU requiring production-process remedies, a separate manufacturing problem not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 faced “an intermittent quality issue on a motor SKU requiring production process remedies.”

surprises.description: The company raised $60 million through ATM block transactions at $30 per share, a financing event the preview did not flag. It leaves the company with substantial cash and no debt, but also involved issuing shares.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised $60 million at $30 per share via ATM block transactions,” ending the quarter with “$229 million cash, no debt.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed substantially to $400,000 from $1.6 million in Q1, despite operating expenses of $13.6 million. The preview focused on the possibility of a sharply widening operating loss if expenses exceeded $12 million, so the EBITDA improvement was a better outcome than that concern implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA loss was “$400,000 in Q2,” down from “$1.6 million in Q1”; operating expenses were “$13.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If opex runs above $12M while gross profit is about $3.3M, the operating loss could widen toward -$9M even on a revenue beat.”

in_line: EPS was -$0.16, matching the preview’s -$0.16 consensus.
Gross margin was 34.7%, within the preview’s estimated 33–35% range and above the preview’s 33% checklist threshold.

surprises.description: Teleflex reported Q2 revenue of $570.3 million, about 1.9% above the $559.6 million consensus cited in the preview. The quarter’s pro forma constant-currency growth was 4.7%, even as reported GAAP revenue growth was amplified by the acquisition comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 pro forma adjusted constant currency revenue grew 4.7% to $570.3 million (up 28.9% GAAP)”; the call says results were “beating expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 Consensus” revenue: “$559.6M ($559.1M alt.).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $1.76, far above the preview’s $1.28 consensus. The beat was substantially larger than the revenue beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS of $1.76 (up 1.7% year-over-year)”; the call says results were “beating expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS (cont. ops)” consensus: “$1.28 ($1.27 alt.).”

surprises.description: Teleflex cut its full-year pro forma constant-currency revenue growth outlook by one percentage point at both ends, rather than maintaining the prior range. Management attributed the cut to the slower-than-expected BIOTRONIK integration, and cautioned that second-half growth would moderate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered its full-year 2026 pro forma constant currency revenue growth guidance to 3.5%-4.5% from 4.5%-5.5%, entirely due to a slower-than-expected Vascular Intervention (BIOTRONIK) integration”; management also said second-half growth “will moderate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY2026 guidance was “pro forma adj. constant-currency growth +4.5–5.5%”; the preview said a plain reaffirmation was expected as a bullish outcome.

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin was 61.7%, below the preview’s roughly 62% base expectation and its stated 62.5%+ sequential-recovery marker. Tariffs, VI mix, and increased R&D spending contributed to the pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin fell 280 bps to 61.7%” and was pressured by “tariffs, the lower-margin VI business, and increased R&D spending (7.9% of sales in H1 2026 versus historical ~6%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Sequential recovery toward 62.5%+” would support the H2 ramp and listed a base case of “Margin near 62%.”

surprises.description: Interventional revenue fell rather than growing around the 3% pace seen in Q1, with the BIOTRONIK integration taking longer than planned. The preview anticipated disruption would moderate in H2, but integration was extended through the second half instead of completing around mid-2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Interventional segment revenue fell 1% to $211.9 million” due to “integration disruptions primarily impacting the acquired BIOTRONIK VI business”; “full integration now extended through the second half of 2026 versus the originally planned mid-2026 completion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview watched for Interventional growth “vs. 3.0% in Q1” and said management expected integration disruption to “moderate in H2.”

surprises.description: Despite cutting revenue growth guidance, Teleflex raised its adjusted EPS range by $0.65 at both ends. The increase was attributed to repurchases, lower interest expense, and a lower tax rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $6.90-$7.20 from $6.25-$6.55, driven by share repurchases, lower interest expense, and a lower tax rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed adjusted EPS guidance of “$6.25–$6.55” and said a “plain reaffirmation” would be a bullish outcome.

surprises.description: Teleflex had already repurchased $250 million of shares in Q2 and announced another $250 million accelerated repurchase starting August 7, while paying off a $700 million term loan and reducing pro forma net leverage to about 1.9x. The preview anticipated the proceeds, buyback activity, and $800 million debt reduction, but did not specify this pace or the resulting leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased 1.9 million shares for $250 million” in Q2 and plans “an additional $250 million accelerated share repurchase starting August 7”; OEM proceeds paid off the “$700 million Term Loan A-2,” reducing pro forma net leverage “to about 1.9x from 2.8x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “About $1.25B of net OEM proceeds landed August 3” and to “Watch buyback pace and progress on the $800M debt paydown.”

surprises.description: Management described a meaningful step-up in 2027 performance and put a steady-state operating-margin target near 23% on the table. It also did not dispute analyst EPS estimates of roughly $11.25–$11.50, figures the preview did not address.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects a meaningful step-up in financial performance in 2027, targeting a steady-state operating margin of approximately 23%, and did not dispute analyst EPS estimates of roughly $11.25-$11.50 for 2027.”

surprises.description: The call reported FDA approval of EZPLAZ freeze-dried plasma and positioned it as a potential 2027 contributor, though 2026 revenue is expected to be immaterial. The preview did not identify the approval or this prospective growth driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New products EZPLAZ freeze-dried plasma (FDA BLA approved late July, targeting military/government market with immaterial 2026 revenue but a 2027 contributor).”

surprises.description: Teleflex highlighted a late-2027 randomized data readout for the Freesolve resorbable scaffold as a future growth driver, a catalyst not mentioned in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Freesolve resorbable scaffold (BIOMAG-II randomized data readout expected late 2027) represent[s] key future growth drivers.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $235.5 million, about $2.4 million below the $237.9 million consensus and at the bottom of the company’s guidance range. Management attributed the low-end result to unexpected softness in the final two weeks of June.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $235.5 million” and landed “at the low end after unexpected softness in the final two weeks of June.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue: $237.9M” consensus; company guidance was “$235–238M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA of $32.9 million substantially exceeded the preview’s implied $28–29 million expectation, but the reported figure included an unexpected $11.8 million tariff refund. The refund offset about $6 million of incremental pre-launch investment, so the headline beat does not reflect the underlying investment burden alone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $32.9 million (14% margin), but this included an $11.8 million tariff refund benefit that offset roughly $6 million of incremental pre-launch investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: ~$28–29M (implied, not a published aggregate).”

surprises.description: Active customer growth was 4.1%, below the preview’s 4.5% watch threshold and below its expected 2.72–2.76 million active-customer range. Average revenue per customer rose 6.6%, while management cited soft traffic and pointed to a Q4 rebound in active customer growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing-12-month active customer growth was only 4.1% while average revenue per customer rose 6.6%,” with management “flagging soft traffic and pointing to a Q4 rebound in active customer growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for 2.72–2.76M. Growth below 4.5% would support the bear case.”

surprises.description: Warby Parker disclosed a $14.4 million tariff refund for the year and said it would reinvest all of the proceeds in the business rather than allow them to flow through to the bottom line. The preview did not flag this refund or this use of the proceeds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is recognizing a total $14.4 million tariff refund this year and plans to reinvest all proceeds back into the business rather than let it flow to the bottom line.”

surprises.description: The company gave a more concrete Intelligent Eyewear rollout than the preview’s general expectation of a launch later in 2026: launch and preorders are planned for the fall, demos will be available in more than 350 stores, and holiday deliveries remain on track. This reduces the risk of a launch slipping past the holiday season, though no exact launch date was provided.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Intelligent (AI) Eyewear launches this fall,” with “demos across all 350+ stores, preorders in the fall, and deliveries on track for the holiday season.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the launch was “later in 2026” and flagged “a slip past the holiday season” as a risk; it called for a firm launch date and distribution details.

surprises.description: The AI glasses are expected to have a lower product-margin percentage because of consumer-electronics costs, a margin trade-off the preview did not specify. Management said the higher price point should still produce equal or higher absolute dollar margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI glasses will carry a slightly lower product margin percentage due to higher consumer electronics costs but will deliver equal or higher absolute dollar margin at a higher price point.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked for “ASP/margin framing” but stated no expectation about the percentage or dollar margin.

surprises.description: Management said out-of-network insurance claim submission penetration has surpassed in-network penetration, and that both are helping drive higher average order values. The preview focused on in-network insurance growth and did not anticipate this out-of-network milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Out-of-network claim submission penetration has now surpassed in-network, both driving higher average order values.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Insurance and eyecare attach” and described in-network insurance as the metric to watch, but did not mention out-of-network claims surpassing it.

surprises.description: The company said roughly half of existing customers still do not know it offers eye exams, while exams currently account for about 7% of revenue and could reach 15–20% over the long term. That points to an awareness and attach opportunity not quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Eye exams were “~7% of revenue,” with “long-term potential of 15-20%,” while “roughly 50% of existing customers are still unaware Warby Parker offers exams.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged eye exams as a key attach metric and expected growth of “+30% Y/Y,” but did not discuss customer awareness or a longer-term revenue contribution.

in_line: FY2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed at $959–976 million and $117–119 million, respectively, as the preview identified reaffirmation as the base case.
Eye exams grew more than 30% year over year, matching the preview’s expectation of about 30% growth.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $181 million, well above the preview’s $161.85 million consensus and the company’s steer of slightly above Q1’s $160.8 million. The preview’s bull case began above $165 million, so the reported result cleared even that threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $181 million,” with “core organic growth of nearly 8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (Q2) ... Consensus $161.85M”; company steer: “Slightly above Q1 levels” (Q1 was $160.8M). The bull scenario was “Above $165M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin fell to 20.3%, below the preview’s 21.5%–22.0% company range and its key watch level of at least 21.5%. This was a meaningful shortfall despite the much stronger revenue result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross profit margin declined 277 basis points year-over-year to 20.3%,” pressured by currency-driven material costs, MirrorEye inventory-related costs, and lower Smart2 tachograph sales.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q1 guidance reaffirmed “Adj. gross margin 21.5–22.0%”; preview issue: “Gross margin durability (≥21.5%).”

surprises.description: MirrorEye sales reached a new quarterly record of $37 million, exceeding the preview’s $35 million watch threshold. The result extended the strong Q1 trend, when sales were $33 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “MirrorEye set a quarterly sales record of $37 million, up 39% year-over-year and 10% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether revenue exceeds $35M in Q2.”

surprises.description: SG&A fell substantially as a share of sales even as revenue increased, providing a favorable cost offset to the gross-margin decline. The preview did not identify this degree of expense leverage as an expected outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A expense fell 182 basis points to 14.3% of sales,” rising less than $400,000 despite a $24 million year-over-year revenue increase.

surprises.description: Stoneridge announced a $42 million estimated-lifetime-revenue bus and coach OEM program, its largest award in that segment, which was not anticipated in the preview. Commercialization is not expected until 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company announced a new bus and coach OEM award representing $42 million in estimated lifetime revenue, its largest program to date in that segment,” with full commercialization expected in 2027.

surprises.description: Stone Ridge Brazil reported record sales and a strong operating margin, a segment result not specifically anticipated in the preview. The call also attributed part of the performance to a temporary competitive supply dislocation, making the strength less clearly repeatable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Stone Ridge Brazil delivered record sales of $20.5 million (up 38%, or nearly 26% excluding currency) and adjusted operating margin of 11.2%,” aided partly by “a temporary competitive supply dislocation.”

surprises.description: The industry outlook cited on the call shifted toward stronger 2026 OEM growth but weaker 2027 growth, with orders pulled forward between years. The preview noted favorable industry data but did not flag this specific timing shift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “IHS raised its 2026 weighted-average OEM end-market growth forecast to 5.5% (up from 1.8% in May) while trimming 2027 growth to 5.4% (from 10%), primarily reflecting a timing shift of orders into 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said recent industry data “points toward strength,” citing June North American Class 8 orders and EU H1 heavy-truck registrations.

in_line: Adjusted consolidated EBITDA was $5.5 million, broadly in line with the preview’s base case of “Around $5M.”
Full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed at $645–$670 million and $20–$25 million, as the preview’s base case anticipated.

surprises.description: ACI reported adjusted diluted EPS of $0.54, above both preview estimates, including the higher and more recent $0.48 mark. The gap was more modest against $0.48 than against the conflicting $0.29 estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS grew 54% to $0.54, boosted by strong operating performance and share repurchases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | ~$0.29 (Aug 5) or $0.48 (Jun 23)”; the preview says the two EPS marks “conflict” and should be treated as “unreliable.”

surprises.description: Payment Software grew 7% in constant currency, below the preview's stated expectation of double-digit Q2 growth. Issuing and acquiring grew strongly, but the segment's overall growth still fell short of that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Payment Software segment grew 9% (7% constant currency) to $196 million,” with issuing and acquiring revenue growth of “33-37%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “management guided to double-digit growth for Q2.”

surprises.description: Net new ARR bookings and new license/services bookings were both down from a strong prior-year period, with more signings pushed to the second half. The preview highlighted bookings mix as a key issue but did not anticipate these declines or the second-half weighting.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net new ARR bookings were $18 million and new license/services bookings were $59 million in Q2, both down against a strong prior-year period, with more signings weighted to the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net new ARR bookings mix. Q1 bookings of $12.4M were driven primarily by Biller, so segment mix matters for the RemainCo growth story.”

surprises.description: The Biller segment grew revenue only 5% and had lower EBITDA year over year, including a one-time charge from a terminated partnership. The preview focused on a possible Biller sale, not on this operating weakness or charge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Biller segment revenue grew only 5% to $234 million with EBITDA declining year-over-year,” pressured partly by “a one-time charge from a terminated partnership representing about one-third of the EBITDA contraction.”

surprises.description: ACI disclosed a back-loaded second-half revenue profile: Q3 is expected to be weaker than Q4 because high-margin Payment Software license renewals are timed later. The preview identified renewal timing as a variable for Q2 growth but did not lay out this Q3/Q4 split or Q3 outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Second-half revenue is expected to skew 40%/60% between Q3 and Q4 due to timing of high-margin payment software license renewals,” implying Q3 revenue of “$417-427 million” and EBITDA of “$90-95 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Renewal timing is the key variable” for Payment Software growth; the preview gives no Q3 or Q4 revenue outlook.

in_line: Q2 revenue was $430 million, essentially matching the preview's approximately $430 million consensus and within the company's $420–440 million guide.
Adjusted EBITDA was $91 million, within the company's $85–95 million guide and the preview's $88–94 million base scenario.
ACI raised FY2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance, as the preview expected; the new ranges are $1.895–1.925 billion and $545–560 million, respectively.

Management did not confirm the reported Biller sale process or provide sale details, consistent with the preview's base scenario of no specifics. The preview had identified a sale-status update as a key issue.

The company reported $41 million of Q2 repurchases and reiterated a 50–60% of operating cash flow buyback target, addressing the preview's capital-allocation question without announcing a commitment of potential Biller proceeds.

surprises.description: Revenue was $435 million versus the preview’s $386.0–386.1 million consensus, and adjusted EPS was $2.21 versus $1.79–$1.81. Both results materially exceeded the preview’s estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue reached a record $435 million” and “Adjusted EPS hit a record $2.21.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $386.0–386.1M” and “Adj. EPS (diluted) | $1.79–$1.81.”

surprises.description: The preview expected long-term flows to narrow toward breakeven from Q1’s $457 million outflow, while Victory reported $4.2 billion of inflows. Management also said flows accelerated further into Q3, a stronger continuation than the preview described.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record net long-term inflows of $4.2 billion represented a nearly $5 billion positive swing from the same quarter last year,” and “flows accelerated further into Q3.”
