surprises.expectation_evidence: “LT outflows narrow to about breakeven”; the preview also said “The first positive net-flow quarter would be the clearest narrative change.”

surprises.description: The adjusted EBITDA margin reached 55.8%, well above Q1’s 52.6% record despite the preview’s expectation of seasonal payroll relief. The preview did not give a Q2 margin forecast, but framed the result as a comparison against 52.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 55.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin vs. 52.6%. Q2 should get seasonal payroll relief.”

surprises.description: The realized fee rate was 47.9 bps, above the roughly 46.6 bps implied by consensus revenue and above the preview’s 46–47 bps long-term range. Management nevertheless said to expect a normalized 46–47 bps going forward, which is consistent with that longer-term range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue reached a record $435 million … at an average fee rate of 47.9 basis points,” and management “guided to a normalized 46-47 bps range going forward.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus revenue of $386M implies roughly 46.6 bps”; “A rate at or above 47 bps would support a revenue beat”; and “Management guides the investment management realized fee rate to 46–47 bps long-term.”

surprises.description: Victory raised its long-term adjusted EBITDA margin guidance by one percentage point, from 49% to 50%, citing structural efficiency gains after Pioneer. The preview did not flag this guidance increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised long-term adjusted EBITDA margin guidance from 49% to 50%, reflecting structural efficiency gains post-Pioneer.”

surprises.description: The preview said integration was substantially complete and $104 million of the $110 million synergy target had been realized. Victory reported completing the integration in five quarters and realizing the full $110 million target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Pioneer integration was completed in five quarters, with the full $110 million in net run rate expense synergies fully realized.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pioneer/Amundi synergies: $104M of the $110M target realized. Integration described as ‘substantially complete.’”

surprises.description: International AUM was $62.6 billion across 61 countries, above the preview’s cited Amundi-channel figure of $55 billion across 60 countries. Management also said the partnership was trending above initial financial expectations and had been cumulatively net-flow positive since the Pioneer close.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International AUM reached $62.6 billion across 61 countries via the Amundi partnership,” which is “trending above initial financial expectations” and “has been cumulatively net flow positive since the Pioneer close.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for … hard figures on the Amundi channel ($55B AUM across 60 countries).”

surprises.description: The ETF platform’s AUM reached $23.2 billion, up 54% year over year, and flagship VFLO reached $7.8 billion with a 5-star Morningstar rating. The preview gave no ETF-specific forecast or benchmark, so this was an unanticipated product update rather than a measurable beat against an estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ETF platform grew AUM to $23.2 billion (up 54% year-over-year) … with flagship VFLO reaching $7.8 billion and earning a 5-star Morningstar rating.”

surprises.description: The Term Loan B repricing was an unanticipated cost-saving update, cutting annual interest expense by about $2.5 million; the preview did not mention a loan repricing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A Term Loan B repricing that cut annual interest expense by ~$2.5 million.”

in_line: Management’s normalized 46–47 bps fee-rate range going forward matched the preview’s stated long-term fee-rate guidance of 46–47 bps.
The $110 million Pioneer synergy target was already disclosed in the preview; the reported result completed that target rather than raising it.

surprises.description: The preview focused on adjusted EPS and did not flag a large license impairment; Townsquare recorded $26.6 million of non-cash FCC license impairments in Q2, contributing to a $41.8 million GAAP net loss, even as adjusted EPS was positive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-cash FCC license impairment charges of $26.6 million in Q2 ($35.2 million year-to-date), driving a Q2 net loss of $41.8 million ($2.36 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview provided an adjusted EPS consensus of “$0.19” and noted that adjusted EPS was not guided; it gave no expectation for an impairment charge or GAAP loss.

surprises.description: Digital advertising grew 11%, ahead of the preview’s 7–8% base case and above its 8% bullish-case threshold; programmatic growth was also stronger than the preview’s expectation of above 20%. Management added that Q3 digital advertising growth should be stronger still.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Digital Advertising revenue grew 11% year-over-year in Q2, accelerating from 6.8% in Q1, with programmatic … up 27%; management expects Q3 digital advertising growth to be even stronger than 11%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “Ignite +7–8%”; its catalyst checklist called for “Ignite growth of 8% or more,” and it expected programmatic to be “above 20%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.21 modestly exceeded the preview’s $0.19 consensus, although it was below the $0.22 reported a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $0.21 versus $0.22 a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 adjusted EPS consensus of “$0.19.”

surprises.description: The media partnership business reported a much larger growth path than the preview discussed: revenue is expected to more than double in 2026, with a $50 million revenue target within four years.
surprises.fact_evidence: Revenue is expected to rise “from ~$6 million in 2025 to over $12 million in 2026,” with a target of “$50 million in revenue at a 20% profit margin … within four years.”

surprises.description: The Interactive recovery outlook was less firm on timing than an early-Q3 inflection might suggest: management now described growth by year-end, potentially as early as Q3, and said the sales force is still 40% below peak and will not be rebuilt to target levels until 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects Interactive to return to month-over-month revenue growth “by year-end (potentially as early as Q3),” while the sales force “remains 40% below peak and won't be rebuilt to target levels until 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “pointed to month-over-month growth as early as Q3'26” and called for a Q3 inflection to be reiterated.

surprises.description: Interactive’s segment profit margin reached a record 37.6%, a substantial step up from the roughly 33% level highlighted in the preview, despite the segment’s revenue decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Townsquare Interactive segment profit margin rose to a record 37.6% (up from ~33% in Q2 2025).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that Interactive’s margin had expanded to “33.7% from 32.5%” in Q1 but gave no expectation for a further increase to a record.

surprises.description: Townsquare completed its first technology licensing deal, adding a recurring-revenue opportunity that the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Townsquare completed its first technology licensing deal, with SummitMedia adopting its in-house 'Blueprint' CRM, creating a new recurring revenue stream and deeper partner integration.”

surprises.description: Management said the company does not expect to become a material cash taxpayer until roughly the end of 2028, a favorable cash-flow outlook not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company does not expect to be a material cash taxpayer until roughly end of 2028 given ~$121 million of federal NOLs.”

in_line: Q2 net revenue of $115.4 million was within the $114–116 million guidance range and close to the preview’s $114.74 million consensus and $114.5–115.5 million base case.
Adjusted EBITDA of $24.8 million was within the $24–25 million guidance range and the preview’s $24.3–25.0 million base case.
Interactive revenue declined about 1.7% sequentially, from $17.5 million in Q1 to $17.2 million in Q2, within the preview’s expected sequential decline of about 2% or less.
Quarter-end net leverage of 5.44x was close to the preview’s expectation of roughly 5.4x.

surprises.description: The preview put Q2 revenue at $203.4–$205.0 million and non-GAAP EPS at $0.89–$0.894; ACLS reported $215 million and $1.06, respectively, exceeding both estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $215 million with EPS of $1.06, both exceeding company expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus | $203.4M – $205.0M”; “Non-GAAP EPS | Consensus | $0.89 – $0.894.”

surprises.description: Instead of holding to the prior expectation of roughly flat full-year revenue, management raised its 2026 outlook to approximately mid-single-digit year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to approximately mid-single-digit year-over-year revenue growth, up from the prior expectation of flat revenue versus 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has guided FY26 to ‘approximately flat vs. 2025, second-half weighted.’”

surprises.description: The preview set a roughly $215 million bar for Q3 revenue and described about $220 million per quarter as the H2 run rate; ACLS guided to approximately $230 million, above those expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of approximately $230 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 revenue guidance … needs to be at least ~$215M”; H2 implied “roughly $220M per quarter.”

surprises.description: Q2 bookings came in well below the preview’s approximately $180 million support level, although the reported book-to-bill ratio of about 1x was better than the preview’s feared sub-0.7 outcome. Backlog was essentially unchanged from the preview’s cited $453 million Q1 level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bookings were $131 million with a book-to-bill ratio of approximately 1x, and total backlog exited the quarter at $452 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “To support H2, Q2 bookings need to be about $180M or more”; a “second straight sub-0.7 quarter” would be concerning. Q1 backlog was cited as “$453M.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin was slightly below the preview’s approximately 43% expectation, with management attributing the shortfall to unfavorable CS&I mix and higher-than-anticipated services costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin was 42.7%, slightly below the 43% outlook, due to unfavorable CS&I mix and higher-than-anticipated services costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 is guided to ~43%.”

surprises.description: The preview portrayed memory as carrying the growth story, but management said memory revenue would remain lumpy in 2026 and second-half revenue would be similar to the first half, with further growth anticipated in 2027 rather than a clear acceleration this year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Memory revenue is expected to remain lumpy in 2026 with second-half memory similar to the first half, but management anticipates continued growth into 2027 driven by DRAM and high-bandwidth memory for AI, with NAND not yet showing a clear trend.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Memory is carrying the growth story”; Q1 memory shipments were “the highest since 2023 on DRAM/HBM AI demand.”

surprises.description: The preview called for concrete SiC conversion in H2; ACLS reported stronger-than-usual first-half SiC bookings, two new China customers, and orders for high-energy channeling superjunction applications, providing more evidence of demand than the preview had specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Silicon carbide bookings in the first half exceeded the average levels of the past two years, with two new China customers added and orders secured for high-energy channeling superjunction applications.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for concrete conversion in H2”; Q1 bookings were described as “encouraging.”

surprises.description: China’s share of revenue was 46%, up from the 40% Q1 figure highlighted in the preview, indicating a higher Q2 geographic concentration than that reference point.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China revenue rose to 46% of total (up from 40% prior quarter).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist cited “China at 40% of Q1 revenue.”

in_line: Q3 gross-margin guidance of approximately 43% was in line with the preview’s roughly 43% base-case margin expectation.
Q3 EPS guidance of approximately $1.11 was close to the preview’s implied H2 run rate of about $1.10 per quarter.

surprises.description: WBD reported streaming revenue above $3 billion for the first time, with subscriber-related revenue growth accelerating to 10% ex-FX. The preview focused on subscriber counts and gave no streaming revenue-growth forecast, so this was a positive operating result it did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Streaming segment revenue exceeded $3 billion for the first time ever in Q2 2026,” and “subscriber-related revenue growth accelerat[ed] 200 basis points sequentially to 10% ex-FX.”

surprises.description: Streaming generated $512 million of adjusted EBITDA at nearly a 17% margin, a more than 60% year-over-year improvement. The preview did not forecast streaming EBITDA or margin, leaving this as a substantial positive result not anticipated there.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Streaming generated $512 million in adjusted EBITDA, a more than 60% improvement over Q2 2025, reaching a nearly 17% adjusted EBITDA margin.”

surprises.description: Linear advertising fell nearly 30%, worse than the preview's forecast of about a 21% decline for Global Linear Networks advertising. The call attributed the decline largely to the NBA rights loss and said international ad markets weakened further.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Linear advertising revenue declined nearly 30%, driven largely by the loss of the NBA,” and “international ad markets weaken[ed] further in Q2 versus Q1 amid consumer caution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total ad revenue is forecast down about 21%.”

surprises.description: The studio film business underperformed expectations, and management acknowledged the studio segment had fallen short of its over-$3 billion adjusted EBITDA goal even in a strong 2025. The preview used about $350 million as its Q2 studio EBITDA base case and identified a target walkback as a bear-case risk; management did not walk back the target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The studio segment underperformed expectations in the film business this year”; management “acknowledg[ed] it fell short of [the over $3 billion adjusted EBITDA] target even in a strong 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Studios adjusted EBITDA about $350M in the base case”; the bear scenario included “$3B Studios target walked back.”

surprises.description: Management gave a positive streaming distribution growth outlook: excluding a previously disclosed related-party deal, growth would have been in the low teens, and it expects teens-level growth for the rest of the year. The preview did not provide a distribution-revenue growth expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding a previously disclosed related-party deal, streaming distribution revenue growth would have been in the low teens,” with “teens-level growth for the remainder of the year.”

surprises.description: Management said 2026 is expected to be WBD's best year ever for streaming retention and its lowest-churn year, supported by expanded distributor and programmer bundles including Disney in the U.S. The preview discussed subscriber counts and the year-end target, but did not anticipate this retention outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects 2026 to be its best year ever for streaming retention and lowest churn,” driven by “expanding distributor and programmer bundles such as the Disney partnership in the U.S.”

surprises.description: Management outlined a larger film-production slate, increasing from 14 films this year to 19 in 2027, with several tentpole franchises. The preview discussed the film-business risk but did not flag this production ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Film production is ramping from 14 films this year to 19 films in 2027,” with a “richer slate of tentpole IP including Lord of the Rings, Batman, Superman, and Minecraft II.”

in_line: Management maintained the long-term goal of over $3 billion in studio adjusted EBITDA, as the preview said the target had been reaffirmed and modeled it as remaining in place.

surprises.description: Appian reported $203.3 million of Q2 revenue, above both the $191.0–195.0 million company guide and the preview’s $191.38–193.4 million consensus estimates. That also cleared the preview’s $200 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose 19% to $203.3 million.”

surprises.description: Cloud subscription revenue reached $131.7 million, above the $126.0–128.0 million guide and roughly $127 million consensus. Growth of 23% (22% constant currency) also exceeded the preview’s 18–20% guided growth range and accelerated for a second straight quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 cloud subscription revenue grew 23% year-over-year to $131.7 million,” with “strongest constant-currency cloud performance (22%) in over two years” and “a second consecutive quarter of cloud acceleration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cloud subscriptions | $126.0–128.0M (+18–20%) | ~$127M”; the preview’s bull trigger was “≥$131M.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $16.2 million, far above the $5–8 million guide and the preview’s roughly $7 million consensus. It also cleared the preview’s $12 million threshold for a strong profitability result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $16.2 million ... well above the guided range of $5 million to $8 million, driven by higher revenue and expense timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | $5.0–8.0M | ~$7M”; the preview said “a print of $12M+ would support the profitability story.”

surprises.description: Appian raised its full-year cloud subscription outlook to $525–529 million, above the prior $515–521 million range and above the preview’s stated $524 million-plus bull trigger. The size of the raise exceeded the preview’s expectation that a raise was needed after Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Appian raised full-year guidance, now expecting cloud subscription revenue of $525–529 million (20% growth at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior FY cloud subscription guidance was “$515–521M”; the preview said “a raise to $524M+ is the bull trigger” and “a raise is needed after the Q1 increase.”

surprises.description: The new full-year adjusted EBITDA range of $104–110 million is above the prior $97–105 million range. The guidance also implies about 13% margin and two additional points of margin expansion, a stronger profitability outlook than the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Appian raised full-year guidance” to adjusted EBITDA of “$104–110 million (~13% margin, 39% growth), up 2 points of margin expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was “$97–105M”; the preview listed a full-year adjusted EBITDA raise as a key catalyst.

surprises.description: Full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance of $1.04–1.12 is higher than the prior $0.94–1.05 range, lifting both ends of the outlook rather than merely reiterating the prior view.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year non-GAAP EPS of $1.04–1.12 (~77% growth at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior FY non-GAAP EPS guidance was “$0.94–1.05”; the preview listed an EPS raise among the key catalysts.

surprises.description: Management disclosed unusually strong AI adoption: customer AI usage was 20 times the prior-year level, and 85% of Q2 new logos purchased AI offerings. The preview sought quantified AI evidence, but the reported metrics measure usage and attach rather than AI revenue or ARR, which the preview specifically said investors wanted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customer AI usage was 20x greater than the prior-year Q2, and 85% of Q2 new logos purchased Appian's AI offerings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for a quantified metric (AI ARR, attach rate, or agent consumption) rather than anecdotes”; “The buy-side wants dollars.”

surprises.description: FX has changed from a tailwind to a modest headwind in the second half, potentially weighing on reported growth; management said constant-currency trends would be a more stable indicator. The preview did not flag this change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FX has flipped from a tailwind to a modest headwind in the second half, making constant-currency trends a more stable indicator than reported growth.”

surprises.description: Appian had already used $65.7 million of its $100 million buyback authorization, including $43.9 million in Q2, indicating a substantial pace of repurchases by midyear. Cash and investments also fell to $167.9 million from $187.2 million at year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased ~1.8 million shares for $43.9 million in Q2, bringing cumulative buybacks to $65.7 million of its $100 million authorization, while cash and investments fell to $167.9 million from $187.2 million at year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the authorization was “intended for completion in-year” and flagged “Buyback pace and diluted share count” as items to watch.

surprises.description: Refinancing the credit facility is expected to cut annual interest expense by about $4 million, a favorable financing benefit not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Appian refinanced its credit facility, cutting annual interest expense by approximately $4 million.”

surprises.description: Management said it is pulling some 2027 sales hiring forward into 2026 because of an unusually strong pipeline. That points to confidence in demand and earlier investment than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[Appian] is pulling forward some 2027 sales hiring into 2026 on the strength of an unusually strong pipeline.”

in_line: Cloud net ARR expansion was 115%, in line with the preview’s roughly 114–115% expectation; it did not reach the preview’s 116% threshold for a new positive story.
Q3 revenue guidance of $214–218 million was within the preview’s implied $212–218 million range.

surprises.description: The preview put spot ARR at about $1.55 billion, while BSY reported $1.536 billion, a modest shortfall. But constant-currency ARR growth accelerated to 12% from the 11.5% streak, reaching the preview’s threshold for improving the growth narrative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 ARR growth accelerated to 12% year-over-year on a constant currency basis, reaching $1.536 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ARR (spot) ~$1,550M”; “At 12.0% cc or above, the narrative improves.”

surprises.description: The preview’s full-year outlook called for about 100 basis points of AOI-less-operating-SBC margin improvement, with improvement expected to come in the back half after Q1 compression. Instead, first-half margins still trailed the prior year, with management citing front-loaded investments and finance/Quote-to-Cash platform go-live costs absorbed within margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AOI less operating SBC was $116 million (28.3% margin) in Q2 and $257 million (30.8% margin) in the first half, with first-half margins trailing prior year due to front-loaded investments and new finance/Quote-to-Cash platform go-live costs absorbed within margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AOI less operating SBC margin | ~+100bp y/y improvement”; “the full-year improvement must come in the back half.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue came in slightly below both preview consensus figures, rather than within the preview’s base-case range: $411 million versus $412.8 million consensus and the $413–418 million base scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 revenues were $411 million, up 12.8% year-over-year (12.2% constant currency).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $412.8M (alt. survey: $416.3M)”; base scenario “$413–418M.”

surprises.description: Management said reaching the high end of the ARR range depends not only on sustained momentum but also on completing an acquisition and closing lumpy Asset Analytics deals, making that outcome more contingent than the preview’s growth-threshold framing suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reaching the high end of the ARR range would require sustained momentum plus completing an acquisition and closing lumpy Asset Analytics big deals.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave an “ARR growth” guide of “10.5% – 12.5% cc” and highlighted “cc ARR growth vs. the 11.5% streak,” without flagging acquisition completion or lumpy Asset Analytics deals as conditions for reaching the high end.

surprises.description: Management identified an incremental second-half FX headwind to revenue of $8–10 million versus outlook assumptions. The preview discussed currency effects on reported growth and the quality of a possible revenue raise, but did not anticipate this specific additional downside to the outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Unfavorable FX could reduce second-half revenue by an incremental $8-10 million versus outlook assumptions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise driven only by FX, with the cc ARR range unchanged, would be a low-quality raise.”

surprises.description: Instead of indicating near-term AI/MCP-server monetization, management said it does not plan to monetize agentic consumption until 2027, prioritizing adoption, exploration, and validation first. That puts monetization later than investors watching for AI or API-consumption developments might have expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management does not plan to monetize AI/MCP-server agentic consumption until 2027, prioritizing adoption, exploration, and validation first.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “quantified AI or API-consumption adoption” and “any quantification of AI or API-consumption adoption.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that Resources was the company’s fastest-growing sector, driven mainly by brownfield mining investment; the preview did not identify this specific sector demand driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Resources was the fastest-growing sector driven primarily by brownfield mining investment.”

surprises.description: Management highlighted substantial international expansion at Power Line Systems: revenue outside the U.S. is now as large as the entire PLS business was at its 2022 acquisition. The preview did not flag this growth or the cited U.S. capacity-gap demand driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Power Line Systems' revenue outside the U.S. is now as large as the entire PLS business was at its 2022 acquisition, benefiting from an estimated 35 GW U.S. capacity gap by 2030.”

in_line: Net revenue retention remained at 109%, in line with the preview’s expectation that it would hold near 109%; account retention was 99%.
The company reaffirmed its $500–570 million full-year free-cash-flow outlook, within the preview’s stated range.

surprises.description: Enovis reported adjusted EPS of $0.90, above the preview’s $0.84 working consensus and $0.88 base case, though within the preview’s wider $0.82–$0.92 estimate range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS reached $0.90,” with “14% underlying growth in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $0.84 (Public.com); $0.82 (Zacks); $0.92 (TradingKey)” and the base scenario forecast “$0.88.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 17.9%, below the preview’s 18.0–18.3% level needed to keep the H2 margin ramp credible. Management also said high-teens margins remain insufficient for its ambitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin was 17.9%, up 70 basis points on an underlying basis,” while management reiterated dissatisfaction with high-teens margins as insufficient for its ambitions.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs roughly 18.0–18.3% to keep [the H2 ramp] credible.”

surprises.description: The 62% adjusted gross margin landed in the preview’s expected range, but it included an unanticipated $8 million benefit from 2025 tariff refunds, alongside ongoing tariff costs and unplanned inflation. That makes the reported improvement partly dependent on a refund rather than solely on recurring operating progress.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margins hit 62%, an underlying improvement of 120 basis points, aided by an $8 million benefit from 2025 tariff refunds but partially offset by $4 million of ongoing tariff impact and $2 million of unplanned inflation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin (est.) | ~61.5–62.0%.”

surprises.description: The quarter faced a previously unflagged Middle East disruption, and management warned that Q3 would be seasonally softer because of Western Europe weakness and continued Middle East disruption, with acceleration expected only in Q4. Full-year guidance was nevertheless reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Middle East conflict created a 100 basis point headwind to international growth and about a 40 basis point headwind to total Enovis growth in the quarter”; management “expects a seasonally softer Q3 due to Western Europe softness and Middle East disruption, with sales acceleration anticipated in Q4.”

surprises.description: Management reported strong competitive adoption of Nebula instrumentation and the start of ARVIS’s full U.S. commercial launch, developments the preview did not identify as expectations or key debates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nebula continued driving growth with over 80% of new instrumentation sets going to competitive users in Q2, while ARVIS moved into full US commercial launch.”

in_line: Reported Q2 sales of $583 million were essentially in line with the preview’s ~$582 million working figure and ~$583 million base case.
Recon organic growth of 6% met the preview’s approximately 6–7% bar, and P&R organic growth of 3% met its stated ≥3% target.
Adjusted gross margin of 62% was within the preview’s 61.5–62.0% estimate, notwithstanding the unexpected refund and cost mix noted above.
Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed, consistent with the preview’s base case, which anticipated reaffirmation.

surprises.description: Cogent was expected to report about $239.7 million of revenue and for consolidated revenue to stop declining sequentially. Instead, revenue was $235.6 million, down 1.5% sequentially—a shortfall of about $4.1 million, or 1.7%, against consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue declined 1.5% ($3.6 million) sequentially to $235.6 million,” marking its 12th consecutive quarter of decline.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Service revenue” consensus was “$239.7M”; the preview says this “Implies +0.2% QoQ.”

surprises.description: Wavelength revenue fell short of the preview’s $15.0–15.5 million base case, coming in at $14.8 million; connection adds were also below the roughly 200 anticipated. The result was at, but not below, the preview’s $14.8 million bear-case threshold, and adds remained above its roughly 150 bear-case level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wavelength revenue grew 63.8% year-over-year and 9.2% sequentially to $14.8 million,” with connections rising from 2,263 to 2,445 (182 net adds).
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “about $15.0–15.5M”; it also watched for “about 200” connection adds and said “Below $14.8M, or fewer than about 150 connection adds” would support the bear thesis.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA came in below the preview’s $72–74 million base case and below the roughly $73 million implied by the guide path. Its 30.2% margin was within the base-case range but well short of the roughly 32% needed to keep the stated annual margin-improvement pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EBITDA as adjusted rose only $0.9 million sequentially to $71.1 million, with margin up 90 basis points to 30.2%,” dampened by severance and integration wind-down costs, including a 6% workforce reduction.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave a base case of “$72–74M / 30.0–30.9%,” said Q2 needed “roughly 32% (about $76–77M) to keep the annual pace,” and noted that “Anything at 30% or below puts the guide at risk.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that the business is not generating positive free cash flow without T-Mobile subsidy payments, which are due to end in under two years. The preview flagged liquidity and the limited operating-cash-flow cushion but did not state this underlying cash-flow dependence.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management acknowledged the business “is not generating positive free cash flow excluding T-Mobile subsidy payments,” which “end in under two years,” and said sustained EBITDA growth is critical to the credit story.

surprises.description: Cogent reported a $130.7 million GAAP gain on the data-center sale, an earnings-related one-off not identified in the preview. The sale itself was expected, so the surprise is the reported gain rather than the transaction.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company sold 10 former Sprint data centers for $225 million cash, “generating a GAAP gain of $130.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “10-facility data center sale” had “closed June 29, 2026, inside Q2,” and cited the $225 million proceeds.

surprises.description: The call disclosed a debt repurchase not anticipated in the preview: Cogent bought back $138.8 million par value of its 2032 secured notes below par, realizing a gain and reducing the outstanding principal. This is favorable for debt reduction, though the call also described a higher-cost refinancing for the 2027 notes.
surprises.fact_evidence: Cogent repurchased “$138.8 million par value” of its 2032 secured notes “at an average price of $90.348,” realizing a cumulative $13.4 million gain and reducing principal to $461.2 million.

surprises.description: The 2027-note refinancing remained planned for Q3 rather than being reported as completed, and management indicated the secured refinancing would carry a higher cost of capital near the existing secured-note yield. The effort to shrink the offering size is a mitigating detail, but the indicated cost is a less favorable financing prospect.
surprises.fact_evidence: Cogent is refinancing its “$750 million 2027 unsecured notes” in Q3 2026 with secured debt, aims to shrink the offering size, and indicated a higher cost of capital near the “8.8%-8.9% yield on existing secured notes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed whether refinancing had been executed and “at what coupon” as unconfirmed; its base scenario described “refi in progress.”

surprises.description: Capex moved in the opposite direction from the preview’s highlighted risk of another overshoot: it declined sharply, and management guided to further sequential declines. This eases the spending concern raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CapEx fell 16.7% sequentially and 31.4% year-over-year to $38.5 million,” with management “guiding to further sequential declines.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warned that “Another capex overshoot against about $14.8M of operating cash flow would be a liquidity concern.”

in_line: Off-net revenue declined 17.3% year over year, close to the preview’s cited expectation that off-net revenue was down 17.0% year over year.
The 10-facility data-center sale closed in Q2 as the preview said it had; the call also reported about 14 facilities remaining for sale, in line with the preview’s estimate of roughly 14.

surprises.description: Chegg reported Q2 revenue of $51.8 million, above both its $49–50 million guidance and the $49.8 million consensus in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $51.8 million, exceeding company expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total net revenue” guidance was “$49–50M”; Zacks consensus was “$49.8M.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $9.1 million, well above the preview’s $5–6 million company-guidance range and above the preview’s bull-case threshold of $7 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA for Q2 was $9.1 million (17% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA guidance was “$5–6M (~11% margin)”; the bull scenario expected “≥$7M.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating expenses were cut nearly in half year over year, with management attributing the reduction to AI-enabled productivity gains and restructuring—an efficiency improvement the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating expenses were cut nearly in half year-over-year to $32.3 million, driven by AI-enabled productivity gains and restructuring.”

surprises.description: Chegg generated positive free cash flow despite substantial severance payments, and ended Q2 with more cash and a higher net-cash position than at the Q1 level cited in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was $6.4 million in Q2 and $9.5 million in the first half, despite $14.4 million in severance payments from prior restructuring”; quarter-end cash and investments were “$72.3 million” and net cash was “$38.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 cash and investments of “$67.9M” and net cash of “$34.1M,” and said to watch quarter-end cash and the cash bridge; it gave no Q2 cash or free-cash-flow estimate.

surprises.description: Chegg disclosed a strategic pivot toward an employability platform for internships and jobs, including a beta already used by more than 10,000 students and a rollout beginning in Q3 and continuing through 2027. The preview focused on Academic Services, Skilling, and AI licensing, not this product direction.
surprises.fact_evidence: Chegg is “pivoting strategically toward an ‘employability’ platform”; “more than 10,000 students have used the beta,” with rollout “beginning in Q3 and continuing through 2027.”

surprises.description: Chegg repurchased $1.7 million of stock in Q2 and said severance payments are now largely behind it, a capital-allocation update not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Chegg repurchased $1.7 million of stock in Q2” and has “$120.7 million remaining on its buyback authorization, with severance payments now largely behind it.”

surprises.description: As the businesses integrate, Chegg will stop giving separate revenue guidance for Academic Services and Skilling. That changes the segment-level visibility the preview treated as important, including its focus on Skilling’s guide and Academic Services’ decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is discontinuing separate revenue guidance for Academic Services and Skilling, instead guiding on total revenue and adjusted EBITDA as the businesses integrate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “Chegg Skilling revenue and growth” and “Academic Services decline” as key metrics, and listed Q2 Skilling guidance of “$17.5–18.0M.”

in_line: Q3 revenue guidance of $43–44 million was consistent with the preview’s expectation for guidance in the mid-$40 millions.
Chegg expects to fully repay its convertible debt in Q3, consistent with the preview’s base case that the converts would be “on track” and its bull case that they would be repaid from cash.

surprises.description: Excelerate raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance from $480–510 million to $490–515 million and narrowed the range. The preview viewed a reaffirmation as the baseline, so the higher range is a positive change, though the increase is modest relative to the full-year outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “raised and narrowed full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $490 million to $515 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 adj. EBITDA guidance ($480–510M). Reaffirmation is the baseline.”

surprises.description: The FSRU conversion is now expected to cost more than the previously communicated approximately $200 million, with the higher-capability vessel purchase contributing to the project update. This is a negative cost revision, although management said returns should remain in line with prior guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “purchase the LNG carrier Methane Patricia Camilla for approximately $79 million as its FSRU conversion candidate”; “FSRU conversion capex is now expected to exceed the previously communicated ~$200 million due to the higher-capability vessel, though returns are expected to remain in line with prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “previously communicated ~$200 million”

surprises.description: Excelerate recontracted the FSRU Express to Colombia on a seven-year charter, with the vessel’s annual EBITDA contribution expected to rise by roughly 35% starting in early 2027. The preview did not flag this contract or uplift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FSRU Express was recontracted to Colombia under a seven-year charter … expected to boost the vessel's annual EBITDA contribution by roughly 35% starting in early 2027.”

surprises.description: The Iraq terminal contract includes a minimum take-or-pay offtake of 250 million standard cubic feet per day, a specific contracted volume the preview did not provide. This adds a concrete contracted floor to the already anticipated five-year project.
surprises.fact_evidence: “under a five-year take-or-pay contract with a minimum contracted offtake of 250 million standard cubic feet per day.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $120 million, within the preview’s derived $118–125 million range and close to its roughly $120 million baseline.
Acadia was deployed to Jordan under the expected nine-month NEPCO charter and is expected to contribute approximately $20 million of 2026 EBITDA, consistent with the preview’s outlook.
Iraq terminal operations remain scheduled for 2027; management specified early Q2 2027, which adds timing detail to the preview’s expectation of a 2027 restart.
The quarterly dividend was $0.09 per Class A share, matching the 13% increase already noted in the preview.
Net leverage was 1.9 times, below the 2-times level the preview flagged as a capital-allocation watch point.
Management said returns on the FSRU conversion should remain in line with prior guidance.

surprises.description: Arhaus reported Q2 revenue of $385 million, above both the $370 million high end of guidance and $365.7 million consensus. The preview said management was aiming for the high end, so this was a clear upside beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record net revenue of $385 million in Q2 2026,” up 7.4% year over year and “above the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Net revenue guidance was “$350–370M” and consensus was “$365.7M”; management had said it was “shooting for the high end.”

surprises.description: Written sales comps surged 12.5%, far exceeding the preview’s threshold of at least flat-to-positive comps for management’s recovery narrative to hold. This was a much stronger demand result than the preview’s cautious benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Comparable written sales surged 12.5% in Q2,” lifting year-to-date comparable written sales to positive 2.8%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said that if written comps were “not at least flat-to-positive, that narrative weakens,” after management described a “V-shaped recovery” in April and May.

surprises.description: Comparable delivered sales rose 4%, versus Q2 guidance of negative 5% to flat. That is a substantial beat against the company’s stated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Comparable delivered sales rose 4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 comparable delivered sales guidance was “−5% to flat.”

surprises.description: The IEEPA tariff recovery produced a sizeable, unexpected benefit: $23.8 million was recognized in cost of goods sold, and the full $37.8 million of requested refunds had been received in cash. The preview noted that guidance excluded refunds and that they were not automatic.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A one-time $23.8 million benefit in cost of goods sold from IEPA tariff recoveries,” including $15.5 million related to inventory sold before April 2026; “total refunds requested were $37.8 million and have since been fully received in cash.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance excludes any refund,” and “Refunds are not automatic”; management had promised clarity by the end of Q2.

surprises.description: Even excluding the tariff benefit, adjusted EBITDA was $55 million, above the preview’s $40–49 million guidance range and roughly $44–46 million consensus range. That underlying result beat expectations despite being down year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding the tariff benefit … adjusted EBITDA would have been $55 million,” down 8.9% year over year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 adjusted EBITDA guidance was “$40–49M,” with consensus “about $44–46M.”

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to $160–171 million from $150–161 million, rather than merely reaffirmed. Net income guidance was also raised, while the revenue range was left unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year net income guidance to $71–80 million and adjusted EBITDA to $160–171 million, while keeping net revenue guidance unchanged at $1.43–1.47 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior full-year adjusted EBITDA guide was “$150–161M”; the preview said reaffirming full-year guidance would amount to an acceleration call.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of 3%–8.8% growth leaves the midpoint below the 6.6%–12.3% second-half growth implied by the preview’s full-year math. The range overlaps that implied growth only toward its upper end, leaving more of the needed acceleration dependent on Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 guidance calls for net revenue of “$355–375 million (3%–8.8% growth)” and comparable delivered sales of “−1% to +5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview calculated that H2 revenue needed to be “roughly +6.6% to +12.3%” to meet the full-year revenue guide.

surprises.description: The company disclosed about $20 million of elevated fuel and shipping costs, including shipping costs tied to Middle East disruption, adding a material headwind beyond the tariff costs the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: Arhaus faces “roughly $10 million in elevated fuel costs and $10 million in higher shipping costs tied to Middle East disruption.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged FY26 tariff costs of $30–40 million but did not mention these additional fuel and shipping costs.

surprises.description: A June delivery-fee increase is expected to contribute $5–6 million of annual run-rate benefit, with virtually no customer pushback. The preview did not identify this new pricing action or its contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: A June delivery fee increase, the first in 3–4 years, is “expected to add $5–6 million in annual run-rate benefit with virtually no customer pushback,” beginning to flow through in Q3.

in_line: Full-year net revenue guidance remained at $1.43–1.47 billion, consistent with the preview’s expectation that management would reaffirm the range.
The estimated $30–40 million 2026 tariff impact matched the range highlighted in the preview.

surprises.description: Cognex’s adjusted EBITDA margin reached 32.2%, well above the preview’s 29.5–30.5% base range and above its 31% bull threshold. The company also said the margin exceeded the guidance midpoint by more than 250 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 32.2%,” “expanding 1,150 basis points year-over-year,” and “exceeding the guidance midpoint by more than 250 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin ~29.5% (implied)” and the base scenario of “29.5–30.5%”; the bull threshold was “≥31%.”

surprises.description: Cognex issued full-year 2026 guidance with Q2 results for the first time and raised its outlook to $1.13–$1.15 billion in revenue and $1.64–$1.68 in adjusted EPS. The preview had no full-year consensus, while the call described the outlook as well ahead of the prior 25% EBITDA-run-rate exit target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $1.13-$1.15 billion (~15% growth at midpoint) and adjusted EPS of $1.64-$1.68 (~63% growth), well ahead of its prior target of a 25% EBITDA run rate exit.” Cognex also issued full-year guidance alongside Q2 “for the first time,” citing improved second-half visibility.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.45, above the preview’s $0.42 consensus estimate, although at the top of the preview’s base-case range. The preview expected 68% year-over-year growth; Cognex reported 80%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS grew 80% year-over-year to $0.45, driven by roughly 100% revenue flow-through in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS $0.42” consensus; the base scenario was “$0.43–$0.45.”

surprises.description: The expected Q3 memory-cost pressure was larger and longer-lasting than the preview’s estimate: management expects a roughly 75-basis-point gross-margin headwind, rather than 50 basis points, with some spillover into Q4. Management expects pricing to fully offset it by 2027, but that is a later offset than the preview’s general expectation that tariffs are offset through pricing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rising memory prices are expected to create roughly 75 basis points of gross margin headwind in Q3 (with some spillover into Q4),” which management views as a timing issue it expects “to fully offset through pricing by 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had guided to a “50bps gross-margin headwind in Q3 from memory-chip costs”; the preview also said the 50bps framing “may prove optimistic.”

surprises.description: Regional performance was sharply divergent: China grew 42% year-over-year in constant currency, while Europe declined 15%. The preview gave no regional growth expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China was the fastest-growing region with revenue up 42% year-over-year in constant currency, while Europe declined 15%.”

surprises.description: Cognex disclosed a fast-growing data-center supply-chain business, reporting growth above 30% year-over-year despite the business still representing only a low-single-digit share of total revenue. The preview did not identify this as a growth driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data center supply chain revenue represents a low single-digit percentage of total revenue but is growing more than 30% year-over-year,” and management positioned it as an early-stage growth platform.

surprises.description: Cognex reported adding about 9,000 customers in 2025 and another 4,500 year-to-date in 2026, a customer-acquisition disclosure not anticipated in the preview. The preview discussed product monetization but did not provide an expectation for customer additions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cognex added ~9,000 new customers in 2025 and ~4,500 year-to-date in 2026.”

in_line: Q2 revenue growth was broadly in line with the preview’s expectation: Cognex reported 17% year-over-year growth, versus the preview’s implied 17.7% growth at consensus.
The full-year logistics outlook of high-single-digit growth matched the preview’s expectation that logistics would normalize to mid-to-high single digits.
The expected year-end cost-reduction target was essentially reaffirmed: Cognex expects approximately $35 million of annualized net reductions, within the preview’s cited $35–40 million target.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $5.9 million, below the preview’s $6.6–7.0 million base case and its roughly $6.8 million catalyst level. That leaves a larger-than-expected gap to the full-year target, which the preview said required about $7.9–8.5 million per quarter for Q2–Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined to $5.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: ... Adj. EBITDA $6.6–7.0M”; “Adjusted EBITDA of about $6.8M or more”; and the FY guide “requires about $7.9–8.5M per quarter for Q2–Q4.”

surprises.description: R&D expense more than doubled because the company began expensing AI development instead of capitalizing it, adding near-term earnings pressure the preview did not anticipate. GAAP net income also fell to $1.1 million from $2.9 million a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expense more than doubled as the company shifted AI development to current expense rather than capitalizing it, pressuring near-term earnings”; “GAAP net income fell to $1.1 million from $2.9 million.”

surprises.description: The company ended Q2 with $13.4 million in cash, substantially above the $3.4 million balance cited at Q1-end, easing the preview’s liquidity concern. However, net working capital was only $695,000 and the company established a new $60 million ATM program, leaving a potential dilution concern despite the preferred-stock redemption being described as zero-dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with about $13.4 million in cash and net working capital of only $695,000, and established a new $60 million at-the-market equity program”; the preferred stock was redeemed “using a $50 million ... credit facility with zero dilution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash was $3.4M at Q1-end”; “Watch the cash balance, revolver draw, and any use of the $60M ATM, which would conflict with the ‘zero dilution’ framing.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed the May acquisition of Empower Healthcare and Compliance Partners, which the preview did not flag. It is expected to have immaterial near-term financial impact, but management described it as a cross-selling opportunity and said its president has historically referred business representing about 10% of CareCloud’s annualized revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The May acquisition of Empower Healthcare and Compliance Partners ... is expected to be immaterial to near-term financials but a cross-selling catalyst”; its president “has historically referred business now representing approximately 10% of CareCloud’s annualized revenue.”

surprises.description: Recurring technology-enabled solutions reached about 75% of revenue, up from 69% a year earlier, with $24 million of revenue. The preview flagged professional-services erosion and the need to assess organic growth, but did not anticipate this specific improvement in recurring-revenue mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recurring technology-enabled business solutions rose to approximately 75% of revenue this quarter, up from 69% a year ago, reaching $24 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “whether professional services erosion stabilizes will determine whether H2 organic growth exists once Medsphere anniversaries in Q3.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $31.9 million was broadly in line with the preview’s $31.85 million and $32.49 million consensus estimates, and its expected year-over-year growth range; the preview’s base scenario was $31.8–32.3 million.

Management reaffirmed all three FY2026 guidance ranges—$128–132 million revenue, $29–31 million adjusted EBITDA, and $0.20–0.23 GAAP EPS—as the preview’s base case expected full guidance to be reaffirmed.

surprises.description: Shift4 cut its FY2026 outlook instead of reaffirming the prior ranges: GRLNF is now $2.48–$2.53B versus $2.50–$2.60B, adjusted EBITDA is $1.15–$1.18B versus $1.165–$1.215B, and non-GAAP EPS is $5.15–$5.35 versus $5.50–$5.70. Management said the midpoint reduction was only 100 basis points on an FX-neutral basis, with about $20M of FX translation and the $25M Q3 Middle East headwind accounting for most of the $40M revision.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year 2026 guidance calls for GRLNF of $2.48-$2.53 billion,” adjusted EBITDA “of $1.15-$1.18 billion,” and non-GAAP EPS “of $5.15-$5.35.” The GRLNF midpoint was “reduced only 100 basis points on an FX-neutral basis,” with “a ~$20 million FX translation impact and the $25 million Q3 Middle East headwind comprising most of the $40 million guidance revision.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (reaffirmed at Q1):” GRLNF $2.50–$2.60B, adjusted EBITDA $1.165–$1.215B, and non-GAAP EPS $5.50–$5.70. The preview says to watch whether the EPS guide is “reaffirm[ed], raise[d], or trim[med]” and calls reaffirmation “the base case.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross revenue was far above the roughly $1.17B guide used as the preview’s anchor, reaching $1.29B. That is about a 10% beat, considerably larger than the preview’s base case of an in-line to modest beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 gross revenue grew 34% year-over-year to $1.29 billion, beating the $1.17 billion guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists Q2 gross revenue guidance and Street at “~$1.17B” and says guidance is used as the revenue anchor because no firm revenue consensus was found. Its base scenario is “In line to modest beat.”

surprises.description: Adjusted free cash flow was more than twice the Q2 expectation, at $21M versus the approximately $10M guide. The preview had described this as the most stretched line in the model.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow of $21 million more than doubled the $10 million guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists Q2 adjusted FCF at “~$10M” and calls it “the most stretched line in the model.”

surprises.description: Management put a roughly $25M Middle East travel-disruption headwind on Q3, a quantified drag beyond the preview’s Q2 $20M embed and its general warning that Q3 travel disruption could extend. The preview’s bullish scenario had travel drag “under $20M.”
surprises.fact_evidence: “Middle East conflict caused travel disruption that management estimates as a ~$25 million headwind for Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says Q2 guidance embeds a “~$20M Middle East travel-disruption headwind” and asks, “Did the $20M Q2 embed prove conservative?” Its bull scenario assumes “travel drag under $20M,” and its bear scenario warns that “Q3 travel drag extends.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA modestly beat the Q2 expectation, and the reported margin was higher than the preview’s guide-level margin assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 39% year-over-year to $284 million at a 46% margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists adjusted EBITDA guidance and Street at “~$278M” with a “45.2% margin.”

surprises.description: Q2 GRLNF came in slightly above the preview’s expected range, while organic growth met—not exceeded—the preview’s key 11% threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross revenue less network fees grew 51% to $624 million (11% organic).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected Q2 GRLNF of “~$615–620M” and said “≥11%” organic growth would support the thesis.

surprises.description: Shift4 One was already live in 12 countries and was on track to exceed the 15-country year-end goal, putting rollout progress ahead of the preview’s checkpoint that ten or more countries would indicate the story was ahead of plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Shift4 One (payments, DCC and tax-free shopping) is now live in 12 countries, on track to surpass the 15-country goal by year-end 2026,” with a target of “adding several thousand merchants per month exiting the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists a “Target of 7 to 15 countries by year-end” and says “Ten or more would mean the international story is ahead of plan.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed that the July term loan pushes maturities out to 2031 but also raises net interest expense, which weighs on free cash flow guidance. The preview knew about the additional $1B loan but did not flag this specific FCF cost or a maturity extension to 2031.
surprises.fact_evidence: The additional “$1 billion Term Loan B” was raised “to prefund the August 2027 convertible note maturity, terming out its capital structure to 2031, which drives higher net interest expense weighing on free cash flow guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says “A $1B secured term loan was added in July 2026” and flags Q2 and FY adjusted FCF, including that “reiteration supports the leverage path.”

surprises.description: Shift4 reported substantial Q2 repurchases, including about 650,000 shares bought at an average price of roughly $38; the preview did not identify this buyback activity or share-count reduction as an expected result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased ~650,000 shares at an average price of ~$38 in Q2,” bringing cumulative buybacks to “$625 million of the $1 billion authorization” and reducing non-GAAP share count by “~11%.”

in_line: Organic GRLNF growth was 11%, matching the preview’s stated threshold of at least 11%.
The 3.7x pro forma net leverage and expectation of deleveraging to the low 3s by year-end matched the preview’s leverage figures and target.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $29.1 million, about 9–11% above the preview’s $26.3–26.6 million consensus range. This was a clear upside beat against the expected quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached $29.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $26.6M” with “Alt. consensus $26.3M”; the catalyst checklist also says “Revenue vs. $26.6M consensus.”

surprises.description: Delcath raised FY26 revenue guidance to $104–108 million, rather than merely reaffirming its “at least $100M” target. The new range also sits above the preview’s $103.2 million analyst consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $104-108 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked “whether management raises the guide, not whether it reaches $100M,” and cited FY26 revenue consensus of “$103.2M.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin reached 90%, well above the preview’s roughly 85% expectation, and the company raised its full-year gross-margin range to 86–89%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin was 90% versus 86% a year ago, with full-year guidance raised to 86-89%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~85% (guide 84–87%)”; the preview also said to treat 84% as the full-year floor.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $7.6 million, far above the preview’s base case of near breakeven. It was still down from $9.8 million a year earlier, but the quarter was much stronger than the preview’s expected level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined to $7.6 million in Q2 2026 from $9.8 million in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “adj. EBITDA near breakeven”; the preview also flagged a negative Q2 as a risk.

surprises.description: The company reported $2.7 million of net income, while the preview’s diluted EPS consensus was a loss of $0.095 per share. The reported positive net income is a materially better profitability signal than that loss expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income held flat at $2.7 million year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) | –$0.095.”

surprises.description: HEPZATO kit volume grew 30%, but revenue grew only 21% because 340B pricing lowered effective ASP from about $185,000 to $170,000–173,000 per kit. That pricing drag limited the revenue conversion of the volume growth and was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HEPZATO revenue grew 21% year-over-year but represented 30% volume growth, with the entire gap attributable to 340B pricing that cut effective ASP from ~$185K to ~$170-173K per kit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Bull requires higher revenue per center, not just a higher center count.”

surprises.description: CHEMOSAT revenue was $2.0 million, above the preview’s expectation that it would remain flat at about $1.7 million per quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$2 million in chemoSAT revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CHEMOSAT has been flat at about $1.7M per quarter for five quarters.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that enrollment in both the colorectal and breast cancer trials is running below expectations because of training challenges. The preview did not identify this enrollment shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management acknowledged enrollment in both colorectal and breast cancer trials is running below expectations due to training challenges.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Enrollment … is running below expectations due to training challenges.”

surprises.description: Instead of the cash-burn concern the preview highlighted, Delcath generated $5.7 million of operating cash flow and ended with $95.9 million in cash and investments, up from the preview’s cited $89.3 million at Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $95.9 million in cash and investments, generated $5.7 million in operating cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview raised “the cash-burn debate against $89.3M of cash” and said to watch for “any hint of ATM or other financing.”

surprises.description: The company had already repurchased about $9 million of stock under its $25 million buyback program, a capital-allocation action the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[The company] has repurchased ~$9 million of stock under a $25 million buyback program.”

in_line: Delcath ended Q2 with 31 active treatment centers after adding two, consistent with the preview’s expected 31–32 centers; it remains on track for 37 by year-end, matching the existing target.

surprises.description: Etsy marketplace GMS reached $2.6 billion, above the preview’s $2.48–$2.53 billion guidance range and its $2.53 billion high-end watchpoint. That is roughly 3% above the high end, a meaningful upside to the key operating measure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Etsy marketplace GMS grew 7.5% year-over-year to $2.6 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Etsy marketplace GMS (Q2 guide) | $2.48B–$2.53B (+3–5% Y/Y)” and “GMS vs. the $2.53B high end of guidance.”

surprises.description: Full-year GMS guidance moved from low-single-digit growth to mid-single-digit growth, exceeding the preview’s expectation that the existing low-single-digit outlook was the floor. The revision is a clear improvement to the growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year guidance was raised to mid-single-digit GMS growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 GMS: ‘Low single-digit’ growth (raised at Q1)” and “‘Low single-digit’ is now the floor. A raise toward mid-single-digit is the main upside lever.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $668 million exceeded the preview’s $645.1–$649.7 million estimates by about 3–4%. The preview cautioned that continuing-operations comparisons were uncertain, but the reported result was still above the stated consensus figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue was $668 million (up 9.3% for the Etsy marketplace stand-alone).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $645.1M (StockStory) / $649.7M (Zacks).”

surprises.description: The Q3 GMS outlook was for 4–6% growth, rather than the soft guide identified in the preview’s downside case. The preview did not provide a specific Q3 consensus range, so the positive difference is against that qualitative concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 GMS is guided to $2.53-$2.58 billion (4%-6% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bear scenario included a “soft Q3 GMS guide.”

surprises.description: Etsy raised the low end of its full-year adjusted EBITDA margin outlook from 28% to 29%, narrowing the range upward. The preview’s 28–30% expectation therefore understated the new floor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year guidance was raised to mid-single-digit GMS growth with adjusted EBITDA margin tightened upward to 29%-30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA margin | 28–30% (unchanged).”

surprises.description: Take rate was 25.9%, 20 basis points above the preview’s approximate 25.7% expectation. The reported increase included contributions from Etsy Ads and off-site ads, in addition to the Reverb divestiture effect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Take rate reached 25.9%, up 130 basis points year-over-year, including roughly 80 basis points from the Reverb divestiture, with additional gains from Etsy Ads and off-site ads.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Take rate | ~25.7%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin came in at 29.2%, slightly above the preview’s 27–29% company guidance range. The beat was modest, and the result was close to the preview’s 29% bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $195 million at a 29.2% margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin | 27–29%” and bull case “≥29%.”

surprises.description: Habitual and repeat-buyer cohorts both grew sequentially for the first time since 2023, adding a positive quality signal beyond the expected sequential increase in total active buyers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Habitual and repeat buyer cohorts showing sequential growth for the first time since 2023.”

surprises.description: Mobile-app GMS grew 12.5% year-over-year and accounted for about 47% of total GMS, with growth primarily from existing app users buying more. The preview did not flag this channel’s growth as an expected driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mobile app GMS growth accelerated to 12.5% year-over-year, now representing about 47% of total GMS, with growth driven primarily by existing app users purchasing more.”

surprises.description: Etsy said YouTube and TikTok investments drove a fivefold increase in visits from millennial and Gen Z audiences in the first half of 2026. This was a new, favorable audience-acquisition metric not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Investments in YouTube and TikTok drove a fivefold increase in visits from millennial and Gen Z audiences in the first half of 2026.”

surprises.description: Etsy quantified agentic AI traffic at less than 1% of total traffic. The preview noted the lack of a quantified disclosure and highlighted agentic commerce as a possible upside topic; the reported figure indicates its current traffic contribution is very small.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Agentic AI traffic remains under 1% of total traffic.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Agentic-commerce disclosure … has not been quantified by the company so far” and “Any hard number could move the stock more than the core print.”

surprises.description: Etsy announced a workforce reduction of about 220 employees, or 12%, alongside roughly $35 million in charges. The preview did not flag restructuring or these costs, making this an unanticipated near-term expense and operational change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restructuring and reducing its workforce by approximately 220 employees (about 12%) to roughly 1,600 people, incurring about $35 million in charges substantially complete by end of Q3 2026.”

in_line: Active buyers increased sequentially by 350,000, consistent with the preview’s expectation that a second consecutive sequential gain would confirm the inflection; the preview did not establish a specific year-over-year growth expectation.
The Depop sale closed July 30 for about $1.4 billion in cash, as the preview had already noted.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $220 million, above both the roughly $203 million consensus and the $208 million high end of guidance. The preview said a result at or above $215 million would imply a higher full-year outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 10% to $220 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA” consensus: “~$203M (midpoint)” and Q2 guidance: “$198–208M”; “At or above $215M would force a higher FY guide under management's H1 framing.”

surprises.description: Frontdoor raised full-year revenue guidance by $25 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance by $20 million, rather than merely reaffirming or nudging up the outlook. The new ranges also imply adjusted EBITDA margin of about 27%, versus roughly 26% previously.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year guidance, increasing revenue expectations by $25 million to $2.19-$2.21 billion and adjusted EBITDA by $20 million to $585-$600 million (~27% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (reaffirmed 4/30/26): Revenue $2.155–2.195B; Adj. EBITDA $565–580M (~26% margin)”; the base scenario expected “FY reaffirmed or nudged up.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS growth was nearly 20%, well above the roughly 8% growth implied by consensus. The preview cautioned that buybacks could widen the EPS-versus-EBITDA growth gap, but EBITDA also came in well above expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS growth of nearly 20%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus adjusted diluted EPS of “$1.76” implied “+8.0%” year-over-year growth.

surprises.description: Member count grew 1% in Q2, delivering the organic growth inflection the preview identified as important, after flat member count in Q1. The preview noted that another flat quarter would make the full-year growth target fragile.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total ending member count grew 1% in Q2, marking the first organic member growth in 5 years (since 2021).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 was flat Y/Y. The 2026 thesis depends on total members turning positive. A second flat quarter makes the back-half target fragile.”

surprises.description: Gross margin expanded to 59%, rather than giving back margin from the unusually strong 58% prior-year quarter as the preview feared. It was also above the roughly 57% Q2 consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 100 basis points to 59%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 gross-margin consensus was “~57%”; the preview called Q2'25 “an exceptional 58%” and said the FY guide “implies some give-back.”

surprises.description: Retention was 79.6%, near an all-time high, rather than slipping for a second consecutive year-over-year quarter as the preview flagged as a risk. The reported 85% autopay enrollment and 84% of jobs routed to preferred contractors provide additional context for the strength.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retention rate remained near all-time highs at 79.6%, supported by autopay enrollment reaching 85% and 84% of jobs routed to preferred contractors.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A second consecutive Y/Y decline would turn ‘integration timing’ into churn”; the preview listed retention versus “79.3% (Q1'26) and 78.3% (Q2'25)” as a key check.

surprises.description: Q2 results included about $9 million of favorable weather and cost-development effects, while management expects most of the weather benefit to reverse in Q3. The preview had highlighted summer claims costs and heat severity as downside risks, not these favorable Q2 contributions and anticipated reversal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 results benefited from approximately $5 million of favorable weather and about $4 million of favorable cost development, but management expects the weather benefit to largely reverse in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 is the air-conditioning failure quarter”; the preview said to watch “contractor cost inflation, HVAC equipment and tariff costs, and summer heat severity.”

surprises.description: Frontdoor now expects to repurchase approximately $330 million of stock in 2026 and said it will complete its authorization nearly a year early. The preview flagged buyback pace as a secondary item but gave no expectation for this scale or timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company now expects to repurchase approximately $330 million of stock in 2026, completing its authorization nearly a year ahead of schedule, having already bought back $181 million through July 31.”

surprises.description: The real estate channel grew member count 7% and improved attach rate by 30 basis points despite the preview's emphasis on weak existing-home sales as a constraint. The preview had no specific expectation for this degree of channel growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The real estate channel grew member count 7% and improved attach rate 30 basis points despite flat existing home sales expected to finish around 4 million for the fourth consecutive year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Real estate channel. Attach rates approached 6% in March. Existing-home sales remain the external constraint.”

surprises.description: Management highlighted the HVAC upgrade program's scale-up from $13 million to an expected $170 million in four years, a longer-term growth opportunity beyond the preview's near-term mid-20% growth framing for “Other” revenue. The opportunity is tempered by only 3% member penetration and margins in the low 20s, below core home warranty.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The HVAC upgrade program has scaled from $13 million to an expected $170 million in 4 years with penetration of only 3% of the 2.1 million member base, though its margins are lower at low-20% versus core home warranty.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “‘Other’ revenue. Management guided mid-20% growth for Q2, down from +73% in Q3'25 and +23% in Q1'26.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $645 million, close to the $642.1 million consensus and the preview's $645 million base-case estimate.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $449 million, versus the preview's $415 million consensus, an 8% beat; reported growth was 15%. Even excluding the episodic customer initiatives, management estimated growth at 11% to 12%, still well above the preview's 6.3% implied growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 15% year-over-year to $449 million”; excluding the one-time customer initiative benefits, “Q2 total revenue growth was still 11% to 12%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS reached $0.35, well above the preview's $0.29 consensus. The 30% year-over-year increase also substantially exceeded the preview's implied 5.6% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS rose 30% year-over-year to $0.35.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $128.5 million, materially above the preview's approximately $116 million estimate. Its 13% year-over-year growth also exceeded the preview's implied 1.8% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 13% to $128.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$116M”; implied year-over-year growth of “+1.8%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 28.6%, above the preview's approximately 28.0% expectation and the 28.5% level it identified as enough to remove a bear talking point. The margin was still below the year-ago 29.2%, but the result was better than the preview's modeled decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 13% to $128.5 million with a margin of 28.6%, up 130 basis points sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~28.0%” and said “a print at 28.5% or higher would remove a bear talking point.”
