surprises.description: Management raised full-year guidance across revenue, EBITDA, and EPS, rather than reaffirming or narrowing it. The revenue floor rose by $45 million, from $1.625 billion to $1.67 billion, while the EPS range moved from $1.15–$1.25 to $1.23–$1.29.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance across all metrics,” to revenue of “$1.67-$1.71 billion,” adjusted EBITDA of “$472-$486 million,” and adjusted diluted EPS of “$1.23-$1.29,” with “the bottom end raised by $45 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed existing FY26 guidance of revenue “$1,625M – $1,700M,” adjusted EBITDA “$460M – $485M,” and adjusted diluted EPS “$1.15 – $1.25”; it described reaffirming as “the low bar.”

surprises.description: Base revenue swung to exceptionally strong 6.7% growth, against the preview's discussion of flat Q1 base volume and a 0% to -2% full-year base assumption. The improvement is partly episodic, however: roughly half came from customer initiatives expected to normalize by Q4, leaving underlying base growth of about 3.3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Base revenue grew an exceptionally strong 6.7%,” with “roughly half attributed to episodic customer-driven volume initiatives expected to normalize by Q4,” implying “underlying base growth of about 3.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Base revenue turned flat” in Q1 and that “FY26 base assumption is 0% to -2%.”

surprises.description: Enterprise bookings increased to 20 from 17 in Q1, alongside 12.5% growth in combined upsell, cross-sell, and new-logo revenue. This was a positive update on a demand area the preview specifically flagged for attention.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Combined upsell, cross-sell and new logo revenue grew 12.5%,” with “20 enterprise bookings” of at least $500,000 expected annual contract value, “up from 17 in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Enterprise bookings and vertical mix” and noted “Q1 had 17 bookings at $500K+ ACV.”

surprises.description: The company made substantial voluntary debt payments, including a $45 million prepayment in the week of the call on top of $25 million in Q2, bringing cumulative repayment since the Sterling acquisition above $165.5 million. The preview did not flag this pace of debt reduction; net leverage was 3.7x, still above the company's below-3x target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $45 million voluntary debt prepayment this week on top of a $25 million prepayment in Q2,” with cumulative repayment “over $165.5 million” and net leverage “3.7x (targeting below 3x).”

surprises.description: The company had repurchased approximately $38 million of shares through July 31, or about 1.9% of shares outstanding, an unpreviewed capital-return update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased approximately $38 million of shares through July 31 at an average price of $11.78,” representing “about 1.9% of shares outstanding,” with “$61.8 million remaining on its $100 million authorization.”

surprises.description: Q2 operating cash flow rose 97% year over year to $73.6 million, a strong cash-generation result not anticipated or quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Generated Q2 operating cash flow of $73.6 million, up 97% year-over-year.”

in_line: Management expected second-half growth to moderate, guiding to mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth in Q3 and low-to-mid single digits in Q4 as it laps strong 2025 comparisons. This broadly fits the preview's discussion that the prior full-year guidance midpoint required only about 4.6% H2 growth.

Sterling synergy execution progressed within the existing $65-$80 million target: $63 million of actions had been taken and $51 million realized, versus $58 million and $47 million, respectively, in Q1. The preview identified a possible further target raise as an upside catalyst, but did not state that a raise was expected.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was $650 million, well below the preview’s $761.9 million to roughly $801 million consensus range; the call attributed the miss to production delays at two new contract manufacturing facilities. The preview had expected roughly $738 million based on guidance and noted that prior-quarter delays had been described as resolved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue of $650 million rose 8% year-over-year but came in roughly $90 million below prior expectations due to production delays at two new contract manufacturing facilities.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue, Q3” consensus: “$761.9M (Zacks, Aug 2026) or ~$801M (StockStory, Aug 4)” and guide-implied “~$738M”; the preview also says Q2 delays were “both described as resolved.”

surprises.description: Fluence cut its FY26 revenue guidance midpoint by about $400 million, from the preview’s $3.2–$3.6 billion range (a $3.4 billion midpoint) to $3.0 billion. The preview explicitly identified a guidance cut as the main risk to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered its fiscal 2026 revenue guidance midpoint by approximately $400 million to $3 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue” guidance: “$3.2–3.6B (reaffirmed May 7, 2026)”; the preview asks whether the company will “hold it, narrow it to the low end, or cut it.”

surprises.description: The FY26 adjusted EBITDA midpoint fell from $50 million to negative $10 million, substantially worse than the preview’s $40–$60 million guidance. Management cited about $44 million of lost margin from shifting revenue into 2027 and a $15 million charge tied to a long-term battery supply agreement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[It] cut its adjusted EBITDA midpoint from $50 million to negative $10 million”; the cut was driven largely by “about $44 million of lost margin” from shifting revenue into 2027 and “a $15 million charge tied to a long-term battery supply agreement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA” guidance: “$40–60M (reaffirmed May 7, 2026).”

surprises.description: The Houston 15 GWh fully automated domestic-content facility has been delayed by construction and automation problems, with full production now expected in fiscal Q1 2027. The preview had discussed prior production-related delays as resolved and did not flag this facility’s later ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Houston 15 GWh fully-automated domestic-content facility has been delayed by construction and automation issues and is now expected to reach full production in fiscal Q1 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the Q2 Vietnam and Spain delays were “both described as resolved” and expected the “push-out” to be recovered.

surprises.description: The data-center announcement was substantial but did not deliver the hyperscaler purchase order the preview was watching for: the $850 million total included a $300 million behind-the-meter developer contract, while the hyperscaler’s $550 million consisted of awards that were not yet purchase orders. The developer contract is a positive first step, but the expected hyperscaler PO was not booked.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fluence received its first data center orders and awards totaling $850 million, including a $300 million behind-the-meter developer contract and $550 million in awards from a hyperscaler that are not yet purchase orders.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s key metric was “First hyperscaler purchase order. Booked in the quarter or slipped?” and its bull case assumed a “hyperscaler PO booked.”

surprises.description: Q3 order intake reached a record $1.44 billion, far exceeding the preview’s indication that more than $600 million had been signed as of May 7 and its call for a strong quarter of orders. This was nearly triple the year-earlier quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fluence signed a record $1.44 billion of orders in Q3 2026, nearly triple the $509 million signed in the same quarter last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Over $600M was signed as of May 7” and said “Backlog growth needs a strong quarter of orders against about $760M of burn.”

surprises.description: Management said record order intake may require an additional $300–$500 million of working capital over the coming year, far beyond the preview’s roughly $100 million inventory-build assumption. The larger funding need is a new potential constraint on supporting growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management flagged that supporting record order intake may require an additional $300 million to $500 million of working capital over the coming year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “another ~$100M inventory build” and flagged liquidity and inventory as items to watch.

surprises.description: The company’s stated gross-margin range was 10%–15%, rather than the preview’s FY26 guided band of 11%–13%. That puts the stated lower end below the expected floor, although the upper end is higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management was “reaffirming its 10%-15% gross margin range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 adjusted gross margin guidance as “11–13% (targeting ~12%).”

surprises.description: Fluence ended the quarter with $863 million of total liquidity, somewhat below the preview’s roughly $900 million reference point, though management expected liquidity to return to $900 million by fiscal year-end. The reported balance was still above the preview’s $800 million level that it said would revive balance-sheet concerns.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total liquidity ended the quarter at approximately $863 million (including $365 million in cash), with management expecting a return to $900 million by fiscal year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said liquidity was “About $900M” and flagged “Below $800M” as reviving the balance-sheet bear case.

surprises.description: Fluence reorganized senior leadership, moving Roman Lewsen to lead supply chain and Peter Williams to focus on product, with both reporting directly to the CEO. The preview did not anticipate this change, and the provided facts do not state its expected operating or financial effect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reorganized leadership, moving Roman Lewsen to head supply chain and Peter Williams to focus on product, both reporting directly to the CEO.”

in_line: The preview expected backlog growth and a strong order quarter; backlog reached a record $6.4 billion, up 14% sequentially and more than 30% year-over-year.
The company reaffirmed its approximately $180 million FY26 ARR target, in line with the preview’s expectation.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $107 million, below the preview’s $118–126 million author estimate. The call attributed the year-over-year decline in part to restatement costs, although EBITDA excluding those costs rose 3.4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell $7.9 million to $107 million due to restatement costs (though excluding those costs EBITDA rose 3.4%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA | Not found. Author estimate: ~$118–126M.”

surprises.description: Management kept the full-year guidance ranges but said results are likely to land near their low ends. That is weaker than simply reiterating the ranges and implies performance well below the $445 million EBITDA midpoint the preview identified as an important threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance … but signaled results will land near the low end of the range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance treatment. Reiteration is the base case. A raise to the low end of the EBITDA range is the bull signal. A midpoint below about $445M would be a de-rating event.”

surprises.description: Full-year restatement costs are now expected near the top of the previously stated $35–45 million range, and about $3 million shifted from Q2 into Q3. The preview anticipated $15 million or more in Q2 and described roughly $15 million as the base scenario, so the top-end full-year outlook and timing shift point to more cost pressure than that base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restatement costs are now expected at the top end of the initial $35M–$45M range, with $20.9M incurred year-to-date and roughly $3M shifting from Q2 into Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Restatement costs (P&L) | $15M+ in Q2”; the base scenario also assumed “restatement costs ~$15M.”

surprises.description: Take 5’s same-store sales were on target, but its EBITDA margin fell about 70 basis points because of inflation and store operating expenses. The preview focused on Take 5 sales and traffic rather than an expected margin decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Take 5 delivered its 24th consecutive quarter of same-store sales growth … but its EBITDA margin declined about 70 basis points due to inflation and store operating expenses.”

surprises.description: Base oil costs rose amid the Middle East conflict, prompting modest price increases at the end of Q2 and plans for further pricing in the back half. This added an input-cost and pricing issue not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rising base oil input costs from Middle East conflict prompted modest price increases at the end of Q2 … [with the company] expecting further pricing in the back half.”

surprises.description: The board unanimously rejected activist ADW’s acquisition proposal, describing it as highly conditional and significantly undervaluing the company. The preview did not mention an acquisition proposal or a potential board decision on one.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The board unanimously rejected activist ADW's acquisition proposal, calling it highly conditional and stating it significantly undervalued the company.”

surprises.description: The lower-income and newer customer groups that had been a concern were reported as stabilized, while other customer cohorts showed rising average checks, premium mix in the low 90s, and attachment rates in the high 50s. This was better than the preview’s concern about softer traffic and higher churn among those groups.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lower-income and newer customers continue to moderate but have stabilized, while remaining cohorts show resilience with rising average check, premium mix in the low 90s, and attachment rates in the high 50s.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had flagged “softer traffic and higher churn among newer and lower-income households” and described its base scenario as “flat-to-slightly-negative traffic.”

surprises.description: Franchise Brands and Auto Glass Now both posted positive same-store sales, at 0.5% and 2.6%, respectively. The preview highlighted moderation across brands but did not set expectations for these Q2 segment comps.
surprises.fact_evidence: “All three reporting segments [posted] positive comps: Take 5 up 3.6%, Franchise Brands up 0.5%, and Auto Glass Now up 2.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited management’s prior-quarter guidance of “moderation across all of our brands in Q2” but gave no Q2 comp estimates for Franchise Brands or Auto Glass Now.

in_line: Revenue of $507.4 million was within the preview’s $505–525 million author estimate.
Take 5 same-store sales of 3.6% were essentially in line with the preview’s roughly 3.5% expectation.

The company reiterated the previously issued full-year revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EPS guidance ranges, as the preview’s base case anticipated; the near-low-end outlook is a separate negative surprise.
Full-year free cash flow guidance remained $125–145 million, matching the range carried in the preview.

surprises.description: Genie reported diluted EPS of $0.43, well above the preview’s $0.25 consensus estimate. The result was about 72% higher than the estimate, despite revenue coming in below consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated net income attributable to Genie common stockholders surged to $11.4 million ($0.43 per diluted share)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $0.25”

surprises.description: Consolidated gross margin reached 33.5%, substantially above the preview’s roughly 24% reference point and its 23–25% base case. Gross profit rose 43.4% even as revenue declined, as GRE margins returned to their historical range after unusually weak year-ago natural gas profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross profit rose 43.4% to $33.7 million with gross margin expanding to 33.5%, as GRE margins normalized to their historical range after unusually weak year-ago natural gas profitability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin versus about 24%”; “Roughly 25% or higher supports the recovery thesis”; base case “23–25%.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $100.4 million, about 4% below the $104.57 million consensus estimate, and declined 4.6% year over year rather than the preview’s implied 0.7% decline. The call attributed the decline to the expiration of low-margin aggregation deals.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated revenue declined 4.6% year-over-year to $100.4 million, driven by a 4.9% drop in GRE revenue to $94.1 million as low-margin aggregation deals expired.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $104.57M”; implied year-over-year change “–0.7%.”

surprises.description: The customer base did not deliver the expected second consecutive quarter of sequential growth: RCEs fell from 354,000 in Q1 to 345,000, while meters slipped from 364,000 to 363,000. Gross new additions also declined to 65,000 from 70,000 a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The customer base shrank to 345,000 RCEs and 363,000 meters from 413,000 RCEs and 419,000 meters a year earlier, with gross new customer additions slipping to 65,000 from 70,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The bull case needs a second straight quarter of sequential growth with churn stable or lower.”

surprises.description: Commodity volumes fell sharply—electricity kilowatt-hours sold declined 17% and natural-gas therms sold declined 23%—while revenue per unit rose 12% and 50%, respectively. The preview did not flag this volume-and-pricing pattern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Electricity kilowatt hours sold fell 17% while revenue per kWh rose 12%, and natural gas therms sold dropped 23% while revenue per therm surged 50%, reflecting a smaller but higher-priced volume base.”

surprises.description: Consolidated SG&A rose 28% to $27.2 million because Genie deliberately shifted toward higher-cost customer-acquisition channels. The preview did not anticipate this near-term cost increase, though management said the channels target customers with higher lifetime value and should benefit future quarters.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated SG&A jumped 28% to $27.2 million due to a deliberate shift toward higher-cost acquisition channels targeting higher lifetime-value customers, expected to benefit future quarters.”

in_line: GREW turned profitable, reporting $0.3 million of adjusted EBITDA versus a year-earlier loss; the preview said Genie Solar was on track to be profitable for the rest of the year.
The company resumed share repurchases and also paid a quarterly dividend, consistent with the preview’s watch for resumed buybacks or other capital returns.

surprises.description: Gogo cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $870–$895 million from $905–$945 million, citing Galileo and 5G equipment shipments slipping into the second half. The new range is below the guidance the preview said had been reaffirmed at Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “lowered its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $870–$895 million, driven primarily by the timing of Galileo and 5G equipment shipments slipping into the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue ... $905–945M (reaffirmed at Q1)”

surprises.description: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance fell to $175–$185 million from $198–$218 million. The preview had the prior range as reaffirmed; the call attributed roughly half the reduction to litigation expense and the rest to product mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was cut to $175–$185 million, with litigation expense accounting for roughly half the reduction and product mix the remainder.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA ... $198–218M (reaffirmed at Q1)”

surprises.description: FY2026 free cash flow guidance was reduced to $65–$85 million from $90–$110 million, despite the preview highlighting the existing range as a key metric to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “full-year free cash flow guidance was revised to $65–$85 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 free cash flow ... $90–110M (reaffirmed at Q1)”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $222.8 million, below the preview’s roughly $229.4 million consensus estimate and below its $227–$232 million base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue was $222.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (Q2) ... ~$229.4M”; “Base ... Revenue $227–232M”

surprises.description: Galileo shipped 108 terminals in Q2, below the preview’s roughly 120–130 unit watch range. At the same time, Gogo lowered its full-year aircraft-online target to the mid-500s from about 600, tempering the rollout outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “108 units shipped in Q2”; “reduced its full-year Galileo aircraft-online target to the mid-500s from a prior expectation of about 600 units.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Q2 number below ~120–130 would put the second-half acceleration narrative in question”; “management said OEM installs come ‘really in Q3, Q4.’”

surprises.description: Military and government service revenue accelerated sharply, rising 20% sequentially and 40% year over year. The preview noted Q1 growth of 7% sequentially and pipeline opportunities, but did not anticipate usage surging with the Middle East conflict.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Military and government service revenue surged 40% year-over-year and 20% sequentially, driven by heightened usage tied to the Middle East conflict under pre-existing blanket purchase agreements.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Military/government momentum. Service revenue rose 7% Q/Q in Q1.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was positive $21.6 million, an improvement from Q1 but below the preview’s derived Q2 estimate of $25–$35 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow improved to positive $21.6 million from negative $19.2 million in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow (Q2) ... Derived estimate ~$25–35M”

surprises.description: A $7.2 million non-cash fair-value increase in the Satcom Direct earn-out was included in Q2 results, an additional reported-loss headwind not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “results included a $7.2 million non-cash Satcom Direct earn-out fair value increase.”

surprises.description: Galileo aircraft online rose to 184, up 66% sequentially from the 111 cited for Q1 in the preview. The preview focused on shipments and the OEM ramp, but did not flag this faster increase in aircraft online.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LEO (Galileo) aircraft online jumped 66% sequentially to 184.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Galileo: ... 111 aircraft online.”

surprises.description: Gogo 5G shipments rose 165% sequentially to 138 units, and C1 systems online reached a record 690. The preview did not set expectations for these 5G operating metrics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gogo 5G unit shipments rose 165% sequentially to 138 units, and C1 systems online hit a record 690, up 24% from Q1.”

in_line: Net leverage was 3.8x, within the preview’s base-case expectation of roughly 3.7–3.8x and below its flagged problem range of about 3.9–4.0x.

surprises.description: LifeStance reported Q2 revenue of $435 million, well above the $414.3 million consensus and above even the preview’s $425–432 million bull scenario. The preview’s base case was $416–421 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 26% year-over-year to $435 million, exceeding expectations on both higher visit volumes and revenue per visit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2'26 Consensus $414.3M”; the preview’s bull scenario was “$425–432M” and base scenario was “$416–421M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $66 million, substantially above the roughly $55 million consensus and the preview’s $60–63 million bull scenario. The 15.2% margin also exceeded the preview’s roughly 13.3% guide-implied margin and its 13%-or-more proof point.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled, rising 94% to $66 million with a margin of 15.2%, an improvement of over 500 basis points versus Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$55M (guide-anchored)”; the bull scenario was “$60–63M.” The preview said “Sustained margin of 13% or more is the key proof point” and that the guide midpoint implied “about 13.3%.”

surprises.description: The FY2026 guidance increase was more than the preview’s expected modest raise: revenue guidance rose by $45 million to $1.685–1.725 billion and adjusted EBITDA guidance by $15 million to $215–235 million. The preview’s bull case anticipated meaningful increases, but its base case was a modest raise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance across all metrics, lifting revenue by $45 million to $1.685-$1.725 billion … and adjusted EBITDA by $15 million to $215-$235 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise is the base case. … The debate is magnitude”; the base scenario called for a “Modest raise,” while the bull scenario said “Revenue and EBITDA raised meaningfully.”

surprises.description: Revenue per visit was higher than the preview’s approximate $163 base-case assumption, reaching $167, and management tightened its full-year rate outlook to mid-single-digit increases. This was a stronger rate result and outlook than the preview’s reference point suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue per visit increased 6% to $167, prompting management to narrow the full-year rate guidance from low-to-mid to mid-single-digit increases driven by payer contracting visibility.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “TRPV about $163”; the preview also noted Q1 total revenue per visit was “$163.50, up 3%.”

surprises.description: Net clinician adds were 193, below the preview’s 230–280 base-case range and just under its roughly 200-add caution threshold. The clinician base still grew 11%, but quarterly additions fell short of the preview’s expected pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The clinician base grew 11% to 8,542, with 193 net adds in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “Adds about 230–280”; the preview said “Adds below about 200 would weaken the 2027 revenue build.”

surprises.description: After deploying nearly all of the existing buyback authorization, LifeStance approved a fresh $100 million authorization. The preview noted the existing February authorization but did not anticipate a replacement authorization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board approved a new $100 million share repurchase authorization after deploying $97 million of the prior program, including $49 million in the second quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The $100M buyback was authorized in February 2026.”

in_line: Visits per average clinician rose 7% year over year for the third consecutive quarter, matching the preview’s expectation that clinician productivity would continue at about +7%.

The outlook for lower second-half adjusted EBITDA dollars was already flagged: the preview said the FY guide implied second-half dollars below first-half levels and identified EHR migration costs and de novo drag as issues to watch. The call’s Q3 guidance of $49–59 million, with second-half strategic investments weighing on EBITDA, is consistent with that concern.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $4.2 billion, above the preview’s realistic $3.75–3.90 billion range and even its $4.00–4.10 billion bull case. The preview expected a strong World Cup contribution, but the reported quarter came in materially higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fourth quarter total revenue jumped 28% to $4.2 billion,” driven by “a 78% surge in advertising revenue tied to the FIFA Men's World Cup.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s realistic revenue bar was “$3.75–3.90B”; its bull case was “$4.00–4.10B.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EPS of $1.79 substantially exceeded both the preview’s $1.40–1.50 realistic bar and the $1.34 published consensus. That is a much larger result than the preview’s already-raised expectations implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EPS increased 41% to $1.79 versus $1.27 in the prior year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited published consensus of “$1.34” and said its “realistic EPS bar” was “$1.40–1.50.”

surprises.description: Q4 EBITDA reached $1.2 billion, above the preview’s $960 million–$1.01 billion base range and its bull-case threshold of $1.10 billion or more. The preview expected World Cup EBITDA accretion, but the reported amount was stronger than its scenarios.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fourth quarter total revenue jumped 28% to $4.2 billion and EBITDA climbed 27% to $1.2 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “$960M–1.01B” adjusted EBITDA and its bull case was “$1.10B+.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EPS was $5.42, well above the preview’s $4.94 FY26 consensus. The preview did not provide a higher full-year EPS scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EPS rose 13% to $5.42.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FY26 consensus $4.94.”

surprises.description: Tubi reported a record quarter, 35% revenue growth, higher viewing time and 110 million monthly active users, while remaining EBITDA positive in every fiscal 2026 quarter. The preview did not identify these Tubi results as an expectation or debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tubi delivered its best quarter ever with 35% revenue growth and 17% higher total viewing time, closing the year with 110 million monthly active users and remaining EBITDA positive in each quarter of fiscal 2026.”

surprises.description: FOX said FOX One subscribers are largely incremental, with minimal traditional MVPD cannibalization and churn well below expectations. This directly addresses the preview’s flagged post-World Cup retention and subscriber-quality debate with favorable commentary, though no subscriber count was provided.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FOX One subscribers are proving truly incremental with minimal cannibalization of traditional MVPD customers and churn running well below expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “FOX One subscribers and post-World Cup churn” as a key issue, noting that “commentary on retention after the World Cup cohort rolls off, is a major swing factor.”

surprises.description: Digital investment losses fell to less than $200 million in FY26 from just under $300 million in FY25, with further improvement expected in FY27. The preview did not set an expectation for this loss trajectory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Digital investment losses moderated from just under $300 million in fiscal 2025 to less than $200 million in fiscal 2026, with further bottom-line improvement expected in fiscal 2027.”

surprises.description: FOX raised its semiannual dividend to $0.29. The preview discussed cumulative buybacks and the remaining authorization but did not flag a dividend increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its semiannual dividend to $0.29.”

surprises.description: The upfront showed double-digit volume growth across sports, news and Tubi, strength in 8 of 10 tracked ad categories, and momentum carrying into fiscal Q1 2027. The preview anticipated World Cup-related advertising but did not set an expectation for this broader upfront demand or its persistence.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The upfront delivered double-digit volume growth across sports, news and Tubi, with strength in 8 of the 10 tracked ad categories, and momentum continuing into fiscal Q1 2027.”

in_line: FOX expects a record midterm political cycle; the preview also flagged a record cycle and cited an estimated $11 billion in total industry spending.

The Roku acquisition is still expected to close in the first half of calendar 2027, consistent with the preview’s stated timing. The preview also identified financing, leverage and continued capital returns as issues to watch.

The preview expected the World Cup to be EBITDA-accretive at the total-company level and to split between Q4 and Q1; the reported quarter’s strong revenue and EBITDA were consistent with that direction, although the amounts exceeded the preview’s scenarios.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue guidance of $415–425 million was far above the preview’s roughly $360–365 million consensus-implied level and even above its bullish scenario threshold of $385 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 FY26 guidance calls for revenue of $415-425 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 consensus of $1.26B implies Q4 of roughly $360–365M”; the bull scenario expected “Q4 guide at or above $385M.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue and adjusted EPS both beat expectations: revenue was $342.2 million versus consensus of about $335 million, while EPS of $1.40 exceeded the $1.34–$1.35 consensus. Revenue also topped the company’s prior $331–339 million guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 FY26 revenue was $342.2 million” and “adjusted EPS of $1.40.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed revenue consensus of “$335.1M” and “$335.5M,” EPS consensus of “$1.34” and “$1.35,” and company revenue guidance of “$331–339M.”

surprises.description: The Q3 book-to-bill ratio reached 1.6:1, exceeding the preview’s 1.3x level that it said would support the FY27 outlook, and bookings set a new company record.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 book-to-bill ratio hit a record 1.6:1 with the highest quarterly bookings in company history.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “At or above 1.3x supports the FY27 consensus.”

surprises.description: Data Center is trending toward roughly 74% full-year FY26 growth, above the preview’s watchpoint of growth “toward ~70%.” Its Q3 revenue also reached a record, with about 40% sequential growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data Center revenue reached a record $137.6 million, up approximately 40% sequentially, and is trending toward roughly 74% full-year growth in FY26.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for a raise “toward ~70%.”

surprises.description: The Q4 Industrial & Defense growth outlook is about 20% sequentially, versus the preview’s estimate of roughly 10% based on management’s segment guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q4 guidance implies “20% I&D growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s build from management’s segment guidance included “~10% Industrial & Defense.”

surprises.description: The gross-margin result was close to expectations at 59.7%, but Q4 guidance of 60–61% and management’s expectation of further quarterly improvements into FY27 extend the margin path beyond the preview’s roughly 60% exit target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 120 basis points sequentially to 59.7%, with Q4 guided to 60-61% and management expecting continued 25-50 bps quarterly improvements into FY27.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “59.8% or higher” would support the margin story and noted the FY26 exit target was “closer to 60%.”

surprises.description: Management laid out a strong operating-margin trajectory—about 37% in Q4 and a target above 40% in FY27—which the preview did not quantify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin rose to 31.5% from 25.2% a year ago, and is guided to approximately 37% in Q4 with a target of breaching 40% in FY27.”

surprises.description: The company raised its 2027 serviceable-addressable-market estimate to about $15 billion, a newly disclosed market-opportunity update not covered in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its 2027 SAM estimate to approximately $15 billion … up 20-30% from 2026.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a $61 million investment in IQE and a $41 million noncash GAAP gain from it, excluded from non-GAAP results; the preview did not flag this investment or gain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Having made a $61 million investment in IQE that generated a $41 million noncash GAAP gain excluded from non-GAAP results.”

in_line: Q4 Data Center sequential growth of about 35% matched the preview’s segment-guidance build of roughly 35%.
The annualized Q4 guidance midpoint implies FY27 company growth of roughly 27–28%, broadly consistent with the preview’s FY27 consensus growth implied by $1.60B revenue versus $1.26B in FY26.
Q3 adjusted gross margin of 59.7% was within the prior 59.0–60.0% guidance range and close to the preview’s approximately 59.5% consensus.

surprises.description: Revenue was $176.1 million, well above the $143.9 million consensus estimate and even above the preview’s $165 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 14% year-over-year to $176.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus” revenue was “$143.9M”; the bull scenario was “$165M+.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS of $1.77 exceeded the preview’s $1.50+ bull-case threshold, although reported GAAP EPS was slightly below the $0.79 consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income was $38.7 million ($1.77 adjusted diluted EPS)” and “net income of $16.8 million ($0.77 diluted EPS).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull scenario listed “Adj. EPS” of “$1.50+”; consensus EPS was “$0.79.”

surprises.description: Centrus raised its 2026 Piketon hiring target from over 100 to over 175 net new employees, a stronger workforce expansion plan than the preview discussed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Centrus raised its 2026 Piketon workforce addition guidance from over 100 to over 175 net new employees.”

surprises.description: More than $3 billion of customer LEU and HALEU contracts no longer had financing contingencies, with $2.4 billion of enrichment backlog under definitive agreements—more certainty than the preview’s general call to watch for backlog additions conveyed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company removed all financing contingencies on its more than $3 billion in customer LEU and HALEU contracts, of which $2.4 billion in enrichment backlog are now under definitive agreements.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “backlog additions” among the items to watch, without anticipating removal of financing contingencies or giving an expected amount.

surprises.description: Centrus disclosed a definitive HALEU offtake contract with X-energy and an Oklo letter of intent covering up to five Aurora powerhouses, both with nondilutive prepayments—specific new commercial arrangements not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed a definitive HALEU offtake contract with X-energy and a letter of intent with Oklo to supply up to five Aurora powerhouses starting in 2029, both structured to include nondilutive prepayments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “backlog additions” and “any new capital-raise commentary,” but did not identify these agreements or prepayments.

surprises.description: Centrus said it expects to complete its first Oak Ridge centrifuge in 2026, adding a specific manufacturing milestone to the preview’s discussion of the centrifuge build and its costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects to complete its first centrifuge at the Oak Ridge facility in 2026, a first-of-a-kind U.S. manufacturing milestone toward commercial enrichment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed advanced technology costs tied to “the Oak Ridge centrifuge build” but did not state a 2026 first-centrifuge completion milestone.

surprises.description: The company did use its ATM, raising $53.9 million, despite the preview’s warning that any new raise would be negative; however, it characterized the use as opportunistic and said it was sufficiently funded for near-term capital needs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Centrus ended Q2 with $1.9 billion in unrestricted cash, using its ATM only opportunistically for $53.9 million in proceeds, and stated it is sufficiently funded for near-term capital requirements.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “any signal of a new raise,” calling it “a clear negative.”

in_line: Centrus reaffirmed FY2026 revenue guidance of $450–500 million, as the preview described as the baseline expectation.
Centrus reaffirmed capital-spending guidance of $350–500 million, matching the existing FY2026 range cited in the preview.
GAAP diluted EPS of $0.77 was close to the preview’s $0.79 consensus estimate.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $54.0 million, above the preview’s $49.35 million consensus. The beat was driven primarily by about $8.4 million of GreenWave environmental-attribute revenue, rather than just the underlying business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenues rose 19.7% to $54.0 million” and were “driven primarily by ~$8.4 million in environmental attribute revenues from GreenWave RIN distributions and pathway dispensing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $49.35M”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $12.3 million, above the preview’s estimated $9–11 million range, exceeding even its high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA surged 144.5% to $12.3 million versus $5.0 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$9–11M”

surprises.description: The electricity outlook was materially lower than the ranges cited in the preview: $23–26 million of revenue versus $33–37 million, and 185,000–195,000 MWh versus 195,000–207,000 MWh. Although the call described guidance as reaffirmed, these figures are below the preview’s stated prior guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Montauk reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of … 185,000-195,000 MWh renewable electricity production ($23-26 million revenue).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “renewable electricity 195–207k MWh; REG revenue $33–37M”

surprises.description: RNG commodity revenue fell sharply as lower-price fixed-contract volumes expired, a deterioration not reflected in the preview’s revenue expectations. The overall revenue beat therefore coexisted with a steep decline in this revenue stream.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RNG commodity revenue fell approximately 63.7% as fixed lower-price contract volumes declined about 80% due to contract expirations, partly offset by a 29.1% increase in RINs sold.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $49.35M” and “RINs sold ≈ generated.”

surprises.description: The preview expected some Q2 contribution from the North Carolina facility, including $2–3 million in its base case, but the call said power sales began only in July and switch-gear modifications were still expected to finish in mid-August. That points to a later start to consistent generation and sales than the preview’s Q2 ramp scenario assumed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company began generating power for sale from its Turkey, North Carolina … facility in July 2026,” with switch-gear programming modifications expected to be completed “by mid-August” to enable consistent REC and power generation.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 is the first quarter with NC revenue, and only two months of it”; base scenario: “NC $2–3M.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that it had already committed the majority of Q3 RNG production RINs at an average of $2.66. The preview said there was no RIN-price guidance, so this adds forward pricing and sales visibility, although the price was roughly in line with the July index rather than a premium to it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has committed to transfer the majority of Q3 2026 RNG production RINs at an average price of $2.66, roughly in line with July's D3 index price of $2.64.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “No EPS or RIN-price guidance.”

surprises.description: Net income turned slightly positive at $0.2 million, versus the preview’s expected GAAP loss. The sign was better than expected, though the absolute difference was small.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income turned positive at $0.2 million compared to a $5.5 million net loss in Q2 2025.”

in_line: RNG production and revenue guidance were reaffirmed at 5.8–6.0 million MMBtu and $175–190 million, matching the preview’s stated ranges.
Q2 realized RIN pricing was $2.45, close to the preview’s expectation of about $2.42 and within its anticipated roughly $2.40 range.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $2.37, well above the $1.84 Q2 consensus cited in the preview. The roughly 29% beat was much larger than the revenue beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS increased 48% to $2.37.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | Consensus (Q2) | $1.84.”

surprises.description: Royalty revenue was $48 million, below the preview’s $55 million level that it said would support the full-year guide and well below its implied $57–65 million quarterly pace. It was just above the preview’s $47 million-or-less risk threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 royalty revenue grew 32% year-over-year to $48 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Royalty of $55M or more would support the guide. Royalty at or below $47M would put the low end in question”; the preview also said the guide implied “about $57–65M per quarter.”

surprises.description: Total revenue beat the preview’s consensus by $2.6 million, or about 4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose 34% to $64 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Consensus (Q2) | $61.4M.”

surprises.description: Ligand raised the low end of its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $9.00 from $8.50, while leaving the $9.50 high end unchanged. The preview identified a possible guidance raise as a bullish outcome, but the increase was limited to the low end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ligand raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance low end to $9.00 … maintaining the $9.50 upper end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 adjusted EPS guidance of “$8.50–$9.50” and said “A raise to the upper half of the range … would be the main bullish trigger.”

surprises.description: The XOMA integration is expected to reduce the acquired business’s annual operating expenses from about $30 million to under $5 million, capturing virtually all anticipated cost synergies—an efficiency detail not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “XOMA integration is expected to cut acquired annual operating expenses from about $30 million to under $5 million, capturing virtually all anticipated cost synergies.”

surprises.description: Ligand disclosed more than $110 million of XOMA Section 174 tax credits and NOLs and said operating cash flow is expected to rise from over $200 million in 2026 to $300 million in 2027. The preview did not discuss these tax attributes or this cash-flow outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The acquisition brings over $110 million in Section 174 tax credits and NOLs to be utilized over 3-5 years, helping drive operating cash flow from over $200 million in 2026 to an expected $300 million in 2027.”

surprises.description: After the financing and XOMA acquisition, Ligand said it still had about $700 million of deployable capital and set an annual investment pace of $100–125 million to support perpetual growth. The preview noted the financing and acquisition but gave no expectation for remaining capital or deployment pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Post-financing and acquisition, Ligand retains approximately $700 million of deployable capital, with a target investment pace of $100-125 million annually needed for perpetual growth.”

surprises.description: The acquired XOMA portfolio adds over 120 assets and about $2.3 billion in publicly disclosed potential milestone opportunities, a scale of contingent upside not covered in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The acquired XOMA portfolio adds over 120 assets and approximately $2.3 billion in publicly disclosed potential milestone opportunities.”

surprises.description: Ligand also disclosed a Tremfya contingent value right entitling it to 25% of any net litigation proceeds, with no downside exposure; this potential source of upside was not mentioned in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A Tremfya contingent value right entitling Ligand to 25% of any net litigation proceeds with no downside exposure.”

surprises.description: Management said up to seven pivotal trial readouts could arrive over the next 18 months, while cautioning that not all may be positive. The preview did not flag this unusually catalyst-rich period.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ligand faces one of its most catalyst-rich periods with up to 7 pivotal trial readouts over the next 18 months, though management cautioned not all will be positive.”

surprises.description: The timeline for Mirum’s volixibat PSC program slipped after the FDA recommended a Phase III study at the pre-NDA meeting. The preview did not flag this setback.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mirum's volixibat PSC timeline slipped after the FDA recommended a Phase III study at the pre-NDA meeting.”

in_line: Ligand reiterated expected XOMA adjusted EPS contributions of roughly $0.50 in H2 2026 and approximately $1.50 in 2027; the preview specifically said to watch for those figures to be reiterated.
Filspari’s strong sales growth was consistent with the preview’s note that it had grown strongly in Q2; the preview also said partner sales were already public before it was written.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $1.25B, above the preview’s $1.19B–$1.21B consensus range and the preview’s bull-case threshold of $1.24B. The result was also reported at the high end or above company guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $1.25 billion” and results were “at the high end or above guidance ranges.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue… Consensus: $1.19B – $1.21B”; the bull scenario expected “≥ $1.24B.”

surprises.description: Reported Q2 diluted EPS of $3.30 was well above the preview’s $2.93–$2.94 consensus and exceeded the high end of guidance. The preview labels its consensus measure non-GAAP EPS, while the call fact describes net earnings per diluted share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net earnings were $232 million or $3.30 per diluted share… exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS… Consensus: $2.93 – $2.94.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $1.35B was materially above the preview’s roughly $1.26B base-case expectation and above its $1.30B bull-case threshold, indicating stronger near-term growth than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $1.35 billion (±$40M).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected Q3 revenue of “~ $1.26B,” while the bull scenario expected “≥ $1.30B.”

surprises.description: The Q3 semiconductor outlook points to year-over-year growth above 50%, versus the preview’s roughly $600M whisper benchmark and concern that a guide below roughly $590M could signal deceleration. The call also said this growth would substantially outpace estimated WFE growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance implies semi YoY growth accelerating to over 50%, well ahead of estimated WFE growth of 25-30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Q3 semiconductor guidance” against “a roughly $600M whisper” and said a guide “below roughly $590M” could be read as deceleration.

surprises.description: Electronics & Packaging revenue reached $381M, above the preview’s $350M ± $15M guidance benchmark and its expectation of growth above 30% year over year. The reported strongest-ever chemistry equipment demand and visibility through 2027 also go beyond the preview’s expectation of durable advanced-PCB and AI-related demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Electronics & Packaging revenue rose to $381 million (up 44% YoY), with chemistry equipment demand described as the strongest ever and visibility now extending through 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Electronics & Packaging | $350M ± $15M” and said it was “Guided above 30% YoY growth” on advanced PCB and AI-related demand.

surprises.description: Q3 gross margin was guided to 47%, below the preview’s 48% guide expectation. The call attributed expected quarterly pressure to factory ramp costs, a headwind the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 gross margin is guided to 47% (±100bps)” and “50-80bps of quarterly headwind” is expected from factory ramp costs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a “48% Q3 guide” would support the multiple and listed “a Q3 margin guide of 48%” in its catalyst checklist.

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin came in at 47.6%, above the preview’s roughly 47% expectation, but the call said about 100 basis points came from discrete benefits, mainly tariff and duty refunds. That makes the reported beat less reflective of underlying margin performance than the headline suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 gross margin is guided to 47%… down from Q2's reported 47.6% which included roughly 100bps of discrete benefits mainly from tariff/duty refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 gross margin guidance of “47.0% ± 100bp” and said the key issue was gross margin “against the 47% level.”

surprises.description: Leverage fell to 3.0x, ahead of the preview’s expectation of about 3.2x and below its 3.3x catalyst threshold. The company also announced additional planned term-loan prepayments beyond the $100M prepayment made that week.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Leverage declined to 3x… (down a full turn YoY), with a $100 million term loan prepayment made this week and additional prepayments planned for Q3 and Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected leverage to move “from 3.5x toward about 3.2x” and flagged “Net leverage below 3.3x and any new term loan prepayment.”

surprises.description: AI-related applications now account for 15–20% of chemistry revenue, above the company’s prior 10% guidance cited on the call. The preview discussed AI-related demand but did not anticipate this higher share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI-related applications now represent 15-20% of chemistry revenue, up from 5% in 2024 and 10% in prior guidance.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a larger capacity ambition than previously guided: Penang can support WFE of $200–250B, and Guangzhou chemistry-equipment capacity is being doubled. The preview flagged capacity updates and 2027 WFE framing but did not anticipate these specific expansion plans or the higher supported WFE range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is doubling capacity at its Guangzhou chemistry equipment factory (online Q3 2027)” and plans for Penang “can support WFE in the $200-250 billion range, an increase from prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist flagged “Malaysia and China capacity updates; any 2027 WFE framing.”

surprises.description: Specialty Industrial revenue was slightly above the preview’s guided range, reaching $313M versus a $300M ± $10M benchmark. The call also described it as the highest level since 2023, driven by datacom and defense.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Specialty Industrial revenue grew to $313 million (up 14% YoY), the highest since 2023, driven by datacom and defense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Specialty Industrial | $300M ± $10M.”

in_line: Q2 semiconductor revenue was $554M, broadly in line with the preview’s $550M ± $15M company-guidance benchmark.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $0.7 million, well below the $3.99 million consensus estimate. The reported amount was only INPEFA sales, with no Q2 licensing revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenues fell to $0.7 million (INPEFA net sales)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 2026 Consensus | $3.99M”

surprises.description: The Zynquista resubmission is now expected by the end of October rather than mid-2026, and a standard review would put an FDA decision in Q2 2027 rather than the preview’s potential 2026 approval window. Management will seek expedited review, but did not say it had been granted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “resubmitting its Zynquista NDA … by the end of October 2026, a slight delay from a previously guided mid-2026 timeline”; a standard six-month review “would place a decision in Q2 2027,” though the company will seek expedited review.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “resubmission ‘mid-2026’ with potential approval ‘in 2026’”

surprises.description: The loss per share was $0.07 versus the $0.05 loss expected. The quarter included an unanticipated $4.3 million loss on early debt extinguishment, equal to $0.01 per share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss was $31.8 million ($0.07 per share)” and included “a $4.3 million loss ($0.01 per share) on early extinguishment of debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS | Q2 2026 Consensus | −$0.05”

surprises.description: Cash and short-term investments were about $10 million above the preview’s approximate Q2 cash expectation, and the company disclosed a new $100 million Hercules debt facility versus the preview’s reference to $45 million of undrawn Hercules tranches. This provides somewhat more liquidity than the preview anticipated, although the facility is debt rather than cash.
surprises.fact_evidence: Lexicon held “$190.6 million in cash and short-term investments” and was aided by “a new $100 million Hercules Capital debt facility.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 cash is expected near $181M, plus $45M of undrawn Hercules tranches.”

surprises.description: The call added a favorable STENO1 update not anticipated in the preview: the study is expected to reach the FDA-required sotagliflozin exposure levels by the end of August, with DKA rates similar to standard care and below those in the earlier inTandem trials.
surprises.fact_evidence: “STENO1 study is expected to achieve the FDA-required sotagliflozin exposure levels by the end of August 2026, with DKA rates similar to standard of care and well below those in the earlier inTandem trials.”

in_line: SONATA-HCM enrollment was already described in the preview as substantially exceeding its 500-patient target, and the Q1 2027 topline timing was expected; the call reaffirmed that timing.
The preview identified a possible third $10 million Novo Nordisk milestone later in 2026; the call likewise said Lexicon could receive one later this year.

surprises.description: NACCO was modeled to earn about $0.70 per share, but it reported a $0.13 loss per share and a $2.3 million consolidated operating loss after recording $12 million of solar-development impairments. The impairment-driven reversal to a quarterly loss was a large downside gap to the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NACCO recorded $12 million in solar development impairment charges tied to two REGEN Resources projects, driving a consolidated operating loss of $2.3 million and a net loss of $1 million (13 cents per share)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | ~$0.70 (range $0.55–$0.85) | Modeled; no consensus found”

surprises.description: The preview expected meaningful consolidated year-over-year improvement, but management now expects full-year operating profit and net income to fall below 2025 levels. Management also warned of possible additional solar curtailment or impairment charges in the second half, making the outlook materially worse than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects full-year 2026 operating profit and net income to fall below 2025 levels due to the solar charges”; it also warned of “possible additional curtailment or impairment charges in the second half of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 outlook: ‘Meaningful year-over-year improvement’ at consolidated level; H2 growth to ‘moderate’”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA came in well above the modeled $11.5 million, rising 72% year over year to $15.9 million. This was a substantial beat even though the metric excludes the solar impairment charges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated adjusted EBITDA, which excludes the solar charges, rose 72% year-over-year to $15.9 million from $9.3 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$11.5M (+24% YoY) | None quarterly [company guidance]”

surprises.description: NACCO disclosed delayed customer payments at Mississippi Lignite Mining Company and said it is actively pursuing remedies, with caution about collection timing and inventory valuation. The preview did not flag this customer-payment and valuation risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Actively pursuing remedies for delayed payments” from the customer under a contract running from 1995 to 2032, with “caution around collection timing and inventory valuation.”

surprises.description: Minerals and Royalties operating profit rose to $6.7 million, while the preview highlighted a decline as the key expectation for the segment. Higher oil prices and a 46% jump in royalty revenues more than offset the production-related concerns in the reported quarter, although management still expects a second-half decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Minerals and royalties operating profit increased to $6.7 million from $5.2 million, aided by a 46% jump in royalty revenues from higher oil prices”; management expects profits to decline in H2.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Minerals & Royalties decline. Guided lower on gas production declines.”

surprises.description: Contract Mining operating profit was $3.8 million, above the preview’s $3.5 million watch level, with revenue net of reimbursed costs up 34%. The reported drivers were the Palm Beach County dragline services contract and higher limestone deliveries.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Contract mining operating profit rose to $3.8 million from $1.0 million on a 34% increase in revenues net of reimbursed costs, driven by the Palm Beach County dragline services contract and higher limestone deliveries.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Contract Mining OP at or above $3.5M, with evidence Florida is margin-positive.”

surprises.description: Utility Coal operating profit was $6.3 million versus the modeled $6.0 million, a modest beat. The result came despite a significant unplanned power-plant outage, with reclamation costs charged to the balance sheet rather than the income statement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Utility coal mining operating profit surged to $6.3 million from $1.2 million” as the company shifted resources to reclamation during an outage, “charging costs to the balance sheet rather than the income statement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating profit | Utility Coal OP to rise meaningfully for FY26, ‘primarily in the first half of 2026’ | ~$6.0M”

surprises.description: Revenue was $72.3 million, modestly above the preview’s modeled $70 million, with strong performance across all reportable segments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated revenues increased 6% to $72.3 million from $68.2 million, with strong performance across all reportable segments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$70M (+3% YoY) | No Street figure found”

surprises.description: The preview cited capex of up to $57 million for the balance of 2026, while management said it plans to invest up to $35 million in the remainder of the year and only if opportunities meet its capital criteria. That is a lower and more conditional spending plan than the preview indicated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Plans to invest up to $35 million in the remainder of the year only if opportunities meet its capital criteria.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capex of up to $57M over the balance of 2026.”

in_line: The preview’s expectation that second-half growth would moderate was echoed for adjusted EBITDA: management expects it to improve year over year, but with moderating growth in the second half.
Debt was below the preview’s roughly $140 million watch level: NACCO reported $120.1 million of outstanding debt, down from $126.4 million at Q1.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $57 million came in above the preview’s $50.0–$52.1 million consensus range, a modest beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue fell to $57 million” from $239 million a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (Q2) … $50.0M … or $52.1M.”

surprises.description: Novavax raised its full-year adjusted revenue guidance by $5 million at the midpoint, rather than merely reiterating the existing range. The increase was small relative to the prior midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 adjusted revenue guidance to $235-$275 million ($255 million midpoint), a $5 million midpoint increase.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 adjusted revenue guidance of “$230–270M” and described the base scenario as “guide reiterated.”

surprises.description: The expected $75 million Sanofi tech-transfer milestone would extend the cash runway into 2029, beyond the preview’s expectation that runway language would remain “into 2028.”
surprises.fact_evidence: “The expected $75 million Sanofi tech transfer milestone would extend the company's cash runway from 2028 into 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management’s funding covered operations “into 2028” and listed unchanged “into 2028” runway language as the expectation.

surprises.description: Sanofi offered additional favorable commercial signals: it intends to be among the first movers in the COVID-flu combination market, is in advanced regulatory discussions on Phase III timing, and is expanding Nuvaxovid launches into three countries. The preview flagged Phase III timing as uncertain and expected Nuvaxovid sales near zero in the seasonal trough, though these launch plans do not establish Q2 sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sanofi confirmed intent to be among the first movers in the COVID-flu combination market” and is “in advanced regulatory discussions on Phase III timing”; Nuvaxovid launches are expanding into “the UK, Germany, and Canada this season.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Sanofi CIC (COVID-flu combo) Phase III timing” as a key issue and its base case expected “Nuvaxovid sales near zero (Q2 is the seasonal trough).”

in_line: The $75 million Sanofi tech-transfer milestone was not reported as a Q2 event and is expected in 2027, consistent with the preview’s inference that it might fall outside FY26 and its scenario that it could be pushed to 2027.

surprises.description: Q1 revenue was $210.4 million, well above the preview’s $196.2–200.1 million consensus range and its $194–198 million implied guide. The reported 12.7% growth also exceeded the preview’s mid-single-digit growth setup.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 total revenue rose 12.7% year-over-year to $210.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $196.2M (+5.0% YoY)” and “Revenue | $200.1M (+7.2% YoY)”; the preview also gave an “Implied Q1 guide” of “$194–198M revenue.”

surprises.description: The $10–15 million order pull-forward means the strong Q1 growth was partly a timing benefit rather than a higher underlying growth rate; management said normalized growth would have been mid-single-digits. Q2 is expected to be roughly flat year over year, a near-term slowdown the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly $10-15 million of primarily government-related orders were pulled into Q1,” and “normalized growth would have been mid-single-digits”; “Q2 revenue is expected to be roughly flat versus the prior-year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview framed Q1 as growing “mid-single digits” and described the base case as a “modest beat” with FY27 guidance reaffirmed; it did not forecast a Q2 flat comparison or a Q1 order pull-forward.

surprises.description: Operating margin reached 20.8%, far above the preview’s roughly 14.5% estimate for Q1. The preview expected Q1 to be the seasonal low point, but reported margin instead expanded substantially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating margin expanded 660 basis points to 20.8%,” reflecting “favorable product mix and disciplined expense management.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus EPS of $0.38 implies roughly flat to slightly higher margin at about 14.5%”; “Q1 is seasonally the low point.”

surprises.description: Reported EPS of $0.52 exceeded the preview’s range of $0.35–0.39, a much larger result than the expected roughly $0.40–0.44 base scenario. The preview characterized a typical print as a modest beat, not a result this far above its estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS [jumped] to $0.52 from $0.34 a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed non-GAAP EPS estimates of “$0.38,” “$0.39,” and “$0.35,” and a base scenario of “$0.40–0.44.”

surprises.description: Cybersecurity grew only 0.6%, despite the preview highlighting organic cybersecurity growth as a key test and warning that growth below 8% would weaken the DDoS narrative. The reported growth was particularly soft against a prior-year comparison of roughly 18%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cybersecurity grew only 0.6% against a tough prior-year comparison that had grown ~18%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sub-8% organic growth would undercut the AI-era DDoS narrative behind the stock's rally.”

surprises.description: Federal government revenue surged to the mid-teens as a share of Q1 revenue, versus its typical mid-to-high single-digit share. That is a sharper concentration than the preview’s discussion of federal revenue running at the high end and monitoring for normalization suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Federal government revenue, typically mid-to-high single-digit percent of total, spiked to mid-teens percent of revenue in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Federal ran at ‘the high end’ in FY26, and management said it is monitoring for normalization.”

surprises.description: The company reported adding about $7 million of inventory to secure hardware amid AI data-center-driven supply constraints. The preview had described the earlier backlog build as driven by late-quarter orders rather than supply constraints, so the new supply-chain-related stocking was not anticipated there.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory rose about $7 million as the company proactively secured hardware amid AI data-center-driven supply chain constraints.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management attributed the backlog build to “late-quarter order intake, not supply constraints.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed FY2027 revenue guidance of $885–915 million and non-GAAP EPS guidance of $2.65–2.80, consistent with the preview’s base case that guidance would be reaffirmed rather than raised.
Gross margin was 80.6%, close to the preview’s 80.8% reference point.
The Arbor Cloud mitigation capacity increase to 33 terabits per second was already noted in the preview.

surprises.description: Q3 home-closing gross margin is guided to 16%–16.5%, below the roughly 17.3% the preview said was needed to support Q3 estimates. This is a clear deterioration from the margin level the market was watching for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for a sharp step-down to just 16%–16.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 consensus embeds a 16% sequential revenue ramp and EPS more than triple Q2 consensus. That requires about 880 closings and margin stabilization”; the preview also calls out “Q3 gross margin guide versus the ~17.3% needed.”

surprises.description: Q2 diluted EPS was $0.03, well below the preview’s live consensus estimate of $0.08. The thin $1.9 million pretax profit and $1.4 million adjusted net income underscore the earnings shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income $1.8 million, or $0.03 per diluted share”; “adjusted net income dropping to $1.4 million from $12.9 million a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “I treat $0.08 as the live number.”

surprises.description: The Q3 closing and ASP outlook implies roughly $260 million–$288 million of home-closing revenue, below the preview’s $291.1 million Q3 consensus. The top end of the closing range does not make up for the lower projected ASP.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects 825–900 closings and a lower average sales price of $315,000–$320,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 2026 consensus is $0.18 EPS and $291.1M revenue”; the preview says Q3 consensus “requires about 880 closings.”

surprises.description: Incentive-related costs rose to 780 basis points from 730 basis points in Q1, rather than stabilizing, and management expects further increases in Q3. That weakens the prospect of a margin floor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Incentive-related costs … jumped to 780 basis points from … 730 bps sequentially, and management expects them to rise further in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “flat or down suggests the margin trough is in” and “up again suggests no floor.”

surprises.description: Q2 closings and revenue beat the preview’s consensus ranges: 839 closings versus about 765–780, and $273 million of revenue versus $255.8 million–$258.1 million. The volume beat drove a stronger top line than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 home closing revenue rose 22% year-over-year to $273 million on 839 closings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Home closings ~765–780”; “Revenue $255.8M … or $258.1M.”

surprises.description: Net new orders reached 970, substantially above the preview’s roughly 800-order whisper. This was a stronger demand result than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net new home orders grew 32% year-over-year to 970.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net orders versus ~800 whisper.”

surprises.description: Q2 average sales price was $325,000, below the preview’s roughly $328,000 expectation. The revenue and closing beat therefore came despite weaker pricing than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “839 closings … at an average sales price of $325,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ASP ~$328K (derived).”

surprises.description: The company recorded $3.1 million of inventory impairments and $4.5 million of lot-option abandonment charges, costs the preview had not flagged. These charges added to the quarter’s earnings pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company took $3.1 million in inventory impairments across three communities and $4.5 million in lot option abandonment charges during the quarter.”

surprises.description: Despite Q2 gross margin of 17.6%, adjusted EBITDA fell to $13.4 million from $19.8 million a year earlier, indicating weaker earnings conversion than the preview’s modeled Q2 outcomes implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined to $13.4 million (4.9% of revenue) from $19.8 million (8.8%) in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Q2 scenarios modeled EPS of about $0.05 in the base case and about $0.09 in the bull case; the live consensus was $0.08.

in_line: Q2 home-closing gross margin was 17.6%, close to the preview’s roughly 17.3% consensus estimate and broadly consistent with the guided range of 17.0%–17.5%.
The company did not reinstate full-year guidance; the preview noted there was no current FY guide after its withdrawal in April.

surprises.description: Q1 revenue was $265.7 million, well above the preview’s $249.7 million consensus and even its bull-case threshold of $253 million. The gap was large, though the preview cautioned that published consensus was stale and did not reflect the acquisitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue rose 6.5% to $265.7 million” and “beating internal sales and earnings expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $249.7M”; the bull scenario was “At or above $253M.”

surprises.description: Organic revenue grew 3.2%, rather than being flat to modestly negative as the preview considered a plausible Q1 outcome. This was a substantially stronger underlying result than the preview’s cautious expectation, beyond the acquisition-influenced headline revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Organic growth of 3.2% excluding FX and the Breathe Right acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Flat to modestly negative organic would be a weak result against that comp”; the base scenario expected “Organic -2% to -4%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.98, beating the preview’s $0.88–$0.89 consensus and its bull-case threshold of $0.93. That also contrasts with the preview’s implied expectation of a year-over-year decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased approximately 3% year-over-year to $0.98.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | $0.88 (MarketBeat) or $0.89 (other feed)”; the preview said this “implies about a 7.5% Y/Y decline.”

surprises.description: Management said retailer order timing added about 2 percentage points to Q1 growth and would reverse in Q2, leading to a modest organic revenue decline in that quarter. The preview did not flag this near-term reversal, so Q1’s strong growth comes with a weaker-than-anticipated Q2 cadence.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retailer order timing added about 2 points of growth in Q1 and is expected to reverse in Q2, prompting guidance for a modest organic revenue decline in the second quarter.”

surprises.description: Clear Eyes remains supply-constrained, and management described its recovery as multiyear, with output improving only in the second half of FY27. The preview expected the H2 line ramp, but did not anticipate the explicit multiyear recovery outlook or that Clear Eyes had fallen below 3% of sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Clear Eyes remained supply-constrained and now represents less than 3% of total sales”; management expects “improving output only in the second half of fiscal 2027 and a multiyear recovery.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management says the incremental line is a back-half FY27 story, so confirmation of the H2 ramp matters more than the Q1 number.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted free-cash-flow guidance increased to at least $270 million, up from the prior guide of at least $250 million. The preview cited the $250 million guide and did not anticipate this higher target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance was raised to at least $270 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FCF of at least $250M.”

surprises.description: Breathe Right’s annualized accretion is expected to be about $0.25, but the near-term stub period will contribute a couple of pennies less because of sales timing, A&M commitments, and debt paydown. The preview did not discuss this near-term accretion shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Breathe Right is expected to deliver about $0.25 of annualized accretion, though the near-term stub period will run a couple of pennies below that due to timing of sales, A&M commitments, and debt paydown.”
