in_line: The full-year revenue and EPS guidance increase was driven by the recently closed acquisitions, consistent with the preview’s warning that any update would likely include acquired revenue; the preview also cautioned that its published FY27 consensus did not reflect those acquisitions.
The projected year-end leverage just below 4x was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of about 4.0x net leverage around the Breathe Right acquisition.

surprises.description: The preview estimated Q2 cash at about $90–94 million and described at least $95 million as a bull-case level. The company reported $100.4 million of cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash at June 30, above that estimate, although the expected runway into 2028 was reaffirmed rather than extended.
surprises.fact_evidence: “cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash totaling $100.4 million as of June 30, 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Estimated Q2 cash is about $90–94M”; bull scenario: “cash at or above $95M.”

surprises.description: The preview did not set an expectation for new OCU410 efficacy results, focusing instead on Phase 3 readiness. The call reported a statistically significant 31% reduction in geographic-atrophy lesion growth and 27% ellipsoid-zone preservation in Phase 2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “OCU410 delivered a statistically significant 31% reduction in GA lesion growth … roughly twice the benefit of approved complement inhibitors from a single injection, plus 27% ellipsoid zone preservation.”

surprises.description: The preview said R&D should step up as the trials progressed; instead, Q2 R&D was $10.7 million, down from $11.3 million in Q1. The quarter’s total operating expenses also fell from Q1’s $19.4 million to $17.9 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total operating expenses rose to $17.9 million … with R&D of $10.7 million”; preview’s Q1 figures were R&D of $11.3 million and G&A of $8.1 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With liMeliGhT fully enrolled (n=140), GARDian3 fully enrolled (n=63), and the OCU410 Phase 3 starting in Q3, R&D should step up. A flat R&D line would be a warning on Phase 3 readiness.”

surprises.description: Q2 loss per share was $0.07, one cent worse than the preview’s $0.06 loss consensus. The preview cautioned that note interest or a debt-extinguishment loss could push EPS below consensus, but the reported figure still missed that estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “a net loss of $0.07 per share versus $0.05 the prior year.”

surprises.description: The preview discussed the expected OCU400 and OCU410ST BLA paths, but did not flag a target for three submissions. The call set a broader goal of three BLA submissions by 2028 and described the first half of 2027 as a catalyst-rich period with top-line data expected from both OCU400 and OCU410ST.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is targeting three BLA submissions by 2028, positioning the first half of 2027 as a catalyst-rich window with top-line data expected from both OCU400 and OCU410ST.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described OCU400’s rolling BLA as expected to “initiate in Q3 2026 and complete in Q2 2027” and OCU410ST’s BLA submission as expected “mid-2027”; it did not mention a three-BLA target.

surprises.description: The preview described the OCU410ST interim analysis as triggered when 24 of 63 participants reached eight-month follow-up. The call instead described an interim outcome decision based on the first 50% of participants; the Q3 timing remained as expected, but the reported decision group differs from the preview’s stated trigger.
surprises.fact_evidence: “an interim outcome decision on the first 50% of subjects expected in Q3 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Triggered when 24 of 63 enrolled subjects reach 8-month follow-up. Readout guided for Q3 2026.”

surprises.description: The preview identified the Root Pharmaceutical MENA term sheet but did not mention a potential priority-review-voucher sale or the Janus Henderson warrants as funding options. The call added those possible sources of capital, while neither represents cash already raised.
surprises.fact_evidence: “a potential priority review voucher sale valued at $100-200 million, 10 million Janus Henderson warrants at $1.50 (expiring August 2027) that could raise ~$15 million, and a MENA licensing term sheet with Root Pharmaceutical.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the Roots term sheet and said non-dilutive ex-US licensing was the bull case’s “answer to dilution”; it did not mention the voucher or warrants.

in_line: Runway guidance remained “into 2028,” consistent with the preview’s expected runway language; the $130 million convertible notes financing had already closed before Q2 ended.
OCU400 remained on its expected timeline: enrollment was complete and top-line Limelight data are expected in Q1 2027, as the preview anticipated.
OCU410ST remained on the expected broad timeline: enrollment/dosing was complete, the interim decision is expected in Q3 2026, and top-line data are expected in Q2 2027.
OCU410’s Phase 3 start remained targeted for Q3 2026, and RMAT designation was already reported in the preview as granted July 29.
The Root Pharmaceutical MENA arrangement was still described as a term sheet; the preview noted the definitive-agreement window ran until about mid-October 2026.

surprises.description: The preview said investors still wanted clarity on relutrigine’s FDA review, including whether an advisory committee or inspection was planned. Praxis reported that neither program had efficacy-related significant issues, that the FDA did not plan advisory committee meetings, and that the BIMO inspection of both programs ended with no findings or Form 483.
surprises.fact_evidence: “For both ulixacaltamide and relutrigine, the FDA completed mid-cycle communications, identified no efficacy-related significant issues, and stated it does not plan to hold advisory committee meetings”; the BIMO inspection “concluded with no findings and no Form 483 issued.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether “label negotiations or an inspection are underway, and whether an advisory committee is planned,” and said to “Confirm no advisory committee and no FDA information request in disguise.”

surprises.description: Against the preview’s expectation of a decision on the paused vormatrigine program, Praxis said it plans to restart redesigned POWER2 and POWER3 trials. That supplies a path forward, although the preview had already noted that a restart could salvage the program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The vormatrigine POWER1 trial missed its primary endpoint … but hit a key secondary endpoint … prompting redesigned POWER2 and POWER3 trials to restart by Q4 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Street expects a decision”; the preview described a restart as a possible way to salvage the program and said the base case was a decision “by year-end.”

surprises.description: Praxis disclosed that about one in five ulixacaltamide patients has early tolerability issues and is pursuing label titration instructions to help patients persist. The preview flagged label discussion and launch readiness but did not identify this tolerability issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “About 20% of patients” experience “early tolerability issues that resolve with continued use,” and Praxis is seeking “a titration approach in the label to improve persistence.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “any label discussion,” but did not forecast early tolerability problems.

surprises.description: The call gives relutrigine’s new PDUFA date as December 27, 2025, whereas the preview gave December 27, 2026. As reported, the dates conflict and the call’s date is already past relative to the August 2026 release, so the timing implication is unclear.
surprises.fact_evidence: Relutrigine is described as “carrying a new PDUFA date of December 27, 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says the PDUFA date moved to “Dec 27, 2026” and lists “Dec 27, 2026” as the upcoming date.

surprises.description: Praxis added that relutrigine and elsunersen are eligible for pediatric review vouchers, a potential regulatory benefit not raised in the preview. Eligibility is not the same as receiving a voucher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Both relutrigine and elsunersen are eligible for pediatric review vouchers.”

in_line: Cash and marketable securities were $1.4 billion and management reiterated runway into 2028, consistent with the preview’s cash and runway baseline.
Ulixacaltamide’s expected approval by January is consistent with the preview’s January 29, 2027 PDUFA target.
Praxis’s approximately $10 billion ulixacaltamide peak-sales estimate is within the preview’s cited range, which included the most aggressive sell-side estimates above $10 billion.

surprises.description: Unity Vector grew 23% quarter over quarter, nearly twice the 12–13% growth Unity had guided, and passed $1 billion in annual run rate two quarters early. Strategic Grow reached $329 million, well above the preview’s roughly $304 million expectation, helping drive 38% growth in total Strategic revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Unity Vector grew 23% quarter-over-quarter in Q2, nearly double the 12-13% growth the company had guided, and reached over $1 billion in annual run rate two quarters ahead of schedule”; “Strategic Grow revenue rose 63% year-over-year to $329 million, while total strategic revenue grew 38%, driven by Vector's momentum.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Strategic Grow $302–306M” and “Strategic Grow growth vs. the +50–52% guide.”

surprises.description: Q3 Strategic revenue guidance of $540–550 million is well above the preview’s roughly $535 million modeling reference and the $530 million revenue threshold it flagged. The guidance calls for Strategic Grow to accelerate to 68–70% growth and Vector to grow 19–21% sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for strategic revenue of $540-550 million (up 44-47% YoY), a material acceleration, with Strategic Grow expected to grow 68-70% and Vector projected to grow 19-21% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The buy side needs sequential Strategic acceleration”; “If Q3 Strategic guidance is below about $525M, FY consensus likely comes down”; and “Q3 total revenue guide at or above $530M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $160 million, above the preview’s $130–135 million company guide and roughly $133 million consensus. The 29% margin also exceeded the preview’s 26% expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 77% YoY to $160 million with margins reaching a record 29%, expanding 800 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA $130–135M”; “Consensus … ~$133”; “26% margin.”

surprises.description: Unity pulled forward its target for GAAP net income profitability from Q4 to Q3 2026, with Q3 set to mark its first-ever GAAP profitability. The preview highlighted the prior GAAP loss but did not anticipate this earlier profitability milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company pulled forward its GAAP net income profitability target from Q4 2026 to Q3 2026, marking its first-ever GAAP profitability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP net loss $(347M), or $(0.80)/share”; the preview gave no expectation for an earlier GAAP profitability target.

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin is guided to 33%, indicating further expansion beyond the already better-than-expected Q2 margin. The preview did not provide a Q3 margin expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 margins are guided to 33% (up 1,000 bps YoY).”

surprises.description: Free cash flow reached $202 million, up 59% year over year, and Unity moved from net debt to net cash with $2.36 billion in cash. It also plans to repay its 2026 convert in November; the preview did not forecast these cash or balance-sheet results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow rose 59% YoY to $202 million, and Unity flipped from a net debt to a net cash position with a $2.36 billion cash balance, planning to pay off its 2026 convert in November.”

surprises.description: Stock-based compensation fell 25% year over year to 14% of revenue, which Unity described as its lowest level ever. The preview did not flag or forecast this reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Stock-based compensation fell 25% year-over-year to 14% of revenue, its lowest level ever.”

surprises.description: The ironSource Ad Network sunset contributed only $3 million to Vector’s growth, indicating that the pronounced acceleration came from organic momentum rather than legacy migration. The preview flagged the sunset and non-Strategic runoff as an issue, but did not anticipate this specific evidence about the source of Vector growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The sunset of the ironSource Ad Network contributed only $3 million to Vector's growth, indicating the acceleration was organic rather than driven by legacy migration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-Strategic runoff. The ironSource Ads Network sunset took effect April 30, 2026.”

surprises.description: Unity closed the Supersonic sale to Tripledot Studios on August 4, resolving the preview’s open question about whether and when a deal would close. The preview did not identify the buyer or report a completed transaction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Unity closed the sale of Supersonic to Tripledot Studios on August 4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Supersonic divestiture status. A financial advisor was engaged in March. Timing and proceeds were not found”; “Whether a deal is signed or closed.”

surprises.description: Unity disclosed a strategic investment in AppsFlyer alongside Meta, Google, and Moloco, a capital-allocation action the preview did not anticipate. The facts provide no investment amount or further terms, so its shareholder impact is unclear.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[Unity] made a strategic investment in AppsFlyer alongside Meta, Google and Moloco.”

surprises.description: Q3 Strategic Create growth is guided to slow to 7–10%, below its Q2 growth of 14%. The preview expected Q2 Create to be around $156 million but did not give a Q3 Create growth forecast, so the deceleration is a negative development relative to the latest reported pace rather than an explicit preview forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Strategic Create revenue grew 14% YoY to $157 million … with Q3 Create growth guided at a slower 7-10%.”

in_line: Q2 Strategic Create revenue was $157 million, within the preview’s $154–158 million company guidance and close to its roughly $156 million consensus estimate.

surprises.description: SEG reported adjusted EPS of positive $0.02, versus the preview’s expected loss of $0.25 per share. The result was a swing to profitability rather than the expected loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP adjusted net income per share improved to positive $0.02 from a loss of $0.58 a year ago.”

surprises.description: SEG achieved its first positive operating EBITDA, at $4.5 million, while the preview’s base case expected EBITDA near breakeven after corporate G&A. This cleared the key milestone the preview identified, though it was not a large positive EBITDA result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Seaport Entertainment achieved its first-ever positive operating EBITDA of $4.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EBITDA near breakeven after G&A”; the preview also called positive EBITDA after corporate G&A the key milestone.

surprises.description: G&A fell more sharply than the preview anticipated: it had warned that the pace of reductions would moderate, while SEG reported a 20% year-over-year quarterly decline and a reduction of more than 20% in trailing 12-month G&A over nine months.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month G&A was reduced more than 20% over nine months to under $27 million from $34 million in Q3 2025,” and “quarterly G&A down 20% year-over-year to $6.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 G&A of $6.7M ex-restructuring, with management warning that the pace of reduction will moderate.”

surprises.description: The entertainment segment’s operating EBITDA declined despite the preview expecting entertainment to carry the quarter. The call attributed the decline to higher rooftop repair and operating costs and the loss of Chase sponsorship revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The entertainment segment's operating EBITDA declined $1 million (23%) year-over-year, hurt by higher rooftop repair/operating costs and lost sponsorship revenue after founding sponsor Chase declined to renew.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sponsorships, Events & Entertainment revenue vs. ~$20M”; the preview said “Entertainment carries the quarter.”

surprises.description: Rental revenue received a sizable, one-time boost from the early Nike lease termination, a driver the preview did not identify. The $2.7 million net termination-related amount accounted for nearly all of the reported $2.8 million year-over-year increase in rental revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rental revenue rose $2.8 million (67%) year-over-year, driven largely by the early Nike lease termination that added $2.7 million net.”

surprises.description: The remaining capital spending estimate is lower than the preview’s cited $70–90 million capex benchmark: management now expects $50–70 million over the next two years. The time frames are not identical, but the stated remaining range is below the preview’s range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expects $50-70 million in remaining capital expenditures over the next two years to reach 2028 stabilization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capex of $70–90M through 2028.”

surprises.description: SEG still had under 50,000 square feet of available seaport leasing space, versus the preview’s description of roughly 20,000 square feet at One Seaport Plaza as the last material vacancy. Management also cautioned that the remaining smaller footprints would take longer to lease.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Available seaport leasing space fell from roughly 150,000-200,000 square feet to under 50,000 square feet (just over 10% of total), though remaining smaller footprints are expected to take longer to lease.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The roughly 20,000 sf space is the last material vacancy against 90% leased or programmed at YE2025.”

surprises.description: Sadie’s Garden Bar revenue grew 125% year-over-year in its first full quarter under company management, an operating result the preview did not specifically anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sadie's Garden Bar grew revenue 125% year-over-year in its first full quarter under company management.”

in_line: The preview identified Q2 as a seasonal peak and flagged a longer-dated asset-repositioning pipeline. Management’s comments that the next three quarters likely will not match Q2’s per-share gain and that the more meaningful earnings inflection is expected in 2027 and 2028 are broadly consistent with that framing.

The preview expected Pier 17 concerts to be a major entertainment driver. The call reported 22 shows, 13 sellouts, and 91% sell-through, consistent with strong concert demand, although the preview did not provide a specific sell-through expectation.

surprises.description: VAC's contract sales came in far above the preview's roughly $470 million consensus and $463–481 million company range, while VPG growth greatly exceeded the expected mid-to-high-single-digit increase. Management also said May and June were the two strongest sales months in company history and July was still growing about 29%, extending the strength beyond the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 contract sales rose 22% year-over-year to $545 million,” with VPG “up 23%” and “exceeding the high end of guidance”; May and June were “the two highest sales months in company history,” and July trends continued at “roughly 29% growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consolidated contract sales: ~$470M”; company guide “+4% to +8% ($463–481M)”; VPG “Up mid-to-high single digits.” The preview also said to ask for the monthly cadence and July-to-date run rate, noting HGV’s back-half weakness.

surprises.description: Owner contract sales grew much faster than the already strong overall result, with a sharp increase in owner VPG. The preview had no owner-sales or owner-VPG estimate, so this was additional segment-level strength it did not quantify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Owner contract sales surged 41% year-over-year, fueled by a 33% lift in owner VPG”; North America contract sales rose 27%.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA exceeded both the preview's approximately $194 million consensus and the midpoint of company guidance by a substantial amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 6% to $215 million, coming in $20 million above the midpoint of Q2 guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA consensus was “~$194M (guide midpoint)” and company guidance was “$187–202M.”

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised well above the range investors were expecting, rather than merely reaffirmed despite the preview's required second-half acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance by $50 million to $805-830 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance: Adjusted EBITDA $755–780M.” The preview said the guide and H2 math were the key metric, and that reaffirming it with hedged H2 language would be a de facto downgrade.

surprises.description: VAC also lifted its full-year contract-sales growth outlook, with the new range implying especially strong growth in the second half. The preview focused on the Q2 sales range and did not provide a full-year contract-sales growth target to compare against.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “lifted contract sales growth guidance to 18-20%, implying 25-29% growth in the second half.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance moved above the preview's range. The year-to-date result itself was around the preview's stated tracking level, but the raised full-year midpoint was an additional improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: Full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance was raised to “$410-460 million” with “a $35 million midpoint increase”; year-to-date adjusted free cash flow was $201 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow $375–425M.” The preview said “H1 FCF tracking above ~$200M keeps the story intact.”

surprises.description: The Inner Circle platform received a much more specific and ambitious scale target than the preview had, which had noted the launch but asked for quantified early reads.
surprises.fact_evidence: Inner Circle is scaling from “about 50 events in 2026 to a targeted 1,000 events in 2027,” with events generating “VPGs well above average.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted the Inner Circle platform launched in June and said, “Investors need quantified early reads, not adjectives.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that it would retain its New York City property for inventory and reframed its noncore-asset disposition target. The preview did not describe an asset-sale target or signal that this property might be kept, so the change cannot be measured against a stated prior target here.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “reframed its noncore asset disposition target to $200 million by end of 2027 after deciding to retain its New York City property for inventory.”

in_line: Year-to-date adjusted free cash flow was $201 million, consistent with the preview's indication that H1 tracking above roughly $200 million would keep the cash-flow story intact.

surprises.description: Revenue was about $285 million, well below the preview’s $308.7 million consensus and even below its sub-$295 million bear-case threshold. That is a 17% year-over-year decline, versus the roughly 10% decline implied by consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 17% year-over-year to approximately $285 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue consensus $308.7M”; “About −10% Y/Y.” The bear scenario expected “Below $295M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was about $7 million, below the company’s $14–$22 million guidance range. The preview identified a result below $14 million as its most damaging outcome; the reported figure was half the range’s low end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was approximately $7 million, coming in below the company's guidance range due to expense timing, FX headwinds from the Israeli shekel, and elevated bad debts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA vs. the $14M–$22M guide”; “A print below $14M is the most damaging outcome.”

surprises.description: Teads suspended all guidance, including its previously stated approximately $100 million full-year 2026 EBITDA target, rather than reaffirming or providing the H2 bridge the preview said investors needed. Management cited volatility in direct response and SME.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company suspended all guidance, including its previously provided full-year 2026 EBITDA guidance, citing volatility in the direct response and SME business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 ~$100M guidance. Watch whether it is reaffirmed, softened, or withdrawn”; the preview said the H2 figure needed “+37% to +52% Y/Y growth” and that investors needed “numbers here, not commentary.”

surprises.description: Direct response and SME XTAC gross profit fell 30% to $34 million, with management citing AI search summaries that reduced publisher page views by 15–25%. That is materially worse than the preview’s expectation that the 2025 direct-response headwind would be mostly behind the company by Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The direct response and SME business posted $34 million in XTAC gross profit, a 30% year-over-year decline amid AI search summaries reducing publisher page views by 15-25%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management’s defense in the preview included “roughly $20M of Y/Y ex-TAC headwind from 2025 direct-response quality cleanups, mostly in H1 and falling to minimal by Q4.”

surprises.description: XTAC gross profit declined 14% year over year, worse than the preview’s expected improving trend of roughly a 9–11% decline in its base case and worse than the level it said would support the headwind-rolloff story. The $123 million amount itself was within the company’s guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “XTAC gross profit fell 14% to $123 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected an “ex-TAC decline −9% to −11%”; it said “Better than about −8% supports the headwind-rolloff story. −12% or worse undercuts it.”

surprises.description: Enterprise advertiser spend was flat year over year for Q2, but May and June both showed positive year-over-year growth; management called this the low point of the downturn and guided to mid-single-digit XTAC growth in H2. That offered a more concrete enterprise recovery signal than the preview’s difficult, largely unquantified H2 bridge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The enterprise business delivered $89 million in XTAC gross profit with advertiser spend flat year-over-year, and management guided to mid-single-digit XTAC growth in H2”; “Both May and June showed positive year-over-year growth in enterprise advertiser spend, which management characterized as marking the low point of the downturn.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said reaching the full-year target required “$77.2M–$85.2M in H2” and “+37% to +52% Y/Y growth,” while describing the H2 bridge as difficult.

surprises.description: CTV revenue grew 67% year over year to about $40 million and rose to 13% of revenue from 7% a year earlier, exceeding the preview’s threshold for a healthy growth rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CTV revenue grew 67% year-over-year to approximately $40 million, rising to 13% of Q2 revenue from 7% in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said CTV needed to “hold above roughly 40%” and flagged a deceleration below about 35% as a concern.

surprises.description: Cash and marketable securities were $91 million, down from $98.7 million at Q1-end, despite the preview expecting a seasonal Q2 cash build. The $3 million of free cash flow and access to a $40 million revolver provide some cushion, but the reported cash balance did not show the expected build.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $91 million in cash and marketable securities plus access to a $40 million revolving credit facility, generating $3 million of free cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 should be a seasonal cash-build quarter.” The preview also said cash falling toward $85 million was part of its bear scenario.

surprises.description: Management said it is deliberately accepting lower near-term EBITDA to keep investing in the higher-margin enterprise business, while running the legacy Outbrain-related DR/SME business for profitability. The preview emphasized cost cuts and the need for a steep H2 EBITDA ramp, but did not anticipate this explicit investment-versus-near-term-earnings tradeoff.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is deliberately trading off near-term EBITDA to continue investing in the higher-margin enterprise business, while running the legacy Outbrain-related DR/SME business for profitability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “more than 20% cut in compensation run-rate” as part of management’s defense of the full-year target and said reaching that target required substantial H2 EBITDA growth.

surprises.description: Omnichannel campaigns reached 16% of branding revenue, up from 9% a year earlier and close to the 18% full-year target. The preview did not flag this metric, so the reported progress was an unanticipated positive operating update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Omnichannel campaigns rose to 16% of Q2 branding revenue from 9% a year earlier, approaching the 18% full-year target.”

in_line: XTAC gross profit of $123 million was within the company’s Q2 guidance range of $121 million–$131 million, although its year-over-year decline was worse than the preview expected.

surprises.description: Tripadvisor’s Q3 continuing-operations revenue outlook calls for a 7%–10% decline, and management described its second-half view as more prudent. That is a weaker near-term outlook than the preview’s FY26 expectation of approximately flat revenue, though the periods and reporting basis are not directly equivalent.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for continuing operations revenue declines of 7% to 10%” and reflects “a more prudent second-half outlook.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY26 revenue: “Approximately flat,” conditioned on macro not worsening.

surprises.description: Q3 Experiences bookings are expected to grow 5%–7%, but revenue is guided to between a 2% decline and 1% growth. Even excluding the roughly 1-point currency headwind, the implied bookings-to-revenue gap is wider than the approximately 3-point gap the preview described as expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 Experiences guidance projects 5% to 7% bookings growth but revenue of -2% to +1% (including ~1 point of currency headwind).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said guidance implied bookings growing “about 3 points faster than revenue” and that a wider gap would suggest structural take-rate pressure.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was higher than the preview’s implied estimate: adding continuing operations and TheFork gives $87 million, versus an implied $80–82 million. On the reported total revenue of $503 million, that is also just above the 17% upper end of the preview’s 15%–17% margin guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Continuing operations reported “adjusted EBITDA of $76 million,” while TheFork contributed “$11 million adjusted EBITDA”; the two sum to $87 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: ~$80–82M (implied)” and company guidance of “15–17% consolidated margin.”

surprises.description: TheFork moved from the previously described put-option arrangement to a signed sale agreement, with closing anticipated before year-end. The preview had noted that the deal was not yet a signed SPA; the call also specified approximately $680 million in net proceeds.
surprises.fact_evidence: Tripadvisor “agreed to sell TheFork to American Express for $700 million,” expects “approximately $680 million in net proceeds,” and said the deal was signed August 2 with closing anticipated before year-end.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The deal “is structured as a put option agreement, not a signed SPA.”

surprises.description: Experiences bookings reached the preview’s expected range, but the result had a notably uneven channel mix: Viator’s point of sale grew 10% while SEO weakness on Tripadvisor’s point of sale dragged overall growth by an estimated 5 percentage points. The preview discussed SEO-related traffic declines for Hotels & Other, not this quantified drag on Experiences.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Experiences bookings grew 5% overall,” with “the Viator point of sale growing 10%” while SEO headwinds on Tripadvisor’s point of sale created “an estimated 5 percentage point growth drag.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 Experiences bookings guidance was “+5% to +8%.”

surprises.description: Hotels & Other’s 28% Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin was above the preview’s reference to an approximately 26% LTM margin, despite the segment’s sharp revenue decline. The comparison is directional because the preview cited an LTM figure rather than a Q2 margin forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: Hotels & Other revenue declined 21% to $163 million, while it remained at a “28% adjusted EBITDA margin,” down only about 100 basis points.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The segment still carries about a 26% LTM EBITDA margin.”

in_line: Experiences bookings grew 5%, at the low end of the preview’s +5% to +8% Q2 guidance.
Hotels & Other revenue declined 21%, at the top end of the preview’s expected 21%–24% decline.

Total Q2 revenue was approximately $503 million including TheFork ($442 million continuing operations plus $61 million TheFork), close to the preview’s $505.5–506.3 million consensus and its warning that discontinued-operations presentation would make the continuing-operations headline much lower.

No shares were repurchased during the portfolio review, consistent with the preview’s base case of deferred capital allocation; the stated use of TheFork proceeds remained broad rather than a specific buyback commitment.

surprises.description: Allstate reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $8.99, far above the preview’s consensus range of $4.90–$5.82. Even versus the highest cited estimate, the result was about 55% higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted net income was $2.3 billion or $8.99 per share.”

surprises.description: Total revenue of $18.6 billion exceeded even the preview’s higher estimate of $17.73 billion, although the preview noted that vendors treated realized gains and scope differently.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenues grew 11.8% year-over-year to $18.6 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (Q2) … $17.73B (Zacks …); $15.46B (StockStory …). Vendors treat realized gains and scope differently.”

surprises.description: Favorable auto reserve releases were substantial: $1.5 billion year-to-date, with about half of the bodily-injury changes tied to the 2023 and 2024 accident years. The preview highlighted Q1’s $840 million of favorable auto development and said adverse development was a serious risk, but did not anticipate releases of this scale continuing year-to-date.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Auto claim reserve releases totaled $1.5 billion year-to-date, with about half of the bodily injury changes relating to the 2023 and 2024 accident years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 carried $840M of favorable auto releases, and management said 2025 contributed minimally. Adverse development would be a serious negative.”

surprises.description: Homeowners new business rose 46.8% to 411,000 policies, a strong acquisition result that the preview did not identify as an expected growth outcome. Homeowners policies in force also increased 2.9%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Homeowners new business rose 46.8% to 411,000 policies” and “homeowners PIF up 2.9%.”

surprises.description: Net investment income surged 33.8% to $1 billion, a notably strong contribution beyond the preview’s general expectation that investment income would remain a tailwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net investment income surged 33.8% to $1 billion,” reflecting “a $7.1 billion increase in public equity holdings made last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net investment income has been a quiet tailwind.”

in_line: Auto policies in force grew 2.8%, close to the preview’s stated bull-case requirement of growth near 3% or more.

Management’s comments about flat pricing, possible margin normalization, and elevated bodily-injury severity were consistent with the preview’s concerns about margin normalization and rising auto bodily-injury severity.

surprises.description: CPS reported an adjusted loss of $0.13 per share, versus preview estimates of adjusted EPS of $0.57–$0.59. The result was a large miss and a swing to a loss rather than the expected profit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company swung to a Q2 adjusted net loss of $2.3 million (13 cents per share) versus adjusted net income of $1 million (6 cents) in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS (Q2) … $0.57 (Zacks) or $0.59 (alternate compile).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $53.9 million, about $11 million below the roughly $65 million implied estimate, and the resulting margin was about 7.5% rather than the preview’s roughly 9% marker. Higher material costs, wages and inflation, and duties and tariffs weighed on the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell to $53.9 million from $62.8 million a year earlier, hurt by $10M higher material costs, $8M in wage/inflation, and $8M in higher duties and tariffs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (Q2) … ~$65M implied”; “A margin well below 9% would weaken the H2 ramp case.”

surprises.description: CPS reaffirmed the midpoint of its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance even though the preview said first-half results were tracking below the range and its base case anticipated a narrowed guide of about $255–$275 million. Management also described a strong second-half ramp, with margins above 12%, roughly $100 million of free cash flow, and more than $50 million in incremental savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed the midpoint of full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance, implying second-half EBITDA margins above 12% and roughly $100 million in second-half free cash flow, supported by another $50+ million in incremental cost savings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “H1 is tracking below the $260–300M range”; the base scenario expected the “FY EBITDA guide narrowed to ~$255–275M.”

surprises.description: Q2 sales of $721.3 million exceeded both preview consensus figures of $699.1 million and $708.9 million. The beat was modest relative to the estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 sales rose 2.2% year-over-year to $721.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (Q2) … $699.1M (Zacks) or $708.9M (MarketBeat).”

surprises.description: The preview said Q2 needed real volume to support the second-half thesis, but sales growth came primarily from foreign exchange; volume/mix and price recoveries together contributed only about $5 million. Thus the revenue beat did not bring the anticipated meaningful volume support.
surprises.fact_evidence: Sales growth was “driven primarily by favorable foreign exchange (~$10M) with a smaller contribution from volume/mix and price recoveries (~$5M).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs real volume to support the H2 thesis.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was positive at $16.3 million, a stronger outcome than merely moving away from Q1’s large outflow. The preview had highlighted the need for a clear improvement and the goal of positive free cash flow in 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow improved $39.7 million year-over-year to $16.3 million in Q2, aided by the Q1 refinancing and working capital optimization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs to show a clear move away from Q1’s –$93.2M, against the stated goal of positive FCF in 2026.”

surprises.description: New business awards were $118 million in Q2 and $246 million for the first half, putting CPS ahead of the pace needed for its full-year target of more than $400 million. The preview had flagged the target as an important test after $127.9 million of Q1 awards.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net new business awards totaled $118 million in Q2 and $246 million for the first half, keeping the company ahead of its full-year target of over $400 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New business awards. Q1 booked $127.9M against a >$400M full-year target.”

surprises.description: Management said gross margins had expanded 160 basis points over two years despite flat-to-lower production and expects further expansion in 2026 even with flat volumes. That supports a margin-improvement path that does not depend on the volume recovery the preview emphasized.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit margins have expanded 160 basis points over two years despite flat-to-lower production, and management expects continued margin expansion in 2026 even with flat volumes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs real volume to support the H2 thesis.”

surprises.description: Management reported a substantial fluid-handling conquest pipeline, with nearly 10 awards expected to generate nearly $40 million in annual sales effective this year as competitors struggle. The preview did not identify this segment opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The fluid handling segment won nearly 10 mid-production conquest awards over 10 months totaling nearly $40 million in annual sales effective this year, as competitors’ struggles create share-gain opportunities.”

surprises.description: Management described a specific mechanism to recover most of the commodity inflation: index-based contracts and July 1 price increases that raised the reference price from about $65 to over $90. The preview did not flag this pricing action or cost-recovery outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects to recover most costs via index-based contracts, with July 1 price increases raising the reference from ~$65 to over $90.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was a $26.6 million loss, substantially worse than the preview’s expected $15–19 million loss and below the preview’s downside marker of a $22 million loss. Management said the quarter included $21.8 million of peak supply-management costs and $3 million of one-time feed-program professional fees.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $26.6 million,” including “$21.8 million in peak supply management costs and $3 million in one-time feed program professional fees.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA: ‘negative mid-to-high teens’”; the catalyst checklist says “Worse than -$20M suggests supply-management costs are running above the $32M plan.”

surprises.description: Gross profit was only 6.6% of revenue, well below the preview’s expected mid-to-high-teens reported gross margin. The reported result was burdened by $28.1 million in discrete costs, including a large excess-breaker-sales impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit fell to $10.9 million (6.6% of net revenue), burdened by $28.1 million of discrete costs including a $19.5 million excess breaker sales impact and $7.8 million in butter wind-down exit costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 reported gross margin should be mid-to-high teens because of supply-management costs.”

surprises.description: Vital Farms ended the quarter with $21.2 million of cash and $30 million drawn on its revolver, then fully drew a new $125 million term loan and added a $60 million ABL facility. That is a broader and larger financing package than the preview’s possible revolver draw, though it also increases available debt capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with only $21.2 million in cash and $30 million drawn on its revolver, then secured a new $125 million term loan (fully drawn) and $60 million ABL facility, boosting debt capacity to $185 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for a revolver draw, a buyback pause, or working-capital release from inventory.”

surprises.description: The board terminated the 2026 share-repurchase program after buying back $50 million of shares, with the termination required to comply with the new loan terms. The preview flagged a possible buyback pause, but did not anticipate that the program would be terminated to meet lending requirements.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The board terminated the 2026 share repurchase program (after $50 million was repurchased at $13.29 per share) to comply with new loan terms.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for a revolver draw, a buyback pause, or working-capital release from inventory.”

surprises.description: Full-year supply-management costs are now expected in the mid-$30 million range rather than the initial $32 million estimate, a modest increase in the cost burden.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year supply management costs are now modeled in the mid-$30 million range versus an initial $32 million estimate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Roughly $32M of ‘supply management’ costs, concentrated in Q2.”

surprises.description: Vital Farms gained more than 200 basis points of retail dollar share in Shell Eggs even as the category faced oversupply and falling prices. The preview identified share and elasticity as a key test but did not anticipate a gain of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Vital Farms gained more than 200 basis points of year-over-year retail dollar share in the Shell Egg category during Q2 despite industry-wide oversupply and falling category pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 is the first clean quarter to test the strategy”; the bull scenario cited “volume elasticity broad-based.”

surprises.description: Distribution is projected to average 150–160 points in 2026 and reach 170–175 in Q4, with the largest yearly gain since the 2020 IPO. The preview’s bull case used TDP above 155 as a positive threshold; the Q4 projection is materially above that marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total distribution points are on track to average 150-160 in 2026 (up from 130 in 2025) and reach 170-175 in Q4, representing the largest yearly TDP gain since the 2020 IPO.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bull scenario said “TDP rises above 155.”

surprises.description: Average price gaps to branded competitors narrowed from $2.51 to $2.36, showing progress on the price-gap strategy, but remained above management’s targeted $1–$2 range. The preview highlighted the strategy as a key debate but gave no expected Q2 price-gap figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Average price gaps to branded competitors narrowed from approximately $2.51 in Q1 to $2.36 in Q2, moving toward the targeted $1-to-$2 range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Evidence the price-gap strategy is working.”

surprises.description: VXR construction is to be paused by year-end, an unflagged project delay in the preview. The release kept CapEx guidance unchanged, so the pause is not presented as a reduction to the full-year spending range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “VXR construction will be paused by year-end within reaffirmed CapEx guidance of $70-$75 million.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $166 million, within the preview’s stated $165–172 million consensus band.
Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $775–800 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $0–10 million, as the preview’s base case anticipated.
The expected Q4 gross-margin recovery target was maintained: management expects to exit Q4 at an approximately 30% gross-margin run rate.
CapEx guidance remained $70–75 million, matching the preview’s stated range.
Breaker-channel reliance was expected to decline sharply in the second half after peaking in Q2, consistent with the preview’s focus on Q2 costs and breaker-channel roll-off.

surprises.description: Zoetis cut FY26 revenue guidance to $9.12–$9.32 billion from the prior $9.68–$9.96 billion range, and cut adjusted diluted EPS guidance to $6.15–$6.25 from $6.85–$7.00. The new EPS range is well below the preview’s stated bear-signal threshold of anything below $6.85.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year revenue guidance was cut to $9.12–$9.32 billion”; “adjusted net income lowered to $2.57–$2.62 billion”; “adjusted diluted EPS of $6.15–$6.25.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue ($9.68–9.96B) and adj. EPS ($6.85–7.00) guidance. Anything below $6.85 is a bear signal.”

surprises.description: U.S. Companion Animal fell 11%, far worse than the preview’s expected decline of roughly 3.5% for the segment. The total Companion Animal portfolio was down 6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. Companion Animal fell 11% as the total Companion Animal portfolio declined 6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus implies about −3.5% reported for the segment”; the preview also said a U.S. Companion Animal print between “−1% and −4%” would support a cyclical rather than structural story.

surprises.description: U.S. revenue declined 7%, considerably worse than the preview’s expected 2.2% decline; international growth of 6% provided a sharp geographic contrast, though the preview gave no international estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. revenue declined 7% while international grew 6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “U.S. total revenue … $1.33B (−2.2% Y/Y).”

surprises.description: Key Dermatology fell 16% globally, and U.S. in-clinic share dropped 5 points sequentially and 10 points year over year. The preview flagged competitive pressure from Numelvi and Zenrelia, but the reported revenue decline and share losses show more acute pressure than that watchlist alone conveyed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Key Dermatology revenue dropped 16% globally to $395 million”; “U.S. in-clinic share fell to approximately 86%, declining 5 points sequentially and 10 points year-over-year”; management cited “intensified competition from a new U.S. entrant in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Apoquel/Cytopoint faces Merck’s Numelvi (launched Feb 2026) and Elanco’s Zenrelia.”

surprises.description: The full-year price outlook deteriorated from the preview’s cited 1–2% price contribution target to 0% to -2%. Management attributed the outlook to Dermatology gross-to-net investments and price cuts on Cerenia and Convenia amid generic competition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 price was approximately flat, and full-year price realization is now expected between 0% and -2%, driven by gross-to-net investments in Dermatology and price cuts on Cerenia and Convenia amid generic competition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Price contribution against the revised 1–2% target.”

surprises.description: Adjusted net income declined 2% and the quarter fell short of company expectations, even as adjusted diluted EPS rose 4% year over year to $1.87. The EPS resilience was supported by unusually high repurchases, rather than stronger net income.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income down 2% to $781 million, falling short of company expectations”; “repurchased over $550 million of shares in the quarter—above its historical quarterly average—helping lift adjusted diluted EPS 4% year-over-year to $1.87.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus (Q2 FY26E)” for adjusted diluted EPS was “$1.84–$1.86.”

surprises.description: Livestock grew 11% globally and 23% in the U.S., a strong result not discussed in the preview. Management cautioned that second-half growth would moderate to mid-single digits because screwworm-related and supply-timing gains were transitory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Livestock grew 11% globally to $731 million, with U.S. Livestock up 23% to $222 million,” while “second-half growth [is expected] to moderate to mid-single digits as screwworm-driven and supply-timing gains are transitory.”

surprises.description: The company announced CFO Wetteny Joseph’s departure and appointed Jay Saccaro to a newly created EVP CFO and COO role overseeing finance, manufacturing, and supply. The preview did not flag a CFO transition or this expanded operating remit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Wetteny Joseph is departing after five years, with Jay Saccaro … joining August 17 in a newly created EVP CFO and COO role overseeing finance, manufacturing, and supply.”

surprises.description: Companion Animal Diagnostics grew 12%, and Zoetis completed the VitalRADS acquisition to enter veterinary imaging—developments not anticipated in the preview’s checklist.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Companion Animal Diagnostics grew 12% to $118 million, and the company completed the VitalRADS teleradiology acquisition to expand into veterinary imaging.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was approximately in line with the preview’s dollar consensus: $2.5 billion reported versus $2.49 billion expected.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 29.4%, above both the 29.0% high end of the company’s Q2 guide and the preview’s roughly 28.5% consensus estimate. Adjusted EBITDA of $53 million also exceeded the preview’s implied estimate of about $51.5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded nearly 100 basis points to 29.4%, outperforming the high end of guidance for the second consecutive quarter, with adjusted EBITDA of $53 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin ~28.5% (implied)” and “Adj. EBITDA ~$51.5M (implied)”; company Q2 margin guidance was “28.0–29.0%.”

surprises.description: Marketplace revenue grew over 7%, its fastest rate outside the 2021 pandemic recovery, and marketplace subscribers reached their highest level since 2023. The preview’s base case anticipated continued growth but did not suggest this pace or subscriber milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marketplace revenue grew over 7% year-over-year, the fastest growth rate in the company's public history outside of 2021's pandemic recovery, with marketplace subscribers hitting their highest level since 2023.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case anticipated “third or fourth consecutive quarter of Y/Y growth” and dealer count “roughly flat.”

surprises.description: OEM and national revenue fell 18% year over year, materially worse than the preview’s base expectation of an 8–12% decline and beyond its bear-case threshold of a 12%+ decline. The reported result therefore leaves the expected H2 recovery less assured, though the facts do not state whether management changed its trough timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “3% dealer revenue growth offsetting an 18% decline in OEM and national revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base case: “OEM/National down 8–12%”; bear case: “OEM/National still down 12%+.”

surprises.description: The Q3 margin guide of 28.5–29.5% is below the roughly 30–31% H2 margin run rate the preview calculated would be needed to achieve the 29–30% full-year target. With the annual target reaffirmed, the guide implies a substantial step-up would still be needed later in the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 margin of 28.5% to 29.5%” and full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was reaffirmed at “29% to 30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Hitting the 29–30% full-year guide would require H2 margins of roughly 30–31%.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted diluted EPS was $0.51, ahead of the preview’s $0.49 consensus estimate. The beat was modest compared with the larger margin and EBITDA outperformance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS increased to $0.51 from $0.41.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS $0.49.”

surprises.description: ARPD reached a record $2,500, above the preview’s roughly $2,480 base case, while Premium Plus penetration was already near double digits mid-year and tracking toward the 15% year-end target. The preview described an early adoption figure as a bull-case possibility, not its base expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 ARPD was $2,500, up 3% year-over-year and 1% sequentially, setting a new record for marketplace-only ARPD driven by Premium Plus”; “Premium Plus penetration stands at or near double digits mid-year, tracking toward the company's 15% adoption target by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base case: “ARPD ~$2,480”; bull case: “ARPD ≥$2,500” and “an explicit Premium Plus adoption figure ahead of the 7%→15% path.”

surprises.description: Website units were still declining, and management laid out a 2–3 quarter product-innovation turnaround plan with renewed website growth not expected until 2027. The preview focused on dealer counts and traffic but did not anticipate this extended website recovery timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Website (DI) units declined year-over-year,” with “a 2-3 quarter product-innovation turnaround plan” and “renewed website growth in 2027.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $179.9 million, about $0.7 million below the $180.6 million consensus estimate, although it remained within company guidance and the preview’s $180–181 million base-case range. This was a slight shortfall rather than a meaningful departure from the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $179.9 million, up 1% year-over-year and within guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $180.6M” consensus; base case: “$180–181M.”

surprises.description: Website traffic and unique visitors continued to decline, but management attributed this to deliberately shedding low-converting traffic and reported double-digit lead-conversion growth and improved performance-marketing cost per lead. The preview flagged traffic as a narrative to watch but did not anticipate these offsetting lead-quality improvements.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Website traffic and unique visitors declined year-over-year due to an intentional shift away from low-converting traffic, while Q2 lead conversion rose double digits and performance marketing cost per lead improved.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “AI and traffic narrative” as an item to watch and noted prior-quarter declines in unique visitors and visits.

in_line: Full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance of flat to 2% and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 29% to 30% were reaffirmed, as the preview’s base case expected.
The company was pacing toward its $90 million full-year buyback target, consistent with the preview’s focus on buyback pace as potential support.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $22.3 million, well below the preview’s $24.5 million consensus and down year over year rather than growing. Management attributed the decline to fewer billed hours even though staffing request volumes were up.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 fiscal 2026 revenue was $22.3 million, down 5.1% year-over-year, driven by lower billed hours”; year-over-year staffing request volumes were up but were “translating into fewer billed hours.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 revenue consensus of “$24.50M (+4.3% y/y implied)” and described revenue near flat as a bear scenario.

surprises.description: The full-year revenue outlook weakened from low- to mid-single-digit growth to revenue roughly consistent with 2025. That is a meaningful reduction from the growth target the preview expected management to reaffirm.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects full-year 2026 revenue to “remain relatively consistent with 2025 levels.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited guidance for “low- to mid-single digits” revenue growth versus 2025 and asked whether management would reaffirm that target.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA remained negative in the seasonal up-quarter, rather than reaching the preview’s expected breakeven-to-positive range. The $298,000 loss was also below the preview’s base-case profit estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA was “a loss of $298,000 in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected Q2 to move “toward breakeven or modestly positive,” with a base case of “+$0.3–0.6M.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin was 35.5%, below the preview’s 35.8%–36.0% base range. However, management kept full-year gross margin in the 36% range, so the shortfall was limited rather than a change to the annual margin outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin was “35.5% versus 35.8% a year ago,” with full-year gross margin guided “in the 36% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “35.8–36.0%”; it said a quarter below 35.5% would be a negative signal.

surprises.description: The GAAP loss per share was larger than the preview’s near-zero consensus, although the adjusted loss was close to the preview’s base-case range. The GAAP result was therefore a modest miss, not a broad earnings collapse.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company reported a GAAP net loss from continuing operations of “$0.08 per diluted share” and an adjusted EPS loss of “$0.02.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed EPS consensus of “~$0.00” and a base-case GAAP EPS range of “$(0.02) to +$0.01.”

surprises.description: PropTech’s expected 1%–2% revenue contribution was pushed from FY2026 to 2027. The preview had anticipated that contribution in FY2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: Following a six-month ramp, the PropTech offering is expected to contribute “approximately 1% to 2% of revenue in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said PropTech/Yardi consulting was expected to be “1–2% of FY26 revenue.”

surprises.description: SG&A was already down 29% year over year in Q2, while the preview said the full benefit of the cost savings would begin in Q3. This indicates a stronger reduction in Q2 than that timing suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A expenses fell 29% year-over-year to $8.9 million,” and the full benefit of completed cost-reduction and restructuring initiatives begins in Q3.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said about $1 million of annualized selling-cost savings had been implemented late in Q1, “with full benefit only from Q3.”

in_line: Full-year gross-margin guidance remained in the 36% range, consistent with the preview’s expectation that margin would trend toward 36%.
Ongoing G&A was estimated at roughly $12 million, including about $2 million in public-company costs, consistent with the preview.

surprises.description: Evergy disclosed a substantially larger pool of potential large-load growth than the preview quantified: expansion opportunities at existing customer sites rose to 2.0–2.5 GW, with another 1–2 GW of Tier 2 opportunities and more than 10 GW in the remaining pipeline. Management said none of this pipeline is in the current five-year plan, so it represents potential upside beyond the preview’s focus on the existing 3.0 GW contracted base and a possible sixth ESA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expansion opportunities at or adjacent to existing customer sites grew to 2.0-2.5 GW (up from 1-1.5 GW last quarter), plus 1-2 GW of Tier 2 opportunities and a remaining pipeline of over 10 additional GW, none of which is included in the current 5-year financial plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch the “Large-load ESA pipeline vs. 3.0 GW” and noted that “A sixth ESA was pre-committed for 2026 and is not in the plan.”

surprises.description: Management reiterated 6% to 8%+ long-term adjusted EPS growth but added that annual EPS growth should exceed 8% from 2028 through 2030. That acceleration was stronger than the preview’s cited FY27 consensus growth estimate of 7.1%, though the preview did not give a long-term EPS-growth expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Evergy “reaffirmed its long-term adjusted EPS growth target of 6% to 8%+ through 2030 off a 2026 midpoint of $4.24, and expects annual EPS growth to exceed 8% beginning in 2028 through 2030.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY27 adjusted EPS consensus of “$4.56, +7.1%” and did not state an expectation for EPS growth above 8% in 2028–2030.

surprises.description: Evergy reported a five-year capital plan of $21.6 billion with about $1 billion of incremental generation capital, raising projected rate-base CAGR through 2030 to approximately 12% from 11.5%. The preview did not flag this upward revision to planned investment or rate-base growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The February 2026 CapEx plan is $21.6 billion over five years, with approximately $1 billion of incremental generation capital raising the projected rate base CAGR through 2030 from 11.5% to approximately 12%.”

surprises.description: In the pending Missouri Metro rate case, data center customers allowed Evergy to reduce its requested revenue requirement by $25 million, about 15%; management also said most residential customers’ increases should be at or below inflation, with Missouri West an exception. The preview identified the rate case as a key debate but did not anticipate this lower request or the stated customer-rate outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data center customers enabled a $25 million (about 15%) reduction in the requested revenue requirement in the pending Missouri Metro rate case,” and management expects “most residential customers' rate increases to remain at or below inflation, though Missouri West customers may see above-inflation increases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the “Missouri Metro rate case” and noted settlement conferences were scheduled for September 2026, without stating an expected change to the request or likely customer increases.

surprises.description: Evergy described preferred IRP plans through 2032 with more than 5 GW of additions, including roughly 3.9 GW of natural gas, nearly 800 MW of solar, and 450 MW of battery storage. The preview did not specify an expected generation buildout or resource mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The IRP preferred plans through 2032 include more than 5 GW of new additions, comprising roughly 3.9 GW of natural gas, nearly 800 MW of solar, and 450 MW of battery storage.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.88, within the preview’s $0.87–$0.90 base scenario and the broad $0.81–$0.90 consensus range.
Evergy kept FY26 adjusted EPS guidance at $4.14–$4.34, as the preview expected, and said it remained on track for the $4.24 midpoint.

The reported 3 GW total of large-customer peak load was consistent with the preview’s 3.0 GW baseline; management’s confidence in at least one additional ESA during 2026 was consistent with the preview’s expectation of a sixth ESA in 2026.
The 7%–8% annual retail-load growth outlook remained consistent with the preview’s stated long-term load-growth guide.
Forward equity sales of approximately $425 million by June 30 were within the expected $700–900 million for 2026, and the 14%–15% FFO-to-debt target matched the preview’s stated 2026–2028 target.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $102.9 million, well below the preview’s $108.9–109.1 million consensus range. The shortfall was accompanied by funeral comparable revenue declining 2.4% and cemetery comparable revenue remaining roughly flat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose only 0.8% to $102.9 million, with funeral comparable revenue down 2.4% to $55.7 million while cemetery comparable revenue was roughly flat at $33.2 million.”

surprises.description: Comparable funeral volume fell 3.5% in Q2, contrary to the preview’s view that flat or better volume was needed to support the recovery. Management said softer mortality rates were negative in every month from January through June.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Comparable funeral volume declined 3.5% in Q2 and 4.7% in the first six months year-over-year, driven by softer mortality rates that were negative every month from January through June.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Flat or better comparable volume is needed to support the recovery story.”

surprises.description: Management cut FY2026 revenue guidance by about $5 million to $435–445 million instead of reaffirming the prior $440–450 million range. The cut was attributed mainly to delayed acquisition timing and weaker first-half volume.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management lowered full-year 2026 revenue guidance by about $5 million to $435-445 million, attributing the cut mainly to delayed acquisition timing and weaker first-half volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue $440–450M”; the preview’s base scenario expected to “Reaffirm $440–450M unchanged.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted diluted EPS was $0.78, below the preview’s $0.82 consensus estimate, despite year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS rose 5.4% to $0.78 from $0.74.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | $0.82”

surprises.description: The company maintained its profitability outlook despite reducing revenue guidance: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA and EPS guidance were reaffirmed, the margin range was raised from 30.5–31.5% to 31–31.5%, and overhead guidance was narrowed lower to 13.5–14% of revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year guidance was reaffirmed on profitability with adjusted EBITDA of $135-140 million, EPS of $3.35-3.55, and margin raised to 31-31.5%, while overhead guidance was lowered to 13.5-14% of revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited prior FY2026 margin guidance of “30.5–31.5%” and overhead guidance of “13.5–14.5%,” and its base scenario expected revenue guidance to be reaffirmed unchanged.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was slightly below the preview’s derived estimate, although the margin result was stronger: EBITDA was $33.3 million versus a derived $33.5–34.5 million range, while margin reached 32.3% versus an expected roughly 31.0–31.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted consolidated EBITDA grew 3.1% to $33.3 million with margin expanding 70 basis points to 32.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$33.5–34.5M (derived)” and “Adj. EBITDA margin | ~31.0–31.5% (derived).”

surprises.description: After six months of declining funeral volume, management reported a sharp change in July: volume returned to strong low-single-digit growth. That is an encouraging early sign for the much stronger second half the preview said the revenue outlook required.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Funeral volume returned to positive strong low-single-digit growth in July after six months of decline, supporting the company's expectation for a much stronger second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY2026 guide implied “+8.1% to +12.9%” year-over-year revenue growth in H2 and flagged “The H2 revenue ramp” as the key issue.

surprises.description: First-half adjusted free cash flow was $13.8 million, down from $20.3 million a year earlier, with $3.2 million of incremental planned capital expenditures contributing to the decline. That leaves a substantial second-half contribution needed against the preview’s FY2026 target of $40–50 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow fell to $13.8 million in the first half from $20.3 million a year earlier, reflecting $3.2 million of incremental planned capital expenditures.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Adjusted FCF $11.2M” for Q1 and a “$40–50M FY26 target.”

surprises.description: Insurance-funded pre-need funeral contracts sold rose 21.1% and financial revenue increased 14%. These reported growth figures were not specifically anticipated in the preview, which focused its pre-need discussion on cemetery production.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Insurance-funded pre-need funeral contracts sold rose 21.1% and financial revenue increased 14% to $9.3 million year-over-year.”

in_line: Bank leverage was 4.0x, matching the 4.0x figure reported in the preview for Q1 and remaining within the preview’s stated 3.5–4.0x year-end target.

surprises.description: Dana reported adjusted diluted EPS of $0.19, far below the preview's $0.60–$0.67 Q2 consensus range. Adjusted net income was $21 million, up from $4 million a year ago, but that growth did not meet the expected earnings level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted adjusted EPS rose to $0.19 from $0.03 a year ago,” with adjusted net income increasing to “$21 million from $4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS” consensus: “$0.66–0.67; a second feed shows $0.60.”

surprises.description: Dana raised its 2026 sales and adjusted EBITDA outlook, rather than simply reaffirming guidance at the upper end as the preview’s base case anticipated. Sales guidance rose by $225 million to approximately $7.75 billion and EBITDA by $25 million to $825 million, primarily on stronger commercial vehicle demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Dana raised full-year 2026 guidance to approximately $7.75 billion in sales (up $225 million) and $825 million in adjusted EBITDA (up $25 million), driven primarily by stronger commercial vehicle demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “FY guidance reaffirmed with the ‘upper end of sales’ language”; it listed FY26 company guidance of “$7.30–7.70B” in sales and “$750–850M” in adjusted EBITDA.

surprises.description: Despite raising sales and EBITDA guidance, Dana cut full-year adjusted EPS guidance to approximately $2 per share. That is below both the prior guidance midpoint of about $2.50 and the preview’s $2.45–$2.62 Street estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year diluted adjusted EPS guidance was cut to approximately $2 per share due to higher depreciation, higher net interest ahead of the Eaton deal, lower China JV equity earnings, and unfavorable tax mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed company FY26 adjusted EPS guidance of “$2.00–3.00 (~$2.50 mid)” and FY26 Street EPS of “~$2.45–2.62.”

surprises.description: Dana restarted buybacks and committed to another $200 million of repurchases before year-end, despite uncertainty in the preview about whether repurchases would continue during the deal process. The company also said its $2 billion authorization is now targeted for completion by 2029 rather than 2030.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Dana is restarting share buybacks with a plan for an additional $200 million in repurchases before year-end 2026,” with the $2 billion authorization “targeted for completion by 2029 (accelerated from 2030).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called the “buyback pace during deal pendency” a key issue and asked “whether Dana keeps buying”; it noted $125 million of Q1 buybacks against a $300 million 2026 target.

surprises.description: Adjusted free cash flow was stronger than the preview’s risk-focused setup implied, and Dana raised its full-year FCF outlook by $25 million to approximately $325 million rather than trimming it. Q2 adjusted FCF was $68 million, improving $75 million year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted free cash flow improved $75 million year-over-year to $68 million,” and “full-year free cash flow guidance was raised $25 million to approximately $325 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1’s $195 million cash burn meant “Q2–Q4 must generate about $495M to reach the midpoint” and identified the FCF line as “most at risk of a quiet trim.”

surprises.description: Dana disclosed a one-time approximately $20 million union signing bonus that will hit Q3, a cash and cost headwind not identified in the preview. The FY FCF guidance was raised despite this payment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A one-time ~$20 million union signing bonus hits Q3.”

surprises.description: The Eaton separation is now structured as a tax-free split-off, and Dana said it can continue buybacks through closing. The preview raised the possibility that the merger agreement might restrict repurchases but had no confirmed answer or update on this structure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Eaton Mobility separation will now be structured as a tax-free split-off, allowing continued buybacks through closing,” with the deal on track to close in Q1 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “I could not confirm whether the merger agreement restricts repurchases during pendency,” and listed deal milestones, including the “Q1 2027 close target,” as items to watch.

surprises.description: Dana provided favorable detail on the cost and payback of the Eaton deal’s synergies: total cash cost to achieve is expected to be under $250 million, with payback in less than two years. The preview flagged integration costs as an open question but had no cost-to-achieve or payback estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: The combined entity targets at least “$250 million in run-rate cost synergies within 24 months (about $75 million in year 1),” with “total cash cost to achieve under $250 million and a payback under two years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “any first estimate of integration or carve-out costs” as a matter that would matter; it also noted the $250 million synergy target.

surprises.description: Dana disclosed that the combination raises its 2030 revenue target to $14–$15 billion from $10 billion standalone, including approximately $1.7 billion in aftermarket sales, and expects pro forma 2026 net leverage of about 1.4x. The preview discussed the pending combination but did not provide these combined-company targets or leverage expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Eaton combination raises the Dana 2030 revenue target to $14–15 billion (from $10 billion standalone), boosts aftermarket sales to approximately $1.7 billion (16% of total), and is expected to maintain pro forma 2026 net leverage of approximately 1.4x.”

surprises.description: Dana said it is still working to eliminate $40 million of stranded Off-Highway costs. This remaining cost burden was not raised in the preview’s discussion of the $325 million savings program.
surprises.fact_evidence: Dana delivered $19 million in Q2 savings and $54 million year to date, while “still working to eliminate $40 million of stranded Off-Highway costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the “$325M” cost program, “$35M realized in Q1,” and “$65M targeted for 2026,” without mentioning stranded Off-Highway costs.

surprises.description: Q2 sales of $2.0 billion exceeded the preview’s $1.92–$1.94 billion consensus range, a modest revenue beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 sales reached $2.0 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus was “$1.94B (range $1.92–1.94B).”

surprises.description: Dana’s 10.3% Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin was below the preview’s implied 10.6%–11.1% range, even though adjusted EBITDA dollars landed within the preview’s implied dollar range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA was $207 million, “delivering a 10.3% margin, up 270 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said implied adjusted EBITDA was “~$205–215M” and implied margin was “~10.6–11.1%.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA of $207 million was within the preview’s implied Q2 range of approximately $205–$215 million.
