The deal remained on track for a Q1 2027 close, consistent with the preview’s stated close target.
The $250 million synergy target was consistent with the preview’s stated target.
Dana remained on track for its $65 million 2026 cost-savings target, as the preview had flagged.

surprises.description: DNOW reported Q2 revenue of $1.3 billion, above the preview’s $1.266 billion to roughly $1.29 billion consensus range and the top of its $1.242 billion–$1.289 billion guidance range. The gap was a modest beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $1.3 billion,” up 10% sequentially.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus was “$1.266B” or “~$1.29B”; company guidance was “$1.242B – $1.289B.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA of $60 million landed within the preview’s implied $54 million–$65 million range, rather than materially exceeding or falling below it. The 4.6% margin was also within the preview’s expected 4.3%–5.0% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $60 million” and “EBITDA margin” was 4.6%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave an implied Q2 EBITDA range of “$54M – $65M (4.3%–5.0% margin).”

surprises.description: Operating cash flow swung to a record $133 million in Q2, overcoming the preview’s concern that another cash-burn quarter would jeopardize the full-year cash target. First-half cash flow was already positive at $38 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company generated a record $133 million in operating cash flow,” driving a “positive $38 million year-to-date cash inflow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a second burn quarter would make the FY cash target very hard to reach.”

surprises.description: The company reduced net debt by $95 million and reached 1.7x trailing leverage in Q2, already inside the preview’s 1–2x year-end path rather than merely progressing toward it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt was reduced by $95 million to $360 million,” lowering leverage to “1.7x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “the guided path to 1–2x by year-end.”

surprises.description: DNOW repurchased $25 million of shares in Q2 and $75 million in the first half, continuing substantial buybacks while the preview had raised questions about the pace at 2.3x leverage. The preview did not specify a Q2 repurchase amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $25 million of shares in Q2 and $75 million in the first half of 2026,” exceeding the share count purchased in the prior 10 quarters combined.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the cash outlook “would raise questions about buyback pace at 2.3x leverage.”

surprises.description: U.S. revenue rose 13% sequentially to $1.1 billion and exceeded company expectations, providing a stronger recovery than the preview’s key question about whether the U.S. business would return to sequential growth after customer attrition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. revenue growing 13% to $1.1 billion, exceeding company expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether the Permian SAP migration “turned into sequential recovery” after Q1 U.S. revenue fell $94 million with customer attrition.

surprises.description: U.S. midstream revenue crossed $1 billion on an annualized basis for the first time. The preview did not identify this milestone as an expectation or give a benchmark for it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. midstream revenue surpassed $1 billion on an annualized basis for the first time.”

surprises.description: Gas utilities grew 15% sequentially to an 11-quarter high, an additional segment strength not anticipated or quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gas utilities grew 15% sequentially to an 11-quarter high.”

surprises.description: DNOW raised its full-year revenue outlook to approximately $5.0 billion–$5.1 billion, improving on the preview’s expectation that it would simply reaffirm revenue “approaching $5.0B.” The EBITDA margin outlook remained around the expected 4.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to approximately $5 billion to $5.1 billion in revenue with EBITDA margin approaching 4.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected FY26 revenue guidance of “Approaching $5.0B” and said the “~4.5%” EBITDA margin needed to be repeated.

surprises.description: Q3 guidance called for low-to-mid single-digit sequential revenue growth and a 5%–5.5% EBITDA margin, which the call facts say was above prior guidance. The preview did not provide a Q3 forecast to benchmark against.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for low-to-mid single-digit sequential revenue growth with EBITDA margin targeted at 5% to 5.5%, above prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview did not state a Q3 guidance expectation.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.12 exceeded the preview’s $0.08–$0.10 consensus estimates, although the company also recorded a GAAP net loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 posted “a GAAP net loss of $21 million ($0.11/share) versus $0.12 adjusted EPS.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed adjusted EPS consensus of “$0.08” or “$0.10.”

surprises.description: DSO improved by seven days and inventory fell by $131 million, reinforcing the working-capital improvement behind the strong cash result. The preview had flagged cash flow and inventory as key concerns but gave no specific Q2 targets for these measures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DSO improved 7 days sequentially to 62 days and inventory fell $131 million to $1.1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Cash flow and inventory” and noted Q1 operating cash flow of negative $95 million.

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $60 million and a 4.6% margin were within the preview’s implied $54 million–$65 million and 4.3%–5.0% ranges.
The full-year EBITDA margin outlook of approximately 4.5% was consistent with the preview’s expected FY26 margin.
The roughly $30 million 2026 exit-rate synergy outlook was already reflected in the preview, which noted that the year-1 synergy run-rate had been raised to about $30 million from $17 million.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.47, above the preview’s aggregate consensus of about $0.41, though it was within the preview’s $0.44–$0.48 base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS grew 47% to $0.47.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS $0.4057 (aggregate)” and base case “$0.44–0.48.”

surprises.description: Core pawn gross profit grew 28% overall, but same-store core pawn gross profit was up only 13%, below the preview’s roughly 18% growth threshold for supporting the thesis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core pawn revenues grew 24% and core pawn gross profit rose 28%, with same-store core pawn gross profit up 13%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Growth above roughly +18% in GP would support the thesis.”

surprises.description: Scrap gross margin was 26%, slightly above the preview’s 20%–25% in-line range, rather than falling fully to the expected normalized range this quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Scrap gross margin fell to 26% from 38% in the prior quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “20–25% is in line”; the base scenario expected scrap to normalize to “about 22–25%.”

surprises.description: Management now expects scrap gross margin to normalize toward 15%–20% if gold prices do not rise further, below the preview’s roughly 22% historical bogey and 20%–25% in-line range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expects continued normalization toward historical levels of 15%-20% if gold prices don't rise further.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a “~22% historical bogey” and said “20–25% is in line.”

surprises.description: Total PLO reached $382 million, a record but below the preview’s roughly $390 million watch level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total PLO reached a record $382 million, up 31%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “PLO versus about $390M” and said consensus implied a record quarter.

surprises.description: EZCORP repurchased $4 million of shares in the quarter, matching the entire $4 million spent during the first half and showing the accelerated buyback pace the preview identified as a possible confidence signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company repurchased “approximately 132,000 shares for $4 million under its $50 million buyback program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Only $4.0M of the $50M buyback was used in H1. An accelerated pace would be read as a confidence signal.”

in_line: Adjusted EPS of $0.47 was within the preview’s $0.44–$0.48 base-case range, even though it exceeded the aggregate consensus estimate.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.65 and adjusted net earnings were $85 million, both below the preview’s $0.78 and roughly $103 million consensus estimates. That is a meaningful earnings miss, rather than the preview’s base case of a modest beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net earnings were $85 million or $0.65 per share in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $0.78” and “Adj. net earnings ~$103M (derived).”

surprises.description: The annualized alternative-investment return fell to 5.9%, well below the preview’s base-case 9–10.5% range and its watchpoint of a return toward 11–12%. This was weaker than even the preview’s bear-case threshold of below 8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Alternative investment income fell to $49 million ($0.38 per share) as the annualized alts return dropped to 5.9% from 8.3% in Q1, well below the 12% long-term expected return.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A return to ~11–12% is worth roughly +$0.15–0.25/share vs. Q1”; the base scenario assumed “Alts 9–10.5%,” while the bear scenario assumed “Alts below 8%.”

surprises.description: Gross sales were $2.7 billion, below the preview’s $3.5–4.0 billion base case. The preview expected stronger overall sales, even though core retail indexed annuity and life sales proved unusually resilient.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross sales were $2.7 billion ($2 billion core, $700 million opportunistic).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base case is gross sales of $3.5–4.0B.”

surprises.description: AUM before reinsurance reached a record, but at $74.7 billion it was below the preview’s $76–77 billion base case. Year-over-year growth was also 8%, versus the 11% growth cited for Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AUM before reinsurance grew 8% year-over-year to a record $74.7 billion at June 30.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base case is … AUM before reinsurance of $76–77B.”

surprises.description: Management’s return outlook was more subdued than the preview’s hoped-for recovery: it expects Q3 alts returns of roughly 7–8% and described a blended return of about 10%. That is below the preview’s 9–10.5% base-case assumption and its expectation that management might reaffirm a 12–14% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects near-term (Q3) alts returns of roughly 7%-8%” and “84% of limited partnerships within their first 10 years suggesting a blended ~10% return.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “reaffirming 12–14%” and used “Alts 9–10.5%” in its base scenario.

surprises.description: The Peak Altitude review moved beyond a general exploration of alternatives: management is targeting a sale of about 51% to a partner. The preview described a full sale as unlikely and said the review was centered on deconsolidation and funding, so a targeted majority-stake transaction is a more concrete step than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Peak Altitude … is being explored for strategic alternatives, targeting sale of ~51% to a partner to unlock value the market currently ascribes little to.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has said a full sale is ‘pretty unlikely,’ with the review centered on deconsolidation and funding.”

surprises.description: Despite the overall sales shortfall, core retail indexed annuity and life sales reached $1.8 billion, described as one of the company’s strongest quarters even as the FIA industry contracted. The preview flagged the core-versus-opportunistic mix but did not anticipate this specific strength.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core retail indexed annuity and life sales of $1.8 billion marking one of the strongest quarters on record despite an industry FIA contraction.”

surprises.description: The company repurchased $120 million of shares in the first half, substantially more than the preview’s $29 million used in Q1 against a stated $100 million authorization. Only $12–15 million remained, while management characterized buybacks as opportunistic rather than a primary capital use.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased 4.5 million shares for $120 million at an average price of $26.44 in the first half, leaving only $12-15 million remaining under authorization,” and “buybacks are opportunistic rather than a primary use of capital.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A $100M buyback was authorized in March 2026, with about $29M used in Q1.”

surprises.description: Fixed-income yield rose to 4.91%, up 14 basis points from Q1, rather than merely holding steady as the preview’s base case assumed. This is a modestly favorable change in investment yield.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fixed income yield rose to 4.91%, up 14 basis points from Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario cited “spreads stable.”

surprises.description: Management quantified the new NAIC CLO capital-charge impact as limited: about 10 RBC points before management action, with the ratio remaining above the 400% target. The preview did not flag this capital issue; the call’s quantified impact was modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New NAIC CLO capital charges are estimated to reduce RBC by only about 10 points before management action, with the company maintaining its RBC ratio above the 400% target.”

surprises.description: KVH ended the quarter with about 10,700 subscribing vessels, above the preview’s expected range of 10,300–10,600 and its 10,600 bull-case threshold. The subscriber growth was therefore stronger than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Added over 1,000 net subscribing vessels in the quarter, ending with approximately 10,700,” an “11% sequential increase.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Look for roughly 10,300–10,600 vessels”; the bull scenario cited “Vessels above 10,600.”

surprises.description: LEO connectivity reached 55% of airtime revenue, a higher share than the preview’s stated baseline of more than 45%, with Starlink described as the fastest-growing segment. This points to a faster shift in the airtime mix than that baseline alone suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LEO connectivity now accounts for 55% of airtime revenue,” with growth driven by Starlink, “their fastest-growing segment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “LEO is now more than 45% of airtime sales.”

surprises.description: KVH disclosed that most of its GEO/VSAT bandwidth commitments expire at the end of 2026, with only a small commitment remaining in 2027. That provides a clearer path to reducing future margin exposure as LEO grows than the preview discussed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GEO/VSAT bandwidth commitments predominantly expire at the end of 2026, with only a small remaining commitment in 2027,” de-risking future margin exposure as LEO grows.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged whether the LEO transition was “margin-neutral or margin-dilutive” and warned that thinner LEO resale margins could pressure service gross margin.

surprises.description: The land-based Starlink business reached about 1,600 sites after adding roughly 500 during the quarter, expanding the recurring revenue base beyond maritime. The preview did not anticipate this scale of land-based activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The land-based Starlink initiative grew to approximately 1,600 sites, an increase of roughly 500 during the quarter,” broadening recurring revenue beyond maritime.

surprises.description: KVH launched new multi-network service plans spanning Starlink, OneWeb, and VSAT during the quarter. This was an unpreviewed expansion of its service offering.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New multi-network service plans (spanning Starlink, OneWeb, and VSAT) launched this quarter.”

surprises.description: Managed IT and cybersecurity services moved from pilots into recurring-revenue conversions, an unpreviewed sign that these offerings are beginning to monetize.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Managed IT/cybersecurity services began converting from pilots into recurring revenue.”

surprises.description: Link streaming advanced into beta trials, an unpreviewed product-development milestone, though it is not yet described as recurring revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Link streaming entered beta trials.”

surprises.description: Cash declined only $1.4 million despite $2.3 million of stock repurchases, and management said it expected to complete the full $15 million buyback authorization within the month. The preview focused on cash and the Starlink commitment but did not anticipate this buyback timing or cash movement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ending cash balance fell $1.4 million to $57.7 million, primarily due to $2.3 million in stock repurchases,” and “the full $15 million buyback authorization is expected to be completed and concluded within the current month.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash at 6/30 shows how much of the $45M pool remains to be funded.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $33.7 million, matching the preview’s $33.7 million consensus.
Service gross margin was 36%, modestly above Q1’s 35% and consistent with the preview’s expectation of 35% or better.
Adjusted EBITDA was $3.0 million, above the preview’s stated Q2 stress threshold of about $2.8 million.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.37, roughly double the preview’s $0.185–$0.19 consensus, despite falling from $0.54 a year earlier. This was a much larger beat than the preview’s base-case range of $0.17–$0.21.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS fell to $0.37 from $0.54 a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | $0.185–0.19”; base case: “Adj. EPS $0.17–0.21.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $1.04 billion exceeded both the $1.009 billion consensus and the top of the company’s $1.003–$1.025 billion guidance range. The preview’s bull case reached $1.040 billion, but its base case was lower.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $1.04 billion … well ahead of guidance of down 7% to 9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $1,009.3M”; company guidance “−7% to −9% y/y → $1,003–1,025M”; base case “$1,005–1,020M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 3.0%, beating the 2.5% floor and the preview’s derived estimate of about 2.6%. The 150-basis-point sequential improvement was also stronger than the preview’s cited expectation of about 100 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin returned to 3% ($31.1 million), exceeding guidance of at least 2.5% and improving 150 basis points sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Company guidance: “≥2.5% (~+100 bps q/q)”; preview derivation: “~2.6%.”

surprises.description: Management now forecasts a low- to mid-single-digit full-year revenue decline and 10–20 basis points of adjusted EBITDA margin improvement, while describing this as a raised outlook. The preview had only cited unquantified expectations for modest second-half revenue growth and measurable margin expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year expectations, now projecting a low-to-mid single-digit revenue decline and 10 to 20 basis points of adjusted EBITDA margin improvement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management expects modest y/y revenue growth and measurable adjusted EBITDA margin expansion in the second half of 2026; it has not quantified 2H.”

surprises.description: The Q4 outlook calls for mid- to upper-single-digit revenue growth and roughly 200 basis points of margin expansion to about 4%, providing a more specific and stronger late-year outlook than the preview’s unquantified second-half language. However, the 53rd week contributes about four points of revenue growth and weighs on the projected margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 guidance calls for mid- to upper-single-digit revenue growth and roughly 200 basis points of margin expansion to about 4%, but includes a 53rd fiscal week that adds ~4 points to revenue while negatively impacting adjusted EBITDA margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management expects modest y/y revenue growth and measurable adjusted EBITDA margin expansion in the second half of 2026; it has not quantified 2H.”

surprises.description: SET revenue grew sequentially for the first time in two years, an inflection the preview did not identify, although the segment still had a 3% year-over-year decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SET revenue grew sequentially for the first time in two years, marking a claimed inflection point, though underlying revenue still declined 3% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: ETM underlying revenue grew 3.1% year over year, with Talent Solutions up about 6% and RPO and MSP specialties both posting double-digit growth. The preview focused on an expected company-wide underlying decline and did not identify this segment growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ETM underlying revenue grew 3.1% year-over-year while Talent Solutions grew about 6% with both RPO and MSP specialties posting double-digit growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Underlying revenue decline ex-discrete items” was the preview’s key metric to watch; it cited a company-wide expectation of “about −2.3% or better.”

surprises.description: SET outcome-based solutions reached 40% of segment revenue, up from roughly one-third a year earlier, as Kelly intentionally shifted toward milestone- and SLA-based work. The preview did not flag this mix shift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SET outcome-based solutions rose to 40% of SET's total revenue, up from roughly one-third a year ago, reflecting an intentional shift toward higher-margin milestone and SLA-based work.”

surprises.description: Kelly cut net debt by $52.4 million to $78.1 million, a substantial debt reduction not specified in the preview’s expectation of a seasonal free-cash-flow reversal. Management said capital allocation remains focused on debt paydown while it eyes potential acquisitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company generated $47.7 million of free cash flow, cut net debt by $52.4 million to $78.1 million … keeping capital allocation focused on debt paydown while eyeing potential acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q2 should seasonally reverse” Q1 free cash flow of −$26.5 million; it did not specify a debt-paydown target.

in_line: Free cash flow turned positive in Q2, as the preview expected a seasonal reversal from Q1’s negative $26.5 million.
The quarterly dividend remained $0.075, matching the preview’s note that the dividend had been maintained.

surprises.description: MetLife reported adjusted EPS of $2.43, above the preview’s $2.30–$2.36 working consensus. The 15% year-over-year earnings growth was within the preview’s expected growth range, but the per-share result was higher than estimated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted earnings of approximately $1.6 billion or $2.43 per share, up 15% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $2.30” and “Adjusted EPS (alt.) $2.36”; the preview says to treat “$2.30–$2.36 as the working consensus.”

surprises.description: Group Benefits’ 79% Group Life mortality ratio was even lower than the preview’s low-80s expectation, contributing to standout earnings. Management cautioned that about 2 points of the favorable result were non-recurring and expected to normalize, consistent with the preview’s concern that some underwriting strength could be temporary.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Group Benefits delivered standout adjusted earnings of $503 million, up 25%,” with a “Group Life mortality ratio of 79%,” and “~2 points as non-recurring favorability expected to normalize.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Mortality ratio still in the low 80s” and the preview asks whether the favorable run “is structural” or “a one-off.”

surprises.description: RIS total investment spread was 97 basis points, below the 100–120 bps guidance range, despite core spread ex-VII reaching 100 bps. The preview had focused on whether core spread would reach 100 bps, so the shortfall in the total spread—attributed to weak private equity returns—was the weaker result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total investment spread of 97 basis points fell below the 100-120 bps guidance range due to weak private equity returns,” while “core spread ex-VII was 100 bps.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Does core spread print at or above 100bps, and does RIS stay on track for $1.6–1.8B?”

surprises.description: MetLife announced a new $3 billion share repurchase authorization and had already returned over $2.4 billion to shareholders year-to-date through July. The preview identified a fresh authorization as a possible positive surprise, but the announced authorization and cumulative return were substantial.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company announced a new $3 billion share repurchase authorization,” repurchased “~$700 million” in Q2 and “~$225 million in July,” and returned “over $2.4 billion to shareholders year-to-date through July.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A fresh buyback authorization is a plausible positive surprise” and “A buyback refresh would be the most likely positive surprise not in consensus.”

surprises.description: Asia adjusted earnings rose 21% (25% in constant currency), above the preview’s 14.1% expectation, while sales also grew strongly in constant currency. This was stronger than the preview’s concern that growth might moderate against tough comparisons.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Asia adjusted earnings rose 21% (25% constant currency) to $420 million, with sales up 17% constant currency.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus expects +14.1% adjusted earnings” and management had “warned of moderating growth against tough comparisons.”

surprises.description: Despite a roughly 50-basis-point PineBridge acquisition drag, the direct expense ratio was 12.1%, and management now expects to beat that full-year target. The quarterly ratio matched the preview’s target, but the full-year expectation is better than simply meeting it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The direct expense ratio was 12.1%, absorbing a ~50 basis point drag from the PineBridge acquisition,” and management “expects to beat its 12.1% full-year 2026 target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Direct expense ratio target 12.1%.”

surprises.description: MetLife Investment Management expects full-year adjusted earnings toward the low end of its $240–280 million range. The preview did not flag this business or indicate that earnings might land near the bottom of its range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “MetLife Investment Management grew AUM to approximately $748 billion” but “expects full-year adjusted earnings toward the low end of its $240-280 million guidance range.”

surprises.description: MetLife said Latin America posted record quarterly adjusted earnings and is on track to reach $1 billion in annual earnings, roughly double pre-pandemic levels. The preview did not discuss this segment or this earnings trajectory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Latin America posted record quarterly adjusted earnings of $268 million (up 15%, 4% constant currency) and is on track to reach $1 billion in annual earnings, roughly double pre-pandemic levels.”

in_line: Adjusted ROE was 17%, at the top of the 15%–17% target range, as the preview expected.
RIS core spread ex-VII reached 100 bps, matching the preview’s key threshold, although total spread fell short of its guidance range.
Adjusted EPS growth of 15% was within the preview’s cited 13.9%–16.8% consensus growth estimates, even though reported EPS of $2.43 exceeded the working per-share consensus.

surprises.description: The preview expected Q2 adjusted EBITDA of about $230–240 million, with sell-side estimates clustered at or just above the high end. Kinetik reported $281 million, well above that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 was a record quarter with adjusted EBITDA of $281 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$230–240M (Q2) | Sell-side clusters at or just above the high end.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for a possible raise toward the low end or upper half of the existing FY26 range. Instead, Kinetik raised the midpoint by $70 million to $1.04–$1.10 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Kinetik raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance by $70 million (7%) at the midpoint to a new range of $1.04 billion to $1.1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for a raise to the low end or ‘upper half’ language.”

surprises.description: The preview said guidance assumed Waha curtailments would persist through December. Kinetik reported about 250 MMcf/d of Q2 curtailments but expects them to fall to about 25 MMcf/d in the second half, with none assumed in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Processed natural gas volumes were flat year-over-year at 1.74 Bcf/d despite an estimated 250 MMcf/d of Waha price-related curtailments, which are expected to fall to about 25 MMcf/d for the second half of 2026 with none assumed in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management modeled about 220 MMcf/d of average full-year Waha-related shut-ins and assumed curtailments persist through December.”

surprises.description: The preview noted that volume growth guidance had been cut to low-to-mid single digits. Kinetik now expects to exit 2026 at about 2.2 Bcf/d, implying roughly 10% growth from the normalized current run rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects to exit 2026 approaching 2.2 Bcf/d of processed gas volumes (a Q4 average), implying roughly 10% growth from the normalized ~1.96 Bcf/d current run rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Volume growth cut from high-single-digit to low-to-mid-single-digit.”

surprises.description: The preview put FY26 capital spending at $450–510 million. Kinetik raised its 2026 capex guidance to approximately $560 million, above the preview’s range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2026 capital expenditure guidance was raised to approximately $560 million, driven by Kings Landing II, optimization projects, compression equipment purchases, and pulled-forward customer development spending concentrated in Delaware South.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 capex (incl. maintenance) | $450–510M.”

surprises.description: The preview described Kings Landing II as a 300 MMcf/d project expected in service in 2H 2028. Kinetik said completion is now accelerated to mid-2028, bringing it forward within that expected window.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Kinetik increased Kings Landing II processing capacity by 50% to 300 MMcf/d and accelerated its completion to mid-2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Kings Landing II received FID on May 19, 2026: 300 MMcf/d, about $260M, in service 2H 2028.”

surprises.description: The preview reported Midstream Logistics growth of 12% in Q1; Q2 growth accelerated to 35% year over year. The preview did not provide a Q2 segment estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Midstream Logistics adjusted EBITDA grew 35% year-over-year to $205 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Midstream Logistics $178.9M (+12% YoY).”

surprises.description: Kinetik’s updated guidance uses materially higher WTI and liquids price assumptions than in February. The preview focused on curtailments and marketing gains but did not flag this change in the pricing assumptions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Updated guidance assumes a nearly 30% increase in WTI pricing and nearly 20% increase in liquids pricing versus February assumptions, with the company substantially hedged at the top of its 40%-80% target range.”

in_line: Pipeline Transportation fell to $83 million, primarily due to the EPIC Crude divestiture, consistent with the preview’s discussion of the divestiture-related decline.
The $0.81 dividend was maintained, and the dividend remained the stated capital-return lever, consistent with the preview’s question about whether it would remain the only capital-return lever.

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $0.08, below the preview’s $0.12–$0.13 consensus range and its $0.09–$0.10 base case. GAAP results also slipped to a $0.01-per-share loss; the preview had warned that the expected SG&A step-up could pressure operating income, but had no GAAP EPS consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income fell to $1 million ($0.08/share) from $1.8 million ($0.15/share)” and “GAAP results swung to a net loss of $0.1 million (negative $0.01 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS, non-GAAP diluted | $0.12 – $0.13”; the base scenario forecast “~$0.09–0.10.” The preview also said the SG&A step-up “determines whether GAAP operating income stays positive.”

surprises.description: Data & AI revenue reached $13.5 million, above the preview’s roughly $13 million base case, and grew 7.2% sequentially—the segment’s first sequential growth since 2024. That was a better near-term trend than the preview’s baseline anticipated, though the segment remained down 14.4% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Data and AI segment grew 7.2% sequentially to $13.5 million, marking its first quarter of sequential growth since 2024, despite being down 14.4% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “Data & AI about $13M”; the bull scenario expected “Data & AI at or above $14M.”

surprises.description: A single top-10 client’s insourcing accounted for nearly 90% of the Talent headcount reduction, but excluding that client, Talent revenue would have declined only about 3% year over year rather than the reported 16.2%. This confirms the preview’s client-concentration risk while showing that the broader Talent business was less weak than the headline decline suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Insourcing from a single top-10 client accounting for nearly 90% of the headcount reduction”; “Excluding the one insourcing client, talent revenue would have declined only about 3% year-over-year, versus the reported 16.2% drop.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Further insourcing” as “the largest downside risk” and highlighted client concentration as a key issue to watch.

surprises.description: The average bill rate rose to a new high of $92.17, up from the prior-quarter record of $90.91, rather than rolling over. This was favorable versus the preview’s concern that a rollover could indicate volume loss rather than mix improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Average bill rates hit an all-time high of $92.17, up from $88.36.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Average bill rate vs. $90.91/hr” and said “A rollover would suggest volume loss rather than mix improvement.”

surprises.description: The company won a strategic AI engagement with a major U.S. convenience-store chain operating more than 10,000 stores globally, an account win the preview did not identify or forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Won a strategic AI engagement with a major U.S. convenience store chain operating over 10,000 stores globally.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $41.4 million modestly exceeded the preview’s $40.8 million aggregator estimate, although it was just below the preview’s $41.8 million base scenario. The result was therefore close to expectations overall, with a small beat versus the consensus anchor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated Q2 2026 revenue was $41.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The consensus table listed Q2 revenue at “$40.8M”; the base scenario forecast “$41.8M.”

in_line: Talent revenue was $28 million, close to the preview’s base-case estimate of about $28.5 million.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $65.5 million beat the preview’s $62.5–$63.5 million company range and roughly $63.3 million buy-side whisper. The beat was qualified by management’s disclosure that underlying organic growth, excluding FX and Martino, was mid-single digits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 6.4% year-over-year to $65.5 million,” with “a $700,000 positive FX impact”; excluding FX and the Martino acquisition, “underlying organic growth was mid-single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave Q2 revenue guidance of “$62.5M – $63.5M” and said the buy-side whisper was “roughly $63.3M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA came in above the top of the preview’s guidance range, and the double-digit growth streak continued rather than ending as the preview thought likely. The 14.3% adjusted EBITDA margin also exceeded the preview’s 13.5% threshold; operating income and operating margin reached reported highs as well.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA “grew 12.9% to $9.4 million—the seventh consecutive quarter of double-digit EBITDA growth,” and margin “expanded 80 basis points to 14.3%.” Operating income “rose 25.6% to $5.9 million” with an “8.9% operating margin at a three-year high.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$8.0M – $9.0M,” said the double-digit growth streak “likely ends this quarter,” and flagged whether margin would hold “at or above 13.5%.”

surprises.description: Recurring revenue grew and reached a record, but its share of total revenue remained below the 50% milestone the preview highlighted as a key bull thesis and catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recurring revenue hit a record $30 million (up 7%), now roughly 45%-47% of total revenue,” with management targeting “over 50% within the next couple of years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Recurring crossing 50%” as one of the two items bulls cite and listed “Recurring revenue crossing 50%” in the catalyst checklist.

surprises.description: The Board authorized a $30 million repurchase program, the largest in company history, and management said buybacks should accelerate in the second half—an unflagged capital-allocation development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board approved a new $30 million share repurchase authorization—the largest in company history—with management guiding investors to expect accelerated buybacks in the second half.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS reached $0.10, above the preview’s $0.08–$0.09 estimate range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS improved to $0.10 from $0.08 a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed adjusted EPS estimates of “$0.08 – $0.09 (sources disagree).”

surprises.description: Management added a more cautious note not anticipated in the preview: client decisions remain measured, and acquisition valuations have become frothier. That tempers the otherwise strong reported growth picture.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management noted “M&A valuations are becoming more 'frothy' than a year ago while client decision-making pace remains measured.”

in_line: AI-related revenue rose 64% to $26 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation that AI revenue growth would stay well above 50%.
Americas revenue returned to year-over-year growth, as management had explicitly guided; it rose 6.7% to $42.1 million.
Q3 revenue guidance of $63.5–$64.5 million was in line with the preview’s estimate of roughly $63.5–$64.5 million needed to hold FY consensus.
APAC revenue of $5.1 million versus $4.1 million in Q1 implies roughly 24% sequential growth, close to management’s prior guidance for roughly 20% sequential Q2 growth.

surprises.description: Murphy had been expected to keep 2026 capital spending within its $1.2–1.3 billion range, but raised the midpoint to $1.55 billion, with nearly all of the roughly $300 million increase going to organic growth. The spending supports projects including Bubale and Eagle Ford, but is a substantial increase over the expected budget.
surprises.fact_evidence: “raised its 2026 capital expenditure midpoint from $1.25 billion to $1.55 billion, with nearly all of the ~$300 million increase supporting organic growth”; roughly $190 million is tied to Bubale and an additional $70 million to Eagle Ford.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 capex | $1.2–1.3B, ~70% H1-weighted (reaffirmed in Q1)” and the base case was “FY guidance reaffirmed but not raised.”

surprises.description: The Hai Su Vang-4X well was dry and Murphy revised the resource estimate downward, contrary to the preview’s focus on appraisal results and potential for a resource upgrade. The field remains a material opportunity, but management also said production may trend toward the lower end of its unchanged peak outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Hai Su Vang-4X well in Vietnam was a dry hole, prompting a downward resource revision”; peak production remains 30,000–50,000 boe/d, though results “may trend toward the lower end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Hai Su Vang appraisal: recoverable resource already expanded to >430 MMBOE; full program results due Q3 2026”; the bull scenario included “a Hai Su Vang resource upgrade.”

surprises.description: After recent noncommercial Côte d’Ivoire wells had made further exploration losses a concern, Murphy reported that Bubale encountered oil in both the Turonian and Cenomanian reservoirs. This is a favorable exploration result, although two of the three wells were noncommercial.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Bubale discovery in Côte d'Ivoire encountered oil in both the Turonian and Cenomanian reservoirs after the first two of three exploration wells were noncommercial.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified exploration expense as a key issue and said “another Côte d'Ivoire write-off could outweigh a headline beat.”

surprises.description: Management said 2027 capital spending will likely exceed the prior $1.2–1.3 billion range and could rise further depending on Bubale appraisal results. It also warned that free cash flow could turn negative in some periods before Hai Su Vang first oil, a more cautious outlook than a simple continuation of the prior spending range would imply.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2027 CapEx will likely exceed the prior $1.2-1.3 billion range and could go higher depending on Bubale appraisal results,” and “free cash flow could turn negative in some periods before Hai Su Vang first oil.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “FY guidance reaffirmed but not raised”; it also listed “cautious FCF framing at a lower strip” as a bear scenario.

surprises.description: Second-quarter production reached the top of the company’s guided range, rather than merely landing around the preview’s base-case level near the midpoint. Tupper Montney and Eagle Ford were cited as the sources of the outperformance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Second quarter production averaged 169,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, above the midpoint of guidance, led by Tupper Montney and Eagle Ford outperformance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 production guidance was “161–169 MBOEPD”; the preview’s base case anticipated “Volumes near 165 MBOEPD.”

in_line: Lac Da Vang’s fourth-quarter 2026 first-oil target was reaffirmed, consistent with the preview’s expectation that management would confirm Q4 2026 first oil.

surprises.description: The preview expected FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to be raised or maintained, but Maximus cut the guidance midpoint by about $0.35, from $8.40 to $8.05, after a customer-directed pause in VA MDE performance incentives.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A customer-directed pause in VA MDE performance incentives, effective July 1, 2026, cut full-year diluted EPS guidance by roughly $0.35, lowering the midpoint to $8.05 from $8.40.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adjusted EPS guidance: third consecutive raise? … A raise to roughly $8.45–8.75 would be the cleanest bull signal. A maintain would likely read as the margin story stalling.”

surprises.description: Cash generation was weaker than the preview’s already demanding outlook: Q3 free cash flow was a $137 million outflow, DSO reached 98 days, and full-year free cash flow guidance was cut to $425–475 million. Collections of about $245 million since June 30 support management’s expectation that DSO will fall below 70 days by year-end, but do not erase the quarter’s shortfall or the guide reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow guidance was reduced to $425-475 million, and Q3 saw a free cash flow outflow of $137 million with DSO elevated at 98 days due to a major federal customer's administrative delays”; “about $245 million received since June 30” and DSO is expected to “finish the fiscal year below 70 days.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The $450–500M FY guide therefore requires roughly $520–570M in 2H”; “DSO (78 days at March 31) stays elevated through June 30 and falls below 70 days only by fiscal year-end.”

surprises.description: The VA MDE incentive pause is expected to last at least through December 31, leaving no incentives in Q1 FY27, and management said Q4’s roughly 13% EBITDA margin is a reasonable near-term run rate. The preview did not anticipate this duration or the near-term margin level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The incentive pause is assumed to continue through at least December 31, 2026, meaning no incentives are expected in Q1 fiscal 2027, and management flagged the ~13% Q4 EBITDA margin as a reasonable near-term run rate.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin was 15.0%, above the preview’s estimated 14.2–14.4% range, with the improvement attributed to efficiency gains rather than surge volumes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 15.0% from 14.7%, driven by efficiency gains rather than surge volumes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin ~14.2–14.4% (est.).”

surprises.description: Awarded-but-unsigned contracts rose significantly to $1.35 billion, a stronger leading-award signal than the preview’s cited $322 million in YTD awarded-but-unsigned work, even though trailing book-to-bill remained low.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Awarded-but-unsigned contracts stepped up significantly to $1.35 billion, driven by longer-term recompete wins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “YTD signed awards were $913M, with $322M awarded but unsigned”; the preview said a move back toward 1.0x book-to-bill would address the durability question.

surprises.description: Management quantified stronger AI adoption and contract-level benefits than the preview specified: 75–80% of new bids and rebids now include explicit AI requirements, and AI-based improvements raised operating margin by 3.5% across five contracts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly 75-80% of new bids and rebids now include explicit AI requirements, and AI-based process improvements across just five contracts delivered a 3.5% operating margin improvement for that group.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview referred to “AI/automation margin capture” as a driver of prior EPS guidance raises, but did not quantify AI requirements in bids or contract-level margin improvement.

in_line: Q3 revenue of $1.28 billion was within the preview’s guidance-implied range and its $1.28–1.33 billion base scenario, although below the $1.33 billion consensus estimate; the preview anticipated revenue could be light versus consensus while consistent with guidance.
Adjusted EPS of $2.22 was essentially in line with the $2.21 consensus and within the preview’s base-case range of $2.20–2.29.

Full-year revenue guidance was reiterated at $5.2–5.35 billion, with a bias toward the lower end, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the range would be maintained and could be framed toward its lower end.
Trailing-12-month book-to-bill remained about 0.5x, matching the preview’s cited 0.5x level and its concern about sub-1.0x book-to-bill.
Despite June 30 DSO of 98 days, management still expects DSO below 70 days by fiscal year-end, as the preview had anticipated; collections since June 30 accelerated.
The Q3 share repurchase was consistent with the preview’s expectation that buybacks would contribute to the EPS result.

surprises.description: Retail adjusted EBITDAR came in above the preview’s $505–515 million estimate, and the 34.4% margin also topped the 33.5% watch-point despite the Aurora transition. PENN reported $517.2 million of retail adjusted EBITDAR and record quarterly retail revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retail segment achieved record quarterly revenues of $1.5 billion and adjusted EBITDAR of $517.2 million,” with “margins of 34.4% and 9 properties setting Q2 records.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Retail revenue ~$1.50B; retail adj. EBITDAR ~$505–515M”; “Retail adj. EBITDAR vs. ~$505M / 33.5% margin, with the Aurora shutdown quantified.”

surprises.description: PENN raised its 2026 retail outlook rather than merely reaffirming the existing range: the new adjusted EBITDAR midpoint is $1.963 billion, up from the prior $1.93 billion midpoint, and revenue guidance is also higher. The preview’s base case anticipated reaffirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PENN raised its full-year 2026 retail guidance to $5.87 billion revenue and $1.963 billion adjusted EBITDAR at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY guide reaffirmed”; the preview also said, “Any trim to the $1.88–1.98B EBITDAR range is the bear trigger.”

surprises.description: Management reported a stronger company-wide 2026 trajectory than the preview specified, saying PENN is on track for more than 20% year-over-year adjusted EBITDAR growth and faster-than-expected deleveraging. The preview discussed leverage progress but did not anticipate this growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PENN is on track to deliver more than 20% year-over-year adjusted EBITDAR growth in 2026,” enabling “faster-than-expected deleveraging.”

surprises.description: Interactive revenue was below the preview’s modeled Q2 range: $349.4 million versus $355–375 million, even though the reported amount included a $185.5 million skin-tax gross-up.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Interactive segment posted revenues of $349.4 million (including a $185.5 million skin tax gross-up).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Interactive revenue ~$355–375M.”

surprises.description: PENN lowered its 2026 Interactive revenue outlook to $1.57 billion from $1.6 billion, a trim not anticipated in the preview. It maintained the planned $20 million full-year adjusted EBITDA loss and Q4 profitability outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PENN lowered its 2026 Interactive revenue guidance to $1.57 billion from $1.6 billion but maintained its full-year Interactive adjusted EBITDA loss guidance of $20 million ... with Q4 expected to turn positive.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Interactive revenue ~$1.6B”; “Interactive adj. EBITDA −$20M”; “positive in Q4.”

surprises.description: Aurora’s early operating indicators were stronger than the preview’s emphasis on the known shutdown drag suggested: the new property roughly doubled several activity and revenue measures versus the prior year, and brought in new guests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hollywood Casino Aurora, opened June 24, roughly doubled admissions, slot volumes, table volumes and non-gaming revenue versus prior year,” with “20% of guests being new to the property.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “a ~2-week shutdown of the legacy riverboat in late May/early June, a known drag on Q2 retail,” and said “The Aurora riverboat closure and opening costs argue for a soft margin.”

surprises.description: Hollywood Columbus had an especially strong first full month with its new hotel tower, setting an all-time net revenue record and drawing substantial outer-market hotel business; the preview noted the tower opening but gave no such performance expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hollywood Columbus set an all-time net revenue record in July, its first full month with the new hotel tower, with outer-market guests accounting for 85% of hotel cash revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Hollywood Casino Columbus hotel tower opened June 12.”

surprises.description: PENN cut its 2026 capital spending outlook, improving the cash-flow outlook versus the preview’s $420 million CapEx figure. Management also said the retail EBITDA guidance increase flows fully into improved cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PENN reduced 2026 project CapEx to $180 million from $200 million (total CapEx cut to $400 million), and the $31 million retail EBITDA guidance increase flows fully into improved cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capex $420M.”

surprises.description: PENN extended debt maturities, repaid convertible notes to remove potential dilution, and set a lease-adjusted leverage target below 5x. This was stronger balance-sheet action than the preview’s stated 5.3–5.7x leverage range to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Refinancing its $1 billion revolver and Term Loan A to 2031, extending Term Loan B to 2033, and repaying $106.7 million of convertible notes to eliminate 4.5 million potentially dilutive shares, targeting lease-adjusted net leverage below 5x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Progress toward 5.3–5.7x lease-adjusted leverage.”

in_line: Interactive adjusted EBITDA loss was $9.5 million, within the preview’s expectation of a small loss; full-year loss guidance remained $20 million and management still expected Q4 to turn positive.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $128.9 million, well above the preview’s $114.0–$116.1 million consensus range. That is a substantially larger beat than the preview’s bull scenario of $122–$126 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales rose 19% year-over-year to $128.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales (Q2) … $116.1M (MarketBeat, Jul 29) or $114.0M (ChartMill).” The bull scenario anticipated “$122–126M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $17.9 million, above the preview’s estimated $14.5–15.0 million and even slightly above its $17–18 million bull-case range’s lower end. The 13.9% margin also cleared the preview’s 13% threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA increased 36% to $17.9 million with margins expanding 170 basis points to 13.9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (Q2) … my estimate ~$14.5–15.0M”; the bull scenario anticipated “$17–18M.” The preview said “a print of 13% or higher” would support the accelerated target.

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year sales and EBITDA guidance rather than leaving the prior ranges in place: the new midpoints are $470 million in sales and $60 million in adjusted EBITDA, versus prior midpoints of $460 million and $57 million. The sales range also reaches $480 million, above the preview’s $475 million raise threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year guidance to sales of $460-480 million, adjusted EBITDA of $55-65 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior FY26 guidance was “$450–470M” in sales and “$52–62M” in adjusted EBITDA. The preview said “A raise above $475M would support the liquid-cooling ramp” and listed a “guide to upper half, not a true raise” as its base case.

surprises.description: The refinancing was a preview-identified possibility, but the reported transaction included a quantified reduction in preferred-stock interest costs: the pick rate fell from 14.5% to 10%, cutting annual pick interest by about $13 million. The preview did not specify savings of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed a $124 million refinancing” that reduced the pick rate “from 14.5% to 10%” and reduced annual pick interest “by approximately $13 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “refinancing options were under review” and flagged “Use of the $75M PIPE and any refinancing.”

surprises.description: The updated new-business-wins guidance lifted the top of the range by $10 million, from $90 million to $100 million, though its $80 million floor was unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year guidance to … new business wins of $80-100 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 new business wins guidance of “$80–90M” and highlighted results versus that range as a key metric.

surprises.description: The preview looked for a hard 2027 data-center or liquid-cooling revenue figure. The call instead gave an $80 million trailing-12-month business level and a $120 million near-term target, without a dated 2027 figure in the supplied facts; it also described a pipeline and an expected monthly sales milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The data center/electric grid business is currently $80 million on a trailing-12-month basis with a near-term target of $120 million and a prospecting pipeline approaching $100 million”; 50 machines are being installed, with monthly sales expected to exceed $1 million starting in November.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A hard 2027 dollar figure is what the buy side is looking for”; the preview also noted that a 2027 data-center or liquid-cooling figure had been promised.

surprises.description: The refinancing involved another 5.5 million shares, taking shares outstanding from the 77.1 million reported after the PIPE to 82.6 million and leaving only 7.4 million of the 90 million authorized shares available. The preview flagged the PIPE and possible refinancing, but did not anticipate this additional share issuance or how little authorized common stock would remain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The refinancing swapped 5.5 million shares for the preferred reduction, bringing shares outstanding to 82.6 million out of 90 million authorized, exhausting available common stock.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said shares outstanding had risen “from 52.7M to 77.1M” after the PIPE and flagged “Use of the $75M PIPE and any refinancing.”

surprises.description: Management raised its long-term adjusted EBITDA margin target to 14–16%, a more specific and higher target than the preview’s discussion of a 13% quarterly margin supporting the accelerated 2029 target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its long-term adjusted EBITDA margin target to 14-16%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a print of 13% or higher would support the accelerated 2029 target” and identified the accelerated target timing, but did not cite a 14–16% long-term margin target.

surprises.description: The call disclosed a multi-year defense weapons agreement worth $12–15 million from one customer, along with medical, data-center, and defense wins that are expected to ramp entirely in the second half. These specific awards and their back-loaded timing were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recently announced wins in medical, data center, and defense will not impact first-half results and ramp up entirely in the second half, including a multi-year defense weapons agreement worth $12-15 million from one customer.”

surprises.description: Management reported a 27% win rate on closed opportunities and more than 150 programs in ramp-up mode, and said new capital investments must meet a 25% floor for both gross margin and IRR. The preview did not identify these pipeline and investment thresholds as expected call disclosures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is running a 27% win rate on closed opportunities, has over 150 programs in ramp-up mode,” with “a 25% floor on both gross margin and IRR for new capital investments.”

in_line: A refinancing was already a preview-identified potential catalyst; the surprise was the reported transaction’s specific interest-cost reduction and share terms.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $117.1 million, around 9–11% above the preview’s $105.3–$106.96 million consensus range and above even its $112 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record quarterly revenue of $117.1 million in Q2 2026,” up 89.6% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $105.3M | $106.96M”; the bull scenario expected “$112M+.”

surprises.description: Bookings and backlog substantially exceeded the preview’s base case: book-to-bill was 1.42 rather than the expected sub-1.0x to roughly 1.0x, and backlog reached a record $542.1 million. The backlog mix also shifted toward Defense Tech compared with Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bookings of $165.8 million produced a 1.42 book-to-bill for the quarter and 1.52 on an LTM basis, driving record backlog of $542.1 million (up 64.5% year-over-year), split $322 million Space and $220.2 million Defense Tech.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Expect a sequential step-down from the IDIQ-inflated Q1”; “Sub-1.0x to ~1.0x is a reasonable base case.”

surprises.description: Defense Tech revenue reached $61.9 million, well above the preview’s $47–50 million modeled range, while Space revenue was close to its modeled range. Management also expects Defense Tech to grow faster than Space.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Defense Tech revenue reached $61.9 million (up ~40% sequentially, largely from the Edge Autonomy acquisition) versus Space revenue of $55.2 million,” with “double-digit growth in both segments but faster growth in Defense Tech” expected.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “No published consensus for segments. Modeled off Q1 mix: Space ~$55–58M, Defense Tech ~$47–50M.”

surprises.description: The company used far more of its ATM capacity than the preview’s estimated share-count range implied: shares reached 249.9 million versus a projected 215–225 million. The proceeds also sharply strengthened the balance sheet, cut debt and reduced interest expense.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash rising over 6x to $557.8 million (aided by $487.9 million in net ATM proceeds), total debt cut 75% to $48.9 million, and net interest expense falling to under $1 million from $23.8 million a year earlier.” “The equity raise pushed common shares outstanding to 249.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch the diluted share count (likely ~215–225M) and any post-quarter ATM draws.” The preview also noted a $500 million ATM had been authorized.

surprises.description: Gross margin reached a record 27.8%, above the preview’s 26%+ durability threshold, but management cautioned that margins could return to the low-to-mid 20s in the near term because of potential EAC adjustments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin hit a record 27.8%, though management guided expectations back to the low-to-mid 20s range near term due to potential future EAC adjustments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Holding 26%+ supports a structural mix shift; slipping toward 22–23% suggests Q1 was a mix artifact.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a high eight-figure, multiyear Penguin Mk3 contract with a NATO customer, larger and more specific than the preview’s expectation that publicly disclosed Q2 awards would be much smaller.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A high eight-figure multiyear Penguin Mk3 contract with a NATO customer.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Publicly disclosed Q2 awards are much smaller.”

surprises.description: Redwire was selected as one of 15 vendors on the $981 million NITE-STAR IDIQ. The preview did not anticipate this selection; it is a vendor position on the IDIQ, not a stated $981 million award to Redwire.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Selection as 1 of 15 vendors on the $981 million NITE-STAR IDIQ.”

surprises.description: SpaceMD agreed to purchase an entire SpaceX Starfall spacecraft for a 2028 launch, with capacity for up to 32 PIL-BOXes—a new, long-dated commercial development not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SpaceMD's agreement to purchase an entire SpaceX Starfall spacecraft (launching 2028) capable of carrying up to 32 PIL-BOXes.”

surprises.description: Inventory rose 23% sequentially and management expects it to rise further in Q3 to support faster UAS delivery turnaround. The preview did not flag this buildup, which is an added operational investment alongside the stated delivery objective.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory rose 23% sequentially (with further increases expected in Q3) to support faster UAS delivery turnaround.”

in_line: Redwire reaffirmed its FY2026 revenue guidance of $450–500 million, as the preview’s base case expected the guide to be reaffirmed without narrowing.
Adjusted EBITDA remained negative, consistent with the preview’s expectation that it would still be negative; the preview provided no specific Q2 EBITDA estimate.
Space revenue of $55.2 million was within the preview’s modeled range of about $55–58 million.
Internal R&D spending was $12.5 million, close to Q1’s $12.6 million; the preview had flagged that R&D might remain elevated or moderate.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted diluted EPS was $3.86, well above the preview’s $2.95 consensus estimate and even its bull-case estimate of about $3.25.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted diluted EPS rose 44% year-over-year to $3.86.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | $2.95 (range $2.90–2.98)” and the bull scenario estimated “~$3.25.”

surprises.description: Insight raised full-year EPS guidance to $12.20–$12.70 and gross profit growth guidance to 8%–10%. That exceeds the preview’s prior EPS range of $11.00–$11.50 and its bull-case range of $11.75–$12.00; the preview expected a raise but not one this high.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance, now expecting gross profit growth of 8% to 10% and adjusted diluted EPS of $12.20 to $12.70.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior guide was “adj. EPS $11.00–$11.50” with gross profit growth “low-single-digit”; the bull scenario anticipated a raise to “$11.75–12.00.”

surprises.description: Net revenue reached $2.4 billion, substantially above the preview’s $2.21–$2.22 billion consensus range, and reported growth of 15% also exceeded the preview’s expected 3.8%–5.6% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenue reached $2.4 billion, up 15% in USD (14% constant currency).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $2.21–2.22B”; expected year-over-year growth was “+3.8% to +5.6%.”

surprises.description: Gross profit grew 18%, far ahead of the preview’s derived estimate of about 6%, while total gross margin reached 21.7%, above the estimated 21.3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total gross profit grew 18%”; total gross margin rose “60 bps to 21.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Gross profit ~$470M” with “+6%” growth and gross margin of “~21.3%.”

surprises.description: Hardware gross profit rose 10%, outperforming the preview’s flat-year-over-year guide, even though hardware gross margin declined 110 basis points from pricing and client mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hardware gross margin declined 110 basis points due to pricing and client mix, even though hardware gross profit rose 10%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified hardware gross profit dollars “against a flat-year-over-year guide” and said flat or down hardware gross profit would be lower quality.

surprises.description: Cloud gross profit grew 39%, beating the preview’s watch threshold of 25% or more and exceeding Q1’s 35% growth despite the preview’s concern about tougher second-half comparisons.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cloud gross profit grew 39% to $171 million,” aided by acquisition contributions.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “Cloud gross profit growth of 25% or more” and noted tougher second-half comparisons.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA rose 29% and its margin expanded 90 basis points, with management attributing the margin improvement partly to pausing back- and mid-office hiring. This was stronger quantified operating leverage than the preview specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 29% to $190 million with margin expanding 90 basis points to 7.9%, aided by a pause in back and mid-office hiring.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario anticipated a “Beat on SG&A leverage,” but did not specify this EBITDA growth or margin expansion.

surprises.description: APAC gross profit surged 67%, driven by cybersecurity acquisition contributions; the preview did not identify this regional result as an expected growth driver or provide a regional forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APAC gross profit surged 67% from cybersecurity acquisition contributions.”

in_line: Hardware gross margin pressure was consistent with the preview’s warning that memory and SSD price increases could compress hardware margins.
Management said Q4 would be the lowest EPS-growth quarter because of tougher comparisons and other headwinds; the preview already expected a sharp second-half slowdown and cautious commentary.
Pausing M&A and prioritizing buybacks were consistent with the preview’s statement that M&A was paused through 2026 in favor of organic growth and repurchases.

surprises.description: Atmos raised its FY2026 O&M guidance floor from $865 million to $875 million, citing spending trends that are slightly higher. The preview had identified an O&M overrun as a risk, but its stated guide extended down to $865 million; management also said annual O&M increases of 4% are expected going forward.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 O&M guidance (excluding net bad debt) was raised to $875 million to $885 million as spending trends slightly higher, with 4% annual O&M increases expected going forward.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “O&M vs. the $865–$885M FY26 guide”; “A gross O&M overrun is the likeliest quiet miss.”

surprises.description: The preview expected June normalization to cap APT's contribution, but Atmos said new takeaway capacity came online sooner than expected and spreads narrowed significantly since June. It now expects the second-half APT uptick at the low end of the $0.08–$0.12 range, after capturing $0.08 in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APT's captured through-system spreads averaged $4.66 in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 versus $1.77 in the prior year, but have narrowed significantly since June as new takeaway capacity came online sooner than expected”; “the second-half APT uptick to land at the lower end of the previously guided $0.08 to $0.12 range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “June normalization caps APT”; the bull scenario expected “APT captures Apr–May spreads,” while the base scenario expected June normalization and guidance to be narrowed to the upper half or reaffirmed.

surprises.description: Atmos disclosed 12 new industrial customers expected to use about 950,000 Mcf per year, adding a specific large-load demand development the preview said had not been discussed previously.
surprises.fact_evidence: “12 new industrial customers expected to use ~950,000 Mcf per year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Large-load / data-center demand. Not discussed on the Q2 call. Any first disclosure would matter more for the multiple than for EPS.”

surprises.description: Year-to-date results included a $132 million benefit from Texas House Bill 4384, or $0.63 per share, which the preview did not identify. The preview did mention a separate Texas Rule 77102 deferral benefit, so the two items should not be treated as directly comparable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date results included a $132 million ($0.63/share) benefit from Texas House Bill 4384, with $71 million in distribution and $61 million at APT.”

in_line: Atmos reaffirmed FY2026 EPS guidance of $8.40–$8.50, consistent with the preview's stated company guidance and its base case, which allowed for reaffirmation.
Atmos added nearly 51,000 customers over the trailing 12 months, including roughly 39,000 in Texas, matching the preview's customer-growth figures.
FY2026 capex remained on track at approximately $4.2 billion, consistent with the preview's stated plan.
The $396 million of annualized operating income increases implemented since the start of the fiscal year exceeded the preview's stated $370 million-plus cumulative confirmation threshold.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $149 million was above the company’s prior expectation of about $147 million and above both preview consensus figures of $143.88 million and $146.81 million. The beat was modest rather than reaching the preview’s $152 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 15% to $149 million,” with “Q2 organic (ex-ArrowEye) growth of 12%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Company guidance was for Q2 revenue “similar to Q1” (about $147M); consensus was $143.88M or $146.81M. The preview’s bull case was “$152M+.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $24 million, above the prior-year $22.5 million and the preview’s expectation of less than $22.5 million based on company guidance. The gap was notable, though more than $3 million of tariff refunds boosted gross margin and contributed to the result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA increased 7% to $24 million,” benefiting from “more than $3 million in tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was guided to be “slightly lower than prior year” (below $22.5M); the preview said “Anything above $22.5M would be a clear beat.”

surprises.description: Full-year revenue growth guidance was raised from high single digits to high single digits/low double digits, even though the preview’s base case was that FY guidance would be affirmed. This is a modest upgrade to the expected annual growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year revenue growth guidance to high single digits/low double digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior FY26 outlook was “high single-digit revenue growth”; the preview’s base scenario was “FY affirmed.”

surprises.description: First-half free cash flow reached a record $36 million, and the company raised its full-year guidance to $45–$50 million. That was stronger than the preview’s expectation of free-cash-flow conversion similar to 2025, although management cautioned that timing-related benefits will not repeat at the same level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First half free cash flow was a record $36 million versus just $1 million a year earlier”; guidance rose to “$45-$50 million,” while management cautioned “this level won't repeat as some benefit was timing-related.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY26 guidance was for “FCF conversion similar to 2025.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin rose to 32.5%, above the 30.9% reported for Q2 2025, interrupting the margin-compression trend the preview highlighted. The improvement was partly due to more than $3 million of tariff refunds, so some of the rebound was non-recurring.
surprises.fact_evidence: Tariff refunds “boosted gross margin ~160 basis points to 32.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said gross margin had “compressed six straight quarters” and flagged “any tariff refund recognition” as a “non-recurring boost.”

surprises.description: Revenue guidance increased, but adjusted EBITDA growth guidance remained at low-to-mid single digits rather than being raised alongside it. The preview had identified a guide raise as the clearest positive outcome and said an unchanged outlook that did not incorporate TRISM would be a quiet negative.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company raised revenue guidance but held “adjusted EBITDA (low-to-mid single digit growth) ... guidance unchanged.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise is the cleanest bull catalyst”; “A reaffirmation that does not incorporate TRISM would be a quiet negative.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed that TRISM is expected to add $3.5–$4 million in the second half of 2026, with its 2027 run-rate expected to be roughly double that, and that it roughly doubles CPI’s instant-issuance addressable market. The preview anticipated the acquisition and an approximately 20% IPT growth target, but did not give these revenue or market-size estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: TRISM “roughly doubles CPI's instant issuance addressable market” and “is expected to add $3.5-$4 million in the second half of 2026, with 2027 run-rate expected to roughly double that.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted the TRISM acquisition and said it “lifts FY26 IPT growth to about 20%,” but did not state an expected revenue contribution or addressable-market expansion.

surprises.description: CPI redeemed $26.5 million of Senior Notes in mid-July, leaving $265 million outstanding at quarter end. The preview discussed leverage guidance and the acquisition’s lack of leverage impact but did not anticipate this debt repayment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company redeemed $26.5 million of Senior Notes in mid-July, leaving $265 million outstanding at quarter end.”

in_line: Integrated PayTech full-year growth guidance of approximately 20% after TRISM was consistent with the preview, which said the deal lifted the target to about 20%; the need for a sharp second-half acceleration was also flagged.

Prepaid Solutions remained soft, consistent with the preview’s warning that another decline could challenge the order-timing explanation; management’s outlook for continued choppiness also matches the concern about uneven ordering.

Q2 SG&A and integration costs were elevated, with costs expected to decline significantly in the second half, consistent with the preview’s expectation that ArrowEye costs would be elevated in Q2 and taper in H2.
Net leverage of 2.7x remained within the preview’s stated year-end target range of 2.5x to 3.0x.

surprises.description: CNR reported diluted EPS of $2.51, far above the preview’s $0.50–$0.51 estimate, with adjusted EBITDA of $324 million. The large beat was aided by $125 million of Q2 EBITDA from the Leer South insurance claim, versus the preview’s expectation of about $100 million of proceeds in Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income rose to $126 million ($2.51 per diluted share) … with adjusted EBITDA jumping to $324 million … aided by insurance proceeds”; “recognizing $125 million in Q2 EBITDA (with ~$30 million in prior quarters).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) | $0.50 – $0.51”; “Management guided to about $100M of additional insurance proceeds, expected in Q2.”

surprises.description: High CV Thermal cash costs came in at $38.58 per ton, better than the preview’s sub-$39 positive threshold, but CNR raised full-year cost guidance by $1 rather than reaffirming it, citing persistent inflation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HCV thermal cash costs dropped to $38.58 per ton from $42.56 in Q1, though full-year guidance was raised $1 to $39-$40.50 per ton due to persistent inflationary pressures.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Q2 figure of $39.00 or better supports the guide”; “FY2026 guidance … Reaffirmation is the expected outcome”; prior FY range “$38.00–$39.50.”

surprises.description: CNR lowered full-year metallurgical cash-cost guidance by $2.50, a favorable guidance change not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Metallurgical segment cash costs fell nearly $7 per ton quarter-over-quarter to $85.65, prompting management to lower full-year met cash cost guidance by $2.50 to a range of $86-$91 per ton.”
