surprises.description: Shareholder returns accelerated: CNR returned $68 million in Q2 versus $47 million in Q1 and signaled another step-up in buybacks for Q3 and Q4, alongside a target of returning about 75% of free cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company returned $68 million to shareholders in Q2 (up from $47 million in Q1) and signaled a further step-up in Q3 and Q4 buybacks … targeting ~75% of free cash flow returned.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Accelerated buybacks would signal confidence in cost normalization”; the bull scenario included “buyback stepped up.”

surprises.description: CNR reported substantial forward contracting for HCV Thermal: nearly all of 2026 volume is contracted at about $58 per ton, and more than half of 2027 is contracted. The preview listed HCV volume guidance but did not anticipate these contracted-volume and pricing updates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The HCV thermal segment is now nearly fully contracted for 2026 at over 31 million tons at approximately $58 per ton, and is more than 50% contracted for 2027 with India tons near $60 and West Elk in the upper $40s to low $50s.”

surprises.description: The marketing team disclosed about 16 million tons of contracted volume through 2030 at attractive prices, a longer-dated contract update not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The marketing team secured ~16 million tons of contracted volume through 2030 at attractive prices.”

surprises.description: CNR disclosed an outage at the DTA terminal, where it owns 35%, though management said the impacts are already reflected in netback realizations. The preview did not flag this outage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core's DTA terminal outage (35% ownership) is being managed with impacts already reflected in netback realizations.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted operating EPS was $2.55, beating the preview’s $2.36 consensus by $0.19 and slightly exceeding even its $2.35 upper end of the alternative polls. That was a stronger result than the preview’s base case of $2.35–$2.50.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted operating earnings were $2.55 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating EPS | $2.36”; alternative polls were “$2.24 – $2.35”; the base scenario projected “$2.35–$2.50.”

surprises.description: Constellation raised its 2026 guidance by $0.50 per share, rather than merely reaffirming the $11.00–$12.00 range. The new midpoint is $12.00—the old range’s top end—although the range remains $1.00 wide rather than narrowing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 adjusted operating earnings guidance by $0.50 to $11.50-$12.50 per share, with the new midpoint equal to the prior range's top end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the $11.00–$12.00 range was “Affirmed at Q1” and characterized a “flat reaffirmation” as neutral; it said narrowing toward the upper half would be bullish.

surprises.description: The company reported new long-term nuclear contracts, a concrete outcome beyond the preview’s hoped-for sign that customer negotiations had resumed. The preview did not identify a specific deal or customer type; the reported customers were investment-grade, and the deals bring contracted clean baseload output to roughly 30%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Signed approximately 920 megawatts of new long-term nuclear deals with investment-grade customers averaging 18.5 years duration, bringing total contracted clean baseload output to roughly 30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A named new long-term PPA, or explicit language that negotiations have resumed, matters more than a few cents of EPS.”

surprises.description: Buybacks were a substantial step-up: the company repurchased about $2.2 billion of shares in four months, far beyond the preview’s Q1 reference point of roughly $335 million and its expectation that a step-up would be a credibility signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Deployed about $2.2 billion toward share repurchases in the four months since late March, with $2.8 billion remaining under authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted the “Buyback pace,” citing Q1 repurchases of “$335M,” and said “A step-up would be a credibility signal.”

surprises.description: Q2 earnings had an unflagged headwind from lower Illinois ZEC bank-credit recognition. Management said the shortfall was a timing item already included in full-year guidance, so it reduced the quarter’s results without changing the stated full-year outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 results were reduced by recognizing only $85 million of Illinois ZEC bank credits versus $200 million last year, a timing item already reflected in full-year guidance ahead of the program's May 2027 expiration.”

surprises.description: The DOJ-required divestitures produced a favorable reported valuation: the Brazos Valley sale was priced at about $1,420 per kW, and total gross proceeds are expected to be about $5.9 billion at nearly $1,200 per kW, above the stated $960 per kW implied Calpine purchase price. The preview did not discuss these divestitures or their proceeds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Agreed to sell the Brazos Valley Energy Center to LS Power for $860 million (about $1,420 per kW)” and “DOJ-required divestitures are expected to generate approximately $5.9 billion in gross proceeds at nearly $1,200 per kW, a healthy premium to the implied $960 per kW Calpine purchase price.”

surprises.description: The Crane restart advanced through NRC fuel-licensing approval and a FERC waiver, while remaining on track for a second-half 2027 return to service. The preview did not flag this project or anticipate these regulatory milestones.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Crane restart progressed with NRC new fuel licensing approval and FERC's waiver to transfer Eddystone capacity injection rights, keeping the facility on track to return to service in the second half of 2027.”

surprises.description: The company added a higher 2029 capital-allocation sensitivity range than the preview had specified, with upside above $0.75 per share. The preview listed capital allocation as a topic to watch but gave no expectation for this range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 2029 capital allocation sensitivity range was updated to a $0.20 per share floor with upside greater than $0.75 per share.”

surprises.description: An updated production tax credit strike-price assumption adds about $0.30 per share to 2030 base earnings, an unanticipated positive change to the longer-term earnings outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An updated PTC strike price assumption ($50.88/MWh in 2030) adds about $0.30 per share to 2030 base earnings.”

surprises.description: Refueling performance was notably better than the preview anticipated by simply identifying Q2 as refueling season: the average outage lasted 23 days, 40% shorter than the industry average despite six planned outages. The preview did, however, set roughly 93% as the level below which capacity factor would draw concern, and the reported 93% was right at that threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The nuclear fleet delivered a 93% capacity factor and 40 terawatt hours in the quarter, with a 23-day average refueling outage duration outperforming the industry average by 40% despite six planned outages.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 is refueling season. Anything below about 93% will draw questions.”

in_line: Nuclear capacity factor was 93%, at the preview’s approximate 93% threshold rather than below it.

surprises.description: Q2 net sales were $207.1 million, well above the preview’s $178.3 million consensus estimate—about 16% higher than expected, rather than the forecast 13.5% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales grew 32% year-over-year to $207.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $178.3M” and “+13.5%” year-over-year.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA growth substantially exceeded the preview’s roughly $31 million estimate at a 17.5% margin. The reported 56% growth implies approximately $42 million using the preview’s $27 million year-ago comparison, or roughly a 20% margin on Q2 sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increasing 56%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$31M at 17.5% margin.”

surprises.description: Cadre raised its full-year sales and adjusted EBITDA ranges instead of merely reaffirming the prior outlook. The new midpoints imply faster year-over-year growth than the preview’s roughly 22% sales growth expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to net sales of $749-769 million and adjusted EBITDA of $139-144 million,” implying midpoint growth of 24.4% and 26.7%, respectively.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (reaffirmed May 2026): Net sales $736–758M (about +22% at midpoint), Adj. EBITDA $136–141M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin expanded despite the prior quarter’s sharp decline, adding another positive margin result beyond the adjusted EBITDA beat. The preview focused on EBITDA margin rather than setting a Q2 gross-margin target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margins expanding 120 basis points (209 bps adjusted for inventory step-up amortization) to 42.6%.”

surprises.description: The Q3 outlook calls for about 18% adjusted EBITDA margins, below the preview’s roughly 20.8% margin requirement for H2 to reach the prior full-year EBITDA midpoint. Management expects Q4 to resemble Q2’s stronger profile, so the implied shortfall is concentrated in the near-term cadence rather than the raised full-year outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue is guided to approximately $190 million with ~18% adjusted EBITDA margins, with Q4 expected to resemble Q2's stronger profile.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EBITDA needs roughly 20.8% margins in H2 versus 13.6% in Q1.”

surprises.description: Alien Gear contributed $4.8 million in the quarter and outperformed expectations, a positive acquisition contribution beyond the preview’s general concern about separating organic growth from acquired growth. Management nevertheless included only $11 million for Alien Gear in full-year guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The recently acquired Alien Gear generated $4.8 million in the quarter and outperformed expectations, though guidance conservatively bakes in only $11 million for the full year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Organic growth ex-TYR and Alien Gear.”

surprises.description: Cadre received a second $8.4 million purchase order for the Med-Eng BEMO program, bringing total orders to $18.4 million against the five-year contract. The preview raised backlog quality as a watch item but did not anticipate this additional order.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cadre secured a second $8.4 million purchase order for the Med-Eng BEMO military program, bringing total received to $18.4 million against a 5-year $50 million IDIQ contract.”

surprises.description: Safariland’s ballistic panel was selected for the FBI and incorporated into a five-year, $61 million multi-agency contract, a new award-related development not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Safariland's SXHP ballistic panel was selected for the FBI, integrated into Predictive Ballistics' 5-year $61 million IDIQ contract that also serves the U.S. Marshals, DEA and other DOJ agencies.”

surprises.description: Nuclear backlog had increased by $13 million since year-end, with growth coming from commercial nuclear energy and environmental remediation in the U.S. and Northern Europe. The preview questioned backlog quality but did not forecast this increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nuclear backlog increased $13 million since year-end, driven primarily by commercial nuclear energy and environmental remediation in both the U.S. and Northern Europe.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Backlog quality,” including whether the blast sensor ships in H2 and whether the seat award remains slipped into 2027.

surprises.description: Net leverage was 2.5x, better than the preview’s estimate of just under 3.0x, giving management more acquisition capacity than that estimate suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage declined to 2.5x, providing substantial dry powder against a 3.5x ceiling.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net leverage is just under 3.0x against a 2.0x long-term target.”

surprises.description: Management said it expects at least one more acquisition in 2026. The preview identified M&A as a topic to watch but did not indicate that another deal was expected this year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects at least one more acquisition in 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “M&A and leverage commentary.”

surprises.description: Foreign exchange reduced Q2 earnings by $6.6 million, an unanticipated headwind alongside the otherwise strong reported results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FX headwinds hurt Q2 earnings by $6.6 million.”

in_line: Organic growth was 5%, at the high end of the preview’s expected 3%-5% range.

surprises.description: Revenue was $153.8 million, about 6% above the $145.09 million consensus, while organic constant-currency growth reached 9%. That is a much stronger underlying result than the preview’s concern about weak ex-FX growth suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 revenue rose 10% year-over-year to $153.8 million, with 9% organic constant-currency growth and approximately $1.3 million of favorable FX tailwind.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was $145.09M, implying +3.9% Y/Y. The preview also flagged organic growth ex-FX as an issue, noting Q1 organic constant-currency growth was only +1%.

surprises.description: Margins recovered much more sharply than the preview’s roughly 8.3% operating-margin expectation: operating margin was 10.2%. Adjusted EBITDA margin also came in at 15.4%, above the preview’s approximately 14.1% bogey.
surprises.fact_evidence: Operating margin rose to 10.2% from 8.4%, with operating income of $15.6 million versus $11.7 million. Adjusted EBITDA was $23.7 million, or 15.4% of revenue.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated operating margin at ~8.3% and adjusted EBITDA at ~$20.5M, ~14.1% margin; it said consensus needed about 160bps of sequential operating-margin expansion while costs were expected to stay elevated through Q3.

surprises.description: Orders and book-to-bill were substantially stronger than the preview’s cycle-turn threshold, easing the concern that Q1’s order strength might have been a one-off. Orders reached a record and book-to-bill was 1.31x, well above the 1.05x level the preview said would support a turn.
surprises.fact_evidence: Orders surged 49% year-over-year and 27% sequentially to a record $201.3 million, producing a 1.31x book-to-bill ratio.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a reading at or above 1.05x would support the turn, while below 1.0x could suggest Q1 pulled demand forward.

surprises.description: Backlog rose well beyond the preview’s watch level of about $255 million, providing a larger near-term visibility increase than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: Backlog was $298 million, convertible within three to nine months.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described $251.0M as the starting backlog and said to watch for a move toward $255M or higher.

surprises.description: Data center and infrastructure sales were a sizable, fast-growing business that the preview did not identify as a key Q2 issue. Management also expects this business to grow faster than Allient overall.
surprises.fact_evidence: Data center and infrastructure sales reached $16.3 million in Q2, up 60% year-over-year, and $57.1 million on a trailing 12-month basis, up 69%; management expects data center growth to outpace company average.

surprises.description: The company reduced debt and improved leverage, a positive balance-sheet development not anticipated in the preview, which instead noted weaker Q1 operating cash flow and higher DSO.
surprises.fact_evidence: Total debt fell $7.1 million since year-end 2025 to $173.3 million, improving leverage to 1.63x, with $42 million cash and $162 million of unused revolver capacity.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 operating cash flow fell to $6.2M from $13.9M and DSO rose to 61 days from 57.

in_line: Management quantified STAND savings at $5–7 million for 2026 and described a two-to-three-year runway of similar annual savings, addressing the preview’s request for a dollar figure on savings.
Expected FY26 restructuring costs of $2–3 million were in line with the preview’s stated company estimate of $2–3 million.

surprises.description: BKV raised 2026 strategic power capital guidance to $400–$475 million, up $128 million at the midpoint from the prior range. The preview’s base case expected guidance to be reaffirmed, so the larger spending plan is a meaningful departure, although it also reflects long-lead equipment orders for Jack County.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BKV increased its 2026 strategic power capital guidance to $400-$475 million, a $128 million increase at the midpoint, driven largely by long lead time equipment orders for the Jack County project.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (~50%) ... FY guide reaffirmed”; prior guidance was “Power growth capital $280–340M.”

surprises.description: BKV raised the midpoint of its 2026 Upstream production guidance to 950 MMcfe/d, implying 3% to 4% year-over-year growth. The preview listed the existing 915–955 MMcfe/d range and expected guidance reaffirmation in its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year 2026 Upstream production guidance to a midpoint of 950 MMcfe/d, a 1.6% increase implying 3% to 4% year-over-year production growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance (FY26, reaffirmed at Q1): ... Production 915–955 MMcfe/d”; base scenario: “FY guide reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: The Upper Barnett Yarbrough appraisal well delivered about twice the type-curve production over its first 30 days and unlocked a 114-well inventory, with breakevens of $3.25/MMBtu for nearly half the inventory. The preview did not flag this appraisal result or inventory potential.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Upper Barnett Yarbrough 8H appraisal well produced approximately 2x above type curve over its first 30 days, lowering breakeven for nearly half the inventory to $3.25/MMBtu and unlocking a 114-well inventory.”

surprises.description: BKV reported unusually low drilling and completion costs alongside stronger-than-type-curve well performance from advanced completions. The preview discussed whether completions would lift production but did not anticipate these specific cost and performance results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BKV achieved the lowest cost per lateral foot of any major U.S. shale gas basin at $525 all-in DC&F, with advanced completions delivering well performance 25% above type curve after 180 days.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether advanced completions show through in Q2 volumes without further LOE increases.”

surprises.description: BKV said Temple and Jack County together could add 1.4 GW of dispatchable generation, roughly doubling capacity to nearly 3 GW. The preview discussed Jack County spending and the PPA thesis but did not describe this potential capacity expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The combined Temple and Jack County developments could add 1.4 gigawatts of dispatchable generation, roughly doubling total capacity to nearly 3 gigawatts within the next few years.”

surprises.description: Management reported that power-purchase discussions had narrowed to a select group of advanced counterparties, adding evidence of progress beyond a generic timeline reaffirmation. No counterparty was named, however, and the expected signing window remained unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed expectations to sign a Temple power purchase agreement within 2026 to early 2027, with commercial discussions narrowed to a select set of advanced counterparties.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a “named counterparty would matter more than another quarter of ‘deliberate and disciplined’ language” and gave the expected signing window as “within 2026 to early 2027.”

in_line: Temple power adjusted EBITDA was $36 million, within the preview’s roughly $30–45 million Q2 power-JV EBITDA expectation, though the reported figure is described as gross power adjusted EBITDA.
Management kept the Temple PPA signing window at 2026 to early 2027, as the preview’s base case expected.

The preview expected Eagle Ford injection to begin by the end of Q2; the call reported three operating carbon-capture projects, including Eagle Ford, with roughly 400,000 tons of CO2 injected through Q2 and retained the 1.5-million-ton-per-year 2028 target.
Hedging was essentially as previewed: 66% of remaining 2026 gas production at $3.88/MMBtu versus the preview’s 67% at $3.86/MMBtu.

surprises.description: Curtiss-Wright raised its full-year sales growth guidance to 8%-9% from 7%-8%, lifted EPS guidance to $15.10-$15.40 from $14.90-$15.30, and raised its operating-margin range to 19.1%-19.3% from 19.0%-19.2%. The increases exceeded the preview’s base case of a high-end narrowing rather than a raise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was raised to 8%-9% sales growth, 14%-16% diluted EPS growth to $15.10-$15.40, and record operating margin of 19.1%-19.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: ... FY guide narrowed to the high end rather than raised”; the preview listed existing guidance of sales growth of 7%-8%, operating margin of 19.0%-19.2%, and diluted EPS of $14.90-$15.30.

surprises.description: Q2 operating income grew 12%, above the preview’s expectation of “high single digits plus,” while operating margin expanded 110 basis points to 19.4%. The preview expected margin expansion to be weighted to the second half, so the Q2 margin performance was stronger and earlier than that framing suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating margin expanded 110 basis points to 19.4% in Q2, driven by favorable mix, cost containment, and improved absorption despite higher R&D investment.” Operating income was “up 12%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 operating income growth: ‘high single digits plus’”; “Margin expansion is weighted to the second half.”

surprises.description: Reported diluted EPS grew 15%, above the preview’s consensus-implied 12.1% growth rate for adjusted EPS. The reported and consensus figures use different EPS bases, but the available growth rates indicate a better-than-expected result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS up 15%,” exceeding company expectations.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave Q2 adjusted EPS consensus of “$3.61–$3.62” versus “$3.23 (adj)” a year earlier, implying “+12.1%.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was strong despite the preview’s expectation that cash flow was back-half loaded: it reached $160 million with 116% cash conversion. The company also raised its full-year free-cash-flow guidance by $5 million at both ends, even while capital expenditures are rising sharply for growth investments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow reached $160 million, a 37% year-over-year improvement, representing a strong 116% cash conversion rate”; guidance was raised to “$585-$605 million” despite a “nearly 30% year-over-year increase in capital expenditures for growth investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “FCF is back-half loaded, so a weak Q2 alone is not a thesis breaker,” and listed full-year FCF guidance of $580-$600 million.

surprises.description: Defense and Electronics orders surged nearly 50% in Q2 and were up more than 30% year to date, a record segment performance. The preview focused on Defense Electronics sales and margins, but did not anticipate this exceptional order growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Defense and Electronics orders surged nearly 50% year-over-year in Q2 and are up over 30% year-to-date, marking a record segment performance.”

surprises.description: The company described a sharper intra-year earnings and margin concentration than the preview’s general expectation of second-half margin expansion: Q3 operating income and margin are expected to be flat sequentially, with a record Q4 and margin above 20% dependent on Defense Electronics timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects a heavily back-loaded year, with Q3 operating income and margin flat sequentially and a record Q4 delivering operating margin in excess of 20%, driven by Defense Electronics timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Margin expansion is weighted to the second half.”

surprises.description: Curtiss-Wright reported approximately $95 million in Maritime Industrial Base funding, up from $70 million at the end of March, supporting an $80 million multiyear Pennsylvania facility expansion. The preview did not flag this funding increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Curtiss-Wright has now been awarded approximately $95 million in Maritime Industrial Base funding, up from $70 million at the end of March, supporting an $80 million multiyear Pennsylvania facility expansion.”

in_line: Q2 sales were essentially in line with the preview: $924 million versus $926.2 million consensus, with 5% reported growth versus the preview’s +5.6% consensus growth and mid-single-digit company framing.
Q2 orders grew 8% with book-to-bill above 1.1x, within the preview’s base-case book-to-bill range of about 1.0x-1.2x and above its key downside threshold of 1.0x.

Management continued to expect the AP1000 reactor coolant pump order in 2026. The preview also said the order was still expected that year and not included in guidance; no award or firm timing was reported.

surprises.description: The Closed Block’s adjusted operating loss was $110 million, far worse than the preview’s base-case range of a $30 million to $40 million loss. The $127 million actual-to-expected loss, primarily in LTC, also led management to warn that full-year A/E losses could exceed the roughly $300 million expectation if first-half trends continue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Closed Block segment posted an adjusted operating loss of $110 million, driven by a $127 million pretax actual-to-expected variance loss primarily in LTC,” and management warned full-year A/E losses “could exceed the ~$300 million expectation if first-half trends persist.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “Closed Block AOI –$30M to –$40M”; it also identified a “Closed Block AOI loss” as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: CareScout Services produced $6 million of Q2 revenue, below the preview’s $7 million-plus pace, and its match volumes are running below what is needed to reach the 7,500 full-year target. The company nevertheless maintained its $25 million full-year revenue outlook and $50 million–$55 million investment plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CareScout Services generated only $6 million of revenue in Q2 ($12 million first half), and match volumes are pacing below the level needed to hit the full-year target of ~7,500 matches.” The company “continues to expect CareScout Services full-year revenue of $25 million while investing $50 million-$55 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 needed “roughly 1,900+ matches and $7M+ revenue to keep the target credible,” against a 7,500-match full-year target, and listed $25 million revenue and $50 million–$55 million investment spend as guidance.

surprises.description: Genworth raised its full-year share-repurchase guidance to $225 million–$250 million, above the prior $195 million–$225 million range. That is a stronger capital-return commitment than the preview’s expectation that the May target would be reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Genworth raised its full-year 2026 share repurchase guidance to $225 million-$250 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 buyback allocation of “$195–225M” and described the base case as “guidance reaffirmed, not raised.”

surprises.description: Enact’s capital returned to Genworth was $103 million in Q2, and Genworth raised its expected full-year receipts to $445 million–$485 million. The quarter exceeded the preview’s roughly $95 million threshold, while the new annual range is above the prior approximately $405 million target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enact returned $103 million of capital to Genworth in the quarter,” and Genworth now expects “$445 million-$485 million from Enact for full-year 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “at least $95M” in Q2 and “reaffirmation of ~$405M for FY26.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating income excluding the Closed Block was $112 million, modestly above the preview’s roughly $107 million estimate; adjusted operating EPS was $0.29 versus $0.28 consensus. This was a small positive beat on the new ex-Closed Block basis, despite the much weaker Closed Block result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income excluding the Closed Block of $112 million ($0.29/share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Adj. operating EPS (ex-Closed Block) $0.28” and “Adj. operating income ex-CB ~$107M (derived).”

surprises.description: The appeal hearing in the AXA/Santander matter had taken place in July, with a decision expected within three to six months. A favorable, fully resolved outcome could produce an approximately $750 million tax-free recovery, a potential catalyst not discussed in the preview and not included in capital plans.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The AXA/Santander appeal hearing occurred in July with a decision expected within 3-6 months; a favorable, fully-resolved outcome would recover approximately $750 million tax-free, though not currently factored into capital plans.”

in_line: Enact contributed $143 million, essentially within the preview’s expected $138 million–$142 million range.

The MYRAP program’s expected full-year value was around $1 billion on a net-present-value basis, consistent with the preview’s guidance of approvals broadly in line with 2025 at roughly $1 billion NPV.

surprises.description: CRA reported $210.8 million of revenue, above the preview’s $203–206 million seasonal bar and well above the published $198.9 million consensus. The result was stronger than the preview’s most likely range, even though its bull case included revenue as high as $212 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record quarterly revenue of $210.8 million in Q2 2026,” representing “12.8% year-over-year growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview treated “$203–206M” as the “more realistic bar”; published consensus was “$198.9M.”

surprises.description: CRA raised full-year revenue guidance to $805–820 million, above the preview’s base-case expectation of $790–810 million and its $795 million catalyst threshold. The increase was a more substantial revision than the base case anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $805-820 million from the prior $785-805 million range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected guidance “nudged to $790–810M”; its catalyst checklist looked for a raise “to at least $795M.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EBITDA grew 15.3%, above the preview’s implied 5–9% growth range. Applying the reported growth to the preview’s cited $23.3 million prior-year EBITDA implies roughly $26.9 million, above the preview’s $24.5–25.5 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EBITDA grew 15.3% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated non-GAAP EBITDA at “~$24.5–25.5M” and implied growth of “+5–9%,” citing Q2 FY25 EBITDA of $23.3 million.

surprises.description: The call reported strong growth across specific practices, including more than 20% growth in both Energy and Life Sciences and a sixth consecutive record quarter for Antitrust & Competition Economics. The preview flagged Antitrust commentary as something to watch but did not set an expected result, and gave no expectation for these practice growth rates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Both Energy and Life Sciences management consulting practices grew over 20% year-over-year, with Antitrust & Competition Economics posting its sixth consecutive record quarter.”

surprises.description: International operations grew 32.9% organically, an unusually strong contribution not anticipated in the preview, which did not give a regional growth expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International operations surged 32.9% year-over-year (all organic) while North American operations grew 8.7%.”

surprises.description: Days sales outstanding rose to 113 days from 100 days in Q1, a deterioration in collections that the preview did not flag or forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DSO rose to 113 days from 100 days in Q1.”

surprises.description: CRA disclosed a new, expanded five-year credit facility of up to $400 million, replacing a facility that was not due to mature until August 2027. The preview did not anticipate a refinancing or facility change; the implications for shareholders are unclear from the provided facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CRA expanded and extended its credit facility to a 5-year, up-to-$400 million agreement ($75 million term loan and $325 million revolver), replacing the prior facility maturing in August 2027.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a 32.6% non-GAAP effective tax rate, up from 29.0% a year earlier because of nondeductible executive compensation. The preview offered no tax-rate expectation, so this was an unanticipated cost headwind rather than a miss against a stated estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The non-GAAP effective tax rate increased to 32.6% from 29.0% a year ago due to nondeductible executive compensation, with full-year rate expected at 32%-33%.”

in_line: Non-GAAP EPS growth of 14.9% was roughly in line with the preview’s consensus-implied growth of 14.4%.
Utilization was 77%, matching the preview’s estimate of approximately 77%.
Management reaffirmed the 12.0%–13.0% full-year non-GAAP EBITDA margin guidance, as the preview said it had been reaffirmed at Q1.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $1.60 billion, roughly 9.6% above the year-ago quarter and about 1.8% above the preview’s ~$1.57 billion consensus. The preview looked for 7.7% growth, so the revenue result was a modest beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 9.6% year-over-year, driven by 5.6% discharge growth and 3.9% higher net revenue per discharge.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net operating revenue | ~$1,570M” and “Implied Y/Y | +7.7%.”

surprises.description: Discharge growth of 5.6% exceeded the preview’s derived expectation of about 4.3% for total discharges. The preview’s key same-store discharge debate cannot be resolved from the reported facts, which do not give a same-store figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue grew 9.6% year-over-year, driven by 5.6% discharge growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total discharges | ~68,000 (derived)” and “Implied Y/Y | +4.3%.”

surprises.description: The company raised full-year guidance, with the new adjusted EPS range reaching $6.25—above the preview’s stated bull-trigger threshold of a raise above $6.15. The preview’s base case instead anticipated guidance being tightened to the upper half of the prior range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance” to adjusted EPS of “$6.02-$6.25,” revenue of “$6.41B-$6.49B,” and adjusted EBITDA of “$1.365B-$1.395B.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise above $6.15 EPS is the bull trigger”; the base case anticipated “guidance narrowed to upper half.”

surprises.description: The expected 2026 provider-tax benefit to adjusted EBITDA was cut by about $11 million from the prior estimate, an unanticipated reduction to the earnings outlook attributed to retroactive Florida Medicaid adjustments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company now expects net provider tax benefit to 2026 adjusted EBITDA of about $10 million, down from the prior ~$21 million estimate,” including “an $11.5 million year-over-year decrease in Q2.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year salary-and-benefit cost-per-FTE growth guidance to 3.5%-4%, a cost pressure that runs against the preview’s expectation of labor improvement contributing to a modest beat. Lower premium labor costs provide an offset, but the higher per-FTE growth guidance is still a less favorable labor signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 SWB per FTE growth guidance was raised to 3.5%-4% due to increased participation in career ladder programs,” while “premium labor costs fell $2.6 million year-over-year to $25 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “modest beat on labor” was part of its base case and noted that labor gains needed to reach the bottom line.

surprises.description: The MA pilot produced a high reported success rate and management plans to scale selected high-success diagnoses. The preview anticipated a possible meaningful data point, but did not anticipate or establish an expected success rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The MA admit-and-appeal pilot across 9 markets has admitted 298 patients through July, with 128 of 144 adjudicated cases won (89% success rate),” and management “plans to scale certain high-success diagnoses in coming quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Quantified approval data or a plan to scale beyond nine hospitals would matter for 2027.”

surprises.description: The reported 2026 opening plan implies eight hospitals and 389 beds for the year, above the preview’s expectation of seven hospitals and 340 beds. The additional post-2026 pipeline and North Carolina market opportunities were also not described in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company opened 3 hospitals (139 beds) and added 54 beds in the first half,” plans “5 more hospitals (250 beds) and 100-150 additional beds in the back half,” and has “a post-2026 pipeline of 13 hospitals with 606 beds, plus 15 prioritized North Carolina markets following CON repeal effective October 1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Seven hospitals with 340 beds are still scheduled to open in 2026.”

surprises.description: The Board raised the dividend and expanded the repurchase authorization, adding shareholder returns that the preview did not flag as an expected action.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board increased the quarterly dividend to $0.21 per share and raised the stock repurchase authorization to $1 billion,” with “$145.8 million of shares repurchased year-to-date.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was $348 million, matching the preview’s derived Q2 estimate of about $348 million.
Adjusted EPS growth of 10.7% implies approximately $1.55 per share, in line with the preview’s derived estimate of about $1.55.
The CMS 2027 IRF final rule’s expected 2.3% increase in net Medicare revenue per discharge matched the preview’s stated final-rule update.

surprises.description: F1 revenue was reported down 15%, a shallower decline than the roughly 28% drop implied by the preview's Q2 group revenue consensus. The comparison is not perfectly like-for-like: the preview noted that Q2 2025 had no MotoGP results.
surprises.fact_evidence: F1's calendar variance was “driving a 15% revenue decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FWON Group revenue consensus was $959.3M versus $1,341M in Q2 2025, “about -28%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted OIBDA fell 30%, which implies about $258M against the prior-year $369M—slightly above the preview's $225M–$250M base-case range. That is a modestly better result than the preview's central scenario, though there was no clean published OIBDA consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: F1's race-calendar variance was “driving a ... 30% adjusted OIBDA decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's base scenario was “Adj. OIBDA $225M–250M”; it also said there was “No clean published consensus.”

surprises.description: Bahrain was moved to Malaysia in October rather than remaining among the lost races, leaving an expected 23-race 2026 calendar. A full 24-race season is now anticipated only in 2027, so the calendar is not fully restored this year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Bahrain GP has been rescheduled to Malaysia in October,” bringing the expected 2026 race count to 23, with a return to a full 24-race calendar anticipated in 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Bahrain among the “four lost races” and said Qatar and Abu Dhabi remained scheduled, while noting contingency plans.

surprises.description: U.S. F1 viewing on Apple TV grew despite the disrupted calendar, with season-to-date hours watched up 13% and a younger, more female audience. The preview did not flag this viewing trend as an expectation or key debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “F1 viewership on Apple TV in the U.S. is up year-over-year with total hours watched up 13% season-to-date,” while attracting a younger and more female audience.

surprises.description: The Las Vegas Grand Prix secured a 10-year extension through 2037, and 2026 ticket sales had already reached the prior year's end-of-September level by the end of July. The preview did not anticipate either the long extension or this early sales pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Las Vegas Grand Prix was extended 10 years through 2037,” with 2026 ticket sales already at “end-of-September 2025 levels” as of end-July on a like-for-like basis.

surprises.description: F1 described strong premium-hospitality demand and plans to expand House 44 from 9 locations in 2026 to 30 in 2027; the Paddock Club was sold out for the rest of the season, with 2028 allocations complete. These commercialization and demand details were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: House 44 is planned to expand “from 9 locations in 2026 to 30 locations in 2027”; the Paddock Club was “sold out for the rest of the season” and “2028 allocations complete.”

surprises.description: MotoGP secured agreements with every manufacturer and team through 2031, alongside new technical regulations starting in 2027, creating a five-year framework for commercial growth. The preview focused on near-term MotoGP results and did not anticipate this longer-term framework.
surprises.fact_evidence: MotoGP “secured agreements with all manufacturers and teams through 2031” alongside “new technical regulations beginning in 2027,” establishing a “five-year framework for commercial growth.”

surprises.description: MotoGP reported positive audience and engagement indicators beyond the growth the preview expected: attendance rose 4%, TV viewership rose 3%, and TikTok engagement increased over 80%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Across the first 11 races, MotoGP attendance was “up 4%,” TV viewership “up 3%,” and TikTok engagement “up over 80%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected MotoGP “constant-currency growth” and flagged growth and operating losses as key things to watch.

in_line: The Q2 F1 race count fell from nine to five, matching the preview's expectation of five races versus nine in Q2 2025.
MotoGP grew year-to-date on revenue and adjusted OIBDA in constant currency, in line with the preview's expectation of constant-currency growth.
Management continued to expect roughly 200 basis points of full-year leverage improvement, consistent with the guidance cited in the preview.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $8.6 million, below the $10–15 million Q2 guide, despite revenue landing within guidance. This was a meaningful shortfall against the preview’s operative expectation of delivering the guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $8.6 million fell below original guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … Q2 2026 Guidance | $10.0–15.0M”; the preview says to use company guidance as the “operative consensus.”

surprises.description: Coiled tubing day rates fell 15% even as days worked rose 16%, and price increases did not keep pace with costs, which rose about 12% quarter-over-quarter. The preview highlighted realized pricing increases as a key swing factor, so the reported pricing and margin pressure was worse than hoped.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Coiled tubing costs including consumables, labor, and repairs rose about 12% quarter-over-quarter, and price increases failed to fully offset the inflation”; days worked “rise 16% but day rate fall 15%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says “pricing” was the “biggest swing factor” and asks whether “any increases actually stuck”; it also says prices “need to go up, full stop.”

surprises.description: Two large-diameter coiled tubing units—about 17% of that fleet—were out of service, with the second not expected back until near year-end. The preview did not flag this equipment downtime as a risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Two large-diameter coiled tubing units (about 17% of the large-diameter fleet) went out of service on maintenance issues,” and the second is “not expected to return until near year-end.”

surprises.description: Q3 guidance implies revenue below $140 million at the midpoint and adjusted EBITDA flat to modestly down from Q2. That is weaker than the preview’s base case framing of a $140–145 million revenue quarter, and it meets the preview’s flagged downside condition of Q3 guidance below $140 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects revenue of $133 million to $143 million, with adjusted EBITDA expected to be flat to modestly down versus Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario has revenue of “$140–145M”; its bear scenario says “Q3 guide below $140M.”

surprises.description: Completion tools revenue rebounded sharply to $37.1 million, up 44% quarter-over-quarter, with stages up 45%; international sales and domestic share gains contributed. The preview flagged the line’s Q1 decline and watched for a recovery, so this was a stronger-than-expected rebound.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Completion tools revenue surged 44% quarter-over-quarter to $37.1 million on a 45% increase in stages,” boosted by “strong international sales and domestic market share gains”; international revenue rose 17% in the first half.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says completion tools “fell about 10% in Q1” and describes a bull case in which “Completion tools stages return to Q1-prior levels.”

surprises.description: The company kept its $20–30 million full-year CapEx range but now expects spending in the middle-to-lower end, supporting cash flow neutrality in the second half. That is a more favorable spending and cash-flow framing than simply monitoring pacing against the full range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year CapEx guidance of $20 million to $30 million was reaffirmed but now expected in the middle-to-lower end, supporting cash flow neutrality in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flags “free cash flow and liquidity” and says to watch “capex pacing against the $20–30M FY guide.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $141.8 million, within the original $136–146 million guidance and close to the preview’s approximately $140.8 million street proxy.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $240 million, well above the preview’s roughly $210.8 million consensus, and management said production was steady enough to meet retail demand and order intake. That suggests the production pause had ended more decisively than an at-or-above-consensus result alone would have indicated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached $240 million, up 12.1% year-over-year and 32.7% sequentially, driven by steady production rates meeting retail and order intake levels.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$210.8M”; the preview said revenue near or above $211M would suggest the pause ended.

surprises.description: Diluted EPS of $0.63 substantially exceeded the preview’s $0.365–$0.39 consensus range, even with $0.11 of OMARS acquisition expenses weighing on the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS surged to $0.63 in Q2 from $0.05 in Q1, despite $0.11 of OMARS acquisition-related expenses weighing on the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | $0.365 (MarketBeat, Jul 29, 2026) or $0.39 (Zacks via Nasdaq).”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin reached 15%, above the preview’s implied 14.0%–14.3% range. The expected full-year normalization to the mid-13% range was still reiterated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit was $35.9 million, or 15% of sales, though management expects full-year gross margins to normalize to the mid-13% range as chassis mix increases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin (implied) | ~14.0–14.3%”; the preview also said the FY guide called for “mid-13%.”

surprises.description: Management’s roughly $250 million quarterly revenue target for the second half is more ambitious than the preview’s estimate that about $458 million of H2 revenue was needed to reach the bottom of the full-year range. At that quarterly pace, H2 would total about $500 million, although the $850–$900 million full-year guidance itself was reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed full-year 2024 guidance of $850 million to $900 million in revenue, targeting roughly $250 million per quarter in the back half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Reaching $850M requires roughly $458M of H2 revenue.”

surprises.description: The manufacturing facility plan was described on a much earlier timeline than the preview expected: construction was said to begin in Q4 2024, with production readiness targeted for late 2025, rather than a late-summer 2026 groundbreaking. Management also expected to fund it largely from organic cash flow, rather than emphasizing the cash drag anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new 200,000+ square foot manufacturing facility is targeted to be production-ready by late 2025, with construction beginning Q4 2024 and funding expected largely from organic cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Ooltewah expansion ($100M) was targeted to break ground in late summer 2026, which starts an H2 cash drag.”

surprises.description: OMARS charges appear somewhat higher over Q2–Q4 than the preview’s estimate: the call reported $0.11 in Q2 and another $0.04–$0.05 still to come, or roughly $0.15–$0.16 over that period.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$0.11 of OMARS acquisition-related expenses” weighed on Q2, with “$0.04-$0.05 remaining” for the year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “About $0.13 per share of non-cash charges remains across Q2–Q4.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed military commitments above $200 million, up from $150 million the prior quarter, with most revenue expected in 2026 and 2027. The preview did not identify these commitments as an expected demand or revenue contributor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Military commitments have surpassed $200 million, up from $150 million last quarter, with production beginning in 2025 and most revenue recognized in 2026 and 2027.”

surprises.description: The company reported debt reduction, a larger cash balance, and shareholder returns during the quarter despite the preview’s expectation that the facility expansion would start an H2 cash drag. It repaid another $20 million of debt, held $55.6 million in cash, and returned about $4.9 million through repurchases and dividends.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced debt by an additional $20 million since Q1 while growing its cash balance to $55.6 million, up $2.6 million sequentially”; it “returned approximately $4.9 million to shareholders via share repurchases and dividends in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Ooltewah expansion ($100M) was targeted to break ground in late summer 2026, which starts an H2 cash drag.”

in_line: Full-year revenue guidance of $850–$900 million was reaffirmed, as the preview expected.
The full-year gross-margin outlook remained in the mid-13% range, as expected.
Domestic retail demand and dealer inventories were reported flat, consistent with the preview’s description of soft retail.

surprises.description: The company kept its full-year guidance, but the outlook within the ranges was uneven: revenue is now expected at the higher end, while gross profit and adjusted EBITDA are expected at the lower end because of margin pressure. That is a weaker profit outlook than the revenue positioning suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management maintained full-year guidance and expects revenue at the higher end of the $1.01–$1.04 billion range, but gross profit of $405–$425 million and adjusted EBITDA of $230–$245 million at the lower end due to margin pressure.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the base scenario was for guidance to be reaffirmed; it also flagged a raise versus reaffirmation as a key issue.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.29 exceeded the preview's $0.26–$0.27 estimates, a clear beat against both cited estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EPS was up 12% to $0.29.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 adjusted EPS consensus was listed as $0.26 (MarketBeat) or $0.27 (Simply Wall St).

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA of $59.4 million came in slightly below the preview writer's estimate of approximately $60–$62 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA was up 6% to $59.4 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave the writer's own Q2 adjusted EBITDA estimate as approximately $60–$62 million.

surprises.description: Payables revenue grew 21.6%, below the preview's threshold for a clean beat of growth above about 25%. Growth was stronger than the preview's mid-teens slowdown scenario, but did not reach the stated beat threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: Payables revenue grew 21.6% to $30.4 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said growth above about 25% would be a clean beat, while a step down to mid-teens would make Q1 look like a pull-forward.

surprises.description: Despite Payables revenue growth, adjusted gross profit fell and margins contracted sharply. The preview focused on revenue growth, not the reported deterioration in Payables profitability as buyer-funded revenue became more prominent.
surprises.fact_evidence: Payables adjusted gross profit fell 10.4% and margins dropped 760 basis points to 21.4%; buyer-funded revenue was up 26.3%, now dominates, and is booked gross at lower margins.

surprises.description: Treasury Solutions revenue growth was roughly in line with the preview's mid-teens expectation, but margins compressed substantially as faster-growing products with lower margins became a larger part of the mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: Treasury Solutions revenue grew 14.9% to $60.5 million, while gross margin compressed roughly 590 basis points to 88.5% due to mix shift from Passport, up 125%, and Priority Tech Ventures, up nearly 400%, which run at 30–40% margins.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Treasury Solutions as the highest-margin profit driver and expected mid-teens growth in balances and revenue.

surprises.description: Recently enacted card-network interchange price increases added another cost pressure on top of the lower-margin gross accounting for growing buyer-funded Payables revenue; this specific cost headwind was not raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Recently enacted Mastercard and Visa interchange price increases raised cost of goods sold, creating a margin “double whammy” alongside gross-revenue accounting on growing buyer-funded Payables.

surprises.description: The call surfaced an ongoing special-committee evaluation of a take-private proposal that the preview did not mention, but management declined to comment, so it provided no update on the matter.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management declined to comment on the ongoing special committee evaluation of a take-private proposal; analysts noted it as a key overhang.

in_line: Q2 revenue of $262.3 million was within the preview's conflicting consensus estimates of $257.8 million and $263.0 million, and near its $259–$262 million base scenario.
Full-year guidance was reaffirmed, as in the preview's base scenario.
Treasury Solutions revenue growth of 14.9% was approximately in line with the preview's mid-teens growth expectation.
Net leverage improved to 3.8x, meeting the preview's stated level of at or below 3.8x.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $258.8 million, above the preview’s $240.3 million consensus and also within its bull scenario of $258–265 million. The beat was about 7.7% versus consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 10.6% to $258.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $240.3M” consensus; the bull scenario projected “$258–265M.”

surprises.description: Energy Storage gross margin reached 56.2%, well above the preview’s roughly 40% base expectation and the 35–40% full-year guide. The preview identified a result above 50% as upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Energy Storage revenue nearly tripled, increasing 195.1% to $42.8 million at a 56.2% gross margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Q2 margin near 40% validates the guide”; “A repeat above 50% would be upside.”

surprises.description: Ormat raised its FY2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA ranges rather than reaffirming them: revenue is now $1.15–$1.2 billion versus $1.11–$1.16 billion, and EBITDA is $630–$650 million versus $615–$645 million. This was the guidance-revision quarter the preview anticipated, though the increase was less than its bull-case thresholds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $1.15–$1.2 billion … and adjusted EBITDA of $630–$650 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said guidance revision was “the most important item” and described the bull case as guidance raised to “≥$1,160M revenue / ≥$645M EBITDA”; its base case was guidance “reaffirmed or narrowed to upper half.”

surprises.description: Product revenue fell 21.6%, a less severe decline than the roughly 26% year-over-year drop expected in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Product segment revenue fell 21.6% to $46.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Product revenue expected to fall about 26% YoY in Q2.”

surprises.description: Despite the less severe revenue decline, Product gross margin compressed to 9.7% amid higher European construction costs and FX. The preview focused on revenue and backlog and did not flag this margin pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Product segment revenue fell 21.6% to $46.7 million with gross margin compressing to 9.7% due to higher European construction costs and FX.”

surprises.description: Product backlog fell further to about $203 million from $239 million after Q1, rather than rebuilding as the preview said was needed to support the 2027–2028 ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog declined to about $203 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Backlog was $239M after Q1”; “a backlog rebuild is what signals whether 2027 Product is fundable,” and “Book-to-bill above 1.0x is needed.”

surprises.description: The company recorded a $6.6 million write-off on a storage project it chose not to pursue, a one-off charge not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net income fell to $27.1 million ($0.43/share) from $28 million ($0.46/share), reflecting a $6.6 million write-off of a storage project the company decided not to pursue.”

surprises.description: Re-contracted and blend-and-extend PPAs, including Blue Mountain, are expected to add roughly $14 million in annual revenue through 2030 with minimal incremental investment; the preview did not identify this revenue opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Re-contracted and blend-and-extend PPAs, including Blue Mountain, are expected to add roughly $14 million in annual revenues through 2030 with minimal incremental capital investment.”

surprises.description: Ormat disclosed about 190 megawatts of contracted capacity for 2031–2034 at roughly $86/MWh, below current market pricing of over $100/MWh, creating potential repricing upside that the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has approximately 190 megawatts under contract from 2031–2034 priced at about $86/MWh, below current market pricing of over $100/MWh, representing embedded repricing upside.”

in_line: Management expects Energy Storage merchant pricing to normalize in the second half, consistent with the preview’s expectation that unusually strong PJM pricing would not repeat and that margins would normalize toward the 35–40% full-year guide.
The company reaffirmed its 2028 portfolio target of 2.6–2.8 gigawatts, as the preview specifically flagged reaffirmation of that target as a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: Adjusted operating EPS was $1.14, well below the preview’s $1.38 consensus estimate, despite revenue coming in above the preview’s estimate range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net operating EPS grew to $1.14.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating EPS: $1.38.”

surprises.description: Specialty’s combined ratio was 98%, above the preview’s 85–90% base case and even above the level the preview identified as strengthening the bear case. The roughly $30 million reserve charge for Middle East conflict claims and updated inflation assumptions contributed to the result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Radian took roughly $30 million in reserves in the Specialty segment for expected and potential Middle East conflict claims plus updated inflation assumptions, pushing the Q2 specialty combined ratio to 98%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “Specialty combined ratio 85–90%”; it said a result “above 95% strengthens the bear case.”

surprises.description: Management said a low-90s Specialty combined ratio is now more representative of the softening market, a less favorable outlook than the mid-80s to high-80s historical range cited for Inigo and the preview’s 85–90% base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A specialty combined ratio in the low 90s is now more reflective of the softening market environment, up from the mid-80s to high-80s seen historically for Inigo.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case assumed a Specialty combined ratio of “85–90%”; it also noted management had stressed “profitability over volume.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $575 million exceeded even the high end of the preview’s $537–557 million estimate range, with the first full quarter of Inigo’s contribution driving the increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenues grew 93% year-over-year to $575 million … driven primarily by the first full quarter of Inigo's specialty insurance contribution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed quarterly revenue estimates of “$556.5M” and “$537.2M.”

surprises.description: Rather than the preview’s concern about weak Specialty premiums from increased competition or business being ceded or walked away from, management expects second-half Specialty earned premiums to be about 20% above the first half, citing seasonality.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Second-half specialty earned premiums are expected to be approximately 20% higher than the first half due to seasonality in premium recognition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warned that “a weak premium line would point to heavier ceded reinsurance or business being walked away from.”

surprises.description: Mortgage credit results were better than the preview’s concern about normalization and possible deterioration: the default rate edged down from Radian’s Q1 level, new defaults fell quarter over quarter, and favorable cures produced positive prior-period development rather than the adverse development in the preview’s bear scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New defaults declined 9% quarter-over-quarter to 12,400, the default rate fell to 2.47%, and favorable cure trends drove $20 million of positive prior-period development.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said MGIC’s delinquency increase was framed as “broad-based normalization,” noted Radian’s Q1 default rate was 2.51%, and listed “adverse mortgage development” as a bear-case tell.

surprises.description: Radian raised its full-year buyback outlook toward the upper end of the $200–250 million range, exceeding the preview’s expectation of reaffirmation and an on-pace program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Radian repurchased $176 million (5 million shares) year-to-date and raised full-year buyback guidance toward the upper end of the $200-$250 million range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case assumed “buyback on pace” and its catalyst checklist called for “Confirmation of the $200–250M program.”

surprises.description: Expected 2026 dividends from Radian Guaranty increased to at least $650 million, above the previously stated minimum of $600 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Increasing expected 2026 dividends from Radian Guaranty to at least $650 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited guidance of “at least $600M of dividends from Radian Guaranty to the holdco in 2026.”

surprises.description: Holding-company leverage had already fallen below the preview’s sub-20% year-end target, reaching 19% after a $75 million revolver repayment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced holding company leverage to 19% by repaying $75 million of its revolver draw.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted leverage of 20.2% and “a target below 20% by year-end.”

in_line: Radian’s new mortgage insurance written rose 14% year over year to $16.3 billion, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a strong industry read-through from MGIC’s $18 billion of Q2 NIW, up 8.5% year over year.

surprises.description: The preview put Q2 political advertising at $120–150 million, and Nexstar reported $147 million, near the top of that range. More positively, management said political pacing was ahead of expectations and that it had raised its internal targets multiple times.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 political advertising reached $147 million” and management indicated “internal political targets have been raised multiple times with pacing running ahead of expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My base case is $120–150M, but the Q3/Q4 pacing commentary matters more than the Q2 number.”

surprises.description: Combined revenue grew 4.7% year over year, modestly above the preview’s derived estimate of about 4% growth. The gap was small, even though the preview’s headline revenue consensus was also essentially met.
surprises.fact_evidence: “On a combined (pro forma) basis net revenue grew only 4.7% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pro-forma YoY is ~+4% against my derived base of ~$1.906B.”

surprises.description: The preview did not discuss the CW outlook, but management said the network remains on track to reach profitability in Q4 2026 and expects full-year losses to improve by more than 30%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The CW remains on track for profitability in Q4 2026 with full-year losses expected to improve by more than 30%.”

surprises.description: The preview did not mention a local measurement change, while management said an August 31 Nielsen change could significantly increase local ad impressions. The potential impact was described as significant but was not quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A planned August 31 Nielsen local measurement change lowering the viewing threshold from 5 minutes to 1 minute could significantly boost local ad impressions.”

in_line: Q2 net revenue was $1.99 billion versus the preview’s $1.98 billion consensus.
Nonpolitical advertising fell 5.8%, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a mid-single-digit decline.
The TEGNA antitrust trial remains scheduled for July 2027, consistent with the preview’s stated proposed timeline.
The reported debt repayment is consistent with the preview’s expectation that excess free cash flow would go to deleveraging; the preview did not give a Q2 repayment estimate.

surprises.description: The preview put adjusted free cash flow at $600–670 million, with anything above $650 million a new record. Permian Resources reported a record $751 million for Q2, beating the top of that range by $81 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q2 2026 free cash flow of $751 million, up nearly 50% quarter-over-quarter,” and “a record $0.88 of free cash flow per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My bogey is $600–670M. Anything above $650M would be a new record.”

surprises.description: The preview listed FY26 oil guidance of 190,000–195,000 barrels per day and treated a reaffirmation as the base case. The company raised its oil guidance to 199,000 barrels per day; only 1,000 barrels per day of the 6,500-barrel-per-day increase came from acquired volumes, with most attributed to higher working interest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 oil production guidance to 199,000 barrels per day”; “only 1,000 bbl/d of the 6,500 bbl/d production increase came from acquired volumes,” with the majority from higher working interest.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 production … 190–195 MBbl/d oil”; the base scenario was “FY guidance reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: The preview anticipated that negative Waha prices could make gas and NGL volumes soft, but the reported commentary also described unexpectedly strong revenue protection: despite curtailing gas production, the company realized a positive price and captured more than $75 million of incremental gas revenue through curtailments, transportation, and hedging.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Proactively curtailed natural gas production by ~20% quarter-over-quarter amid WAHA prices averaging negative $3.14 per Mcf (low of negative $9.52), yet still realized $0.38 per Mcf and captured over $75 million of incremental gas revenue through curtailments, firm transportation, and hedging.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gas and NGL volumes and Waha drag” were a key metric to watch; management had “guided to lower gas and NGL volumes if negative Waha persisted.”

surprises.description: The preview cited a $600–800 million Delaware deal range. Year-to-date acquisitions totaled about $1.05 billion across roughly 190 transactions, above that range; the largest was a $520 million Ward County bolt-on, followed by a trade that expanded operating locations and lateral length.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date the company acquired ~55,000 net acres in the core Delaware Basin for ~$1.05 billion across roughly 190 separate transactions”; the largest deal was “a ~2,000 net acre, 5,000 BOE/day Ward County bolt-on for $520 million,” followed by a trade increasing locations from 50 to 120 and average lateral length by 20%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has flagged a $600–800M Delaware deal range”; the preview also watched for “any bolt-on in the $600–800M band or an equity-funded deal.”

surprises.description: Despite the much larger acquisition program, leverage was about 0.5x at quarter-end and is expected to remain there at year-end, rather than moving up to fund the deals; the preview had highlighted the prior 0.8x leverage and raised the possibility of an equity-funded acquisition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Leverage stood at approximately 0.5x at the end of Q2 and is expected to remain around 0.5x at year-end, giving the company an investment-grade balance sheet while funding acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported “Leverage 0.8x” at Q1 and asked whether there would be “any bolt-on in the $600–800M band or an equity-funded deal.”

surprises.description: The company said working interest in completed wells was about 82%, versus an original expectation of 75%. That higher ownership helped drive production and the guidance increase, beyond what the preview described.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Higher working interest of ~82% in completed wells versus the original 75% expectation.”

in_line: The preview anticipated gas and NGL volume softness and possible curtailments if negative Waha prices persisted; the company did curtail gas production by about 20%.

surprises.description: The preview’s consensus was $5.96–$6.03 of adjusted operating EPS, while Primerica reported $6.41. The beat was partly supported by an unanticipated tax equity investment that reduced income tax expense by $4.6 million, or about $0.15 per share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating EPS rose 17% year-over-year to $6.41, boosted by roughly $0.15 per share from a tax equity investment that reduced income tax expense by $4.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating EPS $5.96” (Zacks) and “Adj. operating EPS (alt.) $6.03” (MarketBeat).

surprises.description: The preview said Q2 policies down more than about 5% would make the full-year flat-to-down-2% guide difficult to reach. Policies issued fell 12%, and management now expects full-year issued policies to decline by mid-single digits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Issued policies dropped 12%,” and management guided full-year issued policies to “decline mid-single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 term life policies issued: flat to down about 2%”; a Q2 print “worse than about -5% YoY” would make that guide “hard to reach and raise[] the risk of a cut.”

surprises.description: The preview cited a full-year life-licensed sales-force outlook of flat to up about 1%. Primerica lowered its outlook to flat to down 2%, saying recruiting improvements came more slowly than hoped and licensing lagged recruiting.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management lowered its full-year sales force size outlook to flat to down 2% versus 2025,” as “recruiting improvements arrived slower than hoped and licensing lags behind recruiting.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 life-licensed reps: flat to up about 1% vs. 12/31/25.”

surprises.description: The preview said the FY2026 ISP sales outlook was upper-single-digit growth. Primerica reported total securities sales growth of 23% and guided full-year ISP sales growth to 10%–15%, above that prior outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total securities sales grew 23% year-over-year,” including managed account sales up 43%, mutual fund sales up 20%, and variable annuity sales up 17%; full-year ISP sales were guided to “increase 10% to 15%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 ISP sales: upper-single-digit growth.”

in_line: The Term Life benefits and claims ratio was 57.9%, broadly in line with the preview’s approximately 58% full-year expectation.

surprises.description: The preview put Q1 revenue consensus at $592.9 million, while the two reported segment revenues total about $524 million ($437 million in tobacco and $87 million in ingredients), roughly $69 million below consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: Tobacco revenue was $437 million, down 13%; ingredients revenue was $87 million, down 3%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $592.9M”

surprises.description: The preview expected adjusted EPS of $0.25; instead, the company reported a $5 million net loss and consolidated operating income fell to $2.3 million. The net-loss figure is GAAP, so it is not directly comparable with the adjusted-EPS estimate, but the reported result was markedly weak.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated operating income fell to $2.3 million from $33.8 million year-over-year, and the company posted a net loss of $5 million versus net income of $8.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (adjusted) | $0.25”

surprises.description: Tobacco operating income plunged to $3.5 million from $35.7 million as customers delayed purchases in an oversupply market. The preview flagged oversupply and unfavorable price/mix as risks, but the reported collapse was far more severe than that discussion alone indicated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tobacco segment operating income collapsed to $3.5 million in Q1 FY2027 from $35.7 million a year earlier, with revenue down 13% to $437 million as customers delayed purchasing amid an oversupply market.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether oversupply is compressing realized price per kg.”

surprises.description: Ingredients fell below the preview’s already weak prior-year comparison: revenue was $87 million versus the $89.1 million Q1 FY2026 base, and the segment moved from $1.7 million of operating income to a $700,000 loss rather than showing a turnaround.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ingredients segment swung to a $700,000 operating loss from $1.7 million of operating income a year earlier, with revenue down 3% to $87 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Q1 FY2026 base is $89.1M revenue and $1.7M operating income.”

surprises.description: Estimated unsold flue-cured and burley stocks increased to about 180 million kilos, up 57 million kilos from December. That stock build runs counter to the hoped-for inventory normalization, although it is not the same measure as the preview’s uncommitted-inventory percentage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Estimated unsold flue-cured and burley stocks reached about 180 million kilos at June 30, up roughly 11 million kilos from March 31 and 57 million kilos above December 31.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Movement toward 20% supports the FY2027 recovery thesis. Flat or higher undercuts management's stated timeline.”

surprises.description: Management said it does not expect to repeat last year’s large dark air-cured inventory write-downs, a favorable update against the preview’s concern about further write-downs and its bear-case assumption of a new $15 million or larger charge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management does not expect to repeat the large dark air-cured tobacco inventory write-downs incurred last year, citing wrapper demand strength and new inventory management initiatives.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Incremental dark air-cured write-downs” were a key issue to watch; the bear scenario assumed “new write-down of $15M+.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s concern about dividend coverage and debt, net debt was about $52 million lower year over year, with approximately $1.1 billion of liquidity available. This is a more constructive debt position than the risk-focused preview discussion suggested, though no specific debt forecast was given.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt was slightly over $1 billion as of June 30, 2026, approximately $52 million lower than a year earlier, with total liquidity availability of about $1.1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Dividend coverage and net debt. ... Net debt direction and capital-allocation language will indicate whether the yield is durable.”

surprises.description: Foreign currency movements created a $4.4 million negative operating-income variance in tobacco, an additional headwind not identified in the preview’s discussion of the segment’s risks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Foreign currency movements caused a $4.4 million negative operating income variance in the tobacco segment versus the prior-year quarter.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed that full-year customer demand remains consistent with its initial sales plan, with shipments weighted toward the second half, and said uncommitted inventories should move back toward the 20% target.
