This is consistent with the preview’s stated FY2027 inventory-normalization and recovery thesis; the call facts do not provide the actual uncommitted-inventory percentage.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.83 and adjusted EBITDA was $35.3 million, both well below expectations; the preview looked for EPS of $1.33–$1.34 and EBITDA of about $47–49 million. Management attributed roughly half the shortfall to gross margin and half to higher operating expenses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell to $35.3 million” and “adjusted diluted EPS dropped to $0.83”; “roughly half the shortfall from gross margin and half from higher operating expenses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS $1.33–$1.34”; “Adjusted EBITDA ~$47–49M (derived).”

surprises.description: Tennant cut its full-year adjusted EBITDA and EPS outlook substantially, even though the preview expected the prior guidance to be reaffirmed. The new ranges are $155–170 million of EBITDA and $3.80–4.45 of EPS, down from $175–190 million and $4.70–5.30.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cut adjusted EBITDA guidance to $155–170 million and adjusted EPS to $3.80–4.45 (down from prior $4.70–5.30).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year guidance (reaffirmed): … adjusted EPS $4.70–5.30, adjusted EBITDA $175–190M”; “FY26 adjusted EPS guide of $4.70–5.30. Reaffirmation is the floor.”

surprises.description: Gross margin came in below the preview’s roughly 40% expectation at 39.5%. Management also described a slower recovery ahead—flat near 39.5% in Q3 and roughly 41% in Q4—rather than a quick return toward the preview’s 42–43% normalized level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin was 39.5%, down 260 basis points year-over-year”; management expects Q3 “flat near 39.5%” before “roughly 41% in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs about 40% or better”; management “targets 42–43% normalized.”

surprises.description: Sales missed the preview’s estimate, growing only 1.7% to $324 million versus expected sales of about $329.6 million and 3.4% growth. North American parts shortages constrained shipments, so reported sales lagged demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales grew only 1.7% to $324 million as North American parts shortages constrained shipments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales $329.55M”; “YoY +3.4%.”

surprises.description: Orders and backlog remained stronger than the shipment picture suggested: orders reached $339 million, while backlog rose to $127 million instead of converting fully into sales. The preview specifically looked for backlog conversion, but parts shortages left a larger queue of work for later in the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Orders reached $339 million, up 6.6% year-over-year”; “Backlog climbed to $127 million, up $18 million from Q1 and $50 million since year-end,” providing second-half momentum as constraints ease.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs to show backlog converting to shipments and a positive volume contribution”; backlog was $109 million after Q1.

surprises.description: The ERP recovery schedule slipped: normal North American operations are now expected in the first half of 2027 rather than the original second half of 2026, and EMEA deployment moved beyond 2026. That extends the disruption beyond the timing investors had previously been given.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ERP optimization timeline slipped one to two quarters”; North American operations are expected to return to normal in “the first half of 2027,” and EMEA deployment is “deferred beyond 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “ERP costs and cash flow” and described the ERP project as an overhang, but did not anticipate this further schedule delay.

surprises.description: Regional results showed weakness beyond the preview’s hoped-for positive volume contribution: EMEA and APAC sales declined, with discounting hurting EMEA pricing and elevated distributor inventories accompanying softer APAC demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EMEA organic sales declined 2.8% with negative net pricing from increased discounting,” and “APAC fell 10.6% on softer demand and elevated distributor inventories.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs to show backlog converting to shipments and a positive volume contribution”; the preview also cited a full-year organic growth guide of +3.0% to +6.5%.

surprises.description: Cash generation remained weak year to date and leverage moved to the top of its target range. The first-half cash outflow was smaller than Q1’s alone, suggesting some sequential improvement, but it was still a $26.2 million use versus cash generation a year earlier; leverage was 2x versus 1.78x after Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half operating cash flow was a use of $26.2 million versus $22.1 million generated a year earlier”; net leverage was “2x … (upper end of the 1x–2x target range).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Operating cash flow inflection from -$31.2M” and reported Q1 net leverage of 1.78x.

surprises.description: Tennant raised its full-year sales outlook even as it cut profitability guidance: the new $1.27–1.31 billion range is above the prior $1.24–1.28 billion range that the preview expected to be reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year net sales guidance to $1.27–1.31 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year guidance (reaffirmed): Net sales $1,240–1,280M.”

surprises.description: The Targa pipeline was expected to enter commercial service in Q3, but management now expects it in early Q4. The timing change is accompanied by a shift of drilling and completion activity from Texas to New Mexico and a 1.2 drilled-to-turned-in-line ratio that will carry DUCs into next year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Targa high-pressure gathering pipeline is expected in service early Q4 2026,” prompting a shift of drilling and completion activity from Texas to New Mexico, with a “1.2 drilled-to-turned-in-line ratio carrying DUCs into next year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the Targa line was “Guided to Q3 commercial operations,” and warned that slippage could push second-half volumes into 2027.

surprises.description: Full-year CapEx guidance rose to $236 million, 12% above the previous guidance midpoint of $210 million and above the prior $200–220 million range. About two-thirds of the revised spend is for infrastructure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year CapEx guidance was raised 12% (or $26 million) to $236 million, with roughly one-third tied to upstream activity and two-thirds to infrastructure.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 CapEx guidance of “$200–220M ($210M midpoint)” and said it had been raised by $10M at Q1.

surprises.description: Instead of reducing debt as the preview anticipated, REPX drew on its credit facility and principal debt rose by $26 million to $273 million. Leverage stayed around 1.0x, so the increase did not raise the reported leverage ratio.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Principal debt increased 11% (or $26 million) to $273 million as the company drew on its credit facility, keeping leverage around 1.0x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the company had $247M of principal debt entering Q2 and that “most post-dividend free cash flow goes to debt reduction.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was only $6 million even as operating cash flow rose 35% sequentially, as cash CapEx jumped 153%. That left little cash available for the debt reduction the preview expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow rose 35% quarter-over-quarter to $64 million, but cash CapEx jumped 153% to $73 million, cutting Q2 free cash flow to just $6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “Free cash flow, debt paydown, and capex” as a key issue and said “most post-dividend free cash flow goes to debt reduction.”

surprises.description: Q3 oil production guidance points to a stronger near-term rate than the preview’s general expectation of sequential growth: the midpoint is 25,600 barrels per day, 5% above the June exit rate and more than 20% above the Q2 average.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 oil production is guided at 25,600 barrels per day at the midpoint, 5% above June's level and over 20% above the full Q2 average.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “guided to sequential growth each quarter,” but gave no Q3 oil-production estimate.

surprises.description: The FY26 oil midpoint was raised to 23,000 barrels per day, rather than merely reaffirming the existing range. The increase is modest, but it moves the midpoint to the old range’s upper end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year oil production guidance was raised 2% to 23,000 barrels per day at the midpoint, implying approximately 30% year-over-year oil production growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 oil guidance of “22.0–23.0 MBbl/d” and asked whether it would be “Reaffirmed or raised?”

surprises.description: REPX reported that Silverback’s production is now roughly twice the buy-side case projection despite no new wells being drilled, while per-well workover costs fell about 59%. This outperformance was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Silverback acquisition's production is now approximately double the buy-side case projection with no new wells drilled, and per-well workover costs fell about 59%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview did not discuss Silverback performance or workover costs.

surprises.description: A relatively small, intentional workover program added about 700 barrels of oil per day from low-decline wells. The preview did not identify this production contribution or spend as an expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly $2.3 million of intentional workover spend added about 700 barrels of oil per day of incremental production from low-decline wells.”

surprises.description: April and May midstream constraints forced temporary shut-ins that reduced Q2 oil production by about 2,000 barrels per day, an operational headwind not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Midstream constraints during April and May forced temporary well shut-ins that reduced Q2 oil production by approximately 2,000 barrels per day.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected Q2 oil production of “20.7–21.3 MBbl/d” and highlighted oil volumes versus that range, but did not mention these shut-ins.

in_line: Q2 oil production grew 5% sequentially, consistent with the preview’s expectation that production would grow sequentially; the supplied facts do not give the Q2 average needed to compare directly with the 20.7–21.3 MBbl/d guidance range.
The approximately 30% year-over-year oil growth implied by the revised FY26 midpoint is consistent with the growth thesis noted in the preview.

surprises.description: SM Energy reported adjusted EPS of $2.19, above the preview’s $1.93 consensus estimate, though within the preview’s independent $2.00–$2.20 estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income was $526 million ($2.19 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $1.93”

surprises.description: Second-half production guidance was raised to 435,000–440,000 Boe/d, above the preview’s expectation of volumes near 430,000 Boe/d; oil guidance of about 238,000 barrels/day was also above the preview’s prior 228,000–235,000 range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised second-half 2026 production guidance to 435,000–440,000 Boe/d (with oil at approximately 238,000 barrels/day).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “2H volumes near 430 MBoe/d are the buy-side expectations”; the preview also listed “Oil production | 228–235 MBbl/d (company guide).”

surprises.description: Q2 capital spending was well below the preview’s expected guidance range, at $717 million versus an $815–855 million range. Management attributed the underspend to D&C timing and reaffirmed full-year capex, so the difference appears to be timing rather than a lower annual plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 capital expenditures were $717 million, below the $835 million guidance midpoint due to D&C timing, while full-year capital guidance of $2.65–$2.85 billion was reaffirmed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capex | $815–855M (company guide)” and “Holding capex at $2.65–2.85B” was the preview’s expected full-year outcome.

surprises.description: The preview identified a synergy target increase toward $425 million or more as a likely positive catalyst, but management did not report raising the $375 million target. It said about $355 million—95% of that target—had been actioned, which is strong progress but falls short of the anticipated target increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has now actioned approximately 95% ($355 million) of its raised $375 million run-rate synergy target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise toward $425M+ would be the cleanest available positive surprise” and “A raise above $375M ... [is] the clearest upside source.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a durable reduction of about $50 million in full-year recurring G&A guidance, a cost improvement the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year recurring G&A guidance was lowered by approximately $50 million at the midpoint, described as a durable run-rate reduction driven by accelerated integration.”

surprises.description: SM Energy generated $467 million of adjusted free cash flow, above the preview’s $300 million-plus threshold for a substantial FCF quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SM Energy generated $467 million of adjusted free cash flow in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a “$300M+ FCF quarter” as the reference point for buyback execution.

surprises.description: Galvan proceeds were used to redeem all $819 million of 2026 notes and call the 2027 notes, leaving no senior-note maturities until mid-2028. The preview discussed debt reduction but did not anticipate this maturity cleanup.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company used Galvan divestiture proceeds to redeem all $819 million of 2026 senior notes and called the remaining 2027 notes, leaving no senior note maturities until mid-2028.”

surprises.description: Management reported that Uinta completion pace had more than doubled from early 2026 and that recent completion efficiencies had saved over $1 million per well; the preview did not identify this operating improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Uinta completion pace exceeded 2,600 feet per day (more than double the early-2026 rate), delivering over $1 million per well in cost savings over the past six months alongside 4-mile lateral development.”

surprises.description: The call described the Galvan divestiture as substantially achieving the $1 billion divestiture target within a year of the merger and as shifting South Texas toward higher-margin, liquids-rich Austin Chalk development; the preview did not flag that strategic repositioning as an expected result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Galvan divestiture substantially achieved the $1 billion divestiture target within a year of the merger and high-graded South Texas toward higher-margin, liquids-rich Austin Chalk development.”

in_line: The company began returning capital through buybacks in Q2: it repurchased $84 million of shares and paid $53 million in dividends, consistent with the preview’s expectation that buybacks would start and with its stated 20% post-dividend FCF policy.
Net debt was approximately $6.25 billion, within the preview’s estimated $6.2–$6.5 billion range.
Full-year capital guidance of $2.65–$2.85 billion was reaffirmed, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: The preview did not flag a CEO departure, but Ladd Wilks is resigning effective August 7 to take a board seat. Executive Chairman Matt Wilks will take over as CEO while retaining the chairman role.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CEO Ladd Wilks is resigning effective August 7th to take a board seat, with Executive Chairman Matt Wilks assuming the CEO role while retaining his chairman title.”

surprises.description: The preview said a Q2 stimulation margin below roughly 11–12% would suggest price increases had not held, and highlighted 11% as the key threshold. The reported margin was 9%, although it improved from Q1’s 8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Stimulation services revenue grew to $430 million with EBITDA rising to $39 million (9% margin)” and the disciplined fleet count remained in the low 20s.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A margin below ~11–12% in Q2 would suggest the price increases did not hold”; the catalyst checklist also asked for “Stimulation margin ≥11%.”

surprises.description: The preview anticipated price increases layering in during Q2, with their effect becoming more pronounced in the second half. Management said most Q2 increases had renegotiation windows that deferred their benefit into Q3 and Q4, indicating less immediate Q2 realization than investors might have expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The majority of Q2 price increases carried renegotiation windows that push the benefit into Q3 and Q4, implying stronger back-half pricing rather than immediate Q2 gains.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said increases were “layering in through Q2 and becoming ‘more pronounced’ in the back half.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $69 million, just below the preview’s roughly $70–75 million consensus estimate and its roughly $72 million catalyst level, though it fell within the preview’s $68–78 million base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose to $498 million from $450 million in Q1, with adjusted EBITDA improving to $69 million (14% margin) from $54 million (12% margin) in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$70–75M”; the catalyst checklist specified “Adjusted EBITDA vs. ~$72M.”

surprises.description: Liquidity was about $72 million, down from the $108 million reported for Q1, while ABL borrowings rose from $116 million to $162 million. The preview flagged liquidity as an issue to watch but did not forecast this level or borrowing increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total liquidity remained tight at approximately $72 million”; “ABL borrowings rose to $162 million from $116 million quarter-over-quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Free cash flow and liquidity” as a key metric to watch and gave Q1 liquidity as “$108M.”

in_line: Revenue of $498 million was within the preview’s $470–490 million base scenario and between the conflicting consensus estimates of about $473 million and $508.7 million.
Proppant EBITDA of $6 million was above the preview’s $5 million watch threshold and consistent with its expectation that proppant would be down as guided.
Free cash flow remained negative at $8 million, but improved from negative $25 million in Q1; the preview identified FCF inflection as an open question rather than forecasting a specific outcome.
The fleet count remained in the low 20s, as in the preview’s Q1 baseline.
CapEx guidance of $155–180 million remained within the preview’s prior FY26 range of $155–185 million, notwithstanding management’s expectation of spending slightly above the midpoint.

surprises.description: APA’s full-year free-cash-flow outlook at current strip is about $2.3 billion, above the preview’s roughly $2.2 billion standing figure. Management also attributed roughly $950 million pretax to its gas trading portfolio, a contributor the preview did not quantify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “At current strip pricing, APA expects approximately $2.3 billion of total free cash flow in 2026, including roughly $950 million pretax from its gas trading portfolio.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 FCF guidance against the ~$2.2B standing figure”; the preview also identified FCF below ~$2.2B as a bear trigger.

surprises.description: APA now expects to reach its $3 billion net-debt target in 2027, earlier than its original three-to-four-year timeline. The preview flagged the target as a capital-allocation issue and included pushing it out as a bear scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repaid $752 million of bond debt in the first half of 2026” and “now expects to reach its $3 billion net debt target in 2027, ahead of the original 3-4 year timeline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited net debt of $4,121 million against a $3 billion target and listed “net debt target pushed out” in its bear scenario.

surprises.description: APA raised its year-end annualized cost-savings target to about $500 million, above the preview’s $450 million year-end goal. The increase is distinct from the additional reported total reductions that include interest savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APA raised its year-end annualized run-rate cost savings target to approximately $500 million, up from the prior $450 million goal.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Run-rate savings are $350M, with a $450M cumulative target by year-end 2026.”

surprises.description: APA raised full-year Permian oil production guidance from 120,000 to 123,000 barrels per day while planning to operate four rigs for the rest of the year and keeping its $1.3 billion capital budget unchanged. The preview highlighted curtailment restoration as a key question but did not give a Permian production forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year Permian oil production guidance to 123,000 barrels per day (up from 120,000) while cutting the rig count to 4 for the rest of the year and holding the $1.3 billion capital budget unchanged.”

surprises.description: APA cut full-year lease operating expense guidance by $25 million to $1.5 billion, with U.S. and North Sea savings offsetting diesel inflation. The preview did not flag this expense outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APA reduced full-year lease operating expense guidance to $1.5 billion, $25 million below prior guidance, driven by U.S. and North Sea savings offsetting diesel inflation.”

surprises.description: APA disclosed higher 2027 exploration spending, including about $100–120 million for two Alaska wells and a Uruguay well planned for late 2027. The Uruguay well is partly funded by new partner ENI; the preview did not discuss these exploration plans.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Exploration spend rises in 2027 (~$100-120 million for two Alaska wells) with a Uruguay well planned for late 2027 partly funded by new partner ENI.”

in_line: Adjusted EPS was $1.89 per diluted share, within the preview’s cited consensus estimates of $1.85, $1.88, and $1.90.

In Egypt, APA maintained its original BOE outlook and indicated minimal free-cash-flow impact, rather than reporting the further overall outlook cut the preview identified as a risk. The revised gross oil and gas figures are not directly comparable to the preview’s adjusted-production whisper.
GranMorgu remained on budget and on schedule for first oil in mid-2028, matching the timing the preview flagged.

surprises.description: The preview put Q2 revenue consensus at $194.3 million, with a base case of $192–198 million. MMI reported $203 million, beating consensus by $8.7 million and exceeding the base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose 18% year-over-year to $203 million in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $194.3M”; the base scenario was “$192–198M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected diluted EPS of $0.03 and positive GAAP profitability. MMI reported $0.10 per share, a larger profit than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income swung to $4 million ($0.10 per share) from a net loss of $11 million ($0.28 per share) a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) | +$0.03”; the preview also said “Consensus expects the first positive Q2 EPS of the cycle.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted private-client brokerage as the key recovery test and noted that multifamily individual-asset sales were down 7% year over year. MMI’s private-client brokerage nevertheless grew 14% to $106 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Private client brokerage grew 14% to $106 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Private-client brokerage revenue… This is the core of the recovery thesis”; the preview also said, “Multifamily individual asset sales fell 7% Y/Y.”

surprises.description: The preview cited middle-market brokerage revenue down 5.9% in Q1, while the Q2 call reported 13% growth and described recovery across price segments. That is a marked reversal from the prior-quarter weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Middle market grew 13% to $22 million,” reflecting “broad-based recovery across price segments for the first time since the market disruption began.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Middle-market ($10–20M) brokerage revenue down 5.9% Y/Y.”

surprises.description: The preview described extended institutional softness but gave no specific expectation for larger transactions. MMI reported 43% growth in deals above $20 million, its strongest growth since Q4 2024.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The larger transaction segment (deals above $20 million) grew 43% to $33 million, the strongest growth since Q4 2024 after an extended period of institutional softness.”

surprises.description: The preview’s base scenario assumed financing growth of about 25%. MMI reported 15% revenue growth, a slower result than that base case, although it was not below the preview’s specific 15% warning threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Financing revenue rose 15% to $30 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario assumed “financing slows to ~25%”; the preview said “Deceleration below +15% would suggest Q1 was a rate-window pull-forward.”

surprises.description: The preview expected SG&A to rise modestly in dollars. Instead, SG&A was virtually flat in dollars as revenue recovered, producing greater operating leverage than that expectation implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A held virtually flat in dollars but fell to 35% of revenue from 42% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management’s Q2 guidance in the preview was “SG&A up modestly in dollars.”

surprises.description: The preview discussed the existing roughly $90 million remaining buyback authorization and flagged buyback pace as a key issue. MMI repurchased $24 million of shares and added authorization to bring the remaining program back to about $90 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased ~913,000 shares for $24 million” and “the Board added authorization bringing the remaining buyback program to ~$90 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “$90M buyback authorization remaining” and flagged “H2 pipeline tone and buyback pace.”

surprises.description: The preview focused on the Q2 cost-of-services range, but the call added that the rate is expected to rise sequentially in Q3. That points to further margin pressure after Q2’s already higher cost ratio.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cost of services rose 50 basis points to 62.4% of revenue” and “is expected to increase sequentially in Q3.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was $12 million, at the low end of the preview’s estimated $12–15 million range.
Q2 cost of services was 62.4% of revenue, within management’s 62.0–63.5% Q2 guidance cited in the preview.
Financing revenue growth was 15%, matching the preview’s stated threshold for the deceleration concern rather than falling below it.

surprises.description: Black Hills reported adjusted Q2 EPS of $0.54, well above the preview’s $0.40–$0.41 consensus range. The roughly $0.13–$0.14 per-share gap was much larger than a routine beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted Q2 2026 EPS was $0.54” (GAAP $0.50 with $0.04 merger costs).
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS (Q2) … Consensus … $0.40 – $0.41.”

surprises.description: The data-center opportunity extends well beyond the 1.8 GW project highlighted in the preview: Black Hills said its pipeline exceeds 3 GW, with more than 2.5 GW in active negotiation beyond the 600 MW already included in its plan through 2030. Those negotiations are not contracted, so this is potential upside rather than committed growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A data center pipeline exceeding 3 gigawatts,” with “only 600 megawatts … currently included in its financial plan through 2030” and “over 2.5 gigawatts in active negotiation as additive upside.”

surprises.description: The 1.8 GW project had not reached definitive agreements by the preview’s June 30 target, but management now says negotiations are advanced and it is optimistic about finalizing agreements in Q3. Management also said Crusoe’s exit has not affected talks because it has negotiated directly with the hyperscale end user; this is more reassuring than the preview’s unresolved partner change, though the project remains unsigned.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In advanced negotiations on a 1.8 gigawatt data center project” and “remains optimistic about finalizing definitive agreements in Q3 2026”; Crusoe’s exit “has had no impact on negotiations” because management had been negotiating “directly with the hyperscale end user throughout.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management targeted June 30, 2026 for definitive agreements,” and “No announcement had surfaced”; the base case expected “data-center talks ongoing.”

surprises.description: The project’s generation reservation agreement now provides for up to $377 million of refundable customer advances, compared with the $201 million of refundable contributions the preview said were already in place. The larger potential funding commitment is constructive, although it is refundable and the agreement was extended only through August 31.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A generation reservation agreement was extended through August 31 and provides for up to $377 million of refundable customer advances funding long-lead generation equipment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$201M of refundable customer contributions is in place.”

surprises.description: Although the company left its EPS guidance range unchanged, management added that it expects to deliver in the upper half of its 4%–6% long-term growth target. That is a more confident outlook than a simple reaffirmation, though the preview had identified upper-half language as a possible bull outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reaffirmed full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $4.25 to $4.45” and “expects to deliver in the upper half of its 4% to 6% long-term growth target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether guidance would be “reaffirmed without qualification?” and listed “Reaffirmed, upper half” in its bull scenario.

surprises.description: Wyoming Electric’s July peak reached 439 MW, up 16% from the prior year’s peak. The preview did not flag this load growth, making the scale of the reported increase new information about demand on the system.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wyoming electric peaked at 439 megawatts in July, a 16% increase over last year’s peak,” with “20 consecutive years of rising peak loads.”

in_line: The $4.25–$4.45 full-year adjusted EPS guidance range was reaffirmed, as the preview’s base case expected.
The 99-MW Lang II generation project remains on schedule for Q4 2026, as the preview expected.
The NorthWestern merger remains pending its final Montana decision, within the preview’s expected second-half 2026 closing window.
Year-to-date ATM equity issuance was $50 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation that equity needs would remain in the $50–$70 million range.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.45, well above the preview’s $0.35 consensus and the $0.39 high end of Q3 guidance. It also grew 32%, slightly faster than adjusted EBITDA’s 30% growth, rather than showing the divergence the preview flagged as a concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP adjusted EPS was $0.45, up 32%”; adjusted EBITDA “increased 30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q3 adjusted EPS consensus of “$0.35” and guidance of “$0.30 – $0.39,” and flagged the “EBITDA versus EPS divergence.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA reached $22 million, exceeding the prior guidance ceiling of $20 million and the preview’s $19–20 million base case. The preview’s bull case began at $21 million, so the result was above base but within its stated bull scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 30% to $22 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q3 guidance was “$17.0M – $20.0M”; the preview’s base scenario was “$19–20M” and bull scenario “$21M+.”

surprises.description: The Q4 adjusted EPS guidance midpoint is $0.455, above the preview’s $0.43 consensus. The range is wide and its $0.41 low end is below consensus, but its high end exceeds the preview’s bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal Q4 guidance” includes non-GAAP adjusted EPS of “$0.41–0.50.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified Q4 adjusted EPS consensus of “$0.43,” with a bull scenario of “> $0.45” and a bear scenario of “< $0.40.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that Q4 earnings will face an effective tax rate approaching the low-to-mid 30s and sequentially lower retail GMV and revenue. The preview raised a higher tax rate as one possible explanation for Q3’s EBITDA/EPS gap, but did not anticipate these specific Q4 headwinds or lower retail activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 earnings are expected to be pressured by a higher effective tax rate approaching the low-to-mid 30s and sequentially lower GMV and revenue in the retail segment.”

surprises.description: Retail GMV growth accelerated to 19% and direct profit grew 30%, with records in both measures. The preview described the prior quarter’s 10% RSCG GMV growth and 29% direct-profit growth, but gave no Q3 expectation for this segment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The retail (RSCG) segment set records with GMV up 19% to $121.6 million and direct profit up 30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 RSCG GMV “grew 10% and direct profit grew 29%”; it provided no Q3 segment forecast.

surprises.description: The retail managed direct-to-consumer consignment business nearly doubled year over year, an additional growth driver the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: The managed direct-to-consumer consignment business “nearly doubled year-over-year.”

surprises.description: GovDeals reported unusually strong buyer-funnel and conversion metrics despite lower marketing spend. The preview focused on whether GMV growth would reach 10%, but did not anticipate these operating metrics.
surprises.fact_evidence: GovDeals had “buyer registrations up 23%, new bidders up 42%, and conversion rates up 35% despite lower marketing spend.”

surprises.description: CAG direct profit rose 13% and its take rate expanded 270 basis points on stronger pricing and mix, even as GMV slipped 1% due to project timing. This is a favorable pricing and mix outcome relative to the preview’s concern that rising consignment mix could compress take rates.
surprises.fact_evidence: CAG GMV “decline[d] 1% due to project timing,” while direct profit “grew 13% as its take rate expanded 270 basis points from stronger pricing and mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Rising consignment mix could compress reported revenue even as margins improve.”

surprises.description: Machinio’s system ARR grew 26%, with its marine vertical up 95%; the preview did not mention Machinio or set an expectation for these growth rates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Machinio’s total system ARR grew 26% year-over-year, with its marine vertical growing 95% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: The company still had the full $50 million repurchase authorization available, so the release offered no indication that the authorization had been used. This is consistent with the preview’s concern about no buyback signal rather than a new capital-return action.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended the quarter with “$50 million remaining in share repurchase authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “has not signaled a buyback” and that “silence on capital deployment would be a mild negative.”

in_line: Consolidated GMV was $453 million, within the preview’s $450–460 million base scenario and the company’s prior $425–465 million guidance range.
GAAP revenue of $129.6 million was within the preview’s $126–132 million base scenario; the preview cautioned that revenue consensus was unreliable.
GovDeals GMV grew 9%: just below the preview’s 10% upside marker, but above its stated below-7% thesis-risk level.

surprises.description: ATN reported adjusted EBITDA of $49.7 million, $1.2 million above the preview’s $48.5 million estimate, and a roughly 27% margin versus the preview’s 26.6% estimate. This was a modest beat rather than the larger $51 million-plus result in the preview’s bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew nearly 9% year-over-year to $49.7 million, with total adjusted EBITDA margin expanding roughly 170 basis points to 27%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … My Estimate $48.5M (26.6%)”; the preview also said “A print of $49M or more” would validate the trajectory.

surprises.description: Revenue came in above the preview’s $183.2 million consensus and $182.5 million estimate, at $184.5 million. The beat was modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue rose 2% year-over-year to $184.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus $183.2M … My Estimate $182.5M.”

surprises.description: The Board expanded the repurchase authorization to $30 million, while the preview viewed silence on buybacks as the most likely outcome. This was a clearer capital-return step than the preview’s base case of capital allocation being under review.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board expanded the share repurchase authorization to $30 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Silence on buybacks is the most likely disappointment”; the base case anticipated capital allocation “under review.”

surprises.description: Net leverage fell to 0.91x, below the preview’s expected post-sale range of roughly 1.0–1.5x. The preview expected meaningful deleveraging, but the reported ratio was better than that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage improved dramatically to 0.91x from 2.36x at year-end 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Post-close it should fall to roughly 1.0–1.5x from 2.30x at Q1.”

surprises.description: ATN disclosed an agreement to sell certain spectrum licenses for up to $41 million, with closing expected in 2027. The preview discussed tower-sale proceeds and deferred tower payments but did not anticipate this separate spectrum monetization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed an agreement to sell certain spectrum licenses for up to $41 million (closing expected in 2027).”

surprises.description: Management cited approximately $150 million of BEAD funding available within ATN’s Alaska and Southwest footprint later this year and into 2027. The preview noted BEAD as an upside option but said it would not have a significant 2026 impact and did not provide this funding amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately $150 million of BEAD government broadband funding is available within ATN's Alaska and Southwest footprint later this year and into 2027 to subsidize rural fiber expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said BEAD “is going to be more like the coming years” and “will not have a significant 2026 impact,” and described 2027 revenue quantification as “an upside option.”

in_line: ATN reaffirmed its FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance; the preview identified reiterating the $183–193 million range as the base case.
Net capital expenditures remained guided at $105–115 million, consistent with the preview’s stated range.

The large positive GAAP result was driven by the tower-sale gain, as the preview anticipated a sharply positive headline EPS from a one-time book gain and cautioned that it was not the best measure of operating performance.
The recurring EBITDA effect of the tower sale was consistent with the preview’s discussion of tower-related drag in the second half of 2026.

surprises.description: The preview estimated that applying the preferred proceeds to debt paydown would bring non-funding debt-to-equity to about 1.7x; management said it fell to 1.2x after the capital raise, a stronger deleveraging outcome than estimated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The non-funding debt-to-equity ratio dropped from a spiked 5.6x at quarter-end to 1.2x post-capital raise.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Applying the $1.65B to debt paydown would take the non-funding debt-to-equity ratio from 6.13x to roughly 1.7x.”

surprises.description: The preview said the warrant count and strikes were undisclosed and highlighted dilution as a key uncertainty. Management disclosed 330 million warrants, split between $2 and $6 strikes; the large count creates potential dilution, but the average strike is above the current stock price and management said that limits near-term dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “330 million total warrants, split evenly between $2 and $6 strike prices, with an average around $4—well above the current stock price—limiting near-term dilution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Warrant strike and share count. Also undisclosed. Together with the rights offering, this sets the true fully diluted dilution.” The preview’s bull case called for “warrants under 5% fully diluted,” while its bear case cited “heavy warrant coverage.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed litigation against Two Harbors and CrossCountry following the failed Two Harbors transaction, an additional legal overhang the preview did not identify; management declined to provide specifics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The failed Two Harbors transaction has led to litigation against Two Harbors and CrossCountry, though management declined to detail specifics.”

surprises.description: The preview anticipated that the platform’s operating business could be fine at roughly $40 billion of volume, but did not describe its capacity. Management said the platform can handle $250–$300 billion annually, highlighting substantial room to scale if rates fall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “UWM's origination platform can handle $250-$300 billion annually (vs. $40 billion in Q2), positioning it to benefit sharply if rates fall.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Margins holding above 125 bps on roughly $40B of volume would suggest the operating business is fine and the problem is capital structure.”

surprises.description: The preview focused on operating performance and the capital structure but did not flag the cost of running two servicing operations. Management said servicing costs are elevated this year because UWM is operating both in-house and Cenlar operations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Servicing costs are elevated this year from running both in-house and Cenlar operations.”

in_line: Management confirmed the preferred coupon at 10%, within the preview’s estimated 10–12% range; the preview also estimated an annual cost of $165–198 million, while the call cited about $165 million in new preferred coupon payments.
The dividend suspension matched the preview, which stated “Dividend: Suspended (previously $0.10 per quarter).”
The capital raise was broadly in line with the preview’s stated $2.05 billion total commitment and $1.65 billion funded preferred equity; the call described it as over $2 billion.
The call’s approximately $40 billion of Q2 origination volume was consistent with the preview’s roughly $40 billion volume reference.

Management’s account of a hedge loss tied to the anticipated Two Harbors transaction was consistent with the preview, which said management attributed most of the loss to a hedge-related event tied to that transaction. The call added that it was one-time and would not recur.

surprises.description: TPL reported about $246 million in revenue, roughly 1.4% below the preview’s $249.5 million consensus estimate. That is a small shortfall despite record revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record quarterly total revenue of ~$246 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Consensus … $249.5M.”

surprises.description: Oil and gas royalty production rose 7% sequentially to a record, stronger than the preview’s broad expectation of flat-to-up volumes and its description of only a marginal uptick in operator activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oil and gas royalty production hit a record ~39,700 boe/d, up 7% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether the well inventory builds”; management had flagged only a “marginal uptick in recent operator activity.” The base scenario expected “flat-to-up volumes.”

surprises.description: Produced-water royalty volumes reached a record and rose 6% sequentially, a stronger result than the preview’s general flat-to-up volume expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Produced water royalty volumes reached a record 4.9 million barrels per day, up 6% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “flat-to-up volumes”; the bull scenario referred to “record water volumes.”

surprises.description: Water sales volumes fell 19% sequentially, contrary to the preview’s base case of flat-to-up volumes. The preview did identify a dip as a bear-case possibility, but the reported decline was substantial.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Water sales volumes declined 19% sequentially to 663,000 barrels per day due to weak in-basin gas prices shifting development away from the Delaware Basin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “flat-to-up volumes”; the bear scenario said “water volumes dip.”

surprises.description: TPL said it was in advanced talks on 25 gigawatts of projects and expected at least one major definitive agreement in the near term. The preview hoped for a third deal, but its base case assumed no new deal announcement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In advanced conversations with multiple hyperscalers, AI labs, and power generators on 25 gigawatts of projects” and “expects to announce at least one major definitive agreement in the near term.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Investors are looking for … a third deal”; the base scenario assumed “no new deal.”

surprises.description: TPL disclosed a roughly $100 million acquisition of more than 10,000 acres in Shackelford and Jones County, extending its data-center and power strategy beyond the Permian Basin. The preview did not anticipate this acquisition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company acquired over 10,000 acres in Shackelford and Jones County for ~$100 million, expanding its data center and power strategy beyond the Permian Basin.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $216 million, up 19% sequentially, with an 88% margin. The preview had no EBITDA consensus, so this strong quarterly result was not captured in its headline estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $216 million (up 19% sequentially, 30% YoY) with an 88% margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … Not found.”

surprises.description: Management said it was prioritizing building cash for acquisitions and other investments over share buybacks, a capital-allocation choice the preview had not flagged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is prioritizing cash build for M&A, land, power, and desal investments over share buybacks.”

surprises.description: TPL completed construction and began commissioning its Orla Phase 2b produced-water desalination facility, targeting 10,000 barrels per day. This execution milestone was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Completed construction and began commissioning its Orla Phase 2b produced water desalination facility, targeting a 10,000 barrel/day capacity.”

in_line: The Chevron Project Kilby connection was already flagged in the preview: it described the June agreement as a Chevron Project Kilby development in Reeves County.

surprises.description: Revenue was expected to be about $211.4 million, but USPH reported $214 million, roughly 1.2% above consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 total revenue rose 8.5% to $214 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Net revenue: $211.4M.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS consensus was $0.85, but adjusted operating results per share fell to $0.75, a meaningful miss rather than the expected year-over-year increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted operating results per share fell to $0.75 from $0.81.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adjusted EPS: $0.85; implied Y/Y +4.9%.

surprises.description: The preview estimated Q2 adjusted EBITDA at about $28.0–28.5 million, but USPH reported $27.0 million, below even the preview's bear-case upper bound and its stated level that would make the full-year guide hard to hold.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA was essentially flat year-over-year at $27.0 million versus $26.9 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adj. EBITDA: ~$28.0–28.5M (derived, not published consensus); “A quarter at or below $27M would make the guide very hard to hold.”

surprises.description: The preview expected only minimal hospital-alliance contribution in Q2, but affiliations contributed $5.6 million to PT revenue, with 31 clinics integrated during the quarter. Management also quantified a $1.5–2 million Q4 EBITDA impact as the remaining clinics integrate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Hospital affiliations contributed $5.6 million to Q2 PT revenue, with 31 clinics integrated in Q2 and the remaining 39 expected to integrate in Q3, projecting a $1.5–2 million EBITDA impact in Q4.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base case: “alliances minimal in Q2”; the alliances “reach full quarterly run-rate only in Q4.”

surprises.description: Visits per clinic were expected to face a hard comparison against the 32.7 record, but average daily visits reached 33.5, a new all-time high and above the preview's bull-case threshold of 33.0.
surprises.fact_evidence: Average daily visits per clinic hit an all-time high of 33.5, up from 32.7 a year ago.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Q2 FY2025 comp is a record 32.7”; bull case: “Visits ≥33.0/day.”

surprises.description: The preview identified $107.50 or higher as the rate level that would confirm pricing progress; USPH reported a record $107.59 per visit, slightly clearing that marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: Physical therapy revenue per visit reached a record $107.59, up $2.26 year-over-year, with Medicare, commercial and workers' comp all contributing.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for $107.50 or higher as confirmation that the Medicare catch-up and commercial pricing are real.”

surprises.description: The preview anticipated partial cost normalization, but USPH disclosed an approximately $3.2 million year-over-year self-insured healthcare-cost headwind, with roughly 80% concentrated in Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: Higher-than-average self-insured healthcare costs created an approximately $3.2 million year-over-year headwind, roughly 80% of which hit in Q2 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base case: “partial cost normalization”; bear case: “costs fail to normalize.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag pre-transition staffing costs, but USPH said it hired about 50 clinicians ahead of the NYU Langone transition, weighing on Q2 margins before reimbursement begins.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company front-loaded approximately 50 clinician hires, estimated at over $100,000 each, ahead of the NYU Langone hospital transition, pressuring Q2 margins before reimbursement kicks in.

surprises.description: The preview gave an adjusted EPS consensus but no GAAP EPS estimate; USPH reported GAAP EPS of $0.25, down sharply from $0.58, with the decline partly attributed to an earn-out fair-value loss and dilutive noncontrolling-interest effects.
surprises.fact_evidence: GAAP earnings per share dropped to $0.25 from $0.58, driven partly by a $992,000 loss on change in fair value of contingent earn-outs and dilutive effects from improving noncontrolling interest partnerships.

in_line: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed at $102–106 million, matching the preview's base case.

surprises.description: Q2 diluted EPS was $4.73, well below the preview’s $5.63–$5.71 consensus range. The shortfall was about 16–17% versus the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Second-quarter net earnings of $727 million or $4.73 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | Q2 FY2026E | $5.63–5.71.”

surprises.description: CF pushed the Yazoo City restart from late 2026 to the first half of 2027, later than the preview’s watched restart timing implied. The delay was attributed to extended procurement of electrical equipment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Yazoo City complex is now expected to resume operations in the first half of 2027 (delayed from late 2026 due to extended electrical equipment procurement).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “the Yazoo City restart timing” as a key swing item and listed the “Yazoo City restart date” as a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: CF raised its baseline mid-cycle EBITDA and free-cash-flow expectations, and said strategic initiatives could lift mid-cycle EBITDA further by 2030. The preview did not flag a higher long-term earnings outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its baseline mid-cycle EBITDA expectation to approximately $2.9 billion and free cash flow to $1.7 billion, with strategic initiatives expected to lift mid-cycle EBITDA to approximately $3.3 billion by 2030.”

surprises.description: CF increased its mid-cycle NOLA urea price assumption by $30 per short ton, from $355 to $385. The preview focused on near-term realized prices and did not anticipate a higher long-term price assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The mid-cycle NOLA urea price assumption increased from $355 to $385 per short ton,” with about $10 attributed to structural geopolitical cost changes and the remainder to higher global capital costs.

surprises.description: CF disclosed a $75 million increase in Q2 fixed costs, including higher purchased-ammonia costs and Yazoo City-related fixed-cost absorption. The preview flagged maintenance costs as a swing item but did not anticipate this quantified cost increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Second-quarter fixed costs rose about $75 million, with roughly $60 million split between higher purchased ammonia costs and Yazoo City-related fixed cost absorption.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “maintenance cost” was among the Yazoo City swing items.

surprises.description: The Yazoo City project will produce ammonium nitrate solution, ammonia, and DEF rather than ammonium nitrate. The preview discussed the outage and restart but did not anticipate this change in the complex’s planned product mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “It will be reconfigured to produce ammonium nitrate solution, ammonia and DEF rather than ammonium nitrate.”

surprises.description: CF reported that low-carbon ammonia already accounted for about 10% of first-half ammonia sales and earned a premium above $20 per ton, a commercial result the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Low carbon ammonia comprised approximately 10% of first-half ammonia sales volumes and earned an average premium of more than $20 per ton.”

surprises.description: CF increased its quarterly dividend by 20% to $0.60 per share. The preview focused on buyback execution and did not anticipate a dividend increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In July, the Board increased the quarterly dividend by 20% to $0.60 per share.”

surprises.description: CF reported nearly $1.3 billion of shareholder returns over the trailing 12 months, including $958 million of repurchases, and said roughly $500 million had been spent under its $2 billion buyback program. This was a substantial capital-return update, though the figures do not specify Q2 repurchases and therefore cannot be directly compared with the preview’s Q2 buyback estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over the trailing 12 months, CF returned nearly $1.3 billion to shareholders, including $958 million to repurchase 10.6 million shares and $314 million in dividends, with roughly $500 million spent of a $2 billion buyback program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Q1 repurchases were small” and expected “buyback ~$100–200M” in its base scenario; it said a quarter below $100 million could be a weak signal.

surprises.description: CF said about half of Blue Point’s capital expenditure was fixed, providing more cost certainty than the preview’s general focus on capex discipline. The preview did not give an expectation for how much of the project’s CapEx would be fixed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Blue Point construction is expected to begin in August with approximately 50% of CapEx fixed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “capex discipline” against the gross JV figure, but did not specify a fixed-cost share.

surprises.description: Chord generated $414 million of adjusted free cash flow in Q2, which the call said exceeded expectations. The preview provided a full-year FCF anchor but no Q2 FCF estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Chord Energy generated adjusted free cash flow of $414 million in Q2 2026, exceeding expectations.”

surprises.description: Chord plans to return at least 75% of adjusted FCF in Q3 and Q4, above the preview’s description of a framework calling for at least 50% when leverage is below 1.0x. This is a higher near-term return commitment than the preview suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company will increase targeted shareholder returns to at least 75% of adjusted free cash flow starting in Q3 2026 and continuing through Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management's framework returns at least 50% of adj. FCF when leverage is below 1.0x.”

surprises.description: Q2 Bakken crude traded at a premium to WTI, stronger than the preview’s expectation of a differential around $1 below WTI or better. Management expects the premium to fade, with differentials moving to just below WTI over the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bakken crude traded at premiums to WTI during Q2 2026”; the company now guides differentials “to just below WTI as the premium is expected to fade over the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A result of −$1.00 or better would be a meaningful beat driver.”

surprises.description: Chord had hedged about 18% of its 2027 oil volumes, above the 14% cited in the preview. That provides more price protection than the preview’s stated position.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has hedged approximately 38% of its second-half 2026 oil volumes and about 18% of 2027 volumes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Hedges: … ~14% of oil for 2027.”

surprises.description: Q2 capital spending finished modestly below the guidance midpoint, a favorable spending outcome versus the preview’s $425 million midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted capital spending finished modestly below the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CapEx: $410–440MM” with a “Midpoint” of “$425MM.”

surprises.description: After dropping its second frac crew in July, Chord expects a meaningful Q3 capital-spending reduction and another decline in Q4, while faster cycle times pulled volumes into the first half. The preview did not describe this quarterly spending step-down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company dropped its second frac crew in July, driving a meaningful capital spending reduction in Q3 followed by another decline in Q4, though faster cycle times pulled volumes forward into the first half.”

surprises.description: Chord reported executing the basin’s first trimulfrac and said it could make up 20%–50% of next year’s development program to reduce completion costs. The preview did not flag this technique or its potential role in the program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Chord successfully executed the basin's first trimulfrac, which could represent 20% to 50% of next year's development program to reduce completion costs.”

in_line: Oil production came in at the high end of the Q2 guidance range of 162.5–165.5 MBopd; the preview treated that range as the company’s guidance and identified 166 MBopd or more as a potential beat scenario.
Full-year oil guidance of 161,000 bpd was consistent with the preview’s 160,000–162,000 bpd range.
Second-half 2026 oil hedges were about 38%, matching the preview’s cited balance-of-2026 position of approximately 38%.
The four-mile-well program’s early performance and cycle times were reported as in line with expectations.
Full-year LOE guidance of $10.30/BOE was within the preview’s stated $9.55–$10.35/BOE range, though near the top of it.

surprises.description: FNF reported a 17.8% adjusted pretax title margin, above the preview’s 16.0–16.5% base case, alongside adjusted pretax title earnings of $448 million. The margin also exceeded the preview’s 17.0%+ bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted pretax title earnings of $448 million in Q2 2026” with an “adjusted pretax title margin of 17.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base case is 16.0–16.5%”; the bull scenario expected a title margin of “17.0%+.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $1.39, above both the preview’s $1.26 headline consensus and its $1.32 alternative-provider estimate. The beat was about 10% versus the headline estimate and 5% versus the higher estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net earnings were $370 million or $1.39 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $1.26” and “Adjusted EPS (alt. provider) $1.32.”

surprises.description: Commercial title revenue appears to have exceeded the preview’s Q2 range: first-half direct commercial revenue was $778 million, and subtracting the preview’s Q1 figure of $338 million implies roughly $440 million in Q2, versus the expected $380–400 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Direct commercial revenue reached $778 million in the first six months,” compared with $626 million in the first half of 2025.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The full preview looks for $380–400M against $333M last year”; it also reports Q1 direct commercial revenue of $338M.

surprises.description: F&G contributed $65 million to adjusted net earnings in Q2, down from $89 million a year earlier, despite AUM growth. That is a meaningful shortfall against the prior-year contribution the preview highlighted as the run-rate to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “F&G’s adjusted net earnings contribution to the segment declined to $65 million from $89 million in Q2 2025”; its AUM “grew 8% year-over-year to $74.7 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'25 contributed $89M. Watch alternatives returns against the assumed run-rate, the source of past F&G shortfalls.”

surprises.description: Despite the stronger-than-expected Q2 title margin, management expects modest margin compression in the second half as recruiting and tuck-in acquisition costs precede revenue growth. The preview noted Q2 seasonality but did not flag this specific expense-led outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management guided to “modest compression in adjusted pretax title margin in the second half of 2026 relative to Q2,” driven by “front-loaded expenses from record recruiting and tuck-in acquisitions,” including over 200 people added in July.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q2 is seasonally the strongest quarter” and cited a 15–20% annual title margin range, but did not forecast second-half compression from these expenses.

surprises.description: F&G has formally begun exploring strategic alternatives for Peak Altitude, a distribution unit in which it has invested nearly $700 million. The preview flagged F&G stake strategy generally but did not anticipate a process involving this specific business; management favors a 51% partner structure and expects proceeds to support core growth rather than M&A.
surprises.fact_evidence: “F&G has launched a formal process to explore strategic alternatives for its Peak Altitude distribution unit” with “nearly $700 million invested” and “$80 million of 2025 EBITDA”; management favors a 51% partner structure and expects proceeds to go toward growing the core business over M&A.

in_line: Refinance orders weakened as the preview anticipated: it flagged the fade from about 2,000 daily orders in Q1 to about 1,600 in April and noted mortgage rates had risen. The call reported refinance orders down 22% from Q1.

surprises.description: The preview warned that New Afton’s production ramp was an execution risk but gave no expected ramp date. Coeur said the move to 16,000 tonnes per day had slipped about three months, from end-Q2 to early Q4, a delay that pushes the ramp later than investors might have expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New Afton's ramp to 16,000 tonnes per day was pushed roughly three months to early Q4 (from end of Q2).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The main risk is whether the FY2026 production guidance holds.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged purchase-accounting costs as an issue and cited about $689 per gold ounce of PPA step-up in Q1. Coeur reported a larger Q2 inventory uplift of $834 per ounce in consolidated CAS, including $2,036 per ounce at Rainy River, with another $38 million of charge expected in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $140 million (~$0.10 per share) noncash charge from acquisition accounting on Rainy River stockpile inventory hit Q2 EBITDA, net income and CAS, with a remaining $38 million expected in Q3”; the uplift “inflated consolidated Q2 CAS by $834 per ounce out of $2,442 total, and Rainy River's CAS by $2,036 out of $3,788 per ounce.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted CAS per ounce, ex-PPA. Investors need a clean full-period unit cost for Rainy River and New Afton. Watch whether management discloses an ex-PPA bridge and whether the roughly $689/oz PPA drag persists.”

surprises.description: The preview said the H2 production ramp leaned on Rochester and called for throughput and recovery updates, but did not anticipate record crushing volumes or all three crushing stages running at near-full throughput. The record quarter and completed Phase 2a leach-pad expansion support a stronger second-half silver contribution than the preview had specifically outlined.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rochester achieved a record 6.8 million metric tons crushed (up 15% quarter-over-quarter) with 97% running through all three crushing stages,” and the Phase 2a leach pad expansion was completed.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The H2 ramp leans on Rochester, so throughput and recovery commentary matter.”

surprises.description: The preview provided no Q2 free-cash-flow estimate or expectation for the cash balance. Coeur reported record quarterly free cash flow of $388 million and ended June with $1.1 billion in cash and more than $2 billion of liquidity, much stronger cash-generation and liquidity figures than the preview had laid out.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record quarterly free cash flow reached $388 million,” and “ending cash balance surpassed $1 billion for the first time ($1.1 billion at June 30), doubling from year-end 2025, with total liquidity over $2 billion.”

surprises.description: The preview did not set expectations for full-year EBITDA or free cash flow. Coeur introduced guidance for about $2.3 billion of EBITDA and $1.5 billion of free cash flow, based on $4,000 gold, $60 silver and $6 copper, while noting that production would be heavily weighted to the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance projects approximately $2.3 billion EBITDA and $1.5 billion free cash flow based on assumed prices of $4,000/oz gold, $60/oz silver, and $6/lb copper, with production heavily second-half weighted.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag a rapid Rainy River underground ramp as an expected catalyst. Coeur said underground mining rates had risen more than 40% from Q2 to July and targeted 5,000 tonnes per day by year-end, with underground grades roughly three times open-pit grades.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rainy River underground mining rates jumped over 40% from 2,300 tpd in Q2 to ~3,300 tpd in July, targeting 5,000 tpd by year-end, with underground grades roughly 3x higher than open pit grades.”

in_line: The preview expected a sharp sequential revenue step-up from the first full quarter consolidating New Afton and Rainy River; Coeur said those Canadian assets drove much of the quarter-over-quarter increase. The facts provided do not give an exact Q2 revenue figure, so they do not establish whether revenue met the preview’s consensus range.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $1.603 billion, well above the preview’s estimated $1.42–$1.47 billion range—about 9% above even the top of that estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA reached a record $1.603 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$1.42–1.47B (derived)”

surprises.description: Record LPG export loadings substantially exceeded the preview’s 435.1 MBbl/d consensus; 14.8 million barrels per month is roughly 0.48–0.49 million barrels per day, above the preview’s 440 MBbl/d marker for a genuine record.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LPG export loadings averaging a record 14.8 million barrels per month.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “LPG export volumes 435.1 MBbl/d”; “A genuine record implies above 440 MBbl/d.”

surprises.description: Permian volumes rose by 450 MMcf/d quarter over quarter, substantially more than the preview’s indication that volumes were running about 250 MMcf/d above Q1, despite ongoing shut-ins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Permian volumes hit 7.2 Bcf/d, up 7% sequentially and 14% year-over-year, adding 450 MMcf/d quarter-over-quarter despite ongoing shut-ins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Volumes were running ~250 MMcf/d above the Q1 average of 6,730 MMcf/d despite 200–400 MMcf/d of temporary shut-ins.”

surprises.description: Marketing businesses outperformed expectations by approximately $250 million in the first half, much of it in Q2. The preview anticipated a Q2 marketing tailwind but did not indicate an outperformance of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marketing businesses outperformed expectations by approximately $250 million in the first half, much of it in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “This is a real Q2 tailwind but is low-multiple, non-recurring EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Fractionation reached 1.2 million bpd, modestly above the preview’s 1,166.1 MBbl/d consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fractionation of 1.2 million bpd.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NGL fractionation | 1,166.1 MBbl/d.”

surprises.description: The company repurchased roughly $80 million of stock, up from the $55 million buyback in Q1, delivering the step-up in repurchases the preview identified as a possible signal of confidence.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased roughly $80 million of stock at an average price of $259.93.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 buyback $55M”; “A step-up in repurchases would signal confidence.”

in_line: The full-year EBITDA guidance range remained $5.7–$5.9 billion, with management expecting results toward the top end; the preview’s base case anticipated a reaffirmation or move toward the upper half.
Net growth capital of approximately $4.5 billion and net maintenance capital of $250 million remained consistent with the preview’s FY2026 estimates.
Management’s assumption of minimal marketing gains in the second half is consistent with the preview’s warning that the Q2 marketing tailwind was low-multiple and non-recurring.

surprises.description: The preview said LBRD had no standalone revenue and that the earnings print carried little new information. The call instead reported $261 million of Q2 revenue and $96 million of adjusted OIBDA, with OIBDA down 11% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $261 million (flat year-over-year) while adjusted OIBDA declined 11% year-over-year to $96 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “LBRD has no standalone revenue.” The preview also said, “The earnings print carries little new information.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag a dividend, but Liberty Capital announced quarterly payments of about $15 million starting in December 2025. Management expects the annual $60 million payout to use about half of next year's free cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Liberty Capital announced a new capital allocation policy initiating a quarterly dividend of approximately $15 million ($60 million annually) beginning in December 2025, which is expected to represent about half of next year's free cash flow.”

surprises.description: The preview gave no operating cash-flow expectation; the call reported trailing 12-month free cash flow of only $59 million, down year over year because of higher capital expenditures, lower OIBDA, and working-capital swings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month free cash flow was $59 million, a decline year-over-year driven by higher capital expenditures, lower OIBDA, and working capital swings.”

surprises.description: The preview offered no capital-spending outlook. Management now expects 2026 to be the peak spending year at approximately $290 million, followed by meaningful declines in 2027 and 2028 to historical capital intensity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects 2026 to be the peak year for capital spending at approximately $290 million, with meaningful declines forecast for 2027 and 2028 returning to historical capital intensity.”

surprises.description: The preview centered on the Charter/Cox merger and did not discuss Quintillion. The call described a pending acquisition expected to close in 2025, contribute $50–$55 million of adjusted OIBDA including synergies in 2026, and be free-cash-flow accretive in its first year after closing; it also projected about $20 million of run-rate synergies over 24 months.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pending Quintillion acquisition is expected to close in 2025, contribute $50-$55 million of adjusted OIBDA including synergies in 2026, and be accretive to free cash flow in the first year after closing.” “The Quintillion deal is projected to deliver approximately $20 million in run-rate synergies over 24 months, with roughly half achieved in the first 12 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The deal terms are the operative anchor.” The preview also said, “No Cox close, no LBRD close.”

surprises.description: The preview said GCI was in discontinued operations and did not discuss consumer operating metrics. The call reported 2,100 wireless-line additions and that 42% of broadband customers took wireless service, with 63% of postpaid lines sold in converged relationships.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consumer wireless lines grew by 2,100 during the quarter, with 42% of broadband customers now taking wireless service and 63% of postpaid wireless lines sold as part of converged relationships.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GCI sits in discontinued operations after its July 2025 distribution. LBRD has no standalone revenue.”

surprises.description: The preview did not discuss broadband subscriber trends. The call reported an organic loss of 500 broadband subscribers, partly offset by 5,400 customers added through a small fixed-wireless-provider acquisition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consumer broadband subscribers declined organically by 500, but a small fixed wireless provider acquisition added 5,400 customers to the base.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag business margins or distribution costs. The call reported business gross margin of 75.5% after distribution costs rose by $9 million, including about $3 million tied to restored Quintillion Network service.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Business gross margin fell to 75.5% due to a $9 million increase in distribution costs, of which about $3 million related to restored service on the Quintillion Network.”

surprises.description: The preview focused on a current $864 million margin loan and asked whether Charter repurchases would continue funding debt service. The call instead reported 2.1x consolidated net leverage, 2.8x GCI net leverage, a long-term operating-level target of about 3x, and approximately $129 million of senior-note repurchases through July 31.
surprises.fact_evidence: “At quarter end, Liberty Capital's consolidated net leverage was 2.1x and GCI's net leverage was 2.8x, with the company targeting a long-term operating-level leverage ratio of approximately 3x and having repurchased about $129 million of senior notes through July 31.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Margin Loan Facility. The $864M is current. Confirm that Charter repurchases from LBRD continue to fund debt service through close.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EPS was $9.27, about 12% above the preview’s $8.30 consensus estimate. The result was also a record, rather than merely another beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 sales rose 10% (8% organic) with adjusted EPS up 21% to a record $9.27.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $8.30 (Zacks); $8.27 (broad street).”

surprises.description: Q4 sales growth of 10% was stronger than the preview’s 6.9% revenue-growth expectation. Using the preview’s $5.24B prior-year revenue, the reported growth implies roughly $5.76B, above the $5.61B consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 sales rose 10% (8% organic).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $5.61B (+6.9% y/y); $5.57B (alternate).”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted segment margin reached 28.0%, above the preview’s expected range of about 27.3–27.5%. It was also the first time the company’s margin exceeded 28%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted segment operating margin reached a record 28.0%, the first time above 28%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. segment operating margin: ~27.3–27.5%.”

surprises.description: FY27 adjusted EPS guidance of $34.75 at the midpoint is above the preview’s $34.03 consensus. The guide excludes pending acquisitions, as the preview’s base case expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 guidance calls for … adjusted EPS of $34.75 at midpoint, an 8% increase, excluding any impact from pending acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 adjusted EPS: $34.03 (+8.9%); a $32.50 figure also circulates.”

surprises.description: FY27 guidance calls for 7% organic sales growth, above the preview’s stated 4%-or-more organic-growth assumption as a constructive threshold. The preview did not give a specific FY27 sales consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 guidance calls for ~$23 billion in sales (7% organic growth at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch the organic growth assumption (4% or more is constructive).”

surprises.description: Parker said it is guiding positive organic growth across every market vertical for the first time. That is stronger breadth than the preview’s concern that industrial growth might stall and its call to look for North America industrial orders to sustain high-single- or double-digit growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “For the first time ever, Parker is guiding positive organic sales growth across all market verticals.”
