surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed prior FY26 total revenue guidance of “$1.0595–1.0705B” and flagged “tariff pass-through fees drop about $5M per quarter in H2” and rising memory costs as hardware risks.

surprises.description: Q3 SaaS and license guidance implies growth slowing to about 8.3%, below Q2’s 11.1% growth and a caution against reading the raised full-year outlook as uniformly strong near-term growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 SaaS/license guidance implies decelerating growth of about 8.3% at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a full-year SaaS and license raise “toward ~$753–755M, would signal confidence in H2.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 115 basis points year over year in Q2, a stronger result than the preview’s concern that faster EnergyHub growth could dilute blended margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin of 20.8%, up about 115 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that EnergyHub’s lower gross margin meant “faster growth there dilutes blended margin” and said to watch whether the “+30bps 2026 adj. EBITDA margin bridge holds.”

surprises.description: Commercial, EnergyHub, and international initiatives together accounted for about 35% of revenue, grew more than 30%, and contributed roughly 900 basis points to Q2 growth. The preview singled out EnergyHub as a metric to watch but did not anticipate this combined scale or growth contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Combined growth initiatives (commercial, EnergyHub, and international) now represent about 35% of revenue and grew over 30% year-over-year, contributing roughly 900 basis points to Q2 growth.”

surprises.description: The newly launched Fire Communicator already had nearly 1,000 units deployed and targets a 4–5 million-panel market, with roughly twice the ARPU of a typical residential account. Its slightly lower hardware margins temper the positive revenue opportunity; the preview did not discuss the product.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The newly launched Fire Communicator targets an addressable market of 4-5 million fire panels, carries roughly 2x the ARPU of a typical residential account at slightly lower hardware margins, and already has nearly 1,000 units deployed.”

surprises.description: Q2 repurchases rose to $25 million from the $20 million reported for Q1, indicating a somewhat faster buyback pace than the preview’s cited recent pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased 570,000 shares for $25 million in Q2 under its $150 million authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “$20M (428K shares) in Q1” had been deployed and listed an “accelerated pace” as a confidence signal to watch.

in_line: Q2 SaaS and license revenue of $188.8 million beat the guidance midpoint by about $3.2 million, consistent with the preview’s base case of a typical $3–5 million beat.
Full-year SaaS and license guidance was raised to $754–754.4 million, within the preview’s anticipated range of $753–755 million.
Revenue retention remained in the 95% range, in line with the preview’s expectation of at least 95%.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $255–290 million is below the preview’s roughly $290–320 million expectation: the midpoint is $272.5 million, and even the high end only reaches the preview’s low end. Management also expects $20–25 million less 100G revenue because customers cannot source 100G switches amid a memory shortage expected to last into late 2026 or early 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $255-290 million”; management expects “a Q3 decline of $20-25 million in 100G revenue” due to customers' inability to source 100G switches, with a memory shortage expected to persist until late 2026 or early 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Hitting the $1.1B FY target requires Q3 revenue of roughly $290M – $320M”; “A Q3 guide below about $280M puts the FY math at risk.”

surprises.description: AOI raised $538.8 million net through its new at-the-market equity offering, a substantial dilution event against a preview that warned equity issuance would likely be poorly received. The call also reported $565.5 million of capital investments, including $280 million in equipment prepayments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AOI made $565.5 million in Q2 capital investments (including $280 million in equipment prepayments)”; it “raised $538.8 million net under its new at-the-market equity offering.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any equity or convertible issuance would likely be poorly received”; “dilution is the main risk.”

surprises.description: The full-year revenue outlook was described as “around” $1.1 billion rather than the prior guidance of above $1.1 billion, a modestly softer formulation. The preview had explicitly flagged the return of “approximately” around $1.1 billion as a bearish signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue of around $1.1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance: revenue above $1.1B”; “Bear signals: the word ‘approximately’ returns around $1.1B.”

surprises.description: Management put Q4 non-GAAP gross margin at roughly 32–33%, below the preview’s estimate that the FY operating-income target would require about 37% gross margin in the second half. That leaves a less ambitious margin path than the preview’s implied bridge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was 29.8% (within guidance),” with management “expecting Q4 to reach roughly 32-33% as 1.6T mix increases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The FY operating income target implies a 2H gross margin near 37%”; “The company needs roughly a 700 bp inflection” in the second half.

surprises.description: AOI returned to non-GAAP profitability at $0.06 per diluted share, above both the preview’s $0.02–$0.03 consensus and the $0.03 upper end of guidance. The beat was aided by foreign tax benefits and government subsidies, which the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income of $5.5 million or $0.06 per diluted share, beating guidance of a $0.03 loss to $0.03 earnings, aided by foreign tax benefits and government subsidies.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS” guidance of “$(0.03) – $0.03”; consensus “$0.02 – $0.03.”

surprises.description: The 800G ramp was already substantial in Q2 and management forecast roughly fivefold sequential growth in Q3, beyond the preview’s expectation that 800G would become the largest data-center line in Q2. The preview did not specify an expected Q3 growth rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “800G revenue reached $12.8 million (11.9% of data center revenue), up more than tenfold year-over-year and more than doubling sequentially, with management guiding for roughly 5x sequential growth in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management expects 800G to become the largest data center line in Q2.”

surprises.description: Monthly manufacturing capacity was approaching 200,000 units, ahead of the preview’s 150,000-unit Q2 target. This indicates a faster capacity ramp than the preview’s stated near-term target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Monthly manufacturing capacity is approaching 200,000 units (up from ~100,000 at end of Q1).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capacity exited Q1 at about 100k units per month, with a Q2 target of 150k.”

surprises.description: AOI reported that Mediacom selected it as the primary vendor for DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades, a customer win the preview did not identify. The call also forecast Q3 CATV revenue of $100–110 million, with no Q3 CATV estimate in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CATV revenue hit a record $80.6 million (42% of total revenue)”; “Q3 guidance of $100-110 million”; “Mediacom selected AOI as primary vendor for DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $191.9 million was within the preview’s consensus range of $190.5–194.3 million and close to the $191.1 million Zacks estimate.
Q2 non-GAAP gross margin of 29.8% was within the 29–30% guidance range and close to the preview’s roughly 29.5% consensus.
Q2 CATV revenue of $80.6 million was only slightly above the $75–80 million guidance range.

The statement that full-year revenue is capped by capacity and supply chain rather than demand was consistent with the preview’s expectation of production constraints and estimated demand above the $1.1 billion target.

surprises.description: The preview said CSL arbitration was not priced in, but Arcturus reported that the collaboration had been terminated, returning global rights to CoStave and the broader infectious-disease portfolio. The company also receives a one-time $12 million payment, is released from roughly $16 million in liabilities, and will split the Japan CoStave profit share with Meiji two ways rather than three.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The CSL Seqirus collaboration was terminated,” returning global rights to CoStave and the broader infectious disease portfolio, “plus a one-time $12 million cash payment and release from roughly $16 million in liabilities.” In Japan, “the CoStave profit share will now be split two ways with Meiji instead of three ways.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ARCT-810 EoP2 scheduling and CSL arbitration. Neither is priced in.”

surprises.description: The preview focused on ARCT-032 enrollment completion and a dated data window, with data guided to H1 2027. Management instead identified a Q4 2026 go/no-go decision on advancing the candidate to Phase 3 as the next catalyst, rather than data disclosure or enrollment completion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pivotal go/no-go decision to advance the CF candidate ARCT-032 into Phase 3 is expected in Q4 2026.” Management “reframed CF guidance to focus on the Q4 2026 Phase 3 decision rather than a data disclosure or enrollment completion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ARCT-032 12-week Phase 2 enrollment and data timing. Enrollment ‘on track’ with a dated data window is what buyers want. Data is guided to H1 2027.”

surprises.description: The preview emphasized ARCT-032 enrollment status but did not anticipate adding international sites. The Phase 2 study was expanded to Israel and Turkey, where management said a higher share of CF patients carry eligible null mutations, boosting recruitment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The CF Phase 2 study was expanded to Israel and Turkey, where 30%-40% of CF patients carry null mutations eligible for enrollment versus up to 10% ineligible-for-modulator patients in the US, boosting recruitment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Enrollment ‘on track’ with a dated data window is what buyers want.”

surprises.description: The preview did not discuss ARCT-032 dosing experience or steroid-free, at-home administration. The call reported that more than 50 participants had been dosed at up to 15 mg daily for 28 days under those conditions, with no serious safety issues requiring disclosure in the ongoing 12-week study.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ARCT-032 has now been dosed in over 50 participants at up to 15 mg daily for 28 days without steroid pretreatment and with at-home self-administration,” and management stated “no serious safety issues have required disclosure in the ongoing 12-week study.”

surprises.description: The preview expected an ARCT-810 End-of-Phase-2 meeting in H2 2026 and said a scheduled date would be useful. Instead, Arcturus reported completed enrollment and dosing and said full Phase 2 data and the regulatory path, including its meeting plan, would be disclosed in Q3 2026; no meeting date was reported.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enrollment and study-drug dosing were completed” for ARCT-810, with “full Phase 2 data (including FDA-requested supplementary Type C data) and the regulatory path forward, including an end-of-Phase-2 meeting plan, to be disclosed in Q3 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ARCT-810 End-of-Phase-2 meeting. Guided to H2 2026. A scheduled date would de-risk the pediatric design.”

surprises.description: The preview did not mention the ARCT-2304 Phase 1 milestone or its regulatory and publication progress. Arcturus reported that the pandemic flu candidate completed Phase 1, its results were accepted by Nature Communications, and EMA scientific advice is planned for Q4 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pandemic flu program ARCT-2304 completed Phase 1 with results accepted by Nature Communications and EMA scientific advice planned for Q4 2026.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $3 million, close to the preview’s $3.1 million consensus and within its $2.5–3.5 million estimate; H1 revenue of $5 million was also close to the preview’s $5.2 million implied by Q1 actual plus Q2 consensus.
Cash was $191.5 million, within the preview’s $190–195 million estimate, and management reaffirmed runway through year-end 2028, consistent with the preview’s expectation of runway beyond Q2 2028.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $125.8 million, about $5.8 million above the preview’s $119.99 million consensus. The reported 9% constant-currency growth was also stronger than the preview’s 6.2% consensus growth estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue was $125.8 million, up 9% year-over-year on a constant currency basis.”

surprises.description: Despite the revenue and EBITDA beat, the full-year adjusted EBITDA range was $92–99 million, below the preview’s stated current guidance of $100–107 million. The revenue range was reaffirmed, but the EBITDA outlook was lower than investors were led to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance of 7-11% constant currency growth ($480-$496 million revenue) and adjusted EBITDA of $92-$99 million, choosing conservatism despite the Q2 beat.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | $100–107M”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA of $26.4 million came in slightly above the preview’s derived $24–26 million range and the $25 million bogey, though the beat was narrow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 7% from $24.8 million to $26.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$24–26M (derived)” and “Bogeys are ≥$25M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin fell about 90 basis points to 21% as R&D investment increased after the Endospan acquisition, rather than showing the margin expansion the preview inferred from the annual outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin declined roughly 90 basis points to 21% due to increased R&D investments following the Endospan acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The FY guide implies ~100bps of margin expansion.”

surprises.description: Stent-graft growth accelerated to 12%, exceeding the preview’s minimum 10% constant-currency bogey and doing so against a tougher comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Stent graft revenue accelerated to 12% growth (from 10% in Q1) against a tougher comp.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bogey is ≥+10% cc, matching Q1.”

surprises.description: ONIX grew 18%, above the preview’s 15% growth bogey, with management attributing growth to global share gains in patients under 65.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ONIX grew 18% on global market share gains in patients under 65.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “On-X constant-currency growth. Q1 was +17% cc … Bogey is ≥+15%.”

surprises.description: Tissue processing revenue included roughly $2 million shifted from Q3 into Q2. That timing benefit helped produce about $26 million of Q2 revenue despite just 1% growth, and leaves a corresponding timing headwind for Q3 that the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tissue processing revenue was approximately $26 million (up 1%), aided by roughly $2 million of upside from tissue releases that shifted from Q3 into Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said preservation services faces difficult comps in Q2 and Q3, normalizing in Q4.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed negative Q2 free cash flow of $12 million, including a $10.2 million transaction bonus expense and $1.5 million of Endospan diligence costs. The preview did not set a free-cash-flow expectation or flag these specific costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was negative $12 million in Q2, impacted by $1.5 million of Endospan diligence costs and a $10.2 million contractually required transaction bonus payment booked as a post-acquisition expense.”

surprises.description: The call reported net leverage of 3.1x after the Endospan acquisition and noted a further $25 million AMDS milestone payment in July. The preview discussed the $150 million borrowing but did not state a leverage level or flag that milestone payment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Endospan/Nexus acquisition closed for a $135 million purchase price funded by $150 million of borrowings, raising net leverage to 3.1x (excluding a $25 million AMDS milestone paid in July).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “May 18: Endospan acquisition closed. $175M headline ($135M upfront cash, funded by a $150M term loan draw)”

in_line: Management reaffirmed the $480–496 million full-year revenue range, matching the preview’s stated current revenue guidance.
The Nexus U.S. commercial launch remains planned for January 2027, with inconsequential revenue expected in 2026, as the preview anticipated.

surprises.description: Q2 combined Ibsrela and Xphozah revenue was $118 million, below the $123.69 million consensus; Ibsrela's $86.2 million was also below the preview's roughly $95 million watchpoint. Xphozah was not the source of the shortfall, with revenue of $31.9 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 combined revenue for Ibsrela and Xphozah reached $118 million ... though it fell short of expectations”; “Ibsrela Q2 revenue was $86.2 million ... while Xphozah revenue was $31.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 consensus” total revenue of “$123.69M”; the catalyst checklist called for “IBSRELA at or above about $95M.”

surprises.description: Ardelyx cut its 2026 Ibsrela revenue range to $350–$370 million from the preview's $410–$430 million company guidance. The new outlook implies a steep second-half contribution despite Q2 coming in below the preview's Ibsrela watchpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management lowered full-year 2026 Ibsrela guidance to $350-$370 million”; the back half is expected to be “roughly 60% of full-year sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed company FY26 Ibsrela guidance of “$410–430M” and said reaffirming or raising that range was the “bull leg.”

surprises.description: The company withdrew its $750 million long-term Xphozah revenue guidance, citing uncertainty around the end of TDAPA, a proposed phosphorus QIP measure, and competing binders in development. The preview discussed Xphozah's 2027 TDAPA and competitive risks, but did not anticipate withdrawal of this long-term target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company pulled its $750 million long-term Xphozah revenue guidance,” citing “uncertainty from the end of the TDAPA period, a proposed phosphorus QIP quality measure, and competitive binders in development.”

surprises.description: Management said stricter payer prior authorizations and step edits were slowing new Ibsrela patient starts. The preview expected a seasonal revenue step-up and described growing prescriber breadth in its bull case, but did not flag these access barriers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Payers implemented more stringent prior authorizations and step edits that slowed new patient starts for Ibsrela,” though scripts were “delayed rather than outright blocked.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's base case expected a “seasonal step-up in line with 2025”; its bull case cited “prescriber breadth grows alongside refills.”

surprises.description: The company drew $50 million from its SLR arrangement, a financing action the preview identified as a negative signal if it accompanied the results. The reported $281.8 million cash balance includes this draw, so it does not erase the financing surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $281.8 million in cash and equivalents and drew down $50 million from its SLR arrangement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “any financing announced with the print” would be “a negative signal.”

surprises.description: Annual operating-expense guidance improved to below $500 million, versus the preview's expectation of about $520 million. This is a lower cost outlook despite higher quarterly SG&A and R&D spending.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company revised “2026 OPEX guidance to below $500 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the company had reaffirmed “opex about $520M” and identified tracking to about $520 million as the watchpoint.

in_line: Xphozah Q2 revenue of $31.9 million was within the preview's roughly $29–$32 million quarterly run rate needed for its FY26 target, and management reiterated FY26 Xphozah guidance of $110–$120 million.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was modestly above the $33.08 million consensus, while non-GAAP operating income of $7 million beat the roughly $6 million estimate and exceeded the company’s guidance high end. Revenue was near the high end of guidance, but the operating-income result was stronger than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $33.8 million” and “non-GAAP operating income of $7 million exceeded the top of its $5.5-6.5 million guidance range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $33.08M”; “Non-GAAP operating income | ~$6.0M (guide midpoint).”

surprises.description: The Q3 revenue midpoint of $32.5 million is below the preview’s derived bar of roughly $33.9 million. The company also guided to lower Q3 non-GAAP operating income of $3.5–4.5 million, citing weaker macro conditions and a $1.5 million seasonal marketing step-up.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 revenue of $31.5-33.5 million” and “Q3 non-GAAP operating income of $3.5-4.5 million (~12% margin), reflecting a weaker macro and a $1.5 million seasonal marketing step-up.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “That implies a Q3 revenue guide midpoint of roughly $33.9M (+3% Y/Y). This is a derivation, not a published figure.”

surprises.description: The outlook for Q4 loan volume was markedly weaker than the preview’s reference to a market-volume forecast of about 19% growth: management now expects the market to contract 11% and Blend’s funded loans to fall 10–15% year over year. The company also cited the final roll-off of a previously disclosed large customer.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 funded loan volume is expected to decline approximately 10-15% year-over-year to 180,000-190,000 loans, reflecting a projected 11% market contraction and the final roll-off of a previously disclosed large customer.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management anchored FY26 to Fannie Mae's ~19% market volume growth forecast, and the 30-year fixed hit 6.66% on July 30, 2026, which weakens that anchor.”

surprises.description: Autopilot’s early commercial traction was more concrete than the preview anticipated: it had six paying contracts, including Onity, and had processed over 45,000 cumulative loans. Early customer results also included higher pull-through, faster cycle times, and substantial task automation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Autopilot became commercially available July 1st, has processed over 45,000 cumulative loans since February, activated 65+ lenders, and already signed six paying contracts including major servicer Onity.” Early data showed “10-15% improvement in pull-through rates, 2-4 days of cycle time improvement, and automation of roughly 4.5 hours of loan fulfillment tasks per loan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 captures at most about one month of paid revenue, so expect little revenue. Look for a dollar figure or paying-customer count. The July 7 announcement named five commercial customers, including Onity Mortgage.”

surprises.description: Management reported more customer churn notices, with some customers switching to lower-cost or free point solutions. The estimated impact is low single digits of annual revenue, making this a newly disclosed headwind rather than a large immediate revenue hit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported an uptick in churn notices this quarter, with customers moving to lower-cost or free point solutions, estimated to have a manageable low-single-digit impact on annual revenue.”

surprises.description: The sales pipeline strengthened substantially, including the portion expected to close within a quarter, and now includes a top-20 financial institution and multiple large Rapid deals. The preview did not flag this pipeline acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Late-stage pipeline (deals expected to close within a quarter) grew nearly 40% between March and June, and overall pipeline remains up more than 40% year-over-year, including a top-20 financial institution and multiple large Rapid deals.”

surprises.description: Engineering throughput rose sharply without a comparable increase in headcount, a productivity development not discussed in the preview. Management is targeting further gains by year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The engineering team increased its throughput (pull requests) 3.6x since January 2026 with roughly the same headcount, up from 1.5x in May, with management targeting 10x by year-end.”

in_line: Q2 economic value per funded loan was $79, within the preview’s $79–80 expectation; Q3 guidance of $80–81 is slightly higher.
The Q2 buyback was broadly in line with the prior-quarter pace: Blend repurchased 11 million shares in Q2 versus 11.2 million shares in Q1.

surprises.description: Blink cut its FY2026 revenue outlook to $83–90 million from $105–115 million, a sharp reduction from the previously reaffirmed range. Management attributed the cut to the Envoy divestiture and a focus on revenue quality rather than weak demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance” was cut “to $83-90 million from the prior $105-115 million,” citing “revenue-quality focus and the Envoy divestiture rather than weak demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance: FY26 revenue $105–115M”; the preview said the key catalyst was whether the guide was “held, narrowed, or cut.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $21.7 million, about 12% below the preview’s roughly $24.6 million consensus and below its bear-scenario threshold of $22 million. It did rise 4.3% sequentially, but that did not close the gap to the expected quarterly level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 revenue fell to $21.7 million from $28.7 million year-over-year, though it rose 4.3% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | ~$24.6M (range $24.25M–$24.6M)”; the bear scenario was “<$22M.”

surprises.description: Service revenue was $11.5 million, materially below the preview’s roughly $14.5 million estimate and below the $14.7 million sequential-uptrend marker. It grew 6.2% year over year but declined from Q1’s $13.3 million, contrary to the hoped-for sequential recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Service revenue grew 6.2% to $11.5 million”; Q1 service revenue was $13.3 million, according to the preview.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Service revenue (est.) ~$14.5M”; the preview said service “needs to clear about $14.7M to restore a sequential uptrend.”

surprises.description: Product revenue came in below the preview’s estimated $8–9 million, at $7.4 million. Its decline from $14.5 million a year earlier was steeper than the preview’s expected range implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Product revenues dropped to $7.4 million from $14.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Product revenue (est.) ~$8–9M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin substantially outperformed the preview’s roughly 33% base-case expectation: Q2 GAAP gross margin reached 38.9%. Blink also raised its FY2026 GAAP gross-margin outlook to about 38% from 35%, rather than merely holding the prior target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP gross margin expanded to 38.9% from 16.8%”; “Full-year 2026 GAAP gross margin outlook was raised to approximately 38% from 35% previously.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “GM ~33%”; the preview listed FY26 GAAP gross-margin guidance of “~35%.”

surprises.description: The adjusted EBITDA loss was much smaller than the preview’s expected $4–5 million loss, narrowing to $2.2 million. That was also a multiyear low, exceeding the expected improvement implied by the consensus range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $2.2 million from $7.9 million a year earlier, a 72% improvement and a multiyear low.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (est.) ~−$4M to −$5M.”

surprises.description: Management gave a concrete adjusted-EBITDA profitability trajectory after the preview said it had declined to provide a 2026 breakeven target: it now targets approximately breakeven exiting 2026 and positive adjusted EBITDA for full-year 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management targets exiting 2026 at approximately breakeven adjusted EBITDA and a positive full-year adjusted EBITDA in 2027, with formal 2027 guidance to come at year-end results.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has declined to give a 2026 adjusted-EBITDA breakeven target.”

in_line: Blink reiterated the aim for recurring revenue to reach roughly 80% of total revenue by 2028, consistent with the preview’s stated 80%-by-2028 goal.

surprises.description: BioMarin reported nearly $1 billion of Q2 revenue, above the preview's $929–939 million consensus range. That is a clear revenue beat, though below the preview's $975–995 million bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached nearly $1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $929M (StockStory) or $939M (Investing.com)”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $1.20, well above both the $0.92–0.95 consensus range and the preview author's $0.98 base case. The result was also within the preview's bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.20.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS | $0.92 (Public.com); $0.93–$0.95 (other feeds)” and “Author's base-case estimate … non-GAAP EPS $0.98.”

surprises.description: BioMarin raised full-year revenue, VOXZOGO revenue, and non-GAAP EPS guidance, whereas the preview's base case assumed guidance would be reaffirmed. The updated ranges are not provided, so the size of the increase cannot be assessed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BioMarin raised full-year 2026 guidance for total revenues, VOXZOGO revenue and non-GAAP diluted EPS.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … FY guide reaffirmed” and “The asymmetry sits in the guide, not the quarter.”

surprises.description: The preview identified the new competitor as the main bear argument for VOXZOGO, but management reported limited switching: about 90% of U.S. patients remained on therapy and roughly 10% switched over about six months. That suggests a smaller competitive impact than the preview's key risk framing implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 90% of U.S. patients remained on therapy despite a U.S. competitor launch in February” and switching was “approximately 10% of VOXZOGO patients, equating to fewer than 100 patient switches over roughly six months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Competitor entry is the main bear argument.”

surprises.description: Management quantified annual cost synergies at about $220 million by 2028, with over 70% weighted toward G&A. The preview expected some integration detail but described the likely disclosure as modest; the quantified savings are substantial relative to Amicus's stated 2025 non-GAAP operating expenses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cost synergies of approximately $220 million annual run rate are expected by 2028,” about “a ~50% reduction” from Amicus's 2025 non-GAAP operating expenses, and “weighted over 70% toward G&A.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Amicus contribution and first synergy/peak-sales disclosure” and the base scenario expected “modest synergy detail.”

surprises.description: BioMarin gave a favorable deal-accretion timeline: the Amicus acquisition is expected to be only modestly dilutive in 2026 and substantially accretive starting in 2027, with more than half of synergies expected next year and deleveraging pulled forward by about a year. The preview focused on financing-related EPS drag but did not anticipate this timing or the accelerated deleveraging.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Close to breakeven (modestly dilutive) in 2026 but substantially accretive to non-GAAP EPS beginning in 2027,” with “half or slightly more of synergies realized next year” and “deleveraging pulled forward by about one year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The optical EPS decline is largely financing-driven” and the author estimated a “$0.15–0.20/share after-tax drag from interest.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a new pipeline asset, BMN 820, an oral CCR2 inhibitor for FSGS, with an estimated 30,000 U.S. addressable patients and Phase III data expected in 2028. The preview's pipeline discussion did not mention this asset.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New pipeline asset BMN 820 (oral CCR2 inhibitor for FSGS) targets an estimated 30,000 U.S. addressable patients with Phase III data expected in 2028.”

in_line: The VOXZOGO hypochondroplasia sNDA was submitted during 2H 2026, consistent with the preview's planned 2H'26 submission.
The approximately $200 million annualized acquisition-debt interest expense is broadly in line with the preview's estimate of $45–55 million per quarter.

surprises.description: The Phase 3 PTCL interim futility analysis is now projected for Q1 2027, later than prior expectations; the preview had identified PTCL enrollment progress as a key potential update but gave no interim-analysis date. Corvus also said no safety or efficacy data will be disclosed at that interim analysis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Phase 3 PTCL trial's interim futility analysis is now projected for Q1 2027 (versus prior expectations), with final data still anticipated in late 2027 and no safety/efficacy data to be publicly disclosed at the interim.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “An enrollment update would be the main upside surprise.”

surprises.description: The Sierra AD trial’s top-line data are now expected in Q3 2027, later than the preview’s secondary-source expectation of mid-2027. Enrollment completion is expected early 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enrollment completion expected early 2027 and top-line data in Q3 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Secondary sources point to topline in mid-2027.”

surprises.description: Instead of the HS Phase 2 start the preview expected, Corvus plans to begin a Phase 1b HS trial, with up to 25 patients and no placebo group. The start is still planned before year-end 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Corvus plans to initiate a Phase 1b HS trial (up to 25 patients, no placebo, 200mg BID for 12 weeks) … before year-end 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “HS and asthma Phase 2 starts, guided ‘later this year.’”

surprises.description: Corvus reported a strong Phase 1 AD signal in the highest-dose cohort: 75% achieved EASI-75 versus 20% on placebo, with additional EASI-90 and IGA 0/1 responses only in the soquelitinib group. The preview did not anticipate this cohort readout.
surprises.fact_evidence: “75% of soquelitinib patients achieved EASI-75 versus 20% on placebo, with 25% achieving EASI-90 and 33% achieving IGA 0/1 (versus none on placebo).”

surprises.description: Management reported that the AD treatment benefit persisted after dosing stopped, without disease rebound, contrasting with rebound seen with dupilumab, JAK inhibitors, and STAT6 agents. This durability claim and its proposed T-regulatory-cell explanation were not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Soquelitinib showed prolonged treatment benefit beyond dosing without disease rebound, contrasting with rebound seen in dupilumab, JAK inhibitors, and STAT6 agents, attributed to enhanced T regulatory cell function.”

surprises.description: Corvus committed $5 million to Angel Pharmaceuticals’ $13.5 million financing, an unflagged use of cash. The investment supports Angel’s AD work and planned early-2027 China asthma trial, while Corvus remains Angel’s largest shareholder.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Corvus invested $5 million in Angel Pharmaceuticals' $13.5 million financing and remains Angel's largest shareholder, with Angel funds supporting AD and a planned early-2027 asthma trial in China.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any partnering or business development commentary.”

surprises.description: Corvus said Angel’s China AD data can be used in Corvus’s FDA filings, a regulatory relevance not anticipated in the preview. The first cohort’s data by year-end 2026 is in line with the preview’s expectation of a late-year China readout.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Partner Angel Pharmaceuticals' Chinese AD trial is expected to complete first-cohort enrollment in September 2026, with cohort 1 data by year-end 2026 and cohort 2 data in Q2 2027, and its data is usable in Corvus's FDA filings.”

surprises.description: The planned Phase 2 asthma trial will include both T2 and non-T2 patients, with non-T2 patients representing an estimated 40–50% of asthma patients. The preview expected an asthma Phase 2 start but did not flag this broader enrollment scope.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A Phase 2 asthma trial enrolling both T2 and non-T2 patients (the latter representing ~40-50% of asthma patients) before year-end 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “HS and asthma Phase 2 starts, guided ‘later this year.’”

in_line: Q2 net loss of $18 million is within the preview’s rough estimate that quarterly burn could be about $17–19 million as the trial portfolio expanded.
R&D spending rose from Q1’s $11.2 million to $16 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation that R&D would step up as the AD trial progressed.
The company reiterated that its cash runway extends into Q2 2028, as previously stated.
The asthma Phase 2 start remains planned for before year-end 2026, in line with the preview’s expectation of a 2H26 start.
Angel’s first China AD cohort data are expected by year-end 2026, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a late-year readout.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $13.5 million, above the top of the preview’s cited $8–12 million guidance range. Favorable margin mix and lower operating expenses drove the outperformance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $13.5 million” and was “above the high end of the $8-12 million guidance range,” driven by “favorable margin mix and lower operating expenses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA vs. the $8–12M band” was identified as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: Cerence raised FY26 free cash flow guidance to $76–82 million from $66–76 million, an improvement beyond the preview’s prior-year guidance baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year fiscal 2026 free cash flow guidance to $76-82 million from the prior $66-76 million,” with “$20 million in free cash flow in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 free cash flow guidance of “$66–76M” and said the market was watching for a guidance action.

surprises.description: The Board authorized Cerence’s first share repurchase program, which the preview did not flag as an expected capital-allocation action.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board authorized Cerence's first-ever share repurchase program of up to $30 million over the next 12 months,” funded from cash on hand and free cash flow.

surprises.description: Variable license revenue fell 15% as Cerence’s vehicle production declined 8%, substantially worse than the roughly 2% drop in global light vehicle production. The preview did not anticipate this unfavorable OEM and regional mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Variable license revenue fell 15% year-over-year to $29.1 million” as Cerence’s vehicle production “dropped 8% versus a roughly 2% decline in global light vehicle production,” reflecting “unfavorable OEM and regional mix.”

surprises.description: The fixed license recognized in Q3 was $12.5 million, above the preview’s roughly $10 million assumption for the deal. This helped support in-range revenue, although total revenue was essentially at consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q4 guidance reflects “the absence of the $12.5 million fixed license revenue recognized in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q3 guidance assumed a fixed license signing of “~$10M.”

surprises.description: Cerence signed a new XUI deal with Stellantis, providing a named commercial win while the preview was looking for XUI progress and possible new named wins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cerence signed a new XUI deal with Stellantis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “xUI commercial progress” and “new named wins.”

surprises.description: Cerence secured its first customer for a Microsoft-developed mobile work agent with a global premium automaker, adding a non-XUI product opportunity the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “secured its first customer for a Microsoft-developed mobile work agent with a global premium automaker,” expanding its addressable market beyond XUI programs.

in_line: Q3 revenue of approximately $70 million was within the $68–72 million guidance range and essentially matched the preview’s approximately $70.1 million consensus.
Connected services revenue grew 20% to $15.5 million, in line with the preview’s expectation of growth around 20% or more.

Q4 revenue guidance of $61–65 million, with a midpoint of $63 million, was consistent with the preview’s implied approximately $63 million quarter; the preview also anticipated a substantial sequential step-down.
Q4 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $1–5 million, with a midpoint of $3 million, was in line with the preview’s implied approximately $3 million quarter.
The high-single to low-double-digit FY27 revenue growth outlook matched the growth framework referenced in the preview.

surprises.description: The preview warned that Q2 cash could fall near $95–105 million and that a low balance could revive dilution concerns. Instead, cash and short-term investments rose to $138 million, from $126 million in March, with less than $5 million left to contribute to the dairy JV.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and short-term investments grew to $138 million at quarter-end (up from $126 million in March), with less than $5 million remaining to be contributed to the Maas Energy Works dairy JV.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 cash could land near $95–105M”; “Anything below about $100M with no financing plan would revive dilution concerns.”

surprises.description: The preview said a quantified 45Z benefit would be a clear upside, but the call gave no finalized benefit and said the GREET guidance is now expected in Q4. Management said a delay into 2027 or minimal benefit could leave adjusted EBITDA below the maintained $70–75 million range, making the guide more contingent than the preview’s upside framing suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Finalized 45Z GREET model guidance—now expected in Q4—could add up to $5 million of incremental adjusted EBITDA, but a delay into 2027 or minimal benefit would push EBITDA below the $70-$75 million range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A quantified 45Z benefit would be a clear upside.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged an early upstream ramp as a potential driver, but the call reported that RNG upstream had already approached EBITDA breakeven in Q2 as South Fork and East Valley ramped. It also gave a schedule for the remaining JV projects: two expected online this fall and the third in early 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The RNG upstream business approached breakeven EBITDA in Q2 as South Fork (Texas) and East Valley (Idaho) ramped, with two of three JV projects expected online this fall and the third in early 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Upstream dairy RNG ramp. Eight projects operating and three under construction. Watch South Fork (TX) and East Valley (Idaho, about 3.5M gal/yr, commissioned Q1).” The preview also described an “early upstream ramp” as a bull-scenario driver.

surprises.description: The call disclosed that X15N truck adoption remains slow, with buyers favoring legacy diesel trucks ahead of uncertainty over 2027 emissions standards. The preview did not flag this adoption challenge; the call noted 35 X15Ns deployed across 7–8 Canadian fleets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “X15N truck adoption remains slow, hurt by a large prebuy of legacy diesel trucks amid uncertainty over final 2027 EPA emission standards, though 35 X15Ns are now deployed across 7-8 fleets in Canada.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a new $27 million Orange County Transportation Authority contract for its largest hydrogen fueling station. The low-capital cost-plus structure also limits exposure to commodity and capital risk, a development not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company secured a $27 million contract with Orange County Transportation Authority for its largest hydrogen fueling station, using a low-capital cost-plus model that avoids commodity and capital risk.”

surprises.description: The call introduced an off-pipeline power-generation opportunity for data centers, fulfillment centers, and EV charging, using existing tube trailers and underused compression capacity at 600 stations with little or no new investment. The preview did not anticipate this potential use of existing assets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Clean Energy is pursuing an off-pipeline power-generation market (data centers, fulfillment centers, EV charging) using existing tube trailers and underutilized compression capacity at 600 stations, requiring little to no new investment.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $106.4 million, adjusted EBITDA of $16 million, and RNG volume of 63.2 million gallons were reported as in line with expectations; the preview’s own estimates were about $108 million, $16 million, and 64 million gallons, respectively.
The company maintained its FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $70–75 million, as the preview’s base case expected the range to be reaffirmed.

surprises.description: The preview highlighted uncertainty around funding Sandersville’s $1.75–2.1 billion build-out and flagged possible equity issuance. CleanSpark said the project’s equity portion is fully funded and that it does not plan equity raises for the project; it also said the high-investment-grade tenant enables financing at favorable rates without credit wrappers or equity backstops, though the call did not say the full financing is closed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The equity portion already fully funded and no equity raises planned for the project”; the tenant is “high investment-grade” and enables “financing without credit wrappers or equity backstops at favorable rates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “non-dilutive project debt versus any hint of equity,” and its base case expected financing to be framed as “multiple paths”; its bear case included an “equity component or ATM disclosed.”

in_line: Revenue of $138 million was essentially in line with the preview’s live consensus of $139.4 million, though above its own $128–133 million estimate.
The $133 million unfavorable Bitcoin mark-to-market adjustment was within the preview’s estimated $120–135 million non-cash loss.

Sandersville’s $6.6 billion contracted revenue, potential to scale to $11.6 billion, and approximately $330 million average annual NOI had already been reported in the preview; the first data hall remains on track for Q4 2027, as previewed.
The Texas portfolio remains under exclusivity but does not yet have a signed lease, consistent with the preview’s focus on possible LOI conversion rather than an already completed agreement.

surprises.description: The preview estimated Q2 revenue at $9.39 million (and its own estimate was $9.3 million), with a year-over-year decline expected. CTSO reported about $9.6 million, flat year over year, a modest beat on the quarter and a better year-over-year comparison than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was approximately $9.6 million, flat year-over-year but up 9% sequentially from Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2'26 Consensus | $9.39M | My Estimate | $9.3M”; “Revenue YoY | –2% | –3%.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 73%, well above the preview’s 69.5% estimate and the roughly 70% level used in its break-even analysis. The company attributed the improvement to manufacturing optimization and cost management.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margins improved to 73%, up from 71% in the prior-year quarter and 69% in Q1 2026, driven by manufacturing optimization and cost management.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | … My Estimate | 69.5%”; the break-even discussion assumes “70% gross margin.”

surprises.description: Operating cash burn was only about $200,000 excluding restructuring, far below the $1.1 million Q1 burn cited in the preview, while management said it remained on track for H2 2026 operating cash flow break-even. This is a stronger cash-burn position than the preview’s revenue-and-cost assumptions implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash burn was reduced to approximately $200,000 excluding restructuring costs, keeping the company on track to reach operating cash flow break-even in the second half of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating burn was about $1.1M excluding restructuring”; “Q2 at $9.3M leaves a gap of about $1.5M per quarter” to the preview’s estimated break-even revenue requirement.

surprises.description: The operating loss was wider than the preview’s $2.4 million estimate, even as adjusted EBITDA matched expectations. This is a modest shortfall on the operating-loss measure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating loss narrowed 27% to $2.6 million versus the prior-year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating loss | … My Estimate | $(2.4)M.”

surprises.description: The reported $0.07-per-share net loss was slightly worse than the preview’s $0.06 GAAP loss estimate. The call said the year-over-year swing to a net loss was driven mainly by non-cash foreign-currency effects.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss was $4.4 million ($0.07/share) versus prior-year net income of $1.9 million ($0.03/share), a swing driven mainly by non-cash foreign currency effects.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS … $(0.04) adj / $(0.06) GAAP”; the preview cautioned that the $(0.05) consensus was “probably an adjusted number.”

surprises.description: CTSO plans to file a new de novo application for DrugSorb-ATR only after collecting additional mechanistic and real-world evidence, while also pursuing pre-submission discussions for a parallel DOAC-removal indication. The preview did not anticipate this application strategy or the additional indication discussions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to file a new de novo application for DrugSorb-ATR after gathering additional mechanistic and real-world evidence data, with two separate FDA pre-submission meetings scheduled later this month, including one for a parallel DOAC-removal indication targeting the ~$20 billion Eliquis/Xarelto market.”

surprises.description: The STAR-T CABG per-protocol analysis showed a statistically significant 58% reduction in severe bleeding or blood loss above 1 liter, with an NNT of six, but the primary MITT endpoint was not statistically significant. The preview did not flag these trial results, so this is a new, mixed clinical update rather than an outcome against a stated forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In the CABG per-protocol analysis of the STAR-T pivotal trial, DrugSorb-ATR achieved a statistically significant 58% risk reduction in severe bleeding or >1L blood loss (win ratio 1.59) with a number needed to treat of six, though the primary MITT endpoint was not statistically significant.”

surprises.description: After reducing headcount by roughly 23%, the company plans to add three to five sales representatives through early 2027, mainly to restore German territory coverage weakened by restructuring. The preview discussed cost reductions and German weakness but did not anticipate these planned hires.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Headcount has been reduced by roughly 23% since September 2025, and the company plans to selectively add three to five sales reps through early 2027, mainly to restore German territory coverage weakened by restructuring.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA loss was $1.6 million, matching the preview’s $1.6 million estimate and falling within its $1.5–$2.0 million base-case range.

Management kept H2 2026 operating cash flow break-even on track, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the company would reaffirm or retime that marker; the much lower reported cash burn is captured separately above.
Germany remained weak, consistent with the preview’s base case of Germany being flat rather than returning to growth.

surprises.description: AVLAYAH generated $3.6 million in its first full commercial quarter, above the preview’s roughly $2.15 million consensus and the $1.5–3 million base scenario, though below the preview’s bull case of more than $5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Avalaya (Ablea) generated $3.6 million in net product revenue in its first full commercial quarter for Hunter syndrome.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus is about $2.15M”; the base scenario forecast “$1.5–3M” and the bull scenario “>$5M.”

surprises.description: Management guided to $10–12 million of Q3 product revenue, implying roughly threefold sequential growth. The preview highlighted the H2 revenue slope but did not give a Q3 forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided to Q3 net product revenue of $10-12 million, implying roughly 3x sequential growth driven by expanding payer access and patient adoption.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “the H2 slope it implies” as a catalyst and said FY2026 revenue consensus “implies ~$31.8M in H2,” but gave no Q3 estimate.

surprises.description: Pro forma cash and securities exceeded $1.15 billion, including $195 million from a July voucher sale—well above the preview’s estimate of about $930 million at Q2 end. The pro forma figure includes post-quarter proceeds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pro forma cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities exceeded $1.15 billion, including $195 million received in July from the sale of a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash of about $930M is estimated for the end of Q2, with runway into 2028.”

surprises.description: The launch had already secured commercial policies covering more than half of lives, with 14 state Medicaid programs listing Ablea as covered in its first quarter. The preview called payer coverage a key metric but gave no expected coverage level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commercial policies covering more than 50% of lives have been established, with 14 state Medicaid programs publicly listing Ablea as covered in the first quarter of launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “payer coverage” among the quantified launch metrics to watch, without specifying an expected level.

surprises.description: Denali had engaged more than 100 families, representing over one-quarter of eligible US patients, and said most adoption is expected to come from switching patients already on Idursulfase. The preview emphasized patient metrics but did not anticipate a quantified level of family engagement or this switching mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Denali engaged more than 100 families, representing over one-quarter of eligible US patients, with the majority of adoption expected to come from switching the ~90% of prevalent patients already on Idursulfase.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Patient starts, patients on therapy, and payer coverage matter more” than the initial revenue figure, but gave no family-engagement or switching estimate.

surprises.description: DNL593 data timing moved from the preview’s end-of-2026 guidance to the first half of 2027, a material delay. Management said it wanted longer biomarker observation, including neurofilament light chain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DNL593 for FTD-granulin data was delayed from end of 2025 to first half of 2027 to allow longer observation of biomarkers like neurofilament light chain.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said DNL593 was guided “by end of 2026” and that “Any softening of that language would be a material negative.”

surprises.description: DNL593 recently received FDA orphan drug designation, an unanticipated positive regulatory milestone in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “It recently received FDA orphan drug designation.”

surprises.description: Both Alzheimer’s programs, DNL628 and DNL921, entered clinical development, with initial biomarker and proof-of-concept data expected in 2027. The preview did not flag these program advances or data timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Both Alzheimer's programs—DNL628 (anti-tau OTV) and DNL921 (anti-amyloid ATV)—have entered clinical development, with initial biomarker and proof-of-concept data expected in 2027.”

surprises.description: SG&A was $36.3 million, below the preview’s roughly $40 million estimate and below its $45 million concern threshold; R&D was also down year over year, leaving overall operating expense roughly flat year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 R&D expenses were $97 million (down from $102.7 million a year earlier) while SG&A rose to $36.3 million (from $32.3 million) reflecting launch investments, keeping overall OpEx roughly flat year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “the estimate is about $40M” for G&A and that “Above $45M would raise questions about launch economics.”

surprises.description: CVRx cut its FY26 revenue outlook to $58–60 million from the preview’s $63–67 million company guide, and now expects only $13.5–14.5 million of Q3 revenue. The FY range is well below the preview’s $65.28 million consensus and even below its bear-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $58-60 million and guided Q3 revenue to $13.5-14.5 million, signaling a weaker second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue | $65.28M (+15%) | $63–67M”; the preview’s bear scenario said “Reaffirmed or trimmed to $61–65M.”

surprises.description: The weakness was tied to a major sales-ramp problem the preview did not flag: roughly 60% of quota-carrying territory managers are new within 18 months, and the highest-turnover regions have negative implant growth. In contrast, stable, seasoned regions are still growing at double-digit rates, making performance unusually uneven.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly 60% of quota-carrying territory managers joined within the last 18 months, straining onboarding and slowing productivity ramps”; in high-turnover regions “implant growth is actually negative year-to-date,” while stable, seasoned regions “continue to post strong double-digit growth.”

surprises.description: The largest Medicare Advantage payer’s approval rate fell sharply after introducing AI-based prior authorization tools, a significant payer-specific setback not anticipated in the preview. Its rate remains below 30% despite CVRx’s countermeasures, even as the overall rate improved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The largest Medicare Advantage payer's 30-day approval rate collapsed from roughly 80% to about 25% in February-March after AI-based prior authorization tools were implemented, and it remains below 30% despite company countermeasures.”

surprises.description: Overall 30-day Medicare Advantage prior-authorization approvals reached 60%, above the preview’s 55%-or-higher threshold and its cited 50% rate in January–February. Humana approvals now exceed 90%, contributing to the improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Overall 30-day Medicare Advantage prior authorization approval rate rose to 60% in Q2 2026 from 44% in 2025, aided by the Humana coverage policy where approvals now exceed 90%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A reading of 55% or higher would support the reimbursement thesis”; the preview said the rate was “50% in Jan–Feb 2026.”

surprises.description: Traditional Medicare reimbursement brought additional favorable news the preview did not discuss: about 96% of submitted claims are now paid across all seven Medicare administrative contractors, and the inpatient payment rate is set to increase from $43,000 to $45,000 on October 1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Traditional Medicare now pays approximately 96% of submitted Barostim claims across all seven Medicare administrative contractors, and the inpatient payment rate rises from $43,000 to $45,000 effective October 1st.”

surprises.description: The cash balance came in above the preview’s roughly $60 million estimate, but the stated runway was only 18+ months rather than the preview’s expected two or more years. The undrawn $40 million debt facility was anticipated, so it does not erase the shorter stated runway.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and equivalents stood at $64.6 million (estimated 18+ months of runway) with $40 million still undrawn on the debt facility.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “About $60M is expected at Q2 end”; “Management says runway is 2+ years, with about $40M of additional capacity tied to revenue milestones.”

surprises.description: CVRx disclosed a DOJ civil investigative demand concerning certain sales and marketing practices, an unanticipated legal and compliance issue. The preview mentioned the CFO transition, but not a DOJ investigation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received a DOJ civil investigative demand in May 2026 related to certain sales and marketing practices, and is undergoing a CFO transition while cooperating with the investigation.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin was 87%, about one percentage point above the preview’s approximately 86% expectation and at the top of the company’s previously stated 85–87% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $15.7 million, up 16% year-over-year, with gross margin improving to 87% from 84% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~86%”; the preview also cited the company’s “85–87% (FY)” guide.

in_line: Q2 revenue of $15.7 million was within the preview’s $15.5–15.6 million consensus range and its $15.7–16.0 million base scenario, even though it was below the high end of the company’s $16.1 million quarterly guide.

surprises.description: MYQORZO sales substantially outpaced the preview’s implied $14–16 million product-sales range: the company reported $25.3 million, helping total revenue reach $28.6 million versus about $17.6 million expected. Total revenue also rose sequentially, contrary to the preview’s expectation of a sequential headline decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “MYQORZO generated $25.3 million in net product revenue”; “Total Q2 2026 revenues” were “$28.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus of about $17.6M for Q2 implies headline revenue falls sequentially”; “Consensus total revenue implies roughly $14–16M of product sales.”

surprises.description: The Phase III Acacia trial succeeded on both primary endpoints with no new safety signals, and management plans to file an sNDA in Q4 2026. That is a favorable outcome and a much earlier filing timeline than the H2 2027 timing assumed in sell-side models.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Phase III Acacia HCM trial in nonobstructive HCM met both dual primary endpoints … with no new safety signals,” supporting “a planned sNDA submission to the FDA in Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sell-side models assume an H2 2027 filing”; the preview said to watch for “FDA feedback on the non-obstructive sNDA” and a possible safety hurdle.

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year combined R&D and SG&A expense guidance, signaling higher spending than investors had been given in the prior range. The increase is attributed to commercial-readiness investment for a potential 2027 nHCM launch.
surprises.fact_evidence: Guidance rose to “$860–890 million from $830–870 million,” driven by “commercial readiness investments for a potential 2027 nHCM launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 combined GAAP R&D + SG&A of $830–870M” was the guidance “in force.”

surprises.description: Reported loss per share was better than the preview’s consensus estimate, at $1.50 versus an expected loss of $1.63 per share, despite the increase in commercial spending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $198.8 million ($1.50 per share).”

surprises.description: The launch reached 1,500 dispensed patients by quarter-end, below the preview’s base-case expectation of 1,600–1,800 cumulative patients. This was a modest shortfall in patient count even as product revenue exceeded expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “MYQORZO was dispensed to 1,500 patients by the end of Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “about 1,600–1,800 cumulative” patients.

surprises.description: More than 80% of Q2 dispensed prescriptions were paid for, ahead of the preview’s expectation that paid conversion would remain near or above 70%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 80% of Q2 dispensed prescriptions paid for.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected conversion “near 70%” in its base case and flagged whether “more than 70% paid” would be maintained.

surprises.description: The company disclosed that June exit new-to-brand prescription share exceeded 40% in the CMI category and set a goal of exceeding 50% by year-end or sooner. The preview focused on patient adds and payer access rather than this share benchmark, so it had no comparable expectation for the reported level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “June exit new-to-brand prescription share above 40% in the CMI category,” with a target of “exceeding 50% share by year-end or sooner.”

surprises.description: Cash and investments rose to about $1.7 billion from the preview’s stated $1.1 billion, largely because of a roughly $760 million May offering. This reduces the preview’s near-term runway concern, while also reflecting an equity financing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cytokinetics ended Q2 with approximately $1.7 billion in cash and investments, up from $1.1 billion,” largely from “a May public offering generating roughly $760 million in net proceeds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “about $1.1B” in cash and described “an equity raise” as “a live risk.”

surprises.description: Funko’s Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $40.9 million, far above the preview’s $5–10 million guidance range. Even excluding the $25 million tariff-related benefit, EBITDA was $15 million, still above the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA swung to $40.9 million from negative $16.5 million a year earlier, and even excluding the tariff benefit was $15 million, exceeding guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA | $5–10M”; the preview also said the catalyst was “Adjusted EBITDA versus the $10M high end of guidance.”

surprises.description: Funko raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $100–110 million from $70–80 million, a much larger increase than the preview’s identified possibility of a raise. The company attributed the change to the $25 million tariff credit and $5 million of improved profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year net sales guidance was reiterated at flat to up 3%, while adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $100-$110 million, driven by the $25 million tariff credit plus $5 million of improved profitability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA | $70–80M”; the preview described a raise as “the highest-leverage positive surprise available.”

surprises.description: Loungefly sales fell only 2%, much less than the preview’s concern that declines of 20% or more could continue. Sales held up despite roughly 50% fewer SKUs, indicating substantially higher productivity per SKU.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Loungefly sales declined 2% but did so with roughly 50% fewer SKUs, signaling substantially improved SKU productivity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Continued declines of 20%+ would suggest the SKU cuts are costing more revenue than they save.”

surprises.description: Q2 sales grew 7% year over year, above the company’s expected Q2 growth range of 1% to 6%. The preview’s consensus revenue estimate was around $200 million, but the supplied call facts do not give the reported dollar amount for a direct comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose 7% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $195–205M (+1% to +6%)”; the preview also cited consensus of “~$200M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 56.6%, well above the expected 42%–44% range, although a $25 million tariff-related credit inflated the reported figure. The normalized 44.4% margin was still a record and slightly exceeded the top of the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin reached 56.6% versus 32.1% a year ago, but this included a $25 million tariff-related credit; normalized margin was 44.4%, still a record high and above the 42%-44% guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | 42–44%”; the preview asked whether “44% hold[s].”

surprises.description: The U.S. returned to year-over-year growth, with sales up 3%, rather than remaining weak as the preview identified as a key test of whether the recovery was broad. Europe also grew 19%, though the preview did not set a specific Q2 expectation for Europe.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Regional growth was uneven, with Europe up 19% and the U.S. up only 3% in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “U.S. sales fell 3.7% in Q1 while Europe rose 25.6%. U.S. growth is the test of whether the recovery is broad.”

surprises.description: Wholesale point-of-sale demand was a strong additional signal not highlighted in the preview: global POS grew 6% in units in Q2 and 9% year to date, with Europe above 20%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wholesale point-of-sale trends were strong, with global POS up 6% in units in Q2 and 9% year-to-date, and European POS growth exceeding 20%.”

surprises.description: Funko reported that its ten largest franchises made up only about 32% of Q2 sales, presenting demand as broad-based rather than dependent on one property. The preview did not identify franchise concentration as an issue to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's top 10 franchises represented about 32% of Q2 sales, reflecting broad-based demand rather than dependence on any single property.”

surprises.description: Management highlighted potential freight and oil cost increases, alongside tariffs currently at 10%–12%, as downside risks to guidance. The preview discussed tariffs as a possible source of upside but did not flag freight or oil costs as risks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management flagged tariffs (currently 10%-12%) and potential freight/oil cost increases as key downside risks to guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “Management flagged tariffs running below plan, which is a possible source of upside,” and listed “tariff-refund commentary” as a catalyst.

surprises.description: Funko sold its IEEPA tariff claims for $19 million and used $15 million of the proceeds to repay debt. This specific claims sale and debt repayment were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company sold its IEEPA tariff claims for $19 million in proceeds and used funds to pay down $15 million of debt, continuing deleveraging.”

surprises.description: Funko announced that Kristin Hamilton would become Chief Commercial Officer starting August 24, an executive appointment not mentioned in the preview. The supplied facts do not indicate whether the appointment changes the company’s outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[Management] announced a new Chief Commercial Officer, Kristin Hamilton, starting August 24.”

in_line: Full-year net sales guidance was reiterated at flat to up 3%, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Cash was about $10 million at June 30, above the preview’s $7.5 million base-case expectation and its $6.5 million downside threshold. That is a better-than-expected cash position despite the decline from year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash, equivalents and marketable securities declined to approximately $10 million as of June 30, 2026, from $11.6 million at year-end 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “cash near $7.5M” in the base scenario; “Cash below $6.5M or a concurrent offering” in the bear scenario.

surprises.description: Management raised its full-year revenue outlook to growth above 30%, rather than merely reaffirming the roughly 30% outlook the preview treated as the base case. The new outlook requires roughly $23 million of revenue in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to greater than 30% growth over 2025, implying roughly $23 million of revenue needed in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY ~30% reaffirmed” in the base scenario; “A raise is the bull trigger.”

surprises.description: The adjusted EBITDA loss was $1.8 million, wider than the preview’s $1.4 million estimate, even though it narrowed from Q1. The gap was $0.4 million versus the preview estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 26% year-over-year and 25% sequentially to $1.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA loss … Preview estimate ($1.4M).”

surprises.description: Prescription gammaCore revenue declined about 4% sequentially, whereas the preview’s $8.2 million VA prescription revenue base case implied growth from Q1’s $7.9 million. The call did not provide a dollar figure for this revenue line.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Prescription gammaCore revenue grew about 11% year-over-year but declined roughly 4% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “VA prescription revenue. $7.9M in Q1, up 48% YoY. Base case is about $8.2M.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed that its top 15 VA accounts generated 54% of Q2 VA revenue, an unflagged degree of account concentration that leaves revenue exposed to a small number of accounts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The top 15 VA accounts produced 54% of Q2 VA revenue.”

surprises.description: A staffing backlog at one facility pushed roughly $145,000 of revenue into Q3, creating a timing shortfall that the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A staffing backlog at one facility pushed roughly $145,000 into Q3.”

surprises.description: Management said it is targeting positive adjusted EBITDA by Q3 2027 using existing cash and without a dilutive raise, subject to operating leverage materializing. The preview emphasized financing risk but did not anticipate this specific profitability timeline or no-raise target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is targeting positive adjusted EBITDA by Q3 2027 using existing cash without a dilutive capital raise, assuming projected operating leverage materializes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management … is evaluating capital resources, including its existing shelf and ATM.”

surprises.description: Management outlined specific cost-reduction goals that were not in the preview: lower sales incentives as a share of prescription revenue, a lower sales-and-marketing expense ratio, and G&A savings from consolidating federal contracts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sales incentive expense [is expected] to fall from about 35% to 27% of prescription revenue and total sales and marketing expense to reach roughly 54% by end of 2027, while consolidating federal contracts under Lovell to cut about 3% of G&A.”

surprises.description: The company added 17 independent sales reps covering 29 VA medical centers and doubled its sales regions from three to six at minimal incremental cost—an expansion of VA coverage not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company added 17 new 1099 sales reps covering 29 VA medical centers (about 20% of the network) and doubled sales regions from three to six with minimal incremental cost.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $9.5 million was essentially in line with the $9.494 million consensus estimate, although below the preview’s $10.0 million estimate and its $9.9–$10.2 million base scenario.
Quell sales reached $1.3 million, just above the preview’s $1.2 million-or-more threshold.

surprises.description: The preview said Q3 sales needed to reach at least $15 million, with a path toward $17.5 million, but guidance was only about $13.5 million. That is below even the preview’s $14–16 million base-case range and weakens the expected trucking-driven ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for net sales of approximately $13.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 needs to guide to $15M+ with a path to $17.5M”; the base case also expected “Q3 guided $14–16M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was reported at 33.0%, well above the preview’s 22–25% expectation, but $1.1 million of tariff refunds boosted the figure. Excluding that benefit, gross margin would be about 24.7%, broadly in line with the preview’s range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 470 basis points to 33.0%, though this included a $1.1 million benefit from tariff refund payments recognized in cost of sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue near $13.2M should support 22–25%.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA is guided to worsen to a $2.4 million loss from Q2’s $1.6 million loss, despite the preview’s expectation of a higher Q3 sales trajectory supporting progress toward the $70 million annualized run rate. Management attributed the decline to temporary timing factors.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for…adjusted EBITDA of approximately negative $2.4 million, with the sequential EBITDA decline attributed to temporary timing factors.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 needs to guide to $15M+ with a path to $17.5M”; the preview also described $70 million annualized sales as the positive adjusted EBITDA marker.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $13.2 million, matching company guidance but falling short of the $13.8 million consensus cited in the preview. The consensus gap was about $0.6 million, or roughly 4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales were $13.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed company guidance of “~$13.2M” and consensus of “$13.8M.”

surprises.description: The lenders deferred senior leverage and fixed charge coverage covenant compliance until September 2027, extending the relief beyond the covenant waiver period the preview described through December 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lenders…deferred senior leverage and fixed charge coverage covenant compliance until September 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described covenants as “waived through 12/31/26.”
