surprises.description: The preview treated Dakota Lithium as a post-quarter acquisition and looked for a FY27 contribution outlook; the call instead said it should contribute meaningful revenue and become adjusted-EBITDA accretive as soon as Q4 2026, with limited added operating expense.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Dakota Lithium is expected to begin contributing meaningful revenue and become accretive to adjusted EBITDA in Q4 2026 with limited incremental operating expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist asked for “an explicit FY27 contribution number and the working-capital cost of restocking inventory.”

surprises.description: The call described a potential trucking opportunity beyond the Stevens order the preview focused on: Stevens’ plan is to convert its full 2,500-truck fleet, while Werner and other carriers are also advancing through the pipeline. These additional opportunities were not part of the preview’s stated trucking expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Stevens Transport shipments have begun as the first phase of a plan to convert its full fleet of 2,500 trucks, with Werner Enterprises and additional carriers advancing through the pipeline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on the “Stevens Transport order” across “about 500 trucks,” with deliveries starting in Q2.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was a $1.6 million loss, better than the company’s $1.9 million-loss guidance, although it was within the preview’s base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was negative $1.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Company guidance was “~$(1.9)M”; the preview’s base case was “$(1.5)M to $(2.5)M.”

in_line: Q2 net sales of $13.2 million matched company guidance of approximately $13.2 million, despite missing the higher consensus estimate.
Stevens Transport shipments began in Q2, as the preview expected deliveries to start during the quarter.
DTC sales were $4.5 million versus $3.7 million in Q1, addressing the preview’s concern about whether DTC would grow sequentially.
The company reiterated its positive adjusted EBITDA target at an approximately $70 million annualized sales run rate, which the preview had identified as a key target to watch.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue grew 5.6%, slightly below the preview’s 6.1% consensus growth estimate—about $78.0 million implied by the reported growth versus $78.4 million expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated Q2 2026 revenues grew 5.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $78.4M … [versus] $73.9M”; “Implied Y/Y +6.1%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA growth was strong, but the implied result of roughly $13.3 million was below the preview’s estimated $15–16 million and its roughly $15 million base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 19.5%”; the preview lists Q2 2025 adjusted EBITDA of $11.1 million, implying about $13.3 million for Q2 2026 at that growth rate.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … ~$15–16M implied by a back-solve”; base scenario: “~$15.0M.”

surprises.description: American Place accelerated sharply rather than continuing the slowdown investors were watching: revenue growth reached 13.4%, and the property set its best quarter ever and a new monthly gaming revenue record.
surprises.fact_evidence: “American Place revenues increased 13.4% to $34.8 million and adjusted property EBITDA rose 13.8% to $10.1 million, marking its best quarter ever”; it set a “monthly gaming revenue record of $12.7 million in May 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said growth had slowed to “+7.1% in Q1 26” and that “Anything below about +5% Y/Y raises questions.”

surprises.description: Chamonix improved substantially but was only approximately at break-even, short of the preview’s hoped-for significant positive Colorado contribution; the call did not establish that the overall West segment turned EBITDA-positive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Chamonix revenues grew nearly 12% but adjusted property EBITDA was only approximately break-even, improving $1.1 million year-over-year from a $1.2 million loss.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had promised “significant positive contributions” from Colorado in summer; “A positive West segment EBITDA would be a first and the clearest operational proof point.”

surprises.description: The financing had not yet closed and was still being documented, with no specific financing terms reported; the only cost indication was that all-in borrowing costs would be in the high single digits. The expected Q3 close gives a timeline, but the key financing details remained unresolved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The complex refinancing … is still being documented but expected to close in Q3 2026, with all-in borrowing costs anticipated in the high single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called financing the “most important item” and said to listen for “size, coupon, whether terms are committed or indicative”; its base case anticipated financing “described as ‘progressing.’”

surprises.description: An unexpected 42-hour power outage turned Rising Star from a $500,000 year-earlier profit into a $100,000 quarterly loss, and management said no business-interruption insurance recovery was expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rising Star lost $100,000 in the quarter due to a 42-hour power outage from a downed power line, versus a $500,000 profit a year earlier, with no business interruption insurance recovery expected.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed substantial conditional upside at Chamonix: win per position per day is about half the Blackhawk average, while matching that average is associated with roughly $30 million of annual EBITDA and a 15% premium with up to $40 million. This was not part of the preview’s expectations and remains a target, not current performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Chamonix's win per position per day is only about $175, roughly half the Blackhawk average of $330, with management targeting roughly $30 million of annual EBITDA at the Blackhawk average and up to $40 million at a 15% premium.”

surprises.description: The company received city approval to keep the temporary Waukegan structure operating as an event center for five years after the permanent casino opens, creating an additional use beyond the temporary casino period discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gained city approval to retain the temporary structure as an event center for five years after the permanent casino opens.”

surprises.description: Management said the permanent casino should lift American Place margins from about 29% toward the mid-30s once rent and temporary-facility costs are removed; the preview discussed the project’s cost and timing but not this margin uplift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The permanent Waukegan casino is budgeted at roughly $302 million … and should lift American Place margins from about 29% currently toward the mid-30s once rent and temporary costs are eliminated.”

surprises.description: Silver Slipper held EBITDA flat despite slightly lower revenue, which management attributed to eliminating unprofitable business and described as a stable cash-cow performance; the preview did not discuss this property.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Silver Slipper produced flat EBITDA of $3.4 million in both years' quarters as revenues declined slightly from eliminating unprofitable business, with management viewing it as a stable cash cow.”

in_line: The Waukegan temporary facility’s extension to February 2029 was already flagged in the preview as approved by the IGB; the call’s report of legislative and gaming board approval through February 2029 was consistent with that expectation.
The permanent Waukegan project’s roughly $302 million budget and expected opening around Q3 2028 were broadly consistent with the preview’s $302 million project cost and mid-2028 target.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $45.5 million, well above the preview’s implied $35–36 million consensus and the $40 million high end of guidance. The roughly $2 million tariff refund helped, but EBITDA was still about $43.5 million excluding it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $45.5 million (including ~$2 million of IEEPA tariff refunds) beat the high end of guidance by roughly $5 million”; margin was 12.7% and 12.2% ex-refund.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$35–36M (implied)” and company guidance of “$32M – $40M.”

surprises.description: The company raised its FY2026 sales outlook above the prior range, while narrowing EBITDA guidance to $176–196 million. The new outlook implies lower margins than the February framework, rather than the substantial H2 margin ramp the preview said the old guide required.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year net sales guidance to $1.42–$1.47 billion and narrowed adjusted EBITDA guidance to $176–$196 million”; implied full-year margin was cut to “approximately 12.4%–13.3% from the 13.1%–14.3% framework given in February.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 (reaffirmed at Q1): net sales $1.328–1.416B; adj. EBITDA $174–203M”; the preview said the guide might be reaffirmed, narrowed, or cut, and that it implied “H2 adj. EBITDA margin of roughly 15–19% versus H1 near 10%.”

surprises.description: Input-cost pressure was more pronounced than the preview’s cost-out-focused discussion suggested: steel, aluminum, freight, and fuel costs are nearly $20 million above plan, with about $15 million expected in H2 and no cost relief assumed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Incremental external input cost inflation (steel, aluminum, freight, fuel) is running nearly $20 million above plan, with about $15 million expected in the second half,” and the company “is not underwriting any commodity or freight cost relief.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The FY guide implies H2 adj. EBITDA margin of roughly 15–19% versus H1 near 10%, on lower revenue. This depends almost entirely on cost-out.”

surprises.description: The savings program appears to be progressing much faster in the first half than its Q1 pace suggested: it captured over $25 million in gross savings in H1 and remains on track for about $50 million for the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The profit optimization program captured over $25 million of gross savings in the first half and remains on track for approximately $50 million in gross savings for the full year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that Q1 “delivered only ‘mid-single-digit millions’” against the $50 million target and said to “demand a cumulative savings figure.”

surprises.description: Powersports was a much stronger source of demand than the preview discussed, growing 22.5% in Q2 and 28% in the first half as OEMs worked through channel inventory imbalances.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Powersports grew 22.5% in Q2 and 28% in the first half year-over-year as OEMs worked through channel inventory imbalances, becoming a stabilizing force.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $358.1 million came in above the $353.1 million consensus and at the high end of company guidance, though it was within the preview’s base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $358.1 million … landing at the high end of the guided range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales $353.1M” consensus and “$343M – $365M” company guidance; the base scenario was “$353–358M.”

surprises.description: AAG’s margin improved despite lower sales and the F-150 supply disruption, but the disruption is expected to persist into Q3 before resolving in early-to-mid September.
surprises.fact_evidence: AAG sales fell 4%, including a “~$5.5 million Phoenix divestiture impact,” while adjusted EBITDA margin improved “~70 bps year-over-year and ~500 bps sequentially”; the Ford F-150 aluminum disruption is “now expected to resolve in early-to-mid September.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said whether the “Ford F-150 aluminum disruption … extends into Q3 matters” and noted management had said Q1–Q2 volume was unrecoverable.

surprises.description: The balance sheet and inventory position improved from the Q1 figures highlighted in the preview: debt declined sequentially, leverage edged lower, and days inventory fell from about 150 to 136.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage was 3.7x against a 5x covenant, total debt declined $20.5 million sequentially to $667.7 million, days inventory improved to ~136 from ~150 days.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Total debt $688.2M, leverage about 3.77x” and flagged the “Balance sheet and FCF” as a key issue.

surprises.description: The company disclosed potential additional recovery of prior tariff costs that is not included in its guidance, creating an upside possibility beyond the reported Q2 refund.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company may recover up to $8 million of additional prior tariff costs not included in guidance.”

surprises.description: SSG sales were still down year over year, although the segment rebounded sequentially and management expects bike to be flat versus the prior year. The bike outlook points toward stabilization, but the reported segment result did not show a year-over-year inflection.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SSG net sales fell 9.4% year-over-year to $124.3 million but rose 12.5% sequentially, with segment margin held essentially flat despite the revenue decline; bike is expected to be flat versus prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “SSG inflection” and said, “Any move to flat or positive is the bull's best evidence.”

in_line: The company’s stated flat-versus-prior-year bike outlook is consistent with the preview’s focus on stabilization in SSG, even though reported total SSG sales remained down year over year.

surprises.description: The preview looked for AI growth to hold near the existing >40% full-year commitment and put AI ARR around $140–150M. Five9 reported AI revenue growth of 78% and an annual run rate above $150M, then raised its full-year AI growth outlook to at least 60% because backlog customers are ramping earlier than forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI revenue grew 78% year-over-year to approximately $39 million (over $150 million annual run rate)” and management “raised full-year 2026 AI growth guidance to at least 60% year-over-year, up from a prior outlook of more than 40%, driven by backlog customers ramping earlier than forecasted.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for an AI ARR figure at or above roughly $140–150M and growth holding near the >40% FY commitment.”

surprises.description: The preview cited roughly $313M as the Q3 consensus and an implied path near $318M. Five9 guided to a $319M midpoint, above both reference points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue is guided to a $319 million midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Street's next-quarter figure of roughly $313M” and “implying Q3 near $318M”; the base scenario expected “Q3 guided $312–317M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected Q2 revenue of $306.6M and company guidance of $303–309M. Five9 reported $312M, exceeding consensus and the top of its guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached $312 million, up 10% year-over-year and above the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Company guidance ... $303.0M – $309.0M | Consensus $306.6M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected a Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin around 23–24%. Five9 reported 22%, and adjusted gross margin was also down year over year; management attributed the pressure to temporary professional-services capacity expansion for accelerated AI deployments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin fell to 61% from 63% a year ago and adjusted EBITDA margin declined to 22% from 24%, pressured by temporary expansion of professional services capacity to meet accelerated AI deployments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin ... Consensus ~23–24% (derived).”

surprises.description: The preview expected the FY2026 revenue midpoint to remain at $1.260B and emphasized that a raise mattered. Five9 raised the midpoint to $1.266B, a modest increase that reached the top of its prior guidance range but remained below the preview's bull-scenario threshold of $1.270B.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to a $1.266 billion midpoint (from $1.26 billion prior).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance ... Revenue $1.254–1.266B (midpoint $1.260B)” and “Raise versus reaffirm matters more than the Q2 beat”; the bull scenario specified “FY raised to ≥$1.270B.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged CCaaS growth of 8% as a key reference point. Reported growth was 7%, although concurrent agent seats grew roughly in line and subscription revenue per seat increased in the single digits, indicating no seat compression.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CCaaS revenue grew a stable 7% year-over-year, with concurrent agent seat count growing roughly in line and subscription revenue per seat increasing in the single digits, showing no seat compression.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Subscription-only DBRR at 107% (up from 106%) and CCaaS at +8% show whether AI is adding to wallet share or substituting for seats.”

surprises.description: The preview did not identify a large new customer win of this scale. Five9 announced a Fortune 100 financial-services contract expected to ramp to roughly $25M in subscription ARR, though it will contribute negligibly in 2026 and meaningfully from 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed a Fortune 100 financial services win with approximately $100 million total contract value over 5 years, expected to ramp to roughly $25 million in subscription ARR with negligible 2026 contribution and meaningful increases beginning in 2027.”

surprises.description: The preview cited Q1 subscription revenue growth of 13%, while Five9 reported 14% growth in Q2 and said this was the third consecutive quarter of acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subscription revenue [grew] 14% year-over-year for a third consecutive quarter of acceleration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Subscription revenue +13%” in Q1 FY2026.

in_line: Subscription-only dollar-based retention was 107%, matching the preview's 107% reference point.
Full-year 2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance remained at a $3.26 midpoint, matching the preview's stated midpoint.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $3.9 million, below the preview’s roughly $4.1 million consensus estimate. The 12 systems sold were within the expected range, so the revenue shortfall came despite unit sales landing as anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $3.9 million”; “The company sold 12 systems in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue and units vs. ~$4.1M and ~11–12 units.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 50.7%, just below the preview’s estimated 51–52% range and its key 51%+ threshold. The result was still above 50% for a fourth consecutive quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached 50.7% in Q2, expanding roughly 150 basis points year-over-year and marking the fourth consecutive quarter above 50%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~51–52% (my estimate)” and “Sustained 51%+ supports the pricing thesis.”

surprises.description: Q2 net cash burn excluding financing was $7.9 million, above the preview’s implied quarterly plan of roughly $6.5–7 million, though just below the preview’s stated level above which dilution risk would reopen. Full-year cash-burn guidance was maintained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net cash burn excluding financing improved to $7.9 million in Q2”; “full-year cash burn guidance maintained at $26-28 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Plan burn implies roughly $6.5–7M per quarter”; “Burn above ~$8M, or softer runway language, reopens dilution risk.”

surprises.description: Cash at quarter-end was $43.5 million, above the preview’s expected $34–35 million exit cash, because the company raised $10.6 million of net ATM proceeds. The added cash extends runway into 2028, but came from issuing shares.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company held $43.5 million in cash as of June 30, 2026, boosted by $10.6 million in net ATM proceeds raised at an average price of $1.52 per share, extending runway into 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A clean Q2 exits near $34–35M.”

surprises.description: The company reported an initial placement within one of the largest national IDNs in early July and expansion beyond first sites at other health systems. The preview flagged IDN wins as an important H2 bridge, but this provided concrete evidence of progress rather than only a potential opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company secured an initial placement within one of the largest national IDNs in early July and expanded beyond first sites at other health systems during Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Multi-unit hospital and IDN wins” were a key metric to watch; “Named or quantified wins are the most useful disclosure on the call.”

surprises.description: The Contrast PMR study was approximately 75% enrolled, with an FDA submission targeted by year-end 2026 to expand labeling to gadolinium-based contrast agents. The preview did not flag this specific regulatory and study milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Contrast PMR study enrollment is approximately 75% complete with an FDA submission targeted by year-end 2026 to expand labeling to gadolinium-based contrast agents, a key catalyst for the office vertical with higher-paying CPT codes.”

in_line: The 12 systems sold in Q2 were within the preview’s expected range of roughly 11–12.
Q2 EPS was -$0.09, matching the preview’s -$0.09 consensus estimate.
FY2026 revenue guidance was reiterated at $20–22 million, as the preview’s base scenario expected; the implied $12–14 million of second-half revenue was also consistent with the preview’s H2 bridge.
Full-year cash-burn guidance remained $26–28 million, as anticipated.

surprises.description: LOCO raised full-year system-wide comp guidance from 2%-4% to 3.5%-4.5%, a stronger outlook than the preview’s existing range. The lower end rose by 1.5 percentage points and the upper end by 0.5 point.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year system-wide comp sales guidance to 3.5%-4.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “System-wide comps: +2% to +4% (raised from +2% to +3%).”

surprises.description: Q3 comps were running at 5.8% through July 29, above the preview’s indications of a step-down in the second half. Management nevertheless guided to 3.5%-4.5% for the full quarter, explaining that July benefited unusually from World Cup advertising and that tougher comparisons were ahead.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3-to-date (through July 29) system-wide comparable sales accelerated to 5.8%, but management guided full Q3 comps to 3.5%-4.5%, citing outsized July benefit from World Cup advertising and tougher upcoming comparisons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management flagged a step-down to about 3% in H2.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance rose to $68-$70 million from $67.5-$69.5 million. This is a modest increase, though it did not exceed the preview’s highlighted $69.5 million upper-end threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $68-$70 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA: $67.5M to $69.5M.”

surprises.description: Capital spending guidance fell to $33-$37 million from the preview’s $37-$40 million range. Management attributed the reduction to remodel timing, so the change appears to reflect timing rather than a stated reduction in underlying project costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cut 2026 capital spending guidance to $33-$37 million due to remodel timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capex: $37M to $40M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.30, a one-cent beat against the $0.29 consensus estimate, although it was within the preview’s $0.30-$0.31 base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was more modest at $0.30 versus $0.28.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $0.29”; the preview’s base case was “$0.30 to $0.31.”

surprises.description: GAAP net income rose to $12.8 million, but a $6.3 million legal settlement materially boosted the result; adjusted EPS was only $0.30. The GAAP increase therefore substantially overstated the improvement in underlying earnings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income jumped to $12.8 million ($0.43/share) from $7.1 million ($0.24/share), largely boosted by a $6.3 million legal settlement, while adjusted EPS was more modest at $0.30 versus $0.28.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $0.29.”

surprises.description: Restaurant labor expense fell 90 basis points to 29.9% of restaurant sales, helped by wage inflation below 1% and lower health insurance and workers’ compensation costs. The preview did not flag this cost improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Labor expense improved 90 basis points to 29.9% of restaurant sales, aided by wage inflation under 1% in the quarter and lower health insurance and workers' comp costs.”

surprises.description: LOCO paid down $21 million on its revolver, leaving $30 million in debt, a capital-structure update not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Paid down $21 million on its revolver leaving $30 million in debt.”

surprises.description: The company extended its $150 million credit facility to 2031, but at a spread roughly 50 basis points higher. The longer facility term is favorable, while the higher spread raises borrowing costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Extended its $150 million credit facility to 2031 at a spread roughly 50 basis points higher.”

in_line: Q2 system-wide comps were 3.9%, within the preview’s cited 3%-4% company guide. Transactions declined 0.9%, consistent with the preview’s expectation of roughly flat-to-negative traffic if pricing ran near the comp.
Restaurant-level margin was 19.5%, at the top of the preview’s 19.0%-19.5% Q2 guide but not above the 19.5% level the preview identified as the most bullish outcome.
Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $19.1 million was within the preview’s implied $19-$20 million range.
Full-year restaurant margin guidance remained 18.25%-18.75%, matching the range in the preview.
The plan to open 18-20 restaurants in 2026 was reaffirmed, consistent with the preview’s 18-20 unit expectation and its focus on development outside California.

surprises.description: The preview anchored Q2 revenue at $478.3 million, while ICF reported $474.5 million, a small miss despite falling within the preview’s broader base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 total revenue was $474.5 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus: $478.3M.

surprises.description: The preview expected non-GAAP EPS of $1.69, but ICF reported $1.86, a sizable beat. The reported increase was helped by a much lower tax rate, lower interest expense, and a reduced share count.
surprises.fact_evidence: Non-GAAP EPS rose 12% year-over-year to $1.86, aided by a lower 17.8% tax rate (versus 21% prior year) that contributed a $0.11 non-GAAP EPS benefit, lower interest expense, and reduced share count.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Non-GAAP EPS consensus: $1.69.

surprises.description: The preview said federal revenue needed to rise to about $190 million or more to keep year-over-year growth by Q4 credible. Instead, federal revenue fell 9.5% year-over-year, a setback to that expected recovery path.
surprises.fact_evidence: A 9.5% year-over-year decline in federal revenue was offset by 6.6% growth in non-federal revenue.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Another gain to about $190M+ is needed to keep the path to Y/Y growth by Q4 credible.”

surprises.description: The preview treated a book-to-bill below 1.0 as a risk to backlog conversion. The in-quarter ratio was 0.85, and backlog slipped to $3.3 billion, although trailing 12-month book-to-bill remained above 1.0.
surprises.fact_evidence: The trailing 12-month book-to-bill was 1.09, but the in-quarter book-to-bill was only 0.85 and backlog slipped to $3.3 billion, driven primarily by slower federal procurement awards.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A reading below 1.0 would weaken the backlog-conversion story.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted commercial energy’s 10% full-year growth target and expected recovery from Q1’s delays. Instead, first-half growth was only about 3%, leaving mid-teens growth needed in the second half to reach the target.
surprises.fact_evidence: Commercial energy grew only about 3% in the first half, requiring mid-teens growth in the second half to hit the roughly 10% full-year target, with back-half-loaded performance fees and a strong pipeline cited as key drivers.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Grew 2% in Q1 (8.3% excluding delays) against a 10% full-year target.”

surprises.description: The preview cited a 20.5% full-year tax-rate assumption and noted that Q1’s higher tax rate affected the EPS ramp. Q2’s 17.8% rate was materially lower and added $0.11 to non-GAAP EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: The 17.8% tax rate contributed a $0.11 non-GAAP EPS benefit.
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY2026 guidance included a 20.5% tax rate; the preview also noted Q1’s 25.1% rate.

surprises.description: The preview identified international milestone timing as part of the expected recovery, but did not anticipate the scale of international government growth. That business rose 35%, with management also expecting double-digit international growth in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: International government revenue surged 35% year-over-year, driven by ramping EU and U.K. contracts won over the past 18 months, with management guiding to double-digit international growth in 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited timing shifts involving “commercial energy and international” and expected recovery of about $6 million in Q2, but gave no international growth estimate.

surprises.description: The preview described an $8.5 billion pipeline after Q1. By Q2 the pipeline had grown 9% sequentially to $9.3 billion, with about 60% in the identified growth markets.
surprises.fact_evidence: The business development pipeline grew 9% sequentially to $9.3 billion, with key growth markets comprising roughly $5.5 billion, or 60%, of that total.

surprises.description: The preview said an unquantified guidance reaffirmation could be a concern and that quantified evidence would be needed. Management reaffirmed the existing ranges and said more than 90% of the revenue needed for the year was already in backlog.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance and said more than 90% of the revenue needed was already in backlog.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A reaffirmation with quantified evidence would be needed. An unquantified reaffirmation risks a negative reaction.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged a possible pause in buybacks as a negative signal. Instead, ICF repurchased a first-half record number of shares and lowered its full-year weighted-average share-count guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company repurchased approximately 435,000 shares in the first half (a first-half record) and lowered its full-year weighted average share count guidance to 18.2 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A pause in buybacks would be a negative signal.” The preview also reported Q1 repurchases of 217,500 shares.

surprises.description: The preview mentioned acquisition interest in commercial energy but did not provide an expectation for debt or leverage. ICF reported lower net debt and leverage, with leverage expected to fall further by year-end, supporting disciplined tuck-in acquisitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net debt fell to $403 million from $457 million a year earlier, cutting adjusted leverage to 2.06 with expectations of under 1.6 by year-end, positioning the company to pursue disciplined tuck-in acquisitions focused on commercial energy.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had signaled acquisition interest in commercial energy.

in_line: ICF reaffirmed its full-year 2026 revenue, GAAP EPS, and non-GAAP EPS guidance ranges, as the preview’s base case anticipated.
Adjusted EBITDA margin was 11.2%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that margins would remain near 11.1%–11.2%; the company remained on track for its full-year margin-expansion target.
The quarterly dividend remained $0.14, matching the preview’s stated dividend.

surprises.description: iRhythm reported Q2 revenue of $224.2 million, above the preview’s $219.33 million consensus and $218–220 million company guide. The result also exceeded the preview’s base scenario of $221–223 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $224.2 million, up 20.1% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 consensus: $219.33M”; “Q2'26 company guide: $218–220M”; base scenario: “Revenue $221–223M.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin was 19.3%, far above the preview’s 11.5–12.5% guide and its implied $25–27 million of adjusted EBITDA. This was a much larger margin beat than the preview’s 12% threshold for supporting the full-year outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $43.3 million or 19.3% of revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin: 11.5–12.5%”; “~$25–27M implied”; “Adj. EBITDA margin of 12% or better in Q2.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 72.8%, well above the preview’s roughly 71% expectation and above even its 71.5% bull-case threshold, putting the quarter close to the 2027 target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached 72.8%, up 160 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin: ~71%+”; bull scenario: “GM ≥71.5%”; the preview also flagged progress toward the “73% 2027 target.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $880–890 million from $875–885 million, but the new midpoint is $885 million, below the preview’s stated $890 million threshold for a clear positive. The increase is positive, but less decisive than that expectation suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $880 million-$890 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A FY raise to at least $890M would read as a clear positive”; the preview said the buy-side was “positioned for a raise to about $890M.”

surprises.description: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance rose to 13–14% from 12–13%, exceeding the preview’s expected range rather than merely supporting it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[The company] raised full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 13%-14%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance … adj. EBITDA margin 12.0–13.0%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was positive $0.58 per diluted share, versus the preview’s consensus loss of $0.04 per share. The preview cautioned that EPS submissions mixed GAAP and adjusted figures, but the reported adjusted profit was still substantially better than that consensus figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS improved to net income of $0.58 per diluted share versus an adjusted net loss of $0.32 per share in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS … consensus: ($0.04)”; the preview noted that “the ($0.04) EPS consensus mixes GAAP and adjusted submissions.”

surprises.description: iRhythm agreed to acquire Vital Connect, which has an approximately $65 million annual revenue run rate, with a positive revenue-growth contribution expected beginning in 2027. The preview did not anticipate the acquisition; the disclosed $50 million equity component implies less than 1.5% dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “iRhythm agreed to acquire Vital Connect, currently at an approximately $65 million annual revenue run rate … with the deal expected to close by year-end and positively contribute to revenue growth beginning in 2027”; it will be “funded partly with $50 million in equity … or less than 1.5% dilution.”

surprises.description: The company generated record positive free cash flow of $37.5 million, an unexpected improvement given the preview’s discussion of roughly $33 million of negative free cash flow in Q1 and seasonal working-capital effects.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was a record positive $37.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported “Free cash flow about ($33M) on seasonal working-capital and comp timing” for Q1, but did not give a Q2 expectation.

surprises.description: The company agreed to pay $50 million to settle the Baxter/Welch Allyn/Bardy Diagnostics litigation, a one-off cash obligation the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company agreed to settle its Baxter/Welch Allyn/Bardy Diagnostics litigation for a $50 million settlement payment on July 31.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that FDA clearance of the third-generation algorithm is expected to cut clinical technician review time by as much as 50% and produce about $100 million of cumulative cost savings over five years. The preview anticipated a later-2026 algorithm clearance but did not identify these operational and cost benefits or the stated first-half 2027 launch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FDA clearance of the third-generation algorithm is expected to reduce clinical technician review time by as much as 50% and generate approximately $100 million of cumulative cost savings over five years upon its first-half 2027 launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Next-generation deep-learning algorithm 510(k): Clearance is expected later in 2026.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed the 15% adjusted EBITDA margin target for 2027, consistent with the preview’s 2027 framework of approximately 15%.

surprises.description: Q2 net loss attributable to common stockholders was about $1.3 million, far below the preview’s modeled $5.2–5.9 million loss. The improvement was driven in part by Australian R&D rebates that management said are not expected to recur at this level over the next 12 months.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss attributable to common stockholders fell to approximately $1.3 million”; R&D expenses “swung to a benefit of roughly $0.8 million,” driven mainly by additional Australian R&D rebates “that are not expected to recur at that level over the next 12 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full preview's own model: Q2 EPS –$0.20 to –$0.23, net loss $5.2–5.9M.”

surprises.description: The UK filing had not been submitted, and management now expects it at the end of Q3 or early Q4, later than the preview’s early-Q3 timing. The preview also cited an FDA BLA in Q4 2026, while management now expects a Q1 2027 submission.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expects to submit the Ebstracell marketing authorization application to the UK MHRA…by end of Q3 or early Q4 2026,” followed by “a US BLA in Q1 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance walked from ‘mid-summer 2026’ to ‘early Q3 2026’ for the UK MHRA MAA filing”; “Confirm the FDA BLA timing” against the Q1 release’s “FDA BLA in Q4 2026.”

surprises.description: The Phase 2 MINDFUL study reported a statistically significant white-matter myelin MRI biomarker effect for XPro, including a larger effect in the biomarker-enriched group. The preview focused on the next XPro trial’s design, timing, and funding, and did not anticipate this efficacy result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Statistically significant treatment effect on white matter myelin MRI biomarkers (p=0.0028, Cohen's effect size 0.46), rising to 0.59 in the biomarker-enriched population.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “XPro Phase 2b/3 in early Alzheimer's. Design, start date, and funding.”

surprises.description: Management extended the expected operating runway into Q2 2027, beyond the previously stated runway through Q1 2027. It also disclosed a plan to raise capital in small ATM increments through the end of 2027, leaving a continuing dilution consideration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expects existing resources to fund operations into Q2 2027”; management plans to “raise capital in small increments via its ATM through the end of 2027,” emphasizing dilution sensitivity.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “Watch for runway extended past Q1 2027, any ATM use in the 10-Q”; for the large XPro trial, it said management’s answer on “partner, dilute, or delay matters most.”

surprises.description: The MHRA formally aligned with the company across CMC, non-clinical, and clinical questions, which management said materially de-risked the filing path. The preview noted prior advice and the PIP approval but still framed whether the filing was on track or slipping as an open question.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The MHRA confirmed formal alignment across all CMC, non-clinical, and clinical questions from the May 12th pre-MAA meeting” and “materially de-risk[ed] the filing path.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “No submission press release had appeared… Filed on the call, or slipping?”

surprises.description: Management gave a concrete confirmatory Phase 3 plan for Ebstracell: an open-label study of roughly 40–45 patients, with data expected around mid-2028. Having 33 patients already lined up supports enrollment, but the preview did not provide this study plan or its timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The confirmatory open-label Phase 3 trial will enroll roughly 40-45 patients (33 already lined up, mostly prior trial participants), run 18 months, and produce data around mid-2028.”

surprises.description: Management introduced a specific commercial outlook for Ebstracell: £400,000–£500,000 per child per year and a goal of about 100 UK patients within two years of approval. The preview did not discuss pricing or a patient uptake target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Priced Ebstracell at an expected £400,000-£500,000 per child per year and projects reaching roughly 100 UK patients within two years of approval.”

surprises.description: Management highlighted that a US accelerated approval could generate a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher, citing recent secondary-market sales of $150–200 million and saying proceeds would fund platform expansion. This potential source of funding was not raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A US accelerated approval would carry a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher,” which management said “recently sold for $150-200 million in the secondary market,” with proceeds “earmarked to fund platform expansion.”

in_line: Cash of approximately $18.4 million at June 30 was broadly in line with the preview’s $16–18 million estimate; including the subsequent $4.2 million rebate gives about $22.6 million, close to the preview’s $20–22 million pro forma estimate.

surprises.description: ICU Medical reported adjusted EPS of $2.37, far above the preview’s roughly $1.91–$1.92 expectation. The gap was about 24% versus consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose 13% year-over-year to $2.37.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS $1.91”; management’s Q2 frame was “~$1.92.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year adjusted EPS and EBITDA guidance rather than merely narrowing the EPS range as the preview’s base case anticipated. The new EPS range also exceeds the preview’s stated buy-side expectation of $8.10–$8.45.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $8.60-$9.00 (from $7.75-$8.45) and adjusted EBITDA to $415M-$435M (from $400M-$430M).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said buy-side expectations leaned toward “narrowing the EPS range toward the upper half ($8.10–$8.45)” and described the base case as a guide “narrowed upward but not raised.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $548 million exceeded the preview’s estimates of $533.4 million and approximately $538 million, although reported growth was only 1% because of the IV Solutions JV deconsolidation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $548 million, up 6% organically but only 1% reported due to the mid-2025 Otsuka JV deconsolidation of IV Solutions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus was “$533.4M” or “~$538M implied by ‘-2% Y/Y’.”

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted gross-margin outlook was raised to around 41.5%, a stronger outlook than the preview’s concern that Q1’s roughly 41% margin might not repeat. The preview’s 40.5%–41% estimate was for Q2, so it is not a directly comparable annual forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted gross margin guidance was raised to around 41.5%,” with “a remaining ~200 basis points of margin opportunity targeted from plant consolidations, pricing, and mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1’s “~41% was called mix-favorable and may not repeat” and identified Q2 adjusted gross margin “at or above 40.5%” as a watch point.

surprises.description: The record IV Systems pump quarter was partly driven by installations occurring earlier than expected, which management said would reduce growth later in the year. That tempers the preview’s focus on whether the record pump run would continue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “IV Systems grew 12% organically to a record pump quarter, but this was inflated by earlier-than-expected installations that will reduce later-year growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “whether the record pump run continues against a tougher sequential comp” as an issue to watch.

surprises.description: Management indicated that overall organic growth would be at or above 6% in Q3, with both Consumables and IV Systems reaching record revenues. The preview did not set out this Q3 growth or revenue outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects overall organic growth at or above 6% in Q3, with Consumables (up 5% organic) and IV Systems both hitting record revenues.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed continuing annual incremental tariff costs of $30–$40 million, a specific ongoing headwind not quantified in the preview, which mentioned $10 million of tariff expense in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ICU still faces $30-$40 million in annual incremental tariffs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Tariff expense $10M (~2% of adj. revenue)” in Q1, but gave no annual incremental tariff estimate.

surprises.description: Management disclosed an approximately $60 million negative currency impact over four years from the Costa Rican colon, Mexican peso, and Japanese yen, a headwind not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A roughly $60 million negative currency impact over four years from the Costa Rican colon, Mexican peso, and Japanese yen.”

surprises.description: ICU repaid $50 million of debt and remained on track to reach its roughly 2x net-leverage target by year-end. The preview did not flag this debt-repayment progress as an expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ICU repaid $50 million of debt in Q2, lowering net leverage to 2.3x and remaining on track to reach its ~2x leverage target by year-end.”

surprises.description: The company received $20 million in tariff refunds that were excluded from non-GAAP results but included in free cash flow, with the possibility of smaller additional refunds later. This provides an unanticipated cash-flow benefit, though it does not boost reported non-GAAP earnings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received $20 million in tariff refunds (excluded from non-GAAP results but included in free cash flow), with potential for smaller additional refunds later.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “~$150M” full-year free-cash-flow target and $28 million of Q1 free cash flow, but did not mention tariff refunds.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $110 million, above the preview’s modeled range of roughly $103–$108 million, though the beat was smaller than the EPS beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 10% to $110 million at a 20% margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s model estimate was “~$103–108M.”

surprises.description: Management said the pump upgrade and replacement cycle has not begun in earnest and is expected more in 2027; current IV Systems strength is mostly from competitive wins. The preview asked about installed-base conversion but did not anticipate this timing clarification.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pump upgrade/replacement cycle has not yet begun in earnest (expected more in 2027), meaning current systems strength stems mostly from competitive wins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked for “any commentary on installed-base conversion to consumables” and flagged Plum Duo / Plum Solo timing, but did not state that the broader upgrade/replacement cycle would begin in 2027.

in_line: Consumables organic growth was 5%, in line with the preview’s expectation that Q1 softness would reverse to historical mid-single-digit growth; the preview said 4% or more would support the thesis.

IV Systems delivered the record pump quarter the preview identified as a possible continuation of Q1 momentum, though the earlier-than-expected installations that temper later-year growth are a separate surprise.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $1.1 million, well below the preview’s $1.7–2.0 million analyst range and $1.84 million consensus. The shortfall was attributed to lower Roche collaboration revenue and the prior-year VAC termination.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenues fell to $1.1 million from $2.8 million a year earlier, driven by lower collaboration revenue under the Roche agreement and the prior-year VAC termination.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $1.84M”; analyst view “$1.7–2.0M.”

surprises.description: Cash was higher than the preview’s $46–49 million estimate, and management extended the expected runway by one quarter, into Q3 2028 rather than Q2 2028. This was better than the preview’s expectation of reaffirming the existing runway.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lineage ended Q2 2026 … with $50.8 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, which is expected to fund operations into the third quarter of 2028, one quarter longer than the prior runway.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash + marketable securities … $46–49M”; company guidance: “Operations are funded into Q2 2028.”

surprises.description: Instead of the expected GAAP loss, Lineage reported a small profit. The reversal was primarily due to a noncash warrant-liability remeasurement gain and the absence of the prior-year VAC impairment, rather than stronger operating performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income of $1.5 million ($0.01 basic EPS) versus a net loss of $30.5 million ($0.13 loss per share) a year earlier,” primarily due to “a noncash warrant liability remeasurement gain” and “the absence of a prior-year $14.8 million VAC impairment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP EPS | ($0.03)”; analyst view “($0.01) to ($0.03).”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a $4.6 million ATM raise shortly before quarter-end, a financing disclosure the preview identified as a downside risk. The higher-than-expected cash balance and extended runway temper, but do not erase, the dilution implication.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised approximately $4.6 million via its ATM on June 26 … at a weighted average price of $1.28 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Shortened runway language or ATM/financing disclosure is the primary downside risk”; the bear scenario also listed “ATM usage.”

surprises.description: Management raised the possibility of shifting OPC1 toward chronic spinal-cord-injury patients, citing their greater prevalence and more reliable trial baselines. The preview flagged chronic-patient data to watch, but did not anticipate this potential change in the program’s patient focus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management indicated it may shift the OPC1 spinal cord injury program toward chronic patients, who are roughly 10x more prevalent than subacute patients and provide more reliable trial baselines, with all current DOSED study candidates being chronic patients.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “OPC1 (spinal cord injury) FDA comparability package. Management guided to filing later in 2026. Watch the timing and any 12-month chronic data.”

surprises.description: Management gave a before-year-end update timeframe for the ILT1 diabetes islet-cell program, adding a near-term program-update catalyst that the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expects updates on the ILT1 diabetes islet-cell program before year-end.”

in_line: Total operating expenses were about $10.0 million ($4.8 million R&D plus $5.2 million G&A), at the top end of the preview’s $9.4–10.0 million analyst view.

The reported warrant mechanics and potential Roche/Genentech milestones remained contingent on a public decision to advance OpRegen; the supplied facts do not state a time-bound controlled-trial decision, consistent with the preview’s base case.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $6.0 million, well above the preview’s derived $4.95–5.15 million base range and even its $5.35–5.5 million bull range. It also rose about 15% sequentially, reversing the seasonal decline the preview said was normal to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $6 million,” up 36% year-over-year and approximately 15% sequentially.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: $4.95–5.15M”; “Bull: $5.35–5.5M”; the preview also said, “A sequential decline from $5.21M is normal.”

surprises.description: The reported 67% gross margin was far above the preview’s 58.5–60% base range, but the apparent recovery was largely a timing effect: about nine percentage points came from a tariff refund, most of which related to prior periods. Excluding that distortion, underlying margin was around 58% and remained pressured by tariffs, the stronger euro, shipping costs, and lower-margin service revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported gross margin rose to 67% from 63%”; roughly $500,000 of the $600,000 tariff refund related to prior periods, “inflating this quarter’s margin by about 9 percentage points.” Only about $100,000 related to Q2 sales, and underlying margin remained pressured.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base” gross margin was “58.5–60%”; the preview said “58.5%” or higher would support a recovery case and “61%+” was the bull scenario.

surprises.description: Core programmatic product revenue grew about 27%, above the preview’s 20% warning threshold and faster than the 23% growth reported for Q1. That strengthens the recurring-reorder story beyond the preview’s stated concern about possible deceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Programmatic product revenue grew approximately 27% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said programmatic revenue grew “23% Y/Y in Q1” and that “Deceleration below about 20% would undercut the recurring-reorder story.”

surprises.description: Profitability was much stronger than the preview’s modest $0.01 diluted EPS estimate might suggest: the call reported approximately $1.2 million of net income and $1.3 million of adjusted EBITDA. The call facts do not give actual diluted EPS, so the precise EPS beat cannot be established from the material provided.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income surged over 400% to approximately $1.2 million” and “adjusted EBITDA rose 260% to roughly $1.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted): $0.01.”

surprises.description: Cash rose to $4.7 million rather than drawing down toward the levels the preview identified as concerning. The company also remained debt-free.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash grew to approximately $4.7 million as of June 30, 2026 (up from $4 million at March 31), and the company remains debt-free.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a “further sequential draw toward $3.0M would raise financing questions” and listed “Cash vs. $3.5M” as a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: Despite the higher cash balance and strong reported earnings, first-half operating cash flow was negative as receivables and inventory grew. This is a weaker cash-conversion picture than the headline balance alone suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half operating cash flow turned negative at negative $990,000 due to rising receivables and inventory.”

surprises.description: The record revenue growth came overwhelmingly from expansion within existing customers rather than new sites, while the total customer count was only slightly above the prior quarter. That leaves the preview’s question about traction from the new Greater New York sales effort unresolved in the reported facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Growth was driven overwhelmingly by expansion within existing customers rather than new sites, with total customer count at 1,724, only slightly above the prior quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “NYC region traction” as a catalyst, noting the new Greater New York sales leader and a cited “$25M annual addressable opportunity.”

surprises.description: Service-only revenue nearly tripled, an unforecasted source of growth that also contributed to the lower-margin mix weighing on underlying gross margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Service-only revenue nearly tripled year-over-year as customers increasingly rely on Nephros for installation, replacement, and ongoing support”; the call also said lower-margin service revenue pressured underlying margin.

surprises.description: Halozyme reported Q2 revenue of $481 million, about 20% above the $402.3 million consensus and well above the preview’s $425 million bull-case threshold. The 48% year-over-year growth also greatly exceeded the preview’s implied 23% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue grew 48% year-over-year to $481 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q2'26 Consensus | $402.3M”; the bull scenario was “≥$425M.”

surprises.description: Royalty revenue was $308 million, roughly 10% above the preview’s implied $280 million consensus and above its $295 million bull-case level. The preview identified royalties as the leading debate and said a result below about $270 million would be a clear negative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Royalty revenue of $308 million (up 50% YoY)”; DARZALEX royalties were “$152.2 million (up 27%)” and VYVGART Hytrulo royalties “surged 143% to $72.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Royalty revenue | ~$280M (implied)”; bull scenario “≥$295M”; “a royalty print below about $270M would be a clear negative surprise.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS and adjusted EBITDA both substantially exceeded the preview’s estimates: EPS was $2.28 versus $1.79, and EBITDA was $328.8 million versus about $245 million. EBITDA margin was above 65%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA rose 46% to $328.8 million with a margin above 65%, and non-GAAP EPS reached $2.28.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS | $1.79”; “Adj. EBITDA | ~$245M (implied).”

surprises.description: Halozyme raised its full-year revenue, royalty, and EPS guidance well above the previously reiterated ranges, rather than merely reiterating or modestly narrowing them. The new midpoint is about 6% higher for revenue, 7% higher for royalties, and 10% higher for EPS than the old midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 guidance to total revenue of $1.835-1.91 billion,” royalty revenue of “$1.22-1.245 billion,” and non-GAAP diluted EPS of “$8.65-9.00.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior guidance was revenue “$1.710–1.810B,” royalties “$1.130–1.170B,” and EPS “$7.75–8.25.” The preview said, “Whether management raises FY26 guidance or only reiterates it,” and that “Reiteration would be a disappointment.”

surprises.description: Halozyme disclosed five collaboration and licensing agreements in 2026 and $35.5 million in upfront collaboration revenue, split roughly evenly between ENHANZE and Hypercon. The preview discussed deal cadence and noted that collaboration revenue can be lumpy, but did not forecast this number of agreements or this upfront amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Signed five new collaboration and licensing agreements in 2026 (four in Q2, one in July), contributing $35.5 million in upfront collaboration revenue split roughly evenly between ENHANZE and Hypercon.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Collaboration cadence and buyback pace” were listed as items to watch; the preview also noted that collaboration revenue is “lumpy.”

surprises.description: Three newer launches—Opdivo SC, Ocrevus SC, and Rybrevant SC—grew their royalty contributions about 80% quarter over quarter, expanding the royalty base to six products. The preview anticipated partner ramps generally but did not identify this pace of growth or the resulting six-product base.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Newer launch products (Opdivo SC, Ocrevus SC, Rybrevant SC) grew royalty contributions approximately 80% quarter-over-quarter, expanding the diversified royalty base to six products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the base case as “Modest beat in line with partner data” and the bull case as “Partner ramps flow through.”

surprises.description: Halozyme expanded ENHANZE into ADCs and nucleic acids through GSK and an undisclosed partner, with management estimating at least 100 commercial and development products could benefit. The preview did not identify these new modality areas or quantify this potential reach.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expanded ENHANZE into two new modality areas—ADCs and nucleic acids—via GSK and an undisclosed partner, estimating at least 100 commercial and development products could benefit.”

surprises.description: Halozyme repurchased $332.8 million of shares in Q2 alone, close to its $400 million full-year target. The preview flagged Q2 buyback dollars but gave no expected quarterly pace or amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased $332.8 million of shares in Q2 against a $400 million full-year buyback target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “Watch ... how many dollars were repurchased against the $400M 2026 minimum.”

surprises.description: Management provided a substantial long-term Hypercon outlook not anticipated in the preview: first two products are projected to launch in 2030–2031, with about $1 billion in royalty revenue by the mid-2030s from five to seven launches.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hypercon is projected to launch its first two products in the 2030-2031 timeframe and reach approximately $1 billion in royalty revenue by the mid-2030s from an assumed five to seven launches.”

in_line: The year-end objective of reaching up to 13 ENHANZE development programs was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation to track “progress toward 13 ENHANZE products” by year-end.

surprises.description: Instead of reaffirming the FY2026 outlook and relying on the expected second-half ramp, management said the shift toward holding more SBA 7(a) loans requires it to reevaluate prior Q4 guidance of $0.79–$0.89. It expects to reissue guidance only after another 45–60 days of calculations.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management said the shift to hold more SBA 7(a) loans will reduce near-term gain-on-sale income and pressure top-line net interest income, prompting a re-evaluation of prior Q4 guidance of $0.79–$0.89; guidance will be reissued within an estimated 45–60 day window.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 EPS (company guide) | $2.15–$2.55” and the catalyst checklist says “Reaffirming $2.15–$2.55 is the base case.” The preview also says the guide midpoint implies a substantial H2 ramp.

surprises.description: The preview looked for SBA 7(a) sales at roughly $200–$225 million with a gain-on-sale premium near $1.10, but management is shifting toward keeping more of those loans on the balance sheet. That directly reduces near-term gain-on-sale income and pressures top-line net interest income rather than following the anticipated sale-driven earnings profile.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is “shifting strategy to hold more SBA 7(a) loans on the balance sheet,” which “will reduce near-term gain-on-sale income and pressure the top-line net interest income.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “7(a) volume $200–225M, premium ~$1.10,” and the preview called the gain-on-sale premium “the most direct EPS lever.”

surprises.description: The planned securitization is smaller than the $400–$500 million pool the preview identified as the key Q4 swing factor: management described a $300–$400 million transaction. The facts do not establish whether its timing is still Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans a securitization out of the bank sized between $300 million and $400 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “the Q4 ALP securitization ($400–500M collateral pool)” as the biggest swing factor and said its “timing and size” must be reiterated.

surprises.description: Deposit growth included a large $297 million increase in core consumer deposits, while non-affiliate deposits grew only $15 million. That is a potentially less favorable mix than the preview's preference for cheaper, stickier business deposits and its concern about consumer-heavy growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core consumer deposits climbing $297 million in the quarter and non-affiliate deposits up $15 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Business deposits are the cheaper, stickier funding” and warned that “heavy consumer skew means lower-quality growth.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a $15 million loan to a summer-camp operator that is in bankruptcy, a specific credit issue not identified in the preview. Management expects full recovery, so the disclosure is concerning but does not indicate an expected loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company disclosed “a $15 million loan to a summer camp operator (Sunmad Holdings) in bankruptcy that management expects to fully recover.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged credit quality as a key issue, noting that “charge-offs are rising as the portfolio seasons,” but did not identify this borrower or loan.

surprises.description: Management reported substantial operating leverage: assets grew 50% year over year while expenses rose only 3.6%. The preview did not set an expectation for this relationship.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Assets grew 50% year-over-year while expenses rose only 3.6%, demonstrating operating leverage.”

in_line: Q2 diluted EPS was $0.47, within the preview's $0.46–$0.49 base-case range and close to its $0.46 consensus estimate.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $1.5 million, above the preview’s primary $1.00 million consensus estimate but below its alternate $1.82 million estimate. The result therefore beat the primary estimate but did not clear the higher estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $1.5 million.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin reached 44%, above the preview’s expected range of about 35%–40%. The preview had cautioned that Q1’s 39% margin was on a thin revenue base and asked whether it would hold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin reached 44% (42% year-to-date)”; the company cited “favorable product mix and supply chain efficiencies.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin: 35% – 40%”; “Gross margin durability. The 39% Q1 margin sits on a very thin revenue base.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year gross margin range to 40%–45% from the 35%–40% range investors had been using. This was a higher forward margin outlook, not just a strong Q2 result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year 2026 gross margin guidance from 35%-40% to 40%-45%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance (FY26): Gross margin 35% – 40%.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash and investments were $27.2 million, below the preview’s expected $30–34 million cash balance. The call also disclosed a $17.5 million minimum-liquidity covenant, which makes the available liquidity more constrained than the preview’s cash estimate alone conveyed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $27.2 million in cash and investments” and “must maintain minimum cash liquidity of $17.5 million under its convertible notes covenants.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Absent new financing, Q2 cash should land near $30–34M.”

surprises.description: Management raised its 2026–2030 booking opportunity projection by 50%, from $500 million to $750 million, and said engagements had grown to more than 130. The preview did not identify this larger opportunity projection as an expected update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its 2026-2030 booking opportunity projection by 50% from $500 million to $750 million across over 130 customer engagements (up ~30% from the prior 100).”

surprises.description: MicroVision said MOVIA S is set to launch in October, with more than 25 active customer engagements and capacity being built for about 15,000 units annually. It also expects the sensor to become a meaningful revenue contributor in 2027; the preview had not flagged this product launch or ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The MOVIA S short-range sensor launches in October 2026 with more than 25 active customer engagements,” with capacity for “roughly 15,000 units annually” and an expected meaningful revenue contribution in 2027.

surprises.description: Management said it had integrated the acquired Luminar business within roughly one quarter and reconstituted about half of the inherited customer accounts. The preview treated whether integration was complete as an open question, though the call facts do not provide the opex data the preview sought.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company integrated the acquired Luminar business within roughly one quarter, reconstituting about half of the ~30 inherited customer accounts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Opex normalization. Q1 opex of $23.9M was inflated by Luminar/Scantinel acquisition and integration costs”; “A drop toward $18–20M would signal the integration is done.”

surprises.description: The call described recent IRIS orders for military UGVs and unmanned aircraft, adding defense applications beyond the defense reorder already noted in the preview. The preview had highlighted conversion of defense programs as a key issue but did not anticipate these specific order use cases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received recent defense orders including IRIS sensors from a prime contractor for military UGVs” and “from a defense/aerospace contractor for unmanned aircraft.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Defense reorder (April 29, 2026) covers 200 additional Movia L units with no financial terms disclosed”; the preview also listed “Dollar values for the MDA or defense program” as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: MicroVision launched MOVIA Air and reported nine prelaunch evaluation partners, a product and partner milestone the preview did not mention.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Launching MOVIA Air with 9 prelaunch evaluation partners.”

in_line: The company reaffirmed its $10–15 million full-year revenue guidance and continued to expect the bulk of revenue in the second half, as the preview’s base scenario anticipated.
The approximately $60 million full-year cash-use guidance was reiterated, matching the preview’s stated guide.
The roughly $41.2 million of ATM capacity was close to the preview’s estimate of about $42 million.

surprises.description: The preview expected Q3 sales of $348.8M–$349.2M, while Natural Grocers reported $334.7M—about $14M below the consensus range and also below the preview’s bear-case threshold of $339M.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales rose 1.8% year-over-year to $334.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $348.8M – $349.2M”; the bear scenario was “≤$339M.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for EPS of $0.51–$0.52, with its base case at $0.55–$0.59 including the recovery; reported diluted EPS was only $0.48 despite the $2M insurance gain. Adjusted EBITDA also fell 7.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income fell slightly to $11.1 million ($0.48 diluted EPS) from $11.6 million ($0.50) a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA dropped 7.6% to $22.5 million.” The call also reported a “$2 million business interruption insurance recovery gain.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | $0.51 (Investing.com) / $0.52 (Public.com)”; the base scenario expected “$0.55 – $0.59” reported EPS, including the recovery.

surprises.description: Comps came in at 1.2%, below the preview’s roughly 2% expectation, and the key traffic measure worsened rather than turning positive or holding roughly flat: transaction count fell 1.8%, even as basket size grew 3.1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 daily average comparable store sales grew 1.2% … driven by a 3.1% increase in basket size that offset a 1.8% decline in transaction count.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “Daily avg comps | ~2%” and identified traffic turning positive as the bull case and “traffic roughly flat” as the base case; it said a second negative traffic quarter would suggest weaker demand.

surprises.description: Gross margin was 29.3%, 70 basis points below the preview’s approximately 30.0% expectation and down 60 basis points year over year. Management attributed the decline to mix, shrink, and freight, while saying the pressures should be isolated to this quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined 60 basis points to 29.3% due to unfavorable sales mix, higher inventory shrink, and freight costs, though management expects these pressures to be isolated to this quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~30.0% (FY guide flat YoY).”

surprises.description: Management lowered the upper end of both full-year outlook ranges: comp growth to 2.0% from 2.5%, and EPS to $2.11 from $2.15, with both floors unchanged. The EPS range is also below the preview’s $2.10–$2.16 base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management narrowed full-year guidance to comp sales growth of 1.5%-2% (from 1.5%-2.5%) and diluted EPS of $2.07-$2.11 (from $2.07-$2.15).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “FY guide narrowed to ~$2.10 – $2.16”; it also listed FY26 EPS consensus of “$2.12.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag a new delivery channel, but the company launched DoorDash delivery across all stores in mid-July and plans to phase in curbside pickup, adding customer-access options not reflected in the preview’s expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company launched a DoorDash delivery partnership across all stores in mid-July and plans to phase in curbside pickup.”

surprises.description: The preview did not discuss the loyalty program’s sales penetration; the call reported that {N}power Rewards penetration rose 2 percentage points year over year to 84%, with management linking it to sales, traffic, and basket-size growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “{N}power Rewards net sales penetration rose 2 percentage points year-over-year to 84%, driving growth in sales, traffic, and basket size.”

surprises.description: The preview did not identify Natural Grocers brand penetration as a watch item; the company reported a 110-basis-point year-over-year gain to 9.7% of total sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Natural Grocers brand penetration increased 110 basis points year-over-year to 9.7% of total sales.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag the Q4 calendar headwind: management noted that Q4 will have one fewer selling day because stores will close for Labor Day.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 will have one fewer selling day due to Labor Day store closures.”

in_line: The approximately $2M business-interruption insurance recovery was anticipated in the preview; the preview estimated it at about $0.065 per share.
Capital expenditure guidance remained at $45M–$50M, as set after Q2.

The preview cited a planned 6–8 store openings for FY26 and highlighted the long-term 4%–5% unit-growth goal; the company reported six openings fiscal year to date and reaffirmed that long-term target.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $31.6 million, up 1% year over year, versus preview consensus of $28.8–$29.0 million and an expected 8% year-over-year decline. The result was a clear beat and reversed the expected year-over-year decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $31.6 million, up 1% year-over-year and up 14% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY26 Consensus | $28.8 – $29.0M | Y/Y comp (Q2'25) $31.4M (−8% Y/Y).”

surprises.description: The preview said product revenue needed to at least hold flat quarter over quarter after Q1’s $18.6 million. Instead, Q2 product revenue was $21.9 million, up about 18% sequentially, although it remained down 5% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total product revenue [was] $21.9 million.” Q1 product revenue in the preview was “$18.6M.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Product revenue needs to at least hold flat Q/Q.”

surprises.description: Gross margin came in below the preview’s roughly 43–45% expectation and fell from Q1’s 43.8% to 42.2%, rather than continuing its recent sequential expansion. It was still up more than 380 basis points year over year, and management said it remained on track toward the 50% milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin reached 42.2%, up over 380 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP GM | ~43–45% (guide: low-to-mid 40s).” The preview also said, “A Q/Q stall would weaken the bull case.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a broader multi-year refresh opportunity of roughly 3,000 consoles and up to $150 million in console revenue, beyond the known $40 million HCA agreement. The HCA agreement itself excludes possible expansion into additional HCA facilities not yet equipped with Tableau.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The broader refresh cycle over the next several years may include roughly 3,000 consoles and up to $150 million in console revenue opportunity”; the $40 million HCA deal “does not include potential expansion into additional HCA facilities not yet equipped with Tableau.”

surprises.description: Consumables declined 12% year over year to $12.4 million. The preview did not give a Q2 consumables forecast; management attributed the decline to timing rather than weaker device utilization, leaving a weaker reported recurring-revenue component than the preview’s discussion had highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consumable revenue declined 12% year-over-year to $12.4 million against a tough double-digit growth comparison,” which management attributed to “timing rather than weakening device utilization.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed FY2026 revenue guidance of $125–$130 million, as the preview’s base case expected; the preview said reaffirmation was meaningful and that reaching guidance depended on second-half acceleration.
