The known $40 million HCA refresh agreement was described as extending through 2028, with no 2026 contribution detail provided. The preview said the company had deferred the 2026 impact and that the base case expected HCA detail to remain deferred.
The company remained on track to use less than $40 million in cash for the full year, consistent with the preview’s stated burn target.

surprises.description: NerdWallet reported $197 million of revenue, about $1.7 million above the $195.3 million consensus and $3 million above the company-guidance midpoint. The beat was modest and still within the $186–$202 million guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $197 million” and “above the midpoint of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus $195.3M”; company guidance was “$186M – $202M (midpoint $194M).”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating income was $12 million, $2 million above the $10 million guidance midpoint and near the upper end of the $6–$14 million range. This was better than the preview’s base scenario of $9–$12 million, although the preview had no NGOI consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income of $12 million at a 6% margin, above the midpoint of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income (NGOI) ... Q2'26 Company Guidance ... midpoint $10M”; the base scenario anticipated “$9M – $12M.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that it is increasing customer-acquisition spending with payback periods beyond the current year roughly fivefold versus 2025, creating a $15–$20 million full-year 2026 NGOI headwind. The preview discussed vertical-integration spending but did not anticipate this specific level of longer-payback acquisition investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Increasing customer acquisition spend with payback periods beyond the current year roughly fivefold versus 2025,” representing “a $15–$20 million NGOI headwind for full-year 2026.”

surprises.description: The largest auto-insurance carrier relationship had stabilized, rather than worsening further, but remained below earlier-year levels. That partly eased the concern that the Q2 shortfall would deepen, while leaving the carrier issue unresolved and prompting efforts to scale other carriers and the in-house agency.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's largest auto insurance carrier relationship has stabilized but remains below levels seen earlier in the year,” prompting a push to scale with other carriers and expand its in-house insurance agency.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the carrier issue “would hit Q2 harder” and framed the key question as whether it was “one carrier's budget cycle or a broader carrier pullback.”

surprises.description: Trailing 12-month adjusted free cash flow reached a record $141 million, up 100% year over year, but management attributed part of the increase to $9 million of tax refunds and no federal corporate tax payments. The preview noted Q1 free cash flow and the need to rebuild cash but gave no expectation for this record or its tax-related contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month adjusted free cash flow grew 100% year-over-year to a record $141 million,” aided by “$9 million in tax refunds and no federal corporate tax payments”; the company expects no federal corporate tax in 2026 and normalized taxes in Q2 or Q3 2027.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance implies 17% year-over-year growth at the midpoint, a stronger stated pace than the preview’s minimum test of simply showing growth from the prior-year quarter. Management cited student-loan regulatory tailwinds and the February college-finance acquisition, which the preview had not identified as Q3 growth drivers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $244–$260 million implies 17% year-over-year growth at the midpoint,” boosted by “student loan regulatory tailwinds and the February college finance acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a Q3 guide that “does not imply growth from that base” would signal search erosion was outpacing growth elsewhere.

in_line: Full-year NGOI guidance was narrowed to $90–$105 million while keeping its midpoint at $97.5 million, matching the preview’s expectation that the company would reaffirm the $85–$110 million range; the preview also noted that the buy side expected reaffirmation.
Consumer credit-card declines and SMB pressure from organic-search headwinds continued, consistent with the preview’s concerns about erosion in those areas.
The company continued repurchases, with $23 million bought back in Q2 and $67 million remaining under authorization, consistent with the preview’s focus on whether buybacks would continue.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $13.4 million, far above the preview’s derived expectation of roughly $5–6 million. Management attributed the more-than-tripling from a year earlier primarily to higher milestone revenue from partner clinical progress.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $13.4 million,” primarily driven by “higher milestone revenue from partner clinical progress.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue vs. ~$5–6M derived consensus.”

surprises.description: OmniAb raised its FY26 revenue outlook to $32–36 million instead of merely reaffirming the prior $28–33 million range. The new range is also above the preview’s cited $30.81 million analyst consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $32-36 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The company’s current guide was “$28–33M”; the preview said reaffirming it was a base-case scenario and that “a raise would validate the milestone story.”

surprises.description: The reported loss per share was substantially narrower than expected: $0.05 versus preview estimates ranging from a $0.10 to $0.15 loss, including a cited consensus of $0.12.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss improved to $5.9 million ($0.05/share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q2 EPS consensus of “–$0.12,” with other estimates of “–$0.10” and “–$0.15.”

surprises.description: The year-end cash forecast rose to $37–41 million, above the prior $33–38 million outlook cited in the preview. Management expects to use about $15 million of the $54 million starting balance during the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: OmniAb “now expects to end the year with $37-41 million in cash,” from a “$54 million starting balance implying roughly $15 million annual burn.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The company’s prior year-end cash guide was “$33–38M.”

surprises.description: Management said milestone revenue is front-end loaded in 2026, implying weaker revenue in the second half. That is a caution against reading the higher full-year guide as a smooth run-rate improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management guided that “milestone revenue is front-end loaded in 2026 (implying weaker second-half revenue).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said reaffirming the prior guide “could be read as a soft back half,” while a raise would validate the milestone story.

surprises.description: The partner and program base expanded rather than remaining flat: active partners rose from 107 at Q1 to 110, and active programs increased from 409 to 425. The quarter also brought new licensing agreements with Argenix and Enrosa Therapeutics.
surprises.fact_evidence: OmniAb ended Q2 with “425 active programs”; it signed agreements with “Argenix and preclinical biotech Enrosa Therapeutics” and had “110 active partners.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that active partners were “107 (flat vs. YE25)” and called the flat count “the soft spot in Q1,” with partner and program adds flagged as key metrics to watch.

surprises.description: Two partner programs moved directly from Phase 1 to Phase 3 during the quarter, including J&J’s romantamig and Merck KGaA’s CEACAM5 ADC. The preview focused on a different Merck program’s Phase 3 dosing and did not anticipate these two direct advances.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Two partner programs jumped directly from Phase 1 to Phase 3 during Q2: J&J's tri-specific myeloma antibody romantamig and Merck KGaA's CEACAM5 ADC for colorectal cancer.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed Merck KGaA dosing the first patient in the Phase 3 PROCEADE-CRC-03 trial of precemtabart tocentecan; it did not mention these two programs’ direct Phase 1-to-Phase 3 moves.

surprises.description: The exploration screening platform showed commercial traction the preview did not discuss: it sold two instruments in Q2, bringing the installed base to four, with management citing strong instrument margins and even better consumables margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The exploration single B-cell screening platform sold two instruments in Q2, bringing the installed base to four units,” with “strong margins on instruments and even better margins on consumables.”

surprises.description: The company reported six clinical-stage programs derived from its genetically engineered chicken platforms, describing the technology as globally unique. This platform-specific clinical validation was not covered in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Six clinical programs (Phase 1 or Phase 2) now derive from the company's genetically engineered chicken antibody platforms (OmniDab and OmniChicken),” which OmniAb claims is “unique globally.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $343 million, about 5% above the $325.6 million consensus and above the $330 million high end of company guidance. The preview expected little cushion above guidance, not a beat of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached a record $343 million” and exceeded the high end of guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was “$325.6M”; company guidance was “$320–330M.” The preview said there was “little cushion above the guided high end.”

surprises.description: Q2 EPS of $1.93 substantially exceeded both the $1.68 consensus and the $1.73 high end of guidance; management said it beat the guidance high end by $0.20.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 EPS came in at $1.93, beating the high end of prior guidance by $0.20.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus non-GAAP EPS was “$1.68”; company guidance was “$1.65–$1.73.”

surprises.description: Management raised the H2 revenue growth outlook to over 25% versus H1, up from the prior 15% expectation, and said Q4 should exceed Q3. This is a substantial improvement over the preview’s H2 framework.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its second-half 2026 revenue growth outlook to over 25% versus the first half, up from a prior 15% expectation, with Q4 expected to exceed Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the H2 framework as “H2 at least 15% above H1.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $380–$400 million was far above the preview’s implied $345–$355 million range. The accompanying outlook was for 32% operating margin and approximately $2.28 EPS, with operating margin exiting the year above 33%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for revenue of $380-$400 million, operating margin of 32%, and EPS of approximately $2.28, exiting the year at 33%+ operating margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s “H2 framework” implied “a Q3 guide near $345–355M”; its base scenario also listed “$345–355M.”

surprises.description: Advanced-packaging growth guidance for the full year rose to approximately 80%, well above the 50% projected last quarter and beyond the preview’s expectation that growth remain above 50%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year advanced packaging growth guidance was raised sharply to approximately 80%, up from the 50% projected last quarter, driven by HBM and OSAT demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said advanced packaging “needs to keep growing above 50% for FY26.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin reached 57% and operating margin reached 30%, above the respective guidance ceilings of 56.5% and 28.6%. Both profitability measures outperformed the preview’s expected in-range result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin hit 57%” and “operating margin reached 30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed non-GAAP gross margin guidance of “56.0%–56.5%” and non-GAAP operating margin guidance of “28.0%–28.6%,” with its base scenario expecting “margins in range.”

surprises.description: The company set full-year targets for 350 basis points of gross-margin expansion and more than 750 basis points of operating-margin expansion. That is stronger than merely reaffirming the preview’s expected quarterly margin-improvement cadence.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year targets now at 350 bps of gross margin and over 750 bps of operating margin expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether the “+50bps per quarter cadence into H2 is reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Backlog surpassed a record $1.1 billion, with roughly 30–40% tied to 2027 deliveries, providing unusually strong visibility into next year that the preview did not identify as an expected result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog surpassed a record $1.1 billion, with roughly 30-40% tied to 2027 deliveries.”

surprises.description: Onto secured more than $200 million of Dragonfly orders from one OSAT partner, mostly for delivery in 2027. The preview discussed Dragonfly unit growth but did not anticipate an order of this size or its concentration and delivery timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company secured over $200 million in Dragonfly orders from a single OSAT partner, with the majority to be delivered in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Dragonfly G5 units were expected to “nearly double each quarter” through Q3.

surprises.description: Advanced Nodes revenue reached approximately $120 million, up 50% sequentially from the $80 million reported in Q1, and management expects full-year growth above 35%. The preview gave the Q1 baseline but no forecast for this segment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Advanced nodes revenue grew 50% sequentially to approximately $120 million” and “full-year growth [is] expected to exceed 35%.”

surprises.description: The company completed a $1.5 billion zero-coupon convertible offering, repurchased about $200 million of stock, and reported nearly $1.9 billion in cash. The preview focused on weak Q1 operating cash flow and the planned Rigaku transaction, not this large financing-and-buyback package.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Completed a $1.5 billion 0% convertible debt offering (net ~$1.2 billion), repurchased ~$200 million in stock, holds nearly $1.9 billion in cash.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 operating cash flow was “only about $26M” and cash and marketable securities were “$654.2M”; it also discussed the expected Rigaku deal.

surprises.description: Management highlighted silicon photonics as a future growth driver, citing a $500 million addressable market by 2030. The preview did not flag this opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management identified “silicon photonics ($500M SAM by 2030)” as a future growth driver.

surprises.description: Management also highlighted the Rigaku X-ray partnership as a future growth driver tied to a $1 billion market, beyond the preview’s discussion of the expected Rigaku stake transaction and its timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management identified “the Rigaku X-ray partnership ($1B market)” as a future growth driver.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “$710M Rigaku deal for a 27% stake is expected to close in H2 2026.”

surprises.description: The preview modeled Q2 fee income of $150K–$200K from modest royalties, but the call reported that royalties declined significantly as SPD emulsion and film production at Gauzy slowed and essentially stopped during its restructuring. That points to a materially weaker royalty result than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 royalties declined significantly because SPD emulsion and film production at principal licensee Gauzy slowed and essentially stopped during its court-supervised financial restructuring.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My Q2 2026 base est.” for fee income was “$150K – $200K”; the base scenario assumed “Modest royalties, no upfront.”

surprises.description: The company recorded a reserve and going-concern accounting treatment on receivables from Gauzy and Vision Systems. The preview flagged possible going-concern language for the company in a bear case, but did not anticipate this specific uncertainty about collecting licensee receivables.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Research Frontiers took a reserve and going-concern accounting treatment on receivables from Gauzy and Vision Systems, citing uncertainty over collection timing rather than ultimate collectability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bear scenario listed “going-concern language,” but did not discuss a reserve or collection uncertainty on receivables.

surprises.description: Despite the expected cash pressure, quarter-end cash was just over $1 million, above the preview’s estimated $0.80M–$0.90M. This was a better cash balance than modeled, though management still said it may need to raise capital.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Research Frontiers ended the quarter with just over $1 million in cash.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Cash & equivalents” at “~$0.80M – $0.90M” and cited a catalyst of “June 30 cash vs. ~$850K.”

surprises.description: The call described concrete steps toward restarting Gauzy production: new financing and court approval of a debt restructuring plan have started funds flowing to rehire workers and restart German production, with smaller creditors such as Research Frontiers to be paid immediately. The preview highlighted cash and royalty risks but did not anticipate these specific recovery developments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A recent $7 million financing from former Gauzy directors and a July 18 Israeli court approval of a debt restructuring plan have started funds flowing to rehire workers and restart German production, with smaller creditors like Research Frontiers to be paid immediately.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described quarterly burn and limited runway, and said to watch for “a new placement or ATM”; it did not mention Gauzy’s financing, restructuring approval, or payments to Research Frontiers.

surprises.description: Management said Gauzy’s successful emergence from bankruptcy and return to full production was the most likely supply-restoration path, potentially as soon as next month, and expressed confidence that automotive production volumes could recover by year-end. That recovery outlook was more encouraging than the preview’s emphasis on a stalled royalty run-rate and cash risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Plan A”—Gauzy successfully emerging from bankruptcy and resuming full production—was “viewed as the most likely outcome, possibly as soon as next month”; management also said automotive volumes could “ramp back up by the end of the year given pent-up demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 revenue suggested “recurring royalties have not yet grown” and described under two quarters of runway if no raise occurred.

surprises.description: The company won two new major aircraft programs, beyond the preview’s expectation that Q2 should show aircraft revenue from windows already being produced. The call also highlighted that aircraft windows carry much higher royalty value per window than automotive applications.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Two new major aircraft programs were won during the period,” and aircraft applications carry “roughly 15x the royalty value per window compared to automotive.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said SPD-Smart windows “were produced for aircraft OEMs in Q1 and Q2 2026, so Q2 should show aircraft revenue.”

surprises.description: A French court ordered the sale of Gauzy’s entire Vision Systems division to Clayens for about EUR 9 million despite a signed EUR 125 million offer for only part of the division. The pending appeal leaves a chance of a different outcome, but the court’s order was a markedly less favorable result than the signed offer suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A French court directed the sale of Gauzy’s entire Vision Systems division to Clayens for about EUR 9 million despite a signed EUR 125 million offer for just part of it,” with “a final appeal scheduled for mid-September.”

surprises.description: Management raised the possibility of acquiring Gauzy’s SPD manufacturing assets under “Plan D,” which could require Research Frontiers to raise capital. The preview anticipated possible financing needs but did not flag a potential asset acquisition as a use of capital.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “may need to raise capital, particularly if it pursues ‘Plan D’ of acquiring Gauzy’s SPD manufacturing assets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warned that cash was under two quarters of runway and said to watch for “a new placement or ATM,” but did not mention acquiring manufacturing assets.

in_line: Management ruled out a reverse stock split, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the Nasdaq stance would remain unchanged and its note that management did not currently intend to do a reverse split.
The possibility of needing to raise capital was consistent with the preview’s warning to watch for a placement or ATM given the company’s limited cash runway.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $21.7 million exceeded the preview's roughly $20.25 million consensus estimate. The beat also marked the first quarter above $20 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $21.7 million,” and it was “the first time the company exceeded $20 million in quarterly revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $20.25M” and “My model vs. consensus: Revenue $20.3M vs. $20.25M (in line).”

surprises.description: AVITA raised FY26 revenue guidance to $86–89 million, above its prior $80–85 million range and the preview's $83.9 million Street estimate. The preview treated holding the existing range as the base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $86-89 million,” up “from the prior $80-85 million range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue | $80–85M”; consensus was “$83.9M (Street),” and “Reaffirmation is the base case.”

surprises.description: Cash use was much lower, and quarter-end liquidity higher, than the preview's base case: net cash use was about $3.2 million and cash plus marketable securities ended at $11.1 million, rather than burn of $5–7 million and cash of $7–9 million. This also exceeded the preview's bull-case cash-use threshold of $4 million or less only narrowly, while topping its $10 million cash threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net cash use improved sharply to approximately $3.2 million in Q2, ending the quarter with only about $11.1 million in cash and marketable securities.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case forecast “Burn $5–7M, cash $7–9M”; the bull case forecast “Burn ≤$4M, cash ≥$10M.”

surprises.description: The company added a Q4 2026 target to reach cash-flow breakeven and begin generating cash, a more favorable financing and liquidity outlook than the preview discussed. The preview focused on near-term burn and possible funding strategies, not a stated breakeven timetable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company introduced new guidance to achieve cash flow breakeven and begin generating cash during Q4 2026.”

surprises.description: The preview identified more than 15 Cohealyx VAC approvals per quarter as a pace that would support the second-half guidance math; the call described 10–15 reviews typically being completed per quarter. That is below the preview's marker, although the call did not provide a specific Q2 approval count.
surprises.fact_evidence: CoHelix had “about 55 active VAC reviews” and “10-15 typically completed per quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cohealyx VAC approvals. Above 15 per quarter would support the 2H guidance math.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that reimbursement will move to a nationally published RVU framework under new Category 1 CPT codes starting in 2027, a future reimbursement change not covered in the preview. The facts provide no estimate of its financial effect, so its direction for shareholders is unclear.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Beginning January 1, 2027, reimbursement transitions from regional MAC pricing to a nationally published RVU framework under new Category 1 CPT codes.”

in_line: Gross margin was 81.9%, within the preview's expected 81–82% range and above its flagged 80% downside threshold.

The $10 million Perceptive debt-facility tranche remained conditional on revenue thresholds, consistent with the preview's description of an available $10 million accordion subject to net revenue thresholds.

surprises.description: Natera reported Q2 revenue of about $753 million, well above the preview’s $700–715 million “real bar” and even above its $730–745 million bull case. Growth was about 38% year over year, or about 40% excluding true-ups.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was approximately $753 million, up ~38% year-over-year (~40% ex true-ups).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The preview's view is that the real bar is about $700M+”; the base scenario was “$700–715M” and the bull scenario “$730–745M.”

surprises.description: Signatera clinical MRD volume reached 283,000 units, above the preview’s 268,000–275,000 expected range. The 34,000 sequential increase also exceeded the roughly 20,000 quarterly increase implied by the preview’s trailing-average expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Clinical MRD (Signatera) units of 283,000 growing ~56% year-over-year and rising 34,000 units sequentially, its largest sequential increase to date.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The preview points to 268–275k units as the expected range”; management had guided to growth “in line with the trailing 12-month average (about +20k per quarter).”

surprises.description: Management expects Q3 Signatera sequential growth to exceed the prior record of roughly 25,000 units, above the preview’s roughly 20,000-per-quarter trailing-average pace. It also cautioned that Q3 would not repeat Q2’s 34,000-unit record increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 Signatera growth will not repeat the record 34,000 units… but expects to exceed the prior sequential record of roughly 25,000 units.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management guided to growth “in line with the trailing 12-month average (about +20k per quarter).”

surprises.description: Gross margin was about 65%, slightly below the preview’s expected 65.5–66.5% base-case range and its stated watch for a recovery above 66%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin held strong at ~65%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “65.5–66.5%”; the preview also said to “watch for gross margin back above 66%.”

surprises.description: Women’s health achieved high-single-digit year-over-year growth despite the seasonally soft quarter, with market-share gains and an improved Panorama test no-call rate. The preview highlighted seasonal softness but did not anticipate these growth and test-performance details.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Women's health delivered high single-digit year-over-year growth despite seasonal softness, aided by market share gains and the enhanced Panorama test, which cut the no-call rate from ~2% to 0.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Q2 as “management's stated seasonally slowest women's health quarter.”

surprises.description: The call quantified about $100 million of spending this year on early cancer detection that currently produces no revenue. The preview noted clinical-trial spending and FIND enrollment timing, but did not flag this specific investment level or the no-revenue status.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Natera is spending roughly $100 million this year on early cancer detection (the FIND trial and development), which currently generates no revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “clinical-trial, new-product and international spending” and said “FIND-CRC enrollment completion [was] expected Q3'26.”

surprises.description: Natera said the seven additional Signatera tumor-type submissions could add an estimated $150–$200 to ASP, with approvals rolling in over 12–18 months and the impact weighted toward 2027. The preview identified the seven histologies as a catalyst but did not quantify the potential ASP increase or timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 7 additional Signatera tumor-type indications submitted to MolDX could add an estimated $150–$200 to ASP, with rolling approvals expected over the next 12–18 months and impact weighted toward 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called an update on “seven additional histologies in MolDX/CMS review” the “highest-torque non-financial catalyst.”

surprises.description: Signatera secured an FDA companion-diagnostic approval for muscle-invasive bladder cancer and an NCCN Category 1 bladder recommendation, milestones not identified in the preview. These add regulatory and guideline support beyond the preview’s named strategic checklist.
surprises.fact_evidence: Signatera became “the first MRD test with FDA companion-diagnostic approval (muscle-invasive bladder cancer)” and received “an NCCN Category 1 bladder recommendation.”

surprises.description: True-ups declined to about $52 million from roughly $60 million in Q1, while DSOs improved by about four days to 57 days. This was better than the preview’s concern about another large true-up alongside rising DSOs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “True-ups declining to ~$52 million in absolute and percentage terms” and “reduced DSOs by ~4 days to an average of 57 days.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “whether another large true-up appears alongside rising DSOs.”

in_line: FY26 revenue guidance rose by $100 million at the midpoint to $2.85–$2.91 billion, a $2.88 billion midpoint within the preview’s $2.86–$2.94 billion base-case range and above its $2.86 billion threshold.
Signatera ASP rose about $25 sequentially to roughly $1,275, as the preview expected it to be “on track to about $1,275.”
Management held OpEx steady, consistent with the preview’s expectation that OpEx would be flat, and reported a narrower loss, as the preview expected the loss to narrow from Q1.
Positive cash inflow was consistent with the preview’s expectation of positive full-year cash flow.
EU IVDR certification was on the preview’s strategic checklist; the call reported certification across 20+ tumor types.

surprises.description: Q2 loss per share was $0.11, substantially narrower than the preview’s $0.21 consensus loss. The call said the net loss actually widened year over year, and the lower per-share loss reflected a larger share count.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss widened to $12.9 million ($0.11 per share) from $9.9 million ($0.30 per share) a year earlier, with the lower per-share loss reflecting a larger share count.”

surprises.description: NDV-01’s IND and Phase 3 start did not meet the preview’s mid-2026/imminent-or-underway expectation. Management now plans to file the IND by year-end, with enrollment only able to begin after clearance; the delay was primarily attributed to the manufacturer’s GMP production schedule.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to file INDs for both NDV-01 […] by year-end 2026, with Phase 3 […] studies to initiate upon IND clearance”; “the mid-2026 IND timeline slipped primarily due to delays getting on the manufacturer’s (Piramal) GMP production schedule”; “patient enrollment [is] able to begin shortly after the 30-day IND review period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance: IND filing and Phase 3 RESCUE initiation for NDV-01 in ‘mid-2026’”; the base scenario expected “IND filed; initiation described as imminent or underway.”

surprises.description: Sepranolone’s IND timing also moved from the preview’s mid-2026 expectation to a planned year-end 2026 filing, with the Phase 2 study to start after IND clearance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to file INDs for both […] sepranolone […] by year-end 2026, with […] Phase 2 studies to initiate upon IND clearance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sepranolone Phase 2b in Prader-Willi. Also guided to mid-2026; a second missed date would raise execution-credibility questions.”

surprises.description: The initial three-month response data expected by year-end 2026 may instead come in the first half of 2027. Management favored waiting for a more meaningful six-month readout with 15–20 patients, but this pushes out the anticipated data catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The previously guided year-end three-month complete response data disclosure may be pushed to first-half 2027, favoring a more meaningful six-month readout with 15-20 patients over early three-month results.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Whether initial 3-month 2L BCG-unresponsive data is reaffirmed for year-end. A slip to early 2027 removes the 2026 catalyst.”

surprises.description: The call reported strong 12-month NDV-01 Phase 2 response results, a data update the preview did not identify as an expected Q2 disclosure. The preview supplied no benchmark for these specific response rates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NDV-01’s 12-month Phase 2 data showed a 95% complete response rate at any time and a 76% durable complete response at 12 months, with a favorable safety profile.”

in_line: Cash ended Q2 at $217.7 million, close to the preview’s roughly $215 million expectation and within its $212–218 million base range; runway through 2029 was reaffirmed.
The roughly 80-site setup was consistent with the preview’s cited ~80 North American sites, although enrollment had not begun pending IND clearance.
R&D expense was $8.4 million, close to the preview’s flat-near-$8-million case and below the $12 million-or-more level it said could indicate Phase 3 spending had started.

surprises.description: PubMatic was expected to report about $68.99 million in Q2 revenue, within its $68–70 million guide; instead, 11% year-over-year growth implies roughly $78.9 million using the prior-year $71.1 million figure. The return to double-digit growth came ahead of management’s previously stated schedule.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 11% year-over-year, marking a return to double-digit growth ahead of schedule.” The preview gives Q2 FY2025 actual revenue of $71.1M.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $68.99M | Company Guide ... $68–70M”; it also says Q1 revenue was down 2% YoY and management reiterated “double-digit revenue growth in the second half of 2026.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $19.6 million, far above the roughly $9 million consensus and $8–10 million guide; its 25% margin also greatly exceeded the preview’s 12–14% guide margin. Free cash flow rose 47% to $13.7 million, though the preview gave no FCF expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 38% year-over-year to $19.6 million (25% margin, up from 20% a year ago), while free cash flow increased 47% to $13.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$9M (guide midpoint)” and the company guide was “$8–10M (12–14% margin).”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $17–19 million implies a margin in the low-to-mid-20% range at the $75–77 million revenue guide, supporting a much faster recovery toward mid-20s margins than the preview’s concern about margins remaining in the teens. Management also said Q4 margin should be similar to last year’s Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $75-77 million ... and adjusted EBITDA of $17-19 million, with Q4 margin expected to be similar to last year's Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “whether 2H margins move back toward the mid-20s” and that “If guidance stays in the teens, the operating leverage argument weakens.”

surprises.description: Global CTV growth was 13%, below the 18% growth cited for Q1 (which was ex-legacy DSP) and well below Magnite’s 36% figure cited in the preview. PubMatic’s Americas CTV growth was stronger at 25%, but the global result leaves the flagged competitive growth gap in view.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CTV grew 13% globally ... with Americas up 25%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Q1 global CTV grew 18% ex-legacy DSP” and that Magnite reported “+36% CTV contribution ex-TAC”; it flagged “CTV growth versus Magnite” as an issue to watch.

surprises.description: Mobile app revenue grew more than 40% and represented about a quarter of total revenue, a substantial growth engine not specifically identified in the preview’s key issues.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mobile app revenue grew over 40% year-over-year (~25% of total).”

surprises.description: Emerging revenue nearly doubled to an all-time high of about 15% of revenue, exceeding the preview’s already strong growth threshold and raising its mix from the 14% reported in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Emerging revenues nearly doubled to an all-time high of ~15% of total revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said emerging revenue had grown “more than 80% YoY to 14% of total revenue,” described growth below about 60% as a negative signal, and included “emerging revenue >85% YoY” in its bull scenario.

surprises.description: The company announced CFO Steve Pantelick’s retirement and a transition to advisory work, alongside the appointment of a new Global Chief Revenue Officer. The preview did not flag a leadership transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Steve Pantelick announced his retirement, remaining CFO into Q1 2027 and then advisory through July 1, with a new Global Chief Revenue Officer, Megan Ramm, joining August 10.”

surprises.description: AgenticOS usage advanced to more than 80 campaigns from 30 in the prior quarter, spanning all five global agency holding companies, and management gave ambitious adoption milestones through 2030. The preview did not discuss agentic trading.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AgenticOS delivered over 80 agentic campaigns (up from 30 the prior quarter) across all five global agency holding companies,” with management projecting 25% of the ecosystem will trade agentically by end of 2028 and 50% by 2030.

surprises.description: PubMatic said it deliberately cut gross impressions sequentially while increasing monetized impressions, a change in operating approach that it expects to improve monetization in future quarters. The preview did not identify this strategy or metric combination.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced gross impressions sequentially by 2% while increasing monetized impressions by 4%, signaling an intentional strategy expected to lift monetization rates in future quarters.”

surprises.description: The company repurchased 2.1 million Class A shares for $21.5 million in the quarter and ended with $137.5 million in cash and no debt; the preview did not discuss buybacks or the balance sheet.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased 2.1 million Class A shares for $21.5 million in Q2, ended with $137.5 million in cash and zero debt, and has $63.6 million remaining in its buyback authorization through 2026.”

surprises.description: Full-year CapEx was raised to $20–25 million to support AI workloads and the NVIDIA partnership, a higher investment outlook that the preview did not anticipate; management said the spending is expected to generate incremental revenue with payback of about 12 months or less.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year CapEx outlook was raised to $20-25 million to support AI workloads and the NVIDIA partnership, with these investments expected to generate incremental revenue at a payback of approximately 12 months or less.”

in_line: Q3 revenue guidance of $75–77 million (midpoint $76 million) was broadly in line with the preview’s roughly $75 million bar and its $74–76 million base-case range, though a little above the bar.
The preview expected double-digit revenue growth in the second half; management reaffirmed that trajectory and said growth should accelerate through the second half.
Emerging revenue’s near-doubling was consistent with the preview’s expectation of strong growth above 80% and its bull-case threshold above 85%.

surprises.description: The preview modeled Q2 operating adjusted EBITDA of $35–45 million, but RILY reported $66 million—well above the top of the range. Management called it the best core operating quarter in nearly three years.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income available to common shareholders was $18.5 million with operating adjusted EBITDA of $66 million, described as the best core operating quarter in nearly 3 years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating Adj. EBITDA | $35–45M”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $239 million, about $56 million below the preview’s roughly $295 million model. Trading gains were only $12.9 million, versus the preview’s $75 million investment-gains estimate, with management attributing the year-over-year decline in trading gains primarily to a lower fair value on the Babcock & Wilcox investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenues rose $14 million year-over-year to $239 million, but trading gains fell $14.8 million to $12.9 million primarily due to lower fair value on the Babcock & Wilcox investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenues | ~$295M”; “Investment gains | ~$75M.” The model assumed “Babcock & Wilcox (BW) was roughly flat over the quarter.”

surprises.description: Common-shareholder net income was $18.5 million, far below the earnings implied by the preview’s modeled diluted EPS of $1.35–$1.85. The call facts do not provide actual diluted EPS, so this comparison is indicative rather than a direct EPS-to-EPS comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income available to common shareholders was $18.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | ~$1.35–1.85.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted the September and December note maturities as a central funding risk and said the September notes were not covered in its base case. Management said the maturities can be covered with $723 million in investment securities and more than $150 million in cash; the reported maturities total just over $300 million, below the preview’s $337 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Two senior note maturities in the remainder of 2026 totaling just over $300 million ($142 million due September 30 and $164 million due December 31), which management says it can cover with $723 million in investment securities plus over $150 million in cash.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Together that is $337M against $175.8M of Q1-end cash”; the base case said September notes were “on track” but “not covered,” and asked whether the September maturity was “fully funded.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $20.2 million, below the preview’s $22.3–$22.65 million consensus range by roughly 9–11%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $20.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $22.3M (Zacks) or $22.65M (broader street).”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 16.1%, below the preview’s estimated 18–22% range and below the 18% level it said was needed to keep the year-end 30% target credible. Management nevertheless retained the 30% year-end target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 16.1% in Q2 2026”; management “targets 30% gross margin by the end of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~18–22%”; “Anything below about 18% would effectively withdraw the year-end target.”

surprises.description: Blue Ops had been expected to have near-zero Q2 USV revenue, but Variant 7 entered mass production and generated its first revenue. Management also said fewer than 10 boats could make the division profitable if Q4 internal targets are met.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Blue Ops moved its Variant 7 uncrewed surface vessel into mass production and received first revenue”; “fewer than 10 boats would make the division profitable if Q4 internal targets are met.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 USV revenue is likely near zero”; the preview also described about 245 boats in 2026 as part of the annual target framing.

surprises.description: The Drone Dominance Program emerged as a potential near-term revenue source: management said it could contribute $14–28 million in Q3, and RCAT advanced to Gauntlet II. The preview did not identify this program as a Q3 revenue driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Drone Dominance Program could contribute $14 million to $28 million in Q3 revenue alone, and the company advanced to Gauntlet II.”

surprises.description: The company’s customer mix was less Army-dependent than the preview’s Army-contract focus might suggest: Army was about 50% of first-half revenue, while Japan and Europe’s NSPA ranked second and third.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Army dependence fell to roughly 50% of first-half revenue from 73% in 2025, with Japan and Europe's NSPA now the #2 and #3 customers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “SRR Tranche 2 / LRIP award timing” and asked whether “Army sUAS obligations are flowing to the company.”

surprises.description: Inventory including prepaid inventory rose to about $84.8 million from $30.4 million at year-end, and management said $50–80 million of drones could ship immediately only if orders materialize. This adds a substantial inventory and order-conversion contingency to the expected H2 ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory including prepaid inventory grew to about $84.8 million from $30.4 million at year-end, and management says $50–80 million of Black Widows and Hellcats could ship immediately if orders materialize.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the low end of the annual target required “about $112M in H2, roughly 3x H1” and asked for a delivery schedule.

surprises.description: Operating expenses were about $41.9 million, with R&D roughly doubling sequentially to $14.2 million. That contrasts with the preview’s base-case expectation that EPS would be helped by opex and points to costs remaining far above quarterly revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 operating expenses totaled approximately $41.9 million, including R&D of $14.2 million (roughly double sequentially), far exceeding the quarter's revenue and signaling continued net losses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “EPS helped by opex”; the preview listed Q1 opex at “$29.3M.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed the $150–180 million full-year 2026 revenue range, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the target would be reiterated; the implied H2 ramp is broadly in line with the preview’s roughly $112 million H2 requirement.
Management retained its target of reaching about 30% gross margin by year-end, as anticipated in the preview, although Q2’s 16.1% margin was below the preview’s expected range.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $434,000, below the preview’s roughly $530,000 consensus estimate by about 18%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was $434,000”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … ~$0.53M (3 analysts)”

surprises.description: PLSE had raised $57.5 million net through its ATM since May, lifting quarter-end cash to over $101.6 million from $68.3 million at the end of Q1. The funding improves liquidity, but it also means the equity financing risk flagged in the preview materialized.
surprises.fact_evidence: “over $101.6 million in cash as of quarter-end (up $33.3 million sequentially), raising $57.5 million in net ATM proceeds since May, including approximately $13 million from insiders and $44.5 million from outside investors”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A concurrent or telegraphed equity raise is a key downside risk on the print.”

surprises.description: The pivotal NanoPulse AF study’s enrollment target increased from 145 to 164, and eligibility was broadened so failure of any one of four AAD classes qualifies. Despite those changes—and several high-volume sites reaching a 15% enrollment cap—PLSE still expects completion by early October, with 12 sites active and more being added.
surprises.fact_evidence: “increased the total enrollment target from 145 to 164 patients”; “loosening AAD failure criteria so patients failing any one of four AAD classes qualify”; “several early high-volume sites have already reached their cap”; “active study site base expanded to 12”; “still expects enrollment completion by early October”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided to completion of NANOPULSE-AF enrollment in ‘early Q4 2026.’”

surprises.description: The European feasibility update reported 96% freedom from AF at one year by 24-hour Holter, alongside 90% Kaplan-Meier freedom from recurrent AF/flutter/tachycardia and a 1.7% serious adverse event rate across 177 patients. The 96% Holter result is higher than the preview’s cited 90% 12-month freedom-from-AF figure, although the reported measures are not fully interchangeable and do not by themselves establish replication in the pivotal study.
surprises.fact_evidence: “100% freedom from AF at six months and 96% at one year by 24-hour Holter, with 90% Kaplan-Meier freedom from recurrent AF/flutter/tachycardia at one year and a serious adverse event rate of just 1.7% across 177 patients”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “whether the 90% 12-month freedom-from-AF in the EFS study replicates in the pivotal trial”; “The EFS 12-month cohort is only n=53.”

surprises.description: Investigational sites were performing five to seven catheter ablations per day, with ablation times of seven to eight minutes or faster, versus the stated two to three cases per day for competing catheters. The preview flagged competitive positioning but did not anticipate this specific throughput advantage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Multiple investigational sites performed five to seven catheter ablation cases per day with ablation times of seven to eight minutes or faster, versus the typical two to three cases per day for competing ablation catheters.”

surprises.description: PLSE supplied a new EU regulatory schedule for its cardiac catheter: CE Mark submission in the second half of 2026, with potential approval around mid-2027. This adds a concrete European timeline that the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “plans to submit for CE Mark for its cardiac catheter in the second half of 2026, targeting potential EU approval around mid-2027, roughly six months post-submission”

surprises.description: The surgical clamp program had progressed to over 70 patients at six EU sites, with 94% pulmonary vein isolation success at three months and average ablation time of 4.41 seconds per patient; PLSE remained on schedule for a CE Mark filing before year-end 2026 and targeted US pivotal-study enrollment completion by the end of the first half of 2027. The preview did not flag this program update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The surgical clamp EU feasibility study treated over 70 patients across six sites with 94% pulmonary vein isolation success at three months and average ablation time of 4.41 seconds per patient, remaining on schedule for CE Mark filing before end of 2026, while the US pivotal NanoClamp AF study targets enrollment completion by the end of first half 2027.”

in_line: NanoPulse AF enrollment completion remained on the early-Q4 schedule: the call gave early October, consistent with the preview’s expectation of “early Q4 2026.”

surprises.description: Rocket guided Q3 adjusted revenue to $2.5–$2.7 billion, below the preview’s expected $2.7–$2.9 billion range and its stated buy-side midpoint of at least $2.75 billion. Management also expects the mortgage market to shrink sequentially, alongside rates rising to 6.8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 2026 adjusted revenue to $2.5–$2.7 billion, expecting the Q3 mortgage market to shrink sequentially”; “The 30-year fixed rate rose to 6.8% in recent weeks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base” scenario: “Q3 guide reiterated at $2.7–2.9B”; “The buy side wants a midpoint of at least $2.75B.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.16, one cent below the $0.17 consensus, though it was within the preview’s broader $0.15–$0.17 working range. This was a modest shortfall rather than the earnings beat the consensus implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.16.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS” consensus: “$0.17”; the preview’s working range was “$0.15–0.17 EPS.”

surprises.description: Rocket raised its Mr. Cooper savings ambition by identifying about $100 million in additional annualized savings beyond the original $400 million goal, with the additional savings targeted for H1 2027. The preview expected delivery of the existing $400 million target, not an increase to it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its Mr. Cooper expense synergy target, identifying an additional ~$100 million in annualized savings … beyond the original $400 million goal.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Synergies need +$100M in Q2 and a $400M annualized total by year-end”; the preview described pulling ahead of or reaching “the $400M” target.

surprises.description: Existing servicing clients made up 57% of refinance closings, up from the 54% level highlighted in the preview, and Mr. Cooper recapture rates reached a record. That indicates stronger recapture and low-cost refinance sourcing than the preview’s baseline suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Existing servicing clients accounted for 57% of refinance closed volume (up from 54% in Q1) at near-zero acquisition cost, with Mr. Cooper recapture rates hitting a record.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Recapture reached 54% of refinance closings, an all-time high” and flagged servicing “with … 54% recapture” as a rate hedge.

surprises.description: Rocket reported record purchase and refinance market shares, with purchase share at 6.2% and refinance share at 14.3%. The preview discussed volume and margins but did not anticipate these market-share records.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rocket hit record market share of 6.2% in purchase … and 14.3% in refinance.”

surprises.description: Redfin integration produced mortgage leads that doubled year over year in June and 45% year-over-year growth in direct-to-consumer purchase volume—developments beyond the preview’s focus on the mortgage attach rate and its 50% target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Redfin integration drove mortgage leads to double year-over-year in June” and “45% year-over-year growth in direct-to-consumer purchase volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the Redfin attach rate, noting Q1 was “about 45%, with management targeting 50%,” but gave no expectation for lead growth or direct-to-consumer purchase volume.

in_line: Adjusted revenue was $2.8 billion, near the midpoint of the $2.70–$2.90 billion company guide and close to the $2.82 billion consensus.
The original Mr. Cooper synergy milestones were on track: $100 million was realized in Q2 and $400 million remained on track by year-end, as the preview expected.
The Redfin mortgage attach rate reached 47%, progressing from the preview’s cited Q1 level of about 45% toward the 50% target.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $14.5 million, above the preview’s roughly $12.9 million consensus and even above the $13.9 million top end of the range implied by FY guidance. U.S. revenue grew more than 150% to $12.6 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenue grew approximately 120% year-over-year to $14.5 million, with U.S. revenue up more than 150% to $12.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue … ~$12.9M”; “Implied $12.3–13.9M by FY guide math.”

surprises.description: Instead of reaffirming FY26 revenue guidance as expected, Senseonics raised it to $62–66 million. The new midpoint is $64 million, above the preview’s $62.2 million consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Senseonics raised full year 2026 global net revenue guidance to $62-66 million from $60-64 million, representing roughly 80% year-over-year growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue guidance ($60–64M). … A reaffirm is expected”; consensus was “$62.2M.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin reached 59%, and the company raised its FY26 gross-margin guidance to 58–61% from 55–58%. The guide increase was better than the preview’s stated FY range, which it expected to remain in place.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached 59% in Q2 … the strongest organic margin in company history, prompting a raise in full-year gross margin guidance to 58-61% from 55-58%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 printed 59% against a 55–58% FY guide.”

surprises.description: The European transition did not close on the expected Q2 schedule, and outside-U.S. revenue grew only about 12% to $1.9 million. Management said the shortfall should shift into Q3 and Q4 and still expects Europe to contribute roughly 20% of full-year revenue, so the timing setback is partly offset by its stated catch-up expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Outside-U.S. revenue grew only about 12% to $1.9 million due to delayed European tender updates from the later-than-planned Ascensia transition, though management still expects Europe at roughly 20% of full-year revenue with the shortfall shifting into Q3 and Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The EU commercial transition was guided to close in Q2 2026. Slippage would delay the direct-revenue uplift that underpins H2.”

surprises.description: The reported loss was larger per share than the preview’s consensus estimate: $0.63 versus an expected $0.55 loss. The preview had cautioned that warrant treatment could make the result look close to a $0.62 loss, making the miss smaller than the headline comparison suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $36.7 million ($0.63 per share) from $14.5 million ($0.36 per share) a year ago, driven by SG&A rising to $32.9 million from $9.7 million after bringing commercialization in-house from Ascensia.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 EPS (GAAP) … $(0.55)”; “If [the 8M pre-funded warrants] sit outside basic shares, EPS could look near $(0.62) on identical operations.”

surprises.description: The Eon Care network was already above 90 nurses and performed about 40% of U.S. Eversense insertions, putting it ahead of its goal of 100 nurses by year-end. The preview did not flag this network milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Eon Care network added 28 providers to exceed 90 nurses (ahead of its 100 by year-end goal), now performs about 40% of all U.S. Eversense insertions, and is expected to exceed half by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “100 by year-end goal.”

surprises.description: Cash at quarter-end was $143 million, above the preview’s expected $115–125 million. The preview also expected about $85 million of undrawn Hercules capacity; the call described an expanded facility with up to $85 million more available over 18 months.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $143 million in cash and $55.5 million in debt after raising over $100 million in early May, including ~$90 million net equity proceeds and an expanded Hercules credit facility (up to $140 million with $85 million more available over 18 months).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Expected cash of about $115–125M at 6/30, plus $85M undrawn Hercules capacity.”

in_line: About 60% of new patients came through DTC and 40% through healthcare providers, consistent with the preview’s expectation that about 60% of new patients came through DTC.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $41 million, well above the preview’s roughly $23 million estimate and above its $30 million high end. The main difference was $24 million of IV TPOXX delivered in Q2 versus about $5 million modeled; oral TPOXX was about $13 million, as expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 product-related revenues were $38 million, comprising $24 million of IV TPOXX delivered to the U.S. Strategic National Stockpile and $13 million of oral TPOXX; R&D revenues were approximately $3 million for the quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Total revenue: ~$23M (range $18–30M); Oral TPOXX: ~$13M; IV TPOXX: ~$5M. The preview also said the $26M IV portion was due by end-Q3 and that the Q2/Q3 split was the main modeling swing factor.

surprises.description: Profit exceeded the preview’s modeled levels: net income was about $12 million and diluted EPS was $0.17, versus about $5 million and $0.07 expected. Pre-tax operating income was also about $14 million versus roughly $6 million modeled.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 net income was approximately $12 million, or $0.17 fully diluted EPS; pre-tax operating income was approximately $14 million for the quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Net income: ~$5M; EPS (diluted): ~$0.07; Operating income: ~$6M.

surprises.description: Management said the new U.S. multi-year procurement contract was progressing more slowly than expected. The final product order under the 19C contract was completed, but no replacement U.S. procurement contract was yet in place.
surprises.fact_evidence: The new multi-year procurement contract has been slower than expected, attributed to HHS restructuring, evolving priorities, the transition from BARDA to SNS, and open leadership positions. The Q2 delivery fulfilled the final product order under SIGA's 19C contract, with no new U.S. procurement contract yet in place.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called U.S. government contract commentary the dominant issue and said the base case assumed language unchanged from May; it also noted that FY2027 consensus assumes a new U.S. contract that does not yet exist.

surprises.description: Cash at quarter-end was higher than the preview’s estimated range: SIGA reported about $118 million, compared with an estimate of $95–105 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: SIGA ended June 30, 2026 with approximately $118 million in cash and no debt.

surprises.description: The preview flagged an international first order as a possible catalyst, but the call reported no delivered new-customer order; management was still targeting a contract and hoped to deliver against it by March next year. That provides a timing target, but not a secured order.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is targeting a new international customer contract with an order, and hopes to deliver against that order by March of next year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: International pipeline: “any first order, milestone, or named country”; catalyst checklist: “Hikma MENA first order or new international procurement.”

in_line: Oral TPOXX revenue was approximately $13 million, matching the preview’s estimate.
Quarterly R&D revenue was approximately $3 million, matching the preview’s modeled run-rate.
No new U.S. procurement contract was in place, consistent with the preview’s recognition that a follow-on contract did not yet exist.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $72.1 million, below the $73.54 million consensus and at the bottom of the $72–77 million company range. Weakness across both domestic and international markets also fell short of the preview’s stabilization scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue came in at approximately $72.1 million” and was “at the lower end of guidance, with weakness across both domestic and international markets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 consensus” revenue was “$73.54M”; the preview’s base scenario was “$73–75M.” Its bull scenario anticipated that “APAC stabilizes.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA substantially exceeded the expected $11–13 million range, reaching $17 million. The preview identified holding the full-year EBITDA guide as a key debate, but the company raised it instead.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $17 million” and was “well above the guided range of $11-13 million”; full-year guidance was raised to “$39-46 million from $35-45 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 adjusted EBITDA consensus was “~$12M” and company guidance was “$11–13M.” The preview said to watch whether FY26 guidance “narrows toward the low end” and described a cut below $35 million as a bear-case trigger.

surprises.description: The full-year revenue range was cut again, with its top end reduced from $295 million to $290 million. The change was limited to the top end, but it went against the preview’s base case of reaffirming guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management lowered full-year revenue guidance to $280-290 million,” cutting the top end.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The existing FY26 guide was “$280–295M.” The base scenario expected the “FY guide reaffirmed,” while the preview flagged a “second consecutive FY revenue guide cut” as a risk.

surprises.description: Delivery systems weakened more than the preview’s base case implied: the company placed 770 systems, below the expected 800–900, and delivery systems revenue fell 18.4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Delivery systems revenue fell 18.4% to $18.3 million, with only 770 systems placed versus 957 in the prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “placements 800–900”; its bull scenario expected placements “above 900.”

surprises.description: Consumables declined 3.5%, a milder fall than the preview’s 4–6% base-case expectation, but the decline continued for a second quarter even as the installed base grew. Lower utilization, rather than a shrinking installed base, was cited as the reason.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consumables revenue declined 3.5% to $53.9 million on lower utilization, marking the second consecutive quarterly decline despite the installed base growing 3.8% to 36,516 systems.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “consumables down 4–6%.” The preview called consumables ex-China “the core of the equity thesis” and said a clean-comp decline would weaken the installed-base monetization argument.

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin expanded sharply to 71.8%, up 590 basis points year over year, despite lower revenue. The preview anticipated cost cuts offsetting volume declines but did not forecast an expansion of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 590 basis points to 71.8% from 65.9%, aided by lower equipment costs, reduced inventory charges, and a favorable consumables mix shift.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario said, “Cost cuts continue offsetting volume declines”; it did not give a Q2 gross-margin estimate.

surprises.description: Management expects second-half adjusted EBITDA to fall below $17 million, versus $25 million in the first half, as gross margins decline and R&D, commercial, and normalized operating expenses rise. This near-term deterioration was not spelled out in the preview, even though the full-year guide was raised.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Second-half adjusted EBITDA is expected to decline to under $17 million versus $25 million in the first half,” due to “lower gross margins (~68%), $4 million more R&D/commercial spend, and normalizing operating expenses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on whether FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$35–45M” would hold or be cut; it did not state a second-half EBITDA outlook.

surprises.description: The company plans to seek shareholder approval for a reverse stock split at a September 22 meeting. The compliance notice itself was already known, but the preview had not expected a concrete reverse-split process to be announced.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received a NASDAQ notice for trading below the $1 minimum bid price and will seek shareholder approval for a reverse stock split at a September 22 special meeting.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Any reverse-split language would be a dilution catalyst” and described a reverse split as something that “could raise dilution concerns.”

surprises.description: Management outlined several new growth initiatives, including a US device-rental program already launched and products targeted for 2027 and 2028. These launches and timelines were not identified in the preview’s watch list.
surprises.fact_evidence: Initiatives include “a US device rental program launched in August, a next-generation HydroFacial platform targeting a 2028 launch, a new clinically validated booster in Q4, and a new non-HydroFacial device planned for 2027.”

in_line: The plan to repay the approximately $103 million October 2026 convertible-note maturity with cash on hand matched the preview’s expectation that the company would use cash for repayment. The projected year-end cash balance of roughly $100 million was not specified in the preview.

surprises.description: U.S. comparable sales rose 6.6%, above the preview’s key threshold of 6% for a strong result and its roughly 5.5% base-case anchor. That is a clear upside surprise in the company’s largest market.
surprises.fact_evidence: “US net sales grew 11.6% to $255 million with comparable store sales up 6.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Above +6% supports a re-rating”; the base scenario expected “U.S. comps ~+5.5%.”

surprises.description: The company raised the low end of its 2026 outlook for sales, comps, adjusted EPS, and adjusted EBITDA, while leaving the upper ends unchanged. The preview treated reaffirmation as the base case and an upward narrowing as a bullish outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised the low end of its 2026 outlook to net sales of $1.77-$1.79 billion, comps of 3-4%, adjusted EPS of $0.47-$0.53, and adjusted EBITDA of $265-$275 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance ($260–275M). Reaffirmation is the base case. A narrowing to the top half would be bullish”; prior guidance included sales of “$1.76–1.79B” and comps of “+2.5% to +4.0%.”

surprises.description: Canada comps were only 0.8%, including an approximately 70-basis-point Easter benefit, but Canadian segment profit still grew nearly 16% and margin expanded 330 basis points. The profit and margin strength was unexpectedly resilient against such modest comparable-sales growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Canada comps rose only 0.8% (including a ~70 bps Easter shift benefit), yet Canadian segment profit grew nearly 16% and segment margin expanded 330 basis points on productivity initiatives.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Canada comps “have been flat to negative for four quarters” and described a positive comp as an upside surprise; it also noted Canada segment profit rose 23.5% in Q1.

surprises.description: Thrift IQ produced about 100 basis points more gross-profit-dollar growth than non-pilot stores while keeping average prices equal to or below those stores. The preview did not anticipate this pricing-platform result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new Thrift IQ pricing platform, live in 58 stores, delivered gross profit dollar growth roughly 100 basis points higher than non-pilot stores while maintaining equal or lower average prices (40-70% off retail).”

surprises.description: Thrift IQ also cut new-grader training time roughly in half, and more than half of the 2025 new-store class reached positive four-wall contribution in Q2, ahead of earlier classes. These operational benefits were not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Thrift IQ has cut new grader training time by approximately half and helped more than half of the 2025 new store class achieve positive four-wall contribution in Q2, ahead of prior classes.”

surprises.description: Management set a longer-term goal of 50–100 basis points of annual adjusted EBITDA margin expansion beginning in 2027 and a return to high-teens margins within three years. The preview focused on near-term guidance and did not anticipate this margin ambition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now targets 50 to 100 basis points of annual adjusted EBITDA margin expansion beginning in 2027 and a return to high-teens margins within the next three years.”

surprises.description: Debt refinancing and repricing lowered annualized interest expense by about $20 million over the past year, a material financing benefit not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Debt refinancing and repricing reduced annualized interest expense by approximately $20 million over the past year.”

surprises.description: Onsite donations plus GreenDrop supplied 84.9% of processed pounds, up from 78.5% a year ago, and management said this supported gross margin as the most cost-efficient supply source. The preview did not identify this sourcing shift as a potential result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Onsite donations plus GreenDrop reached 84.9% of total pounds processed, up from 78.5% a year ago, supporting gross margin as the most cost-efficient supply source.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 16.6%, essentially matching the preview’s 16.5% prior-year comparison benchmark.

Q3 adjusted EBITDA is expected to be modestly below Q2 because of new-store opening and pre-opening expense timing, with comps moderating as comparisons tighten; the preview already highlighted back-half-weighted openings, H2 margin pressure, and tightening compares.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $56.4 million, below the preview’s $60.5 million consensus and below the $58.7–62.1 million range implied by prior guidance. The result was weaker than expected despite the preview’s base case of $58–62 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $56.4 million, essentially flat year-over-year versus $56.8 million, as retail partners kept channel inventory below historical norms through much of the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $60.5M” and “Q2 revenue guidance is effectively implied: management guided Q2 to 17–18% of full-year revenue, which at the $345M midpoint is $58.7–62.1M.”

surprises.description: Retail partners kept channel inventory below historical norms through much of Q2, rather than showing the rebound the preview said Q2 would test for. This continued restraint helps explain why revenue missed expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retail partners kept channel inventory below historical norms through much of the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management attributed Q1 to a temporary dip it expected to rebound. Q2 is the test of that claim.”

surprises.description: Reported gross margin jumped to 38.8%, well above the preview’s 29–32% estimate, but $4.3 million of tariff refunds lifted the figure. Excluding the refunds, margin was approximately 31.2%, within the preview’s estimated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin rose 660 basis points to 38.8% from 32.2%, but excluding $4.3 million of tariff refunds the underlying margin was approximately 31.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~29–32% (est.)”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was positive $1.3 million, ahead of the preview’s estimate of approximately breakeven. That improvement came despite substantially higher operating expenses, which rose to $24.9 million, or 44% of revenue, as marketing increased for launches and brand initiatives.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA improved to positive $1.3 million from negative $3.0 million in the prior year period”; “Operating expenses jumped to $24.9 million (44% of revenue) from $18.6 million (33% of revenue), reflecting increased marketing spend for new product launches and brand initiatives.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$0M (est.)”

surprises.description: The company repurchased roughly $25 million of stock in Q2, a sizable buyback not anticipated in the preview. About $31 million remained under the authorization afterward.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased roughly $25 million of stock (nearly 2 million shares at an average $12.53) in Q2”; “$31 million remaining under its buyback authorization.”

surprises.description: New tariff actions raised the effective rate on China and Vietnam imports from 10% to approximately 12.5%, an unanticipated cost headwind. Management said it expects to largely mitigate the increase without materially affecting profitability, tempering the impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New tariff actions raised the effective rate on China and Vietnam imports to approximately 12.5% from 10%, but management expects to largely mitigate the impact without materially affecting profitability.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $335–355 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $44–48 million, as the preview expected.
Underlying gross margin excluding tariff refunds was approximately 31.2%, within the preview’s estimated 29–32% range.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was about $1.50 billion versus the preview’s $1.46 billion consensus, a roughly 2.7% beat. Non-GAAP EPS was $2.95 versus $2.90, also ahead of expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 FY2026 revenue grew 9% (8% constant currency) to $1.5 billion, with non-GAAP EPS up 16% to $2.95.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $1.46B”; “Non-GAAP diluted EPS | $2.90.”

surprises.description: ResMed issued its first-ever forward guidance, despite the preview expecting no revenue or EPS guidance. The FY2027 core revenue growth range of 5%-7% is below the preview’s cited high-single-digit long-term growth algorithm; reported EPS growth is 7%-10%, while core EPS growth is guided to 12%-14% after transaction-related dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “For the first time in company history, ResMed issued forward guidance: FY2027 core constant currency revenue growth of 5%-7% and non-GAAP EPS of $12 to $12.25 (7%-10% reported growth).” Excluding MatrixCare and Noctrix dilution, “FY2027 core EPS growth is guided to 12%-14%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ResMed does not guide revenue or EPS”; the preview also cites the “high-single-digit revenue growth through 2030” algorithm.

surprises.description: The Astral field safety notice and suspension of new Astral sales create a newly disclosed FY2027 headwind: about $75 million of revenue and $0.15 of EPS, with a provision already booked in Q4. The preview did not flag this issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Astral field safety notice creates a ~$75 million (130bp) FY2027 revenue headwind and ~$0.15 EPS drag, as ResMed suspends all new Astral sales for the year; a $42 million provision was booked in Q4.”

surprises.description: Q4 non-GAAP gross margin was 62.3%, below the preview’s 62.8%-63.0% base range and 62.8% reference point. Management said it also fell about 50 basis points sequentially, citing electronic-component and freight inflation and FX.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 non-GAAP gross margin expanded 90 basis points year-over-year to 62.3%, though it declined ~50 basis points sequentially due to inflation in electronic components/freight and a 20bp FX headwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “gross margin 62.8–63.0%” and its catalyst checklist compared results with “62.8%.”
