surprises.description: The company raised FY27 revenue guidance by $6 million to $671–681 million, rather than simply reaffirming its prior range. The new midpoint is modestly above the preview’s roughly $670 million consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year FY27 revenue guidance by $6 million to a range of $671-681 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for monitoring whether guidance would be “raise[d], reaffirm[ed], or cut,” with consensus of “$670.3M” and prior company guidance of “$664–676M.” Its base case assumed FY27 guidance would be reaffirmed.

surprises.description: The FY27 adjusted EBITDA outlook weakened despite the revenue raise: management lowered the expected margin from 49% to about 47% because of increased AI investment. That is below the preview’s expected roughly $329 million of FY27 adjusted EBITDA and 49% margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered the full-year adjusted EBITDA margin to ~47% due to increased AI investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 adj. EBITDA | ~$329M”; company guidance was “$323–335M (49% margin).”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue guidance of $170–171 million fell short of the preview’s derived $173–176 million Street bar. The gap is notable even though management cited a tough comparison and minimal AI search revenue in the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY27 revenue guidance of $170-171 million,” reflecting “a tough comparison against last year's 23% growth and minimal AI search revenue in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Derived Q2 FY27 bar (my inference, not a published figure): roughly $173–176M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin fell further, to 88% from 89% in the prior quarter, and management expects it to remain in the mid-to-high 80% range for the year. The preview specifically flagged whether gross margin would stabilize, so the continued decline was a negative development on that debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 88% (non-GAAP) from 91% a year ago due to higher AI compute spend,” with management guiding to “the mid-to-high 80% range for the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “Non-GAAP gross margin (89% in Q4)” and asked whether “gross margin stabilizes.”

surprises.description: A Stanford/Harvard study of 24 clinical AI models found Doximity’s Ask product had the lowest clinical error rate, 4.8%, substantially below Anthropic’s best model at 13.6%. The preview did not flag this benchmark or set an expectation for the result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Doximity's Ask product posted the lowest clinical error rate at 4.8%, versus 13.6% for Anthropic's best model.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed strong AI usage growth: record workflow prescribers, nearly half using AI tools, prompt volume up over 25% quarter over quarter, and scribe users up 10x year over year in July. The preview discussed AI search commercialization but did not set expectations for these adoption measures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Quarterly active workflow prescribers grew over 30% year-over-year to record highs with nearly half using AI tools, AI prompt volume rose over 25% quarter-over-quarter, and AI scribe users grew 10x in July versus prior year.”

in_line: AI search generated no Q1 revenue, while the majority of contracted AI search revenue is expected in Q3 FY27. This is consistent with the preview’s expectation that material AI search revenue would begin in Q3 and its watch item that the launch remain on track.

surprises.description: Century reported Q2 net sales of $752 million, about 8% below the $818.7 million consensus estimate, even as shipments and realized prices rose sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales rose $103 million sequentially to $752 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … Consensus $818.7M.”

surprises.description: Century’s Q3 adjusted EBITDA guide of $325–345 million is above the preview’s base-case range of $270–300 million and exceeds the roughly $300 million or more that its consensus math said was needed. The guide includes $10–15 million of summer energy costs and $20–25 million from hedge settlements.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA to a range of $325 million to $345 million, with headwinds including $10-15 million in summer energy costs and $20-25 million from realized hedge settlements.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 guided $270–300M” in the base scenario; the key-issues section says consensus math needs “roughly $300M or more in Q3.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $2.46 beat the $2.35 consensus estimate, although the preview’s broader base-case EPS range of $2.30–2.50 encompassed the result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income of $257 million ($2.46/share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS … Consensus $2.35.”

surprises.description: Q2 shipments were about 131,000 tonnes, below the preview’s expected recovery toward 135,000–145,000 tonnes. The shortfall came despite the company reporting that all assets reached full capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A 6% shipment increase to ~131,000 tonnes”; Century “achieved full capacity across all assets for the first time in over a decade.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 shipments of 122,865t should recover toward 135–145kt.”

surprises.description: Realized LME was $3,250 per tonne, $75 above the $3,175-per-tonne Q2 assumption in the preview. That was a modest favorable difference, though below the preview’s estimate of the quarter’s spot LME average.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Higher realized LME (up $350 to $3,250/tonne).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Realized LME $3,175/t (up from $2,900).”

surprises.description: Century ended July with cash exceeding total debt and had reduced net debt to $98 million, a stronger position than the preview’s $220 million net-debt figure. The preview had noted that 45X credits and insurance recoveries were still pending and that capital returns might follow once they cleared.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt reduced to $98 million and $66 million in debt repayments, and cash on hand exceeded total debt as of end of July after receiving a $94 million 45X tax credit and ~$20 million in insurance recoveries.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net debt is $220M”; “returns are possible once project spend, insurance recoveries and 45X credits clear.”

surprises.description: A new executive order will allow Century to import up to 300,000 metric tons annually at a 25% tariff rather than 50%, starting in 2027—a potentially material benefit the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new July 20 executive order will let Century import up to 300,000 metric tons annually at a reduced 25% tariff (versus 50%) starting in 2027, a potentially material EBITDA and cash flow benefit.”

surprises.description: Century disclosed that its retained 6.8% Hawesville stake could gain value after partner TeraWulf signed Anthropic to a 20-year lease expected to generate about $19 billion in total lease revenue. The preview did not flag this data-center contract or potential monetization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Century's retained 6.8% stake in the Hawesville data center gained value as partner TeraWulf signed Anthropic to a 20-year lease expected to generate ~$19 billion in total lease revenue, with monetization possible beginning one year after 2027 energization.”

surprises.description: Management described a persistent global aluminum deficit of about 1 million tonnes in 2026 continuing into 2027, with inventory days nearing all-time lows. That outlook contrasts with the preview’s concern that lower LME prices could make the second-half earnings target difficult to reach.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects a persistent global aluminum deficit of ~1 million tonnes in 2026 continuing into 2027, with global inventory days of consumption approaching all-time lows, supporting elevated prices.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “LME spot is about $500/t below its Q2 average” and questioned whether volume could offset price in H2.

surprises.description: The new Jamalco turbine will enable full self-generated energy from August and save roughly $20 per tonne, an unexpected cost offset to the input-cost pressures the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new TG4 power turbine at Jamalco enables full self-generated energy starting August, delivering roughly $20/tonne in cost savings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged rising “heavy fuel oil, caustic soda, coke and pitch” costs and said alumina and carbon costs were the main path to a miss.

surprises.description: Management identified lower-quality bauxite as a modest headwind for the next couple of quarters, a specific operating pressure not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lower-quality bauxite remains a modest headwind for a couple more quarters.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $327 million was within Century’s $315–335 million Q2 guidance and the preview’s $320–335 million base-case range.
The Oklahoma joint venture’s year-end 2026 FID and groundbreaking target, the $500 million DOE grant, and the planned 2029 first hot metal remained consistent with the preview.

surprises.description: Expensify raised its full-year free-cash-flow outlook to $12–14 million from $6–9 million, well above the preview’s base case of reiterating the existing range. Q2 free cash flow was $6.4 million, up 162% sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow reached $6.4 million, up 2% year-over-year and up 162% sequentially,” prompting management to raise full-year 2026 FCF guidance “from $6-9 million to $12-14 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected the “FCF guide [to be] reiterated at $6–9M”; the catalyst checklist asked whether it would be “Raised, reiterated, or narrowed to the low end.”

surprises.description: Profitability improved rather than showing the further compression the preview flagged as a risk: adjusted EBITDA was $6.6 million, up from $6.2 million in Q1, and adjusted EBITDA margin was about 19.5% versus 18% in Q1. Non-GAAP net income was also positive at $3.4 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $6.6 million from a negative figure last year” and “Non-GAAP net income was $3.4 million, reversing a non-GAAP net loss in the prior-year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted adjusted EBITDA had fallen 26% year-over-year in Q1 and flagged that “a second quarter of compression would weigh on the profitability story”; its catalyst checklist compared margin with 18% in Q1.

surprises.description: New Expensify showed strong growth and had crossed a user-adoption milestone: net-new customer ARR grew more than 250% to over $10 million, 56% of users were on the new platform, and virtually all incremental revenue came from it. The preview described migration progress but did not anticipate this growth rate or revenue contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net new revenue from customers signing up on New Expensify “grew over 250% year-over-year to more than $10 million in ARR,” and “56% of users are now on New Expensify,” with “virtually all incremental revenue coming from New Expensify.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the platform migration was “about 60% complete” and that the new platform “is not fast enough for the larger customers,” but gave no expectation for New Expensify customer ARR growth or its share of incremental revenue.

surprises.description: Despite New Expensify’s growth, management could not say when it would offset churn from Classic, leaving the timing of a return to growth uncertain. This is less reassuring than a clear crossover outlook, although the preview’s base case also allowed for no date.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “could not provide clear forecasting on when its growth will offset Classic's churn.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “any date attached to ‘return to growth’” as a catalyst and its base scenario described “returning to growth” with “no date.”

surprises.description: Card interchange grew 12% year-over-year to $5.9 million, modestly accelerating from Q1’s 10% growth despite the emphasis on letting customers bring their own card. The preview’s key question was whether double-digit growth could hold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expensify Card interchange revenue rose 12% year-over-year to $5.9 million,” growing despite marketing emphasis on the “bring your own card” message.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said interchange grew 10% in Q1 and asked whether “double-digit growth holds.”

surprises.description: The company bought an additional 712,000 shares in the open market beyond the 6.1 million shares taken in the tender, using some of the remaining repurchase authorization the preview highlighted as an open question.
surprises.fact_evidence: Expensify repurchased “approximately 6.8 million Class A shares (about 7% of shares outstanding),” including “712,000 in the open market at an average of $1.63.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the tender took 6.14 million shares and left “roughly $17.6M of authorization,” adding that “whether that remaining authorization gets used is a likely question.”

surprises.description: July paid members dipped to 634,000 after the Q2 average was around 640,000, interrupting the stabilization picture suggested by the April member count. The preview did not give a July expectation, and management attributed the dip to seasonal summer travel patterns.
surprises.fact_evidence: “July 2026 paid members dipped to 634,000 due to seasonal summer travel patterns.”

surprises.description: Revenue was slightly above the preview’s $33.70 million consensus, at $33.9 million, though it remained under year-over-year pressure as expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $33.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 revenue consensus of “$33.70M” and expected about a 5.9% year-over-year decline.

in_line: Q2 average paid members were 640,000, in line with the preview’s expectation of about 640,000–645,000 and close to the April figure of 641,000.
Interchange growth remained double-digit, as the preview specifically identified as the key threshold to watch.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $202,000 versus the preview's $183,000 consensus, about 10% higher. The beat was positive but modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $202,000”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (Q2) … Consensus | $0.183M”

surprises.description: GAAP loss per share was $0.22, worse than the preview's expected $0.173 loss. The call attributed higher expenses in part to stock-based compensation and non-recurring production ramp costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss widened to $10 million ($0.22 per share) from $8.3 million ($0.18 per share) in Q1”; “GAAP operating expenses rose to $10.6 million from $8.9 million in Q1, with over half the increase from non-cash stock-based compensation and the rest from non-recurring production ramp costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS, GAAP (Q2) … Consensus | $(0.173)”

surprises.description: The call provided no quantified second-half revenue target or FY26 revenue outlook, despite the preview's calculation that about $3.07 million of second-half revenue would be needed to reach the $3.35 million FY26 consensus. The preview had flagged refusal to quantify the second half as a bear trigger.
surprises.fact_evidence: The call facts report Q2 and first-half revenue and reaffirm cash-use guidance, but provide no second-half revenue target or FY26 revenue outlook.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Reaching FY26 consensus of $3.35M requires roughly $3.07M in 2H26”; “Any walk-back, or refusal to quantify 2H, would be the bear trigger.”

surprises.description: AEye reported its first commercial win from the sales pipeline: sports analytics provider Alive3D selected it as preferred LiDAR vendor, opening a market category not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AEye was selected as the preferred LiDAR vendor by sports analytics provider Alive3D, marking entry into an entirely new market category and its first commercial win from the sales pipeline.”

surprises.description: Defense demand showed concrete repeat-order progress that the preview did not flag: engagements doubled quarter over quarter, and the lead customer placed a third consecutive paid order of increasing size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Defense is the largest and fastest-growing vertical, with engagements doubling quarter over quarter and the lead defense customer placing its third consecutive paid order with growing size.”

surprises.description: The quarter included $30,000 of customer-funded engineering revenue, a new stream that management said could become a more meaningful recurring contributor; the preview did not anticipate this source of revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The quarter included a new $30,000 contract development revenue stream from customer-funded engineering work, which management expects to become a more meaningful, recurring contributor over time.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash and marketable securities were about $71.5 million, above the preview's expected $68–69 million absent ATM sales. The call facts do not state whether the ATM was used.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with approximately $71.5 million in cash and marketable securities.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Expected Q2-exit cash is about $68–69M absent ATM sales.”

surprises.description: AEye described LightOn production capacity of up to 60,000 Apollo units annually, an operational scale-up detail not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AEye is ramping production through its LightOn line, which is capable of up to 60,000 Apollo units annually.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed FY2026 cash-use guidance of $30–35 million, as expected; it also said cash consumption would be heavier in the second half.

The NVIDIA update remained a validation milestone rather than reported monetized revenue: Apollo was validated on NVIDIA's Drive AGX Thor platform and positioned as a pre-qualified sensor for OEMs in the Hyperion ecosystem.

surprises.description: FIGS reported Q2 revenue of $196.6 million, up 29%, versus consensus of $186.17 million and the company’s low-20% growth outlook. That is a meaningful beat, and the 29% growth also exceeded the preview’s bull-case range of 26–29% only at its upper edge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net revenues grew 29% year-over-year to $196.6 million,” beating the “low-20% growth outlook.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus” net revenue of “$186.17M”; company guide was “low 20% range” growth. The bull scenario projected “$193–197M” and “+26–29%.”

surprises.description: FIGS raised full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to approximately 20%, well above the prior 14–16% range and even above the preview’s bull-case trigger of a raise to 17–19%. The quarterly outlook calls for about 20% growth in Q3 before slowing to about 10% in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 net revenue growth guidance was raised to approximately 20% from the prior 14%-16%, with Q3 growth projected at ~20% and Q4 growth decelerating to ~10% against tougher comparisons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a raise to “17% or more” was the bull trigger; its bull scenario expected “17–19%,” while its base scenario expected “15–17%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 18.6%, far above the preview’s roughly 13.5% estimate. This was a much larger margin improvement than anticipated, separate from the gross-margin effect of the tariff refund.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin (excluding prior-year tariff refunds) surged to 18.6% from 12.9% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Adj. EBITDA margin” at “~13.5%.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS was $0.15, more than double the preview’s $0.07 GAAP consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS rose to $0.15 from $0.04.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 GAAP diluted EPS consensus as “$0.07.”

surprises.description: Instead of the preview’s expected modest year-over-year gross-margin decline to roughly 66–66.5%, gross margin rose to 75.2%. FIGS also recovered $20.5 million in IEEPA tariff refunds, with $15.4 million of refund benefit accounting for 780 basis points of the 820-basis-point margin increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company recovered $20.5 million in IEEPA tariff refunds, driving Q2 gross margin up 820 basis points to 75.2%, of which 780 basis points came from a $15.4 million refund benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross margin at “~66–66.5%” and cited company guidance for a “modest Y/Y decline.” It also said the duty drawback / IEEPA refund was “not in guidance pending clarity on timing” and that any timing or quantification was “unmodeled upside.”

surprises.description: Customer spending was stronger than the preview’s watch thresholds: AOV reached a record $127 versus the preview’s $124 threshold, and revenue per active customer reached $229, above the prior COVID-era peak. Active-customer growth itself was close to the preview’s anticipated double-digit range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AOV increased 9% to a record $127, and net revenues per active customer hit an all-time high of $229, surpassing the COVID-era peak of $227.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether “AOV ≥$124” and whether customer growth stayed in double digits.

surprises.description: International revenue grew 67%, with more than 50 percentage points of growth from existing comparable markets, alongside expansion to 85 markets and 27 openings year-to-date. The preview did not identify this level of international growth or market expansion as an expected result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International net revenues grew 67% to $37.9 million with over 50 points of growth from existing comp markets,” and the company “now operates in 85 markets, having opened 27 new markets year-to-date.”

surprises.description: Non-scrubwear grew 40% and reached 18% of revenue, its highest growth rate in nearly four years, while scrubwear also grew 27%. The preview did not flag this product-category mix or growth split.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-scrubwear surged 40% (highest in nearly four years) to reach 18% of revenue, while scrubwear grew 27% to represent 82% of net revenues.”

surprises.description: A U.S. Customs withhold release order blocked imports from FIGS’ Jordan supplier, requiring production shifts to other partners and airfreight. Management said the disruption was largely mitigated, but the supplier and logistics issue was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. Customs issued a withhold release order blocking imports from the company's Jordan supplier, prompting a shift of production to other partners and use of airfreight, though management says the disruption is largely mitigated.”

surprises.description: The Board authorized another $100 million for share repurchases, taking available capacity to $119 million. The preview did not flag a new authorization or this level of repurchase activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board authorized an additional $100 million to the share repurchase program (bringing capacity to $119 million) after buying back $24 million in Q2 at an average price of $11.94 and $81 million cumulatively.”

surprises.description: FIGS acquired V Coterie to add pins and jewelry, an expansion into new product categories that the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company acquired V Coterie to expand into pins and jewelry.”

surprises.description: FIGS onboarded Bupa Dental Care as a TEAMS client to outfit nearly 400 U.K. dental centers, a sizable new client win not mentioned in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Onboarded a TEAMS client, Bupa Dental Care, to outfit nearly 400 U.K. dental centers.”

surprises.description: Inventory fell 12% to $119.6 million, with management expecting further double-digit declines in Q3. The preview did not set an inventory expectation, so the significance of the reduction relative to plan is unclear.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory fell 12% to $119.6 million with continued double-digit declines expected in Q3.”

in_line: Q4 growth was projected to decelerate to about 10% against tougher comparisons, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a difficult Q4 comparison and slower second-half growth.

surprises.description: The preview’s base case assumed the tariff refund would still be excluded, although it flagged the refund as the biggest swing factor and estimated a $20–28 million claim. Karat recognized a $25.8 million refund in Q2, lifting reported gross margin to 56.6% and diluted EPS to $1.46; excluding the refund, gross margin was about 37.7% and EPS about $0.46–$0.48.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin surged to 56.6%” but “1,890 basis points came from a one-time IEPA tariff refund of $25.8 million”; the refund “contributed $1.00 per diluted share,” with core EPS “around $0.46-$0.48.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “An estimated $20–28M gross claim” was the preview’s estimate; its base case assumed “refund still excluded.”

surprises.description: Online growth was stronger than the preview’s expectation of double-digit growth: Q2 online sales rose 23.6%, and July growth exceeded 37%, with Amazon sales up 49%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Online sales grew 23.6% year-over-year and accelerated further into Q3, with July online growth exceeding 37% and Amazon sales up 49%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said online had “accelerated to double digits in April” and highlighted the FY26 target above $100M.

surprises.description: Karat added four new chain accounts, with revenue expected to begin contributing in Q4 after an inventory ramp; the preview did not anticipate these account wins. The contribution is not immediate, so the near-term financial impact is limited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company added four new chain accounts during the quarter, with revenue contribution expected to begin in Q4 2026 after a two-to-three month inventory ramp.”

in_line: Net sales of $136.3 million were close to the preview’s ~$135.5 million consensus and within the company’s $133.9–136.4 million implied guidance range.
Core diluted EPS of about $0.46–$0.48 was approximately in line with the preview’s $0.48 consensus, despite reported EPS being much higher because of the tariff refund.
The quarterly dividend increased to $0.47, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: ESCO raised FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to $8.30–$8.40, above the prior $8.00–$8.25 range and the preview’s $8.19 consensus. The new range’s midpoint of $8.35 is also above the preview’s base-case expectation of a nudge to roughly $8.15–$8.35.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ESCO raised full-year FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to $8.30–$8.40.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EPS | Consensus $8.19 | Company Guide $8.00–$8.25”; the preview’s base case anticipated FY26 EPS “nudged to ~$8.15–$8.35.”

surprises.description: Sales growth came in below the preview’s 15.3% expectation, and the shortfall was more pronounced organically: sales rose 14%, with only 8% organic growth and the balance from Maritime acquisition revenue. That is weaker than the preview’s expectation that growth would be essentially all organic and its 10–12% organic-growth watch range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported sales rose 14% (8% organic), with the balance from $23 million of incremental Maritime acquisition revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales (Q3) | Consensus $341.4M … Implied Growth +15.3%”; “Consensus +15.3% is now essentially all-organic”; and “Organic growth ex-Maritime versus ~10–12% expectation.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EPS beat the $2.12 consensus, despite the preview treating roughly $2.12–$2.15 as an in-line outcome. The reported $2.20 was also above the prior guide’s $2.15 top end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew 37.5% to $2.20.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS (Q3, cont. ops) | Consensus $2.12”; “A print of $2.12–2.15 reads as in line.”

surprises.description: Orders and backlog were stronger than the preview’s minimum bar: book-to-bill was 1.21, all three segments were above 100%, and backlog reached a record $1.54 billion rather than merely being near $1.45 billion or higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated book-to-bill reached 1.21 in Q3, with all three segments above 100%, lifting backlog to a record $1.54 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “At or above 1.0x with backlog near $1.45B+ is the bar.”

surprises.description: NRG had not clearly troughed: its margin deteriorated to low double digits amid soft renewables demand, and Utility Solutions adjusted EBIT margin fell 130 basis points. This is the downside outcome in the preview’s stabilization debate and weighed on the segment despite Doble gains.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Utility Solutions adjusted EBIT margins declined 130 basis points, as modest Doble margin gains were more than offset by NRG margin deterioration to low double digits amid soft renewables demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NRG trajectory. NRG fell 35.8% in Q2 on sunsetting U.S. tax credits and European permitting delays. Whether it has troughed matters for Utility Solutions margin (~24.7%).”

surprises.description: Aerospace & Defense margin improved beyond the preview’s durability test: adjusted EBIT margin reached 30%, versus the 28.6% Q2 level the preview said needed to hold. Sales grew 23%, though the preview did not set a specific sales-growth expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aerospace & Defense delivered 30% adjusted EBIT margins (up 120 bps) on 23% sales growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A&D sales and margin. Q2 was 28.6%. Whether that holds sets the margin story.”

surprises.description: Test margins moved further from the feared relapse: they rose to 16.4%, up 50 basis points, rather than falling toward 12–13%. Test orders also grew 42%, adding evidence of demand strength beyond the preview’s margin-focused concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Test orders grew 42, driven by industrial shielding projects and EMI filters for data centers, though sales rose only 5% with margins up 50 bps to 16.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Test margin. Q2 was 15.4%. A relapse toward 12–13% would suggest Q2 was timing.”

surprises.description: The Navy awarded a record-sized submarine shipbuilding contract, with ESCO already under contract for the relevant content. The preview did not anticipate this specific award; because ESCO’s content was already contracted, the call did not describe it as a new award to ESCO.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Navy awarded the largest shipbuilding contract in its history for 9 Block VI Virginia-class and 5 Columbia-class submarines, content for which ESCO is already under contract.”

surprises.description: Inogen cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $355–361 million from $366–373 million, reducing the midpoint growth outlook to roughly 3% from about 6%. This is a clear reversal from the preview’s expected reaffirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $355-361 million (down from $366-373 million), representing roughly 3% growth at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (reaffirmed May 7, 2026): Revenue $366–373M (about 6% growth at the midpoint)” and “Expect a reaffirm and ‘second-half weighted’ language.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to approximately $4 million, a specific and substantial improvement outlook compared with the preview’s general expectation of continued improvement and its base scenario of a reaffirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to approximately $4 million, representing 48% growth over the $2.7 million reported for 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue $366–373M reaffirmed, continued adjusted EBITDA improvement”; the preview’s base scenario expected “FY reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Management said select distributor inventory management is expected to pressure international sales in the second half. The preview expected international sales to carry growth but did not flag this specific second-half headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International sales grew 15% year-over-year to $41.3 million … though select distributor inventory management is expected to pressure the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “International carries” was the preview’s base-case key driver.

surprises.description: U.S. rental revenue fell 12%, a steeper decline than the 8% decline reported for Q1, rather than showing signs of stabilizing. The company attributed the decline to HMEs increasingly prescribing portable oxygen concentrators from day one instead of oxygen tanks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. rental revenue fell 12% year-over-year to $11.6 million due to structural channel shift as HMEs increasingly prescribe POCs from day one instead of oxygen tanks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “U.S. rentals were $12.7M (-8.0%) in Q1, and point-of-care shifts are pressuring the rental base. … Check whether the rental decline is stabilizing.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin rose to 45.6%, improving 65 basis points despite the unfavorable channel mix shift. That was better than the preview’s approximate 44–45% reference range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin improved 65 basis points to 45.6%, driven by cost improvements and lower warranty expenses despite the unfavorable channel mix shift.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2’25 adjusted gross margin as “~44–45%” and said there was “No explicit guide.”

surprises.description: Inogen expanded its estimated total addressable market to more than $3.4 billion across oxygen, sleep, airway clearance, and digital health, from $400 million a year earlier. The preview discussed a narrower mask-market opportunity but did not anticipate this broader expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inogen expanded its estimated total addressable market to over $3.4 billion across oxygen, sleep, airway clearance, and digital health (up from $400 million a year ago).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed Aurora’s “~$2.2B U.S. mask TAM” but did not forecast an expanded company-wide TAM.

surprises.description: Aurora’s customer count more than doubled sequentially, providing a concrete customer-growth datapoint. However, the company still did not provide Aurora revenue, so the update fell short of the preview’s possible first hard revenue figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aurora more than doubling its customer count sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The first hard dollar figure, or continued refusal to give one, is the biggest narrative swing factor.”

surprises.description: Voxy had shipped more than 5,000 units, a product traction milestone the preview did not identify as an expected disclosure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Voxy shipping over 5,000 units.”

surprises.description: The company repurchased over 1.1 million shares for $7.5 million in the first half, a much faster pace than the Q1 repurchase activity cited in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased over 1.1 million shares for $7.5 million in the first half of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Only about 298K shares ($1.9M) were repurchased in Q1 against the $30M authorization.”

surprises.description: Despite declining U.S. sales, POC unit volume grew more than 12% and total U.S. segment unit volume rose at a high-single-digit rate, indicating stronger unit demand than the revenue trend alone suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “POC unit volume grew over 12% and total U.S. segment unit volume rose high single digits, suggesting demand strength despite revenue mix pressures.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said U.S. sales returning to flat or positive “would be the highest-quality surprise” and highlighted soft U.S. trends, but did not forecast unit-volume growth.

in_line: Q2 revenue was $95.1 million, essentially matching the $95.23 million consensus and within the company’s $94–97 million guide.
International sales grew 15%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that international sales would carry growth.
U.S. sales declined 2% and remained soft, broadly in line with the preview’s base case of a weak U.S. segment rather than the upside case of an inflection.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $64 million, above the preview’s $62.49 million consensus and the $62 million company-guidance midpoint. The beat was modest, but the headline result came in stronger than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $64 million,” which was “$2 million above the guidance midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue” consensus was “$62.49M”; company guidance was “$59–65M (midpoint $62M).”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $67–73 million, with a $70 million midpoint, is above the preview’s $64–68 million base-case range and reaches its roughly $70 million catalyst level. However, it remains below the roughly $75 million per quarter that the preview said FY consensus implies for the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $67-73 million,” with the midpoint at $70 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “Q3 guided $64–68M”; the catalyst checklist said “Q3 revenue guide vs. ~$70M”; FY consensus “implies roughly $75M per quarter in 2H.”

surprises.description: The core business’s Q3 guide of about $40 million is below the preview’s expectation of a guide toward $42 million or more, tempering the stronger total-revenue outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 guidance puts “core business at ~$40 million” at the midpoint.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Core revenue near $37M and a Q3 guide toward $42M+ would support the 2H case.”

surprises.description: Cash fell by $35.7 million sequentially to $149 million, with the decline attributed in part to inventory for upcoming ramps, rising receivables, and CapEx. The preview highlighted cash and transaction proceeds as an issue but did not anticipate or quantify this decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and equivalents (including restricted cash) fell $35.7 million sequentially to $149 million,” driven by operating losses, inventory build, rising receivables, and CapEx.

surprises.description: The ams OSRAM image-sensor acquisition is now expected to close by Q4/year-end, rather than the Q3 2026 timing in the preview. Regulatory review is still ongoing.
surprises.fact_evidence: The acquisition “remain[s] under regulatory review” and is “expected to close by Q4/year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the acquisition was “expected to close Q3 2026.”

surprises.description: Indie reported a new radar design win with a Tier 1 supplier serving Volvo, described as a high-penetration, luxury-volume opportunity. The preview focused on the previously disclosed $25 million radar order and its delivery timing, not this additional win.
surprises.fact_evidence: “indie secured a radar design win with a Tier 1 supplier serving Volvo,” described as a “high-penetration, luxury-volume opportunity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted the “$25M radar production order from a Tier-1 partner” and said “Any quantified delivery schedule would reduce uncertainty.”

surprises.description: Management described DRAM price increases as accelerating adoption of the DRAMless iND880, with design wins converting within weeks to a quarter across automotive and physical AI. It also said the processor could generate more 2026 revenue than radar, an unexpectedly strong near-term contribution from the vision business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Surging DRAM prices are accelerating adoption” of the iND880, converting wins “within weeks to a quarter”; management “reiterated it could generate more 2026 revenue than radar.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the 2H step-up “depends mostly on the radar and vision ramps,” but did not anticipate DRAM-driven acceleration or that vision could exceed radar in 2026 revenue.

surprises.description: The company cited humanoid-robot makers Unitree and Agibot as physical AI wins and estimated content of at least $100 per high-end robot. This adds a new potential market beyond the automotive ramps emphasized in the preview, though current volumes are low.
surprises.fact_evidence: Physical AI wins include “Unitree and Agibot”; management cited “potential content of easily $100 per high-end robot” and noted “current low volumes.”

surprises.description: Management said the Wuxi divestiture would remove a gross-margin drag and help move the company toward a 55%+ corporate gross-margin goal. The preview discussed a roughly 48% derived margin but did not flag this higher target or Wuxi’s margin effect.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Wuxi divestiture is “seen as removing a gross margin drag toward the 55%+ corporate goal.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “A non-GAAP gross margin near 48% can be derived from the guidance bridge,” and described it as an approximation.

in_line: Q2 core revenue was about $36 million, close to the preview’s expectation of core revenue near $37 million.
The Wuxi divestiture remains under regulatory review and is still expected later this year, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation that it would close “later this year.”

surprises.description: Innodata held its FY26 growth outlook at 40% or more instead of making the roughly 45% increase the preview said the buy-side wanted and its base case anticipated. Management did note that the outlook excludes several large likely-win opportunities not yet fully booked.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management reiterated full-year guidance of 40% or more year-over-year revenue growth, explicitly excluding several large likely-win pipeline opportunities not yet booked at 100%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the buy-side reportedly wanted at least 45%, and its base scenario expected the guide to be raised modestly to about 45%.

surprises.description: Management cautioned that revenue could decline sequentially in Q3 or Q4, whereas the preview’s base case expected sequential growth to resume. This introduces a near-term timing risk despite the reiterated full-year growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management cautioned that revenues could decline sequentially in Q3 or Q4 depending on project mix.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected that “Sequential growth resumes”; its catalyst checklist also called revenue above Q1 a key test.

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin reached 49%, above the preview’s 45% threshold and its expectation that margin would stay near Q1’s 47%. The increase was attributed to a favorable mix of pretraining programs and IP-retained datasets.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted gross margin hit 49%, up 2 points sequentially and 9 points above the company's stated 40% target, driven by a mix shift toward higher-margin pretraining programs and IP-retained off-the-shelf datasets.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist called for adjusted gross margin “at or above 45%”; its base scenario expected margin “near Q1.” Q1 margin was 47%.

surprises.description: Revenue beat the published consensus and cleared the preview’s $90.1 million Q1 comparison, but only reached the bottom of its $92–100 million buy-side range. The result was therefore a modest upside relative to the published estimate, not a wide beat of the more realistic bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $92.1 million, up 58% year-over-year and 2% sequentially, beating analyst consensus by $5.8 million (7%).
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed $86.3 million consensus, but said a realistic buy-side bar may be in the $92–100 million range and highlighted revenue at or above Q1’s $90.1 million as the test.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA of $25.4 million was above the preview’s estimated $21–24 million range, though the amount exceeded the top of that range by only a little.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA rose 92% year-over-year to $25.4 million (27.5% of revenue).
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave adjusted EBITDA as approximately $21–24 million, explicitly labeled as its estimate rather than a published figure.

surprises.description: The CEO transition was not anticipated in the preview: Jack Abuhoff will become Executive Chairman, with Rahul Singhal taking over as President and CEO. The facts provide no indication of the transition’s likely effect on the business.
surprises.fact_evidence: CEO Jack Abuhoff will transition to Executive Chairman effective September 30, with President/CRO Rahul Singhal becoming President and CEO and joining the Board.

surprises.description: Innodata announced an at-the-market equity program that was not mentioned in the preview. It creates an option to raise growth or strategic capital, while also introducing the possibility of shareholder dilution if shares are sold.
surprises.fact_evidence: Innodata is filing a prospectus supplement establishing an at-the-market equity program with Goldman Sachs as lead agent, providing optional supplemental capital for growth and strategic opportunities.

surprises.description: The effective tax rate was about 18%, below the company’s 23–25% long-term target, because of recognized tax benefits. The preview noted that tax rates are lumpy but did not anticipate this specific below-target rate or tax benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: The effective tax rate was approximately 18% this quarter due to recognized tax benefits, below the long-term target range of 23% to 25%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said effective tax rates are lumpy given Philippines and India operations, but did not specify an expected Q2 rate.

in_line: Fully diluted EPS of $0.41 was within the preview’s base-case range of $0.33–$0.42; although it was far above the stated $0.21 consensus, the preview noted that consensus might not reflect the earnings implied by Q1 margins and results.

Customer concentration moved in the expected direction: the preview anticipated the large Big Tech engagement becoming the #2 customer and called for follow-through in concentration. The reported customer became the second-largest, while the largest customer’s share fell.

surprises.description: Gross bookings reached $5.5 billion, above the preview's $5.31–$5.37 billion consensus range and the top of the company's $5.30–$5.43 billion guide. The reported 23% year-over-year growth also exceeded the roughly 19% growth expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross bookings grew 23% year-over-year to $5.5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross Bookings $5.31–5.37B” consensus; the preview also says implied growth was “~+19%.”

surprises.description: Rides totaled 262 million, modestly above the 259.2 million consensus and at the preview's 262 million bull-scenario threshold. The preview had identified rides as its most important number and highlighted concern about slowing growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Completed 262 million rides in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Rides vs. 259.2M consensus”; the bull scenario listed “Rides ≥262M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA grew 37% year over year, faster than the roughly 31% growth implied by consensus. The call facts do not give the quarter's EBITDA dollars, so the size of any dollar beat cannot be determined from the supplied material.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 37% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected approximately “$169M” versus $129.4 million a year earlier, or “+31%.”

surprises.description: The gap between bookings growth and rides growth was wider than the preview's estimates implied: the call cited an 11-point gap, versus about 8.6 points from the preview's expected bookings and rides growth rates. The call attributed the gap partly to lower-bookings bike mix and higher-value Freenow rides.
surprises.fact_evidence: “There was an 11% gap between gross bookings growth and rides growth, driven partly by mix shifts toward bikes (lower bookings per ride) and higher-value Freenow rides.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross bookings growth of “~+19%” and rides growth of “+10.4%,” and said bookings-per-ride was expected to rise “+8.4%.”

surprises.description: Nearly one in three North American rideshare rides was linked to a partner, a new record, and Lyft said those rides tend to be higher value. The preview discussed mix and higher-value services but did not anticipate or quantify this partner-linked milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 30% (nearly 1 in 3) of North American rideshare rides are now linked to a partner, a new all-time high,” and these rides “tend to skew toward higher-value rides.”

surprises.description: Lyft reported favorable driver-side indicators that the preview did not flag: driver supply was near a record, driver earnings per ride and tipping were both up, and Lyft claimed a sizable driver-preference advantage over its main competitor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Driver supply is near record highs with driver earnings per ride up 8% year-over-year and tipping up 10%, and Lyft claims a roughly 30-point driver preference gap over its main competitor.”

surprises.description: Lyft cited 20% rides growth in San Francisco as evidence that AV entry is expanding the market rather than taking rides from traditional rideshare. The preview discussed AV milestones but did not identify this market-expansion evidence as an expected outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “San Francisco showed 20% rides growth,” which management cited as evidence that AV entry “expands the total addressable market rather than cannibalizing traditional rideshare.”

in_line: The Waymo/Nashville milestones were broadly in line with the preview: an 80,000-square-foot depot is opening in the fall, and Lyft-app supply sharing is on track before year-end, consistent with the preview's expected fall depot and H2 2026 matching launch.
Premium modes continued to grow double digits, consistent with the preview's expectation that bookings growth would be supported by expansion into higher-value services.
Lyft remained on track to exceed 1 billion rides in 2026, consistent with the preview's roughly 1.01 billion FY2026 rides expectation.

surprises.description: Maravai raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $33–35 million from $30–32 million, a larger increase than the preview’s bull-case expectation that guidance would be raised. Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $8.7 million also came in above the preview’s $6–8 million base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised adjusted EBITDA guidance to $33-35 million”; Q2 adjusted EBITDA “improved by $19.1 million to $8.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA guide vs. $30–32M. A raise is the core of the thesis”; the base scenario forecast “$6–8M.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $51.4 million, above the preview’s consensus estimate of roughly $48.7–48.8 million. The preview cautioned that a beat driven by COVID residuals or one-time GMP orders would not count; the call said there was no COVID GMP-related revenue in the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $51.4 million, up 9% year-over-year”; “no COVID GMP-related revenue in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (Q2) … $48.7–48.8M”; “A beat driven by COVID residual or one-time GMP orders would not count.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin reached 58.9%, far above the preview’s threshold of 40% or more for ex-COVID gross margin. The company also raised its full-year gross-margin improvement outlook to more than 1,400 basis points, versus the preview’s reference to more than 1,300 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded more than 1,600 basis points year-over-year to 58.9%”; gross margin is “now expected to improve by more than 1,400 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Ex-COVID gross margin of 40% or more”; the company had given a directional “>1,300bps FY expansion.”

surprises.description: TriLink grew 12% in Q2 and is now expected to grow in the high teens for the full year, stronger than the preview’s low-to-mid-single-digit expectation for base growth in Q2–Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TriLink growing 12%”; “TriLink is expected to grow in the high teens for the full year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided base growth to ‘low-to-mid single digits’ for Q2–Q4.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was a loss of $0.02, better than the preview’s cited consensus loss of $0.04–$0.05, despite a conflicting +$0.01 estimate from another source.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS improving to a loss of $0.02 from a loss of $0.08.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS (Q2) … −$0.04 (LSEG/Reuters) or −$0.05 (Benzinga)”; “Public.com shows +$0.01, a conflicting figure.”

surprises.description: GMP consumables grew 55% and discovery mRNA grew 17% even though the quarter had no COVID GMP-related revenue. The preview highlighted the risk that a revenue beat might rely on COVID residuals or one-time GMP orders, but did not forecast these product-growth rates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GMP consumables grew 55% year-over-year with no COVID GMP-related revenue in the quarter, while discovery mRNA grew 17% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A beat driven by COVID residual or one-time GMP orders would not count.”

surprises.description: Management said commercial launches from the non-COVID pipeline are not expected until around 2028–2029, leaving a long wait for those launches. The preview discussed COVID CleanCap revenue and its non-repeat but did not flag this launch timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commercial launches from the non-COVID pipeline not expected until around 2028-2029.”

surprises.description: ModTill adoption exceeded 125 active customers within a year, but GMP-grade orders are not expected until 2027 despite a planned launch in the second half of 2026. The customer uptake is encouraging, while the later order timing delays expected GMP-grade commercialization; the preview did not discuss ModTill.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ModTill adoption exceeded 125 active customers within one year of launch (up from over 70 in Q1), but GMP-grade ModTill orders are not expected until 2027 despite a planned launch in the second half of 2026.”

surprises.description: The company reported a record 67 new discovery mRNA customers in Q2 and had converted 6 of its targeted 9 GMP customer transitions for 2026, including 4 in Q2. The preview did not provide expectations for these customer-acquisition and transition figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Added a record 67 new discovery mRNA customers in Q2” and “converted 6 of a targeted 9 GMP customer transitions for 2026 (4 added in Q2).”

in_line: Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was maintained at $205–215 million, as the preview’s base case expected the company to reaffirm revenue guidance.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations was $1.5 million, well below the preview’s $3.0–$3.2 million base-case range. The measures differ in scope—the preview cited consolidated EBITDA—so the comparison is not fully like-for-like.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations” was $1.5 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Adj. EBITDA (consol.)” of “$3.0M to $3.2M”; it also said a Q2 print below about $2.9M would make the full-year range hard to reach.

surprises.description: The company cut its full-year new-clinic openings outlook to 22–26 from 30–35, and now expects its net clinic count to end the year below 2025. This is a material reduction from the opening target the preview identified as a key issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year new clinic openings guidance was cut to 22-26 from the prior 30-35, and net clinic count will end 2026 lower than 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 guidance of “30 to 35 new franchised openings” and flagged “Unit growth and closures” as a key issue.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $15.2 million exceeded the preview’s $14.57 million consensus by about 4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 14% year-over-year to $15.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave Q2 2026 revenue consensus of “$14.57M.”

surprises.description: Operating cash flow and free cash flow rose sharply, with free cash flow reaching $1.9 million. The preview supplied no cash-flow expectation, so this was an unanticipated positive result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash flow from operating activities grew 152% year-over-year to $2.2 million, driving free cash flow up $1.6 million to $1.9 million.”

surprises.description: Patient retention reached its best level in more than five years, and the new $35 Align One plan raised lapsed-patient conversion by several hundred basis points. The preview did not flag this result or the plan’s conversion effect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company posted its best patient retention rate in over five years,” with the “$35 Align One option” raising “lapsed-patient conversion by several hundred basis points.”

surprises.description: Pricing increases had reached more than 500 clinics without meaningful patient pushback, and management expected the resulting low-single-digit revenue benefit to reach the high end of that range in the second half. The preview mentioned pricing holding as a possible bull-case driver but did not anticipate this adoption or benefit detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pricing increases of $5 and $10 have been adopted by over 500 clinics with no meaningful patient pushback,” with a “low single-digit revenue benefit expected to reach the high end of that range in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull-case driver included “pricing holds.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed repurchasing about 82,000 shares for $677,000, with $3.8 million still available under the authorization. The preview did not mention a share-repurchase expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased ~82,000 shares for $677,000 (avg $8.23) leaving $3.8 million under its authorization.”

surprises.description: Four RD territory buybacks completed year-to-date are expected to save about $630,000 in annualized royalties, an operational benefit not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Completed four RD territory buybacks year-to-date expected to save ~$630,000 in annualized royalties.”

in_line: Q2 comp sales were negative 2.8%, within the preview’s $2% to $3% negative base-case range and better than the -4% level it identified as undermining the inflection story.

Management reiterated FY2026 system-wide sales guidance of $519–552 million, comp guidance of -3% to +3%, and consolidated adjusted EBITDA guidance of $12.5–13.5 million, matching the preview’s expected reaffirmation.
Management expected continued comp improvement in the second half, with Q4 higher than Q3, consistent with the preview’s description of the prior Q1 commentary.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was $54 million, above both the $50.82 million consensus and the $53 million high end of company guidance. The beat was meaningful but not far above the guidance ceiling.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 total revenue was $54 million…above the high end of prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $50.82M” consensus; company guide “$49–53M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of about $0.34 substantially exceeded the $0.276 consensus, a larger beat than the revenue beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS was approximately $0.34.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | $0.276.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin was about 38%, above the preview’s roughly 35% expectation for a seasonally lower-margin quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 38%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 margin is expected near 35%, down from the record 40.7% in Q2.”

surprises.description: Fraud and identity revenue reached $29 million, above the preview’s $26–28 million estimate, but its 14% growth was below the preview’s roughly 20% watch level. The dollar beat therefore came with weaker growth than the preview viewed as important.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fraud and identity revenue was $29 million (up 14%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The FY guide implies $26–28M in Q3”; “growth slowing below about 20%” would undercut the case.

surprises.description: The reported 37% SaaS growth in fraud and identity was boosted by a one-time EMEA age-verification regulatory surge; management put normalized growth in the high teens to low 20s. The preview had noted 19% SaaS growth in the prior quarter but did not flag this one-time source or qualification.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SaaS growth of 37% was inflated by a one-time EMEA age verification regulatory surge, with normalized SaaS growth in the high teens to low 20s.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “F&I revenue grew 28% year over year, with SaaS inside the segment up 19%.”

surprises.description: Check Fraud Defender ACV surpassed $22 million and grew 73%, exceeding the preview’s expectation that it had crossed $19 million at 50% growth. That is a notably faster pace of product adoption than the preview baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Check Fraud Defender ACV grew 73% year-over-year and now exceeds $22 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Check Fraud Defender ACV crossed $19M, up 50% year over year.”

surprises.description: A top-five U.S. bank completed its pilot and joined the Check Fraud Defender network, and Fiserv went live as a reseller with access to thousands of institutions. These concrete distribution and customer milestones were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A top 5 U.S. bank completed its pilot and moved into the Check Fraud Defender network, while Fiserv went live as a reseller extending access to thousands of institutions.”

surprises.description: Check verification revenue was $25 million, above the preview’s estimated $22–24 million, but management attributed the increase to the renewal timing of two large renewals rather than underlying growth. The business was still expected to remain range-bound around $90 million annually.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Check verification revenue was $25 million, up 24% due to renewal timing of two large renewals rather than underlying growth, with the business expected to remain range-bound around $90 million annually.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Back-solving from guidance suggests roughly $22–24M in Q3”; a check-driven beat was described as “lower quality.”

surprises.description: SaaS grew 36% overall and increased to about 46% of trailing-12-month revenue from 41% a year earlier, indicating a faster shift toward SaaS mix than the preview quantified. The one-time EMEA surge in fraud and identity SaaS growth tempers the quality of that acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total SaaS revenue grew 36% year-over-year and now represents approximately 46% of trailing 12-month revenue, up from 41% a year ago.”

surprises.description: The company ended the quarter with about $46 million of net cash, versus the $23.1 million net-cash position cited in the preview. The increase was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with a net cash position of approximately $46 million (up from $23 million a year ago).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net cash was $23.1M after retiring the $155M convertible notes and drawing $50M on the term loan.”

surprises.description: Trailing-12-month free-cash-flow conversion was 70%, down from 99% a year earlier, with management citing working-capital swings, higher cash taxes, lower interest income, and increased capitalized development costs. The preview did not identify this deterioration as an issue to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month free cash flow was $48.6 million (70% conversion), down from 99% a year ago due to working capital swings, higher cash taxes, lower interest income, and increased capitalized development costs.”

in_line: Management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $195–200 million and fraud and identity guidance to $105–109 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a fourth consecutive guidance raise.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $63–73 million is far below the preview’s $80–86 million base-case range and the roughly $85 million level it said would indicate JLWS was flowing on the expected timeline. Management attributed the outlook partly to about $17 million of product revenue delayed by Chinese supply-chain disruptions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $63-73 million (midpoint $68 million) excludes approximately $17 million of product revenue delayed due to Chinese supply chain disruptions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Q3 revenue guide above about $85M would suggest the award is flowing on the timeline analysts modeled”; the base scenario projected “$80M – $86M.”

surprises.description: The JLWS contract’s stated ceiling for nLIGHT is about $607 million, roughly 75% of the two-vendor award—far larger in stated scope than the preview’s focus on the $44 million initial obligation. The ceiling is not the same as committed revenue, but it substantially expands the disclosed potential scale of the program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “nLIGHT's portion ~$607M of an $847M total two-vendor ceiling,” representing “roughly 75% of the combined award.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The $44M initial JLWS obligation was signed July 9”; the preview said the tranche should push backlog toward $150M or more.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue reached $83 million, about $4.4 million above the $78.59 million consensus and above the company’s $81 million guidance ceiling. Products revenue was also slightly above its approximately $58 million guide at $59 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue hit a record $83 million”; “record products revenue of $59 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus was “$78.59M” and company guidance was “$75M – $81M”; products revenue guidance was “~$58M.”

surprises.description: Management said JLWS begins contributing revenue in Q3 and ramps significantly in 2027, with expected contributions more than offsetting the anticipated HELSI-2 decline. The preview identified the possibility that JLWS timing could slip to 2027, so the Q3 start is encouraging, while the substantial ramp remains weighted to 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “JLWS will begin contributing revenue in the current quarter, ramp significantly in 2027, and management expects it to more than offset the anticipated decline of the HELSI-2 program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bear case cited “JLWS timing pushed to 2027”; its base case expected JLWS to be “described as ramping without dollar figures.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $1–7 million signals a sharp sequential profit decline from Q2’s $10.7 million, with management citing lower expected volumes. The preview did not provide a Q3 EBITDA estimate, so the size of this outlook gap was not explicitly priced there.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $10.7 million in Q2”; “Q3 guidance of just $1-7 million reflecting lower expected volumes.”

surprises.description: Q2 products gross margin was 41.2%, just above the 37–41% guidance range and better than the preview’s expected range, though it did not reach the preview’s 42%+ bull-case threshold. The sequential decline from Q1’s 43.6% was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of a step-down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Products gross margin was 41.2% in Q2”; it was “down from 43.6% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 product gross margin guidance was “37% – 41%”; the preview said “A print at 42% or higher” would indicate Q1 was the new baseline.

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $10.7 million was close to the approximately $10 million consensus and within the company’s $8–12 million guidance.

Management’s expectation of no material cutting and welding revenue in the second half was consistent with the preview’s warning that Q1 included non-recurring legacy-market last-time buys and that a sequential commercial decline was expected.

surprises.description: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA was $28.5 million, below the preview’s $35–45 million base-case range, although it improved by $41 million year over year. The result was also above the preview’s bear-case threshold of less than $25 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated adjusted EBITDA to $28.5 million, a $41 million improvement”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (50%) ... Adj. EBITDA $35–45M”; “Bear (25%) ... Below $25M”

surprises.description: NdPr production was 840 metric tons, just below the preview’s implied 845–890 metric-ton range. That was still an 8.4% sequential decline from Q1, consistent with the expected single-digit decline during planned maintenance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NdPr production reached 840 metric tons, up 41% year-over-year, despite an extended planned plant shutdown in April”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NdPr production versus the single-digit decline guide (roughly 845–890 MT implied).”

surprises.description: GM commercial magnet shipments are now expected to start in Q4, with modest initial volumes. That is later and more gradual than the preview’s general expectation of Independence magnet sales beginning in the second half, though in-vehicle qualification testing was successful.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commercial magnet shipments to GM are expected to begin in Q4 with modest initial volumes ramping over subsequent quarters, following successful in-vehicle qualification testing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Independence magnet sales beginning in 2H26.”

surprises.description: MP disclosed a new multi-year gadolinium oxide supply agreement with a U.S. aerospace and defense manufacturer, expected to total nine figures and with economics locked in rather than exposed to spot pricing. The preview did not flag this contract.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new long-term gadolinium oxide supply agreement with a U.S. aerospace and defense manufacturer is expected to total nine figures over multiple years with locked-in economics unexposed to spot pricing.”

surprises.description: Precursor production generated adjusted EBITDA margins above 40%, and about $46 million of prepaid precursor revenue remains to be recognized over the next three to four quarters. The preview did not discuss this contribution or its declining recognition schedule.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Precursor production generated adjusted EBITDA margins exceeding 40%, with approximately $46 million of prepaid precursor revenue remaining to be recognized over the next 3 to 4 quarters on a declining basis.”

surprises.description: MP said Independence magnet capacity is substantially committed between GM and Apple, a level of customer commitment not described in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Independence magnet capacity is substantially committed between GM and Apple”

surprises.description: The 10X facility is fully contracted with the Department of War and reached vertical construction during the call. The preview did not anticipate either the full contract coverage or this construction milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “the 10X facility is 100% contracted with the Department of War and reached vertical construction during the call.”

in_line: Adjusted diluted EPS of -$0.01 matched the preview’s alternate-compiler estimate of -$0.01, though it was below the contested Zacks estimate of +$0.02.
The 8.4% sequential production decline was within the single-digit decline expected for planned maintenance, despite production landing just below the preview’s implied volume range.
Management expects Q3 NdPr production to exceed 1,000 metric tons, consistent with the preview’s expectation that significant sequential growth would resume in Q3.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $117 million, well below the preview's roughly $125 million consensus and even below its $119–122 million bear-case range. The quarter was a company-record second quarter, but its 2% reported growth did not meet the sales expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 net sales rose 2% year-over-year (4% in constant currency) to a record $117 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 net sales consensus was ~$125M, with a vendor range of $123.7M–$131.9M; the bear scenario was $119–122M.

surprises.description: The company cut both full-year sales and EBITDA guidance, rather than reiterating its prior ranges or raising them. The new sales range is also further below the $517.4 million FY2026 sales consensus cited in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Full-year 2026 net sales guidance was lowered to $490–500 million from $500–515 million, and EBITDA guidance was cut to $48–52 million from $50–54 million, citing FX changes and a China slowdown.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said consensus was above company guidance and appeared to be modeling a raise; it noted that a flat reiteration would likely disappoint and that the base scenario assumed the guide was reiterated.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $11.3 million, below the preview's $12.5–13.0 million model estimate, and was nearly flat year over year rather than growing by the preview's modeled 11–15%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA rose nearly 1% to $11.3 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave an adjusted EBITDA model estimate of $12.5–13.0M and implied year-over-year growth of 11–15%; it also cited a 10.3% margin as a catalyst benchmark.

surprises.description: China sales fell 20% amid operational issues, a sharper reversal than the preview's expectation that the prior surge would not repeat. The preview identified low-single-digit Asia growth as a bear trigger, but did not anticipate a steep China decline tied to operating problems.
surprises.fact_evidence: China sales fell 20% due to operational issues, reversing a prior trend of over 30% growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had said China's +40% quarter was unlikely to be repeated; the preview described low-single-digit Asia growth as the bear trigger.

surprises.description: SG&A reached 38.4% of sales, above the preview's roughly 36% level for operating leverage and slightly above the 38.1% comparison it flagged. The company also said growth investments were ramping toward a $45–47 million quarterly run rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: SG&A increased to $44.9 million, or 38.4% of sales, as growth investments ramp toward a $45–47 million quarterly run rate.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said holding SG&A near 36% would add roughly 200 bps of year-over-year operating leverage and flagged 38.1% as the comparison to watch.

surprises.description: North American digital sales grew 26%, below the preview's roughly 30% threshold for supporting its digital-growth thesis. The business was still on track for $50 million by year-end, but the reported growth rate fell short of the preview's marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: North American digital sales grew 26% year-over-year and are on track to reach $50 million by year-end.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said digital growth below about 30% would undercut the re-rating thesis.

surprises.description: Within digital, social commerce revenue surged 177%, and subscription autoship customers had lifetime value more than three times that of other customers. The preview did not call out this channel growth or customer-value difference.
surprises.fact_evidence: Social commerce revenue within digital surged 177%, with subscription autoship customers carrying a lifetime value more than 3x higher than other customers.

surprises.description: The company set a new long-term vision to double sales to $1 billion and raise EBITDA margin to 15%, beyond its current level just above 10%. The preview discussed near-term estimates and guidance but did not flag these long-term targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company set long-term 'vision for growth' targets to double sales to $1 billion and lift EBITDA margin to 15% from just above 10%.

surprises.description: Japan grew 50% and the Synergy Eagle system in APAC excluding China grew 11%, showing strong growth in parts of the region despite the China decline. The preview focused on Asia's overall growth threshold and China's slowdown, and did not highlight these specific growth pockets.
surprises.fact_evidence: Japan grew 50% and the Synergy Eagle system in APAC (excluding China) grew 11%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Asia constant-currency growth above about 5% would be clean and identified low-single-digit growth as the bear trigger.

surprises.description: The company announced a new CFO and a new North America President, including a CFO appointment effective September 1 after the prior CFO's June departure. The preview did not mention the appointments or a succession process.
surprises.fact_evidence: Ruth Perkins was appointed CFO effective September 1 and Janine Weber as North America President effective August 10, following CFO Shane Jones's June departure.

in_line: Gross margin was 73.7%, consistent with the preview's expectation of about 73%; management also guided to a low-to-mid 73% range for the rest of 2026.

surprises.description: MARA’s diluted EPS loss of $1.60 was worse than the preview’s own estimate of a $1.25–$1.35 loss and below even the low end of the preview’s very wide consensus range. The reported $343 million Bitcoin mark-to-market loss was close to the preview’s roughly $350 million assumption, so it does not by itself explain the full estimate gap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss of $611.3 million (negative $1.60 per diluted share)”; “driven largely by a $343 million unrealized mark-to-market loss on Bitcoin holdings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My Estimate” for GAAP EPS: “−$1.25 to −$1.35”; consensus range: “−$1.38 to +$1.43.” The preview also expected “about $350M fair-value markdown.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $174.9 million came in well below the preview’s $206–210 million consensus, but above its own $140–155 million bottom-up estimate. Thus the result missed the cited consensus while outperforming the preview writer’s lower forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue fell to $174.9 million from $238.5 million a year earlier,” with a “28% drop in Bitcoin's average price” reducing revenue “despite higher Bitcoin production.”
