surprises.expectation_evidence: “Comparable sales: ~5% (implied, not formally polled)”; the preview also flagged comps “vs. the +6.5% Q2-to-date figure.”

surprises.description: Restaurant margin was 16.4%, modestly above the preview’s estimated 16.0%-16.3% range and its 16.1%-16.3% base case, though below the 16.5% level it called bullish.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restaurant margin as a percentage of sales fell 66 basis points to 16.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~16.0–16.3%” and gave a base range of “16.1–16.3%.”

surprises.description: The company will add a 1% menu price increase at the start of Q4, taking effective pricing to 2.9% in both Q4 2026 and Q1 2027. That is more than the 1.9% Q4 carryover cited in the preview, which left any additional pricing undecided.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company will implement a 1% menu price increase at the start of Q4, bringing effective pricing to 2.9% in both Q4 2026 and Q1 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 carryover of 1.9% ‘plus any additional’”; the preview said the Q4 pricing decision was still to come.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was nearly $1.7 billion, slightly above the $1.674 billion consensus and the preview’s roughly $1.69 billion base estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 11.1% to nearly $1.7 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 Consensus” revenue was “$1,673.8M”; the preview’s base scenario was “~$1.69B.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS of $1.85 edged above the $1.83 consensus, but came in below the preview’s $1.88-$1.92 base range. It also declined less year over year than the consensus-implied decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS declined 0.7% to $1.85.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 Consensus” diluted EPS was “$1.83,” while the preview’s base scenario was “$1.88–1.92.”

surprises.description: Management flagged a roughly 75-basis-point Q4 same-store-sales headwind from holiday calendar shifts, a specific drag the preview had not identified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management flagged an estimated ~75 basis point negative impact to Q4 same-store sales from Halloween and Christmas holiday calendar shifts.”

in_line: The company remains on track for approximately 35 company-owned openings in 2026, consistent with the preview’s expectation of about 35 openings.
Store weeks grew 5%, within the preview’s 5%-6% guidance range.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $149.7 million, well above both preview estimates of $130.30 million and $135.09 million. The preview’s higher panel was still about $14.6 million below the reported result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose 51.7% year-over-year to $149.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $130.30M”; “Revenue (alt. panel) | $135.09M.”

surprises.description: GMV reached $1.3 billion, above the preview’s rough base case of about $1.25 billion and at the preview’s bull-case level. The preview expected roughly 35% growth; reported growth was 37.9%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 GMV grew 37.9% year-over-year to a record $1.3 billion, exceeding the prior Q4 2025 holiday season peak.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A rough base case is about $1.25B (+35%).”

surprises.description: Subscriber additions far exceeded the preview’s watchpoint of beating Q1’s 44,000 net adds: Sezzle added 140,000 in the quarter, its largest gain since the program launched.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Active subscribers reached 854,000, up 76.4% year-over-year, with a record 140,000 net new subscribers added—the largest quarterly gain since the subscription program launched.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether subscriber adds exceed Q1's +44K pace.”

surprises.description: Average revenue per monetized user rose 16.2%, an additional sign of stronger user monetization that the preview did not specifically anticipate. Purchase frequency itself was close to the preview’s expected level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Average quarterly revenue per monetized user rose 16.2%”; purchase frequency was “a record 7.2x.”

surprises.description: Management said the full-year outlook assumes no contribution from Sezzle Send and very little from SezzleCash, leaving potential product upside beyond the raised guidance. The preview did not discuss either product.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Guidance assumes zero contribution from the upcoming Sezzle Send product and very little impact from the newly launched SezzleCash, signaling potential upside if either product performs.”

surprises.description: SezzleCash already showed some early adoption: nearly 10% of eligible new subscribers used it as their first transaction, with an average advance of about $165. The preview did not flag the product or anticipate an adoption measure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Newly launched SezzleCash shows early traction with an average advance size of ~$165 and nearly 10% of eligible new subscribers using it as their first transaction.”

surprises.description: Although the preview expected marketing spend to more than double, management characterized the elevated spend as a one-time test and expects lower core marketing spend in Q3. That offers reassurance on the duration of the spending surge, though the call facts do not report the payback metric the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marketing spend surged to $19.4 million (more than double year-over-year), described as a deliberate one-time test rather than a new run rate, with management expecting lower core marketing spend in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Marketing payback. Spend more than doubled YoY, with payback held under six months. Any sign of lengthening payback would undercut the growth story.”

surprises.description: The charter application was still planned for this quarter, but that is somewhat later than the preview’s mid-2026 submission target. Management also said full approval is expected to take 12–18 months.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to submit its National Bank charter application this quarter, expecting the full approval process to take 12-18 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The charter application was targeted for mid-2026 submission.”

in_line: Full-year guidance was raised, consistent with the preview’s base case that it would be reiterated or nudged up: adjusted EPS rose to $5.25 from $5.10, and adjusted net income to $185 million from $180 million. The preview’s bull case called for adjusted EPS of at least $5.40.
Purchase frequency reached 7.2x, slightly above the preview’s expectation that it hold at 7.1x or higher.
Full-year credit loss provisions remained guided at 2.5%-3% of GMV, with a seasonal increase expected in H2, consistent with the preview’s expected range and seasonal normalization.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $116.1 million, about 2.7% below the $119.33 million consensus cited in the preview. It was nevertheless within the preview’s lower, FX-based $115–117 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 3.2% year-over-year to $116.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus | $119.33M” and “the implied Q2 2026 revenue is roughly $115–117M. That is about 3% below the $119.33M consensus.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA came in below the preview’s expected range: $15.1 million versus the preview’s $16–18 million estimate and $16–17 million base scenario. The 13% margin was also below the preview’s 14.4% year-earlier comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA fell to $15.1 million from $17.3 million a year earlier, with margin compressing to 13%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 is estimated at about $16–18M”; the base scenario was “$16–17M.”

surprises.description: Management expressed confidence in second-half acceleration and cited a materially higher weighted pipeline, higher average deal values, and stable win rates and sales cycles. But backlog was broadly flat entering H2, leaving the preview’s concern about the substantial H2 growth required unresolved rather than providing a quantified bridge.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management cited “a weighted pipeline value materially up year-over-year, higher average deal values, and stable win rates and sales cycles” as the basis for confidence in second-half acceleration, “with backlog broadly flat entering H2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the guide “requires roughly $70–77M in H2 2026, versus $64.2M in H2 2025,” and described “9–20% growth on flat-to-declining revenue”; its base case said “H2 back-loading questioned.”

surprises.description: Intelligence & Advisory declined more sharply than the preview’s latest cited trend for the related Tech & Analytics/Omdia business: Q2 revenue fell 7.1%, with softer consulting bookings cited as the main driver. This suggests further deterioration in a segment the preview had already identified as weak.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Intelligence & Advisory revenue declined 7.1% year-over-year in Q2 and 5.5% in the first half, driven primarily by softer consulting bookings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Informa Tech & Analytics / Omdia ($30.9M, −3.9%)” under segment trends to watch.

in_line: Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance for revenue and adjusted EBITDA growth, including adjusted EBITDA of $95–100 million, as the preview expected.
Q2 revenue was within the preview’s FX-based $115–117 million estimate, even though it missed the cited consensus.
The company had $120.1 million drawn on its $250 million revolver, matching the preview’s cited drawn balance; cash was $45.8 million versus the preview’s $47.7 million reference.

surprises.description: Twilio reported about $1.5 billion of Q2 revenue, versus roughly $1.42 billion expected, with organic growth of 17% against the 10%–11% guide. That also exceeded the preview’s 13% growth catalyst by a wide margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue reached a record $1.5 billion, up 22% year-over-year reported and 17% organically.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was ~$1.42B (+16% YoY); Q2 organic revenue guide was +10% to +11%. The preview also identified “Organic growth at or above 13%” as a catalyst.

surprises.description: The full-year outlook moved well beyond the preview’s bullish thresholds: organic growth guidance rose to 13%–13.5%, and non-GAAP operating income guidance rose to $1.135–$1.155 billion. Free cash flow guidance was raised to the same range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Twilio raised full-year organic revenue growth guidance to 13%-13.5% from 9.5%-10.5% previously, and reported growth to 18%-18.5%. Full-year non-GAAP income from operations guidance was raised to $1.135-$1.155 billion from $1.08-$1.1 billion, with free cash flow guidance also raised to $1.135-$1.155 billion.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said bulls needed “FY organic growth of at least 11.5% and non-GAAP op income above $1.12B.” The existing FY guidance was 9.5%–10.5% organic growth and $1.08–$1.10B non-GAAP operating income.

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP operating income was $285 million, above both the roughly $255 million consensus and the $250–$260 million company guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: Twilio generated record non-GAAP income from operations of $285 million, up 29% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 non-GAAP operating income guide was $250–260M; consensus was ~$255M.

surprises.description: DBNE rose to 116%, exceeding the preview’s 115% watch level, although about 5 points came from carrier fees and underlying DBNE improved more modestly.
surprises.fact_evidence: Dollar-based net expansion rate rose to 116%, of which roughly 5 points came from carrier fees, with underlying DBNE still improving about 1 point quarter-over-quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “DBNER at or above 115%” as a catalyst and noted DBNER was 114% in Q1.

surprises.description: Gross margin fell to 49.1% from about 50% in Q1, missing the preview’s margin test as reported gross profit growth of 18% trailed reported revenue growth of 22%. The decline was driven by carrier pass-through fees; excluding them, margin would have risen 60 basis points year over year, and gross profit growth slightly exceeded organic revenue growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: Incremental U.S. carrier pass-through fees of $71 million pressured non-GAAP gross margin to 49.1% (down 160 bps YoY), though margins would have risen 60 bps YoY excluding these fees. Non-GAAP gross profit grew 18% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether gross profit grows in line with revenue and identified “Gross profit growth at or above revenue growth” as a catalyst. It cited Q1 non-GAAP gross margin of about 50%.

surprises.description: The call reported strong growth in software add-ons and Verify, metrics for which the preview gave no growth forecast: software add-ons grew over 25% and Verify accelerated to over 30%. This supplies positive attach-related evidence, though it did not quantify Stytch or AI-native revenue as the preview asked investors to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: Total software add-ons grew over 25%, and Verify accelerated to over 30% growth; self-serve revenue grew over 30% and ISV revenue grew over 25%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Look for a quantified contribution from Stytch and any dollar figure for AI-native revenue,” and noted management had called AI-native revenue “modest” in Q1.

surprises.description: Voice growth accelerated to above 20%, with triple-digit growth in branded calling. The preview cited prior-quarter voice growth of 20% and flagged voice AI inflection as part of its bull scenario, so the acceleration and branded-calling strength were favorable developments beyond that stated baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: Voice growth accelerated above 20% with triple-digit growth in branded calling.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 voice revenue was +20% YoY and described “Voice AI inflects” in its bull scenario.

surprises.description: Management guided to 11%–12% organic growth for Q3, calling it the highest guidance in three years, but also cautioned that investors should not expect the 5%+ beats seen in Q1 and Q2 to continue because second-half comparisons are tougher. The preview did not provide a Q3 growth estimate or flag this warning.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised Q3 organic revenue guidance to 11%-12%, its highest guidance in three years, but cautioned against expecting the 5%+ beats of Q1 and Q2 to continue given tougher second-half comparisons.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of at least $650 million was far below the preview’s derived estimate of roughly $800–810 million, implying about a 12% year-over-year decline. Management also guided to approximately $160 million of adjusted EBITDA, and said its assumptions allow the substantially overhauled leadership team time to ramp up.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of at least $650 million, implying roughly a 12% year-over-year decline, with adjusted EBITDA of approximately $160 million versus $241 million in Q2”; guidance assumptions “allow time for these new leaders to ramp up.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Derived Q3 estimate (my calculation, not sourced) … roughly $800–810M”; the preview also says “Anything below about $790M reopens the deceleration debate.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $715 million, about $37 million below the $751.6 million consensus and also below the company’s $750 million guidance floor. That is a much weaker result than the preview’s expected roughly 8% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $715 million, up just 3% year-over-year … and its own expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 Consensus” revenue of “$751.6M”; company guide: “At least $750M”; implied year-over-year growth “+8.3%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.34, below the preview’s $0.40–$0.41 consensus range. The reported GAAP result was lower still, at $0.14 per diluted share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income was $158 million ($0.34 per diluted share)” and “GAAP net income was only $64 million ($0.14 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS” consensus of “$0.41 (Zacks); $0.40 (StockStory).”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $241 million, below the roughly $260 million expected, and its 34% margin was also below the preview’s roughly 34.6% estimate. Operating expenses excluding stock-based compensation rose 12%, with higher platform operations costs tied mainly to the move to owned data centers and AI investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $241 million (34% margin)”; “Operating expenses excluding stock-based compensation rose 12% year-over-year to $504 million,” driven mainly by platform operations tied to the shift to owned data centers and AI investments.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA” consensus “~$260M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin” consensus “~34.6%.”

surprises.description: Management attributed the underperformance not only to macro pressure on large customers but also to the company’s own execution shortfalls—an internal cause the preview did not identify. Management characterized the problems as cyclical rather than systemic, which tempered the negative admission.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management attributed underperformance to both macro headwinds affecting a handful of large customers and its own execution shortfalls, characterizing the issues as cyclical rather than systemic.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged CTV growth as a key debate and asked for a quantified rate; the call reported CTV growth above 50% year-over-year in both EMEA and APAC, alongside nearly 30% year-to-date growth in each region and over 100% in China. This international strength contrasts with the weak overall revenue result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EMEA and APAC each growing nearly 30% year-to-date, China growing over 100% year-to-date, and CTV growing over 50% year-over-year in both EMEA and APAC.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “CTV and Amazon competition” as a key metric to watch and said: “Watch for a quantified CTV growth rate.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $1.2 million, well above the preview’s base-case range of $0.55–$0.65 million and even above its $0.7 million bull-case threshold. The reported increase was aided by new staking and digital-lending interest income.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose to $1.2 million in Q2 2026 from $948,000 a year earlier, aided by new SUI staking and digital lending interest income.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “$0.55–0.65M” in revenue, while its bull case was “$0.7M+.”

surprises.description: Cash at quarter-end was only $3.1 million, far below the preview’s roughly $11 million base-case expectation and below the level it said could prompt a financing decision. Management nevertheless claimed more than two years of operating runway excluding treasury assets, countering the preview’s concern about near-term funding pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents fell to $3.1 million as of June 30, 2026 from $21.9 million at year-end 2025, though management claims over two years of operating runway excluding treasury assets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “cash near $11M”; it said cash “under $10M would force a financing decision within two to three quarters.”

surprises.description: The reported loss was milder than the preview’s base-case EPS range: net loss was $18.9 million, or $0.23 per share, versus a projected Q2 range of negative $0.34 to negative $0.39 per share. Non-cash digital-asset and receivable losses were $16.6 million, below the preview’s roughly $20 million mark-to-market-loss scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SUI Group reported a Q2 2026 net loss of $18.9 million ($0.23 per diluted share)”; the quarter included “approximately $16.6 million of non-cash losses on digital assets and receivables.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was EPS of “−$0.34 to −$0.39” with “about −$20M mark-to-market loss.”

surprises.description: The reported mNAV of approximately 0.72x was below the preview’s estimated range of roughly 0.78x to 0.91x, suggesting a wider discount than the preview’s NAV views implied. The dates and NAV treatment may differ, so the comparison is indicative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SUI Group's stock traded at an mNAV of approximately 0.72x as of August 3, 2026, signaling a discount to the underlying treasury value.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said its NAV bridge implied mNAV “from roughly 0.78x to about 0.91x” depending on treatment of the deferred income liability.

surprises.description: The company increased its Bluefin loan commitment to 6 million SUI and raised its revenue share from 5% to 11%, with stated returns of roughly 5%–6% plus optionality through September 2028. The preview did not anticipate this expansion of the lending arrangement; the higher share improves economics, while the larger commitment increases exposure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company increased its Bluefin loan commitment to 6 million SUI tokens (adding 4 million) and raised its revenue share from 5% to 11%, with the arrangement yielding roughly 5%-6% plus embedded optionality through September 2028.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed $6 million of new investments in agentic-finance companies, including a $3 million investment in Recursive Superintelligence in a $650 million round valuing it at over $4 billion. This was an unanticipated capital-allocation move compared with the preview’s focus on buybacks, equity issuance, and treasury accumulation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company made new agentic-finance investments of $3 million in AI firm N of 1 (via a SAFE) and $3 million in Recursive Superintelligence as part of a $650 million round valuing that company at over $4 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview framed the capital-allocation debate around the “buyback versus equity line” and asked whether management would resume buybacks or issue equity.

surprises.description: The staking yield was about 1.7%, slightly below the 1.8% running rate the preview cited from May. This is a small deterioration in the latest reported yield, though it does not by itself resolve the preview’s longer-term year-end yield target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A majority [of the 109 million SUI tokens] [is] staked yielding roughly 1.7% annually.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said staking was “running at 1.8% as of May.”

surprises.description: The legacy specialty-finance portfolio was down to $2.2 million of non-bank loans, with no significant new originations expected near-term. That indicates a much smaller and more explicitly run-off legacy lending book than the preview’s general description of the company as holding a legacy specialty-finance book conveyed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The legacy specialty finance portfolio has shrunk to approximately $2.2 million of non-bank loans at fair value, with about $900,000 in repayments received in the first half and no significant new originations expected near-term.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described SUIG as holding “a legacy specialty-finance book” but gave no expected portfolio size or run-off outlook.

surprises.description: Q2 billings and revenue declined 1% year over year, missing the preview’s expected 1.3% billings growth and $127.42 million revenue consensus. The preview looked for North America Local billings to accelerate above Q1’s 2% growth, but the call said the top-line weakness was concentrated in North America Local.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 billings and revenue each declined 1% year-over-year, missing top-line expectations due to weakness concentrated in North America local.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … Consensus (Zacks) $127.42M”; “Gross billings … $422.09M (+1.3% YoY)”; “Q2 needs to accelerate meaningfully above Q1's +2% for the H2 story to hold.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA landed at the high end of the $13–$15 million guidance range, above the preview’s roughly $14 million consensus midpoint. That was a modest upside relative to expectations, though still within the guided range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA finished at the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … $13M – $15M” company guidance; “~$14M” consensus.

surprises.description: The business had already accelerated to mid-single-digit growth in July after Q2 billings and revenue declined. The preview highlighted the steep, unproven H2 ramp, so this was an encouraging early indication of improving momentum, although it does not establish that the full-year targets will be achieved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The business accelerated to mid-single-digit growth in July, signaling improving momentum for the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The H2 ramp is steep”; “H2 ramp unproven.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was positive at $15 million, despite the preview’s recent cash-flow backdrop being negative in Q1. The preview did not give a Q2 free-cash-flow forecast, so the size of the gap versus an explicit expectation is not available.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was positive at $15 million.”

surprises.description: Organic-channel revenue returned to growth in Q2 and reached double-digit growth in July, with AI-generated local content and SEO improvements cited as drivers. The preview did not identify this channel as a catalyst or set an expectation for its performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue from organic channels returned to growth in Q2 and accelerated to double-digit growth in July, driven by AI-generated local content and SEO improvements.”

surprises.description: Managed push and email channels delivered strong double-digit revenue growth in Q2 by sending fewer, more effective messages through the customer data platform. The preview did not discuss managed-channel results or set a benchmark for them.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Managed channels (push/email) delivered strong double-digit revenue growth in Q2 using the scaled customer data platform, sending fewer but more effective messages.”

surprises.description: Management reported that engineering output per developer had more than doubled over six months under Project Foundry and set a target for the organization to be AI-fluent by the end of 2026. The preview did not flag this productivity development or provide an expectation for it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Under Project Foundry, engineering output per developer has more than doubled in the past six months, and management targets the organization being AI-fluent by default by end of 2026.”

in_line: Full-year 2026 outlook was maintained at 3–5% billings growth, $513–523 million revenue, and $75–80 million adjusted EBITDA, consistent with the preview’s base case of reaffirmation.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.88 versus the preview’s $0.63 consensus, a much larger beat than expected. About $0.19 per share came from a one-time $15.6 million IEEPA tariff refund that was not included in prior guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS jumped 47% year-over-year to $0.88, boosted by roughly $0.19 from a one-time $15.6 million IEEPA tariff refund that was not in prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $0.63”; “Analysts have not underwritten a beat.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin reached 45%, far above the preview’s roughly 39.9% expectation, but the gain was heavily boosted by the tariff refund: only 131 basis points came from operations, while 393 basis points came from the refund.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 524 basis points to 45%, but only 131 bps came from operations while 393 bps came from the tariff refund.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | ~39.9%”; “Management flagged 15–20% of COGS exposed to tariffs, with no refund assumptions in guidance.”

surprises.description: Sales exceeded both the $395 million high end of company guidance and the $391.3 million consensus estimate, though only narrowly above the guidance ceiling.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose 5.4% as reported to $395.7 million and 3.8% on a currency-neutral basis, exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $391.3M”; “Company Guidance … $385–395M.”

surprises.description: Currency-neutral orders grew 5%, below the preview’s 7% level that it said would support the second-half guide. However, backlog was up 22% year-to-date, ahead of the prior quarter’s 18% increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog was up 22% year-to-date and consolidated currency-neutral orders grew 5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Orders at or above 7% would support the 2H guide; orders at or below 4% would undercut it.” The preview also reported Q1 backlog “+18% YTD.”

surprises.description: Management said Q4 gross margin is expected to decline year-over-year because of the timing of raw-material cost flow-through, a specific near-term margin headwind not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 expected to decline year-over-year due to timing of raw material cost flow-through.”

in_line: Education billings rose 5%; the preview said Q2 would test management’s explanation that Q1’s weak Education result reflected seasonal timing.

The full-year sales range was raised modestly to $1.455–$1.485 billion, consistent with the preview’s base case of a reaffirmation or a small upward nudge, though below its stronger $1.48–$1.50 billion validation scenario.
Ongoing tariff exposure and the absence of assumed future refunds were consistent with the preview’s warning that 15–20% of COGS was exposed and that guidance assumed no refunds.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was approximately $272 million, above the preview’s $254.5 million consensus estimate. The reported year-over-year decline of 8.1% was also milder than the 13.9% decline implied by consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 total revenue was approximately $272 million, down 8.1% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 FY26 Consensus” revenue of “$254.5M,” implying “-13.9% Y/Y.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.56, more than twice the preview’s $0.26 consensus estimate, even though it was down from $1.12 a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS dropped to $0.56 from $1.12 in the prior-year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 FY26 Consensus” adjusted EPS of “$0.26.”

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance instead of making the trim the preview said was widely expected. The preview’s prior guide implied Q4 revenue of about $287.5 million, while the reaffirmed range implies roughly $270 million, slightly below Street expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $1.015–$1.035 billion”; Q4 guidance “implies revenue of roughly $270 million, slightly below Street expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A trim is widely expected”; the guide “implies Q4 revenue of about $287.5M.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted operating margin reached 25.5%, well above the preview’s estimate of about 20%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin fell to 25.5% from 36.9% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating margin (~20% est.).”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year adjusted operating margin and EPS guidance rather than merely holding or cutting them: margin guidance is now 23.5%–24% and EPS guidance is $1.80–$1.90.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised adjusted operating margin guidance to 23.5%–24% and adjusted EPS guidance to $1.80–$1.90 from $1.55–$1.75.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior FY26 guidance was “adj. operating margin 22.25–23.25%; adj. EPS $1.55–1.75”; the preview said “the size of any EPS ... cut is less clear.”

surprises.description: Net leverage ended at about 3.7x, above the preview’s 3.0x reference level and even above the bear scenario’s expectation of leverage rising toward 3.5x. The company said it borrowed about $180 million for the acquisition and repaid about $53 million during the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Borrowed approximately $180 million to fund the Owen Mumford acquisition but repaid roughly $53 million of debt in the quarter, ending with net leverage of about 3.7x versus a 4.75x covenant limit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Net leverage about 3.0x” at Q2 and a bear scenario where “leverage rises toward 3.5x.”

surprises.description: Management put a value and growth estimate on the auto-injector opportunity created by Owen Mumford: an approximately $2.4 billion addressable market growing at a double-digit CAGR. The preview mentioned the acquisition but did not give an expected market size or growth rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: The acquisition was described as “expanding Embecta's addressable auto-injector market, which management estimates at approximately $2.4 billion growing at a double-digit CAGR.”

surprises.description: Management deferred 2027 guidance and an updated long-range plan until later in calendar 2027. The preview did not set an expectation for their timing, so this is an unanticipated delay rather than a miss against a stated preview date.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management deferred issuing 2027 guidance and an updated long-range plan until later in calendar 2027.”

in_line: U.S. revenue was approximately $121 million, within the preview’s estimated $120–128 million range.
Full-year free cash flow guidance was reaffirmed at about $100 million, within the preview’s $95–105 million guidance range.

surprises.description: Q1 net bookings were about $1.39 billion, roughly $20 million above the top of the previewed $1.32–$1.37 billion guidance range. The beat was modest, but it exceeded the preview’s in-line scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 net bookings reached approximately $1.39 billion, slightly above the high end of guidance ($1.32B-$1.37B)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net bookings | Company guidance: $1.32–1.37B | Street consensus: ~$1.35–1.36B”; the base scenario expected “$1.34–1.37B.”

surprises.description: Recurrent consumer spending declined only 1%, better than the previewed expectation of an approximately 3% decline. The 2-percentage-point difference indicates a modestly more resilient base business than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 recurrent consumer spending declined only 1% (better than the guided 3% decline)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Recurrent consumer spending (RCS) | ~−3% YoY | In line.”

surprises.description: Management described GTA VI preorders as “unprecedented and astonishing,” a notably bullish qualitative signal given the preview’s expectation that management had historically disclosed little. It gave no preorder units or sell-through figures and did not raise guidance, saying no units had yet been sold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management calling preorders ‘unprecedented and astonishing’ but declining to raise guidance since no units have yet been sold.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has historically disclosed little”; the preview flagged “any GTA VI pre-order disclosure: units, sell-through, or edition mix.”

surprises.description: The newly provided Q2 bookings outlook was $1.62–$1.67 billion, sharply below the $1.96 billion reported a year earlier, with recurrent consumer spending expected to decline about 5%. The preview focused on Q1 and the full-year outlook and did not flag this near-term contraction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2027 net bookings guidance of $1.62B-$1.67B is down sharply from $1.96 billion a year ago, with recurrent consumer spending expected to decline approximately 5%.”

surprises.description: Cost of revenue rose 17%, including a $43 million impairment charge for canceling an unannounced third-party developer title. The preview did not anticipate this specific cancellation-related charge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 cost of revenue rose 17% to $651 million, including a $43 million impairment charge from canceling an unannounced third-party developer title.”

surprises.description: NBA 2K26 sold over 12 million units, up 9%, while recurrent spending and engagement measures also grew. The preview did not provide NBA 2K performance expectations, so these strong title-specific metrics were not part of its anticipated Q1 read-through.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NBA 2K26 sold over 12 million units, up 9% versus NBA 2K25, with recurrent consumer spending up 7%, average daily active users up 15%, and average games played per user up 35%.”

surprises.description: Take-Two now expects to end FY2027 in a net cash position and raised capex to about $290 million because of a planned real estate purchase. The preview anticipated operating cash flow above $1 billion but did not mention the net-cash target or the property-related capex.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects FY2027 operating cash flow exceeding $1 billion, a net cash position by fiscal year-end, and raised capex to ~$290 million due to a planned real estate purchase.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s FY2027 framing included “operating cash flow above $1B.”

in_line: Take-Two reiterated FY2027 net bookings guidance of $8.0–$8.2 billion, as the preview’s base scenario expected.
Management reaffirmed GTA VI’s November 19, 2026 release date, the preview’s stated baseline.
Mobile bookings declined 7%, reported as expected in the call; the preview had flagged mobile trajectory as a key watch item.

surprises.description: Aflac Japan's Q2 benefit ratio was 64%, well above the 61.7% consensus estimate, and management now expects the full-year ratio at the high end of its 60%–63% guidance range. The quarter was therefore worse than expected on the preview’s most important metric.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Japan's total benefit ratio came in at 64% (down 250 bps year-over-year), but with year-to-date at 63.4%, management now expects to be at the high end of its 60%-63% full-year guidance range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Japan benefit/premium ratio vs. 61.7% consensus and the 60–63% guide. This is the highest-impact line.”

surprises.description: Aflac reported adjusted EPS of $1.75, a small miss against the preview’s $1.77 consensus, even though adjusted EPS excluding currency effects was $1.80.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aflac reported Q2 2026 net earnings of $1.63 per diluted share and adjusted EPS of $1.75, with adjusted EPS up 1.1% year-over-year to $1.80 excluding foreign currency effects.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $1.77”

surprises.description: Aflac U.S. net earned premium growth is now expected to fall just below the 3%–6% full-year guidance range, a downgrade from management’s prior expectation of growth at the low end of that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aflac U.S. grew Q2 sales 2.6% and net earned premium 2.3%, but management now expects 2026 net earned premium growth to fall just below its 3%-6% guidance range, previously guided to the low end.”

surprises.description: Aflac’s U.S. group sales momentum was weaker than expected: despite growth in dental and vision and other group products, management said results were slightly below the low end of expectations and weighted toward Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. group products showed strong momentum with dental and vision sales up 47% and combined group life/disability/dental/vision plus group voluntary benefits sales up 7.1%, though results were slightly below the low end of expectations with the year weighted toward Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “U.S. group business grew 12.4%” in Q1; the preview also flagged U.S. channel mix and growth as a key watch.

surprises.description: Management disclosed a larger reinsurance ceding capacity than the preview anticipated: it raised the internal limit and said Japan’s FSA reserves provide JPY 10.8 trillion of addressable capacity. The preview focused on the near-term earnings drag from reinsurance, not an increase in the amount that could be ceded.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its internal reinsurance ceding limit from 10% of U.S. GAAP assets to 30% of FSA reserves, with Japan holding JPY 10.8 trillion in FSA policy reserves representing the total addressable ceding capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided to a negative earnings impact from the Japan reinsurance transaction ‘for the next couple of quarters,’ and Q2 falls in that window. Whether management sizes and bounds the drag matters more than the number itself.”

surprises.description: Aflac said portfolio switch trades are expected to add more than $50 million of annualized net investment income, an unanticipated potential offset to the preview’s expectation of a year-over-year decline in net investment income.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The investment team repositioned $4.8 billion (about 5%) of the portfolio via switch trades, expected to boost net investment income by over $50 million annualized with limited capital impact, and sees further opportunity ahead.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net investment income | $918.0M” versus “~$1,081M” a year earlier, or “-15.1%.”

surprises.description: Tsumitasu was driving cross-selling of third-sector products well beyond the initial 25% target, a positive product-mix result the preview did not call out.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First sector products now represent less than 20% of total in-force in Japan, with Tsumitasu comprising about 20% of sales while driving concurrent third-sector sales well above the initial 25% cross-sell target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “initial 25% cross-sell target”

in_line: Japan sales declined 5.6% in Q2 against the tough comparison from the 2025 Miraito launch, consistent with the preview’s expectation that Q1’s launch-driven growth would fade as comparisons hardened. First-half sales were still up 7%, and management expects full-year sales to exceed 2025.
Shareholder returns were within the preview’s expected range: Q2 buybacks were $983 million, versus a base-case expectation of $800 million–$1.0 billion.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $45.4 million, above the preview’s roughly $44 million consensus estimate and its $43.5–44.5 million base case. The year-over-year decline was 4%, milder than the roughly 7% decline implied by consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $45.4 million, a 4% decline year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue vs. $44.0M consensus”; consensus was “$43.94M” or “$44.02M,” with “Implied YoY about −7%.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss was $3.5 million, substantially narrower than the preview’s approximate $7 million estimate. It also narrowed slightly year over year despite lower revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed slightly to $3.5 million (from $3.6 million a year earlier) despite lower revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … my estimate ~$(7)M.”

surprises.description: The company improved its full-year adjusted EBITDA loss outlook to $3–5 million from $4–6 million. The preview listed the $4–6 million loss range as the existing outlook, with no expected improvement specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA guidance was improved to a loss of $3-5 million for 2026 (from a loss of $4-6 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 adj. EBITDA … Loss of $(4)–$(6)M.”

surprises.description: The full-year revenue guidance floor rose by $2 million, to $204 million, while the $212 million ceiling held. The preview described a reaffirmation of $202–212 million as neutral, so raising the low end was a modest positive change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $204-212 million (from $202-212 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A reaffirmation of the full $202–212M range is the neutral outcome”; the preview also flagged whether “the $212M high end holds.”

surprises.description: Case volume growth accelerated to high single digits, above the preview’s expected mid-single-digit growth. This was a stronger volume result than the preview’s base case anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Case volume growth accelerated to high single digits in Q2, up from mid single digits in prior quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Case volume growth … Mid-single-digit growth with decelerating price erosion supports the Q4 inflection.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 78.5%, slightly below the preview’s approximate 79% expectation, with management attributing the decline to a shift toward lower-priced products.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 78.5% in Q2 2026 from 79.7% a year earlier, reflecting the shift toward lower-priced products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … ~79% (not formally consensused).”

surprises.description: About 40% of the LAPAplasty surgeon user base had already used at least one of the three new bunion systems, up from 35% in Q1. That reported uptake provides evidence of adoption ahead of the preview’s expected Q3 full commercialization for products including SuperBite.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 40% of the LAPAplasty surgeon user base has now used at least one of the three new bunion systems, up from 35% in Q1 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SuperBite and SpeedXM were guided to full commercialization in Q3 2026. HyperPlate XM was also guided to Q3.”

surprises.description: Management said the new mid- and hindfoot portfolio expands the company’s U.S. addressable market by roughly $300 million, an opportunity-size estimate not raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management estimates its new mid- and hindfoot portfolio (SuperBite, HyperPlate XM, CardiBlaster, Great Release XM) expands its U.S. addressable market by roughly $300 million.”

surprises.description: Management expressed confidence in achieving positive adjusted EBITDA in 2027, a more affirmative outlook than the prior-quarter stance described in the preview. It still declined to provide formal 2027 guidance, as the preview expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management … expressed confidence in achieving positive adjusted EBITDA in 2027, though declined to provide formal 2027 guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management declined to guide 2027, saying it needed to see Q4 momentum first.”

in_line: The $212 million high end of full-year revenue guidance held, as the preview flagged it as a key check; the change was an increase to the low end.
Full-year cash usage is still expected to fall by about 50%, in line with the preview’s stated expectation that cash usage would be down about 50% versus 2025.
The preview anticipated a Q4 inflection; management’s expectation of positive growth in Q4 was consistent with that outlook.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was well above the preview’s bottom-up estimate: $283.4 million versus $250–255 million expected, with revenue up 8.6% excluding the divested property management business rather than the estimated 3% decline. The reported result also exceeded the preview’s bull-case revenue of about $272 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose to $283.4 million”; revenue increased “8.6%” excluding the divested property management business.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base case Q2 revenue of $250–255M (about -7% reported, -3% ex-property management)”; bull case “~$272M (+4% organic).”

surprises.description: The adjusted EBITDA loss was smaller than the preview’s roughly $2 million loss estimate: the company reported a loss of $986,000. That is a meaningful improvement, though it remained a loss rather than the bull-case $5 million profit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA loss improved to $986,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “roughly -$2M adj. EBITDA”; the bull scenario projected “+$5M.”

surprises.description: Cash at June 30 was $105 million, above both the preview’s $100 million positive-signal threshold and its $92–97 million base case. Cash then rose to $121 million by July 31, partly because of a lawsuit settlement receipt.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended June 30 with “$105 million in cash” and had “$121 million by July 31, 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash of at least $100M would be a positive signal”; base-case cash was “$92–97M.”

surprises.description: The company received an unanticipated $13 million net payment from a stockholder derivative lawsuit settlement, which helped lift cash after quarter-end. This is a one-time cash inflow, not evidence of recurring operating cash generation.
surprises.fact_evidence: July cash was boosted by “a $13 million net receipt from a stockholder derivative lawsuit settlement.”

surprises.description: The development pipeline picture was mixed: actively marketed projects fell to $26.1 billion from the preview’s Q1 figure of $27.2 billion, while the company also cited $9.7 billion of additional transaction value scheduled to come to market through September 2027. The scheduled figure extends six months beyond the preview’s stated period, so it is not a direct like-for-like comparison with the prior $8.4 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: The active pipeline was “approximately $26.1 billion”; “an additional $9.7 billion of gross transaction value is scheduled to come to market through September 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The pipeline was $27.2B at Q1”; “$8.4B scheduled to come to market through March 2027.”

surprises.description: Douglas Elliman disclosed an AI transformation using Google Cloud Agentic AI, an initiative the preview did not flag. The company expects meaningful non-commission expense savings only beginning in 2027, largely by replacing existing technology spending, so the disclosure does not imply near-term savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “launched an AI transformation using Google Cloud Agentic AI,” with meaningful non-commission operating expense savings expected “only beginning in 2027,” funded largely by replacing existing technology spending.

in_line: The preview anticipated that luxury mix and higher average prices could support results; the company reported a first-half average transaction price of about $1.9 million and an LTM average of $1.85 million, up from $1.77 million a year earlier.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $257.5 million, well above the preview’s $242.3–$244.2 million consensus range and the roughly $244.7 million “relatively flat sequentially” framing. That is about 5% above the top of the consensus range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $257.5 million, up 6.6% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue | ‘Relatively flat sequentially’ from Q1's $244.7M (≈$244.7M) | Consensus | $242.3M ... or $244.2M”; the preview also flags “Q2 revenue at or above $244.7M” as a catalyst.

surprises.description: Full-year revenue guidance rose to $1.0–$1.02 billion from $985 million–$1.00 billion, rather than being reaffirmed. The raised low end and new high end indicate a better outlook than the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year revenue guidance by two points to $1.0–$1.02 billion (4–6% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue | $985M–$1.00B”; the preview said this was “Reaffirm expected.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance increased to $610–$620 million, rather than being reaffirmed at $605–$615 million. The dollar outlook improved, although the roughly 61% margin outlook is below the preview’s 61–62% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[Management] lifted adjusted EBITDA guidance to $610–$620 million at roughly 61% margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA | $605–615M (61–62% margin)”; the preview’s catalyst checklist says “FY26 EBITDA guide reaffirmed at $605–615M.”

surprises.description: Quarterly adjusted EBITDA was slightly above the preview’s implied $150–$154 million range. The dollar result was stronger than expected, even though the reported margin was lower than the preview’s anticipated Q2 margin near 61–62%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $155.8 million at a 60.5% margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 adj. EBITDA ... implied ~$150–154M”; the preview also said services investment “should keep Q2 margin near 61–62%.”

surprises.description: Levered free cash flow reached $54.6 million, materially above the preview’s roughly $30 million expectation and even above its greater-than-$40-million bull-case threshold. Full-year free cash flow guidance also rose by $5 million to $5–$15 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Levered free cash flow reached $54.6 million (up 49%), the highest quarterly level in 15 quarters, prompting a $5 million raise to full-year free cash flow guidance to $5–$15 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 FCF | $0–$10M”; “Q2 FCF of about $30M or more”; the bull scenario specified “FCF | >$40M.”

surprises.description: First-half ACV bookings reached about $74 million, implying roughly $30 million in Q2 bookings after Q1’s $44.1 million. That comfortably exceeded the preview’s $20 million Q2 threshold, and first-half bookings had already surpassed the entire 2025 total.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half bookings totaled roughly $74 million of ACV, already surpassing the full-year 2025 total of $67 million and up 150% year-over-year, keeping the company on track for its $100 million full-year target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ACV bookings of $20M or more” was a catalyst; the preview said Q1’s $44.1M was “against an $80–100M FY target.”

surprises.description: The sales pipeline exceeded $300 million, with more than three times coverage and about one-third tied to new verticals. The preview had cited pipeline growth after Q1 but did not set an expectation for this level of pipeline or diversification in Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The active sales pipeline exceeded $300 million exiting June (up 50%), with more than three times coverage and about one-third tied to new verticals.”

surprises.description: The TPA vertical was the largest contributor to Q2 bookings and is expected to account for about 30% of this year’s new bookings. The preview discussed ACV totals but did not anticipate this booking mix or the prominence of TPA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The TPA vertical was the largest contributor to Q2 bookings and is expected to represent about 30% of total new bookings this year, second only to the payer segment.”

surprises.description: Management cautioned that current bookings will not translate quickly into reported revenue: new bookings generally take two to four quarters to generate first revenue and another four quarters to fully annualize, so most are expected to benefit 2027 and 2028 results. This tempers the near-term significance of the unexpectedly strong bookings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New bookings typically take two to four quarters to generate first revenue and another four quarters to fully annualize, meaning most current bookings will primarily benefit 2027 and 2028 results.”

surprises.description: Claims intelligence revenue grew nearly 14%, and total P-SAVE revenue reached $220 million, its highest level in almost four years; management said these areas drove much of the quarterly beat. The preview did not give segment-level expectations or identify these drivers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Claims intelligence revenue grew nearly 14% and total P-SAVE revenue hit $220 million, its highest level in almost four years, driving much of the quarterly beat.”

surprises.description: Management cited NSA arbitration outcomes roughly eight percentage points above the industry and analysis indicating nearly half of IDR submissions are ineligible, presenting these as support for AI-driven efficiency gains. The preview focused on DOJ and litigation exposure and did not flag this favorable operating and analytical commentary.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's NSA arbitration outcomes outperform the industry by roughly 8 percentage points, and analysis indicates nearly half of all IDR submissions are ineligible, supporting AI-driven efficiency gains.”

in_line: The company remained on track for a $100 million full-year ACV bookings target, within the preview’s stated $80–$100 million full-year target range.

surprises.description: AIG reported adjusted EPS of $2.00, above the preview’s $1.89–$1.93 consensus range. The beat was about 4%–6% versus the estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted after-tax income was $1.1 billion, or $2.00 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $1.89 (Zacks) / $1.93 (Barchart)”

surprises.description: The calendar-year combined ratio was 89.0%, better than the preview’s 90.1% consensus. However, the adjusted accident-year ratio was 88.1%, above the preview’s roughly 87% margin-build benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The accident year combined ratio (adjusted) improved 30 basis points to 88.1% and the calendar year combined ratio improved 30 basis points to 89.0%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GI combined ratio | 90.1%”; “At or below 87% supports the margin-build thesis; above 88% favors the mix-shift bears.”

surprises.description: AIG disclosed a sizable intentional reduction in its Lexington Property book: retention fell 9 percentage points and the pullback reduced overall North America growth by more than 3 percentage points. That is a drag on the organic growth investors were watching, although the preview did not forecast this specific action.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AIG intentionally cut its Lexington Property book amid E&S pricing pressure, driving a 9-percentage-point drop in Lexington property retention and reducing overall North America growth by more than 3 percentage points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NPW growth, organic vs. Convex/Everest-driven. The market will discount transaction-driven growth.”

surprises.description: Despite $145 million of net favorable prior-year development, AIG strengthened U.S. excess casualty reserves by $74 million for accident years 2016 and 2023. That adverse casualty development was a specific risk the preview flagged, while it highlighted favorable development as an upside variable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Prior year development was $145 million favorable, led by $177 million of favorable U.S. workers' compensation, but was partially offset by $74 million of strengthening in U.S. excess casualty (accident years 2016 and 2023).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Catastrophe losses and prior-year development. Peers reported low cats and large favorable PYD, so a light cat number is largely expected. PYD is the upside variable”; “US casualty reserve commentary and PYD.”

surprises.description: The quarter included $75 million of catastrophe losses tied to the Middle East conflict, contributing to a 91.3% calendar-year combined ratio in International Commercial. The preview expected light catastrophe losses overall but did not anticipate this conflict-related hit to the segment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Catastrophe charges totaled $210 million, including $75 million in net losses tied to the Middle East conflict that pushed International Commercial's calendar year combined ratio to 91.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Peers reported low cats and large favorable PYD, so a light cat number is largely expected.”

surprises.description: Global Personal Insurance delivered a strong improvement that the preview did not identify as an expected driver: its accident-year combined ratio improved 490 basis points to 91.2%, and adjusted accident-year underwriting income more than doubled.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global Personal Insurance delivered a 490-basis-point improvement in its accident year combined ratio to 91.2% and more than doubled adjusted accident year underwriting income, driven by high-net-worth and Accident & Health momentum.”

surprises.description: Pricing was sharply uneven: North America retail casualty increased 10% (14% in excess casualty), while global energy pricing fell 15% and management said it was inadequate. The preview anticipated broad commercial rate pressure but did not flag the particularly steep global energy decline or the strong North America casualty increases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pricing diverged sharply by line, with North America retail casualty up 10% (excess casualty up 14%) versus international renewal pricing down 6% and global energy pricing down 15%, which management flagged as inadequate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Organic NPW growth and reaffirmation of low-to-mid-teens FY26 growth, given a –6% global commercial rate decline.”

surprises.description: AIG repurchased $641 million of shares, below the preview’s scenario expectation of roughly $700 million–$1.0 billion in buybacks, even though the preview identified Corebridge proceeds as a potential source for stepping up repurchases. Total capital returned was $904 million, including dividends.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company returned $904 million to shareholders ($641 million in buybacks and $263 million in dividends).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A step-up in buyback is a real lever”; “Base | ... buyback ~$0.7–1.0B.”

surprises.description: Alternative investment income fell to $13 million from $48 million a year earlier, including an $8 million private-equity loss. The preview anticipated a decline in total investment income, but did not provide an expectation for this component or signal a decline of this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Alternative investment income fell to $13 million from $48 million a year earlier (including an $8 million private equity loss).”

in_line: First-half net premiums written growth was 13%, consistent with the preview’s low-to-mid-teens FY2026 growth expectation; management said this business should support earnings as it earns in through 2026 and 2027.
International renewal pricing was down 6%, consistent with the preview’s cited 6% decline in global commercial rates.

AIG completed the Corebridge separation by selling 25 million shares for $710 million, in line with the preview’s note that the exit was completed around May 7 and that about $710 million of proceeds were expected.

surprises.description: Revenue was $47.9 million, below the preview’s $51.0 million estimate and well below the cited $55–56 million consensus. The miss was sizeable even though the preview noted that consensus might be stale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $47.9 million, roughly flat versus $48.6 million in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The full preview's own estimates are $51.0M revenue”; consensus was “$55.0M (MarketBeat) / $56.0M (Investing.com).”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 28.9%, far above the preview’s 23.5% estimate and its 24%-plus recovery threshold. The result was partly boosted by a one-time tariff refund, which accounted for 230 basis points of the 500-basis-point expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin expanded 500 basis points to 28.9%, though 230 basis points came from a one-time $1.1 million net refund of IEPA tariffs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The full preview's own estimates are $51.0M revenue, 23.5% gross margin, and $0.05 EPS”; a print of “24% or higher” was identified as supporting the margin-recovery view.

surprises.description: EPS was $0.15, well above the preview’s $0.05 estimate, but below the cited $0.19 consensus. Thus, it beat the preview’s base expectation while missing the higher consensus figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP EPS rose to $0.15 per share ($2.5 million net income).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The full preview's own estimates are $51.0M revenue, 23.5% gross margin, and $0.05 EPS”; GAAP EPS consensus was “$0.19.”

surprises.description: The quarter-end backlog reached a record $117.5 million, above the preview’s expectation that it would hold at or above $110 million. The increase from Q1’s $115.1 million was positive but modest relative to that threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total backlog reached a company-record $117.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said that “backlog held at or above $110M” would signal conversion and replenishment.

surprises.description: Management said backlog rose to nearly $130 million in July after strong order pull-through, extending momentum beyond the quarter-end level. The preview focused on the quarter-end backlog and did not anticipate this further increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management disclosed that backlog grew to nearly $130 million in July following strong order pull-through.”

surprises.description: Communications Systems revenue was $3.8 million—near the preview’s roughly $4 million watch point, but still below $4 million and short of the $5–6 million level the preview said would support the margin thesis. However, revenue grew 39.3% and segment gross margin improved substantially, making the result stronger than the sub-$4 million figure alone implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The communication systems segment grew revenue 39.3% to $3.8 million with gross margin improving to 36.3% from 28.4%, driven by order timing and favorable mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a return toward “$5–6M per quarter would support the margin thesis” and that “another sub-$4M quarter would suggest a structural drag”; its catalyst checklist compared revenue with “about $4M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $6.1 million, above the preview’s approximate $4.5 million estimate. Operating income also recovered to $3.4 million from a loss in Q1, despite one-time litigation and consulting costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled to $6.1 million (12.8% of sales) from $4.1 million (8.5%), with trailing-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA at $17.1 million”; “Operating income increased to $3.4 million (7.2% operating margin) … despite $0.9 million in one-time litigation and consulting costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 adjusted EBITDA as “~$4.5M (estimated, not sourced)” and described Q1 as an “Operating loss of about $(0.2)M.”

surprises.description: One-time litigation and consulting costs totaled $0.9 million, below the preview’s warning level of $1.5 million or more that could undermine the one-time-cost framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: Operating income increased “despite $0.9 million in one-time litigation and consulting costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Another $1.5M or more in ‘one-time’ costs would undermine the one-time framing.”

surprises.description: Management quantified two Newark gross-margin initiatives at approximately $600,000–$800,000 in annual savings, with the second benefit expected in mid-Q3. The preview highlighted margin recovery but did not anticipate these specific savings or timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Two gross margin improvement initiatives at Newark are expected to generate annual savings of approximately $600,000 to $800,000, with the second benefit materializing in mid-Q3.”

surprises.description: Ultralife reported more than $2 million of conformal battery orders shipped in 2026 and over $7 million still in backlog, expected to ship before year-end. The preview did not identify this program or its near-term shipment contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company shipped over $2 million of conformal battery orders in 2026 with a remaining backlog exceeding $7 million expected to fully ship before year-end.”

surprises.description: Management said water-based drone programs are expected to add meaningful revenue starting in Q4, with production beginning in early 2027. The preview did not flag these programs or this prospective revenue contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Water-based drone programs are expected to add meaningful revenue starting in Q4 and production in early 2027.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $1.05, below the preview’s $1.08–$1.09 consensus range. The preview implied 4%–7% year-over-year growth, while reported growth was only 1%, with share issuance diluting higher adjusted net income.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EPS was $1.05, up only 1% year-over-year, as new share issuances diluted a 5% increase in adjusted net income.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin rose 5% to about $150 million, below the preview model of $156–$160 million and 9%–12% growth. The reported regulated segment grew 6%, while the unregulated Energy segment grew 2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted gross margin rose 5% to ~$150 million, with regulated segment margin up 6% to ~$125 million and unregulated Energy segment margin up 2% to ~$25 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The model assumes total AGM of about $156M to $160M (+9% to +12%) for Q2.”

surprises.description: Full-year 2026 capital guidance increased by $100 million, to $550–$600 million, versus the preview’s $450–$500 million guidance. The additional spending is tied to initial FEP costs and higher regulated distribution and infrastructure investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 capital guidance was raised by $100 million to a range of $550 million to $600 million, driven by initial FEP spending and increased regulated distribution and infrastructure investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “2026 capex of $450M to $500M.”

surprises.description: The five-year capital plan rose to more than $2.2 billion for 2024–2028, well above the preview’s prior $1.5–$1.8 billion range. The larger plan indicates substantially more investment, though it also means higher capital requirements.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The five-year capital plan was upgraded, now expecting to exceed $2.2 billion from 2024 through 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “within a 2024–2028 capex plan of $1.5B to $1.8B.”

surprises.description: The company did not issue new 2027–2031 capital or earnings-growth guidance, deferring it until February 2027. Although it raised the existing 2024–2028 capital plan, the call left the preview’s question about growth beyond 2028 unanswered.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed its 2028 EPS guidance of $7.75 to $8.00 but deferred issuing new 2027-2031 capital and earnings growth guidance until the February 2027 call.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The setup in one line: Management has said it will detail the $1.2B Florida Energy Pathway and refreshed long-term capital expectations on this call”; “whether the EPS growth algorithm extends beyond 2028.”

surprises.description: Florida City Gas interim rates were already approved and are expected to contribute over $6 million of 2026 revenue, ahead of the preview’s expectation that interim rates would arrive in Q3. The Office of Public Counsel’s opposing position remains a counterpoint in the broader rate case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $16 million annualized interim adjustment already approved generating over $6 million of 2026 revenue, though the Office of Public Counsel has taken an opposing position.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Interim rates were guided to Q3 2026”; “Confirmation or slippage matters.”

surprises.description: Management quantified transmission-project gross margin at about $33 million in 2026 and a further $51 million in 2027, adding a substantial forward contribution not quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Transmission projects are forecast to contribute approximately $33 million of gross margin in 2026 and an additional $51 million in 2027.”

surprises.description: The company increased its revolving credit capacity by $200 million to $650 million. The preview focused on the FEP’s partner funding and expected debt and equity needs, but did not anticipate this additional credit capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company increased its revolving credit capacity by $200 million to $650 million.”

in_line: The Florida Energy Pathway’s roughly $1.2 billion scale, 2030 in-service timing, and nearly 250,000 dekatherms/day of investment-grade shipper commitments were consistent with the preview’s description of the announced project. The up-to-49% partner-funding structure also matched the preview’s expectation that CPK would sell up to 49%.
The company reaffirmed its 2028 adjusted EPS guidance of $7.75 to $8.00, consistent with the preview’s stated target.
The Worcester Resiliency Upgrade LNG facility is expected online early next year, consistent with the preview’s expectation of an early-2027 in-service date.
The FCG rate-case request of about $47 million and an 11.25% ROE were in line with the preview’s stated $46.9 million request and 11.25% ROE.
The 7.3% dividend increase was consistent with the increase already reported in the preview.

surprises.description: Oklo raised its 2026 operating cash-use guidance to $120–150 million from $80–100 million, above the range the preview identified as the baseline. The company attributed the increase to accelerated first-of-a-kind spending at Aurora-INL.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oklo raised its 2026 operating cash use guidance to $120–150 million (from $80–100 million), driven by accelerated first-of-a-kind project spending at Aurora-INL.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “2026 operating cash use | $80–100M | Company framing / sell-side, mid-2026”

surprises.description: Oklo ended Q2 with $3 billion in cash and marketable securities, well above the preview’s modeled $2.44–2.48 billion. The stronger liquidity came with substantially more ATM issuance than the $1.2 billion raised by March 31, so the cash upside also implies greater dilution than the preview baseline suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $3 billion in cash and marketable securities, including $1.9 billion raised via ATM programs in 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Liquidity: $2.54B cash and marketable securities at 3/31/26, after $1.2B of ATM proceeds. Modeled quarter-end liquidity is roughly $2.44–2.48B.”

surprises.description: Oklo raised its 2026 PP&E capex guidance to $400–500 million from $350–450 million, another increase in planned project spending. The preview flagged the FY26 capex bracket as something to watch but did not state the prior dollar range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oklo raised its…PP&E capex guidance to $400–500 million (from $350–450 million), driven by accelerated first-of-a-kind project spending at Aurora-INL.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Quarter-end liquidity, diluted share count versus 174.0M, and FY26 capex bracket.”

surprises.description: Oklo expects its first isotope revenue in early 2027, likely from its Idaho radioisotope lab, rather than leaving the first-revenue timing unspecified as in the preview’s base case. This gives a more concrete and earlier revenue milestone, though it is not commercial power revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oklo expects first isotope revenue in early 2027, likely from its Idaho radioisotope lab rather than Groves.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario cited “no revenue date,” while its catalyst checklist said to watch for “a date for first isotope revenue.”

surprises.description: Centrus’s letter of intent contemplates HALEU supply for the initial cores and reloads of up to five Aurora powerhouses for multiple years, with deliveries expected to begin in 2029. The preview flagged fuel sourcing as an issue to watch but did not anticipate this specific scale or timing of a supply arrangement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Centrus letter of intent contemplates domestic HALEU supply sufficient for initial core and reload needs of up to 5 Aurora powerhouses for multiple years, with deliveries expected to begin in 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Fuel and grid interconnection. Aurora fuel facility milestones, HALEU sourcing, and PJM interconnection timing…”

surprises.description: DOE selected Oklo for advanced negotiations over a roughly 20-ton surplus-plutonium tranche that could be blended into HALEU-equivalent bridge fuel. This potential additional fuel source was not specified in the preview, and its timing remains uncertain and outside Oklo’s control.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DOE selected Oklo for advanced negotiations on surplus plutonium (from a ~20-ton tranche) that could be blended at 10–13% plutonium content to create HALEU-equivalent bridge fuel, though timing remains outside Oklo’s control.”

surprises.description: Oklo acquired ARMEC and Creative Engineers to bring more engineering and manufacturing expertise in-house; ARMEC is already contributing to Aurora-INL procurement. These acquisitions and their stated capabilities were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “During the quarter Oklo acquired ARMEC and Creative Engineers (CEI) to strengthen in-house engineering and manufacturing, with ARMEC already contributing to Aurora-INL procurement and CEI adding ~30 years of sodium/alkali metal systems experience.”

surprises.description: Oklo signed an MOU with Kiewit for EPC planning on the initial phase of its planned 1.2-gigawatt Ohio campus and is advancing multiple PJM interconnection applications. The preview highlighted Ohio customer conversion and interconnection as issues to watch but did not anticipate this specific EPC-planning step.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oklo signed an MOU with Kiewit to support EPC planning for the initial phase of its planned 1.2-gigawatt Ohio clean energy campus and is advancing multiple PJM interconnection applications.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A binding, priced PPA with a delivery date matters more than pipeline growth” and “Fuel and grid interconnection…PJM interconnection timing…”

in_line: Groves had already achieved first criticality before the release, as the preview stated it achieved first criticality on Aug. 5 and was announced Aug. 6.
Aurora-INL remained on track for a planned 2028 startup, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the project would remain on track for a late-2027/early-2028 timeframe.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $8.1 million, above the preview’s $7.88 million consensus and the company’s $7.7 million minimum guidance. The beat was modest rather than a major upside surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue grew 11% year-over-year to $8.1 million, exceeding the company's May guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: ‘At least $7.7M’” and “Consensus $7.88M (+8% YoY).”

surprises.description: The company ended Q2 with about $20 million in cash and short-term investments, well above the preview’s roughly $14 million base-case ending-cash estimate. The preview expected cash use to decline sequentially, but modeled about $9 million of Q2 use.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with only about $20 million in cash and short-term investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base case Q2 use is ~$9M, leaving ~$14M” and “Cash use declines sequentially.”
