surprises.description: Funding appears less available and more reliant on future financing than the preview’s framing of $25 million undrawn Trinity capacity suggested: management expects a $10 million tranche later this year, describes another $10 million tranche in mid-2027 as potential, and also relies on warrant exercises.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is relying on a $10 million debt tranche from Trinity Capital later this year, a potential second $10 million tranche in mid-2027, and warrant exercises to fund a path to positive cash flow by end of 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 burn was ~$16M. Base case Q2 use is ~$9M, leaving ~$14M, plus $25M undrawn. Management's answer on what gates the undrawn tranche matters.” The preview also described the $25M as “accessible without milestone gates.”

surprises.description: The MilliporeSigma partnership is expected to contribute more in the second half and into 2027, but management said it will not fully meet its calendar-year commitment. That limits the contribution to the heavy second-half placement load the preview flagged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The MilliporeSigma partnership contributed to first-half placements and is expected to increase meaningfully in the second half and into 2027, though it will not fully deliver on its calendar-year commitment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 guided to at least 4 after 6 in Q1. Full-year target is 30–38, which implies a heavy 2H load. Named, dated multi-system commitments matter more than pipeline language.”

surprises.description: Management announced an efficiency program with additional expense and cash-use savings that the preview did not anticipate: about $1 million for the rest of 2026 and roughly $3 million annually beginning in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A newly executed efficiency program is expected to cut expenses and cash usage by roughly $1 million for the rest of 2026 and about $3 million annually beginning in 2027.”

surprises.description: The company raised full-year validation guidance to at least 27 systems, a new operating target not covered in the preview. This is a positive guidance update, though the preview provided no prior validation target for comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year validation guidance to at least 27 systems.”

surprises.description: Management provided long-term targets not included in the preview: greater than 20% average annual revenue growth and gross margin above 50% exiting 2028, with 2027 gross margin expected to exceed the 2026 exit rate. These add a longer-term ambition beyond the preview’s FY26 margin outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management set long-term targets of greater than 20% average annual revenue growth and 50%+ gross margin exiting 2028, with 2027 gross margin expected to exceed the 2026 exit rate.”

in_line: Q2 gross margin was 15%, consistent with the preview’s mid-teens expectation; the company’s mid-to-high-20s Q4 gross-margin outlook broadly fits the preview’s mid-20s exit path.
The company reaffirmed FY26 revenue guidance of $37–41 million and system-placement guidance of 30–38, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Under Armour cut its FY2027 revenue outlook from a slight decline to a mid-single-digit decline, a notable deterioration from the stabilization outlook investors were watching. It maintained adjusted operating income guidance at $140 million to $160 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered its full-year fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to a mid-single-digit decline (from previously slightly down) due to softer consumer demand, while maintaining its adjusted operating income guidance of $140 million to $160 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 guidance (May 12, 2026): revenue slight decline”; the preview also said the key issue was whether the company would “reiterate, raise, or trim” its guidance.

surprises.description: Q1 adjusted operating income and EPS both came in well above the expected range: operating income was $52 million versus company guidance of $30 million to $40 million, and EPS was $0.05 versus guidance of $0.00 to $0.02 and $0.02 consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income of $52 million significantly exceeded the company's outlook range of $30 million to $40 million, and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.05 also beat guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating income” guidance: “$30–40M”; “Adj. diluted EPS” guidance: “$0.00–$0.02,” with “$0.02” consensus.

surprises.description: North America revenue declined 9%, worse than the preview's already-negative 7% to 8% company guide and contrary to the possibility that the region might be tracking better than the guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North America down 9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “North America revenue” company guidance: “-7% to -8%”; the preview highlighted whether North America was “tracking better than -7%.”

surprises.description: Gross margin expanded 590 basis points, far more than the preview's reference to a small gain, although the preview had warned that tariff refunds could inflate the figure. The reported expansion was largely driven by refunds rather than solely by underlying operations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 590 basis points year-over-year to 54.1%, driven largely by 640 basis points of benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds related to fiscal 2026 costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 is the toughest YoY comparison, so a small GM gain should not be read as a miss”; the preview also said to “watch for a one-time refund credit inflating adjusted gross margin.”

surprises.description: The Q2 adjusted EPS outlook was substantially weaker than the preview's expected $0.03 to $0.05: Under Armour guided to an adjusted loss per share instead.
surprises.fact_evidence: “For Q2, the company guided to ... an adjusted diluted loss per share of $0.01 to $0.03.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A UBS preview says ... a Q2 guide of $0.03–$0.05.”

surprises.description: Management reversed the expected increase in marketing investment, now expecting marketing to decline both as a share of revenue and in absolute dollars. That may support near-term costs but is a pullback from the planned investment level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now expects marketing spend to decline as a percentage of revenue (toward the low end of the 10%-11% range) and in absolute dollars, reversing prior guidance for higher marketing investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The FY27 guide “includes ... about $30M of incremental marketing.”

surprises.description: Management reported a sharp deterioration in traffic from mid-to-late May onward, particularly in North America and Asia Pacific, rather than evidence of the stabilization investors were watching. It also cited China stock-outs and aggressive discounting by licensees as additional pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Traffic deteriorated sharply from mid-to-late May forward, particularly in North America and Asia Pacific, with China further hurt by stock-outs and aggressive discounting by licensees.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described FY27 as a “stabilization year,” flagged the Fall/Holiday order book as a signal for the stabilization thesis, and said the “+/- 1–2%” wholesale stabilization target was a key watchpoint.

surprises.description: The regional picture outside North America was uneven: APAC fell 7% (10% in constant currency), while EMEA and Latin America grew 12% and 8%, respectively. The preview emphasized North America but did not anticipate this split across the other regions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APAC down 7% (10% constant currency), while EMEA rose 12% and Latin America rose 8%.”

surprises.description: Under Armour disclosed plans for another 25% SKU reduction over the next 18 months, on top of a prior 25% cut, implying roughly 40% cumulative reduction by fiscal 2028—an additional portfolio action not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is targeting an additional 25% SKU reduction over the next 18 months, building on a prior 25% cut, for a cumulative reduction of roughly 40% by the end of fiscal 2028.”

in_line: Q1 revenue of about $1.1 billion was within the company’s $1.100–$1.111 billion guidance range and the preview’s $1.10–$1.12 billion consensus range, though it was at the low end.
FY2027 adjusted operating income guidance remained at $140 million to $160 million, as the preview expected the company to reiterate that range.
Wholesale revenue declined 2%, broadly in line with the preview’s cited target of roughly +/-1–2% wholesale stabilization.

surprises.description: The preview expected PREPA gross par to remain at $425 million and about $35 million of PREPA-related debt service to be payable during the rest of 2026. National instead reported that gross par had fallen by $35 million to $390 million after claims on bonds maturing July 1, with only $20 million payments due in each of 2027 and 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “National's PREPA exposure fell by $35 million to $390 million of gross par value following insurance claims paid on bonds that matured July 1, 2026, with only $20 million payments due in each of 2027 and 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross par is $425M, unchanged in Q1”; “About $35M of PREPA-related debt service is still payable across the rest of 2026.”

surprises.description: The preview expected National statutory capital of $940–960 million; it ended the quarter at $968 million, above that range. The $31 million increase since year-end also exceeded the preview’s reference point of a $13 million increase in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “National's statutory capital rose $31 million to $968 million versus year-end 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “stat cap $940–960M”; prior-quarter capital was “$950M (+$13M q/q).”

surprises.description: The preview identified leverage below 22:1 as a positive surprise. National reported 21:1, alongside a roughly $1.5 billion decline in insured gross par to about $20.8 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “National's leverage ratio (gross par to statutory capital) improved to 21-to-1 from 24-to-1 at year-end 2025, with insured gross par declining ~$1.5 billion to about $20.8 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sub-22:1 leverage would be a positive surprise.”

surprises.description: MBIA Insurance Corp. reported $27 million of statutory net income, versus $4 million a year earlier, driven by a large loss-reserve benefit tied to reassessments of Zohar CDO recoveries. The preview flagged legacy exposure as a key issue but did not anticipate this reserve-benefit-driven profit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “MBIA Insurance Corp. posted statutory net income of $27 million in Q2 2026 (up from $4 million a year earlier), driven by a large loss reserve benefit tied to Zohar CDO recovery reassessments.”

surprises.description: Adjusted loss per share was a little worse than the preview’s consensus estimate: a loss of $0.14 versus an expected loss of $0.13.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net loss (non-GAAP) was $7 million (negative $0.14 per share) in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | –$0.13”

surprises.description: Management added that the rejected PREPA settlement offer valued bonds at roughly $0.30–$0.40 on the dollar, compared with recent market indications of about $0.75. The preview discussed the offer’s roughly 35% recovery value and its rejection, but did not provide this comparison with market indications.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management estimated the rejected settlement offer valued bonds at roughly $0.30 to $0.40 on the dollar, versus recent market indications of about $0.75.”

in_line: Book value per share was negative $45.58, within the preview’s expected range of negative $45.00 to negative $45.75.
Holdco cash and liquid assets were $337 million, within the preview’s expected range of $335–350 million and above its flagged $330 million threshold.
The Oversight Board’s approximately $3 billion PREPA offer and bondholders’ rejection were already described in the preview.

surprises.description: Wendy’s withdrew its full-year 2026 outlook rather than reaffirming or narrowing it, and said continued traffic headwinds mean it does not expect year-over-year system-wide sales growth in Q3 or Q4. That is worse visibility and a weaker near-term sales outlook than the preview’s base case of narrowing guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management withdrew its full-year 2026 financial outlook, citing a comprehensive turnaround assessment, and expects continued traffic headwinds preventing year-over-year system-wide sales growth in Q3 or Q4.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the base case was that “FY guide [would be] narrowed to the low end,” while “a full cut is the main gap-risk event.” It also listed FY26 global system-wide sales guidance of “~flat.”

surprises.description: Wendy’s cut its quarterly dividend to $0.07 per share, a substantial reduction from the $0.56 annualized dividend discussed in the preview. The preview described that dividend as covered by the free-cash-flow guide, rather than anticipating a cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company cut its quarterly dividend to $0.07 per share, implying an annualized payout slightly above the traditional 50%-60% of adjusted net income range, to create flexibility for turnaround investments.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The $0.56 annualized dividend costs ~$110–115M, which is covered by the FCF guide but roughly equal to guided EPS.”

surprises.description: The quarter’s adjusted EPS of $0.18 exceeded the preview’s $0.16 consensus estimate by $0.02. It was a modest beat, not the $0.13-or-less outcome in the preview’s bear scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EPS was $0.18 for the quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus EPS: “$0.16.”

surprises.description: U.S. restaurant traffic fell 12.5%, and management said the new chicken sandwich platform and movie promotion lifted average check but failed to generate the expected traffic. The preview identified promotions as a potential traffic driver, so their failure to do so was a negative operational surprise even though the U.S. sales decline was within the preview’s range.
surprises.fact_evidence: U.S. same-restaurant sales decline was driven by a 12.5% traffic decrease, partially offset by a 5.6% increase in average check, with negative double-digit traffic in each period of the quarter. New product launches, including a new chicken sandwich platform and a Minions/Monsters movie promotion, boosted average check but failed to drive expected traffic.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull scenario said, “Promotions drive traffic”; it also said the slope of the U.S. sales trend mattered to the turnaround narrative.

surprises.description: U.S. company-operated restaurant margin was 13.8%, above the upper end of the preview’s 13% ±50 basis-point full-year target band. The preview had highlighted the margin target as a key risk, so the reported quarterly level was favorable against that benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: U.S. company-operated restaurant margin was 13.8%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY26 U.S. company-operated margin guidance was “13% ±50bp,” and the preview flagged it as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: Net leverage reached 5.0x, slightly above the 4.9x level cited in the preview and at the threshold of its bear-case warning that leverage could drift above 5x. The difference was small, but it was an unfavorable movement on a preview-highlighted balance-sheet concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended the quarter with roughly $380 million in cash and an elevated net leverage ratio of 5.0x.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “4.9x net leverage” and described its bear scenario as “leverage drifts above 5x.”

in_line: U.S. same-restaurant sales declined 7%, within the preview’s expected range of approximately −6% to −7%.
Global system-wide sales declined 6.5% on a constant-currency basis, in line with the preview’s prior company indication of a mid-single-digit decline.
Adjusted EBITDA of $124.1 million was within the preview’s implied $120–125 million range.
The 289 U.S. restaurant closures in the first half were within the preview’s 200–350 closure target for 2026.

surprises.description: Kingstone reported diluted EPS of $1.05, above the preview’s $0.95 consensus estimate by $0.10, or about 11%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS of $1.05.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | $0.95”

surprises.description: The quarter’s catastrophe loss ratio was negative 0.8%, better than the preview’s threshold for a clean quarter of under 3 points. The preview noted a June storm outbreak as the main risk, but the reported cat result was even cleaner than that threshold implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The quarter benefited from a negative 0.8% catastrophe loss ratio.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Under about 3 points is a clean quarter”; “Q2 2025 cat load was 0.6 points.”

surprises.description: Management reported a softening, increasingly competitive market, particularly in Dwelling Fire, and expects New York growth to moderate in the second half. The preview focused on continued growth and mid-to-high-teens organic DPW growth, without flagging this competitive-market headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management flagged a softening, increasingly competitive market—most visible in Dwelling Fire—and expects New York growth to moderate in the second half.”

surprises.description: Kingstone’s July 1 reinsurance placement added wildfire coverage, increased total catastrophe protection by 14% to $500 million, and reduced the risk-adjusted cost of core catastrophe excess-of-loss cover by over 15%. The preview did not identify these improved coverage and cost terms.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The July 1 reinsurance placement increased total catastrophe protection 14% to $500 million, added wildfire coverage, and cut core cat excess-of-loss risk-adjusted cost by over 15%.”

surprises.description: The quarter included $1.6 million of favorable prior-year reserve development, whereas the preview raised adverse development as a possible downside scenario. The reported development therefore went in the opposite direction from that risk case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$1.6 million (2.7 points) of favorable prior-year reserve development.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bear scenario cited “possible adverse development.”

in_line: DPW grew 19%, within the company’s 15%-20% full-year growth guidance and consistent with the preview’s expectation for mid-to-high-teens growth.
Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance, as the preview expected: DPW growth of 16%-20%, EPS of $2.20-$2.90, and ROE of 24%-30%.
The board’s 20% dividend increase to $0.06 per share had already been reported before the release and was noted in the preview.
The company repurchased about 19,500 shares at an average $14.98, consistent with the preview’s watch for buyback activity below its $20.80 reference price.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.91, well above the preview’s working consensus of $0.70 (and the cited $0.73 estimate).
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EPS more than doubled to $0.91.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Working consensus for this note: $0.70 EPS”; the preview also cites Zacks at “$0.73.”

surprises.description: Revenue reached $4.3 billion, materially above the preview’s working estimate of $3.90 billion and the cited consensus range of $3.80–3.94 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue up 9% to $4.3 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Working consensus for this note: $0.70 EPS / $3.90B revenue”; the preview lists consensus of “$3.92–3.94B” and “$3.80B.”

surprises.description: Fluor lowered its FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $500–525 million from the preview’s $525–560 million range, despite the strong quarter. The new range is below the prior range at both ends.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Set revised adjusted EBITDA guidance of $500 million to $525 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA: $525–560M, narrowed from $525–585M.”

surprises.description: New awards exceeded $6.1 billion, far above the preview’s $3 billion Q2 checkpoint, and management upgraded its full-year book-to-bill outlook to well above 1. Backlog rose to $26.9 billion, whereas the preview’s base scenario expected it to be flat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New awards for the quarter exceeded $6.1 billion, growing backlog to $26.9 billion and supporting management's upgraded guidance for a full-year book-to-bill ratio ‘well above 1.’”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New awards of $3.0B or more”; the preview’s base scenario was “backlog flat,” and it said management was committed to awards “above 2025's $12.0B.”

surprises.description: The adjusted EPS outlook’s low end rose to $2.70 from the previously maintained $2.60, while the high end stayed at $2.80. This is an improvement even as the EBITDA range was cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Implying adjusted EPS of $2.70 to $2.80 at current repurchase pace.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: $2.60–2.80, maintained.”

surprises.description: Urban Solutions still recorded $44 million of additional Gordie Howe losses, including issues from currency swings, a subcontractor bankruptcy, and client-driven changes. The preview highlighted another Urban charge as a key risk, and one materialized despite the segment reporting a profit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Urban Solutions profit of $38 million included $44 million in additional losses on the Gordie Howe bridge project” from “foreign currency swings, a subcontractor bankruptcy, and client-driven changes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Another lump-sum charge, especially in Urban Solutions, would be the most damaging outcome”; the base scenario assumed a “Clean-ish quarter.”

surprises.description: A $357 million NuScale-related tax payment pushed operating cash flow to negative $317 million, a sharp near-term cash-flow drag not anticipated in the preview. Management said normalized operating cash flow would have been positive $40 million and slightly raised the full-year range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow was negative $317 million due to a $357 million NuScale-related tax payment, but would have been positive $40 million normalized”; full-year adjusted OCF guidance was raised to “$300 million to $320 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said operating cash flow guidance was “$300M, maintained” and flagged watching “operating cash flow against the $300M guide”; it did not anticipate this tax payment.

surprises.description: The sale of Fluor’s Mexican joint-venture equity generated $175 million of proceeds and a $90 million pretax gain, but also removed more than $650 million from backlog. The preview did not flag this transaction or its mixed effect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fluor sold its equity in its 30-year Mexican joint venture for $175 million, triggering a $90 million pretax gain (excluded from guidance) and removing over $650 million from backlog.”

surprises.description: The remaining legacy problem-project backlog had fallen to $120 million, with only $94 million of loss-project funding left and potentially all of it concluding in Q3. This suggests the legacy burden may clear sooner than the preview’s risk-focused discussion implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Legacy problem-project backlog has fallen to $120 million, with only $94 million in remaining loss-project funding expected, potentially all concluded in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “any further LOGCAP accrual in Mission Solutions” and noted that “The LOGCAP appeal is pending”; it did not indicate that the remaining loss-project funding could conclude in Q3.

surprises.description: Energy Solutions profit jumped to $88 million, largely because of favorable mega-project closeouts, but management said that benefit would diminish in the second half. The preview’s EBITDA-ramp discussion did not anticipate that a large part of the segment strength was temporary.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Energy Solutions segment profit surged to $88 million from $15 million a year ago, driven largely by favorable closeout of completing mega projects, which management indicated will diminish in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview framed the key test as “Adjusted EBITDA vs. the back-half ramp” and calculated about “$155M per quarter” for Q2–Q4, without identifying a temporary closeout benefit.

surprises.description: Management described a substantial forward pipeline and expects meaningful backlog growth in the first half of 2027, including nearly $30 billion of in-house mining and metals opportunities. That is more constructive than the preview’s flat-backlog base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects meaningful backlog growth in first half of 2027 from front-end power and LNG work, an in-house mining and metals pipeline of nearly $30 billion, and rising as-sold margins on predominantly reimbursable new awards.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario listed “backlog flat”; its discussion of awards focused on 2026 and near-term announced projects.

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $149 million, above the preview’s roughly $135 million warning threshold for a result that would make the full-year guide hard to reach, though slightly below its arithmetic estimate of about $155 million per quarter.
The $1.4 billion FY2026 buyback model was maintained, consistent with the preview’s approximately $1.4 billion target.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was $53.1 million, below the $54.99 million consensus, and organic revenue declined 2% rather than remaining around flat. The shortfall included weaker professional-services revenue and slower transaction revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 FY2026 revenue rose only 2% to $53.1 million”; “organic revenue declined 2%”; management attributed the outlook reduction partly to “decelerating transaction revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $54.99M”; “Organic revenue was flat in Q2. If it stays at zero for a third straight quarter…”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $13.3 million, well below the preview’s modeled roughly $15.4 million, and the 25% margin missed the roughly 27–28% margin expected to support the full-year plan. This meant the anticipated margin step-up had not materialized in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 5% to $13.3 million with margin improving to 25% from 24.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Derived model ~$15.4M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin | ~28.0% (modeled)”; “Q3 is the first quarter where that has to show in reported results.”

surprises.description: Management cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $216–221 million and adjusted EPS guidance to $1.08–1.12, instead of reaffirming or narrowing the existing ranges. The revenue cut reflected about $4.5 million of professional-services pressure, including roughly $3 million of utilities push-outs, plus decelerating transaction revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $216-221 million and adjusted EPS to $1.08-1.12”; the “$6.5 million revenue reduction” was attributed to professional services and decelerating transaction revenue.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A reaffirmation at $221–229M / $61–65M / $1.09–1.15 is the base case”; “A second outright cut is the bear trigger.”

surprises.description: The company lowered its FY2027 revenue growth outlook to mid-single digits from previously guided high-single-digit growth. That was weaker forward growth commentary than the preview’s setup implied, even though formal FY2027 guidance was not expected until November.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY2027 revenue growth guidance was lowered to mid-single digits from previously guided high single-digit growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “This is the last print before FY27 guidance arrives in November”; the preview flagged “organic-growth commentary ahead of November guidance.”

surprises.description: ARR grew 8% to $174.1 million, below the preview’s modeled $179–182 million and its 11–13% expected growth. That fell below the preview’s roughly 10% threshold for sustaining the recurring-growth thesis, although SaaS growth itself remained strong.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Annualized recurring revenue grew 8% year-over-year to $174.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for ~$179–182M ARR (+11–13% y/y)”; “Y/Y growth below ~10% would break the recurring-growth thesis.”

surprises.description: Maintenance revenue fell 13%, with management attributing the decline to the timing of SaaS conversions. The preview highlighted professional-services and utilities weakness but did not flag a maintenance decline of this size; management said the decline should normalize to about 3.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Maintenance revenue dropped 13% due to timing of SaaS conversions, expected to normalize to about a 3.5% decline going forward.”

surprises.description: Elevated interchange rates associated with high commercial-card usage reduced the payments net take rate by more than $1 million, an unexpected current-quarter headwind. Management described it as a data issue it expects to resolve with its processor in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Elevated interchange rates from high commercial card usage cut over $1 million from the payments net take rate”; management “expects to fix” the data issue “in Q4.”

surprises.description: Results included a $9.9 million unrealized gain on a minority equity investment in other income, an unanticipated non-operating item that lifted reported income but was not a recurring operating gain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Results included a $9.9 million unrealized gain on a minority equity investment recorded in other income.”

surprises.description: Buybacks had reduced adjusted weighted-average shares from more than 34 million to fewer than 28 million. The preview mentioned a buyback disclosure as a possible bull-case catalyst, but it was not part of the base-case expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Buybacks reduced adjusted weighted average shares from over 34 million to under 28 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bull scenario listed “buyback disclosed”; the base case listed “In-line quarter; ARR ~$180M; guide reaffirmed.”

in_line: Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.25 was within the preview’s $0.24–0.26 base-case range and slightly above the $0.24 consensus.
SaaS revenue growth of 38% was close to the preview’s roughly 37% modeled growth and above its 30% watch threshold.
The $1.8 million professional-services decline was less than the preview’s expected $2–3 million year-over-year drag; the utilities weakness itself was anticipated.
Management’s expectation that margin improvement would be weighted toward Q4 was consistent with the preview’s stated timing expectation.

surprises.description: Calumet reported $175 million of adjusted EBITDA with tax attributes, well above the preview’s $115–125 million base build and even its $140 million bull-case threshold. The beat came despite three planned turnarounds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Calumet delivered $175 million of adjusted EBITDA with tax attributes in Q2 2026, despite absorbing three planned turnarounds at Princeton, Cotton Valley and Montana Renewables.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Author's base build: $115–125M”; the bull scenario was “$140M+.”

surprises.description: Specialty Products & Solutions generated $161.7 million of adjusted EBITDA, more than doubling year over year. The preview expected March price increases to show up, but did not anticipate this result or a record production quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Specialty Products & Solutions adjusted EBITDA more than doubled year-over-year to $161.7 million,” driven by “over 20 realized specialty price increases and a record specialty production quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Price increases implemented in March should show up in Q2”; Q1 SPS EBITDA was “$44.3M from $56.3M.”

surprises.description: Montana Renewables produced only $17 million of adjusted EBITDA with tax attributes after being offline all of April and half of May, foregoing roughly $40 million of margin. That was less operating time than the preview’s expectation of about two months of Q2 operation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Montana Renewables generated only $17 million of adjusted EBITDA with tax attributes due to being offline all of April and half of May, foregoing roughly $40 million of margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 includes only about two of three months of operation.”

surprises.description: Management said renewable index margins were rising and expected Montana Renewables earnings to be meaningfully higher in Q3 with a full quarter of production. The preview focused on Q2’s partial operating period and did not give this specific Q3 earnings outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Renewable index margins are approximately $2.60 per gallon and rising,” with “Q3 Montana Renewables earnings to be meaningfully higher from a full quarter of production.”

surprises.description: Calumet outlined a new, capital-efficient SAF expansion that could support up to 200 million gallons by 2028 using a repurposed reactor and a patent-pending polishing service. The preview watched for MaxSAF volume growth but did not anticipate this expansion or its stated low capital requirement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A novel, capital-efficient expansion repurposing a second reactor from the fossil refinery into a patent-pending SAF polishing service will enable up to 200 million gallons of SAF at 17,000 bpd throughput by 2028 for a fraction of the originally expected capital.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “SAF gallons, the claimed 4–5x SAF volume increase, and the $1–2/gal premium over RD.”

surprises.description: Management gave a specific ramp: a 60 million gallon SAF run rate now, 80–100 million gallons by year-end, and 120–150 million by spring 2027. It also disclosed a planned roughly two-week fossil-side downtime early this winter, neither of which was specified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SAF production is guided to ramp from a 60 million gallon run rate now to 80–100 million gallons by year-end and 120–150 million gallons by spring 2027, with a ~2-week fossil-side downtime planned early this winter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “the claimed 4–5x SAF volume increase,” but gave no comparable ramp schedule or planned downtime.

surprises.description: By delaying the reactor reconfiguration until winter, Calumet said it could capture more than $50 million of unexpected EBITDA during peak asphalt season before the tie-in. The preview did not flag this near-term earnings benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Delaying the reactor reconfiguration to winter allows CMR to capture over $50 million of unexpected EBITDA during peak asphalt season before the tie-in.”

surprises.description: Beyond the previously disclosed $100 million note redemption, Calumet reported a $115 million repurchase that terminates the CMR truck rack sale-leaseback, with restricted-group leverage already below 4x and expected to fall below 3x next quarter. That is additional debt-reduction progress not specified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restricted group leverage fell below 4x and management expects to surpass 3x next quarter, aided by calling $100 million of 2028 notes and a $115 million repurchase terminating the CMR truck rack sale leaseback.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “Calumet redeemed $100M of 9.75% 2028 notes on July 15, 2026,” but did not mention the $115 million repurchase or the leverage targets.

surprises.description: Management described a tight paraffinic base-oil market, with more than 10% of global capacity offline and tightness expected to persist through 2026. The preview discussed specialty pricing but did not flag this supply disruption or outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 10% of global paraffinic base oil capacity (roughly 700,000 bpd market) is offline due to the Iranian and Russia-Ukraine wars, creating a structurally imbalanced, tight market that management expects to persist through 2026.”

surprises.description: Performance Brands adjusted EBITDA was $6.3 million, with a $7 million LIFO headwind. The preview did not call out this segment or anticipate this headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[Taking] a $7 million LIFO headwind in Performance Brands, whose EBITDA fell to $6.3 million.”

in_line: Q2 cash flow was stronger, consistent with management’s prior guidance; Calumet reported over $90 million of cash flow from operations despite a $70 million working-capital build.
The $100 million redemption of 2028 notes was already disclosed in the preview.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.03, well above the preview’s $0.807 consensus estimate. Management attributed the increase primarily to the share-count reduction from buybacks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS grew 13.2% year-over-year to $1.03, driven primarily by the significant share count reduction from buyback activity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS … Consensus $0.807.”

surprises.description: Tech & Shopping’s decline narrowed to 5%, a much stronger result than the preview’s base expectation of roughly 9%–11% down and better than the preview’s -8% positive-surprise threshold. Adjusted EBITDA in the segment also rose more than 8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tech & Shopping revenue declined 5% year-over-year, a marked improvement from the 13% drop in Q1 and 18% drop in Q4, while its adjusted EBITDA rose more than 8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … T&S ~−9% to −11%”; “Better than −8% would be a genuine positive surprise.”

surprises.description: Ziff Davis reported more than $200 million of buybacks in the first seven months of 2026, including $121.5 million in Q2, and reduced shares outstanding by nearly 11%. The preview identified capital allocation as the main debate and described a dollar-denominated capital return as a bull tell, but its base case anticipated no new authorization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company deployed over $200 million to buy back 4.5 million shares in the first seven months of 2026, reducing shares outstanding by nearly 11%, and repurchased $121.5 million of stock during Q2 alone.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capital allocation of the $1.19B” was the main driver to watch; the base case said “no new authorization,” while a “dollar figure attached to capital return” was a bull tell.

surprises.description: Management described revenue declines continuing through Q3 and Q4, rather than reaffirming H2 growth: Q3 revenue is expected to fall at a low-to-mid-single-digit rate, with Q4 declining more slowly. The slower Q4 decline is an improvement in trajectory, but the outlook is weaker than the preview’s base-case expectation of a qualitative H2 growth reaffirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 2026 revenue to decline low-to-mid single digits year-over-year … and expects Q4 to show a lower rate of revenue decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “H2 revenue growth” as a key issue and said the base case included “H2 growth reaffirmed qualitatively.”

surprises.description: The sale generated an estimated tax obligation of approximately $200 million, a material cash cost that was not quantified in the preview. The preview specifically noted that cash taxes on the divestiture gain were not yet disclosed.
surprises.fact_evidence: The sale “generat[ed] approximately $200 million in estimated tax obligations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net cash, buyback progress, and cash taxes on the divestiture gain are not yet disclosed.”

surprises.description: Health and Wellness revenue fell nearly 5% and adjusted EBITDA fell nearly 10% as pharma clients cut HCP advertising and shifted to lower-cost AI platforms. The preview did not flag this segment pressure or the stated reason for it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Health and Wellness revenues fell nearly 5% and adjusted EBITDA dropped nearly 10% as large pharma clients reduced HCP advertising spend at MedPage and shifted to lower-cost AI-based platforms.”

surprises.description: Management said AI-authored code roughly doubled in one quarter and enabled 24% more code to ship in Q2 versus Q1 despite lower engineering headcount, with a target of nearly all code being AI-authored by year-end. The preview did not anticipate this productivity update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The share of code authored by AI roughly doubled in one quarter, enabling 24% more code shipped in Q2 versus Q1 on lower engineering headcount, with a target of nearly all code being AI-authored by end of 2026.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $286.7 million, close to the preview’s $286.1 million consensus and matching its implied year-over-year decline of about 2.7%.
Adjusted EBITDA was $76.8 million with a 26.8% margin, broadly in line with the preview’s estimate of about $77 million and roughly 27% margin.

surprises.description: ARKO reported Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $72 million, below the preview’s $80–85 million author-estimated bogey. The shortfall was about $8–13 million, despite first-half adjusted EBITDA being up year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA declined to $72 million from $76.9 million a year earlier”; “First-half 2026 adjusted EBITDA rose 14% to $123 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (Q2) … Author's guidance-implied bogey is ~$80–85M.”

surprises.description: Retail fuel margins came in stronger than the preview’s base-case range, and management raised the full-year retail fuel margin outlook. Same-store fuel margin was 48.7 cents per gallon versus the preview’s 45–47-cent base case, while the full-year range rose to 45.5–47.5 cents from 41.5–43.5 cents.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-store fuel cents-per-gallon margin rose 6.5% to $0.487”; “management raised its full-year retail fuel margin outlook to $0.455–$0.475 per gallon.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base” scenario: “Fuel 45–47¢”; the preview also lists the existing FY26 retail fuel margin guidance as “41.5–43.5¢ per gallon.”

surprises.description: Same-store merchandise sales ex-cigarettes turned negative instead of continuing the modest positive trend the preview considered plausible. The reported decline was 0.9%, with lower SNAP EBT sales contributing about 75 basis points of pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-store merchandise sales ex-cigarettes declining a modest 0.9%,” with “lower SNAP EBT sales pressuring comps by approximately 75 basis points across three states.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “comps 0 to +1%,” and it noted that “April continued year-to-date trends” after Q1 same-store sales ex-cigarettes of +0.4%.

surprises.description: The call indicated that the full-year guidance implies second-half EBITDA will be down year over year, citing consumer and fuel-price uncertainty. The preview discussed a possible full-year guide raise or reaffirmation but did not anticipate this implied second-half decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The second half implied guidance suggests down EBITDA year-over-year due to consumer and fuel-price uncertainty.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “A raise to the FY range is the clearest bull trigger” and described its base case as “FY guide reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: ARKO disclosed an unanticipated use of cash to repurchase $38 million of senior notes for $35 million, rather than reporting an equity buyback or APC-stake monetization. The below-face-value repurchase reduces debt, though it also uses cash.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $38 million of its 5.18% senior notes for $35 million cash”; long-term debt ended at “$675 million (down $29 million from Q1).”

surprises.description: Higher credit-card fees were an unexpected cost pressure behind the Q2 EBITDA decline: elevated fuel prices drove $3.3 million of additional same-store fees. The preview focused on fuel margins and merchandise trends but did not flag this expense headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Q2 decline was “largely driven by $3.3 million of higher same-store credit card fees tied to elevated fuel prices.”

in_line: ARKO reaffirmed full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance of $245–265 million, consistent with the preview’s base case of a reaffirmation.

The USPP acquisition’s expected annual adjusted EBITDA contribution of about $30 million and approximately 280 million gallons of added volume matched the preview’s description of the already-announced deal.

surprises.description: Century reported $31.7 million of adjusted EBITDA, below the preview’s roughly $32–33 million estimate, and year-over-year growth was 5% rather than the preview’s anticipated second consecutive double-digit gain. Revenue was also slightly below the $153.9 million consensus at $152 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net operating revenue reached a record $152 million (up 1% year-over-year) and adjusted EBITDA hit a record $31.7 million (up 5%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDAR vs. ~$32–33M”; the preview also said “A second straight double-digit gain supports the cost-program story.”

surprises.description: Poland contributed just $0.1 million of Q2 adjusted EBITDA, with the casino closure, startup losses in Warsaw, and low table hold weighing on results. Management also put normalized Polish EBITDA at about $8 million annually, below its prior $10 million peak; the preview discussed the sale process but gave no expectation for this level of operating performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Poland was a major drag, posting just $0.1 million adjusted EBITDA due to the Rosa Casino closure, startup losses at the new Warsaw casino, and abnormally low table hold that cut gaming revenue by roughly $1 million versus expectations.” Management said “Poland's normalized EBITDA is around $8 million annually (down from a prior peak of $10 million).”

surprises.description: The international sale process had advanced beyond the preview’s status of interested parties and no announced transaction: two groups were in due diligence for Poland and Canadian packages, with management saying a publicly disclosable transaction could come before year-end. No deal was announced, however.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is actively pursuing sales of international operations to become a fully U.S.-centric company, with two groups in due diligence for Poland and Canadian packages potentially yielding a publicly disclosable transaction before year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said there was “no transaction announced as of Aug 6, 2026” and described the base case as Poland “progressing.”

surprises.description: Leverage improved to 6.5x and management expected it to fall well below 6x by year-end, a better trajectory than the preview’s latest reference point of roughly 6.9x after Q1. The preview raised leverage and covenant questions but did not forecast this degree of improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt-to-EBITDA improved to 6.5x and management expects it to fall well below 6x by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 leverage of “roughly 6.9x” and asked to confirm covenant status; it gave no Q2 leverage forecast.

surprises.description: Missouri operations were much stronger than the preview’s modest statewide gaming growth figures suggested: Century’s Missouri casinos led all 13 state casinos in year-over-year gaming revenue growth and extended their EBITDA-growth streak to seven quarters.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Missouri properties posted their 7th consecutive quarter of EBITDA growth, and Century's Missouri operations led all 13 state casinos in year-over-year gaming revenue growth, aided by the Attorney General's enforcement against illegal skill games.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Missouri statewide AGR grew “only +1.1% in April and +1.8% in June.”

surprises.description: Canadian operations delivered a notable improvement, with EBITDA up 11%, margins rising from 28% to 30%, and expenses declining 1.3%; the preview mentioned Canadian asset sales as a possible catalyst but did not anticipate these operating results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Canadian operations grew revenue 2.2% to $20.4 million and EBITDA 11% to $6.2 million, with margins expanding from 28% to 30% and expenses declining 1.3% on lower payroll.”

in_line: 2026 capital expenditure guidance of about $15 million was consistent with the preview’s $14–15 million range.

surprises.description: The preview said second-half CapEx needed to fall toward about $5 million per quarter for the FCF outlook to hold. Management instead said ClearPath investment for Norway will prevent the usual second-half CapEx taper and likely leave full-year free cash flow toward the low end of guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Elevated CapEx tied to ClearPath stabilizer investment for the Norwegian market means the usual second-half CapEx taper won't occur, likely pushing full-year free cash flow toward the lower end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capex needs to fall toward about $5M a quarter for the $17–22M FCF guide to hold.”

surprises.description: The preview noted improving U.S. and Canadian rig counts, but the call reported a sharper near-term pickup: North American rigs in July were more than 10% above the Q2 average. That is a stronger activity signal heading into the second half than the preview’s stated expectation of a timing benefit and improving volumes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North American rig count rose to 777 rigs in July, more than 70 rigs (10%) above the Q2 average”; U.S. land added “over 20 rigs in June and nearly 19 more in July.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q2 may see a timing benefit” from Canadian spring breakup and noted U.S. rigs were “up 48 year over year” and Canada “up 42 year over year.”

surprises.description: The preview expected rental margin to hold above 70% but said pricing pressure persisted. Management reported that pricing compression had stabilized after several quarters of decline, suggesting the pressure may have stopped worsening.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tool rental gross margin remained above 70% even amid pricing compression, which management believes has now stabilized after several quarters of decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Tool rental gross margin held above 70% despite pricing pressure” and that “Pricing pressure on US land persists.”

surprises.description: Q2 CapEx came in below the preview’s approximate $5 million-per-quarter level needed to support the FCF guide, and the quarter generated positive adjusted FCF. This was better than the preview’s indicated CapEx hurdle for the quarter, even though management warned that later investment would limit full-year FCF.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 capital expenditures fell to approximately $4.2 million from $7.7 million in Q1”; adjusted free cash flow was “$4.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capex needs to fall toward about $5M a quarter for the $17–22M FCF guide to hold.”

surprises.description: The preview cited March net debt of $48.9 million and highlighted leverage as a watch item. Net debt rose to $51.7 million by June 30, with the increase attributed primarily to the Norway investment; cash was only $2.5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt rose modestly to $51.7 million as of June 30, 2026, primarily due to the Norway investment, with cash of only $2.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net debt was $48.9M at 3/31, with $32.5M drawn on the revolver”; the preview also noted a July sale-leaseback that “may come up as a liquidity lever.”

surprises.description: The preview’s EPS estimate was a loss of $0.04 per share. Reported GAAP loss was slightly larger at $0.05 per share, while the adjusted loss was smaller at $0.02 per share, making the comparison mixed and dependent on the EPS measure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported a Q2 net loss of approximately $1.8 million ($0.05 per share) and an adjusted net loss of $575,000 ($0.02 per share).”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag the completion of the former sponsor’s share distribution. Management said roughly 90% of shares are now in public float, improving the company’s independence and trading liquidity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Following the completion of former sponsor HHEP's share distribution, approximately 90% of outstanding shares are now in public float, improving DTI's independence and trading liquidity.”

in_line: Revenue of $38.1 million was essentially in line with the preview’s $38.16 million–$38.72 million consensus range.
Adjusted EBITDA of $8.4 million was within the preview’s $8.0 million–$8.8 million base scenario.
Management reaffirmed FY26 revenue guidance of $155–170 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $35–45 million, as the preview expected.
Tool rental gross margin remained above 70%, as the preview’s base case expected.

surprises.description: Q2 net sales were $595 million, about 5.5% above the $564 million consensus in the preview and above its $580 million bull-case threshold. The preview’s base case was $555–570 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose 10% year-over-year to $595 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q2'26 Consensus | $564.0M”; bull scenario: “Revenue | $580M+”; base scenario: “Revenue | $555–570M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA of $49 million substantially exceeded the preview’s estimated $30–33 million, while the reported margin topped 8%. This was a much stronger quarter than the preview’s base-case $29–33 million and bull-case estimate of about $38 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled to $49 million with margin expanding 330 basis points to over 8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$30–33M (est.)”; bull scenario: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$38M”; base scenario: “Adj. EBITDA | $29–33M.”

surprises.description: Instead of merely reaffirming or narrowing its FY26 outlook, Manitowoc raised its sales and adjusted EBITDA ranges; the adjusted EBITDA midpoint increased by $22.5 million. Its EPS guidance midpoint of $1.00 is also well above the preview’s $0.48 FY26 Street EPS consensus, and it provided a new $50–70 million free cash flow outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year guidance to net sales of $2.3-$2.4 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $150-$170 million, adjusted diluted EPS of $0.80-$1.20, and free cash flow of $50-$70 million.” The adjusted EBITDA midpoint “was raised $22.5 million (from $137.5 million to $160 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 company guidance (reaffirmed at Q1, May 5, 2026): Net sales $2.25–2.35B; adj. EBITDA $125–150M.” The preview said the key issue was whether to “reaffirm, narrow, or cut” guidance and listed “FY26 EPS consensus is $0.48.”

surprises.description: The preview warned that tariffs would weigh more heavily in H2 and noted a possible Customs charge, but the call reported tariff refunds as a net benefit: a $12 million Q2 operating income benefit and an estimated $16 million full-year net EBITDA benefit. That is a notably better tariff contribution than the preview’s expected pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tariff refunds contributed a $12 million operating income benefit in Q2 (from $26 million cash received), with the full-year net EBITDA benefit of tariff refunds estimated at $16 million and another ~$4 million benefit expected in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said tariffs would hit more in H2 than H1”; the preview also flagged that “the offsets (restructuring, volume, mix) must carry the load” and that a Customs disclosure “could surface as a charge.”

surprises.description: Aftermarket sales grew 6%, faster than the +3% growth the preview cited for Q1, and reached a record trailing-12-month level. That points to stronger aftermarket momentum than the preview’s reference point suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-new machine (aftermarket) sales grew 6% year-over-year to $172 million in the quarter and reached a record $706 million on a trailing 12-month basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The catalyst checklist identified “Non-new machine sales growth, which was +3% in Q1.”

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate a new competitive benefit from U.S. trade actions against Japanese crawler cranes. The reported 12%–20% import tariffs improve Manitowoc’s competitive positioning.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The U.S. Department of Commerce and ITC confirmed Japanese crawler crane dumping and imposed import tariffs ranging from 12% to 20%, improving Manitowoc's competitive positioning.”

surprises.description: July orders exceeded $200 million despite being a seasonally slow month, providing a positive post-quarter demand update that the preview did not flag. It supports the view that order momentum continued beyond the Q2 order surge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “July orders exceeded $200 million despite being a seasonally slow month.”

surprises.description: Net leverage was approximately 2.6 times, below the company’s three-times target and down from the 3.1 times reported for Q1 in the preview. The preview gave the prior-quarter figure but did not forecast this improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage fell to approximately 2.6 times, dropping below the company's three-times target on stronger first-half performance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported Q1 “net leverage 3.1x” and did not state an expected Q2 leverage level.

in_line: Q2 orders were $709 million, within the preview’s $675–750 million range for matching management’s April pace; the preview’s realistic hurdle was about $550–650 million.

surprises.description: CWST reported adjusted EPS of $0.40, well above the preview's $0.29 consensus estimate. That also reversed the preview's expected 19.4% year-over-year decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income was $25.3 million or $0.40 per diluted share.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $543.7 million exceeded the $526.2 million consensus estimate by $17.5 million. The preview expected 13.1% year-over-year growth; the reported increase was 16.9%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 16.9% year-over-year to $543.7 million.”

surprises.description: Landfill volumes rose sharply, including a 62,000-ton increase in third-party volume, supporting the disposal-capacity story more strongly than the preview could establish before the call. The preview framed Q2 volume as a test of the prior quarter's weather-related weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Landfill volumes surged 8.4% (86,000 tons) year-over-year, with third-party volume up 62,000 tons and internalized volume up 24,000 tons, reflecting tightening Northeast disposal capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Solid waste volume. Management tied the Q1 decline to weather and cited ‘positive trends through April.’ Q2 is the test.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin fell 80 basis points, a larger decline than the preview's estimate of roughly 30 basis points of fuel-related dilution. The call also attributed 70 basis points of pressure to Resource Solutions, a drag not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 12.5% year-over-year to $123.2 million, but adjusted EBITDA margin declined 80 basis points to 22.7%, hurt by 40 bps from fuel and 70 bps from Resource Solutions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Fuel recovery fees pass costs through in dollars but dilute margin percentage, by roughly 30bps by the full preview's estimate.”

surprises.description: CWST lowered its full-year GAAP net income guidance to $0–$6 million from the preview's stated $4–$10 million range, citing higher amortization and taxes. The preview had already noted an earlier reduction to that $4–$10 million range, but not this further cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income guidance lowered to $0-$6 million on higher amortization and taxes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net Income (GAAP) | $4–10M | $16–22M (lowered).”

surprises.description: The company had completed five acquisitions year to date, versus the preview's report of four deals closed. It also disclosed that the five represent about $165 million in annualized revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Five acquisitions completed year-to-date represent approximately $165 million of annualized revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Four deals closed year to date, and guidance excludes unclosed deals.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA of $123.2 million was at the high end of the preview's implied $120–$123 million range.
The company reaffirmed adjusted EBITDA guidance at $473–$483 million; the preview identified a hold as a possible outcome and explicitly flagged the guidance decision as the central question.
Solid waste pricing rose 5.5%, above the preview's 4.5% concern threshold and consistent with its expectation that pricing strength would continue.

The Mid-Atlantic integration remained on track for $5 million of 2026 operating-cost cuts, consistent with the preview's stated $5 million target and expectation that synergies would be back-end loaded.

surprises.description: Vistra kept its 2027 EBITDA opportunity range at $7.4B–$7.8B, but said it is trending toward the lower end because ERCOT forward curves are meaningfully lower. The preview expected the range to be raised or left unchanged, without flagging this deterioration in the outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management maintained the 2027 adjusted EBITDA midpoint opportunity range of $7.4B-$7.8B but acknowledged trending toward the lower end due to meaningfully lower ERCOT forward curves, only partly offset by higher PJM prices, hedging, and the nuclear PTC.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “2027 midpoint opportunity ($7.4–7.8B). Raised or left unchanged?”

surprises.description: Vistra disclosed a new commitment of up to $1B to the Helix Digital Infrastructure platform and a role as its preferred power partner. The preview did not anticipate this investment or partnership.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Vistra committed up to $1 billion to the new Helix Digital Infrastructure platform (with KKR, NVIDIA, and the Kuwait Investment Authority), with amounts above $500 million contingent on milestones, and will serve as preferred power partner.”

surprises.description: Management said the pending Cogentrix acquisition and Meta nuclear PPAs could add roughly $700M to the 2027 midpoint opportunity, providing a quantified combined upside not given in the preview. The preview identified a quantified Cogentrix contribution as a possible update, but did not give an amount or include Meta in that possibility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pending Cogentrix acquisition and Meta nuclear PPAs, both excluded from current guidance, could add roughly $700 million to the 2027 midpoint opportunity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A firm close date and a quantified 2027 EBITDA contribution would be the key updates.”

surprises.description: Vistra reaffirmed its 2026 guidance, as expected, but expressed confidence in delivering at or above the midpoint. That tone was more constructive than the preview's assessment that a midpoint reaffirmation after a record ERCOT summer would read as a soft negative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Vistra reaffirmed 2026 guidance of $6.8B-$7.6B adjusted EBITDA and $3.925B-$4.725B adjusted free cash flow, expressing confidence in delivering at or above the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Reaffirming the midpoint after a record ERCOT summer would read as a soft negative.”

surprises.description: Vistra laid out more than $10B of cash available across 2026–2027, with specific allocations to equity holders and growth investments and another $2B–$2.5B still unallocated through 2027. The preview focused on buyback pace but did not anticipate this broader cash-allocation outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Vistra expects more than $10 billion of available cash across 2026-2027, allocating ~$3B to equity holders, $4.5B-$5B to growth investments, and leaving $2B-$2.5B of additional cash still to be allocated through year-end 2027.”

surprises.description: Management paired news of record July summer peaks in PJM and ERCOT with an estimate that realistic ERCOT data-center load by 2030 is only 12–15 GW, versus more than 400 GW of queue requests. This demand-and-queue assessment was not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PJM and ERCOT hit new all-time summer peaks in July of over 168 GW and 91 GW respectively,” while management estimated “realistic ERCOT data center load of 12-15 GW by 2030 versus queue requests exceeding 400 GW,” supporting a queue cleanup.

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $1.767B, within the preview's $1.76B–$1.79B consensus range.
The 2027 adjusted EBITDA opportunity range remained $7.4B–$7.8B, as the preview identified leaving the range unchanged as a base-case outcome.
Vistra reaffirmed its 2026 guidance ranges, consistent with the preview's expectation of a reaffirmation.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue of $999.4 million was well above the preview’s $948.8–$955.5 million consensus range, a gap of about 5– 5.3%. It also meant year-over-year growth of 28.2%, above the preview’s implied 21.6–22.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 fiscal 2026 revenue reached $999.4 million, up 28.2% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $948.8M”; “Revenue | $955.5M”; “Consensus revenue implies +21.6–22.6% y/y.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 16.3%, below the preview’s 17.0% base case and even below the 16.5% downside case it discussed. Gross profit margin was roughly flat year over year, rather than providing margin expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $163 million (up 24%) with a 16.3% margin, while gross profit margin was roughly flat at 16.8% versus 16.9% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin, about 17.0%”; “a 16.5% print would push the required Q4 margin toward about 18%.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY26 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance, as the preview expected, but the new adjusted EBITDA midpoint is $564 million—just below the buy-side threshold of $565 million or more. The range does extend to $569 million, so the shortfall is limited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised fiscal 2026 guidance to revenue of $3.64–$3.68 billion… and adjusted EBITDA of $559–$569 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guide is: Revenue: $3.590–3.650B; Adj. EBITDA: $552–564M”; “The buy-side wants EBITDA raised to $565M or more.”

surprises.description: Organic growth was 8.9%, above the preview’s 7–8% target and its concern that growth might fall below about 6% as Q2 strength faded. This indicates stronger organic performance than the preview’s cautious scenario anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue… comprising 8.9% organic growth and 19.3% acquisitive growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Organic growth vs. the 7–8% target”; “Organic growth below about 6% would make the story look more like an acquisition roll-up.”

surprises.description: Backlog rose to a record $3.36 billion rather than showing the sequential slowdown the preview warned about. It was up from $3.14 billion at March 31, comfortably above the preview’s $3.10 billion concern level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record project backlog hit $3.36 billion at June 30, 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Backlog vs. $3.14B. A sequential decline below about $3.10B would support the deceleration narrative.”

surprises.description: Ellsworth and earlier acquisitions are expected to contribute about $140 million of carryover revenue into FY27, supporting strong organic growth. The preview noted Ellsworth was not in the current FY26 guide but did not flag this FY27 carryover outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The completed Ellsworth Construction acquisition and prior deals contribute approximately $140 million of carryover revenue into fiscal 2027, supporting expected strong organic growth.”

surprises.description: Management said it expects no disruption to federal funding in FY26 or FY27 and cited potential funding increases and substantial undeployed IIJA funds. The preview did not discuss this funding outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects no disruption to federal funding in fiscal 2026 or 2027,” citing a proposed act that “would raise IIJA-level highway funding by about 7.2%” and that “~45% of IIJA funding remains undeployed.”

surprises.description: Management highlighted substantial data-center-related opportunity in its footprint, including project pipelines above $100 million in Texas and $130 million in Oklahoma. The preview did not identify data centers as a demand driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An estimated 70–75% of new US data center construction is occurring in CPI's 8 states, with Texas and Oklahoma platforms alone showing project pipelines exceeding $100 million and $130 million respectively.”

surprises.description: The company expanded its revolving facility and added incremental Term Loan B borrowing while lowering interest-rate margins. The preview raised leverage as a concern but did not anticipate this refinancing and added borrowing package.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expanded its revolving credit facility from $500 million to $700 million and added $300 million in incremental Term Loan B while lowering interest rate margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Debt/TTM EBITDA was 3.23x at 3/31, against a stated target of about 2.5x. Ellsworth added debt.”

surprises.description: Liquid AC price inflation added $8–$10 million to Q3 revenue, a specific pricing contribution the preview did not anticipate. This was a modest lift to reported revenue, though it was not organic volume growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Liquid AC price inflation added $8–$10 million to Q3 revenue.”

in_line: Management said 80–85% of the next 12 months’ contract revenue was already covered, as the preview specifically asked investors to listen for that coverage statement.

surprises.description: Mercer reported Q2 operating EBITDA of -$21 million, versus the preview’s derived estimate of roughly $20–30 million and its expectation that a quarter with no planned maintenance would test underlying earnings power. Both pulp and solid wood were loss-making.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 operating EBITDA turned negative at -$21 million”; pulp was -$13 million and solid wood was -$8 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My derived estimate is ~$20–30M”; “Q2 has no planned maintenance… Without a repeat impairment, a clean quarter is the test of underlying earnings power.”

surprises.description: The reported net loss was $76 million, or $1.13 per share, far worse than the preview’s roughly $0.58-per-share loss consensus. The loss also widened from Q1’s $52 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss widened to $76 million ($1.13 per share) from a $52 million loss in Q1.”

surprises.description: Instead of expecting compliance with the German facility covenant by Q4, Mercer said it will likely breach the facility’s leverage ratio then and disclosed going-concern status. It also reclassified its Canadian and German revolving facilities as current liabilities.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company disclosed going-concern status, reclassifying its Canadian and German revolving credit facilities to current liabilities and warning it will likely breach its German facility's leverage ratio in Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management expects compliance by Q4 2026”; the base scenario anticipated “no covenant news.”

surprises.description: Mercer has begun negotiating with its 2028 and 2029 noteholders and other stakeholders to restructure its capital structure and improve liquidity, a more urgent step than the preview’s discussion of refinancing the Canadian revolver before its January 2027 maturity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management has engaged advisors and is negotiating with holders of its 2028 and 2029 senior notes and other stakeholders to restructure its capital structure and enhance liquidity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The 10-Q says refinancing talks are ‘expected to be completed before maturity.’ An announced refi would be the most bullish item.”

surprises.description: German fiber costs rose rather than stabilizing, while management expects German pulp fiber to remain elevated in Q3. Canadian fiber costs did decline, so the deterioration was concentrated in Germany.
surprises.fact_evidence: “German pulp and sawmill fiber costs rose roughly 7% quarter-over-quarter to historically high levels… management expects German pulp fiber to remain elevated in Q3.” Canadian fiber costs declined about 4%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided for fiber to stabilize in Q2 on better German availability and US chip supply to Celgar.”

surprises.description: The quarter included a $29 million non-cash inventory impairment, contrary to the preview’s clean-quarter assumption that there would be no repeat impairment. Mercer attributed it to high German fiber costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Including a $29 million non-cash inventory impairment ($0.43 per share) driven by high German fiber costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Without a repeat impairment, a clean quarter is the test of underlying earnings power.”

surprises.description: Aggregate liquidity was about $192 million, slightly below the preview’s $195–215 million base-case range and below its stated $210 million relief level. The preview’s more severe bear-case threshold was below $180 million, which Mercer did not cross.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aggregate liquidity fell $37 million to about $192 million ($79 million cash plus $113 million undrawn revolvers) due to weak operating results.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base scenario: “liquidity around $195–215M”; the preview also said “Above $210M would be a relief signal” and “Below $180M would point to the bear case.”

surprises.description: Management said the German mills are operating below cash break-even and estimated that they need $35–40 million of total improvement, including capital needs, to reach break-even. That is a worse operating position than the preview’s test of a clean, no-maintenance quarter suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The German mills are operating below cash break-even, requiring an estimated $35-40 million total improvement to reach break-even including capital needs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 has no planned maintenance… Without a repeat impairment, a clean quarter is the test of underlying earnings power.”

surprises.description: Mercer announced a substantial Torgau restructuring: reducing shifts, eliminating 100 positions immediately and 250 more by Q2 2027, with a turnaround target exceeding $20 million and severance costs in both 2026 and 2027. The preview did not flag this plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Torgau restructuring includes cutting from four shifts to three, eliminating 100 positions in July with 250 more by Q2 2027, targeting a turnaround exceeding $20 million with severance costs of about $3 million in each of 2026 and 2027.”

in_line: The One Goal 100 program remains on track for its $100 million profitability-improvement target by the end of 2026, consistent with the preview’s stated target and timing.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue of $15.8 million came in below even the preview’s $18–20 million bear case, and well below its $22–24 million base case. The $0.75 diluted loss per share, however, was at the upper-loss boundary of the preview’s bear-case EPS range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 FY2026 revenue fell to $15.8 million” and the company reported “a net loss of $9.7 million ($0.75 per diluted share).”

surprises.description: The PRM contract’s timing slipped by about one quarter because of customer-requested scope changes, whereas the preview’s base case assumed PRM was on schedule. The contract value is unchanged and management said there is no financial impact, so this is a timing setback rather than a reduction in the award.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customer-requested scope changes delayed the PRM contract,” with “no financial impact” and “the total contract value remains unchanged”; final revenue recognition is now expected “between fiscal Q3 and Q4 of FY2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario assumed “PRM on schedule”; the preview listed “PRM slips a quarter” as a bear-case driver.

surprises.description: Energy Solutions revenue fell 28% to $5.9 million, with weak ocean-bottom nodal product demand and the prior-year sale of the streamer recovery device product line contributing. The preview raised OBX rental conversion as a watch point but did not anticipate or quantify this segment decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Energy Solutions Q3 revenue declined 28% to $5.9 million,” hurt by “weak ocean bottom nodal product demand and the prior-year sale of the streamer recovery device product line.”

surprises.description: Intelligent Industrial revenue declined 14% to $5.2 million on lower sensor demand and reduced contract manufacturing services, a segment-specific weakness the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Intelligent Industrial revenue slipped 14% to $5.2 million in Q3 on lower industrial sensor demand and reduced contract manufacturing services.”

in_line: Smart Water revenue was $4.6 million, essentially matching the preview’s approximately $4.5 million watch-point, despite the 56% year-over-year decline.

The preview anticipated the post-quarter $10.84 million Navy award as a commentary item; the call described the $10.8 million contract, with delivery expected by December 2027 and revenue recognized over FY2027 and FY2028.

The preview expected cost savings to be visible in operating expenses. The call reported Q3 operating expenses fell $1.2 million on lower personnel costs, commissions, and legal fees, though it did not provide the total expense figure needed to test the preview’s roughly $11 million benchmark.

The preview highlighted liquidity and the $25 million revolver. The call reported $25 million of available borrowings and $41 million in working capital, while saying management is relying on these resources to bridge to the next Petrobras milestone payment; no cash balance was provided for comparison with the preview’s $9–11 million estimate.

surprises.description: RGA reported adjusted operating EPS of $8.89, far above the $6.51 consensus in the preview. Even excluding the $0.83-per-share benefit from one-time/other items, the reported figure was substantially above consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pretax adjusted operating income of $761 million, equating to $8.89 per share after tax.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted operating EPS” consensus was “$6.51.”
