surprises.description: The quarter included a material one-time/other-items benefit, which boosts the headline result but is not expected to recur. The preview emphasized assessing EPS composition but did not anticipate a $0.83-per-share contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Onetime/other items contributed a material $71 million ($0.83 per share) benefit this quarter,” which management characterized as “nonrecurring” and expected to “net closer to zero over time.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “judge the quarter on EPS composition and claims experience,” but gave no estimate for one-time items.

surprises.description: Trailing 12-month adjusted operating ROE rose to 18.4%, extending further above both the preview’s cited 16.2% level and RGA’s 13%–15% target range. The preview raised the possibility of a target reset, but the reported facts do not indicate one.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The trailing 12-month adjusted operating ROE was 18.4% … tracking above the 13%-15% intermediate-term target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited TTM ROE of “16.2%, against a 13–15% intermediate-term target” and flagged a potential “reset of the 13–15% ROE target.”

surprises.description: Variable investment income substantially exceeded the 7% planned return for 2026, with a 15% annualized return in Q2 and 11% year to date. Management said this increased confidence in meeting or exceeding the plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Variable investment income delivered a strong 15% annualized return in Q2 and 11% year-to-date, well above the 7% planned return for 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “7% planned return for 2026.”

surprises.description: The preview identified buyback acceleration as something investors wanted to see, but repurchases were still $50 million this quarter—the same amount reported for Q1. The announced dividend increase provides a separate positive capital-return development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RGA returned $111 million to shareholders this quarter ($50 million buybacks and $61 million dividends).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Buyback acceleration toward the 20–30% payout target” as a catalyst and said Q1 buybacks of “$50M a quarter look light” against that target.

surprises.description: RGA announced a 5.4% dividend increase for Q3, a specific capital-return step not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Announced a 5.4% dividend increase for Q3.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that cumulative favorable economic claims since 2023 total $375 million and have not yet been fully reflected in earnings. This longer-running favorable claims balance was not quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cumulative economic claims favorability since 2023 totals $375 million not yet fully reflected in earnings.”

in_line: Q2 economic claims were favorable by $31 million, including a $14 million current-period earnings benefit; this was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of claims that were neutral to slightly favorable.
The $400 million debt paydown planned for September matched the preview’s note that $400 million was earmarked for 2026 debt reduction.
In-force deployment remained below the roughly $1.5 billion annual pace, consistent with the preview’s base case that deployment would remain below pace.

surprises.description: Adjusted operating EPS was $0.03, below the preview’s base-case estimate of $0.15 and the cited positive estimates, although the preview showed a very wide range that included a loss estimate. This was a weaker result than the central positive expectations suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating earnings were only $0.03 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario showed “Adj. EPS +$0.15”; cited estimates included “+$0.20” and “+$0.07,” alongside a Zacks estimate of “–$0.14.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $60 million, $5 million below the preview’s roughly $65 million reference point. It was within the preview’s broad $50–82 million implied range, so the shortfall versus the midpoint was limited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled sequentially to $60 million in Q2 2026 with a 7% margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A midpoint near $65M is the reference point”; the preview also said consensus implied “roughly $50M to $82M.”

surprises.description: Management quantified stronger price-and-mix gains than the preview could confirm: they contributed $32 million in Q2, and management expects a further $75–85 million benefit in the second half versus the first half. The preview identified quantified price capture as a key unknown and said silence on it could be viewed negatively.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$32 million favorable price and mix from paper price increases across all regions”; management guides to a “$75-85 million second-half benefit from better price and mix versus the first half,” roughly 70% from price.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management declined to quantify price capture in May”; the preview said “Silence again would likely be read negatively” and described the base case as price offsetting outage and input headwinds.

surprises.description: North American second-half volumes are expected to decline because Riverdale supply is being lost and the Eastover outage will last longer than planned. The preview anticipated an outage headwind, but did not flag the Riverdale loss or an extended outage as causes of lower volume.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North American second-half volumes will decline due to the loss of ~90,000-100,000 tons of Riverdale supply and a longer-than-planned Eastover outage (originally 45 days).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said “price offsets the guided outage and input headwinds”; its Eastover section referred to the planned sheeter installation and ramp, without mentioning Riverdale supply or a longer outage.

surprises.description: New tariffs removed a previously expected $20 million benefit from importing Brazilian tons and pushed the footprint-alignment estimate back to $85 million. The preview did not flag this tariff-driven reversal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New tariffs eliminated the previously expected $20 million benefit from importing Brazilian tons, pushing the footprint alignment estimate back to the original $85 million figure from the February guidance.”

surprises.description: Europe remains under strategic review, with management setting a roughly $50 million improvement target and saying a decision on options such as closure or sale could come in 2027 if the outlook stays unsatisfactory. The preview raised the possibility of a restructuring announcement, so the lack of an immediate action and the potential wait until 2027 are less decisive than that possibility suggested, though the improvement target adds detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “European operations remain under strategic review,” with a target of “roughly $50 million in improvements”; management signaled a “potential decision in 2027” on options “including closure or sale” if the outlook remains unsatisfactory.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “stabilization or restructuring language” and called a “restructuring announcement” a possible positive surprise.

surprises.description: Eastover’s expected annual benefits rose to $55 million from the preview’s $50 million run-rate figure, but management expects only $30–40 million to be realized in 2027. That is a somewhat higher eventual benefit, but a more limited 2027 contribution than the preview’s description implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Eastover investments are “expected to generate $55 million of total annual benefits, with $30-40 million realized in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “The $50M run-rate benefit is a 2027 item.”

in_line: Management continued to describe 2026 as a transition year, consistent with the preview’s framing of a FY2026 transition headwind; the call facts provided do not quantify an updated headwind.

surprises.description: The preview implied a quarterly fiber-build pace of about 53,000 addresses; TDS delivered approximately 66,000 in Q2, and raised its full-year target by 50,000 to 250,000–300,000 addresses.
surprises.fact_evidence: TDS Telecom delivered approximately 66,000 marketable fiber service addresses in Q2 and raised its 2026 guidance by 50,000 to a range of 250,000–300,000.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY guide implied roughly 53–70k per quarter for the rest of the year and flagged Q2 below about 50k as putting the guide at risk.

surprises.description: Instead of holding the prior Telecom outlook, TDS cut 2026 revenue guidance to $1.0–$1.025 billion and narrowed adjusted EBITDA guidance to $310–$330 million, citing legacy copper and cable pressures reaching the bottom line.
surprises.fact_evidence: TDS lowered its 2026 total telecom revenue guidance to $1.0 billion–$1.025 billion and narrowed adjusted EBITDA to $310 million–$330 million, citing copper and cable legacy revenue pressures falling to the bottom line.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed guidance of $1,015–$1,055 million in Telecom revenue and $310–$350 million in adjusted EBITDA, and called a formal cut the clearest downside trigger.

surprises.description: TDS raised Telecom capital spending guidance more than the previewed range, reflecting the faster fiber build and increasing the expected cash investment in the program.
surprises.fact_evidence: TDS increased CapEx guidance to $625 million–$675 million to support the accelerated build.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed TDS Telecom capex guidance of $550–$600 million and flagged free cash flow and capex as a key issue.

surprises.description: Array raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook above the previewed range and lifted the revenue floor, rather than merely maintaining its prior guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Array increased adjusted EBITDA guidance to $220 million–$235 million and lifted the low end of revenue guidance to $205 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Array revenue guidance of $200–$215 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $50–$65 million.

surprises.description: Despite the preview's concern about T-Mobile decommissioning churn, Array reported sharply higher cash site rental revenue, although it said interim T-Mobile site revenue was now beginning to decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: Array's cash site rental revenue rose 65% year-over-year when normalized for DISH, with total year-over-year growth of 81% (92% normalized) driven by T-Mobile interim site revenue that is now beginning to decline.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged Array net site rental trends, including “colocation adds vs. T-Mobile decommissioning churn.”

surprises.description: Array improved its tower tenancy ratio sequentially even excluding DISH, which had stopped paying and filed for bankruptcy; the preview did not flag this operating improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: Array's tower tenancy ratio improved sequentially from 0.94 to 0.96 excluding DISH, which stopped payments in December and has filed for bankruptcy.

surprises.description: Array agreed to monetize roughly 70% of its spectrum holdings while retaining C-band spectrum with no near-term build-out requirement, a portfolio update not anticipated in the preview beyond the already-known Verizon sale.
surprises.fact_evidence: Array reached agreements to monetize roughly 70% of its spectrum holdings, closing a $168 million sale to T-Mobile and a $1 billion transaction with Verizon during Q2, while retaining its C-band with no near-term build-out requirements.

surprises.description: TDS made no Q2 share repurchases, with the pending offer for Array's minority interest restricting buybacks, despite the preview highlighting capital allocation and buyback commentary as important.
surprises.fact_evidence: TDS made no share repurchases in Q2 due to restrictions tied to its pending offer to acquire Array's minority interest, leaving $520 million remaining under its buyback authorization.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said buyback commentary would carry weight and listed buybacks among the capital-allocation issues to watch.

surprises.description: TDS announced an unpreviewed $25 million acquisition of Granite State Communications, adding 11,000 fully fiber service addresses.
surprises.fact_evidence: TDS agreed to acquire Granite State Communications, adding 11,000 fully fiber service addresses for $25 million with an expected Q3 close.

in_line: The $1 billion Verizon spectrum transaction closed during Q2, consistent with the preview's statement that it closed on June 1.
Array's $11-per-share special dividend was already reported in the preview as declared after the Verizon sale.
Interim T-Mobile site revenue beginning to decline is consistent with the preview's warning to watch T-Mobile decommissioning churn.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $839 million, above the preview’s roughly $793 million consensus and $800 million guidance ceiling. The call described revenue as about $9 million above adjusted guidance, while the preview’s stated range implies a larger gap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue reached $839 million, up 9% year-over-year and exceeding the high end of adjusted guidance by about $9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | ~$793M | $780–800M ($790M midpoint)”

surprises.description: Q2 political revenue reached $83 million, above the preview’s $60–70 million company-guidance range and roughly $18 million above its $65 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 political revenue of $83 million far surpassed the $60-70 million guidance range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Political advertising | ~$65M | $60–70M”

surprises.description: The Q3 political-revenue guide of $165–185 million was far above the preview’s stated buy-side desire for at least $70 million, indicating a much larger quarter than that threshold implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 2026 political revenue to a range of $165 million to $185 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buy-side wants a Q3 political figure of $70M or more”; the preview also said “Below $65M would suggest the cycle is more back-loaded.”

surprises.description: Q2 net retransmission revenue was $150 million, above the preview’s $141–143 million guidance range even with a distributor blackout during the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net retransmission revenue of $150 million topped guidance despite including a blackout with a major distributor that ended May 1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net retransmission | ~$142M | $141–143M”; the preview also flagged “Net retransmission and full-year reaffirmation.”

surprises.description: Acquisitions delivered only 0.18x of deleveraging, below the roughly 0.25x initially anticipated, although total net leverage declined to 5.73x from 5.94x.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated total net leverage stood at 5.73x as of June 30, 2026, down from 5.94x in Q1, with acquisitions delivering 0.18x of deleveraging versus the ~0.25x initially anticipated.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “0.18x of deleveraging versus the ~0.25x initially anticipated.”

surprises.description: Q3 core advertising is expected to be flat only on an as-reported basis; excluding acquisitions, management expects a mid-single-digit decline, citing political crowd-out and underlying softness. That points to continued organic weakness rather than a clear firming in the trajectory the preview said investors would watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 core advertising is guided to flat year-over-year on an as-reported basis, but would be down mid-single digits excluding acquisitions due to political crowd-out and underlying softness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Core advertising trajectory and July/August pacing. If the trough was April/May and pacing has firmed, the bear case weakens. Watch crowd-out as political inventory absorbs units.”

surprises.description: Management said refinancing activity could cut interest expense by more than $30 million from the current 2026 estimate, with the savings benefiting free cash flow dollar-for-dollar under the stated tax-deductibility limitation. The preview did not flag this potential reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Refinancing activity could reduce interest expense by over $30 million from the current full-year 2026 estimate of $440 million, benefiting free cash flow dollar-for-dollar due to a 163(j) deductibility limitation.”

surprises.description: Gray lowered full-year CapEx guidance to $120–130 million from $140 million, a reduction not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 CapEx guidance was lowered to $120-130 million from $140 million.”

surprises.description: The full-year tax estimate was reduced to $80–100 million, an additional favorable update not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The full-year tax estimate was reduced to $80-100 million.”

surprises.description: The company redeemed $50 million of Series A preferred equity, an additional capital-allocation action beyond the debt repurchases already noted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company redeemed $50 million of Series A preferred equity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted the July 21 repurchases of $100 million and $20 million of debt and said to expect “continued note repurchases”; it did not mention a preferred-equity redemption.

surprises.description: The Board authorized up to $250 million of additional open-market debt buybacks, adding a specific new authorization beyond the debt repurchases already reported before the release.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Received Board authorization to buy back up to $250 million of debt in the open market.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “continued note repurchases” would be a clear deleveraging signal, but gave no expectation of a new $250 million authorization.

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was $214 million, within the preview’s implied $205–215 million range and close to its roughly $210 million midpoint.

surprises.description: Total revenue was $218 million, below the preview’s $221.9–$224.5 million consensus range; reported year-over-year growth of 46% was also below the expected 48%–50%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total net product revenue reached $218 million in Q2 2026,” up 46% year over year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: $221.9M – $224.5M”; “YoY revenue growth: +48% to +50%.”

surprises.description: Auvelity sales came in slightly below the preview’s roughly $183 million base-case benchmark, although prescriptions and sequential sales growth were strong. The new-to-brand prescription increase also exceeded the more general expectation to watch for sequential acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Auvelity net product sales were $180.3 million,” up 18% sequentially; overall Auvelity new-to-brand prescriptions grew 26% sequentially, versus 12% TRx growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Auvelity revenue versus roughly $183M implied by the base case”; “Watch for sequential TRx acceleration from the Q1 baseline.”

surprises.description: SG&A rose to $208.1 million, above the preview’s roughly $190–$195 million base case and beyond the $205 million level flagged as challenging the operating-leverage story. Management expects SG&A to plateau at this elevated Q2 level for the rest of the year, rather than leveling out at a lower spend level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A surging to $208.1 million from $130.3 million a year earlier”; management guided that “SG&A should plateau at the Q2 level of ~$208 million for the rest of the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything at or below about $195M is consistent with the Pizzie guide. A figure of $205M or more would challenge the operating-leverage story”; the base case expected “SG&A roughly $190–195M.”

surprises.description: SYMBRAVO’s gross-to-net discounts were worse than expected: they reached the high 80% range versus the preview’s high-70% expectation. As a result, sales fell by $1.8 million sequentially even as prescription demand grew.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SYMBRAVO net sales fell to $2.3 million (down $1.8 million from Q1) as gross-to-net discounts deviated into the high 80% range,” while demand “grew 30% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Symbravo was elevated in the high-70% range while access is built.”

surprises.description: Axsome ended the quarter with about $320 million in cash, well above the preview’s roughly $250 million downside threshold for reopening dilution concerns. Management also said the balance should fund operations into cash-flow positivity without additional financing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Axsome ended the quarter with ~$320 million in cash,” which management expects is “sufficient to fund operations into cash flow positivity without additional financing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Q2 exit balance near or below about $250M would reopen dilution risk”; the preview also noted management’s prior “no capital raise contemplated” position.

surprises.description: The early Alzheimer’s agitation launch produced a quantified prescribing signal: new-to-brand prescriptions among patients 65 and older rose 126% versus the comparable period in the prior quarter. The preview expected launch commentary and said that having no quantified metric would be mildly negative, but it did not set an expectation for growth of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In the first 8 weeks of the Alzheimer's disease agitation launch, new-to-brand prescriptions among patients 65 and older rose 126% versus the same period in the prior quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Expect talk of new prescriber activations rather than clean ADA dollars”; “Absence of any number would be a mild negative.”

in_line: EPS of a $0.99 loss per share was within the preview’s –$0.85 to –$0.99 consensus range, at its most negative end.
The AXS-12 NDA acceptance and May 1, 2027 PDUFA date matched the preview’s stated regulatory timing.
ENGAGE Phase III top-line results expected in Q4 2026 were consistent with the preview’s expectation of data in the second half of 2026.

surprises.description: Atmus reported Q2 sales of $528 million, about 3.4% above the preview’s $510.5 million consensus estimate. The record sales figure exceeded the expected growth pace, with the call attributing growth to Koch Filter and Power Solutions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 sales hit a record $528 million,” up 16.4% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $510.5M” for Q2 FY2026 consensus.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.82 beat the preview’s $0.79 consensus estimate. The 3-cent difference was a modest upside surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose to $0.82 from $0.75.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $0.79” for Q2 FY2026 consensus.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $109 million versus the preview’s derived estimate of about $105 million. The EBITDA margin was 20.7%, close to the preview’s roughly 20.5–20.6% expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $109 million (20.7% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (derived) | ~$105M”; the preview also put the margin at “~20.6%.”

surprises.description: Atmus raised its full-year revenue guidance: the new $1.975–$2.03 billion range has a midpoint above the prior $1.945–$2.015 billion range. This was stronger than the preview’s expectation that guidance would be reaffirmed unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year revenue guidance is $1.975 billion to $2.03 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed May guidance of “Net sales $1,945–2,015M” and said, “A reaffirm of the same range would repeat the May setup.”

surprises.description: The company raised the low end of its full-year adjusted EPS guidance by $0.10, to $2.85–$3.00, while keeping the high end unchanged. The preview specifically identified narrowing to this range as a clear positive, rather than its base-case expectation of unchanged guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EPS is guided to $2.85 to $3.00.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “A narrowing to $2.85–$3.00 would be a clear positive,” while its base case was “FY guidance reaffirmed unchanged.”

surprises.description: Atmus narrowed full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 19.75%–20.25%, lowering the ceiling by 25 basis points from the previous 20.5% top end. This limits the prior upside range, with management citing moderating pricing and FX benefits and Middle East-related pressures that continue into the second half, including on India JV income and commodity costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Narrowed full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 19.75%-20.25%, lowering the top end by 25 basis points due to moderating pricing/FX benefits and Middle East-related cost pressures”; the conflict “continues to pressure Middle East, India JV income, and commodity costs into the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed May guidance of “Adj. EBITDA margin 19.5–20.5%” and said its base case was “FY guidance reaffirmed unchanged.”

surprises.description: Koch Filter was more than 95% integrated, but transition services are not due to conclude until Q3, and Industrial Solutions EBITDA margin fell sequentially to 18.9% because of one-time transition inefficiencies. That leaves some integration-related friction beyond the preview’s expectation of full integration in early Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Koch Filter integration is over 95% complete with remaining transition services to conclude in Q3, though Industrial Solutions EBITDA margin dipped sequentially to 18.9% on one-time transition inefficiencies.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full integration was guided for early Q3 2026”; the preview also flagged the integration and a $4M identified synergy target for monitoring.

surprises.description: Management said surplus cash will now be allocated toward paying down gross debt. The preview did not anticipate this capital-allocation direction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now intends to allocate surplus cash toward paying down gross debt.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin was close to the preview’s roughly 20.5–20.6% expectation at 20.7%.
Aftermarket remained flat year-over-year, as the preview said it was guided to be.

surprises.description: Veru reported a $7 million net loss and a $0.30 per-share loss, better than the preview’s roughly $7.4 million consensus net loss and $0.32 per-share consensus loss, and substantially better than its own $11–15 million net-loss estimate and $0.48–$0.65 per-share estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 fiscal 2026 net loss narrowed to $7 million ($0.30 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss (GAAP) ... Consensus Q3 ~$7.4M (implied) ... My estimate $11–15M”; “EPS ... Consensus Q3 $(0.32) ... My estimate $(0.48) – $(0.65).”

surprises.description: Cash at June 30 was $23.9 million, above the preview’s $20–22 million estimate and its $23 million bull-case threshold. The higher balance was supported by $23.3 million of public-offering proceeds, rather than being explained solely by lower operating burn.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash rose to $23.9 million as of June 30, 2026 ... bolstered by $23.3 million in net proceeds from a public offering.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash & restricted cash ... My estimate $20–22M”; the preview also said “above $23M is a genuine positive.”

surprises.description: Veru disclosed a supply agreement with Novo Nordisk that provides Wegovy at no charge and gives Novo a right of first negotiation on enobosarm combinations with any Novo GLP-1 product; the preview had not anticipated this arrangement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Veru signed a supply agreement with Novo Nordisk on June 2, 2026, under which Novo provides Wegovy free of charge and receives a right of first negotiation on enobosarm combined with any Novo GLP-1 product.”

surprises.description: Veru reported a USPTO notice of allowance for a method-of-use patent covering enobosarm with semaglutide, with stated expiry extending to at least October 3, 2044 before extensions—an intellectual-property development the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Veru received a USPTO notice of allowance for a key method-of-use patent covering enobosarm combined with semaglutide, with patent expiry extending to at least October 3, 2044, before any extensions.”

surprises.description: Management gave a more specific commercial rationale for enobosarm than the preview discussed: it cited weight-loss plateaus among GLP-1 users and framed older Medicare patients with sarcopenic obesity as a potential market of roughly 20 million as coverage expands.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management cited “88% of GLP-1 patients” hitting a weight-loss plateau after one year, with “62.6% still clinically obese,” and cited “roughly 20 million potential patients within Medicare Part D” as Medicare coverage of GLP-1 drugs expands starting July 1, 2026.

in_line: PLATEAU was fully enrolled and the interim analysis remained expected in Q1 calendar 2027, with final data in Q4 2027, consistent with the preview’s expectation of enrollment completion and those timing milestones.
Management’s expectation that cash would fund operations beyond the interim analysis matched the runway wording the preview expected; the preview also warned that this left little cushion.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $26.1 million, well above the preview's $17.5 million build and even the $21–23 million bull-case range. Adjusted EBITDA was $2.6 million versus the $1.0 million build, also above the base case, although within the preview's bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue was $26.1 million” and adjusted EBITDA was “$2.6 million (10% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My own build for Q2 revenue is $17.5M, with Adj. EBITDA of $1.0M”; the bull scenario was “$21–23M” revenue and “$3.0–4.0M” adjusted EBITDA.

surprises.description: Management raised FY26 revenue growth guidance to greater than 90%, from greater than 60%, and now expects adjusted EBITDA margins above 10%. The preview expected the prior revenue-growth target and full-year positive adjusted EBITDA to be reaffirmed, not a second increase or a margin target; the second-half outlook also excludes aviation asset sales, leaving those as upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised guidance “for a second time in five months,” now expecting “revenue growth greater than 90% (up from prior >60%)” and “adjusted EBITDA margins in excess of 10%.” “Second-half guidance is based entirely on recurring operating revenue and excludes aviation asset sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue growth: >60%”; the catalyst checklist said “FY26 >60% revenue growth and positive full-year Adj. EBITDA both reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Only 23 aviation assets were generating lease revenue, below the preview's target of about 25 or more on lease. The fleet grew to 38, but 11 recently acquired assets were still awaiting lease placement, leaving a larger deployment backlog than the preview's target implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “23 assets generating lease revenue (up from 21), leaving 11 recently acquired assets pending lease placement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Aviation assets on lease, target about 25 of 27 or more” and said management had guided four of six new engines leased in Q2.

surprises.description: Aviation capital deployment was much heavier than the preview's discussion of a recent engine purchase suggested: Q2 capex rose to $44 million, including about $41.2 million for aviation, and total aviation deployment exceeded $100 million. Liquidity ended at $77 million, while the preview had cited $88.6 million of cash and securities as of May 6.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Capital expenditures surged to $44 million in Q2 from $11.7 million in Q1, with ~$41.2 million going into aviation,” bringing aviation deployment “to over $100 million”; cash and marketable securities totaled “$77 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted liquidity of “$88.6M total” after an engine purchase and flagged “Cash and buybacks” as a key metric, but did not anticipate this level of quarterly aviation spending.

surprises.description: The drilling segment turned adjusted EBITDA positive, alongside a sharp sequential increase in revenue and more than doubled utilization. The preview did not identify drilling as a key watch item or anticipate this improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The drilling segment turned adjusted EBITDA positive ($0.6 million) with revenue up 171% sequentially and utilization more than doubling quarter over quarter.”

surprises.description: The company made its first operating-business acquisitions in eight years, buying two Midwestern fiber-optic services firms for $6.5 million in cash. The preview did not anticipate these acquisitions, and the firms contributed only about three weeks of results in Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed its first operating business acquisitions in eight years,” buying Mission Construction and V-Re Rentals “for $6.5 million in cash,” with “only ~three weeks of contribution in Q2.”

surprises.description: Share repurchases were much smaller than the prior-quarter pace the preview highlighted: about 43,000 shares versus 187,000 in Q1. Management said it prioritized aviation investment, so this reflects a shift away from buybacks toward deploying capital into the business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Share repurchases were minimal at ~43,000 shares averaging $2.99, as management prioritized aviation capital deployment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 buybacks of “$0.4M (187k shares at $2.14)” and listed whether buybacks continued at about 0.54x book as a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: Management described free cash flow positivity as near while citing more than $40 million in actionable aviation deals and about $15 million earmarked for other operating businesses. The preview did not flag this near-term cash-flow outlook or deal pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pipeline includes over $40 million in actionable aviation deals plus ~$15 million earmarked for other operating businesses, with free cash flow positivity described as near.”

in_line: Sand performance improved in the direction the preview expected: adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed by roughly 71% sequentially and gross margin turned positive, consistent with the preview's expectation that the loss would narrow toward breakeven.

surprises.description: Q2 production was 32,044 BOE/day, below the preview’s 34–36 MBoe/day guide and management’s stated expectation of midpoint-or-better production. The shortfall was substantial despite 7.2 net wells turning in line late in the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 production was 32,044 BOE/day (51% oil)” and there were “7.2 net wells turned in line late in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Production | Guide 34–36 MBoe/d”; “Management said it was tracking to the midpoint or better.”

surprises.description: LOE reached $10.27/BOE, above the preview’s $9.50 credibility threshold, and management raised full-year LOE guidance again to $8.25–$9.25/BOE. This was worse than the preview’s already-raised $7.75–$8.75 range and its base-case assumption of about $9.00/BOE.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year LOE guidance by roughly 20% ($1.50/BOE over the year) to $8.25-$9.25 per BOE, after Q2 LOE ran to $10.27/BOE,” citing “Permian water handling and higher early-life pad costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “LOE per Boe vs. $8.75 top of guide”; “A second quarter above $9.50 would undercut the capital-efficiency story”; prior guidance was “$7.75–$8.75”; the base scenario assumed “LOE ~$9.00.”

surprises.description: The company reported $79.6 million of Adjusted EBITDAX, below the preview’s roughly $85 million base-case implication. The gap was modest, though EBITDAX was above the prior-year quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 production was 32,044 BOE/day … generating $79.6 million of Adjusted EBITDAX.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDAX vs. the roughly $85M implied by the base case.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.09, above the preview’s $0.06 consensus estimate, even though it remained below the preview’s $0.11 base-case scenario. Relative to the cited consensus, this was a positive earnings surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income was only $11.1 million ($0.09 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $0.06”; the preview’s base scenario estimated “Adj. EPS … ~$0.11.”

surprises.description: GAAP EPS was $0.23, below the preview’s speculative $0.30–$0.50 range for a positive hedge-mark reversal. GAAP income was positive, but the reported amount did not reach that previewed range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income was $30 million ($0.23 per diluted share),” while adjusted net income was $11.1 million, “reflecting large hedge and one-time impacts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 could show a large positive GAAP EPS (plausibly $0.30–0.50) because WTI fell … reversing part of the Q1 mark.”

surprises.description: Q2 gas realizations and sales were exceptionally weak: Waha weakness drove realization to a company-record low and gas sales to just $9.6 million. The preview noted the lack of Q2 basis protection and weak gas pricing, but did not anticipate this reported severity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Waha basis weakness pushed Q2 gas realization to just $1.12/MCF, the weakest on record, with gas sales of only $9.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Waha basis swaps only start in Q4'26, so Q2 has no basis protection”; the preview also noted Henry Hub averaged $2.95 in Q2 and GRNT realized about 53% of Henry Hub last quarter.

surprises.description: Management forecast a sharp gas-sales rebound, with Q3 sales expected to exceed $30 million and Q4 higher still as takeaway improves and basis firms. The preview discussed Q2 gas-price exposure but did not flag this near-term recovery outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects Q3 gas sales north of $30 million (from $9.6M in Q2) and even higher in Q4 as takeaway improves and basis firms.”

surprises.description: Management laid out a specific 2027 free-cash-flow and growth target: a 10% FCF yield, 1.25x dividend coverage, about 1.25x leverage, and high-single-digit production growth at $65 oil. The preview expected a 2027 FCF bridge but did not provide these target levels.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2026 is guided as the final year of outspend, with a 2027 free cash flow inflection targeting a 10% free cash flow yield, 1.25x dividend coverage, ~1.25x leverage, and high-single-digit production growth at $65 oil.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “2027 free-cash-flow bridge, as promised by management.”

surprises.description: Management said it could cut the development budget by 40–50% if oil stays below about $65, while keeping spending below the $250 million maintenance-capital level. The preview identified capex as a key risk but did not anticipate this degree of downside flexibility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management can flex the development budget down 40-50% if oil holds below ~$65, staying below the $250M maintenance capital level.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capex vs. the $345–385M guide”; “A second capex raise would be the bear-case trigger.”

surprises.description: Management gave a production exit target approaching 40,000 BOE/day, with more than 75% of 2027 capital directed to operated partnerships. These specific forward operating and capital-allocation details were not in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expecting exit production approaching 40,000 BOE/day with over 75% of 2027 capital going into operated partnerships.”

surprises.description: The company said Grey Rock intends to distribute Granite Ridge shares to LPs over the next six to nine months, taking its ownership below 50% and ending controlled-company status. The preview did not anticipate this ownership and governance change; management said it would increase float and liquidity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Grey Rock intends to distribute Granite Ridge shares to LPs over the next six to nine months, pushing its ownership below 50% and ending Granite Ridge's controlled-company status, increasing float and liquidity.”

surprises.description: Management reported 27 Q2 transactions for about $28 million, adding 21.9 net undeveloped locations, and said inventory is being replaced at roughly a 2-to-1 rate, supporting five to six years of runway. The preview did not flag these transactions or the inventory-replacement outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “During Q2 the company closed 27 transactions for ~$28 million (including ~$11M future carry), adding 21.9 net undeveloped locations,” and is “replacing inventory at roughly a 2-to-1 rate versus development, giving five to six years of runway.”

in_line: Oil mix was 51%, within the preview’s 50–52% guide.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $42.9 million, below the preview’s $44.2 million consensus, and declined 2.5% year over year rather than delivering the roughly 0.4% growth implied by consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 fiscal 2026 revenue was $42.9 million, down 2.5% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 consensus” revenue was “$44.2M”; the preview said this implied “YoY about +0.4%.”

surprises.description: Same-center revenue declined about 1%, well short of the preview’s roughly 3% full-year assumption and below the level it said would support the turnaround. Case growth was positive, but a 2% decline in average selling price weighed on revenue per case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-center revenue (excluding London) declining approximately 1%”; average selling price “declined 2% to approximately $12,700.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Same-center sales: About 3% growth assumed in FY guide”; the preview said “Three percent or more would support the turnaround” and “One percent or less puts the guide at risk.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $4.9 million, below the preview’s derived estimate of about $5.5–6.0 million and below the roughly $5.5 million floor it identified as important.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell to $4.9 million (11.5% of revenue), down $900,000 year-over-year, reflecting intentional marketing investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Derived estimate of about $5.5–6.0M, not a published consensus”; the preview also flagged “Adjusted EBITDA of at least about $5.5M.”

surprises.description: The company cut FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $12–14 million from $15–17 million, a bigger reduction than the preview’s identified risk of narrowing the range toward its low end. Management cited an additional $5 million of planned marketing spend.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered its adjusted EBITDA guidance to $12-14 million,” citing “an additional $5 million in planned marketing spend this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed company guidance of “$15M – $17M” and said “Reaffirmation is the base case. Narrowing the EBITDA range toward the low end would effectively be a cut.”

surprises.description: Revenue guidance was reaffirmed only at the low end, rather than as a neutral reaffirmation of the full range. This leaves the outlook weaker than the preview’s base case of reaffirmation might suggest, although the range was not formally cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “reaffirmed revenue guidance at the low end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “FY26 guidance action. Reaffirmation is the base case” and listed guidance of “$151M – $157M.”

surprises.description: Management said Q3 revenue would be down single digits on a comparable basis and reported that sales softened in June and continued into July. It nevertheless expects revenue and adjusted EBITDA to return to year-over-year growth in Q4, giving a weaker near-term outlook but a projected rebound later in the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 revenue to be down single digits on a comparable basis, but expects Q4 to return to year-over-year growth in both revenue and adjusted EBITDA”; “Sales trends softened in June and continued into July.”

surprises.description: Customer acquisition cost rose to about $3,500 per case from $2,900 a year earlier, contrary to the preview’s expectation that CAC would be flat to lower. Marketing also rose to roughly 20% of revenue year-to-date from 18%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customer acquisition cost rose to approximately $3,500 per case from $2,900 a year ago, with marketing spend increasing to roughly 20% of revenue year-to-date versus 18% last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Flat-to-lower CAC would suggest marketing efficiency is improving.”

surprises.description: The term-loan maturity was extended to November 2027, addressing the refinancing overhang the preview highlighted. The company also reported reducing gross debt by over $30 million since the start of 2025, with about $24 million of total liquidity at quarter-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced gross debt by over $30 million since the start of 2025, ending Q2 with approximately $44 million gross debt and $24 million total liquidity, and extended its term loan maturity to November 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A signed refinancing removes the largest overhang. Silence or punitive terms is the main downside risk”; the preview noted the facility “matures May 11, 2027.”

surprises.description: Management announced an Alloclay partnership with Tiger Aesthetics and estimated a long-term GLP-1 revenue opportunity of more than $100 million. These commercial developments were not described in the preview, and management said contributions from the early-stage offerings are excluded from guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AirSculpt announced a new Alloclay partnership with Tiger Aesthetics” and “estimates a $100 million-plus long-term GLP-1 revenue opportunity”; guidance “excludes contributions from these early-stage new offerings.”

in_line: The company provided a skin-excision volume disclosure, reporting over 200 procedures; the preview had specifically said hard numbers on skin-excision and tightening volumes would be new information to look for.

surprises.description: The preview expected FY2026 revenue growth guidance to remain at the top of the 8–12% range. CEVA instead raised its outlook to 13–15%, above the prior range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth outlook to 13-15%, up from the previous 12% guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management guided FY26 revenue to the top end of +8–12%.

surprises.description: The preview expected royalties of about $10 million and highlighted a possible sub-$9.5 million result as a risk. Royalties came in at $10.8 million, above the preview’s bull-case threshold of $10.5 million, although they were only marginally higher year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: Royalty revenue was $10.8 million, up 17% sequentially but only marginally above the prior-year's $10.7 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Royalty revenue versus about $10M. Below $9.5M would undercut the H2 bridge.

surprises.description: The preview expected full-year non-GAAP operating income growth of 40–50%. Management now expects approximately 70% growth, alongside operating margin expansion to 11% from 3% a year ago.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management now expects non-GAAP operating income to grow approximately 70% ... year-over-year for 2026. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 11% from 3% a year ago.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management guided ... non-GAAP operating income and net income up 40–50% YoY.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was modestly above the preview’s consensus estimates of $28.15–28.6 million, coming in at $29 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 revenue rose 13% year-over-year and 7% sequentially to $29 million, exceeding internal expectations.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus Q2'26: $28.15M (Investing.com) or $28.6M (ChartMill/aggregated sell-side).

surprises.description: The preview anticipated the platform-company AI silicon licensing deal, but did not flag the higher royalty economics now described for this customer category. CEVA said the new NPU IP is expected to generate meaningfully higher royalty per unit than typical NPU offerings.
surprises.fact_evidence: A leading global AI and computing platform company selected CEVA's new NPU IP for its next-generation custom AI silicon, a new category of customer expected to yield meaningfully higher royalty per unit than typical NPU offerings.

surprises.description: The preview pointed to a low-to-mid-teens licensing-agreement count, but CEVA signed 10. That was fewer than expected, although two agreements were with first-time customers and two were directly with OEMs.
surprises.fact_evidence: CEVA signed 10 licensing agreements in the quarter, including two with first-time customers and two directly with OEMs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Licensing agreement count (low-to-mid teens) and AI mix (above 20% in Q1).

in_line: Non-GAAP EPS was 8 cents, at the top of the preview’s $0.073–$0.08 consensus range.
Licensing revenue was $18.2 million, close to the preview’s base-case estimate of about $18.5 million.
The new AI-platform licensing deal itself was anticipated in the preview; the higher-than-typical royalty-per-unit potential was not.
Full-year non-GAAP net income growth guidance of approximately 50% was at the upper end of the preview’s expected 40–50% range.

surprises.description: Q2 RevPAR excluding Royal Palm was nearly 7%, far above the preview’s roughly 1.5% midpoint expectation and the +5.7% industry benchmark. Growth also accelerated through the quarter, and July RevPAR was up 8.5%, pointing to continued strength.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 RevPAR increased nearly 7% year-over-year excluding Royal Palm,” accelerating from “~4% in April” to “over 11% in June”; “July RevPAR up 8.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management was expected to guide Q2 to “roughly the midpoint of its full-year range (about +1.5%)”; the preview also identified “+5.7%” as the industry figure.

surprises.description: Park raised full-year RevPAR guidance by about 225 basis points at the midpoint, to 3%–4.5%, exceeding the preview’s expectation that a raise of at least 100 basis points would be a meaningful increase. Management also expects Q3 RevPAR toward the top of the new range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 RevPAR guidance by ~225 bps at the midpoint to a new range of 3% to 4.5%,” with “Q3 RevPAR toward the upper end of that range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise of less than about 100bps at the midpoint would read as weak”; the base scenario anticipated a move to “~1.5–3.0%.”

surprises.description: Group demand was stronger than the preview’s expectations: Q2 group rooms revenue grew 9.5%, reported as 700 basis points ahead of expectations, while forward group pace was also robust for Q3 and 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Group rooms revenue grew 9.5% in Q2 (700 bps ahead of expectations),” full-year group pace was “up nearly 6%,” Q3 pace “up over 15%,” and 2027 core group pace “up over 6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “June group delivers” appeared as a bull-scenario driver, but the preview gave no numerical group-revenue or group-pace expectation.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA and margins beat the preview’s estimate: adjusted EBITDA was $198 million versus an estimated $185 million, with hotel adjusted EBITDA reaching $204 million and margin expanding 80 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $198 million”; hotel adjusted EBITDA “rose nearly 9% to $204 million” with “margin of nearly 32% (up 80 bps).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA $185M (my estimate).”

surprises.description: Adjusted FFO per share came in well above the preview’s derived estimate of $0.60–$0.62, at $0.70.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted FFO was $0.70 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted FFO/share ~$0.60–0.62 (my derivation).”

surprises.description: Disposition progress was much greater than the preview’s reported year-to-date pace: Park has sold 10 of the 19 identified non-core hotels for nearly $200 million, leaving less than 5% of portfolio value in remaining non-core assets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Since its 2025 exit plan, Park has sold 10 of 19 identified non-core hotels for nearly $200 million at ~12.5x EBITDA,” with remaining non-core assets “less than 5% of portfolio value.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Only $31M of the planned program has closed year-to-date, with 12 non-core hotels remaining (<6% of EBITDA). Any signed sale or hard dollar figure would be a clear positive.”

surprises.description: The dispositions also carry a near-term earnings cost: the three sales completed since May are expected to reduce second-half EBITDA by about $3.5 million, a consequence the preview did not quantify.
surprises.fact_evidence: The three sales “reduc[e] second-half EBITDA by ~$3.5 million.”

surprises.description: The balance-sheet update was better than the preview’s leverage concern suggested: net leverage declined from 6.31x to 6.1x, and Park outlined a plan to repay the $1.27 billion Hilton Hawaiian Village mortgage in September.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net debt was “~$3.7 billion (6.1x net debt-to-EBITDA, down ~0.2x from prior quarter)” with “$2.6 billion liquidity”; Park plans to use the delayed draw term loan and Bonnet Creek proceeds to “fully repay the $1.27 billion Hilton Hawaiian Village mortgage in September.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described leverage of “6.31x at Q1 2026” and flagged the “leverage path” as a key issue.

surprises.description: Hawaii showed a stronger operating rebound than the preview’s concern about lagging visitor volumes implied: Hilton Hawaiian Village RevPAR rose nearly 12% and EBITDA more than 13%. The nearly $350 million capital program is nearing completion, though management still sees a $60–$70 million EBITDA gap to the 2023 peak to recover.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hilton Hawaiian Village RevPAR up nearly 12% and EBITDA up over 13%”; the “nearly $350 million Hawaii capital program” is near completion in early 2027, with a “~$60–70 million EBITDA gap to 2023 peak targeted for recovery.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Oahu visitor volumes have lagged” and called Hawaii “the largest single swing factor.”

surprises.description: Royal Palm’s balance-of-year pricing indicators were strong: group and transient ADRs were substantially above pre-renovation levels, adding evidence of a promising reopening ramp that the preview had not quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: For the balance of the year, Royal Palm group and transient ADRs were “up 21% and 53% versus pre-renovation.”

in_line: Royal Palm South Beach reopened on July 22, consistent with the preview’s stated reopening date; the preview had also already identified the approximately $28 million stabilized EBITDA target.

surprises.description: Q2 continuing-operations revenue was $531 million, far below the preview’s $702 million consensus, even allowing for the preview’s warning that deconsolidation could make the comparison optical. Adjusted EBITDA was also only $16 million versus the preview’s roughly $40 million implicit bar, with margin down 80 basis points to 3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue from continuing operations fell 11.9% year-over-year to $531 million”; “adjusted EBITDA declined to $16 million”; margins “compressing 80 basis points to 3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue… Consensus $702M”; “A Q2 print near $40M”; catalyst: “Adjusted EBITDA vs. about $40M, the implicit bar.”

surprises.description: Full-year guidance was reset substantially below the preview’s prior outlook: revenue is now $2.15–$2.25 billion versus $2.80–$2.90 billion, and adjusted EBITDA is $140–$170 million versus $160–$190 million. The revenue reduction reflects discontinued operations, so it is not wholly an operating deterioration; the EBITDA range is nevertheless lower at both ends.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revised its full-year 2026 guidance to reflect discontinued operations, targeting revenue of $2.15–$2.25 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $140–$170 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue… $2.80B – $2.90B (reaffirmed)”; “FY26 adj. EBITDA… $160M – $190M (reaffirmed).”

surprises.description: Commercial revenue fell 13%, worse than the preview’s −12% warning threshold, and the company disclosed that its largest commercial client will end its contract in Q3 2026. The preview highlighted commercial trajectory as a key risk but did not flag this client departure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company’s largest commercial client is ending its contract in Q3 2026, contributing to a 13% year-over-year commercial revenue decline to $316 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A decline past −12% would threaten the FY revenue guide”; preview also identified “Commercial segment trajectory” as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: The preview said allocation of the already-contracted $234 million divestiture proceeds was still under discussion with bondholders. The call now says proceeds are earmarked primarily for debt reduction, resolving that open question in favor of deleveraging.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately $234 million in gross proceeds” from the sales, with proceeds “earmarked primarily for debt reduction.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Use of the $234M in divestiture proceeds”; management said allocation was “under discussion with bondholders.”

surprises.description: The transportation businesses were sold at a mid-teens adjusted EBITDA multiple, which the call described as well above Conduent’s current trading multiple. The preview noted the expected $234 million proceeds but did not describe this valuation comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The transportation divestitures transacted at a mid-teens adjusted EBITDA multiple… well above Conduent’s current trading multiple.”

in_line: The expected gross proceeds from the transit and tolling divestitures were approximately $234 million, consistent with the preview’s report that the businesses had been contracted for $234 million.

surprises.description: The preview expected combined backlog of roughly $1.3–1.5 billion; CECO reported a record $1.82 billion, with record orders of $799 million and a 2.8x book-to-bill ratio. The backlog was therefore well above the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q2 2026 orders of $799 million” and “a quarter book-to-bill ratio of approximately 2.8x”; “Quarter-ending backlog reached a record $1.82 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The preview expects roughly $1.3–1.5B combined. Below $1.25B would be a concern.”

surprises.description: Instead of reaffirming the existing FY26 outlook, CECO raised the low ends of both its revenue and adjusted EBITDA ranges, while leaving the high ends unchanged. This was a positive shift against the preview’s main guidance question.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CECO raised its full-year 2026 outlook to revenue of $1.3-1.375 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $200-225 million, both with higher low ends.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Does management reaffirm $1.275–1.375B revenue and $195–225M EBITDA, or use language such as ‘low end’ or ‘second-half weighted’? A raise is possible.”

surprises.description: The preview’s base case anticipated free cash flow would remain negative but improve from Q1’s $15.7 million outflow. Instead, adjusted free cash flow rebounded to about $53 million in Q2, equal to 132% of adjusted EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted free cash flow rebounded to ~$53 million (132% of adjusted EBITDA).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base” scenario: “FCF negative but improving”; the preview also noted that Q1 FCF was “–$15.7M.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted concern about the margin step-up needed to meet the annual EBITDA midpoint and noted Q1 gross-margin pressure. CECO reported adjusted EBITDA margin expansion of about 150 basis points to 14.1%, its first quarter with mid-teens margins; SG&A also improved materially. The reported combined-company margin is stronger than that concern implied, though it does not by itself establish the legacy business’s margin trajectory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 73% to $40.2 million with margins expanding ~150 basis points to 14.1%, marking CECO’s first quarter with mid-teens EBITDA margins”; “SG&A improved ~400 basis points to 22.4% of revenue, with management not expecting the rate to drift back up.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Legacy margin trajectory” was described as “the thesis’s weakest point”; the preview said Q1 gross margin was “already down YoY” and listed “margin still compressing” in its bear scenario.

surprises.description: The preview cited a $40 million three-year synergy target and said synergies were on or ahead of schedule, but CECO quantified rapid early capture: about $13 million of annualized net adjusted EBITDA synergies in just 60 days, with $17–20 million expected by year one. This adds stronger-than-expected evidence of early execution, without raising the overall target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Captured ~$13 million of annualized net adjusted EBITDA synergies from Thermon in just 60 days (about one-third of the $40 million target), expecting $17-20 million captured by year one and ~$5 million realized in 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the “$40M synergy target (3 years)” as “on-or-ahead” and said “Any raise is a bull signal.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue came in above the preview’s soft estimate and its stated in-line range, but the gap was modest: $285 million versus roughly $279 million implied consensus and a $265–280 million in-line range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was $285 million (up 54% YoY), including one month of Thermon.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$279M (implied)”; the preview also said “$265–280M as in line.”

surprises.description: The acquisition-financed debt increase left leverage at 2.7x, above the stated 2.0–2.5x target range. The company had already paid down $39.5 million by July 31, tempering but not eliminating the leverage concern; the preview did not provide an expected debt or leverage level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross debt rose ~$523 million to finance the Thermon acquisition, pushing leverage to 2.7x, but the company paid down an additional $39.5 million by July 31 to reach $692 million gross debt, targeting 2.0-2.5x leverage.”

surprises.description: PowerFleet cut FY2027 revenue guidance to $468–473 million from $485–490 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $111–114 million from $122–125 million, rather than holding the prior outlook. Management attributed the cuts to forgoing about $17 million of nonstrategic South African revenue, with an estimated $11 million adjusted EBITDA impact, including about $5 million of one-time costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PowerFleet cut full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $468-473 million from $485-490 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $111-114 million from $122-125 million, driven by a deliberate South African revenue reprioritization”; it began “forgoing an estimated $17 million of nonstrategic full-year revenue, with an associated ~$11 million adjusted EBITDA impact including ~$5 million of one-time costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether FY2027 revenue guidance of “$485–490M” was “held, raised, or softened,” and highlighted “reaffirmation of the $122–125M FY27 guide.”

surprises.description: The South African National Treasury deployment is far further along than the preview’s timing suggested: more than 70,000 vehicles are installed and near-term ARR is over $27 million, versus contribution framed as late FY2027 and an expected roughly 10,000 assets at this stage. The reported deployment projection is now 80,000–90,000 vehicles.
surprises.fact_evidence: The contract “has accelerated to over $27 million in near-term ARR and 70,000+ vehicle installations, roughly 7-9x the ~10,000 assets originally expected at this stage, with deployment projected to reach 80,000-90,000 vehicles.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the contract’s contribution was framed as “late FY2027” and “wholeheartedly in FY2028,” with “60,000+ assets in deployment planning.”

surprises.description: Q1 adjusted EBITDA was $21.5 million, below the preview’s estimate of about $25–26 million. That is a material shortfall against the expected quarter, even though EBITDA was up from $20.1 million a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 total revenue was $110.8 million, up 6.4% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $21.5 million (19.4% margin) versus $20.1 million a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q1 adjusted EBITDA at “about $25–26M.”

surprises.description: Q1 revenue came in below the $115.5 million consensus estimate, though it remained within the preview’s roughly $110–115 million guidance-implied range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 total revenue was $110.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed consensus total revenue of “$115.5M” and an implied Q1 range of “about $110–115M.”

surprises.description: Product revenue and margin were pressured by a WiFi chip compatibility issue: about $3.2 million of high-margin product revenue was delayed, product revenue fell 6.7%, and product gross margin was 21.3%. Management expects the delayed revenue to be recaptured within the fiscal year and margin to recover in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: A WiFi chip compatibility issue “delayed approximately $3.2 million of high-margin product revenue in Q1”; product revenue “fell 6.7% year-over-year to $16.5 million” and product gross margin dropped to “21.3% (from ~29% prior quarter),” with recovery expected to “31-32% in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview included a “product air pocket” only in its bear scenario; its base case anticipated an in-line quarter.

surprises.description: The full-year free cash flow outlook was reduced substantially, from $30–35 million to $20–23 million, rather than tracking toward the prior target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow guidance was cut to $20-23 million from $30-35 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY2027 free cash flow was guided to “+$30–35M” and flagged the trajectory toward that target as a key issue.

surprises.description: The profitability outlook shifted from prior guidance for net income to a net loss, rather than maintaining the preview’s watched path toward positive GAAP net income in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss guidance moved to $6-8 million from prior net income of $4-8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist flagged the “Path to positive GAAP net income in H2 FY27” and whether management would reaffirm that milestone.

surprises.description: Despite cutting the FY2027 annual guidance, management gave a higher-looking exit-rate outlook: an approximately $495 million annualized Q4 revenue run rate and over $130 million of adjusted EBITDA at about a 27% margin. The preview did not identify this exit-rate commitment, so it is a positive counterpoint to the annual guide reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “reaffirmed an annualized Q4 fiscal 2027 exit revenue run rate of approximately $495 million (implying over $130 million adjusted EBITDA at ~27% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on whether FY2027 revenue guidance of “$485–490M” and adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$122–125M” would be reaffirmed; it did not state an exit-rate expectation.

surprises.description: PowerFleet reported additional AI-related commercial traction not anticipated in the preview: AI video bookings rose sequentially, Fortune 500 customers expanded on-site, and a European construction leader signed a multimillion-dollar ARR deal spanning 26 countries.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company reported “AI video bookings up 20% sequentially, 12 Fortune 500 on-site expansions, and a new multimillion-dollar ARR deal with a European construction leader across 26 countries.”

surprises.description: The company announced a leadership transition, appointing Paul Lalljie as President and CFO in place of David Wilson, and named Vishal Vallabha Chief AI Officer. The preview did not flag either appointment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PowerFleet appointed Paul Lalljie as President and CFO (replacing David Wilson) and Vishal Vallabha as Chief AI Officer.”

surprises.description: PPL reported Q2 ongoing EPS of $0.33, below the preview’s $0.35 consensus estimate by $0.02. The miss was modest, though it contrasts with the preview’s expectation of a $0.35–$0.37 in-line quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PPL reported Q2 2026 ongoing earnings of $0.33 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Ongoing EPS” estimate: “$0.35”; the base scenario called for an “in-line quarter” with ongoing EPS of “$0.35–$0.37.”

surprises.description: Pennsylvania’s data-center pipeline and conversion to more advanced stages exceeded the preview’s figures: signed agreements reached about 32 GW versus 28.3 GW previously, with over 11 GW under ESAs versus about 10 GW and over 6.5 GW under construction versus about 5 GW.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Signed data center agreements in Pennsylvania rose for the tenth consecutive quarter to about 32 gigawatts, with over 11 gigawatts now under ESAs carrying financial commitments and over 6.5 gigawatts under construction.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited an advanced-stage pipeline of “28.3 GW,” “about 10 GW” under signed ESAs, and “about 5 GW” under construction; its base scenario expected the pipeline at “28–30 GW.”

surprises.description: Kentucky’s large-load opportunity was substantially stronger than the preview indicated: the development pipeline reached 13.7 GW, probability-weighted expected new load rose to 3.7 GW by 2032, and PPL said a new $3.5–4 billion CPCN filing was likely by year-end. The preview discussed Kentucky rate recovery but did not flag this scale of load growth or a likely new filing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Kentucky's development pipeline expanded to 13.7 gigawatts with probability-weighted expected new load now at 3.7 gigawatts by 2032 (more than double the 2025 CPCN), likely triggering a new CPCN filing of $3.5-4 billion by year-end.”

surprises.description: PPL disclosed a sizeable potential investment opportunity beyond its planned $23 billion program: another $10–12 billion of potential capital from Kentucky generation and Invitium through 2032. The preview noted a possible incremental transmission addition of at least $500 million, but did not anticipate this larger, multi-year opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: PPL projected “$23 billion of capital investment through 2029” and “$10-12 billion of potential incremental capital from Kentucky generation and Invitium through 2032.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had flagged “at least another $500M of incremental transmission beyond the $23B plan.”

surprises.description: PPL disclosed strong contractual protections for future large-load customers that the preview did not discuss: 10- to 15-year contracts, minimum 80% capacity-payment guarantees, collateral, and termination fees. Pennsylvania customers will also contribute $11 million annually to low-income assistance starting in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Large-load tariffs require 10-year (PA) to 15-year (KY) contracts with minimum 80% capacity payment guarantees, upfront collateral, and termination fees, while PA large-load customers will contribute $11 million annually to low-income assistance starting 2027.”

surprises.description: The Pennsylvania rate increase was expected to take effect July 1, but the settlement also includes a two-year stay-out provision through July 1, 2028, a regulatory term the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PPL's Pennsylvania rate case settlement took effect July 1 with a $275 million increase (under 4% across rate classes), including a 2-year stay-out provision through July 1, 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “Pennsylvania distribution rate increase (+$275M annualized) took effect July 1, 2026.”

in_line: PPL reaffirmed FY2026 EPS guidance of $1.90–$1.98, midpoint $1.94, as the preview expected; the preview described reaffirmation as the base case.
The Pennsylvania rate increase took effect July 1 at $275 million, as the preview anticipated.
PPL’s $23 billion capital investment plan through 2029 was consistent with the preview’s stated plan.

Management expects one or more Invitium commercial agreements by year-end, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of a meaningful JV announcement during 2026; the call reported reservations and queue progress but no signed commercial agreement.

surprises.description: Revenue reached $14.5 million, above the preview’s higher consensus estimate of $13.26 million and even the bull-case range topping at $14.2 million. The reported 22.1% year-over-year growth was also stronger than the preview’s consensus growth estimate of 11.4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenues rose 22.1% year-over-year to $14.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q1 FY2027E | $13.26M”; the preview also gave a bull scenario of “$13.8-14.2M.”

surprises.description: GMV grew 18.1%, well above the preview’s base-case expectation of 9–12% and its 8% share-gain threshold. Average order value rose to $477 and conversion improved, accompanying growth that was substantially stronger than the preview’s practical bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GMV grew 18.1% to $223.7 million, with average order value up 7.5% to $477 and conversion improving 11 basis points to 1.76%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case assumed “GMV +9-12%”; it said “Growth of 8% or more would indicate share gain.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $7.9 million, above the preview’s $6.3–6.9 million base range and $6.5 million catalyst threshold. Its trailing-12-month total also put the company above the $25 million run-rate goal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA jumped 152% to $7.9 million” and reached “~$27 million on a trailing-12-month basis, above the $25 million run-rate goal.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario was “Adj. EBITDA $6.3-6.9M” and its catalyst was “Adj. EBITDA at or above $6.5M”; it described the annualized run-rate benchmark as “$25M.”

surprises.description: The company swung to positive net income and $0.02 diluted EPS, whereas the preview’s consensus expected a $0.01 per-share loss. That also exceeded the preview’s base-case EPS range of $0.00–$0.01.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income from continuing operations swung to $3.6 million from a $5.9 million loss a year ago” and diluted EPS was “$0.02” versus “a $0.06 loss.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) | $(0.01)”; the preview’s base scenario gave EPS of “$0.00-0.01.”

surprises.description: The 6.47% take rate exceeded the preview’s 6.0–6.1% base range and its threshold of holding at or above 6.06%. The new FFL transfer service also contributed revenue and 39 basis points of take rate in its first quarter, a concrete contribution beyond the preview’s general mention of possible FFL-transfer revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: The FFL transfer service “contributed $0.9 million in revenue and 39 basis points to the 6.47% take rate in its first quarter of operation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case assumed “take rate 6.0-6.1%” and its catalyst checklist called for “Take rate at or above 6.06%.”

surprises.description: Gross margin fell to 84.5%, below the roughly 87% margin framing in the preview and the prior quarter’s 87.6%. Management attributed the decline to non-recurring FFL start-up costs and expected margins to stabilize above 85%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined ~260 basis points to 84.5% due to non-recurring FFL start-up costs, with management expecting margins to stabilize above 85%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview framed the marketplace as having “~87% gross margins” and reported Q4 gross margin of “87.6%.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses fell about 45%, including a $3.7 million reduction in legal and professional fees as litigation, SEC, and audit matters concluded. The preview wanted a clean below-EBITDA P&L, but did not anticipate this scale of expense reduction or the stated resolution of those matters.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total operating expenses fell about 45% ($7.4 million) to $8.9 million,” including “$3.7 million lower legal/professional fees as Delaware litigation, SEC and audit matters concluded.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed a “Clean P&L below EBITDA” as a catalyst and described legal/settlement items as part of the prior-quarter gap between adjusted EBITDA and net income.

surprises.description: The GMV surge had a temporary component the preview did not flag: management said Virginia’s high-capacity firearm ban prompted a non-recurring buying surge, with demand pulled into Q1 not assumed to repeat in Q2. Excluding Virginia, GMV still increased about $23 million year over year, but management also noted slower June velocity and a continuing July seasonal slowdown.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management called the Virginia buying surge “temporary, non-recurring” and warned that “demand pulled into Q1 is not assumed to repeat in Q2”; excluding Virginia, GMV rose “approximately $23 million year-over-year,” while “June velocity slowed and July continued the seasonal summer slowdown.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview emphasized expected share gains, saying “Growth of 8% or more would indicate share gain,” and did not mention the Virginia pull-forward or a Q2 non-repeat warning.

surprises.description: Operating cash flow turned positive at $4.4 million, improving by $11.1 million from a deficit a year earlier, while cash increased to $68.8 million. The preview did not set an operating-cash-flow expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow improved by $11.1 million to positive $4.4 million from a $6.7 million deficit last year, while cash rose $0.7 million to $68.8 million.”

surprises.description: Buybacks were $2 million, versus about $1 million used in the prior quarter, indicating a faster pace than the preview’s most recent reference point. The release said $12 million remained under the $15 million authorization.
