surprises.fact_evidence: “$2 million of buybacks left $12 million remaining under the $15 million authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “about $1M [was] used in Q4” and listed buyback pace as a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: The preview warned that equity issuance below NAV could dilute ETH per share and framed further raises as a bearish risk. SharpLink instead reported a $75 million offering at a premium to NAV, with proceeds used to buy about 10,000 ETH, making this capital raise more favorable than that concern implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: SharpLink completed a $75 million registered direct offering on June 23, 2026 at $7.49 per share/warrant, “at a premium to NAV,” and used proceeds to buy roughly 10,000 ETH.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Below 1.0x, equity issuance is dilutive and buybacks are accretive to ETH per share”; the bear scenario included “hints at further raises.”

surprises.description: The preview left open whether the Galaxy fund would pursue incremental yield or shift toward fee-based asset management. SharpLink described it as targeting ETH returns above the native staking rate, favoring the incremental-yield framing, although no realized excess return was reported.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Galaxy SharpLink on-chain yield fund has $125 million in committed capital and is “targeting incremental ETH returns above the native staking rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The open question is whether it is incremental yield or a shift toward fee-based asset management.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $11.5 million was in line with the preview’s roughly $11–12 million per-quarter operating revenue reference; the $11.53 million figure was also already disclosed before the call.

The Q2 repurchase of about 2.1 million shares and roughly 4 million shares bought back since August 2025 were in line with the preview’s 2.13 million June-tranche and more-than-4-million cumulative figures.
The Galaxy fund’s $125 million commitment was already disclosed in the preview.
Russell 2000 and Russell 3000 inclusion was already identified in the preview as having taken effect June 29.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was approximately $86 million, about 8% above the $79.3 million consensus estimate. The preview expected roughly $78–82 million in its base case, so the reported quarter was stronger than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was approximately $86 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $79.3M”; base scenario: “Revenue | $78–82M”

surprises.description: Target raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $410–$420 million from the preview’s reported $370–$380 million guidance, and raised adjusted EBITDA guidance to $85–$95 million from $75–$85 million. This was a substantial upward revision rather than the reaffirmation the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its 2026 outlook to total revenue of $410-$420 million and adjusted EBITDA of $85-$95 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $370–380M; Adj. EBITDA $75–85M”; key metric: “FY26 guidance: reaffirm, raise, or trim.”

surprises.description: WHS revenue reached approximately $36 million, above the preview’s target of more than $30 million; management also expects WHS to become the largest segment in 2026 at more than half of consolidated revenue. The preview anticipated WHS growth but not this reported scale or projected share of the business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The WHS segment generated approximately $36 million in Q2 revenue, a 142% year-over-year increase, and is expected to become Target's largest segment in 2026 at more than 50% of consolidated revenues.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The target is above $30M in Q2 WHS revenue.”

surprises.description: WHS segment margins were around 53.5%, above the preview’s cited 40–50% margins on new contracts; overall adjusted EBITDA margin also expanded by more than 700 basis points versus Q1. The margin report was stronger than the preview’s reference range, though segment margins and margins on new contracts are not exactly the same measure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion of more than 700 basis points versus Q1, with WHS segment margins around 53.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management cites 40–50% margins on new contracts.”

surprises.description: Capital-spending guidance increased to $490–$510 million, above the preview’s $460–$480 million range. The higher spending accompanies the raised growth outlook, but it also means greater planned investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “capital spending of $490-$510 million excluding acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capex $460–480M, of which $330–340M is WHS growth capex.”

surprises.description: The 2027 exit-rate targets rose to more than $700 million in annualized revenue and more than $260 million in adjusted EBITDA, above the preview’s targets of more than $680 million and $240 million. Management said the projection relies only on the existing contract portfolio, without pipeline contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Target projects exiting 2027 with annualized revenue exceeding $700 million and adjusted EBITDA above $260 million, based solely on the existing contract portfolio without pipeline contribution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “2027 exit run-rate target: >$680M annualized revenue, >$240M annualized Adj. EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Since January, Target had secured more than 9,000 contracted beds representing over $1.4 billion of multiyear contracts. The preview anticipated a possible new award with the release, but did not suggest this cumulative scale of awards.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Since January 2026, Target secured over 9,000 contracted beds representing more than $1.4 billion of multiyear contracts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New contract award announced with the print. TH announced major awards alongside the last two releases.”

surprises.description: Year-to-date operating cash flow exceeded $110 million, including more than $100 million of customer advance payments tied to recent WHS awards. The preview did not flag this cash-flow contribution; the advance-payment component is a significant source of cash but is tied to contract timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date operating cash flow exceeded $110 million, including more than $100 million of customer advanced payments tied to recent WHS contract awards.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed an active pipeline exceeding 20,000 beds, heavily weighted toward AI data centers and power generation, and said multiple definitive agreements for projects of more than 1,000 beds were being finalized. The preview anticipated a possible award but did not flag this scale of near-term pipeline activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The active pipeline exceeds 20,000 beds heavily weighted toward AI data centers and power generation, with management finalizing multiple definitive agreements for projects of 1,000-plus beds each expected in coming quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New contract award announced with the print.”

surprises.description: Management expects net leverage to rise temporarily as capital is deployed, before declining to well below 3x by the end of 2027 as communities ramp. The preview noted the 0.6x current leverage and asked for commentary on ABL utilization, but did not provide this leverage trajectory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects net leverage to temporarily rise from capital deployment but decline to well below 3x by the end of 2027 as communities ramp.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $32.9 million, about 9% below the company’s May guidance and well below the $38.06 million consensus cited in the preview. The preview described consensus as at or just above the top of guidance, so the shortfall was materially worse than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 revenue was $32.9 million, roughly $3 million (9%) below the guidance provided in May, with the shortfall described as broad-based across the business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Company guidance (Q2) | $36.5M – $38.0M ... Consensus ... $38.06M”; “Consensus sits at or just above the top of guidance.”

surprises.description: Full-year revenue guidance fell to $142–148 million from $169–174 million, a midpoint reduction of about $26–27 million. This was a much deeper reset than the preview’s bear scenario, which had modeled a cut to about $158–166 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was slashed to $142-$148 million from the prior range of $169-$174 million, a cut of roughly $26-27 million at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue $169M – $174M (reaffirmed May 6)”; the bear scenario expected “FY guide cut to about $158–166M.”

surprises.description: On a pro forma basis, revenue declined 23% year over year, showing a much weaker underlying trajectory than the preview’s expectation of roughly flat pro forma revenue for FY26.
surprises.fact_evidence: “On a pro forma basis (including pre-acquisition Akoya revenue), total revenue declined 23% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue ... Roughly flat pro-forma.”

surprises.description: Management pushed cash-flow break-even from Q4 2026 to 2027 and lowered expected year-end cash from about $100 million to roughly $80 million. Both changes were worse than the preview’s stated cash and break-even outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company now expects cash flow break-even to slip to 2027 (versus year-end 2026 previously) and projects ending 2026 with roughly $80 million in cash, down from about $100 million guided earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “cash-flow breakeven by Q4 2026, year-end cash about $100M with no debt”; the preview also said a year-end figure “well below $100M” would reset the financing discussion.

surprises.description: The company recorded a $26.9 million non-cash goodwill impairment tied to Akoya. The preview flagged the possibility of further impairment, but did not anticipate a write-off of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management recorded a $26.9 million non-cash goodwill impairment write-off tied to the Akoya acquisition, driven by macro factors and company performance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “questions about the $19M intangible write-off taken in Q1” and listed “any further impairment” as a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue is expected to be only flat to slightly above Q2, with material improvement from the commercial changes deferred until 2027 and beyond. That is weaker near-term momentum than the preview’s expected back-half step-up needed to support the original full-year guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue is expected to be flat to slightly above Q2, with commercial changes expected to drive material revenue improvement only in 2027 and beyond.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY guide required “about $95–100M in 2H against roughly $74M in 1H, a step-up of about 29%,” and described the base case as “back-half-weighted.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was 47.9%, below the preview’s 49–53% full-year margin guidance range, and management lowered that full-year range to 48–50%. The year-over-year margin improvement did not prevent a weaker-than-expected margin outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin improved 600 basis points year-over-year to 47.9%, though full-year non-GAAP gross margin guidance was lowered to 48-50% from 49-53% previously.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin | 49–53% (FY guide)”; “Q1 adj. GM was 50.9%.”

surprises.description: Management announced a new Chief Commercial Officer and a shift from geographic sales territories to solution-based selling. The preview did not anticipate a commercial leadership change or this restructuring; it points to an effort to address execution problems, though the eventual impact is uncertain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company appointed Jim Guth (ex-Exact Sciences and GE Healthcare) as Chief Commercial Officer and is restructuring the sales force from a geographic model to a solution-based selling model to improve execution.”

surprises.description: Q2 cash usage was $5.7 million, or $4 million adjusted, and management characterized cash preservation as better than planned. That was a favorable near-term cash-use result relative to the preview’s concern that the burn path could leave year-end cash at $87–92 million, although the company still lowered its year-end cash outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 cash usage was $5.7 million (or $4 million adjusted), ending the quarter with $96.9 million in cash and no debt, reflecting better-than-planned cash preservation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “At the current burn path, year-end cash could land nearer $87–92M.”

surprises.description: The diagnostics business was tracking ahead of the prior $10 million revenue reference, a positive update not stated in the preview’s diagnostics expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diagnostics revenue tracking ahead of the prior $10 million reference.”

in_line: The preview identified Anthem coverage effective July 1, 2026 and CMS pricing of $897 for Lucent AD Complete; the call reported both as achieved.
The preview expected LucentAD Complete FDA clearance in 2H 2026; the call’s anticipation of clearance around year-end is consistent with that timing.

surprises.description: Q1 revenue reached $50.2 million, above the preview’s $47.5–48.3 million company-guidance range and $48.86 million consensus. That was a clear beat of both reference points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 Q1 revenue grew 26.7% year-over-year to a record $50.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $48.86M” consensus; company guidance was “$47.5–48.3M.”

surprises.description: The U.S.–Jordan duty-free agreement had already prompted new purchase orders and inquiries from new importers, an unexpected source of demand beyond the preview’s discussion of existing order visibility and trade-access risks.
surprises.fact_evidence: The agreement “enhances Jordan's competitiveness and has already generated new purchase orders and inquiries from new importers.”

surprises.description: The largest customer projected orders roughly 15% above last year’s season after the zero-duty tariff announcement. The preview highlighted order visibility as a key debate but did not anticipate this customer-specific increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's largest customer projected orders roughly 15% above last year's season following the zero-duty tariff announcement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “Order visibility beyond December 2026” and whether calendar 1H 2027 was booking.

surprises.description: Diluted EPS was $0.13, versus the preview’s $0.09 consensus estimate, though it landed at the top of the preview’s $0.11–0.13 base scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net income rose to $1.7 million, or “$0.13 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | $0.09”; the base scenario projected “$0.11–0.13.”

surprises.description: Management forecast Q2 gross margin of roughly 14%–15%, below Q1’s 16.4% and including a level below the preview’s 15% lower bound for Q1. The preview did not give a Q2 margin estimate, so this is a new forward-looking warning rather than a miss against a stated Q2 forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 guidance called for gross margin “declining to roughly 14%-15%, reflecting increased raw material transportation costs.”

surprises.description: Jerash onboarded Urban Outfitters with a forecast first-year order of $5 million, plus potential opportunities involving Lee, Wrangler, Reebok, and North Face—new customer and brand prospects not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New customer Urban Outfitters was onboarded with a forecasted first-year order of $5 million,” with the named brands representing “additional potential opportunities.”

surprises.description: The first capacity phase still targets about 15% added capacity by end-2026, but the call associated it with roughly 500 workers, below the preview’s estimate of about 700 workers for that phase.
surprises.fact_evidence: The first phase would add “~15%” capacity by end-2026 with “500 workers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Phase 1 targeted “+15% capacity (about 700 workers) by end of calendar 2026.”

in_line: Q1 gross margin was 16.4%, within the preview’s 15–17% guidance and close to its roughly 16% expectation.
The second capacity phase remained on the preview’s timetable and scale: adding 20–25% by mid-2027.
The Board approved a $0.05 quarterly dividend, consistent with the preview’s expectation to watch for continuation of the dividend.
No FY2027 revenue or EPS guidance was provided, consistent with the preview’s base case that full-year guidance could remain withheld.

surprises.description: Tonmaya sales were far above the preview’s roughly $4.0 million implied estimate: the company reported about $11 million, helping lift total net product revenue to $13.5 million versus consensus of $7.10–$7.65 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tonmaya generated approximately $11 million in net sales in Q2 2026”; “Total net product revenue reached $13.5 million in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “TONMYA net revenue vs. ~$4.0M implied consensus”; total net product revenue consensus was “$7.10M (alternate $7.65M).”

surprises.description: The reported Tonmaya prescription volume suggests the post-April surge continued rather than fading: Q2 prescriptions doubled from Q1, with refills rising especially sharply. The preview had identified whether volume held up after April as a key test.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tonmaya prescriptions totaled 12,592 in Q2, up 100% quarter-over-quarter, with new patient prescriptions up 36% and refills up 207%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Whether Q2 volume held up after the April surge is the key test” and “Check whether management gives specific numbers or only qualitative language.”

surprises.description: Tonmaya’s Q2 gross-to-net was helped by favorable channel mix and lower copay buy-downs, countering the preview’s concern that sales might depend on discounting or copay support. Management cautioned that these factors will continue to fluctuate through the rest of the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Q2 gross-to-net benefited from favorable channel mix and lower copay buy-downs”; management expects “continued fluctuations at similar Q1/Q2 levels through Q3 and Q4 before stabilizing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A drop toward the $400s would suggest volume is being bought with discounts, copay support, and free goods.”

surprises.description: The sales-force expansion is slated to be fully deployed by September, later than the preview’s target of about 150 reps by mid-third quarter. Management also said most of the added reps are expected to cover their costs over 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adding 50 reps (bringing the field force to roughly 150) fully deployed by September,” with “most reps” expected to cover their costs “over the course of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “About 90 reps today and a target of about 150 ‘by mid-third quarter 2026.’”

surprises.description: Management provided a substantial TNX-4800 Lyme-prevention study plan that the preview had not flagged: an FDA-aligned adaptive Phase 2 field study, with enrollment expected to begin in Q1 2027 and most enrollment in 2028. The study could be pivotal if positive, though the timeline is extended.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The TNX-4800 Lyme prevention Phase 2 adaptive field study (~3,300 participants) has FDA-aligned minutes, is expected to begin enrolling in Q1 2027 with the majority enrolled in 2028, and could serve as a pivotal registrational study if positive.”

in_line: The funding-runway statement remained consistent with the prior guidance: runway, including subsequent equity proceeds, is expected into early Q2 2027, matching the preview’s cited Q1 guidance.
The HORIZON Phase 2 MDD study began enrolling in June, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the study would start around mid-2026.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $47.7 million, above the $44–46 million guidance range and roughly $2.6 million above the preview’s $45.1 million consensus. The preview’s base scenario anticipated $46–47 million, so the result beat the stated guide and consensus but was not far beyond the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 33% year-over-year to $47.7 million,” exceeding guidance of “$44 million to $46 million,” driven by stronger-than-forecasted TELOS ID performance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue” consensus: “$45.07M” / “$45.24M”; base scenario: “$46–47M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $6.9 million, above the $5–6 million guidance range and the preview’s roughly $5.5 million consensus proxy. It was within the preview’s $6.5–7.5 million base scenario, making the beat positive but not a major upside surprise relative to the preview’s broader expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $6.9 million, beating the $5-6 million guidance range,” with adjusted EBITDA margin at 14.4%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA” consensus: “~$5.5M (guide midpoint)”; base scenario: “$6.5–7.5M.”

surprises.description: Management raised FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $23.6–28.6 million, including lifting the low end by $3 million. The preview highlighted the possibility of a raise but its base case expected a narrowing without a raise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $23.6-28.6 million (up from $20.6-28 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base scenario: “FY narrowed to upper half but not raised”; the preview also flagged whether the “$20.6M low end” would be removed.

surprises.description: The FY2026 revenue outlook was reduced by about $2.5 million, with the top of the range falling from $200 million to $195 million. The reduction reflects a planned Q4 phaseout of a roughly $33 million annual revenue resale stream that carries only single-digit gross margins, an unexpected trade-off between lower reported revenue and better mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: Starting in Q4, Telos will “phase out a low-margin third-party software resale stream (single-digit gross margin) worth roughly $33 million in annual revenue,” cutting the full-year revenue outlook “by about $2.5 million to a new range of $187-195 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 company revenue guidance as “$187–200M” and sell-side FY26 revenue of “$194.02M.”

surprises.description: Management quantified a substantial future cash gross-margin lift: about 10 percentage points in the second half of 2027 as the low-margin resale stream is eliminated and prior TSA PreCheck investment recognition is completed. The preview did not anticipate this specific margin bridge.
surprises.fact_evidence: Eliminating the low-margin software plus completion of prior TSA PreCheck investment recognition is expected to “boost cash gross margins by approximately 10 percentage points (600 bps + 400 bps) in the second half of 2027.”

surprises.description: Management said it would be open to a change-of-control transaction if one clearly offered a superior path to shareholder value, while also emphasizing continued organic value creation. The preview did not identify this as a possibility.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management indicated “openness to a change-of-control transaction if it clearly represented a superior path to shareholder value,” while emphasizing continued organic value creation.

in_line: The outstanding proposal pipeline was slightly over $500 million in total contract value, with decisions expected in the second half of 2026—close to the preview’s roughly $500 million pipeline and expected award window.

Q3 guidance reflected a slight year-over-year revenue decline due to prior-period non-recurring startup revenue, but 6% growth excluding that item; this was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of seasonally lower second-half growth.
The FY2026 cash gross margin outlook of 39–40% was broadly in line with the preview’s roughly 39% expectation.
The company repurchased more than 1 million shares for $4.7 million, consistent with the preview’s note that management had said the buyback pace would accelerate.

surprises.description: The preview highlighted a $26–31 million quarterly EBITDA run-rate implied by the full-year guide. Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $23.1 million, below that range, although it cleared the preview’s $23 million minimum catalyst threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA rose 40% year-over-year to $23.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA vs. the ~$26–31M quarterly run-rate implied by the FY guide”; “at least $23M, the minimum that keeps the $95M floor live.”

surprises.description: The preview expected Q2 production to accelerate and cited a 1.4–1.5 million MMBtu quarterly pace implied for the rest of the year. Production was 1.3 million MMBtu and management said it was below expectations, leaving utilization in the high-50% range of nameplate capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 RNG production was 1.3 million MMBtu, up approximately 8% year-over-year but below management's expectations, implying utilization only in the high-50% range of the 9 million MMBtu nameplate capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management promised accelerating growth from Q2”; “FY guide implies about 1.4–1.5M MMBtu per quarter for the rest of the year.”

surprises.description: The preview called out $233 million of Q1 liquidity; Q2 liquidity was $162.2 million, a substantial decline. Management said existing resources were nevertheless sufficient to fund projects currently in construction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $162.2 million of liquidity”; “existing resources are sufficient to fund all projects currently in construction.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance language and liquidity”; “the $233M Q1 liquidity against the $407M market cap.”

surprises.description: Renewable Power EBITDA fell to $0.3 million from $2.2 million, and OPAL recorded a non-cash impairment tied to decommissioning a renewable power project as part of the CMS RNG conversion—an adverse segment development the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Renewable Power segment adjusted EBITDA fell to $0.3 million from $2.2 million, and the company took a non-cash impairment from decommissioning a renewable power project tied to the CMS RNG conversion.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was just above the preview’s $23 million minimum catalyst threshold, despite being below the $26–31 million quarterly run-rate implied by the full-year guide.
RNG production reached the preview’s stated 1.3 million MMBtu minimum, even though it was below management’s expectations and the pace implied by the full-year guide.
Management maintained full-year 2026 guidance, as the preview’s base scenario anticipated.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $622.7 million, $12.7 million (about 2.1%) above the $610 million consensus estimate in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total company revenue rose 25% year-over-year to a record $622.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $610.0M (+22.4% Y/Y)”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $99.7 million, just above the preview’s derived $95–99 million range and its roughly $97 million central estimate. The beat was modest rather than the larger result implied by the preview’s bull scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 22.7% to a record $99.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | Not published; ~$95–99M (my derived estimate)” and “Adj. EBITDA vs. about $97M (derived bar).”

surprises.description: June digital-health ARR was $105.5 million, below the preview’s $110 million-or-more checkpoint, although management still said the business was on track to exceed $140 million by year-end. The checkpoint miss tempers, but does not overturn, the stated year-end trajectory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Digital health ARR reached $105.5 million, up 97% year-over-year, with the company on track to exceed $140 million by year-end 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 ended at $96.9M, so about $110M or more at June 30 would make the target look achievable.”

surprises.description: Management’s initial analysis found the proposed 2027 Medicare rates would have a nearly neutral effect on RadNet, with less than $1 million of impact on roughly $2.4 billion of revenue, as RVU increases offset the conversion-factor cut. The preview did not identify this rate analysis as an issue to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A net-neutral impact (less than $1 million negative) on roughly $2.4 billion in revenue, as RVU increases offset the 1.68% conversion factor cut.”

surprises.description: Management said a proposed site-neutrality rule could cut hospital reimbursement by 30%–50% for certain non-contrast studies, while also potentially accelerating health-system partnership discussions. This policy risk and possible partnership opportunity were not covered in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A proposed 2027 site-neutrality provision would cut hospital reimbursement 30%–50% on certain non-contrast studies, which management expects to accelerate health system partnership discussions.”

surprises.description: The call highlighted rapid digital-health AI growth and a broader external customer base: AI revenue rose 136% and non-RadNet customers made up 63% of ARR. The preview discussed total ARR but did not flag this revenue mix or customer-base detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Digital health AI revenue grew 136% year-over-year to $16.1 million” and “external (non-RadNet) ARR now 63% of the base.”

surprises.description: Management added a newly FDA-cleared breast-ultrasound AI product and quantified its potential scale, alongside a forecast for AI-powered draft reporting to cover about 15% of RadNet volumes by year-end 2026 and over 50% by mid-2027. The preview did not discuss this product or adoption outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FDA-cleared breast ultrasound AI targets nearly 1 million annual studies (4x thyroid volume)” and management expects “about 15% of RadNet volumes through AI-powered draft reporting by year-end 2026, rising to over 50% by mid-2027.”

in_line: Imaging-center guidance was raised, as the preview said a raise was expected: revenue to $2.370–$2.421 billion, adjusted EBITDA to $345–$358 million, and free cash flow to $115–$125 million.
Same-center advanced-imaging growth was 9.6%, above the preview’s watchpoint of sustaining about 8% or more.
Management reaffirmed digital-health guidance and said ARR remained on track to exceed $140 million by year-end, consistent with the preview’s stated exit-ARR target.

surprises.description: Revenue was expected to be about $44.64 million; Fluent reported $48.4 million, roughly 8% above consensus. The preview implied about 19% year-over-year growth on continuing operations, while the call reported 25% aggregate continuing-business growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $48.4 million,” up “25% year-over-year on an aggregate continuing business basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 Consensus” revenue of “$44.64M”; consensus “implies ~+19% YoY on continuing operations.”

surprises.description: Commerce Media Solutions revenue was modeled to grow about 75–85% from the prior-year quarter; it grew 90% to $30.5 million. It also exceeded the preview’s bull-case marker of CMS revenue above $30 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commerce Media Solutions revenue grew 90% year-over-year to $30.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Model ~+75–85%” for CMS revenue; the bull scenario cited “CMS above $30M.”

surprises.description: The preview said a CMS annual run rate above $120 million would support the thesis; Fluent exited Q2 above $125 million, more than that threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commerce Media Solutions exited Q2 with an annual revenue run rate of over $125 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Above $120M supports the thesis”; the catalyst checklist also focused on “CMS run rate versus about $120M.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for CMS gross margin of at least 22%, versus 19% in Q1; the call reported CMS media margin of 34%, well above that marker. Separately, consolidated gross margin reached 28.9%, up 650 basis points from Q1, reflecting stronger monetization with key non-rev-share partners.
surprises.fact_evidence: CMS “media margin expanded to 34% from 20% a year earlier”; gross profit was “28.9% of revenue,” a “650 basis point improvement from Q1 2026,” driven by improved monetization with key non-rev-share partners.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CMS gross margin. Q1 was 19%, versus a stated path to ‘mid-20s.’ A print of 22% or higher would be credible.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA loss was expected to be around $2.0 million, and a loss better than $2.5 million was the preview’s progress marker; the reported loss was $1.8 million. Management also said it was guiding to positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4, a more specific near-term profitability signal than the preview’s expectation of full-year improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $1.8 million”; management guided to “a positive Q4 driven by seasonality,” while declining to guide Q3.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “~-$2.0M”; the key-metrics section said “Better than -$2.5M would indicate progress.” The preview also cited prior guidance for 2026 adjusted EBITDA “improvement.”

surprises.description: The preview treated an owned-and-operated decline better than 40% as a sign of stabilization; the decline was 24%, substantially less severe than that threshold. Management nevertheless described the business as a testing tool rather than a growth driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Owned and operated revenue declined 24% year-over-year to $16.3 million” and is “positioned as a strategic testing tool rather than a growth driver.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “O&O decline rate. Better than -40% would signal stabilization.”

surprises.description: The preview identified a signed Fluent In-Store conversion as a potential upside catalyst; the call disclosed that CVS went live in Q3 as one of Fluent’s largest partner wins, opening a pharmacy-vertical opportunity. However, the offering is not expected to contribute meaningful revenue in 2026, limiting the near-term financial impact of the win.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CVS, one of the largest retail pharmacy chains, went live in Q3 as one of Fluent’s largest partner wins”; the new in-store offering is “not expected to contribute meaningful revenue in 2026,” with material impact anticipated in 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Any signed conversion would extend the H2 narrative” and called a concrete Fluent In-Store commercialization update a likely source of upside; deployment had been “slated for mid-July to August 2026.”

surprises.description: Cash was $6.9 million, down from $12.9 million at year-end even as short-term debt was reduced; first-half operating cash flow was only about $300,000. The preview had flagged going-concern and facility availability as issues, but provided no expected cash balance or cash-flow figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and equivalents fell to $6.9 million from $12.9 million at year-end 2025,” short-term debt fell to $26.8 million from $30.8 million, and first-half operating cash flow was “approximately $300,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Going-concern language in the 10-Q” and “Bay View facility availability,” noting that borrowing capacity depended on eligible receivables.

in_line: Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance for improved adjusted EBITDA, consistent with the preview’s account of prior guidance calling for 2026 adjusted EBITDA “improvement.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $28.1 million, above the $27.29 million consensus, and year-over-year growth was 33% versus the 28.7% implied by consensus. Revenue was also within the preview’s $27.8–28.2 million buy-side whisper range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $28.1 million, up 33% year-over-year, accelerating from 29% growth in Q1 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $27.29M”; “Implies +28.7% Y/Y”; and “Buy-side whisper is about $27.8–28.2M.”

surprises.description: The raised FY2026 revenue range of $114–117 million was below the buy-side expectation of roughly $115–118 million, with a smaller increase than the preview said investors were looking for. The result was closer to the preview’s base case than its stated buy-side aspiration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $114-$117 million … from prior guidance of $112-$116 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise to roughly $115–118M is what the buy side is looking for”; “Anything under about a $3M raise reads as H2 caution.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 92%, well above the preview’s 87–88% expectation. Even excluding the $1.6 million tariff refund, margin was 89%, still above expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin hit a record 92%, or 89% excluding a $1.6 million tariff refund, benefiting from manufacturing diversification to Vietnam and cost reductions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~87–88%”; “Guided ‘high-80s’ for the year.”

surprises.description: GAAP loss per share was worse than expected: the reported $0.51 loss exceeded the consensus loss of $0.47 per share, even though adjusted EBITDA loss was narrower than the preview’s $11 million threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $19.3 million ($0.51 per share) from $13.6 million ($0.38 per share) a year ago, while adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed slightly to $9.8 million from $10.0 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP net loss/sh) | ($0.47)”; “Adjusted EBITDA loss of $11M or less.”

surprises.description: The account-add target was met, but the company also said growth relied less on VA accounts than in prior quarters, pointing to greater organic sales-force contribution than the preview specifically anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company added 32 active accounts to reach 712 total, with growth relying less on VA accounts than in prior quarters, indicating organic sales force maturation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for at least 30 in Q2”; “Net new accounts of 30 or more. Confirms Q1 was not a one-off.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed two new FDA-cleared seizure algorithms that will carry no additional charges and are intended to increase utilization and product stickiness; the preview did not flag these clearances.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received FDA 510(k) clearances for two new seizure algorithms (artifact rejection and epileptiform abnormality detection), which will not carry additional charges but aim to boost utilization and stickiness.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a credit-facility refinancing that provides access to up to $60 million of committed capital, reduces interest expense beginning in Q4, and extends repayment into 2031—financing terms not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company held $129.3 million in cash and marketable securities and refinanced its credit facility to access up to $60 million committed capital, reducing interest expense starting Q4 and extending repayment into 2031.”

surprises.description: Management described substantial remaining room to grow in the core seizure market and much higher usage at leading accounts, adding a utilization and market-penetration datapoint not quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cited less than 4% penetration in its core seizure market, with top accounts using the product at roughly three times the rate of average accounts of similar size.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “positive year-over-year same-store growth,” but did not quantify market penetration or the usage gap between top and average accounts.

in_line: The company added 32 accounts, meeting the preview’s expectation of at least 30.
Adjusted EBITDA loss was $9.8 million, within the preview’s expected threshold of $11 million or less.
NTAP’s October 1, 2026 effective date and up-to-$2,171 payment per qualified patient matched the preview’s stated terms.

The preview described delirium as a roughly $1 billion market and anticipated commercialization after NTAP; the call’s Q4 2026 launch plan and stated market size were broadly consistent with that framing.

surprises.description: LINC reported Q2 student-start growth of just 1%, well below the preview’s 8–12% house estimate. Management attributed the shortfall to weaker AI-driven lead generation, financial-aid packaging delays, and student loan defaults.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Student start growth slowed dramatically to just 1% in Q2 versus nearly 20% in Q1”; a lower percentage of enrollments converted to starts due to “weaker AI-driven lead generation, financial aid packaging delays, and student loan defaults.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Student starts: House estimate +8–12%”; the preview also said a “headline slowdown from Q1's +19.5% to high single digits is likely mechanical.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year capex outlook to $95–100 million from the previously guided $70–75 million, rather than keeping investment near the preview’s expected range. The increase reflects the Melrose Park property purchase and Suitland campus spending, with about 75% of capex tied to growth initiatives.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year capital expenditure guidance was raised from $70–$75 million to $95–$100 million,” reflecting the $18.8 million Melrose Park property purchase and Suitland campus spend; “~75% of CapEx” is tied to growth initiatives.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance … capex $70–75M”; the preview also said management guided about half of FY26 capex, or ~$35M, into Q2.

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed the existing full-year guidance instead of making the increase the preview’s base case anticipated. The reaffirmed revenue and adjusted EBITDA ranges are below the preview’s expected raised ranges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reiterated full-year guidance of $590–$600 million revenue, $76–$80 million adjusted EBITDA, $23–$26 million net income, $0.74–$0.83 diluted EPS, and 10–14% student start growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “a guidance raise to roughly $595–605M revenue and $78–82M EBITDA”; it said “an in-line reaffirmation would likely be read as negative.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA came in below the preview’s $14 million base case and below the low end of its $13–15 million house estimate, even as revenue exceeded expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 42.4% to $12.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: Not found (house estimate ~$13–15M)”; the preview’s base case was “adj. EBITDA of $14.0M.”

surprises.description: Management projected a near-term recovery in starts, saying Q3 growth should return to the low double digits and that the August class would be the largest in company history. The preview anticipated a Q2 slowdown but did not forecast this specific strength in the next start class.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects Q3 student starts to return to low double-digit year-over-year growth,” with “the largest August start class in company history” and high school starts expected to be up more than 15%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said “starts decelerate but reconcile,” and its management-signals section said the bull case needed “specific organic start figures.”

surprises.description: Net income and diluted EPS were stronger than the preview’s already modest Q2 EPS expectation: LINC earned $0.06 per share rather than the $0.03 base case or roughly breakeven consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income increased 25% to $1.9 million ($0.06 diluted EPS),” though net income grew more slowly than EBITDA because of higher depreciation.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “EPS of $0.03”; consensus was “~$0.00 (about $0.001; some feeds show a small loss).”

surprises.description: Revenue modestly exceeded both the preview’s base case and published consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 22.4% to $142.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “revenue of about $141M”; published consensus was “$139.49M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected additional campus expansion announcements but did not anticipate the economics of the Suitland focused-campus model. The disclosed model uses substantially less capital than a traditional campus while targeting a 30%+ IRR and meaningful fully ramped revenue and EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Suitland “focused campus” model requires “only ~$10 million in capital (vs. ~$25 million for traditional campuses), targets a 30%+ IRR, and is expected to generate over $50 million revenue and $5 million EBITDA at full ramp.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management was “evaluating about a dozen markets and expected to announce more expansions by Q2 results.”

surprises.description: Student attrition improved by about 150 basis points year over year, helping keep the student population more than 10% higher despite weak Q2 starts; the preview did not identify this retention improvement as an expected offset.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Student attrition improved approximately 150 basis points year-over-year,” helping keep the student population up over 10% (roughly 1,800 students) across 22 campuses.

in_line: The full-year new-campus loss of approximately $10 million remains included in guidance, consistent with the preview’s expectation that those losses would be included in adjusted EBITDA.
Management announced an additional campus expansion, Suitland, meeting the preview’s expectation that it would announce more expansions by Q2 results.

surprises.description: The preview did not flag GCM Grosvenor’s SpaceX investment as a driver, but the firm said its roughly $150 million investment was worth about $3.5 billion as of last week, its largest single-issuer gain ever. The gain remains unrealized and subject to lockup.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The firm's ~$150 million investment in SpaceX (average cost of $6.37 per share) was valued at approximately $3.5 billion as of last week,” with “gains remain unrealized and subject to lockup.”

surprises.description: The preview’s base case put FRE at $48–49 million and expected mid-to-high-teens year-over-year growth. GCM Grosvenor reported $50 million of FRE, up 21%, modestly above that base expectation and at the preview’s bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fee-related earnings grew 21% to $50 million (45% FRE margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: ... FRE $48–49M (44–45%)”; “FRE grows in line” and “FRE should be up mid-to-high teens YoY.”

surprises.description: The call newly quantified substantial prospective performance fees linked to SpaceX, but said most would crystallize in Q4 and the estimate depends on the share price. This adds visibility to potential fees while indicating they are not yet realized and are weighted toward later in the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Unrealized annual performance fees are estimated at $35–40 million (assuming a $110 SpaceX share price)”; “most fees crystallizing in Q4.”

surprises.description: The preview did not give a Q3 ARS fee outlook. GCM Grosvenor said Q2 ARS performance should lift fees by about 10% sequentially and nearly 20% year over year, because fees are billed in advance on beginning-of-quarter AUM.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Strong Q2 performance is expected to drive Q3 ARS fees up ~10% sequentially and nearly 20% year-over-year”; ARS fees are “billed quarterly in advance on beginning-of-quarter AUM.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that individual investors and insurance were disproportionately important sources of new fundraising: together they generated 41% of year-to-date fundraising despite representing only 9% of AUM at the start of the year. The preview noted wealth fundraising as a catalyst but did not anticipate this level of channel contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Individual investor and insurance channels drove 23% and 18% of year-to-date fundraising despite representing only 5% and 4% of AUM at the start of the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 wealth raise was about $500M” and “Wealth and evergreen products” were listed as a catalyst; no channel contribution estimate was given.

surprises.description: AUM ended at $97 billion, above the preview’s $95 billion threshold for its bull scenario. This was a modestly stronger result than that optimistic scenario marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GCM Grosvenor ended Q2 2026 with $97 billion in AUM and $78 billion in fee-paying AUM.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Bull scenario: “AUM above $95B.”

in_line: Q2 fundraising was $2.3 billion, above Q1’s $1.5 billion and within the preview’s roughly $2.0–2.5 billion base range; the preview also said second-quarter fundraising was expected to exceed Q1.
Management’s outlook for second-half fundraising to exceed first-half levels matched the preview’s expectation that the back half would outpace the front half.
Fee-related revenue of $111 million was within the preview’s $109–111 million range implied by its expense and margin discussion.
The 45% FRE margin was within the preview’s expected 44–45% range.
The inaugural credit secondaries fund raised about $1.2 billion, consistent with the preview’s note that the fund had reached its final close in Q3.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.12, twice the preview’s $0.06 consensus, although the preview cautioned that vendors differed on whether that consensus was GAAP or adjusted. Adjusted net income was essentially flat year over year, rather than showing comparable growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income of $6.4 million and adjusted EPS of $0.12 were both essentially flat versus the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS” consensus was “$0.06”; the preview noted that “the adjusted-versus-GAAP basis of the EPS consensus is ambiguous across vendors.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was well above the preview’s $10.2 million back-solve and its $10.5–$11.5 million base case. It still declined 2% year over year and its margin contracted, but the reported $13.6 million was much stronger than those expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell 2% to $13.6 million with margin contracting to 4.2% from 4.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave a “back-solve ~$10.2M” and a base case of “$10.5–11.5M” in adjusted EBITDA.

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 17%, above the preview’s 16.3–16.6% base case and roughly 16.4% catalyst level. Incremental tariffs pressured it, but IEEPA tariff refunds partly offset that pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit was essentially flat at $55 million with gross margin declining to 17% from 17.5%, pressured by incremental tariffs but partially offset by IEEPA tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My base case is 16.3–16.6%”; the catalyst checklist also cited “~16.4%.”

surprises.description: Revenue modestly exceeded the $320.5 million consensus at $323.8 million. Seafood volume growth and improved pricing drove the increase, while lower meat and poultry prices partly offset it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 2.8% year-over-year to a record $323.8 million, driven primarily by seafood volume growth and improved pricing, partially offset by price declines in meat and poultry.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 net revenue consensus was “$320.5M.”

surprises.description: The call described Sea Ray as immediately accretive to margins and EPS and as supporting a 4.5%–5%+ consolidated EBITDA margin target. The preview discussed the acquisition and its funding, but did not flag these accretion claims or this margin target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sea Ray operates at mid-teens EBITDA margins and gross margins north of 20%, making the deal accretive to both margins and EPS from close and supporting the 4.5%-5%+ consolidated EBITDA margin target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on “Searay funding plan” and described the FY2026 framing as “low single-digit growth in both revenue and adjusted EBITDA”; it did not state an acquisition-accretion claim or a 4.5%–5%+ margin target.

surprises.description: After quarter end, HF Foods expanded its credit capacity and extended maturities, an additional financing development beyond the preview’s discussion of the expected Sea Ray funding burden and existing revolver headroom. The facts do not say that the expanded facility funded the acquisition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company refinanced and upsized its credit facility after quarter end, increasing revolving commitments from $125 million to $140 million and expanding term loans from ~$95 million to $125 million, extending maturities to 2031 and 2036.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the deal’s cash portion “nearly exhausts revolver headroom” and that “Revolver funding is manageable”; it did not mention an upsized facility or extended maturities.

surprises.description: The call disclosed a sharp rise in DSNA expense, driven by higher fuel, insurance, and professional-service costs—an operating cost pressure not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DSNA expense rose 2.4% to $52.2 million, driven largely by approximately $1.4 million in higher year-over-year fuel costs plus higher insurance and professional service expenses.”

surprises.description: Reported net income more than doubled, but the call attributed the increase to an employee retention credit, a tariff refund, and a favorable swap valuation change; adjusted net income was essentially flat. The preview had noted unusual gains in Q1, but did not anticipate these Q2 items.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income attributable to HF Foods more than doubled to $2.6 million (EPS of $0.05 vs. $0.02), boosted by a $1.8 million employee retention credit, a ~$1.1 million tariff refund, and a $1.4 million favorable swap fair-value change.” Also: “Adjusted net income of $6.4 million and adjusted EPS of $0.12 were both essentially flat versus the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that Q1 GAAP profit “was helped by a $1.4M gain on a Utah property sale and a favorable interest-rate-swap mark,” but gave no expectation for these Q2 credits or valuation changes.

surprises.description: First-half capex totaled about $20.3 million, including a $12.4 million purchase of the leased Chicago distribution center and $2.8 million for solar. The preview flagged capex and Chicago projects as items to watch, but did not anticipate this purchase or provide an expected spending amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half capex reached ~$20.3 million, driven by a $12.4 million purchase of the leased Chicago distribution center, $2.8 million in solar (eligible for a 40% tax credit refund), and other capacity and fleet investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Free cash flow and capex cadence” and listed “Charlotte, Atlanta Phase II, and Chicago” as projects in progress; it gave no capex forecast or expectation that the Chicago site would be purchased.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $1.0 million, far below the preview’s roughly $3.3 million consensus. Management said revenue also fell meaningfully short of internal expectations as several customer deployments slipped by one to two quarters; service revenue was down $0.2 million year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenues declined 18% year-over-year to $1 million” and “several key customer deployments slipped by one to two quarters,” causing revenue to “fall meaningfully short of internal expectations.”

surprises.description: Gross margin turned negative, sharply below the preview’s expectation that product gross margin would trend toward the mid-30s. Costs rose with higher unit volume, and management said margin improvement depends on scaling 5G product sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin turned negative in Q2 2026 versus 32% a year earlier,” as “cost of revenues rose 49% to $1.2 million on higher unit volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether product GM trends toward the mid-30s.”

surprises.description: The reported net loss widened to $20.4 million, well beyond the loss implied by the preview’s EPS expectations. Much of the loss came from a non-cash warrant-liability revaluation, while adjusted EBITDA loss was essentially unchanged year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened by $8.1 million year-over-year to $20.4 million,” including “$12.3 million in non-cash losses from fair value changes in common stock warrant liabilities.” Adjusted EBITDA loss was “essentially flat year-over-year at $6.6 million (versus $6.7 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the −$0.08 consensus EPS “implies a ~$6.2M net loss” and gave a “realistic band” of −$0.12 to −$0.18.

surprises.description: GCT ended Q2 with $30.2 million in cash, above the preview’s downside scenario of cash below $15 million. The preview had highlighted liquidity and the 2026 debt wall, but the reported cash balance alone does not establish that the maturities were resolved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $30.2 million in cash.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bear scenario listed “cash <$15M”; the preview also flagged “Cash and the 2026 debt wall” as the top metric to watch.

surprises.description: The company expanded its ATM program’s maximum gross proceeds from $75 million to $120 million. The preview had flagged the existing ATM and dilution as risks, but did not anticipate this increase in the program’s capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GCT amended its ATM equity program to raise maximum gross proceeds from $75 million to $120 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the ATM as “persistent overhead supply” and listed “Confirm the current ATM capacity and share count” as a next step.

surprises.description: GCT prepaid for wafer capacity through year-end, adding $7 million to $7.5 million to Q2 cash burn, and guided to quarterly cash burn of $9 million to $9.5 million in the current supply-chain environment. The preview did not anticipate this specific cash outlay or elevated burn guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GCT prepaid for wafer capacity through the end of 2026,” inflating Q2 cash burn by “$7 million to $7.5 million”; management guided quarterly cash burn of “$9 million to $9.5 million” versus a normalized “$8 million to $8.5 million.”

surprises.description: After the quarter, GCT signed a customer in UAV/defense connectivity, a customer addition the preview did not identify as an expected catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: GCT “signed a new post-quarter customer in the UAV/defense connectivity space.”

in_line: GCT shipped more than 5,100 chipsets, roughly matching the preview’s base-case range of 5,000–7,000 and clearing its stated ~5,000-unit threshold for the ramp not to look stalled.

surprises.description: Revita patients maintained more than 80% of their prior GLP-1-induced weight loss at one year, versus 46% in the sham arm, and none in the midpoint cohort restarted GLP-1 therapy. A separate open-label cohort maintained approximately 78%, adding another supportive durability result; the preview did not discuss these clinical findings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revita patients maintained more than 80% of their prior GLP-1-induced weight loss at one year versus 46% in the sham arm, with no patients reinitiating GLP-1 therapy in the midpoint cohort”; the open-label Reveal One cohort “maintained approximately 78% of prior weight loss through one year.”

surprises.description: The company reported no device- or procedure-related serious adverse events over a full year, and only four mild treatment-emergent events, all resolving within two days. The preview did not set expectations for these safety results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over one full year, there were zero device- or procedure-related serious adverse events, with only four mild treatment-emergent adverse events that all resolved within two days.”

surprises.description: Management said both pivotal co-primary endpoints are powered above 95%, with a 73% midpoint responder rate in the MITT population and above 90% among complete-ablation patients, compared with the FDA's 50% threshold. The preview did not anticipate these interim efficacy and power details.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Both co-primary pivotal endpoints are powered above 95%,” with the “midpoint responder rate at 73% (MITT) and above 90% in complete-ablation patients versus the FDA's 50% threshold.”

surprises.description: The $47.1 million cash balance was at the top of the preview's $43–47 million estimate, and management gave a firmer funding assurance: operations are funded beyond pivotal data and through a potential De Novo submission, with no raise planned before pivotal data.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended Q2 with “$47.1 million in cash, funding operations into early 2027 beyond pivotal data and through a potential de novo submission, with no planned raise before pivotal data.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Cash at 6/30/26: “Own estimate $43–47M”; the preview also flagged “into early 2027” runway language and described the bull case as runway “beyond early 2027.”

surprises.description: Q2 R&D expense was slightly below the preview's $14–16 million estimate, at $13.8 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 R&D expenses fell to $13.8 million from $21.2 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “R&D expense, Q2” — “own estimate $14–16M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA loss of $16.3 million was below the preview's $17–19 million base-case range, landing instead in its under-$17 million bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA improving to negative $16.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected an “Adj. EBITDA loss” of “$17–19M”; the bull scenario was “Under $17M.”

surprises.description: Management said Revita is expected to qualify for CMS transitional pass-through payment as a breakthrough device, potentially enabling reimbursement from launch. The preview did not identify this reimbursement pathway or the targeted center-of-excellence launch approach.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects Revita to qualify for CMS transitional pass-through payment as a breakthrough device, enabling reimbursement from day one of launch through a targeted center-of-excellence model in the top 100-200 endoscopy health systems.”

in_line: The company reaffirmed the preview's early-Q4 2026 timing for six-month pivotal top-line data and late-Q4 2026 timing for a potential FDA De Novo submission.

surprises.description: Revenue was $23.3 million, 5% lower year over year, versus the preview’s $24.6 million consensus and flat-growth expectation. Management attributed the entire decline to international pullbacks, including lower-value regions and third-party acquisition channels.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 5% year-over-year to $23.3 million,” with “the entire decline attributed to the international business” as Gaia pulled back from lower-value regions and third-party acquisition channels.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $24.60M”; “Implied YoY 0.0%.”

surprises.description: Management withdrew the prior Q4 net-income breakeven target and now aims only to return to positive free cash flow in Q4. The preview emphasized that an unqualified reaffirmation of Q4 breakeven mattered and that a hedge would be a negative development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management withdrew its prior guidance for Q4 breakeven net income, now targeting only a return to positive free cash flow in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 2026 breakeven language. An unqualified reaffirmation matters more than a revenue beat. Any hedge, such as ‘approaching breakeven,’ is the bear trigger.”

surprises.description: The call also walked back earlier expectations for double-digit Q4 revenue growth, beyond the preview’s expectation that growth would uptick in Q4. This reduces the growth implied by the earlier outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management was “walking back earlier expectations of double-digit Q4 revenue growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided to a ‘short to midterm lull’ in revenue for the next one or two quarters, with growth ‘upticking’ only into Q4.”

surprises.description: The net loss widened to $3.0 million, but EPS was a loss of $0.12, one cent better than the preview’s $0.13 loss consensus. The per-share result was a small positive surprise even as the loss increased year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $3.0 million (-$0.12 per share) from a $1.8 million loss (-$0.07 per share) a year earlier.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 85.3%, below the preview’s approximate 86% model assumption. Management attributed the decline from 86.7% a year ago to lower revenue against a relatively fixed content-cost base.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 85.3% from 86.7% a year ago due to lower revenue against a relatively fixed content cost base.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin: Not found (model ~86%).”

surprises.description: A major advertising partner’s algorithm change caused a CPA spike in April and May and pressured results, an operating headwind the preview did not flag. Management said the issue has since been corrected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A CPA spike in April and May, driven by an algorithm change at a major advertising partner, pressured results, though management states the issue has since been corrected.”

surprises.description: Cash fell to $5.3 million from $13.1 million at the end of Q1, with seasonal renewals, lower revenue, and higher marketing costs contributing. The preview cited the prior cash balance and undrawn $10 million revolver but did not anticipate this decline; the available credit line partly mitigates the liquidity pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash fell to $5.3 million as of June 30, 2026, pressured by a $2.4 million seasonal renewal impact, lower revenue and higher marketing costs, with a fully available $10 million line of credit as backup.”

surprises.description: The company reported more than $3 million in annualized savings executed or identified, with full benefit expected by year-end; G&A also fell to $1.5 million from $2.9 million. The preview did not anticipate this scale of cost reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has executed or identified over $3 million in annualized cost savings since starting its spend review in late February, with full benefit expected by year-end”; “G&A expenses fell to $1.5 million from $2.9 million.”

surprises.description: Management said it does not anticipate another price increase until 2028. The preview discussed the March price increase and its possible churn effects, but did not flag this extended pause in further pricing changes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Following the March 1 price increase, management does not anticipate raising prices again until 2028.”

in_line: Management said it remains on track for its Q4 framework of a 20% improvement in churn reduction and ARPU growth, broadly consistent with the preview’s cited churn and ARPU targets. The preview had looked for evidence of progress after the March price increase.
Management expects Q3 to mark the revenue bottom before sequential growth in Q4, consistent with the preview’s description of a near-term lull followed by growth upticking into Q4.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $8.1 million, about 14% above the $7.1 million consensus, rather than the 6.6% year-over-year decline implied by that estimate. Revenue instead rose 6% year over year, marking the first year-over-year growth since Q3 2024.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue rose 6% year-over-year to $8.1 million” and “This marked the company's first year-over-year revenue growth since Q3 2024.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $7.10M” and “Implied Y/Y | −6.6%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.23, well above both the published $0.12–$0.13 consensus and the preview’s roughly $0.15 functional bar. GAAP diluted EPS was also $0.19, with net income more than doubling year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income rose to $3.2 million ($0.23 per diluted share) from $2.1 million ($0.15)” and “Net income more than doubled to $2.7 million ($0.19 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS | $0.12 (MarketBeat) or $0.13 (Public.com)” and “the functional bar may sit above the $0.12 print consensus,” with a catalyst checklist citing “the roughly $0.15 level the beat pattern implies.”

surprises.description: Systemwide sales grew 6.9% after adjusting for the divested MRI assets, materially ahead of the preview’s near-flat comparison and +2% base case. The result was below the preview’s +8% bull case, but still showed stronger underlying sales than the central expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Systemwide sales declined to $117.8 million from $125.9 million, but grew 6.9% pro forma after adjusting for roughly $17.7 million of divested MRI assets in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Stripping roughly $16M of MRI perm sales from Q2 2025 SWS of $125.9M leaves a base near $110M. Management called ex-divestiture SWS ‘nearly flat’ in Q1”; the base scenario expected “~$112M (+2% ex-MRI).”

surprises.description: Growth strengthened as Q2 progressed and remained strong into early Q3, adding evidence of momentum beyond the reported quarterly beat. The preview’s base case anticipated only modest underlying sales growth and did not flag this acceleration or persistence into Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-over-year revenue growth accelerated within the quarter from roughly 2%-4% early on to as much as 12%-13% in some later weeks, and that momentum has held six weeks into Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario assumed “SWS ~$112M (+2% ex-MRI)” and “commercial carries; on-demand flat to slightly up.”

surprises.description: Management described growth as supported by tightening labor supply, manufacturing and reshoring activity, and national-accounts investment; selling franchisees’ top lines were up nearly 15%. Those specific drivers and franchisee performance were not anticipated in the preview’s more modest base-case outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management attributes growth to tightening labor supply from 2025 immigration policies, a manufacturing/reshoring uptick, and national accounts investments, with selling franchisees growing top line nearly 15%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case said “Commercial carries; on-demand flat to slightly up.”

surprises.description: SG&A fell to $4.0 million from $5.9 million, and management attributed the improvement not only to the absence of prior-year TrueBlue-related legal fees but also to restored economies of scale rather than one-time cost cutting. That suggests an operating-efficiency contribution beyond the preview’s emphasis on prior-year M&A costs and a likely GAAP-versus-adjusted gap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A fell to $4.0 million from $5.9 million, partly reflecting the absence of prior-year legal fees tied to the attempted TrueBlue takeover and restored economies of scale rather than one-time cost cuts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2025 SG&A included $929K of M&A costs, so a wide GAAP-versus-adjusted gap is likely.”

surprises.description: The preview expected Q2 revenue of $7.5M–$7.8M, with consensus at $7.55M. Bionano reported $8.2M, above the top of its guided range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $8.2 million,” above the guided range of “$7.5 to $7.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus $7.55M | Company guidance (Q2) $7.5M – $7.8M.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged consumables growth near 18%–20% as a key benchmark. Consumable revenue grew 30%, materially exceeding that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consumable revenue grew 30% year-over-year to $4.3 million,” driven primarily by increased clinical adoption of OGM.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for consumables growth near 18%–20%.”

surprises.description: The preview's base case expected adjusted gross margin of about 49%. The reported 53% was four percentage points higher and a record.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin reached a record 53% in Q2 2026,” up from 52% a year ago.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GM ~49%” in the base scenario.

surprises.description: The preview's base case anticipated FY2026 guidance narrowing to about $30M–$31M, while the bull case was for the existing $30M–$33M range to hold. Instead, Bionano raised the low end to $31M and kept the $33M top end, though it said manufacturing capacity constrained the upper end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance had its low end raised to $31-$33 million,” with “the top end held back due to manufacturing capacity constraints.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A narrowing to $30M–$31M would be consistent with the trend”; the bull scenario said “FY guide held at $30M–$33M.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for flow-cell sales at or above 9,000, and Bionano sold 9,219. But the call also disclosed that demand was exceeding manufacturing capacity and creating a backlog expected to last until mid-to-late Q4, an unanticipated limit on serving demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Flow cells sold hit a record 9,219 units, up 27% year-over-year,” while “demand continues to outpace manufacturing capacity, creating a backlog expected to clear by mid-to-late Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for ... flow cells at or above 9,000 per quarter.”

surprises.description: The preview gave no Q3 revenue outlook. Bionano guided to $8.2M–$8.6M, implying only flat-to-modest sequential growth, and cited caution about large orders that could slip between quarters.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $8.2-$8.6 million” implies “roughly flat-to-modest sequential growth,” attributed to conservatism around “large orders at risk of slipping quarters.”

in_line: Flow-cell sales were at least 9,000 units, as the preview identified as a key benchmark; the separate surprise was that demand outpaced manufacturing capacity.
Cash of $10.4M and runway into at least Q1 2027 were broadly consistent with the preview's estimated $8M–$10M exiting cash and its expectation that runway would extend into 2027.
The debt retirement was already described in the preview as completed on May 26, so fully retiring the outstanding senior secured convertible debt during the quarter was not new.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $54 million versus the preview’s $5–12 million expected range, a very large headline beat. However, about $45 million came from favorable settlements and prior-year development, leaving roughly $9 million of underlying EBITDA—within the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $54 million”; approximately “$45 million reflected favorable payer settlements ($41 million, affecting only medical claims expense, not revenue) and prior year development,” leaving “underlying adjusted EBITDA of only about $9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA: ~$5–12M”; the preview also said an outcome “Above $12M likely forces a guidance raise.”

surprises.description: Management raised FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $80–110 million, midpoint $95 million, far above the preview’s expected $20–60 million range and its base case of reaffirming that range. The raised outlook still implies about $15 million of additional underlying EBITDA in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $80 million to $110 million with a midpoint of $95 million, implying roughly $15 million of additional underlying EBITDA in the back half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (50%): … FY guide reaffirmed at $20–60M”; “FY26 guidance action: reaffirm is largely priced in; a raise is the bull trigger.”

surprises.description: Q2 medical margin was $98 million, well above the preview’s derived $40–52 million expectation. The call also reported an adjusted medical loss ratio of 85.6% after excluding favorable settlements and prior-year development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 medical margin was $98 million ($311 PMPM) with an adjusted medical loss ratio of 85.6% after excluding favorable settlements and prior year development.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Medical margin: ~$40–52M”; the preview’s catalyst checklist also looked for “medical margin ex prior-period items at or above ~$45M.”

surprises.description: MA medical cost trend was 1.8% below the full-year 2025 baseline, better than the preview’s backdrop of a roughly flat Q1 trend and its expectation that the favorable trend would hold. The reported trend also contrasted with peers’ 5–7% increases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “MA medical cost trend for the first half of 2026 ran 1.8% below the full-year 2025 baseline,” compared with peers “running 5% to 7% year-over-year increases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “P3 reported a roughly flat Q1 Medicare Advantage trend against an industry guide of 7%+”; the bull scenario assumed “Clean trend holds.”

surprises.description: Revenue reached $386 million, modestly above the $377.95 million consensus and just above the preview’s $375–385 million base-case range. The reported year-over-year growth was supported by about 15% higher per-member funding despite fewer at-risk members.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue rose to $386 million from $356 million a year earlier, driven by an approximately 15% year-over-year improvement in per-member funding despite the lower membership base.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q2 FY26 Consensus | $377.95M”; base case “Revenue $375–385M.”

surprises.description: The company ended Q2 with only $21 million in cash, indicating tighter liquidity than the preview’s Q1 reference point of $25.5 million. The preview had flagged liquidity and the remaining preferred commitment as issues to watch, but did not forecast an ending cash level.
