surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.33, below the preview’s $0.42–$0.45 consensus range; adjusted net income also fell 27% year over year. This was a substantial profitability shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted net income fell 27% to approximately $29 million and adjusted EPS declined to $0.33 from $0.45.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adjusted EPS (Q2) consensus: $0.42 – $0.45.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $145 million, below the preview’s $155.9–$159.0 million consensus range. Revenue still reached a second-quarter record, but growth was only 1.9% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue rose only 1.9% year-over-year to $145 million, a company record for any second quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Total revenue (Q2) consensus: $155.9M – $159.0M.

surprises.description: Originations declined about 9% year over year rather than re-accelerating, as the preview said would be important for back-half revenue growth. Management attributed the decline to tighter underwriting in segments with less attractive risk-adjusted returns.
surprises.fact_evidence: Originations declined approximately 9% year-over-year to $212 million as the company tightened underwriting in segments with less attractive risk-adjusted returns.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue growth in the back half depends on originations re-accelerating, and the credit tightening could be limiting growth.

surprises.description: The line of credit launch was pushed to September, a two-month delay the preview did not identify as an issue to watch. The delay was also cited as one reason for the FY2026 guidance cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: The line of credit product launch has been pushed to September, effectively a two-month delay, and will initially open three new geographies to net-new customers.

surprises.description: Despite cutting FY2026 guidance, management reaffirmed a path to approximately $3 of EPS by the end of 2028 and $500 million of adjusted net income within five years. The preview focused on FY2026 and did not set out these longer-term targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management reaffirmed 2027 and 2028 targets, including a path to approximately $3 of EPS by end of 2028 and $500 million of adjusted net income within five years.

surprises.description: Management also gave 2028 return targets for the combined OppFi-BNC entity—at least 10% ROA and 35% ROE—which were not specified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management projects the combined OppFi-BNC entity to generate return on assets of at least 10% and return on equity of at least 35% by 2028.

in_line: Net charge-offs were approximately 52% of receivables, at the upper end of the preview’s 49%–52% base case and below its >53% bear-case threshold; the rate improved sequentially from Q1’s 55.5%, though it remained above Q2 2025’s 43%.
The BNC acquisition remained targeted to close in Q4 2026, as the preview expected; regulatory applications had been submitted to the OCC.

surprises.description: Revenue was expected to be about $0.90 million, but Q2 revenue was approximately $1.7 million—nearly 90% above the preview’s base case. The reported growth was driven by barter advertising, Truth+ Patriot Package subscriptions, and Truth.Fi ETF management fees.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was approximately $1.7 million, up 92% sequentially and 89% year-over-year,” driven by barter advertising, Truth+ Patriot Package subscriptions, and Truth.Fi ETF management fees.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “For reference only, a self-built base case (not consensus) is about $0.90M revenue (+2% y/y).”

surprises.description: The preview expected about $1.01 billion of cash against roughly $962 million of debt, but the company reported only $215 million of cash and $209 million of short-term investments. With nearly $1 billion of convertible notes coming due, management said it was exploring repayment or refinancing options rather than describing a settled solution.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended Q2 with “$215 million cash” and “$209 million short-term investments”; it faces “nearly $1 billion in outstanding convertible notes coming due” and is “exploring multiple repayment or refinancing options,” with over $400 million fully liquid and unencumbered.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash is about $1.01B against about $962M of total debt, a net cash position of roughly $49M.” The preview also said cash below about $900 million would be a problem.

surprises.description: The preview’s base case was a net loss near $180 million, while the company reported a $238 million loss, a moderately larger loss than expected. The loss was still largely attributed to non-cash mark-to-market items, which the preview had anticipated as a major driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported a net loss of $238 million for the quarter,” largely from non-cash mark-to-market losses.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s self-built base case was “a net loss near $(180)M,” while modeling $140–250 million of crypto and securities marks.

surprises.description: The preview noted at least five Truth API firms reportedly signed, while the call reported more than 10 customer agreements, indicating broader early uptake than that report suggested. The call also said revenue recognized remains modest, so the agreements have not yet translated into substantial reported revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: Truth API “has signed more than 10 customer agreements, primarily high-frequency trading firms paying roughly $60,000 to $100,000 per month, though revenue recognized remains modest.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “at least five firms reportedly signed at the top tier” and listed Truth API subscribers, contracted ARR, and pricing tiers as items to watch.

surprises.description: The company disclosed that it acquired additional bitcoin in July by selling part of its IBIT position, a post-quarter asset reallocation not anticipated in the preview. The call did not say whether this shift changed the company’s overall risk exposure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In July [the company] acquired an additional 2,534 bitcoins via a partial IBIT sale.”

surprises.description: The company reported $165.2 million of operating expenses, driven partly by legacy SPAC litigation costs that the preview did not flag. The preview anticipated substantial crypto and securities marks, but did not identify this litigation expense driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses reached $165.2 million,” driven mainly by digital asset mark-to-market and “legacy SPAC litigation costs.”

in_line: The $116.6 million digital-asset loss was attributed to bitcoin’s roughly 13% decline from March 31 to June 30, consistent with the preview’s expected price decline and its warning that crypto marks would drive the quarter’s loss.

The company’s target to close the TAE Technologies merger by year-end 2026, with the S-4 still pending completion of TAE’s audits, was consistent with the preview’s Q4 2026 target and its note that the S-4 had not yet been filed.

The Crypto.com/Yorkville treasury combination had already been terminated before the release, and the preview had also noted that prediction markets were being scaled back. The call’s marketing-agreement pivot therefore did not represent a new departure from the preview.
Truth API launched after the quarter ended, and the preview expected no Q2 contribution; the call’s statement that recognized revenue remains modest is consistent with that expectation.

The preview anticipated vague language on the convertible notes as its base case. The call’s statement that the company was exploring multiple repayment or refinancing options did not provide a specific resolution.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was more than $753 million, well above the preview’s $690–$699 million consensus range and the company’s $680–$700 million guidance. The preview’s higher $730 million screen was itself described as likely stale or mis-mapped, and the reported figure exceeded it too.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew nearly 40% year-over-year to more than $753 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus … $690M – $699M”; company guidance “$680M – $700M.” The preview also notes one screen at “$730.12M” was “likely stale or mis-mapped.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY26 revenue guidance to $3.1–$3.3 billion, above the preview’s expected $2.8–$3.0 billion range. This was a meaningful upward revision rather than the expected reaffirmation of the prior range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $3.1-$3.3 billion (32-41% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists FY26 revenue guidance as “$2.8B – $3.0B (raised)” and says “FY26 revenue raised to $2.8B–$3.0B.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $60 million, above both the $35–$55 million company guide and the preview’s roughly $45 million consensus estimate. The result cleared even the top of the guided range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $60 million (8% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA $35M – $55M”; consensus “~$45M (guide midpoint).”

surprises.description: Subscriber growth came in ahead of the preview’s implied range: the company added 300,000 net new subscribers and ended near 3 million, versus an expectation of about 2.65–2.75 million total subscribers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adding 300,000 net new subscribers to reach nearly 3 million total.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Subscribers … ~2.65M – 2.75M (implied).”

surprises.description: The preview flagged gross margin around 62%–64% and further compression, and the reported 64% was within that range. However, management characterized lower margins as structural because of the branded weight-loss and international mix, rather than establishing that the expected range was a temporary floor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin fell about 6 points quarter-over-quarter to 64%, and management expects margins to remain structurally lower due to the mix shift toward branded weight loss and international revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says management expected compression by “a couple more points,” estimates gross margin at “~62% – 64%,” and says whether that range is “framed as the floor matters.”

surprises.description: The quarter generated negative operating cash flow and free cash flow, despite the prior quarter’s positive $53 million of free cash flow. Management attributed the cash use to working-capital needs from branded weight loss and expects free cash flow to resume in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow turned negative $36 million and free cash flow was negative $68 million in the quarter due to working capital demands from branded weight loss, though the company expects to resume free cash flow generation in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reports “FCF $53.0M” for Q1 but gives no Q2 free-cash-flow expectation.

surprises.description: The reported GAAP loss included about $81 million of nonrecurring costs, including the Eucalyptus acquisition, restructuring, and FTC legal accruals. The preview warned that GAAP results would be well below adjusted results and flagged the possibility of an FTC reserve, but did not anticipate this stated level of charges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss was $86 million, impacted by approximately $81 million of nonrecurring costs including Eucalyptus acquisition, restructuring, and FTC legal accruals.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP will be well below” adjusted EPS; the FTC section says to “watch for any reserve.”

surprises.description: Management said it would vigorously defend the FTC case rather than accept terms it disagreed with. The preview identified the lawsuit and settlement-related issues as a key debate but did not specify this firm a defense posture.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FTC filed a complaint against the company on July 29 after settlement negotiations, and management stated it intends to defend the case vigorously rather than accept terms it disagreed with.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says to watch for “any reserve, consent-decree posture, or changes to the cancellation funnel.”

surprises.description: International revenue reached $131 million, more than 17 times the year-ago level; Eucalyptus contributed about $40 million, and the U.K., Australia, and Germany each exceeded $100 million in annualized revenue. The preview noted international growth and Eucalyptus’s acquisition, but did not anticipate these reported scale figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International revenue grew over 17-fold year-over-year to $131 million, with the newly acquired Eucalyptus contributing approximately $40 million and the U.K., Australia, and Germany each already exceeding $100 million in annualized revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says international revenue was “lifting the consolidated line” and notes “Eucalyptus from its June 2 close,” without giving an expectation for its contribution or the markets’ scale.

surprises.description: The company added substantial financing—a $400 million receivables facility and a convertible debt offering of more than $400 million—while ending with over $840 million in cash and short-term investments after the Eucalyptus payment. The preview did not flag this financing or balance-sheet move.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company shored up its balance sheet with a $400 million receivables facility and a $400 million+ convertible debt offering, ending the quarter with more than $840 million in cash and short-term investments after a $225 million Eucalyptus upfront payment.”

surprises.description: TRT was described as scaling faster than any specialty outside weight loss and on track to become the company’s sixth U.S. specialty with a $100 million annual run rate, with injectable and oral launches planned before year-end. The preview did not identify this as a growth driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Testosterone/TRT is scaling faster than any specialty outside weight loss and is expected to become the company's sixth U.S. specialty to reach a $100 million annual run rate, with injectable and oral TRT launches planned before year-end.”

surprises.description: Management reported sizable AI-related operating gains—33 times higher patient-care team messaging engagement and 50% fewer non-clinical support tasks—and said it expects AI investments to pay back within 12–18 months. The preview did not discuss these rollouts or their expected payback.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI-native rollouts drove 33x higher patient-care team messaging engagement and a 50% reduction in non-clinical support tasks, with management expecting AI investments to pay back within 12 to 18 months.”

in_line: Gross margin was 64%, within the preview’s expected 62%–64% range; the preview also anticipated further compression.
The FTC complaint itself was already known before the release: the preview states it was filed July 29.

surprises.description: PLBY reported Q2 revenue of $31.2 million, above the preview’s consensus range of $29.69 million to $30.29 million. The beat was about 3% over the higher estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew approximately 10.9% year over year to $31.2 million.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was approximately $7 million, comfortably above the preview’s buy-side bar of at least $5 million and its $5.0–$5.5 million base scenario. That result included over $700,000 of litigation expenses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled to approximately $7 million (22% margin) ... though it included over $700,000 of litigation expenses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buy-side bar cited as ≥ $5M”; base scenario: “$5.0–5.5M.”

surprises.description: Licensing revenue returned to growth, and revenue excluding Biborg was about $6.2 million—above the preview’s roughly $5.9 million stabilization threshold. The China transition still reduced the quarter’s licensing revenue by a couple hundred thousand dollars.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Licensing revenue rose about 2% to $11.2 million,” with “a couple-hundred-thousand-dollar quarterly step-down in China”; Biborg contributed “$5 million” at its contractual minimum.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs to show the licensing base is stabilizing; roughly $5.9M or better ex-Byborg supports the thesis.”

surprises.description: Honey Birdette delivered stronger comps than the preview’s double-digit threshold: comparable stores rose 15%, including 13% retail comps and 16% online, with every region positive. The preview’s bull case had called for comps of 12% or more.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total comparable stores up 15% (retail comps +13%, online +16%) and every region positive.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A seventh straight double-digit comp quarter keeps the growth story intact”; bull scenario: “HB comps +12%+.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a sizable share repurchase agreement not flagged in the preview: it will buy back nearly 15% of shares at $1.05, below both the $1.75 conversion price and the preview’s recent trading price. The below-market purchase price benefits remaining shareholders, while the roughly $17 million cash commitment makes the capital-allocation impact mixed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchase approximately 16.6 million shares (nearly 15% of shares outstanding) at a fixed price of $1.05 (roughly $17 million total), below the $1.75 conversion price and current trading level.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed over $320 million of contracted licensing revenue that has not yet been recognized, a future-revenue visibility figure the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over $320 million of contracted but not-yet-recognized future licensing revenue.”

surprises.description: The second paid-voting contest with Honey Birdette drew nearly 50,000 contestants and generated about 2.5 times the first contest’s revenue, with the economics expected to land in Q3. The preview did not flag this additional near-term revenue contributor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Its second paid-voting contest with Honey Birdette drew nearly 50,000 contestants generating about 2.5 times the revenue of the first, with those economics landing in Q3.”

surprises.description: The Playboy.com subscription completed its first full quarter with roughly 2 million unique visitors, July was its strongest month, and sponsorship revenue is expected to begin in Q3. This early audience and monetization update was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The newly launched Playboy.com subscription completed its first full quarter with roughly 2 million site unique visitors, July was its strongest month yet, and first sponsorship deals for content are expected to begin showing revenue in Q3.”

in_line: GAAP net income was approximately break-even, broadly matching the preview’s EPS consensus that rounded to zero.
Net debt was about $108 million, close to the preview’s roughly $110 million figure; the preview had also noted management’s aim of getting below $100 million.
Biborg contributed $5 million of digital licensing revenue at its contractual minimum, as the preview had described.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $87.3 million, about 15% below the preview’s roughly $103.2 million consensus estimate. It was still within the preview’s $78–92 million base-case scenario, so the miss was against the stated consensus rather than that scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $87.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue | ~$103.2M (likely stale)”

surprises.description: The first-half business was much weaker than the preview’s full-year growth forecast implied: revenue fell 28.8% and sales volume fell 24.3%, even though FY2026 revenue consensus called for growth. That raises the gap between the reported first-half trend and the annual outlook embedded in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Six-month revenue declined 28.8% (about $60 million), driven by a 24.3% sales volume drop from roughly 947 MWh to 717 MWh.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was only $3.6 million in Q2 and negative $1.9 million for the first half. The preview’s FY2026 EPS consensus was positive, so this weak adjusted earnings performance is a notable contrast, although it did not provide a quarterly EBITDA estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA collapsed to $3.6 million in Q2 2026 from $25.9 million in Q2 2025, and was negative $1.9 million for the first six months versus positive $54.4 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 EPS | $0.04 (was $0.06 earlier in the year)”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 29.5%, above the preview’s 24–28% base-case range and well above its 25% level of concern. It was just short of the preview’s 30% bull-case marker, but better than the central scenario suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 gross margin fell to 29.5% from 34.7% in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: … adj. GM 24–28%”; “Below ~25%, the resilient-margin case weakens”; “Bull: … adj. GM ≥30%.”

surprises.description: Q2 volume appears to have exceeded the preview’s recovery markers: first-half volume was 717 MWh and Q1 volume was 274 MWh, implying roughly 443 MWh in Q2. That is above the preview’s roughly 400 MWh recovery level and its 425 MWh bull-case threshold, even as first-half volume remained sharply lower year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Six-month revenue declined 28.8% … driven by a 24.3% sales volume drop from roughly 947 MWh to 717 MWh.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A recovery toward ~400 MWh supports the ‘delivery timing’ view”; “Bull … Volumes above 425 MWh.”

surprises.description: Cash generation deteriorated substantially: operating cash flow was negative $33.3 million for the first half, a $77.6 million swing from the prior-year period, and cash, equivalents and restricted cash declined by $26.2 million to $143.1 million. The preview flagged liquidity as a key debate but did not anticipate these reported amounts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow deteriorated to negative $33.3 million for the six months, a $77.6 million swing from the $44.3 million generated a year earlier”; “Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash fell by $26.2 million during the period, ending the quarter at $143.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Liquidity and going-concern language. Does the qualification persist, worsen, or clear?”

surprises.description: Regional performance diverged sharply: Europe grew 35% and rose to 61% of quarterly revenue, while APAC fell 23% in the quarter and 45% year to date amid demand shifting toward lower-cost products in India. The preview did not flag this geographic split.
surprises.fact_evidence: “European sales rose 35% in the quarter and now account for 61% of quarterly revenue (up from 43%), while APAC sales fell 23% in the quarter and 45% year-to-date amid a demand shift toward lower-cost products in India.”

surprises.description: A $2.7 million tariff refund issued to a customer was recorded as a revenue reduction, an unanticipated one-off factor that further lowered the reported Q2 revenue figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $87.3 million, down 4.5% year-over-year, partly reduced by a $2.7 million tariff refund issued to a customer and recorded as a revenue reduction.”

in_line: The preview expected the Huzhou Phase 3.2 startup in 2026; the company reported equipment installation and commissioning complete and production targeted for 2026.
Clarksville construction remained contingent on additional financing or strategic partnerships, as the preview had flagged; no named financing partner was reported in the facts.

surprises.description: The preview said an additional-information request or timeline shift would be the largest FDA swing factor. Management disclosed that FDA sent an additional-information letter in July and requires an SIR alignment meeting before the data package can be resubmitted, although the company still targets authorization later in 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Since the March FDA submission, the company roughly tripled its collected study samples and received an additional information letter in July, requiring an SIR alignment meeting before resubmitting its data package.” The company “continues to target FDA marketing authorization for GraftAssureDx later in 2026,” while noting review timing is not fully within its control.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any mention of an Additional Information request or a timeline shift is the largest swing factor”; the May baseline was “later in 2026, timing uncertain.”

surprises.description: Management raised expected second-half cash burn to about $8 million per quarter, rather than the roughly $6 million per quarter the preview said was expected. The increase reflects regulatory, registry, and commercial-launch costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its second-half cash burn guidance to approximately $8 million per quarter, up from a prior expectation of roughly $6 million per quarter, due to regulatory, registry, and commercial launch costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “H2 burn back toward ~$6M per quarter.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted first U.S. GraftAssureIQ orders and conversion of coverage into purchase orders as a key commercial milestone. Instead, reported kit sales were just $21,000 for the quarter, entirely from ex-U.S. clinical usage, with no U.S. orders reported.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Research use-only kit sales totaled just $21,000 in the quarter, driven entirely by ex-U.S. clinical usage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “First U.S. GraftAssureIQ orders” was a key metric to watch; “Conversion from coverage to purchase orders drives the 2027 consensus ramp.”

surprises.description: Management newly quantified the kidney-testing opportunity at a $2 billion total addressable market, based on two tests per year per kidney patient, and said the opportunity grows with more frequent surveillance, therapy monitoring, and additional organ indications. The preview did not provide a comparable market-size estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company estimates a $2 billion total addressable market based on a conservative 2 tests per year per kidney patient, which grows further with higher surveillance frequency, therapy monitoring, and expanded organ indications.”

surprises.description: Management gave additional favorable commercial-positioning claims not covered in the preview: it believes its kitted product is about two years ahead of competitors and is engaged with more than half of the top 10 U.S. transplant centers, with substantial overlap between FDA study and registry sites.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management believes it is roughly 2 years ahead of competitors in kitted product development and is engaged with over half of the top 10 U.S. transplant centers, with about 50% of FDA study sites overlapping as registry sites.”

in_line: Q2 cash burn was $10 million, consistent with the preview's expectation of burn above $9 million; management described it as the high watermark for the foreseeable future, matching the preview's expectation that Q2 would be the peak.
The company maintained its target of FDA marketing authorization later in 2026, consistent with the preview's stated baseline, despite the newly disclosed additional-information process.
The call cited the expanded MolDX kidney-transplant surveillance coverage and the $2,753 reimbursement rate for GraftAssureCore, both of which the preview had already flagged.

surprises.description: PAL agreed to buy Hansen & Adkins for a $130 million enterprise value, a major acquisition not anticipated in the preview. HNA brings over $400 million of revenue and more than $27 million of EBITDA; the combined company is expected to exceed $800 million of revenue, become North America’s largest auto hauler, and enter Canada.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company agreed to acquire Hansen & Adkins at an enterprise value of $130 million”; HNA generated “over $400 million in revenue and more than $27 million in EBITDA”; the combined entity will have “over $800 million in revenue” and become “the largest auto hauler in North America,” with Canada as a new market.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said M&A language was something to watch, but did not anticipate a specific acquisition: “Buyback pace and M&A language.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was materially below the preview’s implied range and the previously stated margin guide: $7.6 million versus roughly $9.5–10.5 million implied and an expected 8–10% margin. Management attributed the pressure to higher fuel and driver costs incurred ahead of customer payment cycles, rather than the expected Q2 reversal of the prior-quarter fuel-surcharge timing hit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell to $7.6 million in Q2 2026 from $11.3 million,” pressured by “higher fuel and driver costs incurred ahead of customer payment cycles.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said adjusted EBITDA was “~$9.5–10.5M implied from guidance” and cited company guidance for an “8–10% adjusted EBITDA margin.” It also said the Q1 fuel-surcharge hit was “expected to reverse in Q2.”

surprises.description: The standalone Q3 revenue outlook was softer than the preview’s expectation: management expects revenue to be flattish versus Q2, rather than at least $110 million. Management did expect improved profitability, consistent with the preview’s focus on a lower Q3 operating ratio.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects Q3 standalone revenue flattish versus Q2 with improved profitability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buy-side expects at least $110M revenue and an adjusted OR below 96%.”

surprises.description: The acquisition financing adds substantial debt and convertible-bond exposure: the plan includes a $75 million seven-year convertible bond and an equipment facility with roughly $100 million expected outstanding at closing. The capped call is intended to reduce dilution, but the preview had not anticipated this financing or PAL’s reported 2.1x current leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt stood at $62.3 million at quarter-end for a 2.1x leverage ratio”; the deal is being financed with a “$75 million 7-year convertible bond” and an equipment facility with “~$100 million balance at closing,” alongside “a capped call to reduce dilution.”

surprises.description: June’s monthly operating ratio reached 95.7%, the best month of the calendar year, a favorable late-quarter data point versus the preview’s Q2 expectation near 96.7%. This is a monthly figure, not a reported full-quarter adjusted OR.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Monthly operating ratios improved sequentially through Q2, ending with June at 95.7%, the best month of the calendar year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had guided to an adjusted OR “similar to” Q2’25’s 96.7%.

surprises.description: Revenue was above the preview’s primary consensus estimate but below its alternative estimate, making the top-line result mixed rather than an unambiguous beat. The $109.4 million result was also within the company’s previously stated $105–110 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total operating revenue was $109.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “$106.78M” consensus and “Alt. revenue consensus $111.63M,” alongside company guidance of “$105–110M revenue.”

surprises.description: Units fell 8% year over year, just missing the preview’s less-than-7% decline marker for evidence of share gains. The actual 580,962 units were nevertheless within the preview’s implied 575,000–620,000 range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Units delivered down 8% to 580,962.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management guidance implied “roughly 575–620k” units and that “Down less than ~7% YoY would indicate share gains.”

in_line: Revenue per unit rose 2.9%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that flat-to-up year-over-year pricing would support the pricing-turn narrative.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $320.1 million, below the company’s $330–$360 million guidance range and the preview’s cited consensus of about $348.7 million. The shortfall was larger than the preview’s base case, which expected $342–$355 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was approximately $320.1 million,” including “a roughly 1% ($4 million) foreign currency headwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Company guidance (Q2) | $330M – $360M | Consensus (varies by source) | ~$348.7M” and the base scenario expected “$342M–$355M.”

surprises.description: The FY26 revenue range was cut to $1.28–$1.35 billion, below the prior $1.35 billion floor. The preview expected a trim, but said a cut below $1.35 billion was not priced in.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cut full-year revenue guidance to $1.28-$1.35 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 revenue guidance of “$1.35B – $1.50B,” said a trim within the range was largely expected, and noted: “A cut below $1.35B is not priced in.”

surprises.description: FY26 adjusted EPS guidance fell to $0.70–$0.90, putting the low end below the previous $0.80 floor. The preview’s expected trimmed range was $0.80–$1.00.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cut… adjusted EPS to $0.70-$0.90.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior FY26 adjusted EPS guidance was “$0.80 – $1.20,” and the preview’s base scenario expected “adj. EPS cut to $0.80–$1.00.”

surprises.description: Reported EPS was a loss of $5.14, and reported full-year EPS is now guided to a loss of $4.90–$4.73, rather than the prior positive GAAP guidance. The preview did not anticipate the large non-cash charges behind the change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported EPS was negative $5.14,” driven by a “$78.9 million non-cash goodwill impairment” and a “$167.5 million non-cash deferred tax valuation allowance”; reported EPS is guided to “negative $4.90 to negative $4.73.” Adjusted EPS was positive $0.20.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior FY26 GAAP EPS guide was “$0.70 – $1.10.”

surprises.description: Nu Skin pushed India’s formal launch from the previously guided year-end 2026 timing to the first half of 2027. The preview mentioned a 2027 delay only in its bear scenario, not as its base expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “India's formal market launch has been delayed to the first half of 2027 to further refine the business model and operational readiness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said India’s formal launch “is guided to year-end 2026”; its bear scenario identified timing “pushed to 2027.”

surprises.description: Prism device placements and scans showed stronger reported momentum than the preview’s prior adoption datapoint suggested: placements rose nearly 30% quarter over quarter and scans rose 25%. The preview had noted Q1 subscription volume growth of 5%, although placements and subscriptions are different measures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Prism.io device placements reached over 39,000, up nearly 30% quarter-over-quarter, with 2.5 million scans up 25%,” and the company targets 50,000–60,000 devices by year-end.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Q1 subscription volume grew 5%” and listed Prysm iO subscription volume as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: Adjusted operating margin improved to 6.1% from 3.6% in Q1, a notable sequential recovery on the metric the preview highlighted. It remained below the prior-year 8% level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin [was] 6.1% from 8% in the prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “Adj. operating margin vs. 3.6% in Q1” and asked whether management would pull cost actions forward.

surprises.description: Management said recruiting and leadership development remain insufficient for a return to sustainable growth, adding a personnel and execution concern beyond the customer-count debate highlighted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management flagged that recruiting and leadership development remain below the levels needed to return the business to sustainable growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified customer count and its rate of change as the most important issue, but did not flag recruiting or leadership development as a concern.

surprises.description: The company disclosed an East-West operating-model transition expected to generate meaningful savings starting in the second half of 2026, alongside $5–$10 million of transition costs this year. The preview raised the question of whether cost actions would be pulled forward but did not anticipate this specific program or its costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is transitioning to an East-West operating model expected to generate meaningful cost savings starting in the second half of 2026, with $5-$10 million in transition costs anticipated this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether “management pulls cost actions forward” but did not describe an East-West operating model or transition costs.

in_line: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.20, in line with the preview’s cited $0.20 consensus and within the company’s $0.15–$0.25 guidance range.
The company paid $2.9 million in dividends during the quarter, consistent with the preview’s base case that the dividend would be maintained.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $100.7 million, about $1.3 million below the preview’s own $102 million build. That was a small shortfall; the preview noted that no reliable published Q2 revenue consensus was available.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 33% year-over-year to $100.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My $102M Q2 revenue figure is my own build from legacy growth plus one month of KUBRA. It is not a published consensus.”

surprises.description: Organic growth was about 6% including roughly 2 points from political media, or about 4% excluding it. That leaves underlying growth roughly flat with Q1’s 4% legacy growth, rather than the sharp acceleration the preview said was needed to reach the 9–11% full-year legacy growth implied by guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 6% organic growth including about 2 points from political media contributions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The FY26 legacy guide of $340–346M implies roughly 9–11% growth”; “Q1 delivered +4%, so the back half has to accelerate sharply.”

surprises.description: Business Payments growth accelerated to 19% normalized, up from Q1’s 16% normalized growth. The increase was positive, although reported growth of 32% included political-media contributions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Business payments revenue accelerated to 32% reported growth (19% normalized excluding political media).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Business Payments grew +18% reported and +16% normalized” in Q1.

surprises.description: Q2 free-cash-flow conversion was very strong at 75% (81% on an adjusted basis), well above the preview’s cited 30% FY26 conversion guidance. The comparison is between a quarterly result and a full-year guide, but Q2 conversion materially exceeded the level the preview highlighted as a concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was $27.4 million (75% conversion), up 21% year-over-year, with adjusted free cash flow conversion of 81%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance was cut from 45% to 30% for FY26. Watch Q2 conversion.”

in_line: Adjusted EPS was $0.20, matching the preview’s $0.20 consensus estimate.
FY26 revenue guidance of $490–500 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $168.5–176 million were reaffirmed, as the preview’s key watch item anticipated.

Margins were lower with KUBRA’s mix, as expected: adjusted EBITDA margin was about 36% versus the preview’s expectation that blended margin would fall toward 37% because KUBRA has lower margins. Management attributed the decline almost entirely to mix, not pricing or competitive pressure.
The company reported over $4.5 million of annualized run-rate cost synergies exiting Q2 and reiterated a target of over $8 million by year-end, consistent with the preview’s synergy watch item.
Management said organic growth should accelerate into double digits by year-end, consistent with the preview’s expectation that growth would need to accelerate in the back half.

surprises.description: Kopin had been expected to reiterate or narrow its $52–60 million FY2026 revenue guidance, but management now says second-half results should exceed that prior full-year range. This is a substantially more bullish outlook than the preview’s concern that the H2 ramp would be difficult to deliver.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “now anticipates second-half results exceeding prior full-year guidance of $52-60 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance action. Reiterate at $52–60M, narrow, or cut. A narrowing to the low end ($52–55M) is the most likely honest outcome”; the preview also said H2 would need to produce $29–37M.

surprises.description: The preview expected Sentinel volume production to begin in late August after DDP evaluations and awards; the call instead put volume orders in late Q4 2026, with additional opportunity in 2027. The timing is later than expected, although the tens-of-millions opportunity and possible doubling with Gauntlet 2 awards add upside potential.
surprises.fact_evidence: Sentinel secured “multiple prototype orders”; “volume orders [are] expected to begin in late Q4 2026,” and the 2027 opportunity is “in the tens of millions of dollars,” potentially doubling depending on Gauntlet 2 awards.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had said “volume production begins ‘in late August, immediately following DDP Phase 2 evaluations and awards.’”

surprises.description: The preview cited a 2027 Neural I/O revenue expectation of $25–50 million, while the call described $20–30 million of possible 2027 development revenue and said production revenue is not expected until 2028. That points to a lower 2027 development-revenue range and a later start for production revenue than investors had been led to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Fabric.AI collaboration has a “$15 million initial development order”; “development revenue of $20-30 million [is] possible in 2027,” but “production revenue [is] not expected until 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided to “at least $15M of Neural I/O revenue in 2026, rising to $25–50M in 2027.”

surprises.description: Kopin reported net income and break-even EPS rather than the small loss expected, but the positive result depended on investment gains and a tax benefit rather than operating profitability. The headline was better than expected, with a notable one-off contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net income was “$0.9 million ($0.00 per share)” versus a $5.2 million year-ago loss; results were aided by “~$2.3 million of investment gains and a $2.1 million income tax benefit from an expired statute of limitations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 FY26 EPS consensus was “–$0.01.”

surprises.description: Product revenue was about $7.6 million, modestly above the roughly $7 million level the preview said was needed to support the H2 ramp. This was a small positive relative to the watched threshold, rather than a major beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: Total revenue was $12.7 million and non-product revenue was $5.1 million, implying product revenue of about $7.6 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Product revenue vs. ~$7M” as the key metric and said that amount was needed to make the H2 ramp arithmetic plausible.

surprises.description: Product gross margin moved into positive territory at 14%, a sharp improvement from the prior quarter’s product costs exceeding product revenue. The preview highlighted negative product gross margin as a key risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Product gross margin improved to 14% (cost of product revenue fell to 86% of sales from 94%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Product cost of revenue ran 103% of product revenue” in Q1 and described the company as having “negative product gross margin.”

surprises.description: Management added a near-term profitability and cash-flow milestone that the preview had not anticipated: GAAP profitability and positive free cash flow are now expected in Q4 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expects to begin generating GAAP profitability and positive free cash flow in Q4 2026.”

surprises.description: Kopin reported a substantial technical milestone for its color microLED program, clearing the IBAS brightness threshold and targeting product manufacturing in mid-2027. The preview mentioned the government award but did not flag this achievement or manufacturing timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: The color microLED program achieved “over 150,000 nits of single-panel full-color brightness,” “exceeding the IBAS program threshold,” and targets transition to product manufacturing in mid-2027.

surprises.description: The call gave a new, ambitious longer-term commercial outlook: more than $45 million of orders received year-to-date and a $100 million revenue target for 2028. The preview discussed the $21.5 million thermal contract and asked for quantified backlog, but did not provide an expectation for this order total or revenue target.
surprises.fact_evidence: Kopin “has received over $45 million in orders in 2026 year-to-date, including a $21.5 million follow-on thermal imaging contract,” and management is “targeting $100 million in revenue for 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch for a dollar backlog figure” and noted the $21.5 million thermal imaging follow-on contract.

surprises.description: Management said bringing OLED deposition in-house in early 2027 is expected to add at least 15 percentage points of gross margin. The preview focused on current negative product margins but did not flag this future margin contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: Bringing OLED deposition in-house in early 2027 is “expected to add at least 15 points of gross margin.”

in_line: Total Q2 revenue of $12.7 million was close to the preview’s roughly $12 million consensus and within its stated $11.5–13.8 million vendor range.

surprises.description: Q1 revenue was $80.8 million, about $5.8 million above the $75.05 million consensus and above the company’s $75 million guidance midpoint, rather than landing near the expected level.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q1 FY2027 revenue was $80.8 million, exceeding guidance of $75 million (+/- $2 million).
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue guidance was $75.0M ± $2M; consensus was $75.05M.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $8 million, far above the $1.5 million guidance midpoint and $5.5 million above even the high end of guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA was a positive $8 million, $5.5 million above the high end of guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adj. EBITDA guidance was $1.5M ± $1M.

surprises.description: Instead of the expected non-GAAP loss, Quantum reported its first positive non-GAAP adjusted net income since 2023: $4 million, or $0.18 per share, versus the preview’s consensus loss estimate of $0.17 per share.
surprises.fact_evidence: Non-GAAP net income was $4 million ($0.18 per share), the first positive non-GAAP adjusted net income since 2023, versus a $14.5 million loss a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Non-GAAP EPS consensus was ($0.17) (MarketBeat); another estimate was ($0.14).

surprises.description: Q2 revenue guidance was raised to about $82 million at the midpoint, above the preview’s roughly $78 million reference point.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 FY2027 revenue guidance is approximately $82 million (+/- $2 million), representing ~31% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview assessed Q2 guidance against ~$78M and said a guide below about $78M would put the FY number at risk; its base scenario was $78–81M.

surprises.description: Despite the stronger Q2 revenue outlook, adjusted EBITDA is guided down to $6 million, with higher R&D hiring and sales commissions weighing on profitability; the preview had described FY27 opex as flat year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA is guided down to $6 million due to higher R&D hiring and sales commissions.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Opex flat YoY” for FY2027.

surprises.description: The reported GAAP loss was an unusually large $155.3 million, driven by one-time non-cash debt-related charges, including a $129.7 million fair-value loss on convertible notes; the preview focused on non-GAAP estimates and did not anticipate this charge.
surprises.fact_evidence: GAAP net loss was $155.3 million ($7.06 per share), driven by $157.7 million in one-time non-cash debt-related charges including a $129.7 million loss on convertible note fair value change.

surprises.description: Backlog was significantly higher than the prior quarter’s $45 million even though revenue beat expectations, rather than converting into revenue and falling; this points to shipments remaining constrained.
surprises.fact_evidence: Growth was broad-based alongside a significantly higher backlog (prior quarter was $45 million).
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A revenue beat with backlog falling is the best case. Revenue in line with backlog rising means shipments are still constrained.”

surprises.description: Tape-drive supply showed no near-term inflection by August, despite IBM’s projected production increases for the second half of the year, tempering the preview’s expectation that supply would improve later in FY2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: Tape drive supply constraints remain the primary limiter on revenue, with no inflection point seen as of August despite IBM's projected production increases in the back half of the year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: CFO White guided tape-drive supply to improve “later in fiscal 2027.”

surprises.description: The call reported broad-based sequential growth across geographies and services—Americas revenue over 20%, APAC over 50%, and service revenue about 10%—a positive detail the preview did not quantify or forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: Americas revenue was up over 20% sequentially, APAC up over 50%, and service revenue up ~10%.

in_line: GAAP gross margin of 39.3% was within the preview’s expected 38–40% range and close to the company’s stated direction of gross margin “toward 40%.”

surprises.description: Rocket Lab’s Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was 41.5%, above the preview’s 38–40% expectation; GAAP gross margin also exceeded its expected range. The margin beat was helped by a nonrecurring tariff refund, partly offset by an inventory reserve.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP gross margin of 41.5% and GAAP gross margin of 36.1% both exceeded guidance, aided by a nonrecurring tariff refund offset by an inventory reserve on the new light launch vehicle.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin: 38–40%”; “GAAP gross margin: 33–35%.”

surprises.description: The Q3 revenue outlook had a $257.5 million midpoint, above the roughly $245 million implied by FY26 consensus. However, the $250 million low end falls short of the preview’s $255 million threshold for a meaningful beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $250-265 million (10% sequential growth at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 consensus of ~$924M implies roughly $245M per quarter in H2”; “Management’s Q3 guide of $255M or more would be a meaningful beat.”

surprises.description: Rocket Lab disclosed a pending Iridium acquisition that would add a 66-satellite constellation, 2.5 million subscribers, and roughly $870 million in annual revenue, with management saying it provides significant free cash flow. The preview did not anticipate this transaction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pending Iridium acquisition, expected to close mid-2027, adds a 66-satellite constellation with 2.5 million subscribers and roughly $870 million in annual revenue, providing significant free cash flow.”

surprises.description: Q2 ended with $2.36 billion of backlog, above the preview’s roughly $2.2 billion expectation, and Rocket Lab reported more than $1 billion in new contracts across Q2 and post-quarter. The preview anticipated key post-quarter awards, but not this reported combined contract total.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rocket Lab ended Q2 with $2.36 billion total backlog”; “The company signed over $1 billion in new contracts across launch and Space Systems during Q2 and post-quarter, including a record $266 million Space Force contract.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Backlog: Not guided; ~$2.2B”; “Q2 ended before the $266M RSLP award … and the $397M SB-AMTI Flatellite award … so both should show up in Q3 backlog.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow use worsened to $110.1 million from $77.4 million in Q1, and management said cash flow positivity is expected only 18–24 months after Neutron’s first successful launch. The preview did not give a free-cash-flow forecast, although it highlighted the path to breakeven as a point to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow deteriorated to a use of $110.1 million in Q2 (from $77.4 million in Q1)”; “cash flow positivity expected 18-24 months after Neutron's first successful launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Commentary on the path to breakeven would be a new positive datapoint.”

surprises.description: Rocket Lab raised $1.08 billion through its ATM program and ended Q2 with roughly $2.4 billion in cash, then terminated the program. The added funding supports growth and M&A, but the equity issuance also means dilution that the preview had not anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised $1.08 billion through its now-terminated at-the-market equity program, ending Q2 with roughly $2.4 billion in cash and equivalents to fund M&A and growth initiatives.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 cash of “$1.48B (about $2.0B total liquidity)” but did not anticipate a Q2 ATM raise.

surprises.description: Although Q3 revenue is guided higher, its gross margins are forecast below Q2’s reported level because of unfavorable Space Systems mix. The preview did not provide a Q3 margin forecast, so this is a new margin headwind rather than a miss against a stated Q3 estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for … GAAP 29-31%, non-GAAP 35-37% due to unfavorable Space Systems mix.”

surprises.description: Neutron remains on track for delivery to the pad in Q4, but management said the year-end launch window is narrowing. That is less reassuring than a straightforward Q4 schedule reaffirmation, though no delay was announced.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Neutron production remains on track for delivery to the pad in Q4 2026, though management acknowledged the year-end launch window is narrowing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether management “reaffirms Q4 or hedges,” and described the base case as “Neutron ‘Q4, tracking.’”

surprises.description: Management said Neutron is being sold at a $50–55 million average selling price without significant early discounting, and saw more upside than downside to launch pricing in a supply-constrained market. The preview did not discuss expected Neutron pricing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Neutron is being sold at a $50-55 million ASP with no significant early discounting, and management sees more upside than downside to launch pricing given a supply-constrained market.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $234 million was a small beat against the roughly $232 million consensus, though it remained within Rocket Lab’s prior guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q2 2026 revenue of $234 million … landing within prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … $231.6M (Zacks) / ~$232M (LSEG).”

in_line: Q2 revenue remained within the prior company guidance range of $225–240 million.

Neutron’s Q4 pad-delivery target remained on track, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a Q4 schedule reaffirmation, although management cautioned that the year-end launch window is narrowing.
Q3 revenue guidance began with a 2, consistent with the preview’s base-case range of $250–260 million, even though the midpoint was above the roughly $245 million implied by FY26 consensus.

surprises.description: Bakkt reported diluted EPS of $1.94, far above the preview’s +$0.03 consensus, but the gain was largely driven by a Transchem warrant fair-value remeasurement rather than operating performance. The headline beat was therefore much larger than the operating result implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 GAAP net income of $80.8 million with diluted EPS of $1.94,” largely driven by “the Transchem warrant fair value re-measurement rather than operating performance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS | +$0.03” consensus; the preview also cautioned that “Any positive EPS would likely come from non-cash mark-to-market gains.”

surprises.description: Q2 TTV was about $169 million, far below the preview’s $350–550 million base scenario and its warning that anything below about $400 million would make the $2.5 billion year-end target hard to reach. Bakkt left that annual target unchanged, although the first-half total of about $410 million means it now needs roughly $2.1 billion in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Second quarter total transacting volume (TTV) was approximately $169 million, with first-half TTV of approximately $410 million,” requiring “roughly $2.1 billion in the second half to hit its unchanged full-year target of ~$2.5 billion.” Q2 TTV fell primarily due to lower trading activity, partly offset by payments newly entering TTV after the May 1 integration.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Q2 TTV below about $400M would make the year-end target hard to reach”; the base scenario expected “TTV $350–550M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected a Q3 Bakkt Agent launch with an initial MAU disclosure, but the call reported zero current meaningful activity and set a target of about 25,000 monthly active users only by year-end. That leaves the expected launch and user traction unconfirmed at this point.
surprises.fact_evidence: Bakkt set “an initial target of approximately 25,000 monthly active users for Bakkt Agent by year-end (a year-end target, not an annual average),” while “currently reporting zero as products lack meaningful activity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had targeted “a Bakkt Agent launch in Q3 2026 with first MAU disclosure”; the preview said a “slip past Q3, or a launch without MAU data, would be a credibility problem.”

surprises.description: Management introduced a Q4 2026 adjusted EBITDA break-even goal, a more specific profitability milestone than the preview had to work with, though it depends on the timing and scale of client activations.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expects to reach adjusted EBITDA break-even at some point during the fourth quarter of 2026, contingent on the timing and scale of client activations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance: none.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged net revenue and take rate as key metrics to assess, but management declined to provide a blended take rate, leaving that comparison unresolved.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “declined to provide 2027 financial guidance or a blended take rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue and take rate. About $3.6M in Q1. Watch whether it grows faster or slower than TTV.”

surprises.description: TCMD reported diluted EPS of $0.34, well above the preview’s $0.14 consensus estimate. The gap was substantial even though quarterly revenue was near consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income increased 142% to $7.8 million, or $0.34 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP) … $0.14, 3 estimates, range $0.11–$0.18.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $11.4 million, above the preview’s derived estimate of roughly $9–10 million. This was a clear operating-profitability beat beyond the revenue result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 49% to $11.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … Not published; my estimate ~$9–10M.”

surprises.description: TCMD lowered the top of its full-year revenue range by $2 million, from $368 million to $366 million, rather than reaffirming the prior range as the preview considered the base case. The company attributed the change to a more conservative airway-clearance outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered the top end of full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $360–$366 million (9–11% growth), driven by a more conservative airway clearance outlook now expected to be roughly flat year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue guide ($360–368M). Reaffirmation is the base case.”

surprises.description: The prior-authorization process did affect Q2 Medicare lymphedema sales: some orders shifted into Q3, contributing to a Medicare revenue decline. The preview highlighted approval and turnaround risks, but its base case characterized prior authorization as a non-event; TCMD said the timing disruption should normalize.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The April 13th Medicare Prior Authorization requirement pushed some Medicare lymphedema orders from Q2 into Q3, contributing to a Medicare revenue decline in the quarter but expected to normalize.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bull … Prior auth a non-event”; the preview also identified “Medicare prior-authorization approval rates and turnaround times” as the top issue to watch.

surprises.description: Although the preview flagged possible DME-partner order deferrals around the next-generation AffloVest launch, TCMD described the current decline as temporary destocking at a few large partners and expected normalization in Q4. It also said AfloVest remained up 32% on a trailing-12-month basis, tempering the concern about sustained weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AfloVest's decline was attributed to temporary inventory destocking among a few of the largest DME partners tied to the next-generation system launch, with normalization expected in Q4; on a trailing-12-month basis AfloVest is still up 32% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Airway faces a tough comp after +51.6% last year, and the next-gen AffloVest launch in winter 2026–27 could cause DME partners to defer orders.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $85.7 million was within the preview’s conflicting consensus estimates of $85.5 million and $87.2 million.
Gross margin of 76.3% was within the preview’s approximate 76–77% expectation.
Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance remained at approximately $49–$51 million, as the preview expected the range to be maintained.
The airway business faced the flagged tough comparison and partner-deferral risk; TCMD reported airway-clearance revenue down 7% year over year.

surprises.description: Upwork cut FY2026 revenue guidance from $760–790 million to $730–750 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance from $250–260 million to $225–235 million. The new 31% midpoint margin, alongside Q3 guidance for a 29% margin, also falls short of the preview’s H2 expectation of at least 35%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Upwork cut its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $730-750 million and adjusted EBITDA to $225-235 million (31% margin at midpoint)”; Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance is “$50-54 million (29% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance… Revenue $760–790M; Adj. EBITDA $250–260M”; “H2 adjusted EBITDA margin ≥35%.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $64.1 million, well above both the $56–59 million company guide and the roughly $57–58 million consensus; the 33.4% margin also exceeded the expected 30–31% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $64.1 million and a 33.4% adjusted EBITDA margin, exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA” guidance of “$56–59M” and consensus of “~$57–58M”; expected margin “30–31%” and consensus “~30%.”

surprises.description: Active clients fell to 763,000 from the prior quarter’s 784,000, rather than stabilizing sequentially. The preview had flagged stabilization as important, even while allowing for a year-over-year decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Active client count fell to 763,000 under pressure from AI automation, SEO changes, and a subdued labor market.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Active clients vs. ~784K. Sequential stabilization matters more than the YoY print”; the base scenario expected “clients still down 3–5% YoY.”

surprises.description: GSV was $966 million, just below the preview’s $970 million low-end estimate, and management said low-value, highly automatable work was eroding faster than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GSV declined to $966 million as low-value, highly-automatable work eroded faster than expected.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: GSV consensus was “~$0.97–1.00B.”

surprises.description: AI-related jobs grew 22% year over year, slowing substantially from the 40% growth cited in the preview, although the approximately $330 million annualized run rate was above the preview’s $300 million threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GSV from AI-related jobs grew 22% year over year to an approximately $330 million annualized run rate, decelerating from 40% growth the prior quarter and 50% two quarters ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had put AI-related work “above $300M annualized, +40% YoY.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $191.7 million was within the preview’s roughly $190 million consensus and company guidance of $187–193 million, consistent with the preview’s base-case range of $189–192 million.
GSV per active client rose 5% year over year, supporting the preview’s “fewer, bigger projects” thesis as client count fell.

The restructuring savings outlook was as expected: the preview cited about $70 million in annualized savings and about $40 million in 2026, matching the reported annualized reductions and expected fiscal 2026 savings.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $29.5 million, at the high end of company guidance and slightly above the preview’s roughly $29.3 million consensus estimate. The beat was narrow rather than a result above the guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenue was $29.5 million, at the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Street consensus ~$29.3M”; company guidance was “$27.0M – $30.0M.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $35.5–37.5 million is below the preview’s implied $37–42 million per quarter for the second half. With FY26 guidance still reaffirmed, this leaves more of the expected revenue ramp to Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $35.5-37.5 million”; management “reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $128-138 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “That leaves an implied 2H26 of $74–84M, or $37–42M per quarter.”

surprises.description: Management reported an enterprise SurfOS pipeline potentially worth tens of millions annually, although no additional enterprise contract was announced. That is more potential scale than the preview could identify in the known software contributors, which it said did not clearly bridge the revenue gap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management describes an enterprise SurfOS pipeline potentially worth tens of millions annually” and “targets at least one additional enterprise contract by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The known contributors (Wheels Up BrokerOS, up to ~$12.2M over three years, plus BrokerOS take-rate revenue and early OperatorOS launch) do not clearly bridge the gap.”

surprises.description: The financing update included a further $14 million asset-backed loan tranche expected during the month, which was not included in the preview’s description of the funding stack. This adds a prospective source of working capital, though it is not yet described as funded.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company secured a new $21.6 million asset-backed loan for working capital, with a second $14 million tranche expected this month.”

in_line: FY26 revenue guidance of $128–138 million and adjusted EBITDA loss guidance of $25–30 million were reaffirmed, as the preview expected.
Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss of $10.5 million was within the guided $8.5–10.5 million loss range, although at the high-loss end.
Surf On Demand remained strong: the preview expected strong charter growth and highlighted it as the clearest growth line.
The Wheels Up enterprise deal was already known to the preview; its expected value was described there as up to about $12.2 million over three years.
Scheduled-service revenue continued to decline following deliberate exits from unprofitable routes, which the preview anticipated.
The NYSE deficiency and shareholder authorization for a reverse split were already flagged; the facts report no split implementation or cure plan that changes that setup.

surprises.description: The preview expected Q3 constant-currency growth below about 5% to make the acceleration thesis harder, but the guide is only 0.7%–3.3%. The $358–$368 million revenue range is above the preview’s roughly $355 million consensus in dollars, while the underlying growth rate is weaker than its stated threshold; adjusted EBITDA is guided to just $0–$5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for constant currency revenue growth of just 0.7% to 3.3% ($358–$368 million) and adjusted EBITDA of only $0 to $5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything implying less than +5% constant currency weakens the acceleration thesis”; “Q3 revenue guide against about $355M consensus.”

surprises.description: The preview expected Japan to improve from Q1’s -3.4% constant-currency decline, ideally to flat or better. Instead, Japan revenue fell 6.7% constant currency and MPUs fell 9.5%, making the weak spot worse rather than better.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Japan revenue declined 6.7% on a constant currency basis with MPU down 9.5% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Japan improving to flat or better in constant currency is the cleanest proof point”; “It needs to beat Q1’s -3.4%.”

surprises.description: The preview modeled advertising down 4.8% year over year, but advertising grew 11.5% constant currency, with rest-of-world ad revenue growing more than 20% constant currency. This was a clear reversal from the expected contraction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Advertising was a bright spot with 11.5% constant currency growth, including rest-of-world ad revenue growing over 20% on a constant currency basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Advertising re-acceleration. Consensus models -4.8% Y/Y, a low bar.”

surprises.description: Reported revenue was essentially in line with the preview’s consensus, but constant-currency growth of 5.2% exceeded the company’s May guide range, whose upper end was 4.6%. The stronger underlying growth was partly obscured by the reported year-over-year decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $338.5 million, declining 2.8% year-over-year on a reported basis but growing 5.2% on a constant currency basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue, constant currency” company guide: “+1.7% to +4.6%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA exceeded both the preview’s $2–$3 million consensus and the $5 million top end of the Q2 company guide, coming in at $5.5 million. However, it remained below the preview’s bull-case threshold of $6 million, and management attributed lower year-over-year margin to increased marketing investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA came in at $5.5 million, exceeding the high end of guidance but down from $9.7 million a year prior, with margin compressing to 1.6% from 2.8% due to increased marketing investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA about $2–3M”; company guide “$0.0–5.0M”; bull scenario “EBITDA at least $6M.”

surprises.description: The preview described the double-digit-growth goal as a target by the end of 2026; management reaffirmed it but clarified that it means a run-rate exiting Q4, not double-digit growth for the full quarter. The commitment remains, but the clarification makes the stated milestone narrower than a full-quarter reading might imply.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed its expectation to return to double-digit revenue growth by exiting Q4 2026, clarifying this is a run-rate target rather than full-quarter guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management target: double-digit revenue growth by end of 2026”; “Watch for hedged or dropped language.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag Korea as a specific catalyst, but the reported results show unusually broad strength there: revenue grew 20% constant currency, alongside growth in MAUs, MPUs, and ARPU. This is a positive market-level development not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Korea was the standout market with 20% constant currency revenue growth, 5.9% MAU growth, 10.4% MPU growth, and 14.8% ARPU growth year-over-year.”

surprises.description: The preview focused on platform-based growth and did not anticipate two moves into off-platform IP ownership: taking a 60% stake in RI Games Holdings and co-establishing a $100 million IP Adaptation Fund with Naver. The strategic expansion is notable, though the provided facts do not establish its financial effect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company made two strategic pivots into off-platform IP ownership: a 60% ownership stake in RI Games Holdings (across two closings) and a $100 million IP Adaptation Fund co-established with Naver.”

in_line: Reported Q2 revenue of $338.5 million was close to the preview’s roughly $338.8–$339.9 million consensus range and its expected year-over-year decline.
Gross margin reached 26%, matching the preview’s stated 26%-or-higher level that it identified as a positive outcome.

surprises.description: RUM’s Q2 revenue was $40.4 million, about 32% above the preview’s roughly $30.7 million consensus estimate. The preview’s bull case started at $38 million, so the reported figure also exceeded that scenario threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 61% year-over-year to $40.4 million” and set “an all-time company record.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue | ~$30.7M implied (+22.2% YoY off $25.1M)”

surprises.description: The first formal revenue guide was for Q3, at $87–93 million—more than twice Q2 revenue—rather than the FY2026 revenue and EBITDA range the preview identified as the main guidance catalyst. The Q3 range points to a much faster near-term revenue pace than the preview’s roughly $239.6 million FY2026 consensus, although the call facts provide no full-year guide to compare directly.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company issued its first-ever formal revenue guidance, projecting Q3 2026 revenue of $87 million to $93 million, more than doubling the current quarter as Quake AI is fully consolidated.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A credible FY26 revenue and EBITDA range is the highest-variance item of the print”; the preview listed FY2026 revenue consensus of “$239.6M.”

surprises.description: The reported net loss was $80.3 million, substantially larger than the modest loss implied by the preview’s -$0.09 Q2 EPS estimate. The call attributed the loss mainly to $28.3 million of Northern Data acquisition transaction costs and higher depreciation and amortization; the facts provided do not include actual EPS for an exact estimate-to-result comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened sharply to $80.3 million from $30.2 million a year ago, primarily due to $28.3 million in Northern Data acquisition-related transaction costs plus higher depreciation and amortization.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that AI-compute-as-a-service on Blackwell monetizes at roughly $11 million per megawatt annually, versus $1.5–2 million for a power-and-shell model. The preview discussed the 250MW roadmap and its $3 billion-plus revenue ambition, but did not provide this much higher per-megawatt monetization comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI-compute-as-a-service monetizes at roughly $11 million per megawatt per year on Blackwell versus $1.5–2 million for the power-and-shell model, implying nearly 5x greater value creation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Funding of the 250MW roadmap” and cited the ambition of “$3B+ annual run-rate revenue by 2027,” but gave no per-megawatt monetization figures.

surprises.description: The preview looked for Quake AI segment figures in the Q2 release, but management said segment reporting would begin in Q3. That leaves the detailed Q2 segment breakdown deferred, even as the company reported some operating and contract information.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Starting Q3, RUM Group will drop MAU and ARPU as headline metrics … in favor of segment reporting for Rumble Video and Quake AI.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether RUM would “report Quake AI separately, with revenue, adjusted EBITDA, GPU utilization, and contracted backlog.”

in_line: The Northern Data acquisition’s June 17 close and approximately 85.2% ownership were already described in the preview; the combined GPU estate and full Q3 consolidation are consistent with that known transaction.

The preview specifically highlighted GPU utilization and new contracts as Quake AI disclosure items. The call reported over 85% utilization and a multiyear Together AI agreement to deploy NVIDIA HGX B300 capacity.
The 250MW roadmap and its $3 billion-plus annual revenue ambition were already flagged in the preview; reiterating that opportunity was not itself new.

surprises.description: The preview’s base case put revenue at $112–116 million, and even its bear case started at $105 million; reported sales were $102.9 million, below those modeled ranges. However, that was above the preview’s explicitly flagged unreliable $84.9 million consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales declined to $102.9 million from $113.1 million a year earlier, primarily reflecting the closure of the U.K. cast roll facility.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base” revenue: “$112–116M”; “Bear” revenue: “$105–110M.” The preview also said the $84.9M consensus was “Unreliable.”

surprises.description: EPS was slightly below the $0.08 consensus estimate at $0.07. It also fell short of the preview’s $0.10–$0.15 base-case range, although the preview’s bear case was lower.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income was $1.5 million ($0.07 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP) $0.08”; the preview’s base-case EPS range was “$0.10–0.15.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $9.8 million, below the preview’s $12–13 million base case and the roughly $12.3 million quarterly pace it said was needed to reach about $45 million for the year. The result was above the preview’s $7–9 million bear-case range.
