surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 22% year-over-year to $9.8 million, with margin expanding 240 basis points to 9.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “Adj. EBITDA $12–13M” and said reaching “~$45M requires Q2 and H2 to average about $12.3M per quarter”; its bear case was “$7–9M.”

surprises.description: Forged and Cast adjusted EBITDA improved, but at $7.8 million it missed the preview’s key validation threshold of $9 million or more for reversing Q1 timing weakness. It was above the preview’s below-$7-million level that would weaken management’s timing explanation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Forged and Cast segment adjusted EBITDA rose 15% year-over-year and 36% sequentially to $7.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A print at or above $9M supports management’s framing; below $7M weakens it.” The catalyst checklist likewise called for “FCEP adj. EBITDA of $9M or more.”

surprises.description: Backlog reached $385.4 million, above the preview’s derived estimate near $375 million and above its $370–380 million base-case range. The preview had identified the composition of the expected orders and backlog as a risk, but the reported Air & Liquid backlog also grew strongly.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total backlog grew $39.9 million from Q1 to $385.4 million”; Air & Liquid backlog “increased 16% ($23.3 million) in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview derived an “exit backlog near $375M” and gave a base-case backlog range of “$370–380M.” It said “the risk is composition (ALP-heavy, FCEP-light) rather than the total.”

surprises.description: Air & Liquid delivered its highest adjusted EBITDA ever, with strong year-to-date growth and a 16% quarterly backlog increase. The preview highlighted margin durability as something to watch, but did not anticipate a segment record or this reported strength.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Air & Liquid segment delivered its highest adjusted EBITDA in its history, up 34% in Q2 and 43% year-to-date”; backlog rose 16%, “fueled by data center-driven power generation demand and strong U.S. Navy orders.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch whether incremental margins hold as capacity steps up for Navy-funded equipment”; it also noted ALP’s Q1 segment-record operating income and H1 orders up 42%.

surprises.description: Management said the second half would be significantly stronger than the first half, a positive outlook beyond the preview’s general expectation of guidance framing or reaffirmation. No quantitative full-year EBITDA or debt-reduction commitment is included in the supplied call facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects the second half of 2026 to be significantly stronger than the first half despite normal Q3 seasonal maintenance outages in the U.S. and Europe.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for “Any FY2026 EBITDA framing and debt-reduction reaffirmation” and said the base case assumed “guidance reaffirmed”; it noted that AP “does not give formal guidance.”

in_line: Customer orders were approximately $144 million, in line with the preview’s derived expectation of roughly $144 million.

surprises.description: The preview implied INVINCIBLE-3 had resumed in April and called for updates on enrollment since then. Instead, management said new enrollment is expected to begin only within the next couple of months, initially at limited U.S. sites, after FDA review of protocol changes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New patient enrollment in the Phase 3 INVINCIBLE-3 study is expected to begin within the next couple of months at limited U.S. sites,” following FDA review of an amended protocol.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “INVINCIBLE-3 (Phase 3, soft tissue sarcoma) resumed in April 2026”; the preview also said to track “patients enrolled since the April restart.”

surprises.description: The preview estimated a Q2 net loss of about $2.3–2.4 million. Intensity reported a $3.0 million loss, roughly $0.6–0.7 million worse than that estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss for Q2 2026 rose 19% year-over-year to $3.0 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss | ~$2.3–2.4M implied.”

surprises.description: The preview put cash near $8.5–10.0 million and highlighted financing as the key constraint, but the call made the size of the funding gap explicit: current cash is not enough to restart all INVINCIBLE-3 sites, and completing the study requires another $30 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Completing the Phase 3 INVINCIBLE-3 study will require an incremental $30 million over the next several years,” and “current cash is insufficient to fully restart all sites without additional capital.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said capital was “the binding constraint,” and that a bull case required “a funded INVINCIBLE-3 plan”; it estimated Q2-end cash at “~$8.5–10.0M.”

surprises.description: The preview focused on the trial restart and funding rather than a new efficacy comparison. The call reported a substantially higher pathologic complete response rate for INVINCIBLE-4 Cohort A than for standard of care alone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “71% of Cohort A patients (INT230-6 plus standard of care) achieved pathologic complete response versus 42% for standard of care alone,” in a harder-to-treat population.

in_line: Q2-end cash was $9.5 million, within the preview’s estimated range of about $8.5–10.0 million.
R&D increased, as the preview expected as trials restarted: the call reported a 19% year-over-year increase to $1.8 million.
INVINCIBLE-4 remained targeted for completion by end-2027, consistent with the preview’s stated target.

Partnering remained at the discussion stage: the preview cited 20+ discussions and flagged a named term sheet or license as a possible development; the call described 20+ BIO Convention meetings but no firm deal.
The preview anticipated modest ATM use; the call reported $1.6 million in net proceeds during Q2 and another $1.3 million after quarter-end.

surprises.description: The preview expected a Q3 diluted loss of $0.73 per share, but Alico reported diluted earnings of $0.29 per share. The company attributed the turnaround mainly to completion of accelerated depreciation on citrus trees, so the earnings beat was not necessarily a sign of stronger ongoing operations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 net income attributable to common stockholders was $2.1 million ($0.29 per diluted share)” and the turnaround was “driven mainly by completed citrus tree accelerated depreciation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) | $(0.73)” for Q3 FY26.

surprises.description: The preview put Q3 revenue consensus at $2.75 million, but Alico reported $9 million. Also, reported nine-month revenue of $16.3 million already exceeded the preview’s $11.55 million full-year FY26 revenue estimate, despite revenue being down sharply year over year as the citrus wind-down progressed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue rose 7.7% to $9 million,” while “nine-month revenue fell to $16.3 million from $43.3 million due to the substantial completion of the citrus wind-down.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $2.75M” for Q3 FY26 and “FY26 Revenue | $11.55M.”

surprises.description: The preview estimated that cash above about $49 million at June 30 would be a positive surprise; Alico ended Q3 with $55.6 million. It also reported net debt of $29.8 million, down from $47.4 million at fiscal year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: Alico ended Q3 with “$55.6 million in cash,” up $17.5 million since fiscal year-end; “Net debt was reduced to $29.8 million from $47.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash balance at 6/30/26. Cash was $52.9M at 3/31/26… Above about $49M is a positive surprise.”

surprises.description: The preview treated approximately $14 million of FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance as the baseline. Alico raised its guidance to approximately $15 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to approximately $15 million from prior guidance of approximately $14 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adjusted EBITDA guide (~$14M). Reaffirming is the baseline. Raising implies a closing.”

surprises.description: The preview cited year-end cash guidance of about $40 million and net debt of about $45 million. Alico now expects roughly $48 million in cash and $37 million in net debt at fiscal year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: Alico “now expects to end the year with roughly $48 million in cash and $37 million net debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance: FY26 adjusted EBITDA about $14M, year-end cash about $40M, net debt about $45M.”

surprises.description: The preview identified the absence of closings and a follow-on pipeline as a bear trigger. Management instead said its liquidity, including available borrowing capacity, is sufficient to fund operations through at least FY2029 without further asset sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management said liquidity, “including $92.5 million of available borrowing capacity, is sufficient to fund operations through at least fiscal 2029 without any additional asset sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “No closings and no contracted follow-on is the bear trigger” and “No sales and no pipeline” is listed in the bear scenario.

surprises.description: The preview described management’s existing portfolio-value framing as $4,000–$5,000 per acre and flagged the gap with recent sales near $9,100 per acre. Management now explicitly valued the roughly 47,300-acre portfolio at about $9,000 per acre and said it was worth substantially more than the current market capitalization reflects.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management said the “roughly 47,300-acre Florida portfolio, valued at ~$9,000 per acre consistent with recent sales, carries substantially more value than reflected in the current market capitalization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management's $650–750M portfolio value uses $4,000–5,000/acre, while recent sales printed near $9,100/acre.”

surprises.description: The preview did not mention a completed share-repurchase program. Alico reported that it had completed its $10 million program, buying back 245,399 shares.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed its $10 million share repurchase program, buying back 245,399 shares total.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag an acquisition of the remaining Citree interest. Alico acquired the remaining 49% for $2 million in cash and assumed approximately $3.3 million of debt; the shareholder impact is not clear from the information provided.
surprises.fact_evidence: Alico “acquired the remaining 49% of Citree for $2 million in cash while assuming its ~$3.3 million debt.”

in_line: The Hendry County lease and purchase option were already disclosed in the preview; the call facts give essentially the same acreage and approximately $29.5 million option price.
Management’s expectation that Q4 will use EBITDA and have much lower run-rate revenue is consistent with the preview’s expectation of no major closing and its implied quarterly cash burn.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was slightly below the $3.572 billion consensus: the company reported $3.5 billion, citing procurement delays and lower materials volume. The miss was modest, but it fell short of the preview’s roughly $3.54–$3.60 billion base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 FY26 revenue reached $3.5 billion with only ~1% normalized growth, coming in slightly below expectations due to procurement delays and lower low-margin material volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q3 FY26 Consensus | $3.572B”; the base case expected “$3.54–3.60B.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.67 was well above the preview’s $0.611 consensus and the roughly $0.58 implied by management’s prior-quarter guidance. This was a notable earnings beat despite the revenue shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS grew 20% year-over-year to $0.67.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | Q3 FY26 Consensus | $0.611”; the preview also said the Q2 guidance implied “about $0.58.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was about $290 million, above the preview’s derived estimate of roughly $279 million. The reported 8.3% margin and 60-basis-point year-over-year improvement also indicate stronger profitability than the revenue result alone suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 6% year-over-year to $290 million with record quarterly margins of 8.3%, a 60 basis point improvement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said adjusted EBITDA consensus was not published and gave a “Derived estimate ~$279M.”

surprises.description: The company lowered FY26 revenue guidance to $13.8–$13.95 billion, below the prior $13.95–$14.3 billion range. The cited award protests and lower materials volume make the reduction a concrete downside to the preview’s expectation that the range would be reaffirmed, narrowed, or trimmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY26 revenue guidance was lowered to $13.8-13.95 billion (citing ~$175 million from awards under protest and lower materials volume).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 revenue guidance of “$13,950–14,300M” and said to watch whether the company would “Reaffirm, narrow to the upper half, or trim.”

surprises.description: Despite cutting its FY26 revenue outlook, Amentum raised adjusted EBITDA guidance to $1.115–$1.14 billion from $1.10–$1.14 billion and adjusted EPS guidance to $2.40–$2.50 from $2.25–$2.45. The stronger profit outlook contrasts with the revenue reduction and exceeds the preview’s prior guidance ranges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $1.115-1.14 billion and adjusted EPS guidance increased to $2.40-2.50.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$1,100–1,140M” and adjusted diluted EPS guidance of “$2.25–2.45.”

surprises.description: Management now expects only 0–1% total revenue growth in FY27, below the preview’s roughly 4% underlying-growth reference. Mid-single-digit growth in the remaining portfolio will be largely offset by the NASA headwind and intentional exits of low-margin programs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided FY27 to only 0-1% total revenue growth as the 3% NASA headwind and ~1% intentional exit of low-margin base operations programs largely offset mid-single-digit growth in the remaining portfolio.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch the “normalized growth bridge (about 4% underlying growth per management)” and described bookings and funded backlog as supporting “the FY27 growth story.”

surprises.description: The expected revenue impact from NASA’s workforce insourcing directive increased to 3% for FY27, from the roughly 1% impact management had indicated on the prior-quarter call. The company noted that the affected work is low margin, so the revenue hit is margin-accretive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company now expects NASA's workforce insourcing directive to reduce FY27 revenue by 3%, up from the ~1% impact guided on the prior quarter's call, though the impact is margin-accretive given the business's low margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call’s prior-quarter expectation was “~1% impact.”

surprises.description: Amentum reached 3x net leverage one quarter earlier than the Capital Markets Day target, whereas the preview said management was on track to get below 3x by fiscal year-end. The quarter included $125 million of debt repayment, with nearly $700 million repaid over the trailing 12 months.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage was reduced to 3x at quarter end—one quarter earlier than the Capital Markets Day target—supported by $125 million in debt repayments during the quarter and nearly $700 million over the trailing 12 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said net leverage was 3.2x and management was “on track” for below 3x “by fiscal year-end.”

surprises.description: The Savannah River project now has a stated lifetime revenue estimate of over $1 billion, and Amentum may also gain economic interest in commercial operations, tokens, and electrons. The preview identified project economics and Amentum’s role as open questions, so this provides more specific and potentially broader economics than it had established.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The DOE-selected Savannah River AI data center and nuclear project is expected to generate over $1 billion in revenue over its life (consistent with a 2-gigawatt project), with potential additional economic interest in commercial operations, tokens, and electrons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the project as a selected negotiation for a phased lease and said “Lease timing, Amentum's role, capital commitment, and revenue timing are the open questions.”

surprises.description: Amentum announced new nuclear partnerships with Rolls-Royce and Westinghouse, including work tied to Rolls-Royce SMR wins in Sweden, the U.K., and the Czech Republic and Westinghouse’s AP1000 and AP300 platforms. These strategic additions were not among the preview’s stated expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed strategic partnerships expanding its nuclear position, including as global delivery partner to Rolls-Royce (SMR wins in Sweden, U.K., and Czech Republic) and a long-term alliance with Westinghouse covering the AP1000 and AP300 platforms.”

surprises.description: Management expects a 20-basis-point year-over-year margin increase in FY27 even while investing in nuclear and digital infrastructure. The preview focused on whether Digital Solutions could avoid further margin compression, but did not anticipate this company-wide FY27 margin outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects a 20 basis point year-over-year margin increase in FY27 despite investments in nuclear and digital infrastructure.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management guided Digital Solutions margins to be “roughly consistent with first-half levels” and flagged the risk of “a third straight quarter of compression.”

surprises.description: Amentum said 92% of anticipated FY27 revenue is already covered by existing or follow-on work, giving more visibility into next year’s revenue than the preview’s growth-and-bookings discussion specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 92% of anticipated FY27 revenue is already covered by existing or follow-on work.”

in_line: Bookings met the preview’s key threshold: quarterly book-to-bill was 1.1x, above 1.0x, and funded backlog was up 10% year over year. The preview said a ratio at or above 1.0x with growing funded backlog would support the FY27 growth story.

surprises.description: The preview’s base case anticipated no new clinical data, but Bicara reported that at the 1,500 mg weekly dose an estimated one-third of patients were alive at three years—roughly twice the survival observed with standard-of-care pembrolizumab. The update also included follow-up of up to three years across about 90 patients and three dose cohorts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “At the 1,500 mg weekly pivotal dose, an estimated 1 in 3 patients was alive at 3 years, roughly doubling the survival observed with standard-of-care pembrolizumab”; the ASCO data set covered “approximately 90 patients across 3 dose cohorts” with “up to 3 years” of follow-up.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … no new clinical data.”

surprises.description: Claire Mazumdar will leave the CEO role at the start of next year, ahead of the pivotal data, with President/COO Ryan Cohlhepp succeeding her. The preview did not flag a CEO transition; the internal succession and adviser role offer continuity, but the timing makes this a notable leadership change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CEO Claire Mazumdar will transition to Vice Chair and Strategic Adviser at the start of next year, with current President/COO Ryan Cohlhepp succeeding her as President and CEO ahead of pivotal data.”

surprises.description: The CFO is being replaced effective the day after the call, with further senior-role changes planned for January. The preview discussed commercial leadership and a commercial build-out but did not anticipate this CFO change or the additional COO and Chief Business Officer promotions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Ivan Hyep is being replaced by Jenn Larson effective the day after the call,” alongside January promotions of Tanya Green to COO and Jenna Cohen to Chief Business Officer.

surprises.description: Bicara disclosed that Genmab’s LiGeR-HN1 frontline head-and-neck readout is slated for Q4 2026, with overall response rate data expected to offer an early indication of durability. The preview did not identify this competitor catalyst, adding a new near-term source of competitive information, though the eventual data are not yet known.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Competitor Genmab's LiGeR-HN1 frontline head and neck readout is now slated for Q4 2026,” and management expects it to deliver “overall response rate data as an early indicator of durability.”

surprises.description: The preview expected cash of $485–495 million at quarter-end; Bicara reported approximately $497 million, slightly above the top of that range. The expected runway into the first half of 2029 was maintained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bicara ended Q2 2026 with approximately $497 million in cash and marketable securities, providing runway into the first half of 2029.”

surprises.description: Beyond the expected Q3 start of the alternative-dosing study, Bicara said overlap with pivotal-trial sites is limited and enrollment will be stage-gated across regions to keep FORTIFI-HN01 the priority. This provides an unanticipated operational safeguard against the new study competing with pivotal-trial enrollment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FORTIFI-FLEX site overlap with the pivotal trial is limited to about one-third of sites,” with enrollment “stage-gated across Europe, Latin America, Asia Pacific and the U.S. to keep FORTIFI-HN01 the top priority.”

in_line: FORTIFI-HN01 remained on track for substantial enrollment by year-end and a mid-2027 interim analysis, matching the preview’s stated milestones.
FORTIFI-FLEX was initiated in Q3, as the preview expected for the alternative-dosing study.
The company maintained runway into the first half of 2029, as expected.
Operating expenses rose and are expected to rise further; this is consistent with the preview’s expectation of increasing trial spending and a continued commercial build-out.

surprises.description: Q4 diluted EPS was $2.91 versus the preview’s $2.42 consensus, a substantial beat. The reported figure included a nonrecurring $0.31 IEEPA tariff-refund benefit—contrary to the preview’s expectation that no impact had yet been recognized—while EPS excluding that benefit was still $2.60.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 diluted EPS grew 40% to $2.91,” including “$0.31” from a “nonrecurring IEEPA tariff refund benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS | $2.42”; the preview also said, “no financial impact has been recognized and none is in guidance.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $63.7 billion, below the preview’s $65.0–$65.6 billion consensus range, despite growing 6% year over year. This was a notable top-line shortfall against a preview that emphasized revenue as a key issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 enterprise operating income rose 30% to $935 million on revenue of $63.7 billion (up 6%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $65.0–65.6B” and “Revenue at or above $65.0B.”

surprises.description: FY27 EPS guidance of $12.40–$12.60 was well above the $12.01 consensus and also above the preview’s cited $12.04–$12.26 range implied by the company’s longer-term algorithm. Management based the 13%–15% growth outlook on a normalized $10.95 baseline excluding the tariff refund.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal '27 EPS guidance is $12.40 to $12.60,” representing “13% to 15% growth off a normalized baseline of $10.95 that excludes the $0.31 tariff refund benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 non-GAAP EPS | $12.01”; the preview also said the algorithm implied “$12.04–$12.26.”

surprises.description: Q4 Pharma segment profit reached $645 million, above the preview’s $628 million estimate. That was a modest beat even though the segment’s 21% profit growth was stronger than the preview’s expected 17% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Pharma segment posted 21% profit growth to $645 million in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pharma & Specialty segment profit | $628M | +17%.”

surprises.description: Excluding the tariff refund, GMPD Q4 segment profit was $50 million, modestly above the preview’s $42 million estimate. The underlying result was therefore somewhat better than the estimate, even without counting the one-time refund.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding the $100 million tariff refund, GMPD Q4 segment profit was only $50 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GMPD segment profit | $42M | −40%.”

surprises.description: Despite the revenue shortfall, Q4 enterprise operating income rose 30%, with gross profit growing faster than SG&A. The preview focused on the risk of another top-line miss but gave no operating-income or expense-growth estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enterprise operating income rose 30% to $935 million”; “gross profit up 16% to $2.6 billion outpacing SG&A growth of 9.5%.”

surprises.description: The Board increased share-repurchase authorization by $5 billion, bringing total authority to $6.4 billion, and raised the FY27 baseline buyback to at least $1 billion from the preview’s $750 million-plus baseline. This was a larger capital-return commitment than the preview’s stated baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board authorized a $5 billion increase to share repurchase authority (bringing total to $6.4 billion) and raised the fiscal '27 baseline buyback to at least $1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Baseline buyback commitment is $750M+/yr”; the preview said a buyback “above that baseline” would help offset a soft EPS guide.

surprises.description: FY27 adjusted free cash flow is guided to $3.5–$4 billion, below the $5 billion reported for FY26, with CapEx rising to $700 million. The preview anticipated an FY27 FCF guide but did not give a numerical expectation, so the size of the decline was not specified in advance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal '27 adjusted free cash flow is guided lower at $3.5 billion to $4 billion (versus $5 billion in fiscal '26), with CapEx rising to $700 million.”

surprises.description: FY27 Pharma guidance calls for 8%–11% profit growth and only 3%–5% revenue growth, normalizing from Q4’s 21% profit growth and excluding outsized demand. The preview flagged GLP-1 normalization as a risk to watch but did not give a segment outlook, so the degree of the slowdown was not quantified beforehand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal '27 guidance calls for more normalized profit growth of 8% to 11% and revenue growth of just 3% to 5%, excluding outsized demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “GLP-1 normalization” among the issues to watch, but provided no FY27 Pharma growth estimate.

surprises.description: FY27 GMPD segment-profit guidance is $200–$220 million, and management said a protracted Iran conflict could push results to the low end. The preview focused on Q4 GMPD profit and the tariff refund but gave no FY27 GMPD outlook or Iran-related risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal '27 guidance targets $200 million to $220 million, with protracted Iran conflicts potentially pushing results to the low end.”

surprises.description: The other growth businesses guided to 11%–13% revenue growth and 15%–18% profit growth in FY27, with about two percentage points of support from the Strive and AdaptHealth diabetes acquisitions. The preview discussed Solaris/Specialty scale-up but did not anticipate this contribution from these businesses or acquisitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 'other' growth businesses” had FY27 guidance of “11%-13% revenue and 15%-18% profit growth, aided by ~2 points from Strive and AdaptHealth diabetes acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Specialty scale-up” and “Solaris FY27 accretion,” but did not mention Strive or AdaptHealth.

surprises.description: The preview put Q3 organic growth around 7–8% and flagged 8% or more as a positive signal; Aramark reported 9%, or approximately 11% excluding an education calendar shift expected to be recaptured in Q4. Revenue was also $5.0 billion versus $4.95 billion consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 organic revenue grew 9% to $5 billion, and would have risen approximately 11% excluding a calendar shift in education that is expected to be fully recaptured in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus implies about 7%” organic growth; the base scenario was “organic ~7–8%,” and the catalyst checklist said “Organic revenue of 8% or more” would confirm new-business conversion. Revenue consensus was $4.95B.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS came in above the preview’s $0.48 consensus and its $0.48–$0.50 base range. The reported $0.52 was strong even with the education calendar shift; excluding that shift, adjusted EPS rose almost 45%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose nearly 30% to $0.52 … or almost 45% excluding the calendar shift.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $0.48” consensus; the base scenario was “$0.48–0.50.”

surprises.description: Aramark raised its full-year organic revenue growth outlook to 9–10%, above the prior 7–9% range whose high end the preview expected it to deliver. It held, rather than raised, its AOI and adjusted EPS growth ranges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aramark raised its fiscal 2026 organic revenue growth outlook to 9%-10%, while reaffirming AOI growth of 12%-17% and adjusted EPS growth of 20%-25%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 organic revenue growth was guided at “high end of 7–9%” and its base case expected FY organic guidance to be “reaffirmed at high end.”

surprises.description: The Nexus opportunity was quantified as larger and more economically attractive than the preview could size: the first site’s annualized value rose from about $100 million to roughly $140 million, with a second larger site around $160 million and three mobilizing sites expected to generate $400–$500 million annually at above-company-average margins and low capital intensity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Aramark Nexus hyperscaler contract scope increased approximately 40%, raising the first site's annualized value from about $100 million to roughly $140 million, with a second larger site expected at around $160 million per year”; three mobilizing sites are expected to generate “$400-$500 million in annualized revenue” at “above-company-average margins with low capital intensity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called Nexus “the largest potential catalyst” and said sizing the contract, naming additional sites, or folding it into FY26 or early FY27 guidance would be important, but gave no dollar scale.

surprises.description: Management signaled that fiscal 2027 organic growth should exceed Aramark’s prior 5–8% algorithm, giving a stronger forward growth indication than the preview’s general call for FY27 framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “signaled fiscal 2027 growth above its prior 5%-8% organic revenue algorithm.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said bullish management language could include “FY27 framing,” but did not anticipate a signal that growth would exceed the prior 5–8% algorithm.

surprises.description: International delivered 11% organic growth, 24% AOI growth, and nearly 60 basis points of constant-currency margin expansion. The preview highlighted the US/International split as an issue to watch but did not specify an International growth or margin expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The International segment posted 11% organic revenue growth to $1.5 billion with AOI up 24% and margins expanding nearly 60 basis points on a constant currency basis.”

in_line: Adjusted operating income growth and adjusted EPS growth guidance were reaffirmed at 12–17% and 20–25%, respectively, consistent with the preview’s base case of holding the FY26 ranges.

Nexus is expected to begin contributing revenue in FY26: the preview noted that revenue would start this fiscal year, and the call put its Q4 contribution at approximately 1% of revenue. The call also said none of the eight signed sites is fully ramped yet.
The company maintained its commitment to get leverage below 3x by fiscal year-end, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: ARQ reported Q2 revenue of about $30 million, above the preview’s roughly $28.6 million consensus estimate. Chemicals revenue did fall modestly short because of timing, but management expects that shortfall to recover later in the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was approximately $30 million, up modestly year-over-year”; “chemicals revenue fell modestly short due to timing that management expects to recover later in the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$28.6M” for Q2 2026.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA of about $5.8 million topped even the preview’s bull-case range of $4.5–5.5 million, rather than merely matching the prior-year $3.7 million comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached approximately $5.8 million, up substantially from $3.7 million in the prior-year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull scenario expected “Adj. EBITDA | $4.5–5.5M”; it also identified $3.7 million as Q2 2025 actual.

surprises.description: Gross margin rose to about 38.5%, well above the preview’s concern that a result below roughly 34% would weaken the standalone PAC case. Management attributed the improvement to the absence of GAC start-up costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved roughly 520 basis points to approximately 38.5% due to the absence of GAC start-up costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything below about 34% excluding charges weakens the standalone PAC case.”

surprises.description: The GAC outlook extends beyond the preview’s known expectation of no 2026 output: management said no GAC production or sales are expected in 2027, and the investment decision could slip into 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “No GAC production or sales are expected in 2027”; “a GAC investment decision has not been made and could be made later in 2026 or pushed into 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management expected to “complete the strategic review and set a GAC strategy by Q3 2026”; it described deferral to the November call as the likely base case and noted no GAC output in FY2026.

surprises.description: Engineering estimates put Phase 1 GAC conversion at $40–60 million for 25 million pounds of capacity, revealing a substantial project cost range that the preview had not quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAC conversion cost estimates from two independent engineering consultants range widely at $40-60 million for 25 million pounds of Phase 1 capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “repair capex, restart timing” as issues to watch but gave no GAC conversion-cost estimate.

surprises.description: Management set an ambitious core PAC target of roughly $30 million in adjusted EBITDA next year, up to 50% growth and without any bituminous-based GAC contribution—an outlook not specified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company set a goal to grow core PAC business adjusted EBITDA by up to 50% to roughly $30 million next year, entirely without any contribution from bituminous-based GAC.”

surprises.description: ARQ disclosed that its new PAC for PFAS product should have substantially higher average selling prices and margins than base PAC, with meaningful volume and margin contribution anticipated in 2027. The preview did not identify this product opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new PAC for PFAS product is expected to carry substantially higher ASP and margins than base PAC, with only minor sales in H2 2026 but meaningful volume and margin contribution anticipated in 2027.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end unrestricted cash was only about $0.9 million, much lower than the $4.7 million reported in Q1 and a notable deterioration against the preview’s liquidity watchpoint. It rose to about $3.1 million by July 31, but most quarter-end cash was restricted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total cash of $12.1 million (of which $11.2 million restricted); unrestricted cash rose to about $3.1 million by July 31.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported “Unrestricted cash was $4.7M against $30.2M total debt in Q1” and flagged liquidity and any equity-raise language as risks.

surprises.description: Management said it intends to finance a GAC investment with debt rather than equity if it proceeds, directly addressing the preview’s concern about possible equity financing. This avoids stated dilution but would rely on additional borrowing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “They intend to fund it through debt rather than equity dilution if pursued.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Any equity-raise language in the 10-Q would be a significant risk” and flagged liquidity as a key issue.

surprises.description: Chemicals revenue came in modestly below expectations because of timing, even though total company revenue beat the preview’s estimate; management expects the chemicals shortfall to recover later in the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Chemicals revenue fell modestly short due to timing that management expects to recover later in the year.”

in_line: ARQ reaffirmed FY2026 revenue guidance of $120–125 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $17–20 million, as the preview’s base case and key watchpoint anticipated.
Deferring a GAC decision rather than announcing an immediate restart was broadly consistent with the preview’s stated likely base case of deferral to the November call.

surprises.description: NGS reported GAAP EPS of $0.30, below the preview’s $0.37–$0.40 consensus range and its $0.38–$0.42 base-case range. The call attributed the decline to about $3.3 million of Flat Rock transaction costs; adjusted EPS was $0.47.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported net income fell to $3.8 million ($0.30/share) from $5.2 million ($0.41/share) a year earlier, impacted by ~$3.3 million in Flat Rock transaction costs; adjusted net income was $6.1 million ($0.47/share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS | $0.37 ...” and “EPS | $0.40”; the base scenario also expected “$0.38–0.42 GAAP / ~$0.48 adj.”

surprises.description: Post-acquisition leverage was 2.77x, below the preview’s estimate of about 3.0x at close, with more than $170 million of unused facility capacity. That indicates a stronger balance-sheet position than the preview’s starting assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Post-acquisition leverage was 2.77x against a 3.5x covenant, with over $170 million of unused facility capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pro forma leverage was guided to about 3.0x at close” and investors need “a deleveraging path.”

surprises.description: Utilization rose to 88.3% from the prior-quarter record of 86.9%, extending the improvement rather than stalling at the previous high. The preview identified utilization as a key operating metric but did not give a specific Q2 forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Horsepower utilization reached a record 88.3%,” compared with the preview’s prior-quarter figure of 86.9%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Record utilization of 86.9%” and the preview’s “Utilization and rental revenue per HP” key issue.

surprises.description: Rental revenue per average horsepower increased to $28.06 per month from $27.51 in Q1 and was more than 5% higher year over year. That was contrary to the preview’s flagged risk that a flat or lower reading could signal slowing growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pro forma rental revenue per average horsepower per month rose to $28.06 ... and more than 5% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Rental revenue per HP was $27.51 per month in Q1. A flat or lower print would be an early sign that growth is slowing.”

surprises.description: NGS raised its organic deployment target to at least 55,000 horsepower, above the preview’s 50,000-horsepower target. This is an increase in planned deployment rather than merely confirmation that the prior target remains intact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ... raised organic 2026 deployment guidance to at least 55,000 horsepower from 50,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether “organic deployment and $55–70M of growth capex are intact” and described the catalyst as “whether ... the 50,000 HP program” was constrained.

in_line: FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $103–108 million, in line with the preview’s mechanically expected range of roughly $103–108 million.
Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $25.1 million was close to the preview’s approximately $25.0 million base expectation.
The quarterly dividend remained $0.15 per share; the preview focused on whether leverage would constrain the dividend, but the reported facts do not indicate a reduction.

surprises.description: LWLG reached five Stage 3 customers, adding one ahead of the preview’s expectation of one or two additional tier-1 customers by the end of Q3. The new customer was unnamed, whereas the preview’s clearest upside case anticipated a fifth named customer.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expanded to five stage-three customers this quarter, adding a new unnamed Fortune Global 500 customer.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A fifth named customer at this print would be ahead of schedule”; the prior-quarter guide was “1–2 additional tier-1 customers to reach Stage 3 by end of Q3 2026.”

surprises.description: The company reported that one material supply and licensing agreement is already in place, advancing beyond the preview’s description of the lead-customer agreement as still under negotiation. A second agreement remains under negotiation with the most advanced customer, so the preview’s concern about an unsigned agreement was not fully resolved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “One material supply and licensing agreement is already in place, and a second is being negotiated with the most advanced customer.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Lead-customer material supply and licensing agreement under negotiation”; the preview said “The buy side wants it signed, not negotiated.”

surprises.description: Net loss was lower than the preview’s modeled $7.0 million, although it still widened from the prior-year quarter. The gap from the estimate was modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $6.6 million (4 cents per share) from roughly $5 million (4 cents per share) in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss … ~$7.0M”; estimated EPS was “$(0.04) to $(0.05).”

surprises.description: R&D expense came in above the preview’s estimate, while management attributed rising costs to scale-up investments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expense increased to about $3.9 million (from $2.6 million) … reflecting scale-up investments.”

in_line: Revenue was approximately $33,000, close to the preview’s ~$35,000 model and within its stated $25,000–$120,000 range.
EPS was 4 cents per share, matching the preview’s estimated range of a 4- to 5-cent loss.
Quarter-end cash and marketable securities were $95.9 million, within the preview’s $95–105 million estimate.
The company continued to target volume production in 2027, consistent with the preview’s expectation of high-volume production targeted for 2027.

surprises.description: DarioHealth was expected to generate about $6.07 million of revenue, up sequentially and year over year, but reported $5.2 million, down from both Q1 and a year earlier. Management partly attributed the decline to a strategic exit from pharmaceutical services revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined to $5.2 million,” down from “$5.6 million in Q1 2026” and “$5.4 million in Q2 2025,” partly due to “a strategic exit from pharmaceutical services revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $6.07M (+12% YoY, +8% QoQ)” and the preview’s key metric: “Revenue of at least $6.0M and a third straight sequential increase.”

surprises.description: The preview referenced about $30 million of contracted ARR and expected the largest accounts to launch around July 1, with contributions landing in Q3. Instead, Dario reported $13.1 million in contracted and late-stage ARR and said revenue conversion would start in H2, with most of the contribution not appearing until 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Dario ended the quarter with approximately $13.1 million in contracted and late-stage annual recurring revenue”; management expects it “to convert into revenue starting in the second half of 2026,” with “the majority of contribution showing up in 2027” because of a “four-to-five quarter cycle from signature to full run-rate revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 management had flagged “about $30M in contracted ARR, with ‘a few of the largest’ accounts launching by July 1,” and that “These revenue contributions land in Q3.”

surprises.description: Gross margin and reported losses improved more than the preview’s discussion of the cost program and prior-quarter results would suggest: gross margin rose to 62%, while operating loss improved sequentially and year over year and net loss narrowed substantially year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin rose to 62%, up from 57% in Q1 and 55% a year ago”; operating loss improved “11% quarter-over-quarter and 30% year-over-year”; net loss narrowed to “$7.9 million from $13 million a year earlier, a 39% year-over-year improvement.”

surprises.description: Management highlighted a potentially meaningful new monetization opportunity from DarioIQ AI, estimating it could add recurring revenue from existing customers beyond the contracted ARR discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management believes “DarioIQ AI could add approximately 10-15% in recurring revenue from existing customers over time, incremental to the contracted ARR.”

surprises.description: Management also described substantial multi-condition expansion potential per account, an upside opportunity not raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management said “multi-condition expansion can generate two to five times more revenue per account.”

surprises.description: Dario reported that most new accounts are now coming through channel partners, which management said shortens sales cycles and materially lowers customer acquisition costs; the preview did not flag this acquisition-channel development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 75% of new accounts now arrive through channel partners, with shorter sales cycles and materially lower customer acquisition costs than direct sales.”

in_line: Pro forma cash was approximately in line with the preview estimate: Dario reported $36.8 million, versus the preview’s estimate of about $35–36 million.
Operating expenses continued to decline, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the cost program would hold: they were down 8% sequentially and 21% year over year.

surprises.description: MASS reported Q2 revenue of $16.1 million, above the $15.37 million consensus estimate. The beat was about 5%, despite the preview’s base case of $15.4–15.6 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $16.1 million,” up 23% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue … Consensus $15.37M (+18% Y/Y vs. $13.0M).”

surprises.description: The company raised the low end of FY26 revenue guidance by $1 million, from $67 million to $68 million, while keeping the high end at $70 million. The preview expected at least a reiteration, so this was a modest improvement to the outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised the low end of full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $68-$70 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue guide ($67–70M). Reiterate, raise, or narrow to the low end”; the catalyst checklist says “The buy side expects at least a reiteration.”

surprises.description: A $6 million Protector order from an Asia Pacific corrections agency was secured in July and is expected to contribute revenue in both Q3 and Q4. The preview did not anticipate this order, which adds a meaningful source of second-half revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $6 million Protector order from an Asia Pacific corrections agency was secured in July and will be split across Q3 and Q4 2026 revenue.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for an anticipated AVCAD award that could contribute $2–3 million in the second half, but management said the current contract had run its course and excluded AVCAD from guidance. Management still described a $10 million-plus long-term opportunity, but through a future award via Smiths Detection or direct MX-908 sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The AVCAD military program's current contract has run its course and remains excluded from guidance,” though management sees it as “a $10 million-plus long-term opportunity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The $2–3M 2H contribution depends on Smiths converting an anticipated spring award”; whether it had been signed was “the key question.”

surprises.description: NearLab had sold more than 35 devices within about 60 days of the acquisition, each with a multi-year subscription, and is expected to add about $1.25 million of second-half revenue. That is a concrete, fast-start result beyond the preview’s general expectation of early integration or cross-sell proof points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NearLab, acquired in May for $13.5 million net of escrow, sold more than 35 devices within ~60 days each with a multi-year subscription, and is expected to contribute ~$1.25 million in second-half revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NIRLAB integration and further earnout charges. Watch for early U.S. cross-sell proof points.”

surprises.description: Management forecast more than 100 Viper placements for the full year, potentially approaching 150, or two to three times 2025 levels. This is stronger and more specific than the preview’s assumption of in-line placements.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company shipped over 35 Viper devices in Q2 and expects to exceed 100 (potentially approaching 150) full-year placements, doubling or tripling 2025 levels.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario assumed “In-line placements.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA loss was $1.9 million, broadly in line with the preview’s base case of about $2.0 million.
Adjusted gross margin was 57%, consistent with the preview’s company-guidance range of “Mid-to-high 50%” and the prior-quarter 57%.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $41.6 million, about 3.6% above the $40.17 million consensus estimate, and grew 9.1% year over year—faster than the preview’s mid-single-digit growth guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue was $41.6 million, up approximately 9.1% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (Q2) … ‘Mid-single-digit’ y/y growth” and consensus “$40.17M.”

surprises.description: The quarterly loss was substantially smaller than expected: EPS was $(0.05) versus consensus of $(0.11), and adjusted EBITDA was positive rather than negative. The preview had treated $(0.11) as the EPS bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.3 million versus negative $5.6 million a year ago”; “net loss narrowed to $3.4 million ($0.05/share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (Q2) … $(0.11)” and “Treat $40.2M and $(0.11) as the bar.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 51.1%, well above the roughly 48% level the preview said consensus EPS required and above the prior-year quarter’s 46.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded to 51.1% from 46.6% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus EPS needs about 48%, above Q1's 46.9%.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year gross-margin range to 48–50% from 47–49%, improving the outlook beyond the preview’s expected reaffirmation of the prior range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised gross margin guidance to 48–50% (from 47–49%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 gross margin … 47–49%” and the base scenario anticipated “FY guide reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: The full-year revenue range was narrowed to $160–164 million from $160–166 million. It remains within the preview’s expected range and around consensus, but the lower upper bound is a modest reduction to the outlook rather than a reaffirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Narrowed full-year revenue guidance to $160–164 million (from $160–166 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue: $160–166M (reaffirmed May 2026)” and consensus “$161.1M.”

surprises.description: Neurostar revenue declined 2.7% despite double-digit capital-sales growth because treatment-session revenue fell by double digits. That session decline is steeper than the prior quarter’s 5% decline noted in the preview, although the preview did not provide a Q2 segment forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Neurostar revenue was $14.7 million, down 2.7% year-over-year, as double-digit capital sales growth was offset by double-digit declines in treatment session revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “TMS treatment sessions down 5% y/y” in Q1 FY2026; the bear scenario cited “Sessions down 8%+.”

surprises.description: The company introduced a new Neurostar sales model that shifts revenue toward system sales, consumables, and service and away from treatment sessions. Management also warned that the mix shift could make second-half revenue choppier, even as it expects to enter 2027 positioned for renewed growth; the preview did not flag this model change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Launched a new go-to-market model” with outright purchase or lease financing and a la carte support, “shifting revenue toward capital, consumables, and service and away from session revenue”; “second-half revenue may be choppier” but positioning for “renewed and sustainable growth entering 2027.”

surprises.description: Cash increased to $25 million, but the company disclosed that $7.6 million of net proceeds from an at-the-market equity offering helped fund the increase. The preview highlighted liquidity risk but did not anticipate this financing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total cash rose to $25 million as of June 30 from $19 million at March 31, aided by $7.6 million in net proceeds from an at-the-market equity offering.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Operating cash flow and liquidity” and cited “unrestricted cash $13.2M ($19.0M including restricted)” at Q1.

surprises.description: Management highlighted Greenbrook as a potential delivery site for Compass Pathways’ psilocybin therapy, using existing Spravato REMS infrastructure and unused clinic capacity. This potential new use of the clinics was not raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Positioning Greenbrook—with roughly 40% unused capacity—as an early leader to deliver Compass Pathways' psilocybin therapy,” leveraging “existing Spravato REMS infrastructure.”

in_line: Greenbrook clinic revenue grew 16.8% year over year, broadly consistent with the preview’s indication of ongoing growth after Q1 clinic revenue rose 15%.

surprises.description: TTEC reported Q2 revenue of $455 million, well below the preview’s $478.2 million consensus estimate; the 11.3% year-over-year decline was also steeper than the preview’s expected 6.9% decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue fell 11.3% year-over-year to $455 million.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $39 million, far below the preview’s roughly $50–52 million estimate and around the preview’s estimated $39–40 million covenant-breach point. The company also obtained covenant flexibility through an amendment, which was not part of the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declining to $39 million (8.7% margin)”; “The company obtained covenant flexibility through a credit facility amendment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$50–52M”; “My estimate of the covenant breach point is roughly $39–40M of Q2 adj. EBITDA”; the preview’s base leverage range was “3.75–3.85x.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was only $0.03, far below the preview’s $0.253 estimate. An unexpectedly high normalized tax rate of 82.8%, including a valuation allowance against U.S. losses, contributed an $0.08 negative EPS impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS collapsed to $0.03”; “higher normalized tax rate of 82.8% … driving an $0.08 negative EPS impact largely due to a valuation allowance against U.S. losses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | $0.253”; the preview listed a FY26 tax-rate assumption of “38–42%.”

surprises.description: Engage’s outlook worsened instead of showing the improved profitable growth management had promised from Q2: revenue fell 12.1%, and full-year guidance now calls for an 8% revenue decline at the midpoint versus a prior 4.1% decline, with the guided EBITDA margin lowered to 10.1% from 10.6%. The second-half weakness is concentrated in two clients, and TTEC is renegotiating economics with underperforming clients.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Engage segment saw revenue drop 12.1%”; “full-year Engage guidance cut so revenue now declines 8% (from 4.1%) at the midpoint and EBITDA margin lowered to 10.1% from 10.6%”; weakness was “concentrated in two clients”; management is “renegotiating economics with high-single-digit underperforming Engage clients.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management promised that Engage would return to improved profitable YoY growth starting in Q2”; “A YoY margin improvement would confirm the promise.”

surprises.description: Management initiated a strategic-alternatives review for T-TECH Digital with PJT Partners, including a possible sale, rather than simply continuing with the segment as-is. The preview identified such a review as a bear-case trigger, but did not present it as the expected outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management initiated a review of strategic alternatives for the T-TECH Digital segment via advisor PJT Partners, with outcomes ranging from a sale to keeping Digital within T-TECH and no set timeline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bear: Any reference to lender dialogue, a reassessment of the year's shape, or a review of strategic alternatives for Digital.”

in_line: Q2 net leverage was 3.85x, at the upper end of the preview’s 3.75–3.85x base-case range.

surprises.description: JBI cut its FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $150–$170 million, below the prior $165–$185 million range and with a $160 million midpoint. The cut was larger than the preview’s base case of reaffirmed guidance, though it fell within the preview’s bear-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management cut full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $150–$170 million, citing weaker-than-expected demand.
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY26 adj. EBITDA: $165–185M (reaffirmed); the base scenario assumed “FY guide reaffirmed,” while the bear scenario anticipated a cut to “~$155–170M.”

surprises.description: FY26 revenue guidance was cut to $925–$945 million, below the previous $940–$980 million range and below the preview’s $957.4 million consensus. The $935 million midpoint is a meaningful downward revision, although the preview had identified a cut below $940 million as a bear trigger.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management cut full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $925–$945 million, citing weaker-than-expected demand.
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY26 revenue guidance was $940–980M; consensus was $957.4M. The preview called “a cut below $940M revenue” a bear trigger.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $40.2 million, below the preview’s inferred $42–$45 million range, and the 17.2% margin missed the preview’s roughly 18% recovery watchpoint. The margin also contracted about 430 basis points year over year rather than rebuilding.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 adjusted EBITDA fell 18% to $40.2 million, compressing margin by roughly 430 basis points to 17.2%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview derived Q2 adjusted EBITDA of “~$42–45M”; it said to watch for EBITDA margin “back above 18%” and flagged a margin below 17% as stressing the back-half math.

surprises.description: North American organic self-storage revenue is now expected to decline at a high-single-digit rate, worse than the preview’s mid-single-digit decline expectation. Management attributed the weakness to constrained new construction, particularly among smaller customers.
surprises.fact_evidence: North American organic self-storage revenue is now guided to decline high single digits versus 2025, driven by constrained new construction activity, particularly among smaller customers.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described management’s guide as “down mid-single-digit” for NA organic self-storage.

surprises.description: Commercial and other revenue fell 21.2% year over year, sharply contradicting the preview’s expectation that the segment would return to growth in 2026. The continued softness was concentrated in commercial sheet doors used in pre-engineered metal buildings.
surprises.fact_evidence: The commercial and other segment revenue dropped 21.2% year-over-year, primarily from continued softness in commercial sheet doors used in pre-engineered metal buildings.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Commercial & Other was “guided to return to growth in 2026” and that “a second negative quarter would undercut the diversification thesis.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was $21.6 million, well below the preview’s roughly $40 million-or-more watchpoint. This quarterly shortfall contrasts with the separate report that trailing-12-month cash conversion was strong and full-year conversion is expected at the high end of its range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 free cash flow was $21.6 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “FCF of ~$40M or more.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $233.5 million, below the preview’s approximately $238.8 million consensus estimate. The miss was about 2.2%, despite revenue still increasing year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 total revenue was $233.5 million, up 2.4% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 FY26E revenue was “~$238.8M (+4.7% YoY).”

surprises.description: The KB2/Kiwi construction acquisition’s expected inorganic revenue contribution was reduced by about $10 million, with project delays and extended timelines. The preview noted an approximately $90 million annualized acquisition contribution, so the revised $80–$90 million outlook is lower, although management said there were no cancellations.
surprises.fact_evidence: The KB2/Kiwi construction acquisition's inorganic revenue contribution was lowered to approximately $80–$90 million (about a $10 million cut) due to project delays and extended timelines, though no cancellations occurred.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Kiwi II as adding “~$90M annualized” and noted its $18.1 million Q1 contribution.

surprises.description: JBI reported that more than 500,000 Nokia smart-entry units are installed and said this scale is expected to support recurring revenue and improve profitability over time. The preview did not flag this installed-base milestone or its prospective contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company surpassed 500,000 installed Nokia smart-entry units, an inflection point management expects to support recurring revenue and improved profitability over time.

surprises.description: Management said Nokia Infinity, a dual-technology on-door locking system, is expected to become available for factory installation on roll-up and swing doors in Q4. The preview did not anticipate this product launch timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: Nokia Infinity, a dual-technology on-door smart locking system, is expected to be available for factory install on roll-up and swing doors starting in Q4.

surprises.description: Trailing-12-month free-cash-flow conversion of adjusted net income was 129%, and management expects full-year conversion at the high end of the 75%–100% range. The preview highlighted cash flow but did not state an expectation for conversion at this level.
surprises.fact_evidence: Trailing-12-month free cash flow conversion of adjusted net income was 129%, and full-year conversion was guided to the higher end of the 75%–100% range.

in_line: Net leverage ended at 2.7x, matching the preview’s Q1 leverage reference of 2.7x and remaining below its approximately 2.8x watchpoint.

surprises.description: Vestis reported $80.9 million of adjusted EBITDA, slightly above the preview’s $79–80 million bar, with a 12.2% margin versus the expected roughly 11.7–12.0%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 adjusted EBITDA reached approximately $80.9 million” and “margin expanding to 12.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA vs. about $79–80M” and “Margin would need to reach roughly 11.7–12.0%.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $662 million, below the $668.9 million consensus and below the preview’s $665–672 million base scenario. The shortfall reflects a steeper revenue decline than the base case anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue was approximately $662 million, down 1.8% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $668.9M” and the base scenario of “$665–672M (−0.3% to −1.3% YoY).”

surprises.description: Revenue per pound rose 3% to $1.42, a stronger improvement than the preview’s expectation of another flat-to-up quarter. It was also the first year-over-year increase since Vestis became public.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue per pound rose $0.04 or approximately 3% year-over-year to $1.42,” marking “the first year-over-year increase in revenue per pound since Vestis became a public company.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A second clean quarter of flat-to-up revenue per pound would support pricing discipline.”

surprises.description: Pounds processed fell 4.5%, substantially more than the 1.2% decline reported for Q2, as Vestis exited low-priced volume. That exit reduced revenue, although the disclosed volume was loss-making at the stated revenue and cost per pound.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A 4.5% decline in pounds processed” resulted as the company exited volume averaging “only $0.55 revenue per pound versus the business's $1.24 cost per pound.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Revenue per pound and volume” as a “quality check on pricing” and noted Q2 volume was down 1.2%, but did not forecast a Q3 volume decline of this size or an exit of this specific volume.

surprises.description: Vestis raised full-year free cash flow guidance to $160–170 million from $120–150 million, a much larger improvement than the preview’s expectation that the range might simply be maintained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year free cash flow guidance to $160-$170 million” from “the prior $120-$150 million range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A maintained FCF guide is a modest positive. A raise would be a real surprise, given the one-time working-capital help.”

surprises.description: The adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint rose only $2.5 million, to $312.5 million, while the range was narrowed to $310–315 million and its prior $325 million ceiling was removed. That is a small midpoint increase but a lower top-end outlook than the preview’s existing range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was tightened to $310-$315 million (midpoint $312.5 million), up $2.5 million from prior, implying Q4 EBITDA of $84-$89 million while the prior top end of $325 million was removed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$295–325M (midpoint $310M)” and said a “raised EBITDA range” would be a bull signal.

surprises.description: A new outsourcing agreement is expected to generate about $10 million in annualized savings beginning in fiscal 2027, an additional cost-saving measure not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new third-party outsourcing agreement for back-office finance, IT, and customer service functions is expected to generate approximately $10 million in annualized cost savings beginning in fiscal 2027.”

surprises.description: Vestis disclosed a new $15–20 million management incentive bonus expense embedded in EBITDA. The preview did not flag this cost, which was not present in the prior year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 marks the first year Vestis has accrued a management incentive bonus at this level, estimated at $15-$20 million of new expense embedded in EBITDA that was not present last year.”

surprises.description: Management said its bottom 30% of market centers materially drag results and plans to direct about 42% of plant CapEx to them in 2026–2027. This newly disclosed concentration of weak performance and targeted capital spending was not addressed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management identified the “bottom ~30 market centers (quadrant 4)” as significantly dragging results and plans to allocate “about 42% of plant CapEx to these centers in 2026-2027” to close a margin gap described as “material.”

in_line: Transformation savings were broadly on the preview’s implied pace: the preview said roughly $35 million needed to land in H2 from about $15 million realized through Q2; the call reported about $30 million in-year, with the remaining $20 million expected in Q4 toward the ~$50 million target.
The implied Q4 adjusted EBITDA range of $84–89 million was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of 5–10% sequential Q4 growth after Q3 EBITDA of $80.9 million.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $670 million, about 3.7% above the preview’s most-cited $646 million consensus. The call attributed the beat mainly to revenue recognized earlier than expected, rather than a durable increase in demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total GAAP revenue was $670 million” and “beating expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $646M (most cited; range $646M–$664M across sources)”

surprises.description: Private Cloud exceeded its $242–$246 million guidance, but the preview’s flagged overage was not volume growth: it came from an embedded lease treated as a hardware sale. That recognition pulls revenue forward from future periods, and full-year guidance is unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: Private Cloud revenue was “$263 million,” with the upside from “an embedded lease treated like a hardware sale rather than volume growth”; it “pulls forward revenue from future periods including 2H 2026,” and full-year guidance is unchanged.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Private Cloud was “$17.3M above the top of its preliminary range” and asked management to “reconcile the $670.1M actual with the $641M–$649M preliminary, especially the $17.3M Private Cloud overage.”

surprises.description: Rackspace signed the AMD agreement the preview was watching, and disclosed a 30 MW deployment, phased through 2028, with 15 MW targeted by the end of 2027. The commitment size and schedule were not specified in the preview’s expectation of a near-term agreement.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “entered a definitive agreement with AMD to deploy 30 megawatts” in phases from late 2026 through 2028, targeting “15 MW cumulative by end of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Rackspace had been “targeting a near-term definitive agreement” and flagged “committed megawatts” as something to watch.

surprises.description: The preview raised ATM dilution and asked about the GPU-capex funding plan; management said financing for the initial deployment is planned largely through asset-backed and OEM/equipment facilities collateralized by the hardware. That is a more specific, potentially less equity-dependent funding plan than the preview could confirm.
surprises.fact_evidence: The first approximately 2 MW deployment requires “approximately $75 million in capital expenditures,” with financing “planned largely through asset-backed and OEM/equipment facilities collateralized by the hardware.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “ATM shares issued to date and the funding plan for GPU capex” and described the ATM as “a dilution question.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP loss per share of $0.08 was slightly better than the preview’s main estimate of about $0.09 loss, though the preview also noted providers estimating a smaller loss of $0.05.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP loss per share widened to $0.08” from $0.06 a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | ~$(0.09) (other providers $(0.05)).”

surprises.description: Management maintained full-year free-cash-flow guidance of $50–$70 million and expects generation to accelerate in the second half, despite negative Q2 free cash flow and operating cash flow. The preview highlighted the cash-flow and liquidity concerns but did not state a full-year FCF expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “maintains full-year free cash flow guidance of $50-70 million, expecting generation to accelerate in the second half”; Q2 free cash flow was negative $48 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted Q2 operating cash flow of “$(32)M” and asked about the balance sheet and ATM usage.

surprises.description: The company repurchased $11.2 million of senior notes during the quarter, a capital-allocation action not anticipated in the preview. Against the preview’s focus on liquidity and possible dilution, using cash for note repurchases is a mixed signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $11.2 million in senior notes during the quarter” and ended Q2 with “$111 million in cash and $202 million in total liquidity.”

in_line: The full-year GAAP revenue range of $2.45–$2.55 billion was unchanged, consistent with the preview’s stated guidance; the preview had also anticipated a substantial H2 revenue step-down.

The preview flagged Public Cloud’s decline and the question of whether it reflected a deliberate exit or lost demand. The call described a strategic exit of low-margin public-cloud revenue, with full-year Public Cloud guided down 13% at the midpoint and Private Cloud up 4%.
The preview already highlighted negative Q2 operating cash flow of $32 million; the call reported the same figure.

The AMD agreement’s unit economics and initial deployment capex were broadly as previewed: $15–$20 million of annual revenue per megawatt, EBITDA margins above 50%, and approximately $75 million of capex for the first deployment.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $60.7 million, above the preview’s $56–58 million estimate. That is a clear beat, though the full-year guidance midpoint remained unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA reached $60.7 million,” up 12% sequentially.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA: No published sell-side consensus found. Author estimate: $56–58M.”

surprises.description: The company raised 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $100–120 million from the prior $85–105 million range. The preview flagged the capex revision and Double E funding as key issues, but the increase was not expected in its base scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised capital expenditure guidance to “$100-120 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 capex guide of $85–105M”; the base scenario assumed “guidance held.”

surprises.description: The full-year EBITDA range narrowed to $235–255 million while keeping its $245 million midpoint. The midpoint was expected to hold, but the tighter range is a more confident outlook than the preview specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “tightened full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $235-255 million (midpoint $245 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA midpoint of $245M reiterated”; the base scenario assumed “guidance held.”

surprises.description: SMC secured about 30 additional Williston well connections not included in its original guidance, with roughly $10 million of expected 2027 EBITDA. The preview discussed about 40 Q2 connects and about 80 DUCs, but did not anticipate these extra connections or their future contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 30 new Williston well connections not in original guidance,” weighted toward Q4 and expected to contribute “roughly $10 million of EBITDA in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “About 40 connects were guided for Q2”; “with about 80 DUCs behind the systems.”

surprises.description: Double E contracted volume was just over 1.9 Bcf/day, and management cited a sub-6x build multiple for the compression expansion. The preview expected an FID by the end of summer but had no disclosed project cost or build-multiple information; the FID is still expected in the coming weeks, with the open season extended through August.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Double E contracted volume climbed to just over 1.9 Bcf/day,” the “mainline compression expansion open season” was extended through August, and an FID is expected “in the coming weeks at a sub-6x build multiple.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had guided FID “by end of summer”; “Total project cost and SMC's JV share have not been disclosed.”

surprises.description: The Piceance faces an upcoming cash-flow step-down as its MVC shortfall payments expire, leaving a normalized 2027 run rate of about $4–4.5 million per quarter. The preview noted structural decline but did not flag this specific near-term reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Piceance segment faces a cash flow step-down starting Q4 as ~$4 million/quarter in MVC shortfall payments expire,” implying “about $4-4.5 million per quarter for 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Piceance is in structural decline.”

surprises.description: Crude and composite NGL prices each rose about 30% quarter over quarter, benefiting DJ Basin percentage-of-proceeds earnings. The preview did not anticipate this favorable commodity-driven earnings contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Realized crude oil and composite NGL prices both rose approximately 30% quarter-over-quarter, benefiting earnings on percentage-of-proceeds contracts in the DJ Basin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Negative Waha pricing helps the Double E take-or-pay case but does not help Q2 EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Management set a target of more than $100 million in organic EBITDA growth by 2030, primarily from the Rockies and Permian. The preview did not identify this long-range growth target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management targets over $100 million of organic EBITDA growth by 2030 (primarily Rockies and Permian).”
