surprises.description: Although SMC repurchased shares under its $35 million authorization, it used only about $1 million and said it would prioritize debt reduction and dividend reinstatement over buybacks. The preview highlighted buyback execution and the capital-allocation tradeoff, but did not anticipate this stated priority or the small amount used.
surprises.fact_evidence: SMC repurchased “~35,000 shares for $1 million” with “~$34 million remaining,” while management prioritized debt reduction and dividend reinstatement over buybacks.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether any of the $35M buyback was executed in Q2”; the preview also described deleveraging as competing with Double E growth capex.

in_line: The full-year adjusted EBITDA midpoint remained $245 million, as the preview expected.
Management continued to expect a common dividend in the near future, consistent with the prior-quarter statement noted in the preview.

surprises.description: Commercial Foodservice organic growth was 8.3%, above the preview’s 3–7% guide, and revenue of about $631 million exceeded the preview’s $600–620 million range. The segment also posted its second-largest revenue quarter in its history.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commercial Foodservice delivered Q2 revenue of ~$631 million with organic revenue growth of 8.3%, marking the second-largest revenue quarter in the segment's history.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Commercial Foodservice revenue | $600–620M (+3–7% organic)”

surprises.description: Middleby raised full-year Commercial Foodservice organic growth guidance to 6–8%, above the initial 4–6% outlook. Management said the increase was driven predominantly by volume rather than pricing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year Commercial Foodservice organic growth guidance to 6%-8%, up from an initial 4%-6%, driven predominantly by volume rather than pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Commercial Foodservice revenue | $600–620M (+3–7% organic)”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was about $193 million, just above the preview’s $192 million high end of company guidance and above the roughly $186 million implied consensus. Adjusted EPS of $2.35, however, was within the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total company adjusted EBITDA was ~$193 million with adjusted EPS from continuing operations of $2.35.”

surprises.description: The ice and beverage platform was growing faster than expected, but its lower margins and new-product manufacturing ramp reduced Q2 margins by 150 basis points. The preview did not flag this specific faster-growing, lower-margin mix as a source of pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ice and beverage platform, growing faster than expected, carries margins ~400 basis points below the established cooking platform and created a 150 basis point margin drag in Q2 from new product manufacturing ramp-up.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed incremental second-half inflationary margin pressure of about $10–15 million versus prior expectations, with pricing benefits not expected to materialize until Q4. That is a weaker near-term margin outlook than the preview’s bull-case condition of a credible second-half bridge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects incremental inflationary margin pressures of ~$10 million to $15 million in the second half versus prior expectations, with pricing benefits not materializing until Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A print at or above 26% with a credible H2 bridge is the bull case.”

surprises.description: Pro forma leverage at the spin was 2.7x, below the preview’s stated 2.8x RemainCo target. Management still expects to reach about 2.5x by year-end, primarily through debt paydown.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Leverage was 2.4x at quarter-end (2.7x pro forma at spin), with the company targeting delevering to ~2.5x by year-end via debt paydown as the primary use of second-half capital.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Middleby RemainCo targets 2.8x leverage, deleveraging to 2.5x by year-end.”

in_line: Adjusted EPS of $2.35 was within the preview’s $2.27–2.39 company-guidance range and close to its $2.35–2.42 base scenario.
Post-spin full-year adjusted EPS guidance of $6.73–6.89 was in line with the preview’s roughly $6.60–6.90 standalone range and KeyBanc’s $6.77 estimate.
Commercial Foodservice adjusted EBITDA margin was 25.8%, between the preview’s 25.5% downside threshold and 26% bull-case mark.

surprises.description: KLX announced a $125 million backstopped rights offering, guaranteeing at least $94 million of debt reduction and lowering net leverage to about 2.7x. Management also said the balance-sheet actions and coiled-tubing lease roll-off are expected to improve 2027 free cash flow by about $20 million, including $11–14 million of annual interest savings; the preview did not anticipate this financing plan or quantified cash-flow benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$125 million backstopped equity rights offering” that “guarantees at least $94 million of deleveraging” and “would cut net leverage to approximately 2.7x”; actions plus lease roll-off “will improve 2027 free cash flow by about $20 million,” including “$11-14 million of annual interest savings.”

surprises.description: Q3 guidance points to a stronger recovery than the preview’s flat-market expectation: revenue guidance has a $182 million midpoint, and management characterized the implied base-business growth as mid-single digits. This is more specific and constructive than the preview’s base case of a “constructive but non-committal H2.”
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $176-188 million (midpoint $182 million) implies a $15 million sequential increase and mid-single-digit base-business growth against flat market expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Frac spreads fell to about 196 crews by mid-July 2026 from about 205 in early July, which cuts against an H2 ramp”; base scenario: “constructive but non-committal H2.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA and margin came in above the preview’s expected range and margin threshold. EBITDA was $18.7 million versus an implied $16–18 million estimate, while the 11.2% margin exceeded the preview’s 10% catalyst level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 68% sequentially to $18.7 million, expanding margins ~350 basis points to 11.2% on incremental margins of roughly 34%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$16–18M (implied, estimate)”; catalyst: “Adj. EBITDA margin at or above 10%.”

surprises.description: The reported loss per share was substantially smaller than the preview’s roughly $0.82 loss estimate, but the improvement was aided by a nonrecurring bargain-purchase gain. The preview did not flag that one-off gain, so the headline comparison overstates the underlying earnings improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed to $8 million ($0.41 per share) from $24 million ($1.23 per share) in Q1, aided by a nonrecurring $6.5 million bargain purchase gain excluded from adjusted results.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS … –$0.82 (second source: –$0.81).”

surprises.description: Management said Q3 will now mark the company’s liquidity low point, a caution against the preview’s expectation that cash generation would normalize in the second half. Quarter-end liquidity itself was $53.3 million, above the preview’s $50 million watch level, so the surprise is the timing of the expected low rather than a shortfall in reported liquidity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Quarter-end total debt stood at $288.9 million against total liquidity of $53.3 million ($7.9 million cash plus $45.4 million ABL availability), with Q3 now expected to mark the liquidity low point.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said cash generation should normalize in H2 as receivables convert”; watch for “liquidity at or above $50M and positive FCF.”

surprises.description: KLX disclosed that WolfPack, which closed in June, contributed $3.4 million in that month—implying about a $41 million annual run rate—and raised its synergy target to about $2.5 million. The preview mentioned potential M&A generally but did not anticipate this specific acquisition contribution or increased synergy target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The WolfPack acquisition, closed June 2, contributed $3.4 million in June (implying a ~$41 million annual run rate) and its synergy target was raised to ~$2.5 million.”

surprises.description: A lost Haynesville customer reduced natural gas to about 15% of revenue, an adverse customer and mix development not identified in the preview. The preview’s broader discussion of falling frac spreads did not flag this specific customer loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Natural gas fell to about 15% of revenue due to a lost Haynesville customer.”

surprises.description: The Northeast/Mid-Con segment was a notable profitability standout, with a 24% adjusted EBITDA margin and EBITDA up 74% year over year. The preview offered no segment-specific expectation, so this regional strength was not anticipated there.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Northeast/Mid-Con segment posted the strongest profitability at 24% adjusted EBITDA margin with EBITDA up 74% year-over-year.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $167.3 million, near the $167 million company-guidance midpoint and close to the preview’s $167.5 million consensus estimate.
The company elected to PIK 100% of Q2 interest and expected the same in Q3 before moving to a 50-50 cash/PIK mix in Q4, matching the preview’s description of the existing plan.
Quarter-end liquidity was $53.3 million, above the preview’s $50 million watch level.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $229 million, far below the preview’s $254–258 million model and down about 8% year over year. The shortfall was roughly $25–29 million versus the modeled range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 revenue declined to $229 million from $248 million a year earlier, a roughly 8% year-over-year decrease.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY2026 model | 254–258.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $13.7 million, about half the preview’s $26–27 million estimate. The result was also well below the prior-year quarter, rather than delivering the growth embedded in the model.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell sharply to $13.7 million from $24.5 million in the prior-year quarter, reflecting weaker mix and fixed-cost deleveraging.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | Q2 FY2026 model | 26.0–27.0.”

surprises.description: Turnaround activity remained much weaker than the preview’s key timing question anticipated: revenues were down more than 50% year over year, and deferred work was tied to refiners capturing strong crack spreads. Management said the Middle East conflict and deferred turnaround activity reduced first-half revenue by more than $20 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Turnaround revenues are down more than 50% versus the prior year as refining customers deferred maintenance to capture strong crack spreads”; “The Middle East conflict and deferred turnaround activity negatively impacted first-half 2026 revenue by more than $20 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Confirmation that delayed turnarounds land in 2H, rather than get cancelled, separates a timing story from a demand story.”

surprises.description: The segment results showed a sharper decline in Mechanical Services than in the more stable Inspection and Heat Treating business: Mechanical Services fell 11%, versus a 5% decline for Inspection and Heat Treating. The preview specifically flagged the MS segment as an area to watch but did not model declines of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mechanical Services revenue dropped 11% to $97 million, while the more stable Inspection and Heat Treating segment declined 5% to $131 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “MS segment and turnaround commentary.”

surprises.description: Management kept full-year guidance unchanged but said it now expects results toward the lower half of the ranges. That is weaker than a neutral-to-slightly-negative plain reaffirmation and reinforces the preview’s downside scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $920–$945 million revenue, $240–$260 million gross profit, and $68–$73 million adjusted EBITDA, but expects results toward the lower half of these ranges.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A plain reaffirm is neutral to slightly negative given the growth gap”; the bear scenario included “the FY EBITDA guide goes to the low end.”

surprises.description: The newly quantified cost program was larger than the preview’s $15 million-or-more bull-case threshold: it targets $20–35 million of annualized savings, with $8–15 million expected in the second half of 2026 and full run-rate by 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new structural cost improvement program targets $20 million to $35 million of annualized savings, with full run-rate expected by 2027 and $8 million to $15 million of benefit in the second half of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bull: ... cost program sized at 15M or more run-rate”; the preview also said the CEO had pre-committed to “a specific cost-reduction amount in this release.”

surprises.description: Stellex Capital Management became Team’s largest common equity shareholder in a negotiated transaction at a significant premium, buying out CORE Partners. The preview did not anticipate this ownership change, and the supplied facts do not establish its operational or financial effect for the company.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Stellex Capital Management became Team's largest common equity shareholder through a negotiated transaction at a significant premium, buying out prior shareholder CORE Partners.”

surprises.description: Management introduced a target of more than 10% year-over-year growth in LNG, aerospace, commercial nuclear power, and pulp and paper, alongside several incoming senior operating and HR leaders. The preview did not mention this growth target or leadership additions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Team is targeting more than 10% year-over-year growth in new verticals including LNG, aerospace, commercial nuclear power, and pulp and paper, with an incoming COO, CHRO, and SVP of Operational Excellence supporting the transformation.”

in_line: Full-year guidance was reaffirmed rather than raised or trimmed, consistent with the preview’s base scenario of guidance holding on paper; management’s expectation for results toward the lower half of the ranges was worse than a plain reaffirmation.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $187M versus the preview’s $311.3M consensus, a large shortfall. The reported figure included a negative $136M adjustment from exiting the rail contracts, even though underlying revenue grew year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total reported Q2 revenue was $187 million, reflecting a negative $136 million adjustment from exiting the two rail contracts … though underlying revenue grew year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $311.3M”

surprises.description: Adjusted loss per share was $0.63, substantially worse than the preview’s $0.31 loss estimate. The loss was more than twice the expected amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported an adjusted loss per share of $0.63.”

surprises.description: The $247M of unusual P&L items exceeded the approximately $208M in rail-related charges expected in the preview by about $39M. The call facts identify the expected $75M impairment and $133M contract-exit liability among the items, but do not explain the additional amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company recorded $247 million of unusual P&L items, including $75 million in noncash impairment charges and a $133 million liability for contract exit obligations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “It expects a ~$75M noncash impairment and a ~$133M incremental liability, about $208M in total charges.”

surprises.description: Harsco Environmental produced $46M of adjusted EBITDA, above the preview’s roughly $40M expectation, while revenue grew 3%. Its implied adjusted EBITDA margin was about 17.3%, above the 15.5% prior-year margin cited in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Harsco Environmental segment revenue grew 3% to $266 million and adjusted EBITDA rose 15% to $46 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “HE Q2 adj. EBITDA against about $40M and margin against 15.5% a year ago.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA reached $34M, above the preview’s $29–32M base scenario and in line with its bull-scenario threshold; management also said it exceeded company expectations. The preview had no sourced consensus for adjusted EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA rose over 20% year-over-year to $34 million (up 22%), exceeding company expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base | … Adj. EBITDA | $29–32M”; “Bull | … Adj. EBITDA | $34M+.”

surprises.description: Rail’s original-equipment demand was described as at a multi-decade low, a more severe picture than the preview’s note that the order book was only “a little bit behind” historical levels. Aftermarket growth helped offset the weakness, but Rail still recorded a $5M adjusted EBITDA loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rail posted an adjusted EBITDA loss of $5 million on flat adjusted revenue of $58 million, with double-digit aftermarket growth partially offsetting multi-decade-low original equipment demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said in May that the order book was ‘a little bit behind’ historical levels.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed that the exited Deutsche Bahn and Network Rail contracts had consumed roughly $40M of cash in 2025 and were expected to consume a similar amount in 2026. The preview knew the contracts had been concluded, but did not flag this recurring cash drain or its removal as a benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enviri exited its Deutsche Bahn and Network Rail ETO contracts, which consumed roughly $40 million of cash in 2025 and were expected to consume a similar amount in 2026, significantly derisking the rail business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “On Aug 10 after the close, the company said it concluded its Deutsche Bahn and Network Rail engineered-to-order contracts.”

surprises.description: Restructuring actions eliminating approximately 300 positions are expected to generate over $15M of annual margin uplift at full run rate, a cost-improvement program not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restructuring actions eliminating approximately 300 positions are expected to deliver over $15 million in annual margin uplift on a full run-rate basis once completed.”

surprises.description: Management added a target for meaningful earnings and cash flow growth beginning in 2027; the preview discussed the 2026 framework but did not flag this longer-range target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management [is] targeting meaningful earnings and cash flow growth beginning in 2027.”

in_line: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was maintained within the ranges highlighted in the preview: Harsco Environmental at $170–180M and Rail at a $19–26M loss.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $24.3 million, about 28.5% below the preview’s $34.0 million consensus estimate. That is a large shortfall against the expected quarter, despite revenue rising year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenue rose 67% year-over-year to $24.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$34.0M”

surprises.description: The preview’s own estimate was about $2.4 million of adjusted EBITDA; the company reported $1.6 million, a meaningful miss against that estimate. Adjusted EBITDA was nevertheless positive, versus a loss in the prior-year quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA swung to a positive $1.6 million from a $1.1 million loss in the prior year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA consensus was not published; the full preview's own estimate is about $2.4M, which is not company-provided.”

surprises.description: Demand and backlog across the two continuing segments were stronger than the preview’s risk threshold suggested: combined backlog rose 93% year over year and book-to-bill was 1.5x, versus the preview’s warning that below 1.0x ex-wind would be a bear trigger. Industrial Solutions also extended its backlog-growth streak to eight quarters.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Combined backlog for Industrial Solutions and Gearing increased 93% year-over-year as of June 30, with a book-to-bill ratio of 1.5x”; Industrial Solutions backlog reached “$47.4 million,” extending its growth streak to “8 consecutive quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consolidated book-to-bill: Q1 was 1.1x. Below 1.0x ex-wind is the bear trigger”; “Industrial Solutions backlog: a seventh consecutive record, or a break? (Q1: $43.3M)”

surprises.description: Management said Industrial Solutions’ margin, near 19% in Q2, should normalize downward going forward. The preview noted a roughly 19% Q1 margin but did not flag an expected step-down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Industrial Solutions revenue jumped nearly 80% to a record $13.2 million with EBITDA margin near 19%, though management expects margins to normalize downward going forward.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Industrial Solutions ~19%”

surprises.description: Liquidity was reported at over $40 million of cash and credit availability, or $31.3 million after minimum excess availability, with a $6 million inventory reduction supporting the position. The preview highlighted the balance sheet as a key question but did not forecast this level of availability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Broadwind ended Q2 with total cash and credit availability over $40 million ($31.3 million after minimum excess availability), supported by a $6 million inventory reduction from the Abilene wind-down.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash $0.9M… $25.1M available liquidity”; “Balance sheet and capital allocation. Abilene delivered $17.2M cash in April.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that Sanford can support approximately $75 million in revenue and cited primary customer GE Vernova’s 18%–20% growth outlook. The preview discussed demand and backlog broadly but did not identify this facility capacity or customer outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Sanford, North Carolina facility can support growth to approximately $75 million in revenue, with primary customer GE Vernova guiding to 18%-20% growth.”

in_line: Management did not reinstate guidance, consistent with the preview’s base case of “no guidance” and its note that guidance had been withdrawn after the Abilene sale.
The company expects to complete its remaining wind orders in Q3 2026, consistent with the preview’s checklist item to confirm the wind exit completion in Q3.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $15 million: far above the vendor consensus of $2.14 million, which the preview warned did not appear to model staking rewards, but slightly below the preview’s own $16–18 million estimate. The reported $15 million was entirely staking-driven.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose to $15 million in Q2 from $3 million in Q1, entirely driven by higher staking rewards.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $2.14M” and “My Estimate | $16–18M”; the preview also said, “Vendors do not appear to model staking rewards.”

surprises.description: The reported 17% annualized Q2 staking yield was a little above the preview’s roughly 16% June figure. Management nevertheless cautioned that the current staking economics should not be assumed to continue indefinitely.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The gram staking yield was approximately 17% annualized in Q2,” but management “explicitly cautioned it does not assume current staking economics will continue indefinitely.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross yield was ~16% annualized in June” and “Any sign of decay is the key risk.”

surprises.description: The preview estimated treasury value of about $5.85–6.00 per share using roughly 56.5 million shares. The reported $369.5 million fair value for digital assets, against that share count, implies about $6.54 per share—above the preview estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Its digital assets had a fair value of approximately $369.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “TAV/share is estimated at ~$5.85–6.00” and the preview cited “~56.5M shares.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed that winding down legacy VERB operations is expected to remove $4–5 million of annual operating costs, with most of the savings becoming visible in Q4. The preview discussed possible quarterly opex levels but did not flag these specific savings or their timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The wind-down of legacy VERB operations is expected to remove approximately $4-5 million of annual operating costs, with the majority of savings becoming visible in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bull” scenario: “opex below $5M/quarter”; “Base” scenario: “Print as modeled.”

surprises.description: TONX terminated its Kingsway advisory agreement on August 10 and disclosed a $2.9 million non-cash Kingsway-related Q2 charge. The preview did not mention the agreement or anticipate this charge; management said monthly payments had already stopped in March.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company terminated its advisory agreement with Kingsway Capital Partners on August 10th and had already stopped monthly payments under that agreement in March 2026”; it also absorbed “a $2.9 million non-cash Kingsway-related charge.”

in_line: The company achieved positive operating income, as the preview’s base case anticipated a first positive operating quarter; the call reported approximately $0.5 million despite the accelerated stock-compensation and Kingsway-related charges.

The preview anticipated positive GAAP results driven by a Gram fair-value gain. The call reported an $82.8 million non-cash gain and approximately $83.5 million of pretax income, though it did not provide a comparable reported EPS figure in the supplied facts.
The preview estimated approximately 230.5 million Gram holdings and about 4.08 Gram per share; the reported quarter-end holdings were approximately 230.5 million Gram, including 229.9 million staked.

surprises.description: The preview estimated Q3 revenue down about 8% year over year, but the call reported total company sales down approximately 6%. Sales therefore declined less than the preview's estimate, although the call did not provide a revenue figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total company sales fell approximately 6% for the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Estimate for Q3 FY2026: ~$40.2M (-8.0% Y/Y).”

surprises.description: The preview expected EBITDA to improve year over year, to about $1.9 million from $1.79 million. Instead, Q3 EBITDA declined $1.4 million year over year, with lower sales and gross margin not matched by lower payroll costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 EBITDA declined $1.4 million year-over-year, driven by a roughly 6.5% decrease in sales and gross margin without a corresponding reduction in payroll costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … Estimate for Q3 FY2026: ~$1.9M”; “Adj. EBITDA above the $1.79M prior-year figure … would support the margin story.”

surprises.description: The America restaurant was not fully reopened by the early-July target in the preview; it remained partially closed and was expected to fully reopen in September. That pushes the reopening later than anticipated, though the preview had expected a September consumer unveil.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The America restaurant in Las Vegas is partially closed and expected to fully reopen sometime in September.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The roughly 9,800 sq ft, $5M redesign at New York-New York targeted an early-July full reopening and a September consumer unveil.”

surprises.description: Despite New York-New York sales being down 10–11%, management said cash flow improved because of operating efficiencies. The preview discussed cost controls as a broader EBITDA support, but did not anticipate this specific improvement at New York-New York.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Despite sales being down 10-11% at New York-New York, management reported improved cash flow due to increased operating efficiencies.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a new construction deal with MGM at New York-New York, expected to start in two to three months and open early next year; the preview did not flag this project.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new construction deal at New York-New York with MGM is set to begin in 2-3 months and open in early next year.”

in_line: Las Vegas and Florida remained weak: sales were down about 11% and 10%, respectively, matching the regional declines cited in the preview as the recent trend.
The Meadowlands referendum was excluded from this year's ballot, consistent with the preview's expectation that the earliest vote had shifted to next year.

The Bryant Park trial being expected early next year is consistent with the preview's late-2026-or-early-2027 timing; the preview had already noted Ark's win on the breach claim with damages to be set at trial.

surprises.description: Q2 net sales were $383.3 million, below the preview’s $394.9 million consensus (and its alternate estimate of about $397 million). The roughly 3% shortfall came despite the preview’s expectation of a less severe decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales fell 9.7% year-over-year to $383.3 million,” primarily due to divestitures that contributed about $68 million in Q2 2025.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $394.9M (Defense World) or ~$397M (StockStory, implied from −6.4% Y/Y).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $60.4 million, above the preview’s derived $56–58 million range and the $58 million level it highlighted as a key threshold. The 15.8% margin also exceeded the prior-year 13.7%, with acquisitions and tariff refunds cited as support.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $60.4 million (15.8% of net sales) from $58 million (13.7%) a year earlier,” aided by higher-margin Collagen and Kitchen Basics acquisitions and U.S. government tariff refunds.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA vs. $56–58M (my derived range, not a Street figure)” and “Adj. EBITDA at or above $58M. This is the number to trade.”

surprises.description: Base-business sales fell 2.9%, rather than holding flat or better as the preview identified as the level that would beat management’s outlook. The quarter’s volume decline outweighed positive pricing and mix, although year-to-date base-business sales were essentially flat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Base business net sales declined 2.9% to $346.3 million as a 4.3% volume drop outweighed a 1.4% gain in pricing/mix,” while year-to-date base-business sales were essentially flat.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base business net sales. Management guided flat to slightly down, so flat or better would beat its own bar.”

surprises.description: The company reported substantial tariff refunds in Q2, recovering most of the tariffs for which it was importer of record, with more modest refunds expected in the second half. The preview flagged tariffs as a potential pressure but did not anticipate refunds providing a benefit to results.
surprises.fact_evidence: Total incremental tariff exposure was estimated at $8–$9 million; the company was importer of record for less than half and “recovered most of that in Q2,” with additional modest refunds expected in the second half.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Soybean oil costs” and described the bear scenario as “Oil and tariffs outrun pricing.”

surprises.description: A contract-manufacturing business for Green Giant U.S. Frozen generated $23.9 million in its first full quarter and was modestly profitable, running at roughly $100 million annualized—an operating stream the preview did not mention.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new Green Giant U.S. Frozen contract manufacturing business generated $23.9 million in its first full quarter and is modestly profitable, running at roughly $100 million annualized.”

surprises.description: The board appointed Rob Mills CEO, with his first earnings-call appearance scheduled for November. The preview did not flag a CEO change or leadership transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Board member Rob Mills was appointed CEO and will join the Q3 earnings call in November,” bringing digital, AI, M&A and P&L experience from Tractor Supply Company.

surprises.description: The Green Giant Canada divestiture had not yet closed and would remain in reported financials and guidance until closing. The preview specifically listed confirming the close as a catalyst; the call also indicated likely proceeds near $60 million, well above the $32 million held-for-sale carrying value.
surprises.fact_evidence: The pending divestiture was “expected to close in Q3” and “remains in company financials and guidance until closing, with proceeds likely near the ~$60 million level rather than the ~$32 million held-for-sale carrying value.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Green Giant Canada close and capital allocation. Confirm the close and use of proceeds.”

surprises.description: Net interest expense rose 7.5%, partly because the refinancing created a 24-day period of paying interest on both the new 11% notes and the 5.25% notes. This temporary overlapping-interest cost was not noted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net interest expense rose 7.5% to $38.5 million,” partly due to a “24-day overlap during refinancing” when the company paid interest on both sets of notes.

surprises.description: SG&A declined 14%, and management said further reductions would continue into early Q3 to eliminate stranded costs before reaching a stable run rate. The preview did not anticipate these cost reductions or their continuation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A fell 14% to $40.6 million (10.6% of sales) with further reductions expected into early Q3 to eliminate stranded costs before reaching a stable run rate.”

in_line: FY2026 net sales, adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS guidance was reaffirmed at the same ranges stated in the preview.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $14.9 million, about $1.1 million above the preview’s roughly $13.8 million consensus estimate. It was also roughly flat year over year rather than the approximately 10% decline implied by the preview’s consensus comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $14.9 million, roughly flat versus $15.3 million in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue … Consensus ~$13.8M”; the preview also said this “implies roughly −10% Y/Y revenue at consensus.”

surprises.description: The net loss was about $12 million, narrower than the approximately $13 million loss implied by the preview’s Q2 EPS estimate. R&D and SG&A were also lower year over year, which management attributed to reduced headcount and cost controls.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed to $12 million from $13.3 million a year earlier”; “R&D expenses fell to $11.7 million (from $13.8 million) and SG&A dropped to $10.9 million (from $12.3 million), reflecting reduced headcount and cost controls.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 EPS consensus was “~$(0.12),” which the preview said “Implies ~$13M net loss.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year 2026 gross-margin guidance to the high 60s after Q2 product gross margin reached 73%. The preview gave no full-year gross-margin expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Product gross margin reached 73% in Q2 2026, up from Q1 and full-year 2025, prompting management to raise full-year 2026 gross margin guidance to the high 60s.”

surprises.description: The financing was already expected to close, but the reported cash runway now extends through 2028—beyond the preview’s expectation that cash would fund operations through the end of 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $25 million net equity financing closed two weeks before the call, lifting pro forma cash to approximately $79.8 million and extending the cash runway through 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had stated cash would “fund operations through end-2027” and noted the offering was expected to close around July 27.

surprises.description: The most advanced of three CDMO partners has completed its assessment and entered long-term commercial contract negotiations, with a conclusion expected soon. That is more concrete progress toward a paid commercial conversion than the preview’s year-end partnership goal, though no contract has yet been signed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Of three CDMO partners that have completed small-scale technology transfers, the most advanced has finished its assessment and is now in long-term commercial contract negotiations expected to wrap up soon.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the market would want “paid conversions” and cited a “goal of one more strategic partnership by end-2026.”

surprises.description: The biocatalysis business reported four product approvals in 2026 plus a label expansion, ending a multi-year drought of new approvals. The preview did not flag these approvals as an expected development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The biocatalysis business supports 14 commercial products, including four that received approval in 2026 plus one label expansion, ending a multi-year drought of new approvals.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a substantial clinical pipeline—15 Phase 2 or 3 programs, with seven trial readouts expected over two years—and tied it to projected high-single-digit growth over five to seven years. The preview did not discuss this pipeline or growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The clinical pipeline includes 15 programs in Phase 2 or 3 development with data readouts expected on seven trials over the next two years, supporting projected high-single-digit growth over five to seven years.”

surprises.description: Management added a forecast of a sharp future siRNA manufacturing bottleneck and said Ecosynthesis is roughly 70% more capital efficient than solid-phase synthesis; it also set a kilo-scale target before GMP launch. The preview already identified the half-kilo year-end target, but did not anticipate these additional claims and milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects siRNA demand to grow 30-fold by 2035, projects a manufacturing bottleneck within three years, and claims Ecosynthesis is roughly 70% more capital efficient than solid-phase synthesis, targeting half-kilo scale by year-end and kilo scale before GMP launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “0.5 kg production by year-end” target, but no kilo-scale target or demand and efficiency projections.

in_line: Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $72–76 million, the preview’s base case; the preview also expected the year to be heavily weighted to the second half.

surprises.description: The preview cited Q2 revenue consensus of $23.03 million and expected a miss, but reported revenue was only $7.9 million—below even the preview’s $8–11 million bear-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue fell approximately 25% year-over-year to $7.9 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $23.03M”; the preview also said a miss “looks likely” and gave a bear scenario of “$8–11M.”

surprises.description: Management cut 2026 revenue guidance to $60–75 million from the previously reaffirmed roughly $125 million. The preview focused on delivery and feedstock delays as risks, while management attributed the reduction entirely to lower antimony prices.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management lowered full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $60 million-$75 million, attributing the reduction entirely to lower antimony prices rather than delivery delays.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance | ~$125M revenue (reaffirmed at Q1, May 2026)”; the preview called the main question whether “the $125M guide survives the call.”

surprises.description: Gross margin fell to 7%, rather than holding near Q1’s 16% level that the preview identified as a possible trough. Antimony prices fell much faster than unit costs, worsening the margin pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Antimony average selling prices dropped roughly 52% year-over-year to $13.70 per pound … while average cost per pound fell only 33% to $13.34, compressing gross margin to 7% from 27% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether 16% is the trough.”

surprises.description: The first DLA shipment was physically delivered in June, but government acceptance did not come until July, pushing roughly $2.6 million of recognition into Q3 instead of Q2. The preview had cited roughly $2.6 million invoiced in June.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The first two DLA shipments (~82,000 pounds, ~$2.6 million) were delivered in June but only accepted in July, pushing recognition into Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the company had disclosed “Q2 DLA deliveries of about 82,000 lbs and roughly $2.6M invoiced in June.”

surprises.description: Despite the revenue decline, antimony pounds sold rose 26% and zeolite revenue rose 110% as zeolite tons sold increased 114%. The preview highlighted timing and pricing risks but did not anticipate this strength in sales volumes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Antimony pounds sold rose 26% year-over-year to 428,425 pounds and zeolite revenue grew 110% to $1.9 million on a 114% increase in tons sold.”

surprises.description: The company reported about $0.1 million of net income despite a roughly $7 million operating loss, because a large unrealized gain on its Larvotto investment offset the operating loss. This made the small profit dependent on an investment mark rather than operating performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company posted an operating loss of about $7 million … but reported positive net income of about $0.1 million thanks to a $6.8 million unrealized gain on its Larvotto Resources investment.”

surprises.description: Management said it deliberately built inventory to $21.6 million, using $20.7 million of cash in operations, to stockpile low-cost feedstock for DLA and commercial demand. The preview emphasized liquidity and feedstock delays but did not flag this sizable inventory build and operating cash use.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory built intentionally to $21.6 million from $6.4 million a year earlier, driving $20.7 million of cash used in operations, as the company stockpiles low-cost feedstock for DLA and commercial demand.”

surprises.description: The DLA delivery outlook included a notable schedule positive: cumulative orders reached about $57.3 million, and the first $9.9 million delivery order is expected to be completed nearly a year early. The preview identified the undelivered contract backlog as an offset but did not cite this accelerated completion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cumulative orders under the $245 million sole-source DLA contract now total approximately $57.3 million, with the first $9.9 million delivery order expected to complete nearly a year ahead of schedule.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “undelivered DLA backlog of about $54.7M” and called for “a dated 2H DLA shipment schedule against the $54.7M backlog.”

surprises.description: IMUNON said its $6.9 million cash balance funds operations only through year-end and that it needs more capital to complete the Phase 3 trial and support G&A. The preview’s base case anticipated cash bridging the company toward a partnership, so the explicit near-term funding need sharpens the financing risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “only $6.9 million in cash and cash equivalents as of June 30, 2026,” providing a runway “only through the end of the year”; management “will need additional capital to fully execute the Phase 3 trial and support G&A needs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario anticipated “financing bridges to a partnership with no date”; the preview also identified a “further reverse split or dilutive raise” as a bear-case risk.

surprises.description: Final Ovation 2 data showed a 14.7-month median overall-survival improvement in the all-comers population and a 24.2-month improvement among patients receiving PARP inhibitor maintenance. The preview did not flag these final survival results, so they were an unanticipated positive clinical update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “14.7-month improvement in median overall survival (45.1 vs 30.4 months)” overall and “24.2-month improvement (65.6 vs 41.4 months)” among patients receiving PARP inhibitor maintenance.

surprises.description: Ovation 3 enrollment was running at about 0.5 patients per site per month, above the trial’s planned 0.3 rate and the historical 0.2 rate. That is better than the preview’s stated enrollment assumption and gives a more favorable enrollment-rate update than the preview’s site-status discussion alone conveyed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “enrolling approximately 0.5 patients per site per month, exceeding the planned assumption of 0.3 and far above the historical ovarian cancer rate of 0.2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the Q1 call targeted “~80 patients by Q1 2027 toward ~500 total” and called for testing progress against that target.

surprises.description: The Phase 2 MRD trial reported favorable results on several measures: lower MRD positivity, higher ctDNA clearance, and no evidence of disease in all treated patients. The preview did not anticipate or discuss these results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “lower MRD positivity (44% vs 67% control), higher ctDNA clearance (87.5% vs 62%), and 100% no-evidence-of-disease versus control.”

surprises.description: Quarterly operating cash burn was $3.0 million, down from $4.0 million in Q1, while G&A declined about 20% despite higher R&D expense. This was favorable against the preview’s focus on quarterly spending of roughly $4.5–5.0 million, though operating cash burn and total spend are not identical measures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “quarterly operating cash burn dropped to $3.0 million from $4.0 million in Q1”; R&D was “$1.5 million (from $1.2 million)” and G&A “fell about 20% to $1.3 million (from $1.6 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited guidance of “total spend of ~$4.5–5.0M per quarter” and flagged “Quarterly burn vs. the $4.5–5.0M guide.”

surprises.description: The June financing was described as having no warrants and using non-redeemable, non-convertible preferred stock alongside secured notes to minimize dilution. That is a more shareholder-protective structure than the preview’s unresolved financing terms and dilution concerns suggested, although it does not remove the need for additional capital.
surprises.fact_evidence: The financing used “non-redeemable, non-convertible preferred stock and secured promissory notes with no warrants to minimize shareholder dilution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said financing terms, including “warrant coverage” and “settlement features,” were not fully disclosed and could change the dilution picture.

surprises.description: Management said Ovation 3 interim analyses are event-driven and will begin only after full enrollment. The preview identified first-interim timing as a key catalyst, but the call’s sequencing provides no earlier interim milestone and ties analyses to completion of enrollment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Phase 3 interim analyses are event-driven and will begin only after full enrollment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “first-interim timing” among the key items to watch.

surprises.description: Across its clinical programs, IMUNON reported no cytokine release syndrome, systemic toxicities, or serious immune-related adverse events, and the IDMC found no new safety concerns. The preview did not identify safety as a specific expectation or debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “no cytokine release syndrome, no systemic toxicities, and no serious immune-related adverse events” and an “IDMC review finding no new safety concerns.”

in_line: Ovation 3’s full-enrollment target extending into the first half of 2029 is broadly consistent with the preview’s Q2 2029 completion estimate.

surprises.description: The preview’s Q2 revenue consensus was about $9.28 million, while reported revenue was $8.9 million, a modest shortfall. That result was still within the preview’s $8.9–$9.1 million base-case range; the company attributed the year-over-year decline to asset sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue declined slightly to $8.9 million from $9.0 million a year earlier due to asset sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$9.28M”; the preview’s base scenario was “$8.9–9.1M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected Q2 same-location NOI growth of about 5–7%, but NOI grew 12%—roughly double same-location revenue growth of 5.6%. This was a clear acceleration beyond the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same location NOI grew 12% year-over-year to $5.9 million”; it was “roughly double the pace of same location revenue growth of 5.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario anticipated “Same-location NOI +5–7%”; the preview also said Q2 “needs to show acceleration.”

surprises.description: The preview expected the company to narrow full-year guidance toward the low end, but management reaffirmed the existing ranges instead. That leaves the revenue range unchanged despite the preview’s concern that it would be difficult to reach.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed,” at revenue of “$35-38 million,” NOI of “$21.5-23 million,” and adjusted EBITDA of “$15-16.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A quiet narrowing toward the low end is the likely outcome”; the preview also said “Revenue of $35–38M is hard to reach.”

surprises.description: Contract parking volumes grew 12% year over year and 7% sequentially, accelerating from the 6% year-over-year growth cited for Q1. The preview highlighted the Q1 pace but did not forecast this stronger acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Contract parking volumes grew approximately 12% year-over-year and 7% sequentially, accelerating from 6% growth in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Contract parking volume about +6% YoY” in Q1.

surprises.description: The preview cited Q2 FY25 RevPAS of $212 but had no Q2 estimate; reported RevPAS was about $225, the highest second-quarter level in three years. This was stronger than the preview’s cited historical benchmark, although it did not provide a formal forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RevPAS reached approximately $225 in the quarter, the highest second-quarter level in three years, with trailing 12-month RevPAS above $200.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “RevPAS | Not found”; the preview listed Q2 FY25 actual RevPAS as “$212.”

surprises.description: The preview did not forecast utilization, but the reported trailing 12-month rate reached approximately 70%, up five percentage points year over year and the highest average quarterly utilization since the company took control of the portfolio in 2021.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Portfolio utilization on a trailing 12-month basis reached approximately 70%, up 5 percentage points from 65% a year ago,” marking “the highest average quarterly utilization since the company took control of the portfolio in 2021.”

surprises.description: The preview noted more than $30 million of asset sales but did not anticipate the reported additional debt reduction: the company paid down principal and accrued interest, taking net debt below its Q1 level. This is a positive deleveraging development, though the preview also emphasized the upcoming credit-line maturity and did not provide an update on it in the supplied call facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company paid down $3.7 million of principal and $0.8 million of accrued interest during the quarter, reducing total net debt to $197.1 million from $200 million at the end of Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “roughly $200M of notes payable” and “more than $30M of assets sold under a $100M program,” but did not state an expected Q2 debt paydown.

surprises.description: The preview noted the asset-rotation program but did not identify a further transaction pipeline of this size. Management said it was negotiating about $25 million of additional transactions, targeting sub-3% cap rates and possible closings by year-end, which could provide more asset-sale proceeds and debt repayment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is currently negotiating approximately $25 million of additional asset transactions, targeting a sub-3% cap rate with potential closings by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the “$100M” asset rotation program and said more than $30 million of assets had been sold, but did not mention about $25 million of further transactions under negotiation.

in_line: The Special Committee was actively reviewing the take-private proposal, consistent with the preview’s focus on the previously disclosed IOI and the committee process; management provided no further comment.

surprises.description: The preview expected FY26 adjusted EBITDA of roughly breakeven; GrowGeneration instead raised its full-year outlook to $2–3 million while keeping revenue guidance unchanged. That is a sizable improvement over the prior profit outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $2-3 million, up from a prior expectation of roughly breakeven, while reaffirming revenue guidance of $162-168 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA: ~Breakeven”; the preview also says management guided to “about breakeven.”

surprises.description: The preview expected proprietary-brand penetration to approach 40% before Q4. It reached 39.7% in Q2, hitting the full-year target halfway through the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Proprietary brand sales reached approximately 40% of cultivation and gardening revenue (39.7%), up from 32% a year earlier, hitting the company's full-year target halfway through the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “At 37.0% in Q1, with a target near 40% before Q4.”

surprises.description: The preview's base case put gross margin at 27–28%, while the reported 28.5% was above that range and near the preview's bull-case threshold. It was also within the company's 27–29% guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin was 28.5%, a 310 basis point sequential improvement from 25.4% and slightly above 28.3% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's base case expected “GM 27–28%”; it said the bull case required “GM ≥28.5%.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was above the preview's $42.06–$42.41 million consensus range, though still within company guidance and the preview's base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $43.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales: $42.41M (Investing.com); $42.06M (TradingKey)”; the preview's base case was “$42.5–43.5M.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag a Q3 sales decline. Management guided to $44–46 million, implying a year-over-year decline, but attributed it to unusually large durable-goods sales in Q3 2025 rather than weaker demand and expected higher margins this year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $44-46 million implies a year-over-year decline, which management attributed to unusually large durable-goods sales in Q3 2025 rather than weakening demand, expecting higher margins this year.”

surprises.description: The preview discussed second-half EBITDA but did not anticipate a tariff refund as a contributor. The expected refund is more than $2 million and is slated for Q3 recognition, providing a substantial but one-off lift to back-half EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Back-half EBITDA is being boosted by an AIPA tariff refund exceeding $2 million expected to be recognized in Q3 2026.”

surprises.description: The preview gave no operating-expense forecast, but the call reported a sharp year-over-year decline: store and other operating expenses fell about 21.9%, and total operating expenses fell 13.1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Store and other operating expenses fell approximately 21.9% year-over-year to $6.1 million and total operating expenses declined 13.1% to $14.7 million.”

surprises.description: The preview said storage near $8.5 million would be needed in its segment scenario. MMI Storage Solutions reported $8.3 million, a slight shortfall against that level, although revenue still increased from a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The MMI storage solutions segment generated $8.3 million in revenue, up from $8.1 million a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “To reach $43M with storage near $8.5M, Cultivation & Gardening must grow about 4.9%.”

surprises.description: Q2 diluted EPS was one cent better than the preview's consensus estimate of a $0.04 loss, reversing the preview's expectation that EPS was more likely to be a penny light.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss narrowed to $2 million (-$0.03 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted): –$0.04”; the preview said “the most likely outcome is revenue in line or above with EPS a penny light.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA returned to positive territory at $0.3 million, consistent with the preview's expectation that Q2 would “return to positive”; the preview did not provide an expected amount.
FY26 revenue guidance of $162–168 million was reaffirmed, as the preview expected.
Cash and marketable securities were about $41 million with no debt, essentially consistent with the preview's $41.1 million cash-and-securities figure and no-funded-debt position.
The buyback was active: the preview flagged repurchases as a capital-allocation item to watch and included an active buyback in its bull scenario; the call reported 700,000 shares repurchased.

surprises.description: The preview estimated June-end cash and securities at $190–200 million and expected runway into 1H 2028. Absci reported $201.1 million and runway into 2H 2028, slightly above the cash estimate and extending the runway beyond the preview’s stated horizon.
surprises.fact_evidence: Cash, equivalents, and marketable securities were $201.1 million as of June 30, 2026; the balance sheet “extends the company's operating runway into the second half of 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2-end cash of “$190–200M” and listed the existing runway as “into 1H 2028.”

surprises.description: The preview noted positive interim Phase 1 data but did not describe the drug’s half-life or dosing implications. Absci reported an estimated half-life of at least 65 days, supporting a potential regimen of only 2 to 3 injections over six months.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Interim Phase 1 data showed ABS-201 was well tolerated with a half-life estimated at least 65 days,” supporting “2 to 3 injections over a 6-month period.”

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate a receptor-occupancy comparison. New modeling suggests ABS-201 could achieve greater than 90% prolactin receptor occupancy with 2 to 3 doses over six months, while management said competitor HMI-115 reached only 60–70%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New modeling suggests 2 to 3 doses over 6 months can achieve greater than 90% prolactin receptor occupancy,” which management believes is the key efficacy driver that HMI-115 “failed to reach (oscillating at only 60-70%).”

surprises.description: The preview described Lilly’s $40 million investment as equity without option rights and said a collaboration hint would be an upgrade. The call disclosed that Lilly will also place a representative on Absci’s Endometriosis Advisory Board, while confirming that Lilly receives no rights to ABS-201.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Eli Lilly partnership does not confer any rights to ABS-201,” though “Lilly will place a representative on Absci's Endometriosis Advisory Board.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the $40 million was “an equity investment, not a partnership with option rights” and that “Any collaboration hint would be a meaningful upgrade.”

surprises.description: The preview expected a Q4 2026 start for the endometriosis Phase 2 study but did not give a potential readout window. Absci now anticipates a potential proof-of-concept readout in 2H 2027, adding a more specific catalyst horizon.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A Phase 2 endometriosis study is anticipated to begin in Q4 2026, with a potential proof-of-concept readout in the second half of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Phase 2 endometriosis start: Q4 2026” but gave no endometriosis readout timing.

surprises.description: Absci changed the lead indication’s name from androgenetic alopecia to Pattern Hair Loss, a framing not anticipated in the preview. The company said the underlying indication and market estimates are unchanged, so the disclosure does not represent a change in the development program.
surprises.fact_evidence: Absci “renamed its lead indication from androgenetic alopecia to Pattern Hair Loss” and said this was “without changing the underlying indication or market opportunity estimates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview referred to ABS-201 as targeting “androgenetic alopecia.”

in_line: The ABS-201 interim 13-week Pattern Hair Loss proof-of-concept readout remained expected in 2H 2026, and the full 26-week readout remained expected in early 2027.
The endometriosis Phase 2 study remained on track to begin in Q4 2026.

surprises.description: The preview expected EPS of about -$0.13, with its base case at -$0.12 to -$0.15, but INUV reported a $0.27-per-share loss. The loss included $870,000 of debt-extinguishment expense and $470,000 of severance charges, neither flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net loss widened to $4 million ($0.27 per share) versus a $1.5 million loss ($0.10 per share) a year ago, partly due to an $870,000 charge from debt extinguishment and a $470,000 severance charge.
surprises.expectation_evidence: EPS (diluted) Q2'26 Consensus: -$0.13; Base scenario: EPS -$0.12 to -$0.15.

surprises.description: The preview noted the $12.97 million financing and expected to assess pro-forma liquidity, but reported quarter-end cash was only $886,000; another $6.2 million was restricted, and the restricted B note remained undrawn pending redemption-related milestones. The financing proceeds had also been used to repay the convertible note and receivables-based facility, leaving much less immediately available cash than the headline raise might suggest.
surprises.fact_evidence: Inuvo ended the quarter with only $886,000 in cash plus $6.2 million in restricted cash, with the restricted B note (at 5%) still undrawn and its release tied to milestones around redemptions. The company raised $13 million gross ... using proceeds to repay its convertible note and receivables-based credit facility.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The $12.97M financing was announced June 30 and the equity leg closed about July 1, so the June 30 balance sheet may not reflect most of it. Watch cash, pro-forma liquidity, and any breakeven timeline.

surprises.description: The preview's base case put gross margin at 45–48%, against Q1's 46.2%; INUV reported 44%, below that range. The mix shift toward lower-margin audience modeling as legacy search contracted explains the shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin compressed sharply to 44% from 75% a year ago, reflecting the shift in revenue mix as high-margin legacy search contracted and lower-gross-margin audience modeling grew.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base scenario: GM 45–48%. The preview also flagged gross margin versus 46.2% as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate the scale of the workforce and expense reductions: headcount fell from 82 to 51 and operating expenses dropped 67% year over year. The lower cost base is favorable, although the cuts were mostly in legacy search and did not prevent a larger net loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: Headcount was cut to 51 employees as of June 30 from 82 a year earlier, mostly from legacy search, driving operating expenses down 67% ($12.8 million) year-over-year to $6.4 million.

surprises.description: The preview said a dated path to breakeven would be positive and its base case anticipated no breakeven date. Management instead gave a target: IntentKey could become cash-neutral to cash-positive at mid-$20 million revenue sometime in 2027, substantially lower than the prior roughly $100 million breakeven level tied to legacy search.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects IntentKey to reach cash-neutral to cash-positive in the mid-$20 million revenue range, targeting that milestone sometime in 2027, a recalibration from the prior ~$100 million breakeven driven by legacy search.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Any dated path-to-breakeven commentary would be a positive. Base scenario: no breakeven date.

surprises.description: The preview flagged new logos as a key watch item but did not anticipate five new brand-direct relationships or two Fortune 500 pilots. That is more specific and substantial customer-win news than the preview's general expectation of watching for new logos.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company signed five new brand-direct relationships in Q2 (including two Fortune 500 pilots).
surprises.expectation_evidence: New logos and the government contract: management flagged a government contract due 'in the weeks ahead.'

surprises.description: The preview did not flag the Ranger QA tool for sale; INUV reported a $450,000 sale in July, providing an unanticipated source of proceeds.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ... sold its Ranger QA tool for $450,000 in July.

surprises.description: The preview did not mention CFO Wally Ruiz's retirement or the appointment of Derric Ciccone as President and CFO. The experienced replacement is a positive element, but the transition makes the news mixed overall.
surprises.fact_evidence: CFO Wally Ruiz is retiring after 16 years, with industry veteran Derric Ciccone (former Global CFO/COO of Omnicom's Commerce Group) joining as President and CFO on August 17.

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate IntentKey's planned expansion into workforce recruitment and health insurance open enrollment. These are new potential markets, though the call facts do not quantify revenue from them.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company is expanding IntentKey into workforce recruitment and a $150 billion health insurance open-enrollment market.

in_line: Revenue of $7.5 million was slightly below the $7.76 million consensus estimate, but was within the preview's $7.4–$8.2 million base-case range and close to its expected post-reset level.
IntentKey revenue grew 19%, within the preview's 15–20% base-case range and consistent with its expectation of strong double-digit growth.
Legacy search revenue was roughly $4 million, in line with the preview's expected sequential floor near $4 million.

surprises.description: Mineralys reported market research showing physicians prefer lorundrostat’s profile over baxdrostat by roughly 2:1. The preview flagged baxdrostat as a competitive issue but did not anticipate this favorable preference finding.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management cited market research showing roughly a 2:1 physician preference for lorundrostat's profile over competitor baxdrostat based on comparable BAX-HTN and Launch-HTN trials.

surprises.description: The call cited specific CKD differentiation not detailed in the preview: a 52% placebo-adjusted reduction in urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio among patients with baseline albuminuria, and Explore-CKD data extending to eGFR 30 versus baxdrostat’s label down to 45.
surprises.fact_evidence: Lorundrostat achieved a 52% placebo-adjusted reduction in urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio in patients with baseline albuminuria, and Explore-CKD extended data down to eGFR of 30 versus baxdrostat's label to 45.

surprises.description: The preview described the Tanabe repurchase as involving up to $100 million in milestones, while the call put aggregate potential future milestone payments to Tanabe at up to $265 million. That indicates a larger total contingent payment exposure than the preview’s stated buyback milestone amount, though the payments are not guaranteed.
surprises.fact_evidence: Mineralys agreed to repurchase future royalties from Tanabe for $200 million upfront plus up to $100 million in commercial milestones, with aggregate potential future milestone payments to Tanabe now up to $265 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$200M upfront plus up to $100M in milestones”

in_line: The $200 million Tanabe upfront payment drove a Q2 net loss of $241.1 million, close to the preview’s approximately $247 million loss scenario if the payment was expensed; the preview explicitly flagged this accounting risk.

Cash and investments were $661.4 million, within the preview’s $620–670 million range and above its roughly $640 million estimate; management still expects the funds to support operations, including launch, into 2028.
G&A was $24.7 million, just below the preview’s $25 million restraint threshold and below its $28 million base-case estimate.

Management said observed baxdrostat payer rebates were consistent with its expectations and expects parity access for lorundrostat, in line with the preview’s focus on payer coverage; pricing remains undisclosed, as the preview anticipated it might until approval or launch.

surprises.description: The preview put Q2 revenue consensus at $42.6 million; Evolv reported $43.8 million, a modest beat of about 3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 34% year-over-year to $43.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $42.6M (5 analysts)”

surprises.description: The preview expected the $175–180 million full-year revenue range to be reaffirmed, but Evolv raised it to $180–185 million. The bottom of the range increased by $5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Evolv raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $180-185 million … from prior $175-180 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: Results land where guided. The FY range is reaffirmed”; prior guidance was “FY2026 revenue $175–180M.”

surprises.description: Ending ARR was just below the preview’s estimated range and its roughly $133 million checkpoint, though the gap was slight; ARR growth itself matched the preview’s expected growth rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Annual recurring revenue reached $132.7 million, up 20% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Ending ARR | ~$133–135M”; the preview said it “needs to be at least about $133M.”

surprises.description: Evolv raised the low end of its year-end ARR guidance by $3 million, while leaving the high end unchanged. The preview had identified an ARR-guidance raise as an important positive outcome, rather than expecting the range to stay unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised year-end ARR guidance to $148-150 million …”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior guidance was “FY2026 ending ARR $145–150M”; the preview said “an ARR guide raise is worth far more than a revenue-only raise.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin was stronger than the preview’s estimated $3–4 million of adjusted EBITDA: a 10.1% margin on $43.8 million of revenue implies roughly $4.4 million. The full-year $15–16 million outlook, however, was within the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 10.1% in Q2 from 6.5% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$3–4M”; the preview also estimated “about $14–16M” for full-year adjusted EBITDA.

surprises.description: Purchase subscriptions were expected to be about 55% of the year’s mix, but Evolv now expects 60% of new full-year deployed units through that channel. The company also cited refurbishment and supply-chain costs as additional gross-margin headwinds, beyond the mix pressure the preview had highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now forecasts 60% of new full-year deployed units via purchase subscription (up from 55% prior)”; “roughly 2.5 points of combined 2026 headwinds,” including Gen1 refurbishment costs and higher component/supply-chain costs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The company guided about 55/45 for the year”; the preview warned that “a further shift toward purchase-subscription means more upfront revenue and weaker margin.”

surprises.description: The preview did not discuss RPO, while Evolv reported $312.6 million of RPO, up 4.5% sequentially and more than 1.7 times full-year revenue guidance. Management also estimated its gross margin at about 66%, well above the current reported 51%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Remaining performance obligation grew 4.5% sequentially to $312.6 million, exceeds 1.7x full-year revenue guidance, and carries an estimated ~66% gross margin versus current 51% reported gross margin.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged eXpedite adoption and monetization as issues to watch. Evolv reported adoption above 100 customers, about 8% of its base, and plans to raise prices to bring eXpedite ARPU closer to Express; the preview had cited 75+ customers and about 6% of the base and did not mention planned price increases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “eXpedite adoption expanded to over 100 customers (~8% of base, up from 2% a year ago)”; “price increases planned to align eXpedite ARPU closer to Express.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “eXpedite reached 75+ customers, about 6% of the base”; the preview listed “eXpedite attach and SAFETY Act monetization” as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: The preview’s bear case contemplated declining new-logo additions, but Evolv reported 70 new customers and called it its strongest quarter for additions in two years. About 60% of unit bookings also came from existing customers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company added 70 new customers, its strongest quarter for additions in two years, with roughly 60% of unit bookings coming from existing customers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bear scenario said, “New logo adds decline.”

in_line: ARR growth was 20% year-over-year, in line with the preview’s estimated 20–22% growth, despite ending ARR coming in just below its estimated dollar range.
The full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook of $15–16 million was within the preview’s estimate of roughly $14–16 million and was consistent with its expectation of a high-single-digit margin.
Q2 revenue declined sequentially from Q1’s $46.3 million, as the preview said management had pre-announced a sequential decline tied to purchase-subscription backlog timing.

surprises.description: RideNow reported Q2 revenue of $296.8 million, well below the preview’s $321–330 million working range. The company attributed the decline from a year earlier partly to operating five fewer stores, but that does not close the gap to the expected revenue level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 revenue declined slightly to $296.8 million from $299.9 million, primarily due to operating five fewer stores following consolidation efforts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $329.9M (high read) / $321.0M (low read)” and “I would treat $330M / $0.13 as the working number.”

surprises.description: Retail unit results were much weaker than the preview’s base-case volume assumption: new retail units grew only 1.8%, while pre-owned units fell 6.8%. The preview’s base scenario assumed units would grow 8–12%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New retail unit sales grew 1.8% to 10,807 units” and “pre-owned retail units fell 6.8% to 4,924.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “Units +8–12%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA came in above the preview’s modeled $17–19 million range, reaching $20.5 million. That is a positive result, though below the preview’s roughly $22 million bull-case level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 19.2% year-over-year to $20.5 million in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | No published consensus” and “my framework bar is $17–19M (modeled, not consensus).”

surprises.description: Adjusted SG&A was substantially lower as a share of gross profit than the preview’s already-positive threshold: 74.1% versus the preview’s 82% benchmark. Expenses also fell year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted SG&A improved to 74.1% of gross profit (down from 77.4%),” with expenses of “$62.8 million versus $64.9 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SG&A below about 82% of gross profit would be a clear positive.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for positive Q2 free cash flow after the Q1 outflow, but the call did not provide a standalone Q2 figure. It reported strong first-half adjusted free cash flow while also reporting a first-half operating cash outflow, leaving the cash-flow evidence mixed rather than a clear confirmation of the expected Q2 reversal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow for the first six months surged to $20.8 million from $2.9 million” while “operating activities showed a cash outflow of $28.2 million for the six months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 should reverse Q1’s -$28.2M” and “Negative FCF in the peak quarter would undercut the 2026 FCF commitment.”

surprises.description: The preview identified a refinancing announcement as a major catalyst, but management said refinancing was only nearing completion, with details expected in coming weeks. The expected announcement had not yet materialized.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Refinancing efforts are nearing completion with more details expected in coming weeks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “An announced refi” as a bull-case driver and refinancing as “the largest non-P&L catalyst.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that current-quarter same-store sales were already down slightly in the low single digits year over year, signaling a softer near-term trend after the reported first-half growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Current-quarter same-store sales are down slightly in the low single digits year-over-year amid market volatility.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was a substantially larger loss than the preview’s expected range: negative $0.6 million, versus a base case of negative $0.15 million to positive $0.05 million. Management still expects to reach positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4, but Q2 was not the positive quarter the preview identified as a key narrative event.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was negative $0.6 million in Q2 2026 versus negative $0.4 million a year ago,” and management “reaffirmed its goal of reaching positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base” adjusted EBITDA: “–$0.15M to +$0.05M”; a second positive quarter would be “the key narrative event.”
