surprises.description: Managed IT, IPM’s core recurring line, grew only about 8%, well below the preview’s expected 16–19% range and its stated threshold that growth below 15% would weaken the thesis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recurring managed IT technology revenue, the company's core, grew about 8% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “Managed IT +16–19%”; the preview said “Growth below +15% Y/Y would weaken the thesis.”

surprises.description: Procurement revenue surged rather than remaining flat to down as the preview’s base case anticipated. The sales upside came from AI-related hardware and infrastructure, but management noted the line is lower-margin and project-based, making the mix less favorable than the headline growth suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Procurement revenue jumped 64% year-over-year to $2 million in Q2,” driven by AI-related sales, but “carries lower margins and is project-based.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “procurement flat to down”; the preview also warned that “Hardware pass-through carries lower margin.”

surprises.description: Deferred revenue was $4.5 million, below the $4.7 million Q1 level the preview used as its benchmark, rather than showing the sequential growth that the preview said would support the pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended the quarter with “$4.5 million in deferred revenue (up $0.6 million from year-end 2025).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Deferred revenue vs. $4.7M” and said “Sequential growth supports the new-business pipeline. A decline would point to a slowing funnel.”

surprises.description: A large customer order incurred enough extra component and freight cost to become loss-making, compressing margins. The preview identified gross margin and procurement mix as key issues, but did not anticipate an outright loss on a specific order.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A single large customer order fulfilled across two reporting periods incurred higher component and freight costs, producing an outright loss on that order that compressed margins.”

surprises.description: Component shortages delayed shipments and pushed some booked orders into future quarters, so those orders did not contribute revenue in Q2. The preview discussed revenue and segment scenarios but did not flag supply constraints as a risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Supply chain constraints on memory, CPU and GPU components delayed shipments, leaving a portion of booked orders unrecognized as revenue and pushed into future quarters.”

surprises.description: The quarter still produced a substantial GAAP net loss, widening from $1.1 million to $1.4 million year over year; the first-half loss also rose sharply. This contrasts with the preview’s displayed positive EPS consensus, though the preview explicitly warned that estimate was unreliable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $1.4 million in Q2 2026 from $1.1 million a year earlier,” and the six-month net loss grew to “$2.0 million from just $0.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The consensus table showed “EPS (GAAP) $0.02”; the preview cautioned that “The $0.02 EPS estimate does not fit the trajectory” and said not to treat an EPS beat or miss as meaningful.

surprises.description: NewtekOne reduced its IT spending, creating a headwind from the related-party customer base the preview had identified as an area to watch. Growth from new non-related-party customers partly offset the decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue from related party NewtekOne declined as it cut IT spending, a headwind partially offset by growth from new non-related-party customers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Capital allocation and related-party exposure” and said to watch “the NewtekOne referral arrangement and related-party revenue concentration.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $6.5 million was slightly above the single-analyst consensus of $6.40 million, a smaller positive gap than the preview’s bull scenario but consistent with its base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose ~13% year-over-year to $6.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2'26 Consensus | $6.40M”; the base scenario was “$6.3–6.6M.”

in_line: Q2 revenue landed within the preview’s $6.3–$6.6 million base-case range, despite edging above the $6.40 million consensus estimate.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $5.5 million versus the $2.21 million consensus estimate, but the beat came from $3.8 million of ex-US license revenue, not a sharp increase in US product sales. The license revenue included first-time milestones tied to the TEA/Health Canada submission and Everest’s Greater China rights sale, contrary to the preview’s expectation that Q2 revenue would be almost entirely US product revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue was $5.5 million,” including “$3.8 million in ex-US license revenue”; that included “the first regulatory milestone from the TEA/Health Canada submission” and “the first sublicense milestone tied to Everest Medicine's asset sale of Greater China rights to Cork Cell.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” consensus was “$2.21M”; “Q2 FY2026 revenue will be almost entirely US product revenue.”

surprises.description: The reported loss per share was $1.02, less negative than the preview’s $1.21 consensus estimate. This was a better result than expected despite the quarter’s commercial launch activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss was $31.9 million ($1.02 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP)” consensus: “-$1.21.”

surprises.description: Product volume grew more slowly than the preview’s key hurdle: the company sold about 27,000 monthly packs, up 9% from Q1, versus the preview’s roughly 30,000-script threshold for acceptable growth. The reported packs and the preview’s script measure are not identical, but the disclosed sequential growth was below the preview’s approximately 20% benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over $1.7 million in product revenue (~27,000 monthly packs sold, up 9% from Q1).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A print below roughly 30,000 (+20%) would suggest the field-force and TV investment is not converting.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed encouraging repeat-purchase data even though the preview said refill rates and persistence had not been disclosed. More than 60% of e-pharmacy patients bought multiple packs, and the mature Q4 cohort had purchased slightly more than five packs on average before completing a year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “More than 60% of e-pharmacy patients who purchased VIZ since launch have bought more than one monthly pack”; the mature Q4 2025 cohort “has purchased slightly more than five monthly packs on average (before reaching a full year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The company has not disclosed patient refill rates or daily doses per patient. Any refill metric, or continued silence on it, would be informative.”

surprises.description: July prescriptions accelerated by more than 45% month over month, following the launch of telehealth prescribing and a national TV campaign that lifted all sales channels. The preview discussed whether TV and expanded selling efforts would inflect the curve, but did not anticipate this specific post-quarter growth rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “July prescriptions grew over 45% month-over-month versus June,” driven by “the concurrent launch of a telehealth prescribing option and a national TV advertising campaign that lifted all sales channels.”

surprises.description: The call described weak retail uptake and an ongoing conversion problem among prescribers despite broad physician reach and high awareness. Management is shifting toward consumer-driven demand, adding evidence that the field-force and physician-awareness approach has not produced consistent recurring prescribing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retail uptake tracked through Symphony or IQVIA has been described as poor and limited”; despite over 13,000 physicians having prescribed and more than 75% prescribing multiple times, awareness “has not translated into consistent recurring prescribing,” prompting “a pivot toward consumer-driven demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said that “a print below roughly 30,000 (+20%) would suggest the field-force and TV investment is not converting,” and that “a peak-spend commitment matters more to the Street than a revenue beat.”

surprises.description: Management introduced a plan to use Q3 results to move commercial investment toward the best-performing initiatives. The preview highlighted spending levels and a possible peak-spend commitment as key debates, but did not anticipate this specific data-driven reallocation plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management plans “to use Q3 data to reallocate commercial investment toward the highest-performing initiatives.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SG&A and whether management caps spend” was a key metric to watch; “A peak-spend commitment matters more to the Street than a revenue beat.”

surprises.description: Management said gross margins are expected to trend toward approximately 90% over time, a margin outlook not identified in the preview’s expectations or watch list.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margins are expected to trend toward approximately 90% over time.”

surprises.description: NeuroPace reported Q2 revenue of $22.8 million, modestly above the $22.6 million consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $22.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $22.6M.”

surprises.description: RNS revenue grew 21.3%, considerably faster than the preview’s estimate that consensus implied about 16% underlying Q2 growth. This was also above the preview’s stated 20% threshold for a solid result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RNS System revenue of $22.5 million growing 21.3% versus the prior year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus implies about 16% underlying growth in Q2”; the preview also says “20% or better is needed.”

surprises.description: The FDA’s IGE questions concerned the clinical-benefit context and requested additional clinical evidence, keeping the approval path uncertain despite a strong reported seizure-reduction result. The questions were not about safety.
surprises.fact_evidence: The FDA requested “additional clinical evidence”; the 24-month data showed “a 100% median reduction in generalized tonic-clonic (GTC) seizures among evaluable patients,” and the questions were “about clinical benefit context, not safety.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NAUTILUS missed its primary effectiveness endpoint, so the path forward is uncertain”; the preview also says “New clinical data would be negative.”

surprises.description: Management said the FDA may review the IGE amendment without restarting the full 180-day clock, a potentially faster path than the preview’s uncertain-timeline framing. The FDA retains discretion, so this is not assured.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “anticipates the amendment may be reviewed without resetting the full 180-day clock, though the FDA retains discretion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the IGE path as uncertain and asked investors to “confirm the SIR filing status and any FDA timeline commentary.”

surprises.description: The company raised full-year revenue guidance by $0.5 million at both ends, rather than merely reaffirming the prior range. The increase came entirely from expected service revenue; underlying RNS growth guidance did not change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 total revenue guidance was raised to $99.5–$101.5 million (from $99–$101 million), driven entirely by higher expected service revenue of ~$1 million; underlying RNS revenue growth guidance remains 21%–23%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 revenue guide of $99–101M. Whether $99–101M is reaffirmed or trimmed.”

surprises.description: NeuroPace improved its full-year adjusted EBITDA loss outlook by $1 million at both ends, from $8.5–$9.5 million to $7.5–$8.5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA loss guidance improved to $7.5–$8.5 million (from $8.5–$9.5 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA loss $8.5–9.5M.”

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted gross margin range moved up by 50 basis points at both ends, above the preview’s expected range and its focus on whether roughly 82% would hold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin guidance was raised to 82%–83% (from 81.5%–82.5%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin durability at ~82%”; the preview’s May guidance figures were “81.5%–82.5%.”

surprises.description: NeuroPace launched ECOG Assistant, an AI tool built on more than 27 million intracranial EEG recordings, a product milestone the preview did not flag. It is bundled with the RNS system rather than sold separately, so no separate revenue contribution was announced.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NeuroPace launched ECOG Assistant, its first AI tool built on a proprietary dataset of over 27 million intracranial EEG recordings,” and it “is bundled into the RNS system rather than monetized separately.”

surprises.description: Management introduced a target of reaching cash flow breakeven exiting 2027; the preview discussed liquidity and the covenant but gave no breakeven target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Targets cash flow breakeven exiting 2027.”

surprises.description: Management said it expects to submit its remote-care offering to the FDA by the end of 2026, a regulatory milestone and timeline not mentioned in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Remote care is expected to be submitted to the FDA by end of 2026.”

in_line: Underlying RNS revenue growth guidance remained at 21%–23%, consistent with the preview’s stated FY2026 guidance.
Management expects the SIR meeting in the coming weeks, in line with the preview’s reference to a planned Submission Issue Request in the coming weeks.
The implied second-half RNS growth range of roughly 20%–25% broadly matches the preview’s expected 21%–25% H2 bridge; management also expects about 20% growth in Q3.

surprises.description: NRGV reported Q2 revenue of $17.4 million, about 23% above the preview's roughly $14.2 million consensus estimate. This was a clear positive revenue surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $17.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue … ~$14.2M.”

surprises.description: NRGV raised FY26 revenue guidance to $270–310 million from $225–300 million, above the preview's $253.5 million consensus and lifting both ends of the range. The upper bound also exceeds the preview's bull-case threshold of $300 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $270–310 million from the prior $225–300 million range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue … $225–300M … Consensus … $253.5M”; the bull scenario anticipated guidance “raised above $300M.”

surprises.description: FY26 GAAP gross-margin guidance was tightened upward to 20–25% from 15–25%, while Q2 GAAP gross margin was 31% and adjusted gross margin was 38.6%. That is stronger than the preview's concern about margins being at the low end and weakening the scale-into-profitability story.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 GAAP gross margin guidance was narrowed to 20–25% from 15–25%”; Q2 GAAP gross margin was “31%” and adjusted gross margin “38.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Margins at the low end while revenue lags would weaken the scale-into-profitability story.”

surprises.description: NRGV's reported loss per share was $0.17, wider than the preview's consensus loss estimates of $0.13–$0.14 per share. The GAAP net loss narrowed year over year, but the per-share result still missed the stated expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 GAAP net loss narrowed to $29.7 million (loss of $0.17 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 EPS … –$0.13”; alternate estimates were “–$0.14” and “–$0.13.”

surprises.description: Although the backlog reached the preview's roughly $2.0 billion threshold, its reported mix was 60% build-own-operate, down from the preview's cited prior-quarter mix of more than 80% own-and-operate. The larger build-and-transfer share is a less recurring mix than that prior baseline suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “60% tied to build-own-operate recurring revenue and 40% to near-term build-and-transfer projects.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Q1 backlog as “more than 80% now own-and-operate (IPP)” and said to “watch the split between contracted backlog and pipeline.”

surprises.description: NRGV raised the low end of its year-end cash guidance by $10 million, to $160–200 million, and reported $148 million of cash and equivalents including restricted cash at June 30. The cash build was partly supported by an AR facility draw, a financing detail not anticipated in the preview's cash bridge discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-end 2026 cash guidance was raised to $160–200 million from $150–200 million”; total cash and equivalents including restricted cash were “$148 million” and the increase was “aided by an AR facility draw.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited year-end cash guidance of “$150–200M” and said to “watch preferred-equity draws and any equity-raise language.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $17 million despite the sharp revenue increase and stronger gross margins, with management attributing it to higher operating expenses. That is a counterpoint to the preview's scale-into-profitability framing, though it did not provide a specific Q2 EBITDA estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $17 million from $13.6 million on higher operating expenses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview referred to the “scale-into-profitability story” but gave no Q2 adjusted EBITDA estimate.

surprises.description: NRGV laid out a previously unquantified long-term ambition: roughly 5 gigawatts online and about $2 billion in annualized EBITDA by 2030, alongside a $180 million annualized recurring EBITDA target for its current controlled portfolio. The preview noted a possible shift toward recurring-EBITDA metrics but did not anticipate these targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The current 1.1 gigawatt controlled portfolio underpins a targeted $180 million in annualized recurring EBITDA”; management outlined a path to “roughly 5 gigawatts online generating approximately $2 billion in annualized EBITDA by 2030.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the new CFO “could … shift the focus to project-finance metrics such as recurring EBITDA run-rate and MW energized,” but stated no quantitative targets.

in_line: Backlog reached approximately $2 billion, meeting the preview's roughly $2.0 billion bar; the preview reserved a clear beat for $2.5 billion or more.
The 1.25 GW Texas award's revenue was expected mostly in 2027, with a portion in Q4 2026, consistent with the preview's expectation that it would be mostly a 2027 event.
Management continued to describe a back-end-loaded year, with the vast majority of second-half revenue expected in Q4, consistent with the preview's base-case framing.

surprises.description: Peraso’s gross margin was 63.7%, well above its prior “into the 50s” guidance and the preview’s 50–55% estimate. Management attributed the increase to favorable millimeter-wave mix and sales of previously written-down inventory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 63.7% in Q2 2026,” boosted by “favorable millimeter wave product mix and sales of previously written-down inventory.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 gross margin guidance was “into the 50s”; consensus was “~50–55%.”

surprises.description: Cash ended Q2 at $3.3 million, above the preview’s $1.5–2.5 million expectation. The increase was aided by $2.4 million in ATM equity-sale proceeds, so the stronger cash position came with equity issuance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash rose to approximately $3.3 million” from $2.7 million, “aided by $2.4 million in net proceeds from at-the-market equity sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “cash about $1.5–2.5M before the facility”; the preview said to watch for ATM usage.

surprises.description: Peraso reported that it had generated seven-figure revenue from its Israeli defense IFF partner, whereas the preview described drone-related news as unquantified and treated a dollar-quantified defense development as a bull-case possibility. Management also expects increasing volume as the application transitions to drone use.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Peraso has generated seven-figure revenue from its Israeli defense IFF” partner and “expects increasing volume over the coming quarters” as the application transitions to drone-based use.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said drone news was “encouraging but unquantified” and listed “a dollar-quantified defense PO” as a bull-case driver.

surprises.description: Management declined to provide quarterly guidance, despite the preview treating Q3 guidance as a key upcoming catalyst and expecting it might disappoint. The lack of an outlook leaves the near-term revenue picture less defined than the preview’s discussion of a possible flat-revenue Q3 implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management declined to provide quarterly guidance,” citing “limited near-term visibility due to irregular fixed wireless access order patterns.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview ranked “Q3 guidance” as a key metric and said K. Liu expected it “to disappoint”; its base case discussed Q3 opex against flat revenue.

surprises.description: Management said elevated DDR4/DDR5 memory prices are expected to persist into Q4, an input-cost pressure not mentioned in the preview. This adds a near-term cost concern even though Q2 gross margin came in well above expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management cited “elevated third-party memory (DDR4/DDR5) prices expected to persist into Q4.”

surprises.description: The $25 million Roth committed equity facility was reported as entered on June 30, rather than signed July 2 after quarter-end as the preview described. It had not been tapped, so the difference is the facility’s reported timing, not cash proceeds received.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company entered a $25 million committed equity facility with Roth on June 30, 2026” and “had not yet tapped it.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the facility “was signed July 2, after the June 30 quarter end.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA loss was $2.0 million, slightly better than the preview’s approximately $2.1 million expected loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was negative $2 million in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adj. EBITDA was estimated at “~$(2.1)M.”

in_line: Revenue was $1.3 million, within the preview’s $1.25–1.3 million consensus range and close to the prior-quarter guidance of approximately $1.2 million; the delayed fixed-wireless order shipment that helped drive the sequential gain was specifically anticipated as a key test.
Non-GAAP operating expenses were approximately $2.9 million, in line with the preview’s $2.9–3.0 million estimate.
The PRM2145 module was expected to be available for customer evaluation in Q4 2026, matching the preview’s stated timing.

surprises.description: H&R Block guided to fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS of $6.04–$6.24, above the $5.86 consensus, even with the effective tax rate expected to rise to about 23% from 14%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for adjusted diluted EPS of $6.04-$6.24 and an effective tax rate of approximately 23%, up from 14% in fiscal 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 initial consensus” adjusted EPS: “$5.86”; the preview also said a guide “at or above consensus despite the tax headwind” was the bull case.

surprises.description: Fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS was $5.31, above the $5.16 consensus and the company’s $5.10–$5.20 guidance range. However, a one-time IRS tax benefit added $0.65 to EPS, so the reported beat was smaller than the headline comparison suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EPS was $5.31; the $84.1 million one-time noncash tax benefit “added $0.65 to EPS.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 adjusted EPS consensus of “$5.16” and guidance of “$5.10–5.20,” and asked whether the IRS benefit was reflected in the adjusted number.

surprises.description: Fiscal 2026 revenue reached $3.95 billion, above the $3.91 billion consensus and the company’s $3.910–$3.920 billion guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: H&R Block delivered fiscal 2026 revenue of “$3.95 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 revenue consensus of “$3.91B” and company guidance of “$3.910–3.920B.”

surprises.description: Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance of $4.11–$4.16 billion was above the $4.05 billion consensus, while remaining within management’s stated 3–6% revenue-growth framework.
surprises.fact_evidence: Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for revenue of “$4.11-$4.16 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY27 revenue consensus of “$4.05B” and said a guide below the 3% growth floor would break the framework.

surprises.description: Conversion improved by a record 200 basis points and retention by 190 basis points, even though assisted market share was maintained rather than reported as gaining. The preview had raised the question of whether H&R Block would capture share after Direct File’s exit or lose ground.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Conversion improved 200 basis points this season (the largest single-year gain in company history) and retention rose 190 basis points,” while assisted category market share was maintained.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked, “Does HRB capture the Direct File exit?” and noted that Q3 market share was flat.

surprises.description: Management described industry growth as likely to be below the historical roughly 1% norm because job growth is slowing, a newly disclosed demand headwind even though H&R Block’s own revenue guide exceeded consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects “moderated industry growth below the historical ~1% norm due to slowing job growth.”

surprises.description: The share of clients in the $50,000–$200,000 household AGI range has risen from 38% to 50%, indicating a mix shift toward clients the company describes as more complex and higher-lifetime-value.
surprises.fact_evidence: The target-household share “has risen from 38% to 50%,” reflecting a shift toward “more complex, higher-lifetime-value clients.”

surprises.description: A transition to year-round office leadership and streamlined support functions triggered an $8.3 million severance charge in Q1 fiscal 2027; the preview did not flag this cost, although it is excluded from guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: The transition “triggered an $8.3 million severance charge in Q1 fiscal 2027 that is excluded from guidance.”

in_line: Fiscal 2027’s approximately 23% effective tax rate reflects the normalization the preview flagged; it is close to the roughly 24–25% rate discussed there.

The fiscal 2027 revenue guide remains within management’s 3–6% growth framework, and guided EBITDA growth is broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation that EBITDA grow about 1.5 times revenue.
Assisted market share was maintained, rather than lost, consistent with the preview’s report of flat Q3 share; assisted volume rose 2%, close to the prior quarter’s 2.1% increase.
The board raised the quarterly dividend 10% to $0.46, matching the preview’s bull-case scenario of a dividend increase of 10% or more.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $33.9 million beat the preview’s $30.5–31.7 million consensus range by roughly 7–11%, rather than landing in the $30–31.5 million base case. It was also a record quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was a record $33.9 million, up 29.9% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (Q2) … $30.5M (Zacks, Aug 2026) or $31.7M (MarketBeat, Aug 4, 2026)” and the base scenario expected “$30–31.5M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA excluding the tariff refund was $2.9 million, well above the preview’s derived $0.5–1.5 million expectation. Even without the one-time refund, profitability was substantially ahead of the anticipated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA excluding the tariff refund was a record $2.9 million, a $2.4 million increase versus prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (Q2) … Not found; derived ~$0.5–1.5M.”

surprises.description: Owlet recognized an unexpected tariff refund benefit that lifted Q2 gross margin to 64.4% and adjusted EBITDA to $6.7 million, versus the preview’s focus on gross margin above 52% and much lower quarterly EBITDA. The company also raised its full-year gross margin outlook to 53–55% and adjusted EBITDA outlook to $10.75–12.75 million, while saying the outlook increases reflect only the one-time tariff benefits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Owlet received approximately $4 million in tariff refunds, recognizing a one-time $3.5 million benefit to COGS and $3.75 million benefit to adjusted EBITDA”; Q2 gross margin “including the refund … reached 64.4%” and adjusted EBITDA “including the refund it was $6.7 million.” Full-year guidance was raised to “53–55%” gross margin and “$10.75–12.75 million” adjusted EBITDA, “reflecting only the one-time tariff benefits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$7–9M” and FY gross margin guidance of “50–52%”; its Q2 EBITDA estimate was “derived ~$0.5–1.5M.”

surprises.description: Underlying gross margin, excluding the tariff refund, was 54% and expanded 270 basis points year over year. That exceeded the preview’s 52% threshold for supporting a gross-margin guide increase, independently of the refund-driven reported margin spike.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin excluding the tariff refund was 54%, expanding 270 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Holding above 52% would support a GM guide raise,” against FY gross margin guidance of “50–52%.”

surprises.description: Prime Day units fell 8% year over year because of aggressive competitor discounting, and the company said the result underperformed expectations. The preview had flagged retail restocking and sell-through, but did not anticipate this specific Prime Day shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Owlet's Prime Day units sold declined 8% versus last year due to aggressive competitor discounting ahead of Amazon's August 10 deactivation of non-FDA-cleared vital-sign monitors, underperforming expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sell-in should exceed sell-through this quarter” after a retail partner cut weeks-of-supply; the preview also flagged retail restock as a key metric.

surprises.description: U.S. sell-through excluding Prime Day grew 20%, below the roughly 30% growth run rate for Dream Sock and Duo cited in the preview. Dream Sock grew 21%, while Duo’s 29% growth was close to that earlier pace, making the update mixed rather than a broad failure of demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding Prime Day, US Q2 total sell-through units grew 20% year-over-year, with Dream Sock and Duo up 21% and 29% respectively.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had reported that “Q2 sell-through ran +30% YoY for both Duo and Dream Sock.”

surprises.description: Dream Sock U.S. penetration reached 36%, up from 34% in Q1 but short of the preview’s expectation that attach rate would move toward 40%. Subscriber count and subscription revenue met the preview’s stated watch levels, so the shortfall is specifically in penetration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Dream Sock US penetration reaching 36%.” The prior-quarter preview reported a “34% attach rate on U.S. Dream Sock.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for 128–132k subs, $3.0M+ revenue, and attach rate moving toward 40%.”

surprises.description: Owlet secured a new $25 million asset-based credit facility with a much lower interest-rate margin, a financing improvement not highlighted in the preview. The reduction of at least 525 basis points is a concrete positive change to borrowing terms.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new $25 million Wells Fargo asset-based credit facility lowered the interest rate margin to SOFR plus 2-2.25% from 7.5-8.5%, a reduction of at least 525 basis points.”

in_line: The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $118–122 million, as the preview’s base case expected the FY revenue guide to be reaffirmed.

Owlet ended the quarter with 130,000 paying subscribers and $3.2 million in subscription revenue, within or above the preview’s watch levels of 128–132 thousand subscribers and at least $3.0 million in revenue.
Duo sell-through grew 29%, close to the roughly 30% growth pace cited in the preview.

surprises.description: The preview said SINTX did not issue forward guidance, but the company gave Q3 revenue guidance of $900,000–$1.1 million and Q4 guidance of $1.0–$1.3 million. Those ranges imply a sharp step-up from Q2 revenue of $452,000.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company guided to Q3 2026 revenue of approximately $900,000 to $1.1 million and Q4 2026 revenue of approximately $1 million to $1.3 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Company guidance: None. SINTX does not issue forward guidance.

surprises.description: The preview’s rough equity bridge assumed a Q2 net loss of about $3.0–$3.6 million, while the reported Q2 net loss was $2.3 million. The loss was therefore less severe than the preview had allowed for.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net loss was flat at $2.3 million for Q2 2026 versus a year ago.
surprises.expectation_evidence: My rough bridge ... subtracting the Q2 net loss (about $3.0–3.6M) ...

surprises.description: The preview projected Q2-end cash of roughly $3.8–$4.5 million after the June raise, but cash was $3.6 million. That was below the bottom of the expected range and leaves the liquidity concern more acute than projected.
surprises.fact_evidence: Cash and cash equivalents declined to $3.6 million at June 30, 2026 from $4.1 million at year-end 2025, keeping liquidity risk a key concern.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Pro forma for the June raise, Q2-end cash should be roughly $3.8–4.5M.

surprises.description: The preview gave no Q2 gross-margin forecast and cited Q1 gross margin of about 38% as the recent benchmark; reported Q2 gross margin was 61.5%, a substantial step-up. The call attributed the improvement to higher-margin sales, favorable mix, and better OEM pricing.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin improved to approximately 62% (61.5%) from 37.7% a year ago, driven by higher-margin sales, favorable mix, and improved OEM pricing.

surprises.description: The preview discussed the $3.2 million customer orders and expected production into 2027, but did not anticipate a more-than-doubling of inventory. The build supports anticipated customer demand but ties up working capital in a company already facing liquidity risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: Inventory more than doubled to $2.3 million from $1 million at year-end, tying up working capital ahead of anticipated customer demand.

in_line: Q2 revenue of $452,000 was close to the preview’s $460,000 consensus estimate and within its $380,000–$450,000 base case; the reported growth was not a material departure from the preview.

The June purchase orders exceeding $3.2 million, with production continuing into 2027, were consistent with the preview’s account of the orders and its expectation that shipments would begin in the second half of 2026 and continue into 2027.

surprises.description: Revenue was $19.7 million, below the preview’s $22–25 million base case, though within its $19–21 million bear case. The preview warned that the $29 million consensus looked stale and might include revenue that had shifted to Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenue declined 11% year-over-year to $19.7 million” as ASA and ASE sales fell.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Base scenario expected “Revenue $22–25M”; its Bear scenario expected “$19–21M.” It also cautioned that consensus “appears to include the Genesis revenue that slipped to Q3.”

surprises.description: Bookings came in below the preview’s roughly $25 million watchpoint and were only $2.1 million above revenue, rather than well above it. This was a weaker demand signal than the preview’s checklist described.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 bookings fell to $21.8 million from $27.1 million,” reflecting lower ASE and ASA sales.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist said “Bookings versus about $25M” and noted that “a bookings-to-revenue gap is read as bullish this quarter”; its key-issues section said to watch for bookings “well above revenue.”

surprises.description: A lower ARK licensing fee structure added an unanticipated gross-profit benefit during a quarter of declining revenue. The preview did not identify this cost reduction as a potential offset.
surprises.fact_evidence: The reduced ARK licensing fee structure effective April 2026 “saved roughly $500,000 monthly (about $1.5 million per quarter), boosting gross profit even as revenue fell.”

surprises.description: R&D and G&A expenses are expected to stay flat quarter-over-quarter, rather than rise as the preview’s base case anticipated. Management also said investment in three AAA titles is nearing completion and R&D spend is approaching its peak.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management indicated “R&D and G&A expenses should remain consistent quarter-over-quarter” as investment in three in-development AAA titles nears completion, with R&D spend approaching its peak.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s Base scenario listed “opex rises”; its Bear scenario cited “opex overruns.”

surprises.description: Bellwright’s console launch showed stronger visible traction than the preview had flagged: it reached Xbox’s top five paid games list, alongside more than 1 million lifetime units sold and 46.4 million playtime hours. Its Q2 sales also partially offset declines in ASA and ASE.
surprises.fact_evidence: Bellwright’s PlayStation and Xbox launch “reached the top five paid games list on Xbox,” building on “over 1 million lifetime units sold and 46.4 million playtime hours”; it contributed $1.5 million to Q2 revenue.

surprises.description: The call reported phased Fantastic Tames and Dragontopia releases deferring recognition into both Q3 and Q4, extending the timing detail beyond the preview’s specific Q3 revenue bridge. This provides future deferred revenue but also means some content recognition is pushed into Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Current deferred revenue rose to $28.5 million as phased DLC content releases for the Fantastic Tames pack and Dragontopia defer recognition into Q3 and Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on “the roughly $11M” expected to land in Q3 and said Genesis, Tides of Fortune and Dragontopia had launched July 7.

in_line: The approximately $11 million deferred-revenue recognition was reaffirmed for Q3, as the preview had identified as the key call item.

Genesis Part 1 and Tides of Fortune launched in early July rather than June, and additional Tides of Fortune sales shifted from Q2 into Q3, consistent with the preview’s content-gap and Q3-bridge framing.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $3.1 million, below the preview’s $3.55 million consensus and even slightly below its $3.2–3.6 million base-case range. That is a miss of about 13% versus consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $3.1 million,” down roughly 24% year over year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $3.55M (implied −12% Y/Y)” and base scenario “$3.2–3.6M.”

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed the $16–18 million full-year outlook, as anticipated, but the lower-than-expected first-half revenue makes the remaining hurdle tougher than the preview’s bridge. The preview’s consensus-based calculation required second-half revenue 52–84% above first-half revenue; the reported first half was about $5.9 million, implying roughly $10.1–12.1 million in the second half, or about 71–105% above the first half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $16-18 million,” which implies “second-half growth north of 20% after a roughly 30% first-half decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Reaffirming $16–18M would require 2H revenue of $9.66–11.66M, which is 52–84% above 1H” at the preview’s expected Q2 revenue.

surprises.description: Gross margin came in well above the preview’s estimated 40–46% range and avoided the feared sub-40% result. At 49%, it also recovered 1,300 basis points sequentially from Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin was 49%,” down from 52% a year earlier but “up 1,300 basis points sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | Not available (my est. 40–46%)” and “A second sub-40% quarter would raise questions about pricing pressure from competitors.”

surprises.description: Net loss was larger than the preview’s roughly $15 million estimate, despite narrowing year over year and lower operating expenses. The reported $16.9 million loss was about $1.9 million, or 13%, worse than that estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed to $16.9 million from $19.4 million a year earlier,” with operating expenses of $18.3 million versus $22.6 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss | Not available (my est. ~$15M).”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash and investments were higher than the preview’s estimate, at $209.5 million versus an expected $204–207 million. The reported balance therefore suggests a smaller cash decline than the preview modeled, although the company still reported substantial first-half free-cash-flow burn.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended the quarter with “approximately $209.5 million in cash, cash equivalents, and investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My estimate for Q2 is $204–207M, based on roughly $14.6M of quarterly burn.”

surprises.description: Seer disclosed that it repurchased about 1.4 million shares during Q2 while two unsolicited bids were outstanding. The preview flagged whether a repurchase would occur but did not forecast one; the cumulative program has reduced net shares outstanding by about 15%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Seer repurchased about 1.4 million Class A shares at an average of $1.68 in Q2,” bringing cumulative buybacks to 13.4 million shares and reducing net shares outstanding by “~15%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 cash balance and whether the company repurchased stock during an active bid period. A $25M incremental buyback was approved in February 2026.”

surprises.description: The call reported a substantial increase in Proteograph publications and head-to-head studies claiming broader proteome coverage than Olink and SomaLogic, developments the preview did not quantify or forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: Validating publications “surpassed 95, an approximately 80% increase over the prior 12 months,” including head-to-head studies showing broader coverage than Olink and SomaLogic.

surprises.description: Management provided a more specific account of first-half instrument shipments: two-thirds came through prior STAC customers and the SIP program, with some SIP placements converting to owned instruments. The preview discussed prior instrument shipments and programs as possible demand drivers but did not anticipate this channel mix or conversions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In the first half of 2026, one-third of instrument shipments came from prior STAC customers and one-third from the SIP program, with some SIP placements converting into owned instruments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “the consumables reorder cycle from the 82 instruments shipped through YE2025” and “biobank programs (Korea University and PRECISE SG100K)” as potential support for the second half.

surprises.description: The PRECISE SG100K team had already completed 10,000 samples and plans to present preliminary data in September. The preview identified PRECISE SG100K as a possible demand driver but did not flag this completed milestone or the planned data presentation as a near-term catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The PRECISE SG100K team completed running 10,000 samples from the 100,000-sample cohort in May and will present preliminary data at HUPO in September,” which management views as a potential inflection point for large-scale buyback commitments.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “biobank programs (Korea University and PRECISE SG100K)” among management’s stated support for the outlook.

in_line: Management reaffirmed FY2026 revenue guidance of $16–18 million, the guidance already in place before the release; the lower Q2 result nevertheless makes the implied second-half bridge more demanding.
Management said the cash balance was sufficient to reach cash-flow break-even, consistent with the preview’s note that management had said it had sufficient capital to reach break-even.

surprises.description: Stereotaxis reported Q2 revenue of $7.7 million, about 10% below the $8.52 million consensus estimate. The company said the absence of robotic system deliveries drove the year-over-year decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue totaled $7.7 million,” declining year-over-year “due to the absence of any robotic system delivery.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 2026E | $8.52M.”

surprises.description: The quarterly outlook implies roughly $10 million of revenue in Q3 and $11 million in Q4, rather than the prior expectation that each quarter would exceed $10 million. Those quarterly figures also imply roughly $35 million for the year, well below the company’s prior above-$40-million guidance, unless additional revenue comes in beyond these amounts.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management guided recurring revenue to “approximately $7 million in Q3 and $8 million in Q4,” and system revenue to “approximately $3 million in each of Q3 and Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 revenue above $40M, with Q3 and Q4 each above $10M.”

surprises.description: MAGIC catheter sales were already above $1 million and rising sharply after the U.S. launch, indicating stronger near-term sales momentum than the preview’s adoption concerns suggested. However, sales remain supply-constrained and the call did not provide the monthly production run-rate the preview sought.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Robotic catheter revenue surpassed $1 million,” growing “roughly 270-300% sequentially and 450% year-over-year”; catheter sales remain “supply-constrained with a customer backlog.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the bogey was recurring revenue “above $6.0M and rising sequentially,” and sought a “quantified mid-year run-rate” for MAGiC; it noted adoption was “supply-constrained.”

surprises.description: The catheter ramp faces a specific adoption bottleneck: only about a dozen U.S. sites had hospital approval to purchase MAGIC in Q2, while a customer backlog remained. The preview warned that no quantified run-rate would be a negative signal, and the call did not provide one.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Only about a dozen U.S. sites received hospital approval to purchase MAGIC in Q2,” and catheter sales remain “supply-constrained with a customer backlog.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A quantified mid-year run-rate would support the H2 ramp. Silence on the number would be a negative signal.”

surprises.description: Management newly said it is internally modeling cash-flow profitability in the first half of 2027, with most incremental recurring revenue expected to flow to operating profit. The preview did not flag this profitability timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is internally modeling cash flow profitability in the first half of 2027,” with “the majority of incremental recurring revenue flowing to operating profit.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a new system-revenue opportunity from synchrony, which management expects to contribute more than $1 million per quarter at an ASP near $200,000; this was not included in the preview’s expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Synchrony [is] expected to contribute over $1 million in system revenue per quarter at an ASP near $200,000.”

surprises.description: Stereotaxis announced its first U.S. GenesisX purchase, from an academic medical center, with installation expected in the fall. The preview did not anticipate this order.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company announced its first U.S. GenesisX purchase from an academic medical center (install expected this fall).”

in_line: The recurring-revenue bogey appears to have been met: Q2 revenue was $7.7 million with no robotic system delivery, and revenue rose sequentially on higher catheter sales, versus the preview’s expectation of recurring revenue above $6 million.

Cash was within the preview’s modeled range: quarter-end cash was $10.5 million versus an estimate of roughly $9.5–11 million. Free cash flow burn of $3.7 million was close to the roughly $3.5 million per-quarter assumption.
Adjusted operating expenses were roughly flat year over year, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Q2 EPS was less negative than the preview’s $(0.44) consensus estimate: the reported loss per share was $(0.33). The preview had already expected a revenue beat, but this is a distinct earnings-per-share beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Loss per share improving to $0.33” (a loss of $(0.33)).
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 Consensus” EPS: “$(0.44).”

surprises.description: Management’s cash-flow outlook sounded less definite than the preview’s expectation of becoming operationally cash-flow positive during 2026: it said positivity might be only momentary in Q3, declined to give a calendar target for sustained breakeven, and disclosed that about $12.9 million of quarterly revenue at 35% margins would be needed to cover the current cost structure without cuts.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “believes it may reach momentary operating cash flow positivity in Q3 2026” but “declined to provide a specific calendar target for sustained breakeven”; it still aims to achieve breakeven in 2026. “Roughly $12.9 million in quarterly revenue at 35% margins” is needed to cover the current cost structure absent expense cuts.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance (reaffirmed May 13, 2026): FY2026 revenue $35–42M vs. $16.1M in 2025; operationally cash-flow positive during 2026.”

surprises.description: NEXUS showed concrete early traction, with $1 million in cumulative sales within about 10 weeks and roughly $1.5 million in July orders. The preview flagged early NEXUS revenue as something to watch but gave no comparable sales or order target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new NEXUS tonneau cover reached $1 million in cumulative sales within about 10 weeks of its April 13 production launch and generated approximately $1.5 million in sales orders in July alone.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for a hard number and early revenue from SOLIS, COR, and NEXUS.”

surprises.description: Management identified inventory as its largest internal liquidity source, a funding avenue the preview did not flag. The inventory includes substantial raw-material and finished-goods balances, so this adds a new potential source of liquidity but does not establish that it has been converted to cash.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory stood at $12.1 million,” including “$6.6 million raw materials” and “$4.6 million” of finished goods; management “targets [inventory] as its largest internal liquidity source.”

surprises.description: The call added a specific AetherLux certification and launch timeline that the preview did not discuss: certification is expected in fall 2026, with product availability 45–60 days afterward. This is new timing information, though it does not establish that certification or launch has already occurred.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AetherLux heat pump certification in fall 2026 with product available 45-60 days thereafter.”

in_line: Revenue was $5.2 million: above the $4.50 million consensus estimate, but within the preview’s implied $5.0–5.3 million range from the pre-released monthly figures.
Q2 gross margin was approximately 32%, close to the preview’s expectation that blended Q2 margin would be around 31%; June’s roughly 35% margin also matched the preview’s disclosed June figure.

Q2 operating cash use fell sharply from Q1, consistent with the preview’s expectation that burn might fall; the $3.4 million outflow was slightly above the preview’s bull-case threshold of below roughly $3 million. June 30 cash of $1.2 million was within the preview’s estimated $1–2 million range, and the going-concern disclosure continued as expected.

surprises.description: The Board began a formal strategic review of the casino and gaming business and hired B of A Securities as advisor, raising the possibility of a sale or divestiture. The preview discussed the segment’s cyclicality and cash contribution but did not anticipate a strategic review.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board initiated a formal strategic review of the casino and gaming business and engaged B of A Securities as financial advisor,” signaling a potential sale or divestiture.

surprises.description: The EBITDA outlook was raised rather than simply reaffirmed: the call reported a new range of $1.5 million to $2.0–2.2 million, with $1.9 million generated in the first half. The preview listed prior guidance of $1.0–1.75 million and said a raise would be the clearer positive signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to a range of $1.5 million to $2.0-2.2 million,” backed by “$1.9 million of adjusted EBITDA in the first half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA” guidance: “$1.0–1.75M”; the preview said “a raise would be the clearer positive signal.”

surprises.description: FST software revenue grew 47% year over year and 25% sequentially, with growth driven primarily by price increases after the company stopped bundling software for free. That provides concrete evidence of software monetization, beyond the preview’s open question about whether pricing was being realized.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FST software revenue grew 47% year-over-year and 25% sequentially, driven primarily by price increases as the company ended its prior practice of bundling software for free.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any evidence of price realization is a key disclosure.”

surprises.description: Casino and gaming revenue was $7.3 million, below the preview’s $7.6 million comparison point, though the tariff-adjusted figure was $8.3 million and up 9% year over year. The reported shortfall therefore looks weaker than the adjusted result, rather than clearly indicating the demand slowdown the preview was watching for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Casino and gaming revenue was $7.3 million, down 4% YoY and down 13% sequentially, but would have been $8.3 million (up 9% YoY) excluding the $1 million tariff impact.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Casino & Gaming revenue vs. the $7.6M Q2'25 comp”; “A print at or above $7.6M supports the new run-rate.”

surprises.description: Recurring FST revenue rose 13% to $3.4 million, below the preview’s roughly 15% growth threshold for a reassuring result, despite exceeding the prior-year $3.0 million level it cited. The growth rate was also slower than Q1’s 26%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recurring FST revenue reached $3.4 million in Q2, up 13% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Growth below roughly 15% would be the most damaging data point”; Q2'25 recurring revenue was cited as “$3.0M.”

surprises.description: Q2 sales were approximately in line with consensus, but the company said they would have been $14.9 million, up 8% year over year, without an approximately $1 million tariff-refund-related reduction. The preview did not flag this unusual reduction or the stronger underlying sales figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total net sales were $13.9 million, roughly flat versus $13.8 million a year earlier, but would have been $14.9 million (up 8% YoY) excluding an approximate $1 million tariff refund reduction to sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Net sales consensus: “$13.97M (3 analysts).”

surprises.description: The company reported a $50,000 net loss but breakeven earnings per share, slightly better than the preview’s -$0.01 EPS consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company posted a Q2 net loss of $50,000 (breakeven per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted)” consensus: “-$0.01.”

in_line: Q2 net sales of $13.9 million were close to the $13.97 million consensus estimate, notwithstanding the unanticipated tariff-related reduction described above.

Q2 gross margin of 50.2% was just above the preview’s 50%-or-more watch point; management continued to guide to a mid-to-high-40% full-year margin range, in line with the preview’s “high 40s” guidance.
Full-year net sales guidance was reaffirmed, consistent with the preview’s base case of a reaffirmation.
Management reiterated the long-term target of $100–$200 per machine per month in recurring software revenue, consistent with the target cited in the preview.

surprises.description: The preview framed the 1H 2027 six-month interim readout and FDA feedback as the main upcoming catalyst, but management said the six-month analysis of all 17 REVEAL pivotal patients may support the BLA, potentially moving filing at least two full quarters earlier than a filing based on 12-month data.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A planned 6-month interim analysis of all 17 REVEAL pivotal patients may serve as the basis for a BLA submission, potentially accelerating the filing timeline by at least two full quarters versus filing on 12-month data.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The main catalyst, topline 6-month interim data plus FDA feedback on the BLA path, is guided to 1H 2027, not this quarter.”

surprises.description: The preview described the quarter as a status check rather than an efficacy inflection point, but the call reported that all 12 REVEAL Part A patients were responders at 12 months—well above the FDA-aligned 33% pivotal response threshold—and cited 310 functional gains across multiple domains and age groups.
surprises.fact_evidence: “100% of the 12 patients were responders at 12 months,” compared with the “FDA-aligned 33% pivotal response threshold”; patients also achieved “310 functional gains” across communication, fine motor, gross motor, and autonomic domains.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “This print is a status check on timelines and cash, not an inflection point.”

surprises.description: The preview expected no treatment-related SAEs through the June cutoff, but the call disclosed a new treatment-related Grade 2 peripheral sensory neuropathy that qualified as an SAE after overnight hospitalization. The patient substantially recovered within 24 hours of discharge, and the company reported no severe treatment-related SAEs or DLTs across 33 patients as of the August cutoff.
surprises.fact_evidence: “One REVEAL pivotal patient experienced a moderate Grade 2 treatment-related peripheral sensory neuropathy about 6 weeks post-treatment,” was hospitalized overnight, and “demonstrated substantial recovery within 24 hours of discharge”; across 33 patients, there were “no severe treatment-related serious adverse events or dose-limiting toxicities.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “As of the June 2026 cutoff, no treatment-related SAEs and no DLTs were reported across REVEAL Phase 1/2 and pivotal. Any new adverse event is the main single-point risk.”

surprises.description: Cash was higher than the preview’s roughly $415–425 million estimate, and management said the balance provides runway through potential BLA approval. That is more reassuring than the preview’s concern that runway described only as “into 2028” could require another financing before interim data, although the call did not project runway into 2029.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Taysha held $455.4 million in cash as of June 30, 2026,” including $230 million in gross proceeds from a June financing, “providing runway into the second half of 2028 and through potential BLA approval.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My estimate: ... Q2-end cash of about $415–425M”; the preview warned that language still reading “into 2028” “would imply another financing before the interim data.”

surprises.description: The reported net loss and EPS were somewhat worse than the preview’s consensus figures, though the loss was close to the preview’s own estimate and a miss was already considered plausible.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss of $46.6 million ($0.13 per share),” versus the preview’s consensus-implied loss of about $41 million and consensus EPS of -$0.116.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus implies a net loss of about $41M”; “My estimate: Net loss of roughly $44–46M”; “a headline EPS miss is a plausible outcome.”

surprises.description: The preview identified CMC as a potential BLA-delay risk and asked for Catalent capacity details. The call added that the partnership includes commercial manufacturing at an FDA-licensed facility and said CMC/comparability is not currently a critical-path item, offering more reassurance than the preview had specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Catalent partnership now includes “commercial manufacturing at Catalent's FDA-licensed Harmans, Maryland facility,” with PPQ activities expected to complete in Q4 2026; management stated “CMC/comparability is not currently a critical path item.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CMC is a common cause of gene therapy BLA delays”; the preview said to watch whether Catalent capacity is quantified.

in_line: Management reaffirmed that top-line REVEAL pivotal six-month interim data and FDA feedback on the BLA pathway are expected in the first half of 2027.
PPQ activities remain expected to complete in Q4 2026, in line with the preview’s targeted completion timing.

Dosing completion was confirmed for ASPIRE’s four patients aged 2 to under 4, matching the preview’s expectation that dosing would finish in Q2 2026; REVEAL pivotal dosing was also complete, as already noted in the preview.

surprises.description: Revenue was $365.4 million, slightly above the preview’s highest listed consensus estimate of $361.8 million, though still within its $360–366 million base scenario. That makes the revenue beat modest rather than a clear break from the preview’s overall range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 31.3% year-over-year to $365.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue estimates ranged from “$353.3M” to “$361.8M”; the base scenario was “$360–366M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA of $54.7 million exceeded the preview’s roughly $50 million consensus estimate by about 9%, a more substantial beat than the revenue result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 30% to $54.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$50M (~15% margin) | Street compile.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS came in at $0.19, above the preview’s main estimates of $0.17–$0.18 and its $0.18 base scenario, although one estimate was lower at $0.14.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS grew to $0.19 from $0.16.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “$0.17 (Zacks),” “$0.18 (StockStory, GAAP),” and “$0.14 (GuruFocus),” with a base scenario of “$0.18.”

surprises.description: Management said current trends do not point to the low end of the unchanged same-store sales outlook, even though that end would imply slightly negative sales growth. This is more reassuring than simply reiterating a range whose low end allows for a downturn.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The low end of full-year guidance implies slightly negative same-restaurant sales while the upper end implies mid-single-digit growth, with management stating nothing in current trends suggests landing at the low end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “FY26 same-restaurant sales guidance” was a key issue and that “the guide embeds meaningful H2 cushion, so a hold is possible even with a Q3 outbreak drag.”

surprises.description: Following the cyclospora concerns, same-store sales had dipped to flat-to-positive but then recovered sequentially each week to mid-single digits. The preview focused on quantifying a possible Q3 drag; the supplied call facts report a recovery but give no drag estimate in basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-restaurant sales dipped to flat-to-positive amid cyclospora food safety concerns after quarter-end but have since recovered sequentially each week to mid-single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “key number is whether management quantifies the drag below or above 400bp” and its base scenario expected the “drag framed at 300–450bp.”

surprises.description: Restaurant-level margin was 25.7%, modestly above the preview’s stated 25.5% benchmark despite salmon costs and wage investments. The preview had identified salmon and wage costs as headwinds, so the positive difference is the margin landing above its stated threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restaurant-level profit was $93.8 million (25.7% of revenue), down 60 basis points from 26.3% a year ago, pressured by salmon input costs, wage investments, and higher third-party delivery mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The catalyst checklist called for “RLP margin vs. ≥25.5%,” and the preview noted salmon was a “~100bp headwind through Q4, plus wage investment and energy costs.”

surprises.description: Management added fuel surcharges and the premarinated chicken rollout as second-half margin headwinds. Those specific pressures were not identified in the preview, which discussed salmon, wage investment, and energy costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management flagged margin headwinds in the back half from fuel surcharges and the premarinated chicken rollout.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “salmon” as a headwind, “plus wage investment and energy costs,” but did not mention fuel surcharges or the premarinated chicken rollout.

surprises.description: New-restaurant productivity was above 100% across geographies and formats, and systemwide AUV reached $3.1 million, above the preview’s approximate $3.0 million new-class AUV watchpoint. The reported AUV is systemwide, so it is not an exact like-for-like comparison with the preview’s new-class figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New restaurant productivity remained above 100% across all geographies and formats, with the 2024 cohort delivering double-digit same-restaurant sales as the highest-performing vintage in the portfolio, lifting systemwide AUV to $3.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch new-class AUV near ~$3.0M.”

in_line: Same-restaurant sales were up 9% with 5.3% traffic growth, broadly in line with the preview’s approximately 8% implied comp and its base scenario of +9–10%; traffic, rather than price-mix, was the main reported driver.

Management reiterated FY26 same-restaurant sales guidance of 4.5%–6.5%, restaurant-level margin guidance of 23.7%–24.3%, adjusted EBITDA guidance of $181–191 million, and net new restaurant guidance of 75–77. The preview identified holding or changing these ranges as a key issue and anticipated a hold as a possibility.
The company opened 17 net new restaurants and ended the quarter with 476 locations, consistent with the preview’s fairly ratable Q2–Q4 opening cadence and its stated 459 locations exiting Q1.
The preview already expected salmon to remain a margin headwind through Q4; management’s commitment to keep salmon through year-end 2026 is consistent with that expectation.

surprises.description: Managed Services bookings were $4.5 million, down 19% year over year, rather than the preview’s expected $7.0–7.5 million and increase from the $5.6 million prior-year comparison. That is also below the preview’s $6.5 million level described as a real problem.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Managed services bookings declined 19% year-over-year to $4.5 million amid softer enterprise demand and delayed contracting.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Managed Services bookings: $7.0–7.5M (+25–34% YoY)”; the preview also said “Anything below about $6.5M is a real problem.”

surprises.description: The company reported a $0.7 million net loss, or negative $0.04 per share, worse than the preview’s $0.02-per-share consensus loss and its own $0.03-per-share estimate. The preview noted that the consensus bar looked achievable only in the bull case, but the reported loss still fell short of both estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company swung to a net loss of $0.7 million (negative $0.04 per share) versus net income of $1.2 million ($0.07 per share) in the prior year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP) | Consensus $(0.02) | My estimate $(0.03).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was negative $0.4 million, a little worse than the preview’s negative $0.3 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA turned negative at negative $0.4 million compared to positive $1.3 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … My estimate $(0.3)M.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses fell to $3.3 million, materially below the preview’s expectation that they would stay relatively stable at about $4.1 million per quarter. Lower commissions, headcount, and payroll costs contributed to the decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses fell 18% year-over-year to $3.3 million, with G&A down roughly 20%, driven by lower commissions, headcount, and payroll costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CFO Biere guided opex to remain relatively stable (about $4.1M per quarter).”

surprises.description: Cash was essentially unchanged from Q1’s $46.5 million, at $46.6 million, rather than showing the additional large cash draw the preview flagged as a risk. The ending balance was also slightly above the preview’s $45–46 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “IZEA ended the quarter with $46.6 million in cash and no debt, down $4.3 million since the start of the year.” The preview’s Q1 context gives cash of $46.5 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash & equivalents … My estimate $45–46M”; the preview also flagged “A second straight $3M+ unexplained draw” as a risk.

surprises.description: Management said the roughly seven-month lag from contract signing to final revenue recognition means weak Q2 bookings will pressure near-term revenue; July contract awards would benefit later quarters. This adds a near-term timing headwind to the preview’s expectation that H2 would return to year-over-year revenue growth, while offering a later-period offset.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The average lag between contract signing and final revenue recognition is roughly seven months, meaning weak Q2 bookings will pressure near-term revenue while July contract awards benefit later quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said H2 2026 would return to year-over-year revenue growth”; the preview said a slip to late 2026 or 2027 would reset the story.

surprises.description: Management described multiple large enterprise opportunities, each capable of generating more than $1 million in annual revenue, and called the acquisition pipeline its most active ever. The preview discussed enterprise timing and possible M&A framing, but did not anticipate these specific pipeline details; these remain opportunities rather than reported wins or acquisitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reports a pipeline of large enterprise opportunities, including multiple deals each capable of generating more than $1 million in annual revenue”; it also “cited its most active acquisition pipeline ever.”

surprises.description: Repurchases under the $10 million authorization totaled about $1.8 million, somewhat more than the preview’s estimate of about $1.4 million used. The amount reported since the current plan was adopted in May was about $0.5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Under its $10 million buyback authorization, the company has repurchased about 658,000 shares for $1.8 million, including roughly 135,000 shares for $0.5 million since the current plan was adopted in May.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buybacks under the new trading plan (about $1.4M of the $10M authorization used).”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $1.5 million: it matched the published consensus, but exceeded the preview model’s $1.25–1.35 million range despite the Department of War funding delay continuing. That is a modest upside versus the preview model, rather than a consensus beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $1.5 million, up 64% sequentially but down 22% year-over-year, reflecting the ongoing delay in Department of War contract funding.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Preview model: revenue of $1.25–1.35M”; consensus revenue was “$1.50M.”

surprises.description: The reported loss of $0.13 per share was worse than the $0.10 consensus loss, but better than the preview model’s $0.16–$0.18 loss. The result therefore missed the headline consensus while coming in less negative than the preview’s operating model.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $2.6 million ($0.13 per share) in Q2 2026 from $2.0 million ($0.10 per share) in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus EPS was “$(0.10)”; the “Preview model” was EPS of “$(0.16) to $(0.18).”

surprises.description: The preview expected roughly $3.5 million of VigilAigent ARR but questioned whether it was contracted or aspirational. The call said the ARR comes immediately from multiyear customer contracts, resolving that uncertainty favorably.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company acquired VigilAigent… which immediately adds approximately $3.5 million of annual recurring revenue from multiyear customer contracts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “VigilAigent brought about $3.5M of ARR. Watch for… whether the $3.5M is contracted or aspirational.”

surprises.description: Within weeks of the acquisition, the company reported more than $350,000 of annualized new business and renewals, plus signed MSP partners each with potential to generate over $1 million in ARR. The preview identified ARR and retention as questions to watch but did not anticipate this specific post-acquisition sales and partner activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Since the acquisition weeks ago, the company secured over $350,000 in annualized new business and customer renewals and signed several MSP partners each with potential to generate over $1 million in annual recurring revenue.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a $4 million annual contract with Texas, with revenue starting in Q2 and extending into fiscal 2027. The preview anticipated some Texas ramp, but did not specify a signed contract of this size or its revenue timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company secured a $4 million annual contract with the State of Texas for cyber threat intelligence and critical infrastructure protection, with revenue recognition starting in Q2 and extending into fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s scenarios referred to “Texas ramping” and “partial-quarter Texas.”

surprises.description: Cash at quarter-end was just $0.2 million, far below the preview’s estimate of $2.0–2.5 million. The company also said it raised $3.3 million through Streeterville notes and plans further public or private financing, making the liquidity need and financing dependence more acute than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents stood at just $0.2 million as of June 30, 2026, prompting the company to raise $3.3 million via Streeterville notes and to plan further public/private financings including its ATM program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The preview models about $2.0–2.5M of cash at 6/30”; it also noted the “$1.3M obligation due Aug 30” and that an equity raise “would be significantly dilutive.”

surprises.description: Management moved from the prior Q4 2026 cash-flow-positive run-rate target to a goal of cash-flow positive by Q1 2027, and described that goal as not a commitment. This is a later and less firm target than the preview’s year-end 2026 expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management targets transitioning Intrusion to profitability in 2027, with a goal (not a commitment) of becoming cash flow positive by Q1 2027, backing away from a prior Q4 2026 cash flow positive run-rate target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior-quarter section said management “guided… to cash-flow positive by year-end 2026”; the catalyst checklist asked whether that was “reaffirmed… or pushed out.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that acquisition shares could be sold after a six-month holding period. The preview anticipated a shareholder/Nasdaq approval condition for the remaining acquisition closing, but did not flag this specific timing for potential resale of the shares.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Shareholders will vote at the August 27 annual meeting on Proposal 3, which authorizes issuance of common stock above NASDAQ's 19.9% threshold for the VigilAigent acquisition, with acquisition shares eligible for sale after a 6-month holding period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the remaining VigilAigent closing was “subject to shareholder and Nasdaq approval”; it did not mention the six-month share-sale eligibility.

in_line: The $1.5 million revenue result matched the preview’s stated $1.50 million consensus estimate, even though it was above the preview’s own model range.
The Department of War contract funding delay remained ongoing, consistent with the preview’s base case of the extension being pending or late without a catch-up.
Management’s identified annualized cost synergies remained at more than $3 million, as the preview said management had repeatedly cited “>$3M in identified annualized cost synergies.”
The VigilAigent acquisition added approximately $3.5 million of ARR, in line with the amount the preview expected.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $2.1 million, about 17% above the preview’s roughly $1.8 million model, though below its $2.4 million bull-case threshold. The quarter’s 103% year-over-year growth was stronger than the preview’s base-case revenue range implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue increased 103% year-over-year to $2.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue versus about $1.8M in my model”; the base scenario was “$1.7–1.9M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin rose to about 75%, well above the preview’s 62% comparison point and contrary to its concern that another quarter of compression could undermine the margin story.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit rose 217% to $1.5 million with gross margin expanding to approximately 75% from approximately 48% a year earlier.”
