surprises.description: Although the preview emphasized that Helly Hansen’s Q2 is its seasonal trough, it did not anticipate the brand reaching operating profitability in that quarter. Helly Hansen reported roughly $2 million of operating profit in Q2, which management said may be the first time it has done so.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Helly Hansen delivered positive operating profit of roughly $2 million in Q2, its seasonally smallest quarter,” possibly “the first time ever the brand achieved this.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 is the smallest revenue quarter for HH. Watch constant-currency growth and any read on the fall/winter order book.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag the strength of Wrangler’s women’s business. It grew 20% in the first half and accelerated in Q2, despite representing only about 10% of company revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wrangler's female business, currently ~10% of total revenue … grew 20% in the first half with accelerating Q2 trends.”

surprises.description: The preview did not discuss Helly Hansen’s China joint venture, whose revenue was excluded from consolidated results. The JV grew nearly 70% in Q2, lifting the brand’s global pro forma revenue growth to the mid-teens rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Helly Hansen's China JV revenue (excluded from consolidated results) grew nearly 70% in Q2,” and including it, “Helly global pro forma revenue grew at a mid-teens rate.”

in_line: Wrangler U.S. wholesale was flat, matching the preview’s explicitly flagged possibility of a second flat quarter after Q1’s 1% growth.

surprises.description: Q4 non-GAAP EPS was $1.70, well above the preview’s cited consensus estimates of $0.68–$0.96. The preview’s own base case was $1.40–$1.55, so the result also exceeded that model, though it was at the top of the preview’s bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 non-GAAP EPS came in at $1.70 versus guidance of $0.65-$0.79, driven primarily by the outsized gross margin beat.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$0.96 (Street compilation, early Aug 2026); $0.68 (Zacks, Aug 2026)” and “The full preview's own model puts Q4 non-GAAP EPS near $1.48 in a base case”; bull scenario: “$1.60–1.70.”

surprises.description: Q4 non-GAAP gross margin reached 17.6%, above the preview’s latest 15%–17% company guidance. The unusually large gain was mostly attributed to favorable customer and product mix, including deferred contracts, rather than solely to a broad improvement in underlying costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 non-GAAP gross margin surged to 17.6%, more than double the 8.2%-8.4% guidance”; “roughly 75% of the gain” came from “favorable customer/product mix (including deferred contracts).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 gross margin | 15%–17%, GAAP and non-GAAP (July 21, 2026).”

surprises.description: SMCI issued FY27 revenue guidance of $65–$72 billion, above the preview’s $55–$65 billion base scenario and at or above its bull-case threshold. Management also said it would walk away from deals below minimum margin thresholds, pairing the ambitious growth target with a stated limit on sacrificing profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided FY27 revenue to $65-72 billion”; it is “balancing top-line expansion against profitability by walking away from deals below minimum margin thresholds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base scenario: “Revenue $55–65B”; bull scenario: “Revenue ≥$68–70B.” The preview also said “The FY27 guide is the main unknown.”

surprises.description: FY26 non-GAAP EPS was $3.63, substantially above the preview’s $2.84 consensus estimate. The preview did not have a full-year EPS company guide to account for the result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY26 revenue reached a record $39.1 billion (up 78%) with non-GAAP EPS of $3.63 (up 76%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 EPS | Not found | $2.84 (stockanalysis.com, Aug 11, 2026).”

surprises.description: The reported facts give Q1 FY27 gross-margin guidance of 10.4%–10.8%, but no annual FY27 margin outlook. That leaves the preview’s central question—whether Q4’s 17.6% margin can persist—unanswered, and the Q1 range is below the 11%–13% range the preview said the buy side was positioned for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY27 guidance calls for revenue of $14.5-15.5 billion, gross margin of 10.4%-10.8%”; the FY27 guidance reported is for revenue, with no annual FY27 gross-margin range stated in the supplied facts.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2027 gross margin guidance. This drives the print”; “FY2027 gross margin vs. the 11–13% range the buy side is positioned for.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue mix shifted sharply away from AI solutions and toward enterprise and channel sales: AI solutions were about 60% of revenue, while enterprise and channel reached 50%. This was attributed to timing of large AI projects and a push into CPU, storage, and IoT sales, rather than a reported collapse in AI demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI solutions fell to about 60% of Q4 revenue (from over 80% in Q3) due to large AI project timing”; “Enterprise and channel revenue jumped to $5.6 billion, or 50% of Q4 revenue, up from 28% in the prior quarter.”

surprises.description: Net debt fell from $7.5 billion to $1.2 billion, and management said it currently has no plans to use the ATM program. The preview had highlighted further equity issuance and ATM usage as risks, although the June equity-linked issuance itself was already known.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised $5.6 billion in equity ($1.4 billion common, $4.2 billion mandatory convertible preferred), cutting net debt to $1.2 billion from $7.5 billion,” and “stated it currently has no plans to use its ATM program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “further equity issuance” as a concern and said “Continued burn plus ATM usage would be the worst”; it also noted the June announcement of “about $7B of equity and equity-linked issuance, including an ATM of up to $2B.”

in_line: Q4 revenue was $11.1 billion, near the low end of the $11.0–$12.5 billion range, as the preview anticipated after the July pre-announcement.
More than $60 billion of Q4 orders was in line with the preview’s report of “>$60B booked” in the July pre-announcement.
FY26 revenue of $39.1 billion was broadly in line with the preview’s $39.51 billion consensus estimate and within the $38.9–$40.4 billion guide.

The preview flagged customer concentration as a key issue; the reported facts quantified it as one CSP customer accounting for 28% of FY26 revenue, without giving a comparison point for an expected concentration level.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $61.8 million, below the preview’s $65 million estimate, with shipments down across truck mirrors, returnable packaging, and latch/handle assemblies. The 11.9% year-over-year decline was steeper than the preview’s expected roughly 7% decline based on its estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales from continuing operations fell 11.9% year-over-year to $61.8 million from $70.2 million,” driven by lower shipments of truck mirror assemblies, returnable transport packaging, and latch/handle assemblies.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Preview estimates: revenue $65M”; the preview also noted that its consensus revenue estimate was $73.69M but said the “real buy-side bar is closer to $64–67M revenue.”

surprises.description: Adjusted earnings were well below the preview’s expectations: adjusted EPS was $0.15 versus $0.42 expected, and adjusted EBITDA was $3.4 million versus $5.5 million expected. GAAP net income of $5.6 million was lifted by a $6.5 million noncash bargain purchase gain, masking the weaker underlying result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding the bargain purchase gain, adjusted net income from continuing operations dropped to $0.9 million ($0.15/diluted share)”; “adjusted EBITDA fell approximately 49% to $3.4 million.” GAAP net income included “a $6.5 million one-time noncash bargain purchase gain.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Preview estimates: ... adj. EPS $0.42, adj. EBITDA $5.5M.”

surprises.description: Backlog reached $126.2 million, far above the preview’s roughly $80–84 million base case and even its above-$88 million bull-case threshold. About $19 million came from the new aerospace business, while the legacy business also contributed to the increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog surged 45% year-over-year to $126.2 million from $87.1 million,” including “roughly $19 million from the new aerospace book” and the balance from legacy business.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “backlog roughly flat at $80–84M”; its bull case cited “backlog above $88M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 20.8%, below the preview’s 21.5% estimate. The below-margin Big 3 contract runoff was still weighing on results in Q2, contrary to the prior-quarter framing that the damage would be largely behind the company by quarter-end; China tariff costs also remained a burden.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 20.8% ... from 23.3% ... due to lower volume, the below-margin Big 3 contract runoff, and ~$1.9 million of China tariff costs,” although it improved roughly 60 basis points sequentially.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Preview estimates: ... gross margin 21.5%”; the preview said management had described the Q1 damage as “contained to the first half” and “largely behind us by the end of the second quarter.”

surprises.description: The company acquired Crown Precision and Sun Gear for $7.85 million, entering aerospace and defense precision manufacturing—an actual transaction not specified in the preview. The purchase was funded with borrowings, despite the preview noting deleveraging as a priority.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company acquired California-based Crown Precision and Sun Gear for $7.85 million, funded by borrowings, marking its entry into aerospace and defense precision manufacturing effective June 1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “tuck-in M&A” among capital-allocation items to watch and described deleveraging as “a clear priority,” but did not identify a specific acquisition.

surprises.description: The newly acquired aerospace businesses were near breakeven gross margins and are expected to weigh about 120 basis points on overall gross margin near-term; reaching the targeted 20%–30% margin is expected to take several quarters. The preview had no expectation for this new business or its near-term margin burden.
surprises.fact_evidence: The acquired businesses “currently operate near breakeven gross margins due to inventory step-up effects and mispriced legacy backlog,” with a “targeted gross margin of 20%-30% expected over several quarters”; the acquisition is “expected to weigh ~120 basis points on overall gross margin near-term.”

in_line: Management expected a significantly stronger second half, supported by recovering heavy-truck build rates, consistent with the preview’s focus on a second-half recovery.
The company paid the 344th consecutive quarterly dividend of $0.11 per share, as the preview had noted the declared dividend.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.25, well above the preview's $0.17 consensus estimate. The beat was substantially larger than the preview's base-case range of $0.17-$0.18.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose to $0.25 from $0.18 a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $0.17”; the base scenario also expected “Adj. EPS $0.17–0.18.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating margin reached 6.3%, materially above the preview's derived 4.8%-5.2% range, rather than roughly matching the prior-year margin as the preview's base case anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin expanded 140 basis points to 6.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating margin | ~4.8%–5.2% (derived)”; the preview described “Roughly flat Y/Y margin (~4.9%) as the base case.”

surprises.description: The company raised full-year adjusted operating income guidance to $119-$139 million from the preview's standing $107-$133 million range. This was a stronger guidance action than the preview expected, which said a raise was unlikely.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year adjusted operating income outlook to $119-$139 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Standing guidance was “Adj. operating income $107–$133M”; the preview said “A raise is unlikely.”

surprises.description: Despite raising adjusted operating income guidance, the company lowered the top of its revenue range by $10 million and cut the comp-growth ceiling by one percentage point. The preview expected narrowing toward the lower half, but did not forecast this specific reduction in the upper bounds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Narrowing net revenue guidance to $2.03-$2.08 billion and lowering the top end of comp guidance to 3-5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Standing guidance was “Net revenue $2.03–$2.09B” and “Adj. comp store sales +3% to +6%”; the base case expected the FY range to be “narrowed toward lower half.”

surprises.description: Management quantified a more pronounced traffic burden among value-seeking customers: their purchase cycle lengthened about two weeks, creating an estimated two-point full-year traffic headwind. The preview flagged pressure on cash-pay customers but did not quantify this headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Weakness is concentrated in lower-value 'value-seeking' customers whose purchase cycle lengthened by about 2 weeks, creating roughly a 2-point full-year traffic headwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “EYE's cash-pay, lower-income customer is under more pressure” and flagged “Cash-pay traffic” as a key issue.

surprises.description: The company said Q3/Q4 operating-margin expansion would be flat-to-modest because it plans to reinvest a roughly $5 million tariff refund in back-half marketing. That puts a specific limit on near-term margin expansion despite the stronger full-year adjusted operating income outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Plans to reinvest a ~$5 million tariff refund into incremental back-half marketing, keeping Q3/Q4 operating margin expansion flat-to-modest.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “about 100 bps of FY expansion” was expected and highlighted the back-half ramp as “the real story”; it did not anticipate the tariff-refund reinvestment or this Q3/Q4 margin characterization.

surprises.description: Management forecast that Nikon Eyes and store segmentation would add roughly 100-200 basis points to ticket growth in the second half, a specific incremental ticket-growth contribution not called out in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects Nikon Eyes and store segmentation to add roughly 100-200 basis points to ticket growth in the second half.”

surprises.description: Inventory was up about 37% year over year to support the store-segmentation strategy, a substantial build not anticipated in the preview; management expects the pace of growth to moderate through 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory rose approximately 37% year-over-year to support the store segmentation strategy, with management expecting the growth pace to moderate through 2026.”

surprises.description: The company repurchased about 1.2 million shares for $20 million, while ending the quarter at 0.9x net debt to adjusted EBITDA versus 0.8x after Q1. The preview discussed Q1 debt repayment but did not anticipate this quarter's buyback or the higher leverage figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased about 1.2 million shares for $20 million during the quarter, with $30 million remaining on its buyback authorization, and ended with net debt to adjusted EBITDA of approximately 0.9x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported “Q1 FCF supported $101.3M of debt repayment; net debt/adj. EBITDA 0.8x.”

surprises.description: The call's stated full-year adjusted diluted EPS range of $0.90-$1.09 has a higher floor than the preview's standing $0.85-$1.09 range, even though management described the range as maintained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted diluted EPS guidance was maintained at $0.90-$1.09.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Standing guidance was “Adj. diluted EPS $0.85–$1.09.”

in_line: Q2 net revenue of $499 million was essentially in line with the preview's $499.8 million consensus and $498-$503 million base-case range.
Q2 adjusted comparable store sales growth of 2.2% was broadly in line with the preview's derived roughly 1%-2% expectation and its 1.5%-2.0% base case.
More than half of the ticket increase came from mix shift, consistent with the preview's expectation that managed care, progressives, and premium frames would support growth.

surprises.description: The preview’s rough FY27 EPS benchmark was about $11.90, with the long-term algorithm implying $12.15–12.60. Brinker guided to $12.60–13.40, putting even the low end above the rough benchmark and at the top of the algorithm-implied range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal '27 guidance calls for… adjusted diluted EPS of $12.60-13.40.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The 18.6x forward P/E implies roughly $11.90”; “the algorithm implies $12.15–12.60.”

surprises.description: The preview estimated Q4 restaurant operating margin at about 18.2–18.5%, but Brinker reported 18%. That was 20–50 basis points below the estimate, although it met the preview’s separate 18.0% minimum and improved 20 basis points year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 Brinker restaurant operating margin was 18%, up 20 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Restaurant op. margin ~18.2–18.5% (estimate)”; “Restaurant margin of at least 18.0%.”

surprises.description: The preview said Maggiano’s stabilization would be a quiet tailwind, but management said its turnaround was slower than planned and FY27 guidance assumes flat revenue and profits. That points to no near-term growth contribution from the segment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Maggiano's turnaround has been slower than planned,” and FY27 guidance assumes “flat revenues and flat profits year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Stabilization would be a quiet tailwind.”

surprises.description: Management reported that July and August sales and traffic accelerated significantly, with Q1 Chili’s comps running above Q4’s 6%. The preview flagged quarter-to-date cadence as something to watch but did not anticipate this acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “July and August sales and traffic significantly accelerated, implying Q1 Chili's comps are running above the 6% reported in Q4.”

in_line: Q4 adjusted diluted EPS of $3.07 matched the preview’s $3.07 consensus estimate.
Chili’s Q4 same-store sales growth of 6% was within the preview’s 5.5–6.0% base-case range and its cited 5.5–6.0% buy-side chatter.
The $350 million bond redemption matched the preview’s expectation that Brinker would call $350 million of 8.25% notes early in FY27.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $4.4 million, well below the preview's roughly $7.0 million consensus and its $5.4 million base case. The shortfall came despite record Commercial Pool revenue, with lower Water for Energy activity, DPF production constraints, and softer plastics purchasing weighing on results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 12% year-over-year to $4.4 million from $5.0 million,” driven by “lower Water for Energy activity, DPF production constraints, and softer plastics purchasing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (Q2) ~$7.0M”; preview base case: “total Q2 revenue is about $5.4M.”

surprises.description: Management cut FY26 revenue guidance to $20–23 million from $23–27 million, below the preview's $23 million consensus estimate at the low end of the prior guide. The cut followed a major Water for Energy project's delay after a customer organizational change restarted its approval process.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cut its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $20-23 million” after “a major Water for Energy project was delayed” and the customer “restarted its internal approval process.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue: $23.0M (about the low end of guidance)” and company guidance of “$23–27M,” which had been “reaffirmed in February and May 2026.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 8.4%, well short of the preview's 20% on-track benchmark and lower than Q1's 9.5%. The preview expected volume to test the fixed-cost absorption story; instead, unfavorable mix and lower utilization left margins below the level needed to absorb fixed production costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin fell to 8.4% from 9.8% a year earlier,” and remained “below the level needed to fully absorb fixed production costs,” reflecting “unfavorable product mix and lower manufacturing utilization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Margins at or above 20% would be on track.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was negative $1.6 million, substantially worse than the preview's $0.85 million loss base case, though close to its $1.55 million loss bear case. The preview noted there was no published consensus, so this is a miss against its own scenario estimate rather than Street consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined to negative $1.6 million from negative $1.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview base scenario: “Adj. EBITDA $(0.85)M”; bear scenario: “$(1.55)M.” The preview also said, “No published consensus.”

surprises.description: Cash including restricted cash reached $15.7 million, above the preview's $12–13 million pro forma estimate. The June offering also generated about $18 million net, versus the preview's estimate of about $16 million, and enabled repayment of senior promissory and original issue discount notes.
surprises.fact_evidence: The offering “generated approximately $18 million in net proceeds,” boosting cash including restricted cash “to $15.7 million from $2.7 million at the end of Q1,” and “enabled repayment of senior promissory notes and original issue discount notes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “about $16M net” from the offering and “June 30 cash” of “about $12–13M.”

surprises.description: After the quarter, LiqTech secured a $2.1 million follow-on order for four wastewater filtration systems from a U.S. steel manufacturer. The preview did not anticipate this order; roughly 75% is expected to ship by year-end, following 10 months of stable operation of the customer's initial system.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Post-quarter, the company secured a $2.1 million follow-on order for four additional wastewater filtration systems from a U.S. steel manufacturer, with roughly 75% expected to ship by end of 2026.” The customer ordered again after “10 months of stable operation” of its initial silicon carbide membrane system.

surprises.description: The company reported a commercial order in China for four EGR-equipped vessel water treatment systems, with first delivery expected in December. The preview discussed marine timing as a possible risk or upside scenario but did not anticipate this specific commercial order.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marine revenue rose to $0.7 million from $0.4 million a year earlier,” and the company “secured a commercial order for four EGR-equipped vessel water treatment systems in China with first delivery expected in December.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's scenarios mentioned “marine pulled in” or marine slipping to Q3, but did not specify a China order or four systems.

in_line: Commercial Pool delivered the record quarter management had flagged: revenue was $1.5 million, matching the preview's approximate $1.5 million threshold for the record-quarter claim.

surprises.description: The preview flagged the risk that patient starts might be plateauing and asked for June/July cadence. Management said referrals and new patient starts had followed a linear trajectory since launch, offering reassurance on that concern, although it did not provide monthly start figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management cited “a linear trajectory of referrals and new patient starts since launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called monthly starts an open question, asking whether June/July had decelerated or whether starts were accelerating or plateauing.

surprises.description: YUTREPIA’s growth substantially outpaced the overall inhaled prostacyclin market: its growth alone exceeded the category’s entire quarterly growth, and it was approaching 30% net revenue share. The preview discussed category growth but did not set an expectation for this degree of relative share gain.
surprises.fact_evidence: The overall market grew about 6% from $573 million in Q1 to $607 million in Q2, while “YUTREPIA's growth alone exceed[ed] the entire category's growth” and it approached 30% net revenue share.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management reported the inhaled category had grown about 40% since launch; it did not specify an expected Q2 share gain.

surprises.description: The spending outlook was more explicit and heavy on R&D than the preview’s discussion of rising development costs: R&D is expected to double in the second half of 2026 versus the first half and rise again in 2027. That adds pressure to the preview’s concern about whether the 56% EBITDA margin can endure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expense in the second half of 2026 is expected to double first-half levels and increase again in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warned that the “56% EBITDA margin may be a peak if spending keeps building” and noted prior R&D growth, but did not anticipate this stated spending trajectory.

surprises.description: The call introduced a potentially imminent ruling in the 327 patent litigation, saying it could come any day and describing possible royalty or adjunctive relief if Liquidia loses. The preview focused on the '782 case and asked about timing and injunction risk, but did not flag this specific imminent ruling or range of outcomes.
surprises.fact_evidence: A ruling in the “ongoing 327 patent litigation before Judge Andrews could come ‘any day now,’” with outcomes ranging from an unimpeded win to “a royalty or adjunctive relief” if the ruling goes against the company.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified the '782 litigation as the main valuation variable and asked for an update on timing and whether injunction risk was nearer-term.

surprises.description: The call disclosed dose-related improvements in six-minute walk distance in ASCENT PH-ILD without worsening cough scores, a specific clinical result the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: In ASCENT PH-ILD, progressively higher YUTREPIA doses produced 6-minute walk improvements of 21.5, 31.5, and 41 meters at weeks 8, 16, and 24, respectively, “without worsening cough scores.”

surprises.description: Liquidia described a broader near-term clinical program than the preview highlighted: 10 studies for YUTREPIA and L606 are underway or planned to start within 12 months, with the Phase III Re-Spire trial already enrolling. This signals substantial pipeline activity beyond the preview’s focus on Re-Spire and L606 timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company has “10 clinical studies for YUTREPIA and L606 either underway or planned to begin over the next 12 months,” including the Phase III Re-Spire trial, “which is already enrolling.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Re-Spire and L606 enrollment timing as a catalyst to watch, but did not anticipate a 10-study program or say Re-Spire was already enrolling.

in_line: YUTREPIA net product sales of $170.4 million and 31% quarter-over-quarter growth were broadly consistent with the preview’s stated Q2 sales figure and Q1-to-Q2 growth comparison.
The July 31 cumulative commercial figures—about 5,900 prescriptions, more than 5,000 patient starts, and over 1,100 prescribing physicians—matched the preview’s commercial snapshot.
Management reaffirmed its target of at least $1 billion in annual revenue by 2027, consistent with the preview’s stated company target; the call did not provide a tighter revenue outlook.
SG&A was expected to rise as commercial scaling continued, consistent with the preview’s concern about the field-force build and its bear scenario of higher SG&A.

surprises.description: Anterix recognized an approximately $11 million broadband license-exchange gain in Q1 and expects at least a single-digit-million-dollar gain next quarter. That puts sizable gains in the first half, whereas the preview said analysts appeared to place the lumpy gains in the back half; the gains boost reported earnings but are not recurring revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Broadband license exchanges generat[ed] an additional gain of approximately $11 million during the quarter”; management “expects at least single-digit-million dollar broadband license gains in the following quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year consensus of +$5.14 against a –$0.58 quarterly estimate suggests analysts place the lumpy gains in the back half.”

surprises.description: Cash ended the quarter at about $116 million, up from the $98.5 million reported at the prior year-end, rather than tracking toward the preview’s projected FY27 net burn. The increase was substantially supported by $20 million from stock option exercises, so it does not by itself show that operating cash generation exceeded expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Anterix ended the quarter with approximately $116 million in cash and no debt,” with “$16 million in customer payments and $20 million from stock option exercises.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s cash math estimated “roughly $30–45M of net burn in FY27 absent new signings.”

surprises.description: Management described nearly a dozen active utility opportunities across 7-, 8- and 9-digit deal sizes, with conversations accelerating over the prior two months. The preview highlighted FY26’s $23.9 million of new contracts and the need for new agreements, but did not anticipate this breadth of active opportunities; no new signed agreement was specified in the facts provided.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nearly a dozen active utility opportunities spanning 7-digit, 8-digit, and 9-digit deal sizes,” with “conversations accelerating over the past two months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 added only $23.9M”; management said utility talks had moved to “deployment, pricing and time to value,” and “Zero new agreements would be a problem.”

surprises.description: Anterix reported that 40% of counties had been cleared in the full 10 MHz broadband configuration and expressed confidence it could monetize the entire country. The preview discussed clearing costs and the small share of spectrum already contracted, but did not set an expectation for this clearance milestone or for nationwide monetization confidence.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has cleared 40% of counties in the full 10 MHz broadband configuration and expressed confidence it can monetize 100% of the country.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Only ~15% of nationwide spectrum contracted on an MHz-POP basis” and expected clearing costs “slightly above” FY26’s $27 million, but gave no county-clearance target.

surprises.description: SpaceX’s filing covered three FCC dockets, including Anterix’s already-finalized band, rather than only the 900 MHz buildout issue highlighted in the preview. Anterix filed a supporting letter the same day; the broader docket scope was not anticipated, although the preview had already flagged the filing and satellite-related uncertainty.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SpaceX filed an ex parte letter with the FCC across three dockets (including Anterix’s already-finalized band)”; “Anterix filed a supporting letter the same day.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “the SpaceX 900 MHz filing” and said it “could validate satellite demand or erode the terrestrial-exclusive model.”

in_line: Q1 revenue was approximately $2 million, essentially matching the preview’s ~$1.97 million consensus and management’s prior ~$2 million quarterly guide.

Q1 operating expenses of $9.5 million and spectrum-clearing investment of approximately $7 million were broadly consistent with the preview’s FY27 framework of ~$40 million maximum all-in opex and clearing costs slightly above FY26’s $27 million.

The preview expected management to address pricing and the gap between spectrum comparables and the stock’s implied valuation. Management reported utility transactions averaging approximately $1.40 per MHz POP versus $2.50 for the recent AWS-3 auction and an implied value of about $0.60 per MHz POP, reinforcing that expected valuation debate.

The preview expected roughly $25 million of FY27 collections from signed contracts; $16 million was collected in Q1 and roughly $10 million in additional contracted proceeds was expected for the rest of the year, broadly matching that framework.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $33.4 million, about 2% above the preview’s $32.7 million build and grew 2.4% year over year versus the build’s 0.4% growth. This was a modest consolidated revenue upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 2.4% year-over-year to $33.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The preview's own Q2 build: revenue $32.7M (+0.4% YoY).”

surprises.description: SLS revenue came in at $10.1 million, above the preview’s $8.8 million base estimate and its $9.5 million threshold for an upside surprise, although it remained below the $10.8 million year-ago comparison. The segment declined less than the preview’s base case implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SLS (Gander Group casino/gaming) segment revenue declined to $10.1 million from $10.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: ... SLS ~$8.8M”; “Anything at or above $9.5M is a real upside surprise.”

surprises.description: Core Stran revenue was $23.3 million, below the preview’s $23.9 million base estimate, even though it grew 6.9% year over year. It therefore contributed less revenue than the preview’s build assumed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The core Stran segment drove growth with Q2 revenue up 6.9% to $23.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: ... Core Stran ~$23.9M.”

surprises.description: Q2 EBITDA was just $551,000, well below the preview’s roughly $1.25 million estimate; net income also fell year over year to $309,000. The quarter remained profitable, but earnings were substantially weaker than the preview’s build suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net income declined to $309,000 from $643,000 and EBITDA fell to $551,000 from $929,000 in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The preview's own Q2 build: ... EBITDA ~$1.25M, EPS $0.04.”

surprises.description: Management said SLS gross margin should normalize around 26%, below the preview’s expectation that gross margin at or above 31% would support margin repair as structural. The forecast is for SLS specifically, but it signals a lower margin run rate for that segment than the preview’s margin thesis implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided SLS gross margin toward a normalized run rate of roughly 26%, between the recent 24% and prior 28% levels, citing competitive pricing pressure on larger orders.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin at or above 31%. Sustained margins above 31% would support the Gander integration margin repair (+690bps) as structural.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed two sizable enterprise wins—a grocery uniform program expected to generate six figures annually and a construction materials contract projected to deliver nearly seven figures annually—that the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New enterprise wins include a 3-year grocery uniform program expected to generate six figures annually and a construction materials contract projected to deliver nearly seven figures in annual revenue.”

in_line: The company delivered a second consecutive profitable quarter: Q2 net income and EBITDA were both positive, matching the preview’s expectation that consecutive profitability would continue, though the earnings amounts were weaker than its build.
The company resumed buybacks in Q2 and repurchased approximately 131,000 shares for about $272,000, matching the preview’s focus on actual repurchases rather than another statement of intent.

The preview flagged the public warrants’ $4.81 exercise price and Q4 2026 expiration; management’s comment that expiration should remove overhang and simplify the capital structure was consistent with that anticipated narrative.

surprises.description: LiveOne reported Q1 revenue of $19.3–19.4 million, below the $21.23 million consensus and the preview’s roughly $20.7 million base case. That is also below the roughly $21.25 million quarterly average needed to reach the low end of the FY27 revenue guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 consolidated revenue of $19.3-19.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 FY27 Consensus” revenue of “$21.23M”; “The base case is revenue of about $20.7M”; and “Revenue at $85M requires a $21.25M quarterly average.”

surprises.description: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA was $4.3 million, well above the preview’s roughly $1.2 million base-case estimate for a first positive quarter. The audio division also posted record adjusted EBITDA of $6.3 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record adjusted EBITDA of $6.3 million for its audio division, though consolidated adjusted EBITDA was $4.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “That would be the first positive consolidated adj. EBITDA quarter, around $1.2M.”

surprises.description: The strong Slacker EBITDA result was partly driven by non-recurring stock-for-service deals and the elimination of past liabilities, with management saying margins would return to normal without similar deals. This makes the reported contribution less repeatable than the headline EBITDA result suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Slacker's Q1 adjusted EBITDA of $4.7 million was heavily boosted by non-recurring stock-for-service deals and elimination of ~$1.5 million in past liabilities”; management indicated “margins will revert to normal levels absent further such deals.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Slacker trajectory and Tesla conversion. Tesla's exit cost about $65M of annualized revenue. Look for an updated paid-subscriber count and whether Slacker revenue stops declining.”

surprises.description: PodcastOne posted record quarterly revenue of $16.1 million and adjusted EBITDA of $1.6 million, but those figures annualize to about $64 million and $6.4 million—below the lower ends of its FY27 revenue and EBITDA guides if the quarter were carried forward. The preview expected PodcastOne strength, so the record results are tempered by the pace implied against guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PodcastOne delivered record quarterly revenue of $16.1 million and $1.6 million of adjusted EBITDA, now on a run rate exceeding $60 million annually.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “PodcastOne separately guides FY27 to $68–75M revenue and $8–10M adj. EBITDA.”

surprises.description: The balance sheet improved during the quarter: cash rose, stockholders’ equity increased, and liabilities were reduced. That is better than the preview’s emphasis on limited cash, debt maturities, and dilution concerns.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Increased cash by $3.3 million, boosted stockholders' equity by $7 million, and eliminated $5 million in liabilities during the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash was $5.35M and total debt $14.97M at 3/31/26”; the preview also flagged “the maturity schedule on about $14.9M of converts” and stock-for-service issuance.

surprises.description: LiveOne had already completed $7 million of its $12 million repurchase program and said it intended to keep buying shares aggressively. The preview noted buyback activity and authorization, but did not indicate that this much of the program would already be completed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Completed $7 million of its $12 million stock repurchase program” and intends “to continue buying back shares aggressively at current low valuations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “buybacks and additional open-market purchases of PODC shares” and noted that “the company holds buyback authorization.”

surprises.description: Management gave an aspirational target of more than $250 million in revenue within three years and a nearer-term goal of exceeding $100 million, adding ambitious growth targets beyond the FY27 guide discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management set an aspirational target of over $250 million in revenue within three years, with a nearer-term goal of surpassing $100 million.”

surprises.description: Existing Amazon and Paramount partnerships were reported at substantial revenue levels and scaling rapidly, whereas the preview described the B2B pipeline as largely unquantified and focused on other partners.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Amazon now representing over $20 million and Paramount surpassing $27 million in revenues.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “B2B pipeline converting to dollars. AT&T connected car, Samsung TV, Vizio, and LG have not been quantified in revenue.”

surprises.description: LiveOne announced a new four-year agreement with a major global retailer and a podcast-only distribution partnership with Netflix. The preview identified a dollar-sized B2B contract as a potential catalyst but did not anticipate these specific agreements.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Signed a new 4-year retail agreement with a major global retailer and a podcast-only distribution partnership with Netflix and its 700 million members.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A dollar-sized contract is the bull catalyst.”

surprises.description: Management described a potential new AI-content licensing channel, with discussions underway with 17 companies, stated per-hour pricing, and monetization expected to start next quarter. The preview did not flag this opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In discussions with 17 AI companies to license its 500,000+ hours of audio and 250,000+ hours of video content at $100-$500 per hour on a non-exclusive basis, with monetization expected to begin next quarter.”

in_line: Management had previewed continued year-over-year growth in revenue and adjusted EBITDA, as well as buyback activity; the reported quarter showed revenue slightly above the year-ago level, positive consolidated adjusted EBITDA, and continued repurchases.

surprises.description: PFGC’s Q4 sales grew 6.4%, below the preview’s expected 7.2%–7.5% growth, putting the result below both cited sales consensus estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 2026 total net sales grew 6.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Net sales consensus was $18.11B, “+7.2%” year over year, with an alternative estimate of $18.21B, “+7.5%.”

surprises.description: The FY2027 adjusted EBITDA outlook was stronger than the preview’s base expectation: the $2.125B–$2.225B range has a $2.175B midpoint, above the preview’s $2.05B–$2.15B base range and its $2.15B upside threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for … adjusted EBITDA of $2.125-$2.225 billion,” with midpoint growth of 12.7%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected FY27 EBITDA of “$2.05–2.15B”; its catalyst checklist said “above $2.15B supports the re-rating.”

surprises.description: Q4 organic independent restaurant case growth was just below the preview’s 6% bar, rather than reaching the 6%–7% growth expected in its base scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “5.8% organic independent restaurant case growth” in Q4; full-year independent case growth was 5.9%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said growth “below 6% at PFG would weaken the share-gain story” and put base-case cases at “6–7%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was slightly below even the lower of the preview’s two consensus estimates, despite adjusted EBITDA landing at the top of its expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.59,” while the tax rate rose to 26.8% from 25.6%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed adjusted EPS consensus of “$1.60” and an alternative of “$1.62,” with a range of $1.55–$1.64 for the $1.60 estimate.

surprises.description: Management quantified procurement synergies and a multiyear margin opportunity that the preview said had not been quantified beforehand, and expressed confidence in exceeding the high end of the synergy target.
surprises.fact_evidence: PFGC targets “$120-$125 million in procurement synergies,” is confident it will “meet or exceed the high end by fiscal 2028,” and expects “50-60 basis points of EBITDA margin enhancement” over its three-year plan.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Quantified Cheney synergy and cost relief. Management needs to give a number, not adjectives,” and noted that “no quantified figure was available beforehand.”

surprises.description: Convenience showed strength beyond the preview’s broad durability question: EBITDA grew 10.4%, while non-nicotine categories gained mid-single digits against a nearly 6% industry decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The convenience segment delivered 10.4% Q4 EBITDA growth” and key non-nicotine categories were “up mid-single digits against an industry decline of nearly 6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Convenience durability and cash” and said to “watch cigarette carton trends” and the chain pipeline.

surprises.description: Higher diesel expense created a quantified Q4 cost headwind, while management responded with a 12-month hedge for exposure not covered by surcharges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Higher diesel expense created a ~$16 million net headwind in Q4 (mostly hitting foodservice),” and management entered “a 12-month diesel fuel swap in early July” for exposure not covered by surcharges.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bear scenario cited “fuel costs persist,” but did not quantify a diesel impact or describe a hedge.

surprises.description: Management indicated that FY2027 EBITDA growth would accelerate through the year, addressing the preview’s concern that acceleration might be deferred to a second-half-weighted profile.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q1 FY2027 EBITDA guidance is “$510-$530 million,” with management “signaling EBITDA growth will accelerate through the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bear case included management “deferring the FY27 acceleration to ‘second half weighted.’”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a future chain-volume addition from New Jersey Mike’s: business from three of the four awarded regions is expected to begin flowing after mid-FY2027, a named opportunity not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New Jersey Mike's business (3 of 4 awarded regions) begins flowing in past mid-fiscal 2027 to boost chain volume.”

surprises.description: Management said competitive losses will partly offset the Love’s and Racetrack convenience tailwind, an offset not called out in the preview’s discussion of the chain pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Love's and Racetrack provide an incremental convenience tailwind through mid-fiscal 2027 partly offset by competitive losses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described convenience’s “chain pipeline” and noted Love’s and RaceTrac onboarding, without mentioning competitive losses.

in_line: Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $587.5 million was at the upper end of the preview’s $558–$588 million implied range.
Q4 adjusted EPS of $1.59 was close to the preview’s $1.60 consensus, though slightly below it.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $196.3 million, above the preview’s $184.7 million consensus estimate. The preview also cited a lower implied estimate of about $166 million, so the size of the beat depends on which estimate is used.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 revenues rose 27% year-over-year to $196.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 FY26 revenue | $184.7M”; the preview also listed “Q4 FY26 revenue (implied) | ~$166M.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted operating income was $18.6 million, well above the prior-year quarter’s $1.3 million loss and clear of the preview’s stated below-breakeven downside case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income [swung] to $18.6 million from a $1.3 million loss in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything below breakeven is a negative signal”; the preview also said a third straight quarter of negative operating leverage would challenge the bull case.

surprises.description: The Garden’s concert count more than doubled in Q4, a stronger description of the rebound than the preview’s qualitative expectation of a “significant increase.” This was the stated driver of the quarter’s revenue and adjusted operating income improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q4 results were “driven by more than doubling the number of concerts at the Garden.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had guided to a “significant increase in the number of concerts at the Garden in our fiscal fourth quarter.”

surprises.description: Full-year revenue grew 13%, above the preview’s 9.4% growth estimate. The call also reported revenue exceeding $1 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 full-year revenues exceeded $1 billion (up 13%).”

surprises.description: Theaters were only about 60% toward their bookings goal and were pacing behind for both the September and December quarters, unlike the Garden, which was about 90% toward its goal. The preview discussed Garden concert growth and named theater dates but did not flag this theater-booking shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is roughly 90% toward its Garden bookings goal but only ~60% toward its theater goal, with theaters pacing behind for both the September and December quarters.”

surprises.description: The Christmas Spectacular delivered record attendance and approximately $195 million in revenue, details not anticipated in the preview. The preview did already expect the season to expand to 230 shows.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Christmas Spectacular set a record with over 1.2 million tickets sold across 215 performances (highest attendance in 25 years) generating approximately $195 million in revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “a 230-show Christmas Spectacular (+7% shows)” and flagged “Christmas Spectacular pricing and on-sale pace on 230 shows.”

surprises.description: The call put a recurring cash component on Arena license fees at approximately $47 million for fiscal 2027, with 3% annual growth through fiscal 2055; the preview did not discuss these fees.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The cash component of Arena license fees will be approximately $47 million in fiscal 2027 and will grow 3% annually through fiscal 2055.”

in_line: The Christmas Spectacular is expanding to 230 shows for the 2026 season, matching the preview’s expectation of a 230-show season.
The 30-date Harry Styles residency and the expectation of a record number of Garden concerts in fiscal Q1 were already identified in the preview.
The Knicks’ championship-related revenue benefit was anticipated as a key issue: the preview flagged monetization from the Finals run and expected strong arena attendance to help.

surprises.description: Hyliion reported Q2 revenue of $4.9 million, well above the $2.4 million consensus estimate. The result was also above the preview’s $3.5 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $4.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 Consensus” revenue of “$2.40M”; the bull scenario anticipated “$3.5M+.”

surprises.description: Hyliion raised 2026 revenue guidance to approximately $15 million, up from $10 million. The preview expected the $10 million guide to be reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hyliion raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance by 50%, from $10 million to approximately $15 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 company guidance (reaffirmed at Q1): ~$10M revenue”; the catalyst checklist asked whether it was “raised or reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: The 200-kilowatt system’s commercialization moved into 2027, rather than remaining on the preview’s year-end 2026 timeline. This is a delay to a milestone the preview identified as a key debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “200-kilowatt commercialization now pushed into 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had said the 200 kW rating should be reached “by year-end,” and the preview said year-end 2026 commercialization was the key question.

surprises.description: The company ended Q2 with $132.4 million in cash and investments, above the preview’s expected $126–127 million. That indicates a better quarter-end cash position than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $132.4 million in cash and investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for cash and investments of $126–127M at June 30.”

surprises.description: Hyliion now expects year-end cash of $115–120 million, versus the preview’s approximately $100 million outlook. The projected year-end balance improved by about $20 million from prior guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Now expects to finish 2026 with $115-$120 million, a ~$20 million improvement over prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “~$100M year-end cash and investments” in the reaffirmed guidance.

surprises.description: Q2 net loss was $13.9 million, slightly worse than the preview’s estimated $12–13 million loss. The miss was limited, but went against the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss was $13.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss ~$12–13M (est.).”

surprises.description: Hyliion disclosed a production-capacity and investment framework not previously quantified in the preview: its 30 printers could produce up to 15 megawatts of annual Carnot core capacity, with about $1.5 million of printer investment supporting 1 megawatt of capacity and roughly $2.5–3 million in annual revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately $1.5 million in printer investment can support 1 megawatt of annual Carnot production capacity,” representing “roughly $2.5-$3 million of annual revenue”; “the existing fleet of 30 printers is now estimated capable of producing up to 15 megawatts per year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “declined to give 2027–28 production capacity at Q1” and that any first framing of capacity or unit economics “would be new information.”

surprises.description: Management described additive-manufacturing improvements that could raise print speed and throughput by as much as three times, although the gains are still being validated. The preview did not anticipate this specific potential productivity improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Additive manufacturing improvements [management] believes could increase print speed and throughput by up to three times, though this is still being validated.”

in_line: Management expects total new military contracts in 2026 to approach $50 million, in line with the preview’s stated expectation of $40–50 million of additional military contracts in 2H26.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $11.9 million, about 9.8% above the $10.84 million consensus estimate, even though it fell year over year as expected contract work ended. This was a modest beat against the estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 revenue was $11.9 million, down approximately 31% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus: $10.84M.

surprises.description: Stabilis executed a new six-month behind-the-meter LNG data center commissioning contract, with deliveries beginning in August 2026 and the possibility of an extension. The preview did not flag this near-term contract.
surprises.fact_evidence: A new six-month behind-the-meter LNG data center commissioning contract was executed, with equipment deploying now and LNG deliveries beginning in August 2026, and could extend beyond six months.

surprises.description: Management projected adjusted EBITDA margins in the high teens for 2027, an added profitability outlook beyond the preview’s discussion of the expected revenue level. The company said this was a projection, not formal guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management projects 2027 to be a record year with total company revenue exceeding $100 million and adjusted EBITDA margin expanding to the high teens, though no formal 2027 guidance was provided.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the 2027 figure appeared to rest almost entirely on the single data center contract; its bull scenario called for 2027 to be quantified.

surprises.description: Aerospace LNG accelerated well beyond the prior growth rate cited in the preview: volumes rose 79% year over year and aerospace revenue rose 71%. Stabilis also reported serving three rocket-launch customers, with a fourth in discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: Aerospace LNG volumes sold rose 79% year-over-year and 87% sequentially, with aerospace revenue up 71% year-over-year, and the company has served three rocket launch customers with a fourth in discussion.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted aerospace was up 31% year over year in Q1 and called it the cleanest growth line to watch.

surprises.description: Non-power-generation industrial volumes grew more than 67% year over year, an additional growth source the preview did not identify as an expected development.
surprises.fact_evidence: Non-power-generation industrial business volumes grew more than 67% year-over-year.

surprises.description: The preview flagged approximately $2.9 million of vessel charter expense as a major drag and asked whether it was one-time or ongoing. Management tied the excluded cost to a terminated LNG bunkering vessel lease, indicating it was associated with a terminated arrangement.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA fell to just $0.1 million ... and excludes approximately $2.9 million of vessel charter costs from a terminated LNG bunkering vessel lease.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged $2.9M of vessel charter expense as the main drag on EPS and asked whether it was one-time or run-rate.

surprises.description: The company reported that it had received the full $25 million of customer prepayments for the 2027 data center contract, with no further payments expected. The preview highlighted the need to determine how much cash was restricted and tied to future contract revenue, but did not anticipate that the full prepayment amount would already have been collected.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company has received the full $25 million in customer prepayments for the 2027 data center contract ($20 million by end of Q2 plus $5 million early in Q3), funding equipment and mobilization with no further payments expected.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to check how much cash was restricted and how much was customer advances tied to 2027 revenue.

in_line: Management’s expectation that second-half 2026 revenue would be more than 50% above the first half, with profitability building in Q3 and Q4, matched the preview’s stated H2 recovery expectation.
Adjusted EBITDA of $0.1 million was just above breakeven, broadly in line with the preview’s base expectation of EBITDA near breakeven.

The projection for 2027 revenue to exceed $100 million was broadly consistent with the preview’s discussion of the two-year, approximately $200 million data center contract and its scenario for quantified 2027 results.

surprises.description: Atea ended June with $219.5 million in cash and marketable securities, above the preview’s $208–215 million base-case range and its $215 million bull-case threshold. The preview also noted that no cash consensus estimate was available.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$219.5 million in cash and marketable securities as of June 30, 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base case: “cash $208–215M”; bull case: “cash ≥ $215M.” The preview says cash consensus was “Not found.”

surprises.description: Management put a specific, sizeable commercial opportunity on the table: peak annual U.S. net revenue potential above $700 million and a U.S. market that could expand to $2.5 billion annually. The preview focused on pricing risk but gave no sales or market-size estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management projects peak annual U.S. net revenue potential in excess of $700 million, with the total U.S. market potentially expandable up to $2.5 billion annually.”

surprises.description: The call added favorable market-research evidence for uptake: 76% of high-volume DAA prescribers said they would be extremely likely to prescribe bem-rusosvir, while only 6% of surveyed physicians saw no unmet need. The preview flagged payer and pricing questions but did not report prescriber-interest data.
surprises.fact_evidence: “76% of high-volume DAA prescribers saying they would be extremely likely to prescribe bem-rusosvir, and only 6% of surveyed physicians reporting no unmet need in current therapies.”

surprises.description: C-BEYOND showed a favorable safety profile beyond the efficacy result already known: there were no serious adverse events or study-drug-related early discontinuations, and no deaths in the bem-rusosvir arm versus three non-drug-related deaths in the Epclusa arm. The preview discussed the non-inferiority result and subgroup questions, but did not preview these safety findings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “No serious adverse events or early discontinuations due to study drugs, and no deaths in the bem-rusosvir arm versus three (non-drug-related) deaths in the Epclusa arm.”

surprises.description: C-FORWARD is already fully enrolled, a concrete trial-execution milestone not mentioned in the preview. Its early-Q1 2027 topline timing remains consistent with the preview’s early-2027 expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “C-Forward…is fully enrolled with top-line results expected in early Q1 2027.”

in_line: C-BEYOND’s 93.9% SVR rate versus 94.8% for Epclusa and statistical non-inferiority match the preview’s reported topline result and 5% margin.
C-FORWARD topline remains on the expected early-2027 schedule; the preview’s base case anticipated an NDA tied to C-FORWARD, and the call specifies Q2 2027 pending positive results.
The company reaffirmed a cash runway through 2027, as the preview expected.
AT-587’s Phase 1 initiation in July 2026 is consistent with the preview’s expectation of initiation in mid-2026.
A mid-2028 launch is consistent with the preview’s expectation that waiting for C-FORWARD would push first revenue toward 2028.

surprises.description: Revenue was $16.1 million, below the preview’s roughly $18.0 million consensus and its $16.8–$17.5 million base scenario, though within the preview’s bear range. The record result and year-over-year growth therefore fell short of the revenue level investors were led to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue reached a record $16.1 million, driven by audience and advertising growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$18.0M”; the base scenario projected “$16.8–17.5M.”

surprises.description: GAAP profitability was worse than the preview’s near-breakeven EPS scenarios: the company reported a $0.05-per-share loss, versus expectations ranging from a $0.01 loss to $0.01 of earnings. The wider operating loss was attributed primarily to higher stock-based compensation in G&A.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss was $1.6 million, or negative $0.05 per share,” versus $1.1 million, or negative $0.04 per share, a year earlier; “Operating loss widened to $1.6 million from $1.1 million” primarily due to higher stock-based compensation within G&A.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited GAAP EPS consensus of “+$0.01 (range -$0.01 to +$0.02)” and a base scenario of “-$0.01 to $0.00.”

surprises.description: PodcastOne reported a stronger publisher-ranking milestone than the preview discussed: it reached No. 6 in Podtrac’s U.S. rankings, passed Disney, and held that position into July. This is positive evidence of audience scale, with no such milestone anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PodcastOne advanced to the #6 position in Podtrac's U.S. podcast publisher rankings, surpassing Disney, and maintained that spot into July.”

surprises.description: Management described video distribution as enabling higher advertising CPMs and said major brands are entering the space, an advertising-monetization opportunity the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Video-format podcasts and distribution across YouTube, Netflix, and Hulu are enabling higher advertising CPMs, with blue-chip brands like Progressive, State Farm, Macy's, and Lowe's entering the space.”

surprises.description: The call reported new content acquisitions and original launches, along with more than 2.5 million downloads for the renewed Southern Tea partnership. These portfolio and show-traction updates were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expanded its content portfolio through acquisitions including The Magnificent Others with Billy Corgan and Life Happens with Barb and Michelle, plus original series launches”; “The Southern Tea” surpassed “2.5 million downloads across more than 248 episodes.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was $1.6 million, at the top of the preview’s $1.2–$1.6 million base-scenario range; the preview had no published adjusted EBITDA consensus.
The preview looked for contribution-margin improvement, and the call attributed the nearly threefold year-over-year adjusted EBITDA increase partly to “contribution margin improvement.”
Revenue and adjusted EBITDA both grew year over year, consistent with the August 4 pre-announcement of “continued year-over-year growth in revenue and Adjusted EBITDA.”
The call’s description of summer as slower and calendar Q4 as seasonally strongest is consistent with the preview’s expectation that Q1 would be the seasonally softest advertising quarter.

surprises.description: Q2 QUELIMMUNE revenue was $615,000, about 12% above the preview’s $550,000 modeled estimate and just above its $520,000–$600,000 base scenario, though still within the broader modeled range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 QUELIMMUNE net revenue reached $615,000,” up 82% year over year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue about $0.55M (range $0.42–$0.72M)” and base scenario “$0.52–0.60M.”

surprises.description: Cash at quarter-end was approximately $7 million, above the preview’s expected $6.0–$6.6 million range. It was not clearly above the preview’s more optimistic “above $7.0M” bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash fell to approximately $7 million at June 30, 2026 from $12 million at December 31, 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash at June 30: $6.0–6.6M”; the bull case specified “Above $7.0M.”

surprises.description: Enrollment was slightly below the preview’s 225-patient checkpoint, and the reported pace was below what the preview said was needed to complete enrollment by year-end. Management now gave a completion window extending into Q1 2027, rather than the preview’s year-end expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The neutralize AKI adult pivotal trial has enrolled 223 of a targeted 339 patients,” with enrollment expected to complete “around year-end 2026 or in Q1 2027”; current enrollment is “roughly 8-12 patients per month.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Q2 count below about 225 puts the YE2026 completion target and 2027 PMA at risk”; the preview said enrollment needed “about 35+ per quarter to finish by year-end” and listed completion “~YE2026.”

in_line: Net loss of $3.7 million and EPS of -$0.91 were within the preview’s modeled ranges of $3.3–$3.7 million and -$0.83 to -$0.93, respectively.
The company said it remained on track toward its FY2026 net revenue target of $2 million, consistent with the preview’s cited management target.
The late-2027 PMA submission timeline was unchanged, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a 2027 PMA.

surprises.description: The preview estimated June 30 stockholders’ equity at roughly $1.3–2.0 million and expected it to remain below Nasdaq’s $2.5 million minimum. BioCardia reported $2.7 million in equity and said it maintained Nasdaq compliance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BioCardia ended Q2 2026 with $5.4 million in cash and $2.7 million in equity (maintaining NASDAQ compliance).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My roll-forward gives about $1.5M, which is short” of the “$2.5M” minimum; estimated equity was “~$1.3–2.0M, likely below $2.5M.”

surprises.description: Cash ended the quarter well above the preview’s $3.5–4.0 million estimate. The reported runway into 2027 broadly matched the preview’s expectation of runway into Q1 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BioCardia ended Q2 2026 with $5.4 million in cash”; this was “providing runway into 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash, 6/30/26” estimate: “~$3.5–4.0M”; the preview said to check whether runway extended “into Q1 2027.”

surprises.description: BioCardia’s $1.6 million Q2 net loss was substantially lower than the preview’s estimated $2.2–2.4 million loss, despite the preview’s view that the P&L was unlikely to surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed to $1.6 million in Q2 2026 from $2.0 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Net loss” of “−$2.2M to −$2.4M” and said, “The P&L is unlikely to surprise.”

surprises.description: The PMDA supported moving BioCardia’s cardiac cell therapy toward a Japanese Shonin pre-market submission, judging the CARDiAMP outcomes credible. The preview anticipated a Q4 submission but did not anticipate this regulatory endorsement or the stated roughly 12-month path from submission to approval.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PMDA supported BioCardia's advancement to Shonin pre-market regulatory submission,” “deeming the CARDiAMP trial outcomes credible”; submission is expected in Q4 2026 and approval “approximately 12 months after submission.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The company said it expected Japan Shonin submission in Q4 2026.”

surprises.description: FDA meeting minutes indicated that the ongoing CARDiAMP Heart Failure II trial may serve as a confirmatory study supporting premarket approval, reversing the agency’s prior reluctance to accept a single trial for this indication. The preview focused on enrollment progress and did not flag this regulatory change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FDA meeting minutes confirmed the ongoing CARDiAMP Heart Failure II trial may support premarket approval as a confirmatory study, a shift from prior FDA reluctance to accept a single trial for this indication.”

surprises.description: FDA feedback for the Helix catheter was clearer and more favorable than the preview’s general note about active partnering discussions: the agency raised no safety, performance, or compatibility concerns and agreed to two potential clearance pathways.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FDA raised no concerns on Helix catheter safety, device performance, or compatibility, and agreed to two potential pathways for marketing clearance,” including de novo approval that could make Helix the first FDA-approved transendocardial biotherapeutic delivery catheter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Partnering (Helix/Heart3D, CardiALLO)” as an issue to watch and said management described “active discussions. No signed deal has been announced.”

surprises.description: CARDiAMP Heart Failure II had not expanded beyond the four active sites reported at the prior quarter, and management described enrollment as slow while declining to disclose total enrollment. The preview highlighted site expansion and patient enrollment as key progress measures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Only four clinical sites are currently actively enrolling patients”; management called the pace resource-driven and “not going at blazing speeds,” and declined to disclose total enrollment.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Four sites were active at Q1” and identified “Site count and patients enrolled” as the main progress measures, with expansion from four sites as a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: The call added a potentially significant Japanese market reference that the preview had not discussed: the initial indication targets about 20,000 patients, and a comparable cell therapy had recently received reimbursement at $326,000 per treatment. This provides a concrete commercial benchmark, though it is for a peer product rather than BioCardia’s therapy.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The initial Japan indication targets approximately 20,000 patients out of an estimated 300,000 with ischemic heart failure,” and “Heartseed/ReHeart” was “approved for reimbursement in July at $326,000 per treatment.”

surprises.description: Q2 R&D expense was lower than the preview’s estimate, although the decline was attributed to closing out the original CARDiAMP heart failure trial rather than a clearly stated efficiency gain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expense decreased $0.5 million to $0.9 million in Q2 2026, primarily due to the closeout of the original CARDiAMP heart failure trial.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 R&D at “~$1.3M.”

in_line: The expected timing for the Japan Shonin submission remained Q4 2026.
The reported runway into 2027 was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of runway into Q1 2027, even though ending cash exceeded its estimate.
The preview already identified approximately $4.9 million of ATM proceeds raised before June 5, so the reported approximately $4.9 million of Q2 net ATM proceeds was not a new funding surprise.

surprises.description: Comparable sales fell just 0.3%, far better than the preview’s expected decline of 1.5% to 2.0%. Opportunistic comps accelerated during the quarter, and total-company comps turned positive in May and June.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Comparable store sales down 30 basis points,” beating the outlook for a 1.5%-2% decline; opportunistic comps “accelerated about 500bp” from the start of Q1, and total-company comps were positive in May and June.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Comparable store sales” guidance of “-1.5% to -2.0%”; the preview also says a beat needs ticket improvement.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was well above both the company’s $55 million to $58 million outlook and the roughly $56 million consensus, despite remaining below the year-ago result.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA was “$65.7 million,” compared with $67.7 million a year ago.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA” consensus of “~$56M” and company guidance of “$55M to $58M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.20 substantially exceeded the preview’s $0.11 to $0.13 adjusted framework and $0.12 consensus, although it was down from $0.23 a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EPS was “$0.20,” versus $0.23 a year ago.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted adj. EPS” consensus of “$0.12” and company guidance of “$0.11 to $0.13.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 30.2%, topping the company’s 29.8% to 30.0% outlook; its 30-basis-point year-over-year decline was also less severe than the roughly 70-basis-point contraction anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin was “30.2%,” exceeding the “29.8%-30.0% outlook” and declining “30bp year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Gross margin outlook of “29.8% to 30.0%” and consensus of “~-70bp YoY.”

surprises.description: The company raised the low end of its full-year comparable-sales and adjusted EBITDA ranges, rather than merely reaffirming or trimming the prior outlook. It also gave full-year net-sales and adjusted-EPS ranges.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company raised the low end to comps of “-0.5% to 0.0%” and adjusted EBITDA of “$225-$235 million,” and gave net sales guidance of “$4.7-$4.72 billion” and adjusted EPS of “$0.51-$0.55.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior FY26 guidance was comps of “-2.0% to 0.0%” and adjusted EBITDA of “$220M to $235M”; the preview asked whether EBITDA would be “reaffirmed or trimmed.”

surprises.description: A multi-state cyclospora outbreak is expected to weigh on Q3 comparable sales by about 100 basis points, an unexpected near-term headwind in the preview’s discussion of Q3 comps.
surprises.fact_evidence: The outbreak is expected to create “a roughly 100bp headwind to total company comps in Q3,” though products were not involved in recalls.

surprises.description: The company reported a sizable positive comp in grocery, its largest category, and plans to extend the opportunistic playbook into deli and frozen; the preview did not flag this category result or expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The grocery category, the company's largest, comped 3.5% in Q2” as the playbook is extended to deli and frozen next.

surprises.description: Management said the planned $20 million promotional bridge will fully taper by the end of Q3 and could give way to a gross-margin tailwind in 2027 as opportunistic product replaces promotions; the preview anticipated promo roll-off generally, but not this stated timing and potential later benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: The “$20 million incremental promotional ‘synthetic bridge’ is set to fully taper by the end of Q3,” potentially creating “a gross margin tailwind in 2027” as opportunistic product replaces promotions.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “about $20M of planned promotional investment” and said Q2 gross margin at or above 29.8% would support management’s “promo roll-off view.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $1.19 billion modestly exceeded the $1.167 billion consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue was “$1.19 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Net-sales consensus was “$1,167M (Zacks).”

in_line: All 36 underperforming store closures were completed by April, as the preview said they had been; the call said the plan remains on track to eliminate the associated annualized EBITDA drag.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $17.3 billion, above the roughly $16.83 billion consensus and the company’s $16.7–$16.9 billion guide. The beat was about 2.8% versus consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue reached a record $17.3 billion”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus | ~$16.83B”; “Company guide (May 14) | $16.7B–$16.9B”

surprises.description: Q4 non-GAAP EPS of $1.22 exceeded the $1.17 consensus and the high end of the $1.16–$1.18 company guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “non-GAAP EPS of $1.22 up 23%, exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | Consensus | $1.17”; “Company guide (May 14) | $1.16–$1.18”

surprises.description: FY27 revenue guidance of $72.2–$73.4 billion implies roughly 15% growth at the midpoint, well above the preview’s Street assumption of about 9.5% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 guidance calls for revenue of $72.2-$73.4 billion (roughly 15% growth at midpoint)”
