surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 Street assumptions: ~9.5% revenue growth (about $68.7B–$69.0B)”

surprises.description: FY27 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $5.05–$5.11 was above the preview’s roughly $4.80 Street assumption and even above the top of Evercore’s $4.80–$5.00 reference range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “non-GAAP EPS of $5.05-$5.11”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 Street assumptions: ... ~$4.80 EPS”; “Evercore ISI expects $4.80–$5.00 EPS”

surprises.description: Cisco reported $9.3 billion of FY26 hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders, above the $9 billion target; the preview had identified about $3.7 billion of Q4 orders as necessary to reach that target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI infrastructure orders from hyperscalers totaled $9.3 billion in FY26”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 AI infrastructure orders against ~$3.7B needed to reach the $9B target”

surprises.description: The FY27 AI infrastructure revenue target of $7.5 billion exceeded Morgan Stanley’s $6.5–$7 billion expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “guiding to $7.5 billion in AI infrastructure revenue for FY27 versus $4 billion in FY26.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “the FY27 AI revenue target against Morgan Stanley's $6.5B–$7B expectation.”

surprises.description: The preview raised campus-networking saturation as a key concern, but Cisco reported 40% growth in networking product orders, including 20% growth in Campus Networking orders; total product orders rose 35%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q4 product orders grew 35% year-over-year”; “Networking product orders grew 40%”; “Campus Networking orders up 20%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Campus networking saturation is the core bear argument.”

surprises.description: FY27 growth in the core business excluding AI was implied to be about 10%, substantially stronger than the preview’s estimate of roughly 4% ex-AI growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “the core business ex-AI implied to grow about 10%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total growth of ~7% falls to roughly 4% ex-AI.”

surprises.description: Security revenue grew 14% in Q4, well ahead of the preview’s expected 4.7% growth after a flat Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Security revenue grew 14% in Q4”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Security. $2.04B expected, +4.7%, after a flat Q3.”

surprises.description: Management said the security quarter benefited from unusually large on-prem Splunk deals with longer duration, a qualification to the stronger-than-expected security growth that the preview did not specify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “the quarter benefited from unusually large on-prem Splunk deals with longer duration.”

surprises.description: Cisco secured three new hyperscaler AI design wins in Q4 and said it had line of sight to multiple additional wins over the next six months; the preview focused on AI orders and revenue targets rather than new design wins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company secured three new hyperscaler design wins in Q4 ... with line of sight to multiple additional AI design wins over the next six months.”

surprises.description: Q4 non-GAAP gross margin was 66.3%, 40 basis points above the preview’s approximately 65.9% estimate. The FY27 operating-margin framing was also about 35%, versus the preview’s roughly 34% reference.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin ... 66.3%”; “management guiding FY27 for slight further gross margin headwind but ~35% operating margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Street models ~65.9% for Q4”; “Evercore ISI expects ... a ~34% EBIT margin.”

surprises.description: FY26 revenue of $63.3 billion finished above the company’s $62.8–$63.0 billion full-year guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY26 revenue was a record $63.3 billion”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 full-year guide: revenue $62.8B–$63.0B”

surprises.description: FY26 non-GAAP EPS of $4.33 exceeded the company’s $4.27–$4.29 full-year guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “non-GAAP EPS of $4.33”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 full-year guide: ... non-GAAP EPS $4.27–$4.29”

in_line: Management expected slight further gross-margin headwinds in FY27, consistent with the preview’s concern that AI mix could weigh on margins, even though Q4 gross margin and the operating-margin framing were better than the preview’s reference points.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was about $243,000, well below the preview’s $500,000–$900,000 base range and the roughly $600,000 level it said was needed to keep the full-year $2.9 million comparison credible. First-half adjusted EBITDA was a loss of about $224,000.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell to about $243,000 in Q2 2026 from roughly $628,000 a year earlier, and first-half adjusted EBITDA was a loss of about $224,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base” scenario: adjusted EBITDA of “$0.5–0.9M”; catalyst checklist: “Adjusted EBITDA at or above about $0.6M, to keep the $2.9M FY25 comparison credible.”

surprises.description: Loss per share was $0.13, worse than the preview’s $0.07 consensus loss and below its base-case range of a $0.05–$0.10 loss. The reported weighted-average share count was also higher year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Loss per share was $0.13 in Q2 2026 on ~12.8 million weighted average shares, up from ~11.2 million shares a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP EPS” consensus: “$(0.07)”; base scenario: “$(0.10) to $(0.05).”

surprises.description: The quarter included roughly $720,000–$800,000 in retention bonuses and litigation-related legal fees that the preview did not flag. Management said both costs are expected to roll off in Q3, so they weighed on Q2 results but are described as temporary.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately $360,000-$400,000 of one-time retention bonuses and another ~$360,000-$400,000 of litigation-related legal fees, both expected to roll off in Q3.”

surprises.description: Management described a more concrete path to improved free cash flow than the preview laid out: bank debt is expected to mature in about two years, freeing roughly $2.2 million annually in principal and interest, and New York and Los Angeles leases rolling off late next year are expected to save about $1 million annually.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects meaningfully improved free cash flow” from “bank debt maturing in about two years (freeing ~$2.2 million annually in principal and interest) and NY/LA leases rolling off in late next year (saving ~$1 million annually).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had described the bank debt as maturing “in about 2.5 years” and identified liquidity and refinancing as issues to watch.

surprises.description: Cash was $7.7 million at quarter-end, above the preview’s $6.3 million March 31 reference point. That is a quarter-over-quarter build, although cash remained below the $8.8 million reported at year-end 2025.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents declined to $7.7 million as of June 30, 2026, from $8.8 million at year-end 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch cash “against $6.3M at 3/31/26” and that “a build supports the cash-flow claim.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed approximately $127 million in NOLs and said they allow nearly all future cost savings to flow directly to the bottom line, a potential benefit not raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company holds approximately $127 million in NOLs, allowing nearly all future cost savings to flow directly to the bottom line.”

surprises.description: The CEO said he expects to own more than 5% of DLPN within a week or two under his 10b5-1 buying plan. The preview did not anticipate this additional signal of insider alignment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CEO Bill O'Dowd expects to own over 5% of DLPN common stock within the next week or two under his 10b5-1 buying plan.”

surprises.description: Beyond the expected first Dealmaker venture before year-end, management identified two candidates and said it aspires to complete three to four capital-light equity-plus-fee ventures annually within a few years. The pipeline and longer-term pace were not detailed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects its first Dealmaker venture deal in market before year-end, with two candidates identified and an aspiration to complete 3-4 capital-light equity-plus-fee ventures annually within a few years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed a “first deal by YE2026” as management’s target.

in_line: Revenue was $14.4 million versus the preview’s $14.5 million consensus, with reported year-over-year growth of 2.5% versus the preview’s implied 2.8%.
The expected timing for a first Dealmaker deal—to have one in market before year-end—was reiterated.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $18.5 million was below the roughly $22.2 million quarterly pace implied by the preview’s FY26 consensus estimate after Q1. The preview cautioned that the consensus was stale, so this is a shortfall against an indicative pace rather than a reliable Q2 consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose 23% year-over-year to $18.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 consensus of $82.62M less Q1's $16.0M leaves about $66.6M for Q2–Q4, or roughly $22.2M per quarter.”

surprises.description: Emrosi prescriptions accelerated to 20% sequential growth in Q2, and June set a new monthly high, countering the preview’s concern that the April prescription peak might not be sustainable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Emrosi prescriptions totaled approximately 36,000 in Q2, up 20% sequentially from ~30,000 in Q1, accelerating from the 11% sequential growth seen the prior quarter”; “June set an all-time monthly high with over 5,300 new Emrosi prescriptions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “April's prescription peak proves not to be the run rate” was listed as a bear-case risk.

surprises.description: Emrosi revenue rose from $6.3 million in Q1 to $8.1 million in Q2, a substantial sequential increase that supports the ramp the preview identified as central to the story.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Emrosi generated $8.1 million in net revenue in Q2 2026, up significantly year-over-year and sequentially from Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Emrosi net revenue. Q1 was $6.3M. This line drives the equity story”; “Strong growth would restore credibility.”

surprises.description: Emrosi’s average selling price rose about 10% sequentially in Q2, despite the preview’s concern that the April GPO contracts could trade price for volume.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Emrosi's calculated average selling price increased in Q2 over Q1 (about a 10% boost) after also rising in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue per prescription (about $210 in Q1) matters as much as volume, since GPO contracts signed April 1 may trade price for volume”; “GPO rebates compress net price” was a bear-case risk.

surprises.description: Operating expenses increased less than 1% while revenue grew 23%, showing much less expense growth than the preview’s bear case of SG&A rising early as new sales representatives deployed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose 23% year-over-year to $18.5 million … while operating expenses increased less than 1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SG&A rises early as new salesforce reps deploy.”

surprises.description: The reported GAAP loss of $0.01 per share was narrower than the preview’s cited consensus loss of $0.05 and single-analyst estimate of $0.07.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss narrowed to $300,000 ($0.01/share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 EPS … $(0.05)”; “Q2 EPS (single analyst) … $(0.07).”

surprises.description: Formulary access improved and a large national health plan added Emrosi in early August, adding a concrete access catalyst that the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “High-quality formulary coverage … rose from 34% in Q1 to approximately 38% currently”; “A large national health plan added Emrosi to its formulary in early August.”

surprises.description: The company launched Eurax Cream, a niche anti-itch product, in July; the preview discussed the possibility of a future niche-product deal but did not anticipate this product launch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Launched a niche anti-itch product, Eurax Cream, in July.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management targeted [niche dermatology in-licensing deals] for later in 2026.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was positive for a second consecutive quarter, as the preview’s base case expected; the call reported adjusted EBITDA of $2.9 million.

surprises.description: FY2026 revenue grew 28%, above the preview’s roughly 21% FY2026 growth reference, and non-GAAP EPS of $5.61 exceeded even the higher cited consensus estimate of $5.45. The annual results were stronger than the preview’s baseline, although the EPS beat over the higher estimate was modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 pro forma revenue rose 28% to a record $7 billion … with non-GAAP EPS growing 59% to $5.61.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY26 EPS consensus also varies, at $4.70 and $5.45”; the preview also refers to FY2026 growth of “about 21%.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue reached $2.05 billion, above the preview’s roughly $1.98–$1.99 billion consensus, though it was at the top of the company’s prior guidance range. The beat versus consensus was modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 FY26 revenue was a record $2.05 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus … ~$1.98B … ~$1.99B”; prior guidance was “$1.91B – $2.05B.”

surprises.description: Q4 non-GAAP EPS of $1.74 beat the preview’s working consensus of $1.62 and edged above the prior guidance high of $1.72. The beat was meaningful against consensus but small against the guidance ceiling.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $1.74.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identifies “$1.62 (Zacks)” as the working number and prior guidance of “$1.52 – $1.72.”

surprises.description: Data Center & Communications appears to have delivered about $1.62 billion of Q4 revenue (79% of $2.05 billion), above the preview’s roughly $1.50 billion expectation. Data center alone was also up 24% sequentially, supporting the acceleration the preview was watching for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The data center and communications segment, 79% of Q4 revenue, grew 59% year-over-year”; “the data center business alone [was] up 56% year-over-year and 24% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Datacenter & Comms revenue vs. about $1.50B” was the preview’s first-ranked issue and acceleration test.

surprises.description: Q1 FY2027 revenue guidance of $2.2–$2.4 billion has a $2.3 billion midpoint, above the preview’s roughly $2.15 billion consensus and above its $2.25 billion bullish threshold. This was a stronger near-term outlook than the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q1 FY27 revenue to $2.2–$2.4 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The consensus Q1 figure is about $2.15B”; “a guide above $2.25B would support the street’s FY27 number.”

surprises.description: Management now expects data center revenue growth to exceed 80% year-over-year in the current quarter, while indium-phosphide output is expanding faster than planned. That is a stronger growth and supply outlook than the preview’s discussion of acceleration alongside possible supply constraints.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Indium phosphide laser production grew about 80% year-over-year in the June quarter,” and management “expects data center revenue growth to exceed 80% year-over-year in the current quarter”; internal indium-phosphide output is on track to double “one quarter ahead of plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called Q4 an “acceleration test” and identified “supply or yield limits” as a possible reason for a weaker result.

surprises.description: Management added a specific target to reach its first $3 billion revenue quarter by the end of fiscal 2027. The preview cited FY2027 revenue consensus of about $9.66 billion but did not flag this quarterly run-rate target.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expects to reach its first $3 billion revenue quarter by the end of fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited FY2027 models of “about $9.66B revenue (+36.9%)” but gave no $3 billion quarterly target.

surprises.description: The call outlined additional product ramps beyond the preview’s expected CPO scale-out timing: ultra-high-power CW lasers also begin in the December quarter, with multi-rail systems and ThermaDit scheduled for 2027. These provide a broader set of forthcoming revenue streams than the preview discussed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CPO/Photon Link and ultra high-power CW lasers” begin in the December quarter; “multi-rail systems” are expected in the first half of calendar 2027 and “thermal management (ThermaDit)” in the second half.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed “CPO and OCS progress” and said “CPO scale-out revenue begins in H2 CY2026,” but did not mention these additional product ramps.

surprises.description: The company cut debt leverage to 0.7x from 2.0x a year earlier while paying down $513 million of debt. That is a favorable funding development amid the heavy data-center investment the preview had identified as a key concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Debt leverage was cut to 0.7x from 2.0x a year earlier via $513 million in debt payments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview ranked “FY27 capex and funding” as a key issue and said management’s funding framing mattered.

in_line: Q4 non-GAAP gross margin was 40.2%, close to the preview’s roughly 40.0% consensus and within its 40.0–40.8% base-case range.

The preview expected record backlog to extend into 2028 and supply agreements to run through 2030; the call reported customer purchase orders into calendar 2028 and take-or-pay agreements through the end of the decade.
The preview expected CPO scale-out revenue to begin in H2 CY2026; the call’s December-quarter start for CPO/Photon Link remains within that timeframe.

surprises.description: Q2 EPS was $0.79 loss per share, worse than the preview’s base range of $0.60–$0.70 loss per share. The net loss was $14.1 million; higher operating expenses and an approximately $1 million contingent-consideration fair-value expense were reported alongside it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $14.1 million ($0.79 per share)” and “Net expense included roughly $1 million tied to fair value changes in contingent consideration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario estimated EPS of “-$0.60 to -$0.70”; it also gave a derived estimate of “~-$0.60.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was positive but lower than the preview’s base expectation: about 7% of revenue versus 9–12%. The second consecutive positive quarter was an improvement in continuity, but the reported margin level fell short of the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin turned positive at $0.7 million (~7% of revenue), the second consecutive positive gross margin quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario put gross margin at “9–12%.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses reached $13.8 million, above the preview’s $12 million threshold for no operating leverage on $9 million of revenue. The call attributed the increase to R&D and Security Force integration and headcount costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses jumped to $13.8 million from $5.4 million, driven by a $3.9 million increase in R&D and integration/headcount costs from the Security Force acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Opex above $12M on $9M revenue would mean no operating leverage.”

surprises.description: The K7 deployment timing appears later than the preview’s late-summer limited-release expectation: management said initial deployments remain on track for Q4 2026. The preview and call describe different milestones, so the timing shift is not fully like-for-like.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new K7 autonomous security robot passed its Alpha Prototype gate review and remains on track for initial deployments in Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “K7 limited release guided for late summer 2026.”

surprises.description: Management introduced a long-term blended gross-margin target of 50–60% at scale, a specific target not mentioned in the preview. It is an ambitious upside signal, though it is a target rather than a reported margin result.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “targets blended gross margins of 50-60% at scale from its integrated hardware-software-human model.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $9 million, matching the preview’s approximately $9 million preliminary figure.
Cash ended at $8.2 million, within the preview’s $8–12 million base-scenario range.
Management reaffirmed sequential improvement, consistent with the preview’s focus on whether the company would reaffirm its quarter-by-quarter growth framing.

surprises.description: KOMZIFTI recorded 115 new patient starts, above the preview’s 95–110 base case and well above the 85 starts in Q1. Starts grew about 35% quarter over quarter, while prescriptions grew about 60% with no meaningful inventory or stocking effect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “approximately 115 new patient starts and more than 250 total prescriptions”; “New patient starts grew about 35% quarter-over-quarter while total prescriptions grew about 60%,” with “no meaningful inventory or one-time stocking effects.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “New starts 95–110”; the key issue was whether “Flat-to-down KURA starts would suggest Q1 reflected switching rather than penetration.”

surprises.description: Despite entering second, KOMZIFTI captured a majority of new patient starts in the relapsed/refractory NPM1-mutant AML menin inhibitor market. That is stronger than the preview’s cited Q1 claim of about 40% share and its warning that competitive figures needed reconciliation.
surprises.fact_evidence: KOMZIFTI was “capturing a majority share of new patient starts in the relapsed/refractory NPM1-mutant AML menin inhibitor market despite entering second.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Kura claimed ~40% share of R/R NPM1 new starts in Q1. Both can be true only if the figures cover different populations; tonight's new-start number tests the claim.”

surprises.description: Coverage appears particularly favorable: more than 95% of covered lives have no label restrictions, and about 16 million lives have preferred status that requires trying KOMZIFTI before other menin inhibitors. The preview did not identify this level of access or preferred positioning as an expected result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 95% of covered lives with no label restrictions,” and “approximately 16 million lives carry preferred status requiring patients to step through KOMZIFTI before other menin inhibitors.”

surprises.description: Management reported strong KOMET-007 efficacy and survival data, which the preview did not flag among its expected catalysts. The reported 96% ORR and 94% 12-month overall survival contrast with the historical 45%–80% 12-month survival range cited on the call.
surprises.fact_evidence: “KOMET-007 frontline data in 99 patients showed a 96% ORR in relapsed/refractory NPM1-mutant AML, 94% overall survival at 12 months, and median OS not reached at 17.6 months follow-up, versus historical 12-month OS of 45%-80%.”

surprises.description: Physicians were initiating KOMZIFTI in combinations with venetoclax/azacitidine and FLT3 inhibitors in a substantial share of starts, although the company promotes it only for its approved monotherapy indication. The preview did not anticipate this prescribing pattern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Physician-initiated combination use with venetoclax/azacitidine and FLT3 inhibitors represented approximately 40% of new patient starts, though the drug is only promoted for its approved monotherapy indication.”

surprises.description: Darlifarnib showed response rates above the historical range cited for cabozantinib-exposed RCC, plus reported activity in cabozantinib-naive patients. The preview mentioned a possible development decision but did not set an efficacy expectation for these results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Darlifarnib demonstrated a 44% objective response rate and 94% disease control rate in cabozantinib-exposed RCC (versus 17%-22% historical), and 33%-50% ORR with 13-month median PFS in cabo-naive RCC.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “any darlifarnib (KO-2806) development decision” among items to watch, but gave no expected efficacy results.

surprises.description: Management cited data suggesting menin inhibition could apply to a broader AML population through MEIS1 expression, with up to half of AML patients potentially responsive. The preview did not mention this potential expansion beyond its focus on the frontline AML market estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “cited data suggesting up to 50% of AML patients may be responsive to menin inhibition via MEIS1 expression.”

in_line: KOMZIFTI’s $9.1 million in net product revenue was within the preview’s implied $8–10 million range, although management said it exceeded company expectations.
Management’s expected funding runway through KOMET-017 Phase III top-line results in 2028 remained consistent with the preview’s stated runway.

surprises.description: The preview treated a softening of the FY2026 SaaS outlook as the most likely case, but management reaffirmed the double-digit growth target unchanged. That is a more confident outlook than expected, despite Q2 growth being below the preview’s key +8% watch threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management reaffirmed guidance for double-digit year-over-year SaaS growth for fiscal 2026, unchanged from prior guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (most likely): The guide shifts from ‘double-digit’ to ‘year-over-year growth’” and “Growth below about +8% in Q2 makes the full-year target look implausible.”

surprises.description: Q2 SaaS growth was 4.2%, below the preview’s +8% threshold for making the full-year target look plausible, though close to its +5% base scenario. The reaffirmed full-year guide makes the low quarterly growth rate a tension rather than a withdrawal of the target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 SaaS revenue grew 4.2% year-over-year to $1.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Growth below about +8% in Q2 makes the full-year target look implausible”; the base scenario estimated SaaS growth of “+5%.”

surprises.description: The GAAP loss was worse than the preview’s base-case estimate and slightly worse than its bear-case estimate. The preview cautioned that the single consensus EPS datapoint was stale, so the more relevant comparison is its own scenario estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss widened to $1.1 million ($0.24 loss per share) from a $600,000 net loss ($0.13 loss per share) in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s scenarios estimated GAAP EPS of “$(0.14)” in the base case and “$(0.22)” in the bear case.

surprises.description: Professional services revenue fell rather than stabilizing after the customer contract anniversary, contrary to the preview’s expected base case. Management did say it had taken orders to refill the backlog, offering a positive but unquantified sign for subsequent activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Professional services revenue fell 5.8% to $1.8 million in Q2 due to reduced scanning project activity and lower backlog, though the company says it has since taken orders to refill that backlog.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called professional services stabilization a key metric and said “Sequential stabilization from $1.85M separates a base case from a bear case.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses were materially above the preview’s roughly $3.23 million clean run-rate reference, rising to $3.7 million. The increase included higher variable compensation, added engineering staff, and more share-based compensation, consistent with the preview’s concern that elevated spending could push profitability out.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 operating expenses rose 14.7% to $3.7 million,” driven by “a 24.4% jump in G&A from higher variable compensation, added engineering staff, and roughly $229,000 more share-based compensation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Q1’s clean run-rate as “about $3.23M” and said “Opex above the roughly $3.23M clean run-rate would suggest spending into sales hiring, which pushes profitability out.”

in_line: Cash ended the quarter at $1.7 million, within the preview’s expected range of roughly $1.5–1.7 million; the company also remained debt-free, as the preview anticipated.

surprises.description: The preview treated August as the guided timing and said anything later than early September would be negative. Longeveron now expects ELPIS-2 topline data in mid-September, citing MRI and last-patient-visit scheduling; it said the delay was not due to unresolved FDA statistical-analysis-plan issues.
surprises.fact_evidence: “expects to report top-line data ... in mid-September 2026”; the database lock is planned for August 31, with the “slight delay from August to September attributed to MRI and last-patient-visit scheduling rather than any unresolved FDA statistical analysis plan issues.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the trial was guided to “August 2026” and that “anything other than August or early September is a negative signal.”

surprises.description: Cash fell to $10.1 million, below the preview’s bear-case threshold of $10.5 million and well below the $15.8 million reported at the end of Q1. Management says the cash funds operations only into Q4, indicating a near-term need for financing or a partnership.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents were $10.1 million as of June 30, 2026,” which management expects to fund operations “only into the fourth quarter of 2026,” signaling a near-term financing or partnership need.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 cash of “$15.8M” and identified cash “below $10.5M” as a bear-case condition; it also said the prior runway guidance was “into Q4 2026.”

surprises.description: The preview expected management might name partnering interest, but the call described an “auction” among major potential partners for HLHS commercialization, contingent on positive ELPIS-2 data. That is a more concrete and competitive process than simply naming interest.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is pursuing an “auction” among major potential partners for HLHS commercialization contingent on positive ELPIS-2 data, with partnerships positioned as the primary path to commercialization.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case said management might “name partnering interest”; it also said to watch for “named partnering discussions.”

surprises.description: The preview noted Longeveron’s XPRIZE HealthSpan finalist status, but did not mention the associated $1 million award or eligibility for a grand prize of up to $81 million. Those additional award details provide potential upside beyond the finalist news already known.
surprises.fact_evidence: Longeveron was named an XPRIZE HealthSpan finalist out of over 600 applicants, “earning a $1 million award” and eligibility for a grand prize of up to $81 million in 2029.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed the “Aug 11 XPRIZE Healthspan finalist award” as recent company news, but did not mention the $1 million award or eligibility for the grand prize.

surprises.description: The preview focused on the ELPIS-2 readout but did not describe management’s view that a miss on the RVEF primary endpoint might not end the program’s path toward pivotal or BLA status. Management pointed to exploratory event-based outcomes as a possible alternative basis, while acknowledging the primary-endpoint risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Even if the RVEF primary endpoint misses statistical significance,” management believes it can pursue BLA/pivotal status using exploratory endpoints like all-cause mortality and transplant-free survival, and claims sufficient blinded data to demonstrate significance on event-based outcomes.

surprises.description: The preview did not mention the potential priority review vouchers. Management said a successful HLHS approval would come with a voucher recently valued around $215 million, with a second potential voucher tied to the planned pediatric dilated cardiomyopathy program.
surprises.fact_evidence: A successful HLHS approval would come with a priority review voucher “recently valued around $215 million,” with “a second potential voucher” tied to the planned pediatric dilated cardiomyopathy program.

in_line: Revenue was about $0.3 million, consistent with the preview’s bear-case estimate of around $0.3 million, though below its base-case estimate of around $0.35 million. The preview also noted that the contract-manufacturing revenue base was shrinking.

surprises.description: The reported Q2 loss was much smaller than the preview’s expected $0.25 per-share loss: INOVIO reported a $0.07 loss per share and a $6 million net loss. The $9 million non-cash warrant fair value gain materially helped produce that result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed to $6 million ($0.07/share) from $23.5 million ($0.61/share), aided by a $9 million non-cash warrant fair value gain.”

surprises.description: INOVIO reported that it has enough cash runway to cover a potential INO-3107 launch, including pre-launch inventory and marketing costs. That addresses the preview’s concern about whether the company could fund a specialty launch, although the stated runway extends only into late Q1 2027 rather than the preview’s more favorable 2H 2027 scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The July 2026 public equity offering netting approximately $18.3 million, extending its cash runway into late first quarter 2027 and through a potential INO-3107 launch, including pre-launch inventory build and launch marketing costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Ask what the differentiated clinical claim is and whether the company can fund a specialty launch on about $54M in pro forma cash, or whether a partnership is more likely.”

surprises.description: The late-cycle review and scheduled pre-licensure inspections were completed, with just one reported inspection observation that INOVIO believes it addressed. The preview had asked whether the review had occurred and whether it was clean, but did not anticipate this specific, relatively favorable inspection result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FDA [has] completed its late cycle review meeting and all scheduled pre-licensure inspections that yielded only one reported observation, which Inovio believes it has addressed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Late-cycle review (scheduled Q3 2026): has it occurred, and was it clean?”

surprises.description: INOVIO said it expects to begin FDA label negotiations in September, a concrete sign that it believes the review is nearing its final stages. The preview flagged regulatory progress as the main issue but did not identify label negotiations as an expected milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inovio anticipates beginning label negotiations with the FDA in September 2026, signaling it believes it is in the final stages of the regulatory review process.”

surprises.description: INOVIO said it expects INO-3107 to receive seven years of orphan drug market exclusivity if approved, based on its differentiated delivery and mechanism of action. The preview did not mention this potential exclusivity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “If approved, Inovio expects INO-3107 to receive seven years of orphan drug market exclusivity based on its differentiated delivery and mechanism of action.”

surprises.description: The call described very limited uptake of competitor Papz imios—low single-digit penetration and about 200 patients treated—leaving most of the prevalent RRP population open to another treatment. That was a more favorable market-opening detail than the preview’s report of $53.1 million in Papz imios Q2 revenue, which it said weakened INOVIO’s fast-following argument.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The competing product Papzimios has achieved only low single-digit penetration with approximately 200 patients treated, leaving the vast majority of the prevalent RRP population open to a new treatment option.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Precigen's PAPZIMEOS reported $53.1M in Q2 2026 revenue, which weakens the ‘fast-following second entrant’ argument management made in May.”

surprises.description: INOVIO highlighted a specific treatment-burden contrast: 83% of participants in Papz imios’s Phase 1/2 trial needed at least one minimal residual disease surgery during dosing, while INO-3107 does not require scoping or surgery during dosing. The preview asked for a differentiated clinical claim but did not identify this comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In Papzimios's Phase 1/2 trial, 83% of participants required at least one minimal residual disease surgery during the dosing window, whereas INO-3107 does not require scoping or surgery during dosing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Ask what the differentiated clinical claim is”

surprises.description: INOVIO added Fabry disease and hypophosphatasia as new targets for its D-Prop platform and said it is seeking partners for them. The preview discussed pipeline and partnership optionality but did not anticipate these specific new targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inovio added Fabry disease and hypophosphatasia as new targets for its D-Prop platform and is seeking partners.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pipeline and partnership optionality.”

in_line: The FDA did not comment on accelerated approval eligibility at the July clinical meeting because the file remains under active review. The preview’s base case allowed for the meeting to be held with no resolution disclosed.
The October 30, 2026 PDUFA target date remains on track, as the preview identified it as the existing target date and flagged an extension as a major negative.
The company projected Q3 operational net cash burn of approximately $18 million, matching the preview’s stated cash-burn guide of about $18 million.

ApolloBio’s positive Phase 3 results for VGX-3100 in China were already reported in the preview; the call’s update that ApolloBio plans to pursue regulatory approval is consistent with that known development.

surprises.description: Yartemlia net sales were $28.5 million, far above the preview’s roughly $13 million estimate and even the high end of the cited $12.7–$17.0 million consensus range. This was a much faster full-quarter ramp than the preview’s base case of $14–$17 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Yartemlia generated $28.5 million in net sales in Q2 2026”; net sales “grew 188%” quarter over quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “YARTEMLEA net revenue vs. ~$13M”; the base scenario forecast “$14–17M.” Consensus estimates ranged from “~$12.7M” to “$17.0M.”

surprises.description: Yartemlia had 73 ordering accounts, up from 30 at the end of Q1, substantially exceeding the preview’s account-count benchmark. P&T approval had also reached roughly 55–60% across tracked top transplant-center cohorts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “73 unique accounts had ordered Yartemlia (up 143.5% since March 31), with P&T committee approval reaching roughly 55-60% across tracked top transplant center cohorts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Ordering accounts (vs. 30 at Q1)” as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: Adjusted earnings turned positive at $0.02 per share, rather than the adjusted loss anticipated in the preview’s scenarios. The result was a meaningful improvement even after excluding the non-cash derivative gain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP adjusted net income was only $1.8 million ($0.02/share) after excluding a $12.1 million non-cash mark-to-market derivative gain.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario projected “Adj. EPS” of “–$0.18 to –$0.24”; the bull scenario projected “–$0.10 to –$0.15.”

surprises.description: Company-wide operations generated positive cash flow in Q2, ahead of the mid-2027 goal in the preview. A positive quarter does not establish that the company-wide target has been reached sustainably, but it was earlier evidence of cash-flow progress than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Company-wide operations generated $4.1 million of positive cash flow in Q2,” supporting guidance for company-wide cash-flow positivity by mid-2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “targets company-wide positive cash flow within 18 months.”

surprises.description: GAAP EPS was positive at $0.18 and exceeded the preview’s highest cited estimate of $0.06, although the preview warned that GAAP EPS could be distorted by the derivative mark. The reported $13.2 million of GAAP net income included a $12.1 million non-cash mark-to-market gain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 GAAP net income was $13.2 million ($0.18/share),” including “a $12.1 million non-cash mark-to-market derivative gain.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited GAAP EPS estimates of “–$0.27” and “+$0.06” and said GAAP EPS was “Likely distorted again by a non-cash derivative mark.”

surprises.description: The July note repurchase was a substantial post-quarter capital-allocation move not anticipated in the preview: Omeros paid $60.2 million to repurchase $30.5 million of principal. It reduced future interest and potential dilution, but required a large cash outlay.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In July, Omeros repurchased $30.5 million of its 9.5% 2029 convertible notes for $60.2 million,” cutting principal 43%, eliminating $8.6 million in future interest, and reducing conversion shares from 11.4 million to 6.5 million.

surprises.description: Sales were more adult-heavy than the historical mix cited on the call: adults represented about 95% of Yartemlia sales versus a historical 85% adult share, as adult utilization grew at more than twice the pediatric rate. The preview did not flag this mix as a key expectation, so the implication for the pace of pediatric uptake is unclear.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adult utilization grew at more than twice the rate of pediatric utilization, with adults now representing approximately 95% of Yartemlia sales, approaching the historical 85%/15% adult-pediatric split.”

in_line: Gross-to-net was 11.5%, consistent with the preview’s cited Q1 level of 11% and expectation that it would stay in the teens.
Cash and investments were $132 million, above the preview’s stated $110 million level of concern.
The mid-2027 company-wide cash-flow-positive guidance remained in place, consistent with the preview’s reference to a target within 18 months.
The negative CHMP opinion and Omeros’s request for re-examination were already described in the preview.
The permanent J-code effective July 1 and NTAP of up to approximately $287,000 effective October 1 matched the timing and payment mechanics described in the preview.

surprises.description: Revenue was expected to be around the recent $30.3–$30.7 million range, with the preview saying $32 million or more would show backlog converting. Q2 sales reached $33.5 million, above that marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose 9.3% year-over-year to $33.5 million,” from $30.7 million a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A print of $32M or more would support the idea that backlog is converting”; revenue had been “around $30.3–30.7M for four straight quarters.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was expected to remain above the preview’s 16% concern threshold for the margin-recovery story to hold. It rose to 17%, and management said first-half margins were a company record.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved 120 basis points to 17%”; management called first-half margins “a company record.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A second quarter below 16% would weaken” the margin-repair narrative.

surprises.description: The preview questioned whether the prior-quarter operating-expense increase was one-time, and the higher sales and gross margin suggested room for better profit conversion. Instead, operating income declined and net income was essentially flat as incentive compensation rose.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 operating income declined to $623,000 from $742,000” as a “$533,000 increase in incentive compensation offset revenue gains”; net income was “essentially flat” at $316,000 versus $313,000.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Was the Q1 opex increase one-time?”; “The margin repair … is the core of the equity story.”

surprises.description: The preview said the $31.5 million 90-day backlog and $90.8 million total backlog needed to hold. Both increased instead, with the 90-day backlog growing faster than the prior-year rate cited for Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “90-day shipment backlog grew 25.8% year-over-year to $33.4 million,” while “total order backlog rose 19.8% to $93.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The $90.8M total and $31.5M 90-day figures need to hold”; Q1 90-day backlog was “+18% YoY.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted A&D durability after a 41.2% Q1 increase. Q2 A&D sales instead fell 12.8%, which management attributed to one customer reducing post-COVID inventory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aerospace/defense declined 12.8% on one customer reducing post-COVID inventory.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Also watch A&D durability (+41.2% in Q1).”

surprises.description: Medical-device sales accelerated sharply from the prior quarter’s reported growth, rather than merely maintaining that pace. Q2 medical-device sales rose 36% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Medical device sales jumped 36% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q1 end-market results included “medical devices +10.4%.”

surprises.description: The preview described industrial sales as flat in Q1; they moved into decline in Q2, falling 4.7%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Industrial fell 4.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q1 end-market results included “industrial flat.”

surprises.description: The preview asked whether Q2 generated free cash flow and highlighted the company’s cash and borrowing position. Instead, operations used cash in the first half, quarter-end cash was just $1.7 million, and the company had $7.6 million drawn on its revolver with only $3.6 million of unused availability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operations used $2.4 million of cash in the first half,” driven by a “$4.5 million receivables/contract-asset build” and “$3.5 million inventory increase”; cash and restricted cash were “just $1.7 million,” with “$7.6 million drawn” and “only $3.6 million of unused availability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With $1.96M cash and about $18.0M debt, the questions are how much of the $15M revolver is drawn and whether Q2 generated free cash flow.”

surprises.description: Core revenue was $6.5 million, above the preview’s $6.2 million estimate and management’s expected flat sequential result. This was a modest upside relative to the preview’s key core-revenue hurdle.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core revenue fell 21% year-over-year to $6.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 core to roughly Q1's $6.2M”; catalyst: “Core revenue at or above $6.2M.”

surprises.description: Total revenue was $7.3 million, modestly above the preview’s $7.0 million build. The preview noted that this was a self-built estimate rather than a reconciled Street consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $7.3 million … though results exceeded management's expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Q2 2026E ~$7.0M (my build, -18% YoY).”

surprises.description: Operating expenses came in above the preview’s $14–15 million estimate at $15.8 million, despite falling substantially year over year. Management said the restructuring benefits were now at full run rate and expenses should not grow meaningfully going forward.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses fell 25% year-over-year to $15.8 million (from $21.2 million), reflecting full run-rate benefits of 2025 restructuring, with expenses not expected to grow meaningfully going forward.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating expenses … Q2 2026E $14–15M (my build).”

surprises.description: The Genentech deal was described as a multi-platform enterprise-license partnership spanning two clinical allogeneic programs and one preclinical research program, and as MaxCyte’s first move into large pharma. The preview already knew the license had been signed, but had not specified this breadth; no fee size was disclosed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company announced a multi-platform enterprise license partnership with Genentech, marking its first move into large pharma” across “two clinical allogeneic programs and one preclinical research program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Genentech license (signed July 21, 2026). This is a Q3 event with no Q2 revenue, but the call is where it gets framed. Terms are undisclosed. Watch for fee sizing, whether it counts as a new SPL, and whether FY guidance changes.”

surprises.description: Management said five partner programs could be positioned for commercial launch in the next couple of years, including as early as 2027. The preview did not identify this near-term launch pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Five partner programs positioned for potential commercial launch in the next couple of years, including as early as 2027.”

in_line: SPL program-related revenue was $0.8 million, essentially matching the preview’s estimate of about $0.8 million, including roughly $0.75 million of royalties and no expected milestone revenue.
Management reiterated the $30–32 million full-year revenue guidance, as the preview expected; the preview also anticipated approximately $5 million of full-year SPL revenue.
Cash and investments of $141.9 million landed within the preview’s $140–143 million estimate.
Vertex’s reported Casgevy revenue of approximately $76 million was in line with the preview’s cited Q2 sales figure of $76 million.

surprises.description: Net revenue retention fell to 90%, far below the preview’s 110% starting point and its warning that a result below roughly 105% would indicate broader franchise weakness. Average revenue per top-20 pharma manufacturer and revenue per FTE also declined sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenue retention rate fell to 90%”; “average revenue per top-20 pharma manufacturer was $2.7 million, and revenue per FTE was $750,000, all showing sequential declines.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue retention (110%, from 114%). Below about 105% would point to a broader franchise problem.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $0.16, above the preview’s $0.11 consensus estimate. Revenue also modestly exceeded the $20.20 million consensus estimate at $20.5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income fell to $3.1 million ($0.16 per diluted share)”; “Q2 FY2026 revenue was $20.5 million … but exceeded consensus expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (Q2) … Consensus $20.20M”; “Non-GAAP EPS (Q2) … Consensus $0.11.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year gross margin expectations to the high-60% to low-70% range, citing favorable product and channel mix and the wind-down of low-margin managed services. The preview did not identify a gross-margin increase as an expected outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin guidance was raised, with full-year 2026 gross margins now expected in the high-60% to low-70% range,” driven by “favorable product and channel partner mix and the wind-down of low-margin managed services.”

surprises.description: Although the full-year revenue guide was reaffirmed, management said Q4 is expected to contribute 35–40% of full-year revenue. That makes the anticipated second-half rebound notably concentrated in Q4; the preview highlighted the H2 revenue requirement but did not report a comparable Q4 concentration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $95-100 million in revenue”; “Q4 expected to represent 35-40% of full-year revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The guide needs $55–60M in H2”; the preview also called for listening for “how much of that is already contracted versus pipeline.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was reported as $4.9 million, above the preview’s estimated $3.5–4.5 million range, despite severance costs. However, the CFO also cited $4.1 million, which is within that estimate range, so the size of any beat is uncertain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $4.9 million (or $4.1 million per CFO remarks) in Q2 2026,” impacted by “$1.7 million in severance expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (Q2) … ~$3.5–4.5M (est.).”

surprises.description: The company paid down debt faster than scheduled and made another post-quarter principal payment, while refinancing its term loan at SOFR plus 2.25%. The preview did not anticipate these specific debt actions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Paid $5.3 million in principal during Q2 (roughly $5 million ahead of schedule) plus an additional $3 million post-quarter, reducing outstanding debt to about $16.7 million,” and “refinanced its term loan with Fifth Third Bank at SOFR plus 2.25%.”

surprises.description: Management described the $10 million buyback as conditional on the stock declining further, while saying capital allocation was prioritizing debt paydown. The preview flagged buyback activity under the existing authorization as something to watch, but no executed repurchases are reported in the call facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Capital allocation prioritizing debt paydown and a $10 million buyback if the stock declines further.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buyback activity under the $10M authorization effective March 12, 2026.”

surprises.description: The CFO announced he will step down at year-end, with the Chief Business Officer taking over in January 2027 and the outgoing CFO staying on as a strategic adviser through 2027. The preview did not flag a CFO transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Edward Stelmakh will step down effective December 31, 2026, with Chief Business Officer Andy D'Silva succeeding as CFO on January 1, 2027, and Ed remaining as strategic adviser through 2027.”

surprises.description: The AI-enabled Dynamic Audience Activation Platform and AI-enabled software offerings posted strong growth, which was not discussed as an expected result in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The AI-enabled Dynamic Audience Activation Platform (DAAP) grew over 30% year-over-year and AI-enabled software offerings grew 25%,” supporting “the shift toward recurring subscription revenue.”

surprises.description: The DeepIntent DSP integration went live during the call week, and management presented access to programmatic buying as a potential growth lever, including the possibility of doubling the business over two years. The preview did not mention this launch or growth claim.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The DeepIntent DSP integration went live during the week of the call”; management noted “programmatic channels now account for 60% of buys in their space,” positioning DSP access as “a potential driver to double the business over two years.”

in_line: Full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $95–100 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $21–25 million were reaffirmed, matching the preview’s stated guidance and its expectation that reaffirmation was the bar.
The GAAP loss was close to the preview’s approximately $0.05-per-share loss estimate: reported GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.04 per share.
Revenue remained sharply lower year over year, as the preview anticipated: the preview estimated a 31% decline, while reported revenue was down 30%.
The disruption at a major customer remained relevant; the preview had already flagged that client as a key issue and noted that it was too early to include a resolution in the forecast.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $278 million, about $9.4 million above the preview’s $268.6 million consensus estimate. The preview warned that the quarterly estimate’s period alignment was questionable, but the reported result still exceeded the stated estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 revenue fell $6.1 million to $278 million, primarily due to restaurant closures partially offset by higher comp sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $283.7M | $268.6M (−5.3% YoY)”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $18.9 million, below the preview’s $21–22 million implied consensus and its $22–23 million base case. The preview expected marketing spend to be higher, but the reported $4 million year-over-year increase in marketing was a key reason EBITDA fell short.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined $3.5 million year-over-year to $18.9 million, driven mainly by a $4 million increase in marketing spend behind the Big Yum value platform.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | $22.4M | ~$21–22M (implied, not a published consensus)” and “Base … Adj. EBITDA | $22–23M.”

surprises.description: The company kept its $70–73 million full-year EBITDA guidance without providing the post-refranchising rebased outlook the preview expected; it specified that the guidance excludes the transactions’ impact. That leaves the company’s expected EBITDA after the restaurant transfers unbridged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company maintained full-year 2026 guidance … adjusted EBITDA of $70–73 million … excluding any impact from the re-franchising transactions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Re-based FY26 guidance, or a refusal to give one”; “A rough estimate puts the re-based range near $58–65M”; and the base scenario expected “guide re-based to $58–65M.”

surprises.description: Restaurant-level margin rose to 14.7%, rather than declining by the roughly 30 basis points the preview considered a reasonable base case. The result was also above the prior-year 14.5% margin used as the comparison point.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restaurant-level operating margin rose 20 basis points year-over-year to 14.7%, the highest second-quarter margin in four years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A decline of about 30bps is a reasonable base case.”

surprises.description: Traffic was nearly flat but still slightly negative, rather than turning positive as in the preview’s bull scenario. It nevertheless outperformed the industry and was the company’s best traffic performance since Q1 2023, making the result better than the bear case of negative traffic.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Traffic effectively flat (down 20 basis points) but outperforming the industry by 40 basis points, marking the best traffic performance since Q1 2023.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Traffic has to lead” and described the bull case as “Traffic turns positive” and the bear case as “Traffic negative.”

surprises.description: The preview characterized pricing as only about 1%, while the reported price increase was 3.3%. However, Big Yum value offerings reduced mix and discounts by 1.8%, leaving average check growth at just 1.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Average check rose 1.5%, consisting of a 3.3% price increase offset by a 1.8% decline in mix and discounts from Big Yum value offerings, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of below-industry check growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Traffic has to lead, since pricing is only about +1%.”

in_line: Q2 comparable sales grew 1.3%, consistent with the preview’s view that roughly +1% or better was needed and within the company’s full-year comp guidance range of +0.5% to +1.5%.

surprises.description: The preview’s bull case anticipated a guidance raise to 12%–14% growth, while Usio raised its FY2026 revenue-growth outlook to 14%–16%. That is also a substantial increase from the prior 10%–12% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Usio raised full-year fiscal 2026 revenue growth guidance to 14%-16%, up substantially from prior guidance of 10%-12%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bull … FY guide raised to 12–14%”; the preview also said guidance was 10–12% and consensus sat at the top of that range.

surprises.description: The preview put consensus gross margin around 22%–23% and flagged 23% as the important threshold; Usio reported 24%, above both the consensus range and that threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margins of 23%-25% near term (24% this quarter).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~22–23%”; “Anything below about 22% breaks that narrative,” and the catalyst checklist called for gross margin “at or above 23%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA came in above the preview’s estimated range: $1.1 million versus roughly $0.7–$0.9 million. The first-half result was also described as Usio’s best in years.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $1.1 million in Q2, more than double the year-ago quarter, with first-half adjusted EBITDA of $1.9 million representing the best first half in years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$0.7–0.9M.”

surprises.description: Usio’s voucher opportunity was described at a larger scale than the preview’s two-state, up-to-$1 billion framing, expanding to five or six states and an estimated $1.5 billion in total volume. However, initial disbursements were flowing mostly through lower-margin ACH, rather than establishing the anticipated prepaid/card benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “School voucher programs expanded from 2 to 5-6 states with estimated total volumes around $1.5 billion, though initial disbursements are flowing mostly through lower-margin ACH.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had flagged “up to $1B in school-choice voucher distributions across two states” and told investors to watch whether “prepaid turns positive Y/Y” and how much voucher revenue lands in Q2 versus 2H.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue growth was slightly faster than the roughly 18% year-over-year growth implied by consensus, at 19%, though the difference was small.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 fiscal 2026 revenue grew 19% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed revenue consensus of “~$23.6M” versus “$19.96M” a year earlier, implying “+18% Y/Y.”

surprises.description: Usio reported positive GAAP EPS of $0.01, modestly better than the preview’s consensus range of a $0.01 loss to breakeven.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$280,000 or $0.01 per share in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP EPS -$0.01 … or $0.00”; the preview’s base case was “$0.00.”

surprises.description: Management introduced a potentially significant margin-growth opportunity that the preview had not identified: Usio Ion could increase daily float balances from $80–$100 million to more than $200–$300 million, with float income described as 100%-margin revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Usio Ion platform [is] positioned as the key catalyst to push margins above 25% via 100%-margin float income”; management believes Ion could grow float balances “from the current $80-$100 million to potentially over $200-$300 million daily.”

in_line: Usio delivered a second consecutive positive GAAP net-income quarter, as the preview identified that outcome as a key checkpoint.
The reported 24% gross margin was within management’s stated near-term 23%–25% target.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $12.9 million, below the preview’s $14.45 million anchor, although it matched the preview’s alternative $12.90 million estimate. The net loss was $6.2 million, or $0.32 per share, versus the expected $0.17 loss; a customer-directed processing hold pushed treatment revenue into the second half even as Q2 personnel and operating costs had already been incurred.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 revenue fell to $12.9 million”; net loss was “$6.2 million (-$0.32 per share)”; “a customer-directed hold on waste processing” pushed treatment revenue into the second half while related costs were already incurred in Q2.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Treat −$0.17 and $14.5M as the anchor,” while noting an alternative revenue consensus of “~$12.90M.”

surprises.description: The going-concern qualification remained in the Q2 10-Q despite the May offering and a quarter-end cash balance of $20.5 million. The preview specifically identified removal of the qualification as a potential de-risking outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “disclosed a going concern qualification in its 10-Q due to reliance on non-guaranteed government-directed waste shipments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Removal from the Q2 10-Q would be a clear de-risking event. The May offering should support it.”

surprises.description: The call described a much larger potential grout-treatment scale and a sharply lower-cost alternative to vitrification: DOE’s dual glass-plus-grout strategy could deliver up to 300% more throughput, with treatment and disposal costs falling from roughly $1,200 per gallon to under $50. The preview discussed the Hanford contract but did not flag these throughput or cost estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: DOE's “dual glass-plus-grout strategy is projected to deliver up to 300% more throughput while cutting treatment and disposal costs from roughly $1,200 per gallon to under $50 per gallon versus vitrification.”

surprises.description: The company’s planned grouting-permit expansion is substantially larger than the 4.2-million-gallon annual target highlighted in the preview: the call said it is expanding from 1.2 million gallons to over 9–10 million gallons annually, with upgrades expected to be operational in Q2/Q3 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expanding its grouting permit from 1.2 million to over 9-10 million gallons annually”; upgrades are “expected operational by Q2/Q3 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “capex needed for the 4.2M gallons/year target by October 2027.”

surprises.description: The call provided a concrete prospective Hanford grout-volume ramp that the preview did not specify: about 60,000 gallons per month could be available as early as Q4 2026, rising to approximately 130,000 gallons per month by 2028. These are prospective DOE volumes, not committed company orders.
surprises.fact_evidence: DOE estimates “roughly 60,000 gallons per month will be available for grouting as early as Q4 2026” and “approximately 130,000 gallons per month by 2028”; no volumes are yet committed to the company.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to listen for “expected timing and size of the first task orders” and PESI’s “expected share of the ceiling,” but gave no comparable volume ramp.

surprises.description: The call highlighted a location advantage not covered in the preview: Perma-Fix Northwest is the only one of the three master subcontract holders near Hanford, about one mile away, and can grout near the point where waste is generated rather than requiring long-haul transport of liquid waste out of state.
surprises.fact_evidence: Perma-Fix Northwest is “the only one of three master subcontract holders located near Hanford (about one mile away), allowing grouting near the point of generation without long-haul transport of liquid tank waste out of state.”

surprises.description: Nuclear Services revenue grew 44% year over year to $4.6 million, supported by the roughly $24 million Lawrence Livermore agreement and more than $17 million in services backlog over the next 18 months. That provided a favorable business update against the preview’s focus on the services pipeline and the consortium’s lost USS Enterprise award, though the preview gave no numerical revenue expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nuclear Services revenue grew 44% year-over-year to $4.6 million,” supported by the “~$24 million Lawrence Livermore agreement” and “over $17 million in services backlog over the next 18 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Also expect a question on the Nuclear Services pipeline. PESI's consortium lost the USS Enterprise dismantlement to NorthStar Maritime ($418.5M award).”

in_line: Treatment backlog was $15.7 million, above the preview’s key threshold of $15 million (the preview cited $12.2 million at March 31).
Quarter-end cash of $20.5 million exceeded the preview’s $17 million checkpoint.

The H2C master IDIQ award and its roughly $4.4 billion shared ceiling were anticipated in the preview; the call also said no task-order volumes are yet committed, consistent with the preview’s warning that the ceiling was not committed revenue to PESI.
Revenue matched the preview’s alternative estimate of about $12.90 million, even though it was below the $14.45 million anchor.

surprises.description: Enrollment is at 75%, with all clinical sites activated. The preview expected enrollment to be above the prior 50% mark, but this update is more specific and indicates a larger advance than that baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “reached 75% enrollment” and “all clinical sites now activated.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “Well ahead of 50%” and flagged a specific enrollment update as potentially positive.

surprises.description: The preview expected the 2H26 topline timing to be reiterated, but management said enrollment should finish later in 2026 and topline data would follow four to five weeks afterward. That leaves the timing less firmly within 2H26 and allows for a 2027 readout.
surprises.fact_evidence: “remains on track to complete enrollment later in 2026” with “top-line data expected roughly four to five weeks after enrollment completion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for “Reiteration of the 2H26 topline” and said LPO would need to land by “roughly late November” for that timing to hold.

surprises.description: Updated research raised the estimated 2027 U.S. CRRT procedure market to about 200,000 from 165,000, a 21% increase over Talphera’s prior estimate. The preview did not anticipate this larger market estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Updated market research raised the estimated 2027 annual U.S. CRRT procedures to approximately 200,000, a 21% increase from the prior estimate of 165,000.”

surprises.description: The 2026 KDIGO guideline now references Nefamostat as an acceptable regional anticoagulant alternative to citrate, a new endorsement not anticipated in the preview. The guideline was still pending final publication.
surprises.fact_evidence: The guideline “now references Nefamostat as an acceptable regional anticoagulant alternative to citrate for the first time”; final publication was expected roughly three months after the May comment close.

surprises.description: Management described a large potential opening for Nefamostat because about 75% of U.S. institutions lack citrate, which is not FDA approved for CRRT and has usage complexities. The preview did not flag this specific access and adoption opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 75% of U.S. institutions do not have citrate available,” and “citrate is not FDA approved for CRRT and carries usage complexities,” creating “a large potential market for Nefamostat out of the gate.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a specific strategic relationship with CoreMedix: it has a 60-day right of first negotiation after the data readout, and CoreMedix’s CEO sits on Talphera’s board. The preview mentioned possible commercial partnering generally, but not this arrangement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CoreMedix holds a right of first negotiation for 60 days post data readout,” and its CEO “sits on Talphera's board,” representing a potential strategic partnership consideration.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “any early comment on commercial partnering.”

surprises.description: The call offered favorable blinded-study observations that the preview did not anticipate: most patients reached therapeutic range quickly at the starting dose, with titration well below the maximum dose, and the safety committee recommended continuing without changes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly 80-85% of patients reached therapeutic range at the starting dose within about half an hour,” most were titrated to “20-25 mg/hour, well below the 50 mg maximum,” and the independent data safety monitoring committee “recommended continuing without changes.”

in_line: Cash was $17.1 million at June 30, within the preview’s estimated range of approximately $17.0–17.5 million.
The PMA path remained targeted for 2027, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a 2027 filing and potential approval.

surprises.description: The preview’s base case looked for refinancing to be “advanced,” with a term sheet expected before October 30. Instead, SPRU had only preliminary SP1 lender discussions and no committed refinancing arrangements at quarter-end, and it disclosed a GAAP going-concern qualification.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A GAAP going concern qualification” was disclosed because the SP1 and SP2 debt facilities mature within 12 months and “no committed refinancing arrangements were in place at quarter end”; “only preliminary lender discussions” were underway for SP1.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected refi “advanced” with a “term sheet expected before Oct 30,” and said anything short of a signed or imminent term sheet would leave the equity in limbo.

surprises.description: SPRU reported a $3.3 million profit, or $0.14 per diluted share, rather than the preview’s modeled $3.5 million loss and $0.19 loss per share. The reversal was partly helped by favorable non-cash interest-rate-swap valuation changes, which the preview had flagged as a source of EPS volatility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income attributable to stockholders of $3.3 million ($0.14 per diluted share), versus a net loss of $3 million ($0.17 per share) in Q2 2025,” partly aided by “favorable non-cash interest rate swap valuation changes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled “Net loss attrib. to stockholders -$3.5M” and “EPS -$0.19.”

surprises.description: Operating EBITDA was $26.5 million, above the preview’s $24.0 million estimate and its $23–25 million base-case range. The preview had specifically cautioned that Q2 EBITDA strength needed to be checked against the expected shift of O&M and collections activity into the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating EBITDA rose to $26.5 million from $24.6 million a year earlier,” with year-to-date operating EBITDA “21% ahead of the prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Q2 operating EBITDA of “$24.0M” and gave a base-case range of “$23–25M”; it said Q2 strength needed to be checked for whether it was “structural or borrowed from H2.”

surprises.description: Revenue came in below the preview’s $31.5 million estimate, declining 9% year over year rather than the modeled 5% decline. The reported drivers included lower SP5 SREC production and a slower-than-expected Spruce Pro revenue ramp, alongside reduced performance-based incentives.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue declined 9% year-over-year to $30.3 million,” driven by “lower SP5 SREC production, reduced performance-based incentives, and a slower-than-expected Spruce Pro revenue ramp.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated revenue of “$31.5M” and a “-5%” year-over-year change, expecting headwinds including lower non-cash amortization, weather-affected PPA volumes, and customer buyouts.

surprises.description: Underlying contracted portfolio results were stronger than the preview’s expectation of weather-affected PPA volumes: combined PPA and lease revenue grew, and generation increased year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Combined PPA and lease revenue rose 2% year-over-year to $22.5 million” and portfolio generation increased to “approximately 196,000 megawatt-hours from 187,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “weather-affected PPA volumes” as a Q2 revenue headwind.

surprises.description: Unrestricted cash was slightly below the preview’s estimated range, though it remained above the preview’s roughly $42 million downside watch level.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended the quarter with “$81.5 million in total cash (including $44.7 million unrestricted).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Unrestricted cash $46–50M” and said cash below about “$42M” would weaken negotiating leverage.

in_line: Full-year guidance was reaffirmed, consistent with the preview’s expectation that management would reaffirm its full-year outlook absent a walk-down.

Management’s expectation that first-half O&M favorability would reverse with higher second-half service activity was consistent with the preview’s warning that O&M and collections activity would shift into H2.
Core operating expenses remained below $15 million for a fourth consecutive quarter, consistent with the preview’s description of the Q1 cost reductions as structural rather than timing-related.

surprises.description: Revenue was $25.3M, above the $24.07M consensus and up 14% sequentially versus the preview’s note that consensus assumed about 9% sequential growth. However, it was still within the preview’s $24–$25.4M working band and close to the high-end estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 14% sequentially to a record $25.3 million,” up 10% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $24.07M (Investing.com)”; the preview says to treat “$24–25.4M as the working band” and that “consensus assumes only +9%” sequential growth.

surprises.description: Gross margin was 29%, below the preview’s roughly 30% expectation, and sales mix left gross profit growing only 4% while revenue grew 10%. Management expects higher-margin products and B2B supply to help margins in the second half, but gave no quantified recovery target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 29% in Q2 2026 from 30% in Q1, with only 4% year-over-year gross profit growth to $7.3 million, lagging revenue growth as sales mix weighed on margins”; management expects higher-margin products to improve margins “in the back half of the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~30% (no formal consensus)”; the preview says “below 29% would weaken” the case for a mix shift toward proprietary products.

surprises.description: The Gen 3 product had working production samples, but mass production remained contingent on regulatory approvals and management offered no firm timeline beyond hoping for a next-quarter launch. That is less definite than the preview’s expectation of production in the mid-to-third quarter of 2026, though the call did not say it would slip to 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Gen 3 monitoring product has working production samples testing well but remains dependent on FCC and other regulatory code approvals before mass production, with no firm timeline beyond a hoped-for next-quarter launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guided to ‘mid-to-third quarter 2026’ production”; the preview identified slippage to 2027 as a major negative.
