surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenues increased 50% year-over-year and 13% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $9.44M”; the preview also cited Q1 revenue of “$8.72M.”

surprises.description: The company reported its first-ever positive cash flow from operating activities, about $500,000—a milestone the preview did not flag or forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company achieved its first-ever positive cash flow from operating activities of roughly $500,000, described as a significant milestone.”

surprises.description: Sky Harbour raised $40 million in a direct equity placement at a 4.6% discount to the 30-day VWAP, rather than relying only on the construction-facility borrowing the preview expected; the preview had specifically identified new equity as a negative shift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised $40 million via a direct equity placement at $10 per share (a 4.6% discount to the 30-day VWAP).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Drawing on the $200M JPM facility, of which $19.4M is drawn, is expected. New equity would be a negative shift.”

surprises.description: Assets under construction and completed construction increased by $65 million year to date, the company’s highest six-month growth on record—an unusually rapid build-out not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Assets under construction and completed construction reached over $393 million, a $65 million year-to-date increase representing the highest six-month growth in company history.”

surprises.description: Current construction cost of about $242 per square foot was slightly below the preview’s cited $244.37 average GMP for undelivered projects, although the comparison is not identical in scope.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Construction cost is currently about $242 per square foot.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GMPs on undelivered projects averaged $244.37 per square foot, down from $253.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed the $42–$46 million year-end annualized revenue run-rate guidance and $4–$6 million annualized adjusted EBITDA run-rate guidance, matching the preview’s stated outlook.
Lease renewals averaged a 19% rent step-up, down from the 23% cited for Q1 but still well above the preview’s 4% contractual CPI floor and its concern about spreads slowing toward single digits.

The call described a substantial construction and lease-up pipeline, including space under construction expected to roughly double by year-end and 218,000 square feet slated for lease-up by the end of 2026; this is broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation that late-2026 projects would progress without slippage.

surprises.description: The preview estimated roughly $0.8 million of STS revenue in the post-acquisition stub period, but the call said STS contributed only $200,000 to Nano after the May 22 closing. STS reported $3.9 million of unaudited revenue for the first six months of 2026, but that broader figure does not change the much smaller contribution to Nano during the period it owned the business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The acquired STS fuel transportation business generated approximately $3.9 million in unaudited revenue in the first six months of calendar 2026, contributing only $200,000 to Nano after the May 22 closing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The full preview's stub estimate is roughly $0.8M.”

surprises.description: Rather than reporting a completed binding customer commitment, Nano said it was advancing toward an initial framework agreement for a multi-gigawatt AI data center pipeline. The potential preferred-provider position and milestone-based investments of tens of millions up to $100 million represent meaningful commercial progress, but remain prospective.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nano is advancing toward an initial framework agreement with a global infrastructure developer for a multi-gigawatt AI data center pipeline that could name Nano the preferred nuclear provider and include milestone-based investments of tens of millions up to $100 million into the company.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Binding orders, deposits, or a Phase II award would be the most meaningful new evidence”; the bull scenario also called for “a binding commercial or defense commitment.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a completed feasibility study with Berupon for phased deployment of up to 1 gigawatt of Kronos capacity, with Nano moving toward NRC licensing. The preview did not identify this project as a potential catalyst, so it adds a new prospective deployment opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A completed feasibility study with Berupon evaluated phased deployment of up to 1 gigawatt of Kronos capacity, and the company is advancing toward initiating the NRC licensing process for that opportunity.”

surprises.description: Nano disclosed that Kronos can use commercially available LEU Plus fuel now and later switch to HALU without reactor redesign or plant retooling. The preview did not flag this fuel flexibility or the claimed earlier-to-market advantage as an issue investors were watching.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Kronos is designed to run on commercially available LEU Plus fuel today and can switch to HALU in the future without any reactor redesign or plant retooling, giving Nano an earlier-to-market advantage over HALU-dependent competitors.”

surprises.description: The preview described the STS deal as costing up to $13 million in cash and stock. Management said the acquisition required about $7 million in initial payment, with additional payments tied to retention, indicating a more limited upfront cash commitment than the preview's stated deal ceiling.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The STS acquisition required only about $7 million in initial payment plus future retention-based payments,” and management characterized the approach as focused on small, capability-adding deals rather than large outlays.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Secured Transportation Services (STS) closed May 22, 2026, for up to $13M in cash and stock.”

surprises.description: Headcount had grown nearly threefold to 85 employees and contractors from 31 a year earlier, with further significant technical and fuel-cycle hiring expected. The preview anticipated rising expenses but did not flag this scale of workforce expansion, which supports development capacity while also implying a substantial staffing ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Headcount grew nearly threefold to 85 employees and contractors as of Q3 end versus 31 one year prior, with expectations for continued significant expansion of technical and fuel-cycle staff.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “opex up sequentially” and flagged R&D above about $7.5 million as a faster-than-modeled ramp, but did not specify this headcount expansion.

in_line: The KRONOS NRC schedule was effectively reaffirmed: the call cited an environmental assessment in Q1 2027, a safety evaluation in Q3 2027, construction starting in H2 2027, and first power around 2030. This is consistent with the preview's Spring 2027 environmental assessment, early-fall 2027 safety evaluation, and 2H 2027 construction target.
Operating expenses were $15.9 million, modestly above the roughly $15.3 million implied by Q2 R&D and G&A figures, consistent with the preview's expectation that opex would rise sequentially.

surprises.description: The preview identified SP001’s $35 million upfront payment but did not mention the deal’s estimated $1.1 billion in total contingent value. The newly disclosed contingent economics are substantial, though their eventual cost depends on milestones and other conditions.
surprises.fact_evidence: Spero in-licensed SP001 in a deal with “an estimated $1.1 billion in total contingent value” and a “$35 million non-refundable upfront payment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the SP001 in-license as being “for $35M upfront.”

surprises.description: June 30 cash was above the preview’s estimate of roughly $46–48 million. The reported balance was $50.8 million, before adding the July royalty-financing proceeds.
surprises.fact_evidence: Cash and cash equivalents were “$50.8 million as of June 30, 2026,” excluding the net proceeds from the July royalty financing.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash (6/30/26) | ~$46–48M (preview’s estimate).”

in_line: Q2 revenue was zero, consistent with the preview’s base case of $0.0–0.3 million, although it had flagged a possible unmodeled GSK approval milestone as an upside scenario.
The $9.6 million Q2 net loss was within the preview’s implied range of roughly $9.5–10.0 million.
The company reaffirmed cash runway into the second half of 2029, as the preview expected.
GSK’s expected US availability of UTEBSI in the second half of 2026 is consistent with the preview’s expectation of availability by year-end 2026.
The planned SP001 Phase II start in Q2 2027 matched the timing in the preview.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $249 million versus the preview’s roughly $223 million guidance midpoint, and adjusted EPS was $0.83 versus the $0.71–$0.75 guide. Both profitability measures came in above the preview’s expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total adjusted EBITDA grew 19% to a record $249 million”; “Total adjusted EPS grew 26% year-over-year to $0.83.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | Midpoint ~$223M”; “Q2 adj. EPS guide of $0.71–$0.75”; the preview’s base scenario expected “Adj. EPS $0.74.”

surprises.description: Revenue just under $2 billion was above the company’s $1.916–$1.940 billion Q2 guidance range, although it was close to the preview’s roughly $1.98 billion consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue grew 2% year-over-year to just under $2 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Company guidance (Q2) $1,916M – $1,940M”; “Consensus … ~$1.98B.”

surprises.description: The Products & Solutions segment reached 43.6% gross margin, up 70 basis points year over year and extending its expansion streak to 13 quarters. That was a stronger segment margin result than the preview’s price-cost concerns might have suggested, though it does not remove the separately flagged pressure ahead.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Products & Solutions segment posted 4% revenue growth and its 13th consecutive quarter of year-over-year gross margin expansion, reaching 43.6% (up 70 bps YoY, up 100 bps sequentially).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said price actions would lag inflation”; “Further margin pressure is the main bear trigger.”

surprises.description: A large OEM security customer is vertically integrating, and reduced volumes are expected to cut second-half revenue by $40 million to $50 million versus the prior year. The preview did not identify this customer-specific risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reduced volumes from a large OEM security customer pursuing vertical integration are expected to cut second-half revenue by $40 million to $50 million versus the prior year.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA included $27 million of tariff refunds, primarily received by ADI, and management said those refunds would not recur for the rest of 2026. This means part of the strong Q2 EBITDA result came from a nonrecurring benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA included a favorable $27 million of tariff refunds, primarily received by ADI, which will not recur for the remainder of 2026.”

in_line: FY26 standalone guidance was broadly in line with the preview’s roughly $3.0 billion revenue and ~$610 million EBITDA base case: the company guided to $2.9–$2.95 billion of revenue and $605–$625 million of adjusted EBITDA. The EBITDA range was also above the $581 million Investor Day baseline cited in the preview.
The $900 million Term Loan B repayment and additional ~$200 million expected in Q3 matched the preview’s stated deleveraging expectations.

Management’s warning that rising input costs and lagging price increases could pressure Q3 gross margin was consistent with the preview’s flagged price-cost risk and expectation of flat full-year gross margin.

The call provided the cash-flow bridge the preview said investors needed: Q2 operating cash flow was $148 million, with ~$45 million of nonrecurring separation payments and $20 million of higher cash interest cited as drivers.

surprises.description: Virgin Galactic moved its first commercial spaceflight from the Q4 2026 target to February 2027, delaying the start of commercial revenue recognition. The preview treated a Q4 launch as the existing target and identified a move into early 2027 as a key downside scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “delayed its first commercial spaceflight to February 2027” and “revenue recognition now beginning at that start of commercial operations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance: first commercial spaceflight targeted for Q4 2026.” The preview also described a move to “late 2026 / early 2027” as the bear scenario.

surprises.description: Q3 free cash flow is guided to be worse than Q2, at negative $95–100 million, rather than improving to the preview’s expected roughly negative $70–80 million. Management expects improvement to negative $80–90 million in Q4, so the deterioration is presented as temporary but still makes the near-term burn outlook worse than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 free cash flow is guided to negative $95-100 million with a temporary capex increase, improving to negative $80-90 million in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “management flagged ‘sequential improvement’ in FCF from Q2 onward,” and identified a Q3 guide of “about $(70)–$(80)M” as confirming that improvement; it said “at or above $(85)M” would suggest stickier burn.

surprises.description: Cash and marketable securities ended Q2 at $286 million, above the preview’s implied $180–230 million range. The company raised $134 million through its ATM program, so the stronger cash position came alongside substantial equity issuance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “raised $134 million through its now substantially complete ATM equity program and ended Q2 with $286 million in cash and marketable securities, up from $251 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to compare ending cash with “the ~$180–230M implied range for 6/30.”

surprises.description: Management reported that the $750,000 seat tranche was oversubscribed and added more than $50 million to expected future spaceflight revenue, with a higher-priced tranche planned for fall. The preview noted interest in the reopened $750,000 seats but did not anticipate this specific level of sales or revenue commitments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's $750,000 price tranche was oversubscribed, adding over $50 million to expected future spaceflight revenue,” and management plans to open “a new tranche at higher price points this fall.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$750K seats reopened in April with interest from 20+ countries.”

surprises.description: The company raised its flight-rate goal to 10 or more flights per month by the end of Q2 2027, above the preview’s cited prior target of about 8 per month by Q2. The second spaceship is now expected to join the New Mexico fleet in March 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The second spaceship is now expected to join the New Mexico fleet in March 2027,” while maintaining “a target of 10 or more spaceflights per month by the end of Q2 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a prior commitment to “about 8 per month by Q2 2027.”

surprises.description: Q2 capex was $41 million, below the preview’s estimated $43–46 million. This is a modest favorable variance; the reported Q2 free cash flow itself was within the company’s prior guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “capex dropped to $41 million from $58 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q2 capex at “~$43–46M.”

surprises.description: Virgin Galactic reduced principal on its 2027 and 2028 notes by $93 million, leaving only $17.9 million of required 2027-note principal payments and no required 2028-note payments until March 2028. The preview discussed prior debt-for-equity activity and funding risk but did not flag this degree of debt reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “reduced principal on its 2027 and 2028 notes by $93 million,” leaving “just $17.9 million in principal payments remaining on the 2027 notes and no required payments on 2028 notes until March 2028.”

surprises.description: Management laid out strong per-ship economics: approximately $60 million to produce each new spaceship and over $1.4 billion in lifetime contribution margin under its stated flight, pricing, and margin assumptions. The preview did not discuss or set expectations for these unit-economics projections.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Each new spaceship is projected to cost approximately $60 million to produce and generate over $1.4 billion in lifetime contribution margin,” assuming 500 flights, six astronauts per flight, $600,000 average pricing, and over 80% contribution margin.

surprises.description: Management projected annualized adjusted EBITDA of $100 million with two spaceships operating in a quarter within 2028, more than $450 million with a fully utilized four-ship spaceport, and over $1 billion with two spaceports. These longer-term profitability targets were not addressed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management projects annualized adjusted EBITDA of $100 million with two spaceships in a quarter within 2028, scaling to over $450 million with a fully utilized four-ship spaceport and over $1 billion with two spaceports.”

in_line: Q2 free cash flow was negative $91 million, within the company’s prior guidance range of negative $87–92 million.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $34 million, below the preview’s $38–42 million proxy. Core revenue of $33 million was also just below the preview’s $34 million track line, while the much lower battery resale revenue accounted for the overall decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $34 million”; excluding battery hardware resales, revenue was $33 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Derived street proxy ~$38–42M”; for core revenue, “A track line of ≥$34M in Q2 is the bar.”

surprises.description: Battery resale revenue was only $300,000, well below the preview’s $2–5 million base-case assumption. Management also said resale revenue is now expected toward the lower end of the up-to-$40 million annual range, rather than suggesting Q2 dollars had de-risked the high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Battery hardware resale revenue ($300K vs. $5M in Q2 2025)”; resale revenue is “expected to trend toward the lower end of the up-to-$40 million range” and is weighted to the second half.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case assumed “battery $2–5M”; it also said “Any Q2 dollars de-risk the high end.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP gross margin reached 55%, above the preview’s 52% prior-quarter level that it said to watch for holding. Management also said full-year margin is trending toward the higher end of its 40%–50% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin reached a record 55% (up from 49% in Q2 2025)”; full-year margin is “guided to trend toward the higher end of the 40%-50% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether 52% non-GAAP gross margin holds as lower-margin battery resale returns.”

surprises.description: Operating cash flow reached breakeven at positive $300,000, rather than the second negative quarter the preview warned could threaten the annual cash-flow outlook. The improvement was substantial sequentially, though the quarter ended only slightly above breakeven.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow reached breakeven at positive $300K, a ~$9 million sequential improvement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A second negative quarter threatens the $0–10M FY OCF guide”; the bear scenario anticipated “third negative OCF quarter.”

surprises.description: ARR reached $62.4 million, falling short of the preview’s $63 million Q2 track line. PowerTrack grew, but managed services ARR was roughly flat, leaving total ARR below the stated pace for the $65–70 million year-end target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total ARR reached $62.4 million”; PowerTrack ARR was $42.8 million and managed services ARR was “roughly flat at $19.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Track line: ARR ≥$63M”; reaching the $65–70 million year-end target “needs ~$1.3–2.9M of net adds per quarter.”

surprises.description: Stem raised approximately $6 million through its ATM equity program, an equity issuance the preview did not flag. The proceeds add cash, but the share issuance is a potential dilution for existing holders.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “raised approximately $6 million via its ATM equity program at an average price of ~$9.75.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed additional international PowerTrack EMS expansion, including a new 420-MWh Chile project and a Hungary hybridization booking, developments not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Stem “expanded PowerTrack EMS to six countries and three continents including a new 420-MWh Chile project and a Hungary hybridization booking.”

in_line: Stem reaffirmed its full-year 2026 revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and operating cash flow guidance, as the preview’s base case expected.

surprises.description: STAAR reported Q2 net sales of $93.5 million, about $3.3 million above the preview’s roughly $90.2 million consensus. Sales also matched Q1’s $93.5 million rather than declining sequentially as the preview said a result just above $90 million would imply.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales reached a record $93.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 consensus ~$90.2M”; the preview also said “‘>$90M’ would be a decline from Q1's $93.5M.”

surprises.description: Despite returning to profitability, STAAR’s diluted EPS of $0.16 missed the preview’s $0.22 consensus by $0.06. This was a meaningful shortfall against the expected quarterly earnings figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income of $8.1 million ($0.16 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP) … Q2'26 consensus $0.22.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged whether China growth reflected end-market demand or pipeline fill as a key question. STAAR reported China sales up over 100% year over year and 10% sequentially, with no evidence of inventory build at distributors or hospitals, indicating demand-driven growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China net sales grew over 100% year-over-year and 10% sequentially to $52.3 million, with no evidence of inventory build at distributors or hospitals, indicating demand-driven growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “China revenue and distributor inventory” were a key metric to watch; the preview also said to “check how much of Q1 was pipeline fill versus end-market demand.”

surprises.description: EVO Plus had already reached roughly one-third of China unit volume by quarter-end, exceeding launch expectations, and customers had not resisted its considerable price premium. The preview did not flag this product’s uptake or pricing as a specific expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EVO Plus reached roughly one-third of China unit volume by quarter-end, exceeding launch expectations, while commanding a considerable price premium that customers have not resisted.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Exceeding launch expectations.”

surprises.description: U.S. sales were approximately $6 million for a second consecutive quarter, but declined sequentially from Q1. That makes the reported trend less robust than the preview’s focus on U.S. traction might have suggested, with management citing market softness and MTO supply constraints.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. sales delivered a second consecutive quarter of approximately $6 million, though this represented a sequential decline from Q1 partly due to laser refractive market softness and MTO supply constraints.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Competition and US traction” as a catalyst to watch and noted Q1 was the “first US quarter above $6M (+22%).”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that the prior-year Q3 sales figure included a one-time $25.9 million order and recommended using $68.8 million, rather than the reported $94.7 million, as the comparable base for Q3 2026. The preview did not flag this large comparison adjustment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2025 net sales of $94.7 million included a one-time $25.9 million 2024 order, so investors should use an adjusted comparable base of $68.8 million when evaluating Q3 2026 growth.”

surprises.description: Management gave a year-end cash outlook not provided in the preview: cash, equivalents, and investments were $181.5 million at Q2-end, with well over $200 million expected at year-end and no debt. The preview had cited $163.9 million of net cash and said a buyback was possible, but gave no year-end cash target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash, equivalents, and investments rose to $181.5 million from $163.9 million in Q1, with no debt, and management expects to end 2026 with well over $200 million in cash.”

surprises.description: STAAR said it plans to broaden beyond its single-product ICL position, including hiring a chief technology officer and preparing first-in-human studies on next-generation products as early as the first part of next year. This pipeline and platform plan was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “STAAR plans to expand beyond a single-product ICL company into a broader ophthalmology platform, hiring a chief technology officer and preparing first-in-human studies on next-generation products as early as the first part of next year.”

in_line: Gross margin was 74.5%, within the preview’s 74% reference and 75% goal: slightly above the reference but still below the goal. The preview had also flagged possible transition costs and the Switzerland supply move as relevant to margins.

surprises.description: Revenue was $1.8 million, below the $2.30 million consensus and the roughly $2.0 million guidance-implied figure. Instead of the expected 28% year-over-year and 21% sequential growth, revenue was flat on both comparisons.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 revenue ... was $1.8 million, effectively flat both year-over-year and sequentially”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $2.30M (range $1.86–2.33M)”; “Revenue YoY | +28%”; “Revenue QoQ | +21%”; “Guidance-implied | ~$2.0M”

surprises.description: Management said the commercial pipeline had doubled over the past five to six months and that several opportunities had already been won in the current quarter, with those wins expected to boost second-half revenue. The preview highlighted the need for account growth but did not anticipate this pipeline expansion or current-quarter wins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “the commercial pipeline has doubled over the last five to six months, with several opportunities already won in the current quarter expected to boost H2 revenue”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management needs 50–70% growth in hospital accounts to reach the 2027 target.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed the $8 million calendar-2026 revenue guidance, as the preview expected.
Management reaffirmed 2027 revenue guidance of $16–18 million, which the preview identified as dependent on Gen 2 approval and launch.
Gen 2 approval remains expected in H2 2026, with management saying it now likely falls in Q4; that timing remains within the preview’s H2 expectation and end-of-2026 launch window.
Gross margin improved to 13% from 9% a year earlier, consistent with the preview’s focus on sustained positive, expanding gross margins.
The $7.9 million net loss was close to the preview’s roughly $7.8 million implied loss, and the reported $11 loss per share was close to its $11.20 split-adjusted consensus estimate.

The financing’s $10 million in upfront gross proceeds and up-to-$30 million headline size were broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of about $10.2 million upfront from a roughly $30.1 million placement.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $18 million versus preview consensus of $17.3–17.4 million, a modest beat. On a core basis, revenue also grew 16% year over year and 19% sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 GAAP revenue was $18 million,” up “16% year-over-year on a core basis” and “19% sequentially.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP gross margin fell to 38%, below the preview’s expected floor of 44% and near the preview’s warning level of 40%. Management attributed the decline primarily to the canceled wildfire SAP contract and balance-sheet cleanup.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin fell to 38% from 52% a year earlier, primarily due to the canceled wildfire SAP contract and balance sheet cleanup.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Margin holding at or above 44% while revenue ramps would be a bull signal. Slipping toward 40% would suggest growth is being bought.”

surprises.description: Spire described an active negotiation for an eight-figure NOAA hyperspectral microwave sounding contract, with an award expected within about a month. The opportunity was not yet awarded, whereas the preview identified a production-scale NOAA award as a key need but did not identify this specific deal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In active negotiation on an eight-figure hyperspectral microwave sounding contract tied to its HIMSS payload, expected to be awarded within about a month” and “confirmed to be a US government (NOAA pipeline) opportunity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Investors need a production-scale NOAA award and a funded European contract.”

surprises.description: The radio-occultation renewal outlook included a short bridge award expected in August and a longer-term award under an $8 billion IDIQ vehicle, with combined annual value expected to exceed the prior year’s $11.2 million award. The preview had flagged government awards as important but did not mention this renewal or its expected value.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The NOAA radio occultation renewal will come as a short bridge award expected in August plus a longer-term award under an $8 billion IDIQ vehicle, with combined annual value expected to exceed last year's $11.2 million award.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Investors need a production-scale NOAA award and a funded European contract.”

surprises.description: Spire won RFGL awards from four new international customers in Q2, adding to awards from five U.S. and three international customers in Q1. The preview called out the need for a funded European contract but did not identify these customer wins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Spire won RFGL awards from four new international customers in Q2 (on top of five US and three international awards in Q1).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Investors need a production-scale NOAA award and a funded European contract.”

surprises.description: RFGL capacity had increased roughly tenfold year to date, an operational expansion not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Increased RFGL capacity roughly 10x year-to-date.”

surprises.description: Spire reported an approximately $12.4 million award in the dismissed Northstar arbitration, an unexpected favorable outcome; the facts do not say whether or when the award will be collected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Was awarded approximately $12.4 million in the dismissed Northstar arbitration.”

surprises.description: Cash ended at approximately $92 million, with Q2 operating cash burn of $23.4 million. That was somewhat better than the preview’s downside condition of cash falling to roughly $85–90 million if Q2 free cash flow was again worse than about $25 million, though the reported burn measure is operating cash burn rather than free cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with approximately $92 million in cash and marketable securities” and “operating cash burn ($23.4 million in Q2).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If Q2 free cash flow is again worse than about –$25M, cash would fall to roughly $85–90M.”

in_line: Full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $75–85 million was reaffirmed, as expected in the preview’s base case.
More than 85% of the full-year guidance midpoint was under contract, broadly matching the preview’s base expectation of approximately 85–88%.
Adjusted EBITDA was negative $8.6 million, and management maintained the expected break-even timing of late 2026 to early 2027.

surprises.description: Karyopharm said it has only $65.4 million in cash and expects that liquidity to fund operations into September, shorter than the preview’s “late in the third quarter” runway expectation. More importantly, the $15.8 million payment due September 10 would breach the $10 million minimum-liquidity covenant and trigger default unless the company raises financing or gets a waiver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 2026 with only $65.4 million in cash and equivalents, with existing liquidity projected to fund operations into September 2026”; “A $15.8 million principal payment is due September 10, 2026 … and paying it without additional financing or a waiver would breach the $10 million minimum liquidity covenant and trigger an event of default.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether the company still had runway “into late Q3 2026” and flagged that runway not clearing the Oct. 10 covenant step-up was a red flag. It also noted the June installment was deferred to Sept. 10 and said financing or a debt amendment was a key item to watch.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue came in above consensus, and U.S. Xpovio revenue was also above the preview’s estimate. The total revenue beat was modest, with the product line contributing the stronger result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue declined to $33.4 million”; “U.S. Xpovio net product revenue grew to $30.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 total revenue consensus was “$32.19M”; U.S. Xpovio net product revenue was estimated at “~$29M.”

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed FY2026 revenue guidance of $130 million–$150 million, despite the preview saying a trim toward the low end was the most likely outcome after the endometrial-cancer trial failure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year revenue guidance was reaffirmed at $130-150 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the range “needs $63M – $83M in 2H” and that “a trim toward the low end is the most likely outcome.”

surprises.description: The myelofibrosis filing is on track for August, and the FDA gave written feedback that SVR35 appears to qualify as a reasonably likely surrogate endpoint for overall survival. That goes beyond the preview’s expectation of confirming an H2 filing and its concern about the FDA’s view of the missed symptom-score co-primary endpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: Karyopharm is “on track to submit its” sNDA “in August 2026”; the FDA said “SVR35 appears to qualify as a reasonably likely surrogate endpoint for overall survival,” supporting the planned submission based on week 24 SVR35 data.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for “Confirmation of an H2 2026 submission and any comment on FDA's view of the TSS miss.”

surprises.description: Management presented a substantial U.S. commercial opportunity for selinexor plus ruxolitinib—up to about $1 billion in peak annual revenue, targeting roughly 4,000 newly treated frontline patients each year. The preview did not include a peak-sales estimate or this patient-opportunity framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management estimates the combination “could generate up to approximately $1 billion in peak annual U.S. revenue,” targeting “roughly 4,000 newly treated frontline patients annually” among about 20,000 U.S. myelofibrosis patients.

surprises.description: Management raised potential NCCN compendia inclusion in the second half of 2026 as a commercial catalyst and said an NCCN listing alone typically drives about half of a product’s peak revenue; the preview did not flag this catalyst or estimate its potential impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects “potential NCCN compendia inclusion in the second half of 2026” and noted “NCCN listing alone typically drives about 50% of a product's peak revenue.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses were down year over year and the loss from operations improved, while net loss widened because of non-cash financing-related mark-to-market adjustments. The preview sought a quantified post-trial cost outlook but did not anticipate this divergence between improving operating results and a larger reported net loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expenses fell 12% and SG&A fell 9% year-over-year, and loss from operations improved about 8%, though net loss widened to $67 million from $37.3 million due partly to non-cash mark-to-market financing adjustments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said investors would want “a specific revised R&D + SG&A figure” after the endometrial trial failure and warned that vague language would be bearish; it did not mention mark-to-market effects on net loss.

in_line: The Sentry trial’s reported overall-survival hazard ratio of 0.43 and stronger week-24 SVR35 response were consistent with the preview, which already cited those results (HR 0.43; SVR35 49.8% versus 28.0%).

The Q2 cash balance of $65.4 million was within the preview’s $60 million–$70 million base-case range, even though the reported runway and September payment created a worse liquidity/covenant outlook.
Top-line data from the Sentry-2 60mg cohort in the second half of 2026 matched the preview’s expected H2 timing.
Reducing investment in endometrial cancer was expected after the already-disclosed EC042 primary-endpoint failure; the preview specifically noted management planned to reduce investment.

surprises.description: Tapestry’s FY27 EPS guide of $7.80–$7.90 is well above the preview’s $7.45–$7.50 consensus range and reaches the preview’s bullish threshold. The company also expects 50 bps of operating-margin expansion to nearly 24%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for revenue of $8.4-8.5 billion (mid-single-digit growth), operating margin expansion of 50 bps to nearly 24%, and EPS of $7.80-7.90 (low double-digit growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus FY27 adj. EPS is about $7.45–7.50”; “Above $7.75 is a bull signal.”

surprises.description: Kate Spade is expected to decline by high single digits in FY27 and post a modest operating loss, rather than returning to roughly flat-to-up revenue with positive operating income as the preview said the Street needed. This is a material negative contrast to the expected trajectory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FY27 guide embeds … a high single-digit decline at Kate Spade, which is expected to post a modest operating loss.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Street needs FY27 Kate Spade guided to roughly flat-to-up with positive operating income.”

surprises.description: Q4 EPS of $1.32 exceeded the preview’s $1.25 consensus estimate, even with a $0.05 tax headwind. That is a clear quarterly earnings beat, larger than the preview’s implied $1.22 figure as well.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 EPS grew 28% to $1.32, beating guidance despite a $0.05 tax headwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS $1.25” consensus; the preview also said guidance implied “Q4 … $1.22 EPS.”

surprises.description: FY26 finished somewhat ahead of the preview’s roughly $7.95 billion revenue, 23% operating-margin, and $6.95–$6.97 EPS expectations. Tapestry also said it achieved its three-year Investor Day commitments two years early.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 revenue of $8 billion, growing 17% on a pro forma constant currency basis, hitting its Investor Day 3-year commitments two years ahead of plan”; “Full-year operating margin expanded 340 basis points to over 23%, while EPS grew 38% to $7.05.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue ~$7.95B”; “Operating margin ~23% (+300bps)”; “Adj. EPS ~$6.95 guide” and “$6.97” consensus.

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s focus on tariff-related gross-margin pressure, Q4 gross margin expanded by 180 bps. The call does not quantify how much of the tariff headwind abated, but the reported margin expansion is a favorable result against that concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 gross margin expanded 180 basis points to 78.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Gross margin and tariffs” and asked “whether the 180bps headwind … is guided to abate.”

surprises.description: Tapestry plans to return $1.7 billion to shareholders in FY27, including about $1.35 billion of buybacks, and raised its dividend 16%. This indicates a strong return pace against the preview’s question about FY27 capital returns and its cited $3 billion FY26–FY28 buyback target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tapestry raised its dividend 16% to an annualized $1.85 per share and plans to return $1.7 billion to shareholders in FY27, including approximately $1.35 billion in buybacks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$3B buyback targeted for FY26–FY28, with about $1.5B returned in FY26. Watch FY27 pace and any dividend increase.”

in_line: Q4 constant-currency sales rose 11%, broadly matching the preview’s derived estimate of about 11% pro forma growth; Coach’s 14% growth was also broadly consistent with the preview’s low-teens expectation.

surprises.description: Q2 same-station revenue declined 9.6%, slightly worse than the preview’s mid-to-high-single-digit decline guide, and revenue of about $44.1 million was below the roughly $46 million estimate implied by Noble’s FY26 forecast. The result points to somewhat greater top-line weakness than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue fell approximately 9.6% on a same-station basis to about $44.1 million” from $49.1 million a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Same-station net revenue: Down “mid-to-high single digits”; Noble FY26 revenue of ~$205.9M implies roughly $46M.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was stronger than the preview’s base case of a modestly positive result: it reached about $5.3 million, with management attributing improvement to early cost-cut benefits. The preview noted Q2 seasonality, but did not give a numerical EBITDA estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to approximately $5.3 million from $4.7 million in Q2 2025 and reversed a negative $0.4 million in Q1 2026,” reflecting “early cost-cut benefits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base scenario: “Adj. EBITDA” “Modestly positive”; Q2 “is seasonally stronger.”

surprises.description: The May expense-reduction program is now expected to deliver about $10.5 million in annualized savings, above the roughly $7 million in annualized actions described in the preview. The benefit is phased in, with about $5 million expected in 2026 and the full impact in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: The May expense reduction program is “expected to generate about $10.5 million in annualized run-rate savings,” with “roughly $5 million benefiting 2026 and full impact realized in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Cost actions: “~$2M annualized from early-retirement offering, plus ~$5M of further annualized reductions.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a sharp channel split that the preview did not forecast: local direct revenue grew, but national revenue excluding political fell steeply and local agency revenue also declined. That points to weakness concentrated in agency-related channels despite local direct growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-station local direct revenue grew approximately 9% year-over-year, while national revenue (ex-political) fell about 21% and local agency revenue declined about 12%.”

surprises.description: The call added a favorable forward sales signal not covered in the preview: Q4 pacing was described as very strong even though only minimal political revenue had been booked. Management also guided to a mid-single-digit same-station revenue decline in Q3, a less severe decline than Q2’s reported 9.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management guided Q3 same-station revenue to decline in the “mid-single-digit range” year-over-year and characterized Q4 pacing as “very strong” with “only minimal political revenue booked.”

surprises.description: Interest expense fell substantially, an improvement not quantified or highlighted in the preview. The reduction was aided by making the new second-lien obligation payment-in-kind, so some of the lower cash interest reflects deferred rather than eliminated payment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Interest expense fell to about $1.5 million from $3.3 million a year earlier,” aided by converting the new second lien obligation from cash-pay to payment-in-kind.

surprises.description: Beasley agreed to sell two stations in Charlotte and Las Vegas for $8 million, with proceeds intended to reduce debt. The preview did not anticipate this asset sale; management said it should not affect EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “agreed on July 31 to sell two radio stations in Charlotte and Las Vegas to EMF for $8 million,” with proceeds reducing debt and “no expected EBITDA impact.”

surprises.description: Management reported nearly $6 million of closed business from its “Summer of Influence” and “America 250” programs, a sales initiative result not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The enterprise “Summer of Influence” and “America 250” programs “have generated nearly $6 million in closed business.”

surprises.description: The company said it had booked more than 25% of its full-year political budget, tracking with the 2024 presidential cycle. The preview did not provide an expectation for political bookings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Beasley has booked more than 25% of its full-year political budget tracking with the 2024 presidential cycle.”

in_line: The large GAAP debt-restructuring gain was anticipated: the preview expected a large non-cash gain, and the call reported a $91.8 million gain.
Post-restructuring long-term debt of roughly $129 million was broadly consistent with the preview’s estimated mid-$130 million range.

Digital revenue remained positive, as the preview expected growth to hold: same-station digital revenue rose about 7% and was about 26% of total revenue, while owned-and-operated digital revenue grew about 10% in Q2.

surprises.description: Rockwell generated about $2.1 million of operating cash flow in Q2 and ended with $24.8 million in cash, equivalents, and investments, up from $23.9 million in Q1. That was stronger than the preview’s balance-sheet backdrop of negative Q1 operating cash flow and its concern about limited net cash.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company generated approximately $2.1 million in operating cash flow in Q2, ending the quarter with $24.8 million in cash, equivalents, and investments, up from $23.9 million in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating cash flow -$0.17M” in Q1; “Net cash was $8.8M at Q1”; “Watch for any financing or equity issuance language, since net cash is only $8.8M.”

surprises.description: Management said the reverse split was solely to regain Nasdaq bid-price compliance and would not be followed by a capital raise. The preview flagged possible equity issuance as a concern, so this was a direct reassurance against that risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The recently completed reverse stock split was undertaken solely to regain Nasdaq minimum bid price compliance and will not be followed by a capital raise.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for any financing or equity issuance language, since net cash is only $8.8M.”

surprises.description: Rockwell disclosed a new medical-device opportunity that it plans to fund within its existing operating plan. The preview did not anticipate this opportunity or provide for this additional self-funded initiative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new self-funded medical device opportunity is being financed within the existing operating plan.”

surprises.description: The call described customer expansion beyond the preview’s focus on whether a DaVita restock would appear: sales growth was driven by new western U.S. customers and higher purchases from existing customers, while Rockwell added a Heritage Dialysis agreement and renewed with Aqua Dialysis. Management also said the incremental western volume carries above-company-average margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales rose 11% year-over-year ... driven by new western U.S. customers, higher purchasing from existing customers, and annual pricing actions”; “added a new Heritage Dialysis agreement plus an Aqua Dialysis renewal”; “Incremental western U.S. volume growth carries margins consistently higher than the corporate average.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue vs. about $17.9M and the DaVita line. ... If DaVita's Q2 restock shows up in the number, the customer-diversification story holds.”

in_line: Q2 net sales of $17.8 million were at the low end of the preview’s $17.8–18.2 million consensus range.
Q2 gross margin of 18% was within the preview’s 18–19% base scenario, though below its 20% catalyst level.
Management reiterated the FY2026 sales, gross-margin, and adjusted-EBITDA guidance, consistent with the preview’s base case of reaffirmation.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $206 million, below the preview’s $216.3–$219.3 million consensus range by about $10–$13 million, despite revenue more than quadrupling year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached $206 million, more than 4x the prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $219.3M (Zacks) / $216.3M (Street, TipRanks)”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was a $14 million loss, well below the preview’s indicative expectation of roughly breakeven to positive $8 million. Management said a $14.7 million estimate-at-complete adjustment on IM-4 partially offset the improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA improved to negative $14 million … partially offset by a $14.7 million estimate-at-complete adjustment on IM-4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | Not formally surveyed; buy-side roughly breakeven to +$8M”

surprises.description: Backlog reached a record $1.8 billion, above the preview’s $1.3–$1.5 billion base-case range. The reported $1.7 billion in year-to-date bookings, including $1.2 billion in Q2 bookings through the call date, and the commercial wins—including three GEO satellites valued at over $600 million—helped explain the stronger-than-expected order position.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record $1.8 billion backlog”; “generated $1.7 billion in bookings year-to-date, including $1.2 billion in new bookings in Q2 through the call date”; “three GEO communication satellites valued at over $600 million over 30 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base | … backlog $1.3–1.5B”; the preview also said Q1 backlog of $1.1B “needs to climb sharply.”

surprises.description: The expected timing of backlog conversion shifted materially later: management now expects just 25%–30% to convert to revenue in 2026, versus the 60%–65% conversion expectation cited after Q1. It projects 35%–40% in 2027 and the remainder thereafter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects backlog conversion of 25%-30% to revenue in 2026, 35%-40% in 2027, and the remainder thereafter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Backlog $1.1B … with 60–65% expected to convert to revenue in 2026.”

surprises.description: Management said the lunar communications constellation is being accelerated: Altus-1 is planned for Mission 3 in Q1 2027, with the other four Altus satellites deploying together in 2028 to achieve full operational capability ahead of schedule. The preview did not flag this accelerated constellation timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The lunar communications constellation is being accelerated, with Altus-1 launching on Mission 3 in Q1 2027 and the remaining four Altus satellites now planned to deploy together in 2028 to reach full operational capability ahead of schedule.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed FY2026 revenue guidance of $900 million to $1 billion, as the preview expected.
Management continued to expect positive adjusted EBITDA for FY2026, matching the preview’s stated guidance.

surprises.description: Ondas reported Q2 revenue of about $83.8 million, well above the preview’s roughly $68 million reference consensus and even above the preview’s $75–85 million bull-case range’s lower end. The result was about 22% above the top of the cited consensus range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record ~$83.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$66.7M (Zacks) to $68.5M (Street); range $63–69M”; “$75–85M” in the bull scenario.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA loss was about $51 million, far worse than the preview’s base-case loss of $13–18 million and its stated bear-case threshold of more than $20 million. Management still called it the peak loss quarter, as expected, but the size of the loss was a substantial negative gap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of ~$51 million, which management characterized as the peak loss.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A print materially worse than about –$18M, or language walking back ‘peak,’ would hurt”; the bear scenario specified “Loss above $20M.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $140–155 million came in below the preview’s roughly $160 million or more threshold, even though it implies a steep sequential ramp. The guided range’s high end is still below that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue is guided to $140-155 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus needs roughly $160M or more.”

surprises.description: Pro forma backlog reached about $757 million, above the preview’s estimate of roughly $663 million with DZYNE and Cyberhawk. The additional expansion of the strategic pipeline to more than $11 billion was also not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pro forma backlog grew ~66% sequentially to ~$757 million”; “the 2-year strategic pipeline expanded to over $11 billion, up 2.5x since May.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pro forma backlog was $457M at Q1, expected around $663M with DZYNE and Cyberhawk.”

surprises.description: Management said operating-platform profitability had been pulled forward by one quarter, to Q4 2026, and set a Q4 2027 target for company-wide adjusted EBITDA profitability. The preview discussed the peak-loss quarter but gave no such profitability timetable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating platform profitability now pulled forward one quarter to Q4 2026 and company-wide adjusted EBITDA profitability targeted for Q4 2027.”

surprises.description: The full-year revenue outlook now has a $525–550 million range, whereas the preview cited guidance of at least $525 million. The floor matches the prior expectation, but the stated upper end adds some upside rather than merely repeating a floor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $525-550 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue: ≥$525M.”

surprises.description: Management warned of second-half gross-margin pressure from acquired excess capacity, a risk the preview did not flag. The warning is tempered by the reported 50.4% margin and management’s continued 50%+ long-term target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin was 50.4%”; management warned of “second-half margin pressure from acquired excess capacity” while maintaining a “50%+ long-term target.”

surprises.description: Ondas reported about $105 million in additional orders quarter-to-date in Q3, extending order momentum beyond the Q2 order intake discussed in the preview. The preview did not give an expectation for Q3-to-date orders.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company captured $175 million in new orders during Q2 and ~$105 million more quarter-to-date in Q3.”

in_line: Adjusted gross margin was 50.4%, above the preview’s roughly 44% level that would have challenged the defense-platform margin narrative.
Q2 order intake was consistent with the preview’s indication that orders were already above $150 million quarter-to-date: the reported Q2 total was about $175 million.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $1.5 million, modestly above the preview’s roughly $1.43 million consensus estimate, though it was at the top of the preview’s $1.35–$1.50 million base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $1.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue | ~$1.43M”; base scenario: “Revenue | $1.35–1.50M.”

surprises.description: Revenue recognized rose to about 19% of EsoGuard’s billable list-price value, up from the 14% recognition rate cited in the preview. That improvement helped lift revenue even though test volume was essentially flat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2,770 EsoGuard tests…with a billable/pro forma value of about $7.6 million at the list price of $2,749, but only ~19% was recognized as revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Lucid recognizes only 14% of billable value”; the preview also said “ASP roughly flat” in its base scenario.

surprises.description: Test volume came in below the preview’s expected range and its stated operating bar of holding above 3,000 tests: Lucid performed 2,770 tests, even though that remained within the company’s 2,500–3,000 target range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The lab performed 2,770 EsoGuard tests in Q2 2026”; “test volume remaining essentially flat within the 2,500-3,000 target range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EsoGuard tests | ~3,000–3,300”; “Holding above 3,000 while protecting ASP is the operating bar.”

surprises.description: Among adjudicated claims, the share producing an allowable amount and the average allowable were both weaker than the preview’s prior-quarter benchmarks: 28% and $1,424 per test, versus 31% and $1,646.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Of Q2 claims submitted, 65% were adjudicated with only 28% of those resulting in an allowable amount averaging $1,424 per test.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Of adjudicated claims, 31% were paid at an average allowable of $1,646 per test.”

surprises.description: The first VA contribution to test volume is now expected only after October 1, rather than testing beginning in the “very near future” as the preview anticipated; management is still securing purchase orders and building a pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects the VA opportunity to begin contributing to test volume only after the new federal fiscal year starting October 1, as the company currently focuses on securing purchase orders and building pipeline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A first purchase order has been received, with testing to begin ‘in the very near future’”; the preview also listed “First VA revenue” as a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: Lucid reported a new coverage breakthrough not anticipated in the preview: Concert deemed EsoGuard medically necessary, and three client health plans have adopted the policy, covering just under 10 million lives concentrated in the Midwest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lucid secured its first laboratory benefit manager coverage policy from Concert, which deemed EsoGuard medically necessary while classifying competing esophageal precancer tests as investigational”; “Three of Concert's client health plans have already adopted the coverage policy, with the LBM covering just under 10 million covered lives.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed roughly 225 million fully diluted shares including unvested RSAs and abeyance shares, materially above the 190.8 million GAAP shares outstanding cited in the preview. The figures use different share-count bases, but the fully diluted total indicates more potential dilution than the preview’s outstanding-share figure alone conveyed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fully diluted shares including unvested RSAs and abeyance shares would total roughly 225 million, versus GAAP shares outstanding of 190.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Shares outstanding…190.8M.”

in_line: Q2 cash burn was $11.3 million, matching the preview’s approximately $11.3 million quarterly burn benchmark.
The Medicare LCD remained pending and was described as a major near-term revenue catalyst, consistent with the preview’s emphasis on the decision as the key catalyst.

surprises.description: Q1 net sales of $936 million were about $21 million above the preview’s roughly $915 million consensus estimate, although they were close to the company-guidance midpoint of $935 million and within its guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY27 net sales rose 5% year-over-year to $936 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus ~$915M (at time of guide)”; company guidance was “$915M – $955M (midpoint $935M).”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS increased 65% year-over-year, well above the preview’s expected 30%–39% growth for EPS including 45X. The call also cited a $31 million tariff refund and $9 million of expanded 45X benefits, so the reported growth included additional benefits beyond the preview’s stated EPS expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS increasing 65% over the prior year”; results included “a one-time $31 million tariff refund ($0.63/share)” and “$9 million of expanded 45X benefits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q1 adjusted diluted EPS guidance of “$2.70 – $2.90” and expected year-over-year growth of “+30% to +39%.”

in_line: Q1 sales growth of 5% was within the preview’s implied year-over-year range of 2.5%–6.9% based on company guidance.
Industrial Mobility Solutions revenue declined 3%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the segment would remain soft through mid-FY27.

surprises.description: Revenue was $49 million, 6.7% above the $45.9 million consensus and well above the implied 6.7% year-on-year growth rate: reported growth was 13%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $49 million, up 13% year-on-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $45.9M”; implied y/y “+6.7%.”

surprises.description: Same-clinic revenue grew 6% and average spend per visit rose 9%, providing evidence of underlying clinic growth on the preview’s central organic-growth debate, though the preview gave no specific same-clinic forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-clinic revenue grew 6% and average spend per visit rose 9% in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Organic revenue ex-Waqoo” was the top metric to watch; the preview said the return-to-growth thesis depended on whether related-party revenue turned positive and whether organic growth held up.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA of $20 million modestly exceeded the preview author’s roughly $19 million estimate, but the 41% margin was below the 42% author estimate and the 42–44% base scenario. It still cleared the preview’s 40% margin floor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 32% to $20 million with a 41% margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EBITDA: No formal consensus (author estimate ~$19M, ~42% margin)”; base scenario margin “42–44%,” and the key metric was “EBITDA margin at or above 40%.”

surprises.description: Management described about $15 million of annual service-fee increases, mostly flowing directly to profit, with only about half contributing in the second half of this fiscal year and the full contribution starting next year. This was new upside after the prior-quarter CFO had said the fee-structure impact was “now over.”
surprises.fact_evidence: “Planned service fee increases—roughly $11 million per year from enhanced call center functions and $4 million from Gorilla/Lise clinic support—are expected to add about $15 million annually, mostly flowing directly to profit”; “only about half its value in Q3 and Q4” and “full contribution beginning next fiscal year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the Q1 CFO stated that the fee-structure impact was “now over.” It also noted that SBC “has never issued quantitative FY guidance.”

surprises.description: Management said it is considering increasing its ownership in minority-stake partner OrangeTwist, which operates 24 U.S. locations and has recurring revenue above 40% of sales. The preview flagged capital deployment as a key debate but did not identify this potential stake increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SBC’s minority-stake partner OrangeTwist operates 24 U.S. locations across 6 states with recurring revenue exceeding 40% of sales, and the company is considering increasing its ownership stake.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “an executed buyback or a named deal would be the clearest re-rating catalyst.”

surprises.description: Management laid out a long-term ambition to reach 1,000 clinics by 2035 while keeping indirect-department headcount flat through AI-enabled efficiency. The preview discussed clinic growth and margins, but did not anticipate this specific scale-and-staffing target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SBC targets 1,000 clinics by 2035 (up from close to 300 currently) while aiming to keep indirect department headcount flat by leveraging AI for operational efficiency.”

surprises.description: Management said it wants to shift the transaction mix substantially toward non-aesthetic categories over the next decade, despite the current mix being about 84% aesthetic and 16% non-aesthetic. The preview did not flag this strategic mix-change ambition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's transaction value mix remains roughly 84% aesthetic and 16% non-aesthetic, with management targeting a substantial shift toward non-aesthetic categories over the next decade.”

in_line: Clinic locations reached 287, up 34 year-on-year, broadly tracking the prior-quarter figure of 284 and its 33-location year-on-year increase; trailing 12-month visits remained up 10%, matching the prior-quarter growth rate.
The 41% adjusted EBITDA margin remained above the preview’s explicitly watched 40% floor, even though it was below the author estimate and base-case range.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue reached $506 million, above both the $500 million high end of company guidance and the $500.7 million consensus cited in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue grew 6% in constant currency (7% reported) to $506 million, exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance (Q2): $495–500M”; “Consensus: $500.7M (+5.6%).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.40, above the preview’s $0.38 consensus and the top of the company’s $0.35–$0.38 outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose 14% year-over-year to $0.40, beating the company's $0.35-$0.38 outlook.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS: $0.35–0.38” guidance and “$0.38” consensus.

surprises.description: The company raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $1.55–$1.65, moving the midpoint above the $1.51 midpoint of the prior range and into the preview’s bullish scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[Raised] adjusted EPS to $1.55-$1.65 (from $1.43-$1.58).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Investors want the midpoint moved above $1.51”; the bull scenario listed “FY EPS raised toward $1.55–1.65.”

surprises.description: Full-year revenue guidance was raised rather than merely reaffirmed, although the increase was modest relative to the prior range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[Raised] full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $1.98-$2.0 billion (from $1.96-$1.985 billion).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave FY2026 guidance of “revenue $1.96–1.985B” and said a “meaningful Q2 beat with FY revenue merely reaffirmed would imply a flat 2H.”

surprises.description: Saucony grew 9% despite the preview’s warning about its exceptionally difficult comparison and concern that the brand was sputtering; the company also raised Saucony’s full-year growth outlook to mid-teens.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Merrell and Saucony, which represent roughly two-thirds of the business, grew 10% and 9% respectively”; “Saucony's full-year growth outlook was raised to mid-teens (from low-to-mid-teens).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called this “the toughest comp of the year for Saucony,” cited concern that the “lifestyle engine is ‘beginning to sputter,’” and said revenue “below about $145M would point to a flat year-over-year result.”

surprises.description: Full-year gross-margin guidance rose to approximately 46.9% from 46.4%, with management saying the improvement was mostly structural rather than driven by tariff relief.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year gross margin guidance was raised to approximately 46.9% (from 46.4%),” mostly due to “healthier inventories and more full-price sales” rather than “the modest ~$2 million tariff relief.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY gross-margin guidance of “~46.4%” and flagged tariff assumptions and gross margin as key issues.

surprises.description: Adjusted operating margin reached 10%, 50 basis points above the approximately 9.5% level expected in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “80 basis points of adjusted operating margin expansion to 10%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating margin: ~9.5% (+30 bps).”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin was 46.5%, slightly above the preview’s approximately 46.4% expectation, while absorbing the estimated tariff headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin fell 70 basis points to 46.5%, absorbing an approximate 310 basis point unmitigated tariff headwind that mitigation actions largely offset.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected gross margin of “~46.4%” and estimated “about 310 bps of unmitigated tariff headwind in Q2.”

surprises.description: Operating free cash flow guidance was raised by $10 million at both ends of the range, above the prior full-year forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating free cash flow guidance was raised to $115-$130 million from $105-$120 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY operating FCF guidance of “$105–120M.”

surprises.description: Net debt was $443 million, down $125 million year over year, a further reduction from the $519 million level the preview reported at Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt fell $125 million year-over-year to $443 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Net debt was $519M at Q1, down $85M YoY,” but gave no Q2 net-debt forecast.

surprises.description: Inventory was down approximately 17% year over year; management attributed this to timing and efficiency initiatives and said current levels could support the raised second-half outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory ended the quarter down approximately 17% year-over-year due to timing and efficiency initiatives, with management confident current levels support the raised second-half revenue outlook.”

surprises.description: Merrell grew 10% in Q2, but its DTC revenue declined and management left its full-year outlook at mid-single-digit growth rather than raising it after the strong quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Merrell and Saucony … grew 10% and 9% respectively”; “Merrell's DTC revenue declined as marketing dollars shifted to upper-funnel brand building, and its full-year outlook was held unchanged at mid-single-digit growth.”

surprises.description: Net revenue per dispensed unit was about $1,291 ($15.4 million divided by 11,925 units), below the preview’s roughly $1,330 expectation. The shortfall was modest and remained above the preview’s $1,200 downside threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net product revenue grew 45% quarter-over-quarter to $15.4 million” and prescribed units rose “from 8,084 to 11,925 units.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue per unit (about $1,330 needed)” and “Net revenue per unit at or above about $1,330.”

surprises.description: Management expects gross-to-net deductions to rise, rather than remaining stable or showing only modest price erosion: it guided to the low-to-mid 30% range, potentially reaching the mid-to-high 30s with a new PBM contract.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross-to-net was 29.6% in Q2, but management guided GTNs will rise to the low-to-mid 30% range, potentially mid-to-high 30s if a new PBM contract is signed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bull scenario assumed “gross-to-net stable”; the base scenario assumed “modest price erosion.”

surprises.description: SG&A rose 31% quarter over quarter to $27.7 million, contrary to the preview’s expectation that flat or falling spending would demonstrate operating leverage. Management attributed much of the increase to a one-time $5.3 million sales milestone, so the increase does not all indicate a higher recurring cost base.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A rose 31% to $27.7 million largely due to a $5.3 million one-time non-recurring sales milestone.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Flat or falling SG&A on revenue growth would show operating leverage. Continued increases would not.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a restatement of its Q1 financials for convertible-debt fair-value accounting, an unexpected reporting issue. It said the restatement did not affect cash, revenue, expenses, operating loss, or adjusted EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company disclosed a restatement of Q1 2026 financials tied to fair value accounting of convertible debt under a subordination agreement,” but “it does not affect cash, revenue, expenses, operating loss, or adjusted EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Q2 COGS included an out-of-spec API inventory write-off that the preview did not anticipate. The $0.9 million charge is a specific adverse cost item, though the call described it as a write-off rather than an ongoing expense level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “COGS included a $0.9 million write-off of out-of-spec API inventory.”

surprises.description: Zegalyze is now slated for Q3 2027, later than the preview’s mid-2027 timing expectation. The preview’s early-2027 timing for the other product, Zepi, was broadly consistent with its Q1 2027 launch schedule.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Zepi (impetigo) in Q1 2027 and Zegalyze (head lice) in Q3 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “XEPI (early 2027)” and “XEGLYZE (mid-2027)” as the expected timing.

surprises.description: The company said the two upcoming launches can use its existing 67-territory sales force with minimal incremental spend, adding a cost-efficiency detail the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Both products are “leveraging the existing 67-territory sales force with minimal incremental spend.”

in_line: Q2 net product revenue of $15.4 million was essentially in line with the preview’s $15.22 million total-revenue consensus and approximately $15.0 million implied net-product-revenue expectation.
Q2 dispensed units of 11,925 were within the preview’s 11,000–12,500 expected range.
Cash of $24.2 million was within the preview’s expected $22–26 million range.
Adjusted EBITDA improved sequentially to negative $5.7 million from negative $8.0 million, delivering the sequential improvement the preview identified as an important signal.
Zepi’s Q1 2027 launch timing was broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of an early-2027 launch.
The reported 59% commercial insurance coverage was in line with the preview’s stated 59% commercial coverage.

surprises.description: BKTI reported Q2 revenue of $23.4 million, above the preview’s $22.6 million consensus estimate. The roughly 3.5% beat was a modest positive surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 10.6% year-over-year to $23.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (Q2) … Consensus … $22.6M.”

surprises.description: The BKR 9500’s FCC approval was expected in H2 2026, but management now expects approval in early 2027. That pushes the approval milestone later than the preview led investors to expect, although customer deliveries remain anticipated in H1 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[The BKR 9500] was submitted for FCC testing, with approval expected in early 2027 and customer deliveries anticipated in the first half of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The BKR9500 is guided to FCC approval in H2 2026 and shipments in H1 2027.”

surprises.description: The BKR 9500 had purchase orders for more than 200 units before customers had seen the product, a demand signal the preview did not specify. This is a positive product update, though the orders’ value and delivery timing are not quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new BKR 9500 in-vehicle multiband radio has drawn purchase orders exceeding 200 units sight unseen.”

surprises.description: Management reported a Tango Tango licensing agreement that extends InteropONE to more than 1,500 agencies and 35,000-plus active users, creating a recurring licensing-fee pathway. The preview identified InteropONE/Tango Tango monetization as a 2027 narrative but did not anticipate this specific agreement or its reach.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A licensing agreement with Tango Tango extends InteropONE technology to over 1,500 public safety agencies and 35,000+ active users, creating a recurring licensing fee pathway.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “InteropONE / Tango Tango monetization” was listed among the “2027 narrative[s].”

surprises.description: Management gave a January 2027 target for general release of the BKR Play tethering solution, a product timing update not covered in the preview. It adds a future product milestone, but the call facts do not quantify its commercial opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The BKR Play tethering solution is targeted for general release in January 2027.”

in_line: Gross margin was 51.9%, above the preview’s 50% threshold and within its expected 50–52% base-case range.
FY2026 guidance was reiterated rather than raised, consistent with the preview’s base case. The preview noted that a raise was possible in a bull case, but its base case expected reiteration.
GAAP diluted EPS of $0.79 was close to the preview’s $0.77 consensus estimate, and non-GAAP adjusted EPS of $1.01 was within the preview’s $0.92–$1.02 base-case range.

surprises.description: Revenue was $21.5 million, below the $22.3 million sell-side consensus, although it remained within the company’s preliminary $21–$23 million range. The shortfall versus consensus was modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 65% year-over-year to $21.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue, sell-side consensus” was “$22.3M”; company preliminary revenue was “$21.0M – $23.0M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached only 38.6%, well below the preview’s expectation of at least 42% and its roughly 43% implication. Hardware and service margins also fell, and management said a return to 40%+ blended margins is not expected until 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin held roughly flat at 38.6% versus 38.5%, but hardware margin fell to 17.2% from 25.1% and service margin declined to 50.1% from 54.4%, with a return to 40%+ blended margins not expected until 2027.”
