surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cohort 3 enrollment and readout timing. Watch for patients dosed, last-patient-last-visit estimate, and a date for the independent statistician's dose-response analysis.”

surprises.description: Management clarified that it does not plan to test more than three weekly treatments, citing patient tolerability and logistical constraints. The three-treatment regimen would move into a future efficacy trial only if Cohort 3 data are favorable, adding a limit and condition to the development plan that the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management does not plan to test more than three weekly treatments due to patient tolerability and logistical constraints, and would carry the three-treatment regimen forward into a future efficacy trial if cohort 3 data are favorable.”

in_line: June 30 cash of approximately $4.9 million was within the preview’s $4.70–$5.50 million range, though below its approximately $5.15 million estimate; the post-quarter offering was also anticipated as a $4.0 million follow-on.

Management’s statement that current cash resources are sufficient for at least 12 months was consistent with the preview’s expectation that liquidity language could soften and that management might give a runway figure.
Cohort 2’s biomarker direction was already reported in the preview as having replicated Cohort 1; the surprise was the greater consistency and longer persistence described on the call.

surprises.description: Cemetery/Mortuary earnings were much weaker on an operating basis than the preview’s clean-run-rate estimate implied: operating earnings fell 4.8%, while the segment’s 69.5% pretax-earnings increase depended on investment income rising 169.5% to $2 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pretax earnings up 69.5% to $3 million, though the earnings gains were driven by investment income that surged 169.5% to $2 million while operating earnings fell 4.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Excluding it, Q2 segment EBT is roughly $2.0M, about +14% YoY versus the headline +69.5%.”

surprises.description: Mortgage delinquencies deteriorated sharply: loans more than 90 days past due rose to $15.8 million from $6.5 million at year-end, a substantial increase the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mortgage loans more than 90 days past due jumped to $15.8 million as of June 30, 2026 from $6.5 million at year-end, a credit-quality trend management is monitoring closely.”

surprises.description: Life-segment investment income weakness was tied to specific sources: six-month net investment income fell 14%, mainly as homebuilder profit-share income declined $2.8 million and construction-lending income fell about $1.1 million. The preview raised lower investment income as a possible explanation for the life-segment pressure but did not identify these drivers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The life insurance segment's six-month net investment income dropped 14% to $33.4 million, driven mainly by a $2.8 million year-to-date decline in homebuilder profit-share income and roughly $1.1 million lower construction lending income.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Ask for the split between lower funeral-funding case counts, net investment income, and acquisition-cost strain from first-year premium growth.”

surprises.description: The company had increased land and residential-subdivision investments to about $122 million from $98 million at year-end, and said this suppresses current income because GAAP profits are recorded only when lots are sold or construction starts. This added a near-term income drag and a capital-allocation detail not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company deliberately grew its land and residential subdivision investment to approximately $122 million as of June 30 from about $98 million at year-end, suppressing current income since GAAP profits are recognized only upon lot sales or construction starts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capital allocation: any buyback in place of stock dividends.”

surprises.description: Mortgage origination volume was down 11% year over year, although it rose 12% sequentially and market share increased from 9 to 10 basis points. The preview called for mortgage-volume discussion but did not state an expected volume trajectory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mortgage origination volume fell 11% year-over-year to $548 million in Q2 (from $617 million) but rose 12% sequentially, lifting SNFC's industry market share to 10 basis points from 9.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Mortgage volume and gain-on-sale disclosure.”

surprises.description: Cash rose about 60%, or roughly $61 million, as lower loan production left funds earning below-market lending rates while management looked for deployment opportunities. The preview did not flag this idle-cash issue or the accompanying sharp decline in Utah home starts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents rose about 60% (roughly $61 million) since December 31, 2025 due to lower loan production, earning below-market lending rates as management seeks deployment opportunities amid a 40.6% decline in Utah new home starts.”

surprises.description: Management reported sizable cost reductions in commissions and personnel expense, which helped offset revenue declines: the two categories fell 13.5% in the quarter and 11.8% year to date. The preview discussed profitability and revenue pressure but did not identify these expense savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Combined commissions and personnel expense—the two largest cost categories—fell 13.5% ($4.8 million) for the quarter and 11.8% ($8 million) year-to-date, reflecting efficiency efforts.”

in_line: Mortgage remained at breakeven: Q2 pretax income was $71,000, matching the preview’s stated Q2 figure and its focus on whether breakeven held.

surprises.description: Ideal Power reported a long-term supply agreement with an automotive-qualified high-volume wafer foundry in Asia and functional first silicon—manufacturing milestones not identified in the preview. Management said the foundry supports targeted gross margins of 40% or more at scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Entered a long-term supply agreement with an automotive-qualified high-volume wafer foundry in Asia (not China)” and “achieved functional first silicon”; management believes it supports “targeted gross margins of 40%-plus at scale.”

surprises.description: The sales funnel expanded to over $400 million from about $300 million at the mid-May call, exceeding the preview’s reference point. Its mix was roughly evenly split between automotive and AI data center/industrial applications, rather than being described as about 50% automotive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's sales funnel grew to over $400 million in total revenue opportunity, up from about $300 million at its mid-May call, split roughly 50-50 between automotive and AI data center/industrial applications.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “Sales funnel” was “was $300M, about 50% automotive.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for automotive reliability or qualification testing “this summer,” but Ideal Power said it would begin industrial JEDEC qualification this quarter and prioritize that over automotive qualification. No automotive qualification schedule was given in the reported facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to begin industrial JEDEC qualification this quarter with completion in Q4 2026, prioritizing it over automotive qualification to align with nearer-term AI data center and energy revenue opportunities.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Automotive reliability/qualification testing: guided ‘this summer,’ the gate to any production design-in.”

surprises.description: For the U.S. hyperscaler opportunity, the preview identified conversion of the LOI into a named, definitive agreement as the key upgrade. The reported update was co-development of a prototype for customer evaluation, targeted for Q4, and did not report a named definitive agreement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is co-developing an intelligent SSCB prototype for evaluation by a U.S. hyperscaler for NVIDIA Rubin Ultra 800-volt DC data center systems, targeting delivery by end of Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Conversion to a named, definitive agreement is the key upgrade.”

surprises.description: The Asia lead-customer prototype remained on the preview’s Q4 2026 schedule, but Ideal Power also expected initial low-volume orders to support the prototype builds, an additional step not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “B-TRAN-enabled SSCB prototypes for the lead Asia customer's 800-volt AI data center and energy grid customers are expected in Q4 2026, along with initial low-volume orders to support prototype builds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Low-current SSCB prototype timing (Asia lead customer, Q4 2026).”

surprises.description: Despite Q2 cash burn matching the preview’s range, operating expenses rose to $3.6 million from $3.1 million and the net loss widened to $3.4 million from $3.0 million. The call attributed part of the expense increase to noncash patent impairments, a one-off item not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss widened to $3.4 million in Q2 2026 from $3.0 million in Q2 2025, while operating expenses rose to $3.6 million from $3.1 million, driven by higher stock comp, personnel costs, and noncash patent impairments.”

in_line: Q2 cash burn was $2.5 million, within the preview’s $2.5–$2.7 million guide.
FY2026 cash-burn guidance of $10.3–$10.5 million remained within the preview’s $10–$10.5 million range.
The Asia lead-customer SSCB prototype timing remained Q4 2026, as the preview anticipated.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $8.4 million, roughly 10% above the preview’s $7.56–$7.64 million consensus range and slightly above its $8.0–$8.3 million bull scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 19.2% year-over-year to approximately $8.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 Consensus” revenue: “$7.56M” or “$7.64M”; bull scenario revenue: “$8.0–8.3M.”

surprises.description: Direct Patient Services grew about 40%, well above the preview’s 20–28% base scenario and above the more than 30% growth it associated with the bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Direct Patient Services segment revenue jumped ~40% year-over-year to $4.9 million in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base scenario: “DPS growth 20–28%”; bull scenario: “DPS growth above 30%.”

surprises.description: Cash ended June at $6.8 million, exceeding the preview’s $4.5–$5.5 million base scenario and its roughly $6 million level described as extending the liquidity runway. The company also generated $4.4 million from operations in the first half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating activities generated $4.4 million of cash in the first six months,” and cash rose “over 80% to $6.8 million from $3.7 million at year-end 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “cash $4.5–5.5M”; the preview said “Cash above about $6M would extend the liquidity runway.”

surprises.description: The reported credit-loss allowance on Rhode Island receivables was a specific downside not called out in the preview; it was one of the main drivers of the reported net loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported net loss was driven largely by a $909,000 credit-loss allowance on Rhode Island receivables.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bear scenario mentioned “an impairment,” but did not identify a credit-loss allowance or Rhode Island receivables as a risk.

surprises.description: The call disclosed $285,000 of legal and professional costs tied to the credit-agreement amendment, an additional expense item not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$285,000 in legal/professional costs tied to the credit agreement amendment.”

surprises.description: Management said it expects to refinance rather than necessarily sell assets, a different framing from the preview’s focus on the mandated sale process. The call still indicated that the forbearance requires the company to pursue a sale, so the refinancing approach does not remove that requirement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The forbearance agreement reportedly requires the company to pursue a sale of all or part of ASHS's assets,” while management said it is “pursuing all options and expects to refinance rather than necessarily sell.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the agreement “requires the company to pursue a sale of all or part of its assets” and identified details on the “mandated asset-sale process” as a key issue.

surprises.description: The reported expected debt balance of about $13.3 million is below the roughly $17 million debt level cited in the preview, although the preview had already noted the new financing and forbearance agreement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Debt owed expected to fall from ~$15.5 million to ~$13.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described debt as “about $17M” and cited Q1 long-term debt of “$16.8M.”

surprises.description: AMS announced planned radiation-therapy and proton-beam centers in Rhode Island and a Gamma Knife upgrade partnership in Mexico. These new initiatives were not anticipated in the preview, which instead highlighted the need to clarify whether existing commitments would be funded, deferred, or cancelled.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company announced “planned radiation therapy and proton beam centers in Rhode Island” and “a Gamma Knife upgrade partnership with Hospital San Javier in Guadalajara, Mexico.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether the “$13.6M” of commitments would be “funded, deferred, or cancelled under the capex restrictions”; it did not mention these initiatives.

surprises.description: The call disclosed a recent transition to Interim CFO Alexis Wallace, which the preview did not flag. The facts provide no further detail about the transition or its implications.
surprises.fact_evidence: The call facts note “a recent CFO transition to Interim CFO Alexis Wallace.”

surprises.description: The Executive Chairman’s company also bought additional AMS shares from a private investor. The preview had disclosed the expected $2 million related-party financing, but did not mention this separate share purchase.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Executive Chairman’s newly formed company “purchased additional company shares from a private investor.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a “$2.0M note from RCS/TIG Holdings LLC” but did not mention a secondary share purchase.

in_line: The $2 million subordinated financing from an entity controlled by the Executive Chairman was already disclosed in the preview as a July 22 related-party note.

The forbearance agreement’s requirement to pursue a sale of all or part of the company’s assets was already flagged in the preview; the unexpected difference was management’s stated preference to refinance rather than necessarily sell.

surprises.description: Q3 sales of $5.6 million were above the preview’s modeled $5.2–$5.3 million range, but just missed its $5.65 million catalyst and the expected third consecutive sequential increase: sales edged down from $5.64 million in Q2. The top line therefore beat the modeled estimate while slightly breaking the sequential-growth narrative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales grew 20% year-over-year to $5.6 million in Q3 FY2026” and Q2 sales were $5.64 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Q3 sales of “~$5.2–5.3M,” called a third consecutive sequential increase “the core bull case,” and listed “Revenue at or above $5.65M” as a catalyst; it said anything below about $5.5M would damage the narrative.

surprises.description: Gross margin fell to 54.7%, materially below the preview’s 57% level to watch and well short of its 59%+ bull-case assumption. The preview anticipated ongoing mix pressure, but the reported contraction was worse than those thresholds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin contracted sharply to 54.7% from 61.5%,” driven by the wholesale mix shift, repacking labor, and a $187,000 increase in inventory reserves.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether margin “holds above 57%” and used “margin holds at 59%+” in its bull scenario.

surprises.description: Oasis showed a sharp acceleration in distributor activity, despite the preview highlighting Alabama restrictions as a headwind to the brand. July depletions reached a record and August was pacing even higher, alongside a major increase in Texas store access.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oasis THC brand distributor depletions hit a record in July, up 35% over the Q3 average, with August pacing to more than double, and a Texas distributor switch quadrupled store access.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Alabama’s restrictive law was a headwind to Oasis and identified the Oasis beverage line as the company’s designated growth engine.

surprises.description: Management announced a new cost-reduction program targeting $100,000–$150,000 in monthly cash savings, an initiative and quantified savings target not anticipated in the preview. The savings could help cash flow, though the need for payroll cuts and vendor exits also signals retrenchment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management launched a cost-reduction program targeting $100,000–$150,000 in monthly cash savings (about $1.2–$1.8 million annualized) via payroll cuts, warehouse lease renegotiation, and vendor exits.”

surprises.description: A Senate proposal could temporarily exempt cannabinoids through December 11, 2026, offering a possible short-term reprieve from Section 781’s scheduled November 12 effective date. The proposal is temporary and not described as enacted, so it does not remove the underlying regulatory risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Section 781 … is scheduled to take effect November 12, 2026, though a Senate proposal could temporarily exempt cannabinoids through December 11, 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Section 781 as effective November 12, 2026, and emphasized its potential material impact; it did not mention a temporary exemption proposal.

in_line: Management’s cash-flow breakeven revenue estimate remained below $7 million per quarter: the reported low-to-mid $6 million range was consistent with the preview’s expectation that breakeven was “well below $7 million.”

surprises.description: Q4 organic sales grew about 10%, well above the preview’s 4.0%–5.5% company-guidance range and its roughly 5% base case. June growth also held above 10% despite tougher comparisons, rather than weakening as the preview’s bear scenario warned.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 organic sales grew 10% (9.7%), the strongest in more than 3 years and up from 6% last quarter, with June organic sales up over 10% year-over-year despite tougher comparisons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Organic daily sales … +4.0% to +5.5%”; the base scenario expected “organic ~+5%,” while the bear scenario cited “Softer June against the hard comparison.”

surprises.description: Q4 EBITDA margin reached 13.1%, above the preview’s expected 12.6%–12.8% range, despite LIFO and moderating-pricing concerns. The 64-basis-point expansion and reported incremental margins above 19% were stronger than the preview’s anticipated margin step-up from mix and initiatives.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported EBITDA rose 16.1% and EBITDA margin expanded 64 basis points to 13.1%, exceeding guidance of 12.6%-12.8%, driven by incremental margins over 19% (22%+ excluding LIFO).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EBITDA margin vs. the 12.6–12.8% guide”; the preview’s bull case expected “EBITDA margin ≥12.8%.”

surprises.description: Q4 EPS was $3.17, beating the $2.92 consensus and exceeding the $2.85–$2.96 guidance range. That was a substantially larger beat than the preview’s base case of $2.92–$2.96.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 EPS reached a record $3.17, up 13.2% from $2.80 a year ago, despite higher LIFO expense, tax rate, and net interest expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | $2.92”; company guidance was “$2.85 – $2.96,” and the base scenario expected “$2.92–$2.96.”

surprises.description: The FY27 EPS guide midpoint is about $11.90, above the preview’s roughly $11.69 consensus and its base-case midpoint near $11.70. The low end is slightly below consensus, but the high end is $12.15, above the preview’s bull-case threshold of $11.85.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for EPS of $11.65-$12.15 on sales growth of 4%-6.5% and EBITDA margins of 12.5%-12.8%, excluding contributions from future acquisitions or buybacks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 EPS | ~$11.69”; the base scenario expected “$11.30–$12.10 (midpoint near $11.70),” and the bull case cited “FY27 guide midpoint ≥$11.85.”

surprises.description: Engineered Solutions organic growth was 12.9%, materially above the preview’s 7.1% embedded sales-growth expectation. Automation was especially strong, while flow control lagged because of softer process-market MRO activity—a weakness the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Engineered Solutions led with 12.9% organic growth, including automation organic sales up over 20% (strongest in 4 years), while flow control lagged due to softer process-market MRO activity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus embeds +7.1% Q4 Engineered Solutions sales growth.”

surprises.description: The preview expected continued double-digit Engineered Solutions order growth, but the reported July orders were up in the mid-20s percent; Q1 organic sales guidance was 6%–8%, with quarter-to-date trends around 7%. These indicators were stronger than the preview’s unspecified July-trend watchpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 organic sales are projected to grow 6%-8% year-over-year, with quarter-to-date trending at approximately 7% and July orders in Engineered Solutions up in the mid-20s percent.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Engineered Solutions orders” and “M&A and July trends” as key items to watch, and said “A third straight quarter of double-digit organic order growth” would support FY27 numbers; it did not specify an expected July growth rate.

surprises.description: Service Center organic sales growth accelerated to 7.9% from 4% last quarter, alongside double-digit EBITDA growth and a 91-basis-point margin expansion. The preview did not set a segment-specific expectation for this acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Service Center segment organic sales accelerated to 7.9% growth from 4% last quarter, with EBITDA up 16.3% and margin expanding 91 basis points to 14.5%.”

surprises.description: Management raised its five-year sales and margin objectives, lifting the sales target to $7 billion from $5.5 billion and the EBITDA margin target to 14% from 13%. The preview did not anticipate a change to these longer-term targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its 5-year intermediate targets, lifting the sales objective to $7 billion from $5.5 billion and the EBITDA margin objective to 14% from 13%.”

surprises.description: The company reported $461 million of FY26 free cash flow, net leverage of just 0.2x EBITDA, and nearly $2 billion of deployment capacity. The preview discussed capital deployment and possible M&A, but did not anticipate or quantify this balance-sheet capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company generated $461 million of free cash flow in fiscal 2026, ended with net leverage of just 0.2x EBITDA and nearly $2 billion of deployment capacity, deploying ~$425 million across buybacks, dividends, CapEx and M&A.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Over $300M deployed year to date” and said the next 12–18 months “should be a more active M&A period”; it did not give an expectation for leverage or deployment capacity.

in_line: LIFO remained a margin headwind, as the preview anticipated; the preview specifically noted slightly higher Q4 LIFO expense and identified LIFO as a source of margin pressure.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $670.5 million, $23.4 million above the preview’s $647.1 million consensus and above its $655–665 million base-case range. That is a clear beat against the preview’s low revenue bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 13.7% year-over-year to approximately $670.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $647.1M” consensus; the preview’s base scenario was “$655–665M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $95.4 million, above the preview’s derived $86–89 million estimate and its $89–92 million base case. The reported 8% year-over-year increase was within the preview’s anticipated headline range, but the dollar result was higher than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA increased 8% year-over-year to $95.4 million,” with the prior-year period including “roughly $9 million of non-recurring favorable items in the PDS division.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My derived estimate of about $86–89M”; the base scenario was “$89–92M.” The preview also said headline growth “may look flat to +8%.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year guidance well beyond the preview’s expected modest increase: revenue is now greater than $2.68 billion and adjusted EBITDA greater than $365 million. The preview expected $338–342 million of EBITDA guidance previously and described a move to roughly $342–346 million as the likely or base-case outcome; the actual raise was attributed to core organic performance, not just Family First.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue greater than $2.68 billion and adjusted EBITDA greater than $365 million, driven by core organic performance rather than the already-contemplated Family First acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Company guidance was “$2.63–$2.65B” revenue and “$338–$342M” adjusted EBITDA; the preview’s base case expected guidance “nudged to $342–346M.”

surprises.description: Aveanna raised its long-term organic growth targets for both private duty services and home health & hospice, rather than merely delivering against the existing targets. The preview did not anticipate these target increases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its long-term organic growth targets, increasing private duty services from 3-5% to 5-6% and home health & hospice from 5-7% to 8-10%, while keeping medical solutions at 8-10%.”

surprises.description: PDS spread per hour was $12.88, above the preview’s $12.38 comparison and its expectation that the spread hold at $12.30 or higher. This came despite cost of revenue per hour rising faster than revenue per hour, and counters the preview’s concern about PDS margin pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PDS Q2 gross margin was 28.9% with revenue per hour up 1.7% to $44.62, cost of revenue per hour up 7.8% to $31.74, and spread per hour of $12.88 reflecting wage normalization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said holding spread per hour at “$12.30 or higher” would offset the PDS margin concern, and its catalyst checklist compared results with “$12.38” and management’s “low $12s” range.

surprises.description: Preferred payer agreements were already at 37 of the 38 target, far ahead of the preview’s reference point of 30 agreements and expectation that the company would exceed eight new agreements by year-end. Preferred payers also represented a larger share of PDS MCO volumes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PDS preferred payer agreements reached 37 of a 38 target, with preferred payers now representing approximately 64% of PDS MCO volumes, up from 60% at the end of Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “PDS is at 30 with a target of 38 by year-end” and that management “expects to exceed eight new agreements.”

surprises.description: Home health episodic mix reached about 81%, above the company’s 75% goal, while episodic volume grew 18.5% year over year. The preview noted Q1 mix of 80% but did not flag that the 75% goal would be exceeded.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Home health episodic mix reached approximately 81% (above the 75% goal) with episodic volume growth of 18.5% year-over-year and Medicare revenue per episode of $3,202.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported Q1 home health & hospice at “80% episodic mix.”

surprises.description: California’s 2027 budget included a significant pediatric private duty nursing rate increase effective January 1, 2027, a favorable policy development the preview did not mention.
surprises.fact_evidence: “California's 2027 budget includes a significant pediatric private duty nursing rate increase effective January 1, 2027, the state's first rate increase in roughly nine years after four years of advocacy.”

surprises.description: The company’s credit ratings were upgraded by all three major agencies and its term loan was repriced 75 basis points lower, reducing annual interest expense by about $10 million. The preview highlighted leverage and post-acquisition cash concerns but did not anticipate these financing improvements.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received credit rating upgrades from all three major agencies and repriced its term loan 75 basis points lower, cutting annual interest expense by approximately $10 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “Cash and leverage after Family First,” noting that the acquisition “raises net debt” and leverage was “3.8x against a target below 3.0x.”

surprises.description: Cash generation was stronger than the preview’s post-acquisition cash concerns suggested: year-to-date free cash flow was positive $75.4 million, with a similar amount expected in the second half. Management also said sub-three-times leverage is expected to be achievable in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date free cash flow was positive $75.4 million with similar expected in the second half, and management reaffirmed its target of reaching sub-three-times leverage, expected achievable in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q1 free cash flow of “-$3.8M,” FY guidance of “about $131M,” and leverage of “3.8x” after the Family First outlay.

in_line: The reported 8% year-over-year adjusted EBITDA growth was within the preview’s stated possible headline range of flat to +8%; the preview also expected roughly 20% or more underlying growth after accounting for prior-year timing benefits.

surprises.description: Applied guided Q4 revenue of $10.25B, above the preview’s roughly $9.3–9.4B consensus and $10.0B whisper. The guide is also near the preview’s $10.3–10.5B bull range, rather than its $9.6–9.9B base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 guidance calls for revenue of $10.25 billion” and non-GAAP EPS of “$4.02.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus ~$9.3–9.4B”; “Treat ~$10.0B as the whisper line for the Q4 guide.”

surprises.description: Management raised its Semiconductor Systems growth outlook above the prior greater-than-30% forecast for calendar 2026 and expects to gain share. That is more constructive than the preview’s warning that an in-line outlook could signal relative share loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its Semiconductor Systems growth outlook to above the prior ‘greater than 30%’ guidance for calendar 2026 and expects to gain market share during the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “An in-line guide would read as a disappointment”; “an in-line AMAT guide reads as relative share loss.”

surprises.description: The calendar-2026 advanced-packaging outlook rose to more than 70% growth, above the preview’s expectation of more than 50%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Advanced packaging revenue is now expected to grow more than 70% in calendar 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Advanced packaging. Guided to grow more than 50% in CY2026.”

surprises.description: Q3 non-GAAP EPS was $3.50, above the preview’s $3.36–$3.42 consensus range, though at the top of its bull-case range rather than far beyond it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 non-GAAP EPS reached a record $3.50.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS … Consensus ~$3.36–3.42”; bull scenario: “$3.58–3.70,” base scenario: “$3.42–3.50.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was a modest beat: $9.1B versus approximately $9.0B expected, with 25% year-over-year growth versus the preview’s 23% estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $9.1 billion,” up “25% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus ~$9.00B” and “+23%” year-over-year.

surprises.description: China revenue is now expected to grow both this year and next, a more favorable outlook than the preview’s flat-to-slightly-higher calendar-year expectation. The preview had not anticipated the added next-year growth outlook or the specific 28-nanometer investment driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China represented 26% of semiconductor systems plus AGS revenue,” and management “now expects China revenue to grow this year and next, led by 28-nanometer foundry logic investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CFO Brice Hill guided China and global ICAPS to flat-to-slightly-higher for the calendar year.”

surprises.description: AGS delivered $1.8B of Q3 revenue, above the preview’s approximately $1.75B estimate. Its 22% year-over-year growth was also accompanied by a new calendar-2026 outlook of more than 20% growth and a sustainable long-term mid-teens rate, for which the preview gave no comparable forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Applied Global Services grew 22% year-over-year to a record $1.8 billion” and is “now expected to grow more than 20% in calendar 2026, with a sustainable long-term mid-teens growth rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Applied Global Services … Consensus ~$1.75B.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a greater-than-50% calendar-2026 growth outlook for process diagnostics and control, a business outlook the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The process diagnostics and control business is expected to grow more than 50%.”

surprises.description: DRAM, including HBM packaging, reached record revenue after growing 52% year over year, and management expects a very significant second-half-weighted increase as customers add clean-room capacity. The preview did not identify this specific growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DRAM revenue (including HBM packaging) grew 52% year-over-year to record levels,” with “a very significant second-half-weighted increase” expected as customers expand clean-room capacity.

surprises.description: Applied said it expects to double quarterly system-output capacity from current levels by 2028, alongside substantial recent hiring and manufacturing-space expansion. The preview did not flag this capacity plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects to double its quarterly system output capacity from current levels by 2028,” after adding “over 1,500 manufacturing and support staff in Q3” and nearly doubling manufacturing space in recent years.

in_line: Q3 non-GAAP operating margin reached a record 34%, in line with the preview’s derived expectation of roughly 33–34%.
Q4 gross margin guidance of about 50.4% is broadly consistent with the preview’s roughly 50% baseline, though it does not reach the preview’s 51%+ bull-case assumption.

surprises.description: AudioEye reported Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $3.0 million, above the prior $2.6–$2.7 million guide. The beat was meaningful, though smaller than the preview’s bull-case requirement of at least $0.24 adjusted EPS, for which no actual Q2 EPS was provided.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached a record $3 million (28% margin), up 54% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA | $2.6M – $2.7M.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance from at least $12 million to at least $12.7 million, raised adjusted EPS guidance from at least $0.96 to at least $0.98, and now expects over $15 million of run-rate adjusted EBITDA by Q4. That improves on the preview’s expected reaffirmation of the $12 million floor and $15 million run-rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance from at least $12 million to at least $12.7 million”; “over $15 million run-rate adjusted EBITDA by Q4 2026”; “adjusted EPS guidance of at least $0.98.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA: at least $12M”; “Adjusted EPS: at least $0.96”; “Exit-2026 adjusted EBITDA run-rate: $15M”; and “Reaffirmation of at least $12M FY adjusted EBITDA and the $15M exit run-rate.”

surprises.description: The partner and marketplace channel grew 16% year over year and accounted for 59% of ARR, a strong channel result the preview did not forecast because it said the segment split was not covered.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The partner and marketplace channel grew 16% year-over-year and now represents 59% of ARR.”

surprises.description: Enterprise revenue was flat year over year, with ARR growth of only 5%, as revenue shifted from nonrecurring to recurring. The preview identified enterprise ARR reacceleration as a bull-case driver, but did not provide a base-case segment forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enterprise revenue was flat year-over-year (5% ARR growth) due to a shift from nonrecurring to recurring revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bull: ... Enterprise ARR re-accelerates.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted free cash flow was $2.6 million, an additional positive cash-generation result not addressed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 generated $2.6 million of adjusted free cash flow.”

surprises.description: AudioEye said it is evaluating buybacks, dividends, and M&A for excess cash. The preview did not anticipate discussion of these possible uses, and management described options under evaluation rather than a committed action.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is evaluating deployment of excess cash including potential share buybacks, dividends, and M&A.”

surprises.description: R&D spending fell to 12% of revenue from 17% a year earlier, which management attributed to AI-driven headcount efficiencies; the preview did not anticipate this operating-efficiency update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D spend fell to 12% of revenue from 17% a year earlier due to AI-driven headcount efficiencies.”

surprises.description: Europe made its strongest contribution to ARR growth to date amid early enforcement of the European Accessibility Act, an unexpected geographic demand detail not covered in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 marked the strongest EU contribution to ARR growth to date amid early European Accessibility Act enforcement.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $10.7 million was in line with the preview’s consensus estimate of about $10.71–$10.73 million and within company guidance of $10.65–$10.75 million.

ARR ended at $42.3 million, within the preview’s estimated $42.3–$42.5 million range. The $1.1 million sequential increase was below the preview’s $1.5 million bull-case threshold but above its stated bear-case threshold of less than $1.0 million.
Q3 revenue guidance of $10.85–$11.05 million was around the preview’s roughly $11.0 million reference point, though it did not reach the $11.1 million level described as validating the ramp.
Full-year revenue guidance was tightened to $43.5–$44 million while maintaining the midpoint, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the existing full-year outlook could be reaffirmed.
Litigation expenses were down 40% from Q1 and are expected to continue declining in H2, consistent with the preview’s expectation that legal costs would fall substantially after the trial.

surprises.description: HeartBeam submitted an FDA 510(k) pre-submission for heart-attack detection on the call date, with an FDA response expected within 75 days and a pivotal trial potentially starting before year-end 2026. The preview described MI detection as a major expansion but did not anticipate this near-term regulatory step or timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HeartBeam submitted a 510(k) pre-submission to the FDA for heart attack (MI) detection on the day of the call,” triggering a “75-day FDA response window,” with a pivotal trial “potentially starting before year-end 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The current FDA clearance covers only non-life-threatening arrhythmias. Heart-attack detection would be a large expansion.”

surprises.description: The ALIGN-ACS pilot enrolled 134 chest-pain patients, exceeding the preview's expected completed enrollment of 120. The preview said analysis was underway but did not anticipate acceptance of the results for a full TCT presentation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ALIGN-ACS pilot study completed enrollment of 134 chest-pain patients in under 4 months and its results were accepted for full presentation at the TCT conference in October/November 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Enrollment of 120 chest-pain patients finished ahead of schedule on June 30, and analysis is underway.”

surprises.description: The Indonesia-based HEADSTART-ACS study passed 50% enrollment in under three months, alongside a roughly 50-patient patch pilot. The preview did not identify this study's rapid enrollment or these Indonesia-related developments as expected milestones.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Indonesian government-supported HEADSTART-ACS 500-patient study surpassed 50% enrollment in under 3 months,” alongside a “~50-patient patch pilot study.”

surprises.description: HeartBeam disclosed two new patents for acoustic heart-valve sensing and impedance-based fluid monitoring for congestive heart failure, extending its technology beyond the tri-core ECG platform described in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “holds 25 issued patents worldwide” for its tri-core technology and “recently added two new patents for acoustic sensing (heart valve monitoring) and impedance-based fluid monitoring for congestive heart failure.”

surprises.description: The company gave a specific breakeven estimate—roughly 30,000 patients, or fewer with the reduced cost profile—and identified a concierge target market of about 1.9 million across four U.S. geographies. The preview expected more strategy detail but did not provide these patient targets or geographic focus.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management estimated it needs “roughly 30,000 patients (or fewer given the reduced cost profile) to reach cash-flow breakeven,” targeting “approximately 1.9 million patients across four U.S. geographies.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The company “said it would give more detail on strategy on the Q2 call.”

surprises.description: HeartBeam disclosed a 12-lead patch prototype aimed at a stated $2 billion patch market, a product and market target not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 12-lead patch prototype targets a $2 billion patch market.”

surprises.description: Executives and employees chose shares rather than cash for the 2025 bonus program, reducing operating cash outflow by more than $1 million. The preview focused on cost reductions and runway but did not anticipate this specific cash-preservation measure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Executives and employees elected to take shares instead of cash for the 2025 bonus program, reducing operating cash outflow by over $1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the company had promised a “meaningfully lower cost structure” but “gave no numbers.”

in_line: Cash and runway were broadly in line with the preview: cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash were $8.8 million at June 30, close to the preview's base estimate of $9.0 million, and the company said the April raise extended runway further into 2027, as the preview's base case anticipated.

The operating cash-flow outlook met the preview's key cost target: Q2 operating cash use was $3.3 million, and management said baseline Q4 operating cash flow should be below $2.5 million per quarter. The preview specifically identified a target below about $2.5 million per quarter as important; management cautioned that starting the MI pivotal study could raise spending above that level.

The reported $5 million Q2 net loss included one-time leadership-transition costs, while management gave an underlying loss estimate of about $4.1 million. The preview had flagged a restructuring charge as a possible factor that could inflate the loss and warned that the stale EPS consensus was noisy.

surprises.description: Q1 revenue was $30.6 million, about 19% above the preview’s $25.67 million consensus estimate. The beat was driven mainly by newly acquired advertising, technology, and media-services revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 total revenues rose 175% year-over-year to $30.6 million” and were driven primarily by “a $19.4 million increase from newly acquired advertising, technology, and media services revenue streams.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 revenue” consensus: “$25.67M.”

surprises.description: The reported $19.4 million increase from newly acquired revenue streams was above the preview’s roughly $13 million full-quarter marker for adtech and media services, indicating a larger contribution than the preview’s key threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: Revenue was driven primarily by “a $19.4 million increase from newly acquired advertising, technology, and media services revenue streams.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A full quarter at or above ~$13M” in adtech and media-services revenue was the key marker.

surprises.description: Direct operating margin fell to 35%, below the preview’s roughly 38% watch level and 40% catalyst threshold. The call attributed the decline to the new ad-tech stream’s high partner revenue share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Direct operating margin fell to 35% from 57%,” largely because the new advertising technology revenue stream carried an “average 79% revenue-share expense paid to supply partners.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Below ~38%” would signal thinner contribution than modeled and listed “Direct operating margin of 40% or more” as a catalyst.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was positive for a second consecutive quarter, rather than merely carrying the risk of a negative Q1 raised in the preview. It reached $0.5 million despite only one new theatrical release across the two quarters.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $0.5 million, up $2.6 million year-over-year, marking the company's second consecutive positive quarter despite having only one new theatrical release across those two quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview framed Q1 against the “Q1-is-the-trough” debate and noted: “If Q1 prints negative, reaching the $10M low end of the FY27 band requires substantial gains in Q2–Q4.”

surprises.description: Working capital was more negative than the preview’s cited $12.2 million deficit, at negative $18.9 million. The increase includes a larger deferred-consideration balance payable in equity, so it does not all represent a new cash payment burden.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Liquidity remains tight” with “negative $18.9 million net working capital,” including “$18 million of deferred consideration payable in equity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Working capital is -$12.2M, though $12.2M of that is IndiCue deferred consideration settleable in equity.”

surprises.description: Management said technology now accounts for more than 60% of consolidated revenue and is the company’s largest, most recurring revenue source—a pronounced mix shift not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Technology now represents more than 60% of consolidated revenue, positioning it as the company's largest and most recurring revenue source.”

surprises.description: Management introduced a year-end target for its new CTV-focused “audio” ad-tech product: roughly $12 million in annual run rate. The preview did not discuss this product or provide a comparable expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: The new “‘audio’ ad-tech product targeting CTV is guided to a roughly $12 million annual run rate by fiscal year-end,” with an addressable pool of 5%-7% of $3 billion in annual podcast ad spend.

surprises.description: The call reported record streaming engagement and audience metrics, including 4.5 billion minutes watched and 122.8 million viewers; the preview had not flagged streaming metrics or set expectations for them.
surprises.fact_evidence: Streaming hit “a record 4.5 billion minutes (up 33%), 122.8 million viewers (up 12%), and 1.52 million SVOD subscribers (up 12%).”

surprises.description: Management outlined three upcoming theatrical releases with low stated production costs and box-office breakevens, a risk-contained slate detail not covered in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The three releases—Pan's Labyrinth, Air Bud, and Wolf Creek—“each carry under-$5 million all-in costs with sub-$10 million box office breakevens.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed FY2027 revenue guidance of $115 million to $120 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $10 million to $20 million, as the preview’s base scenario anticipated.

Management expected the remaining $5.5 million of cost reductions to be materially complete by September 30, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the remaining cuts were due by the end of Q2 FY2027.

surprises.description: Cibus reported Q2 revenue of about $1 million versus preview consensus of $1.70 million, a substantial shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue of approximately $1 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 2026E | $1.70M”

surprises.description: Q2 GAAP loss per share was $0.29, worse than both preview estimates of $0.26 and $0.19 per share in losses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed to $22.1 million ($0.29 per share)”

surprises.description: The cash runway moved from the prior guidance of funding operations into late Q1 2027 to only early Q1 2027, bringing potential financing needs closer.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and cash equivalents were $20.4 million as of June 30, 2026, projected to fund operations only into early Q1 2027”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Runway language: cash funds operations ‘into late in the first quarter of 2027’”; the preview also said to check for cash “near $21M.”

surprises.description: Cibus pushed the Latin American rice commercial launch from late 2027 to 2028, later than the preview’s 2027 target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management delayed rice commercial launch guidance in Latin America from late 2027 to 2028”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Ecuador/Colombia launch is targeted for 2027.”

surprises.description: Management’s year-end net cash usage run-rate target is about $35 million, above the prior roughly $30 million per-year burn target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “targeting a net cash usage run rate of about $35 million exiting 2026”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company burn target: about $30M per year.”

surprises.description: Cash usage fell materially from the prior quarter and year, a more favorable trend than the preview’s warning that use above $10 million would call the burn target into question. The call facts do not give an absolute quarterly cash-use figure to compare directly with the preview’s $8 million and $10 million thresholds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Quarterly cash usage fell approximately 19% sequentially and 31% year-over-year”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating cash use at or below $8M would be on plan. Above $10M would call the target into question”

surprises.description: The Interoc framework expanded from two rice traits to five, an unanticipated broadening of the collaboration. However, the companies were still working toward a definitive commercial agreement rather than reporting one signed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cibus expanded its Interoc framework from two rice traits to five in August, shifting toward a multi-trait pipeline model as it works toward a definitive commercial agreement”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The January LOI is non-binding”; “A signed definitive agreement would be the most important non-financial catalyst.”

surprises.description: The call highlighted a $9.5 million non-cash royalty-liability interest expense as the main reason net loss exceeded operating loss; the preview did not flag this material earnings driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A large non-cash royalty liability interest expense of $9.5 million (up from $8.7 million) remains the primary driver of the gap between operating loss and net loss.”

surprises.description: Management cited newly favorable regulatory developments across multiple markets, including finalized EU rules for most non-GMO edited crops and favorable determinations in several countries and by U.S. agencies; these developments were not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The EU finalized rules in June treating most non-GMO edited crops as conventional, while Ecuador, Peru, USDA APHIS, and the FDA granted favorable determinations across three continents.”

in_line: Cash was $20.4 million versus the preview’s approximate $21 million estimate.
The U.S. rice launch remains targeted for 2029, as the preview expected, and remains tied to the partner’s herbicide registration.
The rice royalty opportunity remains broadly consistent with the preview’s stated $200 million annual opportunity across 5–7 million acres.

The preview expected biofragrance scale-up orders in 2H26 and cited a $20–40 million annual opportunity; the call continued to expect additional scale-up orders in the second half and gave the same opportunity range.

surprises.description: The preview looked for early Flora Sync LF5 sell-through evidence, including units and repeat rates, but the call only said sales began in July and reported no Q2 revenue from the product. That left the first evidence of post-launch demand unquantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 results include no revenue from it since sales began in July.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Flora Sync LF5 early sell-through. Units, average order value, repeat rate, and CAC would be the first hard evidence of direct-to-consumer commercialization. Qualitative-only commentary is a mild negative.”

surprises.description: Daré had initiated the DARE-HPV Phase II study in roughly 100 women with ARPA-H funding, an advancement not identified in the preview’s list of expected catalysts. Top-line results are expected in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The DARE-HPV Phase II study (~100 women) was initiated with ARPA-H funding,” with top-line results expected in 2027.

surprises.description: Daré secured another $1 million NIAID tranche for the DARE-HPV project, bringing total project funding to $2 million. The preview discussed financing capacity and grant-funded programs but did not anticipate this additional award.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company secured a second $1 million NIAID tranche bringing total project funding to $2 million.”

surprises.description: The call outlined a 2027 commercial-availability target for DARE to RECLAIM through 503B compounding, adding a prospective product and revenue stream that the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DARE to RECLAIM estradiol/progesterone intravaginal ring for menopause is targeted for commercial availability via 503B compounding beginning in 2027,” positioning Daré for a multiproduct revenue profile across 2026–2027.

in_line: Revenue was approximately $0.2 million, within the preview’s expected $0.15–$0.25 million range; the preview had already warned that Q2 product revenue would likely be minimal because Flora Sync sales began after quarter-end.
Net loss was approximately $3 million, consistent with the preview’s base-case EPS range of -$0.20 to -$0.25 and the prior quarter’s $3 million net loss.
DARE to PLAY dispensing remained targeted for Q3 2026, consistent with the preview’s summer 2026 guidance; the call did not report that dispensing had already begun.

Ovaprene continued toward 2026 enrollment, and the call reported a positive DSMB interim review recommending continuation without modification, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of continued trial progress following the earlier positive DSMB review.

surprises.description: The FDA advisory committee voted 9–3 against finding substantial evidence that deramocel is effective for DMD cardiomyopathy. The preview noted the panel had voted on cardiomyopathy effectiveness but did not give the vote result.
surprises.fact_evidence: The committee “voted 9 against and only 3 in favor” on whether deramocel showed substantial evidence of effectiveness for cardiomyopathy in DMD patients.

surprises.description: Rather than proceeding on the preview’s anticipated August 22 PDUFA timeline alone, Capricor plans an amendment seeking a refined indication focused on upper-limb skeletal muscle function; the FDA has agreed to extend the target date once it receives the amendment.
surprises.fact_evidence: Capricor plans to submit an amendment with 24-month HOPE-3 open-label extension data to pursue an indication focused on upper-limb skeletal muscle function. The BLA remains under review, and the FDA agreed to extend the August 22 target date upon receiving the planned amendment.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The PDUFA date for deramiocel is Aug 22, nine days after the call.”

surprises.description: The all-patient left-ventricular ejection-fraction result was weaker in the published analysis than at top line, losing conventional statistical significance. The preview did not discuss this endpoint result.
surprises.fact_evidence: A statistical model correction changed the all-patient LV ejection-fraction difference from 2.4 points (p=0.04) at top line to 1.8 points (p=0.09) in The Lancet; lower endpoints in the hierarchy are now only nominally significant.

surprises.description: HOPE-3’s upper-limb primary endpoint showed a statistically significant benefit, a positive trial result the preview did not identify as an expected outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: PUL 2.0 showed a 4.55% mean difference favoring deramocel (p=0.029), which the company said remained unaffected by the other revisions.

surprises.description: The quarterly loss was worse than the preview’s EPS consensus range, despite the preview’s estimate-quality caveat.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 net loss was approximately $40.7 million, or $0.70 per share, with operating expenses of $42.9 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS $(0.58) – $(0.59)” (the preview’s own estimate was $(0.60)).

surprises.description: Capricor withdrew its preliminary-injunction motion against NS Pharma and will pursue rescission through arbitration expected this fall, rather than reporting an injunction ruling, settlement, or rights reversion.
surprises.fact_evidence: Capricor “withdrew its preliminary injunction motion” and will pursue rescission of the U.S. distribution agreement through arbitration expected to begin this fall.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a “settlement, injunction ruling, or reversion of U.S. rights” as a standalone catalyst and asked investors to watch for hearing dates or settlement posture.

surprises.description: Capricor put all non-deramocel pipeline work on hold, a portfolio-wide pause the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “All non-deramocel pipeline work is on hold.”

surprises.description: The company is slowing commercial-readiness spending and pacing capital deployment until it has more regulatory clarity. The preview had identified a possible spending pause, so this was a flagged risk, but the reported slowdown confirms that risk rather than describing continued readiness spending.
surprises.fact_evidence: Capricor is “slowing commercial readiness spending and pacing capital deployment” pending greater regulatory clarity; second-floor manufacturing expansion validation is targeted for 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any pause or ‘prudent sequencing’ language would signal the company is bracing for a CRL.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $0, consistent with the preview’s $0 estimate and its note that Q1 revenue was also $0.
Cash and marketable securities of approximately $237.9 million were within the preview’s base-case range of roughly $235–248 million and close to its approximately $240 million estimate.

surprises.description: Revenue was $3.9 million, well below the preview’s published $4.79 million aggregator estimate, though it matched the preview’s more realistic $3.90–$4.00 million base case. The preview warned that the aggregator figure was stale and should be treated only as a reference point.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue was $3.9 million for Q3 fiscal 2026,” up marginally from $3.8 million a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Published consensus: “~$4.79M” (described as a “single stale model” and “reference”); Base scenario: “$3.90–4.00M.”

surprises.description: New ARR was sharply lower than the prior quarter’s $875,000 and the preview’s bull-case expectation of more than $1 million. This was so despite 19 subscription contracts, the same contract count as Q2, and a record-tying nine new customer wins.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company closed “19 subscription contracts worth $1.7 million in total contract value and over $370,000 in annual recurring revenue,” including “9 new customer wins” and “10 existing customer expansions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “New ARR versus the $875K comparison,” said the bull case required “new ARR above $1.0M,” and noted that “a sequential decline after ‘best quarter ever’ would reframe Q2 as a pull-forward.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was negative rather than positive or around breakeven, missing the preview’s preferred outcome. Management also said it would prioritize growth investment over bottom-line profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA was “negative $102,000,” versus negative $330,000 a year earlier; management is “prioritizing growth investment over bottom-line profitability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Adjusted EBITDA stays positive” as a catalyst and gave the base case as “about breakeven.”

surprises.description: The preview said management’s goal was for Core/HawkSearch to exceed 70% of overall revenue this year, but the reported share was 62%; management now projects it will exceed 70% next year. That points to the mix milestone arriving later than the preview expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: Core product revenue was “62% of total revenue”; management projects core revenue will exceed 70% of total revenue “next year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had said Core/HawkSearch would reach “over 70% of overall revenue this year”; it was 61% of total revenue in Q2.

surprises.description: Despite the weak quarterly EBITDA result, management gave a more reassuring runway outlook than the preview’s financing-focused discussion suggested: it expects roughly cash-neutral operations in FY2027 and says it has more than a year of cash on hand.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management guided to “roughly cash-neutral operations in fiscal 2027” and said the company was maintaining “more than a year of cash on hand”; quarter-end cash was $1.5 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted the financing question around “$1.4M of cash,” the ATM, and whether another negative EBITDA quarter would bring that question back quickly.

surprises.description: Management disclosed a substantial reduction in quarterly advertising spend, from roughly $500,000 to about $350,000, and expects to maintain that level without significant cash burn—an unanticipated cost-control measure.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “reduced quarterly ad spend from roughly $500,000 to about $350,000” and expects to sustain that level “without significant cash burn.”

surprises.description: Management provided a positive FY2027 growth outlook that the preview had not found in the available guidance: it expects double-digit core growth to translate into double-digit overall revenue growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects “double-digit core CAGR to translate into double-digit overall revenue growth” next year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said there was “No quantitative guidance” on the prior call and flagged “any early FY27 framing” as something to watch.

surprises.description: HawkSearch received an unanticipated competitive endorsement, ranking first for the B2B search use case in Gartner’s 2026 Critical Capabilities report for a second consecutive year.
surprises.fact_evidence: HawkSearch was ranked “#1 for the B2B search use case in Gartner's 2026 Critical Capabilities report for the second consecutive year.”

in_line: Total revenue of $3.9 million was within the preview’s $3.90–$4.00 million base-case range, notwithstanding its much higher caveated aggregator estimate.
Core net revenue retention was 106%, close to the prior quarter’s 107% and above the preview’s below-105% bear-case trigger.

surprises.description: Despite the Q3 revenue shortfall, Genasys reported 12-month backlog of about $69 million, up from $58.2 million at the end of Q2, and said this supported its view that the shortfall reflected timing rather than weaker demand. The preview flagged CROWS timing but did not anticipate a backlog increase of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “12-month backlog grew to approximately $69 million from $58.2 million at the end of Q2,” supporting management's claim that the revenue shortfall was timing rather than demand-related.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CROWS II revenue timing. Confirmation of follow-on production orders would be the strongest bull signal.”

surprises.description: Software revenue grew 21% year over year and 12% sequentially to $2.7 million, with about $2.5 million of bookings in the quarter. The preview did not identify software growth or bookings as an expectation to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Software revenue rose 21% year-over-year and 12% sequentially to $2.7 million, with approximately $2.5 million in software bookings during the quarter.”

surprises.description: A California utility's LRAD 950NXT orders reached $4.4 million this fiscal year, including a recent $2.4 million order, versus about $1 million the prior year. The preview did not anticipate this customer order or the reported expansion in the critical-infrastructure business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A single California utility ordered $4.4 million of LRAD 950NXT critical infrastructure systems this fiscal year (including a recent $2.4 million order), up from about $1 million the prior year.”

surprises.description: Cash, equivalents and marketable securities were $3.1 million at quarter-end, while the preview highlighted a $4.0 million minimum-liquidity requirement. The company extended its term-loan maturity to July 2027; the supplied facts do not say whether it was in compliance with the liquidity covenant.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash, equivalents and marketable securities fell to $3.1 million as of June 30, 2026, down from $8 million at September 30, 2025, prompting a term loan maturity extension to July 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “June 30 cash and covenant compliance. The July 13 loan amendment requires $4.0M minimum liquidity.”

surprises.description: The call reported that Genasys Protect covered about 15% of the U.S. population and 20% of its land area, a deployment-scale update the preview did not identify as an expected result or key debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Genasys Protect now covers approximately 15% of the U.S. population and 20% of the country's land area.”

in_line: Q3 revenue was $7.3 million, within the preview's $7.0 million–$7.5 million guidance range; the decline from the prior year was already anticipated.
Q3 gross margin was 57.1%, within the preview's 55%–58% range.
Adjusted EBITDA loss was $3.1 million, within the preview's expected $3.0 million–$3.3 million loss.

Puerto Rico collections resumed after quarter-end, with about $2.9 million collected over four weeks—consistent with the preview's base scenario of partial collections, though the preview gave no expected dollar amount.

Management reaffirmed a record year in revenue and profitability, in line with the preview's record-year guidance. The supplied facts do not specify whether the profitability claim was reaffirmed on a GAAP basis.
The preview anticipated that Q4 guidance might remain qualitative, and the supplied facts report no explicit Q4 revenue figure.

surprises.description: Celcuity set REVTORPYK’s price at $30,000 per treatment cycle, above the preview’s modeled $26,000–$28,000 per month. That is a higher disclosed price than the Street model anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “priced REVTORPYK at a WAC of $10,000 per vial or $30,000 per treatment cycle”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Street models $26–28k per month”; “A figure at or above $28k supports the market-size math.”

surprises.description: The reported GAAP loss per share of $1.44 was slightly worse than the preview’s estimated GAAP range of $1.30–$1.40. The preview’s headline consensus was adjusted EPS, so that figure is not directly comparable to the reported GAAP result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net loss widened to $78.9 million ($1.44 per share)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “That could push GAAP EPS to −$1.30 to −$1.40 with no operating meaning.”

surprises.description: SG&A reached $35 million, above the preview’s $27–$32 million estimate, as Celcuity built out its commercial launch organization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A rising to $35 million from $7.6 million on commercial launch buildout.”

surprises.description: R&D was $31.1 million, below the preview’s $34–$37 million estimate. The reduction was largely due to lower clinical-trial costs, including the VIKTORIA-1 wind-down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D expenses decreased to $31.1 million from $36.4 million … primarily due to a $7 million reduction in clinical trial costs including VIKTORIA-1 wind-down.”

surprises.description: The PIK3CA-mutant cohort’s doublet achieved median PFS of 11.3 months versus 5.6 months with alpelisib plus fulvestrant. The preview highlighted the triplet comparison but did not set an expectation for this doublet result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “the doublet achieved 11.3 months versus 5.6 months (HR 0.51).”

surprises.description: Updated mutant-cohort discontinuation rates were lower than the preview’s 12% triplet label figure: 5.2% for the triplet and 3.8% for the doublet. They were also well below the 19% rate with alpelisib, indicating better reported tolerability than the preview’s flagged concern suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Updated treatment discontinuation rates due to adverse events in the mutant cohort were 5.2% for the triplet and 3.8% for the doublet, versus 19% for alpelisib.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Label shows stomatitis in 72% of triplet patients (22% severe) and 12% discontinuation on the triplet. Watch for a prophylaxis protocol and medical science liaison deployment.”

surprises.description: Celcuity said its gross-to-net discount should be about 20%, retaining roughly 80% of WAC—better net realization than the roughly 30% discount it cited as typical for oral therapies. The preview did not provide a gross-to-net assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects a gross-to-net discount of about 20% (capturing ~80% of WAC), better than the ~30% discount typical for oral therapies.”

surprises.description: The company extended its stated cash runway to at least 2029, beyond the preview’s expectation that the convertible would likely extend runway past the prior ‘through 2027’ guide, without specifying as long a period.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$754 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments as of June 30, 2026 … providing runway at least into 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The prior guide was ‘through 2027,’ before the convertible. Pro forma cash is about $775M, so an extension is likely.”

surprises.description: Celcuity expanded VIKTORIA-2 to study gedatolisib in treatment-naive, endocrine-sensitive patients, a population the preview did not identify as a development focus. The company cited encouraging Phase Ib results against historical ribociclib-plus-letrozole figures as support for the expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “VIKTORIA-2 was expanded to add a study evaluating gedatolisib in treatment-naive endocrine-sensitive patients … where a prior Phase Ib trial showed median PFS of 48.6 months and 79% ORR versus historical 25 months and 53% for ribociclib plus letrozole.”

in_line: Management maintained the late-Q3 2026 start for REVTORPYK shipments, matching the preview’s base case.
The company still planned to submit the PIK3CA-mutant supplemental NDA in Q3 2026, as expected.
The mutant-cohort triplet median PFS result of 11.1 months versus 5.6 months with alpelisib plus fulvestrant matched the result already cited in the preview.
Cash and investments of $754 million were within the preview’s estimated $740–$790 million range.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $37.6 million, far above the preview’s roughly $26.9–$27.2 million consensus range. The result was about 38% above the high end of that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $37.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 Revenue” consensus: “$26.88M” or “$27.22M”; “Working consensus: about $27M revenue.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $16.2 million, nearly twice the preview’s base-case range of $7.5–$8.5 million and well above the roughly $8.1 million it called on-track. The 43% margin also substantially exceeded the preview’s expectation of a result around the 30% full-year target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $16.2 million (43% of revenue).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “On about $27M of revenue, roughly $8.1M of adj. EBITDA is the on-track number”; base case: “Adj. EBITDA $7.5–8.5M.”

surprises.description: Eaton raised 2026 revenue guidance to more than $145 million, well beyond the prior floor of more than $120 million and the preview’s roughly $121 million consensus. The preview described a raise above $125 million as the bull scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to exceed $145 million, up from the prior guidance of more than $120 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue” guidance: “>$120M”; consensus: “$121.32M”; bull scenario: “FY26 revenue guide raised to >$125M.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.43 greatly exceeded the preview’s $0.13–$0.148 consensus range. GAAP results were also stronger than the preview’s $0.11 GAAP-leaning estimate: Eaton reported $0.35 per diluted share and net income rather than a loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income was $11.6 million ($0.35 per diluted share) versus a prior-year net loss of $2.6 million, with non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.43 compared to $0.03.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 non-GAAP EPS consensus: “$0.148” or “$0.13”; “Q2 EPS (GAAP-leaning)”: “$0.11.”

surprises.description: Eaton raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA margin outlook to more than 35%, up from more than 30%. That is a stronger annual target than the preview’s stated guidance, alongside the much stronger-than-expected Q2 margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was raised to exceed 35% from prior guidance of over 30%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA margin” company guidance: “>30%.”

surprises.description: About 95% of Hemangiol’s roughly 8,000 patients had moved to Eaton’s single-pharmacy model by the end of June, ahead of the three-to-four-month transition timeline cited on the call. The preview had highlighted the program’s potential gross-to-net impact but did not anticipate this pace of transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 95% of Hemangiol's roughly 8,000 patients were transitioned to Eaton's single-pharmacy Eaton Cares model by end of June, well ahead of the expected three-to-four-month timeline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “60–65% of HEMANGEOL volume may be near-zero revenue under the $0 co-pay Eton Cares program.”

surprises.description: The call described a narrower remaining development path for ASN-001 than the preview had laid out: after a completed Phase 3 trial, the only remaining requirement is a 24-patient, 29-day bioavailability study costing about $4 million. It also described a potential patient population two-to-three times larger than Hemangiol’s and said ASN-001 is expected to become Eaton’s largest product—details not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The only remaining ASN-001 development requirement is a 24-patient, 29-day FDA-reviewed bioavailability bridging study costing approximately $4 million over the next 12 months, following an already-completed Phase 3 trial showing efficacy versus placebo”; it “could address a patient population two-to-three times larger than Hemangiol” and is “expected to become Eaton's largest product.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “ASN-001 NDA (2H27), launch 2028” but did not describe the remaining study requirements or the potential patient population.

surprises.description: Eaton ended the quarter with more cash than at Q1 while prepaying debt, and said it plans to accelerate repayment of the remaining facility over the next 6–12 months. The preview had flagged the balance sheet and financing risk, including the possibility that an equity raise could weigh on the print.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $26.8 million in cash after a $3 million debt prepayment, and plans to accelerate repayment of its remaining credit facility over the next 6 to 12 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 ended with $19.7M cash against $30.7M debt”; “Balance sheet and financing risk”; “An equity raise announced with the print would cap any beat.”

surprises.description: Management set substantially more ambitious long-term targets: an annualized run rate above $200 million exiting 2027, a 50% adjusted EBITDA margin by 2028, and at least $500 million in annual revenue by 2030 with ASN-001. The preview cited FY27 revenue consensus of about $187 million but did not identify these longer-term targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised long-term targets, now expecting to exceed the $200 million annualized run rate exiting 2027, a 50% adjusted EBITDA margin by 2028, and to achieve or exceed $500 million in annual revenue by 2030 with ASN-001.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FY27 revenue” consensus of “$186.93M” and did not state longer-term company targets.

in_line: Full-year adjusted gross margin guidance remained above 70%, in line with the preview’s stated guidance; Q2 adjusted gross margin was 73%, although it was down from 75% a year earlier.
ASN-001’s planned NDA filing in the second half of 2027 and potential 2028 launch were consistent with the preview’s stated timing.
