surprises.fact_evidence: “Display Solutions Q4 sales nearly doubled to $164 million (70% of total LSI sales)” and “Q4 sales grew 51%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales… Consensus $222.8M”; the preview’s base scenario was “$220–228M.”

surprises.description: Display Solutions’ 18% organic growth far surpassed the preview’s expectation of mid-to-high single-digit organic growth. Its 12.4% adjusted EBITDA margin also cleared the preview’s 12% threshold, reaching its highest level in nearly three years.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Display Solutions Q4 sales nearly doubled to $164 million… with 18% organic growth,” and “segment adjusted EBITDA margin rose 180 basis points to 12.4%, its highest in nearly three years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Display Solutions (organic): up mid-to-high single digits”; the checklist called for “Display Solutions margin of 12% or better.”

surprises.description: Lighting was materially stronger than the preview’s directional outlook: full-year sales grew 7% rather than declining mid-single digits. Q4 sales were down only 3%, with orders up 5% and book-to-bill above one, supporting a better exit trend than the preview’s trough concern implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lighting segment Q4 sales declined 3%… but full-year lighting sales grew 7% with Q4 orders up 5% and a book-to-bill above one.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Lighting: down mid-single digits against a tough +12% comparison”; the preview asked whether the decline was “the bottom” and flagged lighting conversion as a key issue.

surprises.description: The company reported 8% Q4 organic growth, above the preview’s low-to-mid single-digit directional expectation. Grocery and refueling/C-store were notably strong contributors.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 sales grew 51% (8% organic)” and organic growth was led by grocery display cases “up 21%” and refueling/C-store “up 16%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Overall organic growth: low-to-mid single digits.”

surprises.description: Full-year sales and adjusted EPS both topped the preview’s estimates: sales were $689 million versus about $678 million, and adjusted EPS was $1.25 versus $1.20–$1.22.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2026 net sales reached a record $689 million” and “adjusted EPS growing to $1.25.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s own estimates were “FY26 revenue… ~$678M (+18%)” and “FY26 adj. EPS… ~$1.20–1.22.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EPS of $0.38 beat the $0.35 consensus, though it remained within the preview’s base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4… adjusted EPS increased to $0.38.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS… Consensus $0.35”; the base scenario forecast “$0.36–0.39.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin was below the preview’s estimate despite EBITDA dollars being around the expected level: the reported 10.9% margin was short of the preview’s roughly 11.5% estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EBITDA rose 50% to over $25 million… though Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin of 10.9% came in below expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~$25–26M (~11.5% margin)” and said margins at “10–11% would likely hurt the multiple.”

surprises.description: A newly won multi-year oil-retailer renovation program covering about 2,500 sites was not included in current guidance, creating unanticipated potential business beyond the outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company won a new multi-year program with a large oil retailer to renovate approximately 2,500 sites over roughly 18 months, displacing an incumbent supplier,” and “this award is not yet factored into current guidance.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that lower-margin Royston sign-resources backlog will weigh on margins through the first half of FY2027, with a 50–100 basis-point headwind before it clears. The preview focused on Royston’s margin contribution but did not flag this specific extended backlog drag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lower-margin Royston sign-resources backlog… is expected to create a 50-100 basis point margin headwind through the first half of fiscal 2027 before clearing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said investors would look for Royston margins of “13% or above” and that “margins at 10–11% would likely hurt the multiple.”

surprises.description: Despite the disclosed near-term Royston headwind, management reaffirmed its 12.5% adjusted EBITDA margin target under the fast-forward strategy, giving a firm profitability target alongside the near-term pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed its 12.5% adjusted EBITDA margin target under its fast-forward strategy despite the near-term Royston headwind.”

surprises.description: CFO Jim Galeese announced he plans to retire by October 2027, a management transition not anticipated in the preview; a successor search is already underway.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Jim Galeese announced he will retire by end of October 2027 after nearly a decade of service, with a formal successor search already underway.”

in_line: Q4 adjusted EBITDA dollars were broadly in line with the preview’s estimate: reported EBITDA was over $25 million versus the preview’s estimate of about $25–26 million.

surprises.description: Adjusted pre-tax income was a $2 million loss, below the company’s breakeven-to-$10 million guidance and the preview’s $5–9 million base case. Weak JV income and delayed JV deliveries drove the shortfall, the first miss of the guidance range in 23 quarters.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted pre-tax income was a $2 million loss—the first time in 23 quarters that pre-tax income missed the guidance range, driven largely by weak JV income and delayed new joint venture deliveries.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. income before taxes: Breakeven to $10M”; the preview’s base case was “$5–9M.”

surprises.description: Incentives declined for a third consecutive quarter, extending the improvement beyond the second sequential decline the preview identified as a positive signal—even as mortgage rates rose during Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Incentives have declined for three consecutive quarters (Q1 to Q3) even as mortgage rates rose during the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A second straight sequential decline from 11.9% would be a clear positive.”

surprises.description: Q3 contracts were down 4% year over year, consistent with the preview’s risk of softer orders, but August month-to-date contracts were up 3% and July website visits were the second-highest for that month since 2019. Those later indicators suggest demand persisted despite weak conversion and were not specifically anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Quarterly contracts declined by 57 homes to 1,359 (a 4% drop) year-over-year”; “Month-to-date August contracts were up 3% versus last year, and July website visits were the second-highest for that month since 2019.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bear scenario cited “Soft June–July orders as rates rose.”

surprises.description: The Q4 outlook included JV income of $10–20 million, versus just $3 million in Q3. The preview expected a significant Q4 step-up generally, but did not identify a projected JV-income rebound as part of it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 2026 guidance projects … JV income of $10-$20 million (versus just $3 million in Q3).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had promised “a significant step-up in fourth quarter performance.”

surprises.description: Option lots reached a record 87% of controlled lots, and the option-lot count grew sequentially for the first time in six quarters. The preview discussed community growth and land-related issues but did not anticipate this shift toward option lots or the reported higher-margin replacement lots.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Option lots reached a record 87% of the controlled lot portfolio … and option lot count grew sequentially for the first time in six quarters as newer higher-margin lots replaced delivered lots.”

surprises.description: Backlog conversion was 74%, well above the historical 57% average, and one-third of Q3 deliveries were sold and closed within the quarter. This favorable conversion pace was not addressed in the preview, though it also makes results more sensitive to closing timing and mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog conversion was 74%, well above the historical 57% average, and 33% of homes delivered in Q3 were both sold and closed within the quarter, increasing sensitivity of future results to closing timing and mix.”

in_line: Q3 revenue of $706 million was within the $650–750 million guidance range and the preview’s $680–720 million base case.
Q3 gross margin of 14.6% was within the guided 14.0–15.0% range and the preview’s 14.4–14.8% base case; the sequential improvement also matched the preview’s margin-recovery focus.

Q4 guidance called for revenue of $800–900 million and gross margin of 15–16.5%, consistent with the preview’s expected significant step-up and its bull-case markers of revenue above $800 million and margin of at least 15%.
Community count was essentially flat year over year, while management again projected growth in Q4 and into 2027, broadly matching the preview’s expectation of growth later in FY26 or early FY27.

surprises.description: Q2 billings reached $310 million, far above the preview estimate of $286–290 million. That is a substantially larger beat than the preview’s roughly $288 million watchpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 billings grew 17% year-over-year to $310 million, well above the company's low double-digit growth expectations, driven by record Q2 bookings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 needs about $288M (+9%) reported”; consensus was “~$286–290M.”

surprises.description: Operating margin was 29.4%, 0.9 percentage points above the 28.5% guide despite an FX headwind. The preview expected margins near the guide, not this degree of outperformance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating margin expanded 90 basis points to 29.4%, beating guidance of 28.5% despite a 100 basis point FX headwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin” guide was “~28.5%”; the preview also said, “Operating margin is guided near 28.5% against rising AI inference costs.”

surprises.description: Net retention rose to 106%, above the 105% guide, and management now expects to exit FY27 at 106%. The preview identified 106% or higher as a stronger-than-baseline outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net retention rate improved to 106%, beating guidance of 105% and up from 103% a year ago, with management now expecting to exit FY27 at 106%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “105% holds the thesis. 106% or higher would support a re-rating.”

surprises.description: FY27 EPS guidance is $1.54, below the preview’s desired $1.58–$1.60 and below the previously stated $1.56 guide. The reported underlying increase is only $0.01 after accounting for FX.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 EPS guidance of $1.54 includes a $0.09 FX headwind, representing only a $0.01 underlying increase versus prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed prior FY27 EPS guidance of “~$1.56” and said, “Bulls need revenue near $1.285–1.29B and EPS of $1.58–1.60.”

surprises.description: Q2 repurchases were about $66 million, well below the preview’s approximately $114 million-per-quarter reference. The call did not report a change to the buyback authorization, but the quarter’s repurchase pace was lower.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Box repurchased 2.6 million shares for approximately $66 million in Q2, with $378 million of buyback capacity remaining.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist asked about “any change to the buyback cadence (about $114M per quarter).”

surprises.description: Gross margin is expected to fall to roughly 80% in Q4, with management citing AI workload adoption and limited public-cloud infrastructure capacity. The preview flagged AI inference costs as a margin concern but did not anticipate this specific gross-margin decline or capacity constraint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin came in at 81.2% but is guided to decline to roughly 80% in Q4, pressured by growing AI workload adoption and constrained access to public cloud provider infrastructure capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating margin is guided near 28.5% against rising AI inference costs.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $321 million, modestly above the roughly $319 million consensus and guide, and constant-currency growth was 11% versus the preview’s 10% guide. The preview’s base scenario already contemplated $321–323 million, so the gap was limited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY27 revenue was $321 million, up 9% year-over-year (11% in constant currency), exceeding guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue guide was “~$319M (+9%; +10% cc)” and consensus was “~$319.1–319.3M.”

in_line: Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $0.40 was at the preview’s working consensus bar of $0.40, although it exceeded the company’s $0.39 guide.
Q2 gross margin of 81.2% was within the preview’s 81.0–81.5% guide range.
FY27 revenue guidance of approximately $1.29 billion met the preview’s stated bull-case threshold of at least $1.285 billion.
Q2 free cash flow fell from Q1’s seasonal peak, as the preview expected; the call reported $60 million for Q2.

surprises.description: Q4 net sales rose 17% year over year, far above the preview’s $802.0–814.4 million consensus range; using the preview’s $812.9 million prior-year sales figure, that growth implies roughly $951 million. Full-year sales growth of 6% also implies about $3.22 billion, above the preview’s $3.07 billion consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 net sales rose 17% year-over-year” and “full-year sales grew 6%, driven by strengthening second-half demand and the return of large deals.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave Q4 net sales consensus of “$802.0M (alt: $814.4M)” and FY26 net sales consensus of “$3.07B”; it listed Q4 FY25 actual sales of “$812.9M.”

surprises.description: Q4 non-GAAP EPS was $1.46, well above the preview’s consensus estimates of $1.11–$1.14, and rose 43% year over year to a record.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 non-GAAP EPS grew 43% year-over-year to a record $1.46 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q4 non-GAAP diluted EPS consensus of “$1.14 (range $1.04–$1.19; alt polls $1.11 / $1.13).”

surprises.description: FY27 organic revenue guidance is stronger than the preview’s roughly $3.15–$3.25 billion expectation: 6%–10% growth on the implied FY26 sales base of about $3.22 billion points to a higher range. Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $158–$165 million is also above the preview’s $150–$160 million range at the upper end, though the ranges overlap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 organic guidance calls for revenue growth of 6% to 10% and adjusted EBITDA of $158-165 million (4.6-4.65% margin), excluding any MicroAge contribution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview framed FY27 as “about $3.15–3.25B revenue and $150–160M EBITDA.”

surprises.description: ScanSource signed a definitive agreement to acquire MicroAge, a specific transaction the preview had not anticipated; the stated rationale is to expand into cloud, cybersecurity, data center, and AI. The call provided no deal financial terms, so the shareholder impact is uncertain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed a definitive agreement to acquire MicroAge, expected to close by the end of Q1 FY27, to expand its TAM into cloud, cybersecurity, data center, and AI.”

surprises.description: The newly added Juniper networking line will contribute more slowly than investors might have expected, with supplier constraints delaying its ramp through the first half of FY27; fuller contribution is expected in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The newly added Juniper (HPE) networking line will ramp slowly through the first half of FY27 due to supplier supply-chain constraints, with fuller contribution expected in the second half.”

surprises.description: Full-year free cash flow was $114 million, above the formal guide of at least $90 million but below the $118.6 million already reported for the first nine months. That implies a negative Q4 contribution, a weaker finish than the nine-month cash result might have suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY26 free cash flow reached $114 million, representing 124% cash conversion of non-GAAP net income.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Nine-month FCF $118.6M against a full-year guide of at least $90M.”

surprises.description: Semtech guided Q3 revenue to $410 million, far above the preview’s inferred $340–350 million range. The outlook points to a much faster near-term step-up than the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for net sales of $410 million (+/- $5 million), up 20% sequentially and 54% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Treat the Q3 bar as roughly $340–350M”; the preview also said “$350M+ supports the AI-connectivity story.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $342 million, well above both the $328.4 million consensus and the $328 million guidance midpoint. The beat was larger than the preview’s base-case expectation of only a modest beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached a record $342 million, growing 33% year-over-year and beating the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales” consensus was “$328.4M”; Q2 guidance was “$328.0M ± $5.0M”; the base scenario anticipated “$329–332M” and a “Modest beat.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.71 substantially exceeded the $0.62 consensus and $0.61 guidance midpoint. It was also well above the preview’s base case of $0.62–0.63.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS of $0.71 up 73% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS” consensus was “$0.62” and guidance was “$0.61 ± $0.02”; the base scenario was “$0.62–0.63.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EPS guidance was $1.05, far above the preview’s cited—but explicitly described as stale and unreliable—screen of about $0.61. The preview did not identify a dependable Q3 EPS bar, so the size of this comparison is less certain than the revenue surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for … adjusted EPS of $1.05 up 119% year-over-year at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “One aggregator screen shows about $333M revenue and $0.61 EPS, but it looks stale.”

surprises.description: Data center revenue reached $100 million, modestly above the preview’s roughly $96–97 million expectation, and management then guided to another 45% sequential increase in Q3. That acceleration is stronger than the preview’s focus on watching the timing of the ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data center revenue hit a record $100 million, up 39% sequentially and 91% year-over-year,” with Q3 guided for “45% sequential growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected Q2 data center revenue of “roughly $96–97M” and flagged “ramp timing” as something to watch.

surprises.description: Gross margin exceeded the 54% Q2 guide, and Q3 consolidated gross margin is now guided to 58.3%. That Q3 outlook is a much sharper improvement than the preview’s stated expectation of a roughly 100-basis-point sequential rise to 54%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin was 54.5% in Q2,” and “Q3 consolidated gross margin [is] guided to 58.3% (a 380 basis point sequential increase).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 adjusted gross margin guidance of “54.0% ± 50bp” and described it as “up about 100bp QoQ.”

surprises.description: LoRa-enabled sales reached $58 million, well above the preview’s approximate $51 million expectation, and management expects another 15% sequential gain in Q3. The reported quarter thus substantially outpaced the preview’s minimum-growth threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LoRa-enabled sales hit an all-time record of $58 million, up 31% sequentially and 58% year-over-year,” with Q3 guided to “grow another 15% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected Q2 LoRa to be “more than 15% QoQ (about $51M+, off $44.5M).”

surprises.description: The cellular-module divestiture is still described as pending, whereas the preview highlighted confirming the close. The call also disclosed that the transaction is expected to be EPS-neutral while lifting gross margin by more than 500 basis points, a larger structural margin benefit than the preview had specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pending divestiture of the cellular module business is expected to be EPS-neutral but structurally lift gross margin by over 500 basis points”; ex-module Q3 gross margin is guided to “63.9% versus 58.3% consolidated.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the divestiture was in “final stages” as of May and listed “Confirm the close and whether Q3 guidance strips out the divested revenue clearly.”

surprises.description: Management expects 1.6T FiberEdge and CopperEdge together to make up more than half of data center revenue in Q3, with FiberEdge 1.6T itself expected to exceed half by fiscal year-end. The preview flagged the ramp but did not anticipate these specific mix milestones.
surprises.fact_evidence: “1.6T FiberEdge and CopperEdge combined to surpass 50% of total data center revenue in Q3,” and “FiberEdge 1.6T share [is] expected to exceed 50% by the end of the fiscal year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Data center revenue and the 1.6T/CopperEdge ramp” and said to “Watch ramp timing,” without specifying these mix targets.

surprises.description: Management reported that 800-gig industry volume had risen to about 90 million units, versus an initial forecast of 50 million, while Semtech’s FiberEdge share had grown from 18% two years earlier to well over 50%. Neither the market-volume revision nor this share gain was anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “800-gig transceiver industry volumes have roughly doubled to 90 million units this year (versus an initial forecast of 50 million), and Semtech has grown its FiberEdge share from 18% two years ago to well over 50%.”

surprises.description: Management outlined a future increase in Semtech’s photonics content per transceiver from high single-digit dollars to $80–90 as the industry moves to 3.2T, with meaningful deployment estimated in roughly two years. This longer-term content opportunity was not raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The photonics expansion is “expected to drive content per transceiver from high single-digit dollars to high double-digit dollars (80-90 dollars) as the industry transitions to 3.2T,” with “meaningful deployment estimated in roughly two years.”

surprises.description: Semtech said fiscal 2028 backlog is already more than 70% booked, providing substantial forward visibility that the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog for fiscal 2028 is already over 70% booked.”

surprises.description: The call reported $61 million of free cash flow and net leverage of 1.1x, but the preview set no expectations for cash generation or leverage. These are favorable additional financial details rather than a quantified beat against a stated preview hurdle.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was $61 million (up 48% year-over-year),” with “$204 million cash against $503 million debt” and “net leverage of 1.1x.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $19.4M: slightly above the preview’s derived $19.2M consensus, but below its $19.8M base case. The result therefore met the lower consensus estimate but fell short of the preview’s central scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 net revenue reached a record $19.4 million, up 12% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Revenue ~$19.2M (derived)” and a “$19.8M” base case.

surprises.description: Q4 diluted EPS of $0.39 exceeded both the preview’s derived consensus range of $0.28–$0.31 and its $0.37 base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS hit a quarterly record of $0.39.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Diluted EPS ~$0.28–0.31 (derived)” and a base-case “~$0.37.”

surprises.description: Full-year diluted EPS reached $1.30, above the preview’s $1.20 Zacks estimate and its roughly $1.23 implied estimate, while full-year revenue was close to the $73.6M estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year net income was $11.3 million with diluted EPS of $1.30.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “FY26 EPS $1.20 (Zacks) or ~$1.23 (implied)” and “FY26 revenue: $73.6M.”

surprises.description: Operating income grew substantially faster than revenue, indicating stronger operating leverage than the preview’s flagged concern about costs rising as new reps are onboarded would suggest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 operating income grew 26% year-over-year to $3.8 million”; for the full year, “operating income [was] up 43.7% to $13.9 million (18.8% of revenue).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “Watch whether SG&A rises as new reps are onboarded.”

surprises.description: The FY27 plan calls for 67 territories versus 64 direct sales reps at year-end, implying roughly three more territories—below the preview’s expectation of 4–5 net additions. The plan includes two hospital account liaisons, so the measures are not perfectly comparable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q4 with 64 direct sales reps (up 6 from Q3) and plans to reach 67 territories in fiscal 2027, including 2 hospital account liaisons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “guided to adding 4–5 reps in FY27” and asked whether additions were “confirmed at 4–5, raised, or cut.”

surprises.description: Full-year revenue per weighted-average sales rep was $1.145M, just below the preview’s $1.15M threshold for sustaining productivity, though it exceeded the company’s prior $1.0M–$1.1M target and the FY27 target was raised.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Home care revenue per weighted average sales rep reached $1,145,000 in fiscal 2026, exceeding the $1.0M–$1.1M target, and the fiscal 2027 target was raised to $1,050,000–$1,150,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Holding above $1.15M annualized in Q3 supports growth with few new hires.”

surprises.description: Hospital revenue fell sharply even as the core home-care channel grew; the preview focused on home care and did not flag a hospital-channel decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The core home care channel grew 15% in Q4 and 16.3% for the year to $66.6 million, while hospital revenue declined 29% in the quarter due to longer, less predictable sales cycles.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described direct homecare as “about 90% of the P&L” and focused its key growth watch on that channel; it gave no hospital-revenue expectation.

surprises.description: Payer coverage rose to 87% from the 86% level cited at Q3, rather than remaining flat, with 40 new contracts adding more than 6 million covered lives.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Payer coverage reached 87% of U.S. covered lives with 40 new payer contracts adding over 6 million covered lives.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said coverage was “86% under contract at Q3” and warned that “a flat print there would mean that growth lever is largely used up.”

surprises.description: The CEO announced a planned retirement in April 2027, an unexpected leadership transition for investors assessing the company’s outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CEO Jim Cunniff announced plans to retire in April 2027, with a Board-led succession process underway.”

surprises.description: Management cited roughly 800,000 diagnosed but untreated bronchiectasis patients as part of the addressable market, a sizable market detail not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The addressable market includes roughly 800,000 diagnosed but untreated bronchiectasis patients.”

in_line: Core home-care revenue grew 15% in Q4, matching the preview’s roughly 15% base-case expectation and exceeding its stated threshold of at least 14%.
FY26 revenue of $73.8M was essentially in line with the preview’s $73.6M estimate.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $70.6 million, $3.1 million above the preview’s $67.5 million base estimate, with 7.3% reported growth (about 10% constant-currency growth) rather than the modeled 2.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 7.3% year-over-year to $70.6 million (approximately 10% growth on a constant currency basis).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Q2 FY2026E (my base) $67.5M … YoY +2.6%.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 22.6%, 2.1 percentage points above the preview’s 20.5% estimate and above the preview’s 22% bull-case threshold. The preview had identified a result at or above 20% as the key test of whether Q1’s margin improvement was structural.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached 22.6%, the highest quarterly level in more than five years,” driven in part by completion of the battery upgrade program and better network utilization.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “IFRS gross margin … Q2 FY2026E (my base) 20.5%”; “IFRS gross margin at or above 20%”; bull scenario: “GM at or above 22%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $19.3 million, $1.3 million above the preview’s $18.0 million base estimate, though below the preview’s $20 million to $22 million bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased to $19.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA … Q2 FY2026E (my base) $18.0M”; bull scenario: “$20M to $22M.”

surprises.description: The net loss narrowed by more than $21.6 million year over year, exceeding the roughly $20 million improvement implied by the preview’s estimate of a $6.5 million loss versus a $26.5 million year-ago loss. The call facts do not give the exact Q2 net loss, so the size of the beat cannot be determined more precisely.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss improved by more than $21.6 million year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net loss … Q2 FY2026E (my base) $(6.5)M”; Q2 FY2025 actual: “$(26.5)M.”

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed the full $285 million to $305 million FY2026 revenue range instead of narrowing it toward the preview’s base-case range of $285 million to $295 million. This avoided the further guidance trim the preview said would confirm a pattern of reductions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was reaffirmed at $285 million to $305 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base scenario: “guide narrowed toward $285M to $295M”; the preview also said “A second trim toward $285M would confirm a pattern.”

surprises.description: Entry-level vehicle success was substantial, with the EZZY family contributing more than one-third of scooter sales revenue, but it modestly pressured average revenue per subscriber. That mix pressure contrasts with the preview’s focus on hardware ASP and premium-model commentary as unit growth needed to translate into revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The EZZY family of scooters contributed more than one-third of scooter sales revenue”; “continued entry-level vehicle success modestly pressured average revenue per subscriber.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Hardware ASP and mix. Unit growth needs to translate into revenue. Commentary on the June in-wheel-motor launch and the premium model would matter.”

surprises.description: The company announced that CFO Bruce Aitken is departing after more than eight years, with Jackie Lee replacing him as Principal Financial Officer; the preview did not flag a finance-leadership change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Bruce Aitken is departing after more than 8 years and will be replaced by Jackie Lee as Principal Financial Officer.”

in_line: The battery-swapping business remained on track for non-IFRS profitability in 2026, consistent with the preview’s expectation that management would reaffirm the annual target rather than defer it.

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $1.55, above the preview’s $1.48–$1.50 consensus range and the company’s $1.45–$1.47 guidance. Rather than declining year over year as the preview expected from the $1.53 comparison, EPS rose $0.02; the call said buybacks helped.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP EPS came in at $1.55, beating the high end of guidance by $0.08 and up $0.02 year-over-year, aided by the buyback program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | $1.48 (Yahoo/Benzinga) or $1.50 (ScanX)”; “The EPS comp is down year over year”; company guidance “$1.45–$1.47.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $1.28 billion topped the preview’s roughly $1.27 billion consensus and came in above the company’s guidance range. The beat was modest in dollar terms, but exceeded the preview’s base case of about $1.275 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue grew 4.9% year-over-year to $1.28 billion, coming in $7 million above the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | ~$1.27B”; base scenario revenue “~$1.275B”; company guidance “$1.265–$1.270B.”

surprises.description: The FY27 non-GAAP EPS outlook rose to $6.08–$6.12, above the preview’s roughly $6.00 expectation and the prior $5.96–$6.00 guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Increased non-GAAP EPS guidance to $6.08-$6.12.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 non-GAAP EPS | ~$6.00”; company guidance “$5.96–$6.00.”

surprises.description: FY27 free cash flow guidance increased to $1.78–$1.82 billion, above the preview’s approximately $1.72 billion expectation. The call attributed about $40 million of the increase to lower CapEx after extending a data center’s useful life by two years, rather than describing it as solely stronger operating performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow guidance was raised to $1.78-$1.82 billion, aided by a downward CapEx revision from extending a data center's useful life by two years, adding about $40 million to free cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 free cash flow | ~$1.72B”; company guidance “$1.700–$1.740B.”

surprises.description: Despite an overall increase in the FY27 revenue outlook, management now assumes online revenue will be flat. The preview flagged online churn and FX as issues to watch but did not anticipate a flat online outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enterprise growing faster than expected but online now assumed to be flat.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Online segment. Online is about 39% of revenue. Watch churn against 3.0% and the FX commentary, since FX helped Q1.”

surprises.description: RPO rose 14% year over year, with noncurrent RPO up 25%, and the call characterized bookings as the strongest in several years. The preview identified RPO/cRPO as a figure to check but gave no growth expectation, so the scale of the reported bookings strength was not anticipated there.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RPO increased 14% year-over-year to approximately $4.5 billion, driven by 25% growth in noncurrent RPO, marking the strongest bookings quarter in several years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Check the 10-Q for the updated Anthropic carrying value and RPO/cRPO.”

surprises.description: The preview specifically said investors wanted AI revenue or attach-rate evidence rather than user counts, but the reported AI metrics were adoption counts: licensed Workplace AI monthly active users grew 125% and Virtual Agent customers grew more than 250%. Those gains show adoption, but the facts provided do not establish the monetization evidence the preview was looking for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Licensed monthly active users of Workplace AI features grew 125% year-over-year, and Zoom Virtual Agent customer count grew more than 250% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Investors now want revenue or attach-rate figures, not user counts.”

surprises.description: Margins contracted, with non-GAAP operating margin down to 40% from 41.3% and gross margin down to 79.1% from 79.8%. The preview did not flag margin pressure; the call cited higher AI usage costs and acquisition-related dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin declined to 40% from 41.3% a year ago, and gross margin fell to 79.1% from 79.8%, partly due to higher AI usage costs and the dilutive margin impact of acquisitions like Common Room.”

surprises.description: Zoom Phone continued growing ARR in the teens with all of its top 10 phone deals described as competitive takeouts, while Zoom CX ARR grew at a high double-digit rate and reached a record number of seven-figure deals. The preview did not identify this product-level sales momentum as an expected result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Zoom Phone continued growing ARR in the teens with 10 of the top 10 phone deals being competitive takeouts, while Zoom CX ARR grew at a high double-digit rate and set a record number of 7-figure deals.”

in_line: FY27 revenue guidance rose to $5.085–$5.095 billion, broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of a nudge to about $5.10 billion.
Enterprise revenue grew 7.8%, near the preview’s 8% threshold for supporting the core-business case and above its 7% downside threshold.
The trailing 12-month net dollar expansion rate was 99%, matching the prior-quarter level. That was between the preview’s stated positive trigger of above 100% and negative trigger of a slip to 98%.

surprises.description: The preview did not indicate a forthcoming leadership change, but the call introduced Elliott Rogers as Kohl’s new COO, with a start date of September 9.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Elliott Rogers was introduced as Kohl’s new Chief Operating Officer, who will join on September 9.”

surprises.description: The preview did not mention a new customer leadership role, but the call announced that Brian Parisi would assume the newly created Chief Customer Officer role.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Brian Parisi was announced to assume the newly created role of Chief Customer Officer.”

surprises.description: Q2 total revenue was $161 million, above the preview’s $159.14 million consensus and the $159.75 million top end of company guidance. Subscription revenue also exceeded expectations, at $143.5 million versus roughly $141.5 million expected; growth excluding U.S. mortgage was 12%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenues for Q2 FY27 were $161 million”; “subscription revenues of $143.5 million”; excluding U.S. mortgage, subscription revenues grew 12% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” consensus: “$159.14M”; subscription revenue consensus: “~$141.5M (guide-anchored, not surveyed).”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating income was $40.8 million, well above the preview’s roughly $37 million consensus and the $37.5 million top of guidance. The 25% operating margin also came in above the roughly 23% margin implied by the guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income was $40.8 million (25% of total revenues), up 36% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview: non-GAAP operating income consensus “~$37M”; guidance “$35.5M – $37.5M”; non-GAAP operating margin “~23% at mid.”

surprises.description: The mortgage outlook weakened beyond the preview’s expectation of about a 1% full-year decline: nCino lowered its U.S. mortgage subscription revenue outlook by $700,000 in Q3 and $1.2 million in Q4 because of higher independent mortgage banker churn. Total company churn remained unchanged, so the pressure was specific to mortgage rather than an increase in overall churn.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered its U.S. mortgage subscription revenue outlook by approximately $700,000 in Q3 and $1.2 million in Q4 due to higher IMB churn from persistently high mortgage rates, though total company churn remains unchanged at about $25 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview: U.S. mortgage was “Guided to decline about 2% in Q2 and about 1% for the full year”; it flagged whether “the roughly 1% full-year assumption holds.”

surprises.description: Four of the top 20 U.S. enterprise customers renewed early, each contributing to an average ACV increase of more than 10%. The preview discussed ACV and net-add risks but did not anticipate these sizeable early renewals.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Four of the top 20 U.S. enterprise customers (representing over $900 billion in assets) renewed early with an average ACV increase of more than 10%.”

surprises.description: nCino signed what it expects to be its largest deal of the year, an international customer deal, early in Q3. The preview highlighted the need for H2 reacceleration but did not report or anticipate a deal of this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed what it expects to be its largest deal of the year, an international customer deal, in early Q3 FY27.”

surprises.description: AI adoption had progressed beyond the preview’s already-reported 200-plus purchasers: more than 230 customers had purchased AI intelligence units, production deployments of banking advisor had more than doubled year to date, and one-third of named AI-adopting customers were in production.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 230 customers have purchased AI intelligence units, with year-to-date production deployments of banking advisor more than doubling, and one-third of named AI-adopting customers now in production.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview: “200+ customers bought initial IU bundles” and banking advisor usage was “up more than 38x from October through May.”

in_line: nCino raised FY27 non-GAAP operating income guidance to $171–174 million from $166–171 million, consistent with the preview’s base case expectation of a raise roughly commensurate with the quarterly beat.
FY27 free cash flow guidance increased modestly to $137–142 million from $135–140 million; the preview had flagged a raise as likely and described it as a low-cost move for management.
The Board authorized an additional $100 million buyback, matching the preview’s identification of a new buyback authorization as a likely catalyst.

surprises.description: Q2 diluted EPS was $4.17, far above the $1.80–$2.00 company outlook and roughly $1.90–$1.95 consensus. The call said the beat exceeded even the roughly $1.75-per-share tariff-refund benefit, pointing to a substantial additional earnings beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income per diluted share was $4.17, far above guidance of $1.80 to $2.00, and beat the outlook by more than the roughly $1.75 tariff-refund benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS | $1.90 (Zacks) or $1.95 (broader Street) | $1.80–$2.00.”

surprises.description: The company recognized about $100 million of tariff refunds in Q2 despite having assumed zero refund benefit in its prior guidance, and now expects total refunds of about $120 million, with the remaining $20 million expected in Q3. That Q3 portion is expected to add about $0.35 per share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company now expects a total of ~$120 million in tariff refunds, with $100 million recognized in Q2 and the remaining $20 million expected in Q3 (contributing ~$0.35 to Q3 EPS).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “About $100M of IEEPA tariff refunds applied for, with zero benefit assumed in guidance”; “any recognized refund would be upside not in guidance.”

surprises.description: Q2 operating margin reached 19.9%, versus an outlook and model around 10%. The refund contributed approximately 790 basis points, so the reported margin was exceptionally higher than expected, though much of the gap came from the one-off refund.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating margin was 19.9%, up 600 basis points year-over-year, of which approximately 790 basis points came from a ~$100 million tariff refund recognized in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating margin | ~10.1% (Zacks model) | ~10%, including ~$20M tariff impact.”

surprises.description: Q2 net sales were $1.27 billion, up 5%, above both the company’s 2%–4% growth outlook and consensus of about 2.8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales reached a record $1.27 billion, up 5% year-over-year, exceeding the company's guidance range of 2% to 4% growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $1.24B (+2.8% YoY)”; company guidance “+2% to +4%.”

surprises.description: Full-year EPS guidance rose to $13.10–$13.60 from $10.20–$11.00, a much larger increase than the preview’s central question of whether guidance would be raised or maintained. The new range includes $2.10 per share from tariff refunds, but the call also indicated improvement beyond that benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lifted full-year EPS guidance to $13.10-$13.60, including a $2.10 tariff-refund benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS: $10.20–$11.00”; the preview identified “FY26 EPS guidance: raised or maintained” as a key issue.

surprises.description: Full-year operating-margin guidance increased to 14.5%–15% from 12.0%–12.5%. The company said the improvement goes beyond the roughly 220 basis points of tariff-refund benefit, indicating an underlying increase as well.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year operating margin guidance was raised to 14.5%-15%, with underlying margin improvement beyond the ~220 basis points of tariff-refund benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating margin: 12.0–12.5%.”

surprises.description: Hollister comparable sales fell 3%, worse than the Street’s expected 0.7% decline against the difficult 19% year-ago comparison. Net sales still grew 2%, but the comparable-sales result was a clear miss on a key preview issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hollister net sales grew 2% but comparable sales declined 3% against a 19% year-ago gain.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Hollister comparable sales against the +19% lap. Street expects -0.7%.”

surprises.description: Despite Hollister’s Q2 comp decline, management reported that demand exceeded available inventory at multiple points and that growth accelerated above Q2 levels in August. The new Target dorm partnership, in more than 1,500 stores, also generated incremental sales and reached new customers—stronger momentum and an additional sales channel not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hollister demand exceeded available inventory at multiple points in Q2, with growth accelerating above Q2 levels in August, and the new Target dorm partnership (in over 1,500 stores) drove incremental sales and reached new customers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Hollister comparable sales against the +19% lap. Street expects -0.7%”; the preview said this would test “whether the Hollister-supports-the-brand story holds.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year sales outlook to around 5% growth, signaling the high end of its prior range rather than the broader +3% to +5% range investors had previously been given. This is a modest improvement in the outlook, though it remains within that prior range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year net sales guidance to around 5% growth (to the high end of prior range).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales: +3% to +5%.”

surprises.description: The company increased its full-year buyback plan to at least $500 million, above the preview’s stated $450 million plan; year-to-date repurchases had already reached about $282 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date the company repurchased ~$282 million of stock (about 7% of shares outstanding), raised full-year buyback plans to at least $500 million, and ended the quarter with $568 million remaining on its authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capex: $225M; buyback: $450M.”

surprises.description: APAC delivered 19% net-sales growth and 13% comparable-sales growth, standing out against the preview’s uncertainty about the region and lack of a dependable estimate. The preview cited conflicting APAC estimates and said not to rely on that line, so the result is positive but cannot be measured against a reliable consensus baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APAC was the standout region with 19% net sales growth and 13% comparable sales growth.”

in_line: EMEA returned to 2% net-sales growth, within the preview’s expected range of +1% to +4%; the reported 4% comparable-sales decline had no preview comparison.

surprises.description: Intuit guided FY27 revenue growth to 9%-10%, below the preview’s published-consensus expectation of roughly 11%-12%, although it was in line with the preview’s 9%-10% buy-side whisper. Management attributed the deceleration to weakness in Desktop, TurboTax, and Credit Karma.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 total revenue guidance of $23.279B-$23.512B implies deceleration to 9%-10% growth, driven by weakness in Desktop, TurboTax, and Credit Karma.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Published consensus is about $23.7–23.9B (+11–12%)”; the preview also says “a guide of 9–10% would be a beat against the buy-side whisper and a miss against the model.”

surprises.description: The FY27 non-GAAP EPS range is below the preview’s roughly $26 expectation on its face, but Intuit is now including stock-based compensation, with a stated $5.81 per-share impact. Adding that impact back gives a rough comparable range of $28.69-$28.93, above the preview’s expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Beginning fiscal 2027, share-based compensation will no longer be excluded from non-GAAP measures, carrying a $5.81 per share impact, yet non-GAAP diluted EPS is still guided to grow 23%-24% to $22.88-$23.12.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Published consensus is about $23.7–23.9B (+11–12%) with non-GAAP EPS near $26”; the preview also describes a “defended ~$26 EPS line.”

surprises.description: Online paying-customer growth was weak: the year-end base grew only 3%, about two points slower than the prior year. The preview had flagged price-related DIY filer losses, but did not quantify this broader customer metric.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total online paying customers reached only 8.9 million at year-end, growing just 3% year-over-year (about 2 points slower than the prior year), highlighting the new-customer weakness driving the strategy reset.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that Intuit had “lost on price” with DIY filers and flagged TurboTax’s direction and customer issues, but gave no online-customer growth forecast.

surprises.description: Mid-market results showed substantial momentum, with revenue and customers growing rapidly and Intuit Enterprise Suite annualized revenue reaching more than $145 million. The preview discussed GBS growth and possible IES metrics but did not set a mid-market growth expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mid-market momentum remained strong with revenue up 39%, customers up 28%, and Intuit Enterprise Suite annualized revenue surpassing $145 million in Q4, a 4x increase year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Consumer money results were strong, including rapid growth in online money, personal finance offerings, and fast money refunds. The preview provided no expectation for these specific metrics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Online money portfolio revenue up 31%, personal finance offerings (insurance and home loans) up 44%, consumer money revenue up 26%, and fast money refunds of over $29 billion, up 79%.”

surprises.description: The reported quarterly dividend of $1.38 was higher than the preview’s stated expected level of $1.20 per quarter. The call described the $1.38 dividend as a 15% increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised the quarterly dividend 15% to $1.38 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says “a 15% dividend increase to $1.20/quarter were announced earlier.”

in_line: The cut in long-term GBS growth guidance to a 10%-15% three-year CAGR matched the preview’s cited expectation that the framework could be lowered from 15%-20%.

TurboTax FY27 revenue growth guidance of 2%-3% was broadly consistent with the preview’s flat-to-low-single-digit base-case expectation; the preview had also flagged price-related DIY customer losses.

surprises.description: Q3 sales were $1.413 billion, above the preview’s $1.34–1.35 billion published consensus, although slightly below its own $1.42 billion base estimate. That makes the reported revenue a clear beat to consensus, but not to the preview’s higher scenario-based estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated net sales increased 23% to a record $1,413.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $1.34–1.35B (Zacks / TradingView)” and “Base | ~$1.42B.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS of $1.67 exceeded both the $1.51 published consensus and the preview’s approximately $1.60 whisper estimate. The beat was larger against published consensus than against the preview’s own higher estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated net income rose 33% to a record $235.4 million ($1.67 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | $1.51” and “EPS vs. the ~$1.60 whisper.”

surprises.description: Consolidated operating margin was about 25.1% (operating income of $355.2 million divided by sales of $1,413.1 million), above the preview’s roughly 24% implied expectation and above the 25% level it highlighted as a key threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated net sales increased 23% to a record $1,413.1 million and operating income grew 34% to a record $355.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating margin | ~24% (implied)” and “Holding at or above 25% would mark a second quarter above the guided ranges.”

surprises.description: Parts and distribution organic growth accelerated sharply to 15%, well beyond the preview’s concern about whether the business could re-accelerate from 2% in Q2. This was a stronger recovery than the preview’s qualitative watchpoint implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Within FSG, organic growth was led by parts/distribution at 15%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether parts (+2% in Q2) re-accelerates.”

surprises.description: Component repair organic growth fell to 5%, rather than moving higher from Q2’s 10% as the preview said investors would watch for. Management also said persistent part shortages were constraining component repair revenue growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Component repair at only 5%” and “persistent supply chain part shortages that are constraining component repair revenue growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether … component repair (+10%) moves higher.”

surprises.description: Cash generation was stronger than the preview’s balance-sheet concern contemplated: operating cash flow rose 49%, reached nearly 150% of net income, and management expects full-year free cash flow near $1 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow surged 49% to $345.3 million, representing nearly 150% of net income, with management guiding full-year free cash flow near the $1 billion mark.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A third consecutive leverage increase with weak cash conversion would reopen the balance-sheet question.”

surprises.description: Leverage improved rather than moving toward the preview’s downside concern: net debt-to-EBITDA was 1.57x, below both the 1.6x fiscal year-end figure and the preview’s roughly 1.8x risk threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt-to-EBITDA improved to 1.57x from 1.6x at fiscal year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A third increase past about 1.8x would revive the Q1 concern.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a $70–75 million payment to the estate of the past Chairman that will absorb Q4 operating cash flow; the preview did not flag this cash outflow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 operating cash flow will absorb a $70-$75 million payment to the estate of the past Chairman.”

surprises.description: HEICO disclosed an enlarged and extended credit facility, with committed capital raised to $2.2 billion and an accordion to $3 billion, giving roughly $3 billion of acquisition capacity. The preview discussed acquisition cadence and an excellent pipeline but did not anticipate this financing-capacity update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HEICO extended its revolving credit facility to June 2031, raised committed capital to $2.2 billion with an accordion feature to $3 billion, giving roughly $3 billion of acquisition capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “M&A cadence. Five acquisitions in FY26 so far … Management called the pipeline ‘excellent.’”

in_line: ETG operating margin was about 26%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that a result at or above 25% would support the stronger-margin narrative; it was also close to Q2’s 26.5%.

Management reaffirmed the ETG full-year operating-margin range of 22%–24% rather than raising it. The preview said that range was the formal framework and that reiterating it after two quarters of overshoot would be a soft negative.
FSG operating margin of 25.9% was within the preview’s stated 24%–26% FSG range.

surprises.description: Management warned that the Cyclospora outbreak will make fiscal Q1 2027 materially weaker: sales are expected to be flat, gross margin to show no growth, and operating income to decline about 15%. The preview did not anticipate an outbreak or this near-term outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Cyclospora outbreak is expected to create an approximately 250 basis point net sales headwind in fiscal Q1 2027”; Q1 sales are expected to be “flattish,” with “no gross margin growth” and an “approximately 15% decline in operating income.”

surprises.description: Consolidated Q4 sales were $465 million, about 2.3% below the $476 million consensus and below the preview’s $469 million low-end range. However, sales excluding the discontinued temporary supply agreement were slightly positive, broadly matching the preview’s expectation of roughly flat core sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 consolidated net sales declined 2.2% to $465 million,” while adjusted net sales “grew 40 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $476.0M | $469.0M – $480.7M”; the preview also said “core sales roughly flat.”

surprises.description: Gross-margin expansion was substantially stronger than the preview’s expected 50–80 basis points: adjusted gross margin rose 160 basis points and reported gross margin rose 220 basis points. The 12-quarter improvement streak continued, as the preview had identified that as a key test.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded for the 12th consecutive quarter, up 220 basis points reported and 160 basis points adjusted.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “gross margin +50–80 bps” and said a “twelfth straight Y/Y gain” was the key tell.

surprises.description: Reported diluted EPS of $1.76 substantially exceeded the $1.40 consensus, but the result included an $18.5 million facility-sale gain; adjusted EPS was $1.46, a much smaller beat against the consensus benchmark. The preview had not anticipated that one-off gain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported diluted EPS rose 49.2% to $1.76, boosted by an $18.5 million gain from selling the Milpitas, California facility,” while “adjusted diluted EPS increased $0.12 to $1.46.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | $1.40”; the preview also noted the implied FY26 consensus was about “$6.61 GAAP EPS.”

surprises.description: Management provided a quantified fiscal 2027 outlook despite the preview expecting no formal numeric FY27 guidance: mid-single-digit revenue and operating-income growth, with about 100 basis points of gross-margin expansion. The outlook includes an expected contribution from Bachan’s and base cost savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “guided fiscal 2027 to mid-single-digit revenue growth and mid-single-digit operating income growth,” with consolidated gross margin expected to expand “about 100 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Marzetti gives no formal numeric quarterly guidance and no formal numeric FY27 guidance”; the preview said “Silence on FY27 would itself be negative.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating income grew 17.5%, above the preview’s roughly 12% year-over-year growth implied by the $1.40 EPS consensus, showing stronger operating-income growth than the estimate implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted operating income grew 17.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus of $1.40 implies operating income of roughly $49–50M, about 12% above Q4 FY25 on flat sales.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed unusually strong retail performance for Texas Roadhouse dinner rolls: $58 million in sales, 76% growth, and velocity nearly twice the category average. The preview mentioned the Texas Roadhouse pipeline-build lap but did not anticipate these sales or velocity figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Texas Roadhouse dinner rolls generated $58 million in retail sales over the 52-week period (up 76%), with velocity nearly 2x the category average”; with Sister Schubert’s, the brands held “61.7%” share.

surprises.description: The company reported record full-year operating cash flow alongside higher shareholder returns: a 5% dividend increase and $36.3 million of buybacks, up $28.3 million year over year. The preview noted the existing dividend but did not set an expectation for this increase in repurchases or record cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record full-year operating cash flow of $283.8 million (up 8.5%),” a “5%” dividend increase, and “$36.3 million in buybacks, up $28.3 million year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed the existing “Dividend … $4.00 per share” and asked investors to watch capex, but gave no expectation for buybacks or full-year cash flow.

in_line: Adjusted net sales excluding the discontinued temporary supply agreement grew 40 basis points, broadly matching the preview’s expectation that core sales would be roughly flat.
Bachan’s contributed $15.4 million in incremental sales, close to the preview’s roughly $15 million estimate.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $5.29, well above the $4.62 consensus and the $4.82 high end of company guidance. The gap was substantially larger than the preview’s base-case EPS range of $4.90–$5.20.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS of $5.29 grew 45.3% year-over-year and exceeded the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS… $4.62”; company guidance “$4.40 – $4.82”; base scenario “$4.90 – $5.20.”

surprises.description: The company said about $150 million of wireless revenue would shift from the second half of FY2027 into FY2028. The preview flagged possible wireless deferrals as a downside risk, but the size and timing of this shift are specific; management said overall program scope was unchanged and slightly increased.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company deferred approximately $150 million of wireless revenue from the second half of FY2027 into FY2028,” while “overall program scope is unchanged and slightly increased.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Confirmation of deferrals would support the bear case”; the bear scenario included “deferrals acknowledged.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $315.5 million, about $25.7 million above the preview’s estimate, and the 15.7% margin exceeded the roughly 14.7% consensus and 14.9% company-guidance margin expectation. This was a clear improvement rather than the expected roughly flat margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $315.5 million (15.7% of revenue) rose 53.5% and also beat guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$289.8M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin ~14.7%” and “~14.9% at midpoint,” described as “Roughly flat.”

surprises.description: Communications adjusted EBITDA margin fell 134 basis points to 13.6%, despite the preview’s focus on whether margins could hold or expand. The decline was attributed to scaling investments, wireless-deferral operating leverage, and higher fuel costs, even as total-company margin beat expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Communications adjusted EBITDA margin fell 134 basis points to 13.6%, pressured by scaling investments, wireless deferral operating leverage impacts, and ~35 basis points of higher fuel costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Q2 guide implies roughly 14.9%, flat year over year, after Q1 delivered expansion”; expansion stalling was flagged as a concern.

surprises.description: Building Systems delivered a 24.5% adjusted EBITDA margin, an unusually strong result relative to management’s stated future range of high-teens to low-20s. The preview did not flag this segment-margin outcome, and the company said favorable cost-estimate changes helped.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Building Systems segment delivered exceptional 24.5% adjusted EBITDA margin,” aided by “favorable cost-estimate changes”; future margins were guided to “high-teens to low-20s.”

surprises.description: FY2027 revenue guidance was raised to $7.48–$7.66 billion from $7.38–$7.65 billion. That is a modest raise, with the new upper end just above the preview’s $7.65 billion bar; the midpoint remains slightly below the preview’s roughly $7.59 billion consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY2027 revenue guidance was raised to $7.48–$7.66 billion,” including “~$90 million of second-half revenue from the newly acquired National Technology Integrators.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A simple reiteration would likely be read as a de facto cut. The bar is a raise toward or above $7.65B.”

surprises.description: The company reported more than $1 billion of contracted backlog for long-haul, middle-mile, and inside-data-center fiber, alongside a $20 billion addressable market weighted toward the end of the decade. This longer-term contract and market detail was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Contracted backlog for long-haul, middle-mile and inside data center fiber surpassed $1 billion,” with “hundreds of millions already performed,” targeting a “$20 billion addressable market weighted toward the end of the decade.”

surprises.description: Trailing 12-month free cash flow grew nearly 200% year over year and DSOs improved by seven days. The preview did not set expectations for either cash-flow growth or collections efficiency.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month free cash flow grew nearly 200% year-over-year” and “DSOs improved 7 days to 101.”

surprises.description: The Board approved a new $150 million share-repurchase authorization through February 2028. The preview mentioned buyback pace as a narrative item but gave no expectation of a new authorization or its size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board approved a new $150 million share repurchase authorization through February 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Narrative items: … buyback pace.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $2.01 billion came in modestly above the $1.97–$1.98 billion consensus range and at the high end of company guidance, though it was within the preview’s base-case scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached a record $2.01 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Contract revenues: $1.97B (Zacks); $1.98B (TradingView)”; company guidance “$1.94B – $2.01B.”

in_line: Total backlog reached $12.2 billion, above the preview’s approximately $11.5 billion pass threshold. The reported 1.2x book-to-bill was consistent with the preview’s warning that Q1’s 2.2x rate was unlikely to repeat; no 12-month backlog figure was provided.
Pro forma net leverage was approximately 2.3x, matching the preview’s Q1 reference point of approximately 2.3x.

surprises.description: Q2 net sales declined 2.3%, better than the company’s 3%–5% decline guide and the preview’s roughly 3.4% decline consensus. This was a better result than expected, though the gap was not large.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales declined 2.3% to $1.5 billion, beating guidance of down 5% to down 3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales: −5% to −3%”; consensus “~$1.50B (−3.4%).”

surprises.description: Reported adjusted EPS of $0.62 was far above the preview’s $0.20–$0.25 company guide, but about half of the reported figure came from tariff refunds. Even excluding that one-time benefit, underlying EPS of $0.31 was above the guide range; however, the preview notes that the guide is GAAP, so the comparison with adjusted EPS is not fully like-for-like.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $0.62,” including “~$0.31” from “~$80 million in one-time tariff refunds,” leaving “underlying EPS of $0.31.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS, diluted: $0.20–$0.25 (GAAP)”; consensus “$0.24.” The preview cautions: “The $0.20–$0.25 Q2 guide is GAAP, but the $0.24 consensus is being compared against last year's adjusted $0.37.”

surprises.description: Bath & Body Works raised its full-year adjusted EPS range to $2.60–$2.80 from $2.40–$2.65, a more substantial improvement than the preview’s base case of maintaining the prior range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $2.60-$2.80.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the base case was “Maintaining the $2.40–$2.65 adjusted EPS range.”

surprises.description: The full-year sales outlook improved at the low end: the expected decline was narrowed from 4.5%–2.5% to 4%–2.5%. The high end was unchanged, so the improvement was limited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year net sales guidance was narrowed by raising the low end to down 4% (high end maintained at down 2.5%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales −4.5% to −2.5%”; the preview said a “trim to that range, or narrowing sales to the low end” would be the bear trigger.

surprises.description: Despite the raised full-year EPS range, Q3 guidance calls for adjusted EPS of only $0.07–$0.12, alongside sales down 2.5%–5%. The preview highlighted Q3 guidance as a key debate and calculated that H2 would need to deliver roughly $1.86–$2.11 under the prior full-year range, making the very low Q3 EPS outlook a notable near-term contrast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for net sales down 5% to down 2.5% and adjusted EPS of just $0.07-$0.12.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q3 guidance vs. Street” was a key watch item and calculated that “H2 must deliver roughly $1.86–$2.11 to reach the full-year range.” It did not provide a Q3 consensus estimate.

surprises.description: Management quantified meaningful near-term cost offsets to the tariff refund benefit: about $30 million of forward tariff and input-cost pressure and $35 million of additional consumer-first investment, with most of the investment falling in Q3. The preview anticipated a Q3 spending step-up but did not give these amounts or the Canada-tariff assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The tariff refund benefit is being partially offset by ~$30 million in forward tariff/input cost pressure and ~$35 million of incremental consumer-first investments (70% weighted to Q3), assuming Canada tariffs remain at 50%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “transformation spending steps up in Q3” and flagged tariffs and cost pressure, but gave no comparable dollar estimates.

surprises.description: Owned digital returned to growth for the first time since 2021, improving four percentage points sequentially from Q1 and gaining customers across new, existing, and reactivated groups. The preview did not flag this recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The owned digital business returned to growth for the first time since 2021,” with a “4 percentage points” sequential improvement and gains in “new, existing, and reactivated customers.”

surprises.description: Amazon net sales more than tripled versus Q1, and the company said it was attracting younger, more affluent new-to-brand customers at higher average unit retail. The preview did not identify this channel development as an expectation or key debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Amazon net sales more than tripled versus Q1,” making Bath & Body Works “one of the largest candle brands on the platform,” with younger, more affluent new-to-brand customers “at higher AUR.”

surprises.description: The company expanded into specialty beauty by launching in approximately 600 Ulta Beauty stores during the quarter, a distribution and discovery channel the preview did not mention.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company launched in approximately 600 Ulta Beauty stores during the quarter, expanding into specialty beauty for trial and discovery.”

surprises.description: The Fusion body care launch exceeded sales expectations and generated substantial engagement, while achieving higher AUR than the core assortment. The preview emphasized body care as a key test but did not anticipate this particular launch outperforming.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Fusion body care franchise launch… exceeded sales expectations,” generated “~615 million impressions,” added “over 50,000 social followers,” and delivered “higher AUR than the core assortment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called body care “the largest category and the main test of the turnaround,” but did not give a forecast for Fusion.

surprises.description: Cash and capital plans improved versus the preview: free cash flow guidance rose by $50 million and capex fell by $30 million. The company also redeemed $250 million of 2029 notes and expects to exceed its Fuel for Growth goal by about $25 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised free cash flow guidance to ~$650 million (from $600 million), lowered capex to ~$240 million,” “redeemed $250 million of 2029 notes,” and expects to exceed its Fuel for Growth goal by “~$25 million to ~$200 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Free cash flow about $600M; capex about $270M” and flagged any change to the “~$600M FCF and capital return framework.”

surprises.description: Management said it is targeting revenue growth in 2027, offering a specific growth objective beyond the preview’s discussion of FY2026 guidance and near-term turnaround tests.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is “targeting revenue growth in 2027.”

in_line: The preview expected transformation spending to step up in Q3; management said 70% of the $35 million in incremental consumer-first investments is weighted to Q3.

surprises.description: Q2 net new ARR was $333 million, well above both the $284–286 million company-guidance range and the preview’s $300–310 million buy-side bogey. It exceeded the high end of company guidance by more than $45 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “All-time record net new ARR of $333 million” and “beating the high end of guidance by more than $45 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net new ARR vs. $284–286M guidance and the ~$300M+ buy-side expectation.”

surprises.description: CrowdStrike raised FY27 net new ARR guidance to a $1.355 billion midpoint, above the prior $1.279–1.303 billion range. The increase from the prior midpoint is about $64 million, exceeding the preview’s $40 million threshold for a validating second raise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year FY27 net new ARR guidance to a midpoint of $1.355 billion,” with a “cumulative increase of approximately $116 million” since the initial outlook.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A second raise of $40M+ validates the acceleration thesis.”

surprises.description: Ending ARR reached $5.84 billion, roughly $45–50 million above the preview’s $5.79 billion expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ending ARR reached $5.84 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Ending ARR” consensus was “$5.79B.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating income was $372 million, above the roughly $347 million consensus, and its 25% margin was higher than the preview’s 24.1% estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income hit a record $372 million (25% margin).”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $0.31, a cent above the preview’s $0.29 consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was a record $0.31.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Non-GAAP EPS consensus was “$0.29.”

surprises.description: Q2 free-cash-flow margin was 26%, above the roughly 24.5% margin implied by the preview’s seasonal-trough framing. The company also reported record free cash flow of $377 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was a record $377 million (26% of revenue).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Margins and FCF at the seasonal trough,” with guidance implying “~24.5% FCF margin.”

surprises.description: Flex adoption was stronger than the preview’s concern about possible deceleration: CrowdStrike added more than 935 new Flex accounts in Q2, exceeding the prior three quarters combined, and all of its ten largest deals by value were Flex deals.
surprises.fact_evidence: “More than 935 new Flex accounts added—exceeding the prior three quarters combined”; “the top 10 deals by value all being Flex.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Flex account growth” was identified as a mechanism behind net new ARR, and “deceleration here undercuts the story.”

surprises.description: The call quantified strong Flex conversion and repeat-reflex economics: converters had more than 40% average ending ARR uplift, and customers that reflexed at least twice had ending ARR 53% above their initial Flex baseline. The preview flagged ReFlex economics as important but gave no expected uplift figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customers converting to Flex saw an average ending ARR uplift of more than 40%,” and twice-reflexed customers had ending ARR “53% higher than their initial Flex baseline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Falcon Flex / ReFlex economics” were a key metric to watch; “ReFlex uplift” was described as a mechanism behind net new ARR.

surprises.description: AIDR ending ARR nearly tripled versus Q1, but the call still did not provide the AIDR dollar figure the preview said investors needed. The rapid sequential growth is encouraging, while the requested dollar disclosure remains absent.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AIDR ending ARR nearly tripled versus Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Investors need a disclosed dollar figure, not percentages.”

in_line: The company reaffirmed at least 30% full-year FY27 free-cash-flow margin, as the preview cited that threshold in its FY27 guidance.
Flex ARR grew 101% year over year, close to the preview’s cited 99% growth rate.

surprises.description: Q4 sales were $151.8 million, essentially flat year over year, rather than the 3%–4% decline the preview expected; sales also exceeded the $146.8 million consensus. The smaller-than-expected decline reflected OEM production falling only 1.4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fourth-quarter net sales of $151.8 million were essentially flat year-over-year but beat the company's original 3%-4% decline estimate, as actual OEM production fell only 1.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 revenue $146.8M”; company guidance was “Q4 revenue down 3–4% y/y, or $145.9M–$147.4M.”

surprises.description: Q4 earnings were mixed against the preview: GAAP EPS of $0.95 was below the $1.36 consensus, but adjusted EPS of $2.06 was above the preview’s $1.25–$1.55 base-case range and held steady year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income dropped to $3.9 million ($0.95) from $8.3 million ($2.01) though adjusted EPS held steady at $2.06.”
