surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) Q4 FY26 Consensus: $1.36”; the preview’s base scenario estimated “Adj. EPS $1.25–1.55.”

surprises.description: Management’s FY2027 production outlook was specifically weak at its largest customers: North American production is forecast to fall about 2%, and production at the three largest customers nearly 6%. The preview anticipated a cautious FY2027 framing, but did not identify declines of this size at those customers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guides to softer fiscal 2027 conditions, forecasting an approximately 2% decline in North American production and a nearly 6% decline at its three largest customers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “cautious FY27” in its base scenario and described FY2027 framing as a key debate, but gave no production decline estimates.

surprises.description: Full-year revenue came in above the preview’s implied estimate: $579.4 million versus roughly $573.5–$575.0 million. That is a modest upward difference from the preview’s calculation, not just growth versus the prior year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Strattec delivered record annual revenue of $579.4 million in fiscal 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied FY2026 ... gives roughly $573.5M–$575.0M.”

surprises.description: FY2026 restructuring savings were somewhat higher than the preview’s indicated run-rate implied: the preview reported $4.6 million year to date and an additional $0.8 million annualized benefit starting in Q4, while management reported about $6 million realized for FY2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restructuring actions have delivered $9.5 million in cumulative savings since fiscal 2025, including about $6 million realized in fiscal 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$4.6M YTD, including $1.9M in Q3”; “An incremental $0.8M annualized from Mexico restructuring starts in Q4.”

surprises.description: Management newly said it is pursuing M&A to gain scale and diversify its customer base; the preview discussed customer concentration and EV-program cancellations but did not flag M&A as a plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is “pursuing M&A for scale and customer diversification.”

in_line: The longer-term gross-margin target remains 18%–20% assuming the peso returns to its five-year average, consistent with the preview’s stated target and peso assumption.
The $40 million repurchase authorization was already disclosed in the preview; the amount of Q4 execution was a new disclosure, but the preview did not provide an expected buyback amount or pace.
The broadly cautious FY2027 framing was consistent with the preview’s base-case expectation of cautious FY2027 commentary.

surprises.description: Ooma’s FY2027 outlook was raised well above the prior range: revenue is now $332–333.5 million versus $326–328.5 million, and non-GAAP EPS is $1.35–$1.38 versus $1.29–$1.34. The preview said a raise to at least $328 million and $1.33 EPS was needed to avoid a stall, so the new range clears that bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: Full-year fiscal 2027 guidance projects revenue of $332–333.5 million and non-GAAP EPS of $1.35–$1.38.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Full-year FY2027 revenue: $326.0M–$328.5M; non-GAAP EPS: $1.29–$1.34. The preview also said a raise to at least $328M and $1.33 EPS was needed to avoid reading as a stall.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $83.2 million beat the practical high-end bar of $82.3 million by $0.9 million, and also exceeded the roughly $80.2 million Street consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue reached $83.2 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 company guidance was $81.6M–$82.3M; the preview said to treat the high end of guidance (~$82.3M) as the practical bar. Street consensus was ~$80.2M.

surprises.description: The 25% headline revenue increase was largely acquisition-driven: excluding acquisitions, total revenue grew only 8%. The preview emphasized organic business subscription growth as a key test, with 10% or more considered supportive, so the reported underlying growth figure was softer than that expectation, though it is a different revenue measure.
surprises.fact_evidence: Excluding acquisitions, total revenue grew only 8% year-over-year, indicating FluentStream and Phone.com drove the majority of the 25% headline growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 organic business subscription growth was 9% and that a print of 10% or more would support the plan; it also flagged whether headline growth was mostly acquisition-driven.

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $0.35, above the preview’s practical high-end bar of $0.34; non-GAAP net income of $10.2 million also topped the high end of the $9.4–$9.8 million guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Non-GAAP net income grew 58% to $10.2 million ($0.35 diluted EPS).
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance was $0.33–$0.34, with the preview treating the high end ($0.34) as the practical bar. Non-GAAP net income guidance was $9.4M–$9.8M.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $12.4 million, slightly above the preview’s implied range of roughly $11.5–$12.0 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 adjusted EBITDA hit a record $12.4 million (15% of revenue).
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA was not guided for Q2; the preview implied ~$11.5M–$12.0M from the FY guide and Q1 actual.

surprises.description: Residential users increased by more than 3,000, reversing the historical decline, and the FY2027 residential revenue outlook moved from a 1–2% decline to flat-to-1% growth. The preview expected residential subscription to be flat to down 1% and called a second straight quarter of user growth a meaningful change.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company added over 3,000 residential users, driven largely by MyPhone; residential revenue outlook was raised from a 1–2% decline to flat-to-1% growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The FY27 plan assumed residential subscription was flat to down 1%; the preview said a second straight quarter of user growth would be a meaningful change.

surprises.description: The call disclosed that business-user growth was only 4,000 after 4,000 users of IWG churn and a one-time count correction; without those effects, growth would have been 11,000. The preview focused on strong organic business growth but did not set a business-user count expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Business user growth was dampened by 4,000 users of IWG churn and a one-time count correction, without which business users would have grown 11,000 instead of the reported 4,000.

surprises.description: Ooma reported blended ARPU of $16.95, up 8% year-over-year, despite the preview saying it did not disclose ARPU and that investors should not expect the metric. The growth itself was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Blended ARPU rose 8% year-over-year to $16.95.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Ooma does not disclose net dollar retention or ARPU, so do not expect those metrics.”

surprises.description: The company reported record trailing-12-month free cash flow of $30.2 million, a cash-generation milestone the preview did not identify as an expected result.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company generated record trailing-12-month free cash flow of $30.2 million.

surprises.description: Ooma repurchased $17.6 million of shares over four quarters, an additional capital-return detail not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company spent $17.6 million on buybacks over four quarters.

surprises.description: Debt paydown was substantial: Ooma repaid $6.5 million in Q2 and reduced debt to $47 million from $53.5 million, exceeding the prior quarter’s $5 million repayment pace that the preview highlighted for monitoring.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company paid down debt to $47 million from a $6.5 million Q2 repayment.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that Ooma had paid down $5M of term debt in Q1 to $53.5M and flagged the FY27 term-debt paydown pace as an item to watch.

in_line: FY2027 business subscription growth guidance of approximately 32% was broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of about 31%.

surprises.description: Salesforce raised FY27 revenue guidance instead of maintaining it, as the preview considered possible. The increase is partly acquisition-driven—$200 million from anticipated Contentful and Fin closings versus $100 million organic—so it is a positive revision but not a large organic-growth upgrade.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised FY27 revenue guidance by $300 million in constant currency to $46.1–$46.4 billion, comprising $100 million organic and $200 million from the anticipated Contentful and Fin closings, partially offset by a $100 million FX headwind.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A maintained revenue guide after May's raise would be read as a sign that H2 organic reacceleration is not happening.”

surprises.description: Q2 CRPO growth was stronger than the preview's roughly 13% constant-currency guide: it reached 14%, a one-point beat. The preview had specifically identified 14% or better as a clean beat on the downgrade thesis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CRPO accelerated to $33.5 billion, up 14% in constant currency and one point ahead of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guide is ~13% cc”; “At ≥14% cc, that is a clean beat.”

surprises.description: The Q3 CRPO outlook was approximately 14%, better than the preview's stated concern that a sub-13% guide would undercut the H2 reacceleration story.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue is guided to $11.42–$11.5 billion (11–12% constant currency growth) with CRPO growth of approximately 14%, excluding contributions from Contentful and Fin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A sub-13% guide undercuts H2 reacceleration regardless of Q2.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was slightly above consensus, though the difference was small and the result was at the top of the stated company range. The preview's base scenario was somewhat higher than the reported figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY27 revenue reached $11.35 billion,” and the call facts describe it as above the high end of guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus was “$11.33B”; the base scenario was “$11.36–11.40B.” The preview listed company guidance of “$11.27–11.35B.”

surprises.description: The call supplied stronger-than-quantified evidence of AI and data adoption: Agentforce ARR reached $1.5 billion, AI and data ARR was nearing $4 billion, and production agent usage and bookings were growing rapidly. The preview had highlighted AI monetization and usage conversion as an open question but gave no comparable Q2 targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Agentforce ARR reached $1.5 billion and combined AI and data ARR is about to cross $4 billion”; accounts running agents in production were up 70% quarter-over-quarter, with 2,000 new paying customers. Agentic uses were up 97% QoQ and Agentforce bookings more than doubled QoQ.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AI monetization quality: new-logo vs. expansion split, and AWU consumption-to-revenue conversion.”

surprises.description: Salesforce reported unusually strong customer economics: its strongest net new AOV growth in four years alongside near-record-low attrition. The preview emphasized the risk of organic growth deceleration but did not anticipate these specific customer metrics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Salesforce reported the strongest net new AOV growth in four years alongside near-record-low attrition”; agentic-journey customers reach roughly 2x AOV initially, with potential to reach 3–4x.

surprises.description: Salesforce announced Claudeforce with Anthropic, a new route to premium-edition upgrades that the preview did not mention. The opportunity is tempered by the fact that only 5% of sales/service knowledge workers have upgraded so far.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company launched Claudeforce with Anthropic, targeting general availability in September at Dreamforce,” with premium editions carrying a 60–80% pricing premium; only 5% of sales/service knowledge workers have upgraded so far.

in_line: Non-GAAP operating margin of 34.1% and GAAP operating margin of 20.5% were broadly in line with the preview's estimates of approximately 34% and 20–21%, respectively.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $757 million, above both the $725–745 million guidance range and roughly $738 million consensus. FY26 revenue also finished at $2.854 billion, just above the $2.82–2.84 billion full-year guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue reached a record $757 million, exceeding the guided range of $725-745 million,” and “full-year FY26 revenue was $2.854 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 FY26 guidance” was “$725–745M” and consensus was “~$738.3M”; FY26 guidance was “revenue $2.82–2.84B.”

surprises.description: Q4 non-GAAP operating margin reached 26.2%, well above the 21–23% guidance range and the preview’s roughly 22.5% consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 non-GAAP operating margin was 26.2%, well above the guided 21-23% range due to lower opex from hiring timing and higher revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q4 non-GAAP operating margin guidance was “21–23%” and consensus was “~22.5%.”

surprises.description: FY26 free cash flow was $841 million, exceeding the $760–780 million full-year guide by a substantial amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY26 free cash flow was $841 million (29% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 full-year guidance ... FCF $760–780M.”

surprises.description: Ending ARR was $2.549 billion, above the preview’s estimated $2.52–2.54 billion, and its 16% growth rate accelerated in Q4 rather than continuing the slowdown flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY26 ending ARR was $2.549 billion, up 16% year-over-year, with the growth rate accelerating in Q4 versus the prior quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave “my estimate ~$2.52–2.54B” and noted ARR growth “has slowed each quarter”; it said “holding about 14% growth” would require a seasonally strong Q4 add.

surprises.description: FY27 operating-margin guidance of 24–25% points to improvement, whereas the preview expected a flat-to-down margin guide amid AI investment; the midpoint is also above the preview’s 23% leverage marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 revenue guidance of $3.18-3.23 billion ... with non-GAAP operating margin of 24-25%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said investment “could support a flat-to-down margin guide” and that “a margin at or above 23% would point to leverage.”

surprises.description: The $4.34 Q4 GAAP EPS included a one-time $1.2 billion tax valuation allowance release; excluding it, GAAP EPS would have been $0.21. The preview supplied only a non-GAAP EPS estimate, so there is no comparable GAAP consensus, but this unusually large one-off benefit was not flagged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 GAAP EPS of $4.34 included a onetime $1.2 billion tax valuation allowance release; excluding it, GAAP EPS would have been $0.21.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a restructuring affecting about 5% of its global workforce, with $33–43 million in one-time charges; most savings are to be reinvested in AI, cloud native, and sales expansion. The preview had not anticipated this action or its charges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed a restructuring affecting approximately 5% of its global workforce, incurring $33-43 million in nonrecurring charges with the majority of savings reinvested into AI, cloud native, and sales expansion.”

surprises.description: External storage bookings rose sharply quarter over quarter, with several seven-figure ACV deals; limited-availability NetApp support helped secure multiple large Q4 wins. This product-area strength was not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “External storage bookings saw a sharp quarter-over-quarter increase with several 7-figure ACV deals, and NetApp support (in limited availability) was instrumental in multiple large Q4 wins.”

surprises.description: Q4 average billing duration was slightly below expectations, indicating a modest shortfall on this operating metric.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 average billing duration was 3.3 years (slightly below expectations).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call described the 3.3-year result as “slightly below expectations.”

in_line: FY27 revenue guidance of $3.18–3.23 billion has a $3.205 billion midpoint, essentially matching the preview’s roughly $3.20 billion consensus.

TCV bookings grew in the high teens for FY26, still outpacing 12% revenue growth; management attributed the gap partly to server supply-chain delays and future-start licensing, consistent with the preview’s focus on timing-related bookings-to-revenue conversion.
NRR remained at 106%, unchanged quarter over quarter, matching the prior-quarter level cited in the preview.

surprises.description: Design IP revenue was $474 million, below the preview’s $487.4 million consensus estimate by about 3%, despite returning to year-over-year growth. That missed the preview’s key Design IP revenue catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Design IP segment returned to growth with revenue of $474 million, up approximately 11% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Design IP revenue, Q3 … $487.4M”; the catalyst checklist said “Design IP at or above $487M.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue of $2.477 billion exceeded both the $2.44 billion consensus and the top of company guidance at $2.46 billion, a stronger result than the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue reached $2.477 billion … beating the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue, Q3 … $2.44B” consensus and company guidance of “$2,410–2,460M.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS came in well above the preview’s $3.67 consensus and the $3.69 top of guidance. The 41.6% non-GAAP operating margin also exceeded guidance, though it was broadly near the preview’s roughly 41% margin level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was $3.91 with a non-GAAP operating margin of 41.6%, both exceeding guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS, Q3 … $3.67” consensus and company guidance of “$3.63–$3.69”; the preview said operating margin “is around 41%.”

surprises.description: Synopsys raised full-year revenue guidance by $50 million and lifted the midpoint of non-GAAP EPS guidance by $0.31, rather than merely reaffirming or tightening the prior outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance by $0.31 at the midpoint to $15.04-$15.10 and lifted full-year revenue guidance $50 million to $9.69-$9.74 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said full-year guidance was “to be reaffirmed or revised,” and its bull scenario included “FY26 raised.” Prior guidance was revenue of “$9,625–9,705M” and non-GAAP EPS of “$14.72–14.80.”

surprises.description: The backlog slipped from $11 billion to $10.9 billion, which was weaker than a flat or growing backlog signal. Management attributed the modest decline to the processor IP solutions divestiture, rather than identifying underlying demand weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog remained strong at $10.9 billion but declined modestly quarter-over-quarter due to the divestiture of the processor IP solutions business that closed during Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Backlog was $11B at Q2”; the preview said “A flat or falling Synopsys backlog against that comparison would read as share loss.”

surprises.description: Management gave a substantially stronger cash-flow outlook, raising free cash flow guidance by $600 million and cash-from-operations guidance by $500 million, while lowering planned CapEx. The preview did not flag a cash-flow outlook change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow guidance was raised $600 million to approximately $2.6 billion, with cash from operations guidance up $500 million to about $2.8 billion and CapEx reduced to approximately $225 million.”

surprises.description: Management now expects EDA to accelerate from 8.5% year-over-year growth in Q3 to double-digit organic growth in Q4 and for full-year 2026. The preview did not identify this acceleration as an expected development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EDA revenue grew 8.5% year-over-year against a tough 16% prior-year comparison, and management expects EDA to accelerate to double-digit organic growth in Q4 and for full-year 2026.”

surprises.description: Synopsys launched its first joint Synopsys-ANSYS multiphysics Fusion solution, with customer-validated design-closure improvements of up to 10x, but said it does not expect revenue contribution until 2027. The product launch was not anticipated in the preview, and the revenue timing limits the near-term benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The first joint Synopsys-ANSYS multiphysics Fusion solution launched in Q3 with customer-validated results of up to 10x faster design closure, but revenue contribution is not expected to begin until 2027.”

surprises.description: The call added unusually strong product-win data not highlighted in the preview: hardware-assisted verification revenue reached a record, and IP wins included more than 95% of PCIe 7 opportunities and 25 LPDDR6 designs year-to-date.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record hardware-assisted verification revenue, securing 12 new and 66 repeat HAV customer wins in the quarter”; “over 95% of PCIe 7 opportunities won” and “25 LPDDR6 design wins year-to-date.”

in_line: Design IP returned to year-over-year growth, consistent with the preview’s expectation that it would continue improving through the second half, although revenue fell short of consensus.
The 41.6% operating margin was broadly consistent with the preview’s description of margin around 41%, and remained below the stated mid-40s ambition.

surprises.description: NVIDIA reported Q2 revenue of $96 billion, about $4 billion above the roughly $92 billion consensus and above the preview’s base case. That also means revenue grew more than 100% year over year, rather than the roughly 96–98% implied by the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 fiscal 2027 total revenue reached a record $96 billion, more than doubling year-over-year, with growth accelerating for the fourth consecutive quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus” revenue was “$91.9–92.3B”; consensus Q2 revenue implied “about +96–98% y/y.”

surprises.description: The Q3 revenue outlook is $108 billion, roughly $4 billion above the preview’s $103.8–104.1 billion consensus and above its $103–105 billion catalyst range. It reaches the preview’s bull-case threshold, rather than its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue is guided to $108 billion (plus or minus 2%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 FY27 revenue guide” consensus was “$103.8–104.1B”; the catalyst checklist called out “Q3 guide versus $103–105B.”

surprises.description: The margin outlook is materially weaker than the preview’s roughly 75% expectation: management expects 74% in Q3, a 71–72% bottom in Q4, and only 72–73% in FY2028. The preview discussed a possible drift toward 73.5% in its bear case, but not a Q4 trough at 71–72% or an FY2028 range that low.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margins are being reset lower due to extreme memory pricing, with Q3 expected at 74%, bottoming at 71-72% in Q4, then settling at 72-73% in fiscal 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected gross margin of “~75%” and described a bear case of “GM drifting toward 73.5%.”

surprises.description: Data Center revenue reached $89 billion, about $3 billion above the preview’s roughly $85.7 billion estimate. Within the segment, AC I&E grew faster sequentially than hyperscale, providing evidence of broadening beyond hyperscale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 data center revenue rose 18% sequentially to $89 billion, with hyperscale at $49 billion (up 13% QoQ) and AC I&E at $40 billion (up 25% QoQ and 138% YoY).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Data Center revenue at “~$85.7B” and said “continued ACIE broadening is a positive.”

surprises.description: Management quantified a substantial Vera Rubin contribution in Q3: about 20% of Data Center revenue. The preview expected Q3 shipments to start but did not anticipate a contribution of that size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Vera Rubin expected to account for about 20% of data center revenue” in Q3.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “flagged Q3 shipment start” and asked for Vera specifics including “units, customers, timing, and margin profile.”

surprises.description: Management gave a new FY2028 growth outlook of approximately 70%, while saying supply—not demand—is the constraint: unconstrained demand would support roughly 100% growth. The preview identified the FY2028 slope as an issue to watch but provided no such growth forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided fiscal 2028 revenue growth of approximately 70%, describing it as supply-constrained since unconstrained demand points to roughly 100% (doubling) growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Rubin commentary would “set[] the FY28 slope,” but gave no FY2028 revenue-growth estimate.

surprises.description: NVIDIA disclosed a large customer-financing ecosystem that the preview did not anticipate: nearly $50 billion invested in Frontier AI labs and partnerships aimed at raising more than $500 billion in third-party financing. Management also expects AI labs that use NVIDIA’s balance sheet to generate about one-quarter of next year’s business, making this a significant new demand channel with notable balance-sheet involvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NVIDIA has invested nearly $50 billion in Frontier AI labs and partnered with six capital providers … to raise over $500 billion in third-party financing”; AI labs leveraging NVIDIA’s balance sheet are expected to contribute “roughly one-quarter of next year’s business.”

surprises.description: NVIDIA revealed an unusually large AWS deployment commitment and a near-term Vera CPU shipment start, neither of which was anticipated in the preview. This adds customer and product detail beyond the preview’s general focus on Rubin timing and demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AWS is deploying an additional 2 million GPUs from this quarter through Q2 fiscal 2029, and AWS begins receiving Vera CPU shipments this quarter.”

surprises.description: Management said revenue opportunity per gigawatt has risen from about $18 billion with Hopper to $25 billion with Blackwell and $40 billion with Vera Rubin, with further increases expected. The preview did not discuss this expanding revenue potential from each gigawatt of capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NVIDIA's revenue opportunity per gigawatt has expanded from ~$18 billion with Hopper to $25 billion with Blackwell to $40 billion with Vera Rubin, and is expected to rise further.”

in_line: China compute revenue remained excluded from the forward outlook, as the preview said company guidance excluded China and its base case assumed China would remain excluded. Q2 H200 shipments were less than 1% of Data Center revenue and were dilutive to gross margins.

surprises.description: Okta reported new products at about 30% of Q2 bookings, with deals including a new product carrying about 40% higher average ACV. The preview noted new products were 25% of Q1 bookings but did not forecast a further increase or the ACV uplift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New products represented approximately 30% of bookings in Q2, with an average ACV uplift of about 40% when any new product is included in a deal, and Okta Identity Governance was the leading contributor.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New products about 25% of Q1 bookings.”

surprises.description: Okta had concrete AI-agent deal activity—dozens of deals, including several over $1 million—rather than only qualitative commentary. But management said the business is still too small to register in revenue, limiting the significance of that evidence.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Okta closed dozens of Okta for AI agents deals including several worth over $1 million, but management stated this remains too small to show up in the ~$3 billion revenue base.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for hard numbers on agent-identity bookings, ACV, pipeline, or customer counts. Qualitative-only commentary is the most likely disappointment.”

surprises.description: Okta completed an unpreviewed acquisition of Premiso, adding an identity security platform with 400 native risk detections versus Okta’s existing 90. The strategic capability is clear, but the facts provide no financial contribution or deal terms.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Okta completed its acquisition of Premiso, an identity security platform offering 400 native risk detections versus Okta's existing 90, to strengthen its AI security and agentic runtime controls.”

surprises.description: Okta paid the remaining $350 million of convertible notes in cash, leaving no convertible debt. The preview mentioned an active buyback and $2.589 billion of prior-quarter cash, but did not anticipate this debt settlement; the call also reported $2.3 billion in cash and investments after the payment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Okta settled the remaining $350 million of convertible notes in cash in June, leaving no convertible debt, ended the quarter with about $2.3 billion in cash and investments, and repurchased 1.5 million shares for $125 million with $555 million remaining under its $1 billion buyback.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “cash $2.589B; buyback active”

surprises.description: Management described a substantial unmet need for agent security, citing a survey that 81% of CISOs know they are exposed but lack an adequate platform. It also said the largest Q3 deal was in U.S. Federal, even though the federal/public-sector business is under 10% of the company.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A customer survey cited that 81% of CISOs are aware they are exposed with agents deployed but lack an adequate security platform, and management said federal/public sector is under 10% of the business with the largest Q3 deal being in U.S. Federal.”

surprises.description: The preview expected FY27 operating margin of 25–26% and free-cash-flow margin of 27–28%; Okta’s updated guidance was 26% and 28–29%, respectively. The reported ranges therefore raised the expected margin outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Okta guided FY27 total revenue growth to 10-11% with non-GAAP operating margin of 26% and free cash flow margin of 28-29%.”

in_line: Q2 non-GAAP operating margin guidance was 26%, matching the preview’s stated company guidance of 26%.

Current RPO growth accelerated, consistent with the preview’s expectation that a second consecutive quarter of acceleration was the core debate; the facts do not provide a Q2 RPO amount to compare with the preview’s $2.53 billion bar.
Q3 current RPO growth guidance of 11–12% was around the preview’s roughly 11% threshold for avoiding a stall in the acceleration story.
The approximately 1-point FY27 revenue-guidance drag from shifting professional services to GSI partners was already identified in the preview as an expected headwind.

surprises.description: Q2 comparable sales grew 4.1%, well above the preview’s roughly 1.0–1.5% consensus and above its 2–3.5% whisper range. That also substantially exceeded the company’s approximately 1% guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 comparable sales grew 4.1%, significantly beating guidance of approximately 1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Enterprise comparable sales ~+1.0–1.5%”; the preview also flagged a “~+2% to +3.5% whisper” against the “~+1% guide.”

surprises.description: Best Buy raised its full-year outlook more strongly than the preview’s base case anticipated: comps are now expected to grow 1.9–3% and adjusted EPS is $6.70–$6.90, versus the preview’s expected raise to roughly 1–2% comps and $6.45–$6.70 EPS. The new revenue outlook of $42.3–$42.8 billion is also above the prior $41.2–$42.1 billion range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Best Buy raised full-year fiscal 2027 guidance to comparable sales growth of 1.9%-3%, adjusted EPS of $6.70-$6.90, and revenue of $42.3-$42.8 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The preview's base case is a raise to comps +1% to +2% and adjusted EPS $6.45–6.70.” The guide in force was revenue “$41.2–42.1B; comps -1% to +1%; adjusted EPS $6.30–6.60.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS of $1.47 exceeded the preview’s $1.34–$1.38 consensus range, although it was just below the preview’s bull-case range. The year-over-year increase was stronger than the preview’s consensus estimates implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS rose 15% year-over-year to $1.47.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS $1.34–$1.38 (mid ~$1.36).”

surprises.description: Revenue of $9.8 billion came in above the preview’s $9.58–$9.59 billion consensus, and also above its base-case revenue range of $9.62–$9.70 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue of $9.8 billion (up 3.6% year-over-year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Enterprise revenue $9.58–9.59B”; the base scenario was “$9.62–9.70B.”

surprises.description: The adjusted operating income rate was 4.3%, compared with the preview’s approximately 3.9% expectation. Its roughly 40-basis-point year-over-year expansion was therefore stronger than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income rate of 4.3%, up roughly 40 basis points versus last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted operating income rate ~3.9%.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a $34 million tariff-refund benefit in gross profit and assumed similar IEEPA refunds in Q3, neither of which the preview anticipated. Management also expects full-year gross margin to improve 30–40 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit rate expansion included a $34 million tariff refund benefit, with similar IEEPA refunds assumed in Q3; full-year gross margin expected to improve 30-40 basis points.”

surprises.description: Marketplace GMV was about $300 million in Q2 and the full-year expectation rose to $1.3 billion, above the preview’s cited FY27 target of at least $1.2 billion. The plan to add international sellers later this quarter was also not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The domestic marketplace generated ~$300 million GMV in Q2, with full-year GMV now expected to reach $1.3 billion, and international sellers being added later this quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Marketplace did ~$250M GMV in Q1 against a ≥$1.2B FY27 target.”

surprises.description: Computing remained comp-positive for a tenth straight quarter, but management expects its growth to slow in the back half as it laps the Windows 10 end-of-support tailwind. The preview noted the positive streak but did not flag this slowdown or the reported unit weakness from memory-cost-driven price increases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Computing delivered its tenth consecutive quarter of positive comps, but management expects growth to slow in the back half as it laps the Windows 10 end-of-support tailwind.” Also: “Memory cost increases drove computing ASPs up mid-teens while units declined high single digits, a dynamic expected to persist through the rest of the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Computing (9-quarter positive comp streak).”

surprises.description: Emerging categories including AI glasses, trading cards and health rings more than doubled year over year and now contribute about one point of comp, an area the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Emerging categories including AI glasses, trading cards and health rings more than doubled year-over-year and now contribute about 1 point of comp.”

surprises.description: Domestic TV sales grew more than 10% year over year, while August comps were tracking at the high end of the 1–3% guidance range. The preview flagged home theater as a swing factor and anticipated cautious H2 framing, but did not indicate this strength.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Domestic TV sales grew more than 10% year-over-year, and Q3-to-date comps in August are tracking at the high end of the 1%-3% guidance range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “home theater, where the RGB TV launch in mid-June is the swing factor,” and said its base case included “cautious H2 language.”

surprises.description: Higher incentive compensation is adding about $130 million to full-year SG&A year over year, a cost pressure the preview did not flag. Management expects it to reset lower next year, by roughly $100 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Incentive compensation is pressuring SG&A, increasing approximately $130 million year-over-year for full year, and is expected to reset lower (~$100 million reduction) next year.”

in_line: Computing remained comp-positive, consistent with the preview’s note of a nine-quarter positive-comp streak; the reported result extended that streak to ten quarters.

surprises.description: HP reported Q3 revenue of $15.7 billion, well above the preview’s consensus range of $14.39–$14.60 billion and even above its $15.2 billion bull-scenario ceiling. Revenue rose 13% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q3 revenue of $15.7 billion, up 13% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 FY26 Consensus” revenue was “$14.60B (Zacks) or $14.39B (TradingView)”; the bull scenario was “$14.9–15.2B.”

surprises.description: Q3 non-GAAP EPS was $0.83, above the preview’s highest cited consensus of $0.72 and the company’s $0.71 guidance ceiling. The $0.11 tariff-refund benefit helped, but EPS still exceeded the guidance ceiling excluding that benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was $0.83, up 11%, and included $0.11 from tariff refunds, though EPS still exceeded the top of guidance even excluding that benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus was “$0.66 (Zacks), $0.69 (TradingView), $0.72 (AlphaStreet)”; company guidance was “$0.61–$0.71.”

surprises.description: HP raised FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance to $3.19–$3.29 from $2.90–$3.10, reversing the preview’s concern about another downward revision. The new range includes an estimated $0.19 tariff-refund benefit for the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HP raised full-year EPS guidance to $3.19–$3.29 (from $2.90–$3.10) … including $0.19 of estimated tariff refund benefit for the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026” company guide was “$2.90–$3.10”; the preview said “A third downward revision would break the pattern of beating the quarter and trimming the year” and identified a floor raise to $3.00 or more as the bull trigger.

surprises.description: HP raised FY2026 free-cash-flow guidance to $3.0–$3.2 billion from $2.8–$3.0 billion. The preview had not anticipated a higher range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[HP] raised … free cash flow guidance to $3.0–$3.2 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow” company guide was “$2.8–$3.0B.”

surprises.description: Personal Systems revenue grew strongly, but unit declines deepened to about 16%, versus a 7% decline in the prior quarter cited in the preview. The preview flagged consumer units as an early warning for price-driven demand loss, making the sharper volume drop a weak point behind the revenue growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Personal Systems revenue hit a record $11.8 billion, up 18%, with commercial up 22% and consumer up 10%, despite units declining ~16%, driven by pricing, premium mix, and services.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported that Q2 Personal Systems units “fell 7%, so growth was price/mix” and said, “Consumer units are the early warning sign for price-driven demand loss.”

surprises.description: HP generated over $1.7 billion of operating cash flow and about $1.6 billion of free cash flow in Q3, while paying down over $500 million of debt and returning nearly $600 million to shareholders. That was a strong capital-return outcome despite the preview’s concern that memory inventory might absorb cash.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HP generated over $1.7 billion in operating cash flow and ~$1.6 billion free cash flow in Q3, paid down over $500 million in debt, and returned nearly $600 million to shareholders (over $1.5 billion year-to-date).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “Watch whether cash goes into memory inventory at the expense of near-term capital returns” and cited Q2 buybacks of “$100M.”

surprises.description: HP disclosed a new three-year, $100 million agreement with print services provider RRD, which the preview had not flagged. The call also highlighted 46% growth in key growth areas and 42% tank-printer unit growth with four points of share gain, for which the preview gave no specific expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Key growth areas grew 46% year-over-year, tank printers achieved 42% unit growth with 4 points of share gain, and HP signed a 3-year, $100 million agreement with print services provider RRD.”

in_line: Personal Systems operating margin was 4.6%, close to the preview’s expected 4.3–4.7% base range and roughly its 4.5% watchpoint. The preview also expected Q4 to be the low point before improvement into FY27, matching the call’s outlook.
Q4 EPS guidance of $0.69–$0.79 includes $0.08 of tariff-refund benefit; excluding it, the range is $0.61–$0.71, with a midpoint of $0.66, close to the preview’s roughly $0.67 implied Q4 EPS.
Print operating margin was 18.1%, near the preview’s 18.3% reference and above its sub-18% downside threshold. HP said the margin excluding tariff refunds was at the low end of its long-term range.

surprises.description: CSI Solar disclosed more than 13 GW-peak of contracted backlog for U.S.-made HJT and TOPCon modules, worth over $4.5 billion with deliveries through 2029; the preview did not identify a comparable module backlog expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CSI Solar has secured over 13 GW-peak of contracted backlog for domestically manufactured HJT and TOPCon modules valued at more than $4.5 billion, with deliveries through 2029.”

surprises.description: e-STORAGE shipped 3.7 GWh and recognized revenue on 3.3 GWh, exceeding the previewed Q2 storage guidance of 2.8–3.2 GWh.
surprises.fact_evidence: “e-STORAGE shipped 3.7 GWh and recognized revenue on 3.3 GWh, exceeding guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Storage: 2.8–3.2 GWh (including ~0.4 GWh internal)”

surprises.description: Jeffersonville became the first commercially operational U.S. HJT cell facility, with Phase 1 ramping to 2.1 GW-peak. The preview looked for a first commercial module delivery in Q3, so commercial operation is ahead of that stated milestone, though full production is still targeted for October 1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company opened the first commercially operational HJT solar cell facility in the US (Jeffersonville), ramping Phase 1 to 2.1 GW-peak with full production October 1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Jeffersonville Phase I (2.1 GW) first commercial module delivery is targeted for Q3'26. Confirmation or a slip would matter.”

surprises.description: Management said Section 232-related polysilicon pricing adjustments are not included in the existing 13 GW backlog and are expected to lift contract values as agreements are renegotiated, creating potential value on top of the disclosed backlog.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 13 GW backlog does not yet include any Section 232 polysilicon pricing adjustments, which management expects will push contract values upward as agreements are renegotiated.”

surprises.description: Management expects the company to qualify for Section 232 tariff/MIP exemptions based on its U.S. manufacturing investments and described the policy as accretive even without full rebates. The preview focused on FEOC and 45X eligibility, not this policy benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects to qualify for Section 232 tariff/MIP exemptions tied to its US manufacturing investments and views the policy as net positive and accretive to CSI Solar even without full rebates due to higher US module pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FEOC / Prohibited Foreign Entity status and 45X eligibility. Any definitive commentary on these would be a major change in the story.”

surprises.description: Recurrent Energy reported only $117 million of revenue and a $19 million operating loss, with project sales deferred and a $24 million impairment on an upcoming Latin America sale. The preview flagged project-sale timing and impairment as risks, but the call confirmed those pressures were affecting results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recurrent Energy generated only $117 million of revenue and a $19 million operating loss, dragged by deferred project sales and a $24 million impairment on an upcoming Latin America project sale.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for capital recycling or Recurrent project sales”; the bear scenario cited “impairment or FX loss” and “Recurrent losses widen.”

surprises.description: The manufacturing segment posted a $49 million operating loss. The preview highlighted the Jeffersonville ramp as a catalyst but did not indicate an expected segment loss of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The manufacturing segment posted a $49 million operating loss.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “HJT ramp. Jeffersonville Phase I (2.1 GW) first commercial module delivery is targeted for Q3'26.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue reached $1.2 billion, at the high end of company guidance and above the preview’s roughly $1.17 billion consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached $1.2 billion at the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: ~$1.17B”; company Q2 guidance was “$1.0–1.2B.”

in_line: Q2 gross margin was 13.9%, within the previewed 13–15% guidance range and reported as in line with expectations.

The $1.40 Q2 loss per share falls within the preview’s base-case range of −$1.20 to −$1.60; the preview also noted that vendor EPS estimates conflicted and there was “no reliable beat/miss line on EPS this quarter.”
The $3.5 billion storage contracted backlog and 34 GWh under long-term service agreements matched the preview’s stated figures.
Full-year 2026 CapEx of around $1.3 billion matched the preview’s expectation of about $1.3 billion.
Q3 revenue guidance of $1.3–1.5 billion starts around the previewed Street figure of about $1.3 billion and extends above it; the preview did not supply a specific Q3 gross-margin estimate.

surprises.description: Titan’s equipment margin was 8.5%, well above the preview’s expected 6.5–7.0% band. Management attributed the improvement to inventory-health initiatives, not stronger industry demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated equipment margin improved 190 basis points year-over-year to 8.5%, driven by inventory health initiatives rather than any improvement in underlying industry demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Equipment margin vs. the 6.5–7.0% guided band.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 18.6%, above the preview’s expected 17.0–17.5%. Gross profit stayed essentially flat even as revenue fell.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit held essentially flat at $92.4 million as gross margin expanded 150 basis points to 18.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~17.0–17.5%.”

surprises.description: Europe’s full-year outlook worsened to a 30–40% decline, compared with the prior 20–25% decline outlook in the preview. The company attributed about $44 million of the drop to the German wind-down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year outlook was cut to a decline of 30-40%, with ~$44 million of the drop from the German wind-down.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Europe −20/−25%” in the company guidance column.

surprises.description: Construction’s full-year growth outlook was raised to 5–10%, above the prior 0–5% outlook. The quarter also showed 9.2% same-store growth and a return to pretax profit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Construction was a bright spot, growing 9.2% same-store to $78.6 million with pretax income of $0.4 million versus a $1.2 million loss last year, prompting an upgraded full-year growth outlook to 5-10%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Construction 0/+5%” in the company guidance column.

surprises.description: Australia’s full-year growth outlook was raised to about 15–20%, above the prior 10–15% outlook. Sales rose 22.5% in constant currency, though the reported growth included FX and the segment’s pretax loss widened.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Australia sales rose 36% to $41.4 million (22.5% constant currency) aided by New Holland brand additions”; “full-year growth guidance was raised to about 15-20% though 8 points come purely from FX.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Australia +10/+15%” in the company guidance column.

surprises.description: Quarterly revenue was $496.4 million, above the preview’s $486.5 million consensus estimate, although it still declined year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue declined 9.2% to $496.4 million from $546.4 million a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $486.5M.”

surprises.description: Domestic Ag same-store sales fell 8.4%, a milder decline than the preview’s base-case expectation of a 12–16% decrease.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Domestic Ag segment sales fell 8.4% same-store to $310.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Ag SSS −12% to −16%” in the base scenario.

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was $4.6 million, within the preview’s roughly $4–6 million estimate.
The company reaffirmed its full-year adjusted EBITDA range of $17–29 million and adjusted diluted loss-per-share range of $1.25–$1.75, consistent with the ranges cited in the preview.

surprises.description: The preview warned that temporarily low employee medical claims could reverse and push service costs up. Instead, gross margin rose to about 74% from 71% a year earlier, with management attributing cost reductions to AI-enabled service efficiency.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit was a record $258 million (~74% of revenue), up from 71% a year earlier, driven by AI-enabled service cost reductions while total accounts grew 4%.” AI automation “resolved 85% of routine chat inquiries” and reduced human-handled calls 25% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “About $2M of the Q1 service-cost beat came from temporarily depressed employee medical claims and was pushed back into the forecast as non-sustainable. Watch whether that reverses here.”

surprises.description: New HSA sales were stronger than the preview’s enterprise-pipeline discussion alone implied: new HSAs from sales rose 24% year over year and set a Q2 record. The quarter was also described as the strongest outside open enrollment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New HSAs from sales up 24% year-over-year, setting a Q2 record and the strongest quarter outside open enrollment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management called it ‘the largest pipeline of enterprise sales that we have seen in years.’ Q2 is when the January 1 selling season firms up.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA exceeded the preview’s estimated range, and the company also reported record margin expansion. This was a stronger profitability result than the preview’s concern about service costs normalizing higher suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached a record $167 million, up 11% year-over-year, with a record adjusted EBITDA margin of 48%, up from 46% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … ~$158–163M for Q2 (my estimate).” The preview also said to watch whether service costs “normalize higher.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS came in above the roughly $1.19 consensus estimate, though it was still within the preview’s base-case scenario range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income was $103.8 million ($1.24 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS … ~$1.19 (TradingKey, Aug 26, 2026).” The base case was “$1.19–1.25.”

surprises.description: GAAP EPS was below the preview’s estimated range, even though GAAP net income was a record. The reported figure included a one-time $3.3 million software disposal expense.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income was a record $65.6 million ($0.78 per diluted share), the latter including $3.3 million of one-time software disposal expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP EPS … ~$0.85–0.94 (Zacks/MarketBeat, Aug 2026).”

surprises.description: Revenue slightly exceeded the preview’s approximately $349 million estimate, reaching about $351 million. The gap was modest rather than a large beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue grew 8% year-over-year to approximately $351 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … ~$349M (TradingKey, Aug 26, 2026).”

surprises.description: Custodial revenue came in modestly above the preview’s roughly $174 million reference, but the reported annualized HSA cash yield of 3.83% was slightly below the roughly 3.85% level the preview expected to be reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Custodial revenue up 10% to a record $175.9 million” and “Annualized yield on HSA cash was 3.83%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Custodial revenue versus about $174M and the ~3.85% yield reaffirmation.”

surprises.description: Service revenue growth accelerated from the 3% reported in Q1 to 6% in Q2, reaching another record. The preview focused on service costs rather than anticipating this acceleration in service revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Service revenue up 6% to a record $124.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Service revenue +3% to a record $123M” in Q1 FY2027.

surprises.description: Share repurchases were lower than the prior quarter’s pace: the company bought back about $108 million versus $123 million in Q1. The preview specifically flagged whether the Q1 run rate would continue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased approximately $108 million of shares at an average price below $90.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Buyback pace … against the $123M Q1 run-rate.”

surprises.description: The call reported strong growth in member-facing digital and investing activity that the preview did not specifically forecast: monthly active app users rose 62% year over year, and investing members grew more than 20%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Investing HSA members grew over 20% (about 9% of total members) with a new SimplyInvest no-fee lineup launched” and “monthly active app users hit 1.4 million, up 62% year-over-year.”

in_line: Interchange revenue grew 5%, matching the Q1 growth rate and staying above the preview’s sub-4% level identified as a negative signal.

FY2027 guidance received only a small upward nudge: revenue moved from $1.410–$1.420 billion to $1.411–$1.421 billion, adjusted EBITDA from $625–$633 million to $628–$636 million, and the non-GAAP EPS range remained $4.66–$4.73. This was broadly consistent with the preview’s base case of a modest guide nudge, rather than a substantial EPS upgrade.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $928 million, well above the preview’s roughly $904–905 million consensus and the $902–905 million company guide. It also cleared the preview’s $915 million threshold for a strong beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue reached $928 million,” exceeding company guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $904.1M (Zacks) / $905.3M (street composite) | Company guide ... $902–905M”; the preview also said “A print below about $915M would be a weak beat.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating income was $416 million versus the preview’s roughly $393 million consensus and $392–395 million guide. Along with the revenue result, that implies an operating margin of about 44.8%, above the preview’s roughly 43.6% expectation rather than showing the anticipated further compression.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income of $416 million,” exceeding company guidance; with revenue of $928 million, the implied margin is about 44.8%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income | ~$393M | $392–395M”; “Non-GAAP operating margin | ~43.6%”; and “margin ... is guided down again in Q2 (about −110bps).”

surprises.description: Commercial subscription grew about 13%, with double-digit growth even excluding Crossix and strength across CRM, content, data, and Crossix. The preview did not provide a segment growth expectation, so this is new favorable segment detail rather than a beat against a stated benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The commercial subscription segment grew approximately 13% year-over-year, with double-digit growth even excluding Crossix, driven by broad-based strength across CRM, content, data, and Crossix.”

surprises.description: The call reported three large CRM wins, including Regeneron selecting Vault CRM, and said 12 of the top 20 biopharma companies are now committed, with only two more expected to decide by year-end. The preview already noted Lilly and Biogen wins, but did not report Regeneron or the updated commitment count.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management called it “the best CRM quarter ever,” with “three large deals including two top 20 biopharma companies (Biogen and Regeneron selecting Vault CRM)”; “12 of the top 20 biopharma companies” are committed, with “only 2 remaining” expected to decide by year-end.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “In the Q1 call, management said it expects to win the majority of the four remaining top-20 biopharma CRM migration decisions by fiscal year-end. Lilly and Biogen wins were announced in August, before the report.”

surprises.description: Veeva disclosed that one top-20 customer activated AI across its entire sales force, while Salesforce had no customers live, and that more than 180 Veeva CRM customers are live. The preview did not flag this level of deployed-customer evidence as an issue to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Veeva has over 180 CRM customers live, and one top 20 customer activated AI across its entire sales force this quarter, contrasting with Salesforce having no customers live.”

surprises.description: Management said it expects to maintain more than 70% CRM market share and win back some customers that chose Salesforce, mainly in 2027–2028. This is a more specific competitive outlook than the preview’s focus on the remaining top-20 migration decisions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is targeting maintained CRM market leadership of over 70% share and expects to win back some customers who previously selected Salesforce, primarily in 2027-2028 before the Veeva CRM backstop expires end of 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on “Vault CRM wins and timing” and the “four remaining top-20 biopharma CRM migration decisions.”

surprises.description: Falcon had five early adopters, including a top-20 pharma company, with first go-lives expected this year. The preview discussed a planned November early-adopter release but gave no adopter count or customer detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Veeva Falcon ... has 5 early adopters including one top 20 pharma, with first go-lives expected this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Falcon early-adopter release is planned for November.”

surprises.description: Despite very high customer interest in Falcon, management said product readiness is the key constraint and that Veeva itself is the rate-limiter. This adds a delivery bottleneck to the preview’s discussion of Falcon adoption and monetization.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management identified “being the rate-limiter on product readiness as the key constraint despite very high customer interest.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said quantified Falcon bookings, pipeline, or FY28 revenue framing would be a potential upside, and noted the planned November early-adopter release; it did not flag product readiness as a constraint.

surprises.description: Management said Falcon gross margins should be roughly similar to software margins because much of the work will run through deterministic software, and expected AI-model prices to decline. This offers favorable cost and margin framing on the AI-payback question, though the preview had identified quantified Falcon economics as an open issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects Falcon gross margins to be roughly similar to software margins,” with work shifted to deterministic software and non-deterministic AI model prices “expected to decline over time.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called Falcon monetization a key issue and said the test was “whether the ~$1,610M FY27 operating income line is held, raised, or trimmed” as evidence of whether AI investment is self-funding.

surprises.description: Management described R&D subscription growth as shifting from mature products such as eTMF, CTMS, QMS, and regulatory to newer products including EDC, eCOA, RTSM, Safety, and LIMS; Veeva has nine of the top 20 in EDC. The preview said segment detail was not covered, so it supplied no benchmark for this product-mix commentary.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D subscription growth is transitioning from mature products ... to newer early-stage growth drivers ... with Veeva holding 9 of top 20 in EDC.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed Aspen, a horizontal CRM startup, as a new initiative with minimal financial investment and no revenue included in plans. It expressed full confidence that a market exists but acknowledged uncertainty about execution, and described pricing of $50 per user per month plus usage overages.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Aspen horizontal CRM startup carries minimal financial investment with no revenue factored into plans,” using “$50 per user per month plus usage overages”; management expressed “100% confidence the market exists but uncertainty on execution.”

in_line: The preview noted Lilly and Biogen wins and expected management to win the majority of the remaining top-20 CRM decisions by fiscal year-end. The call’s update that 12 of the top 20 are committed and only two more are expected to decide by year-end is broadly consistent with that expectation.

surprises.description: Q4 net sales were $295.5 million, far above the preview’s $263.9 million consensus and the company’s $261–267 million guidance range. The roughly 12% beat over consensus was substantially stronger than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 net sales rose 42.7% to $295.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $263.9M | Company Guidance (Q4) $261–267M.”

surprises.description: SACSTOR’s Q4 revenue exceeded the preview’s $57–59 million expectation, but its adjusted EBITDA margin was well below the guided 10–11% range. The company attributed the shortfall to Fort Pierce ramp investments and higher input costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The March 2 SACSTOR acquisition contributed $61.2 million in Q4 revenue”; its “Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin (~$4 million contribution) came in below the guided 10-11% range due to Fort Pierce ramp investments and higher input costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided $57–59M revenue at 10–11% adj. EBITDA margin.”

surprises.description: FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $101–109 million is somewhat below the preview’s expected $105–115 million range: the guide midpoint is $105 million, and only its upper portion reaches the expected range. Revenue guidance, by contrast, is broadly in line with the roughly $1.08 billion consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance projects net sales of $1.080-$1.120 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $101-$109 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Street expects about $1.08B revenue and roughly $105–115M adj. EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Legacy Q4 sales grew 13.2%, materially exceeding the preview’s expectation of about flat legacy sales. Cobalt and saltwater fishing both posted volume gains, helping drive the outperformance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 legacy net sales grew 13.2% to $234.3 million, driven by Cobalt (+31% to $70.5 million) and saltwater fishing (+11.1% to $80.9 million) volume gains.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Q4 guide implies legacy (ex-Saxdor) margin of roughly 11.2–12.5% on about flat legacy sales.”

surprises.description: Full-year FY2026 sales reached $914.6 million, about $29 million above the top of the raised guidance range, rather than landing near the preview’s guidance and consensus figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2026 net sales reached $914.6 million (up 13.3%), about $29 million above the raised guidance top end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance is $880–886M net sales”; “Consensus is $883.2M revenue.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $33.9 million beat the preview’s roughly $30 million consensus. The adjusted EBITDA margin, however, was close to the expected level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA [was] up 72.7% to $33.9 million and margins expanding 200 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$30M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin | ~11.4%.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a sharp FY2026 GAAP net-income decline to $1.7 million, primarily from SACSTOR acquisition and integration expenses. The preview focused on adjusted EPS and did not set a GAAP net-income expectation, so this is a newly disclosed reported-earnings burden rather than a direct miss against its adjusted-EPS estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year GAAP net income dropped 88.8% to $1.7 million ($0.09/share), primarily due to SACSTOR acquisition and integration expenses.”

surprises.description: The call added a weak near-term FY2027 earnings outlook: Q1 adjusted EBITDA is guided to only $14–16 million, with first-half margins weighed down by SACSTOR ramp investment. The preview gave an annual FY2027 outlook but did not flag this quarter-level ramp burden.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 guidance calls for net sales of $255-$265 million and adjusted EBITDA of only $14-$16 million, with first-half margins weighed down by SACSTOR ramp investment.”

surprises.description: Within the stronger legacy result, Malibu itself grew only 3.2% and had lower unit volumes, unlike Cobalt and saltwater fishing, which gained volume. This is a softer brand-level outcome amid the preview’s concern that legacy unit declines could strain the offset from sales per unit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Malibu grew only 3.2% to $82.9 million on lower unit volumes,” while Cobalt and saltwater fishing posted volume gains.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Legacy unit declines have been offset by net sales per unit gains. A fifth straight quarter of double-digit unit declines would strain that offset.”

in_line: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $73.9 million was within the preview’s $72–74 million guidance range.
FY2027 revenue guidance of $1.080–$1.120 billion was broadly in line with the preview’s roughly $1.08 billion consensus.
Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin was about 11.5% ($33.9 million on $295.5 million sales), close to the preview’s roughly 11.4% expectation and within the company’s 11.3–11.8% guidance.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $4.7 million, far above the preview’s roughly $1.75 million estimate. The quarter also included $3.1 million of TRISO product revenue, not just development and government-service revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $4.7 million”; “$3.1 million of TRISO product revenue and $1.6 million of government service revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Derived Q2 base case (my estimate, not a survey)”: “I use about $1.75M for Q2.”

surprises.description: The Q2 net loss was much smaller than the preview’s expected range: $3.4 million versus a base-case loss of $9–11 million. The loss also narrowed sequentially from $7.7 million in Q1, rather than widening as management had previously signaled.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed sequentially from $7.7 million in Q1 to $3.4 million ($0.12 per share), driven by first commercial product revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “Net Loss” of “−$9M to −$11M”; the prior-quarter section says “Management has signaled losses will widen as production scales ahead of revenue.”

surprises.description: The company reported a 67% gross margin even though the preview described gross margin as deeply negative on an LTM basis. The preview cautioned that margins carried little signal at the current scale, but a positive quarterly margin was still a substantial departure from that starting point.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company achieved 67% gross margin in the quarter at a 63.3% process yield.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin is deeply negative (−244% LTM) because fixed manufacturing cost is absorbed against a small revenue base. Margin percentages carry little signal this quarter.”

surprises.description: Total backlog was approximately in line with the preview’s cited $245 million at quarter-end, but then rose to $576.9 million after the August Entegris/Antares agreement. That is a much larger quantified post-quarter step-up than the preview’s undisclosed Radiant agreement left investors able to assess.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total contract backlog grew from $91.3 million at March 31 to $241.5 million at June 30, and reached $576.9 million after the August Entegris/Antares agreement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Total backlog … $245M” and said the Radiant agreement had “dollar value undisclosed”; it asked whether Radiant was additive to the $245M.

surprises.description: Funded backlog was close to the preview’s $65 million figure at June 30, but grew to $119.3 million after the August fuel supply agreement—well above the expected baseline for committed business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Funded backlog rose from $8.2 million at March 31 to $61.9 million at June 30, then approximately doubled to $119.3 million after the August fuel supply agreement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said total backlog included “$65M funded” and identified funded backlog conversion as a key issue to watch.

surprises.description: Pro forma cash was roughly $240 million after the IPO, versus the $124.9 million cash balance cited in the preview. The larger cash position, with no debt, is materially above the preview’s stated starting point for its runway concerns.
surprises.fact_evidence: The IPO generated “approximately $137.7 million in net proceeds, bringing pro forma cash to roughly $240 million with no debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash is $124.9M with no debt.”

surprises.description: The preview described SN-TN as adding 2.5 metric tons of throughput to the 0.5 metric tons already operating at SN-0, implying about 3 metric tons in total. Management instead described combined Tennessee and Idaho throughput of up to 2.5 metric tons annually by year-end, a lower stated near-term total on those figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Combined throughput reaching up to 2.5 metric tons annually by year-end, scalable to 5 metric tons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SN-TN … adding 2.5 MTU of throughput to the 0.5 MTU now operating at SN-0, a 6x step.”

surprises.description: Management said investors should model about 154.3 million post-IPO shares, below the 160.67 million share count referenced in the preview. The lower denominator is a modestly favorable difference for per-share calculations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Investors should model ~154.3 million post-IPO shares.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview referred to “160.67M shares now.”

in_line: The June 30 total backlog of $241.5 million was close to the preview’s cited $245 million.
The June 30 funded backlog of $61.9 million was close to the preview’s cited $65 million.
The Tennessee facility remained on a 2026 timeline: the preview expected SN-TN to start in 2H 2026, and the call targeted authorization to operate in Q4 2026.
The Richland Framatome JV’s 2027 production start was consistent with the preview’s stated 2027 target.

surprises.description: Revenue was $124.4 million, above the preview’s roughly $123.2 million working consensus and $0.4 million above the top of company guidance. The beat was modest, and revenue still grew only 1% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was $124.4 million, up just 1% year-over-year but exceeding the top end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With only 8–11 covering analysts, treat $0.30 and $123.2M as the working base”; company guidance was “$122.0M – $124.0M.”

surprises.description: PagerDuty raised its FY27 non-GAAP operating margin outlook to 25%–26% from 24%–25%, a stronger improvement than the preview’s cited margin guidance. The company said this accelerates progress toward its 30% long-term target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY27 non-GAAP operating margin guidance was raised to 25%-26% from the prior 24%-25%, accelerating the path toward the 30% long-term target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op margin | FY guide 24–25%.”

surprises.description: The company completed a restructuring affecting about 15% of employees and expects $5.5 million to $7.5 million in charges, neither of which the preview anticipated. The cuts were concentrated in noncustomer-facing roles.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed a workforce restructuring impacting approximately 15% of employees, concentrated in noncustomer-facing roles, with restructuring charges of $5.5 million to $7.5 million.”

surprises.description: Full-year free-cash-flow margin guidance was raised to match FY26, rather than being 2–4 percentage points lower as the preview said was previously expected. This is a better outlook than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year free cash flow margin guidance was raised to be in line with FY26 rather than 2-4 points lower as previously expected.”

surprises.description: Total RPO was nearly flat year over year at $426 million, an unexpectedly weak backlog update given the preview’s focus on ARR returning to growth and improving retention. The preview did not provide an RPO estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total RPO was $426 million (only $1 million higher year-over-year).”

surprises.description: The Ops Cloud/PD Reliability Platform business was reported to be growing at a double-digit rate and is set to reach general availability this fall with usage-based pricing. The preview discussed watching usage-based ARR mix but did not anticipate this launch timing or pricing update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Ops Cloud/PD Reliability Platform business grew double digits and will move to general availability this fall with usage-based pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Usage-based / Operations Cloud ~10% of total ARR”; the preview said to watch whether usage-based ARR mix rises toward ~13%.

in_line: ARR ended at $501 million, crossing $500 million for the first time; the preview identified at least $500 million with positive year-over-year growth as the inflection threshold.
Dollar-based net retention reached 98%, matching the preview’s stated clean proof point of 98% or higher.

surprises.description: Q2 total revenue was $427.3 million, well above the $396.4 million consensus and the company’s $395–397 million guide; it also exceeded the preview’s $404–410 million bull scenario. Revenue growth was 38%, or 43% normalized for material rights, versus the preview’s roughly 28% growth expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose 38% to $427.3 million (up 43% normalized for material rights).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q2 FY27 Consensus | $396.4M | Company Guide | $395–397M”; “Bull | Revenue | $404–410M.”

surprises.description: Net new subscription ARR was approximately $96 million, above the preview’s $80–90 million whisper range and its $90 million bull-case threshold; the preview’s consensus-based estimate was roughly $70 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net new subscription ARR was approximately $96 million, growing 35% year-over-year, which management characterized as an acceleration from prior quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus of $1,639M implies roughly $70M sequentially”; “Secondary whisper is $80–90M”; “Net new ARR of $90M+.”

surprises.description: Subscription ARR reached $1.66 billion, about $21 million above the preview’s $1.639 billion consensus. Its 33% growth also exceeded the preview’s roughly 31% growth framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subscription ARR reached $1.66 billion in Q2 FY27, growing 33% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Subscription ARR | Q2 FY27 Consensus | $1,639.4M”; “Revenue growth (~28%) runs below ARR growth (~31%).”

surprises.description: The FY27 subscription ARR outlook was raised to $1.88–1.885 billion, at or slightly above the preview’s expected $1.87–1.88 billion base case. The increase was larger than the preview’s minimum catalyst threshold, though short of its $1.90 billion bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY27 subscription ARR guidance was raised to $1.88–$1.885 billion (~29% growth), with the raise adding $24–$25 million and lifting implied net new ARR growth from 7% to 14%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base case is a raise to about $1.87–1.88B”; “A bull case needs $1.90B or more”; “FY27 subscription ARR guide at or above $1.88B.”

surprises.description: FY27 total revenue guidance rose to $1.685–1.693 billion from the prior $1.638–1.648 billion range, a stronger outlook than the preview’s prior-guide baseline despite the material-rights headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY27 guidance calls for total revenue of $1.685–$1.693 billion”; “material rights being a ~$18 million revenue headwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2027 guidance (to be updated): revenue $1.638–1.648B”; “Revenue growth (~28%) runs below ARR growth (~31%) as material-rights benefit rolls off.”

surprises.description: FY27 non-GAAP EPS guidance increased to $0.47–$0.53, well above the prior $0.25–$0.35 range. The preview did not lay out an expected EPS guide increase of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY27 guidance calls for … non-GAAP EPS of $0.47–$0.53.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2027 guidance (to be updated): … non-GAAP EPS $0.25–0.35.”

surprises.description: FY27 free cash flow guidance increased to $323–$333 million, above the preview’s stated catalyst of raising guidance above $303 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY27 guidance calls for … free cash flow of $323–$333 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FCF guide raised above $303M”; prior guidance was “FCF $293–303M.”

surprises.description: The FY27 subscription ARR contribution-margin outlook is about 15.5%, above the preview’s roughly 14% expectation. The reported LTM margin also improved to 14%, up 460 basis points year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subscription ARR contribution margin improved 460 basis points year-over-year to 14% (LTM)”; FY27 guidance calls for “~15.5% subscription ARR contribution margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2027 guidance … subscription ARR contribution margin ~14%”; the preview also called for confirmation that “FCF and margin targets are raised.”
