surprises.description: Agent Cloud had more than 15 paying customers, but management assumed minimal ARR from it for the year. That fell short of the preview’s hoped-for quantified new-product ARR disclosure to support the platform thesis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rubrik Agent Cloud now has over 15 paying customers with minimal ARR assumed this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A quantified combined new-product ARR figure would support the platform thesis.”

surprises.description: Strata Identity contributed no ARR in the quarter and is assumed to contribute none for the full year, so the raised outlook does not rely on an ARR contribution from the acquisition. The call framed this as addressing investor concerns about inorganic growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Strata Identity acquisition contributed $0 ARR in the quarter and is assumed to contribute $0 for the full year in guidance, addressing investor concerns about inorganic growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Investor concerns about inorganic growth.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag non-cloud ARR as a growth driver, but management said it is now growing at roughly 10%, supported by sovereign and regulated-industry demand, and carries higher margins than cloud.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-cloud ARR is now growing (~10% expected) driven by sovereign and regulated-industry demand and carries higher margins than cloud.”

in_line: Subscription net retention remained above 119%, broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation that it would remain near 120%.
The outlook included an approximately $18 million material-rights revenue headwind, consistent with the preview’s warning that the material-rights benefit was rolling off.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $1.9 billion, well above the preview’s $1.76 billion consensus. Management said organic growth was about 5%, but roughly 1 percentage point came from unplanned material purchases that are not expected to recur.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was $1.9 billion with organic growth of approximately 5%, though roughly 1 point came from unplanned material purchases that management does not expect to repeat.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY27 Consensus” revenue: “$1.76B.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS of $3.01 substantially exceeded the preview’s $2.31 consensus, even though EPS declined year over year because the prior-year comparison included a favorable legal settlement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS was $3.01, down year-over-year primarily due to a prior-period favorable legal settlement, partially offset by a lower share count.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY27 Consensus” adjusted diluted EPS: “$2.31 (Zacks $2.32)”; the preview also noted Q2 FY26 was “flattered by a patent settlement recovery.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY27 revenue guidance by 2% to a $7.25 billion midpoint and adjusted EBITDA guidance by 4% at the midpoint. The preview described the existing revenue and EBITDA ranges and anticipated only a modest EPS-guide nudge in its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised FY27 guidance, lifting revenue 2% to a $7.25 billion midpoint, adjusted EBITDA 4% at midpoint (margins of 10.3%-10.5%), while maintaining free cash flow of at least $600 million ($14/share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed existing guidance of “$7.0–$7.2B” revenue and “$720–$730M” adjusted EBITDA; its base scenario anticipated “FY EPS nudged to ~$10.10–10.25.”

surprises.description: Quarterly book-to-bill came in at just 0.6x, with trailing-twelve-month book-to-bill at 0.8x. Management said the quarterly figure would have been near 1.0x if a large recompete had been booked two days earlier, but the reported results were still below the preview’s expectation that full-year book-to-bill would be comfortably above 1.0.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Book-to-bill was a weak 0.6x for the quarter (0.8x trailing twelve months), with management noting it would have been near 1.0x had a large recompete not been booked two days after quarter close.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management expects full-year book-to-bill ‘comfortably over 1.0.’”

surprises.description: Management reported more than $1.6 billion of intel space awards in the first half, a substantial award total not anticipated in the preview. The preview instead noted that a $400 million intel-agency recompete was likely to show up in Q3 bookings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company booked over $1.6 billion of intel space awards in the first half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A $400M intel-agency recompete win announced Aug 5 likely shows up in Q3 bookings.”

surprises.description: Recompete win rates exceeded 90% and new-business win rates were at or above 30%, with management saying both had returned to target ranges after prior weakness. The preview discussed a declining qualified pipeline and bookings risk but did not flag an expected recovery in win rates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recompete win rate exceeded 90% this quarter and new business win rates are at or above 30%, both back within target ranges after prior weakness.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a border-security recompete win after quarter-end, an additional contract win not identified in the preview’s expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[The company] won a border security recompete after quarter-end.”

surprises.description: Project ORBIT was quantified at about $150 million in annual run-rate savings by the end of three years, but roughly two-thirds is planned for reinvestment, leaving about $50 million to support margin expansion. The preview expected a transformation-program update but did not provide a savings target or describe this reinvestment split.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Project ORBIT targets approximately $150 million in annual run-rate savings by the end of a 3-year period, with about two-thirds ($100 million) reinvested and the rest supporting margin expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the CEO “promised a detailed update on the enterprise transformation program on this call.”

surprises.description: Management gave longer-range margin targets not specified in the preview: mid-10% margins next year and a path to approximately 11% by FY30.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management set margin targets of mid-10s% for next year and a path to approximately 11% by FY30.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin was 10.3%, at the top of the preview’s estimated 10.0%–10.3% range and at the preview’s stated clean-margin bullish threshold. The call noted that adjusted EBITDA was up only modestly year over year excluding the prior-year favorable legal settlement.

Second-half margins in the high-9% range are broadly consistent with the preview’s estimate of roughly 9.7%–10.0% across Q2–Q4 after excluding the Q1 gain. The approximately 350-basis-point RITS revenue headwind is also close to the preview’s roughly 3% organic headwind estimate for Q3 and Q4.
Free cash flow guidance remained at least $600 million, in line with the preview’s stated guidance of more than $600 million (at least $14 per share).

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $15 billion, above the preview’s $14.40–14.45 billion consensus range. The roughly $550–600 million gap was a clear upside surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenues were $15 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 consensus” revenue: “$14.40–14.45B.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.77 versus $0.68 consensus, a meaningful beat. At the same time, Pfizer reported a GAAP loss per share of $0.04 rather than the preview’s expected GAAP profit, alongside an unanticipated $4.3 billion in noncash impairments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.77 beat expectations against a reported loss per share of $0.04”; “$4.3 billion in noncash intangible asset impairments in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adjusted EPS consensus: “$0.68”; GAAP EPS consensus: “~$0.45.”

surprises.description: Pfizer raised the midpoint of full-year revenue guidance by $500 million, whereas the preview’s base case expected the existing range to be reaffirmed. The raise came despite lowering the COVID revenue assumption, making the overall guidance action more favorable than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised the midpoint of its full-year 2026 revenue guidance by $500 million to a range of $60.5 billion to $62.5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed guidance of “$59.5–62.5B” and said the base-scenario guidance action was “Reaffirm $2.80–3.00” (with no revenue raise expected).

surprises.description: Pfizer lowered its full-year COVID-19 revenue expectation to roughly $4 billion from roughly $5 billion embedded in the preview. That is a substantial shortfall in the COVID contribution, even though total revenue guidance increased.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cutting COVID-19 revenue expectations from roughly $5 billion to $4 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Embedded assumptions included “COVID franchise $5B”; the preview also focused on commentary “versus the $5B FY assumption.”

surprises.description: The ex-COVID business grew 5% operationally, below the preview’s marker of about 6% or more for validating the post-pandemic growth case. The result was still positive growth, but somewhat short of the stated benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding COVID products the underlying business grew 5% operationally.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything sustaining about 6% or more validates the post-pandemic growth case.”

surprises.description: Pfizer disclosed $4.3 billion of noncash intangible impairments, including after a failed Phase III readout for sigvotatug vedotin and removal of Oxbryta revenue projections. The preview had expected GAAP EPS of about $0.45 and did not flag these impairment events.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$4.3 billion in noncash intangible asset impairments,” “driven by the failed Phase III readout for sigvotatug vedotin in second-line non-small cell lung cancer and removal of Oxbryta revenue projections.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: GAAP EPS consensus was “~$0.45”; the preview did not mention these impairment events.

surprises.description: Pfizer added about $1 billion to its productivity-savings program and set a roughly $3 billion manufacturing-optimization target, bringing stated net savings through 2029 to about $9.7 billion. The preview did not anticipate this expansion of cost actions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adding ~$1 billion to productivity savings (now $6.7 billion through 2029) and targeting ~$3 billion from manufacturing optimization, for approximately $9.7 billion in total net savings through 2029.”

surprises.description: Management made an emphatic commitment to maintain the dividend even in the most stretched scenarios and to resume dividend growth after the post-2028 LOE period. The preview did not discuss this investor concern or anticipate that reassurance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Albert Bourla “repeatedly and emphatically committed to maintaining the dividend even under the most stretched scenarios and resuming growth after the post-2028 LOE period.”

surprises.description: Pfizer reported that CFO Dave Denton is departing, with Cecile Guegan becoming interim CFO. The preview did not flag a leadership transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Dave Denton is departing Pfizer, with Cecile Guegan stepping in as interim CFO.”

surprises.description: Pfizer reported berobenatide Phase III weight-loss results of up to 12.3% placebo-corrected at the median dose and about 16% mean loss at the high dose, with a first approval targeted in 2028 and 10 Phase III studies planned for 2026. The preview flagged Phase III timing but gave no efficacy, approval-timing, or study-count expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Berobenatide achieved placebo-corrected weight loss of up to 12.3% at its median Phase III dose and ~16% mean weight loss at its high dose, with a first approval targeted in 2028 and 10 Phase III studies planned in 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Berobenatide Phase III timing” was “an option value not reflected in the current multiple,” but provided no efficacy or timing estimate.

in_line: FY26 adjusted diluted EPS guidance remained $2.80–3.00, as the preview’s base case expected, although the company said the range now absorbs an unfavorable approximately $0.10 impact from the Innovent-related Acquired In-Process R&D charge.

surprises.description: Net new ARR was $56 million, well below the preview’s roughly $72–$82 million estimate and its approximately $75 million watchpoint. The record for a second quarter and fifth consecutive quarter of positive year-over-year growth did not make up for the sizable shortfall versus expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record second-quarter net new ARR of $56 million (up 4% YoY)” and “fifth consecutive quarter of positive YoY net new ARR growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The implied range is about $72M–$82M” and “A print below about $75M would weaken the read-across.”

surprises.description: Q2 profitability substantially exceeded the preview’s expectations: operating margin reached 10% with 820 basis points of year-over-year expansion, and EPS was $0.08 versus $0.07 consensus. The preview had flagged restructuring savings as something to look for, while sales and marketing expense fell to 34% of revenue, down more than 900 basis points year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 operating margin reached a record 10%, an 820 basis point YoY expansion, while EPS of $0.08 doubled year-over-year and beat expectations”; “Sales and marketing expense fell to 34% of revenue, a 900+ basis point YoY improvement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS” consensus was “$0.07”; Q2 non-GAAP operating income consensus was “~$24M.” The preview also said to watch for “Opex savings visible in Q2.”

surprises.description: The company raised its FY27 revenue outlook, but only modestly: the new $1.202–$1.207 billion range is just above the previous $1.195–$1.205 billion range and remains below the preview’s $1.21 billion-or-higher bull-signal threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SentinelOne raised its full-year FY27 revenue outlook to $1.202-$1.207 billion (~20% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY27 revenue guidance of “$1.195B – $1.205B” and said “A raise to $1.21B or higher would be the cleanest bull signal. A simple reiteration would be negative.”

surprises.description: FY27 operating-income guidance moved above the preview’s expected range: the new $124–$128 million outlook is higher than the $115–$125 million consensus range and implies about a 10% operating margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating income outlook to $124-$128 million (~10% margin, up ~700 bps over FY26).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave FY27 non-GAAP operating income consensus of “$115M – $125M.”

surprises.description: The revenue outlook implies a stronger second-half exit than the preview anticipated: Q3 revenue is guided to about 20% growth, and management said the full-year outlook implies a notably higher Q4 exit rate, rather than the preview’s expectation of no second-half acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 revenue of $309-$311 million (~20% growth) … with the full-year implying a notably higher Q4 exit rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY27 revenue range “implies no second-half acceleration.”

surprises.description: RPO growth accelerated well beyond the prior-quarter trajectory noted in the preview: it reached a record $1.7 billion and grew 45%, versus 30% growth and $1.5 billion in the prior quarter. Management attributed the increase to larger lands and longer contract durations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RPO accelerated to 45% growth, reaching a record $1.7 billion, up from $1.5 billion last quarter, driven by larger lands and longer contract durations.”

surprises.description: The preview expected AI security ARR to be growing quickly from a small base, but management gave a stronger update: revenue from Prompt Security and Purple AI had tripled year over year, and management expects AI security to become the company’s next nine-figure ARR category.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ARR from AI security offerings (Prompt Security and Purple AI) tripled year-over-year and is expected to become the company's next 9-figure ARR category.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “AI security ARR growing quickly from a small base” and said a “Quantified AI-security or non-endpoint ARR” figure would be meaningful.

surprises.description: SentinelOne Flex had already reached more than 10% of total ARR within a year of launch, a scale milestone the preview did not identify as an expectation or key metric.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SentinelOne Flex exceeded 10% of total ARR within a year of launch.”

surprises.description: The company also reported a 6% trailing-12-month adjusted free-cash-flow margin, up about 400 basis points year over year; the preview did not flag this cash-flow improvement as an expectation to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month adjusted free cash flow margin reached 6% (up ~400 bps YoY).”

in_line: Total ARR growth of 22% was broadly in line with the preview’s implied expectation of roughly $1.235–$1.245 billion of ARR against about $1.01 billion a year earlier.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $1.43, above the preview’s $1.29–$1.33 consensus range and even the $1.42 top of its bull scenario. The reported $0.15 Electric Utilities contribution from customer growth and infrastructure investment was the stated driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EPS rose to $1.43” and was “driven by a $0.15 gain in Electric Utilities from customer growth and infrastructure investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS (Q2) … $1.29” (most-republished figure) to “$1.33”; the bull scenario projected “$1.36–$1.42.”

surprises.description: The preview expected Duke’s North Carolina rate-case ROE and capital structure to remain unresolved and go to hearing. Duke reported a DEC settlement with a 9.8% ROE, 53% equity capital structure, and an earnings-sharing mechanism allowing up to 10.3% ROE, though commission orders are still pending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Duke reached a North Carolina DEC rate case settlement featuring a 9.8% ROE, 53% equity capital structure, and an earnings sharing mechanism allowing up to 10.3% ROE,” with orders expected by mid-November.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ROE and capital structure remain unresolved and go to hearing.”

surprises.description: Duke disclosed $5 billion to $10 billion of potential generation and transmission investment beyond its current five-year capital plan, primarily in Indiana and Florida, if data-center service agreements are signed. The preview discussed data-center signings and pipeline but did not flag this additional capital-plan upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$5 billion to $10 billion of potential upside to the current 5-year capital plan for additional generation and transmission, primarily in Indiana and Florida, triggered when ESAs are signed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “About 7.6 GW of signed Electric Service Agreements … with a 15.4 GW high-confidence pipeline”; the preview did not mention potential capital-plan additions.

surprises.description: Signed data-center agreements reached 7.8 GW, only modestly above the roughly 7.6 GW entering-quarter level, but management also gave a conversion timetable for the remaining 15.4 GW pipeline: by the first half of 2027. The preview highlighted new signings but did not provide an expected conversion date.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Secured 7.8 gigawatts of electric service agreements” and expects “to convert the remaining 15.4 gigawatt pipeline to ESAs by the first half of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “About 7.6 GW of signed Electric Service Agreements entering the quarter, with a 15.4 GW high-confidence pipeline.”

surprises.description: Management said near-term customer benefits from accelerated tax-credit flowbacks will reach parity around 2028–2029 for nuclear PTCs, then investment returns are expected to support durable cash-flow growth into the late 2030s. The preview gave no tax-credit or customer-benefit timing, so this adds a new transition timeline rather than contradicting a stated forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Accelerated tax credit flowbacks benefiting near-term customer costs will reach parity around 2028-2029 for nuclear PTCs,” after which “investment returns are expected to sustain durable cash flow growth into the late 2030s.”

surprises.description: Duke disclosed a $600 million ATM equity sale to settle at the end of 2027, but said it does not plan a large-block equity issuance within the five-year plan. This gives a more bounded financing picture than the preview’s open question about increases in equity needs, while still including an equity issuance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Priced $600 million under its ATM equity program to settle at the end of 2027” and “no large block equity is planned within the 5-year plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Track FFO/debt toward 14.5% and any increase in equity needs.”

in_line: Duke reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $6.55–$6.80, as the preview expected, and expressed confidence in the top half of its 5%–7% growth range beginning in 2028, consistent with the preview’s description of that commitment.
Duke said it is on track to reach its 14.5% FFO-to-debt target for 2026, consistent with the preview’s financing checklist to track progress toward that target.

surprises.description: Revenue was $981 million, about $7 million below the $988.47 million consensus and near the low end of company guidance. Prepared Food and Beverage revenue was roughly $20 million short because of logistics constraints and production inefficiencies, with the delayed revenue shifted into the second half and an estimated $5–6 million EBITDA impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated revenue was $981 million”; Prepared Food and Beverage revenue “fell short by roughly $20 million due to logistics constraints and production inefficiencies,” with that revenue “redistributed into the second half at an estimated $5-6 million EBITDA impact.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus was “$988.47M”; company guidance was “$975M–$1,000M.”

surprises.description: A $17 million IEEPA tariff refund boosted adjusted EBITDA, contrary to the preview’s expectation of a net tariff headwind. The refund also contributed about 200 basis points to Protein margins, though higher prior-year tariff expense and accelerated incentive compensation partially offset the benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA “benefit[ed] from a $17 million IEEPA tariff refund,” partially offset by “$4 million in higher prior-year tariff expense and $5 million in accelerated incentive compensation”; Protein margins reached 24%, “about 200 basis points from tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Tariffs were “Guided at a 25–50 bps net headwind.”

surprises.description: Facility consolidations are now expected to produce $25–30 million in annualized savings by 2028, above the previously stated estimate of $10–15 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: Consolidations covering “approximately 1.3 million square feet” are expected to deliver “$25-30 million in annualized savings by 2028, up from an original estimate of $10-15 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The estimate was previously “$10-15 million.”

surprises.description: The company reported an additional $9 million of expected annual savings from AGV restructuring, including consolidating two facilities into one, and said AGV had its strongest volume quarter in six quarters. The preview did not flag this restructuring or volume recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: AGV restructuring is expected to generate “about $9 million in annual savings (~$3 million in H2 2026),” following AGV’s “strongest volume quarter in six quarters.”

surprises.description: Leverage fell to just below 2.5x, moving into the target range, while year-to-date free cash flow was $179 million at 58% EBITDA conversion. The preview’s latest reported leverage was 2.6x and it provided no free-cash-flow expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Leverage ended the quarter just below 2.5x,” reaching the “2x-2.5x target range”; year-to-date free cash flow was “$179 million (58% EBITDA conversion).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Net debt to adj. EBITDA 2.6x” for Q1 2026.

surprises.description: The company announced a new $200 million share buyback, beyond the $200 million authorization the preview noted was already in place. This was an additional capital-return commitment, not merely a report of purchases under the existing authorization.
surprises.fact_evidence: A “new $200 million share buyback” was announced.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted a “$200M buyback authorized through May 2029” and flagged the “pace of buybacks against the $200M authorization.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a non-cash impairment related to the 2021 Prevenio acquisition, which the preview did not anticipate. The amount was not provided in the supplied facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company took “a non-cash impairment on the 2021 Prevenio acquisition.”

in_line: Orders exceeded $1 billion for a third consecutive quarter, as the preview identified as a key threshold to support the second-half ramp.
Management maintained full-year guidance; the preview’s base scenario anticipated a reiterated FY guide.
Adjusted EBITDA was $168 million on $981 million of revenue, or about a 17.1% margin, within the preview’s cited Q2 company margin guidance of 17.0%–17.5%.
Protein revenue grew 11%, slower than Q1’s 22% growth, consistent with the preview’s warning to watch for a slowdown as the poultry backlog converted.
Prepared Food and Beverage orders had double-digit growth, consistent with the preview’s note that management had flagged close to double-digit order improvement.

surprises.description: Havertys reported Q2 EPS of $0.32, well above the $0.23 consensus estimate. The result was about 39% higher than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 EPS doubled to $0.32 from $0.16 a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | Q2 2026 Consensus | $0.23.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $194.9 million exceeded the $189.2 million consensus estimate by about 3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales up 7.7% to $194.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 2026 Consensus | $189.2M.”

surprises.description: Comparable written sales accelerated rather than rolling over: comps rose 12.3%, versus 7.0% in Q1, and growth stayed in double digits in each month of Q2. The preview identified a rollover from Q1’s pace as a key risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total written sales rose 12.6% (comps up 12.3%), with double-digit written growth in every month: April up 10.6%, May up 15.7%, and June up 10.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Comparable written business vs. Q1's +7.0%. … a rollover here would impair Q3 delivered sales”; the preview also said, “A rollover breaks the written-comp narrative.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin was 61.4%, above the preview’s cited full-year range, but the apparent expansion depended on tariff refunds: excluding about $1.5 million of refunds, margin was essentially flat year over year. That makes the reported margin stronger than the underlying result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 60 basis points to 61.4%, but excluding ~$1.5 million in IEEPA tariff refunds, margin was essentially flat at 60.7% versus 60.8% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | Not found” for Q2; the preview cited FY26 guidance of “60.5–61.0%” and said the bull case required gross margin to “hold at or above 61.3%.”

surprises.description: Average ticket growth accelerated from Q1’s 11.9% to 14%, and design average ticket rose 15.7% with design reaching 36.5% of business. This was a stronger ticket and mix update than the preview’s Q1-based comparison suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Average ticket rose 14% to over $3,800 driven by both mid-single-digit unit-per-ticket growth and pricing, while design average ticket jumped 15.7% to over $8,800, with design at 36.5% of business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Average ticket about $3,700 (+11.9%); design 35.3% of written business”; the preview flagged “Ticket and design mix vs. falling traffic.”

surprises.description: Management gave more specific and forward-looking cost warnings than the preview’s general mention of rising fuel costs in Q2: container rates are set to rise in mid-August, diesel is above $5 per gallon, and product input costs are expected to remain higher through year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A 25%-30% container rate increase starting mid-August, diesel above $5/gallon raising transportation costs, and higher product input costs through year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “cited rising fuel costs across vendor input, freight, and home delivery in Q2.”

surprises.description: Havertys had already repurchased about $16.6 million of shares year-to-date, including a large privately negotiated June purchase, leaving only about $1.8 million of authorization. The preview disclosed the available authorization but did not anticipate that most of it would be used.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased ~723,000 shares for $16.6 million year-to-date (including 600,000 shares for ~$13.9 million in a June privately negotiated transaction), leaving only ~$1.8 million of buyback authorization remaining.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “$16.4M of buyback authorization remaining” after Q1.

in_line: Management reaffirmed FY2026 gross margin guidance of 60.5%–61.0%, as the preview’s base case anticipated; it also identified reaffirmation as the positive outcome to watch.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.58, well above the roughly $0.40 consensus and the $0.55 top of guidance; adjusted EBITDA also reached $49 million, above the $48 million guidance ceiling. The earnings beat was substantially stronger than the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $0.58 and adjusted EBITDA was $49 million, both exceeding the top end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS | ~$0.40”; “Adj. EBITDA | $32–48M”; base scenario: “Adj. EPS $0.38–0.44.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin reached 40.7%, above both the approximately 38.5% estimate and the prior 40% guidance ceiling. However, about 170 basis points of the reported margin came from tariff refunds, so the underlying margin result was much closer to 39%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin reached 40.7%, above the top end of guidance, though it included a ~170 basis point benefit from $4.7 million in tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin | ~38.5% (est.)”; company guide: “37–40%”; “39% or higher, with evidence that tariffs are being offset, is the most bullish outcome.”

surprises.description: The Q3 revenue midpoint of $280 million and adjusted EPS midpoint of $0.45 clear the preview’s stated risk thresholds of $275 million and $0.42. But the EPS midpoint is slightly below the $0.46–$0.47 quarterly pace the preview said was implied by the full-year consensus, making the outlook reassuring against the downside trigger but a little short of that pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance is roughly flat sequentially at the midpoint, with revenue of $265-295 million … and adjusted EPS of $0.30-$0.60.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Q3 revenue guide below ~$275M or an EPS midpoint below ~$0.42 would put the full-year number at risk”; “2H EPS of roughly $0.93, or about $0.46–0.47 per quarter.”

surprises.description: Advanced Solutions fell 9% year over year, despite the preview looking for a turn as the Lockheed Crossbow follow-on began generating revenue. The segment did improve 10% sequentially, and semiconductor gains were offset by lower micromachining and defense sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Advanced Solutions revenue declined 9% year-over-year (though up 10% sequentially) as semiconductor gains were offset by lower micromachining and defense sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Advanced Solutions. Watch for a turn as the $10M Lockheed Crossbow follow-on begins revenue recognition this quarter.”

surprises.description: The Lumibird Medical offer came with a first-year accretion claim for gross margin, EBITDA, and adjusted EPS, plus an estimated $1 billion addition to the addressable medical market—benefits the preview had not specified. The expected Q4 close timing itself was in line with the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company announced a binding offer to acquire Lumibird Medical … expected to close in Q4 2026 and to be accretive to gross margin, EBITDA, and adjusted EPS in the first year while adding ~$1 billion to the addressable medical market.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for a definitive agreement, Q4 2026 close confirmation, and what roughly $350M of cash outlay means for buyback capacity.”

surprises.description: Regional results showed a sharper divergence than the preview discussed: Asia grew strongly, while North America declined. The preview did not set expectations for either region.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Asia revenue jumped 19% year-over-year (now ~34% from China), while North America revenue fell 2% due to weaker cutting, defense, and medical applications.”

surprises.description: Industrial Solutions grew 16% year over year, a strong segment result not anticipated or benchmarked in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Industrial Solutions revenue grew 16% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Emerging growth products increased to 58% of revenue from 53% in the prior quarter, with battery manufacturing demand a major driver. The preview did not discuss this mix measure or set an expectation for it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Emerging growth products rose to 58% of total revenue, up from 53% in the prior quarter, driven largely by battery manufacturing demand.”

surprises.description: Management said it expects the existing medical business to more than double over the next two to three years, a growth outlook not addressed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects to more than double the medical business (currently ~7-8% of revenue) over the next 2-3 years.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $279 million was essentially in line with the preview’s approximately $279.98 million consensus.
Book-to-bill stayed above 1 for a third consecutive quarter, as the preview identified as the clearest demand signal.
The company began shipping the Lockheed Martin CROSSBOW order in Q2, as the preview expected the follow-on to begin generating revenue recognition this quarter.
The Lumibird Medical offer retained the expected Q4 2026 closing timing.

surprises.description: Sysco’s FY26 adjusted EPS was $4.61, slightly above the preview’s roughly $4.59 consensus and the $4.60 top of its reiterated guide. Q4 adjusted EPS of $1.53 also edged the $1.51 consensus, though it was within the preview’s base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EPS of $1.53 and full-year adjusted EPS of $4.61, both exceeding prior guidance despite pausing its share repurchase program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS $1.51”; “FY26 adj. EPS ~$4.59”; FY26 guide was “high end of $4.50–$4.60.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue topped the $21.92 billion consensus, coming in above $22 billion with 4.7% growth versus the preview’s implied 3.7% growth. The beat was modest and the result was close to the preview’s bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 total revenue grew 4.7% to over $22 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sales $21.92B”; “+3.7% YoY”; the bull scenario was “$22.1B+.”

surprises.description: Sysco’s initial FY27 EPS range of $5.02–$5.12 was above the $4.96 consensus and the preview’s $4.85–$4.95 standalone base case, despite the paused buybacks. The 9%–11% growth outlook includes a benefit from the 53rd week, which is about 2% of revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 to adjusted EPS of approximately $5.02 to $5.12, representing 9% to 11% growth, though this includes benefit from a 53rd week (about 2% of revenue).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 adj. EPS ~$4.96”; the base scenario expected “$4.85–4.95 standalone.” The preview also said suspending planned buybacks “removes roughly 2 points of EPS growth.”

surprises.description: Q4 gross margin fell 17 basis points to 18.7%, despite the preview’s expectation that the incentive-compensation headwind would ease. Sysco attributed the decline to a tough strategic-sourcing comparison and elevated inbound fuel costs, although gross profit still grew.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 gross margin declined 17 basis points to 18.7%, pressured by a tough prior-year strategic sourcing comparison and elevated inbound fuel costs, though gross profit still rose 3.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 should see the incentive-comp headwind ease. Gross profit growth needs to reach the operating line.”

surprises.description: Sysco announced a new AI-driven efficiency program targeting about $100 million of net in-year FY27 savings, or roughly $160 million at run rate, which the preview had not anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new AI-driven efficiency program targeting approximately $100 million of net in-year cost savings in fiscal 2027 (roughly $160 million on a run-rate basis), weighted to the second half and to the U.S.”

surprises.description: The call provided sizable expected economics for the Restaurant Depot deal—more than 140 basis points of combined EBITDA margin expansion and $250 million of procurement synergies—while the preview focused on regulatory risk and timing and gave no such benefit estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Restaurant Depot acquisition is expected to expand combined EBITDA margins by more than 140 basis points and deliver $250 million of procurement synergies.”

surprises.description: Sysco raised its quarterly dividend by about 2% to $0.55 and plans roughly $1 billion of FY27 dividends; the preview did not flag a dividend increase or payout plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its quarterly dividend ~2% to $0.55 while planning ~$1 billion in fiscal 2027 dividends.”

in_line: USFS local case growth was 2.6% in Q4, within the preview’s expected 2.5%–3.0% range and above management’s 2.5% floor.
The Restaurant Depot closing is still expected by Q3 FY27, consistent with the preview’s stated target; the preview had already noted the regulatory second request.
International continued its double-digit adjusted operating income growth streak, consistent with the preview flagging that streak as a key item to watch.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.14, below the preview's roughly $0.19 consensus estimate. In contrast, adjusted EBITDA exceeded its estimate, making the EPS shortfall a separate negative surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS of $0.14.”

surprises.description: Management raised its full-year inflation expectation to about $150 million, far above the preview's roughly $65 million H1 inflation figure and the previously expected $60 million–$65 million. The broader and more prolonged cost pressure is a substantial deterioration from that outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year inflation expectations [were raised] dramatically to approximately $150 million, up from a prior estimate of $60 million-$65 million,” driven by “logistics, resins, labor, secondary fiber and chemicals.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The CEO flagged about $65M of unexpected H1 inflation” and “Q2 carrying +$20M incremental on top of Q1's $10M.”

surprises.description: The company now expects full-year adjusted EBITDA at the low end of its $1.05 billion–$1.25 billion range, rather than the preview's base-case expectation that the range would be reaffirmed. Higher and more prolonged inflation is weighing on the outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA is now expected at the low end of the $1.05 billion-$1.25 billion guidance range due to higher and more prolonged inflation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's base case expected the “FY range [to be] reaffirmed”; it described a cut to “~$1.00–1.10B” as the bear scenario.

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted cash flow guidance fell to $600 million–$700 million from the prior $700 million–$800 million framework. That is a meaningful reduction from the preview's stated expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted cash flow guidance was lowered to $600 million-$700 million (midpoint $650 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY26 framework was “adjusted cash flow of $700–800M.”

surprises.description: Net debt declined, as the preview expected, but net leverage rose to 4.7x from 4.4x rather than improving sequentially. The higher leverage is a negative deviation despite the debt reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt was reduced by $100 million in Q2 to $5.5 billion, with net leverage at 4.7x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net leverage must show sequential improvement from 4.4x”; the preview also said Q2 should show “net-debt reduction.”

surprises.description: Pricing actions are now expected to contribute about $60 million to 2026 sales and EBITDA, with a roughly $145 million annualized run rate and further announced increases potentially adding over $200 million more annually. That is a more favorable pricing outlook than the preview's concerns about competitive pressure and delayed realization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pricing actions are expected to favorably impact 2026 sales and EBITDA by approximately $60 million,” with “an annualized run rate of roughly $145 million”; additional announced increases could add “over $200 million more annualized.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “unusual competitive pressure” on the non-contractual book and warned that the RISI index lag “can push recognition out 3–6 months.”

surprises.description: The company raised expected 2026 productivity and cost-reduction savings to roughly $85 million, above the previously expected $60 million program. The higher savings provide a stronger offset to inflation than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In-year cost savings from productivity and cost reduction initiatives were raised to roughly $85 million for 2026, up from a prior expectation of $60 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a “$60M of cost cuts” program and noted that “only about $10M of the $60M cost program was realized in Q1.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $247 million, above the roughly $240 million consensus estimate, and its 11.3% margin was above the estimated 11.0% while landing at the top of company guidance. This was a modestly better quarter than expected despite the reported cost headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $247 million”; “Adjusted EBITDA margin was 11.3% … landing at the top of the guidance range despite a $60 million commodity input and operating cost inflation headwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (Q2) … ~$240M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin (Q2) … ~11.0%.”

surprises.description: Q2 net sales declined 1% year over year, a smaller decline than the preview's expected 1.5% decline and slightly above its approximately $2.17 billion estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales declined 1% year-over-year to $2.2 billion.”

surprises.description: The company cut full-year capital expenditure guidance to below $450 million, lower than the preview's expectation of about $450 million. It also reported a substantial first-half capex reduction versus the prior year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered full-year capital expenditures guidance to below $450 million” and “cut first-half capex by roughly $320 million versus the prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY26 framework included “capex of about $450M.”

surprises.description: Graphic Packaging announced entry into the URB market at its Waco mill, an initiative not identified in the preview. It requires no material capital and has an addressable opportunity above 100,000 tons, though initial orders are only a few thousand tons.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Entering the uncoated recycled paperboard (URB) market at its Waco mill with no material capital required,” targeting “an addressable opportunity exceeding 100,000 tons” and having secured “a few thousand tons of initial orders.”

in_line: The $100 million Q2 net-debt reduction and the plan to pay down $400 million–$500 million of debt in 2026 were broadly consistent with the preview's expectation of Q2 debt reduction and its approximately $500 million full-year paydown framework.
The reported approximately $75 million inventory reduction was consistent with the preview's expectation that the company would make progress on reducing inventory.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $15.7 million, about 8% above the preview’s $14.5 million estimate; the resulting roughly 37.8% margin also exceeded the preview’s approximately 35% base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 13% year-over-year to $15.7 million.” Revenue was $41.5 million, implying an adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 37.8%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA ~$14.5M (my estimate; no published consensus)” and the base scenario expected “$14.3–14.8M / ~35%.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS reached breakeven rather than the expected $0.01 loss. The one-cent improvement was a small beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Breakeven diluted EPS versus a $0.01 loss per share in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q1 FY2027 diluted EPS consensus was “($0.01).”

surprises.description: Recorded Music grew much faster than the preview’s aggregate revenue outlook would reveal, with a sharp lift from a couple of large sync deals. The preview anticipated acquisition support and mid-single-digit organic growth, but did not flag this segment-level, deal-driven surge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recorded Music revenue surged 35% to $14.1 million,” driven by “a 23% rise in digital revenue plus outsized synchronization revenue from a couple of large sync deals closed in the quarter.”

surprises.description: The company used cash in operating activities, with the cash flow decline attributed to royalty-payment timing and higher outgoing advances; the preview had not forecast this quarter’s cash use.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating activities used $1.4 million in cash, a $7.4 million decline versus the prior-year quarter, driven by royalty payment timing and higher outgoing advances.”

surprises.description: Reservoir disclosed a Latin-music expansion through joint ventures with TU Publishing and the acquisition of Nacional Records, a development not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reservoir expanded its Latin music footprint through joint ventures with TU Publishing and the acquisition of Nacional Records,” targeting a market that “grew 17.1% in 2025.”

in_line: Revenue was $41.5 million, essentially matching the $41.46 million consensus estimate; 6% organic growth was consistent with the preview’s expectation of mid-single-digit organic growth.
Management reiterated FY2027 revenue guidance of $186–191 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $75–79 million, as the preview expected.
The special committee provided no new update on the acquisition proposals, matching the preview’s base case of no strategic-review update.

surprises.description: The preview treated reaffirming the full-year high end as the baseline, but Energizer lowered its outlook to the low end of the range. It also cut expected second-half organic growth from roughly 4% to flat-to-up 1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Energizer lowered its full-year outlook to the low end of its range, cutting expected back-half organic growth from roughly 4% to flat-to-up 1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Reaffirming ‘high end’ is the baseline”; the preview also says management was “guiding to the high end” of FY26 adjusted EPS and EBITDA.

surprises.description: The preview’s base case assumed a flat category trend and modest organic growth, but management now expects the battery category to be weaker than flat for the rest of the year, after trends softened by 200–300 basis points. The slowdown was attributed roughly equally to volume erosion and promotional or price pressure, not meaningful retailer destocking.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The battery category trends softened by roughly 200 to 300 basis points relative to prior expectations”; the category is “weaker than the previously anticipated flat trend.” Management said the weakness was split roughly between volume erosion and promotional/price pressure, with retailer destocking not expected to be an additional meaningful headwind.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “Organic: 0% to +1%” and described the key issue as organic net sales growth “versus flat.”

surprises.description: The preview’s guidance math implied Q4 adjusted EPS growth of about 38–43% year over year, while management guided to approximately 25% growth at the midpoint. That is still strong growth, but below the step-up implied by the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided to approximately 25% adjusted EPS growth at the midpoint in the fourth quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied Q4 is about $1.45–$1.50, versus $1.05 in Q4 FY25. That is a 38–43% y/y step-up.”

surprises.description: The preview said no cash had yet been received on the IEEPA refund and that the process and timing remained open. Management now said about $11 million has been collected and the remaining $53 million booked is expected to generate meaningful cash into fiscal 2027, although the full amount has not yet been collected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has already collected about $11 million of IEEPA tariffs with a remaining $53 million booked expected to be a meaningful source of cash generation into fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “No cash has been received on the $64.3M IEEPA refund”; management said the “process and timing is a little open.”

surprises.description: The preview focused on whether weak category trends would undermine Energizer’s sales inflection, but management reported U.S. value growth of 1.8% and volume growth of 5% despite a declining category, along with global gains in both volume and value share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In the U.S., Energizer grew value 1.8% and volume 5% against a declining category, and gained both volume and value share globally.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called organic sales the “central issue,” noted four consecutive quarters of organic decline, and said a positive print would keep the inflection promise.

surprises.description: The preview said second-half free cash flow would have to do heavy lifting but did not flag the completion of Project Momentum or the resulting reduction in facility-exit and severance cash costs and capital spending. Management now expects those cash costs to decline significantly and CapEx to fall by roughly $30 million, or 1% of net sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Project Momentum is being completed this year, with related cash costs for facility exits and severance expected to decline significantly, and CapEx expected to fall by roughly 1% of net sales or $30 million going forward.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY26 free-cash-flow target would require H2 to “do heavy lifting.”

surprises.description: Management characterized the category weakness as near-term consumer caution and value-seeking rather than a structural shift away from batteries, citing healthy device usage and replacement frequency. That qualification partly counters the preview’s concern that consumer caution could signal a more persistent problem.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management described the weakness as “near-term consumer caution and value-seeking behavior rather than a structural shift toward battery-free technologies,” citing healthy device usage and change-out frequency.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed a “cautious consumer” explanation for softness as a bear-case signal.

in_line: Q4 gross margin was expected to be in the low 40s; management said it should be north of 40% and clarified that it would exclude IEEPA credits.

The preview expected a Q3 gross-margin headline in the mid-40s, with tariff-refund effects making the headline number higher than underlying margin; management’s Q4 clean-margin outlook excludes those credits.

surprises.description: TPG's fee-related earnings were well above the preview's $265–275 million base case: FRE was $315 million. The 50% quarterly margin also exceeded the preview's roughly 46–47% expectation, although management said pulled-forward transaction fees elevated it and reaffirmed 47% full-year guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fee-related earnings rose 43% to $315 million,” producing “a 50% FRE margin”; management cautioned the margin was “elevated by pulled-forward transaction fees” and reaffirmed “47% full-year FRE margin guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Fee-Related Earnings (FRE) ... base case $265–275M”; “FRE margin ... About 46–47%.”

surprises.description: Fee-related revenue exceeded the preview's revenue estimate by a meaningful amount: $628 million versus the $573.5 million consensus estimate. The preview noted that revenue definitions were inconsistent, so the comparison is not fully clean.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fee-related revenue grew 27% year-over-year to $628 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total fee revenues | $573.5M”; the preview also cautioned that providers disagreed on “the revenue definition.”

surprises.description: After-tax distributable earnings per share came in above the preview's consensus range and base scenario, at $0.69 versus consensus of $0.62–$0.64 and a $0.64–$0.68 base case. The beat was modest against the preview's scenarios, which already allowed for a stronger result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “After-tax distributable earnings of $280 million, or $0.69 per Class A share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “After-tax DE per share | $0.62 (Zacks) or $0.64 (other providers)”; base scenario “$0.64–0.68.”

surprises.description: The dividend stayed at $0.59 per share, above the preview's mechanically inferred level of about $0.53. The higher-than-expected DE per share also makes that dividend less stretched against the preview's payout assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Declared a dividend of $0.59 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Payout is about 85% of after-tax DE, so a $0.62 print mechanically points to a dividend near $0.53, down from $0.59.”

surprises.description: Fundraising exceeded the preview's near-term checkpoint: TPG raised $16 billion in Q2 and more than $26 billion year-to-date, versus an expectation of about $12 billion in Q2 and roughly $22–25 billion in the first half. The annual target was reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised $16 billion in Q2 and over $26 billion year-to-date,” while “reaffirming its target to raise more than $50 billion in 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 capital raised of about $12B or more”; “H1 needs roughly $22–25B to stay credible.”

surprises.description: Despite the strong fundraising total, real estate fundraising is not expected to activate until near year-end, shifting its FRE contribution into 2027. That is later than the preview's back-half-weighted fundraising framing and raises a more specific timing delay than the annual target alone suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Real estate fundraising [is] largely not activating until near year-end and shifting FRE benefit into 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “2026 is back-half weighted” and asked whether “second half” holds or “shifts to ‘fourth quarter.’”

surprises.description: Management said Q2 benefited from transaction closes pulled forward from Q3, and expects transaction and monitoring fees and capital-markets revenue to step down in the second half. The preview anticipated back-half fundraising but did not flag this pull-forward or the resulting revenue step-down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 benefited from a pull-forward of transaction closes originally forecast for Q3,” so “transaction and monitoring fees and capital markets revenue are expected to step down in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described fundraising as “back-half weighted” and flagged the timing of fundraising, but did not forecast a pull-forward of transaction closes or a second-half fee step-down.

surprises.description: TPG disclosed a substantial new AI-related commitment: more than $4 billion of initial capital as lead founding partner of the OpenAI DeployCo platform. The preview did not anticipate this strategic commitment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Committed over $4 billion of initial capital as lead founding partner of the OpenAI DeployCo platform.”

surprises.description: TPG's disclosed software exposure appeared limited: only about 5% of its most software-exposed fund was in the AI-disruption “mitigate” category, with no new additions. This was a favorable, previously unflagged detail against the potential concern that AI disruption could affect portfolio companies.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Only about 5% of TPG's most software-exposed fund (TPG VIII) is classified in the AI-disruption ‘mitigate’ category with no new additions.”

surprises.description: Private-equity portfolio values rose about 6% in the quarter, and net accrued carry increased 15% to $1.4 billion. The preview identified performance allocations as a swing factor but did not set an expectation for this portfolio appreciation or accrued-carry increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Private equity portfolio value appreciated approximately 6% in the quarter,” driven by EBITDA growth, multiple expansion, and debt paydown, “lifting net accrued carry 15% to $1.4 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called realized performance allocations “the main swing factor for DE,” but gave no expectation for portfolio appreciation or net accrued carry.

surprises.description: The Jackson Financial partnership added another $2.5 billion in commitments in the quarter, bringing commitments to $4.5 billion since February. The preview did not mention this partnership or a contribution from it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Jackson Financial partnership added $2.5 billion in new commitments this quarter, bringing total commitments to $4.5 billion since February.”

in_line: TPG reaffirmed its more-than-$50-billion fundraising target for 2026, consistent with the preview's stated annual target.

The preview flagged activation of fee-earning AUM as an important forward FRE indicator; the call reported $39 billion of AUM not yet earning fees and a roughly $290 million annualized revenue opportunity, but did not provide a directly comparable activation target.

surprises.description: PEM EBITDA reached $416 million, well above the preview’s roughly $250 million threshold for supporting the recovery story and even above its $300 million-plus bull-case marker. The sequential surge came with a 21% rise in average sales price and lower North American natural gas and ethane costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The PEM segment's EBITDA jumped to $416 million,” up $380 million sequentially, driven by “a 21% sequential rise in average sales price and lower North American natural gas and ethane costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Anything above about $250M would support the price-increase story” and its bull scenario had “PEM EBITDA above $300M.”

surprises.description: Westlake reported $3.3 billion of Q2 sales, above the preview’s $3.244–$3.25 billion consensus estimates and its $3.05–$3.15 billion base-case range. The beat versus the consensus figures is modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Westlake reported Q2 2026 net sales of $3.3 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 revenue estimates of “$3.244–3.25B” and a base scenario of “$3.05–3.15B.”

surprises.description: The formerly loss-making Epoxy business returned to profitability, a turnaround not identified in the preview’s expectations or key debates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The formerly loss-making Epoxy business turned around from annual losses exceeding $100 million to profitability in Q2 2026.”

surprises.description: Pipe and fittings volume grew about 20% year over year, rather than suffering the permit-related volume hit mentioned in the preview’s bear scenario. Infrastructure spending and data-center construction supported demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pipe and fittings sales volume grew roughly 20% year-over-year,” fueled by U.S. infrastructure spending and data-center construction.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bear scenario cited “HIP volume hit by permits.”

surprises.description: Although the stated HIP revenue and margin ranges remained $4.4–$4.6 billion and 19–21%, management reset expectations toward their lower ends, citing a more muted North American residential construction outlook. That is weaker than simply maintaining the range without a lower-end tilt, though the preview had already identified a formal guide cut as a risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 HIP guidance was reset toward the lower end of prior ranges” due to “a more muted North American residential construction outlook.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the HIP guide as “$4.4–4.6B revenue, 19–21% margin” and said “A formal cut would be the clearest bear trigger.”

in_line: The profitability plan delivered roughly $150 million of Q2 year-over-year EBITDA improvement and management reaffirmed the $600 million full-year target, matching the preview’s expectation that Q2 contribute about $150 million and that the target be reaffirmed.
The $500 million repayment of 2026 notes was in line with the preview, which said $500 million was called for repayment in Q2.
The Wilhelmshaven acquisition closing was anticipated in the preview, which said it had closed in June and flagged the acquisition for follow-up.
The modest Q3 pipe-volume headwind is consistent with the preview’s expectation that Q3 guidance could be down and that management’s comments on fading momentum would be important.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $308 million, about 4% above the preview’s roughly $295.5 million consensus estimate. The 17% adjusted year-over-year growth also exceeded the preview’s implied 11.7% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenues of $308 million, representing 17% year-over-year growth on an adjusted basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | ~$295.5M … | +11.7%”

surprises.description: DAYBUE sales reached $125 million, well above the preview’s implied $112–115 million range, with strong STIX adoption accompanying the beat: about 40% of U.S. patients were on STIX and it made up roughly 60% of June referrals.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DAYBUE net sales reached $125 million in Q2, up 30% year-over-year with 27% driven by volume, fueled by strong uptake of the newly launched DAYBUE STIX formulation”; “Approximately 40% of all U.S. DAYBUE patients were receiving STIX by the end of Q2, and STIX accounted for roughly 60% of all referrals in June alone.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “DAYBUE net sales | ~$112–115M (implied)”; “DAYBUE ≥ $110M and STIX metrics. Needs evidence STIX is adding net new patients.”

surprises.description: ACADIA raised its full-year DAYBUE sales range by $20 million at both ends, rather than simply reaffirming the $460–490 million outlook in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its 2026 DAYBUE guidance to $480-510 million (from $460-490 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “DAYBUE: $460–490M”; “FY26 guidance reaffirmed at $1.22–1.28B.”

surprises.description: Full-year revenue guidance increased to $1.24–1.30 billion, while the preview expected the prior $1.22–1.28 billion range to be reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total 2026 revenue is guided at $1.24-1.3 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: $1.22–1.28B”; “FY26 guidance reaffirmed at $1.22–1.28B.”

surprises.description: The company lowered its 2026 R&D expense guidance by $30 million at both ends. Management attributed this mainly to a BD milestone moving to 2027 and portfolio prioritization, rather than the preview’s anticipated higher run rate for the rest of the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered its full-year 2026 R&D expense guidance to $355-380 million (from $385-410 million), primarily due to a BD milestone shifting to 2027 and portfolio prioritization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “R&D: $385–410M”; Q1 R&D “implying roughly $103–111M per quarter for the rest of the year.”

surprises.description: The RADIANT readout timing moved away from the August start of the preview’s August–October window: management now expects results in September to October 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pivotal Phase II RADIANT readout … is now expected in September to October 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Topline is guided for August–October 2026.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed an estimated $4 billion peak-sales opportunity for remlifanserin across Alzheimer’s disease psychosis and Lewy body dementia psychosis, with about 60% attributed to ADP and 40% to Lewy body dementia; the preview discussed the readout but not this commercial estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Remlifanserin has estimated peak sales potential of $4 billion across Alzheimer's disease psychosis and Lewy body dementia psychosis, with management splitting the opportunity roughly 60% ADP and 40% Lewy body.”

surprises.description: ACADIA gave a more specific EU launch timeline than the preview: it anticipated a final EC decision in Q3 and a Germany launch in early Q4, while the preview only said the EC decision was pending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ACADIA received a positive CHMP opinion for DAYBUE in the EU following a re-examination, with a final European Commission decision anticipated in Q3 and a Germany launch planned for early Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The EC decision is pending”; “EU DAYBU launch economics, including EC decision timing.”

surprises.description: Management said potential first-generation gene therapies are not expected to affect DAYBUE’s commercial forecast in either the short or long term, a competitive-risk reassurance not raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management stated it does not expect potential first-generation gene therapies to impact DAYBUE's commercial forecast in the short or long term.”

surprises.description: NUPLAZID’s sales were broadly in line with the preview’s implied range, but new-patient prescriptions rose 20% and reached their highest quarterly level since Q1 2018, a stronger demand indicator than the preview specifically anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NUPLAZID delivered $183 million in Q2 net sales, up 10% year-over-year on an adjusted basis with 8% volume growth, with new patient prescriptions up 20% year-over-year to the highest quarterly volume since Q1 2018.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said productivity gains ramp ‘through late 2026.’”

in_line: NUPLAZID Q2 sales of $183 million were within the preview’s implied $180–183 million range and above its $178 million downside threshold.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $392.4 million, about 9% above the roughly $360 million consensus and above even the preview’s $383–390 million bull-case range. This was a substantially stronger result than the preview’s $370–375 million base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 revenue reached a record $392.4 million,” up 27% sequentially and 104% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 Consensus” of “$360.2M (Zacks) / $360.7M”; the preview’s “Base” revenue case was “$370–375M” and its “Bull” case was “$383–390M.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $0.80 exceeded the $0.69 consensus and reached the top of the preview’s bull-case range, rather than the $0.74–0.77 base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.80 in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 Consensus” of “$0.69”; the preview’s “Base” EPS case was “$0.74–0.77” and its “Bull” case was “$0.80–0.84.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $540–560 million was far above the preview’s roughly $410 million consensus and above even its $445 million bull-case threshold. The preview’s base case was $415–430 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue is guided to $540-560 million,” representing “approximately 40% sequential growth at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Forward consensus: Q3 about $410M”; the preview’s “Bull” scenario had “Q3 Guide: ≥$445M” and its “Base” scenario had “$415–430M.”

surprises.description: Scorpio is now expected to become Astera’s largest product line in Q3, whereas the preview said management expected it to become the largest by end-2026. That brings the milestone forward by multiple quarters.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Scorpio is expected to become the company's largest product line by revenue in Q3, one quarter ahead of prior expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management says it becomes the largest product line by end-2026.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP operating margin reached 39.1%, materially above the preview’s roughly 36% expectation; management also guided to about 43% in Q3, indicating further operating leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin improved to 39.1% in Q2” and “is guided to approximately 43% in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Non-GAAP op. margin” at “~36% implied.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin was 73.7%, 70 basis points above the approximately 73% guidance and above the preview’s 73.5% level for supporting a warrant-driven interpretation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was 73.7% (above 73% guidance).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 guidance and consensus at “~73%” and said “Reported gross margin at or above 73.5% would support a ‘warrant-driven’ reading.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a Scorpio-X content opportunity growing well beyond $1,000 per XPU, with total content potentially reaching multiple thousands of dollars per XPU in future generations. The preview discussed the X-Series ramp but did not flag this much larger per-XPU opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management sees Scorpio-X content opportunity growing well beyond $1,000 per XPU in future generations, targeting total content of multiple thousands of dollars per XPU.”

surprises.description: The call reported over 10 customers engaged on Scorpio-X, beyond the preview’s discussion of at least two additional hyperscaler wins. Engagement is not the same as a production win, but it indicates a broader customer funnel than the preview described.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has over 10 customers engaged on Scorpio-X, with additional customers expected to ramp to production by late 2025 or early 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had pointed to “Scorpio wins at at least two additional hyperscalers by late 2026.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a new Leo memory-controller design win at a U.S. hyperscaler and expected 2027 CXL shipments to two U.S. hyperscalers, along with optical and custom solutions targeted for production that year. These customer and product-roadmap details were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new Leo memory controller design win was closed at a U.S. hyperscaler, with volume CXL shipments to two U.S. hyperscalers expected in 2027, and optical/custom solutions also targeted for 2027 production.”

in_line: Q3 non-GAAP gross margin guidance of approximately 72% was in line with the preview’s expectation that a guide of about 72% or below would reinforce the margin-fade concern.

surprises.description: Q2 EPS was $1.43, below the preview’s $1.48–$1.49 consensus range. Management attributed the year-over-year decline partly to higher interest and depreciation/amortization expense and lower transmission revenue, which outweighed favorable weather and sales growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 EPS was $1.43,” down $0.15 from Q2 2025, driven by “higher interest expense, higher depreciation/amortization, and lower transmission revenue,” partially offset by favorable weather and sales growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS: $1.48 (Barchart/Yahoo); $1.49 (Zacks).”

surprises.description: Weather-normalized sales grew 9.6%, above the preview’s base-case 6%–8% range and its roughly 7% growth marker. C&I growth was 12.7%—below Q1’s 14.6% pace, but still well above the preview’s roughly 8% bear trigger.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Weather-normalized sales grew 9.6% year-over-year, with commercial and industrial sales up 12.7% and residential up 5.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “sales growth 6–8%”; the preview said growth “holding at or above about 7%” supports the outlook and that C&I growth “below roughly 8%” would weaken the thesis.

surprises.description: Management raised its full-year outlook within the existing range by saying it expects earnings to finish at the top end, a stronger signal than the plain reaffirmation the preview treated as roughly neutral. Consensus was already near the range’s top, so the improvement in language is positive but limited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now expects full-year 2026 earnings to finish at the top end of its $4.55 to $4.75 per share guidance range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A plain reaffirmation is roughly neutral,” while the preview said anything short of “upper-half language would be a negative”; FY2026 consensus was $4.73.

surprises.description: The preview said all 2026 equity needs were funded and cited about $850 million of priced forwards remaining. Instead, the company reported exhausting its existing $900 million ATM program and filing a new $500 million ATM program, creating additional issuance capacity, though no actual issuance under the new program was reported.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company exhausted its existing $900 million ATM equity program” and “filed a new $500 million ATM program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “All 2026 equity is funded, with about $850M of priced forwards remaining. Any signal of 2027 issuance would pressure the $5.56 FY27 consensus.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that TSMC announced another $100 billion of Arizona investment, bringing its total commitment to $265 billion and plans for up to 12 facilities. The preview identified semiconductor and data-center load as important to growth, but did not anticipate this additional investment announcement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TSMC announced an additional $100 billion Arizona investment, raising its total commitment to $265 billion and expanding plans to up to 12 leading-edge fabrication and packaging facilities.”

surprises.description: Despite the growth outlook around TSMC, its fab electricity contribution was flat year over year; the bulk of the more-than-1-gigawatt demand ramp is still ahead and is expected to accelerate next year. That means the anticipated load has not yet translated into comparable current electricity growth, although the future ramp remains intact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TSMC's fab electricity contribution has been relatively flat year-over-year,” with the bulk of its “more-than-1-gigawatt demand ramp” still to come and expected to accelerate into next year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described C&I, reflecting “data-center and semiconductor load,” as “the core of the growth story” and highlighted Q1 C&I sales growth of 14.6%.

surprises.description: The company disclosed a planned Cholla coal-to-gas conversion that could add about $440 million of capital investment, mostly in 2027–2028, while providing roughly 380 MW of dispatchable generation by 2029. This was not in current CapEx guidance and was not raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The planned Cholla coal-to-gas conversion could add roughly $440 million of incremental capital investment (mostly in 2027-2028) and provide about 380 MW of dispatchable generation by 2029,” and “is not yet in current CapEx guidance.”

surprises.description: Customer growth reached 2.1%, above the midpoint of guidance, and customer and sales growth contributed about $0.11 of quarter-over-quarter earnings benefit. The preview focused on sales growth but did not flag this customer-growth result or earnings contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customer growth reached 2.1%, above the midpoint of guidance,” and customer/sales growth contributed “approximately $0.11 of quarter-over-quarter earnings benefit.”

surprises.description: The company set a new all-time peak demand record of 9,164 MW, more than 500 MW above last year’s record. The preview anticipated record heat but did not cite an expected peak-demand record.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company set a new all-time peak demand record of 9,164 MW on August 2, exceeding last year's record by more than 500 MW.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that Phoenix had “its hottest spring on record in Q2'26” and included “record heat” in its bull scenario.

in_line: The rate case remained on schedule for a decision before year-end: management continued to expect a final commission decision before year-end, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a late-2026 decision. No settlement or ROE signal was reported.

surprises.description: Revenue was $368 million, about 3% above the preview’s $356.5–356.7 million consensus, and grew 10% year over year versus the expected 6.1% growth. That was a stronger top-line result than the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 10% year-over-year to a record $368 million.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $59 million, above the preview’s roughly $55–56 million estimate. The resulting margin was about 16.0%, at the high end of the preview’s expected recovery range rather than merely the 15.5–15.7% base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 11% to a record $59 million”; revenue was $368 million, implying an adjusted EBITDA margin of about 16.0%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$55–56M”; a recovery toward “15.7–16.0%” would support management’s explanation, while the base case was “15.5–15.7%.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS was $0.15, below the preview’s $0.18 GAAP estimate even as adjusted EBITDA beat.
