The call said net income was affected by a $2.5 million charge to dispose of legacy warehouse equipment and a $5 million mark-to-market loss on Class A-2 earn-out shares; both were noncash and excluded from adjusted EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS came in at $0.15”; net income was dampened by “a ~$2.5 million charge to dispose of legacy warehouse equipment and a $5 million mark-to-market loss on Class A-2 earn-out shares, neither affecting adjusted EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP diluted EPS | $0.18.”

surprises.description: Chicago locations appear set to start far earlier than the preview’s already-advanced late-2026/first-quarter-2027 timing: management expects the first locations to operate within weeks. Accel had approvals for 17 of 39 establishment licenses, providing concrete progress toward the opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Accel has been approved for 17 of 39 (approximately 44%) of Chicago establishment licenses,” and management expects “the first Chicago locations to begin operating within weeks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had moved timing to “late 2026 or the first quarter of 2027”; the preview also called Chicago timing the largest value driver.

surprises.description: Fairmount Park’s gross profit reached its highest quarterly level since acquisition and was up 33% year over year. That was stronger than the preview’s focus on reversal of a prior $2 million purse-expense timing shift and margin recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fairmount Park delivered its highest quarterly gross profit since acquisition,” representing “33% growth versus Q2 last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management blamed part of Q1 margin weakness on “a $2M Fairmount purse-expense timing shift that should reverse”; the preview expected recovery toward a 15.7–16.0% margin.

surprises.description: Nebraska and Georgia’s growth remained strong, but management described the states as meaningful contributors to earnings growth, not just revenue growth. That goes beyond the preview’s framing of their double-digit growth as coming from small bases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nebraska and Georgia posted revenue growth of 55% and 47% respectively, and are now meaningful contributors to earnings growth rather than just revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Nebraska and Georgia “grew fastest on small bases” and flagged their “durability” as a key issue.

surprises.description: Nevada’s 17% revenue growth came alongside a 15.8% decline in blended hold per day, as rapid convenience-store expansion increased locations and terminals. The preview flagged hold per day and unit growth as metrics to watch but did not anticipate this sharp productivity dilution or the 6–12-month upgrade transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nevada revenue grew 17% year-over-year with locations and terminals up 54% and 53%, but blended hold-per-day fell 15.8%” due to rapid convenience-store expansion; a “6- to 12-month upgrade transition” is underway.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Hold per day and unit growth. Separate price-driven growth from terminal additions.”

surprises.description: Operating cash flow was only $20 million, or 34% of EBITDA, while $17 million spent on a green tax credit purchase shifted cash into Q3. Excluding that timing item, cash flow was $37 million, or 63% of EBITDA; the preview had expected lower capex to lift free cash flow but gave no cash-conversion estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 operating cash flow was $20 million (34% EBITDA conversion) but $37 million (63%) excluding a $17 million green tax credit purchase shifting cash into Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Lower capex should lift FCF.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA margin recovered to about 16.0%, consistent with the preview’s stated 15.7–16.0% recovery range.
Nebraska and Georgia continued to post the strong growth the preview had highlighted: 55% and 47%, compared with 57% and 43% in Q1, respectively.
Full-year capex guidance remained $60–70 million, as previously guided in Q1 and noted in the preview.

surprises.description: The preview highlighted the $90 million year-three synergy target and treated early capture as a potential catalyst. MasterBrand raised the target to over $100 million, said roughly $30 million had already been executed, and identified additional savings outside the target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its cost synergy target to over $100 million of annual run rate by year 3 post-close, exceeding the original target, with roughly $30 million already executed and ~$15 million expected in the second half of 2026.” The target “excludes both the $30 million of legacy MasterBrand cost actions and American Woodmark's completed Monterrey, Mexico facility closure.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The target is $90M run-rate by the end of year three. Any quantified early capture would be a bull catalyst.”

surprises.description: The preview said combined-company guidance was uncertain, with reinstatement or silence identified as the main swing factor. The company gave second-half guidance of $2.05–$2.11 billion in sales and $129–$149 million in adjusted EBITDA, although it did not provide full-year guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Second half 2026 guidance calls for net sales of $2.05-$2.11 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $129-$149 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “No FY2026 guidance exists. Reinstatement, or silence, is the largest swing factor.”

surprises.description: American Woodmark’s contribution was substantially weak on profitability: the call said its fiscal Q3 and Q4 performance came in below expectations, citing excess fixed capacity and absorption pressure. Its 32-day contribution was $126 million of sales but only $4 million of EBITDA, and the company expects about $730 million of American Woodmark sales but just $20 million of EBITDA in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “American Woodmark's fiscal Q3 and Q4 performance came in below expectations due to excess fixed capacity and absorption pressure,” with “$126 million sales and $4 million EBITDA in the 32-day period.” Second-half guidance includes “~$730 million in sales but only ~$20 million in EBITDA” from American Woodmark.

in_line: Legacy MasterBrand sales were $690 million, down 5.6% year over year, consistent with the preview’s expected mid- to high-single-digit decline and its approximate $654–$693 million guidance range.
Legacy MasterBrand adjusted EBITDA was $58 million, within the preview’s $51–$61 million guidance range; its 8.4% margin was also within the preview’s 7.8%–8.8% range.

Combined Q2 sales of $815 million were at the top of the preview analyst’s $770–$815 million build, which explicitly attributed the difference from the $743 million consensus largely to the merger stub.

surprises.description: Revenue was $70.5 million, about $2 million above the preview’s roughly $68.5 million Q2 bar. The 15% year-over-year increase was stronger than the preview’s 11–12% consensus growth estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 15% year-over-year to a record $70.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “At a $68.5M Q2”; consensus revenue was “$67.85M” or “$68.22M,” with “+11% to +12%” growth.

surprises.description: Scoliosis revenue fell 9% rather than growing the 5–10% the preview described as normal comp math. The call attributed the decline to zero 7D unit sales and lower Brazil set sales, despite mid-teens growth in underlying implant sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Scoliosis revenue declined 9% to $16.9 million due to zero 7D unit sales (versus ~$2 million a year ago) and lower Brazil set sales, though underlying implant sales grew mid-teens.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A +5–10% print is normal comp math”; the preview also flagged “International, Brazil, and 7D capital sales” as a key issue.

surprises.description: VertiGlide’s reported evidence of adoption was less conclusive than the preview’s anticipated full-market-release milestone: 124 surgeons were trained, but set deployments were only $2.9 million, down from $4.6 million, with most of the remaining planned deployments still to come in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “VertiGlide now has 124 surgeons trained and set deployments were only $2.9 million (down from $4.6 million), with about $5 million of the planned $10 million full-year set deployment remaining, mostly in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Vertiglyde was “slated as a Q2 event” and expected to move “to full market release”; the preview called for a “hard dollar or unit datapoint.”

surprises.description: Q2 free-cash-flow usage was worse than the preview’s expected breakeven to $2 million of usage, although it improved substantially year over year. Management maintained its expectation of break-even or better for the full year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow usage improved 78% ($10.8 million) to $3.1 million used,” with management confident in “break-even or better for the full year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 at breakeven to $(2)M keeps the FY breakeven claim credible”; the preview said “$(5)M or worse” would make it arithmetic-only.

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 74%, above the preview’s estimated 72–73% range. Management still expects roughly 73% for the full year as some 7D sales resume.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded to 74% from 72% a year earlier, aided by favorable mix, though management expects roughly 73% for the full year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~72–73% (no formal consensus).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA of $6.8 million modestly exceeded the preview’s modeled $5.5–6.5 million range, though it was below the preview’s bull-case range. The roughly $25 million full-year target was reiterated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached a record $6.8 million (nearly 10% margin), up from $4.1 million in Q2 2025, while the ~$25 million full-year adjusted EBITDA target was reiterated.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA at or above $5.5M”; the modeled range was “~$5.5–6.5M.”

surprises.description: Trauma and deformity grew 26%, with early 3P HIP contributions, but the call did not provide the hard dollar or unit datapoint the preview sought for the Q2 3P Hip expansion. The strong segment growth is positive; the ramp’s scale remains unquantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trauma and deformity revenue grew 26% to $52.6 million, aided by early 3P HIP contributions and pull-through of legacy products toward single-source contracts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: 3P Hip was “slated as a Q2 event” and expected to move “to expanded supply”; the preview said to look for “a hard dollar or unit datapoint.”

surprises.description: Specialty bracing delivered over 20% growth, and DF2 had been adopted at more than 150 children’s hospitals with high margins and no inventory requirement—an additional growth driver not highlighted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Specialty bracing (OPSB) grew over 20%, with DF2 now adopted in over 150 of roughly 300 U.S. children's hospitals at high margins with no inventory requirement.”

in_line: The company raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $265–269 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation that guidance would be raised and its stated clean-bull threshold of a $265 million or higher low end.
The approximately $25 million full-year adjusted EBITDA target was reiterated, as the preview expected.
Management remained confident in full-year free-cash-flow break-even or better, in line with the preview’s FY breakeven expectation.

surprises.description: The preview described a third FY26 raise as a bull-case possibility and expected the range might simply be narrowed toward its upper half. Jacobs did raise guidance for a third consecutive time, lifting its net revenue growth range to 9.5%–10% and raising the EPS range floor to $7.20, although the new $7.20–$7.30 EPS midpoint is close to consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “raised FY26 guidance for the third consecutive time,” lifting adjusted net revenue growth to “9.5%-10%” and adjusted EPS to “$7.20-$7.30.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Two raises already; a third raise versus a narrowing to the low end is the likeliest fulcrum.” The base scenario expected the “FY range narrowed toward the upper half”; a third raise was in the bull scenario.

surprises.description: The preview noted net leverage of 2.1x at FQ2 and flagged leverage as an issue to watch. Jacobs reported 1.8x and said it reached its below-2.0x target a quarter early.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage declined to 1.8x, reaching the below-2.0x target a quarter early.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net leverage was 2.1x at FQ2.”

surprises.description: Q3 organic adjusted net revenue growth exceeded the preview’s roughly 7.5% frame, coming in above 8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 was supported by “more than 8% organic adjusted net revenue growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management's FQ3 frame was “~7.5% net revenue growth.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin came in modestly above the preview’s approximately 15% frame, at 15.2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 adjusted EBITDA reached $367 million, up 17%, with margin at 15.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management's FQ3 frame was “~15% adj. EBITDA margin.”

surprises.description: The preview expected FQ4 adjusted EBITDA margin to be above 16%; the call guided to approximately 16%, a little below that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 guidance calls for approximately 16% adjusted EBITDA margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance calls for ~15% in FQ3 and above 16% in FQ4.”

in_line: Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.84 was in line with the preview’s $1.83 Investing.com consensus and $1.84 Barchart consensus.

Cash conversion was broadly in line with the preview’s H2 adjusted FCF target of $600–$700 million: Q3 adjusted FCF was $541 million, and Q4 guidance of roughly $150 million implies about $691 million for H2.

Backlog reached a new record and book-to-bill remained strong at 1.4x gross and 1.2x net, consistent with the preview’s expectation of continued backlog strength and its concern that a ratio below roughly 1.0x would change the narrative.

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was a smaller loss than the preview’s $7.07 loss consensus, at negative $6.75. The acquired IPR&D charge was $11.2 billion versus the preview’s $11.5 billion estimate, while EPS excluding those items and nonrecurring revenue was $2.27 versus the preview’s rough $2.05–$2.10 underlying estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Acquired IPR&D expenses of $11.2 billion … drove non-GAAP diluted EPS to negative $6.75, versus $2.27 excluding those items and nonrecurring revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (non-GAAP, incl. IPR&D) | –$7.07”; “Consensus on the $11.5B charge implies roughly $2.05–2.10 of underlying EPS.”

surprises.description: HIV sales rose 12%, and Gilead raised full-year HIV growth guidance to 9%–10%. That is stronger than the preview’s report that guidance had moved to about 8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HIV sales rose 12% year-over-year to $5.7 billion,” prompting Gilead to raise full-year HIV growth guidance “to 9%-10% from the prior 8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “HIV growth guidance moved to about 8% from about 6%.”

surprises.description: Yeztugo sales were $232 million, below the preview’s roughly $250 million level at which the annual guide was at risk and below the roughly $278 million quarterly average needed across Q2–Q4 to reach the $1 billion guide. Gilead nevertheless maintained the approximately $1 billion full-year outlook and reported over 70% persistency.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Yeztugo generated $232 million in sales, up 40% sequentially,” showed “over 70% persistency,” and had “full-year guidance maintained at approximately $1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Reaching the ~$1B FY guide requires about $278M per quarter across Q2–Q4. A Q2 print well below ~$250M puts the guide at risk.”

surprises.description: PrEP sales doubled year over year, exceeded $1 billion for the first time in a quarter, and reached a $4 billion annual run rate. The preview had no Q2 PrEP consensus or specific quarterly expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The PrEP business doubled year-over-year and exceeded $1 billion in quarterly sales for the first time, now operating at a $4 billion annual run rate.”

surprises.description: Cell therapy’s Q2 sales decline matched the preview, but Gilead’s full-year outlook called for a mid-teens decline, extending the weakness beyond the quarter. The preview identified cell therapy as a weak spot but gave no full-year decline estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cell therapy sales declined 14% year-over-year to $417 million … with full-year guidance now calling for a mid-teens percentage decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cell Therapy | $417M” consensus; “consensus expects –14% for Q2.”

surprises.description: Biktarvy sales of $3.8 billion beat the preview’s roughly $3.6 billion consensus by about 6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Biktarvy sales of $3.8 billion were up 7% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Biktarvy | ~$3.6B.”

surprises.description: Trodelvy sales of $457 million slightly exceeded the preview’s $448 million consensus, with growth supported by its first-line metastatic triple-negative breast cancer approvals.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trodelvy sales grew 26% year-over-year to $457 million,” boosted by “new FDA approvals in first-line metastatic triple-negative breast cancer across PD-L1 status.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Trodelvy | $448M”; the preview said to focus on uptake following the first-line mTNBC approval.

surprises.description: Livdelzi sales more than doubled to $167 million, and positive Phase III IDEAL data supported a potential label expansion as early as next year. The preview did not flag Livdelzi or provide a sales expectation for it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Livdelzi sales more than doubled year-over-year to $167 million, with positive Phase III IDEAL data supporting potential label expansion as early as next year.”

surprises.description: Management attributed slower HIV treatment-market growth in Q2 to ACA subsidy changes pushing patients out of insurance coverage, an access headwind not identified in the preview. This occurred even as Biktarvy sales grew 7% and total HIV sales rose 12%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HIV treatment market growth slowed in Q2 due to Affordable Care Act subsidy changes pushing patients out of insurance coverage.”

in_line: Cell therapy Q2 sales were $417 million, matching the preview’s consensus, and its 14% year-over-year decline matched the preview’s expected decline.

surprises.description: GAAP diluted EPS was $0.16, below the preview’s $0.1931 GAAP consensus estimate, even though the company returned to profitability. The shortfall was modest in absolute terms.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP diluted EPS of $0.16” and “approximately $17 million net income.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP basis) | $0.1931 (Markets Daily)”

surprises.description: Margins rebounded more strongly than the preview’s base case of a partial recovery: adjusted EBITDA margin reached 21%, versus 13% in Q1, while total contribution margin rose to 55%. Secured margin also improved sharply, with the company now expecting secured products to reach breakeven by Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was approximately $77 million … with a 21% margin, up sharply from a 13% EBITDA margin in Q1”; “Total contribution margin improved to 55% (from 50% in Q1)”; “secured margin improving 61 points to negative 35%, with secured products expected to reach breakeven by Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario said “margin recovery partial”; it also flagged whether EBITDA would “rebound from Q1’s 13% margin.”

surprises.description: July origination growth slowed to 34% year-over-year from Q2’s 50%, as UMI rose about 9% during the quarter and reached the top of the company’s guidance range. The preview noted a largely stable consumer in May but did not anticipate this slowdown or the worsening UMI trend.
surprises.fact_evidence: “July origination growth slowed to 34% year-over-year from 50% in Q2,” reflecting “the modest headwind from UMI rising ~9% over the course of the quarter”; UMI rose “to 1.5, the top of its 1.4-1.5 guidance range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the company had described the consumer as “largely stable” in May.

surprises.description: The company reported substantially more funding capacity and less balance-sheet reliance than the preview could quantify: loans held on balance sheet fell to 5.9% of outstanding principal, and committed capital partnerships are expected to add up to $10.8 billion of incremental capacity year-to-date.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Loans held on the balance sheet fell to 5.9% of total outstanding principal, the lowest in nearly two years,” as committed capital partnerships were expected to add “up to $10.8 billion in incremental capacity year-to-date.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “securitization demand, loans held on balance sheet, and operating cash flow” as items to watch, without specifying an expected level.

surprises.description: Auto and Home expanded rapidly and together reached about 14% of originations, a notable increase from their small historical share that the preview did not forecast for Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Auto originations grew 264% year-over-year and 62% sequentially while Home grew 139% year-over-year,” with Auto and Home together comprising “about 14% of total originations versus 1% in Q4 2021.”

surprises.description: Upstart disclosed that it had sunset its Auto Refinance business, a strategic exit not mentioned in the preview. Management attributed the decision to capital discipline, so the shareholder implication is mixed rather than clearly adverse.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company sunset its Auto Refinance business this quarter for capital discipline.”

surprises.description: Beyond the already-known conditional OCC approval, management described a specific operating plan: it aims to launch Upstart Bank in early 2027, move the bulk of originations through it, and raise deposits shortly after launch. The preview anticipated bank commentary but did not state these plans or timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “aims to launch Upstart Bank in early 2027,” expects to “move the bulk of originations through it,” and plans to “raise deposits shortly after launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Upstart Bank commentary: economics, capital needs, and timing after the conditional OCC approval” as an issue to watch.

surprises.description: Management provided unexpectedly strong underwriting and loan-performance figures: its model was reported at 2.74 times the accuracy of traditional credit scoring, and the last 12 loan vintages exceeded Treasuries by about 660 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The underwriting model reached 2.74x the accuracy of traditional credit scoring,” and “the last 12 loan vintages exceeded Treasuries by ~660 basis points.”

in_line: Q2 originations were already disclosed at about $4.23 billion before the release; the reported $4.2 billion and 50% year-over-year growth were therefore broadly in line with what the preview said was already known.

The company reiterated full-year guidance of about $1.4 billion in total revenue, $1.3 billion in fee revenue, and $294 million in adjusted EBITDA, as the preview expected the existing outlook to be reiterated or changed.
Conditional OCC approval for the bank charter had already been reported before the release.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $25.4 million, well below the $30–32 million company guide and $30.82 million consensus; year-over-year growth was 5.6%, rather than the roughly 28% implied by consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 5.6% year-over-year to $25.4 million but came in below prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus $30.82M” and “Company guidance (Q2) $30.0–32.0M”; consensus “implies about +28% y/y.”

surprises.description: The full-year revenue outlook was cut to $100–110 million, far below the prior $130–135 million guide and the preview’s roughly $130 million consensus. The new outlook implies roughly flat year-over-year performance rather than the previously guided 26–30% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue outlook was cut sharply to $100-110 million, down from the prior $130-135 million guidance, implying roughly flat year-over-year performance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue | About $130M” and company guidance of “$130–135M (+26–30%).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was only $52,000, far below the $1–3 million Q2 guide and its roughly $2 million midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA collapsed to just $52,000 versus $1.1 million in the prior-year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | … Company guidance (Q2) $1.0–3.0M”; the preview calls about $2 million the guide midpoint.

surprises.description: The expected EG4 qualified-inverter volume ramp was pushed out to Q4, with the partner’s operational problems helping drive the sharp revenue-guide reduction. The preview flagged the ramp as a key proof point but did not anticipate this delay.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The volume ramp of the key EG4 Section 45X and ITC-qualified optimized inverter partnership was pushed from Q1/Q2 to Q4 2026 due to the partner's internal operational issues, a primary driver of the guidance cut.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Also watch the EG4 inverter ramp.”

surprises.description: GO ESS contributed just $2.2 million, or 8.6% of revenue, because the new GO Battery ramped more slowly than planned; this was another contributor to the full-year guide cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GO ESS contributed only $2.2 million (8.6% of revenue) as the new GO Battery ramped more slowly than planned, another factor behind the guidance reduction.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “GO ESS battery mix” and the “GO ESS 47.9 kWh European launch” as items to watch, but did not forecast a slow ramp.

surprises.description: Gross margin fell to 39.3%, below the preview’s likely 43–44% range. The 42.1% figure excluding GO ESS was also below that expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin fell to 39.3% from 44.7% a year ago, though excluding GO ESS it was 42.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Likely about 43–44%” for Q2 gross margin.

surprises.description: Management’s Q3 adjusted EBITDA outlook ranges from a $1 million loss to only $500,000 of profit, indicating another weak quarter after the Q2 shortfall; the preview provided no Q3 EBITDA outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance ranges from a $1 million loss to a positive $500,000.”

surprises.description: Reported GAAP net income was positive at $2.2 million, but it was supported by a $3.2 million tax benefit despite a $1 million pretax loss. The preview’s roughly breakeven adjusted-EPS expectation did not anticipate this tax-driven gap between reported net income and pretax performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income of $2.2 million was driven by a $3.2 million income tax benefit, masking a pretax loss of $1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “EPS (adj.) –$0.0025 (about breakeven).”

surprises.description: Cash rose materially and inventory declined rather than creating the cash-consumption concern flagged in the preview: cash increased by $5.3 million sequentially while inventory fell 34.3% from year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash rose to $16.9 million, up $5.3 million sequentially and $9.2 million from year-end 2025, while inventory fell 34.3% ($10.7 million) from year-end to $20.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said cash was “$11.6M against a $10M Wells Fargo facility” and flagged inventory because “rebuilding it would consume cash.”

surprises.description: U.S. sales declined 4% year over year following the residential clean-energy tax-credit expiration, offering no evidence of a clear recovery in the channel the preview identified as needing to find a floor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. sales declined 4% following the expiration of the residential clean energy tax credit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 was “the first read on whether that channel has found a floor.”

surprises.description: EMEA, rather than the Americas, was the dominant contributor to revenue: it drove 73.1% of sales, with Germany and Italy growing year over year. The preview did not identify this regional concentration or growth pattern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EMEA drove 73.1% of revenue with Germany and Italy growing 6% and 20% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Management said a return to growth could come as early as Q1 2027, a recovery timetable not addressed in the preview and notable against the newly lowered, roughly flat 2026 outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects a return to growth potentially as early as Q1 2027.”

surprises.description: Management newly characterized U.S. and EU restrictions on foreign-produced or high-risk-vendor inverters as tailwinds for its U.S. manufacturing strategy; the preview did not discuss these potential benefits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management … views FCC restrictions on foreign-produced inverters and EU restrictions on high-risk vendors as tailwinds for its U.S. manufacturing strategy.”

surprises.description: Freshworks reported $55.9 million of non-GAAP operating income, well above the preview’s roughly $42 million estimate. The 24% operating margin also substantially exceeded the prior-quarter 17.9% margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income reached $55.9 million (24% margin)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income” consensus: “About $42M”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $0.17, above the preview’s $0.13 consensus and above its $0.15–$0.16 base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $0.17.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS” consensus: “$0.13”; Base scenario: “$0.15 – $0.16”

surprises.description: Freshworks reached positive GAAP net income in Q2, ahead of its stated target to achieve GAAP profitability by the end of 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Positive GAAP net income of $3.2 million ($0.01 GAAP EPS) ahead of schedule.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Having originally targeted GAAP profitability by end of 2026.”

in_line: Revenue of $237.4 million beat the $235 million high end of prior guidance, as the preview expected; it also fell within the preview’s $236–$238 million base-case range.
EX ARR grew 24% in constant currency, in line with the preview’s expectation of about 24–25% growth and above its stated below-24% warning threshold.
CX ARR grew 4% in constant currency, consistent with the preview’s expectation of low-single-digit growth and above its at-or-below-3% concern threshold.
Net dollar retention was 105% in constant currency, matching management’s approximately 105% Q2 guidance cited in the preview.

FY2026 revenue guidance was modestly raised: the new $963.5–$966.5 million range has a $965 million midpoint, consistent with the preview’s base case of a modest raise and its noted $965 million confidence threshold.
Free cash flow per share remained on track to meet or exceed $0.94, matching the preview’s stated FY2026 expectation.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $443 million, above the preview’s roughly $437 million buy-side bar as well as the $420.6 million consensus. The beat was meaningful versus consensus but only about 1.4% above the buy-side bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $443 million” and beat guidance by “$23 million (5%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus is $420.6M, but a mid-single-digit beat on the midpoint would put the buy-side number near $437M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $92 million, roughly $5.5 million above the preview’s approximately $86.5 million consensus and above the guidance midpoint. The 20.7% margin itself was essentially in line with the preview’s expected margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $92 million” and came in “$5 million above the guidance midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$86.5M” consensus; company guidance was “$86.2–86.9M (20.4–20.8% margin).”

surprises.description: The company raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance by $8 million and free cash flow guidance by $20 million to $255 million. The preview gave the prior FCF range but did not anticipate the size of these additional outlook upgrades.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA guidance raised $8 million to $405 million and free cash flow raised $20 million to $255 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance: adj. EBITDA margin 22.1–22.4%; FCF $234.5–235.5M.”

surprises.description: Full-year GAAP EPS guidance was raised to a $0.10 midpoint, well above the prior $0.02–$0.04 range. The preview expected GAAP-positive full-year results but did not signal guidance at this level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year GAAP EPS guidance was raised to a $0.10 midpoint, well above the prior $0.02-$0.04 range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY guided GAAP-positive.”

surprises.description: Superscale customer and ARPU growth were both 17%, below the preview’s roughly 20% comparison points and its checklist calling for ARPU growth at or above 20%. The reported rates were still described as well above the company’s long-term model growth rates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Superscale customers grew 17% year-over-year to 197 and superscale ARPU rose 17% to $1.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Both grew about 20% in Q1”; the checklist also called for “ARPU growth at or above 20%.”

surprises.description: Sales pipeline growth and sales productivity were notably strong: pipeline was up more than 60%, while per-seller pipeline creation more than doubled, despite quota-carrying headcount rising only 11%. The preview did not flag this operating momentum.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total sales pipeline was up more than 60% year-over-year and over $100 million higher than 90 days ago, with per-seller pipeline creation up more than 100%, while quota-carrying headcount rose only 11%.”

surprises.description: Expansion within existing customers accelerated: customers using multiple use cases grew 90%, cross-sell and upsell wins rose 43%, and average contract values on wins increased more than 40%. The preview did not identify these as expected results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customers using more than one use case grew 90% year-over-year, cross-sell/upsell deals won rose 43%, and average contract values on deals won increased more than 40%.”

surprises.description: The call reported that AI adoption is associated with unusually strong customer retention: the 20% of customers that comprehensively adopted the tools account for roughly 70% of revenue, and their net revenue retention is 400 basis points above the company average. The preview did not anticipate this retention disclosure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 20% of customers who comprehensively adopted AI tools account for roughly 70% of revenue, and these AI adopters have year-to-date net revenue retention 400 basis points above the company average.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for a first joint Palantir enterprise client, but the call reported two Palantir-sourced deals closed out of two, alongside new OpenAI and Snowflake partnerships. These partnerships are largely excluded from guidance, although the facts do not say whether the anticipated client was named.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Newly announced partnerships with OpenAI, Palantir, and Snowflake are largely excluded from guidance, with Palantir-sourced deals achieving a 100% hit rate (two of two closed).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Palantir Foundry integration. Announced in late June, with the first joint enterprise client expected this quarter. A named client is the largest available upside.”

surprises.description: AI costs were kept below 1% of revenue while unit AI costs fell nearly 40%, an efficiency disclosure the preview had not anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total AI costs kept under 1% of revenue as unit AI costs fell nearly 40%.”

surprises.description: Management said a one-time tax benefit later in the year could provide additional upside to GAAP EPS beyond the raised guidance. The preview did not mention this potential item, and no amount was provided.
surprises.fact_evidence: The $0.10 GAAP EPS midpoint excludes “potential additional upside from a onetime tax benefit later this year.”

in_line: Full-year revenue guidance was raised to a $1.818 billion midpoint, within the preview’s base expectation of roughly $1.80–$1.82 billion and above its $1.81 billion softness threshold, though below the bull-case threshold of at least $1.83 billion.
The 20.7% adjusted EBITDA margin was essentially in line with the preview’s approximately 20.6% expectation.
The quarter was GAAP profitable, consistent with the preview’s flagged GAAP-positive-quarter possibility; the preview also anticipated another beat-and-raise.

surprises.description: Total revenue was $169.6 million, above the preview’s consensus range of $157.3 million–$159.2 million. The gap was about $10 million–$12 million, or roughly 7%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue was $169.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Consensus $157.3M (trackers range $157.3M–$159.2M).”

surprises.description: FILSPARI U.S. sales reached $141.1 million, above the preview’s implied estimate of about $132 million–$137 million. The preview’s base case was approximately $134 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FILSPARI contributing record U.S. revenue of $141.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FILSPARI US net sales … implied ~$132M–$137M”; base case “~$134M.”

surprises.description: The FSGS launch was stronger than the preview’s central expectation of a respectable but small initial contribution: management said demand, payer access, fulfillment, and revenue all outpaced the comparable initial phase of the IgAN launch. Uptake was described as rapid but not a temporary demand bolus, while most FSGS prescribers had written for only one patient so far.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FSGS launch is exceeding internal expectations”; “demand, payer access, fulfillment, and revenue all outpacing the comparable initial phase of the IgA nephropathy launch”; “no evidence of a demand bolus in FSGS”; and “the vast majority of FSGS-prescribing physicians have written for only a single patient so far.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base scenario: “FSGS starts respectably but small.”

surprises.description: The call reported more than 2,000 patient start forms across IgAN and FSGS, but did not provide a separate FSGS count, despite the preview identifying that count as a key first disclosure. The combined figure is strong, but it does not fully answer the specific question the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 2,000 new patient start forms across IgA nephropathy and FSGS in the quarter,” with IgAN forms “tracking north of 900 since the Q4 REMS modification.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FSGS patient start forms (first disclosure).” The preview also said, “FSGS PSF count. This was promised for this call.”

surprises.description: The reported R&D and SG&A total of $156.4 million exceeded the preview’s approximate $142 million build for those two expense lines. The reported amount included $22.2 million of non-cash charges, and management cited trial enrollment, manufacturing, and the FSGS launch as drivers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total GAAP R&D and SG&A expenses were $156.4 million (including $22.2 million in non-cash charges), with increases driven by HARMONY Phase III enrollment, pegtibatinase manufacturing, and the FSGS launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Building up R&D (~$58M), SG&A (~$84M), and royalty (~$31M)”—approximately $142 million for R&D and SG&A.

surprises.description: The company reported a $5 million Chugai milestone within license and collaboration revenue, an unanticipated one-off revenue item in the preview. The preview instead flagged the possible classification of a $25 million Mirum milestone; the call facts do not state how that Mirum payment was booked.
surprises.fact_evidence: “License/collaboration revenue was $8.2 million (including a $5 million Chugai milestone).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The $25M Mirum milestone … could land in revenue, other income, or a divestiture gain.”

surprises.description: A substantial convertible-note refinancing was reported: Travere issued $525 million of 0.5% notes due 2032, repurchased about $221 million of 2.25% notes due 2029, and incurred a $40 million inducement expense. The preview discussed cash and the expected July Everest payment but did not anticipate this refinancing or its expense; quarter-end cash was consequently reported at about $489.2 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ended Q2 with approximately $489.2 million in cash and investments after a convertible refinancing (repurchasing ~$221 million of 2.25% 2029 notes and issuing $525 million of 0.5% 2032 notes), incurring a $40 million inducement expense,” and “subsequently paid Everest $112.5 million upfront … in July.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash and financing” was a key item to watch; the preview cited Q1 cash of $264.7 million and noted that the $112.5 million Everest upfront payment “hits Q3 as a cash outflow.”

in_line: Management again provided no numeric FY2026 guidance, consistent with the preview’s expectation that guidance could be deferred after the company had declined to give numeric guidance throughout the year.

surprises.description: AMD’s Q3 revenue guide was expected around $12.5B, with the preview’s base case at $12.6–12.9B. The company guided to approximately $13B, above both expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of approximately $13 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3'26 revenue guide” consensus was “$12.5–12.53B”; the base scenario expected “$12.6–12.9B.”

surprises.description: Data Center revenue was above the preview’s roughly $6.5B consensus, but fell just short of the $6.75B-or-higher buy-side bar identified as needed for a genuine beat. The result was therefore a modest beat on published consensus but a slight miss versus the higher whisper.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data center segment revenue grew 107% year-over-year to a record $6.7 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus was “about $6.5B”; the preview said “the buy-side needs a $6.75B or higher Data Center figure for the print to read as a genuine beat.”

surprises.description: The preview gave no FY2027 growth forecast, but AMD now expects server CPU revenue to grow more than 70% and total Data Center revenue to more than double; management said AI growth could be well over 100%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AMD guided full-year 2027 server CPU revenue to grow more than 70% year-over-year and total data center segment revenue to more than double,” with AI growth potentially “well over 100%.”

surprises.description: AMD said customer demand for Helios is running ahead of its initial forecasts, an upside signal not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management said customer demand is tracking ahead of initial forecasts.”

surprises.description: Management raised its long-term market estimates for both AI accelerators and server CPUs. The preview did not give prior TAM estimates, so the size of the revision cannot be compared numerically.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its market outlook,” expecting the data center AI accelerator TAM to reach “~$1.4 trillion by 2030” and the server CPU TAM “~$220 billion.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue modestly exceeded the preview’s $11.29–11.32B consensus range, though it was within the preview’s base scenario of $11.5–11.7B.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 50% year-over-year to a record $11.5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus was “$11.29–11.32B”; the base scenario forecast “$11.5–11.7B.”

in_line: Q2 gross margin was 56%, in line with the preview’s approximately 55.8% consensus and AMD’s approximately 56% guidance; Q3 gross margin guidance was also approximately 56%, as expected.

The preview expected initial Helios shipments in September and flagged shipment timing as a key issue. AMD said the platform is entering production this quarter, with initial shipments ramping through Q4 into 2027; the call facts do not indicate a clear timing slip.
The preview flagged H2 pressure on PC and Gaming. AMD’s outlook for a softer PC market in the second half was consistent with that concern.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue less ancillary services was $164 million, above the $155.6 million guidance midpoint and both cited consensus estimates; it also exceeded the $159.4 million top of guidance. Management attributed the beat largely to travel and hospitality strength.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue less ancillary services reached $164 million,” beating “the midpoint of guidance,” largely on “Travel/hospitality strength.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave Q2 RLA guidance of “$151.7M – $159.4M (midpoint $155.6M)” and consensus of “$154.3M” or “~$156.6M.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $24 million at a 14.6% margin, well above the preview’s expected $21–22 million base-case range and the company’s approximately 13.75% margin guidance. The margin expanded about 160 bps year over year rather than the roughly 75 bps indicated by the Q2 guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $24 million with a 14.6% margin,” expanding “~160 bps year-over-year” and coming in “above the upper end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “$21–22M (13.5–14.0%),” and company guidance was “~+75 bps Y/Y at midpoint (~13.75%).”

surprises.description: Management raised FY26 FX-neutral revenue growth guidance to 21%–27% from 18%–24%, lifting both ends of the range by 3 percentage points. This is a stronger outlook than the preview’s key question of whether the existing range would be reaffirmed or trimmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “raised full-year 2026 guidance to 21%-27% FX-neutral revenue growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 RLA growth guidance of “18–24% FX-neutral” and flagged the guide as a key issue to watch.

surprises.description: FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin expansion guidance rose to 200–400 bps, versus the prior 175–375 bps range, with the midpoint reaching about 23%. This is a modestly better full-year margin outlook despite the weaker gross-margin trend.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised guidance to “~200-400 bps of EBITDA margin expansion (reaching ~23% at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of “+175 to +375 bps, to ~22.8% at midpoint.”

surprises.description: Gross-margin pressure was worse than the preview’s expected range: adjusted gross margin fell about 450 bps to 56.6%, beyond the preview’s estimated 250–400 bps Q2 compression. Management also now expects the full-year reported decline to be closer to 350 bps, worse than the preview’s cited 200–300 bps FY26 guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin fell ~450 bps year-over-year to 56.6%,” and the “full-year margin decline [is] now expected closer to 350 bps reported.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 guidance called for “200–300 bps of compression” and that “Q2 implies roughly 250–400 bps of Y/Y compression.”

surprises.description: Management explicitly incorporated higher U.K. visa rejection rates and expects U.K. revenue to decelerate, ending the year below overall company growth. The preview identified U.K. visa weakness as a risk but said the outlook did not clearly address the U.K.; this call supplied a concrete, negative outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “baked in higher U.K. visa rejection rates, expecting U.K. revenue to decelerate and exit the year below overall company growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the guidance “does not clearly address the UK” and noted that Truist cited the U.K. in its downgrade; its bear scenario referenced “UK visa weakness quantified.”

surprises.description: Management upgraded its FY26 GAAP net-income outlook to more than $50 million, or fourfold growth. The preview said FY26 EPS guidance was not found and did not flag this earnings target, so the upgrade was not part of the stated pre-release expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “upgraded GAAP net income to grow fourfold to over $50 million.”

surprises.description: Management introduced a multiyear target of $1 billion in annual organic revenue at a 30% adjusted EBITDA margin, and said it expects to reach about 25% margin by 2027 even as transformation investment peaks. The preview did not discuss these targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company set a “multiyear target of $1 billion in annual organic revenue with 30% adjusted EBITDA margin,” and “expects to reach ~25% EBITDA margin by 2027 when transformation investment peaks.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that AI now resolves about 45% of customer inquiries without human intervention, with a target above 50% by year-end. The preview did not discuss this operating metric or a comparable automation target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI now auto-resolves about 45% of customer inquiries without human intervention with a target of over 50% by year-end.”

in_line: Management held its U.S. student visa assumption at a 30% decline, matching the preview’s statement that the guide assumed U.S. student visas down 30%.

surprises.description: Q4 non-GAAP EPS was $0.41, above the preview’s consensus of about $0.36–$0.37 and the company’s $0.36–$0.38 guidance range. That was a clear beat of the expected quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 total revenue was $152.5 million (up 13% YoY) with non-GAAP EPS of $0.41”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 non-GAAP EPS | $0.361 (Aug 3); $0.37 elsewhere” and “$0.36 – $0.38” company guidance

surprises.description: FY27 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $1.58–$1.62 is above the preview’s $1.55 consensus, with the midpoint at $1.60. The low end also clears the preview’s stated disappointment threshold of $1.48.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 guidance calls for … non-GAAP EPS of $1.58-$1.62”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2027 non-GAAP EPS | $1.55 (+25.8%)” and “≤$1.48 EPS” as the bear-case threshold

surprises.description: FY27 subscription revenue guidance of $528.7–$532.7 million exceeds the preview’s $515–$525 million range for a healthy SaaS outcome. This is stronger than the preview’s stated benchmark even though total revenue guidance is broadly in line.
surprises.fact_evidence: “subscription revenue of $528.7-$532.7 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SaaS guidance of about $515–525M would be a healthy outcome.”

surprises.description: Intapp quantified Celeste’s full-quarter contribution at over 20% of net new bookings, doubling sequentially. The preview specifically wanted a full-quarter figure and cited more than 15% in Q3, when Celeste had only been in limited availability for four to five weeks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI now represents over 20% of net new bookings in Q4, doubling sequentially”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management needs to quantify Celeste's share of net new bookings for the full quarter, not just anecdotes”; Q3 had “over 15% of net new bookings in its 4–5 weeks of limited availability.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue of $152.5 million edged above even the preview’s highest cited consensus figure of $152.3 million and cleared its bull-case threshold of $152 million, though the beat versus the high estimate was narrow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 total revenue was $152.5 million”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “other sources quoted up to $152.3M”; bull scenario: “≥$152M”

surprises.description: The company reported more than 30 cloud migrations in Q4, its highest quarterly total ever, and said conversions carry a 20%–30% uplift multiplier. The preview discussed planned migration-driven license runoff but did not anticipate or quantify a quarterly record or the uplift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed more than 30 cloud migrations in Q4, its highest quarterly migration number ever” and “conversions carrying a 20%-30% uplift multiplier.”

in_line: FY27 total revenue guidance of $656.5–$660.5 million was broadly in line with the preview’s $656.3 million consensus and its $650–$660 million normal-guidance range.

Cloud ARR of $495.7 million, up 29%, was within the preview’s expected $495–$501 million range and above its stated deceleration concern threshold of below $490 million, although it fell short of the preview’s $500 million / 30% bull catalyst.
Cloud net revenue retention stayed at approximately 123%, matching the preview’s expectation that stable or higher retention would be the positive signal.

surprises.description: The preview expected Q2 revenue of at least $68.5 million, the low end of guidance; reported revenue before reimbursements was $68.3 million, slightly below that floor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue before reimbursements was $68.3 million … slightly below the low end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance (Q2 …): $68.5M – $70.0M.”

surprises.description: The preview said S&BT needed to grow sequentially from $36.4 million to support the trough narrative; instead, the segment fell 2% to $35.6 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Global S&BT sequential growth. The core segment … needs to grow from $36.4M in Q1. A second sequential decline would break the trough narrative.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag a delay to IBM’s newly launched collaboration; management said IBM had deferred joint go-to-market activities, creating a potential pipeline headwind even as it advances other alliances.
surprises.fact_evidence: “IBM, which launched a global go-to-market collaboration in March, has deferred joint go-to-market activities, while the company is advancing alliances with ServiceNow, TCS, and Genpact to fill its pipeline.”

surprises.description: The preview had no Q3 gross-margin expectation, but management guided to 46–47%, a further step-up from Q2’s 44.1% and above the Q2 margin range the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance [is] targeting a further step-up to approximately 46-47%.”

surprises.description: The preview sought a quantified AI metric but did not anticipate this measure: management estimated it is capturing about 20% of the delivery model’s productivity and margin potential, with a goal of reaching closer to 50% by year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management estimates it is capturing roughly 20% of the productivity and margin potential from its AI-enabled delivery model and expects to reach closer to 50% by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any quantified AI platform metric. Hackett has not disclosed ARR, bookings or attach rates for ZBrain or AI XPLR. A first credible number would be the largest potential re-rating event.”

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate a Q3 AI-transition charge; the company expects to incur about $1 million, primarily for severance tied to AI-driven headcount reductions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company will incur an approximately $1 million AI transition charge in Q3, primarily for severance from headcount reductions tied to AI-driven productivity improvements.”

surprises.description: The preview raised cash and balance-sheet concerns but did not anticipate an increase in borrowing capacity; the company amended its credit facility to provide $125 million of capacity against $81 million of debt.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company amended its credit facility to increase borrowing capacity to $125 million against $81 million of total debt outstanding.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash flow, DSO and the balance sheet. Check operating cash flow, the AR reduction and DSO against the $6.1M cash balance.”

surprises.description: The preview did not provide a Q4 outlook; management said Q4 results should exceed prior-year levels even with significantly fewer high-margin VAR sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[The company] expects Q4 results to exceed prior-year levels despite significantly fewer high-margin VAR sales.”

in_line: Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.34 landed at the midpoint of Q2 guidance and matched the preview’s $0.34 MarketBeat consensus estimate.
Q2 adjusted gross margin of 44.1% was within the previewed 44–45% guidance range.
Q3 adjusted EPS guidance of $0.37–$0.39 had a $0.38 midpoint, meeting the preview’s stated threshold for the promised inflection; the preview said the midpoint needed to be at least $0.38.
Positive Q2 operating cash flow matched the preview’s expectation that cash flow would turn positive.
The company reported stock buybacks, as the preview specifically identified buyback activity as something to watch.

surprises.description: The active selling pipeline reached $140 million, far above the preview’s $24 million threshold for supporting growth. The preview expected a level just above the prior quarter’s $24–25 million pipeline, not a reported pipeline several times that size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The active selling project pipeline reached a record $140 million, up approximately 33% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pipeline above $24M … would support growth.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 21.6%, clearing the preview’s 19% recovery-validation threshold and landing in the low 20s. The improvement was tempered by a year-over-year decline and management’s report that petroleum-based input inflation and higher conversion costs pressured margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 21.6% from 26.1% year-over-year, pressured by petroleum-based raw material inflation and higher conversion costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “At or above 19% validates the recovery”; the preview also listed FY26 gross margin guidance as “Low 20s.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $1.5 million, clearing the zero threshold the preview identified as the key psychological line. The preview had no EBITDA consensus or company guidance, so the positive result was better than that stated threshold rather than a beat against an estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations turned positive at $1.5 million (5.7% of sales), reversing a loss of roughly $300,000 in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A positive print would be the first as a pure-play. Zero is the psychological line.”

surprises.description: The company reported 17 converted commercial opportunities, below the preview’s expectation of at least 25 wins. The reported 26% conversion rate was above the cited industry benchmark, but did not offset the lower opportunity count relative to that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company converted 17 commercial opportunities across 13 customers worth approximately $5.8 million in annualized revenue at a 26% conversion rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pipeline above $24M and at least 25 wins would support growth.”

surprises.description: Management flagged moderate gross-margin contraction in Q4 because of seasonality and custom manufacturing program turnover. That added a specific near-term margin headwind to the preview’s emphasis on recovery toward low-20s margins, although the call facts do not say the full-year outlook changed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided investors to expect moderate gross margin contraction in Q4 due to seasonal patterns and custom manufacturing program turnover, consistent with 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 gross margin guidance as “Low 20s” and said management had expected margins to “normalize throughout the year.”

surprises.description: Cash fell to $28.1 million after a $29.5 million decline from year-end, while the company repurchased $6.9 million of shares and used $7.7 million in operations. The preview called out cash and buybacks as a debate, but the reported cash draw was substantial; total liquidity remained about $46 million with no revolver borrowings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash fell about $29.5 million from year-end to $28.1 million, driven by the Midwest acquisition, $6.9 million in share repurchases, and $7.7 million used by operations, leaving roughly $46 million total liquidity with no revolver borrowings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash is down from $57.6M at year-end, so buyback pace and any use of the July escrow release” were items to watch; continued repurchases would signal confidence, while a quiet buyback would suggest cash preservation.

surprises.description: The cash conversion cycle lengthened by 12 days to 75 days, an unflagged working-capital headwind. Management’s initial goal is to improve it by five days, which it said could release roughly $1–1.5 million in cash.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The cash conversion cycle increased 12 days to 75 days,” with an initial target of “a 5-day improvement worth roughly $1 million-$1.5 million in cash.”

surprises.description: SG&A fell by about $900,000 to $5.5 million, or 21.5% of sales versus 35.5% a year earlier. The preview did not flag this cost reduction, and the reported longer-term target is roughly 15% of revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A fell about $900,000 to $5.5 million (21.5% of sales versus 35.5% prior year), with a longer-term target of roughly 15% of revenue.”

in_line: Midwest Graphic Sales was quantified at $1.9 million in Q2 sales, entered at roughly 26% gross margin, and was immediately accretive to adjusted EBITDA, consistent with the preview’s expectation that it would be immediately accretive.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $214 million, well above the preview’s $181–182 million consensus range. This was a substantial beat against the expected quarterly result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $214 million, the highest quarterly revenue in company history.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus (Zacks) $181.01M”; “Consensus (Investing.com) $182.1M.”

surprises.description: Crysvita revenue of $156 million came in above the preview’s expected rebound toward or above $120 million and the roughly $136–142 million quarterly pace implied by its full-year guide. Its quarterly contribution was stronger than the preview’s framing led investors to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CRISVITA contributing $156 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 Crysvita revenue. Is there a rebound toward or above the $120M booked in Q2 2025?” The preview also said the full-year guide implied “roughly $136–142M per remaining quarter.”

surprises.description: The quarterly loss was narrower than the preview’s EPS consensus range: the company reported a $0.90 per-share loss versus expectations of $1.22–$1.27 per share. That was a sizable earnings beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss for the quarter was $92 million, or $0.90 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS: –$1.27” (Zacks), “–$1.23” (Investing.com), and “–$1.22” (TipRanks).

surprises.description: Operating cash use fell to $97 million, compared with the preview’s bearish scenario of burn staying near $200 million per quarter. The reported burn was materially lower, though the preview did not present $200 million as its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net cash used in operations of $97 million, a significant decrease from Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bear scenario said “burn stays near $200M a quarter.”

surprises.description: Management gave more specific and encouraging Angelman trial context than the preview provided: one of the two endpoints can establish statistical success, and management said prior Phase I/II data showed nearly a 10-point Bayley improvement against a 5–6 point clinically meaningful change and an expected placebo effect of one point or less. These details were not covered in the preview, and they are not a Phase III result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Phase III ASPIRE Angelman study uses a split alpha (80% to Bayley-4 cognition raw score, 20% to MDRI), requiring only one endpoint to hit—Bayley p≤0.04 or MDRI p≤0.01—for statistical success.” Management said “a 5-6 point Bayley cognition change is clinically meaningful,” while prior Phase I/II combined data showed “near a 10-point Bayley improvement at one year,” with an expected placebo effect of “one point or less.”

surprises.description: The preview noted that GTX-102 topline results were expected in H2 2026; management narrowed the ASPIRE readout window to September/October. That gives investors a more precise near-term timing window, without resolving the trial outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The GTX-102 ASPIRE Phase III Angelman readout in September/October.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GTX-102 (Angelman) Phase 3 Aspire topline is expected in H2 2026.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed regulatory hurdles for citruzumab that the preview did not flag: the MHRA may require a new randomized study, and the FDA needs additional clinical data and does not yet accept BMD as a primary approval endpoint. This points to more work before a potential BLA than the preview had indicated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The MHRA may require a new randomized study, while the FDA is open to alternative fracture analyses but needs additional clinical data before a potential BLA, as BMD is not yet accepted as a primary approval endpoint.”

surprises.description: Management identified monetizing priority review vouchers for DTX401 and UX111, if approved, as a source of non-dilutive capital for its profitability plan. The preview discussed cash runway and the 2027 cost target but did not mention this potential funding source.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management targets profitability in 2027 driven by double-digit revenue growth, expense discipline … and non-dilutive capital from monetizing priority review vouchers for DTX401 and UX111 if approved.”

surprises.description: Management described launch-readiness advantages for the upcoming gene therapies that were not quantified in the preview: about 75% institutional overlap with existing products and QTCs already under contract. This adds concrete evidence of existing infrastructure for the launches.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The upcoming gene therapy launches leverage existing commercial infrastructure with ~75% institutional overlap with Dojolvi and Mepsevii,” and “QTCs already under contract.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance; the preview’s base and bull scenarios anticipated the FY26 guide being held.
Management reaffirmed combined R&D/SG&A guidance, consistent with the preview’s expectation of flat to slightly lower full-year expenses.
The 2027 profitability target and at-least-15% reduction in combined R&D/SG&A versus 2025 were consistent with the preview’s stated profitability and expense targets.
The DTX401 PDUFA on August 23 and UX111 PDUFA on September 19 matched the dates in the preview.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue came in well above the preview’s midpoint expectations: total revenue beat the top of company guidance by $11.3 million, and recurring revenue reached $415.6 million. The preview had Q4 total revenue consensus around $430.9–431.4 million and recurring revenue around $405 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 recurring revenue grew 12.4% to $415.6 million and total revenue grew 11%, with results beating the top end of revenue guidance by $11.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Consensus … ~$430.9–431.4M”; “Recurring & other revenue … Consensus … ~$405M.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EBITDA substantially exceeded expectations, beating even the top of guidance by $12.9 million. The preview’s consensus was about $131 million, and the guided margin range was 30.0–30.6%, below the reported 32.7%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EBITDA was $145.5 million (32.7% margin), exceeding the top of guidance by $12.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … Company guide … $128.6–132.6M (30.0–30.6% margin) … Consensus ~$131M.”

surprises.description: Fiscal 2026 total revenue and recurring revenue finished above the company’s prior outlook: total revenue was approximately $1.8 billion, versus guidance of $1.755–1.760 billion, and recurring revenue growth was 12.2%, slightly above the guided 11–12% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal ’26 finished with approximately $1.8 billion in total revenue (11% growth) and recurring revenue growth of 12.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance … total revenue $1.755–1.760B (~+10%); recurring & other $1.638–1.643B (+11–12%).”

surprises.description: Fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA also finished above the prior full-year outlook, reaching $654.9 million versus guidance of $638–642 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA reached $654.9 million (37% margin), up 12.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance … adj. EBITDA $638–642M.”

surprises.description: A newly disclosed accounting change will lift fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA margins by 120–140 basis points as contract-cost amortization is spread over eight rather than seven years. That mechanical uplift is larger than the roughly 100 basis points of margin expansion the preview said the Street modeled, so reported margin improvement will include a sizable accounting benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An accounting change extending deferred contract cost amortization from 7 to 8 years will add approximately 120-140 basis points to adjusted EBITDA margins in fiscal ’27, ratably over the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Street models roughly 100bps of expansion.”

surprises.description: The fiscal 2026 repurchase total implies a much smaller buyback in Q4 than the preview highlighted as a possible signal: after $350 million repurchased through Q3, the full-year total of $398.1 million implies roughly $48 million of additional Q4 repurchases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Paylocity repurchased 2.8 million shares for $398.1 million in fiscal ’26.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$350M repurchased year to date (2.3M shares)”; “Aggressive Q4 buying at sub-$110 prices would be a credible signal.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that the recent AI acquisitions will be a slight margin headwind in fiscal 2027, a near-term cost not specified in the preview. Management said the products should become margin-accretive over time and reaffirmed its 80%+ gross-margin target at $3 billion of revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The recent Grayscale and Aidora AI acquisitions are subscale and represent a slight margin headwind in fiscal ’27, but management expects new products to be margin-accretive over time and reaffirmed the 80%+ gross margin target at $3 billion revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Grayscale and Aidora … are both described as immaterial to revenue”; “Investors need pricing evidence for the premium AI SKU.”

in_line: Fiscal 2027 total revenue guidance of $1.880–1.895 billion was broadly in line with the preview’s approximately $1.89 billion consensus.

Fiscal 2027 recurring/other revenue growth guidance of about 8% was consistent with the preview’s implied recurring/other consensus of roughly $1.77–1.78 billion, although it was below the preview’s 9%+ upside case.
The assumption of flat client workforce levels in fiscal 2027 matched the preview’s stated expectation that management’s model assumed flat year-over-year client workforce.

surprises.description: The preview worried AM&C might post a second straight quarter of low-single-digit growth after Q1’s 3%. Instead, AM&C revenue rose 40% to $105 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Advanced Materials and Chemicals segment grew revenue 40% to $105 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A second straight quarter of low-single-digit growth after +3% in Q1 would undercut the thesis.”

surprises.description: The preview’s base case put operational EBITDA around $23 million, with the bull case calling for a result well above that. Kodak reported $36 million, substantially above the base case and consistent with a strong bull-case outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operational EBITDA jumped 300% to $36 million from $9 million in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: ... Operational EBITDA ... Around $23M”; “Bull: ... Well above $23M.”

surprises.description: The preview’s bull case called for revenue growth of about 10%, while its base case was about 5%. Revenue rose 18%, exceeding even the bull-case growth assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenue rose 18% year-over-year to $311 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bull: Revenue up about 10%”; “Base: Revenue up about 5%.”

surprises.description: The preview identified high aluminum costs as a possible margin headwind and expected silver’s decline to help margins. Instead, gross margin rose 7 percentage points despite higher aluminum and silver costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit increased 61% to $82 million, lifting gross margin to 26% from 19% a year earlier despite higher aluminum and silver commodity costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Silver ... helps margins”; “Aluminum, a Print plate input, was still about $3,400/tonne in June 2026”; the bear case cited “aluminum costs hit Print.”

surprises.description: The preview described silver as having fallen sharply by mid-July and highlighted a risk of write-downs on high-cost inventory. The call instead said silver prices had more than doubled from year-end levels and that inventory increased $37 million, partly because of silver prices and higher volumes under new supply terms.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory increased $37 million, largely due to silver prices more than doubling from year-end levels and higher silver volumes carried under new supply terms.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Silver fell from about $121/oz in January 2026 to roughly $57–58/oz by mid-July, which helps margins, but it raises the risk of write-downs on high-cost inventory.”

surprises.description: The preview expected the June $50 million term-loan payment but did not describe the resulting leverage or interest savings. The call reported debt to EBITDA at 1x and said the repayments cut quarterly interest expense by $9 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total debt to EBITDA improved dramatically to 1x in Q2 2026 from 23x in Q2 2025”; “The company made $100 million in term loan principal repayments year-to-date, including an additional $50 million payment in June, cutting interest expense by $9 million in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Confirm that the $50M term loan payment was made”; “Term loan $200M after a December pension paydown and a further $51M prepaid in Q1. Another $50M is due by June 1, 2026.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag pension income as an earnings issue. The call reported an $11 million year-over-year decline after the CRIP plan termination and said pension income would remain below prior-year levels throughout 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pension income declined $11 million year-over-year following the CRIP pension plan termination, and management expects pension income to remain below prior-year levels throughout 2026.”

in_line: Commercial print revenue grew 10%, consistent with the preview’s base-case expectation that print and AM&C would grow.
The company made the expected additional $50 million term-loan payment in June.

GAAP net income was positive, in line with the preview’s warning that a likely derivative gain could make GAAP results positive for reasons unrelated to operations; the call said the year-over-year improvement was also aided by the absence of the prior-year impairment charge.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $182.2 million, above the preview’s roughly $178.7 million consensus and above its $182 million bull-case threshold. The beat was larger than the preview’s base case anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 revenue grew 11% year-over-year to $182.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (Q2) … Street consensus ~$178.7M”; bull scenario: “Revenue $182M+.”

surprises.description: Qualys raised its full-year revenue range to $732–738 million, above the preview’s suggested constructive raise to roughly $727–731 million and the prior $721–727 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $732-738 million … from prior $721-727 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise to $727–731M with H2 growth lifted is the constructive case.”

surprises.description: Q2 EPS of $1.98 exceeded the preview’s higher cited consensus of $1.79 as well as the company’s $1.73–1.80 guidance range, rather than landing near the preview’s $1.90–1.95 base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EPS was $1.98.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS (Q2) … $1.68 (Benzinga) or $1.79 (Investing.com/MarketBeat)”; base scenario: “$1.90–1.95.”

surprises.description: Full-year EPS guidance rose to $7.74–7.88, above the prior $7.44–7.65 range and the preview’s roughly $7.55 consensus; the preview did not specify an expected EPS guidance raise of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lifted full-year EPS guidance to $7.74-7.88 from $7.44-7.65.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 non-GAAP EPS … ~$7.55”; the preview lists prior guidance of “$7.44M – $7.65M.”

surprises.description: Total NDR reached 105%, one point above the preview’s expected flat 104% and meeting its stated 105%+ upside marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net dollar expansion rate improved to 105% from 104% last quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided total NDR flat this year. 105%+ would be an upside surprise.”

surprises.description: The ETM/CSAM customer cohort NDR stayed at 107% instead of moving toward the preview’s 109–110% watch level, so the cohort expansion rate did not show the expected improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ETM/CTEM customer cohort NDR held steady at 107%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether ETM cohort NDR moves toward 109–110%.”

surprises.description: The revenue mix showed a pronounced channel/direct split: partners grew 22% and reached 54% of revenue, while direct revenue was essentially flat. The preview did not flag this divergence or set an expectation for the channel mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Channel partners now account for 54% of total revenues (up from 49% a year ago) and grew 22%, while direct revenue was essentially flat.”
