surprises.description: Management said post-Mythos AI-threat demand was still early pipeline and conversations, not a Q2 revenue driver, with enterprise budgets expected in later quarters. The preview did not discuss this demand or set an expectation for near-term AI revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Post-Mythos AI-threat demand [was] still early-stage pipeline and conversations rather than a Q2 revenue driver,” with enterprise budgets expected “over subsequent quarters.”

surprises.description: ETM/CSAM’s LTM share of total bookings rose to 12% from 11% in the prior-quarter figures, but remained below the preview’s above-13% marker; its 14% share of new bookings matched the prior-quarter figure. The mix therefore improved in total bookings but did not reach the preview’s stated marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ETM and CSAM combined reached 12% of total bookings and 14% of new bookings on an LTM basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ETM/CSAM is 11% of LTM bookings and 14% of new bookings”; “Movement toward 109%+ and above 13% would support the bull case.”

in_line: Second-half current billings growth guidance remained at 7–8%, matching the preview’s stated baseline rather than accelerating.
ETM/CSAM’s 14% share of new bookings was unchanged from the prior-quarter figure cited in the preview.

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin declined 30 bps year over year, rather than increasing by the 120–220 bps implied by the preview’s 44%–45% guide. Productivity savings and favorable currency were outweighed by inflation, net tariff impacts, and unfavorable mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin declined 30 basis points year-over-year”; ~200 bps of productivity savings and 40 bps of favorable currency were “offset by inflation, net tariff impacts, and unfavorable mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin guide 44%–45%”; the preview described that as “+120–220 bps.”

surprises.description: Q3 organic sales growth was 1.1%, below the preview’s expectation of roughly 2%–3% sales growth. The comparison is not exact because the preview’s consensus was for net sales while the reported figure is organic growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 organic net sales returned to growth, rising 1.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 net sales guide: +2% to +3%”; consensus net sales of $575.9M “implies +2.8% vs. continuing ops.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA came in below the preview’s estimated $85–95M range, at $78.9M. Adjusted operating income also fell substantially year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell to $78.9 million from $81.2 million”; adjusted operating income declined to $53 million from $63.6 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: ~$85–95M (derived).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS beat the preview’s $0.64 consensus, reaching $0.72. It was flat year over year, with a $0.04 favorable currency impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS from continuing operations was $0.72, flat year-over-year (aided by a $0.04 favorable currency impact).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $0.64.”

surprises.description: The company narrowed its FY2026 guidance ranges while keeping the EPS and EBITDA midpoints unchanged; the organic-sales range also became narrower and its lower bound moved up. This was more specific than the preview’s expectation of a simple reaffirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management reaffirmed guidance “at the midpoint”: organic sales “flat to +0.5%,” adjusted EPS “$1.80–$2.00,” and adjusted EBITDA “$250–$260 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 guidance of organic sales “-1% to +2%,” adjusted EPS “$1.70–$2.10,” and adjusted EBITDA “$245–265M,” and said an EPS reaffirmation would be neutral.

surprises.description: International sales declined amid a sizable, unexpected supply-chain disruption from the wet-shave manufacturing consolidation. Management characterized the drag as transitory and expects international sales to return to mid-single-digit growth in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: International sales declined 1.4%; supply-chain disruptions created a “~350–400 bps drag on international sales in Q3,” which management expects to resolve, guiding international back to “mid-single-digit growth in Q4.”

surprises.description: Wet shave remained down overall, but branded wet shave returned to growth while private label fell sharply; the preview had flagged restructuring but did not lay out this split performance or the limited market-share loss amid heavier promotions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wet shave organic sales declined 1.9% as private label fell 10%,” while branded wet shave was “up nearly 1%”; U.S. branded market share was “down only 40 bps amid heightened promotional competition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s wet-shave watch item was “Confirmation that ~$90M of charges holds.”

surprises.description: Management gave a favorable early outlook for FY2027, expecting gross-margin expansion and a return to low-single-digit organic sales growth, ahead of formal guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects fiscal 2027 gross margin to expand year-over-year and signaled a return to low-single-digit organic sales growth,” with formal guidance expected in November.

surprises.description: Hawaiian Tropic’s reported share gains and rise in brand ranking were stronger brand-specific evidence than the preview had provided, which highlighted sun-care share gains as something to watch but did not anticipate this result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hawaiian Tropic grew share 110 bps and rose to the #4 sun care brand from #6 a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q3 needed to show that prior sun-care share gains “reach shipments.”

surprises.description: Cremo continued a long run of strong grooming growth, including especially rapid growth at its top retailer, a brand-specific result not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cremo posted its seventh consecutive quarter of ~20%+ grooming growth and grew 70%+ at its top retailer.”

in_line: North America organic sales rose 3%, consistent with the preview’s expectation of low-single-digit positive H2 North America growth.
FY2026 adjusted free-cash-flow guidance remained $80–$110M, matching the preview.
Year-end net leverage of 3.3–3.4x was within the preview’s expected 3.3–3.5x range.
The call confirmed the previously reported rejection of Yellow Wood’s unsolicited offer; the preview had already noted that the board rejected the bid.

surprises.description: EVgo cut its 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook from a range that could reach positive $20 million to a range of negative $25 million to negative $5 million. The revised range is entirely loss-making, although management still expects Q4 to be positive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to a loss of negative $25 million to negative $5 million, with Q4 expected to be positive while Q3 remains negative.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$(20)M to +$20M” and flagged that trimming the range “to all-negative” would weaken the Q4'26 profitability thesis.

surprises.description: EVgo lowered its 2026 revenue range to $400–430 million, below the preview’s expected reaffirmed range of $410–470 million. Both ends of the range are lower, particularly the upper end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “For full-year 2026, EVgo guided total revenue of $400 million to $430 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described FY26 revenue guidance as “$410M – $470M (unchanged)” and said consensus “Reaffirm expected.”

surprises.description: Daily throughput per stall was weaker than expected: it fell 2% year over year, even though it improved 7% sequentially. The preview highlighted throughput as a key metric and warned that a result below 270 kWh/day would indicate structural utilization dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Daily throughput per stall declined 2% year-over-year but grew 7% sequentially, coming in softer than expected due to legacy equipment weakness and winding-down OEM charging credit programs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch throughput per stall and that “Below 270 would suggest utilization dilution is structural rather than seasonal.”

surprises.description: EVgo disclosed a Tesla agreement to deploy EVgo-branded V4 500-kilowatt Superchargers with Magic Dock, serving both NACS and CCS vehicles—a major expansion that the preview did not anticipate. The financial contribution is expected to begin meaningfully in 2027, rather than in 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EVgo entered an agreement with Tesla to deploy EVgo-branded V4 500-kilowatt Superchargers with Magic Dock technology serving both NACS and CCS vehicles, which management says more than doubles its addressable market”; “meaningful financial impact starting in 2027 rather than 2026.”

surprises.description: EVgo reduced its VIO outlook after a substantially lower long-term EV forecast from S&P, a demand headwind not raised in the preview. The forecast still implies a doubling of the vehicle park, so the outlook is lower but not a contraction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EVgo reduced its VIO outlook, citing S&P's June 2026 forecast of nearly 13 million EVs by 2030, a figure 60% lower than the forecast from three years ago, though still representing a doubling of the vehicle park.”

surprises.description: EVgo reported $835 million of available liquidity, including more than $630 million of undrawn facility capacity—far more financing headroom than the preview’s cash figures alone suggested. Available liquidity includes undrawn borrowing capacity, so it is not directly comparable to cash.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EVgo ended Q2 with approximately $835 million in available liquidity, including over $630 million of undrawn capacity on its DOE and commercial bank facilities.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Cash $122.4M at Q1-end, about $223M after an $81M DOE draw on May 1” and flagged “Capex, DOE drawdown pace, and equity-issuance language” amid estimated cash burn of about $60M per quarter.

surprises.description: EVgo gave a specific 2027 stall-growth outlook: additions are expected to be 2.5–3 times the number of owned-and-operated stalls added in 2025. The preview discussed 2026 build timing but did not set an expectation for 2027 additions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2027 additions are expected at 2.5x to 3x the number of owned-and-operated stalls added in 2025.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $83 million was slightly above the preview’s consensus range of about $79.8–81.5 million, although it remained within the company’s $75–85 million guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue fell 16% year-over-year to $83 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave consensus revenue of “~$79.8M – $81.5M” and company guidance of “$75M – $85M.”

in_line: Charging network revenue was $61 million, at the top of the preview’s expected $59–61 million range; its 19% growth and 18th consecutive double-digit-growth quarter were consistent with the preview’s expectation that the streak would continue.
The preview expected 2026 builds to be weighted to the second half, especially Q4; EVgo said roughly 60% of full-year stall builds are weighted to Q4.

surprises.description: TrueBlue reported Q2 revenue of $443 million, above both the $417.8 million consensus and the top of its $405–430 million outlook range. The 12% year-over-year increase was substantially stronger than the preview’s implied 5.5% growth and was driven by outperformance in skilled businesses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue rose 12% year-over-year to $443 million, exceeding the company's outlook range driven by outperformance in skilled businesses.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $11 million, far above the preview’s implied $1–3 million range. That is a much larger gap than the preview’s expectation of roughly flat EBITDA year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA more than tripled to $11 million from $3 million in the prior-year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$1–3M (implied)”; the preview also described it as “about flat.”

surprises.description: Gross margin came in at 20.7%, below the preview’s 21.1%–21.5% outlook range despite the revenue beat. The call attributed the decline primarily to prior-year workers’ compensation favorability, lower-margin energy mix, and a $3 million government subsidy benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin fell to 20.7% from 23.6% a year earlier, primarily due to non-recurring prior-year workers' compensation favorability, a $3 million government subsidy benefit, and lower-margin energy revenue mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~21.3% (implied) | 21.1%–21.5%.”

surprises.description: The reported result was a $3 million net loss, including a $3 million non-cash write-down of the Tacoma headquarters, even as adjusted net income turned positive at $2 million. The preview flagged impairment risk, but did not anticipate this specific write-down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported a net loss of $3 million that included a $3 million non-cash write-down of its Tacoma headquarters, while adjusted net income turned positive at $2 million versus a $2 million loss a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Workers' comp reserve language and impairment risk. Any new adverse development, or a third straight quarter of ‘differential’ explanations, would hurt the credibility of management's Q1 explanation.”

surprises.description: SG&A fell 7% while revenue grew 12%, a stronger reduction than the preview’s estimate of roughly a 3% year-over-year decline. The call also said all three segments expanded profit margins, showing better operating leverage than the preview’s SG&A estimate implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A was reduced by 7% while revenue grew 12%, demonstrating improved operating leverage, and all three segments expanded profit margins.”

surprises.description: PeopleReady’s on-demand business returned to growth, with all four regions growing at quarter-end and a majority of territories in growth for the year. The preview identified an on-demand inflection as part of its bull case, rather than its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The on-demand business returned to growth in the quarter, exiting with all four regions growing and a majority of territories now in growth for the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull scenario cited “on-demand inflection”; its base scenario instead described an “in-line quarter” with “PeopleManagement still soft.”

surprises.description: PeopleManagement improved from contraction to growth: its revenue trend moved from -7% exiting Q1 to +4% exiting Q2, with July similar to the quarter-end rate. That was better than the preview’s base-case expectation that the business would remain soft.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PeopleManagement improved from -7% to +4%, with July trends similar to the quarter's exit rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “PeopleManagement still soft”; it also noted Q1 PeopleManagement revenue was “down 6% Y/Y on retail volume declines.”

surprises.description: PeopleReady revenue grew 23%, its segment margin improved 260 basis points, and its revenue growth accelerated from +16% exiting Q1 to +30% exiting Q2. The preview highlighted energy strength but also warned that energy work was margin-dilutive, so the segment’s margin improvement was better than that mix concern suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PeopleReady revenue grew 23% with energy sector revenue nearly doubling for a fifth consecutive quarter of growth, and segment profit margin improved 260 basis points.” The call also said PeopleReady growth accelerated “from +16% exiting Q1 to +30% exiting Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said energy was “margin-dilutive” and identified “Revenue mix: energy/skilled vs. PeopleReady on-demand” as a key metric to watch.

in_line: PeopleSolutions’ segment profit margin returned to double digits, meeting the preview’s flagged expectation that management had explicitly committed to a double-digit Q2 margin.

surprises.description: The preview’s bull case said retail margins would “hold,” but Q2 retail adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 880 bps to 26.6% (350 bps excluding the hardware impact), with adjusted EBITDA up 20%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retail revenue grew 4% excluding the hardware impact and retail adjusted EBITDA rose 20% to $97 million, with margin up 880 bps to 26.6% (350 bps excluding hardware).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Retail margins hold” (bull scenario).

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS came in at $0.17, above the preview’s $0.15 consensus estimate, although it was flat because of a higher tax rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS was flat at $0.17 due to a higher tax rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS: $0.15.”

surprises.description: Revenue excluding the hardware-transition impact grew 1%, and recurring revenue grew 3%, including 6% software growth. The preview focused on the ODM reset and total-revenue consensus, but did not set an expectation for this underlying growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue fell 21% to $523 million due to the hardware business transition, but rose 1% excluding that impact, with recurring revenue up 3% (software +6%, services +1%).”

surprises.description: VCP progress fell short of the preview’s stated bar: there were 25 signed contracts and $286 million of remaining contract value, versus expectations to watch for 28–32 contracts and more than $350 million of RCV.
surprises.fact_evidence: “VCP contracts reached 25 signed customers representing $286 million of remaining contract value.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for RCV above $350M and cumulative contracts near 28–32.”

surprises.description: Restaurant weakness did not visibly moderate: revenue was down 6% excluding hardware, matching the prior-quarter decline, while adjusted EBITDA fell 15% versus an 8% decline in Q1. The call cited delayed hardware refreshes, SMB weakness, and the Brazil divestiture.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restaurant revenue declined 6% excluding hardware (a $10 million drop) driven by delayed hardware refreshes, SMB weakness, and the Brazil divestiture, with adjusted EBITDA down 15% to $58 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Restaurants trajectory. Whether the SMB weakness moderates”; Q1 restaurants revenue was “−6%, EBITDA −8%.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a new $20–$30 million memory-chip cost headwind. It is being passed through via pricing, but is contributing to customer caution and delayed hardware and project purchases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Memory chip cost inflation represents a $20-$30 million headwind being passed through via price, contributing to customer caution and delayed hardware and project purchases.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $523 million was close to the $516.9 million consensus estimate and within the preview’s $505–$525 million base-case range.
Adjusted EBITDA of $98 million was within the preview’s estimated $95–$100 million range and the $95–$102 million base-case range.
Full-year 2026 revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EPS guidance was maintained at the ranges already stated in the preview.

surprises.description: Toast added 9,500 net locations, well above the preview’s roughly 8,400 implied adds and above its bull-case threshold of 9,000. It was also a new quarterly record, about 1,000 above the prior high.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company added a record 9,500 net new locations in Q2, roughly 1,000 above its prior high.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied net location adds: about 8,400”; the bull scenario listed “9,000+.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $221 million, above the preview’s guided range of $185–195 million. The beat included an approximately $10 million tariff refund that had not been contemplated in guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 38% to $221 million with margins expanding 240 basis points to 37%, though this included an approximately $10 million tariff refund not contemplated in Q2 guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA $185–195M (guide).”

surprises.description: Recurring gross profit growth came in above the preview’s expected 24–26% range: Toast reported recurring gross profit streams growing over 28%, with subscription gross profit up 32%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Toast grew recurring gross profit streams over 28% year-over-year in Q2”; “subscription gross profit up 32%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP recurring GP: $565–575M (guide)”; the preview described this as “+24–26%.”

surprises.description: The full-year recurring gross profit outlook rose to 23–25% growth from the prior 21–23% outlook, reaching the preview’s bull-case threshold of growth above 23%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Toast raised its full-year 2026 outlook to recurring gross profit growth of 23%-25%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 company guidance: recurring gross profit of $2.29–2.32B (+21–23%)”; the bull scenario expected “Recurring GP raised above +23% growth.”

surprises.description: The full-year EBITDA increase was more limited than the Q2 beat: Toast raised the range to $805–825 million, but said it reinvested the tariff refund into growth initiatives rather than carrying the full Q2 upside into guidance. This is a more restrained flow-through than the preview’s bull case of guidance above $820 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Toast raised its full-year 2026 outlook to … adjusted EBITDA of $805 million-$825 million, but increased EBITDA guidance by less than the Q2 beat because it reinvested the tariff refund into growth initiatives.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior guidance was “adj. EBITDA of $790–810M”; the bull scenario expected “EBITDA above $820M.” The preview also asked whether the increase would “flow through only the Q2 beat.”

surprises.description: Take rate was 98 basis points, below the preview’s stated watch level of more than 103 basis points. Its 5-basis-point year-over-year increase did not meet that higher benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total take rate reached 98 basis points of GPV (up 5 bps year-over-year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The catalyst checklist called for “Take rate above 103 bps.”

surprises.description: Toast had repurchased over 19 million shares for $486 million year-to-date, more than the preview’s Q1 figure of 14 million shares for $378 million. The preview had flagged capital return as something to watch, but did not anticipate this higher reported year-to-date total.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased over 19 million shares for $486 million year-to-date with about $100 million remaining on authorization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Toast repurchased 14M shares for $378M year-to-date as of Q1.”

surprises.description: Toast introduced a notably fast-growing AI product: Toast IQ Grow was on track to be its fastest product to reach $10 million in ARR and was already running at positive, improving gross margins. The preview did not flag this product or its early economics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Toast IQ Grow, the company's new AI marketing agent, is on track to become its fastest product ever to reach $10 million in ARR and is already running at positive and improving gross margins.”

surprises.description: Toast said international, enterprise, and retail businesses were on a path to nearly double ARR to $200 million this year, while also choosing to invest more aggressively to accelerate them. These growth targets and the greater investment emphasis were not covered in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New TAMs (international, enterprise, retail) are on a path to nearly double ARR to $200 million this year, with the company choosing to invest more aggressively to accelerate growth in these segments.”

surprises.description: Q3 subscription and fintech gross profit growth guidance of 22–24% was stronger than the preview’s calculation that the existing full-year outlook implied only about 16–19% growth for H2, easing the concern that growth would slow that far.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for subscription and fintech gross profit growth of 22%-24%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview calculated that the FY guide “implies H2 growth of roughly +16–19% Y/Y.”

in_line: GPV per location was flat year-over-year, within the preview’s expected range of -1% to flat.

surprises.description: Q2 net sales were $305.6 million, about 4.4% above the $292.7 million consensus, with growth of 15.5% versus the preview’s expected 10.6%. The beat was driven by volume growth rather than pricing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose 15.5% year-over-year to $305.6 million,” driven “almost entirely by 15.7% volume growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $292.7M” and “+10.6%” YoY.

surprises.description: Management raised both ends of its FY26 net-sales-growth and adjusted-EBITDA ranges, rather than merely reaffirming the existing outlook. The preview identified a guidance raise as upside but expected a reaffirmation in its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: FY26 net sales growth guidance is now “10%-12% (up from 8%-11%)” and adjusted EBITDA guidance is “$210M-$220M (up from $205M-$215M).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Guidance in force was “FY26 net sales growth 8–11%; adj. EBITDA $205–215M”; the base scenario assumed “FY guide reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin expanded 170 basis points to 48.6%, its highest level since Q1 2020, despite disposal-related quality costs from commissioning new technology. The preview provided no Q2 gross-margin expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 170 basis points to 48.6%, the highest level since Q1 2020,” driven by sales leverage and lower input costs “despite disposal-related quality costs from new technology commissioning.”

surprises.description: Management lifted its 2027 adjusted-gross-margin floor to at least 49%, above the prior 48% floor discussed in the preview. It also described a substantial longer-term benefit from the new bag technology, though only about 25 basis points are expected in 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “raised its 2027 adjusted gross margin floor from at least 48% to at least 49%.” New bag technology is expected to deliver “over 100 basis points” of gross-margin improvement when fully optimized, with “~25 bps” expected in 2026 and full-rate contribution during 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said 2027 targets were “adj. gross margin above 48% and adj. EBITDA margin of 20–22%.”

surprises.description: Price/mix was only slightly negative at 0.2%, much better than the preview’s flagged risk of a decline of 3% or worse. This reduces the evidence, in this quarter, of substantial promotional pressure on sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: Sales growth came with “a slight 0.2% unfavorable price/mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a price/mix decline of -3% or worse would suggest promotional spending against new entrants.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed elevated logistics costs: logistics reached 6.9% of sales, and FY26 guidance now assumes an additional $8 million of elevated costs. The preview did not flag this specific cost pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Logistics costs rose to 6.9% of net sales (from 5.7% a year ago) due to higher fuel and trucking capacity pressures,” with guidance assuming “an additional $8 million in elevated logistics costs for 2026.”

surprises.description: The call reported rapid digital-order growth and a rising share of sales through digital channels, which the preview did not identify as a specific expected Q2 result. Most e-commerce sales were still fulfilled through the fridge network.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Digital orders grew 41% and accounted for 16.7% of total business (up from 16.1% in Q1),” with “approximately 78% of e-commerce sales fulfilled through Freshpet’s fridge network.”

surprises.description: The company had already executed $86.5 million of its $150 million buyback authorization, alongside positive quarterly free cash flow and a sizable cash balance. The preview highlighted a mid-year capacity decision and suggested accelerated installs could delay buybacks, but the call facts do not specify whether installs were accelerated.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “executed $86.5 million of its $150 million buyback authorization, repurchasing 1.6 million shares,” and ended the quarter with “$350.8 million in cash” and “free cash flow of $14.7 million versus $0.5 million a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management’s “decision mid-year whether to accelerate line installs” should come on the call and noted that acceleration “delays buybacks.”

in_line: The 2027 adjusted EBITDA margin target remained 20%-22%, consistent with the preview’s stated target and base-case expectation of no change.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $339 million, about $6.5 million above the $332.5 million consensus and above the $335 million high end of guidance. That was a modest beat, rather than the preview’s base-case range of $335–338 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 FY26 revenue reached $339 million,” exceeding consensus and “the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus” revenue was “$332.5M”; Q4 guidance was “$330.0–335.0M.” The base scenario projected “$335–338M.”

surprises.description: Q4 gross margin reached 62.7%, 70 basis points above the preview’s approximately 62.0% expectation and above the 62.2% high end of guidance. The preview had highlighted margin pressure as a key risk, but the reported quarter exceeded that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 gross margin rose to 62.7%, above guidance,” helped by pricing actions and supply-chain cost management.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q4 gross margin guidance was “61.8–62.2%” and consensus was “~62.0%.”

surprises.description: FY26 non-GAAP EPS was $1.06, above the company’s $1.02–$1.04 full-year guidance. The preview did not provide a separate full-year EPS consensus, so the comparison is to guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY26 revenue grew 13% to $1.28 billion with non-GAAP EPS of $1.06.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY26 non-GAAP EPS guidance was “$1.02–1.04.”

surprises.description: FY27 revenue guidance of $1.38–$1.40 billion is above the preview’s roughly $1.36 billion Street estimate at the midpoint, though the midpoint is just below the preview’s $1.40 billion bull threshold. The outlook implies faster growth than the preview’s 6.5% Street estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 guidance of $1.38-$1.4 billion in revenue (roughly 8-9% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY27 Street revenue was “~$1.36B (~+6.5%).” The preview’s bull threshold was “≥$1.40B revenue.”

surprises.description: FY27 EPS guidance of $1.28–$1.33 is above the preview’s implied estimate of about $1.21, with even the low end representing a meaningful increase over that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 guidance” includes “EPS of $1.28-$1.33, representing more than 20% EPS growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY27 EPS was “~$1.21 implied by 26.7x forward P/E.”

surprises.description: SaaS ARR was $244 million, below the preview’s expected $246–$248 million, and growth of 18% was well below the 25%+ pace the preview flagged. Management did point to a recovery toward mid-20% growth by the end of FY27, but that is later than the near-term growth level the preview was watching for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SaaS ARR grew 18% year-over-year to $244 million,” and management guided “a reacceleration toward mid-20% by end of FY27.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q4 SaaS ARR was expected “around $246–248M,” with the catalyst checklist looking for “growth of 25% or more.”

surprises.description: Platform ONE bookings exceeded the company’s roughly $40 million target, reaching over $50 million, while nearly half of Q4 subscription bookings came from the platform. The preview said bookings were tracking to double but did not specify this target or the reported level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Extreme Platform ONE reached nearly 50% of Q4 subscription bookings” and “exceeded its ~$40 million bookings target with over $50 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Bookings were reportedly tracking to double again in Q4.”

surprises.description: Q4 cash generation was substantially above the preview’s expectation that it would be well above Q3’s $7.8 million, and ending net cash was $47 million versus the preview’s $11.3 million estimate. The reported liquidity position was therefore stronger than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company generated $65 million of cash flow” in Q4 and “ended with $47 million net cash.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 should be well above Q3's $7.8M”; the preview also said net cash was “$11.3M.”

surprises.description: The company reported 187 FY26 customers booking over $1 million, up from 168 in FY25, and average deal size grew by one-third. The preview mentioned Q3’s 44 customers spending over $1 million but did not quantify an FY26 customer-count or deal-size expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “187 customers booked over $1 million in FY26 (up from 168 in FY25), average deal size grew by one-third.”

in_line: FY26 revenue of $1.28 billion was within the preview’s $1.275–$1.280 billion guidance range.
The company’s supply chain was secured into FY28 and beyond, broadly consistent with the preview’s statement that supply was locked through FY27–28.

surprises.description: Equitable reported operating EPS of $1.70, modestly above the $1.66 consensus, and $1.75 excluding notable items. The ex-notables increase of 24% also exceeded the preview's roughly 18% comparison on the prior-year ex-notables basis, though the alternate $1.73 estimate was higher than reported EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 non-GAAP operating EPS was $1.70 ($1.75 excluding notable items), representing a 24% year-over-year increase.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 operating EPS | $1.66 (+50.9% YoY)” and “Q2 operating EPS (alternate) | $1.73”; the preview says consensus implies “about +18% against ex-notables.”

surprises.description: The alternatives portfolio returned only slightly over 1% annualized, below the preview's expected 2–3% return. It created a $49 million below-plan drag, partly offset by a $35 million tax benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The alternative investments portfolio (about 2% of the general account) returned only slightly over 1% annualized due to lagged Q1 private equity impacts, resulting in a $49 million below-plan drag partly offset by a $35 million tax benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Alternatives returns, Q2 | 2–3% (management guidance)” and “Alternatives returns versus the 2–3% Q2 guide.”

surprises.description: Instead of continued AB outflows, AllianceBernstein returned to positive net flows of $0.8 billion. The preview had identified its prior-quarter $7.1 billion outflow as the clearest weak spot; the call also reported positive net flows across all segments and record AUM.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AllianceBernstein returned to positive net inflows of $0.8 billion, boosted by a $9 billion sub-advisory mandate from Equitable”; “Assets under management and administration reached a record $1.2 trillion, up 10% year-over-year, with all segments posting positive net flows.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AB's −$7.1B in Q1 was the clearest weak spot” and the preview flagged “AB outflows and Retirement flows” as an issue to watch.

surprises.description: Equitable returned $449 million in the quarter, including $366 million of buybacks, and reported a 92% payout ratio. That was a notably high quarterly return pace against the preview's question about whether buybacks would hold through the proxy blackout, although management still expects the full-year payout ratio to be 60–70%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Equitable returned $449 million to shareholders including $366 million of buybacks, a 92% payout ratio for the quarter, though management still expects a full-year payout ratio of 60% to 70%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether the Q2 buyback pace held through the proxy blackout, and whether management reaffirms the 2026 targets”; the preview also cites the “60–70% payout target.”

surprises.description: AB raised its full-year 2026 performance-fee guidance to $115–$135 million from $95–$115 million. The preview did not flag an increase to this guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 performance fee guidance to $115-$135 million from $95-$115 million.”

surprises.description: Equitable agreed to sell its unprofitable Employee Benefits business, a transaction not anticipated in the preview. Management expects the near-term earnings impact to be neutral to slightly positive and plans to redeploy proceeds into businesses where it has scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company agreed to sell its unprofitable Employee Benefits business (800,000 customers, ~$500 million premiums) to The Hartford at a neutral-to-slightly-positive near-term earnings impact, redeploying proceeds into at-scale businesses.”

surprises.description: Despite the strong equity markets, Equitable reported a $453 million GAAP net loss because of noneconomic hedge-portfolio impacts. The preview focused on operating EPS and did not flag this GAAP loss; its noneconomic cause makes the result less indicative of underlying operating performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported a GAAP net loss of $453 million, driven by noneconomic hedge portfolio impacts from strong equity markets.”

in_line: Management said the company remained on track for full-year EPS growth above 15%, consistent with the preview's expectation that 2026 growth would be above the 12–15% target range.
The merger had shareholder approval and remained expected to close by year-end 2026, as the preview anticipated; the call reported approval with over 97% support.

Retirement produced $1.7 billion of net inflows, while core spreads increased 1 basis point sequentially to 174 basis points and management expects them to remain near current levels, consistent with the preview's focus on Retirement flows and spread strength.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $76 million, just above the preview’s $65–75 million guidance-implied band and above its roughly $69 million base case. That is a small upside surprise, though it did not reach the preview’s stated level for a clear beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell 12% to $76 million” in Q2.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA vs. the ~$65–75M guidance-implied band”; the preview also says “Above $78M would be a real beat.”

surprises.description: Experiential Services’ revenue growth eased from Q1’s 22.8% to 19%, but EBITDA grew 32%, outpacing revenue growth despite the preview’s concern about whether EBITDA growth would keep pace. Strong event volumes and execution also supported the segment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenues up 19% to $296 million and adjusted EBITDA up 32% to $34 million,” driven by “an 18% increase in event volumes and approximately 95% execution rates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether EBITDA growth keeps pace with revenue.”

surprises.description: Branded Services weakened to a 13% revenue decline, versus the preview’s description of declines around 10–11%, and EBITDA fell much faster at 36%. The revenue decline reached the preview’s bear-case threshold, though it did not exceed the stated “past −13%” trigger.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Branded Services revenue declined 13% to $224 million and adjusted EBITDA dropped 36% to $22 million,” pressured by “client insourcing, softer CPG spending and client losses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “It has declined about 10–11% for three-plus quarters”; “acceleration past −13% breaks it.”

surprises.description: Retailer Services grew revenue 3%, close to its recent growth pace, but EBITDA fell about 25% because of project timing and higher costs on a new project. The preview did not flag a comparable profitability decline for this segment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retailer Services revenue grew 3% to $237 million but adjusted EBITDA fell approximately 25% to $20 million” due to “project timing,” a tough comparison, and higher execution costs on a new project.

surprises.description: Net leverage rose to approximately 4.5x from 4.2x in Q1, rather than moving toward the preview’s deleveraging focus. Management said future free cash flow would go primarily toward debt reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $102 million in cash and net debt of approximately 4.5x trailing EBITDA,” with free cash flow “directed primarily toward debt reduction.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Deleveraging toward 3.5x” and said “Another quarter of paydown would help the equity case.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed divestiture headwinds of about $5 million to Q2 revenue and $3 million to EBITDA, with larger full-year impacts. The preview did not identify these headwinds, which qualify the reported growth and guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Divestitures created a Q2 headwind of roughly $5 million to revenues and $3 million to adjusted EBITDA,” with full-year headwinds of “approximately $20 million to revenues and over $10 million to adjusted EBITDA.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance and the $250–275 million adjusted unlevered free cash flow range, as the preview expected.

Q2 adjusted unlevered free cash flow was weak at $19 million, but the preview explicitly expected a weak quarter because DSO would remain elevated through midyear; the call attributed the pressure to the final SAP implementation phase.
Management’s second-half-weighted EBITDA cadence was broadly consistent with the preview’s base case, which anticipated a reaffirmed full-year outlook and a second-half-weighted year.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $277.8M, well above the preview’s roughly $269.7M consensus and the company’s $268–271M guide. That is a clear upside beat, not merely a result at the guide midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue grew 26.6% to $277.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus revenue sits at the guide midpoint” of “~$269.7M”; company guide was “$268–271M.”

surprises.description: Bookings reached $295.9M, topping the preview’s $282.5M midpoint and the $285M guide high end. Growth of 33% also exceeded the preview’s implied 26.7% growth rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 bookings grew 33% year-over-year to $295.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total Bookings vs. $282.5M midpoint”; catalyst checklist: “Bookings at or above $285M (guide high end).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 36.4%, far above the preview’s roughly 32% estimate. The reported roughly 900 basis points of year-over-year expansion and ~70% flow-through further underscored the margin strength.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin hit 36.4%,” with “roughly 900 basis points of margin expansion year-over-year and ~70% adjusted EBITDA flow-through.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin” consensus estimate “~32%”; catalyst checklist: “at or above 32%.”

surprises.description: Active CLEAR+ reached 8.3M, below the preview’s 8.4M catalyst level; from the prior quarter’s 8.2M, that is about 100,000 net additions, short of the preview’s 150,000 threshold. This fell short of the level the preview said would help show Q1’s growth was not a pull-forward.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Active CLEAR+ members grew 15.2% to 8.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Active CLEAR+ at or above 8.4M with net adds of at least 150k”; “Net adds below ~150k would suggest the Q1 surge was a pull-forward.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $284M–$287M is modestly above the preview’s $283M-or-higher threshold and its stated need for a $280M+ handle to support 20%+ growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for revenue of $284M-$287M.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 revenue guide at or above $283M”; “Q3 revenue needs roughly a $280M+ handle to support 20%+ growth.”

surprises.description: Although the preview did not give a Q3 bookings forecast, the outlook implies bookings growth slowing to 20.5% at the midpoint from Q2’s 33% growth. That is a deceleration from the momentum reported in the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for…bookings of $311M-$316M (20.5% growth at midpoint), signaling a deceleration from Q2's 33% bookings growth.”

surprises.description: The preview identified CLEAR1 as a key debate and said hard figures or named multiyear contracts would be a bull catalyst. Instead, the call reported a sharp sequential acceleration in both net new signings and pipeline, though it did not provide dollar figures or named contracts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CLEAR1 net new customer signings increased over 50% sequentially from Q1 to Q2, and the pipeline also grew over 50% quarter-over-quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Hard dollar figures or named multiyear contracts would be a bull catalyst; vague ‘record quarter’ language would not.”

surprises.description: The company raised standard membership pricing by $10 and said early retention remained healthy with no observed impact. The preview did not flag the price increase or give a retention expectation, so this is a favorable new pricing update rather than a result against a stated bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised standard membership pricing by $10 (from $209 to $219) effective July 1st, with early retention rates remaining healthy and no observed impact on retention.”

surprises.description: eGates covered over 70% of the network, short of the preview’s stated >80% target. At the same time, direct salaries and benefits fell to 17.3% of revenue, a substantial cost improvement that partially offsets the coverage shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “eGates now cover over 70% of the network and drove direct salaries and benefits down to 17.3% of revenue, an improvement of ~450 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview’s next steps called for checking “eGate coverage (target >80%).”

surprises.description: A $315M accrued liability to the Amex credit card partner will be paid in Q3 and will make Q3 free cash flow negative. The preview did not flag this cash outflow, although the company says it is already included in guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $315 million accrued partnership liability with the Amex credit card partner will be paid out in Q3, resulting in negative Q3 free cash flow (already reflected in guidance).”

surprises.description: The company repurchased about $22M of shares in Q3 to date, a new capital-allocation detail not anticipated in the preview, which instead noted ongoing insider sales as a potential supply overhang.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $959 million (over $7 per share) in cash and marketable securities and repurchased ~$22 million of shares in Q3 to date at an average price of $52.73.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview noted that the CEO and Alclear Investments “have been selling under 10b5-1 plans (about $20M+ over six months).”

in_line: FY2026 free cash flow guidance was raised from at least $465M to at least $480M, meeting the preview’s highlighted expectation that guidance be raised above $465M.

surprises.description: Orthofix raised FY26 revenue guidance to $845–855 million, up about $7 million from the May outlook and above the preview’s $843.3 million consensus. However, it stopped short of restoring the pre-cut $850–860 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Full year 2026 net sales guidance was raised to $845–855 million, up approximately $7 million from the May outlook.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Whether the $850–860M revenue and $95–98M EBITDA ranges are restored, or only partly.” The preview also gave FY26 revenue consensus of $843.3M.

surprises.description: The raised full-year outlook came with a softer underlying revenue trajectory: excluding the European distributor benefit, core organic growth is expected to slow to roughly 2–3% in the second half, with Q3 sales roughly level with Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding the ~$15 million EU MDR benefit, core organic revenue growth in the second half is expected to slow to roughly 2-3%,” and “Q3 net sales are expected to be roughly consistent with Q2.”

surprises.description: A European distributor arrangement is expected to add about $15 million of sales in 2026, mostly in Q4, but then create an approximately $22 million sales headwind in 2027—an unusual near-term boost followed by a larger reversal that the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: The arrangement is expected to contribute “~$15 million of incremental net sales in 2026 (mostly in Q4),” but create “an approximately $22 million net sales headwind in 2027.”

surprises.description: Global Spine Fixation grew 10% in constant currency, above the roughly 6% Q2 growth the preview said was needed to meet the H1 target. That headline strength contrasted with only 3% U.S. growth, as smaller distributors declined steeply while the largest distributors continued to perform well.
surprises.fact_evidence: Global Spine Fixation grew 10% constant currency; U.S. Spine Fixation grew 3% “due to steep declines among smaller distributors,” while the top 30 distributors, representing about 80% of sales, continued performing well.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said Q2 needed about 6% constant-currency growth to hit the ~5% H1 target. Tier-2 distributor transition is a risk.”

surprises.description: U.S. Limb Reconstruction growth fell short of expectations despite strong international demand, leaving the 11% global constant-currency growth rate uneven by geography.
surprises.fact_evidence: Global Limb Reconstruction grew 11% constant currency to $37.7 million, led by international demand, “while U.S. growth came in below expectations.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was close to the preview’s roughly flat benchmark: $20.1 million versus the $20.6 million prior-year figure cited in the preview.

CMS’s retroactive restoration of the prior Medicare reimbursement level was consistent with the preview, which said CMS had directed payment at pre-reclassification rates for devices furnished on or after May 18.
FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $95–98 million matched the pre-cut range the preview highlighted as a possible restoration.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $75 million, above the $71–73 million company range and roughly $72 million consensus; it also cleared the preview’s $74 million catalyst and reached its $75 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue grew 15% year-over-year to $75 million, exceeding the guided range of $71 million to $73 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 consensus at “~$72M” and flagged “Revenue at or above $74M” as a catalyst; its bull scenario was “$75M+.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $10 million, roughly twice the $5 million consensus midpoint and well above the $4–6 million guide. It also exceeded the preview’s $8 million catalyst and $9 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA reached a record $10 million (13% margin), roughly doubling the guided $4 million to $6 million range.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed adjusted EBITDA consensus at “~$5M,” a company guide of “$4–6M,” and a catalyst of “Adj. EBITDA at or above $8M.”

surprises.description: Nextdoor raised its full-year outlook more than the preview’s expected roughly 10% revenue growth and high-single-digit adjusted EBITDA margin: revenue growth is now guided to the low teens and adjusted EBITDA margin to approximately 10%.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to low-teens revenue growth and an adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 10%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 revenue guidance of “~+10%” and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of “High single digit,” and said a raise would be a meaningful signal.

surprises.description: WAU reached 22.9 million, above the preview’s 22.3 million reference point and its 22.3–22.6 million base-case range, and even above the 22.8 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: Platform WAU hit an all-time high of 22.9 million, up 5% year-over-year and rising sequentially for the second consecutive quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted WAU versus “22.3M,” gave a base scenario of “22.3–22.6M,” and a bull scenario of “Above 22.8M.”

surprises.description: Self-serve growth accelerated beyond the preview’s 28% expectation, reaching 32%, but its roughly 67% revenue share was below the preview’s expectation of about 70% or more.
surprises.fact_evidence: The self-serve channel grew 32% year-over-year (accelerating from 28% last quarter) and now represents roughly 67% of total revenue.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch whether self-serve metrics held at “about 70% and 28%” and listed “28% or more at 70% or more of mix” as a catalyst.

in_line: WAU rose sequentially for a second consecutive quarter, as the preview expected a second straight sequential gain; the higher-than-expected ending level is listed separately above.

surprises.description: The preview identified CB-3 rent commencement as the main swing factor and said a bull case would show more than 60 MW energized and rent-commencing. TeraWulf entered Q3 with 102 critical MW operating at Lake Mariner, with CB-3 fully online; its completion also activated $600 million of Google credit support for FluidStack’s lease obligations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Entered Q3 with 102 critical megawatts operating at Lake Mariner, with CB-3 fully online” and CB-3 completion “triggering effectiveness of $600 million of Google credit support.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “This is the biggest swing factor” for revenue; a bull case would show “a specific energized-and-rent-commencing MW figure above 60 MW.”

surprises.description: The preview described the Abernathy sale as a planned monetization, with the JV targeted for Q4 2026. TeraWulf had already received $250 million in July from a roughly $530 million sale, with the remaining proceeds scheduled in installments through April 2027; the deal represents a 20% IRR.
surprises.fact_evidence: TeraWulf agreed to sell its 50.1% interest for “approximately $530 million, representing a 20% IRR,” with “$250 million received in July,” another $150 million expected by December 31, 2026, and about $130 million by April 30, 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The Abernathy JV was “targeted for 4Q26”; the preview said to watch “closing timing, proceeds, any gain, and deconsolidation effects.”

surprises.description: The preview identified equity dilution as a central funding concern for the buildout. Instead, TeraWulf reported about $1.45 billion of parent unrestricted liquidity, including the Abernathy payment, and said it could fund near-term commitments without accessing equity markets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Parent unrestricted liquidity of ~$1.45 billion including the Abernathy payment, sufficient to fund near-term commitments without accessing equity markets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Equity dilution is the central bear input” and the preview said to check for “any concurrent ATM or offering.”

surprises.description: The preview cited $8.6 million per critical MW as the amount financed in October 2025. The updated project-cost estimate is about $9.1 million per critical MW—higher than that benchmark, although still within the stated $8–10 million guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Wulf Compute project costs are now estimated at approximately $9.1 million per critical megawatt” and are “above the $8.6 million financed in October 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “~$2.2B of WULF Compute capex remaining” against $1.5B spent; it did not state a revised per-MW cost range.

surprises.description: The preview did not flag a new FluidStack fit-out contribution. The amendments require about $150 million from TeraWulf, but are expected to bring more than $500 million of incremental lease revenue over the initial terms, including higher capacity at CB-4 and CB-5.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FluidStack lease amendments require TeraWulf to contribute ~$150 million for tenant fit-out costs but are expected to generate over $500 million of incremental lease revenue,” including capacity increases “from 162 to 168 megawatts at CB-4 and CB-5.”

surprises.description: The preview did not mention the Muskie site or a further Kentucky expansion. TeraWulf described a gigawatt-scale site with potential capacity of up to 2 GW, though initial electric service is not expected until Q4 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: TeraWulf “expanded the Kentucky platform via the gigawatt-scale Muskie site (potentially up to 2 gigawatts) with initial electric service expected in Q4 2028.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $44.8 million was broadly in line with the preview’s consensus range of $44.71 million to $46.02 million.
HPC lease revenue of $31.9 million was within the preview’s estimated $30–33 million implied by consensus.
The preview anticipated another large noncash GAAP loss related to the Google warrant valuation; the reported loss was primarily driven by a $755.7 million noncash warrant fair-value loss.

surprises.description: Revenue was about 4% above the preview’s roughly $362 million consensus, reaching $376 million. That was a modest upside to the headline estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales reached $376 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$362M (MarketBeat, Jul 28, 2026)”

surprises.description: Cellulose Specialties pricing did more than hold its prior gain: it rose 8% sequentially and 21% year over year, alongside a 19% sequential volume increase. The preview had flagged whether the price gain would hold as customers normalized inventories, so the continued price increases and stronger volumes were better than that concern implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cellulose Specialties pricing increased 8% sequentially and 21% year-over-year, with volumes up 19% from Q1”; management expects pricing “to remain significantly above prior-year levels through the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether the 17% price gain holds as customers normalize inventories.”

surprises.description: Paperboard and high-yield pulp losses worsened to $10 million from $5 million in Q1, despite higher volumes. The preview expected ongoing losses and flagged the segment’s headwinds, but the further deterioration was unfavorable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Paperboard and high-yield pulp segment posted negative $10 million adjusted EBITDA, worsening from negative $5 million in Q1 and negative $2 million a year ago, despite higher volumes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Paperboard & High-Yield Pulp: $5M loss on oversupply”; the preview also flagged “Paperboard & High-Yield Pulp losses and tariff/FX headwinds.”

surprises.description: The call set a target to conclude the strategic review and communicate a clear path forward in Q4 2026. The preview expected an update and said the review would remain ongoing in its base case, but did not anticipate this specific conclusion timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects to conclude its comprehensive strategic review and communicate a clear path forward during the fourth quarter of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any update on the four pathways is likely to dominate the stock reaction”; the base scenario said “Guidance held; review ongoing.”

surprises.description: The company recorded a $13 million noncash impairment related to high-yield pulp, an expense not mentioned in the preview. It weighed on the reported loss, although the charge was noncash.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Loss from continuing operations narrowed to $33 million from $81 million in Q1, though it included a $13 million noncash asset impairment charge related to high-yield pulp.”

surprises.description: New Canadian-origin product tariffs could materially affect the paperboard segment, which sells about 75% of its volume in the U.S. This was an additional tariff exposure beyond the preview’s discussion of paperboard and high-yield pulp headwinds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly 75% of the company's paperboard volume is sold into the U.S., exposing the segment to potentially material impact from newly announced tariffs on Canadian-origin products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Paperboard & High-Yield Pulp losses and tariff/FX headwinds,” but did not mention newly announced tariffs on Canadian-origin products.

surprises.description: Final U.S. tariffs on Brazilian and Norwegian dissolving wood pulp imports could improve U.S. suppliers’ competitiveness if sustained. The preview did not anticipate this potential benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “USTR announced final Section 301 tariffs of 37.5% on Brazilian and 12.5% on Norwegian dissolving wood pulp imports, which management believes will improve competitiveness for U.S. suppliers if sustained.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA rose to $40 million from $8 million in Q1, consistent with the preview’s focus on a sequential EBITDA ramp; the preview did not provide a specific Q2 EBITDA estimate.
Despite the preview’s concern about thin covenant headroom, net secured leverage was 4.2x versus a 4.75x covenant test, slightly improved from Q1’s 4.3x.
The company remained on track for positive full-year free cash flow, in line with the preview’s expectation of positive full-year free cash flow.

surprises.description: XPEL reported Q2 revenue of $143.1 million, well above the preview’s $135.1–$135.62 million consensus and the $137 million high end of company guidance. About $2 million was pulled forward ahead of Q3 price increases, so some of the beat came at Q3’s expense.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue grew 14.7% to a record $143.1 million, exceeding company expectations, though about $2 million was pull-ahead sales ahead of Q3 price increases.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue: company guidance $135M–$137M; consensus $135.1M or $135.62M. The preview also flagged “Revenue ≥ $137M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 44.1%, above the preview’s 43.0%–43.5% estimate and its key 43.5%+ threshold. Management also expected modest further increases through year-end despite cost pressures.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin improved to 44.1% in Q2 from 43.7% in Q1, with management expecting continued modest increases through the rest of the year despite cost pressures.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross margin at “~43.0% – 43.5%” and called out “Gross margin ≥ 43.5%” as a catalyst, with 44%+ supporting the vertical-integration case.

surprises.description: Q2 EPS was above the preview’s roughly $0.60 number to beat, including the high end of its cited $0.57–$0.63 range. Adjusted EPS was $0.68.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 EPS was $0.65 (adjusted $0.68), with net income to stockholders up 10.7% and adjusted net income up 15.6%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: EPS consensus was “$0.57 … or $0.61”; one sell-side model was $0.63, and the preview said to treat “~$0.60 as the number to beat.”

surprises.description: Cash generation was stronger than the preview’s free-cash-flow concern suggested: operating cash flow set a record. However, Q2 also had $65.1 million of CapEx, including a real estate purchase, and the company used a new term loan to help fund it.
surprises.fact_evidence: Cash flow from operations hit a record $30.8 million, while Q2 CapEx was $65.1 million including the real estate purchase, financed partly with a $44.8 million 10-year term loan.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Free cash flow and DSO” and said two negative-FCF quarters during the $110M program would be a real risk; it noted that the program continued through 2H26.

surprises.description: The U.S. grew at a record level, but the independent channel outperformed dealerships while FTC-related dealership headwinds continued—an operating weakness the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: U.S. revenue grew 11.7% to a record $78.6 million, with the independent channel outperforming the dealership channel amid ongoing FTC-related headwinds at dealerships.

surprises.description: China generated $15.9 million of revenue despite domestic car sales in the region falling roughly 20% year over year, indicating resilience against a weak local auto market not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: China contributed $15.9 million in revenue despite domestic car sales in the region falling roughly 20% year-over-year.

surprises.description: India grew more than 60%, a substantial regional growth result that the preview did not call out or forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: India grew over 60%.

surprises.description: Europe’s revenue declined 2.3%; the preview did not flag a European decline or provide a regional expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Europe declined 2.3%.

in_line: Q3 revenue guidance of $137 million to $139 million was within the preview’s expected range of roughly $137 million to $140 million; the lower bound was not below the preview’s $137 million warning threshold.
The combined India/Middle East region’s 5% decline is consistent with the preview’s warning that Middle East exposure was a downside risk.
The manufacturing program’s expected incremental margin benefits beginning in mid-2027 are consistent with the preview’s stated mid-2027 contribution timeline.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $2.70, above the preview’s $2.63 consensus and roughly $2.42 whisper. The beat was modest versus consensus but also cleared the lower whisper scenario the preview considered likely to be exceeded.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS rose 13% year-over-year to $2.70.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2'26 Consensus” adjusted diluted EPS “$2.63”; “Whisper” “~$2.42.”

surprises.description: Sales of about $1.1 billion came in slightly below the preview’s $1.12–$1.13 billion consensus range, even as adjusted EPS beat consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated adjusted net sales declined 4% to $1.1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales” Q2'26 consensus “$1.12–1.13B.”

surprises.description: The unit forecast was cut to 280,000–300,000, below the preview’s expectation of a cut toward 290,000–300,000. The lower end therefore implies a deeper industry-volume outlook than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cut its full-year RV industry wholesale shipment forecast to 280,000-300,000 units from a prior 315,000-330,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY units cut toward 290–300k”; the preview also said a cut toward “PATK's unit framework” was expected.

surprises.description: LCI’s OEM sales declined 10%, a somewhat steeper drop than the preview’s expected 6%–9% decline. The decline was nevertheless less severe than the preview’s cited industry decline, so the shortfall versus the company-specific expectation was limited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aftermarket sales grew 11% while OEM sales fell 10%”; towable RV wholesale units fell “20%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected RV OEM revenue to decline “–6% to –9%” and cited an expected industry unit decline of “–16%.”

surprises.description: RV content per unit rose 11%, down from the 13% growth cited in the preview, and the call noted an unfavorable shift toward lower-content single-axle trailers. Growth remained strong, but the deceleration was the specific risk the preview said could weaken the offset to falling OEM volume.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RV content per unit rose 11% year-over-year to $5,831 … despite an unfavorable mix shift toward lower-content single-axle trailers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Towable content per unit was $5,826 (+13% YoY). Any deceleration breaks the offset story.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating margin reached 9.3%, about 40 basis points above the 8.9% margin the preview said was needed to support consensus. Adjusted operating profit also grew despite lower sales, and management attributed 160 basis points of year-over-year margin improvement to self-help initiatives.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating profit grew 8% to $99 million with margin expanding 110 basis points to 9.3%”; “Self-help initiatives contributed 160 basis points of year-over-year margin improvement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Consensus of $2.63 requires about 8.9% operating margin.”

surprises.description: The preview anticipated that FY26 guidance would be cut, and LCI did lower revenue and EPS ranges, but the resulting ranges were $3.9–$4.1 billion and $8.25–$8.75, respectively. In contrast, the adjusted operating-margin range stayed at 7.5%–8.0%, with management expressing confidence in maintaining it despite lower revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Now guides adjusted revenue of $3.9-$4.1 billion with adjusted EPS of $8.25-$8.75”; management maintained full-year adjusted operating margin guidance of “7.5%-8% despite lower revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: May guidance was “FY26 revenue $4.2–4.3B; operating margin 7.5–8.0%; adjusted EPS $8.75–9.25”; the preview expected “EPS trimmed or withdrawn” and asked whether guidance would be reaffirmed or cut.

surprises.description: Aftermarket operating margin improved 30 basis points to 14%, and management said it expects further improvement as facility and distribution-center investments taper off. The preview focused on aftermarket growth and the First Brands opportunity, but did not anticipate this margin outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aftermarket adjusted operating margin improved 30 basis points to 14%, with management expecting margins to further improve as distribution center and Ranchan facility investments taper off.”

surprises.description: LCI reported a $270 million annualized revenue run rate from its top five innovations and another $140 million of business awarded for the 2027 model year. The preview did not flag these innovation-driven revenue figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The top 5 innovations are generating an estimated $270 million annualized revenue run rate, with an additional $140 million of new business awarded for the 2027 model year change.”

surprises.description: The company will pass nearly $90 million of IHEPA tariff refunds through to customers, with minimal P&L impact, and said it handled the recovery internally rather than paying third-party contingency fees. The preview did not anticipate this refund or the avoided fees.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company will return nearly $90 million in IHEPA tariff refunds to customers as a pass-through with minimal P&L impact, having handled the recovery internally rather than paying third-party contingency fees.”

surprises.description: Net debt was $636 million and leverage had fallen to 1.5x from 1.8x at the start of the year, alongside $812 million of liquidity and repayment of the 2026 convertible notes. The preview did not identify this balance-sheet improvement as an earnings debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt fell to $636 million with net debt to adjusted EBITDA at 1.5x (down from 1.8x at year start), supported by $812 million total liquidity and the payoff of 2026 convertible notes in May.”

surprises.description: The call cited healthy dealer inventories of 18–20 weeks and an installed base of roughly 1.5 million units entering repair cycles, pointing to a future aftermarket tailwind. The preview raised dealer destocking as a bear risk but did not anticipate these inventory and repair-cycle details.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Dealer inventories sit at a healthy 18-20 weeks, and roughly 1.5 million units backed by $15 billion of installed LCI content are entering repair cycles as a future aftermarket tailwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bear scenario cited “dealer destocking”; the preview also flagged aftermarket growth as a key metric to watch.

in_line: The company reduced FY26 guidance rather than reaffirming the prior revenue and EPS ranges, consistent with the preview’s expectation that guidance would be trimmed or withdrawn; the operating-margin range remained 7.5%–8.0%, matching the prior outlook.

Aftermarket sales grew 11%, consistent with the preview’s expectation for double-digit aftermarket growth; the reported figure is for aftermarket sales broadly, rather than a directly comparable automotive-aftermarket growth rate.

surprises.description: The adjusted Q3 loss was $0.26 per share, slightly worse than the $0.24 loss consensus in the preview. The two-cent miss is small, and the preview noted uncertainty about whether consensus included Tennessee on the same basis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted Q3 FY2026 loss from continuing operations improved to $0.26 per share.”

surprises.description: The divestitures produced a $254.6 million after-tax sale gain in discontinued operations, a large reported earnings item not anticipated by the preview. The sales themselves were expected, but the preview did not flag this accounting gain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Spire recorded $253.8 million in earnings from discontinued operations, including an after-tax gain on sale of $254.6 million from divesting Spire Marketing and Spire Storage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed the Marketing and Storage divestitures and their expected proceeds, but did not mention an accounting gain on sale.

surprises.description: Ahead of the Alabama RSE renewal hearings, intervenors recommended 8%–9% ROEs, below both the current 9.9% allowed ROE and Spire’s requested 10.5% and 10.75% adjusting points. The preview did not flag this Alabama ROE dispute.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Alabama RSE renewal hearings on August 6-7 will decide requested adjusting-point ROEs of 10.5% for Spire Alabama and 10.75% for Spire Gulf, with intervenors recommending 8%-9% versus the current 9.9% allowed.”

surprises.description: Spire Tennessee filed its first annual review seeking a $14 million revenue increase, with new rates expected October 1, 2026. The preview focused on Tennessee’s first full quarter and its costs, but did not anticipate this specific rate filing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Spire Tennessee filed its first annual review mechanism seeking a $14 million revenue increase based on a 9.8% ROE and $1.5 billion rate base, with new rates expected effective October 1, 2026.”

surprises.description: O&M rose about $4 million, primarily because of higher bad debt, an expense pressure the preview did not identify. The preview did note Tennessee’s full financing cost, but did not flag bad debt or this O&M increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “O&M expense rose about $4 million primarily due to higher bad debt.”

in_line: Spire reaffirmed FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $3.90–$4.10 and FY2027 guidance of $5.40–$5.60, as the preview expected.
The company reaffirmed its 5%–7% long-term EPS growth target, consistent with the preview.

surprises.description: The new DISCO platform commercial model reached its December 2026 year-end run-rate target by June, with adoption above expectations on both volume and pricing. The preview did not flag this milestone or suggest the target would be reached six months early.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new DISCO platform commercial model hit its December 2026 year-end run-rate target by June, with adoption exceeding expectations on both volume and pricing.”

surprises.description: Management raised FY2026 revenue and software guidance, whereas the preview framed a raise as the clearest bullish outcome but noted that maintaining guidance was also possible. The increase was modest: total-revenue guidance midpoint rose from $174 million to $175.5 million, and software midpoint from $149.25 million to $150 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2026 total revenue guidance was raised to $172 million-$179 million and software revenue to $147.5 million-$152.5 million, reflecting increased second-half confidence.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management can raise, maintain, or trim. ... A raise, especially on software, would be the cleanest bullish signal.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that revenue attributable to generative and agentic AI more than tripled year over year, and that Auto Review set a revenue record. That is more specific monetization evidence than an adoption anecdote, although the preview had asked for AI-attributable revenue disclosure and did not set a growth threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue attributable to generative AI and agentic AI capabilities more than tripled year-over-year, with Auto Review setting a new revenue record driven by record volume and larger average review size.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The market wants attach rates, pricing, or disclosed AI-attributable revenue, not more adoption anecdotes.”

surprises.description: The company launched a Unified Litigation Solution, but management said investors should not model any revenue from it in 2026 because it remains in an unpriced pilot. The preview did not discuss this product or its commercialization timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company launched its new Unified Litigation Solution combining evidence and full U.S. case law, but management explicitly told investors not to build any solution revenue into models for 2026 as it remains in an unpriced pilot phase.”

surprises.description: Management introduced a possible future revenue headwind from lower ingest fees under the new platform model, although it said no meaningful drag has appeared so far. The preview did not flag this potential pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management flagged a potential future revenue headwind from lower ingest fees under the new DISCO platform model, though no meaningful drag has materialized to date.”

surprises.description: Revenue from customers generating more than $100,000 in trailing-12-month revenue grew 15% year over year, compared with 13% growth in the prior-quarter figure cited by the preview. The cohort remained 77% of revenue, so the improvement was in growth rather than its share of the business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customers generating more than $100,000 in trailing-12-month revenue grew to 354, representing $128 million or 77% of total revenue, up 15% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited the prior-quarter cohort at “$124M (77% of TTM revenue, up 13%)” and said to watch whether the large-customer cohort continued to grow.
