surprises.description: Management reaffirmed a long-term target of 20% or more annual growth, well above the preview’s FY2027 Street revenue-growth estimate of 10.8%. The preview did not mention a long-term target at that level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management ... reaffirmed a long-term target of 20%+ annual growth.”

surprises.description: Services revenue was above the preview’s implied estimate, while software revenue was close to its expected level. The services strength helped produce the modest total-revenue beat, rather than a beat driven by software.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Services revenue of $6.3 million (up 18%)” and “software revenue of $36.8 million (up 13%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Services revenue ~$5.9M implied” and “Software revenue ~$36.6M (guide midpoint).”

in_line: Q2 total revenue of $43.1 million was near the $42.67 million consensus and within the prior $41.5–$43.5 million guidance range; the preview treated roughly $0.5 million as noise.
Software revenue of $36.8 million was within the $36.1–$37.1 million guidance range and close to the preview’s approximately $36.6 million estimate.

Adjusted EBITDA of negative $3.4 million was close to the preview’s approximately negative $3.5 million consensus and within the company’s negative $4.5 million to negative $2.5 million guidance range. The Q4 positive-EBITDA expectation was also reaffirmed.
The company ended the quarter with cash and short-term investments and no debt, broadly consistent with the preview’s Q1 figures of about $103 million in cash and zero debt.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $919 million, above the preview’s more reasonable $895–897 million consensus range and even the $906 million high estimate. The 21% year-over-year growth also exceeded the preview’s 17.4% consensus growth estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted revenue reached $919 million” and grew “21% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $895M (Zacks) / $897M (MarketBeat) / $906M (ChartMill)” and “+17.4% (consensus).”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance had a $960 million midpoint, above the preview’s roughly $920 million buy-side bar and above the preview’s $920–950 million base scenario. The preview identified a midpoint below roughly $920 million as a possible sign of a stalled recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance is $945–975 million,” with “4.5% sequential growth at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 revenue guide vs. the ~$920M+ buy-side bar” and the base scenario expected “Q3 guide $920–950M.”

surprises.description: Q2 EPS was $0.19, above the preview’s $0.15 GAAP consensus estimate. That is a larger beat than the preview’s base scenario of $0.15–0.17.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 EPS was $0.19 (both GAAP and adjusted).”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 22.6%, above the 22.0% company guide and the preview’s approximate 22.0% expectation. It also cleared the preview’s 22.5% level associated with operating leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded to 22.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~22.0%” and “Results above 22.5% would point to operating leverage.”

surprises.description: Management now expects Q3 gross margin of 24% and said it would reach that target one quarter earlier than planned. The preview was watching the margin trajectory toward 23%, so this indicates a faster and higher improvement than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 gross margin to 24%, achieving that target one quarter earlier than planned.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin trajectory toward 23%.”

surprises.description: Backlog rose to $1.9 billion, with 6.1 months of coverage, rather than flattening near the prior quarter’s roughly $1.6 billion and 5.7 months. This was a stronger backlog build than the preview’s flagged warning scenario of flattening coverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total backlog growing 18% to $1.9 billion, representing 6.1 months of coverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Flattening coverage would be an early warning sign”; the preview listed prior backlog at “~$1.59–1.6B, about 5.7 months of coverage.”

surprises.description: Industrial revenue rose 30.1% year over year and accounted for over half of the total revenue increase, with smart grid, AI power, and high-voltage DC cited as drivers. The preview said AI growth was strong but had not quantified it; the reported industrial contribution makes that demand strength more concrete and substantial.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Industrial revenue jumped 16.2% sequentially and 30.1% year-over-year,” driven by “smart grid, AI power and high-voltage DC demand,” and “accounting for over half of the total revenue increase.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management called AI growth ‘strong’ with double-digit growth but has not quantified it.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that roughly one-third of running part numbers have announced price increases in response to rising metals, materials, and logistics costs, with some increases already in Q2. The preview did not flag this combination of cost pressure and broad pricing actions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “About one-third of running part numbers have had announced price increases tied to rising metals, materials and logistics costs, with some already reflected in Q2 results.”

surprises.description: The company expects negative free cash flow for 2026. Although the preview already cited $400–440 million of planned CapEx, it did not indicate that spending would result in negative full-year free cash flow.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2026 CapEx is guided at $400–440 million … and the company expects negative free cash flow for the year.”

in_line: Book-to-bill was 1.32 versus 1.34 in Q1, broadly in line with the preview’s reference point and well above its roughly 1.15–1.20 recovery-support level.
2026 CapEx remained guided at $400–440 million, matching the amount cited in the preview.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $783 million, below the preview’s operative $804 million consensus, and management said it was below its own expectations. It was essentially flat with Q1 rather than delivering the sequential growth investors were told to watch for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was approximately $783 million, essentially flat with Q1 and explicitly acknowledged as below the company's own expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “I treat $804M as the operative revenue number”; the preview also says management promised a “return to sequential quarterly revenue growth across our commercial portfolio in the near term.”

surprises.description: The preview expected nebulized Tyvaso to stabilize around $120 million, but management reported it remained pressured by intensifying competition. The call facts do not provide nebulized Tyvaso’s Q2 revenue, so the size of any shortfall cannot be determined.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nebulized Tyvaso remaining pressured by intensifying competition in the inhaled prostacyclin category.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Stabilization near $120M would suggest a one-time channel shift”; the preview also called for nebulized Tyvaso “at or above about $120M.”

surprises.description: Management did not reaffirm or update prior 2026 revenue-growth guidance, leaving the near-term growth outlook less certain than a fresh update would have. The preview did not identify this specific guidance as an expected item.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management declined to reaffirm or update any prior 2026 revenue growth guidance,” while saying the second half should be stronger than the first half.

surprises.description: The $4 billion end-of-2027 run-rate target was expected to be reaffirmed, but management said the path had “certainly narrowed” and now required contributions from IPF and ralinepag launches. The target remains achievable, but is more dependent on those launches than the preview suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: The target was “still achievable but with a path that has ‘certainly narrowed,’ now requiring contributions from IPF and ralinepag launches.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says management targets a “$4B run-rate by end of 2027” and identifies “reaffirmation of the $4B run-rate by end of 2027” as an expectation.

surprises.description: The IPF launch expected in 2027 will initially include nebulized Tyvaso only; DPI and SMI still need bridging data and further FDA engagement. The preview expected the IPF launch but did not flag this formulation limitation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The IPF launch in 2027 will initially be limited to nebulized Tyvaso only, as DPI and SMI formulations still require bridging data and further FDA engagement before approval in that indication.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview anticipated an IPF launch “by Q2 2027 on standard review” but did not specify that it would be limited to nebulized Tyvaso.

surprises.description: The company had already filed the Tyvaso IPF sNDA in late June, earlier than the preview’s expected end-of-summer filing window.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An sNDA for nebulized Tyvaso in IPF (filed late June).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected the TETON sNDA filing “by the end of summer 2026.”

surprises.description: Management reported record patient starts, referrals, total patients, and commercial patients exiting Q2, indicating stronger underlying patient momentum than the essentially flat revenue headline alone would suggest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record levels were reached in patient starts, referrals, total patients, and commercial patients exiting Q2,” which management cited as evidence of underlying momentum despite flat reported revenue.

surprises.description: The company roughly doubled its sales force, with new representatives entering the field around July 1 to expand community reach ahead of the IPF and ralinepag launches; the preview had not anticipated this expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company roughly doubled its sales force, with new representatives entering the field around July 1 to expand reach into the community setting ahead of the IPF and ralinepag launches.”

surprises.description: TETON-1 results surpassed the earlier TETON-2 readout, and TETON-PPF enrollment was already over 95% complete, nearly finished ahead of schedule. The preview did not flag these clinical-development updates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “TETON-1 results surpassed the prior TETON-2 readout, and TETON-PPF enrollment is over 95% complete (nearly finished ahead of schedule) with a Phase III readout expected in the second half of 2027.”

surprises.description: Management described IPF and ralinepag as multibillion-dollar opportunities and said the PPF opportunity could be at least twice as large as IPF, adding a larger opportunity claim than the preview had discussed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management framed both IPF and ralinepag as multibillion-dollar opportunities, and stated the PPF opportunity could be at least double that of IPF.”

in_line: The ralinepag NDA was filed in the expected second-half 2026 window; the preview expected confirmation of a submission in 2H26.
Revenue of $783 million was above the preview’s Q1 sequential reference point of $781.5 million, although it was essentially flat sequentially and below the operative consensus estimate.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $163 million, well above the preview’s $150.6 million consensus and $145–155 million company guide. This was a clear upside surprise on the headline revenue result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 net sales rose 23.2% year-over-year to $163 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Consensus $150.6M; company guide $145–155M.”

surprises.description: MEC raised full-year sales guidance to $620–650 million rather than reaffirming the prior $590–620 million range expected in the preview. The $52–60 million adjusted EBITDA range was maintained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 net sales guidance was raised to $620-650 million while adjusted EBITDA guidance was maintained at $52-60 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance reaffirmed at $590–620M and $52–60M.”

surprises.description: The 8.1% adjusted EBITDA margin was above the roughly 7.6% margin implied by the preview’s $11.5 million guide midpoint at midpoint sales; applied to reported sales, it implies adjusted EBITDA of about $13.2 million, slightly above the $10–13 million Q2 guide. The margin nevertheless remained below the prior-year 10.3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 8.1% from 10.3% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | Company guide $10–13M”; “Adj. EBITDA at or above $11.5M (guide midpoint)”; implied margin “~7.6% at guide midpoint.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was a $6.6 million use rather than turning positive, and MEC cut full-year free cash flow guidance to $7–15 million from $25–35 million. Both the quarter and the revised annual outlook were materially worse than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was a use of $6.6 million versus $12.5 million provided a year earlier, prompting the company to lower full-year free cash flow guidance to $7-15 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow $25–35M”; “Q2 free cash flow needs to turn positive against a $25–35M full-year target”; catalyst: “Positive Q2 free cash flow.”

surprises.description: Net leverage was 2.9x, above the preview’s estimated 2.6–2.8x post-offering range and its checklist threshold of 2.8x. The equity offering was already anticipated, but leverage remained higher than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt rose to $134.7 million from $71.8 million a year ago, pushing the bank covenant net leverage ratio to 2.9x versus a long-term target of 2.5x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Derived post-offering leverage is roughly 2.6–2.8x”; catalyst: “Net leverage at or below 2.8x.”

surprises.description: The company reported $2.1 million of Q2 project launch costs, above the $1.2 million launch-cost figure referenced in the preview’s bull case. That added pressure to a quarter in which the margin was already below last year’s level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 8.1% from 10.3% a year earlier, hit by $2.1 million of project launch costs and higher gain-sharing accruals.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Launch costs below the $1.2M flagged.”

surprises.description: The outlook disclosed a further $5–6 million of launch-related costs and $2–3 million of outsourcing costs, with new equipment taking four to six months before work can move in-house. The preview did not flag this additional cost burden or transition timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year outlook includes $5-6 million of launch-related costs and $2-3 million of outsourcing costs, with new equipment carrying four-to-six-month lead times before work moves in-house.”

surprises.description: MEC plans about $50 million of incremental investment over two years, with a possible additional $25–30 million Southeast facility, to expand capacity beyond the previously cited $850 million level. The capacity opportunity and targeted returns are positive, but the scale of the added spending was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans ~$50 million of incremental investment over two years (plus a potential $25-30 million new Southeast facility) to lift revenue capacity beyond the prior $850 million level, targeting 15%+ IRR and 2-3 year payback.”

surprises.description: A new post-acquisition customer awarded more than $55 million this year, a significant customer-specific award not identified in the preview. Overall Q2 awards of about $40 million met the preview’s award threshold, but this individual award added an unanticipated detail about demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 added ~$40 million in new awards, with one new post-acquisition customer alone awarding over $55 million this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “DC&CP revenue at or above $28M and new awards at or above $40M.”

in_line: DC&CP was expected to contribute roughly 20% or more of FY26 revenue, and MEC said it expects the segment to reach about 20%. Q2 awards of about $40 million also met the preview’s $40 million threshold; the pipeline above $125 million had already been reported before Q2.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $83.9 million, below the preview’s $85–90 million guidance range and $87.44 million consensus. Management attributed about $3 million of the shortfall to KELK shipments delayed by the ERP implementation; most are expected to ship in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $83.9 million”; revenue was reduced by “approximately $3 million” due to temporarily delayed KELK shipments caused by a new ERP system implementation, with those orders expected to ship “mostly in Q4” by year-end.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 company guidance of “$85–90M (constant FX)” and consensus revenue of “$87.44M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.04 fell well short of even the preview’s lower consensus estimate of $0.108; the preview also cited a $0.19 estimate from another source. The quarter had a GAAP net loss of $1.7 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company reported “adjusted net earnings of $586,000 ($0.04 per diluted share)” and “a GAAP net loss of $1.7 million (-$0.13 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave adjusted EPS consensus as “$0.19” or “$0.108,” noting a source conflict.

surprises.description: Sensors’ book-to-bill reached 1.44, above the preview’s 1.36 comparison point, with record bookings. This was stronger than the preview’s benchmark for the segment.
surprises.fact_evidence: Sensors had a “very strong 1.44 book-to-bill ratio with record quarterly bookings of $48.1 million (up 6% sequentially).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist compared Sensors’ book-to-bill with “1.36.”

surprises.description: Management said full-year 2026 organic growth should exceed the 8%–10% target in its three-year plan, a more favorable outlook than the preview had specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects “full-year 2026 organic growth to exceed the 8%-10% target in its 3-year plan.”

surprises.description: The initial humanoid robotics customer issued a formal vendor nomination and projected a ramp from tens of bots per week to hundreds and even thousands weekly by year-end. The preview anticipated near-term shipments of about $1.2 million or more, but did not flag this formal nomination or projected production scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company received a “formal vendor nomination letter” from its initial humanoid robotics customer, which projects production rising “from tens of bots per week to hundreds and even thousands per week by the end of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 shipped about “$600K” and management guided to “more than double” in Q2, or “~$1.2M+.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $84–89 million implies some sequential growth from Q2’s $83.9 million at the midpoint, rather than the flattening scenario the preview identified as a concern, despite seasonal European effects.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 2026 revenue is guided to “$84 million to $89 million despite seasonal European impacts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a Q3 guide that flattens sequentially would support the one-quarter-surge bear case.”

surprises.description: Foreign exchange was a significant reported drag on operating profit, an adverse factor the preview did not identify in its outlook discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: Foreign exchange reduced operating profit by approximately “$900,000 sequentially and $3.3 million year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Backlog rose by roughly $10–11 million sequentially to $135.8 million, indicating a stronger order pipeline than the preview had specifically anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog grew approximately $10-11 million sequentially to $135.8 million.”

surprises.description: The company reported $1.6 million of first-half cost savings and said it remained on track for $6 million this year, providing specific near-term progress against the longer-term cost-reduction plan discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Cost savings totaled “$1.6 million in the first half ($600,000 in Q1 and $1 million in Q2),” and the company is “on track to reach $6 million this year” toward roughly $20 million over three years.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview referenced a “three-year model” but did not state an annual savings target or expected first-half delivery.

surprises.description: The company paid down $5 million of debt rather than simply retaining the liquidity highlighted in the preview; the action reduces interest costs but leaves net cash slightly below the preview’s prior-quarter figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company paid down “$5 million of debt” to reduce long-term debt to $15.6 million, ended Q2 with $60 million net cash, and cut net interest cost by about “$300,000 annually.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the CFO had flagged “ample liquidity to support M&A” and cited prior-quarter net cash of “$62M ($82.5M gross).”

surprises.description: Management said price increases can apply only to new orders, limiting their near-term Q3 ASP benefit to a few hundred thousand dollars. The preview had not discussed this constraint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Price increases can only be applied to new orders, limiting near-term ASP benefit to a few hundred thousand dollars in Q3.”

in_line: Consolidated book-to-bill was 1.14: above 1.0 and within the preview’s 1.05–1.20 base-case range, though just below the preview’s >1.15 confirmation threshold.

surprises.description: Revenue was $25.7 million, about $2.1 million above the roughly $23.56 million consensus estimate and above the preview’s $23.0 million base scenario. That is a clear beat, though close to the preview’s $25.5 million bull scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue grew 32% year-over-year to $25.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue… Consensus… ~$23.56M”; the base scenario was “~$23.0M” and the bull scenario “~$25.5M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 34.6%, well above the approximately 30% guide and the preview’s scenarios. About 130 basis points came from a one-time benefit from tariff changes and refunds, so not all of the margin outperformance appears recurring.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Overall gross margin expanded to 34.6% from 30.1%, though roughly 130 basis points came from a one-time net benefit of tariff changes and refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin: ~30% (guided, Jun 4, 2026)”; the bull scenario expected “~32%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $2.5 million, far above even the preview’s $1.6 million bull scenario. The expected continuation of positive EBITDA arrived with substantially more profitability than the preview modeled.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $2.5 million from $200,000 year-over-year, marking Orion's seventh consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s scenarios estimated adjusted EBITDA of “~$0.6M” in the base case and “~$1.6M” in the bull case; it also flagged the positive-EBITDA streak as something to watch.

surprises.description: GAAP net income turned positive at $2 million, or 47 cents per diluted share, above the preview’s consensus EPS range of a 1-cent loss to 7 cents profit. The preview warned that EPS estimates were split-contaminated, so the comparison is less reliable than the revenue and margin comparisons.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 net income turned positive at $2 million (47 cents per diluted share), a swing from a net loss of $1.2 million (37 cents loss per share) a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP)… Consensus… $(0.01) to $0.07”; the preview cautioned: “Do not trade the headline EPS-vs-consensus print.”

surprises.description: Backlog fell to about $24 million from $30.1 million at the prior quarter-end, below the preview’s supportive threshold of holding at or above $30 million and near its warning of a decline toward the mid-$20 millions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog exiting Q1 stood at approximately $24 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Backlog at 6/30/26 vs. $30.1M”; “holding at or above $30M is supportive” and “a sequential decline toward the mid-$20Ms would undercut the FY27 guide.”

surprises.description: Management said it does not expect the even intra-year revenue pattern previously described in the preview. Q1 was boosted by a roughly $15 million exterior-lighting project recognized largely across Q4 and Q1, making the quarterly cadence less even than investors had been led to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management does not expect the intra-year revenue ramp seen in prior years, as Q1 was bolstered by a ~$15 million exterior lighting project largely recognized across Q4 and Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had indicated FY27 revenue should “play out relatively evenly over the year.”

surprises.description: LED revenue was $17.7 million, above the preview’s roughly $12 million quarterly-average benchmark and its $15 million bull-case marker. The segment also reported a substantial year-over-year margin improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LED lighting segment revenue grew to $17.7 million from $12.9 million with margin improving to 37.8% from 31.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 needs to land well above the ~$12M quarterly average”; the bull scenario assumed “LED holds above $15M.”

surprises.description: EV charging revenue rose to $4 million rather than suffering another sharply down quarter, as the preview warned was possible. This stronger revenue trend came alongside a material margin decline, a separate negative development for the segment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EV charging revenue rose to $4 million from $2.7 million, but gross margin fell to 26.9% from 33.8% amid sector-wide market uncertainty.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a third sharply down quarter would weigh on the multiple.” It did not give an EV charging margin expectation.

surprises.description: Most revenue from the new hyperscale data-center lighting business is now expected in fiscal 2028, later than the preview’s expectation of revenue in late fiscal 2027. The call did add that individual buildings could represent multi-million-dollar opportunities.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The newly entered hyperscale data center lighting business is expected to generate most of its revenue in fiscal 2028, with each building potentially representing seven-figure (multi-million dollar) opportunities.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management expected “data-center revenue in late FY27.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that each potential hyperscale building could represent a multi-million-dollar opportunity, giving a scale estimate the preview did not provide. This is potential opportunity, not booked revenue, and most revenue is expected in FY2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Each building potentially representing seven-figure (multi-million dollar) opportunities.”

surprises.description: Management said a potential interior Home Depot project was progressing, although it remained unbooked. The preview did not identify this project, so the update adds a possible opportunity but not committed revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A potential interior Home Depot project remains unbooked but progressing.”

in_line: Management reiterated fiscal 2027 revenue guidance of $95–97 million and its expectation of positive adjusted EBITDA, consistent with the guidance already in the preview.
Orion extended its positive adjusted EBITDA streak to seven consecutive quarters, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the streak would continue as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: OSS raised its FY2026 revenue-growth outlook to 25%-30% from 20%-25%, rather than reaffirming the prior range. The new outlook is above the preview’s roughly 24.8% consensus growth estimate, which was already near the top of the old guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Increased full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to 25%-30%, up from prior guidance of 20%-25%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company FY2026 guidance: Revenue +20–25%”; “A simple reaffirm is effectively a small miss against estimates. A raise is the cleanest bull catalyst.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $9.3 million came in above the preview’s derived estimate of roughly $8.8 million and just above its $8.6-$9.2 million base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue from continuing operations grew 62.3% year-over-year to $9.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 revenue: Not found as a published consensus”; “Derived only: roughly $8.8M”; base scenario “$8.6–9.2M.”

surprises.description: A $6.25 million legal settlement charge pushed GAAP results to a $7.3 million continuing-operations loss, while the loss excluding the charge was only $0.2 million, or $0.01 per share—better than the preview’s expected $0.02-$0.03 per-share loss. The unusually large one-off charge was not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $6.25 million legal settlement charge drove a GAAP net loss from continuing operations of $7.3 million ($0.29/share), though excluding the charge the non-GAAP net loss narrowed to just $0.2 million ($0.01/share).”

surprises.description: Bookings reached $15.1 million with a 1.7 book-to-bill ratio, comfortably above the preview’s expectation that Q2 would exceed 1.0 and close to Q1’s roughly $15 million and 1.8 ratio. This indicates the strong booking pace continued rather than decelerating toward the preview’s cautionary threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record bookings of $15.1 million in Q2 and over $30 million year-to-date, yielding a book-to-bill ratio of approximately 1.7.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 was about $15M in bookings at 1.8x”; “above 1.0x should be achievable, but a print near 1.0x would read as deceleration.”

surprises.description: The call reported 14 multi-year programs with more than $42 million in combined estimated revenue potential, up from one such program three years earlier, and average order size nearly tripling since 2023. The preview asked for firmer pipeline detail but did not anticipate this scale of program growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Now supporting 14 multi-year programs with estimated combined revenue potential exceeding $42 million, up from just one such program three years ago, with average order size nearly tripling since 2023.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Pipeline and program detail” as a key watch and called out “any firmer pipeline figure.”

in_line: Gross margin was 39.1%, close to management’s approximately 40% pre-guide; the preview specifically cautioned that Q2 margin would likely be well below Q1’s 51.6%.
The company maintained its approximately 40% full-year gross-margin expectation and positive full-year EBITDA outlook, consistent with the prior guidance described in the preview.
The $8.4 million defense award was already expected to fall into Q2, according to the preview.
The preview identified memory and component timing as a key risk, but the reported facts do not indicate that deliveries were pushed out of 2026.

surprises.description: Operating EPS was $1.30, beating the preview’s $1.15 consensus by about 13%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted operating EPS rose 46% year-over-year to $1.30.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating EPS (diluted) | $1.15 (Zacks, ~Aug 3)”

surprises.description: The combined ratio came in better than the 90.7% estimate, and the 87.6% ex-cat result was below the preview’s 88% level that it said would signal a conservative FY guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The overall combined ratio was 89.5% (87.6% ex-cat).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Combined ratio | 90.7%”; “An ex-cat result below 88% would suggest the FY guide is conservative.”

surprises.description: Skyward Specialty’s expense ratio was substantially lower than the preview’s estimate, improving the underwriting result beyond what that estimate implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Skyward Specialty expense ratio improved 2.7 points year-over-year to 24.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Loss ratio / expense ratio | 62.3% / 28.4% (Zacks segment est.)”

surprises.description: First-half underwriting fee income reached $23 million against a $30–35 million full-year target, while the preview noted consensus models expected commission and fee income to decline 23% year-over-year. That first-half pace was stronger than the preview’s consensus concern suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fee-generating GWP rose 29% to $318 million,” and management “reaffirmed full-year underwriting fee income guidance of $30-35 million despite $23 million booked in the first half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus models commission and fee income down 23% YoY, which conflicts with the company's own trajectory”; FY fee income guidance was “$30M–$35M.”

surprises.description: Apollo’s result included 5.4 points of catastrophe losses from the Middle East conflict, an unanticipated source of losses that pushed its combined ratio to 97.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Apollo was at 97.6% due to 5.4 points of Middle East conflict catastrophe losses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “severe convective storm and early wind” as the Q2 catastrophe risks to watch.

surprises.description: Net investment income exceeded the preview’s estimate, though by a relatively small amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net investment income rose over 60% year-over-year to $31 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net investment income | ~$29.5M (Zacks segment est.)”

surprises.description: Management said the full-year accident-year loss ratio is expected to rise roughly 1% or more because of business mix, with lower acquisition costs expected to offset the increase. The preview did not flag this loss-ratio outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects the “full-year accident-year loss ratio up roughly 1%+ offset by lower acquisition costs”; the non-cat loss ratio increase was “driven purely by business mix shift toward higher-loss A&H and agriculture.”

surprises.description: The company repaid $50 million of its term loan and reduced financial leverage by 2 points, an unpreviewed step toward its low-20s leverage target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repaid $50 million of its $150 million term loan, reducing financial leverage 2 points to 26% as it targets a low-20s debt-to-cap ratio.”

surprises.description: Skyward Specialty’s non-cat loss ratio was about 1 point better than the preview’s estimate, even though it increased year-over-year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Skyward Specialty non-cat loss ratio increased 1.4 points to 61.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Loss ratio / expense ratio | 62.3% / 28.4% (Zacks segment est.)”

in_line: Management reaffirmed full-year underwriting fee income guidance of $30–35 million, as the preview expected.
The July doubling of the buyback authorization to $100 million was already noted in the preview.

surprises.description: Q3 net sales, adjusted EBITDA and EPS all exceeded the preview’s consensus: sales were $545 million versus $531.7 million, EBITDA was $162 million versus about $154 million, and EPS was $0.57 versus $0.50. The EPS beat was especially large relative to the estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales increased 24% year-over-year to $545 million, EBITDA rose 25% to $162 million … and EPS grew 21% to $0.57.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenues … $531.7M”; “Adj. EBITDA … ~$154M”; “Adj. EPS … $0.50.”

surprises.description: System-wide same-store sales were 8%, above the preview’s 6.6% published consensus, though around the late-July sell-side marks of about 8%. More than three-quarters of the comp came from ticket, versus the preview’s base case of about two-thirds and its bull case of transaction-led growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “System-wide same-store sales grew 8%, with ticket driving more than three-quarters of the comp.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “System-wide SSS … +6.6%”; “Sell-side models sit higher, around 8%”; the base case expected “about two-thirds of the comp from ticket,” while the bull case anticipated transaction growth accelerating.

surprises.description: Q3 EBITDA margin reached 29.8%, about 100 basis points above the roughly 28.8% implied by the preview’s EBITDA consensus, and expanded year over year despite gross-margin pressure. SG&A fell 90 basis points as a share of sales, offsetting a 50-basis-point gross-margin decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EBITDA … with margin expanding 30 basis points to 29.8%”; “SG&A fell 90 basis points year-over-year to 17% of net sales, while gross margin declined 50 basis points to 40%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus of ~$154M implies a margin near 28.8%”; “Q3 is seasonally the strongest margin quarter, so sequential expansion off Q2's 26.5% is expected.”

surprises.description: The base-oil supply risk the preview had flagged materialized into a sharp and potentially persistent cost shock: management expects finished-lubricant costs to be about 60% above March levels, or $5–$7 more per oil change, and to remain elevated for 4–6 months after the Strait of Hormuz reopens. Management expects Q4 margin compression of 300–400 basis points, nearly all from product costs, even as implied same-store sales are about 8%–10% and largely pricing-driven.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has constrained Group III base oil supply”; finished lubricant costs are expected to be “roughly 60% above March levels,” translating to “a $5-$7 increase per oil change”; elevated costs may persist “at least 4 to 6 months after the Strait fully reopens”; “Q4 is expected to see 300-400 basis points of margin compression driven almost entirely by product cost increases,” with implied same-store sales of “roughly 8%-10% largely driven by pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had “flagged Middle East supply risk to lubricant costs” and noted “base-oil squeeze” as a bear-case risk, but did not anticipate the stated cost increase, duration, or Q4 margin compression.

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook improved: the range was narrowed to $550–$560 million and management now expects about 50 basis points of margin compression rather than the previously planned 100 basis points. This is a better outlook despite the newly quantified product-cost shock.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company narrowed its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $550-$560 million … and now expects only about 50 basis points of full-year EBITDA margin compression versus the previously planned 100 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was “$540–560M”; the preview also said Breeze dilution was sized at “less than 100 bps” of full-year EBITDA margin.

surprises.description: Full-year EPS guidance was narrowed but its ceiling stayed at $1.75, below the preview’s stated level of roughly $1.80 needed to exceed consensus. The higher floor is an improvement over the prior range, but the update did not deliver the above-consensus raise the preview identified as a meaningful upside surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company narrowed its … EPS to $1.70-$1.75.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior guidance was “$1.65–1.75”; the preview said “$1.75” was the consensus and “a figure around $1.80 or higher is needed” to move beyond it. Its base case anticipated EPS guidance of “$1.72–1.78.”

surprises.description: Year-to-date free cash flow and leverage were better than the preview’s reference points, and management is now targeting a restart of share repurchases. The preview cited $45 million of year-to-date FCF and 3.1x leverage, and described buybacks as a catalyst rather than an announced target at that leverage level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date free cash flow reached $112 million (up ~$93 million), operating cash flow improved $105 million to $285 million, and net leverage declined ~10% sequentially to 2.8x as the company targets restarting share repurchases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FCF was $45M year-to-date, up about $57M year over year”; “Net debt / adj. EBITDA improved to 3.1x”; the preview said buybacks were tied to reaching target leverage and that a commitment to restart would be “a new catalyst.”

surprises.description: Twelve Breeze stores have been converted to the Valvoline Instant Oil Change brand, with performance slightly ahead of expectations. The preview discussed Breeze dilution and integration, but did not anticipate this specific conversion update or the favorable performance assessment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “12 Breeze stores have been converted to the Valvoline Instant Oil Change brand with performance slightly ahead of expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Breeze as “in the base for a full quarter” and noted management sized its margin dilution at “less than 100 bps,” without reporting a conversion count or performance assessment.

in_line: The 47 net new stores added were within the preview’s expected Q3 range of about 45–60.
Full-year same-store sales guidance of 7.5%–8% was in line with the preview’s base case of 7.5%–8%, and the preview expected a full-year guidance raise.
The new full-year sales range of $2.05–$2.10 billion was broadly in line with the preview’s roughly $2.07 billion consensus and anticipated modest raise.
The 8% Q3 same-store sales result was around the preview’s late-July sell-side expectation of about 8%, even though it exceeded the cited published consensus.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $10.10, well above the preview’s $8.22 consensus estimate. The reported result exceeded expectations by $1.88 per share, or about 23%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income of $499 million, or $10.10 per share”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS (Q2) | Consensus | $8.22”

surprises.description: Refining capture substantially exceeded the preview’s estimate that consensus assumed about 97%: system-wide capture was 125%, or 112% normalized. The reported $77 million Hawaii net price-lag gain boosted the unnormalized figure, but normalized capture also exceeded the implied expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “System-wide refining capture was 125% (112% normalized), with Hawaii benefiting from a $77 million net price lag gain of $11.49 per barrel.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My estimate is that consensus assumes capture near 97%”

surprises.description: Q3 Hawaii capture is expected to fall below the typical 100%–110% range because turnaround costs are concentrated in the quarter and imported products are being costed then. The preview flagged the turnaround as a major risk, but did not specify capture falling below the typical range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 Hawaii capture is expected to fall below the typical 100%-110% range due to concentrated turnaround costs and increased refined product imports being costed in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The size of that opportunity cost is the largest guidance risk.”

surprises.description: The July refining index was $31.34 per barrel, about $1.60 below Q2’s average, indicating sequential softening rather than the record-level July cracks described in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The July consolidated refining index averaged $31.34 per barrel, about $1.60 below the Q2 average, signaling some sequential margin softening.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A 30–45 day turnaround began in late June, and its financial impact lands mostly in Q3, when July cracks reached record levels.”

surprises.description: The company reported a $312 million working-capital outflow, with roughly half tied to Hawaii pre-turnaround inventory builds. The preview discussed timing and inventory effects but did not flag an outflow of this size; management expects it to substantially reverse after the turnaround and price stabilization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Working capital outflows of $312 million (roughly half tied to Hawaii pre-turnaround inventory builds) are expected to substantially reverse after the turnaround and price stabilization.”

surprises.description: The call put a potential value of about $300 million on full small-refinery exemptions across the three mainland refineries at current RIN prices. The preview highlighted uncertainty around SRE decisions and monetization but did not quantify this potential value; the exemptions were not stated to be confirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full small refinery exemptions across all three mainland refineries could be worth about $300 million at current RIN prices, with a September 1 compliance deadline for 2025 being closely watched.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Whether Par is among them is unconfirmed” and “Monetized less than half of prior SRE-related RINs; wanted EPA clarity on 2025 exemptions first.”

surprises.description: Par reported reducing net debt by more than $220 million and ending the quarter with about $1.4 billion of liquidity, including $185 million of cash. The preview focused on whether buybacks would accelerate, rather than flagging this debt reduction and liquidity position.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced net debt by over $220 million during the quarter,” and “Total liquidity ended the quarter at approximately $1.4 billion with a cash balance of $185 million.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA of $571 million was within the preview’s base-case range of approximately $560–600 million, although below its separate derived estimate of about $600 million.
The Hawaii turnaround remained a significant Q3 headwind, consistent with the preview’s warning that its financial impact would land mostly in Q3.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS reached $3.42, beating the preview’s $2.94 consensus by $0.48 and exceeding the high end of company guidance by $0.44. The call attributed the result to lower operating expenses and stronger acquisition performance, a positive outcome on the preview’s acquisition-dilution watch item.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS reached a record $3.42” and “exceeding the high end of guidance by $0.44 due to lower operating expenses and stronger acquisition performance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | Consensus | $2.94 | Company guidance … $2.88–$2.98”; the preview also identified “Acquisition dilution runoff” as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: Revenue was $313 million, $13.83 million above the preview’s $299.17 million consensus. The preview’s bull scenario called for revenue above $299 million, and the reported result cleared that level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 23% to a record $313 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus | $299.17M”; the bull scenario was “Above $299M.”

surprises.description: Kadant raised its full-year revenue range to $1.19B–$1.21B from $1.178B–$1.203B and lifted the low end of adjusted EPS guidance by $0.10, leaving the high end unchanged. That was better than simply reaffirming the prior ranges, a key issue the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $1.19B-$1.21B and narrowed adjusted EPS guidance to $12.43-$12.68, up from $12.33-$12.68.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 guidance as revenue “$1.178B–$1.203B” and adjusted EPS “$12.33–$12.68,” and said “Any change to the $12.33–$12.68 FY adjusted-EPS range” was important.

surprises.description: Despite the strong quarter and higher full-year guidance, Q3 guidance was cautious: management cited capital-project timing and said the Q2 beat did not translate into upside for the next quarter. The preview emphasized forward guidance but did not provide a Q3 estimate or explicitly anticipate this near-term caution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $297M-$307M and adjusted EPS of $2.90-$3.00, implying no upside from the Q2 beat as management remains cautious on capital project timing.”

surprises.description: Organic capital revenue surged 23%, producing the company’s second-best Q2 capital-equipment revenue in its history despite the prolonged investment downturn. The preview gave no segment-level forecast, so this was an unanticipated strength in a market area described as challenged in the call facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Organic capital revenue surged 23%, representing the second-best Q2 capital equipment revenue in company history despite a prolonged capital investment downturn.”

surprises.description: Bookings rose 16%, but large capital-project orders were delayed. The preview had flagged bookings and backlog momentum as a key demand signal, so the growth was encouraging, while the project delays temper the strength and align with management’s cautious timing commentary.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bookings increased 16% to $312 million, driven by recent acquisitions and strong aftermarket parts demand, even as large capital project orders were delayed.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Bookings and backlog momentum” as a key metric to watch and noted Q1 bookings were a record; its bull scenario said “bookings strength continues.”

surprises.description: Gross margin fell 210 basis points as aftermarket parts made up a smaller share of revenue, even though adjusted EBITDA margin expanded year over year. The preview offered no margin expectation, making this a newly reported mix-related pressure alongside stronger overall profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined 210 basis points to 43.8% as higher-margin aftermarket parts fell to 68% of revenue from 71%, reflecting a higher capital mix”; adjusted EBITDA margin expanded “to 21.8% from 20.5%.”

surprises.description: Acquisition borrowing lifted net debt by $129 million sequentially and raised leverage to 1.72 from 1.27. The preview discussed acquisitions and their purchase-accounting effects but did not flag this increase in debt or leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt rose $129 million sequentially to $373 million after borrowing $181.8 million for acquisitions, lifting the leverage ratio to 1.72 from 1.27.”

surprises.description: The preview described roughly $17 million of tariff refunds as a potential swing factor and said it was unclear whether any would be recognized. The company reported receiving $17.6 million, recognized $6.9 million in Q2, and said the remaining refunds will benefit Q3 and Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received $17.6 million in IEEPA tariff refunds ($6.9 million recognized in Q2) that will benefit Q3 and Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Whether any refund is recognized, deferred, or reinvested is the largest single EPS swing factor”; roughly $17 million of potential tariff refunds were “excluded from guidance.”

surprises.description: The prior full-year gross-margin target was flat, but the company now expects gross margin to improve roughly 150 basis points, with tariff refunds contributing 110 basis points and mix and cost efficiencies providing the rest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year gross margin is expected to improve roughly 150 basis points, with 110 basis points from tariff refunds and the balance from mix and cost efficiencies.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 gross margin would “normalize over the rest of the year” and that management had “kept a flat full-year GM target.”

surprises.description: The preview expected Lacoste to decline 19% in Q2; the reported decline was 16%, a somewhat better result than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lacoste declined 16% against a 44% prior-year comparison.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Lacoste. Down 19% in Q2, with the relaunch not expected until 2027.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag a war-related regional sales shock. The company reported a 24% decline in Middle East and Africa, while Asia Pacific and South America grew 14% and 15%, respectively.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Middle East and Africa region fell 24% due to the ongoing war, while Asia Pacific rose 14% and South America grew 15%.”

surprises.description: The call announced a new share-repurchase program for both Interparfums, Inc. and Interparfums SA, backed by a credit line of up to $250 million; the preview did not anticipate a buyback or new borrowing facility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board authorized a share repurchase program (for both Interparfums, Inc. and Interparfums SA shares) backed by a new line of credit of up to $250 million.”

surprises.description: The preview did not discuss cash flow or inventory expectations. The company reported H1 operating cash flow of $46 million versus $5 million a year earlier, alongside a 12% inventory reduction to $376 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “H1 operating cash flow surged to $46 million (49% of net income) from $5 million (5%) prior year, aided by a 12% inventory reduction to $376 million and the tariff refunds.”

in_line: Management maintained FY26 guidance at approximately $1.48 billion in sales and $4.85 diluted EPS, as the preview expected a reaffirmation; the preview noted those figures were below consensus of $1.50 billion and $4.88.
The Q2 sales movements for U.S.-based operations (+18%) and European-based operations (-4%) matched the figures already cited in the preview.

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance fell to 21.3% excluding refunds from the preview's 22.2% guide. Management attributed the reduction to slower productivity gains, price lagging faster inflation, and unfavorable mix, with modest price/cost headwinds expected through the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year margin guidance was cut to 21.3% (ex-refunds) due to slower productivity realization, price lagging faster inflation, and unfavorable mix”; “modest price/cost headwinds [are] expected to persist through the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin ~22.2% (trimmed from 22.5%)”; management “targets dollar-cost neutrality by mid-2026” and “margin neutrality by year-end.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow guidance was cut by $50 million to $600 million, rather than staying at the preview's $650 million. Stronger AMC growth is requiring more working capital, although management still expects net debt leverage below 3x in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow guidance was reduced by $50 million to $600 million as stronger AMC growth required incremental working capital,” while the company “still expects net debt leverage below 3x in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow $650M (unchanged)” and “the FY guide of $650M is unchanged”; the preview said roughly $130–180M of Q2 FCF was needed to keep the year credible.

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted EPS midpoint stayed at $10.60 instead of being raised, despite the preview saying a raise was needed to clear the bar. The unchanged midpoint now includes a $0.57 refund benefit, implying a lower underlying outlook than the prior midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS midpoint unchanged at $10.60,” with “a $48 million/$0.57 refund benefit now incorporated.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a raise, not just a reaffirmation, is needed,” and described the bull scenario as an FY EPS guide raised toward $10.80–11.00.

surprises.description: Reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $2.99 was well above the $2.58–$2.60 consensus range, but $0.39 of EPS came from tariff refunds; excluding them, EPS was $2.60, essentially in line with consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EPS was $2.99, but excluding $32 million of IEEPA tariff refunds, EPS was $2.60.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus Q2 2026E” adjusted EPS was “$2.58” or “$2.60.”

surprises.description: Management raised its AMC growth outlook to low double digits but lowered IPS to low single digits and PES to flat-to-slightly-down. That is a less broad-based growth outlook than the preview's bullish scenario of sequential gains in all three segments, though the preview noted that segment-level consensus was unavailable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management shifted its segment growth outlook, raising AMC to low double digits (from high single digits) while lowering IPS to low single digits (from mid-single) and PES to flat-to-slightly-down.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's bull scenario cited “sequential gains in all three segments”; it also said “Segment-level consensus was not available.”

surprises.description: AMC orders remained strong, but were slower than the prior quarter's 34% growth, and nearly half of first-half orders reflected longer-cycle projects benefiting 2027–2028. That supports continued demand while tempering the near-term significance of the order growth the preview was watching.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AMC orders up 17.1% (15% excluding data center),” with first-half orders “up over 25%, though nearly half reflects longer-cycle projects benefiting 2027-2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “AMC orders +34% Y/Y” in Q1 and that “the bar is now high”; it flagged a book-to-bill falling toward about 1.05 as a sign the data center order surge might be lumpy.

surprises.description: Commercial rare-earth magnet supply is expected to be mostly mitigated this quarter, better near-term news than the preview's warning about supply constraints, but defense applications remain constrained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rare earth magnet supply for commercial uses should be mostly mitigated this quarter but remains constrained for defense applications.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said rare-earth magnet constraints “cost about 30bps.”

surprises.description: The company now expects an additional $15 million of ePod sales in Q4, an earlier revenue contribution than the preview's discussion of ePod orders shipping in 2027 suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An additional $15 million of ePod sales (at ~20% margins) [is] now expected in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “$735M of ePOD orders ship in 2027” and that Q2 was “about order and funnel confirmation more than P&L contribution.”

in_line: Full-year sales guidance remained at about $6.2 billion, matching the preview's expectation that the base case would reaffirm guidance.
Excluding the tariff refunds, Q2 adjusted EPS of $2.60 was in line with the preview's $2.58–$2.60 consensus range.

surprises.description: Talos was expected to reiterate its full-year production guidance until the acquisition closed, but it raised its stand-alone 2026 guidance before closing: oil guidance is now 64,000–68,000 barrels per day and total production guidance is 87,000–91,000 BOE per day, even after accounting for the shelf divestment.
surprises.fact_evidence: Talos raised full-year 2026 stand-alone production guidance to 64,000–68,000 barrels of oil per day and 87,000–91,000 BOE per day, even after excluding the pending Gulf of America acquisition and including the shelf divestment impact.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management said it will “update 2026 guidance after closing,” so expect guidance to be reiterated rather than re-cut on the call.

surprises.description: The preview flagged BP’s preferential right as a risk that could halve the acquisition’s scope. BP declined to exercise it, leaving Talos with the Coulomb operating role and Na Kika partnership; the transaction is now expected to close in Q3 rather than by year-end, and the assets are reported at approximately 18,000 BOE per day versus the preview’s roughly 16,000.
surprises.fact_evidence: BP declined to exercise its preferential right, allowing Talos to operate the Coulomb field and become a partner in the Na Kika platform. The pending acquisition adds assets producing approximately 18,000 BOE per day and is expected to close in Q3 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: If [BP’s right is] exercised, Talos keeps Coulomb only, roughly halving the deal’s scope. The acquisition was “expected to close by year-end 2026”; it adds about 16 MBoe/d.

surprises.description: Q2 production came in above the quarter’s guidance, rather than merely meeting the 63,000–67,000 barrels-per-day oil and 88,000–92,000 BOE-per-day total ranges.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 oil production averaged approximately 69,000 barrels per day and total production nearly 94,000 BOE per day, both exceeding guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Company guidance (Q2): oil 63–67 MBbl/d; total 88–92 MBoe/d.

surprises.description: The preview warned that hedge losses could claw back much of the benefit from higher oil prices, but Talos reported record adjusted free cash flow and adjusted EBITDA. The preview gave no consensus benchmarks for either measure, so the size of the gap cannot be quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company generated record adjusted free cash flow of approximately $232 million and adjusted EBITDA of approximately $402 million in Q2 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Roughly half of production was hedged entering the quarter, so hedge losses could claw back much of the upside.”

surprises.description: The preview did not mention the shelf divestment’s abandonment-liability benefit. Talos reported that the sale removed approximately $54 million of future abandonment obligations while improving the portfolio’s oil weighting.
surprises.fact_evidence: The noncore gas-weighted shelf divestment eliminated approximately $54 million of future abandonment obligations and improved portfolio oil weighting.

surprises.description: The preview did not flag a refinancing. Talos issued $800 million of 8% notes to redeem $625 million of 9% notes, lowering the coupon and extending maturities, though the fact set does not quantify the net interest or debt impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company issued $800 million of 8% senior notes due 2034 to redeem $625 million of 9% notes due 2029, lowering the coupon and extending maturities.

surprises.description: The preview left the post-acquisition buyback pace open and included a capital-return announcement in its bull scenario. Instead, Talos repurchased no shares in Q2 because of an acquisition-related blackout, although it reported $135 million of shareholder returns since Q2 2025 and a roughly 7% share-count reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: Talos returned approximately $135 million to shareholders since Q2 2025, reducing share count by about 7%, but repurchased no shares in Q2 2026 due to an acquisition-related blackout.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With $450–500M going to Shell, the buyback pace after Q1’s $38.2M is an open question”; the bull scenario included “capital return announced.”

surprises.description: Talos disclosed a substantial Honduras position and a first-ever 3D seismic program that the preview did not mention. This adds a new exploration initiative, though the facts provided do not establish its commercial outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Honduras position spans roughly 4 million acres (equivalent to 700 Gulf of America blocks) with a first-ever 3D seismic program starting in the second half of 2026.

in_line: Mexico’s Block 29 FID target remained 2027, consistent with the preview’s stated 2027 target.
The borrowing-base increase from $700 million to $850 million upon acquisition close was already described in the preview.

surprises.description: Voya reported adjusted operating EPS of $1.51, well below the preview’s $1.88–$1.99 consensus range. The call attributed about $0.90 per share of drag to below-expectation alternative investment performance and severance costs, although the alternative-investment loss had been pre-announced.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted operating earnings of $1.51 per diluted share ($140 million), which included an approximate $0.90 per share drag from below-expectation alternative investment performance and severance costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating EPS (Q2) … $1.88”; another estimate was “$1.99.”

surprises.description: Excess capital generation was about $150 million in Q2, below the preview’s expectation of roughly $200 million per quarter. Shareholder returns were still substantial, but the generation figure itself came in lower than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately $150 million of excess capital in Q2 ($350 million year-to-date).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Roughly $200M per quarter of excess capital.”

surprises.description: Stop-loss claims and reserves were somewhat better than the preview’s base case: Voya reported early 2026 claims running meaningfully better and released $8 million of reserves, whereas the base scenario anticipated no new release. However, reserves remained at the high end of the best-estimate range rather than being lowered.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Early 2026 claims experience running meaningfully better than 2024 and 2025”; Employee Benefits aggregate loss ratios “improved 5 points year-over-year to 74%”; Voya “released $8 million of stop-loss reserves while holding reserves at the high end of its best estimate range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “no new release”; the preview said to watch for “a second reserve release” and whether the 87% pick moved down.

surprises.description: Management gave a concrete recovery timeline for the unexpected severance costs: expense savings are expected to offset them by year-end, supporting meaningfully higher second-half earnings. The preview did not flag this payback timeline or earnings framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 severance costs [are expected] to be fully offset by expense savings by year-end (a six-month payback), supporting confidence in meaningfully higher second-half earnings.”

surprises.description: Voya disclosed that a legacy sub-advised relationship wind-down will pressure Investment Management flows in the second half. The preview did not identify this headwind, although the company said its 2026 revenue impact would be immaterial.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A legacy sub-advised relationship wind-down will pressure H2 flows with immaterial 2026 revenue impact.”

surprises.description: Management committed to at least $100 million of additional buybacks in Q3, a specific near-term repurchase plan the preview had not laid out.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Plans at least $100 million of additional buybacks in Q3.”

in_line: Alternative investment returns were a loss of about 2.5% annualized, consistent with the preview’s pre-announced expectation of roughly -2.5% annualized.
The 24% rate increase for the 2026 stop-loss block matched the preview’s stated 24% increase at 1/1/26.

surprises.description: PACS reported adjusted EPS of $0.63, above the preview’s $0.54 consensus estimate. The 17% beat was a substantial upside gap versus the expected quarterly result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose 34% to $0.63 from $0.47 a year earlier.”

surprises.description: PACS raised full-year adjusted EBITDAR guidance to $640–$660 million, while the preview cited prior adjusted EBITDA guidance of $605–$625 million and said another raise was possible. The higher guidance is favorable, though the preview and call describe the metric differently.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 … adjusted EBITDAR guidance by $35 million to $640-$660 million (implying ~29% adjusted EBITDA growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance ($605–625M). Does Q1 momentum support another raise?”

surprises.description: Quarterly revenue modestly exceeded the preview’s approximately $1.41 billion consensus, coming in at $1.43 billion. The beat was small, rather than a revenue miss or a result exactly at consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 9.1% year-over-year to $1.43 billion.”

surprises.description: PACS disclosed that it had acquired operations of 20 Eduro facilities, with another 14 expected to close later. That is a sizable acquisition update relative to the preview’s stated cadence of about five underperforming-facility acquisitions per quarter, although the call said the 20 facilities contribute only modestly to guidance and the other 14 are not included.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Acquired the operations of the first 20 of 34 Eduro Healthcare facilities in Texas on August 1, with only a modest contribution included in guidance and the remaining 14 facilities excluded pending third/fourth quarter closings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management targets about five underperforming-facility acquisitions per quarter.”

surprises.description: The portfolio has substantial occupancy upside beyond mature facilities: 100 ramping and six new facilities have lower occupancy than mature facilities. The preview flagged occupancy as a key metric but did not describe this specific embedded growth opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “100 ramping and 6 new facilities representing significant embedded organic upside, with mature facilities at 93.8% occupancy versus 87.7% for ramping and 78.7% for new.”

surprises.description: PACS raised full-year revenue guidance to $5.75–$5.85 billion. The midpoint of $5.80 billion is slightly above the preview’s $5.75 billion full-year revenue estimate, though the bottom of the new range is at that estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance by $100 million to $5.75-$5.85 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 revenue | $5.75B (StockAnalysis, July 8).”

surprises.description: The call identified potential Ohio quality incentive payments and another California WQIP supplemental payment that are not included in guidance. The preview did not flag these as possible additional sources of upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Potential upside not reflected in guidance includes anticipated Ohio quality incentive payments and at least one more California WQIP supplemental payment in 2026, neither of which has been accrued.”

in_line: Net leverage was 0.1x, matching the preview’s cited Q1 net leverage of 0.1x.

surprises.description: LP reported adjusted EPS of $0.40, well below the preview’s $0.58–$0.61 consensus range. The shortfall was roughly 31%–34% versus those estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LP reported adjusted EPS of $0.40.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS … Consensus $0.58 (Aug 3) or $0.61 (Jul 29).”

surprises.description: Q2 EBITDA was $79 million, versus the preview’s implied consolidated adjusted EBITDA expectation of about $98–100 million. That is roughly one-fifth below the preview’s expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EBITDA declined $63 million to $79 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consolidated Adj. EBITDA … Consensus ~$98–100M (implied).”

surprises.description: Management’s OSB outlook was much weaker than the preview’s Q2 setup suggested: Q3 OSB EBITDA is expected to be about negative $45 million, and the full-year figure about negative $120 million. LP also said prices had fallen roughly 6% since May, rather than the preview’s read-through that Q2 OSB could be at or better than its guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “OSB EBITDA is guided to approximately negative $45 million in Q3 and negative $120 million for the full year, with prices having fallen roughly $12 (6%) since the May call.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “OSB Adj. EBITDA | Company guidance (Q2) -$10M | Consensus -$14.9M”; “That read-across suggests LPX could land at or better than guide.”

surprises.description: Q2 sales of $664 million were below the preview’s $674–683 million consensus range, a shortfall of about 1.5%–2.8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales fell $90 million year-over-year to $664 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … Consensus $674M (Aug 3) or $683M (Jul 29).”

surprises.description: The preview expected Siding EBITDA near the top of its $115–120 million guide, but management said weather disruptions in Manitoba and equipment downtime at Dawson Creek kept actual EBITDA below what it otherwise would have been. The call did not give the actual Siding EBITDA figure, but management said it would have been at or above the top of guidance without those issues.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Absent unexpected weather-related disruptions in Manitoba and equipment downtime at Dawson Creek, Siding EBITDA would have been at or above the top end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Siding Adj. EBITDA … Company guidance (Q2) $115–120M … Consensus $119.5M”; “A low-end print is a de facto miss.”

surprises.description: LP cut full-year CapEx by $70 million, from the preview’s roughly $390 million plan to about $320 million. The lower spend supports cash preservation, but the reduction primarily comes from delaying OSB maintenance projects.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year CapEx guidance was cut by $70 million to about $320 million, primarily by delaying non-essential OSB maintenance projects.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 capex of ~$390M”; the preview listed “a capex trim” as something to watch.

surprises.description: LP disclosed that CFO Alan Haughie will retire on September 1, with Aaron Howald succeeding him—an unanticipated leadership transition in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Alan Haughie will retire September 1 after nearly 7 years, with Aaron Howald succeeding him as CFO.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed distributor changes involving Boise Cascade and a plan to secure new committed Siding partners by October 1. Management said there would be no coverage lapse, but the preview had not flagged this distribution transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Distributor changes involving Boise Cascade are not expected to cause any coverage lapse, with LP targeting new committed Siding distribution partners by October 1 at the latest.”

in_line: Siding’s 26% EBITDA margin matched the preview’s approximately 26% expectation.
Siding volume fell 11% year-over-year versus the preview’s 10% decline guidance—close to plan—while 7% higher prices helped lift Siding sales 4%.

surprises.description: Primoris’s Energy segment margin was slightly negative, well below the preview’s 2%–4% model and the 5% threshold it flagged as a catalyst. The pressure left consolidated gross margin at 4.9%, down from 12.3% a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin collapsed to 4.9% in Q2 from 12.3% a year earlier,” and renewables overruns pushed “Energy segment margins slightly negative versus 10.8% prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The preview's model puts Q2 Energy GM at 2–4%”; the catalyst checklist also says “Energy gross margin of 5% or more.”

surprises.description: Full-year free cash flow was cut by about $200 million rather than held, as the preview’s catalyst checklist expected. The new $150–$200 million range is well below the prior $350–$400 million forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow guidance was cut by roughly $200 million due to the renewables projects, now expected at $150-$200 million for the year versus a prior forecast of $350-$400 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The catalyst checklist called for “Operating cash flow positive and FY free cash flow held.”

surprises.description: The renewables-project closeout is progressing more slowly than the preview’s timeline implied: two projects are complete, three are now expected to reach substantial completion in Q3, and the last is not expected to reach substantial completion until year-end. The preview had highlighted three projects completing within a month and treated confirmation that all six were done or fully reserved as the key event.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Six renewables projects drove the margin pressure, with two now complete, three expected to reach substantial completion in Q3, and the final project targeted for mechanical completion in early November and substantial completion by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said three of six problem projects would complete ‘within the next month,’ one in Q3, and one in Q4 2026”; the preview called confirmation that “all six are done or fully reserved” the most important disclosure.

surprises.description: The projected Energy-margin recovery is slower than the preview’s outlook: management now guides to 6%–8% in Q3 and 8%–10% in Q4, with a return to the normal 10%–12% range only in 2027. The preview expected Q3 to gravitate back toward normal and Q4 to reach 10%–12%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 Energy segment gross margins are guided to 6%-8%, with sequential improvement to 6%-8% in Q3 and 8%-10% in Q4, before returning to the normal 10%-12% range in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says the CFO described Q3 as “gravitating back toward normal” and Q4 as “reaching the 10–12% target.”

surprises.description: Backlog and awards came in stronger than the preview’s bar: backlog reached nearly $13.9 billion versus the preview’s $12.5 billion catalyst threshold, and Energy awards were $2.4 billion versus about $2.0 billion flagged ahead of the release. Management also cited $2 billion of renewables backlog and another $1.5–$2 billion of bookings expected mostly in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record total backlog of nearly $13.9 billion, up ~$2.2 billion sequentially,” on “more than $3.9 billion in new awards including $2.4 billion in Energy and $1.5 billion in Utilities”; renewables backlog stood at “$2 billion with $1.5-$2 billion of additional bookings expected mostly in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist looked for “Backlog above $12.5B with the $2.0B Q2 Energy awards booked.”

surprises.description: Natural-gas power generation emerged as a sizable booking and growth driver that the preview did not specifically anticipate: about $1.4 billion of new bookings supports expected revenue growth from $500–$600 million in 2026 to $800 million–$1 billion in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Natural gas power generation contributed approximately $1.4 billion of new bookings (all simple cycle in Texas, Missouri and Nevada), supporting expected revenue growth from $500-$600 million in 2026 to $800 million-$1 billion in 2027.”

surprises.description: Pain Crest was contributing more than the preview had led investors to expect: management said the acquisition was exceeding expectations and cited both acquired backlog and new quarterly bookings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Pain Crest acquisition is exceeding expectations, adding ~$200 million of acquired backlog plus $250 million of new bookings in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management said the acquisition was “exceeding expectations.”
