surprises.description: Revenue was slightly below the preview’s consensus estimate: just under $1.7 billion versus $1.734 billion. Its year-over-year decline was also steeper than the preview’s expected 7.7% decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was just under $1.7 billion, down 10.7% (~$200 million) year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The consensus table lists Q2 revenue of “$1.734B” and a year-over-year change of “-7.7%.”

surprises.description: Net debt-to-EBITDA is now 1.6x and is expected to rise toward just under 2x in Q3 before improving. The preview highlighted liquidity and cash-flow concerns but did not flag this leverage level or near-term increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt-to-EBITDA rose to 1.6x following the Pain Crest acquisition and lower Q2 EBITDA, expected to tick up toward just under 2x in Q3 before declining to ~1.5x by year-end and ~1x during 2027.”

in_line: Primoris maintained FY2026 guidance for EPS of $1.30–$1.85, adjusted EPS of $2.05–$2.60, and adjusted EBITDA of $275–$325 million, as the preview expected reaffirmation of the post-cut guidance.

surprises.description: The preview cited Hatch’s roughly $8 billion NPV case. Ramaco reported Brook Mine modeled NPV of $3.4 billion to $8 billion and average adjusted EBITDA of $600 million to $1.3 billion, substantially above FLUR’s 2025 studies; however, the project timeline was pushed out and capital costs increased. The reported economics are strong but the schedule and cost outlook worsened.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Brook Mine project modeling shows a potential NPV of $3.4 billion to $8 billion and average adjusted EBITDA of $600 million to $1.3 billion, up substantially from FLUR's 2025 studies, though timeline and capital costs were pushed out and increased.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base case (1.3 MTPA): installed capex of $2,585M”; “Expanded case (2.6 MTPA): capex of ~$3.2B plus ~$800M contingency, about $4.0B total. Pre-tax NPV is ~$8B.”

surprises.description: The preview put FY26 production at 3.7–4.1 million tons and sales at 4.1–4.5 million tons. Ramaco cut both ranges, to 3.6–3.9 million tons of production and 4.0–4.3 million tons of sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 production guidance was cut to 3.6-3.9 million tons and sales guidance to 4.0-4.3 million tons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Production: 3.7–4.1Mt”; “Sales: 4.1–4.5Mt.”

surprises.description: The preview’s base scenario assumed a $12-per-ton cash margin and warned that below $10 would put the coal business near cash breakeven. Ramaco reported a $17-per-ton margin, above that base case, as realized prices were $116 per ton rather than falling from Q1’s $114; costs were $99 per ton, only slightly above Q1’s $98.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 cash margins fell to $17 per ton from $20 per ton a year ago, driven by realized prices dropping 6% to $116 per ton, while cash cost per ton held at $99.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base ... Cash margin ... ~$12/t”; “Cash margin per ton ... It was $16/t in Q1 with costs guided higher and realizations guided lower”; “A print below ~$10/t would mean the coal business is at or near breakeven on a cash basis.”

surprises.description: Class A EPS was expected to be a $0.23 loss, but the reported loss was $0.26 per share, a modestly larger loss than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA fell to $6 million from $9 million a year earlier, with a Class A EPS loss of $0.26 versus a $0.29 loss in Q2 2025.”

surprises.description: The preview used approximately $90 million of FY26 capex as its reference point and identified a possible increase as a key issue. Ramaco raised capex guidance to $92–97 million, citing funding for the Maven low-vol expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Capex guidance rose to $92-97 million to fund the Maven low-vol expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capex: ~$90M”; “Revised capex guidance. The ~$90M FY26 figure predates the 2Mt→5Mt authorization. How much it rises, and how it is funded, is the central question.”

surprises.description: The preview noted prior repurchases of 2.6 million shares for $37 million and asked whether buying would continue at lower prices. Ramaco reported repurchasing almost 5 million shares—more than 8% of its Class A shares—for about $66 million in Q2, reducing shares outstanding to fewer than 52 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased more than 8% of its Class A shares (almost 5 million shares) for about $66 million, reducing shares outstanding to less than 52 million, with remaining authorization from a $100 million board approval.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “It authorized $100M in December 2025 and repurchased 2.6M shares for $37M at an average of ~$14.50, leaving ~$63M. Whether buying continued at lower prices is a read on management's confidence.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that roughly 75% of Brook Mine’s projected revenue is now expected from non-rare-earth critical minerals tied mainly to semiconductor demand, rather than relying primarily on scandium. The preview discussed Hatch’s project economics and financing but did not flag this change in revenue mix or demand driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly 75% of the Brook Mine's projected revenue is now tied to non-rare earth critical minerals (like gallium, germanium, silica) whose main demand driver is the semiconductor industry, reducing prior reliance on scandium.”

surprises.description: The call gave a concrete longer-term coal expansion plan beyond the preview’s near-term FY26 volume focus: total production targeted above 6 million tons versus about 4 million currently, with low-vol rising to 50% of the slate. Maven sections are expected to add about 600,000 tons, and its rail loadout is expected to reduce transport costs by about $20 per ton on that coal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's strategy targets growing total production to over 6 million tons (from ~4 million currently) with low vol rising to 50% of the slate, including new Maven sections adding ~600,000 tons and a Maven rail loadout cutting transport costs ~$20/ton on that coal.”

in_line: The preview expected cash costs at the higher end of the FY range because of fuel and geopolitical factors; the call said higher diesel prices added about $3 per ton to produced-coal costs and that Q3 costs were expected toward the high end of guidance.

surprises.description: The preview’s base case was $9.50–$9.80 of adjusted EPS, versus reported EPS of $9.93; that also exceeded the preview’s higher consensus estimate of $9.59 and its bull-case threshold of $9.90.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose 20% to $9.93,” exceeding company expectations.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: … Adj. EPS … $9.50–9.80”; “Bull … ≥$9.90”; consensus was “$9.46 … or $9.59.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $105.4 billion was above the preview’s $104.25 billion consensus and just above its $103–$105 billion base-case range, reversing the preview’s concern that revenue had missed repeatedly.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY27 revenue grew 8% to $105.4 billion,” exceeding company expectations.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (Q1) … $104.25B”; “Base: $103–105B”; the preview said McKesson had “repeatedly missed on revenue.”

surprises.description: The full-year EPS range rose by $0.40 at both ends, while the preview’s most likely base case was a reaffirmation or only a nudge upward. The new $44.20–$45.00 range is close to the preview’s bull-case range and puts the $44.28 consensus inside the guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “McKesson raised full-year FY27 adjusted EPS guidance to $44.20-$45.00 from the prior $43.80-$44.60.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … guide reaffirmed or nudged up”; “A raise to about $44.20–45.00 is the bull case”; consensus was “$44.28.”

surprises.description: Medical-Surgical profit fell to $195 million, well below the preview’s $244 million year-ago figure to beat. Rather than returning to growth after the prior quarter’s 5% decline, the segment’s profit dropped 20%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Medical-Surgical business … saw operating profit decline 20% to $195 million on product mix and one-time costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 FY26 operating profit was $244M, the figure to beat”; “A second decline would weigh on the separation narrative.”

surprises.description: The preview warned that Oncology and Multispecialty headline growth could be boosted by acquisitions and emphasized organic growth. Reported growth remained substantial excluding Core Ventures—about 24% in revenue and 15% in operating profit—so the result was not solely dependent on the headline growth rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oncology and Multispecialty revenue surged 33% … (about 24% excluding Core Ventures), with operating profit up 41% … (about 15% ex-Core Ventures).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch the organic versus acquired split, not just the headline”; “Headline growth boosted by M&A will be discounted.”

surprises.description: Management said some Q1 earnings tailwinds arrived earlier than expected and would come at the expense of later quarters. That makes the strong quarter less evenly distributed through the year than the preview’s modest-beat base case implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 benefited from earlier-than-expected generics favorability and new product launch timing that will come at the expense of later quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: … Modest EPS beat”; the preview did not anticipate these benefits being pulled forward from later quarters.

surprises.description: Management flagged accelerated second-half spending on growth and AI, with returns not expected to begin until 2028. The preview did not identify this added near-term investment burden.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Accelerated second-half investments in growth and AI expected to yield returns starting in 2028.”

surprises.description: The board approved a 15% dividend increase, an additional shareholder return action not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of free cash flow and buybacks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board approved a 15% dividend increase marking the tenth consecutive annual raise.”

in_line: The preview said Q1 is seasonally the weakest free-cash-flow quarter and that a negative print was not necessarily concerning; free cash flow was negative $372 million, although better than roughly negative $1 billion a year earlier.

surprises.description: Total revenue was $40 million, slightly above the preview’s $39.62 million consensus. The preview described that estimate as a soft anchor, so this was a small beat rather than a major departure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose 4% to $40 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $39.62M”; the preview also calls $39.6M “a soft anchor.”

surprises.description: Core revenue grew 14%, stronger than the roughly 11–12% growth the preview said would be needed to meet the revenue consensus. The preview also flagged a print below about $36.5 million as a sign the H2 recovery was slipping; reported core revenue was $38 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core revenue grew 14% to $38 million, the highest quarterly growth rate in over two years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Hitting $39.62M would require core revenue to grow about 11–12% YoY”; “A print below about $36.5M suggests the H2 recovery is slipping.”

surprises.description: ARR reached $65 million, ahead of the preview’s approximate $62–63 million estimate and above its expectation that growth hold at least 9%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Annual recurring revenue (ARR) increased from $57 million to $65 million year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ARR ~$62–63M”; “ARR needs to hold growth of at least 9%.”

surprises.description: Bookings showed a stronger volume signal than the preview’s concern about a second decline: trailing 12-month units booked rose 40% to over 112,000. However, quarterly bookings were weighted toward lower-ARPU IoT solutions, tempering the quality of the volume growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month units booked accelerated 40% to over 112,000 units, though quarterly bookings of 48,000 were more weighted toward lower-ARPU IoT solutions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A second straight decline would undercut the H2 ramp”; the bull scenario called for “Bookings turn positive YoY.” The preview also flagged “Smart Operations ARPU drag.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA remained positive for a third consecutive quarter, but the $0.7 million result was below the preview’s estimated $1–2 million range. Thus, the positive streak continued while the quarter’s EBITDA amount fell short of the preview estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company posted its third consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA at $700,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$1–2M (est., no formal consensus)”; Q1 had been “a second consecutive positive quarter.”

surprises.description: Total gross margin rose to 41%, and professional services margin swung from deeply negative to positive. This was a stronger overall margin outcome than the preview’s margin-risk framing suggested, although the call facts do not give the hardware gross margin the preview specifically asked investors to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total gross margin expanded 760 basis points to 41%, with professional services margin swinging dramatically to positive 21% from negative 44% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A second quarter below 20% [hardware gross margin] would undermine the margin story”; the bear case cited “hardware GM below 19%.”

surprises.description: SaaS revenue grew 13%, exceeded 40% of total revenue, and its gross margin expanded to 75% from 70%. The preview did not specify expectations for SaaS growth, mix, or margin, so these are favorable reported details not anticipated there.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SaaS revenue grew 13% to $16 million and now represents more than 40% of total revenue, with SaaS gross margin expanding to 75% from 70%.”

surprises.description: Completed renewal renegotiations are expected to add about $50,000 per month by year-end, with escalation clauses supporting further increases later. The preview flagged repricing beyond the first three renewals as a watch item, but did not describe this level of completed progress or its expected revenue contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Completed renewal renegotiations are expected to add roughly $0.05 per unit per month (about $50,000 monthly) in incremental revenue by year-end, with built-in escalation clauses driving further gains in future years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch ... early renewal repricing (first three renewals at about a 33% uplift)”; catalyst checklist: “renewal repricing beyond the first three contracts.”

surprises.description: Management said second-half 2026 revenue, profitability, and cash flow will exceed the first half, a confident H2 outlook that goes beyond the preview’s emphasis on reaffirming targets and concern that the recovery might slip.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided that second-half 2026 revenue, profitability, and cash flow will exceed the first half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the base case assumed “reaffirmed FY targets” and warned that core revenue below about $36.5 million could mean “the H2 recovery is slipping.”

surprises.description: The installed IoT footprint was nearly 930,000 units, and management tied surpassing 1 million in the first half of next year to a growth and profitability inflection point. The preview did not flag this operating milestone or timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The installed IoT footprint grew 10% to nearly 930,000 units, with management expecting to surpass 1 million installed units in the first half of next year as a growth and profitability inflection point.”

surprises.description: Management described building a data and analytics practice, anchored by Databricks and Hexaware partnerships, to expand the addressable market and drive ARPU growth. The preview mentioned the Hexaware partnership as a catalyst, but not this broader practice or its stated growth ambitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[The company] is building a new data and analytics practice (anchored by Databricks and Hexaware partnerships) to expand its addressable market and drive ARPU growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed the “Hexaware partnership (announced Jul 6, 2026)” as a strategic item and said efficiencies would begin before year-end 2026.

surprises.description: The company bought back 1.5% of shares for $3 million and expanded its repurchase authorization to $25 million. The preview gave no expectation about repurchases or an expanded authorization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expanded its share repurchase authorization to $25 million after buying back 1.5% of shares for $3 million.”

surprises.description: Satellogic was expected to report roughly $9.33–$9.54 million of revenue, with even the preview’s bull scenario at $12.5–$14.5 million. Q2 revenue instead reached $15.9 million, up 259% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 259% year-over-year to $15.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $9.33M (Zacks) / $9.54M (Benzinga)” and the bull scenario forecast “Revenue $12.5–14.5M.”

surprises.description: The preview modeled an adjusted EBITDA loss of about $3.5–$4.5 million, but Satellogic reported positive adjusted EBITDA of $2.8 million and its first positive quarterly operating income. That is a substantial swing to profitability, alongside revenue growing much faster than operating expenses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “positive quarterly operating income (~$300,000) and positive adjusted EBITDA ($2.8 million)” and “operating expenses rose only 46%” while revenue grew 259%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~–$3.5M to –$4.5M (no formal consensus)” and the base scenario’s “EBITDA –$3.5 to –$4.5M.”

surprises.description: The preview’s catalyst checklist looked for Space Systems to be at or below 35% of revenue, favoring a more recurring-revenue-led beat. Instead, Space Systems supplied 55% of Q2 revenue, while Data and Analytics was 45%, so the reported mix leaned much more toward satellite deliveries than that checklist anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Space Systems contributed $8.8 million (55% of Q2 revenue)” and “Data and Analytics revenue reached $7.1 million (45% of Q2 revenue).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue at or above $9.33M, with Space Systems at or below 35% of the total”; the preview also cautioned that a beat driven by “one satellite transfer is lower quality than one driven by recurring subscriptions.”

surprises.description: The preview described full Merlin deployment in H1 2027, but the call put full service in H2 2027. The first satellite remains on track for its October 2026 launch, but the stated service timing is later than the preview’s deployment timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Merlin constellation's first satellite is fully integrated and on track for an October 2026 launch, with full service expected in the second half of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “full deployment H1 2027” and listed “Merlin October launch reaffirmed” as a catalyst.

surprises.description: The preview said the falling stock price could produce a large noncash fair-value gain in Q2. Instead, Satellogic reported a $19.7 million noncash fair-value charge, contributing to a $20 million GAAP net loss; the preview had warned that this accounting line could dominate GAAP results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss was $20 million for the quarter, primarily due to a $19.7 million noncash fair value charge tied to stock price movements.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The same effect could produce a large non-cash gain this quarter, since the stock fell roughly 40–45% between March 31 and June 30.”

surprises.description: The call reported a $12 million equity conversion that reduced secured convertible debt from $30 million to $18 million, an unflagged balance-sheet development. The debt reduction is favorable, though the conversion also involved equity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reduced secured convertible debt from $30 million to $18 million via a $12 million equity conversion.”

surprises.description: The preview noted the defense monitoring contract signed in May and its potential to lift RPO, but did not anticipate a full-scale conversion this quickly. The call said a defense pilot became a program worth more than $18 million in under six months, indicating faster pipeline conversion than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A key defense pilot converted into a full-scale program valued at over $18 million in under 6 months, signaling faster-than-expected pipeline conversion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “$18M+ defense monitoring contract signed in May should lift” RPO and described the bull case as “defense contract ramping.”

in_line: RPO was $80.7 million, in line with the preview’s $80 million-or-more watch level and its $75–$85 million base scenario range.
Cash ended at $112.8 million, above the preview’s $110 million catalyst threshold and well above its roughly $105 million financing-risk level.
The first Merlin satellite remained on track for an October 2026 launch, as the preview’s Merlin checklist expected.
Rick Dunn’s departure effective August 21 and Dustin Greer serving as Interim CFO absent a permanent successor were already described in the preview.

surprises.description: Talen said it now expects to exceed its previously announced approximately $2.6 billion of 2027 EBITDA, whereas the preview treated roughly $2.6 billion as the expected framing. The call did not quantify how far above that level it expects to finish.
surprises.fact_evidence: Talen “now expects to exceed its previously announced pro forma 2027 EBITDA of approximately $2.6 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said 2027 EBITDA framing was expected “versus the roughly $2.6B implied” by the Cornerstone multiple.

surprises.description: The preview cited a path of $36+ in 2027 and $41+ in 2028 free cash flow per share, while Talen’s new pre-buyback outlook is $34 and $40, respectively. However, Talen also forecast $48 per share in 2028 including buybacks, with potential to exceed $50, making the overall per-share outlook mixed rather than simply lower.
surprises.fact_evidence: Talen raised its outlook to “$34 (2027 base) and $40 (2028 base) before buybacks”; including buybacks it forecasts “2028 free cash flow of $48 per share,” with “potential to exceed $50 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had pointed to “$36+ for 2027 and $41+ for 2028.”

surprises.description: Talen’s commitment to return at least 70% of anticipated free cash flow matched the preview’s stated target, but the call put the amount at about $2.8 billion through 2028—well above the preview’s cited $1.9 billion repurchase authorization. The company also repurchased 550,000 shares in Q2, versus 300,000 in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: Talen plans to return “at least 70% of an anticipated ~$4 billion of free cash flow through 2028, or $2.8 billion,” via buybacks, and “repurchased 550,000 shares during the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Q1 repurchases [of] 300k shares for $100M against a $1.9B authorization through 2028” and a target of “about 70% of available FCF for repurchases.”

surprises.description: The PPL-zone discount to PJM West Hub was about $20/MWh, versus a historical level of roughly $9/MWh. That wider basis, attributed to transmission outages, is an adverse development relative to the historical reference point discussed on the call.
surprises.fact_evidence: The PPL zone’s power-price discount to PJM West Hub “widened from a historical ~$9/MWh to ~$20/MWh due to transmission outages.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call cited a “historical ~$9/MWh” discount as the reference level.

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $374 million, within the preview’s derived $340–$400 million range and its $350–$400 million base scenario.
The revised FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint is $2.125 billion, close to the preview’s roughly $2.1 billion implied midpoint and consistent with its “as advertised” scenario.
The 70% free-cash-flow return target was in line with the preview’s stated target of about 70% of available FCF.

surprises.description: Intrepid raised full-year production guidance for both potash and Trio, with potash moving above the prior 270–285,000-ton range. Management attributed the increases to sustainable recovery and throughput improvements, not to shifting production forward from 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year production guidance for both potash (to 290-300,000 tons) and Trio (to 295-305,000 tons), driven by sustainable mill recovery and throughput improvements rather than pulling tons forward from 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year potash production guide is 270–285k tons, tracking the upper end as of May.”

surprises.description: Trio’s cost performance was stronger than the preview’s expectation of costs near $230 per ton: the call described its cost of goods sold per ton as the lowest since Q4 2019. The call did not provide a directly comparable per-ton figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trio delivered its lowest cost of goods sold per ton since Q4 2019.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Trio cost per ton versus about $230”; the base scenario expected “Trio cost near $230.”

surprises.description: Q3 Trio pricing guidance was above the preview’s expected $390–$400 per ton range, with Intrepid guiding to $400–$410. Management also expected pricing to trend up on low-chloride and sulfate value.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for […] Trio sales of 30-40,000 tons at $400-410 per ton, with Trio pricing expected to trend up on low-chloride and sulfate value.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “H2 and Q3 pricing guidance versus $380–390 potash and $390–400 Trio.”

surprises.description: Q2 sales of $66.7 million exceeded the preview’s $62–$65 million base-case revenue range and the cited $64.9 million consensus estimate, though the preview cautioned that consensus was highly dispersed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 sales from continuing operations were roughly flat year-over-year at $66.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base | Revenue | $62–65M”; cited consensus estimates included “$58.9M” and “$64.9M,” with a warning that the figures were badly dispersed.

surprises.description: The call disclosed a $5 million accrual for the Pecos Water Rights matter, an unanticipated charge that was large relative to the $2.4 million of continuing-operations net income reported.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income from continuing operations improved to $2.4 million ($0.18 per diluted share), including a $5 million accrual related to the Pecos Water Rights matter.”

surprises.description: The preview focused on buyback execution and contemplated shares being retired in Q2, but Intrepid said buybacks were expected to begin in Q3 2026. The authorization was already $50 million before the release, so the surprise is the later start of actual repurchases rather than a new authorization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board expanded the share repurchase authorization to $50 million, with buybacks expected to begin in Q3 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Shares retired in Q2 and the average price paid show how management views intrinsic value”; the checklist also called for “Buyback dollars deployed.”

surprises.description: Full-year capex guidance moved down to approximately $40 million, below the midpoint of the prior $40–$50 million range. The reduction reflects the AMAX project deferral and lower costs for Wendover’s primary pond 8, so it preserves near-term cash but also includes a project delay.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance was reduced to approximately $40 million, reflecting deferral of the AMAX project and reduced costs for Wendover's primary pond 8.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capex guide is $40–50M, including Wendover Primary Pond 8.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash was higher than the preview’s roughly $170 million expectation: Intrepid ended with $185 million, no revolver borrowings, and $149.8 million of revolver availability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed the South Ranch sale for $68.9 million net, including $62 million of cash proceeds received in Q2, ending the quarter with $185 million cash, no revolver borrowings, and $149.8 million of revolver availability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash was $99.3M at March 31, plus $70M from the South Ranch sale that closed April 1, for about $170M.”

in_line: Q2 potash volume was 59,000 tons, within the 50–60,000-ton guide; its $391-per-ton realized price was just above the $380–$390 guide.
Q2 Trio volume was flat year over year, consistent with the prior-year 70,000 tons and within the 70–80,000-ton guide; the 6% price increase was broadly consistent with the $390–$400 guide.
Q3 potash pricing guidance of $380–$390 per ton matched the preview’s expected range.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue of $8.3 billion exceeded the $7.60 billion guidance ceiling and even the preview’s $7.9–$8.2 billion bull-case range. The result was a much larger beat than the preview’s base case of $7.6–$7.85 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 FY2026 revenue reached a record $8.3 billion” and “exceed[ed] the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Company guidance ... $7.30B – $7.60B”; “Bull ... $7.9B – $8.2B”; “Base ... $7.6B – $7.85B.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EPS of $2.28 materially topped the $1.70–$1.80 guidance range, the $1.76–$1.80 consensus estimates, and even the preview’s $2.00–$2.15 bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS hit a record $2.28” and “beat[] the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | Company guidance ... $1.70 – $1.80 | Consensus $1.76 ... or $1.80”; “Bull ... $2.00 – $2.15.”

surprises.description: Q1 FY2027 EPS guidance of $2.80–$2.90 was far above the preview’s roughly $1.90 implied run-rate and its $1.90–$2.10 scenario range. Management also indicated December could exceed seasonal norms, adding to the strength of the outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 guidance ... EPS of $2.80-2.90,” with management indicating “December could exceed seasonal norms.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The 12.2x forward multiple implies roughly $1.90 per quarter”; Q1 scenarios were “$1.90–$2.10” in the base case and “at or above $2.10” in the bull case.

surprises.description: The sales beat was less dependent on memory pricing than the preview’s memory-led base case suggested: memory accounted for about one-third of sequential and year-over-year growth, while all three Electronic Components regions grew double digits both sequentially and year-over-year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately one-third of both sequential and year-over-year sales growth came from memory pricing increases”; “all three regions [were] growing double digits both year-over-year and sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case described a “Beat led by memory and Asia pass-through,” and flagged memory pass-through as a concern for the quality of the revenue beat.

surprises.description: Adjusted operating margin reached 3.8%, up more than 70 basis points sequentially and expanding for a fourth straight quarter. That is stronger evidence of operating leverage than the preview’s focus on margin improvement from the prior quarter alone conveyed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin expanded to 3.8%, up over 70 basis points sequentially, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of margin expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “EC segment operating margin ... and SG&A as % of gross profit” as a key metric and said it would show “Evidence of operating leverage.”

surprises.description: Electronic Components margin rose to 4.1%, a two-year high, from the 3.5% cited for Q3. The breadth of regional growth also exceeded what the preview’s margin-and-operating-leverage watch item quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Electronic Components operating margin reached 4.1% (a two-year high)” and all three regions grew double digits both year-over-year and sequentially.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Electronic Components ... operating margin 3.5%” in Q3; the preview flagged “EC segment operating margin (3.5% in Q3)” as a key metric.

surprises.description: Farnell’s margin rose nearly 400 basis points to 9%, a three-year high—an improvement the preview did not specifically forecast, though it had cited the prior-quarter margin of 5.2%. The call also said Farnell remains on track for double-digit margins before the end of 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Farnell operating margin jumped nearly 400 basis points to 9%, a three-year high,” and it “remains on track to reach double-digit margins before the end of 2027.”

surprises.description: Working-capital metrics were stronger than the preview’s inventory and cash-flow concern suggested: inventory days fell to 71, while return on working capital reached 19%, above management’s near-term 16% target. This came despite a $600 million inventory increase, about half of which was attributed to memory pricing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory days improved to 71 (lowest in nearly four years) and return on working capital reached 19%, exceeding the near-term 16% target”; “about half the $600 million inventory increase was memory-related pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Free cash flow, inventory dollars, and leverage” and warned that “Component inflation may pressure cash flow.”

surprises.description: Management reported solidly above-1 book-to-bills across all regions, extending backlog and providing FY2027 visibility. The preview had treated backlog quality and the possibility of speculative ordering as unresolved risks, so this was a more constructive update, though the call facts do not explicitly rule out supply-driven ordering.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management said book-to-bills were “solidly above 1 across all regions,” extending backlog and providing visibility into FY2027; it characterized the cycle as roughly the “third or fourth inning.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Book-to-bill, backlog, and lead times” and asked how much backlog was “real demand versus supply-driven ordering”; it also identified speculative orders as a key risk.

surprises.description: Gross leverage improved to 3.2x from 3.6x, below the preview’s downside scenario threshold of 3.5x or higher, but remained above the 3.0x target. Management still targets approximately 3x by year-end rather than reporting that the target had already been reached.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross leverage improved to 3.2x from 3.6x,” with a target of “approximately 3x by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “3.0x leverage target” and described the bear case as leverage that “stays at or above 3.5x.”

surprises.description: Solventum raised FY2026 EPS guidance to $7.10–$7.20, well above the preview’s expected $6.65–$6.75 raise. The increase is partly less durable than the headline suggests: management attributed much of it to an approximately $100 million one-time tariff refund recognized in Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year EPS guidance was raised significantly to $7.10-$7.20 from the prior $6.40-$6.60 range, largely reflecting a one-time tariff refund of approximately $100 million recognized in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise to $6.60–$6.70 is needed to clear the bar.”

surprises.description: The preview’s adjusted-EPS benchmark was $1.91. Although the call said normalized EPS beat expectations, the stated $1.73 after excluding the ERP-order and tariff-refund benefits is below that preview benchmark; the $2.55 headline includes those benefits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 EPS was $2.55, but excluding a $0.34 advanced-order contribution and a $0.48 tariff refund benefit, normalized EPS was $1.73, which management said beat expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $1.91.”

surprises.description: Solventum raised FY organic sales growth guidance to 2.5%–3.0% from the previewed 2.0%–3.0% range. Management also said the high end reaches the low end of the 2028 long-range-plan targets.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Organic sales growth guidance was tightened upward to 2.5%-3% (or 3.5%-4% excluding SKU exits), with management noting the high end already reaches the low end of the 2028 long-range plan targets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 organic sales growth | +2.0% to +3.0% (company guide).”

surprises.description: Full-year operating-margin guidance rose to 22.2%–22.7% from 21.0%–21.5%. The increase is partly supported by the tariff refund, which contributes about 120 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year operating margin guidance was raised to 22.2%-22.7% from 21%-21.5%, though this includes about 120 basis points from the tariff refund benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior guidance was “21%-21.5%.”

surprises.description: Solventum announced it is advancing the separation of HIS and intends to become a pure-play MedTech company focused on MedSurg and Dental. The preview did not flag this strategic move; HIS itself grew 5.4% organically in the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company announced it is advancing the separation of its Health Information Systems (HIS) business—which grew 5.4% organically to $354 million in the quarter—to become a pure-play MedTech company focused on MedSurg and Dental.”

surprises.description: The buyback pace accelerated sharply: Solventum repurchased nearly 4 million shares for $288 million in Q2, compared with only $67 million executed in Q1. That is a substantially faster start toward the $1 billion authorization than the preview’s Q1 pace suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased nearly 4 million shares for $288 million in Q2 (4.8 million shares for $355 million year-to-date) as it accelerated its $1 billion buyback program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buyback pace against the $1B authorization (only $67M executed in Q1).”

surprises.description: Acera’s reported sales grew roughly 48% year over year to $32 million, with gross margins above 80%; management expects continued double-digit growth. The preview did not identify this acquisition’s performance as an expectation or debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Acera acquisition continued to outperform, growing roughly 48% year-over-year to $32 million in reported sales with gross margins above 80%, and management expects continued double-digit growth.”

surprises.description: The 3M separation had progressed to nearly 70% of transition-service agreements exited and roughly 950 of 1,200 systems migrated. The preview did not provide an expected separation-progress benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 3M separation is nearing completion with nearly 70% of ~200 transition service agreements exited (targeting 90% by year-end 2026) and roughly 950 of 1,200 systems migrated.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was $144 million, but management said it should improve meaningfully starting in Q4, leaving the cash recovery back-loaded. The preview highlighted the need for a strong second half after Q1’s negative $273 million, but the call facts do not state whether the approximately $200 million full-year expectation was maintained or changed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow of only $144 million in Q2 expected to improve meaningfully starting Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 was −$273M against a ~$200M full-year target, so H2 needs to be very large.”

in_line: Q2 sales were about $2.2 billion versus the preview’s $2.17 billion consensus, broadly within its $2.16–$2.20 billion base range. Organic growth of 9.5% was also close to the preview’s 9%–10% like-for-like estimate.

The ERP pull-forward was quantified at approximately $125 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation of more than $100 million and its estimate that roughly five percentage points of growth would come from the pull-forward.
The expected Q3 impact of the ERP-order reversal materialized: management forecast negative 3% to 4% sales growth, while the preview specifically highlighted that the reversal would weaken Q3.

surprises.description: Revenue was expected to be about $509.6 million, or 10.7% year-over-year growth, but OUTFRONT reported 14% growth. That is roughly a 3-point growth-rate beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenues rose 14% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year AFFO growth outlook to the low 20s, above the preview’s mid-teens growth guide and roughly $385–392 million expectation. The preview had identified a raise toward about $400 million as a key catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 AFFO guidance to low-20s percent growth over 2025's reported AFFO of $338 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 AFFO: ~$385–392M (mid-teens growth guide)” and “FY26 AFFO guide raised toward about $400M.”

surprises.description: Transit grew 32%, slightly above the roughly 30% guide, and the reported operating improvement was substantial: transit adjusted OIBDA rose about $26 million to $33 million, with MTA revenue up 48%. This provided stronger evidence of above-MAG dollars flowing through than the preview had quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Transit growth was led by New York MTA revenue surging 48% during the quarter, while transit adjusted OIBDA improved by about $26 million to $33 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 transit growth was guided to about +30%” and “Watch whether above-MAG dollars flow through to cash.”

surprises.description: The World Cup was quantified at more than $35 million of Q2 revenue, with roughly half incremental to normal business, and management indicated a further $16 million benefit in Q3. This addressed the preview’s open question about the event’s contribution and whether it would extend beyond Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FIFA World Cup generated over $35 million of revenue in Q2 (over $50 million overall), with roughly half considered incremental to normal business”; Q3 guidance includes “a $16 million World Cup benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management deferred numbers on this in Q1 and said it would give a fuller explanation in August”; the preview asked whether World Cup revenue was “extending into Q3.”

surprises.description: Billboard growth on the stated adjusted basis was 9.4% excluding the exited low-margin LA contract, above the preview’s expectation of clean growth around 5%. Digital billboard revenue also grew more than 21%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding the exited low-margin LA billboard contract, billboard revenue would have grown 9.4% and digital billboard revenue over 21%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Clean billboard organic growth of at least +5%, excluding condemnation.”

surprises.description: The broader digital business grew more than 23% and reached about 37% of revenue, while programmatic and automated sales rose nearly 50%. The preview did not identify these digital mix and sales-channel results as an expected driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Combined digital revenue grew over 23% and represented about 37% of total revenues (up from 34%), with programmatic and automated sales up nearly 50% to 20% of digital revenue.”

surprises.description: Consolidated OIBDA grew 29% while revenue grew 14%, indicating stronger operating profit growth than the revenue result alone; the preview said no adjusted OIBDA consensus was available and did not forecast this outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated OIBDA [was] up 29% to $160 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted OIBDA consensus was not found.”

surprises.description: Management said SG&A growth would outpace revenue growth for the rest of 2026 as it accelerates investment in programmatic sales and data capabilities. That signals a near-term expense headwind not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A growth is expected to outpace revenue growth for the rest of 2026 due to accelerated investments in programmatic sales, data analytics, and a newly hired Chief Data Officer, aiming to boost 2027 revenue.”

surprises.description: The quarterly dividend rose 10% to $0.33, exceeding the preview’s cited $0.30 level and its potential catalyst of a dividend above $0.30.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board raised the quarterly dividend 10% to $0.33 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Dividend: $0.30 per quarter” and “A dividend above $0.30” was listed as a capital-allocation catalyst.

surprises.description: Net leverage was about 4.0x, below the prior 4.3x level and at the bottom of the company’s 4–5x target range, meeting the preview’s potential below-4.3x leverage catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage stood at about 4x (bottom of the 4-5x target).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net leverage was 4.3x, inside the 4–5x target” and “leverage below 4.3x” was listed as a capital-allocation catalyst.

surprises.description: OUTFRONT refinanced $650 million of 5% notes due 2027 with $500 million of 6% notes due 2034. The transaction extends maturities but carries a higher stated coupon, and the preview did not anticipate or discuss a refinancing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company refinanced $650 million of 5% 2027 notes with $500 million of 6% notes due 2034.”

in_line: Billboard yield remained above the preview’s Q1 reference level: it reached $3,344 per month per display, versus the preview’s note that Q1 yield was over $2,900.

surprises.description: Q2 GAAP EPS was $2.81, above the $2.67 consensus, but below the preview’s roughly $3.05 guidance-implied level. The $30.5 million pretax refinancing charge, which reduced EPS by $1, was a major offset to the reported result and was not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 GAAP net income was $64 million, or $2.81 per share … including a $30.5 million pretax refinancing charge that reduced EPS by $1 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS: $2.67” and “EPS vs. $2.67 consensus and the ~$3.05 guidance-implied level.”

surprises.description: Management raised full-year EPS guidance from $13 to a $13–$14 range, reaching the preview’s bullish $13.50-plus threshold rather than merely reaffirming or modestly nudging the prior guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 EPS guidance to $13-$14 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise to $13.50+ would be bullish; a reaffirm at $13.00 reads as neutral to soft.”

surprises.description: U.S. portfolio purchases reached a record $372 million, above the preview’s $340 million bull-case marker, with 84% of global purchasing dollars going to the U.S. This is stronger than simply tracking toward the high end of the annual purchase range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A record $372 million in the U.S., representing 84% of purchasing dollars amid favorable U.S. market conditions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “US purchases at/above $340M” in the bull scenario; the preview also asked whether the company was “tracking to the high end of the $1.4–1.5B FY range.”

surprises.description: The recovery changes were predominantly cash-driven: $53 million came from collections above forecast, while $18 million reflected higher future recovery expectations. That is reassuring relative to the preview’s concern that mark-ups could account for more than half of the beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Changes in recoveries totaled $71 million, including $53 million of collections above forecast (incremental cash) and $18 million in raised future recovery expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If mark-ups drive more than half the beat, the move may fade.”

surprises.description: The company refinanced $1 billion of debt and expects about $15 million in annualized interest savings. The preview focused on funding the pending convertible-note redemption and interest expense, but did not anticipate this refinancing or its stated savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company refinanced $1 billion of debt … expecting roughly $15 million in annualized interest savings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management should address funding and leverage” for the convertible-note redemption; the preview also noted the roughly $300 million FY interest-expense guide.

surprises.description: Full-year collections guidance was raised to $2.8–$2.85 billion, modestly above the preview’s expected approximately $2.8 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 collections guidance was raised to $2.8-$2.85 billion, reflecting operational overperformance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Collections ~$2.8B (+8%), raised from $2.7B.”

in_line: Global collections were $737 million, up 13% year over year: this matched the preview’s +13% base-case growth assumption and exceeded its $700 million trajectory marker.
Cash efficiency margin was 60.2%, above the full-year guide of more than 58% and broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation that it would remain around 60%.
Leverage was 2.3x, unchanged from Q1 and within the preview’s cited 2.0x–3.0x target range.
Trailing 12-month ROIC was 14.7%, essentially in line with the 14.6% level reported in the preview for Q1.

surprises.description: Schrödinger raised its 2026 drug discovery revenue guidance to $65–75 million from $55–65 million after a $10 million Ajax milestone helped lift Q2 drug discovery revenue to $23 million. The preview described the revenue as lumpy and milestone-driven, but its base case expected the existing guide to hold rather than a $10 million upward reset.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Drug discovery revenue rose to $23 million from $13.9 million, boosted by a $10 million Ajax milestone,” and management raised full-year guidance “to $65-75 million from $55-65 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 drug discovery revenue guidance of “$55M – $65M” and said the base scenario was “Guide held as is”; it described drug discovery revenue as “lumpy and milestone-driven.”

surprises.description: Software gross margin was 71%, above the preview’s 68–69% level to watch for a transitional hosted-license drag. It still fell from 76% a year earlier, but the result was better than that anticipated benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Software gross margin declined to 71% from 76% in Q2 2025, reflecting the planned accelerated transition to hosted licensing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Gross margin holding at 68–69% or better suggests the drag is transitional.”

surprises.description: Hosted software reached 47% of software revenue, with some customers converted ahead of renewal and thus boosting the quarter’s mix. The preview expected hosted licensing to distort reported software revenue but did not give an expectation of this degree of penetration or mention conversions pulled forward.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hosted revenue jumped to 47% of software revenue ($15.2 million of $32.5 million) versus 31% in Q2 2025,” and “some customers were converted ahead of renewal, inflating the quarter's figure.” Management also warned that “each 1% increase in hosted revenue reduces reported revenue by $2-3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Hosted mix and software gross margin” and said reported software revenue was “distorted by the shift to hosted licenses,” but gave no expected hosted mix level.

surprises.description: The BMS expansion was described as monetizing through increased throughput-based platform usage, providing some concrete economic context where the preview said the terms were undisclosed and questioned whether the expansion would have usage-linked economics. The call did not quantify the resulting contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “signed an expanded strategic software agreement with Bristol Myers Squibb, monetizing it through increased throughput-based platform usage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “financial terms [were] undisclosed” and asked whether the deal was “an ACV-accretive enterprise expansion or a co-development arrangement with deferred economics.”

in_line: Q2 ACV excluding contribution was $22.6 million, at the upper end of the preview’s $19–23 million guide.

Management reaffirmed full-year ACV guidance of $218–228 million, as the preview’s base case expected the guide to hold. The preview also anticipated a heavily Q4-weighted back half; the call said Q4 typically accounts for over 50% of annual ACV.

The Ajax-related gain and positive net income were consistent with the preview’s warning that an Ajax gain could produce a large GAAP earnings beat. The call reported $6 million net income, driven largely by $48.9 million of other income tied to Lilly’s Ajax acquisition.

Full-year operating expenses were expected to remain below 2025 levels, in line with the preview; the call said expenses fell 6% year over year and were expected to remain below 2025 for the full year.

surprises.description: Q2 CAFD was $167 million, below the preview’s roughly $190 million estimate and just below its $170 million threshold for a strained full-year guide. The shortfall came as weak wind continued to weigh on results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $409 million and CAFD was $167 million”; 2026 guidance was lowered “driven entirely by weak wind resource” in the first half.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 CAFD vs. ~$190M”; “Below about $170M, the full-year guide looks strained.”

surprises.description: Clearway cut its 2026 CAFD guidance to $430–470 million from $470–510 million, rather than reaffirming the prior range as the preview’s base scenario expected. The preview did flag a possible cut if wind remained weak, and management attributed the reduction to first-half wind conditions tied to the El Niño Southern Oscillation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Clearway lowered its 2026 CAFD guidance to $430-470 million from the prior $470-510 million range,” driven by weak first-half wind resource tied to “the El Niño Southern Oscillation weather pattern.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: … FY Guide Action: Reaffirmed $470–510M”; the preview also said “Trimmed or cut” in its bear scenario if there was a second wind shortfall.

surprises.description: The preview highlighted equity funding as a dilution risk, but management said it could delay equity issuance for the rest of 2026 and wait for the growth outlook to be reflected in the stock price. This eases the near-term timing risk, though the company still plans to raise $0.5–1 billion of external equity over 2026–2029.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management stated it has “flexibility to delay equity issuances for the remainder of 2026,” waiting for the growth outlook to be reflected in the stock price; the plan includes “$0.5-1 billion of external equity,” with $50 million raised.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Equity funding. Management said incremental capital above the $2.5B baseline is about 45% debt and 55% equity. Equity at this share price is costly.”

surprises.description: Clearway disclosed a digital-infrastructure pipeline far beyond the preview’s framing of two Texas PPAs expected by year-end: more than 17 GW of co-located generation is under development, with over 6 GW in the reported pipeline. Management also cited potential corporate capital upside of $400–500 million per gigawatt.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Clearway's digital infrastructure pipeline now exceeds 17 gigawatts of co-located generation under development, with over 6 GW incorporated into the reported pipeline and potential corporate capital upside of $400-500 million per gigawatt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Texas hyperscaler PPAs and data center capital. Two Texas PPAs are guided to close by year-end.”

surprises.description: The call reported completed restructurings on all three ERCOT wind projects, extending their contracts beyond 2040 and making them accretive from the first month of effectiveness. The preview anticipated Texas PPA developments, but did not flag these completed wind-contract restructurings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Completed long-term PPA restructurings on all three ERCOT wind projects (over 600 MW), extending contracts beyond 2040 and making them accretive to EBITDA and CAFD from the first month of effectiveness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Two Texas PPAs are guided to close by year-end.”

surprises.description: Management added a long-term commitment to bring the payout ratio below 70% and said it plans to roll its five-year growth targets forward to 2031 and formalize updated capital-allocation targets at the Q3 call. The preview focused on expected quarterly dividend continuity, not a lower long-term payout-ratio target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management targets rolling forward its 5-year growth targets into 2031 and formalizing updated capital allocation framework targets at the Q3 earnings call, while committing to lower its payout ratio below 70% long term.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Dividend. Expect about $0.475/qtr, versus $0.4676 declared in Q1.”

surprises.description: Management gave stronger detail on growth already secured for the 2030 plan: about 70% of the investment needed to reach its top-end target is commercialized, with over $2 billion of identified growth lined up for 2027–2029. The preview described the $3 billion deployment plan but did not provide this level of commercialization or project-vintage visibility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 70% of the growth investment needed to reach the top end of the 2030 target is already commercialized, with over $2 billion of identified growth lined up for the 2027-2029 completion vintages.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that Clearway had “raised 2026–29 capital deployment plan 20% to $3.0B,” but gave no expectation for how much growth was commercialized or identified.

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $409 million, within the preview’s estimated range of roughly $390–410 million.
The 2030 CAFD-per-share target remained at the top end or better of $3.10, consistent with the preview’s report that the outlook had been raised to the top end or better of $2.90–3.10.

surprises.description: Revenue was expected at $9.74–$9.77 billion, but MELI reported more than $10 billion, its first quarter above that level. That is roughly 2.5% above the consensus range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenue surpassed $10 billion for the first time, growing 50% year-on-year in Q2 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenues & financial income” consensus: “$9.74 – $9.77B”; implied y/y growth “+43.5 – 43.9%.”

surprises.description: Credit performance was stronger than the preview’s expectation that NIMAL would stabilize near 17–18%: NIMAL rose to 21%, while 15–90 day NPLs fell to 7.0% from the preview’s 8.0% reference. The call attributed the NIMAL improvement partly to recovering Brazil consumer spreads and normalized provisions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NIMAL improved from 18% in Q1 2026 to 21% in Q2 2026, driven by recovering Brazil consumer spreads as provisions normalized after a Q1 spike”; “15-90 day NPLs held at 7.0% total and 4.6% for credit cards, near historical lows.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether NIMAL stabilizes near 17–18% or breaks below 17%. 15–90 day NPL was 8.0%.”

surprises.description: Brazil commerce metrics came in above the preview’s warning threshold: overall items grew 56%, rather than decelerating below roughly 45%. Items per buyer and conversion also increased, supporting the share-gain case the preview said was at risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In Brazil, items per buyer grew 19% year-on-year and conversion rose 1.1 percentage points”; “items overall growing 56% versus 26% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Brazil GMV deceleration below about 45% items growth would weaken the share-gain argument.”

surprises.description: Adjusted free cash flow was positive despite substantial investment, better than the preview’s concern that continued negative quarters could raise external-capital questions. The preview did not give a Q2 FCF estimate, so the comparison is to that stated downside concern rather than a numerical forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted free cash flow was $214 million despite capital expenditure of $441 million and $2.1 billion invested into growing the credit book.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Two more negative quarters would raise the question of external capital.”

surprises.description: Brazil card issuance accelerated, but the card book’s NIMAL was negative at -2.5%, despite being near breakeven a year earlier. The preview discussed aggregate NIMAL and credit quality, but did not flag this card-specific profitability trade-off.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Credit card issuance in Brazil accelerated to 2.6 million cards this quarter versus 1.6 million a year ago, with card NIMAL at -2.5% (versus near breakeven a year ago) and each cohort reaching NIMAL breakeven in 12-18 months.”

surprises.description: The call highlighted the scale and economics of customers using both Marketplace and Mercado Pago, including 37% growth in these users and substantially higher activity and profitability. The preview tracked fintech MAU and unique active buyers but did not set an expectation for this cross-platform user group.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ecosystemic users (using both Marketplace and Mercado Pago) generate 70% more GMV, 90% more TPV and double the assets under management, growing 37% year-on-year, and are multiples more profitable.”

surprises.description: Advertising grew rapidly, with management pointing to AI tools as a contributor; the preview did not identify advertising growth or AI-enabled ad tools as a key expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The advertising business grew 73% year-on-year, aided by AI tools including an ad orchestrator whose usage grew 66%.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a sizable increase in AI investment alongside lower product-development spending as a share of revenue and fewer customer-service representatives despite business growth. These were not anticipated in the preview and point to a mixed combination of added AI spend and operating efficiency.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI investment rose roughly $80 million year-on-year, while product development scaled from 8.4% to 7.2% of revenues and customer service reps fell from 10,000 to 7,000 despite 3x business growth.”

in_line: Income from operations was $683 million at a 6.7% margin, within the preview’s derived consensus of about $650–700 million and 6.7–7.1% margin. The year-on-year margin decline of 550 basis points also matched the preview’s indicated 510–550 basis-point decline.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue implied by the reported segment figures was about $31.4 million, above the preview’s roughly $30.7 million consensus. ClearanceJobs was near its estimate, while Dice revenue was higher than expected despite declining year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: ClearanceJobs revenue was $15.6 million and Dice revenue was $15.8 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Total revenue consensus was ~$30.7M; ClearanceJobs consensus was ~$15.5M and Dice consensus was ~$15.5M.

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS of $0.09 exceeded the preview’s $0.05 consensus and even its $0.06–$0.08 base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Non-GAAP EPS rose to $0.09 from $0.07.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 EPS consensus of $0.05 and a base-case non-GAAP EPS range of $0.06–$0.08.

surprises.description: ClearanceJobs organic growth was stronger than the preview’s roughly flat estimate after excluding PSG. Reported bookings and new-business sales also showed unusually strong momentum, with the pipeline at a multi-year high.
surprises.fact_evidence: ClearanceJobs bookings rose 24% year over year, or 7% excluding PSG; new-business sales increased approximately 75%, and the pipeline reached its highest level in over 5 years.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated organic ClearanceJobs growth at roughly flat after stripping out PSG.

surprises.description: Management said Dice bookings are not expected to return to growth in 2026, a weaker outlook than the preview’s reference to management having promised a late-2026 inflection.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management does not anticipate Dice bookings returning to growth in 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a narrowing bookings decline would support the “late-2026 inflection management has promised.”

surprises.description: ClearanceJobs margin was 39%, below the 40% full-year guide highlighted in the preview, and down sharply from the prior-year quarter as PSG labor costs weighed on results.
surprises.fact_evidence: CJ margin compressed to 39% from 45%, partly due to PSG labor costs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged ClearanceJobs segment EBITDA margin against a 40% FY guide.

surprises.description: Dice’s weak renewal rate and the concentration of churn among smaller accounts add a retention concern beyond the expected customer-count decline. The preview expected customers to fall about 15%, but did not flag a 66% renewal rate or the concentration of churn in sub-$15,000 accounts.
surprises.fact_evidence: Dice retention was 98% with a 66% renewal rate due to churn among smaller customers; sub-$15,000 accounts represented 80% of customer-count churn.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged Dice customer counts, reporting the prior level as 3,832 and noting a 15% decline.

surprises.description: The call disclosed a sharp increase in technology postings and in the share requiring AI skills, a potentially favorable demand signal that the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: New technology job postings rose about 30% year over year in Q2, and roughly 75% of new postings required at least one AI-related skill, nearly double the approximately 38% a year earlier.

in_line: ClearanceJobs revenue of $15.6 million was close to the preview’s ~$15.5 million estimate.
Dice bookings declined 14%, within the preview’s 12%–15% base-case decline, although management’s outlook for no return to growth in 2026 was worse than the preview’s late-2026 inflection framing.
Full-year 2026 revenue guidance remained at $124–128 million, matching the preview; the stated $62–64 million contribution from each segment also matched expectations.
Adjusted EBITDA of $8.3 million was within the preview’s $8.0–$8.2 million estimate, and the 27% margin was within its expected 26%–27% range.
ClearanceJobs’ 87% renewal rate was close to the preview’s 88% expectation, and Dice customers fell 15%, matching the decline the preview highlighted.

surprises.description: Deluxe reported Q2 revenue of $499.3 million, above both preview consensus estimates of $486.3 million and $491.45 million. Its reported decline was also smaller than the expected 5.7% decline, while comparable adjusted revenue grew 2.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $499.3 million, down 4.2% on a reported basis but up 2.6% on a comparable adjusted basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $491.45M (Zacks); $486.3M (MarketBeat)” and “The −5.7% revenue decline is mostly the Safeguard divestiture… Underlying comparable-adjusted revenue should be roughly flat to modestly positive.”

surprises.description: Print held up better than the preview’s concern about a 4%–6% core decline: legacy Checks fell only 1.7%. Margins did more than merely hold above 32%, expanding about 110 basis points to the mid-30s.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Print segment revenue declined 4.3% to $235.9 million but EBITDA margins expanded to the mid-30s (up ~110 bps) as legacy Checks fell only 1.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether the core decline stays inside 4% to 6% and whether the 32%+ Print EBITDA margin holds.”

surprises.description: Data Solutions remained a fast-growing business in the quarter, with 21.4% growth and a seventh consecutive quarter above 15%, despite the preview’s focus on moderation against a tough comparison. Management still expects moderation later, as anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Data Solutions segment grew revenue 21.4% to $82.3 million, marking its seventh consecutive quarter of 15%+ growth, though management guides to moderation against tough Q3 and Q4 comps of 46% and 31%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 grew 26.3% against a tough 18.1% comparison in Q2 2025. Management guided full-year mid-to-high single-digit growth and flagged moderation in later quarters. The question is magnitude.”

surprises.description: First-half free cash flow reached $85.9 million, a 65% increase, giving Deluxe a stronger start toward its roughly $200 million full-year target than the preview’s concern about the target’s heavy second-half weighting suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date free cash flow grew nearly 65% to $85.9 million, a $33.8 million improvement over the first half of 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The roughly $200M FCF guide requires heavy second-half weighting from $27.3M in Q1.”

surprises.description: Merchant Services revenue growth slowed to 6.1% from the 7.3% Q1 pace the preview highlighted, though profitability remained strong: EBITDA rose 15.7% and margins expanded 190 basis points. That makes the growth slowdown a concern, but not a broad deterioration in segment performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Deluxe Merchant Services revenue grew 6.1% to $107.6 million with EBITDA up 15.7% and margins expanding 190 basis points to 23.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 grew 7.3% with 360bps of margin expansion. A slowdown would raise questions about why the company bought growth.”

surprises.description: The FY2026 adjusted EPS range stayed at $3.60–$4.00 despite Celero’s addition, rather than meeting the preview’s stated $3.70-or-higher catalyst expectation. Deluxe said Celero’s stub-period earnings roughly offset new interest and integration costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance was raised to revenue of $2.095–$2.120 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $455–$475 million, while adjusted EPS ($3.60–$4.00) and free cash flow (~$200 million) were held, as Celero's stub-period earnings roughly offset new interest and integration costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Catalyst Checklist: Revised FY2026 guidance including Celero: revenue about $2.07B to $2.14B, adj. EBITDA about $455M to $480M, EPS at least $3.70.”

in_line: FY2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance, including Celero, landed within the preview’s anticipated ranges.
The full-year free cash flow guide remained approximately $200 million, as expected.
Management indicated that Data Solutions growth would moderate against difficult Q3 and Q4 comparisons, consistent with the preview’s expectation of later-quarter moderation.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $49 million, far above the prior $34–39 million guidance range. The preview had no EBITDA consensus estimate, so the result exceeded even the top of company guidance by $10 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $49 million… well above the $34-39 million guidance range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA… Company guidance… $34M – $39M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.42 substantially beat the preview’s $0.33 consensus and its $0.32–$0.34 base scenario. That is a much stronger quarter than the preview’s expected in-band result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS of $0.42 (up 35% YoY).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $0.33”; base scenario: “$0.32 – $0.34.”

surprises.description: The company raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $168 million, above the previous $150–165 million range. The preview expected the guide to be reiterated or cut, not raised.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised 6% at the midpoint to $168 million (13% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026… adj. EBITDA $150M – $165M”; the preview’s key issue was whether guidance would be “reiterate[d], narrow[ed], or cut.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $233 million, above both the preview’s $230.7–231.2 million consensus range and the company’s $232 million guidance ceiling, rather than merely landing in the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue was $233 million… $1 million above the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $230.7M – $231.2M”; company guidance: “$227M – $232M.”

surprises.description: The Q2 net charge-off rate was 12%, better than the 12.2% guidance midpoint, and full-year guidance improved to 11.7% from 11.9% ±50 basis points. The preview had highlighted charge-offs as a key risk and expected the existing full-year range to frame the result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The annualized net charge-off rate improved 65 basis points sequentially to 12%, beating guidance… full-year revised down to 11.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Annualized NCO rate… 12.2% ±15bps”; FY2026 guidance: “FY NCO 11.9% ±50bps.”

surprises.description: Delinquencies fell to 4.0%, below the stated 4.1–4.2% expectation and at their lowest level since Q4 2021.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 30-plus day delinquency rate fell to 4.0%, below the 4.1-4.2% expectation and the lowest level since Q4 2021.”

surprises.description: Interest expense fell 30% year over year, and full-year guidance now calls for a decline of at least 15%, an improvement from the prior 10% decline guidance. The reported quarterly reduction included a roughly $7 million noncash change in interest expense recognition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Interest expense fell 30% year-over-year to $42 million, aided by a ~$7 million noncash change in interest expense recognition”; full-year interest expense is “now guided to decline at least 15% versus the prior 10% guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “cost of funds is running ahead of plan and could offset weakness,” and flagged interest expense and funding costs as a concern; it did not state a Q2 expense estimate.

surprises.description: The company reduced corporate debt by $30 million during the quarter while unrestricted cash rose year over year, and leverage improved to 6.5x with management expecting it to approach 6x by year-end. The preview did not flag this deleveraging or the resulting interest savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The debt-to-equity ratio improved to 6.5x… with management expecting to approach 6x by year-end”; “Unrestricted cash rose $43 million year-over-year to $140 million, while corporate debt was reduced by $30 million… generating $15 million in annualized run-rate interest savings.”

surprises.description: The company reported a seventh consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability, with GAAP EPS of $0.17. The preview focused on adjusted EPS and did not provide a quarterly GAAP EPS expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company delivered its seventh consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability with GAAP EPS of $0.17 (up 21% YoY).”

in_line: Full-year adjusted net income guidance of $74–82 million and adjusted EPS guidance of $1.50–1.65 were maintained, as the preview’s key issue anticipated possible cuts but also explicitly considered reiteration.
The preview expected management to reaffirm an H2 “11 handle” for net charge-offs; Q3 guidance of 11% is consistent with that expectation.

surprises.description: BD reported Q3 revenue of $5.0 billion, above the preview’s $4.89 billion consensus and even above its $4.96 billion bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 FY26 revenue was $5 billion, up 4.4% FX-neutral.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $4.89B”; bull scenario: “≥$4.96B.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $3.23, ahead of the preview’s $3.14 consensus. The result was also at the upper end of the preview’s base-case range, though within its functional whisper range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $3.23, up 4.9% year-over-year and ahead of expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | $3.14”; functional whisper: “~$3.20–$3.25.”

surprises.description: BD raised the FY26 EPS range’s low end to $12.62, lifting the midpoint to $12.67. The preview expected an upward narrowing, but its example range was $12.60–$12.72, so the reported low end was slightly higher than that scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Prompting a raise in the midpoint of full-year guidance to a range of $12.62 to $12.72.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Narrowing to $12.60–$12.72 would signal the ramp is on track”; the preview also described the base case as a “range narrowed upward.”

surprises.description: BD said FY27 would start with low-single-digit revenue growth and only modest EPS leverage, well below the Street’s roughly 7% EPS growth expectation. The preview’s FY27 Street EPS estimate was $13.48, versus $12.62 for FY26.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management characterized FY27 as low single-digit revenue growth with only modest EPS leverage as a starting assumption, versus Street expectations of around 7% EPS growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 Street EPS | $13.48”; “FY26 adj. EPS (Street) | $12.62.”

surprises.description: Q4 growth is expected to slow to roughly 2.5% from Q3’s 4.4%, rather than deliver the pronounced sequential step-up implied by the preview’s Q4 bridge. BD attributed the deceleration mainly to the tougher Alaris comparison, not underlying weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue growth is expected to decelerate to roughly 2.5% from 4.4% in Q3, driven almost entirely by the tougher Alaris capital comparison rather than underlying weakness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 consensus implies a Q4 step-up of roughly 31% sequentially, versus a normal ~11%.”

surprises.description: BD disclosed that net leverage was still about 2.9x, above its 2.5x long-term target and constraining balance-sheet flexibility. The preview discussed capital allocation but did not flag this leverage constraint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage ended at approximately 2.9x, still above the long-term target of 2.5x, constraining balance sheet flexibility.”

in_line: Adjusted operating margin was 24.9%, essentially in line with the preview’s approximately 25% expectation, despite a 130-basis-point year-over-year decline and tariff pressure.
The FY27 Alaris headwind was broadly as previously flagged: the preview noted it would rise from about 100 basis points in FY26 to about 200 basis points in FY27.

surprises.description: Q2 net sales and adjusted EBITDA exceeded the preview’s consensus estimates: sales were about 7% above $1.59 billion, and EBITDA about 17% above $734 million.
