The preview gave a wide EPS range, and the reported $3.52 was above the $3.35 Zacks estimate but below Scotiabank’s $4.01.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose 31% year-over-year to $1.7 billion, while adjusted EBITDA more than doubled (up 155%) to $858 million.” Diluted EPS was $3.52.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $1.59B”; “Adj. EBITDA (segment sum) | ~$734M”; “Adj. diluted EPS | $3.35 (Zacks); $3.09–$3.12 (other aggregators); $4.01 (Scotiabank…).”

surprises.description: Albemarle raised its full-year specialties outlook above the guidance in the preview, with the new sales and EBITDA ranges each $50–100 million higher at the endpoints. The increase was attributed to bromine price gains following Middle East supply disruptions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Albemarle raised its full-year specialties outlook to net sales of $1.4-1.6 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $275-325 million, driven by bromine price gains from Middle East supply disruptions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed prior guidance of “Specialties raised to $1.3–1.5B sales and $225–275M EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Full-year energy storage volume guidance was cut from the preview’s flat-volume baseline to a range that allows for a 4% decline. The Greenbushes CGP3 fire was the stated cause, with stronger Wodgina production only partly offsetting the impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 energy storage volumes were cut to 225,000-235,000 tons LCE (flat to down 4% year-over-year) due to the June 9 CGP3 fire at Greenbushes, partially offset by stronger Wodgina production.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FY volume flat” and said “A volume raise above flat FY guidance would be the cleanest bull signal.”

surprises.description: Management guided to sequential Q3 declines in sales, EBITDA, and margins in both segments, contrary to the preview’s expectation that Q3 would be seasonally stronger. Lower energy storage volumes, potentially lower prices, and costly spodumene inventory were cited as headwinds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided that Q3 sales, EBITDA and margins will decline sequentially in both segments,” citing lower energy storage volumes, potentially lower pricing, and “Q2 spodumene at ~$2,500/ton flowing through Q3 while current prices are ~$2,000/ton.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “management guided Q2 and Q3 seasonally stronger” and flagged the risk that recent spot-price declines could weigh on H2 realized prices.

surprises.description: Lithium demand and the physical market were stronger than forecast: demand growth was running above forecast and inventories were near record lows. Albemarle also raised its 2026 stationary-storage forecast and lifted the low end of its 2030 lithium-demand outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global lithium demand grew 45% year-over-year through May, running above forecast,” with carbonate inventories “under 3 weeks” and hydroxide “under a month.” The company raised its 2026 stationary-storage forecast 11% to 900–1,100 GWh and lifted the low end of its 2030 total lithium-demand outlook by 100,000 tons.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described spot lithium prices as “down about 15% in a month” and focused on the risk of lower H2 realized prices; it did not flag above-forecast demand or near-record-low inventories.

surprises.description: Despite the 2026 volume cut, management projected a return to high-single-digit energy storage volume growth in 2027, with CGP3 reaching full run rate by Q1. That was reassuring against the preview’s explicit concern about possible downside framing for 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects high-single-digit energy storage volume growth in 2027 as CGP3 ramps to full run rate by Q1 2027, targeting 240,000-260,000 tons LCE consistent with its 15% CAGR trajectory.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether management would “reintroduce downside framing for 2027.”

surprises.description: The call reported a notable DLE pilot result and a filed environmental permit for a potential multi-train project, developments the preview did not anticipate. The reported recovery rate was substantially above the conventional-pond rate cited on the call.
surprises.fact_evidence: The DLE pilot “has demonstrated over 90% lithium recovery (versus 30-40% for conventional ponds) and recycles ~85% of processed water,” and an environmental permit was filed for up to six trains, starting with one.

in_line: Q2 realized energy storage pricing stepped up from the preview’s Q1 reference of about $17/kg to about $20/kg LCE, while the three-month contract lag left realized pricing below market and was identified as a drag on H2 pricing—the preview had anticipated both the step-up and the lag-related risk.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $2.3 billion, about 4% above the preview’s $2.21 billion consensus; its 11% growth was also well above the roughly 5% growth implied by consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue rose 11% to $2.3 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $2.21B | $2.11B | +5%.”

surprises.description: Q4 segment EBITDA reached $423 million, substantially above the preview’s estimated $355–365 million range. The implied margin was about 18.4%, above the preview’s estimated 16.1–16.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total segment EBITDA surged 31% to $423 million”; the call also reported Q4 revenue of $2.3 billion.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total Segment EBITDA | ~$355–365M (my estimate, not a published consensus)” and “Segment EBITDA margin | ~16.1–16.5% (estimate).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.35, well above the preview’s $0.21 adjusted-EPS consensus; this is a comparison on the adjusted basis the preview identified as matching the company’s reporting.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rising to $0.35 from $0.19 a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “One vendor set shows Q4 adjusted EPS of $0.21” and “The $0.21 adjusted figure matches how the company reports.”

surprises.description: Digital-only subscription net adds were far above the preview’s bar for “notably higher” adds: about 194,000 versus the preview’s estimate that anything below about 60,000 would be a miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Digital-only subscriptions up 9% to nearly 6.3 million and the highest sequential net adds (~194,000) in over two years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Digital-only net adds vs. ‘notably higher’ than Q3’s ~53k” and “Adds below about 60k would read as a miss against its own guidance.”

surprises.description: The call reported that a Meta AI licensing deal was already contributing to Q4 results across Dow Jones and News Media, a current-quarter contribution the preview did not anticipate. The preview’s AI timing discussion instead said the Anthropic settlement share would affect revenue later in the calendar year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Meta AI licensing deal is now contributing to Q4 results across both Dow Jones and News Media, with more deals in the pipeline.”

surprises.description: Full-year revenue and EBITDA came in a little above the preview’s derived estimates: revenue was $9 billion versus about $8.90 billion, and EBITDA was over $1.6 billion versus an estimated $1.55–1.60 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year revenue grew 7% to $9 billion and total segment EBITDA rose 15% to over $1.6 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: ~$8.90B” and “Total Segment EBITDA: ~$1.55–1.60B” in the preview’s derived FY2026 estimates.

in_line: The preview expected strong Q4 free cash flow; the call reported full-year free cash flow of $811 million, up 42%, without providing a Q4 figure to compare with a numeric expectation.

The preview expected Dow Jones and Digital Real Estate to carry results and management had described FY2026 as on track for record profitability; the call reported strong growth in both segments and full-year EBITDA growth.

surprises.description: Envista raised its full-year outlook rather than reaffirming it: core growth is now 3.5%-4.5% versus prior guidance of 2%-4%, adjusted EBITDA growth is 11%-14% versus 7%-13%, and adjusted EPS is $1.50-$1.55 versus $1.35-$1.45. The EPS range is also above the preview’s $1.42-or-better buy-side threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to 3.5%-4.5% core growth, 11%-14% adjusted EBITDA growth, and adjusted EPS of $1.50-$1.55.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EPS: $1.35–$1.45”; “FY26 core sales growth: 2–4%”; “FY26 adj. EBITDA growth: 7–13%.” The preview also says “a reaffirm is the base case” and that the buy-side is looking for “$1.42 or better.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.41, well above the preview’s $0.34 consensus and at the top of its $0.39-$0.41 bull scenario. This was a substantially stronger quarter than the central estimate implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS up 58% to $0.41.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS” consensus: “$0.34”; bull scenario: “$0.39–0.41.”

surprises.description: Core sales growth was 5%, exceeding the preview’s implied 1%-3% consensus range and its 3.5%-4.5% base scenario. Revenue of $731 million was around the higher of the preview’s two revenue estimates, so the clearer beat was in core growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 core sales grew 5% on total revenue of $731 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Core sales growth: About 1–3% (implied)”; base scenario: “+3.5–4.5%.” The preview listed revenue consensus as “$716.1M (MarketBeat) / $730.2M (ChartMill aggregate).”

surprises.description: Free cash flow reached $105 million, above the preview’s bull-case threshold of $90 million and easing the concern that Q1’s cash outflow put the full-year conversion target at risk. The quarter’s cash flow included a $13 million tariff recovery, which qualifies the strength of the result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was $105 million (158% conversion), up $29 million year-over-year, aided by a $13 million IEEPA tariff recovery, with full-year conversion expected near 100%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Envista “needs a large H1 catch-up” after Q1 FCF of “-$15.7M,” and its bull scenario expected “FCF above $90M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded more than the preview’s implied roughly 110-basis-point improvement, reaching 14.7%; gross margin also expanded 70 basis points. The reported adjusted EBITDA margin was comfortably above the preview’s 13.5% threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 230 basis points to 14.7% and gross margin rose 70 basis points to 55.1%, driven by volume, price, productivity, and FX.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview implied an adjusted EBITDA margin of “about 13.5%” and said “13.5% or better” was needed.

surprises.description: China commentary was more constructive on the outlook for implants than the preview’s concern about continued double-digit declines and destocking: management projected a return to moderate growth and cited only 10%-15% price compression for implants, versus roughly 45% for ortho. However, VBP timing is now described as the second half rather than the preview’s Q3 expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China VBP is now expected in the second half, with roughly 45% price compression on ortho (VBP 1) but only 10%-15% on implants (VBP 2), and China is projected to return to moderate growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “China VBP 2.0 was postponed to Q3 2026, so destocking may have continued through Q2,” and identified “a still-double-digit China decline with no inflection” as a bear trigger.

surprises.description: Equipment & Consumables grew 8.5%, with high-single-digit growth in both consumables and diagnostics, and management attributed its outperformance of the estimated mid-single-digit market to share gains. That is a positive indication of segment durability, although the preview had already cautioned that repeating Q1’s 11.5% growth was unlikely.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Equipment & Consumables core sales grew 8.5% with high single-digit growth in both consumables and diagnostics, outpacing an estimated mid-single-digit market via share gains.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “E&C durability” and said “A repeat at [Q1’s 11.5%] level is unlikely.”

surprises.description: The full-year non-GAAP tax-rate outlook was lowered by about two percentage points, providing an additional boost to expected EPS growth beyond the operating improvement reflected in the preview’s estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered its full-year non-GAAP tax rate guidance to approximately 26%, about 2 points below initial guidance, aiding EPS growth.”

surprises.description: The implant F Series launch is running ahead of plan, with about a quarter of sales coming from competitive conversions. The preview did not identify this launch or conversion performance as an expected driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The implant F Series launch is running ahead of plan with about 25% of sales from competitive conversion.”

surprises.description: Brackets & Wires fell by a high-single-digit rate, a weakness not identified in the preview’s discussion of E&C durability or other key debates. Management said the comparison was against a strong prior-year tariff-driven period.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Brackets & Wires fell high single digits against a strong prior-year tariff-driven comp.”

in_line: The preview anticipated a Q4 billing-day headwind; management attributed flat-to-slightly-down Q4 core growth to four fewer selling days and put normalized second-half core growth at about 3.5%.
E&C growth moderated from Q1’s 11.5%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that repeating that level was unlikely.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $3.13 billion, roughly $130 million above the $3.00 billion consensus, with 13% year-over-year growth versus the preview’s expected 8.6%. Strong LMR demand and faster quick-turn conversion drove the outperformance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue grew 13% year-over-year to a record level, beating consensus by $130 million, driven by strong LMR demand and accelerated quick-turn conversion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Consensus … $3.00B” and “Implied Y/Y … +8.6%.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS reached $4.41, well above the $3.86 consensus. The $0.25 IEPA refund benefit contributed to the beat, but EPS was still $4.16 excluding that benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS reached $4.41 … including a $0.25 benefit from IEPA tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS … Consensus … $3.86.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY26 revenue guidance to approximately $12.975 billion and EPS guidance to $17.62–$17.72. That exceeded the preview’s expected revenue bar of at least $12.85 billion and EPS low end of at least $17.00, as well as its cited consensus estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year revenue guidance by $175 million to approximately $12.975 billion and lifted non-GAAP EPS guidance to $17.62-$17.72 from $16.87-$16.99.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The bar is a raise to at least $17.00 EPS at the low end and revenue of at least $12.85B.” The preview also cited FY26 consensus of “~$12.7B” revenue and “$16.48” EPS.

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 330 basis points to 32.9%; even excluding the IEPA refund benefit, expansion was 140 basis points. This was stronger than the preview’s concern that cost headwinds required a steep second-half margin ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 330 basis points to 32.9%, or 140 basis points excluding the $60 million IEPA refund benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The +100bps FY margin target now requires a steep H2 ramp. Investors need to see Q1 confirmed as the trough.”

surprises.description: Memory costs are now expected to reach $150 million, with most of the impact in the second half. That is higher than the preview’s expectation of more than $100 million and raises the anticipated cost burden.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Memory costs are now expected to reach $150 million this year … up $100 million from prior guidance, with most of the impact hitting the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Memory/DRAM spend more than doubles to over $100M in 2026.”

surprises.description: Tariffs were expected to be a roughly $60 million headwind, but IEPA refunds instead offset the planned tariff impact, leaving tariffs net neutral for the year. The company said gross margins would remain comparable to last year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tariffs are now expected to be net neutral for the full year as $60 million in IEPA refunds offset previously planned tariff headwinds, keeping gross margins comparable to last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Tariffs are a ~$60M headwind weighted to H1.”

surprises.description: Silvus’s full-year revenue outlook rose to roughly $850 million, $100 million above the preview’s $750 million target. The company also cited a new Salt Lake City facility that will add capacity in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Silvus generated about $230 million in Q2 (up from $210 million in Q1) and is now expected to deliver roughly $850 million in full-year revenue, with a new Salt Lake City facility adding capacity in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Silvus revenue target was raised to $750M for 2026.”

surprises.description: The company newly projected APX Next software subscribers reaching 300,000 by year-end 2026, representing nearly $100 million in ARR. The preview did not flag this subscriber or ARR milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APX Next software subscribers are expected to reach 300,000 by year-end 2026 (up from ~200,000 in 2025), representing nearly $100 million in ARR at roughly $300 per subscriber.”

in_line: The counter-drone acquisition remained broadly consistent with the preview’s expected transaction: the preview cited a $1.5 billion deal and about $185 million in expected revenue, while the call described a $1.5 billion agreement and roughly $185 million in revenue; a second-half closing is also consistent with the preview’s expected Q4 close.

surprises.description: FY26 adjusted EPS was $29.83, above the $28.16 Street estimate and the $27.70–$28.38 guidance range. The 12.7% increase came despite $120 million of additional interest and tax expense.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted diluted EPS rose 12.7% to $29.83 despite $120 million in additional interest and tax expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS” FY26 Street: “$28.16”; guidance: “$27.70 – $28.38.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EPS was $8.91 versus the preview’s derived consensus of about $7.24, and grew 6.1% rather than the roughly 14% decline implied by that consensus. The preview cautioned that the estimate was reconstructed, but the reported result still substantially exceeded it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EPS of $8.91 grew only 6.1% due to a much lower prior-year tax provision.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS” consensus: “~$7.24 (derived)”; the preview says this “implies about −14% YoY.”

surprises.description: Q4 EBITDA margin reached 13%, well above the preview’s roughly 11.5% expectation for a quarter management had warned would be softer than Q3. About 30 basis points of the reported margin came from a UK divestiture gain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EBITDA margin of 13%, up 150 basis points, though about 30 basis points came from a UK divestiture gain.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EBITDA margin” consensus: “~11.5%”; “Management pre-warned that Q4 would be softer than Q3, so a print in that range is expected.”

surprises.description: FY26 EBITDA margin was 12.3%, above the 11.8%–11.9% guidance range. This was a better full-year margin outcome than the preview’s cited guidance implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CACI delivered fiscal '26 … EBITDA margin of 12.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY26 “EBITDA margin” guidance: “11.8% – 11.9%.”

surprises.description: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance in the high 12% range points to improvement over FY26’s 11.8%–11.9% guidance, while the preview had identified the FY27 margin bridge as an important question but supplied no specific estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “For fiscal '27, CACI guided … EBITDA margins in the high 12% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FY27 EBITDA margin guide versus FY26's 11.8–11.9%” as a catalyst, without a specific FY27 estimate.

surprises.description: FY26 free cash flow was $735 million, modestly above the preview’s minimum guidance figure of $725 million. The reported increase in free cash flow per share was 68%, though the preview did not provide a per-share expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow of $735 million, reflecting a 68% increase in free cash flow per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY26 “Free cash flow”: “≥ $725M.”

surprises.description: FY27 free cash flow guidance is at least $900 million, with about 22% per-share growth, but the preview gave no numerical FY27 FCF bar. The guide also includes a delayed tax refund and a sizable cash benefit from R&D tax-credit changes, so part of the projected cash growth is tax-related.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow of at least $900 million (~22% per-share growth).”

surprises.description: The FY27 cash-flow outlook includes a $115 million benefit from Section 174 R&D tax-credit changes, larger than management had previously discussed because of the ARKA acquisition, plus a delayed $40 million tax refund. That makes the cash-flow outlook more dependent on these tax-related benefits than the preview indicated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal '27 free cash flow includes a delayed $40 million tax refund and a $115 million cash benefit from Section 174 R&D tax credit changes, which was larger than previously discussed due to the ARKA acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call says the Section 174 benefit “was larger than previously discussed due to the ARKA acquisition.”

surprises.description: CACI reduced pro forma leverage to 3.7x in one quarter and now expects to reach the low 3s by June 2027, a quarter earlier than originally communicated. The preview cited leverage of 4.2x after ARKA and a low-threes goal within six quarters.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reduced pro forma leverage to 3.7x, a full turn reduction in one quarter, and now expects to reach the low 3s by June 2027, a quarter earlier than originally communicated.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net debt/EBITDA at 4.2x after the ARKA deal”; management “targets 4.2x net debt/EBITDA returning to ‘low threes’ within six quarters.”

surprises.description: FY26 awards exceeded $10 billion and book-to-bill was 1.1x, above the preview’s flagged downside concern of a sub-1.0x result. Funded backlog growth was strong at 29%, although total backlog grew only 2%, versus the prior quarter’s reported 6% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Won more than $10 billion in awards in fiscal '26 (book-to-bill of 1.1x) … funded backlog grew 29% year-over-year while total backlog of over $32 billion grew only 2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a sub-1.0x Q4 book-to-bill would be a negative signal” and compared FY26 awards with “FY25's $10B.” It also reported prior-quarter backlog growth of “+6%” and funded backlog growth of “+19%.”

surprises.description: Bids under evaluation climbed from $4 billion to nearly $11 billion, with about 75% involving new business. The preview mentioned $22 billion of bids expected to be submitted over the next two quarters, but did not anticipate this increase in the already-evaluated pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bids under evaluation surged from $4 billion to nearly $11 billion (about 75% new business).”

surprises.description: Despite FY27 revenue guidance implying solid full-year growth, management expects first-quarter organic growth to be only in the low single digits. That is below the preview’s roughly 6%–7% FY27 organic-growth bar, although the preview did not specify a quarterly organic-growth estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal '27 revenue visibility comprises approximately 83% from existing programs, 9% from recompetes, and 8% from new business, with first-quarter organic growth expected to be only in the low single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Organic growth below about 6% would undercut the FY27 organic bar of roughly 6–7%.”

surprises.description: CACI disclosed a separate $500 million Domestic Shield counter-drone award, which the preview had not anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CACI received a separate $500 million Domestic Shield counter-drone award.”

surprises.description: CACI said it has export approval for the majority of its counter-UAS systems already delivered to 17 countries, an international-market development not covered in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Holds export approval for the majority of its counter-UAS systems already delivered to 17 countries.”

surprises.description: Fiscal '26 OTA award value exceeded the combined value of fiscal '24 and '25, a sharp acceleration in this award channel that the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Its OTA award value in fiscal '26 exceeded the combined value of fiscal '24 and '25.”

in_line: Q4 revenue was $2.7 billion, broadly in line with the preview’s approximately $2.69 billion consensus and within its $2.641–$2.741 billion guidance-implied range.
FY26 revenue was approximately $9.56 billion, broadly in line with the preview’s $9.55 billion Street estimate and $9.50–$9.60 billion guidance range.

FY27 revenue guidance of $10.65–$10.85 billion, with a $10.75 billion midpoint, was broadly in line with the $10.67 billion Street estimate, though it includes approximately $500 million of acquired revenue.

surprises.description: Avient delivered Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.96, $0.09 above the $0.89 consensus and company guide. The preview described $0.90–$0.91 as the expected result, so the print was stronger than its base expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EPS came in at $0.96, beating expectations by $0.09.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance ($0.89) equals consensus ($0.89)” and “a $0.90–0.91 print would be the expected result, not a positive surprise.”

surprises.description: Organic sales grew 4.3%, with volume up roughly 1% instead of the projected 1%–2% decline. That is a clear improvement over the preview’s expectation that organic growth could remain roughly flat or negative, although price still supplied about three quarters of the growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Organic sales grew 4.3% year-over-year, composed of roughly 25% volume and 75% price”; volume was “roughly +1% versus a projected -1% to -2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Organic growth could still be roughly flat or negative” and “Volume needs to be flat or better to support the FY bridge.”

surprises.description: Avient raised its full-year outlook rather than merely reaffirming it: adjusted EPS is now $3.10–$3.25 versus $2.93–$3.17, and adjusted EBITDA is $575M–$603M versus $555M–$585M. The new free-cash-flow range of $210M–$230M also puts a number above the prior >$200M target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance to adjusted EBITDA of $575M-$603M, adjusted EPS of $3.10-$3.25, and free cash flow of $210M-$230M.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26” guidance was “Adj. EPS $2.93–$3.17,” “Adj. EBITDA $555–585M,” and “Free cash flow >$200M”; the preview said “A reaffirmation is largely expected.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached a record 18.3%, up 110 basis points year over year, while the preview’s implied margin was about 18% and it highlighted raw-material and price-cost pressure. The margin result was modestly ahead of that implied level despite those flagged risks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin reached a record 18.3%, an expansion of 110 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (implied at ~18% margin)” and the preview flagged that “Pricing must stay ahead of raw-material costs.”

surprises.description: Specialty Engineered Materials posted 20% adjusted EBITDA growth and a 310-basis-point margin increase, a strong segment result not quantified in the preview. The margin comparison is partly flattered by lapping about $3M of prior-year maintenance expense, accounting for roughly 100 basis points of the increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Specialty Engineered Materials adjusted EBITDA rose 20% to $76 million with margins up 310 basis points, though about 100 bps came from lapping ~$3M of prior-year maintenance expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Organic growth in both segments expected in Q2”; the preview did not provide a segment EBITDA or margin expectation.

surprises.description: Asia was a particularly strong region, with organic sales up 18% year over year and 20% sequentially, led by electronics, high-performance computing, and functional additives. The preview did not identify this regional strength as an expected driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Asia was a standout with organic sales up 18% year-over-year and 20% sequentially, driven by electronics, high-performance computing, and functional additives.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a substantial data-center and electronics opportunity: about $2B is directly addressable, current related business is near $100M, and it expects that business to double over two to three years. The preview did not flag this opportunity or growth target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company estimates a directly addressable data center/electronics opportunity of roughly $2 billion, with current related business near $100 million (electronics ~$60M) and expectations to double over the next 2-3 years.”

surprises.description: Capex guidance was cut to $120M–$130M from $140M, a reduction not discussed in the preview. Management attributed the change to project timing, so the lower spend is not presented as a structural reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Capex guidance was lowered to $120M-$130M from $140M due to project timing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call described capex guidance as lowered “from $140M.”

surprises.description: Management gave a specific EMEA margin target not covered in the preview: margins are expected to rise by more than 400 basis points from 2023 and exceed 18% by 2026. This adds a favorable profitability target beyond the preview’s expectation of EMEA share gains in packaging.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EMEA adjusted EBITDA margins are expected to improve over 400 basis points from 2023 to reach above 18% by 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said packaging growth was “led by EMEA share gains”; it gave no EMEA margin target.

in_line: Management’s caution that Q4 visibility is lower is consistent with the preview’s warning about “less certainty in the second half” and its expectation of cautious H2 commentary.
Debt repayment remained in line with the preview’s stated capital-allocation priority: management reported $50M repaid in Q2 and continued to target debt paydown.

surprises.description: The preview put Q2 revenue consensus at $873–888 million, with even Needham's estimate at $851 million; CELH reported $818 million, below the cited range and low-end estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 total revenue was $818 million, up approximately 11% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus: $887.7M (Zacks), $873.3M (Investing.com), and $909.8M (one feed); Needham cut its Q2 estimate to $851M.

surprises.description: The preview said the CELSIUS brand bogey was at least 5% growth, but brand net sales declined about 12%. Tracked retail sales were down only 2%, with management attributing roughly half the gap to distributor inventory rebalancing tied to SKU rationalization.
surprises.fact_evidence: Brand CELSIUS net sales declined approximately 12% year-over-year while its tracked-channel retail sales fell only 2%, with roughly half of that gap attributed to distributor inventory rebalancing from SKU rationalization.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The bogey is at least +5%, against +6% in Q1 and +9% in Q2'25.”

surprises.description: The preview emphasized a low-50s gross-margin recovery in the second half, but management now expects gross margin to remain in the high 40s in Q3 as commodity inflation offsets integration and cost savings. The second North Carolina manufacturing line is expected to provide margin benefits as it ramps in the back half.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin was approximately 48%, flat with Q1, and is expected to stay in the high 40s in Q3 as commodity inflation (aluminum, diesel) largely offsets integration and cost savings; a second North Carolina manufacturing line is ramping in the back half.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had guided Q2 to a flat gross margin with “a return toward the low 50s in 2H”; the preview called for reaffirmation of the 2H ramp.

surprises.description: Alani Nu's $364 million of net sales fell below the preview's expected $390–410 million of shipments, although its 56% tracked retail growth exceeded the preview's at-least-50% sell-through marker. The gap points to slower sell-in than expected, not weak retail takeaway.
surprises.fact_evidence: Alani Nu net sales grew approximately 21% year-over-year to $364 million while tracked retail sales grew 56%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Shipments of about $390–410M with retail growth of at least +50%” were expected.

surprises.description: Management expects CELSIUS brand sales to stay flat sequentially in Q3 and says growth returns only as the company exits 2026 into 2027, extending the weak trajectory beyond the quarter in which the preview expected at least 5% brand growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects brand CELSIUS to remain flat sequentially in Q3, in both dollars and percentage terms, before returning to growth as it exits 2026 into 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “at least +5%” as the Q2 CELSIUS brand growth bogey and said management's tone on Q3 trends and 2027 would be a key signal.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $184 million, well below the preview's $210–215 million estimate; its 22.5% revenue margin was also below the preview's modeled 24–25%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA fell to $184 million, or 22.5% of revenue, from $210 million a year ago.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA was estimated at “~$210–215M,” modeled off a 24–25% margin.

surprises.description: The preview highlighted the prior-quarter buyback of only $24.1 million as a pace to watch; the company repurchased about $100 million in Q2 and said it intends to keep using the $300 million authorization this year.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company repurchased approximately $100 million of stock in Q2 ($124 million in the first half) and intends to continue using its $300 million authorization this year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's catalyst checklist flagged “buyback pace (only $24.1M in Q1).”

surprises.description: The preview described international as about 4.5% of revenue and focused on UK regulatory risk; management added a longer-term target for international to exceed 15% of revenue and plans to launch Alani Nu in select international markets in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management targets international markets to represent more than 15% of revenue over the next five years and plans to launch Alani Nu in select international markets in 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said international was about 4.5% of revenue and characterized the UK under-16 ban as “a narrative risk more than a numbers risk.”

in_line: Q2 gross margin was approximately 48%, in line with the preview's 48.0–48.5% estimate and management's expected flat quarter.
Alani Nu tracked retail growth of 56% exceeded the preview's expectation of at least 50%, even though its net sales were below the expected shipment range.

Rockstar sales were approximately $66 million, consistent with the preview's expectation of roughly $65–70 million; management said integration was completed on the nine-month timeline and sales were tracking in line with acquisition-era expectations.

surprises.description: Q2 net revenue of $331 million exceeded both preview estimates, which ranged from about $303 million to $320.7 million, even though revenue fell 13% year over year. The decline was attributed to the planned Western U.S. and Japan refranchising, while organic revenue was essentially flat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenue fell 13% to $331 million due to the planned re-franchising of the Western US and Japan, though organic revenue was essentially flat excluding those deals.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue | $320.7M (−15.6% YoY)” and alternative “~$303M (−20.3% YoY).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $28.8 million, below the preview’s roughly $30 million derived estimate and its $30–33 million base scenario. First-half EBITDA was about $61.9 million including Q1, just short of the preview’s roughly $62–65 million needed for the full-year guide to remain credible.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 43% year-over-year to $28.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA vs. ~$30M”; the base scenario was “$30–33M,” and “H1 needs to clear roughly $62–65M.”

surprises.description: U.S. average weekly sales per door rose to about $697 from the preview’s Q1 reference point of $685, rather than merely holding at that level. It was still below the preview’s $700-plus bull-scenario marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “US average weekly sales per door rose 33% year-over-year to approximately $697.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “U.S. average weekly sales per door. Q1 was $685, +16.7%”; the bull scenario cited “Sales/door above $700.”

surprises.description: The company reported a sharp first-half cash-flow and investment improvement that the preview did not quantify: capex fell 70% and free cash flow improved by more than $100 million year over year. The preview cited a full-year free-cash-flow target above $15 million and Q1 free cash flow of $11.4 million, but did not signal this scale of first-half improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half capex dropped 70% year-over-year to $16.1 million, and free cash flow improved by more than $100 million versus the first half of last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FCF above $15M” for FY26 guidance and Q1 “Free cash flow +$11.4M.”

surprises.description: Net leverage had already reached 5.4x, slightly below the preview’s cited target of getting below 5.5x by year-end. That is a modestly earlier achievement than the preview’s timing implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage improved to 5.4x trailing adjusted EBITDA,” down from 5.5x in Q1 according to the preview’s prior-quarter summary.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 leverage was “5.5x” and listed a “target below 5.5x by year-end.”

surprises.description: Franchisees now generate 42% of system-wide sales, up from about 25% a year ago, with a target of roughly 50% beginning next year. This indicates substantial progress in the refranchising mix despite the preview’s concern that no additional international deals had closed since March.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Franchisees now account for 42% of system-wide sales, up from about 25% a year ago, with the company targeting roughly 50% beginning next year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had guided to “2–3 more international refranchising deals in 2026” and “has closed none since March.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed that Q3 2025 included a $9.3 million cyber-insurance gain, which inflated the prior-year comparison. The preview flagged the need for H2 acceleration but did not identify this additional year-over-year comparison headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2025 included a $9.3 million cyber insurance gain that inflated the prior-year comparison.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q2 is the last quarter with McDonald's in the base” and that management needed “forward evidence of the H2 inflection,” without mentioning the cyber-insurance gain.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded by 340 basis points to 8.7%, an unanticipated operating improvement attributed to productivity initiatives and corporate cost controls; the preview supplied no margin estimate or margin expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 340 basis points to 8.7%, driven by productivity initiatives and corporate cost controls.”

in_line: The company maintained its FY26 guidance for net revenue of $1.25–$1.35 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $140–$150 million, and capex of $50–$60 million; the preview’s base scenario expected guidance to be reaffirmed.

Constant-currency system-wide sales growth of 2.6% and management’s statement that the company remains on track for its $2 billion full-year system-wide sales goal were consistent with the 2%–4% full-year growth guidance cited in the preview.

surprises.description: Total revenue was $31.7 million, above the preview’s $27.12–$27.47 million consensus range. The $23.2 million of IBTROZI product revenue was in line, so the beat came alongside $8.5 million of collaboration/license revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue of $31.7 million (including $8.5 million in collaboration/license revenue) exceeded the median estimate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $27.12M (Zacks) or $27.47M (Street composite)”

surprises.description: About 160 patients started IBTROZI, well below the preview’s expected plateau of roughly 200–216. The call attributed the decline to the finite pool of TKI-pretreated patients being depleted faster than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 160 new patients started IBTROZI in Q2”; “Total new patient starts are declining as the finite TKI-pretreated prevalence pool … has been largely depleted faster than expected.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New patient starts. Flat at ~200–216 for three quarters”; the bear case said “starts flat or down.”

surprises.description: Despite the lower total starts, IBTROZI’s first-line mix rose to about 85%, and first-line starts grew about 30% quarter over quarter. That is substantially stronger first-line momentum than the preview’s cited expectation that more than 50% of starts were TKI-naïve in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “About 85% [of new patients] in the first-line setting—up from roughly 30% at launch a year ago”; “first-line new patient starts grew approximately 30% over the prior quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said more than 50% of new starts were TKI-naïve (vs. ~30% at launch).”

surprises.description: The call reported that IBTROZI is now the most prescribed ROS1 TKI across all treatment lines and is selected for more than half of new first-line patients—market-position data the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “IBTROZI is now the most prescribed ROS1 TKI across all lines of therapy per IQVIA claims (Jan-May 2026) and is chosen for new first-line patients over 50% of the time.”

surprises.description: The call highlighted strong safusidenib Phase II results in Grade 2 IDH1-mutant glioma, including improved ORR and a 79% three-year PFS rate, with results compared favorably against vorasidenib. The preview mentioned new safusidenib studies but did not anticipate this data update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ORR increasing to 52% (from 44%) at 39-month median follow-up with a 79% 36-month PFS rate,” compared with “vorasidenib’s INDIGO 21% ORR and 52% 36-month PFS rate.”

surprises.description: The call described IBTROZI as having a meaningful clinical and safety distinction from newly approved Jideytro: it cited IBTROZI’s results in TKI-naive patients and lack of CNS warnings, versus Jideytro’s CNS warnings and other adverse-event signals. It also said Jideytro is priced about 8% higher despite being a later-line therapy; the preview did not flag this competitor comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “90% ORR and 50-month median DOR and PFS in TKI-naive patients in TRUST-I” and “the only brain-penetrant ROS1 TKI without CNS warnings in its label”; Jideytro “carries CNS warnings plus notable adverse events … and is priced roughly 8% higher as a later-line therapy.”

surprises.description: Nuvation used part of its convertible-note proceeds to prepay a term loan with a 10% minimum rate, materially lowering cash interest expense. The preview discussed the convert and capital allocation but did not anticipate this debt repayment or interest-cost reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “used [the notes proceeds] partly to prepay a 10%-minimum Sagard term loan, materially lowering cash interest expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capital allocation after the convert.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash and equivalents were $661 million, below the preview’s modeled $690–$730 million range, although management said the company had enough capital to reach profitability and fund a safusidenib launch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $661 million in cash and equivalents” and “believes it has sufficient capital to reach profitability and fund the safusidenib launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The full preview models cash near $690–730M.”

in_line: IBTROZI net U.S. product revenue of $23.2 million was in line with the median estimate of covering analysts and within the preview’s roughly $23–25 million implied range.
The roughly $30 million Eisai milestone tied to anticipated European approval in the first half of 2027 matched the preview’s stated expectation.

surprises.description: The preview’s base case anticipated runway into the first half of 2028, while REGENXBIO guided to runway into Q4 2027. The outlook is shorter than that base expectation, though the preview also identified guidance remaining in 2027 as a bear case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The strengthened balance sheet extends the company's cash runway into Q4 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected runway “into first half of 2028”; its bear scenario said runway “stays ‘into 2027.’”

surprises.description: The preview expected FDA alignment that existing data could support accelerated approval for RGX-121, but the call added that the FDA confirmed no additional studies or randomized controlled trial are required. That makes the path to resubmission more concrete than the preview specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FDA confirmed via a July Type A meeting that RGX-121 for Hunter syndrome can be reviewed under accelerated approval with no additional studies or RCT required.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the June FDA alignment indicated “existing data can support accelerated approval” and flagged the July Type A meeting and resubmission date for monitoring.

surprises.description: REGENXBIO disclosed a planned ex-U.S. randomized, placebo-controlled RGX-202 trial that the preview did not discuss. The new study adds a development program beyond the preview’s focus on the U.S. BLA timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new ex-U.S. Affinity Rise randomized placebo-controlled trial for RGX-202 will enroll approximately 100 patients at 2-to-1 active-to-placebo randomization with a planned crossover, and is set to initiate in the first half of 2027.”

surprises.description: Management put a roughly $10 billion potential launch market on CERAVEC’s wet AMD opportunity, a market-size estimate not included in the preview. This adds a notably large commercial-opportunity claim, though it is a management estimate rather than reported sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management estimates the wet AMD market could reach approximately $10 billion at launch, characterizing it as potentially one of the largest opportunities in gene therapy, with AbbVie leading commercialization.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that more than 500 surgeons have already been trained in CERAVEC’s subretinal delivery procedure, an indication of launch preparation that the preview did not mention.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 500 surgeons globally have been trained on the CERAVEC subretinal delivery procedure, supporting scalability ahead of a potential launch.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that U.S. Zolgensma patent protection has expired, while royalties continue in about 20 ex-U.S. countries; it also highlighted worldwide coverage on Abecma’s follow-on product and a potential sales opportunity of up to $2 billion. These royalty and patent details were not covered in the preview, and the U.S. expiry is offset in part by the continuing royalty streams described.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's U.S. patent on Zolgensma has expired, but royalties continue in about 20 ex-U.S. countries, plus worldwide coverage on Abecma/Novartis's follow-on product, which management noted could reach up to $2 billion in sales.”

in_line: The pro forma balance-sheet total was broadly in line with the preview’s estimate: the call reported over $310 million after the AbbVie milestone and offering, versus the preview’s approximately $313 million estimate.
RGX-202’s first BLA module remained targeted for Q3 2026, consistent with the preview’s expected Q3 submission target.
CERAVEC top-line wet AMD data remained expected in Q4 2026, matching the preview’s timing expectation.
RGX-121 resubmission remained targeted for Q3 2026, consistent with the preview’s focus on a Q3 resubmission date.
The reported $106 million cash balance at quarter-end was close to the preview’s approximately $105.5 million pre-announced cash-and-securities figure.

surprises.description: Papa John’s cut FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $180–$190 million from the prior $200–$210 million range, well below the preview’s expected range. The revised outlook includes an incremental $18 million for franchisee and transformation investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management revised 2026 guidance downward, now expecting adjusted EBITDA of $180-$190 million, including an incremental $18 million of franchisee/transformation investment.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Company guidance (FY26): $200M–$210M; the preview also highlighted “FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance ($200M–$210M)” and described reaffirmation as a catalyst.

surprises.description: The Board intends to suspend Papa John’s quarterly dividend beginning in August, contrary to the preview’s expectation that the dividend would be reaffirmed. The preview had specifically warned that anything less than reaffirmation would be a significant negative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Papa John's Board intends to suspend its quarterly dividend beginning in August to increase flexibility for transformation investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Dividend. Reaffirmation is the expected outcome. Anything less would likely be read as a reset.”

surprises.description: Papa John’s reported North America comparable sales down 8.3%, weaker than the preview’s roughly 6%–7% estimate and beyond its stated -8% bear-case threshold. The decline was driven almost entirely by fewer transactions and lower customer acquisition, while ticket was flat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North America comparable sales declined 8.3% in Q2, driven almost entirely by transaction/order volume declines and lower customer acquisition, while overall system ticket was flat year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NA comparable sales: ~-6% to -7% (BofA -6.7%, Jul 13, 2026)” and “-8% or worse would undercut the stabilization story.”

surprises.description: The FY26 sales outlook was reset sharply lower: Papa John’s now expects global system-wide sales down 2%–4% and North America comps down 6%–8%, rather than the previous NA comp range of down 2%–4% and a global outlook of flat to down low-single digits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management revised 2026 guidance downward, now expecting global system-wide sales to decline 2%-4%, North America comps down 6%-8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview lists prior FY26 guidance as “NA comps: -2% to -4%” and “Global system-wide sales flat to down LSD.”

surprises.description: International comparable sales grew 1.5%, below the preview’s expected 2.5%–3.5%. The U.K. and Korea were strong, but the Middle East was roughly flat amid regional conflict.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International remained the bright spot with 1.5% comparable sales growth (seventh consecutive positive quarter), including the U.K. up 10% and Korea up 9%, while the Middle East was roughly flat due to regional conflict.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “International comps: ~+2.5% to +3.5% (BofA 2.5%, Jul 13, 2026).”

surprises.description: The Board’s strategic review concluded that executing the transformation plan—not pursuing a sale—is the actionable value-creation path. The preview noted the unconfirmed $47-per-share proposal and flagged its status as a key issue, but the call reported a clear choice to prioritize the transformation while remaining open to actionable alternatives.
surprises.fact_evidence: “After an 18-month strategic review that explored a potential sale, the Board concluded that executing the transformation plan—not a sale—is the actionable value-creation path, though it remains open to actionable alternatives.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Take-private proposal status (unconfirmed). The Irth Capital proposal at $47/share was reported between March and June 2026. I could not confirm its current status.”

surprises.description: Papa John’s disclosed a broad leadership shakeup beyond the interim CFO situation already known before the call: the CMO is departing, new marketing and international leaders are being appointed, a development role is being created, and the CFO search remains active.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company announced a broad leadership shakeup, including a new Global Chief Marketing Officer, the departure of CMO Jenna Bromberg, a new SVP International, a newly created Global Chief Development Officer, and an interim CFO with an active search underway.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the interim CFO as a key issue: “Chris Collins has served as interim CFO since June 30. This is Collins' first print,” and cited management turnover as a source of uncertainty.

surprises.description: Domestic company-owned restaurant 4-wall margins fell 130 basis points to 11.2%, with lower transactions and higher food costs pressuring profitability. The preview did not identify this margin decline as an expected outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Domestic company-owned restaurant 4-wall margins fell 130 basis points to 11.2% (4-wall EBITDA of $15.6 million), pressured by lower transactions and higher food costs.”

surprises.description: First-half free cash flow was only $9 million, down from $37 million a year earlier, reflecting lower net income and transformation spending. The preview highlighted cash generation and dividend coverage as risks but supplied no first-half FCF estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow through the first half fell to $9 million from $37 million a year earlier, reflecting lower net income and transformation-related investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “Free cash flow and dividend coverage” as a key issue and noted that “Q1 FCF was negative.”

surprises.description: Papa John’s is accelerating portfolio changes, expecting 200–250 North America closures in 2026 and targeting mid-single-digit company ownership, including refranchising 28 Orlando restaurants. The preview did not anticipate this closure pace or the specific asset-light and refranchising plans.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Portfolio optimization is accelerating with 200-250 North America closures now expected in 2026 (versus 300 planned across 2026-2027), and management is pursuing an asset-light model targeting mid-single-digit company ownership, including refranchising 28 Orlando restaurants.”

in_line: Q2 consolidated revenue was $482 million, essentially matching the preview’s consensus estimate of about $481 million.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $3.1 million, well below the preview’s $4.02–4.03 million consensus estimate, a miss of roughly 23%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $3.1 million.”

surprises.description: First-half bookings reached $35.5 million, far above the preview’s analytical bar of roughly $10–15 million and its bull-case marker of above $20 million. The total was driven largely by the $20 million Florida Atlantic University annealing-system sale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First half 2026 bookings surged 1,120% to $35.5 million”; this was “driven largely by a $20 million annealing system sale to Florida Atlantic University.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 bookings against the author's bar of roughly $10–15M”; the bull scenario cited “Q2 bookings above $20M.”

surprises.description: Management now expects Q3 revenue to rise only modestly from Q2 and Q4 to be significantly higher and make up most of the year, with two annealing systems expected to ship in Q4. That is a more specifically Q4-concentrated profile than the preview’s general expectation that FAU revenue would be H2-weighted and at least two systems would be delivered in 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue should be up modestly from Q2, with Q4 up significantly and comprising the majority of full-year revenue, as two annealing systems are expected to ship in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “FAU stays H2-weighted” and cited guidance for “at least two deliveries in 2026.”

surprises.description: Cash and marketable securities ended the quarter at $546.2 million, about $42 million below the preview’s roughly $588 million reference and only slightly above its $540 million downside threshold. The call attributed over 90% of the year-over-year decline to cash used for the Quantum Circuits acquisition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and marketable securities totaled $546.2 million at quarter-end, down 33% year-over-year, with over 90% of the decline tied to roughly $250 million in cash for the Quantum Circuits acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Cash versus about $588M”; its bear scenario included “cash below $540M or ATM usage.”

surprises.description: The call reported that production applications generated more than a third of first-half QCaaS revenue and that six customer applications are now in production. The preview did not provide an expectation for production-application revenue or the number of production customers, so this adds a favorable adoption signal without a stated benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Production applications generated over 37% ($1.3 million) of first-half QCaaS revenue versus just 9.8% (~$300,000) a year earlier, and the company now has six customer applications in production.”

surprises.description: The call highlighted a Nature-published dual-rail result of approximately 99.9% two-qubit gate fidelity at 500-nanosecond gate times, a technical milestone not identified in the preview. The preview provided no expectation for this research result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Nature-published dual-rail research demonstrated approximately 99.9% two-qubit gate fidelity at 500-nanosecond gate times.”

in_line: RPO was $40.7 million, slightly below the prior-quarter $42.4 million level but above the preview’s roughly $40 million burn-down warning level and below its $45 million marker for bookings outrunning conversion.

surprises.description: Datadog reported Q2 revenue of $1.12 billion, about $40 million above the $1.08 billion consensus and above the high end of its $1.07–$1.08 billion guide. That is a stronger beat than the preview’s base case of $1.10 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached $1.12 billion, up 36% year-over-year and above the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $1.08B” consensus; the preview’s base scenario was “$1.10B.”

surprises.description: The sequential revenue addition was $115 million, far above the preview’s implied Q2 range of $64–74 million from the company’s guide. This was a substantial acceleration in quarterly dollars added.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A record quarter-over-quarter revenue addition of $115 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The guide implies $64–74M for Q2.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $4.45–$4.47 billion and EPS guidance to $2.50–$2.54, above the preview’s expected revenue range of $4.40–$4.42 billion in the base case and EPS range of $2.36–$2.44. Revenue guidance also reached the preview’s bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $4.45–$4.47 billion (30% growth) with non-GAAP EPS of $2.50–$2.54.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (current): Revenue $4.30–4.34B”; the base scenario expected “FY26 guide to $4.40–4.42B,” and the bull scenario expected “FY26 guide to $4.45B+.” Non-GAAP EPS guidance was “$2.36–2.44.”

surprises.description: Despite the Q2 beat and raised full-year outlook, Q3 revenue guidance implies growth slowing to 28–29% from Q2’s 36%. The preview emphasized confidence in second-half consumption, so this near-term deceleration tempers the strong full-year raise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue guidance of $1.135–$1.145 billion implies decelerating growth of 28–29% year-over-year, notably below the 36% posted in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise that only matches the Q2 beat would read as no added confidence in second-half AI consumption.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that its largest customer will reduce usage beginning in Q3, matching the kind of optimization language the preview warned about. The customer also signed a nine-figure renewal, and management said it had fully accounted for the reduction in Q3 and full-year guidance, which limits the negative implication.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A usage reduction from its largest customer (a leading AI company) beginning in Q3,” despite “the customer signing a 9-figure renewal”; management “fully derisked in both Q3 and full-year 2026 guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any renegotiation or optimization language would hurt.”

surprises.description: Non-AI customer revenue growth accelerated to the high 20s, rather than merely holding in the mid-20s as the preview’s central expectation suggested. Management said this was the fifth consecutive quarter of acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-AI customer revenue growth accelerated to the high 20s% year-over-year, up from mid-20s last quarter and 18% a year ago, marking five consecutive quarters of acceleration in the core business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The thesis rests on non-AI-native growth holding in the mid-20s.”

surprises.description: Q2 operating margin was 23%, above the preview’s estimated 21–22% margin and above the $225–235 million operating-income guide range’s implied margin level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 operating margin improved to 23% (from 20% a year ago).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income | ~$230M (21–22% margin).”

surprises.description: Datadog ended Q2 with about 4,720 customers above $100,000 in ARR, modestly ahead of the preview’s estimate of roughly 4,633.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customers with $100,000+ ARR grew to about 4,720 from 3,850 a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$100k+ ARR customers | ~4,633.”

surprises.description: Enterprise new-logo annualized bookings more than doubled year over year, and new customers contributed about 30% of revenue growth, up from 25% in Q1. The preview was watching new-logo contribution but did not anticipate this degree of enterprise bookings growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enterprise new logo annualized bookings more than doubled year-over-year, and new customers contributed about 30% of revenue growth, up from 25% in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Look for how much the record Q1 new logo contributes.”

surprises.description: The reported AI customer base included over 750 customers, with 31 spending more than $1 million annually and eight more than $10 million; all ten leading AI companies were customers. The preview anticipated AI lab wins as a possible catalyst but did not set expectations for this breadth or scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI customers now number over 750, including 31 spending more than $1 million annually and 8 spending more than $10 million annually, with all 10 of the top 10 AI leaders as customers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Named AI lab wins” were part of the bull scenario; the preview also cited an “Anthropic consumption ramp.”

surprises.description: Multi-product adoption was notably broad: 13% of customers used at least 10 products, up from 7%, and 37% used at least six, up from 29%. The preview did not identify this operating metric as an expectation or debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “13% of customers now using 10+ products (up from 7%) and 37% using 6+ products (up from 29%).”

in_line: Net revenue retention held in the low 120s, as the preview expected it to remain low-120% absent a move to the mid-120s.
Gross margin was 79.6%, down from 80.2% in Q1 but above the preview’s sub-79% level identified as a material risk.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $1.8 billion, below the preview’s $1.89 billion consensus estimate by about $90 million. Adjusted EPS was $0.58, exactly at consensus, so the revenue shortfall was not accompanied by an EPS miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales were $1.8 billion” and “record adjusted EPS of $0.58.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 net sales … Consensus $1.89B”; “Q2 adj. EPS … Consensus $0.58.”

surprises.description: The company cut its FY26 adjusted EPS range from $3.00–$3.40 to $2.85–$3.15 and lowered expected sales from about $7.8–$7.9 billion to approximately $7.6 billion at midpoint. The industry outlook also weakened from down low single digits to down mid-single digits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance is $2.85 to $3.15 on approximately $7.6 billion of sales at midpoint, with the industry now expected down mid-single digits versus a prior expectation of down low single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EPS $3.00–$3.40”; “FY26 net sales ~$7.8–$7.9B”; “Reaffirmation of $3.00–$3.40 is the base case.”

surprises.description: Mattress Firm sales were about $922 million versus the preview’s derived estimate of about $966 million, despite slight same-store sales growth. The preview had said its sales estimate implicitly required positive same-store sales, so the positive SSS was in line even as reported segment sales fell short.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mattress Firm net sales were approximately $922 million with only slight same-store sales growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Mattress Firm sales … ~$966M, derived”; “Consensus implicitly needs positive SSS.”

surprises.description: Tempur Sealy North America reported much stronger margins, with adjusted gross margin up 680 basis points and operating margin up 400 basis points, alongside $30 million of quarterly net synergy benefit. The preview did not anticipate or quantify this segment margin and synergy performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tempur Sealy North America adjusted gross margin expanded 680 basis points to 61.8% and operating margin improved 400 basis points to 26.7%, driven by $30 million of net synergy benefit in the quarter.”

surprises.description: The July 4 holiday period was notably weak, a deterioration not flagged in the preview, although Mattress Firm same-store sales rebounded to roughly flat after the holiday ended. The sharp holiday weakness and subsequent recovery make the update mixed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The July 4 holiday period was notably weak, but Mattress Firm same-store sales rebounded to roughly flat after the holiday ended around July 15.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Mattress Firm same-store sales and gross margin” were key metrics to watch; the preview’s base scenario expected “SSS flat to slightly negative.”

surprises.description: The company reported record Q2 operating and free cash flow, more than $500 million of trailing-12-month net debt reduction, and over $160 million returned to shareholders. The preview cited strong Q1 cash flow and debt paydown but did not set a Q2 expectation for these measures or shareholder returns.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record operating cash flow of $236 million and free cash flow of $182 million, reduced net debt by more than $500 million over the trailing 12 months, and returned over $160 million to shareholders.”

surprises.description: The Leggett & Platt combination is now expected to close before the end of Q3, ahead of the company’s original expectations. The preview noted pending clearances and the August 20 vote but did not anticipate an earlier close timetable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Leggett & Platt combination is expected to close before the end of Q3, ahead of original expectations, with a shareholder vote August 20.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Canada, EU, UK, and Korea competition clearances and Austrian FDI approval are still pending.”

surprises.description: Management said the Leggett & Platt transaction is expected to add adjusted EPS immediately, even before synergies. The preview explicitly treated accretion information as new, but did not have this positive indication.
surprises.fact_evidence: The combination “is projected to deliver immediate adjusted EPS accretion before synergies.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance excludes the deal, so any quantified synergy or accretion figure would be new information.”

surprises.description: The company extended and upsized its credit facility, with maturities pushed to 2031 and management expecting lower future interest expense. This financing update was not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The credit facility was refinanced and upsized with maturities extended to 2031 to lower future interest expense.”

surprises.description: Management described a demand split in which entry-level bedding remains hardest hit while luxury and mid-market demand is resilient. The preview discussed industry weakness but did not anticipate this specific mix commentary.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Entry-level bedding remains the hardest hit while luxury/mid-market demand stays resilient.”

surprises.description: Kingsdown products are set to expand from a 200-store pilot to nearly 800 Mattress Firm stores over the next six months, a rollout not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Kingsdown products will expand from a 200-store pilot to nearly 800 Mattress Firm stores over the next six months.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.58 matched the $0.58 consensus and was at the top of the $0.56–$0.58 guidance band.
Mattress Firm same-store sales were slightly positive, consistent with the preview’s expectation that positive SSS was needed, though the segment’s reported sales were below its derived estimate.
The roughly $10 million Q2 commodity-cost headwind was in line with the preview’s stated expectation of about $10 million of commodity cost impact.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $49.8 million exceeded the company’s $40–$48 million guide and consensus of about $41.6–$42.4 million. The beat was partly supported by $4.9 million of previously deferred GM settlement revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $49.8 million”; Thermal Barrier revenue “including $4.9 million of previously deferred GM settlement revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue: $40M–$48M”; consensus “$41.6M … or $42.4M.”

surprises.description: The Q3 outlook was substantially stronger than the preview’s expected $46–$52 million range: revenue is guided to $65–$80 million, with adjusted EBITDA of $7–$15 million, indicating a return to positive EBITDA rather than merely approaching the $50 million breakeven threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $65 million to $80 million … with adjusted EBITDA guided to $7 million to $15 million, signaling a return to positive EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “Q3 guided $46M–$52M”; the preview said a Q3 guide “at or above $50M” would support the breakeven thesis.

surprises.description: Energy Industrial revenue in Q2 was $20.4 million, below the preview’s implied $26–$28 million Q2 range. This weakness contrasts with the stronger total-company revenue print.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue was split between “$20.4 million Energy Industrial and $29.5 million Thermal Barrier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Q2 guide implies only about $26M–$28M for that segment.”

surprises.description: Aspen raised its 2026 European Thermal Barrier revenue outlook to $20–$30 million from $10–$15 million, after generating $10.9 million in the first half. The preview did not identify this regional outlook increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its 2026 European Thermal Barrier revenue outlook from $10-15 million to $20-30 million,” with “$10.9 million in the first half.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a new European OEM win and a larger awarded pipeline: Jaguar Land Rover is its seventh European OEM customer, and nine awarded platforms could be worth up to $135 million at full production. No such customer or pipeline expansion was anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Added Jaguar Land Rover as its seventh European OEM customer,” expanding the pipeline to “nine vehicle platforms worth up to $135 million at full production volumes.”

surprises.description: Management set a target to double Thermal Barrier revenue in 2027 to $40–$60 million from its 2026 outlook. This forward target was not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management targets doubling Thermal Barrier revenue to $40-60 million in 2027 from the 2026 outlook, based on conservative volume assumptions.”

surprises.description: GM production assumptions were far above the preview’s 55,000–65,000 annualized assumption: production was about 100,000 annualized in Q2, and Q3 guidance assumes 90,000–125,000 as inventory rebuilds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GM production ran at roughly 40,000 vehicles annualized in Q1 and 100,000 in Q2, with Q3 guidance assuming 90,000-125,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the “GM production range (55–65k annualized)” as the assumption to watch.

surprises.description: The East Providence disruption had a substantial gross-margin impact, with reported gross margin at 7% and $5.3 million of incident costs; charges are expected to continue through Q3, and full production capacity is not expected until the first half of 2027. The preview flagged the costs and restoration timeline as issues but gave no expectation of this scale or timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin was just 7% … or 17% adjusted margin excluding $5.3 million of incident-related costs”; charges of “$5-10 million continuing through Q3”; full capacity “restored in the first half of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked to separate “the one-time disruption cost booked in Q2” and identify “the timeline to full capacity.”

surprises.description: The Plant 2 asset sale is now likely to occur in 2027 rather than in Q4 2026, delaying the asset-sale timing the preview identified as a near-term deleveraging catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Plant 2 asset sale is now likely a 2027 event.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the Plant 2 sale was “expected in Q4 2026, the deleveraging catalyst.”

in_line: Management maintained the approximately 20% full-year 2026 Energy Industrial growth target, which the preview specifically flagged as a key question.

surprises.description: BlackSky reported Q2 revenue of $33.3 million, above the preview’s $29.8–$30.7 million consensus range. That is a meaningful beat after the preview highlighted the need for a sharp step-up from Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 2026 revenue grew 50% year-over-year and 60% sequentially to $33.3 million.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was substantially stronger than the preview’s near-breakeven expectation: BlackSky reported $4.7 million rather than roughly zero or the preview’s base-case range of negative $2 million to zero.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $4.7 million (a 14.2% margin), a $7.5 million improvement over the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 adj. EBITDA… roughly breakeven implied by FY guide”; the base scenario was “−$2M to $0M.”

surprises.description: Space-based intelligence and AI services revenue reached $24.5 million, well above the preview’s roughly $19–20 million sequential target. This segment therefore contributed more to the quarter’s step-up than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record space-based intelligence and AI services revenue of $24.5 million (up 50% from Q1).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether this segment reaches about $19–20M in Q2.”

surprises.description: BlackSky raised $150 million through ATM offerings, making the anticipated financing and dilution issue concrete; the raise also substantially increased cash and liquidity. The preview questioned whether the capex plan could be funded without further dilution but did not anticipate this amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised $150 million through ATM offerings, boosting cash to $244.1 million… and total liquidity above $325 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capital plan: ATM usage, share count, and whether $50–60M capex is funded without further dilution.”

surprises.description: The call reported unusually strong international subscription growth and said multi-year international contracts now make up most funded backlog, developments the preview did not specifically anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International space-based intelligence subscription revenue grew 150% year-over-year, and multi-year international contracts now comprise over 80% of total funded backlog.”

surprises.description: Gen 3-related products and services were said to drive 90% of company growth, with 35-centimeter imagery delivered at roughly one-fifth the cost of legacy platforms. The preview discussed Gen 3 satellite deployment but did not anticipate this degree of growth contribution or the stated cost advantage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gen 3-related products and services are driving 90% of the company's growth, delivering 35-centimeter imagery at roughly one-fifth the cost of legacy platforms.”

surprises.description: Year-to-date bookings reached up to $200 million, above the preview’s prior-quarter reference to about $160 million of YTD contract awards.
