The call also disclosed an 8-figure NRO contract to accelerate AROS development toward a 2028 launch, a specific award not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company secured up to $200 million in year-to-date bookings and won an 8-figure NRO contract to accelerate AROS development toward a targeted 2028 launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “About $160M of YTD contract awards.”

in_line: Full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $130–150 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $12–24 million were reaffirmed, as the preview’s base case expected the guidance to be reaffirmed.
The $50–60 million full-year capex guidance was reaffirmed, matching the preview’s stated guidance.
BlackSky reached a $100 million annual run rate for high-margin imagery and AI subscription services, consistent with the preview’s roughly $100 million annualized-run-rate target.

Management still planned to have at least eight Gen 3 satellites on orbit by year-end, consistent with the preview’s stated commitment; the preview had also flagged launch delays as a risk to the H2 ramp.
Management warned that large, lumpy Mission Solutions deals would create quarter-to-quarter revenue variability, consistent with the preview’s warning that lumpy programs could distort total revenue.

surprises.description: Green Plains reported diluted EPS of $0.83, above the preview’s vendor range of $0.52–$0.65. Even against the highest estimate, the beat was substantial.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income attributable to Green Plains was $67.1 million or $0.83 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) $0.52”; alternates “$0.54” and “$0.65.”

surprises.description: The preview anticipated spring maintenance would reduce 45Z production volumes, but the carbon platform’s net EBITDA rose to nearly $59 million from $55.2 million in Q1. This suggests the carbon contribution held up better than that maintenance concern implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The carbon platform contributed nearly $59 million of net EBITDA in Q2, up from $55.2 million in Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Spring maintenance would reduce 45Z production volumes.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted the risk that 45Z credits were recognized before collection and looked for confirmation that they were converting on schedule. Green Plains received the final $41 million payment for 2025 credits, but had not monetized any of its 2026 credits, leaving current-year cash conversion unresolved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received a final $41 million cash payment for its 2025 45Z credits during Q2”; it “has not yet monetized any of its 2026 45Z credits,” preferring to wait for a partner offering stable, predictable cash flows.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Credits are recognized ahead of collection, so the lag between EBITDA and cash is a real risk”; “Confirmation that credits are converting on schedule would remove a main balance-sheet concern.”

surprises.description: The preview noted market commentary that crush margins had softened from Q2 into Q3 and warned that a similar company outlook could be cautious. Instead, management said Q3 margins were only slightly below Q2’s historically high levels and expected favorable conditions to last into early Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 crush margins are only slightly below Q2's historically high levels, with the favorable margin structure expected to carry into early Q4 before seasonal declines.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Other market commentary suggests board crush softened from Q2 into Q3. If GPRE echoes this, the full-year bridge could be questioned.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA of $93.3 million was essentially in line with the preview’s approximately $93 million UBS estimate.
Spring maintenance affected Q2 operations, as the preview had anticipated; capacity utilization averaged nearly 90%, while the company retained its roughly 95% full-year utilization target.

surprises.description: ATI reported Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $284 million, $29 million above the high end of its prior guidance and well above the roughly $250 million implied expectation. The 22.6% margin, up 440 basis points year over year, also showed stronger profitability than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA reached $284 million” and was “$29 million above the high end of prior guidance”; “adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 440 basis points year-over-year to 22.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$250M (implied)” and company guidance of “$245–$255M.”

surprises.description: Revenue reached $1.3 billion, about $80 million above the preview’s roughly $1.22 billion consensus estimate. The 11% year-over-year increase was stronger than the expected level of sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue up 11% to $1.3 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue ~$1,220M (Zacks).”

surprises.description: ATI raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to a $1.160 billion midpoint, materially above the preview’s $1.010–$1.060 billion range and its expectation of only a modest increase. The new midpoint represents 35% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year guidance across all metrics: adjusted EBITDA midpoint to $1.160 billion (35% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior full-year guide was “$1,010–$1,060M”; the preview said a raise to “roughly $1.05–$1.09B” was needed to match expectations and identified a “modest FY raise” as the base scenario.

surprises.description: The new full-year adjusted EPS midpoint of $5.04 is well above the preview’s $4.20–$4.48 expected range, rather than merely tracking the prior-year guidance context. ATI said the midpoint implies 56% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS midpoint to $5.04 (56% growth).”

surprises.description: ATI raised its full-year free cash flow midpoint to $575 million, above the preview’s $465–$525 million range. That is a larger improvement than the preview’s expected range implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow midpoint to $575 million (51% growth).”

surprises.description: AA&S margins reached 23.7%, substantially exceeding the preview’s expectation that margins move toward 19% or higher. The reported figure included a $10 million asset-sale gain, but margin was still 22% excluding that gain, versus 14% a year ago; management now expects sustained mid-20% margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AA&S segment margins expanded 930 basis points to an all-time high of 23.7%” and were “22% excluding a $10 million asset sale gain, versus 14% a year ago”; management is “now guiding to sustained mid-20% margins.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for AA&S sales returning to growth and margin moving toward 19%+.”

surprises.description: ATI’s backlog rose to $4.4 billion, up 7% sequentially and 18% year over year, above the preview’s $4.1 billion starting point and even the bull scenario’s threshold of more than $4.3 billion. About 70% is expected to convert to revenue within 12 months.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record backlog reached $4.4 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 7% sequentially, with about 70% expected to convert to revenue over the next 12 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “$4.1B record” and listed “backlog above $4.3B” in its bull scenario.

surprises.description: Defense revenue grew 36% to an all-time high, and ATI raised its full-year defense growth outlook to the high teens. The preview did not flag this level of defense growth or an outlook increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Defense revenue grew 36% year-over-year to an all-time high, prompting management to raise full-year defense growth expectations to high teens.”

surprises.description: ATI disclosed a renewed naval nuclear contract worth roughly $1 billion over five years through 2030—about double the prior contract. Its economics are also predominantly price and mix, with about two-thirds of the value attributed to price/mix and one-third to volume.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The renewed naval nuclear contract is a roughly $1 billion revenue agreement over 5 years extending through 2030, roughly double the prior contract, split about two-thirds price/mix and one-third volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Price vs. volume” as a key issue, saying “Price-led growth supports the multiple more than volume-led growth at flat prices,” but did not anticipate this contract or its economics.

surprises.description: ATI raised consolidated incremental margin guidance from 40% to 50%, a stronger outlook for converting additional revenue into profit than the preview described.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year consolidated incremental margin guidance from 40% to 50%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s key metrics discussed price versus volume and capacity, but did not anticipate an increase in incremental margin guidance.

surprises.description: Management said roughly $30–$40 million of high-incremental-margin HPMC revenue shifted from the first half into the second half because of qualification timing at the new Mexico facility and EB2 titanium furnace. The revenue is delayed rather than described as lost, but the timing leaves less of it in the first half than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately $30-40 million of HPMC revenue at 40-50% incremental margins shifted from the first half into the second half due to qualification timing at the new Mexico facility and EB2 titanium furnace.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged capacity and FCF, including that “H1 FCF needs to track toward the $465–$525M guide, which is back-half loaded,” but did not anticipate this specific revenue shift.

surprises.description: ATI’s implied Q4 EBITDA of about $335 million would represent an approximately $1.35 billion annualized exit rate, considerably stronger than the preview’s expected modest full-year guide increase suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Implied Q4 EBITDA of ~$335 million translates to a ~$1.350 billion annualized exit rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected a “modest FY raise” in its base scenario and said a raise to “roughly $1.05–$1.09B” would match expectations.

surprises.description: ATI reported 13% year-over-year jet engine revenue growth and described extended lead times—12 months for nickel, 20 months for premium titanium, and more than 24 months for isothermal forgings—along with sole-source positions on five of the seven most advanced nickel superalloys. The preview did not anticipate these demand and supply-tightness details.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Jet engine revenue grew 13% year-over-year”; ATI produces “6 of the 7 most advanced nickel super alloys (sole source on 5)” and lead times extend to “12 months on nickel, 20 months on premium titanium, and over 24 months on isothermal forgings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed capacity timing, including nickel remelt coming online in Q4 2026 and primary VIM melt in 2027, but did not state an expectation for jet engine growth or these lead times.

surprises.description: Viatris reported Q2 revenue of $3.8 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.69, above the preview’s $3.68 billion and $0.62 consensus estimates. Adjusted EBITDA was also $1.2 billion, above the preview’s estimated $1.00–$1.05 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenues of $3.8 billion,” “adjusted EBITDA of $1.2 billion,” and “adjusted EPS of $0.69, all exceeding expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview: Q2 consensus of “$3.68B” revenue and “$0.62” adjusted EPS; adjusted EBITDA “est. ~$1.00–1.05B.”

surprises.description: Viatris raised the midpoint of its full-year 2026 guidance across key metrics, rather than merely reaffirming guidance or raising it within the existing range. The preview’s base case anticipated a raise to the top half but no range lift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised the midpoint of its full-year 2026 guidance across all key metrics,” now implying operational growth of approximately 2% for revenue, 5% for adjusted EBITDA, and 7% for adjusted EPS.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview: “A reaffirm alone is likely to disappoint”; the base scenario expected guidance “raised to top half but range not lifted.” The bull scenario allowed for a larger raise.

surprises.description: Greater China sales growth was much stronger than the preview’s expected slowdown: sales grew 16% year over year versus the preview’s segment consensus of +7.3%. Management nevertheless expects growth to moderate in the second half, citing a hospital-channel procurement policy change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Greater China net sales grew 16% year-over-year with e-commerce sales up 36%,” but “management expects growth to moderate in the second half due to a hospital-channel procurement policy change.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview segment consensus: Greater China “$631.7M (+7.3% YoY)”; it also said the market models “a sharp slowdown from Q1's pace.”

surprises.description: The Nashik facility fire and a May FDA inspection are expected to create a new second-half revenue headwind that the preview did not identify. The estimated $100–$150 million impact is concentrated in low-margin generics, with no single affected product above $20 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Supply disruptions from the Nashik facility fire and May 2026 FDA inspection are expected to reduce second-half revenues by $100 million to $150 million,” primarily affecting low-margin generics, with “no single impacted product exceeding $20 million.”

in_line: The preview expected Greater China growth to slow from Q1’s pace; management likewise expects moderation in the second half, although it cited a hospital-channel procurement policy change as the reason.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $115.1 million, above the company’s implied $110–112 million guidance range and the preview’s current $111.4 million consensus figure. That was a clear upside to the nearer-term expectations, although the preview also noted a stale $115.7 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales grew approximately 5.7% year-over-year to $115.1 million, exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Positive low-single-digit % Y/Y,” implying “~$110–112M”; consensus was “$111.4M (TradingKey, current).”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA reached $5.8 million, far above the preview’s $0.5–2.0 million guidance range and roughly $1.3 million consensus midpoint. This was a much larger earnings beat than the preview’s bull scenario of $2.5–3.5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA reached $5.8 million (a 5% margin), far outperforming guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 adjusted EBITDA guidance was “$0.5–2.0M”; consensus was “~$1.3M (midpoint).” The bull scenario projected “EBITDA $2.5–3.5M.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $13–15 million, rather than the preview’s expected $9–11 million and characterization of profitability as slightly below FY25’s $12.0 million. The new range implies a stronger full-year profit outlook than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Q2 EBITDA outperformance was “driving a raise in full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $13-$15 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY26 adjusted EBITDA was expected to be “Profitable, slightly lower than 2025,” or approximately “$9–11M”; FY25 adjusted EBITDA was $12.0M.

surprises.description: Gross margin recovered to 57.9%, above the preview’s implied 55–57% range and well beyond its 150-basis-point sequential-improvement test from Q1’s 54.3%. The year-over-year decline was only about 40 basis points, while the sequential recovery was about 360 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin was 57.9%, down about 40 basis points year-over-year but up roughly 360 basis points sequentially from Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Gross margin was “~55–57% (implied)”; the preview said “A sequential GM improvement of 150bps or more from 54.3% is the test.”

surprises.description: Total orders declined about 2% even as AOV rose about 8%, matching the preview’s concern that flat-to-down orders with rising AOV could indicate pressure on unit demand. However, orders excluding sub-$500 purchases rose 5%, and two-year stacked order growth was 16%, tempering that concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total orders declined about 2% year-over-year, but excluding sub-$500 orders (a few percent of sales), orders rose 5%, and two-year stacked order growth was 16%.” AOV “rose about 8% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Flat-to-down orders with rising AOV would suggest price increases are hurting unit demand, which would cap the FY revenue guide.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating expenses showed broad leverage, with total adjusted OpEx improving by 250 basis points and marketing expense falling by 130 basis points as a share of sales. The preview did not anticipate this specific expense performance, which helps explain the unusually strong EBITDA result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company drove year-over-year operating expense leverage across all three adjusted categories, with marketing down 130 bps to 22.8% of sales and total adjusted OpEx improving 250 bps to 53%.”

surprises.description: Showroom-related demand was notably strong: walk-in bookings without appointments grew 47%, while the Beverly Hills flagship recorded over 40% higher bookings and about 10% higher AOVs than prior locations. The preview did not set an expectation for these showroom metrics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Showroom bookings from walk-in customers without appointments grew 47% year-over-year, and the new Beverly Hills flagship delivered over 40% higher bookings and about 10% higher AOVs versus prior locations.”

in_line: Fine jewelry bookings grew about 32% year-over-year and reached about 18% of bookings, broadly sustaining the preview’s diversification thesis: it had noted 33% growth and a 17% share in Q1, and said growth below roughly 25% would be concerning.
FY26 net sales guidance of $459–462 million remained within the preview’s expected company-guidance range of roughly $455–462 million, despite stale consensus of about $466.9 million.

surprises.description: Xeris raised the bottom of its 2026 revenue outlook from $380 million to $385 million and narrowed the range to $385–390 million, matching the preview’s identified bull-case trigger rather than its base case of reaffirming $380–390 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised the bottom end of full-year 2026 revenue guidance and tightened the range to $385–390 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Reaffirming $380–390M is the base case. A raise or narrowing to $385–390M would be the bull trigger.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $92.1 million came in above the preview’s consensus estimate of $90.73 million, although it was within the preview’s $91–93 million base-case scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q2 revenue reached $92.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue (Q2'26) … Consensus $90.73M (alt. $90.22M from 7 analysts).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $19.3 million, above the preview’s roughly $18 million watch threshold, despite the additional commercial and R&D investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose over 50% year-over-year to $19.3 million, an improvement of $6.7 million despite incremental commercial and R&D investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA below about $18M would suggest spending is outpacing revenue.”

surprises.description: The company now expects 2026 SG&A to increase by about $50 million, $5 million more than its prior guidance and the preview’s expected $45 million increase, indicating a larger spending step-up than investors were led to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year SG&A is now expected to increase approximately $50 million versus 2025 (up $5 million from prior guidance).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided to about $45M of incremental SG&A.”

surprises.description: Xeris fully retired its 2028 convertible notes in July, eliminating $34 million of debt and saving about $3 million in annual interest, but the retirement also produced a roughly $31 million non-cash Q2 GAAP charge; the preview did not flag this transaction or charge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fully retired its 2028 convertible notes in July via cash and equity, eliminating $34 million of debt and saving roughly $3 million in annual interest, but incurring a one-time non-cash GAAP charge of about $31 million in Q2.”

surprises.description: Xeris reported new XP-8121 patent progress that the preview had not anticipated: a second U.S. patent was secured and a third received a notice of allowance, adding prospective protection for the program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management secured a second US patent (July 28) plus a notice of allowance for a third.”

in_line: Recorlev revenue was $56.8 million, within the preview’s implied $55–57 million range.
XP-8121 remained on track to start Phase 3 in 2026, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a start later this year.
The planned R&D increase of about $25 million was consistent with the preview.

surprises.description: Heritage reported diluted EPS of $2.05, far above the preview’s $1.19–$1.27 consensus range. The gap was substantial even allowing for the preview’s warning that estimates conflicted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q2 2026 net income of $61.7 million ($2.05 diluted EPS).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS … Consensus (varies by source): $1.19 … or $1.27.”

surprises.description: The loss ratio and combined ratio were markedly better than the preview’s key underwriting concern suggested, and Heritage reported much larger favorable reserve development than a year earlier. The reserve release is a notable contributor to the strong underwriting result, though the preview gave no reserve-development estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The combined ratio improved to 64.9% from 72.9%, and the net loss ratio improved to 30.4% from 38.5%, aided by $23.4 million of favorable prior period reserve development (versus $2.3 million a year earlier).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview ranked “Net loss ratio and weather losses” as the largest EPS driver and noted Q2 2025’s 38.5% loss ratio; it also identified storm losses as a key risk.

surprises.description: Gross premiums written fell 5.5%, rather than showing the positive Q2 print that would support the expected growth inflection. The preview allowed that the turn might come in Q3, but said another decline would undercut the thesis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross premiums written fell 5.5% to $380.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management expected the GPW trend “to turn positive in Q2 or Q3”; the preview said “A positive GPW print supports the growth-inflection thesis. A third consecutive decline would undercut it.”

surprises.description: Management now expects Florida rate reductions of 3%–5% as reinsurance costs fall, a pricing consequence not specified in the preview. Other states are expected to receive modest increases roughly in line with claims inflation, with margins held flat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects Florida rate reductions in the 3%-5% range driven by lower reinsurance costs, while other states should see modest rate increases roughly matching claims inflation to keep margins flat.”

in_line: The approximately $63 million of annualized reinsurance savings was essentially in line with the preview’s estimate of $63.2 million, and the expected larger benefit beginning in Q3 was consistent with the reported Q3 ceded-premium-ratio outlook.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue reached $2.4 billion, about 5% above the preview’s $2.28 billion consensus, despite a 1% smaller fleet. The preview expected revenue at or slightly above plan, so the reported beat was stronger than that framing suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 10% year-over-year to $2.4 billion, achieved with a 1% smaller fleet and beating both consensus and prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $2.28B”; the June 24 pre-announcement said revenue was “at or slightly above” plan.

surprises.description: Pricing and the revenue-to-cost spread outperformed the preview’s build: RPD rose 9% versus an expected 6.5%, and the spread widened 17% year over year after the preview cited about 12% in Q1 and said it might hold or widen. RPU also exceeded the company’s $1,500 North Star target, reaching $1,542.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RPD increased 9% and RPU rose 8% to $1,542, surpassing the $1,500 North Star target, with U.S. airport RPD up 12%; commercial actions drove roughly 6-7 points of the RPD gain versus 2-3 points from industry pricing”; the RPD-to-DOE-per-day spread “expanded 17% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s “Derived base-case build” used RPD “up 6.5%”; it said the RPD-versus-DOE spread was about +12% in Q1 and that “if it holds or widens in Q2” the pricing-driven turnaround thesis holds.

surprises.description: Recall pressure intensified substantially: recalls were up 300% year over year and caused about $30 million of EBITDA headwind, versus the preview’s Q1 reference to more than $25 million of recall-related EBITDA cost. The call also quantified about $55 million of revenue impact and a nearly 200-basis-point utilization drag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Vehicle recalls surged 300% year-over-year, affecting an average of 15,000 vehicles monthly and creating a ~$55 million revenue and ~$30 million EBITDA headwind plus a nearly 200 bps drag on utilization.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 utilization of 79%, “with recalls costing ~200 bps of utilization and more than $25M of EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Liquidity came in below the preview’s pro forma benchmark, and the year-end outlook was reduced: pro forma liquidity was only slightly above $1 billion after the notes offering, while full-year guidance was $1.0-$1.4 billion rather than the prior roughly $1.5 billion expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended Q2 with “$984 million in liquidity,” completed a $350 million notes offering plus a $30 million greenshoe, and brought pro forma liquidity “slightly above $1 billion.” Full-year liquidity guidance was “$1.0-$1.4 billion (lowered from ~$1.5 billion after removing ATM proceeds).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for comparison with “the ~$1.0B guide plus the ~$350M PIK notes,” cited a “~$1.35B pro-forma figure,” and said the earlier year-end liquidity guide was “>$1.5B.”

surprises.description: Q3 net DPU guidance was modestly better than the preview’s base case: the $285-$295 range is below the preview’s $290-$305 expectation and keeps the whole range under the company’s stated sub-$300 target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects ... net DPU of $285-$295.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Q3 DPU guided $290-305” and identified management’s stated target as “<$300/month.”

surprises.description: Oro came with more specific commercial scale than the preview had: the platform was reported active on Uber in four markets with over 6 million driver miles and expected to generate more than $600 million in revenue this year. The call also gave a launch window for its Lucid/Nuro AV partnership in the San Francisco Bay Area.
surprises.fact_evidence: Oro is “active on Uber in four markets with over 6 million driver miles logged,” is “expected to generate more than $600 million in revenue this year,” and has an AV partnership “launching in the San Francisco Bay Area later this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said that “any disclosed economics or contracted volume would be new information” about Oro.

in_line: Net DPU was $302, roughly in line with the approximately $300 company guidance noted in the preview.
The FY26 EBITDA outlook was reduced or reframed to $225-$275 million from the previously stated 3%-6% margin guidance, consistent with the preview’s assessment that a cut was widely expected.
Management reaffirmed the approximately $1 billion EBITDA target for 2027, which the preview identified as an important target to watch and said would support the bull case if retained.

surprises.description: Revenue grew 13% in constant currency, well above the preview’s 7.6%–8.4% consensus growth range and the company’s mid- to high-single-digit guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY27 revenue grew 13% in constant currency, beating the company's mid- to high single-digit guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue ... Consensus ... +7.6% to +8.4% Y/Y”; “Use $1.86B ... as the headline bogey.”

surprises.description: Gross margin expanded 130 basis points and AUR grew 15%, stronger than the preview’s high-single-digit AUR guide and its warning that expansion below about 50 basis points would challenge the premiumization thesis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 130 basis points to 73.6%, driven by 15% AUR growth that more than offset incremental tariff, labor, and non-cotton material costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AUR is guided to high-single-digit growth in Q1”; “Expansion below about 50bps, especially with a promotional explanation, would challenge the premiumization thesis.”

surprises.description: North America grew 13%, far above the preview’s low-single-digit regional outlook, and wholesale rose 22%; however, management attributed roughly 15 points of wholesale growth to shipment timing and resumed shipments to a luxury account, and plans faster off-price and low-tier door reductions in the back half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North America at 13%”; “North America wholesale grew 22%, but roughly 15 points came from shipment timing shifts and resumed shipments to a luxury account”; management plans “accelerated off-price and low-tier door reductions in the back half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “North America is guided to low-single-digit growth”; the preview also flags “Soft NA wholesale” as a bear-case risk.

surprises.description: Asia grew 25%, clearing the preview’s 15% level for sustaining the regional growth narrative; China was especially strong at over 40% in the quarter, even though the preview cited mid-teens China growth as the guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Asia led regional growth at 25% ... with China sales surging over 40% in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Growth below 15% would undercut the narrative”; “China is guided to mid-teens against a 40% comp.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating margin expanded 150 basis points to 18.5%, exceeding the preview’s expected 80–120 basis-point expansion range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin expanded 150 basis points to 18.5% while operating income grew 23%, both ahead of plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating margin | +80–120bps constant currency”; the preview says this “implies roughly 17.4–17.8%.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year gross-margin outlook to roughly 50–70 basis points of expansion from “modest” expansion, a firmer outlook than the preview’s discussion of tariff and second-half margin caution had indicated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year gross margin outlook was raised to roughly 50-70 bps of expansion, up from prior guidance of modest expansion.”

surprises.description: Management reported 1.5 million new DTC customers and growth above 20% in women’s apparel, outerwear, and handbags, outpacing total company growth; the preview anticipated healthy DTC performance but did not flag this level of customer acquisition or category growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company added 1.5 million new DTC customers and grew high-potential categories (women's apparel, outerwear, handbags) more than 20%, outpacing total company growth.”

in_line: The FY27 constant-currency revenue guide rose to 5%–6% from 4%–5%, broadly matching the preview’s expectation of a raise toward about 6%.
The FY27 operating-margin expansion guide rose to 60–80 basis points from 40–60 basis points, matching the buy-side range cited in the preview.
China’s full-year growth is expected to moderate to around the mid-teens, consistent with the preview’s mid-teens guide and the anticipated tough comparison.

surprises.description: Adjusted core EPS was $1.19, above the preview’s roughly $0.90 consensus estimate (and above the cited $1.11 estimate from some feeds).
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted core EPS increased 3% to $1.19.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS, adjusted core (Q2) … Consensus ~$0.90 (some feeds $1.11).”

surprises.description: GAAP diluted EPS was only $0.09, far below the preview’s derived $0.50–$0.65 estimate, as $23 million of legacy-fraud-related charges and operating costs weighed on reported earnings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported diluted EPS was only $0.09 due to $23 million of charges and operating costs tied to legacy fraudulent problem loans.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS, GAAP diluted (Q2) … My derived estimate: $0.50–0.65.”

surprises.description: The company expects another $12 million to $16 million of credit-related charges in Q3 to complete Fannie Mae’s review, contrary to the preview’s expectation of no new charges. Management did say it anticipates no further loan repurchases from either GSE.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An additional $12 million to $16 million in credit-related charges in Q3 2026 to finalize Fannie Mae’s review, with no further loan repurchases anticipated from either GSE.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “repurchase exposure at or below $165M with no new charges” as a key catalyst and said the bull case expected “no new charges.”

surprises.description: Transaction volume was $14.4 billion, below the preview’s $15.5–$16.5 billion base-case range, although it remained above the preview’s bear-case threshold. Financing volume grew, but the preview had already expected refinancing-led activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 transaction volume rose 3% year-over-year to $14.4 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case projected “Volume $15.5–16.5B”; its bear case was “Below $14.0B.”

surprises.description: Management said 95% of losses recognized so far came from a small group of fraudulent sponsors and a banking team no longer at the firm, and that it found no similar issues elsewhere. That provides more specific reassurance about the scope of the fraud problem than the preview had anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “95% of losses recognized to date relate to a small group of fraudulent sponsors and one banking team no longer with the firm, and no similar issues were found elsewhere in the portfolio.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s concern that at-risk defaults and reserves had risen, management described the at-risk portfolio as strong, citing only 28 basis points in default, a 2.0x weighted average debt service coverage ratio, and a 61% weighted average underwritten loan-to-value.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The at-risk portfolio remains strong with just 28 basis points in default, a two-times weighted average debt service coverage ratio, and a 61% weighted average underwritten loan-to-value.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “At-risk defaults rose to 14 loans / $167.5M UPB from 8 / $108.5M” and that “the trend is negative.”

in_line: The $0.68 quarterly dividend was maintained, as the preview noted that the dividend had been affirmed in Q1 and flagged it as a potential capital-allocation watch item.

Management’s conditional outlook—toward the lower end of original guidance if current market conditions persist—was consistent with the preview’s base case that the company could be on track but weighted toward the second half, with a low-end outcome plausible.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.75, far above the preview’s $0.93 consensus estimate. The call said adjusted net income doubled, while EPS grew 33% because equity issued for the PAG acquisition increased the share count.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income rose 101% to $55 million” and “adjusted diluted EPS grew only 33% to $1.75 due to share dilution from the equity-funded PAG acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 EPS ... $0.93 (10 analysts).”

surprises.description: Revenue of $449 million exceeded the preview’s $425 million consensus estimate by $24 million, or about 5.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $449 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue ... $425.0M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA and margin came in above even the preview’s bull-case thresholds: $86 million versus $84 million or more, and a 19.2% margin versus 18.9% or more. The margin also exceeded the prior full-year guidance range’s 18.5% upper end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled, rising 98% to a record $86 million,” with “adjusted EBITDA margin expanding approximately 320 basis points to a record 19.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Bull scenario: “$84M+ (18.9%+).” Base scenario: “$78M–$81M (18.1%–18.5%).”

surprises.description: VSE raised both full-year revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance, rather than merely reaffirming the existing outlook. The preview characterized a reaffirm-only outcome as a mild negative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance to 61%-64% (from 57%-61%) and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 18.7%-19% (from 18.1%-18.5%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “FY26 guide: reaffirm or raise” as a key watch and said “a reaffirm-only outcome is a mild negative”; its base scenario was “FY guide reaffirmed, not raised.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was positive rather than another large outflow after the prior quarter’s negative $68.7 million. The call also expected stronger generation in the second half as working-capital intensity eases, though Q2 FCF was only about 34% of adjusted EBITDA excluding PAG transaction costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 free cash flow was ~$19 million” and “stronger generation [is] expected in the second half as working capital intensity eases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “A second large outflow would undercut the ‘one-off’ explanation and slow deleveraging,” after Q1 free cash flow of “-$68.7M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted net leverage was already 2.4x at quarter-end, below the preview’s below-2.5x year-end goal. That put the company ahead of the stated deleveraging target several months early.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net leverage of 2.4x came in better than pro forma guidance, with management expecting further deleveraging in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “a goal of below 2.5x by year-end” and said this was the “first post-close datapoint.”

surprises.description: Management said PAG synergies would mostly benefit 2027 rather than 2026, and that the guidance increase was driven primarily by core-business strength. The preview highlighted PAG contribution and synergy quantification, but did not specify a timing expectation for those synergies.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PAG synergies (initial run-rate expectation of ~$15 million) will mostly benefit 2027 rather than 2026,” while “the guidance raise [was] driven primarily by core business strength rather than synergy capture.”

surprises.description: The Pratt & Whitney Canada APU distribution agreement ramped ahead of expectations, an operational positive not specifically anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Pratt & Whitney Canada APU distribution agreement ramped ahead of expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Ramped ahead of expectations.”

surprises.description: The preview expected adjusted EPS of about $0.11, but HP reported a $0.11 loss per share excluding the Utica Square sale gain and other selected items. The headline $0.74 EPS therefore obscured a weaker underlying result than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 EPS was $0.74 per diluted share, but excluding the Utica Square sale gain and select items, the company recorded a loss of $0.11 per share.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA of $236 million was well above the roughly $208 million midpoint implied by the preview’s guidance-based estimate, beating even the top of its implied $190–225 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 adjusted EBITDA was $236 million, coming in above the implied midpoint of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance implies ~$190–225M (midpoint ~$208M), derived by the preview author, not company-published.”

surprises.description: HP’s Q4 North America Solutions direct-margin outlook of $245–255 million is stronger than the preview’s in-line outlook and comfortably above the roughly $230 million level it flagged as a downside risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “set Q4 NAS direct margin guidance at $245-255 million on 145-151 rigs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “An FQ4 NAS margin guide below ~$230M would put the $40 targets at risk”; the base scenario anticipated “FQ4 in line.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for NAS margin per day near $17,500–18,000, with $18,000+ confirming pricing strength. HP reported $18,700 per day, above that range, while its $241 million direct margin was just above the prior $230–240 million guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North America Solutions averaged 142 rigs with direct margins of $241 million and industry-leading margins of $18,700 per day, up over $1,000 sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A reading toward $18,000+ would confirm the pricing story”; the base scenario expected “NAS margin ~$17.5–18.0k/day.”

surprises.description: HP’s North America rig ramp appears stronger than the preview’s Q3 range alone implied: it exited with 147 rigs running, expects to surpass 150, and raised full-year rig-count guidance to 140–144. The 95% super-spec utilization also indicates limited idle capacity in that fleet.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company exited Q3 with 147 rigs running in the Lower 48 and is on track to surpass 150 rigs, at least 17 more than the February trough, with super-spec fleet utilization already at 95%”; “H&P raised full-year North America Solutions rig count guidance to 140-144 rigs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “North America Solutions: 137–143 rigs” for Q3; the preview also noted management had called FQ2 “the trough quarter for North America rig count and margins.”

surprises.description: HP described a path to an International Solutions quarterly direct-margin run rate of at least $45 million, well above the preview’s roughly $20 million base-case expectation and the prior Q3 guide’s $32 million upper end. Argentina is a key part of that outlook, with plans to grow from nine rigs to 15 FlexRigs at margins in line with the U.S. Lower 48.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company remains confident in reaching a quarterly International Solutions direct margin run rate of at least $45 million, driven by Argentina growth”; “In Argentina's Vaca Muerta, H&P holds roughly 25% market share with nine rigs and plans to expand to 15 FlexRigs within six to eight months, with margins in line with U.S. Lower 48 levels.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “International Solutions: 58–68 rigs, direct margin $12–32M”; the base scenario expected “Int'l ~$20M.”

surprises.description: Saudi reactivations fell behind plan: only five of seven suspended rigs had restarted, and the remaining two were left out of Q4 guidance. This leaves less near-term activity than the preview’s focus on reactivations might have suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Saudi rig reactivations lagged plans, with only five of seven suspended rigs restarted (22 total rigs in the Kingdom), and the remaining two rigs excluded from Q4 guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Saudi reactivations and nine additional legacy KCAD suspensions (total in-country suspensions 26 rigs) drive” the International margin range; the preview also flagged the “Timing of the nine additional Saudi suspensions.”

surprises.description: HP set out specific cost-reduction and asset-sale targets to help pay down its 2027 bond and reach 1x net debt-to-EBITDA. The preview highlighted the bond and deleveraging as an issue to watch but did not anticipate these quantified measures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management targets reducing corporate costs by an annualized $40 million by end of 2027 and raising over $160 million from asset sales, while prioritizing paying down the $350 million bond due end of 2027 to reach 1x net debt-to-EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch the path to the $350M bond maturing end-2027.”

in_line: Q3 NAS averaged 142 rigs, within the preview’s 137–143 rig guidance range.
The $241 million Q3 NAS direct margin was essentially at the top of the prior $230–240 million guidance range.

HP maintained its $100 million dividend and indicated that expanded returns, including buybacks, are for 2028 onward, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the base dividend would be reaffirmed and incremental returns were a “2028 event.”

surprises.description: Sabre reported Q2 revenue of $712 million, about $15 million above the preview’s $697.4 million consensus and ahead of the company’s flat-to-nominal growth guide. The beat was positive but modest relative to the consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 4% year-on-year to $712 million, exceeding management's guidance of flat to nominal growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $697.4M (+1.5% Y/Y)” and company guidance: “Flat-to-nominal growth.”

surprises.description: Normalized adjusted EBITDA was $151 million, $21 million above the roughly $130 million expectation. The strong EBITDA result also came with a 272-basis-point expansion in adjusted EBITDA margin, rather than merely reflecting higher revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Normalized adjusted EBITDA rose 19% to $151 million versus a guide of approximately $130 million”; “adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 272 basis points to 21.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pro forma Adj. EBITDA | ~$130M”; the preview also said to watch for “rate and cost offsets.”

surprises.description: Air distribution bookings grew 1%, ahead of the preview’s near-flat expectation and the downside scenario it considered plausible after Amadeus’s weak results. Sabre also said its bookings growth had outpaced the broader industry by about 600 basis points since late 2025.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Air distribution bookings grew 1% year-on-year, beating expectations,” and growth “has outpaced the broader industry by approximately 600 basis points since late 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed bookings at “~flat” and company guidance as “Near flat”; it said “-2% to -4% would be consistent with the read-through” from Amadeus.

surprises.description: Sabre raised its full-year EBITDA outlook to approximately $600 million from roughly $585 million and improved its free-cash-flow outlook to about negative $65 million from negative $70 million. Both moved in a better direction than the preview’s expected reaffirmation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sabre raised full-year 2026 pro forma adjusted EBITDA guidance to approximately $600 million and improved free cash flow guidance to approximately negative $65 million (from negative $70 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY2026 pro forma adjusted EBITDA at “~$585M” and free cash flow at “~-$70M”; it framed the catalysts as whether each would be “reaffirmed or trimmed.”

surprises.description: Management quantified a 300-to-400-basis-point drag on Q2 bookings from fuel prices and the Middle East conflict, with fuel the larger factor. The preview focused on Middle East disruption but did not identify higher fuel prices as the larger source of pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The combined global impact of higher fuel prices and the Middle East conflict was 300 to 400 basis points on Q2 bookings, with fuel being the larger factor and impacts more acute in EMEA and Asia Pacific.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “Middle East disruption” and noted “about 11% of air bookings tied to the Middle East.”

surprises.description: Corporate volumes remained resilient and offset weaker leisure demand, reversing the pattern from last year. The preview focused on industry disruption and the need for bookings to recover, but did not flag this corporate-versus-leisure offset.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Corporate volumes, representing nearly half (about 45%) of Marketplace bookings versus 25%-30% industry-wide, remained resilient and offset softness in leisure demand, reversing last year's trend.”

surprises.description: Hotel-related revenue growth accelerated to 11%, with the attach rate reaching approximately 35%. The preview did not anticipate this improvement in hotel-related business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hotel-related revenue growth accelerated to 11% year-on-year with attach rate improving to approximately 35%.”

surprises.description: Payment Suite gross spend exceeded $6 billion, up more than 30% year-on-year and above a $25 billion annualized pace. The preview did not identify this level of payment volume growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Payment Suite gross spend exceeded $6 billion (up over 30% year-on-year), reaching over $25 billion annualized.”

surprises.description: Sabre doubled the number of active agentic AI pilot and production partners from 30 to 60 and signed a new African carrier to SabreMosaic, indicating platform adoption not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sabre doubled its active agentic AI pilot and production partners from 30 to 60 in Q2” and “signed a new African carrier onto its SabreMosaic platform.”

surprises.description: Sabre extended its AR securitization facility to September 2029, leaving no debt maturities until 2029. The preview raised leverage and possible deleveraging as issues but did not anticipate this maturity extension.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Extended its AR securitization facility to September 2029, leaving no debt maturities until 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “roughly 6.2x net leverage” and listed “any deleveraging or strategic update” as a catalyst.

in_line: Airline Technology revenue was $135 million, which the call described as in line with expectations, although it was down year-on-year because of license-fee timing.
Sabre reaffirmed its full-year revenue and air distribution bookings growth outlook, in line with the preview’s expectation that those outlooks would be maintained.

surprises.description: US Foods generated $604 million of adjusted EBITDA, above the preview’s $585–595 million estimate, and expanded adjusted EBITDA margin by 29 basis points to a record 5.7%. Growth was 10.2%, ahead of the preview’s derived 7–8% estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 10.2% to a record $604 million with margin expanding 29 basis points to a record 5.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$585–595M (my estimate)” and implied growth of “+7–8%.”

surprises.description: Independent restaurant case growth reached 5.1%, above the preview’s 4.0–4.5% base scenario and crossing its 5% bull trigger. The preview identified this as the central volume debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Independent restaurant case growth accelerated to 5.1%, the strongest since Q4 2023 and the fifth consecutive quarter of acceleration, with net new account generation the strongest in three years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “+5% or more is the bull trigger” and its base scenario assumed “Independent cases +4.0–4.5%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.44, above the $1.37 consensus estimate and the preview’s base-scenario range of $1.35–1.40.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS jumped 21% to $1.44.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS $1.37”; base scenario “$1.35–1.40.”

surprises.description: The company kept its full-year guidance ranges intact rather than narrowing them toward the lower half, as the preview expected. That left the 9–13% EBITDA-growth and 18–24% EPS-growth ranges unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed full-year FY2026 guidance of 4-6% net sales growth, 9-13% adjusted EBITDA growth, 18-24% adjusted EPS growth, and 2.5-4.5% total case volume growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “I expect the range to narrow toward the lower half.”

surprises.description: Fuel surcharge recovery was about 70%, far above the 30–40% recovery rate described in the preview, and helped offset higher fuel costs. This contributed to the stronger-than-expected Q2 EBITDA result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Q2 EBITDA beat was driven by fuel surcharge recovery of about 70% (versus a typical 30-40%) that offset higher fuel costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “USFD recovers only about 30–40% of increases through surcharge with a one-month lag.”

surprises.description: Some strategic vendor-management gains were pulled forward from the second half, making the Q2 contribution stronger but leaving less of that benefit for the H2 bridge the preview expected to deliver roughly 10.9% EBITDA growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Strategic vendor management gains pulled forward from the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said reaching the 9% full-year EBITDA-growth floor required “H2 adj. EBITDA of about $1.10B (+10.9% Y/Y).”

surprises.description: Pronto’s 2027 sales estimate was raised to over $1.7 billion from the prior $1.5 billion estimate, an improvement not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pronto is now live in 52 markets and is expected to generate approximately $1.3 billion in sales this year, with the 2027 estimate raised to over $1.7 billion from a prior $1.5 billion.”

surprises.description: The company bought back $374 million of shares in Q2, substantially above the $125 million repurchased in Q1 noted in the preview; year-to-date repurchases reached about $500 million while leverage remained within its target range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $374 million of shares in Q2 (about $500 million year-to-date) and ended the quarter with net leverage of 2.6x, within its 2-3x target range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Buyback of $125M in Q1” and “$1B remaining,” but gave no Q2 repurchase estimate.

surprises.description: The new seller compensation plan went live company-wide in June without year-over-year attrition increasing, although management said most local sales staff will take 2–3 years to transition fully to variable pay. The preview did not address the rollout or its timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new seller compensation plan went live company-wide in June with flat year-over-year attrition, and management expects it to take 2 to 3 years for most of the local sales force to fully transition to 100% variable pay.”

in_line: Q2 net sales were about $10.5 billion, essentially matching the preview’s ~$10.48 billion estimate.

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA was $39.9 million, slightly below the preview’s approximate $41 million estimate. The gap was small, and the result was roughly flat year over year, as the preview expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total company Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $39.9 million, down slightly from $41 million a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (derived) ~$41M”; the preview describes this as “approximate.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY26 consolidated adjusted EBITDA guidance to a $230 million midpoint from the prior $224 million midpoint, rather than simply reaffirming the range as the preview considered likely. The increase was driven by Plant Nutrition, whose guidance rose to $49–57 million from $43–47 million as Q3 EBITDA grew 32% despite lower revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year consolidated adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint to $230 million (range $218-242 million), driven by Plant Nutrition outperformance”; Plant Nutrition guidance “was raised to $49-57 million from the prior $43-47 million,” with Q3 adjusted EBITDA “up 32% to $15 million despite a 16% revenue decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a “reaffirmation is the likely outcome” for FY26 total adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$212–236M”; Plant Nutrition guidance was “$43–47M.”

surprises.description: Salt delivered weaker results and a slightly lower full-year outlook: Q3 adjusted EBITDA fell 15%, and the guidance ceiling was reduced from $240 million to $236 million because Goderich production and distribution costs were higher than expected. This contrasts with the preview’s likely-reaffirmation case and its warning that costs were not improving as quickly as hoped.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Salt segment adjusted EBITDA fell 15% to $38.9 million and guidance was narrowed lower to $225-236 million (from $225-240 million) due to higher-than-expected production and distribution costs at Goderich.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a “reaffirmation is the likely outcome” for Salt guidance of “$225–240M,” while flagging that cost improvements were “not as quickly as we would have liked.”

surprises.description: The first read on the 2026–27 de-icing bid season was more specific and stronger than the preview’s base case of constructive but unquantified pricing: management reported roughly double-digit price increases. Historically low industry inventories after a strong winter were cited as support.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 2026-27 highway de-icing bid season is delivering price increases of roughly double digits, supported by historically low industry inventories after a strong winter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected the bid season to be “described as constructive but unquantified”; its bull case contemplated “higher price and tender sizes.”

surprises.description: Management expects to commit to a lower salt demand profile for FY27 if winter weather is normalized, prioritizing per-unit margin growth over volume. The preview focused on the bid season’s price and volume read but did not anticipate this explicit shift in planned demand profile.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects to commit to a reduced salt demand profile for fiscal 2027 assuming normalized winter weather, prioritizing per-unit margin expansion over volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified FY27 de-icing bid-season “pricing” as the main driver and listed “price and volume” as a catalyst, but did not describe a planned reduction in demand profile.

surprises.description: A new tariff exposure emerged that the preview did not flag: Canadian tariffs on goods shipped to the U.S. take effect August 19, with most exposure tied to Goderich highway salt. The company said contract pass-through provisions meaningfully reduce the risk, but do not make the exposure irrelevant.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Canadian tariffs on goods shipped to the U.S. take effect August 19th with most exposure tied to Goderich highway de-icing salt, though the company believes pass-through contract provisions meaningfully reduce this risk.”

surprises.description: The planned Goderich mill project is being delayed, with an updated timeline not expected until early next year. The preview discussed mining costs and execution but did not flag a project delay.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The planned Goderich mill project is being delayed with an updated timeline expected early next year.”

surprises.description: COO Patrick Marin departed and Brandon Reisner replaced him; this management change was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “COO Patrick Marin departed and was replaced by Brandon Reisner.”

in_line: The preview expected deleveraging to be largely complete. Net leverage was 2.8x versus 4.3x a year earlier, and the Board is considering expanded capital-allocation options; no specific buyback, dividend, or capital-return framework was reported.

surprises.description: AmeriGas EBIT fell by $25 million year over year, mainly because of warmer weather and customer attrition, rather than narrowing its loss as the preview’s scenario expected. Retail gallons were down 10%, or 6% on a weather-adjusted basis excluding the Hawaii divestiture.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 total reportable segment EBIT fell to $58 million from $72 million a year earlier, driven primarily by a $25 million decline at AmeriGas from warmer weather and customer attrition.” “AmeriGas Q3 retail gallons fell 10% due to April temperatures being 16% warmer than the prior year, but declined only 6% on a weather-adjusted basis excluding the Hawaii divestiture.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “AmeriGas loss narrows”; it also said AmeriGas needed to show progress after turnaround progress had been “slower than expected.”

surprises.description: Year-to-date adjusted EPS was $3.17, below the preview’s stated $3.35, a shortfall of $0.18. The call attributed the decline largely to the absence of prior-year investment tax credits and higher interest expense.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date adjusted diluted EPS declined to $3.17 from $3.55, largely due to the absence of prior-year investment tax credits and higher interest expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “YTD FY26 adjusted EPS is $3.35.”

surprises.description: AmeriGas had already reduced leverage to 4.3x, down from 4.7x at the prior-quarter reference point, and cut net debt by about $270 million in one quarter. That is meaningful progress toward the preview’s sub-4.0x year-end target, although the target has not yet been reached.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AmeriGas reduced net debt by approximately $270 million versus the prior quarter and lowered leverage to 4.3x, its lowest point in 10 years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited AmeriGas net leverage of 4.7x and a “sub-4.0x FY-end target,” and identified the leverage path toward that target as a key item to watch.

surprises.description: Management now expects AmeriGas to resume meaningful cash distributions to UGI in fiscal 2027, a new prospective source of parent cash flow. The prospect is conditional on leverage falling below 4x by year-end and AmeriGas generating over $100 million of free cash flow this year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects AmeriGas to resume meaningful cash distributions to the parent in fiscal 2027 for the first time in years, contingent on leverage falling below 4x by year-end and generating over $100 million of free cash flow this year.”

surprises.description: A Pennsylvania gas rate-case settlement was recommended for approval before the preview’s expected October decision, with two scheduled increases totaling $65 million. That is below the company’s $99.4 million request, but the recommendation without modification and the specified increases provide a concrete outcome; the settlement also includes a stay-out through January 2029.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The UGI Utilities gas rate case settlement, recommended for approval without modification, provides a two-step $65 million rate increase ($40 million in October 2026, $25 million in October 2027) with a stay-out through January 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “PUC decision [was] due Oct 29, 2026” and noted a “$99.4M (8.05%) request.”

surprises.description: AmeriGas’s year-to-date net customer attrition improved to approximately 2%, while lost-time injuries fell 50% and Net Promoter Score rose 63% versus fiscal 2024. These operating indicators suggest better turnaround progress than the preview’s account of slower-than-expected progress implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date, AmeriGas net customer attrition improved to approximately 2%, its lowest in a long time, with lost-time injuries down 50% and Net Promoter Score up 63% versus fiscal 2024.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the prior guidance cut cited “AmeriGas turnaround progress slower than expected.”

surprises.description: UGI maintained its 5% to 7% consolidated EPS CAGR through 2029 even as it pushed expected midstream growth more toward the middle and latter part of the period. The maintained long-term growth outlook contrasts with the delayed Appalachian production and investment timing highlighted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed its 5% to 7% consolidated EPS CAGR through 2029, though midstream growth is now expected to be more mid- to back-end loaded due to Appalachian production timing and well-pad expansions starting in fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted delayed Midstream growth investments and lower Appalachian production, and said the bigger event was the FY27 outlook, where consensus implied about 16% growth.

in_line: UGI reaffirmed fiscal 2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance of $2.75 to $2.90, as the preview’s main scenario was that guidance would be reaffirmed.

surprises.description: Watts reported Q2 revenue of $763 million and organic growth of 12%, well above the preview’s roughly $726 million revenue consensus and 4%–8% organic-growth guidance. The organic-growth result was also far above the preview’s approximately 6% guide midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 organic sales rose 12% to a record $763 million (up 19% reported).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue ... Consensus $725.8M ... $726.0M”; “Organic sales growth | +4% to +8% | ~+6% (guide midpoint).”

surprises.description: Watts raised FY26 organic-sales growth guidance to 8%–11%, versus the prior 2%–6% range, and raised reported-sales growth guidance to 14%–17% from 8%–12%. This was a much larger upward revision than the preview’s expectation that holding or modestly adjusting the old organic-growth range would be the key debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year organic sales growth guidance to 8%-11%, a more than 5-point increase to the prior midpoint, and reported sales growth guidance to 14%-17%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 organic growth | +2% to +6%”; “Full-year FY26 guidance ... reported sales +8% to +12%”; “Holding the guide a second quarter would be hard to accept without a clear explanation.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $3.66, substantially above the preview’s $3.33–$3.34 consensus. The preview’s bull-case EPS range topped out at $3.70, so the result was near that optimistic scenario rather than the base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew 18% year-over-year to $3.66.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS ... Consensus $3.34 ... $3.33–3.34”; the preview’s base case was “$3.35–3.48.”

surprises.description: Adjusted operating margin reached 21%, above the preview’s 20.0%–20.6% company guidance and approximately 20.3% implied consensus. The year-over-year decline was attributed mainly to acquisition dilution and comparison with a prior-year one-time price/cost benefit, issues the preview specifically wanted explained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin declined 60 basis points to 21%, primarily due to 70 bps of acquisition dilution and a difficult comparison against a prior-year one-time price/cost benefit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating margin | 20.0% to 20.6% | ~20.3% (implied)”; “Margin bridge on the call. How much of the year-over-year decline comes from the non-recurring prior-year price/cost benefit versus underlying performance.”

surprises.description: Data center sales more than tripled year over year, and management now expects full-year sales to reach the mid- to high-single digits as a share of company sales. That exceeded the preview’s focus on a high-double-digit growth reaffirmation and its reference to data center sales having more than doubled in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data center sales more than tripled year-over-year”; “Full-year data center sales are now expected to reach mid- to high single digits as a percentage of company sales, up from 3% last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Data center growth and the ‘high double-digit’ reaffirmation”; “Data center sales more than doubled year over year.”

surprises.description: Watts doubled its estimated served addressable data center market to about $2 billion, adding Europe, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia and incorporating the shift toward liquid cooling. The preview cited a greater-than-$1-billion addressable market, so the revised estimate was materially higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company doubled its estimated served addressable data center market to approximately $2 billion by adding Europe, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia and reflecting the shift toward liquid cooling.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management pointed to a >$1B addressable market.”

surprises.description: The strong Q2 sales figure included about $20 million of demand pulled forward: half ahead of a June SAP implementation and half from data center projects shipped early. The preview highlighted order timing as a risk to watch, but did not anticipate this specific amount of Q2 pull-forward.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 results included roughly $20 million of pull-forward demand—about $10 million ahead of a June SAP implementation and about $10 million of data center projects shipped early across the Americas and APMEA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any deceleration, order-timing commentary, or hedged language on the $2.4B 2028 target is the biggest de-rating risk.”

surprises.description: A favorable tax-rate effect helped the EPS result: the tax rate benefited by 210 basis points from reversing a prior-year tax liability, a nonrecurring item not anticipated in the preview. This makes part of the large EPS beat attributable to a one-time benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew 18% year-over-year to $3.66, aided by a 210 bps favorable tax rate driven by a nonrecurring benefit from reversing a prior-year tax liability.”

surprises.description: APMEA organic sales grew 31%, led by China data center demand, a region-specific growth result the preview did not discuss. The preview explicitly noted that it lacked segment-level detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APMEA organic sales grew 31% led by China data center demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “I did not cover ... segment-level detail here.”

surprises.description: Residential and non-institutional new construction remained soft, and single-family conditions were slightly worse than in the prior quarter. This adds a weaker end-market detail not addressed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Residential and non-institutional new construction remain soft, with single-family conditions slightly worse than last quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “I did not cover ... segment-level detail here.”

surprises.description: Year-to-date free cash flow was still below the prior-year level, with higher receivables and strategic inventory investment weighing on it. The preview had emphasized the need for a working-capital reversal after Q1 and warned that another weak FCF quarter would be a concern; the supplied results do not show that the build had reversed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date free cash flow declined to $98 million from $105 million due to higher receivables and strategic inventory investment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow. After the Q1 build, the ≥90% conversion target needs a large H2 catch-up. A second weak FCF quarter would hurt”; “Whether the Q1 build reverses.”

surprises.description: IBP reported $778 million of Q2 revenue, about 5% above the preview’s $740.4–743.3 million consensus range. That also turned the expected year-over-year decline into 2% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated Q2 2026 net revenue rose 2% to $778 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue | $740.4M – $743.3M” and “Implied Y/Y | −2.3% to −2.6%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $2.91 substantially exceeded the preview’s $2.54–$2.57 consensus range, by roughly 13%–15%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income of $78 million, or $2.91 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $2.54 – $2.57.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $131 million, above the preview’s estimated $115–$120 million. Its 16.9% margin also exceeded the preview’s base-case 15.5%–16.0% range and landed in its bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $131 million (16.9% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$115–120M”; the base scenario projected “15.5–16.0%” EBITDA margin and the bull scenario “16.5–17.0%.”

surprises.description: New residential same-branch sales fell 6%, better than the preview’s implied decline of roughly 8%–10%. This was a milder contraction than the preview’s central residential expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New residential same-branch sales fell 6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus revenue of ~$742M implicitly needs residential same-branch in roughly the −8% to −10% range.”

surprises.description: Heavy commercial same-branch growth was about 16%, below the preview’s bull-case expectation of more than 20%; management also expects the growth rate to moderate in the second half against tough comparisons.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Heavy commercial delivered roughly 16% same-branch sales growth … though management expects the growth rate to moderate against tough comps in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bull scenario cited “heavy commercial above +20%”; the preview also flagged “Heavy commercial growth and backlog” as a key metric.

surprises.description: The other segment grew sharply—50% reported and 28% same-branch—and its gross margin improved to 24.7%. The faster growth in this lower-margin segment nevertheless created a 40-basis-point mix headwind to consolidated gross margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The other segment … grew 50% on a reported basis and 28% same-branch, with gross margins improving to 24.7% from 23%, but remaining well below the installation segment’s 36.5%”; adjusted gross margin faced “a 40 basis point mix headwind from faster growth in the lower-margin other segment.”

surprises.description: Multifamily sales turned positive in June and July and the contract backlog was growing, an encouraging demand development not identified in the preview’s watch list. IBP’s concentration in the South—about 60% of its multifamily revenue versus 43% of national completions—was also newly reported.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Multifamily sales inflected positively in June and July, with a growing contract backlog,” and “the South Census region accounts for ~60% of IBP’s multifamily revenue versus only 43% of national completions.”

surprises.description: Management said the roughly 25% spray-foam material cost increase was being passed through, but warned that timing could make it a Q3 margin drag. The preview highlighted the price increases and the pass-through question, but did not flag a near-term timing lag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A ~25% spray foam material cost increase is being passed through,” expected to be “at least margin neutral longer term but potentially a margin drag in Q3 due to pass-through timing lag.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Spray-foam manufacturers announced 25% price increases. Watch whether IBP passes these through.”

surprises.description: Management indicated it would consider leverage up to 3x for the right commercial or adjacent platform acquisition, above the preview’s stated 2.0x target. Current leverage was also 1.34x, slightly above the preview’s 1.2x figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt to trailing 12-month adjusted EBITDA leverage was 1.34x … well below the 2x target, with willingness to go to 3x for the right platform deal”; management is “targeting a larger commercial/adjacent ‘platform’ deal.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net leverage is 1.2x against a 2.0x target”; the preview also listed “M&A pace” as a key metric and said the 2026 target was “at least $100M of acquired annual revenue.”

surprises.description: Q2 repurchases totaled $76 million, well above the $25.4 million of Q1 buybacks cited in the preview. The preview had flagged a larger program as a possible capital-allocation signal but did not anticipate this reported amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased ~365,000 shares for $76 million in Q2 (with ~$398 million remaining authorization).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 buybacks were $25.4M for 91K shares. A larger program would signal management’s view on valuation.”

in_line: Adjusted gross margin was 33.3%, consistent with the preview’s 33%-or-more key threshold and within its projected ranges; the preview identified the 32–34% full-year range as the guidance benchmark, but the supplied call facts do not state whether that range was reaffirmed.
The Q3 dividend was $0.39 per share, up more than 5% year over year, as the preview described.
Management continued to expect at least $100 million of annual acquired revenue in 2026, in line with the preview’s stated target.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue exceeded the $2.41 billion consensus and the top of Howmet’s $2.39–$2.41 billion guidance range. Organic growth also accelerated to 21% from 19% in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 24% year-over-year (21% organic), with organic growth accelerating from 19% in Q1”; revenue exceeded “the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Company guidance (Q2) $2.39–2.41bn | Consensus (Zacks, Aug 3) $2.41bn.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $1.33 was well above both the $1.23 consensus and the $1.24 top of guidance. The preview’s bull scenario topped out at $1.36, but its base case was only $1.25–$1.28.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS came in at $1.33, up 46% year-over-year”; EPS exceeded “the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS | Company guidance (Q2) $1.22–1.24 | Consensus (Zacks, Aug 3) $1.23”; the base scenario was “$1.25–1.28.”

surprises.description: Howmet raised full-year revenue, EBITDA and EPS guidance substantially beyond the preview’s expected raise: EPS guidance moved to $5.27, versus the preview’s bull case of about $5.10+ and base case of $5.00–$5.05.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year guidance was raised across the board to revenue of $10.05 billion, EBITDA of $3.23 billion, and EPS of $5.27.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Q2 beat alone implies an FY raise of about $0.05 to $0.10 on EPS if H2 holds flat”; scenarios projected a raise to “~$5.10+” in the bull case and “$5.00–5.05” in the base case.

surprises.description: Q2 EBITDA growth and margin both beat the high end of guidance. The margin reached 32.1%, above the 32.0% upper bound, while EBITDA grew 39% against revenue growth of 24%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EBITDA margin expanded 340 basis points to 32.1% and EBITDA grew 39%, outpacing revenue”; EBITDA and margin exceeded “the high end of guidance.”
