surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | Company guidance (Q2) $760–770mn”; “Adj. EBITDA margin | Company guidance (Q2) 31.8–32.0%.”

surprises.description: Full-year free-cash-flow guidance rose to $1.9 billion, above the preview’s prior guidance range of $1.7–$1.8 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year free cash flow guidance of $1.9 billion (±$50 million) at 90% conversion.”

surprises.description: The reported total-spares mix was about 22% of first-half revenue, below the preview’s 24% watch point for Engine Products spares. Spares still grew 37%, but the reported mix and the preview’s metric are not perfectly like-for-like in scope or period.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total spares revenue across commercial aero, defense aero and gas turbine rose 37% to approximately $560 million, now representing about 22% of total revenue in the first half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for spares at or above 24%.”

surprises.description: Howmet bought back $800 million of stock year-to-date—more than in all of 2025—rather than showing an evident slowdown in repurchases at current prices, a possibility the preview specifically raised.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $800 million of stock year-to-date at an average $248 (exceeding all of 2025).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether buyback pace slows at current prices.”

surprises.description: The call highlighted data-center electricity demand as a driver of IGT’s 38% revenue surge, a demand source the preview had not identified while focusing on customer agreements and capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gas turbine (IGT) revenue surged 38%, driven by data center electricity demand,” and Howmet “holds over 50% global market share in IGT turbine blades.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on IGT customer agreements, noting “Six of seven major customers have finalized agreements,” and watched for “a seventh signing or new committed capacity.”

surprises.description: Howmet disclosed capital spending above $500 million for 2026, a further significant step-up in 2027, and a newly approved plant. The preview did not flag this scale of investment, which is intended to support IGT and aerospace capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Capital expenditure is now expected to exceed $500 million in 2026 with a further significant step-up signaled for 2027,” supporting expansions “including a newly approved plant.”

in_line: CAM’s lower margins diluted Fastening Systems sequentially, consistent with the preview’s warning that CAM carried a lower margin than legacy Fastening Systems. The call also kept the expected 2027 benefit: synergies mainly in 2027 and EPS turning positive from the deal in 2027 after being roughly breakeven in 2026.
IGT growth remained close to the prior-quarter pace: revenue rose 38% versus 39% growth in Q1, consistent with the preview’s focus on sustained IGT strength.

surprises.description: Lee reported $5.2 million of net income, its first profitable quarter since 2024, versus the preview’s Q3 EPS consensus of a $0.16 loss. The call facts do not provide actual EPS, but the reported profit is a clear reversal from the expected loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 net income was $5.2 million, marking Lee's first profitable quarter since 2024.”

surprises.description: Lee raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook to 22%–28% growth, far above the prior mid-single-digit-growth guidance. The preview identified a double-digit-growth raise as the most likely positive surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook to growth of 22% to 28%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA: ‘Mid-single-digit % growth’”; “A raise to double-digit growth is the most likely positive surprise.”

surprises.description: Digital-only subscribers ended the quarter at 584,000, below the preview’s 591,000 comparison point and below its base case of roughly 590,000 subscribers holding steady. The count did remain above the preview’s bear-case threshold of 580,000.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with 584,000 digital-only subscribers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Digital-only subscribers vs. 591k”; the base case expected “Subscribers flat near 590k.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $18 million, above the preview’s roughly $17 million base estimate. Although $560,000 came from cyber-event business-interruption insurance, EBITDA still grew 19% year over year excluding those proceeds, showing stronger underlying growth than the preview’s clean-print threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 adjusted EBITDA grew 23% year-over-year to $18 million”; “Excluding $560,000 in cyber-event business interruption insurance proceeds, Q3 adjusted EBITDA still grew 19% year-over-year on underlying operational strength.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “Adj. EBITDA | ~$17M.” It said “about $17M with no insurance help is a solid print,” while $17 million including about $3 million of insurance would not be.

surprises.description: Cash costs fell 15%, or $19 million, and adjusted EBITDA margin improved 400 basis points. The preview specifically questioned whether newsroom reinvestment would interrupt cost reductions, but the reported figures show a substantial continued decline in costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 cash costs declined 15% ($19 million), driving a 400 basis point improvement in adjusted EBITDA margin, with year-to-date costs down $55 million (14%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Newsroom reinvestment. How much cost is coming back, and does it interrupt the cost-reduction trend?”

surprises.description: Lee entered a long-term management agreement with Hoffman Media Group that produces recurring fees and performance-based upside without requiring Lee to deploy capital. The preview focused on possible acquisition targets and funding plans, rather than a named capital-light management-fee arrangement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company entered a long-term, capital-light management agreement with Hoffman Media Group, generating recurring management fee revenue plus performance-based upside without deploying capital.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any move from concept to named targets, sizing, or funding would matter”; the catalyst checklist said to watch “Hoffmann's M&A commentary.”

surprises.description: Lee reported that digital revenue was 57% of company revenue, up 170 basis points year over year, and 76% of advertising revenue, with $284 million over the last 12 months. The preview discussed the digital growth story but gave no expectation for these revenue-mix or scale measures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Digital revenue reached 57% of total company revenue (up 170 basis points year-over-year) and 76% of advertising revenue, with $284 million in digital revenue over the last 12 months.”

surprises.description: Management said digital gross margin is expected to cover all SG&A within three years, a specific profitability milestone the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “expects digital gross margin to fully cover SG&A within three years.”

in_line: Quarter-end cash was $59 million, within the preview’s expected high-$50-million to low-$60-million range.

The preview anticipated the impact of the move from a 9% to a 5% interest rate showing up below EBITDA and in cash or earnings. The call reported a $4.6 million reduction in Q3 interest expense and expected annual savings of about $18 million.

surprises.description: Q2 production came in above the preview’s 34.3 MBoe/d guidance midpoint, and management guided to more than 35,000 boe/d in Q3. The 3% year-over-year increase despite no new drilling or acquisitions also contrasts with the preview’s expectation of a 5% sequential decline in Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 production reached 34,700 barrels of oil equivalent per day, up 3% year-over-year despite no new drilling or acquisitions, with Q3 guidance exceeding 35,000 boe/d.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Production ~34.3 MBoe/d midpoint (−5% q/q)”

surprises.description: Cash rose above $150 million and leverage was 1.2x, better than the preview’s 1.5x level to watch. Management also said it could potentially bring leverage below 1x by year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash on hand grew to over $150 million while net debt fell to $200 million, lowering the trailing 12-month net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio to 1.2x, with management targeting potentially under 1x by year-end 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch net debt/EBITDA against 1.5x.”

surprises.description: Management said successful surety litigation could produce claims reaching hundreds of millions of dollars, with antitrust damages trebled, and estimated resolution in roughly two years. The preview did not identify this potential legal recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Successful surety litigation could yield claims reaching hundreds of millions of dollars, with antitrust damages statutorily trebled, and expects resolution within roughly two years.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow rose 50% sequentially to $31 million, a stronger cash-generation result than the preview quantified or forecast while flagging free cash flow as a key metric.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow rose 50% sequentially to $31 million in Q2, totaling over $52 million for the first half of 2026.”

surprises.description: After Q2 LOE came in below guidance, management said Q3 LOE would rise to $73–81 million as deferred workover and facility maintenance is completed. The preview focused on Q2 costs and did not flag this expected Q3 increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 LOE came in at $72 million, below guidance, but is expected to rise to $73-81 million in Q3 due to deferred workover and facility maintenance work.”

surprises.description: Full-year capital spending is still guided at $20–25 million, but management said it is trending toward the high end as projects are accelerated in the strong pricing environment. The preview did not anticipate this spending update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 capital guidance is $20-25 million (excluding acquisitions), with spending trending toward the higher end as projects are accelerated in the strong pricing environment.”

surprises.description: Management said the company’s enterprise value is below its PDP PV-10, an asset-valuation claim the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management stated the company's enterprise value is below its PDP PV-10.”

surprises.description: Management said produced reserves over the past 10–15 years exceeded 1P reserve estimates by more than double, a favorable historical reserve-performance claim not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Actual produced reserves over the past 10-15 years have exceeded 1P reserve estimates by more than double.”

surprises.description: Management expressed a current preference for returning capital through dividends rather than buybacks. The preview anticipated a maintained dividend in its base scenario but did not identify this preference between dividends and repurchases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management indicated a preference for returning capital via dividends over buybacks currently.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: ... dividend maintained.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was over $54 million, broadly in line with the preview’s approximately $55 million base case.
Q2 LOE was $72 million, within the $71–79 million guidance range and below the preview’s $75 million midpoint checkpoint.

surprises.description: Magnera reported Q3 revenue of $857 million versus preview consensus of about $897 million, a shortfall of roughly 4.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue was $857 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $857M | ~$897M (4 analysts) | Miss, roughly -4.5%.”

surprises.description: Q3 free cash flow was negative, whereas the preview’s estimate implied Q3 contributed positive $32 million to roughly $160 million of nine-month free cash flow. Management said the quarter beat internal forecasts, helped by working-capital reductions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was negative in the quarter as expected but beat internal forecasts, helped by proactive working capital reductions in inventories and receivables.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Nine-month FCF is roughly $160M (H1 $128M plus Q3 $32M).”

surprises.description: The fully synergized adjusted EBITDA target is now $405 million, down from the original estimate of about $445 million, a roughly 9% reduction attributed to the changed macro backdrop.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's pro forma adjusted EBITDA target of $405 million (fully synergized) is down from an original ~$445 million estimate, reflecting a changed macro backdrop.”

surprises.description: Americas pricing was a $13 million negative despite 1% volume growth, with portfolio and mix walk-away actions contributing to the pressure—an unfavorable detail not flagged in the preview’s discussion of organic growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Organic sales grew 1% overall, with Americas volume up 1% led by infrastructure, though Americas price was a negative $13 million due to Project CORE portfolio and mix walk-away actions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Record EBITDA and +1% organic volume offset the revenue miss.”

surprises.description: Full-year CapEx is now tracking to about $60 million rather than the original roughly $80 million guide, providing a cash-flow offset to lower EBITDA that the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year CapEx is now tracking to about $60 million (roughly $15 million per quarter) versus an original ~$80 million guide, serving as the main offset to lower EBITDA in the cash flow bridge.”

surprises.description: Magnera said it will exit its transition services agreement and migrate off legacy Amcor ERP systems before the end of 2026, with integration costs ramping down and a net cash benefit expected—an operational and cash-flow development not covered in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company will exit its transition services agreement and migrate off legacy Amcor ERP systems before the end of calendar 2026, which is expected to be a net cash benefit as integration costs ramp down.”

in_line: Management moved FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance to the low end of the prior $380–410 million range, as the preview anticipated.
Free cash flow guidance was reaffirmed at $90–110 million, as expected in the preview.

The preview flagged synergy and Project CORE progress and possible FY27 incremental capture; the call reported full run-rate benefits in Q3 and roughly $20 million of additional synergy/CORE benefit carrying into FY27.

Rest of World remained weak, consistent with the preview’s focus on European softness; management attributed the slight EBITDA decline to demand softness and inflation outpacing pricing and said a couple million dollars of price recovery should flow into Q4.

surprises.description: Revenue was expected to be about $65.6 million, but Graham reported $71.3 million, roughly 9% above consensus and above the preview’s $70 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue rose 29% year-over-year to a record $71.3 million, with 17% organic growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $65.60M”; the bull scenario was “$70M+.”

surprises.description: The preview expected space to be in its conversion year and warned that flat Q1 revenue could raise back-half risk. Instead, space revenue surged 86%, with a 2.3x book-to-bill, and management described the result as a new sustainable revenue run rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Space revenue surged 86% year-over-year with orders of $14.4 million and a 2.3x book-to-bill,” which management characterized as “a new sustainable revenue run rate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 was framed as the conversion year, so flat Q1 space revenue would raise back-half risk.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for gross margin around 24% or higher, with a 23.5–24.5% base case. Graham reported 25%, above that range, although the margin remained below the prior-year level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin fell to 25% from 26.5% a year ago due to higher lower-margin defense mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 needs to print about 24% or higher”; base case was “23.5–24.5%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.49 exceeded the $0.40 consensus, while GAAP EPS was $0.33 and net income declined. The preview warned the consensus EPS basis was unclear, but had estimated a smaller $0.08–$0.12 gap between adjusted and GAAP EPS; the reported gap was $0.16.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income declined to $3.9 million ($0.33/share) from $4.6 million ($0.42/share), while adjusted EPS rose 9% to $0.49.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS | $0.40”; “With FlackTek in the base, the Q1 FY27 gap is likely $0.08–0.12.”

surprises.description: The preview noted more than $43 million of previously announced defense awards and said only part would land in Q1 backlog, but did not anticipate the reported 40% defense revenue growth or $61.8 million of new and follow-on program orders.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Defense revenue grew 40% and included $61.8 million of new and follow-on orders” for the submarine and torpedo programs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Also note $43M+ in defense awards announced Aug 5, 2026, and that only part of it lands in Q1 backlog.”

surprises.description: The preview discussed the $50 million investment as a source of share dilution, but did not describe the resulting balance-sheet position. The company used part of the proceeds to repay about $13 million of debt and ended the quarter with no debt, $27 million of cash, and revolver capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $50 million strategic investment from T. Rowe Price-advised accounts was used partly to repay ~$13 million of debt, leaving the company with $27 million cash, no debt, and ~$75 million of revolver capacity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The April 2026 PIPE ($50M gross, about 599,808 shares at $83.36) adds roughly 5.4% share dilution.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag quarterly cash use or the facility-related capital spending. Graham reported $12.7 million of cash used in operations because of billing and collection timing and bonus payments, and guided to $18–22 million of capex including a new Arvada facility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating activities used $12.7 million of cash in the quarter due to billing/collection timing and bonus payments, while capex is guided to $18-22 million including a new 30,000-square-foot Arvada facility.”

in_line: Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance of $285–295 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $35–40 million were reaffirmed, as the preview expected.
Backlog reached $557 million, above the preview’s $530 million watch level.
Adjusted EBITDA margin was flat at 12.3%, matching the prior-year margin cited in the preview.

surprises.description: Puma reported $53.6 million in net product revenue, above its $50–52 million Q2 guide, and $56.5 million in total revenue, above the $54.06 million consensus and the company’s $52–55 million total-revenue guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $56.5 million, with net product revenue of $53.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue … Company guidance (Q2) $52–55M … Consensus $54.06M”; “NERLYNX net product revenue $50–52M.”

surprises.description: GAAP net income was $8.2 million, far above the preview’s $2–4 million company guidance and consensus EPS of $0.04–$0.07; reported diluted EPS was $0.16.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 GAAP net income of $8.2 million ($0.16 per diluted share) … with non-GAAP net income of $10.1 million.”

surprises.description: Puma raised its full-year product revenue and net income guidance rather than merely reaffirming it, though each range moved up by only $3 million at both endpoints for product revenue and $1 million for net income.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 net product revenue guidance to $205-209 million (from $202-206 million) and net income guidance to $17-20 million (from $16-19 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance action. The raise versus reaffirm decision matters”; the preview’s base case was “FY guide reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Ex-factory bottle sales reached 2,929, comfortably above the preview’s 2,400-bottle concern threshold, with sequential and year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 ex-factory bottle sales rose 26% quarter-over-quarter and 12% year-over-year to 2,929 bottles.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GTN above 27.5% or bottles below 2,400 would raise quality-of-revenue concerns.”

surprises.description: Despite the strong bottle volume, new patient starts fell 6% sequentially, a weaker demand indicator than the bottle growth alone might suggest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New patient starts declined 6% sequentially.”

surprises.description: Full-year royalty guidance was cut by $1 million at both ends, from $20–23 million to $19–22 million, rather than remaining at the preview’s stated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year royalty guidance was trimmed to $19-22 million from $20-23 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance … royalty revenue $20–23M.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a potential China royalty-rate reduction as early as late 2026 or 2027 once generic NERLYNX reaches a market-share threshold, adding a future royalty risk not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China royalty rates could be reduced as early as late 2026 or 2027 once generic NERLYNX reaches a market-share threshold.”

surprises.description: ALISCA-Breast1 enrollment was narrowed to the 40mg and 50mg dose groups and patients with Aurora kinase pathway biomarkers, rather than the enrollment expansion and 70mg escalation questions the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ALISCA-Breast1 trial was amended to continue enrollment only in the 40mg and 50mg dose groups, targeting patients with Aurora kinase pathway biomarkers, with amended enrollment expected in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Alisertib program status. Enrollment expansion confirmation, 70mg escalation tolerability…”

surprises.description: Management said Puma can fund Phase III trials in both ER-positive breast cancer and small cell lung cancer, potentially staggering them, while remaining committed to positive net income—addressing the preview’s concern about how Phase III work might be funded.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management stated it can fund Phase III trials for alisertib in both ER-positive breast cancer and small cell lung cancer, potentially staggered, while remaining committed to positive net income.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capital allocation. Any hint of a Phase 3 funded by equity would be a negative.”

surprises.description: Management projected that 2026 would be the first time in NERLYNX’s launch history that U.S. demand grew year over year in two consecutive years, a positive forward-looking demand statement not included in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects 2026 to mark the first-ever back-to-back years of positive year-over-year U.S. NERLYNX demand growth in the drug's launch history.”

in_line: Puma’s debt-free status was already established in the preview: it said the Athyrium loan had been retired and the company was debt-free after Q1.

surprises.description: Q1 adjusted EBITDA was $358 million, well above the preview’s derived $305–315 million range; the 35.8% margin also substantially exceeded the roughly 30.7–31.7% expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 29% to $358 million, delivering a 35.8% margin … the second-highest margin in company history.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … My derived range is ~$305–315M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin … Derived ~30.7–31.7%.”

surprises.description: Revenue modestly topped the $992.5 million consensus, reaching more than $1 billion. Organic growth of 9% was at the top of the preview’s estimated 6–9% range, so the headline beat was small rather than a large organic-growth surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue exceeded $1 billion for the first time in company history, rising 21% year-over-year, with organic revenue up 9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $992.5M”; “Consensus of $992.5M implies roughly +6% to +9% organic growth.”

surprises.description: Management quantified $25–30 million of Q2 revenue pulled into Q1 as customers bought ahead of price increases. The preview anticipated a possible pre-buy effect but did not quantify its size, making this a meaningful qualification to the strong headline revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately $25-30 million of revenue was pulled forward from Q2 into Q1 as customers bought ahead of price increases, primarily in the stormwater/nonresidential segment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CFO Scott Cottrill said Q1 volumes may be elevated by agricultural customers buying ahead of announced price increases, with demand normalizing by Q2”; “Listen for how much of the beat they attribute to pre-buying.”

surprises.description: The near-term margin outlook was more pressured than a typical seasonal step-down: management expects Q2 EBITDA margin to compress by more than 300 basis points sequentially, with resin costs peaking in Q2 and Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects Q2 EBITDA margin to compress sequentially by more than the typical 300 basis points as favorable resin costs flip to a significant headwind, with resin costs peaking in Q2 and Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The margin comp is the hardest of the year”; “The base [scenario] … margin falls about 200 bps on mix and pricing”; “price-cost squeeze” was flagged as a risk.

surprises.description: Nonresidential organic sales were stronger than management had anticipated, growing 14% on resilient data center, warehouse, and commercial construction activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nonresidential sales grew 14% organically, driven by resilient data center, warehouse, and commercial construction activity, and are tracking modestly better than expected.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Nonresidential projects soften alongside weak residential demand” was identified as the bear scenario.

surprises.description: Residential organic sales were flat and modestly worse than anticipated, adding downside to the demand picture despite the stronger nonresidential result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Residential organic sales were flat as affordability pressures and elevated interest rates weighed on demand, performing modestly worse than anticipated.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call characterized residential performance as “modestly worse than anticipated.”

surprises.description: Available liquidity was about $901 million, below the more-than-$950 million level cited in the preview as the capital-allocation backdrop.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Available liquidity was approximately $901 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capital deployment … would matter, given leverage of 1.6x and more than $950M of liquidity.”

in_line: Full-year sales guidance was maintained at $3.35–3.55 billion, consistent with the preview’s expectation that guidance would be reaffirmed; the preview viewed a reaffirmation as neutral to slightly negative rather than a surprise.
CapEx guidance of approximately $200 million matched the preview’s stated FY2027 guidance.
NDS contributed revenue and grew organically, addressing the preview’s focus on the acquisition-versus-organic growth split; the preview did not provide a specific expected NDS revenue figure.
Organic revenue growth of 9% was within the preview’s estimated 6–9% range, even though reported revenue slightly exceeded consensus.

surprises.description: Guardian raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $1.43–$1.45 billion and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $129–$131 million, above the prior ranges of $1.40–$1.42 billion and $123–$127 million. The EBITDA range is stronger than the preview’s base case of a modest raise or reiteration, though it falls within its bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Guardian raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $1.43-$1.45 billion (from $1.4-$1.42 billion) and adjusted EBITDA of $129-$131 million (from $123-$127 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA guide raised to at least $126M”; the base scenario anticipated a “modest guide raise or reiteration at high end,” while the bull scenario anticipated “FY EBITDA guide raised to $128–132M.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross profit reached $80 million with a 22.8% margin, above the preview’s expected $74–77 million and roughly 22% margin. Both dollars and margin were better than the preview’s stated watch range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit rising 18% to $80 million and gross margin expanding to 22.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Look for roughly $74–77M of gross profit at about 22% margin.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $351.2 million exceeded the $340.45 million consensus estimate by about 3%, and also cleared the preview’s bull-scenario revenue range’s $348 million lower bound.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was $351.2 million (up 2%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 Consensus” revenue: “$340.45M”; bull scenario revenue: “$348–355M.”

surprises.description: Management now expects second-half reported revenue to decline only low single digits, less than the roughly 4–7% decline implied by the prior full-year revenue guidance in the preview. It also said underlying second-half growth remains high single digits despite IRA pricing effects.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects second-half reported revenue to decline low single digits due to IRA pricing, though underlying growth remains high single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The $1.40–1.42B guide implies 2H revenue down roughly 4–7% Y/Y as IRA effects lap a strong FY25 back half.”

surprises.description: The expected revenue impact from the 2027 IRA drug tranche is now estimated at roughly 40% of the 2026 tranche’s impact, down from the prior 50% estimate. That points to a smaller future IRA headwind than the earlier estimate suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 2027 IRA drug tranche is expected to represent roughly 40% of the 2026 tranche's revenue impact (down from a prior 50% estimate), and management believes the margin impact is mitigated.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call states the prior estimate was “50%.”

surprises.description: Guardian disclosed nearly $90 million of cash, no debt, and potential Omnicare asset opportunities that are not included in guidance. The preview did not flag these opportunities, so this adds a possible source of future activity without a stated commitment or forecast impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Guardian ended the quarter with nearly $90 million in cash (up from ~$65 million) and no debt, keeping dry powder for potential Omnicare asset opportunities not reflected in guidance.”

surprises.description: The call specified that about 13.5 million Class B shares will convert to Class A in late September, with an estimated 35–37 million Class A shares held by insiders subject to trading restrictions until after Q3 earnings in November. The preview did not discuss this timing or the potential for insider-held shares to become tradable afterward.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A final tranche of ~13.5 million Class B shares converts to Class A in late September, leaving an estimated 35-37 million Class A shares held by insiders, subject to trading restrictions until after Q3 earnings in November.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $29.7 million, within the preview’s derived estimate of roughly $28–30 million and its base-case range of $29–31 million.

Resident growth was described as high single digits, consistent with the preview’s expectation of about 211–213 thousand residents and 8–9% growth; the preview also identified the $8.5 million payer settlement as pre-announced and excluded from adjusted EBITDA, as the call facts report.

surprises.description: Gevo reported approval of a Canada Clean Fuel Regulation pathway that opens a compliance market of more than 1 billion gallons per year, and said roughly $17 million of banked credits had already been sold for Q3 recognition. The preview anticipated Canada credit sales appearing in Q3, but did not anticipate this market access or the disclosed sale amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Newly approved Canada Clean Fuel Regulation pathway opens a more than 1 billion gallon per year compliance market and applies retroactively, with roughly $17 million of banked CFR credits already sold for Q3 recognition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Canada CFR credit sales show up in Q3 financials.”

surprises.description: Management now expects the carbon business to generate over $30 million in annual run-rate revenue, excluding sales of banked CFR credits. The preview did not provide an expectation for this recurring-revenue outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects the carbon business to deliver over $30 million per year in run-rate revenue, excluding banked CFR credit sales.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $47 million, matching the preview’s approximately $47 million consensus estimate; reported year-over-year growth of 7% was close to the preview’s expected 8%.

FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance was formalized at more than $60 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation of more than doubling the prior $30 million target and its view that guidance with a “6” handle would be positive.

The more-than-$70 million 2026 45Z monetization target and H2-weighted cash timing were already flagged in the preview; the reported post-quarter collection and remaining year-end proceeds fit that outlook.

The Lake Preston discontinuation and a potentially large non-cash write-down were flagged risks; the reported $176 million impairment and resulting sharply negative GAAP EPS were within that warned scenario.
Northstar’s roughly $600 million capital estimate and year-end decision target were already in the preview; the call continued to identify bankable offtake as a gating item.

surprises.description: BETR guided to Q3 net revenue of $49–$52 million, below the preview’s base case of $56–$62 million and slightly below even its bear-case range of $50–$55 million. Loan volume guidance also implies a sequential decline from Q2, though the preview did not give a Q3 volume estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance implies a sequential decline, with loan volume of $1.375-$1.525 billion, net revenues of $49-$52 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario was “Q3 Revenue Guide” of “$56–68M” in the bull case and “$56–62M” in the base case; its bear case was “$50–55M.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance of a $15–$18 million loss was worse than the preview’s base-case loss of $10–$13 million and landed in its bear-case territory. The preview had said the market needed to see the burn cut roughly in half sequentially to support a 2026 break-even story.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance implies a sequential decline” and an “adjusted EBITDA loss of $15-$18 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “$(10)–(13)M” of Q3 adjusted EBITDA loss; its bear case was “Worse than $(15)M, or withheld.”

surprises.description: Management said it will miss the previously guided goal of adjusted EBITDA break-even by September and would not provide a replacement target month. The preview’s base case already anticipated a push to 1H27, but the lack of any new timeframe is less concrete than that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company will fall short of its previously guided goal of reaching adjusted EBITDA break-even by September, and management declined to re-anchor to a specific target month.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said break-even by end of Q3 had been “reaffirmed on the Q1 call” and described its base case as “Breakeven pushed to 1H27.”

surprises.description: Refinance volume rose sharply despite the preview’s higher-for-longer rate concerns and its bear-case concern that refinance volume could weaken. Management cautioned that the business remains rate-sensitive and expects elevated rates to persist over the medium term.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Refinance volume surged 239% year-over-year to $549 million but remains highly rate-sensitive amid an elevated rate environment management expects to persist over the medium term.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a “higher-for-longer” environment and listed “refi volume weakens” as a bear-case driver.

surprises.description: The company disclosed that signed HELOC partnerships, including Credit Karma, have not launched and are excluded from Q3 guidance, with meaningful contributions not expected until Q4. The preview did not discuss these partnerships or their launch timing, so the Q3 contribution is an unanticipated omission while the later contribution is potential upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Signed HELOC partnerships—including Credit Karma—have not yet launched and are excluded from Q3 guidance, with meaningful contributions expected to begin in Q4 2026.”

in_line: The Q2 loan volume of $1.67 billion and net revenue of $54.7 million matched the preliminary figures and ranges already laid out in the preview.
Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss of $14 million matched the preliminary result; the preview had already flagged that it included a $6.5 million TRID reserve release.
The annual cost-savings target above $45 million was already stated in the preview as management’s raised target.
The interim CEO appointment and transition away from founder Vishal Garg had been announced before the call, as the preview noted.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $124.5 million, above both the $122.3 million high end of guidance and the preview’s live consensus estimate of about $121.4 million. The beat was stronger than the preview’s base case of $122–123.5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue reached $124.5 million” and was “above the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue” guidance was “$120.3–122.3M”; live consensus was “~$121.4M”; the base scenario was “$122–123.5M.”

surprises.description: ARR growth was stronger than the preview’s estimate: total ARR reached $465.1 million versus an estimated ~$460 million, with record net new ARR of $29.9 million, up 35% year over year. The preview’s bull case had used roughly $465 million or more as its ARR threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total ARR grew 27% year-over-year … to $465.1 million, an acceleration from Q1, with record net new ARR of $29.9 million up 35% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total ARR” consensus estimate was “~$460M”; the bull scenario cited “~$465M+.”

surprises.description: Operating income and margin came in above the preview’s expectations: non-GAAP operating income was $20.3 million versus guidance of $18.7–19.7 million, and its 16.3% margin exceeded the preview’s expected range. Separately, the company extended its streak of GAAP operating profitability to eight quarters and expanded GAAP operating margin year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income of $20.3 million (16.3% margin) beating guidance”; it was the “eighth straight quarter of GAAP operating profitability,” with GAAP operating margin expanding “~130 basis points year-over-year to 8.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 non-GAAP operating income guidance was “$18.7–19.7M”; expected non-GAAP operating margin was “15.5–16.1%” and “~15.8%.”

surprises.description: The business showed unusually strong large-customer growth that the preview did not quantify: customers above $100,000 ARR grew 26%, the fastest pace in over three years, and each of the larger ARR cohorts grew at least 30%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customers with over $100,000 ARR grew 26% to 911, the fastest growth in over three years, while all cohorts above $250K, $500K, and $1M grew at or above 30%.”

surprises.description: Control bundle traction was more concrete than the preview’s general request for evidence of AI monetization: deals including AgentPulse averaged two to three times larger in dollar value, and the number of Control package customers roughly doubled quarter over quarter. However, the call said those bundle wins remained largely in the pipeline rather than booked.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Control bundle deals including AgentPulse are averaging 2x-3x larger in dollar value,” and “the number of Control package customers roughly doubled quarter-over-quarter”; AgentPulse bundle wins “remain largely in pipeline rather than booked.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for “Agentic-AI monetization evidence” and “ARR attribution rather than anecdotes.”

surprises.description: Management said it is increasing second-half spending on technology and go-to-market, which will modestly pressure near-term operating income. That adds a near-term margin headwind to the preview’s expectation of a substantial second-half operating-margin ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is increasing H1 second-half spending on technology and go-to-market, which will modestly pressure near-term operating income” while targeting longer-term operating margin of 25%–30%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY operating-income guide “implies a back-half margin near 19.7%” and asked for “a clear 2H margin bridge.”

surprises.description: The reported full-year ARR range is slightly below the prior range, despite management describing an underlying raise: the new $522.1–528.1 million range is $1.3 million lower at each end than the prior $523.4–529.4 million range. The call attributed the offset to incremental FX headwinds, while the FX-adjusted growth midpoint remained 26%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year ARR guidance to $522.1M-$528.1M (26% growth midpoint) but incremental FX headwinds of $5.6M on revenue and $2M on ARR partially offset the underlying raise and Q2 beat.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY2026 ARR guidance was “$523.4–529.4M (+26% FX-adjusted).” The preview noted that if the “reported range falls again on FX,” investors would focus on the constant-currency figure and that “holding 26% FX-adjusted growth at the midpoint matters most.”

surprises.description: The company had spent $121.5 million on buybacks year to date, repurchasing nearly nine times as many shares as in the first half of 2025 at roughly 70% of the prior cost per share. The preview anticipated possible aggressive repurchases but did not anticipate this reported scale relative to the prior year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company spent $121.5 million on share buybacks year-to-date (nearly 9x the shares repurchased in H1 2025 at ~70% of the prior cost per share), with $108.6 million remaining in the program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “an aggressive Q2 buyback would be a confidence signal” and noted that $60.8 million had been repurchased in Q1.

in_line: NRR was 110% (111% reported), matching the preview’s explicitly flagged possibility that it could slip from 111% to 110%; it remained below the 115% long-term target.
The full-year ARR outlook maintained 26% growth at the midpoint on an FX-adjusted basis, as the preview said mattered most, even though the reported range was slightly lower because of FX.
SaaS was 79% of revenue, close to the preview’s Q1 reference of about 80%, consistent with its expectation of a higher SaaS mix and lower upfront term-license recognition.

surprises.description: GMED reported non-GAAP EPS of $1.34 versus the preview's $1.12 consensus, a substantially larger beat than the preview's base case of an in-line to modest beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fully diluted non-GAAP EPS was $1.34,” up 55.8% year over year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS” consensus: “$1.12”; the base scenario expected “In line to modest beat.”

surprises.description: GMED raised its full-year EPS range by $0.25 at both ends, a stronger increase than the preview's base case of an EPS raise only. The preview's bull case anticipated an EPS raise alongside a revenue raise, but GMED left revenue guidance unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised FY26 non-GAAP EPS guidance to “$4.95-$5.05” from “$4.70-$4.80” while reaffirming revenue guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario forecast “EPS raised, revenue reaffirmed”; the bull case forecast “Revenue raised.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 35.4%, above the preview's expectation that it would move toward the mid-30s, and expanded sharply rather than giving back margin sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 740 basis points to 35.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the EPS path depended on adjusted EBITDA margin “moving toward the mid-30s” and warned that “Any sequential give-back” would weigh on the EPS trajectory.

surprises.description: Enabling Technologies revenue fell 25.8%, a pronounced contraction despite the preview only flagging that the segment could be soft. The reported shift toward flexible capital acquisition models helps explain the drop, while deployed units continued to grow.
surprises.fact_evidence: Enabling Technologies revenue “fell 25.8% to $26.1 million due to a shift toward flexible capital acquisition models,” while deployed EGPS and eHub units grew 25% year over year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario listed “Enabling Technologies soft”; the preview said segment detail was “not covered in depth.”

surprises.description: Trauma delivered strong growth tied to restored PRECICE supply and new OUS market activation, a business development the preview did not identify among its expectations or key issues.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trauma revenue grew 31% year-over-year and 18% sequentially,” aided by restored PRECICE supply and new OUS market activation.

surprises.description: Nevro's stand-alone adjusted EBITDA margin turned positive and improved substantially from Q1, a notable profitability improvement not addressed in the preview's Nevro trough discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: Nevro's stand-alone adjusted EBITDA margin was “positive 22.4%” versus “negative 1.4% a year earlier,” and up from 11.8% in Q1.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on Nevro revenue, saying to watch for “a sequential print of about $80M or more” and a reaffirmed recovery timeline; it did not give a Nevro margin expectation.

surprises.description: GMED lowered its full-year non-GAAP tax-rate guidance, providing an additional earnings tailwind that the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Non-GAAP tax-rate guidance was lowered to “23%-24% from 24%-25%.”

surprises.description: GMED repurchased $136.1 million of shares in the quarter, a sizable capital-allocation action not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company repurchased “$136.1 million (1.6 million shares) in Q2,” with “$253.9 million remaining” under its authorization.

surprises.description: Competitive sales hiring accelerated materially from Q1, an operating signal not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Competitive sales hires in Q2 were “double the Q1 level,” the second-highest onboarding in eight quarters.

in_line: Revenue was $789.6 million versus $786.9 million consensus, a small beat; ex-Nevro growth of 9% was close to the preview's roughly 8.6% implied expectation.

FY26 revenue guidance was reaffirmed at $3.18-$3.22 billion, as the preview's base scenario expected; the stated roughly 2%-5% second-half growth range is broadly consistent with the preview's roughly 3% midpoint implication.

Nevro's sequential revenue decline of $1.7 million left it near the preview's roughly $80 million trough watchpoint, and management still described a recovery by year-end, within the preview's anticipated second-half recovery window.
Adjusted gross margin was 69.4%, in line with the preview's expectation that gross margin hold near 69%-70%.

surprises.description: Commerce revenue fell 11% to $12.1 million, rather than tracking roughly flat as the preview’s base case anticipated. That made this a second consecutive decline and weakened the diversification story the preview flagged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commerce revenue fell 11% year-over-year to $12.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (~50%): ... Commerce roughly flat”; the preview also said, “A second consecutive decline would undercut the diversification story.”

surprises.description: Despite the expected sharp DTC contraction, retention improved by over 170 basis points and average order value rose 45 cents per unit, lifting BarkBox subscriber lifetime value near its highest level as a public company. This was encouraging subscriber-quality evidence against the preview’s concern about the subscriber trend.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subscriber retention rate improved by over 170 basis points year-over-year, while average order value grew 45 cents per unit, pushing BarkBox subscriber lifetime value near its highest level as a public company.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The FY27 guide depends on DTC troughing in 1H and recovering in 2H”; “Hard subscriber numbers and retention commentary matter more than the headline.”

surprises.description: BARK received a $7.4 million IEEPA tariff recovery that lifted reported gross margin to 72.7%, but normalized gross margin was 63.4%, slightly below the year-ago 63.8%. The recovery resolved some of the preview’s uncertainty about whether tariff-refund proceeds would arrive, while showing that the headline margin was not an underlying improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported gross margin was 72.7%, inflated by a one-time $7.4 million IEPA tariff recovery from FY26; normalized gross margin was 63.4% versus 63.8% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Check how much landed in Q1 and where it was booked”; “A COGS credit would flatter gross margin and adjusted EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Bark Air revenue grew 37% to $3.2 million, and over 90% of Q2 seats were already sold, a positive business update the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bark Air revenue grew 37% year-over-year to $3.2 million, with over 90% of Q2 seats already sold.”

surprises.description: Cash declined to $16.1 million from $19.3 million at fiscal year-end as working capital built and BARK repurchased shares. The preview had questioned whether the buyback would be carried out given the cash balance; repurchases occurred, but cash fell rather than being preserved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter debt-free with $16.1 million in cash, down from $19.3 million at fiscal year-end due to working capital build and share repurchases under its $40 million buyback program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any Q1 repurchases and the ending cash balance excluding refunds will show whether the buyback is real.”

in_line: Q1 revenue was $78.8 million, within the $77–79 million guidance range and near the approximately $78 million consensus midpoint.
Adjusted EBITDA was approximately $600,000, within the $0–1 million guidance range.
DTC orders declined about 28% year-over-year, close to the preview’s roughly 28% decline expectation.
BARK reiterated its full-year top- and bottom-line guidance, consistent with the preview’s base case.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $133 million, well above the preview’s $124.63 million consensus and $122.5–$127.5 million company range. Growth was 19%, versus the preview’s expected 11.4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue grew 19% year-over-year to $133 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus | $124.63M (+11.4% YoY) | Company guidance ... $122.5M – $127.5M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $14.3 million, above both the preview’s roughly $10.5 million midpoint and the $11.5 million top of the company’s range. A $1.3 million one-time legacy customer project contributed, but the stated normalized baseline of about $13 million would still exceed the preview’s range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $14.3 million”; management flagged “a normalized baseline of ~$13 million after excluding $1.3 million from a one-time legacy customer project.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$10.5M | $9.5M – $11.5M”; the preview also called out the “$10.5M midpoint and the $9.5M floor.”

surprises.description: PAR raised its FY2026 outlook instead of merely reaffirming the existing ranges: revenue guidance increased to $516–$523 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $50–$53 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 guidance, lifting total revenue to $516-523 million (from $500-515 million) and adjusted EBITDA to $50-53 million (from $44-47 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said reaffirming “the $500M–$515M revenue and $44M–$47M EBITDA ranges is the minimum bar” and described a raise as “the bull trigger.”

surprises.description: The preview’s non-GAAP EPS estimate was $0.12, while PAR reported diluted non-GAAP EPS of $0.18 and non-GAAP net income of $7.5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income improved to $7.5 million ($0.18 diluted EPS) from $0.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS | ... +$0.12 non-GAAP”; the preview noted that EPS estimates conflicted across sources and bases.

surprises.description: On the GAAP basis, the reported loss per share was substantially larger than the preview’s GAAP estimate: a $0.41 loss versus an expected $0.09 loss. The preview itself warned that EPS sources used conflicting bases.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed to $17 million ($0.41 per share) from $21 million ($0.52) a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS | −$0.09 GAAP or +$0.12 non-GAAP”; the preview cautioned: “The EPS consensus conflicts across sources.”

surprises.description: PAR reported $3 million of free cash flow, up $11.5 million year over year, which was favorable against the preview’s concern about further cash burn. The supplied facts do not state operating cash flow, the specific measure highlighted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow rose $11.5 million year-over-year to $3 million with cash of $77 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “another large burn would weigh on the balance sheet narrative” and that “Positive, or burn below $5M” cash flow would ease concern.

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating expenses fell to 38% of revenue, a 1,000-basis-point year-over-year improvement, with management saying the largest run-rate step-down occurred in Q2. The preview did not anticipate this degree of operating-efficiency improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP OpEx as a percentage of revenue improved 1,000 basis points year-over-year to 38%, driven by restructuring and AI-enabled operational efficiencies, with the largest step-down in run rate occurring in Q2.”

surprises.description: Hardware revenue rose 31% to $35 million, its strongest quarter in at least 10 years, but management expects the unusually strong level to normalize in the second half and cited tariff and supply-chain pressure on low-20% margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hardware revenue jumped 31% to $35 million in its strongest quarter in at least 10 years, but management expects this to normalize in the second half, with margins staying in the low-20% range due to tariff and supply chain pressures.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Hardware rollouts” as a key metric and noted that “Hardware grew 34% YoY in Q1,” but did not provide a Q2 hardware estimate.

surprises.description: PAR Intelligence had reached about 20,000 live sites, with another 20,000 planned for Q3 and the company still on track for its 50,000-site FY2026 commitment. However, the call gave no dollar monetization figure and said meaningful add-on subscription monetization is expected to start in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PAR Intelligence reached roughly 20,000 live sites ... with another 20,000 planned for Q3, keeping the company on track for its 50,000-site commitment for FY2026, with meaningful monetization expected as an add-on subscription starting in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Any hard dollar figure for PAR Intelligence would be direct evidence against the AI-disruption bear case.”

surprises.description: New Q2 engagements had nearly 100% multiproduct attachment, and the average customer now carried about two products versus roughly 1.5 previously; management also estimated a threefold cross-sell opportunity in the existing base. The preview did not flag these attachment and cross-sell figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Multiproduct attachment on new Q2 engagements was nearly 100%, with the average customer now carrying about 2 products (up from ~1.5), and management estimates a 3x cross-sell opportunity within the existing base.”

surprises.description: The newly acquired Bridg product brought in over $1.3 million of committed ARR from two customers, but temporarily reduced non-GAAP subscription margin to 65.1% from 66.4%; management expects that margin reset to reverse over coming quarters. The preview did not mention Bridg.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The newly acquired Bridg product added over $1.3 million in new committed ARR from two customers signed through 2029, but temporarily lowered non-GAAP subscription margin to 65.1% from 66.4%, a reset management expects to reverse over coming quarters.”

in_line: Total ARR was approximately $338 million, at the bottom of the preview’s $338–$342 million estimate; year-over-year ARR growth was over 17%, and 12.3% organic growth cleared the preview’s 11% threshold.

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin was 57%, above the preview’s 55–56% consensus range and the 56% level it flagged as supportive of the H2 ramp. It also reached the top of the full-year margin guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin reached 57%, improving 5 percentage points year-over-year and 2 points sequentially,” and “representing the second-highest gross margin in company history.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus” gross margin was “~55–56%”; “A Q2 gross margin of 56% or more would support the H2 ramp.”

surprises.description: International sales were $75 million, below the preview’s roughly $80 million company guide and implied 13.5% growth; reported growth was 7%. International pump shipments nevertheless rose 19%, with a distributor inventory buyback also weighing on sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International shipments grew 19% year-over-year to ~11,000 pumps and sales rose 7% to $75 million,” with “~$3 million of distributor inventory buyback headwinds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Intl sales” company guidance of “~$80M” and implied year-over-year growth of “+13.5%.”

surprises.description: Pharmacy coverage reached about 45%, short of the preview’s above-50% watch level. It was up from the 40% Q1 baseline, but did not reach the preview’s stated catalyst threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Formulary coverage now stands at approximately 45%, already approaching the high end of the company's target range for the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 baselines: about 40% formulary coverage”; the preview said to “Watch for coverage above 50%” and listed “Pharmacy coverage above 50%” as a catalyst.

surprises.description: The initial pharmacy pump headwind was about $8 million in Q2, far larger than the approximately $1 million Q1 baseline cited in the preview. Favorable pricing offset some of the pressure, but the larger-than-baseline drag was a downside surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The initial pharmacy pump headwind was approximately $8 million in Q2, but net favorable pricing still drove more than half of total sales growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave “about $1M of Q1 revenue headwind” and said the market should watch PayGo pharmacy metrics.

surprises.description: Pump shipments grew more than 10% year over year while worldwide sales grew 6%, indicating stronger unit volume than the revenue growth rate alone would suggest; the preview did not provide a shipment-volume expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Worldwide Q2 sales were $255 million, up 6% year-over-year,” with “~33,000 pumps shipped and shipments up more than 10% year-over-year and sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected worldwide sales of “~$255.0M” and implied year-over-year growth of “+5.9%,” but did not state a pump-shipment expectation.

surprises.description: Pharmacy reached approximately 10% of U.S. pump shipments and sales in its first full PAYGO quarter, ahead of the preview’s above-8% pharmacy-sales catalyst and up from the 6% Q1 baseline. The company also maintained its 20% full-year shipment target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In its first full quarter of PAYGO, pharmacy pump shipments and pharmacy sales each reached approximately 10% of the U.S. total,” and the company “reaffirmed its full-year target of 20% of U.S. pump shipments through pharmacy.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “6% of US sales through pharmacy” in Q1 and listed “pharmacy above 8% of US sales” as a catalyst.

surprises.description: International direct-channel sales more than doubled to about 13% of international revenue, a channel-mix shift the preview did not flag. This occurred despite the distributor inventory buyback headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Direct-channel sales more than doubling to ~13% of international revenue despite ~$3 million of distributor inventory buyback headwinds.”

surprises.description: Stock-based compensation fell to $16 million and the full-year expectation was reduced from about $80 million to about $65 million, helping operating margin improve to negative 5%. The preview did not identify this as a potential driver of margin improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Stock-based compensation fell to $16 million (6% of sales, down from 11%), and full-year expectations were lowered to ~$65 million from ~$80 million, helping drive an 8-point improvement in operating margin to negative 5%.”

in_line: Worldwide sales were $255 million, essentially matching the preview’s approximately $255 million consensus and company guide.
Full-year sales, gross-margin, and adjusted EBITDA-margin guidance was reaffirmed, as the preview expected.
Mobi Tubeless 510(k) submission and a second-half 2026 scaled-launch target were confirmed, as the preview anticipated.

surprises.description: Perdoceo raised the quarterly dividend to $0.17 from $0.15, announcing the 13.3% increase before the preview’s flagged Q3 dividend review. The preview had not suggested an increase would be announced with the Q2 results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board raised the quarterly dividend 13.3% from $0.15 to $0.17 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The dividend increase review is flagged for Q3 2026.”

surprises.description: Perdoceo lifted the low end of its FY2026 adjusted operating income and adjusted EPS ranges, while leaving both high ends unchanged. The preview described reaffirmation or a modest nudge up as the base case, so the higher floors were a positive, limited upgrade.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 adjusted operating income guidance was set at $258-263 million” and adjusted EPS guidance at “$3.10-$3.16.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The May guidance was “adj. operating income $254–$263M” and “adj. EPS $3.05–$3.16”; the preview said “FY guide reaffirmed or nudged up” in its base scenario.

surprises.description: Management cautioned that CTU’s reported enrollments may trend lower in the second half, with normalization not expected until 2027. That was a newly disclosed enrollment headwind against the preview’s generally constructive outlook for enrollment growth, including faster AIUS growth in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CTU's second-half reported enrollments may trend lower due to lapping record quarters and a record number of 2026 graduates, with normalization expected in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management had said “AIUS enrollments would increase in Q2 and accelerate in Q3”; the preview also said management expected revenue growth in each remaining quarter.

surprises.description: Incremental CTU legal fees tied to previously disclosed litigation weighed on operating income, a cost headwind the preview did not flag. Management said CTU operating income would have grown year over year without those additional fees.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rising legal fees at CTU tied to previously disclosed litigation weighed on operating income,” and management said CTU operating income “would have grown year-over-year excluding these incremental costs.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.80, matching the preview’s $0.80 consensus and the company’s $0.79–$0.80 guidance.
Q2 revenue of $213.4 million was close to the $212.5 million consensus and the preview’s roughly $213 million working bogey.
The preview expected AIUS enrollment growth in Q2; the call reported that all institutions grew except Trident University within AIU System, consistent with broad growth while noting that exception.
The Q2 tax benefit from resolving a state income tax matter was anticipated as a possible roughly $0.05 nonrecurring item; the call reported a 20.3% effective tax rate benefiting from the resolution.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $11.4 million, above the preview’s roughly $10.0–10.5 million consensus range. That was a meaningful beat against the estimate, despite only 1.7% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $11.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “~$10.0–10.5M (~$10.3M cited elsewhere)”

surprises.description: The company reaffirmed its $54–57 million full-year revenue guidance rather than making the cut the preview’s base case anticipated. The reaffirmation also held above the preview’s approximately $53.5 million consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $54 million to $57 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a cut or a ‘low end’ narrowing is the main risk” and its Base scenario expected the “guide trimmed to ~$48–52M or narrowed to the low end.”

surprises.description: Sales-force expansion coincided with a larger adjusted EBITDA loss: sales and marketing spending reached the same amount as quarterly revenue, and the loss widened year over year. The preview flagged sales-force productivity and the new-hire ramp as issues, but did not anticipate this scale of spending relative to revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss widened to approximately $7.1 million from $5.3 million in Q2 2025, driven by sales force expansion costs”; “Sales and marketing expenses surged to $11.4 million from $7.2 million a year earlier, equaling the entire quarter's revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Territories more than doubled, but about 40% were disrupted by rep and manager changes,” new hires had a “6 to 9 month ramp,” and investors should “Watch territory count, rep attrition, and revenue per territory.”

surprises.description: A new CMS G-code extended TriNav reimbursement into office-based labs, opening an additional site of care. The preview did not identify this reimbursement expansion as an upcoming development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In July, CMS granted a new G-code extending TriNav reimbursement into the office-based lab (OBL) setting, expanding site-of-care access.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash was below the preview’s projected range, although management said the balance still fully funds its strategic growth plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with approximately $46.3 million in cash, which management believes fully funds its strategic growth plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview projected “roughly $48–50M at 6/30/26.”

surprises.description: Gross margin slightly exceeded the preview’s estimated range, coming in at 86.8% rather than roughly 85–86%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 86.8% from 83.9% year-over-year due to lower TriNav unit costs and manufacturing improvements.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … ~85–86%”

surprises.description: The call disclosed a clinical footprint and potential publication catalyst not highlighted in the preview: 11 active studies, 27 clinical sites, more than 400 patients treated, and an expected PEDIR study publication that management sees as a commercial catalyst.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has 11 active studies across 27 clinical sites with over 400 patients treated, and expects the PEDIR study publication to be a commercial catalyst.”

in_line: TriNav Advance remained uncleared and was still described as pending, consistent with the preview’s base expectation that it would remain pending; the preview had already flagged that it was past its MDUFA goal date.
Management’s expectation of improving sequential growth through the rest of the year was broadly consistent with the preview’s expectation of continued month-over-month growth in 2026.

surprises.description: Sprout raised its FY2026 non-GAAP operating income and EPS outlook well above the ranges in the preview, and raised its exit-Q4 margin target from about 15% to near 17%. The new operating-income midpoint is about 20% above the prior midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: FY2026 non-GAAP operating income guidance is $68.3–$70.3 million, up 20% at midpoint, and non-GAAP EPS guidance is $1.11–$1.15, up about 22% versus the prior outlook; management expects to exit Q4 2026 near a 17% non-GAAP operating margin.
surprises.expectation_evidence: FY2026 non-GAAP operating income: $54.9–$60.4M. FY26 non-GAAP EPS: $0.88–$0.97. Management targets exiting Q4'26 at ~15% non-GAAP operating margin.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue exceeded the preview’s consensus estimate and the previously announced high-end figure, although the gap was modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 revenue was $123.8 million, up 10.8% year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus: $122.19M (MarketBeat) or $121.29M (alt. source); pre-announced high end, ~$122.5M.

surprises.description: The Q3 revenue range is below the roughly $124–$126 million quarterly pace the preview said was needed to maintain the prior full-year revenue range. It is still above the preview’s specific approximately $123 million level associated with a full-year cut, and the supplied facts do not state a new FY revenue outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 revenue guidance is $123.3–$124.1 million, and management expects deceleration.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Implied H2 needs roughly $124–$126M per quarter to hold the FY range. Anything below ~$123M signals a full-year cut.

surprises.description: Management’s outlook for the smaller-customer cohort is weaker than the preview’s open question of whether it would stabilize: the cohort is expected to turn slightly negative before stabilizing in 2027. Management also expects CRPO to moderate, though no CRPO growth figure was provided to compare directly with the preview’s benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects CRPO to moderate and the sub-$30K cohort to turn slightly negative before stabilizing in 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Sub-$30K ARR cohort and NRR: whether Essentials stabilizes SMB. cRPO growth vs. ~10%; below ~8% is a bearish signal.

surprises.description: Sprout disclosed a roughly 20% workforce reduction and at least $50 million of annualized cost savings, but said the savings will not be fully realized until 2027. The preview discussed a possible RIF but did not specify a reduction of this scale or the savings and timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company announced a roughly 20% headcount reduction expected to cut its non-GAAP cost structure by at least $50 million on an annualized run-rate basis, though full realization will not occur until 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: A reframing of the RIF as deliberate SMB de-emphasis would reset the model, but would need an explicit FY27 framework.

surprises.description: Management identified lapping the Newswhip acquisition starting in Q3 2026 as a continuing headwind, a specific drag not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management flagged continuing headwinds including lapping the Newswhip acquisition starting Q3 2026.

in_line: The preview anticipated approximately $18–$20 million of restructuring charges substantially affecting Q3; the reported charges were approximately $18–$20 million, substantially all impacting Q3.
Management reaffirmed its target of reaching 30% under the Rule of 40 framework by Q4 2027, consistent with the preview’s stated target.

surprises.description: Grindr reported Q2 revenue of $138 million, about $6.6 million above the preview’s $131.4 million consensus estimate. The 33% year-over-year growth was a clear upside to the expected revenue level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 33% year-over-year to $138 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 consensus $131.4M (Zacks)”

surprises.description: Despite adjusted EBITDA reaching the top of the preview’s $56–58 million range, the 42% margin was below the expected 43% and the preview’s assumed Q2 margin. The shortfall was one percentage point.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $58 million at a 42% margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Margin ~43%”; “base case assumes about a 200bp sequential EBITDA margin decline, from 45.0% to 43.0%.”

surprises.description: Management said lower-than-expected churn and better price inelasticity after subscription increases drove much of the first-half outperformance. The preview did not identify this degree of customer retention and pricing resilience as a source of upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The guidance raise was driven primarily by first-half outperformance from lower-than-expected churn and better price inelasticity on subscription increases.”

surprises.description: Management described a substantial AI-related productivity gain: engineering output rose about 2.5 times with roughly the same team size, avoiding an estimated 200 hires and about $60 million in annual cost. The preview did not anticipate this efficiency or cost-avoidance estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Engineering output increased approximately 2.5x from July 2025 to April 2026 with roughly the same team size,” avoiding “an estimated 200 additional engineers and about $60 million in annual cost.”

surprises.description: For Edge, management said retention exceeded expectations and some non-paying users converted directly to the premium tier, contrary to initial assumptions. The preview flagged Edge timing and cohort data but did not anticipate these favorable conversion and retention observations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Edge AI-enabled premium tier is positioned as a key driver of 2027 revenue growth, with retention exceeding expectations and some non-paying users converting directly, contrary to initial assumptions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Grindr Edge timing and pricing”; “A disclosed price point or Q4 2026 window would be a catalyst.”

surprises.description: Grindr executed another accelerated share repurchase, paying $60 million upfront. The preview did not flag a new repurchase execution as an expected event.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company executed another accelerated share repurchase with a $60 million upfront payment and has approximately $300 million remaining under its $900 million buyback authorization.”

in_line: The company raised its FY2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance modestly, consistent with the preview’s base case of a guide “nudged up” rather than its bear case of reaffirmation; revenue guidance moved from $535 million to approximately $540 million and adjusted EBITDA from $227 million to approximately $232 million.
Adjusted EBITDA of $58 million was at the top of the preview’s $56–58 million range, even though the margin was below the preview’s 43% expectation.

Management expected Q3 and Q4 growth to decelerate as subscription-price changes are anniversaried and stronger 2025 comparisons are lapped, consistent with the preview’s expectation that growth would moderate in the second half.
Advertising growth remained strong at 44% year over year, while its growth rate was below Q1’s 68%, consistent with the preview’s concern that advertising growth would slow.

surprises.description: Cable One’s adjusted EBITDA came in below the preview’s $175–179 million working estimate, and its 49.7% margin was lower than the expected 50.8–51% and below the preview’s flagged 50% threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA was $173.5 million (49.7% margin), down from $203.2 million (53.3% margin) a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The working estimate is $175–179M at roughly 50.8–51% margin. A sub-50% margin would worsen the leverage math.”

surprises.description: Reported net leverage was 4.2x, below the preview’s estimated 4.5–4.7x range; Cable One also reduced debt by $63 million in the quarter, including nearly $60 million through voluntary repurchases at discounts.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company reduced debt by $63 million in Q2 and nearly $130 million year-to-date, ending with gross debt of $3.06 billion and net leverage of 4.2x.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pro forma net leverage is estimated at about 4.6x”; the base scenario anticipated “leverage about 4.5–4.7x.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag the sharp shift in sales channels: digital and direct sales rose from less than 10% of sales a year ago to roughly 35% in Q2, with management expecting digital alone to reach 35–40% within 12–18 months.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Digital and direct sales channels grew from less than 10% of sales a year ago to roughly 35% in Q2,” and management expects digital alone to reach “35%-40% within 12-18 months.”

in_line: Revenue of $348.9 million was within the preview’s $346–352 million pre-announced range and close to its roughly $350 million consensus estimate.
CapEx of $74 million matched the preview’s $72–76 million range and $74 million midpoint.
The 17,000 residential broadband customer losses were within the pre-announced range of 16,000–18,000 losses.
Management remained noncommittal on MBI, consistent with the preview’s base scenario; it gave no transaction update and declined financing questions.
Mobile remained small and was expected to take time to help retention, consistent with the preview’s focus on mobile traction as a longer-term issue.

surprises.description: Q1 revenue was $1.34 billion, above the preview’s roughly $1.30–$1.312 billion consensus and the company’s $1.300–$1.325 billion guide. Revenue grew 11%, its fastest rate since Gen was created.
