surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue…grew 11% year-over-year to $1.34 billion,” the “fastest revenue growth rate since Gen was created.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed revenue consensus of “~$1.300B… / $1.312B” and company guidance of “$1.300B – $1.325B.”

surprises.description: Q1 non-GAAP EPS reached $0.71, beating both the preview’s roughly $0.69 consensus and the $0.68–$0.70 guided range. The 19% year-over-year increase also exceeded the stated 13%–17% growth target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS reached $0.71, up 19% year-over-year and beating the guided range of $0.68-$0.70.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed non-GAAP EPS consensus of “$0.69… / $0.688” and company guidance of “$0.68 – $0.70.”

surprises.description: Gen raised its full-year revenue outlook, lifting the range to $5.375–$5.475 billion from $5.325–$5.425 billion. The new midpoint is above the preview’s $5.38 billion consensus midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year FY2027 guidance to 9%-11% revenue growth (to $5.375-$5.475 billion)…up from prior guidance of 8%-10% revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed prior FY27 revenue guidance of “$5.325B – $5.425B” and consensus of “$5.38B.”

surprises.description: Gen also raised its full-year non-GAAP EPS outlook to $2.87–$2.97 from $2.85–$2.95, moving the midpoint above the preview’s $2.90 consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year FY2027 guidance to…14%-18% non-GAAP EPS growth (to $2.87-$2.97), up from prior guidance of…mid-teens EPS.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed prior FY27 non-GAAP EPS guidance of “$2.85 – $2.95” and consensus of “$2.90.”

surprises.description: Cyber Safety bookings and revenue each grew only 4%. That was below the segment’s 5% exit-rate bookings pace highlighted in the preview and below the 6%–8% bookings growth the preview described as the bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cyber Safety bookings and revenue each grew only mid-single digits (4%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Cyber Safety bookings” versus the “+5%” exit rate and said the bull case depended on lifting bookings “toward 6–8%.”

surprises.description: Gross margin fell to 82% because of lower-margin marketplace revenue-share mix. The preview discussed mix risk from lower-margin Trust growth, but did not specifically anticipate this marketplace-related gross-margin pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin dipped to 82% due to lower-margin marketplace revenue-share mix.”

surprises.description: Norton showed stronger product traction than the preview had identified: cross-sell penetration rose to 27%, sales growth was its strongest in two years, and higher-tier Norton 360 memberships reached nearly $0.5 billion in annualized bookings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Norton cross-sell penetration rose one point to 27% with double-digit sales growth, the strongest in two years,” while “Norton 360's higher-tier memberships scaled to nearly $0.5 billion in annualized bookings.”

surprises.description: The Engine embedded marketplace had reached a $0.5 billion annual revenue run rate, with more than 30 new partnerships and annual network inquiries above $425 million—specific traction the preview did not quantify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Engine embedded marketplace surpassed a $0.5 billion annual revenue run rate with over 30 new partnerships added and total network inquiries exceeding $425 million annually.”

surprises.description: MoneyLion’s financial-account network and engagement reached substantial levels: connected accounts exceeded 110 million, and 35% of the paid base engaged with financial wellness. The preview highlighted the H2 embedded-finance contribution as uncertain but did not state expectations for these operating metrics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Connected financial accounts grew to over 110 million from 75 million at MoneyLion's acquisition, with 35% of the paid base now engaging with financial wellness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called the “$100M+ H2 FY27 contribution from embedded finance and Engine expansion” the “highest-variance item on the call,” but gave no account or engagement targets.

surprises.description: Net leverage was 2.95x, slightly below the 3.0x level cited in the preview. Gen also returned $181 million to shareholders, including $100 million of buybacks, though the preview did not set a quarterly return target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company returned $181 million to shareholders ($100 million buybacks, $81 million dividends)…and lowered net leverage to 2.95x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “net leverage 3.0x” and flagged “Buyback pace against the $2.1B authorization.”

in_line: Trust-Based Solution growth was close to the preview’s estimated pace: bookings grew 25% and revenue 24%, versus its estimated requirement of roughly 25%–28% clean growth.
Segment margins matched the preview’s framework: Cyber Safety margin was 61% versus an expectation of 60%+, and Trust-Based Solution margin was 30% versus an expectation of about 30%.

surprises.description: Bad Daddy’s same-store sales fell 2.3%, sharply missing the preview’s roughly +0.5% base-case expectation and moving further from the positive print it said could mark a turnaround. Management attributed the decline to reduced traffic and fewer operating restaurants.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bad Daddy's same-store sales declined 2.3% for the quarter and were down 1.5% year-to-date, hampered by reduced customer traffic and fewer operating restaurants.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (50%): … Bad Daddy's ~+0.5%”; the preview also said “A positive print would be the first in roughly two years.”

surprises.description: EPS was $0.18, twice the preview’s own estimate of about $0.09, a substantial upside surprise. Net income to common shareholders was $1.9 million versus $1.5 million a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income to common shareholders rose to $1.9 million, or $0.18 per share, versus $1.5 million, or $0.14 per share, in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The preview's own estimates are revenue ~$35.4M, EPS ~$0.09, and adj. EBITDA ~$2.3M.”

surprises.description: Good Times same-store sales turned positive, but the +0.6% result was well below the preview’s roughly +2% bar. The preview expected the brand to cross zero, so the positive direction was anticipated; the size of the improvement fell short.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Good Times same-store sales turned positive at +0.6% for Q3 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The preview's bar is roughly +2%”; its base case also expected “Good Times SSS ~+2.5%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $2.5 million, beating the preview’s $2.3 million estimate despite the weaker-than-expected Bad Daddy’s comp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased to $2.5 million from $2.1 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The preview's own estimates are … adj. EBITDA ~$2.3M.”

surprises.description: Good Times produced a stronger recent sales trend than its quarterly comp alone suggests: the Bambinos promotion drove mid-single-digit same-store growth in June, and management said the positive trend continued into Q4 and was considering extending the promotion beyond summer.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The $2 Bambinos slider promotion drove mid-single-digit same-store sales growth at Good Times during fiscal June,” management is “considering extending it beyond its planned summer end,” and the positive trend “has continued into the fourth fiscal quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that the “$2 Bambinos slider promotion began system-wide in June” and focused on whether it would lift traffic, but did not anticipate a mid-single-digit June result, continued Q4 trend, or possible extension.

surprises.description: Management said Good Times will not take further price increases for the rest of the year because of market competitiveness, limiting the near-term pricing contribution and making sales more dependent on traffic and promotions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management does not plan further Good Times price increases for the rest of the year due to market competitiveness,” after a 1.7% average menu price increase this quarter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Traffic vs. price mix” and cited prior-quarter menu price contribution, but did not forecast a pause in Good Times pricing.

surprises.description: The company paid down its revolving credit facility and ended with $3.6 million in cash and about $0.3 million of seller-finance long-term debt, a more favorable capital position than the preview’s Q2 snapshot of $2.7 million in cash and $1.0 million in debt suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company paid down its revolving credit facility and ended the quarter with $3.6 million in cash and only about $0.3 million in seller-finance long-term debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Debt was $1.0M at Q2 with $2.7M cash.”

surprises.description: Bad Daddy’s announced core menu additions for Q1 FY2027, including a sampler platter and an ahi tuna Power Bowl. The preview did not flag these upcoming launches, and their sales impact is not yet established.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bad Daddy's plans core menu additions in Q1 fiscal 2027, including its first-ever sampler platter and a new ahi tuna Power Bowl, absent from the core menu since 2019.”

in_line: Total revenue of $35.2 million was broadly in line with the preview’s own estimate of about $35.4 million.

surprises.description: Grove reported 509,000 active customers and 489,000 DTC orders, below the preview’s watch levels of at least 545,000 actives and more than 510,000 orders. The preview’s bearish cutoff for actives was below roughly 530,000, and the company attributed the declines to reduced ad spend and prior platform disruption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Active customers fell 23.3% year-over-year to 509,000 and DTC total orders declined 23.6% to 489,000, reflecting reduced ad spend and prior platform disruption.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for at least 545K actives and orders above 510K. Below roughly 530K would weaken the trough narrative”; the base scenario expected 535–550K actives.

surprises.description: Gross margin fell to 53.6%, below the preview’s 54.5% threshold for supporting the margin story and also below its roughly 54% warning level. The company cited inventory disposals and the non-recurrence of a prior-year reserved-inventory sell-through.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined 190 basis points to 53.6% due to one-time inventory disposals and the non-recurrence of a prior-year reserved inventory sell-through.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA of at least $0.5M with gross margin held at or above 54.5%”; “Margin below roughly 54% to buy volume would weaken the story.”

surprises.description: Net revenue was slightly below the $36.77 million consensus, though it landed within the preview’s base-case range and rose from Q1. The consensus miss was small rather than a failure to confirm the anticipated trough.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenue was $36.6 million, up 1% sequentially but down 16.9% year-over-year, confirming Q1 as the anticipated revenue trough.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 net revenue … Consensus $36.77M”; the base scenario was “$36.5–37.3M.”

surprises.description: The net loss was substantially smaller than the loss implied by the preview’s flagged EPS consensus. The preview estimated that a $(0.06) EPS result would require about a $2.5 million loss, while Grove reported a $0.9 million net loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed to $0.9 million (-2.5% margin) from $3.6 million (-8.2% margin) in the prior year, driven by structural cost reductions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A $(0.06) Q2 would need a loss of about $2.5M”; the preview cautioned that this EPS consensus might be stale.

surprises.description: Cash increased and operating cash flow turned positive, improving on the prior quarter’s negative operating cash flow. The preview flagged liquidity as an issue to watch but did not forecast this improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash rose to $11.4 million from $10.4 million, supported by $1.3 million of positive operating cash flow.”

surprises.description: CFO Tom Siragusa is leaving on August 16 to pursue another opportunity, with a successor search underway. The preview did not anticipate a CFO departure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Tom Siragusa is departing the company on August 16 to pursue a new opportunity, with a successor search underway.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was $0.5 million, matching the preview’s minimum watch level and the lower end of its $0.5–1.0 million base scenario.

The company reaffirmed FY2026 revenue guidance of $142.5–152.5 million and positive low-single-digit-millions adjusted EBITDA, as the preview’s base case expected; it also maintained the expectation of sequential revenue improvement in each remaining quarter.
Revenue rose 1% sequentially, consistent with the preview’s expectation that Q2 would exceed Q1’s $36.2 million level and confirm Q1 as the trough.
DTC revenue per order rose 6.1%, consistent with the preview’s base-case expectation that revenue growth could come through higher revenue per order while orders and actives declined.

surprises.description: Nerdy cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $168–175 million, below the preview’s $180–190 million outlook. The preview warned that a trim would signal a weaker institutional recovery, but the reported range is below even the preview’s bear-case threshold of $180 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nerdy cut its full-year revenue guidance to $168-175 million from $180-190 million,” attributing the reduction entirely to exiting Varsity Tutors for Schools and First Tutors.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue: $180–190M (affirmed)” and “any trim would be read as management conceding the institutional recovery”; the bear scenario was “FY guide cut below $180M.”

surprises.description: Rather than pursue the institutional recovery the preview was watching, Nerdy is winding down Varsity Tutors for Schools and exiting First Tutors—even though VT4S was profitable. The exits are expected to reduce the annual fixed-cost run rate by about $11 million, but bring $2–4 million of exit costs, mostly in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is winding down Varsity Tutors for Schools (a profitable, low single-digit revenue business) and exiting First Tutors, lowering annual fixed cost run rate by approximately $11 million but incurring $2-4 million in exit costs mostly in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bookings near $4M would support the second-half institutional assumption.”

surprises.description: Year-end cash guidance fell to $30–32 million from $40–45 million, a much steeper reduction than the preview’s roughly $40 million cash watchpoint. The company attributed the shortfall to lost VT4S prepaid annual collections and wind-down costs, not weaker consumer economics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-end cash guidance was lowered to $30-32 million from $40-45 million, driven by lost VT4S prepaid annual collections and wind-down costs rather than changes in consumer economics.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 year-end cash: $40–45M (includes $20M term loan draw)” and “Cash vs. ~$40M and the $20M term loan draw.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA loss was narrower than the preview’s roughly $1 million loss expectation and beat the midpoint of company guidance. This was a modest positive result despite revenue landing near consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 68% year-over-year to $0.9 million from $2.7 million, beating the midpoint of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (Q2): ~−$1M” and company guidance of “−$2M to breakeven.”

surprises.description: The reported 29,100 Active Learning Memberships were well below the preview’s approximately 35,000-member watchpoint. However, the year-over-year decline was 5%—within the preview’s expected range—and management still expects positive member growth by year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Active Learning Memberships fell 5% year-over-year to 29,100,” with the decline moderating for a fourth consecutive quarter; management expects positive member growth by end of 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Active Members vs. ~35K and the −9% decline rate” and “Q2 needs the decline to narrow toward −4% to −6%.”

surprises.description: AI-related expenses rose sharply, reaching $2 million in Q2 versus $0.4 million a year earlier, even as the company substantially reduced staffing. The preview did not flag a comparable AI spending ramp.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total headcount fell 34% year-over-year and the engineering team shrank 30%, while AI-related expenses rose to $2 million (up from $0.7 million in Q1 and $0.4 million a year ago).”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $43.3 million, close to the $43.0 million consensus and within company guidance of $42–44 million.
Membership decline was 5% year-over-year, within the preview’s expected range of a 4%–6% decline, and management reiterated the end-of-2026 positive-growth goal.
ARPUM rose 5% year-over-year to $366; the preview anticipated growth moderating as the company began lapping the February 2025 price increases.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $168.6 million, above both the $165 million high end of company guidance and the $157.8 million consensus estimate. That is a clear upside beat against the preview’s near-guide expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $168.6 million” and “coming in above the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Company guidance (Q2) $150M – $165M” and “Consensus … $157.8M.”

surprises.description: NETGEAR swung to $4 million of non-GAAP operating profit and reported $0.16 in non-GAAP EPS, exceeding the preview’s $0.01 EPS consensus and the 2.0% top end of its Q2 operating-margin guidance. The EPS gap was especially large relative to the estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company swung to a non-GAAP operating profit of $4 million (2.4% margin) from an operating loss a year ago, delivering non-GAAP EPS of $0.16.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op. margin … (1.0)% – 2.0%” and “EPS … $0.01 non-GAAP.”

surprises.description: Enterprise revenue reached $89 million, above the preview’s $85 million watch threshold, while growing 7.7% year over year. The segment therefore cleared the preview’s stated level for supporting the bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enterprise segment revenue grew 7.7% year-over-year to $89 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Enterprise above $85M … would support the bull case.”

surprises.description: Enterprise gross margin was 54.1%, above the preview’s 52% benchmark, and enterprise contribution margin also reached its highest level since Q1 2019. The margin performance was stronger than the preview’s already-positive threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Enterprise non-GAAP gross margin hit an all-time high of 54.1%” and “enterprise contribution margin rose 660 basis points to 25.9%, its highest since Q1 2019.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Enterprise above $85M with gross margin at or above 52% would support the bull case.”

surprises.description: Consumer gross margin fell to 27.3%, below the preview’s 29% bear-case threshold, as memory costs and competitor pricing pressured the business. The decline is a negative result against the preview’s explicit margin watchpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consumer segment revenue fell 9.4% year-over-year to $79.6 million and gross margin declined 210 basis points to 27.3% amid rising memory costs and aggressive competitor pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bear scenario flagged “consumer GM below 29%.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $165–175 million has a $170 million midpoint, below the preview’s roughly $176.1 million consensus. The range overlaps the preview’s base-case range, but the midpoint still signals a modest shortfall versus consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q3 2026 revenue to $165-175 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 FY26 revenue … ~$176.1M.”

surprises.description: Management said APAC enterprise revenue fell 16% year over year, unlike growth in the Americas and EMEA, and responded with a go-to-market restructuring and new regional leadership. The preview did not flag this regional weakness or restructuring.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APAC enterprise revenue declined 16% year-over-year, contrasting with 15% growth in the Americas and 9% in EMEA, prompting a go-to-market restructuring and new regional leadership.”

surprises.description: NETGEAR secured memory supply through the first half of 2027, extending coverage beyond the preview’s reported arrangements for 2026. The preview specifically noted that 2027 coverage was not modeled, so this was an unanticipated positive update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company secured memory supply through the first half of 2027.”

in_line: Management maintained the roughly 200-basis-point second-half gross-margin headwind from memory costs, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a reaffirmed ~200bp headwind.

The company repurchased 560,000 shares for $12.9 million, leaving about $75 million of authorization versus roughly $89 million after Q1; the preview had flagged buybacks near $24 and whether the authorization would be used.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.40, above the preview’s $0.32–$0.35 consensus range. That is a clear beat, even though the preview had anticipated a FY26 EPS guidance increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose 24% to $0.40,” aided by lower interest expense, a lower tax rate, and reduced share count.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. Diluted EPS” consensus was “$0.32–$0.35.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow was a $50 million inflow in a quarter the preview warned could bring a second straight outflow. The full-year free cash flow outlook was maintained, as the preview expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was a positive $50 million inflow in a seasonally cash-use quarter,” while full-year guidance remained “$270–$300 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a second straight quarterly outflow would strain the guide” and listed the FY $270–$300 million guide as a key metric.

surprises.description: Component Repair Services grew 9.2%, falling short of the preview’s expectation for clean double-digit growth. Its margin also declined 270 basis points to 26.3%, with management attributing the pressure to work migration, labor ramp-up, and military input delays.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Component Repair Services revenue grew 9.2% to $195 million,” but segment adjusted EBITDA margin “fell 270 basis points to 26.3%”; management expected a return to high-20% margins in the second half.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “clean double-digit growth is the expectation” for Component Repair Services.

surprises.description: StandardAero announced a $180 million license expansion with an OEM partner that is expected to add about $25 million of annual adjusted EBITDA at full run rate. The preview did not flag a deal of this kind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed a $180 million license expansion with an OEM partner expected to add roughly $25 million in incremental annual adjusted EBITDA at full run rate” ($10 million in 2027, $20 million in 2028, and $25 million in 2029+).

surprises.description: The company reported that LEAP and CFM56 Dallas-Fort Worth had both reached profitability. This was confirmation of the preview’s anticipated H1 profitability milestone, rather than a meaningful departure from expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's LEAP and CFM56 Dallas-Fort Worth programs both reached profitability in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Confirmation that LEAP and CFM56 turned profitable in H1 2026 matters.”

surprises.description: Commercial aerospace growth was mid-teens after excluding the elimination of $300–$400 million of low- or no-margin pass-through revenue in 2026, versus reported growth of 6%. The preview noted a prior-quarter pass-through inventory drawdown but did not anticipate this explanation of the underlying growth rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding the elimination of $300-$400 million of low/no-margin material pass-through revenue in 2026, commercial aerospace grew mid-teens versus the reported 6%.”

surprises.description: Moody’s and S&P upgraded the company’s ratings, a development not identified in the preview. The preview had noted leverage of 2.6x, but did not anticipate ratings upgrades.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received ratings upgrades from Moody's (Ba2) and S&P (BB).”

in_line: Revenue of $1.6 billion was broadly in line with the preview’s $1.58–$1.59 billion consensus range, though slightly above it.
Adjusted EBITDA of $230 million exceeded the preview’s roughly $225.5 million threshold for meeting management’s double-digit growth commitment; reported growth was 12.3%.

Full-year guidance was raised, consistent with the preview’s expectation that guidance would be narrowed or raised. Revenue rose by $50 million to $6.375–$6.5 billion, adjusted EBITDA guidance moved to $885–$910 million, and adjusted EPS guidance to $1.50–$1.57; the preview had specifically identified an EPS raise as a possible bull scenario.
Full-year adjusted free cash flow guidance remained $270–$300 million, as in the preview.
Net leverage was 2.6x, the same level the preview cited after Q1.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $4.44 billion implied by the reported 4.6% growth and the preview’s $4.24 billion prior-year figure, above the $4.36 billion consensus estimate. The revenue result was stronger than the preview’s base-case range of $4.34–$4.37 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue grew 4.6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 consensus” revenue: “$4.36B”; base scenario: “$4.34–4.37B.”

surprises.description: Management raised the full-year revenue, adjusted EBITDA, EPS, and free cash flow guidance ranges, whereas the preview considered a revenue trim likely and expected EPS and FCF to be held. The roughly $40 million EBITDA increase was mostly tied to higher commodity prices and incremental acquisitions, rather than a broad increase in operating assumptions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $17.2-17.3 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $5.525-5.55 billion, adjusted EPS of $7.23-7.28, and adjusted free cash flow of $2.54-2.575 billion”; the “~$40 million EBITDA guidance increase was driven mostly by higher commodity prices (~$25 million) with the remainder from incremental acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A revenue trim with EPS and FCF held is the likely outcome. An FCF guidance cut is the main bear trigger.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $1.85 was above the $1.81 consensus and reached the top of the preview’s base-case range. The beat was modest rather than a match for the preview’s bull-case range, which began at $1.87.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS of $1.85.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 consensus” adjusted EPS: “$1.81”; base scenario: “$1.81–1.85.”

surprises.description: Although reported adjusted EBITDA margin was 32.1%, matching the prior year, management had pre-guided to Q2 margins being somewhat flat to slightly down. Underlying business margins instead expanded 90 basis points, with core pricing outpacing cost inflation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin maintained at 32.1%”; “core price on related revenue was 6.4%,” exceeding cost inflation and “driving 90 basis points of underlying margin expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management pre-guided flat to down, so a print at or above 32.1% is an upside surprise.”

surprises.description: Year-to-date acquisition closings reached nearly $1.2 billion, well beyond the preview’s stated level of more than $700 million deployed year to date. The acquisitions were included in the raised guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Republic invested nearly $1.2 billion in acquisitions closed year-to-date (all included in guidance).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “More than $700M was deployed year to date against a raised FY target of more than $1.0B.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed more than $1 billion of shareholder returns, including buybacks equivalent to about 1% of shares. The preview had noted the dividend increase but did not flag this scale of repurchases or total returns.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Returned over $1 billion to shareholders via dividends and buybacks (~1% of shares) while raising its dividend for the 23rd consecutive year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Dividend: Raised July 30, 2026.”

in_line: Large container volume declined 2.2%, a modest improvement from Q1’s 2.5% decline, consistent with the preview’s expectation that further improvement would support the trough call.

Environmental Solutions revenue rose sequentially and its margin improved; the expectation of year-over-year revenue growth in the second half remained in place, consistent with the preview’s view that Q2 needed to mark the trough.

surprises.description: Gross margin rose to about 43%, well above the preview’s 31% Q1 reference and its concern that pass-through refrigeration content could weigh on margins. The call attributed the improvement to favorable contract mix and Novera QPU contributions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to approximately 43% in Q2 2026 from 31% a year earlier, reflecting favorable contract mix and Novera QPU contributions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin 31%” in Q1; “margins are diluted by pass-through refrigeration content, which can fall as system complexity rises.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted a 99.5% two-qubit fidelity target by year-end 2026, while the call described a target of about 99.9% within roughly three years and identified coherence time as the main constraint. That points to a longer timeline for the higher fidelity milestone than the preview led investors to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Current coherence times of 25-30 microseconds are the primary constraint on fidelity” and management is targeting “99.9% two-qubit fidelity” within “roughly three years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “99.5% median two-qubit gate fidelity on the 108-qubit Cepheus system targeted by year-end 2026.”

surprises.description: Quarter-end cash and investments were about $541.3 million, below the preview’s modeled range of $545 million to $555 million. The company remained debt-free, but cash fell from $569 million at the end of Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 2026 with approximately $541.3 million in cash and investments and no debt, down from $569 million at March 31.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Cash estimates were modeled at “roughly ... $545M to $555M.”

surprises.description: Prepayments for the known C-DAC order drove a significant increase in deferred revenue, providing an additional positive indicator of customer funding ahead of the expected Q4 installation and acceptance. The preview flagged the low RPO and the need to watch for growth, but did not anticipate this specific update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Prepayments [are] driving a significant increase in deferred revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “RPO was only $2.8M at March 31. Watch for growth and new order announcements.”

in_line: Revenue of approximately $5.1 million matched the preview’s $5.09–$5.13 million consensus range.
Non-GAAP net loss of $16 million, or $0.05 per diluted share, matched the preview’s -$0.05 EPS estimate.
Operating loss of $28.1 million was within the preview’s modeled range of roughly $26 million to $29 million.
The $8.4 million C-DAC system remained expected to be recognized in Q4 2026 after installation and acceptance testing, as the preview’s base case anticipated.
The CHIPS Act arrangement remained a non-definitive letter of intent for up to $100 million over three years involving a government equity stake, consistent with the preview’s description.
Elevated 2026 CapEx and a potential investment of up to $100 million over time in the U.K.’s ProQure initiative were consistent with the preview’s warnings about higher CapEx and the U.K. commitment.

surprises.description: HCAT guided FY26 adjusted EBITDA to $18–18.5 million, down from the preview’s cited $30–33 million pre-divestiture guide. The Vitalware sale was expected to require an adjustment, but the reported outlook is sharply lower and the facts do not provide a bridge showing how much of the reduction is solely the expected removal of Vitalware.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year 2026 guidance was cut to… adjusted EBITDA of $18 million to $18.5 million, primarily reflecting the removal of 5 months of Vitalware revenue and EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA… $30–33M”; the preview also says the Vitalware divestiture was expected to close in Q3.

surprises.description: Q3 guidance calls for only $55–56 million of revenue and breakeven to $0.5 million of adjusted EBITDA. That is a particularly weak near-term outlook against the preview’s implied second-half revenue of $120–125 million and its expectation that the FY26 EBITDA guide would be $30–33 million before the divestiture adjustment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for total revenue of just $55 million to $56 million and adjusted EBITDA of only breakeven to $500,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The FY26 revenue guide implies 2H revenue of $120–125M”; “FY26 adj. EBITDA… $30–33M.”

surprises.description: HCAT said full-year adjusted gross margin is now expected below 50%, with technology margins in the low 60s and professional services in the low-to-mid teens. The preview cited Q1 adjusted gross margin of 51% but did not flag an expected decline below that level; the company attributed the pressure to migrations and HIE data-loading costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year adjusted gross margin is now expected to fall below 50%… pressured by client migrations and HIE data loading costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA $9.1M; adj. gross margin 51%.”

surprises.description: Some DOS-to-Ignite churn has pulled forward into the second half, making the timing of the migration headwind worse than the preview’s cited expectation that about $20 million of the remaining $30 million at-risk ARR would affect 2026. The expected retained ARR remained at the $22 million floor, but management said the headwinds will persist through the end of 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Some churn has pulled forward into the second half”; “headwinds expected to persist through end of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The remaining $30M is expected to hit about $20M in 2026 and $10M in 2027”; “at least $22M of the $52M at-risk ARR is now expected to be retained.”

surprises.description: Professional services revenue is now expected to exit the year at the lower end of prior expectations, closer to $55 million annually. The preview highlighted bookings but did not identify this lower services-revenue outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Services revenue is now expected to exit the year at the lower end of prior expectations, closer to $55 million annually.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Lower end of prior expectations, closer to $55 million annually.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.04, double the preview’s $0.02 consensus estimate. This was a positive earnings-per-share surprise even though adjusted EBITDA landed at the high end of guidance rather than above it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income per share was $0.04.”

surprises.description: HCAT reported about $19 million of annual GAAP interest expense and roughly $16.5 million of annual cash interest payments eliminated after repaying its debt. The preview anticipated the facility payoff but did not quantify these ongoing interest savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Eliminate approximately $19 million of annual GAAP interest expense and roughly $16.5 million of annual cash interest payments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Post-close, proceeds plus cash are expected to repay and terminate the facility.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $70.5 million, $0.5 million above the high end of guidance and $1.5 million above the $69 million consensus estimate. The beat was modest, but exceeded the preview’s base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $70.5 million, exceeding the high end of the guided $68 million to $70 million range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue… $68–70M”; “Consensus $69.0M.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $9.9 million, within the $9–10 million guidance range and essentially in line with the approximately $9.5 million consensus estimate.
The $22–26 million FY26 bookings target was maintained, matching the preview’s cited target.
Management expected $22 million of the $52 million at-risk ARR to be retained, matching the preview’s stated floor.

The Vitalware sale and repayment of the credit facility were anticipated; the preview expected the divestiture to close in Q3 and the proceeds plus cash to be used to repay and terminate the facility.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $42.8 million, well below the preview’s $53.7–$59.3 million implied range and $54.27 million consensus. The preview’s estimates were for net product revenue, while the call fact reports total revenue, so the measures are not perfectly aligned.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue declined 58% year-over-year in Q2 2026 to $42.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net product revenue (Q2) … Implied $53.7M – $59.3M … Consensus $54.27M.”

surprises.description: Organogenesis cut FY26 revenue guidance to $179–$215 million, far below the preview’s expected $270–$310 million range. Management attributed the deeper cut to a slower-than-expected recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company slashed its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $179-215 million … down sharply from prior guidance of a 45-52% decline, due to a slower-than-expected recovery.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue … $270M – $310M”; the preview identified whether that range was “reaffirmed, narrowed, or cut” as a key issue.

surprises.description: The preview anticipated about $14 million of annualized savings from the March restructuring; the call reported that two 2026 restructurings, including a June reduction of 138 employees, are expected to save more than $32 million annually combined.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Two 2026 restructurings, including a June workforce reduction of 138 employees, are expected to cut annual operating expenses by more than $32 million combined.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “March restructuring: 88 positions cut and the St. Petersburg site closed, for roughly $14M of annualized savings.”

surprises.description: The company entered an agreement allowing it to sell up to $75 million of common stock. The preview noted a financing overhang, but did not identify this specific potential source of shareholder dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company entered an ATM agreement to sell up to $75 million of common stock, signaling potential shareholder dilution to fund operations and strategic initiatives.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Downside dominates on any guidance cut, given the financing overhang.”

surprises.description: The call reported a roughly $30 million non-cash tax expense from recording a full valuation allowance on deferred tax assets, contributing to a $96.3 million GAAP net loss. The preview listed a GAAP EPS consensus but did not flag this tax charge; the call facts do not provide actual EPS for a direct comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss was $96.3 million versus $9.4 million last year, including roughly $30 million of non-cash tax expense from recording a full valuation allowance on deferred tax assets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS, GAAP (Q2) … Consensus $(0.35).”

surprises.description: Despite the overall revenue shortfall, net product revenue rose 18% sequentially and wound care unit volume rose 30% versus Q1, with management pointing to market share gains. The preview anticipated a recovery in Q2 revenue but did not specifically anticipate this volume and share-gain commentary.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net product revenue increased 18% quarter-over-quarter, with advanced wound care sales up 23% sequentially and wound care unit volume up 30% versus Q1, indicating market share gains as the market resets.”

surprises.description: The FDA accepted the MNUVIX osteoarthritis biologic’s BLA and set an April 24, 2027 PDUFA target date, a regulatory milestone and potential new market opportunity not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The MNUVIX osteoarthritis biologic received FDA BLA acceptance with a PDUFA target date of April 24, 2027, potentially creating a new market category addressing over 30 million Americans with symptomatic knee osteoarthritis.”

in_line: Non-GAAP gross margin was 49%, within the preview’s expected 48–52% range, despite GAAP gross margin being 45%.
Cash of $46.8 million was near the preview’s estimate of roughly $50 million at quarter-end after an expected $35–45 million burn.
Management expects positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 2026, consistent with the preview’s expectation of positive adjusted EBITDA in H2.

surprises.description: Yelp generated $376 million of Q2 revenue, $8 million above the high end of its outlook and above the preview’s roughly $367 million consensus estimate, despite year-over-year growth remaining just 1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net revenue rose just 1% year-over-year to $376 million,” and “came in $8 million above the high end” of outlook.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue | $366.7M (~flat y/y)” and company guidance of “$363M – $368M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $91 million, well above the preview’s roughly $73 million expectation and the company’s $70–75 million Q2 guidance, even though EBITDA declined year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined 9% to $91 million (24% margin), the latter beating guidance by $16 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA | ~$73M (guide midpoint)” and company guidance of “$70M – $75M.”

surprises.description: Paying advertising locations recovered much more than the preview’s stabilization scenario implied: they rose to 510,000 and were down only 1% year over year, versus the preview’s 485,000 Q1 level and 6% decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Paying advertising locations declined only 1% year-over-year to 510,000, an improvement over Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Stabilization near 485,000 would be the strongest bull datapoint”; the preview also cited Q1 at “485,000, -6% y/y.”

surprises.description: Ad clicks fell only 5%, substantially less than the preview’s downside watch of declines faster than 10%; however, CPC growth slowed to 1%, so the offset from pricing was weaker than in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ad clicks fell 5% year-over-year … while average CPC rose 1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for clicks falling faster than -10% while CPC growth slows.”

surprises.description: The ad-revenue mix showed a sharper weakness in RR&O than the topline alone suggested: RR&O ads fell 10% while services ads were flat, with the company citing a challenging local business environment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Services ad revenue was flat year-over-year at $241 million while RR&O ad revenue declined 10% to $102 million, reflecting a challenging local business environment.”

surprises.description: The buyback slowdown became more pronounced than a general risk: Yelp repurchased only $15 million in Q2, about $25 million in Q3, and has paused repurchases while paying down its revolving credit facility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased $15 million of shares in Q2 … and ~$25 million in Q3 (~$200 million total for the year), but has paused buybacks to pay down its revolving credit facility with resumption expected in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buyback pace vs. cash. Repurchases ran about 3x FCF in Q1. A slowdown would remove a main EPS support.”

surprises.description: Yelp’s Q3 outlook signals lower near-term EBITDA profitability: it guided to just $70–75 million of adjusted EBITDA on $365–370 million of revenue, citing increased investment in AI, Hatch, and consumer marketing. That is a roughly 19–21% margin, below the preview’s implied roughly 22.8% H2 margin if the FY EBITDA range were maintained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Third quarter guidance calls for revenue of $365-370 million and adjusted EBITDA of only $70-75 million, reflecting increased investment spending on AI, Hatch, and consumer marketing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “H1 is roughly 47.5% of the midpoint at the Q2 guide, so holding the range implies an H2 margin around 22.8%. A trim is the main risk.”

surprises.description: Yelp Host showed substantial adoption and product expansion that the preview did not flag: its call-handling run rate more than tripled from January, and it added OpenTable integration, 16 languages, and food ordering.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Yelp Host reached an annual run rate of 2.4 million calls handled in July, more than tripling from January, and added OpenTable integration, 16 new languages, and food ordering functionality.”

surprises.description: Hatch’s annualized revenue growth was strong, but Yelp also disclosed that aggressive hiring caused an adjustment period in Q2, an operational headwind not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hatch annual run rate revenue grew 59% year-over-year to $35 million in June, though an aggressive team expansion caused an adjustment period in Q2.”

in_line: Other revenue was $33 million, just above the preview’s $32 million threshold for keeping the path to the $250 million end-of-2028 annual run rate credible.

surprises.description: Gas realizations were reported at 90% of Henry Hub before hedges and 123% including hedges, versus the preview’s Q1 benchmark of 72%. That is a substantial improvement on the gas-realization issue the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gas realizations at 90% of Henry Hub (123% including hedges).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Waha/Permian gas realization percentage relative to the Q1 level of 72%”; “Confirmation of H2 relief matters for 2027 estimates.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s focus on possible Waha relief, management said challenging Waha economics led to curtailments in Permian volumes. The amount curtailed was not provided, so the size of the shortfall from any expected relief is unclear.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Permian volumes were curtailed due to challenging Waha economics.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Waha averaged about –$2.40/MMBtu through mid-2026, improving to –$0.37 by Jun 5 on the GCX expansion. Confirmation of H2 relief matters for 2027 estimates.”

surprises.description: Management added a forceful valuation argument that the preview did not flag: it estimated NOG’s assets were worth more than $7 billion against a $4.6 billion enterprise value, and contrasted the stock’s flat year-to-date performance with peers’ 40%–50% gains. The shareholder implication is ambiguous because the claim is management’s valuation view, while the peer comparison highlights relative underperformance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management asserts a major valuation disconnect, estimating assets are worth $7 billion-plus versus a $4.6 billion enterprise value, and noted the stock was flat year-to-date while peers rose 40%-50%.”

in_line: Q2 free cash flow was $159 million, within the preview’s own $110–$165 million estimate, despite rising more than 400% sequentially.
Q2 capital expenditures of $196 million were within the pre-announced $190–$200 million range.
The approximately $243 million buyback authorization, $20.37 average repurchase price, and $0.45 quarterly dividend were all anticipated in the preview.
Management reiterated full-year production and capex guidance, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Ouster reported $55 million of Q2 revenue, above the $51.6–51.9 million consensus and the $52.5 million high end of company guidance. The beat was larger than the preview’s already-raised estimates implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q2 2026 revenue of $55 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $51.6–51.9M” and company guidance of “$49.5–52.5M.”

surprises.description: The 49% GAAP gross margin was well above the preview’s 42–44% expectation, but a roughly 1,000-basis-point one-time refund lifted the reported figure. Normalized margin in the high-30s was below the preview’s expected reported margin, though within the long-term 35–40% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP gross margin was 49%, but included a one-time refund benefit of roughly 1,000 basis points, meaning normalized gross margin was in the high-30s”; management reaffirmed a “35%-40% long-term range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP gross margin | ~42–44% (buy-side)” and “LT target 35–40%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA loss of $4 million was better than the preview’s expected loss of $5–7 million, an improvement beyond the anticipated modest year-over-year improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was negative $4 million, a roughly $1 million improvement versus Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~–$5M to –$7M (buy-side)” and “Modest improvement.”

surprises.description: The call facts report total revenue but do not provide the organic-versus-StereoLabs split the preview identified as a key issue. That leaves investors without the requested detail on how much of the growth came from the acquired business.
surprises.fact_evidence: The reported revenue figure is “$55 million”; no organic-versus-StereoLabs revenue split is provided in the call facts.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management needs to disaggregate” organic versus StereoLabs revenue; “Silence here will likely be read negatively.”

surprises.description: Ouster disclosed multiple million-dollar-plus Rev8 orders and a Utah DOT deployment covering several hundred intersections, while Rev8 contributed only minor prototype sales in Q2 and production volumes are expected by the end of Q3. The order wins provide an additional commercial validation point not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rev8 contributed only minor prototype sales in Q2, with production volumes expected by the end of Q3”; it “already secured multiple million-dollar-plus orders from Fortune 500 customers, plus a Utah DOT order covering several hundred intersections statewide, its largest lidar deployment to date.”

surprises.description: The call facts do not attach dollar amounts to the defense wins the preview singled out for quantification. As a result, the contribution of those opportunities to revenue remains unclear.
surprises.fact_evidence: The call facts provide no dollar figures for ARGUS, Gecko Robotics, or FUJIFILM defense wins.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Defense revenue attached to the ARGUS, Gecko, and FUJIFILM wins.”

in_line: Q3 revenue guidance of $54.5–57.5 million broadly matched the preview’s $55–58 million buy-side anchor, with a $56 million midpoint.
Normalized gross margin in the high-30s remained within management’s reiterated long-term 35–40% margin range.

surprises.description: ANI cut its full-year Cortrophin Gel guidance to $520–540 million, rather than maintaining the previously guided $540–575 million range. The revised range implies roughly a $30 million reduction, despite Q2 revenue of $117.1 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management modestly lowered full-year Cortrophin Gel revenue guidance to $520–540 million from prior expectations, implying roughly a $30 million cut.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Cortrophin Gel: $540–575M (vs. $347.8M in FY25).

surprises.description: Q3 Cortrophin guidance of $143–153 million is below the roughly $175 million per-quarter H2 pace implied by the preview's prior full-year guidance. Management expects a significantly larger step-up in Q4, so the ramp is more back-end-loaded than that earlier pace implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 2026 Cortrophin revenue is guided to $143–153 million, with management expecting a significantly larger step-up in Q4.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Reaffirmed Cortrophin guidance implies ... about $175M per quarter [in H2].

surprises.description: ANI reported Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $71.6 million, well above the preview's approximately $63 million expectation. That is a roughly 14% gap to the estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA grew 32% to an all-time high of $71.6 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Adj. non-GAAP EBITDA: ~$63M (guided).

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was 62.6%, above the preview's expected 60–61% range, even though the reported margin declined year over year because of product mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: Non-GAAP gross margin declined about 230 basis points year-over-year to 62.6% due to product mix.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Non-GAAP gross margin: ~60–61%.

surprises.description: The gout launch produced strong early case activity: more than 95% of new reps generated multiple new cases, and over one-third of prescribers started two or more patient cases. The preview expected the launch's main impact in 2027, rather than highlighting this degree of early activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: Over 95% of new reps [were] generating multiple new cases and over one-third of prescribers [were] initiating two or more patient cases.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Full deployment was slated for end-June, with revenue first occurring late in Q2 and the main impact in 2027.

surprises.description: The gout launch's commercial deployment was described as a 180-person rare disease sales force, larger than the preview's description of an approximately 90-person dedicated team. The larger deployment also adds operating expense, which management said would weigh on Q3 EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company expanded its rare disease sales force by 50% (from ~120 to ~180 reps) for its acute gouty arthritis flare launch.
surprises.expectation_evidence: A ~90-person dedicated commercial team targets primary care and podiatry for acute gouty arthritis flares.

surprises.description: Management expects Q3 adjusted EBITDA to decline sequentially, citing a smaller Harmony milestone and the first fully loaded quarter of gout expansion expenses. That near-term earnings drag was not called out in the preview's expectation that 55–58% of the year's earnings would come in H2.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 adjusted EBITDA is expected to decline sequentially due to only $2 million remaining Harmony milestone (vs. $8 million in Q2) and the first fully loaded quarter of gout expansion operating expenses.
surprises.expectation_evidence: EPS requires 55–58% of the year's earnings in H2.

surprises.description: The call reported $17.7 million of Q2 revenue from the Harmony licensing deal, a contribution the preview did not anticipate when it noted that the prior quarter's $15 million Harmony upfront would not recur.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Harmony licensing deal contributed $17.7 million in Q2 revenue.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The quarter included a $15M Harmony upfront that does not repeat.

surprises.description: Q2 total revenue of $266 million modestly exceeded the preview's $262.7 million consensus estimate, a gap of about 1.3%.
surprises.fact_evidence: ANI reported record Q2 2026 total net revenues of $266 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Total net revenue | Q2 2026 Consensus: $262.7M.

in_line: Q2 Cortrophin Gel revenue of $117.1 million was within management's previewed $113–132 million framing for the quarter.
The full-year revenue, adjusted EPS, and adjusted EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed, consistent with the preview's base scenario of a reaffirm-only outcome.
The gout sales force was fully operational by the end of June, as the preview said was slated.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $115 million, below the preview’s $130–150 million whisper range (and further below the published estimate of about $173 million). The preview anticipated unfavorable sports outcomes, but the reported result was also dampened by higher-than-expected customer acquisition spending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DraftKings generated $115 million of adjusted EBITDA in Q2 2026,” dampened by “customer-friendly sport outcomes (an ~$80 million revenue headwind) and higher-than-expected customer acquisition spend.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA against the $130–150M whisper”; “Anything at or above $160M would be a clear upside surprise.”

surprises.description: DraftKings maintained its $700–900 million full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance rather than cutting it, despite the preview viewing a cut as plausible and saying the high end looked arithmetically out of reach. Management also said the core business alone was on track to deliver about $1 billion in adjusted EBITDA, with Predictions investment included in the total-company outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company maintained its full-year 2026 guidance of $6.5 billion to $6.9 billion in revenue and $700 million to $900 million in adjusted EBITDA,” with “its core business alone on track to deliver approximately $1 billion in adjusted EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A cut toward $600–750M is a plausible outcome”; “The $900M high end looks arithmetically out of reach”; “A cut to about $650M is largely priced in.”

surprises.description: Sportsbook handle grew faster than the preview’s bullish mid-single-digit scenario and accelerated further in July, even after the World Cup ended. That performance eased the preview’s concern that prediction markets might weaken sportsbook demand; management also said prediction-market volume in Sportsbook states is mostly from professional and institutional traders, with only about 1% customer overlap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sportsbook handle rose 11% year-over-year in Q2 and accelerated to 20% growth year-over-year in July even after the World Cup ended”; “80% to 90% of prediction market volume in Sportsbook states comes from professional syndicates and institutional traders, with only ~1% customer overlap.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said structural hold and handle growth would show “whether the miss is outcome noise or demand erosion,” and described the bull case as “handle up mid-single digits” versus the bear case of “Handle flat or down.”

surprises.description: Predictions showed substantial early activity: annualized trading volume grew nearly fivefold from April to July, more than 600,000 customers had engaged year-to-date, and combos had already reached nearly 20% of volume. The preview wanted engagement disclosure but did not anticipate these specific scale and adoption figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Predictions annualized total volume traded grew nearly 5x from $2.3 billion in April to $11 billion in July, with over 600,000 customers engaging year-to-date”; “combos already represent nearly 20% of Predictions volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Predictions spend and first engagement disclosure” and said “a predictions number near $400M without engagement data would be a bear signal.”

surprises.description: Customer acquisition grew nearly 75% year over year while acquisition costs were about 25% better than anticipated and at their best enterprise-wide level since Q1 2025. Spending was about 10% above plan, but the reported acquisition efficiency was better than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customer acquisition grew nearly 75% year-over-year in Q2 at the best enterprise-wide CAC since Q1 2025, with acquisition costs coming in approximately 25% better than anticipated despite spending about 10% more than planned.”

surprises.description: The preview cited iGaming share slippage as a concern, but management reported that share had stabilized after several quarters of losses, helped by the Lightning Link and Flex Spins launches.
surprises.fact_evidence: “iGaming share stabilized after several quarters of losses, aided by the Lightning Link and Flex Spins launches.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Predictions spend and iGaming share” and said “DB flagged iGaming share slippage.”

surprises.description: Customer monetization and payer growth were positive: trailing 12-month net revenue per unique customer rose 14% year over year, while monthly unique payers grew 9% (over 6% excluding World Cup-only customers). This contrasts with the preview’s cited Q1 headline MUP decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trailing 12-month net revenue per unique customer grew 14% year-over-year in H1 2026, while monthly unique payers grew 9% year-over-year (6%+ excluding World Cup-only customers).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 MUPs: −4% headline, +2% excluding Lottery (Texas exit).”

surprises.description: Management described a more developed Predictions value-chain position than the preview discussed: DraftKings had all three layers live, had recently obtained an FCM license, and said this could let it capture more of the value chain and eventually produce Sportsbook-like gross profit per customer.
surprises.fact_evidence: “DraftKings is the only operator with all three Predictions layers (brokerage, exchange DKeX, and market maker) live, and recently obtained an FCM license, positioning it to capture more of the value chain and achieve gross profit per customer over time similar to Sportsbook.”

in_line: Predictions investment was expected to be about $200–300 million (roughly $250 million); management’s stated incremental 2026 investment of $200–300 million was within that range and was already embedded in maintained guidance.
Unfavorable sports outcomes were a headwind, as the preview had warned about unfavorable Q2 outcomes and sportsbook hold.

surprises.description: CON reported adjusted EPS of $0.52, well above the preview’s $0.42 consensus estimate and the lower $0.39 Most Accurate Estimate. The roughly 24% beat versus consensus was substantially stronger than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EPS grew approximately 40% to $0.52.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 consensus” adjusted EPS: “$0.42”; “Most Accurate Estimate (~$0.39) sits below the $0.42 consensus.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $606 million, above the preview’s roughly $592 million consensus and above the expected growth pace of about 7%. Core revenue also grew 8%, showing the result was not solely driven by Pivot.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue grew 10% year-over-year to $606 million, with core revenue (excluding Pivot) up 8% to $589.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 revenue consensus was “$591.7M – $592.5M”; the base scenario anticipated “$588–594M (+7%).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 23.3%, expanding nearly 240 basis points, rather than the flat-to-down margin outcome the preview identified as a downside risk. The call attributed some of the improvement to about $4 million of Nova integration costs being eliminated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 22.5% to $140.9 million with margin expanding nearly 240 basis points to 23.3%, aided by roughly $4 million of eliminated Nova integration costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA margin. Q2 FY25 base is 20.9%. Flat-to-down margin with soft volume is the bear combination.”

surprises.description: CON raised its FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $485–$495 million, above the preview’s expected raise to roughly $465–$485 million. The new midpoint of $490 million is $15 million above the anticipated midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance to “$485-$495 million (about $20 million higher at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise to roughly $2.30–2.38B revenue and $465–485M EBITDA is the buy-side expectation.”

surprises.description: Patient visits grew faster than the preview’s roughly 1%–1.5% organic growth implication, reaching over 56,000 per day. The reported level was also above the preview’s 55,500–55,800 daily estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total patient visits rose 2.6% to over 56,000 per day.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue implied “roughly 55,500–55,800 visits per day (+1% to +1.5% YoY).”

surprises.description: Employer services visits grew 1.8% rather than turning negative amid the weak payroll backdrop flagged in the preview. That was a better labor-market read-through than the preview’s flat-to-negative concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Employer services [visits were] up 1.8%, both above long-term averages.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch whether employer services visits turn negative YoY” and described the bear case as “Employer services flat-to-negative.”

surprises.description: Work comp visits grew 3.7%, above the preview’s stated downside threshold of below 3% for workers’ comp organic growth. This was another stronger-than-feared volume result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Work comp visits [were] up 3.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bear scenario cited “workers’ comp organic below 3%.”

surprises.description: Revenue per visit grew 4.6%, exceeding the preview’s 3% expectation and its 4%+ bull-case marker. Management did temper the outlook, saying rate growth should be closer to 3% for the rest of the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue per visit grew 4.6%,” driven by rate increases and favorable initial-injury visit mix; management “expects rate growth closer to 3% for the rest of the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Revenue per visit at or above 3%” was the catalyst to watch and set the bull case at “RPV +4%+.”

surprises.description: Onsite Health Clinics’ organic growth excluding Pivot was 27.9%, well above the preview’s 20%+ expectation. Management expects continued above-core organic growth, while noting that mid-to-high-20s rates may not be sustainable long term.
surprises.fact_evidence: The segment grew revenue 72.1% and “27.9% excluding Pivot”; management expects continued above-core organic growth but said mid-to-high-20s rates may be unsustainable long term.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Onsite health organic growth of 20% or more.”

surprises.description: Net leverage fell below 3x well ahead of the preview’s year-end timing, reaching the target during Q2. That also triggered a 25-basis-point Term Loan B spread reduction, an added financing benefit not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage fell to just under 3x from 3.4x in Q1, reaching the year-end target well ahead of schedule and triggering a 25 basis point Term Loan B spread step-down to 175 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited the year-end goal as “comfortably below 3.0x” and noted leverage was 3.4x at Q1.

surprises.description: FY26 free cash flow guidance increased to $220–$240 million, modestly above the preview’s stated $215–$235 million guidance range. The new midpoint is $5 million higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised full-year free cash flow guidance to “$220-$240 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed company FY26 free cash flow guidance as “$215M – $235M.”

surprises.description: CON announced that CEO Keith Newton will become Executive Chairman effective November 1, with President and CFO Matt DiCanio becoming CEO. The preview did not flag a leadership transition, and the shareholder implications are not clear from the provided information.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CEO Keith Newton will transition to Executive Chairman effective November 1, 2026, with current President and CFO Matt DiCanio becoming President and CEO as part of a multi-year succession plan.”

in_line: FY26 revenue guidance of $2.325–$2.375 billion was broadly in line with the preview’s expected raised range of roughly $2.30–$2.38 billion.

surprises.description: VAALCO’s Q2 revenue was approximately $135.2 million ($62.6 million of Q1 revenue plus a $72.6 million increase), above the preview’s $116.25 million consensus estimate. The result was higher than the stated consensus despite the preview’s warning that revenue consensus might be stale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue rose $72.6 million above Q1”; the preview gives Q1 revenue of $62.6 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $116.25M”

surprises.description: Management raised Egyptian production and sales guidance about 10% above original estimates and expanded the drilling program to 10–15 wells, while keeping full-year CapEx unchanged. The preview’s base case was that full-year guidance would be maintained, so the Egypt uplift was more favorable than that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expanded the Egyptian drilling program to 10-15 wells and raised production and sales guidance about 10% above original estimates while keeping full-year CapEx unchanged.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “FY guide maintained”; the preview said a second raise would support the growth story.

surprises.description: Ebouri-5H’s water cut rose faster than modeled, prompting a downward revision and becoming the main reason Gabon guidance is expected at the lower end. This was a negative operational development not identified in the preview’s base case of maintained FY26 guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Water cut rose faster than modeled toward the field average of 75-80%, prompting a downward revision that is the main driver of lower-end Gabon guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “FY guide maintained.”

surprises.description: Q2 ended with net debt of $147 million, below the preview’s estimated Q2 exit range of $160–185 million. That left debt lower than the preview’s funding-capacity bear case implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “VAALCO drew $25 million on its RBL in Q2, ending with $177 million drawn, net debt of $147 million and only $30.4 million unrestricted cash.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net debt could reach $160–185M at Q2 exit.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDAX was $54.8 million, modestly above the preview’s $50 million base-case estimate. It was below the preview’s $70 million bull case, but better than the central scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDAX of $54.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario estimated “Adj. EBITDAX | ~$50M.”

surprises.description: Q2 earnings received an additional, unflagged tailwind from exploration expense dropping by nearly $23 million from Q1, largely because Q1 included West Etame dry-hole and seismic costs. The preview did not identify this expense reduction as a Q2 earnings driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 earnings benefited from a near $23 million drop in exploration expense (from West Etame dry hole and seismic costs in Q1).”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that a new gas supply well should eliminate expensive diesel use on the Teli FSO, saving roughly $500,000–$600,000 per month gross while improving reliability and gas-lift production. The preview did not anticipate this operating-cost and production benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new gas supply well is expected to eliminate expensive diesel usage on the Teli FSO, saving roughly $500,000-$600,000 per month gross (VAALCO ~58% share), while improving reliability and gas lift-driven production.”

in_line: Q2 NRI sales of 17,812 BOPD were within the previewed 16,800–18,300 BOPD guidance range and near its midpoint, consistent with the preview’s base case of volumes around mid-guidance.

The roughly $40 million unrealized hedging gain was consistent with the preview’s expectation that the Q1 non-cash mark-to-market loss could reverse into a Q2 gain. The facts provided do not state the realized hedge result.
The Baobab restart occurred in June, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the field had restarted on schedule.
The midpoint of Q3 WI production guidance (about 25,650 BOPD) is broadly consistent with the preview’s 25,000–27,000 BOPD exit-rate expectation.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was $246 million, $18.5 million below the preview’s $264.5 million consensus, despite the preview noting that consensus had repeatedly missed divestiture timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated Q3 sales fell to $246 million” from $349 million a year ago, with roughly $85 million of divestiture impact partly offset by $4.4 million from Dodge.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $264.5M” for FQ3’26; the preview also said “Consensus has repeatedly missed divestiture timing.”

surprises.description: Matthews cut its FY26 adjusted EBITDA outlook to $158–162 million, versus the preview’s expectation that the company would maintain guidance of at least $180 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $158-162 million,” including its 40% share of Propelis adjusted EBITDA.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance (adj. EBITDA) | At least $180M”; the preview said the key question was whether management would “reaffirm” that bar.

surprises.description: Industrial Technology remained loss-making and worsened to a $5.4 million adjusted EBITDA loss, rather than turning positive as the preview said was needed for the second-half plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The industrial technology segment swung to an adjusted EBITDA loss of $5.4 million versus a $9 million profit a year ago,” hurt by divestitures and declining engineering sales.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Industrial Technologies adj. EBITDA. It was $(3.3)M in FQ2 and must turn positive.” The preview also said a third straight loss would “break the second-half bridge.”

surprises.description: The engineering/OBRA business suffered a sharper order setback than the preview anticipated: two expected orders were lost, others were delayed, and a newly won order was immediately reduced in scope. Matthews responded with a $10 million annual cost-reduction restructuring and a strategic review.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The engineering/OBRA business lost two anticipated orders, saw others delayed to September, and won an order in early June whose scope was immediately reduced,” prompting “a $10 million annual cost-reduction restructuring and a strategic review.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked for “a specific Q4 revenue schedule on the $25M converting-line order” and said that without one “the second-half bridge is unfunded”; it did not anticipate lost orders, a reduced order scope, or a strategic review.

surprises.description: The company did not meet management’s commitment to turn operating cash flow positive in Q3. Nine-month operating cash flow was still negative $69.5 million, versus negative $67.4 million in the first half, implying Q3 cash flow was approximately negative $2.1 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nine-month operating cash flow was negative $69.5 million.” The preview reported first-half operating cash flow of “$(67.4)M,” implying roughly $(2.1) million for Q3.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management committed to positive OCF in both Q3 and Q4”; the preview also listed “Operating cash flow turning positive in Q3, as promised.”

surprises.description: Propelis synergy capture was delayed by SAP implementation timing, creating an estimated $5 million shortfall rather than the expected progress toward the planned exit run rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A delay in Propelis synergy capture caused by SAP implementation timing created an estimated $5 million shortfall.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Propelis exit timing was guided in May to “12–18 months” and flagged the timing as a key watch item; it did not anticipate a $5 million synergy shortfall from SAP timing.

surprises.description: Despite the synergy delay, Matthews moved toward a faster Propelis exit process than the preview’s 12–18-month window suggested, expecting to start marketing the business within the next 12 months.
surprises.fact_evidence: Matthews expects Propelis to exit calendar 2026 at a “~$130 million annualized EBITDA run rate,” triggering a sale marketing process “within the next 12 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guided in May to 12–18 months”; the preview said narrowing that window was “the most likely source of a genuine positive surprise.”

surprises.description: Memorialization sales increased, but adjusted EBITDA slipped as copper, steel, labor, and fuel costs rose faster than price increases, indicating weaker margin conversion than the preview’s segment-strength framing implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: Memorialization sales rose 2.1% to $208.1 million, while adjusted EBITDA fell to $42.2 million from $42.8 million; escalating copper, steel, labor, and fuel costs “outpaced price increases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Memorialization strength is coming from price and the Dodge deal” and flagged “Memorialization price versus volume” and “price runway” as key issues.

surprises.description: CEO Joe Bartolese announced he intends to retire once a successor is hired, an unexpected leadership transition not mentioned in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CEO Joe Bartolese announced his intention to retire once a successor is hired.”

surprises.description: Matthews reported record interest in its dry battery electrode technology, a potentially favorable development that the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company reported “record interest in its dry battery electrode (DBE) technology.”

surprises.description: Matthews announced a new strategic printing partnership with Lynx, an unanticipated commercial development.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company announced “a new strategic printing partnership with Lynx.”

surprises.description: The company planned an additional $5 million in corporate cost reductions for next year, a savings initiative not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Matthews reported “planned $5 million corporate cost reductions for next year.”

in_line: Memorialization sales rose 2.1%, consistent with the preview’s expectation of segment strength from pricing and Dodge despite declining U.S. death rates; the segment’s EBITDA performance was weaker than that sales outlook suggested.

surprises.description: Post said it repurchased 4% of its outstanding shares in Q3, taking fiscal-year-to-date share-count reduction to about 17%. The preview highlighted buybacks as a key metric but did not anticipate a reduction of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Post repurchased 4% of outstanding shares in Q3,” bringing “fiscal year-to-date share count reduction to approximately 17%.”
