surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 buyback pace is a read on management's view of valuation.”

surprises.description: Despite its recent buybacks, Post said it is shifting capital allocation toward debt reduction rather than continuing aggressive repurchases. The preview noted the new $600 million authorization and focused on the Q3 buyback pace, but did not flag a pivot to debt repayment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is shifting capital allocation from aggressive share buybacks toward debt reduction,” driven by rising refinancing rates, “despite having no bond maturity for four years.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A new $600M authorization was approved in May”; “Q3 buyback pace is a read on management's view of valuation.”

surprises.description: Post entered FY2027 with a comparable adjusted EBITDA base of about $1.48 billion and preliminary guidance for EBITDA roughly flat, rather than offering the quantified path back to growth the preview said investors should listen for. The preview did not provide a specific FY2027 EBITDA forecast, so the gap is against that growth-oriented framing rather than a numeric consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Post entered fiscal 2027 with a comparable adjusted EBITDA base of approximately $1.48 billion” after adjusting for about $80 million of comparability items, and “preliminary FY2027 guidance is for EBITDA roughly flat versus this base.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Listen for any quantified path back to growth in FY27.”

surprises.description: Post expects cereal volume to fall about 2.5% in FY2027, so the outlook still implies declining volume even as assortment changes are expected to narrow the business's underperformance versus the category. That is weaker than the preview's growth-oriented FY2027 framing, though the narrowing gap is an improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cereal volume is expected to decline about 2.5% in FY2027,” while the company is “narrowing its underperformance gap to category” as assortment adjustments take effect.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Listen for any quantified path back to growth in FY27”; “Watch whether ... cereal shows the step-down that Jefferies flagged.”

surprises.description: Post identified competitive pressure in pet value brands as a major source of the business's decline: about 60% of the decline came from value brands, mostly 9Lives, which faces rivals promoting at lower prices. The preview flagged whether pet food would decelerate from its prior decline but did not anticipate this specific competitive pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly 60% of the year-over-year pet business decline is attributable to value brands, mostly 9Lives,” which “faces competitive promotions with two rivals pricing below its brand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether pet food decelerates from −14.1%.”

surprises.description: Post reported new plant closures after the AW integration, closing two peanut butter plants using the cost-optimization approach it had applied to cereal plants. The preview did not flag these closures or this specific cost action.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Post is closing two peanut butter plants following the AW integration, applying the same cost-optimization playbook used to close three cereal plants.”

surprises.description: Management pointed to substantial further cost-savings opportunities in pet beyond footprint changes, including portfolio simplification and formula harmonization. The preview focused on pet volume trends, not additional pet cost actions.
surprises.fact_evidence: The pet business has reached “approximately 30% market share,” and management sees “substantial untapped cost-savings opportunities in pet beyond footprint, including portfolio simplification and formula harmonization.”

surprises.description: Post said most FY2027 pricing actions will come later in the year and be concentrated in PCB/pet, while inflation is running toward the high end of prior expectations and pricing is lagging inflation because of retailer negotiations. This adds a prospective cost-and-pricing timing headwind that the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Most FY2027 pricing actions” are expected “later in the year,” concentrated in PCB/pet, where inflation is “running toward the higher end of prior expectations,” with “pricing lagging inflation due to retailer negotiation timing.”

surprises.description: Post described Q3 refrigerated retail pressure from several factors, including egg-market prices falling below its grain-based procurement costs, as well as lapping Easter timing and prior-year HPAI pricing adders. The preview did not identify these refrigerated retail pressures as a key issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 refrigerated retail was pressured by the lapping of Easter timing and prior-year HPAI pricing adders, along with higher fuel/freight costs and unfavorable egg market dynamics where market prices plummeted below the company's grain-based procurement costs.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EPS was $1.92, above every estimate listed in the preview, including the freshest $1.78 estimate. The beat was about 8% versus that freshest figure, although the preview showed a wide consensus range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS reached $1.92.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS (Q3) … $1.55 …; $1.54 …; $1.78 (Yahoo Finance/LSEG-style, Aug 3–4).”

surprises.description: Q3 net sales of $795 million exceeded the preview’s highest listed estimate of $781.1 million, by about 1.8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 net sales rose 8.1% year-over-year to $795 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (Q3) … $771.4M …; $762.2M …; $781.1M (Yahoo Finance, Aug 3–4).”

surprises.description: A $50 million litigation settlement drove GAAP net income down to $0.7 million from $43 million a year earlier, a major one-off drag the preview did not flag. Adjusted EPS nevertheless beat the listed estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net income collapsed to $0.7 million ($0.02 per diluted share) from $43 million ($1.25) a year earlier, primarily due to a $50 million litigation settlement expense.”

surprises.description: Safety & Infrastructure EBITDA and margin weakened despite slightly higher sales; the preview did not identify this segment-specific deterioration as an expected outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Safety & Infrastructure segment EBITDA fell to $28.1 million from $30.7 million, with margin declining to 13% from 14.4% despite a 1.3% sales increase.”

surprises.description: Electrical sales and EBITDA grew, but its margin slipped because input costs rose faster than pricing. This was a negative price/cost result within an issue the preview flagged for investors to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Electrical segment sales grew 10.9% to $578.3 million with EBITDA up 10% to $89.3 million, though margin slipped to 15.4% from 15.6% as input costs outpaced pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash flow and price/cost. I did not verify the full nine-month cash flow figures. The Q2 commentary on sequential improvement is the operating baseline the Street was using.”

in_line: The preview said Atkore did not intend to update or reaffirm FY26 guidance while the deal was pending; the call provided little forward guidance and no further clarity.
Sequential improvement was expected after Q2 guidance called for sequential growth in sales, EBITDA, and EPS; the call reported that all key metrics improved sequentially.

surprises.description: Q3 diluted EPS was $0.05, $0.01 below the $0.06 consensus cited in the preview. The preview characterized this as an approximately 17% miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 fiscal 2026 net income was approximately $550,000, or $0.05 per diluted share”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | $0.06”

surprises.description: Management lowered and narrowed FY26 EPS guidance to $1.29–$1.32, below the previous $1.31–$1.37 range at both ends. That was a worse outcome than reaffirming the prior range or narrowing toward its upper end, as the preview discussed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management narrowed its full-year fiscal 2026 EPS forecast to a range of $1.29 to $1.32”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 EPS guidance: $1.31–$1.37”; “Reaffirming $1.31–$1.37 is a different message than narrowing to the upper end.”

surprises.description: The Roanoke Gas rate case settled at $3.85 million of incremental annual revenue, $450,000 below the $4.3 million sought. The preview flagged a below-request outcome as a downside risk; the settlement also resulted in a $275,000 customer-refund accrual.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Roanoke Gas rate case settled at $3.85 million in incremental annual revenues, below the $4.3 million originally sought”; “The company accrued $275,000 for customer refunds as of June 30 related to rates charged since January 1, 2026”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A $4.3M expedited request was filed Dec 2. Interim rates took effect Jan 1 subject to refund”; “A final order below $4.3M creates a retroactive claw-back.”

surprises.description: The LNG facility’s restored on-system storage capability is not expected until winter 2027–28, extending the outage beyond the preview’s expectation that it would be unavailable for winter 2026–27. That leaves the facility out for an additional winter season.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Restored on-system storage capability not expected until the 2027-2028 winter season.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Damaged mid-Q2 and unavailable for winter 2026-27.”

surprises.description: Industrial gas usage rose more than 25% in Q3, exceeding the preview’s description of steady firm volumes and rising interruptible volumes. The benefit is tempered because the incremental volumes came from the largest industrial customer and carry the company’s lowest margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Industrial gas usage rose more than 25% in Q3 driven by the largest industrial customer, though those incremental volumes carry the company's lowest margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Firm volumes were steady YoY. Interruptible industrial volumes rose, but at lower-tier margins.”

surprises.description: The company established a regulatory asset for LNG outage costs and expects recovery in a future proceeding, providing a path to recovery where the preview said the regulatory-asset treatment was still an open question. The costs were not included in the recent rate case, so recovery is deferred rather than secured there.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The LNG facility outage costs were excluded from the recent rate case, but the company established a regulatory asset and expects recovery in a future proceeding.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The call needs a cost estimate, SCC regulatory-asset treatment, and insurance recovery figures.”

in_line: The $15 million note was refinanced at a higher rate, as the preview anticipated repricing from the legacy 2% coupon and a direct FY27 interest-cost headwind; the call disclosed a 5.2% fixed rate for three years.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $421 million, about $31 million below the preview’s ~$452 million consensus. Sales grew only about 3% year over year, versus roughly 10% growth implied by consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 sales reached $421 million, up approximately 3% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$452M | $410M”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.19, well below the preview’s $0.56 consensus. The call attributed much of the decline to a higher effective tax rate because of prior-year 45Q credits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS dropped $1.05 to $0.19, largely due to a higher effective tax rate from prior-year 45Q credits.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $32 million, about $18 million below the preview’s implied estimate of ~$50 million. The result was also down $24 million year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell $24 million year-over-year to $32 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (implied) | ~$50M (11% margin)”

surprises.description: Management warned that the Q3 plant nutrient sequential earnings headwind will exceed the historical $10–15 million range, citing weak fall-fill pricing and channel inventory liquidation. That is weaker than the preview’s base case that seasonal strength would offset sulfur pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Q3 plant nutrient sequential earnings headwind is expected to exceed the historical $10 million to $15 million range due to weak fall fill pricing and channel inventory liquidation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base | ... Key driver: Seasonal strength offsets sulfur; turnaround on plan; H2 cash reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Volume fell 15% despite favorable pricing, with lower plant nutrient sales as spring ammonium sulfate demand softened. This is a weaker volume and seasonal-demand picture than the preview’s base case of seasonal strength offsetting sulfur pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “18% favorable pricing that offset a 15% decline in volume”; “Volume was a $17 million unfavorable impact primarily from lower plant nutrient sales, as spring ammonium sulfate demand softened.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base ... Key driver: Seasonal strength offsets sulfur.”

surprises.description: The company now expects full-year ammonia sales volume to rise 30% from the prior record, with first-half volume already up to 49,000 short tons from 33,000. The preview flagged the ammonia-allocation decision but did not anticipate this volume outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 ammonia sales volume is expected to rise 30% versus 2025 (a prior record), with first-half sales of 49,000 short tons up from 33,000 a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Ammonia allocation decision. Management is moderating ammonium sulfate output to push merchant ammonia sales. This shifts mix in ways headline revenue won't show.”

surprises.description: Management cited third-party forecasts for sulfur prices to fall by about $200 entering 2027 and said this should be a cost tailwind as domestic ammonium sulfate supply tightens. The preview focused on record sulfur costs and Q3 pressure, and did not flag this later-period relief outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Third-party experts forecast an approximately $200 decline in sulfur prices entering 2027, expected to be a tailwind amid tighter domestic ammonium sulfate supply”; “each $100 per long ton change equating to roughly $35 million in annual cost impact.”

in_line: The preview expected ammonium sulfate pricing to largely offset sulfur input costs rather than expand margins. The call said the company fully offset the $72 million year-over-year raw-material cost headwind and achieved neutral net price-over-raws in Q2.
The preview expected about $18–20 million of 45Q credits in H2 2026. The call expects an $18 million payment in the second half and continues to target $100–125 million in total 45Q credits.
The preview noted Q3 Tampa sulfur at a record $705 per long ton; the call also reported Q3 sulfur at $705 per long ton.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $2.79 including a tariff-refund benefit, but only $0.89 excluding it—well below the $1.49 consensus expectation and down year over year. The reported figure therefore concealed a substantial underlying EPS shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS reached $2.79 including a $1.90 per share tariff refund benefit, but was only $0.89 excluding refunds, down year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $1.49”

surprises.description: Net sales grew 7.7% year over year, ahead of the preview’s roughly 4.7%–5.1% growth expectation. Organic growth was also strong at 6.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales increased 7.7% year-over-year (6.6% organic excluding $7.5 million favorable FX) with all three business units delivering growth in Q3 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $732.4M | +4.7%”; the preview also cited an alternative estimate of “~+5.1% YoY.”

surprises.description: A $60.6 million tariff refund unexpectedly lifted adjusted EBITDA to $158.3 million from $97.7 million excluding refunds. This was a large one-time boost to reported results rather than recurring operating performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A one-time $60.6 million tariff refund lifted reported adjusted EBITDA to $158.3 million”; adjusted EBITDA excluding refunds was “$97.7 million.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook to mid-single-digit growth excluding tariff refunds, rather than simply reaffirming the existing framework. The preview identified a raise as the upside scenario; full-year sales guidance was maintained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to mid-single-digit growth (excluding tariff refunds), while maintaining net sales guidance of flat to up low single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the base case was “FY26 framework reaffirmed, not raised” and listed a raised FY26 EBITDA guide as the “cleanest bull trigger.”

surprises.description: Home & Garden sharply outperformed the preview’s risk-focused setup: sales rose 19% to a record $225 million, even exceeding pandemic-era demand levels. The preview had identified the segment as the main potential source of a revenue shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Home & Garden delivered a record quarter with net sales of $225 million, up 19%, surpassing even COVID-19 pandemic-era demand levels.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called Home & Garden “the largest swing factor” and said “A miss here is the most likely source of a revenue shortfall.”

surprises.description: Global Pet Care organic sales growth was only 2.9%, below the preview’s expectation that growth hold in the mid-to-high single digits. The reported North American result was also helped by an easier comparison, limiting the reassurance from the growth figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global Pet Care organic net sales rose 2.9%”; North American results were “flattered by an easier prior-year comparison from a stop-shipment dynamic.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Global Pet Care organic growth. It needs to hold mid-to-high single digits.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA excluding refunds was $97.7 million, above the preview’s implied $90–93 million segment-build estimate, even before considering the one-time refund. That indicates a better underlying EBITDA result than the preview’s estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA excluding tariff refunds was $97.7 million, up 27.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “No formal consensus found”; the preview’s own segment build implied “~$90–93M.”

surprises.description: The company repurchased about 200,000 shares for $15.8 million, twice the 100,000 shares repurchased in Q2, despite the preview flagging continued restraint as a risk. More than $300 million of authorization remained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased approximately 200,000 shares for $15.8 million during the quarter, with over $300 million of Board authorization remaining.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called the “buyback cadence after the Q2 slowdown” the key question and said “Continued restraint with no M&A is a narrative risk.”

surprises.description: Net leverage ended near 1x, below both the preview’s cited 1.66x level and the company’s 2–2.5x target. That was a stronger balance-sheet position than the preview’s starting point suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $258.9 million in cash, zero drawn on its revolver, and a net leverage ratio of about 1x, well below its 2-2.5x target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net leverage is 1.66x.”

surprises.description: Management highlighted Q4 headwinds from tough Global Pet Care comparisons and elevated Home & Garden retailer inventories, alongside unfavorable late-season weather. The preview discussed weather risk and a possible Global Pet Care pull-forward reversal, but not this combination of Q4 inventory and comparison pressures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management warned Q4 will face headwinds as Global Pet Care laps tough prior-year comparisons and Home & Garden contends with elevated retailer inventories and unfavorable late-season weather.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed Q3 risks: “weather is a risk” for Home & Garden and “the roughly $9M ERP-related pull-forward from Q2 to reverse as a Q3 headwind” for Global Pet Care.

in_line: Full-year net sales guidance remained flat to up low single digits, in line with the preview’s stated company guidance.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.55, below the preview’s $0.68 consensus estimate. That is a meaningful miss even though adjusted EBITDA was strong.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income of $54 million or $0.55 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS | $0.68 | MarketBeat, Jul 30 '26.”

surprises.description: Kodiak raised its FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $830–860 million rather than merely reaffirming the existing $820–860 million range. It also lifted discretionary cash flow guidance to $570–600 million and Compression gross margin guidance to 69–70.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Kodiak raised full-year 2026 guidance, lifting adjusted EBITDA to $830-860 million, discretionary cash flow to $570-600 million, and Compression gross margin to 69-70.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 adj. EBITDA (company guide) | $820–860M”; “Reaffirmation is the base case; any narrowing to the low end is the main bear trigger.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $217 million, above the preview’s bull-case threshold of $215 million and above its base-case range of $203–212 million. The preview did not provide a published EBITDA consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA hit a company record $217 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bull … Adj. EBITDA | $215M+”; “Base … Adj. EBITDA | $203–212M”; “Adjusted EBITDA … estimates are not published consensus.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $391 million came in above the preview’s highest cited consensus estimate of $386.3 million, though only modestly. It was also just below the preview’s $392 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $391 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $386.3M” (highest cited consensus); “Bull | Revenue | $392M+.”

surprises.description: Post-offering leverage was 3.1x, better than the preview’s expected 3.3–3.5x. Management also expected leverage to peak in the mid-3s under its base plan, versus the preview’s concern that it could periodically exceed 4.0x.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Post-May equity offering of ~$836 million, net debt was ~$2.6 billion with a record-low leverage ratio of 3.1x, expected to peak in the mid-3s under the base plan.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A $750M equity raise in May at $71.00 should bring leverage to roughly 3.3–3.5x”; “leverage ‘may periodically exceed 4.0x’.”

surprises.description: Kodiak reported approximately 1.8 GW of power generation capacity available by the end of 2030, including a Baker Hughes deal for 1 GW with an option to expand to 1.8 GW. The preview had identified 260+ MW procured and 1.3 GW in advanced negotiations, so the reported capacity position was larger, although the preview’s separate question about customer contracts is not resolved by equipment availability alone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company secured approximately 1.8 gigawatts of power generation (about 66% turbines) available by end of 2030, including a Baker Hughes turbine supply deal for 1 GW with an option to expand to 1.8 GW.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has disclosed 260+ MW procured and ‘advanced negotiations’ for another 1.3 GW. A July 8 Baker Hughes agreement anchors about 1 GW by 2030.”

surprises.description: Kodiak reached a limited notice to proceed on a sub-100 MW West Texas data center project leased to a hyperscaler, a concrete project step toward customer conversion. However, the long-term contract was still expected before year-end rather than reported as signed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Kodiak executed a limited notice to proceed for a sub-100 MW West Texas data center project leased to a hyperscaler, targeting power supply starting early 2027 with a long-term contract expected before year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Whether capacity converts into signed customer contracts is the key open question.”

surprises.description: Half of 2027 large-horsepower compression deliveries were already contracted, ahead of the preview’s expectation that the share would be above the more-than-40% reported in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Kodiak is … already 50% contracted on 2027 large-horsepower deliveries.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Share of 2027 compression deliveries already contracted (above the >40% reported in Q1).”

in_line: Compression utilization was 98.2%, close to the preview’s Q1 reference of 98.0%, and the reported 70% adjusted gross margin was around the 68.5–70.0% range cited in the preview. These operating metrics were broadly consistent with the strong compression performance the preview discussed.

surprises.description: SSP reported a $12.68-per-share loss versus the preview’s consensus loss of $0.43. The loss included a $1.1 billion noncash impairment of Scripps Networks goodwill and intangibles, an item not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported a Q2 loss of $12.68 per share, including a $1.1 billion noncash goodwill and intangible impairment charge for the Scripps Networks business.”

surprises.description: The preview cited a directional full-year political advertising figure of at least about $340 million; SSP instead expects $225 million–$250 million. The Q3 Local Media revenue guide of about 20% growth, with roughly $75 million of political revenue, points to a strong near-term political contribution but does not erase the lower full-year outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 political advertising revenue of $225 million-$250 million”; “Q3 Local Media division revenue is guided up about 20%, implying roughly mid-$70 million in Q3 political revenue, though core advertising is expected down low double digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A secondary summary of the Q4'25 release cites a full-year political figure of at least about $340M. Treat that as directional, not company guidance, and confirm it on the call.”

surprises.description: Local Media revenue was $317 million, down 1%, rather than the roughly $340 million and low-single-digit growth anticipated. Core advertising was also down 4.8%, adding to the shortfall alongside distribution weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 Local Media revenue was $317 million (down 1% YoY) with core advertising down 4.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Local Media revenue | ~$340M (guide: ‘up low single digits’).”

surprises.description: Local distribution revenue was $161 million, well below the roughly $190 million run-rate the preview highlighted. The blackouts were anticipated, but the reported decline was substantial: down 13%, with Comcast and DIRECTV blackout periods cited as the cause.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Local distribution revenue fell 13% to $161 million due to Comcast and DIRECTV blackout periods.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 distribution revenue versus the roughly $190M run-rate, and whether management quantifies the Comcast and DIRECTV impact.”

surprises.description: Scripps Networks revenue fell 13% to $172 million, a deeper decline than the roughly 10% decline and approximately $185 million revenue level anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Scripps Networks Q2 revenue dropped 13% to $172 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Scripps Networks revenue | ~$185M (guide: ‘down ~10%’).”

surprises.description: Scripps Networks segment profit fell to $26 million from $57 million a year earlier. The preview warned that another quarter of heavy margin compression was a risk, but did not indicate a decline of this scale or identify soft direct-response advertising alongside Nielsen changes as drivers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Segment profit collapsed to $26 million from $57 million a year ago, driven by Nielsen measurement changes and soft direct response advertising.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A second quarter of heavy margin compression would revive concerns about the segment.”

surprises.description: The full-year net distribution outlook is weaker than the preview’s expected low-double-digit growth: SSP now expects mid- to high-single-digit growth. Lower network affiliation costs support net distribution revenue even as gross distribution revenue is expected to decline low single digits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year gross distribution revenue is now expected down low single digits, but net distribution revenue is guided up mid- to high single digits, aided by lower network affiliation costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance: FY26 net distribution revenue growth of ‘low double digits,’ raised at Q1.”

surprises.description: Net leverage was 4.9x, above the preview’s 4.0x warning threshold and its expectation that below 3.9x would indicate progress. The $13 million cash balance is limited, although no revolver was drawn and the credit line was extended to July 2029 with no near-term debt maturities.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage rose to 4.9x at quarter-end from 4.4x in Q1, with just $13 million in cash, no revolver drawn, and no near-term debt maturities after extending the credit line to July 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Below 3.9x is on track; above 4.0x is a negative signal.”

surprises.description: SSP raised its year-end transformation run-rate savings target to $100 million, 33% above prior guidance, rather than merely reaffirming the transformation contribution the preview expected. It maintained the $125 million–$150 million incremental EBITDA target by 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its year-end transformation run-rate savings target to $100 million, up 33% from prior guidance, while maintaining the $125 million-$150 million incremental EBITDA target by 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for reaffirmation of the $20–30M FY26 EBITDA contribution.”

surprises.description: Management reported renewing 70% of pay-TV subscribers this year, with only 5% resetting in 2027 and about 20% in 2028. That provides multiyear distribution visibility that the preview did not anticipate or discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company renewed 70% of its pay-TV subscribers this year, with only 5% resetting in 2027 and about 20% in 2028, providing multiyear distribution visibility.”

in_line: The expected $40 million–$50 million of transformation-related costs was consistent with the call’s $40 million–$50 million in expected cash restructuring costs.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $22.2 million, below the preview’s realistic $24–26 million bar, though above its bear-case range. The preview described the $30 million consensus as stale and high, so the miss versus the realistic bar is the more relevant comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue fell to $22.2 million”; management said results “came in well below analyst expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The preview’s realistic bar is about $24–26M”; base estimate revenue was $25M.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $4.4 million, below the preview’s roughly $6 million base estimate. That was weaker than the expected base case, though above the preview’s $2 million bear-case estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $4.4 million in Q2 2026 versus $18.6 million in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base estimate was “adjusted EBITDA ~$6M”; its bear case was “~$2M.”

surprises.description: Instead of the modest profit implied by the preview’s realistic EPS estimate, Arena reported a small net loss. The prior-year net income was not a useful benchmark because the preview had already flagged the large discontinued-operations gain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported a net loss of $200,000 in Q2 2026”; prior-year net income included “a $96.2 million gain from discontinued operations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base estimate was EPS “~$0.02–0.04,” and it said Q2’25’s one-time gain meant continuing-operations EPS was the meaningful year-ago reference.

surprises.description: Traffic headwinds continued rather than easing, contradicting management’s earlier message that volatility had subsided. Management still expects seasonal ad and sports-calendar tailwinds to help second-half traffic and monetization, but the continuing headwinds were worse than the preview’s hoped-for stabilization.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management said traffic headwinds “continued rather than stabilizing as previously guided”; Google still provides “over 40% of publisher traffic.” Management expects seasonal ad and sports-calendar tailwinds, including NFL season, to improve second-half traffic and monetization.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted whether “traffic volatility has subsided” is reaffirmed or walked back, and noted management had said traffic volatility “has subsided.”

surprises.description: Arena completed a three-year debt extension, addressing near-term refinancing risk, but did so at the same interest rate rather than the lower cost the preview identified as the hoped-for outcome. The refinancing was therefore positive on timing and risk, but did not deliver the expected cost reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: Arena “refinanced and extended its debt facility by three years with its existing lender at the same interest rate,” avoiding dilution and removing near-term refinancing risk.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a signed refinancing “at lower cost” was the catalyst to watch and called a signed refinancing “a major positive.”

surprises.description: Cash stayed at $11.2 million rather than building from the Q1 level, despite more than $2 million of operating cash flow in the first half. That fell short of the preview’s expectation that cash would keep building.
surprises.fact_evidence: Arena “maintained a cash balance of $11.2 million and generated over $2 million in operating cash flow in the first half of 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to confirm “that cash keeps building”; it cited Q1 cash of $11.2 million, up $0.9 million.

surprises.description: Arena added InfoSentience, an AI content-generation firm, using cash on hand, and said it expects the acquisition to be immediately accretive through existing B2B contracts. The preview did not flag this acquisition or its expected near-term contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company acquired InfoSentience, an AI content-generation firm, entirely with cash on hand, and expects it to be immediately accretive to cash flow and profit via existing B2B contracts.”

surprises.description: The company announced a rebrand to Pradium AI and a repositioning from a traditional publisher toward an asset-light AI technology company. This strategic shift was not anticipated in the preview, which focused on near-term publishing, advertising, and commerce metrics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Arena is rebranding to Pradium AI, repositioning from a traditional publisher to an asset-light AI technology company empowering creators.”

surprises.description: Arena described a new Cutter Studios model aimed at about 1,000 video-first creators, turning long-form videos into multiple articles. The reported workflow is less effective than handwritten articles, though management said monetization rates are comparable or better; the preview did not discuss this initiative or these operating trade-offs.
surprises.fact_evidence: Cutter Studios “targets about 1,000 video-first creators,” converting long-form videos into “5-10 derivative articles each” at “roughly one-third the efficacy of handwritten articles but with comparable or better monetization rates.”

surprises.description: Q3 gross margin was 45.3%, far above the preview’s 37.5–38.5% base range, but the improvement depended on about $15 million of tariff refunds. Excluding the refund, margin would have been modestly below the prior year, and management said it does not expect further meaningful refunds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 gross margin improved 7.7 points to 45.3%”; excluding the “~$15 million tariff refund,” margin “would have been modestly lower than the prior year”; management “does not anticipate additional meaningful tariff refunds going forward.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base” gross margin was “37.5–38.5%”; the preview said “Holding 38% or higher would be a positive surprise.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s expectation of 25–30% incremental operating-profit flow-through, operating expenses rose about $7 million, or 11.5%. The reported operating-income increase was more than accounted for by the tariff refund; without it, operating income would have been roughly $3 million, below the prior-year quarter’s roughly $7 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses increased about $7 million (11.5%) year-over-year”; operating income was $18.3 million, up $11 million, “boosted by roughly $15 million in tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 needs incremental flow-through of roughly 25–30% for the profit recovery to look structural.”

surprises.description: Inventory did not show the seasonal drawdown the preview looked for: it was $188.3 million, slightly above the $186.9 million level at Q2, with management describing a build to support sales demand. The build was not necessarily a demand-forecasting error, but it missed the preview’s working-capital expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory rose to $188.3 million,” up about $24.5 million from the prior-year quarter, “reflecting a build to support sales demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called Q3 the “seasonal cash-harvest quarter” and looked for “an inventory drawdown from $186.9M.”

surprises.description: Camping and watercraft had a challenging quarter because of weak market conditions, a segment-level setback the preview did not specifically anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The camping and watercraft business (Jetboil and Old Town) faced a challenging quarter on weak market conditions.”

surprises.description: Diving was identified as a driver of Q3 growth, whereas the preview noted that it had swung to a small operating loss in Q2 and focused its Q3 growth watch on fishing. The call did not quantify diving’s contribution or say whether it returned to profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The fishing (Minn Kota) and diving (ScubaPro) segments drove growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Diving swung to a small operating loss” in Q2 and described fishing as “about 80% of revenue and effectively all of the operating profit.”

in_line: Q3 sales growth of 5% implies sales of about $190 million using the preview’s $180.7 million prior-year comparison, within the preview’s broad $186.2–$193.2 million revenue estimates.

surprises.description: Rapid7 had been expected to report about $0.35 of non-GAAP EPS and $25 million of non-GAAP operating income; it reported $0.44 and $28.9 million, respectively, beating both benchmarks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP operating income of $28.9 million (13.7% margin) and EPS of $0.44 beat guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Working consensus used by the full analysis: $208.5M revenue and $0.35 EPS”; Q2 non-GAAP operating income guidance was “$24–26M” with “~$25M” consensus.

surprises.description: Rapid7's Q3 ARR outlook points to a further decline to about $812 million, rather than signaling that ARR has reached a trough; the preview had identified stabilization as a key test.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance calls for ARR declining further to approximately $812 million, with core solutions roughly flat sequentially and the decline coming from noncore offerings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Exit ARR vs. ~$820M guide. The main test of decline versus trough”; the base scenario expected “ARR on guide,” while the preview said “$825M+ would signal stabilization.”

surprises.description: Detection and response ARR growth came in below the preview's roughly 7% expectation and below its 6% concern threshold; exposure management also underperformed and offset that growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The detection and response business, representing ~55% of total ARR, grew approximately 5% year-over-year, while exposure management underperformed and offset that growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Detection & Response ARR growth (~7% Y/Y)”; “Deceleration below ~6% would undercut it.”

surprises.description: Rapid7 raised full-year non-GAAP operating income guidance to $129–133 million, well above the prior $112–118 million range in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year operating income guidance to $129-133 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance … non-GAAP operating income: $112–118M.”

surprises.description: Management set a Q4 2026 non-GAAP operating-margin target of 20%, a sharp step up from Q2's 13.7% margin; the preview did not give an expectation for this Q4 target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided to a 20% non-GAAP operating margin in Q4 2026, up sharply from 13.7% in Q2.”

surprises.description: The company announced a restructuring affecting about 12% of its workforce, turning the preview's watch for possible cost-out into a substantial workforce action; the plan also brings $10–11 million of charges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company announced a restructuring impacting approximately 12% of its workforce, incurring $10-11 million in charges, to refocus resources on core platform solutions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for cost-out, portfolio pruning, and strategic alternatives language.”

surprises.description: Rapid7's cash and available credit provide a stated means to repay the $600 million notes due in March 2027, addressing the preview's open question about a repayment or refinancing plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $702.6 million in cash and short-term investments plus a $200 million undrawn credit facility to repay its $600 million convertible notes due March 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$597.6M of 0.25% converts due 2027 … A refinancing plan, or its absence, is a catalyst.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin fell to 71.7%, with higher security operations center staffing and cloud usage costs cited as drivers; the preview did not set a Q2 margin expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP gross margin declined ~215 basis points year-over-year to 71.7%, driven by increased security operations center staffing and cloud usage costs.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $210.9 million, above the preview's $208.5 million working consensus and the company's $207–209 million guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue fell ~1.5% year-over-year to $210.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Working consensus used by the full analysis: $208.5M revenue”; company guidance was “$207–209M.”

surprises.description: Total ARR of $824 million was slightly above the preview's $818–822 million consensus range and about $4 million above the approximately $820 million guide, even though ARR declined sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total ARR declined to $824 million in Q2 2026, with the sequential decline driven by noncore products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Exit ARR … ~$818–822M” consensus and “~$820M” guide.

in_line: FY2026 revenue guidance was effectively reaffirmed: $837–841 million versus the preview's prior $836–842 million range.
FY2026 free cash flow guidance was maintained at approximately $130 million, within the preview's $125–135 million range.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $138.6 million, $4.1 million above the $134.49 million consensus, and declined 3.5% year over year rather than the 6.3% decline implied by the preview’s comparison. The result was also above the preview’s $132–138 million base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales declined 3.5% year-over-year to $138.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales (Q2) | $134.49M”; the base scenario expected “$132–138M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin rose to 22.3%, up 110 basis points from Q1’s 21.2%, despite the preview’s concern about Infrastructure freight pressure. The preview did not specify a higher margin target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin improved 80 basis points to 22.3% on favorable business mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin was 21.2% in Q1. Watch whether the Infrastructure freight pressure management flagged is sized and whether UK Rail restructuring savings offset it.”

surprises.description: Backlog increased 17.4% sequentially to $246.1 million, above the preview’s base case of a sequential increase and even above its bull-case threshold of $235 million. The year-over-year decline was expected to look weak, but the stronger sequential rebuild was better than the base case suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated backlog fell 8.8% year-over-year to $246.1 million ... but rose 17.4% sequentially from Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “backlog up sequentially”; the bull scenario said “Backlog rebuilds above $235M.”

surprises.description: Bookings remained just below the 1.0-to-1 level the preview identified as supportive of the second-half ramp, with infrastructure especially weak at 0.85. The reported $16 million reduction in precast concrete orders adds a source of infrastructure weakness beyond the Summit cancellation emphasized in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The trailing 12-month book-to-bill ratio was 0.96 to 1, with rail healthy at 1.03 and infrastructure weaker at 0.85 due to the Summit cancellation and softer precast orders”; backlog was also affected by “$16 million lower precast concrete orders.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Book-to-bill above 1.0x would support the H2 ramp”; the preview attributed about “$19M of the [Infrastructure] decline” to the Summit cancellation.

surprises.description: The preview did not flag the $2.1 million charge for exiting two non-core UK product lines. It was an unexpected cost, even though gross margin improved overall.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin improved “despite a $2.1 million charge related to the exit of two non-core UK product lines.”

surprises.description: Global friction management and technology services and solutions grew sharply, providing an unanticipated offset to weakness in rail products. The preview did not discuss these businesses’ Q2 growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global friction management sales grew 18.1% and technology services and solutions sales grew 66.9% in Q2, partially offsetting rail products weakness.”

surprises.description: Operating cash flow reached $17.9 million, its highest Q2 level since 2017, an unusually strong quarterly result not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 operating cash flow reached $17.9 million, up $7.5 million from last year and the highest Q2 level since 2017, driven by lower working capital needs.”

surprises.description: Net debt fell 45.5% year over year and gross leverage declined to 1.0x, reaching the bottom of the company’s stated target range. The preview did not identify this level of deleveraging as a Q2 expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt fell 45.5% ($35.2 million) year-over-year to $42.2 million, cutting gross leverage in half from 2.2x to 1.0x, within the targeted 1.0–1.5x range.”

surprises.description: Management said at least 80% of current backlog is expected to convert to revenue by year-end, and disclosed a roughly £15 million UK rail order. The preview anticipated named Rail awards only in its bull scenario, not as part of the base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects at least 80% of the current backlog to convert to revenue by year-end, and disclosed a ~£15 million UK rail order.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “backlog up sequentially” with “no new backlog figure”; the bull scenario cited “named Rail or precast awards.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA of $11.7 million was within the preview’s derived $11.5–12.5 million range.
Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, consistent with the preview’s base case of a third reaffirmation.
Free cash flow guidance of $15–25 million, with a $20 million midpoint, and capital spending of approximately 2.7% of sales matched the preview’s stated expectations.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $37.7M was $4.5M below the preview’s $42.2M consensus, and management also said it was below its own expectations. However, it landed within the preview’s independent $36–39M estimate, so the miss was less severe than the consensus comparison alone suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenue was $37.7 million” and was “below their own expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus” Q2 revenue was “$42.2M”; the preview also gave an “independent estimate for Q2 revenue” of “$36–39M.”

surprises.description: Rather than trim the FY26 sales and adjusted EBITDA targets as the preview’s base case anticipated, Heron withdrew both guidance ranges entirely. The preview specifically identified withdrawal of the EBITDA guide as a bear trigger, making this more adverse than a quantified cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company withdrew its full-year 2026 guidance of $173-183 million in net product sales and $10-20 million in adjusted EBITDA,” citing generic uncertainty, spending cuts, and strategic review.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected the “FY revenue guide [to be] cut to about $155–168M” and the “EBITDA guide cut toward breakeven”; it also called “Withdrawal of this guide” the EBITDA “bear trigger.”

surprises.description: Heron said the court decision weakened Cinvanti’s patent protection and that it was preparing for potential generic competition to its largest product. The preview recognized the ruling and asked about generic-entry timing, but framed the issue around prior settlement agreements remaining unaffected; the call’s preparation for generic competition underscores a more immediate commercial risk than that framing conveyed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A June court decision in the District of Delaware weakened Cinvanti's patent protection,” prompting preparation “for potential generic competition to its largest product.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the June 1 ruling “does not affect prior settlement agreements” and framed the key question as “when entry is contractually permitted.”

surprises.description: The Hercules amendment entails paying down up to $17.5M of principal, while reducing pro forma cash from $42.7M at quarter-end to about $28.5M after the first payment and $24.3M after the potential second payment. The preview flagged cash and any Hercules amendment as issues to watch, but did not anticipate this scale of near-term cash reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: Heron agreed to a principal reduction of “up to $17.5 million” ($13.5M paid at execution and a potential further $4M by September 15); pro forma cash falls to “roughly $28.5 million” and then “about $24.3 million,” versus $42.7M at quarter-end.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Cash versus the $44.8M base” and “Hercules covenant status,” including “Any amendment, waiver, or forward-looking covenant caution.”

surprises.description: Heron disclosed that it is exploring strategic alternatives, with no set timetable and no assurance that a transaction will result. The preview did not flag a strategic review, so this adds a material, unresolved outcome alongside the withdrawn guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is “exploring strategic alternatives with no set timetable and no assurance a transaction will result”; the process is also reflected in the amended credit agreement.

surprises.description: Zynrelef reached $11.1M, below the preview’s roughly $11.5M threshold for keeping the acute-care growth story intact. Its sequential and year-over-year growth was positive, but it missed the level the preview identified as important.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Zynrelef net sales were $11.1 million,” up 9% sequentially and 35% year-over-year; average daily units grew 19% year-over-year “but [were] below internal targets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Zynrelef “needs to stay above about $11.5M to keep the acute-care story intact.”

surprises.description: Heron paused its planned second-half Salesforce expansion and tightened spending after the court decision, whereas the preview did not anticipate a pause in the planned commercial buildout. This signals a more defensive operating posture, even as spending cuts may conserve cash.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company paused its planned second-half Salesforce expansion and tightened spending following the June court decision.”

in_line: Cinvanti sales were $21.8M, close to the preview’s roughly $21M reference point and above its roughly $19M warning threshold; the preview’s concern was whether erosion would accelerate.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $117 million, far below the preview’s $135–$136.4 million consensus range. The 10% year-over-year decline was substantially worse than the preview’s base-case expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales fell approximately 10% year-over-year to $117 million from $129 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales (Q2) … $135.0M … or $136.4M”; the base scenario was “$132M–$136M.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was only $6.6 million, well below the preview’s estimated $11.5–$12.5 million and the $11 million reported a year earlier. The 40% decline was also weaker than the preview’s bear-case range of $7–$9 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA dropped 40% to $6.6 million from $11 million a year earlier,” hurt by lower sales, about $2 million in higher freight costs, and weaker manufacturing absorption.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s own estimate was “$11.5M–$12.5M”; its bear scenario was “$7M–$9M,” and it flagged adjusted EBITDA “vs. about $11M in the prior year.”

surprises.description: International sales fell 18%, a sharper deterioration than the preview’s base expectation of roughly flat international sales and a more severe version of the consecutive-decline risk it highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An 18% decline in international sales” was the primary driver of the Q2 sales decline.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “international roughly flat”; the preview warned that “a second consecutive decline would turn the ‘timing’ explanation into a demand concern.”

surprises.description: First-half adjusted EBITDA was $17 million, below the roughly $22 million the preview said was needed to keep the full-year target credible. This leaves more of the year’s EBITDA target to be delivered in the second half, despite year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half 2026 adjusted EBITDA rose more than 20% to $17 million from $14 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “H1 needs to land near $22M to keep the $44M–$48M full-year target credible.”

surprises.description: Cash fell and net debt rose sequentially during Q2 rather than the cash generation the preview expected for a U.S. collection quarter. Management attributed the move to peak seasonal working-capital needs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt increased sequentially to $224.7 million from $194.7 million, while cash fell to $43.9 million from $70.9 million at the end of Q1 due to peak seasonal working capital needs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 is a US collection quarter and should generate cash.”

surprises.description: U.S. crop sales declined 9%, rather than holding or merely moderating after Q1 growth. Management said the decline was largely due to cotton portfolio sales shifting into Q3, which points to timing rather than wholly weaker demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A 9% decline in U.S. crop sales driven largely by cotton portfolio sales shifting into Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “US Crop growth moderates” in its base scenario and flagged “US Crop durability and generic pressure.”

surprises.description: First-half gross margin improved 100 basis points to 30%, an unanticipated positive margin result in a quarter marked by lower sales and sharply lower adjusted EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improving 100 basis points to 30%” in the first half.

surprises.description: U.S. specialty sales grew at a double-digit rate, providing an unexpected source of strength alongside the decline in U.S. crop sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. specialty business grew 11% in the quarter and 10% in the first half.”

surprises.description: Freight was a material margin headwind: it reduced first-half margins by about 90 basis points, or roughly $2 million. July price increases are expected to flow through in the second half, providing a stated offset.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Freight costs were a significant headwind, holding back first-half margins by about 90 basis points (~$2 million), with offsetting price increases implemented in July expected to flow through in the second half.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed expected annual savings of at least $4 million from the LA plant rationalization and headquarters relocation, contributing to lower second-half costs; the preview had not highlighted these savings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The LA plant rationalization and headquarter relocation are expected to save at least $4 million annually, contributing to lower second-half costs.”

surprises.description: Management set a new longer-term target of more than $600 million in annualized run-rate revenue by the second half of 2028, with double-digit EBITDA margins. This was not part of the preview’s near-term expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A longer-term target of exceeding $600 million in annualized run-rate revenue by the second half of 2028, roughly 20% above 2025 levels, with double-digit EBITDA margins.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a five-year product-launch and revenue goal alongside a 12% increase in R&D and regulatory spending: 50 launches intended to generate $100 million in annualized revenue by 2030. The preview had not anticipated this investment or target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “R&D and regulatory spending rose 12% year-over-year to support a goal of 50 new product launches over five years generating $100 million in annualized revenue by 2030.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed FY2026 guidance of $530–$550 million in sales and $44–$48 million in adjusted EBITDA, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $5.6 million exceeded both preview estimates of $4.70 million and $5.15 million, by about 9% versus the higher estimate. The preview expected acquisition-driven growth, but the reported revenue was still above the full consensus range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $5.6 million,” up from $3.7 million in Q1.

surprises.description: Management gave full-year revenue expectations despite having provided no guidance in the prior quarter: $20–25 million for legacy QCi plus $7–16 million from NHanced, or roughly $27–41 million combined. Even the low end is above the preview’s $21.88 million FY2026 consensus, though management cautioned that revenue would be lumpy and back-end weighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 revenue expectations of $20-25 million for legacy QCi, with NHanced expected to add between $7 million and $16 million,” while warning results are “lumpy and back-end weighted.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 revenue | Not found | $21.88M”; “Company guidance: None. Management gave no forward guidance for Q2 or FY2026 in the prior quarter.”

surprises.description: Backlog reached $42.5 million, well above the preview’s watchpoint of roughly $25 million and its base-case range of $16–22 million. The contracts are expected to sustain operations into at least Q3 2027, adding duration information beyond the preview’s focus on backlog growth and NeuraWave shipments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Contract backlog stood at approximately $42.5 million as of June 30, 2026,” consisting of “12-18 month contracts expected to sustain operations into at least Q3 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for a print above ~$25M”; the base scenario expected “backlog $16–22M.”

surprises.description: The reported loss per share of $0.05 was much better than the Zacks estimate of a $0.12 loss, but slightly worse than the aggregator estimate of a $0.04 loss. The net loss narrowed sharply year over year, mainly because the derivative mark-to-market loss was far smaller, consistent with the preview’s warning that these marks can distort EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net loss narrowed to $11.8 million ($0.05 per share) from $36.5 million ($0.26 per share) a year earlier,” driven mainly by a “$1.7 million” derivative loss versus “$28 million” a year earlier.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (GAAP) | –$0.12 | –$0.04”; the preview also said “EPS beats or misses are therefore largely mark-to-market noise.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed that 70–80% of revenue comes from government contracting, primarily as a subcontractor, with commercial customers second and education a distant third. The preview asked how much revenue came from acquired versus QCi-branded products but did not anticipate or quantify this customer-market mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly 70-80% of company revenue currently comes from government contracting, primarily as a subcontractor, with commercial second and educational a distant third.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed planned Fab 2 capital expenditures of $50–100 million, likely around $75 million. The preview flagged Fab 2 and capital allocation as issues to watch but gave no expected spending amount; the indication that only a small portion will be spent in 2026 limits the near-term cash impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Planned Fab 2 capital expenditures are estimated at $50-100 million (likely around $75 million),” with “only a small portion” expected to be spent in 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Fab 2” as a catalyst to watch and asked whether the cash balance would go to “more M&A”; it gave no Fab 2 capex estimate.

surprises.description: NHanced was reported to add advanced packaging capacity of roughly 60,000 wafers per year, a specific capacity disclosure not included in the preview. The preview noted NHanced’s acquisition and asked for capacity detail, but did not set an expectation for this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NHanced adding advanced packaging capacity of roughly 60,000 wafers per year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified NHanced as an acquisition and said investors would want “utilization and capacity detail,” without specifying a capacity figure.

in_line: Operating expenses were $21.8 million, below the preview’s level of more than $25 million described as a concern, although they rose 114% year over year and included approximately $7.3 million in acquisition-related transaction expenses.

surprises.description: Revenue of $26.7 million exceeded the preview’s $25.62–$26.13 million consensus range. The 23% year-over-year increase also cleared the preview’s 20%-plus growth threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $26.7 million, up 23% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue against the $25.6–26.1M consensus range”; the preview also called 20% or above the clean-comparison growth threshold.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 42%, above even the preview’s bull-case threshold of 39% or higher. Rather than stepping down from Q1’s 41% as the preview said management had guided, it increased sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 48% to a record $11.2 million, expanding adjusted EBITDA margin by 7 percentage points to a record 42%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was a 37–38% margin and its bull case was 39% or higher; it said “a sequential step-down is what management guided to.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.50 was well above the preview’s $0.333–$0.34 consensus figures. The preview cautioned that consensus sources mixed GAAP and adjusted EPS, so the comparison is not fully clean.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income rose 58% to $7.2 million, yielding record adjusted EPS of $0.50 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed EPS consensus of “$0.333” and “$0.34,” while noting that “the aggregators mix GAAP and adjusted bases.”

in_line: The company reaffirmed full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance in the high 30s, consistent with the preview’s mid-to-high-30s framework.

The approximately $109 million in offering proceeds and their stated uses—including potential strategic acquisitions—were broadly consistent with the preview’s approximately $108.6 million proceeds estimate and base-case expectation that proceeds might be framed as general purpose. The facts provided do not report a named acquisition pipeline.
FOREWARN’s home-healthcare launch was anticipated: the preview identified the July 20 expansion and called it the first material push outside real estate.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $178.3 million exceeded the preview’s $167.7–$169.1 million consensus range by about 5%–6%, and was above the preview’s $165–$175 million base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $178.3 million, up approximately 9% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 revenue … $167.7M (Zacks) or $169.1M (alternate compile)”; base scenario: “$165–175M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached nearly breakeven at negative 0.9%, substantially better than the preview’s base case of negative 10% to negative 15% and even better than its bull-case threshold of negative 8%. It also reached the preview’s anticipated near-breakeven trajectory earlier than the preview’s Q3 framing implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to approximately breakeven (negative 0.9%),” up from “negative 13% last quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: … gross margin ‑10% to ‑15%”; “Bull: … Gross margin ≥ ‑8%”; preview says positive Q4 EBITDAS “would require gross margin near breakeven by Q3.”

surprises.description: Management raised FY26 revenue growth guidance to 15%–16% rather than merely reaffirming the prior 13%–15% outlook, adding roughly 2 percentage points to the lower end and 1 point to the upper end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year revenue growth guidance to 15%-16% from the prior 13%-15%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue … $802–816M (+13–15%)”; the preview’s scenarios describe the base case as “FY guide reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: Net cash usage fell to $61 million, a much sharper improvement than the preview’s general expectation that burn would step down from Q1’s $150 million. This was a substantial sequential reduction, though the preview did not set a specific Q2 burn estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net cash usage improved to $61 million, down approximately 58% sequentially from Q1 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Burn needs to step down sequentially”; “A burn figure that is not clearly lower than Q1's $(150)M is a negative.”

surprises.description: The preview cited restricted-cash releases of about $50 million per quarter, or roughly $200 million over a year; management said only about $155 million was scheduled to be released over the next 12 months, a slower pace than that benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly $155 million of restricted cash [is] scheduled to release over the next 12 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Restricted cash ($579M at Q1) was guided to release about $50M per quarter.”

surprises.description: The reported $62 million of operating expenses was about half the year-ago level, but the decline included $39.7 million of recoveries, principally a $37 million contract-dispute settlement gain; management put the normalized quarterly run rate near $75 million. The reported reduction therefore overstates the recurring cost improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses fell approximately 50% year-over-year to $62 million, though this included $39.7 million of recoveries (principally a $37 million gain from a settled customer contract dispute), with a normalized run rate expected near $75 million per quarter.”

surprises.description: The adjusted EPS loss of $0.07 was slightly better than the preview’s $0.08 loss consensus. GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.14, with about $104 million of noncash mark-to-market charges, a material GAAP-versus-adjusted difference not specified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.14 (including about $104 million of noncash mark-to-market charges tied to stock price appreciation) … while adjusted EPS loss narrowed to $0.07.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 adj. EPS … Consensus $(0.08).”

surprises.description: GenDrive deployment and service performance were strong, with units deployed more than doubling year over year and service revenue rising 82% at a 27% service margin; the preview did not call out these operating metrics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company deployed 1,666 GenDrive units in Q2, more than double the 739 units deployed a year ago, with service revenue up 82% year-over-year to $29.8 million at a 27% service margin.”

surprises.description: Two major Material Handling customers plan to refresh more than 20,000 GenDrive units over three years, with about 2,000 expected in 2026—an announced customer-driven demand opportunity not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Two of the largest Material Handling customers plan to refresh more than 20,000 GenDrive units over three years, with roughly 2,000 units expected to be refreshed in 2026.”

surprises.description: Fuel revenue grew 15% year over year and fuel gross margin and PPA loss rates improved sharply from year-ago levels, although both measures remained negative. The preview did not flag these fuel-economics metrics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fuel revenue grew approximately 15% year-over-year to $39.5 million, with fuel gross margin improving to negative 48% from negative 91% a year ago, while PPA loss rates improved to roughly negative 30% from negative 92%.”

in_line: June 30 unrestricted cash was $161.9 million, essentially matching the preview’s preliminary estimate of about $162 million.

surprises.description: Purple cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $420–$440 million from $465–$485 million, rather than reaffirming the outlook the preview expected. Management attributed the reduction to wholesale softness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to $420–$440 million” due to “wholesale softness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a “guide reaffirmed” was the base case and described the prior FY2026 revenue guide as $465–$485 million.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $98.3 million, below the preview’s $102.5–$103.9 million consensus range and even below its under-$100 million bear-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenue declined 6.5% year-over-year to $98.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus net revenue was “~$103.9M” or “~$102.5M”; the bear scenario was “Under $100M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 45.2%, far above the preview’s roughly 38% expectation. The result was partly aided by a $5.3 million tariff refund, so the margin improvement included a substantial benefit the preview had not anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP gross margin rose about 470 basis points to 45.2%, helped by a $5.3 million tariff refund (100% of applied amount) and sourcing-driven tariff mitigation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said gross margin was expected “against about 38%” and that the EBITDA bridge needed margin “back toward 40%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was positive $2.1 million, better than the preview’s roughly breakeven expectation and its base-case range of a $2 million loss to $1 million profit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA improved $4.4 million year-over-year to a positive $2.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q2 near breakeven” would keep the guide credible and gave a base scenario of “−$2M to +$1M.”

surprises.description: The GAAP loss per share was $0.74, smaller than the preview’s post-split consensus loss of $1.84. The preview cautioned that split restatement differed across vendors, but both figures are stated on a post-split basis here.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss narrowed by $14.1 million to $3.2 million, or a loss of $0.74 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed GAAP EPS consensus as “−$1.84 post-split” and cautioned that “Post-split restatement is inconsistent across data vendors.”

surprises.description: Wholesale revenue fell 19.1%, contrary to the preview’s expectation that wholesale would inflect and help carry H2. Excluding $5.3 million of incremental customer payments, the decline was about 8%, which makes the underlying weakness less severe than the headline decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wholesale revenue fell 19.1% to $37.4 million,” but “excluding $5.3 million in incremental customer payments (co-op marketing and related-party transactions) the decline was approximately 8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said wholesale “needs to inflect to carry H2.”

surprises.description: Management said consumers reacted more negatively than expected to the 8–10% price increases introduced in mid-June, leaving demand elasticity uncertain until after Labor Day. This introduces a demand risk not raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “took an 8–10% price increase across mattresses and pillows in mid-June” and said “early consumer demand reaction was more negative than expected, with elasticity not fully readable until after Labor Day.”

surprises.description: Showroom comparable-store sales rose 18%, substantially stronger than the prior-quarter pace of 7% cited in the preview, and extended the run of positive comps to four consecutive quarters.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Showroom revenue jumped 16.6% to $18.4 million with comparable-store sales up 18%, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of positive comps.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “Showroom comps were +7% in Q1.”

surprises.description: Purple reported that it had regained Nasdaq minimum bid-price compliance after the reverse split. The preview had flagged continued-listing risk as a concern requiring verification, so this is a favorable resolution of that specific issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Purple regained NASDAQ minimum bid price compliance following a July reverse stock split.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said continued-listing risk was a “secondary concern” and called for confirming the applicable Nasdaq standard.

surprises.description: Management disclosed plans to open five showrooms in H2 and 12–16 more in FY2027, a concrete expansion program that the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “plans to open five showrooms in the second half and 12–16 more locations in fiscal 2027.”

in_line: Management maintained its adjusted EBITDA outlook, consistent with the preview noting that the $20–$30 million FY2026 guide had been held and that near-breakeven Q2 performance would help keep it credible.

E-commerce revenue declined just 1.4% and improved for a third consecutive quarter sequentially; this broadly followed the preview’s evidence of improvement from Q1’s decline and flat March performance.

surprises.description: Attruby revenue was $222.4 million, above the preview’s roughly $205 million implied expectation, and rose $41.8 million sequentially—well above the preview’s expected roughly $25 million increase and the $30 million-plus trend it flagged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Attruby net product revenue reached $222.4 million in Q2” from $180.6 million in Q1, and marked “another quarter with a sequential increase of at least $35 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Attruby US net (implied) | ~$205M (+13% q/q)” and “Consensus implies a slowdown to about +$25M q/q”; the catalyst checklist also flagged “Sequential add of $30M or more.”

surprises.description: Total revenue of $243.7 million exceeded the preview’s consensus range of $218.7 million to $222.2 million by about 10%–11%, and was also above its $230 million to $234 million base scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenues were $243.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $218.7M – $222.2M (commonly cited $220.9M)” and the base scenario was “$230–234M.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s concern that category demand might be normalizing, management reported 19% quarterly growth in the ATTR market and said Attruby was the fastest-growing brand, with estimated first-line share gains of 2–3 percentage points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Attruby was the fastest-growing brand in the ATTR space at 23%, with overall market growth of 19% in the quarter” and “first-line share gains estimated at 2-3 percentage points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Category health after Alnylam's guidance cut,” noting its cut cited “normalization in second-line demand,” and said whether BBIO saw the same pattern “in first-line starts is the key question.”

surprises.description: New kidney-protection data suggested that acoramidis could improve outcomes among patients with acute eGFR dips, reframing a feature previously perceived as a drawback. The preview did not flag this clinical result.
surprises.fact_evidence: For patients with acute eGFR dips at or above the median, “acoramidis favored survival/CV-hospitalization outcomes with a hazard ratio of 0.42 (p=0.006), reframing a previously perceived drawback as a differentiator.”

surprises.description: Management cited new real-world evidence associating Attruby with substantially better outcomes than tafamidis, including separation as early as 30 days; this evidence was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New real-world evidence associated Attruby with a 34% reduction in diuretic intensification, heart failure hospitalization and mortality versus tafamidis, with separation observed as early as 30 days.”

surprises.description: All three late-stage NDAs were submitted, with priority review for BBP-418 and encaleret and specified PDUFA dates; the preview discussed funding three launches but did not identify these filing and review milestones.
