surprises.fact_evidence: “Astaris, acquired in May for approximately $356 million in cash, contributed $12.9 million in initial revenue from about a month and a half of sales”; “raised its full-year Astaris revenue guidance to $65-75 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management was targeting “$60M – $70M” for the rest of 2026 and that the call should check whether that figure was reaffirmed.

surprises.description: The preview described the acquired product deal as $650 million in cash plus up to $135 million in milestones, while the call described the acquisition as approximately $356 million in cash. That is a substantially lower stated cash purchase price than the preview led investors to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Astaris, acquired in May for approximately $356 million in cash.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “The deal was $650M in cash plus up to $135M in milestones.”

surprises.description: Quarterly adjusted EBITDA was $113.8 million, above the preview’s buy-side expectation of about $105–$112 million, though the gap above the top of the range was modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 8% to $113.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2’26 adjusted EBITDA: “~$105–112M (buy-side).”

surprises.description: Belbuca grew 10% year over year and gained formulary access covering an additional 9 million lives effective in Q4; the preview did not flag either development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Belbuca revenue grew 10% year-over-year to $57.7 million and recently secured formulary access for an additional 9 million lives effective in Q4.”

in_line: Total net product revenue was $199.9 million, within the preview’s Q2 consensus range of $199.6–$201.4 million.
Journet guidance remained $190–$200 million, matching the preview’s stated full-year guide.
Journet’s prescriber base remained around the level anticipated: the preview noted about 30,000 prescribers, up 17%, and the call reported more than 30,000, up 17.6%.

surprises.description: Underlying diluted EPS declined 22.9% year over year, a smaller decline than the roughly 25.9% implied by the preview’s consensus estimate. That represents a modest beat against expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Underlying EPS decreased 22.9% year-over-year in Q2 FY2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Underlying diluted EPS | $1.51–$1.52 | $2.05 | -25.9%.”

surprises.description: Net sales declined 3.6% in constant currency, slightly worse than the preview’s expected 3.4% decline. The gap is small.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated net sales revenue declined 3.6% in constant currency.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales revenue | ~$3.09B | $3,200.8M | -3.4%.”

surprises.description: Management now expects full-year Midwest Premium inflation to exceed $130 million, with about $40 million of added year-over-year Q2 COGS. This is a cost headwind beyond the initial $125 million figure, although the preview had already flagged Q2 as the peak inflation quarter and asked whether the surcharge had rolled over.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Elevated Midwest premium added approximately $40 million of year-over-year cost to Q2 COGS, and full-year Midwest premium inflation is now expected to exceed $130 million versus the initial guidance of at least $125 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 was flagged as the peak inflation quarter” and “whether the Midwest Premium has rolled over.”

surprises.description: Q2 repurchases were 1 million shares for $42 million, a substantially slower pace than the $164 million and 3.4 million shares repurchased in Q1, which the preview highlighted as a point to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company returned capital by paying $90 million in dividends and repurchasing 1 million shares for $42 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FCF and buyback pace ($164M, 3.4M shares repurchased in Q1).”

surprises.description: Net debt to underlying EBITDA was already 2.53x at quarter-end, close to the stated year-end goal of below 2.5x. The preview identified that goal as a year-end target, so being near it at this point is favorable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt to underlying EBITDA improved to 2.53x at quarter-end, approaching the company's stated year-end goal of under 2.5x following debt refinancing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net debt/EBITDA is guided below 2.5x by year-end.”

surprises.description: Monaco cocktails is tracking slightly ahead of its top- and bottom-line expectations, a favorable update not specified in the preview’s discussion of potential M&A or strategic actions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Monaco cocktails acquisition is tracking slightly ahead of top and bottom line expectations.”

surprises.description: Management said SG&A should decline in the second half versus the prior year and described restructuring that includes a U.K. brewery closure. The preview noted the cost-savings program and flagged restructuring as a possible topic, but did not state an expectation for a second-half SG&A reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects a reduction in SG&A expenses in the second half versus the prior year,” supported by the cost-savings program and “EMEA/APAC restructuring including a U.K. brewery closure.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cost savings program: $450M over 2026–2028” and “Any CEO strategic action on cost program size, EMEA restructuring, or M&A.”

surprises.description: The company identified Rocky Mountain Metal Company upgrades to address aluminum sourcing concerns. The preview focused on aluminum costs and hedges, but did not anticipate this specific supply-chain investment; the total CapEx commitment itself matches the preview’s guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has committed $650 million in global CapEx to modernize supply chain capabilities, including upgrades at Rocky Mountain Metal Company to address aluminum sourcing concerns.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capex: $650M ±5%” and the preview’s discussion of “Aluminum and COGS per hectoliter.”

in_line: U.S. domestic shipments declined 7.3%, within the preview’s cited company guidance range of 6% to 9% declines.
Management reaffirmed full-year fiscal 2026 guidance, matching the preview’s base case of a reaffirmation.
The U.S. beer industry declined 4.2% in Q2, consistent with the preview’s description of a mid-single-digit Q2 industry decline.

surprises.description: Net operating revenues were $719.7 million, far below the preview’s $1.32 billion operating-revenue consensus, despite rising 47% year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 FY26 net operating revenues rose 47% year-over-year to $719.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total operating revenues” consensus: “$1.32B”; the preview says, “Use the operating revenue consensus.”

surprises.description: Net income and diluted EPS missed the preview’s estimates: net income was $127.9 million versus about $144 million implied, and EPS was $1.00 versus about $1.14 consensus. EPS was also below the preview’s $1.20–$1.28 whisper range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income surged 102% to $127.9 million and diluted EPS climbed 85% to $1.00 (split-adjusted).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS” consensus “~$1.14”; “Implied net income” “~$144M”; the preview also flags “a ~$1.20–1.28 whisper.”

surprises.description: StoneX’s return on equity exceeded its stated target: ROE was 18.4% versus a 15% target, with return on tangible equity at 25%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Return on equity was 18.4% for the quarter (25% return on tangible equity), well above the company's 15% target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call states the company’s “15% target.”

surprises.description: FX/CFD and Self-Directed Retail were notably weak: FX/CFD revenues fell 19% year over year and Self-Directed Retail segment income fell 36%, with ADV down 27%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FX/CFD was the sole weak area with revenues down 19% year-over-year and Self-Directed Retail segment income falling 36%, as ADV dropped 27%.”

surprises.description: Physical contract revenues had a sharp year-over-year increase, driven by precious metals: they rose 106%, including a $40.5 million increase in precious metals.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Physical contract operating revenues rose 106% year-over-year, driven by a $40.5 million increase in precious metals.”

surprises.description: The Benchmark Company delivered its best quarter to date, contributing $29.5 million in Institutional segment net operating revenues; the preview did not identify this as an expected result or a key debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Benchmark Company delivered its best quarter to date, contributing $29.5 million in net operating revenues to the Institutional segment.”

surprises.description: Payments reached record ADV and increased revenues, but the mix shift to high-volume, low-value bank flows on X-Pay reduced rate per million by 7%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Payments hit record ADV of $96 million (up 20%) with net operating revenues up 12%, though rate per million declined 7% due to the shift toward high-volume, low-value bank flows on the X-Pay platform.”

surprises.description: The estimated annual net-income impact of a 100-basis-point rate change was slightly lower than the preview’s estimate, at $46.9 million rather than about $47.6 million, even as StoneX added $750 million of swaps.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company added $750 million in new fixed-rate SOFR swaps, bringing total swaps to $2.55 billion at an average rate of 3.51%, with a 100 basis point rate change now estimated to impact annual net income by $46.9 million ($0.38 per share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Rate sensitivity is about $47.6M of annual net income per 100bp.”

in_line: Net income fell 27% from the record immediately preceding quarter, and physical contract revenues fell 39% sequentially from their record prior-quarter level, consistent with the preview’s expectation that activity would moderate and its focus on how much of Q2’s spike would give back.
R.J. O’Brien’s U.S. FCM consolidation remained on track for substantial completion later in FY26, consistent with the preview’s stated end-of-FY26 integration commitment.

R.J. O’Brien synergies were at a roughly $37–38 million annualized run rate exiting Q3, with a mid-$40 million target by fiscal year-end, broadly consistent with the preview’s prior target of about $45 million in FY26 against a $50 million total.

surprises.description: Revenue was $66.8 million versus the preview’s $60.0 million consensus, a $6.8 million or roughly 11% beat. The reported 31% sequential and 41% year-over-year growth also exceeded the preview’s implied growth rates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $66.8 million, up 41% year-over-year and 31% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $60.00M”; consensus implied “+17.6% QoQ / +26.2% YoY.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $59.8 million, substantially above the preview’s $52–53 million estimate. The 89% margin was close to the expected ~88%, so the main surprise was the dollar amount rather than margin expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $59.8 million (89% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$52–53M”; “Adj. EBITDA margin | ~88%.”

surprises.description: Despite the large Q2 beat, LandBridge reaffirmed the full-year EBITDA range rather than raising it or narrowing it upward, which the preview identified as the more positive outcome investors would look for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $210–$230 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise or upper-half narrowing would be a real positive. A reaffirmed full range would read as soft.”

surprises.description: The call described a much broader digital-infrastructure pipeline than the preview’s focus on the 2 GW PowerBridge campus: seven counterparties representing more than 10 GW are in LOI, option, or late-stage negotiations. Those opportunities were not yet firm leases, with management expecting conversions and revenue to begin by the end of next year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Currently under LOI, option, or in late-stage negotiations with seven power and digital infrastructure counterparties representing more than 10 gigawatts”; management expects “multiple digital infrastructure LOIs and options to convert into firm leases with revenues starting by the end of next year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “PowerBridge Alpha Digital Campus” and said to watch for “option exercise, a definitive lease, or named power partners.”

surprises.description: The board moved beyond evaluating a corporate conversion and unanimously approved converting LandBridge from a Delaware LLC to a Texas corporation, with potential index eligibility and a broader investor base as the stated aims.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The board unanimously approved converting LandBridge from a Delaware LLC to a Texas corporation to enable potential index eligibility (S&P, Russell, CRISP) and broaden its investor base.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The board had formed a special committee “to evaluate converting to a Texas corporation”; “there is no assurance of a recommendation, completion, or inclusion.”

surprises.description: Net leverage improved from 2.7x to 2.5x, reaching the top end of the target range cited in the preview; liquidity also increased from the prior-quarter figure in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage improved to 2.5x from 2.7x last quarter, with total liquidity of $269.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “Leverage versus the 2.0–2.5x target” and noted net leverage of 2.7x with $259.7M liquidity.

surprises.description: After quarter-end, the company expanded its revolving credit facility by $100 million, with capacity to expand it further, and reduced borrowing costs by 25 basis points—financing improvements not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “After quarter-end, the company expanded its revolving credit facility from $275 million to $375 million (with capacity to reach $475 million) and cut borrowing costs by 25 basis points.”

surprises.description: The prevailing produced-water royalty rate for new facilities increased from 14 cents to 15 cents per barrel, and management expects further increases as pore-space scarcity intensifies; the preview did not flag this rate development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The prevailing produced water royalty rate for new facilities is now $0.15 per barrel (up from 14 cents), with management expecting rates to keep rising as pore space scarcity intensifies along the state line.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA margin was close to the preview’s expectation: 89% reported versus approximately 88% expected.

surprises.description: Horace Mann reported Q2 core EPS of $1.17, well above the preview's $0.91 consensus, and up more than 10% year over year despite consensus expecting a decline. This was a large upside surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q2 core earnings of $1.17 per share, up more than 10% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Core EPS | Q2'26 Consensus | $0.91”; the preview said this represented “-14%” year over year.

surprises.description: Management raised FY2026 core EPS guidance to $4.60–$4.90 from the preview's $4.20–$4.50 range. The increase was attributed to operating performance, not acquisition contributions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 core EPS guidance to a range of $4.60 to $4.90, attributing the increase entirely to strong operating performance rather than acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (reaffirmed May 6): Core EPS $4.20–$4.50”; the preview said a raise, narrowing, or reaffirmation was being watched.

surprises.description: P&C results were much stronger than the preview's estimated Q2 combined ratio of roughly 97–99%: the reported ratio was 89.6%, and P&C core earnings rose 56%. Favorable weather and lower catastrophe losses helped, along with $7 million of favorable prior-year reserve development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Property & Casualty combined ratio improved 7 points to 89.6% and P&C core earnings rose 56% year-over-year to $26 million, aided by favorable weather, lower catastrophe losses, and $7 million in favorable prior-year reserve development.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Q2 combined ratio of ~97–99% is an estimate, not a consensus figure”; the preview also cited “Q2 catastrophe losses vs. ~$36–40M normalized” as a key metric.

surprises.description: The company cut its full-year catastrophe-loss assumption to about $75 million from roughly $90 million, a more favorable outlook than the preview's stated load. Management cautioned that it does not expect the favorable weather to continue in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year catastrophe loss assumptions were cut from approximately $90 million to $75 million based on favorable first-half experience, though management does not expect the favorable weather to continue into the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (reaffirmed May 6): … catastrophe load ~$90M”; the preview said H1 catastrophe losses were tracking to ~$90M against that annual load.

surprises.description: Net investment income guidance moved down to $465–$475 million from the preview's $485–$495 million range, reflecting weaker alternative-strategy returns. Higher fixed-income new-money yields were a counterpoint, but did not prevent the guidance cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year net investment income guidance was lowered to $465-$475 million due to weaker returns on alternative strategies … sensitive to higher-for-longer rates, though core fixed income new money yields reached 5.85%, over 100 basis points above portfolio yield.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “net investment income $485–495M pre-tax”; the preview flagged “Annuity spread and alternatives” and noted that further sub-target returns could pressure the guide.

surprises.description: Company revenue grew 8% year over year, slightly ahead of the preview's 7.5% growth expectation. The provided call facts do not give a reported revenue amount for comparison with the dollar consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total company revenues increased 8% over the prior-year quarter.”

surprises.description: Individual Supplemental & Group Benefits sales surged 44% and Life sales grew 20%; the preview did not identify these sales growth rates as an expectation or key debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Individual Supplemental & Group Benefits sales surged 44% and Life sales grew 20%.”

surprises.description: Management raised the blended benefit-ratio assumption for Individual Supplemental & Group Benefits to about 42%, which the preview had not flagged. The higher ratio reflects growth in paid family and medical leave, with higher benefit ratios offset by lower expense ratios.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its Individual Supplemental & Group Benefits blended benefit ratio assumption to approximately 42%, driven by growth in paid family and medical leave, which carries higher benefit ratios offset by lower expense ratios.”

in_line: The acquisitions' expected ROE accretion of about 100 basis points was consistent with the preview's estimate of approximately 100 basis points.

surprises.description: Vontier’s Q2 core sales were flat year over year, slightly better than the preview’s roughly 1% decline expectation and ahead of company guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 core sales were approximately flat year-over-year” and “came in slightly ahead of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Core sales growth: ~-1% (midpoint).”

surprises.description: Vontier raised its full-year adjusted EPS outlook to $3.45–$3.55 from $3.35–$3.50, despite reducing its operating-margin expansion outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $3.45-$3.55, representing 8%-11% growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance reaffirmed: adj. EPS $3.35–$3.50.”

surprises.description: The company cut expected full-year adjusted operating-margin expansion to about 100 basis points from 130, below the preview’s expectation that the prior outlook would be maintained or improved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Trimming full-year operating margin expansion guidance to ~100 bps from a prior 130 bps.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY26 outlook was “about 130 bps of adj. margin expansion” and listed the EPS guide as “maintained, narrowed, or cut.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted operating margin expanded 190 basis points, but a one-time IEEPA tariff refund supplied about 120 basis points of that increase, leaving underlying expansion of only 70 basis points. The preview did not anticipate this refund or the resulting gap between reported and underlying margin growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin expanded 190 basis points year-over-year, though ~120 basis points came from a onetime IEEPA tariff refund, leaving underlying margin expansion of 70 basis points.”

surprises.description: Repair Solutions remained a drag: its margins fell 180 basis points, and Vontier lowered the segment’s full-year margin outlook to down about 150 basis points, or around 19%, alongside a $7–8 million downward revision and a leadership change. The preview had noted the prior-quarter margin decline but did not flag this further outlook revision or management response.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repair Solutions margins declined 180 basis points and were the primary drag, prompting a leadership change and a $7-8 million downward revision, with full-year segment margins now expected down ~150 bps to around 19%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted: “Repair Solutions was flat … with margin down 180 bps to 19.9%,” but gave no Q2 or full-year Repair Solutions outlook.

surprises.description: Environmental & Fueling Solutions grew about 5% in Q2, including double-digit dispenser growth, and Vontier raised its full-year segment growth outlook from low-to-mid single digits to mid-single digits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Environmental & Fueling Solutions delivered ~5% core growth with double-digit dispenser growth, and full-year guidance was raised from low-to-mid to mid-single-digit growth.”

surprises.description: Mobility Technologies’ underlying margins expanded 170 basis points to about 21%, exceeding the preview’s expectation of a recovery toward roughly 19%, even though reported core sales declined on a prior-year shipment comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Underlying demand grew mid-single digits with underlying margins expanding 170 bps to ~21%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management had promised “a Q2 recovery,” cited a Q2'25 comparison level of “about 19%,” and described the bull case as MT margin moving “back toward 19%.”

surprises.description: Vontier lowered Mobility Technologies’ full-year growth outlook from low-to-mid single digits to low single digits after DRB/Patheon car-wash software upgrades slipped because of permitting delays.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mobility Tech full-year guidance was lowered from low-to-mid to low-single-digit growth as DRB/Patheon car wash software upgrades slipped due to permitting delays, with 90% of the installed base still on legacy technology.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY core-growth guide was “about 3%” and that it “implies a meaningful H2 step-up from about -1% in Q2.”

surprises.description: The company increased its share repurchase authorization to $1 billion and now expects about $250 million of full-year buybacks, above the preview’s roughly $150 million full-year assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company increased its share repurchase authorization to $1 billion” and “expects ~$250 million in buybacks for the full year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “a full-year assumption of about $150M.”

surprises.description: Vontier acquired EKOS, a fleet energy-management business with roughly 80% recurring revenue and 25% annual growth, a deal not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company acquired EKOS for $43 million cash plus an earn-out,” with “~80% recurring revenue growing 25% annually” and expected fiscal 2027 revenue of “$15-17 million” at mid-teens margins.

surprises.description: Cost savings were tracking above the $50 million full-year commitment, a favorable operating update not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cost savings are tracking above the $50 million full-year commitment.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted free cash flow rebounded to $98 million from $28 million in Q1, providing the visible catch-up the preview said was needed; the preview did not specify a Q2 FCF target.
Q2 share repurchases were about $130 million, matching the amount cited in the preview; the surprise was the higher full-year buyback expectation.

surprises.description: Gross margin was 65.9%, far above the preview’s roughly 38% expectation. The call attributed most of the increase to the tariff refund, with lower-margin warehouse-club volume partly offsetting it, so the result does not by itself show that underlying margins rose to that level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin surged to 65.9% from 38.6% a year ago, driven mainly by the tariff refund but partially offset by unfavorable product mix from lower-margin warehouse club volume.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management says pricing is embedded and structural, so margin should hold near 38%”; the preview also said a print “below about 36.5%” would challenge that claim.

surprises.description: The preview described the $41.7 million tariff refund as excluded from guidance and still pending court and administrative resolution. Instead, the company recorded a $40.1 million refund benefit and had received about $36 million in cash, making the realization and timing more favorable than that description implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company recorded a $40.1 million IEPA tariff refund benefit (against $41.7 million paid in 2025), of which approximately $36 million in cash had been received to date.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AIPA tariff refund of $41.7M. Excluded from guidance and pending court and administrative resolution. Any change in tone or timing would matter.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA and adjusted net income guidance, rather than leaving the earnings outlook unchanged. The preview highlighted guidance as a key debate and said a raise would be more constructive, although it did not specify that a raise was the base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $90.5-$93 million and adjusted net income guidance to $46-$47.5 million while maintaining net sales guidance of $650-$700 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance treatment. Reaffirm, raise, or trim the $650–700M sales range and the $0.73–0.80 adj. EPS range”; “A raise is more constructive.”

surprises.description: Q2 net sales beat the preview’s $136.64 million consensus by about $5 million, or 3.6%. The 7.4% year-over-year increase came against an easy comparison because tariff actions had largely halted shipments in the prior-year quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net sales rose 7.4% year-over-year to $141.6 million, though the comparison was easy against a prior-year quarter when tariff actions largely halted shipments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $136.64M” for Q2 FY2026 consensus.

surprises.description: The Hagerstown distribution-center startup is weighing on distribution expense, and continued disruption could push one-time costs above prior estimates. The preview had flagged elevated SG&A as a risk but did not identify this specific startup-related cost pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The new Hagerstown, Maryland distribution center startup raised US distribution expense to 11.9% of goods shipped from 11%, and continued operational disruption could push one-time costs above prior estimates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 SG&A rose 16.8% against roughly 2–3% revenue growth. Continued growth at that pace would weigh on the cost-reset narrative.”

surprises.description: The company had repaid $40 million of term debt since Q1 ended, an unpreviewed deleveraging step that reduced net debt by roughly $39 million since year-end 2025.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repaid $40 million of term debt since the end of Q1 ($20 million in Q2 and $20 million in early July), reducing net debt by roughly $39 million since year-end 2025 to approximately $121 million.”

surprises.description: Management said it was refinancing both the revolving credit facility and term loan, with the aim of lowering annualized interest expense and extending all maturities to 2031; signing could be imminent. The preview did not flag a refinancing plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is refinancing its revolving credit facility and term loan, expecting to lower annualized interest expense and extend all debt maturities to 2031, with signing possibly imminent.”

surprises.description: Third-party data indicated that the company’s consumer-durables categories were contracting in both dollars and units, an unpreviewed market headwind. Management said Lifetime outperformed the market, tempering but not eliminating that concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Third-party data showed the company's consumer durables categories down 2-3% in dollars and 7.5-10% in units, though management stated Lifetime outperformed the market.”

in_line: The company maintained its $650–$700 million full-year net sales guidance, within the preview’s stated expectation that guidance could be reaffirmed, raised, or trimmed.

surprises.description: AWR reported Q2 EPS of $1.09, well above the preview’s $0.93 consensus estimate. The 16-cent gap was a substantial upside surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 EPS rose 25.3% year-over-year to $1.09 from $0.87.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 EPS (diluted) … Consensus $0.93.”

surprises.description: Golden State Water earned $0.91 per share, well above the preview’s approximately $0.78 base case. The preview identified water earnings as the most important part of the print, so this was a substantial beat on a key debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Water segment (Golden State Water) earnings grew $0.18 to $0.91 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Water segment EPS … ~$0.78 base case.”

surprises.description: The preview focused on whether the Q1 well outage had resolved and allowed for partial supply drag; instead, AWR reported lower reliance on purchased water and 4% higher consumption as Q2 earnings drivers. That is a more favorable supply mix and demand outcome than the preview’s base case suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 EPS was driven in part by “a 4% increase in water consumption, and lower reliance on purchased water.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case assumed “partial supply drag,” and the preview asked, “Did the Q1 well outage resolve?”

surprises.description: Management cautioned that the stronger consumption and supply mix may not last and could reverse during the rest of 2026. The preview highlighted the earnings sensitivity to consumption and supply mix, but did not anticipate this explicit warning about a possible reversal.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management said favorable Q2 conditions “may not persist and could reverse over the remainder of 2026 due to decoupling and balancing account mechanisms.”

surprises.description: The annual infrastructure investment outlook tops out at $220 million rather than the preview’s $225 million. The lower ceiling is a small downward change to the expected capex range, though the reported pace remains within the preview’s range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Regulated utilities are “on pace to invest $185 million to $220 million in infrastructure in 2026,” with $91.7 million spent in the first half.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Company-funded capex was expected to be “$185–$225M for FY2026.”

surprises.description: The new water rate case requests approximately $1 billion in capital budgets for 2028–2030. That is notably above the preview’s reference point of $573.1 million in authorized capital for 2025–2027, although the new request is not an approved amount and the periods differ.
surprises.fact_evidence: Golden State Water filed a rate case requesting “approximately $1 billion in capital budgets for 2028-2030.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the capital ask mattered and gave “$573.1M authorized capital for 2025–2027” as a reference point.

in_line: ASUS’s FY2026 contribution outlook was reiterated at $0.63–$0.67 per share, matching the preview’s stated guidance range.
The company remains on pace to invest within the preview’s $185–$225 million FY2026 capex range, despite the reported range’s lower $220 million top end.
The $200 million ATM program was completed and management reiterated no plans for additional equity through at least the end of 2029, as already reported in the preview.

surprises.description: SEI reported Q2 adjusted EBITDA of about $108 million, well above its $83–93 million company guide and also above the preview’s $90–93 million base case. The result was driven in part by higher Power Solutions ancillary-service revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $108 million, up 30% sequentially”; Power Solutions adjusted EBITDA was “~$96 million” and was “driven by increased ancillary service revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The company’s Q2 guide was “$83–93M”; the preview’s base case was “$90–93M,” and it said a print at the “$88M midpoint is soft.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $219 million, exceeding either of the preview’s conflicting estimates: $181 million or roughly $205 million. Even against the higher estimate, the result was about 7% above expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached approximately $219 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 revenue consensus as “$181M (Zacks) or ~$205M (implied by StockStory's +37% Y/Y).”

surprises.description: SEI raised Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance instead of merely reaffirming the prior range: the new $90–105 million range is higher at both ends than the earlier $80–95 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $90-105 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited existing Q3 guidance of “$80–95M” and said reaffirming it would be neutral, while an upward narrowing would be a bull trigger.

surprises.description: Adjusted pro forma earnings per diluted share were $0.39, above the preview’s $0.26 adjusted EPS consensus. This is the opposite of the preview’s concern that higher interest expense could leave EPS light despite strong EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted pro forma net income was $37 million or $0.39 per fully diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Q2 adj. EPS | $0.26” and warned that “an EBITDA beat could still show an EPS miss.”

surprises.description: SEI provided initial Q4 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $100–120 million, adding a forward-quarter outlook the preview did not identify as an existing guide. Management linked it to GESA, the Stateline ramp, and a third hyperscaler customer.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Established initial Q4 2026 guidance of $100-120 million, reflecting the GESA acquisition and ramp of Stateline and the third hyperscaler customer.”

surprises.description: The amount under long-term contract with the three investment-grade technology customers was reported at 2.3 gigawatts, above the preview’s prior estimate of roughly 2.0–2.1 gigawatts. SEI also disclosed about 800 megawatts of open capacity with near-term delivery timelines.
surprises.fact_evidence: “2.3 gigawatts currently under long-term contract with three investment-grade technology customers, plus approximately 800 megawatts of open (uncontracted) capacity with near-term delivery timelines.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “~2.0–2.1 GW is under long-term contract with three investment-grade customers.”

surprises.description: The existing Hatchbo deal was amended to a turnkey 660-megawatt capacity and operating contract, with its term extended from up to 15 years to up to 18 years. The preview had identified the 600-plus-megawatt contract and January 2027 equipment deliveries, but not this longer term or turnkey scope.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Hatchbo agreement was amended to a turnkey 660-megawatt capacity and operating contract, extending the term from up to 15 years to up to 18 years”; revenue begins January 2027 and “over 70% of required equipment” is available.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview referred to a “600+ MW contract” and said “new equipment deliveries begin January 2027.”

surprises.description: A large energy customer expanded its contracted capacity from 60 to about 80 megawatts and lengthened the contract from four to six years. The customer’s stated reason was that grid interconnection is now seven to eight years away, a delay not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “One large energy customer, informed that grid interconnection is now 7-8 years away, expanded contracted power capacity from 60 to approximately 80 megawatts and extended the term from 4 to 6 years.”

surprises.description: Management made an unusually strong valuation claim, saying cash flow from current contracts already exceeds SEI’s entire enterprise value. The preview discussed valuation and market concerns but did not anticipate this specific assertion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash flow from current contracts already exceeds the company's entire enterprise value.”

surprises.description: SEI disclosed that its early-stage Deployable Energy SMR investment achieved reactor criticality under a DOE program, an operational milestone not mentioned in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Its early-stage SMR investment (Deployable Energy) achieved reactor criticality under a DOE program.”

in_line: The preview identified the GESA acquisition and the $1.3 billion notes plus $650 million revolver as already completed post-quarter events. The call reported the financing and over $800 million in cash, with roughly $1.4 billion in total liquidity.

The preview flagged late-2026 energization and January 2027 deliveries as timing items to watch. The call said Hatchbo revenue begins in January 2027 and that more than 70% of required equipment is already available; it did not report a timing slip.
No fourth counterparty was announced: the reported long-term contracts remain with three investment-grade technology customers, consistent with the preview’s stated base case of no new contract.

surprises.description: Sotera reported Q2 revenue of $321 million, about 3.6% above the preview’s $309.4–$309.7 million consensus range. Revenue grew 8% in constant currency, stronger than the preview’s roughly 5.2% implied growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 consolidated revenue rose 9.2% to $321 million (8% constant currency).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenues | $309.4M – $309.7M” and “Implied Y/Y | +5.2%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.26, above the preview’s approximately $0.24 consensus. That is a larger beat than the preview’s base-case range of $0.23–$0.24, though it matched the preview’s bull scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased 30% year-over-year to $0.26.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | ~$0.24 ($0.2389)” and the base scenario’s “Adj. EPS | ~$0.23–$0.24.”

surprises.description: Nordion grew 16.7% in constant currency in Q2, rather than showing the year-over-year decline the preview said could occur if Q1’s harvest timing pulled revenue out of Q2. However, first-half revenue exceeded the company’s 40%–45% full-year pacing range because second-half shipments shifted into Q2, leaving tougher comparisons later in the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nordion posted 16.7% constant currency revenue growth, but first-half revenue exceeded the guided 40%-45% of full-year range as second-half shipments shifted into Q2, implying tougher second-half comparisons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Y/Y decline in Q2 would support the bear reading that Q1 pulled from Q2.”

surprises.description: Sterigenics’ 7% constant-currency growth cleared the preview’s 6% threshold for supporting a volume recovery. Pricing contributed 4.3%—above the high end of the preview’s expected 3%–4% range—and volume/mix added 2.7%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sterigenics delivered 7% constant currency revenue growth driven by favorable pricing of 4.3% and volume/mix of 2.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Growth of 6% or more would support the volume recovery” and “Pricing tracking to the high end of 3–4%.”

surprises.description: Nelson Labs grew 5.4% in constant currency, exceeding the preview’s expectation of only a slight return to growth. Its margin also rose 438 basis points sequentially to 32.4%, although the year-over-year margin decline was anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nelson Labs exceeded expectations with 5.4% constant currency revenue growth and improved segment margin 438 basis points sequentially to 32.4%, though margins declined year-over-year due to higher costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Nelson Labs expects a ‘slight return to growth’ in Q2” and “segment margin may fall Y/Y against 34.2% in Q2'25.”

surprises.description: Sotera raised its full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA growth outlook by 25 basis points each, and lifted the low end of adjusted EPS guidance from $0.93 to $0.95 while leaving the high end at $1.01. The preview’s base case was a reaffirmation, so the upward revision was a positive change, though a modest one.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year 2026 outlook, now expecting constant currency revenue growth of 5.25% to 6.75% and constant currency adjusted EBITDA growth of 5.75% to 7.25%, a 25 basis point increase to both from prior guidance”; adjusted EPS outlook rose “to $0.95-$1.01 from $0.93-$1.01.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario anticipated an “In-line quarter, FY reaffirmed”; the bull scenario anticipated “FY guide raised or narrowed to the upper half.”

surprises.description: The company raised the low end of its 2026 capital expenditure range from $175 million to $200 million, with a new X-ray facility set to begin generating revenue in Q3 and a previously paused greenfield project now fully underway. Management also expects a meaningful CapEx step-down in 2027; the preview had not anticipated these project updates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new X-ray facility begins generating revenue in Q3 and a previously paused second greenfield project is now fully underway, driving full-year CapEx guidance of $200-$225 million with a meaningful step down expected in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capex $175M–$225M”; the preview also flagged “capex” as something to watch on the first CEO call.

surprises.description: Net leverage fell to 3.0x from 3.2x in Q1, reaching the company’s stated 2.0x–3.0x long-term target range. Liquidity was about $950 million and the revolver was undrawn, improving on the preview’s Q1 reference to leverage of 3.2x and liquidity above $900 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage ratio improved to 3x, reaching the company's long-term target range of 2-3x, with roughly $950 million of liquidity and nothing drawn on the revolver.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net leverage 3.2x; more than $900M liquidity” and “Watch for a clean Q2 cash quarter and any change in capital-allocation tone.”

surprises.description: Interest expense was down by more than $6 million to $34 million after a 100-basis-point reduction in the term-loan borrowing cost, and Sotera narrowed its full-year interest expense outlook to $135–$142 million. The preview did not discuss an interest expense outlook or this repricing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Interest expense fell over $6 million to $34 million after repricing lowered borrowing costs on the $1.4 billion term loan by 100 basis points in under a year, prompting a narrowed interest expense outlook of $135-$142 million.”

surprises.description: Sotera disclosed that it resolved the New Mexico EO litigation in July for an immaterial amount, while a Georgia appellate ruling is still expected in spring or summer and a California trial is expected in January or April 2027. The preview did not flag these proceedings or their timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management resolved the New Mexico EO litigation in July for an immaterial amount, awaits a spring/summer appellate ruling in Georgia, and expects the California trial in January or April 2027.”

in_line: Nelson Labs’ year-over-year margin decline was in line with the preview’s expectation that its margin might fall against Q2 2025.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $172 million, about 5.6% above the preview’s $162.8 million consensus and at the top of its $168–172 million bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total sales rose 17% year-over-year to a record $172 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q2'26 consensus | $162.80M”; the bull scenario projected “Revenue $168–172M.”

surprises.description: Loar raised its full-year sales, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EPS outlook by more than the preview’s illustrative base-case guide increase: the new ranges are $665–675 million, $265–270 million, and $1.32–1.36, respectively. The sales and EPS ranges also exceed the preview’s bull-case guide levels of roughly $658–668 million and $1.32 at the high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its calendar 2026 guidance to net sales of $665M-$675M, adjusted EBITDA of $265M-$270M (~40% margin), and adjusted EPS of $1.32-$1.36, up from $1.26-$1.30 prior.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “FY guide nudged to ~$650–660M”; its bull case anticipated “FY guide raised to ~$658–668M.”

surprises.description: Defense grew 8% after the preview highlighted that the segment needed to turn positive following a roughly 2% Q1 decline, and noted a mid-single-digit full-year growth guide. The reported growth is stronger than that bar suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Defense grew 8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Defense. Down ~2% in Q1 against a mid-single-digit FY growth guide. Q2 needs to turn positive.”

surprises.description: The organic new-business pipeline and secured orders were not quantified in the preview: management reported about $750 million of five-year revenue potential, up roughly $50 million since May, with about $200 million converted to initial orders.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The organic new business pipeline totals approximately $750 million of revenue potential over five years (up ~$50M from May), with ~$200 million now converted to secured initial orders.”

surprises.description: Management offered stronger confidence in the raised outlook than the preview’s discussion of a required guide raise alone: it said it expects to meet or beat the high end, citing first-half sales and adjusted EBITDA growth of about 38% and 47%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management framed guidance as a figure they expect to “meet or beat” at the high end, “signaling potential conservatism given first-half sales and adjusted EBITDA growth of ~38% and ~47%, respectively.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise is effectively required”; the preview’s bull case described a guide raise but did not anticipate a meet-or-beat-the-high-end stance.

surprises.description: Aftermarket growth slowed to 12% from the 24.5% Q1 rate cited in the preview, although it remained positive. Management said destocking is largely behind the company and expects stronger aftermarket growth in 2027, tempering the slowdown with a better forward outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commercial aftermarket rose 12%”; management said destocking is largely behind them, customer stock levels fell “from 5-7 months in March to 3-5 months,” and this supports expectations for stronger 2027 aftermarket growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Commercial Aftermarket. Up 24.5% Y/Y to $54.6M in Q1. Morgan Stanley's July downgrade cited better-value commercial aftermarket alternatives.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s warning that Harper had been significantly dilutive to margins initially, management said all three recent acquisitions—Beadlight, LMB, and Harper—are performing ahead of expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “All three recent acquisitions (Beadlight, LMB, Harper) are performing ahead of expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Harper Engineering (closed Jan 2026) was called ‘significantly dilutive’ to margins initially.”

surprises.description: GAAP net income stayed flat even as operating income rose, because higher interest expense and non-cash amortization offset the increase; adjusted net income was up 35%. The preview focused on adjusted EPS and noted the GAAP-versus-adjusted gap, but did not forecast this Q2 net-income outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income was flat year-over-year as higher operating income was offset by increased interest expense and non-cash amortization, though adjusted net income rose 35% (~$9M).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “GAAP versus adjusted” was important and that “the gap from GAAP is mostly amortization,” but provided no Q2 net-income estimate.

surprises.description: The company reported strong year-to-date cash conversion and low capital spending, metrics the preview did not quantify despite flagging debt and capital allocation as issues to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capex) reached approximately 1.9x reported net income, with capex held at ~3% of sales (~$20M).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “M&A and capital allocation” and estimated roughly $950 million of total debt, but gave no cash-flow or capex expectation.

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 40.5%, essentially matching the preview’s roughly 40% expectation and the 40.5% Q1 record; the preview’s 41%-or-higher level was described as a bull-case outcome.
The raised outlook implies roughly $337–347 million of second-half sales using the reported first-half figures, broadly in line with the preview’s estimate of about $335 million in 2H.

surprises.description: Koppers exceeded the preview’s headline estimates: sales were $520 million versus $506.1 million expected, adjusted EPS was $1.37 versus $1.12, and adjusted EBITDA was $71 million versus an implied roughly $65 million. The EPS beat was especially large, even though EBITDA was only modestly above the preview’s roughly $70 million “bar that matters.”
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales rose 3% to $520 million”; “adjusted EBITDA fell 7.9% year-over-year to $71 million”; “adjusted EPS of $1.37.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $506.1M”; “Adjusted EPS $1.12”; “Adj. EBITDA (implied) ~$65M”; “The bar that matters may be closer to EBITDA of about $70M.”

surprises.description: The company lowered the top end of its FY2026 adjusted EBITDA and EPS guidance rather than reaffirming the preview’s full ranges. EBITDA guidance is now $240–250 million instead of $240–260 million, and adjusted EPS is $3.80–$4.20 instead of $3.80–$4.60.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reiterated full-year 2026 guidance of ... $240-250 million adjusted EBITDA, and $3.80-$4.20 adjusted EPS.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: $240–260M”; “Adj. EPS: $3.80–4.60”; the preview said to watch whether guidance “narrows toward the low half.”

surprises.description: Performance Chemicals was stronger than the preview’s inventory-payback concern suggested: sales grew 10% excluding FX, adjusted EBITDA rose 31%, and margins exceeded 20%. That margin was above even the preview’s bull-case assumption of about 19%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Performance chemicals adjusted EBITDA jumped 31% to $38 million on 10% ex-FX sales growth ... with margins exceeding 20%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview warned that “A payback quarter would weaken the share-gain story” after Q1 PC volume included “about 6% of customer inventory build”; its bull case assumed “PC margin holds near 19%.”

surprises.description: First-half cash generation was exceptionally strong, with record operating cash flow of $96 million and free cash flow of $73 million, driven by inventory alignment. The preview flagged cash flow and leverage as issues to watch but gave no H1 cash-flow expectation or target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half operating cash flow hit a record $96 million (up from $28 million) and free cash flow reached a record $73 million (up from $1 million), driven by inventory alignment.”

surprises.description: CMC EBITDA of $8 million was above the preview’s roughly $6 million base case, but it did not reach the preview’s greater-than-$10-million upside threshold and remained well below the prior-year $16.8 million. The call also quantified a continuing oil-cost burden, including another $4.6 million expected in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CMC adjusted EBITDA fell to $8 million from $17 million,” hurt by “a ~$2.3 million Q2 oil-price impact, with another $4.6 million impact expected in the second half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The base case is about $6M”; “Above $10M would be a real upside surprise”; Q2 2025 CMC EBITDA was “$16.8M.”

surprises.description: Koppers accelerated the Stickney facility closure to September 30, 2026. The preview focused on the expected Q2–Q3 charge and on confirming the future benefits, but did not anticipate an accelerated closure date.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Accelerating the closure of its Stickney facility to September 30, 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described a “$170–195M landing across Q2–Q3” for the Stickney charge and said to confirm the cash portion and future accretion.

surprises.description: The call reported $33 million of Catalyst transformation benefits through June 30, already at the midpoint of the prior full-year target, and more than $90 million of benefits identified for 2026–2028. The preview did not flag this level of achieved or identified transformation benefits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Catalyst transformation delivered $33 million in year-over-year benefits through June 30 (already at the prior full-year target's midpoint), with over $90 million in benefits identified for 2026-2028.”

surprises.description: Despite net leverage remaining at 3.5x against a 2–3x long-term target, the company returned $47 million to shareholders in the first half and still had about $30 million left under its buyback authorization. The preview identified buybacks versus debt reduction as an open allocation question but did not indicate this level of shareholder returns.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Returned $47 million to shareholders in the first half (with ~$30 million remaining on its $100 million buyback authorization)”; “Net debt stood at $857 million with a 3.5x net leverage ratio ... against a long-term target of 2-3x leverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buyback pace vs. debt paydown is an open allocation question”; net leverage was “3.5x vs. a 2–3x target.”

in_line: FY2026 sales guidance remained $1.9–2.0 billion, as in the preview.
The $15–20 million annual adjusted EBITDA and roughly $1.00–$1.20 per-share EPS benefit expected from Stickney remained the stated target.
The $0.09 quarterly dividend matched the preview, which said the dividend had been declared at $0.09 on August 5.
The need for meaningful future price increases to address copper costs was consistent with the preview’s concern about roughly $50 million of 2027 price adjustments.

surprises.description: Cheniere raised 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $7.9–$8.4 billion and DCF to $5.3–$5.8 billion, with each new low end above the previous high end. The increase was stronger than the preview’s bull-case range, and full-year production guidance also moved up at the low end to 53 million tonnes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 guidance for the second consecutive quarter to $7.9-$8.4 billion consolidated adjusted EBITDA and $5.3-$5.8 billion DCF, with the new low end exceeding the previous high end for both metrics”; production guidance was “tightened and raised to 53-54 million tonnes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed prior guidance of “$7.25–7.75B” EBITDA and “$4.75–5.25B” DCF; its bull case anticipated a raise to “$7.6–8.0B” EBITDA and “$5.0–5.4B” DCF.

surprises.description: Management said the company can sustain an $8-plus-billion EBITDA run-rate even with normalized marketing margins, rather than relying on today’s much higher margins. The preview focused on the near-term guidance revision and did not anticipate this claim about the durability of the earnings level.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management expects “the $8+ billion EBITDA level to be sustainable run-rate even at normalized $2.50-$3 marketing margins (versus current $10-$13), rather than a one-off tied to elevated LNG prices.”

surprises.description: Construction progress was ahead of schedule: Train 6 was substantially complete in June, Train 7 was commissioning, and Trains 8 and 9 were also ahead. The preview anticipated Train 7 production in early August and substantial completion in August or September, but did not describe Train 6 as already substantially complete or the mid-scale trains as ahead.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CCL Stage 3 is over 98% complete with Train 6 substantially completed in June and Train 7 commissioning underway, ahead of its 2027 guaranteed date, while mid-scale Trains 8 and 9 are over 48% complete and ahead of schedule.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Train 7 production was “set to begin in early August” and that “Substantial completion in Aug or Sep 2026 would pull 2027 EBITDA forward.”

surprises.description: Cheniere signed a roughly $4.7 billion turnkey EPC contract for Sabine Pass Phase 1 and said financing was underway. The preview anticipated an LNTP later in 2026 and an early-2027 FID, but did not forecast this contract signing or financing progress.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Signed a ~$4.7 billion lump-sum turnkey EPC contract with Bechtel for Sabine Pass Phase 1,” adding over 6 million tonnes per annum, with “FID expected early 2027 and financing already underway.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “Sabine Pass Expansion LNTP” as guided for late 2026 with “FID in early 2027.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a new accounting designation for most IPM volumes that will remove mark-to-market derivative swings from those volumes. This addresses the reporting volatility the preview warned about, and management said it would have substantially reduced the number of historical negative-net-income quarters; it does not, by itself, change the underlying economics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Designated normal-purchase/normal-sale accounting for ~75% of IPM volumes starting mid-June,” which “will eliminate mark-to-market derivative swings and would have cut negative net income quarters since 2021 from six to two.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “GAAP EPS is dominated by non-cash mark-to-market on IPM gas supply derivatives” and cautioned, “Do not trade the EPS line.”

surprises.description: Management described a substantial supply disruption around the Strait of Hormuz and a resulting tightness in key LNG markets, including a European storage shortfall it expects will persist into winter. The preview noted strong but sequentially softer benchmark prices, but did not anticipate this supply disruption or the stated storage outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: The disruption “cut Qatar/UAE exports by ~18 million tonnes in the quarter,” helped drive U.S. exports to Asia to a record “~11 million tonnes,” and left Europe with an “~11 Bcm storage deficit” that management expects will struggle to reach even 70% fullness before winter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q2 TTF and JKM prices “both softened sequentially.”

surprises.description: Management reiterated a commitment to at least 10% annual dividend growth through the end of the decade, a longer-term dividend-growth commitment not specified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Remains committed to at least 10% annual dividend growth through decade-end.”

in_line: Q2 adjusted EBITDA of approximately $1.8 billion was close to the preview’s roughly $1.7 billion estimate and within its estimated $1.55–$1.85 billion range; DCF of $1.2 billion was at the top of the preview’s $1.1–$1.2 billion estimate.
The $550 million Q2 repurchase was only modestly above the preview’s roughly $535 million Q1 pace, consistent with its stated watch for repurchases above that pace.
The early-2027 FID timing for Sabine Pass was consistent with the preview’s expectation.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $151 million, about $4 million above the $146.7 million consensus; even excluding the $1.6 million patent settlement, revenue of $149.4 million beat consensus and grew 3% year over year rather than being roughly flat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $151 million, or $149.4 million excluding a $1.6 million patent settlement, representing just 3% year-over-year growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $146.7M”; “Excluding it, Q2'25 core revenue was about $146M, so consensus implies roughly flat core revenue.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year revenue range instead of maintaining the prior guidance, with the new range implying 2–5% growth excluding settlement revenue rather than the preview’s expected 0–4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $610–630 million, representing 2–5% growth over 2025 excluding nonrecurring settlement revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance: $600–625M, maintained. This is 0–4% growth excluding 2025 settlements.”

surprises.description: Atera orders had already greatly exceeded the full-year target by Q2, substantially more demand evidence than the preview’s call for a higher unit count or a quantified backlog. However, the company still expects to ship only about 40 instruments because manufacturing capacity constrains shipments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Atera booked orders already greatly exceeded the full-year target of ~40 instruments by the end of Q2, though the ~40 unit shipment outlook remains unchanged due to manufacturing capacity constraints.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The stock needs a higher unit count or a quantified backlog. A reiteration with no new detail is a negative.”

surprises.description: Instrument revenue contracted much more broadly than the preview’s focus on customers delaying spatial purchases: total instrument revenue fell 47%, with Chromium down 46% as well as Spatial down 48%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total instrument revenue fell 47% year-over-year, with Chromium instruments down 46% and Spatial instruments down 48%, as customers moderated purchases ahead of the Atera launch.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said customers are deferring spatial instrument purchases while waiting for Atera”; the preview’s instrument watch was specifically “Spatial instrument revenue” with consensus-style modeling of “$3–4M.”

surprises.description: Management indicated revenue would step down sequentially in Q3 before recovering in Q4, despite the preview describing Q2 as the trough. That signals a later near-term low than the preview’s framing suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects a modest sequential revenue step-down in Q3 as the Spatial transition peaks, followed by a significant Q4 step-up driven mostly by Atera shipments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management pre-guided Q2 as the trough.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 74%, well above the preview’s roughly 64–66% consensus assumption and its 68–69% upside scenario. The company attributed improvement in part to lower manufacturing costs and tariff refunds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 74% from 72% (or from 67% excluding settlement revenue), aided by lower manufacturing costs including $2.6 million of tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~64–66% (implied)”; the bull scenario anticipated “GM 68–69%.”

surprises.description: Single Cell consumables grew only 3% despite double-digit reaction-volume growth, a weaker revenue-to-volume conversion than the preview’s already-flagged Q1 gap and an indication that the gap remained pronounced.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Single Cell consumables grew only 3% despite double-digit reaction volume growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 consumables rose about 6% on double-digit reaction-volume growth, implying price or mix erosion. Watch whether the gap widens.”

surprises.description: APAC revenue declined 19%, while the Americas and EMEA grew; the preview did not flag this regional split, and the company linked part of the APAC decline to prior-year China buying pulled forward ahead of tariffs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APAC revenue declined 19%, partly reflecting ~$4 million of prior-year pull-forward buying in China ahead of tariffs, while Americas grew 6% and EMEA grew 15%.”

surprises.description: Cash and marketable securities ended above the preview’s expected range of $525–540 million, at $552 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $552 million in cash and marketable securities (up $105 million year-over-year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash & securities | ~$525–540M.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed estimated maximum Atera utilization of $2–3 million per instrument annually, roughly twice Xenium’s, providing a new potential revenue-per-instrument upside case. Actual pull-through remains unknown because no units have shipped.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Atera's maximum utilization is estimated at $1.5 million to $2–3 million per instrument annually, roughly 2x that of Xenium, though actual pull-through remains unquantified since no units have shipped.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on Atera’s “~40 units” shipment plan and said the market wanted “a higher unit count or a quantified backlog”; it did not provide a utilization estimate.

surprises.description: The company acquired Proteintech Genomics to expand proteomics and multiomics capabilities, an unanticipated strategic and capital-allocation development in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $552 million in cash and marketable securities ... and acquired Proteintech Genomics to strengthen proteomics and multiomics capabilities.”

in_line: The expected shipment outlook of about 40 Atera instruments remained unchanged, consistent with the preview’s cited plan for roughly 40 units shipping in Q3–Q4.

The preview anticipated customer delays in spatial instrument purchases ahead of Atera; the company attributed the Spatial instrument decline in part to customers moderating purchases ahead of the launch.
The Q4 step-up in revenue driven mainly by Atera shipments is consistent with the preview’s expectation that the roughly 40 planned shipments would be weighted toward Q4.

surprises.description: Matador’s full-year free-cash-flow outlook was about $900 million, below the preview’s latest estimate of roughly $1.0 billion, even though Q2 generated near-record adjusted free cash flow of $303 million. The call also said a significant marketing gain contributed to the quarter but was non-recurring.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Generated near-record adjusted free cash flow of $303 million in Q2 2026” and “expects to generate approximately $900 million in free cash flow for the full year”; the quarter included “a significant marketing gain” characterized as “non-recurring.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. FCF was guided at $1.1–1.2B in May and cut to about $1.0B on July 23.”

surprises.description: Matador had drawn substantial acquisition-related bank debt, with RBL borrowing at $1.25 billion before Q2 paydown, despite the preview saying the RBL had been fully repaid in May. The company had already used $200 million of quarterly cash flow to reduce the balance to under $1 billion and said it expected to largely repay it by year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Used $200 million of the quarter’s cash flow to pay down acquisition-related bank debt, reducing the RBL borrowing from $1.25 billion to under $1 billion, and expects it largely repaid by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “RBL reduced to $185M from $398M” in Q1 and “RBL was fully repaid in May 2026”; the preview also said the Paloma deal “closes in Q4 2026” and would be funded from cash and the RBL.

surprises.description: Production exceeded the high end of Q2 guidance, and Matador raised its full-year year-over-year oil-growth outlook to 4%–7% while reducing capital expenditures by 1%. The preview’s base case anticipated roughly 2% production above the Q2 midpoint and expected full-year guidance and capex to be reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Exceeded the high end of its production guidance and raised full-year year-over-year oil growth guidance to a range of 4% to 7% while simultaneously reducing capital expenditures by 1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case assumed “Production about 2% above midpoint” and “FY volumes and ~$1.0B AFCF reaffirmed”; the preview said FY26 capex was “reaffirmed at $1.45–1.55B.”

surprises.description: Matador reported 5% reserve growth during the quarter, taking reserves from 667 million to 703 million barrels of oil equivalent, a reserve-development result the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oil and natural gas reserves grew 5% during the quarter, rising from 667 million to 703 million barrels of oil equivalent.”

surprises.description: The newly acquired federal acreage was projected to earn returns above 80%, versus over 50% on Matador’s existing assets, supported by higher oil EURs and lower federal royalties. The preview discussed acquisition funding and leverage but did not flag this level of projected asset economics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Newly acquired assets are projected to deliver rates of return above 80%, compared to over 50% on existing assets,” driven by “15%–20% higher oil EURs” and “low 1/8 (12.5%) federal royalty rates.”

surprises.description: Matador said well costs on the new federal acreage could fall to about $600 per foot through batch development across at least nine benches and longer laterals; the preview had not outlined this cost target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Well costs on the new federal acreage are expected to fall to approximately $600 per foot, aided by batch development across 9 or more benches and longer laterals.”

surprises.description: The federal lease sale was said to extend inventory life to more than 15 years, with drilling potentially starting as early as late 2026 or early 2027 across acreage with nine zones. The preview anticipated watching for a follow-up Woodford program or 2027 capital allocation, but did not flag this expanded inventory or the possibility of a late-2026 start.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The BLM federal lease sale extended inventory life to over 15 years,” with drilling “potentially beginning as early as end of 2026 or early 2027” across “9 different zones.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for a follow-up program or 2027 Woodford capital allocation.”

surprises.description: Management described a plan to repay about $100 million of debt per month at current prices and said $70-per-barrel oil would be enough to remain profitable. The preview discussed a 12–18-month path to 1.0x leverage, but did not provide these monthly repayment or profitability thresholds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management targets monthly debt repayment of roughly $100 million at current prices,” aims to “pay off the acquisition debt within 12 to 15 months,” and considers “$70/barrel oil” sufficient to remain profitable.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management targets about 1.0x leverage within 12–18 months of close.”

surprises.description: A significant non-recurring marketing gain affected Q2, an unanticipated one-off that makes the quarter’s cash generation less representative of recurring results. The call also flagged expected gas-realization improvements from Hugh Brinson and Energy Transfer arrangements rather than reporting a new realized-gas result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The quarter included a significant marketing gain that management characterized as non-recurring,” while management flagged “expected natural gas realization improvements from the early startup of the Hugh Brinson pipeline and Energy Transfer deals.”

surprises.description: Matador said drilling efficiency on three-mile laterals had improved from about 20 days to about 10 days, an operating-efficiency gain not called out in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Drilling efficiency on 3-mile laterals improved from roughly 20 days to about 10 days.”

in_line: The preview already reported that the Rae’s Creek exploratory well had tested above 2,200 BOE/d; the call’s report of a result above 2,200 barrels was consistent with that prior information.

The preview framed Hugh Brinson and Energy Transfer gas-realization benefits mainly as a 2H26 opportunity; management likewise described expected improvements, without the provided call facts establishing a different realized-gas outcome.

surprises.description: After GSK terminated its RCC program, Trevi said it is essentially alone across all three of its chronic-cough indications and could be a first-in-class therapy. The preview did not anticipate this competitive change.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Following a competitor's recent RCC program termination (GSK), Trevi believes it is now essentially alone across all three of its chronic cough indications, positioning it as a potential first-in-class therapy.”

surprises.description: The runway remains “into 2030,” but Trevi clarified that it covers the IPF-related chronic-cough program through potential FDA approval—not commercial launch costs or a Phase III RCC trial. That limits what investors can infer from the runway headline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The cash runway funds the IPF-related chronic cough program through potential FDA approval, but explicitly excludes commercial launch costs and any Phase III RCC trial.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the runway was “into 2030” and flagged the need to reaffirm that runway.

surprises.description: Management said the RCC trial could be upsized by as much as 50% after the sample-size re-estimation, but characterized any increase as routine rather than a negative signal. The preview identified how an expansion would be interpreted as a key debate, so this framing is reassuring even though the possible increase is substantial.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The LAKE trial could be upsized by up to 50% following the SSRE,” with any increase framed “as a routine statistical exercise rather than a negative signal.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted “how management frames the interim, and whether an expansion would be read as negative” as a key issue.

surprises.description: Trevi disclosed that its approximately $319 million cash balance is expected to fund the IPF program through potential approval, while leaving launch costs and any Phase III RCC trial outside that runway. This makes the longer-term funding picture less complete than the “into 2030” headline alone suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: Trevi ended Q2 with “approximately $319 million” and said the runway “explicitly excludes commercial launch costs and any Phase III RCC trial.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Pro-forma cash cited at about $334M” and said runway was described as “into 2030.”

surprises.description: Management gave a more explicit commitment that OCEAN-2's expected 2H 2027 top-line results will not be held until OCEAN-1 reports in 1H 2028, and said OCEAN-1 should be largely enrolled by then. This adds reassurance about sequencing beyond the preview's stated readout windows.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management stated it will not hold OCEAN-2 top-line data (expected 2H 2027) until OCEAN-1 reads out (1H 2028), and expects OCEAN-1 to be largely enrolled by the time OCEAN-2 reports.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described OCEAN-2 as having a “topline H2 2027” and OCEAN-1 as having a “topline H1 2028.”

surprises.description: Trevi disclosed a focused RCC commercial strategy: targeting about 1 million treatment-resistant U.S. patients and pursuing specialty pricing to avoid cannibalizing IPF/ILD revenue. The preview did not provide an expectation for the RCC market size or pricing approach.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company targets a treatment-resistant RCC population of approximately 1 million U.S. patients, pursuing specialty pricing rather than the broad market to avoid cannibalizing IPF/ILD revenue.”

surprises.description: Trevi reported that its unbranded awareness campaign has reached more than 17,000 pulmonologists and that all six ATS 2026 submissions were selected for presentations or posters. These are new measures of outreach and scientific visibility not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company's unbranded awareness campaign has reached more than 17,000 unique pulmonologists so far, and all six of its ATS 2026 submissions were selected for presentations or posters.”

in_line: Trevi initiated the OCEAN-1 Phase III trial in Q2, as the preview said the first IPF-related Phase III trial was guided to start in Q2.
Trevi initiated the LAKE Phase IIb RCC trial in Q2, matching the preview's Q2 start guidance for the RCC Phase IIb trial.
The OCEAN-2 Phase III trial is planned for Q3, and its expected 2H 2027 top-line timing is consistent with the preview's stated H2 2027 timing for Phase III trial #2.
The LAKE sample-size re-estimation remains expected in Q4 2026, as flagged in the preview.
The approximately $319 million cash balance supports the previously stated runway into 2030, with no change to prior guidance.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $475.5 million, below the preview’s consensus range of $488.7–$493.9 million by about $13–18 million. This was a modest shortfall against the expected top line.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached $475.5 million.”

surprises.description: Alta reduced the top of its FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance by $5 million, from $182.5 million to $177.5 million, while leaving the bottom at $167.5 million. The preview highlighted holding guidance—and potentially narrowing toward the upper half—as a positive signal, so the renewed reduction was a negative deviation, even though management attributed it to delivery timing rather than weaker demand.
