surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 renewal rates in the largest annual renewal cohort (concentrated in UEM and EDR) fell from the high-80s to the mid-80s during the quarter, driving the net new ARR shortfall and guidance cut.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “N-central security incident… The risk is to narrative and forward guidance”; “no Q2 P&L impact.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance implies reported growth of only about 3%, a weak near-term trajectory alongside the preview’s expectation that FY26 ARR would be back-half weighted with product launches supporting growth. The preview did not provide a specific Q3 revenue estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $134.5-135.5 million implies growth decelerating to approximately 3% year-over-year on a reported basis.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management says FY26 ARR is back-half weighted, tied to DRaaS and Google Workspace backup launches.”

surprises.description: Customers with at least $50,000 of ARR grew about 7%, slowing from the 13% growth the preview cited, although their share of ARR rose from about 62% to 63%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customers contributing $50,000 or more of ARR grew ~7% to 2,706 and now represent ~63% of total ARR, up from ~60% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$50K+ ARR customers grew 13% YoY and make up 62% of ARR.”

surprises.description: N-able disclosed a plan to cut roughly 6% of its workforce, with restructuring charges in the second half. The expense savings are beneficial, but the scale of the cuts and charges were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to reduce total headcount by approximately 6% (from ~2,000 employees), cutting annualized operating expenses by $11-13 million while incurring $4-6 million in restructuring charges in the second half.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 80%, down from 82% a year earlier. The preview discussed the expected 29% adjusted EBITDA margin but gave no gross-margin expectation, so this was an unanticipated operating-pressure signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined to 80% from 82% a year earlier.”

surprises.description: Data protection ARR exceeded $200 million and again led net new ARR growth, while continuing to grow faster than the company overall. The preview focused on other product launches and did not flag this level of contribution from data protection.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data protection ARR surpassed $200 million, continues to grow faster than the total company, and again led net new ARR growth this quarter.”

surprises.description: The preview cited about $393 million of net debt, while the reported figures of approximately $398 million of debt and $116 million of cash imply net debt of about $282 million. That is a materially lower net-debt position than the preview led investors to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Holds ~$116 million cash against ~$398 million debt (1.8x net leverage).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The full preview cites about $393M net debt against FY26 uFCF guidance of $116–120M.”

surprises.description: Management said the newly launched DRaaS product could become one of N-able’s fastest-growing SKUs and reach $10 million ARR. The preview anticipated a back-half product ramp but did not provide this target or growth characterization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The newly GA-launched DRaaS product contributed no revenue in Q2 (launched July), but management expects it to become one of their fastest-growing SKUs to reach $10 million ARR.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “H2 product ramp. Management says FY26 ARR is back-half weighted, tied to DRaaS and Google Workspace backup launches.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was $40 million at a 29% margin, in line with the preview’s approximately $40 million and 29% expectations.
Dollar-based net revenue retention was 106% reported and 103% constant currency, matching the preview’s stated 106% reported and 103% constant-currency figures.
Constant-currency ARR growth of 6% landed at the bottom of the preview’s expected 6–7% range, even though total ARR was below consensus.
Unlevered free cash flow guidance remained $116–120 million, matching the preview’s FY26 guidance.
DRaaS launched in July, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the product ramp would occur in the second half.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was about $125 million, slightly above the preview’s company-implied $122–125 million range, and management said it was ahead of company expectations. The beat was modest rather than a major upside surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $125 million ... ahead of company expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 at 23.0–23.5% of FY adj. EBITDA, implying $122–125M on ≥$530M.”

surprises.description: Same-facility revenue grew 5%, but cases increased only 0.3%, so nearly all the growth came from rate rather than the pickup in volume the preview said was needed. This leaves case growth weaker than the preview’s watchpoint implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-facility net revenue increased 5% in Q2 (4.8% from rate, 0.3% from case growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Same-facility cases. Q1 was +0.6%. Growth has come mainly from acuity and price, so volume needs to pick up.”

surprises.description: Commercial payers fell to about 49% of revenue, down roughly 350 basis points year over year, with government mix rising. The preview did not flag this shift in payer mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Commercial payer mix declined to approximately 49% of net revenue in Q2, about 350 basis points lower year-over-year, with a corresponding rise in government mix.”

surprises.description: Management confirmed it will not meet the $200 million annual M&A investment target in 2026, citing portfolio optimization; acquisitions year-to-date have been immaterial. That makes the shortfall from the stated target explicit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company will not reach its $200 million annual M&A investment target in 2026 ... having completed only an immaterial amount of acquisitions year-to-date.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “M&A deployment: $4M against a stated ~$200M/yr target”; “Capital allocation. Debt paydown versus the $200M buyback authorized Feb 26, 2026, versus M&A.”

surprises.description: The Idaho Falls assets carry substantial capital and lease commitments: about $17 million of annual capex and 32% of finance lease obligations. These transaction-related burdens were not highlighted in the preview and add context to the benefits of the sale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Idaho Falls facilities carried high capital intensity, averaging approximately $17 million in annual capex over three years and representing about 32% of finance lease obligations.”

surprises.description: The sale is expected to leave Medicaid exposure below 2% of the business, a portfolio-mix outcome the preview did not identify as a transaction benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding Idaho Falls ... pro-forma Medicaid exposure falling to less than 2% of the business.”

surprises.description: The 2026 physician cohort’s initial revenue contribution is nearly 16% higher than the prior-year cohort, alongside 191 recruits in Q2. The preview did not discuss physician recruitment or cohort contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company recruited 191 new physicians in Q2 (330 year-to-date), with the 2026 cohort's initial revenue contribution up nearly 16% versus the prior year cohort.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of approximately $849 million was essentially in line with the $846.97 million consensus estimate in the preview.
The company reaffirmed FY2026 revenue guidance of $3.35–$3.45 billion and adjusted EBITDA guidance of at least $530 million, excluding Idaho Falls, as the preview expected.

The Idaho Falls sale’s approximately $795 million gross proceeds were already stated in the preview; the call also provided the anticipated pro forma leverage detail, including an expected reduction of about 0.3 turns.

surprises.description: Q1 net sales were $168 million, below the preview's $183 million consensus and its $180–190 million base scenario. Management called sales in line with expectations, but the reported figure was materially below the preview's estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 net sales were $168 million,” which management characterized as “in line with expectations but impacted by the timing of orders.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q1 FY27 Consensus | $183.0M”; the base scenario also expected “$180–190M.”

surprises.description: Reported gross margin of 16.2% was below the preview's roughly 19–21% model and its warning threshold of about 19.5%. However, the 20.2% adjusted margin was within the preview's modeled range, making the headline shortfall less severe on an adjusted basis.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 gross margin fell to 16.2% from 18% a year earlier,” while “adjusted gross margin was 20.2%” excluding noncash and one-time items.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin: Not found (model ~19–21%)”; the preview also said “Below about 19.5% puts that guide at risk.”

surprises.description: A weakening U.S. dollar versus the Mexican peso created a specific margin headwind that the preview did not flag: an unfavorable impact of about $3.5 million, or 2%, on gross margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A weakening U.S. dollar versus the Mexican peso created an unfavorable foreign exchange impact of approximately 2% or $3.5 million on gross margin.”

surprises.description: Q1 used operating cash rather than generating it, contrary to the preview's expectation of positive cash flow and a seasonal cash build.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company used $11.3 million in cash from operating activities in Q1 due to an inventory ramp-up for new business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 is seasonally a cash-build quarter,” and the catalyst checklist said “Positive operating cash flow” would support the deleveraging story.

surprises.description: Net bank debt was $99.7 million, above the preview's stated benchmark of net debt at or below $80 million. The reported 1.26 net bank debt-to-EBITDA ratio provides a favorable counterpoint, but does not change the higher-than-expected debt level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net bank debt was $99.7 million against trailing adjusted EBITDA of $79.1 million, yielding a low net bank debt-to-EBITDA ratio of 1.26.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's catalyst checklist said “net debt at or below $80M” would support the deleveraging story.

in_line: MPAA reaffirmed fiscal 2027 net sales guidance of $780–800 million, operating income of $86–91 million, and EBITDA of $95–100 million, as the preview expected the guide to be reaffirmed without change.

The company maintained its expectation of more than $100 million of additional annualized sales by the end of fiscal 2027, excluded from guidance due to timing uncertainty, and a target above $900 million in annualized sales. This matched the preview's flagged ramp outlook.
The adjusted gross margin of 20.2% was within the preview's modeled range of roughly 19–21%, despite the lower reported margin.
The Centric acquisition and its scale were already anticipated in the preview, which described the acquisition and cited historical sales of up to $400 million.

surprises.description: The preview expected the bridge refinancing to be completed or committed around the end of Q2 or early Q3. Sonida reported a five-year $380 million term loan that refinanced the $170 million bridge loan and prior debt, leaving 97% of maturities due in 2029 or later; the reported maturity extension is a stronger outcome than simply securing the bridge refinancing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A post-quarter $380 million five-year term loan with Ally Bank refinanced the $170 million bridge loan and prior debt, pushing 97% of total debt maturities to 2029 or later” at a pro forma weighted average rate of 5.43%, with 86% fixed or hedged.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided to refinancing with property-level mortgage debt ‘by end of Q2 or early Q3.’” The preview said a completed or committed refinancing would support the deleveraging path.

surprises.description: The first six transitioned communities produced far more than an unspecified margin lift: their year-over-year NOI improved by more than 60%, with margins expanding 850 basis points. That is a strong result against the preview’s watch for whether the transitions would lift margins at all.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Six communities transitioned to Sonida management in early May delivered year-over-year NOI improvement exceeding 60% and 850 bps of NOI margin expansion versus Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch the completion count and any margin lift on the first six.”

surprises.description: The announced non-core recycling plan represents less than 2% of Q2 NOI, much smaller by NOI than the preview’s expectation that roughly 10% of communities, representing under 10% of NOI, were slated for divestiture. That leaves a smaller stated NOI base for the planned recycling and deleveraging effort than the preview suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management targets a near-term leverage range of 6.0x-6.5x and plans to recycle 14 non-core communities (less than 2% of Q2 NOI) to deleverage and upgrade portfolio quality.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “About 10% of communities by count (under 10% of NOI) are slated for divestiture, primarily in Q3–Q4.”

surprises.description: Sonida disclosed an approximately $88 million acquisition under contract, with mid-teens expected unlevered returns and accretion to normalized FFO and NAV per share once stabilized. The preview focused on refinancing, transitions, and asset sales, and did not anticipate this acquisition commitment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is under contract to acquire approximately $88 million of assets expected to generate mid-teens unlevered IRR and be accretive to normalized FFO and NAV per share on a stabilized basis.”

surprises.description: Sonida had already issued shares through its ATM in July to fund near-term acquisitions, rather than merely raising equity as a possible funding source. The preview flagged equity funding as a possible bear-tone signal, but did not expect or quantify an actual ATM issuance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company issued approximately 672,000 shares via its ATM program in July at an average price of $41.05 for net proceeds of $27.3 million to fund near-term acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A bear tone means … a first-time mention of equity as a funding source.”

in_line: Same-store occupancy was 87.8%, within the preview’s 87.5%–88.0% base-case range.
The 6.0x–6.5x near-term leverage target was consistent with the preview’s expectation of a mid-6x target.

No immediate full-year guidance was issued, consistent with the preview’s note that the company had not given formal guidance. Management said it expects to begin issuing 2027 normalized FFO guidance after CHP and pipeline integrations are complete.

surprises.description: Temporary takeaway constraints reduced Q2 EBITDAX and operating cash flow by about $25 million each. The preview anticipated EBITDAX below the company’s guide, but did not identify this specific operating constraint as a cause.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Temporary takeaway constraints reduced EBITDAX and operating cash flow by approximately $25 million each.”

surprises.description: CRC’s H2 plan was leaner than the preview’s base case, which expected the rig program to be defended: California will run five rigs rather than six in H2, and improved efficiency cut 2026 D&C and workover capital by $10 million. Normalized maintenance also requires one fewer rig than previously projected, with a go-forward capital range of $450–475 million and roughly 5% lower D&C and workover capital.
surprises.fact_evidence: “California operations to run 5 rigs in H2 2026 instead of 6 while keeping production nearly flat, reducing 2026 D&C and workover capital by $10 million”; “Normalized California maintenance now requires 6 rigs (one fewer than previously projected) and ~5% lower D&C and workover capital.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “an unchanged operating plan” and said investors were watching whether management would “defend or trim the 7-rig, $520–560M program.”

surprises.description: Berry integration savings materially outpaced the original target: CRC said it had exceeded the 2026 synergy target six months early and increased its cumulative synergy and structural-cost-reduction opportunity through 2028 to as much as $470 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Berry integration synergies were delivered at over 100% of the 2026 target six months ahead of schedule,” with “~$103 million of annualized savings”; cumulative synergies and structural cost reductions were “raised to up to $470 million through 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “over 100% of the 2026 target” and “six months ahead of schedule.”

surprises.description: Pipeline marketing disputes pressured differentials and left Q3 realizations guided to about 93% of Brent, expected to be the year’s low point. CRC said it contained the impact to roughly $2 per barrel, but the preview did not flag the dispute or this near-term realization weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Temporary marketing disputes with a pipeline operator pressured differentials”; CRC “limited its impact to roughly $2/barrel”; Q3 realizations are guided to “~93% of Brent (expected to be the year's low point)” while full-year realizations remain “~94%.”

surprises.description: Drilling results and efficiency were better than the company’s own benchmarks: about 80% of year-to-date wells outperformed the type curve, with initial production more than 10% above expectations, while time-to-market fell about 25%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 80% of wells drilled year-to-date outperformed the type curve with average initial production more than 10% above expectations”; improved efficiency “cut time-to-market by ~25%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “average initial production more than 10% above expectations.”

surprises.description: CRC announced an all-cash purchase of Crimson’s roughly 2,000-mile California crude pipeline network, priced at about 4.4 times estimated 2027 EBITDA; the preview did not anticipate this acquisition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company announced an all-cash acquisition of Crimson's ~2,000-mile California crude pipeline network at approximately 4.4x estimated 2027 EBITDA, below prevailing midstream valuation multiples,” with tentative PUC approval received.

surprises.description: CRC refinanced its remaining 2029 notes with debt due in 2035, extending average debt maturity and lowering annual expense. This financing action was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The refinancing extended weighted average debt maturity “from 5.5 to 8 years” and cut annual expense by “$5.5 million.”

surprises.description: Despite operating at about 1x leverage with an undrawn revolver, CRC made no share repurchases in the quarter. That was weaker than the preview’s suggestion of at least a passive buyback, though the preview did not present repurchases as certain.
surprises.fact_evidence: CRC “operates at ~1x leverage with an undrawn revolver but executed no share repurchases this quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A passive buyback at current levels would signal limited conviction.”

surprises.description: CRC said the Uinta is a non-core asset unlikely to receive long-term capital, a portfolio-allocation stance not raised in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: CRC viewed “the Uinta as a non-core asset unlikely to receive long-term capital.”

surprises.description: CRC commenced CO2 injection and recorded first revenue at Elk Hills, its first California CCS project, capturing about 270 tonnes per day. The preview did not identify this project milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: CRC “commenced CO2 injection and achieved first revenue at California's first CCS project at Elk Hills, capturing ~270 tonnes/day (targeting ~100,000 tons/year).”

surprises.description: CRC partnered with Beacon on a proposed 275-MW Golden Valley data center hub, with the co-developer funding early-stage development. This potential development was not mentioned in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: CRC “partnered with Beacon on the proposed 275-MW Golden Valley data center hub with co-developer funding early-stage development.”

in_line: Q2 net production averaged 149,000 BOE/day, within the preview’s cited company range of 148,000–150,000 BOE/day.
Adjusted EBITDAX was $338 million, below the company’s $370–410 million guide as the preview expected was likely, and within the preview’s $335–360 million base scenario.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $23 million, below the $24.88 million consensus estimate. The preview also anticipated a roughly 30% year-over-year decline, but the reported decline was steeper than that comparison implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 total revenue was $23 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Q2 FY26 Consensus | $24.88M”; the preview characterized this as “−30%” year over year.

surprises.description: Xtant cut FY2026 revenue guidance by $2 million at both ends, to $99–103 million. The preview highlighted holding the prior $101–105 million range as a key possibility; the actual cut was modest and not as deep as the preview’s bear-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $99-103 million from the prior $101-105 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue guidance: maintained, narrowed, or cut”; the bear scenario assumed a cut “to ~$92–98M.”

surprises.description: Earnings were materially weaker than expected: EPS was a $0.07 loss versus the preview’s $0.02 loss estimate, while adjusted EBITDA was a $2.7 million loss versus an estimated $0.8–1.2 million loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 swung to a net loss of $9.4 million ($0.07 per share)”; “adjusted EBITDA turned to a $2.7 million loss.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) | −$0.02”; adjusted EBITDA estimate “−$0.8M to −$1.2M.”

surprises.description: Legacy biologics and Amnio wound care remained weak instead of showing the second-half pickup the preview said management had anticipated. Those shortfalls were identified as the main drivers of the biologics revenue miss and the guidance reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Legacy ‘workhorse’ product lines (OsteoSelect, OsteoSponge, 3Demin) and the Amnio wound-care line underperformed expectations and were the main drivers of the biologics revenue miss.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Amnio / advanced wound care and stem cell had been soft, with management guiding to a “pickup again in the second half.”

surprises.description: The Dilon-related expense was higher and differently described than the preview’s expected sales cost: Xtant recorded a $5 million exclusive distribution fee in operating expenses, while the preview cited roughly $2.5 million per quarter in added Dilon sales and marketing costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses rose to $22.5 million from $19.7 million, largely due to a $5 million exclusive distribution fee paid to Dilon recorded as an operating expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Dilon sales team adds roughly $2.5M per quarter in S&M, and Q2 is the first full quarter carrying it.”

surprises.description: Liquidity was tighter than the preview’s Q1 snapshot suggested: cash fell to $9.9 million, total debt rose to $23 million, and only $0.7 million of revolver availability remained, versus $11.8 million of availability at Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and equivalents dropped to $9.9 million as of June 30, 2026 from $17.3 million at year-end 2025, with total debt of $23 million and only $0.7 million of revolver availability remaining.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported Q1 cash of “$12.2M” and “$11.8M revolver availability,” and said another cash decline could reopen financing questions.

surprises.description: Management supplied a more concrete, favorable HEMOBLAST volume outlook than the preview’s description of an early-stage ramp: it expects gross transactional volume above $1 million per month and most sales to shift to gross recognition through Xtant’s own contracts. Q2 recognized revenue was only about $1.5 million, primarily net of Dilon’s role.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HEMOBLAST contributed only about $1.5 million in Q2 revenue recognized primarily on a net basis”; management expects volume “to exceed $1 million per month on a gross basis,” with most sales shifting to gross recognition through Xtant.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said HEMOBLAST was “a very small business starting out of the gate,” described its ramp as early-stage, and flagged the first revenue quantification as something to watch.

surprises.description: Xtant had expanded its sales coverage far beyond the small regional team described in the preview context, but management said the buildout temporarily weighed on Q2 momentum and expects it to support sequential biologics growth in the second half.
surprises.fact_evidence: The commercial footprint grew “from roughly 4 regional reps a year ago to over 25 reps plus 17 integrated Dilon salespeople,” temporarily depressing Q2 momentum but expected to accelerate biologics growth sequentially in H2 2026.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY26 guide required a “core inflection from decline to growth in H2” and flagged a second-half pickup, but did not describe this scale of sales-force expansion.

in_line: Gross margin was 57.9%, essentially at the preview’s estimated range of about 58–61% and its roughly 58% checkpoint, though still well below the prior-year margin.

surprises.description: Helios raised FY2026 sales guidance to $880–900 million and adjusted EPS guidance to $3.05–3.25. That is a stronger raise than the preview’s base case of $855–875 million in sales and $2.90–3.05 in EPS, and the EPS range also exceeds the preview’s bull-case high of $3.20.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year 2026 sales guidance to $880-$900 million” and adjusted EPS “to $3.05-$3.25.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected the FY guide to move to “$855–875M / $2.90–3.05”; its bull case listed “$880–900M / $3.05–3.20.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.88 beat the $0.80 consensus by $0.08 and exceeded the high end of company guidance by $0.05. This was a materially stronger earnings result than the preview’s base-case ceiling of $0.88 and its $0.80 consensus estimate suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.88” exceeded the high end of guidance “by $0.05.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview consensus was “$0.80”; Q2 company guidance was “$0.78–0.83.”

surprises.description: Margins came in much stronger than the preview’s downside watch implied: gross margin expanded to 34.6%, while adjusted EBITDA margin reached 21.2%. The result included only about $1 million of net IEEPA tariff refunds, versus the roughly $4 million potential refund the preview warned investors to adjust for.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin “expanded 280 basis points to 34.6%”; adjusted EBITDA margin “reached 21.2%, up 260 basis points”; roughly “$1 million of net IEEPA tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged gross margin “below about 32.5%” as a bear-case tell and said management had guided about “$4M of potential IEEPA refunds excluded from guidance.”

surprises.description: Electronics fell short of the preview’s $87.8 million consensus, reporting $86 million, and its 13.1% operating margin was below the preview’s 14.7% estimate. Management also guided to only about 5% Electronics growth in Q3 as comparisons get tougher.
surprises.fact_evidence: Electronics sales were “$86 million”; operating margin was “13.1%”; management guided Q3 Electronics growth of “only ~5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “$87.8M” Electronics consensus and “14.7% op. margin,” and said holding above $89 million would beat what the Street was modeling.

surprises.description: Despite the substantial full-year raise, Q3 guidance points to a near-term slowdown: adjusted EPS is expected to grow only 2% at the midpoint, and adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to decline 30 basis points at the midpoint. The preview highlighted the conservative implied H2 outlook but did not anticipate this specific Q3 margin and EPS profile.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 guidance implies adjusted EBITDA margin of “19.8%-20.6% (down 30 bps at midpoint)” and adjusted EPS of “$0.70-$0.77 (up only 2% at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the second-half guide looked “conservative” and identified a full-year raise as the key question, but provided no Q3 margin or EPS forecast.

surprises.description: The preview expected an H2 2026 ramp for data-center thermal couplings, but Helios said no 2026 revenue is included in guidance and modeled only a gradual ramp from 2027. At the same time, samples were out to about a dozen customers and an order was expected imminently, providing more near-term pipeline detail than the preview had.
surprises.fact_evidence: Samples were out to “about a dozen customers” and “an order [was] expected imminently,” but “no 2026 revenue is included in guidance” and only a gradual ramp is modeled from 2027.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the product as having “zero revenue to date” with “an H2 2026 ramp expected,” and said pipeline or design-win quantification would matter.

surprises.description: Net leverage improved further to 1.4x, below the target range, and management shifted capital priorities away from debt paydown toward organic growth, buybacks, and M&A. The preview noted leverage of 1.6x and considered an acquisition possible, but did not anticipate this explicit change in capital-allocation priority.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net leverage improved to “1.4x from 2.6x a year ago,” dropping below target and shifting priorities toward “organic growth, buybacks and M&A”; year-to-date shareholder returns were “$18 million,” up 40%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited leverage of “1.6x” and said an acquisition announcement was “a live possibility.”

surprises.description: July set a company record for both monthly revenue and order intake, an additional demand signal beyond the sustained double-digit order growth the preview was monitoring.
surprises.fact_evidence: “July mark[ed] the best-ever monthly revenue and order intake.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview focused on whether order intake would remain “double-digit” and noted an expanding backlog; it did not anticipate a record month.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were a small beat versus consensus: $232 million compared with $230.4 million expected, and the result landed at the high end of company guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 sales were “$232 million,” landing “at the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview consensus was “$230.4M”; company guidance was “$227–232M.”

in_line: Order intake remained double-digit year over year for the fourth consecutive quarter, consistent with the preview’s focus on continued double-digit order growth.

surprises.description: MG raised FY26 revenue guidance to $740–$755 million from $730–$750 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $92–$95 million from $91–$93 million. The preview viewed a reaffirmation as the base case, so the upward revision is better than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to $740-$755 million in revenue and $92-$95 million in adjusted EBITDA.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's base case was “guide reaffirmed”; it said “a narrowing toward the top half ($740–750M revenue, $92–93M EBITDA) would be the bullish signal.”

surprises.description: GAAP EPS was $0.23, well above the preview's estimated $0.14–$0.16 range. That is a much larger result than the preview's expectation, even allowing for its warning that GAAP and adjusted EPS can diverge.
surprises.fact_evidence: GAAP EPS was $0.23.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP diluted EPS | ~$0.14–$0.16 (my estimate).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS came in at $0.28, above the preview's $0.25 anchor. The preview cited conflicting vendor figures, but the reported result beat its chosen consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Non-GAAP EPS was $0.28.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS (ex-special items) | $0.25 (range $0.23–$0.27, 3 analysts)” and “I anchor on Barchart's $0.25.”

surprises.description: Oil & Gas revenue was still down, but the decline narrowed from Q1's 11.5% to 8.2%; after adjusting for turnarounds and exited work, the segment was up 1%. That is better than the preview's concern about persistent crude-related deferrals and its focus on whether the decline would narrow.
surprises.fact_evidence: Oil & Gas revenue “declined 8.2%” due to exited programs and deferred maintenance, “though it was up 1% after adjusting for turnarounds and exited work.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The key question is whether the decline narrows and whether the deliberate-exit share stays near two-thirds”; the preview also said the crude-price headwind “likely persisted.”

surprises.description: Strategic end markets grew 28% in aggregate, above the preview's roughly 20% level needed to offset Oil & Gas weakness. Infrastructure and Power Generation grew strongly, though Aerospace & Defense was up 13.2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Strategic end markets grew 28% in aggregate,” with Infrastructure up 76.5% and Power Generation up 26.4%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Growth markets need to stay above roughly 20% to offset Oil & Gas.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $25.8 million, above the preview's roughly $25 million estimate, and grew 7% year over year versus the preview's estimated 3.7% growth. The quarter also set a second-quarter record and expanded margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: MG delivered “record second-quarter adjusted EBITDA of $25.8 million, up 7% year-over-year,” with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 30 basis points to 13.3%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$25.0M (my estimate)” and “+3.7%.”

surprises.description: Operating income rose 53.6%, and management said nearly 60% of incremental revenue converted into operating income, calling that rate sustainable. The preview anticipated at most a modest beat and did not point to this degree of operating leverage.
surprises.fact_evidence: Operating income increased 53.6% to $12.9 million, converting nearly 60% of incremental revenue into operating income, a rate management called sustainable and slightly higher on a full-year basis.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview's base scenario expected a “Modest beat”; it did not identify this level of operating-income growth or incremental conversion.

surprises.description: Free cash flow improved by $23.9 million quarter over quarter. The preview emphasized weak recent cash flow and management's expected second-half improvement, but the reported quarterly improvement adds a favorable result before that recovery period.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow improved by $23.9 million quarter-over-quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged free cash flow as “a credibility test” and noted that management “promised second-half improvement.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed plans to nearly triple in-lab testing capacity by the end of 2027, citing visible customer demand. The preview mentioned a lab expansion but did not anticipate this scale of capacity growth or the associated demand signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company is “investing to nearly triple its in-lab testing capacity by the end of 2027,” supported by visible customer demand, with investments typically taking 9–12 months to come online.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted the Los Angeles aerospace lab expansion but said “quantified backlog was not found.”

in_line: Management continued to expect a second-half free-cash-flow recovery, consistent with the preview's note that management had promised second-half improvement.
Management maintained the 2.0x year-end leverage target flagged in the preview; leverage was 2.2x at June 30, down from 2.4x at March 31.

surprises.description: Management said occupancy growth had not accelerated as quickly as it anticipated and lowered its full-year occupancy expectation to roughly 83%. It nevertheless kept full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance unchanged, citing new cost efficiencies to offset the lower occupancy expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management acknowledged occupancy growth has not inflected as quickly as anticipated and lowered full-year consolidated occupancy expectation to roughly 83%, offsetting the lower occupancy with new cost efficiencies; it reaffirmed full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance of $502–$516 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call said occupancy growth "has not inflected as quickly as anticipated." The preview listed full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance of "$502–516M" as reaffirmed at Q1'26.

surprises.description: Same-community labor expense improved to 45.2% of revenue from 46.1% a year earlier, a stronger quantified improvement than the preview's unquantified expectation that Q2 flow-through would improve. Management also expects further sequential improvement in Q3 and Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: Same community labor expense improved to 45.2% of revenue from 46.1% a year earlier, with further sequential improvement expected in Q3 and Q4.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, "With +230bps of occupancy, incremental margin should improve in Q2," and called weak flow-through the most bearish datapoint.

surprises.description: Brookdale completed an additional, unpreviewed acquisition of the 244-unit Brookdale Galleria for about $23.4 million, under $100,000 per unit, and closed its negative-NOI skilled nursing operations to reposition the property.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company acquired the 244-unit Brookdale Galleria in Houston for approximately $23.4 million (under $100,000 per unit) and closed its negative-NOI skilled nursing operations to reposition the property.

surprises.description: The already-announced planned purchase of 17 leased communities came with a new quantified benefit: Brookdale expects it to add about $11 million to 2027 adjusted EBITDA by replacing high-cost lease financing with lower-cost mortgage debt.
surprises.fact_evidence: The planned Q4 acquisition of 17 currently-leased communities (735 units) for approximately $157 million is expected to add about $11 million to 2027 adjusted EBITDA by replacing high-cost lease financing with lower-cost mortgage debt.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted the "announced ~$157M acquisition of 17 leased communities (735 units, Q4 2026 close)" as relevant to the 2027 EBITDA bridge, but did not state an expected EBITDA contribution.

surprises.description: Brookdale reported a sharper balance-sheet improvement than the preview had specified: annualized leverage fell to 8.4x, liquidity rose to $566 million, and refinancing all remaining 2027 mortgage maturities left no debt maturities until 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: Annualized leverage improved to 8.4x from 8.8x, total liquidity rose to $566 million from $369 million, and the company refinanced all remaining 2027 mortgage maturities leaving no debt maturities until 2028.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited leverage of 8.8x and liquidity of $369M at 3/31/26, expected a sequential free-cash-flow recovery, and said commentary on the July refinancing mattered; it did not forecast these updated leverage, liquidity, or maturity figures.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA came in slightly ahead of consensus, a small positive versus the preview's derived $121–124 million range, which included the reported $122.1 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $122.1 million, up 4.3% year-over-year and slightly ahead of consensus.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview derived Q2 adjusted EBITDA of approximately "$121–124M" and noted that sourced consensus was unavailable.

in_line: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed at $502–$516 million, as the preview listed this as the existing FY2026 guide and described reaffirmation as the base case.
Consolidated RevPAR growth of 8.2% kept Brookdale on track for its full-year 8%–9% guidance, consistent with the preview's stated full-year RevPAR outlook.
Q2 occupancy of 82.4%, up 230 basis points year-over-year, matched the figure already disclosed before the release.

surprises.description: Q2 production was essentially flat with Q1 and around the preview’s roughly 45 MBoe/d base case, but it exceeded the high end of the 41–44 MBoe/d guidance range. The upside versus guidance was modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 production was essentially flat with Q1 and exceeded the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Production versus the 41–44 MBoe/d guide”; the base scenario assumed “~45 MBoe/d.”

surprises.description: First-half LOE averaged $7.56/BOE, above Q1’s $6.53/BOE level, so the Q1 cost level did not persist. However, LOE was still approximately 13% below the midpoint of full-year guidance, even with an expanded workover program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half unit LOE averaged $7.56 per BOE, approximately 13% below the midpoint of full-year guidance, despite an expanded workover program.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 LOE of $6.53/BoE was 17% below guidance. Whether that holds matters.”

surprises.description: Management expects capital spending to decline meaningfully in the second half after spending $185.9 million in the first half and front-loading roughly the mid-to-upper 60% of the annual budget. The preview emphasized spending discipline but did not anticipate this degree of front-loading or the resulting second-half decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First-half 2026 capital spending totaled $185.9 million,” with capital expected “to decline meaningfully in the second half after front-loading roughly mid-to-upper 60% of the annual budget.”

surprises.description: Management signaled caution about paying more than the required $30 million per quarter on the term loan, prioritizing cash liquidity over faster debt reduction. That is a change in emphasis from the preview’s expectation that a roughly $60 million FCF quarter would reduce debt; the company also ended Q2 with $146 million in cash.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Mandatory term loan amortization of $30 million per quarter begins at the end of Q3 2026”; management signaled caution on prepaying above that level because the loan “cannot be re-borrowed,” prioritizing “a cash cushion for 2027 and beyond.” The company “ended the quarter with $146 million in cash.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management prioritized debt paydown on the Q1 call. A roughly $60M FCF quarter would take gross debt toward $1.12–1.14B.”

surprises.description: Oil weighting came in at 64%, below the guided 67%–68% range. Management attributed the shortfall to fracing high-oil-cut wells and reactivating older, higher-gas-cut wells, and expects the mix to return near 67% for the rest of the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oil weighting fell to 64% in Q2 from the guided 67%-68% range” and management “expects to return near 67% for the remainder of the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guided 67%-68% range.”

surprises.description: Waha differentials improved to near negative $1/MCF after pipeline expansions, compared with HighPeak’s negative $1.50 realized in Q2; management said this points to better gas realizations through the first half of 2027. The preview did not flag this improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Waha gas differentials improved from roughly negative $3-$5/MCF to near negative $1/MCF following pipeline expansions,” versus HighPeak’s “negative $1.50 realized in Q2,” pointing to better gas realizations “through the first half of 2027.”

in_line: Net cash hedge losses were approximately $55 million, at the upper end of the preview’s expected $45–55 million range; the preview also anticipated oil hedges with ceilings in the mid-$60s.
Production remained around 45 MBoe/d rather than accelerating, consistent with the preview’s base case of roughly 45 MBoe/d and management’s stated disciplined production profile.

surprises.description: PicPay's Q2 adjusted net income was BRL 283 million, 15.5% above the preview's BRL 245 million guidance anchor and even above its BRL 275 million bull-case threshold. The company said the result was partly boosted by Brazil's Lei do Bem R&D tax incentive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 adjusted net income reached BRL 283 million,” coming in “15.5% above the high end of guidance,” though “partly boosted by Brazil's Lei do Bem R&D tax incentive.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “IFRS NI / Adj. NI” guidance of “~R$235M / ~R$245M”; the bull scenario projected “R$275M+.”

surprises.description: The Q3 adjusted net income outlook of approximately BRL 265 million is below the preview's expected BRL 270–280 million range. Management expects a roughly 6% sequential decline as the Q2 concentration of Lei do Bem benefits gives way to a normalized tax rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 guidance projects adjusted net income declining ~6% sequentially to approximately BRL 265 million” because “the effective tax rate [is] normalizing after Lei do Bem benefits were heavily concentrated in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q3 adj. NI guide of R$270–280M” in its base scenario and identified “implied adjusted NI of R$270M or more” as keeping the earnings trajectory intact.

surprises.description: NPL over 90 days reached 9.8%, above the preview's 9.3% level for a bear signal. Management expects it to move toward the low teens by year-end, attributing the rise to portfolio aging and intentional risk-taking rather than deterioration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “NPL over 90 days rose to 9.8%” and management guided it “toward low teens by year-end,” attributing the rise to “portfolio aging and intentional risk-taking rather than credit deterioration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “A rise toward 9.3% or higher would be a bear signal” and listed “NPL 90+ at 9.3% or higher” in its bear scenario.

surprises.description: Management now expects Q3 cost of risk to rise to 3.9%–4.1%, above Q2's range, as the private payroll loan portfolio seasons. The preview described cost of risk as flat for two quarters, so the guided increase is an adverse change in the credit-cost trajectory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cost of risk … is expected to increase further to a 3.9%-4.1% range in Q3, driven by seasoning of the private payroll loan portfolio.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described cost of risk as “Flat for two quarters despite 116% YoY book growth” and gave a Q2 range of “3.7%–3.9%.”

surprises.description: The Desenrola renegotiation program had a sizeable Q2 benefit: BRL 59 million, about 5% of total cost of credit, and a 117-basis-point reduction in NPL over 90 days. Management expects the benefit to be more limited in Q3, making this a temporary support to Q2 credit results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Desenrola renegotiation program provided a BRL 59 million positive impact (~5% of total cost of credit) and reduced NPL over 90 days by 117 basis points,” with “benefits expected to be more limited in Q3.”

surprises.description: PicPay's credit portfolio reached BRL 31.9 billion, 3% above the roughly BRL 31.0 billion guidance, a modest upside to the preview's target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total credit portfolio grew 99% year-over-year to BRL 31.9 billion (3% above guidance).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed company guidance of “~R$31.0B (+11% QoQ)” for the credit portfolio.

surprises.description: A larger share of revenue now comes from lower- or no-credit-risk streams: 71%, versus 63% a year earlier. Secured credit revenue also rose 158% to BRL 1 billion, an improvement in revenue mix not quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “71% of revenues now come from lower or no-credit-risk streams … up from 63% a year earlier, with secured credit revenues up 158% year-over-year to BRL 1 billion.”

surprises.description: Adjusted ROE rose to 20.2% from 15.5% in Q1, while the adjusted efficiency ratio improved to 44.8% from 46.9%. Management also targeted low 40s/high 30s efficiency by year-end; the preview supplied prior-quarter figures but no expectation for this degree of further improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted ROE improved to 20.2% from 15.5% in the prior quarter,” and “the adjusted efficiency ratio improved 210 basis points sequentially to 44.8%, with management targeting low 40s/high 30s by year-end.”

surprises.description: AI productivity gains kept headcount flat since October 2025, eliminating a previously planned 10% workforce increase for 2026, while token costs fell 70% since the start of the year. The preview did not anticipate this staffing or cost-efficiency development.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI productivity gains kept headcount flat since October 2025, eliminating a previously planned 10% workforce increase for 2026 and cutting token costs by 70% since the start of the year.”

surprises.description: The Cover (rebranded CAF) insurance acquisition closed in August and is expected to add BRL 80–100 million of net income from August through December 2026, but will use about 150 basis points of capital in Q3. This newly disclosed earnings contribution and capital use were not in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Cover (rebranded CAF) insurance acquisition closed August 3,” is expected to “contribute BRL 80-100 million in net income from August to December 2026,” and “will consume approximately 150 basis points of capital in Q3.”

in_line: Q2 cost of risk was 3.9%, within the preview's 3.7%–3.9% guidance range.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $5.6 million was about 7% below the published ~$6.0 million consensus, although it exceeded the preview’s $5.40–$5.55 million base case. Revenue was also essentially flat year over year, with core press release revenue up only 2%, rather than showing a clear return to growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue was $5.6 million” and “essentially flat versus Q2 2025, with core press release revenue growing just 2% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue | ~$6.00M”; the preview also says “a print around $5.4M is operationally fine” and gives a base case of “$5.40–5.55M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin fell to 73%, below the preview’s 74–76% base range and down again from Q1’s 74%, rather than beginning to recover. Management attributed the pressure to higher distribution costs from new partners, price increases, and variable contract usage.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 gross margin compressed to 73% of revenue from 76% a year earlier,” due to “higher press release distribution costs from new partners, price increases, and variable contract usage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says “a second sequential decline from 74% would undercut management’s recovery message” and models base-case gross margin of “74–76%.”

surprises.description: GAAP loss per share was $0.09, materially worse than the preview’s derived estimate of a $0.03 loss. The net loss also widened year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP net loss widened to $354,000 ($0.09 per share) from $239,000 ($0.06).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 EPS (GAAP) | ~$(0.03) | Derived: FY26 GAAP EPS $(0.06) less Q1 actual $(0.16).”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA of $0.6 million was below the preview’s $0.65–$0.75 million base-case range, with an 11% margin rather than the modeled 13%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA declined to $0.6 million (11% of revenue) in Q2 2026 from $0.8 million (15%) in Q2 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “$0.65–0.75M (13%).”

surprises.description: The call facts provide average ARR per subscription customer, but no ARR-as-a-share-of-revenue figure, leaving the preview’s key mix-progress question unanswered. The disclosed per-customer ARR remained up year over year but edged down sequentially as lower-priced tiers were introduced.
surprises.fact_evidence: The call reports average ARR per subscription customer of “$12,718,” up 15% year over year but down roughly $100 sequentially; it does not provide ARR as a percentage of revenue.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview calls ARR mix “the key re-rating metric,” says management “needs to give a number,” and identifies progress toward “about 65%” as important.

surprises.description: The preview expected Q2 revenue disclosure from Social Monitoring, ACCESS Verified, and MCP, but the call facts provide no Q2 contribution for those products. Instead, management discussed a content studio as a planned add-on, so near-term monetization of the previously highlighted products remained unquantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is “planning new product add-ons—including a content studio priced at an incremental $200-$300/month”; no Q2 revenue contribution from Social Monitoring, ACCESS Verified, or MCP is reported in the call facts.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says those products were “guided to begin contributing in Q2” and that “first revenue disclosure is the swing factor.”

surprises.description: Customer growth and expansion metrics were notably strong beyond the preview’s stated focus on subscription growth and retention: total customers rose 24% year over year and net revenue retention reached 124%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total customer count rose 24% year-over-year and 6% sequentially” and “net revenue retention reached 124%.”

surprises.description: Management gave a concrete second-half cost-saving plan to address the margin decline, estimating about $150,000 of cost-of-revenue savings and aiming to restore gross margin to the high-70% range. The preview anticipated margin recovery but described it as dependent on volume and subscription growth, not this specific cost action.
surprises.fact_evidence: Cost savings are “expected to reduce cost of revenue by approximately $150,000 (125-150 basis points) in the second half,” with the aim of restoring gross margins “to the high-70% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview says management’s targets include “a gross margin recovery as volume and subscription revenue grow.”

surprises.description: Management put a specific industry recovery outlook on the horizon, expecting double-digit PR-industry growth in 2027 and citing a 14% rise in new business incorporations. This was a new longer-term growth claim, rather than evidence of a Q2 rebound.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expects the PR industry to return to double-digit growth in 2027,” citing “a Gartner report and a 14% rise in new business incorporations.”

in_line: Retention improved to 94%, within the preview’s expected Q2 range of 93–94%, though still below the >95% year-end target.
Average ARR per subscription customer increased 15% year over year, essentially matching the Q1 growth rate of 14.9% noted in the preview.
Revenue increased sequentially, consistent with the preview’s base case of a sequential uptick, even though it missed the published consensus.

surprises.description: Prior-authorization approvals were 31% year to date, below the preview’s 35–40% base-case expectation and slightly below Q1’s 32%. That leaves approvals closer to the preview’s flat, near-32% bear-case scenario than its expected improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Internal prior authorization approval rate jumped to 31% year-to-date in 2026 versus 12% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: ... Prior-auth 35–40%”; the preview also said “flat near 32% would suggest policy wins are not turning into claims.”

surprises.description: EPS was a loss of $0.19 per share: 3 cents worse than the $0.16-loss consensus, but substantially less negative than the preview’s estimated GAAP loss of $0.45–$0.50 after the flagged stock-compensation charge. The reported loss therefore gives a mixed comparison against the preview’s two different EPS benchmarks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net loss widened to $2.1 million from $1.7 million a year earlier, though EPS improved to a loss of $0.19 from $0.22.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (Q2) | -$0.16”; the preview also estimated “GAAP EPS near -$0.45 to -$0.50” and said a “$4M+ non-cash stock-compensation charge” was pre-flagged for Q2.

surprises.description: Quarterly burn was about $1.1 million, slightly above the preview’s expectation of about $1 million or less. More importantly, management now expects burn to rise in the second half because of accelerated hiring, contrary to the preview’s expectation of roughly $1 million or less per quarter for the rest of 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Quarterly burn improving to about $1.1 million from $1.5 million in 2025, though management expects burn to rise in the second half due to accelerated hiring.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the CFO “guided to about $1M per quarter of burn or less for the rest of 2026” and listed “burn of about $1M per quarter” as a metric to watch.

surprises.description: IB-Stim’s Q2 average selling price was $992, below the preview’s base-case expectation of about $1,050. The preview’s bull case had called for ASP above $1,100, so the reported price was also well short of that upside scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “IB-Stim average selling price rose 28% to $992 per device in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: ... ASP near $1,050”; the bull scenario specified “ASP above $1,100.”

surprises.description: Management reported meaningful direct-conversation progress with two of its largest remaining uncovered commercial payers, with coverage possible in the second half of 2026 or early 2027. The preview identified payer-policy conversion as the central issue but did not anticipate this specific progress or timing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Meaningful direct-conversation progress with two of its largest remaining uncovered commercial payers, with coverage possibly landing in the second half of 2026 or early 2027.”

surprises.description: Management set a target of exceeding 200 million covered lives by the end of 2027, compared with more than 100 million currently. The preview discussed payer coverage as a key driver but did not provide or anticipate this specific longer-term coverage target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Targets exceeding 200 million covered lives by the end of 2027 versus the current 100 million-plus.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $1.928 million was close to the preview’s roughly $2.0 million model and within its $1.9–$2.1 million base range; it represented about 20% sequential growth, near the expected 20–30%.
Cash on hand of $8.3 million was close to the preview’s expectation of exit cash near $8 million.
The company discussed the VA/Federal Supply Schedule ramp flagged in the preview: it plans to have 10 commission-only representatives trained and selling by September 15.

surprises.description: Revenue was $10.4 million, well above the preview’s $9.2 million house estimate and even above its $10.2 million bull case. The reported 8% year-over-year growth also reversed the preview’s expectation of a 5% decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue rose 8% year-over-year to $10.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “House estimate (this note, Aug 25, 2026): Revenue $9.2M (-5% YoY)”; the bull scenario was “Revenue $10.2M (+6%).”

surprises.description: The company returned to profitability rather than posting the small loss the preview expected: EPS was $0.02 versus the house estimate of $(0.02). Earnings nevertheless remained below the year-ago $0.05 per share, with operating income, net income, and EBITDA all down year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “returning the company to profitability”; “net income declined to $351,000 ($0.02 per share) from $1.2 million ($0.05 per share)”; “Operating income fell to $343,000 from $1 million”; “EBITDA dropped to $551,000 from $1.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “House estimate (this note, Aug 25, 2026): … EPS $(0.02)”; the preview also gave the year-ago EPS as “$0.05.”

surprises.description: Gross margin came in at 64.2%, materially above the preview’s roughly 61% base case and above its 60% watch level. It recovered from Q1, although it remained below the 66.1% year-ago margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin was 64.2%, down from 66.1% a year earlier but up from 60% in the first quarter, reflecting product mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case assumed “GM ~61%”; the preview said “Holding at or above 60% would suggest a mix issue.”

surprises.description: Cash was only $8 million, below the preview’s expected $9.5–10.0 million base-case range and below its $9 million level for raising financing-risk questions. The preview already anticipated the Blickfeld acquisition as the main cash drain, but the ending balance was lower than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and short-term deposits fell to $8 million ($0.34 per share) as of June 30, 2026 from $22.5 million ($0.96 per share) at year-end 2025, mainly due to the 10.4 million euro cash-funded Blickfield acquisition, with the company carrying no debt.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected “cash $9.5–10.0M”; the preview said “A print below about $9.0M would likely raise financing-risk questions.”

surprises.description: APAC emerged as a major growth driver, with revenue up 93% year over year and its share of sales rising to 19% from 11% in Q1. The preview did not identify APAC as a key growth driver or set an expectation for it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “APAC was the fastest-growing region with revenue up 93% year-over-year, lifting its share of revenue to 19% from 11% in the prior quarter.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses reached $6.4 million and included $1.2 million of Blickfield acquisition costs, an expense item not anticipated in the preview. The preview discussed Blickfield’s expected operating contribution, but not these acquisition costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses rose 18% to $6.4 million, including $1.2 million of Blickfield acquisition costs, and reached 60.9% of revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed Blickfeld’s “EBITDA breakeven on more than €6M of 2026 revenue” and modeled roughly “$1.4M” of quarterly opex, but did not anticipate $1.2 million of acquisition costs.

in_line: EMEA continued to grow: the preview expected a second strong quarter after Q1’s 43% year-over-year growth, and the call reported Q2 growth of 14% and year-to-date growth of 26%.

North American weakness was anticipated: the preview said a soft Americas number was expected in H1 and highlighted delayed U.S. projects; the call reported North America revenue down 12% and attributed the U.S. decline to correction-project delays tied to the late-2025 federal shutdown.

The H2 product-launch timing was reaffirmed. The preview expected two launches in H2 2026, and the call said the embedded FiberSense system and Symphony Workflow Engine are expected to launch in the second half and be showcased at GSX in September.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue and non-GAAP EPS were modestly above the preview’s consensus estimates: revenue was $2.739 billion versus $2.71 billion, and EPS was $0.94 versus $0.93. Both also exceeded their guidance midpoints.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY2027 revenue of $2.739 billion” and “non-GAAP EPS of $0.94,” with “both exceeding guidance midpoints.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … Consensus $2.71B”; “Non-GAAP EPS … Consensus $0.93.”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue guidance of $3.15 billion was above the preview’s $3.03 billion consensus and its stated $3.10 billion bar for clearing expectations, implying a stronger ramp than the preview’s roughly 10%–12% sequential-growth case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 FY2027 revenue is guided to $3.15 billion (up 15% sequentially and over 50% YoY).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 FY27 revenue … Consensus $3.03B”; “A figure of $3.10B or higher would suggest Google or AWS ramp pull-forward.”

surprises.description: Marvell raised its FY2028 revenue target by $1.5 billion, from $16.5 billion to about $18 billion. The largest driver was scale-up optics and switching, with scale-up optics accelerating well beyond the prior roughly $300 million category estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FY2028 revenue outlook was raised by $1.5 billion to approximately $18 billion”; “The largest driver of the $1.5 billion FY2028 raise is scale-up optics and switching, with scale-up optics accelerating well beyond last quarter's ~$300 million category estimate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The FY28 target of $16.5B is the cleanest bull confirmation if raised.”

surprises.description: The FY2027 revenue outlook rose by $500 million, from about $11.5 billion to approximately $12 billion. The preview identified target revisions as an issue to watch but did not indicate that this increase was expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its FY2027 revenue outlook to approximately $12 billion (~45% YoY growth), up $500 million from the prior ~$11.5 billion outlook one quarter ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 and FY28 target revisions” were listed as an issue to watch; the prior FY27 target was “$11.5B.”

surprises.description: Data Center growth expectations accelerated: Marvell now expects about 60% growth in FY2027, up from about 50%, and more than 60% in FY2028; the custom business is expected to more than double in FY2028. The preview supplied no comparable segment-growth forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data Center, contributing 79% of total revenue, grew 46% YoY in Q2 and is now expected to grow ~60% in FY2027 (up from ~50%) and more than 60% in FY2028, with the custom business expected to more than double in FY2028.”

surprises.description: The Google/TPU-related agreement was expanded and described as having $120 billion of cumulative revenue potential over six years—far more scale than the preview quantified. However, the call said the FY2028 impact is already in guidance and the major upside is in FY2029 and beyond, rather than describing a large near-term addition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An expanded commercial warrant agreement with a key hyperscaler (Google/TPU ecosystem) was signed, referenced at $120 billion cumulative revenue potential over 6 years, though FY2028 impact is already in guidance with major upside in FY2029 and beyond.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the Google custom-silicon agreement had been signed and that “the first revenue tranche is scheduled for Q3 FY27,” with investors to “watch the first quantification of timing and size.”

surprises.description: Q3 non-GAAP gross-margin guidance of 57.5%–58.5% was below the preview’s flagged 58.5% threshold, with management expecting similar levels through FY2028. This points to more persistent custom-business mix pressure than a one-quarter dip.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 non-GAAP gross margin is guided to 57.5%-58.5% (down ~90 bps from Q2's 58.9%), pressured by the accelerating custom business mix, with similar levels expected through FY2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Q3 non-GAAP gross margin guide below about 58.5% alongside a strong revenue guide would be a negative signal.”

surprises.description: The preview focused on gross-margin dilution but gave no operating-margin outlook. Marvell reported 36.6% non-GAAP operating margin in Q2 and expects to enter its 38%–40% long-term target range in Q4 FY2027, reach the high end in FY2028, and grow FY2028 operating expenses at roughly half the rate of revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin expanded 180 bps YoY to 36.6% in Q2,” with the company expecting to “enter the 38%-40% long-term target range in Q4 FY2027 and reach the high end during FY2028”; “FY2028 operating expenses [are expected] to grow at roughly half the rate of revenue.”

surprises.description: Workday's subscription revenue and total revenue came in modestly above the preview's consensus ranges: subscription revenue was $2.471 billion versus about $2.455 billion expected, and total revenue was $2.649 billion versus $2.63–2.64 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY27 subscription revenue was $2.471 billion” and “total revenue was $2.649 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Subscription revenue: ~$2.455B”; “Total revenue: $2.63–2.64B.”

surprises.description: AI commercial momentum was stronger than the preview's roughly $500 million ARR baseline: AI ARR was nearly $600 million, and AI products generated more than $100 million of new ACV, accounting for over a quarter of new ACV closed. The preview also cited more than 4,000 customers using agents in Q1; the reported count rose to more than 5,500.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI ARR nearly $600 million, up more than 200% year-over-year”; AI products “drove more than $100 million of new ACV, accounting for over 25% of all new ACV”; “More than 5,500 customers are now using one or more organic agents.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “In Q1, agentic ARR was approaching $500M, new agentic ACV grew 200% Y/Y, and over 4,000 customers used at least one agent.”

surprises.description: The Q2 operating margin beat the preview's 30.0% guidance, and Workday raised its FY27 margin outlook above the preview's prior 30.5% guidance. Management also previewed at least 200 basis points of further expansion in FY28, which the preview had not anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin was 31.1% in Q2”; “full-year FY27 margin guidance was raised to 31%”; management previewed “at least 200 basis points of additional margin expansion in FY28.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op margin | 30.0% | ~30%”; FY2027 guidance was “30.5%.”

surprises.description: Workday reported a sharp-looking slowdown in total subscription revenue backlog growth: it grew 8%, compared with 10.9% in the prior quarter, and management attributed pressure to a mix shift toward customer-base bookings versus net new. The preview gave the prior-quarter backlog figure but did not forecast this deceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total subscription revenue backlog grew only 8% to $27.4 billion, pressured by a mix shift toward customer-base bookings versus net new.”

surprises.description: The forward Q3 outlook included CRPO growth of 11–12%, below Q2's reported 14.2%, with management citing the Paradox acquisition comparison. The preview focused on Q2 CRPO and did not set an expectation for Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 CRPO growth of 11-12% impacted by lapping the Paradox acquisition”; 12-month CRPO was “up 14.2%” in Q2.

surprises.description: AI use was growing faster than monetization: although more than 5,500 customers were using organic agents, only about 200 had signed up for Flex credit consumption, delaying revenue monetization into FY28 and beyond. The preview highlighted AI adoption and ARR but did not flag this conversion delay.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Only about 200 have signed up for Flex credit consumption, signaling delayed revenue monetization into FY28 and beyond.”

surprises.description: Workday completed its existing $5 billion repurchase program six months early and approved a new $4 billion open-ended repurchase authorization, an allocation update not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed its $5 billion buyback program six months ahead of target, repurchasing $1.3 billion in Q2, and the Board approved a new $4 billion open-ended repurchase program.”

surprises.description: Q2 GAAP results included a large nonrecurring tax benefit from an internal IP transfer, which the preview did not anticipate. It boosts reported GAAP results but is explicitly one-off rather than recurring performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 GAAP results included a $374 million nonrecurring tax benefit from an internal IP transfer.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow was $460 million and declined year over year because of an extra payroll run. The preview highlighted FCF as a key watch item and cited FY27 FCF guidance of $3.18 billion, but the call facts do not provide an updated FY27 FCF figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow of $460 million declined year-over-year due to an extra payroll run.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 FCF is $3.18B (+15%)”; the preview flagged “Margin and FCF” as key metrics to watch.

in_line: Q2 12-month CRPO growth was 14.2%, within the preview's 13.5–14.5% guidance range and near the roughly 14% consensus.
FY27 subscription revenue guidance of $9.94–9.95 billion was effectively reaffirmed, matching the preview's $9.925–9.950 billion range.
FY27 operating cash flow guidance of $3.45 billion was maintained, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Affirm reported its most profitable quarter ever even excluding the tax allowance release. The preview cited adjusted EPS expectations but did not anticipate this qualitative evidence of record core profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Affirm reported its most profitable quarter ever in fiscal Q4 2026, even excluding the tax allowance release.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Use $0.34 as a reference adjusted print”; Q4 adjusted EPS consensus was “$0.33–0.35.”

surprises.description: Affirm guided FY27 revenue less transaction costs to approximately 4.16%: above its 3.5%–4% midterm range, but just below the preview’s 4.2% watch level. That is a mixed result against the preview’s benchmark rather than a clear reset of the long-term range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 revenue less transaction costs is guided to approximately 4.16%, above the 3.5%-4% midterm range, supported by favorable debt capital markets funding costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “RLTC of at least 4.2% and any reset of the 3–4% range. A raised long-term range is the cleanest bull catalyst.”

surprises.description: Affirm Card attach reached 19% of active users, up from the preview’s cited 17% prior-quarter level and above its watchpoint of getting beyond 17%. Cardholders also spend roughly twice as much as typical customers, a favorable usage detail the preview did not specify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Affirm Card attach rate stands at 19% of active users, with cardholders spending roughly 2x more than typical customers, and management expects the attach rate to rise.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Affirm Card attach beyond 17%”; the preview also cited a prior-quarter “17% attach.”

surprises.description: Pay-in-4 volume grew 41% year over year, with management describing it as becoming an evergreen part of a large merchant’s financing program. The preview did not set an expectation for Pay-in-4 growth or this merchant use case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pay-in-4 volume grew 41% year-over-year, driven partly by a large low-average-order-value merchant making it an evergreen part of its financing program.”

surprises.description: Management said Affirm is available at only 80% of the top 250 merchants and about 10% of e-commerce merchants, leaving a larger stated merchant expansion opportunity than the preview’s general reference to new merchant wins conveyed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Affirm is available at only 80% of the top 250 merchants and roughly 10% of e-commerce merchants, indicating substantial greenfield growth opportunity remaining.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “new merchant wins” as a narrative item to watch.

surprises.description: Services volume nearly doubled year over year after Affirm signed a couple of very large platforms, which management said are still in the early innings. The preview did not identify this vertical or these platform wins as an expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Services vertical volume nearly doubled year-over-year, driven by signing a couple of very large services platforms that management says are still in early innings.”

surprises.description: As Affirm Card scales, management said overall product mix is shifting back toward interest-bearing loans; direct-to-consumer products are already more than 80% interest-bearing. The preview did not flag this mix shift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Affirm's direct-to-consumer products run north of 80% interest-bearing loans, and the scaling of the Affirm Card is shifting overall product mix back toward interest-bearing.”

surprises.description: About 30% of Affirm Card transactions are already offline, while management characterized in-store use as a major untapped market and said it is targeting it with new products. The preview mentioned card attach but did not flag this offline opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “About 30% of Affirm Card transactions are offline/in-store, still a small portion of overall GMV, representing a major untapped market Affirm is targeting with new products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Affirm Card attach beyond 17%” as a narrative item to watch.

surprises.description: Management gave a mid-to-high-20% run-rate GAAP tax-rate outlook but declined to provide exact EPS guidance because it expects effective tax-rate volatility. That leaves earnings guidance less precise than the preview’s EPS estimates might suggest, though the preview did not say to expect company EPS guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided the run-rate GAAP tax rate to the mid-to-high 20% range but declined to give exact EPS guidance due to expected effective tax rate volatility.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave Q4 adjusted EPS consensus of “$0.33–0.35” and FY27 adjusted EPS consensus of “$1.73,” but did not state that Affirm would provide EPS guidance.

surprises.description: In response to credit concerns, management emphasized that it makes about 100 million credit decisions per quarter and would slow growth before allowing a credit disturbance. The preview highlighted delinquencies as a key risk but supplied no reported delinquency result in the call facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Affirm makes credit decisions roughly 100 million times per quarter and manages to a credit-loss target as an input, stating it would slow growth before experiencing a credit disturbance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “30+ day delinquencies versus ~2.8%” and said “Any print at or above 3.0% would change the bear case.”

surprises.description: Q4 sales grew 8%, implying roughly $1.056 billion from the prior-year base, modestly above the preview’s $1.04–$1.05 billion consensus range. Facet contributed about 3 percentage points of growth.
