surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 2026 sales surpassed $1 billion for the first time in company history, growing 8% year-over-year, with the Facet acquisition contributing approximately 3 percentage points of that growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Consensus | $1.04–1.05B” and “Implied YoY | +6.4% to +7.2%.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EPS of $1.15 came in above the $1.12–$1.13 consensus, at the top of the preview’s $1.08–$1.15 all-in implied range. The beat was modest rather than a large upside surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EPS reached $1.15.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS | $1.12 (Zacks) or $1.13 (broad Street)” and the “all-in implied Q4 range is $1.08–$1.15.”

surprises.description: Facet diluted Q4 EPS by $0.06, twice the roughly $0.03 dilution the preview said management had guided. The company also expects a $0.12 full-year FY2027 EPS drag from Facet, including amortization and interest costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Facet diluted Q4 EPS by $0.06 and is expected to dilute full-year fiscal 2027 EPS by approximately $0.12 due to $22 million of incremental amortization and higher interest expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided about $0.03 of Q4 Facet dilution”; the preview also said to look for “FY27 accretion cents.”

surprises.description: Life Sciences grew 10%, far above the preview’s Q4 consensus-implied growth of about 2.4%. The call tied the strength to double-digit disk-drive demand associated with the HAMR technology shift.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Life Sciences grew 10% on double-digit disk drive demand tied to the HAMR technology shift.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Life Sciences | $84M | ~$82M | +2.4%,” and the preview said that consensus “looks low against a 9–11% full-year segment guide and Q3's +13%.”

surprises.description: Industrial Solutions pretax margin fell 450 basis points to 16.4%, with Facet expenses and power-generation headwinds weighing on the segment. The preview discussed Industrial sales and potential A&D upside, but did not flag this degree of margin pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Industrial Solutions Q4 pretax margin fell 450 basis points to 16.4% due to Facet expenses and power generation headwinds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Industrial Solutions ex-Facet. Consensus of $336M includes $25–30M from Facet, which leaves about $307M, roughly flat to -1%. Aerospace & Defense is the swing factor and the cleanest upside lever.”

surprises.description: Donaldson restarted share repurchases after pausing them for the Facet acquisition, with planned buybacks of about 1% of shares to offset dilution. The preview described buybacks as paused for deleveraging, making the restart a positive development versus that baseline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company restarted share repurchases after pausing for the Facet acquisition, expecting to buy back about 1% of shares to offset dilution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buybacks are paused to delever after the $820M Facet deal (leverage 1.8–2.0x). Commentary on restarting them matters for the FY2027 EPS bridge.”

surprises.description: China mobile sales rose 27%, including nearly 40% growth in OE replacement-part sales, a strong regional and channel demand detail not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China mobile sales surged 27%, driven by a nearly 40% increase in OE replacement part sales.”

in_line: Q4 consolidated operating margin was 17.5%, matching the preview’s expectation of roughly 17–18% and its base-case estimate of about 17.5%.
FY2027 EPS guidance of roughly $4.30 landed at the low end of the preview’s modeled $4.30–$4.40 bar, rather than below it.
Management still expects the Mexico production issue to recover by mid-FY2027, consistent with the preview’s expectation that margin normalization would arrive around midyear.
FY2026 EPS of $3.98 was within the preview’s cited FY2026 guidance range of $3.94–$4.01.

surprises.description: The preview expected FY26 revenue to be roughly flat to down versus FY25, but the call reported nearly $121 million of revenue, up 8% on a comparable basis excluding Gridspertise. The growth was driven by 15%+ growth in embedded IoT solutions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full fiscal 2026 revenue reached nearly $121 million, up 8% from just over $111 million in fiscal 2025 (excluding Gridspertise), driven by 15%+ growth in embedded IoT solutions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue is set to be roughly flat to down versus FY25”; the preview also estimated “FY26 total revenue | ~$120.5M | ... $122.9M (−2%).”

surprises.description: IoT System Solutions rose 16% sequentially to more than $15 million as federal shutdown headwinds eased, instead of showing another decline from Q3’s $13.2 million. The preview identified a second straight decline as a concern and a return to growth as part of its bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “IoT systems solutions revenue rebounded 16% sequentially to over $15 million as federal government shutdown headwinds eased, with recovery in out-of-band management, network switches, and federal business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “IoT System Solutions direction from $13.2M. Management framed the Q3 decline as timing, not demand. A second straight decline would make it look structural.” The bull scenario also listed “IoT System Solutions returns to growth.”

surprises.description: The company reported raising more than $44 million in net proceeds during the quarter and ended the year debt-free with over $60 million in cash before the Nero acquisition closed. That is substantially more liquidity than the preview’s estimate of roughly $25–30 million in pro forma net cash, though the larger fundraising also implies more capital raised than the preview’s cited May offering.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised over $44 million in net proceeds during the quarter, repaid the remaining $8.7 million of debt to end fiscal year debt-free, and finished with over $60 million in cash (before the Nero acquisition close).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited a May offering of “about $30M gross” and estimated “Pro-forma net cash ... about $25–30M after subtracting about $11.5M for Vecima.”

surprises.description: The FY27 unmanned-systems outlook was a little higher than the preview’s roughly $24 million implied estimate: management said the business should be 15%–20% of total revenue, or roughly $25 million-plus. The preview’s central math was about $24 million, though it had already highlighted the 15%–20% mix target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects it to represent 15%-20% of total revenue (roughly $25 million-plus) in fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Doubling the ~$12M FY26 figure gives about $24M”; the preview also noted management’s prior guidance for “15–20% of total revenue in FY27.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a sharp increase in unmanned-systems activity: active engagements grew from roughly 10 to over 30, with shipments to more than a dozen customers, including in counter-UAS. The preview focused on the FY27 revenue target but did not anticipate this pipeline and customer-traction detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Active unmanned systems engagements tripled from roughly 10 in Q1 to over 30 today, with products shipped to over a dozen customers including in the counter-UAS area.”

surprises.description: Q4 non-GAAP gross margin was 44.1%, above the preview’s estimate of about 43.5%. Management guided to margins at or near the current level in FY27; the preview mentioned 45% or higher as a possible upside target, not as its base expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 non-GAAP gross margin improved to 44.1%”; management is “guiding to margins at or near current levels in fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Gross margin (non-GAAP) | ~43.5%.”

surprises.description: The Nero acquisition was expected to add high-margin revenue, but the call additionally said it was immediately accretive to earnings. That earnings benefit was not specified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Vecima Industrial IoT business was acquired for “$11.7 million,” adding “approximately $5 million in annual revenue at mid-to-high 60s gross margins, immediately accretive to earnings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described Vecima as adding “high-60s%-margin SaaS” and estimated “about $1.3M per quarter from Vecima,” but did not state that the deal would be immediately accretive.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue and non-GAAP EPS were slightly above consensus, although both remained within the company’s guidance range. The gaps were small: revenue was $31.2 million versus consensus of about $30.7 million, and EPS was $0.04 versus estimates of $0.03–$0.038.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue grew 8% year-over-year to $31.2 million with non-GAAP EPS increasing 300% to $0.04, both within guidance range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed revenue consensus of “$30.69–30.71M” and non-GAAP EPS consensus of “$0.03–0.038.”

in_line: FY26 unmanned-systems revenue was $12.6 million, close to the preview’s roughly $12 million expectation and within the $10–14 million guidance range.
The FY27 unmanned-systems mix target of 15%–20% matched the range the preview said management had previously guided to.
Software and services exceeding 10% of revenue on a pro forma basis after Nero matched the preview’s expectation that the acquisition could push the mix above 10%.
The Q1 FY27 revenue guide of $31–33 million has a $32 million midpoint, consistent with the preview’s $32–33 million base-case range; the preview had no published Q1 consensus.
Management’s confidence in full-year double-digit revenue growth repeated the preview’s base-case expectation of double-digit growth without a hard FY27 revenue figure.
Q4 revenue and EPS were within the company’s guidance ranges, as the preview anticipated.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue growth was stronger than the preview’s roughly 14% implied growth and beat the high end of guidance. The reported 16% growth included about a 2-point tailwind from the new transaction model; constant-currency growth was 14%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY27 revenue grew 16% as reported (14% constant currency) and beat the high end of guidance, aided by a roughly 2 percentage point tailwind from the new transaction model.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed revenue consensus of “$2.01B” against guidance of “$2.005–$2.015B,” with implied year-over-year growth of “+14%.”

surprises.description: Autodesk raised FY27 revenue guidance, and management attributed the outlook to stronger second-half expectations as well as MaintainX. That is better than the preview’s concern that a raise might merely reflect MaintainX and leave the organic outlook unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Autodesk raised its full-year FY27 revenue guidance to $8.295-$8.345 billion … reflecting Q2 outperformance, stronger second-half expectations, and the MaintainX acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The key risk is that a revenue raise matching the MaintainX contribution, with EPS trimmed, is an organic hold, not a raise.”

surprises.description: The organic billings growth outlook improved: excluding the transaction model and currency, Autodesk raised it from 8–9% to 9–10%; including MaintainX, the outlook is 10–11%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding the transaction model and currency, the underlying organic billings growth outlook was raised from 8-9% to 9-10%, reaching 10-11% including MaintainX's roughly 1-point contribution.”

surprises.description: The top of FY27 free-cash-flow guidance was reduced from $2.80 billion to $2.75 billion, while the low end stayed at $2.725 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FCF guidance was narrowed to $2.725-$2.75 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY27 free cash flow guidance of “$2.725–$2.800B.”

surprises.description: Autodesk disclosed about $45 million of MaintainX transaction expenses and said the unprofitable, high-growth business will weigh on FY27 operating margin. The preview anticipated MaintainX dilution, but did not flag these expenses or this explicit margin drag.
surprises.fact_evidence: MaintainX is expected to add “about $45 million in transaction expenses” and is “a drag on FY27 operating margin as an unprofitable high-growth business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “EPS dilution” from MaintainX but did not mention transaction expenses or an operating-margin drag.

surprises.description: Despite the large MaintainX cash outlay, Autodesk repurchased $453 million of shares in Q2 and plans to devote about half of free cash flow to buybacks, rather than signaling a slower pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Autodesk repurchased 2.1 million shares for $453 million and plans to apply about 50% of free cash flow to buybacks.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “a slower buyback pace” after the $3.6 billion outlay and new debt.

surprises.description: Management highlighted Construction growth above 20%, attributing it to low technology penetration and diversification across geographies and segments rather than construction-market cyclicality. The preview did not flag this growth or its drivers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Construction business continues to grow north of 20%, driven by low technology penetration and diversification across geographies and segments rather than construction market cyclicality.”

surprises.description: Autodesk plans to stop disclosing Design and Make revenue and move M&E into an “other” category, reducing the detail investors will receive on those businesses. The preview did not anticipate a change in reporting.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Autodesk will stop disclosing Design and Make revenue and move M&E into an 'other' bucket.”

surprises.description: Management expects stock-based compensation to fall to about 9% of revenue in FY27 from about 11% in FY26, a favorable cost trend not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Stock-based compensation is expected to fall to about 9% of revenue in FY27 from about 11% in FY26.”

surprises.description: Management identified the largest EBA renewal cohort, concentrated in Q4, as a key second-half risk and also pointed to slower new-business normalization in Western Europe. That adds caution to the expected gradual normalization timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “flagged its largest EBA renewal cohort concentrated in Q4 as a key second-half risk, especially amid slower new-business normalization in Western Europe.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “any language extending the ‘gradual through Q4’ normalization timeline, or any hedging on the Q4 EBA cohort, the largest of the year.”

in_line: MaintainX’s expected second-half revenue contribution was broadly in line: the preview estimated roughly $60–85 million, and the call put it at approximately $60 million. The preview also anticipated dilution from the acquisition.
FY27 non-GAAP operating margin guidance remained at 39%, matching the preview’s expectation of about 39%; management also reaffirmed the 41% FY29 target, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: MongoDB reported Q2 revenue of $772 million, above the preview’s consensus of roughly $734–735 million and even above its $760 million bull-case threshold. Revenue growth also reached 30%, the company’s highest quarterly rate since fiscal 2024.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total revenue reached $772 million, up 30% year-over-year, marking the highest quarterly growth rate since fiscal 2024.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus: $734.4–735.1M”; the bull scenario listed “Revenue: $760M+.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $1.90, substantially above the preview’s consensus of $1.61–$1.62. Non-GAAP net income also rose to $163 million from $87 million a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP net income rose to $163 million ($1.90 per share) from $87 million ($1.00 per share) a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS … Consensus: $1.61–$1.62.”

surprises.description: Atlas grew 29%, around the upper end of the preview’s 28–29% base-case range, and added a record $127 million—above the preview’s $117 million sequential-adds benchmark. The growth rate was not a major acceleration, but the dollar contribution exceeded the watchpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Atlas revenue grew approximately 29% year-over-year for the fifth straight quarter and exceeded guidance by roughly 300 basis points, adding a record $127 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Atlas 28–29%”; its catalyst checklist called for “Atlas growth ≥28% and sequential net-new Atlas dollars above $117M.”

surprises.description: MongoDB’s Q3 outlook pointed to slower growth than Q2: total growth of 20–21% and Atlas growth of about 26%. Atlas growth is below the preview’s 27% deceleration-case threshold, with management citing cautious consumption assumptions and a tough comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance implies decelerating total growth of 20–21% and Atlas growth of ~26% as management remains prudent on consumption trends and its toughest Atlas compare.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Below 27% would support the deceleration bear case.”

surprises.description: EA and Other growth reached about 36%, its strongest quarter in three years, and early demand for Search and Vector Search helped lift full-year EA growth guidance to about 11% from prior mid-single-digit expectations. The preview flagged AI/vector-search disclosure as a topic to watch but did not anticipate this reported growth or guidance increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EA and Other revenue grew approximately 36% year-over-year (its strongest quarter in three years), boosted by early demand for the newly launched Search and Vector Search on EA, with full-year EA guidance raised to ~11% growth from prior mid-single-digit expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “AI/vector-search revenue disclosure” among narrative items to watch, but gave no EA growth or guidance expectation.

surprises.description: Operating profitability was stronger than the preview’s roughly 20% full-year margin reference suggested: Q2 non-GAAP operating margin was 24%, and the company raised its full-year margin-expansion outlook to about 250 basis points, 100 basis points above the prior high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 24% from 15% a year ago, with full-year operating margin expansion now guided to ~250 basis points, 100 bps above the prior high end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY27 non-GAAP operating margin at “~20% (high end)” and flagged a guide of “20% or more.”

surprises.description: MongoDB added a record 2,900 net new customers, bringing its total to 70,600, and said many additions were AI-native companies. The preview cited the prior-quarter total customer count but focused its customer-add watchpoint on $100K-plus ARR customers, not record total net adds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company added a record 2,900 net new customers, bringing the total to 70,600 (up from 59,900 a year ago), with many new additions being AI-native companies.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave the prior-quarter total as “67,700” and listed “$100K+ ARR customer adds and multi-product attach” as a metric to watch; it did not state an expectation for total net new customers.

surprises.description: Voyage’s customer count roughly doubled quarter over quarter for a second consecutive quarter, with most new customers having no prior MongoDB relationship and referrals often coming from coding agents. The preview did not anticipate this customer-acquisition signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Voyage customer count roughly doubled quarter-over-quarter for the second consecutive quarter, with the majority of new Voyage customers having no prior relationship to MongoDB and referrals largely coming from coding agents like Claude and Codex.”

surprises.description: Remaining performance obligations grew 91% year over year, a strong forward-demand indicator not addressed in the preview’s expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Remaining performance obligations grew 91% year-over-year to $1.52 billion.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow more than doubled year over year to $138 million; the preview noted uncertainty about a reported FCF figure but did not provide a quarterly expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow more than doubled to $138 million from $70 million a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “$493M FCF, +308%” figure appeared to be FY26 full-year rather than quarterly and should be verified; it provided no Q2 FCF estimate.

in_line: Total net ARR expansion reached 122%, exactly meeting the preview’s key watchpoint of 122% or higher.

Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $2.99–$3.03 billion, with a midpoint of about $3.01 billion—roughly in line with the preview’s expectation of at least $3.00 billion, though the low end remained below that threshold.

surprises.description: Elastic reported Q1 revenue of $478 million, above the $469.49 million consensus and the company’s $469–470 million guidance. The beat was about 1.8% over consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 total revenue was $478 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Consensus | $469.49M | Company guidance (Q1) | $469–470M.”

surprises.description: Sales-led subscription revenue was $399 million, above the preview’s roughly $392 million estimate. This was a modest segment-level beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sales-led subscription revenue grew 18% to $399 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sales-led subscription | ~$392M.”

surprises.description: Q1 non-GAAP operating margin reached 16.2%, well above the approximately 14% expected in the preview. This exceeded the quarter’s margin guidance by about 2.2 percentage points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin was 16.2%, exceeding guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin | ~14% | ~14.0%.”

surprises.description: Elastic raised its full-year non-GAAP operating margin outlook to about 19.4%, above the preview’s roughly 19.0% current guidance. The increase was positive but relatively modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year fiscal 2027 guidance to … non-GAAP operating margin of ~19.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2027 (current guidance, to be updated): … non-GAAP operating margin ~19.0%.”

in_line: FY27 revenue guidance was raised to $1.998–$2.010 billion, consistent with the preview’s base-case expectation of a raise to roughly $2.00–$2.01 billion.
CRPO growth of 21% was consistent with the preview’s favorable threshold of 18–20% or higher.
Net expansion rate was 111%, within the preview’s identified 110–111% downside range.

surprises.description: Same-store sales were essentially flat, below the preview’s roughly +1% bar and its warning that comps below +2% could imply share loss. The gap was modest, though the call characterized comps as in line with expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Same-store sales essentially flat versus last year, in line with expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Same-store sales vs. ~+1% bar”; “Comps below +2% would imply share loss.”

surprises.description: Gross margin rose 50 basis points to 32.5%, rather than facing the pressure the preview expected from firearms and ammunition mix. The improvement came despite heavier promotions, though a one-time tariff benefit contributed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved 50 basis points to 32.5%, aided by disciplined inventory management, lower freight costs, and a one-time tariff benefit despite a heavier promotional cadence.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Firearms and ammo mix pressure likely persists”; the preview also flagged margin erosion as part of its base case.

surprises.description: Fishing sales fell about 2% because of western drought conditions, a specific source of category weakness the preview did not flag. The decline was partly offset by fishing sales being nearly double digits higher on a two-year comp stack.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fishing sales declined about 2% due to western drought conditions, though they are up nearly double digits on a two-year comp stack.”

surprises.description: Inventory was down $44.5 million, or 10%, year over year while the company still delivered flat comps, and management expects to finish FY2026 below FY2025 inventory levels. The preview flagged inventory as a key issue but gave no expectation for this degree of reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total inventory fell $44.5 million, or 10%, year-over-year to $399 million while still delivering flat comps, with management expecting to end fiscal 2026 below 2025 levels.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed one store closure completed on January 31 and two to three more in various stages of negotiation, developments the preview did not mention. The disclosures point to further store rationalization, though the call facts do not quantify its financial impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management confirmed one store closure on January 31st with two to three additional closures in various stages of negotiation.”

surprises.description: The company said it plans to roll out a reinvented loyalty program in early 2027, a new initiative not anticipated in the preview. Its impact is not yet specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Plans a reinvented loyalty program rollout in early 2027.”

surprises.description: Core-product in-stock rates have climbed from about 50% two years ago to over 80% today, and e-commerce grew nearly 3% with more than 70% of online orders picked up in-store. The preview did not set expectations for these availability and channel metrics.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core product in-stock rates improved from about 50% two years ago to over 80% today, and e-commerce grew nearly 3% with over 70% of online orders picked up in-store.”

in_line: Net sales of $295.6 million were close to the preview’s roughly $294 million working bar; the call described sales as in line with expectations.
Adjusted EBITDA of $8.7 million was within the preview’s estimated $8–9 million range, and the $0.11 adjusted loss per share was within its estimated $0.10–$0.14 loss range.
FY2026 guidance was reiterated at net sales down 1% to up 2%, adjusted EBITDA of $30–$36 million, and capex of $20–$25 million, matching the preview’s stated guide.
Hunting and shooting sports grew 6.7%, with firearms up 8% and ammunition nearly 11%; that strength was consistent with the preview’s discussion of NICS and NFA-related demand tailwinds.

surprises.description: Daktronics entered Q2 with $311 million of backlog, well below the preview’s $350 million-plus level to watch, and bookings also declined year over year. Management said several large deals may convert to purchase orders in Q2, with most revenue expected from Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bookings and backlog declined year-over-year, with backlog entering Q2 at $311 million (down from $356 million entering Q1),” while management said “several substantial deals are expected to convert to purchase orders in Q2 and generate revenue mostly from Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Backlog. Entering at $356.2M. Holding $350M or more with strong revenue means replenishment; draining it to fund revenue is lower quality.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 30.5%, above the preview’s expected range and its 29% threshold for a clear positive. The margin expansion included about $3 million of tariff refunds, which the preview had cautioned investors not to assume would arrive that quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit margin expanded 80 basis points to 30.5%,” aided by operating leverage and favorable mix, along with “about $3 million in cash-basis tariff refunds that were largely offset by rising input costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything at or above 29% is a clear positive”; the base scenario forecast “28.5–29.5%.” The preview also said, “do not assume a refund lands this quarter.”

surprises.description: Daktronics disclosed that it is cooperating with SEC and NBA information requests regarding the investigation of Kawhi Leonard and the Clippers, an unresolved legal issue the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management disclosed it is cooperating with SEC and NBA requests for information regarding the investigation of Kawhi Leonard and the Clippers, an unresolved legal overhang for the company.”

surprises.description: The company is considering exiting its highly customized international transportation business and has begun a collective redundancy consultation affecting employees at its Ennistymon facility. The preview did not anticipate a potential business exit or workforce consultation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is considering exiting its highly customized international transportation business, entering a collective redundancy consultation process affecting its Ennistymon facility employees.”

surprises.description: Daktronics plans to raise annual CapEx to around $20 million from $14–16 million to fund manufacturing automation. The preview did not discuss a higher investment plan, so its implications for spending and cash flow were not anticipated there.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Planning to raise annual CapEx to around $20 million (from $14-16 million) to fund manufacturing automation.”

in_line: Net sales grew 7.1% year over year, close to the preview’s working estimate of about 6.9% growth.
EPS was $0.40, matching the preview’s working estimate of about $0.40 and falling within the cited vendor estimates of $0.36–$0.44.
Operating income and margins kept Daktronics within its 10%–12% operating-margin target range, consistent with the preview’s stated FY2028 target.
Free cash flow was $27.5 million; the preview had noted that Q4 free cash flow was depressed by billing timing expected to reverse early in FY2027.
Management reaffirmed the FY2028 revenue growth, operating margin, and ROIC targets that the preview identified as the company’s existing targets.

surprises.description: REX reported diluted EPS of $1.06, far above the preview’s $0.42 consensus and its $0.43–$0.50 base-case range. The result was more than double the consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record second quarter net income of $1.06 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS (to REX) | Q2 FY2026 Consensus | $0.42”; the base scenario also projected “EPS $0.43–0.50.”

surprises.description: REX recognized $18.4 million of 45Z credits in the quarter, well above the preview’s reference point of $7.5 million booked in Q1 at $0.10 per gallon. That larger credit contribution added materially to reported gross profit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company recognized approximately $18.4 million in Section 45 production tax credit income during the quarter,” flowing “directly through gross profit.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “REX is booking $0.10/gal. Watch for a true-up, any rate above $0.10/gal”; Q1’s 45Z credit was “$7.5M.”

surprises.description: Gross profit grew approximately 144% year over year even excluding 45Z credits, indicating much stronger underlying gross-profit performance than the preview’s base case of margins near Q1 levels suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit surged to $53.3 million from $14.3 million a year earlier,” with gross profit “growing approximately 144% year-over-year even excluding 45Z tax credits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “Margins near Q1 levels”; the preview also said lower ethanol prices could pressure results.

surprises.description: The EPA issued draft Class 6 injection well permits for three One Earth carbon-capture wells, a more advanced permitting milestone than the preview’s focus on confirmation of a filing or EPA review progress.
surprises.fact_evidence: “On August 17, the U.S. EPA issued draft Class 6 injection well permits for three wells associated with the One Earth carbon capture project,” now in public comment.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called permit status the “biggest narrative driver” and said confirmation of filing or “EPA review progress” mattered; its bull case included “permit filing confirmed.”

surprises.description: Management said Q3 should be profitable and better than the same period last year, providing a positive near-term outlook where the preview had not provided a Q3 earnings expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Third quarter results are expected to be profitable and better than the same period last year, supported by record ethanol export demand.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “No company guidance is given for the quarter.”

surprises.description: SG&A rose sharply to $15.6 million from $6.2 million, an expense increase not flagged in the preview and a headwind against the otherwise much stronger profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A expenses rose to $15.6 million from $6.2 million a year earlier,” primarily due to higher incentive compensation and restricted stock issued during the quarter.

in_line: Revenue was $168.5 million, below the $194.8 million consensus, but the preview explicitly said a miss was expected and its base case was $160–$172 million.

The One Earth expansion remained on schedule for completion by the end of 2026, consistent with the preview; combined project investment of $191.2 million through Q2 remained below the preview’s cited $220–$230 million expansion budget.

surprises.description: Q2 comps were -1.8%, versus the preview’s +0.3% consensus and approximately -1% whisper; transactions were flat and the basket was lower. Net sales of $741 million also came in below the preview’s roughly $757.9 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales rose 9.1% to $741 million” while “comparable store sales declined 1.8% amid flat transactions and a lower basket.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales ~$757.9M”; “Comparable store sales +0.3%”; and the “Buy-side whisper ~–1%.”

surprises.description: Full-year sales and comp guidance came in below the prior outlook: sales fell to $2.928–$2.941 billion from $2.98–$3.00 billion, and comps to flat to +0.5% from about +2%. The comp range is around the preview’s flat-cut scenario, but weaker than its base case of a trim to roughly +1% to +1.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management lowered full-year guidance,” projecting “flat to +0.5% comps” and net sales of “$2.928-2.941 billion,” with back-half comps near flat in Q3 and up 1% in Q4.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior FY guide was “sales $2.98–3.00B” and “comps ~+2%”; the preview’s base case expected comps “trimmed to ~1–1.5%,” while RBC expected “roughly flat comps.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EPS of $1.42 beat the preview’s $1.14 estimate, but roughly $0.35 came from one-time tariff refunds. Excluding that refund benefit, EPS was about $1.07, below the estimate, so the reported beat was driven by a temporary item rather than underlying earnings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased 43% to $1.42,” but “roughly $0.35 of EPS came from one-time EPA/IEEPA tariff refunds,” offset by a 70bp price investment.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS $1.14.”

surprises.description: Despite cutting sales and comp guidance, Ollie’s raised its full-year adjusted EPS range to $4.57–$4.65, above the prior $4.45–$4.55 range and the preview’s expectation that EPS would be held or cut. The increase is partly supported by tariff refunds, making the higher range less indicative of stronger underlying demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance is now “$4.57-$4.65”; the company expects roughly $28 million in net tariff refunds for the full year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior guide was “adj. EPS $4.45–4.55”; the preview’s base case expected that range to be “held,” and its bear case expected a cut to “$4.25–4.40.”

surprises.description: Gross margin rose 360 basis points to 43.5%, with 380 basis points of benefit from tariff refunds. Even excluding refunds and price investments, however, margin was about 40.3%–40.4%, above the cited 39.9% guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 360 basis points to 43.5%,” with “380bp of the benefit” from tariff refunds; excluding refunds and price investment, gross margin “would have been ~40.3-40.4%, above the 39.9% guide.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call’s cited gross-margin guide was 39.9%.

surprises.description: Management disclosed about $15 million of planned full-year price investments, including roughly $10 million in the back half, and said it was willing to spend more to protect price leadership. The preview anticipated fuel-cost pressure but did not flag this scale of deliberate pricing investment or management’s willingness to increase it.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company plans “approximately $15 million in full-year price investments (~$10 million in the back half)” and signaled willingness “to spend more to protect its price leadership position.”

surprises.description: Ollie’s raised its full-year buyback plan to $175 million, above the approximately $125 million annual target noted in the preview, and had already repurchased $137 million year to date.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company repurchased “$84 million of stock in Q2 and $137 million year-to-date” and “raised its full-year buyback plan to $175 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “about $205.4M of buyback capacity” against a “~$125M annual target.”

surprises.description: Management said the acquired Big Lots stores were comping better than the typical negative mid-to-high-single-digit pattern in their second year, an encouraging comparison that the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Acquired Big Lots stores are comping better than the typical negative mid-to-high single-digit second-year pattern.”

in_line: The expected tariff-refund opportunity was broadly in line with the preview’s estimate: the company expects roughly $28 million in net full-year refunds versus the preview’s $25–$35 million estimate of recoverable refunds.
The 75-store full-year opening target was consistent with the preview, which said the target had been reaffirmed.

surprises.description: The preview flagged possible revenue disclosure from the Eaton deal but did not anticipate a product-shipping update. ChargePoint said early access units of Express Solo, developed with Eaton, had begun shipping; no revenue impact was stated.
surprises.fact_evidence: Richard Wilmer noted Express Solo and its collaboration with Eaton, and said early access units began shipping.

surprises.description: Petco’s adjusted EBITDA was $122 million, above the preview’s $110–112 million guide, and still reached $115 million after excluding the $6.8 million tariff refund. The normalized result therefore beat the guide as well, though by less than the headline figure suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA was $122 million … including a $6.8 million net tariff refund,” while “normalized adjusted EBITDA of $115 million exceeded both prior year and the company's outlook.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA: $110–112M guide; sell-side ~$112M.”

surprises.description: The preview expected a Q2 tariff headwind and assumed no further refunds, but Petco recorded a $6.8 million net tariff refund. Gross margin expanded 37 basis points to 39.7%, although it was roughly flat year over year excluding the refund.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 37 basis points to 39.7%, but was roughly flat year-over-year excluding the net tariff refund.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 carries the expected tariff headwind and assumes no further refunds.”

surprises.description: A Perks relaunch led to point redemptions far above Petco’s projections and reduced Q2 sales by an estimated mid-single-digit millions, mainly in services. The preview did not flag this sales drag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Petco Perks membership relaunch triggered point redemptions that far exceeded projections, negatively impacting Q2 sales by an estimated mid-single-digit millions, primarily in the services business.”

surprises.description: Petco reported double-digit growth in vet visits, doctor days, and vet diet sales, and said new hospital openings are planned to begin in 2027. The preview flagged hospital productivity and a 2027 expansion decision as watch items but did not anticipate this combination of operating strength and a stated opening plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Vet business delivered double-digit growth in total pet visits, double-digit expansion in doctor days, and double-digit vet diet sales growth for both dogs and cats, with new hospital openings planned to begin in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Services and veterinary. Grooming, doctor-day productivity, and the 25 underutilized hospitals under review ahead of a 2027 expansion decision”; “Any commitment on 2027 hospital expansion.”

surprises.description: A seven-store new-format test launched in May is already showing sizable customer and basket lifts, improved margins, and NPS gains of hundreds of basis points, with broader remodels targeted for 2027. The preview did not discuss this test or its results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A 7-store new-format market test launched in May is showing sizable lifts in new and reactivated customers, larger baskets, improved margins, and NPS up hundreds of basis points, with a broader remodel rollout targeted for 2027.”

surprises.description: Despite lapping an approximately $9 million actuarial benefit, SG&A rose by only $1 million, implying underlying expenses declined by about $8 million. The preview did not set an SG&A expectation or highlight this degree of expense control.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A was $543 million (36.5% of sales), up only $1 million despite lapping a ~$9 million actuarial benefit, implying underlying expenses fell about $8 million.”

surprises.description: Petco said its total customer base returned to slight growth, an unanticipated data point beyond the preview’s focus on comparable sales. Management also highlighted that multichannel customers generate 5x higher NPS and digital autoship customers spend 2–3x more than non-autoship customers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The total customer base inflected to slight growth in Q2,” and management said multichannel customers generate “5x higher NPS” while digital autoship customers spend “2–3x more than non-autoship customers.”

surprises.description: Petco voluntarily prepaid another $75 million of debt on September 1, bringing its paydown over nine months to $170 million. The preview identified deleveraging as a key watch item but did not forecast a payment of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company voluntarily prepaid an additional $75 million in debt on September 1st, bringing total pay down over the last nine months to $170 million as it targets a 2x leverage ratio.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Deleveraging. Q1 exited with $1.482B debt and $166.8M cash”; “Debt paydown below $1.48B, FCF, and any refinancing or maturity commentary.”

in_line: Q2 net sales were about $1.5 billion, consistent with the preview’s roughly $1.49–1.52 billion estimate and company guide of about $1.493 billion.
Comparable sales were up 0.6%, within the preview’s buy-side expectation of about +0.5% to +1.0%.
Petco reaffirmed FY26 net sales guidance of flat to +1.5% and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $415–430 million, as the preview’s base case expected.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were about $555 million, roughly $15 million below the preview’s approximately $570 million consensus and company guidance. The shortfall was attributed to European softness and the wind-down of the Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger licenses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales fell 10% year-over-year to $555 million, coming in slightly below plan due to European macro softness and the winding-down of Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger licenses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | ~$570M | ~$570M”

surprises.description: G-III gave Marc Jacobs a concrete sales scale that the preview said had not yet been disclosed: approximately $350 million in global sales this year, with long-term potential of $1 billion in annual revenue for G-III. This is new scale information rather than a quantified earnings contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Marc Jacobs acquisition is expected to generate approximately $350 million in global sales this year, with long-term potential of $1 billion in annual revenue for G-III.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Marc Jacobs standalone revenue, EBITDA, and G-III's financing terms are not disclosed… Treat every Marc Jacobs figure as a question for the call.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged the remaining tariff receivable and cash timing as an open question; the call reported approximately $134 million in tariff refunds helping cash and liquidity. The company ended Q2 with $529 million in cash and roughly $1 billion in available liquidity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q2 with $529 million in cash and roughly $1 billion in available liquidity, aided by approximately $134 million in tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Also watch the remaining IEEPA receivable and its cash timing.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP EPS was $0.26, one cent above the preview’s $0.25 consensus and just above the top of the company’s $0.15–$0.25 range. The beat was modest, rather than the larger upside in the preview’s bull scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 fiscal 2027 non-GAAP EPS was $0.26, exceeding guidance of $0.15 to $0.25.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS | $0.15–0.25 | $0.25”

in_line: Q2 gross margin was 45.2%, essentially matching the preview’s expectation of approximately 45.3%.

The go-forward portfolio excluding Tommy Hilfiger and Calvin Klein grew high single digits, in line with the preview’s expectation that owned brands would deliver high-single-digit growth to offset license runoff.

Full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance was raised modestly to $2.20–$2.30, consistent with the preview’s base case of a held or nudged-up outlook; approximately $2.71 billion of sales guidance was reiterated as expected.
Marc Jacobs was described as dilutive initially and accretive thereafter, consistent with the prior-quarter framing cited in the preview.
Inventory was down year over year, consistent with the preview’s expectation that a clean inventory position would support full-price selling.

surprises.description: Q2 comps were 14%, well above the preview’s 8.7% consensus and the company’s prior 7%–9% guide. Sales reached $1.3 billion, also above the preview’s roughly $1.21–$1.22 billion consensus range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales rose 23% year-over-year to $1.3 billion, driven by a 14% comparable sales increase.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales… Consensus… ~$1.21B – $1.22B”; “Comparable sales… Consensus… +8.7%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS of $1.68 substantially exceeded the preview’s consensus range of $1.32–$1.40, rather than merely landing near the expected $1.35–$1.45 base scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS more than doubled to $1.68.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS… Consensus… $1.32 – $1.33”; other aggregators showed “$1.36 – $1.40.”

surprises.description: Full-year guidance rose well beyond the prior outlook and the preview’s roughly $9 EPS bar: adjusted EPS is now $10.07, versus prior guidance of $8.65–$9.05. The preview’s bull scenario had identified $9.50 as a raised-guide threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year fiscal 2026 guidance… adjusted EPS of $10.07 (up 51% versus 2025).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EPS $8.65 – $9.05”; the catalyst checklist highlighted “the ~$9.00 bar,” and the bull scenario specified “$9.50.”

surprises.description: Full-year sales guidance increased to $5.63–$5.71 billion, above the prior $5.40–$5.48 billion outlook and above the preview’s bull-scenario threshold of more than $5.55 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to sales of $5.63-$5.71 billion (up 19% at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 net sales $5.40B – $5.48B”; the bull scenario called for a raise “above $5.55B.”

surprises.description: Despite the raised full-year outlook, the near-term comp outlook points to a sharp slowdown against the tough second-half comparisons: Q3 comps are guided to 8%–10%, and management’s outlook implies about 3% in Q4, versus prior-year comps of 14.3% and 15.4%. This falls short of the preview’s central question of whether management could guide through those comparisons.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for… comps of 8-10%”; the outlook implies “a low-single-digit (~3%) Q4 comp.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Prior-year compares step up to +14.3% in Q3 and +15.4% in Q4. Whether management can guide through those compares is the key question.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin expanded about 220 basis points to 35.6%, rather than merely facing the tariff and cost pressure the preview identified as a possible source of a guide-down; management said the expansion came despite higher fuel costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded approximately 220 basis points to 35.6%… despite higher fuel costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any quantified tariff drag beyond [July 24] is a likely source of a guide-down”; the bull scenario anticipated gross margin up year over year.

surprises.description: Operating leverage was another strong feature of the quarter: adjusted operating income more than doubled and operating margin expanded about 360 basis points, with SG&A leverage of 140 basis points. The preview did not identify an operating-margin outcome at this level as an expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income more than doubled to $113 million with operating margin up about 360 basis points to 9%, aided by SG&A leverage of 140 basis points.”

surprises.description: The company approved a new $600 million share repurchase authorization with no expiration, after repurchasing $60 million of shares in Q2; the preview did not anticipate a new authorization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The board approved a new $600 million share repurchase authorization with no expiration, following $60 million… repurchased in Q2.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed approximately $170 million in pretax IEEPA tariff refunds in its cash and investments, but excluded those refunds from guidance. The preview focused on tariff exposure and the possibility of tariff-driven guide-downs, not a refund of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with approximately $1.2 billion in cash and investments, including $170 million in pretax IEEPA tariff refunds excluded from guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The current guide assumes today's tariff rates only through July 24. Any quantified tariff drag beyond that date is a likely source of a guide-down.”

surprises.description: Full-year CapEx was raised to $250–$260 million to fund store remerchandising, including tearing down the Five Beyond wall for roughly $40,000–$45,000 per store. The preview noted the 150-store opening plan but did not flag this added investment or teardown program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year CapEx to $250-$260 million to fund store remerchandising (tearing down the Five Beyond wall at roughly $40,000-$45,000 per store).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The company plans 150 openings in FY2026.”

in_line: The company opened 52 net new stores in Q2, close to the preview’s expectation of about 50 net new stores.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was $33 million, below the preview’s $38.82 million consensus estimate and $41.31 million alternative estimate. The preview’s base case was $37–42 million, so the result fell below even its lower bound.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q3 fiscal 2026 revenue fell 29% year-over-year to $33 million,” driven by fewer module deliveries to South Korea, lower generation output, and reduced service and advanced technology revenue.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $38.82M”; “Revenue (alt.) $41.31M”; base scenario: “Revenue lands near consensus,” or “$37–42M.”

surprises.description: The Fit Energy Phase 0 agreement generated substantial losses rather than simply serving as the expected initial deposit-backed order: current costs exceeded the contract price, contributing $17 million of charges and a $24.5 million gross loss. The preview highlighted the 30-MW initial phase but did not anticipate contract economics producing these losses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported a gross loss of $24.5 million,” primarily due to “$17 million in charges” tied to Phase 0 of the Fit Energy agreement, “reflecting current costs exceeding contractual pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The Fit Energy agreement had “a deposit-backed initial 30 MW expected to begin delivery later in 2026”; the preview said the key test was whether “the Fit Energy 30 MW deposit converts into product backlog.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA deteriorated to a $36.7 million loss, versus the preview’s comparison point of a $17.1 million loss in Q2. The loss was more than twice that prior-quarter figure, rather than showing the improvement the preview flagged as important.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EBITDA was “negative $36.7 million this quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview ranked “Adjusted EBITDA vs. $(17.1)M, and cash burn” as a key metric and described a “wider burn” as a weak outcome.

surprises.description: The reported backlog headline reached $3.6 billion, far above the preview’s $1.05–1.15 billion base-case range. But $2.4 billion is newly labeled awarded capacity backlog and is not guaranteed to convert to revenue; the committed portion was $1.3 billion, so the headline increase is less firm than its size suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total committed and awarded capacity backlog reached $3.6 billion,” including “$1.3 billion of committed backlog” and “a new $2.4 billion awarded capacity backlog that is not guaranteed to convert to revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “Backlog flat at $1.05–1.15B” and said to watch whether growth came from “real bookings or reclassification.”

surprises.description: The active pipeline grew to roughly 10 GW, about twice the preview’s 4–5 GW base-case range. The increase is concentrated in data-center proposals, however, and the preview cautioned that pipeline growth without conversion should not be read as progress.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company had “roughly 10 gigawatts of active proposals in fiscal 2026,” with data centers accounting for “approximately 97% of the third quarter pipeline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The prior-quarter pipeline was “4 GW”; the preview’s base scenario expected “pipeline 4–5 GW” and warned, “Pipeline growth without conversion should not be read as progress.”

surprises.description: After quarter end, the company reported a 75-MW capacity reservation with a major data-center co-location operator for a Texas project. That is a concrete development beyond the preview’s base case of no new contract, though definitive agreements and timing are still pending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subsequent to quarter end, the company closed a 75-megawatt capacity reservation agreement” for a Texas project, with “definitive agreements and timing still pending.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case anticipated “no capex change” and described a “named new data-center contract” as a bull-case catalyst.

surprises.description: Management supplied a specific profitability milestone the preview had not found in company guidance: positive Adjusted EBITDA in Q4 fiscal 2027. The target is conditional on backlog conversion, customer delivery schedules, and cost reductions, so it is a forward goal rather than a firm commitment.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management set a “new target of achieving positive Adjusted EBITDA in Q4 fiscal 2027,” contingent on backlog conversion, customer delivery schedules, and cost reductions.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Company guidance: Not found in my searches” and flagged “FY2026 guidance and first FY2027 framing” as a key issue.

surprises.description: EPS was a larger loss than the preview’s cited consensus range, even though the preview warned that rising share count could distort per-share comparisons. The reported $0.64 loss per share exceeded the preview’s most pessimistic cited estimate of $0.50 per share.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net loss attributable to common stockholders was “$45.3 million, or $0.64 per share,” with “70.4 million weighted average shares.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: EPS estimates were “$(0.41),” with alternatives of “$(0.39) / $(0.50).” The preview warned that weighted shares likely would be “around 62–72M” and said a per-share beat could come from share count alone.

in_line: Weighted average shares were 70.4 million, within the preview’s estimated Q3 range of roughly 62–72 million; the preview had already cautioned that the higher share count would affect EPS comparisons.

The Fit Energy agreement’s 380-MW headline did not mean all 380 MW were committed: the preview had already identified the deposit-backed 30-MW initial phase and warned that the larger agreement could amount to an option without conversion.

surprises.description: Q2 sales reached $163.5 million, above the company’s $160 million guidance ceiling and roughly $157 million consensus; comparable sales rose 12.1%, above the guided 6%–10% range and the preview’s +8% base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total net sales rose 8.1% to $163.5 million, with comparable net sales up 12.1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $154M – $160M | ~$157.0M”; “Comparable net sales | +6% to +10%”; base scenario: “Comp | +8%.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross margin expanded to 35.5%, substantially exceeding the preview’s expectation of flat-to-slight growth and its 33.5% threshold for supporting a structural margin story.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved 300 basis points to 35.5%, driven by a 140-basis-point product margin gain and 160 basis points of buying/distribution/occupancy leverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Company guidance was “Flat to up slightly”; the preview said “Above roughly 33.5% supports a structural margin story.”

surprises.description: Q2 diluted EPS of $0.27 was well above both the $0.13–$0.20 company guide and the preview’s $0.14–$0.17 consensus range, even though the preview thought an in-guidance quarter could print as an optical miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net income was $8.4 million ($0.27 per diluted share), up $5.2 million from $3.2 million ($0.10) a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS | $0.13 – $0.20 | $0.14 – $0.17”; “an in-guidance quarter could therefore print as a headline EPS miss.”

surprises.description: Q3 sales guidance was markedly higher than the preview’s estimate: the company guided to $150–$155 million with comps up 10%–14%, versus the preview’s $138–$144 million sales bogey.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for net sales of $150-155 million (comps up 10-14%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My framework bogey is net sales of about $138–144M.”

surprises.description: Q3 earnings guidance also exceeded the preview’s breakeven-to-$0.05 estimate: the company expects $0.07–$0.12 per share, rather than results near breakeven.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for … net income of $2.2-3.7 million ($0.07-0.12 per share), versus a $1.4 million net loss last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My framework bogey is … EPS around breakeven to +$0.05.”

surprises.description: Fiscal August comps accelerated to 14.6%, well above the May +8.3% run-rate the preview identified as a key cadence to watch, despite tougher comparisons.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal August comps accelerated to 14.6%, extending the streak to 13 consecutive months of comparable sales growth despite tougher year-over-year comparisons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether June and July held the May run-rate of +8.3%, and whether August quarter-to-date was disclosed.”

surprises.description: Inventory was lower year over year rather than building into the back-to-school and holiday period the preview flagged as a watch item, while being several percentage points more current.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total inventory decreased 1.3% year-over-year while being several percentage points more current, with Q2 sales up 8% on inventory down 1% in dollars.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Inventory is slightly more current, but growth into the back-to-school and holiday build is a watch item.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed $1.5 million of Q2 bonus accruals, an unmodeled expense that management said will continue to pressure SG&A leverage. The preview gave an SG&A range but did not flag these accruals.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Improved performance triggered $1.5 million in bonus accruals in Q2, an expense absent from the model for four years that will continue to pressure SG&A leverage.”

surprises.description: Tilly’s said it had returned to trailing-four-quarter profitability for the first time since fiscal 2022 and is targeting its first profitable fiscal year since then—an additional turnaround milestone not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company returned to profitability on a trailing four-quarters basis (just under $2 million) for the first time since fiscal 2022, and is targeting its first profitable fiscal year since 2022.”

surprises.description: Argan reported Q2 revenue of $384 million, well above the preview’s $294–298 million consensus range. The roughly 29–31% beat was much larger than the preview’s expected 24–25% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record consolidated Q2 fiscal 2027 revenue of $384 million, up 62% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $297.8M”; “Revenue (alt.) | $294M”; consensus growth of “+25.3%” or “+23.7%.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS was $3.76, far above the preview’s primary $2.68 consensus estimate and its alternate $2.39 estimate. That is a much larger beat than the preview’s expected 7% year-over-year EPS growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q2 net income of $53.3 million or $3.76 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) | $2.68”; alternate EPS estimate “$2.39”; primary consensus implied “+7.2%” year-over-year growth.

surprises.description: Backlog fell to $2.5 billion, below even the preview’s bearish threshold of less than $2.6 billion and below its $2.7–2.9 billion base case. The preview identified backlog as the key indicator, and no major new power projects were added.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total committed backlog fell to $2.5 billion from $2.9 billion at the start of fiscal 2027, as no major new power projects were added despite $260+ million in scope increases and smaller job additions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base scenario backlog: “$2.7–2.9B”; bear scenario: “<$2.6B.” The preview said a third sequential decline “below about $2.7B” would support the bear case.

surprises.description: Industrial gross margin was 7.3%, well below the 11.8% Q1 level the preview highlighted as the reference point for the watched segment margin. The call attributed the weakness to underperforming non-data-center projects.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Industrial revenue surged 111% to $76 million but carried a weak 7.3% margin due to underperforming non-data-center projects.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Industrial $58M (20%) at 11.8%. Watch Industrial margin.”

surprises.description: Argan acquired Valcor Communications, an unanticipated expansion of Tele Data that management says could double the segment’s revenue from fiscal 2026 levels. The preview did not identify this acquisition or segment-growth prospect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company acquired Valcor Communications to expand its Tele Data segment, which could double revenue from fiscal 2026 levels.”

surprises.description: The North Carolina fabrication facility was not mentioned in the preview, and management expects it to add more than $10 million in quarterly Industrial revenue once it is completed in Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new North Carolina fabrication facility (completing in Q3) is expected to add $10+ million in quarterly Industrial revenue.”

surprises.description: Management’s stated window for adding a handful of projects is somewhat sooner than the preview’s 10–18-month expectation: the call put it at 7–15 months. The windows overlap substantially, so the shift is modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects to add a handful of new projects over the next 7-15 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management was expected to add “a handful of new projects over the next 10–18 months.”

in_line: Consolidated gross margin was 19.3%, close to the preview’s roughly 20% expectation and within management’s cited “high teens to low 20s” range; the preview also warned that Q1’s early-completion margin benefit might not repeat.

surprises.description: The non-GAAP operating loss was $36.2 million, $8.3 million better than the guidance midpoint of about $44.5 million and well below the preview’s roughly $44 million expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating loss was $36.2 million, coming in $8.3 million better than the midpoint of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating loss” consensus: “~–$44M”; Q1 company guidance: “–$40.5M to –$48.5M.”

surprises.description: The company generated positive free cash flow of $2.1 million, contrary to the cash-burn concern highlighted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company generated positive free cash flow of $2.1 million,” compared with negative $54.8 million last quarter and negative $34.3 million a year ago.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Operating loss and cash burn” as a key issue to watch, but gave no specific free-cash-flow expectation.

surprises.description: Subscription revenue reached $49.2 million, above the $48.3 million consensus and up from $48.4 million in Q4, rather than remaining roughly flat as the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subscription revenue of $49.2 million representing 94% of total revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Subscription revenue: $48.3M”; the preview described it as “Roughly flat vs. Q4's $48.4M” and said sequential growth would be the first sign of stabilization.

surprises.description: Non-GAAP gross margin rebounded to 50% from 37% in Q4, a sharper improvement than the preview’s focus on the recent margin decline suggested. Management did caution that it expects the margin to moderate to the mid-40s next quarter as it invests in engineering.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin improved sequentially from 37% to 50%, though management expects it to moderate to mid-40s next quarter due to engineering investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged gross margin as a key issue and noted that “Q4 non-GAAP gross margin fell to 37%.”

surprises.description: The call reported strong booking and customer-win activity that the preview did not quantify: bookings grew 73% year over year, federal bookings grew 138%, and the company closed 22 enterprise agreements, including several major commercial and government customers.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bookings grew 73% year-over-year, while federal bookings grew 138% year-over-year, driven by dissatisfaction with an incumbent competitor”; the company “closed 22 enterprise agreements” including Johnson & Johnson, Ford Motor Company, the U.S. Department of Defense, and the Defense Logistics Agency.

surprises.description: The FY2027 non-GAAP operating-loss guidance improved modestly: its range is $123 million to $155 million, compared with the preview’s cited company range of $128 million to $160 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY2027 revenue guidance is $210 million to $240 million with a non-GAAP operating loss guidance of $123 million to $155 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY27 company guidance as “Operating loss –$128M to –$160M.”

in_line: Q1 total revenue was $52.4 million, close to the $51.5 million consensus and within the preview’s $52–54 million base-case range.
FY2027 revenue guidance remained $210 million to $240 million, as the preview identified reaffirmation of that range as the base case.

Restructuring was nearly complete and achieved approximately $135 million in annualized cost savings, consistent with the preview’s report that the company had already cited roughly $135 million of annualized costs removed.

surprises.description: Revenue was $42.9 million, below the preview’s $44.9 million consensus and its $43.5–44.5 million estimate range. The shortfall came despite revenue holding roughly flat quarter over quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenues were $42.9 million, flat versus the prior quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q2 2026 consensus $44.9M | Our estimate $43.5–44.5M.”

surprises.description: Net income was $17.3 million, below the preview’s approximately $19.7 million implied estimate. Reported EPS was $0.46, though the preview’s $0.53 consensus was for adjusted EPS, so those EPS figures are not directly comparable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income was $17.3 million … with EPS of $0.46 for the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net income | ~$19.7M (implied).” The preview also states: “The consensus appears to be on an adjusted EPS basis.”

surprises.description: The Persian Gulf disruption was more severe for LPG trade than the preview’s cited 3% decline in global exports: exports fell 8% in the first half, with Chinese imports down 29% and Indian demand down 20%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Persian Gulf conflict and Hormuz closure cut global LPG exports 8% in H1 2026 and slashed Chinese imports 29% and Indian demand 20%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management flagged a 3% drop in global LPG exports.”

surprises.description: Despite the disruption, rerouting around the Cape of Good Hope boosted ton-miles and VLGC rates reached all-time highs, exceeding the preview’s expectation that firm rates would hold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rerouting via the Cape of Good Hope boosted ton-miles and drove VLGC rates to all-time highs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The bull and base scenarios both assumed “firm rates held.”

surprises.description: Remaining 2026 fleet-day coverage rose to 60%, above the 55% reported at Q1 and above the preview’s bear-case concern that coverage could slip below 50%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “60% of remaining 2026 fleet days are secured (about $50 million in revenue).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “55% of remaining 2026 days” at Q1 and identified a bear scenario where “coverage slips below 50%.”

surprises.description: The forward charter picture did not show the extension investors were looking for: one-year forward coverage remained 45%, and secured revenues through 2029 were about $90 million rather than the roughly $100 million previously cited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “One-year forward coverage of 45% is below historical norms” and “total future secured revenues of about $90 million through 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “45% of forward-year days fixed” and “~$100M contracted into 2029,” adding that investors wanted evidence the backlog was “being extended, not run down.”

surprises.description: The company did not restart share repurchases in Q2, despite the preview identifying a restart or dividend as a central capital-allocation catalyst. Management said the board is still reviewing options and expressed an intention to invest in fleet renewal rather than announcing an immediate payout or buyback.
surprises.fact_evidence: “No shares were repurchased in Q2 as the share price appreciated.” The board is “reviewing options to deploy its record cash pile,” with an intention “to invest in renewing the fleet.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “With $155M in cash, no debt, and a 0.49x price/book ratio, a buyback restart or dividend is the central catalyst. Silence on this would be a negative signal.”

surprises.description: Liquidity ultimately exceeded $250 million after the Echo Wizard insurance settlement was collected, substantially above the preview’s cited cash level of about $155 million as of the June 5 call. The preview noted that the settlement was complete but did not give this collection amount or resulting liquidity level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Liquidity grew 70% in six months from $99 million to $168.3 million by June 30, and has since climbed to over $250 million after collecting more than $77 million from the Echo Wizard insurance settlement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited cash “rising to ~$155M by the June 5 call” and said the insurance “was settled per the July 7 update.”

in_line: The company remained debt-free, consistent with the preview’s report of zero bank debt in Q1.
No formal EPS or full-year FY26 guidance was expected; the preview said the company does not issue formal EPS guidance and that no full-year guidance was found.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $5.0 billion, below the preview’s $5.67 billion estimate and its roughly $5.8 billion base case, though above the alternative $4.26 billion estimate. The result therefore fell short of the higher expectations but landed within the preview’s unusually wide estimate range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue nearly doubled year-over-year, rising 99% to $5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $5.67B | Investing.com / TradingView, pre-print”; “Revenue (alt.) | $4.26B | Zacks”; Base scenario: “Revenue ~$5.8B.”

surprises.description: The company declared a $1.00-per-share special dividend in addition to its regular $0.20 quarterly dividend. The preview identified the special-dividend decision as a key unresolved issue, but its base case did not assume a payout.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company declared a special dividend of $1.00 per share on top of its regular $0.20 quarterly dividend.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management deferred a special-dividend decision until Q4 results”; the base case listed “volumes normalize, contango offsets softer premiums, SG&A ~$72M,” while the bull case included “special dividend declared.”

surprises.description: Management said the demand slowdown had continued into the first two months of Q1 FY2027, with customers holding back amid geopolitical uncertainty. That is weaker than the preview’s base-case expectation that volumes would normalize after Q3, although the preview did identify retail slowdown as a risk scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A demand slowdown that began mid-March/early April and has continued through the first two months of Q1 fiscal 2027,” with “geopolitical uncertainty causing customers to sit on their hands.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case assumed “Volumes normalize”; the bear case cited “Retail slowdown.”

surprises.description: New DTC customer additions fell 77% sequentially to 67,900. The preview had flagged weak new-customer additions and Monex’s contribution in Q3, but did not forecast a further sequential drop of this size for Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New DTC customer additions dropped sharply, down 38% year-over-year in Q4 to 67,900 and down 77% sequentially, with 58% of the prior quarter's new customers attributable to the Monex acquisition.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “New customers fell 67% YoY on an organic basis, and Monex supplied 58% of new additions.”

surprises.description: The Tether partnership was generating gold and silver leasing and storage business at multiples of the levels initially disclosed, an operational upside not quantified in the preview. Management tempered the news by saying the business is low-margin and will take a couple of quarters to fully contribute.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Tether partnership is generating gold and silver leases and storage business at multiples of the levels initially disclosed,” but it is “low-margin” and “benefits will take a couple of quarters to fully materialize.”

in_line: Q4 gross profit was $110.3 million, close to and slightly above the preview’s roughly $107 million base case, the main earnings datapoint it flagged to watch.

surprises.description: HPE reported $1.11 in non-GAAP EPS, far above the preview’s $0.93–$0.95 estimates and the $0.93 high end of company guidance. The call also said non-GAAP operating profit reached a record $2 billion, 2.5 times the year-ago level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS reached a record $1.11,” the first time HPE surpassed $1 in a single quarter and “well above the high end of guidance”; “non-GAAP operating profit hit a record $2 billion (2.5x higher year-over-year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS” consensus “~$0.93,” Zacks “$0.94,” BofA “$0.95”; company guidance was “$0.88 – $0.93.”

surprises.description: HPE raised FY26 EPS guidance to $3.75–$3.85, well beyond the preview’s expectation of roughly $3.40–$3.50 after a modest raise. It also lifted the free-cash-flow floor from $3.5 billion to at least $3.75 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “HPE raised FY26 EPS guidance to $3.75–$3.85 and free cash flow to at least $3.75 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said BofA expected EPS “to go up about $0.05,” and buy-side expectations were “around $3.45–$3.50 or more”; the existing FCF floor was “at least $3.5B.”

surprises.description: HPE raised its FY27 framework substantially: revenue growth is now 13–17% versus the prior 8–12% framework, and the FCF floor is at least $5 billion versus $4.5 billion. The new EPS range is $4.40–$4.60, replacing the prior framework’s 12–16% EPS growth target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lifting its FY27 framework to 13–17% revenue growth, EPS of $4.40–$4.60, and free cash flow of at least $5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s FY27 framework was “revenue growth +8% to +12%, EPS growth +12% to +16%, FCF at least $4.5B.”

surprises.description: HPE’s orders grew 42% on a normalized basis to a record backlog, better than the preview’s concern that backlog could draw down and its base-case assumption of roughly flat backlog. This indicates stronger demand and order accumulation than that cautious setup anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Orders growing 42% on a normalized basis to a record backlog.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “a backlog drawdown with light orders would point to a weak print” and described the base case as “backlog roughly flat.”
