surprises.description: AI systems demand and backlog strengthened rather than showing the drawdown the preview warned about: orders rose more than 30% sequentially to $2.4 billion, enterprise demand more than doubled, and backlog increased 14% sequentially to a new high. The order figure was just below the preview’s $2.5 billion bull-case marker, but the overall direction was stronger than its base-case setup.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI systems orders grew over 30% sequentially to $2.4 billion with enterprise demand more than doubling,” while “backlog rose 14% sequentially to a new high.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “AI systems orders and backlog,” said a drawdown with light orders could signal weakness, and put “AI orders above $2.5B, backlog above $6.5B” in its bull scenario; its base scenario assumed backlog “roughly flat.”

surprises.description: Networking order growth and AI-related demand were stronger than the preview’s focus on roughly 10% normalized revenue growth: orders rose 36%, networks-for-AI orders hit a record $700 million, and HPE raised its full-year networks-for-AI order target to $2.5–$3 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Networking orders grew 36%”; “networks-for-AI orders hit a record $700 million,” bringing FY26 cumulative orders to $2.2 billion and prompting a raised target of “$2.5–$3 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted normalized networking growth of “~10%” and said that figure and synergy progress “matter most”; it did not anticipate a networks-for-AI target increase.

surprises.description: HPE announced significant AI infrastructure customer wins not anticipated in the preview: an expanded, multi-year, multi-gigawatt Oracle collaboration for Juniper networking equipment and a post-quarter multibillion-dollar server deal with a hyperscaler.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An expanded multi-year, multi-gigawatt collaboration with Oracle to deploy Juniper routers and switches for AI cloud build-out,” plus “a post-quarter multibillion-dollar server deal with a hyperscaler for inferencing.”

surprises.description: Cloud and AI revenue reached $9 billion, up 25%, while operating margin rose to 17%, up 460 basis points sequentially. Server revenue also reached an all-time high, although HPE attributed growth primarily to higher selling prices amid supply-constrained unit volumes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cloud and AI revenue rose 25% to $9 billion with operating margin of 17% (up 460 bps sequentially),” and “server revenue grew 35% to an all-time high driven primarily by higher ASPs amid supply-constrained unit volumes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted supply constraints and memory-related margin risk, including a concern that gross margin could compress by 100 basis points or more; it gave no Cloud and AI segment margin or server-revenue estimate.

surprises.description: Networking revenue conversion lagged the surge in orders: normalized revenue grew only 10%, and data-center networking revenue fell 6% because of shipment timing. The 10% normalized growth matched the preview’s expectation, but the data-center decline and order-to-revenue gap were not anticipated there.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Networking revenue grew only 10% on a normalized basis due to supply constraints,” while “data center networking revenue actually declining 6% on shipment timing,” despite 36% order growth.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited normalized networking growth of “~10%” as the figure to watch.

surprises.description: HPE reached 1.8x net leverage, below its 2x target a year ahead of plan, and committed to return at least 75% of Q4 free cash flow to shareholders. The payout commitment matched the preview’s anticipated policy, but reaching the leverage target ahead of schedule was better than the preview’s expectation of confirmation by fiscal year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Exited Q3 with net leverage of 1.8x (below its 2x target and a year ahead of plan)” and “plans to return at least 75% of free cash flow to shareholders in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management expected “2x net leverage by fiscal year-end, a year early,” and identified “confirmation of 2x net leverage and concrete language on the 75% payout” as key.

surprises.description: Management said the raised FY27 framework excludes the AMD Helios opportunity, which it estimated could become a tens-of-billions-of-dollars market ramping in late 2026 and 2027. That creates a potential opportunity outside the newly raised framework that the preview did not discuss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FY27 outlook explicitly excludes the AMD Helios opportunity,” which management estimated “could represent a tens-of-billions-of-dollars total market ramping in late calendar 2026 and 2027.”

in_line: Networking normalized revenue growth was 10%, in line with the preview’s approximately 10% expectation.
The plan to return at least 75% of free cash flow to shareholders in Q4 matched the preview’s expectation for concrete language on the payout policy.

surprises.description: Net new ARR was $54 million, far above the preview’s roughly $33–37 million estimate and its $35 million bar. It also grew 9% year over year rather than declining again, substantially outperforming the concern that the tough comparison would produce another YoY drop.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net new ARR of $54 million growing only 9%” year-over-year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net new ARR: ~$33–37M (my estimate)” and “Bar: at least $35M”; the preview also warned that “A second straight YoY decline weakens the 2H acceleration story.”

surprises.description: Operating margin reached negative 9%, much better than the company’s negative 14% to negative 15% Q2 guidance. The improvement was driven largely by an approximately 8-point reduction in R&D as a share of revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating margin improved 11 percentage points year-over-year to negative 9%, significantly ahead of guidance,” driven largely by an “~8-point improvement in R&D as a percent of revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op. margin” Q2 guidance was “(14)% to (15)%.”

surprises.description: Full-year revenue guidance was raised to $888–892 million, with a midpoint of $890 million, above the preview’s base-case raise of $885–888 million and reaching its $890 million bull-trigger threshold. Management said the increase exceeded the Q2 revenue beat, indicating a stronger full-year raise than the base case anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Netskope raised full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $888-892 million,” lifting it “by more than the Q2 beat.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise only to about $885M is the base case”; “$890M or more signals confidence.”

surprises.description: Q2 ARR reached $899 million, above the preview’s estimated $875–885 million range. Its 27% growth was below the preview’s 28%-or-higher clear-positive threshold, though it remained above the preview’s 26%-or-below structural-deceleration concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 ARR reached $899 million, up 27% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ARR: ~$875–885M (my estimate)” and “28% or above is a clear positive.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $220.5 million exceeded even the high end of the preview’s $212–218 million consensus range and its $219–222 million bull scenario’s lower bound. The preview expected a revenue beat, but the reported result was stronger than its consensus range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue grew 29% to $220.5 million, beating guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus (varies by source)” was “~$212M–$218M”; the preview said, “The revenue beat is likely.”

surprises.description: Q2 free cash flow improved substantially from the prior quarter but was still negative $29.8 million, worse than the preview’s roughly negative $20 million-to-breakeven level for keeping the annual target comfortable. The company retained a full-year target at the low end of its earlier 2–4% range and guided to positive Q3 FCF, with faster annual billing transitions supporting contracted future billings.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow was negative $29.8 million in Q2,” full-year FCF margin was guided to “~2%,” and Q3 FCF to “$10-20 million”; the transition to annual billings was faster than expected and grew contracted future billings 75%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FCF well below roughly −$20M to breakeven puts the full-year guide at risk”; the prior guidance was “+2% to +4%,” and management expected “positive quarterly FCF in the back half.”

surprises.description: Net retention rose to 114%, above the preview’s 113% reference point, and product adoption broadened: 59% of customers used at least four products versus 51% previously, while 41% used at least five versus 35%. This was stronger expansion evidence than simply holding the prior NRR level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net retention rate rose to 114%” and “59% of customers now using 4+ products (up from 51%) and 41% using 5+ products (up from 35%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NRR (113%). Any further slippage would point to weak expansion, not retention”; the preview’s catalyst checklist said “Holding 113% versus slipping toward 110%.”

surprises.description: The preview expected new sales reps to ramp and net new ARR to accelerate in the second half, but management said roughly half of sales reps were still ramping, with full productivity expected later in the year and into next year. That suggests the productivity contribution may take longer to arrive than the preview’s second-half acceleration thesis implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly 50% of sales reps still ramping” and full productivity gains were expected “later in the year and into next year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management “expects net new ARR to accelerate in 2H as new reps ramp.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that about one-third of the AI security pipeline was in or entering POC, giving a new measure of deal maturity. However, most deals take 6–12 months to close, pushing AI revenue contribution toward the second half and Q4 rather than indicating near-term conversion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Roughly one-third of its AI security pipeline is in or entering the POC phase,” while most deals follow a “6-to-12-month enterprise sales cycle” that pushes contribution toward “the second half and Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AI suite conversion. Watch for any dollar disclosure on pipeline converting to ARR.”

surprises.description: The company announced an approximately 5% workforce reduction while redirecting spending toward AI infrastructure and tokens. The preview had not flagged a workforce cut or this resource shift, so the cost action came alongside a new investment priority.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced approximately 5% of its workforce while reallocating spend toward AI infrastructure and tokens” to drive “AI nativeness.”

surprises.description: Netskope positioned AI security as a new revenue pillar and cited a roughly $170 billion greenfield AI security opportunity within a $336 billion total addressable market. This was a new strategic market-sizing claim not addressed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Netskope frames its opportunity as a $170 billion greenfield AI security market within a $336 billion total addressable market,” beyond SASE/SSE.

in_line: The company reported gross retention at an all-time high, consistent with the preview’s prior-quarter note that gross retention was already at a record high.

surprises.description: Wiley’s Learning revenue fell 20%, with both academic and professional down 20%, despite the preview flagging stabilization after FY26 declines of 5% and 10%. The segment’s adjusted EBITDA margin also dropped to 15.1% from 27.4%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Learning revenue fell 20% to $93 million, with both academic and professional down 20%,” and segment adjusted EBITDA margin “collapsed to 15.1% from 27.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Learning stabilization. Academic was −5% and Professional −10% in FY26.”

surprises.description: Net leverage was 2.7x, above the preview’s roughly 2.1x post-Emerald figure on the reported basis. Management gave a 2.1x figure only when including Emerald synergies.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt to EBITDA rose to 2.7x (2.1x pro forma including Emerald synergies) from 1.9x a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Pro forma leverage is ~2.1x post-Emerald, up from 1.4x.”

surprises.description: The year-over-year AI licensing revenue headwind was larger than previewed: $29 million rather than about $25 million. Management said it did not change full-year expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue faced a known $29 million headwind from AI licensing revenue that landed in the prior-year quarter,” which “does not change full-year expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A ~$25M unfavorable year-over-year revenue comparison in Q1 from prior-year AI licensing projects.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS fell 10% year over year, a steeper decline than the roughly 6% decline implied by the preview’s consensus estimate. The call attributed part of the decline to higher net interest expense.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS fell 10% partly due to higher net interest expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed adjusted EPS consensus of “~$0.46” versus “$0.49” a year earlier, or “−6%.”

in_line: Wiley reaffirmed FY27 adjusted EPS guidance of $4.60–$5.05, adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 26.5%–27.5%, and free cash flow guidance of $205 million, matching the preview’s cited guidance.
The company remained on track for more than $50 million of FY27 AI revenue, consistent with the preview’s stated AI revenue guide.
Net leverage was 2.1x on management’s pro forma basis including Emerald synergies, in line with the preview’s roughly 2.1x post-Emerald figure.

surprises.description: Genesco’s adjusted loss per share was $0.83, substantially narrower than the preview’s expected $1.34 loss; the adjusted operating loss also narrowed by $6 million to $8 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted loss per share improved to $0.83” and “adjusted operating loss narrowing by $6 million to a loss of $8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $(1.34)” consensus.

surprises.description: The company lowered its full-year comparable-sales outlook from growth of 1%–2% to flat and now expects total sales to decline about 2%, rather than the prior outlook of down 1% to flat. Management linked the change to greater sales pressure at schuh in the increasingly promotional UK market.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year guidance was cut to flat comparable sales (from up 1%-2%) and total sales down approximately 2%, reflecting greater sales pressure at schuh in the increasingly promotional UK market.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY27 guidance … comps +1–2%; total sales -1% to flat”; the preview also described reiterating the $2.00–$2.40 EPS range as the minimum acceptable outcome.

surprises.description: Despite the weaker sales outlook, Genesco now expects adjusted EPS at the high end of its $2.00–$2.40 range, above the prior midpoint expectation. That is a more favorable earnings outlook than simply reiterating the range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company now expects full-year adjusted EPS at the high end of its $2 to $2.40 range, up from the prior midpoint expectation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 EPS guidance of $2.00–$2.40. Reiterate, raise, or cut”; the base scenario expected the guide to be reiterated.

surprises.description: Schuh’s comps remained down 9%, rather than showing the moderation the preview said investors would watch for. The call attributed the decline to an intentional pullback on discounting, while also noting worsening promotional pressure in the UK.
surprises.fact_evidence: “schuh comps fell 9% due to intentional pullback on discounting”; full-year sales pressure reflects “the increasingly promotional UK market.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Comps were -9% in Q1 by design. Watch for gross margin recovery and whether the UK decline is moderating.”

surprises.description: Gross margin improved more than the preview’s focus on possible schuh recovery established: adjusted gross margin rose 140 basis points, with schuh’s margin up 300 basis points as its full-price mix increased 10 percentage points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 140 basis points to 47.2%, driven largely by schuh's 300 basis point margin improvement as full-price mix rose 10 percentage points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for gross margin recovery” at schuh.

surprises.description: Journeys not only extended its expected positive-comp streak but accelerated to mid-single-digit comps in August, a favorable update amid the preview’s concern that back-to-school demand might shift later into Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Journeys posted its eighth consecutive quarter of positive comps (up 2%) and accelerated to a mid-single-digit comp in August.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Back-to-school intent skewed later in 2026” and identified September and Q3 commentary as a key item to watch; it also noted Journeys’ eight-quarter positive-comp streak.

surprises.description: The call disclosed a Journeys 4.0 format producing over 25% sales lift and raised the rollout target to 95 stores for the year. The preview did not flag this format or rollout as an expectation to assess.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Journeys' 4.0 store format is delivering over 25% sales lift, with the full-year rollout target raised to 95 stores, reaching about 180 stores (20% of the fleet) by year-end.”

surprises.description: Genesco announced an enterprise-wide cost-savings program with a target of $40–$50 million, including up to $20 million in fiscal 2027. The preview did not anticipate this program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The enterprise-wide cost savings program targets $40-$50 million, with up to $20 million expected in fiscal 2027 and $20-$30 million over the following two years.”

surprises.description: Overall comparable sales declined 1%, slightly below the preview’s expectation of roughly flat comps.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Overall comparable sales down 1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Comparable sales ~flat” consensus; the company guide was “Flat to slightly down.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $530 million, close to the preview’s $528.4 million consensus and within the company’s approximately $524–$530 million guide.
Journeys comps were positive at 2%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that its eight-quarter positive-comp streak would continue.
The company received approximately $22 million in tariff refunds, close to the $23–$25 million filed amount discussed in the preview.
Genesco resumed share repurchases, consistent with the preview’s expectation that buyback resumption was a catalyst; the preview did not specify an amount.

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.50 versus the preview’s $0.01 consensus, with $0.44 per share coming from tariff refunds. The refund was also larger than the roughly $12 million the preview said Duluth had applied for: the company recognized $16.3 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.50, which included $16.3 million in tariff refunds contributing $0.44 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS” consensus: “$0.01”; and “IEEPA tariff refund (~$12M). Duluth has applied for refunds, and guidance includes no benefit. Any timing or recognition commentary is upside.”

surprises.description: Duluth raised full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $38–42 million, well above the prior $28–32 million range; the preview identified a raise above the old range as a catalyst but gave no indication of a raise of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $38-42 million from the prior $28-32 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY adj. EBITDA guide ($28–32M). A third consecutive raise is the cleanest re-rating trigger.”

surprises.description: Underlying gross-margin expansion was far stronger than the preview’s expected 200–300 basis points: excluding tariff refunds, margin expanded 490–520 basis points to roughly 59.6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding tariff refunds, underlying gross margin still expanded 490-520 basis points to roughly 59.6%, driven by nearly 6% higher average unit retails and direct factory sourcing savings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Expect the YoY expansion to narrow to roughly +200–300bps.” The preview also listed “Gross margin of 57% or higher” as a catalyst.

surprises.description: Q2 net sales of $121.4 million modestly exceeded the $119.9 million consensus and cleared the preview’s $120 million catalyst threshold, landing near the top of the guidance-implied range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales declined 7.8% to $121.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales” consensus: “$119.9M”; and “Net sales of at least $120M would clear consensus and the top of the implied range.”

surprises.description: Inventory improved substantially again, including a sharp reduction in clearance goods and a much larger share of current products. The preview reported the prior quarter’s inventory decline but did not set an expectation for this quarter’s continued cleanup.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Clearance inventory was cut 43.1% in dollars and 46.6% in units, improving the inventory mix to 85.4% current products versus 77.8% a year ago”; total inventory was “down 15.5% (down $22.9 million) to $125.2 million,” the fifth consecutive quarter of year-over-year improvement.

surprises.description: The company reported a sizable cash and debt improvement that the preview did not discuss: it ended the quarter with no ABL debt and generated $13 million in free cash flow, up $41 million year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ended the quarter with zero debt on its ABL facility (versus $32.5 million a year ago) and generated $13 million in free cash flow, a $41 million year-over-year improvement.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted DTC as a key trajectory to watch, but the reported channel picture included a contracted customer base despite improved retention and NPS. Stores were flat for the first half while DTC sales fell 7.6%, leaving direct notably weaker than stores.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retail stores outperformed direct, delivering flat first-half sales versus a 7.6% DTC decline, though the customer base has contracted as promotions were reset even as retention and NPS (up 11%) improved.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “DTC trajectory. DTC is about 60% of sales. Sequential improvement in its decline is the leading indicator for the H2 guide.”

surprises.description: Management specifically warned that Q3 sales would remain pressured by lapping prior-year clearance events. That near-term caution was not called out in the preview, although the company maintained its H2 sales range and described sequential quarterly improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management warned Q3 top line will remain pressured from lapping prior-year low-margin clearance events, with second-half sales guided to a range of minus 2% to plus 2% and sequential quarterly improvement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The equity story rests on the H2 stabilization. Any softening of this language is the biggest risk.”

surprises.description: Women’s sales fell 15% and AKHG sales fell 26% amid SKU rationalization and exits from low-margin categories such as swimwear. The preview did not flag these specific product and brand declines, though the stated rationale indicates some sales were deliberately shed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Women's product sales fell 15% and AKHG brand sales dropped 26% due to SKU rationalization and exiting low-margin categories like swimwear.”

in_line: The company reaffirmed FY26 net sales guidance of $540–560 million and the H2 sales range of -2% to +2%, as the preview expected.
Excluding tariff refunds, Adjusted EBITDA was $10.7 million, within the preview’s roughly $10–11 million estimate.

surprises.description: Broadcom raised its FY2026 AI revenue target to $58 billion from $56 billion, rather than simply reaffirming the prior target. That is a $2 billion increase to an already expected $56 billion goal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its full-year fiscal 2026 AI revenue guidance to $58 billion ... from the prior $56 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: ... $56B reaffirmed not raised”; the preview also said the bull case involved raising the FY26 AI number above $56B.

surprises.description: Management put a much larger number on its FY2027 AI target: approximately $115 billion, versus the preview’s expectation of only a target above $100 billion. It also extended the outlook to approximately $230 billion in FY2028, with supply secured for both targets—an outlook the preview did not provide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI semiconductor revenue to approximately double to $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and double again to $230 billion in fiscal 2028, with supply already secured for both targets.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 ‘>$100B’ target. Raised, quantified, or merely reaffirmed”; the preview described a specific FY27 figure as a bull-case outcome and gave no FY2028 target.

surprises.description: The Q4 AI revenue guide is $21.7 billion, above the roughly $21 billion implied by the preview’s FY2026 target arithmetic. The preview treated that level as effectively pre-committed, so the guide modestly exceeds the expected run rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 AI revenue guided to $21.7 billion, up 236% year-on-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Q4 AI guide is effectively pre-committed” at “about $21B”; the preview’s base case was “AI ~$21B.”

surprises.description: The call gave an unexpectedly large multi-year customer deployment outlook for Anthropic: 5 gigawatts of TPU v8i in 2027 and another 10 gigawatts in 2028, after 1 gigawatt of Ironwood in 2026. The preview did not identify Anthropic or anticipate this scale of deployment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Anthropic is on track to become Broadcom's largest XPU customer in 2027,” deploying “5 gigawatts of TPU v8i in 2027 and an incremental 10 gigawatts in 2028, after 1 gigawatt of Ironwood in 2026.”

surprises.description: OpenAI’s projected deployment is described at a larger scale than the preview’s limited expectation: more than 5 gigawatts in 2028, with OpenAI projected to become Broadcom’s second-largest XPU customer. The preview had described the roughly $18 billion first phase as stalled and mentioned only 1GW+ deployment in 2027; the call did not say whether the financing issue was resolved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “OpenAI is projected to become Broadcom's second-largest XPU customer, with over 5 gigawatts of deployment in 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The ~$18B first phase reportedly stalled pending a Microsoft offtake commitment of ~40%. Volume XPU deployment is still guided to 1GW+ in 2027.”

surprises.description: Broadcom disclosed a substantial long-term Google TPU agreement, with multiple tens of billions of dollars of TPUs annually over several years. It also said its next-generation TPU v8i is already in production ahead of the prior Ironwood generation; neither development was anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A long-term agreement with Google will deliver multiple tens of billions of dollars of TPUs annually over several years, with next-gen TPU v8i now in production ahead of the prior Ironwood generation.”

surprises.description: Q3 AI semiconductor revenue reached $16.7 billion, above the approximately $16 billion consensus and company guide in the preview. The reported 221% year-over-year growth also exceeded the preview’s 208% expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI semiconductor revenue tripled year-on-year to $16.7 billion in Q3, growing 221% year-over-year and 54% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AI semiconductor revenue ~$16.0B” and “YoY +208%.”

surprises.description: Q4 gross margin is guided to about 73%, below the preview’s roughly 74% margin expectation and its key watch for margin at or above that level. Management attributed the decline to rising XPU and memory mix, while indicating operating margin would remain around 66%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin ... is guided to fall to about 73% in Q4 due to rising XPU and memory mix, though operating margin remains resilient at ~66% from operating leverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin at or above ~74%, and FY27 margin framing”; the preview also listed “Non-GAAP gross margin ~74%.”

surprises.description: Q3 consolidated gross margin was 75%, about one percentage point above the preview’s roughly 74% expectation, despite falling 210 basis points sequentially. The decline was smaller than the roughly 300-basis-point sequential drop cited in the preview’s Q3 guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin declined to 75% in Q3 (down 210 bps sequentially).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin ~74% (–300bps q/q)” and “Company Guide ... gross margin ~74% (–300bps q/q).”

surprises.description: Q3 revenue of $29.6 billion modestly exceeded the $29.43–29.44 billion consensus and the approximately $29.4 billion company guide. The gap was small, rather than the much larger beat described in the preview’s bull scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 FY2026 consolidated revenue reached a record $29.6 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $29.43–29.44B” consensus and “~$29.4B” company guide.

surprises.description: Management said Broadcom is on target to exceed $30 in EPS in FY2028, a long-term earnings milestone not specified in the preview. The preview provided quarterly EPS estimates but no comparable FY2028 EPS expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Broadcom stated it is on target to exceed $30 in earnings per share in fiscal 2028.”

surprises.description: Broadcom reported a record $13.7 billion of free cash flow, equal to 46% of revenue, and said it paid down $5.6 billion of long-term debt and distributed $3.1 billion in dividends. The preview did not set expectations for free cash flow or these capital-allocation amounts.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 free cash flow hit a record $13.7 billion (46% of revenue); the company paid down $5.6 billion of long-term debt, distributed $3.1 billion in dividends.”

surprises.description: Broadcom made an unanticipated competitive claim about OpenAI’s Jalapeno accelerator: that it reportedly outperforms Grace Blackwell Ultra at roughly half the cost of a GPU. The preview discussed OpenAI’s deployment and financing but did not anticipate this product-performance claim.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Its Jalapeno accelerator reportedly outperforms Grace Blackwell Ultra at roughly half the cost of a GPU.”

surprises.description: Management estimated roughly $20–30 billion of Broadcom content per gigawatt of compute deployed, an unanticipated unit-economics disclosure that could help frame the scale of future deployments. The preview gave no comparable estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Estimates roughly $20-30 billion of content per gigawatt of compute deployed.”

in_line: Operating margin was 67.9% in Q3, broadly in line with the preview’s reference to operating margin around 67%; management also said Q4 operating margin would remain around 66% despite lower gross margin.

surprises.description: Americas and Asia organic growth reached 11.6%, above the preview’s >10% bull-case marker, and segment profit rose 43.9% with a 530-basis-point margin expansion. Wire ID growth of nearly 20% helped drive the strength.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Americas and Asia region posted 11.6% organic growth with segment profit up 43.9% to $74.3 million, expanding margins 530 bps to 25.1% (23.7% excluding the tariff benefit), led by wire ID growth of nearly 20%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Sustained growth above [Q3’s +8.2%] supports the bull case”; bull scenario: “Americas organic above 10%.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 52.9%, above the preview’s roughly 52% base case. The roughly $4 million tariff refund boosted the reported figure, but margin still rose 110 basis points excluding one-time items.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved to 52.9% from 50.4%, though this included a ~$4 million tariff refund; adjusting for one-time items, gross margin rose 110 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin ~52%” in the base scenario; the preview also flagged whether engineered-product mix would keep offsetting softness.

surprises.description: Q4 organic sales growth was 8.4%, slightly above the preview’s 7–8% base-case assumption. Total sales grew 10%, including 1.1% from acquisitions and 0.5% from FX.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 2026 total sales grew 10% (8.4% organic, 1.1% acquisitions, 0.5% FX).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Base scenario: “Organic growth ~7–8%.”

surprises.description: Printer unit sales surged 25% in Q4, while high-margin specialty adhesive consumables grew nearly 10% organically and represent over 40% of organic sales. The preview expected engineered-product mix to help, but did not anticipate this specific level of printer growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Printer unit sales surged 25% in Q4 and 10% for the full year, driving high-margin specialty adhesive consumable sales that together represent over 40% of Brady's organic sales and grew nearly 10% organically.”

surprises.description: Europe and Australia’s organic growth was in the expected low-single-digit range, but its segment margin improved to 13.3% from 11%, an improvement not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of the region.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Europe and Australia was notably weaker at just 2.1% organic growth (1.2% for the full year), reflecting persistent manufacturing softness, though segment margin improved to 13.3% from 11%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Continued growth of roughly 1–2% is largely priced in.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a new margin risk from rising input costs, especially memory chips whose prices are shifting quarter to quarter. IPS is responding with price increases, product redesigns, and longer-term supplier contracts, but the cost pressure was not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rising input costs, especially memory chips whose pricing is shifting quarter to quarter, pose a margin headwind,” prompting IPS to “implement price increases, redesign products for alternative memory, and secure long-term supplier contracts.”

in_line: Q4 adjusted diluted EPS was $1.48 versus the preview’s $1.47 consensus.

FY2027 adjusted EPS guidance of $6.25–$6.75 has a $6.50 midpoint, close to the $6.55 consensus and at the preview’s stated $6.50 minimum buy-side bar; the approximately $0.80 of IPS accretion also matched the preview’s expectation.
Europe and Australia organic growth was 2.1%, broadly in line with the preview’s expected roughly 1–2%.
GAAP diluted EPS fell to $0.96 while adjusted EPS rose, with acquisition-related and amortization expenses; the preview had anticipated deal costs pushing GAAP EPS below adjusted EPS.
IPS revenue of about $1.15 billion, low-double-digit segment margins, and roughly $25 million of year-three synergies were consistent with the preview’s acquisition framing.

surprises.description: Adjusted operating income and EPS substantially exceeded the preview’s expectations: operating income was $124 million versus roughly $100 million expected, and EPS was $0.95 versus consensus of about $0.75–$0.77. Both also beat the company’s Q2 guidance ranges.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income surged 125% to $124 million, exceeding the high end of guidance ($90-100M) by $24 million,” and “adjusted EPS nearly tripled to $0.95 from $0.33, beating guidance of $0.65-0.75.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus was “~$100M (implied)” for adjusted operating income and “~$0.75–0.77” for adjusted EPS; Q2 guidance was $90–100 million of adjusted operating income and implied EPS of ~$0.70–0.78.

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year outlook rather than merely reaffirming the June guidance. The new ranges are higher for sales, adjusted operating income, and adjusted EPS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2026 guidance was raised to net sales of $7.10-7.18 billion,” adjusted operating income of “$560-590 million,” and adjusted EPS of “$4.45-4.70.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the existing FY2026 guide was $7.03–7.13B in sales, $550–580M in adjusted operating income, and $4.35–4.60 in adjusted EPS; it noted that “a reaffirmation reads as caution.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin expanded more than the preview’s 240-basis-point repeat benchmark: it rose 320 basis points to 38.8%. Management attributed roughly two-thirds of the expansion to higher merchandise margin from more regular-price selling and fewer promotions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 320 basis points to 38.8%, with roughly two-thirds driven by higher merchandise margin from increased regular-price selling and reduced promotions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether “the 240bp Q1 expansion repeats” and warned that “strategic promotions” or a “competitive environment” could signal margin give-back.

surprises.description: Q2 sales came in slightly below the preview’s consensus estimate, despite landing near the high end of company guidance. The gap was small: $1.611 billion versus consensus of roughly $1.617–1.62 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales increased 10% year-over-year to $1.611 billion, near the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave net sales consensus of “~$1.617–1.62B” and company guidance of “$1.590–1.615B.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed more than $140 million of IEEPA tariff refunds, which were excluded from non-GAAP results but materially boosted cash and left the company with no ABL borrowings. The preview discussed tariff exposure and Q3 tariff assumptions but did not anticipate these refunds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received IEEPA tariff refunds of over $140 million (over 95% of IEEPA tariffs paid), which were excluded from non-GAAP results, boosting the cash balance to $522 million (up $334 million year-over-year) with no ABL borrowings.”

surprises.description: Q3 guidance included positive operating income of $10–20 million in a quarter the preview highlighted as exposed to the full 20% tariff assumption. The preview did not provide a Q3 earnings estimate, so the positive range is a favorable development against the tariff-risk framing rather than a quantified consensus beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for net sales of $1.57-1.60 billion (7-9% growth), with operating income of $10-20 million versus roughly break-even last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q3 is the first fully loaded quarter at the 20% tariff assumption” and that it “matters more to the stock than the Q2 print.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a planned increase in marketing investment, from just over 7% of sales toward the high single digits over the next couple of years. The preview did not flag this spending ramp; it is a new investment commitment that could weigh on margins even as the company funds brand initiatives.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management plans to raise marketing spend from just over 7% of sales toward high single digits over the next couple years, funding investments like the Angels Among Us docu-series and Fashion Show.”

in_line: Comparable sales were up 9%, consistent with the preview’s implied slowdown to roughly 9–11% sales growth; the preview’s key downside concern was comps in the 6% range or below.

surprises.description: Ciena’s adjusted operating margin reached 22.5%, well above the preview’s roughly 19.6% expectation and 250 basis points above company guidance. That is a much larger beat than the preview’s bullish 21% operating-margin whisper.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin more than doubled year-on-year to a record 22.5%, exceeding guidance by 250 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating margin … ~19.6%”; the whisper was “21% operating margin.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $2.11 substantially exceeded both the $1.73 consensus and the more optimistic $1.95 whisper. The beat was especially notable against the preview’s realistic whisper estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS hitting a record $2.11, up 215% year-on-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus … $1.73”; the preview says to treat “~$1.95 EPS as the more realistic whisper.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $1.7 billion beat the $1.64 billion consensus, though it was close to the $1.69 billion whisper and the preview’s $1.70–$1.73 billion bull scenario. It was reported at the top end of guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue reached a record $1.7 billion … at the top end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus $1.64B”; the preview’s whisper was “about $1.69B,” and its bull scenario was “$1.70–1.73B.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin was 46.4%, above the preview’s roughly 45.0% expectation and above its 45.5% level that would support the FY27 earnings case. A one-time tariff-refund benefit contributed 70 basis points, so the reported margin included a temporary boost.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin was 46.4% (including a one-time 70 bps tariff-refund benefit).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin … ~45.0%”; the preview said “45.5% or higher would help the FY27 earnings case.”

surprises.description: Backlog rose by $800 million to $8.5 billion, above the preview’s $8.3 billion buy-side bogey and its $8.2–$8.4 billion base case. Management also said Ciena had booked nearly a full quarter’s orders one month into Q4 and expected backlog above $10 billion at fiscal year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog increased $800 million in Q3 to $8.5 billion”; Ciena expects to exit FY2026 with “over $10 billion in backlog,” having booked “nearly a full quarter’s worth of orders just one month into Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Exit backlog >$8.3B (buy-side bogey)”; the base scenario expected “Backlog $8.2–8.4B.”

surprises.description: Ciena issued a preliminary FY2027 revenue outlook despite the preview saying no formal guide was expected until December. The outlook calls for at least 30% growth to $8.3–$8.4 billion, with management describing that level as a supply-constrained floor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Preliminary fiscal 2027 outlook projecting revenue growth of at least 30% to $8.3–$8.4 billion (a supply-constrained floor).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “No formal guide is expected until December.”

surprises.description: Alongside the unexpected early FY2027 outlook, Ciena projected a record 25–27% operating margin. The preview had no FY2027 margin guidance expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record operating margin of 25–27%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “No formal guide is expected until December.”

surprises.description: Ciena says RLS Hyper-Rail is on track for customer standardization by the end of 2026 and could generate several hundred million dollars of revenue in 2027 at margins above the corporate average. The preview flagged RLS timing as something to watch but did not anticipate this revenue and margin detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RLS Hyper-Rail is on track for customer standardization by end of 2026 and is expected to ramp to several hundred million dollars of revenue in 2027 at margins accretive to the corporate average.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch RLS Hyper-Rail timing” but gave no revenue or margin expectation.

surprises.description: The company reported that “in and around the data center” revenue quadrupled year-to-date, ahead of its 3x target, while interconnects more than doubled. That exceeds the preview’s cited expectation that pluggables would more than double versus 2025, though the metrics are not identical.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Interconnects more than doubled, and ‘in and around the data center’ revenue quadrupled year-to-date, well ahead of the committed 3x growth target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “pluggables (guided to more than double vs. 2025)” and DCOM/data-center wins as items to watch.

surprises.description: Ciena secured negotiated price increases from high single digits to high teens or low 20s on selected existing backlog. The preview did not anticipate these increases, which indicate the company could obtain higher prices even on already-booked business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ciena secured negotiated price increases ranging from high single digits to high-teens/low-20s percent that will selectively apply to existing backlog.”

surprises.description: Ciena also secured long-term agreements for key optical components through 2029, extending supply commitments well beyond the near-term constraint discussion in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New long-term supply agreements securing key optical components through 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified pump lasers and DSP-based modems as supply constraints and asked how much backlog would convert in FY2027 versus FY2028; it did not mention agreements extending through 2029.

surprises.description: Management expects to raise combined optical systems and plug market share by about four points to roughly 30% in Q4, a specific gain not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Expects to raise combined optical systems and plug market share by about 4 points to roughly 30% in Q4.”

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted operating-margin outlook was raised to 20–21%, with Ciena expecting to exceed 20% annually for the first time. The preview gave a Q3 margin bogey but did not set an annual margin expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lifting full-year adjusted operating margin to 20–21%, exceeding 20% annually for the first time in company history.”

in_line: The FY2026 revenue midpoint rose to $6.42 billion, broadly matching the preview’s expectation that Ciena would raise its $6.3 billion guide to $6.4 billion or more. The $1.75 billion Q4 revenue midpoint was also close to the preview’s roughly $1.78 billion implication.

surprises.description: The full-year adjusted EPS guide of $1.65–$1.80 was substantially below the preview’s $1.90 FY27 consensus and matched its bear-case range, rather than the base-case $1.80–$1.90. The call also described a sharp Q1 decline, with EPS turning positive only in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was set at $1.65 to $1.80, with a sharp Q1 decline expected and EPS turning positive only by Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 adjusted EPS: Street $1.90”; the base scenario expected “$1.80–$1.90,” while the bear scenario expected “$1.65–$1.80 or no guide.”

surprises.description: The dividend was reduced, contrary to the preview’s expectation that it would be maintained or affirmed. Management described the cut as necessary.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management confirmed the dividend was reduced as a necessary decision.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base and bull scenarios assumed the “dividend held” or “dividend affirmed,” and it called for “unambiguous maintenance.”

surprises.description: The full-year organic sales outlook of approximately 3% down was weaker than the preview’s cited FY26 guide of down 2% to 1%, which management had already steered toward the lower end. The preview also calculated that the existing outlook implied Q4 organic sales roughly flat to slightly positive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Campbell's guided to fiscal 2026 organic net sales down approximately 3% at the midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adjusted EPS $2.15–$2.25 and organic net sales −2% to −1%, with management pointing to the lower end”; the preview calculated “Q4 organic roughly flat to slightly positive.”

surprises.description: Snacks were expected to fall high single digits in Q1, with margin recovery delayed until the second half, and management did not expect Snacks consumption to return to positive growth during the fiscal year. That is weaker near-term segment commentary than the preview’s base case of Snacks margin holding near 10–11% and its focus on a path back toward the low-to-mid teens.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Snacks are expected to decline high single digits in Q1, hurt by lapping prior holiday shipments ahead of consumption and new trade investment, with margin recovery not occurring until the second half”; management “does not expect Snacks consumption to return to positive growth this fiscal year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “Snacks margin holds near 10–11%”; the catalyst checklist called for a “stated path back toward the low-to-mid teens.”

surprises.description: Campbell’s announced a new $500 million savings program for fiscal 2027–2030, including $350 million of incremental savings. The preview had discussed a pulled-forward $100 million SG&A program as a possible inflation offset, but did not anticipate this larger, longer-term program.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new $500 million cost savings program running from fiscal 2027 to 2030,” including “$150 million rolled over from the prior peak program and $350 million of incremental savings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch how inflation is covered by “productivity and the pulled-forward $100M SG&A program.”

surprises.description: Interest expense was projected to rise by about $25 million year over year, adding a cost burden tied to the La Regina acquisition debt and refinancing. The preview flagged balance-sheet language and a possible hybrid instrument, but did not anticipate this specific increase in interest expense.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Interest expense is projected to be roughly $25 million higher year-over-year, driven by the La Regina acquisition debt and refinancing of a $500 million bond maturing in March, with a hybrid issuance under consideration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted debt and leverage, and said to watch for “any hybrid instrument announcement”; it did not cite an expected increase in interest expense.

surprises.description: Although the preview expected total inflation of 5–6%, the call specified logistics inflation running around double digits before easing later in the year. That points to a particularly severe near-term cost pressure within an otherwise expected overall inflation range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cost inflation of plus 5% to 6% throughout the year, with logistics inflation running around double digits before easing later in the year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected “5–6% total inflation (about 3% base plus 2–3% incremental from geopolitical disruption and oil).”

in_line: The projected 5–6% total cost inflation matched the preview’s expected 5–6% inflation range.
The company had already been expected to take price increases; the call confirmed that posture and quantified the increases at 4–5% across about 60% of the portfolio.

surprises.description: The preview centered on a FY2027 revenue outlook near $995 million, but the company provided no FY2027 guidance. Management said it would wait until a permanent CFO is onboarded, leaving the revenue outlook unresolved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company will not provide guidance until a permanent CFO is onboarded.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2027 revenue guidance vs. ~$995M consensus”; the preview also listed the bear case as “<$950M or withheld.”

surprises.description: Q4 gross margin was 8.0%, 150 basis points below the preview’s 9.5% benchmark and below its 8.5% caution threshold. The improvement from a year earlier was substantial, but it fell short of the margin level the preview said investors would be watching for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 gross profit surged 140% to $19.5 million with gross margin expanding to 8.0% from 3.8% in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin, against 9.5%”; “Below 8.5% puts the operating leverage story in question.”

surprises.description: Q4 awards were only $169 million, below the preview’s roughly $200 million base case and its roughly $220 million backlog-flat threshold; book-to-bill was 0.7x versus the 0.8x base case. Backlog ended at $953 million, and management said it needs to replenish it for the back half of FY2027 and FY2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 project awards totaled $169 million for a weak 0.7x book-to-bill, with backlog ending at $953 million”; management flagged “a need to replenish backlog for the back half of fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 awards vs. the ~$220M backlog-flat threshold”; the base scenario was “~$200M / 0.8x.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $244.5 million came in below the $247 million consensus estimate, although it remained above the preview’s $241 million guidance floor. This was a modest shortfall rather than a miss of the stated floor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue rose 13% to $244.5 million from $216.4 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $247.0M (+14.2% YoY)” and “Revenue vs. $241M (guidance floor).”

surprises.description: Results across segments were uneven: Utility and Power Infrastructure reached a 12.8% margin and Storage/Terminal reached 6.4%, while Process and Industrial Facilities’ margin fell to 2.9% and revenue declined to $33.6 million from $47.3 million. The preview did not flag this segment-level divergence.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Utility and Power Infrastructure improving to 12.8% and Storage/Terminal at 6.4%, while Process and Industrial Facilities fell to 2.9% and revenue dropped to $33.6 million from $47.3 million.”

surprises.description: The company reported $3.4 million of restructuring costs in Q4, which the preview did not anticipate. Management said future restructuring costs should be insignificant, limiting the expected continuation of this expense.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$3.4 million of restructuring costs hit Q4 but future restructuring is expected to be insignificant.”

surprises.description: Matrix was selected for FEED work on America First Refining’s Brownsville storage tank farm, with a larger project award potentially converting to backlog in late Q3 or early Q4 FY2027 if FID occurs. The preview did not mention this specific opportunity, and the potential award remains conditional rather than booked.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Matrix was selected for the FEED on America First Refining's storage tank farm in Brownsville, Texas, with the larger project award potentially converting to backlog in late Q3 or early Q4 fiscal 2027 pending FID.”

surprises.description: Management cited an opportunity pipeline exceeding $7 billion, with more than 40% in LNG and NGL projects. The preview discussed backlog and the need for awards to support growth, but did not report an expectation for a pipeline of this size or composition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The opportunity pipeline exceeds $7 billion, with over 40% comprised of LNG and NGL projects.”

surprises.description: The company said it is actively evaluating a stock buyback, an unexpected capital-allocation possibility given the preview did not anticipate a repurchase program. No buyback commitment or amount was announced.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $283.9 million in total liquidity ($223 million unrestricted cash) and no outstanding debt, and is actively evaluating a stock buyback.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EPS was $0.26, slightly above the preview’s $0.25 estimate. The beat was small.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EPS of $0.26, a $1.19 improvement.”

in_line: Q4 adjusted EPS was $0.16, close to the preview’s approximately $0.17 consensus and within its cited $0.15–$0.18 estimate range.
The preview noted that the CFO was departing; the call confirmed Kevin Cavanah’s departure and named an interim CFO.

surprises.description: Lands’ End’s gross margin reached 52%, substantially above the preview’s roughly 47.5% base-case estimate. The 320-basis-point year-over-year expansion was driven primarily by an IEPA tariff refund, so the outperformance was not entirely from recurring operations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanding approximately 320 basis points to 52%, primarily driven by the IEPA tariff refund.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: ... gross margin about 47.5%”; the bull scenario expected “gross margin ≥48.5%.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was cut to $62–70 million from $68–78 million, putting even the new range’s low end below the preview’s stated $68 million bear-trigger threshold. This was a weaker outlook than the preview’s expected neutral narrowing of revenue guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2026 guidance calls for ... adjusted EBITDA of $62-$70 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “An EBITDA cut below $68M is the bear trigger.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $11 million, at the bottom of the quarterly guidance range and below the preview’s $12–13.5 million base case. It fell $4 million year over year as tariff-refund benefits were offset by the new WHP JV royalty structure and warehouse-system disruptions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA fell $4 million year-over-year to $11 million, as tariff refund benefits were offset by the new WHP JV royalty structure and warehouse management system disruptions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave an “Adj. EBITDA” guide of “$11.0–14.0M” and a base scenario of “$12–13.5M.”

surprises.description: The higher full-year adjusted EPS outlook contrasts with the EBITDA cut: the new $0.44–0.72 range is above the prior $0.32–0.65 range at both ends. The preview did not anticipate an EPS guide increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2026 guidance calls for ... adjusted EPS of $0.44-$0.72.”

surprises.description: The reported 9% growth in U.S. e-commerce did not reflect underlying acceleration: management said Q1 backlog catch-up inflated the quarter, while year-to-date U.S. e-commerce growth was essentially flat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. e-commerce sales grew 9% year-over-year, but management disclosed this was inflated by Q1 backlog catch-up, with underlying year-to-date U.S. e-commerce growth essentially flat.”

surprises.description: Third-party marketplace revenue fell roughly 20% as the company prioritized profitability, while like-for-like gross margin improved by more than 500 basis points. The preview did not flag this revenue-and-margin trade-off.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Third-party marketplace revenue declined roughly 20% as the company prioritized profitability, yet like-for-like gross margin improved over 500 basis points year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Warehouse-system problems continued to delay school-uniform shipments and increase backlog, indicating that shipment disruption persisted into Q2. Management said throughput is now normal or higher and does not expect a Q3/Q4 guidance impact beyond Outfitters catch-up.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Warehouse management system issues delayed school uniform shipments and raised backlog,” but “operations are now running at normal or higher throughput with no expected impact on Q3/Q4 guidance beyond Outfitters catch-up.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “DC systems rollout delayed Q1 shipments” and identified “Shipment recapture” as a bull-case driver.

surprises.description: ABL borrowings were $60 million, up from the roughly $30 million cited at the end of Q1, even though WHP proceeds had repaid the term loan. The term-loan repayment reduced interest expense, partly offsetting the higher ABL balance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ABL borrowings increased to $60 million from $35 million a year ago, though the $300 million WHP Global proceeds were used to fully repay the term loan, reducing interest expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ABL borrowings were about $30M.”

surprises.description: The company repurchased approximately 900,000 shares for about $11 million in the quarter, an unanticipated use of capital in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased approximately 900,000 shares for about $11 million in Q2, leaving $89 million remaining on its $100 million buyback authorization through March 2029.”

in_line: Q2 revenue was $302 million, within the $290–310 million guidance range and the preview’s $298–305 million base scenario.
Q2 adjusted net income of $2.7 million and adjusted EPS of $0.09 were within the previewed guidance ranges of $2–5 million and $0.06–0.16, respectively.
Full-year revenue guidance narrowed to $1.3–1.35 billion, as the preview said was likely and expected to be neutral.

Inventory rose 13% year over year, close to the preview’s cited 14% increase; it remained above 10%, with management attributing the increase largely to an intentionally lean prior-year position and tariff headwinds.
Capital expenditure guidance remained roughly $40 million, consistent with the preview.

surprises.description: Ambarella guided to Q3 revenue of $115M–$124M, a $119.5M midpoint, well above the preview’s derived estimate of about $114M. The preview associated a midpoint below $112M with pressure on the full-year consensus math.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 FY2027 revenue guidance is $115M-$124M ($119.5M midpoint)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A Q3 near $114M”; “A Q3 midpoint below about $112M would push the full year toward the low end of the range.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was 59.3%, below the preview’s roughly 59.8% consensus expectation and the midpoint of the company’s 59.0%–60.5% guidance range. Management said it plans to pass rising supply-chain costs to customers to maintain its long-term margin target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin was 59.3%, below the guidance midpoint, and management plans to pass rising supply chain costs to customers to maintain its long-term 59%-62% gross margin target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin … ~59.8%”; company guidance was “59.0% – 60.5%.”

surprises.description: Inventory days rose further to 157, rather than stabilizing near the 145-day level the preview identified as the expected benchmark. This deepens the inventory concern flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory days rose from 145 to 157 days.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Days need to stabilize at about 145.”

surprises.description: Ambarella raised its five-year serviceable-market growth estimate from about 18% to about 20% CAGR, and said IoT markets now make up about 70% of the terminal-year market, primarily because of edge-infrastructure AI SoCs and standalone accelerators. The preview did not anticipate this larger market outlook or the shift in its mix.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised its 5-year serviceable market (SAM) forecast … to a ~20% CAGR, up from the prior ~18% CAGR estimate”; “IoT markets now represent about 70% of the terminal year.”

surprises.description: Ambarella signed two seven-year indirect-channel partnerships, each expected to generate approximately $0.5 billion in revenue. The preview did not flag these agreements, though meaningful revenue is not expected for two to three years.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Signed two 7-year indirect channel partnerships (Capgemini and Macnica), each expected to generate approximately $0.5 billion in revenue, though meaningful revenue is 2-3 years away.”

surprises.description: The company introduced a standalone AI-accelerator product line and previewed the X7 SoC, with specific low-memory and low-power capabilities for running large language models. This product initiative was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Introduced a new standalone AI accelerator product line, previewing the X7 SoC (currently in simulation), which requires only 4MB of memory and a 4-5 watt power envelope to run large language models as an AI coprocessor.”

surprises.description: The board authorized a new $50 million share-repurchase program, an unexpected capital-allocation action. No shares were repurchased during Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The board authorized a new $50 million share repurchase program valid through June 30, 2027, though no shares were repurchased during Q2.”

surprises.description: A customer cancelled an automotive-autonomy development project, leading to a $9 million reduction in GAAP R&D expense. The expense reduction does not affect the non-GAAP outlook, but the project cancellation was not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $9 million reduction in GAAP R&D expense was recognized from the cancellation of an automotive autonomy customer's development project, with no impact on non-GAAP outlook.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $108.1M was close to the $108M guidance midpoint and within the preview’s range of consensus estimates; non-GAAP EPS of $0.18 was also broadly in line with the preview’s $0.17 consensus and $0.17–$0.19 base-case range.

Memory-price inflation and possible shortages were already identified as risks in the preview. Management reported a small revenue impact in Q2 and Q3 and uncertainty for Q4, broadly confirming that flagged risk.

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $231.7 million, just below the company’s $232 million guidance floor and well below the preview’s $242.1 million Street estimate. Comps fell 6.3%, weaker than the preview’s base-case expectation of a 3%–5% decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales fell to $231.7 million from $262.8 million a year ago, with comparable sales declining 6.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q2 FY26 Guidance | $232–240M”; “Street | ~$242.1M.” The base scenario expected “Comps -3% to -5%.”

surprises.description: The quarter’s 38.7% reported gross margin depended on the tariff refund: excluding it, gross margin was 33.9%, down 170 basis points because of targeted promotions. The preview did not flag a decline in underlying Q2 gross margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 gross margin rose to 38.7% from 35.6%, but excluding the tariff refund, gross margin declined 170 basis points to 33.9% due to targeted promotions.”

surprises.description: The store optimization program is essentially complete after 177 closures, and management expects about $40 million of expense savings in fiscal 2026. The preview did not discuss this program or savings outlook, making this a new cost-reduction update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The store optimization program is essentially complete with 177 total closures, ending Q2 with 457 stores versus 575 a year ago, and is expected to deliver ~$40 million in expense savings in fiscal 2026.”

surprises.description: Paid revenue grew by double digits despite lower spend, while the mobile app reached nearly 40% of digital revenue and converts at roughly seven times desktop/mobile web rates. The preview did not set expectations for these digital-channel results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Paid revenue grew double digits on lower spend, now representing 12% of digital revenue (up from 9%), while the mobile app hit an all-time high of nearly 40% of digital revenue and converts at roughly 7x desktop/mobile web rates.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA excluding the $11.1 million tariff-refund benefit was $12.1 million, within the preview’s cited Q2 guidance of $12–16 million; the refund amount also falls within the preview’s stated Phase 1 and Phase 2 claim ranges.

The company kept underlying full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance at $65–75 million and net sales guidance at $940–960 million, consistent with the preview’s base-case expectation of reaffirmation. The headline adjusted EBITDA range rose to $76–86 million because of the refund, a possibility the preview explicitly identified in its bull scenario.

Management’s expectation of a return to comparable-sales growth in the back half is consistent with the preview’s anticipated back-half recovery. July comps turned positive and all 11 marketing channels improved sequentially.

Sub-brand performance was broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of growth from about 7% to 12% of sales: the call reported approximately 74% year-to-date growth and a 2026 target of $110 million, or about 12% of net sales.
An Investor Day was expected next month; the call announced it would be held in New York next month.

surprises.description: Braze reported Q2 revenue of $227 million, above the preview’s roughly $220.4 million consensus and the company’s $219.5–$220.5 million guidance. That is a clear beat against the expected result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached $227 million, up 26% year-over-year and 8% sequentially, exceeding guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … Consensus ~$220.4M”; “Company guidance (Q2, May 27, 2026) $219.5M – $220.5M.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY27 revenue guidance to $910–$913 million, above the preview’s consensus of about $898.7 million and its stated catalyst level of more than $905 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year revenue guidance to $910-913 million (~23% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 revenue … Consensus $898.65M”; “FY27 revenue guide above $905M, meaning a raise beyond the beat.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating income reached $22 million, versus the preview’s approximately $17.5 million consensus. The 9.7% margin and full-year plan for at least 400 basis points of margin gains also indicate stronger profitability than the preview’s focus on a flat-margin base case suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income surged to $22 million (9.7% margin) from $6 million (3.4%) a year ago”; “on track for at least 400 bps of full-year margin gains.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income … Consensus ~$17.5M”; base scenario: “margin flat.”

surprises.description: Current RPO was $691 million, up 24% year over year—above the preview’s roughly 20–22% expectation and its approximately $670 million catalyst level. Management nevertheless attributed the growth deceleration partly to seasonal renewal timing and lapping the OfferFit acquisition, while investors repeatedly raised the metric in Q&A.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Current RPO growth decelerated to 24% year-over-year ($691 million) partly due to seasonal renewal timing and lapping the OfferFit acquisition, a point of investor concern raised repeatedly in Q&A.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “cRPO at or above ~$670M (about +20% YoY)”; base scenario: “cRPO ~20–22%.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was 68.6%, above the preview’s 67.4% threshold to watch after the prior-quarter margin miss. It still declined from 69.3% a year earlier, but the sequential level was better than the preview’s stabilization test.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin declined slightly to 68.6% from 69.3% year-over-year due to premium messaging volumes and Decisioning Studio headcount.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Holding at or above 67.4% is the threshold to watch”; “Non-GAAP gross margin at or above 67.4%.”

surprises.description: Retention moved differently across customer cohorts: large-customer DBNR improved to 112%, above the preview’s 111% marker, but overall trailing 12-month DBNR stayed flat at 110% rather than showing the recovery the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Dollar-based net retention for large customers ($500K+ annually) rose 100 basis points to 112%, while overall trailing 12-month DBNR held flat at 110%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Dollar-based net retention of 111% would confirm the retention recovery.”

surprises.description: Paid adoption of Braze’s AI tools reached about one-third of large customers and increased roughly 900 basis points from Q1. The preview identified AI as both an upsell opportunity and a central bear-case debate, but gave no adoption benchmark; the reported uptake provides concrete evidence of paid adoption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Paid adoption of Braze's AI tools reached roughly one-third of the large customer cohort, up about 900 basis points from Q1.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management's AI Decisioning Studio … is the main upsell lever, and the AI-disruption debate is the core bear case.”

surprises.description: Braze announced a three-year strategic collaboration agreement with AWS that includes co-sell incentives and marketplace procurement, a commercial partnership not identified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed a 3-year strategic collaboration agreement with AWS establishing co-sell incentives and marketplace procurement.”

in_line: BrazeAI Decisioning Studio generated $6.6 million, up about 16% from Q1’s $5.7 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation that it would grow 15–20% quarter over quarter.
Braze completed a $50 million accelerated share repurchase, matching the preview’s expectation that about $50 million of the $100 million authorization would be executed via ASR.

surprises.description: ABM raised its FY26 adjusted EPS outlook rather than merely reaffirming it: the new $3.95–$4.10 range has a slightly higher midpoint than the prior $3.85–$4.15 range. That is a positive change against the preview’s focus on a possible low-end reaffirmation or cut.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS midpoint to a range of $3.95 to $4.10.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EPS guide language. Reaffirm, narrow to the low end, or cut.”

surprises.description: Revenue came in slightly below the preview’s $2.32 billion estimate, and reported year-over-year growth was 4.2% versus the expected 4.6%. The gap was small, while adjusted EPS matched the $1.04 consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record quarterly revenue of slightly above $2.3 billion, up 4.2% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Technical Solutions fell short of expectations because an important microgrid client deferred roughly $15 million of projects, despite the preview’s expectation of a higher-margin H2 project mix. Management expects the deferred work to resume, with double-digit organic ATS growth and an 11%–13% operating margin in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Technical Solutions revenue missed expectations due to roughly $15 million in project deferrals from an important microgrid client,” with management “expecting double-digit organic ATS growth and 11%-13% operating margin in Q4 as deferred work resumes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management promised a higher-margin project mix in H2 off a ~$500M backlog.”

surprises.description: Free cash flow improved sharply and ABM raised its reported FY26 FCF guidance to about $210 million from $185 million. That is better than the preview’s roughly $250 million figure when its noted $65 million of costs are taken into account, though the figures are not directly comparable because the preview stated its estimate excluding those costs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Year-to-date free cash flow improved by over $150 million to $199.6 million,” and ABM “lifted reported free cash flow guidance to approximately $210 million from $185 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 FCF: ~$250M (ex ~$65M transformation/earn-out/integration).”

surprises.description: ABM reached its sub-3x leverage goal a quarter earlier than planned, rather than waiting until year-end as the preview’s watchpoint implied. The newly closed $300 million accounts receivable facility helped support the reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total debt to pro forma adjusted EBITDA fell to 2.9x, achieving the sub-3x leverage goal a quarter ahead of plan,” supported by “a newly closed $300 million accounts receivable facility.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Leverage was 3.2x at Q2 against a stated target below 3.0x at year-end.”

surprises.description: B&I revenue declined 2.6% amid a large U.K. client exit and West Coast losses, and management said organic growth is not expected to return until mid-FY27. That points to a prolonged recovery beyond the preview’s discussion of the TfL headwind and record bookings as an offset.
surprises.fact_evidence: “B&I revenue declined 2.6% due to a large U.K. client exit and West Coast losses,” with “organic growth not expected to return until mid-fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The TfL contract exit is a roughly 300 bps H2 headwind. Record H1 bookings of $1.2B offset this.”

surprises.description: Despite B&I’s revenue decline, its operating margin expanded by 30 basis points to 7.4%; the preview focused on growth and bookings but did not flag this margin improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating margin expanded 30 basis points to 7.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “B&I organic growth and bookings.”

surprises.description: Aviation grew 12%, but its operating margin compressed to 5.6% as airlines sought cost relief amid elevated jet fuel costs. The preview did not flag this margin pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Aviation grew 12% to $328.1 million but operating margin compressed to 5.6% from 6.8% as airlines sought cost relief amid elevated jet fuel costs.”

surprises.description: M&D revenue rose 18% (8% organically), while its margin was weighed down by nearly $4 million of incremental WGNSTAR amortization. The reported margin was 8.4%, compared with 9.2% excluding that amortization; the preview did not anticipate this cost effect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “M&D revenue rose 18% to $481 million (8% organic) but margin declined to 8.4% from 8.9% due to nearly $4 million in incremental WGNSTAR amortization; excluding amortization, margin was 9.2%.”

surprises.description: Semiconductor, microgrid, and data-center work had become a substantial and fast-growing business, with nearly $775 million in year-to-date revenue and double-digit blended operating margins. The preview did not call out this scale or growth profile.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Semiconductor, microgrids, and data centers generated nearly $775 million in revenue year-to-date, growing 26% organically (about 40% including WGNSTAR) and now representing more than 11% of total revenue with double-digit blended operating margins.”

surprises.description: WGNSTAR was tracking well above its guided $120–$130 million annualized revenue, and ABM had already completed two to three cross-sells. The preview did not discuss WGNSTAR’s revenue trajectory or cross-selling progress.
surprises.fact_evidence: “WGNSTAR is tracking well above its guided $120-130 million annualized revenue,” and management “has already completed 2-3 cross-sells.”

in_line: Adjusted EPS was $1.04 per diluted share, matching the preview’s $1.04 consensus estimate.
