surprises.description: Q1 net sales were $112.6 million, up 32.3% year over year—well above the company’s 15%–20% guidance and the preview’s roughly $98.7 million consensus, and even above the preview’s $102.1 million guide high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 net sales grew 32.3% year-over-year to $112.6 million, well above the company's June guidance of 15% to 20% growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales… Company guidance… +15–20% YoY (~$97.9–102.1M); Consensus ~$98.7M.” The preview also called a result “above the $102M guide high end” the clean upside threshold.

surprises.description: Instead of the roughly $0.055-per-share loss expected, SWBI reported $0.06 EPS and $2.6 million of net income; adjusted EBITDA also grew 86%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EPS turned positive to $0.06 (net income of $2.6 million) versus a loss of $0.08 ($3.4 million net loss) in the prior-year quarter, while adjusted EBITDA grew 86%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS… Consensus ~$(0.055).”

surprises.description: Handgun ASPs rose nearly 9% year over year rather than declining as the preview expected; long gun ASPs also rose sharply, including nearly 11% sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Handgun ASPs were up nearly 9% year-over-year (flat sequentially), while long gun ASPs rose over 18% year-over-year and nearly 11% sequentially, driven by favorable mix and limited promotions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Handgun ASP… Down ~5% in Q1.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 28.7%, above the preview’s 27.9% upper estimate, but most of the year-over-year improvement came from a one-time tariff refund rather than recurring operations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin of 28.7% was up 280 basis points year-over-year, but 260 basis points came from a one-time $2.9 million tariff refund.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin… Company guidance +100–200bps YoY (26.9–27.9%); Consensus ~27%.”

surprises.description: Shipments of 1854 lever action rifles doubled year over year, expanding SWBI’s presence in the higher-priced hunting segment; the preview did not identify this product line as a specific driver to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “1854 lever action rifle shipments doubled versus last year, expanding the company's foothold in the higher-priced hunting segment.”

in_line: Management maintained FY27 revenue growth guidance of 5%–7%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the prior full-year guide could be reaffirmed.
New products were 35% of shipments, above the preview’s roughly 30% concern threshold, though below the 38% reported in Q4.

Capex was elevated for the Springfield facility and advanced manufacturing, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a significant FY27 investment increase; the preview had also flagged capex and dividend coverage as items to watch.

surprises.description: Q3 sales were $1.23 billion, above the preview’s roughly $1.19–$1.20 billion consensus, and grew 8.4% versus the preview’s mid-single-digit quarterly sales outlook. This was a clear upside to the sales expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 net sales grew 8.4% to $1.23 billion (6.2% organically).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales ~$1.19–1.20B”; “Q3 specifically guided to mid-single-digit sales growth.”

surprises.description: Toro raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $4.60–$4.65, lifting the midpoint by over $0.07. The preview emphasized that investors needed a raise and treated a narrow-and-hold as the most likely outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $4.60-$4.65 (midpoint $4.63) from the prior $4.50-$4.62, lifting the midpoint by over $0.07.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A narrow-and-hold at $4.50–$4.62 is the most likely source of a negative reaction”; “the buy-side needs a raise.”

surprises.description: FY2026 net sales growth guidance rose to 6.3%–6.6% from 4%–6.5%, a stronger outlook than the preview’s standing guidance. The preview discussed an EPS raise but did not anticipate this sales-guidance increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year net sales growth guidance was raised and narrowed to 6.3%-6.6% from the prior 4%-6.5% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales growth +4.0% to +6.5%.”

surprises.description: Professional operating margin fell 40 basis points to 20.9%, contrary to the preview’s expectation that it would hold roughly flat or better. The call attributed the decline to product mix, higher manufacturing costs, and Tornado acquisition dilution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The professional segment grew net sales 8.8% (6.1% organic) but adjusted operating margin declined 40 basis points to 20.9% due to product mix, higher manufacturing costs, and Tornado acquisition dilution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Holding margin roughly flat or better despite tariffs supports the ‘AMP plus price offsets tariffs’ thesis.”

surprises.description: Residential sales grew 8.6%: well above the preview’s roughly flat full-year residential outlook, but short of the double-digit rebound the preview identified as the largest upside swing factor. The call also reported a 400-basis-point margin improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The residential segment grew net sales 8.6% and improved adjusted operating margin by 400 basis points year-over-year to 5.9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Residential roughly flat”; “a double-digit rebound is the largest upside swing factor.”

surprises.description: The AMP productivity program had already reached its $125 million run-rate savings target, with additional in-year benefits expected to carry into fiscal 2027. The preview discussed AMP as part of the tariff-offset thesis but did not anticipate that the target had already been reached or that benefits would extend into FY2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The AMP productivity program has already reached its $125 million run-rate savings target, with unrealized in-year benefits expected to carry into fiscal 2027 for continued margin expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “AMP plus price offsets tariffs.”

surprises.description: The tax rate was 22.4%, versus the preview’s roughly 21.7% expectation, and the call said the higher rate reduced Q3 EPS by $0.08. That was a larger tax headwind than the preview’s estimated roughly $0.04 EPS impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 EPS benefited from $0.12 in operational performance, $0.05 from buybacks, and $0.06 from tariff refunds, partially offset by an $0.08 higher tax rate (22.4%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Tax rate ~21.7% (+300bps, ~$0.04 EPS headwind).”

surprises.description: Anticipated IEEPA tariff refunds in guidance were cut from $12 million to $7 million, with $5 million removed from Q4 residential margin. This was an adverse update to the preview’s tariff-refund and Q4 mitigation outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Anticipated IEEPA tariff refunds in guidance were reduced to $7 million from $12 million, with $5 million reclassified outside Phase 2 and removed from Q4 residential margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross tariffs are ~$120M for FY2026, with ~$20M in expected refunds”; “Confirmation that mitigation lands in Q4 is the key test.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $1.33 was slightly above the preview’s $1.30 consensus and just above the top of its $1.29–$1.32 range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 net sales grew 8.4% to $1.23 billion (6.2% organically) with adjusted EPS of $1.33.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS $1.30 (range $1.29–$1.32, 5 analysts).”

in_line: Year-to-date free cash flow conversion was 128%, above the preview’s ≥120% conversion benchmark; the preview also noted 124.5% conversion in the first half.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $216.4 million, above the $215 million top of the guide and $214.15 million consensus. The beat was modest, but revenue also accelerated from Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY27 revenue was $216.4 million, up 10% year-over-year, accelerating from Q1 and exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 revenue guidance of “$213–215M” and consensus of “$214.15M”; its base scenario was “$215–216M.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating margin reached 10%, above the preview’s roughly 8.9% consensus and the 9.3% top of guidance. This was a stronger Q2 margin result than the preview anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin was 10%, expanding roughly 300 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 non-GAAP operating margin guidance of “8.5%–9.3%” and consensus of “~8.9%.”

surprises.description: AI Studio and AI teammates contributed about 25% of net-new ARR, well above the 15% full-year target and up from 17% last quarter. More than a quarter of $100,000+ customers had also bought these products, indicating faster enterprise adoption than the preview’s base case implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI Studio and AI teammates drove approximately 25% of net new ARR (about 22% excluding one large deal), up from 17% last quarter and above the 15% full-year target set in March”; “Over 25% of customers spending $100,000+ have now purchased AI Studio or an AI teammate.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 AI bookings were “17% of net-new ARR, against a 15% full-year target” and described the base case as AI being framed “only as a percentage of net-new ARR, with modest NRR improvement.”

surprises.description: The supplied call facts give AI’s share of net-new ARR but no absolute AI ARR figure, despite the preview identifying a hard dollar figure as an expected disclosure to watch for.
surprises.fact_evidence: The reported AI metric is that AI products drove “approximately 25% of net new ARR”; no absolute AI ARR figure is provided in the supplied call facts.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Watch for a hard AI Studio and Teammates ARR number,” and listed “A disclosed AI ARR number” as a catalyst.

surprises.description: NRR for customers spending $100,000+ rose to 98% from 96%, reaching the preview’s 98% NRR marker in this high-value cohort. This was stronger than the preview’s base case of only modest NRR improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Core customer NRR and $100,000+ customer NRR both reaching 98% (the latter up from 96%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “A further gain to 98% would be the clearest sign that AI attach is offsetting product-led-growth drag,” and gave “NRR 96–97%” in its base scenario.

surprises.description: Asana signed its largest AI expansion deal to date, with AI products accounting for nearly half of the contract value. The preview anticipated an AI contribution update but did not flag a deal of this scale or composition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed its largest AI expansion deal ever, a 3-year multimillion-dollar agreement with a Fortune 500 media company, with AI products representing nearly half of total contract value.”

surprises.description: U.S. revenue returned to double-digit growth for the first time in more than two years, and the technology vertical grew for a second consecutive quarter. The preview did not cover these geographic or vertical trends.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.S. revenue grew 10% year-over-year, returning to double-digit growth for the first time in over two years, while the technology vertical posted a second consecutive quarter of growth.”

surprises.description: Gross margin fell about 120 basis points sequentially to 87%, with higher AI infrastructure costs and AI product mix contributing. The preview discussed StackAI operating-margin pressure but did not flag this Q2 gross-margin decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin declined about 120 basis points sequentially to 87%, driven by higher AI infrastructure costs (80 bps), the Stack AI addition (30 bps), and mix shift toward AI products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed “StackAI carries an expected drag of about 1 point on operating margin in Q2 and the second half,” but gave no Q2 gross-margin decline expectation.

surprises.description: The shift to consumption-based AI revenue recognition and AWM packaging adds a $1.2 million second-half revenue timing headwind and about 150 basis points of second-half gross-margin pressure, a new quantified cost to the outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The transition to consumption-based AI revenue recognition and AWM packaging creates a $1.2 million second-half revenue timing headwind, split between Q3 and Q4, plus about 150 bps of second-half gross margin pressure.”

surprises.description: FY27 revenue guidance did not rise above its existing $863.5 million ceiling, despite the Q2 beat and the preview’s focus on a raise as a key catalyst. The low end moved up, but the unchanged top end fell short of the preview’s stated raise scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY27 revenue guidance is $858.5 million to $863.5 million (9% growth at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a raise “would need FY27 revenue above the current $863.5M top end” and listed “FY27 revenue guide above $863.5M” as a catalyst.

surprises.description: Management quantified a worsening PLG growth drag—about 100 basis points in Q3 and 150 basis points in Q4—and assumed no revenue contribution from five new products. The preview noted PLG drag but did not anticipate this quantified second-half burden or the explicit zero contribution assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: The guidance commentary said “the PLG headwind” is expected to weigh on growth by “~100 bps in Q3 and ~150 bps in Q4,” with “no revenue contribution assumed from the five new products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described NRR as a way to assess whether AI attach is “offsetting product-led-growth drag” and identified self-serve hedging as a bear-case concern.

in_line: Overall NRR improved to 97% from 96%, within the preview’s 96–97% base-case range.
The FY27 revenue-guidance midpoint is approximately $861 million, essentially in line with the preview’s $860.8 million consensus.

surprises.description: Planet Labs reported Q2 revenue of $116 million, well above the roughly $105 million consensus and the company’s $102–107 million guide. The preview’s buy-side expectation was $106–108 million, so the result also cleared that higher bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q2 FY2027 revenue of $116 million,” representing “approximately 58% year-over-year growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus was “~$105M”; the preview says “the buy-side expectation is closer to $106–108M” and lists company guidance of “$102–107M.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin reached 59%, above the 52–55% guide and the preview’s roughly 53–54% consensus. The company also raised full-year gross-margin guidance to 55–57%, better than the preview’s prior-expectation framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin was 59% … but beat expectations, and full-year gross margin guidance was raised … to 55%-57%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The Q2 guide was “52–55%” and consensus “~53–54%”; the preview says “≥56%” would repair the thesis.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $13.9 million, far above the preview’s $2–3 million consensus and its base-case expectation of $3–5 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA profit was $13.9 million for the quarter, exceeding expectations due to higher margins and revenue outperformance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 adjusted EBITDA consensus was “~$2–3M”; the base scenario projected “+$3–5M.”

surprises.description: The company issued $120 million of shares through its ATM, contrary to the preview’s base-case assumption of no drawdown and its note that no shares sold would be a positive signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: Cash and short-term investments were approximately $865 million, “including $120 million raised via ATM at an average $31.96 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario assumed “no ATM drawdown”; the preview says “an explicit statement that no shares were sold would be a positive signal.”

surprises.description: Backlog was about $815 million, well below the preview’s watch threshold of at least $950 million. The fact that about half is expected to be recognized over the next 12 months provides some visibility, but does not close the gap to the expected backlog level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog stood at approximately $815 million (up 11% year-over-year) with about 50% recognizable in the next 12 months.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The preview looks for backlog ≥$950M.”

surprises.description: Q3 guidance implies a sequential revenue decline and only about 27% year-over-year growth, a much slower pace than Q2. Management attributed the drop to point-in-time satellite handover revenue landing in Q2 rather than Q3; the preview did not give a Q3 revenue expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 revenue guidance of $101-$105 million implies only ~27% year-over-year growth and a sequential decline,” because handover revenue landed in Q2 rather than Q3.

surprises.description: FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance now has a $3 million floor rather than breakeven, while keeping the $10 million upper end. That improves the expected minimum profit for the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company raised “adjusted EBITDA guidance to $3-$10 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance was “Breakeven to +$10M.”

surprises.description: FY2027 capex guidance rose substantially above the prior $80–95 million range, with spending directed to next-generation fleets and manufacturing expansion. The investment supports capacity, but raises the planned capital burden.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year CapEx guidance was raised to $100-$115 million to fund Pelican and Owl next-generation fleets and German/San Francisco manufacturing expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Prior FY2027 capex guidance was “$80–95M.”

surprises.description: Planet disclosed more than $4 billion of Satellite Services opportunities, with over $1 billion qualified as near-term. The preview did not identify this pipeline detail as an expected disclosure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over $4 billion of Satellite Services opportunities in its pipeline, with over 25% (~$1 billion) qualified as near-term.”

in_line: FY2027 revenue guidance of $430–441 million stayed within the preview’s expected range of roughly $430–441 million; the preview’s base case anticipated that range.
Management maintained its target of annual adjusted free cash flow positivity, consistent with the preview’s key commitment to watch.

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EPS was $0.69, above the preview’s $0.61–$0.62 consensus range by roughly 11–13%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 at $0.69” adjusted EPS.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus” Q4 adjusted EPS was “$0.61–0.62.”

surprises.description: FY2027 adjusted EPS guidance has a $3.25 midpoint, above the preview’s expected $3.05–$3.10. The $3.00 low end is slightly below that expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for adjusted EPS of “$3.00-$3.50 (23% growth at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the June 9 framework implied “FY27 EPS around $3.05–3.10.”

surprises.description: FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance has a $755 million midpoint, just below the preview’s stated $760–$780 million street bar, although the range reaches $780 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: Fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance is “$730-$780 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the expected FY27 EBITDA bar as “around $760–780M.”

surprises.description: FY2026 adjusted EPS of $2.65 exceeded the high end of the $2.40–$2.60 guidance range, while the preview’s guidance table had $2.60 as the upper bound.
surprises.fact_evidence: Full-year adjusted EPS was “$2.65” and came in “above the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 adjusted EPS guidance of “$2.40–2.60.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EBITDA was $172 million, about $6 million above the preview’s derived $166 million expectation, though still within the implied guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $172 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated Q4 adjusted EBITDA at “~$166M (derived from guide).”

surprises.description: FY2026 free cash flow was $323 million, slightly below the preview’s derived expectation of about $330 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year free cash flow reached a record $323 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview derived “~$330M FY guide” and implied “~$87M” for Q4 free cash flow.

surprises.description: Natural products grew about 7% at the top line, above the preview’s 4% growth bar. The call facts do not specify whether this growth figure is adjusted for project work, so the comparison is not fully like-for-like.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Natural products grew ~7% top line.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview set the bar at “≥4%” for natural growth ex-project work.

surprises.description: Management said the FY2027 EBITDA midpoint is $25 million above the Investor Day target and that the FY2028 margin target will be reached one year early—an improvement on the company’s prior targets not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA midpoint is $25 million above the Investor Day target,” and the company expects to “hit its fiscal 2028 margin target one year early.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The call identified the Investor Day target as the benchmark and stated the FY2028 target timing; the preview did not discuss either target.

in_line: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA was $701 million, near the top of the company’s $685–$705 million guidance range, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the full-year result would finish near guidance.
Net leverage ended at 2.2x, within the preview’s expected Q4 exit range of roughly 2.2–2.3x.
Q4 sales were reported at over $7.6 billion, broadly around the preview’s $7.60–$7.71 billion consensus range.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.79, well above the preview’s $0.66 consensus estimate. That is a substantially stronger result than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS increased to $0.79” from $0.69 a year ago.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS” consensus: “$0.66.”

surprises.description: Sales and adjusted EBITDA both finished above the top of the preview’s ranges: revenue was $501.8 million versus a $495–500 million expectation, and adjusted EBITDA was $72.7 million versus $70–72 million. The resulting margin was about 14.5%, just above the preview’s 14.2–14.45% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated net sales rose 1.3% year-over-year to $501.8 million” and “Adjusted EBITDA grew modestly to $72.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus: “~$495–500M”; adjusted EBITDA consensus: “~$70–72M,” with “Margin 14.2–14.45%.”

surprises.description: Hardware Solutions adjusted EBITDA reached $27.1 million, exceeding the preview’s bullish scenario of $22 million or more and the $24.7 million Q3 FY2025 comparison cited in its catalyst checklist. The result came despite a tariff-related revenue headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: Hardware Solutions adjusted EBITDA “rose to $27.1 million,” aided by “~$3.1 million of pricing benefit and the absence of prior-year Monterrey operational issues.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull scenario cited “Hardware recovers to $22M+”; its catalyst checklist compared the result with “$24.7M in Q3 FY2025.”

surprises.description: The company reported an unanticipated tariff-reimbursement headwind: it reduced consolidated sales by roughly 2% and Hardware Solutions sales by about 4%, or approximately $9 million of Hardware revenue. This was a meaningful offset to pricing gains that the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: Sales were driven by “roughly 3% pricing gains offset by a ~2% negative tariff reimbursement impact”; Hardware had “a ~4% tariff reimbursement headwind (about $9 million in revenue).”

surprises.description: Net leverage was 2.8x, better than the preview’s 3.1x threshold, alongside $42.25 million of debt repayment and higher liquidity. The preview expected positive free cash flow and debt paydown priority, but the reported leverage was stronger than its stated bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “paid down $42.25 million of debt,” lowering net-debt-to-EBITDA leverage “to 2.8 times,” with liquidity “up 10.5% sequentially to about $363 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The catalyst checklist called for “Net debt to LTM adjusted EBITDA at or below 3.1x, with positive FCF”; the preview also said management had “prioritized debt paydown over buybacks.”

surprises.description: Custom Solutions grew 8.5%, supported in part by roughly $10 million per year of new Wood Solutions business—a growth driver not identified in the preview. The segment was the company’s fastest-growing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Custom Solutions was the fastest-growing segment with revenue up 8.5% to $111 million” and was “boosted by roughly $10 million/year of new Wood Solutions business.”

surprises.description: Management offered a more constructive interpretation of housing weakness than the preview’s volume-shortfall downside scenario: it described demand as deferred rather than destroyed and pointed to higher permits and homes authorized but not started. The signal was mixed because single-family starts were still sharply lower.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management characterized weak housing demand as “‘deferred rather than destroyed,’” citing starts down “~16% year-over-year,” while total permits were up 3% and homes authorized-but-not-started were up “~10%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bear scenario cited a “Volume shortfall.”

in_line: Q3 free cash flow was positive at $47.8 million and increased 3.5% year-over-year, consistent with the preview’s expectation that Q3 is seasonally the strongest free-cash-flow quarter.
Q4 guidance points to full-quarter price realization and margin expansion, consistent with the preview’s note that the full pricing benefit was expected in Q4.
The call provided Q4 guidance but did not reinstate FY2026 guidance, consistent with the preview’s warning that continued silence was possible after guidance was withdrawn.

surprises.description: Q1 fee revenue was $756 million, above the preview’s $736.8 million consensus and even the preview’s $748 million bull-case threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY27 fee revenue grew 7% year-over-year to $756 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus: $736.8M”; the bull scenario was “≥ $748M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS came in above the preview’s consensus range: $1.43 versus estimates of $1.36 or $1.39.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS grew 9% year-over-year to $1.43.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS: $1.36 (ChartMill read: $1.39).”

surprises.description: Q2 fee-revenue guidance was stronger than the preview’s expected range: the $860–$878 million outlook has a higher midpoint and a higher top end than the expected $845–$870 million, despite including only two months of AMS.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY27 guidance calls for fee revenue of $860-$878 million (including only two months of AMS).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A credible Q2 fee revenue guide is roughly $845–870M.”

surprises.description: Management expects to reach the $140 million AMS run-rate EBITDA target faster than the one-year timeline the preview anticipated, with revenue synergies the primary driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management targets $40 million of incremental run-rate EBITDA from AMS (raising it from $100 million to $140 million) within one year of closing, and expects to achieve it faster, driven primarily by revenue synergies.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has targeted about $140M EBITDA within one year of close. Watch whether that target is reaffirmed.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 17%, in line with the preview’s expectation of approximately 17%.
Management reaffirmed the $140 million AMS EBITDA target within a year, as anticipated; the faster expected achievement is a separate positive surprise.
Future cash is to prioritize paying down AMS acquisition debt over buybacks, consistent with the preview’s flagged possibility of a buyback pause to deleverage.

surprises.description: Q2 net sales were $3.33 billion, slightly above the $3.32 billion consensus and at the high end of company guidance. The beat was modest rather than a large departure from expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total net sales reached $3.33 billion, up 7.3% year-over-year at the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales … Consensus | $3.32B”; company guidance was “$3.30–3.33B.”

surprises.description: Chewy added 208,000 active customers sequentially, above the roughly 162,000 implied by consensus. However, 43,000 of the additions were unique SmartPack customers, so the excess over expectations was much smaller excluding them.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Chewy ended the quarter with 21.7 million active customers … adding 208,000 sequential net additions, including 43,000 unique SmartPack customers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said consensus of 21.662 million “implies ~162K net adds.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 6.8%, above the 6.3%–6.4% guidance range, but about $15 million of timing and discrete items accounted for essentially all of the outperformance. Thus, the reported beat was stronger than expected, while underlying performance was roughly in line with the range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $227 million (6.8% margin), beating guidance of 6.3%-6.4%, but roughly $15 million of timing and discrete items … accounted for essentially all the outperformance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of “6.3–6.4%.”

surprises.description: Chewy raised its full-year sales outlook rather than merely holding the range, lifting it to $13.46–$13.57 billion from $13.40–$13.55 billion. The increase is modest but exceeds the preview’s base case of reaffirmed guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management … raised total net sales guidance to $13.46-$13.57 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 net sales guidance of “$13.40–13.55B” and its base case as “FY guide reaffirmed.”

surprises.description: The low end of full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance rose by 10 basis points, from 6.6% to 6.7%, while the high end stayed at 6.8%. This is a modest improvement over the preview’s stated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised the low end of full-year adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 6.7%-6.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of “6.6–6.8%.”

surprises.description: Autoship sales grew 9.3%, just below the preview’s roughly 10% watch level, though Autoship’s 84.6% share of sales was above the preview’s 84% threshold. Growth therefore fell short of the stated marker, but penetration remained strong.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Autoship customer sales grew 9.3% year-over-year to $2.8 billion and represented 84.6% of total net sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Autoship growth below ~10%” as a potential crack and listed “Autoship growth ≥10% and penetration ≥84%” as the checklist.

surprises.description: Management put numbers and timing on AI-related savings: low tens of millions in fiscal 2026, scaling to about $50 million annualized in fiscal 2027. The benefit is tempered by management’s warning that savings will partly offset wage inflation rather than fully reach the bottom line.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI initiatives are expected to generate low tens of millions in cost savings in fiscal 2026, scaling to approximately $50 million annualized in fiscal 2027,” but “will partly offset wage inflation rather than fully flow to the bottom line.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “AI cost savings” as an offset to watch, but gave no estimate or timing.

in_line: Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.36, matching the preview’s $0.36 consensus and company guide.
NSPAC was $602, close to the preview’s $603.42 consensus.
Autoship penetration was 84.6%, above the preview’s 84% watch level.

surprises.description: The preview noted management's expected dropdown pipeline over the next four to five years, but the call facts say KNOP removed the Frieda Knudsen and Sindra Knudsen from its drop-down inventory in June. That reduces the identified inventory available for future dropdowns relative to the pipeline discussion investors were watching.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In June 2026, the partnership removed the Frieda Knudsen and Sindra Knudsen from its drop-down inventory.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management flagged sponsor dropdowns over the next 4 to 5 years. Pace and pricing are open questions.”

in_line: The $96.8 million of Q2 revenue was already identified in the preview as a beat against $93.5 million consensus; the call facts add no new headline revenue surprise.
The distribution increase to $0.075 per unit was already reflected in the preview, which showed $0.075 versus $0.050 in the prior quarter.
The $881.2 million backlog matches the preview. The reported 92% firm coverage for 2027 is broadly consistent with the preview's roughly 97% for H1 and 87% for H2.

The refinancing terms were consistent with the preview's expectation of a similar deal: the preview cited the $225 million facility at SOFR plus 165 basis points, and the call facts report that same rate.

surprises.description: Fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $94.6 million, above the preview’s $85–$90 million company-guidance range and its $87.5 million midpoint. Management also said the 9.6% margin puts InnovAge ahead of schedule for its long-term 10%+ margin target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA rose approximately 175% to $94.6 million” and margin improved to “9.6%”; management said it is “ahead of schedule” to hit its “10%+ long-term margin target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$85–90M” and a midpoint of “$87.5M.”

surprises.description: Fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $105–$115 million is above the preview’s $95–$103 million base case and reaches its bull-case range. The preview had identified guidance below about $100 million as a risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance targets” adjusted EBITDA of “$105–$115 million,” implying roughly “10.3% margin expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case was “EBITDA $95–103M,” its bull case was “EBITDA $105–115M,” and it flagged an FY27 guide “below about $100M” as a risk.

surprises.description: Fiscal 2026 revenue reached $989.7 million, exceeding both the preview’s $950–$975 million guidance range and its roughly $944.5 million consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 total revenue grew 15.9% to $989.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 revenue guidance of “$950M – $975M” and consensus of “~$944.5M.”

surprises.description: Fiscal 2026 ending census was about 8,230, above the preview’s 7,900–8,100 range. The result exceeded the range’s upper end by about 130 participants.
surprises.fact_evidence: Fiscal 2026 census increased 6.3% to “approximately 8,230 participants.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave an ending-census range of “7,900 – 8,100.”

surprises.description: Fiscal 2026 GAAP EPS was a loss of $0.02, well below the preview’s full-year consensus estimate of $0.23–$0.253. The near-breakeven net loss included $36.8 million of one-time legal and settlement accruals.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 net loss narrowed to just $0.7 million ($0.02 per share)” and was “driven by $36.8 million in one-time legal and settlement accruals.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 EPS consensus of “$0.23 – $0.253.”

surprises.description: Center-level contribution margin remained strong on a full-year basis: it rose to 23.0% of revenue, up 500 basis points. The preview had highlighted the risk of Q4 margin falling below 19%; the reported figure is annual, so it does not establish the Q4 margin, but it indicates robust FY26 performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Center-level contribution margin jumped 48.2% to $227.8 million in fiscal 2026, expanding 500 basis points to 23.0% of revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q4 below 19% would be a concern” after Q3 center-level contribution margin of “24.2%.”

surprises.description: Fiscal 2026 de novo losses were lower than the preview’s guided range, and management expects them to fall sharply again in fiscal 2027 as more centers leave de novo status.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 de novo losses declined to $10.6 million” and are projected to fall to “$0.4–$0.8 million in fiscal 2027,” with Florida and Crenshaw exiting de novo status.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 de novo losses were guided to “$11.5–13.5M.”

surprises.description: California and Colorado have not finalized their PACE Medicaid rates, adding state-specific rate uncertainty that the preview had not identified. The two states together account for about 70% of census, and management cited their fiscal pressures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “California and Colorado, which together represent approximately 70% of census, have not yet finalized their PACE Medicaid rates,” with both states facing “fiscal pressures.”

surprises.description: Management said InnovAge benefits from favorable dementia coding under the upcoming V22/V28 risk-adjustment blend because dementia is prevalent among its participants. The preview did not flag this as a potential offset to rate pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Effective January 2027, InnovAge transitions to a 50-50 blend of the V22 and V28 risk adjustment models,” and “benefits from favorable dementia coding under V28 given high dementia prevalence among participants.”

surprises.description: InnovAge reported substantial liquidity relative to debt, giving it capacity for potential M&A and growth investments; the preview had raised M&A and growth plans as things to watch but did not describe this balance-sheet capacity.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended the quarter with “$97.9 million in cash plus $43.4 million in short-term investments against only $63.3 million of total debt,” providing capacity for “potential M&A and growth investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “new centers, hospital JVs, or M&A in the FY27 plan.”

in_line: Management’s FY2027 Medicare rate outlook was consistent with the preview’s expectation of softer rates: it guided to a 1.5%–2.0% net increase after V28 adjustments.

surprises.description: SUNB’s adjusted EBITDA margin was 42.2%, far below the preview’s roughly 44.5%–45.5% expectation. The decline was about 330 basis points year over year, versus the preview’s view that a decline of around 100 basis points would keep the full-year margin outlook plausible.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 8.7% to $1.3 billion but margin declined to 42.2% from 43.2% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A decline no worse than about 100bps (roughly 44.8%) keeps the flat-FY margin guide plausible.” The preview also estimated a Q1 margin of “~44.5–45.5%.”

surprises.description: SUNB raised its FY2027 outlook instead of merely reaffirming it: the total-revenue growth range rose to 6%–9%, and adjusted EBITDA guidance rose to $4.92 billion–$5.12 billion from $4.85 billion–$5.05 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised FY2027 guidance to total revenue growth of 6%-9%, rental revenue growth of 7%-10%, and adjusted EBITDA of $4.92 billion-$5.12 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A reaffirmation is the base case.” The preview cited existing FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$4.85–5.05bn.”

surprises.description: Revenue exceeded the preview’s $2.97–$3.00 billion consensus range, reaching $3.1 billion. That is a clear beat, although the reported figure is rounded.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 total revenue grew 11.2% to $3.1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $2.97–3.00bn.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS reached $1.18, above the preview’s cited estimates of $1.04 and $1.08 and its $1.06 practical midpoint. Buybacks contributed alongside higher operating profit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS rose 20.4% to a first-quarter record of $1.18, aided by higher operating profit and share repurchases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS | $1.04 (Investing.com) or $1.08 (stockanalysis)”; “$1.06 is a practical midpoint.”

surprises.description: Despite the revenue beat, adjusted EBITDA was $1.3 billion, below the preview’s derived estimate of about $1.33–$1.36 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 8.7% to $1.3 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$1.33–1.36bn (derived, not a published consensus).”

surprises.description: SUNB raised gross and net rental capex guidance to $2.75–$3.15 billion and $2.4–$2.8 billion, respectively, citing mega-project, specialty, and energy demand. The preview did not flag a capex increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross capital expenditure guidance was raised to $2.75 billion-$3.15 billion and net rental capex to $2.4 billion-$2.8 billion, driven by mega project, specialty and energy demand.”

surprises.description: A sizeable portion of rental growth came from specific contributors not anticipated in the preview: the FIFA World Cup added roughly 250 basis points and the Aries/ARRIS acquisition about 100 basis points to quarterly rental revenue growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FIFA World Cup contributed roughly 250 basis points and the Aries/ARRIS acquisition about 100 basis points to rental revenue growth in the quarter.”

in_line: North American Specialty rental growth of 25.3% was essentially in line with the preview’s comparison point of United Rentals’ 25% specialty growth.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $292.8 million, above the $285.96 million consensus and the preview’s $290–292 million base scenario. The beat was meaningful, though it was just below the preview’s roughly $294 million bull-case marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY27 total revenue grew 21% year-over-year to $292.8 million.”

surprises.description: Q2 operating profitability came in well above the preview’s expectation: the call reported a 15.2% operating margin and $44.4 million of operating income, versus a previewed margin of about 13.4% and operating-income estimate of roughly $38–39 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 operating income was $44.4 million for a 15.2% operating margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op. income (Q2) | ~$38–39M”; “~13.4% margin at midpoint.”

surprises.description: GTV growth slowed more than the preview’s demand-watch threshold: it was 17%, below the expected 23% pace and below the preview’s sub-20% warning level. Management attributed the shortfall mainly to softer lead-volume growth, notably in HVAC, during May and June.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GTV reached $26.8 billion, up 17% year-over-year, which was about 200 basis points below recent quarters, driven primarily by softer lead volume growth (notably in HVAC) during May and June before stabilizing in July.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GTV growth vs. 23%”; “A sub-20% print would be a meaningful macro warning.”

surprises.description: The FY27 revenue outlook was raised only slightly, to $1.139–1.144 billion, despite the Q2 beat. That fell short of the preview’s base expectation of roughly $1.145–1.150 billion and its stated signal of stronger H2 confidence at $1.155 billion or more.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY27 guidance is $1.139 billion to $1.144 billion in revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base | … FY27 raised to ~$1.145–1.150B”; “A raise through the beat (≥$1,155M) would signal real H2 confidence.”

surprises.description: The FY27 operating-income outlook rose substantially versus the company’s prior guide, and management described 25% incremental margins as a floor while guiding to 33% incremental margins for FY27. The preview listed the prior company guide at $142–147 million, but did not find a consensus estimate for the year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY27 guidance is … $152 million to $154 million in operating income”; “now viewing 25% incremental margins as a floor rather than a target, and guiding to 33% incremental margins for FY27.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 non-GAAP op. income | Not found”; “FY27 non-GAAP op. income | $142–147M.”

surprises.description: Max enrollment exceeded the preview’s checkable Q2 doubling commitment: the company said it exceeded its Q2 goal and now targets more than 700 enrolled locations by fiscal year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Max locations more than doubled to just over 100 in fiscal Q1 and are expected to roughly double again, with the company now targeting over 700 enrolled Max locations by fiscal year-end after exceeding its Q2 goal.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management committed to doubling them again in Q2”; “Max locations doubled Q/Q.”

surprises.description: Management reprioritized investment away from entering new commercial trades and broader residential exteriors, focusing instead on Max and its internal AI software factory. The preview highlighted Max adoption and monetization but did not anticipate delaying these expansion plans.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reprioritized investments, delaying planned expansion into new commercial trades and broader residential exteriors to concentrate resources on Max and its internal ‘software factory’ AI initiative.”

surprises.description: The shift toward Max is expected to create a near-term revenue headwind of about $4–5 million over the remainder of the fiscal year, including lower subscription and professional-services revenue; the preview did not flag this cost of the pivot.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The shift toward Max is expected to create a $2 million to $3 million subscription revenue headwind and roughly $2 million lower professional services revenue over the remainder of the fiscal year, totaling a ~$4-5 million near-term headwind.”

surprises.description: The call reported that virtual-agent revenue and call volume each more than doubled sequentially, a growth update the preview did not anticipate or establish a benchmark for. Adoption was split between first-time buyers and customers replacing other solutions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Virtual agent revenue and call volume each more than doubled sequentially in Q2, with adoption balanced between first-time buyers and customers replacing competing solutions.”

in_line: Net dollar retention remained above 110%, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Casey's diluted EPS was $7.37, above the preview's consensus range of $6.59–$6.81. That is roughly 8%–12% above the range, a meaningful beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Diluted EPS reached $7.37, up 28% year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Fuel margin reached 47.8 cents per gallon, above the preview's implied 44.8–46.0 cents. The beat was notable despite the preview's concern that rising wholesale prices could pressure margins.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fuel margin was strong at $0.478 per gallon,” up $0.068 year over year.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS of $6.59 implies roughly 44.8 cpg and $6.81 implies roughly 46.0 cpg.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses rose 8%, exceeding the preview's expected full-year growth range of 5%–7%. Management also expects Q2 expense growth to be similar to Q1, indicating the pressure may persist near term.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total operating expenses rose 8% ($55.9 million)”; “Q2 OpEx growth expected to be similar to Q1 due to elevated fuel prices.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “opex growth +5–7%”; the preview also said, “A print above 7% would offset a fuel beat.”

surprises.description: Inside same-store sales grew 3.2%, below the preview's roughly 3.9% blended expectation. Results were mixed by category: prepared food and dispensed beverage sales beat expectations, while grocery and general merchandise fell short.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inside same-store sales grew 3.2%”; prepared food and dispensed beverage same-store sales were “up 4.8%” and grocery/general merchandise were “up 2.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described “roughly +3.9% blended SSS”; it listed prepared food SSS at “+4.3%” and grocery/GM SSS at “+3.6%.”

surprises.description: EBITDA was $485 million, modestly above the preview's derived $470–480 million estimate; its 17% growth also edged above the preview's implied 14%–16% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EBITDA increased 17% to $485 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied EBITDA | ~$470–480M”; the preview estimated implied year-over-year growth of “+14% to +16%.”

surprises.description: Revenue was $5.68 billion, slightly above the preview's $5.56–$5.65 billion range, though the difference was small.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose 24.3% to $5.68 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | $5.56B – $5.65B.”

surprises.description: Management quantified planned Fikes/Setco integration headwinds that the preview did not identify: about 25 basis points against inside same-store sales and 50 basis points against fuel gallons. These are a drag on the reported operating trends.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Fikes/Setco integration created planned headwinds of ~25 basis points to inside same-store sales and ~50 basis points to fuel gallons.”

surprises.description: Management said the same-store sales benefit from remodels will not show up until Q4, a later timing than the preview discussed. The call also reported roughly 30% prepared-food and dispensed-beverage lift at remodeled stores versus pre-remodel, indicating a substantial eventual benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects same-store sales inflection from remodels won't materialize until the fourth quarter”; remodeled stores showed “~30% PF&DB lift versus pre-remodel.”

in_line: Same-store fuel gallons dipped 0.3%, within the preview's FY27 guidance range of -1% to +1%.
Total gallons sold increased 2.5%, close to the preview's 2.8% consensus estimate.
Casey's remained on track for its 120-store unit-growth target, consistent with the preview's focus on reaching at least 120 new stores.

surprises.description: J.Jill was expected to post sales around the $151 million guidance midpoint and comps down 2% to 4%. Instead, sales were $154.8 million and comps rose 0.5%, exceeding the company’s guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total company sales rose 0.5% year-over-year to $154.8 million with comparable sales also up 0.5%, exceeding company guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales… Working number ~$151M (guide midpoint)”; “Comparable sales… -2% to -4%.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was expected around $19–20 million, but reported adjusted EBITDA was $32.8 million. The underlying figure, excluding tariff refunds and strategic investments, was $20.1 million—only slightly above expectations—so the reported beat was largely attributable to the refund and investment treatment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Underlying adjusted EBITDA (excluding tariff refunds and strategic investments) was $20.1 million, while reported adjusted EBITDA reached $32.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA… $18–20M”; “Street consensus ~$19–20M.”

surprises.description: The company received $13.3 million in net tariff refunds, far beyond the preview’s expectation of only a small early portion and its assumption of no refund benefit in guidance. J.Jill said it chose to invest most of the refunds in marketing and technology rather than letting them flow through to the bottom line.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received $13.3 million in net tariff refunds in the quarter and intentionally chose to invest most of it into marketing and technology initiatives rather than dropping it to the bottom line.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: J.Jill had received “a small portion” of its claim early in Q2, while “assumed zero refund benefit in guidance.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was expected at $0.57, but came in at $1.24. The large gap reflects the unusually high reported EBITDA and tariff refunds; share repurchases added only about $0.01 per share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted diluted EPS jumped to $1.24 from $0.81 a year earlier, aided by roughly $0.01 from share repurchases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS… $0.57 (4 analysts).”

surprises.description: Gross margin was expected to decline about 100 basis points, but excluding tariff refunds it was roughly flat at 68.3%, as stronger full-price margins offset a greater markdown mix. The reported margin reached 76.8%, inflated by the refunds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported gross margin expanded about 840 basis points to 76.8%, but excluding tariff refunds gross margin was roughly flat at 68.3% as higher full-price margins offset a greater markdown mix.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin… About -100 bps (about 67.4%, including ~$4M net tariff).”

surprises.description: J.Jill raised its full-year outlook instead of reaffirming the prior range: adjusted EBITDA is now $75–80 million versus $70–75 million, and sales are now expected flat to up 2% rather than flat to down 2%. It also now expects gross margin to rise 100–150 basis points year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year guidance to adjusted EBITDA of $75-80 million, sales flat to up 2%, comps down 1% to up 1%, and gross margin up 100-150 basis points versus prior year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year guide: adj. EBITDA $70–75M, net sales flat to down 2%”; the base scenario expected management to “Reaffirm[] $70–75M.”

surprises.description: The Q3 outlook points to positive comparable-sales growth and sales growth, following a preview that framed the turnaround around a difficult Q2 comp recovery and expected H2 sales to be flat to up 4%. J.Jill guided Q3 sales up 3% to 5% and comps up 1% to 3%, with flat gross margins and $20–22 million of adjusted EBITDA.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for sales up 3-5%, comps up 1-3%, flat gross margins, and adjusted EBITDA of $20-22 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales guidance implies H2 flat to +4% after H1 down 3.9%.”

surprises.description: Management provided favorable customer commentary not anticipated in the preview: new-to-brand customers are younger, retaining at higher rates, and spending more through higher order values and more trips; reactivation of lapsed customers is also building.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New-to-brand customers are trending younger, retaining at higher rates, and spending more via higher average order value and more trips, while lapsed-customer reactivation is building.”

surprises.description: The company trimmed its full-year net-new-store plan to 1–3 openings because landlord delivery delays pushed two openings into early 2027. The preview did not flag a reduction to the store-opening outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Store count reached 255 (up from 247 a year ago), but full-year net new store openings were trimmed to 1-3 due to landlord delivery delays pushing two openings into early 2027.”

surprises.description: The company now expects approximately $40 million of full-year free cash flow, above the $20 million FY target cited in the preview after Q1 free cash flow was negative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects full-year free cash flow of approximately $40 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow was -$1.1M against a $20M FY target.”

in_line: The remaining buyback authorization was $11.8 million, broadly close to the preview’s estimate of about $13.3 million remaining; repurchases contributed roughly $0.01 to adjusted diluted EPS.

surprises.description: Gross margin was 37.4%, well above the preview’s 34.5% base-case model and also above its roughly 36% bull scenario. The preview had warned that fiber costs could pressure margins, so the reported expansion was a meaningful upside difference.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 gross profit jumped 43.9% to $9.1 million, with gross margin expanding to 37.4% from 31.7% a year earlier due to manufacturing operating leverage.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My model (base case): Revenue of $24.5M, gross margin of 34.5%”; the bull scenario projected “~36%.”

surprises.description: OCC reported $0.21 per diluted share, slightly above the preview’s $0.20 single-analyst estimate and its $0.18–$0.19 model range. This was a small earnings beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 net income surged to $1.9 million ($0.21 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (basic/diluted) | Consensus … $0.20”; the model estimated “EPS of about $0.18 to $0.19.”

surprises.description: Sales were $24.3 million, a little below the $24.5 million estimate, though still inside the preview’s $24–$25 million base-case range. The shortfall was small rather than a break from the expected growth trajectory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 FY2026 net sales rose 22% year-over-year to $24.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales … Consensus … $24.5M”; the base case was “Revenue of $24.5M,” with a scenario range of “$24M to $25M.”

surprises.description: SG&A remained 28.7% of sales, slightly above the preview’s stated operating-leverage threshold of about 28%. It was essentially unchanged from the year-earlier ratio, so the miss against that threshold was limited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 SG&A rose to $7 million from $5.7 million but held essentially flat at 28.7% of sales versus 28.8% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The operating leverage story requires SG&A to stay below about 28% of sales.”

surprises.description: Management said OCC had moved from evaluating workforce and equipment additions to expanding capacity and hiring across facilities. The preview identified such expansion as an open question, although the call facts do not provide a quantified capacity ceiling or capex commitment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company … is expanding capacity and hiring across facilities (notably Roanoke and Dallas).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Management was “evaluating workforce expansion and equipment additions”; the preview said a capacity or capex announcement would be new information.

surprises.description: OCC had begun recording initial sales from Lightera, providing the first reported commercial progress from the collaboration. The preview had identified first quantified Lightera revenue as new information, but the call facts do not quantify the sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company has begun recording initial sales of Lightera products under its strategic collaboration.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any … first quantified revenue from Lightera … would be new information.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s concern that the business was working-capital hungry—with only $146K of cash and substantial inventory and credit-facility borrowings cited at April 30—management said available revolver capacity and operating cash were sufficient to fund growth, with no equity raise indicated. Working capital had also strengthened since fiscal year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Working capital strengthened to $19.2 million from $13.9 million at fiscal year-end 2025, with management asserting the credit revolver and operating cash are sufficient to fund growth without indicating a need for an equity raise.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described OCC as “working-capital hungry” and said “Any equity raise or ATM language would be a clear negative.”

surprises.description: Management reported continued strong demand into August, extending the demand picture beyond the July quarter. The preview focused on Q3 results and did not state an expectation for post-quarter demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported continued strong demand into August.”

in_line: Backlog and forward load reached $13.5 million, within the preview’s $13–$15 million base-case range and slightly above the $13.3 million April figure; the preview had flagged a flat or falling balance as a concern.
The industry-wide optical fiber shortage and longer raw-material lead times remained a constraint, consistent with the preview’s warning that shortages were extending lead times.
The reported sales growth was close to the preview’s implied roughly 23% year-over-year growth expectation.

surprises.description: Gross margin was 40.4%, far above the preview’s 35.0%–35.5% estimate. Management attributed the expansion to 510 basis points of tariff refunds, partly offset by 70 basis points of lower merchandise margin from reinvesting in customer pricing, and said the benefit was non-recurring.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded roughly 440 basis points to 40.4%, driven by 510 basis points of tariff refunds partially offset by a 70 basis point merch margin decline from reinvesting refund proceeds into lower customer pricing, a benefit management flagged as non-recurring.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~35.0–35.5% (est.)”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $2.31, above the preview’s $2.12 consensus and its stated vendor range of $2.07–$2.14. The quarter’s tariff refunds net of reinvestment added only about six cents per share, so they accounted for only a small part of the reported result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew 19.1% to $2.31”; tariff refunds “net of strategic reinvestments added only about six cents to EPS in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $2.12”; “range $2.07–$2.14 across vendors.”

surprises.description: The company raised its full-year gross-margin and EPS ranges rather than merely reaffirming them: gross margin guidance increased to 35.5%–36.0%, and adjusted EPS guidance to $6.50–$6.90. The preview’s base case anticipated reaffirmed EPS guidance, and its prior adjusted EPS range was $6.40–$6.80.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reaffirmed full-year sales guidance ... while raising gross margin guidance to 35.5%-36.0% and lifting EPS guidance to ... adjusted $6.50-$6.90.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Standing FY2026 guidance ... Gross margin 34.5–35.0% ... Adjusted EPS $6.40–6.80”; base scenario: “Reaffirm sales and EPS.”

surprises.description: Management reported low-single-digit positive comps through Labor Day for Q3, providing a quantified positive quarter-to-date signal where the preview said the base case might have no QTD number. The preview specifically identified a quantified positive QTD comp as the most bullish update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 running low single-digit positive comps through Labor Day.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A quantified positive QTD comp would be the most bullish thing management can say”; base scenario: “no QTD number.”

surprises.description: Despite the negative Q2 comp, management kept the full-year comp range at flat to +2% rather than narrowing it to the preview’s base-case 0%–1%. It also described roughly 1% back-half comps, consistent with the 1.1% achieved year-to-date.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reaffirmed ... flat-to-plus-2% comps”; “guided to roughly 1% back-half comps, consistent with the 1.1% comp achieved year-to-date.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base ... Reaffirm sales and EPS; trim comp to 0–1%.”

surprises.description: Traffic from households earning under $50,000 fell high single digits, worsening from the low-single-digit decline in Q1, while traffic from households above $100,000 rose high single digits. The preview flagged the low-income consumer as a bear-case risk, but the reported deterioration and sharp split were concrete evidence of that pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Traffic from households earning under $50K fell high single digits (worse than Q1's low single-digit decline), while traffic from households above $100K rose high single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Bear scenario key driver: “low-income consumer.”

surprises.description: The reported basket mix showed declining transactions and units per transaction, with a 4.5% higher ticket—driven by higher AUR—offsetting some of the pressure. That points to weaker underlying shopping activity beneath the near-flat comp result, a dynamic the preview did not quantify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ticket up 4.5% (driven by higher AUR) offset by units per transaction down and total transactions down about 2%, signaling traffic pressure amid episodic, event-driven shopping.”

surprises.description: Management signaled a slower share-repurchase pace in the back half after repurchasing about $181 million in the first half. The preview highlighted buybacks as an important contributor to EPS growth and asked for the Q2 amount, but did not anticipate a stated slowdown in the coming half.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Repurchased approximately $181 million of stock ... in the first half, with $256 million remaining on authorization but signaled reduced buyback pace in the back half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Buybacks deliver most of the consensus EPS growth”; “Buyback pace and share count” and “Buyback dollars in Q2” were identified as items to watch.

in_line: Q2 comparable sales declined 0.4%, within the preview’s derived expectation of roughly flat, defined as -1% to +0.5%.
Full-year sales guidance was reaffirmed at 3%–5% growth, matching the standing range in the preview.

surprises.description: The preview cited FY2026 operating-income guidance of $390–410 million, while the call gave $540–550 million—a much higher range against the preview’s stated expectation. The company nevertheless described the range as a slight trim versus its prior expectations, mainly because American Eagle is now expected to be flat rather than low-single-digit positive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year operating income is guided to $540 million to $550 million”; management characterized this as “a slight trim to prior expectations,” driven mainly by American Eagle's flat versus previously expected low-single-digit-positive outlook.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 operating income guide: $390–410M”; the preview also said “Reiteration is the floor for the base case.”

surprises.description: Q2 EPS was far above the preview’s $0.21 consensus and $0.20–0.23 implied range. The call also reported a $161 million tariff-refund benefit in operating income, so the result included a substantial one-off benefit rather than reflecting only underlying operations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 EPS was $0.79”; operating income included “a net tariff refund benefit of approximately $161 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS: $0.21”; “Guidance-implied EPS of ~$0.20–0.23.”

surprises.description: Gross margin was dramatically above the preview’s roughly 37.0–37.4% estimate, but the reported expansion was more than explained by tariff refunds. Beneath that headline, merchandise margin deleveraged as American Eagle marked down product, with pressure expected to continue into Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin expanded 980 basis points to 48.7%, but tariff refunds contributed 1,300 basis points, while merchandise margin actually deleveraged 330 basis points due to markdowns at American Eagle”; markdown pressure from seasonal and fashion product “is expected to persist into Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin: ~37.0–37.4% (est.)”; the preview also said it was watching whether “AUR and lower markdowns absorb tariffs.”

surprises.description: Reported Q2 operating income of $211 million greatly exceeded the preview’s $48–50 million expectation, but the call attributed about $161 million to a net tariff refund. Underlying operating profit was roughly $50 million, essentially in line with the preview’s estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 operating income was $211 million versus $103 million last year,” including “a net tariff refund benefit of approximately $161 million,” with “underlying operating profit” roughly $50 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating income: ~$48–50M”; company guidance was “$45–50M.”

surprises.description: American Eagle comps were slightly weaker than the preview’s approximately flat expectation, declining 1%. The sequential improvement from Q1 and men’s fourth consecutive quarter of positive comps softened, but did not erase, the miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “American Eagle brand total sales grew only 1% with comparable sales declining 1%, though improved sequentially from Q1, with men's posting a fourth consecutive quarter of positive comps.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “American Eagle brand comp (vs. ~flat consensus).”

surprises.description: Revenue was modestly above the preview’s $1.37 billion consensus, although comparable-sales growth itself was around consensus and at the high end of company guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue was $1.4 billion, up 8% year-over-year, with consolidated comparable sales growth of 6%, hitting the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue: $1.37B”; comparable sales were estimated at “~+6% (implied).”

in_line: Consolidated comparable-sales growth was 6%, around the preview’s ~6% estimate and at the high end of company guidance.
Aerie (including OFFLINE) comps grew 19%, within the preview’s view that high-teens growth would be fine.
Underlying Q2 operating profit was roughly $50 million, in line with the preview’s $48–50 million expectation.
The reported tax rate of approximately 25% matched the rate used in the preview’s implied EPS estimate.

surprises.description: Signet’s adjusted operating income was $107 million, well above the preview’s roughly $88 million expectation. It also reported 140 basis points of rate expansion, a strong result against the preview’s focus on margin pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating income rose 25% to $107 million with 140 basis points of rate expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating income … Consensus … ~$88M (implied)” and the preview said Q2 was the “last heavy-pressure quarter” for merchandise margin.

surprises.description: The call reported adjusted EPS growth of 36%, far above the modest growth implied by the preview’s $1.72 consensus versus $1.61 a year earlier. The call facts do not give the reported EPS amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS growth of 36%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 FY26 adjusted EPS of “$1.61” and consensus of “$1.72” (with an alternative estimate of $1.74).

surprises.description: Signet signed an early seven-year Bread Financial renewal with more than $1 billion of estimated incremental non-credit revenue and operating income over the agreement’s life, plus a $200–250 million operating benefit over 36 months and about $80 million of cash expected in Q3. The preview did not anticipate a new credit agreement or this benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Signed an early 7-year renewal with credit partner Bread Financial through December 2035,” estimated to generate “over $1 billion in incremental noncomp revenue and operating income” with “no loss sharing”; the deal is expected to deliver “$200-250 million” over 36 months and “roughly $80 million in cash” in Q3.

surprises.description: Signet announced a nearly $400 million increase to its repurchase authorization and a $125 million ASR, alongside returns equivalent to 12% of recent market capitalization in the first nine months. The preview flagged buyback pace as something to watch but gave no expectation of a move this large.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nearly $400 million increase to its share repurchase authorization and a $125 million ASR,” with “$575 million remaining”; combined with dividends, Signet will have returned “12% of its recent market cap” in the first nine months.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s catalyst checklist included “Buyback pace and Q2 exit share count,” but stated no expected authorization increase or ASR size.

surprises.description: Tariff refunds were quantified at $30 million for this year, contrary to the prior expectation that timing was too early to quantify. The benefit is limited, however: it is less than half the incremental tariff headwind, and indirect refunds are not expected to help until fiscal 2028.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tariff refunds of $30 million are expected this year (including $15 million in Q2), but represent less than half of the net headwind from incremental tariffs, with indirect refunds expected to benefit fiscal 2028 instead.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Refund timing was ‘too early to quantify’ in Q1. Any quantified refund should be treated as one-time.”

in_line: Q2 same-store sales were up 2.2%, broadly matching the preview’s expectation of about 2%.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.47, well above the preview’s $0.37 consensus estimate and the preview’s expected range of roughly $0.34–$0.38. The call also said EPS beat the company’s own expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted EPS came in at $0.47 … beating the company's own expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (Q2) … Consensus $0.37”; the base scenario expected “$0.34–$0.38.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance rose to $1.50–$1.65: the low end increased by $0.10 while the high end was maintained. This is better than the preview’s prior $1.40–$1.65 adjusted range and its expectation that guidance might narrow to about $1.45–$1.60.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Caleres raised the low end of full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $1.50-$1.65 while maintaining the high end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 EPS … $1.40–$1.65 adj.”; the base scenario expected guidance to be “narrowed to ~$1.45–$1.60.”

surprises.description: The new full-year GAAP EPS guidance of $2.80–$2.95 is far above the preview’s prior GAAP range of $1.44–$1.69. The call reported a $57.4 million tariff refund, but said it was excluded from adjusted results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP EPS guided to $2.80-$2.95”; the company “received $57.4 million in IEPA tariff refunds” and the refund was “excluded from adjusted results.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 EPS … $1.44–$1.69 GAAP.” The preview also said the tariff refund “is excluded from guidance.”

surprises.description: Sales were below the $702.5 million consensus estimate: reported sales of $695 million were about 1% short, and growth was 5.6% rather than the preview’s expected 6.7%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total sales rose 5.6% to $695 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales (Q2) … Consensus $702.5M (+6.7%).”

surprises.description: Brand Portfolio organic sales grew 8.2%, below the preview’s low-double-digit organic-growth expectation. The call did not provide a directly comparable total segment growth figure, so this comparison is limited to organic growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Brand portfolio organic sales grew 8.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Brand Portfolio sales (Q2) … Up ~mid-20s% (low-double-digit organic).”

surprises.description: Consolidated gross margin excluding the tariff refund expanded 340 basis points, just below the preview’s 345–375 basis-point expectation. The shortfall was small, but the reported increase did not quite reach the guided range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin (excluding the tariff refund) expanded 340 basis points to 46.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The guide calls for gross margin up 345–375 bps.”

surprises.description: Famous Footwear’s gross margin fell 100 basis points, and management expects similar year-over-year pressure through the back half. That continued segment-level pressure is a concern against the preview’s emphasis on strong consolidated margin expansion and its expectation of stronger Famous performance during back-to-school and holiday.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Famous Footwear gross margin fell 100 basis points to 42.7% due to increased promotional and clearance activity,” with “similar year-over-year margin pressure” expected through the back half.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The guide calls for gross margin up 345–375 bps”; the preview also said management “expects stronger Famous performance during back-to-school and holiday.”

in_line: Famous Footwear Q2 comps were down 5.9%, broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of down mid-single digits, though slightly weaker than the preview’s base-case range of down 4% to 5%.
The $57.4 million tariff refund was excluded from adjusted results, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the refund would be excluded from adjusted guidance.
Famous Footwear comps turned flat through Labor Day, consistent with the preview’s focus on management’s expected back-to-school improvement; fashion comps were positive.

surprises.description: Q1 adjusted EPS was $0.59, far above the preview's phasing estimate of about $0.20 and above the cited consensus range of $0.25–$0.32. The 84% year-over-year increase was driven in part by higher product gross margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS jumped 84% year-over-year to $0.59 from $0.32, driven by product gross margin improving to 40% from 36%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Phasing implies ~$0.20”; Q1 consensus was “$0.25 (pre-print) to $0.32 (Zacks).”

surprises.description: Q1 revenue of $480 million exceeded the preview's roughly $440 million phasing estimate and also came in above the highest cited consensus estimate of $474.6 million. That was a better quarterly top-line result than the preview's base case of $445–$465 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AeroVironment reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $480 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Phasing implies ~$440M”; Q1 consensus ranged from “$456.1M ... to $474.6M”; base scenario was “$445–465M.”

surprises.description: Q1 adjusted EBITDA was approximately $46–$53 million, above the preview's phasing estimate of about $35 million. The result was stronger than the preview's on-phasing base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $46-53 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Phasing implies ~$35M” for Q1 adjusted EBITDA.

surprises.description: Product gross margin improved to 40% from 36%, a meaningful expansion despite the preview's focus on weak gross margins, especially service margin. The call's stated margin improvement also helped drive the much stronger EPS result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Product gross margin improving to 40% from 36%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin, especially service margin (2% in Q4).”
