surprises.description: Space, Cyber and Directed Energy remained loss-making and its adjusted EBITDA worsened to negative $9 million, versus negative $3 million for the segment in FY26. The preview identified movement toward breakeven as a key issue, but the reported result went the other way.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Space, Cyber and Directed Energy segment posted negative $9 million adjusted EBITDA and 21% revenue decline year-over-year due to the SCAR contract termination ... and discontinued government programs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SCDE segment EBITDA. Any move from -$3M toward breakeven would matter most”; the preview also listed “SCDE near breakeven” in its bull scenario.

surprises.description: Management described a much larger potential LOCUST business than the preview had discussed: over $500 million annually within roughly a year, potentially larger than loitering munitions within five years. That is a substantial new growth prospect, though it is a forward-looking target rather than current revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects LOCUST to become a franchise exceeding $500 million per year within roughly a year and potentially larger than the loitering munitions business within five years, operating at under $10 per shot.”

surprises.description: The company reported its first international LOCUST direct commercial sale, a new commercial milestone not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Plus a first international LOCUST direct commercial sale.”

surprises.description: Q1 adjusted SG&A rose to $85 million, or 18% of revenue, from $65 million, or 14%, and included an unanticipated $4.2 million bad-debt reserve. The company said the reserve was nonrecurring and projected full-year SG&A of 14–16% of revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted SG&A rose to $85 million (18% of revenue) from $65 million (14%), including a nonrecurring $4.2 million bad debt reserve.”

in_line: Management reaffirmed the FY2027 revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and non-GAAP EPS ranges unchanged, as the preview's base case anticipated.
Negative FY2027 free cash flow and CapEx of 12–14% of revenue were consistent with the preview's stated cash-flow and capital-spending expectations.
Uncertain timing of the FY2027 government budget remained the main risk to guidance, consistent with the preview's discussion of budget assumptions and continuing-resolution risk.

surprises.description: EPS was a $0.50 loss versus the preview’s $0.05-loss consensus, a substantially worse result. The call cited a previously unflagged, non-cash $3.2 million goodwill impairment tied to LHD Germany as part of the explanation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company recorded a net loss of $4.9 million ($0.50 per share)”; this included “a non-cash $3.2 million goodwill impairment tied to LHD Germany.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) −$0.05.”

surprises.description: Adjusted gross margin reached 37.7%, well above the preview’s modeled 34–35% range and substantially above Q1’s 33.6%. This was a stronger recovery than the preview’s 35%-or-higher upside threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanding 410 basis points sequentially to 37.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. gross margin… model ~34–35%”; the preview said “35% or higher would support” management’s claim that Q1 margin pressure was transitory.

surprises.description: Sales of $50.1 million came in modestly below the $51.48 million consensus. However, the company disclosed that $3.7 million of prior-year sales came from divested product lines, making sales growth 2.8% excluding those lines rather than the reported 4.5% decline; the preview had said the divested lines’ revenue was undisclosed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales were $50.1 million, down 4.5% year-over-year…but…up 2.8% when excluding $3.7 million of prior-year revenue from divested product lines.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $51.48M”; the preview also said Lakeland “has not disclosed those lines’ revenue, so organic growth is hard to model.”

surprises.description: Fire services revenue grew 78% year over year, far above the prior quarter’s 11% growth and the preview’s scenario of growth staying near that level. The reported $3.5 million contribution from the ISP business helps explain the acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fire services revenue grew 78% year-over-year, with the independent service provider (ISP) business contributing $3.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported Q1 Fire Services growth of “+11% Y/Y” and said, “If growth stays near 11%, the backlog may be constrained by capacity rather than converting to revenue.”

surprises.description: Foreign exchange was a significant $1.3 million headwind, and management said it was exploring hedging strategies. The preview did not flag a material FX impact or hedging as an issue to watch.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Foreign exchange was a significant $1.3 million headwind versus just $43,000 a year ago, prompting management to explore hedging strategies.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA excluding FX was $2.7 million: within the preview’s modeled $2–4 million range, down from the expected-to-be-difficult $5.1 million year-ago comparison, and more than doubled sequentially from Q1’s $1.1 million.

Management guided to sequential revenue and margin growth in Q3 and Q4, consistent with the preview’s expectation that margin gains would be more visible in the second half. The UK framework update also matched the preview’s flagged catalyst: it described a seven-year program with potential value up to £220 million across suppliers and expected significant brigade contracts over the next 12–18 months.
The preview expected positive operating cash flow for FY27; the call reported $5.4 million of operating cash flow in the first half.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was $43.8 million, below the preview’s roughly $50 million consensus and its $46–50 million base scenario. The call attributed the shortfall to lighter-than-expected lemon sales volume and the transition of citrus brokerage operations to Sunkist.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 FY2026 total net revenue declined to $43.8 million from $47.8 million a year earlier,” driven by “lighter-than-expected lemon sales volume and the transition of citrus brokerage operations to Sunkist.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$50M (range $50–56M)” and the base scenario lists “Revenue | $46–50M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted diluted EPS was only $0.02, well below the preview’s $0.18–$0.19 consensus; GAAP results were a $0.17-per-share loss. That is a substantially weaker per-share result than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported a Q3 net loss of $3 million ($0.17 per diluted share)” while “adjusted diluted EPS turned positive at $0.02.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was positive, as management had promised, but at $3.9 million it fell below the preview’s $5.5–$7.5 million base scenario. The call also said results were below management’s expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $3.9 million in Q3 FY2026 versus $3.0 million in the prior-year quarter, despite results coming in below management's expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario estimated “Adj. EBITDA | $5.5–7.5M”; it also noted management’s commitment to “positive adjusted EBITDA in both Q3 and Q4.”

surprises.description: The FY2026 fresh lemon carton outlook was narrowed to 4.0–4.25 million, at the low end of the previous 4.0–4.5 million range. The call cited heavier Argentine imports and oversupply in the U.S. market.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fresh lemon volume guidance was cut to the low end at 4.0 million to 4.25 million cartons for FY2026 due to higher lemon imports from Argentina oversupplying the U.S. market.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance (FY26): lemon cartons 4.0–4.5M”; the preview listed reiteration or a cut as the key guidance issue.

surprises.description: FY2026 avocado volume guidance rose to 7.0–7.25 million pounds, above the previewed 5.5–6.5 million-pound range. This is a favorable change from the expected harvest catch-up after near-zero first-half shipments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Avocado volume guidance was raised to 7.0-7.25 million pounds for FY2026, well above the prior 5.5-6.5 million pound range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance (FY26): ... avocados 5.5–6.5M lbs”; the preview said most of that year’s volume had to ship in Q3 and Q4.

surprises.description: Management disclosed that FY2027 avocado production is expected to exceed 10 million pounds, about 30% above FY2026, a substantial production-growth outlook not laid out in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects FY2027 avocado production to exceed 10 million pounds, an approximately 30% increase over FY2026,” supported by new and future-bearing acreage.

surprises.description: Long-term debt reached $100.7 million while cash was just $2.2 million, leaving a tighter-looking balance sheet than the preview’s April figures of $94.1 million of debt and $0.9 million of cash. This adds pressure to the covenant and liquidity issue the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Long-term debt rose to $100.7 million as of July 31, 2026, up from $72.5 million at the end of FY2025, while cash stood at just $2.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Covenant and liquidity” as a key issue, noting “cash was $0.9M at 4/30/26” and that “Any commentary on headroom matters.”

surprises.description: Management gave a broader asset-monetization outlook than the preview described: it identified over $200 million in assets for monetization and anticipates about $180 million of real estate proceeds over seven fiscal years, along with $4 million of operating improvements in FY2027. These plans were not quantified in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “identified over $200 million in real estate, non-strategic land and water rights for monetization” and anticipates “~$180 million in real estate proceeds over seven fiscal years plus $4 million in operating improvements in FY2027.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA was positive, meeting management’s explicit Q2 commitment to positive adjusted EBITDA in Q3, even though the $3.9 million amount was below the preview’s base scenario.

Fresh lemon pricing was $19.88 per carton, consistent with the preview’s roughly $19-or-higher expectation; Q3 volume of 1.373 million cartons also cleared the preview’s roughly 1.3 million-carton threshold.
The Windfall Farms sale was still expected to close September 14, as the preview anticipated.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $233 million, above the preview’s $220.5 million consensus and even its $226–230 million buy-side bar. The beat was meaningful, though narrower against the higher buy-side range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Revenue rose 35% year-over-year to $233 million,” and the result was “exceeding expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus for Q2 revenue: $220.5M”; the preview also says “the buy-side bar sits higher, around $226–230M.”

surprises.description: GBV topped $3 billion, above the $2.86 billion forecast, with 45% growth versus the expected 37%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total GBV … grew 45% year-over-year to more than $3 billion in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross Booking Volume … $2.86B (+37%).”

surprises.description: The FY27 non-GAAP operating income outlook rose to $82–86 million from the prior $76–80 million range, an increase the preview did not specifically anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[The company] raised its … non-GAAP operating income guidance to $82-86 million (9% margin), marking the second raise this year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 non-GAAP operating income: $76M – $80M.”

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP operating margin was 7%: above the preview’s 6.4% margin implied by the company’s guide, but below the preview’s 8%-or-more catalyst threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin improved to 7% from 5% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin vs. the 6.4% guide”; the catalyst checklist says “Non-GAAP operating margin of 8% or more.”

surprises.description: Payment volume grew 34%, just below the preview’s 35%-or-more threshold for a positive surprise, although growth accelerated from Q1’s 29%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Payment volumes reached $1.3 billion (up 34%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Payment volume growth of 35% or more would be a positive surprise.”

surprises.description: The company raised FY27 revenue guidance to $927–933 million, within the preview’s $925–935 million bogey. The size of the raise was therefore broadly as anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[The company] raised its full-year FY27 revenue guidance to $927-933 million (32% growth at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The full preview’s bogey is $925–935M”; the checklist says “FY27 revenue raised to $925M or more.”

surprises.description: Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow turned positive at $28 million, far better than the preview’s latest stated TTM figure of about $2 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow turned positive at $28 million on a trailing basis versus a $33 million burn a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Free cash flow … trailing-twelve-month FCF about +$2M.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP gross margin exceeded 75% for the first time, with a 200-basis-point year-over-year improvement; the preview did not flag this outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin exceeded 75% for the first time in company history (up 200 bps year-over-year).”

surprises.description: Navan said its AI agent resolved about 60% of customer interactions and that its own AI models rose to half of usage, with management attributing structural gross-margin gains to the agent. The preview did not anticipate this operating update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI agent Ava resolved approximately 60% of customer interactions in Q2, driving structural gross margin gains, with Navan-owned AI models rising to 50% of usage from 30% in Q1.”

surprises.description: The sales-led enterprise business reported $4 billion of new signed GBV over the trailing 12 months, up 60% year over year, a strong forward indicator not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New signed GBV for the sales-led growth (SLG) enterprise business reached $4 billion over the trailing 12 months, up 60% versus Q2 last year, serving as a leading indicator of future revenue.”

surprises.description: The company reported that RFP volume tripled and that it had added five S&P 500 customers since last quarter, alongside rising win rates and average selling prices. The preview had not flagged these sales indicators.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RFP volume tripled in the first half of the year versus the prior year, and the company now serves 50 companies in the S&P 500, up from 45 last quarter, with rising win rates and ASPs.”

surprises.description: Product-led growth revenue more than doubled and subscription revenue grew 39%, stronger product-stream updates that were not addressed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Product-led growth revenue more than doubled year-over-year” and “subscription revenue was $21 million (up 39%).”

surprises.description: Navan disclosed a BoomPop acquisition aimed at meetings and events, a category described as roughly 30% of business-travel TAM. The deal is expected to contribute very little revenue and drag on FY27 operating income before becoming accretive in FY28, creating an unanticipated near-term earnings cost alongside the expansion opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The BoomPop acquisition targets the meetings and events category (roughly 30% of business travel TAM) with ~30% savings rates, but will have only very low-single-digit revenue impact and mid-single-digit operating income drag in FY27 before becoming accretive in FY28.”

in_line: FY27 revenue guidance of $927–933 million landed within the preview’s $925–935 million bogey, so the anticipated raise to at least $925 million occurred broadly as expected.

surprises.description: The preview’s base case expected the CooperSurgical process to continue without a definitive agreement, while the Board instead ended the review and chose to retain the business. That removes the potential sale the preview described as the largest driver, although the preview did identify retention as a bear-case possibility.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board unanimously concluded its strategic review and decided to retain CooperSurgical rather than sell it,” saying offers did not reflect intrinsic value.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case was “CSI ‘advancing, no definitive agreement’”; the preview also said a bear case could involve “talk of retaining CSI.”

surprises.description: The Q4 EPS range implies FY26 non-GAAP EPS of about $4.51–$4.55 after the reported $2.31 for the first half and $1.15 in Q3, below the preview’s expected FY26 range of $4.58–$4.66. Q4 guidance also cites investment spending, FX and lower tariff refunds as margin pressures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 guidance calls for … non-GAAP EPS of $1.05-$1.09,” with margins pressured by “increased CooperVision commercial investments, FX headwinds, and lower tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY26 non-GAAP EPS guide was $4.58–$4.66 and that maintaining it was the “minimum.”

surprises.description: The two reported segment revenues sum to about $1.066 billion, below the preview’s $1.10 billion Q3 consensus. That is roughly a $34 million, or 3%, shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: CooperVision revenue was “$717 million” and CooperSurgical revenue was “$349 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $1.10B (street range $1.10–1.12B).”

surprises.description: CooperVision revenue was essentially flat year over year, below the preview’s expectation for about 4% organic growth. Management attributed the Americas shortfall to channel destocking, said underlying U.S. consumption remained mid-single-digit, and expected a similar inventory reduction in Q4—so the reported weakness and its continuation are inventory-driven rather than evidence of weaker underlying U.S. demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: CooperVision revenue was “essentially flat year-over-year at $717 million”; management said its guidance reduction was “entirely destock-related,” underlying U.S. consumption was “steady in the mid-single digits,” and a similar inventory reduction was expected in Q4.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “CVI organic ~4%” and its catalyst checklist called for “CVI organic growth of at least 4%.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS of $1.15 exceeded the preview’s $1.11–$1.12 estimate range, extending the company’s streak of consensus beats. However, about $0.03 came from tariff refunds, making EPS excluding that benefit roughly $1.12 and close to the estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS grew 4% to $1.15 (including ~$0.03 from tariff refunds),” marking the “11th consecutive quarter of beating consensus earnings expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview gave Q3 non-GAAP diluted EPS consensus of “$1.11–$1.12.”

surprises.description: The favorable HMRC resolution produced a substantial tax benefit and will provide non-GAAP tax benefits for at least 10 more years, an additional source of earnings support not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company recognized a discrete tax benefit of “~$307 million” after favorable resolution of an HMRC examination, “providing non-GAAP tax benefits for at least 10 additional years.”

surprises.description: The company’s capital return was more concrete and sizable than the preview’s general expectation of an aggressive posture: it repurchased $339 million in Q3 and added $1 billion to its authorization.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Board approved a “$1 billion increase to share repurchase authorization,” bringing capacity to “~$1.5 billion”; Cooper repurchased “$339 million of shares in Q3 and $445 million year-to-date,” while keeping leverage below 2x.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged the “size of buybacks executed in Q3 and any new authorization” and noted management had promised an “aggressive” posture. It also cited only $13 million of repurchases in Q2.

surprises.description: Free cash flow was exceptionally strong, reaching a quarterly record and putting year-to-date cash generation well ahead of the prior year. The preview did not set a free-cash-flow expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 free cash flow reached a record $273 million,” bringing year-to-date free cash flow to “$528 million (up 86% year-over-year).”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a scheduled increase in GILTI that is expected to raise the non-GAAP effective tax rate by about two percentage points in FY27, a future earnings headwind not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A scheduled GILTI increase is expected to raise the non-GAAP effective tax rate from roughly 15.5% this year to roughly 17.5% in fiscal 2027.”

surprises.description: The call reported flat PARAGARD revenue while a non-hormonal IUD competitor’s launch approaches, adding a specific competitive risk that the preview did not identify.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PARAGARD revenue was flat amid an approaching non-hormonal IUD competitor launch.”

in_line: The Q4 revenue range, combined with first-half revenue and the roughly $1.066 billion Q3 total implied by the segment figures, points to FY26 revenue broadly around the preview’s prior $4.28–$4.32 billion guide; the provided facts do not establish a clear full-year revenue shortfall.

surprises.description: Skillsoft cut FY27 revenue guidance to $380–390 million from $388–406 million, below the preview’s expectation that the range would be reaffirmed. Management attributed the cut to accelerating weakness and AI disruption in its coding-focused consumer business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lowered its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to $380-390 million from the prior $388-406 million range, driven by accelerating weakness and AI disruption in its coding-focused consumer business.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 guidance reaffirmed at $388–406M”; the preview also said to watch whether management narrowed toward the low end, “which would amount to a cut.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was well above the preview’s estimated $26–28 million, reaching $33.4 million. The 34% margin, up from 31%, was aided by a 12% reduction in selling and marketing expenses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA from continuing operations rose 7% to $33.4 million, with margin expanding to 34% from 31% a year earlier, aided by a 12% cut in selling and marketing expenses.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: No published consensus found (my estimate ~$26–28M).”

surprises.description: Quarterly dollar retention was 95%, below the preview’s highlighted bull-case marker of a second straight quarter at or above 100%. Although it improved from 94% a year earlier, LTM DRR slipped to 98% from 99%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Dollar retention rate improved to 95% from 94% year-over-year, though the LTM DRR slipped to 98% from 99%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A second straight quarter at or above 100% would support the go-to-market redesign”; the bull scenario also specified “DRR at or above 105% again.”

surprises.description: Skillsoft reported evidence of growing AI-product adoption that the preview did not specifically anticipate: Casey conversation-simulator learners and using organizations increased, and AI Coach was already in pilots.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Casey conversation-simulator learners up 23% year-over-year and using organizations up 9%, plus AI Coach now piloted by seven organizations out of 30-plus early-access customers.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $98.2 million was close to the $99.0 million consensus and within the preview’s $98–100 million base-case range.
Q2 free cash flow was negative $20.5 million, consistent with the preview’s expectation of seasonal cash consumption; management said it should reverse into positive territory in Q4.
Management continued to identify debt maturities/refinancing as its top financial priority, consistent with the preview’s base case of priority language without a concrete refinancing step.

Despite lowering revenue guidance, Skillsoft maintained FY27 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $108–116 million and free cash flow guidance of $14–22 million, in line with the preview’s stated EBITDA midpoint and FCF range.

surprises.description: Q4 diluted EPS was $0.02, half the preview’s current $0.04 estimate. Full-year EPS was also $0.08 versus the published $0.13 consensus, though the preview cautioned that the annual estimate looked stale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 net income fell to $666,000 ($0.02) from $2.4 million ($0.09)”; full-year net income was “$2.8 million ($0.08 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) | $0.04 (TipRanks)” for Q4; the preview also lists full-year FY2026 consensus of “$0.13 EPS” and says it “looks stale.”

surprises.description: Gross margin strengthened more than the preview’s discussion anticipated: FY2026 margin rose 260 basis points to 51.9%, and Q4 reached a record 53%, with platform revenue making up a larger share of sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2026 gross margin improved 260 basis points to 51.9%, with Q4 hitting a record 53%, driven by platform revenue rising to 43% of total revenue from 39% a year ago.”

surprises.description: The AI/MCP opportunity showed concrete commercial traction rather than just the pipeline cited in the preview: Q4 AI-related bookings reached about $800,000, MCP deals were mostly upsells, and about three-quarters of MCP usage was on paid plans. The reported average contract value on MCP/agentic AI access roughly doubled.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI-related bookings reached about $800,000 in Q4, representing 125% sequential growth”; “Adding MCP/agentic AI access roughly doubled contract value on average,” MCP deals were “almost entirely upsells,” and “about three-quarters of MCP usage now comes from paid plans.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said an AI/MCP pipeline “exceeding $1 million” existed and flagged “Closed MCP/AI revenue, not a restated pipeline” as a catalyst to watch.

surprises.description: Management provided a positive FY2027 profitability outlook despite giving no revenue guidance: it expects further adjusted EBITDA and cash-flow growth. The preview identified FY2027 framing as a key watch but described no guidance as the base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided to further EBITDA and cash flow growth in fiscal 2027 despite offering no top-line guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “Any FY2027 guidance or growth algorithm” and described the base case as “no guidance.”

surprises.description: The company ended with more cash than the preview’s estimate and said it was evaluating capital-return options. Management also described the stock as far below fair value, although it did not report an authorized buyback.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company holds nearly $13 million in cash with no debt after funding four quarters of Scite earn-out payments,” and management said the stock was “trading far below fair value” while “evaluating buybacks and other capital options.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “$12.1M of net cash” and said a buyback authorization would be “a clear move,” noting that none existed yet.

surprises.description: Net platform deployments rebounded from the weak Q3 pace, and average sales price also rose. The preview had highlighted the Q3 drop in deployments but did not forecast a recovery of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company added 105 net new platform deployments during the year (29 in Q4) to reach 1,276 total, while average sales price increased 4.7%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “Net new deployments fell to +15 from +47 in Q2” and flagged churned versus new B2B ARR as a key metric to watch.

surprises.description: Full-year revenue came in slightly above consensus, although revenue still edged down year over year as lower transaction revenue outweighed platform subscription growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total fiscal 2026 revenue declined slightly to $48.3 million from $49.1 million in fiscal 2025,” as transaction revenue fell 8.7% and platform subscription revenue grew roughly 10%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed full-year FY2026 consensus revenue of “$48.17M.”

in_line: Exit ARR was $22.5 million versus the preview’s approximately $22.4 million estimate; B2B ARR was about $16.2 million, meeting the preview’s stated threshold.
Q4 transaction revenue’s year-over-year decline narrowed to 6.7%, consistent with the preview’s expectation that it would narrow to mid-single digits.
Management gave no top-line guidance, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the company might provide no guidance.

surprises.description: Gloo reported Q2 revenue of $46.6 million, above the roughly $44 million expected. The beat was about 6% versus the preview’s consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 fiscal 2026 revenue grew 188% year-over-year to $46.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue (Q2) … Consensus ~$44M.”

surprises.description: The Q3 outlook calls for $55 million of revenue, above the preview’s implied expectation of about $52 million. However, adjusted EBITDA is guided to a $3.5 million loss rather than the breakeven the preview identified as the expected target; management now expects adjusted EBITDA profitability in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for revenue of $55 million and adjusted EBITDA of -$3.5 million”; management committed to “reaching adjusted EBITDA profitability in Q4 2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “That is roughly +28% over H1's ~$85.5M, or about Q3 ~$52M and Q4 ~$57M”; “The EBITDA bridge to Q3 breakeven”; “Management volunteers organic growth and holds the Q3 breakeven date.”

surprises.description: Instead of reaffirming the $195 million full-year revenue outlook, Gloo raised guidance by $5 million to $200 million. The preview’s consensus matched the prior $195 million guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance by $5 million to $200 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 revenue … Company guidance … $195.0M … Consensus $195.1M”; “FY2026 $195M reaffirmation.”

surprises.description: The preview estimated July 31 cash at roughly $42–46 million and flagged cash below $40 million as a dilution risk. Gloo reported $39.3 million, below both that estimate and the stated risk threshold, although the $23.7 million net offering was above the preview’s roughly $21 million estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gloo raised $23.7 million net in a follow-on offering [and] ended the quarter with $39.3 million in cash.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My rough math puts July 31 cash at about $42–46M”; “Cash below about $40M … would reopen dilution risk”; “raised about $21M net in July.”

surprises.description: The preview treated a clean organic-growth figure as a key disclosure and said silence would be negative. The reported facts provide no organic-growth percentage and instead say the platform revenue increases were driven substantially by acquisitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: Platform solutions revenue rose 209% and platform revenue rose 170%, “both driven substantially by acquisitions like Masterworks, Westfall Gold, and EMD.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A clean organic number is the most useful disclosure this print could offer. Silence on it would be a negative.”

surprises.description: Cost of revenue fell to 64.0% of revenue, 10.8 percentage points lower than a year earlier. The preview raised concern that the shift toward services could weigh on the business mix, but did not anticipate this margin improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cost of revenue improved 10.8 percentage points to 64.0% of total revenue from 74.8% a year earlier, aided by scale and favorable acquisition mix.”

surprises.description: Gloo recorded a $4.4 million restructuring charge in Q2, primarily for severance tied to integrating business lines. The preview did not flag this charge.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company took a $4.4 million restructuring charge in Q2, primarily for severance related to integrating business lines.”

surprises.description: Gloo extended its $13.2 million senior secured loan to April 2028, a financing-maturity extension not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[Gloo] extended its $13.2 million senior secured loan to April 2028.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that Gloo now has more than 30 customers with over $1 million in annual contract value and its first customer above $10 million in annual contract value—customer-scale milestones the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company now has more than 30 customers with over $1 million in annual contract value and reached its first customer exceeding $10 million in annual contract value.”

surprises.description: Management said future acquisitions would target a 20–25% cash structure, a specific acquisition-financing approach not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management is “targeting a 20-25% cash structure for future deals.”

in_line: Revenue growth remained substantially acquisition-driven, consistent with the preview’s warning that acquisitions formed a major part of reported growth.
The reported shift toward Platform Solutions was consistent with the preview’s expectation that the mix would move toward that segment.

surprises.description: The cash management fee rate was 55 bps, below the preview’s 56–57 bps base-case range. It reached, but did not fall below, the preview’s 55 bps warning threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The annualized cash management fee rate fell 6 basis points year-over-year to 55 basis points,” driven by lower Fed funds rates and higher client incentive costs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base case expected a “fee rate 0.56–0.57%”; the preview also said “below 0.55%” would signal structural pressure.

surprises.description: Management disclosed a one-time employer tax expense of $3–$3.5 million next quarter from former employees exercising options, an expense the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management flagged “a one-time employer tax expense of $3 million to $3.5 million next quarter tied to former employee option exercises.”

surprises.description: Management said the measured Home Lending rollout will continue to weigh on margins near term. The preview mentioned Home Lending as an overhang but did not anticipate this specific near-term margin pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expects near-term margin headwinds from the measured Home Lending rollout.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Home Lending among the topics in a legal investigation, but did not forecast near-term margin headwinds from the rollout.

surprises.description: The company repurchased 3.3 million shares for about $30 million, a modest increase from the prior quarter’s 3 million-plus shares for about $27 million. The preview highlighted buyback pace as a catalyst but did not specify an expected quarterly amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company “repurchased 3.3 million shares for approximately $30 million during the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted Q1 repurchases of “3M+ shares … (~$27M)” and said buyback pace and authorization would be watched.

in_line: Revenue was $91.9 million, essentially matching the preview’s roughly $92 million consensus anchor.

Quarter-end platform assets of $99 billion and cash management assets of $44.9 billion were broadly consistent with the preview’s reported June balances and expectation of cash assets near $44–45 billion.
Adjusted EBITDA margin was 41%, above the preview’s bear-case threshold of below 38%.
GAAP diluted EPS of $0.10 fell within the preview’s widely dispersed $0.08–$0.14 estimates; the preview had cautioned that feeds mixed GAAP and adjusted conventions.
The preview expected June’s cash outflows to moderate or turn positive; management said targeted incentives improved July and August cash net deposits to their best level since March.

surprises.description: Q2 EPS was $4.40, far above the $2.48 consensus and the preview’s $3.60 base scenario, though just below its $4.50 bull scenario. Q2 net income was $139.3 million, compared with $26.8 million a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net income jumped to $139.3 million from $26.8 million (EPS of $4.40 vs $0.67).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) $2.48”; the preview’s “Base” scenario estimated EPS of “~$3.60” and its “Bull” scenario “~$4.50.”

surprises.description: The newbuilding program’s estimated value had appreciated at least 30%, to roughly $3.8–$3.9 billion. That is a positive valuation update beyond the preview’s discussion of the 26-vessel order and its funding needs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 26-vessel, roughly $3.1 billion newbuilding program has already appreciated at least 30% (estimated ~$3.8-3.9 billion in value).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “26 vessels on order (7 delivered); capex versus cash generation is the bear's argument.”

surprises.description: Management signaled that it is considering redeeming the $120 million Series E preferred shares, which could add $0.30–$0.40 per share to the bottom line. The preview did not flag this possible capital-structure move.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is considering redeeming the $120 million Series E perpetual preferred at a 9.25% coupon, which could add $0.30-$0.40 per share to the bottom line.”

surprises.description: The dividend total reported for calendar 2026 was $1.60, versus the preview’s cited $1.50 aggregate, and management signaled a further increase after the November strategy meeting. The preview characterized a release without a dividend headline as the normal pattern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company paid dividends totaling $1.60 per share in calendar 2026 ($0.60 plus $1.00), a yield near 4%, with management signaling a dividend increase to be announced after the November strategy meeting.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “2026 aggregate of $1.50 (+36% YoY)” and “A print without a dividend headline is the normal pattern.”

surprises.description: The pro forma fleet’s fair market value was about $4.9 billion, above the preview’s $4.6 billion figure, while reported cash was $466 million and net debt to capitalization was around 44.5%. This was a stronger balance-sheet and fleet-value update than the preview’s stated starting point.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The pro forma 81-vessel fleet has a fair market value of approximately $4.9 billion against $2 billion of debt, with net debt to capitalization around 44.5% and cash of $466 million (up $179 million year-over-year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Leverage and cash. Deleveraging is the balance-sheet story; fleet FMV was $4.6B.”

in_line: Forward committed earnings were approximately $3.5 billion, consistent with the preview’s statement that backlog was above $3.5 billion.
The sale of two older Suezmax tankers for over $100 million was anticipated in the preview; the reported net proceeds were $100 million, with the gain to be recorded in Q3.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue of $87.1M was about 39% above the preview’s $62.6M consensus estimate, a much larger result than the consensus figure implied. It also exceeded the preview’s roughly $80M base-case scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 revenue reached an all-time high of $87.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 2026 consensus” revenue: “$62.6M”; base scenario: “Revenue ~$80M.”

surprises.description: EPS of $0.75 beat the preview’s $0.58 consensus by about 29%. It was below the preview’s $0.90–$1.00 base-case scenario, however.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net income was $34.8 million (EPS $0.75).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (basic)” consensus: “$0.58”; base scenario: “EPS (basic) ~$0.90–1.00.”

surprises.description: The reported Suezmax market was exceptionally strong: rates exceeded $145,000/day by quarter-end and at times topped $200,000/day. The preview flagged spot rates as a key driver, but did not anticipate Suezmax rates at these levels.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Suezmax daily rates surged to over $145,000 by end of Q2 2026 … and at times exceeded $200,000/day.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Realized spot rates by segment (MR, Suezmax, drybulk). This drives the print.”

surprises.description: Fleet utilization fell to 73.5%, well below the preview’s cited Q1 level of 88.7%, with six drydockings causing technical off-hire and seven more drydockings still scheduled by year-end. The preview had flagged drydock off-hire as a downside risk, but the reported utilization and continuing schedule show a substantial operational drag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operational utilization fell to 73.5% due to 6 drydockings, with technical off-hire consuming 10.7% of fleet calendar days and 7 more drydockings scheduled by year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 was 88.7% on 1,764 days”; the bear scenario cited “Drydock off-hire.”

surprises.description: Costs were a meaningful counterweight to the strong rates: voyage costs rose $14.4M and drydocking costs reached $7.5M, pressuring margins. The preview discussed strong spot-rate scenarios and drydock off-hire, but did not flag this scale of cost pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Voyage costs rose $14.4 million (58% more spot days plus Brent averaging $97 vs $67), drydocking costs hit $7.5 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s scenarios described strong spot-rate capture, including “MR realized above $48k/day,” without estimating these cost increases.

surprises.description: Some IMPP dry bulk vessels remained stranded in the Strait of Hormuz from late May, an adverse company-specific operating issue not identified in the preview. The preview discussed Hormuz-related supply and a possible return of stranded or idling vessels, but not IMPP vessels being stuck.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Some dry bulk vessels remain stranded in the Strait of Hormuz since late May.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed “a reopening” that “could bring restocking demand and return ~186 stranded or idling vessels to supply,” but did not identify IMPP vessels as stranded.

surprises.description: The company sold the Suez Enchanted after quarter-end for a profit exceeding $32M, an unexpected asset-sale gain that the preview did not mention.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company sold the 2007-built tanker Suez Enchanted in August for a profit exceeding $32 million.”

surprises.description: Cash and time deposits reached $245.2M, compared with the preview’s cited $212.6M liquidity level, and subsequently rose to roughly $260M. This was a stronger liquidity position than the preview’s starting figure suggested, while remaining debt-free was consistent with the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash and time deposits rose to $245.2 million as of June 30 and have since increased to roughly $260 million, with the company remaining fully debt-free.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Liquidity $212.6M, zero debt.”

in_line: The preview’s base scenario anticipated a record quarter; Q2 revenue was reported as an all-time high, although it exceeded the preview’s revenue estimates.

surprises.description: Champions reported $15.2 million of revenue, slightly above the preview’s $15.05 million consensus despite the preview’s caution that services growth could moderate. The $150,000 gap is small.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue grew approximately 9% year-over-year to $15.2 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q1 FY27 Consensus | $15.05M”; the preview also says consensus assumes “about 9% sequential growth” and flags “moderate” services language as a caution.

surprises.description: Oncology services margin reached 51%, above the preview’s 47–49% base-case range and its 48% threshold for evidence that in-housing benefits were structural. It was below the preview’s roughly 52% bull case, so the positive gap was meaningful but not large.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oncology services margin improving to 51% from 43%”; gross margin also “expanded to 50% from 43%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario projected “Services margin | 47–49%”; the preview said “Holding 48% or better would suggest the in-housing benefit is structural.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was about $671,000, more than twice the preview’s $300,000 base-case estimate. The preview had no consensus figure, but its own base case anticipated a smaller positive result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA surged to approximately $671,000 from just $59,000,” marking “the fifth consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario projected “Adj. EBITDA | ~$0.3M”; it described the fifth positive quarter as expected.

surprises.description: Data licensing produced $893,000—more than the entire fiscal 2026 total—making the quarter’s licensing contribution more substantial than the preview’s expectation of lumpy, smaller agreements suggested. Management cautioned that the revenue will remain lumpy.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data licensing revenue reached $893,000 in the quarter—more than all of fiscal 2026 combined,” though management cautioned it “will remain lumpy.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the line was “lumpy” and that FY26 had shifted to “smaller licensing agreements across more customers”; its bull case required “at least one data-licensing deal recognized.”

surprises.description: Cash ended at about $4.4 million, just below the preview’s $4.5 million-or-higher catalyst benchmark and down from $4.9 million at year-end. The shortfall was small, and cash remained above the preview’s roughly $4 million level of greater concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with approximately $4.4 million of cash and no debt,” after “using about $500,000 of cash on working capital movements.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The catalyst checklist highlighted “Cash at or above $4.5M vs. below $3.5M”; the preview said a print “below about $4M with no financing or partnership announced” would shift the story toward financing risk.

in_line: The fifth consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA was consistent with the preview’s expectation that the streak would continue.

Management was still pursuing outside funding or a licensing partnership for Corellia, as the preview described; no completed financing or named partner was reported, consistent with its base case of no financing news.

surprises.description: SHOE cut FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $0.75–$0.90 from $1.40–$1.60, and lowered sales guidance to $1.1–$1.111 billion from $1.125–$1.147 billion. Gross-margin guidance also fell from about 34% to 32.5–32.7%, a much steeper reset than the preview’s base case of reaffirmed guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company lowered full-year fiscal 2026 guidance to net sales of $1.1-1.111 billion (down 2-3%), adjusted EPS of $0.75-0.90, and gross margin of 32.5-32.7% (390-410 bps of compression).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 guidance (reaffirmed at Q1 on May 21, 2026): Net sales $1.125–$1.147B (−1% to +1%); Adjusted EPS $1.40–$1.60; Gross margin ~34% (−260 bps vs. FY25).”

surprises.description: Q2 sales were well below the preview’s expected level: $284.3 million versus consensus of $299.19 million, with comps down 7.1% rather than the preview’s estimated 2–3% decline. The call also said sales fell short of the company’s own expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 fiscal 2026 net sales declined 7.2% to $284.3 million with comparable store sales down 7.1%, falling short of the company's own expectations.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | $299.19M”; “Comparable sales | ~−2% to −3% (preview's estimate).”

surprises.description: Gross margin fell to 31.9%, down 690 basis points—worse than the preview’s 33.5–34.0% estimate and more severe than the CFO’s prior warning that compression could exceed 500 basis points. The call attributed much of the decline to lapping a temporary pricing benefit, with the rest from promotions and inventory liquidation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit margin fell 690 basis points to 31.9%, with roughly 390 bps of the 630 bps merchandise margin decline attributed to lapping a temporary prior-year pre-tariff pricing benefit and about 240 bps from promotions and inventory liquidation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ~33.5–34.0% (preview's estimate)”; “CFO warned Q2 would be the steepest gross margin compression quarter of the year, ‘potentially exceeding 500 basis points’ Y/Y.”

surprises.description: Reported diluted EPS was $0.23, below the preview’s $0.32 adjusted EPS consensus estimate; net income fell to $6.3 million from $19.2 million a year earlier. The reported EPS and preview estimate are not explicitly identified on the same accounting basis, so the comparison is not perfectly like-for-like.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net income dropped to $6.3 million ($0.23 per diluted share) from $19.2 million ($0.70 per diluted share) a year earlier, a roughly 67% decline in EPS.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Diluted EPS (adj.) | $0.32.”

surprises.description: The preview flagged August trends as a key data point but gave no expected direction; August comps improved to down 2.7% from down 7.1% in Q2. Even so, management expects roughly flat Q3 comps, growth deferred to Q4, and second-half comps in a range of down 1% to up 1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Early Q3 trends improved materially, with August comparable store sales declining only 2.7% versus the 7.1% Q2 decline, and management expects roughly flat comps in Q3 with growth deferred to Q4”; “guiding second-half comps to a range of down 1% to up 1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A quantified August or September comp is the most useful data point on the call.”

surprises.description: Management said it does not assume the promotional environment will improve in the second half and expects margin recovery toward the historical 35% range only in fiscal 2027. That points to a longer margin recovery than the preview’s warning that Q2 would be the steepest compression quarter suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management does not assume any improvement in the promotional environment for the second half”; “expecting margin recovery toward the historical ~35% range only in fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CFO warned Q2 would be the steepest gross margin compression quarter of the year, ‘potentially exceeding 500 basis points’ Y/Y.”

surprises.description: The company now aims for the low end of its inventory-reduction target, about $50 million by year-end, because sales were weaker. That is less ambitious than the preview’s $50–65 million reduction range, though the new target remains within it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory ended down 5.0% to $426.6 million, with management targeting an approximately $50 million reduction by year-end but now aiming for the low end of that range due to weaker sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Inventory down $50–65M by year-end.”

surprises.description: Online comps rose 18.8% even as store comps fell 9.5%, an unexpectedly strong digital result amid weak store sales; the preview did not provide an online-sales expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “E-commerce was a bright spot with comparable online sales up 18.8% in Q2, even as comparable store sales fell 9.5%.”

surprises.description: Management identified store traffic as the core problem even though conversion reached multi-year highs in both banners, and said it would intensify advertising rather than rely on deeper discounting. The preview discussed whether promotions would be lighter or the company would buy comps, but did not anticipate this specific traffic-and-advertising response.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Store traffic was identified as the core problem while conversion improved to multi-year highs in both banners, prompting a shift toward intensified advertising rather than deeper discounting.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Better than −500 bps suggests promotions were lighter than feared; worse suggests the company is buying comps.”

surprises.description: Rather than leaving the preview’s anticipated CCC discussion unresolved, Copart announced an agreement to acquire ACV Auctions. The offer is all cash, funded from cash on hand with no financing conditions, and Adair said it does not preclude future acquisitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: Copart “had agreed to acquire ACV Auctions”; the transaction is “an all-cash tender offer funded from cash on hand with no financing conditions”; Adair stated “that the ACV deal does not preclude future acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Copart is reportedly bidding against GTCR and Veritas Capital for CCC. A deal at a premium could run $5–6B or more, above Copart's $4.2B cash position, and would add debt to a historically debt-free company. Expect questions on it; a clear answer is unlikely.”

surprises.description: Q1 revenue was $23.5 million, about 32% above the $17.85 million consensus and also above the preview’s $19.5–$21.0 million bull-case range. It set an all-time record, exceeding the expected seasonal-quarter inflection by a wide margin.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue hit an all-time record of $23.5 million, up 70% year-over-year and 52% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $17.85M” consensus; the bull scenario was “$19.5–21.0M.”

surprises.description: Reported EPS was $0.41, far above the $0.15 consensus. The preview cautioned that a tax benefit could affect GAAP EPS, but the call facts also report a sharp increase in operating income; no tax-benefit detail is provided here to explain the EPS result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income surged to approximately $4.2 million ($0.41 per share) from $634,000 ($0.07 per share)”; operating income was “$5.2 million versus $364,000 a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) | $0.15”; the preview also said, “Do not treat a GAAP EPS beat driven by tax as an operating beat.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 45.8%, above the preview’s roughly 40% expectation and its 42% bull-case threshold, indicating a stronger recovery than anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved 9 percentage points to 45.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Reported gross margin vs. ~40%” and described the bull case as “reported gross margin at or above 42%.”

surprises.description: Management went beyond reaffirming the FY2029 targets already expected: it suggested the $150 million-plus revenue target could be reached sooner and be substantially larger. The preview anticipated reaffirmation, not this more ambitious revenue commentary.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management reaffirmed its FY2029 targets while “suggesting the revenue target could be reached sooner and be substantially larger.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management “reaffirmed three-year targets … of at least $150M revenue, 50% gross margin, and 30% operating margin by FY2029.”

surprises.description: The secured communications program appears to be gaining demand beyond the existing production outlook: customers are requesting a monthly production increase of more than 50%, alongside promised follow-on orders. The preview did not flag this program-specific upside.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A secured communications production contract for over 1,000 systems is seeing customer requests to increase monthly production by more than 50% alongside promised follow-on orders.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed substantial near-term backlog conversion and additional unfunded opportunity: about 65% of funded backlog is expected to convert within 12 months, while unfunded backlog visibility is described as multiple times the funded portion. The preview focused on the funded backlog balance, not this conversion and opportunity outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approximately 65% of the $129 million funded backlog is expected to convert to revenue within the next 12 months, with additional unfunded backlog visibility described as multiple times the funded portion.”

surprises.description: Satellite revenue rose more than 80% year over year and made up half of the quarter’s revenue. The preview provided no segment-level expectation for this business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Satellite programs generated $11.8 million (50% of revenue, up over 80% YoY).”

surprises.description: Nonspace DoD revenue also grew sharply, increasing more than 61% year over year and reaching nearly half of total revenue. The preview did not provide a segment-level expectation for this business.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nonspace DoD customers generated $11.1 million (47% of revenue, up over 61% YoY).”

surprises.description: SG&A fell to 18% of revenue from 26% despite a $0.5 million increase in absolute spending, showing stronger operating leverage than the preview specifically anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A fell to 18% of revenue from 26% a year earlier, demonstrating operating leverage despite a $0.5 million absolute increase in spending.”

surprises.description: The company reported approximately $73 million raised, including a $14 million green shoe after quarter-end, versus the preview’s estimate of about $62.5 million in gross company proceeds. The larger capital raise adds liquidity but also reflects more equity issuance than the preview described.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company completed a July secondary offering raising approximately $73 million (including $14 million from the green shoe after quarter-end).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “The company received about $62.5M gross from 1,086,957 new shares.”

in_line: Funded backlog reached $129 million, close to the preview’s approximately $120 million watchpoint and within its $120–130 million base-case range.
Management reaffirmed the FY2029 targets of $150 million-plus revenue, at least 50% gross margin, and at least 30% operating margin, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Bedding gross margin reached 13.6%, up from 10.5%, and management said the improvement was not helped by allocated tariff recoveries. The preview flagged bedding margin as a key risk because bedding had been diluting consolidated margin; the reported improvement was a favorable operational surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Bedding segment sales grew 13.2% to $31.8 million with gross margin expanding to 13.6% from 10.5%, a gain management said was not aided by any allocated tariff recoveries.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bedding gross margin. It was 8.9% in Q4, versus 19.5% for upholstery. Bedding drives the growth but dilutes consolidated margin.”

surprises.description: Management guided to break-even operating income and accelerating adjusted EBITDA in Q2, with sequentially consistent sales and modest year-over-year growth, and said it is targeting net cash by fiscal year-end. This was more constructive than the preview’s stated bear-case concern that management might revert to challenged-demand language without a sequential commitment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided to break-even operating income and accelerating adjusted EBITDA in Q2 with sequential sales consistency and modest year-over-year growth, targeting a net cash position by fiscal year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bear: Refund timing slips, or management reverts to ‘challenged demand’ language without a Q2 sequential commitment.”

surprises.description: Net debt ended Q1 at $3.1 million, well below the preview’s roughly $5 million estimate. The company used the full tariff recovery to pay off all higher-rate U.S. debt; free cash flow was also $7.8 million, versus negative $874,000 a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced net debt approximately 70% to $3.1 million from $10.9 million at fiscal 2026 year-end, using the full tariff recovery to pay off all higher-rate U.S. debt while retaining $13.3 million of low-rate China debt”; “Q1 free cash flow surged to $7.8 million from negative $874,000 a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net debt at 8/2/26 | ~$5M (from $10.8M)”; the preview also said net debt of $8M or more would suggest the refund slipped or working capital absorbed the cash.

surprises.description: Sales were $54 million, about $0.8 million above the $53.2 million consensus and the $51.6 million sequential-improvement floor. The beat was modest, though sales rose despite one fewer selling week.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net sales rose to $54 million from $50.7 million year-over-year despite one fewer selling week.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $53.20M”; “Q1 revenue floor | ~$51.6M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin excluding tariff recoveries was 15.6%, above the preview’s roughly 14% expectation if the refund was booked outside cost of goods sold. The preview anticipated the roughly $7 million refund, but not this higher margin excluding it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding tariff recoveries, gross profit was $8.4 million (15.6% of sales), up roughly 17% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A COGS credit would inflate gross margin, while other income would leave it near 14%.”

surprises.description: EPS was $0.47, modestly above the $0.44 consensus even though the preview already expected EPS to be driven by a roughly $7 million tariff refund. The headline result therefore beat expectations, but the refund itself was not a surprise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 net income was $6 million ($0.47 per diluted share) versus a net loss of $231,000 (-$0.02 per share) in the prior year, though results included approximately $7 million in one-time IEPA tariff recoveries.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS | $0.44”; “Driven by a one-time ~$7.0M IEEPA tariff refund, not operations.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that CFO Ken Bolling will retire effective September 14 and COO Mary Beth Hunsberger will succeed him, with Bolling consulting through December. The preview gave no indication of a leadership transition; the shareholder implications are not specified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CFO Ken Bolling will retire and be succeeded by COO Mary Beth Hunsberger effective September 14, 2026, with Bolling staying on in a consulting capacity through December.”

surprises.description: The call highlighted approximately $95 million of U.S. federal net operating loss carryforwards, associated with about $20 million in future tax benefits. These tax assets were not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company holds approximately $95 million in U.S. federal net operating loss carryforwards (~$20 million in future tax benefits).”

surprises.description: The company also disclosed that it owns its Stokesdale, North Carolina hub, estimated to be worth about $40 million against a $12 million book value. This potentially valuable real-estate asset was not mentioned in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[The company] owns its Stokesdale, NC hub with an estimated $40 million market value versus $12 million book value.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA excluding the tariff recovery was positive $566,000, in line with the preview’s break-even-to-positive guidance and its base-case range of roughly $0.0–$0.5 million.
The approximately $7 million tariff recovery was anticipated, and the company reported receiving and using the full recovery.
Bedding sales growth was consistent with the preview’s expectation that bedding would drive growth.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $164.3 million, above the preview’s $158–160 million consensus range and the $158.2–162.2 million company-implied range. Full-year revenue also finished at $644.1 million, above the $638–642 million guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue grew 12% to a record $164.3 million”; “full-year FY2026 revenue rose 15.4% to $644.1 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q4 revenue consensus “~$158–160M”; company-implied range “$158.2M–$162.2M”; FY2026 guidance “$638M–$642M.”

surprises.description: FY2027 revenue guidance of $700–715 million is above the preview’s $680–700 million expectation and clears its $685 million bar at the low end. The $90–94 million EBITDA guide also meets the preview’s $90 million bar, though it overlaps the preview’s $88–93 million expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FY2027 guidance projects revenue of $700-715 million” and “adjusted EBITDA of $90-94 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Preview expectation: “$680M–$700M revenue and $88M–$93M EBITDA”; “clean reaction” bar: “at least $685M revenue and $90M EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EBITDA was below the preview’s consensus, and the 12.3% margin came in below both the roughly 13.0% expectation and the 12.5–13.4% company-implied range. Management cited client training, work transfers, and higher fuel prices as pressures, rather than the preview’s examples of Egypt buildout or AI-platform investment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EBITDA slipped to $20.2 million (12.3% margin) from $20.5 million (13.9%)”; it was “pressured by new client training costs, nearshore-to-offshore work transfers, and higher fuel prices.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q4 adjusted EBITDA “~$20.8M” and margin “~13.0%”; company-implied margin “12.5%–13.4%.” The preview said compression should be attributed to “investment (Egypt buildout, AI platform spend), not to client pricing.”

surprises.description: The Sierra partnership produced more concrete evidence of deployment and customer results than the preview’s base case, which expected Sierra to remain qualitative. The call cited double-digit deployments across five verticals and proof-of-concept resolution rates up to 40%+, with CSAT above 4.7.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Double-digit client AI agent deployments across five verticals,” with resolution rates of “20%+ (Philippine Airlines) to 40%+ (BJ's Wholesale)” and “CSAT scores above 4.7 out of 5.0.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said investors wanted “quantified results” and that in the base case “Sierra stays qualitative.”

surprises.description: Health Tech substantially exceeded the company’s $100 million target, reaching $114 million for FY2026 after 38% full-year growth. The preview did not flag a Health Tech target or forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Health Tech ... grew 42% in Q4 to $29.4 million and 38% for the full year to $114 million, surpassing the company's $100 million target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$100 million target.”

surprises.description: IBEX reported substantial client wins and expansion: nine new trophy logos in Q4 and double-digit growth among its largest client groups. The preview did not set expectations for logo additions or large-client growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company added nine new trophy logos in Q4 (17 for the full year), with revenue from its top five, top 10, and top 25 clients growing 24%, 22%, and 15% respectively.”

surprises.description: Management said the Q4 tax rate of 10% was helped by discrete benefits and guided to a normalized 20–22% rate going forward. That signals a future earnings headwind not addressed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4's tax rate fell to 10% from 19% due to discrete benefits,” while management guided to “a normalized 20-22% tax rate going forward.”

surprises.description: Full-year free cash flow reached a record and net cash more than doubled from a year earlier, providing a stronger cash-position update than the preview anticipated. The preview instead focused on buyback pace and expected capex of $25–30 million; reported capex of $27.8 million was within that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year free cash flow reached a record $31.2 million and net cash improved to $30.9 million (from $13.7 million a year earlier),” while capex was “$27.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for checking capex “against the FY26 capex raise to $25M–$30M.”

in_line: Q4 adjusted EPS was $0.85, matching the preview’s $0.85 consensus.
FY2026 capex of $27.8 million was within the preview’s anticipated $25–30 million range.

surprises.description: Oracle reported non-GAAP EPS of $1.92, well above the preview’s $1.74 consensus and its $1.72–$1.76 guidance range. The preview’s bull case was $1.80 or higher, so the result exceeded even that threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS rose 30% to $1.92.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | Consensus | $1.74 | Company guidance ... $1.72–$1.76”; the bull scenario was “$1.80+.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $19.3 billion was slightly above the $19.13 billion consensus and at the top of the preview’s base-case range. Oracle also grew revenue sequentially in Q1, breaking its historical pattern of a lighter Q1 after a record Q4—a seasonal development the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 total revenue reached a record $19.3 billion, up 30% year-over-year, and grew sequentially for the first time in a Q1, breaking the historical pattern of a lighter Q1 following a record Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total revenue | Consensus | $19.13B”; the base scenario was “$19.1–19.3B.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s expectation of roughly 43–44% non-GAAP operating margin, Oracle’s margin was roughly 42%, about flat year over year. That it held flat despite declining gross margins from the data-center ramp was better than the preview’s cited expectation that margins would step down, but it still missed the consensus margin estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income up 31% to $8.2 billion and operating margin holding roughly flat at 42% despite declining gross margins from data center ramp-up.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op. margin | ~43–44%”; the preview also said management guided to “step down” on the data-center ramp.

surprises.description: Q1 free cash flow was less negative than expected, at negative $5 billion versus the preview’s negative $8–12 billion estimate, even with $28 billion of CapEx. The preview had highlighted capital spending and financing as a key concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 CapEx was $28 billion, producing negative free cash flow of $5 billion, though cash flow from operations hit a record $23 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Expect Q1 FCF around negative $8–12B.”

surprises.description: Oracle raised its FY27 non-GAAP EPS outlook to $8.10, above the preview’s expected $8.05 reaffirmation. The revenue target remained around $90 billion, but Oracle now described it as “at least” $90 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year fiscal 2027 guidance to at least $90 billion in total revenue (up 34%) and $8.10 in non-GAAP EPS.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY27: $90B revenue (+34%) and $8.05 non-GAAP EPS, both reaffirmed in June.”

surprises.description: Oracle said it closed more than $30 billion in additional AI contracts without requiring additional capital from Oracle, using prepayments and bring-your-own-hardware arrangements. The preview highlighted funding risk and the roughly $70 billion net cash outlay, but did not anticipate this way of securing contracts without added Oracle capital.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company closed more than $30 billion in additional AI contracts in Q1 without requiring additional capital from Oracle, using financing models like prepayments and bring-your-own-hardware arrangements.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Capex, FCF and financing” were a key metric to watch; the preview said FY27 was guided to “about $70B net cash outlay” and flagged financing as a bear trigger.

surprises.description: Oracle delivered 850 megawatts of AI capacity with more than 300,000 GPUs since Q4 end—nearly three times the entire Q4 delivery and 73% of all capacity delivered last fiscal year. That scale of deployment, alongside 97.9% utilization, was not quantified in the preview, which identified capacity delivery as the key question behind OCI growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Oracle delivered 850 megawatts of AI capacity with over 300,000 GPUs since Q4 end—nearly 3x the entire Q4 delivery and 73% of all capacity delivered last fiscal year—while GPU utilization remained at 97.9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “OCI revenue vs. the 58–64% cloud guide. The guide implies OCI roughly doubling Y/Y to about $7.4B. This is a capacity-delivery question. GPU utilization was 97.5% in Q4.”

surprises.description: Oracle said GPUs coming up for renewal—most of them at least four years old—were renewed or resold at a 20% premium to prior contracts. The preview did not anticipate this evidence of continued value and pricing power for older hardware.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GPUs that came up for renewal in Q1, the majority being 4 years or older, were renewed or resold at a 20% premium to prior contracts.”

surprises.description: Oracle disclosed exceptionally strong multicloud database growth and customer additions: revenue rose 353% and multicloud customers increased 180%. The preview did not identify this business or its growth as an expectation to track.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Multicloud Database revenue grew 353% year-over-year with multicloud customers up 180%, as Oracle completed its Azure and AWS regional footprint expansion to 70 multicloud database regions and 119 availability zones.”

in_line: OCI revenue was $7.4 billion, up 121% year over year, within the preview’s implied $7.2–$7.6 billion range and its estimated 110–125% growth range.
Cloud Apps grew 10%, in line with the preview’s approximately 10% estimate for SaaS; Fusion’s 14% growth was also not identified as a miss against expectations.

RPO rose $26 billion sequentially from the preview’s cited $638 billion Q4 balance, implying about $664 billion—within the preview’s $630–$680 billion buy-side anchor and $620–$670 billion base-case range.
Full-year CapEx guidance of $90–95 billion gross and no more than $70 billion net was in line with the preview’s expected $90–95 billion gross and roughly $70 billion net outlay.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was $6.76 billion, above both the $6.67–$6.72 billion company guide and the preview’s $6.69–$6.70 billion consensus range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adobe reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $6.76 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Company guidance (Q3, issued 6/11/26): $6.67B – $6.72B | Consensus: $6.69B – $6.70B.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $6.13, topping the preview’s $6.08–$6.09 consensus range and the company’s $6.05–$6.10 guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $6.13.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS | Company guidance: $6.05 – $6.10 | Consensus: $6.08 – $6.09.”

surprises.description: Adobe raised its FY2026 revenue and non-GAAP EPS guidance rather than merely holding the 10.2% ARR growth target: the updated ranges are $26.576–$26.626 billion and $24.45–$24.50, respectively.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adobe raised its full-year FY2026 revenue guidance to $26.576-$26.626 billion and non-GAAP EPS to $24.45-$24.50, a roughly $50 million midpoint raise, while reiterating 10.2% ending ARR growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance: Revenue $26.5B – $26.6B; non-GAAP EPS $24.35 – $24.45.” The preview also said reaffirming the 10.2% ARR target was the minimum for a positive reaction.

surprises.description: Net new ARR fell about 36–37% year over year as Adobe prioritized freemium user acquisition and deferred Creative Cloud pricing actions. The preview anticipated near-term ARR dilution from that strategy, but did not quantify a decline of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net new ARR declined approximately 36-37% year-over-year,” attributed to “the intentional freemium funnel strategy prioritizing user acquisition over near-term monetization and deferred Creative Cloud pricing actions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The CFO said this ‘lowers our second-half ARR growth expectations from individual subscribers’”; the preview also cautioned that “MAU growth alone will be read as ARR dilution.”

surprises.description: RPO growth slowed to 8%, its first single-digit rate since early fiscal 2023, while cRPO grew 9%. The preview highlighted ARR-target risk but did not flag this degree of backlog-growth deceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RPO growth decelerated to 8% (its first single-digit growth since early fiscal 2023) and cRPO grew 9%.”

surprises.description: BP&C subscription revenue reached $1.91 billion, above the preview’s $1.87–$1.89 billion company-guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Business Professionals and Consumers subscription revenue was $1.91 billion (up 15% CC).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “BP&C subscription revenue | Company guidance: $1.87B – $1.89B”; the preview said the Street assumed it would be in line.

surprises.description: C&MP subscription revenue was $4.65 billion, just above the preview’s $4.61–$4.64 billion company-guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Creative and Marketing Professionals subscription revenue was $4.65 billion (up 12% CC).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “C&MP subscription revenue | Company guidance: $4.61B – $4.64B”; the preview said the Street assumed it would be in line.

surprises.description: GAAP EPS was $4.62: above Adobe’s $4.40–$4.45 guide but below the preview’s $4.86 consensus figure. The preview warned that the consensus figure used a mixed basis, so the comparison is conflicting rather than a clear beat or miss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GAAP EPS of $4.62.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP EPS | Company guidance: $4.40 – $4.45 | Consensus: $4.86 (Barchart, 38-analyst poll)”; “Sits well above Adobe's own GAAP guide. Treat as a mixed-basis number.”

in_line: Adobe reiterated its 10.2% FY2026 ending ARR growth target, as the preview identified reaffirmation (rather than a trim) as the minimum expected outcome.
AI-first ARR exceeded $650 million and Firefly grew 40% quarter over quarter, meeting the preview’s AI-first threshold and its expectation that Firefly sequential growth remain above about 30%.

Q4 revenue guidance of $6.8–$6.85 billion was broadly in line with the preview’s calculated implied range of about $6.79–$6.89 billion, though it was below the preview’s more optimistic bull-case threshold.
The CEO handoff to Anil Chakravarthy on December 1, with Shantanu Narayen becoming Executive Chair, matched the transition already described in the preview.
