surprises.description: Rent the Runway reported Q2 revenue of $97.7 million, above the $91–95 million guidance range and its high end, rather than merely meeting the range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record Q2 revenue of $97.7 million… exceeding the guidance range communicated in June.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 guidance… $91–95M”; the preview said the market would judge revenue “against the high end.”

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was far above the guided 5–8% of revenue: it reached $12.6 million, or 12.9%, rather than landing within the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $12.6 million (12.9% of revenue) in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA… guidance… 5–8% of revenue.”

surprises.description: Gross margin rebounded sharply to 36.1%, well above the preview’s expectation of stabilization near 27% and contrary to its concern that the margin could decline further.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit margin expanded roughly 609 basis points to 36.1%,” with lower fulfillment costs and reduced rental product depreciation and revenue share costs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “stabilization near 27% versus further decline below 26%,” after Q1 gross margin of 25.9%.

surprises.description: Ending active subscribers fell to 140,826, below the preview’s 152,000 bear-case threshold rather than reaching the roughly 152,000–158,000 range it identified as the key debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ending active subscribers fell 3.8% year-over-year to 140,826,” hurt by higher pause activity and reduced promotional acquisition.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “below about 152K would support the bear case” and listed actives versus “about 152K to 158K” as a catalyst.

surprises.description: The Q3 revenue outlook is only $87–90 million, implying flat to 3% growth, a weak near-term growth profile against the preview’s double-digit FY26 growth benchmark and its concern about second-half deceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue guidance of $87 million to $90 million implies only flat to 3% growth,” as the company laps last year’s August subscription price increases.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Double-digit growth” as FY26 revenue guidance and said “implied second-half growth is sharply lower because the comparison base gets harder.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA is expected to turn negative, at negative 3% to negative 6% of revenue, rather than tracking the preview’s positive FY26 margin benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 adjusted EBITDA is guided to negative 3% to negative 6% of revenue” due to seasonal pause activity and higher revenue-share inventory costs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of “4–7%.”

surprises.description: Rent the Runway raised its FY26 rental product investment outlook to $53–55 million from the preview’s $45–50 million benchmark, citing a need to stock more fully for second-half events and launches.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its full-year rental product investment guidance to $53–55 million (up from $45–50 million) to ensure fuller stocking for second-half events and launches.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview table listed FY26 rental product acquired guidance of “$45–50M.”

surprises.description: The company announced a $15 million backstopped rights offering and a new $10 million term loan, providing a financing response to the liquidity concerns highlighted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management announced a $15 million backstopped rights offering plus a new $10 million term loan… to bolster liquidity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged cash of $37.1 million against $157.1 million of debt and said “a second double-digit burn quarter would raise financing questions.”

surprises.description: The company paused Marketplace, on-site advertising and monetization, and new B2B dry-cleaning partnerships, a pullback from initiatives beyond core rental and resale that the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rent the Runway paused several initiatives including Marketplace, on-site advertising/monetization, and new B2B dry cleaning partnerships to refocus resources on core rental and resale execution.”

in_line: The permanent CEO appointment was anticipated as a possible catalyst: the preview flagged a “permanent CEO announcement” as a key item to watch. The call named Paige Thomas as permanent CEO effective September 14.

surprises.description: Q4 GAAP EPS was $(0.06), versus the preview’s estimate of about $(0.01), and the company reported a $4.1 million Q4 net loss. The preview anticipated a non-cash earn-out charge, but the reported full-year $15.6 million remeasurement charge was a substantial headwind to GAAP results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 net loss of $4.1 million ($0.06 per share)” and full-year operating expenses “included a $15.6 million non-cash earn-out remeasurement charge driven by G5's outperformance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP EPS … Consensus ~$(0.01)” and “expect a non-cash charge in Q4 GAAP results.”

surprises.description: Q4 gross margin reached 39.4%, well above the preview’s roughly 37% estimate and near the company’s 40% target. The improvement came from higher-margin product mix and resolving yield and throughput problems, rather than price increases or one-time items.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin … reached 39.4% in Q4, driven by higher-margin product mix and resolved yield/throughput problems rather than price increases or one-time items.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin … Consensus ~37%” and “Anything at or above 37% supports the ramp.”

surprises.description: Revenue modestly exceeded the preview’s estimates: Q4 revenue was $21.2 million versus a derived range topping out at $20.6 million, and full-year revenue was $71.7 million versus $71.16 million consensus. The Q4 result was also a company record.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue set a company record at $21.2 million”; full-year revenue was “$71.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … Consensus ~$20.6M (range $18.7M–$20.6M)” and “FY26 revenue consensus $71.16M.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EBITDA was $2.1 million, above the preview’s estimated $1.4–$1.8 million range; full-year adjusted EBITDA was a $4.2 million profit. The fourth consecutive profitable quarter was expected as a milestone, but the quarterly amount was stronger than estimated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA … [was] a $4.2 million full-year profit”; Q4 adjusted EBITDA was “$2.1 million (10% of revenue).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA … Consensus ~$1.4M–$1.8M.”

surprises.description: The company reported that its camera systems are designed into or being evaluated on seven missile and seeker platforms, including three with Lockheed Martin. The preview did not flag this breadth of platform activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Its camera systems are now designed into or evaluated on seven missile/seeker platforms (three with Lockheed Martin).”

surprises.description: Capacity and supply constraints are shaping the FY27 outlook: glass is the main bottleneck and FY27 capital spending will exceed FY26’s $6.3 million, while detector lead times have lengthened from six to more than ten months and are prompting inventory buildup. The preview did not anticipate these specific constraints or the higher spending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Glass is the biggest capacity constraint driving fiscal 2027 CapEx above fiscal 2026's $6.3 million”; detector lead times “have stretched from six to over ten months, prompting inventory buildup ahead of demand.”

surprises.description: Assemblies, modules, and cameras grew to 43% of Q4 revenue and 44% of full-year revenue, up 281% year over year. This shift toward those products was not quantified in the preview and also contributed to the stronger product mix behind margin expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Assemblies, modules, and cameras rose to 43% of Q4 revenue and 44% of full-year revenue (up 281% year-over-year to $31.9 million), versus just 23% of revenue in fiscal 2023.”

surprises.description: LightPath ended the year with $93.2 million in cash and effectively no debt after a $50 million June primary offering. The preview cited March cash of $55.2 million but did not anticipate the offering or the resulting funding for expansion, working capital, and potential acquisitions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LightPath ended fiscal 2026 with $93.2 million in cash and effectively no debt after a June primary offering raised $50 million, funding capacity expansion, working capital, and potential accretive acquisitions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash $55.2M at March 31, 2026.”

surprises.description: The Army delayed the NGSRI interceptor program by a few months. The preview identified NGSRI as an overhang, but did not specify a delay; management characterized the delay as low-risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The NGSRI interceptor program was delayed a few months by the Army but management views it as low-risk.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The U.S. Army's market survey for additional NGSRI suppliers is the main overhang.”

surprises.description: The China divestiture was expected, but the company added that exiting China qualifies it to bid on defense programs requiring non-China sourcing. That newly stated eligibility benefit was not in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: The divestiture “remov[es] roughly $4.5 million of annual revenue but qualif[ies] LightPath for defense bids requiring non-China sourcing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The China subsidiary sale … removes about $4.5M of annual third-party revenue.”

in_line: The June 30 backlog was $110.9 million versus $110.6 million at March 31, essentially flat; the preview explicitly said a flat June backlog would not be a red flag. The two July orders totaling $24 million were also already identified in the preview.
The China operation was sold for $4.5 million payable over five years, removing roughly $4.5 million of annual revenue, consistent with the preview’s description of the sale and revenue headwind.
A fourth consecutive profitable adjusted EBITDA quarter was the proof point the preview said investors were watching, although the reported $2.1 million exceeded its estimated range.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $155.2 million, slightly above both the $154.43 million consensus and the $155.0 million top of the pre-announced range. The beat was small, but the reported result cleared the range investors had been told to expect.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 2026 net revenue grew 24.1% year-over-year to $155.2 million” and came in “above the high end of IPO estimates.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY2026 revenue | $154.43M (+23.5% y/y)” and “The 424B4 pre-announced Q2 revenue range is $154.0M–$155.0M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA and net income each came in above the top of their pre-announced ranges. The excess was modest: EBITDA was $25.4 million versus a $25.30 million high end, and net income was $12.4 million versus a $12.00 million high end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 54% to $25.4 million” and “net income nearly doubled to $12.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA $24.92M–$25.30M” and “net income $11.73M–$12.00M.”

surprises.description: Full-year revenue guidance of $602–606 million is a little above the $601.33 million consensus and the preview’s implied H2 revenue bogey. The lower end only narrowly exceeds consensus, so the guidance upside is limited.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance calls for net revenue of $602-606 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY2026 revenue | $601.33M (+18.6%)” and “Implied H2 revenue of $334.5M (+13.0%).”

surprises.description: Newly acquired customers lifted the active-customer base, but DTC revenue per customer fell 1.4% as those newer customers spent less. That is a less favorable spending trend than the headline customer growth alone suggests; the preview did not forecast this trade-off.
surprises.fact_evidence: “LTM active customers grew ~23% to 1.2 million, but DTC net revenue per customer declined 1.4% to $417 due to the dilutive mix of lower-spending newly acquired customers.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Known figures include about 1.14M Active Customers” and open questions included whether the company would commit to quarterly customer adds.

surprises.description: Wholesale revenue grew much faster than total revenue, reaching $19.9 million, and management said that faster wholesale growth partially offset gross-margin expansion. The preview flagged channel mix as an open question but did not anticipate this growth rate or its margin trade-off.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Wholesale and other net revenue jumped 48.7% to $19.9 million,” driven mainly by higher orders from existing partners; gross-margin expansion was “partially offset by faster wholesale growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Open questions are whether the company will commit to quarterly customer adds, channel mix, and comparable store sales.”

surprises.description: International revenue grew 36.8%, and new-customer growth in France exceeded 180% year over year in the first half. The preview did not identify this international growth as an expected driver or give a benchmark for it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International revenue grew 36.8% to $31.2 million (about 20% of total), with new customer growth in France accelerating to over 180% year-over-year in the first half of 2026.”

surprises.description: Management described a faster growth cadence in Q3 than Q4, citing tough holiday and tariff-normalization comparisons. The preview highlighted Q3 guidance as a catalyst but did not anticipate this particular H2 cadence or the stated comparison pressures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 growth [is] expected to exceed Q4 due to tough holiday and tariff-normalization comparisons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 guide. I could not obtain a verified quarterly consensus; the ~$150M Q3 figure is an estimate from FY totals and seasonality.”

surprises.description: The company outlined a substantial store-growth plan—79–80 stores by year-end and a doubling of the fleet over five years—and presented Chicago data as evidence that openings accelerate local customer and DTC growth. The preview disclosed the current 70-store count but did not forecast this expansion plan or store-halo evidence.
surprises.fact_evidence: Reformation “plans to reach 79-80 stores by year-end, targeting a doubling of the fleet over the next five years.” In Chicago, new-customer growth accelerated “from 28% to 50%” and DTC revenue growth rose “nearly 1.5x after openings.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Known figures include ... 70 stores (Jun 27, 2026).”

surprises.description: The call disclosed that Reformation borrowed $92 million ahead of its IPO to fund about $90 million of dividends, then used roughly $110 million of IPO proceeds to repay debt, bringing net leverage to about 0.9x. This combination of a debt-funded pre-IPO dividend and post-IPO deleveraging was not laid out in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ahead of the July IPO, Reformation raised $92 million in term loans to fund ~$90 million ($1.63/share) in dividends, then used ~$110 million of $132.2 million net IPO proceeds to repay debt, cutting net leverage to ~0.9x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “Confirm the IPO proceeds split” as a gap and next step, but gave no expected dividend, repayment, or leverage figures.

in_line: Gross margin was 66.7%, at the top of the pre-announced 66.6%–66.7% range. Management attributed the expansion primarily to lower blended tariff rates and higher AUR, partially offset by faster wholesale growth.
The company reported 70 stores at quarter-end, matching the 70-store count cited in the preview.

surprises.description: Kroger’s identical sales ex-fuel grew just 0.2%, well below the preview’s roughly 1.0%–1.3% expectation and below the level the preview said would make a guidance cut likely. The company attributed the result to a combined 265-basis-point headwind, including the Inflation Reduction Act, brand-to-generic shifts, Cyclospora and egg deflation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Identical sales without fuel grew just 0.2%,” dragged down by a “combined 265 basis point headwind” including 140bp from the Inflation Reduction Act, 60bp from brand-to-generic shift, 35bp from Cyclospora, and 30bp from egg deflation.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “ID sales ex-fuel | ~+1.0–1.3% (buy-side)” and “Below ~+0.8% makes a guidance cut likely.”

surprises.description: Kroger cut its full-year identical-sales ex-fuel outlook to 0.2%–0.8% from 1%–2%, a sharper reduction than the preview’s likely outcome of guidance narrowing within the existing range. The cut came even as the company kept its profit and EPS ranges unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Kroger lowered its full-year identical sales without fuel guidance to 0.2%-0.8%, down sharply from its initial 1%-2% range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed guidance of “+1.0% to +2.0%” and said “A narrowing within $5.10–$5.30 is the likely outcome.”

surprises.description: Despite the weak sales result and the sales-guidance cut, Kroger maintained its full-year adjusted FIFO operating profit and adjusted EPS ranges. The preview described holding the EPS range as a positive surprise, while suggesting guidance might be narrowed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company maintained full-year guidance for adjusted FIFO operating profit of $5.0-$5.2 billion and adjusted EPS of $5.10-$5.30 despite the lower sales outlook.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Holding the $5.10–$5.30 EPS range would be a positive surprise” and “A narrowing within $5.10–$5.30 is the likely outcome.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $1.09 beat the preview’s $1.05–$1.06 consensus range, though the difference was modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $1.09.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $1.05 (print line) or $1.06 (sell-side mean).”

surprises.description: FIFO gross margin rate excluding fuel rose 13 basis points, better than the preview’s expectation of flat to down 20 basis points. The preview had identified margin as the key debate after a 9-basis-point decline in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “FIFO gross margin rate excluding fuel rose 13 basis points year-over-year,” driven in part by e-commerce, media, pharmacy mix, tariff refunds and sourcing.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FIFO gross margin rate | Flat to –20 bps” and “Flat or positive is the best bull outcome.”

surprises.description: Adjusted e-commerce sales grew 20%, slightly exceeding the preview’s 17%–19% expectation; Kroger also reported a second consecutive quarter of profitable e-commerce growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted e-commerce sales grew 20%,” delivering “a second consecutive quarter of profitable e-commerce growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted eCommerce growth | ~+17–19%.”

surprises.description: Kroger reported that Cyclospora struck late in the quarter, after most competitors had closed their quarters, and expects lingering effects to weigh on Q3 sales. The preview did not anticipate this outbreak or its continued impact.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Cyclospora outbreak hit late in the quarter after most competitors had closed their quarters, and lingering impacts are expected to weigh on Q3 sales.”

surprises.description: Kroger said the Inflation Reduction Act pharmacy headwind is expected to accelerate to about 150 basis points in Q4 as new high-cost drugs, including GLP-1s, enter the formulary in January. Management said this will affect sales but not profit; the preview did not flag this specific upcoming pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Inflation Reduction Act pharmacy headwind is projected to accelerate to approximately 150 basis points in Q4 as new high-cost drugs including GLP-1s enter the formulary in January, with no profit impact.”

surprises.description: Retail media grew 24%, its best growth since 2021, a strength the preview did not specifically anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retail media grew 24% (best since 2021).”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $15.8 million, down 13% year over year, rather than the preview's $21.53 million consensus estimate, which implied 19.5% growth. The reported figure was about 27% below that estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue fell 13% year-over-year to $15.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ... Consensus ... $21.53M (+19.5% YoY), MarketBeat”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA remained negative at a $1.6 million loss, despite the preview's base case of about $0.9 million positive EBITDA and its emphasis on a second positive quarter. The loss narrowed year over year, but missed the positive result investors were asked to watch for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 17% year-over-year to $1.6 million in Q2”; “constant-FX EBITDA loss narrowed 64% to $0.9 million in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base | ... Adj. EBITDA ... ~+$0.9M”; “A second positive quarter would convert the cost-cutting story into a profitability story.”

surprises.description: Hong Kong revenue was flat year over year at $7.8 million, a sharp deceleration from the growth the preview said had driven the business for two quarters. The preview specifically warned that growth below about 20% would weaken the growth case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hong Kong revenue held flat at $7.8 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Hong Kong revenue growth +33%, after +27% the prior quarter”; “Deceleration below about +20% would weaken the growth case.”

surprises.description: The higher approval rate did not translate into quarter-on-quarter transaction-value growth: approval rates rose to 48%, but Q2 total transaction value was flat at $20.9 million. That fell short of the preview's open question about whether improved conversion would keep offsetting the decline in traffic.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Approval rates expanded 9 percentage points year-over-year to 48%, with approved applications declining a smaller 15%”; “total transaction value held flat at $20.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether conversion keeps offsetting the traffic decline.”

in_line: Cash held stable and finished at $28.2 million, consistent with the preview's preference for flat or rising cash and its $27–28 million base-case range.
Approval rates reached 48%, in line with the preview's reference to improvement from 36% to 48%; the preview had flagged conversion as the key metric to watch.

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EBITDA was $10.4 million, above the preview’s roughly $8.5–9.5 million range, and the adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 240 basis points. The EBITDA result exceeded the preview’s central estimate even though the preview already anticipated margin improvement.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA reached $10.4 million, up 31.6% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 240 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA ~$8.5–9.5M”; the preview described the bar as “about $9.0M” and estimated adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of AGP at “~14.5–15.5%.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue came in at $261.4 million, well above the preview’s implied estimate of about $231 million. Revenue growth was much faster than the preview’s implied 4.7% year-over-year growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue rose 18.5% to $261.4 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue ~$231M” and “Y/Y +4.7%.”

surprises.description: GAAP diluted EPS was $0.15, more than twice the preview’s $0.07 estimate. The unusually low tax rate contributed to the reported result, so the EPS beat was not solely a reflection of underlying operating performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 net income attributable to Radiant was $7.517 million ($0.15 fully diluted EPS), up from $4.907 million ($0.10 EPS) a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “GAAP EPS (diluted) $0.07.”

surprises.description: The domestic freight improvement had only begun late in the quarter, so it contributed for about one month rather than benefiting Q4 throughout. Management nevertheless said more upside should come in later quarters, making the near-term conversion of the freight inflection more limited but the forward commentary stronger.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management said improving domestic freight trends “only began late May/early June,” so “only about one month benefited Q4 results,” with “more upside expected in coming quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted whether “domestic strength converted to gross margin dollars in the June quarter, or stayed at ‘green shoots’ language.”

surprises.description: Airfreight was meaningfully boosted by Western Pacific typhoon disaster-relief work, an unanticipated source of Q4 support. Management said airfreight would still have been up year over year without the work, but the boost makes part of the reported strength event-related.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Airfreight results were meaningfully boosted by Western Pacific typhoon disaster relief work,” though the company “would have been up year-over-year even without it.”

surprises.description: The quarter’s effective tax rate was near 4%, versus a 24.5% pro forma rate, because a tax-law true-up allowed previously capitalized internal software expenses to be deducted. This was a favorable but unusual contributor to reported net income and EPS that the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Q4 effective tax rate was near 4% versus the 24.5% pro forma rate,” driven by a “One Big Beautiful Bill true-up” allowing previously capitalized internal software expenses to be deducted.

surprises.description: Management described a substantially more ambitious acquisition opportunity than the preview could establish: a path to nearly doubling EBITDA within the existing capital structure, supported by a record volume of potential sellers. The preview had flagged whether the expanded facility signaled a larger M&A push, but did not anticipate this specific scale or seller pipeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “sees a path to nearly double EBITDA within its existing capital structure through disciplined tuck-in acquisitions,” aided by “a record volume of potential sellers coming to market post-freight-recession.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch whether the expanded revolver signals a larger M&A push.”

surprises.description: Management reported about 8% organic growth and said trends were strengthening into Q1 FY2027, providing a constructive operating outlook even though the company gave no quantified forecast in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Organic growth was approximately 8% in the quarter,” with management indicating “trends are strengthening into Q1 FY2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that RLGT “rarely gives quantitative outlook” and identified “FY2027 framing” as something to watch.

in_line: The amended $200 million senior credit facility’s extension to 2031 and $100 million of additional acquisition capacity were broadly consistent with the preview’s disclosure of the amended facility and its $100 million accordion.

surprises.description: Revenue was $24 million, about $0.72 million above the $23.28 million consensus estimate. That is a modest beat, though the preview characterized revenue within $1 million of consensus as largely set.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record quarterly revenue of $24 million in Q3 FY2026.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q3 FY26 Consensus | $23.28M”; “Revenue within ±$1M of consensus is largely set.”

surprises.description: Q4 sales are expected to be roughly flat with or above Q3's $24 million, an encouragingly high level of near-term guidance when the preview had found no full-year guidance and described guidance initiation as unpriced.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management guided Q4 FY2026 sales to be roughly the same or above the Q3 level of $24 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “No full-year guidance was found”; “Guidance initiation. Formal numerical guidance would be a notable narrative catalyst. Not priced in.”

surprises.description: DAC was no longer merely qualitative: management now expects the business to exceed $10 million in annual sales and called it a key growth engine. That gives the AI/edge-datacenter thesis meaningful scale beyond what the preview had quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The DAC business, previously immaterial, is now expected to exceed $10 million in annual sales and is viewed as a key growth engine expanding beyond traditional telecom.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Commentary has been qualitative for four quarters. A dollar figure or named customer would matter most for the AI/edge-datacenter thesis.”

surprises.description: Bookings were near the preview's expected dollar level, but book-to-bill was only about 0.94x and backlog was $19.8 million, slightly below the preview's $20–21 million base-case range. The forward demand indicators therefore fell short of the preview's 1.0x book-to-bill watch line.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 bookings were $22.5 million for a book-to-bill ratio of about 0.94x, with backlog rising to $19.8 million as of the call from $18.6 million at July 31.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bookings vs. about $22M”; “Book-to-bill above 1.0x is the line to watch”; base case “$20–23M / $20–21M” for bookings/backlog.

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 35.6%, 60 basis points above the preview's 35% watch level. This was a modestly better result than the expectation that margins would hold around that level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross profit margin expanded 160 basis points to 35.6% from 34% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin vs. 35%”; base case expects “margins hold.”

in_line: Non-GAAP EPS was $0.19, between the preview's conflicting $0.18 and $0.20 consensus figures and close to the stated estimate.
Bookings of $22.5 million were close to the preview's approximately $22 million watch level, even though book-to-bill and backlog were softer than the preview's forward-indicator thresholds.

Small-cell/integrated systems began accelerating in Q3, consistent with the preview's expectation of H2 acceleration; management said the business was still below year-start expectations in dollars, so the recovery was not complete.

surprises.description: The preview identified a signed Personal Care sale as a possible upside catalyst, but Hain instead agreed to sell its international business for $323 million in cash, with $305–$310 million of net proceeds expected. The sale is expected to close in fiscal Q2 and, if completed, would reduce pro forma debt to about $250 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hain agreed to sell its international business to private equity firm Aurelius for $323 million in cash, with net proceeds expected between $305 million and $310 million, and closing anticipated in fiscal Q2”; “pro forma total debt would fall to approximately $250 million, a reduction of about 55%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Personal Care divestiture. A signed deal would be the most likely upside surprise.”

surprises.description: The transaction is not yet a completed refinancing or an unconditional debt solution: it depends on an amendment extending credit-agreement maturity, and lenders can terminate the sale if the amendment is not secured within 30 days. That leaves a significant financing condition unresolved despite the announced deal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The international divestiture is contingent on securing a credit agreement amendment to extend maturity, and lenders can terminate the deal if the amendment isn't obtained within 30 days of signing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Refinancing of the Dec 22, 2026 maturity” was the “largest driver of the reaction”; a bull outcome included “a refinancing commitment letter or maturity extension.”

surprises.description: Hain’s Q4 organic sales decline was less severe than the preview’s estimated 4%–6% decline: the reported decline was 2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Overall Q4 organic net sales declined 2% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Organic net sales: ~−4% to −6% (estimate).”

surprises.description: North America delivered a much stronger Q4 operating picture than the preview’s broad concern about post-Snacks margins suggested: organic sales grew 2%, gross margin expanded nearly 1,200 basis points to 31.1%, and adjusted EBITDA rose 55% to $16 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North America returned to organic sales growth of 2% in Q4, expanded gross margin by nearly 1,200 basis points to 31.1%, and grew adjusted EBITDA 55% year-over-year to $16 million (14.4% of net sales).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch the post-Snacks framing of North America margins.”

surprises.description: Despite International organic sales improving to a 4% decline from an 8% decline in Q3, profitability deteriorated sharply: adjusted gross margin fell 555 basis points and adjusted EBITDA dropped 41%. The preview anticipated improving organic trends but did not flag this degree of International margin and earnings pressure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “International segment organic net sales declined 4% year-over-year (improving from an 8% decline in Q3), but adjusted gross margin fell 555 basis points to 16.6% and adjusted EBITDA dropped 41% due to cost inflation.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said Q4 organic trends should improve.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.05 per share below zero, versus the preview’s single-analyst estimate of a $0.03 loss per share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “An adjusted net loss of $0.05 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS: −$0.03 (TipRanks, Sept 2026)” and “EPS consensus rests on a single analyst.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $19 million, just below the preview’s estimated $20–$24 million range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $19 million (7.1% margin) down slightly from $20 million a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA: ~$20–24M (estimate).”

surprises.description: Hain reduced net debt by $151 million, or about 25%, during FY26, an additional balance-sheet improvement beyond the preview’s focus on whether free cash flow would merely be positive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced net debt by $151 million (about 25%) during fiscal 2026 to $500 million.”

surprises.description: A zero-based budgeting review identified more than $16 million in annual run-rate savings and management said these support pro forma gross margin above 30% and a low-double-digit adjusted EBITDA margin. The plan also carries about $20 million of implementation costs, mostly in FY27, which tempers the benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A zero-based budgeting review identified more than $16 million of annual run-rate cost savings, expected to cost roughly $20 million to implement (70% in fiscal 2027), supporting pro forma gross margin of 30%-plus and low double-digit adjusted EBITDA margin.”

surprises.description: Management plans to raise marketing investment by about 100 basis points of net sales, an unflagged additional spending commitment that could weigh on near-term margins while supporting the named brands.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company plans to increase marketing investment by approximately 100 basis points of net sales to support Celestial Seasonings, Greek Gods, and Earth's Best.”

in_line: FY26 free cash flow was positive, as the preview explicitly expected; the reported amount was $58 million.
Management provided no traditional FY27 guidance, consistent with the preview’s expectation that none would be provided while the strategic review continued.
International organic sales improved to a 4% decline from an 8% decline in Q3, in keeping with the preview’s expectation that Q4 organic trends would improve.

surprises.description: KB Home reported diluted EPS of $1.05, above the preview’s $0.88–$0.90 adjusted EPS consensus. The call fact gives diluted EPS, while the preview estimate is adjusted EPS, so the comparison has a basis caveat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 total revenues were $1.3 billion with diluted EPS of $1.05.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS | $0.88 (Zacks) / $0.90 (Alphastreet)”

surprises.description: Q4 outlook weakened from the preview’s roughly $500,000 ASP assumption: management lowered ASP guidance to about $480,000 and cut gross margin by about 1 percentage point, citing Southern California weakness.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management lowered its Q4 ASP guidance to about $480,000 from roughly $500,000 and cut Q4 gross margin by about 1 percentage point, driven largely by Southern California weakness.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “an ASP near $500K versus about $470K in Q3”

surprises.description: Although full-year delivery guidance was maintained, the housing-revenue range was narrowed to $4.9–$5.1 billion from $4.9–$5.3 billion, lowering the top end by $200 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year guidance was largely maintained: deliveries of 10,500-11,000 homes, housing revenues narrowed to $4.9-5.1 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 guidance (Q2 release): 10,500–11,000 deliveries; $4.90–5.30B housing revenue.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted housing gross margin was 16.8%, above the preview’s roughly 16.3% consensus and above the company’s 16.0–16.6% range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 adjusted housing gross margin was 16.8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Housing gross margin | ~16.3% | 16.0–16.6% ex-charges”

surprises.description: The SG&A ratio came in at 11.3%, better than the preview’s approximately 11.6% consensus and at the low end of the company’s guided range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A ratio rose to 11.3% from 10.0%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “SG&A ratio | ~11.6%” and “Guide of 11.3–11.9%”

in_line: Q3 total revenue of $1.3 billion was approximately in line with the preview’s roughly $1.29 billion consensus.
Q3 deliveries of 2,732 homes were essentially in line with the 2,723-home consensus and within the company’s 2,600–2,800 guidance range.
Full-year delivery guidance remained at 10,500–11,000 homes, matching the preview’s stated range.

The backlog continued to rebuild: the preview noted that backlog had built 45% year to date and highlighted backlog rebuilding as a key issue; the call reported the first year-over-year backlog increase in four years.

surprises.description: The preview’s base case expected Q4 revenue of $54–60 million and a high-single- to low-double-digit decline against the recast comparison. Revenue was within the dollar range at $55.9 million, but was broadly flat year over year, a better trend than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fourth quarter revenues were broadly flat at $55.9 million versus $55.4 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base | ~50% | Revenue | $54–60M”; “Revenue down high-single to low-double digits vs. the recast comp.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA turned positive in Q4 despite the preview having no EBITDA estimate. The $0.6 million result was also a sharp improvement from the prior-year loss, alongside a substantial SG&A reduction.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.6 million, a roughly $10 million improvement from negative $9.6 million a year earlier, driven by a 19% reduction in SG&A.”

surprises.description: For the full year, adjusted EBITDA fell much less than revenue: a 12% decline against an 18% revenue decline. The preview had no EBITDA forecast, so this cost-control resilience was not quantified in its expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year adjusted EBITDA declined only 12% to $25.5 million … despite an 18% revenue decline,” as “over $20 million of operating expense cuts offset a ~$22 million gross profit decline.”

surprises.description: Q4 gross profit and margin were weighed down by about $4 million of non-recurring inventory obsolescence charges, a specific one-off not identified in the preview. This left gross margin at 22.8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 gross profit fell 6% to $12.7 million with a 22.8% margin, hurt by approximately $4 million of non-recurring inventory obsolescence charges.”

surprises.description: The company reported completed debt reprofiling measures: it reprofiled about $28 million of Rizobacter bank debt and extended maturities on $46.5 million of local bonds. The preview flagged these outcomes as a key liquidity issue but had not established that the measures would be completed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reprofiled about $28 million of Rizobacter bank debt and extended maturities on $46.5 million of Argentine local bonds to strengthen liquidity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Rizobacter debt reprofiling. … Watch completion of Argentine bank maturity reprofiling and the outcome of the voluntary local bond extension.”

surprises.description: Management gave forward operating targets, including roughly 40% gross margins for fiscal 2027 and beyond and combined SG&A of 23% of revenue by fiscal 2028. The preview anticipated a possible multi-year plan but had found no guidance, so these targets provide more specific forward numbers than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is targeting approximately 40% gross margins for fiscal 2027 and beyond and a combined SG&A of 23% of revenues by fiscal 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Three-year plan. The Board directed management to build one, and the annual call is a natural venue to disclose it. Watch whether any forward number is given.”

in_line: Q4 revenue of $55.9 million landed within the preview’s $54–60 million base-case range, even though its expected year-over-year trend was more negative.

surprises.description: The preview's base case anticipated a mid-to-high-single-digit sales decline, while Hooker reported consolidated sales down about 9%, or $6 million. The preview also cited revenue consensus of $63.8 million to $67.9 million, but warned that the continuing-operations comparison was uncertain, so the size of any dollar miss cannot be established from the call facts provided.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated net sales fell about 9% ($6 million) year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: ... Continuing-ops sales down mid-to-high single digits”; revenue consensus was “$63.8M” and “$67.9M.”

surprises.description: The preview cited a slight EPS loss consensus and a base-case range from a small loss to near breakeven; instead, Hooker reported $1.7 million of net income and its third consecutive profitable quarter. The call facts do not provide EPS, so the comparison is on profitability rather than per-share results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated net income of $1.7 million in Q2 FY2027, marking its third consecutive profitable quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS $(0.02)” consensus; the base scenario was “$(0.03)–$0.04.”

surprises.description: Consolidated gross margin reached 31.8%, well above the preview's 27–29% base-case range. That is a considerably stronger margin result than expected, although the call attributed much of the improvement to tariff recoveries.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved 690 basis points to 31.8% and gross profit rose $2.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “gross margin 27–29%.”

surprises.description: The preview said roughly $8 million of tariff refund claims had not been booked and that recognition would be a non-operating gain. The call instead reported that Q2 results benefited significantly from tariff recoveries after the court invalidated the IEPA tariffs, making the tariff-related benefit a material part of the quarter's results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 results benefited significantly from tariff recoveries following the U.S. Supreme Court's February 2026 decision invalidating IEPA tariffs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Roughly $8M of refund claims were filed in Q1 and are not booked as a receivable, so recognition would be a non-operating gain.”

surprises.description: Hooker Branded's gross margin was nearly 40%, above the preview's 36% level for a bull case and far above the level it said would suggest Q1's margin was a mix artifact. The segment also expanded margin by 1,000 basis points despite lower sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Hooker Branded segment sales fell 4.5% but gross margin expanded 1,000 basis points to nearly 40%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If Q2 holds at or above 36%, the margin story looks structural. Below about 33%, Q1 looks like a mix artifact.”

surprises.description: Domestic Upholstery was expected to remain a challenged, loss-making segment, but it swung to operating income of $833,000 despite lower sales. Its gross margin also improved by 450 basis points, a stronger turnaround than the preview's discussion of improvement tied to better market conditions suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Domestic Upholstery sales declined 5.3% while gross margin improved 450 basis points to 23%, swinging to $833,000 operating income from a $408,000 loss.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Domestic Upholstery operating result (Q1: $(689)K loss on $28.4M sales). This segment has not turned profitable.”

surprises.description: Hooker Branded's backlog grew nearly 35% year over year, a stronger order signal than the preview's roughly flat base-case outlook for consolidated backlog. The reported figure is for Hooker Branded, however, rather than the consolidated backlog metric highlighted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Its backlog surged nearly 35% versus the prior year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “backlog roughly flat”; the preview identified consolidated backlog as a key metric.

surprises.description: The preview did not flag a sharp Q2 decline in the all-other segment, but sales there fell about 66% and the segment recorded an operating loss. The company attributed the drop to hospitality project timing, with roughly 80% of first-half shipments already occurring in Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The ‘all other’ segment saw net sales plunge about 66% ($2.8 million) due to hospitality project timing, with roughly 80% of first-half shipments occurring in Q1, resulting in a Q2 operating loss.”

in_line: The $17.5 million of annualized fixed-cost savings continued to support profitability, consistent with the preview's account that management had already cut about $17.5 million of fixed costs.

Margaritaville shipments began in Q2 and are expected to build through the second half of FY2027 and into FY2028, consistent with the preview's expectation that shipments were weighted to the second half. The call facts provided no quantified revenue contribution.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $16.1 million, well above the roughly $12.3 million consensus, while EXXUA revenue rose to $3.9 million from $2.4 million in Q3. That was stronger than the preview’s possibility of flat-to-down EXXUA revenue if wholesaler orders only covered replacement demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total Q4 net revenue was $16.1 million”; “EXXUA generated $3.9 million in net revenue in Q4 FY2026, up 63% from $2.4 million in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net revenue” Q4 consensus: “~$12.3M”; the preview also said “flat-to-down EXXUA revenue is possible if wholesalers order only to replacement.”

surprises.description: June 30 cash was $26.3 million, above the preview’s expected $21–24 million, despite the company reducing its revolver and later repaying it in full. The preview had identified cash below roughly $20 million as a key downside risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cash was relatively stable at $26.3 million at June 30 while the company deleveraged its balance sheet, reducing the revolver to $6.1 million (later fully repaid).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Estimated Q4 burn of $3.5–4.5M implies cash of roughly $21–24M”; “Below about $20M raises the odds of a near-term dilutive raise.”

surprises.description: Aytu had nearly 1,200 EXXUA prescribers, far above the preview’s Q3 base of about 450+. However, many had tried the drug with only one or two patients, so breadth of adoption was much stronger than evidence of deep use per prescriber.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Nearly 1,200 unique physicians have prescribed EXXUA to nearly 2,500 unique patients, though many prescribers have only tried it with one or two patients so far.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EXXUA scripts and unique prescribers versus the Q3 base of about 1,300 scripts and 450+ prescribers.”

surprises.description: The company returned to positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4, reporting $0.5 million versus a $2.8 million loss in Q3. That was better than the preview’s loss-oriented base case and its estimate of continued Q4 cash burn, although full-year adjusted EBITDA remained negative.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company returned to positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.5 million in Q4 (versus negative $2.8 million in Q3), while full-year FY2026 adjusted EBITDA remained negative $3.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected EPS of “-$0.45 to -$0.52” and “cash about $22–23M”; it also estimated “Q4 burn of $3.5–4.5M.”

in_line: EXXUA prescriptions were broadly in line with the preview’s projected Q4 range: 3,323 versus an expected 2,900–3,300.
The ADHD portfolio continued to decline from its $13.1 million year-ago comparison, as the preview had flagged; Q4 revenue was $10.4 million, above the preview’s bear-case level of below $8 million.

The preview flagged a FY2027 revenue or EBITDA framework as a catalyst, and management provided operating-expense, gross-margin, and adjusted-EBITDA targets; the preview did not set numerical expectations for those targets.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $98.9 million, well below the preview's $118–123 million estimate, and the reported 18.2% margin reflected a sharp year-over-year decline. The result was also below the preview's bear-case EBITDA range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA dropped to $98.9 million (18.2% margin) from $129.7 million (23.3% margin).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA ~$118–123M (my estimate)” and the bear scenario was “$98–106M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted results swung to a $0.27 per-share loss rather than the preview's expected $0.19 profit. The company also reported a GAAP loss of $0.36 per share, versus $0.32 of GAAP earnings a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net loss of $9.5 million (-$0.27) versus adjusted net income of $13.9 million ($0.40)”; GAAP net loss was “-$0.36 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS $0.19.”

surprises.description: Revenue came in below the preview's near-flat expectation, falling about 2.3% short of its estimate. This was a meaningful miss, though smaller in percentage terms than the EBITDA shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue fell to $544.1 million from $557.4 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $556.8M” and “~flat” year over year.

surprises.description: Q2 same-store sales declined less than the preview's expected 4%–5% drop, at 2.9%. However, comps remained negative despite management's earlier expectation of positive comps from mid-June through year-end; the reported monthly trend improved, but no positive Q3-to-date comp figure was given.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 same-store sales declined 2.9%,” improving from “-5% in June to -1.6% in July,” with “further improvement over the first five weeks of Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~ -4% to -5%” comps and noted management had guided to “positive comps starting today through the balance of the year.”

surprises.description: Management said about $15 million of the EBITDA decline came from non-normalized items, including a $10 million non-cash deferral adjustment, higher pre-opening expenses, and elevated insurance costs. The preview did not anticipate these specific items; they help explain part of the miss but do not change the weak reported EBITDA result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “About $15 million of the EBITDA decline” was attributed to non-normalized items, including “a $10 million non-cash deferral adjustment, $3 million in higher pre-opening expenses, and $2 million in elevated insurance costs.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a cost-saving initiative with $15 million of savings already identified and executed, and a target to at least double that amount in coming months without harming the customer experience. The preview did not flag this program or its savings target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A cost-saving initiative has already identified and executed $15 million in savings to be realized over 12 months,” with management “targeting at least doubling that amount in coming months without impacting the customer experience.”

surprises.description: Management set FY27 net capex at $150 million or less and said recurring core and maintenance capex runs about $95–100 million annually. The preview discussed the FY26 capex ceiling but did not provide this lower FY27 capex outlook or recurring-capex level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net capex of $150 million or less in FY27,” with “recurring core/maintenance capex running about $95-100 million annually.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited FY26 net capex “of at most $200M” and did not give an FY27 capex estimate.

surprises.description: New game pricing changes reportedly increased gameplay and Midway dwell time by 16%–20% or more while maintaining basket size and margins. The preview had flagged amusement weakness but did not anticipate this engagement response; the business nevertheless remained in negative comp territory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New game pricing changes drove a 16-20%+ increase in gameplay and Midway dwell time while maintaining basket size and margins,” while amusement remained “in negative comp territory for roughly eight consecutive quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “amusement, the higher-margin part of the mix, is carrying the decline” and called for amusement comps specifically, but gave no expected gameplay or dwell-time result.

surprises.description: Special events were reported to have grown for seven consecutive quarters, a sustained positive trend the preview did not discuss. The preview had highlighted F&B growth, but not this separate source of strength.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Special events have grown for seven consecutive quarters.”

surprises.description: Management said remodeled locations continue to outperform non-remodeled locations. The preview did not mention this performance difference or the remodel program.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company had completed “six remodels year-to-date (with two more planned)” that “continue to outperform non-remodeled locations.”

in_line: Net capex was $127.6 million through Q2 and management expected FY26 net capex to remain under $200 million, consistent with the preview's FY26 ceiling of $200 million.
The plan for five FY27 domestic openings matched the preview's expectation of about five openings per year in FY27–28.
Food and beverage comps remained positive, consistent with the preview's note that F&B was already growing.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $32.9 million, above the preview’s derived estimate of roughly $30–32 million. The result also came with a 25% margin and $10.8 million of year-over-year EBITDA growth, indicating more operating leverage than the estimate implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $32.9 million with a 25% margin, an increase of $10.8 million year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA: Not found as a published consensus (derived ~$30–32M).”

surprises.description: The Payment Solutions revenue rate was 2.4%, above the preview’s 2.3% level to watch. This was a modestly better rate than expected, although the preview did not give a Q2 managed-payments volume estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total managed payments were $1.626 billion in the quarter, with a Payment Solutions revenue rate of 2.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Payment Solutions rate (2.3%) and managed payments ($1.786B in Q1). Watch whether the rate holds as AccessOne is added.”

surprises.description: Phreesia reported a four-month GLP-1 campaign study showing incremental prescription lift and more than 1,000 new patient starts, with follow-on business converted. The preview did not flag this study or its commercial results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A 4-month GLP-1 category study using Provider Connect showed a 4% incremental lift in new-to-brand prescriptions versus a matched control group and more than 1,000 new patient starts, and converted follow-on business.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted share repurchases as a capital-allocation priority and said a buyback authorization would be a positive surprise, while the reported capital-allocation action was paying down more than $23 million of debt. Debt reduction supports the balance sheet, but the reported action differed from the preview’s buyback focus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reduced debt principal by over $23 million during the quarter while maintaining a healthy cash balance of $74.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management listed share repurchases as a priority. A buyback authorization would be a meaningful positive surprise.”

in_line: Q2 revenue of $129.5 million was within the preview’s $129.1–$130.6 million consensus range, though just below the $130–132 million base-case scenario.
Management maintained FY27 revenue guidance of $510–520 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $125–135 million, as the preview expected.
Management’s deliberate moderation of subscription pricing was consistent with the preview’s base case of subscription revenue being flat to down.

surprises.description: Net sales were $923 million, about $20 million below the $943.3 million consensus and below the company’s $928 million guidance floor. The call attributed the shortfall to softer-than-anticipated North America Contract and Global Retail revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 net sales fell 3.4% year-over-year to $923 million, driven by softer-than-anticipated revenue in North America Contract and Global Retail.”

surprises.description: Management cut FY27 sales guidance to $3.88–$4.03 billion from $3.93–$4.13 billion, reducing the midpoint by $100 million. The preview expected the range to be reaffirmed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management lowered full-year FY27 sales guidance to $3.88-$4.03 billion (3% growth at midpoint) while maintaining adjusted EPS guidance of $1.85-$2.15.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 guidance (6/24/26): Net sales $3.93–4.13B. Adj. EPS $1.85–2.15.” The preview also said, “Reaffirmation at $1.85–2.15 keeps the H2-weighted bridge intact.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $0.53, including a $0.11 benefit from IEPA tariff refunds. Even excluding that benefit, EPS was $0.42—above both the $0.35 consensus and the company’s $0.39 guidance ceiling.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS was $0.53, but excluding a $0.11 net benefit from IEPA tariff refunds, adjusted EPS of $0.42 still beat the company's guidance range.”

surprises.description: Global Retail’s adjusted operating margin rose to 7.0%, up 580 basis points, far above the prior-year Q1 margin of 1.2% cited in the preview. Tariff refunds supplied 410 basis points of the reported improvement, but the margin still improved excluding that contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Global Retail delivered its eighth consecutive quarter of North America order growth (up 7.5%), with adjusted operating margin up 580 basis points to 7.0%, though 410 basis points came from tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q1 Retail margin was 1.2% last year.” The preview also said, “Management needs to show the opex growth is discretionary” and that it “should show the store program is accretive.”

surprises.description: North America Contract orders fell only 1.7%, a much smaller decline than the preview’s 8.2% year-over-year comparison implied. Management said $55–60 million of orders had been pulled forward into Q4 FY25, helping explain the difficult comparison.
surprises.fact_evidence: “North America Contract sales dropped 5.3% to $506 million and orders fell 1.7% to $484 million, partly due to $55-60 million of orders pulled forward into Q4 FY25 from tariff-driven buying.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “NA Contract orders. The comp is $492.2M (down 8.2%). Q4 fell 10.0%.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that new U.S.-Canada tariff actions are expected to reduce full-year EPS by about $0.07, a headwind the preview had not flagged. The company said it was responding with inventory pre-buys and dual sourcing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New U.S.-Canada tariff actions are expected to create an approximate $0.07 per share unfavorable full-year impact, prompting inventory pre-buys and dual-sourcing mitigation efforts.”

surprises.description: Orders accelerated after quarter-end: the first three weeks of September were up 9% year over year across all three segments. The preview focused on whether Q1 orders would signal an inflection, but did not anticipate this early-quarter acceleration.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Order momentum accelerated post-quarter, with the first three weeks of September up 9% year-over-year across all three segments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Orders above about $950M would signal an inflection.”

in_line: Consolidated orders were $914 million, within the preview’s $910–$930 million base-case range and below shipments, as expected. Backlog was $669 million, within the preview’s expected $660–$675 million range.
FY27 adjusted EPS guidance remained $1.85–$2.15, as the preview expected.

surprises.description: Q4 sales were $6.6 billion, below the preview’s $6.70–6.71 billion consensus, and sales growth was 5.6% rather than the 7.4% growth implied by consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 total sales grew 5.6% to $6.6 billion.”

surprises.description: Domestic DIY same-store sales turned negative and traffic fell more sharply than the preview’s already-worsening traffic concern suggested. The preview expected domestic comps around +3.6% and noted that DIY comps could slow unless units improved.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Domestic DIY same-store sales declined 0.6% in Q4 as traffic fell more than 5% while average ticket rose about 5%,” with weakness among financially challenged consumers showing “deferrals and trade-down.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Domestic same-store sales | ~+3.6%”; “Q3 DIY traffic fell 3.6%. With inflation decelerating, comps could slow unless units improve.”

surprises.description: SG&A deleveraged 101 basis points in Q4, a notably weak outcome against the preview’s base case that diesel would offset most operating leverage. The preview did flag deleverage as a bear case, but the reported result was substantial.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A deleveraged 101 basis points in Q4” as total SG&A rose 8.9% and SG&A per store rose 4%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: … diesel offsets most operating leverage”; the bear scenario said “SG&A deleverages.”

surprises.description: The FY28 store-opening target was cut from about 500 to about 430, a pullback from the expansion path described in the preview. FY27 openings are planned at about 400, even after a record 374 openings in FY26.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company opened a record 374 new stores in FY26 … and plans approximately 400 in FY27, while cutting the FY28 target from ~500 to ~430 stores by slowing Brazil expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “365 store openings in FY26 with a path toward 500 per year by 2028.”

surprises.description: Q4 EPS beat the preview’s $54.08–$54.42 consensus at $56.05, but the reported figure included a $4.43-per-share benefit from tariff refunds. That one-time benefit was not anticipated in the preview and materially contributed to the headline beat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “EPS rose 15.1% to $56.05, but EPS included a $4.43 benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds ($96 million).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS | $54.08 (Zacks), $54.22 (Alphastreet), $54.42 (UBS).”

surprises.description: A stronger peso provided an additional, unflagged Q4 earnings tailwind and management expects another benefit in Q1. The preview did not identify this currency contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A peso strengthening of nearly 9% created a $70 million sales, $21 million EBIT, and $0.87 EPS tailwind in Q4,” with a further “~$0.60 EPS benefit in Q1 FY27 at current spot rates.”

surprises.description: Even excluding LIFO charges in both years, EPS growth was 8.5%, below the roughly 11%–12% growth implied by the preview’s consensus EPS and prior-year EPS. The reported 15.1% EPS growth therefore overstated the underlying growth rate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Excluding LIFO charges in both years, Q4 EBIT grew only 4.4% and EPS grew 8.5%, versus the reported 10.1% EBIT and 15.1% EPS growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed consensus EPS of “$54.08” to “$54.42” and prior-year EPS of “$48.71.”

surprises.description: The Q4 LIFO charge was half the amount the preview said management had guided to, reducing the actual drag on earnings versus expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A $0.69 drag from a $15 million LIFO charge.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Company guidance (Q4): LIFO charge of about $30M.”

in_line: Domestic commercial same-store sales grew 8.6%, remaining above the preview’s stated concern threshold of growth below 8%, although below the prior quarter’s double-digit rate.
FY27 CapEx of about $1.65 billion was close to the preview’s prior guidance of about $1.6 billion.

surprises.description: The preview put FY27 revenue consensus at $6.74 million and said management might guide to $7 million or more if delayed revenue returned. Instead, management declined to provide official FY27 revenue guidance, citing just $2.3 million in booked government contracts and another $2 million under discussion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management declined to provide official fiscal 2027 revenue guidance,” citing “only $2.3 million in currently booked government contract revenue” and “a potential additional $2 million under discussion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 revenue guidance vs. $6.74M consensus”; “If the deferred revenue is real, the FY27 guide should land at $7M+.”

surprises.description: FY2026 revenue was within the company’s $4.2–$4.6 million guidance range, but at $4.5 million it came in below the preview’s $4.74 million analyst consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year revenue of $4.5 million, roughly flat versus $4.7 million in fiscal 2025 and near the high end of prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue” consensus “$4.74M”; company guidance “$4.2M – $4.6M.”

surprises.description: Management described multimillion-dollar commercial NRE agreements under negotiation with marquee customers, mostly in AI DataCom, as potential sources of FY2027 revenue. The preview focused on qualifications and a possible production order, and did not anticipate these specific NRE opportunities.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company is negotiating several multimillion-dollar commercial NRE agreements with marquee customers, almost entirely focused on the AI DataCom market, that could add revenue in fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A first production purchase order or a named qualification would be the most important operational datapoint.”

surprises.description: Management put FY2027 capital expenditures at approximately $10–$12 million, largely for two AIXTRON G10 MOCVD reactors. The preview flagged higher spending and burn as issues to watch but did not anticipate a capex program of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Capital expenditures of approximately $10 to $12 million in fiscal 2027,” largely a “one-time cost for two AIXTRON G10 MOCVD reactors.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 opex, burn and ATM intentions.”

surprises.description: The preview’s FY2027 revenue outlook relied on delayed revenue returning soon, but management placed commercial deployment scaling for its photonics products in 2028–2030. That longer timeline suggests broad commercial scaling is later than the preview’s near-term recovery framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management targets “commercial deployment scaling in 2028-2030” for its LINX photodetectors and Quasar quantum dot lasers.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “If the deferred revenue is real, the FY27 guide should land at $7M+”; FY27 revenue consensus was “$6.74M.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue modestly exceeded the preview’s consensus estimate, though it remained within the company’s implied guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue was $582,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q4 revenue consensus “~$0.56M (range $0.53M – $0.59M).”

in_line: FY2026 revenue of $4.5 million remained within the company’s previously stated $4.2–$4.6 million guidance range, despite falling short of analyst consensus.

The CHIPS R&D Office arrangement remained an LOI for up to $30 million, and management expected it to be accounted for as a government equity investment rather than revenue; the preview had cautioned against treating the amount as revenue guidance.

surprises.description: NetApp reported Q1 revenue of $2.03 billion, above the $1.90 billion top of its guidance and $1.836 billion consensus. Even excluding the extra week’s roughly $65 million, revenue was about $1.965 billion, still above the guidance ceiling and consensus.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY27 revenue rose 30% year-over-year to a record $2.03 billion (26% growth excluding the extra week that added ~$65 million), exceeding the high end of all guidance ranges.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | Q1 FY27 guidance … midpoint $1,825M | Consensus … $1,836M”; the preview also notes the extra week adds about $65M.

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS reached $2.58, well above the $2.12 consensus and the $2.15 top of guidance. The result substantially exceeded the preview’s expectations for the quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS reached $2.58, up 66% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS | Q1 FY27 guidance … midpoint $2.10 | Consensus … $2.12.”

surprises.description: Operating margin expanded to 31.9%, about 3 percentage points above the preview’s roughly 28.9% consensus expectation, indicating much stronger margin performance than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating margin expanded 6.1 points to 31.9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Operating margin | … Consensus … ~28.9%.”

surprises.description: NetApp sharply raised its FY27 outlook: the revenue midpoint rose to $8.1 billion and the EPS midpoint to $9.88, well above the preview’s prior guidance and consensus. This was a much larger raise than the preview’s base case of a modest increase and even exceeded its bull-case revenue range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management materially raised full-year FY27 guidance, increasing the revenue midpoint by $650 million to $8.1 billion (17% growth) and lifting the EPS midpoint to $9.88 (22% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 revenue … Consensus ~$7.5B | Company guidance $7.325–7.575B”; “FY27 EPS … Consensus ~$8.90 | Company guidance $8.70–9.00.” The preview’s base case expected FY27 to be “nudged up,” and its bull case projected revenue of “$7.6–7.8B.”

surprises.description: Q2 guidance was far above the preview’s expected $1.84 billion revenue and $2.16 EPS: the company’s midpoints are $2.1 billion and $2.59. Although revenue growth is expected to slow to 23% year over year, the guided dollar results are materially stronger than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 guidance implies decelerating growth of 23% year-over-year at the $2.1 billion revenue midpoint, with EPS midpoint of $2.59.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY27 revenue | Consensus $1,840M”; “Q2 FY27 EPS | Consensus $2.16.”

surprises.description: Q2 gross-margin guidance of 67%–68% is below the preview’s roughly 69.5% expectation and below the level it identified as important for supporting the gross-margin trough call. This is a notable margin shortfall despite the strong earnings outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 guidance … with … gross margin of 67%-68%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “above 69.5% supports the trough call” and that a Q2 gross-margin guide “below about 69%” would put the FY27 EPS bridge at risk.

surprises.description: The July-quarter business did not show the soft book that the preview warned investors to watch for: all-flash revenue accelerated to 47% growth, while product revenue rose 51% and reached a larger share of total revenue. The preview had cited pull-forward risk and asked whether the July book would be soft.
surprises.fact_evidence: “All-flash array revenue grew 47% year-over-year to $1.31 billion, and product revenue jumped 51% to $987 million, rising to 49% of total revenue versus 42% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management conceded ‘probably some amounts of pull forward’ in Q4. Watch whether the July book is soft.”

surprises.description: NetApp reported about 350 AI and data-lake modernization wins, down from roughly 500 the prior quarter, matching the preview’s warning that a change in the win-count metric could be read negatively. Increasing deal sizes temper the decline, but management still did not quantify how much revenue AI contributed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company won approximately 350 AI and data lake modernization deals with increasing deal sizes, down from about 500 in the prior quarter, though management declined to quantify AI's revenue contribution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “About 500 AI wins” in Q4; “Any change to the win-count metric would be read negatively.” The preview also identified conversion into production deployment as an open question.

surprises.description: Product gross margin fell sequentially to 54.6% as component costs rose, but management now expects it to run slightly above its prior low-50% outlook for the rest of the year because pricing actions are being captured faster. That improves the forward product-margin outlook relative to the prior outlook stated on the call.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Product gross margin declined 150 basis points sequentially to 54.6% due to higher component costs, but management now expects it to run slightly better than the prior low-50% outlook for the rest of the year as pricing actions are captured faster.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Prior low-50% outlook” for product gross margin for the rest of the year.

surprises.description: Public-cloud gross margin was 86.4%, above NetApp’s stated long-term target range of 80%–85% for a third consecutive quarter. The preview did not flag this sustained above-target margin performance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Public cloud revenue grew 28% year-over-year to $206 million (19% excluding the extra week), with public cloud gross margin of 86.4% now above the 80%-85% long-term target range for three straight quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “80%-85% long-term target range.”

surprises.description: Inventory nearly doubled sequentially and inventory turns fell to 6 as NetApp secured supply amid rising component costs and strong demand. The preview did not flag this inventory build, which is a new working-capital and supply-position detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory nearly doubled sequentially as the company secured supply against rising component costs and strong demand, with inventory turns falling to 6.”

in_line: Q1 product gross margin pressure was consistent with the preview’s expectation that the July quarter would be the trough: product gross margin was 54.6%, down 150 basis points sequentially.

surprises.description: Upexi ended FY2026 with about 2.34 million SOL, rather than the trackers’ roughly 2.17 million flat holding level. That is close to management’s previously claimed Q3 token growth and makes the reported year-end balance a positive surprise versus the tracker picture.
surprises.fact_evidence: “As of June 30, 2026, the company held approximately 2.34 million Solana tokens.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Trackers show holdings flat at about 2.17M since Dec 31, 2025, but management claims +189,000 tokens in Q3.”

surprises.description: Stockholders’ equity was negative $53.8 million, less negative than the preview’s estimate of roughly negative $90 million. The decline from the prior year was substantial, but the year-end result was materially better than the preview’s anticipated level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total stockholders' equity swung to negative $53.8 million at June 30, 2026, from positive $90.1 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Equity was −$51.9M at 3/31/26 and is likely near −$90M at 6/30/26.”

surprises.description: Upexi reported only $5.8 million in cash, a thin cash balance despite its much larger total assets and positive working capital. The preview focused on whether staking revenue would cover ongoing expenses, but did not anticipate or quantify this low cash figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company holds just $5.8 million in cash … against $180.1 million in total assets and $45.6 million in working capital.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Cash-flow break-even after July 1. The company needs to confirm it is self-funding.”

surprises.description: Upexi retired roughly $20 million of debt for about $10 million and recognized a $10.3 million gain on extinguishment. The preview discussed the debt load and later refinancing, but did not anticipate this discounted debt retirement or gain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company extinguished roughly $20 million in debt in June (retiring nearly $20 million principal for about $10 million) and recorded a $10.3 million gain on debt extinguishment.”

surprises.description: Despite reducing headcount to 10, Upexi’s G&A rose to $26.4 million from $11.9 million, while stock-based compensation increased to $21.9 million from $2.4 million. The preview highlighted a much smaller workforce and the need to become self-funding, but did not flag this substantial expense increase.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Stock-based compensation ballooned to $21.9 million from $2.4 million the prior year, while G&A expenses rose to $26.4 million from $11.9 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Headcount is down to 10, and the 9/14 BitGo amendment cut the rate from 11.5% to 7.5%, saving more than $2M a year.”
