surprises.description: The company repurchased 2.9 million shares for $2.8 million, then issued 2.5 million ATM shares for $2.5 million in gross proceeds, largely offsetting the share-count effect of the repurchases. The preview discussed SOL per share and debt-adjusted value but did not flag this buyback-and-issuance combination.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased 2.9 million shares at an average of $0.96 (totaling $2.8 million) under its $50 million buyback program, but subsequently issued 2.5 million ATM shares for $2.5 million in gross proceeds.”

surprises.description: FY2026 interest expense reached $13.6 million, up from $1.2 million the prior year. The preview anticipated the post-quarter rate reduction, but did not flag the scale of the fiscal-year interest burden before that refinancing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Interest expense surged to $13.6 million from $1.2 million,” while the post-quarter refinancing lowered the rate from 11.5% to 7.5%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The 9/14 BitGo amendment cut the rate from 11.5% to 7.5%, saving more than $2M a year.”

in_line: Management said staking revenue is expected to fully cover ongoing cash expenses, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the company confirm it is self-funding after July 1.
Headcount was reduced to 10, as the preview already noted.
The post-quarter refinancing cut the interest rate from 11.5% to 7.5%, in line with the preview’s account of the BitGo amendment.
The FY2026 loss was driven primarily by unrealized SOL losses, consistent with the preview’s warning that GAAP results would be heavily affected by fair-value marks.

surprises.description: Lululemon cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $10.35–$10.5 billion, down 5–7%, well below the preview’s roughly $11.1 billion consensus and its base case that revenue would be held. The reset was much deeper than the preview’s most likely partial trim suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was lowered to $10.35-$10.5 billion (down 5-7%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 revenue consensus of “~$11.1B” and said the base case was “FY revenue held.”

surprises.description: FY2026 EPS guidance fell to $9.48–$9.73, below the preview’s $10.95–$11.15 company guidance and its expected partial trim to about $10.40–$10.75. The result is closer to the preview’s bear case than its most likely outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year EPS cut to $9.48-$9.73 versus $13.26 in 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed FY26 EPS guidance of “$10.95–$11.15” and said the base case was “FY EPS trimmed modestly to about $10.40–10.75.”

surprises.description: Q3 guidance pointed to a sharper near-term deterioration than the preview’s expectation of second-half improvement: revenue is expected to fall 10–11%, operating margin is about 6.5%, and North America is expected to worsen to a mid-teens decline. SG&A is also expected to deleverage 800 basis points in Q3 and about 450 basis points for the full year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for revenue of $2.29-$2.32 billion (down 10-11%), operating margin of ~6.5% versus 17% a year ago”; “Q3 SG&A is expected to deleverage 800 basis points year-over-year”; and “Q3 North America to worsen to a mid-teens decline.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management needed to “reaffirm 2H improvement” and expected “Q4 markdowns below last year's level.”

surprises.description: Q2 revenue came in below both the $2.46 billion consensus and the company’s $2.450–$2.475 billion guidance range. Revenue declined 4% reported, rather than the preview’s expected 2–3% decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 total net revenue declined 4% (5% in constant currency) to $2.4 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed Q2 revenue consensus of “$2.46B” and company guidance of “$2.450–2.475B,” with “–3% to –2%” YoY.

surprises.description: China Mainland grew only 4% reported, with comps down 8%, far short of the preview’s expected mid-to-high-teens growth. Management attributed the shortfall to negative social/media sentiment and a weaker Tmall 618 event.
surprises.fact_evidence: “China Mainland revenue grew only 4% reported (down 2% constant currency) with comps down 8%, the primary source of the quarterly shortfall driven by negative social/media sentiment and a weaker Tmall 618 event.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed China Mainland guidance of “mid-to-high teens” growth and flagged backlash and Tmall competition as risks.

surprises.description: Q2’s 18.8% operating margin was supported by a large tariff refund that the preview had not anticipated. The $134.5 million refund added 560 basis points to margin and $0.86 to EPS, so the reported margin decline understates the pressure absent that one-off benefit.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 operating margin was 18.8% versus 20.7% a year ago, but included a $134.5 million pretax IEEPA tariff refund that added 560 basis points and contributed $0.86 to EPS.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed tariff costs, saying assumptions embedded “10% incremental in Q2 and 20% in 2H,” but did not anticipate a tariff refund.

surprises.description: Leggings sales fell approximately 20% as customers shifted toward away-from-body silhouettes, an unexpected product-demand change beyond the preview’s general concern about newness and recent launches.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Leggings sales dropped approximately 20% in Q2 as guests shift toward away-from-body silhouettes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed newness penetration and said recent launches had run “short of expectations,” but did not flag a sharp leggings decline or a shift away from body-hugging silhouettes.

surprises.description: Accessories also weakened, with sales down 13% amid softness in bags; the preview did not identify this category-specific decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Accessories declined 13% amid softness in bags.”

surprises.description: Management reduced planned net new store openings from about 40 to 35, cut planned pop-up stores from 65 to about 40, and intensified discretionary expense cuts. These retrenchment steps were not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cut planned net new store openings to approximately 35 (from ~40), is reducing pop-up stores from 65 to ~40, and is intensifying discretionary cost cuts across travel, professional fees, and store labor.”

in_line: North America Q2 comps were down 12%, broadly matching the preview’s expectation of a low-double-digit decline for US comps, although management guided to further deterioration in Q3.
The preview expected the incoming CEO to start shortly after the release and strategy to be deferred to her; the facts say Heidi O’Neill starts next week and will reassess strategy.

surprises.description: Revenue was $54.6 million, above both preview consensus figures of $53.1 million and $54.0 million. Reported year-over-year growth of 55% also exceeded the preview’s roughly 51% estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 fiscal 2027 revenue grew 55% year-over-year to $54.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus | $53.1M (Zacks) or $54.0M (S&P agg.)”; “YoY | ~+51%.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS was $0.06, above the $0.05 consensus estimate. The per-share result beat expectations even though the preview noted that diluted shares were expected to rise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income more than doubled, rising 100.9% to $2.6 million ($0.06 per diluted share).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS (diluted) | Consensus | $0.05.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $5.5 million, modestly above the preview’s $5.3 million base-case estimate. Its margin also expanded year over year to 10.1%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA increased 68.9% to $5.5 million with margin expanding to 10.1% of revenue from 9.3% a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base | Adj. EBITDA | ~$5.3M.” The preview also stated that adjusted EBITDA was “not formally polled.”

surprises.description: Operating expenses fell to 18.5% of revenue from 20.1% a year earlier, showing a year-over-year improvement in expense leverage that the preview did not forecast for Q2.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating expenses fell 160 basis points to 18.5% of revenue from 20.1%, demonstrating operating leverage as the business scales.”

surprises.description: Management described capacity for larger, transformative acquisitions, a more expansive M&A stance than the preview’s cited post-Bay Shore comment that there was “nothing major left to do.” No acquisition itself was reported.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company had “$138.6 million in cash” and management said this enabled “larger and more transformative M&A.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said CEO Adam Michaels had stated after the Bay Shore deal that “there is nothing major left to do,” and noted that the company was evaluating EPS-accretive acquisitions.

surprises.description: Mama’s Creations disclosed a first-time Kroger launch starting next month, with four items in more than 100 Louisville-division stores. The preview discussed new-item sell-through but did not anticipate a Kroger entry.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company will launch in Kroger for the first time next month, starting with over 100 stores in the Louisville division with four items.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s new-item discussion listed Walmart, Food Lion, Target, Albertsons divisions, Publix, Weis, and Fresh Market, but did not mention Kroger.

surprises.description: Costco confirmed a second-half mailer across all eight regions that management expects to be larger than last year’s, an expansion not identified in the preview’s discussion of customer and promotional risks.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Costco confirmed a second-half multi-vendor mailer across all eight regions forecasted to be larger than last year.”

surprises.description: Walmart distribution had grown to more than 2,300 stores from about 2,000, an increase in reach beyond the customer details provided in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Walmart distribution expanded to over 2,300 stores (up from ~2,000) with nine items.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview mentioned Walmart chicken SKUs among Q1 launches and flagged new-item sell-through, but did not state an expectation for Walmart store distribution.

surprises.description: Management said it had a long-term line of sight to $1 billion in revenue, a larger stated destination than the preview’s discussion of capacity to support about $400 million without major new investment. No timeline was provided in the reported facts.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management reiterated “its long-term line of sight to $1 billion in revenue.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the company had “capacity to support about $400M of revenue without major new investment.”

in_line: Gross margin was 24.0%: below the preview’s 24.3% base-case estimate and the mid-to-high-20% target, but within the preview’s stated 24.0–24.9% acceptable range. The preview also anticipated a year-over-year decline; the reported margin improved sequentially from 23.6%.
Management reiterated confidence in double-digit revenue growth, broadly consistent with the preview’s forward anchor of double-digit organic growth.

surprises.description: Snowflake reported Q2 product revenue of $1.49 billion, above the preview’s roughly $1.41 billion consensus and even the preview’s bull-case threshold of $1.47 billion. Growth was 37%, well above the preview’s base-case range of 32–34%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 product revenue reached $1.49 billion, growing 37% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Product revenue” consensus “~$1.41B”; the preview’s bull case was “≥$1.47B (+35%)” and its base case was “$1.44–1.46B (+32–34%).”

surprises.description: Snowflake raised FY27 product revenue guidance to $6.07 billion, above the preview’s bull-case threshold of $5.95 billion or more. The size of the raise was stronger than the preview’s expected $5.88–5.94 billion base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year FY'27 product revenue guidance to $6.07 billion (36% growth), an increase of over 500 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a raise to “$5.95B or more” would support the AI-consumption story; its base case was “$5.88–5.94B.”

surprises.description: The FY27 non-GAAP product gross margin outlook fell to 74%, below the preview’s expected threshold of at least 75% and below its warning level of about 74.5%. The company attributed the reduction to the growing mix of lower-contribution-margin AI workloads.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year non-GAAP product gross margin guidance was lowered to 74% due to a higher revenue mix from fast-growing AI workloads that carry lower contribution margins today.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified “75% in Q1” and said to watch for “at or above 75%”; it warned that “a drop below about 74.5%” would make AI mix a margin-dilution issue.

surprises.description: Snowflake raised its FY27 non-GAAP operating margin guide to 14.5%, a full percentage point above the existing 13.5% guide cited in the preview. That was also above the preview’s approximately 12.5% consensus estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year non-GAAP operating margin guidance was raised from 13.5% to 14.5%, with Q3 guided at 15.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed company guidance of “13.5% (FY27)” and consensus of “~12.5% (Benchmark).”

surprises.description: Net new customer additions exceeded the preview’s expected range: Snowflake added 692 customers, versus the preview’s estimate of roughly 440–490. Total customers reached 14,554, above its estimated range of 14,350–14,400.
surprises.fact_evidence: “692 net new customers added (a 32% year-over-year increase) bringing total customers to 14,554.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “~14,350–14,400 (+440–490 net)” and said to watch whether net new customers held near Q1’s “+616” against consensus of “about +440–490.”

surprises.description: The company guided Q3 product revenue growth of 37–38%, above the preview’s base-case Q2 growth expectation of 32–34% and consistent with sustained acceleration rather than a return to a lower growth pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Guided Q3 product revenue of $1.588-$1.593 billion (37-38% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected Q2 product revenue growth of “+32–34%” and said a result below the Q1 pace would break the acceleration narrative.

surprises.description: Management said roughly half of the revenue acceleration came from AI products and half from core platform strength, migrations, and other products. This was more balanced than the preview’s concern that Q1’s acceleration might reflect a CoCo surge or front-loaded AI experimentation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management attributed roughly half of the revenue acceleration to AI products (CoCo, CoWork, AI functions, AI Gateway), with the other half from core platform strength, migrations, and other products.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview raised the possibility that “Q1’s Cortex Code surge” was “a pull-forward” and described a bear scenario in which “Q1’s acceleration reflected front-loaded AI experimentation.”

surprises.description: Snowflake disclosed rapid growth in AI-product adoption: CoCo exceeded 9,100 accounts, adding more than 2,000 in the quarter, and CoWork had 5,800 accounts. The preview highlighted CoCo’s 7,100-account starting point but did not anticipate or quantify CoWork adoption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CoCo surpassed 9,100 accounts, adding over 2,000 net new accounts in the quarter, while CoWork expanded to 5,800 accounts, up nearly 11% quarter-over-quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch CoCo account counts (7,100 last quarter)” and mentioned Snowflake Intelligence accounts, but did not provide a CoWork expectation.

in_line: NRR was 126%, matching the preview’s base-case expectation of 126% and its stated watch threshold of 126% or higher; it did not reach the 127%+ level identified as the clearest upside signal.

surprises.description: Oxford cut FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $1.60–$2.00, far below the prior $2.30–$2.70 range and even below the preview’s bear-case range of $2.30–$2.50.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Slashed full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $1.60-$2.00.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EPS $2.30–2.70”; the preview said even “FY EPS trimmed to $2.30–2.50” would confirm the bear case.

surprises.description: Lilly Pulitzer weakened more than the preview’s watch for sequential improvement suggested: management said its entry-price dress styles fell from about half the assortment to roughly 35%, and it does not expect a positive trend change until spring 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lilly Pulitzer's performance deteriorated more than anticipated” after entry-price dress styles shifted “from about 50% of its assortment in 2025 down to roughly 35% in 2026”; “a positive trend change is not expected until spring 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for sequential improvement from -8.8%”; the preview also called for “Lilly moving from diagnosis to recovery” as a bull signal.

surprises.description: The Q3 outlook was weaker than the preview’s stated investor hope for positive low-single-digit-or-better Q3 comps: sales are guided below last year’s $307 million, and the adjusted loss is expected to widen from $0.92 per share.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 fiscal 2026 guidance calls for sales of $280-300 million (versus $307 million last year) and an adjusted loss per share of $1.40 to $1.20, wider than the $0.92 loss reported in Q3 2025.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The buy side wants ‘positive low-single-digit or better’” for Q3 quarter-to-date comps.

surprises.description: The full-year sales outlook was cut to $1.43–$1.47 billion, below the preview’s expected $1.475–$1.505 billion range. The new range implies a 3% decline to roughly flat versus last year, rather than the preview’s near-flat to modest-growth outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cut full-year sales guidance to $1.43-1.47 billion (a 3% decline to roughly flat versus $1.478 billion last year).”

surprises.description: The company reported a larger tariff-refund benefit than the preview’s $25 million Phase 1 claims: it reduced cost of goods sold by $42 million and received substantially all of that amount in cash during or shortly after Q2. The benefit was excluded from adjusted results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Recorded a $42 million reduction to cost of goods sold from previously paid tariff refunds (excluded from adjusted results) and received substantially all of it in cash during or shortly after Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The $25M of Phase 1 tariff refund claims, earmarked for debt repayment, are excluded from guidance.”

surprises.description: Debt fell to $73 million by Q2 end, a much sharper reduction than the preview’s discussion of a $25 million refund earmarked for repayment suggested. First-half operating cash flow was $97 million, including $29 million in tariff refunds.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Long-term debt was cut sharply to $73 million from $143 million at the end of Q1 and $116 million at the end of fiscal 2025, aided by $97 million of first-half operating cash flow that included $29 million in tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total debt was $142.7M” and “$25M of Phase 1 tariff refund claims, earmarked for debt repayment.”

surprises.description: Management launched an enterprise-wide margin review and plans to convert select Southern Tide and Johnny Was stores to Lilly Pulitzer. The preview had expected the Lyons distribution-center integration to be complete by early August, but management described the center as still ramping.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management launched an enterprise-wide review to enhance operating margins, including ramping the new Lyons, Georgia distribution center, converting select Southern Tide and Johnny Was stores to Lilly Pulitzer.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “full integration would land ‘by early August’” and flagged a distribution-center transition “still described as ‘ongoing’” as a bear signal.

in_line: Q2 net sales of $394 million were close to the preview’s approximately $394.6 million consensus, and the quarter landed near the high end of the $380–$400 million company range. Adjusted EPS of $1.34 was close to the $1.32 consensus and within the $1.20–$1.40 guidance range.
Total-company comparable sales were down 1%, consistent with the prior guidance for low-single-digit negative to flat comps.
Adjusted gross margin expanded 140 basis points to 63.1%, in line with the preview’s estimate of about 63% and the company’s +100–200-basis-point guidance.
Tommy Bahama’s low-single-digit positive DTC comp and expected slightly positive full-year comps were consistent with the preview’s expectation of positive comps through year-end.
Capex was expected to be about $60 million, and management reiterated a plan to normalize it to about $60 million from $108 million in FY2025.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was expected around $877M and guided at $875–878M, but Zscaler reported $898M, beating both the consensus and the top of its guidance by about 2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue reached $898 million… exceeding the high end of guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue… $875–878M”; “Street consensus… ~$877.0–877.6M.”

surprises.description: Full-year FY26 revenue was expected at about $3.33B, but the reported total was $3.4B, roughly $70M higher.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal '26 revenue of $3.4 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue… consensus ~$3.33B.”

surprises.description: FY26 exit ARR exceeded the preview’s expected guided band: the call reported $3.8B versus $3.740–3.749B expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total ARR grew 25% to $3.8 billion.”

surprises.description: Organic net new ARR accelerated more than the preview’s key threshold: it reached 17% growth, versus the preview’s 14% Q3 baseline and its view that holding at or above 15% would be supportive.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Organic net new ARR… of $232 million accelerating to 17% growth versus 10% in the first half of fiscal '26 and 7% in fiscal '25.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Organic net new ARR grew only 14% in Q3, and holding at or above 15% would support the view that the slowdown reflects conservative guidance.”

surprises.description: Q4 operating profitability was stronger than the preview’s operating-income estimate implied: 24.3% margin on $898M revenue is about $218M of operating income, above the roughly $207M estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin hit a record 24.3% in Q4.” Revenue was “$898 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income… ~$207M.”

surprises.description: Zero Trust Everywhere enterprises reached more than 950, up from more than 700 in Q3; the preview flagged this metric but had only identified growth as something to watch, not this degree of expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Zero Trust Everywhere enterprises grew to more than 950 exiting Q4, up from over 700 in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Zero Trust Everywhere customers were above 700 in Q3… Watch for growth in that count.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed strong Security for AI bookings momentum, a product area for which the preview gave no specific expectation or booking benchmark.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Security for AI bookings increased more than 50% sequentially in Q4, with 70% of security-for-AI deals including a data security solution.”

surprises.description: ZFlex produced substantial Q4 and full-year contract value, with customer ARR uplift, a commercial metric the preview did not discuss or set an expectation for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ZFlex generated over $770 million in TCV in Q4, up more than 60% quarter-over-quarter, and more than $1.7 billion for full fiscal '26,” with average ARR uplift “nearly 30%.”

surprises.description: Non-seat-based metered usage showed significant scale and growth beyond the preview’s general call to watch non-seat ACV mix; the preview supplied no quantitative benchmark for it.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-seat-based metered usage solutions delivered approximately 30% of new and upsell ACV with related ARR growing more than 100% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch for… the non-seat ACV mix.”

surprises.description: The company announced a workforce restructuring affecting about 3% of employees and $30–33M in charges, which the preview had not anticipated; it also said it was adding dedicated new-logo sales executives.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company announced a workforce restructuring affecting approximately 3% of employees with charges of $30–33 million, while simultaneously adding dedicated new-logo sales executives.”

in_line: FY27 revenue guidance of $3.908–3.938B was broadly in line with the preview’s $3.90B consensus and $3.90–3.93B base case, as well as the preliminary 16–17% growth framework.
FY27 ARR guidance of $4.396–4.426B, implying 16.6–17.4% growth, was consistent with the preview’s expectation of preliminary 16–17% ARR growth.

FY27 free-cash-flow margin of roughly 23–23.5% was within the preview’s 22–23.5% base-case range; elevated capex was already expected, though the call attributed it to higher memory and component pricing.
The continuing effect of the two sales-leadership departures on the first half of FY27 was consistent with the preview’s focus on the sales transition and its role in the conservative outlook.

surprises.description: Q1 sales were $37.3 million, about 4.7% above the preview’s $35.64 million consensus. After adjusting for the roughly $6 million of orders shifted between periods, underlying growth was still about 4%, modestly better than the preview’s expectation of growth closer to flat.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 fiscal 2027 net sales rose 25% year-over-year to $37.3 million,” and adjusted for “~$6 million of orders pulled into Q4 fiscal 2025 last year, underlying growth was approximately 4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus | $35.64M”; “Normalized growth is closer to flat.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA came in positive at $1.2 million rather than the preview’s expected slightly negative result. That was a substantial improvement over both the expected direction and the prior-year loss.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA improved by $4.3 million year-over-year to a positive $1.2 million, versus a $3.1 million loss in the prior-year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ‘Slightly negative’”; the preview also estimated roughly “$(2.9)M.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS turned positive at $0.03, far ahead of the preview’s expected loss of $0.24 per share. GAAP loss also narrowed substantially from the prior-year quarter.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS turned positive at $0.03 versus a $0.26 loss a year ago, while GAAP loss narrowed to $0.12 from $0.54.”

surprises.description: Gross margin reached 53%, well above the preview’s mid-40s expectation. About 200 basis points came from tariff-capitalization timing, but management attributed roughly 400 basis points to product mix, channel mix, and pricing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 gross margin expanded 630 basis points to 53%, with roughly 200 bps from tariff capitalization timing and about 400 bps from sustainable product mix, channel mix, and pricing.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin | ‘Mid-40s’”; the preview said a print above “~47%” would need checking for tariff-related content.

surprises.description: Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance, while the preview’s existing outlook was 6.5%–7.5% of sales. The new $14.5 million–$17.5 million range has a $16 million midpoint, above the midpoint implied by that prior margin outlook and the preview’s sales range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $14.5 million–$17.5 million (midpoint up 57% year-over-year).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 adj. EBITDA margin | 6.5–7.5%”; FY27 net sales guidance was “$200–210M.”

surprises.description: Management warned that new Section 301 tariffs will begin reducing gross margin later in Q3, with the full quarterly impact in Q4. The preview discussed tariff-related margin effects but did not flag this specific new tariff timetable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New tariffs (Section 301 at 10%-12.5% plus prior tariffs) will begin impacting gross margin later in Q3 with full quarterly impact in Q4 due to inventory turn timing.”

surprises.description: Products introduced in the last 24 months generated 36% of sales, well above the company’s historical 20%–25% range. The preview did not identify this level of new-product contribution as an expectation or key issue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New products introduced over the last 24 months contributed 36% of Q1 net sales, well above the historical 20%-25% average, driven largely by the Caldwell ClayCopter family.”

surprises.description: Operating cash flow was $13 million, compared with a $1.7 million cash use in the prior-year quarter; the company ended Q1 with $33.3 million in cash and no debt. The preview reported $21.4 million in cash as the balance-sheet reference point but did not forecast this quarter’s cash generation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $33.3 million in cash, no debt, and over $120 million in total available capital, generating $13 million in operating cash flow versus a $1.7 million usage last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Balance sheet: $21.4M cash, no debt.”

surprises.description: POS growth remained positive for a sixth consecutive quarter: Outdoor Lifestyle POS rose 6% and Shooting Sports POS rose 3%. The preview flagged whether e-commerce stabilization would hold, but did not provide an expectation for these POS growth rates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 marked the sixth consecutive quarter of positive POS growth, with Outdoor Lifestyle POS up 6% and Shooting Sports POS up 3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said e-commerce ordering stabilized exiting FY26; Q1 should show whether that holds.”

surprises.description: BUBBA’s paid subscriptions reached the six-figure dollar range on a trailing-twelve-month basis and accelerated in Q1 as complimentary two-year subscriptions began rolling off. The preview did not mention subscription monetization as an expected result or debate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “BUBBA's paid subscriptions reached the six-figure dollar range on a trailing-twelve-month basis and accelerated in Q1 as complimentary two-year subscriptions began rolling off.”

in_line: FY27 net sales guidance remained $200 million–$210 million, as the preview expected the company to reaffirm its existing range.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was $116.8 million, above the preview’s $108.1–$110.2 million consensus range, although it was within the preview’s bull scenario of $114–$117 million. The 13% year-over-year growth also contrasted with the preview’s expectation of a tougher, slower Q3.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 revenue grew 13% year-over-year to $116.8 million, driven primarily by large-scale data center and infrastructure projects in the U.S.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | $110.2M” and “Revenue (alt.) | $108.1M”; the preview also said the guidance midpoint implied Q3 revenue of “about $107M” and that an in-line print may read as a deceleration.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $30.4 million, well above the roughly $26.6 million implied by the preview’s FY26 guidance midpoint, though it matched the preview’s $30–$31 million bull scenario. Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 26%, right at the preview’s durability threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose 13% to $30.4 million with margin improving to 26%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the guidance midpoint implied Q3 adjusted EBITDA of “roughly $26.6M”; its bull scenario was “$30–31M.” It also flagged “26% or better” as the margin threshold.

surprises.description: Management raised FY26 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance rather than merely reaffirming or narrowing the existing ranges. The new ranges are $425–$435 million in revenue and $103–$108 million in adjusted EBITDA, versus prior ranges of $410–$425 million and $98–$105 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance: revenue to $425-$435 million (from $410-$425M), adjusted EBITDA to $103-$108 million (from $98-$105M).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described reaffirming the wide range as caution and said the “clean bull outcome” was narrowing guidance to $418–$425 million revenue and $102–$105 million EBITDA.

surprises.description: FY26 free cash flow guidance increased to approximately $50 million from a floor of at least $45 million, exceeding the preview’s key test of absorbing the roughly $22 million CapEx pull-forward while keeping the prior floor.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Free cash flow to approximately $50 million (from at least $45M).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY26 FCF guide was “≥$45M” and flagged reaffirming that floor “with the $22M pull-forward absorbed” as a catalyst checklist item.

surprises.description: The Board initiated a recurring quarterly dividend, which the preview had not anticipated. The company also retains $11.9 million of buyback authorization, so the new dividend adds a distribution channel rather than replacing the remaining authorization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board initiated a new quarterly cash dividend of $0.13 per share ($0.52 annualized), representing a yield of approximately 5.6%”; “$11.9 million remaining under a buyback authorization.”

surprises.description: U.K. revenue grew 24%, but the increase was mainly acquisition-driven and management reported continued soft underlying construction demand and margin pressure. The preview flagged a possible U.K. recovery, including a catalyst of adjusted EBITDA returning to year-over-year growth, but the reported commentary did not confirm a broad operating recovery.
surprises.fact_evidence: “U.K. revenue grew 24% to $18.7 million driven mainly by the Tenplait temporary power acquisition, though underlying commercial construction stayed soft and margins were pressured by labor inefficiency and higher fuel costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “Q2 adj. EBITDA fell 3.4% YoY and H1 fell 10.6%. Watch whether Templant ... helps,” and listed “U.K. adj. EBITDA back to YoY growth” as a catalyst.

surprises.description: Management gave a specific near-term deleveraging target: reaching 3.0x net leverage in roughly 18 months if there is no major M&A. The preview anticipated leverage at or below 3.7x as a possible checkpoint but did not state this further target or timetable.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage declined to 3.6 times adjusted EBITDA from 3.8 times last quarter, tracking toward a near-term target of 3.0 times that management expects to reach in roughly 18 months absent major M&A.”

surprises.description: Diluted EPS of $0.09 was above both preview consensus figures, although it fell short of the preview’s bull-scenario range of $0.10–$0.12.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income attributable to common shareholders increased to $4.5 million ($0.09 per diluted share) from $3.3 million ($0.07).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed diluted EPS consensus of “$0.08” and an alternate estimate of “$0.066”; its bull scenario was “$0.10–0.12.”

in_line: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 26%, matching the preview’s 26%-or-better threshold.
Net leverage was 3.6x, meeting the preview’s checkpoint of leverage at or below 3.7x.
The company pulled forward roughly $22 million of 2027 replacement CapEx into 2026, as the preview had flagged.

surprises.description: Q2 non-GAAP operating margin was 31.6%, 160 basis points above the guidance midpoint of 29.7%–30.2%; the preview expected sequential margin compression, not an outcome this far above the company’s range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 non-GAAP operating margin was 31.6%” and “160 basis points above the guidance midpoint.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Q2 guide implies about 200bp of sequential operating margin compression.”

surprises.description: Docusign raised its FY27 ARR growth outlook to 8.5%–9.0%, above the prior 8.25%–8.75% range and lifting the top end beyond the preview’s 8.75% threshold for a raise.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its fiscal 2027 ARR growth guidance to 8.5%-9.0% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 ARR growth 8.25% – 8.75%”; the preview described a raise “above 8.75%” as the bull case.

surprises.description: IAM reached 15.1% of ARR, ahead of the preview’s 14.4%–14.5% glidepath. Management also guided to 18%–19% by exiting Q4 FY27, modestly above the preview’s roughly 18% year-end target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “IAM now accounts for 15.1% of total ARR, up from 12.6% in Q1, and is guided to reach 18-19% of total ARR by exiting Q4 fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 would need about 14.4% – 14.5% to stay on that path”; management had reaffirmed “about 18% of ARR by fiscal year-end.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS of $1.16 beat the preview’s $1.08–$1.09 consensus range by roughly 6%–7%, although it landed within the preview’s $1.14–$1.17 base-case scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS of $1.16 (up 26%).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS” consensus: “$1.08 – $1.09.”

surprises.description: Revenue of $876 million modestly exceeded consensus of $866.4–$867.2 million and the preview’s base-case range. The 9% reported growth included a 1.3-point FX tailwind, so growth excluding that tailwind was about 7.7%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue reached $876 million, up 9% year-over-year, including a 1.3 percentage point FX tailwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Revenue consensus was “$867.2M” or “$866.4M”; the base case was “$872M – $875M.”

surprises.description: Direct-customer retention was expected to be judged mainly on whether its improvement streak continued; the call additionally said expansion contributed a larger share of the improvement, rather than the gains coming just from retention.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Dollar net retention from Direct customers was 103% (rounded) … with expansion now contributing a larger share of the improvement rather than just retention.”

surprises.description: The preview did not flag the acceleration in MCP adoption: active accounts more than quadrupled during the quarter ahead of the MCP server’s general availability at month-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “MCP active accounts more than quadrupled during the quarter ahead of the MCP server's general availability at month-end.”

surprises.description: The preview did not identify the pace of growth among larger customers as a key metric; customers spending over $300,000 in ACV grew 14% year over year, marking a second consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customers spending over $300,000 in ACV grew 14% year-over-year to nearly 1,300, the second consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.”

in_line: Direct-customer dollar net retention was about 103%, above 102% and modestly higher sequentially, consistent with the preview’s focus on maintaining the seven-quarter improvement streak.
Non-GAAP gross margin of 81.7% was at the top of the guided 81.5%–81.7% range; the slight year-over-year decline was consistent with the preview’s expectation of cloud-migration pressure.

Diluted shares were 193 million, within the preview’s 191–196 million range and consistent with its estimate of an approximately 8% year-over-year reduction. Q2 repurchases of $307 million were close to Q1’s record $317.5 million pace.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was about $208 million, above the preview’s approximately $202 million working benchmark. The preview’s bull scenario began at $208 million, so the result was better than the midpoint benchmark but at the low end of the bull range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenues rose 10% to $208 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$202M” and the bull scenario: “$208–214M.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA was $114 million, above the preview’s approximately $111 million benchmark. However, advertising timing held reported growth to 7%; management said growth would have been 18% without that timing difference.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA grew 7% to $114 million”; “absent this, EBITDA would have grown 18%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~$111M” and the bull scenario: “$115–117M.”

surprises.description: Q3-to-date same-store sales were tracking above 3%, modestly ahead of the preview’s 3.0% bogey. The preview’s bull case was higher, at 3.5% or more.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 currently tracking above 3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bogey: ≥3.0%”; the bull scenario says “QTD ≥3.5%.”

surprises.description: Management’s FY26 net-unit-growth floor of 8% was below the preview’s 8.5% bogey. The difference is limited, and the preview had already noted Q2 net unit growth of about 8%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year 2026 guidance calls for … net unit growth of at least 8%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Bogey: reaffirm ~8.5% unit growth for FY26.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s concern about a public-company cost step-up, management described lower costs from exiting the area director model and a G&A step-down that would support above-algorithm FY26 EBITDA growth. This points to a more favorable cost trajectory than the preview’s flagged risk suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$8 million in lower costs from exiting the area director model”; “a step-down in G&A driving above-algorithm EBITDA growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Public-company cost step-up. Watch incremental G&A and whether it is in the Q2 base.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a much larger international growth opportunity than the preview discussed: management sees potential for over 15,000 global locations, with 600 committed in Canada and a first UK store expected by year-end. The preview focused on the domestic pipeline, so this adds an unanticipated expansion avenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Runway for over 7,500 U.S. and 15,000 global locations”; “600 committed and 30 opened in Canada,” and “a first UK store expected by year-end.”

surprises.description: Management reported a substantial increase in digital marketing investment and associated gains in loyalty registrations and Hispanic-guest ad awareness, details the preview did not quantify. The preview did identify digital marketing as a support for Q3 comps, so the direction was anticipated but the scale and reported engagement gains were not.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Digital marketing was scaled from under 1% to over 20% of total ad spend”; loyalty registrations were “up 22% year-to-date” and ad awareness rose “6% among Hispanic guests.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said QTD comps were “helped by digital marketing.”

in_line: Q2 same-store sales were 2.3%, matching the preview’s pre-announced figure.
The 83 Q2 openings, 130 first-half openings, and roughly 8% net unit growth were consistent with the preview’s reported operating data.
The more than 1,600-unit domestic pipeline was consistent with the preview’s stated pipeline expectation.
Digital channels were 43% of sales mix, matching the preview’s Q2 figure.
Management said the Cyclospora outbreak had no material impact, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the impact would be immaterial.

surprises.description: FY26 ending ARR was $1.242 billion before a $5 million FX adjustment, putting it above the company’s guidance high end but just below the preview’s $1.243 billion-plus whisper. After the adjustment, reported ARR was $1.237 billion, at the guidance high end and below the preview’s base-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ARR finished FY2026 at $1.242 billion…above the high end of guidance, though a year-end FX adjustment lowered reported ARR by $5 million to $1.237 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Ending ARR: $1,229–1,237M” guidance; Stifel’s whisper was “$1,243M+”; the preview’s base scenario was “$1,238–1,244M.”

surprises.description: FY26 non-GAAP operating income reached $340 million, $16 million above the top of the company’s $314–324 million full-year guidance. That was a meaningful beat against the stated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income surged 63% to $340 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY26 guide: … non-GAAP OI $314–324M.”

surprises.description: FY26 operating cash flow was $390 million, exceeding the top of the $365–380 million guidance range by $10 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow grew 30% to $390 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY26 guide: … OCF $365–380M.”

surprises.description: FY26 total revenue came in at $1.475 billion, $5 million above the high end of the $1.460–1.470 billion full-year guide.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue rose 23% to $1.475 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY26 guide: Revenue $1,460–1,470M.”

surprises.description: Q4 core cloud deals totaled 26, exceeding the 19 deals in Q4 FY25 and providing stronger evidence than the preview’s requested proof that slipped deals had closed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company signed 26 core cloud deals in Q4, bringing the full-year total to 62.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “11 cloud deals in Q3 vs. 19 in Q4 FY25. Proof that Q3’s slipped deals closed is needed.”

surprises.description: Subscription and support revenue was $971 million, $2 million above the high end of the full-year guide. The preview did not have a Q4 consensus estimate for this line, but the actual also narrowly topped the company’s annual range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Subscription and support revenue grew 33% to $971 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Full-year FY26 guide: … S&S $963–969M.”

surprises.description: Guidewire reported exceptionally low customer attrition—less than 1.5% overall and under 1% for core systems—and said it added roughly one percentage point to FY26 ARR growth. The preview did not flag this retention contribution as an expected driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record-low gross ARR attrition of less than 1.5% overall and under 1% for core systems customers,” contributing “roughly 1 percentage point to FY2026 ARR growth.”

surprises.description: The company disclosed a defining multiyear cloud migration agreement with Nationwide, which also became its first U.S. Tier 1 PricingCenter customer for home and auto. The preview did not anticipate this named customer win.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Guidewire signed a defining multiyear cloud migration agreement with Nationwide, a Fortune 100 insurer, which also became its first U.S. Tier 1 PricingCenter customer for home and auto lines.”

surprises.description: Guidewire reported substantial wins for PricingCenter and ProNavigator, with 12 and 28 wins respectively for the year, primarily through cross-selling to existing customers. The preview focused on AI and agentic monetization rather than these products’ adoption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “PricingCenter closing 8 deals in Q4 (12 for the year) and ProNavigator delivering 14 wins in Q4 (28 for the year), primarily via cross-sell into the installed base.”

surprises.description: Guidewire repurchased $606 million of stock during FY26, a capital-allocation action and amount not addressed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased $606 million in shares (4.1 million shares at $148.41 average).”

in_line: FY27 ARR guidance of $1.45–1.46 billion matched the preview’s expected range of $1.45–1.46 billion.
Fully ramped ARR growth was 22%, matching the preview’s stated benchmark of 22%.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $410 million, about 3% above the $397.85 million consensus and above the $395–400 million company guide. Revenue growth was 13%, or 16% after normalizing for FX.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 revenue grew 13% to $410 million (16% normalizing for an $8 million FX headwind), beating guidance on top and bottom lines.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue … Street consensus $397.85M”; company guidance was “$395–400M.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating income materially exceeded the roughly $75 million expectation, and the 22% margin was well above the preview’s implied margin of about 18.9%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income rose to $89 million, a 22% margin expanding over 400 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating income … ~$75M”; company guidance implied a margin of “~18.9%.”

surprises.description: Net new ARR reached $37 million, above the roughly $33 million consensus and the preview’s $28–33 million implied range. It also improved from $31 million a year earlier, rather than remaining flat or declining year over year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net new ARR of $37 million improving from $31 million in the prior year quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus is about $33M”; guidance implied “$28–33M,” and the preview said that would mean “flat-to-down net new ARR year over year.”

surprises.description: The FY27 ARR outlook was raised above the prior range, contrary to the preview’s base case of an unchanged ARR guide. The new range is $2.065–2.070 billion versus $2.058–2.063 billion previously.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year fiscal 2027 guidance calls for … ARR of $2.065-$2.070 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The current range is $2.058–2.063B”; the base case expected “ARR guide unchanged.”

surprises.description: UiPath reported a fourth consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability, a positive result not anticipated in the preview’s discussion of recent EPS conversion concerns.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company delivered its fourth consecutive quarter of GAAP profitability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “UiPath has beaten on revenue and operating income while missing EPS in recent quarters. Watch the tax rate and share count.”

surprises.description: Growth in customers with at least $1 million of ARR accelerated to 21%, above the 18% growth cited in the preview’s prior-quarter figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Customers with $1 million or more in ARR grew 21% to 387.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$1M+ ARR customers grew 18% YoY.”

surprises.description: AI appeared in 18 of the top 20 deals, up from the 16 of 20 cited for Q1, and management said AI- or platform-attached deals are naturally much larger. The preview raised agentic AI monetization as an open question, but the call facts provide no dollar figure for agentic ARR.
surprises.fact_evidence: “18 of the top 20 deals this quarter included AI”; “deals with AI/platform attached are naturally much larger, driving higher ROI and deal values.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “16 of the top 20 deals included AI”; “The open question is whether management puts a dollar figure on agentic ARR.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed that CFO Ashim Gupta is moving to focus exclusively on his COO role and that Deputy CFO Hitesh Ramani will succeed him as CFO. The preview did not flag an impending CFO transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Ashim Gupta moving to focus exclusively as COO and Deputy CFO Hitesh Ramani succeeding him as CFO.”

surprises.description: Coding agents used by forward deployed engineers reduced implementation effort by nearly 60%, an efficiency improvement the preview did not anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Coding agents used by forward deployed engineers reduced implementation effort by nearly 60%.”

in_line: Ending ARR was $1.938 billion, within the preview’s base-case range of $1.935–1.938 billion and described there as roughly in line with expectations.
Dollar-based net retention was 109% (108% FX-adjusted), matching the 109% reported in Q1 that the preview cited.

surprises.description: Non-GAAP EPS was $0.15, well above the preview’s $0.09–$0.10 expectation. That is roughly 50%–67% higher than the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP EPS nearly doubled to $0.15 from $0.08 a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP diluted EPS: $0.09–$0.10.”

surprises.description: Q2 operating cash flow was positive at $1.1 million, versus the preview’s expectation of around negative $5 million. However, the company also withdrew its prior $45 million full-year cash-flow figure and replaced it with the less specific “significant positive” guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company generated positive operating cash flow of $1.1 million in Q2 (versus negative $6.3 million a year ago), but withdrew its prior $45 million full-year cash flow figure in favor of ‘significant positive’ guidance due to deliberate inventory investments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 OCF against the approximately −$5M base case”; the company’s FY27 guidance included “Operating cash flow ~$45M.”

surprises.description: Short-term RPO fell to $313.4 million from $363.4 million in Q1 and $355.0 million a year earlier, contrary to the preview’s expectation that it would increase sequentially and year over year. Total RPO also fell to $470.2 million; management cited multiyear contract consumption and cancelable subscription revenue excluded from reported figures.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total RPO declined to $470.2 million (with $313.4 million short-term), which management attributed to $30 million of multiyear contract consumption and $42 million of cancelable subscription revenue excluded from reported figures.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A sequential and Y/Y increase in short-term RPO would support the guide.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP gross margin reached 73.7%, 40 basis points above the preview’s approximately 73.3% estimate. Management linked the expansion in part to professional services falling to under 8% of revenue from about 15% a year earlier.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin expanded 154 basis points year-over-year to 73.7%, aided by the shift away from professional services, which fell to under 8% of revenue from about 15% a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP gross margin: ~73.3%.”

surprises.description: The company narrowed its FY27 revenue range to approximately $448 million, plus or minus 2%, while keeping the midpoint unchanged. The midpoint reaffirmation matched the preview, but the narrower range was not anticipated.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company narrowed its full-year revenue guidance to approximately $448 million (±2%), roughly 12% growth, while keeping the midpoint unchanged.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $448M ±3% (+12% at midpoint).”

surprises.description: Management said the shift toward subscriptions is masking underlying growth, estimating that growth would be several percentage points higher if the perpetual/subscription mix had stayed constant. The preview focused on reported revenue growth and did not anticipate this explanation of stronger underlying momentum.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management indicated the accelerating shift toward subscriptions is masking underlying momentum, estimating growth would be several percentage points higher if the perpetual/subscription mix had stayed constant with last year.”

in_line: Revenue was approximately $109 million, essentially matching the preview’s $109.2 million consensus estimate.
Recurring revenue reached 51.4% of total revenue, consistent with the preview’s watch for the mix to cross 50%.
Adjusted EBITDA was $14.9 million, close to the preview’s roughly $15–16 million implied estimate.

surprises.description: FY27 revenue guidance rose to $2.043–2.047 billion, above the preview’s roughly $2.02 billion consensus and its $2.03–2.04 billion base case. The preview flagged the size of the guide raise as a key test, and the new range is a stronger outcome than its base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management guided full-year FY27 revenue to $2.043–2.047 billion (26% growth).
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus ~$2.02B (post-raise expected)”; base scenario: “Raised to $2.03–2.04B.”

surprises.description: Non-GAAP operating margin reached 21%, above the preview’s approximately 18% expectation. That is a meaningful margin outperformance against the stated bar.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Non-GAAP operating margin reached 21%, up 6 percentage points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Non-GAAP op. margin” consensus: “~18%”; company guidance: “18%.”

surprises.description: Net new ARR was $134 million, at the top of the preview’s consensus range and above its $125–130 million key-metric bar. The result was a modest upside rather than a miss toward the preview’s bear case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “$134 million in net new ARR that grew 28% year-over-year in constant currency.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus net new ARR: “~$120–135M”; key metric bar: “roughly $125–130M.”

surprises.description: The $1 million-plus customer cohort added a record 20 customers, but its ARR growth was described only as “over 50%,” below the preview’s 60%+ bull-case marker and its 62% comparison point. The record additions are encouraging, while the growth-rate wording does not affirm the expected pace.
surprises.fact_evidence: “20 customers with $1 million+ in ARR”; the cohort “surpassing $500 million and growing over 50% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bull case said the “$1M+ cohort keeps growing at 60% or more”; its key-metric section compared growth “versus 62% y/y.”

surprises.description: Management newly lowered its full-year free-cash-flow-margin outlook to roughly 100 basis points below FY26, citing device purchases, inventory pre-buys, and elevated supply-chain costs. The preview did not flag a lower FCF-margin outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management now expects full-year free cash flow margin to be roughly 100 basis points lower than FY26” because of “more IoT device purchases, inventory pre-buys, and elevated supply chain costs in the second half.”

surprises.description: GAAP EPS was positive, as the preview expected GAAP profitability, but the reported $0.03 was below the preview’s roughly $0.05–0.07 consensus. Profitability itself was in line; the per-share result was weaker than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Positive GAAP EPS of $0.03.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: GAAP EPS consensus: “~$0.05–0.07”; company guidance was “GAAP profitable.”

surprises.description: The $100,000-plus customer cohort accelerated for a fourth consecutive quarter and reached 38% year-over-year growth, alongside a record 242 additions. The preview gave the prior-year cohort growth rate but did not anticipate this continued acceleration or a new additions record.
surprises.fact_evidence: The cohort reached “$1.3 billion in ARR,” was “growing 38% year-over-year and marking the fourth consecutive quarter of sequential acceleration”; Samsara added a record “242 customers with $100,000+ in ARR.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported that customers above $100K ARR were at “3,363 (+169 q/q, +37% y/y)” in Q1 FY27.

surprises.description: Public sector produced its second-highest-ever net-new-ACV mix, including a top-five U.S. city deal with more than $2 million from emerging products. The preview did not identify this vertical or deal as an expected driver.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Public sector delivered its second-highest-ever net new ACV mix,” driven by “a top-5 U.S. city deal that included more than $2 million from emerging products.”

surprises.description: Field services was the largest vertical and reached its highest net-new-ACV mix in more than two years, an unexpected source of strength not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Field services was the largest vertical with its highest net new ACV mix in over two years.”

surprises.description: Adoption of Samsara’s latest AI features increased more than fourfold in two months, with over 1,000 customers engaged. The preview said agentic AI was still in beta but did not anticipate this adoption measure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adoption of Samsara's latest AI features rose more than 4x over the past two months with over 1,000 customers engaged.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Agentic AI is still in beta.”

surprises.description: Large emerging-product transactions increased to more than 60 from 42 the prior quarter, a demand signal not anticipated in the preview. The continued contribution of emerging products above 20% of net new ACV, however, was expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 60 transactions containing $100,000+ in emerging product ACV, up from 42 last quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said emerging products had made up “more than 20% of net new ACV for two straight quarters.”

in_line: Emerging products contributed more than 20% of net new ACV for a third consecutive quarter, extending the trend the preview said had already lasted two quarters.
Samsara remained GAAP profitable, consistent with the preview’s stated company guidance of “GAAP profitable.”
Agentic use cases remained early-stage, consistent with the preview’s description of agentic AI as still in beta.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was expected to be a loss of about $0.04, but DXL reported a profit of $0.05; adjusted EBITDA was also $7.7 million, above the preview’s $4–6 million bull-case range. This was a substantial upside earnings gap.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose to $7.7 million (6.9% of sales) from $4.7 million a year ago, while adjusted EPS improved to $0.05 from $0.01.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 FY26 consensus” adjusted EPS “-$0.04”; the bull scenario expected “adj. EBITDA $4–6M.”

surprises.description: DXL reported $111.6 million in sales, above the approximately $109.3 million consensus estimate, although it was within the preview’s $110–113 million operating base case. The beat was modest rather than a major departure from the preview’s own range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales were $111.6 million, down 3.4% year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue ~$109.3M”; the preview’s operating base case was “$110–113M.”

surprises.description: Gross margin rose 270 basis points to 47.9%, but a one-time $4.6 million tariff refund drove the reported improvement; excluding it, merchandise margin would have been roughly 70 basis points worse year over year. That made the headline margin result much stronger than the underlying trend.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A one-time $4.6 million IEPA tariff refund benefited merchandise margin and drove gross margin up 270 basis points to 47.9%, but excluding the refund merchandise margin would have been roughly 70 basis points worse than last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview flagged “Gross margin and clearance inventory against the 100bps tariff headwind.”

surprises.description: Liquidity was better than the preview’s cash concern implied: cash and investments were $20.1 million versus $16.2 million at the prior quarter, with no debt and no revolver draw. This stayed well clear of the preview’s roughly $12 million downside threshold.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company reported a fortress balance sheet with $20.1 million of cash and investments, no debt, and $61.7 million of excess availability.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch “Cash of $16.2M” and described “cash below ~$12M or a first revolver draw” as a bear-case trigger.

surprises.description: DXL added a concrete multi-year store-rationalization plan that the preview did not anticipate: it expects to close about three stores this year and is evaluating a few dozen 2027 lease renewals. Management expects occupancy-cost and sales-per-square-foot benefits beginning in 2027, so the payoff is prospective.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management is executing a multi-year store rationalization plan closing about 3 stores this year and evaluating a few dozen lease renewals in 2027, expected to reduce occupancy costs and improve sales per square foot beginning in 2027.”

surprises.description: Management reported a more pointed concern about FullBeauty than the preview had described: the board cited deteriorating operating performance and increased indebtedness, saying FullBeauty could have negative equity value and the merger could substantially dilute DXL shareholders. The preview already expected the board to oppose the merger, so the surprise is the severity and detail of the stated rationale, not the vote recommendation.
surprises.fact_evidence: The board cited “Full Beauty's deteriorating operating performance, increased indebtedness, potential negative equity value, and substantial dilution.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “The FullBeauty merger has effectively broken: the board reversed in July 2026 and now recommends voting against the share issuance.”

surprises.description: DXL said GLP-1 use is prompting some customers to pause purchases while losing weight, but a majority of those customers say they plan to return once their size stabilizes. The stated return intention offers a more favorable possibility than the preview’s description of GLP-1-related sizing changes as a structural sales overhang.
surprises.fact_evidence: “GLP-1 medication adoption among a meaningful portion of customers is driving weight-loss-related purchase pauses, though a majority of these customers say they intend to return to DXL once they reach a stable size.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management attributes sales pressure to GLP-1 medications changing customer sizing, which caps the multiple.”

surprises.description: DXL reported an early brand-awareness gain in a targeted core customer group: awareness among 35–64-year-olds in households earning over $100,000 rose from 40% to 49% in seven months. The preview anticipated a substantive standalone-strategy discussion but did not preview this measured progress.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Brand awareness in the core 35-64 demographic (household income above $100,000) rising from 40% to 49% in seven months.”

surprises.description: ThermaChill, a DXL private brand, showed reported demand growth of 56% year to date, an initiative-specific result not anticipated in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ThermaChill private-brand demand up 56% year-to-date.”

surprises.description: FitMap had been used to scan more than 150,000 customers, and those customers showed higher average order value and lower return rates. The preview did not identify this customer-data initiative or its reported outcomes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over 150,000 customers scanned via FitMap showing higher AOV and lower return rates.”

in_line: Q2 comparable sales were down 3.5%, close to Q1’s 3.8% decline, consistent with the preview’s expectation that the comp trend would stabilize against the easier comparison.
The board’s recommendation that stockholders vote against the FullBeauty merger was already anticipated in the preview.

Store traffic remained a central challenge, with store comps weaker than direct-business comps, consistent with the preview’s prior-quarter channel split and its warning about GLP-1-related customer sizing changes.

surprises.description: Q2 sales and comps came in ahead of the preview’s expectations: net sales were $4.9 billion versus estimates of $4.77–$4.82 billion, while comps grew 2.7% (2.8% go-forward) against an implied +1.5% to +2%.
surprises.fact_evidence: Net sales were up 1.1% to $4.9 billion and comparable sales grew 2.7% (2.8% on a go-forward basis).
surprises.expectation_evidence: Net sales consensus was $4.82B or $4.77B–$4.78B; comparable sales were estimated at roughly +1.5% to +2% implied by revenue consensus.

surprises.description: Adjusted EPS of $0.63 was far above the published $0.35–$0.37 consensus, but included about $0.23 from tariff refunds. Excluding that benefit, EPS was about $0.40—above the high end of company guidance and published consensus, but within the preview’s $0.39–$0.43 buy-side bogey.
surprises.fact_evidence: Adjusted EPS was $0.63 versus $0.35 a year ago, but included a roughly $0.23 net tariff refund benefit; excluding this, adjusted EPS rose 14% year-over-year and beat the high end of guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus was $0.35–$0.37, while the preview cited a buy-side bogey of roughly $0.39–$0.43 and Q2 guidance of $0.29–$0.34.

surprises.description: The reported gross margin of 41.5% was well above the preview’s roughly 39.6%–39.7% bogey, but the underlying improvement was much smaller once tariff and fuel effects were excluded: only about 10 basis points of expansion. That makes the headline margin beat less substantial on an underlying basis than the reported rate suggests.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin reached 41.5% of net sales versus 39.7% last year, but underlying gross margin (excluding tariff and fuel impacts) expanded only about 10 basis points.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview set a gross-margin bogey of about 39.6%–39.7% and said to strip out any tariff-refund benefit before crediting a beat.

surprises.description: Macy’s raised its full-year EPS and comp ranges, but the outlook did not include the explicit second-half improvement the preview was looking for: management left second-half sales assumptions unchanged. The EPS midpoint is $2.25, below the preview’s $2.30 catalyst threshold, though the raised range reaches $2.35.
surprises.fact_evidence: Full-year guidance was raised to adjusted diluted EPS of $2.15 to $2.35 and comparable sales of up 1.0% to 1.5%, with second-half sales assumptions unchanged from prior outlook.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview looked for FY26 EPS at or above $2.30 with an explicit second-half raise; prior guidance was $2.00–$2.20 EPS and comps of +0.5% to +1.2%.

surprises.description: Q3 comp guidance was weak relative to the preview’s caution marker: the range runs from down 0.5% to up 0.5%, below the preview’s roughly +1% level. The tougher 3.2% prior-year comparison is management’s stated context, but does not change that the outlook is below the preview’s marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q3 guidance implies a comp sales range of down 0.5% to up 0.5% against a tougher prior-year comp of 3.2%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said a Q3 comp guide below about +1% would signal real caution.

surprises.description: First-half free cash flow was a $262 million inflow, a strong positive cash generation result not addressed in the preview. Macy’s also returned $201 million to shareholders, including $100 million of buybacks, versus the $50 million buyback noted for Q1.
surprises.fact_evidence: Free cash flow was an inflow of $262 million in the first half versus an outflow of $88 million last year, and the company returned $201 million to shareholders (dividends plus $100 million buybacks) with ~$1 billion remaining on its buyback authorization.

in_line: Bloomingdale’s remained in double-digit comp growth, as the preview was watching for: comps were up 11.3%.
The Macy’s nameplate turned positive at +1.1%, and reimagined stores continued to outperform at +1.9%, consistent with the preview’s focus on positive nameplate comps and the Reimagine-store spread.

surprises.description: Lovesac recognized about $20 million of tariff refunds through cost of merchandise sold, far above the roughly $3.4–3.6 million the preview expected to be in the quarter’s gross-margin guide. That drove reported gross margin to 68.4% and EPS to $0.51, including an $0.86-per-share benefit; without the refund benefit, EPS would have been about a $0.35 loss, near the preview’s estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company received approximately $21 million in IEPA tariff refunds, with $20 million recognized through cost of merchandise sold, contributing an $0.86 per diluted share benefit to reported Q2 EPS of $0.51. Gross margin rose to 68.4%, while margin excluding refunds was approximately 56%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “About $3.4–3.6M of tariff refunds sit inside the guide, worth roughly 210–220 bps.” The preview also said “$17.4M remains outstanding” and expected Q2 EPS of “$(0.36) to $(0.39).”

surprises.description: Omnichannel comparable sales fell 1.9%, weaker than the preview’s roughly flat consensus and its base-case range of −1% to +0.5%. Reported net sales were close to consensus, so the comp result showed weaker underlying sales than the headline revenue figure suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Omnichannel comparable sales declining 1.9%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Consensus is roughly flat.” The preview’s base case was “Comp −1% to +0.5%.”

surprises.description: Lovesac cut its FY27 outlook instead of reiterating it: the sales range is now $690–710 million versus $700–740 million, and Adjusted EBITDA is $31.5–35.5 million versus $35–46 million. The preview identified reiteration as the base case, making the lower ranges a meaningful deterioration in the expected second-half contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company cut its full-year outlook, now guiding to net sales of $690-710 million, net income of $0.5-18.5 million, and Adjusted EBITDA of $31.5-35.5 million,” with a wide range and conservative caution.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Reiteration is the base case.” The preview listed FY27 sales guidance of “$700M – $740M” and Adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$35M – $46M.”

surprises.description: The second-half contribution is more concentrated in Q4 than the preview’s back-half bridge implied: Q3 is guided to sales of $140–150 million and a net loss of $9–12 million, while four major launches have shifted toward Q4. That leaves the expected launch-driven recovery later than investors were led to anticipate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 guidance calls for net sales of $140-150 million with an expected net loss of $9-12 million, reflecting the delayed timing of major product launches now shifted toward Q4.” Four major launches are slated for the second half, with meaningful revenue impact “concentrated in Q4 rather than Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the FY27 guide required “H2 sales of $400–440M” and that “most of the full-year $35–46M must come in Q3 and Q4.” It also flagged whether management would provide a quantified Q3 revenue range.

surprises.description: The 0.4% total-business growth figure included a 160-basis-point contribution from the strategic exit of the Best Buy partnership. That previously unflagged driver means the underlying business was weaker than the small positive headline growth rate implies.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The strategic exit of the Best Buy partnership contributed 160 basis points of total business growth.”

surprises.description: Management disclosed a split in Sactionals demand that the preview did not identify: configurations priced above $6,000 grew double digits, while configurations below $6,000 remained pressured and had not returned to growth despite promotions and pricing changes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Sactionals configurations over $6,000 grew double digits,” while the under-$6,000 segment “remained pressured and has not yet returned to growth despite promotional and pricing adjustments.”

in_line: Q2 net sales of $161.2 million were close to the preview’s $161.55–163.39 million consensus range and within company guidance of $157–166 million.

Gross margin excluding tariff refunds was approximately 56%, down 40 basis points from the prior year, broadly matching the preview’s expectation of about 55.3–56.3% and flat to slightly down from 56.4%.
Adjusted EBITDA excluding the tariff refund benefit was a $1.3 million loss, within the preview’s cited Q2 guidance range of a $4 million loss to $2 million of income.

surprises.description: The preview anchored FY26 adjusted EPS at $0.28–$0.38, with the high end as the likely direction. Management raised the range to $0.47–$0.52, a much larger upgrade than that expectation implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year adjusted diluted EPS guidance to $0.47-$0.52, up sharply from prior guidance of $0.28-$0.38.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 diluted EPS: $0.28–$0.38 … Guidance is the anchor”; the preview also said to watch whether “trending toward the high end” was repeated or raised.

surprises.description: The preview said Q2 retail comps were guided to “flat to slightly up,” but comps fell 2.4%. That was a clear miss against the stated turnaround marker.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Comparable store sales down 2.4%”; seasonal sandals accounted for roughly 200 basis points of the retail decline.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management guided Q2 retail to ‘flat to slightly up.’”

surprises.description: Q2 sales were $730.6 million, below the preview’s $735–$750 million implied range and its roughly $742 million base case, despite the stronger Brand Portfolio result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 net sales fell approximately 1% year-over-year to $730.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$735–750M implied”; the base scenario was “~$742M (+0.3%).”

surprises.description: The preview expected IEEPA refunds to be largely offset by new tariffs, but a $20.2 million tariff refund claim contributed 280 basis points to a 430-basis-point adjusted gross-margin expansion. The result included a substantial benefit the preview had not expected to flow through unoffset.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted gross margin expanded 430 basis points to 47.9%, though 280 basis points of that came from a $20.2 million tariff refund claim, leaving 150 basis points of underlying improvement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance excludes tariff impacts and assumes IEEPA refund claims are largely offset by new Section 301 tariffs possibly starting in August.”

surprises.description: The preview listed FY26 sales guidance of negative 1% to positive 1%. The new flat-to-up 1% range removes the downside end, a modest improvement in the full-year outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Lifted sales guidance to flat-to-up 1% from prior negative 1% to positive 1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 net sales: −1% to +1%.”

surprises.description: The preview’s own Q2 base case was $0.32 per adjusted share, while the reported result was $0.34. That was a small beat, although it was close to the prior-year result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 adjusted net income was $19.2 million ($0.34 per diluted share), only modestly above last year's $16.4 million ($0.33).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario estimated “Adj. EPS ~$0.32”; it separately cautioned that the $0.22 consensus figure might be stale.

surprises.description: The preview called out an approximately $10 million Q3 incentive-compensation headwind and asked whether it had grown.
