Management described greater year-over-year Q3 profitability pressure tied to prior-year incentive-compensation comparisons, suggesting a tougher comparison than the preview’s framing.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management flagged greater year-over-year profitability pressure in Q3 due to prior-year incentive compensation comparisons.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management flagged a roughly $10M incentive-comp headwind in Q3. Confirm it has not grown.”

surprises.description: The preview asked for Q3 quarter-to-date comps but gave no positive trend to rely on. Management reported retail sales slightly positive quarter-to-date and athletic demand improving 400 basis points sequentially in August, a more encouraging early-quarter update.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 is off to a strong start with retail sales slightly positive quarter-to-date and athletic demand improving 400 basis points sequentially in August.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “any Q3 quarter-to-date comps” as a catalyst to check, without giving a positive QTD expectation.

surprises.description: The preview highlighted the company’s $475.3 million of debt and leverage concerns. Debt was reported at $423.1 million, with about $198 million of total liquidity, a stronger balance-sheet position than the preview’s latest debt figure showed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reduced total debt to $423.1 million from $516.3 million a year ago (a $93 million reduction) and ended the quarter with roughly $198 million in total liquidity.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview reported “Balance sheet: debt $475.3M” and highlighted “$475M debt” as a leverage concern.

surprises.description: Management disclosed that Topo is expected to exceed $100 million in sales in 2027, while noting it is in only about 1,600 doors and not in DSW. The preview discussed Topo’s prior-quarter growth but did not include this forward sales target or distribution detail.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Topo brand grew revenue over 24% in the quarter and is expected to exceed $100 million in sales in 2027, with distribution still limited to about 1,600 doors and no presence in DSW.”

surprises.description: Retail merchandise margin expanded 140 basis points, including 100 basis points from reduced markdowns, despite a promotional environment. The preview discussed prior-quarter lower markdowns but did not anticipate this Q2 retail-margin result.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Retail merchandise margin expanded 140 basis points (100 bps from reduced markdowns) despite a promotional environment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted prior-quarter gross-margin improvement “on lower markdowns and cleaner inventory,” but gave no Q2 retail merchandise-margin expectation.

in_line: Brand Portfolio sales grew 18%, broadly in line with the preview’s expectation that growth would sustain at about 19%.

surprises.description: Lesaka’s FY26 adjusted EPS was ZAR 6.51, above the preview’s company-guidance range of ZAR 5.50–6.00. The result cleared the top of the range by about 8.5%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EPS grew 210% to ZAR 6.51.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EPS | ZAR 5.50–6.00.”

surprises.description: The preview’s base case expected FY27 guidance to exclude Bank Zero, or for the company to defer it until closing. Instead, Lesaka issued FY27 guidance that includes Bank Zero, which it expects to close before year-end.
surprises.fact_evidence: “For FY27 the company guided to net revenue of ZAR 7.0-7.7 billion, group adjusted EBITDA of ZAR 1.45-1.6 billion, and adjusted EPS of ZAR 7.50-8.50, inclusive of Bank Zero which is expected to close before year-end.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: ... FY27 guided ex-Bank Zero”; “A guide that excludes Bank Zero, or one that defers to ‘update on close,’ is the most likely source of disappointment.”

surprises.description: Merchant revenue did not show a sustained recovery: although it grew 3% for FY26, Q4 revenue fell 10% year over year as take rates declined, including a 25% drop in the ADP take rate, despite higher transaction volumes.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Merchant division struggled, with net revenue up only 3% to ZAR 3.1 billion and Q4 net revenue declining 10% to ZAR 729 million as take rates fell (ADP take rate down 25%) despite acquiring TPV growing 27% and ADP TPV growing 31%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management has implied a return to growth. This division caused the last two revenue shortfalls.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EPS was ZAR 2.40, above the preview’s implied Q4 range of ZAR 1.26–1.76, exceeding its upper end by roughly 36%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EPS rose from ZAR 0.90 to ZAR 2.40.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Implied Q4 ... adj. EPS ~ZAR 1.26–1.76.”

surprises.description: Merchant segment adjusted EBITDA fell sharply, and management also said one-off and restructuring costs will weigh on the division’s Q1 FY27 results.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Merchant segment adjusted EBITDA declined 33% to ZAR 122 million in Q4, and management flagged one-off and restructuring costs that will pressure Q1 FY27 results.”

surprises.description: Net debt to group adjusted EBITDA reached 1.9x, below Lesaka’s 2.0x target and the 2.1x level reported at Q3, so the company moved past the target the preview highlighted.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt to group adjusted EBITDA fell to 1.9x, below its 2x target and down from 2.9x a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net debt/adj. EBITDA improved to 2.1x against a 2.0x target”; the preview also flagged “net debt/EBITDA against the 2.0x target.”

surprises.description: The call described a Bank Zero funding plan that could reduce gross debt to about ZAR 2.3 billion and leverage below 1x by June 2027, with near-zero gross debt possible by June 2028; the preview noted the pending acquisition but did not anticipate this debt-reduction path.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Bank Zero acquisition is expected to reduce gross debt from ZAR 3.8 billion to approximately ZAR 2.3 billion and cut leverage to below 1x by June 2027 by migrating lending books to be funded via customer deposits, potentially reaching near-zero gross debt by June 2028.”

surprises.description: Management introduced FY29 ambitions—including about ZAR 11 billion in net revenue, an EBITDA margin above 25%, and adjusted EPS above ZAR 18—that were not covered in the preview’s expectations.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management set medium-term FY29 ambitions of 3 million active consumers, 200,000 active merchants, Enterprise TPV of ZAR 80 billion, net revenue of circa ZAR 11 billion (over 20% CAGR), EBITDA margin above 25%, and adjusted EPS exceeding ZAR 18 (over $1 at current exchange rates).”

in_line: FY26 net revenue of ZAR 6.33 billion was within the company’s ZAR 6.2–6.5 billion guidance range and above its ZAR 6.2 billion floor.
FY26 group adjusted EBITDA of ZAR 1.27 billion was within the ZAR 1.25–1.35 billion guidance range and near the low end, as the preview expected.
Lesaka achieved positive FY26 GAAP net income, as the preview expected and flagged as a key issue.
Q4 group adjusted EBITDA of ZAR 367 million was within the preview’s implied Q4 range of ZAR 338–438 million.
Merchant revenue grew 3% for the full year, consistent with the preview’s expectation of a return to growth, though Q4 revenue declined.

surprises.description: Q2 revenue was $181 million, above the preview’s $176.5–$178.2 million consensus range and at the favorable end of company guidance. The beat was modest relative to the consensus midpoint.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 net revenue was $181 million, a 25% year-over-year decline, at the favorable end of guidance for a 25%–30% decline.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Consensus revenue was $176.5M–$178.2M; company guidance was a 25%–30% year-over-year decline.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $13 million materially exceeded the preview’s $8–$10 million company-guidance range.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $13 million, beating the $8–$10 million guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: Q2 adjusted EBITDA guidance was $8M–$10M.

surprises.description: The Q3 revenue outlook was much better than the preview’s roughly 20% decline implication: management guided to only about a 5% decline. That is a substantial improvement versus the market’s anticipated pace of contraction.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company guided Q3 net revenue to decline only approximately 5% year-over-year, with management saying the worst of the acquisition-driven pressure was behind it.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said consensus implied about a 20% decline and identified a guide better than -15% as supporting the recovery thesis.

surprises.description: Management quantified full-year adjusted EBITDA at $30–$32 million, rather than leaving the outlook at the previously stated, unquantified commitment to be positive.
surprises.fact_evidence: Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA was guided to $30–$32 million.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said FY26 adjusted EBITDA was described as “Positive,” not quantified, and that a specific number would signal confidence.

surprises.description: Gross margin came in below the preview’s roughly 70% expectation, at 68.7%. Management attributed much of the shortfall to an approximately 8% AOV decline, while characterizing that pressure as non-structural and recoverable.
surprises.fact_evidence: Gross margin compressed approximately 360 basis points year-over-year to 68.7%, driven largely by an approximately 8% AOV decline that management characterized as non-structural and recoverable.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated gross margin at approximately 70% and flagged gross margin at or above 70% as a catalyst.

surprises.description: The full-year revenue outlook implies a slower Q4 than the sharp Q3 improvement might suggest: a roughly 19% full-year decline implies Q4 revenue down about 10%–11%, versus Q3’s guided 5% decline. Management described the implied Q4 decline as conservatism rather than sandbagging.
surprises.fact_evidence: Full-year 2026 net revenue is expected to decline approximately 19%, implying Q4 growth of roughly negative 10%–11% versus Q3’s negative 5%; management framed this as conservatism rather than sandbagging.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q3 revenue guidance was the key number and that a guide better than -15% would support the recovery thesis; it did not provide a full-year revenue expectation.

surprises.description: SpoiledChild was on track for at least 35% growth and nearly $350 million in 2026 revenue, reaching that scale more than a year faster than IL MAKIAGE did. The preview did not identify this brand trajectory as an expected result.
surprises.fact_evidence: SpoiledChild is on track to grow at least 35% and approach $350 million of net revenue in 2026, reaching that milestone more than a year faster than IL MAKIAGE did.

surprises.description: The call disclosed a notable new brand and pipeline outlook: METHODIQ is expected to exceed SpoiledChild’s first-year revenue, with plans to enter longevity and metabolic health—including prescription injectables and peptides—in 2027, alongside a planned fourth brand launch. The preview did not anticipate these specifics.
surprises.fact_evidence: METHODIQ, launched less than a year ago, is expected to deliver higher first-year revenue than SpoiledChild, with plans to expand into longevity/metabolic health including prescription injectable and peptide therapies in 2027, alongside a planned Brand 4 launch.

surprises.description: The company also disclosed repurchasing $50 million face value of its 2030 exchangeable notes for $35 million, a discounted debt buyback not raised in the preview. The strong cash and undrawn credit facilities provide context for that capital allocation.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company ended Q2 with $561 million in cash and investments, undrawn $350 million credit facilities, and repurchased $50 million face value of its 2030 exchangeable notes for $35 million.

in_line: Q2 revenue’s 25% year-over-year decline was within the company’s previously announced 25%–30% guidance range, even though the dollar result exceeded consensus.

The company continued its substantial buyback: year-to-date repurchases reached 11.7 million shares for $163 million, compared with $82.3 million spent in Q1 and $167.3 million remaining at the time of the preview.

surprises.description: Q2 adjusted operating margin was 20.3%, about 190 basis points above the preview’s 18.4% guide, rather than showing the expected margin compression.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted operating margin was 20.3%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. operating income $56.5–57.5M (18.4% margin)”

surprises.description: Total ARR reached $1.231 billion, $11 million above the roughly $1.22 billion Q2 expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q2 FY27 total ARR reached $1.231 billion… exceeding the guidance midpoint by $11 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Total ARR… ~$1.22B”

surprises.description: Instead of holding FY27 ARR guidance at $1.369 billion, SailPoint raised it by $11 million to $1.38 billion. That is an increase, though below the preview’s bull-case threshold of at least $1.385 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY27 guidance was raised by $11 million to $1.38 billion ARR.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base: … FY ARR held at $1.369B”; the bull case called for “FY27 ARR [to be] raised to at least $1.385B.”

surprises.description: AI-driven solutions made up more than 30% of Q2 net new ARR, and the AI-driven pipeline more than doubled to over $200 million in less than three months—strong demand indicators the preview had not quantified.
surprises.fact_evidence: “AI-driven solutions accounted for more than 30% of net new ARR in Q2, and the AI-driven pipeline has more than doubled to over $200 million since Investor Day less than three months ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked for “any quantification of agentic or non-human identity ARR” but gave no pipeline or net-new contribution benchmark.

surprises.description: Existing customers adopting AI-driven solutions increased annual spend by more than 60%, above the 25–50% uplift range discussed at Analyst Day.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Existing customers adopting AI-driven solutions increased their annual spend by over 60%, exceeding the 25-50% uplift range discussed at Analyst Day.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “25-50% uplift range discussed at Analyst Day.”

surprises.description: SaaS ARR contributed 97% of total net new ARR, above the company’s guided 90–95% range. The higher SaaS mix also created an approximately $5 million revenue-timing headwind.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net new SaaS ARR of $66 million… accounting for 97% of total net new ARR—above the guided 90-95% range”; “The higher SaaS mix created an approximately $5 million revenue timing headwind.”

surprises.description: AI-driven ARR had already surpassed $70 million by quarter-end, putting SailPoint well ahead of pace for its $100 million fiscal-year-end target; the preview had identified AI ARR quantification as a key catalyst but gave no expected amount.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total AI-driven ARR already surpassed $70 million by end of Q2, putting the company well ahead of pace to hit its $100 million fiscal year-end target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called for “any quantification of agentic or non-human identity ARR” but did not state an expected figure.

surprises.description: Revenue was $309 million, slightly below the $310.4 million consensus estimate, although it remained within the company’s $308–312 million guidance range. The reported SaaS-mix timing headwind provides relevant context but does not change the small consensus shortfall.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total revenue was $309 million”; “The higher SaaS mix created an approximately $5 million revenue timing headwind.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue $308–312M”; “Consensus $310.4M.”

surprises.description: RPO growth accelerated to 30%, with current RPO up 27%, a forward-demand data point the preview did not flag or set an expectation for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “RPO accelerated to 30% growth ($1.9 billion) and current RPO grew 27% to $931 million on larger deal sizes.”

surprises.description: More than two-thirds of migrations included an AI-driven solution, and those migrations contributed about four points to ARR growth with 2–3x ARR uplift—more substantial AI-related contribution than the preview’s prior-quarter description of agentic contribution as minimal suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Over two-thirds of migrations (contributing ~4 points to ARR growth) included an AI-driven solution with 2-3x ARR uplift.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Management said only a ‘minimal’ agentic contribution is embedded in guidance.”

surprises.description: Entro-based POCs were reported to shorten sales cycles to 30–45 days versus traditional agentic-suite purchases, an unexpectedly favorable sales-cycle development relative to the preview’s stated risk of elongated deal cycles.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Entro-based POCs are shortening sales cycles to 30-45 days versus traditional agentic suite purchases.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “elongated deal cycles” as a bear-case signal.

in_line: FY27 revenue guidance of approximately $1.27 billion was in line with the preview’s roughly $1.27 billion consensus and $1.265–1.275 billion company range.
FY27 adjusted operating margin guidance of about 19%, adjusted EPS of $0.32, and free cash flow of approximately $200 million were in line with the preview’s expectations.
Dollar-based net retention was 113%, matching the preview’s expectation that it would remain near the Q1 level of 113%.

surprises.description: Q1 revenue was $31 million, about 4.7% above the $29.6 million consensus and above the preview’s $30.3 million catalyst threshold. This was a stronger result than the preview’s base case of roughly $30.3 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q1 FY2027 revenue grew 60% year-over-year to $31 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue: $29.6M”; the preview also said “Revenue at or above $30.3M” would clear its catalyst threshold.

surprises.description: Management raised FY2027 revenue guidance by $4 million, from $137 million to $141 million. The preview identified a raise as the key test and said $139–141 million would signal strength.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year FY2027 revenue guidance was raised to $141 million (48% growth) from the prior $137 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A raise to $139–141M would signal strength”; “Guidance raised above $137M” was a catalyst.

surprises.description: Kestra raised its long-term gross-margin goal beyond the prior 70% target, now aiming for the mid-70% range within two to three years. The preview expected roughly 58% gross margin for FY2027 but did not anticipate a higher long-term target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised its long-term gross margin target to the mid-70% range within the next 2-3 years, up from the prior 70% goal,” while expecting “70% for full-year fiscal 2029.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the prior FY2027 guidance as “gross margin expansion of about 700bps, to roughly 58% for the year.”

surprises.description: Management said a significant national payer expanded coverage to non-ischemic patients on guideline-directed medical therapy. The preview did not flag this coverage change, and the newly covered group is substantial given management’s estimate that over 60% of the typical WCD population is non-ischemic.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A significant national payer expanded coverage to non-ischemic patients on guideline-directed medical therapy for the first time,” and “over 60% of the typical WCD population is non-ischemic.”

surprises.description: The call said the higher in-network mix is now boosting revenue per patient and revenue-cycle efficiency, addressing the preview’s concern that the shift had not yet appeared in revenue per prescription. The call did not provide a new numerical revenue-per-fit or revenue-per-prescription figure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “In-network fittings have risen to the low 80% range from about 70% at the IPO 18 months ago, boosting revenue per patient and RCM efficiency.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue per prescription has been flat” and “The in-network shift has not yet shown up in that ratio”; investors wanted “evidence that reimbursement and AI tooling investments are turning into price, not only volume.”

in_line: Q1 gross margin of 56.5% was within the preview’s modeled range of roughly 56–57% and above its 56% catalyst threshold; sequential expansion also continued as expected.
In-network fittings reached the low-80% range, consistent with the preview’s stated target of “low-mid 80s.”
Management said the second half is expected to outpace the first half, consistent with the preview’s description of FY2027 guidance as explicitly second-half weighted.

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA reached $18 million and adjusted diluted EPS was $1.02, far above the preview’s expected adjusted EPS range. The $10.4 million tariff refund was a major contributor, so the reported earnings strength was not purely operational.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA reached $18 million versus $6.7 million in the prior year … including a $10.4 million tariff refund benefit”; “adjusted diluted EPS rose to $1.02 from $0.38 including tariff refunds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EPS $0.11 or $0.27”; the preview’s base scenario was “$0.26–0.30.”

surprises.description: The full-year fiscal 2026 guide was raised above the preview’s expected range for both sales growth and adjusted EBITDA margin. The margin guide is especially higher than the preview’s working estimate.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year fiscal 2026 Vince guidance to net sales growth of 8% to 10%, with adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 9% to 9.5%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the current FY guide as “+7–8% sales” and “5.5–6.0% adj. EBITDA margin.”

surprises.description: The underlying gross-margin result was weaker than the preview anticipated: excluding the tariff refund, gross margin declined 290 basis points, versus the preview’s estimate of about 50 basis points of compression from tariffs.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin rose to 60.9% from 50.4%, but excluding the tariff refund benefit, gross margin actually declined 290 basis points due to higher product and freight input costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said guidance implied “~50 bps of margin compression from tariffs.”

surprises.description: Debt was substantially lower than the liquidity concerns in the preview suggested: the preview cited $29.1 million of Q1 borrowings, while the call reported $12.3 million of long-term debt. The supplied facts do not give updated cash or revolver availability, however.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The balance sheet strengthened with long-term debt reduced to $12.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Q1 had “cash … $0.8M, borrowings $29.1M, and revolver availability $31.2M,” and flagged whether Vince could fund OVO and holiday inventory.

in_line: Q2 sales were close to the preview’s roughly $80.9 million consensus and its $81.5–82.5 million base scenario: reported sales were $81.8 million.
The decline in net income and diluted EPS was consistent with the preview’s warning that GAAP results would fall year over year because of the prior-year ERC benefit.
OVO’s expected FY2027 accretion framing was consistent with the preview, which said management had guided only to accretion in FY2027.

surprises.description: Liquidity was materially tighter than the preview’s roughly $91 million net-debt reference: year-end net debt was $128 million, with only $11 million of cash. The company also amended its credit agreement for extended covenant relief and hired Guggenheim to evaluate debt, equity, and asset-sale options.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net debt rose to $128 million from $114 million a year ago, with cash of only $11 million”; the company “amended its credit agreement to extend covenant relief” and retained Guggenheim “to evaluate capital raising options including debt, equity, and divestitures.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch FY26 free cash flow, net debt against ~$91M”

surprises.description: Gross margin contracted rather than expanding as the preview said would support the cost-out story. Full-year adjusted gross margin fell to 38% from 39.1%, and Q4 margin was 34.7% versus 35.5% a year earlier even with a roughly $7 million tariff refund that will not recur in FY27.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year adjusted gross margin fell to 38% from 39.1%, with Q4 margin of 34.7% including an approximately $7 million tariff refund benefit that is not expected to recur in fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Expansion on falling revenue would support the cost-out story. Contraction would suggest volume is being bought with promotion.”

surprises.description: FY27 guidance still calls for revenue to decline, rather than stabilize, although the expected mid-single-digit drop is a slower decline than FY26’s 10.8%. The outlook therefore offers improvement in the rate of decline but not a return to growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company guided fiscal 2027 revenue to decline in the mid-single-digit range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The question is whether revenue stabilizes”; the bull case assumed “flat revenue,” while the bear case anticipated “another decline.”

surprises.description: Management provided a specific FY27 adjusted EBITDA target of $10–15 million, rather than leaving the outlook qualitative or withholding a number. The target absorbs roughly $12 million of additional variable compensation expense, but is below the preview’s bullish $25–40 million scenario.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $10 to $15 million, which absorbs roughly $12 million of additional variable compensation expense.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The question is … whether management gives an EBITDA number. Absence of a number would itself be a negative signal”; the bull scenario projected “$25–40M EBITDA.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue came in slightly below the preview’s derived consensus range, though the reported Easter timing shift accounts for about 1.5% of overall quarterly revenue and helps explain the shortfall. On that timing-adjusted basis, the result would be around the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 FY2026 consolidated revenue declined 12.9% to $293.1 million”; the Easter shift reduced overall Q4 revenue “by about 1.5%, with no full-year impact.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Revenue | ~$295–300M (derived)”

surprises.description: FY26 adjusted EBITDA finished slightly above the company’s breakeven ±$2 million guidance band, rather than at its upper limit or below it. The outperformance was small, and full-year EBITDA remained far below the prior year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full year adjusted EBITDA [fell] to $2.9 million from $29.2 million a year earlier.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 adj. EBITDA: breakeven ±$2M.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EBITDA loss was modestly narrower than the preview’s derived expectation of a $32–34 million loss, although it still widened from the prior year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $31 million from a $24.2 million loss in the prior-year period.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA | ~−$32M to −$34M (derived)”

in_line: FY26 revenue was $1.5 billion, down 10.8%, broadly matching the preview’s roughly $1.51 billion consensus and the company’s 10%–12% decline guidance.

Consumer floral and gift revenue declined 13.4%, close to the preview’s mid-teens base case and between its stated positive-surprise threshold (better than about 12% down) and structural-concern threshold (18% down or worse).
The $50 million cost-savings target was achieved, and the additional $15–20 million of FY27 savings had already been flagged in the preview.

surprises.description: Vera Bradley reported $3.3 million of net income from continuing operations, or $0.11 per diluted share, versus the preview’s published EPS estimate of negative $0.08. That is a substantial positive gap, though the preview cautioned that the consensus EPS basis was ambiguous.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income from continuing operations improved by $3.8 million to $3.3 million ($0.11 per diluted share), versus a loss of $0.5 million (negative $0.02 per share) a year ago.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS | −$0.08”; the preview adds that “the EPS consensus appears to blend GAAP and non-GAAP bases.”

surprises.description: Direct comparable sales rose 9.2%, above the preview’s published figure of about 5% and its +8% threshold for a supportive result. The result was close to the roughly +9% buy-side whisper, so it beat the published expectation more clearly than the higher informal expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Direct segment (over 90% of business) grew 8% to $65.4 million with comparable sales up 9.2%, its fifth consecutive quarter of sequential improvement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Direct comp against the ~+5% published figure and the ~+9% whisper”; the preview also says “A reading of +8% or better supports the turnaround.”

surprises.description: Indirect revenue was only $6.3 million, far below the preview’s $12 million watch level tied to the Nordstrom back-to-school capsule. The reported decline was attributed to marketplace-strategy timing shifts and reduced liquidation sales, even though strategic wholesale accounts had mid-single-digit selling growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Indirect segment revenue fell 39% to $6.3 million due to marketplace strategy timing shifts and reduced liquidation sales, though strategic wholesale accounts still delivered mid-single-digit selling growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q2 carries the 89-door Nordstrom back-to-school capsule. Watch for $12M+ and any door-count update.”

surprises.description: The reported gross margin reached 59.8%, but most of the increase came from tariff refunds rather than underlying improvement: refunds added about 980 basis points, while gross margin excluding them improved only just over 40 basis points. That makes the headline margin much less indicative of structural progress than a simple comparison would suggest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Reported gross margin surged to 59.8% from 49.9%, but this included $8 million in tariff refunds contributing ~980 basis points; underlying gross margin excluding refunds improved just over 40 basis points.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Gross margin quality. Q1's 51.8% included mix, lower freight and duty, and a tariff step-down. Key question: how much of Q2 margin is one-time tariff refund recovery versus structural.”

surprises.description: SG&A rose to 54% of revenue from 51.2%, with higher variable compensation pressuring operating margin. The preview discussed profitability but did not flag this increase in expenses.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A rose to 54% of net revenues from 51.2%, driven mainly by higher variable compensation, pressuring the operating margin despite the top-line gains.”

surprises.description: The inventory decline was partly driven by a $5.3 million Project Restoration reserve, an unanticipated factor that means the reported reduction was not solely a result of selling or managing down inventory.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Inventory ended the quarter down 28.4% year-over-year to $69.3 million, aided by a $5.3 million Project Restoration inventory reserve.”

surprises.description: The company ended the quarter with $34.2 million in cash, no debt, and $23 million of operating cash flow. The preview highlighted liquidity as an issue to watch but did not anticipate this cash generation or cash balance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended the quarter with $34.2 million in cash (double the prior year's $15.2 million) and no debt, generating $23 million of operating cash flow.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Inventory and liquidity” was flagged as an issue to watch; the preview noted “zero ABL drawn” in Q1 but gave no Q2 cash-flow or cash-balance expectation.

surprises.description: Vera Bradley discontinued its third-party sales-rep agency and plans to rebuild an in-house wholesale sales team. This was a previously unflagged change in its wholesale-sales approach, with no reported financial impact yet.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company discontinued its third-party sales rep agency to rebuild an in-house wholesale sales team.”

surprises.description: Management reported positive Google Search growth for “Vera Bradley” for the first time in more than a decade, an unanticipated favorable brand-demand signal.
surprises.fact_evidence: “[The company] reported positive Google Search growth for 'Vera Bradley' for the first time in over a decade.”

in_line: Revenue was $71.6 million, essentially matching the preview’s $71.6 million consensus and its roughly $72–$74 million base scenario.

Management reiterated FY27 sales guidance of $255–$270 million and its target of at least 50% year-over-year operating-profit improvement, consistent with the preview’s expectation that guidance would be reaffirmed.
Inventory ended at $69.3 million, within the preview’s cited FY inventory guide of $60–$75 million and below its roughly $80 million level of concern.

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $26.7 million, about 23–25% above the preview’s $21.3–$21.8 million consensus range, a much stronger quarter than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 revenue reached $26.7 million, up 33% year-over-year and 43% sequentially.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Quarter revenue … Consensus (3 analysts) | $21.3M – $21.8M.”

surprises.description: The preview’s base scenario expected gross margin of 10–12%, but Q4 margin was only 6.3%. Management attributed the decline to an inventory impairment, rather than identifying launch-phase pricing as the cause.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 gross margin fell to 6.3% from 12.3% a year earlier, driven by an inventory impairment recognized during the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base … margin 10–12%”; the preview also said the call needed to explain whether the low margin reflected “launch-phase nicotine ODM pricing … or more cannabis returns or inventory absorption.”

surprises.description: Credit losses were substantial, with $9.2 million in Q4 and $20.7 million for the full year; the preview’s base case anticipated a moderate provision. Management also said legacy receivable write-offs are expected to be substantially resolved only during FY2027, indicating the cleanup is not yet complete.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Credit losses remained elevated at $9.2 million in Q4 and $20.7 million for the full year, with management expecting legacy receivable write-offs to be substantially resolved during fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario assumed a “moderate provision”; it warned that “a large Q4 provision would mean the AR cleanup is not finished.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted a goal of cash-flow positivity in H2 calendar 2026, but management said upcoming capacity investment payments may delay reaching that goal. This adds a specific potential obstacle to the expected timeline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Upcoming capacity investment payments may delay reaching cash-flow-positive status.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Its only forward marker is a goal of being cash-flow positive in H2 calendar 2026”; the preview also flagged whether that claim would be “reaffirmed, softened, or dropped.”

surprises.description: Management flagged a potential significant liquidity event involving the IKE Tech joint venture during FY2027, which was not anticipated in the preview. The call facts do not clarify the event’s terms or financial effect, so its shareholder impact is uncertain.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management flagged a potential significant liquidity event involving its IKE Tech joint venture during fiscal 2027, separate from any regulatory authorization.”

surprises.description: The company gave a more specific manufacturing outlook than the preview: FY2027 is expected to be the first full year of vapor and nicotine pouch production at its Malaysian facilities, with the second factory capable of holding up to 73 lines. The preview discussed the vapor ODM ramp but did not mention nicotine pouches or this facility scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 will mark the first full year of vapor and nicotine pouch production at company-owned Malaysian facilities”; “the second Malaysian factory can hold up to 73 production lines with potential capacity in the hundreds of millions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described vapor ODM as “launched July 2026 for small and mid-size brands, with large brands targeted for 2027,” but did not mention nicotine pouch production or the Malaysian factory’s capacity.

surprises.description: Full-year operating cash use fell to just $569,000 from $7.4 million, a strong improvement relevant to the preview’s liquidity and cash-flow concerns. The preview gave no expectation for this annual cash-use figure, so the positive difference is directionally clear but not precisely measurable against a forecast.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash used improved dramatically to just $569,000 from $7.4 million a year prior.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the cash-flow-positive goal as “central to credibility” and highlighted liquidity as a key watch item, but gave no forecast for full-year operating cash use.

surprises.description: Q3 revenue was $7.7 million, about 5% above the preview’s $7.35 million consensus estimate and above its $7.2 million base case. The revenue result was better than expected, though not as high as the preview’s $8.0 million bull case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 9.2% to $7.7 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 FY26 Consensus” revenue was “$7.35M”; the base scenario was “$7.2M” and the bull scenario “$8.0M.”

surprises.description: Consolidated gross margin was 65.4%, below the preview’s base-case expectation of about 66.5%. The compression was more pronounced than that base case allowed for.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Consolidated gross margin compressed to 65.4% from 68.3% a year earlier, reflecting shifts in revenue composition and product mix across all three segments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario expected “GM about 66.5%.”

surprises.description: The company reported about $1.4 million of U.S. Navy orders for DAVD tethered systems, including four DAVD Flex systems and Echoscope Sonars. The preview expected Navy orders to start in Q3 but noted there had been no order announcements and that a slip seemed possible, so the specific order amount and systems were a positive realization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Since the last earnings call, the company received approximately $1.4 million in U.S. Navy orders for DAVD tethered systems, including 4 DAVD Flex systems and Echoscope Sonars for training purposes.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked, “Did DAVD untethered orders commence in Q3?” and said “Qualitative language suggests a slip.”

surprises.description: Defense Engineering Services grew much faster than its recent pace: revenue surged 68.3%, compared with 37.9% growth in the prior quarter cited in the preview. The preview did not give a Q3 segment estimate, but the acceleration was stronger than the recent trend it described.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Defense Engineering Services revenue surged 68.3% to $2.7 million on increased funding across long-standing defense programs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Defense Engineering Services grew 37.9% to $2.5M on UK work” in Q2 FY26.

surprises.description: SG&A was lower as a share of revenue than a year ago, but the reported 36.1% ratio implies roughly $2.8 million of quarterly expense at $7.7 million of revenue—above the preview’s $2.1–$2.2 million level to watch. The higher implied dollars are a negative against that expectation, despite the improved ratio.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A improved to 36.1% of revenue from 40.6% a year earlier,” with “higher PAL earn-out contingent consideration” partially offsetting lower payroll costs and favorable FX.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said, “Watch whether $2.1–2.2M holds.”

surprises.description: Marine Technology’s rental revenue rose sharply and helped lift the segment’s gross margin to 78.5%, despite falling hardware revenue. The preview focused on Marine revenue and consolidated margin but did not anticipate this segment-level rental and margin outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Marine Technology rental revenue jumped 131.1% to approximately $0.7 million (from $0.3 million), boosting the segment's gross margin to 78.5% even as hardware revenue fell 17.8% to $2.3 million.”

surprises.description: Coda Octopus said it moved from an accumulated deficit to positive retained earnings for the first time in its history. The preview did not flag this milestone, making it an unanticipated positive signal of accumulated profitability.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Coda Octopus transitioned from an accumulated deficit to positive retained earnings for the first time in its history.”

surprises.description: Management said NANO sonar was nearing SAT trials with an underwater vehicle OEM. The preview discussed NanoGen platform opportunities, but did not mention this specific NANO sonar trial milestone.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management was “advancing NANO sonar toward imminent SAT trials with an underwater vehicle OEM.”

surprises.description: Management also disclosed electronic-warfare opportunities with four prime defense contractors, a new prospective program area not raised in the preview. These are opportunities rather than reported awards, so the development is positive but preliminary.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management was “pursuing electronic warfare opportunities with four prime defense contractors.”

in_line: Marine Technology revenue was $3.4 million: in line with the preview’s approximately $3.4 million whisper and its $3.3–$3.5 million base-case range, and above the preview’s under-$3.0-million downside threshold.
Diluted EPS was $0.12, matching the preview’s $0.12 consensus estimate.

Management continued to characterize the Middle East and Asia disruptions as timing-related, consistent with the preview’s account of the prior-quarter explanation that the UAE project delays were “timing, not structural.”
The company remained debt-free and had $31.7 million in cash, broadly consistent with the preview’s report of $30.6 million in cash and no debt.

surprises.description: FPS guided to FY2027 revenue of $2.4–$2.6 billion, with a $2.5 billion midpoint—about 20% above the $2.09 billion consensus estimate. This is a much higher outlook than the preview’s base case of $2.0–$2.1 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for revenue of $2.4-$2.6 billion (76% growth at midpoint).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 revenue | Consensus | $2.09B (+50%)”; the base scenario was “FY27 revenue $2.0–2.1B.”

surprises.description: Q4 bookings reached $1.5 billion, more than double the preview’s roughly $700 million expectation, and book-to-bill was 3.3x versus the 1.5x level highlighted in the preview. That is a substantially stronger order quarter than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 bookings hit a record $1.5 billion, up 375% year-over-year and 73% sequentially, producing a record book-to-bill ratio of 3.3x.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 bookings versus about $700M, and book-to-bill versus 1.5x.”

surprises.description: Q4 revenue was $462 million, well above the $425.6–$429.9 million consensus range and above the $432 million top of company guidance. The result beat the Street by roughly 7–9%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue rose 94% year-over-year to a record $462 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 revenue | Company guidance ... $392–432M ... | Consensus | $425.6M ... or $429.9M.”

surprises.description: Year-end backlog reached $3 billion, far above the prior $1.98 billion level and the preview’s $2 billion downside threshold; more than 90% of FY2027 revenue guidance is already covered by backlog. The preview had expected roughly half of FY2027 consensus revenue would still need to be booked.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Backlog reached a record $3 billion at year-end, up 256% year-over-year and now representing more than 2x fiscal 2026 revenue”; “over 90% of revenue guidance already covered by backlog.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Only 55–60% of the $1.98B backlog ships in FY27 ... so roughly half of consensus FY27 revenue still has to be booked”; “A sequential backlog decline below about $2.0B would be a bear signal.”

surprises.description: The FY2027 adjusted EPS range of $1.26–$1.40 is above the $1.17 consensus estimate, with a $1.33 midpoint; the $575–$625 million adjusted EBITDA outlook also implies about a 24% margin at midpoint. The earnings outlook is stronger than the preview’s base-case EPS of about $1.00–$1.10, although the midpoint margin is broadly in the range the preview discussed.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for ... adjusted EBITDA of $575-$625 million (86% growth), and adjusted EPS of $1.26-$1.40 (95% growth).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 adj. EPS | Consensus | $1.17 (+73%)”; the base scenario expected “EPS of about $1.00–1.10.”

surprises.description: FPS reported its first direct order from a Frontier AI lab and an MSA with a hyperscaler, with the lab’s first campus expected to exceed 1 gigawatt and the broader opportunity spanning multiple gigawatts. The preview did not identify these customer wins or this scale of opportunity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company received its first direct order from a Frontier AI lab and signed an MSA with a hyperscaler, with the Frontier lab's first campus expected to exceed 1 gigawatt and broader opportunity measured in multiple gigawatts.”

surprises.description: Powertrain Solutions generated $147 million of Q4 revenue, up 187% year over year, grew from 13% to 25% of full-year revenue, and now represents roughly 40% of backlog. The preview noted that segment figures were unavailable and treated a reported growth figure as unverified, so this was a newly disclosed source of growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Powertrain Solutions revenue grew 187% year-over-year to $147 million in Q4, rising from 13% to 25% of full-year revenue and now comprising roughly 40% of backlog.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The Q3 8-K discloses no segment or product-line revenue breakout. Treat [the ‘Powertrain Solutions segment +248%’ figure] as unverified.”

surprises.description: FPS disclosed a new 385,000-square-foot Tijuana facility that will add more than 50% to Powertrain Solutions capacity and lift total revenue capacity to about $5.8 billion in Q4 FY2027. That is above the preview’s previously noted capacity of up to $5 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “A new 385,000 square foot Powertrain Solutions facility in Tijuana will increase that segment's capacity by more than 50% and lift total revenue capacity to approximately $5.8 billion when it comes online in Q4 fiscal 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The $205M expansion is described as ‘meaningfully complete,’ with capacity for up to $5B of annual revenue.”

surprises.description: Data center revenue grew 161%, roughly four times estimated market growth, and the increase was driven mainly by a 121% rise in average revenue per customer rather than by adding customers. The preview did not flag this growth profile or its reliance on higher customer spend.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data center revenue grew 161% year-over-year (roughly 4x estimated market growth), driven mainly by a 121% increase in average revenue per customer rather than customer additions.”

surprises.description: FY2026 revenue was $1.42 billion, above both the $1.39 billion consensus estimate and the $1.39 billion top of the May guidance range. The beat over the annual revenue expectation was modest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2026 revenue grew 89% to $1.42 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue | Company guidance ... $1,350–1,390M | Consensus | $1.39B.”

surprises.description: Full-year adjusted EBITDA also exceeded the high end of guidance raised in May. The preview gave no FY2026 EBITDA consensus or guidance range, so the size of the beat cannot be measured from the materials provided.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Full-year fiscal 2026 ... adjusted EBITDA increased 91% to $323 million, exceeding the high end of guidance raised in May.”

surprises.description: FY2027 operating cash flow is guided to exceed $300 million, versus $109 million in FY2026, but the preview supplied no operating-cash-flow estimate. This is a newly disclosed cash-generation outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Operating cash flow rose 2.5x to $109 million in fiscal 2026 and is guided to exceed $300 million in fiscal 2027.”

surprises.description: FY2027 capital spending is expected to be roughly 3% of sales, above the preview’s 1–1.5% expectation. That implies a higher capex burden than anticipated, despite the decrease from 8% of sales.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Capital expenditures are expected to fall from 8% to roughly 3% of sales.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY27 capex guided to 1–1.5% of revenue.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EBITDA was $113 million, above the approximately $108 million implied expectation and the $110 million top of the prior guidance range. The amount beat expectations even though the reported 24.4% margin was slightly below the preview’s approximate 25% margin expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA jumped 163% to $113 million with margins expanding 200 basis points sequentially to 24.4%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 adj. EBITDA | ... $100–110M ... | Consensus | ~$108M (implied)”; CFO expected Q4 adj. EBITDA margin “about 25%.”

in_line: Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin was 24.4%, close to the preview’s approximate 25% expectation, and expanded about 200 basis points sequentially.
At the midpoint, FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $600 million on $2.5 billion of revenue implies an approximately 24% margin, within the preview’s discussion of roughly 23–25%.

surprises.description: Q3 GAAP EPS was $1.19, below the preview’s $1.28–$1.30 consensus range; even excluding one-time items, EPS was $1.23 and still below that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 EPS came in at $1.19 GAAP ($1.23 excluding one-time items)”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “EPS … Consensus … $1.28–$1.30”

surprises.description: Q3 gross margin was 15.8%, missing the roughly 16% guide. Management attributed the entire gap to land costs, up about 6% per home site, and said it is deliberately sacrificing margin to maintain volume and monetize legacy high-cost land.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Gross margin improved sequentially to 15.8% … but missed the roughly 16% guidance”; “Management attributes the entire margin gap to land cost, which is up about 6% per home site, as it deliberately sacrifices margin to maintain volume and monetize legacy high-cost land.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Homebuilding gross margin … ~16.0%”; “Q3 gross margin vs. the ~16.0% guide”; “Q2 showed the first sequential recovery in three years.”

surprises.description: SG&A was 9.2%, above the preview’s expected 8.8%–9.0% range. The call also reported lower divisional headcount and higher deliveries per corporate associate, but those efficiency gains did not keep the expense ratio within the expected range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SG&A rose to 9.2%, above the 8.8%-9% expected range, though divisional headcount is down ~12% year-over-year and deliveries per corporate associate are up 12%.”

surprises.description: New orders were 20,879, just below the 21,000–22,000 guided range. The preview highlighted orders as a key issue, but did not anticipate a result below the stated range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “New orders of 20,879 fell just below the guided range of 21,000-22,000.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “guided range of 21,000-22,000”

surprises.description: Mortgage rates rose to approximately 7%, above the preview’s roughly 6.77% level, and management said nearly half of visitors cannot immediately qualify. That indicates worse affordability pressure than the preview’s already cautious rate backdrop.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The 30-year fixed mortgage rate rose to approximately 7% from 6.4%-6.5% at the prior call, with the 10-year Treasury near 5%, pressuring affordability as nearly 50% of visitors cannot immediately qualify.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “30-year mortgage rates were about 6.77%, a one-year high, which matters for a builder whose margins depend on affordability.”

surprises.description: The call disclosed an expected Q4 multifamily loss of about $25 million, a segment-specific loss outlook the preview did not flag.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 guidance calls for … a multifamily loss of ~$25 million expected.”

in_line: Deliveries were 20,840, within the preview’s cited Q3 guidance range of 20,500–21,500 and close to the roughly 21,000 expectation.
Q4 gross margin guidance of 15.5%–16% matched the preview’s base-case expectation of roughly 15.5%–16%.
The company continued share repurchases, as the preview identified continued repurchases as a scenario to watch.

surprises.description: Total FY2026 net sales were $348.9 million, about $10.7 million above the preview’s $338.25 million consensus estimate. The reported total includes six weeks of Chaparral and Robalo revenue.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total company fiscal 2026 net sales reached $348.9 million” after including “a 6-week contribution from Chaparral and Robalo.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 revenue” consensus: “$338.25M.”

surprises.description: Legacy FY2026 adjusted EBITDA was $43.8 million, beating the prior $40 million standalone guidance by $3.8 million. That is a clear positive gap against the company’s stated target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Legacy fiscal 2026” adjusted EBITDA rose to “$43.8 million, exceeding prior increased guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guidance (May 7, standalone): FY26” adjusted EBITDA “$40M.”

surprises.description: Q4 legacy sales were $96.6 million, above the preview’s $93 million standalone-implied estimate, and grew 21.5% rather than the implied 17.0%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 legacy net sales grew 21.5% to $96.6 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The implied standalone Q4 is $93.0M revenue (+17.0% YoY).”

surprises.description: Q4 legacy adjusted EBITDA margin reached 19.3%, well above the preview’s implied 15.9% margin. The 340-basis-point gap indicates stronger operating profitability than the expected Q4 profile.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q4 legacy adjusted EBITDA margin “expand[ed] 730 basis points to 19.3%,” driven by “premium X-Series mix and lower discounts.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The implied standalone Q4 is” adjusted EBITDA of “$14.8M (15.9% margin).”

surprises.description: The preview identified falling unit volumes as a concern, but reported retail sales rose low-single digits at MasterCraft and high-single digits at Robalo while the broader powerboat industry declined mid- to high-single digits. Retail performance was more resilient than that concern suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “MasterCraft retail rose low-single digits and Robalo grew high-single digits,” both “outperforming a broader powerboat industry that declined mid- to high-single digits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted that “MCFT’s own unit volumes [were] falling” and flagged “quality of growth” as a key issue.

surprises.description: Inventory ended lower rather than showing a channel refill: legacy field inventory was down about 30%, with turns better than pre-pandemic levels, and Chaparral/Robalo inventory was down about 20%. This provides a more favorable inventory update than the preview’s concern about post-acquisition dealer inventory and possible refill.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Legacy field inventory ended the year down approximately 30% YoY with turns better than pre-pandemic levels,” while “Chaparral and Robalo inventory was down about 20%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to watch for “any shift from ‘demand-driven wholesale’ toward channel refill” and noted that MCFT “did not control” MPX dealer inventory during the destock.

surprises.description: Management now expects retail demand to fall approximately 5% to 10% over the next six months and has paused Chaparral Surf Series production while moderating Chaparral/Robalo volumes. That is a concrete forward demand and production warning, beyond the preview’s general concern about weak marine demand.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “expects retail demand to decline approximately 5% to 10% over the next six months” and “has paused Chaparral Surf Series production while moderating Chaparral/Robalo volumes to align with retail.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s bear case was triggered by language that marine retail “remained challenged through the summer selling season.”

surprises.description: The preview treated full-year FY2027 guidance as the decisive catalyst, including a $604.6 million revenue consensus estimate, but the reported outlook here is for the six-month July–December transition period rather than a full-year FY2027 forecast. The transition-period figures do not establish how management views the full-year consensus target.
surprises.fact_evidence: The company guided the “6-month transition period (July-December 2026)” to net sales of “$287-291 million,” adjusted EBITDA of “$29-32 million,” and adjusted EPS of “$0.66-0.76.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called “FY27 guidance” the “decisive item” and identified “FY27 revenue guide vs. $604.6M consensus” as the key catalyst.

surprises.description: Q4 produced a $7.0 million GAAP loss, with a $10.1 million non-cash Crest brand impairment contributing to it. The preview expected GAAP results to look weak because of purchase accounting, but did not anticipate this specific impairment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 GAAP net loss” was “$7.0 million (-$0.35 per share),” driven by “a $10.1 million non-cash Crest brand impairment plus acquisition-related purchase accounting and transaction costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Expect an inventory step-up hit to gross margin, $84.0M of intangibles beginning to amortize, and $92.8M of goodwill. GAAP results will look weak.”

in_line: Acquisition-related purchase accounting was a source of weak GAAP results, consistent with the preview’s warning that purchase accounting would make GAAP results look weak.
